With its unique combination of Aurora Veil, Snow Warning, and a good Speed tier, Alolan Ninetales establishes itself as a premiere lead for setting Aurora Veil, giving it the advantage over fellow dual screens setters like Grimmsnarl and Deoxys-S, which require two turns instead to set up. Encore shuts down setup sweepers that try to take advantage of Alolan Ninetales's mediocre offensive presence like Kingambit and punishes defensive Pokemon like Ting-Lu, Garganacl, and Corviknight, giving Alolan Ninetales's teammates free opportunities to set up. Freeze-Dry threatens common leads like Landorus-T, Hisuian Samurott, and Gliscor as well as Pelipper, which otherwise removes Alolan Ninetales's snow unthreatened. Freeze-Dry can also target certain threats like Ogerpon-W and Walking Wake. Moonblast serves as a stronger secondary STAB option to slam threats like Darkrai, Zamazenta, and Weavile that Freeze-Dry cannot while hitting Hisuian Samurott slightly harder. Snowscape allows Alolan Ninetales to reset snow in the face of weather setters Torkoal, Ninetales, Pelipper, and Tyranitar, ensuring both Aurora Veil and the advantage in the weather wars. Roar is an option to improve the mirror matchup against offensive teams, as it can stop setup sweepers like Terastallized Dragonite and Zamazenta more reliably in cases where Encore couldn't. Moreover, forcing in the Booster Energy users into the field essentially wastes the item if they're not ready to sweep yet. Though Alolan Ninetales rarely wants to Terastallize, Tera Water is run to shed its Fire and Steel weaknesses, flipping the matchup on Pokemon like Iron Moth, Gholdengo, and Iron Crown. Tera Ghost is also an option to emergency check a boosted IronPress Zamazenta, especially with Encore.

With its invaluable ability to set dual screens in one turn, Alolan Ninetales cements itself as a lead for hyper offense teams. One sweeper that pairs exceptionally well with Alolan Ninetales is Kyurem, as its Dragon Dance set heavily appreciates both Aurora Veil and snow extending its already solid bulk to absurd levels. Other setup sweepers like Zamazenta, Kingambit, and Raging Bolt similarly enjoy Aurora Veil, able to boost with near impunity then crush the opposing team. In particular, Bulk Up Great Tusk is an excellent teammate for its added entry hazard removal in Rapid Spin, which Aurora Veil teams can otherwise struggle with. Rillaboom combines Grassy Terrain's recovery with Aurora Veil to allow even more opportunities for its teammates to set up with ease, which is especially useful for those weak to Earthquake like the aforementioned Raging Bolt and Kingambit. However, Alolan Ninetales's biggest foe, Cinderace, resists both of its STAB moves and can steal Aurora Veil with Court Change. Other major threats include Iron Moth and Steel-types like Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Scizor, which similarly ignore Alolan Ninetales's attacks, can threaten an OHKO, and, in Iron Moth's case, can set up a Substitute freely. Thus, a great partner is Manaphy, which is able to shrug off any Steel- and Fire-type attacks while synergizing well with Aurora Veil, especially for its Double Dance set. Iron Moth easily boosts on Cinderace and threatens Steel-types, as well as snowballing through sun and Sticky Web teams that would otherwise give Alolan Ninetales trouble; Aurora Veil allows Iron Moth to take a hit or two, which is especially useful for the Substitute variants. Dragonite can serve as a useful check to Iron Moth, offensive Cinderace, and other offensive threats with its powerful Extreme Speed. Another Pokemon to watch out for is Corviknight, which can remove Aurora Veil with Defog, so teammates like the aforementioned Iron Moth and Raging Bolt are useful to pressure it from ever entering the field and using Defog freely.

Snow Support (Ice).description:
Alolan Ninetales is a great support Pokemon for Ice teams thanks to its ability to set snow and Aurora Veil to make its team much harder to take down and facilitate its teammates' sweeping attempts with Encore. In addition, its typing and Speed tier let it hit otherwise troublesome Fighting-types such as Keldeo, Urshifu-R, and Great Tusk. Freeze-Dry is useful against Water teams, being able to threaten Pelipper and Quagsire out and dissuade Pelipper from setting rain in its face in an attempt to stop Aurora Veil. Moonblast is useful against the ubiquitous Fighting- and Dragon-types in the tier, as it hits Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Scrafty, and Raging Bolt that are otherwise problems for Ice teams. Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to lock a defensive Pokemon, such as Toxapex, into a weak move or a setup sweeper, such as Swords Dance Iron Hands or Bulk Up Ursaluna, into a stat-boosting move, letting Alolan Ninetales's teammates take care of the aforementioned Pokemon. Icy Rock is used for extending snow turns for the team, particularly assisting allies with snow-related abilities, while Light Clay can be used to extend the amount of time Aurora Veil is up for, supporting its more specially frail teammates for longer.

Mamoswine can threaten Fire-types like Heatran, Torkoal, and Cinderace with Earthquake while packing Thick Fat for a pseudo-Fire neutrality. Additionally, it sets Stealth Rock, which can help Alolan Ninetales pick off weakened threats such as Kyurem. Cetitan is a great partner, as Slush Rush allows it to outspeed and OHKO most of the metagame after a Belly Drum boost, which is easier to acquire thanks to snow and Aurora Veil from Alolan Ninetales. Alolan Sandslash appreciates snow and Aurora Veil both bolstering its bulk and Slush Rush doubling its Speed, allowing it to threaten Fire-, Steel-, and Poison-types like Iron Moth, Iron Treads, and pre-Unburden Sneasler with Earthquake. In exchange, Alolan Sandslash can use Rapid Spin to clear entry hazards and deal with Hatterene and Flutter Mane, which can both take advantage of Alolan Ninetales. Cloyster is a threatening Shell Smash sweeper that can take out threats to Ice like Ogerpon-H and Ceruledge with Rock Blast and has a high Defense stat that makes it nearly unbreakable in snow. In return, Alolan Ninetales facilitates Cloyster's Shell Smash setup thanks to Aurora Veil and snow support. Cloyster also appreciates Alolan Ninetales locking its defensive answers, such as Toxapex, into unfavorable moves. Kyurem is a good offensive teammate that breaks down walls like Archaludon with snow-assisted Blizzards and breaks down Water-types like Toxapex and Swampert with Freeze-Dry. Snow and Aurora Veil also make it significantly harder to revenge kill. Avalugg is a defensive behemoth that, when under snow and Aurora Veil, takes on almost every physical attacker in the tier. It can also remove Stealth Rock with Rapid Spin to improve Alolan Ninetales's lacking longevity. Finally, Frosmoth becomes a dangerous sweeping threat under snow and Aurora Veil thanks to Quiver Dance, letting it potentially win the Ground, Flying, and Fairy matchups.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.
battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Speed EV Benchmarks

  • Alolan Ninetales should almost always use a Timid nature, as this is the most efficient way for it to outspeed a wide variety of threats.

  • 60+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Adamant Urshifu formes.

  • 68+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Modest Iron Crown.

  • 84+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Modest Chi-Yu.

  • 116+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Jolly Landorus-T, Jolly Annihilape, and Jolly Gouging Fire.

  • 156+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Adamant Ogerpon formes and Modest Latios.

  • 164+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Jolly Urshifu formes.

  • 172+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Timid Iron Crown.

  • 188+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Timid Chi-Yu and Jolly Entei.

  • 204+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Jolly Garchomp.

  • 220+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Adamant Roaring Moon.

  • 244+ Spe EVs: This outspeeds Adamant Meowscarada.

Defensive EV Benchmarks

  • 244 HP / 108 SpD EVs: This survives Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast.

  • 244 HP / 92 SpD EVs: This has a 93.7% chance of surviving Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast.

  • 180 HP / 244 Def EVs: This avoids a 2HKO from Adamant Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and almost always avoids an OHKO from Scizor's unboosted Bullet Punch.

  • 196 HP / 244 Def EVs: This spread is not OHKOed by Adamant Scizor's Bullet Punch if it lacks an offensive item, and it is also not 2HKOed by Adamant Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes.

  • 148 HP / 180 SpD EVs: This is the most efficient EV spread for surviving Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast at the cost of serious physical bulk.

Screens Setter.description:
• With the new Defense-boosting mechanic for Ice-types in snow, Alolan Ninetales is the premier screens setter in the current metagame, as well as being a decent check against fearsome physical attackers like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-R.

  • Encore: Encore can thwart bulkier setup foes that would otherwise take advantage of Alolan Ninetales's mediocre offenses.

  • Blizzard versus Freeze-Dry: Blizzard's high Base Power helps make up for Alolan Ninetales's lack of power. Freeze-Dry is much less powerful but is more consistent at pressuring Water-types like Ogerpon-W and Basculegion-M.

  • Pain Split: Pain Split punishes foes that assume Alolan Ninetales will simply allow revenge kills from slower Pokemon, giving it a new lease on life to check physical threats. This especially works well with Rocky Helmet.

Other Options
  • Misty Terrain: Misty Terrain stops common users of status such as Yawn Ursaluna-B and Thunder Wave Porygon2 from having an impact, though it does weaken grounded Dragon-type teammates like Raging Bolt and Roaring Moon.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Thanks to its high Speed and increased physical bulk in snow, Alolan Ninetales does not normally want to Terastallize. It's true it can help with Steel-types moves from Scizor and Choice Scarf Gholdengo, but it is often more advisable to play around this weakness through its teammates.

  • Water: Tera Water is a balanced defensive typing that completely flips Alolan Ninetales's Steel-type weakness, all but guaranteeing it can set Aurora Veil. It also lets it resist Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes—a common counter against screens—though Alolan Ninetales will normally survive it without Terastallizing.

  • Fire: Tera Fire can be used offensively and defensively against Steel-types, with invested Tera Blast usually OHKOing Scizor and 2HKOing Gholdengo. Do note though that this comes at the cost of having a dramatically worse Urshifu-R matchup.

  • Ice: Tera Ice lets Alolan Ninetales keep its Defense boost in snow while increasing its offensive output and making the devastating Steel weakness more manageable.

Items

  • Light Clay: Light Clay extends Aurora Veil's duration and makes it much harder for the opponent to play around it.

  • Rocky Helmet: If using a physically defensive EV spread, Rocky Helmet lets Alolan Ninetales severely punish Urshifu-R that lack Punching Glove.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash is good insurance against fast super effective hits, but it's overall less useful in the majority of matchups.

EV Spread Examples

  • Alolan Ninetales has a wide variety of possible EV spreads. If the examples below don't suit your needs, consider checking out some useful Speed and Defensive benchmarks later in this analysis to help create a custom EV spread!

  • 244 HP / 92 SpD / 172 Spe with Timid: This spread lets Alolan Ninetales outspeed up to Timid Iron Crown and Jolly Urshifu formes while surviving Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera-boosted Moonblast on all but the highest damage roll.

  • 228 HP / 76 Def / 4 SpA / 116 SpD / 84 Spe with Timid: With this investment in bulk, Alolan Ninetales survives Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast, as well as avoiding an OHKO from Ogerpon-H's super effective Ivy Cudgel while the weather is still snow. The Speed investment lets Alolan Ninetales outrun Modest Chi-Yu.

  • 180 HP / 140 SpD / 188 Spe with Timid: This spread sacrifices some physical bulk in exchange for outspeeding Timid Chi-Yu and almost always survives Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera-boosted Moonblast.

  • 180 HP / 244 Def / 84 Spe with Timid: This physically bulky spread avoids a 2HKO from Adamant Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes while outspeeding up to Modest Chi-Yu. It also avoids an OHKO from Scizor's unboosted Bullet Punch on all but the highest damage roll.

Snow Setter.description:
• Alolan Ninetales is the premier snow setter due to its Speed tier and utility. It enables offensive structures that flourish with Aurora Veil support, reducing damage from opposing Pokemon.
  • Alolan Ninetales runs Freeze-Dry in order to force super effective damage on prominent Water-types like Ogerpon-W.
  • Icy Wind is a strong speed control option that allows Alolan Ninetales and its teammates to outpace Chien-Pao and Ogerpon formes. Blizzard can be brought over Icy Wind as a stronger STAB option, allowing it to guarantee a OHKO on Landorus.
  • Encore allows Alolan Ninetales to deter setup from Pokemon like Calm Mind Raging Bolt and bulky Swords Dance Ogerpon-W, which is normally threatening for Alolan Ninetales and its teammates, as well as locking opposing Pokemon like Incineroar and Iron Hands into Fake Out. Moonblast is a secondary STAB option that allows it to hit Incineroar for neutral damage and Chien-Pao for super effective damage. Protect can be chosen to aid Alolan Ninetales in preserving itself to reset snow later.
  • The bulk investment on Alolan Ninetales allows it to survive two Hard Stone-boosted Diamond Storms from Adamant Diancie when behind Aurora Veil and Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-C without Aurora Veil support.
  • The Speed and Special Attack investment allows Alolan Ninetales to outspeed and OHKO Landorus with Blizzard or Freeze-Dry.
  • Tera Ghost is the premier Tera type on Alolan Ninetales due to the Fake Out immunity, allowing it to drop Protect and ensure that Aurora Veil is set up, while also providing a Fighting-type immunity from threats like Iron Hands and a resistance to Glimmora's and Landorus's Sludge Bombs.
  • Teams with Alolan Ninetales often play very offensively, benefitting from the extra bulk that its Aurora Veil provides by enabling setup threats like Raging Bolt, Galarian Moltres, and Kingambit. Kyurem is often Alolan Ninetales's best partner, as it benefits from the snow's Defense boost and an accurate Blizzard.
  • Alolan Ninetales appreciates a strong Fake Out user, like Iron Hands or Incineroar, to allow it to set up Aurora Veil more freely.
  • Alolan Ninetales appreciates Landorus, Iron Hands, Ogerpon-W, and Okidogi because they can offensively threaten prolific Steel- and Fire-types such as Gholdengo, Ogerpon-H, and Incineroar, which check Alolan Ninetales.

Aurora Veil (Ice).description: With access to Snow Warning and Aurora Veil, a great typing, and a key Speed tier that lets it deal with the likes of Keldeo and Urshifu-R, Alolan Ninetales proves to be extremely useful for Ice teams. Freeze-Dry makes it a menace in the Water matchup, dealing heavy damage to Swampert, Gastrodon, and Pelipper. Encore enables Alolan Ninetales to disrupt walls and slower setup sweepers like Ting-Lu and Tapu Fini. Alolan Ninetales's teammates appreciate its supportive capabilities; setup sweepers like Swords Dance Weavile and Dragon Dance Baxcalibur have a lot more setup opportunities, and offensive Pokemon like Galarian Darmanitan have an easier time switching in. Cloyster is a stellar partner; its defensive set removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin and sets Spikes to wear down Keldeo and Toxapex for Alolan Ninetales, while Shell Smash variants can more easily set up with its assistance. SubRoost Kyurem helps Alolan Ninetales pressure Water teams with its own Freeze-Dry and checks Fighting-types like Galarian Zapdos with a Chople Berry. Piloswine lays down Stealth Rock and switches into and checks a variety of Fire-types that Alolan Ninetales hates, such as Volcarona and Iron Moth.

lc.overview: Alolan Diglett is an excellent wallbreaker and late-game cleaner in Little Cup, with a blazing Speed tier and dangerous STAB combination. With solid coverage and the power boost from Life Orb, Alolan Diglett can OHKO or 2HKO most of the tier. Despite its strengths, Alolan Diglett is very frail, making it difficult to get onto the field without support and means it is also susceptible to priority moves.
lc.comments:
Other Options

Alolan Diglett can use Swords Dance to be near unstoppable after a boost, but it is unreliable due to Alolan Diglett's fragility leaving few opportunities to set up. Tera Blast Flying deals heavy damage to Mienfoo and Foongus and OHKOs the two if they lost their Eviolite as well as OHKOing Toedscool from full health with Eviolite, but other Tera types are often more useful. Alolan Diglett can be used as a lead on hyper offense teams with a Focus Sash to set Stealth Rock and faint with Memento for a teammate to set up.

Checks and Counters

Choice Scarf Pokemon: Choice Scarf users such as Hisuian Growlithe and Mienfoo can outspeed and revenge kill Alolan Diglett.

Grookey: Grookey's Grassy Terrain halves the power of Earthquake and lets it threaten Alolan Diglett with priority Grassy Glide.

Bulky Pokemon: Pokemon like Mienfoo, Foongus, and Mudbray can take a hit from Alolan Diglett if they are healthy enough and threaten it back.

Life Orb.description:
Earthquake threatens OHKOs on Pokemon such as Glimmet, Tinkatink, and Chinchou. Rock Blast threatens the Flying-types that otherwise would give Alolan Diglett trouble, notably Vullaby due to the interaction with Weak Armor. Sucker Punch helps Alolan Diglett pick off weakened foes that Speed tie or outspeed it, such as Wingull and Hisuian Growlithe. Iron Head lets Alolan Diglett almost always 2HKO Toedscool and Grookey, with the added flinch chance helping against bulky Pokemon like Mienfoo. Alternatively, Substitute can be used to scout for Terastallizations, switches, and Sucker Punch from Stunky and opposing Alolan Diglett. Alolan Diglett has many viable Tera types available to it: Tera Ground boosts the damage of Earthquake, KOing most neutral targets such as Mienfoo and Foongus after some chip damage, Tera Dark powers up Sucker Punch while giving Alolan Diglett a resistance to opposing Sucker Punch users like the aforementioned Stunky, and Tera Stellar provides a small boost to all of Alolan Diglett's attacks, which can allow it to pick up some surprise KOs.

Alolan Diglett's high Speed and damage output make it a perfect fit on offensive structures. Pivot support is vital for Alolan Diglett to safely get onto the field, which can be provided by U-turn from Mienfoo and Vullaby and Volt Switch from Elekid and Chinchou. Teammates like Vullaby, Stunky, and Tinkatink can remove Eviolite from Pokemon that are usually able to take a hit from Alolan Diglett such as Mienfoo and Mudbray are appreciated.

Choice Scarf.description: Mankey is one of the most powerful Choice Scarf users in Little Cup thanks to its high Speed, which allows it to outpace or tie with the entire unboosted metagame. This allows Mankey to beat other common Choice Scarf users such as Magnemite, Mudbray, and Gothita. U-turn allows it to greatly capitalize on the switches it forces. Earthquake is a powerful coverage move that hits Mareanie, Glimmet, and Voltorb. Assurance is used to deal as much damage as possible to Ghost-types, OHKOing Eviolite variants on the switch if Stealth Rock is up, while Ice Punch OHKOes Toedscool and threatens Flying-types like Wattrel. Stone Edge is an uncommon option to hit Larvesta and Flying-types. Vital Spirit can be helpful on teams lacking a Grass-type, as it provides a switch-in to Toedscool's Spore, while Defiant is very useful in matchups against Pokemon such as Sticky Web Surskit and Parting Shot Shroodle, as the Attack boosts make Mankey nigh unwallable. Tera Fighting allows Mankey to hit as hard as possible with Close Combat in situations where an unboosted hit is insufficient. Some of Mankey's best teammates include Toedscool to switch in on Ghost-types and remove entry hazards, which can hamper Mankey's pivoting abilities, and either Gothita or Diglett, which can remove the bulky Poison-types like Mareanie and Foongus that give Mankey trouble. Mankey also performs well as part of a VoltTurn core with Pokemon like Volt Switch Voltorb and U-turn Zorua.

Hisuian Growlithe serves as a potent wallbreaker with a Choice Scarf. Its ability to spam high-Base Power moves makes it a difficult Pokemon to switch into, often forcing guessing games between Flare Blitz and Head Smash. Psychic Fangs deters more reliable switch-ins to Hisuian Growlithe's STAB moves, hitting Mienfoo and Mareanie. Psychic Fangs also has the additional benefit of breaking screens, something that may hinder Hisuian Growlithe's wallbreaking. The final slot is flexible, with Rock Blast offering a lower-power alternative to Head Smash, with better accuracy and more PP that also beats Terastalized Weak Armor Vullaby. Stealth Rock allows Growlithe to provide role compression to offensive teams through offering entry hazard support, while Sleep Talk lets it sponge Spore from Foongus and still pose a threat. Tera Fire provides a stronger Flare Blitz to power through other bulky checks like Mudbray and the aforementioned Mienfoo.

Much like many other wallbreakers in the tier, Hisuian Growlithe prefers having hazards off the field as much as possible. Defog and Rapid Spin users such as Vullaby and Toedscool enable it to get in frequently, with the former also able to provide pivoting support and the latter providing Spore support. Mienfoo is another good teammate, as it can tank opposing Hisuian Growlithe's attacks and pivot your own in. Partners like Gothita also provide offensive synergy, being able to pressure checks such as Mareanie and Glimmet.

Eviolite.description:
Eviolite Hisuian Growlithe is an amazing wallbreaker that trades the immediate speed of Choice Scarf sets for more utility options and the ability to switch moves, boasting powerful attacks that can 2HKO almost any foe without the drawback of recoil. Stealth Rock helps rack up passive damage on opposing Pokemon, while Flame Charge is sometimes chosen for a more offensive approach to make up for Hisuian Growlithe's middling Speed. Will-O-Wisp helps punish common switch-ins like Mienfoo and Mudbray, while Substitute is a safe way to scout for switches and catch Sucker Punch from opposing Pawniard and Stunky. Tera Fire boosts Flare Blitz's damage, allowing it to 2HKO offensive Mudbray, and removes Hisuian Growlithe's weakness to Fighting, while Tera Flying turns Hisuian Growlithe's weaknesses to Ground and Fighting into resistances.

Hisuian Growlithe enjoys VoltTurn support from teammates such as Mienfoo and Hisuian Voltorb, which in turn enjoy Hisuian Growlithe's ability to nuke Pokemon like Foongus and Pawniard. Landing a Will-O-Wisp on prominent physical attackers like Mienfoo and Mudbray is greatly appreciated by setup sweepers such as Shellder, which appreciate not taking as much damage on setup turns. Hisuian Growlithe struggles with Pokemon that can resist its STAB moves and KO it back such as Mienfoo and Glimmet, so it pairs well with trappers like Gothita and Trapinch that can remove them.

Curse.description:
Arcanine is one of PU's strongest and most threatening sweepers and cleaners thanks to its great natural bulk, decent defensive typing, great ability in Intimidate, and Curse + Extreme Speed naturally synergizing together. Curse boosts Arcanine's physical stats, making it a stronger threat and a bulkier attacker while also naturally synergizing with Extreme Speed and Intimidate. Morning Sun provides recovery, allowing Arcanine to alleviate its Stealth Rock weakness and recover against more passive walls like Altaria and Wo-Chien. An alternative to Morning Sun is Close Combat, which prevents Arcanine from being walled by Coalossal and does more damage to Water-types than Extreme Speed before Terastallization; however, it severely cuts into Arcanine's longevity. Leftovers aids with Flare Blitz recoil, although it does leave Arcanine extremely weak to entry hazards. Heavy-Duty Boots is another viable option to make it completely immune to Stealth Rock and other entry hazards, although it does come at the cost of Arcanine solely relying on Morning Sun to recover off damage. The given EV spread allows Arcanine to outspeed Modest Toxtricity before a Curse. Tera Normal removes all of Arcanine's weaknesses, allowing it to set up on Pokemon like Decidueye and non-Clear Smog Gastrodon while also boosting Extreme Speed, enabling it to pick off faster attackers like Kilowattrel and Staraptor after a Curse.

Arcanine fits on a variety of teams but most commonly finds itself on hyper offense and balance teams looking for a powerful sweeper and setup threat. Arcanine struggles to deal with bulky physically defensive walls that can cripple it with status or phaze it like Bellibolt, Mudsdale, and Galarian Slowbro, so checks to these Pokemon like Golurk and Tatsugiri make excellent partners. Other physical attackers like Decidueye and Flamigo also make great partners, as they work together with Arcanine to chip away at their shared checks like Bellibolt and Houndstone. If Arcanine is using Leftovers as its item, entry hazard control from Pokemon like Tastugiri, Scyther, and Altaria can help alleviate Arcanine's Stealth Rock weakness to make it a more potent sweeper. As Arcanine struggles to set up against special attackers like Toxtricity and Scream Tail, special walls like Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro and Milotic can provide a defensive backbone for Arcanine to fall back on.

Defensive Utility.description:
• A unique combination of Intimidate, Extreme Speed and multiple support tools make Arcanine a versatile and unpredictable defensive option.

  • Extreme Speed: Even on a defensive set, Extreme Speed's strong base power and priority combined with Arcanine's naturally high Attack make it a potent cleaning tool.

  • Roar: Roar lets Arcanine phaze out troublesome set-up foes that are hard for teammates to switch into, such as Wo-Chien and Garganacl.

  • Bulldoze: Bulldoze's speed control can be used to set up your own offense for a countersweep.

  • EV Spread: After Intimidate, the given EV spread lets Arcanine avoid a 2HKO from Choice Band Chien-Pao's Crunch and Baxcalibur's Earthquake. The HP investment minimizes Stealth Rock damage when not running Heavy-Duty Boots, and the Speed investment outspeeds Adamant Breloom.

Other Options
  • Snarl: This move lets Arcanine pester special attackers that switch into it, potentially letting it stay in longer or ease a switch to a teammate.
Items

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: As a defensive switch-in with a Stealth Rock weakness, Arcanine heavily favors Heavy-Duty Boots to remove said weakness.

  • Rocky Helmet: Against targets like Chien-Pao, Arcanine can rack up passive chip damage.

  • Leftovers: Passive recovery is a valuable asset to have on a defensive Pokemon, but since Arcanine is an Intimidate user that switches a lot, Leftovers doesn't always have enough turns to produce good value.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Terastallization can do a lot to further improve Arcanine's unique set of attributes, but it's not necessarily something that Arcanine needs to function.

  • Normal: Tera Normal gives Arcanine even more cleaning power by boosting Extreme Speed. It's also a nice pinch option for blocking Ghost-type moves, as Flutter Mane and Mimikyu are often forced to use them due to Arcanine's Fairy resistance.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy provides defensive insurance against some of the hardest hitting Choice Band users, such as Tera Dark Chien-Pao and Outrage Dragonite.

Offensive.description:
• The given EV spread minimizes Stealth Rock damage, and the Speed investment lets Arcanine outspeed Adamant Tyranitar by 2 points.

  • This set does not have a full write-up yet. If you'd like to finish this, feel free to reserve it here!

Extreme Speed gets the jump on everything in the tier and backs up Hisuian Arcanine's potent STAB moves by letting it revenge kill frailer offensive Pokemon from high HP like Greninja, Ogerpon, and Latios. Notably, it can even prevent Adamant Lokix from revenge killing Hisuian Arcanine with First Impression. The perfect coverage afforded by these moves lets it fit a utility option into its last moveslot. Hisuian Arcanine is a great Stealth Rock setter thanks to its great matchup against Excadrill and Mandibuzz, the most common entry hazard removers, but it can also use Morning Sun to let its user more recklessly switch it in against foes like Tinkaton and Skarmory. Howl can be used over either choice to boost Hisuian Arcanine's Attack, letting it more easily cleave through offense with a boosted Extreme Speed. A Jolly nature with Tera Normal is chosen to let Hisuian Arcanine get the jump on Excadrill and to give Extreme Speed a much-needed power boost against offensive teams.

Hisuian Arcanine best fits on offense teams and is best supported by offensive teammates that can break through the few things that can take on its STAB attacks. Latios can break through Toxapex, Hippowdon, and Gastrodon, and it can help with some offensive foes that Hisuian Arcanine struggles to revenge kill like Sand Rush Excadrill while also switching into Keldeo for it. Stealth Rock setters like Tinkaton let Hisuian Arcanine more freely run Morning Sun, and in return it relieves some pressure on them to switch into Flying-types like Thundurus-T and Tornadus-T. Tinkaton can also check some foes Hisuian Arcanine struggles with, such as the Normal-resistant faster offensive threat Ogerpon-C. Pivot support from allies like Lokix and Tornadus-T can bring Hisuian Arcanine in on prey like Tinkaton and Heatran. Strong Water-types like Azumarill and Greninja can help Hisuian Arcanine with bulky Ground-types like Hippowdon and Rhyperior that cause it problems.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Hisuian Arcanine looks to outspeed its biggest threats, such as Choice Scarf Volcanion, Spectrier, and Meowscarada, in order to OHKO them on the first turn.
  • Head Smash hits Volcanion, opposing Hisuian Arcanine, and Volcarona, with the Choice Scarf helping against the last one in case of Substitute variants.
  • Raging Fury is preferred over Flare Blitz due to its non-recoil-related drawback, which helps it nicely against Choice Band Hoopa-U. It can also KO fast Weakness Policy Iron Crown, which Choice Band sets cannot do, as Iron Crown's higher Speed allows it to set up Iron Defense.
  • Close Combat is able to OHKO Chien-Pao and Darkrai.
  • Outrage hits Dragon-types such as Dragapult and Haxorus.
  • An Adamant nature allows Hisuian Arcanine to pick up more KOs, such as on fast Weakness Policy Iron Crown; however, a Jolly nature allows it to outspeed more threats, such as Dragapult and Choice Scarf Hoopa-U.
  • Hisuian Arcanine may struggle against Water- and Ground-types like Manaphy, Great Tusk, and Donphan, so teammates like Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W make for good partners.

Choice Band.description:
• Head Smash deals with foes such as non-Choice Scarf Volcanion and Skeledirge while also dealing great damage against neutral foes such as Hoopa-U and Sylveon.
  • Flare Blitz is Hisuian Arcanine's best move against Steel-types like non-Choice Scarf Metagross, Corviknight, and Scizor.
  • Outrage secures the matchup against frailer Dragon-types such as non-defensive Haxorus and non-Haban Berry Raging Bolt while also giving Hisuian Arcanine a better matchup against Roaring Moon.
  • Close Combat beats non-Chople Berry and non-Custap Berry Hisuian Goodra.
  • A Jolly nature gives Hisuian Arcanine a better matchup against Hoopa-U and non-maximum Speed Kyurem. Alternatively, an Adamant nature may be used for a better matchup against Raging Bolt.
  • Hisuian Arcanine struggles against Fighting-type foes such as Urshifu and Great Tusk as well as Water- and Ground-types such as Primarina, Landorus-T, and Ursaluna. It is recommended to use it alongside partners such as Primarina, Zapdos, and Ogerpon-W that can deal with these threats.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Rock

Hisuian Arcanine can use Wild Charge over Close Combat to consistently target Water-types such as Primarina, Toxapex, and Alomomola, preserving Head Smash's PP while also providing a more accurate option. However, Head Smash already hits all of Wild Charge's relevant targets, and Close Combat provides significantly better coverage, as Hisuian Arcanine notably cannot break a healthy Archaludon without it.

Choice Band (Rock).description:
Hisuian Arcanine is a terrifying wallbreaker for Rock teams, capable of threatening Steel- and Grass-types due to its strong STAB moves, supporting ability, great coverage, and Fire typing. Head Smash is an immensely powerful move, enabling Hisuian Arcanine to OHKO Primarina after minor chip damage and Pelipper as well as 2HKO Toxapex, physically defensive Gliscor, and Alomomola. Flare Blitz threatens Amoonguss, Corviknight, and Skarmory while breaking through Steel teams in general with ease in conjunction with Close Combat. Notably, it survives all of Meowscarada's attacks and retaliates via Flare Blitz. Rock Head allows Hisuian Arcanine to freely use Head Smash and Flare Blitz without their recoil damage. Close Combat provides coverage for Archaludon, Hisuian Goodra, and non-Choice Scarf Heatran while also fighting off Dark-types such as Ting-Lu and Hisuian Samurott. Extreme Speed allows Hisuian Arcanine to revenge kill faster foes like Greninja, Azumarill, and Sneasler.

Hisuian Arcanine removes troublesome Steel- and Grass-types like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Amoonguss for its teammates. Garganacl is one of Hisuian Arcanine's best teammates due to its ability to force progress against Water and Steel, notably wearing down Archaludon, Swampert, and non-Choice Band Urshifu-R with Salt Cure. Ogerpon-C heavily aids Hisuian Arcanine in the Water and Ground matchups, threatening foes such as Quagsire, Great Tusk, and Swampert. Iron Boulder is a great teammate in the Fighting matchup, outpacing and removing Iron Valiant, Sneasler, and Okidogi. Iron Boulder appreciates Hisuian Arcanine creating dents in the defensive core of teams, allowing it to clean up late-game. Glimmora forms a potent wallbreaking core with Hisuian Arcanine, taking on Grass and Fairy teams effectively. Furthermore, it provides entry hazard control with Mortal Spin and sets its own array of hazards to wear down Hisuian Arcanine's switch-ins such as Archaludon, Great Tusk, and Garchomp. In return, Glimmora appreciates Hisuian Arcanine removing Steel-types for it so it can freely use Mortal Spin. Tyranitar provides sand to help chip down foes and improve Hisuian Arcanine's special bulk, notably allowing it to survive Power Gem and Shadow Ball from Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Spectrier, respectively. Additionally, Tyranitar sets Stealth Rock; spreads paralysis with Thunder Wave to help Hisuian Arcanine outpace and OHKO faster offensive Pokemon such as Greninja, Spectrier, and Choice Scarf Heatran; and provides Knock Off utility.

Choice Scarf (Rock).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Choice Scarf (Fire).description: This is a sample set as we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Substitute + 3 Attacks (Rock).description:
Hisuian Arcanine makes for a strong offensive threat on Rock teams by virtue of its extremely strong STAB options in Flare Blitz and Head Smash, now freely spammable thanks to its Rock Head ability, which allows it to threaten various Pokemon that Rock teams can struggle with, like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Sinistcha. With Substitute, it takes advantage of passive Pokemon like Amoonguss and Articuno, which can give Hisuian Arcanine the potential to snowball through slower teams. Close Combat is useful coverage that threatens Steel- and Rock-types such as Hisuian Goodra, Heatran, and Tyranitar.

Choice Scarf Kleavor makes for a great teammate, being able to set up entry hazards with Stone Axe, threaten the likes of Ogerpon-H and Dragapult with its STAB and coverage, and pivot Hisuian Arcanine in on walls it struggles with, like Corviknight and Amoonguss, with U-turn. Glimmora can set up a wide array of entry hazards in Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Toxic Spikes while also spreading status and removing hazards with Mortal Spin in case Hisuian Arcanine loses its Heavy-Duty Boots. Ogerpon-C forms a great offensive pairing with Hisuian Arcanine, threatening Water-types such as Swampert and Primarina while appreciating Skarmory, Sinistcha, and Gholdengo being taken out in return. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder provides great speed control, and with its part-Psychic typing it threatens Fighting-types such as Iron Valiant, Sneasler, and Keldeo. Terrakion and Rhyperior make for great partners for Hisuian Arcanine, with Terrakion handling Toxapex and Archaludon while Rhyperior's colorful coverage threatens the likes of Scizor, Dragonite, and Landorus-T. Lastly, Hisuian Arcanine's wallbreaking opens up opportunities for Iron Boulder and Shell Smash Minior to clean late-game.

Choice Band (Fire).description:
Hisuian Arcanine makes a name for itself even among the intense firepower of Fire teams with its Rock Head ability and high base-power STAB moves in Flare Blitz and Head Smash, the former of which can break through even targets that resist it like Garchomp and Rotom-W when sun-boosted. Head Smash aids Hisuian Arcanine in matchups against types that resist Fire such as Water and Dragon, 2HKOing some of their bulkiest walls like Dondozo, Toxapex, and Garchomp. Hisuian Arcanine also nets OHKOs on Dragon threats such as Dragonite, aiding in the type matchup greatly. Extreme Speed allows Hisuian Arcanine to pick off weakened, faster foes like Iron Valiant and Greninja. Close Combat can hit bulky Rock-types such as Garganacl and Tyranitar, as well as Flash Fire Heatran. Wild Charge is used for consistent damage against bulky Water-types, often providing equal or greater damage to Head Smash while also not risking the shaky accuracy.

Sporting a Choice Band leaves Hisuian Arcanine vulnerable to Stealth Rock and Sticky Web so hazard control from the likes of Cinderace and Torkoal is greatly appreciated. Torkoal also sets up sun with its Drought ability, strengthening Hisuian Arcanine and its allies' Fire-type attacks and reducing the threat of incoming Water-type moves. Ninetales is an alternative Drought user with a much higher Speed tier and a pool of utility options like Healing Wish to further support Hisuian Arcanine. Ogerpon-H, Ninetales, and Cinderace can all work in tandem to overwhelm shared checks in bulky Water-types like Toxapex and Rotom-W and other Fire-resistant foes such as Garchomp, Heatran, and Raging Bolt. Ogerpon-H specifically makes use of its Grass-type STAB moves to threaten Water- and Rock-types and Mold Breaker to target Flash Fire Heatran. Volcanion provides a crucial immunity to Water, greatly improving the matchup against Water-types faster than Hisuian Arcanine such as Urshifu-R, Greninja, and Aqua Jet Azumarill. Rotom-H and Talonflame can pivot into Ground-type attacks, the latter of the two also serving as entry hazard control for Hisuian Arcanine and tackling threats like Iron Valiant and Ogerpon-W. Heatran is a crucial answer to Choice Specs Flutter Mane, which otherwise spells doom for any team with Drought granting it a Protosynthesis boost; specially defensive Heatran easily tanks hits from Flutter Mane and OHKO it with Heavy Slam while also setting up Stealth Rock and trapping passive nuisances like Toxapex with its combination of Magma Storm and Earth Power. Ceruledge can pivot into predicted Fighting-type moves for Hisuian Arcanine while also taking advantage of Hisuian Arcanine taking out opposing sweepers like Dragonite and weakened Greninja. Choice Scarf Iron Moth's Speed allows it to take on threats that are faster than and threaten to OHKO Hisuian Arcanine like Hydreigon and Iron Valiant.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Clear Amulet Hisuian Arcanine shines on teams that lean towards offense, featuring Coaching and a reliable form of speed control to make up for its average Speed, while the Mirror Herb set prefers to be on teams that appreciate its ability to remove Kingambit and potentially Annihilape.
  • Dragonite and Sneasler are incredible partners for Hisuian Arcanine, especially Clear Amulet sets. Dragonite supports it with Tailwind while having key resistances to Grass-, Water-, and Fighting-type attacks and an immunity to Ground-type attacks, with Scale Shot to remove Focus Sash Sneasler. Sneasler threatens and removes both Ursaluna formes and Archaludon while providing Coaching boosts for Hisuian Arcanine, which can become incredibly problematic for teams to handle after one or two boosts.
  • Rillaboom also has good synergy with Hisuian Arcanine, being able to super effectively hit the Water- and Ground-types like both Ursaluna formes and Dondozo that give Hisuian Arcanine a hard time. Rillaboom can pin Dondozo, forcing it to either Terastallize into the Grass typing and take good chunks of damage from Flare Blitz or not Terastallize and take massive damage from Rillaboom's attacks. Rillaboom also packs Fake Out support and potentially U-turn to help get Hisuian Arcanine onto the field safely and activate Intimidate. Intimidate can help Rillaboom stick around a lot longer throughout the game, allowing it to survive Ursaluna's Guts-boosted Facade and Baxcalibur's five-hit Icicle Spear.
  • Alolan Ninetales is also a good partner for Hisuian Arcanine, providing speed control via Icy Wind and removing the Ursaluna formes with Blizzard In return, Hisuian Arcanine can threaten huge damage to Alolan Ninetales's checks, such as Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Kingambit.
  • Nasty Plot Gholdengo can be a solid pick to pair with Mirror Herb sets, as it appreciates Hisuian Arcanine's ability to remove its common checks, Kingambit and both Ursaluna formes,with Close Combat, as well as Volcarona and opposing Gholdengo.

Strategy Comments

  • Hisuian Arcanine's main role on teams is to function as a decently fast burst damage attacker while providing some utility with Intimidate. It works best early-game, weakening and removing threats on the opposing side for its other teammates like Gholdengo, Sneasler, and Dragonite to clean up, but can be sent out late-game where the opposing team has been weakened enough for Hisuian Arcanine to pick off foes with Rock Slide or Extreme Speed. Clear Amulet Hisuian Arcanine is a great tool against balance compositions with Incineroar, Rillaboom, and Dragonite, while Mirror Herb Hisuian Arcanine is incredibly useful for teams that have a hard time handling teams that have common setup sweepers.
  • Hisuian Arcanine can apply immediate pressure with Intimidate and its STAB moves for its other teammates, threatening common leads such as Rillaboom, Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Volcarona. It can also sweep with Coaching support from Sneasler, and it appreciates Sneasler and Rillaboom being able to weaken or remove both Ursaluna formes, Basculegion-M, and Archaludon for an easier cleanup or sweep.
  • Water- and Ground-types can give Hisuian Arcanine a hard time due to it not having any way to threaten reliable damage against them, especially both Ursaluna formes. Hisuian Arcanine also doesn't appreciate rain compositions, which weaken its Flare Blitz and always use Basculegion-M to revenge kill it and Archaludon to sponge its attacks. Using Hisuian Arcanine with teammates that help against these problems is recommended; Rillaboom can remove and deter the use of Water- and Ground-types with its STAB moves, while Annihilape and Sneasler can reliably threaten Archaludon.
  • Faster threats like Sneasler, Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, and boosted Dondozo can outspeed and cleanly OHKO Hisuian Arcanine with their STAB moves, while Annihilape and Flamigo have a chance to win the Speed tie and can also OHKO Hisuian Arcanine, so it is worth using Hisuian Arcanine with speed control like Tailwind from Dragonite to outspeed the aforementioned checks and redirection support from Amoonguss or Indeedee-F.
  • Teams that center around Trick Room and feature Psychic-type spam cores and strong Trick Room sweepers like Torkoal and Ursaluna also cause problems, underspeeding Hisuian Arcanine in Trick Room and OHKOing it with their strong attacks. The user can stall Trick Room turns until it expires by positioning Rillaboom for Fake Out and using Hisuian Arcanine's Protect. Both Dragonite and Hisuian Arcanine take Eruption from Torkoal well and can fire back with Scale Shot and Rock Slide, respectively. Rillaboom replaces Indeedee's Psychic Terrain with Grassy Terrain, threatening Grassy Glide on Ursaluna and a weakened Hatterene and also allowing Hisuian Arcanine to use Extreme Speed.

Clear Amulet.description:
• With great Attack and decent Speed, good utility in Intimidate, and a good offensive typing in Fire/Rock, Hisuian Arcanine can be a solid offensive pick for teams, threatening metagame staples such as Rillaboom, Gholdengo, Incineroar, and Dragonite.
  • Flare Blitz is Hisuian Arcanine's best STAB attack, threatening massive damage on Grass- and Steel-types like Amoonguss, Whimsicott, and Kingambit, while Rock Slide provides spread damage, avoids redirection, and hits Incineroar, Volcarona, and Dragonite. Extreme Speed lets Hisuian Arcanine pickoff weakened foes and goes before most forms of priority like Grassy Glide and Sucker Punch, allowing it to finish off Rillaboom and Kingambit. Extreme Speed can also outprioritize and evade redirection from Amoonguss's Rage Powder.
  • Clear Amulet prevents Attack drops from Intimidate and Parting Shot from Incineroar and opposing Hisuian Arcanine, though Incineroar can remove Hisuian Arcanine's Clear Amulet via Knock Off. Clear Amulet also blocks other stat drops such as Speed drops from Alolan Ninetales's Icy Wind.
  • Tera Water grants Hisuian Arcanine Water and Steel resistances against Pelipper, Basculegion-M, and Gholdengoas well as a neutrality to Fighting- and Ground- type attacks like Close Combat, Drain Punch, Earth Power, and Headlong Rush from Sneasler, Annihilape, and both Ursaluna formes. Tera Water does make Hisuian Arcanine weak to Grass-type attacks from Rillaboom and Electro Shot from Archaludon.
  • Tera Ghost grants an immunity to Fighting-type attacks from Sneasler and Annilhilape as well as an immunity to Fake Out from the likes of Incineroar, Rillaboom, and Sneasler. Tera Ghost does make Hisuian Arcanine weak to Gholdengo's Shadow Ball and Annihilape's Rage Fist as well as Dark-type attacks like Knock Off or Kowtow Cleave from Incineroar and Kingambit. Some Sneasler sets also utilize Tera Dark with Throat Chop, hitting Tera Ghost Hisuian Arcanine super effectively.
  • Hisuian Arcanine has advantages over Incineroar, another option for a Fire-type with Intimidate, in its much larger offensive presence, being able to actually threaten an OHKO on Pokemon like Volcarona, and access to strong priority in Extreme Speed.
  • Hisuian Arcanine's exploitable typing and subpar bulk against common checks like Sneasler, Archaludon, and Basculegion means it isn't able to switch around often to take advantage of Intimidate. It also can't damage most of the Water-, Ground-, and Fighting-types that roam the metagame while also Speed tying against Annihilape and being outsped by Sneasler, Garchomp, and boosted Dondozo.

Mirror Herb.description:
• Mirror Herb lets Hisuian Arcanine take advantage of Attack boosts from Swords Dance Kingambit, Swords Dance Sneasler, and Bulk Up Annihilape and remove them with boosted Flare Blitz. It can gain Speed boosts from other setup sweepers like Quiver Dance Volcarona and Scale Shot Dragonite.
  • Close Combat threatens the likes of Kingambit and Incineroar much more effectively and can also deal solid chunks of damage against the Ursaluna formes and Archaludon.
  • Tera Fairy Let Hisuian Arcanine resist Dark- and Fighting-type moves, which can be helpful against Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Sneasler's Close Combat. Tera Fairy also grants an immunity to Dragon-type moves, mainly Dragonite's Scale Shot, and a neutrality to Ground-type moves from the Ursaluna formes. Tera Fairy Hisuian Arcanine needs to be wary of Sneasler's Dire Claw and Gholdengo's Make It Rain.
  • The EV spread has enough investment to let Hisuian Arcanine survive +1 Sucker Punch from Black Glasses Kingambit while still having enough Speed to outspeed maximum Speed Archaludon, Gholdengo, and Basculegion-M. The rest of the EVs are put into Attack.
  • Mirror Herb Hisuian Arcanine can be more flexible and act more recklessly with less worry of Defiant or setup moves while also having a way to damage both Ursaluna formes and Archaludon, which would otherwise more heavily trouble it.
  • This set has a worse matchup against Incineroar with the loss of Clear Amulet, making it more vulnerable to Intimidate and Parting Shot cycling as well as other stat drops. The loss of priority also hurts Hisuian Arcanine's presence on the field, losing the ability to finish off weakened foes.

vgc2024.overview:
• Hisuian Arcanine is a potent offensive Pokemon on many teams thanks to its good Attack, great STAB coverage, and excellent ability in Intimidate, giving it good matchups against Tornadus, Rillaboom, and Chien-Pao.

  • Hisuian Arcanine works best in Tailwind compositions where its average Speed and poor defensive typing don't often hold it back, hence why Tailwind setters like Tornadus make good partners. In return, Hisuian Arcanine can provide Tornadus with Intimidate support, letting it stick around longer and support it with Tailwind or Bleakwind Storm damage.

  • Hisuian Arcanine can be severely overwhelmed by Pokemon like Urshifu-R and Landorus, making Pokemon like Rillaboom and Latias good partners. Hisuian Arcanine also can be hindered heavily by other Intimidate users like Incineroar, meaning it appreciates having Pokemon like Landorus that can threaten it.

Choice Band.description:
• Tera Blast Fairy can hit foes like Urshifu-R, Urshifu, and Raging Bolt, the former of which walls Hisuian Arcanine's STABs. Head Smash can be used to threaten Pokemon like Incineroar and Ogerpon-W with an OHKO at the cost of being chipped down by recoil.

  • Choice Band boosts Hisuian Arcanine's damage, allowing for OHKOs on top threats like Urshifu-R, Kingambit, and Ogerpon-H.

  • The given EV spread lets Hisuian Arcanine take two unboosted Flutter Mane Shadow Balls and almost always survive a Stomping Tantrum from Ogerpon-H. The Speed EVs let it outspeed Regieleki in Tailwind.

  • Tera Fairy lets Hisuian Arcanine remove its weakness to Fighting-type attacks, which can be useful in a pinch against Chien-Pao; this can also let it survive Surging Strikes from Mystic Water Urshifu-R. Tera Normal boosts Extreme Speed's damage, which can be helpful against neutral targets like Urshifu-R.

Altarianite.description: Hisuian Arcanine is one of the tier's strongest Stealth Rock setters and revenge killers, thanks to its access to Pixilate-boosted Extreme Speed, along with Morning Sun for extra longevity. Its typing is equally impressive, allowing Hisuian Arcanine to deal tremendous damage to common Extreme Speed switch-ins like Magearna, Corviknight, and Necrozma-DM with STAB Flare Blitz and check opposing Pixilate Extreme Speed users, such as Regieleki and Dragonite, which lets Hisuian Arcanine further threaten a KO. Pre-Mega Evolution, Hisuian Arcanine has the ability Intimidate, which enables it to weaken physical attackers like Dragonite; however, be wary of Kingambit due to its access to Defiant. Hisuian Arcanine commonly fulfills the role of a Stealth Rock setter, especially because it can threaten common Sablenite users such as Magearna, Mandibuzz, and Corviknight. It can utilize Stone Edge to deal with Ho-Oh and Iron Moth, which would otherwise completely wall it. Double-Edge is an alternative that lets Hisuian Arcanine threaten Garganacl, while in niche cases, Howl can be used instead to transform it into a decent setup sweeper. The Speed EVs allow it to outspeed Adamant Aerodactylite Kingambit. Hisuian Arcanine typically fits on bulky offense teams, serving as a powerful revenge killer and also as a hard counter to opposing Extreme Speed users. Due to its weakness to Stealth Rock, entry hazard removers like Great Tusk and Corviknight make excellent partners. It is also recommended to have a Sablenite user, such as Corviknight, Magearna, or Mandibuzz, as any of them can prevent foes from setting up hazards while facilitating Hisuian Arcanine to safely switch into threats like Urshifu-R, Hisuian Samurott, and Lopunnite Iron Boulder. Corviknight and Mandibuzz are also capable of switching into Ground-types such as Great Tusk, Arceus-Ground, and Hippowdon, which Hisuian Arcanine struggles against. Other Ground-type answers or counters, such as Pinsirite Great Tusk, Ho-Oh, Milotic, and Latiasite users like Magearna and Pecharunt, also exhibit great synergy with Hisuian Arcanine. Raging Bolt is an outstanding partner, as it effortlessly deals with walls like Pecharunt, Milotic, and Arceus-Water, while in return, Hisuian Arcanine switches into and KOes Pixilate Extreme Speed users such as Dragonite and Regieleki. Eternatus serves as one of Hisuian Arcanine's best checks; thus, dedicated checks like Arceus-Ground, Arceus-Poison, Corviknight, and Magearna, especially the Blue Orb versions of the latter two, can be used to counter it. Hisuian Arcanine has notable synergy with Future Sight users such as Iron Crown, Lunala, and Galarian Slowking, as it deals with common Psychic-resistant foes like Magearna, Corviknight, and Mandibuzz, while Future Sight, in return, helps Hisuian Arcanine against walls such as Eternatus and Arceus-Poison.

Magic Guard.description: Hisuian Arcanine is a fearsome wallbreaker, using Magic Guard to eliminate the recoil from Life Orb and its incredibly high-Base Power STAB moves and prevent chip damage from entry hazards. Morning Sun allows Hisuian Arcanine to have defensive utility, being a useful check to Pokemon like Scream Tail and Iron Moth. Extreme Speed offsets Hisuian Arcanine's middling Speed and allows it to pick off chipped foes. Stealth Rock lets it leverage its good offensive typing against common Defog users like Corviknight and Mandibuzz to function as an offensive entry hazard setter, while Will-O-Wisp debilitates switch-ins like Great Tusk, Swampert, and Zamazenta, greatly dampening their damage output. Hisuian Arcanine greatly struggles with being revenge killed by faster threats like Roaring Moon, Chien-Pao, and Zamazenta, so it appreciates defensive teammates like Corviknight and Manaphy. Slow pivots like the aforementioned Corviknight and Manaphy can help give Hisuian Arcanine more opportunities to wallbreak. Hisuian Arcanine can struggle with Well-Baked Body Steel-types like Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Skarmory, so teammates like Sandy Shocks and Zamazenta can help by breaking through them.

Choiced Attacker (Rock).description: Compressing obscene wallbreaking capabilities, cleaning potential, and a partial Fire typing that eases the matchup for its team against Grass- and Steel-types, Hisuian Arcanine is a valuable asset for Rock teams. Flare Blitz OHKOes multiple Steel-types that Rock teams can struggle with, such as Ferrothorn, Gholdengo, and, after Stealth Rock, Corviknight and Skarmory. Head Smash hits even harder and is the main option against neutral targets, notably 2HKOing Gliscor, Celesteela, and Skarmory. Extreme Speed mitigates the lacking Speed tier Hisuian Arcanine has, allowing it to revenge kill foes such as Greninja and Barraskewda. Close Combat OHKOes Heatran after Stealth Rock, Ursaluna after minimal chip, and 2HKOes Archaludon, minimizing would-be checks. Choice Scarf can be an alternative option to outspeed and KO foes such as Mega Lopunny, Mega Aerodactyl, and Zeraora, but the lack of damage output and minimal benefit to Extreme Speed makes it more situational. Ogerpon-C can handle the Ground- and Water-types that can easily pressure Hisuian Arcanine such as Hippowdon, Gastrodon, and Swampert. Entry hazards from Shuckle and Mega Diancie can considerably increase Hisuian Arcanine's offensive pressure, with Shuckle's Sticky Web minimizing the reliance on Extreme Speed to outspeed foes, and Stealth Rock from Shuckle or Spikes from Mega Diancie easing KOs on foes. Mega Diancie and Iron Boulder offensively check Fighting-types that check Hisuian Arcanine such as Great Tusk, Iron Hands, and Kommo-o.

Non-Choice Item Attacker (Rock).description: With Heavy-Duty Boots, Hisuian Arcanine can repeatedly switch in and out to force out threats like Mega Scizor, Celesteela, and Gholdengo for Rock teams. Flare Blitz and Head Smash take full advantage of Hisuian Arcanine's solid Attack and Rock Head, allowing it to hit almost everything relentlessly. Morning Sun gives Hisuian Arcanine even more staying power. Substitute capitalizes on its ability to force out Steel- and Flying-types like Ferrothorn and Corviknight. Extreme Speed picks off weakened threats like Mega Lopunny and Sneasler. 28 Defense EVs let Hisuian Arcanine survive a +2 Bullet Punch from Mega Scizor, allowing Hisuian Arcanine to OHKO it back with Flare Blitz. As Hisuian Arcanine is not strong enough to break through dedicated physical walls like Porygon2, Toxapex, and Archaludon, setup sweepers like Swords Dance Iron Boulder and Ogerpon-C that deal with these are greatly appreciated. Ogerpon-C also additionally deals with Water- and Ground-type walls like Hippowdon and Quagsire, which scoff at Hisuian Arcanine's attempts to wallbreak. Mega Diancie and Mega Aerodactyl deal with Fighting-types like Great Tusk and Kommo-o that check Hisuian Arcanine, and in return, they benefit from Hisuian Arcanine weakening or removing Steel-types like Mega Scizor and Skarmory, allowing Mega Diancie and Mega Aerodactyl to heavily pressure teams like Bug, Flying, and Steel late-game. Entry hazard support in Shuckle, particularly Sticky Web, lets Hisuian Arcanine deal with Choice Scarf threats like Excadrill and Gholdengo, and faster Pokemon like Choice Specs Greninja. Special attackers like Shell Smash Omastar and Nihilego deal with annoying walls like Archaludon and Toxapex, respectively, and both benefit from Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor getting obliterated by Hisuian Arcanine.

Bulk Up.description: 96 Spe allows Poliwrath to outspeeds uninvested Milotic, Jolly Rhydon, and 252 Spe Hariyama.

Nasty Plot.description: Alakazam is a powerful offensive threat thanks to Nasty Plot, its high Speed, and its ability allowing it to ignore entry hazards and other forms of passive damage to keep its Focus Sash intact. These assets make it a great revenge killer or wallbreaker for offensive teams. It is able to outspeed and KO top-tier threats like non-Choice Scarf Mienshao and Iron Moth or break sturdy defensive cores with Garganacl, Skarmory, and Mega Venusaur. Focus Blast is used to hit Dark- and Steel-types like Tyranitar, Excadrill, and Celesteela. Shadow Ball hits Mega Latias, Aegislash, and Slowking. Recover allows Alakazam to set up in front of weaker attacks or passive Pokemon, such as Chansey. Encore locks Pokemon like Mega Latias, Clefable, and Excadrill into unfavorable moves, and Alakazam can use these free turns to set up. Counter is a niche option to KO Iron Boulder and Zeraora and should only be used with Focus Sash for its surprise factor, but it's way less useful than Alakazam's other moves in most matchups. Alakazam's choice of item depends on what your team needs the most; Focus Sash allows it to revenge kill fast Pokemon like Speed Booster Energy Iron Moth and Bisharp, while Life Orb or Fightinium Z allows it to pressure defensive staples like Clefable and Celesteela with much more consistency. When not running Focus Sash, 28 Defense EVs should be used to avoid an OHKO from Hippowdon's Earthquake. Alakazam fits best on offensive teams that enjoy a fast revenge killer against Iron Moth and Mienshao. Entry hazard support from Excadrill and Iron Moth is effective at wearing down most of Alakazam's answers; Toxic Spikes from Iron Moth can put Hippowdon and Chansey on a timer, while Spikes can weaken Aegislash and force Scizor to use Roost more often. Magnezone can trap Celesteela and Scizor; in return, Alakazam threatens Mienshao and Buzzwole. Knock Off from Scizor or Clefable can remove Leftovers from Celesteela and Aegislash, and both appreciate Alakazam revenge killing Iron Moth for them.

Focus Sash.description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Choice Specs.description: Mega Alakazam is a powerful special wallbreaker and revenge killer by virtue of its nearly unparalleled Speed tier and sky-high Special Attack. Moongeist Beam provides coverage against opposing Psychic-types and Imposter users, and it also bypasses Ice Scales. Fleur Cannon OHKOes Yveltal and Dragon-types such as Mega Garchomp and Miraidon. Armor Cannon is the best coverage option against Steel-types like Mega Steelix and Registeel. Beads of Ruin provides a general power boost to all moves, but Psychic Surge allows Mega Alakazam to use Expanding Force, which is more spammable than Psycho Boost, and Psystrike, which crushes Blissey and RegenVest users like Primal Kyogre. Mega Alakazam appreciates support from Imposter users and Knock Off users to remove Assault Vest from RegenVest Pokemon that could otherwise wall what move it locks into and Leftovers from Blissey to make it easier to wear down. Entry hazard support from RegenVest users with Stone Axe and Spikes users such as Eternatus can help Mega Alakazam achieve 2HKOes on targets like Ice Scales Arceus formes. RegenVest users like Primal Kyogre can additionally provide slow pivoting to bring Mega Alakazam in safely, as it is frail and susceptible to status conditions; these can also Imposter-proof Mega Alakazam if it isn't using Psystrike. Other Imposter-proofing options include Imposter Chansey and Ice Scales walls neutral to its attacks like Ho-Oh.

Defensive Pivot.description: Tentacruel is outclassed by Brambleghast, Scyther, and Altaria as entry hazard removal that double up as a Fighting-type check.

monotype.overview:
Poison

Tentacruel is a surprising option on Poison teams, as Toxapex's incredible bulk and longevity completely outclass it as a defensive wall in a majority of situations. However, Tentacruel has enough unique tools such that it could be worth considering over Toxapex should a more proactive Water-type threat be needed.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Knock Off synergizes well with Tentacruel's entry hazard-stacking, as it removes Heavy-Duty Boots from users such as Dragapult and Brambleghast. However, some of Tentacruel's teammates like Hisuian Samurott commonly run Knock Off as well. Protect allows Tentacruel to scout moves from Choice-locked Pokemon like Greninja, Meowscarada, and Gholdengo, but this comes at the cost of sacrificing some of Tentacruel's valuable role compression. Haze allows Tentacruel to better deal with Primarina and Sinistcha, but the limited amount of specific foes Haze targets is small enough that it isn't worth running over its main moves.

Poison

Ice Beam can be used over Knock Off and Protect to give Tentacruel more offensive pressure, allowing it to check threats like Adamant Dragonite after chip damage and Gliscor. Toxic can be used with Tentacruel's Speed to spread poison before going down.

Real Squid [Rapid Spin] (Poison).description:
Tentacruel finds a niche on Poison teams thanks to a flurry of unique traits over its competition in Toxapex such as a vastly superior Speed stat and tools such as Rapid Spin, which makes Tentacruel the only form of entry hazard removal on Poison teams not weak to Steel-type attacks, allowing it to comfortably spin against foes such as Corviknight and Empoleon. Flip Turn allows Tentacruel to easily pivot out on foes such as Hisuian Samurott, Terapagos, and Gliscor. Knock Off is used in the final slot as a solid progress-making option, removing items from foes such as Skarmory and Gholdengo. However, Protect can be used to gain Black Sludge recovery and scout moves from foes. The defensive EVs for each spread provide different defensive benefits; the physically defensive spread with a Timid nature allows Tentacruel to survive an Earthquake from Gliscor and Dragonite, while the specially defensive spread with a Calm nature allows it to beat offensive Heatran and Iron Moth with Surf along with being able to reliably use Knock Off against Flutter Mane. The Speed EVs for both spreads allow Tentacruel to outspeed fully invested Pokemon with base 85 Speed such as Ceruledge, Terapagos, and Kleavor, allowing Tentacruel to reliably pivot out against them or threaten them with Surf and Knock Off.

Amoonguss serves as a solid defensive complement to Tentacruel, being able to handle Ground- and Electric-types such as Great Tusk, Sandy Shocks, and Rotom-W along with putting foes to sleep with Spore, allowing Tentacruel to come in safely and use Rapid Spin. Pecharunt provides solid defensive support by taking on powerful physical attackers like Azumarill, Galarian Zapdos, and Hisuain Arcanine. Overqwil enjoys Tentacruel's entry hazard removal not taking away Overqwil's hazards, and it supports Tentacruel by taking on threats such as Iron Boulder and Gallade. Alolan Muk handles special attackers such as Mew, Flutter Mane, and Terapagos. Galarian Slowking can handle high-power special threats such as Zapdos, Latios, and Choice Specs Iron Moth. Iron Moth appreciates Tentacruel removing entry hazards and pivoting it in with Flip Turn; in response, it can handle threats such as Alolan Ninetales, Gholdengo, and Articuno. Galarian Weezing appreciates Tentacruel's Rapid Spin allowing it to drop Defog, and in return, it provides a proper Ground immunity with Levitate and can take on threats such as Garchomp, Dragonite, and Iron Hands with Will-O-Wisp and Strange Steam. Okidogi and Sneasler can threaten Steel- and Dark-types like Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, Hisuian Samurott, and Hydreigon; Sneasler can pivot Tentacruel in safely via U-turn along with handling targets like Hoopa-U and Ogerpon-H, while Okidogi can use Bulk Up and beat threats such as Archaludon and Cloyster.

Rapid Spin (Water).description:
Tentacruel is one of Water's best forms of role compression, removing entry hazards thanks to its access to Rapid Spin, absorbing Toxic Spikes placed by Toxapex and indirectly by Glimmora with its Poison typing, and slow pivoting with Flip Turn. Aside from this, its great ability in Liquid Ooze allows it to punish the Ogerpon formes and Sinistcha, which target it with Horn Leech and Matcha Gotcha. Furthermore, its part-Poison typing gives Water teams an option against Grass- and Fairy-types such as Breloom and Azumarill. Toxic Spikes aids its more offensive-based teammates by afflicting status on incoming foes, and due to Tentacruel's great defensive typing, it finds many opportunities to set one layer of Toxic Spikes. Flip Turn allows it to serve as a great pivot, as with its rather low Speed, it is able to almost always get a teammate in safely. A Calm nature along with 240 Special Defense EVs allows it to survive 2 Earth Powers from Choice Scarf Enamorus and 2 Fickle Beams from Nasty Plot-boosted Hydrapple. Alternatively, a Bold nature along with 240 Defense EVs allows it to survive a Swords Dance-boosted Horn Leech from the Ogerpon formes and KO back, as well as 2 Flower Tricks from Meowscarada. 16 Speed EVs allow it to outspeed Adamant Breloom, effectively checking it.

Hisuian Samurott forms an entry hazard-stacking core with Tentacruel, placing Spikes with Ceaseless Edge while bypassing Taunt and threatening Dark- and Psychic-types that threaten Tentacruel such as Bisharp and Latios. In return, Tentacruel handles Fairy-types for Hisuian Samurott. Poison-types such as Sneasler, Pecharunt, and Toxapex can come in to absorb Tentacruel's Toxic Spikes. Hence, Greninja makes for a great teammate, checking those Poison-types while also threatening bulky Ground-types such as Great Tusk and Clodsire. When Tentacruel is running a physically defensive EV spread, it forms a great defensive pairing with specially bulky Pokemon such as Swampert and Primarina. Swampert provides an Electric immunity, Stealth Rock support, and pivoting via Flip Turn, while Primarina takes on Dragon-types such as Latios, Latias, and Roaring Moon. Alomomola forms a defensive core with Tentacruel, as well as providing Tentacruel recovery via Wish. Tentacruel's ability to spread status and slow pivot is appreciated by late-game sweepers such as Ogerpon-W, Keldeo, and Urshifu-R. Ogerpon-W takes on Landorus, while Keldeo and Urshifu-R break through Steel-types like Archaludon, Hisuian Goodra, and Empoleon. Rotom-W can switch in against Ground-types thanks to Levitate, and it also threatens common hazard removers like Corviknight and Great Tusk with its STAB moves.

Choice Band (Rock).description:
Choice Band lets Alolan Golem OHKO Bisharp with Brick Break.

This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

ru.overview: Thanks to its typing, high HP and Defense, and access to Regenerator, Slowbro does a fantastic job at slowing down or outright stopping some of the most dangerous wallbreakers and setup sweepers of the tier in their tracks, including the likes of Entei, Krookodile, Terrakion, and Barraskewda. In addition to being one of the best damage sponges in the tier, Slowbro also has a vast arsenal of offensive and disruption tools, including Scald, Psychic Noise, Thunder Wave, and Future Sight. These attributes allow Slowbro to trade hits remarkably well against many defensive pieces of the tier, like Jirachi, Cyclizar, and Registeel. This resilience allows Slowbro to use Calm Mind in order to turn into one of the deadliest late-game sweepers the tier has to offer, ending games after it wins the war of attrition against opposing tanks. Despite all these attributes, Slowbro is not unstoppable in what it's set out to accomplish. Its typing and lower Special Defense leaves Slowbro vulnerable to the many Ghost- and Electric-type attackers roaming the tier, such as Gengar, Basculegion-F, and Magnezone. The strongest wallbreakers in the tier, such as Choice Band Krookodile and Crawdaunt, can overpower Slowbro after minimal chip damage. Slowbro also struggles against wallbreakers with super effective STAB attacks, such as Crawdaunt, Bisharp, and Mimikyu, without expending Tera. Because the Pokemon that Slowbro checks often carry Knock Off, it often finds itself losing its item quite early, leaving it vulnerable to passive damage from hazards and status, particularly Toxic, without Heavy-Duty Boots or Leftovers to mitigate it.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Covert Cloak protects Slowbro from Psychic Noise's heal-blocking effect from Reuniclus and opposing Slowbro and status from Scald from Suicune. Colbur Berry reduces damage taken from Knock Off, making it safer to switch into threats such as Krookodile and Bisharp. Body Press can be used to immediately threaten Bisharp and Cyclizar. Iron Defense makes Slowbro much safer against the likes of Bisharp and Mimikyu and is extremely effective against teams with little pressure on the special side when paired with Body Press. Trick + Choice Scarf cripples defensive Pokemon such as Wo-Chien, Empoleon, and Chansey that would otherwise answer Slowbro's other sets while allowing it to steal the foe's Heavy-Duty Boots or Leftovers after Slowbro absorbs Knock Off for its team. Choosing Psyshock over Psychic Noise allows Slowbro to beat opposing Calm Mind users not running Psyshock themselves.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Ghost- and Electric-type attackers such as Gengar, Basculegion-F, and Magnezone threaten huge damage on Slowbro, even after a Calm Mind boost. Other strong special attackers, such as Gardevoir and Choice Specs Hisuian Goodra, can also overpower Slowbro.

Powerful Physical Wallbreakers: Slowbro is unable to switch into the tier's strongest Choice Band wallbreakers, such as Kleavor, Crawdaunt, and Golurk, without risking getting KOed after minimal chip damage.

Poison: Toxic poison is a death sentence for Slowbro, as it is then unable to stay on the field to threaten the attackers it tries to repeatedly stop over the course of a game such as Choice Scarf Flamigo and completely invalidates late-game Calm Mind tactics. This often forces Slowbro to expend Tera to accomplish its goal against teams running Toxic Spikes or the likes of Toxic Amoonguss, Gligar, and Umbreon.

Bulky Water- and Grass-types: Wo-Chien completely stops Slowbro from making progress and almost always wins in one-on-one situations thanks to its typing, bulk, Leech Seed, and Ruination. Other defensive picks such as Grass Knot Empoleon and Shadow Ball Suicune can slow down Slowbro, but they have to be careful against Calm Mind Slowbro.

Spikes: Because Slowbro will often lose its Heavy-Duty Boots early in the game, Spikes stacking teams can force Slowbro to use Slack Off often, making it much more passive and vulnerable against the Pokemon it wants to check. This can drain Slack Off's 8 PP quickly.

Disruption: Usual stallbreaking tools such as Taunt, Encore, and Trick + Choice Scarf slow Slowbro down considerably. Encore from the likes of Jirachi and Politoed and Trick + Choice Scarf from Gardevoir and Jirachi, entirely prevent late-game Calm Mind tactics from working.

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Slowbro makes for one of the best physical walls and late-game cleaners in the metagame. It acts as an excellent check to a wide variety of Pokemon such as Terrakion, Barraskewda, and Jirachi. Calm Mind allows Slowbro to turn into a threatening late-game cleaner capable of ending games easily. Scald can punish switch-ins to special sponges like Assault Vest Cyclizar and Hisuian Goodra and Dark-type physical attackers like Bisharp and Crawdaunt. Psychic Noise is preferred over Psychic and Psyshock to stop bulky and setup Pokemon from recovering, making matchups against Noivern, Reuniclus, and Suicune more favorable. Slack Off and Regenerator give Slowbro incredible longevity and the ability to consistently set up with Calm Mind during the course of the game. Heavy-Duty Boots is an excellent item that allows Slowbro to make full use of its ability in Regenerator to stay healthy throughout the game. Rocky Helmet is also useful, as Slowbro switches into the many Close Combats, Iron Heads, Liquidations while also checking Maushold and dealing damage passively. Tera Poison makes Slowbro immune to Toxic from the likes of Umbreon, Amoonguss, and Quagsire; keeps its invaluable Fighting resistance while granting it a Fairy resistance and removes its Grass- and Bug-type weaknesses to consistently check Flamigo, Breloom, and others. Tera Fairy rids Slowbro of its Ghost-, Bug-, and Dark-type weaknesses.

Calm Mind Slowbro fits best on balance and bulky offense teams, as they enjoy its ability to check the many physical attackers running around the tier. Cyclizar makes for a great partner because it resists Electric- and Grass-type attacks and is immune to Ghost-type attacks, while Slowbro resists Fighting-type attacks and other strong physical attacks for Cyclizar and its teammates. Cyclizar also acts as a sponge for the many special attacks aimed at Slowbro and as entry hazard control. Amoonguss pairs well with Slowbro because it forms a Regenerator core alongside Slowbro while preventing it from getting poisoned from the likes of Quagsire and Umbreon. Amoonguss also eases the pressure off of Slowbro by helping in answering the plentiful physical attackers in the tier. Krookodile is a good partner for Slowbro, as it enjoys Slowbro's ability to check Fighting- and Water-types like Terrakion and Barraskewda, while Slowbro appreciates Krookodile's ability to set Stealth Rocks, remove items with Knock Off and take care of the Steel- and Ghost-types like Hisuian Goodra and Gengar that threaten Slowbro. Jirachi is an excellent teammate because it spreads status and throttles setup sweepers with Encore.

Future Sight.description:
Slowbro is among the best physically defensive walls in the tier with great bulk, multiple forms of recovery, and the ability to use Terastallization very efficiently against a good portion of the metagame. Scald allows Slowbro to punish switch-ins to Dark-types that come in to stop Future Sight, such as Bisharp and Overqwil while also threatening to burn specially defensive walls like Assault Vest Cyclizar and Empoleon. Future Sight has great damage output and enables Slowbro's teammates to force uncomfortable matchups during a game. Thunder Wave, similarly to Future Sight, can enable teammates to apply offensive pressure through forcing switches. Slack Off, combined with Regenerator, makes Slowbro very difficult to take down. A maximum HP and Defense Slowbro with Bold nature has seemingly unbreakable bulk on the physical side, comfortably switching into some of the premier physical threats like Barraskewda, Terrakion, and Entei. Tera Fairy is used to flip the weaknesses to Bug- and Dark-type, maintain the important Fighting-type resistance, and is generally a good Tera type defensively. Tera Poison keeps the Fighting-type resistance and can prevent Slowbro from becoming poisoned, usually the best means of taking it down, although it does make the matchup into Psychic-types like Reuniclus and opposing Slowbro more difficult.

Future Sight Slowbro provides incredible offensive and defensive synergy within many team structures and is especially good on balance or bulky offense teams. Slowbro is pairs well with other Regenerator users such as Amoonguss, Cyclizar, and Reuniclus to form cores that are very difficult to break and can wear teams down offensively through hazard damage and gradual chip from U-turn and Future Sight. Slowbro can support teams through paralysis spam with other teammates like Bellibolt and Jirachi, enabling offensive options like Basculegion-F and Gengar to take advantage of the boosted Hex damage or slow wallbreakers like Golurk and Crawdaunt to outspeed most of the metagame. Slowbro generally likes to be paired with teammates that can absorb special attacks and are immune to Poison, such as Registeel and Jirachi. To maximize the use of Future Sight, you often want to run physical attacking Fighting-types like Flamigo and Terrakion since Future Sight will lure in specially defensive walls such as Assault Vest Cyclizar and Empoleon as well as Dark-types like Bisharp and Alolan Muk.
