Defensive Pivot.description: Slowbro's high physical bulk combined with Regenerator makes it a fantastic defensive pivot, able to check numerous physical attackers such as Victini and Excadrill. As they're forced out, Slowbro can use Teleport to maintain momentum and stay healthy. Scald serves as a spammable STAB attack that can cripple targets with burns, dissuading otherwise decent checks like Tyranitar. Even foes that don't rely on physical attacks, like Hydreigon, tend to dislike the chip from burn. Future Sight supports wallbreakers like Choice Band Tyranitar, Buzzwole, and Enamorus in breaking through their checks such as Tangrowth and Skarmory for the former two and Mega Venusaur for the latter. It also synergizes excellently with Teleport. Slack Off serves as reliable recovery that doesn't require Slowbro to switch out. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Slowbro to avoid taking damage from entry hazards, maximizing HP regained from Regenerator, though Rocky Helmet can be held instead to punish contact move users, notably foes that run U-turn like Victini. A Relaxed nature and 0 Speed IVs are used to make Slowbro as slow as possible, maximizing its odds of moving slower than opposing Teleport users. Slowbro best fits on bulky offense and balance teams looking for a reliable defensive pivot that can also generate momentum for wallbreakers. Hazard-stacking teammates like Skarmory, defensive Clefable, and Hippowdon pair up nicely with Future Sight, further putting pressure on opposing defensive cores. Many hazard-stacking teammates can also double as checks to Pokemon Slowbro struggles against, such as Clefable and Celesteela checking Dark-types like Hydreigon, Skarmory handling Bug- and Grass-types like Buzzwole and Rillaboom, and Hippowdon checking Electric-types like Zeraora. Similarly, pivots like Scizor also check threats like Clefable while pairing nicely with Slowbro's own pivoting potential to maintain offensive momentum. If it isn't running Heavy-Duty Boots, hazard control from teammates like Hydreigon, Excadrill, and Flygon is necessary.

Calm Mind.description: Mega Slowbro's increased physical bulk, reliable defensive typing, and access to Regenerator prior to Mega Evolving form a threatening setup sweeper with Calm Mind with the ability to easily cripple and outlast potential checks such as Assault Vest Tangrowth and Aegislash. However, Mega Slowbro struggles to justify a place over its regular forme because it becomes especially vulnerable to all forms of status and entry hazards given the inability to hold an item. Additionally, the opportunity cost of not being able to use items results in Mega Slowbro competing with other Mega Evolutions such as Latias and Venusaur, which offer more distinctive defensive features in comparison. Scald ensures Mega Slowbro is able to threaten physical attackers such as Iron Boulder and Excadrill and potentially cripple the likes of Scizor and Azumarill with its burn chance. Psychic is preferred to deal as much damage as possible to certain physically defensive Pokemon, such as Rotom-W, Hydrapple, Amoonguss, and Mega Venusaur, but Psyshock allows Mega Slowbro to match up better against Calm Mind sweepers such as Mega Latias and Reuniclus as well as certain specially defensive Pokemon such as Blissey and Assault Vest Primarina. Slack Off gives Slowbro a complementary recovery option that allows it to instantly heal off damage from the likes of Celesteela, Hippowdon, and Enamorus, which it often finds itself pivoting into; it benefits Mega Slowbro in particular, which forgoes Regenerator. The given EV spread ensures Mega Slowbro isn't 2HKOed by unboosted attacks such as Iron Moth's Sludge Wave and Enamorus's Moonblast from full health, allowing it to find opportunities against them. Mega Slowbro fits best on balance and stall teams, where it's able to complement its team's defensive security against threats such as Mega Gallade and Excadrill and find adequate opportunities to safely set up. Hazard support from defensive staples such as Hippowdon, Skarmory, and Blissey is vital to Mega Slowbro's gameplan, weakening offensive Pokemon such as Tyranitar and Aegislash dilutes their ability to deal with it in the long run. Additionally, Mega Slowbro also complements these Pokemon in return by providing a sturdy defensive check to some of the physical attackers that may overwhelm them, such as Victini and Mienshao. Mega Slowbro also dislikes having to contend with the opposing presence of various special threats; notably Alakazam, Hydrapple, and Hydreigon, which are capable of setting up and overwhelming it by targeting its lower Special Defense. Other examples that pair well with Mega Slowbro to check several of these Pokemon include defensive Scizor, Celesteela, and Unaware Clefable. Clefable is notable in particular, as it is also able to further support Mega Slowbro with tools such as Wish and Aromatherapy, keeping it healthy against potential status ailments such as Toxic from Hippowdon and Celesteela. While Mega Slowbro appreciates the increased defenses from Mega Evolving, there are also instances where it would prefer to utilize Regenerator in its base form, which makes hazard removal from Pokemon such as Flygon, Talonflame, and Excadrill crucial to ensure it isn't as vulnerable to certain attacks prior to Mega Evolving, such as Choice Band Tyranitar's Knock Off and Swords Dance Excadrill's boosted Earthquake.

Defensive Pivot (Psychic).description: With formidable physical bulk and longevity with reliable recovery in Slack Off and Regenerator, Slowbro is a wall that provides momentum for Psychic teams. Scald is a STAB option that targets Ground-types such as Great Tusk, Mega Swampert, and Excadrill and discourages several physical attackers such as Meowscarada, Garchomp, and Mega Gallade from directly coming in to avoid a potential burn. Future Sight complements its pivoting with Teleport to make the upcoming ally more difficult to wall; Body Press alternatively minimizes Slowbro's passivity, allowing it to hit Dark-types such as Weavile, Roaring Moon, and Mega Tyranitar, which is further enabled with Colbur Berry. Thunder Wave is an alternative to hinder foes Slowbro lures in such as Sinistcha, Kyurem, and Ogerpon-W. No item held lets Slowbro check Poltergeist users such as Ceruledge and minimizes Knock Off damage. Jirachi can form a good defensive core with Slowbro, with Jirachi acting as a special wall that checks foes that would threaten Slowbro such as Tapu Lele, Mega Diancie, and Alolan Ninetales, while Slowbro checks Fire-types such as Cinderace and Mega Charizard X. Offensive partners such as Mega Gallade, Tapu Lele, and Victini take advantage of Slowbro's utility and pivoting, handling foes for it such as Gholdengo, Mega Sableye, and Iron Hands. Iron Boulder provides speed control to offensively check for Slowbro foes such as Ogerpon-W, Greninja, and Meowscarada.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Slowbro takes advantage of its stellar physical bulk, Regenerator, and Teleport to act as an excellent bulky pivot. Scald is preferred for its good chance to permanently hinder most physical attackers such as Mega Scizor and Landorus-T while also deterring foes like Zapdos and Gholdengo. Body Press can be used while holding a Colbur Berry to survive a hit from Mega Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Hisuian Samurott, allowing Slowbro to retaliate with Body Press. Future Sight is used in combination with Teleport to help offensive teammates such as Mega Lopunny, Urshifu-R, and Zamazenta break Pokemon like Toxapex and Alomomola. Thunder Wave is an alternative to Slack Off that punishes Pokemon such as Volcarona and Ogerpon-W that attempt to set up in front of Slowbro and permanently hinders switch-ins like Tapu Lele and Tornadus-T that Slowbro otherwise struggles against. Heavy-Duty Boots affords Slowbro much more freedom to pivot, while Rocky Helmet punishes weak contact moves, such as Landorus-T's U-turn, and resisted hits from Pokemon such as Urshifu-R and Mega Medicham.

Slowbro fits best on balance and bulky offense teams that feature Pokemon such as Urshifu-R and Zamazenta that benefit from its Future Sight and pivoting capabilities while answering Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott, which Slowbro struggles to beat. Slowbro can also be paired with fellow Regenerator users such as Tornadus-T to form a double Regenerator core, with Tornadus-T answering Grass-type Pokemon such as Kartana and Ogerpon-W. Teammates like Ferrothorn and Gliscor can help against Tapu Koko and Raging Bolt, which Slowbro struggles against. In return, Slowbro deals with Urshifu-R and Mega Medicham. Dark-type Pokemon such as Mega Tyranitar, Kingambit, and Ting-Lu pair well with Slowbro, as they deal with Gholdengo, which easily breaks Slowbro; the former two teammates have the added boon of Pursuit to forcibly remove Gholdengo and help stave off Choice-locked Tapu Lele.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Psychic

Holding no item can be an option, as Slowbro is then able to wall Poltergeist and Knock Off users and has a better time checking them.

Physically Defensive (Psychic).description:
Slowbro is an essential pick for Psychic teams due to its physical bulk, which allows it to tank hits from Excadrill and Meowscarada for the team. Body Press pairs nicely with Slowbro's Defense, dealing with Hisuian Samurott, Bisharp, and Weavile. Scald checks physical threats like Mamoswine and Excadrill while also having a chance to burn them in the process. Thunder Wave allows Slowbro to paralyze fast threats like Meowscarada, Roaring Moon, and Choice Scarf Kleavor that are troublesome to Psychic teams. Thunder Wave also synergizes with Scald, catching switches into potential Scald-resistant foes. Iron Defense can be run over Thunder Wave to help take on physical Dragapult better, but doing so means that Slowbro is unable to spread paralysis to troublesome foes. Colbur Berry is a great item, allowing Slowbro to tank a hit from a Dark-type attack, including +2 Knock Off from Weavile and +2 Ceaseless Edge Hisuian Samurott, and retaliate with Body Press. Eject Button can be used over Colbur Berry to allow Slowbro to act as a pivot for the team. Additionally, after using the Eject Button, Slowbro can take Poltergeist from Ceruledge and Knock Off from Roaring Moon. 248 HP EVs are used to allow Slowbro to get the best use out of Regenerator.

Choice Scarf Iron Boulder is a great teammate for Slowbro, outspeeding and taking out threats like the Ogerpon formes, Greninja, and Meowscarada with Mighty Cleave and Close Combat. Assault Vest Hoopa-U tanks special attacks from troublesome Ghost- and Dark-types like Flutter Mane, Gholdengo, and Greninja and takes them out with Knock Off and Drain Punch. Hatterene eases the matchup against Dark and Dragon teams with Draining Kiss while also preventing entry hazards and status from being set thanks to Magic Bounce. Hatterene can also run Nuzzle to spread paralysis to threats, which can let Slowbro opt for Iron Defense instead of Thunder Wave. Choice Band Metagross deals with Fairy-types like Flutter Mane, Enamorus, and Iron Valiant with Bullet Punch. Metagross also provides entry hazard support via Stealth Rock to break a potential Focus Sash held by Ceruledge. Choice Scarf Latias takes out Choice Specs Dragapult and Choice Specs Hydreigon with Draco Meteor and can also Choice lock walls with Choice Scarf via Trick. Gallade helps Slowbro by handling walls such as Hisuian Goodra, Alolan Muk, and Blissey with Sacred Sword. Indeedee-M provides an immunity to Ghost, an immunity to priority moves via Psychic Surge, and Healing Wish support that gives Slowbro a second chance to wall out physical threats. Indeedee-M also provides utility with Trick, as it can Choice lock walls like Sableye and Ting-Lu by giving them a Choice item. In return, Slowbro deals with Weavile, Bisharp, and Excadrill, which Indeedee-M can't take on by itself. Set-up sweepers like Mew, Deoxys-D, and Latios becomes a threatening wincon for Slowbro's team once Dark-types have been dealt with. Calm Mind Latios is a nice teammate for Slowbro, taking out threats like Landorus, Clodsire, and Ursaluna via Luster Purge and Ice Beam.

Nasty Plot (Psychic).description:
48 Speed EVs may be used if using Psychic to outspeed Toxapex.

This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Physical Wall.description: Mega Slowbro's insanely high Defense and good typing make it an incredibly hard to break Fur Coat wall on balance teams, checking and forcing out common metagame threats like Mega Garchomp and Kyurem-B. Scald threatens to burn setup threats like Ice Scales Arceus-Ground, which could otherwise set up in Mega Slowbro's face, and it also deals solid damage. Future Sight has incredible synergy with Teleport, as it allows Mega Slowbro to support its offensive teammates by preventing opposing walls from safely switching in. Alternatively, Mortal Spin allows Mega Slowbro to serve as an entry hazard remover and cripple foes unaffected by burn, such as Ho-Oh. Covert Cloak prevents Mega Slowbro from being chipped by foes reliant on Salt Cure and Mortal Spin to make progress, while Rocky Helmet consistently chips wallbreakers in exchange for a worse matchup against passive walls like Mega Audino; Rocky Helmet also notably punishes Choice Band foes, such as Kyurem-B, for trying to easily up chip damage with U-turn. The pivoting and Future Sight support Mega Slowbro provides is heavily appreciated by wallbreakers that often fall just shy of 2HKOs, such as Mega Garchomp and Ash-Greninja; teammates with a bad matchup against various physical attackers are also appreciative of its walling capabilities, including the likes of Ice Scales Ho-Oh and Blissey. The aforementioned Blissey and other special walls like Ice Scales Arceus-Ground and Ho-Oh can also cover for dangerous foes like Miraidon and Flutter Mane, forming a solid defensive core. Since Ash-Greninja is one of the only wallbreakers that can dissuade Mega Slowbro from switching in, a check to it like Miraidon or Fur Coat Arceus-Fairy is appreciated. Mega Slowbro should be Imposter-proofed by a Take Heart user, ideally with Thunder Cage, as even if Mega Slowbro is able to burn or poison the Imposter user, it still acts as a free source of healing and Teleport momentum.

ru.overview: Galarian Slowbro is difficult to take down thanks to its great physical bulk, multiple forms of recovery in Regenerator and Slack Off, and solid defensive typing. Calm Mind Galarian Slowbro can snowball quickly, being able to stack up multiple boosts in the face of premier physically offensive threats like Entei, Breloom, and Terrakion while threatening to sweep entire teams. With access to perfectly accurate Toxic, Galarian Slowbro finds plenty of opportunities to disrupt after coming in on physical wallbreakers. However, some physical attackers have the necessary tools to break through it, including staples in the tier like Krookodile and Crawdaunt which can threaten massive damage with strong attacks. Fitting the coverage to hit the plethora of Poison- and Steel-types can also be difficult, so Pokemon like Amoonguss, Hisuian Goodra, and Jirachi can limit Galarian Slowbro's effectiveness as a bulky offensive setup option. Likewise, strong special wallbreakers like Gardevoir and Gengar can threaten to take down Galarian Slowbro before it can establish multiple boosts, forcing it out and deterring setup attempts. Despite access to similar movepools, Slowbro has a tangible upside with moves like Psychic Noise and Scald, and it often fulfills the role of a physical wall and bulky setup sweeper better than Galarian Slowbro can.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Galarian Slowbro has access to Thunder Wave, which can be quite disruptive and can enable slower wallbreakers like Toxtricity and Crawdaunt. Nasty Plot can be used over Calm Mind to expedite the offensive boosting at the cost of being susceptible to special wallbreakers more easily. Belly Drum sets, with Quick Claw and Quick Draw, can be unreliable but incredibly dangerous with access to strong attacks like Drain Punch, Earthquake, and Shell Side Arm. Ice Beam, Shadow Ball, and Surf are other special attacks that can be used for coverage to hit the likes of Slowbro and Krookodile for more damage immediately.

Checks and Counters

Psychic-types: In a metagame with strong Psychic-types like Necrozma, Reuniclus, and Gallade Galarian Slowbro can find itself struggling to capitalize on its physical bulk to set up with Calm Mind reliably. Similarly, Slowbro is among the best Pokemon in the tier and can both compete directly with Galarian Slowbro for a spot on a team while also threatening to win Calm Mind setup battles reliably, especially given its better natural bulk and access to great disruptive attacks like Psychic Noise and Scald.

Special Wallbreakers: Without establishing multiple Calm Mind boosts, Galarian Slowbro is especially vulnerable to the plethora of special wallbreakers in the tier, such as Gengar, Basculegion-F, and Magnezone.

Encore, Taunt, and Trick: Disruptive moves like Encore and Taunt can cause major issues for Galarian Slowbro, as it is incredibly slow and will struggle to set up against the bevy of users like Noivern, Gengar, and Jirachi. Trick can be used by Choice item users, like Gardevoir, Jirachi, and Cresselia, to significantly hinder Galarian Slowbro, as locking into any of its moves can be easy to capitalize on for the opponent.

Pivot Spam: While Galarian Slowbro can absorb many of the attacks from physical wallbreakers like Flamigo and Kleavor, it is susceptible to being used as U-turn fodder for safe entry points for other strong pivot users, like Kilowattrel and Magnezone. Being caught in the blender of pivot spam can quickly wear down Galarian Slowbro and make standing up to the onslaught of physical attacks much more difficult. As it often finds itself switching into Knock Off, Galarian Slowbro is especially vulnerable to chip damage from entry hazards.

Calm Mind.description:
Set Details

Galarian Slowbro is a competent physical wall that can fulfill multiple roles, such as spreading poison, forming Regenerator cores, and being a bulky setup sweeper. In conjunction with its exceptional physical bulk, Calm Mind can make it a herculean task to bring down Galarian Slowbro after a few boosts, and opportunities to set up can be easy to find in a metagame filled with physical wallbreakers that struggle to beat it. Flamethrower is a strong option to hit Steel-types such as Registeel and Jirachi. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Galarian Slowbro to function more capably as a defensive pivot throughout a game, while Covert Cloak can prevent secondary effects like Body Slam paralysis and Psychic Noise recovery-blocking from Jirachi and Slowbro. Regenerator ensures Galarian Slowbro can continue to function as a switch-in to physical attackers multiple times as needed. Tera Water eliminates the weakness to Ground-type attacks and grants a resistance to Fire, creating opportunities to set up against Krookodile and Entei more comfortably. Tera Water also neutralizes the output of strong Ghost- and Psychic-type special attacks, rendering Gengar, Jirachi, and Basculegion-F less capable of beating it after a Calm Mind boost.

A stalwart option for balance and bulky offense teams, Calm Mind Galarian Slowbro is an excellent fit for teams looking to shore up their physical bulk while also hoping to create setup opportunities to clean late-game. Working well in tandem with specially defensive pivots like Assault Vest Cyclizar and Empoleon that can absorb special attacks from threats like Gardevoir and Gengar, Galarian Slowbro can function as a stout physical wall to form resilient defensive cores that wear the opposition down gradually for stronger teammates like Basculegion-F and Gengar to clean up late-game. Cyclizar and Amoonguss are notable teammates that can form Regenerator cores with Galarian Slowbro to maintain health throughout a game, with the former providing Knock Off and U-turn support. Capitalizing on this type of support, Galarian Slowbro teams can keep the pressure on with entry hazard support from the likes of Gastrodon, Krookodile, and Registeel. Covert Cloak sets are weak to hazards, which can offset most of the recovery from Regenerator, so hazard control support from Cyclizar and Noivern is especially beneficial. Offensive options that can capitalize on Galarian Slowbro are fast wallbreakers, such as Entei, Choice Scarf Krookodile, and Bisharp, that can beat the Steel- and Psychic-types that come in on it, like Empoleon, Jirachi, and Magnezone.

Defensive.description:
Defensive Galarian Slowbro fulfills the role of physical wall and disruptor well, capable of absorbing attacks from the wallbreakers like Breloom and Terrakion while disrupting everything else with Toxic. Psyshock is stronger against specially defensive foes like Assault Vest Cyclizar and Hisuian Goodra, offering a means to wear them down faster for its teammates. Psyshock also hits Calm Mind setup sweepers like Suicune and opposing Galarian Slowbro harder than Psychic would. Flamethrower melts Steel-types like Jirachi and Magnezone sufficiently. Toxic is Galarian Slowbro's main form of making progress, as it can help wear down many of its switch-ins like Flygon, Krookodile, and Slowbro. Heavy-Duty Boots helps ensure Galarian Slowbro remains healthy throughout a game to effectively pivot in against physical attackers, while Colbur Berry provides a valuable one-time resistance to Knock Off from strong threats like Crawdaunt and Krookodile. Tera Water removes the weakness to Ground and Ghost, allowing Galarian Slowbro to more effectively check Krookodile and Swords Dance Mimikyu. Tera Ghost can be used to provide a Normal immunity, functioning as a spinblocker against Cyclizar as well as a valuable switch-in to Population Bomb Maushold.

Defensive Galarian Slowbro is a stout choice for balance and bulky offense teams looking for a reliable physical wall and Toxic user. Entry hazard support from the likes of Chesnaught, Gastrodon, and Krookodile can help these teams by forcing chip damage on wallbreakers like Flamigo and Terrakion, both of which struggle to break through Galarian Slowbro reliably. Specially defensive teammates that can tank the Ghost-type attacks from threats like Gengar and Basculegion-F, such as Empoleon, Hisuian Goodra, Umbreon, and Registeel, form excellent defensive cores with Galarian Slowbro that can bulk a majority of attacks seamlessly. Offensive teammates that can capitalize on this gradual chip damage include fast wallbreakers like Choice Scarf users Gardevoir, Gengar, and Krookodile as well as setup Pokemon like Swords Dance Mimikyu. Hazard removal support is vital for Colbur Berry sets, so teammates like Cyclizar and Noivern are valuable to keep Galarian Slowbro healthy enough to reliably check physical wallbreakers multiple times as needed.

Physically Defensive.description:
Galarian Slowbro should run a Relaxed nature when using Shell Side Arm to maximize damage against foes with lower physical bulk like Florges and defensive Bombirdier. Otherwise, a Bold nature is preferred.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

Assault Vest.description:
Flamethrower deals heavy damage to Alolan Sandslash, while Earthquake 2HKOes Skuntank, an otherwise solid switch-in, and still chunks Alolan Sandslash and opposing Galarian Slowbro. With 4 Special Attack EVs and a Relaxed nature, Shell Side Arm will always be a special attack unless the opponent has lower Defense than Special Defense. Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro's EV spread and nature are highly customizable. Running more Special Defense with a Sassy nature can help Galarian Slowbro better withstand boosted attacks from foes like Rotom-Heat and Salazzle. Investing in Special Attack and using a Modest nature is also a viable option to increase Galarian Slowbro's offensive presence.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

Calm Mind.description:
Nasty Plot is an alternative boosting option that makes Galarian Slowbro more immediately threatening, but losing out on Special Defense boosts gives attackers like Delphox an easier time pressuring Galarian Slowbro.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

nu.overview: Galarian Slowbro establishes itself as a solid physical wall in NU thanks to Regenerator, letting it come in and check threats repeatedly without having to waste a turn healing. Its typing allows Galarian Slowbro to be immune to poison, allowing it to avoid Toxic from Overqwil, while letting it consistently check Fighting-types like Mienshao, Toxicroak, and Breloom. Galarian Slowbro's deep utility movepool lets it support its team by whittling away at walls like Incineroar and Diancie with Toxic or slowing down threats like Munkidori and Inteleon with Thunder Wave. It also has access to Calm Mind, which allows Galarian Slowbro to take advantage of common defensive walls like Registeel and Vileplume by making it harder to KO and switch into as well. On the other hand, it can choose to be more immediately threatening with Assault Vest, as it allows Galarian Slowbro to make use of its vast coverage, and it helps act as a blanket check to special wallbreakers such as Munkidori, Dragalge, and Porygon-Z. However, Galarian Slowbro's typing makes it weak to common Ground- and Dark-types like Flygon, Incineroar, and Alolan Muk. Galarian Slowbro is also susceptible to being KOed by repeated special hits from wallbreakers like Inteleon, Toxtricity, and Porygon-Z due to its below-average Special Defense. While Galarian Slowbro checks Fighting-types like Toxicroak and Breloom quite well, other physical wallbreakers with neutral STAB moves like Heracross, Paldean Tauros-W, and Basculegion-M can easily overpower it or force it to Terastallize.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Iron Defense + Body Press can be used to turn the tables against Dark-types like Incineroar, Scrafty, and Alolan Muk, but Galarian Slowbro is still easily forced out by special wallbreakers. Nasty Plot can be used over Calm Mind, turning it into a terrifying sweeper, but unlike Calm Mind, it forces Galarian Slowbro to switch out when it's up against special wallbreakers like Dragalge and Munkidori. Trick Room can be used on Galarian Slowbro to take advantage of its low Speed and decent Special Attack, but without a boost, it struggles to pick up KOs. Colbur Berry lets Galarian Slowbro tank any Dark-type attacks such as Incineroar's and Alolan Muk's Knock Off and Toxicroak's Dark Pulse so that it can respond with an attack afterwards, but the utility of its other items usually outweighs the benefit of using it. Eject Button allows Galarian Slowbro to become a one-time pivot, letting it safely bring in setup sweepers like Swords Dance Incineroar, Dragon Dance Flygon, and Nasty Plot Toxicroak for free. Galarian Slowbro could also opt to go itemless, as it can then wall Brambleghast and reduce Knock Off damage from Incineroar and Mienshao.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Incineroar and Bombirdier can put a lot of pressure on Galarian Slowbro with their STAB attacks, but they have to be worried about getting poisoned by Sludge Bomb when switching in. Alolan Muk is especially noteworthy for being able to switch into its STAB attacks easily without worry of being poisoned, and it can respond with Knock Off.

Ground-types: Flygon, Swampert, and Gligar can tank its Poison-type attacks and threaten Galarian Slowbro with their STAB Earthquake. However, the former two have to fear getting poisoned, and they all have to be cautious about switching into Ice Beam, Grass Knot, or Surf.

Ghost-types: Chandelure, Hisuian Typhlosion, Decidueye, and Brambleghast can easily destroy Galarian Slowbro with their STAB attacks. However, the former two have to fear about switching into Surf, while the latter two have to worry about Sludge Bomb damage and switching into a Flamethrower.

Special Wallbreakers: Special wallbreakers like Choice Specs Meloetta and Inteleon can easily break through Galarian Slowbro and force it to switch out. Calm Mind users like Uxie and Chandelure can put a lot of pressure on Galarian Slowbro too, but they have to be mindful of getting poisoned and switching into Psyshock and Surf, respectively.

Physical Wall.description:
Set Details

Sludge Bomb is Galarian Slowbro's preferred STAB move, as it hits Fairy-types like Sylveon and Florges while also threatening foes like Incineroar, Flygon, and Swampert with poison. However, Psyshock can be used over Sludge Bomb, allowing Galarian Slowbro to deal with Poison-types and special walls like Toxicroak, Tentacruel, and Diancie more easily, and it also helps overwhelm opposing special setup Pokemon like Sylveon and Oricorio-G. Flamethrower allows Galarian Slowbro to hit Steel-types switching in on Sludge Bomb like Copperajah, Registeel, Bronzong, and Tera Steel Sylveon. Alternatively, Surf allows it to target Incineroar trying to blank an incoming Psyshock. Rocky Helmet punishes physical wallbreakers like Mienshao, Cinccino, and Breloom; it also pairs well with Regenerator, as it allows Galarian Slowbro to consistently switch in to rack up chip damage. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Galarian Slowbro avoid damage from entry hazards, meaning its Regenerator can't be negated, while Leftovers gives it passive recovery, minimizing the need to heal off damage with Slack Off. The EV spread lets Galarian Slowbro outpace Bronzong. Tera Water lets it handle Water-, Ground-, and Fire-types like Basculegion, Flygon, and Incineroar; however, Galarian Slowbro loses its matchup against Grass-types like Tsareena and Breloom. Tera Fairy retains the Fighting-type resistance and allows it to resist Dark-type attacks from Incineroar and Bombirdier but makes it weak to foes like Copperajah and Toxicroak.

Galarian Slowbro pairs best with bulky Water-types like Vaporeon, Swampert, and Milotic to handle Ground-types such as Flygon and Swampert; in return, Galarian Slowbro checks Grass-types like Tsareena, Breloom, and Vileplume. Dark-types like Incineroar, Bombirdier, and Scrafty synergize well with Galarian Slowbro by beating Ghost-types like Chandelure and Decidueye; in return, Galarian Slowbro handles Fighting-types like Mienshao, Toxicroak, and Breloom. Galarian Slowbro appreciates Fighting-type teammates like Toxicroak, Breloom, and Paldean Tauros-W, as they can check Dark-types like Incineroar, Bombirdier, and Alolan Muk, which threaten it. Physical wallbreakers like Flygon, Mienshao, and Infernape appreciate Galarian Slowbro's positive matchup against physically defensive walls like Milotic, Vileplume, and Avalugg. Galarian Slowbro can form a defensive backbone with special walls like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Diancie, as they can check special wallbreakers like Choice Specs Meloetta and Toxtricity, while Galarian Slowbro handles the physical wallbreakers like Breloom and Toxicroak.

Assault Vest.description:
Set Details

Shell Side Arm is preferred over Sludge Bomb, as it will do more damage to special walls. However, Sludge Bomb can be used for its higher poison chance. Similarly, Psyshock hits special walls harder, but Psychic can be used for its raw power. Flamethrower allows it to hit Steel-types like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Klefki, while Earthquake targets Alolan Muk and Tentacruel with a trade-off of not hitting Bronzong and Orthworm. Ice Beam lets Galarian Slowbro hit Ground-types like Flygon and Gligar, while Surf targets Fire- and Rock-types like Chandelure, Talonflame, and Diancie. Grass Knot can be used as well to hit Water- and Ground-types like Swampert, Milotic, and Gastrodon more effectively. The given Speed EVs outpace Bronzong, though a spread of 180 HP / 252 SpA / 76 Spe could be run to outspeed Gastrodon if it runs Grass Knot. An alternative bulkier EV spread of 252 HP / 128 Def / 4 SpA / 96 SpD / 28 Spe can be run with a Bold nature to live a +2 Wave Crash from Paldean Tauros-W and ensure that Shell Side Arm is a special attack, but Galarian Slowbro can fail to put its coverage to great use at times if it doesn't invest heavily in its offenses. Tera Water lets Galarian Slowbro handle Fire- and Water-types like Choice Specs Chandelure and Inteleon. However, Tera Fairy retains the Fighting-type resistance while letting it handle Dark-types like Incineroar and Bombirdier.

Bulky Water- and Grass-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Tsareena are great partners for Galarian Slowbro, as they can check Ground-types like Flygon and Swampert. Dark-types like Incineroar, Scrafty, and Wo-Chien appreciate Galarian Slowbro for checking Fighting-types like Mienshao, Toxicroak, and Breloom. In return, they can handle the Ghost-types like Chandelure, Basculegion, and Hisuian Typhlosion. Galarian Slowbro's typing leaves it weak to common Knock Off users like Incineroar and Alolan Muk. Thus, it pairs well with Pokemon like Bellibolt, Swampert, and Toxicroak, as they can check the aforementioned Knock Off users. Defensive walls like Bellibolt, Sylveon, Vaporeon, and Orthworm are great partners for Galarian Slowbro, as they can check physical wallbreakers like Basculegion and Flygon. Physical wallbreakers like Life Orb Mienshao and Choice Band users such as Paldean Tauros-W and Flygon are great partners to form a wallbreaking core with Galarian Slowbro. Special walls like Bronzong, Milotic, and Incineroar can check special wallbreakers like Meloetta, Inteleon, and Chandelure, since Galarian Slowbro can't always beat them.

zu.overview: Magneton secures itself a place in the ZU metagame by virtue of its excellent power, a typing that is useful both offensively and defensively, and its ability to reliably pivot against many teams. Magneton's Steel typing is very rare in ZU, and it can hold Eviolite to shore up its mediocre bulk. This gives it a unique niche as a bulky pivot that provides a rare form of defensive utility while still hitting quite hard. Alternatively, Choice item sets are effective offensive threats thanks to Magneton's excellent STAB combination and great ability in Analytic, which can situationally boost its already good power even further. Magneton's Steel-type STAB moves are very threatening to most of the tier's Ground-types, which allows all sets to pivot reliably against many teams. However, Magneton's bulk is very poor, which prevents Choice item sets from providing much defensive utility, and Eviolite sets are simply not as threatening as their Choice item counterparts. Magneton's Steel typing also saddles it with unsavory weaknesses to Fire-, Fighting-, and Ground-type attacks; the first two are especially problematic, as Magneton is slower than most of the tier's Fire- and Fighting-types.
zu.comments:
Other Options

A bulkier spread on the Eviolite set can work if you want to focus on Magneton's ability to take hits. More defensively oriented Tera types, such as Tera Fairy and Tera Ghost, can be considered, as they give Magneton a Fighting resistance while turning its other weaknesses into neutralities. Thunder Wave on Eviolite sets is a decent option to spread paralysis, but most Magneton switch-ins don't mind being paralyzed that much or are outright immune to the move. Metal Sound is an additional option on the Eviolite set that lets Magneton break through Dipplin and Whiscash, but it is overall niche compared to the other options.

Checks and Counters

Special Walls: Special walls such as Venusaur and Muk are decent checks to Magneton due to their ability to sponge its main STAB attacks. Steel Beam's immense power pressures even them, however, and neither of them prevent Magneton from pivoting out of the bad matchup with Volt Switch.

Ground-types: Bulky Ground-types, such as Sandaconda and Sandslash block Volt Switch from Magneton and threaten to OHKO it with their STAB moves. They are not true switch-ins, however, as Magneton's Analytic boosted Steel-type STAB moves are still greatly threatening to them.

Fire-types: Fire-types such as Charizard, Typhlosion, Magmortar, and Pyroar can OHKO Magneton with their STAB moves, and they are all faster than variants lacking a Choice Scarf. They also resist Magneton's Steel-type STAB moves, but none of them are true switch-ins due to their inability to block Volt Switch or reliably switch into Thunderbolt.

Fighting-types and Fighting-type coverage: Fighting-types such as Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel threaten to revenge kill Magneton; Choice Scarf Primeape is even faster than Choice Scarf Magneton. Additionally, common Fighting-type coverage from the likes of Orthworm, Regirock, and Naclstack prevents Magneton from comfortably dealing with them one-on-one depending on what coverage move it is locked into. None of them can directly switch in, however.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Magneton's Steel typing makes it an excellent offensive answer to common Pokemon like Mesprit and Weezing, giving it plenty of opportunities to switch in, attack, and pivot out. Most Ground-type Pokemon like Sandaconda and Sandslash that would otherwise block Magneton's Volt Switch cannot reliably switch into Magneton's Analytic-boosted Flash Cannon and avoid being KOed by a follow-up Flash Cannon. Tri Attack is Magneton's strongest neutral attack against Electric-types as well as Camerupt and Whiscash, while Steel Beam gives Magneton substantial power for breaking down special walls in exchange for massively weakening itself. Magneton primarily uses Terastallization to increase its power, but shedding its 4x Ground weakness is a nice plus. Analytic makes Magneton painful to switch around; it's also complemented by Magneton's many resistances and solid bulk when holding Eviolite. 84 Speed allows Magneton to outrun defensive pivot Mesprit, with rest in bulk giving it more longevity.

VoltTurn teams welcome Magneton as a strong offensive pivot that adds to their defensive backbone with its Steel typing. Other pivots like Primeape and Clawitzer can create cores with Magneton and cause opponents to end up lost in the vortex. Strong wallbreakers like Virizion and Clawitzer appreciate Magneton bringing them in safely with Volt Switch, and they have the bulk and power to answer problematic Ground-types for Magneton. Specially defensive Pokemon like Regirock and Muk are excellent answers to Fire-types like Charizard and Typhlosion that threaten Magneton. Magneton cannot afford to run Heavy-Duty Boots given the greater bulk provided by Eviolite, so it often ends up worn down by entry hazards; hazard removers like Lurantis and Sandslash can mitigate Magneton's vulnerability to this as it pivots in and out, and they appreciate Magneton checking threats to them like Mesprit and Dodrio. Psychic-weak Pokemon like Primeape and Weezing appreciate Magneton checking Mesprit for them. Magneton's Steel typing similarly gives it opportunities to switch in and threaten Articuno out as well, which is appreciated by Ice-weak teammates such as Venusaur. Physical attackers like Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel benefit from Magneton threatening Weezing, one of their most significant checks, and they support Magneton in return by threatening special walls like Naclstack for it.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Magneton is one of the most feared wallbreakers in the entire tier. Many teams are completely incapable of safely switching into Magneton thanks to its great STAB combination and access to Analytic, which amps up its power even further. Volt Switch complements Magneton nicely, as it is still quite powerful and allows Magneton to keep up momentum for its team. Magneton is generally quite good at pivoting, as many of the Pokemon immune to Electric, such as Sandslash and Sandaconda, fear Magneton's Steel-type STAB moves. Steel Beam is a monstrously powerful attack that is capable of hitting several notable power benchmarks, including OHKOing Sandaconda and Regirock so they can't KO Magneton back. While the massive recoil damage prevents it from being a staple attack, it gives a teammate free entry into battle should Magneton take itself out due to recoil. Tera Steel is preferred to jack up the power of Flash Cannon and Steel Beam even more, allowing the former to reliably 2HKO Jolteon and specially defensive Mesprit. As an alternative, Tri Attack lets Magneton deal solid damage to Ground- and Electric-types without damaging itself. Analytic allows Magneton to hit switch-ins much harder than it would be able to otherwise, which has great synergy with its threatening wallbreaking profile as well as Volt Switch. It also boosts its power should it have to take a hit before moving, which can be useful versus weak moves that Magneton resists, such as STAB moves from Mesprit and Farigiraf. However, such situations should generally be avoided due to Magneton's middling bulk. A Timid nature is recommended in order to outrun Timid Farigiraf.

Choice Specs Magneton fits well on teams ranging from offense to balance teams due to its ability to act as a strong wallbreaker and a reliable pivot. Magneton's toolkit is appreciated by a variety of offensive teammates. Teammates with powerful Fighting-type coverage, such as Primeape and Regirock, are good teammates, as are Grass-types, such as Dipplin and Virizion. Their ability to threaten Ground-types that might try to absorb Magneton's Electric-type STAB moves while still being able to break through standard special walls is very useful for Magneton, and they can also switch into annoying Ground-types, such as Sandaconda and Sandslash. Magneton, in return, can bring them in safely with Volt Switch and threaten physical walls such as Weezing and Orthworm. Switch-ins to Fire-types are also needed, as Magneton is easily revenge killed by foes such as Charizard, Typhlosion, and Pyroar. Bulky Water- and Rock-types, such as Poliwrath and Regirock, are therefore good teammates. Faster, frailer partners also appreciate Magneton's wallbreaking and pivoting capabilities; Primeape, Clawitzer, and Hisuian Sneasel appreciate Magneton threatening to break down defensive cores and bringing them in safely with Volt Switch. The first two can also form a pivoting core with it, while Primeape can also use Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from specially defensive Magneton checks, making them even more vulnerable to chip damage. On a related note, Magneton also benefits significantly from entry hazards being on the opponent's side of the field, as several of its bulkier checks, such as Muk, do not normally hold Heavy-Duty Boots. Stealth Rock setters such as Mesprit, Sandaconda, and Regirock can set up the hazard reliably to assist Magneton's wallbreaking capabilities, and they are generally not significantly threatened by Magneton's bulky checks. Spikes setters such as Sandslash and Orthworm also work well.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf turns Magneton into an effective revenge killer and general anti-offense Pokemon, as it outruns the entire unboosted metagame bar Jolteon. It also has a limited, but still notable, defensive profile, and its ability to pivot brings a lot of utility to the table. Volt Switch allows Magneton to keep up momentum for its team and effectively pivot. Steel Beam allows Magneton to wallbreak should the need arise and hits extremely hard with an Analytic boost. However, the massive recoil makes it a situational attack. Tera Steel allows Magneton to power up Flash Cannon and Steel Beam significantly. On the other hand, Tera Electric leaves Magneton with a single weakness and minimizes its vulnerability to Hitmontop's Mach Punch. A Timid nature is required so Magneton can outrun Whimsicott and Alolan Persian. Analytic allows Magneton to pick up several KOs, such as 2HKOing Sandaconda with Flash Cannon on the switch and doing the same to Orthworm with Thunderbolt.

Choice Scarf Magneton is a good choice for many bulky offense and outright offensive teams. Magneton is the slowest viable Choice Scarf user, and it is unsuitable for revenge killing Speed-boosting sweepers, such as Beartic and Lapras, and other Choice Scarf users, such as Primeape, Hisuian Sneasel, and Typhlosion. Other ways of taking care of these threats are therefore necessary. Prankster Encore users like Whimsicott and Sableye can greatly irritate and deter setup from the aforementioned setup threats, while the former can form a pivoting core with Magneton. Meanwhile, defensive checks to the other Choice Scarf users, such as Sandaconda and Weezing for the former two, and Naclstack for the latter, serve to greatly assist Magneton. Magneton can help these teammates out by bringing them into battle safely with Volt Switch and revenge killing unboosted offensive foes for them. Magneton also benefits from teammates that can effectively take down problematic Ground-types. Strong Grass-types, such as Virizion and Alolan Exeggutor, can switch into and pressure these foes. Magneton's tendency to force these threats to switch in also opens the door for them to enter battle via advantageous double switches. Other powerful wallbreakers, such as Typhlosion, Sneasel, and Clawitzer, can also threaten these foes, while Magneton can bring them into battle safely with Volt Switch; the first three pressure special walls, such as Muk, that can sponge Magneton's attacks. Articuno is another notable teammate, as it forms a pivoting core with Magneton, threatens many of its checks with Freeze-Dry, and can annoy setup sweepers that Magneton cannot deal with via Haze.

Wallbreaker.description:
Thanks to a solid typing with one weakness and good defensive stats, Alolan Grimer is able to use Knock Offs consistently throughout a game, weakening the opposing team for its teammates to take advantage of. Gunk Shot is used to hit Pokemon that have already been hit by Knock Off, while Drain Punch OHKOs Pawniard and provides some recovery to increase Grimer's longevity. Drain Punch also allows it to damage other Alolan Grimer neutrally, making it valuable in matchups against opposing Alolan Grimer. Sleep Talk can be used to make Alolan Grimer a great Foongus check and sleep absorber for the team, while Memento gives sweeper teammates a chance to set up. Imprison, together with a bit of Speed investment, lets Alolan Grimer completely shut down opposing Alolan Grimer. Tera Grass eliminates Grimer's only weakness to Ground and lets it take on opposing Hisuian Voltorb more easily.

Alolan Grimer is forced out by Ground-types like Mudbray, Numel, and opposing Toedscool, so checks to those Pokemon like Drifloon, Toedscool, and Shellos are essential. Alolan Grimer pairs well with offensive sweepers like Unburden Shroodle, Shellder, and Numel, which can sweep more easily due to Alolan Grimer weakening the enemy team with Knock Off. Grookey is a good partner as well, since Grassy Terrain gives Alolan Grimer much appreciated passive recovery and cuts damage from Earthquake in half, while Alolan Grimer's Knock Off makes switching into Grookey's Wood Hammer much harder. Volt Switch users like Hisuian Voltorb and Wattrel can help get Alolan Grimer in safely, and they can help pressure and overwhelm Ground-types for each other.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Assault Vest can be used to boost Muk's already solid special bulk, and Drain Punch can be utilized to give Muk more longevity and to hit such foes as Magneton and Mabosstiff. However, Muk prefers to run Leftovers most of the time due to its lack of reliable recovery, and it generally wants different coverage moves like Zen Headbutt. Shadow Sneak is another option to let it pick off weakened foes like Mesprit. Tera Ghost lets Muk block Rapid Spin from Cryogonal, Hitmontop, and Sandslash.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types and Ground-type Coverage: Ground-types, notably Camerupt, Sandaconda, Sandslash, and Whiscash, can reliably threaten Muk with STAB Ground-type moves while shrugging off its attacks. Additionally, Venusaur with Earth Power and Toxicroak with Earthquake are capable of forcing it out.

Psychic-types: Psychic-types like Farigiraf and Mesprit can easily force Muk to either switch or Terastallize. However, these Pokemon do not like switching in on Knock Off.

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Orthworm and Perrserker can easily switch in on Poison Jab or Toxic and are able to wear Muk down over time. Orthworm can also easily set up entry hazards while walling it.

Physical Wallbreakers: Due to Muk's average Defense, it has a hard time trying to switch into physical wallbreakers such as Basculin, Lycanroc, and Sneasel.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Muk struggles to break through Naclstack and Regirock, and the two can set up Stealth Rock while walling its attacks. Additionally, Naclstack has access to Purifying Salt and Recover, making Muk almost worthless unusable against it. However, it must be wary of Knock Off to keep its Eviolite-boosted bulk. Weezing can also wall Muk by neutering it with Will-O-Wisp.

Defensive.description:
Muk is a good defensive Pokemon thanks to its great defensive typing and Special Defense, which allow it to act as a blanket check to a plethora of the tier's special attackers. Knock Off lets Muk cripple Pokemon reliant on their items, like Heavy-Duty Boots Sableye, Rocky Helmet Sandslash and Skuntank, and Leftovers Regirock, while punishing Psychic-types including Mesprit. Zen Headbutt is coverage that allows Muk to hit other Poison-types like opposing Muk, Toxicroak, and Hisuian Sneasel, while Rest is its only source of recovery aside from Leftovers and allows it to absorb status. Toxic can be used to cripple foes that try to switch in on it such as Mesprit and Sandslash, but Toxic Spikes is an alternative option to wear down grounded non-Poison-type Pokemon, like Clawitzer, Jolteon, and Whimsicott, especially if the latter two are running Choice Specs sets. Haze can be used to prevent setup sweepers, especially Jolteon and Toxicroak, from snowballing. Protect has great synergy with Leftovers and lets Muk scout Choice item users such as Basculin, Mesprit, and Typhlosion. Sleep Talk should only be used on Rest sets and allows Muk to be less passive while asleep. Muk has a choice between two EV spreads. It can opt for a specially defensive spread with a Careful nature, which further enhances its ability to check opposing special attackers such as Clawitzer and Jolteon; however, it can also run a physically defensive one that utilizes an Impish nature to patch up its average Defense, allowing it to better take on physically offensive foes such as Hitmontop and Sneasel. Tera Dark lets Muk blank Psyshock from Mesprit and Spiritomb while providing a useful Dark resistance. Tera Dragon lets it flip the matchup against Pyroar and Typhlosion and respond back with either a Poison Jab or Knock Off to cripple them.

Muk is a good pick on balance and bulkier teams looking for the ability to check Grass-types like Whimsicott. Muk appreciates Water- and Grass-type teammates, such as Basculin, Clawitzer, Arboliva, and Venusaur, as they offensively pressure the Ground-types like Sandaconda and Whiscash that Muk struggles against. Dark-types like Houndoom and Sneasel are ideal partners, as they help handle the Psychic-types such as Farigiraf and Mesprit that Muk fails to deal with. In return, Muk punishes the Fighting-types that the Dark-types have trouble against, such as Hitmontop and Hisuian Sneasel. Muk appreciates teammates such as Hitmontop, Pyroar, and Camerupt that pressure Steel-types like Magneton and Orthworm. Hitmontop, in particular, provides crucial entry hazard removal via Rapid Spin, which Muk appreciates.

ru.overview: Utilizing its large special bulk and the incredible progress-making combination of Poison Touch and Knock Off, Alolan Muk stands out as a potent special wall in the tier. Common special attackers such as Gengar and Yanmega struggle to get past it and are threatened by Knock Off. Alolan Muk can be incredibly difficult to switch into for defensive teams, as common walls like Slowbro and Quagsire hate losing their items and potentially getting poisoned. However, Alolan Muk can struggle a lot against powerful physical attackers such as Terrakion and Krookodile, as they deal massive damage to it. Alolan Muk also relies entirely on Rest to keep itself healthy throughout a battle, leading it to be potentially overwhelmed or exploited if it cannot find safe opportunities to burn sleep turns.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Curse can be utilized on Alolan Muk to try and turn it into a sweeper, but it generally doesn't have the power or bulk to effectively sweep after setting up. Shadow Sneak can be used in order to pick off weakened foes, but with no STAB boost, it is pretty weak and only does good damage to Pokemon weak to it such as Gengar and Mimikyu. Protect can be used on stall teams so that Alolan Muk can safely absorb Future Sight from Pokemon like Reuniclus and Slowbro, and it can allow Alolan Muk to gain even more Leftovers recovery. Assault Vest can be used to increase Alolan Muk's special bulk but prohibits the use of Rest, thus heavily cutting into its longevity; due to this, Assault Vest Alolan Muk is relegated to more offensive teams. Heavy-Duty Boots can be used in order to solve Alolan Muk's entry hazard weakness, but this cuts into its longevity and forces Alolan Muk to use Rest more often against repeated attacks.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Steel-types like Bisharp can easily switch into Knock Off and threaten Alolan Muk back. However, Steel-types that rely on their items for recovery such as Registeel and Hisuian Goodra still do not like taking Knock Off, and they have to be wary of Drain Punch, which can allow Alolan Muk to potentially win one-on-one.

Ground-types: Ground-types such as Quagsire and Krookodile can target Alolan Muk's Ground weakness while also easily taking Poison Jab. However, they do not like getting poisoned by Poison Touch, as that lessens their longevity.

Fighting-types: Fighting-types such as Terrakion and Chesnaught can easily take Alolan Muk's Knock Off and threaten it with their STAB moves. However, some item-reliant Fighting-types like Choice Scarf Flamigo still do not appreciate the item removal, and all of the Fighting-types still are threatened by the poison chance.

Entry Hazards: Due to Alolan Muk's reliance on Leftovers, hazards can heavily cut into its longevity, forcing Alolan Muk to use Rest more often. Spikes setters such as Chesnaught and Quagsire can not only force Alolan Muk out but also make it more difficult for Alolan Muk to switch in over the course of a game due to the Spikes they set up.

RestTalk.description:
Set Details

Drain Punch allows Alolan Muk to regain health from targets while helping it against Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra and Bisharp. Haze allows Alolan Muk to stop setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Slowbro, Suicune, and Reuniclus by negating the boosts they have attained. Rest is Alolan Muk's main form of recovery and, in longer-paced games, lets it continue to threaten opposing Pokemon. Sleep Talk makes Alolan Muk not too passive even while it's asleep, so it can continue threatening defensive cores. Leftovers allows Alolan Muk to keep itself healthy without relying on Rest as much, enabling it to be more proactive. Tera Water helps Alolan Muk against powerful Water-type special wallbreakers such as Basculegion-F and Kingdra. Tera Fairy can be used to give Alolan Muk a Fighting resistance to help against Pokemon like Gallade and Chesnaught while also being a solid defensive typing overall. Alolan Muk typically doesn't enjoy Terastallizing, however, as it loses the valuable neutralities and resistances its original typing comes with, so Terastallizing should be a last resort.

Alolan Muk fits best on balance and stall teams, as it's able to utilize its immense special bulk to wall powerful Pokemon like Gengar and Basculegion-F while threatening solid damage and status. Blissey in particular pairs amazingly with Alolan Muk on stall, with Blissey walling the special wallbreakers that Alolan Muk struggles to handle such as Choice Specs Toxtricity and Yanmega, while Alolan Muk in return can take on the Ghost-types that Blissey can struggle to hit such as Gengar and Basculegion-F. Physically defensive walls such as Gastrodon and Slowbro pair well with Alolan Muk, as they can cover the physical attackers that threaten it such as Flamigo and Bisharp. In return, Alolan Muk can take on the special attackers that threaten them such as Gengar and Tornadus. Flying-type Pokemon such as Noivern and Gligar pair well with Alolan Muk, as they can easily switch into Ground-types such as Krookodile and Quagsire, and Fighting-types that threaten Alolan Muk, such as Flamigo and Terrakion, and in return, Alolan Muk can switch into the various Electric-types that threaten them such as Magnezone and Kilowattrel. Entry hazard control options such as Cyclizar and Noivern pair well with Alolan Muk, allowing it to leverage Leftovers recovery more often, while Alolan Muk can threaten Ghost-type spiblockers, such as Gengar and Basculegion-F, and Empoleon, which might try to punish Defog. Alolan Muk heavily appreciates Pokemon like Gastrodon, Noivern, and Slowbro that can help chip away at enemies health, as they can increase the damage that Alolan Muk does with moves such as Spikes or can help deny recovery with Taunt or Psychic Noise.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dark

Rock Slide can be a solid option over Drain Punch to check non-Will-O-Wisp Volcarona and Yanmega. However, its shaky accuracy is a notable deterrent and makes Alolan Muk less reliable against Steel-types such as Heatran and Bisharp.

Poison

Rock Slide can be used over Poison Jab, as it can reliably check Volcarona and Frosmoth as well as threaten Zapdos without risking paralysis from Static.

Specially Defensive (Poison).description:
Alolan Muk serves a critical role on Poison teams thanks to its immense special bulk and Dark typing, allowing it to switch in and threaten out several Psychic- and Ghost-types like Hatterene, Galarian Slowking, Flutter Mane, and Hisuian Zoroark with ease. Knock Off deals with the aforementioned Psychic- and Ghost-types while removing crucial held items from the likes of Blissey, Swampert, and Archaludon. Drain Punch provides Alolan Muk with a solid recovery tool and gives it coverage for Dark- and Steel-type threats such as Hydreigon, Greninja, and Heatran. Poison Jab provides a decently consistent option of spreading poison when paired with Poison Touch while dealing with foes such as Hatterene and Primarina reliably. Curse can be used to let Alolan Muk act as a win condition as well as allowing it to comfortably take on physical threats like Ceruledge. Rest provides a form of recovery, letting Alolan Muk stick around longer against bulkier teams. If it's running Rest, Sleep Talk can be used over Protect to prevent Alolan Muk from being too passive during its sleep turns.

Physically defensive Amoonguss is an incredible partner for Alolan Muk thanks to its Ground neutrality, Water resistance, and Grass-type STAB moves, as it can handle the Ground- and Water-type threats that would normally feast on Alolan Muk like Great Tusk, Gastrodon, and Urshifu-R without much worry. Galarian Weezing provides a crucial form of entry hazard removal, allowing Alolan Muk to get the most out of its Black Sludge recovery while also checking Dragon-type foes like Dragonite and Roaring Moon. Physically defensive Toxapex can handle threats such as Kleavor and Mimikyu thanks to Haze and Toxic. Both Galarian Slowking and Clodsire complement Alolan Muk as fellow special walls, as Assault Vest Galarian Slowking handles threats such as Enamorus, Iron Moth, and Latios as well as creating pressure with Future Sight, while Alolan Muk helps deal with the Ghost-types that would normally threaten it. Unaware Clodsire deals with setup sweepers like Gholdengo, Volcarona, and Sneasler while providing entry hazards, which can put pressure on them after Alolan Muk removes their Heavy-Duty Boots. Iron Moth can break past the Steel-type threats and physical walls that Alolan Muk is unable to dent such as Scizor, Skarmory, and Amoonguss. Okidogi and Sneasler strongly appreciate Alolan Muk's Psychic immunity, and in return, they handle threats such as Bisharp, Hisuian Goodra, and Ogerpon-C, which otherwise cause significant issues for Alolan Muk.

Specially Defensive (Dark).description:
Alolan Muk is an amazing defensive part of Dark teams thanks to its Poison typing that grants it a solid neutrality to the Dark-type's weaknesses, which can provide comfort against foes such as Flutter Mane and Enamorus. Poison Jab puts pressure on Fairy-types like Primarina, Flutter Mane, and Hatterene while also spreading poison around to help wear down foes such as Volcarona and switch-ins like Great Tusk. Knock Off removes problematic items such as Skarmory's Rocky Helmet and Moltres's Heavy-Duty Boots, helping out teammates like Hisuian Samurott. Finally, Drain Punch grants Alolan Muk a form of recovery while also enabling it to check Steel- and opposing Dark-types such as Heatran, Darkrai, and Greninja.

Alolan Muk greatly appreciates support from the likes of Meowscarada and Greninja, which are able to check problematic Ground-types such as Ting-Lu, Hippowdon, and Ursaluna. They can also use their Ice-type coverage in Triple Axel and Ice Beam, respectively, to handle Flying- and Dragon-types like Gliscor, Dragonite, and Roaring Moon. Furthermore, Choice Scarf Meowscarada can continue to support Alolan Muk by using Flower Trick to check Water-types like Urshifu-R and Manaphy along with Choice Specs Flutter Mane, preventing Alolan Muk from being worn down as easily. Greninja, meanwhile, can use coverage such as Sludge Wave to deal with the Ogerpon formes and Iron Valiant reliably alongside using Extrasensory to break problematic Fighting- and Poison-types like non-Assault Vest Iron Hands and Toxapex. Ting-Lu can check Electric-types like Raging Bolt and Sandy Shocks for Alolan Muk and is able to set Stealth Rock to wear down would-be checks such as Ogerpon-H and Landorus. Mandibuzz can come in on and check Ground-types and physical attackers such as Iron Treads, Garchomp, and Scizor using Foul Play. Hisuian Samurott can check Fire-types such as Heatran and Ceruledge for Alolan Muk while also setting Spikes using Ceaseless Edge. Hoopa-U can smash apart threats to Alolan Muk such as Galarian Weezing, Skarmory, and Archaludon with options such as Psychic, Thunderbolt, and Focus Blast.

Ghostbuster (Stall).description:
• Alolan Muk is one of the strongest dedicated checks to Calyrex-S for stall teams, boasting incredible Special Defense and a dual typing that isn't weak to Calyrex-S's most common Tera types or Psyshock.

  • Poison Jab: Combining Poison Jab with Poison Touch gives an amazing 51% chance to inflict poison per hit, making Alolan Muk an excellent status spreader just by attacking.

  • Protect: Since Alolan Muk's most reliable source of healing is Black Sludge, using Protect for extra recovery turns is critical, as well as for racking up extra damage on poisoned enemies.

  • Shadow Sneak: Shadow Sneak deals significant damage to Calyrex-S if it hasn't Terastallized and is great for picking off weakened Focus Sash users in general.

  • Toxic: When forcing switches against Calyrex-S, Toxic can be used to catch problematic checks and put them on a strict timer.

  • Black Sludge: Even without Tera Poison, Black Sludge is largely preferred over Leftovers because it punishes Trick attempts from Calyrex-S and Lunala.

  • 15 Speed IV: This is an option for underspeeding the slowest Alomomola, making it much harder for the opponent to safely pivot would-be checks into Alolan Muk.

  • EV Spread: Maximum special bulk means that Calyrex-S's +2 Astral Barrage cannot 2HKO Alolan Muk.

Other Options

  • Minimize: While evasion tactics can be devastating for poisoned targets, it is very inconsistent and risks unnecessary damage that can compromise Alolan Muk's ability to check Calyrex-S long term.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Any Terastallization on Alolan Muk needs to be meticulously timed, as Terastallization sacrifices its long term survivability against Calyrex-S.

  • Poison: Tera Poison's Fighting-type and Fairy-type resistances can buy an extra turn against Tera Blast Calyrex-S and Flutter Mane. It also keeps the healing effects of Black Sludge.

  • Flying: Tera Flying can be used in a pinch to avoid Alolan Muk's sole Ground-type weakness.

RegenVest (Mienshao).description: The alternative EV spread sacrifices some bulk to allow Alolan Muk to threaten special attackers that can recover more effectively, most notably Magic Guard Primarina.

Specially Defensive (Poison).description: Alolan Muk serves excellently as a premier special wall for Poison teams, taking on special attackers like Greninja and Enamorus with ease. Knock Off threatens Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Latias and Sinistcha along with removing crucial held items such as Celesteela's Leftovers and Chansey's Eviolite, making them far easier to take down. Pursuit is used to eliminate threats switching out from Alolan Muk, such as Tapu Lele, Assault Vest Galarian Slowking, and Blacephalon. Drain Punch allows Alolan Muk to not only heal but also deal with Dark-, Steel-, and Ice-types like Hydreigon, Heatran, and Kyurem, while Poison Jab can reliably spread poison to foes such as Volcarona as well as check Fairy-types like Enamorus and Calm Mind Clefable. The EV spread maximizes Alolan Muk's special bulk while allowing it to survive an unboosted V-create from Victini after Stealth Rock. Mega Venusaur serves as an excellent complement to Alolan Muk, providing Leech Seed support to help it stay healthy and deal with problematic Ground- and Water-types such as Mamoswine, Mega Swampert, and Hisuian Samurott. Crobat provides full-on Ground immunity, which makes it capable of coming in and handling the likes of Great Tusk and Hippowdon, as well as checking fast Fighting-type threats like Mega Gallade and Iron Valiant. Galarian Weezing similarly provides Ground immunity, enabling it to check Garchomp and Ting-Lu in addition to dealing with Dragon-types like Kommo-o and Roaring Moon. Toxapex supports Alolan Muk with Scald, pressuring physical attackers such as Kleavor, Weavile, and Sneasler and checking Fire-types like Ceruledge and Cinderace. Assault Vest Galarian Slowking can serve as a specially defensive complement to Alolan Muk, being able to check Zapdos and Latios while appreciating Alolan Muk's removal of Ghost-types like Hisuian Zoroark. Nidoking can remove physical walls that check Alolan Muk such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Gliscor while also handling Electric-types such as Raging Bolt. Choice Scarf Sneasler can outspeed and remove several dangerous targets like Excadrill and Roaring Moon for Alolan Muk with Close Combat.

Assault Vest (Poison).description: Assault Vest Alolan Muk finds a pivotal role on Poison teams, with its high special bulk and secondary Dark typing providing a much-needed immunity to Psychic-type attacks. Knock Off provides a strong STAB option with immense utility by removing held items. Poison Jab is Alolan Muk's most consistent STAB move, being able to reliably spread poison and make progress thanks to Poison Touch. Pursuit is used to trap Choice-locked threats like Hisuian Zoroark, Greninja, and Tapu Lele for solid damage. For Alolan Muk's final moveslot, Drain Punch provides some much-needed recovery and hits Steel- and Dark-type threats like Heatran and Hydreigon for solid damage. Alternatively, Shadow Sneak can allow Alolan Muk to pick off weakened threats, while Rock Slide checks Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y. The EV spread maximizes Alolan Muk's special bulk, with the 12 Defense EVs allowing it to survive an unboosted Victini's V-create after Stealth Rock. Crobat complements Alolan Muk thanks to its secondary Flying typing, which can support Alolan Muk against threats like Great Tusk, Clodsire, and Mega Gallade. Mega Venusaur helps Alolan Muk by dealing with Water- and Ground-type threats including Barraskewda, Mega Swampert, and Mamoswine. Galarian Slowking pairs with Alolan Muk to create a specially defensive core by handling threats such as Choice Specs Latios, Tornadus-T, and Kyurem. Toxapex handles powerful physical threats like Kleavor, Mega Lopunny, and Weavile and has Z-Haze for special attackers that can overwhelm Alolan Muk like Kommo-o. Choice Scarf Sneasler can remove threats to Alolan Muk such as Excadrill, Hisuian Arcanine, and non-Choice Scarf Iron Boulder with its powerful Close Combat. Nidoking can remove walls that can sit on Alolan Muk, including Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Corviknight, thanks to its strong coverage moves.

Specially Defensive (Dark).description: Alolan Muk is an amazing defensive part of any Dark team, with its Poison typing and an amazing Special Defense stat providing Dark a comfortable switch-in to the likes of special Iron Valiant, Enamorus, Volcarona, and Tapu Lele. Poison Touch gives Alolan Muk the ability to poison common switch-ins such as Great Tusk, Rotom-W, and Zapdos. Poison Jab provides an accurate and solid way to deal damage to Fairy-types such as Tapu Lele and Tapu Koko. Knock Off makes progress against item-reliant Pokemon such as Porygon2 and Celesteela. Pursuit grants Alolan Muk the ability to trap Pokemon like Alolan Raichu, Gholdengo, and Galarian Slowking that attempt to switch out against it. Alternatively, Drain Punch gives Alolan Muk both another form of recovery and a tool to deal with Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra, Heatran, and Hydreigon. Finally, Protect can allow Alolan Muk to scout Choice-locked threats such as Meowscarada and Enamorus and take advantage of Black Sludge recovery. Investing 20 EVs in Attack helps Alolan Muk always break Kyurem's Substitute with Poison Jab. Mandibuzz is a great partner to complement Alolan Muk, as its immunity to Ground makes it easier to switch into threats such as Excadrill, Garchomp, and Great Tusk. And it has access to Defog to remove entry hazards that would whittle down Alolan Muk, allowing it to make the most out of Black Sludge. Furthermore, Mandibuzz checks physical setup sweepers like Scizor and Mega Gallade by using Foul Play. With its Ghost typing and Will-O-Wisp, Mega Sableye can handle threatening Fighting-types such as Sneasler, Iron Hands, and Mega Gallade. Mega Sableye is also excellent to pair with Alolan Muk, as it grants Dark a bulky Magic Bounce user. Meowscarada helps threaten out several Water- and Ground-type threats that threaten Alolan Muk like Choice Band Urshifu-R, Mega Swampert, and Great Tusk with its powerful Flower Trick. Both Hydreigon and Weavile appreciate having Alolan Muk on the team, as it can effectively Pursuit trap Tapu Lele. Alolan Muk complements Ting-Lu's hazard-stacking capabilities by spreading poison to wear down foes or removing Heavy-Duty Boots. Hydreigon is a wallbreaker that checks defensive Pokemon that Alolan Muk struggles to break like Hippowdon, opposing Alolan Muk, and Toxapex. Weavile checks Ground-, Dragon-, and Flying-types such as Garchomp, Mega Altaria, and Landorus.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Gunk Shot is a much stronger alternative to Poison Jab that OHKOes bulky Tera Fairy Calyrex-S after Terastallization, but Poison Jab is more consistent and reliable. Haze may be used over Clear Smog for deterring setup sweepers that rely on Substitute, mainly against Baton Pass teams. However, it is shut down by Taunt from Calyrex-S and thus inferior to Clear Smog in most cases.

Checks and Counters

Physical Attackers: Due to Alolan Muk's middling Defense, it is forced out by popular wallbreakers like Koraidon, Swords Dance Arceus, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, and Zacian-C that deal huge damage to it or even outright OHKO it. The latter two can notably switch in and set up freely, though Arceus-Ground must be wary of Poison Touch.

Gliscor: Gliscor threatens to 2HKO Alolan Muk with Earthquake and removes its Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off. Gliscor also switches into Alolan Muk's Poison Jab and Knock Off freely once Toxic Orb is activated.

Miraidon: Miraidon's Hadron Engine blocks Alolan Muk's primary source of recovery in Rest, preventing it from staying healthy. Furthermore, Miraidon's strong STAB moves easily 2HKO Alolan Muk, though it dislikes taking Knock Off.

Tera Poison Users: Calm Mind sweepers like Arceus-Fairy often run Tera Poison, which lets it freely set up on Alolan Muk if it doesn't have Clear Smog. Even then, Judgment's considerable damage and Alolan Muk's lack of reliable recovery make Arceus-Fairy a threat.

Specially Defensive.description:
Possessing a unique typing and decent bulk, Alolan Muk is one of the best Calyrex-S checks on stall teams, particularly against Tera Fairy sets. Thanks to this typing and Fairy neutrality, Alolan Muk comfortably takes on Calyrex-S's STAB moves, along with checking Tera Fairy Calyrex-S better than other Dark-types like Mandibuzz and Ting-Lu. However, Mandibuzz is still a frequent competitor on stall teams due to having a more consistent recovery option in Roost. Knock Off OHKOes Calyrex-S, and the lack of switch-ins in the metagame makes it a great progress-making move. It removes Leftovers from Ting-Lu and Heavy-Duty Boots from Miraidon, Arceus, Ho-Oh, and Kyogre, synergizing with entry hazards set by Alolan Muk's teammates. Poison Jab hits Tera Fairy Calyrex-S and Arceus-Fairy, 2HKOing the former. The poison chance, further boosted by Poison Touch, allows Alolan Muk to slowly wear down bulky switch-ins like Ting-Lu and defensive Arceus formes. Clear Smog halts setup sweepers like Tera Fairy Nasty Plot Calyrex-S and Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy from overwhelming Alolan Muk with stat boosts. Rest is Alolan Muk's primary source of healing, but due to the commonly used Miraidon's Hadron Engine, it is unreliable. Pain Split is another option for recovery that isn't blocked by Electric Terrain and reduces Alolan Muk's dependency on Rest for staying healthy. However, it can be hindered by targets with low HP. Sleep Talk, on the other hand, discourages Calyrex-S from setting up Nasty Plot while Alolan Muk is asleep. Due to no Tera being particularly beneficial against Calyrex-S, Alolan Muk generally prefers not to Terastallize. However, Tera Poison has a few uses, as it turns Draining Kiss into a resistance and strengthens Poison Jab, which comes in handy against Tera Fairy Calyrex-S. It also makes Alolan Muk resist Arceus-Fairy's Judgment. However, Terastallizing Alolan Muk comes with the drawback of removing its resistance to Astral Barrage.

Alolan Muk exclusively fits on stall, where its passivity and weakness to physical attackers are not an issue compared to the defensive value it provides in checking Calyrex-S; this is particularly appreciated by teammates like Skeledirge, Gliscor, Alomomola, and Dondozo. Alolan Muk is vulnerable to strong physical attackers like Koraidon, Zacian-C, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, Ho-Oh, and Swords Dance Arceus. Hence, Gliscor is a great teammate, as it can switch into Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground as well as opposing Gliscor's Knock Off; the latter greatly hinders Alolan Muk's longevity by removing Heavy-Duty Boots. Gliscor also sets up entry hazards such as Spikes and Toxic Spikes, which exert a lot of pressure on opposing teams and make use of Alolan Muk's Knock Off removing Heavy-Duty Boots. Similarly, Skeledirge, Alomomola, and Dondozo take on threats like Koraidon, Zacian-C, and Swords Dance Arceus, which greatly threaten Alolan Muk. In particular, Alomomola provides additional healing with Wish, letting Alolan Muk stay healthy without having to use Rest. Although Alolan Muk possesses decent special bulk, strong special attackers like Miraidon, Calm Mind Arceus-Ground, and Kyogre are capable of brute-forcing through it. Therefore, special walls like Tera Grass Ho-Oh and Blissey make for good teammates, as they can handle the aforementioned threats. In return, Alolan Muk acts as a safeguard against Calyrex-S; it can afford getting a Choice item through Trick much more than Ho-Oh or Blissey, as it offers little outside of checking Calyrex-S. Furthermore, it switches in on Psyshock, which would otherwise deal massive damage to them.

monotype.overview:
Water

Cloyster is generally outclassed on Water teams, its poor defensive typing and lacking offensive prowess before setting up compared to options like Primarina and Urshifu-R makes finding that turn to get in and use Shell Smash difficult. However, should it overcome these hurdles, Cloyster can be a meance being able to rip through types like Dragon and Ice and completely flip games on their head.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ice

Ice Beam is an alternative option, useful for hitting physically defensive walls, such as Archaludon without massively boosting its defense, Skarmory, or Hippowdon.

Shell Smash (Water).description:
Thanks to its excellent offensive movepool and access to Shell Smash, Cloyster finds a niche on Water teams. Thanks to Cloyster's high Defense stat, it can reliably use Shell Smash in front of some of the tier's premier physical attackers, such as Ceruledge and Mamoswine. Ice Beam is a great option to hit physically defensive foes such as Archaludon, Skarmory, and Great Tusk; it hits the former without activating Stamina. Hydro Pump is an option to prevent Cloyster from being entirely passive against Steel-types, namely Gholdengo and Heatran, whereas Ice Shard is helpful for picking off threats that may move before Cloyster even after a Shell Smash boost, such as Sucker Punch Dragapult and Choice Scarf Flutter Mane. Icicle Spear is excellent for hitting Flying-, Ground-, and Dragon-type Pokemon, such as Tornadus-T, Clodsire, and Latios, as well as breaking Focus Sash or Sturdy on Pokemon such as Breloom and Ogerpon-C. After a Shell Smash, the given EV spread, coupled with Never-Melt Ice, allows Cloyster to OHKO Choice Scarf Archaludon with Ice Beam, as well as defensive Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra with Ice Beam and Icicle Spear, respectively, after a layer of Spikes.

Hisuian Samurott is a great teammate for Cloyster, as the Spikes it provides with Ceaseless Edge are very important for Cloyster. If Cloyster opts to use three Ice-type moves, then Hisuian Samurott can weaken opposing Steel-types, such as Heatran and Empoleon, with Sacred Sword. Ogerpon-W is a fantastic teammate for Cloyster, as Cloyster's moveset notably leaves it weak against other Water-types, such as Alomomola and Primarina. Ogerpon-W remedies this issue by threatening these Pokemon with either Horn Leech or Power Whip. Swampert and Alomomola are both great teammates for Cloyster, as they both act as slow pivot options to help Cloyster get in more easily. Swampert can also provide Knock Off and Stealth Rock support while being immune to Electric, whereas Alomomola can use Wish to keep Cloyster healthy in case it takes some entry hazard damage. Fighting-types such as Urshifu-R and Keldeo complement Cloyster excellently, as they can help weaken Steel-types, such as Gholdengo and Skarmory, so that Cloyster can have an easier time sweeping. Additionally, both of these Pokemon have pivoting options in the form of U-turn and Flip Turn, respectively, allowing Cloyster to come in when the Fighting-types scare something out. Toxapex can use Toxic to weaken foes that Cloyster cannot OHKO, such as Urshifu-R and Iron Hands.
