Toxapex can also use Haze to prevent opposing setup sweepers from getting too out of hand, which gives Cloyster more opportunities to use Shell Smash. Tentacruel can provide hazard control with Rapid Spin, ensuring Cloyster will have an easier time finding an opportunity to use Shell Smash, as well as using Toxic Spikes of its own to chip down opposing Pokemon. Additionally, Tentacruel has Flip Turn to help Cloyster hit the field more easily.

Shell Smash Sweeper (Ice).description:
Cloyster is one of Ice's best setup sweepers thanks to its access to Shell Smash in addition to its high Defense stat, which gives it opportunities to set up on the tier's physical attackers like Garchomp, Iron Treads, and Ceruledge. Icicle Spear targets opposing Flying-, Ground-, and Dragon-type Pokemon such as Tornadus-T, Clodsire, and Dragapult while breaking Focus Sash on Pokemon such as Breloom. Rock Blast benefits from Skill Link and threatens Fire-types like Ceruledge and other Ice-type Pokemon like Kyurem. Ice Shard is useful for revenge killing faster Choice Scarf Pokemon that are weakened like Spectrier, Meowscarada, and Roaring Moon. Hydro Pump is the alternative in order to not be walled by opposing Steel-types like Gholdengo and Forretress. It is also beneficial for threatening Heatran and Mamoswine, both of which are troublesome for Ice teams, as well as Torkoal and Ninetales, easing the Fire matchup. Maximum Speed investment with a Jolly nature allows +2 Cloyster to outspeed Choice Scarf users such as Walking Wake and Great Tusk; a Naive nature with the remaining 4 EVs going into Special Attack should be used if opting for Hydro Pump to not reduce its damage. White Herb is Cloyster's preferred item, as it is able to offset the stat drops of Shell Smash, which makes Cloyster harder to revenge kill. Focus Sash is the alternative to always guarantee one turn of setup when at full health, but it is less preferred because Cloyster is already difficult to OHKO under snow or Aurora Veil.

Cloyster's best partner on Ice is Alolan Ninetales. Alolan Ninetales allows Cloyster to have an easier time to set up thanks to it setting snow, which, when combined with Aurora Veil, allows Cloyster to set up on Pokemon that can usually threaten it out like offensive Great Tusk and Cinderace. Alolan Ninetales also provides Encore support to force uncomfortable switches, thus granting Cloyster an easier entry, as well as handling Unaware Pokemon like Quagsire and Dondozo with its STAB Freeze-Dry. Cloyster is able to threaten Fire's weather setters Ninetales and Torkoal after a boost, which benefits Alolan Ninetales, as it can come back in to reset snow for its teammates. Cloyster appreciates Kyurem as an offensive partner, as Choice Specs sets are able to weaken Cloyster's defensive checks like Toxapex and Archaludon. Mamoswine is an excellent partner for Cloyster, as not only can it provide entry hazard support in the form of Stealth Rock, but it can also remove items from opposing defensive staples such as Corviknight and Toxapex with Knock Off. Alolan Sandslash can provide Knock Off support for Cloyster and use Rapid Spin to remove entry hazards, allowing for easier entry to set up and making it much more difficult to KO, Avalugg can also support Cloyster with Rapid Spin and handle its physical offensive checks like Great Tusk under snow. Froslass is Ice's only viable option for Spikes, which Cloyster appreciates, as defensive Pokemon like Hatterene and Iron Hands aren't able to check it properly after a boost and entry hazard damage. Additionally, Froslass can hinder opposing threats with Thunder Wave, allowing Cloyster to outspeed Pokemon that are normally faster than it even with a Shell Smash boost, such as Choice Scarf Roaring Moon and Unburden Sneasler.

Shell Smash Sweeper.description:
• Shell Smash and Skill Link more than make up for Cloyster's weak Attack stat, making it a formidable sweeper that Focus Sash and Mimikyu can't easily stop.

  • Ice Shard: Priority may seem like overkill, but it helps pick off weakened threats without setup. It also gets around priority attacks from Breloom, Dragapult, and Meowscarada after a Shell Smash.

  • Rock Blast: This is Closyer's best shot at dealing with the many Tera Fires that resist Icicle Spear, as well as OHKOing Chien-Pao, Iron Bundle, and Iron Moth.

  • Drill Run: This hits Gholdengo and other Steel-types hard without needing to Terastallize.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is the preferred nature to maximize offensive power, as a single Shell Smash lets you outspeed the entire unboosted metagame. However, Cloyster is in the same speed tier as Breloom, so Jolly is a consideration if you want to minimize Speed tie scenarios in that matchup.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: As a Focus Sash user, Cloyster wants to avoid using Tera when possible, but opposing priority attacks and defensive typings can sometimes make it a necessity.

  • Ghost: Since Cloyster will often be at extremely low health after Shell Smash, Tera Ghost helps it avoid getting revenge killed by Breloom's Mach Punch and Dragonite’s Extreme Speed. It also provides coverage against Gholdengo with Tera Blast.

  • Ice: The increased damage from Tera Ice makes it very difficult for Pokemon to wall Cloyster without resisting it, with even Corviknight getting OHKOed by +2 Adamant Icicle Spear after Stealth Rock damage.

  • Ground: Volt Switch users like Rotom-W love to take Cloyster down to its Focus Sash and pivot to a priority attacker; Tera Ground both nullifies the damage and prevents the switch, giving Cloyster significant momentum with a free turn to Shell Smash. It also lets Cloyster challenge defensive Gholdengo, blocking Thunder Wave and giving +2 Adamant Drill Run a strong chance to OHKO.

  • Fire: While Tera Fire Tera Blast actually does less damage to Corviknight than Tera Ice Icicle Spear, Tera Fire otherwise helps Cloyster muscle past Steel-types it traditionally struggles to beat, such as Scizor.

  • Normal: Tera Normal is a niche option that offers no offensive benefits to Cloyster, but it does prevent Mimikyu and Gallade from revenge killing it with Shadow Sneak.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Considering Cloyster's paper-thin Special Defense, Focus Sash gives Cloyster by far the most setup opportunities.

  • King's Rock: King's Rock is a risky option that doesn’t help Cloyster set up, but it does give Icicle Spear and Rock Blast a 41% chance of flinching.

Defensive Utility (Ice).description: Due to Cloyster's Water typing, high Defense stat, and utility, it is able to tank hits from Steel-type Pokemon that are often threatening to Ice-types, such as Excadrill. Rapid Spin is an asset for defensive utility sets, allowing Cloyster to remove entry hazards such as Stealth Rock. Spikes can help provide chip damage to threats such as Iron Valiant and Heatran. Teleport allows Cloyster to keep momentum when it comes onto the field and pivot out of Pokemon that threaten it into teammates such as Weavile and Galarian Darmanitan. Hidden Power Fire can be used over Teleport to effectively deal with Scizor. Rocky Helmet allows Cloyster to punish physical moves it often switches into, such as U-turn from Corviknight and Crobat. Overcoat also helps reduce the damage Cloyster takes over time by negating sand damage. Defensive Cloyster works best on offensive teams that can take advantage of the Spikes it sets. Wallbreakers such as Galarian Darmanitan and Kyurem are very good teammates, as they can remove threats like Gholdengo, Archaludon, and Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine. Revenge killers such as Weavile, Cetitan, and Alolan Sandslash can check Pokemon such as Hisuian Goodra and Mega Gallade after Spikes damage, allowing sweepers to snowball more easily. Alolan Ninetales is another useful teammate, as it helps Cloyster with Aurora Veil, allowing it to tank special attacks better and set Spikes more easily against Pokemon that can often deny them, such as Keldeo.

Shell Smash Sweeper (Ice).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

ru.overview: A solid choice for both speed control and wallbreaking, Gengar is a dynamic option for teams, as it can provide immense upside due to its versatility and offensive prowess. Gengar is a good Choice Scarf user, comfortably outpacing other Choice Scarf users in the metagame like Basculegion-F, Gardevoir, and Krookodile. Nasty Plot Gengar is a fast, potent setup sweeper that can decimate teams after just one boost. Gengar, using status-spreading moves such as Thunder Wave, Toxic Spikes, and Will-O-Wisp and disruption moves in Encore and Taunt, can disrupt its primary checks like Cyclizar, Umbreon, and Registeel. Despite this tremendous upside, Gengar is incredibly frail and susceptible to getting OHKOed by much of the metagame, including notable checks like Bisharp, Cyclizar, and Alolan Muk, so getting it on the field can be difficult. Gengar also directly competes with other great Ghost-type Pokemon in the tier, such as Basculegion-F, Mimikyu, especially on more bulky team structures.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Thunder Wave, Toxic, and Toxic Spikes can provide great value for Hex Gengar. Destiny Bond is always a nice option to trade against something slower than Gengar, such as Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon, which can be otherwise tricky to take down. Knock Off gives Gengar its own item removal option, which can help on entry hazard-stacking teams at the cost of not being offensively threatening due to its low Attack. Pain Split is Gengar's only form of recovery, which it can use against foes like Cyclizar and Hisuian Goodra well. Taunt similarly shuts down slower setup sweepers like Bisharp and can pair well with Destiny Bond to ensure it trades effectively. Choice Specs can be used to threaten OHKOs on Pokemon like Assault Vest Cyclizar and Jirachi.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Although Gengar can use Focus Blast to hit Dark-types like Bisharp and Krookodile for massive damage, it struggles to effectively take down either of them, as Sucker Punch from Bisharp threatens an immediate OHKO while Krookodile often uses Choice Scarf, outpacing and taking Gengar down with ease. Umbreon is susceptible to Encore and Trick as well as being used as setup fodder, but it can reliably tank attacks and threaten to take Gengar out with Foul Play. Alolan Muk, while more niche, can comfortably take hits from Gengar before KOing it with Knock Off, though it must be wary of Will-O-Wisp.

Faster Pokemon: Non-Choice Scarf Gengar is outpaced and immediately threatened by a majority of the Choice Scarf users in the metagame, including Basculegion-F, Gardevoir, Krookodile, and even opposing Gengar. Similarly, Gengar is in a pretty comfortable Speed tier naturally, but it is still outsped by plenty of Pokemon that threaten to OHKO it with slight chip damage, such as Barraskewda, Maushold, and Noivern.

Cyclizar: Assault Vest Cyclizar is a common Gengar check and can disrupt it significantly, switching in and threatening big damage with Knock Off while also being able to pivot out into Ghost-type teammates on an expected Focus Blast.

Nasty Plot.description:
Set Details

Nasty Plot Gengar is a potentially devastating setup sweeper thanks to its great Speed tier, outpacing base 100 Speed Pokemon like Jirachi and Entei, and strong STAB combination. Focus Blast gives Gengar the coverage to hit bulky Steel-types like Bisharp, Hisuian Goodra, and Registeel and Gengar's primary check in Cyclizar for massive damage, though it comes at the cost of accuracy issues. Encore can be really disruptive to lock slower walls into unfavorable positions, such as forcing Suicune to use Calm Mind and Umbreon to use Wish, giving Gengar free setup opportunities. Air Balloon is quite powerful on Gengar, affording it safe entry and setup chances against Gastrodon and Quagsire as well as Choice-locked Krookodile if it locks into Earthquake. Colbur Berry similarly gives Gengar great defensive value, allowing it to comfortably survive Knock Off from Pokemon like Cyclizar and Krookodile to threaten them back safely. Tera Ghost allows Shadow Ball to OHKO Jirachi after Spikes damage and Reuniclus, while Tera Fighting can be used to flip the weakness to Dark and boost the power of Focus Blast to annihilate Hisuian Goodra after taking Spikes damage and Assault Vest Cyclizar.

Nasty Plot Gengar fits best on balance and bulky offense teams that can provide it entry points where it can set up and clean late-game. Choice Scarf users like Gallade and Gardevoir pair well with Gengar, fulfilling the speed control role over Gengar to help against Cyclizar and Krookodile, and they grant it safe entry opportunities against their checks like Slowbro and Jirachi with U-turn and Healing Wish respectively. Defensive pivot support options like Cyclizar and Jirachi are key teammates; Cyclizar provides entry hazard and item removal to wear down Gengar's checks like Hisuian Goodra and Registeel, Jirachi can help enable Gengar by spreading paralysis and providing Wish passing, and they serve as Ghost- and Psychic-type switch-ins against Pokemon like Basculegion-F and Gardevoir, respectively. Hazard setters like Chesnaught, Gastrodon, and Jirachi are valuable to accrue chip damage on the opposition, which improves Gengar's ability to clean; the first two also help to absorb Knock Off attempts from Cyclizar and Krookodile. Other offensive setup options like Bisharp, Flygon, and Terrakion can help enable Gengar to sweep late-game, as they can wallbreak effectively against its checks like Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon early- to mid-game or can swap roles with Gengar and clean late-game themselves.

Hex.description:
Set Details

Hex takes advantage of status spread by Gengar and its teammates, notably Thunder Wave from users like Reuniclus and Slowbro, to bolster its damage to seemingly unwallable range. Sludge Bomb is used over Sludge Wave because of the increased odds to poison, which can similarly help to enable Hex damage. Dazzling Gleam gives Gengar a reliable attack for its most common check, Cyclizar, along with Krookodile and Umbreon. Will-O-Wisp is used to disrupt Cyclizar and offensive Pokemon like Bisharp and Maushold that may try to switch into Gengar and force it out. Heavy-Duty Boots helps Gengar hit the field more often to spread status and use its strong attacks. Leftovers can be run to similarly maintain health on Gengar, though it requires entry hazard removal support to maximize its effectiveness. Colbur Berry is a nice item for Gengar to have against the aforementioned Cyclizar and other Knock Off users like Krookodile, allowing it to comfortably survive an attack and ensure an attempt at burning and hindering the opposition. Tera Fairy can provide a boost to Dazzling Gleam and flips the weakness to Dark, which can allow Gengar to take down Dark-types, like Choice Scarf Krookodile, while also helping absorb strong Dragon-type attacks from threats like Hisuian Goodra and Noivern. Tera Dark similarly flips the weakness to Dark while providing a key immunity to Psychic, which is useful to help against the bulky Psychic-types that can stomach a hit like Jirachi and Reuniclus.

Hex Gengar fits best on balance and bulky offense teams that aim to spread status to enable a late-game sweep for Gengar. Teammates that can help spread status, like Body Slam Jirachi, Thunder Wave Slowbro and Reuniclus, and Toxic Umbreon can help wear down Gengar checks like Hisuian Goodra and Registeel while also helping bolster the damage from Hex. Offensive partners that can also take advantage of this type of status spam are slower wallbreakers like Breloom and Crawdaunt, which can outspeed a lot of threats after they are paralyzed to consistently dish out strong attacks. Defensive partners that can help absorb Knock Off and other Dark- and Ghost-type attacks from threats like Bisharp, Krookodile, and Basculegion-F—like Chesnaught, Cyclizar, and Umbreon—are important for Gengar, as they allow Gengar to fall back on them to wear down foes before threatening to sweep late-game. Leftovers Gengar also appreciates Cyclizar for its entry hazard removal abilities, with Noivern also offering similar hazard removal and pivot support. Gengar does struggle to break through some of the special walls in the tier, especially Hisuian Goodra, Registeel, and Umbreon, so hazard support from teammates like Chesnaught and Jirachi can go a long way. Physical attackers like Gallade, Krookodile, and Terrakion also help Gengar break through Dark- and Steel-types like Bisharp and Umbreon.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

Choice Scarf Gengar is one of the fastest Pokemon in RU, leaving speed demons like Cyclizar and Barraskewda as well as Choice Scarf users like Krookodile and Gardevoir in the dust. Ghost / Poison is an excellent offensive typing that can hit most of the metagame for at least neutral damage, only resisted by Krookodile, Bisharp, Overqwil, and Alolan Muk. Choice Scarf Gengar functions as a revenge killer against Pokemon without priority like Basculegion-F, Modest Shift Gear Toxtricity, and slower Choice Scarf users such as Jirachi and Krookodile. Trick gives Gengar a way to incapacitate setup sweepers like Feraligatr and Suicune that it doesn't have the power to reliably OHKO and walls like Hisuian Goodra and Gastrodon that can easily switch into one of Gengar's attacks. Gengar can lean into its utility options, setting Toxic Spikes for more entry hazard-focused teams. Focus Blast allows Gengar to threaten Steel-types like Bisharp, Empoleon, and non-Assault Vest Hisuian Goodra. It can use Thunder Wave as speed control to allow a slower sweeper like Gallade or Weakness Policy Basculegion-F to outspeed foes. Destiny Bond can be used as a last resort to stop sweepers or when Gengar is weakened and simply needs to trade one-for-one. Tera Ghost boosts Gengar's Shadow Ball and lets it function as a cleaner against teams that are chipped down, notably OHKOing physically defensive Slowbro and having a chance to OHKO maximum HP Jirachi after Stealth Rock damage. Additionally, it removes Gengar's weaknesses to Ground and Psychic, allowing it to survive Psychic-type attacks from Reuniclus or Earthquake from Quagsire. Tera Dark allows Gengar to live a Sucker Punch from even a +2 Bisharp and OHKO it with Focus Blast and turns Gengar's weaknesses to Psychic, Dark, and Ghost into resistances. This lets it switch into Choice-locked Psychic-type attacks from Gardevoir and the strong Psychic-type STAB attacks of Reuniclus, Slowbro, and Necrozma without worry. Tera Dark also allows Gengar to win the mirror match by resisting Shadow Ball and OHKOing back with its own Shadow Ball.

Gengar can fit on a wide variety of team structures, from offense to balance, due to its ability to revenge kill, shut down walls like Hisuian Goodra and Empoleon with Trick, use Toxic Spikes to spread hazards, and leverage Thunder Wave to slow down opposing revenge killers like Noivern and Maushold. Gengar is a great addition to hazard stack teams with its ability to leverage hazard chip damage to meet damage thresholds like OHKOing Hisuian Goodra with Focus Blast after three layers of Spikes and shutting down Heavy-Duty Boots Pokemon like Alolan Muk and Blissey with Trick. Teammates like Suicune and Necrozma love Gengar's ability to use Trick on special walls and give them its Choice Scarf, letting them set up for late-game sweeps. Cyclizar makes an excellent teammate for Gengar, as it is able to keep the field clear of hazards for it while pivoting into Gengar to absorb pesky Fighting- and Fairy-type moves that threaten the little bike lizard. Entei can threaten the Steel-types that switch in when Gengar locks into Sludge Wave or punish Bisharp trying to revenge kill it with Sucker Punch. Defensively, Gengar loves having a Dark-type that can resist the Dark-, Ghost-, and Psychic-type moves that threaten it, making Pokemon like Krookodile and Umbreon enticing choices. Krookodile can set up Stealth Rock for Gengar to take advantage of, while Umbreon can keep it healthy with Wish and cripple walls with Toxic. Knock Off absorbers like Rocky Helmet Chesnaught and Slowbro can switch in to prevent Gengar from being heavily damaged and losing its item. Noivern can lure in Pokemon looking to hit it with a strong Moonblast, then U-turn into Gengar, which resists the move. It can also threaten their common checks, Steel-types, with Flamethrower.

monotype.overview:
Poison

Gengar's amazing Special Attack and Speed along with its solid Ghost typing give it a solid offensive role. However, it has major competition in Iron Moth, which has overall superior utility thanks to its higher bulk and Special Attack, usually performing better against most types.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Poison

Energy Ball provides solid coverage, allowing Gengar to remove Ground-types like Swampert, Hippowdon, and Mamoswine.

Choice Specs (Poison).description:
Gengar finds a niche on Poison teams thanks to its secondary Ghost typing and unique coverage, allowing it to serve as a solid alternative to Iron Moth. Shadow Ball threatens Ghost- and Psychic-type Pokemon like Gholdengo, Pecharunt, and Hatterene. Thunderbolt provides solid coverage by hitting dangerous Flying- and Water-types like Corviknight, Pelipper, and Primarina. Focus Blast allows Gengar to deal with Dark-, Normal-, and Steel-type threats in Hydreigon, Ursaluna, Heatran, and Archaludon, while Dazzling Gleam provides a less risky option to hit Dark-types along with Dragon-types like Walking Wake. Finally, Trick allows Gengar to disrupt special walls like Alolan Muk, Iron Hands, and Ting-Lu by granting them a useless Choice Specs, along with Choice locking Bisharp, which can prove problematic for Poison teams. Icy Wind, however, has the solid role of removing Landorus and Gliscor, which pose significant threats to Poison teams.

Amoonguss can take hits from Water- and Ground-types that Gengar cannot handle such as Ogerpon-W, Swampert, and Great Tusk, along with using Spore to grant Gengar safe entry. Amoonguss can also use Foul Play to remove threats to Gengar such as Dragapult and Mimikyu. Galarian Weezing threatens potent Dark-types like Meowscarada, Ting-Lu, and Roaring Moon thanks to its Fairy-type STAB move and Will-O-Wisp. Galarian Weezing can also use Defog to remove entry hazards, ensuring Gengar stays healthy. Toxapex can handle priority from threats like Scizor, Mimikyu, and Lokix attempting to remove Gengar, along with being able to handle threats like Weavile and Barraskewda. Overqwil pairs nicely with Gengar with its immense physical bulk, being able to take hits from fast physical Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Ceruledge, Iron Boulder, and Gallade. Overqwil's entry hazards also provide utility in chipping down special walls such as Hisuian Goodra and Ting-Lu, which can both prove problematic to Gengar. In return, Overqwil appreciates Gengar's Ghost typing allowing it to block Rapid Spin from the likes of Forretress and Tentacruel. Alolan Muk can handle special attacking Ghost- and Dark-type threats like Flutter Mane, Spectrier, Greninja, and Darkrai. Galarian Slowking can switch into revenge killers Gengar can struggle with, such as Choice Scarf Latias and Choice Scarf Enamorus, and threaten them back with its strong coverage moves. Both Sneasler and Okidogi can handle Dark-types like Alolan Muk, Hisuian Samurott, and Bisharp while appreciating Gengar removing Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo, Hatterene, and Slowbro. Choice Scarf Sneasler can also blitz past problematic foes such as Hoopa-U, Hisuian Goodra, and non-Choice Scarf Darkrai without worry. Okidogi, meanwhile, appreciates Gengar weakening physical walls like Galarian Weezing, Toxapex, and Sableye that prevent it from setting up safely. In response, Okidogi can handle Dark-type menaces like Bisharp, Meowscarada, and Roaring Moon without any issues.

Toxic Spikes Lead (Ghost).description:
Gengar's solid Speed tier and its access to Toxic Spikes, Taunt, and Destiny Bond allow it to have a niche as a lead on Ghost teams. Setting up Toxic Spikes is Gengar's main objective, as the extra chip damage helps wear down Pokemon that would otherwise give Ghost teams lots of trouble, such as Ting-Lu and Porygon2. Taunt is used to prevent opposing leads from setting up their own entry hazards, such as Skarmory, Swampert, and Tinkaton. Destiny Bond can be used in tandem with Taunt to force foes to attack and secure a trade. Sludge Bomb allows Gengar to not be completely passive, as well as having a 50% chance to OHKO Hatterene, dissuading it from trying to block Toxic Spikes.

Toxic Spikes greatly helps offensive teammates muscle through bulkier foes. Spectrier appreciates its would-be checks getting worn down by poison damage, such as Porygon2 and Hoopa-U. Additionally, Spectrier can utilize Hex's double-damage effect immediately rather than having to spend a turn using Will-O-Wisp. The same goes for Dragapult which notably secures an OHKO on poisoned Choice Specs Flutter Mane. Ceruledge appreciates Gengar preventing foes from setting entry hazards with taunt, thus keeping its Focus Sash intact. In turn, Ceruledge can handle the Steel-type Pokemon that Gengar is useless against. Gholdengo's ability, Good as Gold, blocks Defog from the likes of Braviary and Mandibuzz. It is also yet another Pokemon that can use Hex to its fullest potential without having to spend a turn using Thunder Wave. Both Froslass and Brambleghast can stack additional hazards in spikes, ensuring that even foes unaffected by Toxic Spikes will still take some hazard damage.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
With Paradox Pokemon being introduced, Series 2 is bringing big changes to Battle Stadium Singles! This is a modified Series 1 analysis that takes Paradox Pokemon into account. We will update this overview and analysis again once the metagame settles more. For more information on Series 2, check out the resource thread.

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Disruptor.description:
• Gengar's useful immunities and great support movepool give it a niche as an incredibly disruptive Pokemon, especially if taking the correct predictive risks.

  • Destiny Bond: Destiny Bond is excellent at making foes second-guess attacking Gengar. When slower foes don't take the bait and use a setup move, Gengar can punish them with Encore.

  • Encore: Gengar's excellent speed makes it an especially disruptive user of Encore, being able to disrupt key threats such as Garchomp and Dragonite.

  • Icy Wind: Icy Wind's Speed control can give Gengar the upper hand against fast Focus Sash leads such as Flutter Mane, and lets Gengar outspeed faster threats that it may want to Destiny Bond, such as Meowscarada.

  • Thunder Wave: Thunder Wave is great at crippling faster sweepers if Gengar's Focus Sash is intact, and punishing fast, common switch-ins such as Roaring Moon.

  • Sludge Bomb: This covers Meowscarada and Fairy-types, in addition to being Gengar's most powerful attack.

  • Dazzling Gleam In addition to OHKOing Hydreigon after Stealth Rock damage, Dazzling Gleam is an appealing secondary STAB move when using Tera Fairy.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast is Gengar's best shot at beating Kingambit outside of Destiny Bond.

Other Options

  • Will-O-Wisp Gengar does a great job of burning bulky sweepers that Gengar can be forced to Destiny Bond against, such as Dragonite, Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Tera Annihilape.

Tera Types

  • Normal: Tera Normal Gengar can turn slower Ghost-types such as Mimikyu, Flutter Mane, and Annihilape into easy Encore targets.

  • Fairy: A Dragon-type immunity gives Gengar new Encore targets and better threatens Dragon-types.

  • Flying: Earthquake is a common attack against Gengar, so Tera Flying can turn the tables effectively. It also takes advantage of common Fissure users such as Dondozo and Garganacl.

  • Dark: A Dark Tera type lets Gengar surprise Espathra, letting it Encore Stored Power and potentially ruin its sweep.

Sheer Force.description: Gengar makes for an amazing wallbreaker, breaking through offensive threats like Gholdengo, Great Tusk, and Enamorus-T, as well as having a decent Speed tier. Focus Blast hits Dark-types that try to switch in such as Chien-Pao and Roaring Moon as well as Steel-types such as Heatran and Hisuian Goodra. Nasty Plot turns Gengar into a threatening wallbreaker, allowing it to 2HKO RegenVest Hisuian Goodra and Manaphy with its coverage options. Sludge Wave hits Fairy- and Grass-types like Enamorus-T, Hisuian Electrode, and Ogerpon-W. Energy Ball hits Ground-types like Swampert and Great Tusk, while Thunderbolt hits non-Volt Absorb Corviknight and Mandibuzz. Gengar is great at threatening physical walls like Corviknight and Deoxys-D, so it partners well with physical wallbreakers like Galarian Zapdos and Chien-Pao; in return, they can pressure special walls that Gengar struggles to break through like Hisuian Goodra and Blissey. Due to Gengar's frailty, it struggles against faster threats such as Azelf, Roaring Moon, and Chien-Pao, so defensive switch-ins to them like Mandibuzz, Great Tusk, and Intimidate Corviknight make for good partners. Gengar greatly appreciates Knock Off support from Pokemon like Swampert, Manaphy, and Deoxys-D to remove Assault Vest from RegenVest Pokemon such as Swampert, Hisuian Goodra, and Meloetta, allowing it to have an easier time breaking past the opposing team.

Normalize.description: Normalize Gengar not only threatens to remove opposing RegenVest pivots, often the best check to more conventional Gengar sets, but also reliably sets Toxic Spikes and wins one-on-one against slower setup threats like Swords Dance Iron Hands and Calm Mind Cresselia. Mean Look in conjunction with Skill Swap traps and removes opposing specially defensive walls like Swampert, Manaphy, and Empoleon that are aiming to check it. Skill Swap also reliably forces out and generates a free turn against any Pokemon slower than Gengar such as Sandy Shocks and Beads of Ruin Walking Wake, as they will be unable to hit it through Normalize. This makes Gengar one of the most reliable Toxic Spikes setters, as it threatens most common removal options like Corviknight and Great Tusk. Gengar is an excellent teammate for fast special cleaners like Azelf, Deoxys-S, and Iron Moth, as they benefit tremendously from opposing special walls being removed or weakened with Toxic Spikes. Gengar struggles against teams with fast Dark-types like Roaring Moon, Meowscarada, and Chien-Pao, as it cannot meaningfully damage them and is immensely threatened by them, making Pokemon like Fluffy Corviknight and physically defensive Manaphy great partners; they can also provide a slow pivot to get Gengar in safely. Weather Ball from Pokemon with Primordial Sea or Desolate Land bypasses Normalize, meaning Gengar cannot reliably force out common users like Walking Wake and Volcanion, so sturdy checks to them like RegenVest Swampert and Blissey make solid teammates.

Choiced Attacker (Ghost).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Pivot.description:
Hisuian Electrode is an effective pivot in PU thanks to its incredible Speed stat that lets it outspeed the entire unboosted tier, great STAB combination, and useful utility options. It is so fast that it is not reliant on Choice Scarf, allowing Hisuian Electrode to find a niche over its most direct competitor, Rotom-Mow. Leaf Storm is generally preferred as its Grass-type STAB move, allowing Hisuian Electrode to OHKO specially defensive Palossand and Mudsdale after slight chip damage, though Giga Drain can be opted for instead, sacrificing power for the lack of Special Attack drop and marginal amounts of recovery. Hisuian Taunt is most common in the fourth moveslot to prevent setup attempts from Pokemon like Florges and Scrafty as well as preventing entry hazards from being set up from the likes of Alolan Sandslash and Uxie. Foul Play is another option that OHKOes Hoopa in addition to picking off weakened boosting sweepers like post-Tera Rhydon and chipping Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro, but its usefulness is low otherwise. Tera Ghost is a valuable Tera type utility-wise, allowing Hisuian Electrode to emergency check Normal- and Fighting-type attacks such as Ambipom's Fake Out and Pawmot's Mach Punch. Tera Steel guards Hisuian Electrode from being revenge killed by Choice Scarf Bruxish, though it doesn't offer much else utility. Soundproof lets Hisuian Electrode wall Galvantula and block Psychic Noise from threats like Florges and Hoopa, but this is typically far less useful than Aftermath's consistent chip damage against physical attackers.

Hisuian Electrode finds itself primarily on balance teams looking for a strong form of natural speed control. Hisuian Electrode's ability to directly threaten Pokemon like Mudsdale, Milotic, and Bombirdier and use them as pivoting potential enables partners like Paldean Tauros-F, Arcanine, and Rhydon to set up and break through teams. In return, these three can deal with Pokemon Hisuian Electrode can't handle on its own, like Alolan Sandslash and Galarian Slowbro. Other offensive pivots like Galarian Articuno, Bruxish, and Ambipom can create a fast and strong VoltTurn core with Hisuian Electrode that can be difficult to stop. Even with Tera Fire, Hisuian Electrode can often struggle to break through Grass- and Steel-types like Venusaur, Wo-Chien, and Magneton; counters to these threats like Goodra, Pawmot, and Paldean Tauros-F thus make great partners.

Offensive Pivot (SpA).description:
Hisuian Electrode is a strong pivot that utilizes its high Speed and decent STAB combination to chip away at and eventually break through opposing teams. Thunderbolt provides a consistent source of damage, while Leaf Storm acts like a nuke against neutral targets and Ground-types looking to block Volt Switch such as Landorus. Tera Blast Ice nails Grass- and Dragon-type Pokemon like Hydrapple and Eternatus for super effective damage, while Tera Blast Fire hits Zacian-C, Iron Treads, and specially defensive Excadrill. Volt Switch is Hisuian Electrode's most spammable move, allowing it to pivot out and maintain momentum against checks such as Kyurem-W and Galarian Slowking. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Hisuian Electrode to safely pivot on and off the field throughout the game.

Hisuian Electrode best fits on teams looking for a strong, special attacking pivot. However, a high Special Attack god like Kyurem-W or Eternatus is required to allow it to actually make progress. Hisuian Electrode pairs well with other offensive pivots such as Landorus-T, Meowscarada, and Hisuian Samurott, as they can chip away at each other's checks. Meowscarada in particular is helpful, as Triple Axel nukes the aforementioned Grass- and Dragon-types that wall Hisuian Electrode, allowing it to comfortably run Tera Fire over Tera Ice. Alternatively, slower pivots such as Pecharunt, Corviknight, and Mandibuzz are helpful in bringing Hisuian Electrode onto the field safely, circumventing its relative frailty. Hisuian Electrode also appreciates powerful physical attackers such as Great Tusk and Weavile, as they are able to break special walls such as Eternatus and Galarian Slowking. Lastly, entry hazard setters like Skarmory, Clefable, and Landorus-T are helpful, as they let Hisuian Electrode's constant pivoting force chip damage onto its checks, allowing it to beat them long-term.

Magic Guard.description: Hisuian Electrode is a great offensive pivot thanks to its amazing Speed, access to Volt Switch, and powerful STAB Chloroblast for Ground-types like Swampert, Great Tusk, and Sandy Shocks. Thunder Wave cripples switch-ins like Roaring Moon, Hisuian Goodra, and Ogerpon-H, potentially letting Hisuian Electrode's teammates outspeed and threaten them, while Leech Seed lets it chip down walls such as Blissey and Hisuian Goodra and heal. Worry Seed removes Volt Absorb from walls like Corviknight and Empoleon and Regenerator from Hisuian Goodra and Meloetta, letting it chip the latter two, especially with entry hazards on the field. Hisuian Electrode forms a great VoltTurn core with other offensive pivots like Barraskewda, Roaring Moon, and Slither Wing, as they can bring it in on physical walls like Corviknight and Great Tusk, and it can bring them in on special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Meloetta. Entry hazard setters like Heatran, Scream Tail, and Deoxys-D are great teammates thanks to hazards wearing down Hisuian Electrode's switch-ins like Roaring Moon, Hisuian Goodra, and Heatran; in return, it can threaten common hazard removers like Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Mandibuzz. Hisuian Electrode struggles to break through specially defensive walls like Blissey, Hisuian Goodra, and Meloetta, so physical wallbreakers like Ceruledge and Galarian Zapdos are appreciated. Hisuian Electrode is also frail and has a middling defensive typing, so slow, bulky pivots that can take a hit and safely pivot it in like Corviknight and Swampert make good partners.

Tank.description:
Koffing establishes itself as an excellent physical tank in Little Cup due to its high base Defense stat and Poison typing, which let it check physical attackers like Mienfoo and Timburr. Koffing's best use comes from its ability Neutralizing Gas, which has useful applications, such as denying Mienfoo and Foongus recovery from Regenerator, preventing Snivy from gaining a Special Attack boost from Leaf Storm with Contrary, and denying Hisuian Growlithe the ability to avoid recoil from Head Smash and Flare Blitz. Thunderbolt gives Koffing an option to hit Vullaby and Mareanie for super effective damage. Will-O-Wisp can weaken physical attackers that may switch into Koffing such as Mudbray and Trapinch. Pain Split is Koffing's only good recovery option. Fire Blast can be used over Will-O-Wisp or Pain Split to hit Steel-types and Foongus super effectively. Koffing's EV spread allows it to leverage its already high Defense stat and boost its attacks, letting it 2HKO Pokemon like Foongus with Sludge Bomb if its Eviolite is removed. Koffing uses Tera Water, as it's a generally good defensive type, and it additionally lets Koffing take minimal damage from Shellder's Icicle Spear.

Teammates that appreciate Koffing's presence include Mudbray, as Koffing can check Snivy, which can come in easily against Mudbray. Pawniard also makes use of Koffing's ability to deny Mienfoo's Regenerator, making it easier to remove it for Pawniard. Koffing struggles against Glimmet and Hisuian Growlithe, as neither are threatened by any of Koffing's attacks. Mudbray is a good teammate, as it can switch in to both Pokemon and scare them out with Earthquake. Additionally, Gothita can assist Koffing with Glimmet due to Shadow Tag, letting it trap Glimmet for Koffing.

nfe.comments:
Other Options

While Levitate allow Koffing to wall offensive Ground-types like Gabite, it comes at the cost of Koffing's critically important ability to absorb opposing Toxic Spikes as a grounded Poison-type and various interactions that Neutralizing Gas makes favorable. Toxic is great at making progress and preferable against Dunsparce and special attackers, but it renders Koffing even more passive against Steel-types.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Tinkatuff and Hisuian Sliggoo both wall Koffing and are not immediately deterred by Will-O-Wisp, freely able to set Stealth Rock or start wallbreaking.

Psychic-types: Girafarig and Duosion are both extremely immediately threatening to Koffing and can potentially sweep if given free turns to set up. Duosion is particularly fearsome as it is unaffected by the passive damage from Toxic Spikes due to Magic Guard once Koffing is forced out. RestTalk Hattrem is comfortable switching into Koffing and healing off status damage while threatening to use its STAB moves or Nuzzle.

Ghost-types: Drakloak commonly run Night Shade and status sets, which commonly lets it win against Koffing due to its low HP and special bulk. While rare, Lampent is also a nightmare to deal with thanks to its strong special attacks and Flash Fire turning Will-O-Wisp into a beneficial effect.

Special Wallbreakers: Pikachu and Choice Specs users like Frogadier, Drakloak, and Hisuian Sliggoo all threaten enormous damage on Koffing and are difficult for its teammates to switch into.

Defensive.description:
Thanks to its typing and exceptional physical bulk, Koffing is a great defensive glue and the premier Toxic Spikes setter of the metagame. Sludge Bomb is Koffing's best STAB option and its high chance to poison can punish common switch-ins like Girafarig and Drakloak. Will-O-Wisp prevents attackers like Pawniard and Coil Dunsparce from setting up on Koffing and puts Steel-types like Tinkatuff and Hisuian Sliggoo on a timer. Toxic Spikes creates extreme pressure against most team structures due to the limited usage Heavy-Duty Boots sees. Thief turns Koffing into a Knock Off absorber and allows it to steal back Eviolite. Flamethrower gives a more direct way to punish Steel-type switch-ins. Neutralizing Gas allows Koffing to bypass Magic Guard and Magic Bounce from Clefairy and Hattrem respectively, use Thief on Tinkatuff without Pickpocket activating, and induce status effects on Naclstack.

Koffing fits best on slower balance or stall archetypes that create longer games, need more long-term answers to threats like Thwackey, and get more value from Toxic Spikes's incremental damage. Drakloak is essential to block spinners like Quaxwell and Wartortle. Steel-types like Tinkatuff and Hisuian Sliggoo can halt special wallbreakers like Girafarig and Frogadier that pose big threats once let in. Koffing's best defensive trait is that it walls common Grass-types like Servine, Ivysaur, and especially Thwackey. Therefore, wallbreakers that can make immediate progress but let those in for free like Piloswine, Wartortle, and Drakloak are all most appreciative of its defensive utility. Lastly, bulkier wincons like Duosion and Dunsparce really appreciate Toxic Spikes's passive damage as it eases setup for them and makes them even harder to keep checked.

zu.overview: With its incredible physical bulk, great typing, and ability, Weezing serves as an excellent physical wall. Its Poison typing gives it a resistance to Fighting-type attacks, making it an incredible check to Fighting-types, such as Virizion and Primeape. Its bulk allows it to easily spread status through Will-O-Wisp and Sludge Bomb, making Weezing incredibly irritating to switch into. However, Weezing lacks any reliable recovery, making it easy to wear down over the course of a game. Its mediocre special bulk means it folds to any strong special attack.
zu.comments:
Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Weezing's lacking Special Defense makes it susceptible to any strong neutral attack from the likes of Charizard, Clawitzer, and Jolteon. However, Sludge Bomb's nasty poison chance makes it hard to repeatedly switch these attackers in.

Residual Damage: As tanky as Weezing is, its lack of reliable recovery leaves it prone to being overwhelmed, especially in longer games versus bulkier teams. Strong attacks can easily bypass Pain Split's weak healing, leaving Weezing vulnerable to being forced past by attackers like Sneasel and Dodrio.

Psychic-types: Mesprit can easily switch in on Weezing, only fearing Sludge Bomb's poison chance, threaten it out, and use it to set entry hazards, pivot with U-turn, set up Substitute or boosts, or do any other of the million things it does. Farigiraf can also easily enter on Weezing and start boosting. Less common Psychic-types like Malamar, Indeedee-F, and Veluza still scare Weezing out with super effective Psychic-type attacks and use it to force progress throughout the game, though none of them enjoy being poisoned or burned.

Physical Wall.description:
Sludge Bomb's poison chance makes it the preferred attack of choice, threatening otherwise safe switches like Mesprit and Cryogonal with uncomfortable chip damage. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers and spreads chip damage on common switch-ins like Muk and Mesprit. Pain Split gives Weezing some staying power and helps it stick around in longer games. Haze denies setup sweepers like Swords Dance Virizion. Taunt messes with defensive foes, denying attempts at setting entry hazards, spreading status, and recovery. Toxic Spikes messes with grounded Pokemon like Regirock and is great into bulkier teams. Rocky Helmet chips away at physical attackers using contact moves. Levitate lets Weezing hover over Spikes as well as Ground-type moves, letting it ignore Earthquake from Primeape and Sandaconda. Tera Steel makes Weezing resist Psychic-type attacks from Mespirit and Farigiraf, as well as a ton of other types like Flying, Normal, and Ice, making it a better check to many physical attackers like Dodrio and Beartic. However, Tera Steel makes Weezing weak to Fighting-type attacks, reducing its effectiveness as a check to Fighting-types like Hitmontop and Primeape.

Balance teams can tend to struggle against the many strong Fighting-types like Primeape, so Weezing is a great fit on these teams to take this pressure off its teammates. Because of this, Fighting-weak partners like Sneasel appreciate Weezing's presence. Beartic is another wallbreaker that balance teams struggle with, and Weezing can help its team dance around it. As Weezing can't take special hits very well, special walls like Cryogonal and Orthworm are helpful for sponging the special attacks aimed at Weezing. Orthworm coincidentally form a powerful defensive core with Weezing, with Weezing covering Fighting-types for Orthworm. Offensive threats like Beartic and Sneasel appreciate having Weezing to fall back on against would-be revenge killers like Primeape.

Physically Defensive (Poison).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Utility.description:
Galarian Weezing combines a fantastic defensive typing, solid defensive stats, and its unique ability to support the OU tier through reliable entry hazard removal. It can use Defog to remove hazards against even Gholdengo due to Neutralizing Gas suppressing Good as Gold. Will-O-Wisp furthers Galarian Weezing's physical sturdiness while statusing otherwise immune foes such as Garganacl, Gholdengo, and Hatterene. Pain Split is Galarian Weezing's primary method of recovery, as even with full investment, its measly base 65 HP stat allows it to usually heal up in front of foes such as Alomomola and Corviknight. On sets with Leftovers, Protect can be used instead to secure an additional turn of healing, as well as leverage Neutralizing Gas to the fullest extent against Pokemon greatly annoyed by it, such as Gliscor and Clefable. Galarian Weezing has a great deal of flexibility for its last move, but Sludge Bomb is generally preferred because it is a solid attack into Ogerpon-W, Iron Valiant, and Rillaboom. Strange Steam is an alternative attack to hit Great Tusk, Kyurem, and Darkrai harder and enjoys the upside of free turns given via confusion. Other alternatives include Toxic Spikes to pressure teams without reliable hazard removal or a Poison-type and Toxic to offer a higher damage status option to more quickly put down dangerous threats to Galarian Weezing's team, such as Ceruledge and Hatterene. Galarian Weezing usually opts for a fully defensive spread to best cover dangerous threats such as Ogerpon-W, Zamazenta, and Dragonite, as it can tank a hit from them while threatening back a crippling burn. However, on teams that need help covering Kingambit, a spread of 252 HP / 80 Def / 176 Spe with a Bold nature can be used to outspeed Adamant Kingambit, allowing Galarian Weezing to usually get off a burn and cripple it. Galarian Weezing typically prefers to Terastallize into the Grass-type, as this resists Ogerpon-W's STAB attacks in a pinch as well as turning Galarian Weezing's Ground-type weakness into a resistance. However, Tera Ghost is also popular to block opposing hazard removal such as Great Tusk's Rapid Spin and match up better into Ursaluna and Dragonite, and Tera Flying can also be used to gain a full immunity to incoming Ground-type attacks such as Landorus-T's Earth Power. Heavy-Duty Boots are usually favored to give Galarian Weezing easier entry against the hazards it wants to remove. However, on teams with secondary hazard removal, Leftovers can be used to help Galarian Weezing stay healthier, while Rocky Helmet can be employed to punish contact moves such as Alomomola's Flip Turn, Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge, and Corviknight's U-turn.

Teams looking for the most reliable entry hazard removal in the tier will find Galarian Weezing to be an invaluable teammate. Balance and Stall teams in particular appreciate this support, as well as Galarian Weezing's ability to help contain the ever-terrifying Ogerpon-W. Corviknight is a standout teammate on both playstyles, switching into Ground-type attacks such as Great Tusk's Headlong Rush and Psychic-type attacks such as Deoxys-S's Psycho Boost. Moreover, Corviknight and Galarian Weezing also complement each other by both being able to clear hazards, forcing teams to contend with both threatening to undo progress via Defog. This consistent hazard removal greatly enables balance teams by allowing Rock-weak wallbreakers such as Kyurem and Nasty Plot Tornadus-T to flourish. Stall teams also greatly enjoy the support Corviknight and Galarian Weezing provide, allowing Pokemon such as Blissey, Dondozo, and Toxapex to use Leftovers instead of Heavy-Duty Boots. Alomomola is another great teammate for Galarian Weezing, as it is bulky enough to confidently switch into threatening Ground-type and Steel-type attacks and compensate for Galarian Weezing's limited recovery options via Wish. Assault Vest Alomomola also greatly appreciates Galarian Weezing's prowess at removing hazards. Balance and bulky offense teams also appreciate Galarian Weezing keeping hazards off to give their powerful breakers, such as Ogerpon-W and Choice Specs Raging Bolt, more opportunities to safely enter the field and make progress. These teams also value Galarian Weezing suppressing Regenerator on common pivots like Alomomola and Galarian Slowking, so attackers that struggle with these such as Dragapult and Zamazenta will appreciate this additional offensive pressure. Galarian Weezing broadly fears strong special attackers such as Gholdengo, Glimmora, and Iron Moth, as these do not particularly fear getting burned and can target Galarian Weezing's poor Special Defense. Ting-Lu is therefore an excellent partner to answer these threats by soaking up most special attacks in the tier; in particular, it easily absorbs any incoming Psychic-type attacks that Galarian Weezing would be weak to. In return, Galarian Weezing can answer Rillaboom, Ogerpon, and Hisuian Samurott that trouble Ting-Lu. Lastly, limited recovery options can force Galarian Weezing to get worn down over a match as it repeatedly removes hazards, so other teammates that can help shoulder the burden, such as Great Tusk and Iron Treads, will help take the pressure off Galarian Weezing and keep it healthy.

Physically Defensive (Poison).description:
Galarian Weezing serves a pivotal defensive role for Poison teams due to its solid support movepool and vital immunities to Dragon- and Ground-type attacks courtesy of its Fairy typing and Levitate, allowing it to wall otherwise problematic threats such as Swords Dance Garchomp, Great Tusk, and Dragonite. Strange Steam pressures Dragon-, ​Fighting-, and Dark-types like Roaring Moon, Iron Hands, and Sableye. Defog clears away entry hazards for teammates like Iron Moth and Alolan Muk, preventing them from getting worn down. Pain Split enables Galarian Weezing to stay healthy long term while siphoning HP from bulky walls such as Blissey and Clodsire. Finally, Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers such as Gallade, Hisuian Goodra, and Azumarill. 12 Speed EVs enable Galarian Weezing to outspeed Tyranitar and burn it.

Galarian Weezing greatly appreciates special walls like Alolan Muk, which can handle problematic special attackers such as Flutter Mane, Hatterene, and Greninja. Assault Vest Galarian Slowking can also assist in handling special attackers such as Choice Specs Latios, Heatran, and Zapdos. Toxapex can assist into Steel-, Water-, and Fire-types that Galarian Weezing can struggle with, ​like Scizor, Barraskewda, and Cinderace, ​along with being able to more comfortably take Knock Off from foes like Empoleon and Tornadus-T. Amoonguss can similarly help out against Water-types like Ogerpon-W and Keldeo, alongside being able to handle Ground-types Galarian Weezing struggles with, like Sandy Shocks and Mold Breaker Excadrill. Iron Moth can break through Steel-types such as Gholdengo, Scizor, and Archaludon for Galarian Weezing while appreciating Defog support to prevent it from being worn down. Choice Scarf Sneasler can check threats that switch into Galarian Weezing freely, such as Ogerpon-H, Blissey, and Heatran, while also outspeeding and checking Dark-types like Choice Specs Greninja and Hoopa-U. Okidogi greatly appreciates Galarian Weezing's Will-O-Wisp, enabling it to comfortably set up with Bulk Up; in return, it can check threats like Garganacl, Bisharp, and Terapagos for Galarian Weezing.

Bulky Support.description:
Set Details

  • Galarian Weezing is a great disruptive support Pokemon that can support offensive teams by shutting down the abilities that many teams depend on with Neutralizing Gas. Galarian Weezing has a good matchup against teams that rely on Grimmsnarl to take hits, as it is able to disrupt it with Taunt before it can set up dual screens, allowing powerful partners like Koraidon and Calyrex-S to sweep through teams. Neutralizing Gas also makes it a lot harder for Miraidon and Kyogre, which are quite reliant on their respective field effects, to damage Galarian Weezing's partners.
  • Taunt allows Galarian Weezing to effectively shut down Grimmsnarl, Amoonguss, and Brute Bonnet, as well as preventing the opposing team's Trick Room. Will-O-Wisp can easily cripple physical attackers such as Zamazenta-C, Calyrex-I, and Iron Hands. Toxic Spikes and Poison Gas negate recovery on Terapagos and Calyrex-I while also making it easier for a partner Calyrex-S to clean up a team that has been chipped down. Strange Steam is guaranteed to OHKO Koraidon while getting around Wide Guard, and Dazzling Gleam is a slightly weaker spread option that can consistently chip down enemies. Play Rough is a physical Fairy-type STAB move that allows Galarian Weezing to do much much more damage to Assualt Vest Iron Hands and Miraidon.
  • Covert Cloak prevents Fake Out flinches from Iron Hands, Incineroar, and Rillaboom, allowing it to support its team without being slowed down and making it easier to stop Trick Room. Rocky Helmet does good chip damage to Koraidon, Zamazenta-C, and Iron Hands. It's also useful to break Urshifu-R or Chien-Pao's Focus Sash. Safety Goggles gives Galarian Weezing an immunity to Brute Bonnet and Amoonguss's Spore and Rage Powder.
  • The EVs guarantee Galarian Weezing can survive a Behemoth Bash or Heavy Slam from Zamazenta-C, allowing Galarian Weezing to burn it with Will-O-Wisp. Galarian Weezing is also guaranteed to survive a Choice Specs Miraidon Electro Drift without Terrain, forcing the opponent to double target Galarian Weezing. The Speed investment lets Galarian Weezing outspeed Grimmsnarl and shut down its supportive capabilities with Taunt.
  • Tera Water is used to give Galarian Weezing resistances to Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance, Koraidon's Flare Blitz, and Zamazenta-C's Behemoth Bash and Heavy Slam. Tera Dark grants Galarian Weezing an immunity to Calyrex-S's Psychic and a resistance to its Astral Barrage.

Teambuilding

  • Incineroar, Tornadus, and Flutter Mane can all outspeed Galarian Weezing and use Taunt, reducing its effectiveness on the field. Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade can OHKO Galarian Weezing with a good roll, and its Steel typing gives it a resistance to Dazzling Gleam and Strange Steam as well as an immunity to Poison Gas and Toxic Spikes. Amoonguss can also check Galarian Weezing, as Spore can completely shut it down, and Amoonguss easily shrugs off Strange Steam and Dazzling Gleam while having an immunity to Poison Gas and removing Toxic Spikes on entry.
  • Galarian Weezing is a good partner for Koraidon and Calyrex-S, as it turns off many of the main defensive tools of balance teams. Although Neutralizing Gas forces Koraidon to use the Ability Shield, shutting down Incineroar's Intimidate and Grimmsnarl's Prankster makes it much easier for Koraidon to sweep through teams unchecked. Disabling abilities like Protosynthesis, Quark Drive, and Prankster allows Calyrex-S to outspeed almost everything in the metagame and pressure teams with Astral Barrage. Koraidon is able to heavily threaten Incineroar, Amoonguss, and Zacian-C, while Calyrex-S can help against Flutter Mane.
  • Galarian Weezing pairs well with Dondozo and Tatsugiri, as it is able to spread status with Poison Gas and Toxic Spikes, allowing Dondozo to clean up late-game while taking little damage from foes and healing with Leftovers.

Galarian Weezing benefits its allies by disabling almost all abilities with Neutralizing Gas and spreading poison. It can be used with Pokemon with abilities that cannot be disabled like Calyrex-S and Pokemon with abilities that are not always necessary for them to function such as Iron Hands and Roaring Moon. It works best against Pokemon with abilities that are important to their performance, such as Prankster Whimsicott and Tornadus, and those that boost their damage and set up Terrain or weather to help their team, such as Miraidon, Koraidon, and Kyogre. Dazzling Gleam can be used for reliable damage and to break Focus Sashes while ignoring redirection, but Strange Steam can be used for a higher chance to OHKO Roaring Moon and Koraidon. Toxic Spikes is used to wear down foes over time, allowing Galarian Weezing's partners to easily clean up late-game. Additionally, it works well against teams without a grounded Poison-type like Amoonguss to absorb Toxic Spikes. Poison Gas is best against Pokemon that intend to set up and stay on the field for a while, such as Calm Mind Terapagos, especially since it is a spread move and cannot be redirected, though it can be blocked by Wide Guard. Protect can bait out Fake Out if Covert Cloak is not being used and can stall turns to rack up poison damage. Covert Cloak can ensure Toxic Spikes is set up against Fake Out users, Sitrus Berry improves survivability, and Mental Herb stops Taunt and Encore from disrupting Toxic Spikes and Poison Gas setup. 12 Speed EVs is used to outspeed Farigiraf and Incineroar with low Speed investment. The EVs in Special Defense allow survival of Astral Barrage from Choice Specs Calyrex-S and Water Spout from Mystic Water Kyogre, given that rain is not active. The defensive investment allows for a high chance to survive Precipice Blades from Groudon and guaranteed survival of Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R. Tera Dark gives Galarian Weezing a resistance to Calyrex-S’s STAB attacks. Tera Grass grants an immunity to Spore and turns its weakness to Ground-type attacks such as Landorus-I's Earth Power into a resistance as well as granting a resistance to Electric-type attacks like Electro Drift from Miraidon. Tera Water grants a resistance to Glacial Lance from Calyrex-I.

Faster Taunt users such as Whimsicott shut down the status options of Galarian Weezing without Mental Herb, and sets without Sitrus Berry are vulnerable to high damage from double targeting. Poison-types such as Amoonguss wall Galarian Weezing and absorb Toxic Spikes, preventing it from inflicting poison. Since Galarian Weezing typically cannot deal immediate damage, it relies on its teammates to win games, and it will often lose late-game against offensive Pokemon. Galarian Weezing is often partnered with Calyrex-S because its As One ability is unaffected by Neutralizing Gas. Additionally, Galarian Weezing is commonly paired with Dondozo and Tatsugiri, as a Commander-boosted Dondozo can sweep teams that have been weakened by poison damage, and it can effectively stall out poison damage by using Protect and recovering from Leftovers. Fighting-type teammates like Urshifu-R and Iron Hands can take advantage of Terapagos's Tera Shell being disabled to OHKO it with Close Combat. Indeedee-F supports these teams by providing redirection and providing Psychic-type offense on its own. Ogerpon-C can use Follow Me to guarantee Galarian Weezing's Toxic Spikes setup. Roaring Moon can threaten Psychic-types with Knock Off and provide Tailwind for the team.

Defensive.description:
Galarian Weezing establishes a niche for itself over other defensive Poison-types thanks to its two unique and potentially very useful abilities. Neutralizing Gas and Levitate give Galarian Weezing two very interesting defensive niches that teams can explore, although its lack of reliable recovery proves to be a significant hinderance in practice. Strange Steam is the preferred STAB move, as it has good neutral coverage and can potentially harass foes with confusion. Will-O-Wisp allows Galarian Weezing to impair physical attackers like Ogerpon-W, Landorus-T, and Hisuian Samurott. Pain Split is Galarian Weezing's only form of recovery, albeit the flawed nature of the move makes it much less consistent than the options available to its competitors. Defog allows Galarian Weezing to remove entry hazards set by the likes of Hisuian Samurott, Ferrothorn, and Kommo-o. Flamethrower allows Galarian Weezing to severely pressure Ferrothorn and potentially catch Steel-types like Mega Scizor, Melmetal, and Kartana as they switch in. Toxic Spikes is a rare move in National Dex, so Galarian Weezing can potentially use them to seriously irritate foes such as Garchomp, Ogerpon-W, and Urshifu-R. Galarian Weezing's two viable abilities are the main reason to run it, and both have very different benefits that change the way it plays and the kind of teams that it fits on. Neutralizing Gas grants Galarian Weezing several very unique benefits, such as using Defog against or burning Gholdengo switching in; denying Regenerator from common Pokemon like Alomomola, Toxapex, and Galarian Slowking; and enabling setup of Toxic Spikes against Mega Diancie and Hatterene switch-ins. On the other hand, Levitate allows Galarian Weezing to become immune to Spikes and counter several dangerous Ground-types, such as Garchomp, Landorus-T, and Great Tusk. Black Sludge gives Galarian Weezing some passive recovery, allowing it to mitigate its lack of reliable recovery as much as possible. It is used over Leftovers to mess with Trick users such as Gholdengo and Iron Valiant. Heavy-Duty Boots can be used on Neutralizing Gas variants to mitigate Galarian Weezing's vulnerability to Spikes. Rocky Helmet is an option to punish contact moves from the likes of Urshifu-R, Landorus-T, and Mega Lopunny, although it noticeably impacts Galarian Weezing's already mediocre longevity.

The types of teams that Galarian Weezing fits on depends largely on its choice of ability. Neutralizing Gas is a great option for bulky balance and stall teams that appreciate Galarian Weezing's ability to harass several Pokemon that often give balance teams trouble, such as Gholdengo, Gliscor, and Alomomola. These teams are well equipped to shore up its poor longevity and accommodate for its Ground-type weakness. Teammates such as Landorus-T, Ferrothorn, and Gholdengo are common on bulky balance teams and appreciate Galarian Weezing's ability to help them check Fighting-types that can sometimes overwhelm them in addition to the benefits that Neutralizing Gas provides. The aforementioned Ground-type weakness requires good Ground-immune teammates such as Gliscor, Moltres, and Celesteela to help out Galarian Weezing. Wish passers like Alomomola can help mitigate Galarian Weezing's lack of a reliable recovery move. Teammates vulnerable to entry hazards, such as Mega Scizor, Zapdos, and Ting-Lu, appreciate how Neutralizing Gas Galarian Weezing can absorb Toxic Spikes and use Defog even in the face of a potential Gholdengo switch-in. Although they still work on balance teams, Levitate variants of Galarian Weezing can also fit on more offensive builds, which don't mind Galarian Weezing's lack of reliable recovery but appreciate the unique defensive profile that it provides. Galarian Weezing countering most Ground- and Fighting-types in one slot frees up these teams considerably. Steel-types have excellent defensive synergy with Levitate Galarian Weezing, as they appreciate it dealing with Ground- and Fighting-types while assisting it with problematic Psychic-types. Gholdengo, Heatran, and Melmetal can help out against Psychic-types like Tapu Lele and Mega Latios, while they love Galarian Weezing switching into Great Tusk, Mega Lopunny, and Landorus-T. A Dragon-type, such as Mega Latios, Raging Bolt, or Dragonite, is a good partner as well, as it helps out with Galarian Weezing's weakness to strong special attacking Fire-types such as Heatran and Mega Charizard Y while also assisting with Ogerpon-W, which Galarian Weezing is a shaky check to. Slower offensive Pokemon that can be revenge killed by common Ground- and Fighting-types make for good partners for Levitate Galarian Weezing. Raging Bolt, Kingambit, and Gholdengo are good teammates as a result.

Physically Defensive (Poison).description: Galarian Weezing serves as a strong defensive piece for Poison teams thanks to its strong supportive movepool and incredible immunities provided by its Fairy typing and Levitate, enabling it to comfortably take on threats such as Swords Dance Garchomp, Dragonite, and Ting-Lu. Strange Steam allows Galarian Weezing to pressure Dark- and Dragon-types like Mega Sableye, Roaring Moon, and Dragonite. Defog clears away entry hazards for teammates such as Alolan Muk and Mega Venusaur, preventing them from getting worn down. Pain Split can keep Galarian Weezing healthy by siphoning HP away from foes such as Blissey and Ting-Lu. Finally, Will-O-Wisp can be used to shut down physical attackers like Iron Treads and Iron Hands. Mega Venusaur pairs particularly well with Galarian Weezing, with Leech Seed being able to make up for Galarian Weezing occasionally lacking self-preservation while also checking Water- and Ground-type threats such as Mega Swampert, Keldeo, and Iron Treads that can overwhelm it. Toxapex can similarly help against Water-types like Urshifu-R and check Steel-types such as Scizor and Celesteela and Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y with Scald and Toxic. Alolan Muk provides a special wall capable of handling Psychic- and Ghost-types that can easily threaten Galarian Weezing such as Tapu Lele, Blacephalon, and Hisuian Zoroark by trapping them with Pursuit. Assault Vest Galarian Slowking can check special attackers for Galarian Weezing like Zapdos, Latios, and Kyurem. Choice Scarf Sneasler can outspeed and handle Steel-type threats such as Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and Heatran along with checking other problematic threats such as Hisuian Arcanine and Ursaluna. Nidoking can break through Poison- and Steel-types like Toxapex and Gholdengo that use Galarian Weezing as free entry while also checking Electric-types like Raging Bolt and Regieleki.

Stealth Rock.description:
Megahorn can be used over Swords Dance to smash Wo-Chien. Rhydon can invest in Speed to move before slower foes like uninvested Hariyama, though it doesn't gain much from doing so and loses out on some of its bulk this way.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

nu.overview: Chansey stands out as the ultimate special wall in the tier, with its gargantuan bulk further boosted by Eviolite allowing it to tank many special attacks from foes like Raikou, Munkidori, Chandelure, and non-Body Press Duraludon. Chansey is a key component on stall teams, as it tanks special moves for its teammates while having great support utility. It has access to Stealth Rock to set entry hazards; Heal Bell to remove annoying status effects like poison from Toxic Chain Munkidori and Bellibolt, Will-O-Wisp from defensive Altaria, and paralysis from the likes of Bellibolt and Scream Tail; and Natural Cure to remove status for itself. However, due to its reliance on Eviolite, Chansey is vulnerable to hazards, so it is easily chipped over time. Moreover, Chansey is extremely passive, with its only reliable attacking move being Seismic Toss, resulting in easy setup opportunities for special sweepers such as Galarian Articuno and Chandelure, as well as physical sweepers that can take advantage of it such as Decidueye and Incineroar. Chansey also struggles to include all its moveslot choices, as it has trouble slotting in Shadow Ball to hit Ghost-types and Thunder Wave to spread paralysis on the same set.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Healing Wish is an option to fully heal a teammate that can be vital late-game but is very niche. Ice Beam gives it a solid option to hit Ground- and Flying-types like Flygon, Gligar, and Scyther. Tera Steel gives Chansey a Psychic resistance against Pokemon such as Munkidori and Espeon, while Tera Dragon can be used over Steel, allowing Chansey to better handle Water- and Fire-types such as Inteleon, Basculegion-M, and Chandelure.

Checks and Counters

Physical Attackers: Strong physical attackers such as Decidueye, Basculegion-M, Scyther, and Flamigo can do major damage against Chansey, forcing a switch or freely setting up for a sweep. However, none of them enjoy switching into Thunder Wave, and the former two dislike getting hit by Shadow Ball.

Fighting-types and Fighting-type Coverage: Fighting-types such as Flamigo, physical Infernape, and Paldean Tauros-W can pressure Chansey with strong Fighting-type attacks. However, all of them must be cautious about switching into its Thunder Wave while not getting chipped down by Seismic Toss. Special attackers such as Duraludon and Assault Vest Reuniclus can put dents in Chansey and force it to heal due to their access to Body Press and Focus Blast, respectively.

Setup Sweepers: Setup sweepers that have access to recovery such as Calm Mind Reuniclus, Galarian Articuno, and Chandelure can use Chansey as fodder, and the former two can either prevent it from healing thanks to Psychic Noise or outright OHKO it with Psyshock. Other setup sweepers like Double Dance Bronzong and Substitute Meloetta can beat Chansey one-on-one due to it relying on Seismic Toss to do any type of damage.

Item Removal: Knock Off users such as Incineroar, Assault Vest Reuniclus, and Copperajah are threats to Chansey because they can remove its Eviolite, reducing its bulk. Trick users like Munkidori, Chandelure, and Meloetta can also often cripple Chansey by giving it their Choice items.

Entry Hazards: Chansey is required to hold Eviolite to boost its bulk instead of running Heavy-Duty Boots. As a consequence, it can be worn down by entry hazards repeatedly on each switch in.

Defensive.description:
Set Details

Seismic Toss prevents Chansey from being completely passive by dealing reliable, consistent damage against non-Ghost-type targets. Heal Bell allows Chansey to cure status ailments for team members like Houndstone. Thunder Wave enables Chansey’s teammates like Basculegion-M and Flamigo to cripple faster foes like Paldean Tauros-W, Munkidori, and Chandelure, which is especially useful on bulky teams reliant on paralysis and Toxic poison to deal with such threats. Alternatively, the combination of Shadow Ball and Calm Mind provides solid coverage against Ghost-types like Decidueye and Chandelure that would wall Chansey while better handling any Calm Mind attempts from Reuniclus, Galarian Articuno, and Sylveon. The mixed defensive EV spread allows Chansey to have better special bulk while minimizing damage from physical moves that could chip it down and should be run on sets lacking Calm Mind. Alternatively, the physically defensive EV spread supports Calm Mind + Shadow Ball sets in setting up. Tera Dark gives Chansey a Psychic immunity for Psyshock, Psychic Noise, and Stored Power from Reuniclus, Meloetta, and Galarian Articuno, while Tera Fairy offers Chansey a better defensive typing that allows it to better handle Pokemon like Flygon, Paldean Tauros-W, and Incineroar. Alternatively, Tera Ghost boosts the power of Shadow Ball while providing a Fighting immunity to help against Pokemon such as Toxicroak, Infernape, and Paldean Tauros-W.

Chansey pairs with other stall staples such as Gligar, Scream Tail, Houndstone, and Altaria that handle Fighting-types like Flamigo and Paldean Tauros-F. In particular, Gligar synergizes greatly with Chansey, as the former handles wallbreakers like Flamigo and Flygon while offering great utility in the form of Knock Off to remove held items from Incineroar and Toxic to cripple Pokemon like Galarian Articuno and Houndstone. In return, Chansey handles special attackers like Chandelure, Inteleon, and Sylveon that force Gligar to use up its Tera. Chansey also appreciates partners such as Static Belibolt and Rocky Helmet Galarian Slowbro that can deal with pivot spam cores consisting of foes like Flamigo and Grafaiai. Steel-types like Copperajah and Duraludon can handle Pokemon such as Munkidori and Galarian Articuno while allowing Chansey to forgo Stealth Rock in favor of another move. Chansey also benefits from entry hazard stack support due to its relative passivity, appreciating partners like Spikes Gligar and Brambleghast and Stealth Rock Bronzong to wear down Pokemon like Choice Specs Chandelure and Paldean Tauros-W. Due to Chansey's reliance on Eviolite, hazard removal options like Tsareena, Avalugg, Brambleghast, and Altaria prevent it from getting worn down. Knock Off absorbers like Scream Tail and Houndstone, which are also good switch-ins to Fighting-types, are necessary partners. Secondary special walls like Bronzong and Goodra can prevent Chansey from being overwhelmed by special wallbreakers, with the latter especially having utility such as Dragon Tail, Knock Off, and Toxic. Dark-types such as Incineroar and Scrafty can help take on Ghost-types like Choice Specs Chandelure, Decidueye, and Basculegion-M that Chansey struggles with if lacking Shadow Ball.

Pink Blob:2.description: With its enormous bulk due to one of the largest HP stats in the game alongside Eviolite, Chansey is the premier special wall for bulky teams looking to stifle the tier's most threatening special attackers, namely Iron Moth, Enamorus, and Hydreigon. Seismic Toss is Chansey's most reliable way of dealing damage, letting it punish Toxic-immune targets like Iron Moth and Mega Venusaur while also ensuring Substitute users like Hydreigon and Enamorus cannot use Chansey as setup fodder. Soft-Boiled provides instant reliable recovery, but Wish alongside Protect is an option to grant Chansey increased recovery PP while also potentially passing massive Wishes to teammates. However, this comes at the cost of being more exploitable, as threats like Galarian Moltres and Thundurus can use Nasty Plot on forced Protect turns. Toxic restricts special sweepers like Calm Mind Enamorus and Mega Latias while also punishing physical attackers that switch in to threaten Chansey like Buzzwole and Tyranitar. Thunder Wave is an alternative on bulky teams that are less capable of handling setup sweepers like Iron Moth to allow teammates like Keldeo to outspeed and KO them before they can retaliate. Given the number of opportunities Chansey gets to switch in, Stealth Rock is a great move for it, but Aromatherapy can be used on teams with another entry hazard setter to keep the team free from status. Given its weakness to hazards as well as its passivity, Chansey is typically only seen on stall and bulky teams. Chansey can struggle with many of the tier's most common physical attackers, particularly Tyranitar and Buzzwole, so teammates like Hippowdon and Skarmory are appreciated, and Chansey can check special threats that target them like Hydreigon and Iron Moth in return. Chansey also struggles with Fighting-types like Keldeo and Mienshao, so teammates like Mega Latias and Clefable are good partners. Teammates like Mega Venusaur and Mega Latias that can handle strong setup sweepers like Nasty Plot Thundurus are appreciated. In return, Chansey can help handle special threats that don't rely on setting up such as Choice Specs Enamorus and Hydreigon. Chansey's complete inability to touch Ghost-types without Toxic and staples like Aegislash even with Toxic is problematic, so reliable answers to these threats like Celesteela are appreciated. Chansey is threatened heavily by Knock Off, so good Knock Off absorbers like Buzzwole and Clefable are important alongside it, while Chansey can handle any special threats that might threaten them, including Galarian Moltres and Magnezone.

Special Wall.description:
• Chansey is a staple Pokemon on stall teams thanks to its excellent cleric utility, useful status absorbing ability in Natural Cure, and absurd special bulk with Eviolite that allows it to wall threats such as non-Taunt Arceus-Fairy, Eternatus, and Palkia-O.
  • Aromatherapy allows Chansey to serve as a crucial cleric by removing status from Arceus-Dark and Ho-Oh. In addition, it removes sleep from allies such as Dondozo and Giratina that rely on Rest for recovery.
  • Confide allows Chansey more easily wall Primal Kyogre, non-Taunt Arceus-Fairy, and Eternatus by nullifying any Calm Mind or Meteor Beam setup attempts, although Chansey should be aware of its PP lest these threats have an opportunity to set up later.
  • Seismic Toss is another option that allows Chansey to break Palkia-O’s Substitute and to do damage to Taunt Arceus formes. Toxic allows Chansey to slowly wear down the Pokemon it walls such as wallbreaker Primal Kyogre and non-Taunt Arceus-Fairy while punishing typical switch-ins such as Primal Groudon, specially offensive Yveltal, Rayquaza, and Arceus-Ground. However, using Toxic means Chansey is completely shut down by Taunt, and it is easier for defensive Primal Kyogre and Substitute Palkia-O to deal with.
  • Minimal Speed allows Chansey to underspeed Alomomola's Flip Turn, allowing Chansey to hinder the foe Alomomola would otherwise safely bring in, and to Speed tie Calyrex-I under Trick Room. The EV spread maximizes mixed bulk to let Chansey act as a special wall while also withstanding weak physical attacks such as Yveltal's U-turn and Giratina-O's Dragon Tail.
  • Tera Grass allows Chansey to wall wallbreaker Primal Kyogre by tanking Water Spout more comfortably, in addition to minimizing the damage defensive Primal Kyogre can do to it.
  • Chansey should not be afraid to switch into special threats such as Primal Kyogre, Meteor Beam Eternatus, and Palkia-O. However, it must be wary of its HP or it will easily be overwhelmed by threats such as Water Spout Kyogre and +1 Deoxys-A under Psychic Terrain. After sustaining damage, Soft-Boiled should be used on free turns such as when Chansey forces out wallbreaker Primal Kyogre and Palkia-O.
