  • Thunder Wave Grimmsnarl is a standout speed control Pokemon that can help Ditto avoid Speed ties, which are important in the cases of Calyrex-S and Zamazenta-C. It can also apply Reflect and Light Screen to help transformed Ditto survive attacks from Restricted Pokemon, which is especially helpful given its low HP.
  • Incineroar and Miraidon can help pivot Ditto into advantageous transformations with U-turn or Parting Shot and Volt Switch, respectively.
  • Calyrex-I particularly has a hard time against Calyrex-S and Zamazenta-C, especially if they are paired together, so it appreciates Ditto being able to check one or both of them. Calyrex-I also threatens Rillaboom and Landorus, which Ditto struggles against.

Choice Scarf.description:
Ditto is used for its phenomenal ability to transform into strong opposing Pokemon, which is invaluable in a format with Restricted Pokemon, giving you access to an extra extremely powerful Pokemon. Ditto is a good late-game cleaner that likes copying Pokemon such as Calyrex-S and Miraidon, since it outspeeds and threatens an OHKO onto both of them. Choice Scarf is used to allow Ditto to outspeed the Pokemon it transforms into, giving Ditto the advantage while fighting it. Tera Ghost is used to give Ditto an immunity to Fake Out, which can severely hinder its momentum.

Terapagos can be an issue for Ditto, since if Terapagos Terastallizes, Imposter will not work, and Terapagos will OHKO it. Ditto also struggles with Pokemon that can slow its momentum, such as Rillaboom and Incineroar with the aforementioned Fake Out and Amoonguss with Spore and Rage Powder. Fighting-types, such as Iron Hands and the Urshifu formes, can help against Incineroar and Terapagos, and Ice-types, such as Chien-Pao and Calyrex-I, can help against Amoonguss and Rillaboom. Incineroar and Amoonguss are also good partners for Ditto, as they help it get attacks off with Spore, Rage Powder, and Fake Out support. The aforementioned Urshifu-R, Iron Hands, and Incineroar can help Ditto position itself and transform into the ideal foe with U-Turn, Volt Switch, and Parting Shot respectively.

zu.overview: Ditto sets itself apart from other revenge killers by using Imposter, which makes it an especially flexible Choice Scarf user for picking off setup sweepers like Charizard, Beartic, and Trailblaze Hisuian Sneasel. Ditto's ability to outright deter setup sweepers is tough to replicate for other revenge killers that only work in more specific matchups. For example, Basculin is excellent at finishing off Charizard and Minior, but it can struggle against Beartic in snow as well as Virizion. Ditto's ability to threaten to reverse sweep can even make it a great wincon in its own right. However, Imposter is thwarted by Substitute, and setup sweepers like Mesprit, Minior, and Hisuian Sneasel commonly fit the move. Some setup sweepers, such as Jolteon and Primeape, can even utilize their defensive boosts and higher HP stats to keep setting up in front of Ditto and wear it down with their attacks. Despite Ditto being generally useful as a revenge killer, it's often overshadowed by more independently powerful and versatile fast attackers like Jolteon, Sneasel, and Choice Scarf Basculin.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Ditto's Tera type is the only flexible thing about it. Tera Fairy is an option over Tera Steel for a different defensive profile. A Fighting resistance is handy against Hitmontop's Mach Punch, Beartic's Close Combat, and Regirock's Body Press, and a Dragon immunity can help Ditto switch into and phaze Dipplin more easily. Tera Ghost is another alternative, one that pushes the Fighting resistance from Tera Fairy even further into an immunity.

Checks and Counters

Substitute Users: Mesprit, Hisuian Sneasel, and other Substitute users can deny Ditto's ability to copy them using Imposter, though they must set up with Substitute before Ditto copies them.

Item Removal: If Ditto loses its Choice Scarf to Knock Off or Trick, it loses most of its reliability as a revenge killer and utility option for deterring setup.

Residual Damage and Status: Relying on Choice Scarf means that Ditto will get worn down by repeatedly taking entry hazard damage, as it will hardly have easy opportunities to heal even if it copies recovery moves. Status also sticks around on Ditto, and paralysis nullifies most of Ditto's potential as a revenge killer.

Trick Room Users: Ditto is helpless to prevent offensive Trick Room users like Spiritomb and Alolan Exeggutor from sweeping past it due to it moving second under Trick Room.

Revenge Killer.description:
Ditto's sole access to Imposter puts it in a class of its own as an adaptable Choice Scarf revenge killer against a wide range of setup sweepers in ZU, boasting a non-exhaustive list that includes threats like Beartic, Minior, Lycanroc, Hisuian Sneasel, Farigiraf, Charizard, and more. The EV spread is for the rare occurence where Ditto is in a mirror matchup, pushing it to activate the opposing Ditto's Imposter first to proceed to PP stall. Tera Steel gives Ditto a good blanket defensive typing and helpful resistances against setup sweepers like Mesprit and Farigiraf. The Rock resistance of Tera Steel is handy for dampening damage from Stealth Rock, Lycanroc's Accelerock, and Minior's Stone Edge.

Bulkier teams appreciate Ditto's flexibility for blanket checking and deterring volatile setup sweepers like Charizard, Beartic, and Charizard. As Ditto can reverse sweep with stolen stat boosts, it acts as a unique wincon option for stall teams, which can often be so passive as to enable many sweepers to get set up. These more defensive teams, including balance teams, can also have bulky teammates like Eelektross, Drifblim, and Regirock waiting in the wings to pivot in for Ditto once it's locked itself into one of its moves. As Ditto is so dependent on its item to function in its role, it relies heavily on Pokemon that can't have their items removed, namely Dipplin and Muk. Knock Off absorbers like Weezing can similarly cover this flaw for Ditto. Since Ditto won't be dealing with Substitute setup sweepers like Mesprit and Mismagius, it appreciates being able to fall back on Haze users and phazers like Weezing and Articuno as well as Prankster Encore users like Sableye and Whimsicott. Ditto suffers against entry hazard stacking teams, notably Toxic Spikes and Sticky Web, so it appreciates teammates like Hitmontop and Sandslash that can remove hazards.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Ditto is a niche revenge killer that can also be used to attempt a reverse sweep, but it must be wary of threats that may counter it with a surprise Terastallization, such as Tera Fairy Miraidon, Tera Fire Koraidon, Tera Ice Iron Bundle, and Tera Water Gholdengo.
  • Ditto doesn't add much value to teams on its own outside of helping overwhelm opposing checks. It is also strongly prediction reliant.
  • Maximum bulk and minimum Speed allow Ditto to force opposing Ditto to trigger Imposter first and run out of PP quicker.
  • Tera Fairy defeats Choice Scarf Miraidon, Koraidon, and Walking Wake that may try to attack it with a Dragon-type move.
  • Ditto is rarely a reliable check for reasons explained earlier, so it appreciates support from backup checks, especially for potent threats that it fails to revenge kill such as Swords Dance Chien-Pao, Double Dance Miraidon, and Bulk Up Great Tusk. Thus, teammates like Toxapex, Skeledirge, Ting-Lu, Clodsire, and Iron Treads are good picks.
  • Ditto's ability to revenge kill many strong threats makes teambuilding flexible, allowing offensive Pokemon like Miraidon, Iron Bundle, Chien-Pao, and Koraidon to fit more easily.

Imposter.description: Ditto is a great revenge killer that fits mainly on stall and balance teams for its ability to punish and discourage opposing setup sweepers; however, Ditto's strengths allow it to be useful to any teamstyle. Ditto runs 248 HP to minimize Stealth Rock damage and allow it to use Struggle up to five times from full HP. A Quiet nature and 252 Special Attack EVs allow Ditto to maximize Future Sight Damage when transformed into Pokemon like Slowbro and Reuniclus, as Future Sight damage is based on Ditto's Special Attack before transforming. A Choice Scarf lets Ditto outrun the Pokemon that it is transforming into without having to rely on a Speed tie. Tera Steel reduces Stealth Rock damage and is a good defensive Tera type, helping out specifically when transformed into Gardevoir and Hisuian Goodra. Ditto pairs well with defensive Pokemon such as Hippowdon and Hisuian Goodra, which can take hits directed at Ditto after it revenge kills or forces out the opposing Pokemon. Ditto also pairs well with passive Pokemon such as Empoleon, Chansey, and Chesnaught that may get set up on, which can allow Ditto to come in and revenge kill those setup sweepers. Ditto also benefits from strong entry hazard control from Pokemon like Cyclizar and Talonflame, which allows it to come in multiple times over the course of the game. Ditto has trouble when transforming into opposing Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Mienshao, Gengar, and Gardevoir, due to having to rely on winning a Speed tie. Similarly, Ditto has trouble with Pokemon running Substitute like Suicune.

nu.overview: Ditto holds a small but valuable niche in NU as a safety-net revenge killer that can copy opposing setup sweepers with Imposter and turn their boosts against them. Choice Scarf lets Ditto immediately come in and threaten boosted foes such as Dragon Dance Flygon and Scrafty, Shell Smash Drednaw, Tidy Up Cinccino, and setup variants of Meloetta and Scream Tail, giving teams an emergency answer to sweepers that can otherwise snowball quickly. Ditto also affects the game from Team Preview, as its sole presence can make opponents more reluctant to set up or commit to a sweep too early. Upon entering the field, Ditto can scout opposing movesets and obtain valuable information, such as whether Munkidori is using Trick with a Choice item, Chandelure is running Will-O-Wisp, or Duraludon is carrying Roar or Thunder Wave. However, Ditto is extremely matchup dependent and offers very little if the opposing team lacks setup sweepers or strong attackers worth copying. It also keeps its own low HP after transforming, making it much easier to wear down than the Pokemon it copies. Substitute users such as Basculegion-M and Flygon can block Imposter if Ditto switches in after Substitute is already active, while priority users such as Brute Bonnet and Houndstone can pick off Ditto due to its low HP after transforming. The prevalence of paralysis from Pokemon such as Klefki, Bellibolt, Dudunsparce, and Duraludon also limits Ditto's revenge killing, as a paralyzed Ditto can lose the Speed advantage it relies on even with Choice Scarf. Ditto can also fail to reverse sweep if the opponent still has bulky teammates such as Vaporeon, Copperajah, and Goodra healthy enough to take a copied attack.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Ditto can use other Tera types to help itself against particular targets. Tera Dark provides an immunity to Psyshock to turn the tables on Calm Mind Meloetta and Galarian Slowbro.

Checks and Counters

Unburden Sweepers: Grafaiai and Hitmonlee won't have their Unburden boost copied by Imposter.

Substitute Users: Sweepers like Raikou, Uxie, and Meloetta can protect themselves from Ditto's Imposter with Substitute.

Item Removal: Without Choice Scarf, Ditto is not as effective of a revenge killer. However, Ditto can absorb Knock Off to improve its matchup against stall teams that depend on Regenerator users.

Residual Damage: Ditto's bad HP sticks with it even after it copies its target, and its role as a Choice Scarf user limits its longevity against anything but Regenerator users.

Among Us (Imposter).description:
Set Details

Ditto distinguishes itself with the entirely unique combination of Imposter + Choice Scarf. Ditto's ability enables it to morph into a revenge killer with great potential to reverse sweep teams with the boosts it copies, so it deters setup sweepers like Flygon, Cinccino, Munkidori, Paldean Tauros-W, Toxtricity, and Scyther. Maximum physical bulk and minimum Speed help Ditto to trigger an opposing Ditto's Imposter first and PP stall it. Tera Steel helps Ditto against Cinccino, Flygon, Alolan Ninetales, and Oricorio-P, and it can turn the tables for Ditto in risky Speed ties against Choice Scarf variants of Flamigo and Porygon-Z. Lessened damage from Stealth Rock and a Toxic Spikes immunity are also nice perks from Tera Steel. Tera Fairy provides Ditto a neat defensive typing with helpful Dark, Bug, and Fighting resistances to better stomach priority moves like Sucker Punch, First Impression, Mach Punch, and Vacuum Wave. The Normal and Fighting immunities from Tera Ghost help Ditto against Cincinno and Porygon-Z, Paldean Tauros-W and other Fighting-types, and bulky Body Press sweepers like Bronzong.

Ditto is a good filler option for teams in need of an emergency answer to setup sweepers, and most teams can appreciate Ditto's ability to check weather teams by copying Speed-boosting weather abilities like Swift Swim, Slush Rush, and Chlorophyll. Stall teams can rely on Ditto as an anti-setup option that provides opportunities they'd otherwise lack for reverse sweeping. Offensive teams can worry less about fitting defensive counterplay for major offensive threats by running Ditto, and Ditto itself can work as a wincon if it copies a setup sweeper. Balance teams appreciate Ditto's ability to deter offensive setup sweepers, and they have the defensive backbone necessary to compensate for Ditto needing to switch out after being locked into a move by Choice Scarf. The virtually infinite PP Ditto can bring with Imposter helps in matchups against stall teams, and it can use Imposter to copy abilities like Regenerator from Amoonguss and Natural Cure from Altaria. Imposter's ability to overwrite the Speed drop from Sticky Web and copy Speed-boosting weather abilities helps Ditto out against hyper offense teams, lessening the strain Cinccino and other fast threats like Choice Scarf Flygon are under to answer these teams. However, Ditto itself can be surprised by Terastallization from threats like Flygon and Scyther, so it relies on secondary checks to setup sweepers. Scream Tail can disrupt setup sweepers with its fast Encore, while Ditto exploits threats that continue to try and boost against it, such as Oricorio-P.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Ditto fills a role as a revenge killer with a chance to reverse sweep entire teams. Its presence discourages setup from foes such as Zacian-C, Mega Salamence, and Primal Groudon. Its ability to generate endless PP also helps against stall teams.
  • In the rare case there is a Ditto mirror, the EVs, IVs, and nature maximize the chance that the opposing Ditto’s Imposter ability activates first, thus causing it to run out of PP first.
  • Tera Ghost allows Ditto to block Extreme Speed from Arceus, since it cannot OHKO Arceus with Extreme Speed or Tera Ghost Arceus with Shadow Claw at +2 from full, while Arceus can at the expense of Tera Normal thanks to Ditto’s low HP stat.
  • Tera Fairy provides a resistance to Sucker Punch and Foul Play, making it harder for Yveltal and Arceus-Dark to revenge kill Ditto. Tera Fairy also provides a useful immunity to Dragon-type moves, letting Ditto soft check Eternatus and Palkia-O.
  • Tera Dark also resists Sucker Punch and Foul Play while also providing a resistance to Marshadow’s Shadow Sneak. Thanks to Tera Dark’s immunity to Psychic, it allows Ditto to absorb powerful attacks such as +1 Light that Burns the Sky from Ultra Necrozma and Psycho Boost from Deoxys-A.
  • Hidden Power Ice allows Ditto to hit Zygarde and Mega Salamence with a super effective move in the rare case Ditto copies a Marshadow with Hidden Power.
  • Ditto should be swapped in carefully, as any unnecessary damage can compromise its role. Due to its low HP stat, Ditto struggles defensively even when transforming into walls such as Chansey.
  • Ditto greatly helps in the hyper offense matchup by restricting the opponent from setting up in addition to Imposter taking away Sticky Web's Speed drop, keeping teammates such as Eternatus, Ho-Oh and Yveltal from being overwhelmed by boosting threats such as Primal Groudon, Zacian-C, and Ultra Necrozma.
  • Ditto can be used to greatly help in the stall matchup thanks to its ability to generate endless PP. Ditto stays healthy by copying recovery moves from Chansey, Dondozo, and Arceus-Dark. Ditto also increases its longevity by copying abilities such as Natural Cure from Chansey and Regenerator from Ho-Oh, and Alomomola.
  • Ditto is a good fit on balance teams, as it helps Defoggers such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal from being overwhelmed by hyper offense threats such as Primal Groudon and Ultra Necrozma. In return, Ho-Oh and Yveltal keep entry hazards off the field, since Ditto can easily get worn down by them.
  • Teammates such as Primal Groudon and Zygarde are free to use more offensive sets thanks to Ditto being able to check threats such as Zacian-C, Eternatus, and opposing Primal Groudon for them. In addition, Zygarde appreciates Ditto allowing it to run a specially defensive set for Arceus-Water instead.
  • Due to being locked into one move, Ditto can be countered by a surprise Tera from threats such as Tera Fairy Eternatus and Tera Ghost Arceus, so another form of reliable revenge killing such as Arceus and Choice Band Marshadow is appreciated.

Choice Scarf Revenge Killer.description:
Thanks to Ditto's signature ability Imposter, which also copies enemy stat changes, Ditto is one of the best revenge killers in the tier. Ditto's presence alone scares off sweepers like Ogerpon-W and Azumarill from setting up. Ditto does not copy the enemy HP stat, so 248 HP EVs are used to minimize damage taken from entry hazards before transforming while maximizing Ditto's HP stat, as well as allowing Ditto to use Struggle four times before it faints. 252 Defense EVs minimize the damage Ditto takes from opposing Ditto in the extremely rare mirror matchup. Finally, a Relaxed nature coupled with 0 Speed IVs guarantees that Imposter will never activate first, which ensures that Ditto will have more Transform PP in the aforementioned mirror match.

Ursaluna is a great teammate for Ditto, as it can switch into walls and begin applying immediate pressure. Ditto also appreciates Ursaluna's unrivaled ability to punch holes in the opposing team, making a late-game Ditto sweep much easier. If Ditto copies certain targets like Iron Valiant and a majority of the opposing team is weakened, Ditto can win the game. Terapagos removes entry hazards, is a one-time check against threats such as Latios, Urshifu-R, and Sneasler, and beats bulky setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Gliscor that Ditto struggles with despite copying their boosts. Porygon-2 is a defensive wall that goads opposing types such as Dragon, Dark, and Fire to setup its threats to break through Porygon-2, allowing Ditto to come in and clean up these types by copying a boosted Dragonite, Darkrai, or Ceruledge late-game. Indeedee is a good teammate for Ditto, as its Psychic Surge ability prevents Ditto from being picked off by priority moves. Blissey is a nice partner for Ditto, as it can absorb status moves that would otherwise cripple Ditto and then shrug them off via Natural Cure. Blissey can also use Thunder Wave to slow down opposing Choice Scarf users that would otherwise Speed tie with Ditto such as Meowscarada and Enamorus. Choice Specs Hisuian Zoroark is a powerful teammate that pairs well with Ditto, as Ditto can copy the stat boosts from setup sweepers that aim to take advantage of a Choice-locked Hisuian Zoroark. Maushold can use its high speed tier to lock Bulk Up users like Landorus-T that would otherwise be able to stall out Ditto. Additionally, Maushold is able to break down walls due to the sheer power of Population Bomb. Pivots are great teammates for Ditto because they can lure in targets for Ditto to copy. Choice Scarf Staraptor and Defensive Braviary are solid picks, as they can use U-turn to go right into Ditto. Braviary is also capable of using Defog to keep Ditto alive for longer.

Revenge Killer.description:
• Ditto is widely hailed as the best revenge killer and finds a small niche with a Choice Scarf.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Ditto rarely needs to Terastallize unless it is being threatened by Dragon Dance Dragonite's Extreme Speed at +3.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost gives Ditto immunity to Dragonite's Extreme Speed, preventing it from defeating Ditto after three Dragon Dances.

Items
  • Choice Scarf: The safest option, Choice Scarf guarantees that Ditto will always outspeed the foe unless said foe is holding a Choice Scarf.
  • Focus Sash: A high-risk yet high-reward option, Focus Sash allows Ditto to switch moves at the cost of being nullified by entry hazards. However, it should be noted that Imposter doesn't copy Protosynthesis or Quark Drive boosts, making Focus Sash a lot less niche, as it allows Ditto to beat foes such as Flutter Mane more consistently assuming the field is clear of hazards.
EV Spreads
  • Effort Values: The given EVs maximize Ditto's bulk in the rare case of a mirror matchup.
  • Individual Values: 0 Speed IVs and a minus Speed nature is key to beating opposing Ditto, as the Ditto that moves last on the fourth turn will win the mirror.

Scarf Imposter.description: Ditto solidifies itself to once again be the goo that holds balanced and offensive Normal teams together thanks to its incredibly strong ability in Imposter. Reversing the momentum of fast offensive threats such as Iron Valiant, Mega Charizard X, and Excadrill allows Ditto to force counterplay against offensive teams. Ditto can also take advantage of entry hazard setters and removers, such as Ferrothorn, Kleavor, and Zapdos, using their own longevity or utility against them. In order to take advantage of Pokemon that use either Return or Frustration, such as Mega Altaria or Mega Pinsir, Ditto likes to run 128 Happiness instead of 255 or 0. Walls like Blissey and Porygon2 appreciate Ditto being able to prevent threats such as Baxcalibur and Spectrier from using them as setup fodder, while Ditto appreciates both defensive switch-ins and slow pivots via their use of Teleport. Mega Lopunny is a staple on Normal teams that accents Ditto's role expertly; many of the offensive threats and setup sweepers that revenge kill Mega Lopunny, such as Mega Charizard X, Kommo-o, and Galarian Moltres, are usually very weak to their own sets or coverage. Mega Lopunny can lure a threat in and pivot with U-turn, allowing Ditto to come in safely and transform. Ditto appreciates Mega Lopunny's Speed tier and fast pivot with U-turn, as well as potentially setting up Ditto with Encore Sets to stop foes from using Substitute or setting up completely. Hisuian Zoroark makes for another stellar teammate for Ditto, as Hisuian Zoroark disguised as a passive Pokemon, such as Blissey, or another offensive threat, such as Diggersby or Mega Lopunny, can lead to Hisuian Zoroark wallbreaking and netting KOs on vital foes, making it easier for Ditto to sweep once it has transformed. While Ditto is immune to Sticky Web, it is susceptible to other hazards such as Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes, so forms of hazard control such as Staraptor or Cyclizar are appreciated. Staraptor is another defensive option, while Cyclizar can enable Ditto to utilize Transform with a Substitute from Shed Tail. Smeargle on more offense-oriented teams' pairs well with Ditto, as Smeargle can set hazards with Stone Axe or Ceaseless Edge and spread status with Nuzzle, Mortal Spin, or Spore, allowing Ditto to exploit the opposing team easier. Smeargle will usually give up Sticky Web when paired with Ditto so as to not hinder Ditto's revenge killing prowess.

Choice Scarf.description:
248 HP EVs ensure that Ditto will be able to use Struggle four times before fainting, and 252 Defense EVs minimize Struggle damage from an opposing Ditto. The minimum possible Speed allows Imposter to not activate first and therefore allow Ditto to have more Transform PP.

This is a sample set, stay tuned for future updates!

anythinggoes.overview: Ditto is a niche yet potent revenge killer, leveraging its Imposter ability to quickly reverse sweeps, which would otherwise pose a significant threat to its team. Choice Scarf is both Ditto's biggest strength and Achilles' heel, allowing it to outspeed the Pokemon it copies; however, it is limited to choosing one move, allowing its opponent to respond accordingly by switching to a check. Partially due to being Choice-locked, Ditto struggles against opposing defensive Terastallization, where foes may gain a resistance or immunity to Ditto's moves and fire back with a powerful attack. However, due to Ditto’s lack of any defensive utility and being somewhat situational as well as matchup dependent, Ditto is not a common Pokemon.
anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Due to Ditto being incredibly one-dimensional and lacking almost any versatility, it mostly lacks other options. However, Ditto can choose to run Tera Steel. Tera Steel acts as a midground between Tera Fairy and Tera Ghost, giving Ditto a resistance to Dragon-type moves, a Toxic and Toxic Spikes immunity, and maintaining a resistance to Arceus's Extreme Speed. However, due to Ditto's poor bulk, a resistance might not be enough to keep Ditto alive against powerful attackers such as Koraidon and Miraidon.

Checks and Counters

Protect Users: Protect users like Gliscor take advantage of Ditto being Choice-locked to scout and respond accordingly.

Entry Hazards: Entry hazards significantly cripple Ditto due to its inability to run Heavy-Duty Boots, slowly wearing them down every time it switches in.

Revenge Killer.description:
Tera Ghost grants Ditto an immunity to Arceus's Extreme Speed and Koraidon's Low Kick, while Tera Normal gives Ditto an immunity to Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage while adding a STAB boost when copying Arceus's Extreme Speed. On the other hand, Tera Fairy gives Ditto immunity to moves such as Koraidon's Outrage and Scale Shot and Miraidon's Draco Meteor. 0 Speed IVs and a Relaxed nature ensure Ditto has the best chance against other Ditto, making Struggle move last and therefore causing recoil the latest, and 248 HP EVs ensure that Ditto gets five uses of Struggle and minimizes entry hazard damage.

Ditto mainly fits on bulkier balance teams, where being passive is less of an issue due to its great revenge killing and reverse sweeping abilities. Furthermore, on more defensive teams, Ditto’s lack of defensive utility is supplemented by other teammates, while it can also more easily rely on teammates to scout for an opponent Terastallizing. More passive teammates like Eternatus, Gliscor, and Alomomola enjoy having extra insurance against powerful threats like Zacian-C or Scale Shot Koraidon. Due to Ditto being Choice locked, defensive Pokemon such as Ho-Oh can take great advantage of Ditto being locked into an unfavorable move. Therefore, Ditto appreciates the support of Eternatus, which provides a Toxic poison immunity and a strong STAB attack in Dynamax Cannon in combination with Toxic, which can quickly wear Ho-Oh down. Ditto also appreciates teammates like Alomomola, which can help Ditto that are Choice-locked into Dragon- or Ghost-type moves and safely switch out against Pokemon like Zacian-C and Arceus.

ru.overview: Vaporeon establishes itself as a useful defensive Pokemon, utilizing its ability Water Absorb and the recovery of Wish to slow down great Water-type Pokemon such as Suicune and Basculegion-F. Vaporeon can support its teammates by passing Wish to them and using Flip Turn to bring in strong attackers such as Choice Specs Hisuian Goodra, or it can use Haze to neutralize setup sweepers like Mimikyu. Vaporeon also helps immensely against rain teams by blanking the Water-type attacks of common rain attackers such as Barraskewda and Basculegion-F. Vaporeon, however, struggles immensely into Electric-types such as Raikou and Magnezone, as while they may not appreciate a Scald burn, they can generally force Vaporeon out into a teammate. Dragon-types such as Cyclizar and Noivern also can give Vaporeon trouble, as their disruptive moves such as Knock Off and Taunt can force it out by threatening to cripple it. Vaporeon's biggest issue, though, is its passivity, and thus it can be exploited very easily by Pokemon such as Reuniclus and Wo-Chien that do not care about Scald.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Calm Mind can be used to turn Vaporeon into a self-sufficient sweeper. Shadow Ball helps deal damage against Water-types such as Basculegion-F and Slowbro, though the damage usually isn't enough and Vaporeon is better off being paired with Pokemon that can deal with these Pokemon. Roar can be used to phaze setup sweepers while also racking up entry hazard damage. However, it cannot be used in last Pokemon scenarios against Pokemon such as Suicune and Slowbro, so Haze is usually preferred. Ice Beam deals significant damage to Dragon- and Grass-types such as Noivern and Chesnaught that otherwise wall Vaporeon.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Electric-types such as Raikou and Magnezone can threaten Vaporeon with immense damage or use it as a setup opportunity. However, they do not appreciate Scald burns.

Dragon-types: Dragon-types such as Cyclizar and Noivern can easily switch into Scald from Vaporeon and can use disruptive moves such as Knock Off and Taunt to ruin it.

Defensive.description:
Vaporeon establishes itself as a great defensive Pokemon that is able to take on a variety of foes like Volcanion, Empoleon, and Basculegion-F with its ability, Water Absorb, while also Wish passing to its teammates to heal them up. Haze allows Vaporeon to remove stat boosts from setup sweepers such as Reuniclus, Slowbro, and Suicune, while Flip Turn allows Vaporeon to safely bring in its teammates so they can recover through Vaporeon's Wish passing without taking damage. Protect allows Vaporeon to scout Choice-locked attacks from wallbreakers such as Galarian Zapdos and Gengar while allowing it to safely recover using Wish. Leftovers helps Vaporeon to keep itself healthy and can synergize well with Protect to help it stall out burned foes. Tera Poison makes Vaporeon immune to Toxic, allowing it to easily switch into Pokemon such as Umbreon. Tera Dark makes Vaporeon immune to Psychic Noise from Slowbro and Reuniclus, which allows it to recover using Wish, as well as allowing it to take Knock Off from Krookodile much more easily.

Vaporeon fits best on bulky offense and balance teams where it can form crucial backbones in order to wall Pokemon such as Suicune and Basculegion-F. Bulky attackers such as Hisuian Goodra, Raikou, and Galarian Zapdos heavily appreciate Vaporeon, as it grants Wish support to them while they pair nicely with it defensively. Special walls such as Registeel and Jirachi synergize with Vaporeon and take powerful special attacks from Pokemon such as Calm Mind Reuniclus and Raikou, while Vaporeon is able to keep them healthy through Wish passing. Dragon-types such as Cyclizar and Hisuian Goodra pair well with Vaporeon, as they can take on the Electric- and Grass-type attacks aimed at it from Raikou, Rotom-H, and Amoonguss. Entry hazard removers such as Talonflame and Cyclizar pair well with Vaporeon, removing hazards that may overwhelm it, while Vaporeon is able to Wish pass to them to keep them healthy. Stealth Rock setters such as Krookodile and Registeel can help wear down foes, while Vaporeon can keep them healthy with Wish, so they can continue to come in and set Stealth Rock up multiple times during the game.

nu.overview: Vaporeon's typing and good defenses let it check common physical attackers like Paldean Tauros-W, Incineroar, and Flygon, and Water Absorb makes it one of the best answers to opposing Water-types like Inteleon and Basculegion-M. Compared to other physically bulky Water-types like Swampert, Vaporeon excels due to its access to reliable recovery in Wish and its ability to pivot and potentially pass Wish to its teammates with Flip Turn. Vaporeon can also run Haze or Roar, which allows it to check bulky setup sweepers like Bulk Up Scrafty and Calm Mind Sylveon. However, more powerful or more aggressively boosting foes, such as Swords Dance Scyther and Nasty Plot Munkidori, can overwhelm Vaporeon. Additionally, while Vaporeon can be a great blanket check to certain physical and special attackers, it can be easily overwhelmed at times by either how many it has to check in a battle or their sheer power. Grass- and Electric-type attackers, such as Decidueye, Brambleghast, and Kilowattrel, are quite common as well and easily force Vaporeon out.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Calm Mind can be used on Vaporeon to let it take advantage of forced switches and passive Pokemon, usually alongside Ice Beam to make progress against Toxicroak and Grass-types like Amoonguss. However, this set is still walled by opposing Water-types. Tera Ghost can be used to completely wall Paldean Tauros-W.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types and Grass-type coverage: Vaporeon is weak to common Grass-type attackers such as Brambleghast and Decidueye. However, all of these hate switching into a Scald burn. Grass-type coverage, like Chandelure's Energy Ball and Tera Grass Paldean Tauros-F's Trailblaze, can also be threatening.

Electric-types: Electric-type attackers like Kilowattrel and Raikou force Vaporeon out, and they can take advantage of this by gaining momentum or setting up.

Special Attackers: Strong special attackers, such as Meloetta, Chandelure, and Goodra, scare out Vaporeon, and the first two have Trick to cripple it while Goodra carries Knock Off + Toxic.

Water-immune Pokemon: As Vaporeon only runs Water-type attacks, it cannot actually damage opposing Water-immune Pokemon. Most prominently, Toxicroak can set up on Vaporeon or throw out powerful attacks, and opposing Vaporeon are untouchable.

Wish Passer.description:
Set Details

Flip Turn allows Vaporeon to pivot in teammates for free and more easily pass Wish. Alternatively, Roar gives Vaporeon an option to prevent opposing setup sweepers like Nasty Plot Uxie and Calm Mind Sylveon from boosting out of control. However, Haze can be used to avoid Throat Chop blocking sound moves from Scrafty, Flygon, and Overqwil. Leftovers gives Vaporeon additional healing, particularly in combination with Protect to gain free turns to heal. However, Heavy-Duty Boots allows Vaporeon to pivot more frequently without concern for entry hazard chip damage. Tera Poison gives Vaporeon a resistance to Fighting- and Grass-type attacks from common physical attackers such as Flamigo, Paldean Tauros-W, and Brambleghast, as well as an immunity to being poisoned by Bellibolt's Toxic. Tera Dark, on the other hand, allows Vaporeon to temporarily check Stored Power sweepers like Bronzong if it doesn't have Haze or Roar. Tera Fairy can be used to resist Fighting- and Dragon-type attacks from Paldean Tauros-W, Toxicroak, and Goodra.

Vaporeon benefits from teammates that can take powerful special attacks from foes like Chandelure, Dudunsparce, and Munkidori, so special walls like Incineroar, Bronzong, and Klefki support it well. These teammates also benefit from Wish being passed to them, as they lack reliable recovery. A backup physical wall such as Brambleghast or Gligar is useful to ensure Vaporeon isn't overwhelmed by Ground- and Fighting-types like Flygon and Flamigo. On non-Heavy-Duty Boots sets, entry hazard removal from Pokemon such as Altaria and Brambleghast is vital to ensure Vaporeon doesn't become excessively passive by being forced to heal each time it comes out. Powerful wallbreakers such as Flamigo, Flygon, and Chandelure benefit from Wish and Flip Turn support from Vaporeon, allowing them to repeatedly switch in and break opposing walls.

zu.overview: Jolteon establishes itself as a premier fast pivot with its great Speed and solid power. Its fast Volt Switch makes it an easy candidate on VoltTurn teams, and its adequate coverage with Alluring Voice and Shadow Ball discourages specially bulky Pokemon like Virizion and Mesprit from switching into it. Jolteon's decent set variety means it can be a deadly Calm Mind sweeper or a dangerous wallbreaker with Choice Specs. Jolteon's defensive utility with Volt Absorb and passable special bulk also makes it a situational switch-in to special attackers like Articuno and opposing Jolteon. However, the lacking power of its coverage moves causes it to struggle quite hard against specially defensive Pokemon like Cryogonal as well as Ground-types like Sandaconda. Said Ground-types make Jolteon quite reliant on Terastalization to bypass its checks, which causes it to demand for more team support.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Jolteon has no other viable options to mention.

Checks and Counters

Special Walls: Specially defensive Pokemon like Cryogonal and Regirock are not particularly bothered by even Choice Specs Jolteon, as they have the bulk to weather repeated hits and can threaten huge damage on it back with their respective STAB moves.

Ground-types: Toedscruel and bulky Tera Ground users like Articuno are Jolteon's biggest obstacles, preventing it from pivoting, and Toedscruel can proceed to set up Spikes against it. However, Ground-types that have mediocre special bulk like Sandaconda and Sandslash must be wary of Jolteon's Choice Specs-boosted coverage.

Grass-types: Grass-types like Dipplin, Alolan Exeggutor, and Virizion have excellent natural bulk which makes them a reliable Grass-type switch-in, since they can threaten it back with STAB-boosted moves, but must watch out for coverage options.

Revenge Killers: Despite being the second fastest unboosted Pokemon in the metagame, Jolteon has mediocre longevity and can get picked off easily by faster Choice Scarf users like Primeape without too much trouble. Both of these Pokemon can also pivot on it in return, causing Jolteon's teammates to lose momentum. Slower cleaners or wallbreakers with priority moves like Sneasel can exploit Jolteon's low physical bulk without too much prior damage.

Calm Mind.description:
After one Calm Mind boost, Jolteon's Thunderbolt 2HKOes unboosted Orthworm. Volt Switch maintains momentum and allows it to escape bad matchups like Crygonal, Regirock, and Virizion. Jolteon's fourth moveslot is flexible and can depend on the team's need for coverage. Alluring Voice discourages certain Grass-types like Virizion from switching in and also targets Dragon-types like Dipplin and Alolan Exeggutor that would be comfortable switching into its Electric-type STAB moves. It also hits Tera Dragon users like Sandaconda and Regirock, walls that would otherwise switch into Jolteon without too much trouble. Shadow Ball hits Mesprit and Trevenant super effectively, and it synergizes with Tera Ghost. Volt Absorb allows Jolteon to switch in against predicted Electric-type attacks from Pokemon like Magneton.

Jolteon's blistering Speed makes it a prime candidate for VoltTurn teams, pairing well with pivots like Mesprit and Primeape. In addition to pivoting, they all can provide utility with Knock Off. Knock Off support works especially well with Jolteon, as its Volt Switch is able to put more pressure on Pokemon reliant on items like Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots for longevity, such as walls like Muk and Regirock. Wallbreakers like Toxicroak benefit from Jolteon's Volt Switch and can capitalize on its checks. Grass- and Water-types like Virizion and Poliwrath can switch in and force out the Ground-types Jolteon struggles against and delay its need to Terastallize. Similarly, checks to Grass-types like Orthworm and Articuno can similarly benefit Jolteon either through entry hazard and status support or through pivoting, respectively, allowing it to Terastallize as a later time.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs boosts Jolteon's decent power to more threatening levels while still leveraging its excellent Speed. Volt Switch allows Jolteon to escape from walls like Cryogonal and Regirock and maintain momentum for its team. Alluring Voice and Shadow Ball are Jolteon's strongest options for coverage against Ground-type foes; the former strikes at Fighting- and Dragon-types like Virizion and Alolan Exeggutor, while the latter pressures Ghost-types like Rotom. Despite Jolteon's frailty, Volt Absorb gives it limited defensive utility by making it a situational switch-in against Electric-types like opposing Jolteon and Magneton.

While Choice Specs's enhanced power makes Jolteon more threatening as a pivot, it still struggles to tackle Ground- and Grass-types. Water- and Grass-types like Clawitzer, Virizion, and Whimsicott are great candidates to threaten these walls. Jolteon can form VoltTurn cores with fellow pivots like Primeape and Perrserker, keeping momentum while threatening Jolteon's checks like Cryogonal and Alolan Exeggutor. Water-types like Clawitzer pair excellently with Jolteon, threatening out Ground-types like Sandslash that intend to block Jolteon's Volt Switch while maintaining a VoltTurn core. Similarly, checks to Grass-types like Charizard and Hisuian Sneasel can take advantage of Jolteon's Volt Switch and threaten heavy damage.

Lord Helix (Shell Smash Sweeper) (Rock).description: Omastar finds itself in a valuable role on Rock teams for its potent setup move in Shell Smash, along with STAB Hydro Pump bringing a deluge onto Ground teams as a rare special attacker for the type. It starts rallying its coverage options with Ice Beam, which targets Garchomp and Water Absorb Clodsire as well as Flying- and Dragon-types like Zapdos and Dragonite. Hidden Power Grass lets Omastar punch through important Water-types like Gastrodon and Swampert. Alternatively, Earth Power allows Omastar to threaten Steel- and Poison-types like Empoleon and Toxapex as well as Dragon teams by hitting Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra hard. Air Balloon provides some protection against super effective Ground-type attacks, helping to create safer setup opportunities against foes like Excadrill and Mamoswine. Weak Armor takes advantage of weak feeble attacks like Knock Off from Gliscor and U-turn from Tornadus to increase Omastar's Speed. After a Shell Smash and Weak Armor boost, Omastar can outspeed common weather abusers like Excadrill, Barraskewda, and Alolan Sandslash in their respective weather conditions and threaten them with boosted attacks, forcing them out or achieving a KO. Physical attackers like Iron Boulder, Hisuian Arcanine, and Ogerpon-C can break down or eliminate special walls that stomach Omastar's hits like Hisuian Goodra, Blissey, and Galarian Slowking. Ogerpon-C also helps help take some of the pressure off Omastar running Hidden Power Grass with its own Grass-type STAB moves to threaten Water-types like Mega Swampert and Manaphy, as well as form a strong foothold with Omastar in the Ground matchup. Shuckle's access to Sticky Web can ensure Omastar outspeeds even grounded Choice Scarf Pokemon like Sneasler and Meowscarada after a single Shell Smash. Shuckle is also useful for its other utility like Encore to help Omastar set up and Stealth Rock to soften foes over time for Omastar to OHKO, such as Celesteela and Alolan Muk. Mega Diancie can cleave through Fighting teams thanks to its STAB Moonblast, a matchup where Omastar may struggle to find setup opportunities. Tyranitar Pursuit traps certain revenge killers that outspeed boosted Omastar, such as Choice Scarf Latias and Hisuian Zoroark, wears opposing teams with its brutal Choice Band-boosted Knock Off, and provides Omastar with a boost to its Special Defense by setting up sand.

Offensive.description: Mega Aerodactyl's unrivalled Speed tier, attacking prowess, and decent defensive profile make it a great all-around offensive threat in the metagame, outpacing and forcing out a huge portion of faster threats, such as Iron Moth, Galarian Moltres, and Enamorus lacking Choice Scarf. Dual Wingbeat provides a secondary STAB option that ensures Mega Aerodactyl hits important targets such as Buzzwole, Mega Venusaur, and Amoonguss super effectively. Earthquake provides Mega Aerodactyl with perfect neutral coverage, hitting Rock-resistant Pokemon as well as targets that are weak to it, such as Tyranitar, Zeraora, and Bisharp, allowing Mega Aerodactyl to threaten them. Taunt can be used instead to deny the likes of bulkier targets, such as Clefable, Skarmory, and Hippowdon, from accessing their healing moves, on top of shutting down setup options from specific setup sweepers, such as Mega Latias. Mega Aerodactyl can even serve as an effective Pursuit trapper; with the Tough Claws boost, it makes for an effective option to use against the likes of Iron Moth, Victini, and Alakazam. Roost is mandatory in the last slot to offset Mega Aerodactyl's Stealth Rock weakness while also allowing it to repeatedly switch into foes such as Iron Moth, resisting most of its attacks in the process. An Adamant nature is preferred to maximize Mega Aerodactyl's power, allowing it to OHKO Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur and Hydrapple with Dual Wingbeat after Stealth Rock while still getting the jump on Iron Boulder. However, a Jolly nature can be used to ensure Mega Aerodactyl outspeeds Jolly Zeraora. Mega Aerodactyl fits best on bulky offense and balance teams in need of an offensive backbone with solid secondary defensive applications. Bulkier Pokemon such as Excadrill and Rotom-W appreciate Mega Aerodactyl's ability to relieve pressure in dealing with offensive threats which they may be overwhelmed by, such as Victini and Enamorus. In return, the former provides hazard support to help Mega Aerodactyl secure damage rolls against Pokemon it would otherwise miss out on, such as against Autotomize Celesteela with Stone Edge and Tyranitar with Earthquake, whereas the latter provides additional pivoting support, hazard removal in Defog to offset Mega Aerodactyl’s weakness to Stealth Rock, and the ability to take on several setup sweepers which it struggles to take on, such as Sand Rush Excadrill and Swords Dance Scizor. Similarly, other Pokemon that can remove entry hazards, such as Excadrill and Mandibuzz, are effective at ensuring Mega Aerodactyl isn’t being dug into by Stealth Rock. On the other hand, offensive Pokemon such as Life Orb Mienshao, Nasty Plot Hydreigon, and Tapu Bulu can benefit from Mega Aerodactyl's ability to check or remove faster Pokemon which they may be dissuaded by, such as Iron Moth and Keldeo. Mega Aerodactyl's ability to force in defensive Pokemon can also lead to some interesting synergies with other offensive Pokemon, particularly when carrying Taunt; setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Enamorus and Bulk Up Buzzwole benefit from Mega Aerodactyl's ability to lure in and weaken walls such as Skarmory, Slowbro, and Mega Venusaur.

Dragon Dance.description: Dragon Dance turns Mega Aerodactyl into a threatening sweeper, leveraging its combination of power, Speed, and coverage to great effect. It particularly preys on faster teams that over-rely on using faster speed control options to check most sweepers, such as Choice Scarf users Mienshao and Keldeo. Earthquake nails several Ground-weak targets in Excadrill, Tyranitar, and Bisharp after a Dragon Dance, OHKOing the latter. Dual Wingbeat, especially with the boost from Tough Claws, flattens many neutral targets after a Dragon Dance, such as Clefable, Slowking, Gastrodon, and Mega Latias, while also allowing it to beat walls such as Buzzwole and Tangrowth. Alternatively, Mega Aerodactyl can run Roost in the last slot to offset its lack of longevity, potentially grabbing multiple setup opportunities against weaker Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur and Clefable lacking Thunder Wave. Due to its offensive prowess, this Mega Aerodactyl set fits best on fast-paced teams as an effective mid-to-late game cleaner. Early-game wallbreakers such as Enamorus can help Mega Aerodactyl by opening up gaps in the opposition through their numerous offensive applications against walls which the latter may find itself being stopped by, such as Slowbro, Scizor, and Iron Defense Skarmory. Conversely, Mega Aerodactyl’s tendency to find opportunities against specific targets such as Hippowdon and Mega Venusaur can also work to the benefit of other late-game cleaners, such as Booster Energy Iron Moth. As Mega Aerodactyl often finds itself leveraging its bulk to make the most of its setup capabilities, teammates that can prevent entry hazards from going up, such as Taunt Mew and Excadrill make for excellent partners. Mega Aerodactyl also benefits from entry hazard support provided by the former two, which helps it secure OHKOs against Pokemon such as Hydreigon after a Dragon Dance.

Offensive Utility (Flying).description: By virtue of its great coverage as well as its sky-high Attack and Speed, Mega Aerodactyl finds a great spot on Flying teams as a late-game cleaner. Earthquake pairs well with Stone Edge, threatening the likes of Heatran and Hisuian Goodra and OHKOing Tapu Koko after Stealth Rock damage. Ice Fang is a great coverage option against Ground- and Dragon-types such as Landorus and Garchomp. Dual Wingbeat breaks through Fighting- and Grass-types such as Kommo-o, Mega Gallade, and Ogerpon-W. Pursuit allows Mega Aerodactyl to take advantage of foes like Victini and Latias that are forced out due to being Choice-locked into an undesirable move, and it punishes Gholdengo if it switches out expecting Earthquake. Stealth Rock aids both Mega Aerodactyl and its teammates in their wallbreaking or sweeping, while Taunt shuts down passive Pokemon such as Toxapex and Clodsire. Mantine and Corviknight are essential teammates, as they remove Stealth Rock with Defog so that Mega Aerodactyl finds more opportunities to switch in; they also provide a defensive backbone to shield Mega Aerodactyl from Water- and Ice-types like Mega Swampert and Choice Scarf Weavile. In return, Mega Aerodactyl deals with Fire- and Electric-types that the two of them hate like Volcarona, Zapdos, and Zeraora. Moltres is helpful in dealing with Mega Scizor and Ferrothorn. Landorus and Gliscor both set up entry hazards to aid Mega Aerodactyl in its cleaning when it's not running Stealth Rock; the two of them also act as stallbreakers, provide an Electric immunity, and bust through Toxapex. Despite its great Speed tier, Mega Aerodactyl is outsped by Kommo-o and Hisuian Lilligant at +1 and by Choice Scarf users such as Nihilego, making Choice Scarf Enamorus a great teammate that is able to revenge kill these threats. Special wallbreakers like Zapdos, Tornadus-T, and Thundurus-T deal with physically defensive walls like Celesteela, Slowbro, and Ferrothorn, which would otherwise wall Mega Aerodactyl; they can also pivot Mega Aerodactyl in against specially defensive walls like Galarian Slowking and Hisuian Goodra.

Dragon Dance (Rock).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

CurseLax.description: With Snorlax's Normal typing and Thick Fat, it nets itself a niche as a wall to Chandelure that can also snowball into a dangerous bulky sweeper with Curse. Crunch nails Ghost-types like Chandelure and Basculegion-M as well as Bronzong, Heat Crash allows Snorlax to hit Steel-types like Copperajah and Bronzong, and Earthquake targets Steel- and Rock-types like Duraludon, Diancie, and Rhyperior, though it misses out on hitting Bronzong.

Curse.description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Wall.description:
Articuno's amazing bulk and reliable recovery make it a solid wall against special attackers like Tatsugiri, Venusaur, and Shaymin in spite of its bad typing, differentiating it from more popular walls like Milotic and Snorlax. Freeze-Dry has the best combination of coverage and power of any of Articuno's attacks, dealing good damage against foes like Cramorant and Palossand while deterring physical attackers like Rhydon and Bruxish from switching in. U-turn helps Articuno avoid conceding momentum, taking advantage of switch-ins like Paldean Tauros-F and Rotom-H, and its massive special bulk makes it a good defensive pivot against special attackers such as Florges and Alolan Ninetales. Haze or Roar shuts down setup sweepers like Quiver Dance Venomoth and Terastallized Tatsugiri; Haze doesn't force Articuno to take a hit, while Roar can rack up chip damage from entry hazards and further waste the HP of Substitute users like Uxie. Tera Dragon grants Articuno several new resistances so it can check Fire- and Electric-type special attackers like Delphox, Rotom-H, and Hisuian Electrode. Alternatively, Tera Steel improves Articuno's matchups against Alolan Ninetales and Hisuian Braviary, gives it a useful Toxic immunity for its responsibilities as a wall, and provides a Stealth Rock resistance that allows it to continue functioning as a defensive pivot even if it loses its item. However, the newfound weaknesses from Terastallizing can compromise some of Articuno's good matchups, as Tera Dragon makes it vulnerable to Tatsugiri and Ice-type move users like Alolan Ninetales and Milotic, while Tera Steel makes Articuno weak to Earth Power from Shaymin and Venusaur as well as STAB moves from bulky Ground-types like Mudsdale and Palossand.

Bulkier teams can rely on Articuno as a solid pivot and blanket check to special attackers. Physically defensive Pokemon like Mudsdale complement Articuno, appreciating that it can handle special attackers like Whimsicott and Shaymin for them while they answer physical attackers like Arcanine and Rhydon for it. Articuno's reliance on Freeze-Dry and passivity mean it invites in Fire-types, so it appreciates checks to them; Snorlax and Rhydon can answer specially offensive Fire-types like Rotom-H and Delphox, while Palossand and Cramorant can answer physically offensive ones like Arcanine and Paldean Tauros-F. Articuno can even bring these partners in to freely take advantage of its checks with U-turn. As a defensive pivot, Articuno excels at bringing in strong wallbreakers like Pawmot, Golurk, and Zoroark on other special walls, such as Porygon2 and Snorlax. Other wallbreakers like Paldean Tauros-F and Hariyama excel at breaking Alolan Sandslash, which Articuno invites in. Other pivots, including Rotom-H, Hisuian Decidueye, and Ambipom, can form VoltTurn cores with Articuno, forcing opponents using common defensive cores to continuously react to their low-risk pivot moves.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Flying

Hurricane can be used over Substitute or U-turn as a way to make Articuno more threatening against foes such as Iron Valiant and Okidogi; however, it has poor accuracy and using it foregoes the generally greater utility of these two moves. An alternative EV spread of 240 HP / 84 SpD / 184 Spe allows Articuno to outspeed maximum Speed Pelipper, Frosmoth, and Hisuian Braviary while still avoiding a 2HKO from Choice Specs Greninja.

Specially Defensive (Flying).description:
Articuno's special bulk lets it serve as a special wall on Flying teams, dealing with threatening foes such as Kyurem, Greninja, and Galarian Moltres. Freeze-Dry lets Articuno handle Dragon-, Ground-, and Water-types such as Choice Specs Dragapult, Gastrodon, Landorus, Toxapex, and Primarina. Futhermore, it can be used against other Flying-types to counter threats like Enamorus and Gliscor. Substitute allows Articuno to avoid status conditions such as Toxic from Toxapex and Gliscor while also leveraging Pressure to PP stall special attackers. Alternatively, U-turn pairs well with its mediocre Speed stat, which can be used to pivot out and provide a safe switch to setup sweepers such as Dragonite and Gliscor. Haze is used to nullify special setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Hatterene and Nasty Plot Galarian Moltres. The provided EVs allow Articuno to outspeed Jolly Azumarill and uninvested Landorus-T.

Articuno pairs well with Gliscor, as it is immune to Electric-type moves, and it can switch into Knock Off to prevent any attempt to take out Articuno's Heavy-Duty Boots, provided it's already poisoned. Additionally, Gliscor can switch into Fire- and Steel-type attacks and hit foes back with Earthquake. Corviknight and Skarmory form a defensive core with Articuno, as they both serve as physical walls, and Articuno serves as a special wall. IronPress Corviknight and Skarmory easily take down physical threats such as Bisharp, Ogerpon-C, and Weavile. Corviknight also removes entry hazards using Defog in case Articuno's Heavy-Duty Boots have been removed. In return, Articuno checks special threats like Greninja and Kyurem. Landorus-T also enjoys Articuno's company, as Articuno can wall super effective Ice-type moves. In exchange, Landorus-T removes threats like Ceruledge and Empoleon. Tornadus-T also benefits from Articuno's ability to take out threats like Clodsire, Enamorus, and Primarina. Enamorus is a great partner for Articuno, as it can revenge kill Rock-types that beat Articuno such as Tyranitar, Kleavor, and Hisuian Arcanine.

vgc2024.overview:
• Articuno has a unique niche in the metagame thanks strong Ice-type STAB attacks and great bulk. Blizzard allows Articuno to tear through common cores utilizing Rillaboom, Landorus, and Raging Bolt.

  • Alolan Ninetales is mandatory with Articuno, patching up Blizzard's accuracy and amplifying its bulk and damage output through snow, Aurora Veil, and Helping Hand. Landorus makes for a great offensive partner, threatening Ice-resistant foes like Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Kingambit. Articuno is capable of removing Ground-immune foes like Dragonite and opposing Landorus in return.

  • Articuno's lack of coverage means the aforementioned Ice-resistant Pokemon such as Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Kingambit are problematic. Opposing weather from setters like Sunny Day and Rain Dance Tornadus are also an issue, as Articuno becomes a lot easier to remove without the added bulk and accurate Blizzards.

Choice Specs.description:
• Blizzard is used as Articuno's primary Ice-type STAB move, as it threatens both foes. Ice Beam is used for a strong single-target attack, and Freeze-Dry is chosen to threaten Water-types like Ogerpon-W, Urshifu-R, and Terastallized Amoonguss, which otherwise take it's hits exceptionally well. Sheer Cold is preferred in the last moveslot to threaten bulky Ice-resistant foes such as Incineroar, Dondozo, and Kingambit.

  • Choice Specs allows Articuno to 2HKO Flutter Mane and Terastallized Ogerpon-W with Ice Beam and Freeze-Dry, respectively.

  • The given EV spread lets Articuno almost always avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Dazzling Gleam and almost always survive Ogerpon-H's Tera Fire Ivy Cudgel under snow and Aurora Veil.

  • Articuno utilizes Tera Ice to shed its weakness to Raging Bolt's Thunderclap and keep the Defense boost from snow as well as make up for its mediocre damage output. This is because snow and Aurora Veil allow Articuno to function in seemingly bad matchups without a defensive Tera type.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Hurricane is less reliable than Freeze-Dry but is stronger and much more significant against foes that resist Ice such as Typhlosion, Sneasel, and Beartic. A more offensive EV spread using Hurricane can catch faster or more offensive Pokemon expecting to get the jump on Articuno off-guard, letting Articuno nail foes weak to Freeze-Dry like Rock Blast Sandaconda and Clawitzer while still maintaining its good bulk. However, Articuno is not very strong on its own and tends to be outclassed by other offensive pivots like Mesprit, Passsimian, and Whimsicott for their superior power, coverage, and utility from moves like Knock Off, Trick, and Switcheroo. Tera Ground alleviates Articuno's 4x Rock weakness and gives it an immunity to Electric to enable it to block Volt Switch, but it worsens Articuno's matchups against specially offensive Grass-types like Whimsicott, Calm Mind Virizion, and Alolan Exeggutor that it's meant to check.

Checks and Counters

Rock-types and Rock-type Coverage: Articuno's 4x Rock weakness makes Rock-type moves a huge threat to it. Regirock and Lycanroc can threaten out Articuno and use it as an opportunity to set up entry hazards. Naclstack cannot get frozen, can recover off chip damage from Articuno, and wears Articuno down with Salt Cure. Sandaconda and Virizion commonly run Rock-type coverage but must be wary of Articuno's Freeze-Dry and strong Hurricane.

Item Removal: Articuno depends on its Heavy-Duty Boots to avoid losing 50% of its HP to Stealth Rock as it switches in, so losing them hurts its longevity and pushes it to Terastallize. Mesprit is a common special attacker that can lure Articuno in and threaten to use Knock Off or give it a Choice item with Trick. Indeedee-F and Whimsicott respectively run Trick and Switcheroo.

Steel-types: Orthworm shrugs off attacks from Articuno, threatens it with its Steel-type STAB moves, and can set up Coil or entry hazards on it. Magneton is only chipped by Articuno's attacks, threatens it with its STAB moves, and can keep up momentum if Articuno switches out with its STAB Volt Switch.

Electric-types: Jolteon, Rotom, and Alolan Raichu resist Hurricane, threaten Articuno with their Electric-type STAB moves, and can gain momentum with Volt Switch. All three of the Electric-types can use setup moves to blow through Articuno.

Fire-types: Charizard and Typhlosion overcome Articuno's massive special bulk thanks to their super effective STAB attacks. Although Typhlosion resists Freeze-Dry, it prefers not to take damage in order to preserve the power of its Eruption. However, they struggle to break through Tera Dragon Articuno.

Special Wall.description:
Amazing bulk and reliable recovery make Articuno a cool special wall in the ZU metagame. Special attackers like Whimsicott and Arboliva struggle to break through Articuno on their own. Roost keeps Articuno healthy and lets it take repeated hits from special wallbreakers like Alolan Exeggutor and Clawitzer while stonewalling more passive Pokemon like Dipplin and Cryogonal. Freeze-Dry has the best coverage and reliability of any of Articuno's moves, nailing Grass- and Water-type special attackers like Arboliva and Clawitzer. U-turn helps Articuno keep up momentum against wallbreakers that might switch in against it like Charizard, Typhlosion, and Magneton. Haze immediately removes boosts from special setup users like Mesprit and Farigiraf. Roar is an alternative to Haze that lets Articuno rack up residual damage from entry hazards, but it forces Articuno to move second and fails if the target is the last active member of its team. Tera Dragon helps Articuno beat Fire-types it struggles against like Charizard and Typhlosion. Tera Steel gives Articuno a Toxic immunity and lets it more reliably check attackers like Muk, Alolan Exeggutor, and Farigiraf.

Articuno is a great choice for balance teams in need of a specially defensive Pokemon. However, Articuno can also support more offensive teams thanks to U-turn enabling teammates like Typhlosion, Charizard, and Clawitzer. Pokemon vulnerable to Grass-types and special attackers such as Sandaconda and Dipplin greatly appreciate Articuno's support, and they can assist it against threatening physical attackers like Primeape and Lycanroc, respectively. Articuno can form cores with other pivots like Primeape and Jolteon, helping it to keep up momentum and support its teammates despite being a wall. Articuno's 4x weakness to Rock is a major vulnerability that can be covered by partners like Virizion, Orthworm, and Sandslash. Entry hazard setting partners like Naclstack, Regirock, and Sandslash complement Articuno running Roar, as Articuno racks up hazard damage with Roar, forces Dipplin out even if it Terastallizes, and pressures other Pokemon vulnerable to hazards like Muk and Regirock to switch in. Knock Off users like Mesprit and Primeape support Articuno if it runs Roar to rack up entry hazard chip damage by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes dependent on them to avoid hazard damage such as opposing Articuno, Sandslash, and Charizard. Articuno struggles with Fire-types like Typhlosion and Charizard, so Muk and Regirock partner well with it by bolstering against these bad matchups. Steel-types like Orthworm and Magneton can respectively set up on Articuno and break through it, so teammates like Primeape and Virizion can threaten them for Articuno.

Brrrd (Specially defensive) (Flying).description: Articuno is a useful specially defensive Pokemon for Flying teams thanks to its ability to comfortably take special Ice-type attacks that can otherwise pose a major threat to Flying teams like Ice Beam from Choice Specs Greninja and Kyurem. Substitute takes advantage of Articuno's ability, Pressure, helping it to viably run PP stall against weaker foes such as Mega Sableye, Pecharunt, Porygon2, and Mega Venusaur. U-Turn instead lets Articuno act as a slow pivot to keep up momentum for its team. Haze is a rare anti-setup tool available for Flying teams, letting Articuno negate stat boosts from setup sweepers like Kommo-o, Tapu Fini, and Omastar, granting Articuno more PP to outstall SubRoost Kyurem when paired with Substitute. Whirlwind is an alternative anti-setup move that pairs especially well with entry hazards. Heal Bell could also be considered to let Articuno act as a cleric in the face of status-heavy matchups like Poison and Ghost. The given EV spread ensures Articuno outspeeds Jolly Azumarill and Ursaluna while being as specially bulky as possible, notably it allows Articuno to avoid getting 2HKOed by Nidoking's Flamethrower or Thunderbolt. Zapdos is an excellent partner for Articuno, as it can shock other Flying-types that Articuno struggles to beat like Corviknight, Celesteela, and Moltres. Articuno in return threatens Brambleghast as well as Ground-types like Gliscor and Mega Swampert for Zapdos, forming a strong BoltBeam combination for Flying. Physically defensive partners like Corviknight and Celesteela are helpful for their ability to come in on various Steel- and Rock-type attacks that threaten Articuno, while Articuno comes in on powerful Ice-type special attacks that can muscle through them. Ground-types like Gliscor or the Landorus formes are also useful partners, as they can switch in on Electric- and Rock-type attacks for Articuno. Articuno in return can come in on special Water- and Ice-type attacks and threaten Water-types with its Freeze-Dry.

Defensive.description:
Zapdos is a defensive pivot that is able to take hits, spread status, and build momentum for its team. Volt Switch is a strong option for a pivoting move, being both STAB-boosted and non-contact, but U-turn is a solid alternative to avoid being blocked by Ground-types like Gliscor and Ting-Lu. Thunder Wave is a powerful support move for slowing down the opposing team, crippling foes like Iron Moth and Darkrai, whereas Discharge should only be used with U-turn to still give it an Electric-type STAB that also allows Zapdos to paralyze foes, albeit less consistent. Additionally, Discharge even allows Zapdos to paralyze foes that are otherwise not threatened by Thunder Wave, like Gholdengo and Hatterene. Heat Wave is an option that gives Zapdos a coverage option to hit Iron Treads while also 2HKOing other offensive Steel-types like Kingambit and Gholdengo. Heavy-Duty Boots is important for mitigating Zapdos's weakness to Stealth Rock. Tera Steel gives Zapdos favorable matchups against foes like Kyurem and Galarian Slowking, allowing it to resist attacks like Ice Beam and become immune to status moves like Toxic while giving it the opportunity to spread paralysis, which it may not have been able to do otherwise. Tera Grass provides a Water resistance, allowing Zapdos to more easily check Hisuian Samurott and Ogerpon-W. Tera Fairy is very useful for giving Zapdos a Dark resistance, allowing it to take hits from Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge and Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave, thus providing more chances for Static to activate, as well as emergency Dragon immunity against Dragapult. Tera Water provides a Water and Fire resistance against foes like Primarina, Hisuian Samurott, and Cinderace while granting an Ice resistance against Weavile similar to Tera Steel. Most of the EVs are put into Zapdos's Defense, with 16 Speed EVs allowing it to outspeed neutral-natured base 70s like Volcanion.

Zapdos is extremely useful on balance teams. Galarian Slowking is an excellent choice of teammate to tank special attacks from threats like Kyurem and Iron Valiant, while Zapdos can help it in return by switching into Ground-type moves that threaten it from Pokemon like Great Tusk and Landorus-T, pivoting back and forth between each other to support this. Zapdos can also form strong defensive cores with other bulky Pokemon like Zamazenta and Ting-Lu. Zamazenta is able to deal with less favorable matchups for Zapdos, such as Kyurem and Weavile, and Zapdos is able to help by pivoting to it safely. Ting-Lu can support Zapdos by setting entry hazards that can wear down foes like Gholdengo and Walking Wake so that they can be KOed by Zapdos more easily. Hex Gholdengo becomes much stronger with Zapdos as a paralysis-spreading partner, and it is then able to support Zapdos and its teammates with speed control, taking out threats like Dragapult and Darkrai. Zapdos struggles to make progress against common Ground-types like Gliscor, which are immune to Volt Switch, thus preventing it from pivoting. Gliscor can also threaten Zapdos with Knock Off. Teammates like Weavile and Kyurem are great at putting pressure on these counters, and they in turn appreciate Zapdos's ability to get them in safely. While Weavile and Kyurem make good teammates, they also make difficult foes for Zapdos, both of them outspeeding and KOing it. The aforementioned Zamazenta as well as Kingambit can put pressure on these threats. In exchange, Zapdos can help by taking hits from Pokemon like Great Tusk and opposing Zamazenta and crippling these threats with Static and Thunder Wave, giving a teammate like Kingambit more chances to sweep. Knock Off users like Gliscor and Tinkaton threaten to remove Zapdos's Heavy-Duty Boots. Pokemon that can take hits from Knock Off, like Clefable and Gliscor, are great at helping Zapdos avoid this.

Offensive.description:
Offensive Zapdos stands out as a very proactive Pokemon that can help gain momentum and chip down important walls for its team while taking on dangerous foes such as Great Tusk and Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta. Volt Switch allows Zapdos to get out of difficult matchups safely such as against Galarian Slowking and Raging Bolt. Heat Wave hits Iron Treads for super effective damage, which can otherwise completely wall Zapdos, while also severely damaging other Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Kingambit that might be able to take a hit or two from it. Roost keeps Zapdos healthy over the course of a game so it can continue checking Pokemon like Scizor and battering opposing defensive cores. Weather Ball can be used over Heat Wave if Zapdos is paired with Galarian Slowking, giving it Ice-type coverage to snipe an otherwise solid check in specially defensive Gliscor while providing a strong hit against other foes like Raging Bolt, Dragonite, and opposing Zapdos. Heavy-Duty Boots allow Zapdos to switch in more easily in the face of Stealth Rock. Tera Fire allows Zapdos to OHKO Iron Treads with Heat Wave while also giving it a resistance to Ice-type attacks from Pokemon such as Weavile and Kyurem in a pinch.

Zapdos fits best on balance teams, which heavily appreciate its ability to output great damage while checking Pokemon such as Kingambit and Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta. Due to its lack of bulk investment, Zapdos cannot reliably switch into Pokemon such as Ogerpon-W and Dragon Dance Dragonite. Thus, teammates such as Corviknight and Pecharunt are crucial to help it take on these powerful foes. Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking and Iron Crown that can take on special attackers are incredibly useful, as they can form pivot cores to weaken opposing defensive structures, and Zapdos can help take on Pokemon such as Kingambit that they may otherwise struggle with. Pokemon such as Kyurem and Rillaboom that struggle with Steel-types such as Iron Treads and Kingambit heavily appreciate Zapdos luring them in with Heat Wave, while in return, they can take on foes such as Ting-Lu that Zapdos may struggle with. Zapdos struggles immensely with Raging Bolt. Therefore, checks such as Ting-Lu and Iron Treads are very much appreciated; in return, Zapdos can handle Pokemon such as Zamazenta and Great Tusk that might threaten out its partners. Zapdos can effectively lure in and KO Pokemon such as Hisuian Samurott, Gholdengo, and Pecharunt by using its high Speed and powerful attacks, which means partners such as Iron Crown, Dragonite, and Gholdengo that typically struggle a lot against them heavily appreciate its support. Ice-type attackers such as Weavile and Kyurem are great teammates, as they can take on common Ground-types such as Ting-Lu and Gliscor that Zapdos otherwise can struggle against, and in return, Zapdos can help them get in through Volt Switch and take on Fighting-types such as Zamazenta and Keldeo that they may struggle against. Pokemon such as Dragapult like the extra damage that Zapdos outputs with Hurricane to help chip down Pokemon such as Ting-Lu; they form a pivoting core together to switch into each other's checks.

Defensive.description:
Zapdos is a key defensive piece on teams due to its typing and bulk, letting it handle Pokemon like Great Tusk, Urshifu-R, and Zamazenta, crippling them with Static for its teammates. Heat Wave allows Zapdos to deal meaningful damage to Pokemon that would usually come in against it, like Gholdengo and Ferrothorn, as well as letting it become a stopgap for Kingambit. Defog allows it to remove entry hazards for its teammates as well as itself if loses its Heavy-Duty Boots, as it has a good matchup against common hazard setters like Ferrothorn and Landorus-T. Hidden Power Ice allows it to get a surprise 2HKO on Gliscor, as well as giving Zapdos a more reliable option against Garchomp and Landorus-T. 72 Speed EVs allow Zapdos to outspeed Modest Heatran.

Zapdos can easily be slot in on a defensive backbone on bulky offense and balance teams looking for a solid defensive pivot, since it is able to easily take a hit and bring in its teammates. Pokemon like Mega Medicham and Kingambit can also take advantage of the paralysis that Zapdos spreads to outspeed Pokemon like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant that would otherwise threaten them. Kingambit in particular can threaten Pokemon like Gholdengo, Mega Latios, and Weavile that would normally force Zapdos out while also trapping Pokemon like Gholdengo and Galarian Slowking, while Zapdos can chip down Fighting-types like Great Tusk and Zamazenta, which would normally stop a Kingambit sweep. Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Weavile also appreciate Zapdos bringing them in on Pokemon like Heatran and Raging Bolt, respectively, while also eliminating Ground-types like Garchomp, Gliscor, and Ting-Lu so that Zapdos can keep on pivoting without worrying about Volt Switch being blocked. Knock Off users like the aforementioned Weavile as well as Gliscor, Mega Tyranitar, and Kingambit can also prove annoying for Zapdos, as they can remove its Heavy-Duty Boots, forcing it to take Stealth Rock damage and get chipped down over the course of the game, so Pokemon that can deal with these foes, like Zamazenta and Urshifu-R, or Pokemon that can absorb Knock Off from these Pokemon for Zapdos, like Mega Tyranitar and your own Gliscor, can go a long way in keeping Zapdos healthy. Great Tusk in particular can remove hazards for Zapdos should its Heavy-Duty Boots get removed by Knock Off, so it can still switch into Great Tusk's checks for it like Urshifu-R and Alomomola without getting chipped down.

Offensive.description:
Zapdos serves as a great wallbreaker, boasting natural bulk that allows it to take hits from physical attackers like Rillaboom and Urshifu-R and threaten them with paralysis through Static. If rain is active, Weather Ball lets Zapdos nuke defensive Ground-types such as Iron Treads, Gliscor, and Landorus-T, while Supersonic Skystrike can be used to finish off weakened defensive Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Galarian Slowking or on important turns when the risk of missing a Hurricane would prove way too costly.

Zapdos can be a great addition to offense teams where its ability to inflict foes with paralysis is greatly appreciated. Zapdos has the ability to loosely check Fighting-types like Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Mega Medicham, which can go a long way for teammates like Kingambit and Ferrothorn. The aforementioned Fighting-types can also be great teammates to Zapdos, as they help in dealing with Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Mega Tyranitar. Additionally, Great Tusk can remove Stealth Rock. When used on rain, staples like Barraskewda and Mega Swampert appreciate Zapdos's help in dealing with bulky Water-types such as Alomomola and Slowbro as well as Grass-types like Ogerpon-W and Ferrothorn. Galarian Slowking and Raging Bolt are both frustrating for Zapdos to break, so teammates such as Pursuit Kingambit or bulky Ground-types like Iron Treads and Ting-Lu are good to deal with them.

Clear Amulet.description:
• Eerie Impulse enables Zapdos to beat the likes of Primarina, Sylveon, non-Choice Band Hisuian Goodra, Spectrier, and Volcarona.
  • Clear Amulet helps Zapdos by blocking moves that lower Special Defense like Fake Tears from Sylveon, Acid Spray from Hisuian Goodra and Icy Wind from Primarina.
  • This EV spread allows Zapdos to survive Timid Choice Specs Spectrier's Hyper Beam and grants good chances of surviving Adamant Urshifu-R's Choice Band Surging Strikes.
  • Zapdos should always Eerie Impulse on the first turn against Volcanion, since Choice Scarf Volcanion can outspeed and 2HKO Zapdos if it uses Thunderbolt.
  • Zapdos struggles against physical attackers like Ursaluna and non-Choice Specs Hoopa-U. Pokemon that can outspeed and deal super effective damage to Zapdos like Meowscarada, Chien-Pao, and Jolly Choice Band Landorus-T also beat it. It is advised for Zapdos to be used with a Steel-type Pokemon like Corviknight to tackle these weaknesses.

Life Orb.description:
• Life Orb Zapdos is able to dish out high damage against several of the Water- and Fighting-type Pokemon in the tier, such as Primarina, both Urshifu formes, and Iron Valiant.
  • Hurricane deals with Urshifu-S, non-Substitute Ogerpon-W, and Iron Valiant.
  • Thunderbolt targets Urshifu-R, Volcanion, Galarian Moltres, and Corviknight.
  • Protect is helpful to deal with Custap Berry users such as Primarina.
  • Charge doubles the power of Thunderbolt while increasing Zapdos's Special Defense, dealing massive damage to Pokemon like Choice Specs Primarina and Assault Vest Azumarill.
  • U-turn is pivotal for dealing with non-bulky variants of Hoopa-U.
  • Maximum Special Attack investment allows Zapdos to deal with most Primarina sets without needing to use Charge, while the HP and Defense EVs help Zapdos survive a Choice Band Urshifu-S's Wicked Blow.
