  • Zapdos can be often paired up with Water-type Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Primarina, as they can usually handle the Rock- and Ground-types that would usually pose a problem for it such as Donphan, Rhyperior, Landorus-T, and Hisuian Arcanine.

Specially Defensive (Electric).description:
Years pass, but Zapdos remains a staple on Electric teams thanks to its good special bulk, Ground type immunity, access to Heat Wave, and two great abilities. Pressure is preferred for this set, given its better synergy with Substitute, as it allows Zapdos to effectively PP stall Draco Meteors from the likes of Latios and Raging Bolt. Discharge is preferred over Zapdos's other Electric-type STAB moves, since it lets it spread paralysis among foes like Dragonite, Latios, and Dragapult with much more ease, preventing them from becoming long-term threats. Heat Wave makes Zapdos a potent Steel- and Grass-types breaker, leaving only Heatran unscathed, while Hurricane can put more pressure onto Fighting and Grass teams. Substitute often gives Zapdos two chances to paralyze its foe and to let it better use Pressure. With Zapdos's good general bulk, a Substitute can most of the time take more than one hit from weak attacks such as Knock Off and Dragon Tail from Hisuian Goodra and Poison Jab from Clodsire, making its target effectively lose four PP per Substitute. The given spread maximizes Zapdos's special bulk while ensuring it outspeeds Adamant Bisharp, Cloyster, and defensive variants of Gholdengo.

With its specially defensive profile, Zapdos is best paired with Pokemon that can take on physical moves as well as Ice moves, such as Rotom-W. Rotom-W's good typing lets it come in on Mamoswine, Gliscor, and Iron Hands and cripple them with Will-O-Wisp or outright KO them with Hydro Pump. With Will-O-Wisp support, Zapdos can more easily handle physical foes and can even put a Substitute in front of some of them. Assault Vest Iron Hands and Magnezone offer some more specific walling capabilities, with the former improving the Dragon matchup and the latter helping in the Fairy matchup by putting a stop to Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Calm Mind Hatterene. In return, they both benefit tremendously from Zapdos's Ground immunity and its ability to PP stall problematic moves like Draco Meteor and Luster Purge in Iron Hands's case. Sandy Shocks provides invaluable support through entry hazard stacking; it can also address sun variants of Fire teams with Protosynthesis's Speed boost and Earth Power and Power Gem, preventing Volcarona from wreaking havoc. Regieleki provides much-needed support through dual screens, ensuring Zapdos can answer even Choice Specs Flutter Mane, and can paralyze targets to ensure Zapdos always has the initiative in its interactions. Pawmot can deal offensively with pesky Ground-type foes like Landorus, Garchomp, and Mamoswine with Ice Punch and Close Combat, and it can give Zapdos a second breath with Revival Blessing. Lastly, Raging Bolt is a formidable late-game sweeper that benefits a lot from Zapdos's ability to weaken foes both through PP stalling and direct damage. Raging Bolt is also a more direct answer to rain Water teams by threatening them with Thunderclap.

SubRoost (Flying).description:
Zapdos, thanks to a solid Speed stat and offensive prowess, finds a slot on Flying teams as an incredible threat versus opposing Flying- and Water-types. Substitute can be used to take advantage of passive foes such as Corviknight and Klefki to safely pressure the opposing team. Discharge spreads paralysis against foes such as Heatran and Hoopa-U while dealing with Water- and Flying-types such as Primarina, Pelipper, and Corviknight. Hurricane deals with problematic Grass- and Ground-types that handle Zapdos's Discharge such as Amoonguss, Sinistcha, Gliscor, and Swampert. The primary EV spread prevents Gliscor's Knock Off from breaking Substitute while always OHKOing Urshifu-R and 2HKOing Corviknight after Stealth Rock damage. The second EV Spread can be used to allow Zapdos to always set up a Substitute against Toxapex and OHKO Skarmory.

Both Skarmory and Corviknight serve as excellent teammates to Zapdos, as their Steel typing allows them to take on threats such as Weavile, Mamoswine, and Ogerpon-C. Skarmory continues to assist Zapdos by being able to set entry hazards to chip down Zapdos's checks such as Swampert and Iron Treads, while Corviknight can pivot Zapdos in with U-turn. Gliscor and the Landorus formes appreciate Zapdos dealing with Water-types like Primarina and Keldeo, and Zapdos appreciates them being able to deal with Steel- and Electric-types such as Heatran, Hisuian Goodra, Magnezone, and Raging Bolt. Choice Scarf Enamorus handles Dragon-types such as Latios, Garchomp, and Kyurem that can threaten Zapdos. Articuno provides a solid special wall that is capable of removing Ground-types such as Gastrodon and Gliscor with Freeze-Dry. Dragonite can deal with special walls such as Galarian Slowking and Blissey that handle Zapdos and appreciates Zapdos removing physical walls such as Skarmory and Sinistcha. Tornadus-T can handle threats such as the Ogerpon formes and appreciates threats like Sneasler and Meowscarada getting paralyzed to help offset the low accuracy of Bleakwind, giving it a safer time to setup with Nasty Plot.

Choice Specs (Electric).description:
Choice Specs Zapdos is a potent wallbreaker for Electric teams, being able to threaten Pokemon that give its teammates a hard time such as Great Tusk, Gastrodon, specially defensive Iron Treads, and Landorus-T. Aside from that, its Flying typing provides Electric teams an immunity to Ground and a resistance to Fighting. Hurricane is Zapdos's strongest STAB move, being able to OHKO Sableye, Amoonguss, and possibly Quagsire, and also being able to 2HKO physically defensive Skeledirge and Ursaluna. Zapdos can also take advantage of matchups against rain teams by being able to spam Hurricane without fear of missing. Volt Switch allows Zapdos to bring in teammates safely against special walls like Assault Vest Iron Hands, Assault Vest Galarian Slowking, and Heatran. Heat Wave provides Zapdos great coverage, allowing it to 2HKO Magnezone, as well as Klefki under Light Screen and Iron Treads. Static has a chance to paralyze Pokemon that make contact with Zapdos such as Dragonite and Mimikyu.

Sandy Shocks makes for a great partner, being able to provide entry hazard support with both Stealth Rock and Spikes, as well as being able to threaten Heatran with Earth Power. Regieleki is another great partner, as it is able to remove hazards with Rapid Spin so that Zapdos can switch in more often without losing a good amount of its health to Stealth Rock. It is also able to outspeed Pokemon that outspeed Zapdos such as Flutter Mane and non-Choice Scarf Greninja. Pokemon with great special bulk such as Assault Vest Galarian Slowking and Tyranitar can be tough for Zapdos, with the latter being able to threaten it with Stone Edge. Hence, Iron Hands pairs well with Zapdos, as it is able to threaten Galarian Slowking with Earthquake and Tyranitar with Drain Punch. In return, Zapdos can switch into anticipated Ground-type attacks from the likes of Great Tusk and Iron Treads. Magnezone is another great partner, being able to threaten Hatterene and Flutter Mane. Lastly, Zapdos's wallbreaking opens up sweeping opportunities for fast sweepers such as Nasty Plot Rotom-W and Choice Scarf Pawmot. Both of them can beat Landorus-T with Hydro Pump and Ice Punch, respectively, and Pawmot has the added merit of potentially reviving Zapdos with Revival Blessing.

Offensive Pivot (Electric).description: This is a sample set as we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Zapdos can opt for a physically defensive set with Intimidate or Fluffy, although it would often be switching into Knock Off and therefore requires strong entry hazard control. Zapdos can also run Choice Specs to be a stronger wallbreaker or Choice Scarf for speed control, although it would also be weak to Stealth Rock and still lack the power to beat common checks like Iron Treads, Ting-Lu, and Swampert. Volt Switch is another pivoting option over U-turn, although it can be blocked and is far less consistent.

Checks and Counters

Electric-immune Pokemon: Ground-types like Swampert, Iron Treads, and Ting-Lu as well as Volt Absorb users like Corviknight all wall Zapdos easily.

Special Attackers: Strong special attackers like Choice Specs Latios, Deoxys-S, and Gholdengo can potentially outspeed and threaten Zapdos.

RegenVest Users: Zapdos struggles with breaking through RegenVest users such as Iron Hands, Roaring Moon, and Hisuian Goodra.

Primordial Sea.description:
Zapdos leverages Primordial Sea to boost the accuracy of its Thunder and Hurricane, letting it be a threatening special attacker and offensive pivot. Weather Ball is another move that has fantastic synergy with Primordial Sea, although Zapdos would have to give up either Hurricane or U-turn, both of which are essential. Weather Ball allows Zapdos to wear down Volt Absorb Corviknight and non-Bulletproof Iron Treads, while Roost keep Zapdos healthy to check Fire-types when Primordial Sea is active like Cinderace, Heatran, and Ogerpon-H as well as Ground-types like Great Tusk and Landorus-T. Zapdos can opt for either a offensive or bulky EV spread, although it needs 184 Speed EVs with a Timid nature to outspeed maximum Speed Landorus-T and Zarude.

Zapdos fits on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its mix of offensive pressure and defensive utility. Wallbreaking teammates like Choice Specs Gholdengo, Ogerpon-H, and Latios appreciate the U-turn support to get them safely on the field as well as the semi-reliable paralysis support offered by Thunder, which lets them outspeed Roaring Moon. Zapdos also threatens two of the most common RegenVest users in Primarina and Manaphy, which helps other wallbreakers such as Chien-Pao and Roaring Moon. Zapdos is walled by Bulletproof Iron Treads and RegenVest users like Ting-Lu, Iron Hands, and Swampert, so teammates like Garchomp and Zamazenta can help break through them; in exchange, Zapdos can force out physical walls like Corviknight and Great Tusk. Zapdos can be susceptible to Stealth Rock if it gets its Heavy-Duty Boots removed by Knock Off from Great Tusk, so entry hazard removal like Corviknight and Iron Treads is important, while Zapdos can handle the Fire-types that threaten them. Zapdos is also a solid switch-in to Choice Band Zamazenta, although it does have to be wary of Stone Edge on the switch as well as from non-Choice Band sets.

No Guard.description:
Zapdos is able to take advantage of No Guard to spam its normally inaccurate but powerful STAB moves and reliably spread paralysis with Zap Cannon. U-turn does solid damage to Roaring Moon, and lets Zapdos pivot out against special walls like Swampert and Iron Treads, generating momentum for its team. Roost gives Zapdos longevity, letting it check Great Tusk, while Heat Wave hits Volt Absorb Corviknight and Bulletproof Iron Treads, which normally shut down Zapdos.

Zapdos fits on balance and bulky offense teams, where it enables other offensive wallbreakers with paralysis and U-turn support. Zapdos matches up well against physically defensive Corviknight and Manaphy, so it's a great partner to help physical attackers like Kingambit and Chien-Pao wallbreak. The Ogerpon formes are especially good teammates, since they outspeed and threaten paralyzed Roaring Moon, even if it has Choice Scarf, while also handling Swampert and Iron Treads. Zapdos is weak to physical threats like Chien-Pao and Zamazenta, so it needs backup from physically defensive walls like Corviknight and Pecharunt. Zapdos is also threatened by faster special attackers such as Latios and Deoxys-S, so RegenVest users like Swampert and Manaphy are appreciated.

Magic Guard (Clefairy).description: 152 Speed EVs without a boosting nature allows it to outspeed max Speed Adamant Great Tusk

Fur Coat (Persian A).description: 152 Speed EVs allows it to outspeed max Speed Jolly Great Tusk

Choice Specs (Electric).description: With Choice Specs equipped, Zapdos's already amazing Special Attack is boosted to even greater heights, turning it into an incredible wallbreaker. Its Flying typing also grants an invaluable Ground immunity for Electric teams. Hurricane is Zapdos's most powerful move, threatening a variety of Pokemon that resist or are immune to Electric such as Mega Venusaur and Gastrodon. Heat Wave beats Steel-types such as Mega Scizor, Iron Treads, and Ferrothorn, thus making it an incredible asset in the Steel and Grass matchups. Hidden Power Ice cleanly OHKOes Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Garchomp; alternatively, Hidden Power Grass can be used if reliably eliminating Gastrodon and Swampert is more important. Volt Switch lets Zapdos switch out of its checks like Tyranitar and Blissey, keeping momentum in favor of Zapdos's team. As dangerous as Zapdos is, it is highly susceptible to Stealth Rock; hence, Rotom-W is a great partner that can use Defog while also helping Zapdos beat Ground-types thanks to Hydro Pump. Iron Hands and Zeraora help Zapdos wallbreak by wearing down special walls like Heatran, Blissey, and Clodsire. Regieleki and Alolan Raichu can take advantage of Zapdos weakening teams and removing Ground-types so that they can clean up with their deadly Rising Voltage later in the game.

Physically Defensive Pivot (Electric).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Defog (Flying).description: Zapdos is one of the few Defog options Flying teams have access to that heavily punishes Gholdengo. Aside from this perk, defensive Zapdos is also able to switch into Iron Valiant, Mega Pinsir, and Mega Scizor thanks to its decent bulk and typing. Heat Wave deters Gholdengo from switching in to block Defog, lets Zapdos check Mega Scizor and Bisharp, and roasts Ferrothorn and Jirachi. Alternatively, Hurricane when paired with Discharge makes Water teams unable to switch into Zapdos, and it lets Zapdos answer Mega Venusaur, Mega Pinsir, and Great Tusk. Volt Switch pivots in teammates like Mega Charizard Y and Dragonite, letting Zapdos keep the momentum going. Pressure ensures entry hazards stay off by draining the opponent's Stealth Rock PP, but Static is useful for punishing Triple Axel users like Mega Gallade and Mega Lopunny, both of which are problematic for Flying teams due to their high Speed. The given EV spread allow Zapdos to avoid the 2HKO from Choice Scarf Tapu Lele's attacks and Mega Lopunny's Return and the OHKO from +2 Iron Valiant's Ice Punch, allowing Zapdos to retaliate or pivot out to the appropriate teammate. 16 Speed EVs let it outspeed Adamant Bisharp, and a Modest nature allows Zapdos to 2HKO Gholdengo. The alternative EV spread lets Zapdos outspeed Urshifu-R and OHKO it with Discharge. Mega Charizard Y and Dragonite appreciate Zapdos's pivoting capabilitie, and they deal with Heatran, Blissey, and Gliscor, which readily check Zapdos. Celesteela is the preferred Steel-type partner to Zapdos, as it deals with Fairy- and Ice-types like Mega Diancie, Alolan Ninetales, and Kyurem, which take advantage of Zapdos. In return, Zapdos keeps hazards off to improve Celesteela's staying power. Nasty Plot Tornadus-T checks Ogerpon-W, Kommo-o, and Iron Valiant for Zapdos and loves its ability to pivot it in against Mega Venusaur to use as setup fodder.

monotype.overview:
(Flying)

Often overshadowed by other speed control options such as Choice Scarf Enamorus and Landorus-T as well as wallbreakers like Landorus and Dragonite, it tends to be difficult to slot Galarian Zapdos into the average Flying team. However, Galarian Zapdos is incredible in the Steel and Dark matchups; doesn't fear Aqua Jet from Urshifu-R, unlike the Landorus formes; and, in contrast to Enamorus, takes neutral damage from Stealth Rock while having access to a pivoting move in U-turn.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

(Flying)

Choiced Attacker Galarian Zapdos may opt for Thunderous Kick over Close Combat to avoid the stat drops while also pressuring walls with a Defense drop; however, Close Combat is significantly more powerful and allows it to OHKO Ting-Lu and Archaludon with a Choice Band.

Choiced Attacker (Flying).description:
Galarian Zapdos possesses a great STAB combination, reliable Speed tier, and great ability in Defiant, allowing it to threaten Dark and Steel teams. Close Combat targets Dark- and Steel-types such as Hydreigon, Hisuian Goodra, and Heatran. Brave Bird hits Fighting-resistant and immune threats like Amoonguss, Iron Valiant, and Brambleghast. Knock Off allows Galarian Zapdos to hit Gholdengo as well as other Ghost-types to minimize Brave Bird's recoil damage over time. U-turn allows it to predict and pivot out of switch-ins like Alomomola and Slowbro, preserving momentum and leaving behind decent chip damage. A Choice Scarf enables Galarian Zapdos to outpace and remove threats such as the Ogerpon formes, Flutter Mane, Greninja, and bulky Volcarona after a Quiver Dance; meanwhile, a Choice Band allows it to OHKO Ting-Lu and Archaludon after minor chip damage as well as 2HKO Mandibuzz, Corviknight, and Skarmory with Close Combat and Toxapex with Brave Bird.

Specially defensive Corviknight is heavily cherished as a switch-in to opposing Fairy-types like Enamorus and Flutter Mane. It also provides Defog support, removing Stealth Rock to minimize chip damage on Galarian Zapdos, which is especially important with the use of Brave Bird. In return, Galarian Zapdos threatens Hisuian Samurott, Magnezone, and especially Bisharp, which can capitalize off Corviknight's Defog via Defiant. Gliscor provides an essential Electric-type immunity, combating Raging Bolt and Iron Hands while providing entry hazards to ease Galarian Zapdos's wallbreaking. Skarmory walls physical attackers like Meowscarada and Dragonite while also providing Spikes and phazing via Whirlwind to wear down threats such as Great Tusk, physical variants of Garchomp, and Archaludon lacking Thunderbolt. Galarian Zapdos is appreciated by both Gliscor and Skarmory, as it can deter Defog users from clearing their entry hazards with Defiant. Furthermore, Galarian Zapdos removes Ice-types like Kyurem and Choice-locked Mamoswine for Gliscor as well as Fire-types such as Hisuian Arcanine, Heatran, and Volcarona for Skarmory. Landorus removes threats like Pecharunt, Zapdos, and Moltres via Earth Power and Rock Slide; using a Choice Scarf, (AC) it threatens Choice Specs Greninja and Choice Band Meowscarada as well. It values Galarian Zapdos's ability to OHKO Sinistcha, Assault Vest Gallade, and Araquanid. Assault Vest Tornadus-T is a great bulky pivot that provides utility in Knock Off and U-turn, enabling Galarian Zapdos's wallbreaking throughout the match. Tornadus-T appreciates Galarian Zapdos threatening the aforementioned Steel-types as well as Kyurem. Dragon Dance Gyarados is capable of cleaning up late-game once Galarian Zapdos has severely weakened defensive backbones, particularly Ground, as it doesn't fear Mamoswine's Ice Shard and can typically set up freely once Ting-Lu has been removed. Articuno provides a great Ice-type neutrality that allows it to handle Alolan Ninetales's and Greninja's Ice-type coverage. Moltres provides an answer to threatening wallbreakers like Ogerpon-H and Choice Band Iron Valiant.

Choice Band (Fighting).description:
Galarian Zapdos makes for a great asset to Fighting teams by virtue of its part Flying typing, easing the Fighting, Ground, and Grass matchups. Brave Bird breaks through troublesome physical walls that Fighting teams struggle with such as Amoonguss, Sinistcha, and Zamazenta, while Close Combat targets Corviknight and Skarmory. Knock Off grants coverage against Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo and Iron Crown and removes items such as Black Sludge from Toxapex and Tentacruel. Alternatively, Drill Peck is a weaker but safer option against targets like Urshifu-R and Rillaboom, as it doesn't come with recoil damage. However, using it comes with the downside of not having coverage against targets that its teammates can struggle with. U-turn allows Galarian Zapdos to act as a pivot to bring a teammate in safely while OHKOing Hoopa-U.

Choice Scarf users such as Iron Valiant and Sneasler pair well with Galarian Zapdos, as the two of them can deal with Dragon- and Fairy-types that threaten it. Iron Valiant handles the likes of Dragapult, Walking Wake, and Latias, while Sneasler deals with opposing Iron Valiant and Enamorus. In return, they appreciate Galarian Zapdos OHKOing Gholdengo with Knock Off and bringing them in with U-turn. Great Tusk makes for another great teammate, setting up Stealth Rock to support Galarian Zapdos's wallbreaking potential, serving as an asset against Fire teams thanks to Protosynthesis helping it under sun, and taking on the likes of Heatran, Ceruledge, and Hisuian Arcanine thanks to its bulk; it also provides hazard removal with Rapid Spin and an Electric immunity. Great Tusk also appreciates Galarian Zapdos handling Grass-types like Hydrapple and Amoonguss for it. Iron Hands, with its great special bulk, takes on Greninja and Flutter Mane while also forming a VoltTurn core with Galarian Zapdos, and Galarian Zapdos returns the favor by handling Great Tusk for it. Choice Scarf Keldeo threatens faster Fire- and Ground-types that can threaten Galarian Zapdos such as Choice Specs Iron Moth and Choice Scarf Landorus. Breloom immobilizes a threatening foe with Spore and deals with bulky Water-types such as Primarina and physically defensive Rotom-W. Lastly, Galarian Zapdos's wallbreaking opens up sweeping opportunities from late-game cleaners such as Hisuian Lilligant and Choice Band Zamazenta.

vgc2024.overview:
• Galarian Zapdos is one of the few Flying-type threats with powerful Flying-type STAB moves that can threaten popular metagame threats like the Ogerpon formes, the Urshifu formes, Rillaboom, and Amoonguss. Its Fighting-type STAB moves paired with Defiant can break through the popular Intimidate users Hisuian Arcanine and Incineroar.

  • Galarian Zapdos can be used in a more supportive role with Coaching next to partners like Ting-Lu and Dragonite to boost their sweeping potential and survivability on the field. Thanks to Defiant, partners boosted by Galarian Zapdos's Coaching will feel less threatened by Intimidate, as the opponent will not want to give Galarian Zapdos a free boost to its Attack.

  • Supportive Flutter Mane can slow down Galarian Zapdos with Thunder Wave, causing it to be slower than the Ogerpon formes and other threats that it normally outspeeds and making Galarian Zapdos easier to KO. Trick Room slows down the momentum of both the offensive and supportive capabilities of Galarian Zapdos by making it almost always go last. Galarian Zapdos struggles to deal any damage to Gholdengo due to its Steel / Ghost typing, which lets it set up with Nasty Plot freely and blow through with Make It Rain.

  • Ting-Lu can help Galarian Zapdos inside of Trick Room due to its low Speed and ability to threaten Flutter Mane and Gholdengo while benefiting from Coaching. Chien-Pao can indirectly support Galarian Zapdos by boosting its damage with Sword of Ruin, and Chien-Pao threatens Gholdengo and Raging Bolt. Dragonite appreciates Galarian Zapdos's support deterring Intimidate users like Incineroar with Defiant. Dragonite also appreciates Coaching boosts from Galarian Zapdos, as they, in tandem with Dragonite's ability Multiscale can make it hard to KO. Gouging Fire can use Howl as Galarian Zapdos uses Coaching, causing Gouging Fire to become extremely threatening while becoming bulkier. Sinsitcha can redirect damage away from Galarian Zapdos, reverse Trick Room so that Galarian Zapdos can regain its momentum, and provide recovery via Hospitality.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Galarian Zapdos is primarily used as a fast offensive wallbreaker that doesn't need to worry about Intimidate thanks to Defiant. The secondary mode for it is being a fast support Pokemon with Coaching to help a partner improve their offensive and defensive capabilities. Galarian Zapdos matches up particularly well against Incineroar with Close Combat, as well as Rillaboom and the Ogerpon formes with Brave Bird.

  • Close Combat is able to OHKO most Incineroar as well as Hisuian Arcanine while unboosted, and it has a chance to OHKO the Ursaluna formes with low bulk investment. Brave Bird is used for immense damage and can OHKO the Urshifu formes along with the Ogerpon formes. Dual Wingbeat is an alternative Flying-type STAB move that can break the Focus Sash of the Urshifu formes while picking them off on the same turn if Galarian Zapdos is at +1 Attack or if Sword of Ruin is active. U-turn is used to pivot from a bad situation while getting damage done on a foe. Taunt can be used to stop Trick Room from Porygon2 and Farigiraf as well as Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss.

  • Choice Scarf helps Galarian Zapdos outspeed Chien-Pao, Choice Scarf Urshifu formes, and non-Speed Booster Energy Flutter Mane.

  • The bulk gives Galarian Zapdos a high chance to survive Moonblast from bulky Flutter Mane and helps it survive five-hit Scale Shot from Dragonite. The Speed allows it to outspeed Adamant Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. The rest of the EVs along with an Adamant nature are used to maximize Galarian Zapdos's Attack, giving it a chance to OHKO Okidogi, Amoonguss, and bulky Flutter Mane with Brave Bird.

  • Tera Ghost provides an immunity to Fake Out from Incineroar so that Galarian Zapdos can keep its momentum and isn't to use Covert Cloak. Tera Ghost also provides an immunity to Extreme Speed from Hisuian Arcanine and Dragonite. Furthermore, it removes Galarian Zapdos's Fairy- and Electric-type weaknesses so that Galarian Zapdos can survive Moonblast from Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Thunderclap from Raging Bolt. However, Tera Ghost will make Galarian Zapdos weak to Sucker Punch from Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S.

Choice Band.description: Choice Band Galarian Zapdos is an excellent wallbreaker whose power is further boosted by Sword of Ruin. Boasting two powerful STAB moves with excellent neutral coverage in Close Combat and Brave Bird, Galarian Zapdos can most notably 2HKO Deoxys-D and Intimidate Corviknight. Knock Off beats Gholdengo and hinders switch-ins like Fluffy Corviknight and defensive Zapdos, while U-turn allows for pivoting against Fluffy users. Adamant is the preferred nature for better odds to 2HKO Intimidate Corviknight, while Jolly allows Galarian Zapdos to Speed tie with the plethora of base 100 Speed Pokemon, at the cost of only 3HKOing Intimidate Corviknight. Galarian Zapdos is a relatively slow and frail wallbreaker and is forced out by offensive threats such as Azelf and Chien-Pao, so it appreciates being brought in by pivots such as Azelf and Iron Moth; in return, it can threaten special walls like Swampert and Hisuian Goodra for them. Slow pivots like Corviknight and Swampert are also appreciated, as they can take a hit for it and pivot it in safely, with the former also providing entry hazard control, extending Galarian Zapdos's longevity. Galarian Zapdos struggles against Fluffy walls such as Corviknight, so Fire-types such as Ceruledge and Iron Moth make for great teammates. Stealth Rock setters such as Great Tusk and Deoxys-D are also good teammates, allowing Galarian Zapdos to always 2HKO Intimidate Corviknight; in return, it can threaten opposing Great Tusk, preventing it from removing entry hazards. Galarian Zapdos's wallbreaking prowess is further empowered when paired with other offensive threats such as Barraskewda and Roaring Moon, as they can wear down shared checks like Fluffy Corviknight.

Magic Guard.description: Galarian Zapdos is a threatening physical wallbreaker thanks to its high base Attack and powerful STAB moves in Brave Bird and Thunderous Kick. Magic Guard prevents chip damage from Stealth Rock as well as Rocky Helmet, which is commonly used by Corviknight and Skarmory. Thunderous Kick is used because the Defense drop it causes allows Galarian Zapdos to KO Pokemon like RegenVest Iron Hands with Brave Bird afterwards. Knock Off allows Galarian Zapdos to threaten switch-ins such as Gholdengo and Deoxys-D while OHKOing Iron Boulder. Galarian Zapdos can use U-turn to function as an offensive pivot as well as to switch out on uncomfortable matchups such as Corviknight, Skarmory, and Fluffy Mandibuzz, while Close Combat can be used as a second STAB option that, unlike Thunderous Kick, OHKOes Archaludon and has a very high chance to OHKO specially defensive Garganacl and Chansey. Galarian Zapdos struggles against physical walls such as Gholdengo, Corviknight, and Skarmory; special attacking wallbreakers like Sandy Shocks, Iron Moth, and Heatran are heavily appreciated, since they are able to counter them. Galarian Zapdos is also threatened by fast foes such as Dragonite, Iron Boulder, and Deoxys-S. Teammates like defensive Gholdengo and Fluffy Corviknight are appreciated to counter both Dragonite and Iron Boulder, while special walls like RegenVest Manaphy and Swampert can check Deoxys-S.

Choice Scarf (Fighting).description: Galarian Zapdos is an excellent Choice Scarf user on Fighting teams thanks to its unique set of traits within the type. Steel Wing notably OHKOes a huge threat to these teams in Mega Diancie while also nailing Tapu Lele and Alolan Ninetales. Knock Off targets Psychic- and Ghost-types like Galarian Slowking, Jirachi, and Galarian Corsola. Finally, U-turn can bring in teammates while getting chip damage on the foe as well as switching Galarian Zapdos out of bad matchups like Slowbro and Gholdengo. Iron Valiant equipped with Choice Specs or a Z-Crystal is able to break through Pokemon that wall Galarian Zapdos such as Kyurem, Latias, Raging Bolt, and Tapu Koko. Mega Gallade is another great teammate for Galarian Zapdos, as it acts as a great setup sweeper and wallbreaker with Swords Dance and greatly improves the Poison matchup. Iron Hands also pairs well, as it has a neutrality to Flying and can hit Flying-types with Ice Punch or Thunder Punch and has access to a slow Volt Switch that can bring it in safely. Iron Hands's great bulk also allows it to take on otherwise problematic threats like Enamorus-T, Tornadus-T, and Pelipper. Great Tusk is a nice support Pokemon for Galarian Zapdos, as it provides an Electric-immunity as well as Rapid Spin and Stealth Rock support, helping Galarian Zapdos get more KOs. It's also a great physical wall and can take out threats such as Iron Hands and Zeraora. In return, Galarian Zapdos handles Grass-types like Ogerpon-W, Tapu Bulu, and Mega Venusaur for it. Finally, Hisuian Lilligant can be a good team member for Galarian Zapdos, as it provides sleep support, taking counters to Galarian Zapdos out of the picture and easing the Water and Ground matchups. Hisuian Lilligant and Galarian Zapdos also make a great late-game cleaning duo.

Defensive.description:
Moltres is an excellent defensive Pokemon, using its typing and ability to punish a multitude of physical attackers in the tier, threatening a burn with Flame Body to stop pivoting from U-turn or reliably walling the likes of Zamazenta lacking Stone Edge, Kingambit, Rillaboom, and most Dragonite and Great Tusk sets. U-turn turns Moltres into a pivot, letting it get in teammates safely, keep up momentum, and chip down switch-ins like Garganacl and Alomomola. Will-O-Wisp reliably cripples physical attackers like Kingambit, Ogerpon-W, and Dragonite, even bypassing the former's Sucker Punch, and slowly chips down walls like Alomomola, Ting-Lu, and Galarian Slowking. Roar prevents Moltres from being used as setup fodder, especially by Tera Fire foes like Zamazenta and Kingambit and special attackers like Iron Valiant and Iron Moth that can't immediately threaten it out, as well as being a good way to rack up damage with entry hazards. Scorching Sands can be used to hit foes like Raging Bolt, Garganacl, Glimmora, Cinderace, and the aforementioned Tera Fire users while fishing for burns in general. Tera Fairy is a solid defensive typing that notably gives Moltres a good matchup against foes like Weavile and Dragapult while maintaining its positive matchup versus Zamazenta and Great Tusk. Tera Grass flips Moltres's Water and Electric weaknesses, letting it take on various hits from the likes of Ogerpon-W and Hisuian Samurott while being able to safely phaze Calm Mind Primarina and Raging Bolt. Terastallization in general allows Moltres to ease its weakness to Knock Off and Stealth Rock, letting it not fear huge chip damage from them. 12 Speed EVs allow Moltres to outspeed Jolly Kingambit.

Moltres is a great fit on offensive teams and more bulky teams. Its great typing and its ability to spread burn help its teammates against prominent physical attackers. Partners like Clefable and Kingambit appreciate it being able to check threats like Great Tusk and opposing Kingambit, while Clefable and Kingambit are able to switch into threats to Moltres, such as Weavile. Offensive partners like Ogerpon-W and Zamazenta appreciate Moltres's pivoting, forcing in Pokemon like Garganacl and Heatran, which have bad matchups against the aforementioned teammates. Zamazenta is also able to check Ogerpon-W with its ability's initial Defense boost. Darkrai and Weavile are also potent offensive partners, being able to amend Moltres's bad matchups such as Gliscor and Galarian Slowking by threatening huge damage on both targets. Threats to Moltres are potent attackers such as Primarina and Ogerpon-W. A partner like Galarian Slowking works well with Moltres, as it enjoys burns allowing it to switch into physical attackers, such as a burned Zamazenta, as well as being able to switch into attacks from Primarina. Offensive threats like Ogerpon and Dragapult can check Ogerpon-W, either helping in taking attacks, revenge killing, or crippling it with status. Defensive partners such as Gliscor, Great Tusk, and Corviknight can switch into Knock Off for Moltres, with Gliscor itself being able to use Knock Off and set Spikes, which pairs well with Roar variants of Moltres. Great Tusk and Corviknight offer entry hazard removal. Ground-types like Clodsire and Ting-Lu are able to cover Moltres's bad matchups against Electric-types like Raging Bolt and Zapdos, as well as providing hazards, which make Moltres's phazing more of a threat.

Moltres holds a strong place in the metagame thanks to its unique defensive profile, letting it check dangerous threats like Great Tusk, Mega Charizard Y, and Volcarona, and its good natural bulk lets it help out versus threats such as Gholdengo. U-turn allows Moltres to retain momentum for its team; this is important, as it can be somewhat passive into threats such as Heatran, Alomomola, and Toxapex on its own depending on its moveset, and it often relies on giving its teammates free switches to revenge kill or force out foes. Hurricane gives Moltres a strong STAB move that threatens Zamazenta, Volcarona, and Great Tusk. Toxic allows Moltres to cripple potential switch-ins like Mega Charizard Y, Mega Tyranitar, Ting-Lu, and Alomomola. Scorching Sands allows Moltres to appreciably threaten Heatran while also allowing it to potentially spread burns against foes such as Toxapex. Defog is a possibility in this moveslot if the team needs entry hazard removal and cannot fit it elsewhere, but Moltres is a poor defogger overall, as it doesn't reliably beat many of the tier's entry hazard setters, it is very weak to Knock Off, and Defog takes up a valuable moveslot. Roost allows Moltres to stay healthy throughout the match. A physically defensive EV spread allows Moltres to better check Great Tusk, Melmetal, and Zamazenta, whereas a specially defensive spread allows it to better check Mega Charizard Y, Gholdengo, and Volcarona. Flame Body helps Moltres punish contact moves from Melmetal, Mega Lopunny, and Kingambit with a potential burn. Heavy-Duty Boots is mandatory thanks to Moltres's extreme weakness to Stealth Rock, which severely impacts its ability to function as a pivot.

Moltres fits well on bulky offense and balance teams thanks to its solid defensive profile and ability to retain momentum with U-turn. A Knock Off absorber is an important teammate, as Moltres loses a significant amount of its efficacy without Heavy-Duty Boots. Teammates such as Gliscor, Mega Scizor, and Great Tusk are good choices as a result. Moltres also pairs well with Dragon-types such as Dragonite, Mega Latios, and Kommo-o, which can shore up Moltres's weakness to common Water-types such as Ogerpon-W, Urshifu-R, and Mega Swampert, as well as helping it check Mega Charizard Y, while they appreciate Moltres checking Fairy-types like Iron Valiant. In a similar vein, Moltres benefits from Ground-types such as Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu, as they can check Rock- and Electric-types such as Mega Tyranitar and Raging Bolt, while Moltres can check Grass-types such as Rillaboom, Serperior, and Kartana in return. Moltres is a good pivot thanks to its ability to take a hit from and force out common Pokemon like Landorus-T, Mega Charizard Y, and Great Tusk, so frail wallbreakers, such as Mega Medicham, Weavile, and Ogerpon-W, that appreciate getting free switch-in opportunities are good teammates.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

(Flying)

Roar is an alternative option to force out setup sweepers that Moltres has a tough time dealing with, such as Dragon Dance Dragapult and Volcarona.

Physically Defensive (Flying).description:
Thanks to its ability and bulk, Moltres finds itself on Flying-type teams as a deterrent to threatening physical attackers such as Dragonite, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, and Sneasler. Flamethrower is a reliable STAB move that does solid damage to Pokemon such as Archaludon and Klefki. Will-O-Wisp is used to guarantee a burn on prominent attackers such as Azumarill and Iron Hands while negating Leftovers and Black Sludge recovery from passive Pokemon such as Ting-Lu and Toxapex without having to rely on Pressure. U-turn allows Moltres to pivot out of unfavorable situations and keep itself safe from harm, such as in front of Araquanid and Blissey. Alternatively, Scorching Sands can be used in order to hit unsuspecting Heatran that would hope to switch in on Fire-type attacks to protect its teammates. The given Speed EVs allow Moltres to outspeed Jolly Azumarill to neutralize its setup with Will-O-Wisp.

Corviknight forms a great defensive core with Moltres, as they both cover each other's threats well. Corviknight is able to switch into threats such as Choice Band Excadrill and Glimmora for Moltres, while Moltres is able to cover Corviknight by switching into Ogerpon-H and Ninetales. Mandibuzz also makes for another great defensive addition for a defensive trio, as it shields Moltres from incoming Ghost-, Psychic-, and Dark-type attacks from Dragapult, Hoopa-U, and Hydreigon while also threatening various physical attackers with Foul Play. Once Gliscor's Toxic Orb has activated, it acts as a fantastic Knock Off absorber, ensuring Moltres doesn't lose its extremely important Heavy-Duty Boots. Additionally, Moltres can support Gliscor by burning foes, allowing Swords Dance variants of Gliscor to have an easier time setting up in front of some physical threats. Assault Vest Tornadus-T is a great teammate for Moltres, as it can switch in on Special threats that force Moltres out, such as Iron Valiant and Keldeo. Tornadus-T can use Knock Off to remove recovery items from defensive staples such as Toxapex, Galarian Weezing, and Clodsire, causing them to be chipped down more quickly when coupled with burn, as well as being able to outspeed and OHKO Punching Glove Urshifu-R, which is unaffected by Flame Body. Landorus-T is able to handle Fire-type Pokemon that wall and take advantage of Moltres, such as Heatran and Ceruledge, while being a deterrent to Electric-types such as Raging Bolt and Sandy Shocks. Additionally, Landorus-T and the aforementioned defensive trio all have access to U-turn, allowing Flying-type teams and Moltres in particular to retain momentum throughout a battle. In return, Moltres is able to soak up Ice-type attacks from Mamowsine and Great Tusk. Choice Scarf Enamorus is also able to help Moltres deal with Heatran while also sweeping Dragon-, Steel-, and Fire-type teams with the appropriate coverage, and it provides Healing Wish support for Moltres should it need the immediate recovery. In return, Moltres can cover incoming Ice-type attacks from the aforementioned Mamoswine and Great Tusk, as well as Steel-type attacks from Choice Scarf Roaring Moon and Scizor, both of which can threaten to cut Enamorus's sweep short. Dragonite is a great potential wincon with access to Dragon Dance and a colorful movepool, and it greatly appreciates Moltres wearing down troublesome physical walls such as Toxapex, Galarian Weezing, and Quagsire with Will-O-Wisp.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Scorching Sands is an alternative to Solar Beam or Will-O-Wisp that threatens Iron Moth, Iron Treads, and Well-Baked Body Gholdengo. Magic Guard + Life Orb with Brave Bird and Flare Blitz takes advantage of Moltres's offensive capabilities, and Magic Guard complements Moltres fantasically due to its granting immunity to Stealth Rock. However, this set lacks viability due to Moltres's suboptimal Attack and Speed stats.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Special attackers like Gholdengo and Latios threaten to 2HKO Moltres.

Physical Attackers: Physical attackers like Zamazenta, Roaring Moon, and Chien-Pao all can OHKO or 2HKO Moltres.

Knock Off Users: Knock Off users like Roaring Moon, Manaphy, and Swampert threaten to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from Moltres, which is very important to keep it immune to Stealth Rock.

Electric-types: Electric-types like Zapdos and Sandy Shocks are able to OHKO Moltres.

Desolate Land.description:
Thanks to its solid stats, decent typing, and great utility moves, Moltres can wall the tier's many Water- and Fire-types. Desolate Land lets Moltres wall Ogerpon-W, Primarina, and Swampert lacking Stone Edge, with the latter two being unable to pivot with Flip Turn. Solar Beam threatens Water-types like Manaphy, Swampert, and Primarina, whereas Will-O-Wisp punishes physical attackers like Roaring Moon, Zamazenta, and Iron Hands. U-turn helps generate momentum for Moltres and its allies. Roost gives Moltres longevity against dangerous wallbreakers like Cinderace, Ogerpon-H, and Iron Moth.

Moltres works best on bulky offense and balance teams due to its valuable utility and defensive capabilities. Teammates like Great Tusk and Swampert benefit from Moltres being able to check threats like Primarina, Ogerpon-W, and Iron Moth with Solar Beam. Moltres is heavily reliant on its Heavy-Duty Boots due to its massive Stealth Rock weakness, so Knock Off users like Roaring Moon, Swampert, and Great Tusk are very threatening; therefore, it appreciates Knock Off absorbers like Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Skarmory. Special attackers like Gholdengo, Zapdos, and Latios threaten Moltres, so specially defensive partners like Swampert, Manaphy, and Iron Treads are quite helpful. Moltres is also vulnerable to physical attackers like Roaring Moon, Zamazenta, and Chien-Pao; thus, physically defensive allies like the aforementioned Great Tusk and Corviknight work well with it. They also help Moltres by removing Stealth Rock, which is very threatening to it if its Heavy-Duty Boots have been removed.

Specially Defensive.description:
Thanks to its solid defensive stats, great typing, and high Special Attack, Moltres functions as a specially defensive check to many of the tier's strong special attackers such as Iron Moth and Heatran while being able to threaten good damage with the boost from Desolate Land. Desolate Land prevents Swampert and Primarina from switching out with Flip Turn and lets Moltres check Water-type attackers like Ogerpon-W and Primarina. Weather Ball is the generally preferred Fire-type move due to its higher strength and ability to hit Primordial Sea Zapdos, but Flamethrower hits Bulletproof Iron Treads. Scorching Sands hits Iron Moth, Well-Baked Body Gholdengo, and Bulletproof Iron Treads when using Weather Ball while annoying most switch-ins with a potential burn, whereas Solar Beam nails Water-types like Manaphy, Swampert, and Primarina. U-turn hits Roaring Moon and provides valuable access to pivoting, while Roost grants Moltres longevity against strong special attackers like Scream Tail, Iron Moth, and Choice Specs Primarina.

Moltres is best suited for offense and balance teams due to its defensive prowess. Bulletproof Iron Treads checks special attackers like Zapdos, Gholdengo, and Latios for Moltres; in return, it deals with Iron Moth and Primarina. Physical attackers such as Zamazenta, Roaring Moon, and Kingambit are quite threatening to Moltres, so checks to them like Pecharunt, Corviknight, and Great Tusk are much appreciated. The last two are also Knock Off absorbers and entry hazard removers, which Moltres requires, as it is heavily reliant on its Heavy-Duty Boots and it needs hazard removal in the scenario it loses its item. Hazard setters such as Great Tusk, Garchomp, and Ting-Lu benefit Moltres greatly, as they allow Moltres to have an easier time chipping down foes.

Nasty Plot.description:
With Nasty Plot, Galarian Moltres is a solid late-game setup sweeper and wallbreaker. With an Agility boost, Galarian Moltres matches up better against offensive teams, as it can outspeed threats like Iron Valiant, Dragapult, and Choice Scarf Enamorus, only remaining threatened by Raging Bolt's Thunderclap and other priority moves. Taunt can instead potentially turn Galarian Moltres into a stallbreaker as it blocks status moves like Whirlwind from Ting-Lu, Toxic from Gliscor and Clodsire, and Calm Mind and Soft-Boiled from Blissey, giving it more opportunities to set up and sweep against bulkier teams. Sitrus Berry is a must-have, allowing Galarian Moltres to potentially secure an extra boost from Berserk and its setup moves. Tera Ghost gives Galarian Moltres an immunity to Dragonite's Extreme Speed, Zamazenta's Body Press, and Blissey's Seismic Toss, as well as allowing it to double as a Rapid Spin blocker. Meanwhile, Tera Fairy is a solid typing that allows it to keep the resistance to Kingambit's Sucker Punch while making it immune to Dragpult's powerful Draco Meteor and Dragon Darts. Galarian Moltres typically runs maximum Special Attack and Speed to increase its sweeping potential. Alternatively, it can run a bulkier spread to give itself more chances to set up; this specific EV spread allows Galarian Moltres to outspeed uninvested Gliscor while surviving two Ivy Cudgels from Ogerpon-W after Sitrus Berry and two Ice Beams from Darkrai. This set can more safely run Taunt, whereas the more offensive set is better suited to running Agility for setting up.

Galarian Moltres fits best on hyper offensive teams. It pairs best with other offensive sweepers and wallbreakers similar to itself, such as Iron Valiant, Iron Moth, and Gholdengo, that can keep up pressure throughout a battle. Iron Valiant takes on foes like Darkrai and Raging Bolt, while Galarian Moltres handles Gholdengo and Pecharunt, forming a dangerous offensive core. Gholdengo can block any attempts to wear down Galarian Moltres with status and force damage on Ting-Lu and break through Fairy-types that Galarian Moltres struggles with. Iron Moth can help wallbreak and allow Galarian Moltres to sweep late in the game. Galarian Moltres can also fit well into Dark-type spam archetypes alongside teammates like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott, breaking through bulkier foes like Kingambit and Tinkaton. Galarian Moltres, in return, can pressure Dark-resistant Pokemon like Zamazenta and Great Tusk. Galarian Moltres is particularly helped by entry hazards, the damage from which can chip down enemies that Galarian Moltres can then break through. Great Tusk and Iron Treads can set Stealth Rock to assist in this, use Rapid Spin to protect Galarian Moltres from entry hazard damage and let it setup on spinblockers, and check some of Galarian Moltres's tougher matchups like Raging Bolt and Iron Moth. Deoxys-S can also provide excellent support with entry hazards, while Hatterene can prevent opponents from setting their own hazards and can act as an additional setup sweeper for the team with Calm Mind. Sticky Web is also particularly helpful for Galarian Moltres. It allows it to sweep more of the tier by letting it outspeeding faster threats like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant without needing an additional boost from Agility, so Galarian Moltres can safely run Taunt instead; Araquanid and Ribombee are great teammates for this reason. Alolan Ninetales can facilitate another type of hyper offensive team; its Aurora Veil turns allow Galarian Moltres additional setup opportunities, especially when attempting to get a boost from both Nasty Plot and Agility back-to-back. Galarian Moltres is particularly susceptible to fast, powerful sweepers that can take it out before it has the chance to set up, including Iron Valiant and Zamazenta, and priority users like Raging Bolt and Dragonite that ignore its Agility boost. Pecharunt is an excellent teammate to take these hits and threaten back with Nasty Plot-boosted Malignant Chains; this can help overwhelm foes like Ting-Lu with poison, as well as Fairy-types that threaten Galarian Moltres like Iron Valiant and Clefable. Bulkier Pokemon that can spread Toxic like Gliscor and Clodsire can cut off Galarian Moltres's sweeping potential should it opt to forego Taunt; Kyurem is a strong teammate that can break through these checks. Other offensive teammates that form solid pairings with Galarian Moltres are Dragonite, which Galarian Moltres can help sweep by taking out Gholdengo, Zamazenta to deal with Kingambit while Galarian Moltres deals with Ghost-types in return, and Ogerpon-W, which can break through bulkier teams if Galarian Moltres is running Agility.

Weakness Policy.description:
• Fiery Wrath lets Galarian Moltres easily clean up Ghost- and Psychic-type foes such as Spectrier, Cresselia, and Iron Crown.
  • Hurricane enables Galarian Moltres to handle Fighting- and Grass-type Pokemon like Great Tusk, Ogerpon-W, and Iron Valiant.
  • Nasty Plot allows Galarian Moltres to boost its Special Attack in order to compete with threats such as Take Heart Manaphy and specially defensive, Weakness Policy Iron Crown; it also lets it remove foes that are not OHKOed such as Pecharunt.
  • Air Slash gives Galarian Moltres a second STAB option for the Encore + Disable Iron Valiant matchup while also providing a more reliable way to hit foes. Alternatively, Taunt can be used to disrupt foes such as Ogerpon-W, Weakness Policy Iron Crown, and Serperior.
  • The EV spread allows Galarian Moltres to survive Spirit Break from Jolly Choice Band Iron Valiant and Moonblast from Timid Choice Specs Iron Valiant.
  • Pair Galarian Moltres with Ground-types like Great Tusk, which covers its Electric weakness, protecting it from threats like Raging Bolt while also checking foes such as Choice Band Ursaluna and Tyranitar. In return, it checks Great Tusk answers like Ogerpon-W and Serperior. Steel-types like Iron Crown and Metagross are also good partners for Galarian Moltres, backing its Fairy weakness and checking foes such as Sylveon and Alolan Ninetales. In exchange, Galarian Moltres checks threats to these Steel-types such as Spectrier and Volcarona.

Assault Vest.description:
• Assault Vest allows Galarian Moltres to win matchups against strong special attackers, like Volcanion and Iron Crown.
  • Hurricane is Galarian Moltres's main Flying-type STAB move, hitting Grass-types like Ogergon-W and Fighting-types like both Urshifu formes.
  • Fiery Wrath enables Galarian Moltres to beat Pokemon such as Iron Crown, Pecharunt, and Cresselia.
  • Air Slash allows Galarian Moltres to beat Encore + Disable Iron Valiant, and is more accurate, letting it break Sneasler's and Volcarona's Substitute more reliably.
  • Sucker Punch allows it to win against Custap Berry users like Urshifu-S and Skeledirge, as well as Liechi Berry Sneasler.
  • The EV spread lets Galarian Moltres survive Modest Choice Specs Porygon-Z Hyper Beam as well as Choice Band Haxorus Outrage.
  • Galarian Moltres struggles to beat bulky Fairy- and Steel-types like Sylveon, Primarina, Corviknight, and Registeel as well as Electric-types like Iron Hands. Thus, Steel-types like Iron Crown and Metagross, Ground-types like Ursaluna and Landorus-T, and Fire-types like Volcanion and Volcarona are good partners for it.

Nasty Plot (Flying).description:
Galarian Moltres is a powerful special attacker on Flying teams that keeps Ghost- and Psychic-type threats in check thanks to its access to Nasty Plot. Fiery Wrath serves as a way for it to deal damage and take down Ghost-types such as Dragapult and Gholdengo. Hurricane provides Galarian Moltres with a way to deal significant damage to foes like Zamazenta, Volcarona, and the Ogerpon formes, except Ogerpon-C. However, due to Hurricane's low accuracy, Substitute can be be used in place of it to protect Galarian Moltres from status conditions, such as Toxic from Toxapex and Clodsire. Agility lets Galarian Moltres outspeed threats like Latios and Gholdengo. Alternatively, Pain Split lets it recover and allows it to activate its Berserk ability to get multiple Special Attack boosts.

Skarmory is a great partner for Galarian Moltres, as it is a physical wall that can switch into Rock- and Ice-type moves from foes such as Iron Boulder, Kleavor, and Weavile. Corviknight removes entry hazards using Defog in case Galarian Moltres's Heavy-Duty Boots get removed; specially defensive Corviknight provides Galarian Moltres a safe switch-in to Ice-types moves such as Ice Beam and Freeze-Dry from foes like Kyurem, Greninja, and Alolan Ninetales. Gliscor pairs well with Galarian Moltres, as it is immune to Electric-type moves, and it can switch into Knock Off to hinder any attempt to remove Galarian Moltres's Heavy-Duty Boots, provided that it's already poisoned. Additionally, Gliscor can switch into Rock-type attacks from foes like Iron Boulder and Hisuian Arcanine and hit them back with Earthquake. The Landorus formes form an offensive core with Galarian Moltres by removing threats like Empoleon and Gouging Fire. Enamorus revenge kills Rock-types that beat Galarian Moltres such as Tyranitar, Kleavor, and Hisuian Arcanine with Superpower and Earth Power, along with providing Healing Wish support. Articuno synergizes well with Galarian Moltres, as Articuno serves as a special wall and Galarian Moltres serves as a special attacker, forming a special core that exterminates foes like Greninja, Landorus, Clodsire, and Spectrier. Zapdos provides Galarian Moltres a safe switch-in to Electric-type attacks and can paralyze Pokemon that make contact with it due to Static. It also acts as a pivot thanks to Volt Switch, allowing Galarian Moltres to come in safely. Galarian Moltres is greatly assisted by Nasty Plot Tornadus-T due to its ability to remove Steel-type threats like Hisuian Goodra, Heatran, and Archaludon with Focus Blast. Assault Vest Tornadus-T can switch into attacks like Thunderbolt and Power Gem from foes like Iron Valiant, Flutter Mane, and Heatran and subsequently use U-turn to bring Galarian Moltres in safely. Dragonite forms an offensive core with Galarian Moltres, as Dragonite acts as a physical setup sweeper taking out foes like Alolan Muk, Corviknight, Clodsire, and Toxapex, while Galarian Moltres acts as a special setup sweeper taking out foes such as Dragapult and Latios. Dragonite finishes off enemies weakened by Galarian Moltres with Extreme Speed.

Nasty Plot (Dark).description:
With its respectable bulk, access to Nasty Plot and Agility, and a great ability in Berserk to further bolster its offensive prowess, Galarian Moltres makes for an incredible wallbreaker and setup sweeper for Dark teams, threatening Fighting- and Bug-types like Scrafty and Volcarona. Hurricane OHKOes Fighting-types like Iron Valiant, Urshifu-R, and, when at +2, Assault Vest Gallade. It is also Galarian Moltres's strongest option for hitting Fairy-types, outright OHKOing Flutter Mane and Hatterene at +2 and OHKOing non-Assault Vest Primarina at +2 after minimal chip damage. Fiery Wrath is a more reliable STAB option, hitting Flying-resistant Pokemon like Heatran, Corviknight, and Zapdos. Agility allows Galarian Moltres to mitigate its low Speed, allowing it to outspeed would-be faster foes like Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf users like Iron Valiant.

Ting-Lu provides entry hazard support and leverages its Electric immunity and Rock resistance to handle foes like Raging Bolt and Tyranitar. It can also break through special walls like Clodsire, Hisuian Goodra, and Alolan Muk. Grimmsnarl provides dual screens support for easier setup, potentially letting Galarian Moltres survive super effective moves like Iron Valiant's Moonblast and Iron Hands's Thunder Punch to activate both Berserk and its Weakness Policy. Grimmsnarl can also use Taunt to deny hazards from being set up and provide safe a switch in to Galarian Moltres using Parting Shot. Alolan Muk, with its Poison typing and excellent special bulk, can stave off Fairy-type attacks from foes like Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Enamorus, threatening them back with Poison Jab. Bisharp serves an offensive answer to Fairy-, Ice-, and Rock-types, utilizing Sucker Punch to pick off Flutter Mane and Iron Boulder. Choice Band Meowscarada, Choice Specs Greninja, and Swords Dance Weavile can eliminate bulky Ground-types like Clodsire and Ting-Lu. Meowscarada and Greninja can help alleviate the Rock matchup for Galarian Moltres, with Meowscarada also threatening Water-types like Primarina and Dondozo. Meowscarada, Hoopa-U, and Weavile eliminate special walls like Blissey and Hisuian Goodra; Hoopa-U and Greninja also assist in Fighting and Fairy matchups. Sableye, with the combination of Will-O-Wisp and Knock Off, can wither down foes like Iron Hands and Dragonite, making it easier for Galarian Moltres to set up and eliminate them. Mandibuzz serves as a Defogger and can provide safe entry to Galarian Moltres using U-turn. Choice Scarf Darkrai can use its superb Speed tier and coverage options to revenge kill opposing Choice Scarf users like Iron Boulder, Meowscarada, and Greninja.

Black Glasses.description:
Galarian Moltres utilizes its great bulk, typing, and movepool to become a great offensive support Pokemon that can also beat the powerful Calyrex formes. Fiery Wrath provides a consistent spread STAB option paired with its chance to flinch, complimenting Galarian Moltres's bulk as a great tool to rack up damage. Foul Play on the other hand is a great anti-physical attacker tool, giving Galarian Moltres a fairly good matchup into Calyrex-I. Tailwind gives Galarian Moltres a supportive role in providing speed control for its team, allowing it to outspeed and fire off Fiery Wraths and Foul Plays. Black Glasses helps boost Galarian Moltres's damage output even more, allowing it to OHKO Calyrex-S and pairing well with potential Berserk boosts. The Speed investment allows Galarian Moltres to outspeed Choice Scarf Urshifu-R with Tailwind active, as well as naturally outspeeding most Gholdengo. The defensive investment allows Galarian Moltres to have a good chance of surviving a +2 Tera Fairy-boosted Draining Kiss from Calyrex-S or a Flare Blitz from non-Tera Fire Koraidon. Tera Dark sheds Galarian Moltres's Ice and Electric weaknesses, and the increased damage to its Dark-type STAB moves allow it to threaten an OHKO on Calyrex-I.

Galarian Moltres typically struggles against Pokemon that can reliably win the damage trade versus it like Raging Bolt and Zamazenta-C. Amoonguss is able to comfortably tank Galarian Moltres's attacks and retaliate with Spore. Miraidon and Urshifu-R are also problematic matchups for Galarian Moltres, as Miraidon is able to outspeed and OHKO it, while Urshifu-R takes minimal damage from Galarian Moltres and can hit it in return with a Surging Strikes. While Zamazenta-C is is a great check against Galarian Moltres, it is also an amazing partner. Galarian Moltres gives it speed control and strong super effective damage against the Ghost-types Zamazenta-C would typically struggle against while Zamazenta-C grants Wide Guard support for Galarian Moltres, allowing it to effectively counter Calyrex-I. Fairy-types that would try to counter Galarian Moltres like Flutter Mane and Tera Fairy Calyrex-S are also covered by Zamazenta-C's Heavy Slam. Rillaboom is able to deal with opposing Urshifu-R trying to take advantage of their Dark resistance, as well as overriding Electric Terrain from Miraidon and threatening an OHKO with Choice Band-boosted High Horsepower.

Bulky Spread Attacker.description:
• Choice Specs Galarian Moltres is amazing at spreading damage across the opposing team, being able to heavily damage most Pokemon in the format.

  • With Tera Dark's boost, Dark Pulse is a strong option against rain-centered teams, as it can bypass Pelipper's Wide Guard and 2HKO Archaludon. It is also strong and the most damaging option against Dondozo after Commander has been activated. Tera Blast Steel allows Galarian Moltres to threaten Fairy- and Ice-types such as Flutter Mane, Chien-Pao, and Articuno. Air Slash allows it to pick up OHKOs against common threats such as the Urshifu and Ogerpon formes. Snarl allows it to control damage when facing two opposing special attackers.

  • Because of its ability Berserk, Galarian Moltres gets the most value out when its below half HP, so a bulky EV spread fits it very well. The given spread allows it to survive attacks such as Tera Stellar Sacred Sword from Chien-Pao when Galarian Moltres is Terastallized, Choice Band Close Combat from both Urshifu formes, and Sword of Ruin-boosted Mystic Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R.

  • Tera Dark allows Fiery Wrath to 2HKO most Pokemon in the format, such as the Ogerpon and Ursaluna formes, while Tera Steel helps with Flutter Mane, Articuno, Ogerpon-C, and Chien-Pao by turning Galarian Moltres's weaknesses into resistances and allowing it to hit them super effectively with Tera Blast.

Nasty Plot.description: Leveraging its excellent defensive profile and bulk, on top of its access to a multitude of boosting moves, Galarian Moltres makes for an excellent mid-to late-game cleaner on more offensive teams. It provides an important buffer against offensive threats such as Aegislash and Alakazam while also finding setup opportunities against a large portion of defensive staples, such as Slowbro and Mega Venusaur. Nasty Plot boosts Galarian Moltres's Special Attack to absurd levels, allowing it to reliably pressure specially defensive tanks such Hippowdon and Clefable. Agility allows Galarian Moltres to outspeed common revenge killers such as Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Scarf Enamorus after one round of setup while giving it the opportunity to clean up opposing teams late-game when its wallbreaking prowess with Nasty Plot isn't as necessary. Taunt, on the other hand, can be used to prevent status and healing from Pokemon such as Blissey and specially defensive Hippowdon, allowing Galarian Moltres to wear them down or use them as setup fodder. Hurricane, in conjunction with Flyinium Z, gives Galarian Moltres a powerful one-time nuke in Supersonic Skystrike that can break through neutral targets such as Blissey and Gastrodon, threatening to outright OHKO the latter at +2 while also offsetting Hurricane’s middling accuracy in the process. As Galarian Moltres can struggle to safely find setup opportunities against faster threats such as Mega Aerodactyl and Enamorus, it pairs best with offensive teammates that can also complement its wallbreaking prowess; late-game cleaners such as Swords Dance Aegislash and Booster Energy Iron Moth capitalize on Galarian Moltres's ability to weaken specific answers, such as Unaware Clefable and Skeledirge, respectively, allowing them to sweep opposing teams with greater ease late-game. The latter can also invite in and weaken Rock-types such as Tyranitar, which Galarian Moltres can struggle to break through otherwise. Galarian Moltres's Stealth Rock weakness and inability to run Heavy-Duty Boots necessitates strong anti-hazard options, leads such as Excadrill and Mew can all shut down common entry hazard setters, the former via Rapid Spin and the latter via Taunt.

Double Dance.description:
Galarian Moltres leverages Nasty Plot and Agility alongside a good STAB combination to become a fearsome setup sweeper that can break through special walls. Agility allows Galarian Moltres to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame, and 208 Speed EVs let it outspeed Pokemon with base Speed of 110 such as Ogerpon-W and Iron Moth at +1. Sitrus Berry synergizes extremely well with Berserk, providing recovery in the middle of a sweep and potentially allowing Berserk to activate twice. Meanwhile, Tera Steel greatly improves Galarian Moltres's defensive profile by turning its Fairy-, Ice-, and Rock-type weaknesses, such as attacks from Zacian-C and Kyurem-White, into resistances while also helping it withstand priority moves like Extreme Speed from Arceus.

Galarian Moltres is essentially exclusive to hyper offense, fitting best on Aurora Veil and dual screens teams, where it can find more opportunities to set up safely. It relies on Gods that donate high Special Attack, such as Kyurem-White or Mewtwo, to enable it to sweep effectively. However, it can still struggle against the likes of Ho-Oh and Unaware Dondozo, so it can be used either as a late-game sweeper after these checks have been chipped or as a way to soften them for teammates such as Polteageist and Mewtwo. Additionally, as Galarian Moltres is vulnerable to Stealth Rock, it appreciates teammates that provide entry hazard control, such as Magic Bounce Hatterene, Rapid Spin Great Tusk, and Mortal Spin Glimmora.

Nasty Plot.description: The speed investment allows Moltres-G to outspeed Max Speed Booster Energy Gouging Fire and Choice Scarf Landorus-T in Tailwind.

Double Dance (Dark).description: With access to both Nasty Plot and Agility as well as a Special Attack-boosting ability in Berserk, Galarian Moltres is a great late-game sweeper for Dark teams. In addition, its part-Flying typing provides Dark teams with a great offensive option against Fighting and Bug teams, as well as a greatly appreciated neutrality to the aforementioned types. After one Nasty Plot boost, Galarian Moltres 2HKOes physically defensive Toxapex, physically defensive Ting-Lu, and Celesteela. After one Agility boost, it is able to outspeed would-be faster Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, Regieleki, and +1 Volcarona, as well as Mega Swampert in rain. With Flyinium Z , a Nasty Plot-boosted Supersonic Skystrike OHKOes Mega Diancie, Tapu Koko, and specially defensive Toxapex. An unboosted Supersonic Skystrike is still able to OHKO Terrakion after Stealth Rock damage. Hisuian Samurott provides entry hazard support in order to wear down incoming foes into OHKO range for Galarian Moltres, and in return, Galarian Moltres can threaten the Grass- and Fighting-types the two of them struggle with such as Mega Venusaur and Urshifu-R. Grimmsnarl is another great teammate, as it is able to set up dual screens to further make Galarian Moltres difficult to KO, and it can also run Taunt to prevent Stealth Rock from being set. Because of Galarian Moltres's part-Flying-typing, it is vulnerable to Stealth Rock. Because of this vulnerability, it appreciates hazard control from Mega Sableye's Magic Bounce, and Mega Sableye is also able to cripple opposing foes with Will-O-Wisp and Knock Off. Choice Band users such as Weavile, Roaring Moon, and Meowscarada can check walls Galarian Moltres struggles with like Dondozo and Clodsire. In return, Meowscarada and Weavile appreciate Galarian Moltres matching up well against Volcarona and Roaring Moon appreciates Galarian Moltres matching up well against Great Tusk. Lastly, Galarian Moltres can be paired with other sweepers such as Swords Dance Weavile and Dragon Dance Roaring Moon to soften each other's checks to enable each other to sweep. For example, Weavile is able to threaten Ting-Lu and Clodsire, while Galarian Moltres is able to handle Choice Scarf Gholdengo in return. When Galarian Moltres is not able to complete an outright sweep, it can set up for Choice Scarf users such as Meowscarada and Greninja to clean up.

Nasty Plot (Flying).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

ou.overview: Dragonite stands out as one of the most dominant Pokemon in SV OU, able to wield a myriad of coverage moves, Tera type options, and items to threaten most teams with the right set while also possessing a remarkable defensive profile, essentially letting it fit onto an incredibly wide array of team archetypes. It is one of the tier's most potent setup sweepers, as Dragon Dance enables a variety of sweeping methods and couples with any mix of strong physical attacks and crafty utility moves that Dragonite pleases. Dragonite can also wallbreak and revenge kill foes more reliably with its Choice Band set. Furthermore, all of this is enabled by its natural bulk, typing, and potentially Roost, as not only do these give Dragonite easy setup opportunities, but they also allow it to check common threats like Ogerpon-W, Iron Moth, and Rillaboom; furthermore, with Multiscale intact, it can also emergency check even threatening foes like Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Raging Bolt, making it a menace against offensive teams. This also allows Dragonite to employ a utility-focused bulky attacking set that lets it act as a catch-all answer to most offensive threats of the tier while not being entirely passive like most walls. With all this variability, checking Dragonite can be a headache, but physically bulky Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Corviknight can often break its Multiscale and force it to reveal its set, if not beat it in a one-on-one outright. Dondozo also stands out as a particularly good answer, ignoring any boosts from Dragon Dance that Dragonite may have accrued while having the bulk to take it on. Even after a Dragon Dance, Dragonite is still outsped by threats such as Deoxys-S, Iron Valiant, Choice Scarf Enamorus, and Speed Booster Energy Great Tusk, particularly if it's not running Extreme Speed, with Zamazenta and Dragapult being added to the list if Dragonite is not running a Speed-boosting nature. While Dragonite's typing is incredible in most situations, it also presents a serious 4x weakness to Ice-type moves such as Darkrai's Ice Beam, Kyurem's Freeze-Dry, and Great Tusk's Ice Spinner, meaning that Dragonite often will need to Terastallize to avoid being revenge killed and continue its sweep. Its Stealth Rock weakness also warrants strong hazard control from its teammates or the use of Heavy-Duty Boots, which presents another issue where foes like Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W that it wants to check often carry Knock Off as well.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Hurricane alongside a Naughty or Naive nature can be used as a flex option on its Dragon Dance set to surprise Zamazenta and Great Tusk while also potentially 3HKOing Dondozo, even preventing them from matching Dragonite with their own boosts. Dragon Dance sets can run Dragon Tail to prevent IronPress users like non-Roar Zamazenta, Corviknight, and Skarmory from beating it one-on-one; stop opposing phazers like Ting-Lu and Zamazenta if it's running a Jolly nature from forcing it out first; and let it act as a sturdier emergency check against opposing setup sweepers that it can't immediately KO. Iron Head can be used in conjunction with Tera Steel to gain resistances to incoming Ice-, Dragon-, and Fairy-type attacks while OHKOing Hatterene, Iron Valiant, and Clefable, as well as potentially flinching its way out of otherwise impossible situations. Many teams try to limit Dragonite via Will-O-Wisp or Flame Body, so Facade can be used on Tera Normal + Extreme Speed sets to surprise these teams thinking they're safe once Dragonite is burned. Defensive sets can be used alongside moves like Thunder Wave to long-term cripple dangerous threats and Ice Beam to hit Gliscor, Landorus-T, and opposing Dragonite hard. If the team has enough hazard control, this set can even employ Rocky Helmet to punish foes that rely on making contact to deal damage, like Rillaboom and Zamazenta, or Red Card to further make use of its hit-taking ability to act as an emergency check to boosted foes.

Dragon Dance.description:
Dragon Dance Dragonite is one of the tier's most formidable setup sweepers due to its plethora of coverage variations and defensive profile. Extreme Speed maximizes its matchup against offensive teams, compensating for Dragonite's subpar Speed tier by taking care of the archetype's frail or boosted foes like Darkrai, Iron Valiant, and Kyurem while also outprioritzing revenge killers like Weavile and Raging Bolt. Earthquake covers Pokemon like Garganacl, Pecharunt, Galarian Weezing, and Steel-types like Kingambit and Gholdengo. Ice Spinner dents foes like Gliscor, Landorus-T, Zapdos, Sinistcha, and opposing Dragonite while popping Air Balloon from Gholdengo, Pecharunt, and Tera Ghost Kingambit. Dragonite can forgo Extreme Speed, as Ice Spinner + Earthquake grants it with sufficient coverage to hit most of the metagame for at least neutral effectiveness. Either Roost or Encore gives it more setup opportunities; Roost lets it activate Multiscale repeatedly and is the preferred move on bulkier playstyles to emphasize its defensive utility further, while Encore punishes opposing setup and passive plays from threats and walls like Zamazenta, Raging Bolt, Landorus-T, and Corviknight. A coverage move can be used instead; Rock Slide obliterates a would-be check in Moltres, OHKOing it at +1, and hits Zapdos without triggering Static, with the riskier but stronger Stone Edge being an alternative that has good chances to straight up OHKO the former and 2HKO the latter unboosted. Similar to Ice Spinner + Earthquake, either of the Rock-type moves + Earthquake can be used as the sole attacking moves so it can run Encore or Roost in its last moveslot. Fire Punch super effectively hits Corviknight, Skarmory, and Air Balloon Steel-types like Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Tinkaton. On hyper offense teams, Outrage alongside Life Orb is an option to exacerbate its wallbreaking power, letting it nuke neutral walls like Alomomola, Moltres, and Zapdos much more easily. While Heavy-Duty Boots is preferred to reliably keep its Multiscale intact even in the face of Stealth Rock, teams that commit to strong entry hazard removal can run other items; Leftovers improves its general longevity, while Lum Berry ignores crippling status from foes like Dragapult, Moltres, Pecharunt, and Gholdengo. More offensive choices like Silk Scarf and Soft Sand can be used with their appropriate Tera types. Tera Normal is only used on sets running Extreme Speed, as it importantly boosts the move while giving Dragonite a neutral typing against all of its weaknesses, such as against Enamorus, Kyurem, Ice Spinner Great Tusk, and Ice Beam Darkrai. Non-Extreme Speed sets can go for Tera Ground to boost its Earthquake, such as letting it 2HKO Pecharunt and OHKO Garganacl at +1, and defensively grants Dragonite an immunity to Gholdengo's Thunder Wave and Raging Bolt's Thunderclap. An Adamant nature is preferred, but Jolly can be used to outspeed Dragapult and Zamazenta at +1 and, at worst, Speed tie opposing Dragonite. Particularly for Tera Normal + Extreme Speed variants, Dragonite can invest its Speed EVs into bulk instead to make setup much easier, such as an EV spread of 164 HP / 252 Atk / 92 Spe, running enough Speed to outrun Jolly Kingambit; Roost is preferred as the last move to accentuate the extra bulk.

Dragonite's sweeping potential and defensive utility make it an exceptional pick for most playstyles, anything that ranges from hyper offense to balance. Physically offensive teammates like Ogerpon-W, Zamazenta, and Kingambit can either overwhelm, surprise, or pressure a majority of its checks, which include the likes of Pecharunt, Alomomola, Zapdos, and Clefable. Special attackers like Darkrai, Iron Moth, Raging Bolt, Gholdengo, and Iron Valiant are similarly great to immediately threaten Dragonite's checks, especially Defense-boosting users like Zamazenta, Corviknight, Dondozo, and Great Tusk looking to go one-on-one against Dragonite. Moreover, they're particularly capable of forcing damage onto Air Balloon users like Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Tinkaton, giving Dragonite an easier time against them later on. Leads like Deoxys-S, Hisuian Samurott, and Landorus-T can also soften the opposition with their entry hazards so Dragonite can sweep more easily. The aforementioned Great Tusk and other hazard control options like Cinderace, Iron Treads, Glimmora, and Hatterene—even running a combination of them simultaneously—on offensive teams give Dragonite more freedom to forgo Heavy-Duty Boots. On bulkier teams, Dragonite immensely loves teammates like Galarian Weezing, Corviknight, Pecharunt, Sinistcha, and Alomomola that can switch into and check foes such as Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, and Weavile that force it out. Other walls like Ting-Lu, Gliscor, and Clefable are also great hazard setters for Dragonite's sweeping mission. The aforementioned Corviknight also provides Defog as extra insurance in case Dragonite's Heavy-Duty Boots is removed by Ogerpon-W, Great Tusk, and Hisuian Samurott, but Corviknight itself alongside Gliscor and Clefable are great Knock Off absorbers in the first place. In return, all of them appreciate Dragonite's defensive utility, such as checking Iron Moth for Corviknight, Tinkaton, and Galarian Weezing; Ogerpon and Rillaboom for Alomomola, Ting-Lu, and Garganacl; and Ogerpon-W for all of them. On top of providing these teams with a setup sweeper that they might lack, Dragonite's ability to emergency check most threats in general also alleviates the pressure against these walls, especially with its good matchup against offensive teams that can otherwise run them over.

Dragon Dance + Scale Shot.description:
Utilizing Loaded Dice and Scale Shot, Dragonite speeds through OU, giving it a powerful STAB move to hit many threats at least neutrally, OHKOing its fellow Dragon-types like Kyurem and Raging Bolt and, after a Dragon Dance, the likes of Ogerpon-W and Darkrai. Furthermore, after a Speed boost from Scale Shot or Dragon Dance, Dragonite can outspeed almost the entirety of the unboosted metagame, excluding Dragapult, Zamazenta, and Deoxys-S, and further usage of Scale Shot can make it extremely difficult to outspeed Dragonite without priority. Fire Punch slams the Steel-types that Scale Shot misses, like Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Kingambit, while letting it hit Fairy-types like Clefable and Hatterene.
