Finally, Encore shuts down both defensive and offensive Pokemon that dare to set up or recover on Dragonite, like Corviknight, Zamazenta, and Garganacl. Tera Fire boosts Fire Punch, pushing Corviknight into the 2HKO range and guaranteeing the 2HKO on Skarmory, Gholdengo, and Kingambit, and nullifies Cinderace's and Moltres's Will-O-Wisp, allowing Dragonite to turn potential checks into setup opportunities. Tera Fire also flips its weakness to Ice and Fairy from Pokemon like Weavile, Iron Valiant, and Clefable. Due to Scale Shot's Speed-boosting side effect, Jolly can be used to outspeed crucial targets like Dragapult and Zamazenta at just +1. Dragonite can also opt to run an Adamant nature, guaranteeing the OHKO on threats like Kyurem and Raging Bolt with 4 hits.

With its power and versatility, Dragonite finds itself on offense and hyper offense teams. Due to Dragonite's lack of Heavy-Duty Boots, entry hazard control is more important than ever to maintain both Multiscale and to avoid chip damage, so hazard control teammates like Iron Treads, Great Tusk, and Hatterene are crucial, with the latter also serving as a status blocker from pesky defensive Pokemon like Moltres and Gliscor. Speaking of status spreaders, Dragapult is a flight hazard for Dragonite, with a speedy Will-O-Wisp and devastating Dragon Darts, so partners like Primarina and Iron Valiant are solid picks to scare it away. An exceptional partner for Dragonite is Landorus-T, which brings hazard support in Stealth Rock, a fast Taunt that can deny Stealth Rock from setters like Glimmora and Ting Lu, and the ability to bring Dragonite in safely through U-turn. Other strong partners for Dragonite are Gholdengo and Iron Crown, as they can scare threats like Iron Valiant and Zamazenta, which Dragonite often struggles to switch into; the latter also works as a pivot through Volt Switch. Similarly, Dragonite also enjoys pairing with Galarian Slowking, which threatens Iron Valiant, Primarina, and other Fairy-types that halt Dragonite's attack and can also pivot with Chilly Reception. Dragonite alongside other physical attackers like Ogerpon-W can overwhelm physical walls like Gholdengo and Skarmory together, clearing the way for each other to wreak havoc. Dragonite can also take advantage of Water- and Grass-types like Hisuian Samurott and Ogerpon-W, covering for defensive partners like Primarina, Landorus-T, and Great Tusk. Kingambit also appreciates Dragonite as a teammate, as Dragonite can lure in checks like Cinderace and Moltres before flipping the tables with Tera Fire, allowing for an easier late-game sweep with Kingambit.

Bulky Phazer (3 Attacks + Roost).description:
Dragonite can fully lean into its defensive profile even more and complement it further with its strong STAB Dragon Tail and Extreme Speed to become a remarkable anti-offense tool. Its hit-taking ability allows it to emergency check and phaze even dangerous threats like Darkrai, Dragapult, and Raging Bolt with Dragon Tail more reliably; the move is also helpful against other setup sweepers like Zamazenta, Gliscor, and Air Balloon Gholdengo that can otherwise set up on and overwhelm Dragonite after enough boosts. Moreover, potentially forcing offensive staples like Zamazenta, Iron Moth, and Raging Bolt into the field when they're not ready to sweep yet essentially wastes their Dauntless Shield and Booster Energy. Dragon Tail has the added benefit of forcing out walls and switch-ins like Skarmory, Dondozo, and Alomomola that it can't easily threaten, especially preventing the latter from passing Wish to the desired teammate via Flip Turn. Once the offensive threats are weakened enough, they are picked off easily by Extreme Speed, especially frail ones like Iron Valiant and other priority users like Raging Bolt and non-Tera Ghost Kingambit. Earthquake rounds out its coverage to hit Steel-types like Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Iron Treads. At the cost of no longer hitting Gholdengo, Low Kick is an alternative option that similarly hits the Steel-types hard, particularly Kingambit—OHKOing even bulky variants and doesn't care about Air Balloon sets—while also providing strong coverage against foes like Ting-Lu, Garganacl, and Tyranitar. Tera Normal boosts the power of its Extreme Speed, letting it reach crucial benchmarks such as 2HKOing Iron Valiant, Darkrai, and Hisuian Samurott. Additionally, it sheds all of Dragonite's weaknesses and grants it a solidly neutral typing, notably improving its matchup against threats like Enamorus, Kyurem, and Dragapult. 16 Speed EVs are enough to let Dragonite outspeed Adamant Kingambit.

Dragonite is used on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its defensive utility and decent pressure, especially against offensive teams. It pairs well with all manner of walls found on these archetypes; Steel-types like Gholdengo, Corviknight, and Tinkaton can cover most of its shortcomings by handling foes like Kyurem, Weavile, Iron Valiant, and Enamorus, with Tinkaton and Gholdengo in particular being great as a stopgap to other Fairy-type setup sweepers like Clefable and Hatterene that not only threaten Dragonite out but cannot be phazed by its Dragon Tail. In return, Dragonite can switch into Ground-type moves from the likes of Landorus-T aimed at Gholdengo and Tinkaton. The aforementioned Corviknight and other Pokemon like Clefable and Gliscor are great Knock Off absorbers against Pokemon like Great Tusk and opposing Gliscor and Clefable, letting Dragonite keep its valuable Heavy-Duty Boots. However, Pokemon that Dragonite is supposed to switch into, like Ogerpon-W and Hisuian Samurott, will inevitably hit it with a Knock Off; Great Tusk, Galarian Weezing, and the aforementioned Corviknight are great as entry hazard removers to make sure Stealth Rock still won't be an issue. Additionally, Gliscor, Clefable, and other Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Skarmory are valuable as hazard setters themselves, letting the team rack up chip damage when paired with Dragonite's Dragon Tail, and notably put offensive threats like Enamorus and Iron Moth closer into Extreme Speed range, with Ting-Lu's Ruination forcing immediate progress in that regard for Dragonite to clean late-game more easily. Ting-Lu and Clefable are also great at switching into Dragapult, which otherwise cannot be revenge killed and forces out Dragonite. In return, Dragonite covers threats such as Ogerpon-W and Iron Moth for all of them, with its ability to emergency check other offensive threats in general giving them more breathing room. Gliscor, Clefable, and more offensive Pokemon like Darkrai and Weavile are also great Knock Off users, removing Heavy-Duty Boots to synergize well with the team's entry hazards and Dragonite's Dragon Tail, softening up the opposition more effectively for Dragonite to clean late-game. The aforementioned Darkrai and Weavile alongside other offensive Pokemon like Zamazenta also match up well against offensive teams so Dragonite isn't overwhelmed defensively when facing highly aggressive teams. On more bulky offensive teams, Dragonite can even employ an even wider range of offensive teammates, including Ogerpon-W, Kingambit, and Iron Valiant. Ogerpon-W in particular matches up well against the bulky teams that Dragonite struggles with, while Iron Valiant and its Encore can limit Fairy-type and Tera Fairy setup sweepers like Clefable and Raging Bolt that Dragonite cannot phaze. Moreover, Dragonite's propensity to force offensive threats like Iron Valiant, Darkrai, and Weavile to Terastallize into a Ghost-type to avoid its Extreme Speed allows Kingambit, Darkrai, and Weavile to deal with them more easily. While offensive, these threats also provide defensive utility for Dragonite; for instance, Kingambit checks Dragapult and Kyurem, Zamazenta handles Kingambit, and both of them deal with Weavile.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band Dragonite is a strong wallbreaker and revenge killer for offensive teams, with a strong Outrage capable of 2HKOing would-be checks like Alomomola, Pecharunt, and Cresselia. Extreme Speed enables Dragonite to revenge kill a myriad of threatening sweepers such as Iron Valiant and Iron Moth while doing solid neutral damage to most of the tier with the use of Tera Normal. Earthquake hits Steel-types like Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Heatran and provides a safer option into certain Pokemon like Raging Bolt, Pecharunt, Garganacl. Fire Punch is Dragonite's highest damage option against Ground-immune Steel-types, capable of 2HKOing Pokemon like Skarmory, Corviknight, and Air Balloon variants of Kingambit and Gholdengo. Ice Spinner OHKOes both Gliscor and Landorus-T, common physical answers that often switch in against Dragonite to stuff potential Dragon Dance sets. It also safely hits foes like opposing Dragonite, Hydrapple, and Great Tusk without being locked into Outrage. An Adamant nature is chosen because Extreme Speed reduces the need for a Jolly nature and it importantly removes the need for good damage rolls against aforementioned Pokemon like Corviknight and Primarina. Tera Normal enables revenge killing with Extreme Speed further while removing all of Dragonite's original weaknesses. This reduces damage it takes from Stealth Rock, lets it take on foes like Enamorus and Iron Valiant more comfortably, and allow it to even survive attacks like Dragapult's Dragon Darts, Weavile's Triple Axel, and Kyurem's Icicle Spear and Scale Shot, which can otherwise bypass its Multiscale.

Choice Band Dragonite needs specific support to thrive. As it is weak to Stealth Rock, wants to preserve Multiscale, and does not run Heavy-Duty Boots, it appreciates entry hazard control from the likes of Great Tusk or Hatterene. Similarly, to preserve Multiscale and to find good opportunities to break, pivots are great teammates. Galarian Slowking, Landorus-T, and Primarina can all support the team defensively while using their pivot moves to safely get in Dragonite. Primarina additionally can switch into and force out threats like Dragapult, while Galarian Slowking can set up dangerous checkmate scenarios with Future Sight to limit defensive checks like Clefable and Zamazenta. Hazards greatly help to set up consistent 2HKOs and the potential for a late-game Extreme Speed sweep, so Spikes setters like Hisuian Samurott and Ting-Lu also fit in, as do Stealth Rock setters like Landorus-T and Great Tusk. Other offensive Pokemon fit best with Dragonite, with fast sweepers like Iron Valiant and Iron Moth especially appreciating Dragonite's breaking power and defensive utility in Multiscale and priority. Gholdengo and Iron Moth are strong teammates, as they take advantage of the Fairy- and Steel-types that threaten Dragonite while keeping up offensive pressure. As the set relies on a Choice item, Protect users like Alomomola, Garganacl, and Gliscor can greatly lessen the threat that Dragonite poses. Ogerpon-W is a teammate that threatens all of them while also generally helping against the style of teams that those Pokemon find themselves on. Kingambit deserves a mention, as both it and Dragonite can wear down physical walls for each other and threaten to clean late-game with their strong priority attacks. Tinkaton is another option as a Stealth Rock setter that also helps to check opposing would-be revenge killers like Dragapult and Darkrai while spreading Thunder Wave paralysis to give Dragonite more opportunities to attack freely.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dragon Dance (Flying)

Encore can be used on threats such as Raging Bolt, Primarina, and Bisharp to lock them into setup moves while also allowing Dragonite to take advantage of Gliscor, Skarmory, and Toxapex on a predicted non-damaging or non-status move. A combination of Thunder Punch and Ice Spinner can be used to deal with opposing Flying teams with its perfect coverage, but such a set needs to have Iron Defense Skarmory removed prior.

Dragon Dance (Dragon).description:
Dragonite is a great setup sweeper boasting nearly unresisted coverage, a useful Flying typing, and a convenient ability in Multiscale, allowing for an easier time setting up. Outrage is preferred due to the lack of Fairy-types and its utter power, allowing Dragonite to sweep opposing Dragon teams with the help of Baxcalibur and Dragapult late-game. Earthquake allows Dragonite to nail Poison- and Steel-type switch-ins such as Toxapex, Clodsire, and Gholdengo. Alternatively, Fire Punch threatens would-be checks like Corviknight and Air Balloon Gholdengo. Extreme Speed picks off weakened threats such as Greninja and Iron Valiant attempting to revenge kill it, while Encore may be used to lock physical walls like Dondozo, Quagsire, and Ting-Lu into a move, either letting Dragonite deal extra chip damage or effortlessly set up in front of them. A Jolly nature allows Dragonite to outpace Dragapult after a Dragon Dance so that Dragonite can OHKO them with Outrage, at the cost of power.

Dragonite appreciates Baxcalibur's immunity to Will-O-Wisp from threats such as Sableye and Skeledirge, neutrality to Ice-type moves, and ability to threaten Ting-Lu. In return, Dragonite checks troublesome Fighting-types like Quaquaval and Slither Wing. Garchomp sets up entry hazards in the form of Stealth Rock and Spikes, chipping down Dragonite's switch-ins such as Forretress, Archaludon, and Quagsire. Dragapult breaks past walls such as Dondozo and Corviknight and prevents Rapid Spin users like Great Tusk and Iron Treads from clearing Garchomp's entry hazards. Dragalge's secondary Poison typing and commendable bulk allow it to check Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Flutter Mane, and it supports Dragonite's sweeping with Toxic Spikes, notably wearing down Ting-Lu, Slowbro, and Quagsire. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon is a great revenge killer and method of speed control, as it outpaces and deals with Choice Scarf Latias and Choice Specs Greninja. Walking Wake is another plausible Choice Scarf user due to its ability to threaten Weavile and singlehandedly sweep Fire teams.

Choice Band (Flying).description:
Dragonite is a terrifying wallbreaker on Flying teams by virtue of its high Attack stat further boosted by Choice Band as well as its great coverage moves. Furthermore, a great ability in Multiscale allows it to survive super effective attacks from the likes of Iron Valiant and Hydreigon. Extreme Speed allows Dragonite to serve as a sweeper, easily sweeping through frail foes that don't resist it, and it also revenge kills boosted, albeit weakened, setup sweepers such as Volcarona. Earthquake targets Steel- and Poison-types like Iron Treads, Bisharp, Heatran, and Toxapex. Fire Punch allows Dragonite to threaten foes that resist Outrage and are immune to Earthquake like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Air Balloon Gholdengo.

Corviknight is an essential teammate for Dragonite, since it handles Rock-, Fairy-, and Ice-types like Ogerpon-C, Hatterene, and Weavile with Iron Head, pivots it in with U-turn, and uses Defog to remove Stealth Rock that would otherwise wear Dragonite down over time and break Multiscale. In return, Corviknight appreciates Dragonite handling the aforementioned Fire-types as well as Electric-types like Magnezone and Raging Bolt. Skarmory and Gliscor set up entry hazards to help Dragonite in its wallbreaking. Additionally, Skarmory can wall physical attackers like Bisharp and Iron Boulder with Iron Defense and threaten them back with Body Press, while Gliscor aids in the Electric matchup thanks to its Ground typing. Zapdos makes for a great partner, as it can pivot Dragonite in with Volt Switch and take care of physically bulky threats like Amoonguss and Iron Defense Corviknight. Dragonite handles Iron Treads and Clodsire in return. Choice Scarf Enamorus is great speed control, as it takes care of faster threats that can threaten Dragonite like Dragapult, Garchomp, and Choice Specs Greninja. In return, Enamorus appreciates Dragonite taking out Steel-types like Gholdengo and Iron Treads with Earthquake and Fire Punch. Landorus, with its colorful coverage, takes out threats to Dragonite like Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine, Kyurem, and Archaludon. Dragonite's wallbreaking is appreciated by late-game sweepers like Galarian Moltres that take advantage of Dragonite removing its checks like Clodsire and Toxapex to set up and sweep.

Choice Band (Dragon).description:
Equipped with a Choice Band, Dragonite makes for a strong wallbreaker on Dragon teams with its great coverage. With Extreme Speed, Dragonite not only revenge kills weakened threats, but it also serves as a cleaning option against foes that lack the proper physical bulk to deal with it. Earthquake breaks through bulky Poison- and Steel-types such as Toxapex, Alolan Muk, non-Air Balloon Heatran, and Hisuian Goodra. Fire Punch handles Grass- and Ice-types like Amoonguss and Frosmoth, as well as foes that can otherwise ignore Dragonite's other moves like unboosted Corviknight and Skarmory.

Dragonite appreciates entry hazard support from the likes of Archaludon and Garchomp. Additionally, Archaludon's great physical bulk allows it to switch in on physical attackers it easily shrugs off hits from like the Ogerpon formes, Meowscarada, and Kleavor, while Garchomp has to potential to set up and sweep late-game with Swords Dance and Scale Shot. In return, Dragonite handles Volcarona for Archaludon, while Garchomp appreciates the removal of Corviknight and Skarmory. Dragapult with Will-O-Wisp pairs well with Dragonite, as it weakens physical attackers such as Bisharp and Iron Hands so that Dragonite deals with them more easily, and Dragonite removes Alolan Muk for Dragapult in return. Hisuian Goodra makes for a great defensive partner, as with its great special bulk, it shrugs off attacks from the likes of Greninja and Flutter Mane, and it threatens Fairy-types like the aforementioned Flutter Mane. Hisuian Goodra also has access to Knock Off to remove items like Leftovers and Black Sludge from their holders so that Dragonite can threaten them more easily. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon provides great speed control, and with its colorful moveset, it threatens Ghost- and Fairy-types like Dragapult, Spectrier, non-Choice Scarf Flutter Mane, and Iron Valiant and brings Dragonite in safely with U-turn. In return, Roaring Moon appreciates Dragonite handling Bug- and Fighting-types like Scizor, Volcarona, and Okidogi. Choice Scarf Latias is another great form of speed control, as it handles fast Dragon- and Fighting-types like Choice Specs Dragapult, Iron Valiant, and Great Tusk and it can use Trick to shut down walls like Amoonguss and Skarmory so Dragonite can more easily deal with them. Additionally, it provides Healing Wish support to not only give Dragonite another chance at wallbreaking also restore its Multiscale. Dragonite's wallbreaking opens the door for late-game sweepers such as Swords Dance Garchomp, Calm Mind Raging Bolt, and Calm Mind Latios to set up and start their own sweep.

Dragon Dance (Flying).description:
Dragonite is the premier setup sweeper on Flying teams thanks to its access to Dragon Dance and diverse movepool. Outrage or Dragon Claw are the STAB attacks of choice, hitting Dragon-type threats such as Dragapult, Latios, and Kyurem, while Earthquake provides solid coverage, removing Steel-types like non-Air Balloon Heatran and Gholdengo along with hitting Fire- and Rock-types such as Hisuian Arcanine and Glimmora. Extreme Speed provides utility in allowing Dragonite to clean up weakened threats along with catching Choice Scarf threats that outspeed it even after a Dragon Dance such as Meowscarada. Alternatively, Fire Punch hits both Skarmory and Corviknight, which could otherwise wall Dragonite, while Roost provides a way to keep Dragonite healthy, regain Multiscale, and safely tank resisted hits from the likes of Barraskewda. An Adamant nature is preferred, allowing Dragonite to remove Raging Bolt without a boost, while Jolly is an option to outspeed threats like Dragapult and Flutter Mane at +1.

Corviknight and Skarmory both make great support for Dragonite, with both handling Ice- and Rock-type threats like Weavile, Mamoswine, and Tyranitar. Corviknight can continue to support Dragonite by using U-turn to provide safe entry and Defog to remove Stealth Rock should Dragonite lose its Heavy-Duty Boots, while Skarmory supports Dragonite with entry hazards to chip down bulky walls such as Galarian Weezing, Corviknight, and opposing Skarmory, which can prove problematic. Gliscor and the Landorus formes remove Electric- and Rock-type threats such as Raging Bolt, Regieleki, and Iron Boulder along with using Stealth Rock to provide additional entry hazard support. Choice Scarf Enamorus removes Dragon- and Dark-type threats like Latios, Dragapult, and Sableye, giving Dragonite safer sweeping opportunities, and provides Healing Wish support to reactivate Multiscale, allowing Dragonite another chance to set up. Tornadus-T forms a solid wallbreaking core, with its powerful special attacks removing physical walls such as Galarian Weezing and Great Tusk, along with taking on foes like Ogerpon-H, which can pose challenges to Dragonite.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Dragonite is a very common bulky physical attacker on balance and physically offensive Coaching teams. Dragonite shines particularly well against weakened teams. It also appreciates redirection or speed control to make up for its mediocre Speed. It works well at supporting teams against hyper offensive teams, with its Multiscale sets allowing it to survive attacks from many common wallbreakers, including Garchomp and Kingambit. Dragonite works well on balance teams, which value more the great consistency and versatility in matchups and the support it can provide to the team through Haze and Tailwind.
  • Dragonite works very well in tandem with Gholdengo and Kingambit, which can cover the Fairy- and Ice-types that may threaten Dragonite. Dragonite also appreciates Coaching support from partners such as Sneasler, which can allow it to mitigate Defense drops from Scale Shot and become difficult to remove for many teams with just a few Coaching boosts. Additionally, redirection from Amoonguss and Fake Out from Rillaboom and Incineroar allow it to better fulfill both its offensive and supportive roles on a team.
  • Dragonite's main issues are its relatively low Speed, weakness to Intimidate, and inability to hit Fairy- and Steel-types except with relatively weak coverage options. Therefore, partners like Kingambit and Sneasler can help hit Dragonite's checks heavily. Additionally, Coaching can help shore up its lesser damage output, particularly against Intimidate from Incineroar, and Defiant from the aforementioned Kingambit as well as Annihilape can help punish Intimidate cycling. Another issue for Dragonite are Pokemon that are faster than it and can threaten to OHKO it, such as Dragapult, Alolan Ninetales, and Garchomp. Therefore, redirection is of great use to these Dragonite sets to deal with such threats.

Strategy Comments

  • Dragonite's main role on teams is as a bulky attacker that can also provide support for its team through Haze and Tailwind. It uses its power and priority to clean up weakened teams while maintaining usefulness throughout the game.
  • Dragonite is best used for its heavy damage output and large bulk, so it must be positioned it carefully around potential threats. Dragonite is at its best when Multiscale is kept intact, so keeping it away from weak attacks that may break it is crucial, as having Multiscale can allow Dragonite to tank a powerful hit from a threatening Pokemon and KO back. It can be used as a strong lead into offensive strategies or as a late-game cleaner against more balanced teams. It can also provide important support for its team if it is running Tailwind.
  • Dragonite's biggest issues are against Steel-types that are capable of withstanding its coverage options, such as Gholdengo and Corviknight, and strong Fairy- and Ice-types like Alolan Ninetales. To mitigate these threats, position your other Pokemon that can handle them and hit them with heavy damage early in the game with partners such as Sneasler and Incineroar so Dragonite can pick them off later in the game once correctly positioned. Another way around these threats is with redirection to protect Dragonite or Coaching support so it can overpower its checks.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Dragonite uses its high Attack and strong defenses, which are further boosted by Multiscale, to be a very powerful bulky physical attacker. It can be used to check a variety of metagame threats, including Sneasler, Rillaboom, and Torkoal, and provide support for itself and its teammates through the likes of Tailwind and Haze.

  • Scale Shot gives Dragonite a consistent and powerful STAB option, and the Speed boost gives it the potential to sweep teams. Tailwind allows Dragonite to support its team through speed control. Extreme Speed gives Dragonite a strong priority option to finish off low HP foes. Additionally, Haze can be used to counter setup sweepers like Dondozo. Ice Spinner provides coverage for Dragon-types with a 4x weakness to Ice such as Garchomp and can be used to clear Terrains, namely Psychic Terrain, from the field, whereas Stomping Tantrum gives it coverage for Steel- and Fire-types such as Kingambit and Incineroar.

  • Tera Fairy gives Dragonite an important immunity to Dragon-type moves, particularly Scale Shot from opposing Dragonite, giving it strong defensive utility and the ability to check powerful Dragons like Garchomp while removing Dragonite's Fairy and Ice weaknesses. Fairy is also a good defensive typing, being neutral or resistant to the majority of metagame-relevant attacks. However, this Tera type can leave it vulnerable to other important attacks, including Dire Claw from Sneasler and Make It Rain from Gholdengo. Tera Steel gives Dragonite a resistance to Ice-, Dragon- and Fairy-type attacks, including Blizzard from Alolan Ninetales, Moonblast from Primarina, and Dragon Claw from Garchomp that threaten it, while providing an immunity to Sneasler's Dire Claw and a resistance to Gholdengo's Make It Rain. This Tera type can also make it vulnerable to Ground-, Fire- and Fighting-type attacks.

  • 52 Speed EVs with an Adamant Nature allow Dragonite to outspeed Dragapult under Tailwind while allowing it to naturally outspeed Rillaboom and Archaludon and Ursaluna-B with low Speed investment while maximizing its damage output and maintaining its massive bulk. This Speed investment should only be used with an Adamant nature; a Jolly nature and maximum Speed investment can be used to increase the scope of things that Dragonite can outspeed after a Scale Shot; an example of a threat that Dragonite now outspeeds is Dragapult.

vgc2024.overview:
• Dragonite's great movepool, well-rounded stats, great ability in Inner Focus that makes it immune to Fake Out and Intimidate from Incineroar, and stellar matchups into threats like Urshifu-R, Rillaboom, and Ogerpon-W makes Dragonite a great Pokemon in Regulation F.

  • When holding a Choice Band, Dragonite becomes one of the scariest Pokemon in the metagame for its breaking power. Its best partner, Chien-Pao, supports it with Sword of Ruin and pressures Pokemon that prevent Extreme Speed, such as Indeedee and Flutter Mane. Dragonite and Chien-Pao also are good into Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W, making Dondozo and Tatsugiri, which struggle with these two, great partners as well.

  • Flutter Mane is also a great partner, as it breaks through Iron Hands and Gholdengo for Dragonite, while Dragonite is a great switch into Scarf Urshifu-R and Rillaboom.

Choice Band.description:
• Extreme Speed is a priority move that hits the majority of the metagame for neutral damage, making it ideal to lock into.

  • Aerial Ace allows Dragonite to OHKO Pokemon like Urshifu-R, Rillaboom, and Amoongus without having to be lock into Outrage. Aqua Jet is secondary priority and allows it to double up with its partner on Ghost-types like Flutter Mane, and Ice Spinner allows it to remove Indeedee-F's Psychic Terrain while still having coverage for Pokemon like Rillaboom and Amoongus.

  • Outrage is used as its Dragon-type STAB move and allows it to OHKO almost the entire metagame.

  • Stomping Tantrum gives coverage into Steel-types like Kingambit and Archaludon.

  • The Speed EVs allow Dragonite to outspeed Dragapult in Tailwind, with the remaining EVs maximize its Attack and round out its bulk, allowing it to live attacks such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Dazzling Gleam

  • Normal is used as the Tera type, boosting Dragonite's Extreme Speed to stellar levels of power and removing its weaknesses to common Fairy- and Ice-type moves.

Loaded Dice Sweeper.description:
• Loaded Dice Dragonite threatens heavy damage and a boost to its Speed with Scale Shot, allowing it to outspeed Adamant Chien-Pao and Modest Flutter Mane. Inner Focus can be used to stop Incineroar from slowing it down, while Multiscale can make it difficult to remove, letting it get a key Scale Shot off.

  • Dragonite is common on teams with partners that make it even harder to remove, especially if it has Multiscale, such as Ting-Lu's Vessel of Ruin weakening foes like Flutter Mane and Raging Bolt, or Sinistcha's Hospitality healing it back to full HP and reactivating Multiscale. Partners that struggle into Incineroar, such as Chien-Pao and Gouging Fire, appreciate Dragonite blocking Intimidate with Inner Focus and threatening it with damage.

  • Scale Shot is Dragonite's strongest Dragon-type attack without risking locking into Outrage. Iron Head can threaten an OHKO on opposing Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and deal large damage to Tera Fairy Raging Bolt after Scale Shot pressures it to Terastallize. Extreme Speed can pick off low-HP targets and beat out other priority moves like Sucker Punch and Thunderclap.

  • Loaded Dice turns Scale Shot into a much more powerful move on average, with four hits OHKOing less bulky variants of Raging Bolt and five hits nearly always securing an OHKO.

  • After a Speed boost from Scale Shot, Dragonite outspeeds most of the unboosted metagame, allowing it to run an Adamant nature to improve damage rolls. Once its Speed is boosted, it can OHKO Focus Sash Chien-Pao with a five-hit Scale Shot and flinch slower foes with Iron Head. An Adamant nature is necessary for OHKOs on bulky Raging Bolt, and a Chien-Pao on the field can further improve damage rolls with Sword of Ruin.

  • Tera Steel turns Dragonite's weaknesses to Dragon-, Fairy-, and Ice-type moves into resistances, helping against Draco Meteor from Raging Bolt, Moonblast from Flutter Mane, and Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao. Additionally, it boosts Iron Head's damage output, guaranteeing an OHKO on bulky Flutter Mane.

Dragon Dance + Z-Move.description:
Dragonite is an elite offensive Pokemon that can disrupt common balance structures when holding a Z-crystal; common switch-ins to Dragonite like offensive Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Gliscor fall to +1 Devastating Drake. Dragonite also has great defensive utility, using Multiscale to effectively set up Dragon Dance in front of foes such as Ogerpon-W and Urshifu-R. Earthquake grants Dragonite the opportunity to hit Pokemon such as Heatran and Toxapex, which can discourage any Stealth Rock-setting or Haze attempts, respectively. It also threatens other Steel-type Pokemon like Kingambit and Melmetal. Fire Punch discourages bulky Steel-types that don't mind Earthquake such as Ferrothorn, Air Balloon Gholdengo, and Corviknight from coming in freely. A Jolly nature is usually preferred, as it allows Dragonite to outspeed foes like Zamazenta and Tapu Koko at +1.

This variant of Dragonite is found on more offensive structures, where it is paired with Pokemon such as Mega Diancie; it can deny any attempts of entry hazard setting from the opposition, as this Dragonite set lacks Heavy-Duty Boots. Dragonite, in return, provides a valuable Water- and Grass-resistant teammate for Mega Diancie to aid against foes such as Rillaboom and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. These teams appreciate Dragonite providing a valuable Water-resistant ally, as it is an effective answer to foes like Ogerpon-W and Urshifu-R. Kingambit values Dragonite weakening its checks, such as Great Tusk and Zamazenta, to give it a more favorable end-game. In return, Kingambit can remove key items from checks like Corviknight and Great Tusk to enable Dragonite to use its moves more freely. Heatran is also an effective partner, since it is able to answer Pokemon Dragonite doesn't immediately threaten such as Clefable while also being a good answer to Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, which still threatens Dragonite after a Dragon Dance. Even at +1 Speed, Dragonite is still outsped by Choice Scarf users like Landorus-T and Tapu Lele, so it appreciates partners like Air Balloon Gholdengo as a partner to potentially use those foes as setup fodder. Spinners such as Great Tusk and Terapagos are also effective teammates, as they can provide hazard removal through Rapid Spin to ensure Dragonite does not take Stealth Rock damage to keep Multiscale intact. Great Tusk and Dragonite often form a core to overwhelm their shared checks, such as Alomomola, Slowbro, and Skarmory. Volcarona also appreciates Dragonite being able to provide a crucial Water resistance, helping it against Pokemon such as Ogerpon-W. At the same time, Volcarona can find setup opportunities versus Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, which usually comes in to revenge kill Dragonite with Moonblast. Dragonite values hazard-setting leads such as Mega Diancie and Landorus-T, as the latter is able to provide Taunt to keep opposing hazards off whereas the former denies hazards through Magic Bounce while breaking down the opposition with its strong STAB moves.

Offensive Dragon Dance.description:
Dragonite is a very unique sweeper, as it is able to set up reliably in the face of offensive Pokemon like Urshifu-R, Ogerpon-W, and Mega Charizard Y. Earthquake allows it to target foes such as Gholdengo, Heatran, and Toxapex, preventing them from staying in to spread status through moves such as Thunder Wave from the former and Toxic from the latter two. Ice Spinner grants Dragonite the ability to threaten foes like Gliscor and Landorus-T, which are usually key defensive pillars of their teams, and stops them from coming in for free to land Toxic on Dragonite. Ice- and Ground-type coverage additionally hits a vast amount of Pokemon in the metagame. Roost gives Dragonite the longevity to answer Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Urshifu-R and also provides more setup opportunities, which allows Dragonite to break through foes like Toxapex and Ferrothorn. Extreme Speed can be used over Roost, as it helps Dragonite pick off weakened faster Pokemon like Iron Valiant and Tapu Koko that would normally outspeed and threaten it. Dual Wingbeat hits Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Zamazenta significantly harder.

Dragonite is used on a plethora of different bulky offense and balance teams, as they appreciate Dragonite's defensive utility, with it being able to switch into offensive Water-types like Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-W and find many different opportunities to set up Dragon Dance. Pokemon like Mega Diancie appreciate Dragonite's ability to respond to foes like Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Landorus-T. In return, Mega Diancie can pressure Dragonite's checks like Ferrothorn with Mystical Fire and Zapdos with Diamond Storm. Dragonite can have a difficult time in the face of Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Tapu Lele that still outspeed it after a Dragon Dance, so it values the presence of Steel-types like Gholdengo and Heatran to switch into it. Scale Shot Garchomp and Icicle Spear Kyurem also outspeed and break through Dragonite's Multiscale. Therefore, allies such as Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Speed Booster Energy Speed Iron Valiant are appreciated to outspeed and threaten these foes. Kingambit also helps versus Air Balloon Gholdengo, which Dragonite does not immediately threaten. Volcarona is also an effective partner, as it can respond to Pokemon that directly threaten Dragonite like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant, the former of which blocks Dragonite's Extreme Speed with Psychic Terrain. Great Tusk is an effective partner, since it is able to wear down checks such as Landorus-T with both Stealth Rock and Ice Spinner, letting Dragonite break through opposing teams more easily mid-game. Great Tusk can also help break through Toxapex with Headlong Rush and hit Ferrothorn with Close Combat. In return, Dragonite responds to Water-types like Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-W that force out Great Tusk.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the return of the Regulation G format and its powerful restricted threats!
battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Speed EV Benchmarks

  • After a single Dragon Dance or Scale Shot, Dragonite will always outspeed up to Adamant Urshifu-formes regardless of Dragonite's Speed investment.

  • 12 Spe: At +1, this outspeeds Modest Chi-Yu.

  • 44 Spe: This outspeeds uninvested Archaludon.

  • 76 Spe: At +1, this outspeeds Jolly Urshifu-formes.

  • 92 Spe: This outspeeds uninvested Landorus-T. At +1, this outspeeds Timid Chi-Yu. At +2, this outspeeds Timid Calyrex-S.

  • 100 Spe: This outspeeds the uncommon Jolly Ursaluna.

  • 132 Spe: This outspeeds uninvested Mimikyu.

  • 140 Spe: This outspeeds uninvested Urshifu-formes.

  • 172+ Spe: At +1, this outspeeds Adamant Zacian-C.

  • 204+ Spe: At +1, this outspeeds Pokemon with base Speeds of 135 and a positive Speed nature such as Jolly Chien-Pao and Timid Miraidon.

Choice Band.description:
• Choice Band makes Dragonite both an effective late-game cleaner and revenge killer with Extreme Speed, and a powerful wallbreaker against foes such as Ting-Lu, Ursaluna-B, and Dondozo.

  • Extreme Speed: Boosted by both Choice Band and Tera Normal, Extreme Speed easily 2HKOes up to maximum HP Miraidon that aren't running Electric Seed.

  • Outrage: Outrage is strong enough to potentially 2HKO Bold Ursaluna-B and Impish Dondozo after Stealth Rock damage, though it leaves Dragonite very vulnerable to getting revenge killed.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake provides the best overall coverage against Steel-types that resist Extreme Speed and Outrage.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick is Dragonite's best move against Ursaluna-B, making it much more difficult for Ursaluna-B to stall with Moonlight without defensive Terastallization.

  • Ice Spinner: Ice Spinner is primarily used to punish Landorus-T that try to switch in, and being super effective against common Dragon-types makes it a rather effective midground option when trying to predict switches.

Other Options

  • Tera Blast Flying: While not as dominating as in past regulations, Tera Blast Flying is still one of Dragonite's hardest-hitting moves that has no type immunities to worry about. If using this option, a Special Attack IV of 17 or lower is needed to prevent Tera Blast from flipping to a special attack after being hit by Flutter Mane's Charm.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: This Dragonite will usually want to Terastallize to either increase its revenge killing or wallbreaking capabilities, but Choice Band's power doesn't make this strictly necessary.

  • Normal: Tera Normal massively boosts Dragonite's revenge killing potential with Extreme Speed and cuts off Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage from doing any damage.

  • Flying: With Tera Blast, Tera Flying is a strong wallbreaking option that lets Dragonite potentially 2HKO bulky Pokemon like defensive Ursaluna-B. It also lets Dragonite demolish offensive Urshifu formes without the need for Outrage.

Scale Shot Sweeper.description:
• Dragonite is a great user of Scale Shot, utilizing its bulk and Multiscale to set up easily.

  • Dragon Dance: A single Dragon Dance makes Scale Shot much more consistent at OHKOing Focus Sash Chien-Pao while also enabling five-hit Scale Shot to OHKO offensive Urshifu.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head punishes Fairy-types and Tera Fairy users that try to block Scale Shot.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake provides great all-around coverage while reliably hitting common Steel-types.

  • Extreme Speed: Extreme Speed is useful for revenge killing faster foes and helps Dragonite outrun other priority users trying to exploit Scale Shot's Defense drops.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Jolly allows Dragonite to outspeed Chien-Pao, Flutter Mane, Koraidon, and Miraidon after a single Dragon Dance. However, many of these targets employ means of raising their Speed, so it is usually more worth it to maximize damage with Adamant and try to hit +2 Speed instead.

Other Options

  • Low Kick: Low Kick gives Dragonite the most damage output against Ursaluna-B, which is otherwise strong at stopping Dragonite's momentum.

  • Encore: Encore with Dragon Dance makes it easier to set up on passive foes, but the sacrifice in coverage can make it difficult to fit.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Dragonite's bulk and Multiscale still go a long way in helping it set up, but Terastallization can extend its reach and make it harder to revenge kill.

  • Steel: Tera Steel is a powerful response to Fairy-types like Flutter Mane, resisting Moonblast and boosting Iron Head. The resistance to Normal-type moves is also strong, helping cushion Ursaluna-B and opposing Extreme Speed Dragonite.

  • Normal: Tera Normal remains a strong option for boosting Extreme Speed and shedding Dragonite's Dragon-type weaknesses. It also shuts down Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S.

Extreme Killernite.description:
• With Tera Normal, Dragonite can do its best impression of Arceus, with a powerful Extreme Speed that makes Dragonite a great revenge killer, and even a sweeper if using Dragon Dance!

  • Earthquake: Earthquake offers the best coverage against the widest variety of Normal-type resistances, with Archaludon, Glimmora, and Scizor being big targets.

  • Encore: Encore lets Dragonite disrupt passive Pokemon and gives it incredible switch-in opportunities, making it a worthy move to consider. It can give free setup when paired with Dragon Dance, or it can turn Dragonite into a long-term defensive disruptor when paired with Roost.

  • Tera Dependency - High: This set benefits immensely from the ability to Terastallize to both boost Extreme Speed's power while also removing Dragon type weaknesses. However, care should be taken on the timing of Terastallization depending on the matchup, as Dragonite more effectively checks several prominent threats, such as Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-H, with its base typing.

Other Options

  • Dragon Tail: Dragon Tail is a unique alternative to Encore, allowing Dragonite to phaze out fast setup attackers that are risky to switch into or otherwise catch with Encore, such as Calyrex-S.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet lets Dragonite play more passively against physical threats, which is especially relevant before it Terastallizes. In particular, Urshifu-R without Punching Gloves takes a lot of damage from using Surging Strikes.

  • Silk Scarf: Silk Scarf gives a small but significant boost to Extreme Speed's cleaning power. When used with Tera Normal, Dragonite can 2HKO offensive Miraidon!

  • Leftovers: The residual recovery of Leftovers makes it easier to maintain Multiscale when using Roost.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Stealth Rock is commonly set up specifically to break Dragonite's Multiscale, so Heavy-Duty Boots are a good way to always preserve Dragonite's ability to set up and revenge kill.

Alternate EV Spread

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Impish Going fully defensive means Dragonite won't sweep nearly as easily, but Dragonite is still capable of being an effective defensive Pokemon even after Terastallization.

Phazer.description:
• With Multiscale's incredible bulk potential and Dragon Tail bypassing Taunt, Dragonite is a unique and very effective phazer that massively ups the danger of entry hazards!

  • Dragon Tail VS. Roar: Dragon Tail is preferred for it disregarding Taunt and providing some good chip damage. However, Roar can phaze out meddlesome Fairy-types and users of Substitute.

  • Entry Hazard Teammates: For this Dragonite to be at its most effective, you'll need some partners to at least set up Stealth Rock. Ting-Lu and Archaludon are particularly bulky examples that pair well, but other options include Landorus-T, Swampert, and Annihilape.

  • Earthquake VS. Iron Head: Earthquake is the most wide-reaching coverage move, ensuring good damage against Normal resistances like Garganacl and Archaludon. If using Roar, Iron Head prevents Levitate Pokemon from completely walling Dragonite, and its flinch rate synergies well with Thunder Wave.

  • Thunder Wave: Dragonite's bulk makes it an ace at spreading paralysis, making it more of a team supporter.

  • Substitute versus Encore: Substitute is a fantastic option against Pokemon with status moves that threaten Dragonite's phazing cycles, such as Garganacl, Porygon2, and Toxapex. Encore won't do as well against these threats but does punish opposing foes carrying Substitute that can be a problem for Dragon Tail along with slower foes that use status moves in general such as Ting-Lu and Ursaluna-B. Encore can even be used over extra coverage if teammates can deal with Fairy-types.

  • Extreme Speed versus Aqua Jet: Extreme Speed's ability to pick off threats is useful, even on defensive variants of this set. Despite being half as powerful, Aqua Jet is still worth considering for its ability to pick off weakened Flutter Mane, which can be difficult for this set to handle due to its power when Multiscale isn't in play.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is a high value item, but it's worth using on Dragonite if using Substitute, as it gives Dragonite a serious chance of passively gaining Multiscale's effect back.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet allows Dragonite to play more passively, punishing Pokemon that rely on contact moves like Choice Item Urshifu-R and Annihilape.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots' Stealth Rock immunity makes Multiscale more flexible, especially if Dragon Tail brings in a threat Dragonite isn't equipped to handle.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 76 Def / 180 Spe with Impish: This spread gives up quite a bit of bulk in exchange for outspeeding Adamant Breloom, while still often mantaining a Substitute against Garganacl's Salt Cure.

  • 252 HP / 124 Atk / 108 Def / 4 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread is optimized for use with Earthquake and Aqua Jet, allowing Dragonite to 2HKO 4 Defense Flutter Mane with that combination of moves without needing to Terastallize. Only Modest Tera Fairy Flutter Mane will have a chance to OHKO through Multiscale.

  • 252 HP / 252 Atk / 4 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread is a far more offensive approach, mainly for use with Extreme Speed to pick off threats more effectively.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Dragonite's defensive typing can be quite helpful against foes like Urshifu-R and Chi-Yu, but some of the huge exploitable weaknesses to Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane will require Terastallization to cover.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy's Dragon immunity gels well with Dragonite and is a great defensive typing in general against foes like Chien-Pao and Urshifu.

  • Steel: Tera Steel is not only an incredible defensive typing that covers much of Dragonite's former weaknesses, but the power boost it provides to Iron Head lets it OHKO all but the most bulky Flutter Mane.

  • Normal: Tera Normal isn't that incredible defensively, but it can be worth it for boosting Extreme Speed's power, letting offensive EV spreads 2HKO Chien-Pao with it.

Paraflinch.description:
• Paraflinch Dragonite is a defensively oriented Dragonite set that takes full advantage of Terastallization and the element of surprise to cripple and downright defeat numerous Pokemon. Multiscale allows Dragonite to paralyze its foes relatively safely, becoming a massive nuisance for unprepared opponents.

  • Air Slash vs. Iron Head: Air Slash is a more practical move for this set, as it can cover a wider range of Pokemon for at least neutral damage. Air Slash also does not trigger Rocky Helmet and is naturally boosted by Dragonite's STAB. The Iron Head variant of Paraflinch, however, gives Dragonite an easier time against a number of common threats such as Flutter Mane, at the cost of struggling against Gouging Fire before they Terastallize.

  • Encore vs. Substitute: Encore will allow Dragonite to effectively check a wider variety of Pokemon such as Ursaluna-B by locking them into an unfavorable move, giving it a free opportunity to land Thunder Wave on your opponent's switch-in on the following turn. Substitute, on the other hand, will give Dragonite a much easier time dealing with defensive Pokemon that rely on status infliction such as Porygon2 and Dragon Tail Archaludon.

Other Options
  • Waterfall: Waterfall can be a viable option. However, the move is less reliable for the application of this set, as its chance to flinch is 20% as opposed to Air Slash and Iron Head's 30%. It does deal more damage to common Electric-types like Thundurus-T though.
EV and IV Spreads

  • 244 HP / 236 Def / 28 Spe: 52 Speed EVs are the minimum Speed requirement to outspeed paralyzed Iron Bundle that lack Booster Energy.

  • 252 HP / 140 Def / 116 Spe: This is the minimum requirement to outspeed paralyzed Modest Choice Scarf Chi-Yu.

  • 0 Attack IVs: If using Air Slash, 0 Attack IVs are highly recommended for having a high chance of retaining Substitute against STAB Foul Play users such as Porygon2

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: In order for Dragonite to survive multiple turns against the likes of Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane, Terastallizating into a better defensive typing is usually a must.

  • Steel: Steel is a great defensive type that provides resistance to Fairy-type attacks, such as Moon Blast from Flutter Mane. If using the physical set, Tera Steel also provides a significant boost to the damage of Iron Head.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is Dragonite's best option against opposing Dragon-types, such as Roaring Moon and Gouging Fire.

  • Water: Tera Water provides Dragonite with the much-needed defensive versatility to paralyze and wall common threats, such as Chien-Pao and Azumarill. Water is an excellent defensive type in general with its only weaknesses being Electric and Grass.

Defensive Dragon Dance.description:
• Dragonite's good bulk gives it plenty of chances to set up Dragon Dance, while still providing a solid defensive backbone.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake is a reliable move for covering Steel-types, and Fire-types like Gouging Fire if using Iron Head and Tera Steel.

  • Breaking Swipe: While weak, Breaking Swipe's Attack drop makes it even easier for Dragonite to set up, making it preferred over Dragon Claw.

  • Encore: Encore makes setting up on slower defensive foes such as Corviknight fairly easy, though the lack of coverage makes Terastallizing far more important.

  • Thunder Punch versus Electric Tera Blast: If using Tera Electric, Thunder Punch is a low-power but reliable STAB option. However, while Tera Blast almost certainly requires Dragonite to Terastallize, it does avoid Rocky Helmet chip damage and is a tad more powerful.

Other Options
  • Ice Spinner: Ice Spinner deals massive damage to Landorus-T and other Flying-types, making it a reasonable coverage option to consider if using a Tera type that can deal with Steel-types, like Water or Electric.
Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet lets Dragonite play more passively thanks to the chip damage, and can be paired with Encore to severely punish slower physical attackers like Scizor.

  • Clear Amulet: Clear Amulet stops common Attack debuffers such as Charm Flutter Mane and Intimidate Landorus-T from ruining Dragonite's offenses, making it much harder to cycle around. As a bonus, it also stops Rock Tomb Speed drops from common foes like Ogerpon-H.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Preserving Multiscale even when Stealth Rock is set up can help Dragonite survive attacks in emergencies.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers's passive healing gives Dragonite a better matchup against passive foes it can Encore.

  • Covert Cloak: With Covert Cloak and Encore, Dragonite becomes a very solid check to Garganacl, as well as no longer fearing Breaking Swipe or flinches.

  • Weakness Policy: Since Multiscale makes Dragonite very difficult to OHKO, Weakness Policy is a viable option to turn the tables on foes targeting Dragonite's weaknesses.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 188 Defense / 76 Spe with Impish: This EV spread outspeeds up to Jolly Urshifu after one Dragon Dance, and Iron Bundle after two Dragon Dances.

  • 252 HP / 52 Def / 204 Spe with Jolly: This is the minimum Speed needed to outspeed Timid Iron Bundle after a boost, and it also outspeeds Flutter Mane and Chien-Pao.

  • 252 HP / 140 Defense / 112 Speed with Impish: This spread outspeeds Adamant Roaring Moon, Jolly Garchomp, and Timid Chi-Yu after Dragon Dance, all of which are threats that can easily revenge kill Dragonite once Multiscale is broken.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High / Almost Required: This Dragonite lacks a powerful STAB attack without Terastallization, making it highly recommended. If using Tera Flying with Tera Blast as the only attack, this set will need Terastallization to function.

  • Steel: Tera Steel covers Dragonite's former weaknesses very well, and can still work somewhat well even if not Terastallized thanks to Iron Head, though note it makes this Dragonite much more vulnerable to Urshifu and Ogerpon-H.

  • Flying: With Tera Blast, Tera Flying gives Dragonite a solid mono-attacking option and defensive typing in one, at the cost of almost always needing to Terastallize to function.

  • Electric: Though this requires extra coverage to be viable, Tera Electric shields Dragonite from paralysis, which can be combined with Clear Amulet to ruin more supportive Flutter Mane sets! Being only weak to Ground-type attacks also makes it a solid defensive Tera Type for Dragonite.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy gives Dragonite an excellent mono-attacking Tera Blast that gives it an advantage over other Dragon-types.

  • Water: Tera Water gifts Dragonite a resistance to Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash without being weak to Sacred Sword, plus it pairs well with Waterfall.

Encore Trapper.description:
• Due to Dragonite's offensive presence and high bulk, many opponents choose to either check it defensively or set up against it to break through Roost + Multiscale. Against either option, Encore can turn Dragonite practically invincible allowing it to reside on the field indefinitely in most cases.

  • Fire Spin: This allows Dragonite to defeat almost any Pokemon universally by simply making full use of its longevity. Trapping an Encore locked Pokemon in the field is also highly valuable. Fire Spin is used instead of Wrap because it affects Ghost-types and doesn't trigger chip damage from Rough Skin and Rocky Helmet.

  • Earthquake versus Iron Head: Earthquake prevents Dragonite from being entirely passive against Archaludon, Gouging Fire, and Flutter Mane. Meanwhile, Iron Head fits using Tera Steel, and does massive damage to Flutter Mane.

  • Draco Meteor: With a Bold Nature, Draco Meteor is a powerful move that can catch opposing Dragon-types off-guard and deal big damage to Ursaluna-B and Urshifu formes.

Items

  • Leftovers versus Heavy-Duty Boots Generally, Leftovers preserves Dragonite’'s longevity best, as it cancels out the damage from Sandstorm and makes timer stall easier. However, the increased usage of entry hazard setters in response to Dragonite makes Heavy-Duty Boots a strong option.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet makes it easier for Dragonite to defeat Pokemon such as opposing Dragonite, Urshifu-R, and Gouging Fire (while Dragonite is Terastallized), and its residual damage can be used to execute a win condition.

  • Covert Cloak: With Covert Cloak, this Dragonite becomes a very effective check to Garganacl, in addition to no longer being vulnerable to flinches from Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash while Terastallizing.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Dragonite's typing does have some fairly exploitable weaknesses that can harm its defensive capability, but an immunity to Toxic Spikes and useful resistances to common attack types such as Ground, Fire, and Fighting mean that Terastallization is not always the right play.

  • Fairy: Due to Dragonite’'s low Speed compared to other Dragon-types, Tera Fairy is a great response against them. This also retains its advantage against Urshifu formes.

  • Steel: Tera Steel massively improves Dragonite's matchups against Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle, at the cost of being even more vulnerable to Salt Cure and Urshifu formes.

  • Water: Tera Water adds a resistance to Ice without losing Dragonite's innate Fire-type resistance, which is helpful against Chien-Pao and Urshifu-R.

  • Poison: The niche Tera Poison gives Dragonite a way to remove its common weaknesses without being vulnerable to Toxic Spikes, while still resisting Fighting unlike Tera Steel.

Double Priority Lure.description:
• With Flying-type Tera Blast OHKOing physically frail and Flying-weak Pokemon such as Flutter Mane, Ogerpon-H, and Urshifu-R, this set is effective at fooling opponents into thinking that it's Choice Band Dragonite.

  • Aqua Jet: It may seem redundant with Extreme Speed, but Aqua Jet is a key move for picking off weakened Ghost-types, such as Flutter Mane, and surprising Focus Sash Pokemon that might use Tera Ghost to avoid being sniped by Extreme Speed, such as Iron Bundle. This can also work against Chien-Pao, but Icicle Crash's flinch chance makes this rather risky.

  • Earthquake versus Low Kick: Earthquake is the preferred coverage move for dealing big damage against Archaludon and Gholdengo, common responses to a Dragonite locked into Tera Blast. Low Kick trades smacking Gholdengo for revenge killing opposing Tera Normal Dragonite and dealing massive damage to Ting-Lu.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is the best nature for needing less chip damage to revenge kill weakened targets with priority attacks, but Jolly can make sense if outspeeding foes like Modest Gholdengo, Adamant Gouging Fire, and the rare Jolly Breloom is appealing.

  • Tera Dependency - Almost Required: This set is highly reliant on using Tera Blast as a luring tool, so Terastallization should be a top priority for Dragonite.

Items

  • Sharp Beak: Sharp Beak gives Dragonite the most offensive presence with the fewest drawbacks, giving Flying-type Tera Blast just enough of a boost to usually 2HKO Ursaluna-B, or 3HKO defensive variants.

  • Assault Vest: Assault Vest vastly improves Dragonite's matchup against Iron Bundle and Flutter Mane, especially if Multiscale's protection has been lost.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots means Stealth Rock will no longer remove this set's ability to trade blows with powerful threats.

Bulky Offensive Dragon Dance.description:
• While giving up Extreme Speed and Scale Shot may seem unusual, it allows Dragonite to use both Multiscale and the unpredictability of Terastallization to become an extremely dangerous bulky sweeper that teams often have the wrong response to!

  • Roost: Despite this set's more offensive approach, Roost is still highly recommended for taking full advantage of Multiscale.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head is a good choice if using Tera Steel, but even outside of that, it offers much more damage against Flutter Mane and common Tera Fairy foes like Raging Bolt and Toxapex than Earthquake.

  • Outrage: Outrage has tremendous power compared to any other attack from Dragonite, but Flutter Mane flipping it into a chance to revenge kill means it's best to lock-in late-game when the sweeping shot is clear.

  • Ice Spinner: Ice Spinner works best with Clear Amulet, making sure Landorus-T and Dragonite are easy to break through before they Terastallize.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is usually preferred for the extra damage output, and the given EV spread still outspeeds Adamant Chien-Pao after a Dragon Dance. Jolly is required for outspeeding Timid Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle though.

Other Options

  • Fire Punch: Fire Punch is handy for roasting Scizor and dealing good damage to Corviknight, but it can't replace Earthquake, since hitting Archaludon hard is extremely important.

  • Thunder Punch: If using Tera Electric, Thunder Punch is a less risky alternative to Tera Blast in exchange for getting hit by Rocky Helmet. It's best used with Ice Spinner over Earthquake.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick is an easy way to OHKO Chien-Pao compared to Earthquake, but Flutter Mane laughing at it means Iron Head becomes required coverage, and it does less damage to Archaludon than Earthquake.

Items

  • Clear Amulet: Clear Amulet protects Dragonite from Pokemon that can ruin its sweep with Attack debuffs, such as Landorus-T and Charm Flutter Mane, as well as Breaking Swipe users like Gouging Fire and opposing Dragonite.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry is an effective way around common status spreaders like Flutter Mane, Archaludon, and Dragapult.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Heavy-Duty Boots ensures that Stealth Rock won't break Multiscale.

  • Rocky Helmet: If using Roost, Rocky Helmet is a good way of punishing Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes if it lacks Punching Glove or if switching into Aqua Jet.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High / Medium: If making use of Tera Blast for Tera types like Flying, Dragonite will usually want to Terastallize as much as possible. Without Tera Blast, it becomes less necessary, but it's still often worth doing due to it making Dragonite a nightmare to OHKO!

  • Flying: Tera Blast Flying offers incredible power with no drawbacks outside of Terastallizing, making it a great choice for sweeping!

  • Steel: Tera Steel is a more defensive approach to this set, covering Dragonite's common weaknesses to Fairy, Dragon, and Rock.

  • Ground: When combined with Clear Amulet, Tera Ground gives Dragonite the tools to defeat common support Flutter Mane moves like Thunder Wave and Charm in addition to a powerful Earthquake.

  • Electric: Tera Electric works great with Ice Spinner covering Landorus-T, giving Dragonite another way to soak up Thunder Wave and even Serperior's Glare!

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy isn't as great defensively for Dragonite as Tera Steel, but the Dragon immunity is great for keeping Multiscale intact, and it makes Dragonite a good check against Urshifu-S.

Defensive.description:
Dragonite is an incredible defensive utility Pokemon thanks to its good stats and useful typing that let it check foes such as Landorus, Ogerpon-W, and Ogerpon-H. It also has a good movepool, with Haze and Dragon Tail making for great anti-setup moves and Roost providing recovery for its team; Multiscale also helps to improve the team's defensive capabilities. Dragon Tail and Haze are good against setup sweepers like Iron Hands, Gholdengo, and Swords Dance Ogerpon formes. Dragon Tail is good for accumulating chip damage, especially on entry hazard-stacking teams, while Haze can clear both foes' stat boosts and teammates' Intimidate drops, and it also works against Fairy-types like Primarina and Diancie as well as Tera Fairy users like Archaludon. Iron Head is good against the aforementioned Fairy-types and Alolan Ninetales as well as Chien-Pao. Ice Spinner hits both Landorus formes, as well as clearing Psychic Terrain. Roost helps provide the team with longevity, helping Dragonite fulfill its role as a defensive wall better. The given EV spread allows Dragonite to survive an Adamant Chien Pao's Icicle Crash and a Life Orb Kyurem's Blizzard with Multiscale. Dragonite struggles against foes that can hit it super effectively like Porygon2, Chien-Pao, Primarina, and Raging Bolt. Dragonite also does not like Incineroar, as it can weaken Dragonite's damage output with Intimidate, prevent it from moving with Fake Out, and remove its Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off to prevent it from switching in as often if Stealth Rock is up. Tera Steel grants Dragonite a boost to its Iron Head's damage and allows it to flip the matchup on the aforementioned checks, gaining a resistance to the Ice-, Fairy-, and Dragon-type moves that would otherwise threaten it. However, Tera Steel does worsen the matchup against Incineroar and prevents Dragonite from checking foes that it normally checks, like Landorus and Ogerpon-H.

Notable Partners

Entry Hazard Setters: Teammates like Landorus-T and Ting-Lu make for good partners, as Dragonite can take advantage of their entry hazards and its ability to phaze foes to rack up extra hazard chip damage. In return, Dragonite helps them with the longevity issues they struggle with. Be wary of stacking up Ice-weak teammates when using these partners, as foes like Chien-Pao and Kyurem may become problematic to deal with.

Fire- and Steel-types: Pokemon like Incineroar, Volcanion, and Gholdengo appreciate Dragonite's ability to switch in on the Ground-type moves that threaten them. Dragonite can also provide recovery to the former two, helping them stay on the field for longer. In return, these partners are good against the Ice- and Fairy-types that Dragonite struggles with, and Incineroar can help Dragonite tank physical attacks better thanks to Intimidate, while Gholdengo gives Dragonite a Spore immunity with Good as Gold.

Altarianite.description: Dragonite is one of the most formidable setup sweepers in the metagame, capable of unleashing incredibly powerful Pixilate-boosted Extreme Speed, further amplified by Dragon Dance. Additionally, it boasts exceptional coverage options to deal with foes that can safely switch into its Extreme Speed. Fire Punch handles Magearna and Corviknight. Alternatively, Earthquake deals more damage to Magearna, Pecharunt, and Garganacl, but is completely walled by Latiasite variants of the former two, as well as setup Corviknight. Waterfall, on the other hand, hits all the aforementioned foes reliably, albeit weakly, along with dealing super effective damage to Ho-Oh and Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk; it can also be used to fish for flinches in dicey situations. Dragonite may also utilize Facade to severely punish attempts to burn it by foes like Milotic, Ho-Oh, and Arceus formes, as well as turn the tables against Gyaradosite Pecharunt when Pecharunt poisons it. Roost is nearly essential to provide Dragonite with reliable recovery. The Speed EVs allow it to outspeed uninvested Manectite Magearna. Dragonite can fit seamlessly into various offense and balance teams, where it can serve as a potent revenge killer and sweeper. Pairing it with entry hazard setters such as Magearna, Great Tusk, and Swampert applies immense offensive pressure on the opposing team as Dragonite spams Extreme Speed. Similarly, hazard removers like Great Tusk and Corviknight are amazing allies, allowing it to avoid getting easily chipped and preventing Multiscale from breaking pre-Mega Evolution. Dragonite is vulnerable to other Altarianite Extreme Speed users, such as Entei, Hisuian Arcanine, and Regieleki, making checks to these like defensive Eternatus and Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk excellent pairing options. Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk also applies pressure on Magearna and Pecharunt, two of Dragonite's most troublesome walls.

Aerilate.description: Aerilate Dragonite sacrifices its defensive utility to become a more offensively potent setup sweeper; it uses its already good Attack stat boosted by Pinsirite as well as Multiscale pre-Mega Evolution to maul defensive staples like Pecharunt, Hippowdon, and Ho-Oh that Altarianite variants struggle with while still keeping its revenge killing prowess for Urshifu-R and Spectrier. Salamencite is also a usable option if a teammate is already using Pinsirite, as it still gives Aerilate as well as boosting Dragonite's Defense, which can come in handy with setting up. Earthquake lets Dragonite deal with Pokemon like Raging Bolt and non-Latiasite Magearna and Garganacl that would otherwise give Dragonite major trouble. Fire Punch prevents Dragonite from being completely countered by Corviknight and Latiasite Magearna, while Facade allows Dragonite to take advantage of burns from Arceus-Water, Milotic, and Ho-Oh, as well as poison from Pecharunt and Eternatus. If more longevity is required, Roost can be used in order to keep Dragonite healthy in the span of longer games. The Speed EVs allow Dragonite to outspeed Pinsirite Magearna unboosted. Aerilate Dragonite has an amazing offensive presence, but due to its Stealth Rock weakness and overall limited longevity, it is only usable on more offensive teams. Dragonite appreciates entry hazard control from removers like Great Tusk and Regieleki or Sablenite users like Swampert and Magearna, so it doesn't take huge damage from Stealth Rock and can keep Multiscale active before Mega Evolving. Hazard setters like Swampert, Great Tusk, and Magearna help wear down Dragonite's checks like defensive Arceus formes, Great Tusk, and Raging Bolt. They also help in checking Altarianite Extreme Speed users like Hisuian Arcanine, Regieleki, and opposing Dragonite, preventing them from revenge killing it. Pokemon like Entei, Lunala, and Great Tusk can also help in wearing down Dragonite’s checks, as they can break down walls Dragonite heavily struggles with like Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Ho-Oh for it to sweep, and vice versa. Other Pokemon that can deal with the aforementioned walls, like Raging Bolt and Iron Crown, are also greatly appreciated.

Priority Attacker.description:
• Dragonite is one of the best physical attackers in the tier, due to its excellent Attack and access to Inner Focus, which ignores Intimidate and grants immunity to the effects of Fake Out. It's especially threatening as a lead in combination with Chien-Pao or late-game when picking off weakened Pokemon.

  • With Choice Band, Extreme Speed applies immense pressure, especially in combination with Terastallization or Chien-Pao's Sword of Ruin. This combination can OHKO Pokemon lacking defensive investment, such as Tornadus, Landorus, and Ogerpon, before they can move. However, being locked into Extreme Speed can be risky due to Pokemon such as Diancie and Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Sinistcha taking little or no damage from it. Tera Ghost or Tera Steel Landorus and Tera Ghost Chien-Pao can also minimize the damage dealt by Extreme Speed, so it is often better to wait for the opponent to Terastallize.

  • Dragon Claw is the most reliable option for damage and does the same amount of damage as Extreme Speed without having to Terastallize; it also allows Dragonite to deal a lot of damage to Dragon-types like Raging Bolt and Kyurem. Outrage, while less consistent due to its random targeting, deals incredible damage even against bulky Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Iron Hands and is devastating on a field without Dragon-resistant or Fairy-type Pokemon.

  • Iron Head is crucial for OHKOing unboosted Diancie and Alolan Ninetales, as well as hitting common Tera Fairy Pokemon like Raging Bolt and Gholdengo.

  • Stomping Tantrum, while not being the main gameplan, allows Dragonite to hit Gholdengo, which can't be hit by Extreme Speed, to OHKO Glimmora, and to almost OHKO Pokemon like Incineroar and Iron Hands. Alternatively, Fire Punch also allows Dragonite to hit Gholdengo as well as other Pokemon that don't take a lot of damage from Extreme Speed or Stomping Tantrum, like Sinistcha and Bronzong.

  • Tera Normal, while being part of Dragonite's core sweeping gameplan, is also a great defensive typing, leaving it weak only Fighting-type moves, which are commonly used by Okidogi, Iron Hands, and Diancie, while also allowing it to dodge OHKOs from Raging Bolt's Dragon-type moves, Chien-Pao's Ice Spinner, and Kyurem.

  • As mentioned previously, Dragonite's best partner is Chien-Pao, as it can boost Extreme Speed with Sword of Ruin, remove Psychic Terrain with Ice Spinner, and threaten Pokemon like Farigiraf and Indeedee-F with Throat Chop, both of which would block Extreme Speed. Both Throat Chop and Sucker Punch allow Chien-Pao to deal with Ghost-types that are immune to Extreme Speed.

  • Other valuable partners include Landorus, which can eliminate Steel-types and bulky Pokemon like Iron Hands, Diancie, and Incineroar. Follow Me users like Ogerpon-W and Ogerpon-H can redirect attacks to let Dragonite safely use Extreme Speed, and they also appreciate the damage boost from Chien-Pao. Gouging Fire is another great teammate, as it can further boost Dragonite's Attack with Howl.

  • Dragonite also appreciates entry hazard support from Glimmora and Ting-Lu, as they can chip opposing Pokemon into Extreme Speed's KO range and break Focus Sashes on threats such as Tornadus and Chien-Pao.

Dragon Dance Sweeper (Dragon).description: With its useful typing, wide offensive movepool, and strong boosting capabilities bolstered by Multiscale, Dragonite can become a frightening setup threat on Dragon teams. After a Dragon Dance boost, Dragonite can outrun and defeat numerous threats to Dragon teams such as Iron Valiant, Mega Gallade, Tapu Koko, Keldeo, and Volcarona depending on the coverage moves given. At +1, Dragon Claw eliminates Kyurem and, after chip damage, Garchomp, Latios, and Latias. Dual Wingbeat smashes the aforementioned Fighting-types that cause issues for Dragon teams. Earthquake is a solid coverage option that allows Dragonite to blow up Steel- and Poison-types like Gholdengo, Toxapex, and Alolan Muk for its teammates that may struggle to break through them. Thunder Punch enables Dragonite to hit common switch-ins like Corviknight and Celesteela, along with bulky Water-types like Tapu Fini and Slowbro. Fire Punch is another option for coverage, as it can deal with Corviknight, Celesteela, Mega Scizor, and Ferrothorn. Extreme Speed prevents Dragonite from being easily revenge killed by Choice Scarf threats that outspeed it after a boost, such as Meowscarada and Greninja. Alternatively, Roost grants Dragonite the ability to heal itself, potentially letting it regain Multiscale for further setup opportunities. Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra are essential teammates for Dragonite, as both cover its crippling Ice weakness on both sides of the defensive spectrum. Additionally, Archaludon can answer Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Iron Boulder with its ability to resist the common moves they use against Dragonite such as Mighty Cleave, Play Rough, and Triple Axel, while Hisuian Goodra can switch into threats like Tapu Lele and Kyurem alongside providing an extra way to stop Volcarona’s setup via Dragon Tail if Dragonite chooses to forgo Dual Wingbeat. Kommo-o is a strong partner for Dragonite, using its own boosting capabilities to crush Steel-types like Air Balloon Heatran and Ferrothorn, as well as picking off Ice-types that threaten Dragonite like Weavile and Mamoswine with Vacuum Wave. Roaring Moon appreciates Dragonite dealing with the Fighting-types that threaten it, and in return, Roaring Moon can allow entry for Dragonite via U-turn and pick off threats like Mega Diancie with Iron Head. Choice Scarf Latias enjoys Dragonite removing Steel-types with Earthquake and can provide a second chance for Dragonite to sweep with Healing Wish. Additionally, Latias can revenge kill threats like Kommo-o and Iron Valiant for Dragonite. Kyurem provides an Ice-type neutrality and destroys potential walls to Dragonite such as Skarmory, while also removing Gliscor, which can prevent Dragonite from sweeping with Toxic or Taunt.

Choice Band (Flying).description: Choice Band Dragonite is a fearsome wallbreaker that also has access to strong priority in Extreme Speed, allowing it to both break through defensive cores and revenge kill major offensive threats to Flying teams like Greninja and Volcarona. The immediate boost in power that Choice Band gives it means that common defensive staples like Toxapex and Archaludon struggle to switch in. Fire Punch and Thunder Punch both give Dragonite the ability to hit Ground-immune Steel-types like Corviknight and Celesteela, which otherwise completely wall it. The former is generally better against Steel-types and threatens an OHKO on Ferrothorn, while the latter can also hit Water / Fairy type Pokemon like Tapu Fini and Azumarill. Earthquake rounds out Dragonite's offensive profile, hitting Steel-types like Archaludon and Rock-types like Mega Diancie. While it makes Dragonite a bit worse against the Pokemon that most threaten Flying team structures, Superpower poses an even greater threat to Dark and Normal team staples like Ting-Lu and Porygon2. It also allows Dragonite to easily remove common Air Balloon users like Iron Treads and Heatran. For teammates, Spikes Gliscor is a great partner that can chip opposing Pokemon into Extreme Speed range with entry hazards and pivot Dragonite into wallbreaking opportunities with U-turn. Corviknight is able to remove Stealth Rock for Dragonite while checking revenge killers like Weavile and Meowscarada. Tornadus-T can use Knock Off against shared checks to Dragonite like Corviknight and Porygon2 while helping create openings with Nasty Plot or bring it in with U-turn. Choice Scarf users like Enamorus and Landorus-T are able to revenge kill faster threats like Greninja and Zeraora while offering support in the form of Healing Wish and U-turn, respectively. Mega Charizard Y is a powerful wallbreaker that can help Dragonite break through defensive cores. It also acts as an important stopgap to certain Pokemon that can use take advantage of a Choice-locked Dragonite to set up, like Swords Dance Gliscor and Calm Mind Tapu Fini.

Dragon Dance (Flying).description: Dragonite makes for a great wallbreaker and late-game cleaner on Flying teams, outspeeding threats such as Zeraora and Mega Diancie after a Dragon Dance boost. Earthquake threatens Steel-, Poison-, and Rock-types like Gholdengo, Alolan Muk, and non-Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine. Roost grants Dragonite longevity as well as potentially reactivating Multiscale if its HP is restored to full. Substitute allows it to take advantage of passive Pokemon such as Toxapex, Will-O-Wisp Rotom-W, and Clodsire to set up Dragon Dance, but Roost is preferred since it grants Dragonite more opportunities to sweep. Heavy-Duty Boots is preferred so that Dragonite doesn't need to rely on entry hazard removal to switch in, while Leftovers grants it a form of longevity when it chooses to forego Roost. Mega Charizard Y is Dragonite's most important teammate, forming a great offensive pairing, with it threatening Ice-, Steel-, and Water-types such as Articuno, Alolan Ninetales, Corviknight, and Swampert, while Dragonite handles Galarian Slowking and Mega Charizard X. Corviknight and Celesteela deal with Fairy-, Ice-, and Rock-types such as Tapu Lele, Weavile, and Ogerpon-C; Corviknight also acts as a slow pivot to bring Dragonite in on Gholdengo. Choice Scarf Enamorus provides great speed control, outspeeding and threatening the likes of Mega Altaria and Iron Valiant while also dealing with Dark-types such as Mandibuzz and Mega Sableye. Additionally, Dragonite appreciates Healing Wish from Enamorus, as it can give Dragonite another opportunity to sweep. Thanks to Dragonite acting as a wallbreaker, it can enable fellow sweepers such as Mega Aerodactyl and Galarian Moltres.
