  • Fire: Tera Fire blocks Will-O-Wisp, and the Tera Blast coverage can hit Steel-types like Scizor and Corviknight hard even without Belly Drum.

  • Grass: Tera Grass turns both Grass- and Electric-type weaknesses into resistances, and when combined with Tera Blast, it makes dealing with Unaware Dondozo and Rotom-W much easier. It can also be used to block Spore and set up Belly Drum for free, but this must be done with discretion, as Spore users like Loaded Dice Breloom may just attack and leave Azumarill heavily wounded after Belly Drum.

  • Electric: Tera Electric with Tera Blast is Azumarill's best option to beat Toxapex, and it still deals big damage to Unaware Dondozo and Corviknight.

Substitute + Encore.description: • This set does not have a full write-up yet. If you'd like to finish this, feel free to reserve it here!

Z-Belly Drum (Fairy).description: Azumarill's presence is greatly appreciated on Fairy teams, where it tends to be the Z-Crystal user of choice and a good answer to the Fire, Ground, Rock, Poison and Steel matchups. Z-Belly Drum guarantees a +6 boost to Azumarill's already impressive Attack, turning it into a redoubtable setup sweeper with access to priority, and it can even offer a second setup opportunity if Azumarill gets forced out with its Z-Move unused. Aqua Jet is Azumarill's answer to threats that outspeed it, such as Volcarona, Tapu Koko, and Nidoking. Aside from dealing with Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Slowbro, and Sinistcha, Knock Off is Azumarill's best coverage option against walls that resist its other attacks, such as Ferrothorn, Toxapex and Water Absorb Clodsire. Breakneck Blitz coming off Return beats Mega Venusaur as well as Icium Z Toxapex, which doesn't fear Knock Off. Alternatively, Liquidation could be used as a stronger STAB option for slower foes like Iron Hands, Ting-Lu, and Celesteela, which is important if a Jolly nature is used. Ice Spinner is an alternative that can be used to defeat both Ting-Lu and Mega Venusaur after some chip, along with getting rid of Psychic Terrain to allow for Aqua Jet to be used without being blocked. Klefki is an amazing partner for Azumarill, offering a Poison immunity and dual screens support to ease setup and spreading Spikes to chip the opposing team. Mega Diancie helps in the Fire and Flying matchups and provides entry hazard control, contributing to keeping Azumarill healthy as well as providing Stealth Rock to help its wallbreaking. Tapu Koko deals with Water-types such as Pelipper and Toxapex, making Azumarill's sweep easier down the line, and it also handles Steel- and Flying-types like Celesteela and Corviknight should Azumarill opt for Return. Tapu Bulu also aids in the Water and Electric matchup, handling foes like Quagsire and Rotom-W that Azumarill can struggle to bring down. Iron Valiant deals with most Fighting-types and, when paired with Tapu Koko, outspeeds and defeats faster foes such as Mega Lopunny and Mega Swampert under rain, but it competes with Azumarill for a Z-Crystal. Tapu Lele handles Poison-types like Mega Venusaur and Clodsire, but be cautious of Psychic Terrain preventing Azumarill from using Aqua Jet. Babiri Berry Clefable can be used as an alternative to Tapu Lele for checking Scizor, and it also handles Mega Venusaur well, as it can use it as setup fodder.

ru.overview: Politoed is an excellent wielder of the Drizzle ability, with good natural bulk to go with its offensive coverage options and utility that serve it well. Drizzle enables the plethora of strong Swift Swim users, such as Barraskewda, Basculegion-F, and Overqwil, while also giving Hurricane users like Kilowattrel and Noivern perfect accuracy. Perish Trapper Politoed is a valuable asset for rain teams, as it can trap and eliminate walls like Blissey and Umbreon. Politoed can use its own rain to throw off powerful STAB attacks like Surf and Weather Ball, which can be powerful when used in conjunction with Choice Specs. The main limiting factor of Politoed, however, is its inability to pivot, which means it has to rely on defensive pivots like Eject Button Amoonguss, Forretress, and Jirachi to give safe entry points to the powerful wallbreakers on rain teams. Similarly, Politoed lacks reliable recovery outside of Rest and can struggle to establish rain multiple times a game against the other weather setters in the tier like Ninetales and Alolan Ninetales.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs Politoed can use its rain to dish out powerful STAB attacks like Surf and Weather Ball. Rest can give Politoed a bit more longevity, allowing it to establish rain more often for its teammates. Hydro Pump and Weather Ball are powerful but less consistent STAB attacks for Politoed, offering more immediate power at the cost of accuracy and reliance on rain, respectively.

Checks and Counters

Assault Vest Cyclizar: Assault Vest Cyclizar does not take much damage from uninvested Ice Beam and can remove Politoed's Damp Rock, shortening rain turns for its teammates.

Disruption: Encore Jirachi and Gengar can disrupt Politoed significantly, locking it into unfavorable positions and giving them momentum to set up or pivot into teammates.

Pivots: Perish trapper Politoed struggles with the tier's pivots, such as Flamigo and Kilowattrel, and can find it difficult to trap the Pokemon it seeks to remove.

Water-immune Pokemon: Water-immune Pokemon, like Gastrodon and Vaporeon, can stop Whirlpool from trapping them.

Wallbreakers: Wallbreakers like Basculegion-F and Gardevoir can break through Politoed before it can effectively Perish trap them.

Opposing Weather: Politoed lacks recovery outside of Rest, meaning it gets worn down easily and can struggle to establish rain against opposing weather setters like Ninetales and Torkoal despite its type advantage against them. Alolan Ninetales is another weather setter that can use its faster Encore to prevent Politoed from effectively trapping it.

Perish Trapper.description:
Set Details

Whirlpool is an effective means to trap unsuspecting checks like Blissey, Suicune, and Umbreon, enabling Perish Song to break through these defensive pieces. Ice Beam nails Grass- and Dragon-types like Amoonguss, Chesnaught, and Cyclizar. Encore can disrupt slower Pokemon like Reuniclus and Slowbro and put a stop to offensive setup attempts from threats like Bisharp, Suicune, and Mimikyu as well, though this is prediction-reliant, as they're faster than Politoed. Earth Power can be used to hit Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra, Jirachi, and Magnezone. The provided EV spread allows Politoed to outpace neutral-natured threats like the aforementioned Hisuian Goodra and Magnezone. Tera Ghost allows Politoed to function as a spinblocker against Cyclizar as well as providing a Fighting immunity to help in the matchup against faster wallbreakers like Terrakion and choiced Gallade.

Politoed is essentially mandatory for dedicated rain teams because of its access to Drizzle, though it can also be seen on bulky offense teams as well. Perish trapper Politoed can be quite effective in removing special walls like Blissey and Umbreon, which can enable special attacking teammates like Basculegion-F to use the rain to the fullest. Teammates that can help these rain users, as well as Barraskewda and Overqwil, include Eject Button Amoonguss and Volt Switch Forretress, both of which can provide safe entry points for the frailer offensive options while effectively utilizing rain turns. Similarly, Kilowattrel is a fine Pokemon on rain structures, using perfectly accurate STAB Hurricane and Thunder to great effect and functioning as a Volt Switch user and Electric-immune Pokemon in one slot. Balance teams can also appreciate Perish trapper Politoed for its ability to remove difficult foes like Blissey and Umbreon, allowing teammates like Gengar and Basculegion-F to wallbreak more effectively. Steel-type teammates like Jirachi can benefit from rain support as well, more effectively checking powerful Fire-types like Entei. Rain is effective in minimizing the healing from foes that use weather-dependent recovery moves, like Synthesis Chesnaught and Moonlight Cresselia, making them more susceptible to being worn down.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Because of its passivity, Jumpluff requires partners that deal meaningful damage on their own to foes; this means that they will likely need to have spread moves such as Heat Wave to damage both foes at once.
  • Pokemon that set up with either boosting moves or other options like Trick Room appreciate Jumpluff's ability to redirect attacks or shut down foes altogether with Sleep Powder.
  • Jumpluff heavily appreciates allies with Drought, as it makes it so that Jumpluff isn't forced to waste a turn setting up the sun for itself with Sunny Day.
  • Charizard is a great offensive ally for Jumpluff, using Heat Wave to damage foes and appreciating Jumpluff's access to Sunny Day and Rage Powder, activating Charizard's Solar Power and protecting the frail threat from powerful attacks, respectively.
  • Torkoal can damage both foes with Eruption and sets up the sun for Jumpluff. Jumpluff can additionally use Pollen Puff to heal Torkoal to fire off a more powerful Eruption.
  • Ursaluna is another ally that can consistently damage foes with spread moves, this time with Earthquake, which is able to be used freely next to Jumpluff thanks to its Ground immunity. In return, Jumpluff can put foes to sleep, namely Sneasler, before they can move so Ursaluna is free to attack. Jumpluff can also redirect attacks or disrupt foes with Encore to ensure that Ursaluna's Flame Orb activates safely. Jumpluff, when used with faster Ursaluna sets, can use Tailwind to allow Ursaluna to outspeed a significant portion of the unboosted metagame.
  • Jumpluff is very supportive and cannot do any meaningful damage on its own. It is particularly useless in front of Gholdengo or Pokemon with Safety Goggles such as Incineroar, as they can ignore Jumpluff entirely or KO it with Make It Rain and Flare Blitz, respectively. Allies such as Charizard and Hisuian Typhlosion are able to break through many of these Pokemon with their devastating attacks. Jumpluff also has a pretty poor defensive typing, being weak to top Pokemon such as Alolan Ninetales and Sneasler. Allies such as Incineroar can help out by threatening them with Flare Blitz or mitigating their damage with Intimidate, respectively. Jumpluff can also outspeed them with Drought support from Torkoal, putting them to sleep with Sleep Powder before they can threaten Jumpluff.

Strategy Comments

  • Jumpluff's main objective is to be a nuisance under then sun, putting foes to sleep, changing the Speed order with Tailwind, and resetting sun if necessary. Jumpluff loves to be in scenarios where it can spam Sleep Powder easily without worry. To help it achieve this, roadblocks such as powder-immune Pokemon like Safety Goggles Clefable and Rillaboom and sleep-immune Pokemon like Magmar and Electabuzz should be removed early on.
  • Jumpluff tends to prefer being brought in the front, getting off early Sleep Powders that could easily sway the battle in Jumpluff's favor. Jumpluff can be brought in many matchups, but certainly not Trick Room; because of its relatively poor bulk and lack of Protect, it won't be able to survive.
  • Jumpluff accentuates its potential in matchups against opposing weather teams, namely rain teams, as it can shut down their weather with Sunny Day before they can move. Additionally, Jumpluff can lock common rain Pokemon like Pelipper and Ursaluna into Protect with Encore, or it can redirect powerful Water-type attacks like Wave Crash from Basculegion away, protecting allies like Incineroar and Charizard.
  • Shutting down the sun with Pokemon such as Pelipper and Alolan Ninetales will sever Jumpluff's Speed boost, leaving it vulnerable to Pokemon such as Sneasler. Removing weather setters early-game and preserving Jumpluff's allies such as Torkoal will ensure that Jumpluff's preferred weather will be up. Jumpluff is also susceptible to Taunt from the likes of Whimsicott and Annihilape, considering most of its options are status moves. To counter this, removing the Taunt users early with explosive damage in the form of Charizard or Ursaluna will be helpful.

Sun Support.description:
• Jumpluff is a sun staple, providing fast and invaluable support in the form of speed control and sleep, among others.
  • Sunny Day is a good option because of Jumpluff's high Speed, letting it reliably override opposing weather before anything moves while boosting the power of allies such as Charizard. Rage Powder is the preferred last option, keeping frail allies like the aforementioned Charizard safe by redirecting away opposing attacks such as Wave Crash from Basculegion. Encore, on the other hand, punishes passive play like Fake Out and Protect. Pollen Puff can heal up allies like Ursaluna while also giving it an attacking move, making sure that Jumpluff isn't entirely useless when Taunted. Leaf Storm is a more offensive option, allowing Jumpluff to hit foes such as Ursaluna-B, Tera Water Gholdengo, and Basculegion in a pinch.
  • Covert Cloak blocks Fake Out from the likes of Rillaboom, letting Jumpluff continue to support its team without disturbance.
  • Tera Water flips Jumpluff's weaknesses to Fire- and Ice-type attacks such as Flare Blitz from Incineroar and Blizzard from Alolan Ninetales into resistances while granting a resistance to Make It Rain from Gholdengo, boosting its longevity.
  • The bulk lets Jumpluff survive Draco Meteor from Life Orb Hydreigon, Overheat from Magmar when not in the sun, 4 hits of Scale Shot from Dragonite, and almost always avoids a 2HKO from Iron Head from +1 Kingambit. The Speed investment lets Jumpluff always outspeed Adamant Sneasler.
  • Especially when the sun is active, Jumpluff is able to very easily outspeed a lot of threats such as Sneasler and put them to sleep. After that, however, Jumpluff relies entirely on its partners to deal damage, leaving it very easy to ignore and its partner vulnerable to being double targetted. This can be taken further with moves like Taunt, which removes Jumpluff's ability to attempt to save its partner with moves such as Rage Powder and Sleep Powder.

Unaware Wall.description:
Quagsire is a notable physical wall thanks to its ability Unaware, which allows it to ignore boosts from setup sweepers like Salamence and Scizor. Toxic puts many notable Pokemon in the tier on a timer such as Hippowdon and Gastrodon. Quagsire ideally wants Spikes over Stealth Rock to force more chip damage on potential switch-ins; however, Stealth Rock is fine as an alternative if none of its other teammates can afford to fit it into their moveset. Alternatively, Ice Beam with a Relaxed nature allows Quagsire to 2HKO Hawlucha after Stealth Rock and lets it beat Substitute + Dragon Dance Tera Flying Tyranitars. The passive recovery of Leftovers allows Quagsire to check Choice Band Tyranitar and Mimikyu more easily; however, if the team can not fit entry hazard removal, Heavy-Duty Boots is much more appealing. Quagsire only uses Terastallization defensively to check certain dangerous offensive threats. Tera Poison grants Quagsire a perfectly accurate Toxic and a poison immunity while also allowing it to handle Grass-types and offensive threats that use Grass-type moves such as Tsareena, Trailblaze Scizor, and Seed Bomb Pawmot. Tera Ghost allows Quagsire to beat Maushold by becoming immune to Population Bomb as well as check Slither Wing and Lucario more easily. Tera Ghost also has the added benefit of letting Quagsire serve as a spinblocker against spinners such as Tsareena.

Quagsire primarily fits on balance, stall, and bulky offense teams as a defensive glue that holds these teams together. Common teammates for Quagsire include Stealth Rock setters such as Tinkaton and Tyranitar, which can allow Quagsire to run Spikes. Both can check Gengar, special Salamence, and Iron Jugulis, which pose a threat to Quagsire. Tinkaton can also use Knock Off on Heavy-Duty Boots users such as Sticky Hold Gastrodon, Scream Tail, and Wo-Chien to rack up more damage from Quagsire's Spikes. Scream Tail is another Pokemon that complements Quagsire, as it is able to handle special Salamence as well as Gallade, while Quagsire is able to keep Bisharp and non-Trailblaze Scizor in check. Talonflame is another ideal partner for Quagsire as it can check Tsareena and Giga Drain variants of Wo-Chien. Blissey on stall teams is also a strong partner for Quagsire by virtue of walling almost every special attacker in the tier such as Iron Jugulis, Noivern, and Sandy Shocks.

Quagsire is an excellent wall and entry hazard setter in Ubers UU, as it has Unaware, a solid defensive typing, and a vast utility movepool, allowing it to check setup sweepers like Roaring Moon and Zacian. Spikes, Stealth Rock, and Toxic Spikes allow Quagsire to support its team with hazards, reducing the team's passivity and forcing chip damage on key threats like Palkia-O and Ogerpon-H. Toxic allows Quagsire to put opposing threats such as Zacian and Great Tusk on a timer. Unaware allows Quagsire to stifle setup sweepers like Swords Dance Zacian and Dragon Dance Arceus-Poison while also allowing it to handle Nasty Plot Mewtwo fairly well. Tera Poison allows Quagsire to handle Fairy- and Grass-type attacks from Pokemon like Zacian and Arceus-Grass, respectively, while also keeping it safe from Poison. Quagsire appreciates help from special walls like Blissey and specially defensive Magearna, as they can patch up its weaker Special Defense, and they fit well alongside it on stall and balance teams, handling threats like Arceus-Dark, Palkia-O, and Dialga. Dragon- and Steel-types like Arceus-Dragon and Skarmory also pair well with Quagsire, as they can relieve it of entry hazard setting duty while also switching in on Grass-types like Rillaboom and Ogerpon formes. Quagsire enables offensive threats like Zacian, Arceus-Poison, and Deoxys with its hazard setting, putting their checks, such as Arceus-Poison and Giratina, into KO range of their attacks.

ru.overview: Facing RU with a stalwart expression, Quagsire is a decent physical wall, utilizing its ability Unaware to stonewall very pertinent setup sweepers such as Bisharp and Mimikyu. Quagsire uses Pokemon such as Bisharp and Mimikyu as opportunities to heal off chip damage or establish Spikes, while Toxic allows Quagsire to help hinder pesky foes immune to Earthquake like Noivern and Yanmega. Quagsire's main issue is that it fears most special attackers, as due to its poor special bulk, it is obliterated by Pokemon such as Basculegion-F, Toxtricity, and Gardevoir. Quagsire also immensely struggles with Grass-types such as Breloom and Amoonguss, as they can not only take its Earthquake but also hit it for 4x super effective damage. Grass-type coverage such as Wood Hammer from Mimikyu or Grass Knot from Jirachi can also OHKO Quagsire unexpectedly. Quagsire is also unable to effectively take on Pokemon such as Suicune with Unaware sets.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Toxic Spikes can be used over Spikes in order to further spread poison by threatening Pokemon such as Suicune and Raikou that Quagsire does not want to directly switch into. Encore can be used to lock opposing Pokemon into status moves such as Roost and Recover, which can help Quagsire to spread Toxic, although it is prediction reliant because of Quagsire's low Speed. Whirlpool can be used to trap opposing Pokemon while dealing chip damage, allowing Quagsire to beat foes such as Tera Steel Flygon and Rotom-H it might otherwise not be able to touch. Stealth Rock can be used if there aren't any other Stealth Rock setters on the team. Body Press is an option on Quagsire to hit Bisharp a lot harder while also hitting Tera Steel Levitate Pokemon such as Flygon and Cresselia it would otherwise struggle with. Counter can be used to surprise foes such as Kleavor and Krookodile that think they can chip down Quagsire with their strong moves, dealing massive damage back to them. Rocky Helmet is an option on Quagsire in order to deal chip damage to Pokemon such as Flamigo and Maushold that it might otherwise be overwhelmed by. Water Absorb can be used over Unaware to help with matchups against Water-types such as Barraskewda and Suicune.

Checks and Counters

Special Wallbreakers: Due to Quagsire's low special bulk, wallbreakers like Gardevoir, Hisuian Goodra, and Toxtricity threaten it immensely. Unaware can also hurt it, as it can ignore the Special Attack drops from moves such as Draco Meteor, meaning it can't even stay in on stat-lowered foes like Noivern.

Grass-types: Grass-types such as Torterra and Breloom threaten Quagsire with 4x super effective moves. Pokemon with Grass-type coverage such as Wood Hammer from Mimikyu and Grass Knot Jirachi can also annihilate Quagsire unexpectedly.

Toxic- and Ground-immune Foes: Toxic- and Ground-immune foes such as Gligar, Tera Steel Rotom-H, and Tera Steel Flygon can easily switch into Quagsire, as it cannot touch them back. This means they can either make progress with entry hazards in the case of Gligar or constantly chip Quagsire in the case of Rotom-H and Flygon, forcing Quagsire to use more Recovers.

Disruption Moves: Quagsire is extremely restricted by moves such as Taunt and Psychic Noise, as they mean it can't use Recover and potentially cannot use Spikes or Toxic, forcing it to either switch out or immediately use Earthquake, which Pokemon it can usually beat such as Noivern and Terrakion can take advantage of. Quagsire is also vulnerable to Choice Scarf + Trick and Encore from Pokemon like Gardevoir and Maushold, which can lock it into a disadvantageous move.

Spikes.description:
Set Details

Toxic allows Quagsire to threaten Flying-types such as Noivern and Yanmega while also helping wear down Pokemon such as Gastrodon and Swampert. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Quagsire to ignore chip damage from entry hazards that might otherwise overwhelm it, while Leftovers accentuates Quagsire's longevity by giving it passive healing. Unaware allows Quagsire to ignore offensive stat boosts from Pokemon such as Terrakion, Bisharp, and Rhyperior while also ignoring defensive stat boosts from Pokemon such as Registeel and Chesnaught in order to hit them harder, though it has the downside of ignoring stat drops such as the ones Hisuian Goodra's and Noivern's Draco Meteors cause. Tera Poison allows Quagsire to resist the Grass-type moves aimed at it from Pokemon such as Breloom and Comfey, helps it check Fighting-types such as Flamigo and Terrakion, makes its own Toxic 100% accurate, and allows it to become immune to Toxic from Umbreon and Amoonguss. Tera Fairy gives Quagsire a Fighting resist whilst not leaving it weak to Ground letting it check Torterra, and not leaving it vulnerable to Ground-type attacks like from Choiced Krookodile after it Terastallizes.

Quagsire fits best on bulky offense and balance teams, where it can be paired with other defensive Pokemon like Chesnaught and Chansey to help wall large amounts of the metagame. Wo-Chien pairs really well with Quagsire, as it can use Knock Off in order to help Quagsire's Spikes stacking while also switching into Pokemon such as Basculegion-F and Hisuian Goodra that threaten out Quagsire. In return, Quagsire can switch into Pokemon such as Entei and Flamigo that can threaten out Wo-Chien. Poison-immune Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Alolan Muk pair well with Quagsire, as they can not only take on the Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Hisuian Liligant that threaten it immensely but also take Toxic from Pokemon such as Umbreon and opposing Amoonguss, which Quagsire would otherwise have to Terastallize for. Specially defensive Pokemon such as Cyclizar, Chansey, and Umbreon pair well with Quagsire, as they can take on the special wallbreakers such as Reuniclus and Gengar that threaten it, while in return, Quagsire can take on Pokemon such as Bisharp and Mimikyu that threaten them. Wallbreakers such as Mamoswine and Armarouge appreciate Quagsire's chip damage helping wear down their checks. Stealth Rock setters such as Registeel and Jirachi can form entry hazard-stacking cores with Quagsire, which can heavily chip down foes.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

(Ground)

Ice Beam threatens Gliscor, which does not fear Toxic, and Landorus-T utilizing Taunt or Substitute, which prevents Quagsire from inflicting it with Toxic poison; however, these matchups are specific and other teammates can handle them, letting Quagsire retain its useful utility moves. Body Press may be used to better check Roaring Moon, Hisuian Samurott, Cetitan, and Weavile, but the damage discrepancy with Earthquake is minimal, and Earthquake will do more damage in most other matchups.

Unaware Wall (Ground).description:
Quagsire is a great option for Ground teams due to its physical bulk and Unaware, checking a wide range of physical attackers like Hisuian Samurott, Cetitan, and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. Stealth Rock or Spikes wears down threats like Greninja, Iron Valiant, and Meowscarada. Toxic allows Quagsire to further wither down opponents alongside the entry hazards, notably putting Dragonite, Ting-Lu, and Great Tusk on a timer. Leftovers grants Quagsire passive recovery, improving its longevity and ability to repeatedly take hits more reliably. Meanwhile, Heavy-Duty Boots prevents detrimental entry hazards from wearing it down, allowing it to freely pivot. Rocky Helmet punishes multi-hit moves such as Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and Weavile's Triple Axel as well as Roaring Moon, Hisuian Samurott, and Cinderace attempting to pivot.

Quagsire's ability to wall setup sweepers like Dragonite and Ceruledge is heavily appreciated by its teammates. Water Absorb Clodsire switches into attacks from Greninja, Walking Wake, and Ogerpon-W while also contributing to entry hazard stacking via Toxic Spikes. Iron Treads removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin should Quagsire forgo Heavy-Duty Boots and checks Fairy-types like Hatterene and Flutter Mane. Great Tusk, Garchomp, and Landorus value Quagsire's entry hazards, which aid in their wallbreaking. Choice Scarf Great Tusk checks Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Greninja, and Hoopa-U while removing held items from Mandibuzz, Brambleghast, and Tornadus-T to make them more susceptible to Quagsire's entry hazards. Garchomp threatens Steel-types like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Air Balloon Gholdengo with its Fire-type coverage. Landorus checks the Ogerpon formes with Sludge Wave when using a Choice Scarf set and can utilize Rock Slide to catch Volcarona and Moltres off-guard. Ting-Lu and Quagsire make a great entry hazard-stacking core, as Ting-Lu is able to phaze opponents out with Whirlwind as well as check special attackers such as Latios, Gholdengo, and Raging Bolt. Mamoswine appreciates Quagsire's entry hazards; in return, it can fend off Ice-types such as Alolan Ninetales and Articuno while also threatening Meowscarada, Enamorus, Gliscor, and Landorus. Gliscor aids in setting up entry hazards and spreading Toxic poison while also being able to switch into opposing Toxic for Quagsire. Additionally, Gliscor provides Knock Off support to better accentuate the team's entry hazard setting while threatening opposing Gliscor and Gholdengo with its Swords Dance set.

Unaware Wall (Water).description:
Quagsire is a decent choice on Water teams thanks to its good bulk, access to Recover, useful typing, and ability to get Spikes up against threats that it walls, like Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta, Dragon Dance Roaring Moon, and Iron Hands. Toxic lets Quagsire force progress on defensive Pokemon and offensive switch-ins such as Meowscarada, Latios, and the Ogerpon formes, which in conjunction with Spikes racks up a significant amount of chip damage on opposing teams over time. Spikes can wear down threatening special attackers that force out Quagsire like Ursaluna-BM and Choice Specs Flutter Mane. Alternatively, Stealth Rock can be run if Quagsire has no teammates setting it up. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Quagsire ignore treacherous entry hazards such as Spikes and Toxic Spikes, which can easily wear it down over the course of a game. Leftovers let Quagsire passively regenerate HP, which can help it conserve Recover PP. Alternatively, Rocky Helmet lets Quagsire punish common physical attacks, such as IronPress Zamazenta's Body Press and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon's U-turn, and wear down said opponents over time in conjunction with Toxic and Spikes.

Toxapex is a good teammate for Quagsire, as it complements Quagsire's defensive typing well, being able to take on Grass-types like Meowscarada while Quagsire handles Electric-types like Iron Hands. Ogerpon-W and Greninja appreciate Quagsire giving them extra chip damage to force progress against answers like Archaludon and Iron Hands, respectively, with Spikes. Primarina and Keldeo appreciate Quagsire being able to scare off Poison-types like Alolan Muk, allowing them to set up, while Spikes forces very handy damage onto their answers. In return, Primarina can switch in on Dragon-types like special attacking Dragapult. Empoleon provides a nice Grass neutrality and Fairy resistance to the team, letting it take on threats like Hydrapple and Hatterene, alongside being a specially defensive tank that pairs nicely with Quagsire's Electric immunity and physical bulk. It also sets up Stealth Rock to form an entry hazard-stacking core alongside Quagsire.

nu.overview: Espeon is a Magic Bounce support Pokemon that compresses entry hazard denial, status spreading, and possibly momentum grabbing into one slot. It punishes common utility Pokemon such as Gligar, Swampert, Bronzong, Klefki, Bellibolt, Dudunsparce, and Vaporeon for setting hazards and using disruptive moves like Thunder Wave, Toxic, Glare, and Roar. Unlike more passive providers of hazard control, Espeon can also make offensive progress, whittling down walls with its Psychic Noise, and it can beat common hazard setters like Swampert and Rhyperior thanks to Grass Knot. Rocky Helmet lets Espeon function as a soft check to contact-reliant Pokemon such as Paldean Tauros-W, Flamigo, Tsareena, Cinccino, and Ambipom by punishing them for attacking or pivoting into it. Eject Button fits better on more offensive teams, especially weather builds, giving Espeon a way to deny entry hazards and immediately bring in a wallbreaker without wasting momentum or limited turns of weather. This allows Espeon to enable extremely powerful wallbreakers such as Choice Band Staraptor, Choice Specs Chandelure, and Tornadus. However, Espeon's frailty even with bulk investment allows strong attacker such as Flamigo, Scyther, and Incineroar to quickly overwhelm it with U-turn and Knock Off; meanwhile, bulkier hazard setters like Copperajah and Duraludon can force progress with their powerful attacks while it struggles to threaten them back. Dark-types are especially problematic, as Incineroar, Scrafty, Brute Bonnet, Wo-Chien, and Overqwil can exploit Espeon, especially if it lacks Alluring Voice. Espeon's reliance on Morning Sun and lack of Heavy-Duty Boots also leave it vulnerable to being worn down over longer games, so it often needs secondary hazard control such as Tidy Up Cinccino or a more offensive team structure that can either discourage hazards from going up or end games before repeated chip damage becomes too costly.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Weather Ball can be used on weather teams as a coverage option, with sun turning it into a Fire-type attack that lets Espeon hit Steel-types such as Copperajah and Bronzong, while rain turns it into a Water-type attack that can heavily pressure Incineroar and Chandelure. Choice Specs + Trick can be used to punish defensive Pokemon such as Chansey, Vaporeon, Bellibolt, and Dudunsparce, making them easier for Espeon's teammates to exploit. However, being locked into one attack can make it easier for Dark-types such as Incineroar, Scrafty, Brute Bonnet, and Wo-Chien to take advantage of Espeon. Calm Mind sets can attempt to turn Espeon into a setup sweeper, with Magic Bounce blocking status and phazing attempts, but they are difficult to justify over the support set because Espeon is very frail and can struggle to fit the coverage it needs in one moveslot.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Incineroar, Scrafty, Brute Bonnet, Wo-Chien, and Overqwil block Espeon's Psychic-type attacks and threaten it with Knock Off or other strong Dark-type STAB moves. Incineroar and Overqwil are especially troublesome because Espeon has no way to hit them hard. Scrafty and Brute Bonnet can use Espeon as setup fodder if it lacks Alluring Voice, though they must be careful when playing around Thunder Wave and Tera Fairy.

Ghost-types: Chandelure, Houndstone, and Brambleghast threaten Espeon with their Ghost-type attacks. Houndstone and Brambleghast are especially troublesome because their Shadow Sneak can pick off a weakened Espeon before it can use Morning Sun. However, all three must be careful against Shadow Ball sets, Chandelure hates being crippled by Thunder Wave, and Brambleghast dislikes taking Rocky Helmet chip damage when using Rapid Spin.

Knock Off and U-turn: Espeon relies heavily on Rocky Helmet or Eject Button to provide value, so Knock Off from Pokemon such as Incineroar, Tsareena, Swampert, and Tornadus can neuter its offensive potential, denying future chip damage or sinking momentum. U-turn users such as Scyther, Flygon, Incineroar, and Tsareena can also punish Espeon by forcing decent damage while keeping momentum, though Rocky Helmet can punish them for making contact.

Bulky Steel-types and Special Walls: Copperajah, Duraludon, Bronzong, Goodra, Bellibolt, and Vaporeon can stomach Espeon's attacks and limit its progress. Psychic Noise can stop recovery from Pokemon like Bellibolt, Chansey, and Vaporeon, but Espeon often needs teammates to break through these bulkier foes rather than trying to do so itself.

Magic Bounce Support.description:
Set Details

Psychic Noise makes it harder for Pokemon such as Vaporeon, Bellibolt, and Chansey to sit in front of Espeon after Magic Bounce denies their utility moves. Thunder Wave provides speed control, letting Espeon punish faster threats like Munkidori, Flamigo, and Scyther as well as setup sweepers such as Meloetta and Cinccino that try to take advantage of it. Grass Knot heavily damages Ground- and Rock-types like Swampert and Rhyperior, preventing them from freely setting entry hazards against Espeon, while Alluring Voice hits Dark-types such as Scrafty, Wo-Chien, and Brute Bonnet. Shadow Ball is another option for hitting Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Bronzong, Galarian Slowbro, and Chandelure. Rocky Helmet punishes contact moves from Pokemon such as Tsareena, Scyther, and Cinccino while letting Espeon beat Chansey one-on-one. Eject Button is useful on faster teams, especially weather teams, to immediately bring in a teammate after Espeon denies a utility move. Espeon can also switch in on a weak pivoting move such as Gligar's U-turn, Swampert's Flip Turn, and or Bellibolt's Volt Switch to activate Eject Button and bring in a teammate. The Speed investment lets it outspeed Jolly Flygon and Flamigo, while the Defense investment lets it survive Rhyperior's Earthquake and Scyther's U-turn from full HP. Tera Fairy improves Espeon's matchup against Dark- and Fighting-types; Tera Steel gives it a stronger defensive profile against Pokemon like Sylveon, Cinccino, and Goodra; and Tera Ghost lets it block Rapid Spin while gaining a useful Boomburst immunity, letting it slow down Dudunsparce. However, Tera Fairy makes Espeon weak to Duraludon's Steel-type attacks and Munkidori's Poison-type attacks, Tera Steel leaves it vulnerable to Choice Scarf Flamigo's Close Combat, and Tera Ghost faces competition from the more impactful defensive utility of Tera Fairy and Tera Steel.

Espeon fits on balance, bulky offense, and sun teams that appreciate Magic Bounce denying entry hazards and status without losing momentum. Eject Button is especially useful on sun teams, bringing in wallbreakers such as Venusaur, Scovillain, and Brute Bonnet while preserving limited sun turns. Outside of sun, frail wallbreakers such as Flamigo, Basculegion-M, and Meloetta also appreciate Eject Button bringing them in safely. Hazard-weak teammates such as Choice item Chandelure and Staraptor appreciate Espeon's hazard control giving them more chances to switch in and apply pressure. Entry hazard setters such as Klefki, Gligar, Swampert, and Duraludon also appreciate Espeon making opposing hazard control a pain, as Rocky Helmet punishes Tsareena for using Rapid Spin, while Tera Ghost can be used to spinblock when needed. In return, Gligar can act as a check to both Incineroar and Overqwil, while Paldean Tauros-W and Flamigo threaten Dark-types such as Incineroar, Scrafty, and Brute Bonnet that can otherwise force Espeon out. Dark- and Water-type teammates such as Incineroar, Wo-Chien, and Vaporeon help cover Ghost-types like Chandelure, Houndstone, and Basculegion-M. Espeon also appreciates teammates that can handle strong pivoting attackers; Bellibolt can punish U-turn from Flamigo, Scyther, and Tsareena with Static, while Rhyperior outright blocks Volt Switch from Kilowattrel and pressures it with Stone Edge. Steel-types such as Copperajah and Duraludon can help against common attackers like Cinccino and Scyther while also giving Espeon sturdier defensive support against Ambipom and Munkidori.

Support.description:
Boasting excellent defenses and a plethora of utility moves, Umbreon finds itself a niche in providing bulky support along with Inner Focus ignoring the ever so common Fake Out from the likes of Incineroar and Rillaboom. Access to Foul Play allows Umbreon to tackle physical threats such as Calyrex-I as well as threatening Calyrex-S with a huge amount of damage. Snarl helps tremendously against special attackers like Terapagos, Calyrex-S, and Lunala, dealing a decent chunk of damage to the latter two. Helping Hand can also be used in this slot to further boost the team's offensive pressure to help secure KOs, such as Helping Hand-boosted Tera Fairy Zacian-C OHKOing Incineroar with Play Rough. Yawn is Umbreon's primary means of disruption, forcing the opponent to keep switching their Pokemon to prevent them from being put to sleep, while Taunt helps shut down opposing support Pokemon like Amoonguss or any Trick Room setters such as Farigiraf and Calyrex-I. Moonlight, on the other hand, increases Umbreon's longevity on the field and is especially useful in sun teams. Safety Goggles gives it a much needed immunity to Amoonguss, which can otherwise completely shut down Umbreon with Spore and Rage Powder. The EV spread allows Umbreon to survive a Collision Course from Koraidon outside weather, a Tera Fairy Moonblast from Flutter Mane, and prevents the 2HKO from a rain-boosted Weather Ball and Thunderbolt from Pelipper and a Special Attack Booster Energy Raging Bolt, respectively. Tera Water is an excellent defensive Tera type, further bolstering Umbreon against Calyrex-I, Kyogre, and Urshifu-R. On the other hand, Tera Poison provides a resistance to Fairy and Fighting-type moves such as Flutter Mane's Moonblast, Koraidon's Collision Course, and Urshifu's Close Combat.

Despite its longevity and disruptive options, Umbreon provides little to no offensive pressure most of the time. Pokemon like Zacian-C, Zamazenta-C, Koraidon, and the Urshifu formes instantly threaten Umbreon with their STAB moves, while faster Taunt users such as Incineroar and Flutter Mane shut down its support options. Umbreon pairs well with offensive Pokemon such as Zacian-C and Koraidon that can handle the aforementioned threats and take advantage of its Yawn pressure, with the latter setting up sun to maximize the healing provided by Moonlight. Rillaboom partners well with Umbreon because it functions as a Kyogre and Urshifu-R check while providing Grassy Terrain recovery and positioning through its U-turn. Meanwhile, Urshifu-R compliments Umbreon's support role by providing solid offensive pressure by pinning opponents with Surging Strikes, OHKOing Incineroar and Flutter Mane with the move.

ru.overview: Umbreon provides tremendous value as a specially defensive wall that can support its teammates through Wish passing and status spreading. Umbreon often provides Wish support to some of the tier's strong Choice item wallbreakers such as Yanmega, Hisuian Goodra, and Krookodile. Umbreon also props up balance and bulky offense structures by comfortably tanking attacks from special wallbreakers like Basculegion-F and Gengar and spreading status while maintaining its own health with Moonlight and Wish. Umbreon is efficient in neutralizing setup sweepers because of its natural bulk and ability to use their strength against them with Foul Play. Umbreon is, however, severely allergic to Bug- and Fighting-type attacks, which are commonplace in a metagame with strong threats that can force it out like Yanmega, Terrakion, and Gallade. Using Terastallization on Umbreon grants it several key benefits, notably Tera Poison to flip the weaknesses to Bug and Fighting and become immune to poison. This, however, is not enough to help it break through important checks to Umbreon like Krookodile, Hisuian Goodra, and Registeel.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Umbreon can use Thunder Wave over Toxic on teams that use slower wallbreakers like Golurk and Crawdaunt, allowing them to outspeed the opposition. Roar provides an option to phaze opposing setup sweepers like Tera Poison Slowbro and Calm Mind Suicune, while Taunt is another option that can prevent setup attempts. While Umbreon often skews specially defensive, it can opt to run physical bulk instead to better check the plethora of strong physical attackers in the tier like Krookodile, Torterra, and Feraligatr.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-type wallbreakers: There is no shortage of strong Fighting-type wallbreakers that immediately threaten Umbreon, such as Gallade, Terrakion, and Flamigo.

Disruption: Umbreon suffers from a low Speed stat, which makes it easy to disrupt with faster Encore users like Jirachi and Maushold. Taunt users like Krookodile and Noivern similarly make life difficult for Umbreon as it struggles to check them effectively without healing support in Moonlight and Wish. Pokemon like Gardevoir and Gengar can threaten to Trick a Choice item onto Umbreon, rendering it nearly useless as a support Pokemon.

VoltTurn: Umbreon is often used to check special wallbreakers like Magnezone and Noivern, though both of these have access to pivot moves and can quickly wear it down with VoltTurn cores utilizing teammates like Flamigo and Yanmega.

Wish Support.description:
Set Details

Foul Play hits Jirachi and Dragon Dance Necrozma for large chunks of damage. Toxic helps Umbreon be less passive, threatening to secure a big poison on difficult-to-take-down Pokemon such as Slowbro and Wo-Chien. Protect is a valuable move on Umbreon to scout for Choice-locked attacks from wallbreakers like Gardevoir and Flamigo while also allowing for a Wish to land safely and gaining a turn of Leftovers recovery; alternatively, Moonlight can provide more immediate healing in a similar vein. Inner Focus prevents Umbreon from getting flinched down by faster Pokemon like Bisharp and Jirachi, while Synchronize can allow Umbreon to act as a status absorber while returning the favor to Pokemon like Body Slam Jirachi and Thunder Wave Reuniclus. Leftovers is the preferred item for Umbreon to maximize its longevity, though Heavy-Duty Boots can be used to prevent entry hazard chip from accruing too quickly as well. Tera Poison flips weaknesses to Bug, Fairy, and Fighting, which is important to survive the onslaught of attacks from wallbreakers like Terrakion, Gardevoir, and Yanmega, while also providing a key immunity to poison. Similarly, Tera Ghost can provide an immunity to Fighting and Normal, notably letting Umbreon punish Maushold with Foul Play; it can also help Umbreon function as a spinblocker against Cyclizar.

Umbreon is an excellent fit on balance and bulky offense structures, fulfilling many key roles such as Wish passing and status spreading. Using its defensive prowess to provide reliable recovery to Choice item wallbreakers like Basculegion-F, Hisuian Goodra, and Galarian Zapdos is a defining trait of Umbreon's, as it can be difficult for teams to survive the onslaught of strong attacks while also trying to break through Umbreon. Slowbro pairs well with Umbreon defensively, as they can be quite difficult to break through using their immense bulk and type combination of Dark and Psychic. Given that Toxic is Umbreon's most notable way of dealing out damage, poison absorbers like Gligar and Registeel can reliably switch into Umbreon, so teammates like Barraskewda and Basculegion-F are important to threaten these checks. Entry hazard removal is important for Umbreon, as it often opts for Leftovers over Heavy-Duty Boots, making Noivern and Cyclizar two great partners that can provide hazard removal. The former also resists Bug and Fighting, which helps to form dynamic defensive cores that can use Umbreon's access to Toxic to wear down the opposition. Other defensive partners like Gligar and Hisuian Goodra, which lack reliable recovery of their own, can use Wish pass support from Umbreon to improve their longevity.

Wish Tank.description:
• Umbreon's high bulk allows it tank a slew of offensive Pokemon. Alongside excellent utility moves, Umbreon can generate tempo while surviving even surprise Tera-boosted attacks.

  • Foul Play: In such a physically leaning format, Foul Play is a strong reliable move to chip the opponent's Pokemon. In particular, it punishes Dragon Dance from Lum Berry Dragonite.

  • Wish and Protect: Wish + Protect provides excellent recovery opportunies for both Umbreon and its teammates. With Leftovers's animation as well, its great at stalling out the timer. Protect also scouts for U-turn and Tera.

  • Yawn: Yawn's ability to force switches generates extra Leftovers recovery and generates momentum for its teammates.

  • Thunder Wave: Thunder Wave has excellent synergy with Wish. If the opponent's Pokemon is unable to attack on the turn Umbreon uses Wish, Umbreon can easily pass the Wish to a teammate.

  • Taunt: Umbreon can Taunt opposing walls and deny their recovery, with foes such as Hippowdon and Corviknight being especially vulnerable.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Despite its incredible bulk, Umbreon's Fighting- and Fairy-type weaknesses are exploitable by several top threats and often needs to be removed.

  • Fairy: In a heavily Dragon-centric metagame, Tera Fairy on defensive Pokemon is highly valuable. Removing Umbreon's Fighting- and Fairy-type weakness also helps deal with Sacred Sword Chien-Pao and Mimikyu.

  • Poison: Tera Poison resists Fighting, Bug, and Fairy and provides an immunity to Toxic, but makes it more vulnerable to Earthquake from the likes of Dragonite and Baxcalibur.

Items

  • Leftovers: Combined with Protect, Leftovers keeps Umbreon healthy and a little less reliant on Wish.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet's chip damage is serviceable, but many top physical threats have suitable non-contact moves they can use on Umbreon, especially after Umbreon Terastallizes.

Abilities

  • Inner Focus: Inner Focus avoids flinches from Chien-Pao and Kingambit, making Umbreon a more reliable check.

  • Synchronize: Synchronize punishes attempts to burn Umbreon.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD with Bold: With Terastallization, this spread allows Umbreon to tank a majority of the physical metagame.

  • 172 HP / 252 Def / 60 SpD / 20 Spe with Bold: If running Taunt, 20 Speed EVs outpace Skeledirge and Corviknight while retaining all-around bulk.

Utility Pivot.description:
Slowking leverages its good typing and Regenerator to be a great pivot in UU. Scald punishes foes trying to threaten it out such as Lokix and Ogerpon. Thunder Wave slows down foes such as Tornadus-T and Latios. On teams where the speed control is not needed, Future Sight is a good alternative to support its teammates with extra damage. Chilly Reception is key for bringing teammates in safely while pairing very well with Future Sight. It can also be used to clear sand. The first EV spread allows it to take on physical attackers like Mamoswine and +2 Excadrill, while the second EV spread lets it survive Choice Specs Tera Dragon Draco Meteor from Latios. 0 Speed IVs make Slowking as slow as possible to ensure that Chilly Reception can pivot in a teammate without taking any damage. Tera Fairy flips its weakness to Dark and Bug while gaining a Dragon immunity, letting it paralyze Greninja and Ogerpon while more safely switching into Hydrapple. Tera Water is a decent alternative that retains its Water resistance so it can still check Azumarill and Keldeo while boosting Scald’s damage, OHKOing Rhyperior and Excadrill with slight chip damage.

Slowking fits best on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate the speed control and consistent pivoting. Hydrapple forms a fantastic Regenerator core with Slowking, as it can easily handle Ogerpon as well as shared checks in Lokix and Latios if it Terastalizes. Slowking can also use Thunder Wave to slow down Tinkaton and opposing Hydrapple. Lokix is another excellent partner for Slowking, as it can be brought in safely by Chilly Reception to revenge kill a foe like Excadrill. It is also able to threaten Dark-types, which are immune to Future Sight, such as Tyranitar, opposing Lokix, and Mandibuzz with Knock Off. Slower wallbreakers like Choice Specs Hydrapple and Mamoswine love Slowking slowing down Cobalion, Tinkaton, and Tornadus-T for them. The latter also appreciates the Defense boost from snow, letting it easily take priority moves from Lokix, Scizor, and Azumarill. Slowking also appreciates teammates that handle Grass-types like Hydrapple and Ogerpon. Scizor and Assault Vest Tornadus-T form a good pivot core, with the latter helping on take on Latios for physically defensive variants. Skeledirge appreciates Slowking spreading status for Hex to deal more damage as well. Tinkaton can run Thunder Wave itself, opening up Slowking to use Future Sight while checking Ogerpon-C, Lokix, and Latios. Weather Ball users like Nasty Plot Tornadus-T, Thundurus-T, and Raikou also appreciate the Ice coverage from snow, allowing them to nail Hydrapple and Ogerpon-C.

Specially Defensive Pivot.description: With great special bulk, Regenerator, and Teleport, Slowking is an effective pivot and defensive check to prominent threats like Iron Moth, Enamorus, and Keldeo, being able to switch in against their powerful moves and either bring another teammate to maintain momentum or set up Future Sight and switch out right after. Scald allows Slowking to punish switch-ins like Tyranitar, Celesteela, and Tangrowth. Future Sight synergizes well with Teleport by threatening Pokemon like Buzzwole and Mega Venusaur while aiding wallbreakers like Scizor, Thundurus, and Bisharp by giving a free entry with Teleport to better pressure the opposing walls in conjunction with Future Sight. The extra damage provided is useful even against neutral or resistant targets like Gastrodon and Celesteela. Thunder Wave cripples faster targets like Mega Latias, Hydreigon and Enamorus. Teleport is preferred over Chilly Reception due to its negative priority, but the latter can be useful to disrupt sand from Tyranitar and Hippowdon to prevent Excadrill from activating Sand Rush. A Sassy nature with 0 Speed IVs is used to ensure Slowking is as slow as possible to possibly switch out after an opposing Teleport user like Slowbro. Heavy-Duty Boots blocks damage from entry hazards, notably allowing Slowking to better check Choice Specs Enamorus while maximizing recovery from Regenerator. Slowking fits best on balance and bulky offense teams where its defensive and support capabilities are appreciated by both defensive and offensive partners. Ground-types like Hippowdon and Excadrill can block Volt Switch from Zeraora; in return, Slowking can check Water-types like Keldeo and Volcanion. Fighting-types are also amazing partners by pressuring Dark-types like Tyranitar and Hydreigon for Slowking while enjoying Future Sight discouraging common switch-ins like Mega Venusaur and Clefable. Tyranitar deserves a special mention, as it usually tries to switch in and Pursuit trap Slowking. Good partners to deal with Dark-types include Buzzwole and Mienshao. Choice Specs Enamorus can put heavy pressure on Slowking with repeated Moonblasts respectively, making secondary checks like Celesteela and Scizor useful to help with Enamorus while Slowking scouts dangerous moves like Mystical Fire for them. Finally, frail offensive Pokemon like Thundurus and Victini enjoy the free entry Slowking provides with Teleport or Chilly Reception. Nasty Plot Thundurus is especially notable by threatening most Dark-types like Tyranitar and Hydreigon with Focus Blast or All-Out Pummeling.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Slowking's increased special bulk lets it fill a similar role to Slowbro while better taking on special attackers like Tapu Lele, Heatran, and Mega Diancie. Its neutrality to Ground and resistances to Water and Fire are advantages over Galarian Slowking, allowing it to pivot around threats like Great Tusk, Urshifu-R, and Mega Charizard Y. Teleport allows Slowking to pivot its teammates in safely while avoiding the doubled damage from Pursuit. Scald's 30% burn chance deters physical attackers like Dragonite, Garchomp, and Landorus-T from using Slowking as setup fodder. Future Sight synergizes greatly with Teleport, allowing Slowking's teammates to exert additional offensive pressure after Slowking has pivoted them in. Thunder Wave provides speed control against setup sweepers and Choice Scarf users. Slack Off gives Slowking an immediate method of healing without having to rely heavily on Regenerator. Toxic is best suited against bulkier teams, where Slowking leverages their lack of damage output to put them on a timer. Heavy-Duty Boots is essential to improve Slowking's longevity against entry hazards, especially since it will be switching out a lot thanks to Teleport. The given EV spread allows it to live two Diamond Storms from Mega Diancie.

Slowking fits on balance and bulky offense teams that require a specially defensive pivot, acting as a hybrid of the defensive typing of Slowbro and special bulk of Galarian Slowking to form its niche. Fighting-type teammates like Zamazenta, Mega Medicham, and Great Tusk have great synergy with Slowking, threatening Dark-types like Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Mega Tyranitar that Slowking fears. In return, Slowking provides safe switch-in opportunities via Teleport, with Future Sight hitting the Poison-types that resist their Fighting-type STAB moves. Slowking is threatened by physical Grass-type attackers like Ogerpon-Wellspring, Rillaboom, and Kartana, so Pokemon like Mega Scizor, Ferrothorn, and Corviknight are great teammates, and Slowking can shore up their weaker special bulk by switching into the likes of Mega Charizard Y, Mega Diancie, and Heatran. Because Slowking is susceptible to Knock Off, teammates that can switch into it safely are appreciated, such as Mega Scizor, Iron Valiant, and Gliscor. The former two also appreciate Slowking wearing down their checks with Scald and status, while the latter appreciates Slowking's ability to switch into special attacks. Thunder Wave's speed control and Teleport's safe switch-ins allow Slowking to enable slower wallbreakers early-game, like Choice Band Rillaboom, offensive Heatran, and Melmetal. The latter two are also Steel-types, a valuable typing for pivoting around Kyurem. In return, Slowking can safely switch into the Fighting- and Fire-type moves targeted at them while not being threatened by Ground-type attacks, giving it an advantage against Great Tusk, Heatran, and Fire Fang Garchomp.

monotype.overview:
Psychic

Slowking finds stiff competition from Slowbro, which is the far superior physical wall that can be a potential wincon with Iron Defense + Body Press. Additionally, Psychic teams greatly wish to have more offensive teammates, which creates issues with fitting Slowking onto these builds. However, Slowking's access to Chilly Reception can enable this offense, which is desirable.

Water

Slowking finds a niche as a special bulky pivot for Water teams. It allows free entrance for Water breakers life Urshifu-R while denying other weathers thanks to Chilly Reception. Future Sight into Chilly Reception creates a devastating delayed double attack when paired with a breaker, forcing the opponent to choose between sending out a Pokemon that resists the attacks of the breaker or one that resists Future Sight; the extra damage allows these breakers to obtain better ranges.. Slowking's excellent special bulk allows it to take a hit from full HP from special attackers like Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Spectrier, and Latios and paralyze them. However, it can become free setup fodder for threats like Raging Bolt, Iron Hands, and Dragapult. Moreover, Slowking struggles in this metagame composed mostly by physical attackers, especially because it's weak to two common moves in Knock Off and U-turn.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Ice Beam can be helpful on defensive archetypes, denying setup from Garchomp, and Dragonite.

Bulky Pivot (Psychic).description:
Slowking finds a role on Psychic teams thanks to its serviceable natural bulk along with access to Chilly Reception, enabling teammates like Hoopa-U, Latios, and Iron Boulder with safe entry. Scald is able to pressure Fire- and Ground-types like Cinderace and Mamoswine while also allowing Slowking to fish for burns. Thunder Wave can let Slowking cripple faster threats like Dragonite and, with a Kasib Berry, paralyze Ghost-types like Spectrier and Flutter Mane, enabling its teammates to safely outspeed and remove them. Foul Play can punish threats such as Swords Dance Garchomp. Heavy-Duty Boots is recommended, as it grants Slowking immunity to entry hazard damage. Alternatively, Slowking can use no item to reduce the damage from Knock Off, notably allowing itself to survive two Knock Offs from Choice Scarf Meowscarada, along with preventing Ceruledge from removing it with Poltergeist so that it can remove Ceruledge in response with Foul Play.

As mentioned before, teammates like Hoopa-U and Iron Boulder are great beneficiaries of Slowking's Chilly Reception, which enables them to hit the field safely. Hoopa-U can check Ghost-types such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Spectrier with its Dark-type STAB moves, and it can use powerful coverage such as Thunderbolt to remove Flying- and Water-types such as Moltres, Pelipper, and Toxapex. Alternatively, Choice Scarf Hoopa-U can outspeed and remove foes like Flutter Mane and opposing Hoopa-U comfortably with Hyperspace Fury. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder, meanwhile, provides incredible speed control, outspeeding threats such as Meowscarada and Choice Specs Flutter Mane, and can handle Fire- and Bug-types like Ogerpon-H, Volcarona, and Kleavor with ease. Choice Specs Latios provides handy Grass and Electric resistances and can use Draco Meteor to nail specially offensive Dragon-types that threaten Slowking such as Raging Bolt and Kyurem along with using coverage in Ice Beam to remove Grass-types like Brambleghast. Hatterene is a strong defensive complement to Slowking, being able to handle Dark-types such as Roaring Moon and break other problematic threats like Primarina and Blissey with Calm Mind; in return, it appreciates Slowking checking Steel-types such as Heatran and Corviknight. Metagross can provide Stealth Rock support to wear down foes that don't mind entering in on Slowking like Ogerpon-W and Rotom-W, and it can use Bullet Punch to check Iron Valiant and Flutter Mane. Slowking can enable safe entry for Armarouge, and in return, Armarouge can smash Steel-types like Gholdengo and Archaludon. Nasty Plot Deoxys-S can outspeed and handle the likes of Greninja and Landorus with Thunderbolt and Ice Beam, respectively. Gallade can threaten Dark- and Steel-types like Ting-Lu, Alolan Muk, and Hiusian Goodra for Slowking. Indeedee-M can provide Healing Wish support while using its Normal typing to come in on Ghost-types like Pecharunt and threaten them back with a powerful Psychic Terrain-boosted Expanding Force.

Bulky Pivot (Water).description:
Slowking has serviceable natural bulk along with access to Chilly Reception, granting teammates like Urshifu-R, Basculegion-F, Keldeo, and Greninja safe entry. It also helps against other weathers like sand, sun, and rain by replacing them and disrupting their strategy. Future Sight is the main offensive move, creating a nice combination with Chilly Reception to pressure the opposing team and maintain momentum. Scald prevents Slowking from being entirely passive through its threat to burn, which helps its teammates tank some hits. However, Thunder Wave can let Slowking hinder faster threats like Dragapult, Flutter Mane, and Latios, enabling its teammates to safely outspeed and remove them. Heavy-Duty Boots is recommended, as it grants Slowking immunity to entry hazard damage; Water teams typically lack entry hazard removal, and Slowking wants to switch in frequently. The given spread maximizes Regenerator recovery while maximizing Special Defense.

Slowking's best teammate is Urshifu-R. It benefits greatly from Slowking's Future Sight and Chilly Reception, which enables it to hit the field safely while threatening with a dangerous combination of Close Combat + Future Sight or Surging Strikes + Future Sight against Alolan Muk, Corviknight, Clodsire, and Toxapex. Basculegion-F appreciates the slow pivot and perfect accuracy for Blizzard. Basculegion-F can use Blizzard to punch holes in Dragon-type teams, as well as using Shadow Ball to take care of Ghost- and Psychic-type Pokemon, such as non-Choice Scarf Gholdengo, Latias, and Hatterene. Keldeo and Greninja are other options for wallbreakers. Keldeo deals with Hisuian Goodra and picks off Meowscarada with Vacuum Wave. Greninja with a Choice Scarf is able to outspeed Dragapult, Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, as well as threatening the Ogerpon formes with Sludge Wave. Hisuian Samurott resists a Ghost, provides hazard support with Ceaseless Edge, and packs a priority option in Sucker Punch. Toxapex is a great defensive option that creates a nice Regenerator core with Slowking, spreading poison and taking hits from Meowscarada, the Ogerpon formes, and Roaring Moon. Swampert is another bulky pivot that able to deal with Electric-type moves coming from Raging Bolt and set up Stealth Rock. Rotom-W is also a nice pivot that is immune to Ground-type moves and able to deal with Dragonite or Dragon Dance Dragapult with Will-O-Wisp or Foul Play, respectively.

Specially Defensive (Water).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Specially Defensive Pivot.description: Galarian Slowking is a fantastic specially defensive pivot in Ubers UU with Future Sight, a great defensive typing for the tier, Chilly Reception, and an excellent utility movepool. Future Sight makes stallbreaking much easier, amplifying wallbreakers like Chi-Yu due to the extra damage it provides. Flamethrower hits Magearna and Solgaleo, which are immune to Sludge Bomb and resist Future Sight. Toxic allows Galarian Slowking to cripple offensive Pokemon trying to switch in, like Palkia-O and Arceus formes, whereas Toxic Spikes allows it to shut down teams lacking a Poison-type while also crippling entry hazard-weak Pokemon like Arceus-Dark and Kyurem-W. Tera Water allows Galarian Slowking to resist Palafin's Water-type moves and handle Palkia-O better while shedding its Ground-type weakness, making it better at taking on Landorus. Alternatively, Tera Grass makes Galarian Slowking resistant to Ground and Water, meaning it still handles Palafin and Palkia-O well, at the cost of being weak to Kyurem-W and Chi-Yu. Lastly, Tera Fairy allows Galarian Slowking to shed its Dark-type weakness, flipping the matchup against Chi-Yu and Arceus-Dark. Galarian Slowking forms good cores with physical walls, which can mitigate its mediocre physical bulk, and as a result, it pairs well with Great Tusk and Giratina. Galarian Slowking can also support less bulky wallbreakers that can struggle to get on the field safely, like Deoxys and Chi-Yu.

Physically Defensive Pivot.description: Galarian Slowking is one of the best physically defensive pivots in Ubers UU, checking threats like Zacian and Sneasler with its wide support movepool and having the coveted combination of Future Sight and a pivoting move in Chilly Reception. Sludge Bomb allows Galarian Slowking to hit Fairy-types like Zacian and Clefable for good damage while also fishing for poison on Pokemon like Arceus formes. Future Sight assists greatly in breaking stall and makes wallbreakers like Kyurem-W more threatening. Flamethrower hits Steel-types like Magearna and Solgaleo that Sludge Bomb cannot. Slack Off allows Galarian Slowking to recover HP without switching out, letting it poison stall Pokemon like Zacian and Palkia-O and offset entry hazard damage if its Heavy-Duty Boots gets removed by Knock Off. Toxic allows Galarian Slowking to put switch-ins like Arceus formes and Mewtwo on a timer, whereas Toxic Spikes can support its team by spreading status, forcing foes to take passive damage, and poisoning Substitute users like Palkia-O. Tera Water allows Galarian Slowking to resist Palafin's Water-type attacks and handle Palkia-O better; it also removes its Ground-type weakness, making it better at handling Landorus-T. Alternatively, Tera Grass makes Galarian Slowking resistant to Ground- and Water-type attacks, meaning it still handles Palafin and Palkia-O well and is better into Landorus-T, at the cost of being weak to Arceus-Poison. Lastly, Tera Fairy allows Galarian Slowking to shed its Dark-type weakness, letting it take Knock Off and Kowtow Cleave from Great Tusk and Kingambit in a pinch. Galarian Slowking pairs well with Pokemon that struggle to switch in safely, such as Kyurem-W and Chi-Yu, as it can slowly pivot them in. Galarian Slowking is relatively passive and is particularly weak to Mewtwo, Deoxys, and Arceus-Dark, so it forms a very strong core with Arceus-Dark and Zacian, which can check those three foes.

Assault Vest.description:
Assault Vest Galarian Slowking can blanket check hard-hitting special attackers like Walking Wake, Iron Valiant, and Enamorus, with Regenerator allowing it to maintain longevity throughout the course of a game. Moreover, the added bulk from Assault Vest means Galarian Slowking can afford to invest into its Special Attack, improving its offensive prowess significantly by making use of its colorful coverage options to be a respectable special attacker as well. Psyshock punches holes through special walls like opposing Galarian Slowking, Blissey, and Clodsire much more effectively than its other Psychic-type STAB options and also immediately threatens Iron Moth, which can snowball past Galarian Slowking if given enough turns. It also allows Galarian Slowking to handle threatening Calm Mind users like Raging Bolt and Iron Valiant that can otherwise break past it with enough boosts. Psychic Noise allows it to annoy walls like Garganacl and Gliscor while similarly threatening Iron Moth immediately, even doing so through its Substitute. Sludge Bomb's poison can prove devastating against bulkier foes like Alomomola and Ting-Lu that can otherwise switch into Galarian Slowking. Flamethrower is useful coverage to hit Steel-types like Kingambit and Gholdengo, which would otherwise have ample switch-in opportunities. Ice Beam allows Galarian Slowking to hit Ground-types like Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Great Tusk while denting foes like Dragapult and Dragonite. 8 Defense EVs let Galarian Slowking survive a Ceaseless Edge or Knock Off from Hisuian Samurott and 96 Special Defense EVs allow it to take two Earth Powers from Choice Specs Kyurem. The rest of its EVs are pooled into Special Attack, letting it reach feats such as OHKOing Speed-boosting Iron Moth with Psyshock; 2HKOing Darkrai and OHKOing Rillaboom with Sludge Bomb; and 2HKOing Iron Crown and bulky variants of Gholdengo and Kingambit with Flamethrower. Alternatively, a physically defensive spread of 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD with a Bold nature can be used to trade its offensive potency for a better matchup against mixed attackers like Deoxys-S and Iron Valiant and physical attackers like Zamazenta, Ogerpon-W, and Rillaboom, all while still providing the team with a check to the aforementioned special threats. Tera Water gives Galarian Slowking a resistance to Water and Fire, allowing it to check Pokemon like Walking Wake, Primarina, and Iron Moth better, and drops its weaknesses to Dark-, Ghost-, and Ground-type moves, which allows it to act as an emergency check to Pokemon like Darkrai, Dragapult, and Great Tusk. Tera Grass similarly provides a Water resistance against Walking Wake with the added benefit of not being vulnerable to Garganacl's Salt Cure and Raging Bolt. The Ground resistance can also be helpful against foes like Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Gliscor.

Galarian Slowking is a recommended pick for balance and bulky offense teams due to it being able to check multiple top metagame threats like special attacking Iron Valiant, Iron Moth, and Walking Wake while also having respectable offensive presence and respectable longevity. It has a lot of trouble dealing with Ground-type Pokemon like Great Tusk and Landorus-T, so Flying-types like Corviknight and Skarmory pair extremely well with it. Corviknight and Skarmory are also able to sponge physical attacks from other Pokemon Galarian Slowking struggles with like Weavile, Dragonite, and Kingambit. Offensive partners like Rillaboom and Primarina can hit Ground-types instead of just simply walling them. Great Tusk itself is a great teammate for Galarian Slowking on the balance teams they fit on, serving as a Kingambit check and as entry hazard removal, especially versus hazard stacking teams. In return, Galarian Slowking is able to beat Pokemon like Enamorus, Walking Wake, and special attacking Iron Valiant sets for Great Tusk. Dragapult pairs neatly with Galarian Slowking, since it's also a frequent balance pick, serves as useful speed control, and appreciates Galarian Slowking being able to spread poison thanks to Sludge Bomb, allowing it to fire off Hex more frequently late-game without fearing Fairy-types stopping its sweeps. Gliscor fits on balance builds with Galarian Slowking, serving as a blanket check to physical attackers, a hazard setter, and a Knock Off absorber, along with having great longevity. Galarian Slowking is able to take advantage of the hazards Gliscor sets up by forcing switches with its vast array of coverage options, since many offensive threats prone to taking hazard damage like Primarina, Enamorus, Iron Valiant, and Raging Bolt don't want to stay in and take repeated hits from it. Landorus-T is the Ground / Flying teammate of choice on bulky offense teams because of its better offensive presence and pivoting capabilities. Hisuian Samurott is another hazard setter that pairs well with Galarian Slowking, since it's able to soft check Pokemon that threaten Galarian Slowking like Weavile, Gholdengo, and Kingambit, whereas Galarian Slowking can take on Iron Valiant and Serperior for it while still retaining a threatening offensive presence thanks to its great coverage and solid offensive stats. Zamazenta is a great partner on bulky offense teams due to its favorable Kingambit matchup and ability to soft check many other physical attackers that threaten Galarian Slowking like Meowscarada, Ogerpon-W, and Weavile. IronPress sets can set up and sweep after Galarian Slowking has removed their checks and chipped the opposing team into KO range. Various other offensive Pokemon such as Primarina, Kingambit, and Ogerpon-W also greatly appreciate Galarian Slowking functioning as a defensive Pokemon with a notable offensive presence, allowing for more flexibility when teambuilding. Other bulky Regenerator Pokemon like Alomomola and Hydrapple can form Regenerator cores with Galarian Slowking, outlasting many offensive builds while covering each other's weaknesses. Alomomola can wall Fire- and Ground-types like Cinderace, Heatran, and Great Tusk, while Hydrapple is able to beat Water-types like Ogerpon-W, Hisuian Samurott, and Dondozo.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Poison (Specially Defensive)

Shuca Berry can be an alternative held item to allow Galarian Slowking to survive a Ground-type attack that would otherwise KO it such as a +2 Landorus's Earth Power or Choice Scarf Landorus-T's Earthquake from full health and OKHO in response with Ice Beam.

Specially Defensive (Poison).description:
With a pair of Heavy-Duty Boots, Galarian Slowking can provide itself with an entry hazard immunity while still preforming its role as a special tank for Poison teams, capable of switching into threats like Choice Specs Latios. Future Sight can handle threats such as Toxapex, Pecharunt, and Great Tusk that can prove problematic for Poison teams and helps to break stalemates against more passive teams. Ice Beam hits Flying- and Dragon-type threats such as Landorus, Zapdos, Enamorus, and Latios. Chilly Reception allows Galarian Slowking to pivot in frail teammates such as Sneasler and Iron Moth safely and, when paired with Future Sight, allows for said teammates to get through checks such as Toxapex and Clodsire, respectively. Alternatively, Toxic can pressure threats such as Raging Bolt and Volcarona, while Thunder Wave provides a speed control option for Poison teams against Pokemon such as Tornadus-T.

Sneasler and Okidogi appreciate Galarian Slowking pivoting them in with Chilly Reception and using Future Sight to nail would-be checks in Toxapex, Hippowdon, and Rotom-W. In return, Sneasler and Okidogi can remove special walls and Dark-types like Hisuian Goodra, Alolan Muk, and Hisuian Samurott. Iron Moth appreciates Galarian Slowking giving it safe switches with Chilly Reception, and its Future Sight support allows Iron Moth to break past special walls such as Clodsire; In return, Iron Moth can handle threats like Gholdengo, Metagross, and Sinistcha. Amoonguss provides a solid answer to powerful physical Water- and Ground-type threats like Barraskewda, Urshifu-R, and Great Tusk. Pecharunt's high Defense allows it to take on threats like Azumarill, Iron Hands, and Kleavor, along with using Parting Shot to create a bulky pivot core with Galarian Slowking. Thanks to levitate and its Fairy typing, Galarian Weezing provides a solid check to Dragon-, Ground-, and Dark-type threats such as Roaring Moon, Garchomp, and Ting-Lu, along with providing Defog support, should Galarian Slowking lose its Heavy-Duty Boots. Alolan Muk helps to check special Ghost- and Psychic-types that threaten to overwhelm Galarian Slowking such as Flutter Mane, Spectrier, Indeedee, and opposing Galarian Slowking. Overqwil can check physical Ghost- and Psychic-type threats such as Ceruledge, Dragapult, and Gallade, and it can set Spikes to pressure threats attempting to switch into Galarian Slowking's attacks such as Gholdengo. Clodsire can provide Stealth Rock support and can take on special threats such as Raging Bolt and Flutter Mane that can overwhelm Galarian Slowking.

Assault Vest (Poison).description:
Galarian Slowking is a solid defensive piece for Poison teams with its incredible Special Defense, especially with an Assault Vest, able to shrug off hits from threats such as Heatran, Latios, and Raging Bolt. Future Sight is used to create pressure and helps to break opposing teams by nailing threats like Toxapex, Great Tusk, and Amoonguss that may want to switch in against Galarian Slowking's physical teammates like Sneasler and Okidogi for high amounts of damage. Sludge Bomb gives a much more consistent STAB option and helps to nail Fairy-type threats like Enamorus, Iron Valiant, and Primarina. Ice Beam stops threatening Dragon- and Flying-type threats like Latias, Raging Bolt, and Landorus. Flamethrower serves as a solid coverage option, melting problematic Steel-types like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Gholdengo that can otherwise shrug off Galarian Slowking's attacks, along with acting as a lure for Heatran. Finally, Earthquake gives Galarian Slowking a good way to break Heatran, which Poison teams detest, once its Air Balloon pops.

Sneasler and Okidogi benefit from Galarian Slowking immensely, as they can deal with threats attempting to take Galarian Slowking's Future Sights like Articuno, Blissey and Alolan Muk thanks to their high-powered Fighting-type STAB moves. Galarian Slowking, meanwhile, benefits from them removing dangerous Dark-type threats like Ting-Lu, Bisharp, and Hisuian Samurott. Amoonguss complements Galarian Slowking by being a physical wall capable of handling physical attacks from the likes of Great Tusk and Iron Treads with its Grass-type STAB moves and Foul Play, along with creating openings with Spore so Galarian Slowking can pivot in to heal and set Future Sight. Galarian Weezing provides similar support thanks to Levitate and its ability to handle threats like Garchomp, Dragonite, and Mamoswine with Strange Steam and Will-O-Wisp as well as remove entry hazards thanks to Defog. Toxapex completes the Regenerator core while also handling high-powered physical attacks from the likes of Scizor, Chien-Pao, and Ceruledge. Alolan Muk handles Ghost- and Psychic-type threats attempting to overwhelm Galarian Slowking like Flutter Mane, Spectrier, and Latias with Knock Off. Overqwil, with its far higher physical bulk and Intimidate, checks physical Ghost- and Psychic-type threats such as Ceruledge and Iron Boulder and sets Spikes to make Galarian Slowking's answers, Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra, take considerable chip damage. Iron Moth enjoys Galarian Slowking's ability to handle Heatran, which allows it to deal with the Steel-types like Corviknight and Gholdengo that would otherwise sit on Galarian Slowking and use its lacking Flamethrower as setup bait, along with melting Chien-Pao and Iron Treads if it is using a Choice Scarf. Salazzle similarly appreciates the removal of Heatran and helps out Galarian Slowking by inflicting Toxic onto special walls such as Hisuian Goodra and Alolan Muk with Corrosion, putting them on timers. Glimmora provides similar Toxic support with Corrosion while also setting entry hazards, chipping at switch-ins like Alolan Muk, Ting-Lu, and Hisuian Goodra when they come to stop Galarian Slowking.

Specially Defensive (Psychic).description:
Galarian Slowking finds a niche on Psychic teams thanks to its incredible solid Special Defense and strong support moves such as Toxic Spikes. Sludge Bomb can spread Poison along with dealing with Fairy-type threats like Primarina and Enamorus. Ice Beam deals with Flying- and Dragon-type threats such as Zapdos, Tornadus-T, Latios, and Raging Bolt. Chilly Reception allows Galarian Slowking to safely pivot into its teammates.
