Wallbreakers such as Kyurem, Zamazenta, and Iron Valiant pair well with Scizor, enjoying a safe switch-in from U-turn. Dark-types like Darkrai, Hisuian Samurott, and Kingambit appreciate Scizor's ability to scare out the Fairy-types that threaten them such as Iron Valiant and Clefable. In return, the Dark-types can threaten the physically defensive Ghost-types that can shrug off Scizor's Knock Off, such as Pecharunt and bulky Gholdengo. Water-types like Hisuian Samurott and Alomomola pair well with it defensively, scaring out the Fire-types that threaten Scizor such as Moltres and Cinderace. In return, Scizor offers a 4x resistance and threatens U-turn on the Grass-types that scare the Water-types, such as Rillaboom and Meowscarada. Due to Scizor's crippling 4x weakness to Fire-type moves, it appreciates teammates that resist such moves, such as Dragonite and Raging Bolt. Dragonite appreciates Scizor's resistance to Ice- and Fairy-type moves while also threatening these foes back with Bullet Punch. Scizor's Defog support is also great for Dragonite, allowing it to hold items other than Heavy-Duty Boots. In return, Dragonite can KO Scizor checks with its multitude of coverage options, such as Ice Spinner for Flying-type Pokemon like Zapdos and Gliscor; Fire Punch for Pokemon like Corviknight; and Earthquake for Pokemon such as Ceruledge, Heatran, and Iron Treads. Raging Bolt is also a great teammate, threatening the bulky Flying- and Water-types that wall Scizor, like Corviknight, Moltres, Alomomola, and Toxapex while resisting Fire-moves as well. In return, Scizor threatens the Ice- and Fairy-types that scare Raging Bolt, as well as Ting-Lu, with either U-turn or Knock Off. Additionally, the two form a double priority and pivoting core, constantly keeping momentum and preventing setup sweepers from snowballing out of control. Due to its lack of power, Pokemon like Kingambit, Raging Bolt, and Dragonite can use Scizor as a setup opportunity, so teammates that punish such attempts like Ogerpon-W with Encore and phazers such as Roar Zamazenta and Moltres are appreciated.

Offensive Swords Dance.description: Accounting for its diverse movepool, priority options, and huge base Attack, Scizor makes for an incredibly threatening wallbreaker and cleaner on more offensive teams. Furthermore, Scizor's Steel typing and decent bulk also complements its ability to keep many faster threats in check, such as Enamorus, Mega Latias, and Alakazam, while using them as setup fodder. Knock Off allows Scizor to break past Slowbro and Skeledirge while also OHKOing Victini; it can even prove useful for removing items from several soft checks otherwise reliant on them, such as Leftovers from Rotom-W. Dual Wingbeat is usually preferred in the last slot for its coverage against specific physical walls able to blank its other attacks, such as Buzzwole, Mega Venusaur, and Tangrowth, but Close Combat can be used instead to deal more damage to Steel-types such as Skarmory, Magnezone, and Bisharp, putting immense pressure on the former at +2 while OHKOing the latter two unboosted. Quick Attack can also be used to give Scizor an extra priority attack, allowing it to finish off weakened foes that would otherwise resist Bullet Punch, such as Iron Moth and Zeraora, although its lack of coverage can leave Scizor to struggle with breaking through the aforementioned defensive targets. Due to its lack of longevity and early- or mid-game prowess, this Scizor set usually fits best on select offensive teams that appreciate its versatility in being able to deal with faster threats. Entry hazard support from the likes of Excadrill and Lead Mew can help push several Pokemon, such as Iron Moth and Tyranitar into Scizor's KO threshold. Scizor also appreciates specific teammates that can help weaken or take advantage of Fire- and Steel-types, like Iron Moth and Greninja, as it can often be dissuaded from sweeping by their presences in a vacuum while they remain healthy. Conversely, other late-game cleaners such as Swords Dance Bisharp, Z-Celebrate Victini, and Dragon Dance Mega Aerodactyl appreciate Scizor's own ability to force damage onto shared checks such as Hippowdon, Skarmory, and Choice Scarf Keldeo while allowing Scizor to forgo its late-game approach if attacking early may be more optimal for enabling the rest of its teammates.

Bulky Swords Dance.description: A fantastic defensive typing alongside powerful priority allow Scizor to be an important defensive piece as well a great late-game cleaner on most teams. Swords Dance is essential to allow Scizor to sweep weakened teams, and it pairs well with Bullet Punch, allowing Scizor to ignore its mediocre Speed and KO faster threats, like Alakazam and Iron Boulder. Knock Off allows Scizor to overwhelm checks such as Celesteela and Rotom-W that rely on Leftovers to check Scizor over a longer game. U-turn is another option that allows Scizor to pivot in threats such as Iron Moth and Greninja on typical Scizor checks such as Skarmory and Skeledirge. Roost is essential to allow Scizor to consistently perform defensive roles over a long game, as well as set up on weaker defensive foes, like Hippowdon and Tangrowth. Heavy-Duty Boots is typically preferred on Scizor to prevent it from being worn down too quickly by entry hazards, but Leftovers can also be used on teams with more reliable hazard removal. Buginium Z can be utilized alongside U-turn to defeat foes such as Amoonguss at +2 while also allowing Scizor to threaten foes such as Hydrapple without being forced to switch out. 112 Attack EVs with an Adamant Nature allow Scizor to OHKO Mega Gardevoir with Bullet Punch, 12 Speed EVs allow Scizor to outspeed Skeledirge, and 76 Special Defense EVs allow Scizor to survive 2 Shadow Ball from uninvested Aegislash. However, EVs can be moved from Attack to Defense or Special Defense to help Scizor better check threats such as Iron Boulder or Aegislash respectively, though 16 Attack with an Adamant nature is recommended to OHKO Mega Gardevoir after Stealth Rock. Bulky Swords Dance Scizor can be used on offensive and bulky teams that appreciate Scizor's priority and defensive profile. Teammates such as Mega Gardevoir and Alakazam appreciate Scizor removing Leftovers from shared checks such as Aegislash and Celesteela; Scizor's defensive profile provides support against threats such as Zeraora and Iron Boulder. Scizor often struggles to break through Skarmory, so teammates that can take advantage of it, like Aegislash, Iron Moth, and Magnezone are appreciated. Scizor is also heavily threatened by Fire-types like Iron Moth and Skeledirge, so partners such as Rotom-W, Slowking, and Hippowdon that can handle these threats are mandatory; in return, Scizor can check common switch-ins to these defensive pieces such as Hydrapple and Mega Venusaur. Scizor can also struggle to threaten certain offensive Pokemon that resist Bullet Punch, like Iron Moth and Greninja, so teammates such as Hippowdon and Celesteela that can handle these threats or wear them down until Scizor can pick them off later in the game are appreciated.

Choice Band.description: Choice Band provides Scizor with immediate power on its attacks, allowing it to be more proficient as a wallbreaker, pivot, and late-game cleaner all at once. Bullet Punch puts substantial pressure on win conditions such as Calm Mind Clefable and Tapu Bulu, outright OHKOing the latter from full HP. Knock Off allows Scizor to remove important items from Pokemon otherwise reliant on them to deter it, such as Leftovers from Rotom-W and Celesteela and Rocky Helmet from Buzzwole and Amoonguss. Pursuit takes advantage of Scizor's excellent typing against several Psychic-type Pokemon to trap them, most notably Mega Latias, Alakazam, and Slowking. Alternatively, Close Combat and Dual Wingbeat are options to pose a more immediate threat to their respective targets, such as Excadrill and Magnezone with Close Combat and Buzzwole and Mega Venusaur with Dual Wingbeat. Scizor fits best on bulky offense teams that can best take advantage of its strong momentum-grabbing capabilities and cleanup potential. Pivots such as Rotom-W, Choice Scarf Hydreigon, and Iron Moth can help Scizor by threatening the physical walls used to stifle it, including Skarmory and Buzzwole; in return, Scizor can help force damage onto walls that normally handle these pivots, such as Tangrowth and Blissey. Scizor also appreciates strong entry hazard removal options to avoid being worn down quickly, including Defog from Rotom-W and Volcanion and Rapid Spin from Excadrill; the aforementioned Defog users are also capable of taking advantage of Fire-types that may pose a threat to Scizor, such as Victini. On the other hand, entry hazard support from the likes of Clefable and Skarmory is imperative to increase the overall impact of Scizor's pivoting capabilities as well as extend its capacity to revenge kill threats like Galarian Moltres with Bullet Punch.

Bulky Swords Dance.description:
Mega Scizor functions as an excellent late-game wincon due to its access to strong priority in Technician-boosted Bullet Punch, as well as being an excellent defensive piece, being able to switch in reliably on threats such as Iron Valiant, Kartana, and Rillaboom. Knock Off can be used in order to cripple would-be switch-ins such as Gholdengo, Zapdos, and Moltres. U-turn allows Mega Scizor to pivot out and gain momentum on threats such as Heatran and Mega Charizard Y switching in as well as defensive Pokemon such as Corviknight, Ferrothorn, and Alomomola. Sand Tomb is a more niche option that can be used in order to deal large damage to non-Air Balloon Heatran, as well as trapping Pokemon such as Toxapex switching in. 112 Defense EVs allow Mega Scizor to live 2 Mega Lopunny Close Combats after Stealth Rock and 20 Speed EVs allow Mega Scizor to outspeed uninvested Heatran.

Mega Scizor fits well on offense, bulky offense and balance teams due to its defensive capabilities as well as its ability to clean up in the later stages of the game with Swords Dance and Bullet Punch. Mega Scizor is extremely vulnerable to Fire-type moves from Pokemon such as Heatran, Volcarona, and Mega Charizard Y, meaning switch-ins such as Heatran, Toxapex, and Alomomola are appreciated. Mega Scizor also struggles to break through Steel-type Pokemon such as Kingambit, Melmetal, and Ferrothorn, making Fighting-types such as Urshifu-R and Zamazenta excellent partners. In return, Fighting-types benefit from Mega Scizor breaking through Fairy-type Pokemon such as Clefable and Iron Valiant. Mega Scizor provides an excellent switch-in to Psychic-types such as Tapu Lele, making teammates that benefit from this such as Great Tusk and Toxapex great partners. Mega Scizor also appreciates Stealth Rock setters such as Landorus-T, as they chip switch-ins such as Heatran and Corviknight, while Mega Scizor can help setters by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon such as Moltres and Zapdos, making them vulnerable to Stealth Rock.

Offensive Swords Dance.description:
Offensive Mega Scizor punches through the opposition with its three-attacks set thanks to its great base Attack stat, colorful coverage options, and surprisingly good natural bulk. Bullet Punch, when boosted by STAB and Technician, lets Mega Scizor beat faster threats like all-out attacking Zamazenta despite its mediocre base Speed stat. Close Combat hits Steel-types that normally stuff Mega Scizor, like Heatran and Kingambit, while being a great neutral option when boosted against the likes of Raging Bolt, opposing Mega Scizor, and Urshifu-R. Knock Off 2HKOes defensive and OHKOes offensive Gholdengo, which is otherwise a major annoyance, after a boost, while providing good utility into the likes of Toxapex and Moltres without needing a Swords Dance boost. Sand Tomb is a good alternative, as it directly breaks through Toxapex and other checks like Iron Moth while still retaining the ability to scare off Gholdengo, but it forgoes any chance of beating Moltres.

This particular Mega Scizor set fits best on hyper offense teams, which want Mega Scizor's cleanup ability and defensive utility without the drawbacks of being checked by annoyances like Toxapex and Heatran; not having Roost is not very noticeable due to these teams' plan to win quickly. Entry hazard setters like suicide lead Landorus-T, Glimmora, and Iron Treads greatly help Mega Scizor's wallbreaking ability by chipping foes like Toxapex and Raging Bolt down into range of Mega Scizor's attacks. They also pair well with Knock Off, allowing Mega Scizor to use said hazards to heavily pressure Moltres and Volcarona. Dragon-types like Dragonite and Raging Bolt are great partners, as they set up on Fire-types like Heatran and Moltres that otherwise stop Mega Scizor while loving Mega Scizor's ability to beat Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Tapu Koko and clean up once they are finished wallbreaking. Kingambit forms a great priority spamming duo with Mega Scizor, letting one wallbreak for the other to clean while appreciating Mega Scizor's neutrality to Ground and Fighting as well as its Fairy resistance, which let it switch into foes like Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, defensive Great Tusk, entry hazard setter Garchomp, and Mega Diancie.

Life Orb.description:
• Scizor uses its strong defensive typing and unique offensive profile to carve itself a role as a setup pokemon with Swords Dance.
  • By using Life Orb over Choice Band, Scizor can gain important favorable matchups against Pecharunt, Chople Berry Hisuian Goodra, and non-Choice Band Metagross by using Swords Dance before attacking.
  • Bullet Punch is the move to use against foes such as Iron Valiant, Pecharunt, Alolan Ninetales, and Sylveon.
  • Bug Bite is a reliable STAB option, allowing Scizor to beat non-Fire Punch Hoopa-U, Meowscarada, non-Defense invested Ogerpon-W, and Cresselia.
  • Close Combat is used to defeat Hisuian Goodra and non-Speed invested Ursaluna after a Swords Dance as well as Porygon-Z.
  • If Scizor is looking to 2HKO the foe, it is generally better to use Swords Dance and then attack rather than attack twice—such as against Ursaluna and Pecharunt.
  • The defensive EVs allow Scizor to survive two Earthquakes from non-Choice Band Adamant Metagross after one turn of Life Orb recoil. The special bulk lets Scizor survive a Hyper Beam from Choice Specs Modest Porygon-Z.
  • 44 Speed EVs let Scizor outspeed uninvested Metagross, which allows it to beat Metagross via the sequence of Swords Dance, Bug Bite, and Bullet Punch without being outsped by Metagross's own Bullet Punch.
  • Scizor needs to be covered for its weaknesses against Fire-types such as Volcarona and Volcanion as well as physically bulky Pokemon such as Landorus-T, Corviknight, and both Urshifu formes. For this, it can be paired with Pokemon such as Primarina, Raging Bolt, and Alolan Ninetales to great effect.

Choice Band.description:
• Choice Band Scizor is a strong threat that can deal with some of the biggest metagame threats such as Iron Valiant, Hoopa-U, and Primarina.
  • Bullet Punch hits Alolan Ninetales, Diancie, Iron Valiant, and Primarina.
  • Bug Bite is important for non-Fire Punch Hoopa-U, Ogerpon-W, and Serperior.
  • Close Combat can hit opposing Steel-type Pokemon like non-Chople Berry Hisuian Goodra and Registeel.
  • Knock Off is good coverage for Ghost-type Pokemon such as Spectrier.
  • The HP EVs allow Scizor to survive a Choice Band Hyperspace Fury from Jolly Hoopa-U, while the Special Defense allows it to live a Hex from Life Orb Spectrier after one turn of burn damage and after its Life Orb has been removed by Knock Off.
  • Scizor naturally struggles against Fire-types such as Volcarona, Skeledirge, and Volcanion, as well as physical tanks such as Landorus-T, Ursaluna, and Urshifu-R, so strong special attackers like Walking Wake and Manaphy make for excellent partners.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Bug (Swords Dance)

In teams with solid hazard control, Leftovers can be used to provide Scizor with passive recovery, notably letting it win its duel against Toxapex.

Swords Dance Scizor (Bug).description:
Thanks to its Steel typing, powerful STAB priority, and decent coverage moves, Scizor punches holes in the Fairy, Ice, Rock, Ghost, and Steel matchups. Technician-boosted Bullet Punch is Scizor's most spammable attack, serving as a priority STAB move to revenge kill sweepers like Belly Drum Azumarill and Flutter Mane. Close Combat answers Steel teams and OHKOes slower walls like Ting-Lu and Corviknight at +2 after Stealth Rock chip. Knock Off deals with Gholdengo, while Dual Wingbeat improves the Fighting and mirror matchups and lets it deal with Toxapex. Trailblaze allows Scizor to outspeed threats like Great Tusk and Urshifu-R at +1 Speed and hits Swampert, Gastrodon, and Primarina hard. Metal Coat enhances the power of Bullet Punch without drawbacks, while Life Orb secures OHKOs on Primarina and Porygon2 after a Swords Dance. Heavy-Duty Boots is another option in the event the team has poor entry hazard removal support. The EV spread allows Scizor to reach 324 Speed at +1 to outspeed Urshifu-R and makes it naturally faster than Adamant Azumarill.

With its impressive physical bulk and wide variety of support options, Forretress makes for an excellent partner, providing entry hazard support as well as Rapid Spin and a slow pivot to help Scizor. Due to its lackluster Speed, Scizor pairs well with Sticky Web setters like Araquanid and Galvantula. Thanks to its solid special bulk and Water Bubble, Araquanid provides both an offensive and defensive presence, checking and KOing opposing Volcarona and Ninetales. Alternatively, Galvantula can improve the Water matchup thanks to its access to Grass-type coverage moves, easily pressuring foes such as Toxapex and Pelipper. Offensively, Scizor greatly appreciates other wallbreakers that can remove or weaken its answers such as Kleavor, Volcarona, and Lokix. Choice Scarf Kleavor provides utility in Stone Axe and helps deal with Fire-types like Volcarona, Ceruledge, Ninetales, and Cinderace. Bulky Quiver Dance Volcarona can set up on physical walls that can prove troublesome to Scizor such as Moltres and Skarmory while removing Gholdengo and opposing Scizor. Lokix synergizes well with Scizor, as they both benefit from the holes they create in the opposing team: Scizor appreciates Lokix's ability to deal with Gliscor and Gholdengo, while Lokix enjoys Scizor taking on Fairy-type threats like Iron Valiant and Hatterene. Finally, Frosmoth can take most special sweepers such as Walking Wake, Greninja, and Raging Bolt head-on in Scizor's place, letting it crush Rock-type threats like Iron Boulder and Kleavor.

Swords Dance (Steel).description:
With Swords Dance, Scizor is an adept wallbreaker for Steel teams, removing the likes of Empoleon and Swampert. With Bullet Punch, Scizor also serves as a cleaner, easily picking off faster threats like Darkrai, Iron Valiant, and Iron Boulder. Close Combat allows Scizor to threaten Normal-, Steel-, and Dark-types like Blissey, specially defensive Heatran, Hisuian Goodra, and Alolan Muk. Trailblaze threatens Water- and Ground-types like the aforementioned Swampert, Gastrodon, and Primarina. With 216 Speed EVs, Scizor outspeeds and threatens Hisuian Goodra and Archaludon.

Archaludon and Skarmory provide entry hazard support to aid Scizor in its wallbreaking. Skarmory and Corviknight both provide a Ground immunity for Steel teams, and their physical bulk coupled with access to Iron Defense and Body Press allows them to wall out physical attackers and sweepers such as Choice Scarf Hoopa-U and Barraskewda. Corviknight also removes hazards for Scizor via Defog. Scizor is easily forced out by Fire-types such as Volcarona and Skeledirge. Hence, Heatran makes for a great partner, as it walls those Fire-types thanks to Flash Fire, and it is also able to handle walls Scizor struggles with such as Amoonguss. In return, Scizor deals with Water-types that Heatran struggles with like Gastrodon and Swampert. Hisuian Goodra is a great teammate that can cover Scizor against special attackers like Choice Scarf Heatran and Choice Specs Greninja. Choice Scarf users like Gholdengo and Iron Treads provide speed control, with Gholdengo handling Hex Dragapult while Iron Treads removes Choice Specs Iron Moth. In return, Gholdengo appreciates Scizor removing Alolan Muk, while Iron Treads appreciates the removal of Iron Valiant. Scizor forms a scary offensive partnership with Bisharp, with Scizor threatening Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Enamorus, while Bisharp handles Ghost-types that can wall Scizor such as Gholdengo and Pecharunt.

Choice Band (Steel).description:
Scizor utilizes a Choice Band to provide immediate pressure, OHKOing threats such as Mamoswine and Kyurem with Bullet Punch. Close Combat breaks through targets such as Porygon2, Iron Treads, and Archaludon that could otherwise take on Scizor's Bullet Punch. Knock Off smacks Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Pecharunt and allows Scizor to make progress against Skarmory and Gouging Fire. Finally, U-turn allows Scizor to pivot out while dealing immense damage to threats like Hydrapple and Ogerpon-W. The chosen EV spread allows Scizor to outspeed and easily remove Adamant Azumarill and uninvested Heatran while enabling it to reliably survive an Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel after entry hazard damage.

Heatran is a crucial ally for Scizor, being able to come in on Fire-types that wall it such as Iron Moth, Volcarona, and Skeledirge and remove threats that can handle Scizor like Skarmory and Toxapex. Gholdengo appreciates Scizor removing Flutter Mane, and in response, Gholdengo can handle Fighting-types like Iron Hands and Body Press users like Archaludon and Skarmory with ease. Skarmory provides Spikes, enabling Scizor to break through checks such as Pecharunt and Okidogi, and can use IronPress to beat Ground- and Fighting-types like Excadrill and Great Tusk. Iron Treads provides entry hazard removal with Rapid Spin, can remove Electric-types that resist Scizor's Bullet Punch such as non-Air Balloon Raging Bolt and Sandy Shocks, and can KO Landorus with Ice Spinner. Archaludon provides Stealth Rock support and can check foes such as Gouging Fire and Urshifu-R, which would otherwise easily remove Scizor. Hisuian Goodra can easily take on special attackers such as Greninja, Zapdos, and Sinistcha, which threaten Scizor.

Choice Band (Bug).description:
With a Choice Band, Scizor becomes a potent wallbreaker and revenge killer for Bug teams, providing immediate power to remove threats like Choice Scarf Iron Boulder and specially defensive Heatran while also proving to be a valuable asset against Rock teams. Bullet Punch targets Rock-, Fairy-, and Ice-types like Ogerpon-C, Flutter Mane, and Kyurem. It also serves as a countermeasure against setup sweepers like Unburden Sneasler, Dragon Dance Dragapult, and Belly Drum Azumarill. Close Combat smashes Steel-types like Archaludon and the aforementioned Heatran and 2HKOes specially defensive Corviknight after Stealth Rock damage. Knock Off threatens Ghost-types like Gholdengo while also messing with defensive switch-ins like Toxapex, Corviknight, and Great Tusk by removing their Heavy-Duty Boots or Leftovers. U-turn allows Scizor to gain momentum against switch-ins like Skarmory and Mandibuzz, bringing in teammates like Volcarona and Choice Scarf Kleavor. On the other hand, Dual Wingbeat handles Fighting-types like Urshifu-R and Great Tusk, while also dealing with bulkier targets like Amoonguss and Primarina.

Scizor's teammates benefit from its ability to remove Rock-types like Choice Scarf Iron Boulder and Ogerpon-C. Choice Scarf Kleavor leverages its Rock typing and Stone Axe to threaten Fire- and Flying-types like Ninetales, Ogerpon-H, and Zapdos while setting Stealth Rock. Volcarona eliminates Steel-types such as Skarmory and Corviknight as well as Toxapex when using Psychic. Additionally, its bulky sets can punish physical attackers like Dragonite and Iron Hands with its Flame Body and Will-O-Wisp while also absorbing Will-O-Wisp from foes like Sableye and Moltres. Araquanid boasts a valuable Fire resistance, allowing it to stave off threats like Volcarona and offensive variants of Heatran; it also offers a Will-O-Wisp immunity and Sticky Web, which allows Scizor to outspeed foes like Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine and Iron Treads. Frosmoth can dispatch bulky Ground- and Flying-types like Hippowdon, Gliscor, and Mandibuzz. Forretress complements Scizor's wallbreaking capabilities by setting entry hazards, which also synergizes with Scizor's Knock Off to wear down the opposing team. Forretress also provides hazard removal with Rapid Spin and can bring Scizor in safely with Volt Switch. Teammates like Lokix, Heracross, and Slither Wing value Scizor's removal of Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Flutter Mane; in return, Lokix threatens Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Pecharunt, while Heracross and Slither Wing can break through walls like Toxapex, Rotom-W, and Skarmory.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Pivot.description:
• Thanks to its high Attack, great defensive typing and solid bulk, Scizor is an effective bulky pivot that can also punish faster foes with Technician-boosted Bullet Punch, such as Flutter Mane, Chien-Pao, and Latios.

  • Knock Off versus Thief: Beyond being a fantastic support move, Knock Off is a great option against Gholdengo. Thief does offer more consistent damage than Knock Off though, thanks to Technician.

  • Dual Wingbeat: Dual Wingbeat is Scizor's best option against Ogerpon-H as well Fighting-types like Annihilape and Urshifu formes.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat is Scizor's best option to hit opposing Ursaluna-B and Chi-Yu as well as Steel types, even when using defensive EV spreads.

Other Options
  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf is a shocking twist against Ogerpon-H and Urshifu formes to launch off a strong Dual Wingbeat, but this does mean Scizor's bulk is heavily compromised against the threats it usually checks, like Flutter Mane.
Items

  • Assault Vest: While much less immediately threatening than Choice Band, Assault Vest lets Scizor more comfortably switch into stray special attacks like Gholdengo's and Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball or Rotom-W's Volt Switch, improving its longevity.

  • Choice Band: Choice Band lets Scizor function as a scary late-game cleaner, especially with Tera Steel-boosted Bullet Punch. The high damage output also helps Scizor to break down walls for its teammates.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet is perfect for more defensive Scizor, letting it continually switch into weaker physical attacks and wear down the team with U-turn and residual damage.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 92 Atk / 164 SpD with Adamant: This spread is meant to be used with Assault Vest, letting Scizor almost always avoid a 2HKO from Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball. It also maintains enough Attack investment to always OHKO uninvested Chien-Pao after Stealth Rock chip.

  • 236 HP / 68 Atk / 204 Def with Adamant: This spread avoids an OHKO from Tera Dark Life Orb Chien-Pao, is not 2HKOed by Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast, and reduces the amount of residual damage Scizor receives thanks to the HP stat being 1 lower than divisible by 16.

  • 236 HP / 68 Atk / 204 Def with Adamant: This bulky spread lets Scizor survive +2 Life Orb Adamant Tera Ghost Mimikyu's Shadow Claw.

  • 252 HP / 4 Atk / 252 Def with Impish: Defensive Scizor might seem strange, but when paired with Rocky Helmet, it becomes an effective pivot that can survive extreme attacks: it avoids the OHKO from Choice Band Tera Dark Chien-Pao's Crunch as well as the 2HKO from Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquake. Just note that this will make Scizor focus more on pivoting than revenge killing with Bullet Punch.

  • Brave or Relaxed with a Speed IV of 8 or 9: This Speed IV can be used to use U-turn after some Hippowdon use Yawn, but still outspeed Ting-Lu. Note that being slower than Ursaluna-B can be troublesome.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: While Terastallization can be quite helpful in either cleaning teams or preparing against Scizor's classic Fire-type issues, the power of its priority and pivoting don't make it needed for it to function consistently.

  • Water: Tera Water turns its Fire weakness into a resistance, giving Scizor a fighting chance against dangerous Fire-types such as Chi-Yu, Gouging Fire, and Ogerpon-H.

  • Steel: Tera Steel is ideal for more offensive Scizor variants, making Bullet Punch an even better cleaning tool. Tera Steel also softens Scizor's weakness to Fire, letting it avoid the OHKO from attacks like Flutter Mane's Mystical Fire.

  • Fire: Tera Fire is a great response most Ogerpon-H sets, and shields Scizor from burns that foes like Entei like to deal out.

  • Flying: Increasing Dual Wingbeat's power with Terastallization nets Scizor some useful new OHKOs against offensive Urshifu formes and Annihilape.

  • Dragon: While not an incredible defensive typing, Tera Dragon is fantastic against most Fire and Water Pokemon that give Scizor trouble, with Ogerpon formes being a particularly prominent example. As a downside though, it harms Scizor's ability to check Flutter Mane and Chien-Pao.

Swords Dance.description:
• Scizor's incredible power and good typing make it one of the premier priority sweepers, being able to sweep through huge threats such as Flutter Mane and Chien-Pao!

  • Close Combat: Close Combat lets Scizor smash through Ursaluna-B, Archaludon, and Ting-Lu after a boost.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off is Scizor's best bet against Gholdengo, in addition to being a great support move in general.

  • Dual Wingbeat: After a boost, Dual Wingbeat smashes through bulky Fighting-types like Urshifu-R and Annihilape.

  • U-turn: While pivoting doesn't gel well with sweeping, it makes this kind of Scizor very adaptable, and is especially effective at getting away from Pokemon that threaten with residual damage like Garganacl.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry and 244 HP EVs: Sitrus Berry trades late-game sweeping power for new setup opportunities, such as avoiding a 2HKO from Modest Gholdengo that lack Choice Specs. Make sure to run 244 HP EVs to gain an even HP number, letting Sitrus activate after getting hit by Ruination once.

  • Life Orb: While Life Orb does compromise Scizor's bulk, it's worth it for being able to OHKO Iron Bundle with a boosted Bullet Punch. Boosted Close Combat will also OHKO even physically defensive Ursaluna-B, and it has good shot of OHKOing physically defensive Ting-Lu.

  • Rocky Helmet: Best used with U-turn, Rocky Helmet transforms this Scizor into a good bulky pivot that has the surprising option to sweep late-game.

EV Spreads

  • 236 HP / 228 Atk / 20 Def / 20 SpD / 4 Spe with Adamant: This spread gives Scizor enough bulk to survive Tera Dark Life Orb Chien-Pao's Crunch, and less residual damage if using U-turn. It also avoids a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast. With Sitrus Berry, Modest Gholdengo's Shadow Ball is also no longer a 2HKO.

  • 228 HP / 124 Atk / 156 SpD with Adamant: This Sitrus Berry optimized spread avoids a 2HKO from Jolly Chien-Pao's Crunch, Iron Bundle's Hydro Pump, and Modest Choice Specs Tera Fairy Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

  • 252 HP / 28 Atk / 204 Def / 20 SpD / 4 Spe with Adamant: This bulky spread avoids the OHKO from Adamant Tera Ghost Life Orb Mimikyu's +2 Shadow Claw. When used with Sitrus Berry and 244 HP EVs, it also avoids the 2HKO from Modest Gholdengo's Shadow Ball.

  • 252 HP / 4 Atk / 252 Def with Impish: This defensive spread is best used with U-turn and Rocky Helmet, making Scizor function more like a bulky pivot that can sweep late-game.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium / Low: Terastallization works very well at shutting down common methods of revenge killing or walling Scizor, but its typing is good enough to function without Terastallization. If using U-turn, Scizor can focus on pivoting in some matches, making Terastallization even less needed.

  • Water: Tera Water lets Scizor ambush Chi-Yu, Iron Bundle, and Incineroar with a resistance and is especially handy against Fire-types when using Tera Blast.

  • Steel: Boosting Bullet Punch is Scizor's best ticket for revenge killing and late-game sweeping, and it gains a Flying-type resistance into powerful Tera Flying Choice Band users like Dragonite and Landorus-T.

  • Fire: Tera Fire ensures that Siczor's hard work won't get ruined by Will-O-Wisp or Sacred Fire, in addition to stopping revenge kills from common Fire-types like Ogerpon-H, Gouging Fire, and Incineroar.

  • Dark: Tera Dark can cushion Shadow Ball from Gholdengo and Flutter Mane, giving it an extra turn to set up or hit back with Tera-boosted Knock Off.

  • Electric: Tera Electric is Scizor's best shot of breaking past Toxapex and Urshifu-R with Tera Blast, and it does good chip damage to Dondozo.

Offensive Swords Dance (Steel).description: Mega Scizor makes for a strong wallbreaker and sweeper on Steel teams thanks to its access to Swords Dance, high Attack stat, and well-rounded bulk. Bullet Punch is Mega Scizor's strongest STAB move, and its priority allows it to revenge kill faster threats such as Mega Diancie, Iron Valiant, and Mega Lopunny. Close Combat is Mega Scizor's strongest coverage move, enabling it to more easily beat Corviknight, Ting-Lu, and Heatran. After a Swords Dance boost, Mega Scizor becomes strong enough to 2HKO Celesteela, opposing Mega Scizor, and physically defensive Gastrodon. Knock Off removes essential items such as Heavy-Duty Boots from Tornadus-T and Black Sludge from Toxapex, and it also provides Mega Scizor with strong coverage against Aegislash, Skeledirge, and Gholdengo. Alternatively, Trailblaze can also be used to 2HKO bulky Water- or Ground-type Pokemon most other Steel-types struggle with such as Mega Swampert and Gastrodon, as well as potentially OHKO Azumarill and Rotom-W after a Swords Dance boost and Stealth Rock damage. 132 Speed EVs are invested in order for Mega Scizor to outspeed Jolly Azumarill as well as Hydreigon and Urshifu-S after a Trailblaze. Heatran and Ferrothorn are great teammates because they are able to set entry hazards to wear down incoming foes, and Heatran also has the added benefit of providing a Fire immunity thanks to its ability. Ferrothorn can also provide passive healing for Mega Scizor via the use of Leech Seed. In return, Mega Scizor is able to threaten faster Fighting-types such as Sneasler and Iron Valiant with Bullet Punch. Gholdengo is able to threaten Toxapex and Tapu Lele, and it along with Aegislash can also hinder foes with Toxic and Thunder Wave respectively if they are running defensive sets, easing set up for Mega Scizor. In return, Mega Scizor can remove Dark-types such as Meowscarada, Ting-Lu, and Galarian Moltres. Specially defensive Celesteela is an excellent special wall that can wall Choice Specs Tapu Lele and Mega Altaria, while also being able to spread status and use Leech Seed to aid Mega Scizor in its sweeping. As Mega Scizor is more vulnerable to hazards compared to other Steel-types, it appreciates hazard removal from the likes of Corviknight, Excadrill, and Iron Treads. Excadrill and Iron Treads also have the added merit of handling Fire-types like Victini and Ogerpon-H. Excadrill can also bypass Mega Sableye's Magic Bounce and inflict poison on it thanks to Mold Breaker, while Iron Treads can threaten both Landorus formes with Ice Spinner.

Bulky Swords Dance (Steel).description: Mega Scizor's neutrality to Ground and Fighting and role compression as a wall and sweeper make it a formidable asset for Steel teams. Knock Off hinders predicted checks that Mega Scizor lures in on the switch such as Celesteela, Porygon2, Skeledirge, and Rotom-W, notably removing Heavy-Duty Boots to enable entry hazards that are characteristic of Steel teams. The first EV spread with an Adamant nature maximizes damage output, notably OHKOing Hisuian Lilligant, Meowscarada, and Kyurem with +2 Bullet Punch; it also outspeeds Adamant Azumarill and has the rest invested in HP to optimize mixed bulk. The second EV spread with an Impish nature also outspeeds Adamant Azumarill and avoids a 2HKO after Stealth Rock from Mega Lopunny's Close Combat and Adamant Mega Swampert's Earthquake, yet requires a layer of Spikes to OHKO Hisuian Lilligant and Meowscarada with +2 Bullet Punch. Mega Scizor is extremely vulnerable to Fire-type moves, so Heatran is a solid partner to mitigate this weakness. As Mega Scizor can often have a difficult time sweeping because Bullet Punch is easy to resist, Excadrill and Iron Treads make an offensive core with Mega Scizor, as they can pressure the Fire-, Electric- and Steel-types that would check it; notably, the former can additionally handle Rotom-W and the latter offensively checks Landorus. Ferrothorn and Hisuian Goodra are also options to further complement and handle Water-types for it. Gholdengo can wear down the opposing team as it stallbreaks past foes such as Toxapex, Mega Sableye, and Hisuian Goodra, easing Mega Scizor's sweep late-game; it also acts as an additional check for Fighting-types Mega Scizor can't consistently switch into such as Iron Valiant. Corviknight can remove entry hazards, increasing the longevity of Mega Scizor and the rest of its team, as well as pivot to it with U-turn to ease switching. Skarmory is also an alternative that can set Spikes, letting Mega Scizor reach OHKOes that it wouldn't otherwise.

Swords Dance (Bug).description: Swords Dance Scizor is an incredible wallbreaker for Bug teams, threatening offensive teams like Fairy, Dragon, and Ice. After a Swords Dance boost, Scizor becomes a powerful revenge killer that deals with fast frail threats like Iron Valiant, Mega-Diancie, and Sneasler using Bullet Punch. Close Combat is mandatory coverage, being able to take out Ferrothorn, Hisuian Goodra, and Blissey after a boost. Knock Off handles Psychic- and Ghost- types like Jirachi, Slowbro, and Gholdengo while hindering walls that switch in. Alternatively, Trailblaze increases Scizor's mediocre Speed while taking on Water- and Ground- types like Azumarill, Swampert, and Hippowdon. Metal Coat is the optimal item for the boost to Bullet Punch it provides without the downside of Life Orb recoil, which secures OHKOs on Pokemon like Latios and Mega Lopunny at +2. 216 Speed EVs let it outspeed base 100 Pokemon after -1 from Sticky Webs or a single Trailblaze boost. Sticky Web is often provided by Galvantula, which also takes care of Pokemon like Corviknight and Toxapex that Scizor struggles with. Araquanid handles Fire- types like Volcarona and Blacephalon while also providing Sticky Web support and a burn immunity. Volcarona appreciates Scizor's removal of walls and Choice Scarf users like Nihilego while in return dealing with bulky physical walls such as Zapdos or Great Tusk. Kleavor sets Stealth Rock, which chips down opposing teams into boosted Bullet Punch range while also handling Fire- types like Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y. Finally, Mega Pinsir removes Fighting- types and can more easily pick off teams that have been weakened by Scizor's powerful priority move.

Mega Swords Dance (Bug).description: Thanks to its humongous power after a Swords Dance boost, powerful priority in Bullet Punch, amazing defensive typing, and a colorful array of coverage options, Mega Scizor is an incredibly versatile offensive threat. Close Combat smashes the Steel-types resistant to Bullet Punch, such as Ferrothorn and Archaludon, and is Mega Scizor's go-to way of chunking physically bulky Pokemon like Porygon2 and Celesteela. Dual Wingbeat ties up Mega Scizor's coverage beautifully by delivering a clean 2HKO on Toxapex at +2 and nailing threats such as Keldeo and Mega Venusaur, thus allowing it to excel in the Fighting, Dragon, and Poison matchups. Alternatively, Knock Off is a more useful move to use while unboosted and lets Mega Scizor pressure Steel and Psychic teams much better by hitting Gholdengo, Slowbro, and Jirachi the hardest. Sticky Web support from Araquanid or Galvantula is paramount for Mega Scizor to effectively perform in the matchups it's supposed to by letting it outspeed the likes of Kommo-o and Mega Gallade. In particular, Araquanid soaks up the Fire-type moves aimed at Mega Scizor, and Galvantula forms a nice wallbreaking core with it courtesy of its ability to threaten Flying- and Water-types like Skarmory and Dondozo. Choice Scarf Kleavor revenge kills Fire-types and common Fire-type coverage users such as Mega Charizard Y and Zapdos and provides Stealth Rock via Stone Axe for Mega Scizor to nab extra kills. Other setup sweepers like Volcarona, Buzzwole, and Lokix greatly appreciate Mega Scizor's ability to soften the opposing team and vice versa, making them good offensive partners.

Choice Band (Bug).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Priority Attacker.description:
• The given EV spread allows Mega Scizor to outspeeed Chien-Pao during Tailwind while maximizing its Attack, allocating the remaining EVs in HP.
  • Mega Scizor's Bullet Punch is one of the metagame's most reliable ways of dealing with Flutter Mane. Bug Bite is Mega Scizor's strongest STAB move, but Close Combat help Mega Scizor OHKO Heatran and Incineroar at +1.

Suicide Lead.description:
• Shuckle is an extremely passive Pokemon with a poor typing, preventing it from contributing much mid-game. However, thanks to its decent bulk, great ability in Sturdy, and ways to maintain momentum in Final Gambit and Encore, it is an excellent suicide lead for hyper offense teams.

  • Final Gambit allows Shuckle to safely bring in an ally such as Zacian-C or Arceus-Ground after entry hazards are set.

  • Encore prevents Shuckle from being easily set up on by threats such as Arceus-Ground, Zacian-C, and Mega Salamence while additionally providing switch-in opportunities for teammates.

  • The given EV spread allows Shuckle to avoid a 2HKO from Life Orb Yveltal's Dark Pulse, preventing the latter from denying Sticky Web with flinches. The rest is dumped into Defense.

  • Tera Steel blocks Mortal Spin attempts from Glimmora and Smeargle. However, Terastallizing Shuckle should not be done in most cases unless the opponent has no other form of entry hazard removal. This means Tera Steel is only useful against opposing hyper offense teams with these Mortal Spin leads, as balance and stall teams usually have other hazard removal means like Giratina-O and Ho-Oh that Shuckle cannot block.

  • Shuckle should prioritize getting Sticky Web up against opposing hyper offense, offense, and balance teams. Against slower teams such as stall and Trick Room teams, Stealth Rock is more useful. Though, setting entry hazards up against Trick Room teams is harder due to Hatterene. The best play is to lead with Necrozma-DM instead, as it can burn Hatterene's Trick Room turns thanks to its resistance to Calyrex-I's and Melmetal's STAB moves. Shuckle should instead attempt to set Stealth Rock up against Calyrex-I, burning a turn of Trick Room in the process.

  • If Shuckle survives the first few turns by letting a teammate in with Encore, it can continue to provide value by being sacrificed to safely switch in a teammate or to burn a turn of Trick Room from Hatterene or Psychic Terrain from Tapu Lele.

  • Pokemon that appreciate Sticky Web support from Shuckle like Swords Dance Arceus formes, Primal Kyogre, Primal Groudon, and Eternatus make excellent teammates.

  • Shuckle cannot keep entry hazards up against common Defoggers such as Giratina-O, Yveltal, and Ho-Oh due to its passivity, so teammates that can threaten these Pokemon such as Zacian-C and Meteor Beam Eternatus are appreciated.

Sticky Web (Rock).description: Shuckle is an essential member of any hyper offensive Rock team due to its access to Sticky Web, which allows teammates such as Mega Diancie and Terrakion to dominate the Steel and Dark matchups. With Mental Herb, it isn't scared to set up entry hazards in front of common Taunt users such as Deoxys-S and Zeraora. Encore shuts down setup sweepers such as Mega Scizor and bulky walls such as Hippowdon and Ferrothorn, locking them into their setup and recovery moves. Shuckle can generate momentum after setting up hazards by using Final Gambit, allowing teammates such as Shell Smash Omastar, Mega Diancie, and Choice Band Tyranitar to come in and start exerting pressure. Toxic can also be used to punish more passive Pokemon such as Gastrodon and Hippowdon. Mega Diancie can bounce back any hazards or status moves directed at Shuckle and provides amazing offensive pressure and coverage against Poison-, Steel-, and Dragon-types. Sticky Web allows Choice Band Tyranitar to outspeed Choice Specs Gholdengo and Nidoking, both of which are threats to Rock. Omastar and Minior benefit from Stealth Rock breaking potential Focus Sashes and are great partners to have in the Grass and Fighting matchups. Thanks to Sticky Web, Omastar outspeeds Sand Rush Excadrill after one shell smash and +1 Spe Nihilego outspeeds Barraskewda in the rain. Power Herb Nihilego is able to sweep teams as well with Meteor Beam and amazing coverage. Thanks to Sticky Web, Choice Scarf Terrakion outspeeds Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Greninja, which are threats to Rock teams. Hisuian Arcanine is able to deal massive damage, OHKOing Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Heatran, Mega Gallade, and Corviknight after Stealth Rock.

Flame Orb.description:
Trailblaze lets Heracross get around ordinary revenge killers such as Rotom-Heat and Choice Scarf Florges. Swords Dance is better if Heracross wishes to focus purely on wallbreaking, allowing it to push past physically bulky foes like Palossand. Megahorn slams walls like Vileplume and Amoonguss without requiring Heracross to Terastallize or set up.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

Choice Scarf.description:
Spikes can be used to capitalize on the switches Heracross forces, though Megahorn offers strong coverage against the likes of Galarian Slowbro and Venusaur, which can otherwise blank Heracross.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

nu.overview: Heracross offers itself to teams as a strong wallbreaker that can break holes into foes. Its access to Guts allows Heracross to switch in against status attempts from foes like Vaporeon and Amoonguss while giving it an extra power boost. Heracross's above average bulk lets it handle wallbreakers such as Scrafty, Breloom, and Overqwil. Furthermore, Heracross can punish teams that rely on common defensive Pokemon like Bellibolt, Wo-Chien, and Vaporeon. However, it lacks any longevity, making repeatedly switching in difficult for Heracross due to entry hazards and burn damage. Furthermore, Heracross's mediocre Speed tier makes it easily revenge killed by faster Pokemon like Munkidori, Barraskewda, Flamigo, and Choice Scarf Chandelure.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Throat Chop allows Heracross to better handle sound users like Sylveon and Toxtricity, but it prefers to run Knock Off to better handle item-reliant foes like Avalugg and Gligar. Heracross can run a Choice Scarf set with Moxie to outpace faster threats like Kilowattrel and Chandelure, but it's completely outclassed by other Choice Scarf users like Flygon, Munkidori, and Flamigo due to them having a higher Speed stat. Spikes can also be used, making Heracross a solid entry hazard setter with the ability to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from walls like Amoonguss and Avalugg. However, Spikes is very niche, and Heracross prefers to run the Guts set.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: Offensive Flying-types like Flamigo, Tornadus, and Kilowattrel can destroy Heracross with their attacks, but none of them enjoy switching into its Guts-boosted Facade. Defensive Flying-types like Gligar and Altaria can tank its Close Combat; the former can freely set up entry hazards, while the latter can destroy Heracross with Brave Bird. However, neither of them enjoy switching into Knock Off and Facade.

Fire-types: Choice Scarf Chandelure, Infernape, and Paldean Tauros-F can outspeed Heracross and destroy it with their STAB attacks, but they have to be cautious of switching into its powerful attacks.

Psychic-types: Faster Psychic-types like Munkidori, Scream Tail and Meloetta can easily revenge kill Heracross, but none of them enjoy switching directly into Knock Off and Facade. Bulky walls like Galarian Slowbro and Uxie can tank its Close Combat while threatening Heracross back with their attacks or free setup.

Bulk Up.description:
Bulk Up lets Heracross become a threatening setup sweeper and late-game cleaner, capable of taking games with its above-average bulk and great Attack. Knock Off lets Heracross hit Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Galarian Articuno, Munkidori, Chandelure, and Basculegion-M while removing Heavy-Duty Boots from entry hazard-weak foes like Incineroar, Scyther, and Tornadus. Heracross can opt for Earthquake or Megahorn as its final move; Earthquake is coverage for the likes of Klefki as well as Poison-types like Galarian Slowbro, Toxicroak, Overqwil, and Tera Poison users such as Vaporeon and Scrafty. Stone Edge allows Heracross to hit Flying-types such as Tornadus, Altaria, and Scyther, which would otherwise resist its STAB combination. Megahorn, however, gives Heracross a powerful Bug-type STAB move, damaging Fighting resists such as Scream Tail. Leftovers lets Heracross gain extra longevity, while Heavy-Duty Boots can be used on teams that provide little to no entry hazard removal, allowing it to get on the field without taking damage from them. Tera Dragon flips the matchup against Chandelure, Incineroar, and Paldean Tauros-W, but Tera Steel can be used to give Heracross a resistance to Fairy- and Flying-type moves like Moonblast from Sylveon and Brave Bird from Flamigo.

Heracross makes for a good pick on offense teams looking for a Fighting-type sweeper that utilizes its typing and stats well. Heracross finds itself weak to common Fairy- and Flying-type attacks from Sylveon, Flamigo, and Scyther. As such, it appreciates teammates able to handle these threats. Rhyperior in particular is an excellent teammate, helping check the Flying-types that Heracross otherwise struggles with, while Duraludon and Copperajah both set up Stealth Rock while checking the Fairy-types that it struggles with. It also benefits from slow pivots like Vaporeon, Bellibolt, and Incineroar, which help get Heracross on the field safely. Heracross appreciates entry hazard support from Gligar and Klefki to help it clean through weakened teams more easily. Heracross's Knock Off synergizes well with the aforementioned entry hazard setters, removing Heavy-Duty Boots from opposing Pokemon and wearing them down via hazard support. Psychic-types like Galarian Articuno, Reuniclus, and Espeon also benefit from Heracross checking the Dark-types that they struggle with. Ambipom and Cinccino benefit from Heracross dealing with foes such as Scrafty and Steel-types including Copperajah and Duraludon, both of which they struggle to deal with.

Guts Wallbreaker.description:
Set Details

Knock Off is good coverage against Ghost-types like Chandelure and Decidueye as well as Psychic-types like Galarian Slowbro and Uxie that also threatens Pokemon heavily reliant on their held items like Incineroar, Kilowattrel, and Porygon2. Facade synergizes well with Guts, allowing Heracross to put major damage on foes that resist its Close Combat like Toxicroak, Amoonguss, and Sylveon. Trailblaze lets it outpace foes like Kilowattrel and Infernape after one use, whereas Megahorn can hit Grass- and Psychic-types like Tsareena and Meloetta. Alternatively, Heracross can opt to run Swords Dance, which makes it a terrifying setup sweeper. Tera Dark boosts the power of Knock Off while giving Heracross a useful Psychic-type immunity against foes like Munkidori and Galarian Articuno. Tera Normal gives Facade an extra power boost, allowing it to 2HKO defensive tanks like Galarian Slowbro and Amoonguss, while giving Heracross a useful immunity to Ghost-type attacks from Chandelure and Decidueye.

Heracross partners well with Fire-resistant Pokemon like Incineroar, Vaporeon, and Basculegion-M, as they handle Fire-types such as Chandelure and Paldean Tauros-F. Pivots like Flygon, Munkidori, and Inteleon can bring in threats Heracross can easily take advantage of like Amoonguss, Copperajah, and Vaporeon while also helping Heracross activate its Flame Orb safely. Additionally, slow pivots like Swampert, Bellibolt, and Incineroar can help Heracross enter the field and activate its Flame Orb safely. Steel-types like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Duraludon are great partners, since they can handle Flying- and Psychic-types like Tornadus and Munkidori. Heracross synergizes with other wallbreakers like Flygon, Barraskewda, and Munkidori to overwhelm defensive tanks like Amoonguss, Bronzong, and Rhyperior. Entry hazard removers like Avalugg, Tsareena, and Altaria help it avoid getting pressured when switching into hazards.

Swords Dance.description: Mega Heracross uses its gigantic Attack stat alongside Swords Dance to be a powerful wallbreaker, pressuring common physical walls like Skarmory and Mega Venusaur. Swords Dance boosts Mega Heracross's Attack to incredible heights and lets it OHKO a majority of the Pokemon in the tier, including walls like Skarmory and Hippowdon. Close Combat OHKOes threats like Tyranitar while 2HKOing bulkier Pokemon like Skarmory. Rock Blast threatens Flying-types such as Enamorus, Galarian Moltres, and Thundurus, as well as Fire-types like Iron Moth that could otherwise take Close Combat and force Mega Heracross out. Pin Missile threatens Slowbro and Mega Venusaur, while Substitute lets Mega Heracross avoid Will-O-Wisp from Mega Sableye, capitalize from the forced switches it generates, and ease prediction against Pokemon it forces out. Physical cleaners like Swords Dance Scizor appreciate Mega Heracross being able to threaten their switch-ins, such as Skarmory and Mega Venusaur, allowing them to sweep late-game. Mega Heracross is prone to being revenge killed by faster threats like Alakazam, Iron Moth, and Enamorus, so teammates that can deal with them such as Tyranitar and Celesteela, respectively, are appreciated. Fire-type partners like Victini and Iron Moth can threaten Buzzwole, which walls Mega Heracross; Poison-types like Amoonguss can threaten Fairy-types like Unaware Clefable, which also wall it.

All-out-Attacker.description: All-out attacker Mega Heracross functions as an incredible wallbreaker, being able to threaten common defensive staples such as Mega Venusaur, Celesteela and Slowbro with its fear-inducing Pin Missile and Close Combat off of its gargantuan base Attack stat. However, its poor typing and mediocre Speed cause it to be easily chipped down throughout the course of a game and forced out on many occasions. In addition, there are switch-ins to Mega Heracross, such as Buzzwole, that limit the damage it can do each time it switches in, as well as competition in the form of Buzzwole that can outlast it and deal more damage over the course of a game. Despite these flaws, though, Mega Heracross carves out a solid niche for itself in the NDUU metagame thanks to its raw power. Rock Blast nails the few Pokemon that resist both of Mega Heracross's STAB moves like Enamorus, Iron Moth, and Blacephalon. The final slot is interchangeable: Earthquake allows Mega Heracross to hit Aegislash, which otherwise would wall this set, while Trailblaze lets Mega Heracross patch up its middling Speed, outspeeding the likes of Alakazam and Mega Latias at +1, at the cost of being completely walled by Aegislash. Mega Heracross fits on balance teams that appreciate its ability to force tons of damage onto any foe and ease late-game cleanup. Hazard removers such as Excadrill and Defog Rotom-W allow Mega Heracross to find switch in opportunities without fearing Spikes set by Mew or Skarmory, while both help Mega Heracross in additional ways: Excadrill serves as a temporary stopgap to Fairy-types like Choice Scarf Enamorus and Clefable and scares Aegislash, while Rotom-W provides pivot opportunities for Mega Heracross to come in and wreak havoc. Celesteela is another great partner, as it is a far sturdier Fairy resistance alongside chip damage in the form of Leech Seed or cleaning potential with Autotomize; it also deals with Buzzwole, a major hurdle for Mega Heracross.

monotype.overview:
Bug

Heracross finds a niche as a physical wallbreaker, leveraging its Fighting typing and Guts to alleviate Rock and Steel matchups while also dismantling Poison team cores with its combination of Swords Dance + Guts-boosted Facade; however, due to that same typing and its below average Speed, it struggles against common Fairy- and Psychic-types like Iron Valiant and Latios and is a less-than-ideal choice. Furthermore, Heracross faces direct competition for its role from Life Orb Slither Wing, which also has U-turn and has access to reliable recovery. Heracross is also outclassed by other physical attackers like Scizor and Lokix, both possessing crucial priority options, with Scizor also being more adept at handling Rock and Fairy teams. Lastly, Volcarona, with its Fire typing and access to Quiver Dance, serves as a powerful special wallbreaker, outclassing Heracross as an answer to Steel-types barring Heatran.

Guts Attacker (Bug).description:
Heracross is a niche wallbreaker for Bug teams by virtue of its high Attack, Fighting typing, Swords Dance, and the ability Guts, capable of easing Rock, Steel, and Poison matchups. Close Combat eliminates Rock- and Steel-types like Tyranitar and Heatran and, when at +2, allows Heracross to break through walls like Skarmory, Mandibuzz, and Great Tusk. Facade complements Close Combat by targeting Flying-, Fairy-, and Poison-types, outright OHKOing Gliscor and Primarina at +2 and OHKOing Galarian Weezing and Toxapex at +2 after minimal chip damage. Knock Off threatens Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo and Slowbro, and it removes Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots from the aforementioned walls, wearing them down, which is especially helpful if Heracross opts to use Trailblaze as its fourth move. Trailblaze allows Heracross to outspeed faster foes like Ogerpon formes, Latios, and Choice Scarf Heatran, making it an excellent late-game cleaner. However, without Swords Dance, Heracross struggles to break walls like Toxapex, Galarian Weezing, and Iron Defense Skarmory.

Choice Scarf Kleavor is an essential teammate, serving as a revenge killer and utilizing its Rock typing to eliminate pesky Fire- and Flying-types like Ogerpon-H, Ninetales, Tornadus-T, and Dragonite, which pose a serious threat to Bug teams, while simultaneously setting Stealth Rock with Stone Axe. Araquanid provides Sticky Web support, which allows Heracross to outspeed would-be faster foes like the Ogerpon formes, Dragapult, and, when at +1, even Choice Scarf users like Meowscarada and Greninja. Araquanid can also take advantage of its superb special bulk and Fire resistance provided by Water Bubble to take on Fire-types like Volcarona and Iron Moth. Additionally, Araquanid can use Mirror Coat to get a surprise OHKO on foes like Choice Specs Latios and Flutter Mane. Scizor and Lokix cover Heracross's weaknesses; Scizor eliminates Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Iron Valiant, while Lokix threatens Psychic- and Ghost-types like Latios and Dragapult; both teammates also deal with faster Rock-types like Iron Boulder and Ogerpon-C, which Heracross might struggle against. In return, Heracross can handle physical walls like Archaludon, Toxapex, and Mandibuzz. Forretress sets entry hazards, provides safe entry to Heracross with its slow Volt Switch, and removes hazards with Rapid Spin. Heracross's ability to break through special walls like Alolan Muk, Heatran, and Hisuian Goodra is greatly appreciated by teammates like Volcarona and Frosmoth. In return, Volcarona can spread burns to weaken physical attackers like Dragonite and Zamazenta, and Frosmoth can eliminate Flying-, Ground-, Dragon-types like Zapdos, Hippowdon, and Dragonite.

Wreck-It Ralph (Wallbreaker) (Bug).description: Sporting the highest Attack stat in the entire metagame, boosting capabilities with Swords Dance, and a great ability in Skill Link, Mega Heracross makes for a monstrous wallbreaker on Bug teams, blowing past numerous troublesome foes with its nuclear Fighting-type STAB moves, such as Ursaluna, Ting-Lu, and bulky Heatran variants. Earthquake is good coverage for foes that resist Mega Heracross's Close Combat, such as Toxapex, Clodsire, and Gholdengo. Rock Blast allows Mega Heracross to hit numerous Flying-types that don't care about Close Combat or Earthquake, such as bulky Zapdos variants and Pelipper. Swords Dance enables Mega Heracross to boost its damage output to even further heights, granting it OHKO chances that it wouldn't otherwise achieve, like on Gliscor via Rock Blast, as well as Skarmory and Celesteela with Close Combat. Alternatively, Bullet Seed is a powerful option to quickly remove threats like Mega Swampert and Rotom-Wash before they have a chance to threaten the rest of Mega Heracross's team. Moxie is the best available pre-Mega ability, as it can potentially allow Mega Heracross to gain attack boosts without taking a setup turn. With an Adamant nature, Mega Heracross guarantees a 2HKO on Skarmory with Close Combat after Stealth Rock damage. Ribombee can set up Sticky Web to help shore up Mega Heracross's middling Speed tier, and it also pressures certain Dragon-types like Latios, Latias, and Kommo-o that would otherwise threaten Mega Heracross. Scizor uses its excellent typing as well as access to STAB Bullet Punch and U-turn to assist Mega Heracross against threatening Fairy- and Psychic-types like Iron Valiant, Mega Diancie, non-Hidden Power Fire Tapu Lele, and Mega Gallade. Kleavor sets up Stealth Rock for Mega Heracross, allowing it to more easily dispatch common foes like Archaludon and Skarmory. Additionally, Kleavor threatens both Mega Charizard formes when holding a Choice Scarf, both of which would otherwise erase Mega Heracross. Lokix leverages its typing and ability to help Mega Heracross, as its STAB moves allow it to break past bulky Psychic-types for Mega Heracross such as Slowbro, and its Tinted Lens allows it to smash other walls like Tapu Fini after a Swords Dance boost. Volcarona appreciates Mega Heracross shattering checks to it such as Blissey, Alolan Muk, and Iron Hands, allowing for an easier late-game sweep with Quiver Dance. In return, Volcarona can destroy Mega Scizor and Mega Pidgeot after a Quiver Dance, both of whom pose a threat to Mega Heracross with their Flying-type attacking options in Dual Wingbeat and Hurricane, respectively.

Swords Dance.description:
Sneasel is an effective Swords Dance sweeper in PU thanks to its incredible STAB combination alongside a decent Attack stat, which both let it hit threats such as Espeon, Hisuian Decidueye, and Delphox, and a great Speed tier that allows it to outspeed all of the previously mentioned Pokemon. With Knock Off, Sneasel can hinder common switch-ins such as Paldean Tauros-F and Hariyama by removing their items. Ice Shard is useful to pick off Choice Scarf users such as Florges and Pawmot while also stopping setup sweepers like Oricorio-F and Jolteon. While Heavy-Duty Boots is generally preferred due to Sneasel's Stealth Rock weakness, Life Orb is an option on some hyper offense teams to allow Sneasel to ensure rolls such as OHKOing Calm Mind Florges and Rhydon at +2. Inner Focus is chosen as Sneasel's ability, as the immunity to Fake Out and Intimidate is helpful against Ambipom, Arcanine, and Paldean Tauros-F. In terms of Tera type, Tera Ice boosts the power of Triple Axel to nuclear levels, allowing Sneasel to OHKO Mudsdale after a Swords Dance and 2HKO even Pokemon that resist Ice-type moves, like Arcanine and Qwilfish. It also boosts Ice Shard to make Sneasel a more reliable revenge killer. Alternatively, Tera Ghost benefits Sneasel defensively by giving it immunity to priority such as Arcanine's Extreme Speed and Pawmot's Mach Punch while allowing it to set up in the face of Pokemon that would otherwise threaten it out, like the aforementioned Pawmot and Choice item-locked Paldean Tauros-F.

Sneasel is used almost exclusively on offense and hyper offense teams as a secondary sweeper and cleaner and is usually paired with another sweeper like Arcanine or Espeon to help it in its sweep. Espeon's Magic Bounce also comes in handy if Sneasel is running Life Orb. Sneasel's ability to rip holes through common Ground- and Grass-types like Mudsdale, Rhydon, and Venusaur helps enable teammates such as Rotom-H, Salazzle, and Golurk to more easily steamroll an opposing team. Since Sneasel's poor defenses keep it from coming in safely, offensive pivots that can bring it onto the battlefield like Jolteon, Ambipom, and Bruxish are excellent teammates. Even after a Swords Dance, Sneasel still needs help chipping walls like Milotic and Terastallized Rhydon so they can be in range of its attacks. As such, Goodra and Delphox are excellent teammates in this role.

Choice Band.description:
Despite its NFE status, Sneasel is a real threat in PU due to it being one of the fastest Pokemon in the tier. When holding Choice Band, Sneasel packs a punch with its relatively high Attack stat and can break through even some of the best walls in the tier such as Venusaur and Amoonguss with Triple Axel. Ice Shard helps Sneasel by KOing low-HP foes such as sweepers like Espeon and Oricorio, or getting damage on faster Pokemon such as Hisuian Electrode and Choice Scarf Zoroark. Low Kick allows Sneasel to hit Steel- and Dark-types such as Alolan Sandslash and Alolan Persian for good damage. Sneasel typically runs Tera Ice to amplify the power of Triple Axel and Ice Shard, making it so that Triple Axel always OHKOes Florges no matter how much bulk it has invested. Tera Dark also benefits Sneasel by removing its weakness to Stealth Rock and Fire-type moves.

Sneasel typically appears on teams ranging from hyper offense to bulky offense, where it acts as a wallbreaker alongside Pokemon such as Paldean Tauros-F and Hoopa. Sneasel benefits these partners by providing chip damage on opposing Pokemon such as Florges and Amoonguss, while also removing their item, making them easier to deal with for the rest of the team. Sneasel likes partners that can deal with Fighting- and Fire-type Pokemon such as Paldean-Tauros-F, Delphox, and Arcanine; such partners include Espeon, Bruxish, and Hisuian Braviary. However, even with a Choice Band, Sneasel still can't muscle through bulkier walls such as Milotic and Qwilfish, so Sneasel enjoys having partners that check them such as Pawmot and Palossand, respectively. When using Sneasel, entry hazard control is imperative, as it cannot function well without it, so having teammates such as Espeon, Tatsugiri and Alolan Sandslash really help Sneasel. Sneasel profits off having other wallbreakers such as Dudunsparce and Arcanine, since it can often struggle to OHKO opposing Pokemon. Since Sneasel is so frail, it really enjoys having teammates that are slow pivots so Sneasel can safely get in to threaten opposing Pokemon such as Florges, Hariyama and Goodra. Some such teammates are Uxie, Milotic, and Frosmoth.

zu.overview: With its blisteringly fast Speed and a deadly STAB combination, Sneasel carves a place for itself in ZU as a powerful wallbreaker and cleaner. STAB Knock Off makes Sneasel excellent at forcing progress, especially since the primary Knock Off absorber, Dipplin, fears its Ice-type attacks, and it outruns many already fast threats like Charizard and Virizion. However, Sneasel's paper-thin defenses mean it crumples to most strong neutral attacks and, combined with its many weaknesses, give it near to no defensive utility outside of switching into Psychic-type attacks. Sneasel also can be left wanting in power and struggles to break past walls like Regirock and Orthworm. Choice Band sets don't have this problem but are vulnerable to entry hazards and very prediction reliant. Lastly, Sneasel is incredibly vulnerable to getting revenge killed by most Choice Scarf users in the tier, like Primeape, Sneasel-Hisui, and Typhlosion, as well as priority attacks such as Mach Punch from Hitmontop.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Sneasel has no other options.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Sneasel greatly fears Fighting-types like Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel. Most of them don't enjoy switching in on Sneasel's attacks, however, though Poliwrath resists Sneasel's STAB moves and doesn't take much damage from Low Kick.

Choice Scarf Users: Sneasel's lack of bulk means that Choice Scarf users have an easy time outspeeding it and taking it out. All of Hisuian Sneasel, Primeape, and Mesprit can revenge kill Sneasel with ease.

Physical Walls: Physically bulky Pokemon like Regirock, Orthworm, and Weezing don't fear much from Sneasel and can force it out with status conditions or super effective attacks. However, since all three of them lack reliable recovery, and the former two hate losing Leftovers, Sneasel can slowly wear them down over a longer game. All of them except Weezing also must be wary of Low Kick.

Fast Attacker.description:
Ice Shard lets Sneasel pick off weakened foes and faster attackers like Whimsicott and Jolteon as well as dance around priority like Mach Punch from Hitmonchan. Swords Dance lets Sneasel pick up OHKOs on Charizard and Dipplin and gives it an easier time cleaning up weakened teams, while Low Kick lets it threaten Orthworm and Regirock more immediately. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Sneasel come in without taking damage from entry hazards, allowing it to come in many times over the course of a game. Tera Ice boosts Triple Axel and Ice Shard's power immensely, netting a 2HKO on Regirock and Weezing at +2, but does nothing to help Sneasel's terrible defensive typing. Tera Ghost flips Sneasel's Fighting weakness into an immunity, letting it blank Close Combat from revenge killers like Choice Scarf Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel.

Sneasel's powerful Knock Off makes it an excellent pick on entry hazard stacking teams where teammates such as Sandslash and Orthworm help Sneasel push past bulkier foes like Magneton and Poliwrath. Sneasel struggles to break past physically bulky foes like Regirock, Orthworm, and Weezing, so teammates that share these checks like Charizard, Mesprit, and Virizion, respectively, can team up to wear down said walls. Poliwrath notably takes little damage from Sneasel's STAB attacks, so teammates that handle it like Whimsicott and Venusaur are quite helpful. Physical wallbreakers like Lycanroc and Swords Dance Charizard also help wear walls down so Sneasel can sweep. Fighting-types like Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel threaten Sneasel immensely, so defensive fallbacks like Weezing make for great teammates. Other defensive teammates such as Venusaur and Poliwrath help make up for Sneasel's lack of defenses, dealing with threats like Whimsicott and Typhlosion for it. As Sneasel struggles to switch in directly, pivots like Jolteon, Primeape, and Whimsicott are all helpful in assisting Sneasel to hit the field safely. On more offensive teams, it can pair up with other setup sweepers like Toxicroak and Mesprit to overwhelm the opposing team.

Choice Band.description:
Sneasel has very strong STAB moves and a great Speed tier to spam them. A Choice Band gives Sneasel the immediate raw power to make quick offensive progress against bulky Pokemon like Orthworm and Regirock. Choice Band also makes Sneasel a more reliable revenge killer to offensive threats like Charizard, Nasty Plot Mesprit, and Virizion. Low Kick is Sneasel's strongest move against physically bulky Pokemon like Regirock and Orthworm, which take neutral or resisted damage from its STAB moves, but its limited coverage and variable power make it a difficult option to lock into. Tera Ice cranks up the power of Sneasel's strongest STAB move to ice out bulkier Pokemon such as Tera Fairy Nasty Plot Mesprit and Weezing. Tera Ice also boosts Sneasel's priority to more effectively pick off Jolteon and Whimsicott.

Choice Band Sneasel has great immediate damage output, quickly cutting through teams with Triple Axel and making progress with Knock Off. Choice Band Sneasel's ability to lure in and remove Leftovers from Regirock makes it a great enabler to offensive Pokemon that struggle against it such as Charizard and Minior, and it functions similarly against Orthworm to support Mesprit and Whimsicott. Knock Off removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes creates excellent synergy with entry hazard setting Pokemon such as Sandslash and Orthworm. Choice Band Sneasel is vulnerable to being worn down by entry hazards, particularly Stealth Rock, so hazard removers like Sandslash and Lurantis are critical to maximizing Sneasel's offensive presence. Defensive pivots like Eelektross and Mesprit can bring Sneasel in safely in spite of its poor bulk and vulnerable defensive typing. While Sneasel resists Shadow Sneak and Sucker Punch from foes like Muk and Hitmontop, its frailty leaves it prone to strong and super effective priority users; Sandaconda and Weezing can check Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel for Sneasel. Choice Band Sneasel is fast but still struggles with revenge killers like Primeape, Choice Specs, and Choice Scarf Typhlosion, which can be respectively handled by teammates like Orthworm, Weezing, and Regirock.

zu.overview: Hisuian Sneasel is a powerful and versatile threat in ZU, leveraging its excellent Speed tier and powerful STAB attacks to great effect. Not much in the metagame can withstand its potent Close Combat and Gunk Shot combination, and those that can, like Mesprit and Froslass, are threatened by Throat Chop. With Switcheroo to disrupt foes that otherwise give it issues, like Iron Defense Regirock, Hisuian Sneasel has the tools to position itself to wreak havoc. Swords Dance Hisuian Sneasel can utilize Trailblaze to become a devastatingly fast and powerful late-game cleaner. It does, however, have subpar bulk without Eviolite and can struggle at times to pick up KOs against premiere walls like Dipplin and Regirock if they use Terastallization. Hisuian Sneasel's weaknesses to common types like Flying, Ground, and Psychic mean it struggles to hit the field safely and use its offensive traits to great success against notable foes like Charizard, Sandslash, and offensive Mesprit.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Hisuian Sneasel has access to Toxic Spikes, which can cause disruption without needing to swap items with Switcheroo. Toxic, similarly, can be used to reliably status checks Hisuian Sneasel can't normally get past, such as Spiritomb. Taunt can be used to stop slower setup sweepers like Mesprit or prevent recovery attempts from foes like Dipplin and Muk, though it is difficult to use given how frail Hisuian Sneasel is.

Checks and Counters

Psychic-types: Mesprit is a notable Hisuian Sneasel check with the bulk to withstand its powerful attacks and the ability to threaten it with an OHKO back. Farigiraf is similarly difficult for it to deal with.

Ghost-types: Spiritomb can sponge Hisuian Sneasel's attacks and threaten it back with Psyshock. Tera Ghost users like Magneton can also use their brute power to threaten an OHKO against it.

Faster Revenge Killers and Wallbreakers: Despite its excellent Speed tier, non-Choice Scarf Hisuian Sneasel is slower than common Choice Scarf users like Primeape and Mesprit, which can threaten it immensely with Earthquake and Psychic Noise, respectively. Likewise, Choice Specs Jolteon is able to pick Hisuian Sneasel off cleanly with Thunderbolt.

Poison-types: Weezing can reliably sponge attacks from Hisuian Sneasel and threaten to disrupt it with Will-O-Wisp. Muk is less reliable as a check but can nail it with Zen Headbutt after tanking an attack. Tera Poison Dipplin can stonewall Hisuian Sneasel with Sticky Hold to prevent disruption from Switcheroo and the ability to phaze it with Dragon Tail to stop setup attempts. Likewise, Tera Poison Regirock can use IronPress against Hisuian Sneasel to great effect, threatening to reverse sweep after just one boost.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Hisuian Sneasel is a great setup sweeper in the ZU metagame, capable of blowing through teams as a late-game sweeper thanks to its strong STAB moves and good typing. Throat Chop provides the coverage to hit foes like Mesprit and Muk hard, preventing the former from hitting it back with Psychic Noise; Trailblaze, alternatively, can allow Hisuian Sneasel to outpace the entire metagame after one boost to more consistently threaten a sweep. Hitmontop. Tera Dark can stop Psychic-type attacks from halting a sweep, as well as boost Throat Chop tremendously, securing an OHKO on offensive Mesprit after a Swords Dance. Tera Dark also prevents niche Prankster users like Sableye from disrupting a potential sweep. Tera Grass, meanwhile, flips the weakness to Ground and allows Hisuian Sneasel to set up against foes like Sandslash.

With its prolific Speed tier and snowballing ability, Swords Dance Hisuian Sneasel is a great fit on bulky offense and offense teams alike. Teammates that can provide entry hazards to chip down walls like Dipplin and Sandslash are much appreciated; on offensive teams, Primeape is a great lead, while on bulky offense teams, Mesprit and Orthworm provide Hisuian Sneasel hazards and reliable defensive pivots, if needed. Teammates that can lure in foes like Arboliva and Dipplin that Hisuian Sneasel can set up against include VoltTurn users like Magneton and Mesprit. Jolteon is another notable teammate, capable of setting up for its own sweep and flexibly pivoting into Hisuian Sneasel. Other setup sweepers like Mesprit, Farigiraf, and Jolteon are great teammates, similarly helping break the opposition down for Hisuian Sneasel or taking advantage of worn down foes themselves to clean late-game. Vikavolt is a powerful support option, helping check Mesprit and providing Sticky Web so Hisuian Sneasel can outpace Choice Scarf users like Primeape and Mesprit. Other physical wallbreakers that can wear down shared checks include Virizion, which can help break down foes like Sandaconda and Sandslash that Hisuian Sneasel usually struggles with.

Choice Item.description:
Hisuian Sneasel is an exceptional wielder of Choice items, with its high Speed, coveted access to Switcheroo, and hard-hitting STAB attacks in Close Combat and Gunk Shot. Throat Chop provides Hisuian Sneasel a powerful attack to break past Ghost-types like Froslass, as well as threatening big damage against Psychic-types like Farigiraf and Mesprit, even blocking Psychic Noise; Swords Dance is an alternative that gives Hisuian Sneasel the capacity to function as a setup sweeper after it has shed its item. Switcheroo is a big reason Choice item sets function so well, as it can disrupt common switch-ins like Sandslash immensely.
