Choice Band grants Hisuian Sneasel the damage output needed to pick up 2HKOs on notable foes like Dipplin and Mesprit; Choice Scarf sets, on the other hand, trade power for Speed, turning Hisuian Sneasel into the fastest late-game cleaner and revenge killer, which is useful against usually speedier foes like Jolteon and Whimsicott. Tera Fighting boosts Close Combat tremendously, with Choice Band sets being capable of OHKOing Farigiraf, while also removing Hisuian Sneasel's weakness to Ground. Tera Dark grants Hisuian Sneasel a useful immunity to Psychic while making Throat Chop far more difficult to stomach for foes like Mesprit. Tera Dark also blocks Prankster from affecting Hisuian Sneasel, turning foes like Sableye and the more niche Volbeat into setup fodder.

A natural fit on bulky offense and balance teams, Hisuian Sneasel is a great choice as a Choice Band wallbreaker or Choice Scarf cleaner. Given Choice Band Hisuian Sneasel's propensity to blow holes in teams and force switches every time it hits the field, teammates that can help wear down walls like Dipplin, Regirock, and Spiritomb with entry hazards are much appreciated; Orthworm and Sandslash are great Spikes setters, and Mesprit is a notable Stealth Rock setter and pivot option. Choice Scarf Hisuian Sneasel appreciates other wallbreaker teammates that can enable it to pull off a late-game sweep, such as Choice Specs Magneton and Nasty Plot Spiritomb. Teammates that can help keep Charizard and Mesprit in check, like Naclstack, are valuable to provide defensive pivots for Hisuian Sneasel. Poison-type foes like Muk and Weezing can be difficult for Hisuian Sneasel to break through consistently, making Psychic-type partners like Farigiraf and Mesprit especially valuable. Similarly, Spiritomb can sponge Hisuian Sneasel's hits comfortably and use it as setup fodder, which makes Whimsicott valuable to threaten it back. Choice Band Hisuian Sneasel pairs well with setup sweepers like Swords Dance Virizion, as it can break holes in teams for Virizion to clean late-game or vice versa.

nfe.overview: With its impressive stats, versatile movepool, good typing, and notable ability, Piloswine cements itself as one of the premier staples of the metagame. All these traits allow it to function as an excellent wallbreaker, entry hazard setter, revenge killer, and Thunder Wave absorber. As a hazard setter, being unsusceptible to Taunt owing to its ability is a major plus point. While Eviolite provides bulk and flexibility, Choice Band enables Piloswine to capitalize on its unresisted STAB combination to dismantle opposing teams. However, despite its strength and bulk, it lacks longevity due to the absence of non-Rest recovery moves and faces competition from other Stealth Rock setters like Tinkatuff and Dunsparce, which have relatively better longevity, better matchup against the tier's premier hazard removal option in Quaxwell, and greater overall utility.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Trailblaze over Ice Shard or Stealth Rock with more Speed EVs is an option for Piloswine. For instance, it outspeeds Frogadier at +2 with 104 Speed EVs. Trailblaze transforms Piloswine into a good late-game cleaner, potentially bypassing checks like Thwackey at low HP and picking off foes like Monferno. This alternative also helps it in winning mirror matchups. However, if one drops Stealth Rock, it's advisable to run another setter like Tinkatuff, or if one drops Ice Shard, consider other revenge killers like Thwackey and Choice Scarf Frogadier. Similarly, Curse is an option over Stealth Rock, making Piloswine a dangerous late-game cleaner and enabling it to beat its former checks such as Thwackey and Raboot. Choice Scarf sets can surprise faster checks like Pignite, Monferno, and Frogadier that would otherwise revenge kill it.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Quaxwell can switch into any move from Piloswine and use Rapid Spin to remove Stealth Rock. It can do so multiple times thanks to Roost and threatens Piloswine out with its STAB moves. Other Water-types like Wartortle and Frogadier can check Piloswine with their STAB attacks too. Wartortle also has Rapid Spin to remove Stealth Rock and is bulky enough to switch into Piloswine once or twice; Frogadier is relatively frailer but stronger.

Wallbreakers and Revenge Killers: Thwackey can check Piloswine, but it usually needs support to get Piloswine weakened to Grassy Glide range, generally with Knock Off, strong super effective moves, or pivoting moves, as it would rather not risk Wood Hammer. Raboot, Monferno, and Pignite heavily damage Piloswine with their Fighting-type moves. Pokemon such as Choice Specs Girafarig, Servine, and Pawniard do a decent job in picking Piloswine off.

Dunsparce: Dunsparce is physically bulky enough to easily take all of Piloswine's STAB moves with impunity. Dunsparce cripples Piloswine with Toxic and can recover the damage off with Roost.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description:
Piloswine's strong matchups against the tier's other dominant entry hazard setters, such as Tinkatuff and Koffing, and the tier's premier Defogger, Vullaby, allow it to excel as a highly effective Stealth Rock setter. As a wallbreaker, its unresisted STAB combination is extremely threatening to unprepared teams and those that have been weakened by Knock Off, hazards, or other residual damage. High Horsepower allows Piloswine to work effectively even in Grassy Terrain, but Earthquake is also a viable alternative due to its extra power and accuracy. Ice Shard allows Piloswine to pick off weakened threats like Girafarig and Fraxure.

Piloswine is a strong fit for most archetypes, and it's especially effective on bulky offense and balance teams. Drakloak is a good teammate for Piloswine; its spinblocking ability, which allows it to handle Quaxwell, complements Piloswine's Stealth Rock setting perfectly. In addition, Drakloak can spread status to support Piloswine's wallbreaking or work in tandem with it to dismantle the opposing team through pivoting. Frogadier is also a superb partner, forming an entry hazard-stacking core with Piloswine; moreover, it provides pivoting support to Piloswine, creating valuable entry opportunities. In a similar vein, Koffing sets Toxic Spikes to maximize hazard pressure; it also acts as a great switch-in to many foes that Piloswine is weak to, handling Grass-types like Thwackey and Servine and absorbing Fighting-type moves from threats like Raboot, Monferno, and Pignite. In general, wallbreakers and cleaners appreciate Piloswine's Stealth Rock support and offensive pressure; Thwackey, Girafarig, Fraxure, and Raboot synergize extremely well with Piloswine, working hand in hand with it to dismantle defensive cores, which may include Pokemon like Dunsparce, Ivysaur, Quaxwell, and Koffing. Thwackey, in particular, is an excellent teammate for Piloswine, dealing with pesky Water-types that check Piloswine, namely Quaxwell, Wartortle, and Frogadier. Thwackey also offers invaluable Knock Off, pivoting, and passive recovery support, bolstering Piloswine's wallbreaking prowess and longevity. In return, Piloswine deals with foes that can prove to be problematic for Thwackey, such as Koffing, Vullaby, and Tinkatuff. Piloswine appreciates Knock Off support a ton; thus, Knock Off users such as Monferno, Pignite, and Ivysaur make amazing teammates, pairing nicely with Piloswine and amplifying its offensive pressure, even allowing it to reach thresholds like 2HKOing maximum Defense Quaxwell that has lost its Eviolite with minimum chip damage. Defensively, Quaxwell is a remarkable teammate, providing Rapid Spin support to ensure Piloswine's side of the field is free of hazards, thus maximizing hazard pressure on the opposing team. Quaxwell also acts as a switch-in to multiple Pokemon that Piloswine can struggle against, especially if it's chipped or if its Eviolite has been removed by Knock Off, such as Frogadier, Pignite, Monferno, and Raboot; in exchange, Piloswine can deal with foes that Quaxwell is weak to, like Drakloak, Fraxure, and Girafarig. Wartortle is also a good teammate in this regard, though it has less longevity, which is a fair trade for the added offensive pressure. Ivysaur defensively takes care of Grass- and Water-types like Thwackey and Quaxwell for Piloswine, while Piloswine takes care of threats like Girafarig and Tinkatuff.

Choice Band.description:
Thanks to its insane Attack and amazing movepool, Choice Band Piloswine is one of the deadliest wallbreakers and revenge killers of the metagame. High Horsepower is the preferred move under Thwackey's Grassy Terrain, while Earthquake serves as a more consistent option outside of it. Ice Shard picks off foes like Fraxure, Gabite, and low-HP Girafarig. 124 Speed EVs ensure Piloswine outspeeds Quaxwell without Speed investment. Maximum Attack and Speed investment can also be used to not risk Speed tier shenanigans.

Piloswine fits on bulky offense and balance teams. It is best paired with entry hazard setters like Tinkatuff, Frogadier, and Koffing to relentlessly pressure foes like Quaxwell and wallbreak as effectively as possible. Tinkatuff and Koffing also act as Knock Off absorbers, aiding Piloswine in keeping its Choice Band, and they also check Grass-types like Thwackey, Ivysaur, and Servine. Tinkatuff can also try to steal Quaxwell's Eviolite with Pickpocket, invalidating it as a potential Piloswine answer. Monferno and Pignite provide Knock Off support and offensively pressure Quaxwell structures Piloswine may face some difficulty against. Special stallbreakers and wallbreakers such as Servine and Choice Specs Girafarig can work in tandem with Piloswine to dismantle opposing defensive cores with Pokemon like Quaxwell, Dunsparce, Ivysaur, and Tinkatuff. Thwackey and Ivysaur check pesky Water-types that check Piloswine, namely Frogadier, Wartortle, and Quaxwell, while also providing Knock Off support and, in Thwackey's case, passive recovery. In return, Piloswine handles Tinkatuff and Vullaby for them. Piloswine likes taking as little chip damage as possible, so hazard control options such as Quaxwell, Wartortle, and Vullaby are appreciated. Fraxure can take advantage of the holes Piloswine blows into opposing teams to set up and sweep. Servine is also an excellent partner for similar reasons and aids Piloswine by checking Water-types and providing Glare support, potentially mitigating its issue of having mediocre Speed. Pikachu also checks Water-types and provides Volt Switch support to Piloswine, bringing it in on forced switches and enabling its wallbreaking.

Specially Defensive Wall (Ice).description: Piloswine is one of Ice teams' best specially defensive walls, capable of filling some of Ice teams' biggest roles of being an entry hazard setter and Electric immunity. Thick Fat coupled with Eviolite gives Piloswine tremendous bulk, with which it can check dangerous Fire-type threats to Ice such as Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y by disposing of them with Rock Slide. 12 EVs in Attack guarantees an OHKO on offensive Volcarona. Another one of Piloswine's amazing traits is its Ground typing, which makes it a great asset in the Electric matchup by preventing a Volt Switch onslaught while also letting it hit Electric-types super effectively with STAB Earthquake. Toxic is an option to put defensive switch-ins such as Skeledirge and Rotom-W on a timer, helping Piloswine's teammates overpower them, but Roar is an alternative choice to force out threats that may use it to set up, such as Mega Scizor, and to rack up hazard damage from its Stealth Rock and Cloyster's Spikes to wear down threats such as Urshifu-R and Mega Venusaur. Piloswine appreciates Alolan Ninetales's snow and Aurora Veil, which let it wall the opposition more easily. Piloswine is, however, extremely vulnerable to Water-types, so partnering it with Kyurem or Arctozolt is appreciated, as they can easily break Water teams. Substitute Baxcalibur also threatens Poison teams, which can cripple Piloswine with Toxic. Weavile with a Z-Crystal is also a good Knock Off absorber for Piloswine, as losing Eviolite ruins Piloswine; Weavile also forces immense progress by removing key items from Celesteela and Skeledirge, which become susceptible to Stealth Rock afterwards, or outright breaking through them with a Z-Move. Galarian Darmanitan and Shell Smash Cloyster can threaten Steel teams with Flare Blitz and Hydro Pump or Hidden Power Fire, respectively. The Stealth Rocks and Toxic spread by Piloswine also accentuates the breaking power of teammates such as Swords Dance or Dragon Dance Baxcalibur and Belly Drum Cetitan. IronPress Avalugg and defensive Cloyster with Hidden Power Fire are also good partners in being able to shut down Mega Scizor. Avalugg, Articuno, and Cloyster are also capable of removing entry hazards, with the latter two also being able to pivot in Piloswine with U-turn and Teleport, respectively.

Defensive.description: Galarian Corsola walls Choice Specs Kyurem, Nidoking, Mega Diancie, and Mega Charizard Y with its Eviolite-boosted defenses and provides much-needed entry hazards in Stealth Rock for Ghost teams. Night Shade provides Galarian Corsola with a reliable form of damage to threaten these special attackers. Paired with Whirlpool, it has an easier time overcoming these threats, turning 3HKOs into 2HKOs. Mirror Coat allows Galarian Corsola to nab a surprise OHKO on Regieleki and Blacephalon, both of which deal too much damage for it to handle with just Night Shade. Alternatively, Will-O-Wisp makes Galarian Corsola a solid check to physical attackers like Mega Lopunny and provides chip damage, similar to Whirlpool. Strength Sap gives Galarian Corsola a form of recovery and allows it to deal with Choice Band Excadrill and Mega Swampert. As Galarian Corsola is reliant on Eviolite to be a competent wall, Knock Off absorbers like Mega Sableye and Gholdengo with a Z crystal are appreciated. Mega Sableye also spreads burn on the opposing team, which helps Galarian Corsola take on physical attackers, and Gholdengo prevents Defog users like Corviknight from removing the hazards Galarian Corsola sets. Setup sweepers like Sinistcha, Mimikyu, and Ceruledge love Galarian Corsola's ability to handle Landorus, Tapu Lele, and Mega Diancie, and in return, they deal with Mega Swampert, Alolan Muk, and Toxapex, which Galarian Corsola struggles with. Hisuian Zoroark, Gengar, and Blacephalon appreciate the residual damage Galarian Corsola provides with entry hazards, and in return, Hisuian Zoroark provides a Ghost-immune teammate, and Blacephalon and Gengar clean teams late-game.

Water Absorb (Flying).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Mixed Defense.description:
Skarmory leverages its incredible defensive typing and physical bulk to act as an effective entry hazard setter and blanket check to physical attackers like Excadrill, Lokix, and Ogerpon. Body Press lets it target the aforementioned Excadrill as well as Scizor and Tyranitar, preventing them from using it as setup fodder. Brave Bird lets it hit Hydrapple, Conkeldurr, and Lokix for solid damage while letting it check Clodsire better. Whirlwind can instead be used to stop setup sweepers like Zarude and Revavroom in their tracks, as well as accrue chip damage from Spikes on the opposing team. Iron Defense bolsters the power of Body Press while also making Skarmory nigh-impossible to KO with physical attacks. Roost keeps Skarmory healthy, notably letting it retain Sturdy in case it needs to revenge kill or phaze a threat. 48 Speed EVs allow Skarmory to outrun max Speed Modest Hydrapple, letting it punish Choice Specs sets with Brave Bird. Rocky Helmet wears down the physical attackers it checks and punishes U-turns from Pokemon like Mandibuzz and Zarude. Tera Dragon grants Skarmory several useful resistances, including to Fire and Water; this lets it take on the likes of Hisuian Arcanine and Keldeo in a pinch.

Skarmory provides bulky offense and balance teams a reliable Spikes setter and physical wall. Slowking is an incredible defensive partner for Skarmory due to its ability to take on special attackers like Keldeo and Heatran as well as its ability to spread burn with Scald, letting Skarmory wall physical threats better. In return, Skarmory takes on Pokemon that offensively threaten Slowking, like Lokix and Tyranitar, as well as Grass-types like Hydrapple. Hydrapple itself is another bulky pivot that pairs nicely with Skarmory, helping keep dangerous physical attackers that can be too much for Skarmory to handle, like Ogerpon-C, in check. It also appreciates the chip damage provided by Spikes, letting it sweep teams with Nasty Plot easier. Other cleaners, like Thundurus-T, Choice Scarf Latios, and Battle Bond Greninja, appreciate Skarmory chipping away at opposing offensive threats with entry hazard damage and Rocky Helmet. Offensive pivots like Choice Scarf Zarude, Keldeo, and Sandy Shocks also enjoy the additional chip damage provided by Spikes, letting them muscle through foes better. Sandy Shocks in particular appreciates the Ground immunity provided by Skarmory as well as its ability to check Grass-types like Zarude; in return, Sandy Shocks can set Stealth Rock on top of Skarmory's Spikes while providing a useful Volt Switch immunity. Excadrill is another excellent Ground-type partner due to its ability to remove Stealth Rock, letting Skarmory preserve Sturdy. Additionally, it can keep dangerous special attackers like Latios in check while appreciating Skarmory's ability to stop opposing Excadrill as well as check priority users like Lokix and non-Belly Drum Azumarill.

Physical Wall.description: Skarmory is one of the tier's best entry hazard stackers and physical walls thanks to its excellent typing allowing it to check many prominent Pokemon like Zacian and Sneasler. Body Press is preferred on Skarmory over other attacks thanks to its Defense being significantly higher than its attacking stats. Iron Defense is typically run alongside Body Press to allow Skarmory to function as a wincon while also making it a better check to Pokemon like Zacian, Palafin, and Baxcalibur. Whirlwind can be used over Iron Defense to rack up entry hazard damage from the Spikes Skarmory sets and phaze foes trying to set up on it. Tera Water allows Skarmory to beat Pokemon like Tera Fire Zacian and Palafin. Skarmory has trouble with special attackers like Kyurem-W, Arceus-Dark, and Chi-Yu, which can easily OHKO it, so specially defensive walls like Giratina and Arceus-Dark form excellent cores with it. In exchange, Skarmory can check Pokemon like Zacian and Zamazenta-C for its teammates. Pokemon like Life Orb Mewtwo and Palkia-O appreciate Spikes chipping their checks like Solgaleo and Arceus-Dark into KO range of their coverage moves.

Defensive.description:
Skarmory's great bulk and strong defensive typing let it check common offensive physical threats such as Kingambit, Great Tusk, and Dragonite as well as providing opportunities to set up multiple layers of Spikes. Skarmory is able to set up Iron Defense on physical attackers, preventing it from being overwhelmed and massively boosting the power of Body Press; with enough Defense boosts, it can go toe-to-toe against setup sweepers like the aforementioned Kingambit and Dragonite while letting it turn into a usable late-game win condition, only being stopped by Ghost-types like Pecharunt and Dragapult. However, it can run Brave Bird and Whirlwind instead; Brave Bird gives it an immediate way to hit Ogerpon-W, Great Tusk, and Iron Valiant, while Whirlwind allows it to still deal with setup sweepers like Kingambit and non-Roar Zamazenta that can otherwise take advantage of Skarmory lacking IronPress. Rocky Helmet makes it impossible for even fully Attack-boosted Pokemon to match its Defense boosts, as Skarmory's access to Roost grants it longevity, letting it outlive almost every physical setup Pokemon in the long term while also letting it chip them early-game, such as stray U-turns and Knock Offs from Pokemon like Landorus-T, Rillaboom, and Ogerpon. Tera Dragon lets it reliably deal with Ogerpon-W even more and gives it a resistance to Fire, which lets it check Pokemon such as Cinderace. Tera Fighting should only be used on IronPress variants; on top of boosting Skarmory's Body Press, it also gives Skarmory extra insurance against Kingambit thanks to its Kowtow Cleave resistance and is especially useful for teams that are weak to Kingambit late-game. 96 Speed EVs let IronPress Skarmory outspeed Adamant Kingambit and Ursaluna, but a fully defensive spread alongside an Impish nature should be used if going for Brave Bird and Whirlwind.

Iron Defense Skarmory is outstanding on balance teams that struggle against setup Pokemon that take advantage of the team's passivity, synergizing with Pokemon like Gliscor, Ting-Lu, and Clefable, as they can set up entry hazards to pressure foes as well as remove opposing Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off. It also pairs well with Toxapex and Galarian Slowking, which can sponge special moves that Skarmory is unable to take, and they also check dangerous threats such as Iron Moth and Cinderace. These Pokemon are often fodder for opposing Swords Dance Kingambit or Bulk Up Great Tusk; however, Skarmory handles them with ease. Skarmory is also great against Pokemon such as Iron Defense Zamazenta and Rillaboom thanks to its solid typing and immense bulk. Chip damage from Rocky Helmet disincentivizes the aforementioned Pokemon from using physical moves, and Skarmory outlives them eventually thanks to its longevity and recovery capabilities with Roost. Despite Skarmory's great physical bulk, it is vulnerable to special attackers and Ghost-types that may take advantage of it, such as Iron Moth, Gholdengo, and Dragapult. Ting-Lu and Galarian Slowking are great for tanking special attackers' hits, the former being a great Ghost-type check. Heavy-Duty Boots Kingambit is also a good choice alongside Skarmory, as it can find opportunities to set up against Ghost-types while being a reliable sponge, as well as having strong priority moves against the special attackers that Skarmory would otherwise struggle against. In return, Skarmory can set Spikes for Kingambit and act as a reliable wall to some of Kingambit's checks, particularly Bulk Up Great Tusk and Iron Defense Zamazenta. Due to its lack of pivoting capabilities unlike Corviknight, Skarmory also appreciates Pokemon that can tank hits and pivot around, such as Rotom-W, U-turn Gliscor, and Meowscarada.

Skarmory is a great physical wall in the metagame thanks to its impressive defensive typing and great physical bulk allowing it to handle threats such as Excadrill and Scizor among other foes. Skarmory also serves as a valuable Spikes user thanks to it being able to set up against threats such as Buzzwole, Blissey, and non-Flamethrower Clefable. The combination of Iron Defense and Body Press is Skarmory’s preferred choice to make progress against teams, as it allows it to stonewall threats such as Scizor, Bisharp, and Tyranitar while also further pressuring threats such as Blissey and Hippowdon. Dropping Iron Defense and Body Press for Whirlwind or Toxic and Brave Bird respectively is also an option on more offensive teams to pressure threats such as Buzzwole and Mega Venusaur more effectively while also offering extra team support by phasing or spreading poison damage. However, this comes at the cost of being far more passive against Excadrill and lacks a proper response to Bisharp. 96 Speed EVs allows Skarmory to outspeed Adamant Ursaluna and Azumarill. On stall teams, Skarmory has the choice of running Defog in place of either Spikes or Iron Defense and can also run an EV spread of 248 HP / 76 Def / 184 Spe with an Impish nature to outspeed Choice Band Tyranitar, allowing it to boost or safely heal up before Tyranitar can 2HKO it. Skarmory’s main item of choice is Rocky Helmet to get residual damage off against foes with U-turn such as Scizor while also chipping setup sweepers, but it can also run Shed Shell on bulkier playstyles such as balance and stall in order to avoid being trapped by Magnezone. Skarmory can struggle a lot against special attackers such as Iron Moth and Enamorus, so specially defensive walls such as Blissey, Chansey, and specially defensive Skeledirge are good partners to shore up that weakness. Tyranitar is another good partner, since it can switch into and Pursuit trap threats that pressure Skarmory such as Iron Moth and Hisuian Zoroark. Common pivots that take advantage of Skarmory such as Victini and Thundurus also hate being Pursuit trapped by Tyranitar. Skarmory also has issues against Fire-types such as Iron Moth and Victini, so bulky Water-types such as Slowbro, Slowking, Gastrodon, and Alomomola can help deal with them. Electric-types such as Thundurus and Zeraora can also threaten Skarmory, so bulky Ground-types such as Hippowdon and Gastrodon are good partners to hinder them, but bulky Grass-types such as Tangrowth, Amoonguss, and Mega Venusaur also work as teammates at the cost of being unable to block Volt Switch. The aforementioned Ground-types can also form strong entry hazard stacking cores with Skarmory that bulkier playstyles such as stall enjoy greatly. Offensively, wallbreakers such as Life Orb Mienshao make for good partners, since they appreciate Skarmory's Spikes helping them chip their checks so they can wallbreak easier.

Physical Wall.description:
Skarmory is one of the purest physical walls available, as its great defensive typing and superb physical bulk lets it take on most of the tier's dangerous physical attackers, such as Great Tusk, Melmetal, and Zamazenta. Iron Defense allows Skarmory to beat boosting physical attackers like Mega Mawile, Swords Dance Gliscor, and Kingambit. Body Press immediately threatens Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Mega Lopunny while also doing significant general damage when boosted. It can also dissuade Pokemon such as Heatran and Terapagos from easily switching in to remove Skarmory or the entry hazards it sets. Spikes are quite effective in the metagame, as they hit and chip down several very prominent defensive Pokemon, most notably Ferrothorn, Gholdengo, and Melmetal. Skarmory also gets many opportunities to set them up thanks to its ability to easily switch into common Pokemon like Gliscor, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T. 96 Speed EVs allow Skarmory to outrun Adamant Kingambit and Ursaluna. Rocky Helmet chips down physical attackers such as Melmetal, Urshifu-R, and Great Tusk, the latter of which is especially notable, as it will take damage should it try to spin away Skarmory's Spikes.

Skarmory's limitations as a defensive Pokemon lead it to fit best on bulky balance and stall teams, as they greatly appreciate Skarmory's prowess as a catch-all physical wall that can use Spikes to force progress, and it notably beats several prominent wallbreakers, most notably Kingambit and Mega Mawile. While Skarmory has an impressive physically defensive profile, its poor Special Defense and reliance on Body Press to do damage leave it helpless against prominent special attackers such as Gholdengo, Tapu Lele, Mega Diancie, and Calm Mind Clefable. The latter three are especially problematic, as many teams expect their Steel-type to at least help out versus them, whereas Skarmory needs a teammate to pick up its slack. Gholdengo and Galarian Slowking can help out with the Fairy-types, while Heatran or Ting-Lu can help out with opposing Gholdengo. These teammates appreciate Skarmory handling powerful physical threats such as Great Tusk, Garchomp, and Ursaluna. Skarmory also greatly appreciates a check to Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y and Moltres, as they can switch into it without much trouble. Toxapex is an excellent partner that checks these dangerous Fire-types as well as Mega Diancie. Toxapex in turn greatly appreciates Skarmory checking dangerous Ground-types like Landorus-T and Great Tusk. Dragon-types such as Mega Latios and Dragonite can come in on these threats multiple times, and they also take pressure off of Skarmory to beat Ogerpon-W, which can occasionally cause trouble for Skarmory when boosted. Skarmory in turn takes care of powerful physical threats that can trouble these teammates, such as Mega Tyranitar, Mega Lopunny, and Weavile. Electric-types such as Raging Bolt and Zapdos are also problematic, so Ground-types such as Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu are good partners.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Flying

Stealth Rock can be used over Spikes, freeing up moveslots on teammates like Gliscor and Landorus. However, this does come at the cost of being able to stack both entry hazards.

Physically Defensive (Flying).description:
Thanks to its Steel typing and incredible physical bulk, Skarmory can easily handle Rock- and Ice-type attacks thrown towards Flying teams from the likes of Kleavor, Weavile, and Meowscarada. Body Press enables Skarmory to weaponize its incredible Defense, allowing it to handle foes like Iron Treads, Meowscarada, and Ogerpon-C with ease. Spikes wears down would-be threats to Flying teams like Iron Hands, Mamoswine, and Flutter Mane. Whirlwind can force out threats that Skarmory is less comfortable checking, such as Gliscor and Dragonite, along with racking up entry hazard damage. Alternatively, Iron Defense can be used to further increase Skarmory's physical bulk and Body Press's damage, enabling it to easily clean through the likes of Ground and Rock if given momentum.

Gliscor complements Skarmory by being able to handle Electric-types that threaten Skarmory, like Raging Bolt and Sandy Shocks, thanks to its Ground typing along with Toxic putting timers onto foes such as Volcarona and Hoopa-U. Gliscor also absorbs status such as Will-O-Wisp from Galarian Weezing and Sableye thanks to Poison Heal. Corviknight complements Skarmory incredibly well by dealing with threatening special attacks from the likes of Flutter Mane, Greninja, and Kyurem, and its Defog can give Skarmory safe entry. Articuno can similarly help against special attackers like Kyurem, Latios, and Greninja, and it can use Freeze-Dry to pressure Water- and Dragon-types like Primarina, Kingdra, and Latias. Assault Vest Tornadus-T can help to check threats capable of overwhelming Skarmory such as the Ogerpon formes and Iron Valiant, and with Heat Wave, it pressures Gholdengo and opposing Skarmory. Landorus can break through Electric- and Steel-types that Skarmory is unable to handle like Raging Bolt and Gholdengo, and if using a Choice Scarf, it is capable of using coverage such as Rock Slide and Sludge Wave to handle threats like Volcarona and the Ogerpon formes, respectively. Choice Scarf Enamorus greatly appreciates Skarmory's Spikes softening up checks like Hisuian Goodra and Alolan Muk. It can also support Skarmory by using Moonblast to deal with problematic Dark- and Dragon-types like Sableye, Darkrai, and Latios, along with using Healing Wish to heal Skarmory back up in matchups where it is especially needed, such as Ice. Dragonite similarly appreciates Spikes wearing down its checks like Archaludon and Porygon2 and in return can use its Dragon typing to help against Water-types like Urshifu-R and Barraskewda.

Physically Defensive (Steel).description:
Skarmory is a great defensive piece for Steel teams thanks to its Ground immunity, Fighting neutrality, and incredible Defense, which let it comfortably check problematic threats such as Gliscor, Great Tusk, and Sneasler. Spikes helps to wear down threats like Excadrill, Urshifu-R, and Raging Bolt. Body Press weaponizes Skarmory's high Defense, enabling it to deal with opposing Steel-, Normal-, and Dark-types like Iron Treads, Hisuian Goodra, Ursaluna, and Hisuian Samurott. Whirlwind forces out foes, removing boosts from the likes of Swords Dance Gliscor and racking up Spikes damage. Alternatively, Iron Defense can be used to enable Skarmory to completely wall physical attackers like Mamoswine while increasing Body Press's damage. Rocky Helmet helps wear down threats such as Hisuian Samurott and punishes U-turn from foes like Roaring Moon and Corviknight.

Heatran and Gholdengo make for incredible teammates thanks to their immunities and ability to enable an entry hazard-stacking core. Heatran checks Fire-types such as Volcarona and Iron Moth along with setting Stealth Rock. Gholdengo helps keep said hazards up thanks to its Ghost typing and Good as Gold while dealing with Fighting-types that can handle Skarmory like Iron Valiant and Okidogi. Iron Treads, Hisuian Goodra, and Scizor can all provide incredible utility and help further rack up hazard damage thanks to Knock Off removing Heavy-Duty Boots from the likes of Hisuian Samurott, Amoonguss, and Great Tusk. Iron Treads also provides a useful Electric immunity, making it capable of handling threats such as Raging Bolt and Magnezone while using Earthquake to deal with opposing Poison- and Steel-types such as Toxapex and Gholdengo. Hisuian Goodra wards off threats like Spectrier and Greninja with its immense special bulk while also using Dragon Tail to rack up more hazard damage. Scizor greatly appreciates Skarmory's entry hazards wearing down opposing walls like Hippowdon and Archaludon. In return, it can use Bullet Punch to handle the likes of Flutter Mane and Hoopa-U. Archaludon helps against physical attackers that can overwhelm Skarmory like the Ogerpon formes, Barraskewda, and Ceruledge while greatly appreciating Skarmory's ability to absorb Knock Off from the likes of Alolan Muk and Gliscor.

Defensive (HP).description:
Skarmory is a prolific defensive Pokemon; it's able to switch into and threaten out many common physical attackers like Zacian-C, both Urshifu formes, and Ogerpon-W. It also has access to entry hazards and can deal with the tier's common spinners. Iron Defense lets Skarmory match the boosts from setup sweepers like Roaring Moon and Calyrex-I while also boosting Body Press, potentially turning it into a late-game sweeper. Brave Bird can be run to more instantly threaten Ogerpon and Great Tusk. With Brave Bird, Skarmory should run Whirlwind instead of Iron Defense, enabling it to wear down foes with hazards while still hindering setup sweepers. Should the team not have a Stealth Rock setter, or have another Spikes setter, like Hisuian Samurott or Meowscarada, Skarmory can run Stealth Rock instead. Tera Fairy is used, as it's a good defensive type that doesn't overlap with any of Skarmory's weaknesses, letting it handle attackers like Cinderace and Zekrom that would otherwise have a type advantage over it. Tera Ghost is an alternative that lets Skarmory spinblock Great Tusk and Iron Treads to keep hazards up while making it more resilient against Fighting-types like Zamazenta. However, the Dark weakness does hurt, especially against Urshifu-S and Weavile. Tera Dragon is an alternative that can make Skarmory into a better Ogerpon-W answer but does come with a worse matchup against Zacian-C and Calyrex-I, making it more situational.

Skarmory appreciates an HP donation from almost any god. However, it does tend to fit better on bulkier teams, so gods like Arceus and Ho-Oh are great fits. Teammates with Knock Off like Weavile, Clefable, and Great Tusk rid the opponent of their Heavy-Duty Boots, allowing Skarmory to rack up chip damage with Whirlwind and entry hazards. The latter two also provide Stealth Rock to complement Skarmory's Spikes. Ghost-types like Arceus-Ghost, Pecharunt, and Gholdengo can spinblock for Skarmory to allow it to keep entry hazards up; the latter also blocks Defog thanks to Good As Gold. Lastly, strong special attackers like Kyogre, Hisuian Electrode, and Gholdengo can use Skarmory as a relatively free entry point, so pairing it up with specially defensive Pokemon like Eternatus, Ting-Lu, and Dondozo makes for a very solid defensive core.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Skarmory can make use of Flame Body or Static to fish for burn or paralysis on Pokemon that commonly make contact with it, such as Roaring Moon, Great Tusk, and Corviknight. Specially defensive variants of Skarmory with max Special Defense instead of Defense can run Water Absorb to better check Manaphy and Ogerpon-W or Volt Absorb to reliably check Zapdos and Sandy Shocks.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Skarmory's low HP and Special Defense leave it quite weak to special attackers like Gholdengo, Primarina, and Deoxys-S.

Fire-types: If Skarmory isn't using Well-Baked Body, it struggles against Fire-types like Ceruledge, Cinderace, and Ogerpon-H.

Electric-types: Electric-types like Zapdos, Iron Hands, and Sandy Shocks as well as Hadron Engine users like Latios and Deoxys-S can reliably outspeed and threaten an OHKO on Skarmory without Volt Absorb.

Physical Wall.description:
Thanks to its high Defense stat, solid utility movepool, and amazing typing, Skarmory functions as a physically defensive wall as well as an entry hazard setter. Fluffy lets Skarmory better check strong physical attackers such as Roaring Moon, Zamazenta, and Kingambit, whereas Intimidate allows it to check Chien-Pao and the Ogerpon formes excluding Ogerpon-H; alternatively, Well-Baked Body enables Skarmory to check Fire-types like Moltres, Ogerpon-H, and Iron Moth lacking Discharge. Body Press hits Steel-types like Heatran, Iron Treads, and Kingambit for a great deal of damage, while Brave Bird is slightly stronger than an unboosted Body Press and nails Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and the Ogerpon formes. Spikes is very useful on hazard stacking team archetypes and can quickly wear down Great Tusk, Manaphy, and Swampert, whereas Stealth Rock gives Skarmory valuable role compression and wears down Chien-Pao and Corviknight. Whirlwind works well in conjunction with Spikes to wear down the opposing team quite fast and forces out setup sweepers like Bulk Up Great Tusk and Iron Defense Zamazenta, while Iron Defense, which should only be used with Body Press, is a move that lets Skarmory set up along with setup sweepers like Zamazenta, Kingambit, and Great Tusk. Otherwise, Taunt can be used to prevent Corviknight from using Defog or Roost as well as Ting-Lu from setting up Spikes or Stealth Rock, Heavily punishing both. Leftovers gives Skarmory extra longevity against Pokemon like Zamazenta, Chien-Pao, and Kingambit, though Rocky Helmet can be used instead to punish Pokemon like Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Zamazenta. Heavy-Duty Boots grants Skarmory immunity to Stealth Rock chip, which is quite helpful when it needs to repeatably switch in with Stealth Rock up.

Skarmory functions on more defensively focused teams that tend to slowly wear down the opposing team with Spikes. Partners like Roaring Moon, Zapdos, and Gholdengo appreciate the entry hazards that Skarmory sets up, as it allows them to slowly wear down their checks, like Great Tusk, Swampert, and Manaphy. Skarmory struggles with the tier's many special attackers, so specially defensive teammates like Iron Treads, Swampert, and RegenVest Roaring Moon are much appreciated. Depending on its ability, Skarmory will need teammates to help it on the physical side. If Skarmory is not using Fluffy, Pecharunt is a nice partner to aid against Choice Band Zamazenta, while physically defensive Manaphy can help against Chien-Pao for non-Intimidate Skarmory. Lastly, Skarmory without Well-Baked Body very much appreciates a Fire-resistant or Fire-immune partner like Swampert or Primordial Sea Zapdos. A Ghost-type Pokemon like Pecharunt or Earth Eater Gholdengo works as a great partner for Skarmory, as it can prevent Great Tusk and Iron Treads from using Rapid Spin to remove the entry hazards that Skarmory sets up.

IronPress (Steel).description: Providing a neutrality to Fighting and a immunity to Ground, Skarmory is a valuable option for Steel teams to mitigate their most common weaknesses and set entry hazards. Its IronPress combination enables Skarmory to act as a win condition, notably using foes such as Tapu Bulu, Mega Aerodactyl, and Excadrill as setup fodder. As Skarmory is passive against Ghost-types, Gholdengo is a solid partner, as it can apply offensive pressure against them and also keeps entry hazards set by Skarmory on the field to ease wearing down the opposing team. Heatran's high special bulk and Fire immunity support Skarmory by acting as a switch-in to foes that can easily overwhelm Skarmory such as Mega Latias, Volcarona, and Mega Pidgeot. Defensive Electric-resistant teammates such as Ferrothorn can switch into Electric-types that threaten Skarmory such as Tapu Koko, Rotom-W, and Zapdos; Ferrothorn also makes a hazard stacking core with it. Archaludon similarly checks Electric-types that threaten Skarmory and handles physical attackers Skarmory can't properly handle such as Ceruledge, Ogerpon-W, and Mega Charizard X. Iron Treads offensively checks Electric-types, as well as some foes Skarmory has trouble against such as Landorus and Gholdengo.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Tera Dark powers up Houndoom's spammable STAB Dark Pulse, hitting Fire-resistant foes harder, but this leaves it with a weakness to Fairy-type moves and U-turn. Destiny Bond can be used as an emergency check to stop setup sweepers like Toxicroak from snowballing.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Poliwrath and Hitmontop both shrug off Houndoom's attacks and can threaten an OHKO with their STAB Fighting-type moves. Additionally, Hisuian Sneasel and Choice Scarf Primeape can outspeed it, either forcing Houndoom out or to Terastallize.

Special Walls: Specially defensive foes like Camerupt and Eelektross can withstand Houndoom's STAB moves, with Camerupt pressuring it out and Eelektross slow pivoting into an offensive answer. Muk can wear down Houndoom via Toxic on the switch-in.

Rock-types: Lycanroc can threaten Houndoom with its STAB Rock-type moves and force it out. Additionally, Naclstack and Regirock can withstand Houndoom's STAB attacks, and the former can threaten it with Salt Cure on the switch-in, while the latter can easily break its Substitute with Rock Blast.

Water-types: Water-types like Clawitzer, Basculin, and Whiscash threaten Houndoom with their STAB Water-type moves, forcing it to either switch out or Terastallize.

Faster Attackers: Faster physically offensive foes like Virizion, Choice Specs Jolteon, and Pyroar easily pick off Houndoom with their STAB moves.

Wallbreaker.description:
Thanks to Nasty Plot, an excellent offensive typing, and respectable Speed tier, Houndoom is a terrifying wallbreaker and late-game cleaner in the metagame. Its STAB combination is only resisted by itself, Poliwrath, and the rare Dachsbun, which makes it difficult to switch into once it sets up. Substitute lets Houndoom avoid status effects like Toxic from Muk and Thunder Wave from Regirock, while also allowing Houndoom to set up against bulkier teams. Heavy-Duty Boots mitigates Houndoom's entry hazard weakness, allowing it to come in many times over the course of a game. Flash Fire provides Houndoom an immunity to Fire-type moves and also gives it an opportunity to set up against Choice-locked Fire-types such as Typhlosion. Tera Ghost provides a useful immunity to Fighting-type moves, most notably Close Combat from Hisuian Sneasel and Hitmontop or a Mach Punch revenge kill while also blocking Rapid Spin.

Houndoom appreciates offense and hyper offense teams able to take advantage of its sweeping and wallbreaking capabilities. Entry hazard setters like Orthworm and Whiscash make for excellent partners to let Houndoom snowball through teams more easily. Houndoom is not very bulky, so pivots like Mesprit, Jolteon, and Basculin are good teammates to safely bring in Houndoom on the field, providing entry on walls such as Venusaur, Orthworm, and Weezing. Houndoom also finds itself weak to many common physical attacks, most notably physical priority moves from the likes of Hitmontop and Lycanroc. Because of this, physically defensive teammates like Weezing and Naclstack pair well with it. Grass-types such as Brute Bonnet, Whimsicott, and Virizion pair nicely with Houndoom, as they help check the Ground-, Rock-, and Water-types like Whiscash, Regirock, Naclstack, and Clawitzer that it otherwise struggles with. Water-types like Basculin and Clawitzer benefit from being paired with Houndoom, as they appreciate Houndoom dealing with the Grass-types they struggle against such as Venusaur and Abomasnow. Fighting-types like Toxicroak and Hitmontop also appreciate Houndoom checking the Psychic-types like Mesprit that they otherwise struggle with.

monotype.overview:
Water

Kingdra is a solid Swift Swim special attacker for Water teams; however, it is only functional in this role and faces competition from Basculegion-F, which has superior Special Attack. Along with that, rain teams can opt to not run a special attacking Swift Swim threat and instead choose to run Choice Specs Greninja to be less reliant on rain overall.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

A Modest nature can be used to push out a slight bit more damage from Kingdra, allowing for its Dragon Pulse to OKHO Raging Bolt after Stealth Rock, but it will no longer be able to outspeed Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Roaring Moon. Hurricane can check the Ogerpon formes reliably without having to rely on Draco Meteor; however, it is still only able to 2HKO Amoonguss, while Brambleghast can use it as a free entry point. Flip Turn can be used to keep up momentum against threats that Kingdra can struggle to break through such as Hisuian Goodra and Assault Vest Hoopa-U.

Choice Specs (Water).description:
Kingdra finds a nice place on rain teams thanks to its incredible secondary Dragon typing and solid Speed and Special Attack enabling it to outspeed and check the likes of Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, and Kyurem in rain. Draco Meteor lays on the pressure removing the likes of Ogerpon-W and Archaludon reliably after minor chip damage. Dragon Pulse lets Kingdra reliably pressure Dragon-types like non-Choice Scarf Dragapult and Latios without having to deal with dropping its Special Attack. Surf can easily wash away threats such as Iron Valiant, Alolan Muk, and Ogerpon-H after minor chip damage. Alternatively, Hydro Pump can be used as a way to 2HKO specially defensive Articuno along with getting an OHKO against Flutter Mane. Finally, Ice Beam threatens Grass teams and pressures Water Absorb Clodsire.

Pelipper is a mandatory teammate for Kingdra because it sets up rain along with providing safe entry with U-turn. Pelipper can also use Knock Off to remove items like Assault Vest from threats like Tornadus-T and Hisuian Goodra. Barraskewda makes for a great secondary Swift Swim partner, being able to threaten special walls like Articuno, Assault Vest Hoopa-U, and Blissey as well as outspeed foes like Choice Scarf Flutter Mane and Unburden Sneasler. Swampert can provide support against Electric- and Steel-types Kingdra struggles against such as Assault Vest Iron Hands and Hisuian Goodra with Earthquake. It can also set Stealth Rock to provide crucial chip damage against threats like the Ogerpon formes and Archaludon while also being able to pivot Kingdra in with Flip Turn. Eject Button Toxapex can be used to safely pivot Kingdra in, threaten Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Primarina, and put Iron Hands and Dragonite on a timer with Toxic. Alternatively, Tentacruel can be used as a Poison-type teammate that can remove entry hazards with Rapid Spin to keep Kingdra healthy as well as pivot it in with Flip Turn. Hisuian Samurott can set Spikes with Ceaseless Edge to help wear down Water Absorb Clodsire and Hisuian Goodra along with being able to use Sucker Punch to remove faster threats like Choice Scarf Dragapult. Ogerpon-W can use its Grass-type STAB moves to handle Water-types like Alomomola, Azumarill, and Primarina.

Swift Swim (Water).description:
A Timid nature outspeeds Choice Scarf Roaring Moon.

This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Choice Band.description:
• Donphan uses its combination of Sturdy + Choice Band and its wide range of moves to always survive a hit while also dishing out huge damage.
  • Earthquake nets Donphan the highest damage output against the more important threats, most notably against Iron Hands, Sneasler, and Raging Bolt.
  • Gunk Shot is important coverage that allows Donphan to hit the strong Fairy-type Pokemon roaming the tier, like Choice item Iron Valiant and non-Weakness Policy Primarina and Sylveon.
  • Head Smash can hit Zapdos, Kyurem, and Galarian Moltres, and the mere presence of the move also helps against Volcarona, since it is forced to guess if the Donphan user will use Earthquake or Head Smash and act accordingly.
  • Ice Shard helps Donphan against both Landorus formes and Garchomp.
  • Counter is helpful against threats that Donphan cannot OHKO like Haxorus and Ursaluna.
  • Bulldoze gives Donphan better odds against Sturdy Pokemon like Magnezone as well as non-Air Balloon Volcanion.
  • Play Rough is used for Urshifu-S and Darkrai, though the latter is only a chance to KO.
  • An alternate spread of 252 Atk / 252 SpD / 4 Spe can be used with Knock Off in order to boost Donphan's odds against Iron Crown and Life Orb Spectrier.
  • Donphan can really struggle against Water-type foes, like Manaphy and Dondozo, so Electric- and Grass-type Pokemon like Zapdos and Ogerpon-W are good teammates for it.
  • Pokemon like Corviknight and Air Balloon Registeel can also be problematic for Donphan, as they tend to resist or be immune to its coverage attacks, so Fire-type Pokemon like Volcarona can help patch these weaknesses up.

Offensive Trick Room.description:
Shadow Ball deals heavy damage to Galarian Slowbro and Hoopa and also hits Alolan Sandslash neutrally, while Ice Beam has better coverage against bulky Ground-types in Rhydon and Mudsdale.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Thanks to its offensive and defensive tools, Porygon2 fits well on balance teams with a Trick Room mode. It benefits from teammates that provide utility, such as Fake Out or redirection, enabling it to set up Trick Room and go on the offensive, as well as teammates that can take advantage of Trick Room.
  • Porygon2 is most commonly paired with Incineroar, which offers Fake Out support to allow Porygon2 to set up Trick Room. It also provides Intimidate and Parting Shot utility, enhancing Porygon2’s survivability. Parting Shot is especially valuable, as it allows Incineroar to pivot to a Trick Room sweeper while Porygon2 sets up Trick Room. Additionally, Incineroar’s access to Flare Blitz and Knock Off helps to threaten Pokemon like Gholdengo, which would otherwise wall Porygon2.
  • The preferred Trick Room sweeper for Porygon2 teams is Ursaluna, as it takes full advantage of Trick Room by securing OHKOs on many Pokemon with its Guts boost. This pairing also works well because Porygon2 threatens special damage, while Ursaluna dishes out massive physical damage. Garchomp is another excellent offensive partner for Porygon2 because Garchomp provides a faster-paced, non-Trick Room-dependent offensive option for Porygon2 but with a less explosive damage output than Ursaluna.
  • Amoonguss is a common support partner for Porygon2, taking full advantage of Trick Room with its low Speed and putting foes to sleep with Spore to allow Porygon2 to attack unthreatened. It also provides Rage Powder redirection, enabling Porygon2 to set up Trick Room freely, and Pollen Puff to heal Porygon2, reducing the need for it to constantly use Recover.
  • Gholdengo is a common offensive partner for Porygon2, as it walls Pokemon like non-Throat Chop Sneasler, which can threaten massive damage to Porygon2, and Amoonguss, which can disrupt Porygon2 by putting it to sleep with Spore before it sets up Trick Room or deals much damage. Additionally, the threat of Nasty Plot boosts forces opponents to focus on Gholdengo, potentially allowing Porygon2 to move freely.
  • Flamigo and Sneasler are used on Porygon2 teams, as they threaten Incineroar, which can hinder Porygon2 with Knock Off and Parting Shot, as well as threats like Archaludon, Kingambit, and, in Flamigo's case, Gholdengo with Close Combat. Sneasler has the added benefit of threatening status with Dire Claw and Poison Touch, while Flamigo has Wide Guard utility to protect Porygon2 from moves like Eruption from Hisuian Typhlosion and Make It Rain from Gholdengo.

Strategy Comments

  • As a defensive unit with offensive potential, Porygon2 excels when it is minimally threatened by high-damage moves, such as Close Combat from Sneasler and Choice Specs Tera Fire Eruption from Hisuian Typhlosion. This necessitates pivoting and relying on its teammates to handle major damage dealers, enabling Porygon2 to safely set up Trick Room, heal itself as needed, and retaliate with substantial damage.
  • The optimal strategy for using Porygon2 involves pivoting between Pokemon like Incineroar and Amoonguss until Porygon2 and its partner sweepers like Ursaluna achieve a strong offensive position. This includes cycling Intimidate and Parting Shot with Incineroar to stack stat drops while using Amoonguss's Spore to stop opposing threats. By doing so, you create a window for Porygon2 and its offensive partners to safely attack and capitalize on the advantageous board state.
  • Due to Porygon2's relatively unoppressive presence, it's susceptible to being outpaced offensively, which is largely unavoidable. However, the best way to deal with this is by pivoting between teammates like Incineroar and Amoonguss to cycle Intimidate, use Spore, or provide redirection until Porygon2 and its offensive partner are in a favorable position. As mentioned earlier, Incineroar's Knock Off and Parting Shot significantly impair Porygon2's offensive and defensive capabilities, which is why Pokemon like Garchomp and Flamigo are employed to take down Incineroar. Additionally, cycling Fake Out from Incineroar and Rillaboom can be particularly threatening for Porygon2, as it may allow an opposing Pokemon to set up or chip away at Porygon2, potentially causing it to faint before it can use Recover. This is why Pokemon like Flamigo and Sneasler are often included, as they can threaten common Fake Out users as well as setup threats like Kingambit and Gholdengo.

Offensive Trick Room Setter.description:
• Porygon2’s primary role is to absorb hits, set up Trick Room, and exert offensive pressure while Trick Room is active. With Eviolite, Porygon2 becomes one of the bulkiest Pokemon in the format, and its access to Recover allows it to heal and remain difficult to remove. Additionally, the Download boost helps it gain more offensive pressure.
  • Tera Blast is essential to Porygon2's set, as it provides the necessary coverage to make Porygon2 offensively threatening once it's Terastallized. Ice Beam is also crucial, offering good coverage against Pokemon like Garchomp and Dragonite.
  • Tera Fighting is used for Fighting-type Tera Blast, enabling Porygon2 to deal significant damage to Steel- and Dark-type Pokemon such as Kingambit, Archaludon, and Incineroar. Tera Blast Ground also targets Steel-types but has the niche of threatening Pokemon like Electabuzz, Magmar, and Gholdengo. Tera Flying serves a slightly different purpose; while Flying-type Tera Blast is effective against threats like Rillaboom and Annihilape, it is primarily used for its resistance to Fighting-type moves and immunity to Ground-type attacks. This allows Porygon2's common partner, Ursaluna, to freely use Earthquake without worrying about hitting Porygon2.
  • With the provided Defense and HP investment, Porygon2 can almost always survive two Kowtow Cleaves from Black Glasses Tera Dark Kingambit, a Wave Crash from Tera Water Choice Band Basculegion-M in rain, and two Wood Hammers from most Assault Vest Rillaboom. The Special Defense investment allows it to live three Hyper Voices from Life Orb Primarina as well as a Make It Rain from Leftovers Gholdengo after two Nasty Plot boosts. The Special Attack investment ensures that Porygon2 can KO Garchomp with Ice Beam or with a Download-boosted Tera Blast Fighting or Ground if Garchomp has Terastallized into a Steel-type. With the Download boost, it also guarantees an OHKO on most Assault Vest Kingambit with Tera Blast Fighting and a 2HKO on non-Sitrus Berry Amoonguss with Ice Beam.

nu.overview: Porygon2's good Eviolite-boosted defenses and access to Trace make it one of the best special walls in the tier. Porygon2 utilizes Trace to great effect, copying abilities such as Chandelure's Flash Fire, Vaporeon's Water Absorb, Amoonguss's Regenerator, and Toxtricity's Punk Rock. Boasting an impressive Special Attack, Porygon2 circumvents its passivity by threatening 2HKOs or 3HKOs on most offensive Pokemon with its Tri Attack and super effective coverage options. Porygon2's Normal typing is great for letting it be a general blanket check, but its lack of resistances can lead to it being overwhelmed, especially with its susceptibility to entry hazards, since it cannot run Heavy-Duty Boots. Porygon2 is also very vulnerable to physical attackers such as Incineroar and Gligar using Knock Off as well as Choice item users like Chandelure and Munkidori using Trick, since it relies heavily on Eviolite to boost its bulk. Additionally, Porygon2 struggles to threaten bulky Steel-types, such as Registeel and Bronzong, which can allow them opportunities to come in on it for free. On top of that, Porygon2 cannot handle Calm Mind setup sweepers like Sylveon and Scream Tail on its own, especially if they have recovery moves, but it can slow them down with Thunder Wave, allowing a teammate to handle them.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Discharge can be used as an alternative to Thunder Wave, since it gives Porygon2 space for more offensive options while still letting it fish for paralysis, though Thunder Wave's guaranteed paralysis is generally preferred. Download can be used over Trace, boosting Porygon2's offensive power and making it more difficult for offensive threats to safely switch into it. However, Trace's overall utility is usually much better.

Checks and Counters

Item Displacement: Porygon2 relies on Eviolite for much of its walling power, meaning it is very susceptible to moves like Knock Off and Trick, which can remove the Eviolite. Many physical attackers such as Incineroar, Swampert, Alolan Muk, and Gligar carry Knock Off and can hinder Porygon2's bulk to allow partners to break through it more easily. Additionally, special attackers with Choice items, such as Chandelure, Porygon-Z, and Munkidori, can cripple Porygon2 by giving it a Choice item, using Trick.

Steel-types: Porygon2 struggles against bulky Steel-types such as Registeel, Bronzong, and Copperajah. They aren't generally hindered by Thunder Wave and have ways to set entry hazards or boost their own stats, letting these Steel-types exploit Porygon2's lack of coverage to hit them. The first two also threaten Porygon2 with a powerful Body Press.

Fighting-types: Powerful physical Fighting-types such as Paldean Tauros-F and -W, Breloom, and Flamigo all threaten Porygon2 with their strong Close Combat. While most do not want to switch into a Thunder Wave, they can pivot in and force Porygon2 out, and Lum Berry Paldean Tauros formes as well as Poison Heal Breloom ignore Thunder Wave altogether and can use Porygon2 as a chance to setup with Bulk Up, Swords Dance, or Substitute.

Special Wall.description:
Set Details

Shadow Ball complements Tri Attack, hitting Ghost-types such as Chandelure, Decidueye, and Hisuian Typhlosion while also dealing super effective damage to Bronzong. Porygon2 can also run a BoltBeam set. Ice Beam threatens Ground-types that might be tempted to switch into a Thunder Wave, such as Flygon and Gligar as well as Grass-types such as Breloom and Amoonguss, which are otherwise very threatening to Porygon2. Thunderbolt handles bulky Water-types like Milotic and Vaporeon that could chip down Porygon2 or Wish pass to allies for free. Foul Play is useful against any physical attackers, such as Basculegion-M, Scyther, and Tera Steel Flygon, as well as physically frail Pokemon such as Espeon and Munkidori. Trace gives Porygon2 amazing defensive utility, providing a massive advantage against a number of Pokemon. For example, it can Trace Vaporeon's Water Absorb, Porygon-Z's Adaptability, Munkidori's Toxic Chain, Toxtricity's Punk Rock, Chandelure's Flash Fire, Incineroar's as well as Paldean Tauros-W's Intimidate, and Klefki's as well as Tornadus's Prankster. Tera Poison is an excellent defensive typing overall and prevents Porygon2 from being poisoned, which is vital against Pokemon like Munkidori, Alolan Muk, and Amoonguss that attempt to cripple Porygon2 by poisoning it. Alternatively, Tera Ghost makes Porygon2 Fighting-immune and boosts the power of Shadow Ball. Finally, Tera Fairy, if Porygon2 copies Flygon's Levitate, allows it to completely wall both of Flygon's STAB attacks while being a generally useful defensive typing. In addition to that, unlike Tera Ghost, Tera Poison and Fairy allow Porygon2 to resist Scrappy Flamigo's Close Combat.

Porygon2's weakness to Knock Off users and physical attackers, especially Fighting-types such as Flamigo, Toxicroak, and Heracross, means that it appreciates teammates that can switch into these Pokemon. Amoonguss and Galarian Slowbro make for excellent partners thanks to their Poison typing and Regenerator, allowing them to come in repeatedly throughout the game and tank hits from these threats. Avalugg is another physical wall that pairs well with Porygon2. Despite Avalugg still being weak to Fighting and Knock Off, Porygon2 covers many of its weaknesses by being a blanket special wall that can take on special attackers for it. In return, Avalugg removes entry hazards for Porygon2. Other hazard control options such as Defog Scyther and Altaria are also good partners for Porygon2, since they remove hazards for it while providing good defensive synergy with their Fighting resistances. Porygon2 also appreciates teaming up with physical wallbreakers, especially Fighting-types that can take advantage of bulky Steel-types, which Porygon2 tends to allow in. Flamigo, Paldean Tauros-W and -F, and Heracross are great for this, since they also have good defensive synergy with Porygon2 and appreciate it spreading paralysis to faster Pokemon. Bulky Water-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Tentacruel can spread status to physical attackers like Flamigo, Flygon, and Scyther that threaten Porygon2 while also checking Hisuian Typhlosion, one of the only special attackers that consistently carries Fighting-type coverage moves. These bulky Water-types also often carry phazing moves, which are very helpful against bulky setup sweepers like Registeel and Bronzong, which Porygon2 struggles against. Additionally, Tentacruel can also provide Rapid Spin support for Porygon2.

Physical Defensive.description:
Porygon2 is an amazing physical wall on Normal teams due to its good bulk and access to Eviolite. Discharge threatens Flying- and Water-types like Corviknight, Gyarados, and Barraskewda. Ice Beam checks Ground-, Flying-, and Dragon-types like the Landorus-T, Dragonite, and Garchomp. Foul Play is a great anti-setup move that dissuades physical sweepers like Scizor, Ceruledge, and the Ogerpon formes from setting up. Substitute can be run over Foul Play, as it allows Porygon2 to block status from Toxapex and Amoonguss while also protecting itself from incoming threats like Great Tusk or Keldeo. However, doing so will make Porygon2 vulnerable into setup sweepers like Ogerpon-H and Gouging Fire due to not having Foul Play. Trace is the ideal ability for Porygon2 to copy Regenerator and Poison Heal from Toxapex and Gliscor, respectively. Trace also allows Porygon2 to copy Sword of Ruin, which helps it take hits from Chien-Pao better. Download can be run over Trace to make Porygon2 a bulky wallbreaker, making it notably effective in the Flying matchup by taking out Corviknight and Skarmory with ease.

Blissey is the ideal partner for Porygon2, forming a strong defensive core by providing a switch-in to special threats like Flutter Mane, Dragapult, and Choice Specs Greninja, while also spreading paralysis with Thunder Wave. Blissey also provides utility in setting up Stealth Rock. Braviary provides entry hazard removal with Defog for Porygon2 while also checking Sneasler, Ogerpon-W, and Breloom with Brave Bird. In return, Porygon2 deals with Iron Boulder and Ceruledge for Braviary with Foul Play. Choice Specs Hisuian Zoroark is a nice teammate due to its Fighting immunity, and it can threaten important targets like Urshifu-R, Gholdengo, non-Choice Scarf Heatran, and Pecharunt with Shadow Ball and Focus Blast. Calm Mind Ursaluna-B is a great wallbreaker, KOing defensive threats like Galarian Weezing, Gouging Fire, and Heatran at +1. Ursaluna-B is also a Knock Off absorber for Porygon2 due its bulk and access to Moonlight. Choice Scarf Indeedee is a great revenge killer, taking out Fighting- and Poison-types like mixed Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, and Clodsire, and it can use Healing Wish to bring Porygon2 back to full health if it gets weakened. Ditto becomes a great reverse sweeper for Porygon2 by transforming into sweepers like Gouging Fire and Chien-Pao. Cinccino not only removes hazards and boosts its stats with Tidy Up, but also threatens a lot of specially bulky Pokemon with Bullet Seed, Rock Blast, and Triple Axel for Porygon2, most notably Articuno and Swampert. Cinccino can also run a Choice Band set to potentially wallbreak, letting it OHKO Clodsire with Triple Axel. Terapagos can run an offensive utility set with Rapid Spin for Porygon2, but it can also become a fierce setup sweeper with Calm Mind and Tera Starstorm. Terapagos notably threatens Steel-types like Excadrill and Heatran with Earth Power, which Porygon2 appreciates.

vgc2024.overview:
• Porygon2 is one of the bulkiest Pokemon in the format with Eviolite, which allows it to set up Trick Room for it and its partners and beat most Pokemon in the format one-on-one with Recover. With a Download Special Attack boost, it is able to OHKO Pokemon such as the Landorus formes, Tornadus, and Dragonite with Ice Beam.

  • Porygon2 appreciates redirection, damage reduction, and Fake Out support to set up Trick Room and to allow it to Recover safely, making Amoonguss, Ogerpon-W, Gouging Fire, and Incineroar excellent partners. Amoonguss especially benefits from Trick Room, since it is able to utilize its low Speed under Trick Room to incapacitate foes with Spore. Ursaluna is also a great partner for Porygon2, since, as a slow and offensive Pokemon, it appreciates Trick Room letting it deal great damage to faster foes that threaten it outside of Trick Room like Flutter Mane and Urshifu. This damage output is something that Porygon2 lacks.

  • Porygon2 struggles against Snarl, Taunt, Amoonguss, Incineroar, and Urshifu. Snarl makes it deal significantly less damage, which allows opponents to ignore it without being punished. Taunt removes valuable options from Porygon2 such as Trick Room and Recover. Spore from Amoonguss can stop Trick Room setups and makes Porygon2 vulnerable to strong attacks such as Close Combat from Urshifu, Moonblast from Flutter Mane, and Sacred Sword from Chien-Pao without being able to heal the damage off with Recover. Amoonguss also underspeeds Porygon2, punishing Trick Room setups, meaning that once Trick Room is set up, Amoonguss can Spore Porygon2 before it attacks, removing its access to recovery and damage. Incineroar pressures Fake Out, which helps stop Trick Room. Additionally, Incineroar can use Knock Off to remove the Eviolite from Porygon2, making it easier to KO. Finally, Urshifu can threaten Porygon2 with a 2HKO with Close Combat if Porygon2 does not Terastallize.

Offensive TR Setter.description:
• Tera Blast is used as strong Normal-type STAB move that offers coverage once Porygon2 Terastallizes. When Tera Blast is paired with a Download Attack boost, Tera Blast becomes a physical move when Porygon2 Terastallizes. This allows you to hit Assault Vest users like Raging Bolt and Rillaboom harder, as well as Pokemon with high base Special Defense such as Flutter Mane. Ice Beam is used as coverage against Landorus and Amoonguss, and Recover is used for longevity, allowing it to set Trick Room up multiple times.

  • With the bulk investment bolstered by the Eviolite, this Porygon2 always survives three Sacred Swords from Chien-Pao, Timid Choice Specs Chi-Yu Overheat, and two Moonblasts from Special Attack Booster Energy Flutter Mane. It also almost always lives a Sword of Ruin Close Combat from Adamant Urshifu.

  • Tera Poison is the main Tera type for Porygon2. It offers resistances to Grass-, Fighting-, and Fairy-type attacks, which are important against Rillaboom, Urshifu, and Flutter Mane, respectively, as well as offering a solid overall defensive typing. Additionally, it allows it to hit Grass- and Fairy-types like Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Tera Fairy Flutter Mane for super effective damage with Tera Blast. Tera Fairy is used to wall Urshifu and hit it and Raging Bolt for super effective damage. Tera Flying is used to hit Grass- and Fighting-types like Urshifu, Ogerpon, and Rillaboom. Additionally, it makes Porygon2 immune to Earthquake from Ursaluna, giving its partner a valuable spread move. Finally, Tera Ghost is used for an immunity to Fighting-type attacks and Fake Out, as well as giving it the ability to hit Flutter Mane.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon is a new addition from the Indigo Disk that happens to be relevant!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Immortal Duck.description:
• With its wide movepool and impressive bulk courtesy of Eviolite, Porygon2 is a great defensive option.

  • Tri Attack vs Tera Blast: Tri Attack offers Porygon2 consistent damage and the chance of inflicting status, while Tera Blast allows Porygon2 to make use of Tera to damage foes it might miss out on with Tri Attack such as Flutter Mane.

  • Foul Play: Foul Play prevents Porygon2 from being used as setup fodder by the likes of Dragonite and Ogerpon, punishing their attempts to boost with increasing damage.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam allows Porygon2 to more immediately threaten important targets like Dragonite and Landorus-T without relying on Tera.

  • Discharge: Discharge gives Porygon2 coverage against the likes of Primarina and enables it to attempt to spread paralysis even through Taunt.

EV Spreads
  • 244 HP / 192 Def / 60 SpD / 12 Spe with Calm: This spread gives Porygon2 good mixed bulk and allows it to outspeed paralyzed Urshifu.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Porygon2 is a great defensive presence even without Tera; however, the right Tera type is still crucial in allowing it to lock down important targets.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy gives Porygon2 resistances to Dark- and Fighting-type attacks, allowing it to better stand up to foes such as Urshifu. The immunity to Dragon is also useful in denying Scale Shot attempts from the likes of Dragonite.

  • Poison: Tera Poison grants a resistance to Fighting as well as an immunity to Toxic and Toxic Spikes, enabling Porygon2 to function better against bulkier teams.

Trick Room.description: • This EV Spread survives two Deoxys-A Expanding Forces in Psychic Terrain, as well as two Iron Hands Drain Punches.

Physically Defensive.description: Porygon2 has found itself to be an excellent defensive staple for Normal teams, with Eviolite boosting its great defenses to a higher level. With the ability Trace, it's able to come in on certain Pokemon such as Intimidate Landorus- T, Stamina Archaludon, and Technician Scizor and utilize their abilities. Alternatively, Download can raise its Special Attack and deal good damage to more passive teams along with Flying- teams. Ice Beam helps to threaten Dragon- and Ground-type Pokemon such as Dragonite, Landorus, and Garchomp. Discharge can spread status while also threaten Flying- and Water-type Pokemon such as Corviknight and Pelipper. Hidden Power Fire can be used to take out opposing Steel-types like Mega Scizor and Ferrothorn. Substitute in conjunction with Download can give Porygon2 more opportunities to freely use Ice Beam or Discharge to threaten Flying-types. Porygon2 can utilize Teleport to bring in teammates such as Ursaluna and Mega Lopunny. Foul Play can also be used to check physical setup sweepers such as Mega Scizor and the Ogerpon formes. Mega Lopunny can take out Ghost- and Steel-types like Gholdengo and Heatran while also taking out Landorus, something Porygon2 can't wall; alternatively, Mega Pidgeot be used to deal with Mega Gallade and Keldeo. Chansey and Blissey provide a specially defensive core that can sponge special moves while taking advantage of entry hazards. Defensive Staraptor provides hazard control along with its ability Intimidate, making it easier to pivot Porygon2 in with U-turn. Hisuian Zoroark, with its Ghost typing and the ability Illusion, can bait in Fighting type moves if positioned to look like one of Porygon2's teammates while being able to take advantage of Teleport pivoting. Ursaluna is a powerful teammate that can deal high damage when switched in by Teleport and remove bulky walls such as Archaludon and Mega Sableye.

Hazard Setter.description:
Silk Trap is chosen over similar moves like Burning Bulwark for its ability to slow down foes like Paldean Tauros-W and Scyther; this gives Smeargle an easier time setting entry hazards or denying Defog attempts.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

Disruptive Support.description:
Set Details

  • Smeargle uses its wide movepool to support its offensive teammates. It is the fastest Spore user in the format, and it can shut down foes such as Calyrex-I and Raging Bolt before they can move. Its Moody ability can punish the opponent for not KOing it quickly enough, and a possible Speed boost will allow it to outspeed and incapacitate Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R with Spore. Trick Room sets use Technician or Own Tempo on Smeargle to prevent a Moody Speed boost from altering the turn order in Trick Room.
  • Follow Me protects teammates susceptible to OHKOs such as Calyrex-S, redirecting Moongeist Beam from Lunala and Shadow Ball from Flutter Mane. Fake Out can stop a foe for a turn, which can allow for a Restricted partner such as Calyrex-S with Nasty Plot or Calyrex-I with Trick Room to set up. Decorate increases the offenses of Smeargle's partners, punishing passive play from the opposing side such as using Protect to stall Fake Out. Wide Guard blocks powerful spread moves in the format like Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S and Glacial Lance from Calyrex-I.
  • Focus Sash ensures survival against most moves and can force the opponent to double target Smeargle.
  • Maximum Speed with a Jolly nature can be used to ensure Decorate occurs before Calyrex-I's and Terapagos's moves outside of Trick Room, or Smeargle can run minimum Speed with a Relaxed nature while Calyrex-I is one Speed point faster than it in order for Decorate to go first in Trick Room.
  • Tera Grass can be used to ensure Tera Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R will never OHKO Smeargle, and it lets Smeargle be immune to Spore and Rage Powder. Tera Ghost provides an immunity to Fake Out and Fighting- and Normal-type attacks such as Body Press from Zamazenta-C, Close Combat from the Urshifu formes, and Facade from Ursaluna.

Teambuilding

  • Urshifu-R threatens an OHKO onto Smeargle through Focus Sash with Surging Strikes. Taunt from Pokemon such as Tornadus and Chien-Pao shuts down Smeargle's support options. Spore-immune redirectors like Amoonguss, the Ogerpon formes, and Safety Goggles Indeedee-F can save their partners from being put to sleep and also stop Decorate from boosting Smeargle's partner.
  • Smeargle can be partnered with Rillaboom in order to remove Psychic Terrain from Indeedee-F to use Fake Out, which helps Nasty Plot Calyrex-S set up. Rillaboom also threatens an OHKO against Urshifu-R with its Grass-type STAB moves.
  • Smeargle can use Fake Out on Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, which threatens Calyrex-S with an OHKO, so Calyrex-S can instead OHKO it; it can also support Calyrex-S with Follow Me if Fake Out is not available. Calyrex-S enjoys Wide Guard blocking spread moves it is weak to such as Astral Barrage from opposing Calyrex-S and Snarl from Chi-Yu.
  • Decorate can target bulky slower Restricted Pokemon such as Calyrex-I and Terapagos to quickly boost their offenses to high levels before they attack. Terapagos can also Terastallize to remove Miraidon's Electric Terrain from the field in order for Smeargle to put foes to sleep with Spore.

Support.description:
Smeargle's access to almost every move with Sketch grants it a great niche in Regulation G as a support Pokemon. Follow Me allows Smeargle to protect its more offensive partners, and Spore threatens to shut down opposing Pokemon, making it easier for Smeargle's partners to set up and sweep. Wide Guard blocks the plethora of spread moves in the metagame that ignore Smeargle's Follow Me, such as Tera Starstorm and Glacial Lance from Terapagos-S and Calyrex-I, respectively. This can, however, be replaced with Decorate on more offensive Calyrex-I teams, letting Trick Room threats like Calyrex-I and Ursaluna-B do significantly more damage quickly. Fake Out is the best last move on Smeargle, providing lots of pressure when it enters the field and opening up room for repositioning or setting up. Smeargle can use Spiky Shield over Fake Out for added longevity and to keep Focus Sash intact against opposing Fake Out. Transform can be used to utilize Smeargle as an offensive threat and win condition, especially when transforming into partner Calyrex-S or opposing Restricted Pokemon. Smeargle requires Focus Sash to make up for its horrendous bulk. Smeargle can also opt for an EV spread of 252 HP / 252 Def with a Relaxed nature and 0 Speed IVs on Trick Room teams, enabling Smeargle to boost its partners with Decorate before they attack. Moody is the primary ability on Smeargle, as it has a good chance of allowing Smeargle to take more attacks or threaten fast Spore. Calyrex-I teams can utilize Own Tempo to make sure Smeargle is always slow to function under Trick Room. Smeargle prefers Tera Ghost to escape Fake Out, but it may use Tera Grass on a team with Farigiraf for the immunity to Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss, as well as the resistance to Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes, which would otherwise OHKO it through Focus Sash.

Smeargle struggles due to its lack of offensive pressure as a full support Pokemon. This makes it incredibly vulnerable to Taunt from Pokemon like Tornadus and Incineroar. Smeargle also lacks longevity, even with Focus Sash, so its chances to support its allies are limited. Hence, Smeargle is strongest with incredibly offensive Restricted Pokemon like the Calyrex formes. Smeargle's Follow Me and Fake Out helps the Calyrex formes set up Nasty Plot and Trick Room, respectively. Smeargle also protects them with Wide Guard from opposing Calyrex-S and Kyogre, which can otherwise threaten major damage if not an OHKO.
