These teams will usually carry Urshifu-R and Ursaluna-B to threaten Incineroar. The two also appreciate Smeargle's support as some of the most oppressive non-Restricted Pokemon available. Farigiraf can pair with Smeargle on hyper offensive Calyrex-I teams to form a strong Trick Room core and enable Smeargle to utilize Tera Grass without fear of Fake Out and Prankster Taunt.

Sticky Web Lead.description:
• Due to having nearly every move in the game, Smeargle has fantastic qualities as a versatile suicide lead and Sticky Web setter for hyper offense teams due to the large amount of roles it can compress, such as being able to anti-lead opposing hyper offense leads, punishing entry hazard removers with status, controlling hazards on either side of the field, and minimizing impact from Taunt users. These combined factors make it difficult to shut down Smeargle.
  • Sticky Web can help to enable threats such as Eruption Primal Groudon, wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, and Ultra Necrozma by letting them outpace threats such as Deoxys-A and Zacian-C.
  • Nuzzle can cripple common Taunt users such as Yveltal, Arceus-Dark, and Arceus-Fairy. Spore is great for crippling opposing hyper offense leads such as Shuckle and Iron Treads. Both options are also valuable in order to punish attempts to remove Smeargle's hazards from Ho-Oh and Giratina-O.
  • Rapid Spin or Mortal Spin allows Smeargle to clear hazards from opposing hyper offense leads such as Shuckle and Mega Diancie. Rapid Spin is more valuable if Smeargle needs to clear hazards from Steel-types such as Necrozma-DM, and it provides a Speed boost to cripple threats such as Yveltal and Palkia-O with Spore or Nuzzle. Mortal Spin can clear hazards against spinblockers such as Lunala and Arceus-Ghost and poison them in the process, but it's at the cost of being more susceptible to Tera Steel Pokemon such as Yveltal. The poison chip damage is also valued by Smeargle's partners such as Ultra Necrozma and Rayquaza to break through checks like Arceus-Dark easier.
  • Perish Song prevents Dragon Dance Zygarde from using Smeargle as setup fodder to facilitate a sweep from the lead slot. Due to the frailty of most hyper offense teams Zygarde is often able to sweep if it uses Dragon Dance twice, while Dragon Tail's phasing makes it easier for the opposing team to remove Sticky Web. Ceaseless Edge and Stone Axe can grant Smeargle access to extra utility with unblockable hazards.
  • Smeargle's moveset is very flexible and can be mixed and matched to however you feel to deal with specific scenarios. Running Parting Shot or Teleport can generate momentum for the team while still preserving Smeargle potentially, and running both Stone Axe and Ceaseless Edge in the last two moveslots is possible if you don't care about opposing hazards. However, the given moveset is generally the most optimized variant of Smeargle.
  • Technician is the default ability of choice to slightly increase the damage output of Smeargle's utility-focused attacks, without potential inconsistencies by becoming slower at the end of a turn with Moody, but otherwise Moody is a viable alternative to punish passive play from the opponent.
  • Tera Ghost and Steel are used only for dealing with opposing suicide leads such as Iron Treads and Glimmora in order to block their attempts to clear Smeargle's hazards with Rapid Spin and Mortal Spin, respectively. Terastallization should only be used on Smeargle for absolute emergencies, as it takes the opportunity away from its wallbreaking partners.
  • Smeargle only should be used as a lead in order to enable its teammates as fast as possible.
  • Attempts to conserve Smeargle for use later in the game are unnecessary, as its sacrifice generates momentum for its teammates.
  • After setting Sticky Web, Smeargle should make every effort to keep Sticky Web up and spread status for as long as possible before it goes down.
  • In addition to partners such as Dragon Dance Rayquaza and Arceus enjoying Smeargle's Sticky Web to outpace threats like Zacian-C and Marshadow, Smeargle can benefit from spinblockers such as Arceus-Ghost and your own Zacian-C to block Rapid Spin and Mortal Spin, respectively. Nasty Plot Chi-Yu's strong matchups against common forms of hazard removal such as Ho-oh and Yveltal also makes it a great partner for Smeargle.

Entry Hazard Setter.description:
Thanks to Smeargle's nearly endless movepool, it finds a place in the metagame as the premier entry hazard setter for hyper offensive Normal teams. Ceaseless Edge and Stone Axe are able to set up Spikes and Stealth Rock, ignoring Magic Bounce from Hatterene. Sticky Web support is the driving force behind hyper offensive Normal teams, as the Speed reduction greatly helps its powerful wallbreakers such as Terapagos and Ursaluna. Spore, in tandem with Focus Sash, allows Smeargle to immobilize a foe for a few turns, giving Smeargle an opportunity to set up hazards.

Hisuian Zoroark is a great teammate for Smeargle, as its Ghost typing blocks Rapid Spin; it also appreciates the wide range of entry hazards Smeargle can provide, which aids its wallbreaking capabilities. With Sticky Web set up, Hisuian Zoroark is able to outspeed Choice Scarf Great Tusk and Choice Scarf Gholdengo, stopping them from revenge killing it. Terapagos is another incredibly strong wallbreaking teammate that thrives with entry hazard support. Tera Starstorm turns from a 3HKO to a 2HKO on Pokemon such as Clodsire and Swampert. Terapagos also has a lot of great coverage moves, such as Earth Power for Steel- and Fire-types like Heatran and Ceruledge and Ice Beam for Flying-types such as Landorus and Gliscor. Braviary is a strong physical attacker that takes advantage of Smeargle's Sticky Web support, as its Defiant ability punishes Defog. Indeedee is also a great teammate, as its Psychic-type support helps greatly in the Poison and Fighting matchups. Psychic Terrain also protects its teammates against priority moves, blocking foes such as Hisuian Samurott, Bisharp, and Scizor from revenge killing setup sweepers. Ditto can take advantage of Sticky Web, having an easier time coming in for revenge kills against Choice Scarf users such as Meowscarada and Great Tusk.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

With access to virtually every move it could want, Smeargle can run other move combinations to deny entry hazard removal. Curse + Conversion lets Smeargle spinblock non-Scrappy Great Tusk and Iron Treads while punishing most setup sweepers from using it as setup fodder; this also grants its team a free switch under the right circumstances. Taunt and Encore deny or punish Defog and setup attempts. Memento and Healing Wish grant Smeargle's team a safe switch and deny Rapid Spin, and Spikes can be opted for over Stealth Rock.

Checks and Counters

Entry Hazard Removers: Rapid Spin users like Great Tusk and Iron Treads as well as Defog Corviknight all can remove the entry hazards Smeargle has set up. While Smeargle has options to deny removal attempts, the same cannot be said when it is off the field. Cinderace notably punishes Smeargle with Court Change, and it thus needs to be careful with when it sets up hazards.

Setup Sweepers: Setup Sweepers like IronPress Zamazenta, Swords Dance Kingambit, and Nasty Plot Gholdengo can use Smeargle as setup fodder if it is not running Taunt or Encore.

Fast Choice Scarf or Heavy-Duty Boots Users: Fast Choice Scarf users like Roaring Moon and Meowscarada, as well as Heavy-Duty Boots users like Zamazenta and Cinderace, can outspeed most of Smeargle's teammates, with their items essentially negating the effects of Sticky Web.

Lead.description:
Smeargle's niche lies within its access to every move in the game, including the rare Sticky Web, as well as countless options to deny entry hazard removal and cripple the opposing team. Sticky Web benefits threats that are commonly forced out by speed control options, like Iron Moth, Tail Glow Manaphy, and Nasty Plot Tornadus-T, and appreciate revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Latios and Deoxys-S being slowed down. Rapid Spin allows Smeargle to remove any hazards that may have been set on its side of the field by a faster Prankster user and pairs well with Imprison, which it completely shut down Rapid Spin as a means of removing the Sticky Web it sets up. Imprison also denies Stealth Rock from being set up against Smeargle if it is run. Stealth Rock can be used as an additional entry hazard for Sticky Web teams, which usually lack sources of residual damage, while Burning Bulwark can be used as an alternative to cripple strong physical attackers that might pose a threat to frailer hyper offense teams like Zamazenta and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon.

Smeargle's best teammates tend to be wallbreakers that struggle with speed control like the aforementioned Iron Moth and Manaphy; however, even setup sweepers that have great Speed stats like IronPress Zamazenta and Swords Dance Garchomp pair well with it, deterring their usual revenge killers like Deoxys-S and Choice Scarf Scream Tail from forcing them out. Smeargle's entry hazards can be easily removed once it is off the field by spinners like Great Tusk and Iron Treads, making a solid Ghost-type like Gholdengo or Sinistcha a must-have. While Corviknight is capable of Defogging Smeargle's entry hazards away, Smeargle is capable of stalling out Defog's PP and forcing its hazards up as long as it remains on the field.

Rapid Spin.description:
Hitmontop is unviable in PU, as it is generally outclassed as a Fighting-type by other Pokemon such as Paldean Tauros-F, Hariyama, and Pawmot and as a form of offense entry hazard control by the likes of Tatsugiri and Scyther.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

zu.comments:
Other Options

Fake Out benefits from Technician, though Hitmontop struggles to fit it over its other priority moves without becoming less consistent as a revenge killer. Alternative items like Assault Vest and Heavy-Duty Boots can be valid options with solid item removal support to get rid of Rocky Helmets from users like Mesprit and Weezing.

Checks and Counters

Weezing: Although Weezing doesn't stop Hitmontop from removing entry hazards, it can comfortably wall its attacks, threaten debilitating burns with Will-O-Wisp, and keep itself healthy with Pain Split. If Hitmontop loses or lacks Protective Pads and uses Triple Axel, then Weezing can inflict a ton of damage with Rocky Helmet.

Residual Damage: Hitmontop is worn down quickly by Spikes and Toxic Spikes because it doesn't hold Heavy-Duty Boots and almost never runs any recovery. If Hitmontop loses its Protective Pads, it's liable to being worn down by Rocky Helmet users like Mesprit, which carries Knock Off.

Whimsicott and Tera Fairy Users: Although Hitmontop has Bullet Punch to threaten many Fairy-types, particularly the frail Whimsicott, it's often not strong enough to OHKO them. Whimsicott outspeeds Hitmontop, resists Mach Punch, and can threaten an OHKO with Moonblast if it's holding a Choice Specs. Similarly, Tera Fairy users like Magneton and Jolteon can use the offensive and defensive benefits of the Fairy typing to improve their matchups against Hitmontop.

Flying-types: If Hitmontop can't outspeed Flying-types and take them out with Triple Axel, then it can be left in a vulnerable position due to only having a potentially resisted priority move. Charizard can neuter Hitmontop with a burn from Will-O-Wisp if it doesn't just take it out with STAB Hurricane. Drifblim can spinblock against Hitmontop and threaten to burn it, but it takes a substantial amount of damage from Triple Axel.

Sableye: Hitmontop struggles to use Rapid Spin or even Close Combat if Sableye can switch in and lock it into these moves with Encore, and Sableye can also threaten to burn Hitmontop.

Rapid Spin.description:
Hitmontop is a solid offensive entry hazard remover for its uncommon access to Rapid Spin, solid matchups against spinblockers such as Spiritomb and Trevenant, and high threat level from Close Combat and Technician-boosted Triple Axel. Triple Axel threatens checks to Hitmonotp like Whimsicott and Trevenant, and it also pressures Ice-weak physically defensive Pokemon like Dipplin and Sandslash. Bullet Punch and Mach Punch are important offensive utility to make up for Hitmontop's middling Speed, finishing off weakened sweepers and threatening faster Pokemon. Bullet Punch, despite not benefitting from STAB, is preferred over Mach Punch for its stronger matchups against Whimsicott, Tera Fairy Jolteon, and Hisuian Sneasel. However, Mach Punch is still a fine option and distinguishes itself by improving Hitmontop's potential to pick off Fighting-weak Pokemon like Sneasel, Lycanroc, and Beartic, as well as Basculin. All of Triple Axel, Bullet Punch, and Mach Punch benefit from Hitmontop's Technician powering them up, giving Hitmontop enough power to generally OHKO weakened Minior with Bullet Punch and assuredly OHKO offensive Venusaur with Triple Axel. As Hitmontop's moves make contact and it often runs into Rocky Helmet users like Mesprit and Weezing, Hitmontop should run Protective Pads to worry less about taking massive residual damage by using Triple Axel. Running 176 Speed EVs lets Hitmontop outspeed neutral-natured variants of Abomasnow, Clawitzer, and Farigiraf, and +1 Hitmontop will outspeed Charizard. With Tera Steel, Hitmontop can better shrug off Psychic-, Fairy-, and Flying-type attacks from special attackers like Mesprit, Whimsicott, and Minior; it also boosts Bullet Punch.

As an offensive spinner, Hitmontop's entry hazard removal is appreciated by more offensive teams that want to keep hazards off for threats such as non-Heavy-Duty Boots Jolteon, Clawitzer, Sneasel, Whimsicott, and Basculin. Similarly, Hitmontop is a good fit as the hazard remover for Sticky Web teams anchored by Vikavolt, which can check Mesprit and Weezing. As Hitmontop can be quite threatening against walls like Regirock and Cryogonal if it's given a free switch against them, it pairs nicely with pivots like Vikavolt, Jolteon, and Mesprit that tend to draw them in. Whimsicott can put Hitmontop on the back foot by outspeeding it and threatening it with STAB Moonblast, so Hitmontop should be paired with teammates like Muk, Articuno, and Charizard that can switch into Whimsicott until it's safely in range of being KOed by Bullet Punch. Mesprit is another threat that can bother Hitmontop, making Steel-types that answer it, such as Perrserker and Magneton, good partners. Weezing is a major pain for Hitmontop, making switch-ins to it, such as Mesprit, important.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Elekid is an elite pivot in Little Cup, with an unmatched Speed tier and a wide range of coverage options that threaten much of the metagame. Vital Spirit provides teams another option to switch in on Spore from Foongus. Elekid's moveset is highly customizable to fit the role it plays on a team. Thunderbolt threatens high damage on Vullaby, Mareanie, and Wingull. Knock Off can weaken checks such as Mudbray and Chinchou for Elekid to KO them later in the game. Focus Blast can be used over either Thunderbolt or Knock Off to OHKO Alolan Diglett and Alolan Sandshrew. Psychic hits Foongus and Mienfoo super effectively. Volt Switch offers frail attackers such as Wingull and Stunky a safe way to enter the field on the switches that Elekid forces, while Ice Punch can be used to KO Toedscool after minimal chip from Knock Off or Psychic. Alternatively, Tera Blast Grass is used to more directly threaten the aforementioned Chinchou and Mudbray. Tera Psychic boosts the damage of Psychic against targets like Mienfoo, Foongus, and Glimmet and also makes Elekid resistant to Choice Scarf Gothita's Psychic.

Elekid complements powerful but frail Pokemon like Alolan Diglett and Wingull through Volt Switch, offering safe entry for them to wallbreak. Additionally, Elekid can use Tera Blast Grass to remove their checks such as Mudbray and Chinchou, respectively. Elekid struggles to break through Grass-types like Foongus and Grookey, so Vullaby and Alolan Sandshrew make good teammates. In return, Elekid can threaten opposing Alolan Sandshrew for Vullaby and Mareanie for ally Alolan Sandshrew. Without Tera Blast Grass, Elekid struggles to get past Mudbray. A partner that can weaken Mudbray like Vullaby or Stunky can help with this.

Calm Mind.description: Blissey is the best special wall in Ubers UU thanks to Calm Mind and reliable recovery. Shadow Ball hits Mewtwo and Deoxys hard on the switch while also helping it beat Solgaleo and Spectrier. Alternatively, Ice Beam 2HKOes Landorus and Great Tusk. Calm Mind is important for Blissey to keep up with the few special attackers that are too strong for it to stall initially, like Chi-Yu and Palkia-O under rain, while also boosting alongside Pokemon like Calm Mind Hatterene and Arceus-Electric. Seismic Toss provides consistent damage output that Blissey is usually devoid of. Tera Dark is needed for Blissey to resist Arceus-Dark's Judgment and be immune to Stored Power and Psyshock from Hatterene and Psystrike from Mewtwo. Blissey is incredibly specially bulky, which makes it a great teammate for Pokemon like Great Tusk and Dondozo, which are very specially frail. In turn, physical walls like Great Tusk and Giratina help Blissey out immensely, as they can take care of the physical threats to Blissey, like Palafin-H, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T. Giratina is an especially good pairing with Blissey, as it can switch into the Fighting-type moves Blissey is weak to and burn the threat to neutralize it.

Pink Blob (Specially Defensive).description:
• Blissey functions as an blanket check to special attackers on balance and stall teams, being especially useful against hard-to-check special threats such as Calm Mind Miraidon, Chi-Yu, Iron Bundle, and Walking Wake.
  • Seismic Toss is Blissey's only way to reliably deal damage to most opposing Pokemon, while Shadow Ball is able to do decent damage to Flutter Mane.
  • Thunder Wave is extremely useful to cripple common switch-ins such as Koraidon and can also find use against Flutter Mane and Terastallized Miraidon.
  • Blissey is a reliable setter of Stealth Rock, which can free up moveslots on Great Tusk and Iron Treads, but you should note that opposing Great Tusk and Iron Treads as well as Corviknight have little difficulty clearing entry hazards on Blissey.
  • The Tera Type is quite flexible. Tera Ground is very useful against Calm Mind + Parabolic Charge Miraidon sets, as it completely negates their recovery and allows Blissey to force out them out.
  • Tera Fire gives Blissey the ability to better take on Chi-Yu, with Heavy-Duty Boots negating the Stealth Rock weakness.
  • Tera Ghost provides a Fighting-type immunity and allows Blissey to switch out of Dugtrio and Gothitelle.
  • Solid defensive walls such as Skeledirge, Great Tusk, Dondozo, Scream Tail, and Dachsbun are good teammates to take on physical attackers like Koraidon that commonly come in on Blissey.
  • Blissey is not capable of handling all Miraidon sets on its own, so Ting-Lu, Clodsire, and Iron Treads are heavily recommended teammates. In turn, these Ground-types have less pressure on them to stay healthy and can focus more on setting entry hazards.
  • Care should be taken against Miraidon and Iron Bundle, which often use pivoting moves or Taunt to gain momentum on Blissey. Proper prediction with Blissey's teammates may be required to handle this.
  • As a result, Rocky Helmet is an option, as it does damage to U-turn, Flip Turn, and Electro Drift users, making Miraidon and Iron Bundle unable to pivot on Blissey for free. If running Rocky Helmet, make sure you have plenty of Pokemon that can deal with entry hazards, such as Corviknight, Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Hatterene.
  • Flutter Mane is difficult for Blissey to reliably check due to Taunt and Psyshock sets, so Corviknight and Garganacl can help pick up the slack. In return, both appreciate Blissey being a safe switch-in to Iron Bundle.

Defensive.description:
With its staggering special bulk, Blissey is the greatest wall to most special attackers in the tier. Thanks to Natural Cure, it also acts as a solid status absorber, preventing the likes of Pecharunt's Malignant Chain, Galarian Slowking's Toxic, and Dragapult's Will-O-Wisp from ruining it permanently. Calm Mind gives Blissey a way to check dangerous setup sweepers like Gholdengo, Darkrai, and Raging Bolt more reliably, able to match their Special Attack boosts with its own Special Defense boosts, as well as boosting its coverage moves in case it runs them. Seismic Toss is Blissey's go-to damaging move, compensating for its lack of offensive stats and preventing it from being entirely passive. Blissey can also be used to compress roles as the team's Stealth Rock setter, giving it another way to wear down the opposing team, as its longevity and bulk allow Blissey to set Stealth Rock multiple times over the course of a game. If another Stealth Rock setter is present, it can run either Shadow Ball to hit problematic Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Dragapult as well as Tera Ghost users like Primarina and Raging Bolt looking to exploit its Seismic Toss or Flamethrower to similarly hit Gholdengo hard and fish for burns in longer games, especially against phsyical attackers like Ogerpon-W and Kingambit attempting to switch in and threaten Blissey out. Protect is a niche option that allows Blissey to safely absorb Future Sight, scout Choice item users like Gholdengo and Darkrai, stall out weather turns, and waste the PP of powerful moves like Close Combat, Headlong Rush, and Pyro Ball. Heal Bell is also an option, allowing Blissey to take a cleric role for the team, particularly helpful to support Rest Dondozo.

With such high HP, Blissey chooses to invest EVs in Defense and Special Defense instead, still bolstering its absurd special bulk while lessening the damage from physical moves that would otherwise chip it down, particularly improving its matchup against mixed attackers like Dragapult. While Heavy-Duty Boots is preferred to prevent it from being overwhelmed by entry hazards in longer games, Leftovers can be used if the team has strong hazard removal options; in particular, this improves the rolls of avoiding the 2HKO from Choice Specs Protosynthesis Tera Water Modest Walking Wake on sun, which can otherwise be a difficult matchup for stall teams without expending Tera Water on Blissey. Tera Dark gives Blissey a crucial Psychic immunity, allowing it to ignore the dangerous Psyshock, Stored Power, Psychic Noise, and Future Sight from the likes of Hatterene, Primarina, and Gholdengo. Tera Water offers Blissey a resistance to Water and Fire, useful for checking threats like Choice Specs Walking Wake under sun and Heatran. Tera Fairy is a niche option that turns Blissey's Fighting weakness into a resistance as well as a better matchup against mixed attackers like Dragapult and Iron Valiant. Tera Poison or Steel can be used to let it stay in and check Nasty Plot Pecharunt, with the former also letting it take on Fighting-types like Zamazenta in a pinch and the latter giving it a better matchup against even mixed Kyurem.

Blissey's titanic bulk makes it mandatory on stall teams, which can tolerate its passive nature. Dondozo pairs exceptionally well with Blissey, forming an excellent stalwart defensive core that can wall the vast majority of threats in the metagame. Blissey also enjoys teammates like Alomomola, Gliscor, and Clefable, which can switch into physical threats like Great Tusk and Zamazenta that Blissey cannot wall, as well as absorb Knock Off that would otherwise cripple Blissey, while Blissey can handle special attackers like Raging Bolt and Iron Moth that would threaten Blissey's teammates. Another excellent partner is Clodsire, which can check boosted special threats like Darkrai, Gholdengo, and Raging Bolt that can overwhelm Blissey throughout a game, with the pairing making stall team's sturdiest backbone against the metagame's special attackers. Furthermore, either Blissey or Clodsire can run Stealth Rock, freeing up the other to run moves like Heal Bell or Flamethrower for Blissey or Amnesia for Clodsire, and running Tera Dark on Clodsire gives Blissey more freedom to run Tera Water. Corviknight also works well with Blissey, serving as a Knock Off absorber, entry hazard remover, and a check against dangerous physical threats like Kingambit and Zamazenta. Galarian Weezing is also an adept Defogger and a check to physical attackers like Zamazenta, Hisuian Samurott, and Lokix that can threaten Blissey out.

Pink Blob.description:
Although it competes for a teamslot with its bulkier pre-evolution, Blissey retains a niche thanks to a couple of traits that are of interest to certain bulky and stall teams. Notably, Blissey does not have to hold Eviolite. Heavy-Duty Boots makes Blissey impervious to entry hazards, something Chansey cannot claim. This makes Blissey significantly less fickle to use than Chansey, which can be vulnerable to entry hazard chip damage otherwise. Leftovers is a viable alternative that gives some passive recovery, a useful trait in matchups versus very powerful special attackers like Tapu Lele, Gholdengo, and sun-boosted Raging Bolt. Blissey is also less crippled by Knock Off, and it can run a Calm Mind set that lets it beat Gholdengo. Seismic Toss lets Blissey to chip every Pokemon that isn't a Ghost-type and allows it to damage any Steel-types looking to switch in on Toxic. Soft-Boiled gives Blissey instant recovery; however, Wish is an alternative with greater PP, which can be useful for the prolonged games that Blissey often finds itself a part of, and it allows Blissey to heal teammates if necessary. However, it also encourages running Protect in the last moveslot, which can be restrictive. Both Wish and Soft-Boiled can be run on the same set to maximize recovery PP and still allow Blissey to pass Wish to its teammates, although Blissey generally prefers other moves in the last moveslot. Toxic allows Blissey to impair threats such as Raging Bolt, Mega Charizard Y, and Mega Latios. This also makes it risky for many physical attackers to switch in, such as Zamazenta, Landorus-T, and Garchomp. Calm Mind is a niche alternative that should only be used on stall teams lacking Clodsire, as it allows Blissey to beat most Gholdengo sets at the cost of becoming extremely passive in many other matchups. Many variants of Blissey can afford to fit Stealth Rock in their moveset, and it has a good matchup versus some hazard removal options like Zapdos and Terapagos. Teleport is an option that gives Blissey a small niche on non-stall teams, as it lets it keep up momentum for some balance teams. Flamethrower is used on the Calm Mind set to beat Gholdengo. An alternative EV spread with maximum HP and Special Defense investment can be considered to make Blissey even bulkier specially and notably let it survive a +6 Supersonic Skystrike off of Bleakwind Storm from specific stallbreaking variants of Tornadus-T, but this noticeably worsens Blissey's already poor physical bulk, and the benefits are generally very marginal.

Blissey is primarily seen on stall teams as a special wall that handles dangerous wallbreakers such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Latios, and Volcarona. Thanks to Heavy-Duty Boots, Blissey is much less reliant on entry hazard control from the likes of Mega Sableye and Corviknight than Chansey is, which can make it much less restrictive to build with and facilitate. As Blissey's defensive profile is inherently flawed due to its passivity and bad physical bulk, it needs teammates that can reliably switch into dangerous physical wallbreakers such as Zamazenta, Urshifu-R, and Garchomp. Dondozo is an excellent choice that blanket checks the vast majority of physical attackers in the tier thanks to its immense physical bulk, access to Curse, and Unaware, which also lets it beat physically boosting threats like Dragonite and Swords Dance Urshifu. Iron Defense Corviknight and Skarmory are also good choices, as they do a great job of pressuring certain physically boosting wallbreakers like Kingambit, Ursaluna, and Mega Mawile. Blissey is also very poor against Gholdengo if it isn't running Calm Mind. Clodsire is a nice option that counters all relevant Gholdengo sets, and it also takes pressure off Blissey to check other special attackers. Gliscor is another great partner that fits on stall, as it can stack hazards for its team and give Blissey a Knock Off absorber that still checks Gholdengo. Blissey can also pass all of these Pokemon Wish, which is helpful even in spite of their own recovery moves so they can preserve their PP and not waste turns recovering themselves, and it also means that Dondozo doesn't have to shut itself down with Rest. Teleport is to be run on more balanced teams. While it competes with the excellent Galarian Slowking and Assault Vest Alomomola as a specially defensive pivot, Blissey's sheer special bulk and lack of relevant special weaknesses make it superior against certain wallbreakers, such as Mega Latios, Mega Charizard Y, and Raging Bolt. On such teams, Blissey can pivot in strong wallbreakers such as Zamazenta, Garchomp, and Landorus-T. These especially appreciate Blissey baiting in Steel-types for them to take advantage of with a free switch.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Healing Wish enables Blissey to bring a teammate such as Porygon2 or Ursaluna back up to full HP in matchups where they are vastly preferred over Blissey. Shadow Ball, while a major decrease in pressure compared to Seismic Toss, prevents Blissey from being hard-walled by Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Froslass.

Defensive.description:
Blissey is an invaluable wall on Normal teams thanks to its gigantic HP and incredible Special Defense, making it the premier special wall for the type, easily handling threats like Landorus, Latios, and Darkrai. Seismic Toss acts as Blissey's main form of damage, providing a consistent form of pressure against bulky targets like Moltres and Toxapex. Stealth Rock wears down would-be problems for Normal teams like Enamorus and Ogerpon-H. Finally, Thunder Wave can cripple offensive threats such as Flutter Mane and Iron Moth, making it far easier for teammates like Ursaluna and Hisuian Zoroark to outspeed and remove them. The main EV spread maximizes Blissey's Defense, enabling Blissey to handle weak physical attackers like Clodsire comfortably. The alternative EV spread still retains respectable physical bulk while increasing Blissey's capabilities to handle special attacks from foes such as Kyurem.

Porygon2 serves as a wonderful physically bulky Pokemon to complement Blissey; it handles threats like physical Dragapult, Landorus-T, and Ogerpon-W while appreciating Blissey checking threats like Zapdos and Greninja for Porygon2. Braviary can also work as a physically bulky support for Blissey, being capable of handling Ground- and Fighting-types like Excadrill, Great Tusk, and Sneasler along with providing Defog support should Blissey lose its Heavy-Duty Boots. Hisuian Zoroark checks Ghost-types such as Gholdengo and Sinistcha that Blissey is unable to hit, along with checking Body Press from the likes of Skarmory and Avalugg. Terapagos can provide Rapid Spin support for Blissey and has coverage options like Ice Beam and Flamethrower to handle foes like Gliscor and Scizor, respectively. Ursaluna can eliminate bulky targets such as Hatterene, Hippowdon, and opposing Blissey quickly while appreciating its own Blissey's Thunder Wave, enabling Ursaluna to outspeed Choice Specs Greninja and Iron Crown. Choice Scarf Ditto can copy threats like Swords Dance Iron Hands, which attempt to use Blissey as setup fodder, and turn that power against them. Ditto also helps to stall out bulky walls like Amoonguss and Tornadus-T, which are not particularly bothered by Blissey. Choice Scarf Indeedee-M can outspeed and check problematic Fighting-types like Choice Specs Keldeo, Great Tusk, and Iron Valiant and provides Healing Wish should Blissey need it.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Calm Mind Support.description:
• The old reliable special wall is still viable, but it now takes a more active role through the use of Calm Mind.

  • Flamethrower: Flamethrower is great at hitting Tera Steel users like Latios that are commonly employed against stall teams.

  • Alluring Voice: Alluring Voice catches targets trying to set up alongside Blissey, confusing them if they boosted their stats in the same turn.

  • Fling with Poison Barb: Fling with Poison Barb gives Blissey a one-time opportunity to poison foes, and is preferred over Toxic Orb since it doesn't poison Blissey itself prior to being thrown. Fling also gets rid of Choice items from Trick users.

  • Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock remains a trusty support move for Blissey, punishing teams that are forced to switch around Blissey and its teammates.

Other Options

  • Shadow Ball: Shadow Ball can deal good damage to special Ghost-type sweepers like Flutter Mane and Gholdengo. However, Blissey will no longer be able to reliably hit Ursaluna-B, which is a matchup Blissey is normally expected to handle.

  • Fling with Flame Orb or Toxic Orb: This is as close as it gets to Blissey regaining Toxic, though getting burned or badly poisoned is devestating if Blissey is the last Pokemon around, making it a risky option.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Blissey is known for shrugging off big special hits with ease. However, its presence at team preview often attracts hard counters, and Tera is one way of dealing with that.

  • Steel: Steel Tera resists the STAB attacks of Latios and Archuladon while also granting a Fairy resistance for the Flutter Mane matchup. It also prevents poison, which can otherwise force Blissey to switch out.

  • Dark: Dark Tera completely ruins Latios's attempts to break through Blissey with Stored Power or Psychic Noise, at least forcing a Calm Mind war. However, Blissey becomes much more vulnerable to Choice Specs Flutter Mane.

  • Ghost: The Fighting-type immunity comes in handy for Blissey and prevents it from being trapped, though it does become more vulnerable to Gholdengo.

  • Water: Tera Water puts the brakes on Choice Specs Tera Fire Chi-Yu’s wallbreaking parade, ruining its ability to reliably 2HKO Blissey.

Items

  • Poison Barb: Poison Barb complements Fling, letting Blissey use poison to outlast targets that can't heal.

  • Covert Cloak: Covert Cloak grants a huge immunity to the healing block of Psychic Noise. Beyond that, it is also fantastic for blocking the passive damage from Garganacl's Salt Cure, flinches from Chi-Yu's Dark Pulse, and Special Defense drops from Latios's Luster Purge.

  • Leftovers: As is the case with most walls, Leftovers’ passive recovery is a great supplement to Softboiled and helps Blissey be less passive itself.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 Def / 252 SpD with Calm or Bold: Beyond making Tera Blissey that much harder to break by foes like Ursaluna-B and Chi-Yu, going all-in on Special Defense means less frequent Softboiled uses against special attackers, especially with Leftovers.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spd with Bold: Maximizing both HP and Defense gives Blissey a little extra boost in physical bulk.

Bulky Offense.description: • This set does not have a full write-up yet. If you'd like to finish this, feel free to reserve it here!

Special Wall.description: Blissey is a decent, albeit niche, wall and utility Pokemon in AAA with its ability to check most special attackers and extremely diverse movepool. Seismic Toss allows Blissey to not be completely passive and gives it consistent damage. Blissey's last two moveslots are flexible. Calm Mind + Shadow Ball is enough to beat the few special attackers that can otherwise defeat Blissey one-on-one such as Sheer Force Gengar and Gholdengo. Stealth Rock provides entry hazard support to free up a moveslot for a teammate, while Thunder Wave spreads status, crippling Pokemon like Azelf and Manaphy, and Heal Bell allows Blissey to operate as a cleric. Unaware allows Blissey to check special attackers attempting to set up on it like Gholdengo, Tail Glow Manaphy, and Iron Moth, while Well-Baked Body allows it to check Iron Moth while also giving it a more favorable matchup into Volcarona and Heatran. Magic Guard allows Blissey to avoid chip damage from entry hazards, letting it function as a better wall. Blissey most commonly runs Leftovers, as the extra healing can be extremely helpful, although on teams with more shaky hazard control, Heavy-Duty Boots can be opted for instead. A Calm nature is used to make Blissey function better as a special wall, notiably allowing it to always avoid the 2HKO from Sheer Force Gengar's Focus Blast. Blissey is most notably a special wall that does not require the use of Regenerator, which allows physical walls such as Great Tusk to run it instead. Blissey is most commonly seen on stall and fat team structures. Physically defensive walls like Corviknight and Deoxys-D are a must, as they help deal with Blissey's weakness to physical attackers and make a potent defensive core with it.

balancedhackmons.overview: Blissey is a solid special wall thanks to its gargantuan HP and good Special Defense, allowing it to tank almost any special attack. This special bulk allows Blissey to forgo Ice Scales for abilities like Magic Guard and Regenerator that give it extra survivability against all forms of chip damage. Its low Attack also lets it deny Strength Sap's healing from most special attackers like Miraidon and Arceus-Fairy. Blissey has the fatal flaw of having nonexistent Defense, so it is forced out by physical attackers; however, this can also be used to your advantage to offensively Imposter-proof Blissey with said attackers. Blissey faces competition from Chansey as a Magic Guard user because of Chansey's increased bulk from Eviolite; however, Blissey has the advantage of not being deterred as much by Knock Off. Additionally, Blissey is quite passive, especially against Regenerator users, so it can struggle to progress the game apart from slow pivoting.
balancedhackmons.comments:
Other Options

Status-inducing moves such as Glare and Toxic are potential options on the Magic Guard set, but they make Blissey far too passive without providing other utility to be worth it. Miscellaneous utility abilities like Drought and Pressure can be utilized on specific teams, but they are generally niche.

Checks and Counters

Physical Attackers: Blissey's abysmal Defense means that virtually any physical attacker threatens it. They have to be careful of Burning Bulwark, however.

Attackers That Target Defense: In a similar vein, Blissey cannot check mixed attackers like High Jump Kick Mega Sceptile and Secret Sword or Psystrike users like Arceus-Ghost and Mega Gardevoir, since they target Blissey's Defense stat.

Regenerator Users: Regenerator users like Ting-Lu can shrug off Ruinations from Blissey and use it as an entry point for their various utility.

Pain Split Flutter Mane: With Pain Split, Flutter Mane can heavily damage Blissey while healing itself to full HP every time, wasting Blissey's recovery PP and weakening it so other foes such as Eternatus can break through it.

Magic Guard.description:
With Magic Guard, Blissey is immune to all kinds of passive damage like entry hazards, Thunder Cage chip damage, and poison. This lets Blissey very consistently check most special attackers without fear of said passive damage cutting into its longevity. Shore Up is the preferred move option thanks to its consistency, though Wish can also be used as an alternative for more PP and the ability to heal other teammates. Ruination, compared with the Strength Sap blocking potential of Blissey, will completely brick most Strength Sap reliant foes that aren't physical while efficiently wasting recovery PP from other foes that rely on it. It also prevents Blissey from being entirely passive, though it's still questionable against Regenerator users. Topsy-Turvy deters setup from various special attackers, like Torch Song Mega Sceptile and Take Heart Arceus-Fairy. Burning Bulwark scouts moves, especially from Choice Band users like Mega Garchomp thinking they can use Blissey as a free entry point to start wallbreaking only to get permanently crippled by a burn, while additionally letting Blissey use Wish safely. However, it can make Blissey hard to Imposter-proof offensively with your own physical attackers. Teleport is the preferred pivoting move thanks to its negative priority, but Parting Shot can also be used to annoy switch-ins with lowered offenses, and U-turn bypasses Taunt.

Blissey's ability to block Strength Sap's healing means that virtually every single Choice Band user appreciates it, especially ones that are slower and thus more vulnerable to Strength Sap neutralizing them like Mega Blaziken. Additionally, they can also reverse Imposter-proof Blissey if it's not carrying Burning Bulwark. Other teammates like RegenVest Celesteela and Ice Scales Arceus-Steel appreciate Blissey checking threats they cannot, such as Encore Miraidon, alongside the occasional Imposter-proofing that Blissey can provide. Blissey is vulnerable to foes that run coverage specifically for it like Shell Side Arm Eternatus and Secret Sword Arceus-Ghost, strong physical attackers like Ash-Greninja using it as an entry point, and mixed attackers like Ultra Necrozma. Therefore solid checks to them like Fur Coat Mega Audino, Ice Scales Arceus-Ground, and RegenVest Ting-Lu make for good partners. Fast offensive teammates like Koraidon also synergize well with Wish variants of Blissey to revenge kill setup threats weakened by Ruination.

Regenerator.description: Blissey uses its enormous special bulk and minimal Attack to simultaneously wall special threats and disrupt their Strength Sap recovery while maintaining momentum from Regenerator. Knock Off is a staple move on RegenVest users, while Wish in conjunction with Blissey's HP helps keep teammates healthy. Ruination reduces Blissey's passivity, though Salt Cure is an alternative that can be more effective into Pokemon like Celesteela and Flare Boost Flutter Mane. Clear Smog, Topsy-Turvy, and Glare prevent Blissey from being setup fodder, with the latter being particularly useful against Magic Guard Eternatus and Imposter users, while Stone Axe provides utility if setup control is not necessary. Assault Vest further amplifies Blissey's Special Defense against powerful wallbreakers like Mega Alakazam that could otherwise outdamage Regenerator healing, while Heavy-Duty Boots prevents entry hazard damage and allows Blissey to access the aforementioned status moves. Blissey pairs incredibly well with very fast offensive Pokemon like Mega Alakazam and Mega Sceptile, as it provides slow pivoting, Wish support to offset residual damage for Mega Alakazam and allow Mega Sceptile to forgo Strength Sap, and healing denial against special walls like Ice Scales Arceus formes, while they revenge-kill numerous threats that Blissey can pivot into, especially those that Blissey cannot beat by itself such as Eternatus and Flare Boost Flutter Mane. Strong physical attackers also work well, as they can offensively Imposter-proof Blissey without conceding momentum; particularly, Ash-Greninja can pick off chipped Ice Scales Arceus formes. Blissey cannot handle certain special attackers like Psystrike Mega Alakazam, Shell Side Arm Eternatus, and various Secret Sword users, mandating a secondary special wall like Ice Scales users. Depending on the moveset, Blissey can be Imposter-proofed by other RegenVest users or Magic Guard users.

Specially Defensive.description: Blissey's high Special Defense stat is pivotal to its role as a wall. In addition to its great bulk, it gets access to great utility moves such as Teleport for momentum, Soft-Boiled for reliable recovery and longevity, Toxic to cripple foes, and Stealth Rock to put pressure on Mega Charizard X and Choice Scarf Cinderace. Seismic Toss additionally provides a consistent damaging move to chip incoming Pokemon without the means to recover and deal with special attackers such as Greninja and Landorus by taking hits. Blissey runs Heavy-Duty Boots to prevent passive chip from entry hazards to help it create momentum for its teammates. Staraptor pairs well with Blissey as part of Normal's defensive core with access to Intimidate and ability to take hits from threats such as Great Tusk and physically offensive Iron Valiant. It can also use Defog to remove hazards if Blissey's Heavy-Duty Boots have been removed by Knock Off. Since Blissey is able to take hits from Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Blacephalon, it can freely switch into them and then use Teleport to bring in one of Normal's offensive threats such as Ursaluna, Terapagos, or Mega Lopunny. Ursaluna and Mega Lopunny provide Normal with physical wallbreaking capabilities, while Calm Mind Terapagos can be used as a special wallbreaker. Terapagos can also be used as a bulkier presence to remove hazards with Rapid Spin and poison foes with Toxic. Hisuian Zoroark allows for mind games to be played, as its secondary typing provides an immunity to Fighting. In addition, it is able to disguise itself as a more passive Pokemon such as Blissey to provide a false sense of security to the opponent. Ditto provides a counter to setup Pokemon like Mega Scizor and Ceruledge, being able to transform into them and outspeeding them while also potentially reverse sweeping the opponent's team. Mega Pidgeot provides strong Flying-type coverage with Hurricane against Fighting-types such as Choice Specs Iron Valiant and Kommo-o.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Tera Ground can be used for an immunity to Miraidon's Electro Drift if needed. However, it leaves Blissey susceptible to Water-type moves from Kyogre, making it generally an inferior version of Tera Grass. Thunder Wave is a choice to cripple Tera Poison + Calm Mind users like Kyogre and Arceus-Fairy, as well as Calyrex-S. Heal Bell is a niche supporting option for Blissey, curing status effects like Toxic on Alomomola and Ho-Oh while also awakening Dondozo after Rest. However, these two moves are typically not used, as Blissey benefits more from using others.

Checks and Counters

Physical Attackers: Blissey takes massive damage from physical attackers such as Koraidon, Zacian-C, Arceus, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground.

Taunt Users: Taunt prevents Blissey from using Calm Mind and Soft-Boiled, allowing Taunt users such as Miraidon and Calm Mind Arceus-Ground to break it much more easily.

Psyshock Calyrex-S: Psyshock targets Blissey's poor Physical Defense, allowing Calyrex-S to break through Blissey after boosting its Special Attack.

Trick Users: Choice item users with Trick like Choice Scarf Ribombee and Calyrex-S can cripple Blissey with Trick, as it removes Blissey's Heavy-Duty Boots and locks it into one move, greatly hindering its ability to check opposing Pokemon and making it susceptible to setup.

Knock Off Users: Knock Off users like Gliscor threaten Blissey, as it can be worn down by entry hazards after having Heavy-Duty Boots removed.

Special Wall.description:
Thanks to its tremendous special bulk, Blissey finds itself as a staple on stall teams, comfortably taking special attacks from the likes of Miraidon, Calyrex-S, and Kyogre while staying healthy with Soft-Boiled. Blissey's ability allows it to safely absorb status moves such as Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave from support Arceus formes and Toxic from Eternatus. Calm Mind allows Blissey to check setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Miraidon, Kyogre, and Arceus-Fairy. Shadow Ball allows Blissey to threaten Calyrex-S. If needed, Blissey can also provide teams with Stealth Rock support, but at the cost of being unable to hit Calyrex-S. Seismic Toss enables Blissey to deal consistent damage against non-Ghost-types and Calm Mind users like Kyogre and Arceus-Fairy. Tera Grass provides Blissey with a resistance to Water-type moves from Kyogre, stopping its Choice Specs Water Spout from 2HKOing it, and Electro Drift from Miraidon, though it leaves Blissey susceptible to U-turn. Tera Dark, on the other hand, gives Blissey an immunity to Psyshock from Calyrex-S while keeping a resistance to Astral Barrage, but it also renders it vulnerable to U-turn. Due to already having an enormous HP stat, Blissey prefers to run maximum Defense EVs over maximum HP EVs to help against U-turn Miraidon.

Although Blissey has great Special Defense, it is very vulnerable to physical attacks. Because of this, physically defensive Pokemon such as Dondozo, Alomomola, and Skeledirge complement Blissey very well. Dondozo and Skeledirge can check most physical attackers like Koraidon, Zacian-C, and Arceus, all Pokemon that are very troublesome for Blissey. Alomomola also checks these physical attackers, although not as well as Dondozo and Skeledirge do, and provides Blissey with extra healing support through Wish. In return, Blissey takes hits from strong special attackers, like Miraidon and Calyrex-S, which would otherwise threaten massive damage or outright KO the aforementioned physically defensive Pokemon. Blissey also appreciates other special walls like Ho-Oh and Clodsire, as they help relieve pressure from Taunt Miraidon and Kyogre, which can power through it after enough chip damage. They in turn value Blissey's ability to beat Calm Mind Arceus formes one-on-one. Pokemon like Alolan Muk and Mandibuzz can wall most Calyrex-S sets and switch into Psyshock. Blissey dislikes Knock Off, so Gliscor can be used as a good Knock Off absorber.

ru.overview: Raikou makes for a powerful sweeper and pivot, utilizing its great Special Attack that is further powered up by Calm Mind and Choice Specs. Its speed tier lets it outspeed many opposing threats in the metagame, including Maushold and both non-Choice Scarf Gengar and Jirachi. With Calm Mind, Raikou becomes a dangerous late-game cleaner and wincon because of its potential to break down opposing special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Empoleon. Equipped with a Choice Specs, Raikou can act as a pivot that also serves as a dangerous wallbreaker in the tier. However, it can run Heavy-Duty Boots to prevent chip damage from entry hazards, letting it get on the field more. Furthermore, Raikou's typing gives it resistances to Noivern's Hurricane and Jirachi's Iron Head. With good coverage moves in Scald and Aura Sphere, it's no wonder that Raikou can also threaten Bisharp, Cyclizar, and Rhyperior. However, Raikou's below-average defensive typing makes it vulnerable to Krookodile and Terrakion's Earthquake and in exchange doesn't give it many good resistances. Raikou struggles to break through opposing special walls such as Alolan Muk, Cyclizar without Aura Sphere, and Umbreon. Raikou is also not helped by its rather frail physical bulk, which leaves it prone to many physical priority attacks, namely Crawdaunt's Aqua Jet, Bisharp's Sucker Punch, and Breloom's Mach Punch.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Discharge is an alternative over Thunderbolt that allows Raikou to spread paralysis against opposing walls. However, Raikou prefers to burn its foes with Scald most of the time. Raikou can utilize Choice Scarf over Choice Specs to outpace the entire unboosted metagame, but this comes at the price of its wallbreaking strength. Life Orb also works as an alternative for a bit of extra power on Calm Mind sets, OHKOing Slowbro and 2HKOing Gardevoir. However, this would hurt Raikou's longevity. Extrasensory is also a viable option, allowing it to damage Breloom, Chesnaught, and Amoonguss.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Storm Drain Gastrodon walls Raikou's STAB Thunderbolt and Scald and can freely set up Spikes while hitting it back with STAB Ground-type moves. Torterra can also set up against Raikou while walling its attacks, and Krookodile and Flygon can easily threaten it with STAB Earthquake. However, the latter three must be cautious of a Scald burn.

Special Walls: Without multiple Calm Mind boosts, Raikou struggles to break through Alolan Muk and Umbreon, and the aforementioned two can immediately threaten it back with Knock Off and Toxic, while Hisuian Goodra threatens it with Knock Off and Earthquake, and Blissey shrugs off Raikou's attacks easily. However, all of these Pokemon are not Electric-immune and can be easily worn down via entry hazard chip damage in combination with Volt Switch.

Faster Physical Attackers: Choice Scarf users like Krookodile, Flygon, and Terrakion easily threaten Raikou, damaging it back with their STAB moves. Priority users like Lycanroc, Crawdaunt, Mimikyu, and Breloom also do not mind the Calm Mind boosts from Raikou and can easily chip it down if weakened.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Set Details

Scald is an excellent coverage move on Raikou, melting Ground-types like Krookodile and Rhyperior while also threatening to burn common checks like Cyclizar and Umbreon. Aura Sphere allows Raikou to hit Dark-, Normal-, and Steel-types like Bisharp, Cyclizar, and Hisuian Goodra for considerable damage. Heavy-Duty Boots prevents Raikou from taking entry hazard chip damage, helping to form robust VoltTurn cores with teammates like Cyclizar and Flamigo; Choice Specs is an alternative to threaten 2HKOs on walls like Cyclizar and offensive Hisuian Goodra. Tera Water removes Raikou's Ground weakness and boosts the damage output of Scald, helping take on threats like Mamoswine and Rhyperior.

Raikou is an excellent choice for balance and bulky offense teams that want a fast, powerful Volt Switch user to pair with other staples like Krookodile and Gengar. Stealth Rock setters like Jirachi and Rhyperior make for great teammates, ensuring that the opposition gets worn down more effectively by the VoltTurn core Raikou forms with partners like Barraskewda and Cyclizar. Similarly, Chesnaught is a great teammate for its ability to sponge the Ground-type attacks thrown at Raikou from foes like Krookodile and Rhyperior, which it can use to set up Spikes to further rack up hazard chip damage. Choice Specs Raikou appreciates teammates like Cyclizar and Noivern that help with entry hazard removal, allowing it to become a bit more threatening offensively without sacrificing its longevity.

Calm Mind.description:
Set Details

Calm Mind, in conjunction with Pressure, allows Raikou to become an excellent setup sweeper that can hit hard immediately while also handling opposing Calm Mind threats like Reuniclus and Suicune. Scald lets Raikou take on Ground-types like Krookodile and Rhyperior, as well as punish walls like Cyclizar and Umbreon with the chance to burn. Aura Sphere can be used to hit Normal- and Steel-types like Cyclizar and Hisuian Goodra; Substitute is an alternative that grants Raikou safety from status while setting up, protection from moves like Knock Off and Dragon Tail, and allows it to PP stall foes like Suicune with Pressure and Calm Mind. Leftovers allows Raikou to maintain health while attempting to setup and sweep, while Heavy-Duty Boots can be used instead to mitigate entry hazard chip damage. Tera Water removes the weakness to Ground and boosts the damage of Scald, which helps Raikou OHKO foes like Krookodile and Rhyperior. Tera Dark can be used on Substitute sets to prevent Psychic Noise Reuniclus and Slowbro from disrupting Raikou while it sets up.

Calm Mind Raikou fits well on balance and bulky offense teams, using its great Speed and coverage moves to rack up boosts and threaten to sweep late-game. Status spreaders like Slowbro and Umbreon are excellent teammates for Raikou; Slowbro can use Scald to burn physical attackers like Bisharp, as well as check foes like Krookodile and Flamigo, while Umbreon can use Toxic to wear down foes like Cresselia and opposing Umbreon. Stealth Rock setters like Krookodile and Rhyperior can help break through Raikou's checks, like Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra, as can wallbreaker teammates like Basculegion-F and Flamigo, which also offer pivot support. Gastrodon is a notable Raikou counter, being immune to Thunderbolt and using Storm Drain to absorb Raikou's Scald, so teammates like Amoonguss and Breloom that can threaten it are much appreciated. Cresselia and Gardevoir are great teammates as well, offering to restore its HP with Lunar Dance and Healing Wish, respectively, to give Raikou a second chance at a setup sweep.

nu.overview: Raikou is a decent pivot and setup sweeper, using its high Speed and Special Attack, along with Calm Mind boosts, to wear down opposing special walls like Copperajah and Bronzong. Its typing allows it to resist Kilowattrel's STAB moves and Brave Bird from Flamigo, which enables it to begin setting up with Calm Mind or use its high Speed to revenge kill non-Choice Scarf Flamigo. It has a variety of coverage moves, such as Scald and Shadow Ball, but to actually threaten the Ground- and Grass-types that wall it like Flygon, Gligar, Swampert, and Tsareena, it relies on teammates or the weak Shadow Ball. Furthermore, Scald is impotent against Covert Cloak Tsareena, and if it doesn't burn Flygon, that foe is still very threatening. While Raikou can, given either time or sufficient Calm Mind boosts, break special walls like Bronzong, they can threaten it back with Earthquake. Raikou can also be picked off by physical Choice Scarf users like Flygon, Flamigo, and Infernape. In addition, Raikou faces competition from other common Electric-types Kilowattrel and Toxtricity, with the former being faster and Ground immune and the latter having more immediate power and an easier time setting up.
nu.comments:
Other Options

A set of Substitute / Calm Mind / Thunderbolt / Scald, Shadow Ball, or Protect can be run on Raikou so that it can lean more into its identity of a setup sweeper, allowing it to simultaneously avoid status attempts as well as more easily boost its stats. Raikou can utilize Aura Sphere, along with Tera Fighting, to handle specially defensive Steel- and Dark-types like Copperajah, Incineroar, and Wo-Chien, but it loses the ability to threaten non-Rhyperior Ground-types at all. It can also slot Roar over Volt Switch to force out foes that may try to set up alongside it with Calm Mind like Bronzong and Sylveon. Discharge can be used to threaten faster foes like Choice Scarf Munkidori and Infernape with paralysis at the cost of Thunderbolt's power.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Raikou is threatened by a variety of common Ground-types like Flygon, Gligar, and Swampert, and it requires Scald to deal with them. However, it relies on a burn to truly threaten them.

Special Walls: Specially defensive walls like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Wo-Chien are difficult for Raikou to break without several boosts, and the former two often carry Earthquake to hit it super effectively, while Wo-Chien threatens to remove its item with Knock Off and sap Raikou's health with Leech Seed. However, none of these foes are Electric immune, so they can be worn down over time by being forced to repeatedly switch into Raikou's attacks.

Revenge Killers: Raikou's Speed is very good, but Choice Scarf users still threaten to revenge kill it, particularly physical attackers that don't care about its Calm Mind boosts like Flygon, Flamigo, and Infernape. Priority moves, such as Basculegion-M's Aqua Jet, Decidueye's Shadow Sneak, and Arcanine's Extreme Speed, can also pick it off if it is sufficiently weakened.

Calm Mind.description:
Set Details

Volt Switch allows Raikou to keep up momentum against and chip common switch-ins like Tsareena, Altaria, and Wo-Chien. Scald hits Electric-immune foes like Flygon, Swampert, and Kilowattrel while threatening with burns. Shadow Ball, often boosted by Tera Ghost, has solid neutral coverage, but Thunderbolt can provide a strong STAB attack that doesn't force Raikou to leave the field and, consequently, lose its Calm Mind boosts. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Raikou to pivot in and out more freely without concerns about entry hazards, while Leftovers grants longevity and better supports Substitute sets. Beyond boosting Shadow Ball, Tera Ghost also gives it an immunity to Fighting-type attacks from foes like Infernape, Heracross, and Scyther. Tera Flying offers a similar beneficial Fighting resistance as well as a Ground immunity to help against Flygon.

Raikou benefits from teammates that can switch into Ground-type attacks from foes that wall it, like Flygon and Swampert. As a result, teammates that can take advantage of Ground-types, such as Swords Dance Decidueye, Trailblaze Scyther, and Iron Defense Bronzong support it well. Particularly on sets that pivot with Volt Switch, entry hazard-setting teammates like Gligar, Diancie, and Gastrodon can help it wear down opposing walls, along with Knock Off users like Incineroar and Alolan Muk to remove Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers. Pivoting teammates like Flamigo, Flygon, and Basculegion-M can help bring Raikou in and weaken foes like Vaporeon and Avalugg. Other special attackers like Toxtricity, Uxie, and Munkidori can also help Raikou overload special walls like Gastrodon, Copperajah, and Alolan Muk. On non-Heavy-Duty Boots sets, hazard removal from teammates such as Tsareena and Avalugg can help Raikou pivot in and out more freely.

Choice Band.description:
Entei fulfills the role of a powerful sweeper, using its high Attack in tandem with Choice Band and an Intimidate and Fake Out immunity to become a powerful offensive threat that can easily weaken or clean up teams with Extreme Speed and Sacred Fire. Flare Blitz can be used as a more powerful and accurate alternative to Sacred Fire, allowing Entei to OHKO Calyrex-I and defensive Flutter Mane. Its coverage includes Stomping Tantrum, which can help it hit Incineroar and Tera Fire Pokemon such as Calyrex-I whilst additionally allowing Entei to hit Electric-types such as Miraidon for heavy damage, and Stone Edge, which is used for hitting Flying-types such as Pelipper and threatening Fire-types, namely the Ground-neutral Ogerpon-H, whilst being naturally stronger then Stomping Tantrum. Choice Band bolsters Entei's physical power significantly, guaranteeing an OHKO on Calyrex-I with Sacred Fire in tandem with Chien-Pao's Sword of Ruin and giving Extreme Speed a high chance to OHKO defensively invested Chi-Yu when bolstered by Sword of Ruin and Tera Normal. The HP and Special Defense investment allows Entei to play more flexibly against special attackers, increasing its ability to take on the likes of Calyrex-S, most notably allowing it to always survive Astral Barrage from Choice Specs Calyrex-S and Electro Drift from Choice Specs Miraidon out of Electric Terrain. However, running maximum Attack investment allows Entei to maximize its damage output without hindering its natural bulk significantly. Tera Normal boosts Entei's Extreme Speed significantly, allowing it to pick up OHKOs on Tornadus and Landorus-I with Sword of Ruin and 2HKOs on Urshifu-R and Kyogre whilst providing defensive utility in removing Entei's weaknesses to Water-, Ground-, and Rock-type attacks, namely Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R, Earth Power from Landorus-I, and Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-C, and notably allowing it an immunity to Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S.

Entei, whilst being a powerful offensive threat, does struggle with many metagame threats, namely powerful Water-types in Urshifu-R and Kyogre, which can tank Entei's attacks easily and KO back; Raging Bolt, which can easily survive the majority of its moves and threaten back with heavy damage; and Landorus, which can threaten it with Ground-type STAB moves whilst utilizing Tera Ghost to avoid Extreme Speed. Additionally, Entei can struggle with being locked into moves by Choice Band, so foes like Incineroar and Pelipper and faster offensive Pokemon like Miraidon can take advantage of it being locked into its Fire-type STAB moves, whilst Ghost-types such as Calyrex-S can benefit if Entei locks into Extreme Speed. Additionally, Entei's reliance on a priority move for its damage output can lead to it struggling greatly against priority-blocking effects from the likes of Indeedee-F and Farigiraf. Entei partners particularly well with Chien-Pao, as it can assist Entei in wallbreaking through increasing Entei's damage output with Sword of Ruin and threaten the Ghost-types that can take advantage of Entei as well as Landorus, Miraidon, Farigiraf, and Indeedee-F, whilst Entei in turn threatens Chien-Pao's counters, namely Chi-Yu. Other great partners for Entei include Rillaboom, which provides Fake Out support for Entei whilst also providing Terrain control that can help against Miraidon and Indeedee-F, and Flutter Mane, which can control the speed of the battle and also threatens Miraidon, and both can threaten Entei's main answer in Urshifu-R. The Restricted Pokemon Entei is most commonly partnered with is Zamazenta-C, as Zamazenta-C threatens Entei's potential answers, such as Incineroar and Ogerpon-C, and Entei can chip some of its common checks, namely Landorus, whilst being able to threaten Ogerpon-H and Chi-Yu, which can assist Zamazenta-C greatly.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Snarl slows down strong special attackers such as Flutter Mane, Raging Bolt, and Iron Crown. Tera Blast can be used instead when using Tera Grass to hit Water-types.

  • Assault Vest helps increase Entei's longevity against special attackers such as Flutter Mane, making Entei even harder to remove taking into account Sacred Fire's burn chance.

  • The EV spread allows Entei to survive a 116 Special Attack Modest Earth Power from Landorus and, when Terastallized, almost always survive Mystic Water Urshifu-R's Tera Water-boosted Surging Strikes, the rest of the EVs are used to maximize its damage output.

  • Tera Grass provides resistances to Water- and Ground- types like Urshifu-R and Landorus, as well as granting a Spore immunity. Tera Normal boosts Entei's Extreme Speed power while also removing its original weaknesses.

ru.overview: Entei acts as one of RU's deadliest wallbreakers, boasting a high Attack stat and an incredible STAB move in Sacred Fire. Sacred Fire's 50% burn chance lets Entei wear down even physically bulky checks, like Rhyperior and Gastrodon, as well as deter physically offensive Pokemon like Crawdaunt and Krookodile from switching in. Entei also has access to the coveted Extreme Speed, letting it revenge kill dangerous attackers like Shift Gear Toxtricity and Maushold. Additionally, its surprisingly solid bulk allows Entei to momentarily check the likes of Jirachi and Bisharp, allowing it to take a hit before eliminating them with Sacred Fire. However, Entei has middling and unreliable coverage, making it struggle against bulky Water-types like Suicune and Slowbro as well as Ground-types like Rhyperior and Quagsire if they do not mind getting burned. Entei's otherwise-solid Speed tier still leaves it outsped by dangerous threats like Noivern and Gengar; the former can take even an Extreme Speed boosted by both Tera Normal and Choice Band and resists Sacred Fire, while the latter is flat-out immune to Extreme Speed.
ru.comments:
Other Options

A Swagger set with Mirror Herb is an option to let Entei act as a setup sweeper, giving it immense power without locking it into a move like Choice Band. However, Swagger's lackluster accuracy and Entei's vulnerability to hazards in conjunction with its lack of immediate power makes it unreliable. Entei can utilize its surprisingly high Special Attack to run a set with Calm Mind, Protect, Substitute, and Lava Plume with Leftovers and Pressure, letting it PP stall foes while accruing boosts, though Entei's Stealth Rock weakness makes it rather inconsistent. Stomping Tantrum can be used over Stone Edge as a reliable coverage option against opposing Entei, as well as to dent Empoleon and Terrakion, though it misses out on Noivern and lacks power compared to Stone Edge which makes it less than ideal.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Because of Trailblaze's weak Base Power bulky Water-types like Slowbro, Quagsire, Gastrodon, and Suicune can survive being 2HKOd by Entei and heal the damage off. Offensive Water-types like Feraligatr, Basculegion-F, and Crawdaunt are capable of threatening Entei as well. All of them struggle to switch in to its moves, however: Feraligatr and Crawdaunt hate being burned by Sacred Fire, while Basculegion-F must be wary of Crunch.

Ground-types: Rhyperior, Gligar, and Flygon are all capable of taking hits from Entei before threatening it out with Earthquake. However, none of them enjoy being burned by Sacred Fire.

Entry Hazards: Entei's pure Fire typing leaves it vulnerable to every entry hazard in the game, especially Stealth Rock. While Entei can run Heavy-Duty Boots to mitigate them, it is vulnerable to having them removed by Knock Off from Cyclizar or Hisuian Goodra as well as Trick from Gardevoir or Jirachi.

Faster Revenge Killers: Naturally faster Pokemon that can take an Extreme Speed, like Noivern, Terrakion, and Gengar, can KO Entei before it has a chance to act, especially if it has already been worn down. Additionally, Choice Scarf users like Krookodile and Basculegion-F can take an Extreme Speed while being able to get the jump on Entei.

All-Out Attacker.description:
Set Details

Entei is a phenomenal wallbreaker that can eviscerate common Pokemon like Bisharp, Jirachi, and Registeel. Extreme Speed is used to help Entei pick off faster Pokemon, such as weakened Noivern, Cyclizar, and Choice Scarf Krookodile. It's especially useful against more offensive teams, being able to revenge kill foes like Shift Gear Toxtricity and Bisharp. Stone Edge hits targets such as Noivern and opposing Entei. Trailblaze deals solid damage on Water- and Ground-types, like Gastrodon, Quagsire, and Rhyperior in addition to letting it outrun threats like Gengar and Choice Scarf Gardevoir after one use. Crunch is used mainly on Choice Band sets to target Slowbro, which would otherwise come in comfortably. Double-Edge can be substituted for Crunch on Choice Band sets, granting Entei the opportunity to hit foes that resist its Fire-type STAB moves like Gastrodon, Suicune, and Cyclizar harder. Heavy-Duty Boots is usually preferred, as it prevents Entei from being quickly worn down by entry hazards. Choice Band is good for teams that have strong entry hazard removal, in exchange for being weak to hazards. On Choice Band sets, Tera Normal boosts Extreme Speed to secure a 2HKO on faster foes like Noivern. Tera Normal also provides decent defensive utility, providing an immunity to Ghost-type STAB moves from the likes of Gengar and Mimikyu. Tera Normal grants Entei the opportunity to 2HKO targets such as Slowbro and Suicune, which would otherwise come in comfortably on Entei, with Choice Band-boosted Double-Edge. Tera Grass ensures that Entei will 2HKO Gastrodon and Quagsire and resist Krookodile's Earthquake. Tera Dark can also be used to further boost the power of Choice Band Entei's Crunch, being able to cleanly 2HKO maximum Defense Slowbro and OHKO Basculegion-F.

Entei is an excellent fit on balance and bulky offense teams, as they appreciate its ability to dispatch common threats, spread burns, and provide strong priority. Pokemon such as Krookodile and Bisharp appreciate Entei's ability to directly threaten bulky Pokemon such as Chesnaught and Registeel, in addition to possibly crippling Rhyperior with burn from Sacred Fire. This opens up teammates such as Choice Scarf Krookodile and Bisharp to sweep. In return, Krookodile sets Stealth Rock and utilizes Knock Off to help wear down Pokemon that like to come in on Entei, such as Slowbro, while Bisharp directly threatens Slowbro and can blow holes in the opposing team to allow Entei a clean sweep late-game. Bisharp has the ability to threaten faster Pokemon that Entei is vulnerable to like Gengar with its Sucker Punch. Special attackers like Gardevoir and Basculeigon-F pair well with Entei, as it can deal significant damage to their checks such as Hisuian Goodra and Empoleon. Choice Band Entei can struggle to get in if Stealth Rock is up, so it appreciates hazard removal from Pokemon such as Cyclizar and Noivern. In addition to this, Cyclizar brings Entei in safely against Pokemon that like to come in on it, such as Talonflame and Chesnaught, which Entei takes advantage of. Entei also appreciates entry hazard support from Pokemon such as Jirachi and Chesnaught. This helps weaken checks such as Slowbro and Rhyperior and weakens other Pokemon to be picked off with Extreme Speed. Jirachi also provides U-turn, which allows Entei to come in safely against foes such as Registeel.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Access to strong priority and an ability that prevents Intimidate cycling give Entei a strong niche over other bulky Fire-types like Incineroar and Gouging Fire!

  • Sacred Fire: Sacred Fire's stupendous burn rate makes switching physical attackers into Entei a terrifyingly risky prospect!

  • Stone Edge: Despite its notorious reliability issues, Stone Edge is useful for being Entei's strongest attack against Dragonite and Terastallized Ogerpon-H.

  • Tera Blast Grass VS. Trailblaze: Tera Blast Grass has a chance of OHKOing offensive Primarina, OHKOes Swampert, and deals massive damage to Urshifu-R. Trailblaze misses out on these KOes, but the Speed boost can lead to easier sweeping late-game.

  • Bulldoze VS. Stomping Tantrum: Bulldoze is both a way to deal decent damage to opposing Fire-types and a useful support move with its Speed drop. Stomping Tantrum offers a bit more power and can match Sacred Fire in power if Entei misses an attack.

  • Crunch: Crunch is Entei's best coverage option for Latios and Latias.

Other Options
  • Iron Head: Iron Head does a bit of extra damage against Flutter Mane but has limited use otherwise.
EV Spreads

  • 148 HP / 244 Atk / 84 Def / 12 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread avoids an OHKO from Adamant Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch after Stealth Rock damage and a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball without Stealth Rock.

  • 132 HP / 228 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 140 Spe with Adamant: This spread spread lets Entei outspeed Iron Bundle after using Trailblaze or Bulldoze while only having a 2% chance of being 2HKOed by Choice Specs Timid Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

  • 196 HP / 132 Atk / 156 Def / 4 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This physically defensive spread survives Tera Dark Choice Band Adamant Chien-Pao's Crunch while still dodging a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball without Stealth Rock.

  • 116 HP / 116 Atk / 4 Def / 252 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This specially defensive spread dodges a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane even when with Stealth Rock!

  • 4 HP / 236 Atk / 4 Def / 76 SpD / 188 Spe with with Jolly: This speedy and frailer spread outspeeds all Landorus-T that lack Choice Scarf while still having enough special bulk to almost always avoid a 2HKO Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Entei's Fairy resistance is a big selling point as an Assault Vest Pokemon, but Terastallization can help with some of its poor matchups.

  • Grass: Tera Grass helps Entei with Water-types like Primarina and offensive Urshifu-R. Just note that Suicune and Bulk Up Urshifu-R avoid a 2HKO from Tera Blast.

  • Normal: While this Entei doesn't have enough firepower to sweep until late-game, boosting Extreme Speed is still helpful in this regard. It can also save Entei from Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy isn't as helpful against bulky Water-types, but it makes Urshifu-S and Choice Band Chien-Pao much more manageable and surprises Gouging Fire that may attempt to set up with Breaking Swipe and Dragon Dance.

Choice Band.description:
• Being immune to Intimidate cycling and a better Speed stat make Entei a reasonable alternative to Choice Band Dragonite for priority cleaning.

  • Sacred Fire: Sacred Fire's horrifying coin-flip burn chances are a powerful deterrent to problematic foes like Urshifu-R, so it's preferred over Flare Blitz.

  • Stone Edge: As unreliable as Stone Edge can be, it's needed to do maximum damage to Dragonite.

  • Bulldoze: Bulldoze's Speed drop is useful for team support and 2HKOes most Focus Sash Flutter Mane, potentially saving Entei from a KO!

  • Crunch: Crunch deals massive damage to Latias, which can otherwise stall out Stone Edge with Recover.

EV Spreads

  • 116 HP / 252 Atk / 140 Spe with Adamant: This spread lets Entei outspeed up to Iron Bundle after using Bulldoze.

  • 148 HP / 252 Atk / 84 Def / 4 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: This bulkier spread lets Entei survive Adamant Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Jolly: Entei can make use of its often overlooked Speed stat to outspeed Adamant Urshifu formes and Adamant Ogerpon formes, and it can even Speed tie with Chi-Yu.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Entei is a perfectly fine priority cleaner, but Terastallization makes that task much easier.

  • Normal: Tera Normal lets Entei do its best Dragonite impression, giving Extreme Speed such a boost that Chien-Pao can be OHKOed by it after Stealth Rock!

  • Grass: Tera Grass trades easier Extreme Speed sweeping for shredding through opposing bulky Water-types with Tera Blast, like Urshifu-R and Suicune.

Offensive.description:
• Entei is fast enough to be a surprisingly effective offensive Pokemon thanks to its immunity to Intimidate cycling and decent Speed.

  • Sacred Fire: Even though Flare Blitz is more powerful and doesn't contend with a irritating 5% chance to miss, the insane burn rate Sacred Fire provides is generally preferred.

  • Stone Edge: Stone Edge is Entei's best chance at breaking through Dragonite and Gouging Fire before without Terastallization.

  • Trailblaze VS. Grass Tera Blast: Trailblaze does decent damage to offensive Water-types and lets Entei outspeed the troublesome Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, but Tera Blast is needed to break through bulky Water-types like Suicune.

  • Swagger and Mirror Herb: This is the closest Entei gets to setting up, giving Entei the chance to pull off a shocking sweep and even be a nuisance with confusion! Outside of Swagger, Mirror Herb can be used for some risky switch-ins to punish setup moves with a boosted Extreme Speed.

  • Jolly VS. Adamant: Jolly Entei will outpace the prominent Urshifu-R, but Adamant is worth considering if using Tera Normal for easier priority sweeping.

Alternate EV Spreads
  • 148 HP / 252 Atk / 84 Def / 4 SpD / 20 Spe with Adamant: If using Swagger, Mirror Herb, and Tera Normal, this bulkier EV spread can fit to avoid an OHKO from Adamant Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch after Stealth Rock.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Entei can function without Terastallization, but there are some matchups that will need it for.

  • Grass: Tera Grass is Entei's trump card against bulky Water-types like Suicune and Primarina and can save it from getting revenge killed by Choice Scarf Urshifu-R.

  • Normal: Tera Normal gives Entei a more late-game focus with Extreme Speed sweeping, especially if using Swagger.
