  • 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA with Quiet: With 0 Speed IVs, this is used to underspeed uninvested Hippowdon, giving Pelipper the initial advantage in weather wars.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpA with Relaxed: This spread gives Pelipper a better matchup against dominant, powerful physical attackers like Choice Band Dragpault and Extreme Speed Dragonite.

  • 4 Def / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Modest: This offensive spread can be used to outspeed uninvested Corviknight and others in that Speed tier.

Items

  • Eject Button: This extra method of pivoting makes it much easier to switch Pelipper in just for getting rain up.

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs can be used to take advantage of Pelipper's powerful STAB moves.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry provides longevity on defensive sets.

Rain Setter.description: • Outspeeds non-Booster Energy Iron Bundle under Tailwind.
• This EV Spread survives Choice Specs Flutter Mane Moonblast and outspeeds Iron Bundle in Tailwind.

ru.overview: Gardevoir graces RU with a strong offensive typing and good utility in Trace, Trick, and Healing Wish, making it one of the tier's premier Choice Scarf users. Very few Pokemon in the tier are able to come in on its STAB combination, and the few that do, like Registeel and Hisuian Goodra, often find themselves crippled by being given a Choice Scarf with Trick. Additionally, Gardevoir can give powerful teammates like Feraligatr, Necrozma, and Hisuian Goodra a second chance to break through teams with Healing Wish. However, Gardevoir's awkward natural Speed tier makes it heavily reliant on holding a Choice Scarf to outrun threats like Noivern and non-Choice Scarf Gengar, making it rather prediction-heavy. Its otherwise great offensive typing leaves it walled by Steel-types like Jirachi and Empoleon; while these Pokemon are often crippled by Trick, this forces Gardevoir to have to choose between continuing to act as speed control or crippling a Pokemon that otherwise walls it. Gardevoir's typing is also underwhelming defensively; when combined with its poor bulk, this leaves it vulnerable to faster revenge killers, such as Choice Scarf Krookodile, and priority from the likes of Bisharp and Entei.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Psychic Noise is an alternative Psychic-type STAB option that, while weaker than Psychic, can let Gardevoir hinder bulkier Pokemon like Slowbro and Cresselia by preventing them from recovering. Psyshock is another alternative STAB move that lets Gardevoir target the likes of Blissey and Calm Mind Suicune, hitting their weaker Defense stats. Gardevoir can run Focus Blast or Mystical Fire to prevent it from being walled by Steel-types like Registeel, letting it retain its Choice Scarf for longer. Mystical Fire also lets it reliably hinder special attackers like Nasty Plot Mew and Hisuian Goodra on the switch. However, running coverage forces Gardevoir to forgo one of its valuable utility moves. Knock Off and Will-O-Wisp are usable utility alternatives; the former lets Gardevoir retain its item while forcing progress, while the latter can cripple physical sweepers like Bisharp and Mimikyu as well as Steel-type switch-ins like Jirachi. Teleport lets Gardevoir keep up momentum for its team and bring in threatening wallbreakers, though its poor bulk makes it vulnerable to being KOed before it can pivot out. Choice Specs can be run over Choice Scarf to amplify Gardevoir's damage output, notably guaranteeing a 2HKO on Choice Specs Hisuian Goodra, though Gardevoir's awkward Speed tier leaves it vulnerable to faster attackers like Krookodile.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Gardevoir's STAB combination is resisted by the tier's many bulky Steel-types, like Empoleon, Assault Vest Magnezone, Registeel, and Jirachi, with the last three being able to threaten it out with their Steel-type STAB moves. Hisuian Goodra, while lacking a resistance to Moonblast, can also come in safely thanks to its good special bulk and threaten Gardevoir out. However, all of these Pokemon must be wary of being given a Choice Scarf, though Jirachi can run a Choice Scarf of its own to get the jump on Gardevoir.

Special Walls: Blissey can sponge Gardevoir's attacks comfortably, cripple it with Thunder Wave, and wear it down with Seismic Toss, while Alolan Muk is similarly able to take a Moonblast from Gardevoir before threatening it out with Poison Jab. Both must be wary of Trick, however.

Faster Revenge Killers: Faster Choice Scarf users, like Krookodile and Gengar, can get the jump on Gardevoir before KOing it with their strong STAB moves, though they struggle to come in safely against it.

Priority: Gardevoir's poor Defense stat leaves it vulnerable to many of the tier's common forms of priority after it has sustained chip damage, such as Entei's Extreme Speed, Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak, and Bisharp's Sucker Punch.

Choice Scarf.description:
Draped in its finest attire, Choice Scarf Gardevoir has established itself as one of the premier options for speed control in RU. Choice Scarf ensures that Gardevoir outpaces the entirety of the unboosted RU metagame as well as giving it the edge over slower Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-F. Trick gives Gardevoir the option to bog down common switch-ins like Jirachi and Registeel with a Choice Scarf, limiting their survivability by removing potential Leftovers as well as forcing them to lock into a move should they decide to stay in. It also provides the added benefit of preventing slow Calm Mind users like Slowbro and Reunicles from setting up. Healing Wish allows Gardevoir to bring back a weakened teammate from the brink. Notably, Trace provides unique depth to this set. For example, being able to Trace Cyclizar's or Slowbro's Regenerator gives Gardevoir an avenue for self-sufficient recovery, while Basculegion's Adaptability allows Gardevoir to supercharge its Psychic and Moonblast without needing to expend Tera. Tera Fairy is Gardevoir's Tera type of choice, bolstering its already formidable Moonblasts and allowing it to secure guaranteed 2HKO's on Pokemon such as Slowbro and Reuniclus as well as an important OHKO on Assault Vest Cyclizar, which is otherwise capable of tanking one Moonblast from full. Defensively, dropping the Psychic typing gives Gardevoir key resistances to a common priority move in Bisharp's Sucker Punch that would otherwise be liable to revenge kill Gardevoir.

The host of tools that Gardevoir brings to the table means that it finds itself as a competent addition to several meta-relevant playstyles. Hyper offense finds itself greatly appreciating Gardevoir's defensive profile with its Dragon immunity and 4x Fighting resist, Healing Wish giving one of its teammates like Bisharp or Maushold a second chance to sweep, and its role as a revenge killer for a structure that often struggles against Swift Swim sweepers like Barraskewda and Overqwil. Outside of hyper offense, Gardevoir can find success on balance and bulky offense builds for much of the same reasons it thrives on hyper offense while also contributing a high-impact Trick. Being able to pawn off the Choice Scarf and cripple an opponent's wall or wallbreaker like Registeel or Necrozma is a huge boon to fat structures looking to wear down the opposing team. Fighting-types such as Breloom and Flamigo are great running mates with their ability to take on common Steel-types like Registeel and Empoleon that Gardevoir would otherwise struggle against. Special breakers like Toxtricity and Magnezone serve a similar role with their ability to threaten Steel-types, and Magnezone specifically is able to trap and remove certain Steel-types entirely. As a Choice Scarf user, Gardevoir immensely benefits from entry hazard support to soften the opposing team up before attempting to clean, so setters such as Chesnaught, Klefki, and Krookodile make for great teammates.

Stallbreaker.description: With Pixilate-boosted Hyper Voice and an incredible Special Attack stat, Mega Gardevoir is one of the tier's most effective stallbreakers, able to threaten many defensive staples like Tyranitar with its STAB moves and rip through neutral and even resistant targets like Clefable and Skarmory. However, Mega Gardevoir faces competition from Enamorus as a wallbreaker and other Fairy-types with more defensive utility like Clefable. Psyshock allows Mega Gardevoir to do decent damage to Blissey and also threatens Pokemon that resist Hyper Voice, like Mega Venusaur. Mystical Fire hits the Steel-types that resist both of its STAB moves, such as Celesteela and Aegislash. These three moves make Mega Gardevoir a potent threat on its own, so the fourth slot can be changed to whatever suits the team best. Teleport takes advantage of the many switches Mega Gardevoir forces thanks to its high power, letting it pivot out of checks like Celesteela and Chansey and bring out Pokemon like Magnezone that can trap the former, and Pokemon like Choice Band Bisharp and Choice Band Tyranitar that can Pursuit trap both. Taunt prevents status and recovery moves from Pokemon like Chansey. Calm Mind is another great option against defensive teams, as it takes advantage of these slower structures by boosting up its Special Attack. This allows it to break through foes that would normally stop it, notably being able to 2HKO the likes of Chansey and Celesteela after a boost. Mega Gardevoir commonly finds itself on offensive teams that appreciate a strong wallbreaker, such as teams with VoltTurn cores, as these teams may struggle to properly break stall and bulkier teams. However, Mega Gardevoir can struggle against specially defensive Pokemon like Chansey, Celesteela, and Jirachi. Chansey is able to poison Mega Gardevoir lacking Taunt, and defensive Celesteela and Jirachi can both take a hit and retaliate with Heavy Slam and Iron Head, respectively. Mega Gardevoir greatly appreciates help from strong physical attackers like Mienshao and Victini and good entry hazard setters, such as Swampert and Excadrill, to pressure these Pokemon. Pokemon like Thundurus that can pressure its aforementioned checks with special attacks are also great teammates. Mega Gardevoir's Speed also leaves it susceptible to being picked off by Choice Scarf Mienshao, Iron Moth, Mega Aerodactyl, and Excadrill in sand, making Skarmory and Rotom-W great defensive partners. In return, Mega Gardevoir can threaten the bulky cores that these Pokemon may struggle to break apart.

Special Attacker.description:
• The given EV spread allows Mega Gardevoir to survive Shadow Ball from Flutter mane while still able to outspeed scarfed Chi-Yu during Tailwind, allocating the remaining EVs into Special Attack.
  • Psyshock will deal greater damage to Flutter Mane, but Expanding Force is preferred if Indeedee-F or Tapu Lele is on the same team for Psychic Terrain.

Offensive.description:
Mega Gardevoir's stellar Special Attack in tandem with its ability, Pixilate, decent Special Defense, and respectable Speed tier make it a vicious wallbreaker against slower defensive Pokemon, especially Dark-, Dragon-, and Fighting-types such as Ting-Lu, defensive Garchomp, and Great Tusk. A strong Psychic-type STAB move in Psyshock ensures Poison-types like Toxapex and Galarian Slowking take a lot of damage if they try to switch into a Hyper Voice, as well as letting Mega Gardevoir hit Blissey and Clodsire. Mystical Fire prevents Mega Gardevoir from being walled by Steel-types like Ferrothorn while also denying switch-in opportunities to Gholdengo and Mega Scizor, making sure it isn't setup fodder. Taunt allows it to shut down setup attempts from Calm Mind users such as Raging Bolt, Tapu Lele, and Tapu Fini while also preventing defensive Pokemon such as Gliscor, Toxapex, Blissey, and Ting-Lu from using status moves like Toxic and Thunder Wave, setting entry hazards, or using recovery moves. Focus Blast, similarly to Mystical Fire, makes sure Mega Gardevoir isn't walled by Steel-types; however, it hits Heatran and Melmetal harder. Its base ability, Trace, allows it to come in on Pokemon, copy their abilities, and take advantage of them. For example, it can copy Dauntless Shield from Zamazenta, Regenerator from Pokemon such as Alomomola and Tornadus-T, Swift Swim from Mega Swampert, and Flash Fire from Heatran. Maximum Speed investment enables Meg Gardevoir to outpace threats like non-Choice Scarf variants of Urshifu-R and Kyurem, making it harder to revenge kill.

Mega Gardevoir works best on offense, bulky offense, or balance structures due to its poor physical bulk, lack of reliable recovery, and vulnerability to Spikes, which limits its entry opportunities. It works best with slow pivots like Corviknight, Galarian Slowking, and Alomomola that cover its weaknesses to Steel and Poison and can bring it in safely multiple times. It also greatly appreciates partners that can set entry hazards on forced switches, like Hisuian Samurott, offensive Garchomp, and Great Tusk. Thanks to Mega Gardevoir's incredible matchup against Ting-Lu, it has great synergy with Pokemon that are walled by it, like Ghostium Z Gholdengo and Raging Bolt. Fast physical attackers like Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, Zamazenta, and Mega Lopunny, as well as priority users such as Mega Scizor and Mega Medicham with Bullet Punch and Kingambit with Sucker Punch, can revenge kill Mega Gardevoir if let in by a slow pivot. As such, physically defensive Pokemon like Corviknight, Toxapex, and Pecharunt are great partners. Meanwhile, since it's easily revenge killed by Choice Scarf users like Urshifu-R and faster threats like Tapu Koko and Weavile, Pokemon that can switch into them and apply offensive pressure—like Ogerpon-W, Kingambit, and Iron Treads—are great partners that help maintain momentum.

Choice Specs (Psychic).description:
Choice Specs Gardevoir is a niche wallbreaker on Psychic teams. With Moonblast, it can OHKO Dark-types such as Mandibuzz and Sableye, as well as shutting down Dragon-type threats such as Latios, Kyurem, and Raging Bolt. Psyshock beats specially defensive walls such as Blissey and Articuno. Focus Blast provides coverage against Steel-type foes, letting Gardevoir OHKO Archaludon and Heatran. Thunderbolt lets it handle Flying- and Water-types like Skarmory, Pelipper, and Alomomola. Trick can be used as a niche pick to neutralize threats such as Gouging Fire, Dragonite, and Alolan Muk. Vacuum Wave lets Gardevoir finish off fast weakened foes like Choice Scarf Weavile and Excadrill in sand; with a Modest nature, Gardevoir can OHKO Meowscarada after Stealth Rock. Timid Gardevoir can outspeed threats such as Adamant Dragonite and Timid Heatran. Trace lets it benefit from being sent against Pokemon with powerful abilities such as Kingdra, Dragonite, and Greninja.

Gardevoir requires Stealth Rock in order to OHKO many Pokemon; for this purpose, Jirachi and Metagross can easily set Stealth Rock, as well as covering most of each other’s weaknesses. Gardevoir also faces problems with Ghost-type Pokemon; for this, Hoopa-U and Indeedee are the best partners for it, as Hoopa-U takes neutral damage from Ghost-type attacks and can reliably take care of Flutter Mane and Gholdengo. Indeedee is immune to Ghost and sets Psychic Terrain for the team, which boosts the power of Gardevoir's Psychic-type moves and protects it from priority moves from Pokemon like Scizor and Bisharp. Gardevoir also forms a wallbreaking core with Choice Scarf Iron Boulder, allowing Gardevoir to handle foes like Archaludon and Skarmory, while Iron Boulder deals with foes like Gouging Fire, Hisuian Goodra, and Choice Specs Flutter Mane. Deoxys-S is an incredible partner for Gardevoir, as it can set Spikes to boost Gardevoir's wallbreaking potential and use Teleport to grant it safe entry. Latios and Latias form a wallbreaking core with Gardevoir, with Latias providing additional aid through Healing Wish, which allows Gardevoir to battle at full potential once again.

Bulky Offense.description:
• Between using Trace to cancel Ruin abilities and burning foes with Will-O-Wisp, Gardevoir can overwhelm some of the meta's strongest physical sweepers.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Beyond crippling physical attackers for the remainder of the match, the passive burn damage breaks Focus Sash on Chien-Pao and Multiscale on Dragonite.

  • Psyshock versus Psychic: The choice of Psychic-type STAB comes down to what you need to hit hardest. Psyshock is the best option into Flutter Mane, Iron Moth, and Clodsire, while Psychic puts more pressure on Toxapex and many variants of Bulk Up Annihilape.

Other Options
  • Sitrus Berry versus Pinch Berry: Sitrus Berry is normally the preferred recovery item for bulky Gardevoir sets, but it is a highly sought-after item. If needed elsewhere, Gardevoir's bulk profile is strong enough that running a pinch Berry can work.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Using Tera usually improves common matchups like Flutter Mane and is certainly an option if a target is deemed high enough priority. Otherwise, Gardevor's impressive suite of defensive attributes combined with excellent STAB coverage are great as is.

  • Fire: Tera Fire’s resistances to Ice, Steel, and Fairy are all excellent, greatly improving the matchups against Flutter Mane, Scizor, and Kingambit. Tera boosted Mystical Fire will also 2HKO maximum HP Kingambit without Assault Vest.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy can patch up this set's lacking power by boosting Moonblast, and the removal of Gardevoir's Psychic typing makes dealing with opposing Ghost-types like Flutter Mane and Mimikyu more manageable.

  • Normal: Tera Normal's defensive attributes are lacking overall, but nullifying a key Ghost-type attack from the likes of Flutter Mane and Mimikyu can give an opening to deal extra damage or inflict a crucial burn.

EV Spreads

  • The spreads listed below all have an even HP stat to guarantee that Sitrus Berry activates after getting hit by Ruination. All spreads are also capable of surviving one unboosted Shadow Ball from Flutter Mane.

  • 244 HP / 244 Def / 20 Spe: Near maximum HP and Defense gives Gardevoir fantastic defensive calcs; after Sitrus Berry recovery and inflicting a turn 1 burn, Gardevoir has a strong chance of avoiding the 3HKO from Focus Sash Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash and Assault Vest Ting-Lu's Heavy Slam. The Speed investment outspeeds maximum Speed Adamant Kingambit.

  • 244 HP / 204 Def / 60 Spe: A little extra Speed investment lets Gardevoir outspeed defensive Gholdengo with 20 Speed EVs, but Gardevoir is much less likely to avoid the 3HKOs mentioned in the main spread.

Offensive.description: • EV Spread: This spread allows Assault Vest Gardevoir to survive Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball from full health, while outspeeding Adamant Breloom.

Poison Heal.description:
Set Details

Breloom's unique defensive profile makes it a great check to the tier's Dark-types like Krookodile, Umbreon, and Wo-Chien as well as Rhyperior, and it's a decent wallbreaker with good resilience. It's also able to switch into the many Scalds and Thunder Waves in the tier after it activates Poison Heal. In addition, status-boosted Facade allows Breloom to damage Flying- and Poison-type Pokemon such as Noivern and Amoonguss. Protect scouts the intention of Choice-locked Pokemon, like Gengar and Basculegion-F, while also racking up Poison Heal recovery. Protect also ensures Toxic Orb is activated when Breloom first enters the field. 176 Speed EVs allow Breloom to outspeed Modest offensive Empoleon and Hisuian Goodra. Maximum HP allows Breloom to stomach hits such as Psychic Noise from Jirachi and Slowbro, allowing it to outlast them long-term. Tera Steel allows Breloom to flip its Fairy, Psychic, and Flying weaknesses into resistances, turning the tables on revenge killing attempts from the likes of Gardevoir and Flamigo, while Tera Normal lets Facade 2HKO the likes of Amoonguss.

Breloom fits best on bulky offense to balanced teams due to its ability to stomach Knock Offs and status while keeping up offensive pressure. Breloom is a great partner for special attackers such as Raikou, Gardevoir, and Basculegion-F, all of which can bring it in safely versus special sponges such as Cyclizar and Hisuian Goodra. Breloom also a great teammate for Gengar, which dispatches bulky Psychic-type Pokemon like Slowbro and Reuniclus while Breloom switches into the plenty of bulky Dark- and Steel-type Pokemon like Umbreon and Empoleon that Gengar might struggle with. Similarly, Slowbro pairs well with Breloom, as it resists Fire- and Psychic-type attacks like Sacred Fire and Psychic Noise from Entei and Reuniclus for it, while Breloom resists Electric- and Dark-type attacks like Thunderbolt from Raikou and Magnezone and Knock Off from Krookodile. Krookodile is also a great partner for Breloom, as it removes Heavy-Duty Boots and Rocky Helmet from foes like Slowbro, Chesnaught, and non-Sticky Hold Gastrodon while also setting up Stealth Rock to chip it's usual checks like Chesnaught. Physical sweepers like Bisharp and Feraligatr enjoy Breloom weakening physical walls like Slowbro, Chesnaught, and Gastrodon while absorbing Toxic and Thunder Wave from the likes of Umbreon and the aforementioned Slowbro.

Focus Sash (Fighting).description:
Breloom fulfills a variety of roles for Fighting teams, with Spore immobilizing threats like Corviknight, Pelipper, and Toxapex and operates as a revenge killer with Mach Punch. Swords Dance further boosts its great Attack and lets Breloom take advantage of forcing foes out after they have been afflicted with Spore to set up. Bulldoze can be used in place of Spore or Swords Dance to handle Poison-types that would otherwise give it problems like Okidogi and Toxapex. However, Spore and Swords Dance are usually preferred, since the former grants Breloom great utility while the latter can potentially turn it into a setup sweeper. Bullet Seed is a strong STAB move that threatens Ground-types like Clodsire and Great Tusk as well as breaking Ogerpon-C's Sturdy and OHKOing it outright after a Swords Dance boost. Mach Punch, when boosted with Swords Dance, turns Breloom into a setup sweeper, taking on faster threats like Hoopa-U, Kyurem, and Excadrill.

Offensive Great Tusk is one of Breloom's best teammates, as it sets up Stealth Rock to bolster Breloom's breaking and sweeping capabilities, removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin to preserve Breloom's Focus Sash, and handles sun teams thanks to Protosynthesis. In return, Breloom handles Water-types that threaten Great Tusk such as Greninja and Primarina. Keldeo and Urshifu-R not only handle Fire-types like Heatran and Ceruledge, but Keldeo also outpaces and threatens non-Choice Scarf Landorus, while Urshifu-R can revenge kill weakened sweepers and cleaners like Volcarona, Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, and Flutter Mane with Aqua Jet. Choice Scarf Sneasler and Assault Vest Iron Hands make for great teammates, as they handle Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Enamorus for Breloom thanks to their great special bulk and, in the case of the former, its Poison typing. Additionally, Sneasler can potentially spread status with a combination of Poison Touch and Dire Claw and pivot Breloom in with U-turn, while Iron Hands handles Flying-types like Corviknight, Mandibuzz, and Articuno thanks to its Electric typing. Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, with its colorful coverage, threatens a multitude of pesky threats such as Dragapult, Latios, and physically defensive Gyarados. Lastly, Breloom's wallbreaking enables sweepers like Victory Dance Hisuian Lilligant and Unburden Sneasler to sweep late-game.

Focus Sash (Grass).description:
Breloom is a great late-game cleaner for Grass teams by virtue of its great Attack stat, access to Swords Dance to increase it further, and great ability in Technician boosting many of its attacks. Spore allows Breloom to incapacitate a threat to open up opportunities for it to set up Swords Dance. Mach Punch boosted by Technician allows Breloom to not only revenge kill fast cleaners like Meowscarada, Greninja, and Barraskewda but also sweep through teams that lack a check to it like Dark and Ice. Rock Tomb provides great coverage, targeting Fire- and Flying-types that switch in on an anticipated Bullet Seed such as Ogerpon-H, Talonflame, and Zapdos. Close Combat is more powerful than Mach Punch, making it suited for slower foes such as Archaludon, while Bulldoze allows Breloom to handle one of its biggest counters in Gholdengo. Bullet Seed is Breloom's strongest wallbreaking STAB option thanks to Technician boosting each of its hits. A Swords Dance + 3 attacks variant can be used as well to further Breloom's role as a sweeper. However, Spore is preferred, since it helps Breloom find chances to set up.

Breloom appreciates entry hazard support from Toedscruel and Brambleghast wearing down foes, as well as breaking Ogerpon-C's Sturdy so Breloom can immediately OHKO it with Mach Punch. Additionally, the two of them provide entry hazard removal with Rapid Spin so that Breloom's Focus Sash does not break. Amoonguss is a great defensive partner that threatens Fairy-types such as Enamorus and Iron Valiant, and it can also run Spore so that Breloom can choose to run Swords Dance instead. Meowscarada appreciates Breloom immobilizing threats with Spore and removing Toxapex and Ting-Lu, and in return, it handles Ghost- and Psychic types such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Latios. Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-C appreciate Breloom handling their checks such as Greninja, Barraskewda, and Ogerpon-W for them. In return, Ogerpon-H handles bulky Grass-types such as Sinistcha and Amoonguss, while Ogerpon-C threatens Flying-types such as Articuno and Moltres. Abomasnow sets up Aurora Veil to make Breloom harder to take down, allowing it to find more opportunities to set up and sweep.

Choice Band (Grass).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis is for the Regulation C format of Battle Stadium Singles, which lasts until June 30th, 2023. For more information on this format and its current events, check out this page!

If you feel this analysis is missing anything important or needs an update, feel free to suggest any changes here.

Offensive.description:
• Since it can sleep foes without restriction, Breloom is a monstrous foe that applies serious pressure at Team Preview!

  • Bulldoze: This is Breloom's best option against Gholdengo and provides valuable speed control.

  • Spore: As good as Spore is, it's well prepared for enough by threats such as Gholdengo, Garganacl, and Lum Berry that going without it can make sense.

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb provides a form of speed control that can't be walled by Flying-types like Dragonite.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat lets Breloom muscle past bulkier threats more easily, such as Wo-Chien.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low / Medium: While Breloom can certainly take advantage of Terastallization, Focus Sash variants are used fairly early in the game and often don't need it. Loaded Dice Breloom, however, does like Terastallization covering up its iffy defensive typing.

  • Fire: With Tera Blast, Tera Fire provides an alternative way to get past Gholdengo, avoids getting burned by other foes, and gives bulkier Breloom a chance against Flutter Mane and Focus Sash Chien-Pao.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting is a good choice for picking off foes more easily with Mach Punch.

  • Grass: Bullet Seed's boost from Tera Grass means it will OHKO Chien-Pao through its Focus Sash if Breloom rolls at least three hits.

  • Rock: Besides boosting Rock Tomb's damage output, Tera Rock prevents Sandstorm from breaking Breloom's Focus Sash.

  • Ground: Tera Ground-boosted Bulldoze has a 93.8% chance to OHKO 4 HP Gholdengo, making Breloom a situational lure. It also severely punishes Rotom-W that attempt to Volt Switch out, and Hippowdon that don't Terastallize.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Since Breloom's bulk isn't very good, Focus Sash is the most reliable way to fire off Spore.

  • Loaded Dice: Guaranteeing 4 hits from Bullet Seed can be quite useful for bulkier Breloom sets, clinching an OHKO on Flutter Mane, Chien-Pao, and Iron Bundle regardless of them running Substitute or Focus Sash.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe: If using Focus Sash, maximizing Speed is important to deal with slower foes that might invest in Speed, such as Corviknight and Skeledirge.

  • 252 HP / 180 Atk / 76 SpD: This bulkier spread makes sense if using Loaded Dice and Swords Dance, letting Breloom survive one hit from Iron Bundle, Chien-Pao, or Choice Specs Flutter Mane with the correct Tera type.

SubSeed.description:
• With Poison Heal, Breloom can act as a pivot versus defensive Pokemon such as Dondozo and Umbreon as it is unaffected by Yawn.

  • This set can catch opponents expecting the more popular Focus Sash set off guard. However, do note that this set is very susceptible to Taunt and Encore, which can make it difficult to even select Breloom in the team preview phase.

  • Protect: Protect gives Breloom an opportunity to scout out its opponents and further stall them out once Leech Seed has been set up.

  • Timer Stalling: If you obtain a numerical advantage early in the match, you can utilize Breloom to win on timer. This is particularly effective since the Leech Seed damage happens after recovery from Leftovers and Poison Heal.

  • Bulldoze: Bulldoze allows Breloom to further support its teammates and threaten Gholdengo, which likes to absorb status moves. Do be wary that many Gholdengo are Tera Flying, which can render Breloom ineffective versus it.

Other Options
  • Toxic: Toxic can be difficult to fit into the set, but it allows Breloom to punish Tera Grass foes that attempt to circumvent Breloom's Spore and Leech Seed.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: While Breloom's typing does have some useful resistances, its low bulk means more favorable resistances granted by Terastallization can be key to setting up.

  • Water: This defensive Tera type allows Breloom to resist Baxcalibur's Icicle Spear and Skeledirge's Torch Song, both of which are threats to Substitute. It also helps against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, though note that Choice Specs Chi-Yu can still OHKO with Tera Fire Overheat.

  • Fire: This Tera type allows Breloom to resist Ice- and Fire-type attacks while also providing Breloom with a Fairy-type resistance. With Toxic, Breloom is able to fight back against common Grass-type switch-ins. However, this type has more weaknesses when compared to Water.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Impish: This spread allows for maximum physical bulk.

  • 156 HP / 100 Def / 252 Spe with Jolly: This spread allows for maximum Speed and can survive a Choice Band Extreme Speed from Tera Normal Dragonite after Stealth Rock.

  • 204 HP / 164 Def / 140 Spe with Impish: This spread hits a Speed stat of 108 which ties 4 Spe Adamant Baxcalibur. Furthermore, the defensive investment means that after Terastallization, Breloom's Substitute has a high chance of surviving three hits from Baxcalibur's Icicle Spear.

Swords Dance (Grass).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Dual Status (Ghost).description: Shedinja is an effective answer to several Pokemon that otherwise do well against Ghost teams, such as Mega Swampert, Manaphy, Raging Bolt, and Tapu Koko, due to Shedinja's Wonder Guard ability blocking all of their common attacks, bolstering Ghost's matchup versus types like Water and Electric. Protect scouts potential super effective coverage from popular Choice item users such as Tapu Lele, Keldeo, and Iron Valiant, as well as giving Shedinja a free turn to slowly accrue more burn or poison damage. Will-O-Wisp allows Shedinja to burn many physical attackers that it beats, such as Mega Swampert, Ogerpon-W, and Iron Hands. Toxic lets Shedinja put dangerous threats to Ghost switching into it such as Greninja, Hydreigon, and Mega Charizard X on a timer, allowing its team to more easily outplay them. Shadow Sneak can pick off weakened threats such as Iron Boulder and Blacephalon. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Shedinja to not be immediately KOed by entry hazards, offering it more opportunities to switch into the aforementioned threats. Alternatively, Focus Sash may be used to inflict status onto these threats in a pinch as well as escape a Pursuit attempt by the likes of Weavile and Mega Aerodactyl. Minimum bulk investment allows Shedinja to guarantee an OHKO on Ditto transformed into it with Shadow Sneak. Shedinja is commonly found on slower paced Ghost teams, making Gholdengo and Mega Sableye fantastic partners; they are able to absorb status effects for Shedinja, and the latter also reflects entry hazards with Magic Bounce to protect Focus Sash Shedinja. Mimikyu greatly appreciates Shedinja wearing down the opposing team with its status moves, and Shedinja appreciates Mimikyu threatening Dark-types such as Roaring Moon and Hisuian Samurott. Brambleghast is able to remove hazards for Focus Sash Shedinja with Rapid Spin and further wears down the opposition with Spikes, while Shedinja takes the burden off of Brambleghast to check Water-types such as Mega Swampert and Urshifu-R. Skeledirge forms a solid defensive core with Shedinja, handling many physical threats that Shedinja can only do so much against like Victini and Mega Charizard X.

nu.overview: Hariyama stands out in NU as a powerful wallbreaker and can double as a devastating sweeper or as a reliable tank. It utilizes Guts to punish status-inflicting moves from many common defensive Pokemon such as Bellibolt, Vaporeon, and Altaria. With access to Drain Punch, Hariyama can keep itself healthy by capitalizing on Steel-types such as Duraludon, letting it come out unscathed and take on threats like Flygon and Scrafty one-on-one. Hariyama also benefits from Assault Vest, which allows it to handle powerful special attackers such as Chandelure and Goodra. However, Hariyama can struggle a lot with common Fairy- and Flying-types in the tier such as Sylveon, Flamigo, and Cramorant, as they can take the majority of its attacks and hit it back for super effective damage. Hariyama is also very slow, meaning even Pokemon with mediocre Speed such as Tsareena, Klefki, and Altaria can hit it before it has a chance to respond, limiting its sweeping potential. This, on top of Hariyama's average abilities and proclivity to being overwhelmed, leaves it outclassed at times by other Fighting-types such as Flamigo, Scrafty, and Paldean Tauros-W.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Belly Drum alongside Sitrus Berry can be used to give Hariyama an immediate power boost on more offensive teams, but setup is difficult with Hariyama's low defenses. Headlong Rush is an alternative on sets using Earthquake to allow Hariyama to cleanly 2HKO the likes of Galarian Slowbro while having a solid chance to 2HKO Overqwil at the cost of losing defensive utility. Flame Orb, especially alongside Facade, can be used to give Hariyama an immediate boost and a strong neutral option against the likes of Altaria and Amoonguss.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Fairy-types such as Sylveon and Scream Tail can be a pain for Hariyama, as they take both Drain Punch and Knock Off very easily and hit it back for massive damage in return with their STAB attacks. However, Heavy Slam can significantly damage both of them, and they can struggle against Hariyama if it uses Tera Steel.

Flying-types: Flying-types such as Flamigo, Altaria, and Cramorant are a real struggle for Hariyama, as they can easily take Drain Punch and threaten it out with Brave Bird or Hurricane, though the first two must be wary of Ice Punch. However, Tera Steel can potentially allow Hariyama to either hit them all back for massive damage or use these Pokemon as a setup opportunity.

Psychic-types: Psychic-types such as Munkidori, Galarian Articuno, and Meloetta are massive threats for Hariyama, as they can force it out very easily with their STAB Psychic-type attacks. However, they do have to be careful about switching into Hariyama, as Knock Off deals massive damage to them, and Munkidori in particular has to be careful because Toxic Chain can give Hariyama a free Guts activation.

Bulk Up.description:
Set Details

Drain Punch allows Hariyama to sustain itself over the course of the battle, helping versus powerful Steel-types like Duraludon. Meanwhile, Close Combat hits much harder, OHKOing Flygon and 2HKOing Vaporeon at +1. Knock Off enables Hariyama to hit common Ghost-types such as Chandelure and Houndstone while also removing items from switch-ins such as Altaria and Gligar. Bullet Punch gives Hariyama the ability to pick off faster weakened Pokemon such as Flamigo and Munkidori, while Heavy Slam allows Hariyama to OHKO the likes of Sylveon and Scream Tail at +1. Leftovers grants Hariyama recovery outside of Drain Punch, which allows it to set up much more easily. Guts allows Hariyama to punish common status-inflicting moves such as Will-O-Wisp, Scald, Thunder Wave, and Toxic from common defensive Pokemon like Altaria, Vaporeon, Klefki, and Amoonguss. 124 Speed EVs enable Hariyama to outspeed the likes of Vaporeon, Sylveon, and Swampert while maximizing Attack. Tera Steel boosts the power of Bullet Punch and Heavy Slam, allowing the former to 2HKO Flamigo and Munkidori at +1 after Stealth Rock and the latter to OHKO both Sylveon and Scream Tail. It also flips Hariyama's weakness to Flying-, Psychic-, and Fairy-type attacks from the likes of Flamigo, Munkidori, and Sylveon.

Hariyama fits primarily on bulky offense and balance teams, which appreciate its ability to punish common defensive staples such as Vaporeon and Bellibolt. Dealing with these walls aids partners such as Chandelure and Tornadus in their wallbreaking. Steel-types such as Bronzong and Copperajah are great for Hariyama, as they can take on popular Fairy- and Psychic-types such as Sylveon, Scream Tail, and Munkidori that Hariyama struggles with; in return, Hariyama can help take on common Dark-types such as Incineroar and Scrafty that may threaten them. Hariyama appreciates entry hazard setters such as Gligar, Rhyperior, and Bronzong that can help chip opposing Pokemon that it struggles with such as Sylveon and Scream Tail. In return, Hariyama can use common hazard removal options such as Tsareena and Altaria as potential switch-in opportunities to either start setting up or activate Guts through the latter's Will-O-Wisp. Pivots that can help get Hariyama in, such as Vaporeon and Incineroar, are great partners, as they lure in Pokemon such as Rhyperior, Amoonguss, and Scrafty so Hariyama can start setting up.

Assault Vest Wallbreaker.description:
Set Details

Close Combat can be used over Drain Punch, giving Hariyama the ability to 2HKO tanks such as Vaporeon and Bellibolt with a Guts boost. Knock Off allows Hariyama to hit common Ghost-types such as Chandelure and Houndstone while also removing items from switch-ins such as Altaria and Gligar. Bullet Punch gives it the ability to pick off faster weakened Pokemon such as Flamigo and Munkidori. Heavy Slam allows Hariyama to hit Fairy-types such as Sylveon and Scream Tail that might otherwise wall it. Ice Punch enables it to hit the likes of Altaria, Gligar, Scyther, and Flygon. Earthquake can hit Poison-types that usually wall Hariyama, such as Galarian Slowbro and Overqwil, for big damage. Assault Vest allows Hariyama to soak up special attacks from the likes of Chandelure and specially offensive Basculegion-M before responding with its own powerful attacks. Facade, when paired with Guts, gives Hariyama a powerful attack that can put pressure on Pokemon like Cramorant and Scream Tail. With Guts, Hariyama can take advantage of foes that carry status-inflicting moves, like Vaporeon with Scald and Klefki with Thunder Wave, to become an even more threatening wallbreaker. Thick Fat allows it to tank Fire-type attacks from Incineroar and Chandelure. The given EV spread enables Hariyama to outpace Vaporeon and Adamant Rhyperior while tanking attacks from Chandelure and Duraludon. Tera Steel boosts the power of Bullet Punch and Heavy Slam, allowing the latter to OHKO both Sylveon and Scream Tail while giving Hariyama an advantage against Flying-, Psychic-, and Fairy-types like Tornadus, Munkidori, and Sylveon.

Hariyama synergizes with bulkier and more offensive styles alike, handling common walls like Bellibolt and Will-O-Wisp Houndstone. Due to Hariyama's lack of longevity, it heavily appreciates Pokemon that can help sustain it, such as Wish Vaporeon and Sylveon as well as Leech Seed Wo-Chien. Steel-types such as Duraludon, Bronzong, and Klefki are heavily appreciated by Hariyama, as they can take on common Flying-, Psychic-, and Fairy-types such as Scyther, Munkidori, and Sylveon that Hariyama struggles against; in return, Hariyama can take on powerful special attackers such as Chandelure and Goodra that might threaten those Steel-types out. Hariyama particularly struggles against Poison-types such as Galarian Slowbro and Tera Poison Sylveon if it does not have Earthquake. Therefore, Pokemon such as Rhyperior and Copperajah that can help take on these Poison-types are great partners for Hariyama. Pivots such as Flygon, Bellibolt, and Vaporeon can help Hariyama get into battle and start wallbreaking against Pokemon such as Bronzong and Tsareena. Hariyama folds to physical attackers like Paldean Tauros-W, Flygon, and even Ambipom, so physically defensive partners such as Houndstone, Sylveon, and Bellibolt are necessary.

Assault Vest.description:
• With threats such as Chi-Yu, Iron Moth, Volcarona, and Chien-Pao around, Hariyama carves a niche for itself as an Assault Vest user capable of taking them on. Along with its decent bulk, Thick Fat gives it key resistances to Fire- and Ice-type attacks.

  • Bullet Punch: Bullet Punch provides Hariyama with a non-situational priority move that can grab KOs on weakened targets, and, when boosted by Tera Steel, turn the tides against Fairy-type opponents such as Flutter Mane and Mimikyu.

  • Fake Out versus Knock Off: Fake Out gives Hariyama another source of priority, and it can even be used to scout for Covert Cloak users if the opponent doesn't get flinched by it. Knock Off cripples switch-ins by removing their items; however, it can't remove a Booster Energy from an opponent with the Protosynthesis or Quark Drive in Sun or Electric Terrain, respectively, as it's consumed before Hariyama gets to move.

  • Close Combat versus Drain Punch: Close Combat is the stronger move but at the cost of cutting into Hariyama's bulk with each use. Drain Punch can fail to get a 2HKO on specially defensive Ting-Lu more than 90% of the time, but it provides Hariyama with some recovery, bolstering its bulk.

  • Headlong Rush: Headlong Rush drops Hariyama's defenses with each use, but it 2HKOes defensive Toxapex and Gholdengo.

Other Options

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch gives Hariyama a strong option to hit Dragonite with and can catch it by surprise, considering it isn't pressured to Terastallize against Hariyama's other moves.

  • Heavy Slam: Heavy Slam, coupled with Tera Steel, provides Hariyama with a strong move against lightweight foes such as Flutter Mane, Iron Bundle, Chien-Pao, Mimikyu, and Terastallized Iron Moth and Volcarona that doesn't drop its defenses.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Hariyama can work without Terastallization, it can provide an extra kick to its coverage or improve its defensive presence against certain threats.

  • Steel: Steel Tera gives Hariyama STAB on Bullet Punch, a resistance to Fairy, Psychic, and Steel, and an immunity to Poison, greatly improving its matchup against Flutter Mane, Mimikyu, Psychic Chi-Yu, Gholdengo, and Tera Fairy Iron Moth and Volcarona. Thanks to Thick Fat, it can take on non-Choice Specs variants of Chi-Yu even after Terastallizing if it's kept healthy.

  • Fire: Besides the burn immunity, Tera Fire capitalizes on Hariyama's Thick Fat, discouraging threats like Tera Fire Chi-Yu and Choice Band Chien-Pao from using their most powerful moves.

  • Fighting: While Tera Fighting doesn't provide anything defensively for Hariyama, it makes Close Combat a force to be reckoned with.

Guts Attacker.description:
• Thanks to Guts, Hariyama can work as a status absorber and boost its high Attack at the same time, making it a threat to Toxic Spikes-stacking teams.

  • Bullet Punch: Bullet Punch gives Hariyama a consistent priority move and an option to hit Fairy-type foes.

  • Fake Out versus Knock Off: Fake Out is an option to safely activate Flame Orb and Guts, while Knock Off provides utility in removing items from the opponent.

  • Close Combat versus Drain Punch: Guts-boosted Close Combat is a force to be reckoned with, being one of the few moves capable of OHKOing physically defensive Wo-Chien. Drain Punch is weaker, but the recovery can help offset the burn damage.

  • Earthquake versus Headlong Rush: Earthquake complements Hariyama's coverage nicely, hitting Poison-types that resist Close Combat. Headlong Rush is stronger, but comes with the drawbacks of lowering defenses and being a contact move, triggering Rocky Helmet.

Other Options
  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch is Hariyama's best hope of hitting Dragonite, as it doesn't fear much from Hariyama's other moves.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Terastallization gives a much appreciated boost to Bullet Punch, but it isn't necessary on every match.

  • Steel: Terastallizing into the Steel-type turns Hariyama's Fairy and Psychic weaknesses into resistances along with giving STAB to Bullet Punch.

Stallbreaker (Dark).description:
Sableye is a good pick for Dark teams thanks to its Fighting immunity, spinblocking prowess, and ability to pester opposing teams with a wide array of status moves. Night Shade provides a consistent form of damage, preventing Sableye from being too passive, as well as letting it deal with Skarmory and Iron Hands one-on-one. Prankster Will-O-Wisp shuts down Physical attackers, such as Sneasler, Excadrill, and Urshifu-R, regardless of their Speed. Encore locks foes into passive moves, such as Recover and Roost, as well as setup moves such as Dragon Dance and Iron Defense, usually forcing a switch thereafter. Thunder Wave is an alternative option that can be used to slow down opposing Pokemon in order to make Dark's threatening breakers, such as Choice Specs Greninja, outspeed faster foes, such as Dragapult and Choice Scarf Enamorus.

Ting-Lu is a great teammate for Sableye, as it can supply a multitude of entry hazards in the form of Spikes and Stealth Rock. Coupled with Sableye's Rapid Spin immunity, some teams will have a very difficult time removing entry hazards as long as Sableye is around. Alolan Muk is another fantastic teammate for Sableye, as its Poison typing is key when it comes to dealing with Fairy-types, such as Hatterene and Primarina. Bisharp can utilize Swords Dance to help deal with bulkier Pokemon, such as Galarian Weezing and Toxapex, and pick off Flutter Mane via Sucker Punch. Bisharp can prevent hazard removal as well, as its Defiant ability will make foes think twice about using Defog. Strong wallbreakers such as Choice Specs Greninja, Darkrai, and Hydreigon are good teammates, as are Choice Scarf Hoopa-U and Meowscarada; the pressure applied by entry hazards makes it incredibly difficult for defensive Pokemon, such as Clodsire and Archaludon, to switch in repeatedly. Furthermore, they can deal with Pokemon that Sableye is largely ineffective against, such as Hatterene, Gholdengo, and opposing Dark-types. In return, Sableye can switch in on threatening Fighting-type attacks from Pokemon such as Iron Hands, Skarmory, and Corviknight.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Foul Play can be run over Knock Off to further punish setup, especially against Dark-types that would otherwise freely set up on Sableye such as Sneasel and Tera Dark Toxicroak. Taunt can ruin opposing defensive Pokemon like Lanturn and Venusaur, as well as deny entry hazards from being set, but Encore is better at handling offensive threats. Calm Mind sets may seem tempting with priority recovery, but Sableye's poor overall stats leaves it outclassed in this role by Spiritomb.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Dark-types are immune to Prankster and resist Sableye's attacks, meaning they can easily switch into it. Spiritomb, Skunktank and Sneasel turns Sableye into setup fodder, Brute Bonnet with Booster Energy doesn't care about Knock Off, and Houndoom can grab a Flash Fire boost from Will-O-Wisp. Hisuian Sneasel and Toxicroak can flip around their poor matchup to Sableye with Terastallization.

Special Attackers: Special wallbreakers like Jolteon, Arboliva, and Clawitzer don't mind Will-O-Wisp and can capitalize on Sableye's poor special bulk. Whimsicott in particular can OHKO Sableye with its STAB Moonblast.

Priority Blocking: While rare, priority blocking from Indeedee-F's Psychic Surge and Farigaraf's Armor Tail completely shut down Sableye's status moves.

Physical Wall.description:
Prankster-boosted status moves and an excellent matchup into top tiers like Mesprit make Sableye well-suited to be a physical wall in ZU. Encore allows Sableye to shut down opposing offensive Pokemon, stifling setup attempts from Minior, Toxicroak, and more. Will-O-Wisp neuters physical attackers, while Thunder Wave slows down foes and deters special attackers like Whimsicott from switching into Sableye. Knock Off removes crucial items like Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots, giving Sableye an easily spammable move that ensures progress. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Sableye switch in and out of battle without fearing entry hazard chip damage, while Rocky Helmet further punishes physical attackers and deters U-turn from the likes of Perrserker and Mesprit. Tera Poison gives Sableye a Fairy resistance while retaining a good matchup into opposing Fighting-types and giving it a Toxic immunity.

Sableye's ability to deny opposing setup paired with its excellent defensive typing makes it a great glue piece to round out a balance or bulky offense team. Its myriad immunities deter Fighting-types like Hitmontop and Psychic-types like Mesprit from using their STAB attacks. Special walls like Lanturn and Muk enjoy having Sableye to fall back on against physical threats, while Sableye appreciates their ability to handle special wallbreakers like Jolteon and Whimsicott. Dark-types like Spiritomb, Brute Bonnet, and Skunktank, as well as Tera Dark users like Hisuian Sneasel and Toxicroak are immune to Sableye's Prankster moves, easily using it as an entry point. As such, checks to these special threats like Whimsicott and Hitmontop are crucial teammates for Sableye. Entry hazard setters like Regirock, Orthworm, and Whiscash have great synergy with Sableye, as it naturally blocks Rapid Spin and can remove Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off. Sableye is also a good Knock Off absorber itself, which helps these Leftovers-reliant Pokemon.

Calm Mind (Dark).description: On offensive Dark teams, Calm Mind Mega Sableye can serve as a sturdy setup sweeper that brings some defensive utility to the table and ignores common anti-setup moves such as Taunt, Encore, and Whirlwind. Additionally, its ability to spread status with Will-O-Wisp enables the team to handle threatening physical attackers like Urshifu-R, Mega Scizor, and Great Tusk. Prankster can be used before Mega Evolving to cripple faster attackers like Mega Lopunny that threaten Mega Sableye and its teammates. For its attacking move, Sableye can choose between Hex or Dark Pulse; Hex does more damage to statused targets, but Dark Pulse has greater base power and nothing is immune to it. Most offensive Dark teams do not run entry hazard removal, so they appreciate Mega Sableye's ability to make opponents think twice before attempting to set hazards. Grimmsnarl is Mega Sableye's best teammate, setting dual screens to provide Mega Sableye with the initial durability increase it needs to start stacking Calm Mind boosts. With screens active, Mega Sableye always dodges being 2HKOed by Mega Lopunny's Close Combat and Meowscarada's Play Rough, and it can use Calm Mind to dodge 2HKOs from threatening special attackers such as Choice Specs Tapu Koko and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, effectively turning them into setup fodder. In return, Grimmsnarl appreciates Mega Sableye's ability to prevent opposing hazard setters like Skarmory and Ting-Lu from stacking hazards in front of it. Hazard-weak teammates such as Flyinium Z Galarian Moltres, Weavile, and Focus Sash Hisuian Samurott hugely appreciate Mega Sableye's ability to prevent Stealth Rocks from being set easily. In return, Galarian Moltres helps handle troublesome Fighting-types like Mega Lopunny and Iron Valiant, while Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge limits foes from repeatedly switching into Mega Sableye. Revenge killers like Meowscarada, Greninja, and Weavile can help threaten opposing setup sweepers that would overwhelm Mega Sableye like Calm Mind Enamorus and Swords Dance Ceruledge.

Mixed Wall (Dark).description: Mega Sableye is a relevant defensive backbone for Dark teams because it serves as a switch-in to Fighting-type moves and is a good punisher of entry hazard setters such as Archaludon, Klefki, and Clodsire thanks to its solid mixed bulk and Magic Bounce. Metal Burst lets Mega Sableye reduce its passivity by damaging foes more than Knock Off, notably OHKOing Kommo-o after withstanding Clangorous Soulblaze and Mega Diancie. Protect is an alternative that lets it safely Mega Evolve when it's threatened by foes such as Mega Diancie and Mega Lopunny, ensuring that it can block entry hazards mid-game with Magic Bounce and easing its prediction against Choice-locked foes such as Galarian Darmanitan and Enamorus. The given EV spread allows Mega Sableye to avoid an OHKO from Mega Diancie's Moonblast and a 2HKO from Excadrill's Earthquake. Mega Sableye is forced out by Fairy-types such as Iron Valiant and Tapu Koko, so Alolan Muk and Ting-Lu are good partners to mitigate this weakness; the latter also sets hazards up, which Mega Sableye can maintain by blocking Rapid Spin from Excadrill, Iron Treads, and Terapagos. Mandibuzz complements Mega Sableye by checking Fighting-types it can't consistently handle such as Mega Lopunny and Great Tusk and providing hazard control as further backup if Mega Sableye is unable to keep entry hazards off of its side of the field. As Mega Sableye cripples foes throughout a battle, setup sweepers such as Hydreigon and Weavile and cleaners like Choice Scarf Meowscarada find easier setup opportunities to KO foes on the other team.

Mixed Wall (Ghost).description: Mega Sableye is a staple on bulkier Ghost teams due to its Dark typing, great abilities before and after Mega Evolution, and great defensive stats. Knock Off hinders Chansey and Porygon2 for Mega Sableye's wallbreaking teammates and eases the matchup against Landorus and Nidoking. Due to Sableye's meager HP and need for longevity, Recover's a must-have utility option, further enabling Metal Burst. Protect allows Sableye to Mega Evolve safely, ensuring it can utilize Magic Bounce later into the game. Metal Burst retaliates against Fairy-types such as Mega Diancie, while Dazzling Gleam eliminates Mega Sableye's passivity in front of Hydreigon and Roaring Moon. Will-O-Wisp in conjunction with Prankster renders physical attackers like Mega Gallade, Dragonite, and Mamoswine less threatening. The given EV spread avoids a 2HKO from Life Orb Nidoking's Earth Power, assuming Mega Sableye uses Knock Off after the first Earth Power. Mimikyu threatens Dark-types such as Mandibuzz, Galarian Moltres, and opposing Mega Sableye. Gholdengo checks Fairy-types such as Tapu Lele, Mega Diancie, and Iron Valiant as well as preventing foes from removing entry hazards set by Froslass and Galarian Corsola. Blacephalon handles opposing Gholdengo and utilizes Choice Scarf to clean through Steel, Ghost, and Psychic teams once Heatran, Mega Sableye, and Galarian Slowking, respectively, are removed. Skeledirge has great synergy with Mega Sableye, appreciating the prevention of opposing Stealth Rock and in return walling Volcarona, Mega Lopunny, and Alolan Ninetales.

Swords Dance.description:
Mega Mawile is a threatening setup sweeper and wallbreaker due to its amazing typing, giving it setup opportunities against Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, Clefable, and Tornadus-T, and useful priority in Sucker Punch. What sets Mega Mawile apart from other wallbreakers is the immediate power it gains from Huge Power, meaning it doesn’t require setup to become threatening to defensive staples such as Ting-Lu and Zapdos and switch-ins such as Landorus-T. Swords Dance gives it the power to OHKO Ferrothorn and Slowbro with Knock Off and revenge killers like Garchomp and Mega Charizard Y with Sucker Punch. Knock Off is crucial coverage against Toxapex and Gholdengo and removes key items such as Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from Pokemon like Moltres, the aforementioned Toxapex, and Melmetal. Sucker Punch makes Mega Mawile a potentially dangerous late-game cleaner if boosted, as frail revenge killers such as Ogerpon-W, Mega Lopunny, and Tapu Koko cannot handle boosted Sucker Punch if small amouns of chip damage is accrued on them earlier. Intimidate is the chosen ability before Mega Evolving to make setting up against foes like Hisuian Samurott and Mega Tyranitar an easier task. 140 Speed EVs allow Mega Mawile to outspeed uninvested Corviknight.

Bulky offense teams are where Mega Mawile fits best, as they use defensive pieces such as Heatran and Pecharunt to shore up its vulnerability to foes such as Cinderace and Volcarona. Pecharunt in particular is a good teammate because it pivots in Mega Mawile on foes such as Ting-Lu and Galarian Slowking while being a stellar check to revenge killers like Ogerpon-W, Mega Lopunny, and Zamazenta. Other slow pivots like Galarian Slowking and Landorus-T do a similarly good job at bringing Mega Mawile in on foes such as Tornadus-T and Mega Tyranitar. Offensive partners such as Serperior and Hisuian Samurott appreciate Mega Mawile taking advantage of defensive pieces such as Tornadus-T and Clefable. They, along with other Spikes setters and paralysis spreaders such as Clefable and Ferrothorn, also provide valuable utility for Mega Mawile. In particular, paralysis support lets Mega Mawile outspeed foes such as Garchomp and Ogerpon-W. Hisuian Samurott and Ferrothorn provide Spikes support so Mega Mawile overwhelms checks such as Melmetal and Heatran more easily. Due to Mega Mawile being easily outrun and threatened by offensive foes such as Great Tusk, Mega Diancie, and Iron Valiant, a defensive backbone with teammates such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Zapdos are appreciated. In return, Mega Mawile provides offensive pressure against Pokemon such as Tornadus-T and Galarian Slowking, which would easily take advantage of them. Steel-Types such as the aforementioned Heatran, Ferrothorn and Gholdengo are needed alongside Mega Mawile, as it cannot safely check foes that they can cover, such as Tapu Lele, Roaring Moon, and Melmetal; Tapu Lele’s Psychic Terrain also blocks Mega Mawile's Sucker Punch. Mega Mawile in return takes advantage of Pokemon that can switch in on these Steel-types, such as Alomomola and Ting-Lu.

All-Out Attacker.description:
Mega Mawile is a truly devastating wallbreaker, boasting a wide array of coverage options that makes it a terror for defensive teams to pivot around safely. Ice Punch targets foes like Landorus-T and Gliscor, with the former not being a reliable switch-in at all, as Ice Punch OHKOes it even after Intimidate. Thunder Punch hits defensive Water-type Pokemon like Slowbro, Alomomola, and Toxapex attempting to come in on Play Rough. Fire Fang nails Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Mega Scizor, and Melmetal. Knock Off is another option that can be utilized to discourage Gholdengo, as well as stopping Pecharunt from switching in. Lastly, Brick Break can be used to completely eviscerate Kingambit, in addition to preventing Heatran from otherwise walling Mega Mawile. The 204 speed EVs allow Mega Mawile to outrun bulky Swords Dance Mega Scizor.

Mega Mawile is found mostly on bulky offense teams. These teams appreciate its ability to exert pressure on common defensive staples like Ting-Lu and Ferrothorn. Landorus-T makes an effective partner, as it is a crucial switch-in to faster Ground-type foes like Great Tusk and opposing Landorus-T that force out Mega Mawile. In return, Mega Mawile is able to punch holes in its checks like Corviknight and Slowbro. Additionally, entry hazard support from teammates such as the aforementioned Great Tusk and Landorus-T makes Mega Mawile more difficult to switch into. Mega Mawile in return puts great pressure on the Flying-types that Landorus-T brings in, such as Tornadus-T and Zapdos, limiting their ability to use Defog. It also values pivot support from allies such as Raging Bolt and Tapu Koko bringing it in on their checks like Ferrothorn and Galarian Slowking. Mega Mawile is prone to getting worn down fast with hazards, so it appreciates hazard removal from teammates like Great Tusk and Terapagos.

Mega Medicham is a destructive wallbreaker that is hugely threatening to several common defensive staples like Ferrothorn, Toxapex, Great Tusk, and Melmetal. Its immense power even allows it to 2HKO bulky neutral targets like Corviknight and Alomomola. Fake Out allows Mega Medicham to pressure faster and more offensive Pokemon like Mega Lopunny, Iron Moth, and Ogerpon-W. This lets Mega Medicham act as a revenge killer if these threats are weakened, and it chips much of the metagame decently. Ice Punch blows past Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Dragonite with ease. Bullet Punch alongside Fake Out improves Mega Medicham's revenge killing capabilities versus offensive teams, and it notably applies significant pressure onto Mega Diancie and Iron Valiant. Fire Punch hits Gholdengo, which is a very common check, and almost always OHKOes Mega Scizor. Fire Punch's targets are very specific, however, which makes it less consistent than Ice Punch and Bullet Punch on a game-to-game basis.

Pursuit trapping checks is hugely beneficial to Mega Medicham. Assault Vest Kingambit and Weavile can trap and remove checks such as Gholdengo, Mega Latios, Mega Latias, and Slowbro. Mega Medicham threatens several Pokemon that are irritating for them in return, such as Great Tusk, Alomomola, and Toxapex. Mega Medicham's poor defensive profile makes it hard to switch into battle safely, so it appreciates slow pivots like Alomomola, Galarian Slowking, and defensive Landorus-T that can ease prediction and help it get on the field. A solid defensive backbone is advised when using Mega Medicham, as several very common offensive threats revenge kill it with ease, including Iron Valiant, Mega Latios, and Ogerpon-W. Teammates like Toxapex, Ferrothorn, Ting-Lu, and Assault Vest Kingambit are very helpful in this regard. Hisuian Samurott is another great teammate that checks threatening Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo and Mega Latios while also laying down Spikes, and it can use Flip Turn to pivot Mega Medicham into battle. Other forms of entry hazard support, like Spikes from Ferrothorn and Stealth Rock from Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu, are generally very helpful, as they help wear down checks such as Gholdengo. Fast late-game cleaners like Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Cinderace appreciate Mega Medicham blowing up opposing defenses before they come into battle to sweep later on.

Physical Attacker (Water).description: This is a sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Trick Room Attacker.description: • Eruption is Mega Camerupt's most powerful move, but Nature Power allows Mega Camerupt a way to deal with Tapu Fini through Grassy Terrain or Mega Salamence through Misty Terrain. Substitute is a move that Mega Camerupt can use when the opponent is trying to stall out Trick Room.

ru.overview: Torkoal is a solid weather setter in the RU metagame, using its great physical bulk and utility to establish sun and provide entry hazard control for its typically frail teammates. While it competes directly with Ninetales for the role of sun setter, Torkoal carves out a niche because of its access to both Stealth Rock and Rapid Spin, providing great role compression and allowing sun teams to stack more offensive options like Scovillain and Venusaur. It can also leverage its great Defense stat to use the powerful Fighting-type attack Body Press, which threatens the most common spinner in the metagame in Cyclizar. While Torkoal is quite bulky physically, it does struggle to tank many special attacks, with common Choice Specs wallbreakers like Basculegion-F, Toxtricity, and Hisuian Goodra all threatening OHKOs, which can make it difficult to reliably establish and maintain hazards.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Torkoal can use Solar Beam to nail Water-types like Basculegion-F and Slowbro. Earth Power lets Torkoal hit Entei super effectively. Will-O-Wisp can catch physical setup sweepers like Feraligatr and Mimikyu by surprise. Choice Specs Eruption sets can fit on Trick Room teams, blowing through would-be checks like Cyclizar and Slowbro with Tera Fire, though Trick Room teams are not a reliable playstyle in this tier. Torkoal can opt to use Shell Smash in conjunction with an Eject Pack, allowing Copycat users like Espeon to secure an enormous boost.

Checks and Counters

Opposing Weather: Politoed rain can outmuscle Torkoal with its strong team members like Basculegion-F and Kilowattrel.

Special Wallbreakers: Despite sponging physical attacks comfortably, Torkoal is threatened by nearly every special wallbreaker in the tier, such as Gengar, Hisuian Goodra, and Basculegion-F.

Water-types: Basculegion-F, Slowbro, and Quagsire can comfortably sponge non-Solar Beam attacks from Torkoal. Empoleon can threaten Knock Off to remove Heat Rock and Surf that is still threatening under sun. Substitute + Calm Mind Suicune can use Torkoal as setup fodder with ease, burning sun turns in the process.

Sun Support.description:
Set Details

Torkoal can function as the primary Stealth Rock user on sun teams because of its immense physical bulk, allowing it to establish entry hazards while sponging attacks for its teammates. Lava Plume is used to potentially spread burns, which can help whittle specially defensive walls like Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra down and cripple physical attackers like Rhyperior and Terrakion. Body Press uses Torkoal's enormous Defense stat to nail Cyclizar, Empoleon, and Hisuian Goodra. Heat Rock is used to extend the duration of sun, though it does make Torkoal susceptible to hazard chip damage. Tera Ghost is used to spinblock against Cyclizar in an emergency and provide an immunity to Fighting-type attacks from Gallade and Terrakion.

Torkoal supports Offensive Chlorophyll Pokemon like Scovillain and Venusaur that can enter the field and provide immediate wallbreaking power while also having the potential to snowball as setup sweepers. Other defensive partners like Eject Button Amoonguss and Slowbro can be used to provide safe pivots into these offensive teammates, maximizing the amount of sun turns while using Regenerator to recover the damage taken. Bulky offense teammates that can use the sun to their advantage include Entei and Scovillain, which can threaten massive damage while sun is active, as both are comfortably able to 2HKO even Fire-resistant Pokemon like Noivern and Entei.

Sun Setter.description:
With Drought and a number of utility options, Torkoal is OU's best option for a sun setter. Rapid Spin and Stealth Rock grant Torkoal excellent role compression as both an entry hazard remover and setter that can threaten other common leads like Skarmory, Ribombee, and Iron Treads with Lava Plume while also being naturally slower than both Tyranitar and Pelipper, ensuring that sun is the weather that stays up in the lead matchup. Will-O-Wisp can cripple physical attackers like Great Tusk and Dragonite looking to scare Torkoal out and use it as setup fodder without fully relying on Lava Plume's burn chance. A physically defensive EV spread lets Torkoal easily take hits from common threats like Ogerpon-W, Zamazenta, and Rillaboom, but a specially defensive EV spread can instead help bolster Torkoal's middling Special Defense against the likes of Gholdengo and Galarian Slowking. Though Torkoal is rarely the choice to be Terastallized, Tera Flying can be used to remove its Ground-type weakness versus Pokemon like Landorus-T and Great Tusk, while Tera Grass is an all-around solid defensive typing that greatly improves its matchups against Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Hisuian Samurott while still maintaining a good matchup against the aforementioned Ground-types.

Torkoal should only be used on sun teams, where wallbreakers like Walking Wake take great advantage of the sun to activate Protosynthesis and power up their Fire-type moves and Hydro Steam. Raging Bolt is also an appreciated addition to sun teams to threaten Water-types like Ogerpon-W and Dondozo. Hisuian Lilligant is also a strong late-game cleaner on sun teams, helping check Ground-types while significantly improving the often difficult matchup against Iron Boulder thanks to outspeeding it with Chlorophyll active, and Venusaur can also serve as a slower if slightly bulkier Chlorophyll sweeper. Because Torkoal's primary role is to set sun, it appreciates teammates like Kingambit and Eject Button Hatterene that can switch into Knock Off and allow it to keep its Heat Rock. Despite also serving as an entry hazard remover, Torkoal is weak to Stealth Rock and lacks any form of reliable recovery, so it benefits from secondary removal support from teammates like Great Tusk and Iron Treads. Hatterene is a great teammate that can serve as a tertiary form of hazard control with Magic Bounce, help keep its own threats healthy with Healing Wish, and check common Ground-types like Gliscor and Great Tusk with Calm Mind sets.

Torkoal is an excellent choice for sun-based Fire teams thanks to its valuable role compression that consists of setting up sun and Stealth Rock, removing entry hazards, and tanking physical attacks. Lava Plume provides decent damage and a high chance to burn, which proves particularly useful against physical attackers like Sneasler, Ogerpon-W, and Iron Hands. Body Press allows Torkoal to make use of its high Defense to heavily damage the likes of Hisuian Samurott, Blissey, and Tyranitar as well as preventing Roaring Moon from setting up freely and Heatran from switching in freely. Heavy-Duty Boots greatly increases Torkoal's longevity, while Heat Rock provides more turns of sun for setup allies to benefit from, such as Morning Sun Volcarona. If using Heavy-Duty Boots, getting fewer turns of sun also allows Fire teams to better manage opposing Protosynthesis sweepers, such as Flutter Mane or Walking Wake.

Ogerpon-H is an excellent wallbreaker under sun that greatly threatens Water. Thanks to its ability to wallbreak past Dondozo due to Mold Breaker, Ogerpon-H pairs well with other teammates naturally as it checks Dondozo with Mold Breaker. Ceruledge provides valuable speed control with Shadow Sneak, allowing it to deal with troublesome threats to Fire teams such as Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Iron Boulder. These sweepers also greatly appreciate Torkoal’s Stealth Rock support. Volcarona benefits from Torkoal’s sun support, as the additional healing with sun-boosted Morning Sun and weakening of Water-type moves from Greninja and Keldeo greatly eases its ability to set up; in return, Volcarona deals with walls such as Toxapex. Flame Body can also be useful to cripple threats like Great Tusk and Azumarill. Choice Scarf Iron Moth is an excellent check to Walking Wake and Great Tusk with a Speed boost from Protosynthesis; it can also be an excellent late-game cleaner against Steel and Fairy once checks such as Heatran and Primarina are removed. Cinderace can aid Torkoal in keeping off hazards with Court Change. Pyro Ball under sun also forces a lot of switches, which allows Cinderace to use U-turn to safely pivot in wallbreakers. Torkoal appreciates Rotom-H, as its Ground immunity combined with Volt Switch allows it to easily switch in for Torkoal and safely pivot in a sweeper.

Other Options

Yawn can be used over Body Press to force switches, allowing Torkoal to freely bring a teammate that can benefit from sun.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Torkoal performs best at supporting a variety of Pokemon thanks to its sun-setting capabilities. Torkoal additionally functions well as a powerful sweeper when its partners set up Trick Room.
  • When used as a supportive sun setter, Torkoal is often paired with Jumpluff, which takes advantage of the sun via Chlorophyll, allowing it to set Tailwind or put foes to sleep with Sleep Powder before they can move. Torkoal boosts the power of its partners' Fire-type attacks like Heat Wave and Eruption with the sun, making it a great pairing alongside Charizard and Hisuian Typhlosion. Charizard gains an additional damage boost from the sun thanks to Solar Power.
  • Offensive Torkoal pairs well with reliable bulky Trick Room setters like Hatterene and Indeedee-F. Hatterene is capable of providing additional special offense with its powerful Dazzling Gleam as well as Expanding Force when paired with Indeedee-F. Indeedee-F on the other hand provides redirection and can boost Torkoal's damage with Helping Hand as well as using Heal Pulse to provide healing, mitigating the damage reduction of Eruption and increasing Torkoal's longevity. Indeedee-F's Psychic Terrain protects Torkoal from priority attacks, ensuring Torkoal can deal maximum damage with Eruption. Other offensive Trick Room-reliant partners like Ursaluna and Gallade pair well with Torkoal by threatening devastating physical damage. Ursaluna threatens specially defensive foes like Tyranitar. Meanwhile, Gallade deals with bulky foes Torkoal struggles to damage like Incineroar and Annihilape. Gallade additionally protects Torkoal from threatening spread attacks like Earthquake with Wide Guard.
  • Supportive Torkoal can be very passive with Overheat as its primary offensive attack. It is very reliant on enabling its partners to take the KOs it can't achieve alone. Offensive Torkoal struggles to sufficiently damage Water-types like Primarina, so it relies on partners like Hatterene and Ursaluna to defeat them. Torkoal is easily threatened by powerful sweepers that move before Torkoal and threaten super effective damage like Garchomp and Tyranitar. Hatterene can set up Trick Room to ensure they do not attack before Torkoal moves and threatens both of them with its Fairy-type attacks.

Strategy Comments

  • Supportive Torkoal is best positioned when it can easily enable sun and provide support for its partners. Offensive Torkoal, on the other hand, is best used to sweep once Trick Room is active.
  • As a supportive sun setter, Torkoal should be lead to set sun immediately for its partners. When it is lead, this set can potentially switch out immediately after Intimidate from Incineroar is triggered, allowing an offensive partner like Hisuian Typhlosion to switch in safely before you and the opponent can select their attacks for the turn. When using an offensive set, Torkoal is best kept in the back and should only be switched in while Trick Room is active.
  • Foes capable of KOing Torkoal and its Trick Room-setting partners before Trick Room is set up are huge threats. To mitigate this, Indeedee-F can redirect attacks to protect Torkoal or the Trick Room setter from damage. Rain setters like Pelipper override the sun set by Torkoal, weakening and disrupting its partners; to prevent this, the rain setters should be KOed as soon as possible.

Supportive Sun Setter.description:
• This Torkoal set is used for setting up sun and providing additional support for its partners.
  • Overheat is a powerful nuke that allows Torkoal to switch out immediately after use thanks to Eject Pack. Eruption deals strong spread damage if Torkoal stays on the field. Clear Smog clears foes' stat boosts, most notably from Dondozo.
  • Eject Pack allows Torkoal to switch out on lead when it has its Attack dropped by Intimidate from Incineroar, allowing its partners to take advantage of the sun immediately, as well as using Overheat to allow a partner to switch in safely and at the end of the turn.
  • Tera Fire allows Torkoal to OHKO Ursaluna-B with Overheat.

Trick Room Sweeper.description:
• Torkoal is a threatening sweeper under Trick Room that sets up sun, providing support for its partners.
  • Eruption deals powerful Fire-type spread damage; meanwhile, Heat Wave provides consistent spread damage regardless of Torkoal's remaining HP. Weather Ball deals strong, consistent damage while sun is active, and Overheat is often used as a single-use nuke attack. Earth Power allows Torkoal to threaten Fire-types like Incineroar. Protect is used on Charcoal sets, while Clear Smog is used on Choice Specs sets to disrupt Dondozo and setup sweepers like Volcarona.
  • Charcoal and Choice Specs are used to increase Torkoal's damage, with Charcoal guaranteeing Eruption OHKOes Assault Vest Rillaboom and Choice Specs Weather Ball 2HKOing Assault Vest Archaludon.
  • Tera Fire boosts Torkoal's damage, allowing it to OHKO Ursaluna with Eruption.

vgc2024.overview:
• Torkoal is a premier offensive Pokemon seen on Trick Room teams thanks to its great STAB moves, fantastic ability, and good defenses. Its low Speed also makes it faster than most of the tier when in Trick Room, and it has great matchups into Pokemon like Amoonguss

  • Some of Torkoal's strongest partners are Trick Room setters like Cresselia and Farigiraf, which can help set up Trick Room and protect it from damage with Ally Switch and Armor Tail, respectively. Torkoal also pairs well with other Pokemon that benefit from Trick Room like Ursaluna-B and Iron Hands, which can threaten neutral damage onto most of the tier, notably threatening Pokemon like Raging Bolt and Tera Water Ogerpon-W, respectively.

  • Torkoal struggles against bulky Pokemon that resist Fire like Raging Bolt, Incineroar, as well as Tera Water Ogerpon-W, and Assault Vest Rillaboom, as they can withstand its boosted Eruptions and burn Trick Room turns, making partners like Ursaluna-B, Amoonguss, and Rillaboom appreciated.

Trick Room Sweeper.description:
• Earth Power hits foes that resist Fire like Entei, Incineroar, Arcanine-Hisui, and Raging Bolt.

  • Charcoal boosts the damage of Torkoal's Fire-type moves, letting it OHKO Assault Vest Kingambit.

  • Tera Fire further bolsters Torkoal's Fire-type moves, letting it even 2HKO foes that resist Fire like Raging Bolt, Chi-Yu, and Tera Water Amoonguss.

Sun Setter.description: Torkoal is the only viable sun setter in Ubers UU, and this combined with its great bulk and deep expansive utility movepool makes it one of the tier's most powerful weather setters. Rapid Spin and Stealth Rock allow Torkoal to operate as both an entry hazard setter and remover for its team, freeing up moveslots on its partners.
