Yawn gives Torkoal the ability to force switches, help bring in teammates safely, and potentially sleep Pokemon attempting to take advantage of its relatively passivity, but Will-O-Wisp is an option to particularly cripple physical attackers like Zacian and Kingambit. Although Torkoal does not Terastallize much, Tera Ghost gives it the ability to spinblock and potentially spread status to Pokemon like Arceus formes and Great Tusk. Torkoal is the backbone of sun teams, and as a result, it should only be used on them. Sun wallbreakers like Chi-Yu, Walking Wake, Roaring Moon, and Gouging Fire are appreciated partners, as they get their STAB moves boosted and Protosynthesis enabled under sun. Hazard control from Pokemon like Great Tusk can allow Torkoal to not operate as the primary form of hazard control for its team and give it more opportunities to switch in to set up sun multiple times in a game.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Sun Support.description:
• Torkoal's Drought and disruption support helps set up heavy-hitting Protosynthesis users like Flutter Mane, Roaring Moon, and Gouging Fire.

  • Overheat versus Lava Plume: Overheat with Eject Pack lets Torkoal act as a one-use pivot to safely let good sun teammates in. If running Heat Rock as Torkoal's item instead, Lava Plume is used for the consistent damage and decent burn chance.

  • Solar Beam: Solar Beam takes advantage of Drought to let Torkoal pressure offensive Water-types like Urshifu-R.

  • Gyro Ball: Torkoal makes excellent use of a slow Gyro Ball and can surprise semi-bulky Flutter Mane that try to use Taunt against it with a potential OHKO.

Other Options

  • Clear Smog: Clear Smog allows Torkoal to disrupt opposing setup while still attacking. However, its weak Base Power usually means it does not fix Yawn's problem of being weak against Substitute.

  • Fissure: Torkoal's great defensive profile complements Fissure well, sometimes allowing it to bail itself and its team out of a bad matchup.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Torkoal's high bulk and support focus means that it normally saves Terastallization for its teammates.

  • Grass: Tera Grass flips Torkoal's Water and Ground weaknesses into resistances and is Torkoal's best option for cushioning Hydro Steam from Walking Wake.

  • Fire: Tera Fire can be used in a pinch to give Torkoal more offensive presence with Overheat or Lava Plume.

  • Flying: Tera Flying's Ground immunity is an alternative to Tera Grass that doesn't make it weak to opposing Flying-type moves, making it situationally better against Tera Flying sweepers like Dragonite and Landorus-T.

Items

  • Eject Pack: Eject Pack with Overheat is the preferred choice for pivoting in teammates safely.

  • Heat Rock: Heat Rock gives some extra flexibility with managing sun turns, which can be particularly useful if running multiple sun teammates.

EV Spreads

  • Negative Speed nature and 0 Speed IV: This is the standard for the slowest Eject Pack pivot possible, as well as maximizing Gyro Ball's power.

  • 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpD with Sassy: This avoids an OHKO from Choice Specs Latios from all but the highest damage roll. It also gives Torkoal a decent chance of surviving Modest Ursaluna-B's Earth Power as well as Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Stellar Power Gem.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD with Relaxed: Maximizing physical bulk doesn't help in nearly as much places as special bulk, but one place it does is avoiding a 2HKO from Adamant Dragonite's Earthquake.

Sun Setter.description: • 9 Defense IVs allow for Torkoal to get a Special Attack boost from Protosynthesis.

Torkoal provides great support for Fire teams thanks to its ability to set sun and Stealth Rock as well as remove entry hazards with Rapid Spin. Lava Plume can potentially burn offensive threats like Dragonite and Iron Hands. Body Press allows Torkoal to use its great physical bulk to its advantage by threatening Dark-types such as Roaring Moon and Tyranitar. Heat Rock allows Torkoal's sun to support teammates for longer, but Heavy-Duty Boots can also be used so that Torkoal can switch in more freely without fearing entry hazards and have an easier time removing them. Yawn is an option that pairs well with Stealth Rock because it forces switches. Volcarona makes for a great partner, as it appreciates the sun Torkoal sets so that its Flamethrower can hit new benchmarks, notably OHKOing Landorus and 2HKOing Empoleon and Alolan Muk after a boost, as well as now being able to survive a Hydro Pump from Choice Specs Greninja to set up one Quiver Dance. In return, Volcarona is able to deal with Fighting- and Ground-types such as Kommo-o, Swampert, and Great Tusk thanks to its coverage. Cinderace threatens Normal- and Rock-type foes such as Porygon2, Ogerpon-C, and Hisuian Arcanine and can don a Choice Scarf to dispatch speedy threats such as Choice Scarf Iron Treads and Tapu Lele. Heatran deals with problematic walls such as Toxapex and Archaludon by trapping them with Magma Storm and removing them with Earth Power as well as Diancie with Flash Cannon. Heatran also runs Stealth Rock so that Torkoal can opt to use another option such as Yawn. Late-game sweepers and cleaners such as Mega Charizard X, Ceruledge, and Blacephalon appreciate the sun Torkoal provides so that they can mop up more efficiently.

With its access to Drought and good utility options, Torkoal acts as an enabler for dedicated sun teams while also functioning as an entry hazard setter and remover. Lava Plume's relatively high burn chance lets Torkoal cripple foes that could set up on it, such as Raging Bolt and Mega Latios. Body Press enables Torkoal to hit Heatran, with it otherwise being able to switch in reliably on Torkoal's Fire-type moves; it also hits Mega Tyranitar that could otherwise come in and remove Torkoal's sun. Stealth Rock's chip damage allows its sun-boosted teammates to sweep more easily, while Toxic is also an option in order to punish Water-types such as Alomomola and Slowbro that could otherwise come in relatively risk-free; however, it should only be used if your team has another Stealth Rock setter. Rapid Spin's hazard removal helps its team greatly due to the fact that Torkoal runs Heat Rock over Heavy-Duty Boots, but it is advised to run other hazard removal options as well due to Torkoal's vulnerability to hazards. Maximum Defense investment is used in order to boost the power of Torkoal's Body Press, letting it hit Mega Tyranitar and Heatran harder while also letting it function as an emergency check to foes such as Cinderace.

Torkoal only fits on designated sun teams, where its ability to set sun while also setting and removing entry hazards is greatly appreciated. A Pokemon that benefits greatly from this sun is Great Tusk, with its activated Protosynthesis letting it do increased damage to foes such as Ferrothorn and Alomomola. In return, Great Tusk can set and remove Stealth Rock and other hazards, letting Torkoal come in to set sun more time; it is also a much-needed Rock-resistant teammate and Knock Off absorber against foes such as Mega Tyranitar and Kingambit, which could otherwise threaten to remove Torkoal's Heat Rock. Other teammates that benefit from Torkoal's sun include Raging Bolt and Venusaur. Protosynthesis boosts the former's Special Attack, allowing it to do greater damage to would-be switch-ins such as Ting Lu; in addition, sun making its Weather Ball a Fire-type move lets it hit foes such as Ferrothorn. Sun doubles Venusaur's Speed stat, courtesy of Chlorophyll, and boosts the effects of Growth, allowing it to become a dangerous setup sweeper. In return, Raging Bolt can threaten Pelipper, which would otherwise be able to remove Torkoal's sun via Drizzle. Torkoal finds itself vulnerable to Ground-type attacks from foes such as opposing Great Tusk and Landorus-T, meaning Flying-types such as Corviknight and Mega Charizard Y are appreciated. In exchange, Torkoal can, to some extent, sponge physical hits from foes such as Cinderace that could otherwise be threatening underneath sun. Torkoal especially struggles with Mega-Tyranitar, meaning that teammates such as the aforementioned Great Tusk and Landorus-T are enjoyed. Pivots to bring in Torkoal and its sun-enjoying teammates are also appreciated, with Eject Button Hatterene and Landorus-T being excellent choices due to their ability to deny hazards via Magic Bounce and Defog, respectively.

Trapper.description:
Trapinch's respectable bulk, insane Attack stat, and access to Arena Trap make it a powerful trapper. Earthquake OHKOes many targets, including Elekid, Alolan Diglett, Tinkatink, Glimmet, Stunky, and Hisuian Growlithe. Stone Edge completes its EdgeQuake coverage, letting Trapinch hit Flying-types like Vullaby and Wingull. First Impression can finish off chipped foes and revenge kill Gothita. Feint is another form of priority and can bypass Protect. Trapinch has very low base Speed, so it is better to invest in bulk. This EV spread prevents 2HKOs from Stunky's Knock Off and Elekid's Psychic while also avoiding OHKOs from Terastallized Hisuian Growlithe's Flare Blitz and Terastallized Alolan Diglett's Earthquake. Tera Bug is used to further boost First Impression's damage, OHKOing Toedscool and Grookey. In a pinch, it can be used to resist Earthquakes from Alolan Diglett.

Flying-types like Vullaby and Wingull appreciate Trapinch's ability to trap Steel- and Electric-types. Vullaby can U-turn on Glimmet and Tinkatink, bringing Trapinch in safely to trap and remove them with Earthquake. Wingull struggles with Elekid and Stunky, both of which Trapinch can eliminate. In return, these partners handle Grass-types like Foongus, Toedscool, and Grookey that threaten Trapinch. VoltTurn support from teammates like Mienfoo, Elekid, and Chinchou makes switching in and trapping easier for Trapinch.
This is a winning set from the Monotype Rising sets project.

ru.overview: Flygon is one of the most versatile Pokemon in the metagame, being able to serve as a wallbreaker, revenge killer, setup sweeper, or entry hazard setter depending on the needs of its team. Its phenomenal STAB coverage and access to U-turn allow it to threaten a majority of the metagame with strong neutral attacks and pivot out of physically defensive switch-ins like Chesnaught. Flygon's immunities to Ground- and Electric-type moves as well as Spikes from Pokemon like Hippowdon, Magnezone, and Chesnaught supplement its defensive utility and longevity as a pivot. However, Flygon suffers from Attack and Speed stats that are middling for an offensive Pokemon along with a lack of access to utility options such as Defog and recovery, often putting it below alternatives like Choice Scarf Krookodile as a revenge killer, Dragon Dance Gyarados as a setup sweeper, and Noivern as pivot support. Furthermore, Flygon's mediocre bulk, which cements its place as a jack of all trades, master of none, renders it vulnerable to faster offensive threats including Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Galarian Zapdos as well as the most common Pokemon in the tier, Draco Meteor Cyclizar.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Psychic Noise is an option on pivot sets that allows Flygon to make progress against its switch-ins like Hippowdon and Chesnaught. Lum Berry can be used on Dragon Dance sets to either provide a free turn to set up on the likes of Will-O-Wisp Talonflame and Stun Spore Amoonguss or neutralize confusion from Outrage.

Checks and Counters

Physical Walls: Many common physical walls in the metagame, including Slowbro, Umbreon, and Chesnaught, take little damage from Flygon's attacks as well as threaten it back with their own attacks and, in the case of the former two, status conditions.

Fairy-types: Faster Fairy-type Pokemon like Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Ribombee can threaten non-Choice Scarf Flygon with an OHKO. Mimikyu is also able to take a hit from Flygon and eliminate it thanks to Disguise, though Flygon is able to break Disguise and pivot out simultaneously with U-turn if it isn't locked into a move.

Dragon-types: Common Dragon-types like Noivern and Cyclizar outspeed non-Choice Scarf Flygon and threaten it with Draco Meteor.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description:
Stealth Rock Flygon is an excellent offensive Ground-type that is able to make progress even against its best switch-ins with Stealth Rock. Scale Shot improves Flygon's ability to act as an offensive threat and cleaner. U-turn enables it to deal decent damage to and pivot out of its defensive checks like Slowbro and Chesnaught. Stone Edge is an alternative that provides coverage against Flying-types such as Talonflame and Gyarados. Loaded Dice helps guarantee OHKOs on Dragon-types like Cyclizar and Noivern with Scale Shot. Levitate provides Flygon with great defensive utility in an immunity to Ground-type moves and most entry hazards, which pairs well with its natural resistance to Stealth Rock and cements it as a reliable pivot. Tera Steel flips all of Flygon's weaknesses to resistances, allowing it to strike back against threats such as Noivern and Choice Scarf Gardevoir. It also provides a valuable immunity to poison and synergizes with Levitate by making Flygon immune to one of the Steel-type's most glaring weaknesses in Ground-type attacks. Tera Ghost is an option that gives Flygon valuable immunities to strong attacks such as Galarian Zapdos's Close Combat, Maushold's Population Bomb, and Entei's Extreme Speed. Tera Fairy is viable due to its immunity to Draco Meteor from Dragon-types like Hisuian Goodra and Cyclizar that Flygon can proceed to promptly take out, along with its resistance to common physical attacks such as Krookodile's Knock Off and Bisharp's Sucker Punch.

Stealth Rock Flygon is a great fit on both balanced and offensive structures looking for an offensive Ground-type entry hazard setter. Flygon's decent natural bulk makes it an easy-to-fit pivot and Volt Switch absorber in almost any team. It sets itself apart from other options like Krookodile with its defensive utility in its Ground immunity and resistance to Fire-type moves, which pairs well with common Steel-types like Empoleon, Jirachi, and Bisharp by providing a switch-in to threats such as Krookodile and Armarouge. These Steel-types in turn can comfortably tank Fairy- and Dragon-type attacks from Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Draco Meteor Cyclizar looking to take Flygon out. Special wallbreakers such as Gengar, Basculegion-F, and Armarouge work well with U-turn Flygon, as they can pivot into its defensive checks like Slowbro and Chesnaught and immediately threaten to blow holes in the opposing team. Thanks to Scale Shot, Flygon can serve as a decent late-game cleaner and therefore, it fits nicely in bulkier structures with Spikes setters such as Gastrodon and Chesnaught that aim to wear down the opposing team by stacking hazards.

Choice Band.description:
Flygon's access to STAB Earthquake along with U-turn, strong priority, and defensive utility from its Ground and Electric immunities make it a potent wallbreaker in the tier. Outrage hits Ground-resistant foes such as Chesnaught and Talonflame hard. Dragon Claw can be used for a safer option that doesn't lock Flygon in. Stone Edge is another option that decimates the likes of Talonflame and Noivern without locking itself into Outrage. First Impression provides valuable priority, allowing it to keep setup sweepers such as Dragon Dance Feraligatr and Tidy Up Maushold in check; this provides immense utility against hyper offense teams. U-turn allows it to pivot out of bad matchups such as Chesnaught and Slowbro and bring in dangerous wallbreakers like Armarouge and Volcanion. Choice Band lets Flygon threaten physically defensive Pokemon such as Hippowdon. Levitate provides Flygon with a Spikes immunity, allowing it to function as a resilient pivot. Tera Steel flips the Fairy- and Dragon-type weakness into a resistance, turning the tables on Pokemon like Choice Scarf Gardevoir, Noivern, and opposing Flygon. Tera Bug strengthens Flygon's U-turn and makes First Impression even more potent at revenge killing threats such as Armarouge and Maushold.

Choice Band Flygon fits best on bulky offense teams, which enjoy its role compression with its Ground and Electric immunities as well as its wallbreaking prowess, pivoting ability, and priority. Flygon likes pairing up with partners such as Life Orb Reuniclus, Choice Scarf Gardevoir, and Nasty Plot Mew, which rip apart Flygon answers such as Chesnaught and Slowbro, while Flygon takes care of Steel-type Pokemon such as Hisuian Goodra and Jirachi that trouble them. Gardevoir is also capable of bringing Flygon back from the brink with Healing Wish, letting it continue to break walls. Frail special attackers such as Noivern and Gengar also enjoy Flygon's ability to bring them in safely in front of specially frail Pokemon like Chesnaught and Slowbro. Slow special wallbreakers like Volcanion, Empoleon, and Magnezone appreciate the easy entry Flygon provides with U-turn on Pokemon such as Slowbro and Hippowdon, while Flygon busts through special tanks such as Umbreon and Hisuian Goodra for them; all of them resist Fairy-type moves from Pokemon such as Gardevoir and Mimikyu for Flygon, and the latter two resist Dragon-type moves from the likes of Noivern. Rotom-C is another great partner, as it threatens Hippowdon and Slowbro while forming a VoltTurn core with Flygon. Calm Mind Suicune is also a great teammate that enjoys free setup opportunities on the likes of Talonflame and Hippowdon while still providing Flygon a switch-in against the likes of Basculegion-F and Noivern; in return, Flygon is immune to Electric and deals with Hisuian Goodra. Bulky Steel-type pokemon such as Jirachi and Registeel make great partners, as they check the aforementioned Fairy- and Dragon-type Pokemon.

Dragon Dance.description:
Dragon Dance Flygon is able to utilize its fantastic STAB combination and good defensive utility to serve as a devastating setup sweeper. Stone Edge allows it to take out Flying-types like Talonflame. Scale Shot hits Grass-types like Chesnaught hard and helps Flygon to sweep by further boosting its Speed. Fire Punch, usually paired with Tera Fire, is an alternative that can similarly threaten Grass-types and hits certain targets like Chesnaught and Forretress for super effective damage. Loaded Dice helps guarantee OHKOs on Cyclizar at +0 as well as Galarian Zapdos after Stealth Rock at +2. Leftovers instead boosts Flygon's longevity, which can allow it to set up multiple times. Levitate provides immunities to Earthquake from Krookodile and Hippowdon as well as Spikes, creating more opportunities for Flygon to switch in safely. Tera Steel is fantastic defensively, as it flips all of Flygon's weaknesses into resistances, enabling it to turn would-be threats like Noivern and Choice Scarf Gardevoir into setup opportunities. Tera Fire instead boosts the power of Fire Punch and gives Flygon an immunity to burn from Will-O-Wisp Talonflame, which also provides it with a free turn to set up.

Dragon Dance Flygon fits best on offense structures, varying from hyper offense to bulky offense, looking for a powerful setup sweeper and late-game cleaner with good defensive utility. Its decent bulk combined with Levitate frequently allows it to set up without fear of getting eliminated easily by Ground-types like Krookodile and priority attacks such as Sucker Punch from Bisharp and Extreme Speed from Entei. It appreciates teammates that can wear the opposing team down to being in range of Flygon's attacks and enable a late-game sweep. Entry hazard setters like Kleavor, Jirachi, and Chesnaught therefore pair well with Flygon. Other wallbreakers and sweepers, notably Bisharp, Basculegion-F and Choice Scarf Gardevoir, can similarly help Flygon fulfill its role by wearing down its defensive checks like Chesnaught and Slowbro. Status spreaders such as Thunder Wave Slowbro, Will-O-Wisp Talonflame, and Thunder Wave Reuniclus can also support Flygon by crippling targets such as Noivern, Mimikyu, and Cyclizar, respectively.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Flygon utilizes its strong STAB attacks to be a powerful offensive threat and late-game cleaner. Stone Edge threatens Flying-types like Talonflame and Gyarados for super effective damage. U-turn allows Flygon to maintain momentum and pivot out of defensive switch-ins like Slowbro and Chesnaught. A Choice Scarf lets Flygon outspeed the entire unboosted metagame and a few other Choice Scarf users, including key targets like Cyclizar, Noivern, and Choice Scarf Gardevoir. Levitate enables Flygon to handle Krookodile and Hippowdon more effectively and improves its reliability as a pivot with an immunity to Spikes. Tera Steel flips all of Flygon's weaknesses to Dragon-, Fairy- and Ice-type moves into resistances, enabling it to survive a hit from and take out would-be checks such as Noivern, Choice Scarf Gardevoir, and Basculegion-F. Tera Dragon is an offensive option that strengthens Outrage, guaranteeing a 2HKO on Krookodile after Intimidate and providing good odds to OHKO Basculegion-F after Stealth Rock.

Choice Scarf Flygon fits best on balance and offense teams looking for a reliable revenge killer and late-game cleaner. It pairs well with entry hazard setters like Jirachi and Chesnaught that can wear down the opposing team so that Flygon is able to KO them and potentially pull off a sweep. Special pivot partners like Raikou, Basculegion-F, and Magnezone are able to form VoltTurn cores with Flygon, maintaining momentum and threatening its defensive checks such as Slowbro, Hippowdon, and Chesnaught, while Flygon can take care of special sponges like Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and Assault Vest Cyclizar. Similarly, strong Choice Band wallbreakers like Crawdaunt, Golurk, and Entei can more reliably wear down the aforementioned shared defensive checks so that it is able to clean late-game. Status spreaders, including the likes of Toxic Umbreon, Flame Body + Will-O-Wisp Talonflame, and Thunder Wave Reuniclus, are also able to support Flygon by crippling Pokemon that it otherwise could have trouble with such as Slowbro, Mimikyu, and Choice Scarf Galarian Zapdos.

nu.overview: Flygon's great set versatility makes it an elite Pokemon and one of the best Ground-types in NU. Choice Scarf Flygon fits on many teams, outspeeding and limiting many wallbreakers such as non-Choice Scarf Infernape and Munkidori. Choice Band gives Flygon an incredibly spammable Earthquake and makes it a lot harder to switch into. Flygon can also pivot out with U-turn, allowing it to maintain offensive pressure and momentum. Dragon Dance Flygon can use Clear Amulet, which makes it a great late-game sweeper, and it also threatens lead entry hazard setters like Duraludon and Smeargle. Additionally, it can run moves like Fire Blast to threaten would-be checks like Bronzong and Avalugg. However, as a Choice Scarf user, it faces competition from Munkidori and Infernape, both of which are faster than it and can revenge kill it with Close Combat or Psychic. Additionally, Flygon's average Attack leaves it struggling when facing physical walls like Vaporeon, Amoonguss, and Avalugg, as they can still take its attacks even after a Dragon Dance. Choice Scarf Flygon can be very easy to play around due to both of its STAB options having common immunities and resistances.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Flygon can run a Choice Specs set with Tera Normal, which gives it a powerful Boomburst. However, it's not common due to Flygon's low Special Attack. Flygon can also run a utility set with Stealth Rock / Earthquake / Dragon Tail / U-turn with a bulkier EV spread. This set allows it to set entry hazards for its teammates and check foes like Copperajah and Infernape. Sadly, Flygon lacks any recovery, making it very easy for it to get worn down by chip damage.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Sylveon and Alolan Ninetales are able to tank hits from Choice Scarf Flygon and KO it back with their STAB Fairy-type attacks; however, neither of them can handle Choice Band sets too well, and they can be setup fodder against Tera Steel Dragon Dance Flygon.

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Physically defensive Pokemon such as Gligar and Amoonguss have enough bulk to win against any of Flygon's sets, but Amoonguss has to be careful directly switching into +1 Flygon if entry hazards are present. Bulky Water-types like Vaporeon, Swampert, and Milotic are bulky enough to tank a boosted attack and threaten Flygon back with status and Knock Off.

Priority Users and Faster Attackers: Infernape, Toxicroak, and Basculegion-M can revenge kill Flygon after it has been weakened a bit. Choice Scarf users like Munkidori and Infernape can outspeed even Choice Scarf Flygon and destroy it with Psychic and Close Combat.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

Outrage is one of Flygon's strongest STAB attacks for late-game cleaning, and it can 2HKO foes like Tsareena and Kilowattrel on a switch. Dragon Claw is a safer option to avoid getting locked into Outrage, but it's significantly weaker and is harder to revenge kill foes with. U-turn allows Flygon to maintain momentum and provide free switches to teammates. Flygon's last move is commonly Stone Edge, which allows it to hit Flying-types like Kilowattrel as well as Ice-types such as Alolan Ninetales. Alternatively, Stealth Rock allows it to set entry hazards for its teammates. Flygon can run Throat Chop last for a move with great neutral coverage into the entire tier while hitting Bronzong super effectively. First Impression can be used over Stone Edge, allowing Flygon to revenge kill weakened boosted and faster threats like Drednaw and Choice Scarf Munkidori. Tera Steel gives Flygon a resistance to Fairy- and Dragon-type attacks from Pokemon like Sylveon, Florges, and opposing Flygon. This also allows it to check some special wallbreakers like Alolan Ninetales, and Munkidori.

Wallbreakers like Chandelure, Infernape, and Basculegion-M appreciate Choice Scarf Flygon for giving them free entry with U-turn. Flygon can form a VoltTurn core with special attackers like Bellibolt, Raikou, and Kilowattrel. They can threaten physical walls like Vaporeon, Avalugg, and Amoonguss; in return, Flygon can pressure special walls like Duraludon and Copperajah. Choice Scarf Flygon struggles to break past bulky Water-types like Vaporeon, Swampert, and Milotic, which tank its attacks and punish it with Scald, Knock Off, or a slow Flip Turn. Grass-types like Tsareena, Decidueye, and Amoonguss similarly appreciate Flygon's U-turn giving them free entry to handle the aforementioned bulky Water-types. Steel-types like Copperajah and Bronzong appreciate Flygon for checking Fire-types like Chandelure, Infernape, and Incineroar; in return, they can check Fairy-types like Sylveon, Florges, and Scream Tail. Choice Scarf Flygon appreciates entry hazard support from Copperajah, Klefki, and Swampert, as it can wear down foes to help with Choice Scarf Flygon's low damage output.

Choice Band.description:
Set Details

Choice Band gives Flygon more immediate power, allowing it to always 2HKO non-Heavy-Duty Boots Amoongus after Stealth Rock with Earthquake. Outrage is still an option to allow Flygon to 2HKO Vaporeon, but Scale Shot is preferred so Flygon isn't easily revenge killed by Fairy-types, and it makes Flygon harder to revenge kill overall. Alternatively, Dragon Claw offers Flygon a reliable and decently powered STAB move. First Impression revenge kills weakened foes like opposing Flygon, Munkidori, and Raikou. However, Throat Chop provides coverage for Bronzong and shuts down Hyper Voice Sylveon whereas Stone Edge pops Kilowattrel and Alolan Ninetales on the switch. Tera Steel is a great defensive typing and allows Flygon to pivot without getting chipped heavily by Stealth Rock, but Tera Bug gives First Impression a power boost.

Choice Band Flygon likes having entry hazard support from teammates like Klefki, Copperajah, and Duraludon to wear down foes that can repeatedly switch into it. Many Pokemon that tend to struggle against bulky Water-types like Vaporeon and Milotic, such as Flamigo, Infernape, and Basculegion, appreciate Choice Band Flygon's ability to 2HKO them on the switch. However, while it can 2HKO most bulky Water-types, it can't always beat them one-on-one, so it pairs well with Grass-types like Tsareena and Amoonguss. Physically defensive Pokemon like Gligar and Whimsicott can take Flygon's attacks with ease, so it pairs best with Pokemon like Basculegion-M, Munkidori, and Chandelure that can handle these physical walls.

Dragon Dance.description:
Set Details

Dragon Dance with a Scale Shot boost allows Flygon to outspeed the entire tier, including common Choice Scarf users like Munkidori and Infernape. Dropping Scale Shot for Outrage is acceptable to run a different item, but this makes Flygon significantly more reliant on obtaining multiple Dragon Dance boosts to avoid being revenge killed. Fire Punch allows Flygon to hit Grass-types like Tsareena, Amoonguss, and Decidueye, as well as Steel-types like Bronzong, Copperajah, and Tera Steel Flygon. Alternatively, Throat Chop lets Flygon target Bronzong, and it blocks Sylveon from using Hyper Voice. Tera Steel allows it to take attacks from Alolan Ninetales, Sylveon, Munkidori, and Flygon more easily. With Tera Steel, Flygon can also exploit Pokemon like Amoonguss for easier setup. Tera Fire gives Fire Punch a much-needed power boost and retains the resistance to Fairy-type attacks that Tera Steel gives while offering a burn immunity. Clear Amulet is preferred to avoid Incineroar's and Paldean Tauros-W's Intimidate, but Loaded Dice can be used to improve Scale Shot's effectiveness. However, more niche items like Leftovers and Muscle Band are usable, and Dragon Dance Flygon's EV spread is so malleable that many sets can get away with running Adamant.

Dragon Dance Flygon appreciates entry hazard support from Klefki and Swampert to guarantee a 2HKO on Pokemon like Amoonguss and Vaporeon. Flygon is a perfect pick for hyper offense teams due to its Sticky Web immunity and because it can sweep opposing hyper offense teams. It can also punish lead hazard setters like Cinccino and Smeargle by setting up a Dragon Dance and breaking their Focus Sashes with Scale Shot. Other sweepers like Cinccino, Munkidori, and Scyther appreciate Dragon Dance Flygon's ability to weaken teams so they can win late-game. Choice Scarf users like Munkidori and Infernape can force Flygon to switch out even if it's at +1 because they can still outspeed it. Thus, slow pivots like Bellibolt, Swampert, and Flip Turn Vaporeon can help by bringing Flygon in safely. Other Pokemon that overwhelm Bronzong alongside Flygon synergize especially well. Therefore, Scream Tail, Munkidori, Alolan Ninetales, and Tornadus make for great partners.

Stealth Rock.description:
Scale Shot paired with Loaded Dice allows Flygon to damage and outpace foes like Munkidori, Kilowattrel, and Choice Scarf Flamigo while crucially threatening the tier's most common Defog user in Altaria. First Impression allows Flygon to revenge kill weakened foes like Drednaw, Munkidori, and Scream Tail. Throat Chop allows Flygon to block sound-based attacks from foes like Sylveon and Roar Vaporeon as well as hit Bronzong. Dragon Tail can also be used to force out sweepers like Shell Smash Drednaw and Bulk Up Scrafty; however, Flygon prefers to run other moves due to them having more utility and being more usable. U-turn lets Flygon freely pivot and chip walls like Bronzong, Swampert, and Gligar while bluffing a Choice Scarf set. Insect Plate increases the power of both First Impression and U-turn, while Leftovers provides Flygon useful recovery. Rocky Helmet can be used to punish Pokemon like Munkidori and Flamigo by chipping them, but Flygon's lack of any recovery makes running other items preferred. Tera Steel lets it better handle threats such as Munkidori and Sylveon, while Tera Fairy allows it to better handle Fighting- and Dark-types like Flamigo, Scrafty, and Incineroar on top of walling opposing Flygon. Tera Bug gives First Impression and U-turn an extra power boost but grants Flygon a weakness to Stealth Rock.

Faster Pokemon like Munkidori, Kilowattrel, and Choice Scarf Flamigo can easily revenge kill Flygon, so it best partners with walls like Bronzong, Galarian Slowbro, and Bellibolt that can check them. Wallbreakers like Chandelure, Substitute Basculegion-M, and Swords Dance Flamigo appreciate Flygon’s U-turn giving them free entry on passive walls such as Vaporeon, Bronzong, and Amoonguss. Spikes setters such as Gligar, Klefki, and Overqwil synergize greatly with Flygon, since they can help each other wear down shared checks like Bronzong, Wo-Chien, and Amoonguss. Special walls like Bronzong, Copperajah, and Wo-Chien can help Flygon by better handling special attackers like Sylveon, Alolan Ninetales, and Uxie. Wish passers like Vaporeon and Sylveon provide Flygon useful recovery, allowing it to repeatedly switch into threats like Toxicroak, Munkidori, and Raikou.

Mixed Attacker.description: 88 Attack EVs ensures Flygon can come in and OHKO Incineroar with Earthquake.

Defensive Utility.description: Flygon is a niche role compression option for bulkier teams that is an effective check to a variety of defining offensive threats like Aegislash, Iron Moth, and Victini while providing Defog support and blocking Volt Switch from the likes of Rotom-W and Zeraora better than Ground-types like Hippowdon and Swampert. Earthquake and Toxic allow Flygon to properly perform its role by checking the aforementioned options as well as ensuring that Flygon can beat certain entry hazard setters such as Hippowdon and Swampert. However, Flygon can fail to prevent hazards being set up by Clefable and Skarmory given its inability to threaten them. While Defog is essential for Flygon to perform its primary role, alternative utility options such as U-turn, Dragon Tail, and Psychic Noise are options on bulkier hazard-stacking teams that appreciate Flygon's defensive profile but do not need Defog. Leftovers is generally preferred on Flygon, as its Spikes immunity and Stealth Rock resistance mean that Heavy-Duty Boots is not necessary. Groundium Z is an alternative option to allow Flygon to threaten OHKOs on certain Ground-weak foes like Aegislash and Iron Boulder that may otherwise be able to survive an Earthquake. The given EV spread avoids a 3HKO from Choice Band Iron Boulder's Mighty Cleave, lets Flygon take Shadow Ball twice from maximum Special Attack Aegislash and not be 4HKOed by Iron Moth's Sludge Wave, and outspeeds Timid Magnezone and positive-natured Aegislash. When using Groundium Z, an alternative EV spread of 16 Attack and 148 Special Defense with an Adamant Nature is recommended to always OHKO maximum HP Shield forme Aegislash and always take Shadow Ball twice from maximum Special Attack Aegislash. Given Flygon's inability to handle many of the metagame's premier threats such as Alakazam, Mega Venusaur, and Excadrill and inability to use Defog on common hazard setters like Skarmory and Clefable, heavy team support is necessary to facilitate it, leaving Flygon generally only used on stall or other bulky team styles. Reliable answers to Clefable and Skarmory such as Jirachi, Mega Venusaur, and Aegislash are required alongside Flygon; in return, Flygon can check Fire- and Ground-types such as Victini and Hippowdon. Mega Venusaur, in particular, is a common partner for Flygon, as it appreciates Flygon's ability to remove hazards, can check both Clefable and Skarmory, and appreciates Flygon absorbing burn from Rotom-W. While Flygon provides great utility, its middling bulk means it can often struggle to handle common threats Ground-types are tasked with handling, such as Choice Band Tyranitar and Choice Band Iron Boulder. For this reason, partners like Skarmory and Tangrowth are important alongside Flygon to help handle such threats and patch up holes Flygon may leave in these bulky teams' defensive structures.

nu.overview: Altaria is a good entry hazard control option with a great defensive typing and decent mixed bulk, allowing it to consistently remove hazards. Altaria also has amazing defensive utility, as it can wall powerful threats such as both Paldean Tauros formes, Basculegion-M, and Infernape. Natural Cure allows Altaria to double up as a status absorber, enabling status-hating Pokemon like Vaporeon, Incineroar, and Substitute Basculegion-M. With Perish trapping sets, Altaria can surprise bulky walls and offensive foes alike that plan to take advantage of it like Bronzong and Scrafty, and by removing these foes, Altaria can open up its teammates to more easily break through and take on the opposing team. However, utility sets are very passive, meaning many Pokemon such as Dudunsparce, Sylveon, and Alolan Ninetales can capitalize on it by switching in freely. Additionally, Altaria's 4x Ice weakness means that it must be extremely careful around Pokemon carrying Ice-type coverage like Inteleon and Milotic as well as Ice-types like Alolan Ninetales, Froslass, Rotom-Frost, and Avalugg. Altaria requires its Heavy-Duty Boots so that it can reliably use Defog, which forces it to be cautious around Knock Off users it would check otherwise such as Infernape and Scrafty.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Cloud Nine lets Altaria be a very potent counter to rain and sun teams by disabling the weather and resisting their attacks. However, Alolan Ninetales's snow is the most prevalent weather, and Altaria's 4x Ice weakness makes it struggle against snow teams without Terastallizing. Perish trap Altaria sets can utilize Protect to stall out Perish Song turns, but this forces it to give up some much-needed utility.

Checks and Counters

Ice-types and Ice-type coverage: Altaria's 4x Ice weakness makes it very vulnerable to Ice-type Pokemon, such as Alolan Ninetales, Froslass, and Avalugg, as well as Pokemon carrying Ice-type coverage, such as Inteleon and Golurk.

Fairy-types: Sylveon and Scream Tail can all capitalize on Altaria by using it as a free switch in to wallbreak, set up entry hazards, or boost their stats, though they dislike the pressure that Perish Song puts on them.

Steel-types: Bronzong, Duraludon, and Copperajah can use Altaria as an opportunity to set their hazards. However, Bronzong and Copperajah hate Will-O-Wisp and easily get taken advantage of by Perish Song sets. Additionally, if Altaria Terastallizes or Duraludon already dropped its Special Attack by using Draco Meteor, Altaria can beat Duraludon as well.

Item Displacement: Altaria relies on Heavy-Duty Boots so that it can switch in repeatedly to remove hazards and wall foes, meaning Knock Off users such as Incineroar, Gligar, and Ambipom are threatening. Trick users such as Munkidori and Chandelure can also give Altaria a Choice item, permanently crippling it.

Utility.description:
Set Details

Will-O-Wisp lets Altaria burn physical attackers such as Basculegion-M, Flamigo, and Scyther. Alternatively, Altaria can use Haze to prevent setup sweepers like Arcanine and Incineroar from taking advantage of it. Roar works similarly, and it can rack up entry hazard damage on foes, though it's worse in one-on-one scenarios. Natural Cure allows Altaria to be a very valuable status absorber, being able to take Vaporeon's Scald burns, Amoonguss's Toxic, and Houndstone's Will-O-Wisp. Both EV spreads allow Altaria to be faster than Thwackey, Milotic, and Bulk Up Scrafty, but the first one improves its matchup against physical attackers like Paldean Tauros-W, Flamigo, and Basculegion-M, whereas the second lets it better handle powerful special attackers such as Chandelure, Munkidori, and Kilowattrel. However, a physically defensive set is generally preferred due to the lack of Pokemon in the tier that can also handle both STAB attacks from powerful wallbreakers like Paldean Tauros-W, Infernape, and Paldean Tauros-F. Tera Steel complements Altaria's base typing quite well, gifting Altaria resistances to attacks it would take big damage from otherwise like Alolan Ninetales's Blizzard and Moonblast, Sylveon's Hyper Voice, and Flygon's Dragon-type STAB moves. On the other hand, Tera Fairy grants Altaria a Dragon immunity to help its matchup against Flygon while still maintaining Altaria's Fighting resistance.

Altaria appreciates Steel- and Fairy-type defensive partners, such as Bronzong, Sylveon, and Copperajah, which can switch into Ice-, Dragon-, and Fairy-types that threaten Altaria, such as Alolan Ninetales, Flygon, and opposing Sylveon. Powerful special wallbreakers such as Chandelure, Inteleon, and Meloetta can overwhelm Altaria, especially if they have Ice-type coverage, making special walls such as Copperajah and Chansey good partners. In return, Altaria's great defensive typing lets it switch into Fighting- and Ground-type attacks that threaten them. Altaria's typing also has great synergy with other defensive Pokemon, such as Avalugg, Chansey, Incineroar, and Wo-Chien, switching into attacks from Pokemon that threaten them like Infernape, Swampert, Paldean Tauros-W, and Heracross. Altaria's entry hazard removal further helps keep these defensive cores healthy. However, Altaria is very susceptible to item displacement, making Knock Off absorbers such as Amoonguss, Paldean Tauros-W, Paldean Tauros-F, Sylveon, and Wo-Chien good partners. Finally, Altaria's passivity makes it vulnerable to bulky setup sweepers, especially special attackers that do not care about Will-O-Wisp such as Sylveon, Calm Mind Scream Tail, and Nasty Plot Uxie, making Pokemon that can disrupt them with Encore, such as Whimsicott and Grafaiai, or phazers and Haze users such as Roar Sylveon and Vaporeon as well as Haze Overqwil and Milotic good partners.

Perish Trap.description:
Set Details

Perish Song and Fire Spin let Altaria trap and KO foes that lack pivot moves, such as Bronzong, Amoonguss, and Wo-Chien. Roost lets it heal up and stall turns until Perish Song kicks in. However, Rest can also be used, since Altaria's Natural Cure allows it to heal to full HP and then switch out while removing the sleep status. Altaria's fourth move is very flexible. Defog allows Altaria to remove entry hazards, which it can find opportunities to use when stalling turns for Perish Song. Brave Bird makes Altaria a bit more threatening and not entirely reliant on Perish Song for KOing foes, aiding it against Pokemon that either don't care about Fire Spin or can pivot out of it like Chandelure and Incineroar. Will-O-Wisp lets Altaria cripple physical attackers, allowing it to more easily weather their attacks while waiting for Perish Song. Finally, Haze lets Altaria remove stat boosts from the foe, which prevents setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Incineroar and Bulk Up Scrafty from breaking through Altaria. Natural Cure removes status such as poison from Bellibolt and Amoonguss or paralysis from Klefki and Static Bellibolt when it switches out. A Bold or Calm nature should be used if Fire Spin is Altaria's only attack, but Impish or Careful can be used if Altaria has Brave Bird. Altaria can run either a physically defensive or a specially defensive EV spread, depending on what its team requires defensively. Either way, the given Speed investment lets it outpace Milotic and Bulk Up Scrafty. Tera Steel flips Altaria's matchup against Ice- and Fairy-types such as Alolan Ninetales, Froslass, and Sylveon as well as Pokemon with Ice-type coverage, such as Inteleon or Milotic. Alternatively, Tera Fairy can be used, as it lets Altaria more reliably handle Dragon-types and continue checking Fighting-types after Terastallizing.

Perish trap Altaria pairs well with offensive teammates that struggle to break through bulky foes, such as Paldean Tauros-W, Chandelure, and Munkidori. These Pokemon can bait in their bulky checks, such as Amoonguss, Bronzong, and Copperajah, letting Altaria trap and KO them. Altaria also pairs well with defensive partners that struggle to make progress against bulky teams, such as Houndstone, Vaporeon, and Chansey, helping very passive teams make progress against opposing walls. Knock Off and entry hazard support is very useful for Altaria, as Altaria can force a lot of switches once it is revealed to be a Perish trap variant . This makes Altaria useful on hazard stack teams, with partners such as Gligar, Duraludon, and Bronzong. As Pokemon with pivot moves like Volt Switch Kilowattrel, Flip Turn Basculegion-M, and U-turn Infernape don't fear Perish Song + Fire Spin, teammates that can punish these attacks such as Electric-immune Pokemon like Swampert and Volt Absorb Kilowattrel, Water-immune Pokemon like Vaporeon, and Rocky Helmet users like Milotic and Galarian Slowbro have great synergy. Decidueye, Basculegion-M, and Incineroar enjoy Altaria's great defensive profile, which allows it to switch into checks of theirs like Paldean Tauros-W, Arcanine, Scrafty, and Heracross. Steel- and Fairy-type Pokemon such as Bronzong, Copperajah, Sylveon, and Alolan Ninetales naturally complement Altaria quite well, with the former two being specially defensive partners and the latter two offensively handling Dragon-types.

Offensive Dragon Dance (Dragon).description: Mega Altaria's unique typing and offensive potential allow it to serve as a valuable setup sweeper that checks threats like Kommo-o, Roaring Moon, Iron Hands, and Keldeo. Pixilate-boosted Return checks the aforementioned Dragon-types as well as Fighting- and Dark-types such as Terrakion, Mega Sableye, and Mandibuzz. Earthquake is essential coverage, as it hits Steel- and Fire-types like Heatran and Magnezone and—in conjunction with Return—eases the Dark and Electric matchups. Roost increases Mega Altaria's longevity so it can continuously Dragon Dance throughout the match or use its bulk to switch into threats. The given EV spread allows Mega Altaria to survive Mega Lopunny's Triple Axel. Choice Specs Kyurem is a great teammate, as it breaks past the likes of Toxapex, Corviknight, and Dondozo for Mega Altaria. Garchomp sets up Stealth Rock and Spikes, wearing down Mega Altaria's switch-ins. Kommo-o breaks past Steel-types like Skarmory, Aegislash, and defensive Celesteela as well as other troublesome walls like Toxapex and Hippowdon for Mega Altaria. Roaring Moon threatens obstacles such as Mega Diancie, Choice Specs Greninja, and Skeledirge.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Earthquake can be run over Earth Power to hit Calm Mind Jolteon harder. Hydro Pump is an alternative Water-type STAB move that reduces passivity and is stronger than Surf, but is unreliable.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types and Grass-type coverage: Foes like Arboliva, Dipplin, Brute Bonnet, Venusaur, and Whimsicott completely wall both of Whiscash's STAB moves and threaten it back with their STAB moves. However, Dipplin and Whimsicott should be wary of Ice Beam on switch-in. Pokemon with Grass-type coverage like Energy Ball Vikavolt are typically able to KO Whiscash even from full health, either forcing it to switch out or Terastallize.

Wallbreakers: Wallbreakers like Clawitzer, Nasty Plot Mesprit, and Spiritomb all deal with Whiscash well because of its passive nature, and Mesprit and Spiritomb can freely set up against it.

Hazard Removal: Cryogonal and Hitmontop can force Whiscash out or to Terastallize. However, Cryogonal is threatened by it if it carries Stone Edge. Drifblim can take Whiscash's moves comfortably and whittle it down with Will-O-Wisp and Hex or Shadow Ball.

Entry Hazard Setter.description:
Leveraging its excellent typing, respectable bulk, and access to both Stealth Rock and Spikes, Whiscash is one of the tier's premier entry hazard setters. While Stealth Rock is preferred if the team's sole entry hazard setter is Whiscash, Spikes can be used to hit Pokemon that resist Stealth Rock like Sandslash, Magneton, and Orthworm harder, and Whiscash can run both Stealth Rock and Spikes on the same set for role compression. Whiscash's final moveslot can be either Ice Beam or Stone Edge; Ice Beam lets it hit switch-ins like Dipplin, Whimsicott, and Alolan Exeggutor hard, which would usually resist Whiscash's STAB moves. Stone Edge can be run over Ice Beam to hit Cryogonal hard, which would shake off Ice Beam and Surf due to its excellent Special Defense. However, Whiscash would only opt for Stone Edge if it chooses to run Spikes. Heavy-Duty Boots allows it to reliably come in multiple times to set hazards and block Volt Switch from the likes of Magneton and Jolteon more often without the fear of taking entry hazard chip damage, while Leftovers provides more longevity. Whiscash can choose to run either a physically defensive EV spread or a specially defensive one; the physically defensive spread gives Whiscash a more reliable way to withstand hits from Hitmontop, Sandslash, and Sneasel, while the specially defensive one allows Whiscash to check other special attackers such as Jolteon and Typhlosion. With Tera Ghost, Whiscash can block Rapid Spin from Hitmontop, Sandslash, and Cryogonal. Tera Poison flips its Grass weakness to have an easier time dealing with Arboliva and Virizion, while still keeping a solid defensive typing.

Whiscash fits on a myriad of teams that are looking to have an entry hazard setter that has both Stealth Rock and Spikes. Whiscash appreciates a spinblocker like Spiritomb or Sableye to keep entry hazards up at all times. Setup sweepers such as Jolteon, Mesprit, and Sneasel admire Whiscash's ability to reliably dent entry hazard-weak Pokemon like Venusaur, Magneton, and Regirock for them to grasp KOs more easily. Whiscash benefits from teammates like Magneton, Cryogonal, and Muk, as they can handle Grass-types such as Whimsicott, Arboliva, and Venusaur. Whiscash also appreciates Knock Off users such as Mesprit, Skuntank, and Sableye, which complement its entry hazards by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon such as Drifblim and Sneasel, allowing them to be worn down more easily. Whiscash makes for an excellent partner for Pokemon vulnerable to Poison-types and Fire-types, such as Whimsicott, Arboliva, and Magneton.

ru.overview: The big bad crawdad of competitive Pokemon, Crawdaunt remains a relevant wallbreaker and stall dismantler several generations after its debut. Choice Band and Adaptability make switching into Crawdaunt nigh impossible, as it fires off massive Knock Offs and Crabhammers. With little regard to physical walls' existence, Crawdaunt excels in taking advantage of safe entry points provided by teammates to force concessions every time it hits the field, as switching into the combination of Dark- and Water-type attacks is difficult for even the bulkiest of walls like Umbreon and Slowbro. With access to Aqua Jet, Crawdaunt can overcome its relative slowness against offensive foes, picking up KOs and dealing big damage before it can be taken out in return. Unfortunately, Crawdaunt is still a bit slow and frail and competes for a spot against notable faster and bulkier wallbreakers like Feraligatr, Basculegion-F, and Terrakion. Along with the lack of Speed, Crawdaunt also suffers from a frailness that makes it susceptible to being taken out by the faster Pokemon in the metagame like Gardevoir, Kleavor, and Flamigo.
ru.comments:
Other Options

With a Jolly nature, Dragon Dance improves Crawdaunt's Speed enough to outpace notable threats like Kleavor and Entei after just one boost. Liquidation can be used over Crabhammer for a more accurate attack. Covert Cloak allows Crawdaunt to set up against Scald users, like Slowbro and Suicune, without fear of getting burned.

Checks and Counters

Faster Wallbreakers: Crawdaunt struggles to keep pace against offensive teams, often relying on Aqua Jet, as it can't outspeed the opposition. Faster wallbreakers like Porygon-Z, Gallade, and Gardevoir threaten to KO Crawdaunt before it can leverage its absurd offensive output for balance teams reliant on it.

Water-type Pokemon: Gastrodon, because of its ability Storm Drain prevents Crawdaunt from freely using Crabhammer to power its way through teams. Suicune does not have an immunity to Water but does prevent Crawdaunt from staying in comfortably by threatening Scald burns, while Barraskewda can use the threat of Close Combat to pivot into more favorable matchups.

Entry Hazards and Rocky Helmet: Coming in multiple times throughout a game to fire off massive attacks is Crawdaunt's specialty, which makes it susceptible to getting worn down by entry hazards. Similarly, Rocky Helmet Pokemon like Amoonguss and especially Chesnaught cause problems for Crawdaunt, racking up chip damage while making Crawdaunt far less imposing by recovering their health back.

Grass-type Pokemon: Amoonguss and Chesnaught are two defensive Grass-types that can often switch into Crawdaunt's STAB attacks and recover off most of the damage, with both threatening to KO it back with Giga Drain and Body Press, respectively. Wo-Chien similarly can take many of Crawdaunt's strongest attacks and recover HP back with Leech Seed. Breloom matches up well into Crawdaunt, using it to set up Bulk Up and threaten a sweep late-game.

Swords Dance.description:
Set Details

Swords Dance Crawdaunt functions as an unstoppable wallbreaker and setup sweeper, capable of dismantling defensive cores with ease while threatening offense with strong priority. Aqua Jet ensures an already set up Crawdaunt can fire off strong attacks before being revenge killed, preventing faster Pokemon like Flygon, Gardevoir, and Gengar from stopping a potential sweep. Adaptability-boosted Knock Off is Crawdaunt's most spammable attack, providing utility in item removal with the benefit of being incredibly difficult to switch into generally. Life Orb maximizes the breaking potential of Crawdaunt, enabling it to comfortably 2HKO nearly the entire unboosted metagame, including notable walls like Amoonguss, and Slowbro. Crawdaunt does not get much value from using Terastallization, as the interaction between Terastallization and Adaptability provides minimal gain generally, but Tera Water is still the default choice to boost damage output for Aqua Jet while also removing the weakness to Bug and Fighting.

Balance and bulky offense teams looking for a powerful wallbreaker, setup sweeper, and priority revenge killer can use Swords Dance Crawdaunt to fill all of these roles comfortably. As one of the strongest physical attackers in the metagame, Crawdaunt often is paired with strong Volt Switch users, namely Magnezone and Raikou, to form a dynamic duo that keeps the opponent from getting comfortable, as specially defensive walls like Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon get worn down quickly trying to keep pace with the pivoting. Similarly, other strong physical setup sweepers, like Mimikyu and Terrakion, can take advantage of Crawdaunt racking up massive damage on physically defensive walls like Slowbro to secure their own late-game sweep. However, Crawdaunt is often on a time crunch with regards to health, as it takes all forms of entry hazard chip damage in addition to its own Life Orb recoil and potential Rocky Helmet chip, making hazard removal teammates that can pivot Crawdaunt in safely like Cyclizar and Noivern crucial to minimize the damage it takes and provide safe entry points against common switch-ins like Hisuian Goodra, and Slowbro. Teams that utilize Crawdaunt often want to support it with their own hazards to capitalize on its strong Knock Off, making partners like Chesnaught, Jirachi, and Klefki valuable as both hazard setters and defensive pivots into Electric- and Fighting-type attacks from Pokemon like Raikou and Terrakion. Defensive teammates like Bellibolt, Empoleon, and Jirachi can provide immense value as switch-ins to revenge killers like Flamigo and Gardevoir while being able to provide safe pivots into Crawdaunt. Chesnaught and Wo-Chien are two of the few reliable Crawdaunt counters in the metagame, making teammates that can handle them like Ribombee and Gallade appreciated.

Choice Band.description:
Set Details

Choice Band Crawdaunt dishes out massive damage with every attack it uses, making it a seemingly unwallable wallbreaker. Aqua Jet functions as a STAB priority attack that allows Crawdaunt to overcome its relative slowness, picking up valuable revenge kills and chip damage on faster threats like Gengar, Maushold, and Terrakion. Close Combat gives Crawdaunt additional breaking power against Dark- and Steel-type Pokemon like Bisharp and Hisuian Goodra. Adaptability, in conjunction with Crabhammer and Knock Off, renders physical walls neutral to its STAB attacks like Amoonguss and Quagsire unable to weather the storm as Crawdaunt 2HKOes them with ease. Tera Water does not get much value offensively, as Adaptability offsets a majority of the boost provided by Terastallization, so Crawdaunt does not often Terastallize outside of the rare instances where it can improve a damage roll against a foe. Tera Water does remove Crawdaunt's weaknesses to common priority attacks like First Impression and Mach Punch, though it also eliminates the Adaptability boost for Knock Off, which is a tough concession to make.

Balance and bulky offense teams needing a reliable Knock Off user and wallbreaker appreciate Crawdaunt's ability to do both well. Teammates like Cyclizar, Jirachi, and Flamigo can pivot to Crawdaunt against incoming physical walls, such as Amoonguss, Gastrodon, and Slowbro, to provide safe opportunities to use its raw power to break holes into the opposition. Cyclizar and Noivern are exceptional teammates, as they can both pivot and remove entry hazards from the field, which Crawdaunt appreciates to retain health throughout a game. Similarly, defensive partners like Bellibolt and Magnezone can slowly pivot to Crawdaunt, providing valuable entry points against bulkier walls like Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon. Choice Scarf users like Gardevoir and Krookodile appreciate Crawdaunt's ability to break through defensive Pokemon like Quagsire, Hisuian Goodra, and Umbreon, enabling them to clean late-game. Slowbro and Jirachi provide speed control in the form of Thunder Wave, giving valuable opportunities for Crawdaunt to break through faster Pokemon like Jirachi, Terrakion, and Bisharp. Defensive teammates that can absorb Fairy- and Fighting-type attacks from revenge killers like Gardevoir and Terrakion are a necessity for Crawdaunt, making Jirachi and Noivern key teammates that can take attacks and provide safe entry points with U-turn. Hazard stacking cores, with setters like Chesnaught, Jirachi, and Klefki, can use Crawdaunt's Knock Off as a way to remove Heavy-Duty Boots while forcing switches, accruing damage quickly.

Physically Defensive.description:
Flip Turn allows Milotic to maintain momentum and safely get in offensive teammates. Ice Beam deals decent damage to Grass-types like Venusaur and Amoonguss. Alluring Voice stops Tatsugiri from switching into Milotic and also notably punishes Scrafty. Haze prevents setup sweepers like Snorlax and Grimmsnarl from getting out of hand, though it can be blocked by Taunt. Dragon Tail also stops boosting foes and synergizes well with entry hazards, though it fails against Florges and Tera Fairy users. With 8 Speed EVs, Milotic outspeeds Adamant Hariyama. Milotic's EV spread is highly flexible depending on the needs of its team. For example, Milotic can use 48 Speed EVs to get the jump on Adamant Golurk.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

Offensive Utility.description: Leveraging its respectable stat spread, Intimidate, and useful set of resistances, Salamence makes for a decent offensive presence that is able to consistently check the likes of Excadrill, Scizor, and Rillaboom. It can use these opportunities to fire off its strong attacks capable of ripping through significant portions of the defensive metagame, including the likes of Clefable, Slowbro, and Mega Venusaur. However, Salamence struggles to fit on teams in practice due to significant competition from other Pokemon capable of fulfilling similar defensive roles, notably Mega Aerodactyl, Hydrapple, Mega Latias, which possess similar defensive utility turned offensive potential. Mega Aerodactyl's much higher Speed tier also lets it outpace and revenge kill notable offensive threats such as Iron Moth, Alakazam, and Thundurus, while Hydrapple and Mega Latias's immense bulk and lack of exploitable weaknesses make them much more sturdy defensive checks to the aforementioned Pokemon. Flamethrower's better accuracy and PP make it the preferred coverage move to hit Steel-type Pokemon, notably maximizing Salamence’s effectiveness at checking Scizor and Skarmory long-term. Fire Blast is a stronger alternative that improves Salamence's odds to 2HKO Aegislash and Celesteela through Leftovers while also potentially OHKOing offensive Excadrill from full HP. Toxic is best used as a way to cripple specially defensive answers such as Tyranitar and Hippowdon long-term, opening them up for Salamence to break through them later on in the match. Alternatively, Draco Meteor provides Salamence with a stronger STAB option that applies immediate pressure to Flying-resistant Pokemon such as Mega Aerodactyl and Rotom-W, preventing them from switching into it for free. Lastly, Salamence can use Defog to provide crucial entry hazard removal for its team. 136 Speed EVs allow Salamence to outpace Adamant Rillaboom, and a Modest nature in conjunction with maximum Special Attack investment allows it to potentially 2HKO physically defensive Clefable with Hurricane. However, maximum Speed investment in conjunction with a Timid nature can be used instead if outspeeding offensive threats such as Hydreigon is necessary. Salamence fits best on offensive teams that appreciate its unique defensive profile and ability to conserve offensive momentum in return. Good examples of wallbreakers that complement Salamence include Life Orb Mienshao, Swords Dance Aegislash, and Choice Band Rillaboom; these Pokemon can easily take advantage of specially defensive checks such as Celesteela and Garganacl that Salamence tends to invite in. In return, Salamence can provide them with a soft answer to the likes of Keldeo and Victini. Salamence also heavily appreciates hazards and Knock Off support, which goes a long way in overwhelming the likes of Celesteela, specially defensive Hippowdon, and Rotom-W. Teammates such as Clefable, Scizor, and Swampert can assist in this regard; Scizor and Swampert can also U-turn and Flip Turn to bring Salamence in safely against the likes of Okidogi and Hydrapple, which are otherwise able to potentially threaten it on the switch. Clefable provides an amazing defensive answer to Knock Off users such as Life Orb Mienshao and Lokix, which are otherwise capable of wearing down Salamence in conjunction with Stealth Rock. Lastly, hazard removal options such as Defog Rotom-W and Rapid Spin Excadrill are highly valuable for their ability to alleviate Salamence's moveslot constraints while also ensuring that it can manage its HP in the face of its Stealth Rock weakness after losing Heavy-Duty Boots to Knock Off.

Dragon Dance.description:
• Mega Salamence excels as an offensive powerhouse due to its formidable Attack stat, access to Dragon Dance, and its potent ability, Aerilate, achieving multiple roles like wallbreaker, sweeper, and late-game cleaner.

  • Double-Edge is Mega Salamence's most powerful STAB move, being able to 2HKO most defensive Pokemon such as Yveltal and Ferrothorn. Return serves as a weaker but safer STAB move, although it misses out on the 2HKO on foes like Ho-Oh and offensive Primal Groudon.

  • Earthquake is Mega Salamence's best coverage move to hit Steel-types like Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM and to hit Primal Groudon almost as hard as Double-Edge without the recoil damage. At +1, it can OHKO Zacian-C and additionally OHKO Zekrom after Stealth Rock.

  • Roost provides Mega Salamence with reliable recovery and helps it find more setup opportunities throughout the battle, while Facade punishes foes that try to status it like Ho-Oh, Primal Groudon, Arceus-Water, and Arceus-Dark at the cost of making Mega Salamence more sensitive to chip damage while setting up.

  • Mega Salamence, especially when not running Roost, should aim to switch in after a foe has fainted or on a predicted Earthquake from foes like Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Arceus. By pressuring these Pokemon to switch out, it can take on the opportunity to set up and start wearing down its checks.

  • In certain scenarios, retaining access to Salamence's Intimidate can prove advantageous due to its capability to mitigate foes that threaten to set up such as Rayquaza and Necrozma-DM. Additionally, the Attack drop can let Mega Salamence avoid a 2HKO from Choice Band Marshadow's Poltergeist, offensive Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, and Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent and set up on them.

  • Having weaknesses to Fairy and Ice, Mega Salamence appreciates Fire- and Steel-type teammates such as Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Zacian-C that can threaten the likes of opposing Zacian-C, Arceus-Fairy, and Calyrex-I.

  • Fairy-type teammates like Zacian-C and Arceus-Fairy love Mega Salamence's ability to check Steel- and Fire-types such as Necrozma-DM and Primal Groudon and threaten them with Earthquake.

  • Mega Salamence works well on hyper offense teams, and suicide entry hazard leads such as Deoxys-S and Glimmora are invaluable in helping it sweep; the aforementioned Pokemon can also prevent hazards. Mega Salamence also appreciates dual screens support from Deoxys-S and Grimmsnarl to make it harder to knock out.

Mixed Attacker.description: • The given EV spread allows Mega Salamence to 2HKO Iron Hands with Double Edge while maximizing its Speed, allocating the remaining EVs into Special Attack.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
With Paradox Pokemon being introduced, Series 2 is bringing big changes to Battle Stadium Singles! This is a modified Series 1 analysis that takes Paradox Pokemon into account. We will update this overview and analysis again once the metagame settles more. For more information on Series 2, check out the resource thread.

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Specsmence Returns.description:
• Salamence finds a niche for itself among other special attacking Dragon-types due to an incredible ability in Intimidate and a useful typing that provides a handy Fissure immunity.

  • Hurricane versus Air Slash: Hurricane's accuracy may not be very reliable, but the sheer damage output makes it worth it. Air Slash is much weaker than Hurricane, but the more reliable accuracy and flinch chance make it a reasonable alternative. It becomes especially attractive if using Tera Flying.

  • Hydro Pump: If not using Tera Fairy, Hydro Pump is a reasonable choice that deals massive damage to Hippowdon and Fire-types without risking Draco Meteor.

Tera Types

  • Fairy: Not only does Tera Fairy give Salamence an edge against many Dragon-types, but it also pairs extremely well with Intimidate, transforming Salamence into an effective hit-and-run threat.

  • Steel: Tera Steel comes in handy against Dragon- and Fairy-types alike, though the added weaknesses to Ground and Fighting make it less effective at taking physical hits with Intimidate.

  • Flying: Air Slash becomes much easier to justify with Tera Flying, and if you're willing to risk it, Hurricane can be used to become almost impossible to wall with Choice Specs.

  • Fire: Tera Fire doesn't offer as much defensive utility, but the powerful STAB attacks come in handy against Steel-types like Corviknight.

  • Dragon: Tera Dragon trades defensive advantages for an extremely powerful Draco Meteor that catches defensive foes like Dondozo by surprise.

Items

  • Choice Specs: With Salamence already standing at a decent Speed tier, it can get away with Choice Specs, making it extremely difficult to wall outside of using Blissey.

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf trades wallbreaking power for the ability to get the jump on major offensive threats, such as Dragapult, Meowscarada, and Garchomp.

Physically Offensive.description:
• Salamence is somewhat overshadowed by other physical Dragon-types like Roaring Moon and Dragapult, but it has a trick up its claws: Dual Wingbeat, which OHKOes Breloom and Meowscarada through their Focus Sash.

  • Earthquake versus Fire Blast: Earthquake is the best option for hitting Steel-types such as Gholdengo hard, but Fire Blast is Salamence's best shot at 2HKOing Corviknight.

  • Dragon Dance: After a boost, Dual Wingbeat's Focus Sash slaying powers go into overdrive, being able to bust through Flutter Mane, Iron Bundle, and Great Tusk.

Tera Types

  • Flying: With a Flying Tera type, a boosted Dual Wingbeat has a 75% chance to OHKO offensive Mimikyu through its disguise! It also means Salamence no longer needs a boost to OHKO Great Tusk and Flutter Mane.

  • Electric: Tera Electric lets Tera Blast Salamence OHKO Azumarill and Iron Bundle, and potentially 2HKO Dondozo after Stealth Rock damage.

Abilities

  • Intimidate: While Salamence isn't particularly bulky, Intimidate makes setting up far easier when paired with a Flying Tera type that removes Salamence's common weaknesses.

  • Moxie: With Moxie, Salamence has the potential to seriously punish Breloom leads or snowball through teams even without Dragon Dance.

Mixed Attacker.description:
• Salamence's great mixed offenses, Intimidate, and decent Speed give it a niche as a powerful wall breaker.

  • Dual Wingbeat: Dual Wingbeat lets Salamence OHKO Breloom regardless of its Focus Sash, something very few Pokemon can do.

  • Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor deals massive damage to Dondozo, usually doing more than 50% to physically defensive ones.

  • Substitute: Substitute makes the Dondozo match-up even better, making Yawn a non-issue. It's also a good way to scout Terastallization against slower threats.

Tera Types

  • Steel: A Steel Tera type covers a lot of Salamence's weaknesses and makes dealing with Mimikyu, Iron Bundle, and Flutter Mane much easier.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy gives Salamence a great match-up against most Dragon-types, and pairs especially well with Intimidate to turn Salamence into a good hit-and-run attacker.

  • Fire: With a Fire Tera type, Salamence gains a resistance to Fairy-type attacks and deals massive damage to Assault Vest Magnezone.

  • Electric: Tera Electric gives Salamence a great tool against Dondozo with Tera Blast.

  • Dragon: While this Tera type fails to help Salamence much defensively, it makes Draco Meteor 2HKO physically defensive Dondozo.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band Metagross is a solid wallbreaker thanks to its great Attack and strong STAB and coverage moves. Its good bulk also allows it to survive strong attacks like Knock Off from Heavy-Duty Boots Lokix and Surf from Choice Specs Keldeo. Heavy Slam deals a lot of damage to neutral targets; Earthquake hits many Pokemon that resist Heavy Slam, like Cobalion, Toxapex, and Heatran. Knock Off can make good progress against Slowking, Skarmory, and Rotom-Wash. Alternatively, Thunder Punch can be used to hit Water-types like Keldeo and Slowking as well as Flying-types that resist Steel, primarily Skarmory. Bullet Punch's priority allows Metagross to swiftly KO Pokemon that outspeed it like Weavile, Alolan Ninetales, and Fezandipiti. Clear Body blocks attack drops from Intimidate Pokemon like Krookodile. Tera Steel increases the damage of Heavy Slam and Bullet Punch. Tera Steel-boosted Heavy Slam allows Metagross to consistently OHKO Pokemon like Tyranitar, specially defensive Mandibuzz, and Hydrapple, while the damage boost to Bullet Punch allows it to consistently 2HKO Pokemon like Latios, Lokix, and Galarian Zapdos.

Choice Band Metagross fits on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its wallbreaking capabilities; Water-types like Rotom-Wash are useful switch-ins to Fire-type attacks, and Metagross, in return, resists Grass-type attacks that threaten most Water-types. Fighting-types like Keldeo and Conkeldurr appreciate Metagross's ability to switch into Latios, Gardevoir, and Fezandipiti. Ground-resistant and Ground-immune Pokemon like Hydrapple and Skarmory are also useful, since Metagross is weak to Ground-type attacks and loses to most Ground-types; the latter can set up Spikes to help Metagross pick up more KOs. Metagross also benefits from pivots that can bring it in safely, like Lokix, Keldeo, and Mandibuzz. Mandibuzz can also deal with opposing Metagross and run Defog to remove entry hazards. Metagross also benefits from entry hazards, since they make it easier to KO targets like Latios and Choice Specs Hydrapple. Stealth Rock setters such as Donphan, Tyranitar, and Sandy Shocks are useful for this; Sandy Shocks can also run Volt Switch to serve as a pivot for Metagross. Setup sweepers like Weavile and Slither Wing also benefit from Metagross's wallbreaking capabilities to weaken teams and allow them to sweep late-game.

Bulky Attacker.description:
Metagross's great typing, stats, and movepool allow it to function as a solid bulky attacker, handling threats like Latios and Ogerpon-C. Heavy Slam is a reliable STAB move, taking advantage of Metagross's large weight to do solid damage to threats like Hydrapple, Mandibuzz, and Greninja. Stealth Rock also allows Metagross to function as an entry hazard setter, while Bullet Punch gives Metagross a STAB priority move to circumvent its below average Speed, hitting foes like Ogerpon-C and Mamoswine. Knock Off can be used to cripple checks like Slowking and Hydrapple by removing their items, while Earthquake can be used to hit Steel-types such as Excadrill, Heatran, and Cobalion. Leftovers is crucial for maintaining Metagross's longevity, since it doesn't get a recovery move. 96 Speed EVs allow Metagross to outspeed maximum Speed Adamant Azumarill. Tera Dark allows Metagross to turn its weaknesses to Dark and Ghost into resistances while also boosting the power of its Knock Off, while Tera Water allows it to resist Fire-type attacks from Hisuian Arcanine and Skeledirge and tank Belly Drum Azumarill's boosted Aqua Jet.

Metagross does best on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its good mix of power and bulk. Teammates like Tornadus-T, Mandibuzz, and Hydrapple all provide a Ground resistance that covers Metagross's weakness. In return, Metagross answers Ogerpon-C, which is scary for the former two and takes pressure off of Hydrapple. However, it is important to note that Tornadus-T cannot switch into Rhyperior safely, so answers to it like Slowking or the aforementioned Hydrapple are appreciated. Metagross is also weak to Fire-type moves from Pokemon like Hisuian Arcanine and Skeledirge, so Water types like Rotom-W and Slowking can help tank these attacks, both of which can use pivot moves to bring Metagross in safely. In general, Metagross benefits greatly from pivots that can bring it in safely, so U-turn users like Lokix, Ogerpon, and Scizor also make great teammates. Metagross tends to struggle with bulky Flying-types like Skarmory and Mandibuzz, so it benefits from teammates that can handle these two, such as Rhyperior and Sandy Shocks. These two Pokemon also act as alternate Stealth Rock users, which not only synergizes well with Metagross's Knock Off but also allows it to run Bullet Punch. The latter can also act as a spiker to form a hazard-stacking core with Metagross.

Suicide Lead.description:
Explosion Metagross is an offensive Pokemon with some defensive utility and a simple gameplan: set Stealth Rock then use Explosion. Explosion does a lot of damage to the tier's defensive Pokemon like Hydrapple and Slowking. Earthquake lets it hit the Steel-types that resist its Explosion and Heavy Slam, like Heatran and Excadrill. Stealth Rock gives it excellent utility, setting entry hazards while the foe switches out. Bullet Punch is useful when running an alternative hazard setter, as it can clean up foes at low HP. Metagross can utilize its fantastic typing to defensively check Pokemon like Latios and Hydrapple. Custap Berry alleviates how low Metagross may get in the process by gaining priority on Explosion. Normal Gem can allow it to KO some important targets, such as maximum Defense Hydrapple after Tera Normal. The given Speed investment allows Metagross to outspeed Mandibuzz and Azumarill but 196 Speed EVs can allow it to outspeed targets like Tinkaton and Choice Band Tyranitar; however, doing so would sacrifice some of the bulk that lets it check Ogerpon-C and Latios. Tera Normal lets Metagross power up its Explosion, letting it potentially OHKO Slowking and Hydrapple with chip, but beware that most of its defensive utility comes from its typing, so only use Tera if Metagross needs Tera Normal to KO the foe.

Metagross fits best on offensive structures, as it lures in Skarmory and Hydrapple and weakens them for the rest of the team to exploit. Excadrill is an amazing partner, especially considering how much it threatens Skeledirge and Rotom-W, Pokemon that Metagross hates. Thundurus and Sandy Shocks also are good partners, as they enjoy Metagross's ability to switch into Latios and weaken Hydrapple. Sandy Shocks can also act as an alternate Stealth Rock setter. Metagross also enjoys Sticky Web support from Araquanid, allowing it to outspeed Pokemon like Tyranitar and Tinkaton while keeping its bulk as well as offensive checks like non-Heavy-Duty Boots Mamoswine. Ghost-type Pokemon like Sinistcha and Pecharunt can cause problems, as they block Metagross's Explosion attempts while threatening it with Shadow Ball, so it appreciates offensive Dark-types like Tyranitar and Lokix.

Weakness Policy.description:
• Heavy Slam is for Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Whimsicott as well as light Pokemon such as Meowscarada and Porygon-Z.
  • Meteor Mash can be used for consistent damage, being particularly useful against heavy Rock- and Ice-type Pokemon
  • Bullet Punch is useful for securing KOs on faster Pokemon, Encore + Disable Pokemon such as Iron Valiant and Alolan Ninetales, and pinch Berry users such as Sneasler.
  • Earthquake is for Hisuian Goodra and Metagross mirror matchups.
  • Psychic Fangs is for Pecharunt and some Urshifu-R sets. It also helps break Reflect from Pokemon like Primarina and Kyurem.
  • Hone Claws allows Metagross to set up against Counter users like Hisuian Goodra, which cannot be OHKOed by Metagross's Earthquake, allowing it to OHKO Hisuian Goodra with +1 Earthquake.
  • The bulk EVs let Metagross survive Modest Choice Specs Kyurem's Earth Power and Adamant Choice Band Haxorus's Earthquake. The rest of the EVs are put into Attack.
  • If Metagross is not running Hone Claws to set up Attack against Counter Hisuian Goodra, it can chip away at Hisuian Goodra's HP with Bullet Punch, since Counter won't do much, then it can KO Hisuian Goodra when it's in Earthquake's KO range.
  • Since Metagross is weak to Fire-, Dark-, and Ground-type moves, a Water- or Fairy-type Pokemon like Manaphy or Primarina makes a good teammate.

Assault Vest.description:
• Heavy Slam is for Primarina, Iron Valiant, and Sylveon.
