  • Bullet Punch lets Metagross deal with Encore + Disable Iron Valiant and KO Haxorus and Custap or Sitrus Berry Primarina after Heavy Slam.
  • Earthquake beats Iron Crown and is the best option Raging Bolt.
  • Psychic Fangs gives Metagross a better matchup against Pecharunt and Reflect Primarina, while Ice Punch gives Metagross the best odds against Assault Vest Landorus-T, and Life Orb Landorus.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Metagross to survive Knock Off from Jolly Choice Band Meowscarada. The Special Defense EVs allow Metagross to take 2 Thunderbolts from Booster Energy Raging Bolt. The remaining EVs are put into Attack to maximize odds against Choice Band Earthquake Haxorus.

Air Balloon.description:
• Air Balloon + Iron Defense + Body Press allows Metagross to lure in physical Ground-types like Ursaluna and Donphan to gain a surprise win.
  • Heavy Slam + Bullet Punch allows Metagross to maintain good matchups against all common Fairy-types. Having two Steel-type moves secures the matchup against Fairy-type Encore + Disable users like Iron Valiant, Alolan Ninetales, and the rare Gardevoir. Meteor Mash lets Metagross defeat Kyurem at the cost of losing to Primarina and lower accuracy.
  • This EV spread allows Metagross to always survive a Knock Off from Adamant Choice Band Meowscarada or a Focus Blast from Timid Choice Specs Valiant. The Speed EVs enable Metagross to always outspeed base 50 speed Pokemon without a Speed-boosting nature, such as Ursaluna, Iron Hands, and Donphan.
  • Do not use Iron Defense against strong Dark-types like Meowscarada and Chien-Pao. Body Press followed by Bullet Punch KOes Meowscarada and Chien-Pao, although Chien-Pao's Throat Chop can sometimes OHKO Metagross.
  • Against Ursaluna, use Iron Defense twice, and then OHKO it with Body Press to play around Counter.
  • To make an effective team with Metagross, be sure you are covering Fire-types like Volcanion and Volcarona, Ghost-types like Spectrier, Dragapult, and Pecharunt, strong Dark-types like Urshifu-S, Galarian Moltres, and Hoopa-U, and miscellaneous strong special attackers like Raging Bolt and Zapdos. Some examples of partners that could cover some of these weaknesses include Ursaluna, Walking Wake, and Galarian Moltres.

Choice Band.description:
• Heavy Slam is used to defeat non-Custap Berry Primarina, while Meteor Mash allows Metagross to beat Kyurem. Both moves do well into Sylveon, Porygon-Z, and Azumarill.
  • Psychic Fangs is for Pecharunt and Iron Hands.
  • Bullet Punch targets Iron Valiant and Alolan Ninetales.
  • Earthquake hits Iron Crown, Hisuian Goodra, Registeel, and has favorable odds to beat most Raging Bolt sets.
  • The HP investment allows Metagross to survive Earthquake from Choice Band Iron Hands, while the Special Defense EVs allow it to survive Dark Pulse from Choice Specs Porygon-Z. The Attack EVs and an Adamant nature allow it to beat Encore + Disable Iron Valiant due to Struggle 2HKOing after a Bullet Punch.
  • An alternative EV spread of 232 HP / 236 Atk / 40 Def can be used to survive Focus Blast from Timid Choice Specs Iron Valiant and Earthquake from Choice Band Haxorus. The remaining EVs are put in Attack for maximum damage output.
  • Choice Band Metagross should almost always use the move that does the most damage to an opposing Pokemon. Notable exceptions to this rule are Alolan Ninetales and Iron Valiant, as Bullet Punch allows Metagross to beat Encore + Disable variants of these Pokemon.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Metagross trades winning matchups against foes like Choice Band Meowscarada and Encore + Disable Iron Valiant to have better matchups against both relatively faster Pokemon, like Garchomp and Iron Moth, and stall Pokemon, like Registeel and Cresselia.
  • Metagross should use Heavy Slam against Sylveon, Alolan Ninetales, Diancie, and Espathra.
  • Earthquake is especially strong on Metagross and is used to beat Iron Crown, Pecharunt, Iron Moth, and non-Liechi Berry Sneasler.
  • Trick allows Metagross deal with Registeel, Pecharunt, and Cresselia.
  • Ice Punch lets Metagross defeat Garchomp, Landorus, and non-Choice Scarf Landorus-T. Hammer Arm allows Metagross to defeat Porygon-Z and gives it the best matchup against Body Press Corviknight after using Trick.
  • The HP and Special Defense EVs allow Metagross to survive Tachyon Cutter from Weakness Policy Iron Crown four times, which lets Metagross use Trick before repeatedly using Earthquake to defeat it. It should be noted, however, that if Iron Crown's Booster Energy activates, Metagross should opt not to use Trick and use Earthquake repeatedly instead. The Speed EVs allow Metagross to outrun Iron Moth. The remaining EVs are in Attack to bolster its damage output.
  • Choice Scarf Metagross struggles against Water-types, such Manaphy, Volcanion, and some Primarina sets. It also struggles against certain Dragon-types, such as Choice Band Haxorus with Earthquake, Dragapult, and Raging Bolt. Choice Scarf Metagross, like other Metagross sets, also struggles against both Ursaluna formes and Dark-types like Hoopa-U, Zarude, and Chien-Pao. However, it also loses to Encore + Disable Iron Valiant, which no other Metagross set struggles with. To counteract these weaknesses, Fairy-type Pokemon like Sylveon can be good teammates, as they beats many of the Dark- and Dragon-types that Metagross struggles with. Choice Band Meowscarada is another good option, as it can beat many Water-types with Flower Trick while also beating many Dragon- and Grass-types that Metagross detests facing.

Stealth Rock (Psychic).description:
By virtue of its great bulk and defensive typing, Metagross makes for great entry hazard support for Psychic teams, dealing well with common hazard controllers like Hatterene and Tentacruel. Psychic Fangs threatens the aforementioned Tentacruel as well as other Poison- and Fighting-types such as Sneasler and Okidogi; it also eases the Fairy and Ice matchups due to breaking dual screens. Knock Off threatens Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Gholdengo, Brambleghast, and Indeedee while also removing items from foes that are reliant on them like Heavy-Duty Boots from Dragonite and Leftovers from Corviknight. Bullet Punch can be run over Psychic Fangs or Knock Off to revenge kill faster threats such as Iron Valiant, Flutter Mane, and Weavile. However, most of Metagross's teammates provide great speed control, and running a second Steel-type STAB move on Metagross restricts its number of potential targets. Heavy Slam threatens Fairy- and Ice-types such as Hatterene, Alolan Ninetales, and Articuno. 96 Speed EVs allow Metagross to outspeed Adamant Azumarill.

Wallbreakers such as Choice Band Hoopa-U and Choice Specs Latios appreciate Metagross setting entry hazards to help them wallbreak. Hoopa-U also takes on Dark-, Ghost-, and Steel-types such as specially defensive Ting-Lu, Gholdengo, Heatran, and Hisuian Goodra, while Latios provides a Ground immunity and handles Steel- and Ground-types like Archaludon, Corviknight, Gliscor, and Great Tusk. Deoxys-S forms a hazard-stacking core with Metagross thanks to Spikes, appreciating it running Stealth Rock so it can run another utility option such as Taunt. Hatterene is a potential wincon for Psychic teams that appreciates entry hazards wearing down incoming foes such as Choice Band Dragonite and Choice Scarf Enamorus, and it is a useful asset in the Dark and Dragon matchups to deal with threats such as Sableye, Hydreigon, Garchomp, and Raging Bolt. Additionally, Hatterene provides hazard control thanks to Magic Bounce. Choice Scarf Latias appreciates Metagross taking out Fairy-types like Hatterene and Iron Valiant, and in return, it provides a Ground immunity to switch into and deal with Great Tusk and Landorus, as well as Choice-locking walls like Ting-Lu and Corviknight by giving them its Choice Scarf with Trick. Lastly, late-game sweepers such as Agility Iron Crown, Agility Gallade, and Choice Scarf Iron Boulder appreciate Metagross setting entry hazards, weakening walls with Knock Off, and revenge killing boosted sweepers with Bullet Punch to start a sweep of their own. Additionally, Iron Boulder threatens the likes of Ogerpon-H, Hisuian Arcanine, Volcarona, and Meowscarada.

Choice Band (Psychic).description:
With a Choice Band, Metagross becomes a devastating wallbreaker for Psychic teams thanks to its incredible Attack stat, immunity to Intimidate, and incredible priority move. Heavy Slam makes full use of Metagross's immense weight to deal with threats like Azumarill. Alternatively, Meteor Mash allows Metagross to OKHO heavier targets like Kyurem and Tyranitar along with getting a possible Attack boost at the cost of some accuracy. Bullet Punch provides a solid form of priority to deal with faster targets such as Flutter Mane, Alolan Ninetales, Weavile, and weakened Hoopa-U. Knock Off allows Metagross to force progress against targets that can otherwise handle it like Skarmory and Corviknight by removing crucial held items; it also threatens Ghost-types such as Air Balloon Gholdengo and Sinistcha. Finally, Earthquake hits Steel- and Electric-type threats like Hisuian Goodra, Magnezone, and Raging Bolt. The EV Spread used allows Metagross to outspeed Adamant Azumarill while surviving hits such as Modest +1 Raging Bolt's Thunderbolt.

Choice Specs Latios, when paired with Metagross, forms a devastating wallbreaker core; Latios cleanly removes physical walls such as Skarmory, Corviknight, and Hippowdon, while Metagross can remove threats Latios struggles against such as Hisuian Goodra, Blissey, and Flutter Mane. Deoxys-S provides solid entry hazard stacking capabilities, further increasing Metagross's wallbreaking capabilities. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder provides a solid form of speed control along with dealing with Fire-type threats such as Iron Moth, Volcarona, and Ogerpon-H. Assault Vest Hoopa-U can deal with problematic Ghost-types that handle Metagross like Gholdengo and Hisuian Zoroark with ease. Slowbro supports Metagross by dealing with Fire- and Ground-types like Cinderace, Great Tusk, and Mamoswine along with providing Thunder Wave support, allowing Metagross to outspeed threats such as Heatran and Cinderace. Choice Scarf Latias can support Metagross by dealing with threats such as non-Choice Scarf Roaring Moon and non-Choice Scarf Dragapult and provides Healing Wish support to heal Metagross. Hatterene provides utility in Magic Bounce to prevent entry hazards along with dealing with Dark-type threats such as Sableye, Mandibuzz, and Roaring Moon, which otherwise threaten Metagross. Armarouge deals with Steel-type threats such as Scizor, Archaludon, and Skarmory that handle Metagross.

vgc2024.overview:
• Metagross serves as a good defensive Pokemon on balance teams thanks to its great defenses that are bolstered even further by Assault Vest, its good ability, and its nice defensive typing against foes like Raging Bolt and Iron Crown. Its access to coverage and high Attack stat make it appreciated as an offensive threat too.

  • Metagross can pair well with offensive Pokemon like Flutter Mane and Landorus, which can help deal with the Dark-, Ghost-, and Fire-types that threaten it like Urshifu-S, Gholdengo, and Entei. Another excellent partner can be Ogerpon-W, which has great synergy with Metagross, being able to deal with Ground-types like Landorus and redirect Sucker Punch from Chien-Pao, while Metagross can help Ogerpon-W against Rillaboom and Raging Bolt.

  • Before Terastallizing, Metagross can be overwhelmed by Pokemon like Kingambit, Chi-Yu, and Entei, making defensive partners like Amoonguss and Incineroar appreciated. Rillaboom can also be a good teammate for Metagross, providing it with passive recovery and utility via Grassy Terrain and Fake Out, respectively.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Stomping Tantrum lets Metagross hit Fire- and Steel-types likeIncineroar, Entei, and Kingambit and can also help against targets like Raging Bolt. Stomping Tantrum in particular is important to hit Steel-types like Iron Crown, as they wall Metagross's STAB moves.

  • Bullet Punch can be used to help pick off weakened foes like Flutter Mane.

  • With an Assault Vest, Metagross can almost always survive Earth Power from Landorus

  • With the given EV spread, Metagross almost always survives Icicle Crash from Adamant Chien-Pao when using Tera Dragon, and it is only 3HKOed by -1 Adamant Chien-Pao's Sacred Sword when using Tera Steel. The Speed EVs let it outspeed -1 Adamant Landorus-T, as well as Roaring Moon and Adamant Chien-Pao when in Tailwind.

  • Tera Dragon lets Metagross handle Fire-types like Chi-Yu and Entei in a pinch, and it can also be useful to deal with Water-types like Ogerpon-W and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. Tera Steel helps remove its weakness against Pokemon like Kingambit, Flutter Mane, and Chien-Pao, and it can also give Bullet Punch a chance to OHKO offensive Flutter Mane.

Bulky Offense.description:
• Good bulk, priority, and Clear Body stopping common Attack debuffers like Flutter Mane and Dragonite from easily setting up gives Metagross a niche over Scizor, despite the irritating weakness to Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

  • Psychic Fangs: Despite the iffy coverage, Psychic Fangs is a great STAB attack for having a high chance of OHKOing offensive Urshifu-R and nullifying Aurora Veil from the troublesome Alolan Ninetales.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake provides fantastic coverage against most Steel-types like Gholdengo and Archaludon, although it misses out on Corviknight and Tera Steel Latias.

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch chills Landorus-T, Dragonite, and Garchomp to the bone, all of which are common Metagross checks otherwise.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off gives Metagross some useful utility, particularly against Porygon2's Eviolite and Assault Vest holders that may switch in like Ursaluna-B. It's also good coverage against Gholdengo.

  • EV Spread: This spread survives Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquake and Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

Other Options

  • Alternate Steel-type STAB Moves: Hard Press can be used to OHKO Flutter Mane, but the poor coverage can make it difficult to justify. Meteor Mash doesn't even have to worry about the target being at full HP, and the Attack boost can be dangerous, but the accuracy is an issue.

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot smacks Ursaluna-B and Dondozo for far more damage than Metagross's physical attacks do, although it's a difficult move to fit in.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Despite Metagross's typing being decent in a vacuum, the Ghost and Dark weaknesses are a big enough problem to often justify Terastallization.

  • Water: Tera Water stops Tera Water Urshifu-R from breaking through Metagross, and it even helps against Choice Specs Chi-Yu if it's locked into a Fire-type attack. It also cushions Metagross from Ogerpon-H's Ivy Cudgel, although Horn Leech will now easily 2HKO.

  • Ground: Tera Ground gets rid of Metagross's troublesome Dark, Ghost, and Ground weaknesses and powers up Earthquake enough to put offensive Archaludon into the KO range of Bullet Punch. Thanks to Metagross's original typing, it can also shock Raging Bolt's attempts to revenge kill.

  • Steel: Buffing up Bullet Punch is helpful for cleaning up weakened teams, with most offensive Flutter Mane in particular now being OHKOed by it. While it doesn't OHKO Chien-Pao, removing the Dark weakness means any that lack an offensive item will fail to 2HKO Tera Steel Metagross with Sucker Punch.

  • Dark: Tera Dark works nicely with Knock Off, OHKOing offensive Gholdengo and giving Metagross important resistances to Ghost and Dark.

Items

  • Assault Vest: Assault Vest is Metagross's best tool for tanking hits, ensuring foes like Flutter Mane and Raging Bolt won't easily cleave through it.

  • Weakness Policy: Weakness Policy is a high-risk, high-reward approach to Metagross, taking advantage of its great physical bulk to turn the tables on common physical attackers and sweep late-game with Bullet Punch, like against Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch and Landorus-T's Earthquake.

Utility.description: 180 Speed EVs let Metagross outspeed Adamant Tyranitar.

zu.comments:
Other Options

On paper, Sturdy gives a healthy Regirock a guaranteed turn to set up Stealth Rock, but between Regirock being so bulky and entry hazards being ubiquitous, it's unlikely that Regirock would be at risk of being OHKOed from full HP outside of uncommonly strong hits like Clawitzer's Water Pulse or Alolan Exeggutor's Leaf Storm. Regirock is totally dependent on the passive recovery from Leftovers to be a reliable wall, so even items like Heavy-Duty Boots and Rocky Helmet are suboptimal. Stone Edge is generally stronger than Rock Blast but has unreliable accuracy and poor PP, and it and Rock Slide cannot break past Substitute Pokemon. Curse can be used as a setup move over Iron Defense to power up Regirock's Rock Blast, but the extra Defense from Iron Defense is more useful to stonewall physical attackers, and Regirock's Body Press is more powerful and reliable than its STAB move anyway. Protect can enhance Regirock's recovery from Leftovers and allow Regirock to scout common Choice item attackers like Jolteon and Whimsicott, but it makes Regirock much more passive. Tera Ghost lets Regirock become immune to Fighting-type moves from major offensive threats like Virizion and Primeape while enabling it to block Rapid Spin from Sandslash and Toedscruel. Tera Grass helps Regirock manage its common Grass, Water, and Ground weaknesses, whereas Tera Water lets Regirock better handle Beartic, and Tera Steel shares Tera Poison's poison immunity and Grass resistance while giving Regirock an easier time against Mesprit and Farigiraf. Regirock can run a Careful nature to patch up its relatively lower special bulk, but Regirock is often tasked with taking on physical attackers, and more Defense investment benefits its IronPress combination.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Sandaconda has great longevity, while Sandslash and Toedscruel can remove Regirock's entry hazards with Rapid Spin, but all three must be wary of Regirock boosting too much with Iron Defense.

Special Attackers: Regirock's lower special bulk leaves it prone to being overwhelmed by special attackers like Mesprit, Jolteon, and Rotom. Magneton can hit Regirock super effectively with its STAB Flash Cannon. However, most special attackers are physically frail, and Magneton takes a lot of damage from Regirock's Body Press. Many special attackers also cannot KO Regirock without significant chip or several boosts.

Fighting-types: Regirock's Fighting weakness can lead it to fall victim to Fighting-types like Primeape and Virizion. Hitmontop and Hitmonchan can both remove Regirock's Stealth Rock. However, Regirock can turn the tables on physically offensive Fighting-types with its IronPress combination and Terastallization.

Grass-types: Whimsicott, Alolan Exeggutor, and Sceptile can blow through Regirock with their strong super effective STAB moves, and Whimsicott is distinguished for avoiding a 2HKO from Regirock's Body Press after Stealth Rock. Alolan Exeggutor annihilates Regirock, while Dipplin can phaze Regirock with Dragon Tail and use Recover to wall it back.

Water-types: Poliwrath can use non-IronPress Regirock as setup fodder. Clawitzer can OHKO Regirock with Water Pulse but cannot switch into Regirock's Body Press more than once with Stealth Rock up. Veluza resists Body Press and can break through Regirock's Defense boosts with Aqua Cutter.

Knock Off, Trick, and Switcheroo: Regirock relies on its Leftovers for recovery, so Knock Off users like Sneasel and Mesprit are disruptive to Regirock. Mespirit and Hisuian Sneasel can use Trick and Switcheroo to disrupt Regirock by giving it their Choice items.

Residual damage: Burns and poison neutralize Regirock's already limited passive recovery. Burns from Will-O-Wisp users like Weezing and Rotom halve Regirock's damage output, while Toxic from Muk and Toedscruel puts Regirock on a timer. Entry hazards like Stealth Rock and Spikes cause Regirock to struggle to stay healthy.

Taunt and Encore: Encore users like Whimsicott and Mesprit can lock Regirock into a move to exploit it though neither enjoy taking Body Press. Froslass and Primeape can use Taunt to stop Regirock from setting up Stealth Rock or Iron Defense. Sableye can run Taunt or Encore and does not fear Regirock's Body Press.

Physical Wall.description:
Thanks to its titanic Defense, Regirock can stonewall popular physical attackers like Sneasel and use them as an opportunity to set up Stealth Rock. Rock Blast deals reliable damage to Typhlosion and Charizard and breaks Substitute on users like Minior and Jolteon. Body Press crushes Ice-types like Beartic and Sneasel, and Steel-types like Orthworm and Magneton. Iron Defense boosts Regirock's physical bulk and powers up Body Press, turning Regirock into a bulky setup sweeper capable of suffocating physical attackers like Hitmontop and overwhelming walls like Sandaconda. Thunder Wave slows down setup sweepers like Hisuian Sneasel and fast Pokemon like Whimsicott but makes Regirock more passive. Clear Body helpfully denies stat debuffs from Intimidate, Shadow Ball, and Triple Arrows. 16 Defense EVs and an Impish nature is a useful jump point to balance Regirock's bulk. Tera Poison helps with Regirock's Grass and Fighting weaknesses and gives it an immunity to poison.

Regirock fits best on teams looking for a physically defensive backbone that can set up Stealth Rock. While Regirock has great physical bulk, its typing and comparatively lesser special bulk leave it more prone to strong special attacks. Specially defensive partners like Muk and Articuno complement Regirock's physical bulk and can intercept special attackers like Clawitzer, Whimsicott, and Mesprit. Sandslash and Hitmontop can form entry hazard cores with Regirock and help keep it from taking entry hazard chip damage. Other Grass-type partners like Alolan Exeggutor, Dipplin, and Virizion are also appreciated by Regirock, as they can cover its Ground, Grass, and Water weaknesses by taking on Sandslash, opposing Dipplin, and Clawitzer, while Regirock can take on threatening Flying-types like Minior and Articuno.

vgc2024.overview:
• With an extremely high Defense stat and access to the coveted IronPress combination, Registeel serves the role of the format's late-game sweeper. Steel is an incredibly good typing defensively, and Clear Body stops Intimidate from the likes of Incineroar, which could otherwise prevent the OHKO on Flutter Mane with Heavy Slam.

  • Registeel fits best on balance teams that feature its favorite partners. Incineroar and Amoonguss can slow down the pace of the game, Latias provides crucial speed control in Tailwind, and Rillaboom's Grassy Surge and Fake Out is appreciated by Registeel. Additionally, Latias and Rillaboom threaten Urshifu-R. Similarly, Raging Bolt is also a good Registeel partner, being the premier Urshifu-R counter in the format.

  • Notable good matchups for Registeel include Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W, both of which get cleanly 2HKOed by Body Press after a single Iron Defense boost. Kingambit also does poorly against Registeel, as Swords Dance can be mitigated by Iron Defense and Body Press hits Kingambit very hard if it does not Terastallize.

  • However, not all physical attackers are helpless against the IronPress Registeel. Both Urshifu formes can pose a threat, depending on Registeel's choice of Tera type. Chien-Pao can threaten heavy damage with Sacred Sword if Registeel has not used Terastallization. Gholdengo is also a hard counter to Registeel, as it is immune to Body Press and resists Heavy Slam while also being able to set up with Nasty Plot and break through Registeel's high bulk.

IronPress.description:
• Heavy Slam allows Registeel to hit opposing Ghost-types like Flutter Mane. 52 Attack EVs allow Heavy Slam to OHKO bulky Flutter Mane.

  • Leftovers keeps it healthy throughout the game, with Protect providing additional turns of recovery.

  • Tera Water is the standard Tera Type for Registeel, allowing it to resist Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and being a generally good defensive typing. However, with the rise of Urshifu-S, Tera Fairy is a viable option to resist Wicked Blow and Fighting-type moves while also being neutral into the majority of the metagame. Be careful using this, however as Teratallized Urshifu-R threatens a 2HKO with Surging Strikes, and Landorus can easily pin you with Earth Power and Sludge Bomb.

  • The Special Defense investment allows Registeel to almost always survive Timid Earth Power from Landorus. The rest of the Defense EVs along with an Impish nature maximize its damage output.

ru.overview: Registeel is an excellent mixed wall and Stealth Rock setter, capable of standing firm in the face of many attackers throughout the game and keeping up entry hazards. IronPress allows Registeel to turn into an offensive threat while walling any physical attacker, letting it set up against a myriad of foes like Mimikyu and Bisharp, while Thunder Wave can cripple Pokemon like Noivern and Basculegion-F. Registeel's typing allows it to check the Fairy-, Poison-, and Dragon-types in the tier like Gardevoir, Gengar, and Cyclizar with ease, while its incredible bulk allows it to take neutral attacks from Empoleon and Gengar. However, Registeel lacks reliable recovery, relying on the meager healing of Leftovers, which means that it can be chipped down across the game by hazards and is vulnerable to item removal like Knock Off. Pokemon that defeat Registeel, like Terrakion, Entei, and Suicune, are all very common in the metagame. Registeel also poses very little threat to the Ghost- and Psychic-type Pokemon that shrug off Body Press, like Basculegion-F and Slowbro, granting them easy entry points. In addition, Registeel's ability to keep Stealth Rock up is hindered by its matchup against common hazard removers, as it does not want to switch into Cyclizar's Knock Off or Noivern's Flamethrower.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Registeel can use a combination of Fling and Toxic Orb to poison a Pokemon such as Gastrodon or Slowbro, providing a single-use offensive option that is not expected in its arsenal. Curse is an alternative setup option that slows the Defense boosts in exchange for boosting the damage of Heavy Slam, but it is recommended to use a different Tera type alongside it. Tera Poison grants Registeel a resistance to Fighting while maintaining its Fairy resististance and poison immunity. Tera Fairy also grants a Fighting resistance in addition to a Dark resistance. Thunderbolt can be used to hit common checks like Basculegion-F and Slowbro. Protect can be used to improve the effectiveness of Leftovers and to scout for moves from Choice-locked Flamigo and Krookodile. ChestoRest can provide emergency healing and remove negative status effects.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Pokemon like Terrakion, Breloom, and Chesnaught threaten significant damage on Registeel if it has no Defense boosts. Gallade in particular is incredibly threatening to Registeel as not only does it resist Body Press, but Sacred Sword can ignore any Defense boosts Registeel has attained.

Fire-types: Fire-types like Ninetales, Entei, and Scovillain can deal super effective damage to Registeel and/or burn it, neutering its Leftovers and damage.

Ghost-types: Basculegion-F and Gengar are immune to Body Press, forcing Registeel to hit with its unboosted attack. Tera Ghost is also a common Tera type for physical walls like Chesnaught, Gastrodon, and opposing Registeel.

Knock Off: Knock Off users like Krookodile, Cyclizar, and Hisuian Goodra are capable of removing Registeel's Leftovers, harming its longevity.

Disruption: If Registeel has its moves disrupted through the use of moves like Encore, Taunt, and Trick, it is severely hindered and forced to switch out.

Stealth Rock.description:
Set Details

Body Press takes advantage of Registeel's high Defense and can hit Pokemon like Bisharp and Cyclizar. Iron Defense improves Registeel's survivability and turns it into an offensive threat thanks to Body Press. Thunder Wave can paralyze Cyclizar and Noivern for Registeel's allies to deal with them better. Leftovers is necessary due to Registeel's natural lack of recovery. Clear Body prevents stat drops from attacks like Liquidation, Crunch, and Shadow Ball. 180 Defense EVs allow Registeel to survive two Earthquakes from Krookodile most of the time while guaranteeing Registeel can OHKO Umbreon with a +2 Body Press after Stealth Rock damage. Tera Ghost provides Registeel with an immunity to Fighting to beat Pokemon like Gallade and Terrakion and to block Cyclizar's Rapid Spin. This also allows Registeel to set up against Pokemon with Ground-type attacks like Gastrodon and Earthquake Gyarados.

Registeel is a great fit on both bulky offense and balance teams. Because Registeel wants to enter the field often, it is particularly susceptible to Spikes, so entry hazard removers like Noivern, Cyclizar—which Basculegion-F struggles against—and Defog Noivern—which checks Fighting-types like Breloom and Chesnaught—make valuable teammates. Due to Registeel's reliance on its Leftovers, a Knock Off absorber is a necessity, a role that Pokemon like Chesnaught, Gastrodon, and RestTalk Wo-Chien are able to perform. Registeel's lack of natural recovery makes Wish a useful option, which can be used by Umbreon and Vaporeon. As Ghost- and Psychic-types like Basculegion-F and Slowbro are able to stand against Registeel's Body Press, it is useful to have allies that can hit them like Gengar, Krookodile, and Mimikyu. Setup sweepers like Slowbro, Reuniclus, and Cresselia can take advantage of Registeel's struggle to touch them, so allies that can disrupt them like Trick Gardevoir and Gengar and Encore Maushold are useful.

Stall.description:
• Registeel is one of the bulkiest Pokemon in the entire metagame. With its pure Steel typing, sky-high defenses, and access to Amnesia, Iron Defense, and Rest, it's easily able to stall a huge chunk of the metagame, including Alolan Ninetales, Primarina, Iron Crown, and non-Trick Metagross.
  • Body Press with Iron Defense is Registeel's best attacking move, allowing it to break through Pokemon such as Calm Mind Cresselia and Iron Defense Iron Crown.
  • Leftovers is used for general healing against the majority of the metagame, especially helping against Encore Primarina and Encore + Disable Iron Valiant.
  • Air Balloon helps tremendously against Ground-type Pokemon such as both Ursaluna formes and Garchomp.
  • It's important to note that Registeel is crippled by its weakness to Fire- and Fighting-type attacks from the likes of Volcarona and both Urshifu formes, so Pokemon like Primarina and Volcanion make for good partners.
  • Registeel is also weak to a lot of common status moves such as Taunt from Raging Bolt and Corviknight, Encore from Ogerpon-W, and Curse from Pecharunt. Finding a Pokemon that can deal with these, such as Raging Bolt, Passho Berry Volcarona, or Choice Scarf Hisuian Arcanine, is crucial for Registeel to fit on a team.

Calm Mind.description:
Thanks to its considerable bulk and more than reasonable attacking capabilities, Calm Mind Latias is a solid setup sweeper that can easily snowball out of control with its STAB Stored Power. Aura Sphere is the preferred coverage move for its most immediate way to deal with Dark- and Steel-type foes, most notably Kingambit but also Ting-Lu, Hisuian Samurott, Iron Treads, and Heatran, but Draining Kiss alongside Tera Fairy is a decent alternative that provides it with crucial longevity while still threatening most of the aforementioned Dark-types. Recover gives it multiple setup opportunities, but Agility is also an option to outspeed most of the metagame, particularly potential revenge killers like Darkrai and Dragapult. Weakness Policy grants it an immediate way to boost its Stored Power in a single turn, taking advantage of common attacks like U-turn and Knock Off to let it snowball more easily, especially with dual screens support to soften the blow of most super effective hits. Kee Berry is an option to let it set up on physical attackers more comfortably, such as Great Tusk and Ogerpon-W, while boosting its Stored Power. Similarly, it can run Grassy Seed instead if used on Grassy Terrain teams with Rillaboom. Leftovers is a fine alternative that gives it longevity and thus more opportunities to set up, especially if it forgoes Draining Kiss or Recover. Mental Herb is a niche option that allows Latias to bypass Taunt and Encore from Landorus-T, Iron Valiant, and Ogerpon-W. Tera Poison is the way to go to avoid Toxic damage, turning opposing Gliscor into setup fodder, while maintaing its Fighting resistance against Zamazenta and Great Tusk. Tera Steel similarly allows Latias to bypass Toxic while adding some valuable immunities and resistances, negating efforts from Galarian Slowking and Primarina to stop it. Both Tera types are also complemented by Levitate to remove the newfound Ground weakness, letting Latias comfortably check foes like Enamorus and, for Tera Steel in particular, Kyurem and non-Fire Punch Dragonite. Tera Fairy shuld only be used with Draining Kiss to boost its damage while obtaining a valuable Dragon immunity and Dark resistance in the face of foes like Dragapult, Raging Bolt, Hisuian Samurott, and non-Heavy Slam Zamazenta. Agility variants can afford more bulk instead, just running 24 Speed EVs to outrun Choice Scarf Darkrai after an Agility boost; this also lets it avoid the OHKO from Choice Band Rillaboom's Knock Off and 2HKO from Great Tusk's Ice Spinner and Zamazenta's Crunch.

Latias finds itself a niche pick in hyper offense teams; in particular, it can support teams by dealing with Unaware foes like Dondozo and Clodsire as a way to open through and act as a win condition. Latias's base typing makes it vulnerable to several metagame threats such as Gholdengo and Dragapult. Gholdengo can overwhelm it by either outdamaging it with a Nasty Plot-boosted Shadow Ball or crippling it with paralysis, sustaining its not very effective hits with Recover, and attacking back with Hex, while Dragapult outspeeds it before an Agility boost and threatens it with STAB moves or status. Kingambit makes for a great partner overall, checking Dragapult and Gholdengo along with other Ghost- and Dark-type foes that Latias may be stopped by. Opposing Kingambit poses an existential threat to Latias, as without Aura Sphere, it fails to do much in return, and without spending your Tera on Latias, it leaves itself exposed to Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave and even Iron Head if it goes Tera Fairy. Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Iron Valiant can prove decisive in this matchup, as well as mixing well with the fast-paced plan a Latias team should have. Furthermore, breaking through Ting-Lu can prove to be challenging, so a strong wallbreaking partner such as Ogerpon-W or other special attackers like Raging Bolt could overwhelm it. Grassy Seed variants require Rillaboom as a partner, especially as it can bring Latias in safely via U-turn and overwhelm Steel-types like Corviknight and Tinkaton. Hazard support is really appreciated overall to help Latias clean in the endgame against a worn-down team, so Glimmora and Hisuian Samurott make for excellent partners. Latias also is a perfect match for teams championed by dual screens Deoxys-S or Alolan Ninetales, allowing it to set up multiple times with minimal damage taken.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dragon

Latias is able to carry a plethora of coverage if it wishes to, such as Thunderbolt and Ice Beam to easily dispatch of Water- and Flying-types such as Gliscor and Enamorus after Stealth Rock. Aura Sphere is another move that Latias can utilize to bait in and knock out opposing Bisharp and Weavile in conjunction with Spikes. Latias can even use Thunder Wave in a pinch to slow down threats such as Choice Scarf Enamorus and Flutter Mane for its teammates.

Choice Scarf (Dragon).description:
Latias is a great Choice Scarf user on Dragon teams, offering a wide variety of of both offense and support. Latias's typing and ability coupled with its great defenses grant it the ability to switch into many common moves, such as Landorus-T's Earthquake and Sneasler's Close Combat, and retaliate with STAB Draco Meteor. Psychic allows it to take care of the many Poison-types that can trouble its teammates Dragapult and Dragonite, such as non-Choice Scarf Sneasler, Amoonguss, and Galarian Weezing. Psyshock is an alternative to more easily take care of specially defensive Clodsire as well as 2HKO Assault Vest Iron Hands after Spikes from Garchomp. Trick is another option to provide utility by crippling foes such as Bisharp, Alolan Muk, and Heatran. Lastly, with Healing Wish, Latias gains the ability to grant a second life to its teammates when it is in a pinch. The given EV spread allows Latias to survive a Flutter Mane Moonblast and retaliate with Psyshock, KOing it after Spikes damage.

Pivot Dragapult is a great partner to cripple the opposition with status and easily pivot in Latias with U-turn, while offensive Choice Specs Dragapult aids Latias in bombarding foes with a barrage of Draco Meteors as well as being able to take care of Ghost-types such as Flutter Mane and Sinistcha. Hisuian Goodra and Archaludon are able to easily dispatch of Fairy-types as well as Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Chien-Pao, which are threatening to Dragon teams. Archaludon is also able to set Stealth Rock, allowing Latias to break through opposition more easily. Garchomp is another great partner for setting both Stealth Rock and Spikes, as well as phazing threats such as Calm Mind Ursaluna-B with Dragon Tail. Raging Bolt and Choice Specs Kyurem have a great matchup against Water and Flying teams. Raging Bolt is also able to beat Choice Scarf Greninja with Thunderclap. Lastly, Dragonite is the biggest beneficiary of Latias's Healing Wish, reinstating its Multiscale if it doesn't carry Roost, making it extremely threatening with its ease of setup. Kommo-o is a great partner by virtue of its mixed wallbreaking capabilities to deal with Steel- and Dark-types like Empoleon, Gholdengo, and Bisharp for Latias. Latias holding Choice Scarf also allows other common Choice Scarf teammates, such as Walking Wake and Roaring Moon, to run an alternative item, such as Choice Specs and Choice Band, respectively.

Choice Scarf (Psychic).description:
Choice Scarf Latias makes for great speed control on Psychic teams, outspeeding and threatening the likes of non-Choice Scarf Dragapult, Choice Specs Greninja, and +1 Dragonite. Draco Meteor is a powerful attack that takes out Latios and Sableye. Trick allows it to greatly weaken foes that are reliant on their items, such as Heavy-Duty Boots users such as Amoonguss and Dragonite as well as Leftovers and Black Sludge users like Corviknight, Archaludon, and Alolan Muk. Healing Wish allows Latias to sacrifice itself to cure status and restore HP to a weakened teammate. 8 Special Defense EVs allow Latias to survive Choice Scarf Flutter Mane's Moonblast from full health.

Indeedee makes for a great partner, as it sets up Psychic Terrain to boost its teammates' Psychic-type STAB moves. Furthermore, Indeedee's part-Normal typing makes it a great asset in the Ghost matchup, performing well against threats like Spectrier and Choice Specs Flutter Mane. Slowbro is a good defensive partner, walling the likes of Mamoswine, Bisharp, and Weavile and taking them out with Scald and Body Press. It also spreads paralysis with Thunder Wave so Latias is able to outspeed faster threats such as Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Dragapult. Metagross and Deoxys-S both set up entry hazards to aid Latias, and Deoxys-S can act as a suicide lead, able to take out speedy threats such as Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Sneasler. Metagross and Iron Crown both appreciate Latias handling Ground-types they don't like matching up against such as Choice Scarf Great Tusk and Landorus. In return, Iron Crown takes out Corviknight, Hatterene, and Clefable. Choice Band Hoopa-U beats bulky threats that Latias struggles with such as Hisuian Goodra, Blissey, and Gholdengo, and it appreciates Latias’s removal of Pecharunt in return. Hatterene provides hazard control through Magic Bounce, and with its part-Fairy typing, it takes on Dark-types like Mandibuzz, Roaring Moon, and Meowscarada. In return, Latias handles Poison-types that threaten Hatterene such as Choice Specs Iron Moth and Pecharunt. Iron Boulder forms a great offensive pairing with Latias, with Iron Boulder dealing with the likes of Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Enamorus, while Latias handles Dragapult and Archaludon.

vgc2024.overview:
• Latias is an exceptional Tailwind setter thanks to its great bulk, defensive typing, Levitate, and solid Speed. It also checks common threats such as Landorus and Urshifu-R.

  • Assault Vest Kingambit is a great partner, beating most of Latias's counters like Flutter Mane, Gholdengo, and, to an extent, Incineroar. It also makes great use of Tailwind, and Latias beats most of its counters as well.

  • Latias can be very tough to remove especially if it Terastallizes into a Poison-type, which, when combined with Levitate, has only one weakness and many valuable resistances. This becomes extra apparent when using Recover, which lets it clean up late-game when positioned well, especially if Mist Ball gets some Special Attack drops.

Bulky Tailwind Setter.description:
• Ice Beam is great coverage in general and very important for OHKOing Landorus, one of Latias's best and most important matchups.

  • Rocky Helmet lets Latias punish common and important moves like Fake Out and U-turn. It also breaks Chien-Pao's Focus Sash if it opts to run Ice Spinner and heavily discourages the prevalent Urshifu-R from attacking it.

  • The Speed EVs allow it to outspeed max Speed Landorus, the Special Attack EVs let it OHKO Urshifu-R and Landorus more consistently, and the rest of the EVs are used to optimize its bulk.

  • Tera Poison, when paired with Levitate, makes Latias very difficult to break, as Psychic-types, besides opposing Latias, are not common, and the Poison typing offers resistances to many relevant offensive types, the most important of which being Fairy, because of Flutter Mane.

Mega Calm Mind.description: Mega Latias uses its solid bulk, Speed tier, and typing alongside Levitate to become a potent win condition. This defensive prowess allows it to reliably answer threats such as Iron Moth, Buzzwole, and Keldeo, while the likes of Magic Guard Clefable and Choice Scarf Hydreigon struggle to break through it after it has boosted with Calm Mind. Psyshock provides Mega Latias with a strong STAB move that targets specially defensive Pokemon such as Blissey, Assault Vest Primarina, and Slowking on their weaker Defense stat while ignoring the boosts of opposing Calm Mind sweepers such as Reuniclus, Clefable, and Keldeo. Recover allows Mega Latias to leverage its huge bulk and consistently check the likes of Iron Moth and Thundurus by providing reliable recovery. Lastly, Aura Sphere provides Mega Latias with critical coverage against common Pokemon such as Excadrill and Hydreigon while preventing Tyranitar and Bisharp from being able to Pursuit trap it reliably. However, on teams that can reliably deal with Tyranitar, Mystical Fire is an option that allows Mega Latias to completely flip the script against Scizor while ensuring Mega Latias isn't walled by Celesteela and Aegislash, though it should be noted that Mega Latias will require significant chip damage to break past the last two. Given its lack of immediate damage output against bulkier Pokemon and methodical playstyle, Calm Mind Mega Latias is best suited to balance and entry hazard stacking teams that emphasize longevity. Entry hazard setters such as Clefable, Skarmory, and Gastrodon are pivotal to Mega Latias's ability to sweep through weakened teams, chipping down various Pokemon such as Aegislash, Hippowdon, and Iron Boulder to where it can comfortably finish them off; in return, Mega Latias provides them with a solid natural check to offensive threats such as Iron Moth and Thundurus that may threaten them early in the match. Additionally, Knock Off users such as the aforementioned Clefable, Assault Vest Tangrowth, and Scizor can assist Mega Latias by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Slowking, Hydrapple, and Victini and Leftovers from Celesteela and Hippowdon. Without Mystical Fire, Mega Latias also struggles to break past certain Steel-type Pokemon such as Aegislash, Scizor, and Celesteela, making dedicated answers such as Rotom-W, Iron Moth, and Skeledirge as well as early-game wallbreakers that can help pressure them such as Life Orb Mienshao and Alakazam important teammates. Lastly, Mega Latias is very weak to all forms of status; the likes of Zeraora, Mega Venusaur, and Hippowdon threaten to poison it, cutting into its longevity significantly, whereas paralysis from Slowking and Clefable cripples it similarly. This makes status absorbers such as Amoonguss and cleric support from Blissey and Chansey highly valuable to ensure Mega Latias isn't stopped by these Pokemon.

Offensive.description: With offensive investment augmenting its huge Special Attack stat and decent coverage, Mega Latias becomes a threatening wallbreaker that retains its valuable defensive utility against threats such as Iron Moth and Life Orb Mienshao, allowing it to fit on more aggressive teams. Aura Sphere is preferred as a coverage option to ensure Mega Latias can hit Steel- and Dark-types such as Excadrill, Tyranitar, and Bisharp consistently while avoiding Pursuit trapping attempts from the last two. Alternatively, Mystical Fire trades its ability to hit the aforementioned Dark-types for additional coverage against Aegislash and Celesteela; it also notably OHKOes Scizor from full. Draco Meteor provides Mega Latias with a stronger STAB option, threatening massive damage to traditional checks such as Slowbro and Victini on top of OHKOing Hydrapple and opposing maximum HP Mega Latias after Stealth Rock. However, Calm Mind can be used to boost Mega Latias's natural power, allowing it to tear through defensive Pokemon such as Clefable and Gastrodon after a boost. Entry hazard setters such as Clefable and Mold Breaker Excadrill are solid choices to help weaken certain Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur, Hippowdon, and Tyranitar to where Mega Latias can KO them. Offensive Mega Latias is also more vulnerable to revenge killing attempts from faster Pokemon such as Iron Boulder and Zygarde-10%, meaning checks such as Scizor, Zeraora, and Lokix pair extremely well with it; these Pokemon also benefit from Mega Latias's ability to threaten physically defensive Pokemon such as Buzzwole while being able to overwhelm walls such as Blissey and Celesteela in return. When running Aura Sphere, Magnezone is also a notable teammate, as its Magnet Pull ability can immediately dispatch Scizor and Celesteela, ensuring Mega Latias doesn't have to deal with them. Lastly, while Mega Latias can still afford to switch into Mienshao and Iron Moth in a vacuum, its lack of bulk investment means it is more vulnerable to being overwhelmed by them, making pivoting teammates such as Scizor, Choice Scarf Mienshao, and Rotom-W valuable to ensure it can hit the field safely and force them out.

Calm Mind.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • 252 HP / 236 Def / 20 Spe with Timid: This outspeeds up to Jolly Dragonite, so Encore and Scale Shot won't be as problematic.

  • 252 HP / 244 Def / 4 SpA / 4 SpD / 4 Spe with Bold: This physically bulky spread survives Adamant Focus Sash Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash without Terastallization.

Calm Mind (Dragon).description: Calm Mind Mega Latias excels at sweeping Fairy, Electric, Normal, and Ground teams thanks to its immense bulk and unique resistances. Stored Power eventually breaks through Unaware users like Quagsire and Clodsire after three Calm Mind boosts, and it is immediately strong after one boost thanks to it being a STAB attack. Thunderbolt wears down Celesteela and Mantine more efficiently. Ice Beam is another option and allows Mega Latias to OHKO Mega Garchomp and Landorus without needing boosts, making it an effective check to these threats. Alternatively, Refresh helps Mega Latias shrug off Toxic from threats like Clodsire and Tapu Koko, preventing it from being stalled out. Using Mega Latias can be a liability due to not being able to run the Dragon-immune Mega Altaria, so teammates like Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra that can stave off Dragon-type attacks are mandatory. Archaludon also helps Mega Latias by setting Stealth Rock to chip down Celesteela and Corviknight, taking on Triple Axel users like Meowscarada and Weavile, and being able to check the aforementioned Mega Altaria. Hisuian Goodra deals with Fairy-types like Mega Diancie and Tapu Lele, checks Gholdengo and Heatran, and annoys Celesteela and Ferrothorn with its coverage and ability in Sap Sipper. Kommo-o breaks down Steel, Normal, and Dark teams that Mega Latias has difficulty with, and in return, Mega Latias deals with Toxapex, Clodsire, and Mantine, which usually check Kommo-o with ease. Physical setup sweepers like Swords Dance Garchomp and Dragon Dance Roaring Moon form a wallbreaking core with Mega Latias, as they take care of the Steel- and Psychic-types that Mega Latias struggles with like Celesteela and Mega Gallade. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon or Latios provides speed control and deals with threats like Kommo-o, Mega Charizard X, and Iron Valiant.

Choice Scarf (Psychic).description: Choice Scarf Latias is an effective form of speed control on Psychic teams, differentiating itself from other Choice Scarf users like Tapu Lele and Iron Boulder with its excellent utility options such as Healing Wish. Latias's part-Dragon typing alongside Levitate lets it switch into and threaten many Electric- and Ground-type attackers such as Alolan Raichu and Landorus. Trick is preferred over Defog, as it allows Latias to shift its Choice Scarf to special walls like Ting-Lu and Blissey that would otherwise trouble it. However, Defog can be used over Trick to allow it to clear entry hazards for its teammates thanks to its great Speed. Healing Wish lets Latias stand out from other Choice Scarf users by allowing it to give one of its teammates a second chance in battle. Victini is a fantastic teammate for Latias because it that helps break through Steel-type Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Skarmory. Similarly, Mega Gallade can support Latias by breaking down Steel- and Dark-type Pokemon such as Heatran, Hisuian Goodra, Tyranitar, and Ting-Lu. In return, Latias can provide Healing Wish and Defog support for both Mega Gallade and Victini, check Zapdos for Mega Gallade, and check Ground- and Water-type Pokemon such as Garchomp and Ogerpon-W for Victini. Choice Scarf Tapu Lele is an excellent teammate for Latias, threatening Dark-type Pokemon such as Mega Sableye and Weavile. Jirachi is also a great teammate because it can deal with Fairy-type Pokemon such as Tapu Lele and Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, sponge attacks from Pokemon like Kyurem and opposing Latias, set up entry hazards, and provide safe switch-ins for Latias with U-turn.

Choice Scarf (Dragon).description: Choice Scarf Latias is a premier revenge killer on Dragon teams for its decent revenge killing capabilities, as it's able to outspeed common threats to Dragon teams such as Iron Valiant, Choice Specs Greninja, and Mega Garchomp while providing useful utility options in Defog and Healing Wish. Psychic lets Latias revenge kill troublesome Fighting-type Pokemon such as Hisuian Lilligant and Mega Lopunny. However, Psyshock can instead be used to hit Assault Vest Iron Hands and Clodsire harder. Defog allows Latias to work as emergency entry hazard removal thanks to its great Speed. Trick can be used over Defog to allow Latias to cripple special walls like Galarian Slowking and Blissey. Healing Wish lets Latias restore the health and status of one of its teammates, allowing them to have a second chance in the battle. Mega Altaria and Roaring Moon are superb partners that threaten the Dark- and Ghost-type Pokemon that Latias is weak to such as Tyranitar and Gholdengo. Kyurem is another great offensive partner, as it can destroy threats that Latias struggles against such as Mamoswine and Ting-Lu; in return, Latias can inconvenience special walls like Blissey and Galarian Slowking with Trick, beat Fighting-type Pokemon such as Keldeo and Urshifu-R for Kyurem, and provide Healing Wish support for it to take advantage of. Garchomp is also a great partner that pressures Steel-type Pokemon that Latias struggles against. It can also punish most physical attacks directed at Latias with Rough Skin if using a defensive set, while its Swords Dance set takes advantage of special walls that Latias struggles with such as Blissey and Galarian Slowking. Garchomp can also set up hazards, which allow Latias to OHKO threats such as Greninja for its team. Kommo-o is also a fantastic partner for Latias, as it beats Steel- and Dark-type Pokemon such as Mega Scizor and Ting-Lu while also appreciating Healing Wish support for a second assault. Archaludon is a great partner for Latias as well, as it provides a buffer against threats such as Roaring Moon and Mega Altaria that would otherwise beat Latias or take advantage of it while also setting up hazards for Latias.

Choice Specs.description:
With its high Speed and Special Attack, Choice Specs Latios is a very deadly wallbreaker in UU, able to even break past checks such as Metagross, Slowking, and Tyranitar over time with its nuclear Draco Meteor. Surf nails Heatran and Excadrill while having good neutral damage against Scizor and Metagross. Flip Turn allows Latios to preserve momentum off of checks like Blissey and Tinkaton coming in. Trick hinders Pokemon like Slowking and Tyranitar with a useless item for them but should only be used when Latios's Choice Specs is no longer needed, is not useful in the current matchup, or is more valuable to weaken said checks to open up another teammate to win. Latios can run other coverage moves too; Thunderbolt threatens Mandibuzz and Slowking, Shadow Ball hits Metagross super effectively while retaining coverage for Slowking, while Aura Sphere slams Tyranitar and retains the ability to break Heatran and Excadrill, but they generally are difficult moves to lock into compared to more standard options. Tera Dragon boosts Latios's Draco Meteor to absurd levels, being able to OHKO Assault Vest Tornadus-T after Stealth Rock and Slowking after very little chip damage as well as 2HKO specially defensive walls like Tyranitar. Tera Steel is an alternative that gives Latios greater defensive utility, being able to avoid revenge killing attempts from Pokemon like Greninja, Lokix, Mamoswine, and opposing Latios.

Choice Specs Latios is a powerful asset on bulky offense and balance builds for its powerful wallbreaking capabilities. Physical attackers such as Scizor, Weavile, Excadrill, and Cobalion excel at pressuring checks to Latios such as Metagross, Slowking, Tinkaton, and Tyranitar. Excadrill also provides entry hazard removal to keep Stealth Rock from wearing down Latios and switches into Tinkaton reliably. Tornadus-T and Lokix act as pivots that can wear down shared checks like Tyranitar and Tinkaton and enable Latios to wallbreak by bringing it in on other foes like Hydrapple and Toxapex. Entry hazard support from Pokemon like Tinkaton, Heatran, and Sandy Shocks does a great job at wearing down Metagross and Tyranitar into range of Latios's attacks. Defensive Pokemon like Slowking and the aforementioned Tornadus-T can defensively solidify Latios's team due to its need to predict correctly or otherwise risk losing momentum while the being additional checks to threats like Keldeo. Slowking can also provide paralysis support to mess with revenge killers like Lokix, Tornadus-T, and Greninja.

Soul Dew 3a.description:
With Soul Dew amplifying the power of its STAB moves, key defensive utility, and longevity, Latios is a formidable wallbreaker that can use its serviceable defensive utility in tandem with Recover to be an offensive threat that has longevity and key traits to bring to a team. Flip Turn allows Latios to gain momentum against and wear down threats like Excadrill, Slowking, and Tyranitar. Recover lets Latios pivot into the likes of Keldeo, Thundurus-T, Cobalion, and Sandy Shocks while not having to worry about being worn down. Soul Dew amplifies Latios's STAB moves while keeping its move flexibility. Tera Steel lets Latios avoid getting revenge killed by Pokemon like Greninja, Weavile, and Lokix. It also lets Latios act as a reliable switch-in against Hydrapple, Clodsire, and Gastrodon as well as giving it a Poison immunity, although it can no longer switch into Cobalion and Keldeo after Tera Steel.

Latios largely fits on offense and bulky offense teams as a useful wallbreaker that provides much-needed defensive utility against foes like Keldeo and Cobalion. Pivots like Lokix and Tornadus-T can bring Latios in safely to wallbreak while helping it overwhelm shared checks such as Tinkaton and Tyranitar. Tornadus-T also checks Pokemon that threaten Latios such as Lokix and Excadrill, while Lokix revenge kills faster threats like Greninja and Choice Scarf Zarude. Tornadus-T can also bring Latios in safely while being a good source of defensive utility against the likes of Greninja and can wear down Pokemon like Slowking and Metagross for it. Tinkaton and Cobalion can provide Stealth Rock support to put threats like Slowking and Assault Vest Tornadus-T in range of KOs more easily. Sandy Shocks can set up Spikes, help wear down Tornadus-T, and bring Latios in against Hydrapple. Araquanid is a good enabler for Latios on Sticky Web teams, slowing down faster threats like Greninja and Choice Scarf Mienshao, as well as helping it avoid a Speed tie with Ogerpon-C.

Calm Mind.description:
Thanks to Terastallization, Latios utilizes Calm Mind in tandem with a STAB Thunderbolt to become an extremely powerful sweeper that plays a defining role in UU. Latios's natural bulk and high Speed allow it to gain setup chances with Calm Mind to snowball against common Pokemon like Heatran and Rotom-W as well as others like Greninja and Tornadus-T post Tera, working in tandem with Draco Meteor to offset the Special Attack drops. Dragon Pulse is a weaker alternative that offers the benefit of not dropping Latios's Special Attack. Thunderbolt complements Latios's Dragon-type STAB attack to be an unwallable combination outside of Excadrill, targeting many Pokemon such as Azumarill, Toxapex, Tinkaton, and Heatrann. Recover allows Latios to maintain longevity throughout the game and gain multiple chances to sweep while simultaneously providing natural defensive utility to its team against foes like Rotom-W, Keldeo, and Thundurus-T. The passive recovery of Leftovers allows Latios to set up more easily without relying on Recover, but Ability Shield is an alternative to bypass Excadrill's Mold Breaker, allowing Latios to now set up on its biggest counter. However, this item relies on surprise factor and is vulnerable to being removed via Knock Off from Pokemon like Tornadus-T and Weavile. Maximum investment in Special Attack and Speed allows Latios to be a fast, hard-hitting natural threat that doesn't need to rely on boosts to be effective. Alternatively, 96 Speed EVs to outspeed Hisuian Arcanine, maximum HP investment, and the remaining EVs in Defense let Latios act as a bulkier sweeper to better stand up to foes like Metagross and Lokix at the cost of immediate power. Tera Electric is the driving point of this set, boosting Thunderbolt to powerful levels to get past foes like Tinkaton and Metagross more easily while also making it safer into Lokix and Tornadus-T, not to mention giving Latios no weaknesses thanks to its synergy with Levitate. Latios also gains an immunity to Thunder Wave from foes like Slowking and Tinkaton.

Calm Mind + Tera Electric Latios fits on a multitude of archetypes ranging from offense to semi-stall, but it finds itself most at home on bulky offense and balance teams thanks to its role as a reliable sweeper. Latios's biggest obstacle is Mold Breaker Excadrill, which handles its otherwise unresisted move combination, so Slowking and Hydrapple are great teammates to keep Excadrill in line. Slowking also provides slow pivoting support with Chilly Reception to get Latios in safely as well as provide speed control with Thunder Wave or amplify wallbreaking with Future Sight. Pivots like Tornadus-T and Lokix can bring Latios in to set up for a sweep while wearing down shared checks like Tyranitar and Tinkaton. Tornadus-T checks dangerous threats to Latios like Lokix and Ogerpon, whereas Lokix exerts offensive pressure on the likes of Excadrill and Greninja for Latios. Stealth Rock support from Tinkaton and Cobalion wears down foes like Toxapex and Assault Vest Tornadus-T into range of being KOed more easily. Tinkaton can also wear down Excadrill and Tera Fairy Hydrapple, while Cobalion can pressure foes like Zarude and Mandibuzz. Skeledirge is another issue for this set, so Pokemon that handle it such as Excadrill, Ogerpon-C, and Greninja make great teammates. Latios is quite Tera reliant to function at its very best, so offensive threats that do not use Terastallization often like the aforementioned Excadrill and Weavile as well as others like Keldeo and Quaquaval form great offensive cores that can take out checks to Latios such as Tyranitar, Clodsire, and Tinkaton.

Soul Dew.description:
With Soul Dew equipped, Latios is a powerful offensive threat with a unique defensive profile that gives it a notable niche in the metagame, being one of the only offensive Pokemon with a complete immunity to Spikes. Psychic Noise allows Latios to shut down recovery attempts from defensive Pokemon, particularly Blissey and Corviknight. Calm Mind gives Latios enough power to easily pressure defensive walls, notably OHKOing specially defensive Gliscor with Draco Meteor after Stealth Rock; however, Aura Sphere can be considered as an alternative option that can hit Steel- and Dark-types like Kingambit and Ting-Lu that would otherwise force it out. Shadow Ball, while less common, can be used to smack the likes of Gholdengo and Iron Crown. Recover gives Latios more opportunities to fire off powerful attacks over the course of a game, combining with its Spikes immunity to shrug off most forms of passive damage. Tera Steel is invaluable as a defensive Tera type, granting Latios a total immunity to Toxic and also allowing it to set up against the likes of Galarian Slowking, Dragonite, and Enamorus, as well as alleviating pressure against Pokemon such as Weavile and Kingambit.

Latios finds its niche on balance and bulky offense teams that enjoy its wallbreaking capabilities. Zamazenta is a phenomenal partner for Latios, capable of switching into and forcing out Dark-types such as Kingambit, Darkrai, and Weavile, and it appreciates Latios for being able to smash through physical walls like Gliscor and Alomomola. Kingambit is another Pokemon that enjoys Latios smashing holes through defensive teams carrying defensive Pokemon like Alomomola and Moltres, and in turn, it can offensively check the likes of Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Hatterene; conversely, Tinkaton is a good alternative to Kingambit as a Steel-type, instead providing Latios with entry hazard support and being able to leverage its superior defensive profile to more reliably check threats like Iron Valiant, Darkrai, and Weavile. Knock Off support from the likes of Ogerpon, Weavile, and Meowscarada is also greatly appreciated and enables Latios to put even more pressure on defensive teams, allowing for the aforementioned faster teammates to clean up late-game; all of these Pokemon also appreciate Latios for being able to lure in and remove Kingambit with Aura Sphere. Hisuian Samurott is another excellent partner, as it provides both Knock Off support and hazard pressure in Ceaseless Edge, and acts as an offensive check to Kingambit and Gholdengo which Latios greatly enjoys, while Latios can easily come in on and threaten massive damage on Pokemon like Alomomola and Zapdos that can check Hisuian Samurott. Similarly, Ting-Lu is also appreciated as a teammate, providing Latios with a sturdy check to Dragapult, Darkrai, and Iron Crown while also being able to set hazards. Cinderace can offensively pressure many of the tier's Steel-types and can bring Latios in with U-turn against Pokemon such as Gliscor and Garganacl that Cinderace struggles to break past; Moltres is another great teammate for Latios, as it can act as a stopgap to threats like Kingambit, Kyurem, and Iron Valiant while also bringing Latios onto the field safely with its slow U-turn. Lastly, Great Tusk is another Pokemon that can remove items for Latios with Knock Off and provides Latios with a resilient offensive check to Kingambit; on the other hand, Great Tusk enjoys having Latios rip through its checks, particularly Alomomola, Zapdos, and Moltres.

Choice Specs.description:
With its good Speed and great Special Attack compounded by Choice Specs, as well as an immunity to Spikes that makes it harder to wear down, Latios becomes a wallbreaker able to OHKO key metagame threats such as Landorus-T and Zapdos as well as overwhelm would-be checks like Ting-Lu and Galarian Slowking. Luster Purge's high power and potential to drop foes's Special Defense allows Latios to break past Pokemon that might otherwise stand against it such as Assault Vest Primarina and Galarian Slowking. Aura Sphere lets Latios blow past Kingambit and target Iron Treads, Heatran, and Tyranitar. Trick grants Latios with the opportunity to cripple defensive Pokemon trying to switch into it such as Blissey and Corviknight while also deterring slower setup Pokemon such as Hatterene from using Latios as setup fodder as well as revenge killing attempts from Kingambit without getting hit by Sucker Punch. Due to several Pokemon resisting or being immune to one of Latios's STAB moves, Flip Turn may be used as a way to preserve momentum and bring a teammate onto the field while easing the need for prediction. A Timid nature allows Latios to outspeed the likes of Enamorus and Walking Wake as well as Speed tie with Ogerpon-W and opposing Latios; however, a Modest nature may instead be used to enhance Latios's wallbreaking prowess, threatening 2HKOs against the likes of offensive Gholdengo and Garganacl after a round of Stealth Rock. Tera Dragon boosts Latios's Draco Meteor, letting it OHKO Gliscor and 2HKO would-be checks like Assault Vest Alomomola and Corviknight; Tera Dragon also removes Latios's weakness to moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Darkrai's Dark Pulse.

Choice Specs Latios finds itself on bulky offense and balance teams; particularly on teams with either temporary or non-existent entry hazard removal. Zamazenta, particularly Heavy-Duty Boots variants, often finds itself on these teams, and it threatens Dark- and Steel-types that resist one or both of Latios's STAB moves such as Kingambit, Darkrai, Ting-Lu, and Iron Treads as well as being able to absorb a hit from faster physical foes such as Weavile and offensive Cinderace; in turn, Latios can threaten the physical walls that trouble Zamazenta such as Pecharunt, Zapdos, and Dondozo. As Latios finds itself exposed after being locked into a move, defensive teammates that it can rely on to absorb incoming attacks are appreciated. Galarian Slowking can fill such a role, handling Fairy-types such as Primarina, Enamorus, and Hatterene. Pecharunt and Zapdos aid Latios against physical attackers such as Swords Dance Iron Valiant and Cinderace, as well as against Scizor and Lokix in Zapdos's case. Furthermore, all of Galarian Slowking, Pecharunt, and Zapdos can act as pivots to safely bring Latios on the field. Ting-Lu is another teammate that can handle Steel-types such as Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Heatran, as well as Dragapult and Darkrai, which outspeed and greatly threaten Latios. Furthermore, Ting-Lu, as well as other partners like Landorus-T, Gliscor, Hisuian Samurott, and Great Tusk, may provide entry hazard support, softening up foes for Latios to break through while assisting it at handling the likes of Gholdengo and Kingambit. Finally, Kingambit is able to deal with defensive Gholdengo, Assault Vest Hatterene, and Galarian Slowking that greatly annoy Latios, while in return, it appreciates Latios's ability to blow past Landorus-T and Moltres and bring it in safely with Flip Turn.

Choice Scarf.description:
Thanks to its superb stats and solid movepool, Latios proves to be an amazing speed control option with Choice Scarf, outspeeding fast foes like Walking Wake, Choice Scarf Landorus-T and Enamorus, Zamazenta, and +1 Speed Great Tusk as well as Speed tying Iron Moth. Psychic Noise helps Latios break past fat teams in a better fashion by denying recovery like Gliscor's Poison Heal and Garganacl's Leftovers and Recover and hits foes like Iron Moth and Zamazenta behind a Substitute. However, Luster Purge's power can be preferred to revenge kill Enamorus and Zamazenta more reliably and, with the drops, potentially wallbreak bulky foes like Galarian Slowking at the cost of having very low PP. Aura Sphere is a great coverage option that allows Latios to destroy Kingambit and Iron Treads. Trick cripples its would-be checks like Ting-Lu and Iron Crown while also shutting down Calm Mind users like Clefable, Hatterene, and Sinistcha. Tera Steel flips all of its Ice and Fairy weakness from foes like Weavile, Kyurem, Enamorus, and Iron Valiant and provides a resistance to Dragonite's Extreme Speed; it works well with Levitate to ignore even the aforementioned Kyurem, Enamorus, and Dragonite's Ground-type coverage move.

Latios works best on bulky offense and balance teams. It really appreciates entry hazard support to maximize its pressure against the opposing team. Therefore, Spikes setters such as Hisuian Samurott and Gliscor are great teammates, as is Ting-Lu, which can also choose to run Stealth Rock. Garganacl is a great option for Stealth Rock support, and it racks up damage on the opposing team by spamming Salt Cure, opening up win paths for Latios and its teammates. These Pokemon also help Latios deal with its own threats like Gholdengo and Iron Crown. Zamazenta pairs excellently with Latios, taking care of specially bulky foes that Latios struggles against such as Ting-Lu and Blissey as well as answering checks like Kingambit and Darkrai. In addition, both of them do a great job in pressuring shared checks like Gholdengo and Primarina. Other physical wallbreakers such as Kingambit and Ogerpon-W also have great synergy with Latios. Kingambit handles Gholdengo for Latios, and together, they form a great late-game duo. In a similar vein, Ogerpon-W can deal with Pokemon like Ting-Lu and pressure opposing teams enough in the early- and mid-game for Latios to pick off chipped foes late-game. Other special attackers such as Darkrai, Dragapult, Gholdengo, and Iron Crown also pair well with Latios because they can pressure shared checks like Dark-types, most notably Ting-Lu. Finally, Great Tusk is a stellar teammate that can help Latios deal with Gholdengo, Tinkaton, Dark-types, and special walls while also providing valuable Stealth Rock and hazard removal support.

Wallbreaker.description:
Mega Latios uses its superb Special Attack, great typing and bulk, and amazing coverage to become a threatening special sweeper capable of switching into and threatening Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Mega Charizard Y, and Toxapex. Aura Sphere takes out Pokemon that would normally switch into Luster Purge, like Melmetal, Heatran, and Hisuian Samurott, and threatens Pursuit users like Kingambit, Weavile, and Mega Tyranitar on the switch. Mystical Fire helps with Steel-types unfazed by Aura Sphere, such as Mega Scizor and Gholdengo, and also hits Ferrothorn harder. Draco Meteor picks up KOs against Dragon-types like Dragonite, Roaring Moon, and Raging Bolt and is Mega Latios's strongest option against Pokemon like Gliscor and Ogerpon-W. Ice Beam can deal with other Dragon-types without dropping Mega Latios's Special Attack while also hitting Flying-types like Landorus-T and Tornadus-T.

While Mega Latios fits on a variety of teams from offense to balance, it fits best with teammates that appreciate Mega Latios breaking down Pokemon like Alomomola, Toxapex, Moltres, and Galarian Slowking for them to sweep later in the game. Examples of Pokemon that appreciate these defensive staples getting broken down are Volcarona, Cinderace, Urshifu-R, and Zamazenta. The latter two also stonewall Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Weavile, each of which would normally come in and Pursuit trap Mega Latios. These same Pursuit trappers are also great teammates, as they can trap Pokemon like Gholdengo and opposing Mega Latios, while Mega Latios can weaken Mega Charizard Y and Ogerpon-W for them to wreak havoc. Even with Aura Sphere, Mega Latios can struggle with Steel-types like Assault Vest Melmetal, Heatran, Gholdengo, and Mega Scizor if not running Mystical Fire, so teammates like Great Tusk, Moltres, and Ting-Lu should be considered; Great Tusk and Ting-Lu in particular can set up hazards to chip down Pokemon like Melmetal and Heatran into range of Mega Latios's attacks. Since Mega Latios is a very good check to Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Ogerpon-W, and Great Tusk, Pokemon that appreciate these being chipped down, like Cinderace, Landorus-T, and Tapu Koko, make great teammates. In return, these teammates can easily bring in Pokemon such as Alomomola and Ferrothorn, allowing Mega Latios easy access to wreak havoc on the opposing team. Ferrothorn itself is a great partner for Mega Latios, as it can deal with faster threats such as Iron Valiant as well as Choice Scarf Pokemon like Tapu Lele and Hisuian Samurott.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dragon (Expert Belt)

Earthquake catches and heavily damages typical switch-ins to Latios like Alolan Muk, Hisuian Goodra, and Heatran. However, losing out on Recover can make Latios have a harder time breaking bulky Flying teams. Life Orb paired with a Naive nature can also be used if using Earthquake, as it guarantees an OHKO on Heatran and a 2HKO on Hisuian Goodra and Alolan Muk after a layer of Spikes. Furthermore, a Life Orb-boosted Luster Purge followed by Thunderbolt eliminates Articuno and Empoleon if Luster Purge drops their Special Defense, which is something Expert Belt cannot achieve. However, Life Orb recoil limits the number of attempts Latios has to break down the opposing team and reveals its item.

Psychic (Choice Specs)

Latios can use Flip Turn to keep up momentum against the many switches it forces and bring in teammates to better answer the incoming threat. Psychic Noise is an option to better counter defensive walls such as specially defensive Articuno and RestTalk Dondozo, denying their recovery and decreasing their longevity overtime. Psychic Noise also has the added benefit of shutting down Draining Kiss Primarina completely. Energy Ball can be used to more easily counter Water/Ground types such as Gastrodon and Swampert.

Expert Belt (Dragon).description:
Latios blasts through Flying, Ground, and balanced Water teams with less reliance on prediction when using an Expert Belt. Luster Purge's Special Defense drop complements its coverage, as it sets up KOs on Corviknight, Primarina, and Assault Vest Iron Hands. Ice Beam hits Gliscor and Dragonite, completing its coverage against Flying teams. Recover lets Latios be less threatened by repeated Knock Offs from Assault Vest Tornadus-T, allowing Latios to remain a threat throughout the match. Alternatively, Energy Ball OHKOes Swampert and Gastrodon, the best answers to Thunderbolt on a Water team, after minimal chip damage.

While Expert Belt Latios excels in breaking Flying and balanced Water teams, it fails to be as threatening in matchups like Fighting and Poison because it is unable to deal significant damage to Assault Vest Gallade and Alolan Muk without Choice Specs. Wallbreakers like Choice Specs Dragapult and Garchomp help, as Dragapult forces these checks to get worn down over time and also deals with faster threats like Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Greninja. On the other hand, Garchomp deals with Steel-types like Gholdengo and Hisuian Goodra that Latios struggles against, and it can run Spikes to wear down opposing teams or Swords Dance to clean up types like Flying after Corviknight has been dealt with. Archaludon deals with Meowscarada and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, slows down threats like Ogerpon-H and Roaring Moon with Thunder Wave, and sets Stealth Rock to wear down Latios's checks like Assault Vest Tornadus-T. In return, Latios purges Fighting- and Ground-types like Urshifu-R and Landorus. Hisuian Goodra tanks special attacks from faster threats like Darkrai, Dragapult, and Spectrier and loves Latios's ability to remove annoying threats like Gliscor and Garchomp. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon helps Latios get more chances to break opposing defensive cores, as Roaring Moon lures in Toxapex and Skarmory that Latios can handle. Kommo-o can also be considered, as it breaks down Steel teams and packs priority to remove Greninja and Meowscarada, which give Latios a hard time.

Choice Specs (Dragon).description:
Choice Specs Latios is a dangerous wallbreaker thanks to its good Speed tier, array of high-powered options, and solid coverage to hit potential checks. Luster Purge obliterates Fighting- and Poison-types like Great Tusk, Iron Hands, and Toxapex for teammates like Roaring Moon. Its Special Defense drop chance also allows Latios to take on neutral targets like Clefable and Articuno. Thunderbolt hits bulky Flying- and Water-types like Corviknight and Empoleon. Draco Meteor is Latios's strongest STAB move, most notably annihilating threats like Archaludon, Walking Wake, and Kyurem. Ice Beam forms a deadly BoltBeam combination with Thunderbolt and allows Latios to hit Ground-types like Gliscor and Landorus-T without the drawback of dropping its Special Attack. Aura Sphere can be run over Ice Beam to hit Steel-types like Heatran. Trick allows Latios to majorly hinder defensive staples like Assault Vest Galarian Slowking and Hisuian Goodra that can otherwise take it on.

Archaludon functions as a wonderful teammate for Latios, as it can take on Bisharp and other Dark-types like Ting-Lu with Body Press and Stamina. It also provides entry hazard support in the form of Stealth Rock. In return, Latios can switch in on Ground-type attacks, like Earthquake from the likes of Choice Scarf Great Tusk and Choice Band Excadrill, thanks to Levitate; this also allows it to find opportunities to fire off its strong attacks. Another good defensive partner for Latios is Hisuian Goodra, which can take special Fairy-type attacks from Flutter Mane and Hatterene and remove them with Heavy Slam. Hisuian Goodra also removes important items like Articuno's Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off, allowing Latios to more easily break through it with the help of hazards.
