Specifically, Choice Scarf allows Infernape to revenge kill faster Pokemon like Munkidori, Inteleon, and Kilowattrel, while Choice Specs sets capitalize on Infernape's set ambiguity by unleashing a powerful Overheat or Fire Blast on the physical walls that Choice Scarf Infernape forces in. Additionally, Choice Scarf sets outspeed most other Choice Scarf users, such as Flygon, Munkidori, and Flamigo. However, Infernape faces competition against these exact Choice Scarf users due to them fitting on more teams easily. Additionally, Choice Specs sets can struggle to break through Pokemon like Vaporeon, Chandelure, and Basculegion-M due to their decent bulk and ability to take both of Infernape's STAB moves comfortably. Infernape also fights for a slot on teams with other Fighting-types, since Toxicroak reliably beats Water-types, Flamigo has access to recovery, Paldean Tauros-W can switch into Incineroar without fear of Knock Off due to being less item reliant than Infernape, and Paldean Tauros-F can easily fit Stone Edge to hit would-be checks like Altaria and Chandelure.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Infernape can run a Choice Band set, letting it break through defensive tanks like Galarian Slowbro and Overqwil, but it's largely outclassed by other Fighting-types like Flamigo, Toxicroak, and the Paldean Tauros formes. Infernape can run a Swords Dance or Nasty Plot set, making it a excellent setup sweeper; however, it struggles to run all of the moves that it needs and is easily revenge killed by common Choice Scarf users like Munkidori, Chandelure, and Flygon. A lead set of Stealth Rock / Taunt / Endeavor or Encore / Mach Punch or Knock Off with a Focus Sash can be run on hyper offense teams to aid in both setting up and preventing entry hazards. Infernape can run a mixed set of Fire Blast or Overheat / Close Combat / U-turn or Grass Knot or Stone Edge / Knock Off with a Life Orb, allowing it to threaten many walls like Avalugg, Galarian Slowbro, Vaporeon, and Gligar; however, it gets revenge killed by faster foes like Kilowattrel, Munkidori, and Choice Scarf Flamigo, and due to EV constraints, it often is a weaker and worse off wallbreaker than a fully physical or special set.

Checks and Counters

Faster Threats and Priority Users: Cinccino, Kilowattrel, and Scream Tail can outspeed Infernape and destroy it with their attacks, but none of them enjoy switching into Infernape's STAB attacks. Choice Scarf users such as Flygon, Munkidori, and Chandelure are able to outpace and destroy non-Choice Scarf variants of Infernape. Infernape can be picked off by priority users like Shadow Sneak Decidueye and Aqua Jet Basculegion-M.

Fire-resistant Pokemon: Bulky Water-types like Vaporeon can fairly tank Infernape's attacks and threaten it back with their attacks, but none can repeatedly switch into its Fighting-type attacks. Offensive Water-types like Barraskewda and Paldean Tauros-W can KO Infernape with their attacks, and they can pick it off with Aqua Jet. Chandelure is immune to both of its STAB attacks and easily destroys it; however, Chandelure doesn't enjoy switching directly into Scorching Sands and Knock Off. Basculegion-M can tank Infernape's Fire-type attacks and blank its Fighting-type attacks, but it doesn't enjoy tanking Grass Knot and Knock Off. While Altaria doesn't enjoy switching into Stone Edge variants, it can easily resist both of Infernape's STAB attacks and KO it. Goodra walls Infernape's Fire-type attacks and Choice Specs sets, but it doesn't enjoy switching into Close Combat.

Ground-types: Flygon, Rhyperior, and Swampert can easily OHKO Infernape with Earthquake or freely set up entry hazards; however, none of them enjoy directly switching into Infernape's Fighting-type attacks. Gligar is notable for tanking Infernape's physical attacks very well and destroying Infernape with Earthquake, but it can be lured and punished by Choice Specs sets.

Choice Specs.description:
Set Details

Flamethrower is preferred for its reliability, but Fire Blast is stronger, allowing Infernape to 2HKO foes like Gligar and Munkidori. Overheat allows Infernape to break through common walls like Galarian Slowbro and Gligar; however, Grass Knot offers a coverage move that hits Rhyperior, Swampert, and Basculegion-M super effectively. Focus Blast allows it to 2HKO foes like Swampert, while Aura Sphere can be used for improved accuracy. Scorching Sands allows it to threaten Chandelure, which otherwise walls it, as well as bulky Poison-types like Galarian Slowbro. Infernape can run Vacuum Wave to pick off weakened targets like Flygon and Inteleon, while Switcheroo can cripple defensive walls like Galarian Slowbro, Altaria, and Bellibolt. U-turn can also be used to ease prediction, allowing Infernape to do some chip damage and bring a partner in against threats like Rhyperior and Uxie. Tera Fire allows Infernape's Fire-type attacks to do major damage on threats like Munkidori and Tornadus while giving it the ability to OHKO foes like Gligar and Galarian Slowbro with Overheat.

Infernape appreciates Grass-types such as Tsareena, Amoonguss, and Decidueye that beat Water- and Ground-types like Vaporeon, Paldean Tauros-W, and Flygon. Infernape pairs nicely with wallbreakers like Substitute Basculegion-M and Flygon, since they handle special walls like Vaporeon and Goodra. Psychic- and Ghost-types like Munkidori, Galarian Slowbro, Scream Tail, Chandelure, and Basculegion-M can easily KO Infernape; thus, Dark-types like Overqwil, Incineroar, Scrafty, and Wo-Chien make for good partners, as they can easily handle them. Infernape appreciates entry hazard removers like Altaria and Brambleghast, as they allow it to not be worn down by hazards, though they are not outright necessary because Infernape can intentionally use hazards to lower its HP into Blaze range. Due to Altaria, Basculegion-M, and Chandelure resisting or being immune to both of Infernape's STAB attacks, Infernape requires teammates that can threaten them like Sylveon, Wo-Chien, and Incineroar, respectively. Choice Scarf users like Flygon, Munkidori, and Flamigo can easily revenge kill Infernape, so it partners with switch-ins like Bronzong, Rhyperior, and Bellibolt to handle them. Pivots like Flygon, Munkidori, and Bellibolt pair well with Infernape, since they can draw in Steel-types like Copperajah and Bronzong.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

U-turn gives Infernape the ability to pivot while letting it chip down defensive tanks like Galarian Slowbro and Swampert. Knock Off allows it to pressure foes like Rhyperior and Kilowattrel that rely on their items, as well as hitting both Chandelure and Basculegion-M, while Stone Edge allows Infernape to beat Chandelure as well as Flying-types like Altaria and Tornadus. Switcheroo lets it cripple defensive tanks like Amoonguss, Bellibolt, and Vaporeon. Infernape can use Thunder Punch alongside Iron Fist, letting it threaten Water- and Flying-types like Inteleon, Basculegion-M, and Flamigo. Tera Fighting enables Infernape to threaten a 2HKO on Paldean Tauros-W and Flygon with Close Combat. Tera Dark allows Infernape to tank Psychic- and Ghost-type attacks from Munkidori, Uxie, Chandelure, Decidueye, and Brambleghast.

Choice Scarf Infernape often draws in Fighting-resistant foes like Galarian Slowbro, Gligar, and Sylveon, so it best partners with specially offensive Basculegion-M, Paldean Tauros-W, and Munkidori to check these switch-ins. Infernape can form a VoltTurn core with other pivots like Kilowattrel, Flygon, and Gligar, since they can pressure defensive tanks like Vaporeon, Bellibolt, and Amoonguss. Additionally, they bring in foes like Bronzong and Amoonguss that Infernape can take advantage of. Bulky Water-types like Vaporeon and Swampert can act as blanket checks to its attacks and threaten Infernape back with their STAB attacks; thus, it pairs with Grass-types like Decidueye, Amoonguss, and Tsareena to check them. Steel- and Dark-types like Bronzong, Klefki, and Overqwil are great partners for Infernape, since they can beat Psychic-types like Munkidori, Uxie, and Scream Tail. Entry hazard removers like Altaria, Scyther, and Brambleghast allow Infernape to continuously switch in without getting worn down by hazards.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Fire

Thunder Punch and Knock Off are other options Infernape can choose to run over Close Combat or Flare Blitz. Thunder Punch allows Infernape to threaten several bulky Water-types. It can 2HKO mixed defensive Toxapex most of the time and OHKO Pelipper and Gyarados. With Knock Off, Infernape can not only threaten Ghost-types, such as Skeledirge, but it can also remove key items, such as Heavy-Duty Boots and Eviolite, from the likes of Pelipper, Toxapex, and Porygon2 to make it easier to wear these walls down. However, Close Combat is generally more useful due to the amount of targets it can remove like Ursaluna and Ting-Lu, benefiting Fire teams. Fire Punch can be run over Flare Blitz. Although weaker, using Fire Punch doesn't result in Infernape taking recoil damage, improving its longevity. However, Flare Blitz is more reliable despite its recoil damage, and the recoil damage can be solved when running Ninetales thanks to the its access to Healing Wish. Choice Scarf is another option for Infernape, as this can allow it to outspeed and threaten would-be faster Pokemon, such as Flutter Mane, but this trades away its ability to win one-on-one against more bulky Pokemon like Ursaluna.

Choice Band (Fire).description:
Infernape is a great wallbreaker and cleaner on Fire teams. Its Fighting typing grants Infernape and Fire teams a better matchup against Dark teams, being able to threaten the likes of Hydreigon and Greninja while also resisting Bisharp's Sucker Punch, and with Flare Blitz, it can threaten Landorus. Close Combat is Infernape's primary Fighting-type STAB move, massively threaten the likes of Ursaluna and Kyurem. With U-turn, Infernape can safely pivot out of its switch-ins, such as Dondozo, into a teammate that can threaten them. Infernape is also able to serve as a great revenge killer thanks to its access to an Iron Fist-boosted Mach Punch, being able to pick off weakened threats such as Roaring Moon, Iron Treads, and Darkrai.

Ninetales and Torkoal make for great partners for Infernape, as the two of them up sun to further boost Infernape's Flare Blitz. Ninetales also commonly uses Solar Beam, allowing it to OHKO threats to Infernape, such as physically defensive Quagsire, and can heal Infernape with Healing Wish, while Torkoal can remove entry hazards for Infernape with its access to Rapid Spin. Torkoal and Heatran can set Stealth Rock in order to wear down foes for Infernape to pick off. For example, Infernape is guaranteed a 2HKO on Galarian Weezing after Stealth Rock damage. In return, Infernape can OHKO Landorus with Flare Blitz under sun as well as both Ursaluna and Mamoswine without sun. Cinderace is another noteworthy teammate, as not only can it remove hazards with Court Change, but it is also able to revenge kill faster Ghost-types Infernape cannot such as Dragapult and Speed-boosted Ceruledge with Sucker Punch. In return, Infernape's Fighting-type STAB move frees up a moveslot for Cinderace, as the latter no longer needs High Jump Kick. Volcanion is another great teammate, as it provides Fire teams an immunity to Water, and in return, Infernape is able to threaten the likes of Iron Treads and Landorus for it. Talonflame and Moltres provide a Ground immunity, Will-O-Wisp support, and they can bring Infernape in via U-turn. The two of them are also able to lure bulky Pokemon like Ursaluna-B and Ting-Lu for Infernape to break. Talonflame also provides Defog support, while Moltres's bulk allows it to take on Dragonite, which Infernape greatly appreciates. Infernape's wallbreaking enables other wallbreakers and sweepers such as Ogerpon-H, Volcarona, and Ceruledge to clean late-game. In particular, Infernape can remove Alolan Muk and Heatran to enable a sweep from Volcarona.

Mixed Wallbreaker.description: 168 Attack EVs let -1 Close Combat OHKO Krookodile.

ru.overview: Empoleon is a fantastic Water-type that can fill either a defensive role with the help of its myriad utility options or an offensive role by utilizing its phenomenal coverage depending on the needs of its team. Empoleon's incredible defensive typing gives it natural resistances to the STAB moves of many of the tier's top Pokemon, including Jirachi, Speed Boost Yanmega, Slowbro, and Cyclizar, which can give it many opportunities to make progress over the course of a game. Empoleon can also utilize its offensive power to blow holes through teams, as there are few Pokemon that can safely switch into all of its attacks, especially after a Competitive boost. Empoleon is mainly held back by its low Speed that allows strong Fighting- and Electric-type wallbreakers to easily force it out and threaten the rest of its team. Furthermore, Empoleon's inability to manually boost its offenses means that special walls like Umbreon can usually tank its attacks with very little consequence. Defensive Empoleon sets particularly can suffer from four-moveslot syndrome, as it often wants to fit more utility moves than it can afford, thereby leaning it into a passive role that can be exploited by setup sweepers.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Flash Cannon is a STAB option that can enable Empoleon to deal with Fairy-types like Alolan Ninetales and Gardevoir more easily. Agility can be used on offensive sets to solve Empoleon's Speed problem and enable it to act as a cleaner at the cost of Roost or a coverage move. Shuca Berry allows Empoleon to take out Ground-type Pokemon like Krookodile and Rhyperior after safely absorbing an Earthquake. Chople Berry similarly enables Empoleon to survive a hit from wallbreakers such as Flamigo and strike back. Tera Water is another option on offensive Empoleon that can boost Surf enough to secure certain rolls, such as a 2HKO on Bisharp.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Fighting-type wallbreakers like Flamigo and Gallade threaten Empoleon and force it out, which give them the opportunity to fire off an attack or pivot safely out of the switch-in.

Setup Sweepers: Many of the common Calm Mind users in the tier such as Cresselia, Reuniclus, and Slowbro can outheal Empoleon's damage and use it as setup fodder if it isn't running Roar or the right coverage move. Because of its relative passivity, defensive Empoleon can be similarly exploited by other threatening setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Crawdaunt, Swords Dance Bisharp, and Dragon Dance Feraligatr.

Special Walls: The most specially defensive Pokemon in the tier like Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon can easily shrug off Empoleon's attacks and force progress against it or create an opportunity for a physical wallbreaker to switch in and threaten Empoleon out.

Offensive.description:
Offensive Empoleon is uniquely equipped to provide teams with a strong defensive and offensive presence given its natural bulk and exceptional coverage. Its Water / Steel typing and Special Defense is valuable in a metagame with strong Choice Scarf users such as Basculegion-F, Gardevoir, and Gengar threatening to use their strong STAB attacks to clean games. Surf is a reliable STAB option for Empoleon, as it hits a lot of the metagame for neutral damage. Ice Beam gives Empoleon coverage to hit Dragon- and Grass-types such as Cyclizar, Noivern, and Amoonguss. Grass Knot hits Water-types like Basculegion-F and Slowbro while also giving it a means to damage Suicune to prevent it from getting a free Substitute. Roost assures Empoleon can reliably recover throughout a game. Leftovers gives Empoleon even more longevity and offsets most entry hazard damage. Competitive is useful for getting a boost from Defog attempts, Intimidate Attack drops, and notably from Moonblast Special Attack drops, as Empoleon often switches into Gardevoir and Cresselia. Modest is used given Empoleon has great natural bulk without much investment, giving it more wallbreaking power without offsetting the defensive utility it has. The EV spread provided covers a few relevant defensive and offensive benchmarks. The defensive investments allow Empoleon to survive Kleavor's Close Combat. Offensively, Empoleon threatens to 2HKO Assault Vest Cyclizar with Ice Beam after it takes Stealth Rock damage, 2HKO Slowbro with Grass Knot, and it can OHKO Entei after minimal chip. The Speed investment allows Empoleon to outspeed Adamant Crawdaunt and Golurk. Tera Fairy flips its Fighting weakness into a resistance while also making Electric- and Ground-type attacks neutral, allowing Empoleon to stay in against Krookodile and Flygon if needed.

Offensive Empoleon fits on balance and bulky offense teams, as it pivots into many of the special attackers in the tier and provides an immediate offensive response. Strong Fighting- and Ground-types like Rhyperior, Gallade, and Krookodile appreciate Empoleon switching into Fairy- and Water-type attacks, namely from Basculegion-F and Gardevoir. Offensive Empoleon fits well on teams that can use alternative entry hazard setters like Jirachi so that it can maximize its offensive presence. Noivern can switch into to Ground- and Fighting-type attacks while removing entry hazards and pivoting. Magnet Pull Magnezone can partner with Empoleon to trap and eliminate Steel-type Pokemon like opposing Empoleon and Jirachi, two of the better defensive checks to offensive Empoleon. Sticky Web Ribombee can partner with and enable offensive Empoleon, as it outspeeds Magnezone, Breloom, and Bisharp after they get slowed down.

Specially Defensive.description:
Specially defensive Empoleon is among the best utility Pokemon in the metagame for its capacity to counter most special attackers, establish entry hazards, remove items, and phaze setup attempts. Roost allows Empoleon to remain healthy enough to switch in against the strong special attackers like Basculegion-F, Gardevoir, and Gengar multiple times throughout a game. Flip Turn can be used to gain switch momentum after switching into an attack, allowing teammates to position into whatever enters the field against Empoleon. Knock Off provides excellent utility in the form of item removal, namely Heavy-Duty Boots, allowing entry hazard damage to rack up as Empoleon forces multiple switches by absorbing attacks. Roar provides similar utility in accruing entry hazard damage while stopping setup attempts from the likes of Calm Mind Cresselia, Slowbro, and Reuniclus. Ice Beam gives Empoleon coverage to hit the Grass- and Dragon-types in the tier like Chesnaught, Cyclizar, and Noivern. Leftovers ensures Empoleon can recover off damage taken from entry hazards and switching into special attackers. Competitive gives Empoleon a needed Special Attack boost when activated by Moonblast drops from Cresselia and Gardevoir, Intimidate from Krookodile, and Defog from Noivern, making even bulky utility sets capable of outputting good damage. Being a Defog deterrent gives Empoleon an advantage in maintaining hazards, as the notable Defog users often struggle to deal with its coverage, especially after a boost from Competitive. A Calm nature with full investment in HP and Special Defense makes Empoleon seemingly impervious to damage from special attacks. Tera Fairy flips the critical weakness to Fighting into a resistance, allowing it to not be as threatened by the likes of Chesnaught, Flamigo, Gallade, and Terrakion, while also flipping the Ground weakness into neutrality, making Krookodile and Flygon much less imposing. Tera Ghost similarly helps with the litany of Fighting-types prevalent in the metagame and gives Empoleon a valuable immunity to Rapid Spin attempts from the primary form of removal in Cyclizar.

Empoleon is a staple on balance and bulky offense teams needing to shore up their matchups into the strong special attackers in the tier, a stalwart Steel-type that can establish entry hazards, and another form of item removal or phazing. With access to Roost, Empoleon has instant and reliable recovery, unlike other Steel-types like Jirachi and Hisuian Goodra. Choice Scarf Basculegion-F, Gardevoir, and Gengar pose many problems for Fighting-type breakers like Gallade, Terrakion, and Flamigo, making Empoleon an excellent choice to support them through defensive switch-ins and subsequent pivots with Flip Turn. Physically defensive teammates that can absorb Fighting- and Ground-type attacks from Krookodile, Flamigo, and Terrakion like Noivern, Cresselia and Chesnaught are excellent in creating cores that can cause issues for opposing teams, accumulating entry hazard damage and whittling teams down. Chesnaught benefits from Empoleon handling the main forms of removal in the metagame, such as Cyclizar with Ice Beam and Noivern due to Competitive, forming a strong defensive pairing that can remove Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off and rack up hazard chip. Slower teammates such as Rhyperior and Crawdaunt that appreciate Empoleon's ability to sponge special attacks and safely pivot into them can assist in removing items and breaking teams through forcing multiple switches and hitting very hard into Empoleon checks like Cyclizar, Hisuian Goodra, and Jirachi. The combination of Water and Steel gives Empoleon favorable matchups into rain abusers like Basculegion-F and Kingdra, making physically defensive teammates like Amoonguss, Bellibolt, and Chesnaught, which also functions as a Knock Off absorber for Empoleon, valuable for their ability to switch into Barraskewda. Empoleon can gradually get worn down by hazard chip itself, making teammates that can pivot and maintain hazard control like Cyclizar and Noivern excellent partners.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Empoleon can also run Flip Turn to maintain momentum and keep the opponent in a vortex of switching and entry hazard chip damage, but Empoleon struggles to replace any of its moves with Flip Turn. Surf Empoleon can run 60 Speed EVs to outspeed uninvested Corviknight, making it more dangerous for Corviknight to try to clear hazards. Empoleon can run Leftovers instead of Heavy-Duty Boots if it is paired with hazard removal, enhancing its natural bulk. If not running Knock Off or Flip Turn, it is optimal for Empoleon to run 0 Attack IVs.

Specially Defensive (Water).description:
Empoleon's unique defensive typing makes it valuable to Water teams, providing an answer to threats that are difficult to deal with like Kyurem, Flutter Mane, and Articuno. It also has an excellent toolkit for winning games with entry hazards, through the combination of Stealth Rock and either Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots or Roar to rack up hazard damage on whatever gets dragged in, as well as Competitive threatening to turn it into a powerful offensive threat if the foe uses Defog. Flash Cannon makes Empoleon better at threatening the aforementioned Ice- and Fairy-types, whereas Surf allows it to punish Corviknight attempting to use Defog. Roar allows Empoleon to put a stop to special sweepers like Spectrier and Sinistcha; however, Knock Off allows Empoleon to mitigate Pokemon that depend on their item like Kyurem, Corviknight, and Hisuian Goodra. Empoleon doesn't struggle to set Stealth Rock in the crucial Flying matchup, like Water's other setters, because it can set them on Articuno.

As a special wall, Empoleon wants to be part of a defensive core with physical walls and special walls that fill the gaps in Empoleon's coverage, including Toxapex, Alomomola, and Gastrodon. Toxapex's Toxic Spikes make Empoleon's Roar far more dangerous, and Toxic puts a timer on the opposing Pokemon, meaning Pokemon like Primarina and Volcarona don’t have enough turns to boost past Empoleon; this is otherwise a major weakness of non-Roar sets. Empoleon can switch in on Psychic-type moves targeting Toxapex, while Toxapex can switch in on Fighting-type moves targeting Empoleon, as well as a range of powerful physical attackers like Choice Band Meowscarada and Ceruledge. Alomomola can Wish pass to keep Empoleon from being worn down by the barrage of Choice Specs-boosted special attacks that it gets thrown into from Flutter Mane, Kyurem, Dragapult, and the like. Specially defensive Alomomola also takes pressure off of Empoleon by switching into special attacks and healing off the damage with Regenerator, allowing Empoleon to conserve its health for the most threatening special attackers, and it switches well into Choice Scarf Landorus's Earth Power that Empoleon is unable to help with. Empoleon appreciates Gastrodon setting Spikes, forming a strong entry hazard stacking core, and Gastrodon protects Empoleon from having its Heavy-Duty Boots removed with Sticky Hold and switches into the Electric-type moves that Empoleon struggles with. Similarly, Empoleon appreciates Hisuian Samurott's effectiveness in getting up Spikes with Ceaseless Edge. Empoleon is mostly useless in the Ground matchup, and this weakness is pronounced because it is almost always paired with Toxapex, which is also unhelpful into Ground. As such, Empoleon appreciates partners that can pick up its slack in the Ground matchup, such as Choice Specs Greninja, Suicune, Ogerpon-W, and Manaphy. Choice Specs Greninja is an excellent complement for the bulky Water teams Empoleon usually resides on, being able to stop sweeps by Pokemon like the Ogerpon formes, Gholdengo and Pecharunt in their tracks. Manaphy can break the Steel and Flying teams that Empoleon struggles to make progress against while appreciating Empoleon switching into Grass-type moves or powerful neutral hits from would-be revenge killers such as Iron Moth and Latios.

Stealth Rock Support.description:
• Empoleon's fantastic typing and good movepool make it a great choice for a specially defensive Stealth Rock setter.

  • Yawn versus Roar: Yawn has fantastic synergy with Stealth Rock, forcing foes to either take damage or be put to Sleep. Roar is more reliant on Stealth Rock being set up first, but it isn't as vulnerable to common Substitute foes like Iron Bundle.

  • Flash Cannon versus Ice Beam: Flash Cannon is the preferred STAB move for dealing good damage to Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle. Ice Beam is still worth considering for dealing far more damage to Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Gliscor though.

  • Flip Turn versus Surf: Flip Turn makes Empoleon a good pivot despite its low damage output, though Surf is still a reasonable alternative for doing good damage against Ground-types.

  • Roost: Despite Empoleon's good defensive profile, Roost can be hard to fit in since it means either giving up support or coverage. Still, it does make Empoleon a better check with Flutter Mane when paired with Flash Cannon.

  • Calm versus Sassy: In addition to making Flip Turn stronger, Sassy's lower Speed can help Empoleon pivot out last. However, Sassy forces a Speed tie with 4 Speed EV Ursaluna-B unless 20 Speed EVs are used. If the power drop isn't an issue, a Calm nature with a Speed IV of 17 can be used to reach the same Speed.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Empoleon's superb typing means Terastallization should only be used to flip certain troublesome match-ups.

  • Flying: Tera Flying floats above common Ground-types such as Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Ursaluna-B, and it additionally grants an important Fighting-type resistance.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is a good response against Fighting-types like Urshifu while making Electric-types such as Zapdos and Vikavolt less problematic.

  • Grass: In addition to a Ground-type resistance (though this can be risky against Landorus-T), Tera Grass saves Empoleon from Breloom's Spore.

  • Bug: Bug isn't normally a great defensive type, but the resistances to Fighting and Ground, combined with not being weak to Electric, makes it a viable choice on Empoleon.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is the most reliable healing item, especially when getting free turns with Yawn.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's quick burst of recovery is a decent alternative to Leftovers. Make sure to use 244 HP EVs with it so it activates after getting hit by Ting-Lu's Ruination.

  • Air Balloon: Empoleon is an especially effective user of Air Balloon with its offensive advantages against Ground-types, doing especially well against Gliscor thanks to Empoleon's Toxic immunity.

Assault Vest.description:
• Empoleon's vital advantages against Fairy-types and good Special Attack make it a fantastic Assault Vest tank.

  • Surf: Surf is a reliable secondary STAB move that's particularly good against Ursaluna-B.

  • Ice Beam versus Grass Knot: Ice Beam has a multitude of high value targets, such as Dragonite, Garchomp, Landorus-T, and Gliscor. Grass Knot's coverage is less impressive, but it prevents Empoleon from being totally walled by bulky Water-types like Dondozo and Milotic.

  • Flip Turn: Flip Turn will require giving up coverage or priority, but Empoleon is a bulky enough pivot to justify it.

  • Vacuum Wave: While not being a strong priority move, Vacuum Wave is great for picking off weakened threats, especially Chien-Pao.

  • Competitive versus Torrent: Competitive is the most reliable option for checking Flutter Mane, punishing Charm variants and ensuring that Special Attack drops from Moonblast turn into an advantage. Torrent can make some sense with Tera Water though, making Surf very difficult to switch into.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Empoleon relies on its excellent typing to be a great Assault Vest tank, but its lack of recovery means Terastallazation can still be important for flipping certain match-ups.

  • Water: Tera Water vastly improves Empoleon's match-up against common Ground-types like Ursaluna-B and Landorus-T, removing the Earthquake / Earth Power weakness and having a powerful Surf.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is a great response against Fighting-types like Urshifu and also lets Empoleon tank Electric-types like Zapdos and Vikavolt more reliably.

  • Flying: Tera Flying's Ground-type immunity is perfect for saving it from sweepers like Garchomp and Landorus-T, and it additionally removes grievances with Dondozo's Fissure.

  • Grass: Tera Grass protects Empoleon from Breloom's Spore and makes Grass Knot more desirable.

Specially Defensive (Water).description: Empoleon is one of Water's best options for role compression thanks to its wide array of utility options. Furthermore, its great special bulk coupled with a great defensive typing allows it to easily shrug off hits from some of the biggest threats to Water teams such as Tapu Lele and Kyurem. Defog removes entry hazards, allowing its teammates to switch in more safely, and it also removes opponents' dual screens to ease the Fairy matchup. Alternatively, Empoleon can run Stealth Rock to wear down foes over time to aid its offensive partners. Flash Cannon targets Fairy-types such as Mega Diancie and Tapu Lele. Knock Off targets Ghost- and Psychic-types like Hisuian Zoroark and Jirachi while removing items from foes that rely on them like Rotom-W and Corviknight. Alternatively, Flip Turn allows Empoleon to take advantage of its low Speed by acting as a slow pivot to bring its teammates in safely. Pelipper pairs well with Empoleon, as the two of them form a pivoting core, and it appreciates Empoleon taking on Tapu Lele and Kyurem. In return, Pelipper can run Defog so that Empoleon can choose to run Stealth Rock instead. Rain-boosted sweepers like Mega Swampert and Barraskewda appreciate Empoleon taking on Kyurem's Freeze-Dry and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, respectively, and in return, it provides an Electric immunity and can sweep under rain. Urshifu-R and Keldeo appreciate Empoleon setting up Stealth Rock and challenging Fairy-types; in return, the two of them challenge Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Hisuian Goodra. Choice Specs Greninja, with its great coverage, handles a myriad of threats to Empoleon such as non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, Great Tusk, and the Landorus formes, and it appreciates Defog and Stealth Rock support in return. Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott can stack Spikes with Ceaseless Edge, and it takes on Ghost- and Psychic-types if Empoleon forgoes Knock Off. Ogerpon-W's Ground-resistant typing allows it to deal with the likes of the Landorus formes, Great Tusk, and Mamoswine in the Ground matchup.

Utility.description: 76 Defense EVs let Empoleon avoid an OHKO from Cobalion's Close Combat.

nu.overview: Staraptor lands itself a niche in NU thanks to its high Attack and Speed stats, which can be further boosted with either Choice Band or Choice Scarf. Choice Band paired with Reckless lets Staraptor do major damage towalls like Galarian Slowbro and Overqwil while putting pressure on resistant foes such as Klefki and Bronzong. On the other hand, Choice Scarf lets it outpace threats like Kilowattrel, Flamigo, and Inteleon. Staraptor fits on many balance teams thanks to its ability to handle common defensive cores of Amoonguss, Vaporeon, and Wo-Chien. Despite its strengths, Staraptor is outclassed by Flamigo in almost every aspect as a Flying-type Choice Scarf user, as Flamigo isn't weak to Stealth Rock and has a more useful secondary typing in Fighting, which allows it to hit Steel-types much more effectively. Staraptor is held back by its weakness to Stealth Rock, which, alongside recoil from its STAB moves, hurts its longevity greatly. It is also held back by its struggles to break commonplace defensive Pokemon such as Galarian Slowbro, Avalugg, Bellibolt, and Duraludon thanks to their natural bulk. Staraptor's competition as a Choice Scarf user is fierce, as Munkidori and Flamigo both provide a similar Speed tier while not needing to use recoil inflicting moves, which allows them to last longer in games more effectively and still do large amounts of damage. There are other naturally fast, offensive Flying-types like Kilowattrel and Tornadus that Staraptor competes with, and both of them have much better coverage options, which further discredits using Staraptor.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Choice Scarf, along with Starptor's high Speed tier, makes it an excellent user of Final Gambit, allowing it to grab surprise KOs and deal solid damage to foes like Flygon and Bronzong and letting its teammates benefit at the cost of losing Staraptor itself.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Staraptor is threatened by fast Electric-types like Kilowattrel and Raikoun as they can outspeed and threaten to KO it with their STAB moves; however, Staraptor can surprise KO them if it is using Choice Scarf. Bellibolt is also threatening, as it punishes Staraptor's moves with Rocky Helmet chip damage and the risk of paralysis from Static. None of these Pokemon can switch into Staraptor's Choice Band attacks without being 2HKOed at best, however.

Stealth Rock: Staraptor's reliance on Choice items makes it threatened by Stealth Rock. Furthermore, Staraptor consistently switching in and out can make this worse, since Stealth Rock greatly limits Staraptor's longevity and its ability to repeatedly enter the field.

Physical Walls: Physical walls like Galarian Slowbro, Rhyperior, and Avalugg can all take hits from Staraptor and threaten it back with their own attacks, and the former also threatens it with status. Due to Staraptor's raw power, these walls do not enjoy switching into its attacks directly though.

Steel-types: Steel-types like Klefki, Duraludon, Bronzong, and Copperajah resist Staraptor's STAB attacks, so they can freely switch into them and either set up entry hazards or hit back against Staraptor with their own attacks. Staraptor can use Close Combat though, which threatens all the aforementioned Steel-types with heavy damage.

Revenge Killers: One of Staraptor's largest threats comes from faster Pokemon that are able to revenge kill it, such as Inteleon, Kilowattrel, and Alolan Ninetales; however, none of these can switch into Staraptor's attacks safely. Faster Choice Scarf users like Infernape and Munkidori can threaten and KO Staraptor once it gets worn down, but they also cannot risk switching into its attacks. Staraptor can also be picked off by strong priority users like Choice Band Paldean Tauros-W, Toxicroak, and Arcanine.

Choice Attacker.description:
Set Details

Quick Attack allows Staraptor to pick off weakened Pokemon like Flygon and Munkidori, while Double-Edge can be used to 2HKO foes like Galarian Slowbro and Swampert. Close Combat allows Staraptor to hit Steel-types such as Bronzong, Klefki, and Copperajah. U-turn lets Staraptor capitalize on switch-ins such as Bronzong and Diancie by wearing them down. Choice Band can put huge dents into walls such as Altaria and Klefki, making them very limited in how often they can switch into an attack, whereas Choice Scarf makes Staraptor capable of outpacing threats like Flamigo and Kilowattrel. Tera Flying lets Brave Bird OHKO Basculegion-M and Munkidori. On the other hand, Tera Normal makes Quick Attack a stronger priority option, allows Double-Edge 2HKO Gligar, and removes Staraptor's Stealth Rock weakness. Tera Fighting provides some defensive value by giving Staraptor a resistance to Stealth Rock and a resistance to Dark-type moves from foes like Scrafty and Incineroar.

Staraptor alone can struggle to break physically defensive Pokemon such as Bellibolt, Duraludon, and Galarian Slowbro. Partners such as Chandelure, Flygon, and Toxtricity can effectively break through them and appreciate Staraptor's U-turn support. Staraptor also benefits from other fast pivots like Inteleon, Kilowattrel, and Munkidori by chipping down their checks such as Incineroar and Bronzong and allowing them to potentially KO them. Slower pivots like Incineroar, Bellibolt, and Swampert give it free entry to capitalize on switch-ins such as Heracross, Wo-Chien and Amoonguss. Furthermore, Staraptor enjoys being partnered with entry hazard removal Pokemon like Tsareena, Avalugg, and Altaria to maximize its longevity. Tsareena in particular is a useful partner, as its Knock Off is especially helpful for Staraptor to break Steel-types.

Kamikaze (Normal).description:
Choice Scarf Staraptor provides hyper-offensive Normal teams a way to deal with fast threats like non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, Ogerpon-W, and Choice Specs Greninja and momentum in U-turn and Final Gambit. Close Combat complements Brave Bird because it thrashes Steel-types, OHKOing Bisharp and threatening Iron Treads and Heatran with a 2HKO. Final Gambit, boosted by 28 HP EVs, OHKOes targets Staraptor wouldn't otherwise beat, such as Toxapex, Hatterene, Klefki, and Skarmory after Stealth Rock damage—denying potential dual screens and entry hazards. Finally, U-turn allows this reckless bird to pivot into a teammate that better handles switch-ins such as against Gholdengo or Corviknight. Equipping a Choice Scarf will let it outspeed Greninja, Flutter Mane, and Darkrai, which otherwise force it out, and threaten them instead.

A great partner for Staraptor is Hisuian Zoroark. When it uses Illusion to disguise as Staraptor, pairing its Fighting immunity with Staraptor's Ground immunity could make an apparent "Staraptor" immune to either type. Disguised as Staraptor, Hisuian Zoroark can bait in an unsuspecting Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Archaludon to cripple or OHKO it. Making good use of Staraptor's U-turn, Ditto is a teammate that can turn a bleak situation into a winning one, copying setup sweepers such as Dragonite and Spectrier to reverse sweep opponents. Terapagos provides a one-time check to threats like Unburden Sneasler, Choice Scarf Meowscarada, and Sand Rush Excadrill, which all outpace Staraptor. In return, Staraptor takes out Klefki and pivots Terapagos into Archaludon and Skarmory, both of which check Staraptor. Swords Dance Ursaluna crushes bulky walls like Assault Vest Iron Hands, Porygon2, and Archaludon that Staraptor struggles with. In return, Staraptor deals with fast threats that can OHKO Ursaluna like Greninja and pivot it in against the aforementioned walls. Smeargle provides entry hazards with Sticky Web and Stone Axe, allowing Staraptor to outspeed and remove Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Roaring Moon. Cinccino can use a Choice Band set to deal with Primarina or use Tidy Up to clean up weakened Fairy, Flying, and Water teams after Staraptor has removed Klefki, Skarmory, or Toxapex. Maushold is another great partner thanks to Tidy Up, which keeps both Stealth Rock and Reflect off the field for Staraptor to not worry about. Also, its Population Bomb can break through Ting-Lu and non-Rocky Helmet Toxapex for Staraptor. Indeedee likewise offers offensive support in the form of Healing Wish while checking physically bulky walls like Toxapex and Pecharunt that Staraptor struggles with.

Physically Defensive (Normal).description: As a switch-in to Fighting-types that compresses utility to support its team, Staraptor is a common part of defensive cores in Normal teams. Brave Bird lets Staraptor apply offensive pressure on Fighting-types such as Breloom and Mega Lopunny. Close Combat complements its coverage to hit Flying-resistant foes including Excadrill, Heatran, and Empoleon, discouraging the latter two from keeping Stealth Rock on it; alternatively, U-turn provides utility to more safely bring in allies such as Ditto, Hisuian Zoroark, and Mega Lopunny. The given EV spread lets it outspeed Adamant Tapu Bulu, with the rest being invested in physical bulk to ease handling foes including Mega Scizor, Dragonite, and Mega Pinsir. Chansey and Blissey's high special bulk lets them comfortably check a wide variety of special attackers that Staraptor can't handle such as Zapdos, Nihilego, and Nidoking, making a good defensive core that includes Ditto benefiting from the safe entry provided by Staraptor to minimize their potential passivity against setup sweepers. Mega Lopunny and Ursaluna can act as offensive pressure for opposing Rock-types, which Staraptor can't properly handle. Hisuian Zoroark benefits from Staraptor's entry hazard control to better bluff as another ally with Illusion, with Staraptor supporting it by checking Fighting-types in return.

Defensive.description: 136 Speed EVs let Roserade outspeed Adamant Tapu Bulu.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Cranidos is a second-rate revenge-killer with a massive Attack stat. Cranidos threatens to 2HKO the entire tier with its coverage, notably Zen Headbutt for the Poison-types and Mienfoo, Fire Punch for Tinkatink and Alolan Sandshrew, either Rock Slide or Head Smash for Vullaby and general damage, and Trailblaze for Mudbray. Choice Scarf makes Cranidos prediction reliant in order to land these 2HKOs. Head Smash is used over Rock Slide for greater damage, at a detriment to accuracy. Cranidos runs Jolly and maximum Speed investment to Speed tie with Choice Scarf Hisuian Growlithe and Choice Scarf Vullaby. Tera Psychic Zen Headbutt threatens to OHKO fast Mienfoo, while Tera Grass Trailblaze 2HKOs Impish Mudbray.

Cranidos is used on bulkier Tinkatink, Toedscool, and Mareanie teams, as they have a broader defensive profile to switch in after Cranidos finishes off a Pokemon or whiffs. Cranidos outspeeds and threatens the Pokemon that break the Tinkatink, Toedscool, Mareanie core, like Elekid and Chinchou. Cranidos is weak to Mudbray teams and slow or Scarf Mienfoo, especially when used together. Toedscool makes the Mudbray matchup much easier. Cranidos is also weak to entry hazard and recoil damage.

Choice Band.description:
Floatzel is a niche but threatening wallbreaker and pivot thanks to its good Attack, amazing Speed, and STAB Flip Turn, escaping its problematic matchups against Milotic, Amoonguss, Goodra, and Qwilfish; it finds use over the more common Bruxish thanks to its higher Speed. Aqua Jet allows Floatzel to revenge kill faster threats like Salazzle, +1 Speed Paldean Tauros-F, and +2 Speed Rhydon. Ice Spinner targets Grass-types such as Hisuian Decidueye and Venusaur. Tera Water boosts Wave Crash to the point where it OHKOes bulky Florges and 2HKOes Dudunsparce, and it lets Aqua Jet reliably OHKO Salazzle.

Floatzel generally is used on balance and offense teams needing good speed control and consistent offensive pressure. On these teams, it forms powerful VoltTurn cores with Pokemon like Alolan Persian, Uxie, and Rotom-H. Floatzel is relatively frail and quickly worn down by residual damage and Wave Crash recoil, so it appreciates having entry hazard control from Pokemon such as Hisuian Decidueye, Espeon, and Alolan Sandslash. Floatzel also appreciates having entry hazards of its own from partners like Rhydon, Mudsdale, and Qwilfish to help wear down Floatzel's few good switch-ins such as Milotic, Goodra, and Lanturn. In return, Floatzel can help these partners pivot onto the battlefield safely with Flip Turn and deal with faster threats that threaten them such as Hisuian Decidueye, Alolan Ninetales, and Paldean Tauros-F.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
With Paradox Pokemon being introduced, Series 2 is bringing big changes to Battle Stadium Singles! This is a modified Series 1 analysis that takes Paradox Pokemon into account. We will update this overview and analysis again once the metagame settles more. For more information on Series 2, check out the resource thread.

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Swift Weasel.description:
• Wave Crash: This is your main offensive option. When further boosted by rain, Tera Water, and Choice Band, it becomes one of the most powerful physical moves in the game, 2HKOing the likes of Bold Amoonguss and OHKOing maximum Defense Corviknight. Mystic Water is an option for flexibility but sacrifices the listed KOs.

  • Liquidation versus Waterfall: Liquidation is a secondary option, and it's preferred when facing frailer offensive teams due to the significant recoil drawback of Wave Crash. However, Waterfall is worth considering for its possible flinch chance.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet allows Floatzel to maintain offensive presence outside of rain, as well as being a great response to opposing priority moves, such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch.

  • Rain Setter: Pelipper's rain is mandatory for both Swift Swim and maximum damage output.

Tera Types

  • Water: Tera Water massively bolters Floatzel's damage output, and the weasel simply doesn't have the bulk needed for more defensive options.

EV Spreads

  • 60 HP / 252 Atk / 196 Spe:196 Speed EVs are used to outspeed the entire tier in rain, including Choice Scarf Dragpault.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe: Maximum Speed investment outspeeds Hydreigon and Mimikyu outside of rain, in addition to tying with Salamence, at the cost of having less buffer HP for Wave Crash recoil.

Defensive.description:
Shellos is a solid entry hazard setter with its high defenses and its ability Sticky Hold, which allows it to always keep its Eviolite. With its bulk and access to Recover, Shellos can reliably set up Stealth Rock in front of powerful threats like Hisuian Growlithe and Alolan Diglett. Although it's mainly defensive, Shellos's Ground- and Ice-type coverage is a potent offensive combo, as no type resists both. Earth Power hits Steel-types like Tinkatink and Alolan Sandshrew, Electric-types like Chinchou and Elekid, and Rock-types like Glimmet and Hisuian Growlithe for super effective damage, while Ice Beam threatens foes such as Vullaby, Toedscool, and Mudbray. This EV spread maximizes Shellos's bulk, allowing it to sponge multiple hits and regain health via Recover. The added bulk prevents 2HKOs from Vullaby, Alolan Diglett, and Stunky as well as OHKOs from Wingull. Tera Poison is good defensively—it lets Shellos resist Mienfoo's High Jump Kick, Stunky's Gunk Shot, and both of Foongus's STAB moves. It can also prevent Shellos from being poisoned, increasing its longevity.

Shellos's passivity makes it fits best on balance structures where it can use its bulk to repeatedly switch in and outlast threats such as Vullaby, Alolan Sandshrew, Alolan Diglett, and Hisuian Growlithe. It can also beat Rapid Spin users, helping keep Stealth Rock up, which benefits VoltTurn users such as Mienfoo, Elekid, and Vullaby. Shellos supports frail, offensive wallbreakers like Alolan Diglett and Hisuian Growlithe, since it soft checks most of the metagame. Additionally, Stealth Rock can provide extra chip for them to secure KOs. Shellos can be weak to hazards, so it appreciates Rapid Spin users such as Toedscool and Alolan Sandshrew. In return, Shellos checks threats such as Hisuian Growlithe and Vullaby. Foongus is another hard matchup, so teammates like Elekid, Gothita, and your own Foongus can be helpful.

ru.overview: Gastrodon holds a place as one of the premier defensive Spikes setters in the tier. Its good natural bulk, coupled with a fantastic defensive typing that renders it weak only to a rare offensive type in the metagame, ensures that it can be very difficult to take down. Sticky Hold provides Gastrodon with further utility as one of the best Knock Off absorbers available, improving its matchup against Rapid Spin Cyclizar, which is the most common Pokemon in the tier. However, Gastrodon's mediocre attacking stats and lack of status spreading and disruption moves mean that it often struggles to punish setup sweepers like Calm Mind Slowbro and Suicune for staying in. Despite Gastrodon's high HP stat, its low Defense stat leads to strong physical wallbreakers such as Kleavor, Golurk, and Crawdaunt often being able to take it down. Lastly, its Water / Ground typing's sole weakness comes into play as a vulnerability to Grass-type coverage attacks, including Trailblaze from Kleavor and Entei, and Grass Knot from Empoleon.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Gastrodon has the ability to set Stealth Rock on teams that lack other entry hazard setters; however, this is not optimal, as Gastrodon becomes passive after just one turn of setting up Stealth Rock, which can allow bulky wallbreakers and sweepers such as Basculegion-F and Calm Mind Slowbro to exploit it without fear of it setting up more hazards. Sludge Bomb is a decent coverage option over Ice Beam that similarly hits Grass-types like Wo-Chien while possessing a useful chance to spread poison. Clear Smog is an option that can mitigate Gastrodon's general weakness to setup sweepers, though it can be neutralized by Covert Cloak or Substitute. Leftovers is an alternative defensive item that can improve Gastrodon's longevity. Covert Cloak can also be used to prevent Gastrodon from being affected by moves like Slowbro's Scald and Reuniclus's Psychic Noise.

Checks and Counters

Calm Mind Sweepers: Bulky Calm Mind sweepers like Slowbro, Suicune, and Reuniclus take little damage from Gastrodon's attacks and can exploit it as setup fodder.

Grass-type Attacks: While there is a lack of offensive Grass-type Pokemon in RU, Breloom and certain special attackers with Grass-type coverage, such as Trailblaze Kleavor and Entei, Energy Ball Reuniclus, Grass Knot Empoleon, and Giga Drain Yanmega, can threaten Gastrodon with significant damage. While an uncommon option, some Mimikyu opt for Wood Hammer which OHKOs Quagsire.

Powerful Physical Wallbreakers: The strongest physical wallbreakers in the tier, like Krookodile, Gallade, and Crawdaunt, can threaten Gastrodon with massive damage, while they themselves don't fear staying in due to Gastrodon's weak offenses and lack of status moves.

Defensive.description:
Set Details

Spikes is Gastrodon's main tool for making progress and chipping away at the opposing team's health. Earthquake is used over Earth Power to deal more damage to common specially defensive Pokemon like Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and Assault Vest Cyclizar. Ice Beam is very useful coverage that targets Flying-, Dragon-, and Grass-type Pokemon that can switch in on Earthquake like Noivern, Flygon, and Chesnaught. Rocky Helmet punishes weak attacks from Pokemon like Cyclizar, Jirachi, and Chesnaught while pairing well with Sticky Hold. Heavy-Duty Boots can help keep Gastrodon healthy on teams lacking reliable entry hazard control. Sticky Hold is the preferred ability, as it enables Gastrodon to act as a Knock Off absorber at little cost to itself, with the additional utility of blocking Trick from Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Jirachi. Storm Drain alternatively lets Gastrodon answer threatening Water-types, like Empoleon and Basculegion-F. Tera Ghost provides Gastrodon with invaluable immunities to strong Fighting- and Normal-type attacks, including Terrakion's Close Combat, Maushold's Population Bomb, and Toxtricity's Boomburst, and allows it to spinblock Cyclizar. However, Tera Ghost Gastrodon's weakness to Knock Off from attackers like Krookodile and Crawdaunt can be very detrimental to it, especially if Sticky Hold is used, as Knock Off's power will always be boosted. Tera Poison is an alternative that provides Gastrodon with an immunity to Toxic from Umbreon and Poison Touch Alolan Muk, flips its weakness to Grass-type attacks like Giga Drain from Amoonguss, and offers resistances to Fighting-, Bug-, and Fairy-type attacks from offensive threats such as Yanmega and Mimikyu.

Gastrodon fits best on balance teams that rely on stacking entry hazards to overwhelm the opposing team. Stealth Rock setters such as Jirachi, Registeel, and Krookodile are therefore important partners for Gastrodon. Knock Off users such as Cyclizar, Krookodile, and Wo-Chien can further the hazard stacking gameplan by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from defensive Pokemon like Slowbro and Quagsire. Late-game cleaners, including the likes of Entei, Choice Scarf Gardevoir, and Choice Scarf Krookodile, can operate well in these teams, as they can eliminate many of the common Pokemon in the metagame after marginal chip damage from hazards. Gastrodon's vulnerability to special setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Slowbro, Suicune, and Reuniclus necessitates the presence of Pokemon with access to disruption moves like Encore Jirachi, Taunt Noivern, and Trick + Choice Scarf Gardevoir that can prevent these sweepers from winning the game outright.

Physically Defensive.description: Gastrodon's typing, serviceable bulk, and broad range of utility moves make it a sturdy defensive anchor against top metagame threats such as Iron Moth, Iron Boulder, and Mega Aerodactyl. Spikes and Stealth Rock take advantage of Gastrodon's ability to threaten Excadrill and Rotom-W, two of the most common forms of hazard control. Clear Smog deters any setup from sweepers immune to status like Calm Mind Clefable. Toxic prevents Pokemon such as Hydrapple, Hydreigon, and Mega Latias, which can take Gastrodon's STAB moves, from freely taking advantage of it. Scald's ability to spread burn gives it a chance to punish any attempt at setup or entry from Pokemon such as Azumarill, Scizor, and Mega Venusaur; with the alternatives of Earthquake and Earth Power having the ability to immediately threaten Iron Moth and Aegislash. Said options can also break potential Substitutes from Pokemon such as Aegislash, Keldeo, and Mega Gardevoir, which Scald cannot do. Recover allows Gastrodon to be a more consistent answer to U-turn Iron Moth and Tyranitar. Heavy-Duty Boots prevents entry hazard damage that may disrupt Gastrodon's ability to safely take attacks. Leftovers ensures that Gastrodon does not have to recover every bit of damage it takes when attempting to pivot in on weaker moves, making it a useful alternative on teams with reliable entry hazard removal. Maximum HP and Defense EVs give Gastrodon the physical bulk to take on threats like Iron Boulder, Mega Aerodactyl, and Choice Band Tyranitar. Gastrodon fits well onto balance and hazard-stacking teams, with its ability to check threats such as Victini, Iron Boulder, and Keldeo and stop Volt Switch momentum from Rotom-W and Zeraora. Specially defensive Pokemon like Slowking, Blissey, and Amoonguss work well with Gastrodon, answering Pokemon that threaten it like Choice Specs Greninja, Serperior, and Alakazam. Celesteela in particular is a good partner, covering Gastrodon's weakness to Grass-types like Mega Venusaur, Amoonguss, and Hydrapple while benefiting from Gastrodon's Electric immunity and resistance to Fire-type moves in return. Stealth Rock users like Clefable and Skarmory enjoy Gastrodon's ability to stack Spikes. Gastrodon's inability to check Energy Ball Iron Moth means it appreciates Booster Iron Moth checks like Mega Aerodactyl and Mega Latias, which in turn enjoy the entry hazards set by Gastrodon. Win conditions and wallbreakers like Swords Dance Aegislash, Calm Mind Reuniclus and Keldeo, and Stallbreaker Enamorus relish in Gastrodon's profile of resistances, ability to lure in and potentially punish Grass-type Pokemon with status, and its tendency to be able to set entry hazards multiple times a game.

monotype.overview:
Ground

Unlike the alternative Water-type immune option on Ground teams, Clodsire, Gastrodon is extremely weak to Grass-type moves from the likes of Meowscarada and Ogerpon formes; it also has inferior bulk and an arguably worse ability as opposed to Clodsire's Water Absorb. However, Gastrodon boasts a niche in beating Water-type Pokemon like Greninja and Barraskewda due to its neutrality to Ice Beam and Psychic Fangs, respectively, as well as its neutrality to Ground-type moves.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ground

Eject Button may be used for Gastrodon to act as a pivot for threatening teammates such as Excadrill and Landorus; however, Gastrodon misses out on the defensive utility from its recommended held items.

Water

Clear Smog helps Gastrodon stop Primarina, which can otherwise set up easily on it. Storm Drain has some utility at blocking certain Pokemon, notably Rotom-W variants with just Hydro Pump and Discharge along with Calm Mind Primarin using Surf into Gastrodon. However, this makes Gastrodon weak to Trick and Knock Off from the likes of Iron Valiant, Gholdengo, and Alolan Muk.

The Slug (Ground).description:
Gastrodon's great bulk, typing, and ability allow it to function as a sturdy mixed wall and check to Water-types such as Greninja, Urshifu-S, and Barraskewda. Earth Power targets Gholdengo and Archaludon, while Earthquake deals more damage to Hisuian Goodra, Clodsire, Flutter Mane, and Calm Mind Keldeo. Ice Beam hits Dragon-types like Dragonite and Garchomp while also preventing Landorus-T and Gliscor from using Gastrodon as setup fodder. Furthermore, Ice Beam can pop Air Balloon on common users such as Gholdengo, Heatran, Raging Bolt, and Iron Treads to let Gastrodon threaten them with Ground-type coverage. Clear Smog may be used to prevent Primarina and Keldeo from setting up. Stealth Rock and Spikes are interchangeable depending on what teammates like Ting-Lu, Hippowdon, and Gliscor opt for. Gastrodon prefers maximum Defense investment to check aforementioned Pokemon like Barraskewda and Urshifu-S as well as Keldeo's Secret Sword; however, an EV spread of 252 HP / 156 Def / 100 SpD with a Calm nature can be used to prevent a 2HKO from Choice Specs users such as Greninja and Kingdra with their Ice Beam and Dragon Pulse, respectively, at the cost of getting 2HKOed by Barraskewda's Close Combat.

Gastrodon's immunity to Water-type attacks and ability to set entry hazards is heavily appreciated by Great Tusk, Landorus, and Mamoswine. In return, Choice Scarf Great Tusk outpaces and deals with threats such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Kyurem, and Ogerpon-W; furthermore, it removes Heavy-Duty Boots from common users like Sableye, Alomomola, and Brambleghast with Knock Off, enhancing Gastrodon's hazard stacking. Landorus removes threatening Flying-types like Skarmory and Corviknight with the help of Gravity, as well as checking Articuno and Volcarona via Rock Slide. Mamoswine is able to take Freeze-Dry from Kyurem, Articuno, and Alolan Ninetales and aids in the Flying matchup by using Smack Down to threaten Moltres. Garchomp's Fire-type coverage is valued for threatening roadblocks such as Corviknight and Skarmory. Garchomp also threatens Dragon-types via Draco Meteor and can become a devastating wallbreaker using a combination of Swords Dance and Scale Shot, with it especially appreciating Gastrodon's hazards. Iron Treads removes hazards with Rapid Spin, easing Gastrodon's pivoting if its Heavy-Duty Boots were removed or if the user opted for Leftovers, and it checks Fairy-types like Flutter Mane, Hatterene, and Alolan Ninetales. Furthermore, with a combination of Iron Defense and Body Press, Iron Treads can serve as a check to Hydreigon, Bisharp, and Choice Scarf Meowscarada. Excadrill heavily threatens the aforementioned Fairy-types and Freeze-Dry users as well as Ogerpon formes. Excadrill, in return, values Gastrodon's hazards and ability to catch Landorus-T and Gliscor off guard with Ice Beam.

Specially Defensive (Water).description:
Gastrodon carves out a solid role on Water teams thanks to its secondary Ground typing, which grants it an Electric immunity and a unique set of tools. Earth Power and Earthquake are its main Ground-type STAB moves of choice with both providing solid utility. Earth Power is able to take advantage of Gastrodon's superior Special Attack to chunk foes like Toxapex, Arcahludon, and Pecharunt with ease, while Earthquake helps to ease matchups against specially bulky targets like Hisuian Goodra and Calm Mind Raging Bolt. Ice Beam grants Gastrodon a way to threaten Ground-immune targets like Landorus and scare away Dragon- and Flying-type threats like Dragapult, Dragonite, and Zapdos. Stealth Rock and Spikes provide pressure to threats like Meowscarda and Breloom that can come in to easily scare Gastrodon out. Sticky Hold is Gastrodon's ability of choice, preventing it from having its item removed from Trick and Knock Off from threats like Iron Valiant, Gholdengo, and Alolan Muk.

Toxapex serves as an incredible complement as a physical wall, being able to stave off Grass-type attacks from the likes of Amoonguss and Meowscarada. Toxapex also helps Gastrodon by spreading poison, which complements the chip damage from Gastrodon's entry hazards. Tentacruel can provide similar support to Toxapex while also being able to remove its foes' Heavy-Duty Boots via Knock Off and check the Ogerpon formes, which majorly threaten Gastrodon. Both strongly appreciate Electric-types like Raging Bolt, Regieleki, and Zapdos being dealt with effectively. Empoleon complements Gastrodon's Spikes by running Stealth Rock along with threatening Defoggers with a potential Competitive boost. Empoleon also helps by dealing with Freeze-Dry from the likes of Kyurem, Articuno, and Alolan Ninetales. Choice item users Keldeo and Greninja have their attacks greatly benefit from Gastrodon's hazards chipping down their switch-ins like Alolan Muk, Blissey, and Corviknight. In return, Keldeo provides Vacuum Wave as a way to deal with threats like Weavile and Meowscarada, while Greninja provides Sludge Wave to remove the Ogerpon formes, which take advantage of Gastrodon. Primarina assists Gastrodon by taking on powerful Dark- and Dragon-types like Hisuian Samurott, Roaring Moon, and Dragapult. Ogerpon-W appreciates Gastrodon's hazards chipping down its switch-ins like Skarmory, and it also has access to Encore to stop setup from Bisharp and Raging Bolt, as they attempt to take advantage of Gastrodon's passivity.

Gastrodon makes for a great Electric-immune teammate for Water teams thanks to its great utility options, special bulk, and defensive typing, which allows for Gastrodon to take on Choice Specs Zapdos. Clear Smog allows Gastrodon to negate setup attempts from sweepers such as Dragonite, Kommo-o, and Tapu Fini, while Ice Beam provides coverage against Dragon-types such as Dragonite and Hydreigon. Earthquake deals with Steel-types such as Hisuian Goodra and Gholdengo, whereas Toxic can be run to put switch-ins like Mantine and Rotom-W on a timer. Sticky Hold prevents Gastrodon from obtaining an unwanted Choice item from Hisuian Zoroark and Blacephalon by Trick. Toxapex forms a great defensive core with Gastrodon, as it is able to handle Grass-types such as Tapu Bulu, Ogerpon-W, and Meowscarada and stack entry hazards with Toxic Spikes. Empoleon makes for another great defensive partner, as not only can it set up Stealth Rock, but it also walls and takes on the likes of Kyurem and Alolan Ninetales. Ogerpon-W appreciates Gastrodon taking on Poison-types such as Sneasler and Alolan Muk, and in return, it aids in the Water mirror matchup, taking on the likes of Urshifu-R and Mega Swampert. Wallbreakers such as Choice Specs Greninja and Choice Band Urshifu-R appreciate Gastrodon placing Spikes and inflicting poison on foes so that they can more easily wallbreak against foes like Alolan Muk and Porygon2, respectively.

Physically Defensive (Ground).description: Gastrodon is a mainstay on Ground teams due to its vast utility options, great bulk along with reliable recovery, and a stellar ability in Storm Drain, checking a myriad of Water-types like Mega Swampert, Barraskewda, and Keldeo. Scald threatens physical attackers such as Dragonite, Mega Lopunny, and Mimikyu with a burn. Thanks to Gastrodon's bulk, it is able to stack multiple layers of Spikes to wear down opposing teams. Alternatively, Stealth Rock can be used, freeing a moveslot from a teammate such as Garchomp or Hippowdon. Toxic puts troublesome walls such as Mantine, Ting-Lu, and Araquanid on a timer. Earthquake may be used alongside a Relaxed nature to break Calm Mind Keldeo's Substitute. All of Gastrodon's teammates appreciate its ability to switch into Water-type attacks. Unaware Clodsire checks Grass-types such as Meowscarada and Tapu Bulu as well as setup sweepers Gastrodon can't beat like Volcarona and Galarian Moltres. Iron Treads removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin so Gastrodon can better perform its defensive duties. Wallbreakers like Landorus and Great Tusk appreciate Gastrodon's entry hazard support so that they can net more damage. Mamoswine acts as a secondary Ice-type switch-in that checks the likes of SubRoost Kyurem and Alolan Ninetales, relieving pressure off of Gastrodon.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Ambipom is a capable offensive pivot that can create momentum as an anti-offense lead, or it can revenge kill foes and clean up late-game with its Technician-boosted Fake Out and impressive Speed tier. Opposing sweepers, other revenge killers, and fast pivots such as Salazzle, Choice Scarf Bombirdier, and Hisuian Electrode, which have Speed tiers that make them otherwise hard to deal with, can be picked off or forced out by using Fake Out. U-turn allows Ambipom to escape after dealing Fake Out chip or maintain pressure on an anticipated switch. Knock Off serves as coverage for Ghost-types such as Hoopa and Hisuian Typhlosion while also making progress by removing key items like Heavy-Duty Boots from users such as Galarian Slowbro and Bombirdier as well as Eviolite from foes such as Rhydon and Hisuian Qwilfish. Triple Axel provides Technician-boosted coverage for potential switch-ins, being most effective against Rhydon and Amoonguss. Alternatively, Double-Edge provides a more accurate and STAB-boosted option that has a chance to OHKO frailer offensive Pokemon—Tatsugiri and Salazzle being two examples. Double Hit is another STAB-boosted option that trades accuracy and some power for longevity, especially when paired with Protective Pads. Because of its frequent pivoting, Ambipom often uses Heavy-Duty Boots for greater longevity throughout games, avoiding chip damage from entry hazards. Protective Pads guards Ambipom from contact effects like Flame Body burns and Rocky Helmet chip damage, which are most inhibiting to sets with Triple Axel and Double Hit. Silk Scarf and Tera Normal achieve a similar effect for Ambipom, improving key Fake Out rolls in a pinch by consistently 2HKOing Salazzle and Jolteon, as their high Speed can mandate trading Pokemon for Fake Out hits. Tera Ice turns Triple Axel into a powerful tool for both revenge killing and wallbreaking, letting Ambipom both OHKO threats like Heracross and bust through walls such as Rhydon, Cramorant, and Calm Mind Florges, among others. Tera Normal or Silk Scarf Double-Edge and Double Hit also have respectable damage outputs, OHKOing Tatsugiri and Zoroark. When used together, Ambipom gains legitimate wallbreaking potential; Tera Normal Silk Scarf Double-Edge has a favorable roll to 2HKO Galarian Slowbro and Milotic, two of the best physical walls in the tier.

Ambipom is well suited for bulky or fast offense and balance teams susceptible to fast threats and opposing setup. Sweepers such as Dragon Dance Scrafty and Agility Hisuian Braviary that have fewer chances to set up may be picked off by speed control or trade damage with bulkier Pokemon like Rhydon and Bombirdier. Thus, Ambipom's ability to apply pressure after they faint and prevent counter sweeps is a helpful addition. Entry hazard users like Alolan Sandslash and Palossand also synergize with Ambipom, taking advantage of Knock Off removing Heavy-Duty Boots to wear down susceptible foes—removal options like Cramorant and Hisuian Avalugg rely on Heavy-Duty Boots to switch in several times. Hazards also allow Ambipom to wear down teams by repeated switching and enable Silk Scarf sets to break through chipped switch-ins like Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro, which it 2HKOes with Stealth Rock up. Unfortunately, without Protective Pads, Ambipom is very susceptible to contact abilities like Effect Spore and Flame Body, and it struggles to break common physical walls like Galarian Slowbro and Hisuian Avalugg that it cannot consistently 2HKO after Terastallizing without Silk Scarf or running niche coverage like Low Kick. As such, it benefits from wallbreakers such as Golurk and Delphox that clear through these checks. Ambipom also appreciates bulky teammates with recovery such as Milotic and Florges, allowing a safe switch in after using U-turn. Finally, variants of Ambipom not using Heavy-Duty Boots are easily worn down by opposing hazards and appreciate removal from teammates like Coalossal and Hisuian Decidueye, which in turn appreciate Ambipon providing more opportunities for them to be brought in on favorable matchups and remove hazards or make progress with other utility moves.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Tera Water is an alternative Tera type that lets Drifblim have an easier time against Basculin and Ice-types such as Beartic and Sneasel. However, it keeps the weakness to Electric-type moves.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Dark-types such as Brute Bonnet, Houndoom, Skuntank, and Sneasel can easily switch in on a non-boosted Hex and threaten it with their Dark-type STAB moves. However, aside from Houndoom, none of them appreciate switching in and being neutered by Will-O-Wisp.

Rock-types: Naclstack and Regirock easily check Drifblim with STAB Rock-type attacks. Naclstack, in particular, is immune to both Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave; it can force Drifblim out with Salt Cure or to Terastallize. Drifblim also must be wary of Lycanroc, which possesses STAB priority in Accelerock, often forcing Drifblim out. However, Lycanroc risks being crippled by Will-O-Wisp.

Item Removal: Drifblim is extremely reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots or Terastallization to avoid the super effective chip damage from Stealth Rock. It fears Knock Off from Mesprit, while Choice item Hisuian Sneasel and Whimsicott both run Switcheroo.

Electric-types: Jolteon, Magneton, and Vikavolt all pose a threat to Drifblim, pressuring it with their STAB Electric-type moves. Jolteon and Magneton in particular can also chip it down while pivoting with Volt Switch.

Defog.description:
Drifblim uses its typing, access to Strength Sap, and status moves to carve out a niche in ZU as the tier's best Defog user. Strength Sap provides Drifblim a source of healing while checking physical wallbreakers like Hitmontop, Hisuian Sneasel, and Toxicroak. Will-O-Wisp further neuters physically offensive foes such as Basculin and the aforementioned Hisuian Sneasel and Toxicroak, but Thunder Wave is an alternative option that can be used over Will-O-Wisp to punish setup sweepers like Mesprit and Farigiraf. Hex complements status being spread, but Air Slash is another STAB move that can be used to threaten the likes of Hitmontop, Venusaur, and Whimsicott. Drifblim can run two different EV spreads; it can run maximum Speed investment to speed tie with the other base 80 Speed Pokemon such as Mesprit and Venusaur. Drifblim can also run a physically defensive spread to better withstand hits from foes like Basculin and Hitmontop. Tera Fairy lets Drifblim blank Dragon Pulse from Clawitzer while flipping the matchup against Dark-types such as Brute Bonnet, Mabosstiff, and Sneasel.

Drifblim fits on bulky offense and balance teams that benefit from its typing and ability to remove entry hazards. Drifblim has somewhat lackluster bulk, so it appreciates teammates that can take hits better than it can, like Muk and Naclstack. Pivots such as Basculin, Jolteon, and Mesprit all enjoy Drifblim removing entry hazards, which prevents them from being worn down. Pokemon such as Hitmontop, Hisuian Sneasel, Naclstack, Regirock, and Toxicroak help check the Dark-types like Brute Bonnet, Houndoom, and Sneasel that Drifblim otherwise struggles against. In particular, Naclstack and Regirock's typing allows them to check Houndoom defensively. Drifblim appreciates partnering with Ground-types such as Whiscash and Sandslash, as they check Electric- and Rock-types like Magneton, Jolteon, and Lycanroc that Drifblim fails to deal with. Choice Band or Life Orb Sneasel and Choice Specs Typhlosion can independently form a good offensive core with Drifblim. Typhlosion pressures Ice-types such as Abomasnow and Beartic, while Sneasel greatly appreciates burn and paralysis support. They both value entry hazard removal from Drifblim and in return, Drifblim handles Ground-types such as Sandaconda and Sandslash by providing burn support and having a free opportunity to use Strength Sap.

All-Out Attacker.description: Mega Lopunny is the best Mega Evolution available for Normal teams due to its blistering Speed tier, great offensive prowess, and unique ability in Scrappy. Fake Out lets Mega Lopunny serve as an exceptional revenge killer, dealing with worn down foes like Meowscarada, Barraskewda, and Alolan Raichu. It also puts Pokemon like Keldeo, Cinderace, and Tapu Koko in range of its other attacks safely. With Scrappy, Close Combat notably lets Mega Lopunny take on threats like Mega Sableye, Aegislash, and Gholdengo, threatening the defensive cores of Dark and Steel teams. U-turn enables Mega Lopunny to work as a potent offensive pivot, escaping unfavorable situations against walls like Slowbro and Mega Venusaur while keeping momentum. Triple Axel threatens common switch-ins such as Gliscor and Mandibuzz, while Return is Mega Lopunny's hardest-hitting move against most Psychic- and Fairy-types, such as Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant. Blissey is a great teammate, taking on the likes of Volcarona and Zapdos thanks to its bulk while offering support in the form of Stealth Rock, Toxic, and Teleport. Staraptor switches into Fighting-type attacks from Pokemon like Great Tusk, Buzzwole, and Tapu Bulu, and its access to Defog and U-turn also prolongs Mega Lopunny's longevity and lets it switch in unscathed. Special attackers like Hisuian Zoroark and Porygon-Z are able to break past physical walls Mega Lopunny can't, like Skeledirge, Corviknight, and Slowbro. Hisuian Zoroark also prevents Fighting-types from spamming their STAB moves aimed at Mega Lopunny.

Wallbreaker (Normal).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Offensive.description:
With virtually perfect coverage thanks to Scrappy and a high Attack stat, Mega Lopunny is an excellent choice of speed control that can help pressure the many bulky Steel-types in the tier, such as Ferrothorn, Gholdengo, and Kingambit. Fake Out is one of Mega Lopunny's most valuable tools, as it can revenge kill weakened threats such as Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant and Scale Shot Garchomp. U-turn makes use of Mega Lopunny's ability to force out many Pokemon by generating momentum to continue applying pressure, but Quick Attack can be used instead to further improve Mega Lopunny's revenge killing capabilities. Triple Axel is another option that can OHKO Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Dragonite, as well as dealing heavy damage to Great Tusk and Mega Latios.

Mega Lopunny is a staple for many balance and bulky offense teams as a great speed control and revenge killer. Wallbreakers such as Raging Bolt, Tapu Lele, and Kyurem appreciate Mega Lopunny bringing them onto the field and in return can threaten out its checks such as Toxapex, Great Tusk, and Zapdos. Mega Lopunny can also help put pressure on their checks in return, such as Gholdengo and Ferrothorn. Other pivots such as Landorus-T and Tapu Koko can form a VoltTurn core with Mega Lopunny, with the former setting Stealth Rock and both being able to break Toxapex. In return, Mega Lopunny helps break Ting-Lu and Ferrothorn. Since Mega Lopunny forces a lot of switches, entry hazard setters such as Ting-Lu, Hisuian Samurott, and Ferrothorn make good teammates. Due to Mega Lopunny's low defenses and weakness to hazards, defensive Pokemon such as Gholdengo, Ferrothorn, and Zapdos also make great partners, as they can switch into Fairy-, Fighting-, and Flying-type attacks from Iron Valiant and opposing Zapdos. Hazard removal from Terapagos, Zapdos, and Great Tusk is also greatly appreciated to prevent Mega Lopunny from accumulating too much chip damage from hazards.

Physical Attacker.description:
Stunky serves as an effective wallbreaker, using its strong STAB combination to dismantle opposing defensive cores. Being a grounded Poison-type, Stunky also helps teams by clearing Toxic Spikes. Knock Off strips off Eviolite, while Sucker Punch provides a priority option against foes that outspeed Stunky, like Alolan Diglett and Hisuian Growlithe. Temper Flare is good against Steel-types like Tinkatink, and it is complemented by Gunk Shot, receiving a damage boost if the move misses. Alternatively, Substitute helps Stunky dodge status from foes like Foongus while also allowing it to scout defensive Terastallizations from foes such as Mienfoo. The maximum Speed investment along with a Jolly Nature enables Stunky to outspeed metagame staples like Mienfoo and Chinchou. Tera Dark boosts Knock Off even more and empowers Sucker Punch to give Stunky stronger priority presence, whereas Tera Poison boosts its strongest move in Gunk Shot and grants better defensive positioning against Fighting-types.

Stunky's ability to strip items with Knock Off makes it an excellent partner for Alolan Diglett, which appreciates facing weakened targets. Vullaby is another supreme teammate, as the combination of powerful STAB moves from the core is extremely difficult to mitigate for the majority of team structures. Ground-types like Mudbray and Alolan Diglett comfortably threaten Stunky and impede its progress. Options like Toedscool, which can pivot into them safely, and Mudbray, which can favorably trade against them, are great teammate choices for Stunky.

Utility.description:
Skuntank's unique typing, ability in Aftermath, and movepool tailored for both stallbreaking and revenge killing establish it as a solid glue Pokemon in the metagame for a variety of team structures.
