Its typing allows it to check a variety of threats, such as Galarian Slowbro and Hoopa, which creates reliable opportunities to debuff walls like Mudsdale, Rhydon, and Milotic on the switch, as not much in the metagame can resist its STAB combination of Gunk Shot and Knock Off. Sucker Punch is able to pick off weakened offensive threats such as Delphox and Frosmoth as well as Choice Scarf users like non-Dazzling Bruxish and Rotom-Mow. Taunt is useful to stop the likes of Milotic and Vileplume from healing freely and also inhibits setup sweepers such as Snorlax. Toxic or Toxic Spikes can be used instead to cripple and wear down switch-ins like Mudsdale and Hisuian Avalugg. However, stay wary that the latter can be easily removed by common Poison-types like Salazzle, Venusaur, and opposing Skuntank. Rocky Helmet is useful to punish opposing Knock Off users like Bombirdier and other Skuntank, as Skuntank is often the designated Knock Off absorber for many teams. Rocky Helmet also synergizes well with Aftermath to allow Skuntank to trade with contact-attacking threats like Pawmot, Paldean Tauros-F, and Bruxish as needed. The boost from Black Glasses works exceptionally well with an Adamant nature and Tera Dark, as Skuntank can break through walls like Palossand and defensive Venusaur with these boosts stacked while also notably giving Adamant variants a guaranteed chance to OHKO Delphox from full with Sucker Punch. Some teams may opt for Heavy-Duty Boots, as it can be used to more reliably handle Hoopa for teams that need that support, avoiding the 3HKO from Shadow Ball after Stealth Rock chip damage. A Jolly nature is useful to outspeed the likes of Tatsugiri and Jolly Bombirdier, while an Adamant nature can be used for additional power, for example, guaranteeing an OHKO against Golurk with Knock Off even without Black Glasses. Tera Ghost can be used over Tera Dark for its defensive merits versus certain hyper offensive sweepers; for example, Skuntank becomes immune to Facade and Close Combat from Heracross and Tri Attack from Porygon2 and can then fire back with Gunk Shot or Knock Off.

Skuntank functions well on entry hazard-stacking archetypes thanks to its ability to lure in and remove Heavy-Duty Boots from the likes of Milotic and Hisuian Avalugg. Spikes setters such as Alolan Sandslash and Coalossal are able to wear down offensive threats like Tatsugiri and Salazzle into range of Skuntank's Sucker Punch as well. Additionally, Skuntank is a valuable asset for hyper offense teams, providing role compression by being able to defensively check problematic threats like Choice Scarf Hoopa while also supporting setup sweepers such as Salazzle, Rhydon, and Hisuian Decidueye by wearing down shared checks such as Coalossal and Mudsdale with Toxic and Knock Off support. These offensive threats also appreciate Skuntank's ability to pivot into annoying defensive threats like Galarian Slowbro and Wo-Chien fairly reliably. Offensive Water-types such as Tatsugiri and Bruxish appreciate Skuntank's ability to pressure Grass-types like Wo-Chien and Brute Bonnet, while in return, they can switch into Ground-types like Sandaconda immediately after Skuntank has crippled them with Knock Off. Skuntank's ability to offensively check the likes of Delphox and Hisuian Decidueye can also be beneficial for defensive pieces such as Wo-Chien and Cramorant to not become overwhelmed, which can allow them to return the favor by better handling threats to Skuntank such as Mudsdale and Paldean Tauros-F, respectively.

Specially Defensive (Poison).description:
Skuntank fills a very important role on Poison teams by packing a much-desired Psychic immunity, which allows it to switch into Psychic-type moves from many common threats such as Greninja, Flutter Mane, and Hatterene. It proceeds to force them out with its hard hitting Poison Jab-which can spread poison around, while Sucker Punch picks them off should they be weakened enough. Protect is also very valuable in scouting their coverage moves, letting Skuntank accumulate Black Sludge recovery, and stalling out poison damage. Aftermath punishes contact attackers like Bisharp and Azumarill, which allows teammates such as Toxicroak to safely come in and finish them off. Skuntank can run Play Rough to threaten common Dark-types of the metagame, such as Weavile and Hydreigon.

Physically defensive Amoonguss and Toxapex are valuable teammates that deal with the physical attackers that threaten Skuntank, like Mimikyu, Quaquaval, and Dondozo. Amoonguss also deals with threatening Ground-types such as Great Tusk, Quagsire, and Sandy Shocks thanks to its good bulk, Grass-type STAB move, and Ground neutrality. Toxapex, on the other hand, deals with threats like Weavile, Cloyster, and Scizor with Infestation and Haze while laying down Toxic Spikes. Specially defensive Clodsire complements Skuntank by dealing with special attackers it can't handle by itself, such as Gholdengo, Magnezone, and Volcarona. Iron Moth deals with the multitude of Steel-types like Gholdengo, Iron Treads, and Corviknight that Skuntank can't do much against. Corrosion Glimmora and Salazzle help cripple Steel-types and opposing Poison-types with Toxic, with each also providing different utilities; Glimmora packs Poison's only entry hazard removal thanks to Mortal Spin, which allows Skuntank to come in safely, while Salazzle's Encore acts as a counterplay against powerful setup sweepers such as Volcarona and Bisharp.

nu.overview: Bronzong is an elite Steel-type in NU thanks to both its great mixed bulk and an excellent ability in Levitate, which, unlike other Steel-types, allows it to check many Ground-types like Flygon and Gligar, along with other Pokémon that rely on Ground-type coverage to hit Steel-types like Avalugg. Bronzong is remarkably resistant to entry hazards, as it simultaneously resists Stealth Rock and has an immunity to Spikes, making it a centerpiece on teams with little to no hazard removal. Furthermore, Bronzong excels at being a great hazard setter thanks to its ability to check threats like Munkidori, Sylveon, and Porygon-Z. It can take advantage of these positive matchups and its already tremendous bulk by instead being a bulky setup sweeper, becoming very difficult to take out. However, Bronzong's only form of recovery is Leftovers, meaning that it has to be even more wary about switching into the already threatening Knock Off from Pokemon that it would check otherwise like Copperajah, Tsareena, and Toxicroak. Additionally, foes that Bronzong is typically expected to check like Munkidori, Florges, and Rotom-C often run Trick to cripple it severely and especially hurt its setup sets.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Bronzong can opt to run a fully physically defensive EV spread, letting it handle physical wallbreakers like Flygon, Staraptor, and Flamigo a bit better, but this makes it worse against Pokemon like Goodra, Inteleon, and Munkidori. Heatproof allows Bronzong to handle Pokemon that carry Fire-type coverage like Fire Punch Flygon and Flamethrower Galarian Slowbro, but the Ground immunity from Levitate is almost always superior. Future Sight lets it limit switch-ins for wallbreakers like Flygon, Flamigo, and Paldean Tauros-W. Gyro Ball lets Bronzong hit faster opponents like Tornadus and Flygon much harder. Protect can be used on utility sets, providing Bronzong a bit more Leftovers recovery and letting it scout out Choice item users like Flygon and Munkidori; however, it struggles to fit it because it prefers to run other utility moves. Trick alongside Toxic Orb allows Bronzong to cripple defensive tanks like Incineroar, Bellibolt, Goodra, and Vaporeon. Colbur Berry lets Bronzong tank Dark-type attacks like Dark Pulse from Inteleon and Knock Off from Tsareena, but it prefers Leftovers for gaining extra recovery.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types and Dark-type Coverage: Incineroar, Overqwil, and Scrafty can tank Bronzong’s attacks very well and threaten it back with their STAB attacks. However, none of them want to switch into a +2 Body Press. Pokemon that have Dark-type coverage like Throat Chop Flygon, Dark Pulse Inteleon, and Knock Off from Tornadus or Cinccino can put a lot of pressure on Bronzong as well.

Ghost-types: Chandelure, Houndstone, Decidueye, and Brambleghast easily destroy Bronzong with their STAB attacks, and the former can cripple it with Trick. However, the first two have to be mindful about switching into Bronzong variants that run Earthquake.

Item Removal: Knock Off users like Copperajah, Tsareena, Gligar, Ambipom, and Cinccino can threaten Bronzong by getting rid of its Leftovers, cutting into its longevity over the course of the battle. Choice Scarf users like Munkidori and Meloetta can both bother utility sets and ruin Bronzong's sweeping attempts by crippling it with Trick.

Fire-types: Infernape, Incineroar, and Salazzle threaten Bronzong with their high-Base Power attacks or take advantage of it by getting free turns to set up. Salazzle is especially annoying with its access to Encore and, thanks to Corrosion, can threaten Bronzong with Toxic.

Utility.description:
Set Details

Body Press pairs well with Bronzong's good Defense, letting it threaten Dark- and Steel-types like Incineroar, Scrafty, and Copperajah. Earthquake lets Bronzong target Fire- and Poison-types like Chandelure and Galarian Slowbro, and even after Intimidate, it hits Overqwil harder than Body Press can. Heavy Slam allows Bronzong to hit Fairy-types like Sylveon, Florges, and Scream Tail. Night Shade can be used over Heavy Slam, allowing Bronzong to make solid progress against Ghost and Dark-types like Chandelure, Basculegion-M, and Incineroar. Optionally, Bronzong can invest 164 Defense EVs in order to 2HKO offensive Incineroar with Body Press while better taking hits from physical attackers like Flygon. Tera Fairy gives Bronzong a useful resistance to Dark- and Fighting-type attacks from Incineroar and Flamigo. Tera Water, on the other hand, provides it a resistance to Water- and Fire-type attacks, helping it against Pokemon like Inteleon and Chandelure.

Bronzong pairs well with Fighting-types like Flamigo, Scrafty, Toxicroak, and Paldean Tauros-W, as they can handle Incineroar, and the last three are great switch-ins to Knock Off; in return, Bronzong checks Fairy- and Psychic-types such as Sylveon, Uxie, and Munkidori. Ghost-types like Chandelure, Decidueye, and Brambleghast can take Bronzong's attacks fairly easily and threaten it back with their own STAB attacks. Thus, it best partners with Dark-types like Incineroar, Overqwil, and Bombirdier to check the aforementioned Ghost-types. Bulky Water-types like Vaporeon and Swampert can beat Fire-types like Chandelure and Incineroar for Bronzong. Spikes users like Overqwil, Brambleghast, and Heracross are excellent partners for Bronzong, as they can spread entry hazards to help each other wear down their checks. Wish passers like Vaporeon and Sylveon let Bronzong repeatedly switch in against special wallbreakers like Munkidori and Goodra by offsetting its lack of recovery. Bronzong synergizes well with physical walls like Gligar, Bellibolt, and Vaporeon for their positive matchups against physical attackers like Toxicroak, Paldean Tauros-W, and Incineroar. In return, Bronzong handles special wallbreakers like Munkidori, Toxtricity, and Sylveon.

Bulky Setup Sweeper.description:
Set Details

Body Press lets Bronzong pressure Steel- and Dark-types like Copperajah, Klefki, and Incineroar. Stored Power lets it more easily break through Fighting-resistant and -immune Pokemon that try to switch in like Sylveon, Amoonguss, and Decidueye, while the scaling power from both Bronzong's boosted offenses and defenses helps it break past opposing Calm Mind setup from the likes of Sylveon, Dudunsparce, and Galarian Slowbro. The EV spread allows Bronzong to outspeed non-Speed-invested Rhyperior so that Bronzong can check it reliably while giving it enough special bulk to tank many hits. Tera Fairy gives it a resistance to Fighting-, Dark-, and Dragon-type attacks from Heracross, Scrafty, and Flygon. However, Tera Water lets it better handle foes like Inteleon, Chandelure, and Infernape. Tera Poison could also be used, as it allows Bronzong to check Fighting- and Poison-types like Flamigo and Toxicroak, and it maintains Bronzong's immunity to Toxic.

Wish passers like Vaporeon and Sylveon appreciate Bronzong for checking threats like Munkidori, Goodra, and Dudunsparce. In return, they provide it recovery by passing it Wish. Bronzong greatly appreciates partners like Florges, Flamigo, and Scrafty, as they often bring in foes like Munkidori, Sylveon, and Flygon for Bronzong to take advantage of. Fighting- and Fairy-types like Flamigo, Paldean Tauros-F, Florges, and Whimsicott are great partners for Bronzong, as they can handle Dark-types like Incineroar and Scrafty, and the last three are good Knock Off absorbers; in return, Bronzong checks and can capitalize on Poison-types like Galarian Slowbro, Amoonguss, and Munkidori. Bronzong partners well with Dark-types like Incineroar and Overqwil, as they can check Ghost-types such as Chandelure, Decidueye, and Brambleghast and bulky Psychic-types like Uxie and opposing Bronzong that it can struggle with. Fire-types like Chandelure and Incineroar can force Bronzong to switch out, so it best pairs with bulky Water- and Dragon-types like Vaporeon and Goodra to check them.

Iron Defense (Psychic).description:
Will never be OHKOed from full HP by an unboosted Chien-Pao's Crunch.

This is a sample set as we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

zu.comments:
Other Options

Physically offensive and mixed variants of Spiritomb can be used due to its access to Sucker Punch and Poltergeist, but there are far better options for physically offensive Dark-types like Mabosstiff and Sneasel, which boast superior Attack and Speed stats. Spiritomb can opt to use Pain Split or Will-O-Wisp instead of Psyshock on the offensive Trick Room set in order to improve its survivability and potentially ease setup at a heavy cost to its coverage, losing out on key targets like Virizion and Poliwrath.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Offensive Dark-type foes like Mabosstiff and Sneasel resist Spiritomb's STAB Dark Pulse and retaliate with excellent damage themselves, though they must be wary of physically defensive variants that can debilitate them with Will-O-Wisp.

Fairy-types: As the tier's best Fairy-type Pokemon, Whimsicott can take on Spiritomb's boosted attacks and threaten heavy damage with Moonblast. Tera Fairy walls like Mesprit and Dipplin can resist Spiritomb's STAB Dark Pulse to stop its sweep or further their own setup.

Wallbreakers: Spiritomb's lackluster natural bulk can be easily preyed upon by wallbreakers like Mabosstiff, Jolteon, and Vikavolt regardless of what set it's running, though they must be careful when switching in.

Encore: While it is immune to Prankster Encore from the likes of Whimsicott and Sableye, Spiritomb must be wary of a potential Encore from other foes like Mesprit, Beartic, and non-Prankster variants of the previously mentioned Whimsicott.

Special Walls: Specially defensive walls like Cryogonal and Articuno can wipe away Spiritomb's Nasty Plot boosts with Haze; in addition, Articuno can also phaze Spiritomb with Roar.

Offensive Trick Room.description:
Spiritomb utilizes its defensive profile to switch into foes like Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel, setting up and devastating teams in a tier almost completely lacking Fairy-type Pokemon. Dark Pulse serves as an amazing neutral STAB attack for a vast majority of the tier, threatening OHKOs on metagame staples like Jolteon and Mesprit after a Nasty Plot boost; it is the preferred STAB over Shadow Ball to avoid letting Normal-type Pokemon like Pyroar and Farigiraf switch in for free. Psyshock compliments Dark Pulse excellently with its ability to hit Fighting-types like Poliwrath and Virizion while targeting opposing special walls like Cryogonal and Tera Fairy Naclstack on their comparatively worse Defense. Tera Dark further amplifies the power of Spiritomb's Dark Pulse to OHKO as many foes as possible once boosted, securing guaranteed OHKOs on foes like Charizard.

Spiritomb works well alongside wallbreakers like Virizion, Mesprit, and Hisuian Sneasel, which can wallbreak for each other and enable Spiritomb's sweep. Spiritomb struggles with strong physical attacks from the likes of Mabosstiff and Sneasel, so it appreciates physical walls like Regirock and Weezing that can reliably switch into them. Special attackers like Jolteon, Vikavolt, and Mesprit pair well with Spiritomb to break down walls for each other. Teammates with pivoting moves like Basculin, Jolteon, and Primeape can help bring Spiritomb in safely to help ease its setup. Entry hazard support from the likes of Regirock, Sandslash, and Mesprit is also greatly appreciated to help whittle foes into range for Spiritomb to sweep. Pokemon that can threaten Whimsicott like Muk and Magneton are appreciated to help cover for Spiritomb's lone weakness to Fairy.

nfe.overview: Gabite uses its powerful Dragon and Ground typing in conjunction with Swords Dance to become a potentially devastating setup sweeper in the NFE metagame. Sitting at a comfortable speed tier ahead of other offensive threats like Monferno and Thwackey, Gabite is a solid choice for teams that need a powerful wallbreaker and setup option. On top of this, Gabite can establish Stealth Rock for its team and use its Ground typing to absorb paralysis attempts from the likes of Hattrem and Tinkatuff. While these traits are quite tantalizing, Gabite does suffer from having poor matchups into other NFE staples like Dunsparce, which can threaten Gabite with paralysis and coverage, and Piloswine, which can revenge kill Gabite with Ice Shard after minor chip damage.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Scale Shot can be used to provide a Speed boost, helping outpace Frogadier and Girafarig, though it does mean Gabite is much less threatening offensively, as it relies on the multi-hit nature of the move. Similarly, Gabite can opt for a fully offensive set, using a Choice Scarf to outspeed the aforementioned Pokemon without needing to rely on Scale Shot and coverage moves like Iron Head to hit Fairy-types harder, like Clefairy.

Checks and Counters

Faster Wallbreakers: Gabite is slower than notable revenge killers like Drakloak and Frogadier, both of which can threaten an OHKO with Draco Meteor and Ice Beam, respectively.

Piloswine: Piloswine's Ice Shard threatens an OHKO after Gabite takes minor chip damage.

Dunsparce: Dunsparce is quite difficult for Gabite to break through and can use Ice Beam to threaten an OHKO.

Wartortle: Wartortle can be problematic for Gabite, as it can use the threat of Ice Beam to get a free Shell Smash opportunity.

Swords Dance.description:
Gabite is a solid choice as an offensive setup option that also offers excellent utility in Stealth Rock and its Ground typing, which helps against notable entry hazard setters like Koffing and Tinkatuff. Substitute can be used to block status attempts from slower foes like Body Slam Dunsparce and Will-O-Wisp Koffing, allowing Gabite to use Swords Dance more freely; alternatively, Gabite can use Stealth Rock to free up a moveslot for teammates like Dunsparce and Tinkatuff. Scale Shot turns Gabite into a threatening cleaner since it can outspeed revenge killers like Girafarig, Frogadier, and Drakloak. The given EV spread maximizes its damage output, with Adamant granting more immediate wallbreaking power at the expense of being slower than Monferno and Thwackey.

Gabite is a fine addition to many team structures, notably finding a role on balance and bulky offense teams as an offensive setup sweeper and wallbreaker. While Gabite can use its Ground typing to find setup opportunities against common foes like Koffing, Monferno, and Tinkatuff, it struggles with capitalizing on its boosts with the abundance of threats that can OHKO it, like Drakloak, Frogadier, and Piloswine. Teammates like Tinkatuff can help handle these threats by providing Knock Off support while sponging attacks from Drakloak and Frogadier. Quaxwell can also help handle them by providing slow pivots with Flip Turn, entry hazard removal with Rapid Spin, and it can take hits from Frogadier. Drakloak makes an excellent partner too, as it can threaten Will-O-Wisp on Piloswine to limit the damage output of Ice Shard while acting as a spinblocker against opposing Quaxwell. Ivysaur, Monferno, and Pignite are fine teammates for Gabite as well, offering Knock Off support to help remove Eviolite from physical walls, like opposing Ivysaur and Vullaby, to make wallbreaking easier for Gabite. Paralysis spreaders like Dunsparce, Drakloak, and Tinkatuff can enable Gabite offensively, allowing it to use Substitute to set up against paralyzed foes a bit more safely. Frogadier, as a partner to Stealth Rock Gabite, can create powerful hazard-stacking cores with Drakloak as the spinblocker. Girafarig is a great teammate to help Gabite get through Drakloak, providing a special wallbreaker to go with Gabite's physical wallbreaking. Raboot can help Gabite set up by providing safe entry points against common switch-ins like Koffing.

Defensive.description:
Defensive Gabite is an annoyance for physical attackers like Monferno and Quaxwell, punishing their attempts to pivot with its Rough Skin while capably setting up Stealth Rock for its team; Quaxwell can, however, use Ice-type coverage to hit Gabite. Dragon Tail gives Gabite great utility, as it can phaze setup threats, like Thwackey and Duosion, while also providing a way to rack up chip damage against common switch-ins like Dunsparce and Piloswine. Rest is Gabite's only form of recovery and can help accrue more Rough Skin and entry hazard chip damage throughout a game as well as remove pesky burns and poisons it may acquire from Koffing. A fully defensive EV spread ensures Gabite can sponge hits from the strongest physical attackers in the tier, like Monferno, Pignite, and Thwackey.

Spikes setters like Frogadier, and the more niche Quilladin, pair well with defensive Gabite, using the Stealth Rock it sets in conjunction with Dragon Tail to capitalize on the entry hazard stacking nature of these cores. Koffing can also function well with Gabite on hazard-stacking cores, using its potent Toxic Spikes to spread poison efficiently as, Gabite can deter opposing Koffing from coming onto the field to clear them. Drakloak can similarly maintain these hazards by acting as a spinblocker against Quaxwell. Dunsparce appreciates Gabite as a teammate, which can free up its moveslots, allowing it to run either Calm Mind or Coil sets more effectively; Dunsparce deals with threats like Drakloak and Piloswine in return. Similarly, Piloswine is a powerhouse that can capitalize on its wallbreaking proficiency with the support of Gabite, using Choice Band sets to great effect with the support of hazard chip that is accrued. While Gabite can use Rest to remove status from itself, it appreciates teammates that can more comfortably absorb Will-O-Wisp from Koffing, like Monferno and Pignite. These two also provide Gabite with Knock Off support, removing Eviolite to wear foes down even more quickly. Wallbreakers and cleaners like Girafarig, Wartortle, and Fraxure pair well with Gabite, as they can use the chip damage it accrues to enable their late-game cleaning, breaking past checks such as Dunsparce and Tinkatuff. Frogadier and Piloswine are enormous threats to Gabite, using their powerful Ice-type attacks to threaten an OHKO on it; Quaxwell is a valuable teammate to both sponge these attacks and remove hazards from the field for Gabite and its teammates. Similarly, Drakloak and Frogadier can threaten Gabite out with ease, making Ivysaur and Servine valuable teammates to take their attacks while also providing Knock Off support.

TankChomp.description:
Garchomp works as a good defensive piece thanks to its access to both Stealth Rock and Spikes, good defensive typing backed up by solid defensive stats, and phazing to deal with foes attempting to set up on it. Dragon Tail allows Garchomp to deny foes such as Swords Dance Gliscor and Swords Dance Ogerpon-W the opportunity to set up on it. In addition, it can switch out non-Heavy-Duty Boots users such as the aforementioned Ogerpon-W as well as Ting-Lu and force them to take large amounts of entry hazard damage when attempting to switch back in. Another benefit of its phazing is that it can nullify Booster Energy, making foes like Terastallized Raging Bolt and Iron Moth waste their Booster Energy against Garchomp. Rough Skin, when paired with Rocky Helmet, makes Garchomp a nightmare for the common Rapid Spin users in Great Tusk and Iron Treads while punishing reckless U-turn uses from foes such as Landorus-T and Cinderace. Tera Ghost allows Garchomp to both stop the aforementioned Rapid Spin users from removing hazards while shedding its Ice and Fairy weaknesses. It also gives Garchomp a Fighting immunity to check Great Tusk and Swords Dance Iron Valiant and completely stop Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta. On the other hand, Tera Steel allows Garchomp to turn the tables on Fairy-types like Hatterene and beat them one-on-one while affording a handy Ice resistance to phaze foes like Kyurem and Ice Beam Darkrai. The given EV spread allows Garchomp to outspeed Raging Bolt.

This Garchomp set fits well on balance teams that appreciate its ability to force damage through entry hazards and punishing contact moves, especially Rapid Spin, while being able to phaze out dangerous setup sweepers and act as a general anti-offense tool. Garchomp despises Ice-type moves from the likes of Kyurem, Darkrai, and Dragon Dance Dragonite with Ice Spinner as well as Fairy-types like Clefable, Hatterene, and Tera Fairy Gliscor, so checks like Gholdengo, Zamazenta, and Galarian Slowking are great partners. Air Balloon Gholdengo in particular is a great partner, as it blocks any attempts to remove the hazards set by Garchomp by foes like Great Tusk and Corviknight that otherwise wall Garchomp while being able to scare them away. Pecharunt fills a lot of the same roles as Gholdengo while also providing pivoting in the form of Parting Shot and absorbing Toxic Spikes, making it another viable option. Moltres is another good partner, as it both helps phaze foes with Roar as well as add on even more chip damage and punish Rapid Spin attempts through Will-O-Wisp and Flame Body burns, respectively, while checking threatening Fairy-types like Enamorus and foes like SubTect Kyurem. Galarian Slowking checks Fairy-types like Enamorus and Hatterene well while setting up Future Sight to force out foes Garchomp is walled by, such as Zamazenta, Pecharunt, and defensive Great Tusk, allowing Garchomp to set more hazards up. Wallbreakers that appreciate Garchomp's hazard setting capabilities such as all-out attacking Zamazenta, Heavy-Duty Boots Kyurem, Darkrai, and Kingambit are also good picks alongside it.

Swords Dance.description:
Garchomp's ability to boost its offensive stats using Swords Dance and Scale Shot enable it to be a solid sweeper. Its STAB combination is excellent, with Earthquake and Scale Shot hitting a majority of the metagame and giving Garchomp a chance to OHKO foes like Dragonite, Iron Moth, and Kyurem even before boosting. Swords Dance massively amplifies Garchomp's offensive pressure, and after a Speed boost from Scale Shot, Garchomp can outspeed many of the tier's fast staples like Zamazenta, Dragapult, Darkrai, Weavile, and Meowscarada, as well as Landorus-T and Gholdengo that use Choice Scarf. Fire Fang allows Garchomp to threaten Corviknight and Skarmory after a Swords Dance, in addition to hitting Air Balloon Gholdengo and Scizor super effectively. Alternatively, Dragon Tail may be used to force out foes stacking Defense boosts like Zamazenta, Corviknight, and Garganacl. Terastallizing into a Fire-type can flip Garchomp's matchup against Fairy- and Ice-types like Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Kyurem, as well as blocking Will-O-Wisp from the likes of Dragapult, Cinderace, and Darkrai. It also boosts the damage of Fire Fang, with +2 Tera Fire Fire Fang being a guaranteed 2HKO against Leftovers Corviknight and having a chance to OHKO physically defensive Gholdengo. Tera Ghost can be utilized instead to grant Garchomp better matchups into attackers using Fighting-type moves like Zamazenta and Corviknight.

Swords Dance Garchomp thrives on offensive teams that can eliminate potential obstacles and enable its sweep. Some of the metagame's fastest threats, such as Booster Energy Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf users like Enamorus and Darkrai, outspeed boosted Garchomp and OHKO it. Garchomp immensely appreciates entry hazard support from teammates like Great Tusk and Glimmora that can help it more reliably handle bulky foes, with Stealth Rock and one layer of Spikes allowing it to 2HKO +1 Defense Zamazenta with either STAB move and OHKO physically defensive variants of Primarina and Hatterene with Earthquake after using Swords Dance. Great Tusk has the additional benefit of matching up well against Gliscor and Dragonite, while Glimmora can threaten Clefable, Zapdos, and Moltres. Gholdengo is a fantastic teammate for Garchomp, checking some of Garchomp's hardest counters in Iron Valiant and Enamorus and ensuring that entry hazards from other teammates remain up. In return, Garchomp has favorable matchups into Gholdengo's checks like Kingambit and Blissey. Teams can also benefit from pairing Iron Valiant and Garchomp, with Garchomp handling common Iron Valiant checks like Gholdengo, Clodsire, and Iron Moth while Iron Valiant can eliminate strong Dragon-types that threaten Garchomp like Kyurem and Dragapult. Kingambit can similarly check these Dragon-types while also matching up well against Hatterene, Alomomola, and Clefable, and Garchomp's offensive pressure can facilitate Kingambit's late-game sweep. Ogerpon-W is another useful companion, helping muscle through obstacles like Clefable and Moltres and checking Dondozo.

Offensive Swords Dance.description:
Using its numerous strong points, including a great typing, powerful STAB moves, and the immediate and devastating power of its held Z-Crystal, Garchomp can be a very effective wallbreaker and entry hazard setter. Its great type combination allows it to find plenty of setup opportunities against Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona. Swords Dance lets it pick up KOs against various entry hazard removers like Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Gliscor, making Garchomp a very effective hazard setter. Outrage has limited usage, as it leaves Garchomp vulnerable to Fairy-types and Steel-types, but it can allow Garchomp to trade with a Ground-immune switch-in like Landorus-T or Gliscor in a pinch; however, Dragonium Z with Outrage allows Garchomp to bruteforce past some of its biggest checks like Landorus-T, Great Tusk, and Alomomola. Stone Edge is a much safer move than, letting Garchomp hit Flying-types like Mega Charizard Y, Zapdos, and Moltres super effectively and also hit Ground-immune Pokemon like Corviknight and Landorus-T. Rockium Z allows Garchomp to hit Corviknight, Landorus-T, and Gliscor for bigger damage, but it leaves Garchomp weaker against its other checks.

Utilising its various traits, such as a great defensive profile and high power STAB moves, Garchomp can find a spot on team structures like hyper offense and bulky offense. Its role as a great entry hazard setter shouldn't be ignored either, as it can scare away certain defensive Pokemon like Gholdengo and Toxapex, giving it good opportunities to set up hazards as they switch out. Due to being able to take care of Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona, it can form a great hazard stacking core with Ferrothorn, which is otherwise very weak to the aforementioned Fire-types. Ferrothorn can act as a great switch-in against Dragon-types such as Dragonite and Roaring Moon and Fairy-types such as Tapu Lele and Tapu Koko. Special attacking cleaners like Iron Valiant, Mega Diancie, and Volcarona are helped by Garchomp's ability to eliminate most of the defensive Poison-types including Toxapex, Clodsire, and Galarian Slowking. Pokemon like Iron Valiant, Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, and Weavile are all great checks to Garchomp, being able to immediately shut it down. Mega Scizor can help against them, being able to take hits and dish out big damage in return. Garchomp may also help circumvent Mega Scizor's four times weakness to Fire-type moves. A notorious wall to Garchomp's Z-move set is Corviknight, which via its typing and bulk is able to shrug off Garchomp's attacks and recover with Roost. As such, special attackers like Raging Bolt, Zapdos, and Mega Charizard Y prove great allies to Garchomp, which in return can deal with common specially defensive walls such as Clodsire, Toxapex, and Heatran.

TankChomp.description:
Garchomp leverages its good defensive typing and decent bulk to become a solid tank that checks several prominent Pokemon, including Mega Charizard Y, Heatran, and Volcarona. Toxic allows Garchomp to deal with Mega Charizard Y and bulky Volcarona while also punishing several Pokemon that would otherwise switch in easily, such as Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Moltres. Protect allows Garchomp to rack up Toxic damage, keep itself as healthy as possible with Leftovers, and scout Choice-locked foes such as Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott and Choice-locked Tapu Lele. Garchomp is a solid entry hazard setter, as it can pressure some common hazard removal options, most notably Great Tusk, Terapagos, and Zapdos, with Toxic. Dragon Tail is a good alternative if the team has other hazard setters, as it lets Garchomp rack up hazard damage and temporarily remove foes that might try to set up on it, such as Air Balloon Gholdengo, Swords Dance Gliscor, and Swords Dance Kartana. Leftovers allows Garchomp to stay healthy throughout the game and synergizes well with Protect, while Rough Skin punishes contact moves from the likes of Urshifu-R, Hisuian Samurott, and Great Tusk. The given EV spread allows Garchomp to best check special attackers like Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona, while the Speed EVs allow it to outrun Modest Heatran. 40 Speed EVs with a Jolly Nature let Garchomp outrun Raging Bolt, but the reduction in bulk makes Garchomp noticeably worse against Gholdengo and Heatran, and Garchomp can't safely switch into Raging Bolt anyway.

This Garchomp set fits well on offense and bulky offense teams, as it has limited longevity but provides these teams with much needed role compression in checking Mega Charizard Y, Heatran, and Volcarona while also setting up entry hazards. Garchomp does well supporting offensive teammates that dislike these specific threats, such as Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Kartana. Gholdengo is an especially good teammate, as it can deny hazard removal attempts from Terapagos and Zapdos, which is important as Garchomp has limited longevity and will likely not be able to repeatedly set up hazards in longer games. Alomomola is another solid teammate, as it can pivot into threatening physical attackers such as Great Tusk, Mega Lopunny, and Zamazenta that Garchomp cannot reliably handle, due to the frequency with which they run Ice-type coverage. It also can Wish pass to keep Garchomp healthy. Knock Off users such as Kingambit, Kartana, and Mega Scizor can remove Heavy-Duty Boots from the likes of Zapdos, Moltres, and Terapagos, therefore letting Garchomp's hazards make significant progress by themselves. Fast and powerful offensive teammates such as Tapu Koko and Zamazenta appreciate Garchomp taking a few strong hits from the likes of Mega Charizard Y, Gholdengo, and Heatran, and they can make up for Garchomp's lack of longevity by generating significant offensive pressure. The aforementioned teammates can also help revenge kill certain faster threats that Garchomp dislikes, such as Ogerpon-W, Kartana, and Mega Diancie.

Swords Dance + Loaded Dice.description:
Garchomp serves as a dangerous cleaner due to Loaded Dice giving the possibility of boosting its Speed and dealing damage at the same time. It is able to leverage its great typing to find setup opportunities against Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and unboosted Volcarona. Fire Fang gives it great coverage against Mega Scizor, Corviknight, and Ferrothorn.

Garchomp fits best on bulky offense and hyper offense structures, where its combination of Swords Dance and Scale Shot can quickly overwhelm the opposing team if not taken care of properly. It uses its powerful combination of STAB moves to prey on a lot of bulky Pokemon like Toxapex, Dragonite, and Galarian Slowking, to the benefit of teammates like Volcarona, Raging Bolt, and Iron Valiant. Garchomp's typing leaves it weak to attacks from notable Pokemon like Tapu Lele, Iron Valiant, and Weavile while also not being able to do much against Landorus-T, which can come in very often to drop Garchomp's Attack via Intimidate. Mega Scizor is a great solution to this problem, as it can take hits from the aforementioned Pokemon while being able to consistently force Landorus-T out. Urshifu-R can also be a great teammate for it, as it can lure in Toxapex and Raging Bolt, which then get removed by Garchomp. The Defense drops from Scale Shot leave Garchomp vulnerable to strong priority users like Weavile, Dragonite, and Kingambit. Tapu Lele's Psychic Surge is able to circumvent this issue by making these priority moves unable to hit. In exchange, Garchomp is able to take care of Tapu Lele's counters like Gholdengo and Heatran. Tapu Lele is also able to eliminate Great Tusk, which also presents itself as a threat to Garchomp by being able to shrug off its hits easily and KO it in return with an Ice Spinner.

Choice Band.description:
• Choice Band Garchomp looks for the opportunity to utilize its unique offensive profile to deal massive damage to slower targets such as Volcanion, Iron Hands, and Diancie.
  • Outrage can hit Spectrier, Air Balloon Volcanion, and Hoopa-U.
  • Earthquake hits Raging Bolt, non-Custap Berry Hisuian Goodra, and non-Weakness Policy variants of Metagross and Iron Crown.
  • Scale Shot is able to break Substitute from foes like Volcarona and Ogerpon-W.
  • Iron Head easily breaks through non-physically defensive Diancie, while Poison Jab is helpful for non-Kebia Berry Whimsicott.
  • The Special Defense EVs allow Garchomp to survive a Life Orb Hex from Spectrier after 1 turn of burn damage, while the Speed EVs are enough to outspeed non-Choice Scarf Hoopa-U.
  • Garchomp really appreciates Steel-type partners like Iron Crown and Scizor, as they are able to defeat the common Fairy- and Ice-type Pokemon that are usually able to defeat Garchomp, such as Iron Valiant, Alolan Ninetales, and Kyurem.

Life Orb.description:
• Garchomp's great typing and good Speed tier allow it to check many top threats in 1v1. Life Orb allows Garchomp to change its moves while giving it an important boost in power.
  • Outrage is Garchomp's strongest STAB move, allowing it to blast through neutral targets like Hoopa-U and Galarian Moltres, as well as other Dragon-types slower than it like non-Choice Scarf Haxorus and Kyurem.
  • Scale Shot breaks through Substitute from Pokemon like Volcarona, SubSeed Ogerpon-W, and Serperior, letting Garchomp outspeed and KO them with another move.
  • Earthquake allows Garchomp to pummel Pokemon weak to Ground such as Iron Hands, Hisuian Goodra, Iron Crown, and Volcanion.
  • Swords Dance allows Garchomp to break through Pokemon that would otherwise survive a hit from it and win the matchup, such as Air Balloon Pecharunt and Weakness Policy Metagross.
  • The EVs allow Garchomp to survive an uninvested Stored Power from boosted Weakness Policy Iron Crown after taking Life Orb recoil damage, and maximum Speed allows it to get the jump on the fairly competitive base 100 Speed tier, which includes Pokemon such as Volcarona and Manaphy, as well as all Iron Crown. The rest of the EVs are dumped into Attack.
  • Garchomp loses to Pokemon that can tank its STAB moves and KO it back such as Primarina, as well as faster Pokemon that threaten to OHKO it such as Dragapult, Chien-Pao, and Meowscarada. Teammates like Volcanion, Iron Hands, and Corviknight have great synergy with Garchomp because they cover its weaknesses.

Haban Berry.description:
• Garchomp aims to use its Haban Berry to defeat Dragon-types such as Dragapult and Raging Bolt while retaining its unique offensive profile.
  • Swords Dance helps counter Weakness Policy users such as Metagross as well as Pokemon that use Attack-lowering moves, such as Parting Shot Pecharunt.
  • Outrage should be used against Dragon-types such as Raging Bolt, Roaring Moon, and Dragapult.
  • Earthquake hits Metagross, Pecharunt, Hisuian Goodra, and non-Air Balloon Volcanion for solid damage.
  • Scale Shot breaks any Substitute from Pokemon like Volcarona, Non-Speed Booster Energy Roaring Moon, and Ogerpon-W while raising its Speed, allowing it to beat these Pokemon.
  • The defensive EVs will allow Garchomp to survive a Dragon Darts from Choice Band Dragapult as well as a Draco Meteor from Booster Energy Raging Bolt. The Speed EVs allow Garchomp to always outspeed Raging Bolt.
  • Being a Dragon-type, Garchomp naturally struggles against Fairy-type Pokemon such as Primarina, Iron Valiant, and Alolan Ninetales, as well as physically bulky Pokemon such as Corviknight and Ursaluna. It is wise to pair Garchomp with Pokemon like Volcanion, Pecharunt, and Spectrier to counter these weaknesses.

Swords Dance (Ground).description:
With access to both Swords Dance and Scale Shot, Garchomp is a potent setup sweeper capable of taking on a majority of the metagame. Earthquake and Scale Shot form a strong STAB combination that allows Garchomp to be nearly unwalled; Scale Shot's Speed boost also lets it outspeed threats such as Choice Specs Dragapult and Choice Specs Flutter Mane. Stone Edge and Fire Blast hit foes that can generally shrug off both Earthquake and Scale Shot. Stone Edge hits foes such as Tornadus-T and Pelipper, while Fire Blast deals with Skarmory and Corviknight.

Hippowdon is a necessary teammate for Garchomp, as it is able to switch into foes that can threaten Garchomp such as Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Choice Scarf Dragapult while also setting Stealth Rock to make Garchomp's job of sweeping easier. Landorus's access to Gravity helps Garchomp hit foes that aren't grounded such as the aforementioned Corviknight and Skarmory with its strongest STAB move while also allowing it to hit other foes that hold Air Balloon like Heatran and Gholdengo. Additionally, Landorus's colorful coverage pool allows it to hit foes that can prove to be a major hindrance to Garchomp such as Primarina and Ting-Lu with Sludge Wave and Focus Blast, respectively. Clodsire's position as the premier Water-immune Pokemon on Ground teams makes it a valuable teammate for Garchomp; it can take on foes such as Choice Band Barraskewda and special attackers like Choice Scarf Greninja and Choice Scarf Enamorus that can otherwise scare Garchomp out. Mamoswine and Excadrill both make for an excellent wallbreaking core with Garchomp. Mamoswine is able to take on foes such as Mandibuzz and threaten foes such as Dragapult and Latios with its strong priority in Ice Shard. Excadrill is able to work in tandem with Landorus's Gravity to spam Choice Band Earthquake against Pokemon such as Galarian Weezing to allow Garchomp to sweep easier late-game.

Mixed Attacker (Ground).description:
Mixed Garchomp makes use of its colorful coverage to catch supposed checks such as Amoonguss, Archaludon, and Skarmory off-guard with Fire Blast and Draco Meteor. With Spikes, Garchomp serves as great support, helping both its own offensive prowess as well as its teammates'. Draco Meteor is a powerful nuke that severely weakens and lures physically bulky foes like Sableye, Rotom-W, Great Tusk, and Archaludon after Stamina boosts. Fire Blast allows Garchomp to threaten Ground-immune Steel-types such as Corviknight, Skarmory, and Air Balloon Gholdengo as well as Bug- and Grass-types like Scizor, Forretress, and Amoonguss. Coupled with Earthquake, Garchomp is able to heavily dent Steel and Dragon teams by eliminating specially defensive Gholdengo and Hisuian Goodra.

Hippowdon is a key teammate for Garchomp, as it sets up both Stealth Rock to stack entry hazards with Spikes and sandstorm to help chip down foes. Excadrill is a key offensive partner for Garchomp under sandstorm, as it takes on both Ice- and Fairy-types such as Kyurem, Alolan Ninetales, and Enamorus. In return, Garchomp weakens annoying defensive pieces like Archaludon and Skarmory for it. Clodsire also stacks hazards thanks to Toxic Spikes, is a Water-immune Pokemon that deals with Walking Wake, and aids in both the Fairy matchup thanks to its Poison-typing and against special attackers such as Volcarona and Flutter Mane thanks to its bulk. Garchomp's offensive teammates appreciate its Spikes support so that they can beat foes more easily. Great Tusk provides hazard removal with Rapid Spinand coverage against Dragon-types such as Dragonite and opposing Garchomp thanks to its great physical bulk and access to Ice Spinner. Choice Scarf Great Tusk also performs well against Ice-types, notably outspeeding and handling Weavile. Landorus assists in the Ground mirror matchup thanks to its immunity, and with its colorful coverage, it deals with Dark-, Grass-, and Fairy-types like Nasty Plot Hydreigon, Hydrapple, and Primarina. Landorus also provides U-turn support to safely bring Garchomp in and Gravity Support so that Garchomp can threaten Rotom-W and Zapdos. Mamoswine covers pesky Grass-, Flying-, and Dragon-types such as Sinistcha, Gliscor, Tornadus-T, and Dragapult. Quagsire is a great physical wall, as with its great defensive typing and access to Unaware, it handles physical setup sweepers such as Dragonite, Urshifu-R, and Weavile and wears them down thanks to Toxic.

Choice Scarf (Ground).description:
Choice Scarf Garchomp is a great speed control option on Ground teams, catching faster threats such as Flutter Mane and Latios after Stealth Rock off guard, as well as outpacing and OHKOing bulky Volcarona after a Quiver Dance. Draco Meteor removes Hydreigon, non-Choice Scarf Dragapult, and the aforementioned Latios after Stealth Rock damage. Fire Blast threatens Earthquake-immune Steel-types like Skarmory, Corviknight, and Air Balloon Gholdengo as well as Grass-types such as Brambleghast. Stone Edge OHKOes Volcarona and Articuno while also having an 87.5% chance to OHKO Ogerpon-H after Stealth Rock chip. 72 Attack EVs ensure Garchomp OHKOes Articuno with Stone Edge. Furthermore, the EVs allow Garchomp to 2HKO Toxapex with Earthquake.

Clodsire and Gliscor provide entry hazard support to wear down Garchomp's checks like Ting-Lu, Porygon2, and Alomomola once Heavy-Duty Boots are removed, further wearing them down with Toxic. Landorus threatens Galarian Weezing, Skarmory, and Air Balloon Gholdengo by grounding them via Gravity, allowing Garchomp to clean up Steel and Poison teams late-game. Additionally, Landorus is able to OHKO Archaludon, which can survive an Earthquake from Garchomp and retaliate with its own Draco Meteor. In return, Garchomp threatens Kyurem, Dragonite after minor chip damage, and Latios for these teammates, and can shut down Volcarona attempting to set up on them. Mamoswine can pick off Gliscor, Choice Scarf Meowscarada, and Enamorus, as well as further threatening Flying teams by grounding Skarmory and Corviknight via Smack Down. Additionally, Mamoswine threatens Grass-types like Amoonguss and Sinistcha. Iron Treads checks Fairy-types like Hatterene, Choice Scarf Flutter Mane, and Alolan Ninetales, and can stomach Ice-type moves such as Ice Beam from Greninja and Kyurem, threatening them back with a Steel-type STAB move. Iron Treads also offers entry hazard removal via Rapid Spin and grants Knock Off support. Iron Treads appreciates Garchomp threatening Fire-types like Ogerpon-H, Cinderace, and Volcarona. Quagsire is able to switch into Triple Axel and Ice Spinner from Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Urshifu-R, respectively, and provides chip damage with entry hazards and Toxic. Excadrill threatens the aforementioned Fairy- and Ice-types, provides entry hazard removal, and is able to pick off faster Choice Scarf users that Garchomp cannot outpace such as Meowscarada, Greninja, and Darkrai. Excadrill appreciates another speed control option outside of sand and Garchomp threatening previously mentioned Ground-immune Steel-types that wall Excadrill otherwise.

Offensive (Dragon).description:
Garchomp is a great setup sweeper on Dragon teams by virtue of Swords Dance and the ability to outspeed normally faster threats such as Dragapult, Choice Scarf Gholdengo, and Latios after using Scale Shot. With a Swords Dance boost, it OHKOes Toxapex and 2HKOes specially defensive Ting-Lu and Corviknight. Fire Fang allows Garchomp to threaten bulky Steel-types such as Skarmory and Air Balloon Gholdengo. Alternatively, Stone Edge can be run to target Flying-types such as Articuno, Moltres, and Talonflame.

Archaludon is a great teammate, as it sets up entry hazards with Stealth Rock and, thanks to its ability and amazing physical bulk, takes on physical attackers such as Ogerpon-H, Weavile, and Rillaboom. Garchomp takes on Landorus, Hydreigon, and non-Air Balloon Gholdengo in return. Hisuian Goodra is a great special wall that takes hits from threats to Garchomp such as Kyurem, Flutter Mane, and Greninja and threatens them back. In return, Hisuian Goodra appreciates it dealing with Okidogi and Great Tusk after a Swords Dance boost. Garchomp forms great offensive pairings with Latios, Kyurem, and Dragapult. Latios takes on Fighting-types such as Iron Hands, Keldeo, and Hisuian Lilligant; Kyurem handles Grass- and Flying-types such as Amoonguss, defensive Gyarados, and Landorus-T; and Dragapult is great against pesky threats such as Latios and Flutter Mane. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon is a great partner, as it can take on Iron Valiant, non-Choice Scarf Dragapult, and Enamorus with its Speed and great coverage, and it can pivot Garchomp in on walls like Corviknight with U-turn.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Garchomp fits well onto a variety of teams. It isn't capable of surviving multiple strong attacks, so it relies on partners that allow it to attack without receiving a lot of damage in return. Priority Tailwind setters like Talonflame and Whimsicott are great partners, and they both provide additional Taunt support to disrupt Trick Room setters like Porygon2. Fake Out users like Incineroar disrupt foes for Garchomp. Incineroar additionally provides damage reduction via Intimidate and Parting Shot. Garchomp also works well on balance teams featuring Porygon2, as Garchomp threatens Gholdengo and Incineroar, both of which Porygon2 and its common partners struggle to damage. Garchomp additionally performs well on beatdown teams featuring Dragonite, as Garchomp can freely attack with Earthquake without damaging it.
  • Amoonguss and Vivillon provide redirection and sleep support; Amoonguss is bulkier and has a more consistent way of putting foes to sleep, while Vivillon is faster and is immune to Garchomp's Earthquake. Garchomp pairs well with Porygon2; Porygon2 setting Trick Room can allow Garchomp to attack before threats like Dragapult. Porygon2 additionally deals significant damage to Grass- and Flying-types with Ice Beam and can comfortably survive Earthquake while regaining the lost HP with Recover. Dragonite also synergizes well with Garchomp. Dragonite can deal strong damage with Extreme Speed, allowing Garchomp to secure KOs with Earthquake and removes Grass-types like Rillaboom, which Garchomp struggles to KO, with Tera Blast Flying.
  • Garchomp is threatened by Dragon-, Fairy-, and Ice-type attacks like Dragon Darts and Outrage from Dragapult, Moonblast from Clefable, and Blizzard from Alolan Ninetales. All of these attacks can be switched into by Steel-type partners such as Gholdengo and Kingambit. Garchomp also struggles to damage Flying-types like Pelipper, especially when it isn't using Rock Slide, so a partner like Alolan Ninetales easily threatens Flying-types with Blizzard and Freeze-Dry.

Strategy Comments

  • As a glass cannon, Garchomp's task is to deal as much damage as possible uninterrupted. Garchomp performs best when it outspeeds its foes and when it is supported by redirection, allowing Garchomp to attack freely.
  • Garchomp excels at being an early-game sweeper as well as a late-game cleaner. Garchomp primarily attacks using Earthquake to damage both foes. It uses Stomping Tantrum when Garchomp's partner is vulnerable to the damage from Earthquake or when Grassy Terrain is active. Dragon Claw and Rock Slide are used to damage foes that resist Earthquake and Stomping Tantrum.
  • Dragapult outspeeds and threatens Garchomp. To beat Dragapult, Garchomp needs Tailwind or Trick Room support, allowing it to threaten Dragapult with Dragon Claw before it attacks. A partner Kingambit can also survive an attack from Dragapult and threaten it in return with Kowtow Cleave or before Dragapult attacks with Sucker Punch. Rillaboom is also troublesome for Garchomp, as Grassy Terrain weakens the damage of Earthquake. Garchomp is very reliant on partners like Talonflame and Dragonite to remove Rillaboom, as it struggles to deal threatening spread damage when Grassy Terrain is active.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Garchomp utilizes its high Attack and good Speed to outspeed and greatly weaken foes with powerful spread damage.
  • Using both Stomping Tantrum and Earthquake allows Garchomp to switch between dealing single-target and spread damage. Earthquake, however, is used most effectively when Garchomp's partner is able to use Protect or is immune to Ground-type attacks. Rock Slide is most commonly used by Choice Band Garchomp to threaten Flying-types like Talonflame and Pelipper. It is used as an alternative spread damage attack that doesn't affect Garchomp's partner and is unhindered by Grassy Terrain set by a partner Rillaboom.
  • Life Orb boosts Garchomp's damage, allowing it to threaten an OHKO onto +1 Defense Sneasler with Stomping Tantrum or Earthquake and Dragonite with Dragon Claw. Clear Amulet is used to block Intimidate and Parting Shot from Incineroar. Choice Band provides a greater damage increase than Life Orb, allowing it to threaten an OHKO onto Gholdengo with Stomping Tantrum or Earthquake at the cost of being unable to switch between attacks. The item choice greatly affects Garchomp. Life Orb and Choice Band sets are subject to having its Attack dropped by Incineroar cycling Intimidate and Parting Shot, while the damage from Clear Amulet sets is less.
  • Tera Steel inverts Garchomp's weaknesses to Fairy-, Dragon-, and Ice-type attacks such as Moonblast from Clefable, Outrage from Dragonite, and Blizzard from Alolan Ninetales; additionally, it allows Garchomp to resist Choice Specs-boosted Tera Steel Make It Rain from Gholdengo. Tera Ground increases the damage of Stomping Tantrum and Earthquake, allowing Garchomp to OHKO Gholdengo. Tera Fire provides similar resistances as Tera Steel while not granting a weakness to Fighting-type attacks, and it provides an immunity to burn.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Sweeper.description:
• Thanks to its good bulk, unique Speed tier, and excellent use of Terastallization, Garchomp is a solid offensive threat.

  • Scale Shot: While the Defense drop is troublesome against priority users like Chien-Pao, the Speed boost makes Garchomp far more difficult to revenge kill overall.

  • Iron Head: While Iron Head only deals 10 extra base power of damage against Fairy-types, it works great with Tera Steel and lets Garchomp get past Tera Fairy Levitate Pokemon like Latias.

  • Substitute: Both of Garchomp's STAB attacks are vulnerable to common Tera types; Substitute not only gives it a way to scout for these, but makes setting up on Garganacl and bulky status users much easier.

Other Options

  • Stealth Rock: Despite the offensive nature of this set, Garchomp is still a great setter of Stealth Rock, especially when using Focus Sash.

  • Fire Fang: If your team is extremely weak against Tera Steel Latias or the rare Corviknight or Skarmory, Fire Fang is the only way past them without Terastallization.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium / Low: While Garchomp isn't slow, it's typing leaves it very vulnerable to major speedy threats like Flutter Mane, Chien-Pao, and Iron Bundle, which is an issue Terastallization can flip on its head. If using Focus Sash, Terastallization becomes far less needed.

  • Steel: A Steel Tera type has excellent synergy with Garchomp's typing, letting it more effectively tackle faster Dragon-types, Flutter Mane, Iron Bundle, Mimikyu, and Normal-type priority from Dragonite, Entei, and Ogerpon-H.

  • Fire: While the Stealth Rock weakness is unfortunate against bulkier teams, a Fire Tera type still gives out a vital Fairy and Ice resistance, and gives a powerful Tera Blast against levitating Tera Steel Pokemon like Latias.

  • Fairy: Fairy is an even stronger option against Dragon-types, and gives Garchomp a better matchup against Urshifu-S.

  • Water: Tera Water not only gives that sweet Ice resistance to Garchomp, but it makes Choice Scarf Urshifu-R regret ever using Surging Strikes thanks to Rough Skin!

Items

  • Loaded Dice: Loaded Dice keeps Scale Shot at its most reliable damage output, making it the ideal tool for sweeping.

  • Focus Sash: Surviving shocking attacks with Focus Sash gives Garchomp new sweeping and revenge killing potential, and makes it a reliable setter of Stealth Rock if needed.

  • Life Orb: If used with Tera Steel and Iron Head, Life Orb's damage boost can potentially push Garchomp past the dreaded Charm Flutter Mane with a 2HKO even after the Attack drop!

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry lets Garchomp deal with major Yawn users more easily, such as Swampert and Hippowdon.

Entry Hazard Setter.description:
• While Garchomp is known for its offensive prowess, its access to incredible tools like Rough Skin, Dragon Tail, and a good Speed stat make it a viable alternative to Archaludon and Ting-Lu for setting entry hazards and phazing.

  • Dragon Tail: Dragon Tail has marvelous synergy with setting up hazards, making it the prime choice for a Dragon-type STAB despite the lowered priority.

  • Rock Tomb: Garchomp's solid speed tier means it can fully take advantage of the Speed drops Rock Tomb provides itself, not just as support for teammates.

  • Substitute: Substitute severely punishes foes that rely on Yawn like Hippowdon and Swampert.

  • Iron Head: Beyond pairing well with Tera Steel, Iron Head prevents Garchomp from being walled by Tera Fairy Latios and Latias.

  • Spikes: thanks to its Speed and Dragon Tail, Garchomp is arguably one of the few viable Spikes setters in the metagame! Just make sure using it is worth the cost of losing coverage for the team.

Other Options
  • Bulldoze: Bulldoze is a good alternative speed control option over Rock Tomb for its higher reliability and STAB, but it can make Garchomp rather passive.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: This Garchomp's bulk means it can set up hazards against a wide variety of foes, but Terastallization will be needed to take on some major physical threats, such as Chien-Pao, Urshifu formes, and

  • Water: Tera Water gives Garchomp a vital Ice and Steel resistance without making it weak to Fighting, making it a fantastic option against Chien-Pao and Urshifu-R.

  • Fairy: Fairy Tera type provides Garchomp with an immunity to Dragon-type attacks, making Dragonite less of an awkward guessing game and a solid check to Urshifu-S.

  • Steel: Terastallizing into a Steel-type makes Garchomp resist Dragon-, Ice- and Fairy-type attacks, making it a safer lead against opposing Dragon-type leads and Iron Bundle, at the cost of being vulnerable to Ursaluna-B and Urshifu formes.

EV spreads

  • 252 HP / 244 Def / 12 Spe with Impish: This simple looking EV spread avoids a 2HKO from Life Orb Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash when Garchomp has Terastallized, while outspeeding Adamant Breloom and the rare Timid Magnezone.

  • 252 HP / 116 Def / 140 Spe with Jolly: While this spread doesn't take physical hits as well, it lets Garchomp outspeed Modest Chi-Yu and Adamant Urshifu formes.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Combined with Rough Skin, Rocky Helmet severely punishes contact moves, with Choice Scarf Urshifu-R in particular being a big target.

  • Sitrus Berry: This prevents Tera Water Choice Scarf Urshifu-R from 2HKOing Impish Garchomp.

  • Red Card: With Red Card, Garchomp will be able to phaze foes Terastallizing into a Fairy type once, like Archaludon.

All-Out Attacker.description:
• Garchomp's fantastic Speed tier and power means it doesn't have to set up to be dangerous.

  • Scale Shot: Choice Band appreciates the Speed boost, giving Garchomp another option for late-game cleaning. Even on Choice Scarf sets, Scale Shot is a less risky Dragon-type attack over Outrage, and outspeeding extremely fast threats like Booster Energy Iron Bundle is welcome.

  • Iron Head: With Tera Steel, Iron Head lets Choice Band Garchomp 2HKO Charm Flutter Mane, who can otherwise edge out a victory with Pain Split and repeated Attack drops.

  • Stone Edge versus Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb is fairly weak, but the speed control can be very useful on Choice Scarf variants if sacrificing Garchomp. Stone Edge deals massive damage to common Tera Flying Pokemon such as Gholdengo, and it prevents it from being walled by Tera Fairy Levitate Pokemon like Latias.

Other Options
  • Fire Fang While weak, this is Garchomp's best option against Corviknight and Tera Steel Latiias when not Tera Fire.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium / Low: When using the slower Choice Band variants, Terastallization becomes important for avoiding revenge kills. If using Choice Scarf Garchomp, it's fully capable of revenge killing threats without needing Terastallization, only worrying about Ice Shard from Chien-Pao and Baxcalibur.

  • Steel: Tera Steel is a fantastic defensive Tera Type for Garchomp with key resistances to Ice and Fairy, and it makes Iron Head a much more powerful option.

  • Fire: When combined with Tera Blast, Tera Fire lets even Choice Scarf Garchomp 2HKO Tera Steel Latias. The Fairy and Ice resistance is also very helpful.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy goes all in on the Dragon immunity, no longer being worried about common Fire and Ground coverage from other Dragon-types like Dragonite.

  • Ground: The incredible power boost Earthquake gets from Tera Ground is worth considering, with Choice Band possibly 2HKOing physically defensive Porygon2 and Dondozo with it.

Items

  • Choice Band: Choice Band trades revenge killing for wallbreaking, letting Garchomp deal massive damage to Porygon2 and Ursaluna-B with Outrage.

  • Choice Scarf: With Choice Scarf, Garchomp is able to revenge kill several other major Choice Scarf users, such as Gholdengo, Landorus-T, and Chi-Yu.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Swords Dance variants can consider an Adamant nature on Garchomp for more forgiving odds to OHKO Primarina and Manaphy, though this comes at the risk of getting outsped by maximum Speed Landorus-Therian before a Scale Shot, as well as Deoxys-S and Booster Speed Manaphy after one. Mold Breaker foregoes extra power to hit common Ground-immune ability users like Gholdengo, Tinkaton, and Galarian Weezing.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Scream Tail forces Garchomp out while being able to come in relatively safely against it; similarly, Primarina checks non-Swords Dance variants very well and can punish a switch with Flip Turn. Levitate Tinkaton and Galarian Weezing are completely immune to Garchomp's STAB moves and can threaten it out with Gigaton Hammer and Will-O-Wisp, respectively.

Ground-Immune Steel-types: Against Garchomp variants lacking a Fire-type move, Skarmory, Corviknight, and Levitate Gholdengo can easily set up entry hazards, pivot out, and set up with Nasty Plot, respectively. This is further amplified when the former two have Well-Baked Body, preventing Garchomp from meaningfully making progress.

Swords Dance.description:
Garchomp serves as an incredibly strong Swords Dance sweeper with its excellent STAB moves and well-suited stats. Scale Shot pairs excellently with Loaded Dice to grant Garchomp a potent Dragon-type STAB option while increasing its Speed, preventing would-be revenge killers like Zamazenta and Deoxys-S from forcing it out. Substitute allows Garchomp to set up safely on predicted switches and weak pivoting moves from Corviknight and Manaphy and denies Intimidate; with dual screens support, it also prevents Manaphy from burning Garchomp with Scald. Fire Fang prevents Levitate Gholdengo and Tinkaton, as well as non-Well-Baked Body Corviknight and Skarmory, from checking it. Adaptability is best fit on Substitute sets, where Garchomp can secure an OHKO on Primarina after a Swords Dance and has solid odds to OHKO physically defensive Manaphy after minor chip damage. If Adaptability is used on another teammate, Garchomp can instead employ Dragon's Maw or Sword of Ruin; the former has better odds to OHKO physically defensive Manaphy than any other ability while making Corviknight and Skarmory struggle to consistently stomach multiple Scale Shots, and the latter grants a similar damage boost to Garchomp's STAB moves and Fire Fang simultaneously.

Swords Dance Garchomp fits best on more offensive teams, notably hyper offense teams, where it fits perfectly with other setup sweepers. Notably, Garchomp's raw power allows it to wear down physical walls like Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Pecharunt, opening up opportunities for other physical wallbreakers on the team like Zamazenta and Kingambit. Garchomp's worst matchup is against Scream Tail, especially Choice Scarf variants, which Garchomp struggles to make progress against, requiring teammates that can punish Scream Tail, such as Agility Iron Moth and Double Dance Iron Crown.

Swords Dance (Dragon).description: Garchomp is an incredible wallbreaker and setup sweeper for Dragon teams because of its high Attack stat and access to Swords Dance and Scale Shot. Earthquake threatens Steel- and Poison-types like Gholdengo, Hisuian Goodra, Alolan Muk, and Toxapex. At +2, Fire Fang OKHOes Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor; when boosted by Firium Z, it can also OHKO Skarmory, Corviknight, and Celesteela after Stealth Rock damage. Stone Edge targets Flying-types like Tornadus-T, Mega Aerodactyl, and Galarian Moltres and, in tandem with Rockium Z, allows Garchomp to OHKO Rotom-W at +2 after Stealth Rock damage. Loaded Dice is another option that synergizes with Scale Shot, providing a reliable STAB move to threaten Dragon-types like Kyurem, Mega Latias, and opposing Garchomp. Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra are excellent partners for Garchomp thanks to their partial Steel typing and exceptional bulk aiding against Fairy-types. Archaludon handles Mimikyu, Mega Altaria, and other physical attackers like Weavile, Meowscarada, and Roaring Moon while also providing Stealth Rock support. Hisuian Goodra takes on Tapu Lele, Mega Diancie, and other special attackers like Kyurem and Greninja. Kyurem can break through bulky Ground- and Flying-types like Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Mandibuzz. Teammates like Mega Altaria, Mega Latias, and Latios form formidable wallbreaking cores with Garchomp for their ability to threaten Fighting and Dragon teams. Additionally, Latios and Mega Latias can also wear down or eliminate Pokemon like Mega Venusaur, Skarmory, and Slowbro. In return, Garchomp can eliminate Steel- and Poison-types like Mega Scizor and Toxapex for Mega Altaria and Alolan Muk and Heatran for Mega Latias and Latios. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon can take on faster threats like Choice Scarf Latias and Enamorus, which Garchomp is unable to outspeed even at +1.

Defensive Hazard Setter (Dragon).description: Garchomp offers excellent utility as an entry hazard setter on Dragon teams due to its bulk, access to Spikes and Stealth Rock, and the ability to phaze opponents out via Dragon Tail. Earthquake allows Garchomp to threaten Steel- and Fire-types like Gholdengo, Hisuian Goodra, and Mega Charizard X. Dragon Tail phazes out setup sweepers such as Dragonite, Mega Latias, and Galarian Moltres, dealing a decent amount of chip damage; Roar may be used instead to force Fairy-types out. Fire Blast threatens Steel-types like Mega Scizor and Corviknight. Alternatively, a combination of Spikes and Stealth Rock in conjunction with Dragon Tail or Roar enable Garchomp to cause an incredible buildup of damage. Toxic may be used instead, as it puts opposing walls such as Ting-Lu, Staraptor, and Mandibuzz on a timer. Rocky Helmet in conjunction with Rough Skin provides even more chip damage on top of the entry hazards, heavily damaging foes with multi-hit moves such as Urshifu-R, Meowscarada, and Weavile while also punishing U-turn and Flip Turn from Sneasler and Barraskweda, respectively. The given EV spread permits Garchomp to outpace Pokemon with a base Speed of 100 like Mega Charizard X, Jirachi, and Volcarona while maintaining maximum defensive bulk. Kyurem capatalizes greatly on Garchomp's hazards, appreciating special walls such as Toxapex, Hisuian Goodra, and Alolan Muk being worn down. In return, Kyurem removes Flying-types like Landorus-T, Zapdos, and Mandibuzz and greatly weakens Mega Sableye, preventing it from repeatedly switching in to bounce back hazards being set by Garchomp. Hisuian Goodra provides a Fairy- and Ice-type neutrality, combating foes such as Tapu Koko, Alolan Ninetales, and, notably, Mega Diancie, which also hinders Garchomp's ability to stack hazards. Mega Altaria offers a much-valued immunity to Dragon-type moves, threatening Roaring Moon, Walking Wake, Kommo-o, and Latios while also cherishing Garchomp's hazards and ability to check Poison- and Steel-types like Toxapex, Gholdengo, and Iron Treads. Mega Latias is incredibly threatening in the Flying matchup due to its BoltBeam coverage, though it struggles against Celesteela, while also easily sweeping teams lacking Galarian Moltres via Stored Power and Calm Mind. Roaring Moon is a versatile teammate capable of handling multiple roles; a Choice Scarf set allows it to threaten Fairy-types such as Mega Diancie, Alolan Ninetales, and Tapu Lele via Iron Head, while Dragon Dance sets can overpower physically defensive Pokemon like Rotom-W, Slowbro, and Celesteela. Kommo-o is a great setup sweeper that removes pesky walls such as Porygon2 and Mega Scizor and is a massive threat to opposing Dragon teams. Both Roaring Moon and Kommo-o value Garchomp's entry hazards, with the latter also appreciating the removal of Clodsire. Choice Scarf Latias and Latios are excellent speed control options due to their ability to force switches in the Dragon matchup, luring out Hisuian Goodra for Garchomp. Choice Scarf Archaludon can catch Fairy- and Ice-types like Iron Valiant, Alolan Ninetales, and Kyurem off-guard while also being a secondary speed control option in a pinch in the Dragon mirror matchups.

Mixed Wallbreaker (Ground).description: Mega Garchomp's incredible mixed attacking prowess makes it one of the best wallbreakers available to Ground teams. Draco Meteor's sheer power lets Mega Garchomp land a surprise blow on physically defensive Pokemon such as Slowbro, Archaludon, and Mega Venusaur that would be tough to break otherwise. Fire Blast scorches Ferrothorn, Mega Scizor, and Skarmory, letting Mega Garchomp melt entire Steel teams in tandem with Earthquake. Lastly, Stone Edge turns Mega Garchomp into a force against Flying by hitting defensive Zapdos, Mantine, and Tornadus-T for super effective damage. Choosing the right time to Mega Evolve is important, as base Garchomp is able to revenge kill capital threats to Ground like Kyurem, Mega Charizard Y, and Volcarona thanks to its higher Speed. Hippowdon is a near-mandatory teammate because it lays down Stealth Rock and sets sand, letting Mega Garchomp 2HKO Chansey, Gliscor, and Swampert with its Sand Force-boosted attacks. Gastrodon is able to set Spikes and switch into most Ice-type attacks aimed at Mega Garchomp. In a similar vein, Clodsire provides Toxic Spikes support and resists the Fairy-type moves Mega Garchomp can't afford taking. Mamoswine is an auxiliary wallbreaker that further threatens annoying Pokemon that Mega Garchomp may struggle to break through, like Corviknight, Celesteela, and Porygon2. Revenge killers like Sand Rush Excadrill and Choice Scarf Landorus are able to beat the likes of Mega Diancie and Greninja, which outspeed and KO Mega Garchomp.

Swords Dance (Ground).description: Garchomp's excellent Attack, good Speed, and viable coverage options lets it run a fearsome Swords Dance set that's able to muscle through most walls, and even some entire teams, after a boost. Dragonium Z powers up Outrage to sky-high levels, letting Garchomp blast through non-resistant physical walls like Mega Venusaur and Slowbro at +2 with Devastating Drake. Alternatively, Scale Shot allows Garchomp to work as a late-game sweeper and synergizes better alongside Garchompite because of Mega Garchomp's increased bulk and power as well as lower Speed. Stone Edge rounds out Garchomp's coverage by letting it hit Flying-types such as Mega Charizard Y and Thundurus-T without locking itself into Outrage or relying on multiple Scale Shot hits. However, Fire Fang harms Celesteela, Mega Scizor, and Ferrothorn more and is the better choice should Garchomp Mega Evolve. Entry hazard setters like Clodsire, Gastrodon, and Hippowdon are essential partners to soften the aforementioned walls for Garchomp. In particular, Clodsire and Gastrodon switch into most Fairy- and Ice-type attacks, respectively, and the sand Hippowdon sets further chips the opposition. Life Orb Landorus provides Garchomp Gravity support and relieves pressure off of it by weakening physical walls like Porygon2 and Galarian Weezing. Sand Rush Excadrill outspeeds and KOes the likes of Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Weavile for Garchomp, forming an excellent offensive core alongside it.

balancedhackmons.overview: Mega Garchomp is one of the tier's most powerful wallbreakers thanks to its exceptionally high Attack, great STAB coverage, and strong STAB moves. Its raw power practically mandates a sturdy Fur Coat user to check it, as even Celesteela, which at least resists both STAB types, is 2HKOed by Glaive Rush without Fur Coat. The excellent coverage from its STAB moves also allows it to have good flexibility with its remaining moveslots to snipe checks, and Mega Garchomp also in particular has a strong non-contact STAB move in Precipice Blades. Mega Garchomp also resists Stealth Rock, which allows it to enter the field more often and help differentiate it from other wallbreakers like Mega Blaziken and Mega Gardevoir. It is also able to run a setup set that can sweep weakened teams with the boosted Speed. However, Mega Garchomp has a very middling Speed stat without boosts, which leaves it outsped by several prominent walls, such as the Arceus formes and Zamazenta, mandating teammates that can prevent Strength Sap healing from them. It also means it is vulnerable to revenge killing from every other offensive Pokemon, such as Flutter Mane, Eternatus, and Mega Gardevoir. The setup sets lose out on some initial power and miss out on an often crucial coverage move. Mega Garchomp's STAB moves, while having good coverage, also both have fairly common immunities, requiring correct predictions.
balancedhackmons.comments:
Other Options

Choice Band sets can opt for a Jolly nature to outspeed certain Pokemon like neutral-nature Mega Blaziken and Yveltal, but the loss of power is notable against checks like Fur Coat Arceus formes. Setup sets can have some deviations. Swords Dance + Speed Boost trades lower initial power for boosting faster than Strength Sap's Attack drops and outspeeding Imposter users that are pivoted in, while Flame Orb + Guts provides pseudo status immunity and Knock Off resilience in return for lower damage output and residual damage.

Checks and Counters

Fur Coat: Fur Coat users that are not weak to Mega Garchomp's STAB moves or V-create can stave it off in the short term even if their healing from Strength Sap is denied, especially with Leftovers. Shore Up users can be particularly problematic, since they can handle Mega Garchomp for much longer due to the move not being blockable, requiring it to PP stall out their recovery.

Faster Pokemon: Mega Garchomp's low Speed tier means a majority of the tier can outspeed it. Offensive Pokemon like Mega Gardevoir and Eternatus threaten to OHKO it, while defensive Pokemon like Yveltal and the Arceus formes neutralize it with moves like Knock Off and Strength Sap.

Ground-immune Pokemon: While they fear V-create, as well as Bolt Strike particularly in Celesteela's case, Celesteela and Levitate Steel-types like Arceus-Steel and Melmetal resist Dragon and are immune to Ground. Regenerator Celesteela can scout the Choice Band set's Choice lock, while Fire-immune sets do not fear V-create and can sacrifice itself to burn Mega Garchomp with Beak Blast. These Pokemon also can answer the setup set depending on coverage.

Pixilate: Pixilate users like Iron Valiant and Mega Gardevoir carry Extreme Speed, which can revenge kill Shift Gear and Speed Boost Mega Garchomp variants after Headlong Rush's Defense drops or with Glaive Rush's effect.

Choice Band.description:
Precipice Blades is less accurate than Headlong Rush and requires Sword of Ruin, which hits Imposter users for less damage due to the ability cancelling out, but it is valuable as a non-contact move to avoid Rocky Helmet and moves like Burning Bulwark; Headlong Rush should be used with Tough Claws. V-create is the best option to hit Fur Coat Celesteela and Levitate Steel-types like Arceus-Steel and Melmetal. Sunsteel Strike allows Mega Garchomp to OHKO Fur Coat Mega Audino and Arceus-Fairy after Stealth Rock, while Bolt Strike 2HKOes Fur Coat Mega Slowbro and Dondozo. First Impression offers useful priority that can let Mega Garchomp threaten faster Pokemon like Ultra Necrozma and Mega Alakazam, though other priority moves like Extreme Speed or Shadow Sneak are also options depending on desired targets.

Mega Garchomp is most commonly seen on slower balance teams that can repeatedly pivot it in to gradually break down opposing teams. Thus, slow pivots, including RegenVest users like Dialga-O and Teleport users like Blissey, are excellent to safely bring it in. Mega Garchomp's slow Speed mandates teammates that can deny Strength Sap healing from its checks; Chansey and Blissey can block Strength Sap from most Fur Coat Arceus formes, but they cannot handle other users like Zamazenta and Secret Sword users, making Pokemon like utility Flutter Mane and Magic Bounce Clodsire or Arceus-Poison more reliable.
