Pairing Gliscor with an Ogerpon-W check such as Hydrapple, Sinistcha, or Amoonguss forms a potent core, which should be used alongside stall staples like Dondozo, Blissey, Alomomola, Corviknight, Skarmory, and Clodsire.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the return of the Regulation G format and its powerful restricted threats!
battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Common Teammates

  • Dondozo: Tera Fairy Gliscor and Dondozo make an incredible defensive core against two of the metagame's strongest Choice Band attackers: Koraidon and Urshifu-R.

  • Koraidon: Gliscor has a much easier time playing next to Koraidon's sunny weather, as the weather effect is a huge deterrent to one of Gliscor's biggest checks in Urshifu-R.

  • Eternatus: Eternatus is a great defensive switch for Gliscor's Urshifu-R problem. On the other hand, Earthquake Gliscor can pressure Steel-types to Terastallize into something that Eternatus can more easily deal with. Finally, Tera Fairy Eternatus can pair with Gliscor to make a good defensive core against Miraidon.

Speed EV Benchmarks

  • 124 or 36+ Spe: This outspeeds uninvested Ogerpon formes.

  • 140 or 44+ Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Dragonite.

  • 188 or 92+ Spe: This outspeeds Modest Glimmora.

  • 172+ Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Urshifu formes.

  • 188+ Spe: This outspeeds Timid Glimmora.

  • 196+ Spe: This outspeeds Modest Chi-Yu.

  • 228+ Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Landorus-T.

Glis.description:
• With its great typing and incredible longevity thanks to Poison Heal, Gliscor is a frustratingly potent defensive threat that may be the single largest cause of matches being determined by the match timer running out!

  • Toxic: Gliscor is one of few Pokemon to be given Toxic via TM, allowing it to put opposing walls on a timer while it stays healthy itself.

  • Protect + Substitute: Stalling turns with Protect + Substitute allows Gliscor to keep itself healthy despite not having access to a manual healing move. This also pairs well with Toxic to keep Gliscor safe as the opponent succumbs to poison.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake allows Gliscor to threaten Steel- and Poison-types that are otherwise immune to its Toxic-stalling antics.

Other Options

  • Knock Off: Knock Off’s item removal can allow Gliscor to be more of a team player, removing items such as Leftovers and Rocky Helmet to assist a teammate’s sweep.

  • Baton Pass: Gliscor’s immense longevity makes it particularly well suited to passing Substitutes, bolstering its team’s defense while giving them turns to set up.

EV Spreads

  • 228 HP / 36 Def / 244 SpD with Impish: The physical bulk on this set allows Gliscor to live Jolly Choice Band Koraidon's Outrage on all but the highest damage roll. The special bulk gives Gliscor roughtly a 19% chance to place a Substitute after getting hit with Timid Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage.

  • 228 HP / 4 Atk / 28 Def / 20 SpD / 228 Spe With with Jolly: The Speed investment allows Gliscor to outspeed major foes like Jolly Landorus-T and Adamant Urshifu-R, making it more of a nuisance against faster-paced teams at the cost of some survivability. Enough special bulk is maintained to avoid the OHKO from Timid Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage. The leftover EVs are mostly used for some extra physical bulk, but can be reallocated to maximize Speed if desired.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Gliscor's natural immunities to troublesome attacks like Electro Drift, Volt Switch, and Fissure are huge benefits, but its vulnerability to popular multi-hit and sound-based attacks means Terastallization has strong defensive utility.

  • Steel: Tera Steel allows Gliscor to resist Ice-, Fairy-, and Dragon-type moves, giving it increased survivability against a wider array of threats, with the resistance against the Substitute-ignoring Hyper Voice from Ursaluna-B being a big boon. However, Steel leaves it more vulnerable to Fighting-types like Urshifu-S and Fire-types like Ogerpon-H. When using Tera Steel, make sure not to Terastallize on the first turn, or else Toxic Orb will fail!

  • Water: Tera Water gives Gliscor crucial Ice- and Water-type resistances, allowing it to get emergency Toxics off against threats like Urshifu-R and Primarina, both of whom can ruin Substitute with Surging Strikes and Sparkling Aria respectively. It's also a great response against Chien-Pao, especially since Substitute and Protect scout against Electric Tera Blast.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy completely negates Dragon-type attacks, making it impossible for Scale Shot and Outrage to overwhelm Gliscor. Tera Fairy also retains Gliscor's Fighting-type resistance, which can be important for bulky cores trying to defend against Choice Band users like Koraidon and Urshifu-R.

  • Dark: Tera Dark's Ghost-type resistance and Psychic-type immunity can make handling Calyrex-S more feasible. Neutralizing Psychic Noise is particularly notable for keeping Poison Heal working.

Stallbreaker (Flying).description: Gliscor is a great addition to Flying teams, as its part-Ground typing allows it to be a useful asset in the Electric and Rock matchups, threatening the likes of Magnezone, Zeraora, and Hisuian Arcanine. Knock Off removes important items such as Heavy-Duty Boots from Volcarona, Tornadus-T, and Dragonite and Leftovers from Corviknight. Taunt shuts down entry hazard attempts as well as attempts to remove its teammates' hazards with Defog. Roost grants Gliscor a form of longevity on top of Poison Heal. 244 HP and 20 Defense EVs allow it to survive a V-create from Choice Band Victini, while 8 Speed EVs outspeed Modest Raging Bolt. Corviknight and Mantine remove hazards with Defog so Gliscor can switch in more safely. Additionally, Corviknight provides slow pivoting and threatens Fairy-types like Tapu Lele and Mega Diancie, while Mantine handles Water-types like Barraskewda and Mega Swampert. Thundurus-T takes pressure off Gliscor by providing an additional Electric immunity; it also threatens Water- and Flying-types such as Urshifu-R, Swampert, Mantine, and Corviknight with its coverage. It appreciates Gliscor removing Clodsire and blocking entry hazard setup with Taunt. Late-game sweepers such as Mega Charizard Y and Galarian Moltres appreciate Gliscor's stallbreaking against Toxapex, Clodsire, and Heatran so they can start their own sweep. In return, Mega Charizard Y handles Ferrothorn, Gastrodon, and Alolan Ninetales, while Galarian Moltres handles Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Gholdengo, Ceruledge, and Slowbro.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Gliscor could opt to use a Swords Dance + Facade set, which allows it to break through most stall teams, and Substitute Ho-Oh. These sets frequently utilize Tera Normal, which boosts the power of Facade while providing an immunity to Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage. However, without entry hazards, Protect, or Toxic, Gliscor is much weaker when facing any other team structure. Gliscor may also use a specially defensive set, which allows it to survive hits from Modest Draco Meteor Miraidon and Calyrex-S and threaten with Knock Off. Nevertheless, without as many EVs in Defense, Gliscor is much worse at dealing with the physical attackers it would normally check. Gliscor can choose to use U-turn over Knock Off or Earthquake, which helps with positioning and healing low-HP Regenerator Pokemon. However, if Gliscor chooses not to use Knock Off or Earthquake, it is far less capable against opposing stall teams or Taunt + Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, respectively. Gliscor could opt to use Tera Rock, which allows it to wall Substitute Ho-Oh, but since it is uncommon and Tera Rock makes Gliscor weak to Ting-Lu's Earthquake, Gliscor tends to see more value in Tera Fairy or Tera Water.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Special attackers like Calyrex-S, Miraidon, Kyogre, and Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy threaten OHKOs or massive damage on Gliscor, due to its poor special bulk.

Calyrex-I: Calyrex-I's super effective Glacial Lance threatens an OHKO on Gliscor. However, Gliscor may switch in against Calyrex-I to stall Trick Room turns for teammates like Foul Play Mandibuzz and Skeledirge.

Hatterene: Hatterene can bounce back Gliscor's entry hazards while setting up Calm Mind boosts and threatening with Baton Pass. Pain Split sets can also heal off of Gliscor's recovery to prevent chip damage.

Defensive.description:
Due to Gliscor's diverse defensive capabilities and extensive utility movepool, it cements itself as a top-tier pick on stall teams. Toxic helps Gliscor put setup sweepers like Swords Dance Koraidon and Extreme Killer Arceus on a timer while also crippling defensive Pokemon like Ho-Oh and defensive Arceus formes. Knock Off removes Heavy-Duty Boots from the likes of Ho-Oh and Eternatus, chipping them down especially when used in combination with entry hazards. Knock Off also removes Koraidon's Loaded Dice, making Koraidon easier to check for teammates like Skeledirge, and it threatens to OHKO Calyrex-S. Alternatively, Earthquake provides consistent damage against foes like Taunt + Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, Zacian-C, and Kingambit, which Gliscor is otherwise incapable of damaging effectively. Protect allows Gliscor to maximize Poison Heal recovery while scouting the sets of opposing Pokemon, particularly Kyogre, Koraidon, and Miraidon. Protect also grants Gliscor the ability to activate its Toxic Orb against Pokemon it would normally be forced to switch out against, particularly special attackers that may threaten an OHKO on Gliscor. Spikes is the preferred hazard on Gliscor due to its longevity, which allows it to set up three layers of Spikes more consistently than its peers. However, if a team has a different Spikes setter, like Skarmory or Clodsire, Gliscor can also use Toxic Spikes, which can alleviate pressure off its teammates by putting key wallbreakers on a timer. Tera Fairy grants Gliscor an immunity to Koraidon's Scale Shot and Outrage, as well as Miraidon's Draco Meteor, which can be helpful in an emergency. Tera Water grants Gliscor a resistance to Koraidon's Flare Blitz, Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, and Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance. Choice Band Koraidon also frequently uses Tera Fire Flare Blitz to catch Gliscor off-guard and OHKO it, which Tera Water can avoid. Gliscor's HP EVs maximize Poison Heal recovery, while the remaining 12 EVs are invested in Special Defense.

With its considerable support options and defensive proficiencies, Gliscor finds itself on the vast majority of stall teams. Knock Off, in combination with entry hazards set by itself or its teammates, allows Gliscor to make progress against opposing Heavy-Duty Boots Pokemon. Thus, Gliscor is an invaluable teammate to hazard setters like Clodsire and Blissey. Furthermore, Gliscor's ability to switch in against physical attackers like Choice Scarf Koraidon, Ho-Oh, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground helps remove load from Pokemon like Alomomola and Skeledirge that may otherwise be overwhelmed against a combination of physical attacks. In addition, Gliscor's ability to absorb Knock Off, once it activates its Toxic Orb, makes it the most important tool a stall team has when facing another stall team. Without Gliscor, the combination of Knock Off and hazards can slowly wear teams down. Gliscor is particularly vulnerable to special attackers like Calyrex-S, Miraidon, and Kyogre, due to its relatively poor special bulk. Teammates like specially defensive Tera Grass Ho-Oh, Blissey, and Clodsire can assist with this weakness, as they easily soak up special attacks. Blissey and Clodsire also help set hazards, which aid Gliscor to progress. If Gliscor is not running Earthquake, it is also vulnerable to Zacian-C, which can use it as setup fodder. Teammates like Unaware Skeledirge and Dondozo ignore Zacian-C's Swords Dance boosts, which let them wall it, while threatening it with burns or Fissure, respectively. Similarly, Kingambit can pose issues for stall teams if Gliscor chooses not to use Earthquake, and Tera Fire sets are immune to Skeledirge’s Will-O-Wisp. Thus, stall teams can force Kingambit to Terastallize in order to put it on a timer with Toxic. Gliscor is weak to setup sweepers with Taunt or strong attacks, including Swords Dance Koraidon and Swords Dance Arceus. Alomomola, Skeledirge, and Dondozo all help in covering for this weakness. Furthermore, Dondozo and Alomomola also help Gliscor against Calyrex-I, whose super effective Glacial Lance threatens an OHKO on Gliscor. Gliscor is also unable to effectively damage offensive Substitute Ho-Oh, whose powerful Tera Flying Brave Bird 2HKOes Gliscor. Garganacl is the most effective Substitute Ho-Oh counter and permanently walls it while setting hazards.

Substitute.description:
Mamoswine functions as an excellent wallbreaker thanks to its nearly unwallable Ice / Ground STAB combination and high base Attack, allowing it to break through common threats such as Hydrapple, Heatran, Toxapex, and Skeledirge. Ice Shard is a reliable priority move that allows Mamoswine to bypass its below average Speed to revenge kill foes such as Ogerpon-C, Latios, and Thundurus-T. Trailblaze not only raises Mamoswine's otherwise subpar Speed but also allows it to hit Rotom-W, the only Pokemon in the tier that can wall Mamoswine's STAB combination. Knock Off can be used as an alternative to cripple Rotom-W and other checks like Slowking by removing their items, allowing Mamoswine or another teammate to break through them more efficiently later on. Substitute can also be used as an option to force switches and grant Mamoswine a safety net, though it must be used in tandem with Leftovers to preserve Mamoswine's longevity. Never-Melt Ice further boosts the power of Mamoswine's Ice-type STAB attacks. Heavy-Duty Boots can be used instead to prevent Mamoswine from being chipped down by hazards, though it comes at the price of lower power. Thick Fat reduces the damage Mamoswine takes from Hisuian Arcanine's Flare Blitz and Heatran's Magma Storm, allowing it to easily OHKO them back while also allowing it to take Heat Wave from Tornadus-T better. Tera Grass boosts the power of Trailblaze while allowing Mamoswine to tank powerful Water-type moves from foes like Greninja, Azumarill, and Quaquaval. It also helps Mamoswine handle Grass-types like Hydrapple and Ogerpon-C better, though it also makes Mamoswine weak to Tornadus-T's Hurricane and Lokix's First Impression. Tera Ice bolsters the power of Mamoswine's Ice-type moves even further, allowing it to score OHKOs with Ice Shard on Ogerpon-C, Latios, and Tornadus-T after Stealth Rock. Tera Fairy can be used to give Mamoswine a resistance to Fighting-type moves, allowing it to better handle Cobalion and Quaquaval while still taking neutral damage from Water-type moves.

Mamoswine fits best on bulky offense and offensive teams that appreciate its ability to wallbreak with its powerful STAB combination. Mamoswine's lackluster Speed and poor defenses make it hard for it to get in safely, which can be made easier by pairing it with pivots such as Lokix, Thundurus-T, Tornadus-T, and Slowking. Lokix also helps revenge kill threats like Weavile and Greninja that cannot be revenge killed with Ice Shard, and the latter three also handle checks like Quaquaval and Cobalion that threaten Mamoswine. Mamoswine's biggest checks are Water-types like Rotom-W, Slowking, and Greninja, so Grass- and Electric- types like Hydrapple, Ogerpon, Serperior, and the aforementioned Thundurus-T make great partners to handle these threats. Entry hazard setters such as Cobalion, Tinkaton, and Excadrill help to soften up threats like Latios and Assault Vest Tornadus-T for Mamoswine in the late-game via chip from Stealth Rock. Excadrill in particular makes a great partner, as it can put pressure on Rotom-W with Mold Breaker Earthquake and spin hazards away. In return, Mamoswine handles threats like Hydrapple and Sinistcha, making it easier for Swords Dance Excadrill to clean up teams late in the game. Offensive teammates such as Sandy Shocks and Latios make for great partners, with the former providing hazard support, an offensive check to Cobalion and Scizor, and pivot support with Volt Switch to safely bring Mamoswine in against Hydrapple and Latios, while the latter revenge kills Quaquaval and Cobalion for Mamoswine while working in tandem with it to overwhelm their shared check, Slowking.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ground

Stone Edge slices through Articuno, Moltres, and Kyurem. Heavy Slam can make Galarian Weezing an unsafe switch-in as well as OHKOing Hatterene.

Ice

Ice Shard can be used for additional priority, picking off faster Choice Scarf users such as Meowscarada and Enamorus.

All-out Attacker (Ground).description:
All-out attacker Mamoswine is an incredibly versatile wallbreaker and revenge killer, capable of switching between moves unlike Choice Band sets. Icicle Crash threatens Grass-type Pokemon such as Sinistcha, Brambleghast, and Amoonguss as well as Flying-types like Gliscor, Tornadus-T, and specially defensive Corviknight, which is 2HKOed after Stealth Rock and minor chip damage. Ice Shard cleans up faster threats such as Landorus, Dragonite once Multiscale has been broken, and Meowscarada after Stealth Rock and one layer of Spikes. Smack Down removes foes like Volcarona and 2HKOes Articuno as well as Moltres. Additionally, Smack Down allows Mamoswine to ground Skarmory, physically defensive Corviknight, and Galarian Weezing to threaten them via Earthquake. Knock Off may be used instead to force progress by removing vital held items such as Corviknight's Leftovers, Alomomola's Heavy-Duty Boots, and Porygon2's Eviolite. Stone Edge is an option to guarantee an OHKO on the aforementioned Smack Down targets, especially defensive Volcarona. Never-Melt Ice improves the damage output of Icicle Crash and Ice Shard, ensuring the aforementioned damage roll against specially defensive Corviknight and enabling Ice Shard to KO Meowscarada after Stealth Rock and a layer of Spikes.

Mamoswine appreciates Clodsire's Water Absorb and neutrality to Grass-type moves that allow it to check Barraskewda, Primarina, and Ogerpon-W. Furthermore, Clodsire provides entry hazard support, similar to Hippowdon. Hippowdon can also passively wear down threats like Flutter Mane, Spectrier, and Iron Valiant with chip damage from Sand Stream and offers phazing with Whirlwind, which Ting-Lu can do as well. In return, Mamoswine combats dangerous wallbreakers like Meowscarada, Latios, and Kyurem that threaten these teammates. Landorus can pressure physical walls while also setting up Gravity to allow Mamoswine to hit Skarmory, Corviknight, and Moltres without needing to use Smack Down. Landorus appreciates Mamoswine's ability to threaten Gliscor and Assault Vest Tornadus-T. Excadrill and Mamoswine work together to take care of Ice-types like Kyurem and Articuno. Excadrill removes strong Fairy-types such as Iron Valiant and Flutter Mane in sand while valuing Mamoswine in the Flying matchup and for its speed control via Ice Shard outside of sand. Choice Scarf Great Tusk removes non-Choice Scarf Greninja, Meowscarada, and Hisuian Samurott as well as Air Balloon Heatran and Iron Treads. Quagsire provides further support using hazards and spreads Toxic, limiting the longevity of foes such as Rotom-Wash, Primarina, and Sableye. Iron Treads offers hazard removal via Rapid Spin and can help fight off Flutter Mane, Kyurem, and Choice Specs Greninja.

Choice Scarf (Ice).description:
Choice Scarf Mamoswine is a specialized niche option for Ice teams, being just fast enough to provide relevant speed control, notably just outspeeding Choice Specs Dragapult with a Jolly nature while helping shore up the awful Fire matchup with fast and strong EdgeQuake coverage. In addition, it offers nice role compression, combining a potential Stealth Rock user and a Fire neutrality due to Thick Fat in one slot. Earthquake is Mamoswine's most powerful and consistent STAB option, OHKOing important targets like Choice Band Sneasler, Flutter Mane, and Hisuian Goodra. Stone Edge completes EdgeQuake coverage and notably hits important targets such as Ogerpon-H after some chip, Moltres, and bulky Volcarona, which Choice Scarf Mamoswine outspeeds even after a Quiver Dance. Icicle Crash serves as an alternate STAB move, OHKOing Dragapult and Latios. The last slot can be Knock Off for better utility and a way to consistently hit Latios and Latias, or Stealth Rock if the team lacks another user.

Alolan Ninetales is a nice teammate with Aurora Veil, allowing Mamoswine to use Thick Fat a bit better, notably being able to take offensive Volcarona's Fire Blast under Aurora Veil even at +1. Furthermore, Alolan Ninetales also deals with some threats that bother Choice Scarf Mamoswine, such as Pelipper and Urshifu-R. Choice Scarf Mamoswine appreciates additional speed control options such as Thunder Wave Froslass, as it's a bit slow for speed control, being outsped by almost every other relevant Choice Scarf user in the format. Notably, Focus Sash Froslass can use Thunder Wave or Will-O-Wisp on common threats aiming to anti-lead the ubiquitous Alolan Ninetales such as Choice Scarf Kleavor, Choice Scarf Iron Boulder, Trailblaze Ogerpon-H, and Choice Scarf Greninja. In addition, the chip from Froslass's Spikes helps secure some OHKOs; for example, important targets such as Ogerpon-H, Choice Specs Greninja, and Kommo-o are all put into OHKO range after Spikes damage. Avalugg is a nice teammate to remove hazards for Mamoswine's team; furthermore, Avalugg can take some of the physical hits coming from faster Choice Scarf users such as Meowscarada, Iron Boulder, Sneasler, and Roaring Moon. Strong special attackers like Kyurem can break down physical walls for Mamoswine, such as Skarmory, Galarian Weezing, Quagsire, and Avalugg.

Choice Band (Ground).description:
Mamoswine is a great offensive option for Ground teams thanks to its huge Attack stat, access to priority, and unique STAB combination. Thick Fat's extremely valuable Ice resistance allows Mamoswine to switch into foes like Articuno and Alolan Ninetales. Icicle Crash shreds Grass-type Pokemon, such as Amoonguss and Sinistcha, and Flying-type Pokemon, such as Mandibuzz and Gliscor. Ice Shard allows Mamoswine to stand its ground against faster Pokemon such as both Landorus formes, Meowscarada, and Dragapult. Knock Off helps it deal with walls that may take a bit more time to whittle down, such as Alomomola and Corviknight, as well as creates permanent progress against Pokemon such as Galarian Weezing and Porygon2, which both rely heavily on their items.

Mamoswine greatly appreciates entry hazard support from Pokemon like Quagsire and Hippowdon, as the extra damage could be the difference in damage benchmarks such as OHKOing Flutter Mane and Meowscarada with Ice Shard, 2HKOing on Corviknight with Icicle Crash, and OHKOing Toxapex with Earthquake. Additionally, Quagsire can deal with Belly Drum Azumarill and Urshifu-R, while Hippowdon can apply additional chip damage via sand. Mamoswine fits nicely on sand teams, as it can help Excadrill deal with Flying-types and, when sand is not active, faster threats such as Meowscarada and Dragapult. Clodsire is a good teammate for Mamoswine, as it can switch into Water- and Fighting-type attacks from Pokemon like Keldeo, Sneasler, and Walking Wake that would otherwise make quick work of Mamoswine, as well as providing Toxic poison and hazard support. Iron Treads is another good teammate for Mamoswine, as it keeps hazards off the field in order to prevent Mamoswine from being chipped down, and it sets up hazards of its own. Alternatively, Choice Scarf Iron Treads outspeeds Iron Valiant and Flutter Mane, which both threaten Mamoswine, and can deal super effective damage to them. Choice Scarf Great Tusk is another teammate that pairs well with Mamoswine; Great Tusk is able to outspeed and OHKO Pokemon that check Mamoswine such as Choice Specs Greninja and Cinderace. Once faster threats have been taken care of, Mamoswine will have an easy time breaking the opposing team with its extremely powerful attacks. Gliscor can absorb status moves as well as Fighting-type attacks, which Mamoswine does not want to deal with. Gliscor is also able to support it with Spikes, Toxic, and Knock Off, so foes have a harder time switching in. Landorus forms a potent offensive core with Mamoswine, destroying physical walls such as Quagsire and Archaludon, while Mamoswine deals with special walls such as Gliscor and Blissey. Additionally, Landorus can set Gravity for Mamoswine so that it can freely spam Earthquake and a perfectly accurate Icicle Crash. Lastly, Sandy Shocks is capable of dealing with Pokemon such as Pelipper and Corviknight, as well as providing hazard and Gravity support.

Entry Hazard Support (Ice).description:
Mamoswine is a fantastic pick on Ice teams that provides colorful utility with its access to Stealth Rock and immunity to Electric-type attacks along with great coverage against Steel-types. Earthquake enables Mamoswine to clear troublesome Steel-types such as non-Air Balloon Heatran, Hisuian Goodra, and Bisharp, which are a great threat to Ice teams. Ice Shard lets Mamoswine get around its mediocre Speed stat and allows it to finish off faster weakened threats such as Dragapult, Meowscarada, Landorus formes, and Tornadus-T. Smack Down cripples Flying-types that are weak to Ground-type moves without the immunity such as Zapdos and Corviknight. In addition to this, Smack Down threatens foes such as Articuno, Moltres, and Volcarona. Alternatively, Icicle Crash gives Mamoswine leverage to eliminate foes such as Roaring Moon, Mandibuzz, Ting-Lu, and Hippowdon. The given EVs allow Mamoswine to outlast defensive Corviknight by getting 3HKOed by Body Press after Leftovers recovery, survive +1 Flamethrower from offensive Volcarona and OHKO it in return with Smack Down, and outspeed maximum Speed Adamant Iron Hands.

Alolan Ninetales is a great partner for Mamoswine, as it sets snow and Aurora Veil, allowing Mamoswine to stand longer on the battlefield to take on foes such as Ceruledge and easily set up entry hazards. It also threatens Fighting-type foes such as Great Tusk and Urshifu-R. Cloyster is a great ally that can become very threatening after a Shell Smash, taking care of Fire-type threats such as Ogerpon-H and Ceruledge. Similarly, Cetitan is another partner that can set up with Belly Drum to become very fierce and wipe out foes such as Metagross and Iron Treads. Avalugg provides Mamoswine a clean path to enter by removing hazards with the help of Rapid Spin, while the IronPress combination allows it to outlast physical attacking Water-types foes such as Ogerpon-W and Barraskewda. Kyurem and Weavile are offensive partners for Mamoswine, with Kyurem being a special-attacking powerhouse that removes a lot of annoying Pokemon such as Archaludon and Toxapex, while Weavile is a great physical attacker that dismantles threatening foes such as Gholdengo and Gallade. Froslass is an ally that serves as a suicide lead, providing great utility by setting up hazards with Spikes; spreading status with Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave on foes like Dragapult, Sneasler, and Excadrill; and eliminating foes with Destiny Bond, allowing Mamoswine to wreak havoc more easily.

Assault Vest (Ground).description:
The given EV spread allows for Mamoswine to survive a choice specs Latios Draco Meteor and get the OHKO in reponse with Icicle Crash.

This is a winning set from the Monotype Rising sets project. This will be updated as we work on new analyses. Stay tuned!

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Choice Band lets Mamoswine either pick up 2HKOs against Intimidate Pecharunt and RegenVest Manaphy more easily with Sword of Ruin-boosted Earthquake, or OHKO Roaring Moon and Meowscarda with Technician-boosted Ice Shard. Choice Band unfortunately comes with the trade-off of not having a reliable Icicle Spear, although it can be stronger compared to Loaded Dice if it hits enough times. Throat Chop with Sword of Ruin and Bite with Technician can help to deal with Levitate Gholdengo but are otherwise not as useful in most other situations.

Checks and Counters

Fast Pokemon: Although they can’t switch in on Mamoswine reliably, most faster Pokemon can easily take advantage of Mamoswine's typing and take it down. Notable examples include Cinderace, Zamazenta, and Iron Moth.

Ground-immune Steel-types: Besides Corviknight and Skarmory, most Ground-immune Steel-types are able to wall all of Mamoswine’s attacks. Notable examples include Gholdengo, Cobalion, and Heatran.

Wallbreaker.description:
Mamoswine's amazing offensive typing and high Attack combine to make a decent wallbreaker, with it being able to easily take down some of the bulkiest Pokemon in the tier such as Great Tusk, Pecharunt, and Fluffy Corviknight. Adaptability leverages Mamoswine's strong STAB combination in conjunction with Life Orb to be a wallbreaker with a unique offensive typing that doesn't take up a Sword of Ruin slot. Alternatively, Technician paired with Loaded Dice turns Icicle Spear into a strong, consistent STAB move capable of reliably 2HKOing Fluffy Corviknight while also boosting the power of Ice Shard and Trailblaze. Alternatively, Sword of Ruin notably boosts the power of Mamoswine's Earthquake, allowing it to reliably 2HKO RegenVest Manaphy with Stealth Rock up. Ice Shard is mainly used as a way for Mamoswine to revenge kill weakened Pokemon like Latios, Roaring Moon, and Zapdos. Stealth Rock lets it set entry hazards without worry due to it threatening common hazard removers like Fluffy Corviknight and Great Tusk, while Knock Off allows it to cripple potential switch-ins like Levitate Gholdengo and Pecharunt. Trailblaze allows for Mamoswine to pose as a bulky physical cleaner to broken-down teams due to it becoming faster than Pokemon like Meowscarada, Cinderace, and Cobalion. A Jolly nature allows for Mamoswine to get the jump on non-Ground-immune Heatran and Modest Gholdengo, while an Adamant nature lets it take more reliable 2HKOs on Fluffy Leftovers Corviknight and Skarmory as well as Regenerator Manaphy, each after Stealth Rock damage.

Offensive Pokemon such as Roaring Moon, Zapdos, and Latios all appreciate Mamoswine for being able to take down their checks like Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Ting-Lu; additionally, each of these Pokemon can provide an easy way for Mamoswine to get onto the field through their pivoting moves. With Mamoswine’s low Speed and bad defensive typing, it struggles to deal with most faster Pokemon such as Zamazenta, Iron Moth, and Gholdengo, so having Pokemon like Pecharunt, Hisuian Goodra, and Swampert can help to patch up these weaknesses. Mamoswine also struggles to deal with Ground-immune Steel-types like Gholdengo, Cobalion, and Empoleon, so it helps to have Fighting- or Fire-type Pokemon like Zamazenta and Iron Moth.

Choice Band (Ground).description: Mamoswine is an incredible Choice Band user for Ground-type teams thanks to its raw power and excellent STAB coverage, making it a force to be reckoned with. Ice Shard helps it pick off faster Pokemon that can threaten it, such as Thundurus-T, Enamorus, and Latias. Knock Off heavily weakens Pokemon reliant on their items, such as Corviknight, Porygon2, and Celesteela, making them much easier for Mamoswine to take advantage of later on. Alternatively, Superpower is Mamoswine’s best option for beating bulky Pokemon such as Blissey, Ferrothorn, and Rotom-W. Landorus is an outstanding teammate for Mamoswine to have, as it can threaten physical walls Mamoswine would rather not face, such as Mega Venusaur, Tapu Fini, and Slowbro, and help it beat Ground-immune Pokemon such as Skarmory and Rotom-W with Gravity. Scale Shot Mega Garchomp and Sand Rush Excadrill appreciate Mamoswine wearing down bulky Pokemon such as Celesteela and Gliscor for them to clean up late-game. Ting-Lu and Hippowdon help Mamoswine do its job more effectively by setting up entry hazards, allowing it to net more KOs. They also can rack up chip damage with Whirlwind, and Hippowdon sets sand for further residual damage. Clodsire and Gastrodon can safely switch into Water-type moves that threaten Mamoswine, and they can set hazards to help its wallbreaking. Clodsire, in particular, is able to switch into Grass-type attacks from the likes of Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Ogerpon-W, and Brambleghast, and it can inflict status and set Toxic Spikes up, limiting the longevity of stall Pokemon such as Slowbro, Ting-Lu, and Blissey. Gastrodon is an excellent Water Absorb user that can ease up Water matchups for Mamoswine, as it can safely wall Water-type Pokemon such as Choice Specs Walking Wake, Dondozo, and Mega Swampert with the proper moveset to take advantage of later on.

Entry Hazard Lead (Ice).description: This is a sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

ru.overview: Glitching its way into SV RU, Porygon-Z acts as a niche, yet deadly, setup sweeper and wallbreaker. Its monstrous Special Attack stat combined with Download and Agility lets Porygon-Z clean up weakened teams, while its Normal typing lets it maintain a reliable STAB move with Tera Blast, even if it needs to Terastallize. Additionally, Porygon-Z's movepool includes several solid coverage options, such as Shadow Ball to nail Ghost-types and Jirachi as well as Thunderbolt to muscle through bulky Water-types like Empoleon and Volcanion. Porygon-Z is let down by its poor bulk and defensive typing, which make finding setup opportunities difficult due to the fact that it risks being dented by even defensive Pokemon like Slowbro and Hippowdon. Additionally, Porygon-Z's middling Speed tier leaves it outsped by common Pokemon, like Galarian Zapdos, Gengar, Jirachi, and Entei, without any Agility boosts; these factors mean that Porygon-Z's team must dedicate resources in order to facilitate a sweep. Porygon-Z also faces competition from more reliable setup sweepers; in particular, Armarouge has a stronger STAB combination and can boost its Speed without having to use a moveslot thanks to Weak Armor.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Porygon-Z can run a bulkier Agility set with 128 HP EVs alongside Recover, letting it stay on the field longer while still outspeeding Choice Scarf Galarian Zapdos at +2 Speed. However, its iffy natural bulk and poor defensive typing make other options like Calm Mind Reuniclus, Suicune, and Slowbro better choices for bulky setup sweepers. Nasty Plot can be used to further bolster Porygon-Z's already high Special Attack, letting it muscle through traditional checks like Umbreon, though its lacking Speed, leaving it outrun by threats like Krookodile and Mimikyu, makes it risky to use. A Double Dance set with both Nasty Plot and Agility is a usable option, though Porygon-Z struggles with the inability to fit coverage, especially if it does not Terastallize. Porygon-Z can opt to run a Choice item alongside Trick to cripple defensive Pokemon like Registeel and Blissey; Choice Specs lets it immediately punch holes through teams, while Choice Scarf patches up Porygon-Z's poor Speed stat without the need for Agility, notably letting it outspeed Choice Scarf Gardevoir and +1 Gyarados. Adaptability paired with Tri-Attack offers more consistent power than Download and Tera Blast, though the fact that Porygon-Z loses the power boost to Tri-Attack after Terastallization makes it unreliable.

Checks and Counters

Ghost-types: While they must be wary of Shadow Ball, Gengar, Basculegion-F, and Mimikyu are immune to Porygon-Z's Tera Blast and, thanks to its poor bulk, can heavily damage it with their secondary STAB attacks. Mimikyu in particular can take a hit with Disguise, using the opportunity to damage Porygon-Z with Play Rough.

Steel-types: Common Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra, Registeel, and Jirachi are able to switch in on Porygon-Z's attacks before taking the opportunity to KO it or, in the case of the latter two, cripple it with Thunder Wave. However, all three must be mindful of Tera Blast Ground or Fighting, with Jirachi needing to be wary of Shadow Ball as well. If Porygon-Z is not Tera Fighting, Bisharp can revenge kill it with Sucker Punch and take most of Porygon-Z's attacks, though it struggles to switch in reliably, especially if Porygon-Z is running Thunderbolt.

Specially Defensive Pokemon: Blissey is unable to be 2HKOed by Tera Blast Fighting Porygon-Z, even with a Download boost, letting Blissey wear it down with Seismic Toss or cripple it with Thunder Wave. Depending on Porygon-Z's Tera type, other special walls like Umbreon and Alolan Muk can also take it on.

Priority: Porygon-Z's poor bulk means that it only needs to sustain a little chip damage to be picked off by the tier's prominent priority moves, such as Extreme Speed from Entei, Accelerock or Sucker Punch from Lycanroc-D, and Aqua Jet from Feraligatr or Barraskewda.

Agility.description:
An impressive Special Attack and good coverage land Porygon-Z a niche in RU as a ferocious wallbreaker and cleaner. Agility lets Porygon-Z outpace everything in the unboosted metagame, including Choice Scarf users like Krookodile and Mienshao. Ice Beam nails Ground-types like Hippowdon, Flying-types like Galarian Zapdos, Grass-types like Wo-Chien, and Dragon-types like Cyclizar. Thunderbolt crushes Water-types like Suicune and Empoleon, while Shadow Ball slams Ghost-types like Gengar and Psychic-types like Jirachi. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Porygon-Z stay healthy in the face of entry hazards and also gives it an advantage against Sticky Web teams. Download potentially nets Porygon-Z a Special Attack boost against physically defensive foes such as Slowbro, which it can OHKO with Thunderbolt at +1, and Chesnaught that it scares out, making it more difficult for opposing walls to deal with Porygon-Z. Tera Ground lets Porygon-Z eviscerate Steel-types like Jirachi and Hisuian Goodra with Tera Blast. Tera Fighting still lets Tera Blast hit Steel-types while also letting Porygon-Z blow Umbreon up. Tera Fighting also grants a crucial resistance to Sucker Punch from Bisharp.

Porygon-Z is best used as a wallbreaker and cleaner on offensive teams. Other special wallbreakers like Calm Mind Armarouge, Calm Mind Jirachi, and Choice Specs Hisuian Goodra can help Porygon-Z sweep by softening up special walls such as Umbreon, Empoleon, and opposing Jirachi. As Porygon-Z struggles to hit the field on its own due to its frailty, it appreciates pivots like Galarian Zapdos and Flygon baiting in physically defensive Pokemon like Slowbro and Hippowdon for it to take advantage of. Entry hazards set by teammates like Terrakion, Chesnaught, and Krookodile help in wearing down Porygon-Z's checks like the aforementioned special walls. Knock Off users like Galarian Zapdos and Crawdaunt remove items like Assault Vest and Heavy-Duty Boots from foes, making it easier for Porygon-Z to clean up lategame. Porygon-Z is easily taken down by priority attacks such as Extreme Speed from Entei and Sucker Punch from Bisharp; thus, teammates that can take these threats on like Galarian Zapdos and Talonflame are useful partners for it. Porygon-Z is most effective when it uses Terastallization; hence, teammates that don't rely on the mechanic to be threatening, like Gardevoir and Basculegion-F, are helpful partners, which can also help pressure defensive foes like Jirachi and Hisuian Goodra. Status support like Thunder Wave from Slowbro, Will-O-Wisp from Talonflame, and Thunder Wave Reuniclus can give Porygon-Z more opportunities to set up and sweep by weakening foes.

Choice Specs.description:
• Porygon-Z is one of the strongest Pokemon in 1v1, being able to output a lot of damage with its Adaptability-boosted Hyper Beam, going through specially bulky Pokemon like non-Assault Vest Ursaluna, Landorus-T, and Sylveon, as long as the last one doesn't predict its Hyper Beam and goes for Endure.
  • Uproar can go through Substitute from Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Entei, and Whimsicott.
  • Dark Pulse hits Ghost-types like Spectrier and Pecharunt.
  • Thunderbolt is Porygon-Z's best option against Corviknight.
  • Ice Beam damages both Landorus formes and Dragapult.
  • Trick can Choice-lock Pokemon like Pecharunt and Clear Amulet Cresselia and is usually combined with Recover, which helps Porygon-Z at healing off damage from low-damage foes like the previously mentioned Clear Amulet Cresselia.
  • Its HP is made to tank a Modest Volcanion's Overheat, while its Defense bulks an Ogerpon-W's Power Whip. Finally, its Speed lets it outspeed Modest Raging Bolt. The remaining EVs are put into Special Attack.
  • It's important to know when to use a STAB attack or when to use one of Porygon-Z's coverage moves; it's usually recommended to use Hyper Beam against bulky targets like Ursaluna over Ice Beam, since the Adaptability boost means a neutral STAB hit does as much damage as a super effective non-STAB hit.
  • Porygon-Z struggles against strong Fighting- and Steel-types that can easily take its attacks or outspeed it, such as Sneasler and Metagross, so Pokemon that can deal with them, like Landorus-T and Skeledirge, are excellent partners.

Life Orb.description:
• Life Orb Porygon-Z uses its freedom of moves to launch powerful attacks, which are backed by Nasty Plot boosts or the defenses from Substitute.
  • Hyper Beam is capable of OHKOing many Pokemon that do not resist it, such as non-Assault Vest Ursaluna, Raging Bolt, and non-Assault Vest Azumarill.
  • Nasty Plot lets Porygon-Z threaten an OHKO versus opposing Pokemon that would be able to tank Porygon-Z's unboosted Hyper Beam and KO it back, such as Maranga Berry Corviknight and Clear Amulet Cresselia.
  • Against Pokemon using the combination of Endure and Custap Berry that would be OHKOed by Porygon-Z's Hyper Beam, like Urshifu-S and Primarina, Porygon-Z can use Substitute when predicting Endure and fire off a Hyper Beam the next turn, while still being protected behind Substitute if Endure happens to work twice. However, it is advisable to be wary of Encore from Primarina.
  • Uproar lets Porygon-Z hit foes behind Substitute, such as Serperior and Whimsicott. It also gives Porygon-Z another Normal-type STAB move when the recharge turn of Hyper Beam is undesirable.
  • The Speed EVs help Porygon-Z outpace Modest Raging Bolt, and the HP and Defense EVs allow it to tank Choice Scarf Volcanion's Overheat and Jolly Ogerpon-W's Power Whip. The rest of the EVs are distributed into Special Attack.
  • This Porygon-Z set can struggle against faster Pokemon that can OHKO it, such as Haxorus and Meowscarada, so teammates like Corviknight or Primarina that can handle these Pokemon are well-warranted.
  • Like most Porygon-Z, Pokemon that can tank its Hyper Beam such as Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra, Assault Vest users like Ursaluna, and Ghost-types like Skeledirge are hard counters to it, so Pokemon like Choice Band Meowscarada and Urshifu-S are great partners for it.

Choice Scarf.description:
• A Choice Scarf allows Porygon-Z to outspeed many fast threats, such as non-Choice Scarf Haxorus, Meowscarada, and Chien-Pao, that would otherwise beat it.
  • Trick allows it to beat foes that try to stall it out, such as stall Manaphy and Agility Corviknight.
  • Ice Beam allows Porygon-Z to beat Garchomp and Landorus-T.
  • A Modest nature allows it to get consistent knockouts against Alolan Ninetales.
  • However, a Timid nature allows it to outspeed other Choice Scarf users and Speed-boosting threats, such as Speed Booster Energy Great Tusk.
  • Porygon-Z cannot break through bulky Steel-type Pokemon, like Iron Crown, Metagross and Hisuian Goodra, so its best partners are Pokemon with good matchups against those foes, such as Urshifu-S, Fire-types like Volcarona and Volcanion, and Ground-types like Landorus-T.

Z-Conversion Sweeper.description: Porygon-Z is among Normal's best avaliable setup sweepers due to its coveted access to Z-Conversion. Shadow Ball, when on the first moveslot, ensures Porygon-Z turns into a Ghost-type upon using Z-Conversion. After Z-Conversion, Adaptability-boosted Shadow Ball hits insanely hard, OHKOing the likes of Archaludon, Tapu Koko, and specially defensive Jirachi as well as 2HKOing the majority of its neutral targets, making Porygon-Z a fearsome late-game sweeper against Steel, Electric, and Psychic teams. Thunderbolt zaps Dark-types weak to it such as Greninja, Hisuian Samurott, and Galarian Moltres, preventing these threats from halting Porygon-Z's sweep in the Water and Flying matchups. Alternatively, Substitute lets Porygon-Z avoid status moves from Pokemon it doesn't OHKO, such as Celesteela and Hisuian Goodra, at the cost of additional coverage. Recover makes Porygon-Z last longer versus bulky walls that can't 2HKO it after the omniboost, such as Mega Venusaur and specially defensive Heatran. Ice Beam, while hard to fit, is a viable option should Porygon-Z be used to further threaten Flying, Ground, and Dragon teams. Mega Lopunny pummels the bulky Dark-types that Porygon-Z can't do much against, like Alolan Muk and Ting-Lu, and greatly appreciates Porygon-Z removing physical walls like Slowbro and Skarmory for it. Blissey, Chansey, and Porygon2 can tank most attacks aimed at Porygon-Z and bring it safely into the field with their Teleport. Particularly, Blissey and Chansey also set Stealth Rock for Porygon-Z to net more KOs when boosted, such as an OHKO on offensive Galarian Moltres with Thunderbolt. On hyper offensive Normal builds, Smeargle's Sticky Web support slows down faster Pokemon like Choice Scarf Iron Boulder and Sand Rush Excadrill, allowing boosted Porygon-Z to outspeed and dispatch them.

ru.overview: Gallade is a very threatening wallbreaker that uses its Sharpness-boosted offensive coverage options to threaten big damage on most of the metagame. It can notably 2HKO walls like Slowbro and Chesnaught making it an excellent tool at dealing with defensive teams in particular, as nothing can reliably take its hits. It is, however, held back by its average bulk. While its special bulk can let it tank some pretty big hits like Gengar's Shadow Ball, Noivern's Draco Meteor, and Magnezone's Discharge, its physical bulk is terrible, and it will have trouble taking hits it doesn't resist from any mildly threatening foes such as Bisharp's Sucker Punch and Krookodile's Earthquake. Its biggest weakness is its mediocre Speed leaving it vulnerable to revenge killing attempts from faster threats like Krookodile, Gardevoir, and Noivern; Choice Scarf users such as Gardevoir; and priority users like Mimikyu and Bisharp. It therefore struggles against more offensive teams containing more of these fast threats.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Knock Off or Night Slash can be used over Leaf Blade to hit bulky Psychic-types like Cresselia, Reuniclus, and Necrozma harder. Night Slash has consistently high damage and good synergy with Scope Lens thanks to its higher critical chance. Knock Off hits for slightly less and only gets its boosted Base Power once, resulting in it being less effective against the likes of Slowbro, Reuniclus, and Cresselia, but it has the upside of removing items like Rocky Helmet and Heavy-Duty Boots.

Checks and Counters

Faster Wallbreakers: Faster wallbreakers like Gardevoir and Maushold can threaten Gallade prior to it using Agility, while Choice Scarf users like Gengar are still faster than +2 Gallade.

Priority Users: As a setup sweeper with mediocre Defense, Gallade is especially weak to priority moves; it's weak to Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak and neutral to Sucker Punch and Aqua Jet from the likes of Crawdaunt and Bisharp, which can easily revenge kill it. While Extreme Speed from Entei hits it hard, it can, in a pinch, use Tera Steel to take less damage.

Setup Sweeper.description:
Set Details

Gallade has a unique niche in being a wallbreaker that threatens a 2HKO on the main physical walls of the tier such as Chesnaught and Slowbro. Psycho Cut not making contact comes in handy against Rocky Helmet Chesnaught. Leaf Blade is useful coverage for hitting bulky Water-types like Slowbro, Gastrodon, and Quagsire. With Swords Dance, Gallade gets the opportunity to OHKO most physical walls in the tier like Chesnaught, Suicune, and Slowbro, while Agility allows it to outspeed foes that would normally revenge kill it like Gengar and Gardevoir. Lum Berry allows it to shrug off status effects that can be inflicted by Slowbro, Gengar, and Quagsire; it works best on Swords Dance sets, as they don't need more damage. Life Orb is an alternative that fits the most on Agility variants, as it adds damage that can be lacking, letting them OHKO some notable threats like Gardevoir after Stealth Rock. Scope Lens is another option to get additional damage on Agility sets; it is less reliable than Life Orb but crucially doesn't cause recoil, which can help Gallade to tank important hits such as Earthquake from Krookodile and Shadow Sneak from Mimikyu. It can also let Gallade break through Terastilized Iron Defense setup sweepers such as Tera Ghost Registeel. Tera Steel is at its best on Swords Dance sets, letting Gallade sponge hits from Fairy-types such as Gardevoir and Diancie extremely well while neutering some of its original weaknesses. Tera Fire resists Entei's Sacred Fire and protects Gallade from Gengar' Will-O-Wisp.

Gallade is a huge threat on Sticky Web and bulky offense teams, as it's able to dig holes in the opponent's defensive structure and can take advantage of paralysis and Sticky Web to fix its speed issue. Because of its average bulk, it also loves pivots, thus working well with allies such as Jirachi and Noivern; Jirachi can also spread paralysis to allow it to outpace foes like Krookodile and Entei. Teams stacking multiple physical setup sweepers such as Bisharp, Mimikyu, and Maushold appreciate Swords Dance Gallade's ability to help wear down shared checks like Quagsire and Slowbro. Agility Gallade benefits most from other wallbreakers like Entei, Crawdaunt, and Breloom thanks to their ability to weaken physical walls, letting it clean a weakened team. After using Agility, it can outspeed most Choice Scarf users aside from Gengar, helping it clean teams relying on the likes of Flamigo and Gardevoir for speed control. Entry hazard support such as Stealth Rock or Spikes can help greatly with putting foes such as Gardevoir or Yanmega in KO range of Gallade's attacks.

Choice Band.description:
Set Details

Choice Band Gallade can act as an extremely powerful wallbreaker with its Sharpness-boosted STAB moves. Leaf Blade targets Water-types like Slowbro and Gastrodon. Knock Off provides utility by removing items from possible switch-ins like Krookodile and Slowbro, and it hits Psychic-types like Reuniclus and Cresselia. Shadow Sneak lets it revenge kill weakened Agility Bascluegion-F, Gengar, and Choice Scarf Gardevoir. Trick can cripple walls like Reuniclus, and removing Gallade's Choice item can help ease prediction against teams with multiple Pokemon resistant to its STAB moves. Tera Steel lets it flip the matchup against Flying- and Fairy-types like Noivern and Gardevoir, while Tera Dark boosts Knock Off, guaranteeing a 2HKO on Slowbro; helps answer Ghost-types like Gengar as well as Psychic-types; and provides a resistance to Bisharp's Sucker Punch.

Choice Band Gallade often finds itself on balance and bulky offense teams that can patch up its physical frailty and mediocre Speed while appreciating its ability to punch holes through defensive cores. Cleaners like Bisharp, Maushold, and Toxtricity can sweep teams after Gallade has weakened shared checks like Gastrodon and Slowbro. Due to Gallade having the coverage to 2HKO any Pokemon in the tier, no slower Pokemon want to stay in on it, letting it effectively force switches; this synergizes well with entry hazard setters such as Gastrodon, Klefki, and Krookodile, since their hazards can help chip down the opposing team and make Gallade less reliant on prediction. If Gallade is running Shadow Sneak over Knock Off, answers to bulky Psychic-types such as Cresselia and Reuniclus are necessary. Alolan Muk and Encore Jirachi can help alleviate this weakness. Pivots like Cyclizar and Noivern can help bring Gallade onto the field safely after inviting in Umbreon and Hisuian Goodra. Paralysis support from the likes of Jirachi, Slowbro, and Klefki can make Gallade a terrifying foe by crippling its faster checks, like Noivern and Suicune, making them unable to outspeed it. Gallade should be paired with defensive Pokemon like Slowbro, Chesnaught, and Umbreon that can switch into revenge kill attempts from the likes of Noivern and Krookodile.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

Choice Scarf Gallade is a strong revenge killer and late-game cleaner with good utility. Leaf Blade lets it revenge kill Water-types like Feraligatr and hit Pokemon like Quagsire. Knock Off lets it hit Psychic-types like Necrozma and Reuniclus as well as removes items from defensive checks like Slowbro. Trick can cripple walls such as Suicune, Cresselia, and Calm Mind Reuniclus. Tera Steel changes Gallade's Fairy and Flying weaknesses into resistances, which helps it tank hits from Gardevoir and Noivern. Tera Dark boosts Knock Off damage, guaranteeing a 2HKO on Reuniclus, and it gives Gallade a resistance to Ghost- and Dark-type attacks from Pokemon like Gengar and Bisharp.

Choice Scarf Gallade performs best on balance and bulky offense structures, as they can help weaken its checks. Stealth Rock users like Registeel can help weaken Gallade's checks throughout the match to allow it to eventually clean late-game. Spikes setters like Chesnaught and Gastrodon can fulfill a similar role. These Pokemon appreciate Gallade's Knock Off support to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from the opposing team. Wallbreakers such as Krookodile and Entei can help weaken physical walls that Gallade struggles with such as Reuniclus and Slowbro. Gallade appreciates pivot support and hazard removal from the likes of Jirachi and Cyclizar, allowing it to enter the field easily and leverage its useful special bulk more consistently.

Assault Vest (Fighting).description:
Gallade offers incredible value to Fighting teams due to its Sharpness ability, access to a variety of slicing moves, and Assault Vest complementing its natural specially defensive bulk, giving the invaluable utility to beat threatening Psychic-type Pokemon such as Latios and Choice Specs Greninja. Psycho Cut is able to help combat a plethora of Poison-type Pokemon that annoy Fighting teams such as Galarian Weezing, Toxapex, and Amoonguss. Sacred Sword complements Psycho Cut by threatening Dark-type Pokemon that attempt to switch-in while also having the incredible ability to ignore Defense raises such as Archaludon's Stamina and Iron Defense Skarmory. Night Slash is another boosted coverage option that deals with threatening Psychic- and Ghost-type Pokemon such as the aforementioned Latias, Gholdengo, and Sinistcha. Knock Off is a possible alternative that provides the utility of removing items such as Rocky Helmet and Heavy Duty Boots but lacks the consistent damage output of Night Slash. Shadow Sneak complements Night Slash and Knock Off by being useful priority that can threaten and revenge kill fast Ghost- and Psychic-type Pokemon such as Flutter Mane, Dragapult, Iron Boulder. 96 Speed EVs enables Gallade to outspeed Modest Magnezone while the given investment in HP and Special Defense in tandem with Assault Vest, allowing Gallade to survive an attack from Choice Specs Flutter Mane in order to OHKO it back with Psycho Cut, alleviating pressure on Fighting teams.

Iron Valiant is an essential teammate for Gallade, being able to remove troublesome Dark-type Pokemon such as Sableye and Mandibuzz. Great Tusk is another incredible teammate, providing a defensive switch-in for physical attackers that could otherwise overwhelm Gallade such as Excadrill, Ceruledge, and Dragonite. Great Tusk also has the utility of removing entry hazards, which could otherwise hinder Gallade. Sneasler complements Gallade by removing Fairy-type Pokemon such as Enamorus, Hatterene, Primarina, and Iron Valiant. Sneasler also has utility in crippling set up Pokemon with Switcheroo, spreading status via Poison Touch and Dire Claw and pivoting with U-turn so that Gallade can enter the battlefield at the most opportune times. Keldeo is an incredible teammate that complements Gallade by removing physical walls such as Hippowdon, Skeledirge, and Gliscor. Iron Hands is a useful teammate, being able to sponge Flying-type STAB coverage from Pokemon such as Galarian Zapdos, Galarian Moltres, and Tornadus-T. Breloom is another option that helps Gallade by inflicting sleep, crippling troublesome foes such as Skeledirge and Torkoal, as well as putting offensive pressure on physical walls such as Slowbro and Quagsire. Similarly, Hisuian Lilligant is a physical sweeper that thrives on Gallade's ability to remove its checks in Pokemon such as Latias, Greninja, and Volcarona. Galarian Zapdos offers a Ground-immune Pokemon to add aditional protection from threats such as Excadrill and Great Tusk.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Gallade isn't a particularly bulky Pokemon, so it is often paired with partners more capable of setting up Trick Room while Gallade threatens foes that threaten its partners. Gallade also can be paired with redirection that allows it to set up Trick Room.
  • Hatterene pairs well with Gallade, as it is more capable of setting Trick Room up thanks to its bulk, while Gallade threatens foes such as Incineroar and Kingambit that Hatterene struggles to damage in return. Hatterene additionally threatens physically defensive foes that Gallade struggles to OHKO such as Amoonguss and provides powerful spread damage with Dazzling Gleam, which complements Gallade when it fails to achieve an OHKO. Indeedee-F provides redirection, allowing Gallade to safely set up Trick Room. It is additionally capable of setting up Trick Room itself while Gallade provides Wide Guard support. Indeedee-F setting up Psychic Terrain further supports Gallade by preventing Fake Out disruption and increasing the damage of Psycho Cut.
  • Amoonguss threatens to put Gallade to sleep with Spore, often forcing it to Terastallize into a Grass-type. A partner Torkoal threatens Amoonguss with Eruption and Weather Ball and outspeeds it while Trick Room is active. Gholdengo is difficult for Gallade to remove and threatens to deal significant damage with its STAB attacks. Torkoal and Ursaluna can survive Gholdengo's attacks and threaten it in return with Eruption and Headlong Rush. Basculegion-M threatens Gallade with its STAB attacks, so a partner Kingambit is capable of surviving these attacks and threatening it with Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave.

Strategy Comments

  • Gallade is a sweeper and a support Pokemon for Trick Room teams. It performs best early-game by removing threats preventing Trick Room from being set up or setting up Trick Room itself.
  • Gallade should always be led with a partner capable of setting Trick Room such as Hatterene or Indeedee-F. If paired with Hatterene, Gallade can be used to remove threats such as Kingambit and Incineroar. When facing Gholdengo, it can use Wide Guard to protect Hatterene from Make It Rain. If Gallade is paired with Indeedee-F, it can set Trick Room as Indeedee-F redirects attacks with Follow Me. However, there may be situations where Indeedee-F can be used to set up Trick Room itself while Gallade removes an opposing threat like Kingambit. Gallade can also use Wide Guard while Indeedee-F sets up Trick Room, protecting both Pokemon from attacks like Eruption from Hisuian Typhlosion.
  • Gallade is checked by Ghost-types and threatened by their attacks like Shadow Ball and Last Respects. As a result, Gallade is very reliant on redirection from Indeedee-F or switching to it if Indeedee-F is not lead. Gallade also relies on Kingambit to threaten them.
  • Foes with Imprison like Indeedee-M disrupt Trick Room teams and are often difficult for Gallade to remove, so it relies on partners like Ursaluna and Kingambit for this. If the opponent pivots around to stall out Trick Room turns, getting KOs while Trick Room is active becomes difficult for Gallade and its partners. To mitigate this, overwhelming the foes with powerful attacks from teammates like Ursaluna helps to reduce the effectiveness of the switches.

Offensive Trick Room Sweeper.description:
• Gallade is an offensive threat thanks to Sharpness and its ability to set Trick Room up for itself and its partners.
  • Sacred Sword ignores the Defense boosts of foes like Archaludon and Dondozo. Psycho Cut is used as a consistent Psychic-type STAB move that is also boosted by Sharpness. Its damage can be boosted further by a partner's Psychic Terrain. Wide Guard protects Gallade and its partner from spread attacks such as Make It Rain and Eruption.
  • Clear Amulet prevents Gallade's Attack from being hindered by Intimidate and Parting Shot, allowing it to always deal threatening damage to metagame staples such as Incineroar.
  • Tera Grass provides Gallade with an immunity to Spore, Sleep Powder, and Rage Powder while allowing it to resist Electro Shot from Archaludon. Tera Fire, unlike Tera Grass, removes Gallade's weakness to Flying-type attacks such as Hurricane from Pelipper without gaining a weakness to Poison-type attacks such as Dire Claw from Sneasler, and it also allows Gallade to resist Make It Rain from Gholdengo. Tera Fire additionally provides an immunity to burn.

vgc2024.overview:
• Gallade is a strong option on Trick Room teams thanks to its high physical damage output, unique coverage and utility movepool. It can deal with many problematic matchups for Trick Room, such as set up sweepers via Sacred Sword and spread moves via Wide Guard.

  • Gallade is used on teams with Indeedee-F, as the Fighting-type coverage it provides is crucial in dealing with Incineroar, Ting-Lu and other Dark-types that give Trick Room sweepers such as Hatterene trouble. Sharpness-boosted Sacred Sword does massive damage, putting pressure on opponents from turn one, as well as checking several problematic matchups, such as Dondozo. Wide Guard removes the most common way to bypass Indeedee-F's Follow Me, spread moves, and presents mind games on opponents on whether Gallade will use Wide Guard or set up Trick Room.

  • Gallade's typing is amazing offensively, but defensively leaves much to be desired. Its Defense and HP are low, making it vulnerable to attackers like Rillaboom and Urshifu that can take one attack from Gallade while OHKOing it back. While its Special Defense is high, it is made moot by relevant special attackers such as Flutter Mane and Tornadus, which both resist Sacred Sword and hit it for super effective damage. However, it should be noted that Wide Guard blocks both Bleakwind Storm and Dazzling Gleam.

Trick Room Abuser.description:
• Psycho Cut and Sacred Sword are the highest base power moves that take advantage of Sharpness.

  • The Defense EVs allow Gallade to survive a Wicked Blow and Surging Strikes from Urshifu-S and Urshifu-R, respectively.

  • Tera Grass allows Gallade to ignore powder moves from Amoonguss, a common Trick Room counter, and resist common physical attackers such as Rillaboom. Alternatively, Tera Fire can be used to resist common anti-Trick Room leads such as Chi-Yu and Flutter Mane, as well as giving Gallade a Fairy resist.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This Pokemon has been updated to reflect Regulation H, that lasts until January 5h, 2025. After this, Regulation G will return.

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

All-out Attacker.description:
• With its wide range of moveset options and its offense-boosting ability Sharpness, Gallade is excellent at dueling a wide variety of threats. Especially notable is Scared Sword, letting Gallade ignore Stamina Archaludon's accumulated boosts.

  • Night Slash versus Knock Off: Night Slash's consistent power is best for pure offense, potentially 2HKOing targets like Bold Gholdengo, assuming they can't stall with Recover and Rocky Helmet. If more utility is desired, Knock Off can be used for removing opposing items.

  • Shadow Sneak: Shadow Sneak Gallade's most consistent as a priority move, dealing good damage to targets like Gholdengo and Mimikyu.

  • Leaf Blade: Leaf Blade OHKOes Primarina and is Gallade's best hope of muscling past Dondozo.

  • Triple Axel: Though it suffers from some reliability issues, Triple Axel makes Dragonite rue the day it didn't Terastallize against Gallade!

Other Options

  • Aqua Cutter: Aqua Cutter benefits from Sharpness, but it doesn't add a lot of extra coverage.

  • Feint: Feint lets Gallade pick off weakened Dragonite before they can launch Extreme Speed, but otherwise hitting Gholdengo with Shadow Sneak is usually more useful.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Gallade uses Focus Sash or Assault Vest as its main tool for cushioning a big hit and has great natural coverage. Therefore, Tera is reserved mostly for emergency situations.

  • Fire: Beyond offering a useful Fairy-type resistance, Tera Fire blocks Volcarona from burning Gallade.

  • Dark: Tera Dark not only boosts Night Slash and Knock Off, but provides a key Ghost-type resistance against Gholdengo.

  • Steel: Tera Steel flips Gallade's weakness to Fairy-type attacks to a resistance. The Ice resistance can also be used in a pinch to keep Baxcalibur's Icicle Spear from OHKOing Gallade through Focus Sash.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost's immunity to Normal- and Fighting-type moves can thwart revenge kill attempts from Mach Punch users and Extreme Speed Dragonite, giving Gallade an opportunity to break Multiscale on the latter.

Items

  • Assault Vest: Gallade has enough Special Defense to make good use of Assault Vest, which lets it survive Tera Normal Ursaluna-B. Compared to Focus Sash, Assault Vest isn't rendered useless by Stealth Rock chip, making Gallade a safer mid- or late-game option.

  • Focus Sash: With Focus Sash, Gallade duels opposing Focus Sash users with its hard-hitting STAB attacks and priority moves, letting it focus on Speed investment.

  • Scope Lens: While Scope Lens is risky due to Gallade's average bulk and Speed, it pairs well with the increased critical hit ratio many of Gallade's attacks have.

EV Spreads

  • 140 HP / 244 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 116 Spe with Adamant: This spread is to be used with Assault Vest, surviving Silk Scarf Tera Normal Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon and Vacuum Wave together, while outspeeding even Timid Ursaluna-B and Jolly Ursaluna.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Adamant or Jolly: A maximum offense spread is standard for Focus Sash and Speed ties with offensive Adamant Dragonite. Jolly can be used to get the jump on Modest Archaludon, especially if using Shadow Sneak to stop Sturdy variants from activating Custap Berry in time.

  • 236 HP / 244 Atk / 28 SpD with Adamant: Sacrificing Speed for bulk lets Assault Vest Gallade survive Life Orb Tera Normal Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon followed by Vacuum Wave.

Choice Scarf.description:
• With Choice Scarf, Gallade is a decent anti-lead against several early-game setups and an unexpected revenge killer.

  • Knock Off versus Night Slash: Knock Off remains a strong disruption move with or without Trick, provided you exercise caution if you've already used Trick. Night Slash has more offensive presence than Knock Off and is a good choice if you really need to hit Gholdengo with consistent damage.

  • Triple Axel versus Leaf Blade: Triple Axel makes Gallade a surprising revenge killer against Garchomp and severely punishes Dragonite that don't Terastallize. Leaf Blade helps against more defensive foes, being a great coverage option for slashing through Primarina and being your best move against Dondozo.

  • Trick: Trick with Choice Scarf lets Gallade permanently cripple setup Pokemon like Annihilape and Garganacl.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Choice Scarf Gallade normally isn't a strong user of Tera. It is best used in situations where Gallade already has momentum and needs to preserve it.

  • Fire: Tera Fire makes facing down Volcarona far less risky thanks to the burn immunity, as well as providing a useful Fairy-type resistance.

  • Steel: Tera Steel provides a welcome resistance to Fairy-type attacks and Dragonite's Extreme Speed.

  • Dark: Tera Dark stops Choice Scarf Gholdengo from revenge killing with Shadow Ball, while boosting Night Slash and Knock Off

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost grants immunity to Extreme Speed and Mach Punch, letting Gallade keep its speed advantage against Dragonite and Breloom even when its low on health.

  • Grass: Tera Grass can surprise Spore users like Breloom, letting Gallade score an easy KO or cripple them with Trick. Leaf Blade also becomes a 2HKO against Dondozo.

Swords Dance (Fighting).description: For Fighting teams, Mega Gallade is one of the best choices, courtesy of its incredible offensive power, typing, and Speed, being the best counter to Fighting's biggest roadblock, Toxapex. Swords Dance increases Mega Gallade's power to the maximum, letting it freely overpower the likes of Mandibuzz and Celesteela. Zen Headbutt beautifully complements a Fighting-type STAB move, as it lets Mega Gallade easily break through any opposing Poison-types that may be annoying walls such as Mega Venusaur, Toxapex, and Clodsire. Knock Off is another tool in Mega Gallade's arsenal, which lets it take care of Psychic- and Ghost-types—such as Gholdengo, Slowbro, and Aegislash—and wears down Celesteela into range of Close Combat finishing it off. Triple Axel is another option to easily take care of Flying-types such as Landorus-T, Dragonite, and Enamorus. Shadow Sneak can also be considered to pick off faster weakened threats such as Gengar, Choice Scarf Blacephalon, and Mega Alakazam. With all its benefits, Mega Gallade has a few checks in Skeledirge and defensive Gholdengo; hence, offensive Great Tusk and Urshifu-R are great partners in helping take these down. Defensive Great Tusk also helps in setting and removing entry hazards, which is appreciated by Mega Gallade. Mega Gallade is also easily revenge killed by faster offensive threats such as Tornadus-T and Choice Scarf Blacephalon, so Assault Vest Iron Hands is a good check to stop these in their tracks and deal good damage back while also being able to pivot in Mega Gallade with Volt Switch. Breloom and Lilligant-H also helps significantly in the Water matchup against the likes of Mega Swampert and Barraskewda; they can also put opposing foes to sleep to make Gallade's setup easier. Choice Scarf Sneasler helps in the Fairy matchup against the likes of Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Tapu Koko while also being able to set and absorb Toxic Spikes and can U-Turn to pivot in Mega Gallade safely. Iron Valiant is also an amazing partner in the form of a specially offensive threat, complementing Mega Gallade, as it can easily take care of Mega Sableye. Choice Scarf Iron Valiant also outspeeds Mega Swampert under rain and Regieleki under Electric Terrain, making it a great revenge killer if Mega Gallade gets knocked out.

Swords Dance (Psychic).description: Mega Gallade is a potent wallbreaker on Psychic teams thanks to its greatly appreciated Dark neutrality and good coverage in Knock Off and Triple Axel. Swords Dance allows Mega Gallade to grab a boost on a forced switch and potentially win the game with its high base Speed and astronomical Attack after one boost. Knock Off is crucial to hit opposing Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Slowbro and Gholdengo that would otherwise wall this set, and its item removal is always handy in breaking defensive teams reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots down with Stealth Rock damage and removing key items from Celesteela and Toxapex. Finally, Zen Headbutt does massive work against Poison teams after a single Swords Dance and deals high amounts of damage to Fighting-resistant Pokemon such as Buzzwole and Toxapex. Triple Axel is another alternative, allowing Mega Gallade to hit Flying- and Dragon-types such as Landorus-T and Garchomp. Shadow Sneak can allow Mega Gallade to outspeed and take out Ghost-types such as Choice Scarf Gholdengo and Choice Scarf Blacephalon that could otherwise beat it. Tapu Lele forms a wallbreaking core with Mega Gallade, as they both threaten common checks to each other. Tapu Lele beats Mega Sableye with Moonblast, while Mega Gallade crushes Steel-types such as Heatran and Celesteela that trouble Tapu Lele with Close Combat. Jirachi can take Fairy-type attacks such as Tapu Lele's Moonblast aimed for Mega Gallade, as well as paralyze threats and beat them down with Thunder Wave and Serene Grace-boosted Iron Head, letting Mega Gallade break through them with a timely paralysis. Finally, Jirachi provides Stealth Rock support and a safe pivot in with U-turn. Victini provides speed control with Choice Scarf and defeats Steel-types such as Choice Scarf Gholdengo that Mega Gallade is forced out by while appreciating Mega Gallade's ability to pound Heatran to dust. Deoxys-S provides entry hazard and dual screens support, which Mega Gallade can take advantage of with Knock Off and Swords Dance to break through bulkier teams. Slowbro provides crucial momentum with Teleport while also being able to annoy teams with Scald burns and Future Sight and switch in repeatedly through Regenerator. Celebi can break through troubling physical walls such as Hippowdon and Dondozo that Mega Gallade struggles to make progress against. Finally, Choice Scarf Latias can both remove entry hazards with Defog and use Healing Wish to give Mega Gallade a second chance to break through the opposing team.

zu.overview: Froslass's access to Spikes alongside a plethora of utility options makes it an excellent setter on both offensive and balance teams. It excels as a dedicated lead on hyper offense teams, providing early entry hazards while generating momentum through Destiny Bond. Alternatively, its bulkier sets can check physical attackers such as Toxicroak and Hitmontop with the aid of Will-O-Wisp. Furthermore, Froslass's Ghost typing allows it to block Rapid Spin, helping keep Spikes on the field throughout a match with minimal support.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Taunt can be used over Will-O-Wisp on utility sets to shut down passive Pokemon and prevent opposing entry hazards, though this leaves Froslass less capable of deterring physical attackers. Thunder Wave is another option that can cripple faster threats, especially on lead sets, but it is generally harder to justify over Will-O-Wisp due to its lower overall utility. A faster, more offensively inclined EV spread can be used to better pressure threats such as Charizard and other offensive Pokemon. However, Froslass's relatively modest offensive presence often leaves it unable to secure important KOs, and he loss of bulk significantly reduces its ability to switch into attacks, spread status, or consistently set Spikes. Tera Dark provides a resistance to Dark-type attacks without introducing a weakness to Poison-type moves from Skuntank, though the added Fighting weakness is often undesirable.

Checks and Counters

Fire-types: Fire-types such as Charizard, Houndoom, and Pyroar threaten Froslass with their super effective STAB attacks, while the latter two also resist its Ice- and Ghost-type moves. Houndoom can additionally use Froslass as setup fodder with Nasty Plot. Camerupt can take Froslass's attacks and either retaliate with Lava Plume or set Stealth Rock, though it dislikes switching into Spikes repeatedly. Furthermore, Fire-types are immune to Will-O-Wisp, giving them additional opportunities to switch in safely, while Houndoom can take advantage of Flash Fire to gain a power boost. However, they must be careful around Destiny Bond from lead variants, as Froslass can trade with them.

Faster Pokemon: Froslass's lackluster bulk leaves it susceptible to revenge killing from faster threats. Pokemon such as Whimsicott, Jolteon, and Sneasel can outspeed and threaten Froslass with their STAB attacks, with Sneasel notably hitting it super effectively. Additionally, Choice Scarf users such as Mabosstiff and Basculin can revenge kill Froslass reliably. Priority moves such as Hitmontop's Bullet Punch can also pick off weakened variants.

Dark-types: Dark-types like Skuntank and Mabosstiff threaten Froslass with their strong Dark-type STAB attacks. However, both must be wary of Will-O-Wisp, which limits their offensive presence, and Choice-locked sets can be disrupted by Cursed Body, forcing them to switch out entirely. Special attacking Dark-types such as Spiritomb and Houndoom are less concerned about burn and can use Froslass as setup fodder. However, lead variants of Froslass can potentially trade with them using Destiny Bond.

Cryogonal: Cryogonal resists Froslass's Ice-type STAB attacks and has access to reliable recovery, giving it greater longevity over the course of a match. It can 2HKO Froslass with Flash Cannon and force it out to gain opportunities to use Rapid Spin, removing the Spikes set by Froslass.

Lycanroc: Lycanroc can shut down lead variants of Froslass with Taunt, preventing it from setting Spikes and allowing Lycanroc to set Stealth Rock itself. It can also pressure Froslass offensively with Accelerock, potentially knocking it out through repeated use despite Icy Wind's Speed drops.

Lead.description:
Froslass functions as a dedicated offensive lead thanks to its Ghost typing, which blocks Rapid Spin, and its wide array of utility options, allowing it to reliably set Spikes to wear down opposing teams and make wallbreakers such as Lycanroc, Toxicroak, and Jolteon more difficult to switch into. Taunt prevents entry hazards from setters such as Mesprit, Orthworm, and Sandslash while also shutting down setup attempts from opposing Pokemon like Toxicroak. Destiny Bond allows Froslass to trade with threatening foes such as Charizard, Vikavolt, and Magneton. Icy Wind provides valuable speed control by slowing faster threats such as Whimsicott and Lycanroc, allowing Froslass to 2HKO the former while also creating setup opportunities for teammates such as Venusaur and Hisuian Sneasel. Alternatively, Avalanche pairs well with Destiny Bond, as its negative priority lets Froslass move after slower foes and potentially take them down with Destiny Bond after being KOed. Shadow Ball hits Pokemon such as Mesprit and Drifblim super effectively while also dealing greater damage to Fire-types such as Charizard and Typhlosion. Froslass can use a fully offensive EV spread to threaten targets such as Whimsicott and Dodrio or invest in HP to improve its ability to set multiple layers of Spikes against passive Pokemon such as Sandslash. Tera Ghost is the preferred option, as it preserves Froslass's immunity to Rapid Spin removes its weakness to Steel-type attacks such as Hitmontop's Bullet Punch and Cryogonal's Flash Cannon and boosts the power of Shadow Ball if it is run. However, because Froslass primarily functions as a suicide lead, it is rarely a worthwhile Terastallization candidate.

Froslass fits best on hyper offense teams, making teammates such as Toxicroak, Jolteon, Mesprit, Lycanroc, and Vikavolt that benefit from the Spikes it provides especially valuable.
