These Pokemon also threaten common entry hazard removers such as Drifblim, Hitmontop, and Sandslash, helping preserve Froslass's Spikes. Taunt users such as Pyroar and Skuntank can further support hyper offense teams by preventing Defog and opposing entry hazards. Sets lacking Icy Wind can struggle against faster threats such as Whimsicott and Sneasel, making fast Pokemon such as the aforementioned Jolteon and Choice Scarf users such as Basculin and Mesprit useful teammates. Pokemon that can pressure Lycanroc, such as Hisuian Sneasel, are also appreciated, as Lycanroc's Speed and access to Taunt can limit Froslass's ability to set Spikes and disrupt opposing teams.

Utility.description:
With excellent Speed and access to useful utility moves like Spikes, Froslass functions as an effective defensive entry hazard setter. Its Ghost typing allows it to block Rapid Spin from users such as Sandslash and Hitmontop. Hex pairs well with Will-O-Wisp, allowing Froslass to threaten targets such as Drifblim and Mesprit. Ice Beam provides coverage against Ground-types such as Sandslash and Sandaconda while also hitting Flying-types like Dodrio and Drifblim. Shadow Ball is a more consistent Ghost-type STAB option that does not rely on status to deal more damage. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers such as Regirock, Toxicroak, and Skuntank by limiting their offensive presence and wearing down common switch-ins like Magneton, Jolteon, and Clawitzer. Pain Split improves Froslass's longevity while simultaneously chipping bulkier foes that have high HP like Whiscash and Brute Bonnet. A Timid nature with 56 Speed EVs allows Froslass to outspeed Skuntank and Toxicroak, letting it burn them before they can attack and reducing the damage it takes from their Dark-type moves. Tera Water can be used to improve Froslass's defensive utility against Fire-types such as Charizard and Houndoom while also letting it survive Water-type attacks from Basculin and priority moves such as Hitmontop's Bullet Punch in emergency situations. Tera Fairy can be instead used, allowing Froslass to resist Dark-type attacks from Pokemon such as Mabosstiff and Sneasel while maintaining a favorable presence against Fighting-types like Hitmontop. It also grants an immunity to Clawitzer's Dragon Pulse, improving Froslass's matchup against it.

Froslass fits well on both offensive and balanced entry hazard stacking teams thanks to its combination of offensive and defensive utility. Knock Off users such as Skuntank can remove Heavy-Duty Boots from opposing Pokemon, making them more vulnerable to Spikes damage while also appreciating the additional chip damage Spikes provides to increase their offensive pressure. Wallbreakers such as Whimsicott, Charizard, and Toxicroak similarly benefit from Spikes wearing down their checks and threaten many Pokemon such as Perrserrker and Morpeko that force Froslass out. Stealth Rock setters such as Whiscash and Camerupt further support hazard stacking while checking powerful special attackers that pressure Froslass, such as Charizard and Jolteon. Mesprit notably provides additional utility by setting Stealth Rock, removing Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off, and using U-turn to bring Froslass safely onto the field. Pokemon such as Skuntank, Sandslash, and Hitmontop that can switch into Knock Off users such as Hisuian Sneasel and Skuntank and threaten them in return are highly valuable.

Spikes Lead.description:
Froslass's rare combination of high Speed, vast utility movepool, and its typing, which lets it take advantage of spinners like Tatsugiri and Alolan Sandslash and aids it in beating the Defoggers such as Scyther and Altaria one-on-one, helps it solidify a niche as a dedicated hyper offense lead that can beat common Ground-type entry hazard setters like Mudsdale and Golurk. Ice Beam is Froslass's preferred STAB move for its power, but Icy Wind could be run instead to slow down foes like Salazzle and Choice Scarf Meloetta for its teammates. Taunt stops Pokemon like Coalossal and Gastrodon from setting up their entry hazards on Froslass as well as Pokemon such as Bronzong from using it as setup fodder. On the other hand, Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers like Paldean Tauros-W and messes with Sucker Punch users such as Skuntank and Bombirdier. Destiny Bond lets Froslass get either a KO or an extra turn to set up another layer of Spikes unharmed due to its threat. Thunder Wave can be used over Taunt or Will-O-Wisp so that Froslass can cripple special attackers like Delphox and Florges better, but its matchups into the aforementioned Sucker Punch users worsen a bit. Avalanche could also be run as Froslass's STAB move because its negative priority means Destiny Bond might get a surprise KO on a foe, but it misses out on the power of Ice Beam and the utility of Icy Wind, and it can be played around easily once revealed. Since Froslass's goal is to set up hazards and then provide an entry point for its partners when it faints, its Tera types are for the niche situations in which it has difficulty achieving this, and therefore, Froslass should be Terastallized sparingly. Tera Fairy gives Froslass a strong defensive typing that provides a Dark resistance, helping it against Sucker Punch Bombirdier and Skuntank. Alternatively, Tera Dark gifts Froslass a Dark resistance as well alongside a Ghost resistance, which helps it versus Decidueye and Golurk, and it blocks status moves like Encore and Taunt from Prankster users such as Sableye and Grimmsnarl. However, Froslass gains a Fighting weakness.

Froslass works exclusively as a dedicated lead on hyper offensive teams, which enjoy Spikes weakening checks. As Froslass's Spikes can be easily removed after it's KOed, a Defog deterrent like Competitive Kilowattrel, Pokemon such as Toxtricity and Skuntank that threaten out Defoggers, and spinblockers like Oricorio-G and Tera Ghost Salazzle are vital partners to help keep up pressure. Pokemon like Arcanine, Salazzle, and Minior, which prefer to run other items like Leftovers, Focus Sash, and White Herb instead of Heavy-Duty Boots, appreciate Froslass's ability to deny opposing hazards from being set up. Teammates like Bulk Up Paldean Tauros-W and -F, both Nasty Plot and Swords Dance Zoroark, and Throat Spray Toxtricity all benefit greatly from their checks like Gastrodon, Wo-Chien, and Golurk being whittled into range of a 2HKO or OHKO. Fighting-type teammates like Paldean Tauros-W and Scrafty that can take advantage of common switch-ins to Froslass such as Coalossal and Dark-types like Skuntank and Zoroark are greatly appreciated, as Froslass fails to effectively threaten the latter two otherwise, barring status conditions from moves like Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ghost

Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave can be solid options, weakening switch-ins attempting to play around Destiny Bond like Alolan Muk. Shadow Ball is a solid option to threaten out Hatterene attempting to stop entry hazards going up with Magic Bounce. Avalanche can be used to catch slower targets like Hoopa-U and Bisharp attempting to play around Destiny Bond by making Froslass move slower; however, it gives up offensive pressure.

Ice

Curse can be used to deter setup while also denying entry hazard removal. Icy Wind reduces the foe's Speed, allowing Froslass to get another turn to set up Spikes or deal damage.

Spikes Suicide Lead (Ice).description:
Froslass is an incredible addition for Ice teams, not only providing a nice Fighting immunity and spinblocker, but also giving Ice teams access to a fantastic entry hazard in Spikes. Froslass's attack of choice can be either Shadow Ball or Poltergeist; both cleanly 2HKO Hatterene, deterring it from switching in when Froslass uses Spikes. Note that Shadow Ball is generally preferred, as it's more reliable and hits users of Body Press such as Skarmory, Archaludon, and Great Tusk, harder; however, Poltergeist has higher Base Power, dealing more damage to Hatterene and Hisuian Goodra. The last two moves can be any two of Thunder Wave, Taunt, Will-O-Wisp, and Destiny Bond; the best choices here depend on Froslass's teammates. Thunder Wave is generally the best option, helping fix Ice's questionable speed control as well as hindering dangerous threats such as Cinderace, Ogerpon-H, and Iron Valiant. Will-O-Wisp weakens important targets like Bisharp, Hisuian Goodra, and Urshifu-R. Taunt is an excellent option for an offensive type weak to Stealth Rock like Ice, as it prevents hazard moves such as Toxapex's Toxic Spikes from being used. Destiny Bond can net Froslass KOs that it otherwise wouldn't get, and is run often enough to force opponents to respect the possibility; sometimes, even the mere threat of Destiny Bond can let Froslass get three layers of Spikes. As a rule of thumb, teams without a reliable defensive spinner like Avalugg should run Taunt Froslass to prevent hazards from coming up, and teams running Light Clay on Alolan Ninetales should run Thunder Wave Froslass to help Alolan Ninetales safely set up Aurora Veil. Focus Sash is used to help Froslass get an additional layer of Spikes or ensure a crucial Thunder Wave or Will-O-Wisp against dangerous targets such as Scizor, Choice Scarf Kleavor, and Choice Specs Greninja.

Alolan Ninetales appreciates the speed control granted by Thunder Wave to help it set up Aurora Veil without losing too much health; in return, Alolan Ninetales generates snow, letting Froslass more reliably switch into Fighting-type physical attackers. The halved physical damage from Will-O-Wisp, Thunder Wave support, or even a Cursed Body activation can allow sweepers such as Cetitan, Swords Dance Weavile, and Cloyster to set up and sweep more easily; in addition, Spikes help chip away at their defensive answers such as Shuca Berry Iron Hands, Choice Scarf Iron Boulder, and Choice Specs Kyurem. Knock Off users such as Weavile and Alolan Sandslash appreciate Spikes more than other teammates, as it gives Knock Off a bit more punch against defensive switch-ins such as Toxapex, Archaludon, and Alomomola. Rapid Spin users such as Avalugg and Alolan Sandslash can help preserve Froslass's Focus Sash. Stealth Rock users such as Mamoswine and Piloswine can form a nice entry hazard stacking core with Froslass and also help deal with some Pokemon that do well against it like non-Air Balloon Heatran.

Suicide Lead (Ghost).description:
Froslass is the premier lead on Ghost teams thanks to its blazing Speed stat allowing it to comfortably outpace other fast leads like Alolan Ninetales, Galvantula, and Garchomp. Setting up Spikes is Froslass's main job, wearing down switch-ins to Ghost-type attacks such as Alolan Muk and Hoopa-U. Taunt is used to prevent other leads like Sandy Shocks, Torkoal, and Mamoswine from getting their entry hazards up, along with stopping status moves from the likes of Galarian Weezing and Talonflame. Destiny Bond allows Froslass to take foes down once it has finished setting Spikes, along with creating mind games around when it will be used. Finally, Ice Beam when running a Timid nature and Triple Axel when running Jolly are Froslass's main STAB moves, with Ice Beam threatening Ground- and Flying-types like Garchomp, Gliscor, and Enamorus straight away. Meanwhile, Triple Axel can break past Focus Sash on other leads like Breloom, along with having a higher but less consistent damage output.

The more pressure Froslass causes as a lead, the happier its teammates will be. Flutter Mane, for example, enjoys Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra being unable to take multiple Choice Specs Moonblasts when it comes in, which can open it up majorly against Poison- and Dragon-type teams that cannot stop its special offense. Ceruledge enjoys not having its Focus Sash broken by entry hazards, which are prevented by Taunt, and loves chip damage on would-be checks, including Archaludon and Overqwil. Gengar can help with hazard-stacking by setting up Toxic Spikes, forcing threats like Ting-Lu, Tyranitar, and Primarina onto timers they can't outlast. Dragapult enjoys Fairy-types, including Iron Valiant and Primarina, which naturally tank its Dragon-type STAB moves, to be chipped upon entry for its boosted Phantom Force to pick them off. Gholdengo's ability, Gold as Gold, blocks Defog from the likes of Corviknight and Galarian Weezing, keeping Spikes pressure up even longer, and Gholdengo itself can remove Hatterene trying to prevent Froslass's Spikes. Spectrier enjoys Ghost-resistant foes being chipped down throughout a game so that they cannot handle its threatening Grim Neigh boosts.

ru.overview: Rotom-H's unique typing, access to Levitate, and solid bulk lets it carve out a niche as a pivot that can check threats like Bisharp and Jirachi. Rotom-H can function as a decent Nasty Plot user thanks to its ability to force out Pokemon like Chesnaught and Breloom as well as a solid burn spreader with Will-O-Wisp. However, Rotom-H lacks recovery outside of Pain Split, making it prone to getting worn down throughout a game or brute-forced through by strong attackers like Choice Band Krookodile and Terrakion. Additionally, Rotom-H's Stealth Rock weakness leaves it vulnerable to Knock Off, preventing it from effectively checking Chesnaught and Krookodile. Rotom-H's merely decent Special Attack stat and lacking coverage mean that it often struggles to hit the tier's many prominent Dragon-types, particularly Cyclizar and Hisian Goodra.
ru.comments:
Other Options

A Choice Scarf set with Trick can be used to hinder defensive Pokemon like Hisuian Goodra and Quagsire; however, it leaves Rotom-H vulnerable to Stealth Rock. Thunderbolt can be used over Volt Switch to trade momentum for power, letting it more heavily dent Electric-weak targets like Slowbro. Thunder Wave can be used to cripple faster Pokemon like Cyclizar and Noivern, letting faster teammates outspeed them.

Checks and Counters

Dragon-types: Cyclizar can switch into Rotom-H's attacks before removing its Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off and/or forcing a boosted Rotom-H out with Dragon Tail. However, Cyclizar that don't run Draco Meteor dislike being burned by Will-O-Wisp. Other Dragon-types that can check it include Flygon and Hisuian Goodra, due to the former's immunity to Volt Switch and the latter's excellent special bulk.

Item Disruption: Rotom-H's weakness to Stealth Rock leaves it heavily reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots to function. As such, Knock Off from Pokemon like Krookodile, Chesnaught, and Cyclizar can cripple it. Additionally, Trick from foes like Gardevoir, Jirachi, and Cresselia can prevent Rotom-H from sweeping effectively while making it vulnerable to Stealth Rock.

Strong Wallbreakers: Special wallbreakers, like Gengar, Toxtricity, and Gardevoir, don't mind being burned and can heavily damage Rotom-H. If lacking Will-O-Wisp, Rotom-H struggles to beat physical wallbreakers like Rhyperior and Krooodile. Entei deserves a special mention due to its natural immunity to Will-O-Wisp and ability to KO Rotom-H with Stone Edge.

Special Walls: Blissey can take any of Rotom-H's moves, absorb Will-O-Wisp, and wear it down with Seismic Toss. However, Blissey can be exploited by Pain Split variants and be forced to burn through Soft-Boiled's low PP. Gastrodon resists both of Rotom-H's STAB moves and can freely set up Spikes, but it struggles to do much back. Rhyperior is similarly resistant to Rotom-H's attacks and can KO it with Stone Edge; however, it hates being burned and is walled by Tera Steel.

Nasty Plot.description:
Set Details

Rotom-H can take advantage of its good typing, excellent ability in Levitate, and bulk to act as a solid Nasty Plot user. Volt Switch lets Rotom-H pivot out of unfavorable matchups, such as against Dragon-types like Cyclizar, while maintaining momentum. It also allows Rotom-H to hit slower Water-types like Slowbro for solid damage. Pain Split is Rotom-H's best form of recovery, letting it heal against bulkier Pokemon that try to switch in, such as Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon. Will-O-Wisp can be used instead to cripple physical attackers like Krookodile and Bisharp. Tera Steel gives Rotom-H a myriad of resistances, most notably to Rock, while maintaining its Ground immunity thanks to Levitate; this lets it check Ground-types like Krookodile and Torterra much more easily. Tera Steel also gives Rotom-H a valuable immunity to Toxic, letting it wall Umbreon and Amoonguss.

Rotom-H is a good fit for bulky offense teams that need an offensive pivot and potential setup sweeper. As Rotom-H relies on Heavy-Duty Boots to come in safely, Pokemon that can absorb Knock Off, like Gastrodon and Chesnaught, make for good partners. Flamigo is a U-turn user that makes for a good pairing with Rotom-H, as it can pressure specially defensive Pokemon like Cyclizar and Hisuian Goodra. In return, Rotom-H can take Fairy-type attacks from the likes of Mimikyu and Gardevoir while chipping away at physically bulky Pokemon like Slowbro. Setup sweepers like Bisharp and Dragon Dance Necrozma appreciate Rotom-H's ability to bring them in safely with Volt Switch and wear down teams with its Nasty Plot-boosted attacks. Calm Mind Slowbro and Suicune in particular can also check physical wallbreakers for Rotom-H, such as Rhyperior and Entei. Entry hazard setters, such as Chesnaught and Krookodile, can help chip down Rotom-H's checks, like Cyclizar and Rhyperior.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis is for the Regulation C format of Battle Stadium Singles, which lasts until June 30th, 2023. For more information on this format and its current events, check out this page!

If you feel this analysis is missing anything important or needs an update, feel free to suggest any changes here.

Choice Attacker.description:
• Rotom-H sets itself apart from other Fire-types, with its Ground immunity and Volt Switch pivoting. When compared to Rotom-W, it is also much more effective at pressuring Flutter Mane, Gholdengo and Wo-Chien.

  • Trick: Trick gives Rotom-H an excellent tool against defensive foes, such as Dondozo and Skeledirge.

  • Using a neutral nature with a Timid mint: Make sure to get a Rotom-H with a neutral nature and then use a Timid Mint on it. This way, it can't be confused by any Berries given with Trick.

Other Options
  • Discharge: While weaker than Thunderbolt, the 30% paralysis chance can be devastating for some of Rotom-H's more troublesome matchups, such as Chi-Yu. Do note though that Choice Scarf Rotom-H will have a much harder time 2HKOing Assault Vest Azumarill and certain variants of Dondozo.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low / Medium: If not running Tera Blast, Rotom-H normally wants to keep its unique typing for defensive purposes, allowing it to switch into several key threats. The most common exception to this is sets that run Tera Fairy for Dragon-type matchups.

  • Electric: Electric is an easy Tera type to recommend, as it increases damage output and removes all of Rotom-H's weaknesses.

  • Fairy: A Fairy Tera typing with Tera Blast makes Rotom-H much better equipped to handle normally problematic Dragon-types, such as Garchomp, Roaring Moon, and Dragapult.

  • Fire: When paired with Tera Blast, Rotom-H now has a much more reliable Fire-type STAB move than Overheat, but at the cost of retaining all of its normal weaknesses.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf lets Rotom-H outspeed normally problematic threats such as Iron Bundle.

  • Choice Specs: The extra power makes Rotom-H far more difficult to wall, with defensive Skeledirge getting 2HKOed by Thunderbolt.

Defensive Pivot.description:
• Rotom-W's defensive set might be the more known one, but Rotom-H's key resistances to Fairy-type attacks and U-turn, plus its ability to put serious pressure on Gholdengo, make it a good alternative as a bulky pivot.

  • Foul Play: Foul Play is a must-have, as otherwise, Rotom-H is extremely passive against Baxcalibur, which is likely to switch in for an Attack boost from Overheat.

  • Will-O-Wisp versus Thunder Wave: Will-O-Wisp is the preferred status move, potentially shutting down major physical threats such as Dragonite, Mimikyu, and Iron Hands. Thunder Wave is still a reasonable choice, though, stopping special attackers such as Flutter Mane and Iron Moth in their tracks.

  • Trick and Flame Orb: This one-use method of burning may seem silly, but taking away important items can be devastating against certain Pokemon such as Ting-Lu, and Rotom-H can use this to get rid of troublesome Choice items if it's taken a Trick as well. Note that Rotom-H will burn itself if it Terastallizes while holding Flame Orb, which is generally not good outside of blocking sleep or Toxic poison.

  • Using a Neutral Nature with a Bold Mint: If using Trick, it's best to run a neutral nature such as Serious and change the stat boosts with a Bold Mint. This way, Rotom-H won't get confused by any Berry it receives.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Rotom-H's defensive typing is very valuable, so Tera is normally reserved for very specific situations.

  • Steel: Tera Steel with Levitate is a sublime defensive typing, letting Rotom-H better handle huge threats like Dragonite, Garchomp, and Baxcalibur.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is an alternative option to soak up Dragon-type attacks, and it also gives Rotom-H a better matchup against Great Tusk and Iron Hands.

  • Ghost: While this unfortunately makes Gholdengo a much bigger issue, Tera Ghost is still worth considering for making Rotom-H immune to Dragonite's Extreme Speed and Iron Valiant's Close Combat. It also lets Rotom-H switch out of trapping moves without using Volt Switch.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is Rotom-H's ticket to staying around the longest, usually avoiding 2HKOs from powerful unboosted attacks such as Dragonite's Outrage and Iron Valiant's Close Combat.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rotom-H's typing makes it a good user of Rocky Helmet, passively punishing physical Fairy-types such as Mimikyu and Iron Valiant and making it a good response to expected uses of U-turn.

Offensive Pivot.description: 44 Defense EVs as a benchmark to avoid the 2HKO from Adamant Life Orb Mamoswine whilst maintaining speed.

Physically Defensive.description:
Rotom-W thrives as a pivot within the tier thanks to its unique typing, solid bulk in tandem with access to Pain Split, and access to a great ability in Levitate. Hydro Pump gives Rotom-W an excellent STAB option and makes the life of Ground-types wishing to block Volt Switch such as Rhyperior and Excadrill hard. Volt Switch lets Rotom-W generate momentum on Pokemon that would easily take a Hydro Pump such as Azumarill, Tornadus-T, and Slowking. Will-O-Wisp helps Rotom-W cripple physically offensive threats that dislike being burnt such as Ogerpon and Excadrill while slowly chipping down any burnt Pokemon. Thunder Wave, on the other hand, punishes Tornadus-T and Latios by slowing them down while helping teammates take advantage of the Speed cut as well as the chance of paralysis. Pain Split in tandem with Rotom-W's naturally low HP stat allows it to recover a significant amount of health on foes like Hydrapple and Slowking, keeping itself healthy throughout the game. Leftovers is used to increase Rotom-W's longevity over the course of the match, letting it passively recover its health. Rotom-W is able to run two distinct EV spreads, both of which maximize its HP while allowing it to outspeed Adamant Scizor and Tyranitar. Investment into Rotom-W's Defense with a Bold nature lets it handle Sand Rush Excadrill and Metagross while living a Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine Head Smash. Rotom-W with a Calm nature and EVs in Special Defense make it a solid check to Greninja, Tornadus-T, and Heatran. Tera Steel combined with Levitate removes the Ground weakness it would otherwise gain while gifting Rotom-W a spectacular defensive typing, letting it check Ogerpon-C and Latios better.

Rotom-W's traits fit best on bulky offense teams that love its ability to cripple opposing Pokemon while pivoting on and off the field. Wallbreakers such as Ogerpon-C and Metagross fit excellently with it, being able to take advantage of Latios, Hydrapple, and Clodsire, which may want to switch into Rotom-W to block its shenanigans, with Metagross also functioning as a solid Latios check. Other pivots that synergize well with Rotom-W such as Lokix, Scizor, and Tornadus-T are excellent teammates, with Lokix and Scizor forming a strong VoltTurn core while handling Ogerpon, Hydrapple, and Latios for Rotom-W, while Assault Vest Tornadus-T can pivot into Latios and Keldeo for it. Ogerpon specifically both functions as a pivot and a way of punishing setup sweepers like Dragon Dance Salamence and Calm Mind Latios with Encore thanks to Rotom-W's Volt Switch giving it free entry. Clodsire is particularly annoying for Rotom-W, blocking both of its STAB options with Water Absorb while giving it an opportunity to throw off a nasty Toxic, so teammates like Metagross and Air Balloon Tinkaton work amazingly with it. Entry hazard setters like the aforementioned Skarmory and Tinkaton, as well as Cobalion, are fantastic partners for Rotom-W that support it with their strong defensive profiles. Hydrapple is an great check to Excadrill as well as the Ogerpon formes that appreciates Rotom-W's ability to handle Flying- and Ice-type types like Tornadus-T, Weavile, and Mamoswine. Hisuian Arcanine functions excellently with Rotom-W, being able to maximize its offensive potential thanks to Rotom-W baiting in the likes of Hydrapple and Tinkaton for it, with Will-O-Wisp chipping down opposing checks like Mamoswine and Thunder Wave allowing Hisuian Arcanine to outspeed Pokemon like Latios and Keldeo.

Specially Defensive.description:
Specially defensive Rotom-Wash's excellent Water / Electric typing and Levitate allow it to deal with many special attackers and defensive Pokemon like Heatran, Greninja, Donphan, and Skarmory. Thunder Wave allows Rotom-Wash to paralyze faster foes such as Latios, Salamence, and Weavile, helping its slower offensive teammates like Metagross, Scizor, and Tyranitar outspeed those foes; it is also useful for crippling opposing Alolan Ninetales that wants to set up Aurora Veil in front of Rotom-Wash. Will-O-Wisp is a decent tool that shuts down physical attackers like Tyranitar, Lokix, and Metagross, enhancing Rotom-Wash's mixed bulk. Pain Split helps Rotom-Wash maintain longevity and feed off HP from bulky Pokemon like Clodsire, Blissey, and Slowking. Leftovers increases Rotom-Wash's longevity by providing passive recovery every turn and offsetting sandstorm damage. Tera Steel allows Rotom-Wash to resist Latios's STAB moves and Leaf Storm from Hydrapple and Serperior, letting it paralyze them with Thunder Wave in return and cripple their Speed for the rest of the game, making them less overwhelming. Tera Steel can also be used to wall Clodsire with its Steel typing and Levitate, which would otherwise be a problem for Rotom-Wash.

With its defensive role, pivoting, and status support, Rotom-Wash fits on bulky offense and VoltTurn teams, pairing well with Pokemon like Scizor, Lokix, and Fezandipiti. Rotom-Wash is a great counter to Heatran, switching into its Magma Storm and threatening it with Hydro Pump while also dealing with common special attackers like Keldeo, Iron Jugulis, and Thundurus. It is also a strong pivot and momentum generator, which enables wallbreakers like Hisuian Arcanine, Weavile, and Latios to come onto the field in favorable matchups when opponents try to resist Rotom-Wash's Hydro Pump or Volt Switch. Common counters to Rotom-Wash include Water Absorb Clodsire, Gastrodon, Substitute sets of Hydreigon and Latios, and most Grass-types. Teammates like Weavile and Lokix help deal with these threats, and Rotom-Wash's Volt Switch allows them to enter the field safely.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Rotom-W is a defensive pivot that takes advantage of its good defensive typing and ability, providing it with a crucial immunity to Spikes even after Terastallizing for it to switch around freely and letting it bring in a teammate more safely. Hydro Pump synergizes well with Volt Switch, punishing Ground-types like Ting-Lu and Great Tusk attempting to block it. Pain Split serves as a semi-reliable recovery option that lets it more consistently check threats like Great Tusk, Gliscor, and Darkrai throughout the course of a game. It also uses defensive Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Blissey as an opportunity to get back to full health due to the large differences in health. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical threats like Kingambit and Dragonite while punishing the likes of Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom from switching in. Leftovers is run to give Rotom-W additional passive recovery, but Rocky Helmet can also be used on physically defensive sets in order to punish contact attackers like Landorus-T, Cinderace, and Zamazenta. 44 Speed EVs allow Rotom-W to outspeed Jolly Kingambit. Tera Steel is used to gain a Toxic immunity, letting it completely wall Pokemon like Galarian Slowking, Gliscor, and Clodsire, and makes use of Levitate to wall foes like Kyurem, Dragonite, and Enamorus without Fire coverage.

Rotom-W best fits on balance and bulky offense teams utilizing pivoting cores like Landorus-T on bulky offense and Galarian Slowking on balance to make progress. Rotom-W is able to threaten Gliscor and Corviknight for Landorus-T, and Landorus-T is able to alleviate the Raging Bolt matchup, as well as checking Zamazenta. Rotom-W helps Galarian Slowking by switching into Ground-types like Landorus-T and Great Tusk that Galarian Slowking hates facing, and Galarian Slowking is able to check threats such as Kyurem's special attacking variants, Ogerpon, and Serperior for it. Gliscor is able to set Spikes, which stacks up chip alongside Rotom-W's frequent pivoting, and Swords Dance variants greatly appreciate Rotom-W being able to take on Corviknight and Skarmory for it. Bulky Grass-types like Amoonguss and Sinistcha are excellent partners because they are able to take on Ogerpon-W, which can switch in on Hydro Pump and threaten Rotom-W with Power Whip or Encore. Rotom-W is able to return the favor by checking Weavile and Fire-types like Heatran and Moltres for them. Garganacl is another good partner for Rotom-W, as Rotom-W can threaten Ground-types like Great Tusk and Ting-Lu that Garganacl struggles against, while Garganacl can stack chip damage through Stealth Rock and Salt Cure, as well as checking threats like Dragapult and Kyurem. Ting-Lu fits with physically defensive Rotom-W on balance teams to check Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Dragapult, since Dragapult resists both of Rotom-W's STAB moves and can threaten it back with Choice Specs-boosted Draco Meteor or Shadow Ball, while Gholdengo has enough natural special bulk to avoid the 2HKO from Hydro Pump and is immune to Rotom-W's status moves. Dragapult and Gholdengo themselves work well with Rotom-W because it can spread status effectively for both Pokemon to fire off boosted Hex later, which is especially good since Rotom-W also cripples Dark-types like Kingambit and Darkrai. Tinkaton can also work well with Rotom-W as a hazard setter that can punish setup sweepers and check Kyurem without needing to use Terastallization on Rotom-W.

Rotom-W is an excellent pivot, wielding a great STAB combination that lets it freely use Volt Switch on most Pokemon, with common Ground-types like Ting-Lu, Hippowdon, and Excadrill in perpetual fear of taking Hydro Pump or Will-O-Wisp. Defensively, Rotom-W doubles as a momentum-maintaining check to offensive threats such as Excadrill and Mega Aerodactyl for more offensively oriented teams. Rotom-W can utilize Defog effectively thanks to a good matchup into the aforementioned Ground-types, as well as Skarmory, the premier Spikes setter in the tier. Will-O-Wisp allows Rotom-W to cripple common physical attackers such as Swords Dance Aegislash, additionally wearing down Mega Venusaur. Toxic threatens some of the few Pokemon that do not fear Rotom-W's STAB moves, such as Tangrowth, Mega Latias, and Gastrodon. Lastly, Pain Split allows Rotom-W to maintain longevity, especially helping it stick around versus fatter teams utilizing Chansey or Blissey and further chip down Mega Venusaur. The given EV spread allows Rotom-W to outrun max Speed Tyranitar and get ahead of most offensive Aegislash variants. Given its nature as a pivot, teammates like Tyranitar, Alakazam, and Bisharp that can capitalize on foes Rotom-W often forces in, such as Chansey, Mega Latias, Mega Venusaur, and Clefable work incredibly well. Ground-types that do not fear Hydro Pump, such as Gastrodon and Swampert, give Rotom-W trouble; Mega Venusaur is a great teammate to threaten these foes for it while Rotom-W can often bring it in on Clefable and Hydrapple.

Choice Scarf.description: With a threatening STAB combination alongside a great defensive profile, Rotom-W is an excellent option for teams looking for speed control that provides a blend of power and utility and can repeatedly threaten foes like Excadrill and Iron Moth lacking Booster Energy throughout a game. Trick allows Rotom-W to cripple otherwise great counters like Gastrodon and Amoonguss, and while this leaves it unable to provide speed control, it also prevents foes like Ting-Lu and Tapu Fini from taking advantage of it being locked into Volt Switch or Hydro Pump, respectively. Defog is useful, as it grants Rotom-W even more utility, especially for offensive teams that find it hard to fit entry hazard control, and it lets it deal with common hazard setters in Ting-Lu and Skarmory. On teams with other forms of hazard control, Will-O-Wisp can be utilized to check bulkier physical attackers, such as Swords Dance Aegislash. 236 Speed EVs ensure Choice Scarf Rotom-W outspeeds Mega Aerodactyl while 32 Special Attack EVs allow it to OHKO Excadrill with Hydro Pump; the rest being invested in HP. Rotom-W is utilized most effectively on offensive teams that appreciate its power and utility, but it can also be used on bulkier teams if given proper team support. Teammates like Mienshao and Hydreigon appreciate the pivot support Rotom-W provides, bringing them in on foes like Blissey and Hydrapple, while forming a pivoting core that can bring it in on their checks, like Slowbro and Tapu Fini. Rotom-W is stifled by Grass-types, especially Mega Venusaur, as Rotom-W cannot use Trick to cripple it with Choice Scarf, so checks to them like Celesteela and Scizor are appreciated. In return, Rotom-W can check Fire-types such as Iron Moth and Victini for its partners. Choice Scarf Rotom-W also suffers from a lack of longevity, as it must invest heavily in Speed and cannot utilize Pain Split or Leftovers; therefore, it appreciates faster team compositions with teammates like Enamorus, Excadrill, and Tyranitar that aim to win quickly, which allows Rotom-W to leverage its defensive profile efficiently short-term to grant it and its teammates more attacking opportunities. On bulkier team structures alongside defensive options like Celesteela and Ting-Lu, Rotom-W appreciates Wish support from partners like Clefable and Chansey to allow it to stay healthy throughout the game, given its lack of recovery.

Nasty Plot.description: Supported by its good typing, Levitate, and decent Speed tier, Rotom-W can become a solid offensive threat with Nasty Plot, able to leverage its defensive profile to consistently find setup opportunities against Pokemon it checks such as Scizor, Sand Rush Excadrill, and Ting-Lu. Nasty Plot also allows Rotom-W to potentially beat setup variants of Clefable and Roost Scizor one-on-one, outboosting them before they can deal significant damage back. Hydro Vortex not only allows Rotom-W to immediately OHKO threats such as Iron Moth and Iron Boulder that would otherwise survive Hydro Pump at full HP, but it can also break past weakened Amoonguss and Mega Latias at +4 and Blissey at +6, respectively. Volt Switch allows Rotom-W to support its team in scenarios where it is unable to wallbreak effectively, facilitating frail offensive threats such as Life Orb Mienshao and Iron Boulder with safe entry. Lastly, Pain Split keeps Rotom-W healthy by sapping HP from defensive targets such as Celesteela and Blissey, making it easier to shrug off potential aliments such as Leech Seed and Toxic from them while trying to set up with Nasty Plot. 56 Speed EVs allow Rotom-W to outspeed Adamant Tyranitar, while the rest are put into HP and Defense to maximize its ability to handle physical attackers such as Mega Aerodactyl and Swords Dance Aegislash when combined with a Bold nature. However, additional Speed EVs can be considered to ensure Rotom-W outpaces specific threats such as Swords Dance Scizor and Bisharp at the cost of some physical bulk. Nasty Plot Rotom-W fits best on hazard-stacking bulky offense and balance teams, which are best suited to helping it overwhelm potential checks such as Mega Venusaur and Mega Latias with sheer offensive pressure or residual damage, respectively. Hazard setters such as Gastrodon, Clefable, and Skarmory are critical for their ability to set Stealth Rock and Spikes, which can wear down and deplete the recovery options of some of the aforementioned checks; Gastrodon and Skarmory can also lure Hydrapple and cripple it with Toxic, which otherwise doesn't mind taking hazard chip damage thanks to Regenerator and otherwise completely counters Rotom-W, whereas Clefable can remove Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Blissey with Knock Off. Conversely, dedicated wallbreakers such as Life Orb Mienshao, mixed Aegislash, and Mega Gardevoir are highly effective as partners for their ability to force progress against Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur, Calm Mind Clefable, and Slowking, paving the way for Rotom-W to break past them later; in return, Rotom-W can assist these Pokemon by providing a safety net against potential revenge killers such as Sand Rush Excadrill and Scizor. On either archetype, paralysis support from Serperior, Thunder Wave Clefable, and Prankster Thundurus is appreciated for luring in and crippling Pokemon such as Mega Latias, Serperior, and Alakazam early in the match, as losing the ability to outspeed Rotom-W dilutes their ability to answer it after a boost.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Rotom-W's exceptional typing, Levitate, and decent utility movepool give it a solid place in the metagame as a defensive pivot capable of switching into offensive staples like Melmetal and Heatran while also being able to threaten out Ground-types like Landorus-T and Great Tusk from blocking Volt Switch. Will-O-Wisp shuts down threats like Mega Scizor, Kingambit, and Urshifu-R, allowing Rotom-W to more easily check them throughout the course of a game. Rotom-W also threatens their teammates that would normally absorb Will-O-Wisp such as Gliscor and Heatran. Thunder Wave deals with faster threats like Mega Lopunny and Iron Valiant, helping teammates that these Pokemon would otherwise outspeed and threaten out like Mega Tyranitar and Gholdengo. Pain Split is Rotom-W's only form of reliable recovery, so it often struggles with longevity; it lets Rotom-W gain back health from switch-ins such as Galarian Slowking and Raging Bolt. Leftovers is used to gain extra healing, as Pain Split is somewhat unreliable in the face of chipped down threats that can mitigate that healing.

Rotom-W fits best on offense and bulky offense teams that appreciate it pivoting in their big threats and benefit from it crippling the opposing team. Pokemon like Mega Medicham and Mega Tyranitar specifically like the fact that Rotom-W can take on faster threats like Great Tusk and Choice Scarf Landorus-T that would otherwise threaten them out while also appreciating it luring its checks such as Ting-Lu and Galarian Slowking, respectively. Both also value the potential Thunder Wave support Rotom-W can give. Rotom-W can't take on Grass-types like Ogerpon-W, Kartana, and Rillaboom, so Pokemon that help in this regard, like Dragonite and Volcarona, can be very useful. Due to Rotom-W's below-par special bulk, it's very susceptible to attacks from Raging Bolt, Mega Latios, and Serperior, which means that special walls like Ferrothorn and Galarian Slowking are very appreciated. Galarian Slowking in particular can form a pivoting core with Rotom-W, which fits beautifully on the teams that Rotom-W is usually found on, while Ferrothorn can easily handle Grass-types like Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom for it. Since Pain Split is not a reliable source of recovery, Rotom-W's Leftovers is very important to it; therefore, Knock Off absorbers like Mega Diancie and Clefable are great partners so Rotom-W can stay healthy over the course of a longer game.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Rotom-W acts as a niche speed control option, being able to leverage its amazing defensive typing and access to Levitate to switch in on Landorus-T and Gliscor and threaten them with its STAB moves. Volt Switch allows Rotom-W to gain momentum on switch-ins such as Ferrothorn, Raging Bolt and Roaring Moon while also hitting Hydro Pump-resistant foes such as Toxapex and Alomomola for good damage. Trick can be used in order to cripple defensive pieces that would otherwise beat Rotom-W such as Ferrothorn and Galarian Slowking. After using Trick, Will-O-Wisp can be used in order to weaken Roaring Moon, Garchomp and Ogerpon-W, all of which might otherwise switch in on Rotom-W's STAB moves, while Thunder Wave is another option to slow down special attacking sweepers such as Volcarona and Iron Valiant.

Choice Scarf Rotom-W fits predominantly on bulky offense teams, where its ability to switch in on Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Great Tusk and gain momentum is appreciated. Rotom-W struggles to break through Grass-types such as Ferrothorn and Serperior, meaning Fire-types such as Heatran and Volcarona are appreciated in order to break these as well as defensively answer them. In return, Rotom-W provides a Ground-immune switch-in against Garchomp, Gliscor, and Landorus-T and can threaten them with Hydro Pump. Rotom-W is also prone to faster threats such as Mega Lopunny and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele due to its lack of reliable recovery, meaning consistent switch-ins to them such as Toxapex and Gholdengo respectively are appreciated, with both also absorbing Toxic from Melmetal for Rotom-W. Rotom-W also finds itself prone to entry hazard chip damage across the course of a game due to its lack of Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots, meaning hazard removal options such as Great Tusk, Defog Gliscor, and Terapagos are all great partners. In exchange, Rotom-W can switch in on and force out bulky Water-types such as Slowbro and Alomomola, which would otherwise switch in on them comfortably. Rotom-W's ability to deal heavy damage to Flying-types like Moltres and Corviknight is appreciated by teammates like Garchomp and Zamazenta, which in return can break through bulky Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Melmetal, which would otherwise cause Rotom-W trouble. Wallbreakers such as Mega Latios and Zamazenta appreciate Rotom-W being able to get them in on foes they specialize against, such as defensive pieces like Mega Venusaur and Toxapex for the former and Steel-types like Heatran and Ferrothorn for the latter; Rotom-W can also bring Pursuit trappers such as Kingambit and Weavile in on Psychic-types such as opposing Mega Latios and Galarian Slowking. Trick can also annoy defensive teams, being able to cripple bulkier Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Ting-Lu to the benefit of teammates like Zapdos, Raging Bolt, and Tapu Koko, all of which would otherwise be walled by them. Rotom-W can also form a VoltTurn core with partners like Mega Scizor and Mega Lopunny, with Rotom-W being able to switch in on their would-be answers such as Toxapex and Alomomola. In return Mega Lopunny can threaten Ferrothorn, and Mega Scizor can pivot into offensive Grass-types such as Rillaboom and Kartana for Rotom-W.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Hydro Pump allows Rotom-W to threaten Fire- and Ground-types that would normally check it like bulky Gouging Fire and Excadrill. However, most of Rotom-W's teammates can handle said checks, so it is best for Rotom-W to have coverage against other types.

Electric

Thunder Wave is a nice option to slow down enemies and give Pokemon like Zapdos and Iron Hands an easier time taking them down. 192 HP / 108 Def / 208 Spe with a Bold nature is an alternative spread, outspeeding Choice Band Dragonite, which can be problematic for Electric teams. 248 HP / 180 Def / 68 SpD / 12 Spe with a Calm nature gets the jump on uninvested Great Tusk, avoids the 2HKO from Sheer Force Life Orb Landorus's Psychic, and allows Rotom-W to switch into mixed Iron Valiant and Greninja in a pinch. This spread also leaves Rotom-W capable of surviving a Blood Moon from Ursaluna-B.

Physically Defensive (Electric).description:
Thanks to Levitate, decent physical bulk, and access to tools like Will-O-Wisp and Pain Split, Rotom-W is the premier physical wall for Electric teams, holding its ground against most Ground-type physical sweepers such as Mamoswine and Excadrill. Will-O-Wisp virtually doubles its defensive bulk against afflicted foes and is thus crucial to handle sweepers like Barraskewda, Roaring Moon, and Dragon Dance Dragonite. Hydro Pump threatens Ground-type Pokemon that Electric teams would otherwise struggle against, such as Great Tusk, Gliscor, and Mamoswine. Volt Switch allows Rotom-W's more threatening wallbreaking teammates to come in more easily. Pain Split is Rotom-W's best option to heal itself and helps it to weaken defensive foes it would have trouble damaging otherwise like Hisuian Goodra, Archaludon, and Blissey.

As Rotom-W may lack recovery due to Pain Split's mechanism, pairing it with a dual screens setter like Regieleki is advised. Thanks to its blitzing Speed, Regieleki can safely set dual screens before the opponent can act. Regieleki can also perform as great spinner to keep Stealth Rock away while pivoting in Rotom-W with Volt Switch to avoid Ground-type moves, which allows Rotom-W to better handle Roaring Moon and Choice Band Dragonite. Zapdos forms a potent defensive core with Rotom-W, taking care of special attackers such as Iron Valiant and Gholdengo, while Rotom-W handles physical attackers like Iron Hands and Mamoswine. Assault Vest Iron Hands is another prominent partner that helps tremendously in the Dragon matchup by addressing Choice Specs Dragapult and Raging Bolt. Sandy Shocks can set up both Stealth Rock and Spikes to weaken the opposing team and can also act as a great anti-sun sweeper in the Fire matchup by making use of Protosynthesis's Speed boost and its access to Power Gem and Earth Power. With the Will-O-Wisp support from Rotom-W, Raging Bolt can leverage its great bulk and power to muscle through teams such as Fighting and Dark. Assault Vest Magnezone is another option to improve the Dragon and Fairy matchups by directly addressing Latios, Flutter Mane, and Hatterene, which would be otherwise hard to deal with.

Nasty Plot (Electric).description:
Rotom-W is a great Nasty Plot sweeper for Electric teams due to Levitate and its bulk, which lets it greatly ease the Ground matchup. Stored Power deals with Unaware and Water Absorb users such as Quagsire and Clodsire, letting it threaten the entirety of Ground teams in conjunction with Hydro Pump. Substitute lets it avoid status and take advantage of passive Pokemon such as Klefki and Toxapex, eases prediction, and forces its checks such as Greninja and Ting-Lu to take damage. The given EV spread prevents Rotom-W's Substitute from breaking to Clodsire's Poison Jab while outspeeding threats such as Gholdengo and Kleavor.

Teammates such as Choice Scarf Sandy Shocks and Iron Hands love Rotom-W's ability to deal with or wear down bulky Pokemon such as Clodsire and Gastrodon, allowing them to clean up types like Poison and Water late-game. In return, Choice Scarf Sandy Shocks deals with fast threats such as Choice Specs Greninja, Flutter Mane, and Choice Band Sneasler, while Iron Hands pressures matchups such as Dark and Dragon due to its sheer bulk and coverage in Ice Punch. Pawmot can revive Rotom-W with Revival Blessing, which allows it to take more risks. Additionally, Pawmot has good coverage moves in Seed Bomb and Ice Punch, which lets it break down types such as Water, Flying, and Ground alongside Rotom-W. Assault Vest Magnezone deals with special attackers such as Flutter Mane, Hatterene, and Greninja for Rotom-W. Magnezone also tend to invite in passive Pokemon, which provides Rotom-W with more setup opportunities.

Nasty Plot (Water).description:
Substitute + Nasty Plot Rotom-W is a great wallbreaker for Water teams. By virtue of its Ground immunity thanks to Levitate and its part Electric typing, it eases the Ground, Water mirror, and Flying matchups. Thunderbolt threatens a multitude of metagame staples such as Corviknight, Skarmory, and Toxapex. Discharge, although having less power than Thunderbolt, has a decent chance to spread paralysis, potentially hindering setup attempts from the likes of Dragonite and Dragapult. Stored Power in conjunction with Nasty Plot allows Rotom-W to threaten Poison- and Fighting-types such as Clodsire, Amoonguss, and Great Tusk. Substitute allows Rotom-W to take advantage of passive walls like Toxapex and Swampert to set up a Nasty Plot. 144 HP and 112 Defense EVs allow Rotom-W's Substitute to withstand a Poison Jab from Clodsire, while 88 Speed EVs allow Rotom-W to outspeed Adamant Scizor.

Toxapex is a nice defensive partner for Rotom-W, as its Poison typing and natural bulk help against Grass-types such as Meowscarada and Ogerpon-H. In return, Rotom-W handles Ground-types that Toxapex struggles with like Great Tusk and Gliscor. Entry hazard support from the likes of Swampert and Hisuian Samurott helps Rotom-W wallbreak. Swampert also acts as a slow pivot, bringing Rotom-W in safely against Corviknight and Great Tusk, while Hisuian Samurott takes on fast Ghost-types such as Dragapult and Gholdengo. Choice Scarf users such as Keldeo, Greninja, and Urshifu-R act as speed control against speedy threats. Keldeo and Urshifu-R threaten Choice Specs Iron Moth, Roaring Moon, and Landorus, while Greninja threatens Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Ogerpon-W. Primarina handles Dragon-types such as Latios, Gouging Fire, and Roaring Moon, and in return, Rotom-W handles passive Poison-types such as Toxapex and Clodsire. Lastly, Rotom-W's wallbreaking allows sweepers like Ogerpon-W to clean late-game.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis is for the Regulation C format of Battle Stadium Singles, which lasts until June 30th, 2023. For more information on this format and its current events, check out this page!

If you feel this analysis is missing anything important or needs an update, feel free to suggest any changes here.

Offensive.description:
• Rotom-W's Speed access to Volt Switch and great typing make it an excellent pivot and revenge killer.

  • Trick and Neutral Natures: If using a Choice item, Trick is seriously worth considering for its ability to cripple defensive Pokemon such as Garganacl and Dondozo. Make sure Rotom-W is a neutral nature that has had a Timid Mint used on it. This way, Rotom-W can eat any Berry without getting confused.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Rotom-W's excellent typing means its fully functional without Terastallizing, but thanks to Levitate, it's still a powerful user of it.

  • Fairy: When combined with Tera Blast, a Fairy Tera type lets Rotom-W take on Chien-Pao Dragon-types such as Dragapult and Roaring Moon far more effectively.

  • Electric: Not only does the damage boost from Tera Electric come in handy, but it also removes any weaknesses Rotom-W has.

  • Ghost: Terastallizing back to its Ghost-type roots gives Rotom-W a vast array of immunities, helping against Dragonite and Great Tusk in particular. It also makes Shadow Ball viable for picking off Ghost-types with Choice Scarf.

Items

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs tends to be safer to Trick than Choice Scarf, and it gives a big power boost.

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf lets Rotom-W outspeed major threats such as Iron Bundle, Chi-Yu, and Chien-Pao.

  • Assault Vest: Increasing Rotom-W's special bulk gives it a far better matchup against foes like Flutter Mane, Chi-Yu, Iron Bundle, and Gholdengo.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 SpA / 4 SpD with Modest: This spread sacrifices Rotom-W's revenge killing potential, but, in exchange, it makes it a better pivot, and the better bulk makes Rotom-W more suited to finding the right time to cripple a wall with Trick.

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Timid: Maximizing Rotom-W's Special Attack is part of what makes it an effective revenge killer if using a Choice Scarf.

  • 252 HP / 4 Def / 108 SpA / 140 SpD / 4 Spe with Calm: This spread is meant for Assault Vest, letting Rotom-W avoid a 3HKO from Modest Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry.

Defensive Pivot.description:
• Levitate and excellent status moves make Rotom-W a clean choice for a bulky pivot!

  • Foul Play: Foul Play is essential for hitting Baxcalibur hard, since it's immunity to burns would otherwise let it set up on Rotom-W.

  • Will-O-Wisp versus Thunder Wave: Will-O-Wisp's ability to cripple top-tier physically offensive threats such as Dragonite, Chien-Pao, and Scizor as well as punish the otherwise problematic Iron Hands makes it the best support option. However, Thunder Wave does provide additional insurance against Baxcalibur and punishes special attackers such as Flutter Mane.

  • Hydro Pump: Hydro Pump gives Rotom-W offensive presence against foes that don't care about the rest of the moveset, like Garganacl, Chi-Yu, Volcarona, and Skeledirge.

Other Options

  • Discharge: Giving Rotom-W an Electric STAB attack to better deal with Flying-types like Corviknight and Tera Flying Roaring Moon is useful, but it can be tricky to fit into the set.

  • Hex: If using Tera Ghost, Hex gives Rotom-W a much fiercer offensive kick than usual after inflicting status.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Defensive Rotom-W works fine without Terastallizing, but some Tera types do make it harder to break through.

  • Steel: Tera Steel gives Rotom-W an incredible defensive typing, vastly improving its matchups against Pokemon that rely on Ground-type coverage such as Dragonite, Baxcalibur, and Garchomp. It also provides a useful Freeze-Dry resistance against Iron Bundle.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy guards against fearsome powerful Dark-, Dragon-, and Fighting-type attacks that Rotom-W can have trouble handling and lets it use Tera Blast to hit Dragonite and Chien-Pao hard.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost offers Rotom-W a vast array of immunities with Levitate, enabling it to defeat certain Dragonite sets and do much better against Iron Hands and Iron Valiant when Rotom-W lacks Will-O-Wisp. Being a Ghost-type also prevents Rotom-W from getting trapped, letting it escape faster trappers without Volt Switch.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry will turn many powerful, unboosted attacks such as Jolly Life Orb Chien-Pao's Crunch, Dragonite's Outrage and Baxcalibur's Glaive Rush into 3HKOs. Just make sure to run an even HP stat so that Sitrus Berry activates with one use of Ruination.

  • Leftovers: If Sitrus Berry is already in use, Leftovers is a reasonable alternative.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet's extra chip damage can make Rotom-W a less passive pivot.

Nasty Plot.description:
• With a great typing, ability, and good bulk, Rotom-W makes for an effective user of Nasty Plot.

  • Fairy Tera Blast: This move is essential for getting past Dragon-types like Dragapult and Roaring Moon. Even when not Terastallized, it's a decent coverage move.

  • Hydro Pump versus Substitute: Hydro Pump is by far Rotom-W's strongest STAB, but it can be worth sacrificing for Substitute, which lets Rotom-W effectively defeat most Garganacl and defensive Dondozo.

Tera Types
  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While this Rotom-W can sweep on its own, Terastallization can prevent revenge kills from the likes of Iron Bundle.
  • Fairy: With a Fairy Tera type, Rotom-W can turn the tables on its Dragon-type adversaries, as well as catch Crunch Chien-Pao off guard.
Items

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry lets Rotom-W easily set up on Hippowdon, and avoid getting put to sleep by Dondozo.

  • Sitrus Berry: If Sleep isn't a big issue, Rotom-W appreciates the burst recovery Sitrus Berry provides. Make sure to run an even HP stat so it activates after Rotom-W gets hit by Ruination once.

  • Covert Cloak: If using Hydro Pump, this is Rotom-W's best way around Garganacl.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe: Maximizing Speed with a Timid nature gives Rotom-W the jump on Gholdengo. If Gholdengo isn't an issue, a Modest nature will still outspeed Jolly Breloom.

  • 252 HP / 252 SpA / 4 SpD with Modest: Rotom-W's good bulk can be maximized instead of outspeeding Breloom; this spread avoids the 2HKO from Timid Gholdengo's Shadow Ball.

  • 244 HP / 180 Def / 84 SpA with Bold: This Sitrus Berry optimized spread avoids a 2HKO from Jolly Life Orb Chien-Pao and Timid Flutter Mane.

Defensive Pivot (HP).description:
Rotom-Wash is a versatile pivot that uses its solid mixed bulk and good type combination to bring frailer teammates in safely while also being able to support them by spreading status effects to the opposing team. Hydro Pump provides solid STAB damage to keep Rotom-Wash from being too passive and punishes Ground-types like Great Tusk and Iron Treads that can switch into Volt Switch. In the last two moveslots, Rotom-Wash can run any combination of Thunder Wave, Will-O-Wisp, and Protect; Thunder Wave cripples Pokemon that rely on their Speed, like Weavile, Sneasler, and Zacian-C, while Will-O-Wisp neutralizes physical attackers like the previous three, as well as Calyrex-I and Rillaboom. Pain Split works better when receiving lower HP stats from gods such as Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C, as it heals more than when receiving HP from gods like Arceus and Eternatus, in which case it's better to use Protect to stall turns while Rotom-Wash regains HP from Leftovers. Tera Steel allows Rotom-Wash to defend against Grass-types like Rillaboom, Ogerpon, and Meowscarada, and being a Steel-type with an immunity to Ground gives it a generally sound defensive typing. Leftovers is important because it provides Rotom-Wash with much needed recovery, as it lacks consistent healing options, so it needs to be careful switching into Pokemon with Knock Off like Weavile, Great Tusk, and Hisuian Samurott.

Rotom-Wash fits well on offensive teams that can make full use of the momentum it creates while also typically playing shorter games, which gives opponents less time to exploit its lack of longevity. Rotom-Wash is able to switch into physical attackers such as Weavile, Hisuian Samurott, and Zamazenta and even some gods such as Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Calyrex-I and scare them out with the threat of Will-O-Wisp or Thunder Wave. Setup sweepers like Weavile, Ogerpon-W, and Landorus appreciate Rotom-Wash's ability to pivot them in safely while also crippling opposing wallbreakers with status effects. Rotom-Wash also creates free switch-ins for wallbreakers with more immediate power such as Choice Band Urshifu-S, Choice Band Rillaboom, and Power Herb Glimmora, which can KO bulky foes like Pecharunt, Hydrapple, and Clefable that Rotom-Wash and its teammates struggle with. Gods with high base HP stats, like Eternatus and Arceus, are ideal donors for sets using Protect, while gods with lower base HP stats like Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C are better for sets running Pain Split. Rotom-Wash struggles greatly with Grass-types so it's happiest alongside teammates that can reliably switch into them such as Heatran, Corviknight, and Galarian Slowking; the latter two have the additional benefit of U-turn and Chilly Reception, respectively, allowing them to form strong pivoting cores that excel at getting the right Pokemon onto the field.

Bulky Pivot (Electric).description: With its access to Levitate, Rotom-W is nearly mandatory on all Electric teams. Its Ground immunity and Water-type resistance make Pokemon like Mega Swampert unable to bother it; it also has access to Hydro Pump to hit annoying Ground-types such as Great Tusk and Hippowdon. Rotom-W is also a really good blanket check to Ice- and Fire-types like Mamoswine, Victini, and Galarian Darmanitan. Volt Switch provides great momentum, which is needed in hyper offense teams. In addition to providing momentum, Rotom-W has access to Will-O-Wisp and Toxic, crippling foes such as Mega Garchomp and Mimikyu with Will-O-Wisp, while Toxic punishes switch-ins such as Gastrodon and Kyurem. Defog lets Rotom-W compress roles, freeing up Zapdos to run Choice Specs, while Rotom-W prevents hazards from hurting teammates. Pain Split is another option, as it massively improves Rotom-W's longevity; however, this requires Zapdos to run Defog. The 44 invested Speed EVs ensure Rotom-W outspeeds Jolly Azumarill so that it can punish Azumarill for setting up Belly Drum with Will-O-Wisp or Volt Switch. Zapdos covers Rotom-W's weakness to Grass-types with access to Hurricane and Heat Wave, being able to OHKO the likes of Mega Venusaur and Ferrothorn, respectively, while also being immune to Mold Breaker Excadrill's Earthquake. Regieleki can be used as a Rapid Spinner, removing pressure from Rotom-W to function as the only hazard removal while also luring in Ground-types that Rotom-W can punish such as Iron Treads or Great Tusk. With access to Taunt and having an amazing Speed tier, Zeraora can prevent hazards from coming up and allow Rotom-W to switch in freely and get off a strong Hydro Pump or gain a lot of momentum and Volt Switch into one of its offensive teammates. Zeraora also pressures Hydreigon and Gholdengo, which can use Rotom-W as setup fodder. Iron Hands provides the coverage and bulk against Pokemon like Dragon Dance Dragonite, Volcarona, and SubRoost Kyurem that Rotom-W can't deal with while also putting a lot of pressure on Normal teams, as Rotom-W can Volt Switch against Blissey into Iron Hands and force Blissey to tank a hit or switch out. Alolan Raichu gives Rotom-W's slow Volt Switch a lot of value as it is strong but frail, being able to deal with Ice-types like Baxcalibut with Focus Blast and Poison-types like Mega Venusaur and Clodsire with Psyshock. Magnezone provides a valuable Poison immunity while also checking other threats like Tapu Lele, Meowscarada, and Alolan Ninetales.

Choice Scarf.description:
Rotom-C makes for a decent Choice Scarf user with its solid typing, useful moves such as Trick and Volt Switch, Levitate, and solid stats all-around. While Rotom-C's Speed is average, with the Choice Scarf, it still outspeeds the entire unboosted metagame, other Choice Scarf users like Hoopa, and Speed-boosted Pokemon like Rapid Spin Tatsugiri and Dragon Dance Scrafty. Rotom-C's typing is what differentiates it from other fast Electric-types like Kilowattrel and Choice Scarf Toxtricity, letting it resist moves like Paldean Tauros-W's Wave Crash and Aqua Jet and threaten foes that can absorb Volt Switch like Golurk, Mudsdale, and, most notably, Gastrodon. While Rotom-C shares its typing with Hisuian Electrode, it is the preferred offensive option because it has naturally higher Special Attack, offers different utility moves, and does not need to hold Heavy-Duty Boots; Choice Scarf even allows Rotom-C to make up for its lower Speed. Thunderbolt gives Rotom-C a stronger Electric-type move and a more spammable STAB attack without the need to switch out or worry about stat drops. Discharge can help support slower teammates thanks to its high paralysis chance, and its lower Base Power is almost never a significant drawback. Electric is the go-to Tera type on Rotom-C, improving its ability to wear foes down with Volt Switch and clean up with either Thunderbolt or Discharge. Tera Electric also leaves Rotom-C with no weaknesses and allows it to tank certain moves like Brave Bird from Staraptor and Flamigo.

Rotom-C will often click Volt Switch, letting it form a solid VoltTurn core with other pivots such as Scyther, Staraptor, Gligar, and Bruxish. This momentum ideally leads to the opponent switching a lot, making Gligar and other hazard setters like Duraludon and Qwilfish useful for building up chip damage. Being Choice-locked can leave Rotom-C very prediction-reliant, especially against foes immune to Volt Switch such as Gastrodon, Golurk, and Mudsdale. Gastrodon is especially notable, since it sometimes runs Sticky Hold for an immunity to Trick. Offensive checks to these Pokemon such as Meloetta, Staraptor, and Paldean Tauros-W help ease a wrong prediction, and the first two have pivot moves of their own. Teammates that can lure in and weaken these threats throughout the match such as Goodra, Ambipom, and Copperajah can also help with this. With Grass- and Dragon-types such Decidueye, Virizion, and Goodra resisting both of Rotom-C's STAB moves, it appreciates pairing with checks to them like Skuntank, Galarian Slowbro, and Florges, respectively. In return, Rotom-C offers resistances to some of their threats, such as Ground-types like Mudsdale and Steel-types like Bronzong and Copperajah. A handful of Electric-types such as Rotom-H, Kilowattrel, and Toxtricity also resist both of Rotom-C's STAB moves, so their own checks like Goodra, Gastrodon, and Golurk also come in handy. As Choice Scarf Rotom-C does not outspeed certain boosted setup sweepers like Shift Gear Toxtricity and Shell Smash Minior and other Choice Scarf users like Flamigo, it may be useful to have another form of speed control such as priority users like Extreme Speed Arcanine and Sucker Punch Skuntank. Rotom-C also loses its speed control capabilities after Trick, making these Pokemon even more valuable to have around.

nu.overview: Uxie's deep movepool and solid bulk carve a role out for it as either a bulky setup sweeper or utility pivot. Nasty Plot sets have an easy time setting up thanks to Uxie's high defensive stats, which also make them good candidates for defensive Terastallization. Options like Encore, U-turn, Stealth Rock, and Knock Off make Uxie an excellent role compressor. However, Uxie's mediocre Special Attack makes it very passive unless it's set up multiple times, and it struggles to break through common Steel-types like Bronzong and Copperajah even after setting up. Uxie's passivity means its utility sets are easily taken advantage of by common Dark-types like Incineroar and Overqwil. The mono-Psychic typing does few favors for Uxie defensively, which can make it reliant on Terastallization to reliably sweep.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Nasty Plot Uxie can invest more EVs into its bulk to make it more difficult to take out, but doing so makes Uxie both far more passive and reliant on multiple Nasty Plot boosts to sweep. Said set can consider using Psyshock over Psychic Noise to hit specially defensive foes like Goodra and Calm Mind Sylveon much harder. Pivot sets can use Future Sight over Psychic Noise to put its teammates in even better positions against pressured foes. Utility Uxie can function as a setter for rain, sun, and Trick Room teams with Stealth Rock and Memento, though such dedicated teams tend to be more niche.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Setup Uxie sets are almost incapable of beating Steel-types on their own without setting up several times, locking them into ineffective moves with Encore, and keeping up pressure with Psychic Noise. Utility sets are too passive to beat Steel-types at all, but Bronzong and Copperajah dislike losing their Leftovers to Knock Off.

Dark-types: Nasty Plot Uxie cannot break through Incineroar easily, and it especially dislikes losing its item to Knock Off. However, it can be overwhelmed by Uxie Terastallizing. More offensive Dark-types like Skuntank, Grimmsnarl, and Bombirdier provide a larger threat with Sucker Punch if Uxie lacks Substitute to ease the guessing game.

Ghost-types: Basculegion-M, Chandelure, and Brambleghast all threaten Uxie, but they should be wary of Knock Off from utility sets.

Toxic: If Nasty Plot Uxie is not behind Substitute, then Munkidori and Gligar can at least put it on a timer. Utility sets are especially vulnerable to users like Goodra and Amoonguss punishing it given their lack of recovery beyond Leftovers.

Nasty Plot.description:
Set Details

Psychic Noise helps Uxie suffocate walls like Sylveon, Tera Steel Wo-Chien, and Vaporeon, somewhat compensating for its passivity. Draining Kiss covers Dark-types, but it's primarily used in tandem with Terastallization to increase Uxie's longevity. Encore can shut down walls and utility Pokemon like Bronzong and Gligar by locking them into utility moves, creating opportunities for Uxie to use them as setup fodder and eventually overwhelm them. Uxie can similarly use Encore against slower offensive Pokemon like Swampert and Scrafty to force them into repeatedly using less effective attacks against it, opening windows for itself to sweep. Substitute protects Uxie from slower Toxic users like Gligar and Bellibolt as well as Leech Seed from Wo-Chien, helping maintain its great longevity as it sweeps, and it can proceed to use them as opportunities to set up. Uxie also has more breathing room against revenge killers like Paldean Tauros-W and Scyther when it's protected by Substitute. Shadow Ball allows Uxie to blow past would-be walls in Scream Tail and Bronzong, though it comes at the cost of the utility of other status moves. Tera Fairy powers up Draining Kiss and gives Uxie a great defensive typing, one that notably resists its usual weaknesses to Dark and Bug. Uxie can use Flygon as setup fodder once it's Terastallized.

Uxie is a much-needed defensive backbone for hyper offense teams, flexing both its great bulk and capability to stallbreak against Vaporeon and Altaria. Fellow setup sweepers like Scyther, Dragon Dance Flygon, and Booster Energy Scream Tail can blow holes in teams to get Uxie in position for its own sweep. Uxie can beat physical walls like Avalugg that Scyther and Flygon struggle against, while they can break past special walls like Incineroar and Copperajah. Special setup sweepers like Scream Tail can work with Uxie to overwhelm their shared checks like Bronzong and Duraludon. As many of Uxie's answers are grounded, Klefki and other Spikes setters support it well. Alolan Ninetales can set dual screens for Uxie to give it greater windows for accumulating multiple boosts. Both Alolan Ninetales and Cinccino can create additional opportunities for Uxie to set up by using Encore on foes.

Utility.description:
Set Details

Uxie is a decent bulky pivot capable of compressing plenty of utility onto one set. As Uxie isn't an especially strong attacker, Psychic Noise is helpful to smother bulkier Pokemon with recovery moves, such as Vaporeon and Bellibolt. Knock Off punishes Pokemon that depend on their items, such as Gligar, Duraludon, and Incineroar. Uxie's ability to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from entry hazard removers like Avalugg and Altaria makes it an especially effective hazard setter. Uxie's ability to subject a foe to Encore and pivot out with U-turn makes it an especially adept support option. Thunder Wave especially annoys faster Pokemon like Scream Tail and Scyther, and it especially deters them from using Uxie as setup fodder. Heavy-Duty Boots helps to preserve Uxie's health, as it pivots out frequently and takes chip damage from Stealth Rock, while Leftovers can better benefit Uxie's longevity on teams with decent hazard control. 216 Speed EVs and a Timid nature give Uxie enough Speed to outrun Flamigo and other base 90 Speed Pokemon like Brambleghast. Tera Dark flips Uxie's Dark and Ghost weaknesses into resistances to potentially let it handle Toxicroak, Chandelure, and Basculegion-M in a pinch, and it boosts Knock Off's damage. Tera Steel has better synergy with Levitate, lets Uxie wall Flygon, and grants it a useful Toxic immunity and many resistances.

Uxie's entry hazards and pivoting are appreciated by wallbreakers like Paldean Tauros-W, Basculegion-M, and Chandelure, and they can make up for Uxie's passivity thanks to their great power. Setup sweepers like Flygon and Scyther similarly benefit from hazards, the safer positioning provided by U-turn, and Uxie's Encore and Thunder Wave creating opportunities for safer setup. Other pivots, such as Kilowattrel, Swampert, and Incineroar can form pivot cores with Uxie and catch foes in the vortex. Incineroar notably checks Dark-types and Ghost-types for Uxie, while Uxie can handle Fighting-types for it. Wish users like Vaporeon and Sylveon can supplement Uxie's otherwise lacking recovery. Dark-types are problematic for Uxie, so wallbreakers like Paldean Tauros-W, Flygon, and Nasty Plot Alolan Ninetales are welcome teammates. Dark-resistant walls like Scrafty, Sylveon, and Heracross also cover for Uxie.

Mesprit can opt not to hold an item to reduce the damage it takes from Knock Off and, thanks to Levitate, wall Golurk. However, Mesprit generally prefers having an item to increase its overall reliability.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

Nasty Plot.description:
Running a third coverage option expands the range of foes Mesprit can break through. For example, Shadow Ball can help it get past opposing Psychic-types in Galarian Slowbro and Hoopa, while Grass Knot OHKOes Rhydon and Mudsdale and smacks Milotic.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

zu.overview: Mesprit is a highly flexible Pokemon that is capable of fulfulling a multitude of roles within the ZU metagame. Its balanced stats and useful movepool allow Mesprit to work well in offensive and defensive utility roles, while its Nasty Plot set is a threatening sweeper that is extremely challenging for bulky builds to deal with. Mesprit is also a good check to Fighting-types such as Virizion and Primeape, and Levitate lets it deal with many Ground-types, such as Sandslash and Sandaconda. Unfortunately, Mesprit's balanced stats means that it isn't truly exceptional at any role that it tries to play, as its offensive stats aren't fantastic, and bulky sets are prone to getting chipped down over time. Its Psychic typing also leaves it vulnerable to common Dark-types, such as Sneasel, Spiritomb, and Skuntank, while also leaving it weak to the ubiquitous U-turn. Finally, Mesprit's coverage is quite limited, as it lacks a way to hit Steel-types hard and doesn't hit much of the metagame for super effective damage. This can lead to it sometimes struggling to break through bulky threats such as Vikavolt and Magneton.
zu.comments:
Other Options

A Choice Specs set utilizing Psychic, Dazzling Gleam, Psyshock or Shadow Ball, and either Trick or U-turn is feasible. However, Mesprit isn't powerful enough to consistently break down defensive cores without perfect prediction, it can't hit Steel-types for significant damage, and its mediocre Speed tier means it isn't especially good against offensive teams either. The Nasty Plot set can consider Psychic Noise or Stored Power as its Psychic-type STAB move. The former prevents recovery from the likes of Articuno, Naclstack, and Sandaconda, while the latter will become extremely powerful if Mesprit accrues multiple Nasty Plot boosts. However, Psyshock's ability to pressure common special walls like Naclstack and Articuno makes it the most consistent option. The defensive pivot set can consider Colbur Berry as an alternative item to take Knock Off from the likes of Primeape and Sneasel, as well as Dark-type attacks from Spiritomb. However, the loss of Leftovers recovery means that only offensive teams looking to play fast should consider this, and it loses value if Mesprit is forced to Terastallize. The defensive pivot could also use other Tera types, such as Tera Fairy to give a Dark resistance that is useful when facing down Sneasel, Spiritomb, and Primeape and Tera Water to grant useful resistances for Typhlosion and Clawitzer. Tera Water, however, leaves Mesprit open to common Grass- and Electric-type attacks from Jolteon and Virizion. Options like Thunder Wave to deter setup or and Pain Split to give Mesprit some form of recovery may seem appealing for the defensive set, but Mesprit tends to perform its role more consistently with the given moves.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types and Dark-type Coverage: Dark-types such as Sneasel, Spiritomb, and Persian-Alola threaten Mesprit with their STAB moves and either force it to switch out or Terastallize. Mesprit is capable of pivoting out or hitting them with Fairy-type coverage as they switch in, however. Pokemon that Mesprit would otherwise check, such as Primeape, Hisuian Sneasel, and Sandslash often run Dark-type coverage, limiting its ability to comfortably deal with them. Sableye and Spiritomb don't fear Mesprit's STAB moves, and Sableye can threaten to lock Mesprit into an ineffective move with Prankster Encore, though neither of them appreciate Fairy-type coverage, Knock Off, or Trick.

Ghost-types: Ghost-type attackers such as Froslass and Rotom threaten Mesprit with their STAB moves, but they can't comfortably switch in to most sets due to the threat of Knock Off, Trick, or a STAB move.

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Orthworm, Magneton, and Perrserker resist Mesprit's common coverage options, and they can use it as an opportunity to fire off a strong attack or, in Orthworm's case, set up Stealth Rock, Spikes, Coil, or Iron Defense. However, they must be wary of Trick or Knock Off. Additionally, certain Pokemon Mesprit usually checks, such as Weezing and Articuno, often run Tera Steel and can therefore turn the tables on Mesprit.

Strong Wallbreakers: Mesprit's rather modest bulk means it can't comfortably answer many of the tier's strongest offensive threats. Typhlosion and Jolteon outrun non-Choice Scarf Mesprit and threaten to do serious damage, even to the defensive set. Even slow wallbreakers such as Alolan Exeguttor and Clawitzer are still faster than the defensive pivot set and threaten it with extreme damage.

Physically Defensive Pivot.description:
Mesprit acts as a great defensive pivot thanks to its solid physical bulk with investment, as it can check physical attackers like Hisuian Sneasel and Primeape. On top of Mesprit's bulk and defensive profile enabling it to act as a reliable Stealth Rock setter, it also has good matchups against common entry hazard removers like Sandslash and Hitmontop. However, Mesprit can drop Stealth Rock to fit Healing Wish, a rare and especially good support move that helps more offensive teams. Psychic Noise is Mesprit's preferred STAB move for its secondary effect of stifling recovery from walls like Naclstack and Dipplin. U-turn is crucial for Mesprit to keep up momentum, especially against Dark-type switch-ins like Alolan Persian, Skuntank, and Sneasel. Knock Off rounds out Mesprit's moveset, compressing even more utility and punishing Dark-weak or item-reliant Pokemon like opposing Mesprit and Magneton. However, Mesprit has a handful of other utility options that it can fit over Knock Off, including Encore, which punishes setup sweepers like Shell Smash Minior, Nasty Plot Mesprit, and Iron Defense Regirock looking to break through or take advantage of Mesprit.
