If Mesprit can't afford to fit Healing Wish over Stealth Rock, then it can use Healing Wish in its last slot to compress hazard and cleric support in one slot. As Mesprit tends to not need to stick around as a defensive pivot, it often runs Rocky Helmet to push as much passive damage onto the opposing team as possible, especially against spinners like Sandslash and pivots like Basculin. 96 Speed EVs help Mesprit outspeed neutral-natured base 60 Speed Pokemon like Abomasnow as well as slower threats like Clawitzer. Mesprit can use Tera Steel for fantastic defensive synergy with Levitate on top of a great defensive typing in general to better answer Whimsicott and Dipplin and surprise physical attackers like Beartic and Lycanroc. Tera Steel has its own drawbacks, including giving Mesprit a weakness to Fighting, which worsens its matchups against Fighting-types and users of Fighting-type coverage moves, such as Virizion and Regirock, respectively. Alternatively, Mesprit can consider Tera Fairy as its Tera typing to gain useful resistances to Dark and Bug to take Knock Off and U-turn from Primeape and Poliwrath better, and this can give Mesprit critical breathing room against Sneasel to use U-turn. However, Mesprit's role as a support Pokemon means it often does not want to exhaust a resource as powerful as Terastallization unless it absolutely has to.

As a physically defensive pivot with plenty of utility options and role compression, Mesprit is capable of fitting on a variety of teams and adjusting its set for its team's needs. Bulky offense teams and balance teams alike enjoy Mesprit's capabilities of acting as a midground against physical attackers and bringing in its more offensive teammates with U-turn. Wallbreakers like Hisuian Sneasel, Clawitzer, and Choice Specs Whimsicott enjoy the free entry provided by Mesprit, and the last two create pivot cores with Mesprit. Other pivots like Basculin, Jolteon, and Primape make great cores with Mesprit for their combined ability to keep up momentum. Sandslash is a standout partner with Mesprit, as the two can compress plenty of utility moves between the two of them; Mesprit can run Stealth Rock to free Sandslash up to run coverage moves or Spikes, while Sandslash has Knock Off to free up Mesprit to run Encore or Healing Wish. Healing Wish variants are appreciated by Pokemon that lack recovery or tend to rely on Rest, including Regirock, Sandslash, and Perrserker. Basculin often wears itself down with recoil damage from Wave Crash on top of repeatedly taking damage from entry hazards as an offensive pivot, and Mesprit can relieve it from KOing itself thanks to Healing Wish. Healing Wish is also much appreciated by setup sweepers, as it gives them a free switch in and often allows bulkier sweepers like Spiritomb a second chance at winning. Mesprit can't do much against Steel-types like Perrserker and Orthworm on its own, so it depends on Fighting-type teammates like Hisuian Sneasel, Primeape, and Virizion in its stead. Conveniently, these Fighting-types also match up well against Dark-types, such as Alolan Persian and Sneasel, that would threaten Mesprit. Teammates like Whimsicott, Sneasel, and Houndoom can help manage Mesprit's problematic matchups against Spiritomb and Sableye.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Mesprit is a great revenge killer to handle fast Pokemon like Jolteon and Hisuian Sneasel. Dazzling Gleam is Mesprit's best complementary coverage move for Psychic, covering Dark-types like Sneasel and Sableye. U-turn lets Mesprit keep up offensive momentum against switch-ins like Orthworm, Farigiraf, and Skuntank. Healing Wish lets Mesprit give teammates like Virizion, Jolteon, and Toxicroak a second chance to set up and sweep. Mesprit can alternatively use Trick to make a defensive Pokemon like Cryogonal or Orthworm less threatening. Tera Fairy Mesprit is a more effective offensive and defensive answer to Sneasel and Primeape given their Dark-type coverage moves, and Tera Fairy lets Mesprit not play guessing games with Psychic and Dazzling Gleam against Tera Dark Primeape. Tera Steel has good synergy with Levitate and gives Mesprit several new resistances to more easily answer Whimsicott, Sandslash, and Farigiraf.

Offensive pivots like Jolteon and Magneton make great cores with Mesprit and appreciate Mesprit's Levitate to more easily play around Ground-types. Fighting-types like Virizion, Primeape, and Hitmontop are great offensive checks to Steel-types like Orthworm and Perrserker, which give Mesprit trouble, and they appreciate Mesprit offensively checking Poison-types like Weezing and Hisuian Sneasel. Mesprit benefits from Ground-type teammates like Sandslash and Sandaconda patching up its poor matchup against Sneasel-Hisui, while it can check foes like Virizion for them. Setup sweepers like Primeape, Regirock, and Virizion benefit from Mesprit providing them second chances to sweep with Healing Wish or making foes more exploitable with Trick. Physical wallbreakers like Beartic and Hisuian Sneasel all benefit from Healing Wish giving them an additional chance for breaking, as they can break special walls that Mesprit cannot.

Nasty Plot Sweeper.description:
Nasty Plot Mesprit is a fearsome mid- or late-game sweeper thanks to the combination of Levitate and a somewhat high base 105 Special Attack stat. Its biggest perk is the ability to set up in front of most bulkier Pokémon. Mesprit can choose between Encore and Substitute as its setup tool; Substitute can be very good versus bulkier teams, as Mesprit can tank a hit from most of the passive mons such as Regirock and Orthworm if not being hit super effectively, obtaining a free turn to either set up Nasty Plot or fire off an attack. Encore helps to circumvent Mesprit's passivity and can take advantage of checks that need to set up or use status moves like Haze to wall Mesprit, like Articuno for the Haze case, and Regirock for the setup. Psyshock is great to deal with specially defensive Pokémon such as Naclstack. Draining Kiss allows Mesprit to outlast Dark-type checks such as Spiritomb and Sneasel while healing in the process, Thunderbolt allows it to hit Water-types such as Clawitzer hard. Tera Fairy lets Mesprit set up in front of the aforementioned Dark-types, grants immunity to Dragon Tail from Dipplin and Appletun, and increases the power of Draining Kiss, letting Mesprit restore more HP on the aforementioned threats and making it even harder to take down. Tera Steel improves Mesprit's defensive capabilities, making it take neutral damage from Dark- and Ghost-type attacks and giving it a Bug resistance, while only being weak to Fighting- and Fire-type moves due to Levitate. Tera Electric boosts the power of Thunderbolt and removes all of Mesprit's weaknesses.

Nasty Plot Sweeper Mesprit works well with specific entry hazard setters and Fighting-types. Hazard setters like Orthworm and Naclstack both cover each other's weaknesses and let Mesprit get rolls it wouldn't otherwise, such as KOing Honchkrow with Tera Fairy Draining Kiss after Stealth Rock chip damage. Fighting-types such as Virizion and Primeape deserve a highlight, as when paired with Mesprit, they provide good coverage for it, pressuring Dark- and Steel-types with their STAB moves and Ghost-types with Knock Off. Both of them offer additional utility, with Virizion being bulky enough to enter in and provide wallbreaking prowess and Primeape having access to U-turn to let Mesprit in safely and Knock Off to offer utility. Secondary wallbreakers that don't rely on Setup to make progress such as Clawitzer and Magneton will also appreciate being by Mesprit's side. Some cleaners also enjoy Mesprit's ability to make progress so they can clean late-game, such as Dodrio and Hisuian Sneasel.

Specially Defensive Pivot.description:
Mesprit's decent defensive profile and access to useful utility moves like Stealth Rock and Healing Wish allow it to act as a good defensive pivot. Its bulk and typing allows it to check foes such as Jolteon, Pyroar, and Passimian locked into Close Combat. Psychic Noise is a useful STAB move that allows Mesprit to force out Hitmonchan and Hitmontop, which are among the few viable hazard removers of the tier. Its decent Base Power and ability to prevent healing allow Mesprit to annoy other defensive Pokemon like Dipplin and Sandaconda. U-turn allows Mesprit to pivot out of poor matchups such as Skuntank and Spiritomb while keeping up momentum for its team. Knock Off allows Mesprit to punish foes that would feel comfortable coming in otherwise, such as Orthworm, Articuno, and Skuntank. Healing Wish is another option for offensive teams that allows Mesprit to fully heal an offensive teammate and give it another go at breaking down the opponent's team. It is capable of running both Knock Off and Healing Wish if your team already has another Stealth Rock user. Maximum Special Defense investment is preferred in order to better take hits from the likes of Magneton and Pyroar. A Sassy nature is preferred to give Mesprit a slow U-turn and maximize the damage that its physical attacks do. Steel is the preferred Tera type, as it turns each of Mesprit's weaknesses into a neutrality or a resistance and gives it a superb general defensive typing. It notably lets Mesprit handle opposing Mesprit and Whimsicott with more confidence. Tera Steel also has good synergy with Levitate and allows Mesprit to comfortably handle foes such as Sandslash and Sandaconda. Leftovers grants Mesprit passive recovery and helps it stay as healthy as possible throughout the match.

Mesprit is one of the few bulky Stealth Rock setters in the tier that also has access to a pivoting move, which makes it highly useful for both balance and offense. Mesprit lacks reliable recovery, so teams utilizing it shouldn't expect it to be a stalwart wall. Rather, its good support movepool and defensive traits allow it to act as a stopgap that can take a few hits while also supporting its offensively oriented teammates via pivoting and utility moves such as Knock Off and Healing Wish. Mesprit's physical bulk is somewhat lacking, so physically defensive teammates such as Weezing and Sandaconda, make for good partners. These two help out against Fighting-types such as Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel, which Mesprit struggles to check in the long term. Dipplin serves as a good physically defensive partner and in particular a Knock Off absorber, which is highly useful for Mesprit because it fears Knock Off greatly. Mesprit is also vulnerable to Dark-types such as Spiritomb and Sneasel. Teammates such as Hisuian Sneasel and Virizion can help with the latter, while Articuno and Whimsicott can help with the former. Teammates such as Primeape, Virizion, and Typhlosion can help check Steel-types such as Magneton and Orthworm, which Mesprit struggles to deal with on its own. Strong wallbreakers, such as Typhlosion, Clawitzer, and Alolan Exeggutor, appreciate Mesprit's slow U-turn getting them in safely, and they benefit from Mesprit's ability to use Knock Off to remove various items from defensive Pokemon such as Regirock, Orthworm, and Articuno. Mesprit also pairs well with other VoltTurn users; Primeape and Whimsicott also benefit from Mesprit bringing them in safely and can form a pivoting core that can slowly wear down the opponent's team. Pokemon such as Typhlosion and Toxicroak appreciate Healing Wish support should Mesprit choose to run it, as they are all vulnerable to being worn down over the course of a match, and many teams are not prepared to deal with them a second time.

Choice Specs.description:
• Dialga's unique typing and good offensive stats give it a niche as a strong wallbreaker that is also able to soft check Pokemon such as Primal Kyogre, Eternatus, Palkia-O, and utility Arceus formes. However, its middling Speed and weakness to common Ground-types such as Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground mean Dialga can struggle to get into a game safely, especially without reliable recovery; it also faces heavy competition from Eternatus and Palkia-O as a powerful attacker in bulky offense and balance teams alike.
  • Trick allows Dialga to cripple switch-ins such as Ho-Oh, Zygarde, Ferrothorn, and Chansey, allowing its teammates to break through the opposing team much more easily.
  • Draco Meteor is Dialga's strongest attack, being able to 2HKO defensive Primal Groudon, offensive Primal Kyogre, and utility Arceus formes and OHKO offensive Primal Groudon, Zygarde-C, and specially offensive Yveltal.
  • Fire Blast allows Dialga to OHKO Zacian-C on the switch and 2HKO defensive Necrozma-DM, preventing the latter from being a reliable switch-in.
  • Thunder hits defensive Primal Kyogre, Arceus-Water, and Ho-Oh for great damage while preventing Arceus-Fairy or Zacian-C from switching in reliably, unlike Draco Meteor. Flash Cannon prevents Fairy-types from walling Dialga, being able to OHKO Arceus-Fairy after Stealth Rock, thus preventing Dialga from being setup fodder for it while also being able to break through Tera Fairy Eternatus and Zygarde variants; however, it is generally less desirable, since it lets Ho-Oh come into Dialga more often.
  • The given EV spread avoids the 2HKO from Tera Normal Extreme Speed from Arceus and Arceus-Fairy's uninvested Judgment while always outspeeding Adamant Necrozma-DM.
  • Tera Dragon not only removes Dialga's weakness to Ground- and Fighting-type attacks but also pushes Draco Meteor's damage to new heights, being able to OHKO Extreme Killer Arceus, utility Arceus formes, and defensive Yveltal while also being able to 2HKO defensive Primal Kyogre and offensive Necrozma-DM.
  • Dialga is quite prediction reliant, so spamming Draco Meteor is heavily discouraged, as it can turn Dialga into setup fodder, especially if there are Steel- or Fairy-types on the opposing team. Double switching against predicted switch-ins such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM into checks such as Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh can maintain the team's momentum while keeping the pressure Dialga brings on defensive backbones. Using Trick can also be somewhat difficult, since Arceus formes barring Extreme Killer, Zacian-C, and Z-Move Necrozma-DM can stop it. Therefore, Trick should mostly be used against more passive and slower teams, such as stall, against Pokemon Dialga would typically come in on like defensive Yveltal, defensive Eternatus, Ferrothorn, and Alomomola.
  • Dialga typically fits on balance and bulky offense structures that appreciate its offensive and defensive capabilities while not worrying about its mediocre Speed tier. It appreciates teammates that can setup entry hazards so it can reach important damage thresholds such as OHKOing Arceus-Fairy after Stealth Rock with Flash Cannon. Teammates such as Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and utility Arceus formes are good for this; the former also appreciates Dialga briefly checking Primal Kyogre for it. Ground-type switch-ins such as Giratina-O, Ho-Oh, and Yveltal are great partners to handle Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground, with all three also being good switch-ins to Marshadow, which can threaten Dialga with Low Kick. Zygarde is also a good switch-in to Marshadow and Primal Groudon while offering Glare support to help Dialga handle faster threats such as Zacian-C or Palkia-O.
  • Strong special attackers such as Primal Kyogre, Eternatus, and Calm Mind Arceus formes like Dialga crippling special walls like Ho-Oh or Chansey so they can clear through teams much more easily. Strong physical attackers such as Primal Groudon, Marshadow, and Zacian-C also appreciate Dialga smashing through physical walls like Zygarde, Primal Groudon, Arceus-Dark, and Dondozo, while they can help overwhelm the defensive backbone of many balance teams.

Wallbreaker.description:
• Palkia-O uses its powerful Water / Dragon STAB combination, further bolstered by Lustrous Globe, its high Special Attack, supplemented with Fire-type coverage, to become a nuclear wallbreaker that excels at eviscerating the defensive backbone of many balance teams. Palkia-O is capable of 2HKOing defensive stalwarts such as Ho-Oh, Primal Groudon, Eternatus, and support Arceus formes.
  • Fire Blast roasts Ferrothorn while also hitting Tera Grass Ho-Oh for slightly more damage than Spacial Rend.
  • Palkia-O's last moveslot is rather flexible. Substitute takes advantage of the many switches Palkia-O forces and protects it from status moves. Alternatively, Draco Meteor enables Palkia-O to nab some OHKOs on Pokemon that Spacial Rend cannot, such as defensive Eternatus, Zygarde-C, and Eruption Primal Groudon after Stealth Rock.
  • A Modest nature is preferred to enhance Palkia-O's wallbreaking capabilities. A Timid nature is usable if outspeeding Adamant Ultra Necrozma and Speed tying Calm Mind Arceus formes is desired. However, running a Timid nature comes at the cost of never OHKOing defensive Eternatus, turning defensive Primal Groudon into a roll to 2HKO, and rarely 2HKOing Primal Kyogre with Spacial Rend.
  • Tera Water is used over Tera Dragon, since Primal Groudon is 2HKOed by Spacial Rend regardless. Tera Water Hydro Pump is capable of OHKOing Ho-Oh, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM after a single layer of Spikes, and support Arceus formes after Stealth Rock and a layer of Spikes.
  • Palkia-O is best used as an early- or mid-game wallbreaker on balance and bulky offense teams to tear through the defensive backbone of balance teams. It struggles against hyper offense teams, as it can be outsped or set up on, limiting the damage it can do. Against these teams, Palkia-O is often limited to trading. Additionally, Palkia-O completely thuds into stall, as it is fully walled by Chansey.
  • Choice Band Marshadow is an excellent teammate, as it is able to revenge kill many Pokemon that use Palkia-O as setup fodder on hyper offense teams, such as Ultra Necrozma, Deoxys-A, Arceus, and Zacian-C.
  • Ho-Oh makes an excellent partner, as it is able to switch in on Pokemon that scare Palkia-O out, such as Arceus-Fairy, Deoxys-A, and Zacian-C. Furthermore, Palkia-O greatly appreciates Defog support from Ho-Oh due to its vulnerability to every entry hazard and lack of recovery.
  • Palkia-O also appreciates teammates that match up well into stall, such as specially offensive Yveltal and Overheat Primal Groudon.

Nasty Plot.description: Palkia-O is a strong setup sweeper that has an unremovable item and a strong matchup against the likes of Arceus-Ground and Ho-Oh. Speed Boost denies offensive counterplay from Pokemon like Ash-Greninja and Flutter Mane, and it prevents slow pivots like Teleport Blissey from forcing Palkia-O out via switching to Imposter users. Magic Guard can exploit defensive Pokemon that rely on status moves to deal damage, lets Palkia-O sit on common Knock Off users, and helps keep Dragon Energy's power high. Jungle Healing provides some recovery and removes debilitating status conditions like paralysis, but Strength Sap can provide much greater amount of healing. Pokemon like Ultra Necrozma and Mega Gardevoir appreciate Palkia-O beating Ho-Oh and Arceus-Ground, and they can help it beat checks like Mega Audino and Blissey in return. Speed Boost Palkia-O essentially ceases to function if statused, so a status absorber like a Take Heart Arceus forme can help. Teammates such as Blissey that can take on faster attackers like Eternatus and Flutter Mane are also greatly appreciated by Magic Guard variants. Imposter-proof Palkia-O with Ice Scales Mega Audino, Arceus-Fairy, or Imposter Chansey.

Offensive.description:
Earth Power hits Fire-resistant foes such as Skeledirge and opposing Flash Fire Heatran. Solar Beam with Sun present allows Heatran to hit Water-types such as Slowking and Rotom-W that would normally wall it, but Dark Pulse is another option that hits Latios and doesn't rely on sun being up, improving Heatran's matchup against Chilly Reception Slowking. Taunt allows Heatran to stop recovery attempts from Pokemon such as Skeledirge and Gastrodon. Stealth Rock is another option, as Heatran has a good matchup versus entry hazard removers such as Excadrill as long as Air Balloon is intact. On Hyper Offense teams, Heatran can run this alongside Taunt to dominate the early hazard game. Flash Fire gives Heatran a power boost if it is able to switch into Skeledirge or opposing Heatran's Fire-type attacks, meaning even Fire-resistant targets such as Rotom-W can struggle to take Magma Storm. Air Balloon gives Heatran a one-time switch-in opportunity against Ground-types such as Excadrill and Gastrodon, allowing Heatran to hit them for massive damage without fearing retaliation while also walling opposing Heatran's attacks. Power Herb lets Heatran potentially lure in Slowking and KO it with Solar Beam when sun is no longer up. A Modest nature allows Heatran to 2HKO Skeledirge with Earth Power and possibly 2HKO Assault Vest Tornadus-T with Magma Storm. A Timid nature allows Heatran to outspeed the likes of utility Excadrill and Slither Wing. Tera Ghost lets Heatran take Close Combats from the likes of Slither Wing, Cobalion, and Galarian Zapdos. However, Heatran does lose its Dragon resistance, making Pokemon such as Latios and Hydreigon much more difficult to answer while also becoming weak to Dark-types moves from foes such as Lokix and Zarude that it would normally answer.

Heatran fits best on hyper offense teams, particularly sun teams; these teams appreciate its ability to check Pokemon such as Tornadus-T and Skeledirge they might struggle with while applying massive offensive pressure. Ninetales is a great partner for Heatran, as it can set sun to remove Solar Beam's charge turn and boost the power of Magma Storm, making even Fire-resistant foes such as Hydreigon wary of switching into Heatran. Venusaur and Hisuian Lilligant can switch into Ground-types such as Excadrill and Clodsire that Heatran may struggle to beat if its Air Balloon is popped, while Heatran is able to threaten Pokemon such as Skeledirge and Revavroom that these Chlorophyll users may struggle to OHKO. Pokemon that can threaten Water-types, such as Ogerpon-C and Thundurus-T, are heavily appreciated by Heatran, as they can help against Pokemon such as Slowking and Gastrodon that Heatran may struggle to break. This is especially useful against Slowking, as it can deny Sun with Chilly Reception. Sets that lack Dark Pulse are heavily walled by Latios, as it can switch into any one of Heatran's attacks and launch a powerful Aura Sphere or Surf. Therefore, Pokemon such as Greninja that can help take on Latios pair well with Heatran.

Heatran is a fearsome wallbreaker capable of easily shutting down defensive teams, leveraging its defensive profile to find multiple opportunities to switch in and wreak havoc. Magma Storm is a powerful Fire-type STAB move that can trap Pokemon like Blissey and Toxapex. Earth Power allows Heatran to hit Fire-types that would otherwise resist Magma Storm such as Iron Moth, Skeledirge, and opposing Leftovers Heatran. Taunt completely shuts down recovery from defensive Pokemon that would otherwise withstand its offensive assault such as Galarian Slowking and Blissey, and it allows Heatran to beat each of these Pokemon 1-on-1 in tandem with Magma Storm. Stealth Rock can be considered in the last slot, as Heatran's consistency in forcing switches can give it a free turn to set up Stealth Rock; however, Will-O-Wisp can be used to hinder switch-ins such as Dragonite and Ting-Lu that would otherwise freely switch in against Heatran. A Timid nature lets Heatran outspeed and threaten Choice Band Rillaboom, in addition to quickly burning Adamant Dragonite with Will-O-Wisp, though a Modest nature could be considered to guarantee an OHKO on bulky Kingambit variants. Tera Grass flips Heatran's matchup against Water- and Ground-types such as Hisuian Samurott and Landorus-T and synergizes very well with Flash Fire; Tera Ghost grants Heatran a crucial Fighting immunity that can help against Zamazenta, in addition to blocking Rapid Spin from the likes of Great Tusk and Iron Treads. Leftovers provides Heatran with passive recovery and allows it to stick around over the course of the match; Air Balloon could also be used to provide Heatran with a temporary Ground immunity, letting it safely switch into Landorus-T and opposing Heatran.

Heatran fits primarily on offense and bulky offense teams where it excels in ripping apart defensive cores for its teammates to exploit. Special sweepers such as Primarina and Raging Bolt greatly enjoy Heatran trapping and removing their checks, particularly Blissey. In return, Primarina discourages Ground-type switch-ins such as Landorus-T and Ting-Lu, while Raging Bolt can force out Water-types like Barraskewda and Hisuian Samurott. Rillaboom is another fantastic teammate for Heatran that not only provides it with extra passive recovery and more resistance against Earthquake but can form a formidable offensive core with it, with Rillaboom capable of handling Ground- and Water-types such as Great Tusk and Ogerpon-W and Heatran taking advantage of Rillaboom's switch-ins like Corviknight and Skeledirge, alongside setting Stealth Rock to spread chip damage for both itself and Rillaboom. Additionally, some of Rillaboom's teammates like Hawlucha and Hatterene appreciate Heatran removing their checks via Magma Storm, allowing them to more easily sweep late-game, while both Pokemon can force out Ground- and Fighting-types like Great Tusk and Zamazenta. Lastly, Heatran enjoys Rapid Spin support from Great Tusk removing entry hazards that cut into its longevity, and it also enjoys having a check to Dragonite. In exchange, Heatran can easily switch in on and threaten Pokemon such as Meowscarada, Weavile, and Calm Mind Iron Valiant that Great Tusk struggles against.

Specially Defensive.description:
Specially defensive Heatran is a useful glue Pokemon that can stallbreak, set entry hazards, spread status, and check notable special attackers like Gholdengo, Hatterene, and Galarian Slowking. Magma Storm in conjunction with Taunt lets Heatran one-on-one walls like Galarian Slowking, Blissey, and Toxapex, trapping and preventing them from pivoting and healing in the process. Lava Plume gives it a more reliable STAB move that can cripple checks and would-be switchins like Ting-Lu, Ogerpon-W, Dragonite, and Hisuian Samurott. Earth Power is a much-needed coverage move to hit Pokemon like Iron Moth, Glimmora, Raging Bolt, Toxapex, and opposing Heatran super effectively. Taunt has the added benefit of preventing setup from both slower hazard setters like Clefable and Ting-Lu and slower setup sweepers like Terastallized Kingambit and Primarina. Stealth Rock is an extremely good fit since Heatran threatens common forms of hazard removal like Corviknight and prevents Great Tusk and Iron Treads from switching. It is also able to punish Hatterene from switching in to deflect Stealth Rock back with Magic Bounce since it is unable to hit Heatran back for any notable damage. If there's another Stealth Rock setter on the team, Will-O-Wisp can be used as a way to spread burns, particularly on sets that forgo Lava Plume, and it most notably lets Heatran neutralize Kingambit safely by bypassing its Sucker Punch. Will-O-Wisp also pairs with Magma Storm quite nicely by stacking up further chip damage. 40 Speed EVs allow Heatran to outspeed Adamant Kingambit so it can secure a Magma Storm or Will-O-Wisp on it before it can retaliate. 4 Defense EVs guarantees Heatran will live an Earthquake from Clodsire. Leftovers gives Heatran much-needed longevity, but Air Balloon is also a good choice to allow Heatran to come in on Ground-types such as Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Clodsire, especially as they might not have the move to pop the item; makes Heatran immune to Spikes, allowing it to come in much more safely against hazard stacking teams; lets Heatran emergency check Dragonite, non-Close Combat Great Tusk, Kyurem, and Enamorus. Flash Fire gives Heatran a Fire-type immunity to check Iron Moth and Cinderace and letting it better handle even the occasional Fire coverage from Dragonite, Kyurem, and, with Air Balloon, Enamorus and its Earth Power. Flame Body threatens burns against contact attackers such as Weavile, Meowscarada, and Rillaboom. Tera Grass allows Heatran to remove its weaknesses to Water- and Ground-type attacks so it can wall Water-types like Dondozo and Ogerpon-W and Ground-types like Clodsire, Ting-Lu, and Gliscor. Tera Grass also works well with Flash Fire to mitigate its newfound Fire weakness. Tera Ghost is used to remove its weakness to Fighting-type attacks so it can wall Zamazenta, particulary punshing if it runs Flame Body. Tera Ghost also gives it a Normal immunity, preventing Great Tusk from using Rapid Spin on it to remove its Stealth Rock and, if paired with Air Balloon, outright walling Dragonite if its only attacks are Extreme Speed and Earthquake or Fire Punch. Tera Fairy is also worth mentioning as a niche option to check physical attackers like Zamazenta without the Dark weakness from foes like Meowscarada and Hisuian Samurott.

Heatran is best used on Grassy Terrain bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to check Fire-types while also being a great progress maker itself. Rillaboom is by far its best teammate, as they both have near-perfect synergy with each other; Rillaboom's Grassy Terrain not only provides additional recovery for it on top of Leftovers, it also weakens Earthquake from common Ground-types like Gliscor and Landorus-T. Rillaboom itself also threatens the Water- and Ground-types that constantly give Heatran trouble, like Gliscor, Alomomola, and Ogerpon-W, and brings in Heatran safely on its checks like Skarmory and Corviknight with U-turn. In return, Heatran is able to check Fire-types Rillaboom doesn't want to face, like Skeledirge and opposing Heatran. Great Tusk is another stellar teammate since Heatran is extremely weak to entry hazards, so its hazard removal support is much appreciated. Hatterene is a teammate that can prevent hazards from being set up altogether thanks to Magic Bounce and wall Gliscor in Grassy Terrain, which is super useful since Heatran often struggles to check numerous threats consistently when Spikes are on the field. Grassy Terrain sweepers like Hawlucha, Ogerpon-W, and Raging Bolt love Heatran's ability to wear down bulkier Pokemon like Skeledirge, Galarian Slowking, Dondozo, and Ting-Lu so they can clean up late-game. On bulkier teams, Alomomola is a fitting teammate for it since its Wish support allows Heatran to stay alive for a prolonged period of time, and its typing checks common physical Water-types like Barraskewda and Hisuian Samurott. Spikers like Hisuian Samurott, Gliscor, and Ting-Lu all work well with Heatran since they have good synergy typing-wise and their Spikes increases the potency of Magma Storm + Will-O-Wisp pressure. They can also form a hazard stacking core together with Stealth Rock Heatran.

Offensive.description: • The given EV spread allows Heatran to outspeed Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane during Tailwind while maximizing its Special Attack, allocating the remaining EVs into HP.

Specially Defensive.description:
Heatran's well-rounded stats, great typing, and unique ability allow it to be one of the best specially defensive Pokemon in the tier, capable of sponging hits from Volcarona, Tapu Lele, and Tapu Koko. Earth Power hits Fire-resistant foes such as opposing Heatran, Toxapex, and Raging Bolt. Toxic is useful to wear down Pokemon such as Ting-Lu and Alomomola, preventing them from reliably switching in. Heatran also functions as a consistent Stealth Rock user, threatening foes with entry hazard removal such as Terapagos lacking Earth Power and Tornadus-T. If Stealth Rock is already being used by another teammate, Taunt can be used to shut down defensive Pokemon like Toxapex and Galarian Slowking allowing Heatran to trap them more effectively. Taunt also prevents Substitute Volcarona and Calm Mind Raging Bolt from spiraling out of control. Protect both enables more passive damage from Magma Storm and Toxic to build up and grants Heatran additional healing from Leftovers, as well as allowing Heatran to scout common Choice item users such as Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant. 40 Speed EVs allow Heatran to outspeed Adamant Kingambit and Mega Mawile.

Heatran is easily removed by Ground- and Water-type Pokemon such as Landorus-T, Urshifu-R, and Gliscor, meaning teammates that can handle these threats, such as Mega Latios, Zapdos, and Rillaboom, are greatly appreciated. Rillaboom in particular is good, since the Grassy Terrain it sets provides Heatran with another source of passive healing, which can greatly assist in Heatran's longevity to check foes like Raging Bolt and Mega Latios for teammates like Toxapex and Great Tusk. Heatran's offensive pressure is helpful for wearing down threats like Raging Bolt and Toxapex for teammates like Tapu Koko and Mega Lopunny. In return, Tapu Koko can handle Water-types like Hisuian Samurott and Alomomola.

Offensive.description:
Offensive Heatran serves as an effective wallbreaker with its powerful Magma Storm and Z-Moves while also functioning as a reliable Stealth Rock setter, pressuring common entry hazard control like Tornadus-T and Terapagos. Earth Power grants key coverage against opposing Fire-resistant foes like Toxapex, Mega Diancie, and opposing Heatran. Grassium Z with Solar Beam is the main combination, as it allows Heatran to lure and OHKO Water-types such as Alomomola, Slowbro, and Mega Swampert while also dealing a good amount of damage to Mega Tyranitar and Garchomp. Alternatively, Toxic cripples threats like Ting-Lu, Mega Latios, and Mega Charizard Y, while Hidden Power Ice threatens Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Garchomp. Taunt stops walls such as Galarian Slowking and Toxapex from pivoting out or using a recovery move, letting Heatran overwhelm them with Magma Storm's chip damage. Heatran can also use Firium Z to hit foes with a powerful Inferno Overdrive, which OHKOes most Landorus-T sets. However, without the combination of Solar Beam + Grassium Z, Heatran won't break past the Water-types mentioned above. Air Balloon is another option, granting Heatran an immunity to Ground-type attacks like Landorus-T's Earthquake, Mega Charizard Y's Scorching Sands, and Mega Diancie's Earth Power, letting it beat or force out Ground-types 1-on-1 when paired with Hidden Power Ice. Air Balloon also helps Heatran against opposing Heatran by avoiding Earth Power and threatening it back with its own Earth Power. Modest nature allows Heatran to OHKO defensive Landorus-T with Inferno Overdrive, while Timid nature helps Heatran outrun Raging Bolt.

Heatran fits best on bulky offense and balance teams, where its ability to trap and remove problematic walls shines the most. Volcarona and Raging Bolt are teammates that appreciate this ability, as they both benefit from Heatran trapping and removing walls like Toxapex and Galarian Slowking. Offensive Pokemon like Kingambit, Tapu Lele, and Mega Diancie benefit from Heatran's ability to pressure opposing Steel-types like Melmetal, Ferrothorn, and Gholdengo, and they also appreciate its access to Stealth Rock. Due to its weakness to Ground-type attacks, teammates like Landorus-T, Zapdos, and Tornadus-T are appreciated. Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Urshifu-R, and Rillaboom are great partners thanks to their ability to threaten opposing Ground-type Pokemon, such as Ting-Lu and Great Tusk, for Heatran. Rillaboom, in particular, provides Grassy Terrain support that offers passive healing, something Z sets lack, for improved longevity. Despite the combination of Grassium Z and Solar Beam, Heatran is generally weak against Water-type foes like Slowbro, Alomomola, and Ogerpon-W; therefore, Pokemon that can handle them, such as Tapu Koko, Raging Bolt, and Ferrothorn, are great partners. Heatran also likes partners that can switch into Fighting-types, like Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, and Mega Lopunny, that threaten Heatran with an OHKO; these include Pokemon like Landorus-T, Gholdengo, and Zapdos. Teammates that carry entry hazards removal, like Gliscor and Terapagos, are solid teammates for Heatran due to its vulnerability to entry hazards and complete lack of recovery without Leftovers. Although Heatran is a solid check to offensive Pokemon like Volcarona and Tapu Lele, its lack of recovery doesn't allow it to repeatedly switch into their attacks. Therefore, defensive Pokemon that check these threats, such as Toxapex and Gholdengo, are solid partners.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Fire

Leftovers can be used over Air Balloon if Talonflame or Air Balloon Volcanion are already on the team and feel sufficient as Ground-immune Pokemon, and if the user would prefer longevity on Heatran. Stealth Rock can be changed to Taunt if the user feels uncomfortable running a Stealth Rock setter along with Court Change Cinderace or has opted for Torkoal or Hisuian Arcanine as their Stealth Rock user. Flame Body is a possible option instead of Flash Fire on Heatran varients that opt to drop Air Balloon, as checking Gouging Fire is no longer possible. It can be used to burn and punish threats like Kingambit, Azumarill, and Sneasler in a pinch.

Steel

Heavy Slam can be used to handily deal with Flutter Mane and Clefable. Running Ability Shield can be an option to check Ogerpon-H, but it gives up Heatran's passive recovery. Substitute can be used over Heatran's other utility option, making the mirror much rougher for opposing Steel teams, along with enabling it to more reliably fish for Lava Plume burns.

Steel (Choice Scarf)

Heavy Slam is an alternative option to target Flutter Mane's lower Defense stat.

Choice Scarf (Steel).description:
Choice Scarf Heatran is a solid option for Steel teams, as it is able to provide offensive pressure while still having a minor defensive role thanks to Flash Fire. Fire Blast torches Iron Treads and Corviknight, while 2HKOing physically defensive Gliscor even after Poison Heal recovery. Flamethrower is an option for more PP and better accuracy but with a bit of a power tradeoff. Flash Cannon is an excellent move to hit Fairy-types such as Hatterene, non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, and Flutter mane, which has a 50% chance to get OHKO'd after Stealth Rock. Dragon Pulse is an alternative option for teams that already have an abundance of Steel-type coverage and is useful for 2HKOing Latios and Dragapult. Earth Power is a great option for hitting Pokemon such as Toxapex, Raging Bolt, and Iron Moth. Power Gem is a fantastic way to punish opposing Fire-types that would hope to switch in on a Fire-type move, such as Moltres and opposing Air Balloon Heatran, and it is a Steel team's best way of dealing with Volcarona.

Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra are both superb teammates, forming a great defensive core with Heatran that is hard to break through. Archaludon can support Heatran by using Stealth Rock to chip Pokemon that might want to switch in on Heatran, such as Tornadus-T and Gliscor, and slow down foes that outspeed Heatran, such as Dragapult and Choice Scarf Greninja with Thunder Wave. Hisuian Goodra is a fantastic special wall with excellent longevity, allowing Heatran to opt for a more offensive role. Hisuian Goodra can use Knock Off to remove items from defensive Pokemon that would like to switch in on Heatran, such as recovery items from Toxapex, Clodsire, and Ting-Lu. Skarmory is another great teammate, as it can switch into Ground- and Fighting-type moves and punish foes that use contact moves, such as Close Combat from Great Tusk and Sneasler. Skarmory can also use Spikes to weaken foes, making it so that Heatran has an easier time cleaning up at the end of games, and use Body Press to weaken opposing special walls such as Blissey and Alolan Muk, that Heatran may struggle with. Air Balloon Iron Treads has a temporary to Ground, as well as providing Knock Off support and clearing entry hazards so that Heatran can come in safely. Iron Treads is also able to beat non-Choice Scarf Landorus with Ice Spinner. Gholdengo is another teammate capable of providing Thunder Wave support,and it blocks Defog, ensuring opponents can't remove hazards. Corviknight is also immune to Ground and a great slow pivot option to help Heatran get in easier.

Bulky Heatran (Steel).description:
With a bulkier spread, Heatran can hold the line reliably against attempts to break Steel teams from threats such as Choice Specs Dragapult and Iron Moth. Magma Storm eliminates Steel-types such as Skarmory and Scizor while also enabling Heatran to trap and deal chip damage to threats like Toxapex and Hisuian Goodra. Alternatively, Lava Plume can be used to fish for burns, and for its superior accuracy. Earth Power handles Steel-types capable of handling Heatran's Fire-type moves such as opposing Heatran and Hisuian Goodra along with dealing with Poison- and Electric-types like Galarian Slowking and Raging Bolt. Power Gem nails Volcarona and Air Balloon Heatran on the switch along with hitting Flying-types such as Moltres and Zapdos. Protect can allow Heatran to scout against Choice-locked threats like Greninja and Iron Moth. Alternatively, Stealth Rock can be used to set entry hazards, freeing up moveslots from teammates like Archaludon, while Will-O-Wisp can punish physical attackers attempting to switch into Heatran such as Hisuian Samurott. The given EV Spread enables Heatran to outspeed Modest Magnezone and survive a +2 Ceruledge Poltergeist from full HP while putting the rest into its Special Defense. The alternative EV Spread maximizes Heatran's special bulk, preventing Choice Specs Spectrier from 2HKOing it.

Heatran can form an immunity core for Steel teams when paired with Skarmory and Gholdengo, with Heatran providing a Fire immunity that both appreciate. In return, Skarmory provides a Ground immunity and physical wall capable of handling threats like Excadrill and Hisuian Samurott, while Gholdengo provides a Fighting immunity, allowing it to easily check Fighting-types such as Sneasler and Iron Valiant. Together they also make a strong entry hazard-stacking core with Heatran providing Stealth Rock, Skarmory providing Spikes, and Gholdengo being able to block removal attempts from Forretress and Corviknight. Archaludon can handle Water-types like Ogerpon-W and Barraskewda along with physical Fire-types such as Ogerpon-H and Cinderace that can handle Heatran, while Choice Scarf sets are able to outspeed and check foes like Walking Wake with Draco Meteor and Urshifu-R with Thunderbolt. Air Balloon Iron Treads can handle Electric-types like Sandy Shocks and Raging Bolt while also being able to use Ice Spinner to check Gliscor and Landorus. Hisuian Goodra provides a sturdier special wall capable of handling special threats that can threaten to overwhelm Heatran like Choice Specs Greninja, Darkrai, and Walking Wake while appreciating Heatran checking Iron Moth and Volcarona. Swords Dance Scizor is capable of handling threats like Iron Valiant and Flutter Mane for Heatran with Bullet Punch along with using Trailblaze to pressure Water-types such as Swampert and Primarina.

Special Defensive Wall (Fire).description:
Possessing a great typing and a high Special Defense stat, Heatran finds itself as both an amazing utility Pokemon and specially defensive wall for Fire teams, utilizing its bulk and Steel typing to sponge attacks from prominent special-attacking threats that otherwise rip apart most Fire-types, such as Dragapult and Latios. Heatran's Steel typing also allows it to take neutral damage from Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Power Gem, avoiding up to a 3HKO after Stealth Rock damage. Heavy Slam OHKOes Flutter Mane while also hitting the aforementioned Dragapult and Latios. Magma Storm is a strong STAB move that does immense damage and allows Heatran to trap and 1v1 foes such as Toxapex. However, Magma Storm lacks accuracy in comparison to Lava Plume, the weaker-yet-safer option that trades trapping and residual damage in favor of more PP and a chance to burn prominent physical attackers such as Swampert and Dragonite. Earth Power pairs nicely to hit opposing Fire-, Rock-, and Poison-types such as opposing Heatran, Glimmora, and Toxapex. Stealth Rock provides entry hazards to Fire teams, allowing them to rack up further chip damage and break Focus Sash or Sturdy on Pokemon like Skarmory, Ogerpon-C, and Ceruledge. 28 Speed EVs with a Sassy nature allows Heatran to outspeed Skarmory, Sinistcha, and Volcanion with no Speed investment, with the rest of its EVs maximizing its special bulk. Air Balloon allows Heatran to turn its 4x weakness to Ground-type attacks into an immunity, allowing it to temporarily check certain Ground types such as Excadrill, Mamoswine, and Choice Scarf Landorus if it is locked into Earth Power.

Heatran primarily serves to provide a defensive backbone to Fire teams' usually offensively focused cores. Ogerpon-H helps in wallbreaking Water and Ground teams, and Heatran helps cover Ogerpon-H by switching into potential revenge killers, such as Choice Specs Greninja and Choice Scarf Landorus's Sludge Wave. Focus Sash Ceruledge is also a commonly used Swords Dance sweeper that can help clean through types such as Ghost and Psychic. Heatran's Stealth Rock can help Ceruledge get past opposing Focus Sash Ceruledge and turn the +2 Shadow Sneak roll on Iron Boulder into a guaranteed OHKO. Ninetales is a strong option, as its ability to set sun enables every Fire-type Pokemon to deal increased Fire-type damage and absorb Water-type moves much easier, notably letting Heatran switch into Choice Specs Greninja Hydro Pump and perfectly avoid a 2HKO. Cinderace and Talonflame are both options on Fre-teams for hazard control with Court Change and Defog respectively.

Air Balloon (Steel).description:
Heatran's Flash Fire ability is an invaluable asset to Steel teams, as they are otherwise completely mowed down by powerful Fire-types like Volcarona. Heatran is a very reliable Stealth Rock setter, capable of threatening most entry hazard removers like Corviknight, Torkoal, and Galarian Weezing with its powerful Fire- and Ground-type coverage moves. Magma Storm lets Heatran effectively trap and KO bulky pivots, like Toxapex, with a combination of Magma Storm's passive damage and Earth Power as coverage. Power Gem allows Heatran to effectively hit the Fire-types it's meant to wall, easily OHKOing Moltres and Volcarona, both of which can easily take an Earth Power from Heatran.

Heatran appreciates Corviknight as a teammate, as it offers an immunity to Ground and a neutrality to Fighting while also granting Heatran a safe entry onto the field with its slow U-turn. Other Ground-immune teammates, like Skarmory, and Air Balloon users, like Gholdengo, find themselves alongside Heatran to pivot into Ground-type attacks for Heatran in the event that Heatran's Air Balloon gets popped. Skarmory and Gholdengo also create a great entry hazard-stacking core with Heatran, as Skarmory provides Spikes and Gholdengo blocks Defog and Rapid Spin. Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra offer a Water resistance for Heatran, the former of which appreciates Heatran using Stealth Rock to free up a moveslot of its own. Choice Scarf Iron Treads offers much-needed speed control and an immunity to Electric-type attacks from the likes of Zapdos and Thundurus-T. Furthermore, Iron Treads takes out threats to Heatran like Landorus and Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine with Ice Spinner and Earthquake, respectively. Setup sweepers like Bisharp and Scizor appreciate Heatran weakening bulky walls like Haze Toxapex and Unaware Quagsire to facilitate a sweep.

Stallbreaker (Fire).description:
Heavy Slam OHKOs Flutter Mane.

This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

vgc2024.overview:
• Heatran is a niche bulky offensive threat thanks to its solid stats and great typing, bolstered by Flash Fire. This makes Heatran have an incredible matchup against most of the metagame, such as Flutter Mane and Gholdengo.

  • Rillaboom is a great partner for Heatran, as it resists Heatran's prominent weaknesses, while also hitting Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Urshifu-R for huge damage. Heatran also pairs well with Ogerpon-W, which supports Heatran with Follow Me, as well as threatening Urshifu-R and Landorus.

  • Although Heatran resists a lot of attacks with its typing, it's weak to both of the Urshifu formes, Ogerpon-W, Landorus, and Iron Hands. Heatran also faces tough Fire- and Steel- competition, especially with Incineroar.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• The combination of Heatran's STAB moves, Heat Wave and Flash Cannon, can hit a lot of Pokemon in the metagame super-effectively, while Earth Power is a good coverage move that can hit Pokemon that resist Heatran's STAB combination, like Incineroar. Magma Storm is also another option as a Fire-type attack, as it traps the opponent, which works well with Leftovers.

  • Leftovers is a good item choice for Heatran, as it can live two Shadow Balls from Flutter Mane with a Special Attack-Booster Energy, and with Rillaboom's Grassy Surge, Heatran can constantly restore HP. Life Orb can increase Heatran's damage output, making it more of a threat.

  • 228 HP, 84 Defense EVs, and 20 Special Defense EVs allow Heatran to take an Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-W, almost always survives a Sludge Bomb from Landorus after Heatran Terastallizes and Life Orb recoil, and finally, with 20 Speed EVs, Heatran outspeeds both Urshifu formes after a Speed drop.

  • Tera Grass is an excellent Tera type for Heatran, allowing it to resist Water- and Ground-type moves from the likes of Pokemon like Urshifu-R and Landorus. Tera Fairy can allow Heatran to resist Urshifu-S's STAB moves and be a neutral type against the metagame.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Heatran can be used with the abilities Earth Eater or Levitate to turn its 4x Ground weakness into an immunity and improve its matchups against the likes of Iron Treads and Landorus-T. Offensive sets that utilize Heatran's strong base 130 Special Attack are rare due to its exploitable typing and stat distribution, but include Choice Scarf Desolate Land sets and Magic Guard with a held Life Orb to fire off strong STAB-boosted Steel Beam and Flare Blitz off of its respectable Attack Stat.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Heatran has no real means of mitigating its weakness to Fighting-type attacks and is OHKOed by Close Combat from Zamazenta and Great Tusk as well as Superpower from Protean Deoxys-S. It also struggles to switch in against Focus Blast Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Deoxys-S, all of which can cleanly 2HKO it.

Primordial Sea Users: The likes of Zapdos and Ogerpon-W can switch in on Fire moves and immediately threaten Heatran. Zapdos in particular can even chip Heatran in the strong sunlight with Fire-type Weather Ball, leaving it in a precarious position.

Bulky Water-types: RegenVest Swampert and Manaphy are not threatened if Heatran foregoes Solar Beam, taking hits comfortably. The former completely walls any Heatran not carrying Solar Beam, threatening OHKOs with Earthquake, and Manaphy is able to remove Heatran's Leftovers with Knock Off and chip it down over the course of a match.

Desolate Land Heatran.description:
A strong offensive typing in Fire / Steel and a high base Special Attack stat enable Heatran to function as a Stealth Rock setter that deters the tier's premier entry hazard removal Pokemon, Corviknight and Great Tusk, from switching in freely. Desolate Land effectively grants Heatran a Water immunity on activation, helping it check Water-types such as Manaphy and Primarina, especially blocking the latter's Flip Turn, as well as act as a switch-in to common Primordial Sea users like Zapdos and Ogerpon-W. Solar Beam is essential for Heatran to deal with RegenVest Swampert, allowing Heatran to 2HKO it. Will-O-Wisp can cripple physical attackers like Roaring Moon, and it is a generally useful move for racking up chip damage alongside Stealth Rock and Magma Storm. Earth Power is a strong alternative that OHKOes Iron Moth and deals strong damage to Well-Baked Body Steel-types like Gholdengo and Iron Treads as well as opposing Heatran. Power Gem may be used to hit Moltres, cleanly OHKOing physically defensive sets, while also being useful against the aforementioned Zapdos and Iron Moth. 60 EVs in Speed allow Heatran to outspeed uninvested Gholdengo, with the rest of its EVs being utilized to maximize its special bulk to live hits from the likes of Deoxys-S, Iron Crown, and Gholdengo.

Heatran is a strong piece that can fit on slower paced teams and bulky offensive structures. It appreciates offensive support from physical threats like Roaring Moon and Zamazenta that threaten specially bulky Pokemon it cannot muscle through such as RegenVest Manaphy and Swampert. These teammates, in turn, benefit from Heatran threatening Corviknight and Great Tusk, which would otherwise trouble these physical attackers. Heatran's 4x Ground weakness also requires a teammate such as Zapdos or Corviknight to cover for it as well as an answer to common Primordial Sea users like Zapdos and Ogerpon-W that can threaten it by switching in to reset the weather. RegenVest Roaring Moon is a potent teammate for Heatran, with a synergistic defensive typing and strong Knock Off. Heatran is almost always forced to run Leftovers due to its lack of access to natural recovery, so it appreciates teammates that can absorb Knock Off as well as consistent entry hazard removal. Great Tusk is an example of such a teammate, as it is able to come in on Knock Off and keep hazards off the field for Heatran to switch in repeatedly.

Assault Vest.description: Assault Vest Heatran uses its unique typing and defensive stats to match up well against common special attackers such as Flutter Mane and Gholdengo and threaten them back with its great offensive stats and wide coverage. While Heatran boasts an innately good defensive typing, Tera Grass allows it to turn its common weaknesses to Ground and Water into resistances, letting it match up better against the likes of Landorus-T and Palafin-H. Heat Wave is a spread STAB attack that chips away at foes, notably 2HKOing Amoonguss. Flash Cannon is Heatran's best way of hitting Fairy-types, as it OHKOes Diancie and 2HKOes Flutter Mane. Heavy Slam OHKOes Flutter Mane but is generally less reliable because it can be weakened by Intimidate and does less damage to Diancie and opposing Tera Grass Heatran mirror. Tera Blast hits Water- and Ground-types super effectively once Heatran has Terastallized, notably OHKOing Great Tusk and 2HKOing Bulk Up Palafin-H. Earth Power hits the Fire-types such as Volcanion, Chi-Yu, and opposing Heatran that otherwise resists all of Heatran's attacks. Heatran's base resistances let it take common Fairy-, Ice-, and Steel-type attacks such as Flutter Mane's Moonblast, Chien-Pao's Ice Spinner, and Gholdengo's Make It Rain much better. After Terastallization, Heatran matches up better against Palafin-H, Volcanion, and Iron Hands at the cost of receiving more damage from the aforementioned attacks. Heatran has a lot of defensive responsibilities on most teams, so Terastallization should not be used too frivolously. Heatran commonly finds itself in Fire / Water / Grass cores with Rillaboom and Palafin, as they complement each other offensively and defensively, with Rillaboom eradicating Water-types and Palafin punching through Fire-types. Iron Hands is a common Heatran partner that can pressure Palafin and Volcanion with Wild Charge and Chi-Yu and Tera Dark Kingambit with Drain Punch. Heatran has no form of recovery, so it appreciates teammates that can extend its longevity, such as Cresselia with Lunar Blessing and Amoonguss with Pollen Puff.

Air Balloon Stallbreaker (Steel).description: When soaring through the skies on an Air Balloon, Heatran can afford to invest in its powerful Special Attack and passable Speed while maintaining a useful defensive presence via its good natural bulk and immunities to Ground- and Fire-type attacks. While Air Balloon remains intact, Heatran can safely set Stealth Rock in front of or threaten foes that typically would beat it, such as Earthquake Mega Latios, Excadrill, and Gliscor. Magma Storm ensures that foes trying to pop Heatran's Air Balloon can be trapped and more easily dealt with, and its trapping damage can guarantee meaningful 2HKOs on opposing switch-ins such as Gliscor after Stealth Rock chip. Earth Power hits foes that do not fear Magma Storm such as opposing Heatran, Ceruledge, and Raging Bolt. For its last moveslot, Hidden Power Ice lets Heatran deal massive damage to Mega Garchomp, Dragonite, and Landorus; Power Gem prevents Mega Charizard Y, Araquanid, and bulky Volcarona from switching in freely on Heatran; and Taunt, in combination with Magma Storm, enables Heatran to trap and defeat walls such as Clodsire, Galarian Slowking, and Toxapex one-on-one. Toxic is another option to put Mega Latios, Mega Altaria, and bulky Water-types—like Gastrodon and Slowbro—on a timer. Since Air Balloon Heatran trades the longevity of bulkier Leftovers variants to enable it to initially set Stealth Rock more reliably, Gholdengo is an especially useful teammate that ensures Heatran's Stealth Rock stays in place while also absorbing Fighting-type attacks; in turn, Air Balloon Heatran can reliably switch in on Gholdengo's checks like Clodsire and opposing Heatran. Hisuian Goodra can tank Water-type attacks aimed at Heatran while raking foes across Heatran's Stealth Rock with Dragon Tail, and it can use Protect to scout for Fire- and Ground-type attacks from Choice-locked attackers, like Galarian Darmanitan, Landorus, and Blacephalon, to allow Heatran safe entry. Ferrothorn, which switches into Water-type attacks and relies on Heatran to switch into Fire-type attacks, forms a great defensive pairing and can also scout Choice-locked attackers with Protect while providing support for Heatran via Spikes and Leech Seed. Heatran is Spikes-immune while its Air Balloon remains intact, but its lack of recovery means it appreciates Iron Treads and Excadrill providing a reliable source of entry hazard removal via Rapid Spin. Mega Scizor also appreciates Heatran setting Stealth Rock and sponging Fire-type attacks aimed its way, and in return, Mega Scizor handles foes Heatran lures like Mega Altaria, Roaring Moon, and Gliscor.

Stallbreaker (Fire).description: Heatran is a great addition to Fire teams, serving as a stallbreaker with its access to Magma Storm and Taunt, and with Air Balloon, it answers Mega Diancie, Excadrill, and the Landorus formes while also providing excellent utility in Stealth Rock and Flame Body. Magma Storm is a powerful trapping tool against walls like Toxapex, Hippowdon, and Clodsire. Earth Power targets Fire- and Poison-types like opposing Heatran and Toxapex, which are immune to or resist Magma Storm. Flash Cannon allows Heatran to OHKO Fairy-types like Mega Diancie and Enamorus, which threaten Fire teams. On the other hand, Hidden Power Ice threatens Ground-types like Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Garchomp. With Taunt, Heatran can stop recovery for foes like Toxapex and Clodsire while also denying entry hazards from these foes as well as others like Gliscor. Alternatively, Stealth Rock allows it to support itself and its teammates like Ceruledge and Volcarona by wearing down the opposing team. Air Balloon provides Heatran with a Ground immunity, allowing it to deal with the aforementioned threats safely as long as its Air Balloon is intact. Torkoal and Ninetales serve as sun setters, boosting the power of Heatran's Magma Storm and softening Water-type moves. Torkoal also provides entry hazard removal with Rapid Spin and acts as an alternate Stealth Rock setter. Dragon Dance Mega Charizard X handles Dragon-types like Kyurem and Hydreigon. In return, Heatran can sponge attacks from Choice Scarf Latias. Mega Charizard Y is another sun setter that also provides a Ground immunity in case Heatran's Air Balloon has already been popped and offensively threatens Sand Rush Excadrill and Mega Swampert, which pose an immense threat to Fire teams, by resetting the weather and threatening them back with Fire Blast and Solar Beam, respectively. Z-Celebrate Victini deals with Fighting-types like Great Tusk and Iron Hands. Teammates like Volcarona, Iron Moth, and Blacephalon appreciate Heatran's ability to trap and eliminate foes like Toxapex and Clodsire. Volcarona can threaten Dark-types like Ting-Lu and Hydreigon that pose problems for Heatran. Choice Scarf Iron Moth and Blacephalon serve as revenge killers; Iron Moth deals with Kommo-o, while Blacephalon threatens Mega Gallade and can eliminate the Landorus formes for Heatran if running Hidden Power Ice, allowing Heatran to run a different move. Focus Sash Ceruledge can use its Fighting immunity to switch into Fighting-types like Iron Valiant, and Sneasler, threatening them back with its STAB moves. It also serves as a wallbreaker, removing special walls like Blissey and Swampert and Rock-types like Mega Tyranitar and Iron Boulder. In return, Heatran can deny entry hazards with Taunt to keep Ceruledge's Focus Sash intact, allowing it to reliably take on the aforementioned foes. Volcanion boasts a Water immunity, which allows it switch in against Water-type attacks from Choice Specs Greninja, Azumarill, and Choice Band Barraskewda; it can also eliminate bulky Ground-types like Hippowdon and Ting-Lu with Steam Eruption, which can potentially burn other foes.

Specially Defensive (Steel).description: Heatran is a mainstay on Steel teams due to its ability, Flash Fire, letting it switch into threats like Blacephalon, Victini, and Iron Moth. Lava Plume makes Heatran annoying to switch into thanks to its burn chance, while Magma Storm softens walls like Toxapex and Rotom-W by trapping them. Earth Power threatens Poison- and Fire-types and makes Heatran an important asset against opposing Steel teams by hitting opposing Heatran. Roar lets Heatran phaze the likes of Nasty Plot Hydreigon and Z-Celebrate Victini and synergizes well with Stealth Rock to deal extra damage. Alternatively, Toxic cripples walls like Mantine and Rotom-W, as well as Pokemon that fancy switching into Heatran such as Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y. Substitute pairs well with Toxic and allows Heatran to be massively annoying against types like Steel, Electric, and Psychic by capitalizing on the many switches it forces in these matchups. Thanks to their typing and bulk, Corviknight and Celesteela are excellent teammates to check Ground- and Fighting-types like Mamoswine and Great Tusk for Heatran. Setup sweepers like Mega Scizor and Z-Happy Hour Jirachi appreciate Heatran wearing down teams with burn and Toxic. Iron Treads removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin and deals with Mega Charizard Y, Zeraora, and Cinderace with its Choice Scarf set. Ferrothorn checks Water-types like Mega Swampert and Urshifu-R and aids Heatran with Spikes and Leech Seed.

Physical Wall.description:
• Giratina is an excellent wall on stall teams thanks to its massive mixed bulk and useful typing. This makes it an excellent check to threats such as Primal Groudon and Arceus. Giratina has useful utility with Defog and pairs well with Ho-Oh as a double Defog core. The two are able to consistently keep entry hazards off throughout the game, as Giratina can use Defog against Primal Groudon, while Ho-Oh can use Defog against defensive Eternatus. In addition, Giratina has a very valuable PP stalling ability in Pressure, allowing it to stall the PP of Choice Band Rayquaza, an extremely dangerous wallbreaker against stall.
  • Dragon Tail allows Giratina to phaze setup sweepers such as Arceus, Zekrom, and Necrozma-DM while dealing respectable damage to frailer Dragon-type setup sweepers such as Rayquaza and Mega Salamence. Dragon Tail is also a great way to spread chip damage against the opposing team, especially with entry hazard support from Arceus-Dark, Eternatus, or Mega Tyranitar.
  • Toxic allows Giratina to slowly damage targets such as Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh while preventing wallbreakers such as specially offensive Yveltal, Lunala, and Rayquaza from switching in freely.
  • Defog allows Giratina to remove hazards from the field, aiding hazard-vulnerable allies such as Dondozo, Chansey, and Arceus-Dark. This provides stall teams with much more longevity, allowing them to outlast hazard setters such as defensive Primal Groudon and Ferrothorn. However, Giratina is unable to use Defog against Taunt Arceus-Fairy.
  • Tera Fairy allows Giratina to check Palkia-O and non-Sludge Bomb Eternatus more efficiently while enabling it to emergency check the rare Zekrom and force it out with Dragon Tail.
  • Tera Poison gives Giratina a resistance to Fairy as well as a useful immunity to Toxic and the ability to absorb Toxic Spikes, allowing it to effectively check Arceus-Fairy and defensive Eternatus.
  • Giratina is useful early-game to scout Primal Groudon sets so that Dondozo isn’t sniped by Eruption or Overheat. Thanks to its ability to check every Primal Groudon set, Dondozo is free to preserve its HP to check threats such as Mega Salamence and Arceus.
  • Throughout the game, Giratina is an excellent setup disruptor with Dragon Tail. Against balance teams, Giratina should attempt to stay on the field and spread chip damage against foes by using Toxic and then Dragon Tail on Pokemon such as Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh. Against Choice Band Rayquaza, Giratina can be sacrificed in order to waste four of Dragon Ascent’s PP if necessary, although it should not directly switch into Rayquaza.
  • Giratina is easily set up on by Zacian-C, as Giratina cannot phaze it with Dragon Tail or use Toxic on it. Dondozo is an excellent teammate, as it is one of the few Pokemon that counters Zacian-C thanks to Unaware. Giratina cannot deal with Ultra Necrozma after setup, so Arceus-Dark is an excellent teammate, as it is immune to Photon Geyser and heavily punishes setup with Foul Play.
  • Taunt or Refresh Arceus-Fairy easily sets up on Giratina, while Eternatus can overwhelm Giratina with Dynamax Cannon, so Chansey makes a great teammate, as it is an excellent special wall to deal with these threats.

ubers.overview: Giratina-O is most notable for being the only offensive Defog user in Ubers, giving it a distinct niche. Its high bulk and unique typing combined with Levitate give it great use against top metagame threats like Arceus-Ground, Extreme Killer Arceus, and Kyogre. While its offensive stats are a bit low by Ubers standards, it makes up for it with Griseous Core's boost and access to high-Base Power moves like Poltergeist, Draco Meteor, and Hex. Furthermore, Will-O-Wisp, Thunder Wave, and Shadow Sneak are all great utility options at Giratina-O's disposal. Giratina-O is also one of the best users of Terastallization in the tier, becoming extremely tanky with Tera Steel or Poison in combination with Levitate. However, Giratina-O has no reliable recovery and thus can be chipped down by Stealth Rock and Ruination damage over time. It also stacks weaknesses with Koraidon and Miraidon, two of the most common Pokemon in the tier.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Shadow Ball is possible over Hex to have a stronger attack in the short term; this may notably help against Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground. Calm Mind sets are a possibility, but Giratina-O's lack of recovery really limits its ability to sweep.

Checks and Counters

Support Arceus Formes: Arceus formes like Arceus-Fairy and Arceus-Water can shrug off any attack Giratina-O throws at them, though neither appreciate status.

Ho-Oh: Ho-Oh can handle most attacks from Giratina-O, as it has high bulk and is immune to Will-O-Wisp. However, Stone Edge, Thunder Wave, and Tera Ghost-boosted Poltergeist all threaten Ho-Oh.

Chip Damage: Giratina-O has no recovery, so damage from poison, burn, or Stealth Rock can add up over time. Ting-Lu's Ruination can also greatly reduce Giratina-O's ability to check threats.

Physical Utility.description:
Although it necessitates teammates like Necrozma-DM to not run Knock Off, Poltergeist is a strong Ghost-type attack that is very spammable due to how few Pokemon that resist Ghost there are in the tier. Dragon Tail is a decently strong Dragon-type attack that has utility for forcing out Extreme Killer Arceus, which often runs Taunt, and Ting-Lu. Of the two status options, Will-O-Wisp should be run with Defog, as it pressures Ting-Lu much more; Ting-Lu can otherwise heal off damage with Leftovers, pressure Giratina-O with Ruination, and set entry hazards. Thunder Wave pressures common switch-ins like Ho-Oh and Arceus-Fairy much more, and as such is preferred when not running Defog. Access to Defog is extremely few and far between in Ubers, and therefore Giratina-O's access to it provides immense utility. It can be critical for maintaining an advantage in entry hazard management, especially once opposing entry hazard setters like Ting-Lu are taken out of the picture. Despite this utility, other options are still available for more offensively-minded teams. Shadow Sneak is a useful priority move that becomes very strong when combined with Tera Ghost; the combination of Tera Ghost Poltergeist and Shadow Sneak will even take out Koraidon. Alternatively, Stone Edge can be used to KO Ho-Oh, which otherwise takes non-Tera Ghost Poltergeist without worry. The given EVs allow Giratina-O to survive +2 Tera Ghost Arceus's Shadow Claw as well as +2 Life Orb Arceus's Shadow Claw after Stealth Rock damage. The Speed EVs are enough to outspeed uninvested Gliscor, with the rest dumped into Attack. Tera Steel should be run on Defog sets, as it negates all of Giratina-O's normal weaknesses, allowing Giratina-O to turn the tide against many Pokemon such as Koraidon using Scale Shot and Gliscor using Toxic. Tera Poison is another option, as it provides similar utility to Tera Steel without being weak to Koraidon's Flare Blitz.

Giratina-O is an excellent way to finish off most defensive cores in the tier, as its Defog support and ability to check Arceus-Ground, Extreme Killer Arceus, and Kyogre are very valuable. As such, classic defensive Pokemon like Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Fairy, Ting-Lu, and Arceus-Water are all fantastic partners. Miraidon deserves mention, since it can pressure Ting-Lu, Clodsire, and Gliscor extremely well, potentially leading to a huge advantage in entry hazard management. Giratina-O's Defog support can also enable some powerful wallbreakers like Choice Band Chien-Pao and Choice Specs Kyogre, which may not normally fit on most teams due to being too weak to entry hazards.

Special Utility.description:
Thunder Wave is Giratina-O's best option for punishing Ho-Oh and Arceus-Fairy, while Will-O-Wisp is a stronger option against Arceus, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, and Ting-Lu. Giratina-O's access to Defog gives it a unique niche on bulky offense and balance teams that can sufficiently pressure Ting-Lu. The given EV spread lets Giratina-O survive Shadow Claw from both Life Orb Arceus and Heavy-Duty Boots Tera Ghost Arceus after a Swords Dance and Stealth Rock damage while outspeeding uninvested Gliscor. Tera Steel lets Giratina-O stonewall Gliscor and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, pivot into Arceus-Fairy more easily, and take on Scale Shot Koraidon and Miraidon. Tera Poison is an alternative that still punishes Gliscor and Arceus-Fairy without giving Giratina-O a weakness to Low Kick and Flare Blitz from Koraidon and Close Combat from Zacian-C.

Giratina-O pairs well with teams that appreciate its ability to both check Arceus-Ground, Necrozma-DM, and Extreme Killer Arceus and keep entry hazards off the field against Spikes stacking teams. Arceus-Fairy and Gliscor are strong partners for their ability to punish Ting-Lu while pivoting around Koraidon and Miraidon, respectively. Necrozma-DM is a great partner to pressure Ho-Oh with Knock Off, Stone Edge, or boosted Photon Geyser. This is appreciated, since Ho-Oh can pivot into Giratina-O and entirely wall Will-O-Wisp variants while also checking Arceus-Fairy. Teammates that use Choice items such as Choice Scarf Koraidon, Choice Specs Miraidon, Choice Specs Kyogre, Choice Specs Flutter Mane, and Choice Band Chien-Pao appreciate Giratina-O removing hazards from the field, letting them not take hazard damage when they switch in and thus giving them more opportunities against bulkier teams that can annoy Giratina-O. Other teammates that appreciate Defog include Calm Mind Kyogre with Leftovers, Draco Plate Miraidon, and defensive Arceus formes. Miraidon is an especially notable partner for forcing progress on Ting-Lu while pivoting around Ho-Oh, letting Giratina-O win the hazard war in the long run. Ting-Lu and Gliscor pair well with Giratina-O by checking Miraidon and complementing Giratina-O's ability to spread status with additional hazard damage.

Physical Utility.description:
• Giratina-O's great offensive typing, coupled with Levitate, allows it to reliably Defog against staple entry hazard setters such as Primal Groudon and Necrozma-DM; it is also able to check strong attackers including Extreme Killer Arceus, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, and Ho-Oh. However, although its typing is excellent offensively, it leaves a bit to be desired defensively, since Giratina-O is weak to a lot of common types in the tier, which doesn't go well with Giratina-O's lack of reliable recovery. Regardless, these useful traits make Giratina-O a staple on bulky offense and balance teams alike.
  • Dragon Tail prevents setup from opposing threats such as Arceus and Primal Groudon, which Giratina-O would otherwise struggle to slow down due to their natural bulk.
  • Toxic punishes switch-ins such as Arceus-Fairy and Yveltal, as well as threatening defensive Primal Groudon that would handle Poltergeist more directly, making it the most consistent of the bunch because it will always be useful in a game. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM, preventing Giratina-O from being too passive against the former, while Thunder Wave handles threats such as Eternatus and Calm Mind Arceus formes lacking Refresh.
  • Shadow Sneak is a niche alternative that allows Giratina-O to revenge kill frailer foes such as Deoxys-A and Mega Mewtwo Y, but this comes at the cost of not being able to punish bulkier switch-ins like defensive Yveltal or Arceus-Fairy.
  • The following EV spread allows Giratina-O to avoid the 2HKO from Mega Salamence's Double Edge while 2HKOing defensive Necrozma-DM and offensive Eternatus with Poltergeist. An alternative EV spread can be used for Shadow Sneak variants, allowing Giratina-O to avoid the 2HKO from Mega Mewtwo Y's Psystrike while ensuring a 3HKO on defensive Primal Groudon and an OHKO against offensive Necrozma-DM, both after Stealth Rock.
  • Giratina-O's typing is really important to the balance and bulky offense playstyles it fits on, so Terastallizing Giratina-O is only useful in emergencies. Tera Poison allows Giratina-O to gain a poison immunity while also providing a resistance to Fairy, which is useful versus Arceus-Fairy and Play Rough Zacian-C. Unlike Tera Steel, it avoids being weak to Fire and Fighting, preventing Giratina-O from being weak to Low Kick Marshadow and Overheat Primal Groudon.
  • Tera Steel, however, grants a Rock resistance, which is useful versus Stone Edge Primal Groudon and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, while also letting Giratina-O handle Mega Salamence, Rayquaza, and Ultra Necrozma more comfortably. It also lets Giratina-O tank Dragon-type attacks from offensive Eternatus and phaze it away with Dragon Tail, removing its boosts and hitting it hard. However, it makes Giratina-O a riskier switch-in to Overheat and Heat Crash variants of Primal Groudon, as well as making it weak to Fighting-type moves from Marshadow and Zacian-C.
  • Because Giratina-O cannot reliably heal, health management is very important, which includes avoiding status, such as poison from Ho-Oh. This is to ensure Giratina-O has enough HP to reliably check what it needs to, since it would otherwise be overwhelmed by boosted attacks from Primal Groudon and Extreme Killer Arceus.
  • Against bulkier teams, it would be more beneficial for Giratina-O to use status moves such as Toxic or Thunder Wave to benefit its teammates more rather than attempting to deal damage with Poltergeist. This is because the status moves have better long-term impact against switch-ins like Arceus-Dark and Arceus-Fairy, while they would otherwise be able to just heal up any damage taken from Poltergeist. This is also why Toxic is generally the best option out of the three status moves, since it allows Giratina-O to make more progress versus Zygarde and Primal Groudon; the latter is a Pokemon Giratina-O should ordinarily check but can't due to its lackluster damage output against it.
  • Due to Giratina-O's lack of healing, Alomomola is an excellent teammate for it, as it is able to pivot into Giratina-O against Pokemon that would otherwise take advantage of it, such as Necrozma-DM and Primal Groudon, while also healing it up via Wish; Alomomola is also a great status absorber for Giratina-O, letting the latter avoid the residual damage it hates taking, such as Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire burns, while letting Giratina-O run status moves aside from Toxic such as Thunder Wave to better handle Zacian-C and Eternatus. Alomomola is also good at enabling Pokemon that Giratina-O appreciates, such as Chien-Pao, which threatens out Zygarde and Yveltal, and Ditto, which helps pressure out offensive sweepers such as Zacian-C and Meteor Beam Eternatus.
  • Arceus-Fairy makes up for Giratina-O's weaknesses to Dark-types including Yveltal and Arceus-Dark while handling Marshadow and switching into opposing Dragon-type attacks from Palkia-O to preserve Giratina-O's health. Stealth Rock variants are especially appreciated, since Giratina-O can abuse hazards well with Dragon Tail. This also applies to other hazard setters including Primal Groudon and Necrozma-DM, both of which handle the Fairy-types that Giratina-O cannot deal with; the former also helps versus Primal Kyogre, which would chip Giratina-O down with Ice Beam.
  • Offensive teammates such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM appreciate Giratina-O breaking down defensive walls such as Primal Groudon and defensive Necrozma-DM, while they in return handle the Dragon-, Fairy- and Ice-types that Giratina-O cannot handle, including Eternatus, Arceus-Fairy and Calyrex-I; the former also handles Dark-types such as Yveltal and Arceus-Dark.

Special Utility.description:
• Thanks to its excellent typing paired with Levitate, Giratina-O serves as an excellent Defogger on bulky offense structures and checks common threats such as Primal Groudon, Coil Zygarde, and Arceus. With a Specially Offensive set, Giratina-O is able to more immediately threaten Primal Groudon and Zygarde while dealing much more damage to Yveltal and Eternatus. Giratina-O can also fit on balance structures with Alomomola's Wish support due to the amazing role compression it offers. Giratina-O needs Alomomola support in order to offset its longevity issues and survive for the longer games balance teams tend to have.
  • Giratina-O's choice of status determines what it is able to cripple long-term and what it cannot deal with. The status selection highly depends on the team composition Giratina-O finds itself on.
