Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave are strong into offense, while Toxic can help break down Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh balances. Will-O-Wisp is able to cripple threats such as Zacian-C, Arceus, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground. Thunder Wave is able to deal with Pokemon such as Zacian-C and Eternatus by allowing teammates such as Marshadow and Eternatus to outspeed these threats. Toxic chips down Ho-Oh, Zygarde, Primal Groudon, and support Arceus formes, allowing allies such as Zacian-C and Marshadow more easily sweep late-game. However, Toxic sets greatly struggle with Zacian-C, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, and Calm Mind Arceus formes running Tera Poison.
  • The given EV spread avoids a 2HKO from Primal Groudon's Eruption and Mega Mewtwo Y's Psystrike after Stealth Rock. In addition, it guarantees a 2HKO on Eruption Primal Groudon with Draco Meteor. Giratina-O can invest 12 Speed EVs to outspeed paralyzed Zacian-C, though this means defensive EVs must be sacrificed. The second EV spread allows Giratina-O to survive a +3 Behemoth Blade from Zacian-C, a +2 Stone Edge from Primal Groudon, a Life Orb Yveltal's Dark Pulse, and a Tera Ghost Deoxys-A's Shadow Ball from full HP. It also is highly likely that Arceus-Dark's Foul Play is a 3HKO. In addition, Hex 3HKOes Coil Zygarde after status and Draco Meteor 2HKOed utility Swords Dance Primal Groudon, and Giratina-O can outspeed uninvested Zygarde and paralyzed Zacian-C.
  • A well-timed Terastallization is extremely powerful with Giratina-O. Tera Poison allows Giratina-O to tank any +3 attack from Zacian-C or Dynamax Cannon from Eternatus. This allows Giratina-O to deliver a devastating Will-O-Wisp or Thunder Wave to cripple these threats for the rest of the game. In addition, it is useful to check Marshadow, offensive Eternatus, and non-Taunt Arceus-Fairy. The poison immunity also gives Giratina-O much more longevity against bulky balance and stall structures.
  • Tera Steel provides similar utility as Tera Poison such as tanking a hit from Zacian-C lacking Close Combat or defensive Eternatus while delivering a crippling status and gaining a poison immunity. Tera Steel is able to wall Arceus-Ground, Ultra Necrozma, defensive Eternatus, and Mega Salamence more efficiently. However, Giratina-O loses the ability to check Primal Groudon sets with Overheat or Eruption and is still vulnerable to offensive Eternatus with Fire Blast. In addition, Giratina-O becomes vulnerable to Close Combat from Zacian-C and Low Kick from Marshadow.
  • Giratina-O serves as a Defogger and a reliable switch-in to all Primal Groudon sets on bulky offense, though it does not appreciate getting hit by Toxic. It is also valued for its status, allowing it to cripple threats such as Zacian-C and offensive Eternatus. Due to Giratina-O's limited longevity, it should be used sparingly early-game so that it has enough HP to fulfill these roles. As Zacian-C and Meteor Beam Eternatus can quickly run through defensive cores, Giratina-O should preserve its HP to cripple these threats with status in most cases. Teammates that have better longevity such as Arceus-Fairy and Calm Mind Arceus-Dark should be used to scout sets from threats such as Yveltal early-game. In addition, Coil Zygarde and Primal Groudon are appreciated to check physical wallbreakers such as Choice Band Marshadow early-game. Giratina-O also appreciates offensive teammates such as Marshadow and Dragon Dance Zygarde.
  • Giratina-O does not have the longevity to fit well on most balance structures, but Alomomola patches Giratina-O's longevity issues with Wish. This allows Giratina-O to be more aggressive in checking threats such as Primal Groudon and Zygarde early-game. In addition, Alomomola is able to easily use Toxic against Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh, allowing Giratina-O to drop Toxic to better check Zacian-C and Eternatus. However, this core struggles against Calm Mind Arceus formes, so Pokemon such as Taunt Arceus-Fairy, Fezandipiti, and defensive Eternatus are essential.
  • Giratina-O struggles massively against Taunt + Calm Mind Arceus-Dark and Arceus-Fairy. Therefore, Pokemon such as Zacian-C make excellent teammates. Giratina-O also struggles against specially offensive Yveltal, so Calm Mind Arceus-Dark, Fezandipiti, defensive and Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy, and Heavy-Duty Boots defensive Eternatus are great allies. Giratina-O is able to cripple threats such as Zacian-C, Eternatus, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground lacking Taunt with status moves. Giratina-O can become setup fodder to defensive Primal Kyogre, so Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and defensive Primal Groudon are useful teammates. In exchange, Giratina-O checks opposing Primal Groudon that threaten them. Giratina-O is also bad into stall and walled by Chansey. Therefore, Defensive Kyogre is a great teammate.

Defensive.description: Thanks to its bulk, typing, and Levitate ability, defensive Giratina-O checks Pokemon like Arceus, Arceus-Ground, and Choice Scarf Kyogre, and it is the only metagame-relevant Defog user. Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave both debilitate physical attackers, but Will-O-Wisp chips away at walls and affects Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, while Thunder Wave additionally impairs special attackers such as Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy. Poltergeist breaks Arceus-Ground's Substitute, which would otherwise block Will-O-Wisp and Dragon Tail, in one hit; alternatively, running Hex lets Giratina-O hit statused walls harder and makes burn affect it much less. Dragon Tail quickly racks up entry hazard damage on the opposing team and prevents foes from continuously setting up against Giratina-O, which is especially useful against Taunt users. The given EV spread lets Giratina take unboosted Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage and outspeed Taunt Landorus-T. Tera Steel makes Giratina-O immune to poison from foes such as Toxapex and gives it a resistance to moves like Arceus-Fairy's Judgment, Zacian-C's Play Rough and Behemoth Blade, Koraidon's Scale Shot, and Arceus-Ground's Dragon Claw and Ice Beam. Tera Poison similarly removes Giratina-O's Dragon weakness and provides it with an immunity to Toxic and a resistance to Fairy, but it doesn't make Giratina-O weak to Koraidon's Low Kick. Defensive Giratina-O fits best on balance teams that otherwise have trouble dealing with Ground-types such as Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground or need the increased longevity Defog provides. Toxapex and Skeledirge handle Pokemon like Zacian-C and Koraidon for Giratina-O; in return, it handles Ground-types and helps check Arceus. Giratina-O appreciates Ting-Lu and Arceus checking Calyrex-S for it; Ting-Lu also checks Miraidon and helps check Calm Mind Arceus-Ground. Calyrex-S likes Giratina-O being able to deal with its two main switch-ins, Arceus and Ting-Lu, by checking the former and removing the latter's Spikes. Because it lacks recovery, Giratina-O can get overwhelmed by the Pokemon it checks when facing hyper offense teams, so it appreciates revenge killers such as Extreme Killer Arceus and Choice Scarf Koraidon.

ru.overview: Cresselia's obscene bulk and colorful movepool make it a versatile wall in the metagame. It can act as either a hard-to-kill setup sweeper with Calm Mind and Moonlight or a supporting teammate that can paralyze Pokemon that try to set up on it, like Gyarados. Cresselia's exclusive access to Lunar Dance lets it fully heal and even cure teammates such as Galarian Zapdos, Basculegion-F, and Bisharp of status so that they can continue to break walls. Additionally, Cresselia has solid coverage in Ice Beam and Moonblast, threatening slower Pokemon like Hippowdon and Crawdaunt. However, Cresselia's mono-Psychic typing is underwhelming defensively, leaving it weak to common attackers like Gengar and Krookodile while offering few notable resistances in return. This means that Cresselia is often forced to Terastallize in order to wall threats effectively. Additionally, its Special Attack is rather pitiful, forcing Calm Mind sets to accumulate several boosts in order to break through defensive Pokemon like Hisuian Goodra and Slowbro; as such, it is often crippled by disruption such as Trick or Encore from Jirachi as well as Taunt from the likes of Krookodile. Cresselia also faces stiff competition from the tier's many Psychic-types, namely Slowbro and Jirachi, as a Calm Mind wall and utility Pokemon, respectively.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Shadow Ball has lower Base Power than Ice Beam or Moonblast but can be used to nail opposing Psychic-types, most notably Jirachi, while being solid neutral coverage overall. Thunderbolt is another coverage option, and it can nail bulky Water-types such as Empoleon. However, both coverage options leave Cresselia vulnerable to Dark-types. On the Calm Mind set, Stored Power can be used over Psyshock due to its higher potential power with enough boosts. Colbur Berry can be used as a one-time shield against Bisharp's Sucker Punch or Knock Off from the likes of Krookodile, letting Cresselia either nail them with a boosted Moonblast or use Lunar Dance.

Checks and Counters

Disruption: Cresselia's passivity makes it vulnerable to being afflicted with Taunt by the likes of Cyclizar and Krookodile as well as Encore by Maushold or Jirachi. Calm Mind sets are also vulnerable to being given a Choice item by Trick users like Gardevoir or Gengar

Ghost-types: Ghost-types like Basculegion-F, Gengar, and Mimikyu can take most of Cresselia's attacks before retaliating with a Ghost-type move. However, all three hate being paralyzed by Thunder Wave.

Dark-types: Defensive Dark-types, such as Umbreon and Wo-Chien, can comfortably take even Moonblast from Cresselia before whittling it down with Toxic and Leech Seed, respectively. Krookodile and Crawdaunt also threaten it offensively; however, neither like switching in to a potential Moonblast.

Steel-types: As Cresselia lacks coverage against Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and Bisharp, these Pokemon can wall Cresselia handily. On top of that, the former two can easily whittle it down, while the latter threatens it with Throat Chop. However, all three must be careful not to get crippled by Trick. Jirachi can also handle Cresselia easily thanks to its defensive typing and access to a variety of disruption methods, namely Body Slam paralysis and its own Trick, though it must be wary of being paralyzed by Thunder Wave.

Lunar Dance.description:
Set Details

Lunar Dance lets Cresselia bring back weakened teammates like Rhyperior and Galarian Zapdos from the brink, letting them continue to break walls and, in the latter's case, sweep teams. Ice Beam targets Ground-types like Hippowdon and Gligar, while Moonblast can dent Dark-types, like Crawdaunt and Krookodile, that attempt to switch in well as Fighting-types like Mienshao. Both options target Dragon-types that may try to take advantage of Cresselia like Cyclizar and Flygon. Trick should only be used alongside a Choice Scarf, as it can then allow Cresselia to cripple Pokemon that wall it, such as Registeel, as well as sweepers that try to set up on it, like Bisharp. Thunder Wave lets Cresselia act as speed control for its team, crippling fast threats like Galarian Zapdos and Barraskewda; it can also be used against Pokemon that Cresselia has given a Choice Scarf via Trick so that it can cripple them further and prevent them from reaping the benefits of the item. Moonlight acts as semi-reliable recovery, and it should always be used over Trick if Rocky Helmet is being held. However, it can be used on Trick sets over Thunder Wave. In addition to Choice Scarf being able to cripple setup sweepers and fellow walls, it lets Cresselia act as emergency speed control and reliably use Lunar Dance against even strong wallbreakers like Mimikyu and Basculegion-F. Rocky Helmet can be used instead to punish physical attackers like Maushold as well as a weak U-Turn from the likes of Galarian Zapdos and Talonflame. Additionally, Rocky Helmet can let Cresselia move some Speed EVs into its Defense, letting it take on physical attackers like Terrakion better. Tera Fairy grants Cresselia a resistance to Dark-type attacks and removes many of its weaknesses, letting it check the likes of Crawdaunt, Krookodile, and Golurk. Additionally, it also grants a power boost to Moonblast, guaranteeing a 2HKO on the aforementioned Krookodile.

Cresselia makes its home on bulky offense and balance structures that appreciate its ability to cripple a variety of Pokemon and revitalize an important teammate with Lunar Dance. Wallbreakers such as Galarian Zapdos and Basculegion-F benefit greatly from Cresselia's ability to bring them back from low health with Lunar Dance, giving them another chance to punch holes through teams. Slower attackers, like Bisharp and Mamoswine, appreciate Cresselia being able to heal them with Lunar Dance as well as crippling faster threats and physical walls with Thunder Wave and Trick, respectively. In return, they are able to dispatch Ghost- and Steel-types, respectively, with their STAB attacks. Fighting-types, such as Chesnaught and Galarian Zapdos, can deal with the Dark-types that threaten Cresselia, most notably Krookodile; in exchange, they appreciate Cresselia's ability to check opposing Galarian Zapdos as well as the speed control provided by its Thunder Wave. Cyclizar makes for a great partner with Cresselia, as it's able to check Ghost-types like Basculegion-F while keeping Stealth Rock off the field. In turn, Cyclizar appreciates Cresselia's ability to check opposing Dragon-types such as Noivern as well as cripple defensive Steel-types like Empoleon with Trick. On the defensive side, Pokemon like Wo-Chien and Umbreon can safely switch into Dark-type attacks while appreciating Cresselia's ability to cripple setup sweepers that could otherwise exploit them.

Calm Mind.description:
Set Details

Thanks to Cresselia's excellent bulk and access to recovery in Moonlight, it makes for a potent late-game Calm Mind sweeper that can be difficult for many teams to break through. Psyshock gives Cresselia the ability to beat opposing Calm Mind users like Slowbro and Suicune even after they've accumulated several boosts. Moonblast targets the Dark-types that attempt to switch in on Cresselia, such as Krookodile, as well as Dragon-types like Noivern. Leftovers helps keep Cresselia healthy during a sweep, making it less reliant on Moonlight for recovery, so that it can make progress quicker. This is especially important against bulkier teams that use Hippowdon, as Moonlight's recovery is reduced in sand. Covert Cloak protects Cresselia from Slowbro and Suicune's Scald as well as flinches and paralysis from Jirachi's Iron Head and Body Slam, respectively. Covert Cloak also blocks Psychic Noise's heal-blocking effect, letting Cresselia recover even against foes like Reuniclus and Slowbro. 136 Speed EVs are used to allow Cresselia to outspeed Bisharp and Modest Volcanion with the remaining EVs going into Defense so that Cresselia may check physical attackers like Galarian Zapdos and Entei. Tera Poison removes Cresselia's weaknesses; maintains its Fighting resist, letting it check Galarian Zapdos more easily; and grants it an immunity to Toxic from users like Umbreon and Quagsire, letting it completely wall them. While Tera Electric has less resistances than Tera Poison, it lets Cresselia have zero weaknesses thanks to Levitate; it also makes Cresselia immune to paralysis and gives it a resistance to Flying-type attacks from the likes of Galarian Zapdos.

Cresselia offers bulky offense and balanced teams a durable wincon. Fighting-types like Galarian Zapdos and Terrakion are able to switch into Dark-type attacks and put pressure on Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra and Bisharp, while Cresselia is able to handle opposing Psychic-types that give them trouble, like Slowbro and Reuniclus. Magnezone makes for a great partner thanks to its ability to handle Jirachi and Empoleon, two of Cresselia's best checks, as well as providing a slow Volt Switch to bring Cresselia in safely. In return, Cresselia provides a Ground immunity with Levitate and can handle the likes of Raikou for it. Other pivots that can pressure Jirachi, like Basculegion-F and Talonflame, also work well with Cresselia. Assault Vest Cyclizar is an annoyance for Cresselia, as it can take a boosted Moonblast before phazing it with Dragon Tail. Therefore, physical revenge killers like Galarian Zapdos and Krookodile make for great teammates, especially since they can also revenge kill problematic Pokemon like Gengar. Assault Vest Cyclizar and Umbreon make for good defensive pairings with Cresselia, as they appreciate its ability to handle problematic Pokemon such as Mienshao and Mamoswine; in return, they check the Ghost-types that give it a headache, such as Gengar and Basculegion-F.

Utility.description:
Cresselia leverages its fantastic bulk and support options to have a solid niche in the tier, checking threats such as Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Iron Valiant while disrupting the opposition and providing support to its teammates. Lunar Dance allows Cresselia to provide a second chance for an offensive teammate at either wallbreaking, sweeping, or revenge killing while preventing it from being too much of a momentum sink. Ice Beam allows Cresselia to super effectively hit Pokemon such as Dragonite, Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Great Tusk while chipping at Ting-Lu and Zapdos. However, Cresselia can opt for another attack instead. Moonblast lets Cresselia hit Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Dark-types such as Darkrai and Hisuian Samurott hard while still targetting Great Tusk. It can also use its STAB Psychic to better deal with Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Iron Valiant. Thunder Wave serves to immediately cripple many foes that Cresselia couldn't otherwise deal with such as Ogerpon-W, Darkrai, and Tornadus-T, especially if it lacks the corresponding attack to threaten them. Its ability to spread paralysis via Thunder Wave also works well with Ice Beam to hit the aforementioned Ground-types. Moonlight keeps Cresselia healthy, letting it consistently check Pokemon such as Great Tusk. Trick + Choice Scarf is an option to permanently shut down a foe, particularly setup sweepers like Clefable, Hatterene, and Kingambit that can otherwise exploit Cresselia's general passivity, as well as walls like Alomomola, Galarian Slowking, and Blissey. Eject Button allows Cresselia to pivot once after taking a hit, preventing the loss of momentum from directly switching out, which is particularly useful on archetypes that rely on preserving turns as much as possible, such as sun teams. Because it's a consumable item, Eject Button has the additional benefit of weakening Knock Off from foes such as Swords Dance Gliscor and Hoopa-U. Rocky Helmet is an alternative choice, letting it spread chip damage by punishing contact moves such as Rapid Spin from Great Tusk and Iron Treads, Flip Turn from Alomomola, and the ever-present U-turn from foes like Landorus-T, Corviknight, Cinderace, and Moltres. It also prevents Ice Beam Cresselia from losing to non-Rest IronPress Zamazenta, since Cresselia cannot deal meaningful damage otherwise. Steel is the preferred Tera type, turning Cresselia's weakness to U-turn into a resistance, making it immune to Toxic, and synergizing well with its ability, allowing Cresselia to wall Pokemon such as Kyurem, Enamorus, and Gliscor while improving its matchup against Dragonite. Tera Fairy is another option that allows Cresselia to resist Dark-type moves such as the prevalent Knock Off from Pokemon like Hisuian Samurott and Iron Valiant as well as Darkrai's Dark Pulse, boost Moonblast's damage output, and still resist U-turn. An EV spread of 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 Spe with a Timid nature should exclusively be used on Choice Scarf variants, letting it outspeed even Choice Scarf Gholdengo, +1 Dragonite, and Zamazenta.

Cresselia best fits on fast-paced teams that appreciate its support options while making up for its general passivity. It notably synergizes well with sun teams, as setters like Torkoal and Ninetales are very susceptible to chip damage from entry hazards, while teammates that take advantage of the sun such as Life Orb Venusaur, Great Tusk, Raging Bolt, and Walking Wake get regularly chipped down by trading attacks and taking damage from hazards. Therefore, Lunar Dance support is very much appreciated. Eject Button is preferred to allow Cresselia to perform the role of a safe pivot, giving a free switch to the aforementioned sun teammates, which is invaluable given the limited sun turns. In return, the weather boosts Moonlight's healing to absurd levels, allowing Cresselia to consistently stay healthy until Lunar Dance is needed. Cresselia synergizes well with more than just sun teams; Dark-types such as Kingambit, Darkrai, and Hisuian Samurott all appreciate Cresselia checking Fighting-type Pokemon like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant. In return, these Dark-types support Cresselia by switching into Ghost- and Dark-type moves, such as Gholdengo's and Dragapult's Shadow Ball and Knock Off from Pokemon like Hisuian Samurott and Tyranitar. Ogerpon-W appreciates Cresselia paralyzing foes that would usually outspeed it, such as Cinderace, Dragapult, Tornadus-T, and Booster Energy Iron Moth, as well as Lunar Dance support, since Ogerpon-W is susceptible to hazards and other forms of chip damage. Particularly, Cresselia can hit Dragon-types like Dragonite and Hydrapple with Ice Beam and Kyurem with Moonblast; these Pokemon can switch in on and threaten Ogerpon-W. Cresselia also handles opposing Ogerpon-W, taking its STAB moves and crippling them in return with Thunder Wave. In return, Ogerpon-W can deal with bulky Ground-type Pokemon that can switch into Thunder Wave and shrug off Cresselia's attacks, such as Ting-Lu, Iron Treads, and Ursaluna. Cresselia also makes for a great partner for Raging Bolt, as it can switch into Ground-type attacks such as Great Tusk's Headlong Rush and Earthquake from foes such as Gliscor and Dragonite. Paralysis support allows Raging Bolt to outspeed opposing Dragon-types like Dragapult, Kyurem, and Walking Wake and eliminate them with its Dragon-type STAB options. Thunder Wave can also slow down other foes, such as Enamorus, Iron Valiant, and Zamazenta, removing Raging Bolt's reliance on Thunderclap. In return, Raging Bolt can check Zapdos, which blocks Thunder Wave, and bulky Water-types that don't mind paralysis, such as Alomomola and Dondozo. Cresselia is on the passive side, which leaves it vulnerable to being setup fodder for Pokemon such as Gholdengo, Raging Bolt, and Substitute Zamazenta. Teammates that deal with such threats, such as Encore Iron Valiant, Roar Zamazenta, and Whirlwind Ting-Lu, are greatly appreciated by Cresselia. In a similar vein, Kingambit can easily set up on Cresselia and threaten it with Dark-type STAB options, so allies that check Kingambit such as Great Tusk and Zamazenta are valuable.

Trick Room Setter.description:
Cresselia functions as a niche Trick Room setter due to its excellent natural bulk that allows it to get off Trick Room reliably across a game, as well as its access to supporting moves such as Lunar Dance, which allows Cresselia to safely bring in its teammates to maximize Trick Room turns while also keeping them healthy for more opportunities for a late-game sweep. Moonlight lets Cresselia leverage its excellent bulk to set Trick Room more reliably. Ice Beam is used in order to hit Dragonite and Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Gliscor, while Moonblast allows Cresselia to pressure Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Dark-type switch-ins such as Darkrai and Hisuian Samurott. At the cost of being very vulnerable to Taunt, Cresselia can also run dual screens with Light Clay instead to further support its offensively-inclined teammates, particularly ones that appreciate the easier turns of setting up, like Ursaluna, Iron Hands, and Kingambit. Mental Herb allows Cresselia to reliably set Trick Room against Taunt users such as Landorus-T, Ogerpon-W, and Deoxys-S. Tera Poison gives Cresselia a solid defensive typing, removing its weakness to U-turn and giving it an immunity to poison, greatly improving its longevity while also pairing well with Levitate, while Tera Fairy removes Cresselia's Dark weakness and powers up its Moonblast, allowing it to flip common matchups against threats such as the aforementioned Darkrai, which it can now 2HKO.

Cresselia's ability to set Trick Room is greatly appreciated by slow, bulky wallbreakers such as Ursaluna, Iron Hands, and Kingambit, all of which find opportunities to break under Trick Room easily with their low Speed. Iron Hands is able to break down common defensive pieces such as Alomomola and Gliscor, which would otherwise stall out Trick Room turns, with its STAB combination and Ice Punch. Iron Hands also provides Cresselia with a switch-in against common Dark-type threats such as Kingambit, Darkrai, and Hisuian Samurott. Kingambit also handles Darkrai as well as handling Gholdengo. Other excellent partners under Trick Room include Raging Bolt and Enamorus-T, due to their low Speed, high bulk, and ability to break through defensive Pokemon, with the former dealing with certain Steel-types such as Corviknight and Skarmory and the latter threatening Dark-types such as Ting-Lu. Cresselia also appreciates other Trick Room setters to set it multiple times in a game; Hatterene is its best partner, due to its ability to deny entry hazards from Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Ting-Lu. In return, Cresselia can use Lunar Dance in order to keep Hatterene alive so it can continue to deny hazards and set Trick Room again. Lunar Dance is also able to heal teammates such as Iron Hands and Kingambit after a burn and allow Ursaluna to stay alive and break for longer. Cresselia also finds itself vulnerable to Ghost-types such as Dragapult, Gholdengo, and Pecharunt, meaning checks such as Hoopa-U, Assault Vest Hisuian Samurott, and Ting-Lu are appreciated. Ting-Lu also sets Stealth Rock, chipping down defensive pieces for some of the aforementioned Trick Room sweepers to make the most of the turns Cresselia can give. Faster partners include Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, and Ogerpon-Wellspring, with the former two threatening Dark-types for Cresselia, while in return, Cresselia is able to keep them healthy using Lunar Dance.

• Cresselia is an excellent Trick Room setter due to its high bulk, useful utility, and access to Levitate. Due to these qualities, it can set Trick Room on powerful wallbreakers such as Primal Groudon, Primal Kyogre, and even Yveltal.
  • Lunar Dance allows Cresselia to keep momentum for the team after setting Trick Room. Its ability to restore PP allows teammates such as Melmetal and Calyrex-I to wallbreak mid-game without worrying about the PP of their STAB moves late-game.
  • Magic Coat prevents foes such as Ferrothorn and Primal Groudon from setting up entry hazards. If Cresselia's Mental Herb is used up, Magic Coat can be useful to deny threats such as Arceus-Ground and Yveltal from using Taunt, although it is a risky choice against the latter.
  • Toxic is useful to deal chip damage to walls such as Primal Groudon, Arceus-Dark, and Giratina-O. This allows Melmetal and Calyrex-I to wallbreak past these checks more easily. Alternatively, Future Sight can produce similar pressure and makes switching in harder for the opponent, being able to OHKO defensive Ho-Oh after Choice Band Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance and defensive Primal Groudon after Tera Ice Choice Band Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance.
  • The given EV spread avoids an OHKO from a fully powered Primal Kyogre's Water Spout, Double Dance Primal Groudon's Heat Crash after Stealth Rock, +3 Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, +2 Tera Ghost Arceus's Shadow Claw, and Life Orb Yveltal's Dark Pulse or Knock Off.
  • Tera Water allows Cresselia to set Trick Room on +2 Heat Crash Primal Groudon, although this is a dead Tera slot otherwise and is wasted if the opposing Primal Groudon isn't carrying Heat Crash. Therefore, Cresselia should not use Tera often, as teammates such as Melmetal and Calyrex-I need it to wallbreak.
  • Cresselia is best used as a mid- to late-game setter. Due to its great bulk, Cresselia can usually switch in for a teammate once Trick Room ends, tank a couple of hits from threats like Arceus and Primal Groudon, and set Trick Room. Cresselia switches in for Melmetal especially well, as it is immune to Ground-type attacks directed at Melmetal thanks to Levitate.
  • When Cresselia is up against Pokemon that cannot 2HKO it such as defensive Primal Groudon and Arceus Ground, it may be best to first use Toxic or Future Sight in order to weaken them for teammates. This should not be done against Zygarde, however, as it can wall Calyrex-I and Melmetal with Tera Water after a Coil. When entry hazard setters such as Ferrothorn are on the field, it may be best for Cresselia to use Magic Coat first to punish attempts to set Spikes.
  • Pokemon that appreciate Trick Room support on top of PP restoration such as Melmetal and Calyrex-I make excellent teammates. Calyrex-I specifically greatly appreciates Cresselia keeping off Stealth Rock with Magic Coat.
  • Cresselia needs support in setting Trick Room, as usually it is only able to set one round of it. As a result, additional setters such as Hatterene and Arceus are great teammates.

Clear Amulet.description:
• Cresselia can opt to run a Clear Amulet to prevent moves such as Hisuian Goodra's Acid Spray, Primarina's Icy Wind, and Sylveon's Fake Tears from disrupting its ability to set up and defeat the foe with Stored Power.
  • Stored Power becomes Cresselia's strongest move after it has used Calm Mind multiple times.
  • Calm Mind allows Cresselia to KO the foe with Stored Power.
  • Moonlight lets Cresselia regain HP when necessary to continue setting up with Calm Mind.
  • Reflect is usually used in the last moveslot to help Cresselia take strong physical attacks from Pokemon like Choice Band Ursaluna.
  • Future Sight can be used instead to defeat Encore + Disable Iron Valiant, which would otherwise be able to beat Cresselia.
  • Cresselia's Special Defense EVs are meant to take Draco Meteor from Choice Specs Kyurem twice with a Calm Mind boost, and its Speed EVs allow it to outspeed base 60 Speed Pokemon like Primarina and Hisuian Goodra. The rest of the EVs are placed in Defense.
  • Cresselia will never win a matchup against Dark-types like Urshifu-S and Meowscarada, while other Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Alolan Ninetales can lock Cresselia into an unfavorable move with Encore. Fairy-type Pokemon like Diancie and Sylveon can help Cresselia defeat the former foes, while faster Pokemon that do not mind Encore like Iron Moth can help Cresselia with the latter.

Choice Scarf.description:
• With use of a Choice Scarf, Cresselia can make use of the additional Speed and ability to disrupt Pokemon with Trick.
  • Cresselia outspeeds and uses Psychic to threaten to 2HKO on Pokemon like Annihilape, Iron Moth, and Urshifu-R.
  • Moonblast lets Cresselia to deal with Haxorus and less bulky variants of Urshifu-S.
  • Trick allows Cresselia to lock foes into a non-damaging move, such as Manaphy, Espathra, Clear Amulet Zapdos, and Serperior.
  • Moonlight allows Cresselia to heal itself in matchups where it can lock foes into a weaker attacking move, such as against Weakness Policy Iron Crown.
  • The defensive EVs allow Cresselia to survive two Choice Band Haxorus Outrages and two non-Choice Specs Volcanion Steam Eruptions with burn chip damage. The Speed EVs allow Cresselia to outpace Iron Moth with a Choice Scarf and Hisuian Goodra after a Trick, and the rest of the EVs are dumped into Special Attack.
  • Choice Scarf Cresselia is a great way to surprise players expecting Clear Amulet Cresselia, but without Reflect,it could struggle versus strong physical attackers like Ursaluna and Haxorus, so teammates like Corviknight and Urshifu-S are great partners.
  • Cresselia will inevitably lose against Dark-types like Meowscarada, Chien-Pao, and Galarian Moltres, so Fairy-type and Steel-type teammates like Alolan Ninetales and Heatran can cover these weaknesses.

Calm Mind.description: This is a sample set as we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

vgc2024.overview:
• Cresselia shines in VGC as an incredibly bulky Trick Room setter with access to Lunar Blessing. Cresselia is a great check to Amoonguss and Urshifu-R, nullifying Spore with Lunar Blessing and pressuring the latter with a 2HKO.

  • Cresselia's strongest partner is Ursaluna, as it's a strong Trick Room sweeper that appreciates Lunar Blessing negating the burn chip damage. Cresselia's Levitate also allows Ursaluna to freely click Earthquake. Cresselia also appreciates Pokemon like Amoonguss and Iron Hands, which help get up Trick Room and act as threats under Trick Room themselves.

  • Cresselia struggles against Incineroar, as Fake Out can allow Incineroar's partner to get off another hit, which can be the difference between setting up Trick Room and not. Cresselia also faces issues against Farigiraf, which can reverse or Imprison Trick Room. Tornadus can also prove to be difficult, as Taunt prevents Trick Room from going up and takes advantage of Cresselia's passivity.

Trick Room Support.description:
• Cresselia uses Moonblast to hit more of the metagame for super effective damage, including Urshifu-S, while Ice Beam can be used to threaten the Landorus formes and Dragonite. Cresselia may opt for Psychic for the extra power before Terastallization.

  • Helping Hand allows Cresselia to more actively support its partners, especially Ursaluna and its Earthquake. Cresselia can use Ally Switch to provide game-deciding mind games and a way to protect its partners in a pinch.

  • Cressellia uses Safety Goggles to protect itself from Amoonguss's Spore and be able to consistently protect its teammates with Lunar Blessing.

  • The EV spread allows Cresselia to almost always survive two Mystic Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R, and always avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

  • Tera Fairy is the most consistent for Cresselia, as it provides a resistance to the common Dark-type moves such as Urshifu-S's Wicked Blow or Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave, as well as gaining STAB on Moonblast. Tera Poison is a generally good defensive typing further bolstered by Levitate, and it provides key resistances to Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Rillaboom's STAB moves.

Serene Queen (Calm Mind).description:
• With its great bulk and the advent of Terastallization, Cresselia is a formidable defensive presence with the ability to take over late in the game.

  • Calm Mind: Calm Mind allows Cresselia to bolster its defensive profile while also increasing its damage output.

  • Moonblast: While lacking STAB, Moonblast has no immunities, which makes it Cresselia’s most reliable offensive move.

  • Stored Power: While blanked by Dark-types, Stored Power allows Cresselia to threaten walls like Unaware Dondozo and more reliably win Calm Mind wars against foes like Flutter Mane. It also allows Cresselia to potentially beat Heatran with sheer power should it accrue enough boosts.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam allows Cresselia to immediately threaten the many Ice weak Pokémon in the metagame, such as Dragonite, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu.

  • Thunderbolt - Thunderbolt allows Cresselia to immediately threaten Urshifu-R and is a great general attacking move if used with an Electric Tera.

Other Options

  • Substitute: While difficult to fit, Substitute can protect Cresselia from debilitating status from the likes of Toxapex and Dondozo, giving it a wider reach against slower paced teams without relying on Covert Cloak as much.

  • Lunar Dance: While seemingly odd on a defensive set, Lunar Dance allows Cresselia to bring back a battered teammate in the event it itself cannot finish the game, giving formidable partners such as Chien-Pao and Ursaluna a second chance to break down the opponent.

Items

  • Covert Cloak: Covert Cloak guards Cresselia from adverse effects such as flinches and Defense drops that would otherwise impede its ability to take over the endgame. It also negates the passive damage from Garganacl’s Salt Cure, allowing Cresselia to heavily punish it.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers’s passive recovery allows Cresselia to better conserve its limited Moonlight PP, more safely set up against powerful attackers like Flutter Mane, and be a more active presence on the field by not mandating it use a turn to heal off every hit it takes manually.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Cresselia makes excellent use of Terastallization thanks to its bulk and Levitate, especially since its presence at team preview attracts hard counters.

  • Electric: Thanks to Levitate, Tera Electric grants Cresselia a complete lack of weaknesses, giving it an extremely diverse defensive profile courtesy of its immense bulk. It also guards against paralysis, minimizing the chance of an ill-timed lost turn ruining a sweep.

  • Poison: Tera Poison protects Cresselia against Toxic, allowing it to more safely set up against Pokémon like Toxapex. It also grants security against even Tera Fairy Choice Specs Flutter Mane by allowing Cresselia to resist Fairy.

  • Steel: Tera Steel combined with Levitate puts the brakes on Tera Normal Ursaluna-B while also giving a great defensive matchup into Tera Flying Dragonite and Tera Fairy Choice Specs Flutter Mane.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy grants Cresselia a crucial resistance to Dark, allowing it to better take on foes like Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu.

Trick Room Support.description:
• WIth the combination of Trick Room and Lunar Dance, Cresselia can give bulky attackers like Ursaluna-B another chance for dangerous comeback sweeps!

  • Moonblast: Due to the support nature of this set, Moonblast is preferred over a STAB move; otherwise, Cresselia is walled by common Dark-type threats like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S.

  • Moonlight: Moonlight makes Cresselia less of a one-and-done support Pokemon, increasing its longevity and potentially letting it stall out weaker attackers.

  • Ice Beam: Ice Beam is more effective at pressuring Dragonite than Moonblast, which can be useful if wanting to force an early Terastallization.

  • Bold versus Relaxed : Thanks to a decent base Speed stat, a Bold nature with regular Speed is an option if wanting to make Cresselia more flexible outside of Trick Room.

Other Options
  • Skill Swap: Skill Swap can be used to take away Multiscale from Dragonite, which otherwise can use Roost on the turn that Cresselia uses Lunar Dance. Since Dragonite can still switch out to reset its ability, this option works best with Stealth Rock support.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: This set's support focus and bulk usually do not require Terastallization, making Cresselia an excellent partner for the sweepers it supports.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy lets it resist Dark-type attacks from the likes of Chi-Yu while also nullifying Scale Shot setups from attackers like Dragonite and Roaring Moon.

  • Electric: Tera Electric remains a solid option thanks to Levitate, giving Cresselia essentially no weaknesses and providing an important paralysis immunity.

  • Steel: Tera Steel makes it much harder for Latios to muscle through Cresselia while still maintaining a very favorable matchup against Dragonite thanks to the synergy with Levitate.

Items

  • Mental Herb: Cresselia is frequently targeted by Taunt users like Flutter Mane, making Mental Herb a great option to guarantee Trick Room is set.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is a strong general option for further augmenting Cresselia's longevity.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet is useful for breaking Focus Sash from targets like both formes of Urshifu, making it more difficult for them to stall out an incoming Trick Room sweep.

Unaware.description: Cresselia's titanic bulk and access to Calm Mind allow it to pose a major threat to the opponent's team, turning other setup sweepers into fodder. It can also leverage its Psychic typing to check huge threats such as Azelf and Deoxys-S. Late game, Cresselia can function as a terrifying and offbeat set-up sweeper, boosting and using Moonblast to hit Dark-types such as Chien-Pao and Roaring Moon. Cresselia's ideal opportunity to set up is in front of passive walls like Manaphy, Swampert, and non-Unaware Blissey. Cresselia's best teammates are Pokemon that can take on Dark-Type moves like Corviknight and Great Tusk. Prankster Corviknight and Deoxys-S can set dual screens to make Cresselia's setup easier. Cresselia also appreciates teammates such as Mandibuzz, Blissey, and RegenVest Hisuian Goodra that can switch into Ghost-types.

Trick Room.description: This EV spread survives a Dark Pulse from Timid Choice Specs Chi-Yu.

Tail Glow.description:
Tail Glow Manaphy puts the spotlight on the power of Tail Glow combined with Manaphy's deep movepool, transforming it into a powerful wallbreaker. With a single Tail Glow, Manaphy's Surf washes away common walls, 2HKOing Ting-Lu, Galarian Slowking, and Assault Vest Iron Crown, as well as threatening to OHKO offensive threats like Great Tusk and Iron Moth without a boost. Alternatively, Scald trades damage for a chance to burn targets like Kingambit and Meowscarada, punishing their attempts to switch into Manaphy, and defensive checks like Primarina. Alluring Voice threatens Hisuian Samurott and Dragon-types like Raging Bolt, Dragonite, and Kyurem as well as punishing setup opportunities. Substitute allows Manaphy to set up comfortably on status spreaders like Galarian Slowking and Tera Water Gliscor, avoid Salt Cure from Garganacl, and punish Thunderclap and Sucker Punch from Raging Bolt and Kingambit. Energy Ball slams Water-resistant foes like Primarina, Tera Water Garganacl, Assault Vest Alomomola, and Terastallized Ogerpon-W hard. Rest can also be used on rain teams, taking advantage of Hydration to give it much-needed longevity to keep wallbreaking against bulky teams. While the recovery from Leftovers is generally preferred, Covert Cloak is an option to let Manaphy set up freely on the likes of Garganacl's Salt Cure and Galarian Slowking's Sludge Bomb. Tera Fairy boosts the power of its Alluring Voice and eases the matchup against threats like Kyurem, Dragapult, Zamazenta, Ogerpon-W, and Raging Bolt.

With its sheer power but middling Speed, Manaphy slots best as a wallbreaker on offensive teams, such as Sticky Web and rain builds. Araquanid is a natural partner as the cornerstone of the Sticky Web archetype, with its Sticky Web allowing Manaphy to outspeed all threats besides Deoxys-S and Heavy-Duty Boots users like Zamazenta, giving many opportunities for setup and sweeping. Ribombee is another solid Sticky Web setter with better matchups against threats like Raging Bolt and Kyurem, which Araquanid can struggle with. Gholdengo and Raging Bolt greatly appreciate Manaphy's excellent matchup against Ting-Lu, while the former threatens Kyurem and Iron Valiant as well as preserving the entry hazards that enable Manaphy, and the latter threatens Ogerpon-W, Tera Water Garganacl, and Toxapex. Physical attackers like Kingambit and Dragonite pair well with Manaphy, with both taking advantage of Manaphy's wallbreaking against walls like Zamazenta, Corviknight, and Dondozo to clean the weakened teams left in its wake. On rain teams, Pelipper is a must-have as the only viable Drizzle user in the tier, boosting Manaphy's already powerful Surf to new heights, such as OHKOing Ting-Lu after a Tail Glow boost. Pelipper's Drizzle also enables Manaphy's Hydration, washing away status effects that might otherwise cripple it. Darkrai and Iron Valiant especially appreciate Manaphy weakening walls like Primarina, Ting-Lu for the former, and Galarian Slowking for the latter, while Iron Valiant beats Kyurem, and Darkrai threatens Ogerpon-W. In general, hazard removal from a Pokemon like Great Tusk or Iron Treads is useful as well, ensuring Manaphy can switch in repeatedly without fear of hazards, as well as checking Raging Bolt. Stealth Rock setters like the aforementioned Great Tusk and Iron Treads as well as Landorus-T and Glimmora are also appreciated by Manaphy, wearing down switch-ins like Ogerpon-W to ease Manaphy's sweep. In addition, Landorus-T and Iron Treads can safely bring Manaphy in through U-turn and Volt Switch, respectively, while Glimmora can clear Toxic Spikes.

Take Heart.description:
Take Heart Manaphy takes advantage of Manaphy's decent bulk and strong arsenal of boosting moves to power its way through weakened teams. Take Heart and Acid Armor form a potent combination that allows Manaphy to quickly become unassailable and snowball through unprepared teams, especially with Take Heart clearing status that would normally cripple it, such as from Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Gliscor. Scald complements the set excellently as a reliable STAB option that can burn threats Manaphy can struggle with like Kingambit, allowing it to set up on these foes, while wearing down phazers like Ting-Lu and Moltres, which can stop Manaphy's sweep. Stored Power works well with its boosting antics and threatens the vast majority of the tier, slamming the likes of Kyurem, Zamazenta, Raging Bolt, and Ogerpon-W hard. 216 Speed EVs with a Timid nature ensure Manaphy outspeeds Kyurem, with the rest invested into bulk to maximize Manaphy's survivability. Tera Poison makes it less reliant on Take Heart to deal with Toxic, flips its Grass resistance against foes like Rillaboom, and gives it a better matchup against the likes of Zamazenta and Iron Valiant. Tera Dragon keeps the crucial Grass-type resistance, particularly against Ogerpon-W, while also being handy against foes like Zapdos.

While powerful with enough boosts, Take Heart Manaphy can struggle to gain said boosts due to its middling Speed and bulk, so it works best on hyper offense teams like dual screens and Sticky Web builds, which make up for these shortcomings. On Aurora Veil teams, Alolan Ninetales is a natural partner as the only OU-viable setter, giving Manaphy much greater ease in setting up with the added bulk as well as threatening Ogerpon-W and Raging Bolt. Sweepers like Iron Moth and Darkrai work well with Manaphy, weakening teams and overwhelming shared checks like Tera Water Garganacl and Tera Water Ting-Lu, clearing a path for Manaphy to sweep late-game. Similarly, bulkier options like Zamazenta and Swords Dance Gliscor act as great fallbacks, with Zamazenta taking on Ogerpon-W and Kyurem and Gliscor checking Raging Bolt. On Sticky Web teams, Araquanid is the premier setter and is thus a must-have partner for Manaphy. Teammates like Gholdengo and Raging Bolt synergize well with Manaphy, with both threatening Rillaboom, the former checking Kyurem and Iron Valiant while keeping Sticky Web on the field, and the latter beating Ogerpon-W and Primarina. Physical sweepers like Dragonite and Great Tusk also are appreciated by Manaphy; the former checks Ogerpon-W and wears down teams for a late-game sweep, while the latter offers entry hazard removal to ensure Manaphy can maximize its bulk, as well as a check to Raging Bolt.

Stall.description:
• Acid Armor should be used against Ursaluna, Metagross, and Choice Band Hoopa-U.
  • Take Heart is Manaphy's preferred way of boosting its Special Defense, as it allows Manaphy to bypass being burned by Will-O-Wisp + Hex Spectrier sets.
  • Scald's ability to burn can further hinder physical attackers with Swords Dance, such as some Garchomp and Haxorus sets.
  • The HP and Special Defense EVs allow Manaphy to survive Earth Power from Choice Specs Landorus twice after using Take Heart, while the Special Attack EVs allow Manaphy to OHKO it back with with a Take Heart-boosted Scald. The Speed EVs allow Manaphy to outspeed and defeat non-Icy Wind Primarina, and the remaining EVs are invested in Defense.
  • Combined with Acid Armor and Take Heart, Sitrus Berry further enhances Manaphy's ability to safely use these moves against Pokemon like Choice Band Dragapult. After boosting up its defensive stats, Manaphy can start using Scald to KO the foe.
  • Stall Manaphy struggles against strong Electric-type attackers, like Raging Bolt and Zapdos. It also struggles with Taunt and Encore users, such as Corviknight, Iron Valiant, and Alolan Ninetales. Teammates like both Landorus forms, Ursaluna, and Garchomp are appreciated, as they can deal with Electric-types, while teammates like Booster Energy Iron Crown can handle many of the Taunt and Encore users in the tier.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Manaphy may use Energy Ball to hit opposing Water-types that otherwise aren't much affected by its coverage such as Hisuian Samurott. Alluring Voice is an alternative to Ice Beam as coverage for Dragon-types, although if Manaphy forgoes Psychic or Ice Beam, it can no longer hit Water Absorb Clodsire effectively. Manaphy can also use Rest in conjunction with Hydration to increase its longevity tenfold in the face of passive foes. Heavy-Duty Boots allow a more offensive Manaphy spread to safely enter the field successively.

Offensive Setup Sweeper.description:
Manaphy is an incredibly potent wallbreaker for Water teams, making use of the highly coveted Tail Glow in tandem with its great bulk and coverage to blast through bulky Water answers. Ice Beam targets Dragon-types like Dragonite and Roaring Moon and Grass-types like Hydrapple and Sinistcha. Psychic allows Manaphy to break through many Pokemon troublesome for Water teams, such as Toxapex, Amoonguss, and Clodsire. The given defensive EVs let Manaphy use Substitute safely in front of Alolan Muk as well as other passive foes like Toxapex and Blissey. The remaining speed lets Manaphy outpace the likes of Adamant Dragonite and Mamoswine.

Manaphy's wallbreaking powers greatly aid speedy sweepers like Greninja, Urshifu-R, and Swift Swim Pokemon like Barraskewda and Kingdra, which can be slowed down by the aforementioned Water answers like Toxapex and Water Absorb Clodsire as well as other special walls like Articuno. Manaphy appreciates Electric-immune teammates like Swampert and Quagsire, both of which can set up entry hazards to support Manaphy's wallbreaking. Since Ogerpon-W can very easily pivot into Manaphy and pose a huge threat to it and its teammates, offensive checks to it are a necessity for Manaphy to succeed, such as Sludge Wave Greninja, Choice Scarf X-Scissor Hisuian Samurott, and Hurricane Pelipper. In return, Manaphy opens up holes in the opponent's defenses for these faster teammates to clean up late-game. Grass-neutral teammates like Toxapex, Tentacruel, and Ogerpon-W all help shore up Manaphy’s weaknesses as well. Tentacruel provides great hazard control with both Toxic Spikes and Rapid Spin, and with Rain Dish it can stay quite healthy in the Rain. Ogerpon-W outspeeds powerful threats to Manaphy like Landorus and Thundurus-T and can KO them with rain-boosted Ivy Cudgel. Should Manaphy be paired with Drizzle Pelipper, the Rain allows Manaphy's Hydration to shrug off status effects, making it impossible to wear down with poison or slow down with paralysis.

Tail Glow + 3 Attacks.description:
Manaphy is a wallbreaker that can become very threatening thanks to Tail Glow. Manaphy has a great defensive typing and good natural bulk, allowing it to set up on and match up well against Heatran, Landorus-T, and Great Tusk. Manaphy has valuable coverage in Ice Beam, which helps against Dragon-types such as Dragonite, Raging Bolt, and Mega Latios. Manaphy also has access to Psychic, which allows it to better hit Toxapex and Mega Venusaur; this stops the former from using Haze. Manaphy could also choose to run Energy Ball to hit opposing Water-types like Alomomola, Slowbro, and Hisuian Samurott.

Manaphy is a powerful but often unreliable wallbreaker, as it is incredibly reliant on Tail Glow to set up. Manaphy struggles to set up on common Pokemon like Ferrothorn, Haze Toxapex, and Pokemon like Gholdengo, which can status it. In addition, Pokemon with more immediate power, like Zamazenta and Tapu Lele, can stop Manaphy from setting up or easily revenge kill it. This causes Manaphy to function best on hyper offense structures, as partners like Dragonite, Hatterene, and Volcarona break past the aforementioned Pokemon. Manaphy only struggles against Ferrothorn once it is set up, as Ferrothorn can take its boosted attacks comfortably, making Volcarona, Iron Moth, and Zamazenta, all of which can break past Ferrothorn, good teammates. Manaphy specifically thrives on Sticky Web hyper offense teams, thanks to Sticky Web making it harder for faster Pokemon like Tapu Koko or Ogerpon-W to revenge kill it. This means Sticky Web setters like Araquanid and Ribombee are valuable partners. Manaphy can also keep Sticky Web up by threatening common entry hazard removers like Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Moltres. Manaphy is weak to priority from common Pokemon like Kingambit and Raging Bolt. Tapu Lele helps to solve Manaphy’s priority weakness with its Psychic Surge. In return, Manaphy is able to beat Pokemon like Heatran, Gholdengo, and Corviknight that Tapu Lele struggles to break past.

Rain Wallbreaker.description:
Manaphy is an effective wallbreaker on rain teams, using Tail Glow to sharply boost its Special Attack and threaten bulky Pokemon like Alomomola, Toxapex, and Slowbro with a powerful rain-boosted Hydro Vortex. Thanks to Hydration and Rest, it also turns common status users into setup fodder, giving it free turns against defensive staples, such as Toxapex, that would normally cripple it with Toxic. However, despite its power, Manaphy can be difficult to fit on rain teams, which are already strapped for slots and often prioritize speed control, entry hazard removal, or stronger immediate wallbreakers. Psychic allows Manaphy to overwhelm Toxapex and Mega Venusaur without expending its Z-Move. Alternatively, Ice Beam can be used in order to preserve the Z-Move against the likes of Raging Bolt, Mega Latios, and Dragonite. Hydro Vortex is essential to Manaphy's wallbreaking power, allowing it to break through even the bulkiest of Pokemon like Ferrothorn, Galarian Slowking, and Rotom-W after a Tail Glow boost in rain. Modest nature is preferred over Timid to enable valuable damage rolls with Hydro Vortex such as OHKOing Rotom-W after a Tail Glow boost under rain.

Manaphy thrives exclusively on rain teams, where it can fully capitalize on its wallbreaking potential. As a result, rain support from Pelipper is mandatory, as it enables Manaphy to fully utilize Hydration alongside Rest for reliable recovery while significantly boosting Hydro Vortex's power, allowing Manaphy to secure key KOs after a Tail Glow boost against walls like Galarian Slowking and Blissey. Late-game cleaners like Mega Swampert and Barraskewda pair well with Manaphy, taking advantage of it using key checks like Slowbro and Alomomola as setup fodder. Mega Swampert, in particular, is mandatory on rain teams and also serves as a solid Electric-type check. Ferrothorn is a great partner for Manaphy, as it pivots into threats Manaphy struggles against, such as Tapu Koko and Ogerpon-W. Additionally, Ferrothorn supports Manaphy by offering Knock Off to remove key items from walls like Assault Vest Tornadus-T and Toxapex or by spreading Thunder Wave to slow down faster threats such as Mega Lopunny and Ogerpon-W, making it easier for Manaphy to break through. It also provides valuable entry hazard support like Stealth Rock and Spikes, which chips away at teams and helps Manaphy secure more KOs. Manaphy is vulnerable against faster Grass-types such as Kartana, Serperior, Ogerpon-W, and Grassy Glide Rillaboom. Therefore, Zapdos and Archaludon are good partners because of their ability to easily pivot into said Grass-types and threaten them out. In return, Manaphy helps break through bulky Ground-types that might otherwise slow down Zapdos and Archaludon, such as Ting-Lu, Gliscor, and Garchomp.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Level 99 Manaphy is a tempting option, guaranteeing a slower U-turn against opposing standard RegenVest Manaphy, but it is generally not worth having an overall less bulky Manaphy. RegenVest Manaphy can afford to use a different EV spread than the maximized ones here if looking to survive specific rolls. A physically defensive set with 200 Speed EVs may be considered to outspeed and better check Great Tusk, but it is usually not worth losing the slower U-turn or the extra bulk investment. Dazzling Gleam is interchangeable with Alluring Voice; the former checks Throat Chop Roaring Moon, and the latter dissuades setup sweepers and hits Substitute users. Psychic is an option in the final moveslot to dissuade Iron Moth and Pecharunt from switching in while still hitting Zamazenta, whereas Ice Beam can be used to hit Zapdos and Desolate Land Landorus, but the other options are generally considered better. Alternatively, a physically defensive Regenerator set with Rocky Helmet and Take Heart is an option to act as a bulky wincon while still checking physical attackers, but this Manaphy set is easily forced out by special attackers without a boost and may struggle to find setup opportunities. Tail Glow sets may consider running Primordial Sea and Weather Ball for the additional power and being able to hit Desolate Land users, but this set becomes extremely slow and easier to switch around or pressure out. Tail Glow sets can also consider running Scald, trading some damage for additional utility and the chance to burn something before fainting, but the drop in power isn't worth sacrificing for. Hydro Pump is another option on these sets for additional power, notably 3HKOing Empoleon after a Tail Glow boost, but the reduced PP and accuracy is usually not worth it. Alternatively, hyper offense teams can run a potent set with Fluffy, Unaware, or an immunity ability alongside Take Heart, Acid Armor, and Stored Power to muscle through checks like even opposing RegenVest users, Heatran, and Empoleon after enough boosts.

Checks and Counters

Electric-type Moves: Zapdos, Sandy Shocks, and Pokemon with Electric-type moves like Deoxys-S, Latios, and Gholdengo are often able to muscle through non-Motor Drive Manaphy even with an Assault Vest and maximum Special Defense investment.

Desolate Land Users: Aside from Knock Off, most Manaphy sets lack any effective tools against Desolate Land users like Iron Moth, Moltres, and Heatran, giving them free switch-in opportunities to either set up entry hazards or threaten Manaphy with Solar Beam.

Grass-types: Even the most physically defensive Manaphy sets can't reliably deal with Meowscarada or the Ogerpon formes, and Hisuian Electrode is a major annoyance for any spread.

Passive Damage: Without Take Heart, Manaphy is extremely vulnerable to passive damage in the form of Toxic from Iron Moth, Pecharunt, or Mandibuzz. Likewise, Manaphy is worn down extremely quickly by entry hazards set by the likes of Great Tusk, Skarmory, and Scream Tail.

RegenVest.description:
Manaphy leverages a great defensive typing, solid mixed bulk, and incredible utility moves including the coveted Scald to be among the tier's premier RegenVest users. Manaphy is able to comfortably switch in and scout dangerous special attackers like Scream Tail, Azelf, and Gholdengo and, when running the more physically bulky spread, powerful wallbreakers like Chien-Pao, Cinderace, and Great Tusk. Knock Off is notable for threatening decent damage against Gholdengo and removing key items like Assault Vest and Heavy-Duty Boots from would-be switch-ins like opposing Manaphy, Iron Moth, and Moltres. While obviously used for slow pivoting, U-turn is also able to threaten an OHKO on Meowscarada, which would otherwise switch in easily. Alluring Voice is the most common final move for its ability to threaten Latios, Zamazenta, and non-Throat Chop Roaring Moon, but Energy Ball is an option to smack opposing Manaphy, Swampert, and Primarina. An EV spread with full Defense investment is the most common spread, turning Manaphy into a potent mixed wall that can check Cinderace, Great Tusk, and non-Choice Band Roaring Moon while still acting as a solid secondary check to special wallbreakers like Deoxys-S, Primarina, and Gholdengo; it can also choose to run a full Special Defense-invested set to more solidly check these nuclear special attackers.

RegenVest Manaphy is renowned for being able to sturdy up the defensive backbone of almost any team style, but balance and bulky offense teams tend to benefit the most from its presence. Manaphy is excellent at taking hits from powerful wallbreakers like Roaring Moon, Primarina, and Gholdengo and pivoting out with U-turn, so frail wallbreakers like Chien-Pao, Sandy Shocks, and Deoxys-S naturally appreciate its ability to eat a hit then bring them in damage-free. Similarly, Manaphy can be an asset to slower wallbreakers like Gholdengo and Primarina that appreciate its hit-taking capability. Corviknight is the most classic pairing with Manaphy, with both defensive and specially defensive sets able to shore up Manaphy's less-invested stat. If running physically defensive Manaphy, a sturdier check to powerful Choice Band users like Roaring Moon, Zamazenta, and Meowscarada is necessary; consider Skarmory, Great Tusk, or especially Pecharunt as a teammate. Similarly, any RegenVest Manaphy set appreciates a Steel-type special wall like Heatran, Iron Treads, or specially defensive Gholdengo that can help versus threats like Zapdos, Sheer Force Deoxys-S, and Latios. Manaphy is especially vulnerable to getting worn down by entry hazards and being overwhelmed by foes if it loses its Assault Vest, so hazard removers like Iron Treads, Corviknight, and Great Tusk are mandatory teammates, with the latter two doubling as Knock Off absorbers.

Tail Glow.description:
Tail Glow Manaphy is a decent setup sweeper, utilizing Tail Glow to boost its mediocre Special Attack to staggering numbers. Alluring Voice smacks Dragon-types like Roaring Moon and Latios while being Manaphy's best move against Meowscarada. Energy Ball allows Manaphy to beat its Water-type checks in RegenVest Swampert, Primarina, and opposing Manaphy, while Psychic invalidates Desolate Land Iron Moth from being a check. Protosynthesis + Booster Energy grants Manaphy a one-time Speed boost, preventing would-be revenge killers in Roaring Moon, Scream Tail, and Zamazenta from forcing it out. Surge Surfer allows Manaphy to gain a greater Speed boost, allowing it to outspeed even Choice Scarf users like Roaring Moon, Meowscarada, and Azelf while electric terrain is active at the caveat of requiring teammates with Hadron Engine. Electric Seed makes it harder to revenge kill Manaphy when using Surge Surfer, while Life Orb boosts Manaphy's damage output. Motor Drive allows Manaphy to surprise and turn the tables on Electric-types like Sandy Shocks and Regieleki and gain a free Speed boost, trading in consistency for the potential of multiple activations and defensive utility.

Tail Glow Manaphy fits best on hyper offensive teams due to their nature of being fast-paced and possessing strong setup sweepers. Although Manaphy has immense damage potential, it is unable to muscle past counters like RegenVest Hisuian Goodra, Desolate Land Heatran, and if not using Psychic, Iron Moth. Thus, teammates who can threaten them and use them as setup fodder pair well with Manaphy, making IronPress Zamazenta, Dragon Dance Roaring Moon, and Double Dance Iron Crown good partners. Manaphy also appreciates dedicated leads that hyper offense teams employ, like Ribombee and Dual Screens Corviknight; the former shutting down revenge killing attempts from foes like Choice Scarf Roaring Moon and Azelf, which would outspeed Manaphy even after a Speed boost, and the latter allowing Manaphy to set up safely, allowing it to brute force its way through the opposing team. When using Surge Surfer, Manaphy should always be paired with teammates that use Hadron Engine like Sandy Shocks and Latios.

Choice Specs.description:
• Darkrai uses its high Speed and Special Attack with its vast movepool to blast through a wide range of opposing Pokemon.
  • Dark Pulse is Darkrai's most consistent move, beating Pokemon such as non-Assault Vest Metagross, Pecharunt, Cresselia, and non-specially defensive Iron Crown, with the added benefit of a flinch chance.
  • Ice Beam lets Darkrai defeat Landorus-T, non-Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Garchomp, and Zapdos.
  • Thunder is Darkrai's best option against Corviknight, Urshifu-R, Manaphy, and non-Assault Vest Volcanion.
  • Focus Blast helps Darkrai against non-Choice Scarf Kyurem, Zarude, Roaring Moon, and non-Choice Scarf Porygon-Z.
  • Sludge Bomb assists versus non-specially defensive Ogerpon-W, Whimsicott, and non-Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant.
  • 4 Special Defense EVs give Darkrai slightly better odds against a Hyper Beam from Life Orb Spectrier.
  • Darkrai struggles to break through specially bulky Steel-, Fairy-, and Dragon-types, like Hisuian Goodra and Sylveon, even when it is using super effective moves. Pokemon that beat these, such as Landorus-T, Sneasler, and Corviknight, are robust partners.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dark

Choice Specs makes Darkrai a threatening wallbreaker, aiding Dark teams against Fighting, Fairy, Steel, and opposing Dark matchups with Psychic, Sludge Bomb, and Focus Blast. However, it's susceptible to being revenge killed by faster threats like Dragapult and Choice Scarf users like Sneasler, Iron Valiant, and Enamorus, so partners like Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Greninja are a necessity.

Nasty Plot

Darkrai can opt to use Sludge Bomb or Psychic over the second coverage move, with Sludge Bomb dealing with Iron Valiant and Ogerpon formes and Psychic blasting Toxapex, Iron Hands, and Iron Valiant, all of which are troublesome for Dark teams. However, these coverage moves are quite niche and other teammates like Greninja and Hoopa-U can be used to handle these threats instead.

Bulkyrai (Bulky Darkrai).description:
Opting for a bulkier spread overall enables Darkrai to stick around far longer, letting Darkrai cripple physical attackers attempting to handle it and its teammates while still remaining a capable threat with Nasty Plot and Dark Pulse. Will-O-Wisp takes would-be problematic threats for Dark such as opposing Meowscarada and Corviknight and cripples their ability to apply pressure. For its last option, Darkrai has plenty of tools: after a Nasty Plot, Focus Blast rips through the likes of Hisuian Goodra and Ting-Lu; Thunder easily fells Corviknight and Toxapex; and Ice Beam can apply strong pressure against the Landorus formes and Clodsire. The EV spread used enables Darkrai to tank a Body Press from Skarmory and Archaludon along with a Play Rough from Choice Scarf Meowscarada and respond with a Will-O-Wisp, and it lets Darkrai still outspeed non-Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Torandus-T. Leftovers can provide Darkrai with some stability while setting up, while Heavy-Duty Boots grants Darkrai safe entry, as Dark lacks good entry hazard removal.

With its decrease in immediate damage, Darkrai greatly appreciates entry hazard support from the likes of Ting-Lu and Hisuian Samurott to pressure foes it cannot break past as reliably such as Hoopa-U and Unaware Clodsire. Ting-Lu also is a strong special wall capable of handling foes like Raging Bolt and Terapagos. Swords Dance Hisuian Samurott can pick off special walls such as Blissey and Articuno along with being able to use Sucker Punch to deal with Flutter Mane after a boost. Mandibuzz can come in on Choice Scarf Fighting-types such as Sneasler and Urshifu-R alongside using U-turn to safely bring in Darkrai and providing Defog support if it opts to run Leftovers. Choice Scarf Meowscarada provides essential speed control, taking out threats such as opposing Darkrai and Iron Valiant with Play Rough, while checking Primarina and Ting-Lu with Flower Trick. Choice Specs Greninja can eliminate Fire-types looking to absorb Will-O-Wisp such as Volcarona and Moltres while also being able to use Extrasensory to threaten Fighting-types like Iron Valiant and Iron Hands. Alolan Muk can handle problematic Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Hatterene along with removing Choice Scarf with Knock Off from threats like Meowscarada and Latios. Mixed and physical Hoopa-U variants can provide solid Knock Off support along with being able to handle Fighting-types such as Gallade and Okidogi.

Choice Scarf (Dark).description:
Choice Scarf Darkrai is an incredible revenge killer for Dark teams due to its colorful coverage options and an incredible Speed stat, allowing it to outspeed common Choice Scarf users like Meowscarada, Iron Boulder, Sneasler, and Greninja. Sludge Bomb is a crucial coverage move, threatening Fairy-types like Iron Valiant, Hatterene, and Primarina while also hitting the Ogerpon formes. Psychic lets Darkrai handle Fighting-types like Sneasler, Urshifu-R, and Okidogi, while Ice Beam deals with Ground- and Dragon-types like the Landorus formes, Garchomp, and Dragonite. Trick lets Darkrai hinder walls like Clodsire, Corviknight, and Ting-Lu, which switch into it. Alternatively, Focus Blast targets Dark- and Steel-types like Bisharp, Roaring Moon, Archaludon, and Heatran.

Physical attackers like Weavile, Meowscarada, and Roaring Moon can eliminate special walls like Clodsire, Swampert, and Hisuian Goodra; Choice Specs Greninja can also weaken foes like Archaludon, Corviknight, and Toxapex as well as aid against Fighting- and Fairy-types with Extrasensory and Sludge Wave, respectively, allowing Darkrai to clean up late-game. In return, Darkrai can deal with faster threats like non-Choice Scarf Dragapult and common Choice Scarf users like Iron Valiant, Meowscarada, and Sneasler that threaten them. Alolan Muk and Bisharp threaten Fairy-types like Flutter Mane, Clefable, and Primarina, while Darkrai can handle Ground-types such as the Landorus formes, Hippowdon, and Gliscor with Ice Beam. Sableye provides a Fighting immunity and can cripple foes like Zamazenta, Iron Hands, and Gallade with Will-O-Wisp. Ting-Lu is a great partner, setting entry hazards, wearing down bulky foes, and enabling Darkrai to OHKO threats like Hydreigon, Kyurem, Great Tusk, and Enamorus. Mandibuzz provides entry hazard removal and safe entry to Darkrai using U-turn, along with checking threats such as Scizor and Belly Drum Azumarill.

Nasty Plot.description:
Darkrai, with its access to Nasty Plot, great offensive stats, and a colorful coverage pool, makes for a very threatening wallbreaker, being faster than threats like the Ogerpon formes, Meowscarada, and Tornadus-T. Darkrai's remaining moves, aside from Dark Pulse, depend on the matchups it wants to excel in. Ice Beam and Focus Blast provide the best general coverage, letting Darkrai heavily pressure Dark, Water, Dragon, and Steel teams. Focus Blast breaks through special walls such as Ting-Lu, Empoleon, and Hisuian Goodra. Ice Beam is nearly mandatory, as it OHKOes Gliscor and Assault Vest Tornadus-T at +2 after Stealth Rock damage and 2HKOes Clodsire at +2. Thunder can be used over Focus Blast, as this lets Darkrai pressure bulkier Flying teams. At +2, it nearly OHKOes Articuno and OHKOes Corviknight while also being able to OHKO Empoleon and Toxapex. Hypnosis temporarily incapacitates checks like Hisuian Goodra, Alolan Muk, and Assault Vest Iron Hands, providing Darkrai with more room to set up or a safe switch in for teammates that deal with these threats, but it has worse accuracy than Darkrai's other moves. Heavy-Duty Boots is preferred, as it allows Darkrai to come in more freely against Steel, Dark, and Flying teams, which usually set multiple entry hazards.

Greninja and Meowscarada make a fantastic offensive core when paired with Darkrai. Either threat can use multiple sets to complement Darkrai's chosen coverage. Choice Specs Greninja deals with Fighting-, Fairy-, and Grass-types like Iron Hands, Primarina, and Ogerpon-W with its coverage, while Choice Band Meowscarada obliterates Flying and Water teams after minimal chip damage from their other teammates. Alternatively, Choice Scarf Meowscarada is able to revenge kill faster threats such as Dragapult, Choice Scarf Gholdengo, and opposing Choice Scarf Greninja, while Choice Scarf Greninja cleans up Flying and Dragon teams after Darkrai has eliminated Articuno and Hisuian Goodra. Hisuian Samurott greatly helps the Dragon matchup through its coverage and access to priority, which lets it remove Hisuian Goodra and Dragapult, respectively, and it sets Spikes to chip down walls like Hisuian Goodra and Ting-Lu for Darkrai to OHKO late-game. In return, Darkrai removes Archaludon, Moltres, and Toxapex. Mandibuzz is a Ground-immune teammate that checks faster physical threats such as Choice Scarf Sneasler and Sand Rush Excadrill and provides slow pivoting with U-turn. Ting-Lu is able to switch into strong special attackers such as Choice Scarf Flutter Mane, Enamorus, and Hatterene while threatening them back with Heavy Slam; it is also able to set a wide array of entry hazards, which makes Darkrai's job of wallbreaking or sweeping easier. Hoopa-U is a mixed wallbreaker that complements Darkrai by dealing with walls like Toxapex, Hisuian Goodra, and Iron Hands that Darkrai struggles with without the correct coverage. Darkrai threatens annoying U-turn users such as Corviknight, Tornadus-T, and Cinderace that hinder Hoopa-U. Sableye and Alolan Muk are also plausible defensive teammates, as Sableye is able to wear down specially defensive Pokemon such as Clodsire and Corviknight with access to Knock Off and Will-O-Wisp while also being able to use Encore against threatening setup sweepers such as Volcarona and Iron Hands, all while providing an invaluable Fighting immunity. Alolan Muk can switch into Fairy-type attacks while also providing further utility with Knock Off and Poison Touch. Swords Dance Bisharp provides useful resistances, is immune to Toxic, and deals with Fairy- and Poison-types like Hatterene and Alolan Muk, and in return, Darkrai removes Moltres and Archaludon, both of which check Bisharp

Utility (HP).description:
Darkrai functions as an extremely fast utility Pokemon that becomes deceptively bulky when supplemented with an HP donation. Ice Beam offers excellent coverage, pressuring targets such as Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Eternatus. Will-O-Wisp allows Darkrai to cripple physical attackers such as Ogerpon-W and Hisuian Samurott before they move, while also wearing down bulky switch-ins such as Ting-Lu over time. Knock Off removes crucial items, especially Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots, from the likes of Clefable and Ho-Oh. Leftovers is essential for longevity, letting Darkrai consistently pivot into threats over the course of longer games, while Tera Ghost flips Darkrai's Fighting weakness, grants it an immunity to Extreme Speed, and allows it to spinblock in a pinch.

Darkrai is highly flexible, fitting onto nearly any team structure, and can do so without even revealing its set during team preview. Although almost any sort of HP donation is beneficial, higher HP stats such as those of Arceus-Ghost and Eternatus are typically always preferred. Because of Darkrai's lack of Heavy-Duty Boots and reliable recovery, it is prone to chip damage over time from entry hazards. Thus, it strongly appreciates hazard control from teammates like Magic Bounce Hatterene and Rapid Spin Great Tusk. Additionally, Darkrai pairs well with Fairy- and Fighting-resistant Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking and Clodsire, which help cover Darkrai’s weaknesses. Furthermore, Darkrai's ability to cripple foes through removing items and burn allows it to synergize extremely well with teammates like Clodsire and Calm Mind Arceus-Ghost.

Nasty Plot.description:
Darkrai is an excellent wallbreaker and cleaner, gaining many opportunities to use Nasty Plot due to its amazing base Speed and a diverse coverage movepool backed up with a good Special Attack stat and enough bulk to set up against passive Pokemon. Sludge Bomb hits Fairy-types like Clefable, Iron Valiant, Primarina, and Enamorus as well as Pokemon that commonly use Tera Fairy like Gholdengo and Garganacl. Ice Beam hits Dragon- and Ground-type Pokemon like Raging Bolt, Dragonite, Gliscor, and Great Tusk that can take its Dark Pulse. Focus Blast tears through Dark-types like Ting-Lu, Kingambit, and Hisuian Samurott, hitting the former harder than Ice Beam. Psyshock can be used to hit Blissey and Clodsire hard, improving its matchup against stall teams. Will-O-Wisp can be used to completely neuter Kingambit, even bypassing its Sucker Punch, as well as other offensive threats it can't immediately OHKO, like Terastallized Ogerpon-W. Leftovers give it general longevity and fits better on teams with entry hazard removal, but Heavy-Duty Boots can be used on teams that lack it. More offensive teams can opt for the power of Life Orb to wallbreak more easily, opening up fellow setup sweepers to clean late-game. Expert Belt is a niche alternative as a boosting item that makes use of Darkrai's ability to hit most of the metagame for super effective damage with its coverage moves, letting it pressure checks like Ting-Lu and Clefable more easily without cutting into its longevity. Tera Poison boosts Darkrai's Sludge Bomb and allows it to avoid revenge killing attempts from Iron Valiant and Zamazenta thanks to the Fairy- and Fighting-type resistances it gains. Tera Ghost is a niche option that gives a full immunity to Zamazenta's Fighting-type moves and is helpful to prevent Dragonite from revenge killing Darkrai with Extreme Speed. Tera Fighting can also be used to power up Focus Blast to extreme levels of power to become Darkrai's strongest viable move, notably being able to OHKO Ting-Lu at +2 after Stealth Rock.

Darkrai's wallbreaking capabilities are useful on offensively oriented teams, having strong synergies with other Dark-types like Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit and other special attackers like Raging Bolt and Dragapult. Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit pair with Darkrai to overwhelm or lure shared checks like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant while gaining opportunities to wallbreak by switching into each other's counters. Darkrai's Bad Dreams punishes Dondozo's Rest, further enhancing its synergy with Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott as well as other physical attackers like Zamazenta, as switching into Darkrai as Dondozo comes in to wall them will result in Bad Dreams chip without burning a sleep turn. Raging Bolt and Dragapult appreciate Darkrai's ability to break through balance teams, tearing through walls like Ting-Lu and Galarian Slowking, while mixed Dragapult and Raging Bolt, especially with Taunt, can help break through Clodsire. Dragapult provides a stop to Zamazenta and punishes Kingambit with Will-O-Wisp if Darkrai isn't running Focus Blast. Darkrai appreciates support from entry hazard setters like Hisuian Samurott, Landorus-T, and Glimmora, as their hazards, especially Spikes, make Darkrai much more threatening, wearing down switch-ins like Zamazenta, Ting-Lu, and Heatran. Darkrai heavily pressures hazard removers like Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Cinderace.
