Hisuian Samurott and Landorus-T in particular have deeper synergy with Darkrai; Hisuian Samurott wears down Primarina, switches into Darkrai checks like Blissey and Clodsire to set up Spikes on forced switches, and can use Flip Turn to safely bring in Darkrai on physically defensive Pokemon like Corviknight, Dondozo, and Alomomola to gain free turns. Landorus-T is an excellent physical blanket check and can switch into threatening Fighting-types like Zamazenta and Booster Energy Great Tusk that can threaten Darkrai, and it can use U-turn to bring in Darkrai safely on Pokemon like Gliscor and opposing Landorus-T. Gholdengo is an excellent teammate due to it providing a check to Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Enamorus while being able to counter most Zamazenta variants if running a physically defensive set. Rillaboom can threaten answers to Darkrai like Primarina, Ting-Lu, and Clodsire while being able to pivot Darkrai in on Pokemon like defensive Gholdengo, Skarmory, and Corviknight to keep up momentum. Assault Vest Primarina is an excellent partner that blanket checks many special attackers including Iron Valiant and Deoxys-S, pivots Darkrai in on its checks like Galarian Slowking, and pressures shared walls such as Blissey and Terastallized Clodsire for Darkrai to break through.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Darkrai, owing to its already impressive Speed stat, is one of the more consistent revenge killers and an outstanding piece of speed control. Outspeeding the entirety of OU's metagame, it can threaten Deoxys-S and Dragapult as well as boosted threats like Dragonite, Iron Valiant, and Iron Moth. Trick allows Darkrai to incapacitate a sweeper, like Dragonite and Hatterene, or a wall, like Clodsire and Blissey, long-term and grants it the flexibility of being able to switch moves when the extra Speed isn't needed, such as against bulkier teams. Ice Beam effectively nails many foes like Great Tusk, Gliscor, Dragonite, and Ting-Lu. Sludge Bomb threatens Fairy-types like Enamorus, Iron Valiant, Primarina, and Clefable. Will-O-Wisp can be used to permanently cripple foes like Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and even faster threats like Zamazenta and +1 Dragonite. Tera Ghost, especially for Will-O-Wisp variants, lets it more reliably emergency check and either revenge kill or shut down boosted Extreme Speed Dragonite and IronPress Zamazenta. Tera Poison is used to resist the many Fairy-types' Moonblast and Zamazenta's STAB moves as well as strengthening Sludge Bomb's damage output. Alternatively, Tera Dark gives its STAB Dark Pulse an easier time to clean up weakened teams.

Darkrai fits best on offensive teams that necessitate its revenge killing talents. It’s important to note that Darkrai actually has issues revenge killing as a result of Terastallization, with many usually clean revenge kills being complicated by this mechanic. This issue is only compounded by the fact that all of Darkrai’s moves all have common switch-ins, so it’s very important to have other answers to the Pokemon Darkrai aims to revenge kill. As a result, Primarina is a solid partner, with its typing and firepower being able to check switch-ins to Dark Pulse like Iron Valiant, Enamorous, and Heatran, safely scout for potential Terastallizations against them, and provide momentum with Flip Turn. Landorus-T is similarly a good partner, with its ability to check physical attackers that Darkrai can't safely revenge kill in the event of Terastallization, such as Dragonite and Great Tusk; it also provides momentum with U-turn and helps put Darkrai's victims into range of its attacks with Stealth Rock. Additionally, it can disrupt many of Darkrai's switch-ins with Taunt, like Ting-Lu, Clodsire, and Blissey. On the topic of entry hazards, Great Tusk and Cinderace are also good partners, as they provide hazard control that is seriously appreciated by Darkrai, which otherwise will get chipped down as it switches in and out of the field to apply pressure. Great Tusk checks many priority users that would otherwise deny Darkrai its ability to revenge kill, such as Kingambit, Raging Bolt, and Dragonite. It also can pressure Clodsire, Ting-Lu, and Garganacl, denying their hazards and threatening them with significant damage that prevents them from switching into Darkrai. Cinderace is effective as a result of its ability to remove entry hazards with Court Change and spread burns to Pokemon that could otherwise outpace Darkrai, such as Rillaboom and Dragonite, while its U-turn dents Hisuian Samurott. Dragapult is also a great partner due to its anti-offensive nature, with its speedy Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave allowing it to be Darkrai's fallback line in the event of an unexpected Tera. It handles many switch-ins like Rillaboom, the Ogerpon formes, and Zamazenta by debilitating them with status and providing pivoting with U-turn. Dragapult can also deconstruct stall, which Darkrai matches up poorly into. Kingambit also loves Darkrai's ability to outpace Iron Valiant, as Darkrai opens up Kingambit late-game by KOing or at least forcing chip damage on key targets, putting them in range of Sucker Punch. Furthermore, Darkrai can also cripple physical walls like Dondozo and Skarmory with Trick, while Darkrai enjoys Kingambit's Sucker Punch putting targets in range of its attacks and Iron Head eliminating Clefable and Primarina. Raging Bolt is an effective partner, as Darkrai's ability to use Trick and shut down special walls like Blissey, Skeledirge, and Clodsire is great for opening it up against bulkier teams. Darkrai's coverage in Focus Blast can help simplify Raging Bolt's endgame, as it pressures Ting-Lu and Kingambit, notably simplifying the mindgames between it and Kingambit, while Ice Beam can also help eliminate Ground-types like Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Gliscor for it to use Thunderclap late-game.

Choice Specs.description:
With Choice Specs, Darkrai can boost its already excellent Special Attack and fantastic Speed tier to become an immediately devastating wallbreaker, further taking advantage of its coverage movepool while still potentially having the utility Trick. Sludge Bomb helps to shred Fairy-types and common Tera Fairy users like Clefable, Primarina, Gholdengo, and Garganacl that would switch into Darkrai’s deadly Dark Pulse while still capable of putting foes like Ting-Lu looking to switch into the move on a timer. Focus Blast tears through Dark-types like Kingambit, Tyranitar, Hisuian Samurott, and Ting-Lu, even 2HKOing the latter, and 2HKOes Tinkaton. Ice Beam tears through the likes of Dragonite, Great Tusk, and Gliscor and has solid odds to 2HKO Clodsire while also hitting other common foes like Raging Bolt and Tornadus-T, especially Assault Vest variants. Either of these coverage moves can be eschewed for Trick, trading a coverage option for the ability to cripple a would-be wall or setup sweeper like Blissey or Terastallized Dragonite and thus allowing Darkrai to freely switch up its moves in matchups where the added power is not needed. Tera Dark can be used to take advantage of Darkrai's tendency to spam and be Choice-locked into Dark Pulse, powering up the move to overwhelm even neutral walls like Garganacl and Terastallized Galarian Slowking. Tera Poison doubles as a defensive Tera type to let Darkrai tank Fighting- and Fairy-type moves like Zamazenta’s Close Combat and Enamorus’s Moonblast while also crucially powering up Sludge Bomb.

Choice Specs Darkrai fits best on bulky offense and balance teams looking for a strong wallbreaker that can still outspeed most offensive threats like Ogerpon-W and Cinderace. Darkrai appreciates slow pivots like Alomomola, Galarian Slowking, Corviknight, Moltres, and Pecharunt that can bring it in easily and give it more entry points to wallbreak. These Pokemon also help form a strong defensive backbone to answer foes that could benefit from whatever move Darkrai is locked into to set up or revenge kill, with Pecharunt and Galarian Slowking helping with Zamazenta and Iron Valiant. Galarian Slowking, in particular, also helps with Primarina and Enamorus, while Moltres helps with Kingambit. Even with Darkrai’s coverage options and power, Ting-Lu still poses a large threat, forcing it to rely more on predictions rather than spamming Dark Pulse, so Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom that can switch into Ting-Lu and threaten it help in that regard. Darkrai also helps physical attackers like the aforementioned Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom, as well as Dragonite and Zamazenta, by blowing past physical walls like Pecharunt and bulky Gholdengo. Gholdengo is a great partner that can help overwhelm shared checks like Ting-Lu and Kingambit. It can also switch into and threaten Zamazenta and Iron Valiant, both of which are great at revenge killing Darkrai. With its Choice Scarf set, Gholdengo can cripple walls like Blissey with Trick and outspeed threats that naturally outpace Darkrai, such as Dragapult and Zamazenta. Darkrai’s lack of Heavy-Duty Boots allows it to be chipped down easily by entry hazards, so hazard removal options like Great Tusk, Galarian Weezing, Cinderace, and Iron Treads are paramount.

All-Out Attacker.description:
Leveraging its high Speed, impressive power, and access to a wide range of offensive coverage moves, Darkrai is able to thrive in OU as a powerful wallbreaker. Ice Beam lets Darkrai OHKO Gliscor while being its strongest option against Great Tusk, Raging Bolt, and Dragonite. Sludge Bomb complements Darkrai's STAB Dark Pulse by targeting Fairy-types like Clefable, Primarina, and Hatterene while also giving Darkrai powerful coverage into Ogerpon-W. Focus Blast enhances Darkrai's coverage further by targeting bulky Dark-types like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott. Darkrai can also become a mixed attacker by going for Knock Off + Sucker Punch; Knock Off can provide fantastic support by removing Heavy-Duty Boots and Assault Vest from switch-ins like Blissey, Alomomola, and Tornadus-T, while Sucker Punch can pick off foes like Dragapult and Deoxys-S as well as other weakened ones like Iron Moth and Walking Wake that can otherwise revenge kill Darkrai. This variant should run Black Glasses + Tera Dark to propel all of its Dark-type moves to higher levels. Life Orb is a fantastic option that bolsters Darkrai's power even further, giving it a clean 2HKO on Corviknight after Stealth Rock along with OHKOs on max HP Great Tusk with Ice Beam and Ogerpon-W with Sludge Bomb after any entry hazard chip; with Life Orb, 29 HP IVs can be used to minimize recoil. Alternatively, Expert Belt takes advantage of Darkrai's excellent coverage without sacrificing its longevity, maintaining OHKOs on offensive Gholdengo and Enamorus. Tera Poison boosts Sludge Bomb's damage and flips Darkrai's Fighting- and Fairy-type weaknesses into resistances, allowing it to take hits from Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, and Choice Scarf Enamorus if necessary, as well as granting it a resistance to Rillaboom's Grassy Glide. Tera Ghost gives an outright immunity to Zamazenta's Fighting-type moves and blocks Extreme Speed Dragonite from picking Darkrai off. Tera Fighting can instead be considered to increase the power of Darkrai's Focus Blast to monstrous levels at the expense of not granting much defensive value; Tera-boosted Focus Blast allows Expert Belt Darkrai to 2HKO even Ting-Lu, and grants Life Orb Darkrai a roll in its favor to 2HKO Blissey. A spread of 4 Atk / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with a Naive nature is used on Knock Off + Sucker Punch variants, and it is chosen over Hasty to minimize damage from common priority moves like Dragonite's Extreme Speed and Rillaboom's Grassy Glide.

Darkrai provides a huge amount of value to offense teams that appreciate its high Speed along with its ability to threaten Galarian Slowking, though even slower, more balanced teams can still find value in its ability to threaten a significant proportion of the tier and force switches to take advantage of entry hazards. Landorus-T is a strong partner that can not only set Stealth Rock but is also able to switch in on threats to Darkrai like Zamazenta and help to offset Darkrai's relative frailty by bringing it in safely with U-turn. Similarly, Gliscor makes a good pairing on bulkier structures with its ability to come in on both Zamazenta and Clodsire. As Darkrai typically makes its home on more offensive builds, partners that can handle Darkrai's checks without being momentum sinks are much appreciated; Assault Vest Primarina forms a great core with Darkrai, able to switch in on Iron Valiant and Enamorus and force them out. Primarina also appreciates Darkrai threatening Galarian Slowking. Offensively, special attackers like Iron Valiant and Raging Bolt that can help to overload shared checks like Clodsire and Blissey make great partners. Darkrai doesn't only work with special overload, though; Dark-type spam teams benefit greatly from Darkrai pressuring and being able to deal heavy damage to threats like Clefable, Ting-Lu, and Primarina, allowing for threats like Hisuian Samurott to later break through. In return, Hisuian Samurott and other Dark-type attackers like Kingambit are able to weaken Zamazenta for Darkrai while also being able to take advantage of Darkrai's more passive switch-ins like Clodsire and Blissey; Ogerpon-W is another powerful partner that can force damage onto Zamazenta and turn passive walls into setup fodder. Hisuian Samurott is another partner that benefits from this support in overloading shared checks while also setting up Spikes, which Darkrai appreciates greatly. Particularly when opting not to run Heavy-Duty Boots, Darkrai appreciates hazard removal to give it more turns on the field; Great Tusk is a natural pick that is also able to pressure Zamazenta and can invite in Iron Valiant to burn its Booster Energy. Another partner that can help Darkrai both defensively and offensively is Gholdengo, as Gholdengo can switch in on Fighting- and Fairy-type attacks from Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, and Clefable while Gholdengo in turn appreciates Darkrai's ability to weaken or eliminate opposing Dark-types like Ting-Lu, Kingambit, and Hisuian Samurott. Bulkier teams can opt to pair Galarian Slowking with Darkrai with its ability to pivot around Enamorus, Iron Valiant, and Zamazenta, and the Future Sight support it provides turns Darkrai into a devastating threat that Clodsire cannot switch into and Zamazenta cannot safely force out.

Extreme Killer.description:
• With its sheer power, decent bulk, and solid movepool options, Arceus defines itself as one of the tier's most devastating setup sweepers, wallbreakers, and revenge killers. Terastalization, whether it be Normal or Ghost, makes Arceus even more difficult to answer for balance and bulky offense teams due to either its extreme power or improved trading capabilities with would-be revenge killers. Due to it not requiring specific support to function effectively, it is a staple for various hyper offense structures that appreciate a bulky setup sweeper that works well against opposing hyper offense teams.

  • Extreme Speed lets Arceus clean through weakened teams, since not many viable Pokemon resist or are immune to it. Combined with Swords Dance, Arceus can clean up the majority of the offensive metagame, including threats such as Eternatus, Ultra Necrozma, and Sucker Punch Yveltal. Shadow Claw synergizes perfectly with Extreme Speed, hitting Ghost-types such as Giratina-O, Marshadow, and Lunala, which are immune to Extreme Speed, and preventing them being reliable checks to Arceus.

  • Double-Edge makes the most out of the limited number of foes that can switch into Normal-type moves to enhance Arceus's wallbreaking capabilities. It is able to OHKO defensive Ho-Oh and defensive Primal Kyogre after a boost. With Tera Normal, it can also OHKO Coil Zygarde at +2, preventing it from being a consistent check.

  • Taunt denies status conditions from Giratina-O, Alomomola, and support Arceus formes as well as opposing setup from slower foes such as Coil Zygarde and IronPress Garganacl. It has good merit for hyper offense teams too, denying Defog from Ho-Oh and the aforementioned Giratina-O.

  • Recover is a niche option that lets Arceus shrug off attacks, such as Giratina-O's Draco Meteor, Choice Specs Lunala's Moonblast, and support Arceus's Judgment; it notably let Arceus beat Thunder Wave variants of Giratina-O due to its Special Attack drops. However, Arceus is usually better off just attacking instead of using Recover, especially compared to the usefulness of Taunt.

  • Earthquake is another niche option for Sticky Web teams over Double-Edge or Taunt, letting Arceus OHKO Zacian-C after a boost while hitting Garganacl. However, this is very specific because +2 Tera Normal Double-Edge has a roll to OHKO the former, even if Earthquake is better for Tera Ghost variants that do not use Double-Edge.

  • Silk Scarf gives Arceus a consistent damage output to Extreme Speed and Double-Edge that doesn't suffer from the recoil issues of Life Orb, giving Arceus improved longevity while still letting it OHKO offensive Primal Kyogre and Rayquaza with Extreme Speed after a boost.

  • Alternatively, Life Orb maximizes Arceus's offensive capabilities, allowing it to OHKO offensive Eternatus and offensive Ho-Oh after a boost. Unlike Silk Scarf, it improves the power of Shadow Claw as well, notably letting Arceus OHKO Giratina-O and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM with +2 Tera Ghost Shadow Claw. However, the recoil hinders Arceus's longevity significantly, making it less capable of trading with other offensive threats, since it often faints itself from recoil.

  • Lum Berry can also be considered, since it enables easier setup against Ho-Oh, Alomomola, and Giratina-O. Unfortunately, it is too matchup-dependent, and the drop in power is very noticeable, making Arceus less threatening as a whole.

  • The first EV spread lets Arceus outspeed Adamant Kyurem-B as well as Marshadow and Zacian-C after Sticky Web. The rest is dumped into bulk, notably letting Arceus survive Mega Salamence's boosted Double-Edge from full HP. The second EV spread lets Arceus outspeed Chi-Yu while having enough bulk to survive Primal Kyogre's Origin Pulse and Life Orb Deoxys-A's Psycho Boost from full HP.

  • Tera Normal allows boosted Arceus to OHKO Double Dance Primal Groudon with Extreme Speed after Stealth Rock damage, as well as OHKOing defensive Yveltal and offensive Eternatus. It also empowers Double-Edge, letting it OHKO Zygarde and defensive Primal Groudon at +2 while even having a chance to 2HKO Dondozo. However, it lacks any defensive qualities unlike Tera Ghost and makes Giratina-O and Marshadow more difficult to handle, limiting its use to Sticky Web teams where Marshadow is no longer an issue.

  • Tera Ghost forces Marshadow to play a coinflip between its STAB moves, making Arceus more challenging to punish. It completely shuts down revenge killing attempts from Close Combat Zacian-C, Ditto, and Rayquaza. Offensively, it empowers Shadow Claw, notably letting boosted Arceus OHKO Choice Specs Lunala with Shadow Shield up as well as Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM with Life Orb.

  • Arceus lacks any notable defensive qualities outside of its raw bulk, limiting it just to hyper offense structures that want to capitalize on its fabulous wallbreaking and cleaning abilities. Depending on the moveset, Terastalization option, and opposing team structure, Arceus fluctuates between these two roles.

  • Double-Edge variants of Arceus are more suited to the early- or mid game where it can break through Pokemon such as defensive Ho-Oh and Coil Zygarde for teammates to profit from, especially since its poor longevity makes it difficult to trade with opposing offensive Pokemon or act as a sufficient sweeper.

  • Yveltal is a fantastic partner for Arceus, since it is able to threaten common checks to Arceus, such as Giratina-O, Zygarde, and Ferrothorn, while still being great at breaking past other physical walls such as defensive Primal Groudon and defensive Arceus-Dark. In return, Arceus helps break past specially defensive Pokemon such as Arceus-Fairy, Ho-Oh, and Fezandipiti. They are both capable of overwhelming a shared check in Zacian-C, with other offensive teammates such as Primal Groudon handling that further.

  • Zacian-C itself is a good partner, since it helps Arceus to overwhelm physical walls such as defensive Primal Groudon and Tera Water Zygarde. Zacian-C can help break through Giratina-O, similarly to Yveltal, as well as helping against opposing Arceus and Ditto attempting to revenge kill Arceus. They can both overwhelm a shared check in Necrozma-DM too.

  • Arceus fails to do anything meaningful against stall teams, since both Dondozo and Giratina shut it down with ease. On structures utilizing Sticky Web, Chi-Yu is a fantastic wallbreaker for Arceus, since it notably shreds through stall with its boosted attacks while still beating opposing Ghost-types such as Lunala and Giratina-O. It can even lure in and remove defensive Ho-Oh with +2 Black Hole Eclipse, letting Arceus clean through opposing teams more smoothly. Chi-Yu's fast Taunt helps maintain entry hazards for Arceus too, especially against Giratina-O.

  • Meteor Beam Lunala and Eternatus are very similar when it comes to wallbreaking, letting Arceus clean up better afterwards. Ultra Necrozma appreciates Arceus breaking past both Arceus-Dark and Yveltal, while it can blow through Necrozma-DM and Primal Groudon with Earthquake.

  • Suicide leads such as Deoxys-S and Glimmora provide entry hazards for Arceus to break through teams more easily, notably guaranteeing the OHKO on defensive Primal Groudon with +2 Tera Normal Double-Edge and letting Arceus more reliably OHKO Lunala with Shadow Claw once Shadow Shield is removed. Sticky Web support from Smeargle and Shuckle enables Arceus to outspeed foes such as Marshadow and Zacian-C, that would ordinarily revenge kill it.

  • These leads appreciate Arceus using Taunt to maintain their hazards. It should be noted that, barring Shuckle, they can prevent opposing hazards from going up, improving Arceus's longevity, which is especially important for Life Orb or Double-Edge variants.

Trick Room Setter.description:
• Due to its excellent bulk and Normal typing, Arceus is an excellent Trick Room setter. These qualities combined with a Mental Herb make it extremely difficult for threats such as Primal Kyogre, Zacian-C, and even Marshadow to stop Trick Room from being set up. Arceus also serves as a weak but useful revenge killler that can take out extremely chipped threats such as Primal Groudon and Yveltal with Extreme Speed.

  • Taunt prevents slow entry hazard setters such as Ferrothorn and Primal Groudon from setting hazards. It also prevents threats such as Necrozma-DM and, most importantly, Coil Zygarde from setting up or hindering it with Thunder Wave or Glare. In addition, Taunt prevents Ho-Oh from using Whirlwind to cancel Trick Room or from using Defog to remove entry hazards.

  • Extreme Speed allows Arceus to revenge kill any weakened targets that a teammate wasn’t able to finish off such as a defensive Primal Groudon; however, the lack of Attack investment makes Extreme Speed extremely weak, so the move should not be used often.

  • The given EV spread avoids an OHKO from Choice Band Marshadow’s Low Kick and a 2HKO from Life Orb Yveltal’s Dark Pulse.

  • Tera Steel prevents Glimmora and Smeargle from using Mortal Spin to clear entry hazards. Tera Ghost is more niche, allowing Arceus to set Trick Room against Extreme Speed Arceus in an emergency. However, Arceus is a poor user of Terastallization and it should be saved for teammates such as Calyrex-I or Melmetal.

  • Arceus is an excellent Trick Room setter throughout the game thanks to its giant bulk allowing it to set up Trick Room against nearly any unboosted threat. However, it is not to be used as the lead Trick Room setter due to its inability to deny entry hazards from opposing leads such as Deoxys-S, Mental Herb Shuckle, and Mega Diancie.

  • Pokemon that appreciate Trick Room support such as Calyrex-I and Melmetal make excellent teammates for Arceus. They also appreciate Arceus denying Necrozma-DM from using Morning Sun and Zygarde from using Coil and Rest, allowing them to wallbreak past these threats more efficiently.

  • Arceus appreciates additional Trick Room setters to support it in setting Trick Room and preventing entry hazards. Therefore, Hatterene and Cresselia make excellent teammates. Hatterene is able to deny entry hazards from most leads such as Shuckle, Deoxys-S, and Mega Diance, unlike Arceus. Cresselia is also able to restore the PP of teammates with low-PP STAB moves such as Melmetal and Calyrex-I.

Divine Retribution (Extreme Killer).description:
• Arceus has arrived to take its rightful place as the undisputed king of Battle Stadium Singles, unleashing the true power of Extreme Speed in ways Dragonite could only dream of.

  • Swords Dance versus Dragon Dance: Swords Dance allows Arceus to boost its Attack to near unwallable levels with just one turn, while Dragon Dance grants it a Speed boost to better make use of its coverage moves.

  • Shadow Claw: Shadow Claw allows Arceus to break through otherwise problematic Ghost-types such as Calyrex-S and Flutter Mane.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake doesn't threaten Ghost-types as much as Shadow Claw, but it allows Arceus to hit other problematic foes such as Archaludon much harder.

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot is great for making quick work of Dondozo, which is otherwise a fantastic foil to most setup sweepers.

Other options

  • Taunt: Taunt allows Arceus to prevent its targets from recovering off its hits, making it much harder for bulkier teams to deal with.

Items

  • Silk Scarf: Silk Scarf is perhaps the most sensible item for Arceus, boosting the already unfathomable power of its Extreme Speed with no downsides whatsoever.

  • Life Orb: While the recoil can be annoying, Life Orb provides a boost to all of Arceus's attacks, making it an even more potent cleanup artist.

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry grants Arceus more freedom in finding opportunities to set up by shrugging off otherwise ruinous status like burns from the likes of Ho-Oh, allowing for more liberal use of Arceus throughout the game.

  • Mental Herb: Mental Herb is useful as a last resort against Encore Calyrex-S.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Arceus will almost never need to terastallize, but it does nonetheless make fantastic use of terastallization.

  • Normal: Tera Normal Arceus is a sweeper of unmatched magnitude, performing astonishing feats of power such as 2HKOing maximum HP Ho-Oh.

  • Ghost: While Tera Ghost offers limited offensive utility, it shines as a defensive Tera option by granting Arceus an immunity to Extreme Speed from opposing Arceus as well as the many Fighting-type attacks aimed at it, such as Koraidon's Close Combat.

  • Fire: Tera Fire hampers Arceus's defensive utility somewhat but gives it a valuable immunity to burn, allowing it much more freedom against bulkier teams.

EV Spreads

  • 212 HP / 252 Atk / 44 Spe with Adamant: This Spread maximizes power while letting Arceus outspeed up to Jolly Dragonite.

  • 148 HP / 252 Atk / 108 Spe with Adamant: Dragon Dance variants of Arceus should consider investing more into Speed to more liberally use their non-Extreme Speed moves; this spread lets Arceus outspeed up to Calyrex-S after a boost and Choice Scarf users such as Koraidon at +2.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Jolly: Using max Speed sacrifices the power and survivability of slower spreads to make the most of Arceus’s incredible auxiliary movepool.

Extreme Killer.description:
With strong base stats, Arceus can focus on using Swords Dance and Extreme Speed as a cleaner at the end of a game or as a wallbreaker in the middle of the game to set its teammates up for success. With Extreme Speed's priority, EVs in Speed are unnecessary, barring potential investment to outspeed some Pecharunt and Great Tusk, allowing Arceus to use them in HP to tank hits in situations where it needs to boost or use coverage. The fourth move of choice will depend on what Arceus's needs are and what its team can handle for it. Shadow Claw is used against foes like Air Balloon Pecharunt and Arceus-Ghost, Earthquake is used to hit Pokemon like Eternatus and Garganacl, and Flare Blitz can remove Steel-types like Skarmory and Corviknight. Terastallization, similarly, will depend on what Arceus is most worried about, with Tera Ground and Tera Fire preventing paralysis and burn, respectively, on non-Lum Berry variants alongside the potential STAB boost on coverage; Tera Ghost flipping the script on Pecharunt, Fighting-types, or IronPress users; and Tera Normal increasing the power of Extreme Speed.

Arceus is a versatile god that is able to take any slot that a team needs it to take. With perfectly balanced stats, it cannot meet the astronomical highs that most gods can donate to a stat or two, it provides a respectable boost in offensive stats, above-average defensive boosts for HP receivers like Rotom-Wash, and defensive stats for teammates like Clodsire and Clefable that appreciate having high bulk on both sides. However, base 120 offensive stats are limiting, so receivers that do not desperately need a standout boost, such as Meowscarada or Hisuian Electrode, can take those slots. Arceus should not be placed in Speed, as it would waste the boost by mostly using Extreme Speed; however, it can be positioned in any other slot. Balance teams appreciate Arceus, as it can serve as a win condition for a team otherwise missing one while often appreciating consistent stat donations and revenge kills on wallbreakers like Kyogre and Lokix. Arceus appreciates teammates like Landorus and Rotom-Wash that can force out strong defensive options that don't mind Extreme Speed like Pecharunt, Skarmory, and Clodsire via super effective special attacks.

ubers.overview: Arceus is debatably Ubers's most terrifying and dangerous setup sweeper thanks to a powerful STAB-boosted Extreme Speed, decent defenses, and a wide array of utility and coverage moves, letting it mix and match to win problematic matchups easily. Arceus also has an excellent defensive profile, allowing it to take on Ghost-types like Lunala and Flutter Mane. Extreme Speed allows Arceus to operate as a revenge killer, making it difficult for opposing setup sweepers like Scale Shot Koraidon, Miraidon, and Rayquaza to sweep. However, Arceus is not without its flaws, as physically bulky walls like Ting-Lu, Arceus-Water, and especially Necrozma-DM all check it and give it difficulty when attempting to sweep. Furthermore, while more uncommon, Arceus often struggles to beat bulky Ghost-types like Tera Ghost Koraidon, Tera Ghost Miraidon, Giratina-O, Lunala, and Skeledirge, as they can tank unboosted Shadow Claw and cripple Arceus with status. Arceus's lack of resistances and weakness to status moves like Will-O-Wisp, Toxic, and Thunder Wave can make it potentially hard to switch onto the battlefield safely. Despite that, Arceus is still one of the best Pokemon in Ubers, and every team must prep for it if they do not want to get easily cleaned by it.

Swords Dance Extreme Killer.description:
Shadow Claw is Arceus's best option into Pokemon like Necrozma-DM, Giratina-O, and Skeledirge if it does not run Earthquake, making it valuable coverage. Arceus's final moveslot is extremely flexible; Taunt shuts down recovery and status from Pokemon like defensive Arceus formes and Giratina-O and also prevents it from being phazed by Pokemon like Ho-Oh. Recover allows Arceus to negate chip damage, potentially set up multiple times in a game, and also take on Calm Mind Arceus variants. Earthquake allows Arceus to hit Pokemon like Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM for better damage than Shadow Claw. On Silk Scarf and Life Orb sets, Double-Edge is an option to OHKO Gliscor after a Swords Dance and deal heavy damage to opposing bulky Arceus formes. Generally, Arceus most commonly runs Heavy-Duty Boots to negate entry hazard damage, allowing it to sweep more easily. Silk Scarf is an option instead, allowing Arceus to achieve thresholds like OHKOing Miraidon after a Swords Dance and Koraidon after a Swords Dance and layer of Spikes. Although niche, Lum Berry gives Arceus the one-time ability to avoid crippling status from Pokemon like Ho-Oh and Giratina-O, while Leftovers can be used to slightly negate chip damage. Tera Fire is the preferred Tera type, as it allows Arceus to set up against Ho-Oh, check Koraidon and Zacian-C, and become immune to Will-O-Wisp. An alternative is Tera Ghost, giving Arceus the ability to set up on Pokemon like Zacian-C, opposing Extreme Speed Arceus, and Choice Scarf Koraidon. Finally, Tera Normal can be used to boost Extreme Speed, allowing Arceus to achieve thresholds like OHKOing Koraidon and offensive Eternatus after a Swords Dance.

Arceus fits on practically every playstyle, but it best fits on more offensive structures looking for a late-game cleaner that can also potentially operate as a mid-game wallbreaker and revenge killer. One of Arceus's bigger issues is Necrozma-DM, which sponges the majority of its attacks and checks it; Pokemon that can lure in Necrozma-DM and chip it down like Zacian-C and Calyrex-I thus make excellent partners. Other physical attackers like Koraidon and Rayquaza can be good partners to wear down shared checks like Arceus-Water and Arceus-Fairy. Arceus also baits out Terastallization, which is useful to prevent Pokemon like Scale Shot Koraidon from being walled by Tera Fairy. Pokemon like Flutter Mane, Kingambit, and Chien-Pao can all wear down bulky Ghost-types that Arceus struggles with like Giratina-O. Miraidon can take out Pokemon like Ho-Oh, Zacian-C, and Necrozma-DM, all of which Arceus can struggle against. Arceus also appreciates entry hazard support from teammates like Ting-Lu and Gliscor on balance teams and Glimmora and Deoxys-S on hyper offense teams, as they put Koraidon into OHKO range by +2 Extreme Speed.

Bulk Up.description:
Between its great natural bulk, ability to boost its Defense with Bulk Up, and singular weakness, Bulk Up Arceus has incredible survivability and is capable of beating many popular physical attackers and walls like Necrozma-DM, Ho-Oh, and Arceus-Fairy. Extreme Speed and Shadow Claw provide nearly perfect neutral coverage in Ubers. With Tera Fire and Taunt, Arceus sets up on nearly every passive and some offensive Pokemon in the tier, most notably turning Ho-Oh and Zacian-C into setup fodder. 56 EVs in Speed allow Arceus to outspeed unboosted Adamant Rayquaza and Kyurem-B while also outspeeding Zacian-C after Sticky Web. Leftovers is the preferred item for its passive recovery, allowing Arceus to comfortably run Taunt, but Heavy-Duty Boots can be used with Recover on teams that are susceptible to Toxic Spikes. Do note, however, that this significantly worsens the matchup into Ho-Oh.

This Arceus set fits great on both bulky teams and Sticky Web hyper offense teams as a stallbreaker and sweeper that is difficult for even offensive teams to pick off. On bulky teams, Landorus-T is an excellent partner that can act as a short-term check to Pokemon like Koraidon and Zacian-C, accumulating chip damage on them to the point that Arceus can revenge kill them with Extreme Speed. With Sticky Web support on hyper offense, Bulk Up Arceus gains the ability to outspeed many Pokemon that might give it trouble setting up, most notably Koraidon and Zacian-C. More than many other Pokemon, Bulk Up Arceus hates Toxic Spikes. Thus, Eternatus is an excellent partner, being a remover of Toxic Spikes, Kyogre check, and a sweeper facilitated by Arceus breaking down Eternatus's checks. Checking Miraidon and Kyogre is especially important, as they are among the few Pokemon that can threaten Arceus even if boosted. The aforementioned Eternatus can check Kyogre and remove Toxic Spikes, and Ting-Lu can check Miraidon and set Spikes. Miraidon and Zacian-C can overwhelm defensive Arceus-Ground and Arceus-Water, which can survive even boosted Extreme Speeds and threaten Arceus.

Stall.description:
Defensive Arceus makes use of its fantastic bulk to wall many offensive tier staples such as Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Ground, Extreme Killer Arceus, Calyrex-I, and Kyurem-B. It can even survive a Close Combat from Zacian-C and cripple it with Will-O-Wisp, though it cannot switch directly into it. Its ability to run Heavy-Duty Boots lets it fit onto teams without dedicated hazard control, allowing it to constantly re-enter the field without being whittled down by hazards. Iron Defense turns Arceus into an excellent physical check, being able to beat many common physical attackers as well as Pokemon such as Koraidon and Zacian-C, which might have coverage against it. Dragon Tail provides phazing and allows Arceus to rack up hazard damage on switch-ins with entry hazards, as well as shutting down sweepers at the cost of HP if they choose to attack instead of using setup moves. While Arceus will not always Terastallize, it can use it to great effect against teams running Koraidon or Zacian-C. Tera Water helps wall Tera Fire Pokemon, as well as resisting attacks such as Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, and Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance. Tera Fairy is an excellent defensive typing that especially improves the matchup against Koraidon. A Bold Nature can be run over Impish if Arceus chooses to run Foul Play as its only damaging move.

Despite the set name, Stall Arceus is not limited only to stall; it can be used on bulky balance teams as well. Regardless of team composition, Arceus requires hazard support from partners such as Gliscor, Clodsire and Necrozma-DM. It also appreciates the support of Knock Off absorbers such as Gliscor to help prevent Arceus from losing its Heavy-Duty Boots, which would leave it vulnerable to hazards. As Foul Play and Will-O-Wisp both target opposing physical attackers, Arceus tends to invite in special attackers such as Miraidon and Kyogre, so it likes to be paired with special walls such as Blissey, Clodsire, or Ting-Lu. Finally, Ho-Oh is another excellent partner, preventing physical attackers from wearing Arceus down with Regenerator and helping it preserve Recover PP. As Arceus cannot take every physical attack, it fits well on teams with other bulky Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Skarmory, Skeledirge, and Dondozo. On more offensive teams, Arceus likes being paired with pivots like Miraidon, Koraidon, and Iron Bundle as well as powerful wallbreakers like Kyogre and Miraidon.

anythinggoes.overview: Arceus is one of the best setup sweepers and revenge killers in AG thanks to its STAB-boosted Extreme Speed. Extreme Speed allows Arceus to act as a revenge killer, making it problematic for opposing setup sweepers like Miraidon and Scale Shot Koraidon. Thanks to its Normal typing and bulk, it can reliably take on Calyrex-S and heal with Recover while forcing Calyrex-S out with Shadow Claw. Physical walls such as bulky Arceus formes and Ho-Oh check Arceus, making it difficult for it to set up and sweep. Arceus struggles with Tera Ghost users such as Koraidon and Miraidon, as they threaten it. Additionally, Zacian-C is a threat, as it beats Arceus with either its boosted STAB moves in Play Rough and Behemoth Blade or Close Combat while Arceus cannot deal any significant damage in return. Arceus is also weak to status moves like Will-O-Wisp, Toxic, and Thunder Wave, making it hard for it to safely switch in. Regardless of these vulnerabilities, Arceus is one of the best Pokemon in AG, and every team must have adequate counterplay for it.
anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Arceus can opt to run Lum Berry to aggressively set up without worrying about burn and paralysis from Ho-Oh, Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Giratina-O. Lum Berry comes with giving up Heavy-Duty Boots, however, reducing Arceus's longevity by making it difficult to repeatedly switch in on the battlefield. Earthquake used with Tera Fire is a good option on teams that are weak to Zacian-C. On hyper offense structures, Arceus can run Life Orb with Double Edge, allowing it to go wild after a single boost and enabling it to OHKO Ho-Oh before Tera Normal and OHKO Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Landorus-T after. Stone Edge is a niche option to surprise Ho-Oh that OHKOes it at +2, as it likes to switch in on Arceus frequently. Taunt can be used occasionally to stop bulky Arceus formes and Eternatus from phazing Arceus with their status moves and prevents healing with Recover. Taunt also stops Ting-Lu from using Whirlwind to stop Arceus from sweeping and blocks status moves like Will-O-Wisp from Skeledirge and defensive Arceus formes.

Checks and Counters:

Zacian-C: Zacian-C doesn't take significant damage from Arceus's Extreme Speed and unboosted Shadow Claw; meanwhile, it 2HKOes Arceus with Close Combat. However, Arceus can run Tera Fire in conjunction with Bulk Up to set up on Zacian-C.

Koraidon: Koraidon threatens to OHKO Arceus with its powerful Low Kick, runs Tera Ghost to nullify Extreme Speed, and lives +2 Extreme Speed when healthy.

Unaware Users: Arceus is unable to break past Unaware users like Dondozo and Skeledirge, whose solid bulk and access to recovery in Rest and Slack Off let them check Arceus throughout the game, with the latter threatening to burn Arceus with Will-O-Wisp. However, both need to be wary of Taunt, which can prevent them from healing.

Garganacl: Thanks to Purifying Salt backed by great bulk, Garganacl can wall Arceus. Purifying Salt means Arceus cannot do significant damage to it with Shadow Claw. Furthermore, Garganacl can set up Iron Defense to increase the power of Body Press to beat Arceus. However, Garganacl must be wary of Arceus using Earthquake, as +2 Earthquake 2HKOes Garganacl.

Status Moves: Status moves like Toxic from Eternatus and Gliscor and Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave from Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Giratina-O prevent Arceus from safely switching in and hinder its ability to set up in a one-on-one situation against these foes.

Bulky Swords Dance.description:
Bulky Swords Dance Arceus is one of the best late-game cleaners and revenge killers in the metagame. Its typing and bulk allows it to reliably take on Calyrex-S and heal itself with Recover. Shadow Claw allows Arceus to OHKO Calyrex-S and, at +2, 2HKO Necrozma-DM and Giratina-O. Heavy-Duty Boots increase Arceus's longevity, allowing it to safely come onto the field at any point in time, which makes it a difficult threat to deal with late-game. Tera Fire grants Arceus immunity to burn from Arceus-Fairy's Will-O-Wisp and Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire, allowing it to set up without fear. It allows Arceus to take on +2 Calyrex-S in a pinch, giving it a resistance to Calyrex-S's Grass Knot. Tera Fire also flips the tables on Zacian-C, granting a resistance to both of its STAB moves, which gives Arceus a better chance to take it on. However, the drawbacks of Tera Fire are that it removes Arceus's immunity to Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage and makes it weak to Earthquake from Ting-Lu and Arceus-Ground as well as Arceus-Water's Judgment, being 2HKOed by the latter outside of sun. Tera Normal, on the other hand, boosts Extreme Speed's power to respectable levels, allowing Arceus to OHKO uninvested Miraidon at +2, 2HKO Arceus-Fairy, Ho-Oh, and Arceus-Water, and OHKO Koraidon after one layer of Spikes. Furthermore, Tera Normal retains Arceus's defensive utility to check Calyrex-S.

Arceus excels on almost every archetype, fitting best on structures that want a late-game cleaner and revenge killer. Calyrex-S can take advantage of Arceus locked into any move that is not Shadow Claw via Encore and use it as an opportunity to set up Nasty Plot. Choice item Calyrex-S sets like to carry Trick, which cripples Arceus by significantly decreasing its sweeping capabilities. Secondary checks to Calyrex-S such as Ting-Lu and Kingambit are appreciated to share the burden of dealing with it. Furthermore, Ting-Lu can set up Spikes, which assist Arceus in acting as a late-game cleaner by chipping bulky Arceus formes and Koraidon. When unboosted, Arceus is forced out by Miraidon's powerful Electro Drift, so Ting-Lu's ability to take on Miraidon thanks to its bulk and 2HKO it with Earthquake is appreciated. Koraidon can OHKO Arceus thanks to Low Kick, and even when chipped and in range of boosted Extreme Speed, it can use Tera Ghost to avoid being KOed, which often forces Arceus to Terastallize in order to survive Low Kick. Hence, Arceus appreciates walls that can check Koraidon such as Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, Ho-Oh, and Landorus-T. The former two carry Will-O-Wisp to cripple Koraidon, with Arceus-Fairy also scaring it out with Judgment. Ho-Oh can burn Koraidon with Sacred Fire or 2HKO it with Brave Bird. Landorus-T, meanwhile, likes to carry Rocky Helmet to chip Koraidon. Arceus also struggles with Zacian-C, as it cannot break through with either Extreme Speed or Shadow Claw, making Arceus-Water and Landorus-T good partners because they help check Zacian-C. Arceus-Water resists Behemoth Blade and can burn Zacian-C with Will-O-Wisp, while Landorus-T can nullify its Intrepid Sword with Intimidate, chip it with Rocky Helmet, and 2HKO it with Earthquake. Additionally, Choice Scarf Koraidon and Calyrex-S can revenge kill Zacian-C. Arceus finds it difficult to break through staple defensive Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Arceus-Fairy, and Arceus-Water. Consequently, special attackers such as Calyrex-S and Miraidon are great teammates to pair with Arceus. Miraidon can beat these checks with its raw power and access to Electro Drift, while Calyrex-S can break through them with a variety of options such as Nasty Plot + Astral Barrage or Choice item sets. Furthermore, Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy and Kyogre can also beat the aforementioned checks, as well as Ting-Lu, which can stop Arceus from sweeping with Whirlwind if healthy, and, with Tera Poison, Eternatus, which otherwise can Toxic Arceus and put it on a timer.

Bulk Up.description:
Bulk Up Arceus is a potent late-game setup sweeper and revenge killer that leverages Extreme Speed—the strongest priority move in the tier. Shadow Claw allows it to hit Calyrex-S, Tera Ghost Koraidon, and Giratina-O. Recover allows Arceus to set up on Pokemon such as other Arceus lacking Bulk Up, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, various defensive Arceus formes lacking Will-O-Wisp, and Koraidon after Terastallizing. Tera Fire gives Arceus a burn immunity, which lets it set up on Pokemon that would otherwise check it, such as support Arceus formes with Will-O-Wisp and non-Whirlwind Ho-Oh. It also grants a resistance to Koraidon's Flare Blitz and Calyrex-S's Grass Knot at the cost of Arceus's immunity to Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage. Arceus's Special Defense and HP EVs allow it to survive a +2 Tera Grass Calyrex-S Grass Knot or a +2 Tera Stellar Psychic from the same foe. Its Speed creeps it above fully invested, neutral-natured base 90 Pokemon such as Kyogre and Ho-Oh.

Bulk Up Arceus applies offensive pressure on Pokemon such as Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and defensive Ho-Oh, forcing them to stay at high enough HP to successfully stop a sweep. Its longevity relative to regular Extreme Killer Arceus makes it much more prominent on bulkier balance and bulky offense teams, where it frequently acts as a great Calyrex-S check and often threatens to sweep once the opponent's defensive Arceus formes and Ho-Oh are worn down. Bulk Up Arceus struggles with special wallbreakers, like Miraidon and Kyogre, as it can't OHKO them without multiple boosts, allowing them to force out or heavily damage it. Thus, Eternatus is a great partner for Bulk Up Arceus, leveraging its Water resistance to be one of the best Kyogre switch-ins, as well as spreading poison with Toxic Spikes and Toxic. Ting-Lu, being balance's best and only Miraidon check, is also a great partner to Bulk Up Arceus due to its Electric immunity and great Special Defense. Before Terastallizing, Arceus is also weak to Koraidon's Low Kick and burn inflicted by defensive Arceus formes, Ho-Oh, and Giratina-O. Arceus-Fairy is a great burn absorber, can force out Ho-Oh with Power Gem, acts as a great Koraidon switch-in, and easily spreads paralysis with Thunder Wave to make it easier for Arceus to set up. Arceus-Water is also a great switch-in to Ho-Oh, leveraging its Fire resistance and threatening it out with Judgment. It also helps slow down Zacian-C, using its Water typing to resist Behemoth Blade and threatening Zacian-C with Will-O-Wisp but at the cost of letting opposing Koraidon use Low Kick more freely than Arceus-Fairy. Bulk Up Arceus is a deadweight against stall due to Dondozo, Skeledirge, Skarmory, and Garganacl walling it effectively. Thus, it appreciates stallbreaking teammates, such as Miraidon and Calyrex-S, which also assist in breaking Arceus-Fairy and Arceus-Water. Zacian-C also proves to be a challenge for Bulk Up Arceus to break on its own, so it usually relies on teammates such as Ho-Oh or the aforementioned Arceus-Water to force Zacian-C to switch out and slowly chip it with entry hazard damage. Choice Scarf Koraidon is also a great offensive check to Zacian-C and Miraidon, threatening OHKOes with Flare Blitz and Outrage, respectively.

Utility.description:
• With access to STAB Foul Play, high defensive stats, and its mono-Dark typing, Arceus-Dark effectively checks Pokemon such as Primal Groudon, Arceus, Necrozma-DM, Ultra Necrozma, and Mega Salamence, making it one of the most reliable defensive Arceus formes in NatDex Ubers.
  • Foul Play is absolutely essential for Arceus-Dark, as it serves two crucial roles: first, it allows Arceus-Dark to effectively revenge kill boosted threats such as Primal Groudon, Arceus, Ultra Necrozma, and Mega Salamence. Second, it acts as a deterrent, dissuading these threats from setting up until Arceus-Dark has been sufficiently weakened.
  • Toxic is the preferred status move for Arceus-Dark, primarily to cripple common switch-ins such as Ho-Oh, Yveltal, Primal Kyogre, and Arceus-Fairy. Will-O-Wisp presents a viable alternative for hitting Zacian-C and Marshadow, which is particularly relevant given Zacian-C's resistance to Foul Play.
  • Refresh is a solid choice when Arceus-Dark is utilized as a primary Knock Off and status absorber for the team, since it can reliably switch into Toxic Yveltal or Eternatus. However, in other scenarios, it's not recommended since it would render Arceus-Dark too passive against the aforementioned threats.
  • Taunt allows Arceus-Dark to greatly limit most of the entry hazard setters in the tier, namely Primal Groudon, Defensive Necrozma-DM, and Ferrothorn. Additionally, it can neutralize status spreaders like Toxic Yveltal, Ferrothorn, and Giratina-Origin, while also restricting the former's ability to use Defog. Taunt Arceus-Dark is also one of the best checks to Zygarde-C, as it can completely shut down its ability to spread paralysis and set up.
  • Defog serves as a good filler move when Arceus-Dark acts as hazard control over common Defoggers like Ho-Oh and Giratina-O. Stealth Rock can be a viable option to free up teammates to fulfill other roles; for example, it alows Primal Groudon to run more offensive sets such as Swords Dance, or fit Spikes on defensive set. In addition, Arceus-Dark's typing and movepool allow it to set up Stealth Rock on common Defoggers such as Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and most opposing Arceus formes, all of which are threatened by Arceus-Dark's status moves.
  • Arceus-Dark's EV spread enables it to be faster than common base 90 Speed foes and also facilitates its role as a revenge killer against offensive Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre. Alternatively, investing in Speed with EVs of 248 HP / 164 Def / 96 Spe and a Timid nature allows Arceus-Dark to outspeed Pokémon like Yveltal, Zekrom, and Rayquaza, and still survive a Life Orb Low Kick from Marshadow.
  • Tera Poison lets Arceus Dark acts as an emergency check to boosted Marshadow and Tera Fighting Zacian-C, making it possible to safely revenge kill them. Moreover, by becoming a Poison-type, Arceus-Dark becomes immune to Toxic, making it possible for non-Taunt versions to beat Toxic Yveltal one-on-one. However, Tera Poison makes Arceus-Dark extremely vulnerable to Photon Geyser Ultra Necrozma, Primal Groudon, Arceus-Ground, and Deoxys-A, thus trainers should think twice before Terastallizing Arceus-Dark.
  • Utility Arceus-Dark is an excellent fit for balance and defensive teams, offering a check to Zygarde-C and and other common physical sweepers such as Ultra Necrozma. Depending on the set used, some precautions should be taken with Arceus-Dark. Non-Refresh sets need to scout for Toxic before switching into Primal Groudon and Necrozma-DM. Similarly, it is important to scout for Glare Zygarde since Arceus-Dark doesn't enjoy being paralyzed.
  • Stealth Rock from Arceus-Dark itself or a teammate like Primal Groudon can wear down Fairy-types such as Arceus-Fairy that can switch into Arceus-Dark.
  • Since Necrozma-DM, the premier Toxic absorber of the tier, is heavily threatened by Foul Play, Arceus-Dark can often freely use Toxic on a predicted switch-in.
  • Primal Groudon and Swords Dance Arceus can overwhelm Arceus-Dark. To improve its matchup against these threats, teammates like Zygarde-C, Ferrothorn, and Ditto can provide valuable support.
  • Defensive Primal Groudon serves as a great partner for Arceus-Dark, threatening Eternatus, which walls Arceus-Dark. A similar role is accomplished by Ho-Oh, especially sets carrying Thunder Wave, which can make Arceus-Dark faster than it. Additionally, Ho-Oh appreciates Arceus-Dark's ability to deal with Knock Off Necrozma-DM and Ultra Necrozma.
  • Necrozma-DM is another partner that benefits from Arceus-Dark's ability to cripple Primal Groudon and Yveltal, and it provides a Fairy resistance and Toxic immunity in return.
  • Cleric support from Pokemon such as Magearna and Chansey can mitigate non-Refresh Arceus-Dark's weakness to status conditions.

Calm Mind.description:
• Calm Mind Arceus-Dark is an appealing option for balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate the role compression this set is able to provide. Arceus-Dark provides these teams with a sturdy win condition, a special wall, and a counter to Pokemon such as Ultra Necrozma and specially offensive Yveltal.
  • Arceus-Dark has some flexibility in its fourth moveslot. Refresh enables Arceus-Dark to shrug off status and enables a stronger mid-game presence, as it is able to switch into Pokemon such as Giratina-O and Ho-Oh with impunity. Refresh also enables Arceus-Dark to position itself for a sweep more easily, as it is not hampered by Toxic.
  • Taunt allows Arceus-Dark to easily shut down much of the defensive metagame and set up on Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Zygarde, but it has to come in cautiously, as status conditions such as Toxic poison and paralysis from Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Zygarde heavily impede its ability to sweep prior to Terastallizing.
  • 4 Defense and 96 Speed EVs enable Arceus-Dark to survive Choice Band Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance and outspeed Chi-Yu. The remaining EVs are dumped into Special Defense, which enables Arceus-Dark to better function as a special wall. This is particularly important against specially offensive Yveltal, as Arceus-Dark is easily able to shrug off Oblivion Wing as opposed to being forced to use Recover. This investment also enables Arceus-Dark to use Meteor Beam Eternatus as setup fodder, as it can withstand the combination of Meteor Beam followed by +1 Dynamax Cannon.
  • Arceus-Dark's Tera type depends on whether it opts to run Refresh or Taunt. As Refresh Arceus-Dark does not have to worry about status, the defensive utility of Fairy is preferred. Tera Fairy enables Arceus-Dark to still check specially defensive Yveltal while also countering Palkia-O, as it is no longer concerned about Spacial Rend's critical hits; it also provides an immunity to attempts to phase it with Dragon Tail from Pokemon such as Giratina-O. Taunt Arceus-Dark opts for Tera Poison due to the poison immunity, as Toxic prevents it from sweeping; Tera Poison also provides additional utility by absorbing Eternatus's Toxic Spikes.
  • Against balance and bulky offense teams, Calm Mind Arceus-Dark is often used mid-game to defensively check Pokemon such as Giratina-O, Ho-Oh, Yveltal, and Zygarde. As the opposing team is worn down, Arceus-Dark often finds itself in a position late-game to start boosting and sweep.
  • As Arceus-Dark requires multiple boosts to become offensively threatening, it is often unable to sweep but plays an essential defensive role by checking Pokemon such as Ultra Necrozma and specially offensive Yveltal. Arceus-Dark's role against stall teams is heavily dependent on whether it opts to use Refresh or Taunt. If running Refresh, Arceus-Dark is an excellent pivot and status sponge that is capable of sweeping once Chansey is removed. Taunt Arceus-Dark has a more active role in stallbreaking, often utilizing Tera Poison and Taunt to preserve progress.
  • Zygarde is the best teammate for Arceus-Dark. As Arceus-Dark invests in Special Defense, it relies on Zygarde to check physically offensive threats that it itself is unable to such as Marshadow, Zacian-C, and Primal Groudon. In return, Arceus-Dark checks Pokemon that overwhelm Zygarde such as Eternatus and specially offensive Yveltal. Arceus-Dark also appreciates Defog and status support from Giratina-O and Ho-Oh in addition to their ability to check Primal Groudon and Zacian-C, respectively.
  • Arceus-Dark can struggle against other Calm Mind Arceus formes, especially Arceus-Fairy. Consequently, physical attackers such as Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C are good teammates. Their ability to offensively check defensive Primal Kyogre is appreciated, as Arceus-Dark struggles to beat it without Taunt.

Defensive.description: Arceus-Electric's main draw is its Electric typing, which grants it both STAB on Thunder Cage and a resistance to it, giving Arceus-Electric a niche over other mostly neutral options like Arceus. Ice Beam provides generally good coverage, hitting Dragon- and Ground-types like Eternatus and Mega Garchomp that can otherwise switch into Thunder Cage safely. Secret Sword is an option that lets Arceus-Electric bypass Blissey, an otherwise hard stop to it that also denies Strength Sap healing. Ice Scales variants can struggle to answer powerful threats like Mega Alakazam and Flutter Mane long-term, making a secondary specially defensive teammate, such as a RegenVest user or Blissey, helpful. Fur Coat variants can handle most physical threats but are notably weak to Mega Garchomp, making a teammate like Celesteela or a secondary Fur Coat user necessary. Arceus-Electric usually can Imposter-proof itself, but Pokemon like Imposter Chansey can act as a secondary Imposter-proofer if it is weakened or inflicted with Salt Cure.

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy has a very well rounded set of credentials, sporting reliable bulk, a sound typing both offensively and defensively, good power after Calm Mind boosts, and a solid Speed tier, allowing it to function as a reliable bulky wincon. Calm Mind grants Arceus-Fairy extra power and shores up its special bulk, and Recover lets it stay healthy and get more boosts off. Judgment is a strong STAB move that can score 2HKOs on common special walls such as Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Mandibuzz, while Earth Power allows Arceus-Fairy to hit Steel-types such as Excadrill, Heatran, and Zacian-C. The Speed EVs allow Arceus-Fairy to outspeed Ogerpon-W and unboosted Iron Moth and eventually beat them. Tera Ground gives Earth Power a little more power to OHKO Zacian-C at +1 after Stealth Rock and allows it to 2HKO Eternatus and physically defensive Clodsire, with the additional benefit of allowing Arceus-Fairy to resist Poison-type moves from the likes of Sneasler, Iron Moth, and Eternatus that would otherwise KO it.

Arceus-Fairy has an amazing set of stats to donate, allowing it to build a very wide variety of teams around itself, but Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy works best on balance and bulky offense structures that can wear down the opposing team to prepare for Arceus-Fairy to finish them off. A multitude of Pokemon love to receive Arceus-Fairy's great HP stat, including but not limited to: Rotom-W, Pecharunt, and Landorus-T. Arceus-Fairy's high defensive stats also lend themselves to bulky pivots such as the aforementioned three Pokemon, which support Arceus-Fairy by getting it in safely. Hisuian Samurott and Meowscarada are great choices to receive Arceus-Fairy's Attack stat, as they provide Spikes, pivoting, and Knock Off support. Entry hazard setters such as the aforementioned Hisuian Samurott, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T help wear down specially defensive Pokemon so that Arceus-Fairy has a better shot at 2HKOing them later. Arceus-Fairy struggles to break bulky Pokemon such as Skarmory, Dondozo, and Ho-Oh, so it appreciates Pokemon that beat these walls, such as Ogerpon-W and Zapdos. Other special attackers like Hisuian Electrode and Hoopa-U can force in mutual checks such as Clodsire, Galarian Slowking, and specially defensive Excadrill and chip them so that Arceus-Fairy can overpower them with Calm Mind boosts further down the line, with Hisuian Electrode also being able to pivot with Volt Switch.

ubers.overview: Arceus-Fairy is a defensive behemoth that cements itself a place in Ubers as one of the best checks to Koraidon. An immunity to Dragon and a resistance to Low Kick give Arceus-Fairy ample opportunities to switch in while also forcing Koraidon to use Flare Blitz more often and decrease its longevity as a result. Furthermore, Arceus-Fairy's bulk and resistances make it a useful soft check to Pokemon such as Arceus, Giratina-O, Kyurem-B, Zekrom, Chien-Pao, Rayquaza, and even Miraidon and Flutter Mane. Good neutral coverage with Fairy-type Judgment allows Arceus-Fairy to take full advantage of its ample support movepool featuring Thunder Wave, Will-O-Wisp, Stealth Rock, and Taunt. Outside of being a bit passive against Necrozma-DM, Ho-Oh, and Zacian-C and having to play around opposing Terastallization carefully, Arceus-Fairy has little to no flaws and should be strongly considered for any balance team.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Earth Power and Power Gem are coverage options for a fully dedicated Calm Mind set. The problem is that Arceus-Fairy always loses to either Necrozma-DM or Ho-Oh, so while these coverage options are viable, they require dedicated team support. Of the two, Earth Power is more plausible, as Ho-Oh may be crippled by Knock Off support. Losing access to status or Stealth Rock also leaves Arceus-Fairy more passive in general.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-Resistant Tanks: Necrozma-DM, Ho-Oh, and Zacian-C take little damage from Judgment and can use Arceus-Fairy as an opportunity to set up, although none of them like taking Thunder Wave.

Tera Fire Users: Arceus-Fairy cannot burn common physical attackers like Koraidon and Necrozma-DM after they have used Tera Fire, which also greatly weakens the power of Judgment. Koraidon can notably guarantee the OHKO on Arceus-Fairy at +2 with Tera Fire Flare Blitz, necessitating Arceus-Fairy to use Tera Water itself. These Pokemon are still vulnerable to Thunder Wave, but they may still be able to sweep with enough boosts.

Chip Damage: Arceus-Fairy is vulnerable to all forms of status and entry hazard damage, which force it to use Recover more often and lose momentum.

Calm Mind: Calm Mind users like Arceus-Ground, Kyogre, and Arceus-Grass take little from Judgment and can use Calm Mind relatively freely as a result.

Defensive Wall.description:
This set gives Arceus-Fairy its best chance at taking on Koraidon. Thunder Wave is extremely useful for crippling all of Arceus-Fairy's most common switch-ins in Necrozma-DM, Ho-Oh, and Zacian-C. It is also a safe move to use against Koraidon should you expect it to use Tera Fire and is especially useful because Arceus-Fairy discourages all Ground- and Electric-types bar Clodsire from switching in. Will-O-Wisp more directly cripples physical attackers like Koraidon and Necrozma-DM, although it cannot hit Ho-Oh and Tera Fire users. The third moveslot is fairly flexible; Stealth Rock is a good option, as it frees up moveslots for Arceus-Fairy's teammates. Taunt prevents Clodsire and specially defensive Gliscor from being able to use Spikes and Toxic. Dragon Tail can be a good way to rack up entry hazard damage and can phaze setup sweepers that may not mind being hit with status, and it is highly recommended when running Will-O-Wisp. Calm Mind turns Arceus-Fairy into a dangerous setup sweeper, albeit one that requires significant team support to handle Necrozma-DM and especially Ho-Oh. It is a good option on teams that already have plentiful ways to spread status. Tera Water is mandatory in case Arceus-Fairy needs to take a boosted Flare Blitz from Koraidon, and it can be useful in a pinch against Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C. Tera Water in combination with Calm Mind can more easily clean up weakened teams, as Necrozma-DM won't have a coverage option to hit Arceus-Fairy. The EVs allow Arceus-Fairy to outspeed maximum Speed neutral-natured base 90 Pokemon such as Kyogre, with the rest being dumped into physical bulk.

While Arceus-Fairy is a great wall, it's unable to take on notable physical attackers like Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C without Terastallizing. As a result, defensive Necrozma-DM is a fantastic partner, and the two together reasonably cover nearly all physical threats in the tier. Ting-Lu and Clodsire can take on Miraidon and appreciate Arceus-Fairy's Dragon immunity that allows it to pivot into Draco Meteor, making them fantastic teammates. Defensive Ho-Oh, Gliscor, and Eternatus can handle offensive Ho-Oh without much fear of Sacred Fire burns, with Eternatus having the added benefit of checking Kyogre and absorbing Toxic Spikes. Strong but relatively slow wallbreakers such as Kyogre, Swords Dance Necrozma-DM, and offensive Ho-Oh like the paralysis support that Arceus-Fairy can provide. Kyogre notably helps with the Koraidon matchup, as it can pivot into Flare Blitz and bring rain that negates Koraidon's ability, making it a great partner. Giratina-O can handle Arceus-Ground and provide much-appreciated Defog support.

Iron Defense + Calm Mind.description:
Leveraging its great bulk and typing, Arceus-Fairy can utilize Iron Defense and Calm Mind to become an excellent late-game wincon and act as a defensive anchor on bulkier teams and defensive cores to take on the dangerous Koraidon. Iron Defense allows it to set up in front of threats such as Koraidon and physical Arceus formes lacking Taunt, while Calm Mind helps Arceus-Fairy to OHKO or 2HKO foes with Judgment and become nigh-unstoppable when paired with Defense boosts. Tera Poison stops Eternatus from crippling Arceus-Fairy with Toxic, removes its weakness to Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, gives it a resistance to offensive Eternatus's Sludge Bomb, and lets it act as a Toxic Spikes absorber later on in the game if Arceus-Fairy's partner Eternatus has been knocked out. Tera Water allows Arceus-Fairy to resist Koraidon's Flare Blitz, Kyogre's Water Spout and Origin Pulse, Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, and Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike. However, it makes Arceus-Fairy weak to Zacian-C's Wild Charge and Kyogre's Thunder. The Speed EVs allow Arceus-Fairy to outpace maximum investment base 90 Speed Pokemon, such as Kyogre, Zekrom, and Groudon, while the rest are dumped into physical bulk.

Iron Defense + Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy is incredibly potent in late-game scenarios where it is the last Pokemon standing, which prevents it from being phazed by Whirlwind or Dragon Tail if it has Terastallized. However, due to the limited PP of Recover, Arceus-Fairy should refrain from taking too much damage early on to preserve its ability for a late-game sweep. Eternatus can absorb Toxic Spikes for Arceus-Fairy in late-game scenarios, letting it set up more easily. Eternatus can also switch into Ho-Oh, which frequently forces Arceus-Fairy to switch out, and cripple it with Toxic. Kyogre can take on Koraidon for Arceus-Fairy much more comfortably by deactivating Orichalcum Pulse and weakening Flare Blitz with Drizzle. Landorus-T could provide entry hazard support with Stealth Rock, since this Arceus-Fairy set is not running it, while also serving as a temporary check to the dangerous Zacian-C. Defensive Ho-Oh can help check Steel-types such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM, which could pressure Arceus-Fairy, especially with hazards up. Ho-Oh can check opposing special Arceus formes and Eternatus, though Ho-Oh could also run offensive sets, and Arceus-Fairy and Kyogre could take on the task of checking Koraidon instead. As Arceus-Fairy is vulnerable to entry hazards, teammates that could help with hazard control, such as Giratina-O and Terapagos, should also be considered.

Defensive.description:
• Arceus-Fairy can perform a wide variety of defensive roles thanks to its Fairy typing, solid stats, wide movepool, and a nice Speed tier. It is able to switch into multiple top threats of the metagame such as Mega Salamence, Yveltal, Zygarde, Arceus-Dark, and Marshadow and cripple them with various options or set Stealth Rock as they're forced out, enabling it to fit in balance and defensive team structures.
  • Taunt allows Arceus-Fairy to prevent setup, recovery, entry hazards, hazard control via Defog, and crippling status moves such as Glare and Toxic from Pokemon such as Primal Groudon, Zygarde, Ho-Oh, and Giratina-O. This move isn't recommended on specially defensive variants, as it's relatively easy for foes, such as some variants of the Pokemon listed above, to outspeed Arceus-Fairy, thus rendering most of Taunt's purposes niche.
  • Toxic complements Judgment to cripple foes that can easily switch into it, including Ho-Oh, Arceus-Ground, and Primal Groudon, Will-O-Wisp alternatively allows Arceus-Fairy to cripple the Poison- and Steel-types it lures in, such as Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM, and Eternatus, while also creating an easier matchup against multiple physical attackers such as Terastallized Zygarde and Marshadow.
  • Stealth Rock forces progress for Arceus-Fairy's team, as it forces out relevant hazard removers such as Yveltal and Giratina-O. With Stealth Rock active, Arceus-Fairy has high odds to OHKO Ultra Necrozma and Palkia-O with Judgment.
  • Given Arceus-Fairy can often stay in on common hazard setters such as Primal Groudon and opposing support Arceus formes, if Arceus-Fairy has Toxic, it can act as a viable Defogger.
  • Refresh increases Arceus-Fairy's longevity and consistency at checking foes, reducing the potential risk of switching into Glare from Zygarde and Toxic from Ho-Oh, Arceus-Dark, and Primal Groudon. It also renders special sets of Giratina-O unable to do much in return, as Hex does poor damage without a status condition.
  • The given EV spread with a Bold nature allows Arceus-Fairy to outspeed Primal Groudon to better facilitate using Taunt and Recover, with the rest of the EVs being placed in Defense to render it as physically bulky as possible, letting it avoid a 2HKO from Choice Band Marshadow's Poltergeist.
  • Alternatively, a specially defensive spread of 248 HP / 136 Def / 108 SpD / 16 Spe with a Calm nature lets Arceus-Fairy avoid a 2HKO from Palkia-O's Hydro Pump and Primal Groudon's Overheat and a 2HKO from Choice Band Marshadow's Spectral Thief after Stealth Rock, and it can outspeed uninvested Primal Groudon. Additionally it also allows Arceus-Fairy to check Mega Mewtwo Y, and after Terastallizing to the Poison-type, Eternatus. This spread, however, has the flaws of being easier to overwhelm by physical attackers and vulnerability to Taunt from Pokemon such as other defensive Arceus formes and Terastallized Yveltal.
  • Tera Water lets Arceus-Fairy more comfortably wall foes such as Primal Groudon, Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM, in turn allowing Arceus-Fairy to cripple them with a status condition. Arceus-Fairy also gains a resistance to Palkia-O's Hydro Pump, granting it the momentum to greatly damage it even if it uses its physically defensive spread.
  • Tera Poison increases Arceus-Fairy's longevity by giving it an immunity to Toxic and removing its weaknesses to Steel- and Poison-type moves, letting it switch into Zacian-C, Eternatus without Meteor Beam, Giratina-O, Arceus-Dark, and opposing Arceus-Fairy.
  • Arceus-Fairy is a Pokemon that does not Terastallize often, as its innate typing already provides the option to act as a wall for a good portion of the metagame, and its allies often make better use of it.
  • Arceus-Fairy's Judgment is often easy to switch into early- to mid-game, so most of the time utility moves are used instead for consistency and to continue making progress by crippling the other team.
  • Depending on the moveset, Arceus-Fairy can't respond to foes that resist Judgment such as Primal Groudon, Ho-Oh, and Necrozma-DM; therefore, it appreciates Pokemon that can answer them, which include Giratina-O, Primal Kyogre, and Marshadow.
  • Arceus-Fairy's bulk can be lacking on one side depending on its EV spread. Physically defensive variants can struggle against Palkia-O, Eternatus, and Arceus formes with Calm Mind, so it appreciates checks to them to complement its own defensive attributes like Ho-Oh, Necrozma-DM, and Primal Groudon. Meanwhile, specially defensive variants can have notable difficulties checking physical sweepers, which include Primal Groudon, Mega Salamence and Arceus, so Pokemon that can switch into them such as Giratina-O and Necrozma-DM are appreciated.

Calm Mind.description:
• Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy is an excellent bulky setup sweeper and wincon due to its excellent stats across the board, Fairy typing, and extensive coverage. Due to these qualities, it fits on a multitude of playstyles such as hyper offense, bulky offense, and balance.
  • Will-O-Wisp allows Arceus-Fairy to easily set up on Arceus, physical Arceus-Ground, and Mega Salamence lacking Facade. Power Gem is an option to hit Ho-Oh for meaningful damage. Taunt can be used to prevent Giratina-O, Primal Groudon, and Ho-Oh from crippling Arceus-Fairy with status such as Toxic or Thunder Wave and phazing it with Roar or Whirlwind. In addition, Taunt blocks Glare from Zygarde. Earth Power allows Arceus-Fairy to hit Primal Groudon, Eternatus, and Steel-types like Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM.
  • The given EV spread invests enough Speed for Arceus-Fairy to outspeed Primal Kyogre and Primal Groudon. The rest is invested into Defense and HP, giving Arceus-Fairy a high chance to survive a +2 Precipice Blades from Double Dance Primal Groudon while also avoiding an OHKO from Deoxys-A’s Psycho Boost after Stealth Rock and a 2HKO from Marshadow’s Poltergeist. The alternative EV spread with a Timid nature allows Arceus-Fairy to outspeed Modest Palkia-O and avoid a 2HKO from Choice Band Marshadow’s Spectral Thief after Stealth Rock.
  • Tera Dark provides Arceus-Fairy with a Psychic immunity, helping its team against powerful attacks such as Light That Burns the Sky from Ultra Necrozma, Psycho Boost from Deoxys-A, and Psystrike from Mega Mewtwo Y.
  • Tera Poison provides Arceus-Fairy a valuable immunity to Toxic and Toxic Spikes, allowing it to serve as the team’s Toxic Spikes absorber and check to opposing Arceus-Fairy and Eternatus.
  • Tera Ground ensures that Earth Power 2HKOes defensive Primal Groudon at +0 and gives it a chance to 2HKO defensive Necrozma-DM at +1.
  • On hyper offense, Arceus-Fairy is an excellent late-game wincon against a weakened team when checks such as Ho-Oh and Eternatus have been removed. On bulky offense and balance, Arceus-Fairy serves as an excellent check to Marshadow, Yveltal, and unboosted Mega Salamence throughout the game. It should not be afraid to switch into attacks from the aforementioned Pokemon, as any damage can be healed off with Recover. Arceus-Fairy must be wary of Toxic from Yveltal, Ho-Oh, and Giratina-O, which can heavily undermine its ability to sweep.
  • Arceus-Fairy’s sweeping ability is often hampered due to it being outsped by common threats such as Eternatus, Zacian-C, and Deoxys-A. For hyper offense, Sticky Web support from Shuckle flips these matchups and allows Arceus-Fairy to beat these checks. For bulky offense and balance, Thunder Wave support from Necrozma-DM eliminates this problem. Arceus-Fairy also appreciates duel screens support from Deoxys-S or Grimmsnarl, as this eases setup.
  • Regardless of what is chosen in the fourth moveslot, Arceus-Fairy will always suffer from a lack of coverage, as having Power Gem means it struggles against Primal Groudon, and having Earth Power means it cannot break past Ho-Oh. Teammates that can cover these vulnerabilities such as Primal Kyogre and Ultra Necrozma are helpful. Gothitelle is also a good teammate, as it effectively traps and removes walls such as Tera Steel Giratina-O, Ferrothorn, and Ho-Oh.

Calm Mind + Refresh.description:
• Compressing the roles of a stallbreaker, wall, and sweeper, Arceus-Fairy uses its lack of common weaknesses, well-rounded stats, and high longevity to act as a usable win condition against bulky team structures for balance teams.
  • Refresh ensures that Arceus-Fairy can't be hindered long-term by moves such as Toxic from Ho-Oh and Primal Groudon, easing the act of applying pressure on the opposing team and allowing more aggressive play compared to Taunt by not requiring it to safely switch into and outspeed a foe to avoid being inflicted with a status condition.
  • The first EV spread with a Bold nature outspeeds base 90 Speed foes such as Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre, with the rest invested into physical bulk to have high odds at avoiding a 2HKO from Double Dance Primal Groudon's Precipice Blades; it additionally avoids a 2HKO from Choice Band Marshadow's Poltergeist as well as an OHKO from Life Orb Deoxys-A's Psycho Boost after Stealth Rock. The second EV spread with a Timid nature outspeeds neutral-natured base 120 Speed foes including Palkia-O and Mega Salamence and avoids a 2HKO from Choice Band Marshadow's Spectral Thief after Stealth Rock.
  • Tera Dark allows Arceus-Fairy to beat Psychic-types such as Ultra Necrozma and Mega Mewtwo Y one-on-one and become immune to status moves from the niche Grimmsnarl, all while retaining a Dark resistance to still handle foes such as Yveltal and Chien-Pao.
  • Arceus-Fairy should be used primarily as a wall early- to mid-game, as the need to use Calm Mind several times to break past Fairy-resistant foes makes it setup fodder for foes such as Double Dance Primal Groudon, Ho-Oh, and Zacian-C.
  • Arceus-Fairy can often brute force past bulky foes such as Terastallized Coil Zygarde, Primal Kyogre, and defensive Primal Groudon thanks to its high longevity, but it should be careful to preserve its Judgment and Recover PP.
  • While Arceus-Fairy acts as a good status absorber for its team thanks to Refresh, a turn is required to use it, which can often lead to scenarios where the opponent exploits this detail to safely bring in an offensive check against Arceus-Fairy. Therefore, it sometimes may be desirable to not immediately use Refresh after being subject to a status condition.
