  • As Arceus-Fairy can struggle with Fairy-resistant foes such as opposing Primal Groudon, Ho-Oh, and Necrozma-DM, often limiting its potential against bulky team structures. Partners such as Zygarde and Primal Groudon can apply offensive pressure against these foes, and Gothitelle can trap and remove Ho-Oh and Necrozma-DM.
  • Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, Giratina-O, and Primal Kyogre handle Taunt users that can heavily limit Arceus-Fairy such as opposing Arceus-Water and Arceus-Ground. Ferrothorn, in particular,also supports Arceus-Fairy by discouraging switches with the entry hazards it sets, easing Arceus-Fairy's wallbreaking.

balancedhackmons.overview: Arceus-Fairy is a great, flexible, defensive option for most teams thanks to its typing, good bulk that allows it to serve a role as either a Fur Coat or an Ice Scales Pokemon, and high Speed that eclipses most physical attackers for the Fur Coat set. Its bulk also makes it a solid choice for a bulky Take Heart sweeper, with Thunder Cage + Strength Sap allowing it to beat most Imposter users one-on-one. A mixed set with Pixilate allows Arceus-Fairy to scare potential checks and counters with a powerful Extreme Speed. Arceus-Fairy's main flaw is arguably its dependence on Strength Sap for healing, which means Magic Guard Blissey and Chansey are perfect counters, since they have the perfect kits to freely switch into Arceus-Fairy and stall it out; Arceus-Fairy can't reliably use Recover instead, as doing so completely forfeits its advantage against Impostor users. Additionally, Fur Coat Arceus-Fairy can struggle against common Steel-type coverage from Choice Band users like Mega Garchomp, while Ice Scales variants are vulnerable to Eternatus and super effective coverage like Noxious Torque Ash-Greninja and Gigaton Hammer Mega Sceptile.
balancedhackmons.comments:
Other Options

Heavy-Duty Boots serves as a good option for Arceus-Fairy in general, as preventing entry hazard damage can end up being important in the long run. Covert Cloak is also a viable option, preventing a lot of chip damage from Salt Cure. Arceus-Fairy can run a more support-oriented moveset with moves such as Spikes, but this makes it quite challenging to Impostor-proof.

Checks and Counters

Blissey and Chansey: Their immense bulk and Magic Guard render Take Heart Arceus-Fairy almost helpless against them, and their tiny Attack means Arceus-Fairy heals for basically nothing with Strength Sap.

Ice Scales: Other Ice Scales users, such as various Arceus forms, Meloetta, and Mega Audino, can check Take Heart Arceus-Fairy, though they should be wary of Thunder Cage's residual damage.

Steel-types: Strong Steel-type wallbreakers such as Mega Lucario greatly threaten Arceus-Fairy. Defensively, Pokemon like Solgaleo and Arceus-Steel can check all variants of Arceus-Fairy.

Salt Cure: Unless Covert Cloak is used, Salt Cure puts Take Heart Arceus-Fairy on a timer, making it more difficult to set up, as well as making it so Arceus-Fairy is unable to Impostor-proof itself.

Eternatus: Eternatus can pressure unboosted Arceus-Fairy out with Poison-type moves. Unaware Eternatus can switch in on any Arceus-Fairy and use it as setup fodder.

Take Heart.description:
Take Heart provides boosting while denying poison from Mortal Spin, which would otherwise force it out. The Fairy-type move of choice can vary: Moonblast is the 2nd strongest Fairy move of the bunch, has higher PP, and has a decent Special Attack drop, while Revelation Dance is effective against Normalize. Leftovers allows Arceus-Fairy to not have its healing cut off by Pokemon with low attack, as well as giving it increased longevity.

Arceus-Fairy is typically splashed onto bulkier teams as a wall against threats like Mega Garchomp, Mega Sceptile, and Ash-Greninja, in addition to compressing a late-game win condition at the same time. Arceus-Fairy's solid typing and bulk mean it can serve as a good Imposter-proof to Pokemon like these. Arceus-Fairy does falter to fast Pokemon that can easily slot Steel or Poison-type coverage, like Koraidon for Fur Coat sets, and Sheer Force Ash-Greninja for Ice Scales sets, so defensive Pokemon that can stonewall them like RegenVest Dialga-O, Mega Swampert, and Zamazenta can assist with that, and, in Mega Swampert's case, provides a very valuable check to the threatening Mega Lucario. Arceus-Fairy is both stonewalled and has its healing denied by Blissey and Chansey, so a teammate with Psystrike or a similar move that can pressure them out, like Mega Gardevoir or High Jump Kick Mega Sceptile, is highly recommended.

anythinggoes.overview: Arceus-Fairy is one of the best walls in AG and one of the very few defensive Pokemon that is able to reliably check Koraidon thanks to an immunity to Dragon-type moves letting it block Scale Shot and a resistance to Low Kick and Close Combat. This forces Koraidon to use Flare Blitz to KO Arceus-Fairy, which derails its longevity. Additionally, Arceus-Fairy's good bulk allows it to soft check Pokemon such as Extreme Killer Arceus, Ho-Oh, and Giratina-O. Arceus-Fairy can sometimes be a bit passive versus Steel-types such as Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C; although, both are unable to switch in on Arceus-Fairy because it likes to carry Will-O-Wisp to cripple them. Furthermore, Eternatus is able to take on Arceus-Fairy and use Toxic on it. If not, then it can set up Toxic Spikes without taking any significant damage. Apart from these weaknesses, Arceus-Fairy is almost flawless and should always be considered on balance and bulky offense teams.
anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Arceus-Fairy can run Stealth Rock in conjunction with Ting-Lu's Spikes. Although, this means that Arceus-Fairy has to drop either a status-inducing move or Power Gem. On more offense-oriented teams, Arceus-Fairy can opt to run Taunt paired with Thunder Wave, paralyzing foes and stopping Ho-Oh, bulky Arceus formes, and Eternatus from using Recover.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM are able to brute force their way through Arceus-Fairy thanks to their powerful Steel moves. Although, both must be wary of Arceus-Fairy Terastallizing into a Water-type and burning them with Will-O-Wisp.

Kyogre: Kyogre is a great lead and likes to carry Thunder Wave to cripple Arceus-Fairy. Furthermore, Kyogre's Drizzle-boosted Origin Pulse 2HKOes Arceus-Fairy.

Tera Fire Users: Setup users such as Extreme Killer Arceus, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, Koraidon, and Calyrex-I like to run Tera Fire to block Arceus-Fairy's Will-O-Wisp. Although, Thunder Wave can cripple them.

Eternatus: Eternatus can poison Arceus-Fairy without taking any significant damage in return. Furthermore, it is able to set up Toxic Spikes, which derails Arceus-Fairy's longevity.

Calyrex-S: Calyrex-S is able to take on a low HP Arceus-Fairy with Astral Barrage or 2HKO it with Tera Ghost or Choice Specs. Although, Calyrex-S must be wary of Thunder Wave when switching in on Arceus-Fairy.

Taunt Users: Although mostly seen on offensive teams, Taunt users such as Extreme Killer Arceus and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground can prevent Arceus-Fairy from using Will-O-Wisp to burn them.

Defensive.description:
This set allows Arceus-Fairy to reliably take on Koraidon. Judgment hits Dark- and Dragon-types like Ting-Lu, Koraidon, and Miraidon super effectively, deterring Miraidon from switching in freely. It also acts as good neutral coverage that deals good damage to Calyrex-S, Arceus formes, Kyogre, and Hatterene. Power Gem gives Arceus-Fairy a reliable way of hitting Ho-Oh, having a chance at 2HKOing it. Will-O-Wisp prevents setup sweepers such as Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM, Extreme Killer Arceus, and Calyrex-I from safely switching in on Arceus-Fairy. Although, Will-O-Wisp is unable to burn Ho-Oh and Tera Fire users such as Calyrex-I, Extreme Killer Arceus, Arceus-Ground, Koraidon, and Necrozma-DM. Thunder Wave on the other hand cripples the likes of Ho-Oh, Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, Eternatus, and bulky Arceus formes, as all of them commonly switch in on Arceus-Fairy. Arceus-Fairy can opt for a dual status set to punish not only physical attackers with Will-O-Wisp but also Calyrex-S, Kyogre, and Eternatus on a switch in with Thunder Wave. Although, running this set means that Arceus-Fairy cannot do reliable damage to Ho-Oh because it is not carrying Power Gem. Tera Water allows Arceus-Fairy to check Zacian-C and Koraidon in a pinch and burn both with Will-O-Wisp. A drawback of Tera Water is that it makes Arceus-Fairy weak to Miraidon's Electro Drift, Zacian-C's Wild Charge, and Calyrex-S's Grass Knot. Additionally, Tera Water makes Arceus-Fairy no longer immune to Dragon-type moves and removes its resistance to Koraidon's Low Kick. Tera Poison on the other hand grants Arceus-Fairy an immunity to poison, lets it absorb Toxic Spikes, and makes it resist opposing Arceus-Fairy's Judgment. A major downside of both the aforementioned Tera types is that with them Arceus-Fairy is unable to block Koraidon's Scale Shot, which can cause a snowball into a quick sweep.

Arceus-Fairy is a staple on balance and bulky offense teams. Despite Arceus-Fairy being an almost flawless wall, it is still unable to check physical attackers such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM without Terastallization. Ho-Oh makes a great teammate for Arceus-Fairy, as it is able to check both because of Sacred Fire having a 50% burn chance. Also, thanks to Koraidon's omnipresent Sun, Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire can 2HKO Necrozma-DM and OHKO Zacian-C. Calyrex-S and Miraidon are able to do great amounts of damage to Arceus-Fairy; to effectively deal with them, Arceus-Fairy greatly appreciates Ting-Lu as a teammate, which can pivot in on both foes. Ting-Lu can also soft check Necrozma-DM and set up Spikes, keeping opposing sweepers on a timer. Defensive Ho-Oh and Eternatus are able to keep up with offensive Ho-Oh, with Eternatus threatening to poison it. Furthermore, Eternatus can check Kyogre and both absorb and set up Toxic Spikes whenever required. Due to being tasked to deal with so many physical attackers, Arceus-Fairy can get overwhelmed. It appreciates Choice Scarf users such as Koraidon and Calyrex-S, which can revenge kill these attackers with their powerful STAB moves. Koraidon may run Tera Steel in conjunction with Substitute and Iron Head to get the better of Arceus-Fairy, forcing it to Terastallize in most interactions. To beat Tera Steel Koraidon, Arceus-Fairy once again likes Ting-Lu as its teammate, since it is able to phaze Koraidon with Whirlwind. Necozma-DM can also beat this Koraidon set one-on-one thanks to its bulk and access to Dragon Dance. Although, both Necrozma-DM and Ting-Lu must be careful of Low Kick, which Tera Steel Koraidon can sometimes run over Substitute. Furthermore, Choice Scarf Koraidon and Calyrex-S can revenge kill this foe too.

Offensive Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy is a fantastic wallbreaker and sweeper on bulky offense and offense teams that takes advantage of the Fairy-type's amazing offensive prowess and good defensive capabilities in AG to set up against a vast majority of the metagame. Judgment hits Dragon- and Dark-types like Koraidon, Miraidon, and Ting-Lu super effectively, notably OHKOing the former two and 2HKOing Calyrex-S without any boosts. At +1, it 2HKOes neutral targets like bulky Arceus formes and Kyogre and deals significant damage to Eternatus. Power Gem allows Arceus-Fairy to break past Fire-types like Ho-Oh, Tera Fire Arceus, and Skeledirge. Tera Poison flips the matchup on Eternatus, allowing Arceus-Fairy to set up Calm Mind freely and absorb Toxic Spikes. However, it comes with the drawback of making Arceus-Fairy weak to Ting-Lu's Earthquake, though the latter needs to Terastallize into a Steel- or Poison-type to avoid taking heavy damage from boosted Judgment. Tera Poison also leaves Arceus-Fairy weak to Calyrex-S's Psychic and Psyshock, with the latter inflicting heavy damage to even a boosted Arceus-Fairy. Additionally, it makes Arceus-Fairy vulnerable to Koraidon's Scale Shot, which can revenge kill a weakened Arceus-Fairy while threatening a sweep. A Timid nature is preferred for outspeeding Modest Miraidon and max Speed Arceus formes without a Speed boosting nature, though Modest is still a viable alternative for the increased damage output, notably 2HKOing Eternatus and having a chance to OHKO Ho-Oh, both at +1.

Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy serves as an excellent addition to teams looking for a potent, self-sufficient wallbreaker and setup sweeper that applies tremendous pressure on the opponent's defensive backbone, clearing a path for teammates like Calyrex-S, Choice Scarf Koraidon, and Swords Dance Arceus to clean up late-game. Arceus-Fairy takes advantage of passive switch-ins like Ho-Oh, Ting-Lu, Landorus-T, and bulky Arceus formes to set up Calm Mind and punch holes through opposing teams. It finds ample setup opportunities to sweep against most teams; however, the lack of coverage for Steel-types, particularly Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C, renders it ineffective against them. Both are capable of surviving boosted Judgment and take advantage of Arceus-Fairy to set up Dragon Dance and Swords Dance, respectively. Necrozma-DM, backed by recovery from Moonlight, has no issues against Arceus-Fairy long-term. Due to this set not having any defensive investment, it is easily overwhelmed by strong attackers such as Calyrex-S, Swords Dance Arceus, Kyogre, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground. Arceus-Fairy also takes massive damage from Koraidon and Miraidon, but neither likes to switch in directly due to fearing an OHKO from Judgment. Hence, it appreciates teammates such as Ting-Lu, Arceus-Water, Eternatus, and Landorus-T. Ting-Lu provides entry hazard support and switches in on strong attacks such as Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage and Miraidon's Electro Drift, which threaten Arceus-Fairy out. Arceus-Water and Landorus-T help cover a myriad of physical attackers such as Koraidon, Swords Dance Arceus, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, Zacian-C, and Necrozma-DM. Landorus-T also helps to bring in Arceus-Fairy via U-turn, thereby increasing setup chances. As Arceus-Fairy is vulnerable to status, especially Thunder Wave, Eternatus is a good partner that takes on Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire and switches in on Kyogre's rain-boosted Water Spout and Origin Pulse as well as Thunder Wave. It also cripples defensive cores by spreading poison with Toxic Spikes, making it easier for Arceus-Fairy to clean up weakened teams. Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Koraidon are great revenge killers, threatening both Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C. Special walls such as Clodsire, Whirlwind Tera Grass Ho-Oh, and Calm Mind Blissey are capable of stopping Arceus-Fairy from sweeping by phazing it or shrugging off boosted hits. Thus, partners such as Choice Specs Calyrex-S, Koraidon, offensive Ho-Oh, and Swords Dance Arceus that can break the aforementioned walls make for great teammates. Koraidon and Miraidon provide opportunities for Arceus-Fairy to set up through pivoting with U-turn against common switch-ins such as defensive Arceus formes, Ho-Oh, and Ting-Lu.

Calm Mind.description:
• Flying-type Judgment is what differentiates Arceus-Flying from other Arceus formes like Arceus-Dark and Arceus-Fairy at its bulky sweeper role, since Flying-resistant Pokemon are much less common in the tier. Its immunity to Sticky Web and Toxic Spikes is also a distinct advantage, with the former immunity being especially useful against hyper offense structures. However, the lack of notable resistances makes it somewhat difficult for Arceus-Flying to reliably set up against strong attackers, especially since many outspeed Arceus-Flying such as Marshadow and Zacian-C, and a weakness to Stealth Rock means that it lacks defensive utility for the hyper offense teams it fits best on, meaning it suffers heavy competition from other Flying-types like Mega Salamence and Yveltal.
  • Taunt stops Arceus-Flying from being passive as it sets up against Pokemon like Necrozma-DM, prevents Ho-Oh from using Whirlwind against it, and limits the progress made by Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and support Arceus formes by restricting their entry hazard and status-spreading abilities. Alternatively, Refresh allows Arceus-Flying to play more aggressively, ignoring the risk of coming into status moves from Alomomola, Zygarde and Giratina-O.
  • The given EV spread allows Arceus-Flying to avoid the 2HKO from physical utility Giratina-O's Poltergeist and the OHKO from offensive support Primal Groudon's Overheat, all while 2HKOing Tera Grass Ho-Oh. The alternative EV spread maximises Arceus-Flying's offensive capabilities, notably letting it 2HKO Giratina-O with Judgment after a boost.
  • Tera Steel allows Arceus-Flying to remove its Ice and Rock weaknesses, potentially letting it set up on Pokemon like Chien-Pao, changes its Stealth Rock weakness into a resistance, and grants it a Toxic immunity, which is very useful for the less aggressive Taunt variants. Tera Fairy removes these weaknesses too alongside granting a Dark resistance, letting Arceus-Flying handle Yveltal and Arceus-Dark better and using Taunt to stop the latter from using recovery options, while keeping its Fighting resistance against Marshadow.
  • Arceus-Flying is best used mid- or late-game when the opposing team has been broken down enough so that it can clean up after one or two boosts. It should be careful about being statused though, since Taunt variants have no way to remove status, and Refresh variants have to take a turn to remove them, which could lead to the opponent getting a free opportunity to bring in a Pokemon that checks Arceus-Flying such as Zacian-C.
  • Arceus-Flying struggles greatly against Flying-resistant foes, and, although there are few in number, Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and the more niche Zekrom and Garganacl can all be problems for Arceus-Flying. Double Dance Primal Groudon and Tera Blast Ground Zacian-C are potent teammates, being able to break through the aforementioned foes, while Arceus-Flying is able to break through opposing Primal Groudon and Zygarde for them in return. Marshadow is also able to break through both Necrozma-DM and Garganacl for Arceus-Flying, as well as breaking through specially defensive walls such as Chansey for it, while Arceus-Flying can soft-check Yveltal for it in return.
  • Suicide leads such as Deoxys-S, Glimmora and Mega Diancie, that can not only provide hazard support, letting Arceus-Flying 2HKO Primal Kyogre with boosted Judgment after Stealth Rock, but deny entry hazards from opposing Pokemon such as Ferrothorn or Primal Groudon, are fantastic teammates, helping in Arceus-Flying's wallbreaking capabilities and longevity. Smeargle and Shuckle providing Sticky Web support lets Arceus-Flying outspeed opposing Calm Mind Arceus formes more consistently, letting it beat them one-on-one.

Calm Mind Arceus-Ghost is a threatening setup sweeper and utility option that leverages its great typing, bulk, and decent Speed to break through teams. With the lack of Ghost-type answers, Judgment is able to hit a vast majority of tier, providing a strong, consistent STAB option that scales quickly with Calm Mind boosts. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers like Meowscarada, Zacian-C, and Ogerpon-W, although Aura Sphere can be used to deal with most Ghost-resistant Pokemon such as Ting-Lu, Hisuian Samurott, Garganacl, and Pokemon that run Tera Normal and Tera Dark. Alternatively, Taunt shuts down Toxic from the likes of Pecharunt and Clodsire, Thunder Wave from Clefable, and Whirlwind from Ho-Oh and Ting-Lu, preventing them from hindering Arceus-Ghost’s progress. 176 Speed EVs with a Timid nature allow it to outspeed Ogerpon-W, Iron Moth, and other base 110s, letting it set up or spread status before they can retaliate. Tera Poison prevents it from being worn down by Toxic from Pecharunt, Eternatus, and Clodsire, while Tera Fairy allows Arceus-Ghost to flip its Dark weakness into a resistance, helping it withstand the likes of Roaring Moon, Weavile, and Meowscarada.

Arceus-Ghost is highly flexible and can fit onto a wide variety of team structures, as its well-rounded stats mean that almost any Pokemon can be paired with it. For example, Arceus-Ghost shines alongside Stealth Rock and Spikes setters like Clefable, Ting-Lu, and Hisuian Samurott, since Arceus-Ghost spinblocks the likes of Great Tusk while threatening it with Will-O-Wisp or boosted Judgment. Furthermore, since it can struggle against faster threats like Zacian-C, Speed slot Urshifu, and Darkrai, Arceus-Ghost appreciates Sticky Web from Ribombee, which alleviates its Speed issue. Arceus-Ghost also values Fighting-type partners such as Urshifu and Great Tusk that, just like Aura Sphere, can deal with the aforementioned Ghost-resistant Pokemon. Arceus-Ghost is also vulnerable to hazards, making hazard control in Pokemon such as Iron Treads, Corviknight, and Hatterene very important. These Pokemon, alongside other examples such as Roaring Moon, Primarina, Galarian Slowking, and Ting-Lu, can fully take advantage of Arceus-Ghost's decent but not exceptional stat donations. Although Arceus-Ghost's Speed is decent, it is still slower than threats such as the aforementioned Zacian-C, so the largest beneficiaries of a Speed donation are slow Pokemon such as Hydrapple and Hatterene.

Arceus-Ghost makes use of its good Speed, amazing bulk, and a lack of Ghost-resistant Pokemon in the tier to become a frightening setup sweeper, capable of taking advantage of common walls like Magearna and Arceus-Water. Substitute allows Arceus-Ghost to take advantage of its bulk to set up on more passive walls, such as Milotic and Garganacl, as well as block status moves from foes such as Pecharunt, Clodsire, and Magearna. Similarly, Taunt blocks status moves from non-Sablenite versions of the aforementioned Pokemon and prevents foes from healing or setting up. Will-O-Wisp can cripple Pokemon like Urshifu-R, Dragonite, Regieleki, and Kingambit, allowing either Arceus-Ghost or its teammates to take advantage of their lessened damage output. Imprison is a niche, but useful, move, allowing Arceus-Ghost to completely stonewall other Calm Mind Arceus formes; however, its utility outside of that is highly outclassed by Taunt. Ghost-resistant Pokemon such as Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Arceus as well as Gyaradosite users such as Pecharunt and Clodsire are a pain for Arceus-Ghost, as it can’t reliably break through them, although all of them fear being burned by Will-O-Wisp. Pokemon like Great Tusk and Urshifu-R are wonderful teammates for Arceus-Ghost, as they can deal with these foes. Urshifu-R, in particular, can lure in Ghost-types like Lunala and non-Gyaradosite Pecharunt for Arceus-Ghost to come in and force them out, while Great Tusk can remove entry hazards for Arceus-Ghost. Similarly, other Pokemon that can give hazard removal, such as Regieleki and Corviknight, are great teammates so that Arceus-Ghost doesn't get worn down by switching in constantly. As Arceus-Ghost doesn't have much of an offensive presence until it sets up, hazard setters like Magearna, Garganacl, Great Tusk, and Hippowdon are great teammates to help wear down bulkier Pokemon like Garganacl and Eternatus.

ubers.overview: Arceus-Ghost finds itself in a rather unique position in the tier, being the best Ghost-type in a tier run by Koraidon and also carrying an immunity to Extreme Killer Arceus's Extreme Speed. This, along with having a largely unresisted STAB type, means that Arceus-Ghost is able to find many safe opportunities to come in and wreck havoc against some of the major tier staples. It can be an offensive powerhouse on the right teams and a solid support Pokemon on others, but it does find itself held back by its lack of useful resistances. While few Pokemon can hit it super effectively, it can be still overshadowed by Arceus formes with better defensive typings.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Tera Fighting can be used over Tera Stellar if a Timid spread is opted for and the team can still aptly handle Ho-Oh. Taunt and Will-O-Wisp can also have uses on support sets over Dragon Tail and Calm Mind, but they can struggle to make progress against special attackers and can give free entry points for them. A sacrificial lead set running Stealth Rock, Healing Wish, Taunt, and Judgment is possible, as Arceus-Ghost is able to spinblock, but it is usually outclassed by the same set on Arceus-Fairy.

Checks and Counters

Ting-Lu: Not even +1 Tera Stellar Focus Blast can get close to an OHKO on Ting-Lu, which can then phaze Arceus-Ghost, and support sets find themselves quickly overwhelmed by Ruination, as well as Ting-Lu using Arceus-Ghost as a free opportunity to set up entry hazards.

Kingambit: Arceus-Ghost can struggle into Kingambit, as it cannot threaten Kingambit if it does not have Focus Blast, and even when it does, Kingambit can threaten to OHKO Arceus-Ghost with Sucker Punch with minimal chip or just a few fallen allies. Kingambit can also use Arceus-Ghost as a free setup opportunity and threaten to sweep through the entire team.

Faster Setup Pokemon: Setup threats such as Swords Dance Koraidon, Calm Mind Miraidon, and Swords Dance Zacian-C completely obliterate Arceus-Ghost and can even use it as a safe opportunity to set up, as it cannot threaten to KO them outright.

Arceus: Thanks to its immunity to Ghost-type Judgment, Arceus can safely switch into Arceus-Ghost and threaten it with Taunt or use it as setup fodder for Swords Dance.

Calm Mind + 3 Attacks.description:
This set aims to be a setup sweeper that can also prevent Iron Treads from being able to use Rapid Spin. Ghost-type Judgment is naturally resisted by very few Pokemon such as Arceus and Ting-Lu, neither of which appreciate taking a Focus Blast. Power Gem allows Arceus-Ghost to hit Ho-Oh, which can otherwise stomach a Judgment and phaze Arceus-Ghost. A Modest nature in conjunction with Tera Stellar allows for +1 Arceus-Ghost to OHKO opposing Arceus and Ho-Oh with Focus Blast and Power Gem, respectively, while also ensuring that Judgment can OHKO Zacian-C at +1.

This set is usually found on Sticky Web teams, as it can spinblock for its teammates while also being able to outspeed most of the unboosted metagame and work well alongside Pokemon such as Swords Dance Koraidon and Zacian-C, which both appreciate Ho-Oh being pressured. It can also free up Tera types for its teammates, as they will not need to run Tera Ghost to deal with Arceus. The major drawback to Arceus-Ghost is the opportunity cost of not being able to run Extreme Killer or Arceus-Ground as the Arceus forme of choice on a team. These Pokemon have far more snowballing potential, as they can use Swords Dance and Dragon Dance while also being far less entry hazard- and Tera-reliant.

Support.description:
Support Arceus-Ghost attempts to capitalize on the lack of Ghost-weak Pokemon on most teams while also providing entry hazard-stacking offense with a valuable Rapid Spin immunity, leveraging its strong natural bulk to both act as a soft check to physical attackers and also find late-game setup opportunities. It acts as a soft check to threats such as Choice Scarf Koraidon and Calyrex-I, giving it a unique role as an Arceus forme that can keep Koraidon in check without being easily exploited by Zacian-C. Ghost-type Judgment is incredibly strong, with only one relevant Ghost-resistant Pokemon and one Ghost-immune Pokemon in the entire tier in Ting-Lu and Arceus, respectively, although note that both Pokemon as well as other special walls such as Whirlwind Ho-Oh do shut it down incredibly well. Thankfully, Dragon Tail allows Arceus-Ghost to punish most of these Pokemon by forcing them off the field, with the exception of Arceus-Fairy and Tera Fairy Ho-Oh. Recover is the preferred final move of choice, as this set is not an all-out attacker but rather leverages its bulk to be an unbreakable late-game sweeper. Tera Water provides Arceus-Ghost with a resistance to Koraidon's Flare Blitz while also allowing Arceus-Ghost to survive Glacial Lance from Calyrex-I and Steel-type attacks from Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM, allowing it to safely dispatch them if they've set up. Tera Fairy maintains Arceus-Ghost's ability to check Koraidon while also providing an immunity to Dragon-type attacks from it and Miraidon. Tera Poison allows Arceus-Ghost to become immune to being poisoned by Eternatus's Toxic and Toxic Spikes while still keeping a resistance to Koraidon's Fighting-type STAB moves. A Timid nature and 56 Speed EVs allow Arceus-Ghost to outspeed all unboosted base 95 and slower Pokemon while also covering for defensive Arceus formes and Ho-Oh so that it can safely use Dragon Tail against them first.

This set is usually found on entry hazard-reliant balance builds that desperately want a spinblocker, but it can also be seen on standard hyper offense teams for similar reasons. It works well alongside bulky hazard setters such as Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Ting-Lu; Eternatus can also work here, as Toxic Spikes can be incredibly deadly for opposing teams if they are unable to remove them. Sadly, support Arceus-Ghost does run into a plethora of issues, most notably because it isn't Arceus-Fairy or -Water and therefore does not resist Koraidon's harder-to-check attacking moves in Scale Shot, Outrage and Flare Blitz as well as Draco Meteor from Miraidon and Origin Pulse from Kyogre. Ghost is not a premier typing for an Arceus forme to have, as having a defensive backbone where one of its core parts is unable to safely check either Koraidon or Miraidon can lead to Arceus-Ghost and its teammates being more easily pressured into Terastallizing to handle either of these threats, which can lead to teams having far weaker Terastallization flexibility.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Arceus-Ghost's singular Ghost typing gives it a unique presence both offensively and defensively. For the hyper offense structures it fits on, it serves as a check to Extreme Killer Arceus, as well as a spinblocker against Rapid Spin Smeargle. With Ghostium Z, Arceus-Ghost makes for a strong wallbreaker that is able to push past would-be checks such as Zygarde and defensive Ho-Oh.

  • However, Dark-types such as Yveltal and Arceus-Dark are a major nuisance for Arceus-Ghost, especially their defensive variants that can take hits with ease. Meanwhile, other Ghost-types, such as Marshadow and Lunala, don't have to worry about them as much due to their superior coverage combined with access to Terastalization.

  • Additionally, taking up a Z-Move slot on the hyper offense teams it is mandatory on makes it hard to justify over Ultra Necrozma and Chi-Yu, both of which perform similar roles to it. There's also the issue of it taking up the Arceus slot compared to using Extreme Killer Arceus or Arceus-Ground, both of which are more consistent. Regardless, Arceus-Ghost's combination of offensive and defensive traits, as well as it being naturally Imposter-proof against Ditto, carves it a small niche.

  • Swords Dance allows Arceus-Ghost to OHKO Zygarde and defensive Primal Groudon with +2 Never-Ending Nightmare as well as offensive Eternatus with +2 Shadow Force. Alternatively, Dragon Dance allows it to outspeed Chien-Pao, Zacian-C, and Deoxys-A, preventing the former from revenge killing it as easily. Arceus-Ghost can still OHKO defensive Ho-Oh and defensive Primal Kyogre with +1 Never-Ending Nightmare, as well as Necrozma-DM and Giratina-O with +1 Shadow Force, even if its wallbreaking capabilities are limited.

  • Shadow Force is mostly used to provide the strongest possible Never-Ending Nightmare for Arceus-Ghost. Its two-turn nature can be awkward, which is why Ghostium Z is needed for circumvent this issue . More notably though, this makes Arceus-Ghost Imposter-proofed against Ditto, since the latter will always outspeed it, thus never hitting it if they both use Shadow Force at the same time.

  • Stone Edge allows Arceus-Ghost to snipe Ho-Oh and Yveltal, removing Arceus-Ghost's need to use its Z-Move to OHKO the former to prevent it from phazing. Unboosted Stone Edge OHKOes offensive Ho-Oh and can more reliably OHKO defensive Ho-Oh and specially offensive Yveltal after a boost.

  • Alternatively, Brick Break enables Arceus-Ghost to 2HKO Arceus-Dark and Arceus at +1. It also hits more niche targets, such as Chien-Pao, Garganacl, and Kingambit, that may be annoying for Arceus-Ghost to deal with. It should be noted that both coverage options hit Chi-Yu super effectively, although +2 Shadow Force OHKOes it regardless.

  • Extreme Speed is a niche option that can snipe Deoxys-A for Swords Dance variants while limiting Yveltal and Chien-Pao's ability to revenge kill it with Sucker Punch, but it is quite weak and only works well against opposing offense teams, not bulkier ones.

  • Substitute protects Arceus-Ghost from harmful status conditions, such as burn from Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire and poison from Alomomola's Toxic, and limits Yveltal's and Chien-Pao's ability to revenge kill it with priority moves. Dragon Dance variants also benefit from Substitute limiting Marshadow's ability to pick it off with Shadow Sneak too; however, it can simply outspeed and bypass Substitute with Spectral Thief against Swords Dance variants.

  • Alternatively, Taunt denies status moves, whether it be entry hazards from Ferrothorn or opposing setup such as Coil Zygarde and Curse Dondozo, preventing the former from reliably checking it. It also maintains hazards against Ho-Oh and Giratina-O. Recover is a niche option that provides Arceus-Ghost more longevity, but it is much less useful than the other two options.

  • The first given EV spread is ideal for Swords Dance variants, allowing Arceus-Ghost to survive Choice Band Marshadow's Tera Ghost Shadow Sneak, and maximum Speed investment lets it Speed tie with Modest Palkia-O and Adamant Mega Salamence, although this may be problematic against Substitute variants of the former.

  • Alternatively, the second EV spread is used for Dragon Dance variants. It still avoids the OHKO from Choice Band Marshadow's Tera Ghost Shadow Sneak—now after Stealth Rock—as well as Choice Band Tera Flying Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent and wallbreaker Primal Kyogre's Origin Pulse. However, it also makes Arceus-Ghost significantly slower; it is unable to outspeed fully invested Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre, but it does still outspeed Deoxys-A after a boost.

  • Arceus-Ghost relies heavily on Ghostium Z to maximize its wallbreaking capabilities against Coil Zygarde, defensive Primal Groudon, and support Arceus formes. It should only be used against these bulkier foes and not frailer targets such as Deoxys-A and Mega Mewtwo Y. This is especially true for Swords Dance variants that focus more on wallbreaking early- or mid game than sweeping.

  • Dragon Dance variants of Arceus-Ghost should be preserved until late-game where Dark-types such as Arceus-Dark and Yveltal have been worn down significantly either by hazards or by teammates such as Meteor Beam Eternatus and Mega Salamence. Waiting until late-game also minimizes the risk of a sudden Terastalization, such as Tera Dark Ho-Oh and Arceus-Fairy, even if these are niche situations. Arceus-Ghost does not need significant boosts to clean up weakened teams.

  • Pokemon that are able to break through Dark-types are greatly appreciated. Zacian-C can use offensive variants of Yveltal and Arceus-Dark as setup fodder due to resisting all their STAB options barring the niche Heat Wave from Yveltal. Meteor Beam Eternatus does well against defensive Yveltal and defensive Arceus-Dark while also sniping Ho-Oh. Both of these partners appreciate Arceus-Ghost's ability to break past common defensive Pokemon, such as Primal Groudon, Zygarde, and Ho-Oh.

  • Suicide leads are essential for supporting Arceus-Ghost. Smeargle and Shuckle are great for Swords Dance variants, making up for its low Speed and preventing Chien-Pao and Marshadow from easily revenge killing it. Deoxys-S and Glimmora work well with Dragon Dance variants, making up for its lesser power with hazard support; this also limits Choice Scarf Yveltal's ability to switch into Arceus-Ghost, since it can be OHKOed by +1 Stone Edge after Stealth Rock. They all appreciate Arceus-Ghost discouraging Giratina-O and Ho-Oh from removing their hazards via Defog, if not denying removal entirely with Taunt.

balancedhackmons.overview: Arceus-Ghost is one of the most defining centerpieces of Balanced Hackmons thanks to its built-in self Imposter-proofing due to Spooky Plate + Judgment that allows it to run Shore Up without worrying about Imposter, good bulk, great offensive typing, and versatility. It is able to soft check a lot of would-be annoyances such as RegenVest Celesteela without Nuzzle and Mega Lucario depending on its ability. Its ability to block Rapid Spin also differentiates it from other Arceus formes. However, Arceus-Ghost can be hard walled rather easily by certain walls such as Mega Audino and Meloetta. Its low immediate damage output can also lead to fast offensive threats like Eternatus forcing it out. Its ability choice of Magic Guard or Fur Coat also mean it either has limited defensive presence or is a physical wall that's weak to Choice Band Ash-Greninja, respectively.
balancedhackmons.comments:
Other Options

Thunder Cage can constantly chip down most bulkier walls and hits Celesteela hard, but Mortal Spin is generally better at chipping down walls on utility sets, which leaves Thunder Cage mostly just for Celesteela. Other offensive abilities such as Speed Boost and Good as Gold can be chosen over Fur Coat on the setup set, but this provides little defensive utility and would leave Arceus-Ghost with fewer opportunities to set up. Taunt is an option on the setup set to deny recovery and other utility such as Spikes and Topsy-Turvy, but giving up a moveslot for utility such as Knock Off or coverage is often not desirable. Plus, it either locks Arceus-Ghost into using Judgment as its only attack or means it has no recovery, both of which are very easily exploitable.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Arceus-Ghost struggles against most Dark-type foes in general, especially faster attackers such as Ash-Greninja. However, they dislike switching in on Secret Sword or Knock Off especially with entry hazards up. Magic Guard Yveltal in particular, however, is a great annoyance, as it completely halts anything Arceus-Ghost can do.

Normal-type Walls: Blissey and Mega Audino handily beat setup sets via Topsy-Turvy and their immunity to Judgment, although Blissey needs to watch out for Secret Sword. Utility sets are hard stopped by Magic Guard Blissey, and even if it is not running Magic Guard, Arceus-Ghost can only make progress through Knock Off and Spikes.

Faster Threats: Most faster threats, like Flutter Mane, Eternatus, and Mega Alakazam, threaten Arceus-Ghost out with direct damage. They can't really switch in, however.

Status Effects: Fur Coat Arceus-Ghost sets hate status, as chip damage from poison cuts heavily into its longevity, and paralysis completely cripples it. Magic Guard sets don't mind poison but still dislike paralysis.

Ice Scales + Take Heart Arceus Formes: Ice Scales Acreus amplified with Take Heart's Special Defense boosts means that all of Arceus-Ghost's attacks, including Secret Sword, will do basically no damage to these Arceus formes. Many of them also carry a Plate, which means they can easily sponge Knock Off.

Utility.description:
Arceus-Ghost can provide very consistent utility to its team with its immunity to item removal and built in self-Imposter-proofing through Judgment. Shore Up is the preferred healing move because it isn't blocked by the likes of Blissey and Mega Audino, but Strength Sap heals more HP at once and fares better against Choice Band users. Knock Off removes crucial items from walls like Heavy-Duty Boots and Covert Cloak from Mega Audino, making them susceptible to entry hazard damage or getting poisoned by Mortal Spin. Potentially removing Eviolite from Imposter users is also nice but should not be relied on, as these foes rarely want to switch in on Arceus-Ghost. Spikes takes advantage of Arceus-Ghost's conventional switch-ins, like Blissey, being passive and lacking hazard removal; alternatively, Rapid Spin and Mortal Spin provide hard-to-block hazard removal. Magic Guard is the preferred ability, as it provides an immunity to entry hazards and other chip damage such as Salt Cure and Mortal Spin, but Fur Coat makes Arceus-Ghost function as more of a wall capable of soft checking foes like Koraidon.

Arceus-Ghost fits well on entry hazard-stacking teams, as it can easily provide item removal support and reliably block Rapid Spin. Teams that stack hazard-immune teammates also enjoy Arceus-Ghost as a Knock Off absorber. Most attackers such as Ash-Greninja or and Eternatus appreciate Arceus-Ghost stacking Spikes to wear away at their checks or, in Eternatus's case, directly damage checks like Ice Scales Arceus formes. Other teammates such as RegenVest Celesteela and Mega Audino also synergize well with Arceus-Ghost defensively alongside the occasional Imposter-proofing Arceus-Ghost can provide for them. Arceus-Ghost is particularly vulnerable to Dark-types and opposing Ghost-types that are faster such as Ash-Greninja, Yveltal, and Flutter Mane; therefore, checks to them like the aforementioned Mega Audino are valuable.

Setup Sweeper.description:
Setup Arceus-Ghost acts as a fairly dangerous Imposter-proof sweeper that can also function as a bulky physical wall. Shore Up provides consistent recovery and isn't stopped by Strength Sap blockers like Blissey and Mega Audino, the latter of which Arceus-Ghost can't feasibly threaten; alternatively, Strength Sap has higher instant healing and makes it much more solid against physical attackers and Imposter users. Nasty Plot provides an immediately threatening boost, letting Arceus-Ghost immediately 2HKO neutral non-Ice Scales Arceus formes without any prior chip damage. Torch Song boosts slower but damages while boosting and provides a strong tool against RegenVest Celesteela. Take Heart bolsters Arceus-Ghost's special bulk and gets rid of crippling status such as paralysis from Glare and poison from Mortal Spin, but it is not advised if not using Strength Sap or Knock Off, as Imposter users can wall Arceus-Ghost barring critical hits. Knock Off is the preferred last move, as it removes crucial items such as Heavy-Duty Boots from the likes of Mega Audino and Assault Vest from Celesteela. Secret Sword is an alternative that provides no support but ensures Arceus-Ghost can break through Blissey and certain Take Heart Arceus formes such as Ice Scales Arceus-Electric if running Take Heart itself.

Arceus-Ghost best functions as both a sturdy physical wall early-game and a late-game wincon when most of its checks have been chipped down or crippled, so it pairs well with early- to mid-game wallbreakers or defensive progress-makers, such as Mega Garchomp and Spikes users like Mega Audino; Arceus-Ghost can in return help Imposter-proof them or block Rapid Spin. Arceus-Ghost enjoys entry hazard support in particular, as it forces a lot of switches after setting up, forcing quite a bit of free chip damage. Arceus-Ghost is mostly checked by Mega Audino, so another teammate that can pressure it such as Eternatus is also helpful. Arceus-Ghost should not be used as your only physical wall, as it is very vulnerable to Choice Band Ash-Greninja, and Shore Up sets can be prone to running out of PP in longer games; therefore, another physical wall such as Fur Coat Mega Audino or Fur Coat Zacian pairs well with it.

Calm Mind + Taunt.description: Arceus-Grass is a potent stallbreaker and sweeper in Ubers UU thanks to its excellent bulk and decent typing enabling it to repeatedly Calm Mind. Taunt blocks common anti-setup measures like Roar from Solgaleo and Giratina and Encore from Magearna and Ogerpon-H, allowing Arceus-Grass to stack massive amounts of boosts. Recover allows Arceus-Grass to check Pokemon like Palafin and Palkia-O throughout the course of the game, as well as giving it multiple attempts to sweep. Tera Poison grants Arceus-Grass a resistance to Poison-type attacks from Pokemon like Sneasler and Arceus-Poison, along with removing its other weaknesses like to Ice- and Fire-type moves from Kyurem-W and Chi-Yu. Alternatively, Tera Fairy can be opted for, as its ability to block Dragon Tail from the likes of Dialga and Giratina removes some of the only defensive counterplay to Arceus-Grass that's not covered by Taunt. Arceus-Grass is forced out by foes like Ogerpon-H, Tera Fire Zacian, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Poison, so Pokemon that can handle these threats like Toxapex, Giratina, and Landorus-T are excellent partners. Arceus-Grass can check Pokemon like Palkia-O, Palafin, and Landorus for its teammates, which Pokemon like Chi-Yu, Solgaleo, and Zamazenta-C appreciate. Arceus-Grass can struggle to break through Grass-resistant foes like Dialga and Galarian Slowking, so Pokemon like Chi-Yu and Landorus that can remove them pair excellently with it.

Calm Mind.description:
• Arceus-Ground serves as one of the tier's best special attackers, working as a strong wallbreaker and setup sweeper with Judgment and a coverage move of choice thanks to its strong matchups into top Pokemon, such as Primal Groudon and Eternatus. Arceus-Ground also works as a sweeper by saving its HP for late-game after its checks have been worn down. It typically fits best on bulky offense and balance teams.
  • Calm Mind boosts Arceus's already-strong Special Attack and Special Defense. While the offensive upside is obvious, it is also valuable defensively. At +1, Arceus-Ground survives attacks such as defensive Primal Kyogre's Scald and Life Orb Deoxys-A's Ice Beam. Arceus-Ground can set up on Pokémon that it forces out such as Meteor Beam Eternatus and offensive utility Primal Groudon.
  • Judgment hits key targets for super effective damage, such as OHKOing offensive Zacian-C, offensive Primal Groudon, and Meteor Beam Eternatus. Defensive Primal Groudon is OHKOed after Stealth Rock and a layer of Spikes. At +1, Judgment threatens to 2HKO defensive Arceus sets, such as Arceus-Dark and Arceus-Water, along with securing the 2HKO on defensive Necrozma-DM. Also at +1, Judgment OHKOs defensive Primal Groudon and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM while 2HKOing offensive Primal Kyogre and Calyrex-I.
  • Ice Beam provides coverage for Flying-type Pokemon, OHKOing offensive Mega Salamence, Zygarde, and Rayquaza. It also 2HKOes offensive Yveltal sets and does good chip damage to Giratina-O.
  • Power Gem also hits Flying-types for super effective damage, even if it misses out on hitting Dragon-types such as Giratina-O and Zygarde. One major benefit to running Power Gem, however, is hitting Ho-Oh. Defensive Ho-Oh walls Ice Beam variants but gets 2HKOed by Power Gem, forcing it to Terastallize if it wants to continue to wall Arceus-Ground.
  • Recover is used to prevent Arceus-Ground from getting worn down over the course of a game by healing off damage from entry hazards or weak moves such as Alomomola's Flip Turn. It can also be used to soft check certain attackers in a pinch, such letting Life Orb Marshadow chip itself down into range of Judgment, or helping Arceus-Ground beat defensive Primal Groudon and Eternatus more reliably.
  • An alternative EV spread of 72 HP / 60 Def / 252 SpA / 124 Spe with a Modest nature can be used. This spread gives it an excellent matchup against Trick Room teams, as after Tera Water, it is 3HKOed by Choice Band Melmetal's Double Iron Bash and Choice Band Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance, and it has enough offensive EVs to OHKO uninvested Eternatus with Judgment and OHKO uninvested Zygarde with Ice Beam. Without Tera, Arceus-Ground also survives two offensive Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strikes, and it can survive Draco Meteor from Choice Specs Eternatus after a layer of Spikes. The downside of using this spread comes primarily at the cost of lowering its Speed, letting it get outsped by maximum speed Arceus formes and Palkia-O.
  • Tera Ground is used to bolster the offensive power of Judgment, turning defensive Necrozma-DM from a likely 2HKO after Leftovers to a guaranteed 2HKO. It also secures the OHKO against defensive Primal Groudon and turns specially defensive Eternatus from a 2HKO into a likely OHKO after hazard damage. It also allows Arceus-Ground to brute force past potential checks such as defensive Primal Kyogre and Arceus-Water.
  • Tera Water turns Arceus-Ground's weaknesses to Ice-type and Water-type moves into resistances, which allows it to beat defensive Primal Kyogre easily while also handling offensive variants, albeit less comfortably. Tera Water also flips the matchup against Calyrex-I, allowing Arceus-Ground to tank Glacial Lance.
  • This Arceus-Ground set is best applicable to bulky offensive and balance teams. Its raw strength and good bulk allow it to come into the game multiple times to get setup opportunities. It enjoys hazard support from teammates such as Primal Groudon. Another option is Wish support, such as Alomomola, whose Wish and Flip Turn combination allows Arceus-Ground to be brought in against many of the tier's threats. Alomomola also serves as a status absorber for Arceus-Ground. Choice Band Rayquaza is another great partner to pivot Arceus-Ground into the game while also OHKOing wallbreaker Primal Kyogre. It also serves as a stallbreaker, a needed role on Arceus-Ground teams, as it struggles to break stall teams long-term.
  • Other good partners for Arceus-Ground include strong physical attackers such as Choice Band Marshadow, whose strength allows it to break through special walls that Arceus-Ground may struggle to break through, such as Ho-Oh and support Arceus formes, and other special setup Pokemon such as Calm Mind Primal Kyogre.

Physical Setup Sweeper.description:
• Physical Arceus-Ground is an excellent wallbreaker and sweeper on hyper and bulky offense teams. It easily finds turns to boost due to scaring out common Pokemon such as Primal Groudon and Necrozma-DM. Additionally, physical Arceus-Ground benefits from the presence of the more common defensive and Calm Mind Arceus-Ground sets, as it is able to beat switch-ins expecting to check other Arceus-Ground sets such as Primal Kyogre and Palkia-O.
  • Dragon Dance is Arceus-Ground's primary boosting move. Alternatively, Swords Dance is a viable option, as Sticky Web support enables Arceus-Ground to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame with the exception of specially offensive Yveltal.
  • Arceus-Ground's last moveslot should be tailored to best support its team. On hyper offense teams, Taunt prevents Pokemon such as Giratina-O and Yveltal from removing entry hazards while also protecting Arceus-Ground from status moves. Recover enables Arceus-Ground to perform the defensive duties expected of it on bulky offense teams, such as switching into Primal Groudon multiple times while remaining healthy enough to sweep late-game. Healing Wish is also an option on hyper offense teams to give a teammate such as Zacian-C or Ultra Necrozma a second chance at sweeping.
  • As Ultra Necrozma is a staple on hyper offense teams, Arceus-Ground typically equips an Earth Plate. However, bulky offense teams appreciate Arceus-Ground's ability to OHKO Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and wallbreaker Primal Kyogre after Stealth Rock with Tectonic Rage. Arceus-Ground's ability to OHKO defensive Primal Groudon and utility Arceus formes with Tectonic Rage after a Swords Dance is appreciated by many Sticky Web teams.
  • The given EV spread maximizes Arceus-Ground's mixed bulk while allowing it to outspeed Primal Groudon and maximize damage output. This ensures that it outspeeds most of the defensive metagame and can revenge kill Pokemon such as Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre. The defensive investment prevents Arceus-Ground from being OHKOed by Necrozma-DM's Searing Sunraze Smash, Life Orb Deoxys-A's Psycho Boost, and after a layer of Spikes, Choice Band Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent, Choice Band Melmetal's Double Iron Bash, and Choice Specs Eternatus's Draco Meteor. Arceus-Ground also survives Tectonic Rage and +1 Tera Ground Earthquake from opposing Arceus-Ground.
  • Tera Ground enables Arceus-Ground to OHKO some targets without a boost, such as Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM after a single layer of Spikes and defensive Primal Groudon after Stealth Rock and a layer of Spikes. Tera Rock is an alternate option to OHKO switch-ins such as Mega Salamence switching in on a Dragon Dance after Stealth Rock with Stone Edge. At +1, Tera Rock Stone Edge OHKOes defensive Yveltal and 2HKOes Giratina-O after Stealth Rock. Tera Rock can also be used defensively to resist common priority move such as Arceus's and Rayquaza's Extreme Speed.
  • On hyper offense teams, Arceus-Ground is best used as a mid-game wallbreaker to remove Pokemon such as Primal Groudon, Ho-Oh, and Necrozma-DM. On bulky offense teams, it is best used early-game due to its positive matchups against both common hazard setters such as Primal Groudon and Defoggers such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal. Arceus-Ground should be kept reasonably healthy, as it is often able to sweep late-game after a boost. It also struggles against stall teams, as it is walled by Dondozo and phazed by Giratina-O, though Taunt is disruptive to many stall teams.
  • Shuckle is a great Sticky Web user to enable Swords Dance Arceus-Ground. Kyurem-B synergizes well with Arceus-Ground, as it is able to break through Dondozo and exploit Tera Grass Ho-Oh, which walls Arceus-Ground. Zacian-C also appreciates Arceus-Ground's efficacy in removing Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh while helping against Arceus-Dark. Specially offensive Yveltal is also a great partner that threatens most of the defensive metagame and dissuades Ditto from using Earthquake after copying Arceus-Ground.
  • On bulky offense teams, utility Swords Dance Primal Groudon provides Stealth Rock support and a switch-in to Primal Kyogre, which scares out an unboosted Arceus-Ground. Choice Band Marshadow is an excellent teammate that is able to revenge kill Pokemon such as Ultra Necrozma and Zacian-C, which threaten a chipped Arceus-Ground.

Defensive.description:
• Arceus-Ground covers a wide variety of foes and utility roles, thanks to its solid mixed bulk and wide movepool. Its typing hits some of the most relevant threats in the metagame super effectively while also giving it few weaknesses and relevant resistances, allowing it to answer a variety of foes such as Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, Eternatus, and Yveltal and turning it into a versatile pick for a wide variety of team structures.
  • Toxic allows Arceus-Ground to hinder switch-ins immune to Judgment like Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, Mega Salamence, and Yveltal; Ice Beam alternatively complements Judgment to hit all previously mentioned foes but Ho-Oh, as well as Zygarde, super effectively. Taunt prevents entry hazards from Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Ferrothorn, Defog from Ho-Oh and Giratina-O, disruptive moves such as Glare, Toxic, and Will-O-Wisp from Zygarde, Yveltal, and Giratina-O, and setup and recovery moves from Zygarde, Primal Groudon, and Necrozma-DM, rendering them easier to beat.
  • Stealth Rock provides general utility to support the rest of Arceus-Ground's team, helping wallbreaking allies such as Primal Groudon and Zacian-C to net more OHKOs as they force switches.
  • The given EV spread avoids a 2HKO from Life Orb Marshadow's Low Kick after Stealth Rock and a 2HKO from Zacian-C's Play Rough after Intrepid Sword and Stealth Rock. The Speed investment ensures Arceus-Ground outspeeds fully invested Primal Groudon, and the remaining EVs are used on Special Attack to raise the odds to OHKO Zacian-C and Zekrom after Stealth Rock with Judgment.
  • Arceus-Ground is a Pokemon that doesn't Terastallize often, as its allies usually make better use of the mechanic. Tera Poison renders it unable to check Ground-types such as Primal Groudon, opposing Arceus-Ground, and Zygarde and makes it weaker to Stealth Rock. However, Tera Poison raises the accuracy of Toxic, increases Arceus-Ground's longevity by making it immune to Toxic itself from foes such as Giratina-O, Ho-Oh, and Yveltal, enables it to wall further foes such as Marshadow and Eternatus, and lets it absorb Eternatus's Toxic Spikes, supporting its team with entry hazard control.
  • Arceus-Ground's special bulk can be too lacking at times to handle foes such as Mega Mewtwo Y and Lunala; as such, it appreciates partners to make a defensive core with, such as Ho-Oh, Necrozma-DM, and Yveltal. Water-types such as Primal Kyogre, Palkia-O, and Arceus-Water can easily break past Arceus-Ground; therefore, it appreciates Pokemon on its side like Primal Groudon, Eternatus, and Ferrothorn to handle them.
  • Wallbreakers that can break past foes Arceus-Ground can't do much against on its own are valuable to ease progress. For example, Zacian-C threatens Giratina-O and Mega Mewtwo Y for Arceus-Ground sets without Toxic, Primal Kyogre covers Ho-Oh and Zygarde for variants without both Ice Beam and Toxic, and Marshadow can make progress against Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Primal Groudon independently of Arceus-Ground's set, especially with Stealth Rock support from Arceus-Ground to wear down the other team.

Arceus-Ground boasts amazing defensive capabilities, effectively checking wallbreakers such as Great Tusk and Raging Bolt, while also maintaining a formidable offensive presence. Ice Beam offers a valuable coverage option that deals significant damage to opposing Arceus-Ground, Great Tusk, and Dragonite. Alternatively, Power Gem can be employed to counter foes like Ho-Oh, which would otherwise force Arceus-Ground to switch out. Gravity may also be used to enable Arceus-Ground to neutralize common Latiasite users, such as Magearna, Garganacl, and Pecharunt, as well as Flying-types like Ho-Oh and Corviknight, rendering them vulnerable to Judgment. Calm Mind amplifies Arceus-Ground's potential as a setup sweeper, whereas Will-O-Wisp enhances its defensive utility by crippling physical attackers. It can also be employed as a Stealth Rock user, as most Sablenite foes such as Magearna, Garganacl, and Pecharunt find it really difficult to switch into. The Speed EVs allow Arceus-Ground to outspeed Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk. Arceus-Ground's versatility as both an offensive and defensive Pokemon makes it an excellent addition to all team archetypes. Pairing it with other defensive partners like Magearna, Corviknight, and Pecharunt creates a robust defensive core, allowing them to check each other's weaknesses, such as the former two being able to check Ice-types like Weavile and Baxcalibur, while Arceus-Ground switches into Fire-type foes. Arceus-Ground struggles to counter Water-type Pokemon such as Arceus-Water and Urshifu-R, making Pokemon like Raging Bolt, Eternatus, and Regieleki valuable partners, with the latter also providing entry hazard removal support.

ubers.overview: Arceus-Ground is one of the tier's most dangerous sweepers, exploiting the tier’s scarcity of Ground-type checks and the valuable offensive benefits of its Ground typing. Very few Pokemon in the tier can take its Earthquake and Stone Edge, making it a ferocious sweeper that can decimate many teams after a single Dragon Dance. Arceus-Ground is also a Ground-type sweeper that Ho-Oh, the most common Ground immunity and physical check, cannot check without Terastallization. However, the few Ground-type checks are among the best Pokemon in the tier, despite their scarcity, with Arceus-Water in particular being difficult for Arceus-Ground to get past. Phazing is also not uncommon in the tier, with Giratina-O, Arceus-Water, and Terastallized Ho-Oh being bulky enough to consistently phaze Arceus-Ground. Furthermore, because of Species Clause, Arceus-Ground's lack of bulk compared to other Arceus formes and the fact it cannot be used alongside Arceus-Fairy makes it incredibly difficult to justify using it outside of offense.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Lead Arceus-Ground can use Tera Fairy to block Scale Shot from Koraidon, which can more easily allow a teammate to revenge kill it without the Speed boost being gained. It can also use Tera Ground to break things offensively, notably being guaranteed to 2HKO maximum HP investment Kyogre. Power Gem can also be used in place of Ice Beam, allowing for more pressure against Ho-Oh at the cost of the coverage for Landorus-T and Gliscor. Recover can be used in place of Ice Beam, which is aiming to target teams without a Ground immunity. This provides excellent longevity and pressure against said teams but at the cost of consistency due to the prevalence of targets like Ho-Oh and Landorus-T.

Dragon Dance.description:
Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground is one of the most dangerous sweepers in the tier, to the extent that opposing teams can be measured by their ability to deal with it. It is found in a wide range of team structures, but is most commonly seen on hyper offense. With minimal help from entry hazards, Arceus-Ground can break through the majority of the tier's non-Ground-resistant Pokemon at +1, and after Tera Ground, it bursts through those that are bulky enough to barely tank one Earthquake. Arceus-Ground can humiliate passive checks with Recover. Arceus-Ground is well known for its diverse coverage options such as Ice Beam, which can OHKO Landorus-T and physically defensive Gliscor after Stealth Rock, even with an Adamant nature, while providing consistent chip damage against physically defensive Groudon and Giratina-O to facilitate a later sweep. Taunt stops foes' phazing and status moves such as Roar or Will-O-Wisp from defensive Arceus formes and Whirlwind from Ho-Oh, in addition to stopping opposing Pokemon such as Extreme Killer Arceus, Trick Room Necrozma-DM, Calyrex-I, Tera Flying Zacian-C, and Air Balloon Kingambit attempting to boost against it with their natural bulk or surprise immunities. Flare Blitz not only provides coverage against Skarmory, Corviknight, Air Balloon Kingambit, and Tera Steel Giratina-O, but is also boosted by the omnipresent Sun in the tier, letting it OHKO Calyrex-Ice at +1. Other options such as Gravity, Substitute, Supercell Slam, and Outrage are occasionally seen, contributing to the unpredictability of Arceus-Ground.

Tera Ground hits damage benchmarks after one Dragon Dance, such as guaranteeing an OHKO on Koraidon, a favored damage roll of OHKOing physically defensive Kyogre after Stealth Rock or one layer of Spikes, and 2HKOing the bulkiest sets of Arceus even if they have Iron Defense. Tera Fire provides burn immunity, voiding attempts to burn Arceus-Ground from Terastallized Ho-Oh with Sacred Fire or Will-O-Wisp users such as Skeledirge. Tera Fairy provides an important immunity to Scale Shot and Dragon Tail, which can give Arceus-Ground a critical Dragon Dance opportunity to turn the tables.

Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground appreciates teammates that can take care of Giratina-O and Kyogre — especially the Air Balloon variant — for its late-game sweeping. Teammates such as Koraidon, Eternatus, and Kyogre help deal with and chip opposing Kyogre. Ting-Lu and physically defensive Ho-Oh can reliably take hits from Giratina-O and make progress against it. Terapagos provides entry hazard removal, status spreading, and emergency phazing that are valuable to help Arceus-Ground reach its sweeping position easier. Additionally, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground will require extra caution and patience against potential Air Balloon users, such as Kyogre, Kingambit, and occasionally Necrozma-DM.

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Arceus-Ground is a core defensive Pokemon that soft checks various physical threats while threatening a sweep late-game, allowing it to fit on bulky offense and occasionally on hyper offense. The coverage enables it to hit the majority of the tier, and its exceptional bulk allows it to set up Calm Mind against physical threats such as Necrozma-DM, Groudon, Ho-Oh, and even Zacian-C without an Intrepid Sword boost. The Ground typing provides it a STAB move with wide coverage and an immunity to paralysis that is valuable with the increasing usage of Thunder Wave on Arceus formes.

This variant of Arceus-Ground appreciates teammates that helps to overcome obstacles such as Kyogre, Giratina-O, and Ting-Lu. Koraidon being omnipresent in the tier definitely helps to threaten Ting-Lu and ease the pressure from Kyogre. Ho-Oh's ability to spread burn helps to cut opposing Pokemon's longevity, which also provides crucial advantages for Calm Mind Arceus-Ground in a prolonged Calm Mind war. Terapagos, Giratina-O, and Eternatus provide entry hazard removal and status spreading, which are also very helpful for Calm Mind Arceus-Ground to perform. Zacian-C, with its Fairy-type STAB moves and Wild Charge, can threaten lethal damage on all three of Kyogre, Giratina-O, and Ting-Lu. Tera Poison helps this set to stand against threats from Toxic users, such as Eternatus, Terapagos, and Gliscor; meanwhile, it also removes Arceus-Ground's Water weakness, which is critical against Kyogre, although caution is needed to play around a potential Thunder Wave. Tera Fairy provides a critical resistance to Koraidon's STAB moves, which helps Arceus-Ground win one-on-one versus the best Pokemon of the tier. Tera Water provides Fire, Ice, and Steel resistances that help Arceus-Ground to deal with Koraidon's Fire-type moves, Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance, Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, and Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike. Tera Ground secures important KOs, such as 2HKOing Kyogre at +1 and OHKOing Zacian-C, while providing advantages in Calm Mind wars against opposing Arceus formes.

The bulk investment ensures Arceus-Ground endures two attacks from Koraidon other than five-hit Scale Shot; 124 Speed EVs allow Arceus-Ground to outspeed maximum Speed base 90s such as Kyogre, Ho-Oh, and Groudon. An alternative spread of 252 HP / 180 Def / 76 Spe with a Timid Nature allows Arceus-Ground to outspeed maximum Speed Lunala, which helps in Calm Mind wars against it, and maximum Speed Rayquaza but with the price of possibly getting 2HKOed by Koraidon. Another option is 252 HP / 240 Def / 16 Spe, which lets Arceus-Ground outpace only maximum Speed Necrozma-DM and neutral-nature maximum Speed base 90s but provides more bulk.

Lead.description:
Arceus-Ground finds itself in an interesting position, using an effective Stealth Rock lead set as the mandatory Arceus slot most teams require. With Judgment and Ice Beam, this set can threaten most Pokemon with either super effective or strong neutral damage, allowing it to not be as passive as some other entry hazard leads like Deoxys-S and Glimmora. Thunder Wave dissuades setup attempts from Pokemon like Koraidon, Lunala, and opposing setup Arceus formes trying to take advantage of a Stealth Rock attempt. The given EV spread allows Arceus-Ground to outspeed Lunala, with maximum Special Attack and the remaining EVs in HP. Notably, having the Special Attack investment means the best anti-hazard tool in the tier, Hatterene, cannot safely switch into Judgment, as it will always 2HKO. A Poison Tera type is useful to cover for Toxic Spikes from opposing Eternatus or Glimmora should Arceus-Ground stick around into a longer game, since it will rarely Terastallize using this set but appreciates any utility if it is forced to do so.

Lead Arceus-Ground is essentially relegated to hyper offense teams, meaning most strong setup Pokemon are its best teammates. Swords Dance Koraidon, Meteor Beam Lunala, and Swords Dance or Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, among others, are the best partners for this set, since they can naturally swing a game as soon as Arceus-Ground goes down after setting entry hazards. Necrozma-DM in particular, as well as Pokemon like Zacian-C, also appreciate potentially breaking non-Heavy-Duty Boots Lunala's Shadow Shield against opposing offense to assist in their sweep. Pokemon that can deal with Kyogre are also vital, as Kyogre threatens an OHKO on Arceus-Ground and can anti-lead, with Choice Scarf Kyogre's Water Spout denying any hazards at all. Against Kyogre, Arceus-Ground sometimes cannot safely lead depending on team compositions, so being able to beat Kyogre is essential to ensure Arceus-Ground can get positioning later to set up Stealth Rock or use Thunder Wave on opposing threats. A Kyogre of your own paired with it works well to trade into opposing Kyogre, with items like Assault Vest, Sitrus Berry, Wacan Berry, and Choice Specs assisting in the one-on-one to open up Arceus-Ground. Meteor Beam Eternatus and other Dragon-types like Koraidon and Kyurem-B can also fill the role of threatening opposing Kyogre but are less successful as leads attempting to trade into the opposing team than your own Kyogre would be. Calyrex-I is also threatening in the lead if it can set up a Swords Dance and Trick Room against Arceus-Ground, so the aforementioned Lunala, Necrozma-DM, and Kyogre are all strong tools against that.

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Arceus-Ground is an amazing wallbreaker and setup sweeper thanks to its good natural bulk and coverage that cement it as a threat that cannot be ignored. Power Gem 2HKOes Ho-Oh and hits Ground-immune targets such as Gliscor and Landorus-T for decent damage after a Calm Mind boost. Tera Ground allows Arceus-Ground to 2HKO Ting-Lu at +1 after a layer of Spikes, 2HKO Arceus formes at +1, and OHKO Arceus formes at +1 them after 3 layers of Spikes. Tera Fairy makes Arceus-Ground immune to Miraidon's Draco Meteor and Koraidon's Outrage and Scale Shot while giving it a resistance to Low Kick from the latter and a neutrality to Calyrex-S's Grass Knot, making it difficult to revenge kill. However, it makes Arceus-Ground more vulnerable to Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade. More often than not, Arceus-Fairy ends up being the Calm Mind user that's easier to fit thanks to its defensive utility, which enables it to take on Koraidon. Although, Arceus-Ground fits on teams that tend to be weak to Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C.

Calm Mind Arceus-Ground is best suited for balance and bulky offense teams where it is able to open up holes for its teammates. Calyrex-S in particular is a great teammate for Arceus-Ground, with both pressuring Ting-Lu and opening up a potential sweep for each other. Similarly, Miraidon helps to overwhelm their mutual check in Ting-Lu, paving the way for Arceus-Ground to clean up later. Calyrex-S can take advantage of Arceus-Ground locked into Calm Mind or Recover via Encore and use it as an opportunity to set up Nasty Plot. Grass Knot also does massive damage to unboosted Arceus-Ground; hence, Arceus-Ground appreciates Arceus, which is able to check Calyrex-S by effectively switching in on its Grass Knot and threatening it out with Shadow Claw. Koraidon, with its various sets such as Choice Scarf and Swords Dance, is able to brute force its way through Arceus-Ground, so Ho-Oh is another teammate that Arceus-Ground appreciates, helping keep Koraidon in check while soft checking Calyrex-S and Arceus. Arceus-Ground can struggle with entry hazards, which makes Hatterene a good partner, as it is able to bounce them back and can also bring in Arceus-Ground via Baton Pass, allowing it to set up on common switch-ins to Hatterene, such as Ho-Oh. Arceus-Ground also appreciates Choice Scarf Koraidon, which is able to bring it in via U-turn. Eternatus and Ting-Lu are also amazing teammates, setting up Toxic Spikes and Spikes, respectively, chipping foes and allowing Arceus-Ground to sweep more easily; Eternatus also helps keep Kyogre in check thanks to its bulk and access to Toxic. Arceus-Ground struggles to break through Giratina-O because of its Ground immunity, hence Arceus-Ground appreciates Arceus-Fairy because it is able to beat Giratina-O with Judgment. Arceus-Ground on the other hand is able to handle Arceus-Fairy's checks such as Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C and punish them with Judgment. Although, running both Arceus-Fairy and Arceus-Ground means that entry hazards like Spikes and Toxic Spikes could cause a big problem to them.

Offensive Dragon Dance.description:
Offensive Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground is a potent setup sweeper, leveraging its high Speed tier and Dragon Dance to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame after one boost and all Choice Scarf users after two boosts while punching holes through teams with boosted Earthquake. Taunt stops Pokemon such as Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and defensive Arceus-Ground from burning Arceus-Ground with Will-O-Wisp while also stopping Ting-Lu and Terastallized Ho-Oh from phazing it with Whirlwind. Furthermore, Taunt blocks recovery from defensive Pokemon like support Arceus formes and Dondozo, allowing Arceus-Ground to break through or cripple them for a teammate. Stone Edge allows Arceus-Ground to OHKO Ho-Oh at +1. Tera Fire is used to block Will-O-Wisp, resist Koraidon's Flare Blitz, resist Calyrex-S's Grass Knot, resist both of Zacian-C's STAB moves, and resist Arceus-Fairy's Judgment. However, it does make Arceus-Ground weak to Stealth Rock and Ting-Lu's Earthquake, and it maintains its weakness to Arceus-Water's Judgment.

Arceus-Ground is a staple on hyper offense teams, alongside suicide leads such as Deoxys-S, Ribombee, and Glimmora. Other offense staples like Zacian-C, Arceus, and Koraidon greatly benefit from Arceus-Ground's presence, as they both struggle with defensive Arceus formes. Arceus-Ground can help chip down the aforementioned Arceus formes that frequently switch in on it, using Taunt to deny Recover and entry hazards, allowing its teammates to eventually break through them. This works the other way around as well, with Koraidon and Zacian-C doing a great deal of damage to defensive Arceus formes and Koraidon knocking support Arceus formes into Earthquake's KO range, potentially enabling a sweep. Arceus-Ground also serves a vital role on hyper offense teams as an Electric-immune Pokemon, which allows it to force out and set up on Miraidon, an otherwise potentially significant threat. Calyrex-S and Arceus-Ground share a common check in Ting-Lu, which they chip into KO range of each other, allowing for one of them to sweep. Arceus and Arceus-Ground also both struggle with Giratina-O, as Giratina-O's Ground and Normal immunity makes it a hard-to-break wall. This can be circumvented by using Arceus to chip Giratina-O with Swords Dance-boosted Shadow Claw, which can allow Arceus-Ground to sweep with Stone Edge without having to fear Dragon Tail or Will-O-Wisp.

Utility.description:
• Arceus-Rock's unique typing and access to Will-O-Wisp allow it to carve out a niche as a check to foes such as Extreme Killer Arceus, Mega Salamence, and Rayquaza while putting pressure on common Defoggers like Ho-Oh and crippling would-be checks like Necrozma-DM and Zygarde with Will-O-Wisp.
  • Will-O-Wisp allows Arceus-Rock to check Extreme Killer Arceus, Mega Salamence, and Rayquaza more effectively and lets it cripple other physical attackers, such as Calyrex-I and Zekrom. It also greatly annoys common Rock-resistant Pokemon, such as Zygarde, Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM, and Arceus-Ground.
  • Stealth Rock is a good option, since Arceus-Rock threatens common Defoggers like Ho-Oh and Yveltal, keeping it up consistently. Taunt lets Arceus-Rock deny foes' attempts to recover health or spread status. Refresh lets Arceus-Rock shrug off Toxic and burns from Ho-Oh, defensive Eternatus, and Arceus-Dark. Ice Beam can be ran in the third slot to lure in and catch Zygarde off guard.
  • The given EV spread enables Arceus-Rock to avoid a 2HKO from specially offensive Yveltal's Dark Pulse, avoid an OHKO from +1 Adamant Mega Salamence's Earthquake after Stealth Rock, and almost always avoid an OHKO from +1 Life Orb Rayquaza's Earthquake while having enough Speed to outpace Chi-Yu. The rest of the EVs are invested to OHKO defensive Ho-Oh.
  • Tera Rock lets Arceus-Rock fire off more powerful Judgments, notably letting it OHKO defensive Yveltal and 2HKO defensive Primal Groudon, offensive Eternatus, and offensive Primal Kyogre after Stealth Rock, while retaining its ability to check Extreme Killer Arceus, Mega Salamence and Rayquaza. Tera Grass can also be used to turn its weaknesses to Ground and Water into resistances, providing defensive insurance for Zygarde, Arceus-Ground, and Primal Kyogre.
  • Arceus-Rock should be used aggressively to chip the opposing team with STAB Judgment, which is difficult to switch into, while burning the opposing Rock-resistant foes, such as Zacian-C and Marshadow, and pressuring common forms of hazard control. This role is expanded upon when facing Extreme Killer Arceus, Rayquaza, Ho-Oh, Yveltal, and Mega Salamence, in which case Arceus-Rock should be preserved to check these threats.
  • Arceus-Rock appreciates teammates like Yveltal, Ho-Oh, and Eternatus that cover its numerous weaknesses to common moves, such as Arceus-Ground's Earthquake and Kyogre's Origin Pulse, while they, in turn, appreciate Arceus-Rock's ability to check strong physical attackers like Extreme Killer Arceus and Mega Salamence.
  • Running Stealth Rock on Arceus-Rock can allow Primal Groudon to run more offensive sets. Pokemon that appreciate Arceus-Rock burning Steel-types, such as Eternatus, Zacian-C, and Mega Salamence, are good partners, as they can set up more easily. Mega Salamence is especially good to pair with, as it checks Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre offensively and can use a burned Necrozma-DM lacking status moves as setup fodder.
  • Arceus-Rock and Gothitelle make a good pairing, since Arceus-Rock can burn physical attackers such as Zygarde, Necrozma-DM, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground to make Gothitelle's trapping more consistent; in turn, Gothitelle takes out these Ground- and Steel-types that threaten Arceus-Rock.

balancedhackmons.overview: Arceus-Steel serves as a powerful hybrid Pokemon, capable of checking threats like Flutter Mane and Mega Gardevoir while sporting good offensive presence. A particularly distinguishing trait of Arceus-Steel is its ease of self-Imposter proofing as a setup Pokemon while still possessing good coverage and not being dependent on Strength Sap. Its Steel-type STAB moves are also valuable for being super effective on Mega Audino, the most common Ice Scales user, as well as utility Flutter Mane, which annoys most special Arceus formes. Additionally, Arceus-Steel has numerous viable variations in its ability and Plate, which allow it to circumvent specific checks or offer additional defensive utility. Arceus-Steel's typing does leave it susceptible to the most common wallbreakers in Mega Garchomp and Mega Blaziken, as well as Fire-type coverage from the likes of Eternatus and Mega Sceptile should it not have Well-Baked Body. This, combined with it also taking up the Arceus forme slot, means its teammates will be tasked with handling many dominant wallbreakers. It is also weak to Fighting-type moves from popular Pokemon like Zamazenta, and Steel is only a mediocre offensive type, being resisted by Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Miraidon, and opposing Steel-types.
balancedhackmons.comments:
Other Options

Arceus-Steel can run a variety of utility abilities to deny counterplay options or provide additional defensive capabilities.
