In return, Excadrill can handle the aforementioned Primarina and Meowscarada for Hippowdon. Landorus is another great teammate, as it is a very potent wallbreaker that handles physical walls that Excadrill struggles against, such as opposing Hippowdon, as well as Corviknight and Skarmory if it has set Gravity, which Excadrill can also take advantage of. In return, Excadrill takes care of Pokemon that can wall Landorus, like Chansey and Articuno. Another great defensive teammate is Clodsire, which provides a Water immunity with Water Absorb, as well as great utility with its access to a wide array of entry hazards, which further aid in Excadrill's sweeping and wallbreaking capabilities. Mamoswine is another appreciated teammate, as it has access to Thick Fat, which allows Ground teams to have a relatively safe pivot into Pokemon such as Kyurem and Greninja Choice-locked into Ice-type moves, which both outspeed Excadrill outside of sand. Additionally, it threatens a myriad of Pokemon that prove troublesome to Excadrill such as Gliscor, Amoonguss, and Zapdos with its Ice-type STAB moves, as well as revenge killing Dragon-types such as Dragonite and Dragapult, making Excadrill's job of sweeping much easier.

Choice Band (Ground).description: Boasting a powerful Attack stat and the ability Sand Rush, Excadrill is a powerful sweeper for sand teams. While sand is active, Excadrill outspeeds Choice Scarf Meowscarada, which otherwise poses a threat to Ground-type teams. Earthquake in tandem with Choice Band 2KHOes defensive switch-ins like Archaludon and Ferrothorn. Iron Head poses a threat to Fairy-types like Iron Valiant, Tapu Lele, and Mega Diancie, while hitting Pokemon with Levitate such as Latios. Rock Slide helps to target Flying- and Bug-type threats like Zapdos and Volcarona. Poison Jab is excellent coverage that deals with Grass-types like Ogerpon-W and Tapu Bulu. X-Scissor can alternatively be used to check Psychic-type switch-ins like Slowbro while still being good against Ogerpon-W. Eject Button Hippowdon is a necessary teammate to pair with Excadrill due to its ability to set sand while also being an excellent defensive pivot that sets entry hazards. Landorus, with the help of Gravity, allows Excadrill to hit Pokemon with Levitate like Rotom-W, and it is also a great answer to defensive Steel- and Flying-types like Skarmory and Corviknight once Gravity is active. It also assists in dealing with Tapu Bulu and Slowbro, depending on which move Excadrill lacks. Mamoswine helps Excadrill by wallbreaking Flying-types that it naturally cannot deal with, like Gliscor, with its powerful Ice-type STAB moves. Clodsire, with the ability Water Absorb, turns into a great specially defensive wall, as it is immune to any incoming Water-type attacks while also being an excellent means of spreading status and setting up hazards with Poison Jab and Toxic Spikes, respectively. Alternatively, Sandy Shocks is another great Gravity setter for Excadrill that can naturally check Flying- and Water-types like Pelipper and Celesteela with its Electric-type STAB moves. Sandy Shocks is also a great answer to Mega Charizard Y, as Drought activates its Protosynthesis. Great Tusk, in conjunction with Excadrill, utilizes a Choice Scarf to remove Dark-types like Weavile and Ting-Lu with its powerful Fighting-type STAB moves.

Swords Dance (Ground).description: Having multiple ways to boost its Speed and holding a nearly unresisted STAB combination, Excadrill is a potent setup sweeper for Ground-type sand teams, as it can take advantage of forced switches by posing as its Choice Band set. Corkscrew Crash lets Excadrill overwhelm multiple checks, OHKOing Tornadus-T when unboosted; Sinistcha, Mega Latias, and Mega Sableye at +2; and Mega Venusaur at +2 after Stealth Rock damage. Rapid Spin lets Excadrill compress utility by removing entry hazards for its team while also raising its Speed; Rapid Spin is also a good move to finish foes off to make Excadrill more difficult to revenge kill. Excadrill appreciates Hippowdon, which is a sand setter required to easily enable Sand Rush. Excadrill can struggle against Water-types that are immune to Ground such as Rotom-W and Pelipper, so it appreciates Gastrodon and Clodsire as allies to pivot to; in turn they can support Excadrill by setting entry hazards or crippling the aforementioned foes with status. Flying-types such as Mega Charizard Y, Zapdos, and Skarmory can also be problematic for Excadrill to deal with, so checks such as Mega Garchomp and Mamoswine are appreciated.

Defensive.description: Mega Audino utilizes its very rare typing, good bulk, low Attack capable of stifling Strength Sap healing, and low Speed to be a versatile wall and an effective pivot. The ability chosen is up to team preference; Fur Coat can let it check Dragon- and Dark-type physical attackers like Mega Garchomp and Choice Band Ash-Greninja, Ice Scales can let it check various special threats like Flutter Mane and Take Heart Arceus formes, and Magic Bounce can reflect key status moves like Spikes, Glare, Strength Sap, and Toxic. Topsy-Turvy heavily deters setup from threats like Flare Boost Flutter Mane, Take Heart Arceus formes, and Mega Garchomp. Knock Off removes key items such as Assault Vest from Mega Steelix; if consistent progress making throughout the game is desired, Mortal Spin can instead be used to remove entry hazards and spread poison. Teleport is a consistent pivoting option with the switches Mega Audino often forces by denying Strength Sap healing or threatening to remove items. Moonblast hits Magic Guard Miraidon for good damage and dissuades other Magic Guard users from freely switching in. Mega Audino fits on balance or bulky teams looking for a flexible check to most of the metagame, a Pokemon with a Ghost-type immunity, or more importantly a Strength Sap blocker; thus, strong physical attackers like Ash-Greninja and Kyurem-B are good partners that appreciate its ability to limit Strength Sap healing and slow pivoting. In return, Mega Audino can Imposter-proof these attackers. Mega Audino is weak to Sunsteel Strike users like Mega Lucario, so solid checks to them like Mega Slowbro and Celesteela makes for good partners. Imposter-proof Mega Audino with Steel-type teammates, Regenerator users, or Take Heart Arceus formes carrying a Plate.

SubSeed.description:
• Whimsicott can utilize its ability Prankster to go first against most targets such as Dragapult and non-Taunt Spectrier to set up Leech Seed on them while also being able to survive a hit with its decent natural bulk.
  • Moonblast is utilized for the matchup against both Urshifu formes, as usually one or two uses are enough to KO Urshifu-S and Urshifu-R, respectively, while they struggle to KO it back.
  • The combination of Protect and Substitute allows it to stall most Pokemon in the tier thanks to the recovery from Leech Seed; Substitute can also be utilized to give Pokemon like Choice Band Ursaluna and Donphan more chances to miss Gunk Shot, which would otherwise OHKO Whimsicott, allowing it to set up Leech Seed.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Whimsicott to survive Choice Band Poison Jab from Urshifu-R thanks to its Kebia Berry, as well as potentially survive any poisoning effects from the same attack, while the Speed EVs are enough to outspeed Adamant variants of both Urshifu formes.
  • Due to the nature of both Leech Seed and Prankster, Whimsicott struggles against most Grass- and Dark-type Pokemon, such as Ogerpon-W, Meowscarada, and Darkrai, and despite the Kebia Berry it holds, it's still not enough to live STAB Poison-type attacks from the likes of Sneasler and Pecharunt, so Pokemon that can beat most of these, such as Scizor, Hisuian Goodra, and Dragapult, make for good partners.
  • It's also worth mentioning that Steel-types like Scizor and Iron Crown can also give big trouble to Whimsicott, so good Steel-type answers like Ursaluna and Landorus-T are good teammates as well.

Choice Specs.description:
Shadow Ball threatens Delphox and Bronzong and hits Alolan Sandslash slightly harder than Moonblast. Pranskter should only be used alongside Switcheroo, since this makes the move better at disrupting teams.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

monotype.overview:
Grass

Whimsicott finds niches with its Fairy typing, allowing it to take on Dragon-types, along with Prankster boosting its great utility movepool such as Encore, which enables it to lock targets like Dragonite and Skarmory into undesirable moves. However, Whimsicott's low stats outside of Speed leave much to be desired in terms of power, and its utility movepool can often be stifled by opposing Grass-types and bulky Dark-types such as Ogerpon-H and Alolan Muk, which will happily remove it.

Offensive Disruptor (Grass).description:
Whimsicott finds a niche on Grass with its Fairy typing and vast support movepool boosted by Prankster to act as a disruptor against threats such as Dragonite and Volcarona. Encore allows Whimsicott to lock otherwise game-winning sweepers like Victory Dance Hisuian Lilligant and Dragon Dance Dragapult into their setup options, enabling Whimsicott or its teammates to remove them. Moonblast provides a form of offense for Whimsicott, allowing it to threaten Dragon- and Dark-type threats such as Archaludon, Roaring Moon, and Sableye. Stun Spore grants Whimiscott a vital form of speed control, slowing down foes like Sneasler and Dragapult. Alternatively, Tailwind provides long term speed control and is useful to use before Whimsicott is KOed. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Whimsicott to safely enter the field, while Pixie Plate enables it to 2HKO Archaludon.

Ogerpon-H serves as a vital ally, being able to handle Poison- and Steel-types that beat Whimsicott such as Alolan Muk, Amoonguss, Heatran, and Gholdengo. Ogerpon-H also appreciates Whimiscott paralyzing Sneasler and Tornadus-T so it can check them. Alternatively, Ogerpon-C can be used to nail Fire- and Flying-types such as Ninetales and Ogerpon-H that cause Whimsicott trouble while also appreciating Tailwind to outspeed +1 Volcarona and Meowscarada with a Speed boost from Protosynthesis. Choice Scarf Meowscarada provides an incredible form of speed control, being able to check threats such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Gholdengo that cause Whimsicott issues; it also benefits from Stun Spore, enabling it to outspeed Choice Scarf Dragapult. Amoonguss provides a solid defensive pivot for Whimsicott, as it can absorb Toxic Spikes should Whimsicott opt for Pixie Plate along with using Foul Play on a setup threat such as Swords Dance Ceruledge to remove it once hit with Encore. Amoonguss can also use Sludge Bomb to take on Fairy-types like Hatterene that can deflect Whimsicott's utility via Magic Bounce. Hisuian Lilligant and Breloom appreciate Whimsicott's Encore, granting safe setup opportunities and can use their Fighting-type STAB moves to deal with Ice- and Steel-types such as Kyurem, Alolan Sandslash, and Hisuian Goodra in return. Hydrapple appreciates Whimsicott removing Dragon-types like Roaring Moon and Raging Bolt and, in return, can use its Fire neutrality and Earth Power to take on Fire-types like Heatran, Hisuian Arcanine, and Iron Moth. Sinistcha similarly provides a Fire neutrality along with a Poison neutrality, enabling it to take on threats such as Sneasler, Clodsire, and Toxapex with Calm Mind and Strength Sap.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Whimsicott generally works well on hyper offensive teams that appreciate its ability to provide speed control and shut down opposing setup threats with Encore. Pokemon that have middling or high Speed tiers and strong offenses pair especially well with Whimsicott. Whimsicott can also work well on sun-centric teams, utilizing its ability to overwrite Pelipper's Drizzle with Sunny Day to maintain speed and weather control.

  • Whimsicott pairs especially well with strong special attackers, namely Hisuian Typhlosion, Glimmora, Power Herb Archaludon, Gholdengo, and Garchomp. Their middling Speed tiers benefit greatly from Tailwind, and Hisuian Typhlosion in particular also appreciates Whimsicott's ability to set sun, boosting its Eruption further while mitigating its Water weakness. Annihilape can be used on some teams that want to employ Beat Up strategies, which can also be effective.

  • Whimsicott can struggle into teams that can handle its partner's offensive onslaught or mitigate Whimsicott's Tailwind Speed advantage. However, by changing up Whimsicott's partner, it can break through some defensive cores that may stop one pairing but not the other. For example, while Incineroar may be able to beat Whimsicott and Hisuian Typhlosion, it loses to Meteor Beam Glimmora. Since Whimsicott generally pairs with strong, fast offensive threats, its playstyle is very vunerable to Trick Room, especially teams that have Psychic Terrain, which blocks Whimsicott's Prankster Encore. Due to this, Whimsicott generally likes to pair with Incineroar to shut down Trick Room teams while also allowing Whimsicott's frailer partners to pivot in safely.

Strategy Comments

  • Whimsicott exists as a support Pokemon, providing speed control through Prankster Tailwind and amplifying its partner's damage output through Helping Hand or Sunny Day.
  • Whimsicott is almost always a lead Pokemon, with a hard-hitting partner that takes advantage of its Tailwind support. It almost always wants to be clicking Tailwind to gain the Speed advantage immediately, unless it is facing a Trick Room team that can turn that advantage on its head. Against bulkier cores that may not have speed control or care about moving first, Whimsicott may choose to use Helping Hand or Sunny Day to try to break through those cores with its partner's sheer power.
  • Whimsicott is mainly weak to strong priority that can take it out before it can set Tailwind, mainly Tera Normal Extreme Speed from Dragonite and Brave Bird from Talonflame. Pokemon that can stomach many hits and slow down the level of offense coming from Whimsicott's side can also be a problem, since Whimsicott is so frail that it can usually only afford to set Tailwind or Sunny Day once. By choosing certain partners for Whimsicott, this matchup problem can be turned on its head. Pokemon such as Glimmora can beat common counters to Whimsicott, including Talonflame, Dragonite, and Incineroar. Pokemon that block priority moves can also support Whimsicott, such as Indeedee with Psychic Terrain and Farigiraf with Armor Tail.

Tailwind Support.description:
• Whimsicott is a staple on hyper offense teams due to its ability to set Tailwind with its Prankster ability. Whimsicott also provides valuable support to its team through the use of Encore to disrupt opposing strategies or Helping Hand and Sunny Day to boost its partner's damage output.
  • Encore is generally preferred to be able to pin opposing Pokemon into positions where they cannot use Protect, dissuade setup, and lock opposing Pokemon into moves such as Fake Out or Tailwind. Helping Hand is the preferred last move on Whimsicott for most teams because it provides a damage boost to any of Whimsicott's partners. Sunny Day is used on certain hyper offense teams to boost Hisuian Typhlosion's Eruption and provide weather control against Pelipper. Protect is almost always used on Focus Sash sets to block Fake Out without the need to Terastallize into a Ghost-type. Beat Up is specifically used with Annihilape to boost its Rage Fist; this, in conjunction with Tailwind, makes it into a threat as quickly as possible.
  • Covert Cloak is generally preferred on Whimsicott to block the effects of Fake Out, allowing Whimsicott to get Tailwind off without having to run Protect. However, Focus Sash is sometimes used on teams that want Whimsicott's support on the field for longer. Focus Sash also allows Whimsicott to set Tailwind in front of Talonflame, which would otherwise KO Whimsicott before it can set Tailwind with Brave Bird in conjunction with Gale Wings.
  • Tera Water can be used to give Covert Cloak Whimsicott an extra turn on the field against common Pokemon such as Incineroar, Hisuian Typhlosion, and Gholdengo, though it must watch out for Rillaboom's now supereffective priority Grassy Glide. Tera Ghost gives Whimsicott an immunity to common priority moves, namely Fake Out and Extreme Speed and is usually seen on Focus Sash sets, as they are susceptible to Fake Out. Tera Fire offers similar defensive benefits to Tera Water while still resisting Rillaboom's Grassy Glide after Terastallization. However, Tera Fire makes Whimsicott weak to common moves such a as Primarina's Liquid Voice Hyper Voice and Pelipper's Weather Ball under rain. Tera Dark is a niche option on Focus Sash sets that gives Whimsicott an immunity to opposing Prankster moves from the likes of Murkrow and opposing Whimsicott.
  • The first spread for Covert Cloak Whimsicott maximizes HP investment over damage output to live attacks that would otherwise prevent it from setting Tailwind. Focus Sash sets, on the other hand, invest more into Special Attack.

Covert Cloak.description:
Whimsicott is a potent Tailwind setter in the Regulation G metagame thanks to Prankster in conjunction with its good supporting movepool, and its typing lets it take on staples such as Raging Bolt and both Urshifu formes. Moonblast lets Whimsicott consistently damage bulky Pokemon such as the aforementioned Raging Bolt while also chipping down Rillaboom and Incineroar. It also lets Whimsicott take full advantage of its good matchup against both Urshifu formes, threatening Urshifu-R with a 2HKO and Urshifu-S with an OHKO once its Focus Sash is broken. Whimsicott's ability to punish passive play like Protect via Encore allows fast-paced teammates like Choice Specs Miraidon and Choice Scarf Chi-Yu to safely output huge damage. Encore also has other immensely useful applications like forcing non-Dark-type Fake Out users like Rillaboom and Iron Hands to switch out if they choose to use the move and reversing Trick Room in the face of threats such as Calyrex-I; this is crucial, as Tailwind teams inherently struggle against Trick Room, especially when they have multiple Pokemon weak to the aforementioned Calyrex-I. Light Screen helps bolster Whimsicott and its allies' bulk against threats such as Calyrex-S and Choice Specs Terapagos. Covert Cloak lets Whimsicott safely ignore Fake Out and set up Tailwind, allowing it to threaten with Encore on the following turn. The physical bulk investment allows Whimsicott to avoid an OHKO from -1 Zamazenta-C's Heavy Slam while never being 2HKOed by +1 Body Press. The special bulk investment enables Whimsicott to never be OHKOed by Choice Specs Tera Stellar Terapagos-S's Tera Starstorm and Mystic Water Kyogre's Water Spout in rain even at full power. Maximum Speed is run in order to let Whimsicott have the best chance to force opposing Whimsicott to repeatedly use Tailwind with Encore, which is an interaction that can also be put to use against the slower Tornadus. Tera Fire rids Whimsicott of its weakness to Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash and Incineroar's Flare Blitz among other powerful moves like Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance and Koraidon's sun-boosted Flare Blitz, crucially never getting 2HKOed by Glacial Lance. Alternatively, Tera Water lets it retain its initial resistance to Kyogre's Water Spout and Origin Pulse in addition to the resistances provided by Tera Fire in exchange for sacrificing the positive defensive matchup against Rillaboom and Raging Bolt. Tera Water also provides Whimsicott with a better matchup against Calyrex-I and Pelipper.

Whimsicott, being rather frail, is vulnerable to many relevant Pokemon, most notably Tornadus, as not only does it compete with Whimsicott as a Prankster Tailwind user on nearly every team apart from Miraidon hyper offense, but it also threatens an OHKO with Bleakwind Storm because Whimsicott lacks a Focus Sash. Thus, Miraidon makes for a good partner, as it can easily OHKO Tornadus. Whimsicott supports Choice Specs Miraidon exceptionally well, letting it dish out massive amounts of damage with Tera Electric uncontested under Tailwind. Encore punishes opposing Fake Out users, allowing Choice Specs Miraidon to stay on the field more safely. Whimsicott also helps Chi-Yu do great amounts of damage onto foes thanks to Tailwind and checks Raging Bolt for both it and Miraidon thanks to Beads of Ruin; this is of great value, as Miraidon is otherwise forced to lock into Draco Meteor. Whimsicott is susceptible to being removed by faster Pokemon like Calyrex-I under Trick Room and Chien-Pao, so you should be wise with managing its health and speed control. Iron Hands allows this to happen quite well, not only taking advantage of Trick Room with its low Speed but also heavily threatening Chien-Pao. Its good bulk, access to Fake Out, and healing from Drain Punch allow it to keep Whimsicott safe for multiple turns.

Focus Sash.description:
Whimsicott is an excellent Tailwind setter with a deep support movepool, mainly setting itself apart from Tornadus with its higher Speed, access to Encore and Helping Hand, and useful typing that gives it defensive utility against staples like Miraidon, Kyogre, Rillaboom, Raging Bolt, and both Urshifu formes. Moonblast provides a reliable STAB move that lets Whimsicott deal solid damage to common Fairy-weak Pokemon like Miraidon, Koraidon, Chien-Pao, and the Urshifu formes. Encore is Whimsicott's most infamous support option, letting it punish setup sweepers like Calm Mind Terapagos, IronPress Zamazenta-C, and Nasty Plot Calyrex-S for attempting to boost in front of it; the move also punishes foes from trying to stall out Tailwind turns with Protect, and it discourages Rillaboom from using Fake Out lest it be locked into it. Additionally, it forces Trick Room setters like Calyrex-I to untwist the dimensions. Taunt is a similarly useful disruption tool that can be used with or in place of Encore, notably allowing Whimsicott to deny Tailwind from other setters like Tornadus and Lunala unless they use Tera Dark. Protect helps Whimsicott keep itself on the field and stay in a position to use its other moves repeatedly, especially in the face of Fake Out users, but the last moveslot can also be spent on more aggressive options like Helping Hand, which is useful with any attacker, or Fake Tears, which is especially devastating alongside strong special threats like Chi-Yu. Whimsicott enjoys holding a Focus Sash to make up for its poor bulk, and Tera Ghost is useful to prevent the item from being wasted by Fake Out.

Whimsicott's reliable Tailwind support is a blessing to almost every Restricted Pokemon, especially those with middling Speed tiers such as Groudon and Terapagos, as well as Pokemon that want to be faster against opposing Tailwind teams such as Miraidon and Calyrex-S. All four of those Pokemon also benefit from Encore, which can create space for them to set up with Swords Dance, Nasty Plot, and Calm Mind. Clear Amulet Koraidon is another notable partner that reliably discourages opponents from bringing Incineroar, which is easily the worst Pokemon for Whimsicott to face in a battle. Other strong attackers that benefit from Tailwind support are also great with it; Landorus and Urshifu-S both fall into this category, and Chi-Yu is a standout example because it augments Whimsicott's modest damage output with Beads of Ruin. Other setup Pokemon that enjoy Encore are especially useful to justify using Whimsicott on a team over Tornadus, including Calm Mind Raging Bolt, Swords Dance Ogerpon-H, and Nasty Plot Gholdengo. It's important to make sure Whimsicott has teammates that can deal with problematic Dark-types like Chi-Yu, Ting-Lu, and Kingambit due to their Prankster immunity, and a Fighting-type like Urshifu-R or Iron Hands can help with that significantly.

Sun Setter.description:
• Moonblast keeps Whimsicott from being passive and hits threats like Raging Bolt and Urshifu-S for super effective damage.

  • Whimsicott can opt for Beat Up instead, allowing it to trigger Annihilape's Rage Fist and Terrakion's Justified ability.

  • Sunny Day activates Pokemon like Flutter Mane and Raging Bolts's abilities, making them more potent threats, as well as weakening Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-W.

  • The fourth move slot is customizable; Fake Tears allows Whimsicott to weaken Pokemon for partners like Flutter Mane and Landorus, Encore locks foes into unfavorable moves like Protect and Fake Out, Taunt helps shut down more passive Pokemon like Amoonguss and opposing Whimsicott.

  • The EV spread allows Whimsicott to live Tornadus's Bleakwind Storm and outspeed Maximum Speed Tornadus.

  • Tera Water grants Whimsicott valuable resistances to Fire-, Ice-, and Steel-types like Incineroar, Chien-Pao, and Kingambit while generally being a great defensive typing.

  • Covert Cloak allows Whimsicott to be immune to Fake Out.

Offensive Utility.description:
• Protect is valuable for dealing with Fake Out, but it does not allow fitting Sunny Day.

  • Tera Ghost makes Whimsicott immune to common priority moves like Fake Out and Extreme Speed as well as providing a resistance to Poison-type moves like Landorus' Sludge Bomb.

  • Focus Sash allows Whimsicott to have another chance to set up Tailwind or support its team later on in the game, as its mediocre defensive stats and plethora of weaknesses otherwise leave it potentially OHKOd by most Pokemon in the metagame.

  • Note that if Whimsicott is running Beat Up, an EV spread of 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 Spe with a Jolly Nature is more optimal.

zu.overview: Blessed with the rare Fairy typing and an excellent Speed tier, Whimsicott makes for an excellent revenge killer and utility Pokemon. Whimsicott's unique typing allows it to beat many dangerous threats like Persian-Alola and Virizion. A powerful Moonblast and pivoting coupled with Choice Specs allow Whimsicott to break past bulkier threats like Orthworm and Skuntank. However, Whimsicott's low offensive stats leave it often wanting for power, especially without Choice Specs, and it's incapable of fitting every move it wants. Furthermore, lack of reliable recovery and only average bulk makes it unable to consistently check the Pokemon it's supposed to like Regirock and Sandaconda.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Psychic is an option that nails Poison-types like Weezing. However, this comes at the cost of either losing U-turn's pivoting or the utility of Switcheroo or Encore. Whimsicott can use a SubSeed set to mess up its usual defensive checks like Cryogonal and Orthworm and be a general nuisance. This set struggles to find setup opportunities however and relies heavily on getting a free Substitute on a forced switch.

Checks and Counters

Poison-types: Whimsicott's 4x weakness to Poison and inability to hit Poison-types with its STAB attacks makes Poison-types like Muk and Weezing good checks. However, these Pokemon lack reliable recovery and can thus be worn down over a game.

Steel-types: Steel-types like Magneton and Orthworm can take Whimsicott's STAB attacks with ease. Orthworm can start setting entry hazards or set up with Coil or Iron Defense, while Magneton can generate momentum with Volt Switch.

Fire-types: As Whimsicott's STAB attacks do little to them, Fire-types like Charizard, Typhlosion, and Magmortar can use Whimsicott as an entry point to start firing off powerful attacks. These Pokemon aren't usually defensively invested however and can struggle to switch in consistently.

Special Walls: Special walls like Cryogonal and Articuno aren't bothered by Whimsicott's attacks and can use it to start forcing progress with entry hazards, status, pivoting, or boosts. However, Switcheroo completely ruins these walls, especially Articuno, and Encore can force them to repeat their status moves, allowing Whimsicott to safely bring in a teammate.

Choice Scarf Users: Many common Choice Scarf users like Hisuian Sneasel and Gunk Shot Primeape get the jump on Whimsicott and can easily take it out.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Whimsicott takes advantage of its high Speed and Moonblast to be a powerful cleaner and revenge killer. U-turn lets It scout for switches and pivot out of unfavorable matchups like Weezing and Orthworm, allowing it to bring in a more suitable teammate. Switcheroo allows Whimsicott to cripple its defensive checks, greatly hindering special walls like Orthworm and especially Articuno, letting Whimsicott and its teammates break past them later in the game. However, Whimsicott loses a substantial amount of power without its Choice Specs, so one must be careful about when to use Switcheroo. Infiltrator allows Whimsicott to bypass Substitute from foes like Beartic and opposing Whimsicott.

Choice Specs Whimsicott best fits on balance and bulky offense teams looking for a fast offensive cleaner that also provides some defensive utility. Whimsicott loves entry-hazard stacking teammates like Sandslash and Orthworm to help push its otherwise average damage output. It can't handle Fire-types like Charizard and Typhlosion, so answers to them like Regirock and Naclstack help immensely. Whimsicott can in return take advantage of the Grass- and Fighting-types like Virizion and Primeape that these Pokemon are at a disadvantage against. Whimsicott struggles with Poison-types like Weezing and Muk who resist its STAB attacks and threathen it with 4x super effective attacks, so answers like Magneton and Sandaconda make for great teammates. Whimsicott pairs well with offensive Fire-types like Typhlosion and Charizard that handle the Steel-types like Orthworm that it has difficulties breaking past, and in return, it handles their Water and Rock-type answers such as Clawitzer and Regirock.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Whimsicott leverages its superb Speed and access to Prankster to be a competent offensive pivot. Giga Drain is used for its ability to give Whimsicott staying power in longer games. Encore is key to this set, allowing it to force defensive foes into unfavorable moves like Stealth Rock and Recover, as well as shutting down setup sweepers like Jolteon and Regirock by locking them into their setup moves. U-turn pairs beautifully with Encore, scouting any forced switches and allowing Whimsicott to bring in powerful teammates like Clawitzer and Typhlosion. Tera Steel gives Whimsicott an immunity to Poison-type attacks from Muk and Weezing, and a resistance to Flying-type attacks from Dodrio as well as Ice-type attacks from Sneasel in a pinch. However, this still leaves Whimsicott vulnerable to Fire-type attacks from Charizard and Typhlosion and makes it weak to Fighting, making it unable to reliably switch into Primeape and Virizion. Tera Fire provides emergency resistances to Ice and Fire, but this makes Whimsicott unable to safely check Ground- and Rock-types like Sandaconda and Regirock.

Balance teams enjoy Whimsicott's pivoting and Prankster Encore helping them deal with bulky defensive Pokemon and dangerous setup sweepers. Powerful physical wallbreakers like Toxicroak and Primeape pair well with Whimsicott, as it baits in special walls like Articuno and can bring these teammates in with U-turn. Ground-types like Sandaconda make for excellent partners, as Whimsicott helps them handle the Water- and Grass-types like Clawitzer and Virizion that they struggle with, while they can handle Poison-types like Muk that scare Whimsicott out. Fire-types like Charizard and Magmortar can easily gain entry on Whimsicott, so Fire-resistant teammates like Regirock and Naclstack are helpful partners. Partners such as Charizard or Primeape that threaten Steel-types like Orthworm and Magneton can come in after a U-turn on these Steel-types to fire off attacks. Electric-types like Jolteon and Magneton appreciate Whimsicott's ability to handle Ground-types like Sandaconda, and in return, they handle the Flying-types like Dodrio and Articuno that Whimsicott struggles to beat. Other offensive pivots like Primeape and Mesprit can form a powerful VoltTurn core with Whimsicott, quickly racking up damage against walls like Regirock and Muk, especially with entry hazards up.

nu.overview: Whimsicott functions as a solid pivot in the metagame, being able to check a variety of threats such as Scrafty, Paldean Tauros-W, and Flygon. With Prankster and its wide movepool, it can annoy fast setup sweepers such as Shell Smash Drednaw, Nasty Plot Uxie, and Tidy Up Cinccino. In addition, it can bother walls like Copperajah and Bellibolt as well as entry hazard setters such as Duraludon and Rhyperior. However, Whimsicott struggles against certain threats, such as Scyther, Munkidori, and Flamigo, as they can outspeed certain Whimsicott variants and force it out. It also lacks coverage moves, which leaves it struggling against Fairy-resistant Pokemon such as Copperajah, Duraludon, and Klefki. It also has trouble balancing physical bulk and Speed. With Speed investment, it can outspeed the likes of Flamigo, Paldean Tauros-W, and even Ambipom but risks a 2HKO from Flamigo and Paldean Tauros-W's Close Combat.
nu.comments:
Other Options

A set of Sunny Day / Moonblast / Memento / Encore and Eject Button can let Whimsicott serve as a dedicated setter on sun teams that enables sun sweepers such as Venusaur, Scovillain, and Brute Bonnet. A set with Choice Scarf and Switcheroo can be used to surprise walls such as Chansey, Bellibolt, and Copperajah, and Tailwind as a fourth move can be used to help wallbreakers such as Basculegion-M, Flamigo, and Heracross get the jump on opposing threats. Leech Seed can be used to give Whimsicott more recovery and allow it to punish switch-ins such as Bronzong and Chansey.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Bronzong and Copperajah take very little damage from Whimsicott's attacks and can threaten it with their STAB Steel-type attacks. Duraludon and Klefki can use Whimsicott to set up their entry hazards or to attack, although they do not want Whimsicott using U-turn to bring in Fire- and Fighting-types.

Faster Threats: Faster threats like Scyther and Tornadus as well as Choice Scarf users such as Munkidori and Flamigo can all outspeed Whimsicott and force it to switch or be KOed. However, Scyther, Tornadus, and Flamigo do not want to switch in directly.

Poison-types: Poison-types such as Amoonguss, Munkidori, and Galarian Slowbro take very little damage from Whimsicott's moves and can force it to switch. Toxicroak can force Whimsicott into mind games, as it commonly runs Tera Dark, forcing Whimsicott to use either Moonblast or Encore. Amoonguss in particular is problematic, as it resists both Moonblast and Giga Drain, has an immunity to Stun Spore, and can punish pivoting attempts with Rocky Helmet.

Fire-types: Fire-types such as Chandelure, Incineroar, and Infernape do not take much from Whimsicott's moves and can threaten major damage with their STAB moves. However, Chandelure does not want to deal with Stun Spore and is often vulnerable to entry hazards due to commonly running Choice items. Incineroar can also be worn down over the course of the match through repeated Moonblasts, especially if its Heavy-Duty Boots are removed or if entry hazards are up.

Pivot Support.description:
Set Details

U-turn allows Whimsicott to pivot out on Fairy-resistant Pokemon such as Klefki, Chandelure, and Copperajah, letting it bring in teammates such as Infernape, Incineroar, and Paldean Tauros-W. Encore is the defining characteristic of this set, allowing Whimsicott to disrupt opposing setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Scream Tail, Nasty Plot Uxie, Shell Smash Drednaw, and Tidy Up Cinccino. Giga Drain can enable Whimsicott to greatly damage the likes of Rhyperior and Swampert while also providing recovery and the ability to chip Vaporeon. On the other hand, Stun Spore can be used to paralyze faster foes like Munkidori, Infernape, and Choice Scarf users such as Flamigo and Flygon. However, Memento can be used on offensive teams to safely bring in a threat such as Flamigo or Munkidori or create opportunities for a setup sweeper like Swords Dance Scyther, Nasty Plot Munkidori, or Dudunsparce. Heavy-Duty Boots is the preferred item, as it allows Whimsicott to avoid taking entry hazard damage. Alternatively, Rocky Helmet allows Whimsicott to punish U-turn from Munkidori and Flygon as well as Flip Turn from Vaporeon. Additionally, it means that Whimsicott does not need to attack foes like Paldean Tauros-W and Heracross to damage them. The listed EV spread allows Whimsicott to outspeed non-Choice Scarf Chandelure. However, other benchmarks can be reached with different EV spreads: 248 HP / 212 Def / 48 Spe and a Timid nature lets Whimsicott outpace non-Choice Scarf Flamigo and Heracross while optimizing bulk, and 248 HP / 132 Def / 128 Spe and a Timid nature allows Whimsicott to outspeed Flygon and Paldean Tauros-W. Tera Steel gives Whimsicott a resistance to Steel and an immunity to Poison, which is handy against Duraludon, Munkidori, Amoonguss, and Overqwil. However, it removes Whimsicott's Fighting and Ground resistance while maintaining its Fire weakness. Tera Water gives Whimsicott a resistance to Fire while keeping its Water resistance, which is handy against the likes of Chandelure, Incineroar, and Vaporeon. On the other hand, Tera Fire gives Whimsicott both a Fire resistance and a Steel resistance, which is handy to deal with Incineroar and Copperajah. However, Tera Fire gives Whimsicott a weakness to Stealth Rock and removes its Water resistance, which makes it worse against Vaporeon, Basculegion-M, and Paldean Tauros-W.

Whimsicott best fits on balance or offense teams as a blanket check to setup sweepers and Fighting-types. Fire-types such as Incineroar and Chandelure appreciate Whimsicott bringing them in against Steel- and Poison-types such as Bronzong, Copperajah, and Galarian Slowbro. In return, Whimsicott can check the likes of Vaporeon, Rhyperior, Flygon, and Swampert for them. Water-types such as Vaporeon and Swampert check Fire-types like Incineroar and Chandelure, which Whimsicott struggles with. Pokemon such as Dudunsparce and Flygon appreciate Whimsicott checking the likes of Paldean Tauros-W and Scrafty for them. Setup sweepers such as Shell Smash Drednaw, Swords Dance Scyther, and Nasty Plot Munkidori greatly enjoy the setup opportunities that Whimsicott creates with Memento. Slower Pokemon such as Uxie, Chandelure, and Basculegion-M appreciate Whimsicott's ability to spread paralysis, as they are able to outspeed threats such as Scyther, Munkidori, and Choice Scarf Flamigo. Entry hazard setters such as Klefki, Swampert, and Bronzong, as well as Knock Off users like Tsareena, Gligar, and Wo-Chien, can help wear down Whimsicott's checks such as Incineroar and Chandelure by removing their Heavy-Duty Boots and forcing them to take repeated hazard damage, making it easier for Whimsicott and its Fire-type teammates to make progress over time.

Tailwind Support.description: • This EV Spread outspeeds Timid Glimmora and neutral nature Base 100s such as Chi-Yu.

Focus Sash Support.description: • This set is more useful for Beat Up support, however if Moonblast is chosen, 36 HP / 220 SpA / 252 Spe can be used to OHKO Chien-Pao with Moonblast.

Utility (Grass).description: Whimsicott is a unique and effective pivot option for Grass teams by virtue of its Prankster ability and many viable support moves. U-turn provides Whimsicott with a means to pivot into another teammate in order to maintain momentum. Alternatively, Knock Off can be used over U-turn to take advantage of Encore forcing switches by providing important item removal. The given EV spread makes Whimsicott as fast as possible while maximizing the damage of its Moonblast, letting it 2HKO Mega Sableye and Mandibuzz, and OHKO pokemon like Iron Valiant. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Whimsicott to switch in several times per match without being worn down by entry hazards. Ferrothorn is an excellent partner, since its Steel typing lets it wall Poison- and Steel-type attacks that threaten Whimsicott, and its entry hazards also pair well with Whimsicott's ability to force switches. Celebi is an excellent partner for Whimsicott thanks to its ability to threaten Poison and Steel teams that can make Whimsicott's opportunities to switch in very limited. Ogerpon-C benefits greatly from Whimsicott clearing away hazards so that it can make use of Sturdy to tank a hit it otherwise can't, and it appreciates Encore to help create setup opportunities. A Sunny Day set with Heat Rock can turn Whimsicott into a makeshift sun setter for teams that utilize Chlorophyll sweepers like Venusaur, Hisuian Lilligant, and Scovillain.

Sun Sweeper.description:
Hisuian Lilligant shines on sun teams as a solid speed control, late-game cleaner, and revenge killer, using Chlorophyll to outspeed boosted threats such as Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf Darkrai. Its strong dual STAB combination in Close Combat and Solar Blade allows it to clean up against offensive threats including Great Tusk, Darkrai, and Ogerpon-W. Triple Axel provides essential coverage against Dragapult and Flying-types such as Dragonite and Zapdos, preventing them from walling Hisuian Lilligant. Swords Dance gives Hisuian Lilligant a way to boost its offensive power to sky-high levels, notably 2HKOing Pecharunt with Stealth Rock damage and letting it OHKO even Ceruledge. Victory Dance can instead be used to make it less reliant on Chlorophyll for its speed, boosting its bulk against would-be revenge killers like offensive Zamazenta while still securing an OHKO on Zapdos and Raging Bolt after a single boost; this can even be used with Leaf Blade to allow it to continue a sweep after the harsh sunlight fades. Encore is an alternative option to lock down opposing setup sweepers like Iron Defense Zamazenta and punish Kingambit's Sucker Punch, while Healing Wish gives Hisuian Lilligant the ability to provide a second life for other offensive threats on its team. Defensively, Tera Fire prevents foes like Moltres and Dragapult from crippling it with a burn and flips its Fairy, Ice, and Fire weaknesses from foes like Galarian Weezing, Weavile, and Iron Moth, while Tera Ghost makes Hisuian Lilligant sturdier against IronPress users such as Zamazenta and Corviknight and prevents revenge killing attempts from Extreme Speed Dragonite.

Hisuian Lilligant is exclusively found on sun teams. Either Torkoal or Ninetales must set sun to activate Hisuian Lilligant's Chlorophyll, with each providing unique utility. Torkoal is bulkier, sets Stealth Rock, and removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin, while Ninetales brings greater Speed, Encore to disrupt setup, and Healing Wish to give Hisuian Lilligant a second chance to sweep. Walking Wake and Raging Bolt are excellent teammates, threatening the physical walls that Hisuian Lilligant struggles with, notably Moltres and Pecharunt. In return, Hisuian Lilligant pressures special walls such as Garganacl and Ting-Lu, giving Walking Wake and Raging Bolt space to break teams. Great Tusk supports Hisuian Lilligant with hazard control and physical pressure on Pecharunt and Gholdengo, as well as removing the Heavy-Duty Boots from Moltres to wear it down with hazards, while appreciating Hisuian Lilligant's ability to soften Alomomola, Dondozo, and Ogerpon-W. Zamazenta is a major obstacle, but Hatterene can help limit its setup opportunities, as well as blocking hazards or using Healing Wish to keep Hisuian Lilligant healthy and spreading paralysis with Nuzzle to ensure that it can clean up out of sun.

monotype.overview:
Fighting

Hisuian Lilligant, on paper, has a lot of appealing traits for Fighting, thanks to Victory Dance making it an incredible setup threat. Its secondary Grass typing also provides nice resistances to Water, Electric, and Ground, making it a solid answer to threats like Urshifu-R, Raging Bolt, and the Landorus formes. However, Fighting has far better immediate powerhouses like Ursihfu-R, Iron Valiant, and Sneasler, while Hustle can often stop a Victory Dance sweep short by missing crucial attacks.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Grass

Healing Wish can serve as a niche option to help support another teammate such as an Ogerpon forme or Sinistcha in matchups where Hisuian Lilligant is less useful such as against Fire and Bug teams.

Victory Dance (Fighting).description:
Hisuian Lilligant serves as a solid setup sweeper for Fighting teams thanks to its signature move, Victory Dance, which enables it to easily set up and clean through types like Water and Ground. Leaf Blade slashes through Water- and Ground-types like Primarina, Swampert, and Great Tusk. Close Combat is Hisuian Lilligant's strongest move, muscling past Scizor and Iron Hands. Finally, Ice Spinner nails the Flying- and Grass-types that handle Hisuian Lilligant's STAB moves, such as the Landorus Formes, Amoonguss, and Sinistcha. Wide Lens is used to help offset Hustle's accuracy reduction.

Keldeo and Urshifu-R serve as excellent partners for Hisuian Lilligant by checking Fire-types such as Ceruledge and Moltres while appreciating Hisuian Lilligant checking Water-types like Primarina and Rotom-Wash that can deal with them. Keldeo can further support Hisuian Lilligant by breaking through physical walls such as Iron Defense Skarmory and Pecharunt. Assault Vest Iron Hands can handle faster special attackers such as Choice Scarf Enamorus and Gholdengo while pressuring Pelipper with Thunder Punch. Threats such as Choice Scarf Greninja and Latias are checked by Assault Vest Gallade, which can also use Psycho Cut to slice through Poison-types such as Iron Moth and Okidogi. Great Tusk's Stealth Rock support wears down Ogerpon-H and Choice Scarf Enamorus, and its Knock Off removes Rocky Helmet from threats like Skarmory and Toxapex. Iron Valiant can pressure Flying-types like Gyarados and Moltres with Thunderbolt or use Shadow Ball to pressure Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Pecharunt, while Choice Scarf Sneasler can deal with faster Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Iron Valiant with Dire Claw.

Victory Dance Sweeper (Grass).description:
Hisuian Lilligant serves as a strong wincon for Grass teams thanks to its solid Fighting typing and strong setup option in Victory Dance, which enables it to outspeed and remove problematic threats such Tornadus-T, Dragapult, and Choice Specs Flutter Mane. Close Combat tears through Steel- and Ice-types like Heatran, Bisharp, Mamoswine, and Frosmoth. Ice Spinner provides solid coverage against Flying- and Dragon-types such as the Landorus formes, Dragonite, and Dragapult as well as Grass-types capable of taking its STAB moves like Amoonguss and Sinistcha. Finally Sleep Powder can prevent would-be checks like Galarian Weezing and Okidogi from handling Hisuian Lilligant if it hasn't gotten a Victory Dance yet, while Leaf Blade enables it to break foes like Primarina, Slowbro, and Toxapex, which wall its combination of Close Combat and Ice Spinner. Wide Lens is used to help offset the accuracy lowering of Hustle along with helping Sleep Powder land.

Choice Scarf Meowscarada provides immediate speed control that enables it to handle Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Galarian Slowking, Latios, and Hisuian Zoroark along with using Knock Off to remove Rocky Helmet from the likes of Skarmory and Forretress. Ogerpon-C can help by removing Fire- and Flying-types that could handle Hisuian Lilligant like Volcarona, Moltres, and Zapdos. Alternatively, Ogerpon-H helps to pressure Ice- and Steel-types like Alolan Ninetales, Archaludon, and Gholdengo along with checking threats like Galarian Weezing. Amoonguss pressures Fairy-types such as Iron Valiant, Choice Scarf Enamorus, and Flutter Mane with Sludge Bomb, and it can use Stun Spore to slow down Choice Scarf threats like Dragapult and Greninja, which outspeed and remove a boosted Hisuian Lilligant. Sinistcha can help to handle physical walls like Galarian Weezing and Hatterene with its powerful Shadow Ball. Brambleghast can help Hisuian Lilligant by setting and removing Spikes, enabling it to wear down would-be checks like Iron Moth and Iron Hands. Brambleghast can also wall Tornadus-T and Zapdos thanks to Wind Rider while being able to remove Ghost-types like Gholdengo with Poltergeist. Hydrapple possesses a nice Fire neutrality, which enables it to check foes like Choice Scarf Hisuian Arcanine and Iron Moth prior to Hisuian Lilligant setting up, and its powerful Special Attacks helps it break physical walls like Sableye and Mandibuzz.

Victory Dance (Grass).description: With Close Combat and Victory Dance, Hisuian Lilligant is a powerful wallbreaker on Grass teams, covering the difficult Flying, Dragon, and Steel matchups. Close Combat nails bulky Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra and Heatran. Leaf Blade is a reliable secondary STAB move that can break Toxapex and offensive Gholdengo while also dealing with Gastrodon, Rotom-W, and Slowbro; however, Sleep Powder can be used instead to facilitate setting up with Victory Dance. Hustle-boosted Ice Spinner takes out Dragon-, Ground-, and Flying-types like Garchomp, Landorus, Dragonite, Mega Aerodactyl, and Zapdos after a Victory Dance. At +1, All Out-Pummeling can reliably KO tanks like Celesteela, Corviknight, and Iron Hands and, thanks to the Hustle boost, Fighting-resistant foes like Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y while ignoring the accuracy drop. Meowscarada is a perfect teammate that appreciates Hisuian Lilligant's removal of walls like Ferrothorn and Archaludon that switch into it. Meowscarada in return threatens Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo, Latios, and Latias, which Hisuian Lilligant can't touch. Mega Venusaur and Ferrothorn are defensive partners that deal with Fairy- and Poison-types like Tapu Lele and Sneasler while wearing down teams with Leech Seed and entry hazards, respectively. Ogerpon-C threatens Flying- and Fire-types like Moltres and Torkoal while benefiting from the removal of Steel-types. Whimsicott is a great support ally that removes hazards and can use Encore to give Lilligant more chances to set up. Brambleghast is another hazard removal option and spinblocker that can defend against Zapdos and Tornadus-T's Hurricane and Heat Wave with Wind Rider while providing crucial Spikes support.

nfe.overview: Krokorok is one of the tier's premier Knock Off users, thanks, in no small part, to its complementary STAB Earthquake, which deters common Knock Off absorbers such as Tinkatuff and Neutralizing Gas Koffing. Its unique dual typing is excellent not just offensively but also defensively, granting Krokorok important immunities to Psychic-type attacks from threats such as Girafarig and Hattrem, as well as Thunder Wave from users such as Tinkatuff and Drakloak. Access to Stealth Rock and Taunt cements Krokorok's niche as the most comprehensive counter to one of the most central Pokemon in the tier, Tinkatuff. However, with its mediocre Attack stat, Krokorok struggles to break through common physical walls such as Quaxwell, Quilladin, and Ivysaur, all of which threaten it back with super effective STAB moves. Furthermore, its unremarkable Speed tier leaves it outpaced by prominent threats such as Monferno, Raboot, Frogadier, and Choice Specs Drakloak, all of which easily OHKO Krokorok.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Non-Choice item Krokorok can still run Moxie over Intimidate, especially on Sticky Web structures.

Checks and Counters

Quaxwell: Krokorok's hardest counter. Short of removing its Eviolite, Krokorok struggles to get value against any Quaxwell set. Even without Eviolite, Quaxwell comfortably outheals non-Choice Band Krokorok's Earthquake, removes Stealth Rock, and hits Krokorok incredibly hard with even uninvested Flip Turns.

Water- and Grass-Types: Krokorok loses to any Water- or Grass-type in the metagame. Defensively oriented Pokemon such as Seadra, Ivysaur, and Quilladin wall Krokorok even after losing Eviolite and threaten it with any Grass- or Water-type coverage. Worse still, sweepers such as Wartortle and Servine are able to set up on Krokorok, barring Taunt in the case of the former.

Piloswine: Krokorok simply drops to Piloswine's attacks. It is notable, however, that in specific late-game scenarios, Krokorok's Intimidate can be instrumental to teammates surviving Piloswine's attacks.

Faster Attackers: With its frail defenses, Krokorok is susceptible to OHKOs from a number of faster Pokemon, including Thwackey, Monferno, and Raboot.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description:
Krokorok is an effective Stealth Rock setter thanks to its great typing and strong matchup against many prominent Pokemon in the tier. The offensive pressure of STAB Knock Off and Earthquake's coverage often results in Krokorok getting free turns to use Stealth Rock on a switch. Earthquake deters common dedicated Knock Off absorbers such as Tinkatuff and Koffing. Taunt prevents entry hazards, recovery, and status spam, and it crucially stops sweepers like Scraggy, Dunsparce, and Wartortle from setting up on Krokorok for free. Rock Slide is an option to OHKO Fletchinder, and it can also be handy for breaking Tinkatuff's Air Balloon on the switch in without making contact and allowing Tinkatuff to steal Krokorok's Eviolite with Pickpocket.

Stealth Rock Krokorok wins most of its interactions with opposing entry hazard setters, notably including Tinkatuff and Glimmet, while remaining a good progress maker with STAB Knock Off. It therefore fits on team structures that are able to capitalize on this by applying sustained offensive pressure. This can be achieved with setup sweepers like Scraggy and Wartortle, naturally strong hitters like Pignite and Thwackey, and offensive pivots like Drakloak and Monferno. Krokorok needs teammates that are able to deal with Quaxwell, which not only completely walls and counters it but also threatens to spin away its hard-earned Stealth Rock. This weakness can be covered by the likes of Thwackey, Servine, or Drakloak, though all three must be wary of Quaxwell with Triple Axel. Piloswine is the main Stealth Rock setter that beats Krokorok one-on-one, so Piloswine countermeasures are absolutely necessary. This can include Seadra, Dunsparce, and Duosion. Finally, Krokorok appreciates some hazard control from its teammates, since Spikes and Toxic Spikes severely hinder its ability to get value in longer games. Quaxwell and Fletchinder emerge as prime candidates that can compress both of these last two roles, albeit to different extents.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Krokorok is a solid form of speed control that can also act as a late-game sweeper. With Moxie, Krokorok constantly threatens to run away with the game, only fearing being revenge killed by faster Choice Scarf users such as Monferno and Girafarig, as well as strong priority moves from Piloswine and Thwackey. Earthquake makes for an excellent late-game sweeping tool once Ground-immunitie and -resistant foes have been dealt with. Knock Off guarantees progress in the mid-game. Stone Edge allows Krokorok to OHKO Fletchinder, which is often the only Ground-immune Pokemon standing between it and an Earthquake sweep. Brick Break hits Scraggy, Piloswine, and Dunsparce harder than Earthquake under Grassy Terrain while also breaking dual screens. Aqua Tail is an option to deal more damage to Piloswine and opposing Krokorok. Stealth Rock is a niche option on teams desperate for a Stealth Rock setter. It can also potentially bluff a non-Choice Scarf set.

Choice Scarf Krokorok fits on teams that need both strong speed control and a solid cleaner. For instance, defensively oriented entry hazard stacking structures appreciate Krokorok's Knock Off and late-game offensive pressure. Offensively, Krokorok appreciates hazard support from the likes of Quilladin, Dunsparce, and Glimmet to secure OHKOs against the likes of defensive Drakloak and Tinkatuff. Krokorok also needs help breaking Water- and Grass-type physical walls such as Quaxwell, Ivysaur, and Quilladin. Strong special attackers such as Drakloak, Girafarig, and Hisuian Sliggoo, as well as Fire-types such as Raboot, Monferno, and Pignite, help here. Defensively, Krokorok needs sturdy answers to Pokemon that can revenge kill it, such as Quaxwell for Choice Scarf Monferno and Piloswine, Koffing for Thwackey, and Hisuian Sliggoo for Choice Scarf Girafarig. Fletchinder is an exceptional teammate for Krokorok, countering major threats to Krokorok such as Monferno and Thwackey on account of its great defensive typing, STAB Brave Bird, and, for the latter, Flame Body. Ivysaur is another strong partner for Krokorok since its typing enables it to deal with Water- and Grass-types both offensively and defensively. It also absorbs Toxic Spikes, which Krokorok appreciates, while Ivysaur appreciates Krokorok's Psychic-type immunity.

ru.overview: Krookodile is a fantastic progress maker in RU due to having access to Knock Off and important utility moves like Stealth Rock and Taunt while being incredibly threatening offensively thanks to its high Attack and the perfect coverage provided by its STAB moves and Gunk Shot. Although Krookodile is most often seen taking advantage of Intimidate and its decent defensive typing to act as an entry hazard setter and physical sponge, its Choice item sets can easily run away with games if not handled carefully thanks to its spammable STAB attacks, especially when assisted by Moxie. However, Krookodile suffers from a lack of recovery options, which hinders its longevity and ability to keep hazards up throughout the game. Its overreliance on immunities and resistances to switch in on wallbreakers like Magnezone and Mimikyu further holds it back defensively. Lastly, Krookodile's mediocre Speed tier renders it vulnerable to faster threats such as Terrakion and Focus Blast Gengar.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Scale Shot + Bulk Up or Moxie can be used alongside Loaded Dice to transform Krookodile into a deceptively strong setup sweeper, but it is often difficult to pull off due to it being very situational. Roar and Dragon Tail are decent options for phazing out setup sweepers such as Dragon Dance Flygon that could otherwise take advantage of Krookodile.

Checks and Counters

Physical Tanks: The common physically defensive Pokemon in RU, particularly Quagsire, Slowbro, and Chesnaught, can often wall Krookodile and keep it from making progress. While Krookodile can hit the last two with Knock Off and Gunk Shot, it is still fearful of their retaliation through Scald and Body Press, respectively.

Fighting-types: Fighting-type wallbreakers such as Breloom, Flamigo, and Terrakion either take little damage from or outspeed Krookodile, which allows them to blow holes through Krookodile's team after threatening it out.

Wallbreakers: Despite Intimidate, Krookodile's subpar bulk often prevents it from switching into strong physical attacks such as Maushold's Population Bomb and Entei's Sacred Fire. It is also quite vulnerable to coverage from special wallbreakers such as Moonblast Gardevoir, Boomburst Toxtricity, and Focus Blast Gengar, which serve as deterrent for its entry; otherwise, Krookodile would want to switch in on one or both of their STAB moves because of its immunity or resistance to them. Therefore, Krookodile's defensive utility is often heavily prediction-reliant and can be exploited by offensive structures.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band Krookodile is a ferocious wallbreaker with its nearly unresisted STAB combination of Earthquake and Knock Off. It is difficult to consistently weather Krookodile's attacks due to its resistance to Stealth Rock and serviceable natural bulk combined with Intimidate giving it many opportunities to hit the field against Pokemon such as Rotom-H, Necrozma, and Reuniclus. Gunk Shot gives Krookodile great coverage, hitting common checks to it like Chesnaught for decent damage, while also having the ability to spread poison. Close Combat gives Krookodile the ability to annihilate Dark-types like Umbreon and opposing Krookodile. Crunch can be used to consistently hit Pokemon such as Slowbro and Noivern once their item has been removed. Tera Dark allows for freakishly powerful Dark-type STAB moves, allowing it to OHKO Slowbro with a boosted Knock Off or Crunch after Stealth Rock and 2HKO Amoonguss with Knock Off. It also gives Krookodile the ability to shed its Ground typing, removing its Water- and Grass-type weaknesses and improving matchups into Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Choice Scarf Basculegion-F. Alternatively, Tera Poison can be used to flip its Bug- and Fighting-type weaknesses, giving it better matchups into Pokemon such as Flamigo and Terrakion. It also strengthens Gunk Shot, allowing Krookodile to completely crush its common checks like Chesnaught.

Krookodile thrives on bulky offense and balance teams where it acts as a wallbreaker that provides defensive utility due to its Electric and Psychic immunities. Krookodile fits well with pivots that allow it to freely switch in without taking any sort of damage such as Magnezone, Noivern, and Jirachi, since it lacks recovery. Slowbro pairs well with Krookodile, as it resists the Fighting- and Water-type attacks from Pokemon like Terrakion and Barraskewda aimed at Krookodile, while Krookodile resists the Electric- and Ghost-type attacks from Magnezone and Gengar aimed at Slowbro. Slowbro also spreads paralysis with Thunder Wave, which Krookodile greatly appreciates, as it is slower that some potent offensive threats such as Noivern and Gengar. Future Sight support from Slowbro and Reuniclus can threaten the Poison- and Fighting-types such as Amoonguss, Breloom, and Chesnaught that switch into Krookodile. Krookodile enjoys entry hazard control from the likes of Cyclizar and Noivern due to its vulnerability to Spikes. They are also pivots that invite in Steel-types for Krookodile, while Noivern is a great defensive presence capable of switching into a plethora of strong attackers such as Breloom, opposing Krookodile, and Flamigo. Balance teams that slowly whittle down the opposition, especially with Spikes support from the likes of Chesnaught and Quagsire, enjoy Krookodile's unique defensive profile as well as strong STAB Knock Off to remove the ever-present Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers. Bulky offense teams with multiple switch moves like U-turn from Pokemon like Cyclizar, Noivern, and Jirachi provide Krookodile with many entry points, capitalizing on its offensive and defensive utility to maintain hazards and wear down teams.

Stealth Rock.description:
Krookodile solidifies its place in the metagame as the premier offensive Ground-type, with access to Stealth Rock and Intimidate giving it great utility for an offensive Pokemon. Krookodile has advantages over other entry hazard setters like Registeel and Empoleon because of its combination of good Speed and access to Knock Off, which helps accumulate hazard chip damage by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from checks such as Slowbro. Taunt helps Krookodile disrupt slower Pokemon trying to setup on it like Cresselia and Torterra while also being used to prevent other Pokemon like Quagsire and Umbreon from setting up hazards and using status moves. Gunk Shot helps against switch-ins that would otherwise resist its STAB moves, hitting Chesnaught for super effective damage. Leftovers is preferred on Krookodile to passively recover on Pokemon it forces out, giving it more longevity and offsetting Stealth Rock damage. Tera Poison flips the weaknesses to Bug, Fairy, and Fighting into valuable resistances while giving Gunk Shot a STAB boost. Resisting Bug- and Fighting-type attacks is great for Krookodile, allowing it to resist U-turn from Cyclizar and take on Fighting-type Pokemon faster than it such as Terrakion and Choice Scarf Flamigo. Tera Ghost similarly flips the weaknesses to Bug and Fighting, and allows Krookodile to block Rapid Spin from the tier’s most common hazard removal, Cyclizar.

Stealth Rock Krookodile fits on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate having a more offensive entry hazard setter that is able to force progress with Knock Off, stack hazard chip damage on Heavy-Duty Boots users, and threaten common hazard removal options like Cyclizar and Noivern. Steel-types such as Empoleon and Jirachi make for good teammates, resisting Fairy-type attacks from Gardevoir that would otherwise threaten Krookodile. Empoleon also covers its Water-type weakness, and Jirachi appreciates having a teammate that can take Dark-type moves for it. Krookodile also appreciates physically defensive Pokemon like Slowbro and Noivern that can switch into Fighting-types that threaten Krookodile such as Flamigo and Breloom. Offensive teammates such as Gengar and Basculegion-F benefit from Krookodile removing Assault Vest from their most common switch-in, Cyclizar, as well as Heavy-Duty Boots from Noivern.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Krookodile can fill many roles in a match; it can revenge kill weakened foes, force progress against bulky teams with Knock Off, switch into attacks that it resists to threaten slower foes with a KO, and clean up teams weakened by its teammates. Gunk Shot threatens Grass-types like Wo-Chien and Chesnaught and can poison Slowbro, which is otherwise able to check Krookodile once its item is removed. Stone Edge hits Flying-types like Noivern and Kilowattrel hard. Close Combat can OHKO Cyclizar and provides strong coverage for opposing Krookodile, Wo-Chien, and Crawdaunt. Stealth Rock allows Krookodile to be an entry hazard setter, letting more offensive teams forgo a more defensive hazard setter like Quagsire or Empoleon. Choice Scarf makes Krookodile outspeed the entire unboosted metagame and other common Choice Scarf users like Basculegion-F and Gardevoir. Intimidate lets Krookodile take hits from physical attackers like Jirachi to force them out or revenge kill them. Moxie lets Krookodile be a late-game cleaner and sweeper that makes sacrificing Pokemon to bring others in much riskier for the opponent. Tera Poison lets Krookodile resist normally super effective attacks such as Moonblast from Gardevoir, Close Combat from Terrakion, and Giga Drain from Amoonguss allowing it to score KOs it may otherwise not have and begin its sweep with Moxie boosts. Tera Poison also empowers Gunk Shot, turning it into Krookodile's strongest STAB attack. Tera Dark is an alternative that boosts Knock Off, letting it OHKO Jirachi and Reuniclus after a bit of chip damage. It also removes Krookodile's weakness to Aqua Jet from Crawdaunt and Feraligatr.

Choice Scarf Krookodile fits on more offensive teams that are looking for a sweeper that doesn't need to take time to set up or a revenge killer that can safely switch into or force out physical wallbreakers. Krookodile can switch into predicted Electric- and Psychic-type attacks from Magnezone, Gardevoir, and Reuniclus and force them out, but it needs to be careful when doing so, as these Pokemon carry coverage moves that threaten Krookodile. Spikes stacking teams can benefit immensely from Krookodile due to its ability to get rid of Heavy-Duty Boots with STAB Knock Off and sweep a weakened opposing team with Moxie boosts. Chesnaught can take the Grass- and Water-type attacks that threaten Krookodile while also taking Knock Off handily and setting Spikes. Poison-types like Gengar and Amoonguss can swap into the Fighting-, Fairy-, and Grass-type attacks that Krookodile would rather avoid while also baiting out Psychic-type attacks for Krookodile to freely switch into. Steel-types additionally can easily take the Grass- and Fairy-type attacks that threaten Krookodile, making Jirachi and Magnezone excellent partners. Krookodile is a great partner for Cyclizar, as it is able to threaten Ghost-types that come in and spinblock Cyclizar. It also synergizes with another entry hazard remover in Noivern, which can take Fighting-, Water-, and Grass-type attacks aimed at Krookodile. Strong wallbreakers like Gengar can threaten defensive checks to Krookodile like Slowbro and Chesnaught, making progress against Pokemon that it struggles with. Defensive checks to Krookodile like Quagsire and Gastrodon can also be threatened by strong special attackers like Toxtricity and Hisuian Goodra.

Choice Scarf Krookodile is a decent revenge killer and Pursuit trapper, sporting good matchups into common offensive threats such as Aegislash, Iron Boulder, Zeraora, and Alakazam as well as the ability to deal with special walls such as Slowking and Jirachi. Additionally, Krookodile's access to Intimidate alongside its decent physical bulk can also help it deal with or play around other physical attackers such as Excadrill, Victini, and Tyranitar. However, Krookodile faces heavy competition in this role, being difficult to justify over other Pursuit trappers such as Tyranitar, Mega Aerodactyl, and Bisharp as well as other Choice Scarf users such as Mienshao and Enamorus, which provide more offensive flexibility and better defensive utility options on most teams. The aforementioned Pursuit users also have a much easier time eliminating said targets due to their higher Attack stats, requiring less chip damage. Knock Off allows Krookodile to cripple incoming defensive Pokemon by removing their item, notably removing Leftovers from Clefable and Celesteela and Heavy-Duty Boots from Scizor and Amoonguss and assisting its teammates in breaking past them. Earthquake is Krookodile's strongest Ground-type STAB option, being able to OHKO Excadrill as well as Victini and offensive Aegislash after slight chip damage; it also allows Krookodile to apply decent pressure to defensive Pokemon such as Scizor and Amoonguss after it has removed their item with Knock Off. Toxic allows Krookodile to punish incoming defensive Pokemon such as Buzzwole, Hydrapple, and Hippowdon that otherwise don't mind taking a Knock Off. Alternatively, if Krookodile's team necessitates it, Stealth Rock enables Krookodile to set entry hazards for its team to help gradually wear down defensive Pokemon such as Mega Venusaur. Choice Scarf Krookodile is used on select bulky offense and balance teams that require its ability to outspeed and trap important threats such as Swords Dance Aegislash and Iron Boulder, relieving its teammates of having to deal with them throughout the match. Special attackers such as Keldeo, Enamorus, and Iron Moth benefit the most from Krookodile's ability to deter revenge killing attempts from these Pokemon and remove dedicated checks such as Slowking, making them far more offensively threatening as a result. Entry hazard support from Pokemon such as Clefable, Skarmory, and Blissey is crucial to help force chip damage to where Krookodile can comfortably KO the aforementioned offensive Pokemon, allowing it to trap them much more effectively. Additionally, they can also help Krookodile defensively check Pokemon such as Mienshao, Hydrapple, and Mega Venusaur that typically force it out. Lastly, pivoting teammates such as the aforementioned Blissey as well as Scizor and Rotom-W are similarly important in assisting Krookodile with finding opportunities to get onto the battlefield and trap its desired targets; Blissey and Scizor can use Teleport and U-turn, respectively, on Aegislash, whereas Rotom-W can use Volt Switch on Slowking and Mega Latias, ensuring Krookodile doesn't have to take risk being crippled or taken out by their coverage moves in the process.

Offensive Pivot.description: EV spread avoids an OHKO from Cobalion’s Close Combat while still outpacing Jolly Lucario.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Galarian Darmanitan makes for a strong yet niche revenge killer against top threats such as Zacian-C, Eternatus, Arceus-Ground, and Deoxys-A for balance and bulky offense teams. It also assists its teammates with U-turn support, making it a solid source of speed control. However, its Stealth Rock weakness limits its overall longevity and makes it weaker to priority moves from Marshadow and Arceus, which other speed control options such as Pheromosa do not have to deal with, and it is often setup fodder for Pokemon such as Tera Water Zygarde, defensive Primal Kyogre, and Alomomola. This means that Galarian Darmanitan is mostly used to strengthen the team against opposing offense matchups, rather than being consistent into other structures such as fat balance or stall.

  • Earthquake complements Icicle Crash nicely, hitting the Steel- and Fire-types, such as Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Chi-Yu, that resist the latter while also hitting Primal Groudon super effectively. Rock Slide is necessary to prevent Ho-Oh from scouting Galarian Darmanitan's chosen move and cleanly OHKO it, which is very useful for Galarian Darmanitan's teammates to capitalize on afterwards. U-turn is necessary for pivoting against foes Galarian Darmanitan cannot handle, which is needed early-game against healthy Primal Groudon, Zygarde, Ho-Oh, and support Arceus formes. Flare Blitz can be considered over Earthquake, notably for being able to OHKO Zacian-C more reliably while also OHKOing Ferrothorn and Calyrex-I after Stealth Rock. However, the recoil combined with Galarian Darmanitan's weakness to Stealth Rock; its inability to hit Water-types, notably offensive Primal Kyogre; and its inability to hit Primal Groudon super effectively makes this rarely worthwhile, especially because Ferrothorn is already at risk of being 2HKOed by Icicle Crash.

  • Tera Ground not only removes Galarian Darmanitan's Stealth Rock weakness but also bolsters Earthquake's power to new heights. It notably gives Earthquake a chance to OHKO Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and offensive Primal Kyogre after Stealth Rock, more reliably OHKOes Zacian-C and Eternatus, and is useful against Tera Fire variants of Eternatus.

  • Galarian Darmanitan works best on bulky offense structures where its ability to pivot and prevent setup sweepers from getting out of hand is valued. Due to its horrendous bulk, Galarian Darmanitan works best as a revenge killer and should only come in after a fainted ally or a slow pivot such as Landorus-T, after which it can safely remove an offensive threat like Zacian-C or Eternatus.

  • Outside of hyper offense matchups, Galarian Darmanitan works best as a cleaner rather than a wallbreaker. The latter role is performed much better by other offensive Ice-types such as Chien-Pao and Kyurem-B, but Galarian Darmanitan's higher Speed and unresisted coverage allow it to make quick work of opposing teams in the late-game after offensive pressure from teammates such as Eternatus and Primal Groudon have worn down would-be checks such as Necrozma-DM or Ho-Oh. Galarian Darmanitan can also be used as a lead thanks to its fast U-turn, but switch-ins to other common leads such as Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground are necessary, making Giratina-O and Ho-Oh fantastic partners.

  • Eternatus is one of Galarian Darmanitan's best partners; offensive sets, such as Meteor Beam and Choice Specs, are able to break through physical walls such as Zygarde and Primal Groudon, with Meteor Beam sets sniping Ho-Oh too, making Galarian Darmanitan harder to pivot into with its colorful coverage. Eternatus may also encourage Ho-Oh to use Tera Grass to avoid being OHKOed by Meteor Beam, opening itself up to Galarian Darmanitan afterwards. Meanwhile, defensive sets utilize Toxic Spikes to slowly wear down foes, allowing Galarian Darmanitan to easily clean up afterwards thanks to all the switches it forces. In return, Galarian Darmanitan is able to revenge kill Zacian-C and Deoxys-A and wear down Necrozma-DM, all three of which Eternatus does not like dealing with. It can also snipe Ho-Oh with Rock Slide, removing one of Eternatus's best checks, and pivot into Eternatus against Water-types such as Alomomola, Arceus-Water, and defensive Primal Kyogre, against which it can begin to set up easily. It should be noted that Choice Specs sets on Eternatus are able to both wallbreak and set up Toxic Spikes for Galarian Darmanitan.

  • Galarian Darmanitan is both weak to Stealth Rock and weakened by Sticky Web, which heavily limits what it is capable of revenge killing against hyper offense teams; this makes Defog users such as Giratina-O and offensive Ho-Oh fantastic partners. They are both good at wearing foes down with Toxic support, and the former is able to check Double Dance Primal Groudon, which Galarian Darmanitan cannot outspeed and revenge kill. Giratina-O is also good at breaking through Tera Water Zygarde, which completely walls Galarian Darmanitan, while also containing Extreme Speed Arceus, which is able to revenge kill Galarian Darmanitan with ease. Mega Diancie is another strong option to pair with Galarian Darmanitan, as it is able to prevent Sticky Web from going up, while Galarian Darmanitan easily removes Pokemon that outspeed and OHKO Mega Diancie such as Zacian-C and Deoxys-A.

  • Galarian Darmanitan also enjoys entry hazard support, which allows it to achieve more damage thresholds such as OHKOing offensive Eternatus with Earthquake. This makes Primal Groudon and Ferrothorn good allies; these two are also able to check Primal Kyogre and Arceus-Water, while Tera Grass Ferrothorn does well against Tera Water Zygarde. Offensive teammates such as Zacian-C, in conjunction with Galarian Darmanitan, can easily wear down their common checks such as Necrozma-DM and Ho-Oh. Zacian-C and offensive Ho-Oh are able to check Calm Mind Arceus-Dark and Arceus-Fairy, both of which are threats to the offense teams Galarian Darmanitan fits best on.

Galarian Darmanitan easily applies offensive pressure thanks to the sheer damage output of its moves and Speed with the combo of Gorilla Tactics + Choice Scarf, allowing it to act as a potent revenge killer and wallbreaker for Ice teams. Flare Blitz provides coverage against Steel-types including Corviknight and Ferrothorn. Earthquake further complements Galarian Darmanitarian's moveset to provide nearly unresisted coverage alongside its STAB Icicle Crash, OHKOing Fire-types that resist its other moves such as Ceruledge and Heatran. U-turn allows Galarian Darmanitan to gain momentum on predicted switches and wears down checks over time. As Galarian Darmanitan can struggle with Water-types such as Toxapex, Slowbro, and Araquanid, Kyurem and Alolan Ninetales make for formidable partners, as they hit these foes super effectively with Freeze-Dry and can take advantage of their passivity to apply further pressure on the opposing team. Getting Choice locked into the wrong move often forces Galarian Darmanitan to switch out; therefore, Piloswine and Articuno act as defensive partners to resort to in such scenarios. Articuno and Cloyster can provide entry hazard control to mitigate Galarian Darmanitan's weakness to Stealth Rock, raising its longevity, with the former also providing pivoting to ease Galarian Darmanitan's entry into the field. Other offensive partners such as Weavile and Cetitan can complement Galarian Darmanitan in applying offensive pressure to overwhelm opposing walls and potentially sweep.

nfe.overview: Scraggy is one of the most threatening end-game sweepers the tier has to offer, having good bulk, a strong offensive typing, excellent STAB moves in Knock Off, Drain Punch, and High Jump Kick. It also has two great setup options in Dragon Dance and Bulk Up, letting it use two different sweeper sets. Scraggy is especially great at dealing with bulky teams, which the tier is full of, and takes advantage of many defensive Pokemon such as Dunsparce, Dusclops, and Hattrem.
