Scraggy also checks several special attackers such as Hisuian Sliggoo, Drakloak, and Girafarig.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Rock Slide can be used over Taunt on the Dragon Dance set to lure and take down Fletchinder. Running 100 EVs in Speed allows Scraggy to outspeed Ivysaur, giving it a chance to win against it if it does not have Leech Seed or has been significantly weakened.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Monferno and Pignite can both come in on Scraggy easily and threaten it with a super effective Close Combat. Additionally, Raboot can turn into a Fighting-type when using High Jump Kick thanks to Libero, and opposing Scraggy threaten Scraggy despite not wanting to come in on Knock Off or a Fighting-type STAB move.

Fairy-types: Despite Clefairy being quite rare, it checks both Scraggy sets very comfortably. Tinkatuff also deals with it easily if it has Play Rough.

Anti-Setup: Quilladin and Mareanie prevent Scraggy from setting up with Roar and Haze, respectively. Encore users such as Tinkatuff and Quaxwell lock Scraggy into setup moves, although such Pokemon struggle to check the Dragon Dance set due to Taunt and High Jump Kick's strong damage.

Fletchinder: Fletchinder walls Scraggy and threatens to 2HKO with Brave Bird.

Ivysaur: Ivysaur with Leech Seed walls Scraggy and deals with it long-term due to Rest not having enough PP to stall Ivysaur's STAB moves. However, it cannot deal with Dragon Dance sets effectively.

Setup Pokemon: Scraggy has a hard time setting up against offensive teams that have Pokemon able to set up such as Servine, Fraxure, and Gabite, as they will outdamage it pretty quickly.

Bulk Up.description:
Thanks to its great special bulk, typing, and ability, Scraggy with Bulk Up acts as a special wall and a bulky setup sweeper at the same time, checking special attackers such as Girafarig, Drakloak, and Hisuian Sliggoo. Knock Off helps make progress by removing foes' items, making it easier for Scraggy's teammates to break through. Rest paired with Shed Skin provides a reliable recovery option thanks to Shed Skin curing Scraggy's status effects, giving it more opportunities to set up.

Bulk Up Scraggy works best on bulky teams looking for a solid sweeper. Physical walls such as Koffing and Dusclops appreciate Scraggy's ability to check special attackers that switch in easily on them such as Hisuian Sliggoo, Girafarig, and Drakloak. Entry hazard setters that cannot break through Hattrem like Quilladin and Glimmet appreciate Scraggy coming in on Hattrem freely. Offensive Pokemon such as Drakloak, Piloswine, and Raboot each struggle against a different wall— Hisuian Sliggoo, Dunsparce, and Dusclops— making Scraggy a great partner, as it can set up on many walls with ease. Pokemon that cover Scraggy's Fighting weakness such as Koffing and Fletchinder are greatly appreciated; in return, Scraggy can take advantage of Glimmet for them. Encore users such as Quaxwell and Tinkatuff disrupt Scraggy by locking it into a move, so Pokemon that can break them, such as Drakloak for the former and Piloswine for the latter, will make good partners. Pokemon that prevent setup like Mareanie and Quilladin prevent Scraggy from sweeping, so Pokemon that can take advantage of them like Girafarig and Piloswine are appreciated. Ivysaur walls Scraggy, meaning that Pokemon like Quilladin and Hisuian Sliggoo that check it will pair well with Scraggy. Fletchinder deals with Scraggy thanks to its Flying-type, so Pokemon like Glimmet and Pikachu that can take advantage of it make great partners for Scraggy. Scraggy struggles with Fairy-type moves such as Play Rough from Tinkatuff and Dazzling Gleam from Girafarig, so switch-ins like Tinkatuff are appreciated.

Dragon Dance.description:
Scraggy is one NFE's scariest setup sweepers, with its typing, stats, and Dragon Dance allowing it to steamroll teams after a boost. At +1 Speed, it can outrun opposing attackers like Monferno, Thwackey, and Gabite. +1 High Jump Kick is able to accomplish feats like OHKOing Monferno, non-Eviolite Thwackey, and having reasonable odds of OHKOing Pignite after Stealth Rock. Drain Punch sacrifices these damage thresholds for additional recovery and a better safety net. Knock Off rattles Fighting-resistant and -immune walls like Ivysaur, Hattrem, and Drakloak. Taunt disrupts walls like Tinkatuff, Koffing, and Ivysaur looking to lock Scraggy into unfavorable moves or trying to recover their health. Shed Skin provides a luck-reliant safety net against status-reliant Pokemon like Dunsparce, Drakloak, and Dusclops, though Moxie can be used to make Scraggy even more frightening at late-game cleaning. A Jolly nature can be used over an Adamant nature to let Scraggy outspeed Raboot and Girafarig at +1 at the cost of sacrificing damage breakthroughs.

This Scraggy set is best used on offensive and hyper offensive builds as a mid- or late-game cleaner. Wallbreakers like Fraxure, Pignite, and Monferno are able to pressure Scraggy into switching out, preventing it from sweeping early, so walls to these threats like Tinkatuff, Seadra, and Quaxwell can be good as fallback options. Poison-types like Koffing and Ivysaur can trade with Scraggy with relative ease via Neutralizing Gas and Knock Off, respectively, so Piloswine and Psychic-types like Girafarig and Hattrem can be good at forcing them out. While rare, Clefairy is able to stave off both of Scraggy's STAB moves and rapidly wear it down with Night Shade. Scraggy also appreciates having Thunder Wave and dual screens support from utility Pokemon like Morgrem and Drakloak to make its sweeping capabilities easier. Other setup sweepers and wallbreakers like Fraxure, Gabite, and Thwackey can collaborate to overwhelm shared checks to either make Scraggy's sweeping job easier or to take advantage of Scraggy's wallbreaking themselves. Fletchinder can be troublesome thanks to Flame Body and Brave Bird; checks to it like Quaxwell and Hisuian Sliggoo are appreciated.

nu.overview: Thanks to its solid mixed bulk, many resistances, and great abilities, Scrafty is a potent setup sweeper. Both Bulk Up and Dragon Dance sets are major setup threats because of Scrafty's access to STAB Knock Off, Close Combat, and Drain Punch for great overall power, utility, and sustainability. Staple Pokemon like Alolan Muk and Amoonguss can be setup fodder for Scrafty, letting it prey on common defensive cores. Bulk Up turns Scrafty into a bulky booster that can overwhelm defensive cores relying on Swampert and Bronzong. Dragon Dance sets can snowball out of control and use Scrafty's great bulk to secure multiple boosts. Scrafty is an especially good user of Terastallization, as it's bulky and enabled by flipping its few major weaknesses into resistances. Shed Skin is a fantastic ability to make status users like Vaporeon and Galarian Slowbro insecure checks to Scrafty, and Scrafty even has other good abilities like Intimidate and Moxie to facilitate its sweeping. However, Scrafty has major vulnerabilities to Fairy-types like Diancie and Scream Tail and Fighting-type revenge killers like Paldean Tauros-W and Paldean Tauros-F, so it's often pressured to exhaust Terastallization. Dragon Dance sets can struggle if they don't have the opportunity to acquire multiple boosts, and Bulk Up sets can be overwhelmed by strong special attackers like Toxtricity and Sylveon. Scrafty's low Speed trips it up by making it vulnerable to Encore and Taunt, and its average Attack makes it even more prone to Trick and phazing.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Ice Punch hits Flying- and Dragon-types like Altaria, Gligar, and Flygon very hard, but Scrafty struggles to fit it for this one matchup over its coverage moves for Fairy-types. Tera Ghost is an option for a useful immunity against Fighting-types like Paldean Tauros-W and Body Press users like Bronzong, potentially turning them into setup fodder or giving Scrafty a critical turn where it doesn't have to take any damage when it's weakened.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Diancie can OHKO Scrafty with Moonblast and is capable of beating it with Body Press and boosts from Diamond Storm. However, Diancie can be overwhelmed due to its dependence on Leftovers for recovery and lack of Fighting resistance. Klefki can force Bulk Up sets to either Terastallize or fall to Dazzling Gleam, but Dragon Dance Scrafty can threaten to OHKO Klefki with +1 Close Combat after Spikes damage. Calm Mind and lead Scream Tail variants can both beat Scrafty, but utility sets are setup fodder for Dragon Dance Scrafty. Fairy-types like Sylveon and Florges and Tera Fairy users like Uxie and Milotic should stay wary of Scrafty's coverage moves.

Fighting-types: Flamigo, Toxicroak, and Heracross all deal major damage to Scrafty with their STAB moves and resist both of Scrafty's STAB types. Paldean Tauros-F and Paldean Tauros-W can run Choice Scarf to outspeed Dragon Dance Scrafty variants, and they both soften it up with Intimidate. Breloom and Infernape can both pick off weakened Scrafty with Mach Punch.

Flying-types: Scyther, Staraptor, and Kilowattrel both outspeed and threaten Scrafty with their super effective STAB attacks, and the last one even outspeeds Jolly Scrafty at +1. Neither of these Pokemon, or most Flying-types in general, enjoy switching into Knock Off. Gligar can beat Dragon Dance sets in a vacuum, but it can lose to Bulk Up sets. Trapper Altaria sets can remove Scrafty with Perish Song.

Poison-types: Toxicroak and Amoonguss both resist Scrafty's Fighting-type moves; Toxicroak can hit Scrafty back hard with Fighting-type moves, and Amoonguss is bulky enough to chip down Scrafty with Sludge Bomb and Giga Drain. However, Amoonguss can lose to Shed Skin Bulk Up Scrafty sets.

Item Removal and Disruption: Chandelure, Munkidori, and Meloetta can cripple Scrafty with a Choice item if they're not able to KO it, leaving it exploitable. Fast Encore users like Scream Tail, Cinccino, and Uxie can force Scrafty to repeatedly set up or use Rest, which enables them and their teammates to begin exploiting it.

Bulk Up.description:
Set Details

Drain Punch's healing makes Scrafty less reliant on Rest. Knock Off is especially useful to soften up Gligar and punish Scrafty's checks, including Scyther, Diancie, and Altaria. Throat Chop stops Sylveon from using Hyper Voice and prevents Bronzong from using Psychic Noise if Scrafty has Terastallized into a Poison-type. Rest is less passive on Scrafty than other Pokemon thanks to Shed Skin's potential to wake up Scrafty early, and it's helpful both as a recovery move and immediate method to heal status. The EV spread allows Scrafty to outpace foes like Vaporeon and Sylveon. Shed Skin has good synergy with Rest and keeps Scrafty healthier against status spreaders like Alolan Muk, Gligar, and Vaporeon. Both Tera Poison and Tera Steel flip Scrafty's problematic 4x Fairy weakness into a resistance, which improves its matchups against Diancie, Sylveon, and Scream Tail. Tera Poison helps Scrafty against Fighting-types like Toxicroak and opposing Scrafty, while Tera Steel is more useful against Alolan Ninetales and Kilowattrel.

Scrafty is unlikely to sweep unless Fairy-types like Scream Tail, Florges, and Sylveon have been weakened. Bronzong, Klefki, and Orthworm check Fairy-types for Scrafty, and they can set entry hazards to wear down Diancie and Amoonguss. Ground-types like Flygon, Gastrodon, and Swampert can handle Poison-types like Toxtricity and Toxicroak for Scrafty. Spikes setters like Klekfi, Gligar, and Orthworm are especially good at making sure foes like Amoonguss are softened up for Scrafty, and Scrafty's Knock Off synergizes with them by removing Heavy-Duty Boots. Specially defensive Pokemon like Diancie, Bronzong, and Porygon2 are great answers to problematic special attackers like Alolan Ninetales, Kilowattrel, and Chandelure that can pressure Scrafty with their super effective and powerful STAB moves, and the former two walls can set up hazards for Scrafty as well. Physical walls like Galarian Slowbro, Vaporeon, and Gligar support Scrafty by handling physical attackers like Paldean Tauros-F, Incineroar, and Flamigo.

Dragon Dance.description:
Set Details

Drain Punch helps keep Scrafty healthy enough to stay out of range of priority users like Basculegion-M and Choice Scarf revenge killers like Flygon. Knock Off can be helpful to soften up checks to Scrafty such as Scream Tail, Gligar, and Sylveon so that Scrafty can more easily sweep past them late-game. Throat Chop lacks Knock Off's general utility and initial additional power, but its effect of disabling sound-based moves helps against foes like Sylveon and Toxtricity. Scrafty can run Encore to navigate around problematic foes like Milotic and Vaporeon, and it can turn passive walls like Avalugg and Amoonguss into setup fodder. Poison Jab is preferred as a coverage move for its synergy with Tera Poison, but Iron Head nails Alolan Ninetales and Diancie. Similarly to Drain Punch, Leftovers helps keep Scrafty out of range of revenge killers like Basculegion-M. However, a Lum Berry is very helpful for non-Shed Skin sets to help against status spreaders like Gligar, Incineroar, and Klefki if Scrafty Terastallizes. Shed Skin makes Scrafty less prone to status spreaders like Incineroar, Gligar, and Bellibolt, which can also open Scrafty up to use these Pokemon as setup fodder. Intimidate creates windows for Scrafty to set up more easily against physical attackers like Flygon and Swampert. Moxie helps Scrafty to snowball with boosts and punish opponents who eagerly sack Pokemon against it. Tera Poison helps Scrafty match up better against Fairy-types, Fighting-type revenge killers like Paldean Tauros-W, and Body Press users such as Bronzong. Tera Steel shares Tera Poison's offensive and defensive qualities against Fairy-types while giving Scrafty a better defensive typing against Flying-types like Kilowattrel and Psychic-types like Uxie.

Scrafty is a good fit for offense and balance teams as a wincon that isn't lacking a defensive backbone. Sets with Shed Skin are especially valuable as status absorbers. Scrafty can take advantage of Alolan Muk, which is appreciated by Psychic-types like Scream Tail, Oricorio-P, and Bronzong. Psychic-type pivots like Munkidori and Uxie are excellent at drawing in Alolan Muk for Scrafty and giving it free entry with their pivot moves. Setup sweepers like Flygon, Scyther, and Diancie can all overwhelm Fairy- and Poison-type walls for Scrafty. In return, Scrafty can beat Steel-types like Bronzong for the three aforementioned Pokemon. Fast Encore users like Scream Tail and Cinccino can lock passive Pokemon like Bronzong and Amoonguss into moves that let Scrafty use them as setup fodder. Alolan Ninetales supports Scrafty with Aurora Veil and Encore to widen its opportunities for setting up. Steel- and Poison-type teammates like Klefki and Munkidori can handle Fairy-types like Scream Tail and Sylveon.

Bulk Up (Fighting).description:
Scrafty makes the difference in the Dragon and Ghost matchups. Thanks to its Psychic-type immunity and good special bulk, it can tank special moves from Choice Specs Dragapult, Latios, and Gholdengo, while Shed Skin allows Scrafty to absorb status for the team. With Bulk Up, Scrafty enhances both its offensive and defensive utility and becomes able to win its duel against Archaludon. Drain Punch recovers part of the damage it inflicts and synergizes well with Bulk Up, while Knock Off deals with Psychic- and Ghost-type targets that Drain Punch does not cover such as Latios, Galarian Slowking, Dragapult, and Gholdengo. Combined with Shed Skin, Rest becomes a reliable recovery move and lets Scrafty withstand multiple powerful special moves from the likes of Greninja, Latios, and Dragapult; with a Careful nature, Scrafty is only 3HKOed by Latios's Draco Meteor.

Scrafty is well supported by Great Tusk, which can clear entry hazards from the field, set Stealth Rock, and use Knock Off to remove items such as Leftovers and Rocky Helmet from the likes of Corviknight and Garchomp. In return, Scrafty can take special moves from Dragapult and Latios. Assault Vest Iron Hands and Gallade are two prominent partners that can ease Scrafty's defensive burden for the team while also threatening out Fairy-type Pokemon like Iron Valiant and Primarina that it cannot hurt significantly. Iron Hands can especially make the difference in the Flying and Water matchups by removing Tornadus-T, Choice Scarf Enamorus, Choice Specs Kingdra, and Primarina. Gallade, on the other hand, improves the Fighting and Poison matchups, as it slashes through Keldeo, Iron Valiant, Toxapex, and Galarian Weezing. By virtue of its more defensive role, Scrafty needs to be surrounded by powerful wallbreakers that can make progress in the game like Sneasler, Iron Valiant, Urshifu-R, and Keldeo. Choice Scarf Sneasler provides an offensive check to Fairy-type foes such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Iron Valiant and can cripple Toxapex with Switcheroo, while Unburden Sneasler is a great finisher in the Fairy and Dragon matchups. Iron Valiant puts the pressure on the Steel, Flying, and Water defensive cores, easily disposing of Skarmory, Gliscor, defensive Gyarados, and Toxapex. It also synergizes well with Scrafty defensively by providing a Dragon immunity to shut down both Choice Specs Dragapult and Latios. Lastly, Urshifu-R and Keldeo are both solid options to improve specific matchups like the Ground and Dark matchups, respectively, destroying their offensive and defensive cores with their STAB combination.

Wallbreaker.description:
Hisuian Zorua provides excellent utility to a team with its combination of a high Special Attack stat, unique defensive typing, and its ability to spread burns and Knock Off. Thanks to its Normal typing, Hisuian Zorua can use Tera Blast as a STAB move even before Terastallizing to hit threats like Alolan Grimer and Shroodle. Tera Fighting lets it hit Pawniard and provides defensive value by flipping its Dark-type weakness, while Tera Ground allows it to hit Alolan Grimer, Glimmet, and Tinkatink. Hex in combination with Will-O-Wisp's burns does massive damage to even bulkier foes like Mudbray and Toedscool while cleanly OHKOing Drifloon. Will-O-Wisp helps neutralize physical attackers like Pawniard and Crabrawler and can turn them into setup fodders for other sweepers. Knock Off lets Hisuian Zorua soften up opposing teams and is also its best option for hitting opposing Hisuian Zorua. U-turn is an alternative that lets Hisuian Zorua capitalize on the switches it forces from foes like Drifloon. Nasty Plot is an option on dual screens teams where Hisuian Zorua can become a threatening sweeper.

Illusion is a highly unique ability that lets Hisuian Zorua create uncomfortable turns for your opponent by disguising as Pokemon whose checks it might beat, and Glimmet and Mudbray appreciate its ability to chip or beat opposing Mudbray and Drifloon, respectively. Pawniard enjoys Hisuian Zorua checking Crabrawler. Hisuian Zorua is often competing with Drifloon for the team's Ghost-type, so it appreciates teammates like Wattrel and Toedscool that can cover for its lack of Ground-type immunity. Crabrawler and Mudbray check opposing Pawniard for Hisuian Zorua when Tera Fight is not an option, and Alolan Grimer, Mudbray, and Croagunk switch into opposing Alolan Grimer.

pu.comments:
Usage Tips

Having Zoroark on a team provides a slightly different lead selection at the beginning of a match, in that you choose the specifc order of the entire team. The way this mechanic works is that Zoroark will be disguised as the last selected teammate, unless it is KOed in which Zoroark will disguised as the second-to-last. Therefore, teammates that Illusion benefits from as like like Golurk, Salazzle, and Tauros-Paldea-Blaze should be in the back. Furthermore, if Zoroark is not leading it should be selected for the second slot to make the most of Illusion.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Zoroark is a powerful wallbreaker that, unlike others, can surprise opponents thanks to Illusion and net KOs, paving the way for partners like Galarian Slowbro and Paldean Tauros-F. Sludge Bomb hits incoming Fairy-types that plan on taking a Dark Pulse like Florges and Grimmsnarl. Flamethrower OHKOes Alolan Sandslash, 2HKOes defensive Frosmoth, and still covers bulky Grass-types like Amoonguss and Venusaur. Focus Blast still destroys Alolan Sandslash but also 2HKOes specially bulky Normal-types like Snorlax and Porygon2 while also punishing Dark-types that try to take on Zoroark's Dark Pulse like Skuntank and Bombirdier. Grass Knot OHKOes Rhydon and Mudsdale and 2HKOes Milotic without requiring Zoroark to Terastallize. Options like U-turn and Trick can be run to give extra utility to Zoroark, allowing it to gain momentum or cripple switch-ins, though these come at the cost of valuable coverage. Tera Dark is preferred to boost Zoroark's wallbreaking capabilities to insane levels, allowing it to 2HKO Gastrodon after a layer of Spikes and non-Assault Vest Goodra, but Tera Poison gifts Zoroark a boost to its Sludge Bomb and a resistance to Fighting-type attacks, letting it survive a hit from Heracross and Paldean Tauros-F. However, Tera Fighting can also be used to boost Focus Blast's damage output, preventing Pokemon like Skuntank and Wo-Chien from taking on Zoroark as well as they could otherwise. Though, with the latter two Tera types, Zoroark's Psychic-type immunity turns into a weakness, worsening its matchup against Delphox, Meloetta, and Galarian Articuno.

Zoroark's access to Illusion allows it to pair well with Paldean Tauros-W and Calm Mind Florges, as it can disguise as them to lure in and beats Pokemon such as Decidueye, Bronzong, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro, which tend to switch in to check them. Some of Zoroark's checks, namely Milotic and Assault Vest Hariyama, are open to getting chipped away at by entry hazards, so Spikes setters like Gastrodon, Alolan Sandslash, and Heracross pair well alongside it. When paired with physical wallbreakers like Emboar and Hariyama, Zoroark can have its specially defensive checks like Scrafty and Gastrodon overpowered while together they can chip away at shared checks like Milotic and Scream Tail. Fairy- and Fighting-types like Grimmsnarl and Flamigo force Zoroark out, so checks to these Pokemon like Salazzle and Bellibolt make for strong teammates. In return, Zoroark can chip away at bulky Water- and Ground-types they struggle against, such as Qwilfish and Gligar. While Zoroark can play mind games with Illusion, how healthy a Pokemon is can easily give away who's out on the battlefield, so it must be paired with teammates that have access to entry hazard removal like Altaria, Alolan Sandslash, and Tatsugiri.

Choice Scarf.description:
Although suffering competition from other Choice Scarfers such as Florges and Flamigo due to more spammable STAB moves and more utility, Zoroark finds itself a niche thanks to a spammable STAB attack in Knock Off, great Attack and Speed stats, and Illusion allowing it to create mindgames against the opposing team. U-turn allows Zoroark to pivot against awkward matchups such as Florges and Mudsdale while generating momentum for its team. Trick cripples walls such as Bellibolt, Milotic, and Terastallized Wo-Chien as well as setup sweepers like Florges and Scrafty that would otherwise try and switch into Knock Off or try to setup and sweep. Low Kick targets Pokemon like Coalossal and opposing Dark-types such as Wo-Chien for decent damage. Tera Dark boosts the power of Knock Off, allowing Zoroark to achieve rolls such as 2HKOing Rotom-H and OHKOing Bronzong and Ambipom after minimal chip and helping Zoroark to clean up games with Knock Off. Alternatively, Tera Fighting boosts Low Kick, OHKOing Alolan Sandslash while also providing a valuable defensive typing that allows Zoroark to resist Stealth Rock and U-turn, although it makes Zoroark lose its valuable immunity to Psychic.

Choice Scarf Zoroark finds itself fitting on balance teams looking for a revenge killer and fast pivot. Zoroark struggles to break through bulky physical walls such as Bellibolt, Coalossal, and Mudsdale, so checks to these threats like Golurk and Paldean Tauros-W make good partners. Zoroark's ability to threaten out Bronzong, Delphox, and Galarian Slowbro makes it an excellent partner to Pokemon like the aforementioned Paldean Tauros-W, Toxtricity, and Salazzle. In return, Zoroark appreciates disguising as these three in order to play mindgames with its checks such as Wo-Chien and Milotic. Hazard control from Coalossal, Altaria, and Tatsugiri allows Zoroark to be a more effective pivot and revenge killer while also helping it to keep its Illusion intact. Zoroark appreciates teammates like Decidueye, Paldean Tauros-F, and Toxtricity that can take advantage to setup or revenge kill offensive Pokemon that threaten it out, such as Paldean Tauros-W, Scrafty, and Florges.

Nasty Plot.description:
Zoroark's high Speed and Special Attack alongside decent coverage allow it to serve as a threatening Nasty Plot sweeper. However, what allows Zoroark to excel in this field is its unpredictability, with its wide variety of sets and unique ability in Illusion giving it a definite niche over other Nasty Plot users such as Delphox and Salazzle. Sludge Bomb provides coverage for Fairy-types such as Florges and Grimmsnarl, as well as hitting other Dark-resistant foes such as Emboar, Hariyama, and Bombirdier neutrally. Flamethrower hits any remaining threats, OHKOing Skuntank and Heracross at after a Nasty Plot. Focus Blast is another option that hits many of the same neutral targets harder and, after using Nasty Plot, OHKOes some of Zoroark's largest roadblocks, such as Snorlax, Assault Vest Copperajah, Bulk Up Scrafty, and specially defensive Wo-Chien. However, this extra power is often not needed once boosted, and Focus Blast missing can put an end Zoroark's sweep instantly. While vast, Zoroark's special movepool falls short in power, so the extra boost from Life Orb is greatly appreciated and needed for many of the previously mentioned KOes. Heavy-Duty Boots can help Zoroark set up more safely and further help it bluff the opponent via Illusion, but losing out on the power boost from Life Orb is suboptimal. Tera Dark further helps with the lacking power, giving Dark Pulse its much-needed boost to KO bulky threats such as Milotic, Goodra, and Gastrodon with little previous damage. Tera Poison boosts Sludge Bomb to further its reliability against neutral targets and grants resistances to all of Dark's weaknesses, allowing Zoroark to tank a hit from threats like Florges, Flamigo, and Pawmot. Tera Ghost supplies similar resistances while giving up any offensive prowess for the useful immunity to priority moves like Arcanine's Extreme Speed and Pawmot's Mach Punch, and it can punish Choice-locked Pokemon like Emboar and Paldean Tauros-F. However, this also leaves Zoroark weak to previously resisted priority moves like Decidueye's Shadow Sneak and Skuntank's Sucker Punch. The defensive utility and surprise factor of Tera Poison and Ghost can also give Zoroark a chance to start setting up.

Nasty Plot Zoroark is ideally run on offensive teams seeking a late-game special sweeper rather than the utility ran on Zoroark's other sets such as item control, pivoting, and speed control. As such, it should have teammates that can take out common revenge killers like Ambipom, Choice Scarf Staraptor, and Choice Scarf Paldean Tauros-F. Bellibolt and Mudsdale make for good defensive checks to these revenge killers, with the former notably being able to paralyze these faster threats with Static and safely bring Zoroark in with its slow Volt Switch. Knock Off users like Copperajah and Gligar can also be helpful with this due to being able to remove a foe's Choice Scarf. Smeargle or Vikavolt's Sticky Web is a niche option to slow down foes but is rarely run outside of teams centered around it. Fighting-types like Pawmot, Flamigo, and Hariyama pair well with Zoroark, simultaneously luring Psychic-type moves that it can take advantage of while benefitting from the opponent's hesitance to use them. Furthermore, they are able to check special walls like Scrafty and Snorlax for Zoroark. Psychic- and Ghost-types like Delphox, Hoopa, and Golurk can accomplish similar feats alongside Zoroark while keeping Fighting-types in line. The former two pair especially well with Zoroark due to also being able to run sets with both Choice items and boosting moves, leading to more mind games with the opponent. Wallbreakers like Goodra and Choice Specs Toxtricity can wear down special walls like Wo-Chien and Gastrodon to put them in KO range for a boosted Zoroark. Florges is an especially notable threat to Zoroark due to its bulk and Fairy typing, so checks to it such as Copperajah, Galarian Slowbro, and Arcanine are much appreciated.

Swords Dance.description:
Zoroark stands out as a very strong Swords Dance user, leveraging the lack of defensive Dark-resistant Pokemon; the various Dark-weak staples like Galarian Slowbro, Delphox, and Golurk; and Illusion allowing it to disguise itself as other Swords Dance users to give it setup opportunities and tear holes in the opposing team. Knock Off and Sucker Punch are great STAB options that give Zoroark a devastating mix of wallbreaking power and priority, with Sucker Punch allowing it to pick off weakened Choice Scarf users like Staraptor and Rotom-C. Aerial Ace allows Zoroark to hit Fighting-types like Heracross and Emboar that would survive a +2 Knock Off as well as weakening all Paldean Tauros formes, while Low Kick removes Coalossal, Regirock, and Duraladon consistently; both of these options let it remove or severely weaken Scrafty and Wo-Chien. A Life Orb in conjunction with Tera Dark gives Zoroark outstanding power at +2; it gains great odds to OHKO physically defensive bulwarks like Bellibolt and Mudsdale after a single layer of Spikes, as well as always OHKOing Milotic, Altaria, and specially defensive Alolan Sandslash. Heavy-Duty Boots forgoes the power on Life Orb in favor of more bluffing potential and less chip damage, getting more setup opportunities as a result. Black Glasses can be used to hit similar damage benchmarks compared to Life Orb without taking recoil; however, it misses out on the guaranteed OHKOs stated above and has worse odds to OHKO Bellibolt and Mudsdale under the same circumstances.

Swords Dance Zoroark is an effective wallbreaker but struggles with faster Pokemon that resist Sucker Punch and slower priority users that resist Sucker Punch, like Skuntank, Paldean Tauros-W, and Choice Scarf users like Flamigo, so checks to these Pokemon are highly recommended. Bellibolt and Houndstone are solid switch-ins on bulkier playstyles, while Paldean Tauros-F and Decidueye can use Skuntank and Paldean Tauros-W, respectively, as setup fodder or can easily revenge kill them with priority after Zoroark has weakened them. Zoroark heavily appreciates partners that it can disguise itself as effectively; some notable ones include Bruxish, Scyther, and Delphox, since Zoroark disguised as them can take advantage of their switch-ins like Milotic and Meloetta. Bruxish and Scyther's access to Swords Dance as well as Scyther's and Delphox's Speed tiers make it hard to tell if it's Zoroark or not.

Nasty Plot.description: Hisuian Zoroark's combination of high Special Attack and Speed, access to Nasty Plot, and excellent typing and ability that provide setup opportunities makes it a great wallbreaker and sweeper. Focus Blast primarily targets the Dark- and Normal-types that resist or are immune to Hisuian Zoroark's Shadow Ball, notably OHKOing most variants of Tyranitar and 2HKOing Hydreigon unboosted. It also targets Steel-types like Excadrill. Fightinium Z serves the dual purpose of letting Hisuian Zoroark avoid having to rely on Focus Blast's terrible accuracy while giving it the power to OHKO foes like Hydreigon and Tyranitar unboosted and Garganacl at +2. Grass Knot hits Ground-types like Hippowdon and Gastrodon, OHKOing most of them after Nasty Plot. Hisuian Zoroark fits best on offense teams with other wallbreakers and sweepers. Teammates like Iron Moth can KO or weaken Hisuian Zoroark's checks like specially defensive Celesteela, while it can remove foes like Hippowdon. Despite its good Speed, Hisuian Zoroark is vulnerable to being revenge killed by faster foes like Choice Scarf Mienshao and Choice Scarf Hydreigon, making walls such as Skarmory for the former and Clefable for the latter useful partners. Illusion makes Hisuian Zoroark pair nicely with Pokemon weak to Fighting and Ghost, such as Tyranitar and Victini, forcing the opponent into an uneasy guessing game that can allow it or its teammates to set up. Pretending to be a physical attacker can also lure in physical walls like Skarmory and Buzzwole. Hazard setters like Excadrill and Mew can weaken checks like Mega Venusaur into Hisuian Zoroark's KO range.

Choice Specs.description: Hisuian Zoroark's high Speed, power, and spammable Shadow Ball make it a potent wallbreaker. Focus Blast OHKOes Dark-types such as Tyranitar and Hydreigon and Steel-types such as Excadrill. Grass Knot 2HKOes Ground-types like Hippowdon and Gastrodon; it also 2HKOes or 3HKOes most variants of the Tyranitar formes, easing prediction and letting Hisuian Zoroark sometimes avoid having to rely on the inaccurate Focus Blast. Trick can cripple walls Hisuian Zoroark otherwise can't touch, such as Blissey and Chansey. Hisuian Zoroark fits best on offense teams. Pivots such as Victini and Iron Moth can provide Hisuian Zoroark safe entry for it to wallbreak. Hisuian Zoroark struggles against Dark-types after being locked into Shadow Ball, especially Pursuit users like the Tyranitar formes, making Fighting-types like Buzzwole great partners for their ability to threaten them. They also work well at threatening Normal-types like Chansey and Blissey. In return, Hisuian Zoroark can eliminate physical walls like Clefable and Skarmory, and can notably lure them in thanks to Illusion. Setup sweepers like Booster Energy Iron Moth and Hydreigon can take advantage of Hisuian Zoroark weakening the opposing team's defensive cores by sweeping late-game. Entry hazard setters like Mew and Excadrill can chip Hisuian Zoroark's targets into KO range, something which notably punishes checks with limited longevity like Tapu Fini and the Tyranitar formes.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ghost (Swords Dance)

Poltergeist can be used in place of Shadow Ball, as it does more damage to foes such as Gallade and Spectrier and OHKOes Flutter Mane, but due to its lack of accuracy and Hisuian Zoroark's high Special Attack stat, Shadow Ball is more favorable.

Normal (Choice Specs)

U-turn can be used to give Hisuian Zoroark a way to pivot against would-be checks such as Clodsire, Hoopa-U, and Hisuian Goodra and bring in teammates like Ursaluna that can handle them. Psychic allows it to check Fighting-types like Keldeo, Okidogi, and Great Tusk. However, both of these options either give up crucial coverage or Trick, and Hisuian Zoroark's Speed tier leaves it slower than threats such as Sneasler and Iron Valiant, making Psychic a less desirable option overall. Grass Knot can be used to ease Normal's Water and Ground matchups, cleanly removing threats like Swampert and Hippowdon. Will-O-Wisp can spread burn, crippling switch-ins like Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra.

Choice Specs (Normal).description:
Hisuian Zoroark provides a vital role on Normal teams thanks to its Fighting immunity, empowering it to check otherwise problematic threats like Choice Specs Keldeo and Body Press Skarmory. Shadow Ball consistently blasts through threats like Archaludon, Gholdengo, and Sinistcha. Flamethrower melts through Steel-types such as Iron Treads, Corviknight, and Excadrill. Focus Blast slams Dark- and Normal-types such as Ting-Lu, Hydreigon, and Porygon2, along with majorly pressuring Hisuian Goodra. Finally, Trick can cripple would-be checks to Hisuian Zoroark, such as Blissey and Alolan Muk.

Ursaluna serves as a great offensive complement to Hisuian Zoroark, easily breaking through special walls like Clodsire, Hisuian Goodra, and Swampert while appreciating Hisuian Zoroark checking physical walls such as Skarmory and Sinistcha. Blissey provides strong support with Stealth Rock to wear down threats such as Landorus and Hoopa-U and Thunder Wave to enable Hisuian Zoroark to outspeed Flutter Mane and Darkrai while checking these threats thanks to its titanic special bulk. Porygon2 checks physical attackers that outspeed Hisuian Zoroark, like Iron Boulder, physical Dragapult variants, and Cinderace. Braviary's Ground immunity enables it to check the likes of Choice Scarf Great Tusk and Sand Rush Excadrill, and it can use U-turn to safely bring Hisuian Zoroark in. Terapagos can use Rapid Spin to help Hisuian Zoroark stay healthy, along with powerful coverage options like Ice Beam and Flamethrower to deal with annoying threats such as Gliscor and Choice Scarf Gholdengo. Choice Scarf Ditto can turn setup attempts on Hisuian Zoroark from foes like Hisuian Samurott and Calm Mind Raging Bolt against them. Choice Scarf Indeedee-M can outspeed and check non–Choice Scarf variants of threats like Sneasler and Iron Valiant, along with providing Psychic Terrain that prevents priority from Scizor and Bisharp from removing Hisuian Zoroark.

Swords Dance (Ghost).description:
With a Swords Dance set, Hisuian Zoroark becomes a surprising threat for Ghost teams, removing problematic walls such as Ting-Lu and Blissey. At +2, Poltergeist can allow Hisuian Zoroark to deal with troublesome foes such as Clodsire, Gliscor, and Swampert. Low Kick threatens the Normal- and Dark-types that can take on Poltergeist such as Blissey, Ursaluna, and Ting-Lu. Shadow Sneak allows Hisuian Zoroark to pick off weakened and faster threats such Tornadus-T, Flutter Mane, and Dragapult. Life Orb enables Hisuian Zoroark to reliably OHKO specially defensive Ting-Lu at +2 with Low Kick after entry hazard chip damage and gives a solid 50% chance to OHKO Flutter Mane with an unboosted Shadow Sneak. Spooky Plate is less powerful than Life Orb but doesn't cut into Hisuian Zoroark's health, allowing it to be more convincing with its Illusion.

Flutter Mane serves as a crucial ally in supporting Hisuian Zoroark with its Choice Specs Moonblast and blazing Speed, dealing with Dark- and Dragon-types that Hisuian Zoroark cannot handle like Mandibuzz, Greninja, and Archaludon. Gholdengo can provide Thunder Wave support, slowing down faster targets like Tornadus-T and Iron Valiant while also absorbing Will-O-Wisp from the likes of Galarian Weezing and Sableye. Pecharunt serves as a physical wall that can pivot Hisuian Zoroark in with Parting Shot along with putting physically bulky targets like Porygon2 and Mandibuzz on a timer with Malignant Chain. Sinistcha can check bulky Ground- and Water-types that could handle Hisuian Zoroark such as Hippowdon, Great Tusk, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, and Alomomola. Dragapult provides an incredibly useful Speed tier and a powerful Dragon-type STAB move such as Dragon Darts to remove problematic targets like Roaring Moon, Dragonite, and Kyurem for Hisuian Zoroark. Mimikyu can come in on Dark-types like Hisuian Samurott and Bisharp attempting to deal with Hisuian Zoroark with Sucker Punch and handle them with Drain Punch thanks to Disguise. Froslass and Brambleghast provide Spikes support, wearing down physical walls such as Toxapex, Iron Hands, and Archaludon. Froslass can also prevent entry hazards from the likes of Garchomp and Skarmory and use Destiny Bond to remove problematic walls like Moltres, while Brambleghast provides hazard removal to keep Hisuian Zoroark healthy.

Choice Scarf (Ghost).description:
Hisuian Zoroark's combination of high Special Attack and Speed, incredible typing, and an excellent ability makes it an important asset of Ghost-type teams. Shadow Ball pairs well with Illusion against Ghost teams, as it is immune to Ghost-type attacks and can attack back with Shadow Ball, knocking out foes like Dragapult and Gholdengo. Focus Blast allows it to deal with Dark-types such as Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott and Choice Specs Greninja, which threaten it. Flamethrower lets it handle Steel-types such as Scizor and Skarmory. Alternatively, Grass Knot can be used to keep Ground- and Water-types such as Hippowdon, Swampert, and Urshifu-R in check. U-turn benefits from Hisuian Zoroark's high Speed stat allowing it to deal chip damage and safely pivot out while also eliminating threats like Choice Scarf Hoopa-U and Choice Band Meowscarada. Trick can be used in place of U-turn and allows Hisuian Zoroark to neutralize threats such as Alolan Muk, Dragon Dance Dragonite, Iron Hands and Toxapex.

Hisuian Zoroark's high stats and immunity to Ghost-type moves allow it to be a great partner for all Ghost-types. Gholdengo is a great partner for Hisuian Zoroark, as its Speed tier and typing allow Hisuian Zoroark to use Illusion to its advantage. Gholdengo also serves as a great wallbreaker, eliminating foes such as Primarina and Iron Boulder and providing Hisuian Zoroark with a safe switch-in from incoming Thunder Wave from Pokemon like Blissey and Klefki. Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Mimikyu pair well with Hisuian Zoroark, as they take care of Dragon-type foes such as Roaring Moon and Hydreigon. Dragapult synergizes well with Hisuian Zoroark, forming an offensive core as Choice Scarf Dragapult takes out foes such as Hoopa-U, Kyurem, and Dragonite, which otherwise trouble Hisuian Zoroark, while Hisuian Zoroark eliminates threats like Gholdengo, Mamoswine, and Archaludon. Froslass provides Spikes support to Hisuian Zoroark. Pecharunt assists Hisuian Zoroark by spreading poison and using Parting Shot to bring Hisuian Zoroark in safely. Ceruledge appreciates Hisuian Zoroark, as it clears Ceruledge's enemies such as Toxapex and Air Balloon Heatran, which limit its sweeping capabilities.

Choice Scarf (Normal).description: This is a winning set from the Monotype Rising sets project. This will be updated as we work on new analyses. Stay tuned!

Sheer Force.description: Hisuian Zoroark serves as a threatening sweeper and wallbreaker thanks to its great Special Attack, good Speed, and incredible moveset. Body Slam allows Hisuian Zoroark to hit specially defensive walls such as Manaphy, Swampert, and Meloetta. Focus Blast hits foes like Hisuian Goodra, Roaring Moon, Chien-Pao, Blissey, and Mandibuzz. Knock Off allows Hisuian Zoroark to remove crucial items like Manaphy's and Swampert's Assault Vests and Mandibuzz's Heavy-Duty Boots, helping it and its teammates break through these Pokemon and allowing it to be more self sufficient, as it does not rely on teammates to get rid of said items. Psychic is an alternative option that dents Iron Hands, Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Iron Moth. Sheer Force lets Hisuian Zoroark hit harder to achieve feats such as 2HKOing non-Unaware Mandibuzz. A Timid nature should be used on sets with Nasty Plot, as a higher Attack is not needed. Teammates such as Iron Moth and Azelf appreciate Hisuian Zoroark's ability to force chip damage on special walls such as RegenVest Manaphy and Meloetta. Hisuian Zoroark is very frail, leaving it prone to revenge killing attempts from revenge killers like Roaring Moon and Azelf, so it appreciates slow pivots like Corviknight and Manaphy that can help it switch in safely. Hisuian Zoroark appreciates entry hazard setters like Great Tusk and Deoxys-D, as they can help chip walls that would otherwise beat it.

Magic Guard.description: Hisuian Zoroark finds a niche on semi-stall and offensive teams as a progress maker or as an offensive pivot with its wide variety of utility options and ability to ignore passive damage thanks to Magic Guard. Knock Off cripples special walls by depraving RegenVest users such as Manaphy and Swampert of their Assault Vests or by limiting Blissey's, Empoleon's, and Mandibuzz's longevity by removing their Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots, allowing Hisuian Zoroark or teammates like Iron Moth and Azelf to break past them later in the game. Will-O-Wisp further weakens these special walls, forcing them to be worn down over time and notably enabling Hisuian Zoroark's Hex to break past them; it also cripples physical threats like Great Tusk and Iron Hands. U-turn allows Hisuian Zoroark to generate free momentum for its team while forcing its switch-ins to take chip damage from entry hazards as it pivots out, whereas Taunt denies Blissey and Empoleon recovery. Hisuian Zoroark should be paired with offensive entry hazard setters like Sandy Shocks, Pixilate Scream Tail, and Galvanize Kommo-o that can keep up the pressure on hazard removers to maximize its ability to wear the opposing team down over time. Sturdy checks to offensive threats that force Hisuian Zoroark out like Roaring Moon, Choice Scarf Gholdengo, and Azelf are needed, so good teammates that can stave them off like Great Tusk and Empoleon are recommended.

Z-Happy Hour (Ghost).description: With a Ghost immunity, Hisuian Zoroark covers a crucial weakness for its team and makes use of it alongside Illusion to bluff as any of its allies efficiently and gain opportunities to set up and sweep. Focus Blast is unresisted alongside Shadow Ball and hits Dark-types that could be difficult to answer otherwise such as Hydreigon and Mega Tyranitar. Hyper Voice provides a complementary STAB option that shines in neutral matchups, 2HKOing Mega Venusaur and Toxapex after a boost, but Flamethrower complements Focus Blast to hit Steel-types such as Corviknight and Scizor. Hisuian Zoroark's sole weakness to Dark can lure in checks that can threaten a good portion of its team such as Alolan Muk and Mandibuzz. Mega Sableye is a good partner to check them in turn, and it can also prevent entry hazards from being set on its side with Magic Bounce to increase Hisuian Zoroark's longevity and allow it to bluff with Illusion further. Mimikyu discourages Dark-type attacks thanks to its Fairy typing, giving a safe option for Hisuian Zoroark to bluff as with Illusion, and an intact Disguise also lures the opposing team to expect setup and either bring in a physical wall or use utility moves such as Taunt and Will-O-Wisp that don't hinder Hisuian Zoroark as much they would Mimikyu, easing setup. Hisuian Zoroark's Illusion in general can be used to bluff as other Pokemon to lure counterplay to them that it exploits; for example, as Gholdengo, it can discourage status moves by pretending to have Good as Gold, and as Sinistcha, it can revenge kill unsuspecting foes that would normally outspeed Sinistcha.

Z-Happy Hour (Normal).description: Hisuian Zoroark provides defensive utility relevant to its team by being immune to Fighting, allowing it to easily pose as any of its allies with Illusion to find setup opportunities and sweep. Focus Blast and Shadow Ball provide unresisted coverage, allowing Hisuian Zoroark to defeat checks such as Mega Tyranitar, Heatran, and Hydreigon. Flamethrower hits foes it wouldn't OHKO otherwise, even after a boost, such as Ferrothorn, Corviknight after minimal chip, and opposing Hisuian Zoroark. Flamethrower alongside Focus Blast considerably eases the Steel matchup for its team, but Hyper Voice is an alternative that deals the most damage in neutral matchups, OHKOing Tapu Koko and Tornadus-T at +1 after Stealth Rock. Hyper Voice can also be used to trigger Breakneck Blitz over Z-Happy Hour to allow Hisuian Zoroark to lure in and overwhelm foes such as Keldeo, Hisuian Lilligant, and Landorus in a pinch. As Hisuian Zoroark lures in Dark-types to check it, Mega Lopunny is a solid partner to keep momentum against such foes, especially as Hisuian Zoroark can bluff as Mega Lopunny more effectively than other teammates, as both hold an item that cannot be removed by Trick or Switcheroo. Mega Lopunny also pressures special walls that Hisuian Zoroark can otherwise struggle with, such as Mega Sableye, Blissey, and Alolan Muk. Entry hazard control by Staraptor is also valuable to ensure Hisuan Zoroark's bluffing capabilities and raise its longevity; Staraptor can also provide a slow pivot to let Hisuian Zoroark come in safely. Chansey and Blissey can set Stealth Rock to let Hisuian Zoroark more easily threaten a sweep and can support it by providing safe pivoting for it with Teleport. In particular, it is easier for Hisuian Zoroark to disguise as Chansey due to a shared vulnerability to entry hazards.

nu.overview: Cinccino's blistering Speed and access to Technician, which it can fully take advantage of with Loaded Dice, make it a dangerous setup sweeper that can end games as easily as it can wallbreak for its partners. Passive Pokemon that might try to take advantage of Cinccino like Orthworm and Bronzong aren't safe from it either, as Cinccino can lock them into setting up entry hazards or using Iron Defense with its Encore, giving it free turns to boost with Tidy Up. On top of that, after a turn of setup, its myriad of coverage moves lets it beat anything from Flygon to Swampert easily. However, Cinccino has terrible four-moveslot syndrome, and its STAB move can be easily punished by common Rocky Helmet users like Amoonguss and Galarian Slowbro. Pokemon like Inteleon and Choice Scarf Flamigo can outpace it and threaten it with a KO, but they fail to check it after it boosts. Cinccino's Tidy Up is also a double-edged sword, as it needs the power to achieve many of its KOs, but in using the move, it removes the hazards that were helping limit its switch-ins in the first place, making it somewhat difficult to fit on many teams. Cinccino also struggles to find setup opportunities due its frailty typically only letting it survive one hit.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Protective Pads could be run to not be vulnerable to contact punishment, but with how Cinccino is then forced to use Skill Link, it becomes weaker. On teams that would like an offensive form of entry hazard control, Heavy-Duty Boots + Skill Link can be run on Cinccino alongside U-turn, letting it reliably remove hazards and bring in a wallbreaker for incoming Steel-types. However, the weaker power, along with the fact that there are better hazard removal options generally, causes it to be unused.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Orthworm, Duraludon, and Copperajah can take all of Cinccino's attacks comfortably and retaliate with a Body Press or powerful Iron Head; on top of that, the latter two can even paralyze and phaze it. Bronzong can also wall Cinccino and retaliate with Body Press, but it must beware of Knock Off. If any of them set up entry hazards or used Iron Defense as Cinccino came in, they are easily beat one-on-one due to its Encore.

Contact Punishment: Pokemon like Flame Body Chandelure and Static Bellibolt can all cripple Cinccino with a burn or paralysis, and Rocky Helmet users like Overqwil, Amoonguss, and Galarian Slowbro can chip away heavily at Cinccino if it uses Tail Slap, opening it up to being revenge killed even more easily. However, Cinccino can run Rock Blast to take out Chandelure and Knock Off to remove these crippling items.

Revenge Killers: Fast Pokemon, such as Inteleon and Kilowattrel, and Choice Scarf users, like Infernape and Munkidori, outspeed Cinccino and can threaten it with a KO if Cinccino hasn't boosted yet. On top of that, Pokemon with priority like Mach Punch Infernape and First Impression Flygon can revenge kill Cinccino as well. However, for some of these revenge killers, Cinccino can Terastallize into a Ghost- or Fairy-type and use Encore, which then provides it with setup opportunities.

Tidy Up.description:
Set Details

Knock Off hits Ghost-types that blank Cinccino's STAB attack as well as Bronzong. Encore allows Cinccino to take advantage of passive Pokemon like Swampert, Bronzong, and Palossand that use Stealth Rock or heal up, which gifts it more setup opportunities. It also helps Cinccino handle slower setup sweepers like Calm Mind Sylveon, Bulk Up Scrafty, and Iron Defense Bronzong. Bullet Seed hits some of these physically defensive checks like Swampert, Vaporeon, and Bellibolt. Alternatively, Endeavor can be used on Focus Sash sets to heavily dent Steel-types for partners like Munkidori, Scyther, and Uxie. Triple Axel can be used as a strong coverage move to nail Brambleghast, Gligar, Flygon, and Goodra. A Cinccino that aims to sweep teams should run Loaded Dice + Technician for maximum damage output. In contrast, if it chooses to be a dedicated lead, Focus Sash + Skill Link allows it to take advantage of both Tidy Up's entry hazard-clearing potential and its multi-hit moves. Tera Ghost allows Cinccino to become immune to Choice Scarf Paldean Tauros-W's as well as Infernape's Close Combat, and it lets Cinccino take advantage of it with Encore, giving Cinccino free turns to set up. Tera Fairy, while not granting an immunity to Fighting-type attacks, allows Cinccino to set up on Flamigo—which runs Scrappy— as well as other foes like Flygon, Duraludon, and Scrafty.

Cinccino struggles with breaking through Steel-types like Copperajah, Klefki, and Duraludon, so partners such as Meloetta, Overqwil, and Munkidori pair well, as they can help overwhelm these shared checks. Teammates that can benefit from Cinccino's Tidy Up removing hazards like Air Balloon Chandelure, Weakness Policy Incineroar, Choice Scarf Staraptor, and Agility Hisuian Braviary enjoy its presence; on top of that, the former two can handle Steel-types easily with their STAB moves, whereas the latter two can help wear them down. Spikes leads like Froslass and Brambleghast can help wear down checks like Orthworm and Copperajah, and a Sticky Web lead like Galvantula can help Cinccino outspeed Choice Scarf users like Infernape, Hisuian Typhlosion, and Munkidori; however, these teams must be wise about when to send out Cinccino to ensure their hazards aren't completely wasted. Physical walls that carry a way to punish contact moves through their ability like Bellibolt or item users like Rocky Helmet Amoonguss and Galarian Slowbro are issues for Cinccino, so teammates with access to Knock Off such as Incineroar and Heracross can help deal with these walls. Cinccino's frailty often hinders its ability to set up, so partners that can create opportunities like Memento Chandelure or slow pivots like Swampert and Incineroar are greatly appreciated.
This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Trapper.description:
Gothita serves as a support Pokemon in Little Cup thanks to its ability to trap Poison-types such as Foongus and Mareanie and other metagame staples such as Mienfoo, forcing them to Terastallize to survive once in range of Psychic. Trick is very important on Gothita because without it, Gothita cannot reliably threaten a healthy Foongus due to the threat of Spore, and Trick is effective at crippling bulky foes. Thunderbolt provides coverage against Vullaby, while Energy Ball deals extra damage to Ground-types such as Mudbray. Tera Psychic is the most common Tera type to enable Gothita to secure earlier KOes such as OHKOing a healthy Mienfoo.

Gothita fits best on bulky offense or balance teams with other pivots, most notably Mienfoo and Hisuian Voltorb, which typically struggle against bulky Regenerator Pokemon like Foongus and Mareanie. Choice Scarf Hisuian Growlithe also has significant synergy with Gothita, as bulky Fire resistant Pokemon such as Mareanie and Glimmet are vulnerable to being trapped. Gothita's biggest weaknesses are that it gives free entry to offensive Dark- and Steel-types after it secures a KO and that it lacks power by itself. Therefore, Gothita needs both a defensive backbone with teammates such as Mienfoo, Mudbray, and Glimmet to switch into Dark-types.

Supportive Trapper.description:
Gothitelle's Shadow Tag and vast supportive movepool provide it with a unique niche in Regulation G, allowing its partners to take full advantage of lead matchups. Gothitelle utilizes Foul Play as its offensive move to threaten the Calyrex formes. Taunt helps Gothitelle trap and shut down support Pokemon like Amoonguss and Clefairy. Helping Hand can make up for Gothitelle's lack of offensive pressure; however, Protect can be used instead on Safety Goggles sets to protect against Fake Out. Covert Cloak protects Gothitelle from Fake Out, while Safety Goggles allows Gothitelle to ignore Spore and Rage Power from Amoonguss. The EV spread lets Gothitelle survive Flutter Mane's Choice Specs Shadow Ball and Adamant Koraidon's Flare Blitz, as well as avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Tera Starstorm from Terapagos-S. Tera Dark is used to grant Gothitelle a resistance to Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage, Incineroar's Knock Off, and Chi-Yu's Dark Pulse, as well as an immunity to Prankster Taunt from Tornadus. Tera Dark also boosts Foul Play, allowing Gothitelle to threaten an OHKO on Calyrex-S and +1 Attack Calyrex-I.

Gothitelle partners especially well with hyper offensive teams, as Shadow Tag makes it easier to remove crucial pieces from the opponent's team. This is especially prevalent with Koraidon, as Gothitelle prevents Pelipper from switching in and significantly weakening Koraidon. Gothitelle trapping Pokemon that struggle to threaten Koraidon like the Ogerpon formes also allows Koraidon to set up for a sweep through Flame Charge. Choice Specs Terapagos also appreciates Gothitelle, as Gothitelle can trap the opponent's Fake Out user and Taunt Amoonguss, minimizing issues for Terapagos throughout the game. Gothitelle can also utilize its own Fake Out to help Terapagos remove Urshifu-R, which is otherwise problematic. Raging Bolt can pick off Pokemon with Thunderclap and shut down special attackers with Snarl significantly easier thanks to Gothitelle's trapping. Gothitelle struggles with Flutter Mane and Pokemon that can pivot like Rillaboom and Incineroar, as it can't trap them and does minimal damage with Foul Play. The aforementioned Koraidon can remove all of these checks reliably.

Trapper.description:
• Gothitelle's access to Shadow Tag and Taunt gives it a unique niche in the National Dex Ubers landscape. It lets Gothitelle trap common walls, such as defensive Ho-Oh and Coil Zygarde, forcing them to use Struggle, and it can deny setup from certain sweepers such as Ultra Necrozma. The ability for it to trap many key defensive Pokemon lets it aid offensive threats such as Zacian-C, Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy, and Mega Salamence and lets them forgo coverage for stronger move options. While Gothitelle needs a lot of support from allies, since it cannot trap most offensive Pokemon, its unique toolkit gives it a useful niche on specific bulky offense and balance structures

  • Taunt stops attempts to status, such as Ho-Oh and Primal Groudon's Toxic, from cutting into Gothitelle's longevity. It also blocks phazing attempts such as Primal Groudon's Roar and Ho-Oh's Whirlwind, and it denies attempts to recover health, like Zygarde's Rest.

  • Rest lets Gothitelle stay healthy throughout the trap, decreasing the reliance on Leftovers recovery. It also lets Gothitelle recover from status conditions, like Sacred Fire burns from Ho-Oh and Primal Groudon's Toxic.

  • Charm is Gothitelle's most reliable way to decrease the damage dealt by foes, since most of the Pokemon Gothitelle aims to trap, like Ho-Oh, Zygarde, and Ultra Necrozma, are primarily physical attackers.

  • Cosmic Power is a source of extra physical bulk, boosting Gothitelle's Defense after dropping the foe's attack to -6, and, when fully boosted up, Gothitelle can outheal the foe's damage with Leftovers. Cosmic Power also gives Gothitelle a boost to Special Defense, which can come in handy when trapping defensive Eternatus and Primal Groudon. After forcing a foe to Struggle, very few Pokemon can reliably break through a fully set-up Gothitelle, meaning it can trap foes it normally can't, such as Mega Salamence and Zacian-C.

  • Substitute gives Gothitelle a temporary immunity to the phazing effect of Dragon Tail from Zygarde and Primal Groudon and various status conditions, such as Toxic and Sacred Fire burns from Ho-Oh and Salt Cure from Garganacl. It also blocks Overheat from Primal Groudon and forces it to drop its Special Attack without Gothitelle taking the full-power Overheat. It also keeps Gothitelle safe from critical hits that can deal too much damage for it to comfortably tank. Substitute does have the downside of having less PP than Cosmic Power, which can give Gothitelle trouble when trapping multiple targets in certain matchups, such as against stall or when facing both Rock Tomb Primal Groudon and Brave Bird Ho-Oh, and when forced to run the faster EV spread, since otherwise, it can't outspeed Primal Groudon and block its Overheat.

  • The first EV spread is fully focused on Defense to grant Gothitelle the most consistency when trapping the mainly physical foes, like Zygarde, Ho-Oh, and Ultra Necrozma, giving it an easier time when switching in. The second EV spread invests in enough Speed to outspeed base 90s, like Primal Groudon, Ho-Oh and Zygarde-C. This lets Gothitelle use Charm to lower their Attack before they can use an offensive move, or Gothitelle can use Taunt to block an attempt to status. An alternative set with Choice Scarf, Trick, and enough speed to outpace Yveltal can also be used to bait and trap Yveltal and offensive Eternatus and set up on them with Calm Mind and deal a ton of damage with a boosted Stored Power. This set can struggle when trapping other foes, however, as many Pokemon such as the Calm Mind Arceus formes and Primal Groudon cannot be tricked. It also sacrifices the good matchup it has against Pokemon it usually traps, such as Ho-Oh and Zygarde, as Gothitelle cannot afford to run Charm on Trick variants.

  • Tera Ghost grants Gothitelle an incredible matchup against stall, letting it trap common stall Pokemon Chansey, which only runs Seismic Toss as a damaging move. With the immunity to Seismic Toss, Gothitelle can fully trap Chansey. This, alongside the ability to trap Dondozo and Ho-Oh, means Gothitelle allows both physical and special setup sweepers to break through the stall matchup more easily. It also grants a nice bonus benefit in letting Gothitelle escape trapper Zygarde's Thousand Waves after draining all the PP of its offensive moves in case Gothitelle's trapping is needed at another point in the game. Tera Water gives Gothitelle a resistance to Fire and Steel, letting it trap Overheat Primal Groudon, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, and defensive Ho-Oh with higher consistency. It also lets Gothitelle trap Choice-locked Pokemon such as Chien-Pao, Calyrex-I, and Melmetal. Tera Fairy gives Gothitelle an immunity to Dragon Tail phazing from Coil Zygarde, letting it trap it. It also lets Gothitelle trap Chien-Pao locked into Crunch and Choice Scarf Yveltal.

  • Taunt should be used first when facing foes that can give Gothitelle a status condition or phaze it, like defensive Ho-Oh. Charm should be used first when facing a foe that has a high immediate damage output, such as Primal Groudon, or when facing a foe that can boost up, such as Coil Zygarde or Dragon Dance Ultra Necrozma, immediately decreasing their damage output before using Taunt on them to prevent further setup. Charm should also be used when facing a Pokemon that only has offensive moves, such as a Choice item foe like Calyrex-I. If using Rest is needed, using Taunt the turn before Rest is important, as it ensures Gothitelle grants the foe as few turns as possible, being able to use Taunt again right after waking up and only giving one free turn, and when facing a Whirlwind Ho-Oh, this prevents phazing completely.

  • Scouting the moveset of the foe is important when using Gothitelle, since almost all foes that Gothitelle aims to trap have sets that can break through it. Dragon Dance Zygarde has Substitute, which means it doesn't fear Gothitelle's Charm. Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh can also run offensive sets, and Gothitelle does not have the bulk to take their hits comfortably; in Primal Groudon's case, it can OHKO Gothitelle outright with a Heat Crash from its Double Dance set. Rare coverage options can also take Gothitelle by surprise and KO it. Dragon Dance Ultra Necrozma can run Outrage or X-Scissor, which OHKO Gothitelle at +1 after Stealth Rock. Z-Moves also need to be accounted for, as at +1, Arceus-Ground and Necrozma-DM can OHKO Gothitelle with their respective Z-Moves, Tectonic Rage and Searing Sunraze Smash.

  • Playing around critical-hit ranges is crucial when using Gothitelle, as since the PP stall can take a long time, it is likely Gothitelle will take a critical hit at least once. Keeping it at high HP with Rest or consistently maintaining a Substitute, even when the foe is dealing little damage, means Gothitelle has to worry less about fainting to a random critical hit, further boosting its consistency. Foes with a faster Taunt, like Yveltal and Arceus formes, can completely shut down Gothitelle, since it only runs status moves. A Substitute from an opposing Kyurem-B or Zekrom can also block Charm, but Taunt still bypasses their Substitute and can still block their attempts to use a boosting move.

  • Gothitelle pairs incredibly well with strong offensive threats that can take advantage of its ability to trap common defensive checks and counters. Zacian-C and Mega Salamence appreciate Gothitelle trapping Coil Zygarde, defensive Primal Groudon, and Dondozo; Zacian-C also benefits from it trapping Ho-Oh. Calm Mind Arceus formes value Gothitelle trapping Ho-Oh, and Eternatus values it trapping defensive Primal Groudon and both appreciate it trapping Chansey. Gothitelle often only needs to take out one or two of these foes to enable a sweep from one of its allies. These offensive allies can in turn handle the matchups Gothitelle struggles in, like the hyper offense matchup. Zacian-C can reliably come in on Calm Mind Arceus-Dark and -Fairy that counter Gothitelle with a faster Taunt, Mega Salamence can boost its Speed and then punch holes through a usually defensively weak hyper offense team and provides utility with Intimidate, and Calm Mind Arceus formes can aid Gothitelle versus Meteor Beam Eternatus and Chi-Yu. Gothitelle doesn't even need to fully take out one of its foes, as fainting after using Charm once or twice can mean a free turn of setup for an ally to turn into a sweep. For example, at -2, a defensive Primal Groudon deals no meaningful damage to Calm Mind Arceus formes, which means Arceus can get a free Calm Mind off as Primal Groudon is forced out.

  • Preparing for hyper offense is very important, as aside from countering Dragon Dance Ultra Necrozma, Gothitelle is almost useless, since many common hyper offense Pokemon, like Zacian-C and Double Dance Primal Groudon, have too much immediate damage output for Gothitelle to be able to trap or switch into them. Pairing Gothitelle with allies that have a good matchup against hyper offense, like Ditto, Coil Zygarde, and Choice Scarf Yveltal, can help in this matchup. Ditto also has the added bonus of easily being able to scout sets. In turn, Gothitelle helps Coil Zygarde and Choice Scarf Yveltal in the stall matchup.

  • Toxic and Toxic Spikes support from allies like offensive Ho-Oh and Eternatus, respectively, allows Gothitelle to speed up the trapping process, risking less critical hits versus foes like Primal Groudon and saving crucial PP in the stall matchup, since Taunt has limited PP. A badly poisoned foe also means that Gothitelle can trap foes it normally can't, such as support non-Taunt Arceus-Dark, which usually deals too much damage for Gothitelle to reliably trap without fainting, or Dragon Dance Zygarde when running Tera Fairy. Offensive Ho-Oh also has a good matchup against Calm Mind Arceus formes, since Ho-Oh is not reliant on status moves to deal with them. Choice Scarf Yveltal the fastest Defogger in the tier, and it is the most reliable way to clear Sticky Web from the field. This enables Zacian-C and other setup allies to break through hyper offense teams.

Choice Item.description:
• Shadow Tag Gothitelle can trap most defensive Pokemon, paving the way for its teammates to sweep.
  • Trick facilitates trapping defensive walls like Ting-Lu and Great Tusk by locking them into an unfavorable move. Psychic targets Great Tusk and Toxapex, while Psyshock helps Gothitelle trap Clodsire better. Thunderbolt allows Gothitelle to trap Corviknight if it's not running U-turn or has a Choice item. Grass Knot KOes Great Tusk, Dondozo and hits Ting-Lu hard. Taunt is used to limit phazing attempts and Choice locked status moves, forcing the trapped Pokemon to use Struggle.
  • Rest allows Gothitelle to more effectively PP stall foes and remain healthy.
  • Choice Specs Gothitelle plays a more offensive role, aiming to rack up KOs. On the other hand, Choice Scarf variants are more likely to use Trick to beat opposing walls.
  • 32 HP and 4 Defense EVs allow Gothitelle to avoid being 2HKOed and 3HKOed from Ting-Lu's and Clodsire's Earthquake, respectively. 220 Speed EVs allow Choice Specs variants to outspeed defensive Great Tusk and Annihilape and Choice Scarf variants to outspeed offensive Great Tusk.
  • Gothitelle usually uses its Tera type to trap and beat Choice locked foes it otherwise would not trap; Tera Fairy beats Miraidon and Koraidon Choice locked into Dragon-type moves, Tera Water tanks Koraidon's Flare Blitz and Iron Bundle's Ice Beam, and Tera Flying avoids Earthquake from Ting-Lu and Great Tusk.
  • Gothitelle's favorite partners are powerful sweepers and cleaners such as Miraidon, Koraidon, Flutter Mane, Iron Bundle, Kingambit, and Chien-Pao, all of which appreciate Gothitelle removing one or more of their checks.

Delay Goth (Trapper).description:
• This Gothitelle set aims to trap and PP stall weak walls so that its offensive teammates can take over mid- to late-game. This Gothitelle set can come in on weak walls like Clodsire, Ting-Lu, Alomomola, and defensive Great Tusk and beat them by PP stalling them.
  • Charm and Calm Mind are use to boost Gothitelle's survivability while PP stalling its foe.
  • Taunt is used to stop phazing attempts and make the trapped Pokemon use their attacking PP, thus depleting their PP faster. Stored Power is an alternative for teams that benefit from having more wallbreaking potential or that have a good matchup against the Dark-types of the tier like Chien-Pao and Kingambit.
  • The 24 Speed EVs allow Gothitelle to be faster than uninvested Corviknight, trapping it if it's not running U-turn. The Defense investment is used to tank hits well for PP stalling purposes, with attacks such as Ting-Lu's Earthquake being only a 4HKO.
  • Tera Fairy is used for its solid defensive typing and ability to trap Choice-locked Dragon-types like Miraidon and Koraidon, Tera Water is an option for its overall great defensive typing, granting resistances to Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash, Koraidon's Flare Blitz, and Iron Bundle's Hydro Pump or Ice Beam. Lastly, Tera Ground is used to allow Gothitelle to trap Miraidon locked into an Electric move or defeat Double Dance sets one-on-one.
  • Gothitelle's favorite partners are powerful sweepers and cleaners, especially setup sweepers that take advantage of defensive Pokemon having their PP drained to set up easily and without risk. Common examples include Swords Dance Koraidon, Swords Dance Chien-Pao, Double Dance Miraidon, and Calm Mind Flutter Mane.

nfe.overview: Duosion is a unique special wall, that has access to Future Sight and an excellent Special Attack, making it the best Future Sight user. Thanks to its ability Regenerator and decent bulk, Duosion checks specially offensive Pokemon such as Girafarig and Ivysaur while offering many opportunities for its teammates to break through defensive backbones with the help of Future Sight. Duosion also has access to Magic Guard, which is useful in a metagame where entry hazards are dominant, and can use setup moves like Calm Mind and Acid Armor, letting it fulfill the role of a setup sweeper.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Trick can be used if all of your Pokemon dislike losing their items, thus, enabling Duosion to act as a Knock Off absorber against weak Pokemon such as Tinkatuff and Thief users like Dunsparce and Fletchinder. Duosion can run Magic Guard in teams that have no way of dealing with entry hazards, but it is generally outclassed by Regenerator otherwise.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Dark-types like Scraggy and Krokorok are completely immune to Duosion's STAB moves and do not fear being paralyzed either. Stunky also threatens Duosion, but it dislikes being paralyzed.

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Hisuian Sliggoo and Tinkatuff can take on Future Sight with ease, preventing Duosion from making progress. Hisuian Sliggoo can use Acid Spray to outpace setup Duosion variants and Tinkatuff can use Encore to discourage Duosion from setting up.

Physically Offensive Pokemon: Thwackey, Raboot, and Choice Band Piloswine all force out Duosion by threatening it with powerful STAB moves.

Psychic-types: Psychic-types like Hattrem and Girafarig with Shadow Ball check Duosion, as they do not fear Future Sight or Night Shade. Girafarig, especially, can use Duosion as a setup opportunity if it runs Substitute + Nasty Plot and Duosion is not running Encore.

Knock Off: Knock Off users such as Servine and Ivysaur significantly hinder Duosion, as Eviolite is needed for it to effectively wall foes and to fire Future Sight without needing to waste a turn healing.

Drakloak: Despite Duosion being a special wall, it fears Drakloak's Ghost STAB moves.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Duosion is used as a special wall thanks to its decent bulk and Eviolite, checking specially offensive Pokemon such as Girafarig, Ivysaur, and Hisuian Sliggoo. Duosion's most unique tool is Future Sight; in combination with its excellent Special Attack, Duosion can break through defensive cores. For immediate damage, Duosion runs Psychic to threaten Pokemon like Monferno and Glimmet. Duosion can also use Night Shade to hit Steel- and Dark-types like Tinkatuff and Krokorok consistently. Duosion has access to utility moves like Thunder Wave to hinder offensive Pokemon that would want to aggressively come in on it such as Raboot and Thwackey. Encore is a secondary option to not let Pokemon such as Fraxure and Substitute + Nasty Plot Girafarig set up on Duosion. Regenerator is the preferred ability due to allowing Duosion to not need to waste a turn healing with Recover when coming on passive Pokemon such as Koffing and Quaxwell.

Duosion fits best in balance teams that have a good offensive synergy with it. Duosion's offensive teammates like the help of Future Sight to break through defensive backbones with ease, especially Pokemon that cannot hit Poison-types such as Monferno, Scraggy, and Thwackey. In return, Monferno checks Thwackey and Scraggy, which are two Pokemon that threaten Duosion. Additionally, Pokemon with Knock Off such as the aforementioned Monferno, Scraggy, Thwackey, Pignite, and Krokorok, pair well with Duosion since they can remove the foe's Eviolite to let Future Sight hit them for even more damage. Pokemon such as Fletchinder and Raboot that can pivot on Pokemon like Quaxwell, Koffing, and Glimmet are appreciated, as it gives an opportunity for Duosion to use Future Sight. Physically defensive Pokemon like Koffing and Quaxwell appreciate Duosion's ability to wall specially offensive Pokemon like Girafarig and Hisuian Sliggoo. Despite being a special wall, Duosion cannot deal with Drakloak, so it appreciates other Pokemon like Scraggy and Dunsparce beating it. Additionally, Pokemon that can absorb Knock Off like Dunsparce, Tinkatuff, and Koffing cover Duosion's weakness to it. Pokemon with U-turn can quickly overwhelm Duosion, so Pokemon like Koffing and Mareanie that can take U-turn and check offensive pivots are appreciated, as well as Fletchinder and Seadra, which punish U-turn thanks to their abilities Flame Body and Poison Point, respectively. Duosion cannot hit Dark-types if not running Night Shade, so Pokemon that can check Scraggy like Monferno, Fletchinder, Clefairy, and Pignite, or Pokemon that take on Krokorok like Dunsparce, Piloswine, and Thwackey are appreciated. Furthermore, Duosion struggles to damage Steel-types if not running Night Shade, so using Ground-types like Krokorok and Piloswine or Fighting-types like Monferno and Pignite to prevent them from absorbing the upcoming Future Sight makes for a good combination. In the same vein, Mareanie can lure Steel-types like Tinkatuff and all-out attacker Hisuian Sliggoo and take them down slowly with Infestation. Pokemon with access to Roar such as Quilladin and Piloswine pair well with Duosion's Future Sight, having a chance of forcing in Pokemon that do not want to take a hit from Future Sight. In case Duosion is not running Encore, Pokemon that deal with Girafarig's Substitute are desirable, such as Scraggy and Hisuian Sliggoo.

Double Dance.description:
Double Dance Duosion is a lethal wincon that can very quickly get out of hand, especially once it accumulates its boosts against ill-prepared teams. Magic Guard grants Duosion immunity to indirect forms of damage such as poison and entry hazards, while its natural bulk enables it to take hits from and set up on all but the strongest Pokemon in the tier and Dark-types. Acid Armor and Calm Mind rapidly boost Duosion's defensive stats, making it nearly impossible to KO without a critical hit. At the same time, they increase Duosion's Special Attack and the Base Power of Stored Power. Alternatively, Psyshock is a strong STAB move that is not reliant on stat boosts to deal significant damage. Finally, Recover allows Duosion to continue setting up on attacks that it shrugs off more easily with each boost. With 252 Defense EVs and a Bold nature, Duosion can take multiple Knock Offs from the likes of Monferno, Thwackey, and Pignite while boosting its Defense with Acid Armor to more than offset the loss of its Eviolite.

Double Dance Duosion's main weakness is its complete inability to hit Dark-type foes like Krokorok and Scraggy. It therefore needs teammates that can consistently switch into and deal with these Pokemon such as Clefairy and Seadra. It also struggles against the two main Steel-types in the tier. Hisuian Sliggoo can beat this set with Acid Spray, while Tinkatuff can stop it with Encore. Strong physical attackers that can hit these Pokemon super effectively, like Pignite, Piloswine, and Monferno, therefore make great teammates. Alternatively, specific lures for Dark- and Steel-type Pokemon can punch important holes in opposing team structures for Duosion to take advantage of. These include Fire Punch Alolan Grimer for Tinkatuff, Drain Punch or Hammer Arm Thwackey for Hisuian Sliggoo, and Play Rough Tinkatuff for Krokorok. In addition to Tinkatuff, other Encore users like Quaxwell and Clefairy pose similar threats to Double Dance Duosion, as do Taunt users like Servine, Fletchinder, and Hakamo-o. Finally, status spreaders help Duosion by either giving it free setup opportunities with paralysis or putting opposing Pokemon on a timer with poison.
