• Thanks to its great physical bulk, utility, and excellent typing, Alomomola fills valuable niches on bulkier balance teams. Alomomola is useful as a defensive pivot that can shrug off damage thanks to Regenerator, as a status spreader, and as a Wish passer that increases the longevity of its teammates.
  • Toxic allows Alomomola to cripple the longevity of Ho-Oh, Primal Groudon, and support Arceus formes lacking Refresh. Toxic is especially useful against Primal Groudon and Zygarde, as it keeps Alomomola from being easily set up on while forcing Zygarde to waste Rest PP.
  • Wish allows Alomomola to increase its longevity as well as the longevity of its teammates by providing recovery for allies such as Primal Groudon, Primal Kyogre, Giratina-O, and Specially Offensive Yveltal that have no reliable recovery options. A slow Flip Turn allows Alomomola to safely pass a Wish to the aforementioned Pokemon. Increased longevity allows these teammates to check Zacian-C, Primal Groudon, Arceus, and Marshadow with more efficiency during the game.
  • Protect allows Alomomola to more easily receive a Wish from itself, scout Choice item sets from Marshadow, Yveltal, and Eternatus, and maximize Toxic damage on the foe.
  • Heavy-Duty Boots allows Alomomola to freely pivot without worrying about entry hazards.
  • The first EV spread maximizes Alomomola's mixed bulk, allowing it to shrug off hits from support Arceus formes and Eternatus. The second EV spread maximizes Alomomola's physical bulk, allowing it to survive a +3 Wild Charge from Zacian-C and two uses of Glacial Lance from Choice Band Calyrex-I. Having 0 Speed IVs allows Alomomola to perform a slow Flip Turn against Chansey and Calyrex-I.
  • Tera Dark allows Alomomola to absorb powerful Psychic-type attacks such as Light that Burns the Sky from Ultra Necrozma and Psycho Boost from Deoxys-A. Tera Dark also makes Alomomola one of the few walls capable of handling Deoxys-A thanks to Alomomola's low weight lessening the power of Low Kick. After switching in, Alomomola can immediately threaten to OHKO Deoxys-A with Flip Turn after Stealth Rock and a turn of Life Orb damage.
  • Tera Poison prevents Alomomola from becoming poisoned, allowing it to serve as a switch-in to Toxic Ho-Oh and utility Arceus formes. Tera Poison also allows Alomomola to absorb Toxic Spikes from Eternatus to keep teammates such as Primal Groudon, Primal Kyogre, and support Arceus formes status-free, although switching into Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground becomes harder.
  • Alomomola is able to swap into any unboosted physical attack besides Bolt Strike from Zekrom throughout the game consistently, since it can use Regenerator to heal itself back up. It can swap in on Mega Salamence or Arceus-Ground and pivot with Flip Turn to safely bring in an answer such as Arceus-Fairy or Arceus-Dark.
  • Thanks to Alomomola's Wish support, teammates without reliable recovery such as Primal Groudon and Giratina-O can switch into Primal Kyogre and Arceus more aggressively throughout the game without worrying about slowly being chipped down.
  • Wallbreaker Primal Kyogre makes it near impossible for Alomomola to safely pass a Wish, so teammates such as Ferrothorn and Primal Groudon are helpful.
  • Alomomola will often get overwhelmed by physical attackers such as Zacian-C, Mega Salamence, and Arceus, so teammates such as Primal Groudon and Arceus-Dark help ease Alomomola's workload.
  • Alomomola provides excellent slow pivoting, so Pokemon that capitalize on a free switch such as Deoxys-A, Choice Band Marshadow, Choice Band Chien-Pao, and Meteor Beam Eternatus make excellent teammates.

Defensive.description:
Alomomola's massive HP stat allows it to be an effective user of Wish to support its ability to give teammates safe entry through Flip Turn. It can make use of Toxic to wear down opposing Pokemon that switch in on it and Pokemon that try setting up on it such as Terapagos, Ogerpon-W, and Great Tusk. Alomomola also appreciates Protect as a way to ensure it is able to use Wish and regain its own HP safely, scout opposing Pokemon's moves, notably Choice-locked attackers such as Tapu Lele as well as being able to build up Toxic damage on foes like Garchomp and Terapagos. Heavy-Duty Boots are another great tool for Alomomola, allowing it to safely switch into hazards to gain back health safely with Regenerator and use Wish to support teammates. The EV spread and Relaxed nature used allows Alomomola to comfortably sponge up hits from strong physical attackers such as Kingambit, Urshifu-R, and Great Tusk, while a Sassy nature allows it to have a more comfortable matchup into Mega Diancie and Terapagos. Alomomola makes use of 8 HP EVs to remain at an odd number HP stat so it can switch into hazards more optimally if its Heavy-Duty Boots are removed.

Slower Pokemon that lack reliable recovery, like Ursaluna, Kingambit, and Melmetal, appreciate Alomomola's ability to bring them in safely and recover their HP with Wish against bulky Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Ferrothorn. Frail Pokemon such Iron Valiant also appreciate Alomomola's ability to safely get them on the field with Flip Turn. Alomomola's vulnerability to Grass- and Electric-type Pokemon like Rillaboom, Tapu Koko, and Kartana make Raging Bolt and Ferrothorn excellent partners due to their ability to easily shrug them off and regain whatever health is lost through Alomomola's ability to safely Wish pass into these Pokemon.

Assault Vest.description:
With an Assault Vest, Alomomola's Special Defense is bolstered, which allows it to act as a powerful defensive pivot. Its defensive capabilities are further improved by Regenerator, enabling it to pivot reliably. Alomomola provides valuable utility for its team in Knock Off, as it can remove the Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon like Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Zapdos so its teammates to break more easily. Mirror Coat deals huge damage and even OHKOes unsuspecting special attackers such as Mega Charizard Y, Tapu Koko, and Tapu Lele that switch in because they can break past non-Assault Vest Alomomola. Flip Turn lets Alomomola safely bring in powerful attackers like Mega Diancie, Tapu Lele, and Urshifu-R. Scald can be used to status opposing Pokemon with burn, while Liquidation is an alternative STAB move that can prevent foes such as Volcarona from turning Alomomola into setup fodder.

Alomomola is very valuable on offense and balance teams due to its ability to check a wide variety of Pokemon and bring in its team's attackers via Flip Turn. Alomomola can switch into powerful physical attackers such as Urshifu-R, non-Choice Band Zamazenta, and Hisuian Samurott. Despite this, Alomomola cannot wall some strong physical attackers like Ogerpon-W and Choice Band Zamazenta; therefore, Pokemon that can deal with these foes like Pecharunt and Landorus-T to be valuable partners. In return, Alomomola can easily take on Pokemon they can’t handle like Tapu Lele. Alomomola can take powerful Water-type attacks from Urshifu-R, Hisuian Samurott, and Tapu Fini. It is also able to check powerful special attackers like Gholdengo, Tapu Lele, and Mega Diancie and use Mirror Coat to OHKO them. However, this becomes more difficult to pull off once Alomomola's Assault Vest set is revealed, as Mirror Coat is easy to predict; this makes hiding its set important for picking up OHKOs on unsuspecting special attackers. Alomomola can also struggle with special attacking Electric-types such as Raging Bolt and Tapu Koko, so it appreciates Ground-types like Ting-Lu and specially defensive Gliscor. In return, Alomomola can take powerful Water-type attacks from Urshifu-R, Hisuian Samurott, and Tapu Fini. Due to Alomomola’s reliance on its item to check special attackers, it greatly dislikes having it removed; therefore, Knock Off absorbers like Gliscor, Mega Scizor, and Mega Venusaur make great partners, and in return, Alomomola can take the Fire-type attacks the latter two dislike and the Water-type attacks Gliscor hates. Alomomola’s defensive capabilities can also be crippled by entry hazards, which leads to hazard removers like Great Tusk, Terapagos, and Landorus-T being valuable. Pokemon with Magic Bounce like Mega Diancie and Hatterene can also help keep hazards off Alomomola's side of the field. Powerful attackers like Zamazenta, Mega Diancie, and Ogerpon-W greatly enjoy Alomomola on their team, as it can safely bring them in on offensive threats like Tapu Lele, Terapagos, and Hisuian Samurott.

Defensive.description:
Alomomola's colossal HP, solid Defense, and incredible ability allow it to act as a great pivot option for bulkier Water teams. The combination of Wish and Flip Turn allows Alomomola's teammates to safely switch in and restore a substantial amount of HP. Scald is Alomomola's best way of dealing damage, as well as having the added benefit of being able to burn opposing Pokemon such as Excadrill and and Okidogi. Protect allows Alomomola to stall out a turn and recover its own HP using Wish. Alternatively, Alomomola can utilize its low Special Defense stat to bait strong special attackers, such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Latios, into hitting it with a special attack, then turn the tables via Mirror Coat.

Alomomola is almost exclusively seen on stall teams due to its passivity. Teammates without reliable recovery, such as Dondozo and Swampert, are excellent partners for it. Dondozo can switch into dangerous setup sweepers, such as Azumarill and Bisharp that Alomomola struggles in the face of. Meanwhile, Swampert is immune to Electric-type attacks, which threaten Alomomola, and can utilize Flip Turn to help get Alomomola in for safe Wishes. Special walls such as Empoleon, Swampert, and Toxapex are able to cover Alomomola's low Special Defense stat by switching into Pokemon like Dragapult and Gholdengo. Additionally, Toxapex and Alomomola form an incredibly tough-to-break Regenerator core that breaks down opposing teams via poison and burn, all while restoring HP naturally. Pokemon that can provide hazard support such as Gastrodon, Quagsire, and Hisuian Samurott are great teammates for Alomomola, as they form a hazard-stacking core and are capable of wearing down foes across the course of long games. Greninja and Urshifu-R can beat Pokemon such as Ogerpon-H and Landorus, both of which massively threaten slower-paced Water teams. Additionally, Greninja and Urshifu-R are great recipients of Alomomola's Wish passing, which allows them to remain healthy and continue to provide offensive pressure for their team.

Wish Pass.description:
• With Wish and a slow Flip Turn, Alomomola has a strong combination for providing team healing.

  • Protect: Alomomola can use Wish and Protect to give itself reliable self-recovery, and this combination makes Alomomola great at stalling out turns against weather, Terrains, and Trick Room.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet is weak on Alomomola but still excellent at picking off severely weakened threats such as Focus Sash Chien-Pao.

  • Play Rough: Play Rough deals sizable damage to Koraidon without Terastallization but is otherwise fairly situational.

Other Options

  • Scald: Scald's burn chance can punish physical attackers like Dragonite and Chien-Pao for trying to set up on it, but it's rather inconsistent.

  • Skill Swap: Skill Swap is a unique way to prevent Gliscor that lack Taunt from setting up on Alomomola and its team. It can also be used on Ogerpon-W's Water Absorb to make Flip Turn possible against it.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low / Medium: Physically bulky Alomomola already has good typing against the threats it wants to wall, but there are times when Terastallization is needed to augment its role.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy's Fighting-type resistance can be used to buy more time against Koraidon and Urshifu-R as well as just outright walling powerful Dragon-type moves like Outrage and Scale Shot.

  • Poison: Tera Poison improves the Flutter Mane matchup and provides important support for removing Toxic Spikes.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet is fantastic for chipping the likes of Koraidon and Dragonite just by switching into their contact moves. Paired with Alomomola's recovery support, it has great potential to stack this damage up over time.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers synergizes well with Protect, and the extra passive recovery can give Alomomola greater freedom to pass Wish to its teammates.

EV Spreads

  • 116 HP / 252 Def / 140 SpD with Relaxed: The physical bulk on this EV spread is tuned for Scale Shot from Jolly Koraidon, guaranteeing Alomomola can survive up to nine individual hits before recovery. With Leftovers and Protect, it almost always guarantees that Alomomola can live two unboosted Moonblasts from Timid Flutter Mane.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD with Relaxed: A simple spread that tops out physical bulk, but the main benefit is that maximizing Alomomola's HP bumps the recovery teammates will receive from Wish.

  • 4 HP / 252 Def / 252 SpD with Relaxed: While it sacrifices some physical bulk, the higher special bulk investment helps Alomomola to almost always avoid the 2HKO from Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast, all without needing Leftovers.

Assault Vest Pivot.description:
• Flip Turn and Regenerator combine to make Alomomola one of the hardest pivots to efficiently take out.

  • Mirror Coat: Alomomola makes excellent use of Mirror Coat with its high base HP, retaliating comfortably against top special attackers like Ursaluna-B and Raging Bolt.

  • Scald: Scald's moderate burn chance makes Alomomola even more threatening to physical attackers like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-R.

  • Aqua Jet: Uninvested Aqua Jet may not do much, but it's still useful for picking off common Focus Sash users and Sturdy Archaludon.

  • Play Rough: Play Rough lets Alomomola deal more direct damage to the likes of Chien-Pao and Urshifu-R, especially when paired with Tera Fairy.

  • Icy Wind: Icy Wind's speed control can be useful for wallbreakers like Choice Band Chien-Pao and Choice Specs Chi-Yu. Furthermore, targets like defensive Dragonite are still faster than Alomomola after a single Speed drop, allowing it to maintain its safe pivoting support.

Other Options

  • Liquidiation: Liquidation helps Alomomola deal decent overall damage if forced into a situation where it has to play offensively such as against Calm Mind Flutter Mane.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low / Medium: Alomomola is extremely difficult to OHKO, and with Terastallization, it can thwart its counters and live even longer! Do note though that losing its original typing can make it much more vulnerable to wallbreakers like Tera Water Urshifu-R.

  • Poison: Tera Poison grants pivotal Fairy and Grass resistances against Flutter Mane, Rillaboom, and the Ogerpon formes. The immunity to Toxic and Toxic Spikes is also a big help.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy helps against Dark- and Fighting-type attacks from Chien-Pao and the Urshifu formes and can be used alongside Play Rough to give Alomomola more kick against these targets.

EV Spreads

  • 52 HP / 212 Def / 244 SpD with Relaxed: This EV spread gives Alomomola a balanced defensive profile. The Special Defense investment avoids the OHKO from Modest Choice Specs Chi-Yu's Overheat even if Alomomola is Terastallized.

  • 188 HP / 76 Def / 244 SpD with Relaxed: This spread contributes extra to surviving special attacks; in particular it has an approxiately 90% chance to avoid the 2HKO from Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast as well as having about a 75% chance to avoid the 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Chi-Yu's Dark Pulse. Enough Defense investment is maintained so that Jolly Chien-Pao's Tera Blast Electric only OHKOes Alomomola on the highest damage roll.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Rocky Helmet is an alternative item choice on teams with entry hazard control like Defog Mandibuzz. Notably, the chip damage compounded by Brave Bird's recoil makes Alomomola have a much better time against Ho-Oh. Leftovers prevents a 2HKO from Adamant Koraidon's Outrage or five-hit Scale Shot and makes use of Protect to get slightly more recovery. Tera Rock lets Alomomola wall Tera Flying Ho-Oh conveniently while adding an Extreme Speed resistance. However, such teams are limited, and Tera Rock leaves Alomomola weak to Koraidon's Low Kick and Arceus-Ground's Earthquake, so the aforementioned options are rarely used. Tickle is useful against Tera Fire users like Bulk Up Arceus, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground lacking Taunt. Furthermore, the Defense drop comes in handy for Alomomola's teammates like Ditto to revenge kill threats such as Swords Dance Arceus. Play Nice can be used in place of Tickle, as it bypasses Substitute, while Chilling Water is effective against Taunt users like Arceus-Ground and Arceus. However, using these moves comes at the expense of being unable to threaten Koraidon and makes Alomomola need additional support from teammates to deal with Swords Dance Koraidon.

Checks and Counters

Special Wallbreakers: Due to Alomomola's mediocre Special Defense, it is easily threatened by common special wallbreakers like Calyrex-S, Miraidon, and Kyogre, all of which are capable of OHKOing it and taking advantage of its passivity to set up.

Tera Fire Users: Tera Fire users like Swords Dance Koraidon, Bulk Up Arceus, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM safely set up on Alomomola without worrying about Scald burns after Terastallization.

Substitute Users: Tera Steel Koraidon and Zacian-C often carry Substitute, which lets them set up freely. Furthermore, they can't be revenge killed by Ditto.

Knock Off Users: Knock Off users like Gliscor and Necrozma-DM greatly limit Alomomola's entry, as losing Heavy-Duty Boots means it can no longer pivot without being chipped by entry hazards like Spikes and Toxic Spikes.

Toxic Users: Toxic users like Eternatus, Clodsire, and Gliscor can cripple Alomomola, severely affecting its longevity.

WishPass.description:
Thanks to its great defensive capabilities enhanced by Regenerator and access to utility moves like Wish and Flip Turn, Alomomola solidifies itself as a premier Wish passer and a decent physical wall on stall and semi-stall teams. Alomomola's high physical bulk lets it take hits from the strongest of physical attackers in the metagame like Koraidon, Arceus, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, Ho-Oh, and Calyrex-I. Wish + Flip Turn is Alomomola's defining trait, making it function as a Wish passer for walls without reliable recovery such as Ting-Lu and Alolan Muk and also bringing in frailer teammates like Calyrex-Shadow and Ditto safely. Protect scouts Choice item users like Choice Specs Kyogre and Choice Band Koraidon and ensures Alomomola can heal itself with Wish without any risk of getting KOed. Play Rough 2HKOes Koraidon, which could otherwise set up Swords Dance and, less frequently, Substitute. However, Koraidon can Terastallize into a Fire- or Steel-type and render Alomomola helpless. Scald alternatively wards off most physical attackers from the fear of a burn, bar Tera Fire users. Heavy-Duty Boots is vital for Alomomola to switch in repeatedly through the course of the game by making it unaffected by entry hazards, which would otherwise whittle down Alomomola slowly. Tera Fairy provides a crucial immunity to Koraidon's Outrage and Scale Shot, as well as a resistance to Close Combat. Additionally, Tera Fairy-boosted Play Rough OHKOes Koraidon after a Defense drop from Scale Shot or Close Combat. However, it comes with the cost of losing the resistance to Fire-type moves like Koraidon's Flare Blitz and Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire and gaining a weakness to Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade and Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike.

Alomomola best fits on stall and semi-stall teams that appreciate a blanket check for a plethora of physical attackers. As Alomomola's special bulk is subpar, it is vulnerable to strong special attackers like Calyrex-S, Miraidon, and Kyogre. Ting-Lu is a great partner that can handle Miraidon and Calyrex-S and benefits from Wish extending its longevity. It also sets Spikes, which helps to limit threatening switch-ins like Swords Dance Koraidon. Similarly, other special walls like Eternatus, Tera Grass Ho-Oh, and Blissey assist in checking Kyogre, Miraidon, and Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy. In return, Alomomola switches into dangerous physical attackers like Koraidon, Swords Dance Arceus, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, and Calyrex-Ice. However, wallbreakers like Choice Band and Life Orb + Swords Dance variants of Koraidon, Tera Flying Ho-Oh, and Swords Dance Zacian-C are capable of breaking past Alomomola without much difficulty. Thus, Unaware walls like Skeledirge that alleviate the pressure off Alomomola by checking Zacian-C and Koraidon are good teammates. Meanwhile, Alomomola can stall out the Koraidon's sun with Protect, giving Skeledirge an easier time. Garganacl checks Tera Flying Ho-Oh and is immune to Ho-Oh's Sacred Fire burns and Eternatus's Toxic thanks to Purifying Salt. Gliscor is valuable for absorbing Knock Off and status from opposing Gliscor, Eternatus, and Clodsire. It also checks Taunt Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, which can stop Alomomola from using Wish and set up using Tera Fire. Ditto and Encore Calyrex-S are fantastic teammates for revenge killing threats like Swords Dance Zacian-C and halting setup sweepers, respectively, thereby reducing the stress on Alomomola. Furthermore, Alomomola brings them in safely with Flip Turn and passes Wish.

Sticky Web.description: Galvantula carves out a niche in Ubers UU thanks to it being the fastest available Sticky Web setter, having solid offenses, and having the ability to threaten out common forms of entry hazard control like Great Tusk and Mandibuzz. Energy Ball gives Galvantula coverage against Ground-types like Great Tusk and Landorus, although Bug Buzz is an option to give it a secondary STAB option hit Pokemon like Mewtwo, Arceus-Dark, and Deoxys. Thunder Wave allows Galvantula to cripple Pokemon like Zacian, Kyurem-W, and Arceus-Poison after setting up Sticky Web. Although Galvantula will not often Terastallize, Tera Ghost allows it to block Rapid Spin from Great Tusk and Cyclizar. Focus Sash guarantees Galvantula will set up Sticky Web and potentially fire off an attack or paralyze something afterwards. Galvantula should be exclusively used as a Sticky Web lead for hyper offense teams. The most obvious partners for Galvantula are Pokemon that appreciate having their faster offensive counters slowed down, as well as Pokemon commonly revenge killed by faster threats. As a result, Pokemon like Choice Specs Kyurem-W, Mewtwo, and Landorus all make solid teammates. Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Dragapult and Taunt users like Arceus formes can prevent Rapid Spin and Defog and keep Sticky Web up. Counter leads like Taunt Arceus-Dark, Deoxys, and Hatterene can prevent Sticky Web being set up and give Galvantula issues, so Pokemon like Hatterene and Palafin that can deal with these threats are good to have as partners.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Electric

Volt Switch can be used instead of Energy Ball to provide a pivoting move after setting up Sticky Web, but the loss of Energy Ball means that Galvantula can't hit Ground-types, especially Great Tusk.

Entry Hazard Lead (Bug).description:
Sticky Web Galvantula is a decent lead on Bug teams due to its ability to set Sticky Web up, allowing teammates such as Volcarona and Scizor to sweep more easily. Thunder, combined with the accuracy boost from Compound Eyes, is Galvantula's strongest move, which hits Water-types such as Toxapex and deters Flying-type Defoggers such as Corviknight. Thunder Wave allows Galvantula to cripple faster threats such as Weavile and Flutter Mane. Energy Ball gives Galvantula coverage against Ground-types such as Quagsire and Great Tusk, Great Tusk in particular being another Pokemon that can remove Sticky Web. Volt Switch can be used instead of Energy Ball to provide a pivoting move after setting up Sticky Web, but the loss of Energy Ball means that Galvantula can't hit Ground-types, especially the aforementioned Great Tusk. Focus Sash gives Galvantula a guaranteed Sticky Web, attack, or chance to paralyze. The given EV spread with a Timid nature allows Galvantula to get up Sticky Web consistently while also maximizing its Special Attack in order to deal the most damage possible.

Pokemon that benefit from Galvantula's Sticky Web are ideal partners for it. The aforementioned Volcarona and Scizor both appreciate their threats being slowed down so they can set up with Quiver Dance and Swords Dance, respectively. Scizor is able to take out Hisuian Arcanine, Glimmora, and Galarian Weezing, while Volcarona outspeeds faster threats like Greninja and Iron Valiant under Sticky Web. Slither Wing and Lokix also appreciate Sticky Web, as it helps them wallbreak and revenge kill against normally faster threats, such as Ogerpon-H, Gholdengo, and Choice Specs Iron Moth. Choice Scarf Kleavor is a great teammate for Galvantula because it can deal with Fire-types such as Ogerpon-H and Moltres. Kleavor's Stone Axe also pairs nicely with Galvantula's Sticky Web, as more entry hazards further help the sweepers and wallbreakers on the team, while also breaking Ceruledge's Focus Sash, which is a huge problem for Bug teams. Forretress removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin, provides a strong physical wall on Bug teams, and is a slow pivot for Galvantula with Volt Switch to ensure its safe entry.

Sticky Web (Electric).description:
With its high base Speed, Galvantula is an excellent lead due to it being the only consistent Sticky Web setter on Electric teams. Thunder, combined with the accuracy boost from Compound Eyes, is Galvantula's strongest move, which hits Water-types such as Toxapex and deters Flying-type Defoggers such as Corviknight. Bug Buzz is used to hit Pokemon that resist Thunder like Hydreigon and Latios, while Thunder Wave allows Galvantula to cripple faster threats such as Weavile and Flutter Mane. Energy Ball gives Galvantula coverage against Ground-types such as Quagsire and Great Tusk, which is valuable, as Great Tusk can remove Sticky Web. Focus Sash gives Galvantula a guaranteed chance to set Sticky Web, attack, or paralyze the opponent.

Pokemon that can take advantage of Sticky Web are great teammates for Galvantula. Rotom-W and Zapdos both benefit from Sticky Web, as they can outspeed threats such as Iron Valiant and the Ogerpon formes at -1 while also providing a Ground immunity. Raging Bolt especially benefits from Sticky Web, as its underwhelming Speed tier holds it back, and it appreciates the Speed drop from Sticky Web so it can set up and wallbreak more easily. Sandy Shocks pairs well with Galvantula, forming an entry hazard-stacking core combining Sticky Web with its Stealth Rock and Spikes. Regieleki provides hazard removal for Electric teams with Rapid Spin and pivoting with Volt Switch so wallbreakers like the aforementioned Raging Bolt can come in repeatedly. Although Iron Hands doesn't really benefit from Sticky Web, it is still a great teammate due to its high bulk and can take out threats that wall Galvantula, such as Tyranitar, Hisuian Goodra, and Blissey. In return, Galvantula takes out Quagsire and Great Tusk for Iron Hands.

Sticky Web (Bug).description: Galvantula serves as an excellent Sticky Web lead, supporting its offensive team members with speed control. Thunder in conjunction with Compound Eyes gives Galvantula an offensive presence, takes on opposing hazard-setting leads, threatens paralysis, and dents Water- and Flying-types. Energy Ball threatens bulky Ground-types like Great Tusk, Hippowdon, Swampert, and Gastrodon. Hidden Power Ice deals with Flying- and Dragon-types like Gliscor, the Landorus formes, Garchomp, and Dragonite. Thunder Wave can be used over Hidden Power Ice to paralyze setup sweepers and fast threats that can't be effectively slowed down with Sticky Web, most notably Dragonite, Galarian Zapdos, Mega Aerodactyl, opposing Mega Pinsir, and Volcarona, without having to rely on Thunder to do so. This comes at the cost of losing coverage against Pokemon that resist both Thunder and Energy Ball, however. Sticky Web lowers the amount of Quiver Dance boosts needed for Volcarona to outspeed Regieleki, Unburden Sneasler, and Sand Rush Excadrill, making its setup more efficient. Sticky Web also allows choice Scarf users like Kleavor and Buzzwole to outspeed those Pokemon, limiting the amount of revenge killing options against them and improving their effectiveness against Fire- and Rock-types by taking care of Choice Scarf Blacephalon, Hisuian Arcanine, and Iron Boulder. Sticky Web gives Mega Pinsir more opportunities to use Return instead of Quick Attack to increase its damage output or Earthquake to KO Pokemon that would usually threaten it like Choice Scarf Nihilego and Hisuian Arcanine. Scizor can OHKO or force Diancie out before it can Mega Evolve to allow Galvantula to set up Sticky Web against Fairy- and Rock-teams.

Specially Defensive.description:
• Ferrothorn's stellar typing, high bulk, and rare access to Spikes grant it a unique position in the metagame as the cornerstone of hazard-stacking balance teams over Pokemon such as defensive Necrozma-DM. Ferrothorn serves as a sturdy roadblock to wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, which otherwise easily overwhelms most balance teams. Additionally, Ferrothorn checks Ground-types such as Arceus-Ground and Zygarde. However, Ferrothorn struggles against more offensive teams, as Pokemon such as Zacian-C and Mega Salamence are able to take advantage of Ferrothorn's passivity to use it as setup fodder.
  • Power Whip provides Ferrothorn the means to scare out Pokemon such as Primal Kyogre and Arceus-Ground. Wallbreaker Primal Kyogre is OHKOed after Stealth Rock, and defensive Arceus-Ground is 2HKOed after a single layer of Spikes. Ferrothorn is able to capitalize on the switches it forces to set a layer of Spikes or use Leech Seed to help keep itself healthy. Leech Seed also ensures that Ferrothorn can still defeat defensive Primal Kyogre even when burnt and provides some valuable healing for Pokemon such as Primal Groudon and Giratina-O.
  • Knock Off is preferred in the last moveslot, as many of Ferrothorn's common switch-ins, such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal, are heavily dependent on their items to function. Protect is an alternative that enables Ferrothorn to rack up healing from Leftovers and Leech Seed and scout Choice-locked Pokemon such as Rayquaza, Marshadow, and Lunala, but Protect makes it significantly more passive.
  • A Sassy nature and 0 Speed IVs are used to enable Ferrothorn to outspeed Melmetal under Trick Room. This gives Ferrothorn the flexibility to set a layer of Spikes or Knock Off Melmetal's Choice Band, preventing it from being able to 2HKO Ferrothorn with Tera Steel Double Iron Bash. Ferrothorn maximizes its special bulk to better check wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, as even Water Spout fails to 2HKO.
  • Ferrothorn rarely Terastallizes, as it is reliant on its natural typing to function, but it does benefit from Terastallization in some scenarios. Tera Water swaps Ferrothorn's quadruple Fire weakness for a resistance. While Ferrothorn is not able to meaningfully damage any of the Fire-types in the tier, Tera does enable it to beat Ho-Oh if it is the last Pokemon alive, as Ho-Oh seldom runs recovery and is worn down by Iron Barbs and Leech Seed damage before it is able to knock out Ferrothorn. Tera Grass is an alternative to help Ferrothorn better check Arceus-Ground and Zygarde by turning its neutrality to Ground into a resistance. Tera Grass Power Whip is capable of OHKOing Calm Mind Arceus-Ground after a single layer of Spikes and Leech Seed damage. While Ferrothorn cannot beat Coil Zygarde directly even with Tera Grass, its newfound Ground resistance provides it with extra turns to use Knock Off or Leech Seed before switching to a teammate that can handle Zygarde. Ferrothorn does still have some issues with Dragon Dance Zygarde, however, as it commonly runs Substitute.
  • Ferrothorn is best used in the early- and mid-game to set Spikes against defensive Pokemon such as utility Arceus formes and Alomomola. If Primal Kyogre is on the opposing team, Ferrothorn should prioritize preserving HP until the set is revealed, as it can easily get chipped to where it is unable to switch into wallbreaker Primal Kyogre's Water Spout. Ferrothorn can be used as a lead against hyper offense teams due to its immunity to Smeargle's Spore and Glimmora's Mortal Spin enabling it to break their Focus Sashes easily. Ferrothorn matches up poorly into most hyper offense teams due to its overall passivity, so sacrificing Ferrothorn to deal with suicide leads enables teammates such as Primal Groudon and Arceus-Dark to preserve HP and better handle common threats such as Zacian-C and Ultra Necrozma.
  • Ferrothorn shines against balance and stall teams, as the passive damage it deals racks up over the course of longer games. Many defensive Pokemon are unable to meaningfully damage Ferrothorn, which makes it difficult to wear down. Stall teams in particular have a tough time preventing Ferrothorn from making progress; the only Knock Off absorber, Arceus-Dark, is unable to meaningfully hurt Ferrothorn, as Foul Play activates Iron Barbs. This allows Ferrothorn to keep both itself and its teammates healthy with Leech Seed while freely laying down Spikes.
  • Ferrothorn pairs best with defensive Pokemon that are vulnerable to wallbreaker Primal Kyogre. As such, Zygarde is an excellent teammate for Ferrothorn due to it countering the tier's prominent Fire-types, Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh. Zygarde is also the best blanket physical wall in the tier and is able to help check physical attackers such as Marshadow and Mega Salamence that are able to break Ferrothorn. Defensive Primal Groudon is also an excellent teammate for Ferrothorn, as it can set Stealth Rock and work in conjunction with Ferrothorn to ensure that Primal Kyogre rarely poses a threat. Ferrothorn can check wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, which often overwhelms Primal Groudon and leaves it unable to check Pokemon such as Zacian-C, while Primal Groudon can remove Pokemon such as Ho-Oh and Eternatus that that threaten Ferrothorn.
  • Ferrothorn struggles against Taunt users such as Yveltal and utility Arceus formes. Consequently, Arceus-Fairy is a solid teammate for Ferrothorn, as it counters specially offensive Yveltal and can use Taunt to prevent Ho-Oh, Yveltal, and Giratina-O from removing Ferrothorn's Spikes.
  • Choice Band Marshadow is a decent offensive partner for Ferrothorn due to its ability to revenge kill many Pokemon found on hyper offense teams, including Ultra Necrozma, Deoxys-A, and Zacian-C. Ditto can also fill this role, as it threatens to reverse sweep by copying Pokemon such as Zacian-C and Mega Salamence.

Entry Hazard Wall (Grass).description:
Ferrothorn is a highly reliable wall in Grass teams, boasting good defensive stats, recovery, and an immunity to Poison. It's an incredible asset for Grass teams, as it can manage notable threats such as Kyurem, Tapu Lele, and Melmetal. Gyro Ball capitalizes on its low Speed and threatens Fairy-types and fast foes like Alolan Ninetales and Tapu Lele. However, Iron Head provides more consistent damage against slower foes like Hatterene and is less susceptible to PP stalling, which is particularly useful against Kyurem if Ferrothorn isn't running Body Press. Depending on its teammates, Ferrothorn can opt for Stealth Rock or Spikes, as Cradily can also set up Stealth Rock, while Meowscarada has access to Spikes and Toxic Spikes. With the combination of Leech Seed and Leftovers, Ferrothorn gains substantial recovery each turn, enabling it to wear down and punish switch-ins such as Heatran, Aegislash, and Nidoking. Protect serves as a scouting tool and extends the benefits of Leech Seed and Leftovers, while Body Press allows Ferrothorn to utilize its high Defense and deal significant damage to Steel- and Dark-types, like Melmetal and Weavile. When in conjunction with Gyro Ball, Body Press ensures that Substitute Kyurem won't be able to PP stall Ferrothorn, and when used with Iron Head, it guarantees an OHKO against Weavile. The featured EV spread both prevents a 2HKO from Choice Band Weavile's Icicle Crash and lets Ferrothorn almost always beat SubRoost Kyurem.

Ferrothorn forms a formidable defensive core with Mega Venusaur, as the latter's typing and ability enable it to come in on Fighting- and Ice-types such as Iron Valiant, Iron Moth, and Galarian Darmanitan. Additionally, Mega Venusaur's Sludge Bomb can poison foes, allowing Ferrothorn's combination of Leech Seed and Protect to wear them down more quickly. Cradily is another valuable partner, providing natural special bulk and a favorable matchup against Blacephalon and Nidoking. Offensive partners such as Rillaboom, Meowscarada, Iron Leaves, and Zarude greatly appreciate Ferrothorn weakening the opposing team with entry hazards and Leech Seed. In return, Rillaboom sets up Grassy Terrain for additional recovery and provides strong priority damage, while Choice Scarf Meowscarada can revenge kill threats such as boosted Kommo-o. Whimsicott and Celebi handle Fighting-types such as Iron Valiant and Kommo-o, which would otherwise pose a threat to Ferrothorn. Whimsicott also punishes setup sweepers like Volcarona or Mega Scizor, which could otherwise use Ferrothorn as setup fodder, while Celebi helps ease the Poison matchup, as well as the Steel matchup in a pinch.

Hazard Setter (Steel).description: As a check to Water- and Ground-types that can support its team with a wide variety of utility options, Ferrothorn is a notable defensive asset for Steel teams. Protect allows Ferrothorn to maximize the HP it gains per turn between Leftovers and Leech Seed, as well as easing prediction against Choice-locked foes such as Enamorus, Galarian Darmanitan, and Hisuian Arcanine. Power Whip minimizes passivity against the foes it's meant to check, notably OHKOing Mega Swampert and Gastrodon. Knock Off provides utility by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes such as Volcarona, Mantine, and Victini, leaving them vulnerable to the entry hazard stacking that is characteristic of Steel teams. The given EV spread with a Careful nature avoids a 2HKO from Landorus's Earth Power, with the rest invested in Defense to ease checking foes such as Mega Swampert, Ogerpon-W, and Mega Aerodactyl. The alternate EV spread with an Impish nature instead maximizes physical bulk, notably avoiding a 2HKO from Ogerpon-C's Low Kick. As Ferrothorn is easy to force out by Fire-type moves, Heatran is a solid partner to make a defensive core with it, especially because it can also set Stealth Rock, allowing Ferrothorn to run Spikes to hazard stack further; this can be further complemented with a check to Fighting-types in Gholdengo, which keeps entry hazards set by Ferrothorn on the other side of the field by blocking hazard removal. Offensive Pokemon such as Mega Scizor and Excadrill benefit from Ferrothorn wearing down and hindering the opposing team for a late-game sweep, mitigating Ferrothorn's passivity issues. Chople Berry is a niche alternative over Leftovers, as it enables Ferrothorn to withstand an attack from Fighting-types such as Keldeo and Urshifu-R, then KO back with Power Whip.

Defensive.description:
Ferrothorn is an excellent defensive Steel-type and entry hazard setter, since its Grass typing lends it resistances to Water and Electric as well as a neutrality to Ground, allowing it to more comfortably handle Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Mega Swampert, Tapu Koko, and Raging Bolt, which other Steel-types like Mega Scizor and Gholdengo have more trouble against; being a Steel-type also naturally improves its matchup against Melmetal, Tapu Lele, and Rillaboom. Iron Barbs lets Ferrothorn pressure foes like Urshifu-R, Mega Lopunny, Melmetal lacking Protective Pads, and U-turn users like Landorus-T, forcing them to play more carefully lest they rack up chip damage very quickly with contact moves. Leech Seed is Ferrothorn's most reliable recovery, allowing it to pressure other passive Pokemon like Toxapex and Gliscor into wasting their healing moves, deal valuable chip damage to switch-ins that have no means of healing such as Cinderace and Heatran, and gradually recover HP with each use. Knock Off allows Ferrothorn to punish Heavy-Duty Boots users like Zapdos, Toxapex, and Tornadus-T as well as Leftovers users like Landorus-T, which is extremely valuable in forcing progress by making foes more susceptible to hazards or removing their recovery. Body Press allows Ferrothorn to surprise Kingambit and Kyurem, dealing massive damage to both and avoiding getting PP stalled by Kyurem; it also lets Ferrothorn hit Heatran on the switch and damage opposing Ferrothorn instead of idling. Gyro Ball snags Fairy-types like Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant on the switch and is better neutral coverage against foes like Dragonite, although it should be run with a Relaxed nature and 0 Speed IVs. Thunder Wave is niche, providing great value against offense teams, but since it is easily blocked by Gholdengo, it is often undesirable. Spikes is used over Stealth Rock when another setter is present on the team. The Special Defense EVs allow Ferrothorn to survive Choice Specs Tapu Lele's Focus Blast from full HP. Leftovers is nigh mandatory, providing much more consistent healing than Leech Seed and taking advantage of Ferrothorn's ability to sit on the field for many turns at a time. Rocky Helmet is a viable alternative, punishing U-turn users like Landorus-T and Urshifu-R as well as Rapid Spin from Great Tusk much harder; overall, it rewards risky play compared to Leftovers’s relative safety and should therefore allow Ferrothorn to be used more aggressively.

Most wallbreakers pair well with Ferrothorn, taking advantage of the entry hazards it sets to break through defensive targets, but those that switch in on Ferrothorn's counters such as Gholdengo, Zamazenta, and Mega Charizard Y are particularly good; these wallbreakers include Kingambit, Mega Charizard Y, Tapu Lele, and Mega Tyranitar; Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar can also Pursuit trap Gholdengo. Gholdengo itself is also a good teammate, as it can deny Defog and switch in more easily against Pokemon like Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant. Ferrothorn's defensive utility is also appreciated by teammates like Toxapex and Landorus-T, which struggle with Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Water- and Ice-types like Hisuian Samurott and Kyurem, all of which Ferrothorn helps check. However, Ferrothorn does have a host of issues that require some support to cover. Ferrothorn's glaring Fire weakness is not even its biggest problem, given that having teammates like Toxapex, Heatran, and Alomomola around can easily blank Fire-type moves from the likes of Mega Charizard Y and opposing Heatran. Its main problem stems from its lack of instant recovery, making it more inclined to offensively oriented teams. Having Leftovers removed by Knock Off from foes like Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and opposing Ferrothorn or getting burned by Scald from foes like Toxapex renders it unable to heal without Leech Seed, and Leech Seed fails against Gholdengo and common Grass-types like Ogerpon-W and opposing Ferrothorn. Therefore, Ferrothorn is best played more offensively, using its unique defensive utility, Leech Seed, and Iron Barbs to force switches and hazard chip damage, granting immediate momentum when played aggressively while also not punishing the user for playing more carefully. Teammates that can absorb Knock Off, like Mega Tyranitar, and those that can absorb Will-O-Wisp, like Heatran and Clefable, are incredibly valuable teammates. Finally, Pokemon that can cover Ferrothorn's Fighting weakness are good defensively, including the aforementioned Gholdengo as well as Zapdos, Landorus-T, and Toxapex.

nu.overview: With Chandelure's tremendous Special Attack and STAB attacks, it can hit the entire tier for at least neutral damage, barring Incineroar. Chandelure, donning a Choice Specs, easily breaks through would-be checks like Rhyperior and Goodra. However, with Choice Scarf, it becomes a dangerous revenge killer that’s able to check setup sweepers like Munkidori and Uxie. Chandelure also learns Trick, which allows it to cripple walls and bulky setup sweepers alike such as Vaporeon, Incineroar, and Uxie. However, Chandelure has to deal with being extremely weak to entry hazards, limiting its opportunities to switch in. On top of that, Chandelure itself is quite easily revenge killed due to faster Choice Scarf users that are able to threaten it with their own STAB moves or through coverage moves like Flygon, Flamigo, and Munkidori.
nu.comments:
Other Options

With a moveset of Will-O Wisp / Pain Split / Energy Ball / Hex, an EV spread of 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe, and a Bold nature, Chandelure, with Heavy-Duty Boots, can become an effective physical wall, spreading burns on the opposing team quite easily; however, most things it would want to check typically carry super effective coverage in Knock Off. Heavy-Duty Boots Chandelure can also run Flame Charge or Trailblaze to pick off weakened threats and sweep with its boosted Speed. Chandelure can run Hex on a status spreading team; however, it must give up a powerful STAB attack, coverage, or Trick to do so. Choice Scarf Chandelure can run Memento on a hyper offense team to try to aid its teammates in setting up once it becomes useless. Chandelure can also run Heavy-Duty Boots or Air Balloon to circumvent its entry hazards weakness and Ground-type weakness, respectively. If it runs these, though, it becomes noticeably weaker and slower.

Checks and Counters

Fire-resistant Pokemon: Incineroar, Goodra, and Vaporeon are a pain for Chandelure mostly because they tend to be able to take one attack and retaliate with Knock Off, Draco Meteor, or Scald. Specifically, Incineroar is quite problematic, since it resists all of Chandelure's attacks and is quite specially defensive. However, due to the former two's to lack of recovery and entry hazards vulnerability, they can be chipped over the course of a game whereas all can be taken advantage of with Trick, giving Chandelure their Heavy-Duty Boots.

Ghost-types: While Chandelure is able to beat Ghost-types like Basculegion-M, Brambleghast, and Houndstone offensively, it struggles to switch into and take priority attacks from them, and more often that not, it will get outsped and KOed by the Brambleghast.

Revenge Killers: With Chandelure's middling Speed, even with Choice Scarf, it is quite easily revenge killed by faster threats. Most notably, faster Choice Scarf users like Flygon and Flamigo threaten Chandelure through their super effective STAB attacks or coverage, respectively.

Choice Specs.description:
Set Details

Fire Blast is preferred for better damage rolls against Goodra and Incineroar as to not let them switch in safely, but Flamethrower can be used to be more accurate. Energy Ball hits Fire-type checks such as Swampert and Rhyperior. Trick cripples walls like Vaporeon and Incineroar, but Overheat allows Chandelure to overwhelm Incineroar and Goodra over the course of a battle. Timid provides Chandelure the Speed to beat Jolly Basculegion-M and other Pokemon in that range like Tsareena and Goodra. However, Modest's sheer damage output can make it more valuable than Timid's Speed. Tera Grass allows Chandelure to take a Ground- or Water-type attack in a pinch while boosting its Energy Ball, but Tera Fire can be used to give it insane breaking power.

Chandelure has issues with switching in, so Pokemon that can pivot like Flamigo, Flygon, and Tsareena pair well, drawing in defensive Psychic-, Grass-, and Steel-types such as Galarian Slowbro, Whimsicott, and Copperajah for Chandelure to prey on. With Trick crippling specially defensive foes like Incineroar and Vaporeon, a partner that can take advantage of this like Munkidori or Uxie helps with overwhelming these shared checks. Pairing Chandelure with Fighting-types like Flamigo, Toxicroak, and Scrafty helps it take on Dark-types like Incineroar and Skuntank, which it tends to struggle against. With how vulnerable Chandelure is to entry hazards, it pairs greatly with hazards removal from Scyther, Cinccino, and Altaria. Whimsicott, Wo-Chien, and Tsareena are great teammates for Chandelure, as they check the Ground- and Water-types that scare it out like Flygon, Basculegion-M, and Inteleon; on top of that, the former two teammates can spread paralysis with Stun Spore.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

Fire Blast gives Chandelure a powerful STAB Fire-type attack, but Flamethrower can be run for a more accurate move. Energy Ball hits Fire-resistant Pokemon like Rhyperior, Vaporeon, and Swampert. Trick cripples walls and bulky setup sweepers like Incineroar and Scrafty. When backed into a corner, Tera Grass lets Chandelure take a Water- or Ground-type attack and boosts its Energy Ball, but Tera Fire can help it clean more easily.

With how Chandelure fails to do much of anything versus specially defensive Fire-resistant walls like Incineroar and Goodra, partners that can overwhelm, chip away at, or cripple these Pokemon are vital. So, pair Chandelure with teammates like Munkidori, Uxie, and Meloetta. Chandelure's middling Speed means more common opposing Choice Scarf users like Flamigo, Flygon, and Munkidori will easily outspeed and OHKO it. Chandelure's weakness to being worn down by entry hazards stops it from revenge killing as often as it would want to, so teammates like Scyther, Cinccino, and Altaria are crucial.

Calm Mind.description:
Fire Blast is preferred for improved damage rolls after a Calm Mind boost and deal greater damage to other special walls like Incineroar and Sylveon, but Flamethrower can be used for its accuracy. Energy Ball targets common Water-, Rock-, and Ground-type switch-ins like Vaporeon, Rhyperior, and Swampert. However, Pain Split, which is always run with the second EV spread, allows Chandelure to stick around for longer, punishing normal counterplay options like Incineroar and Vaporeon. Flash Fire gives Chandelure the ability to take advantage of Choice-locked Fire-types like Hisuian Typhlosion, Infernape, and opposing Chandelure. On the other hand, Flame Body lets Chandelure punish contact moves like Flygon's U-turn and Tsareena's Power Whip, but these targets and most others usually carry another move to hit Chandelure super effectively, which is why it is ran with the bulkier EV spread and Tera types such as Fairy, Water, and Dark so as to not entirely negate its utility. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Chandelure to ignore entry hazards, letting it switch in repeatedly without worry. However, Air Balloon can be used instead to give Chandelure a temporary immunity to Ground-type attacks, giving Chandelure opportunities to set up against Earthquake Paldean Tauros-F and Choice-locked Flygon. The first EV spread maximizes offensive prowess, while the second lets Chandelure outpace Jolly Incineroar and survive bulky Incineroar's Knock Off into U-turn while maximizing damage output. Tera Grass boosts Energy Ball while giving Chandelure a resistance to Ground- and Water-type attacks from Pokemon like Flygon, Swampert, and Vaporeon. Tera Fairy can be used on Air Balloon sets to completely wall Flygon's STAB moves, and in general, it helps with taking Dark-type attacks from the likes of Bombirdier and Incineroar. Tera Water is best used on Flame Body Chandelure with the bulky EV spread, since it allows Chandelure to flip matchups against Vaporeon and Incineroar on their head. Tera Dark offers a Ghost and Dark resistance, though, helping in checking foes like Houndstone and opposing Chandelure in an emergency.

Ground-types like Flygon and Gligar can destroy Chandelure with their STAB Earthquake, and they can also force it to Terastallize. Therefore, it best partners with defensive Water-types like Vaporeon and Swampert, as they can check the aforementioned Ground-types; in return, Chandelure handles Grass-types like Tsareena, Amoonguss, and Whimsicott. Fairy- and Fighting-types like Sylveon, Toxicroak, and Paldean Tauros-W are great teammates for Chandelure, as they can handle the switch-ins like Goodra, Vaporeon, and Incineroar. Chandelure appreciates slow pivots like Swampert, Vaporeon, and Bellibolt giving it a safe entry without the risk of taking damage. Galvantula and Araquanid are great partners for Chandelure, as they can set up Sticky Web to remedy Chandelure's underwhelming Speed, letting it outspeed and KO faster foes like Flamigo, Inteleon, and Paldean Tauros-W. On these teams, fellow setup sweepers like Swords Dance Toxicroak, Nasty Plot Munkidori, and Shell Smash Drednaw can take advantage of Water-types, overwhelm Dark-types, and help beat Ground-types for Chandelure, respectively. Air Balloon Chandelure is vulnerable to Stealth Rock; thus, it pairs well with hazard removers like Brambleghast, Cinccino, and Scyther.

nfe.overview: Fraxure is an excellent wallbreaker and setup sweeper, possessing one of NFE's highest Attack stats and an offensive typing that's narrowly resisted. Access to Scale Shot enables it to bypass its low Speed and outspeed revenge killers like Frogadier and Girafarig, and its defensive typing allows it to set up on staples like Quaxwell and Thwackey. Choice Band sets are extremely threatening for their immediate power and access to First Impression, while Swords Dance sets terrify structures with their immense power after setup and Scale Shot to bypass Fraxure's mediocre Speed and ability to threaten revenge killers. However, Fraxure is held back by its low Speed and bulk; if it cannot use First Impression, much of the metagame can easily outspeed it, and even after a boost, Choice Scarf users like Frogadier and Monferno can easily revenge kill it. Fraxure's typing is a double-edged sword: while it is fantastic offensively and can let Fraxure set up against weaker walls, it also leaves Fraxure very vulnerable against metagame staples like Piloswine and Wartortle.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Poison Jab can be used over Scale Shot to target Clefairy and the uncommon Morgrem while potentially poisoning bulky threats like Piloswine and Dunsparce, though the low poison chance combined with the move's narrower coverage makes it difficult to fit over another attack. Loaded Dice on Swords Dance sets can be used to buff Scale Shot's power, though this gives up some of Fraxure's already mediocre bulk. Dragon Dance can be an alternative way of setting up, though Scale Shot's immediate damage output makes Swords Dance the preferred option.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Tinkatuff, Clefairy, and the uncommon Morgrem are some of Fraxure's biggest threats; barring the rare Poison Jab, they can switch into Fraxure relatively easily and threaten it with either Thunder Wave or STAB attacks. Tinkatuff can even run Air Balloon to completely wall Fraxure barring First Impression.

Physical Walls: Physical walls like Koffing, Dunsparce, and Naclstack can comfortably stomach even a boosted Fraxure, threaten it with status, and heal off the damage with their recovery moves, with the latter two even using it as setup fodder. Koffing and Mareanie can set up Toxic Spikes to cut into Fraxure's sweeping potential, while Dunsparce can threaten it out with Ice Beam or set up Coil against it.

Faster Pokemon: Without First Impression, Fraxure's mediocre Speed leaves it vulnerable to most faster Pokemon, with threats like Girafarig, Frogadier, Drakloak, and Raboot easily able to pick it off with some prior damage.

Piloswine: Piloswine has good odds of surviving a +2 Outrage after Stealth Rock and can retaliate with its STAB moves, picking it off with Ice Shard after some chip damage or Defense drops from Scale Shot.

Residual Damage and Status: Fraxure is vulnerable to all entry hazards, and its sweeping potential can be dashed through burn or paralysis. Examples of common paralysis-spreading users include Hattrem, Servine, and Dunsparce, while Koffing and Drakloak can burn it.

Setup Sweeper.description:
With a Jolly nature and after a Swords Dance boost, Outrage is able to OHKO threats like Pignite and, with Stealth Rock, Wartortle. It also 2HKOes defensive staples like Quaxwell and Hattrem. Scale Shot can avoid Outrage's trapping effects and is used to finish off weakened foes or capitalize on Pokemon that can potentially switch out against it, like Quaxwell and Ivysaur. Stomping Tantrum provides key coverage against Tinkatuff and Pawniard while still letting Fraxure hit Fire-types like Pignite and Monferno hard without locking into Outrage. While a Jolly nature is helpful to outspeed Glimmet and Hakamo-o, an Adamant nature strengthens Fraxure's attacks and has improved odds of OHKOing threats like Piloswine with Outrage after a Swords Dance boost.

Fairy-types like Tinkatuff and Clefairy are some of Fraxure's biggest threats, being immune to Fraxure's STAB moves and having ways to work around its coverage. Pokemon like Piloswine and Koffing are excellent partners, with both providing entry hazards and absorbing paralysis and the latter even providing Toxic Spikes and Will-O-Wisp support to wear down foes. Paralysis spreaders like Tinkatuff and Hattrem are similarly good partners, slowing down faster foes like Frogadier and Girafarig that would otherwise easily revenge kill Fraxure. Tinkatuff also provides Knock Off support, and Hattrem can use Healing Wish to give Fraxure a second chance at sweeping. Other wallbreakers and cleaners, like Thwackey and Raboot, are also helpful in working together with Fraxure to more easily break down the opposition. Popular revenge killers like Frogadier, Piloswine, and Drakloak can threaten Fraxure out without too much trouble, so teammates like Clefairy, Quaxwell and Dunsparce can provide defensive backbones against these threats.

Choice Band.description:
Fraxure is one of the best wallbreakers and revenge killers in the metagame owing to its colossal Attack and amazing movepool. First Impression is its primary revenge killing tool, being able to pick off several top-tier threats such as Girafarig, Thwackey, and Frogadier. Dragon Claw, unlike Outrage, doesn't lock Fraxure in and helps it avoid being crippled by Fairy-types like Clefairy and Tinkatuff. Stomping Tantrum hits Tinkatuff, 2HKOes Koffing, and OHKOes Pawniard after Stealth Rock damage. An Adamant nature maximizes Fraxure's offensive potential, letting it hit thresholds like always 2HKOing Quaxwell with Outrage and maximum Defense Tinkatuff with Stomping Tantrum.

Fraxure fits on bulky offense and balance teams as a dedicated physical wallbreaker and anti-offense revenge killer. It works best when paired with pivots and entry hazard setters, as they provide it with entry opportunities and facilitate its wallbreaking. Frogadier excels in both roles, making it a wonderful partner. Quaxwell, Raboot, and Thwackey provide pivoting support and handle Piloswine, one of the best checks to Fraxure; moreover, Quaxwell provides Rapid Spin support, ensuring Fraxure stays for long in the game. Fraxure can't afford to take Knock Off because it loses too much power; Tinkatuff helps by acting as a Knock Off absorber and also provides Stealth Rock and Knock Off support. Other hazard-setting teammates include Piloswine and Koffing. Piloswine can also act as a Tinkatuff switch-in in case Fraxure is Choice-locked into a move other than Stomping Tantrum. Fraxure is vulnerable to paralysis spreaders like Hattrem and Clefairy, which can cut into its offensive prowess. Thus, paralysis absorbers like Gabite and Koffing are great teammates. Special wallbreakers work excellently with Fraxure, ripping apart defensive cores with ease. Choice Specs Drakloak, Hisuian Sliggoo, and aforementioned Girafarig are all suited for the job. Fraxure appreciates Knock Off support a lot because Eviolite removal makes it even deadlier in its job. Thus, Pokemon like Monferno, Pignite, Vullaby as well as the previously mentioned Thwackey pair amazingly with it, with Vullaby even providing Defog support. Fraxure often gets Choice-locked in the wrong move, so having a solid defensive core backing it up is of utmost importance, especially on balance teams. Defensive options to pair Fraxure with include Pokemon like Ivysaur, Drakloak, and the aforementioned Quaxwell and Koffing.

• Bolstering a massive Attack stat, Haxorus uses its natural strength combined with a Choice Band to overwhelm its foes.
  • Outrage is Haxorus's strongest option, threatening KOs on many Pokemon that don't resist it, such as Pecharunt, Volcarona, and Volcanion.
  • Scale Shot allows Haxorus to break through Substitutes created by SubSeed Pokemon such as Serperior.
  • First Impression allows Haxorus to get the jump on Meowscarada and Chien-Pao.
  • For the last move, Close Combat can be used to threaten KOs on Steel-types such as Heatran and Hisuian Goodra. Iron Tail can be used to KO Diancie and Sylveon. Finally, Poison Jab can OHKO Whimsicott.
  • Unnerve is Haxorus's generally preferred ability to prevent Pokemon that use resistance berries such as Haban Berry Raging Bolt and Chople Berry Hisuian Goodra and Urshifu-S from preventing an OHKO. However, Mold Breaker can be used to break through Hisuian Avalugg's Sturdy.
  • As Choice Band Haxorus is locked into a move after it selects one, it is advised to select the move that does the most damage.
  • Steel-types that don't care for Haxorus's coverage moves such as Corviknight and Iron Crown can defeat Haxorus, while faster Ice- and Fairy-type Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Kyurem and Iron Valiant can threaten a KO on Haxorus. Good Fire- and Steel-type partners like Volcanion and one's own Iron Crown can help Haxorus in these poor matchups.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Haxorus looks to outspeed and KO a variety of different Pokemon with high-Base Power moves while using Unnerve to prevent Custap Berry on Hoopa-U and Haban Berry on Raging Bolt and Garchomp from being activated.
  • Outrage allows Haxorus to OHKO most other Dragon-types like Raging Bolt and Dragapult.
  • Close Combat can hit Porygon-Z and Choice Specs Darkrai.
  • The remaining moveslots can be tailored to beat specific notable Pokemon in the tier. Rock Slide can be used to target Volcarona. X-Scissor hits Hoopa-U, Meowscarada, and both offensive and SubSeed Ogerpon-W without the downside of confusion chances from Outrage. Iron Tail hits Diancie and Alolan Ninetales. Earthquake can hit non-Air Balloon Heatran.
  • Adamant maximizes Choice Scarf Haxorus's damage output, which can be important for matchups versus bulky Porygon-Z, while a Jolly nature gives Haxorus maximum Speed to outpace Choice Scarf Porygon-Z.
  • Haxorus struggles with most Steel- and Fairy-types like Hisuian Goodra and Primarina as well as physically bulky Pokemon even if they don't resist Outrage like Landorus-T and Ursaluna, so it pairs well with Pokemon like Iron Hands and Air Balloon Volcanion that can deal with them.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to the next generation of Battle Stadium Singles! In this new and exciting metagame, new ideas are constantly developing, so this analysis will constantly be updated to reflect metagame trends.

If you feel this analysis is not up to date, feel free to check out the thread for this Pokemon and post suggestions. For more resources on Series 1 in general, check out this thread.

Mold Breaker Funny Moments Compilation.description:
• With its workable Speed, sky-high Attack stat, and the ever-valuable Mold Breaker, Haxorus is notable as one of the few setup sweepers not bothered by Mimikyu or Unaware.

  • With one Dragon Dance, it can outspeed most unboosted foes, but Choice Scarf users still cause issues, notably Hydreigon and Play Rough Meowscarada.

  • Dragon Claw may be worth using in place of Outrage to avoid locking Haxorus in.

  • Earthquake is extremely valuable on Haxorus due to Mold Breaker nullifying Levitate and Earth Eater, allowing Haxorus to hit foes like Rotom-W and Hydreigon hard without the need to lock into Outrage, and giving it a way to hit Orthworm hard at all

Items

  • Life Orb: Life Orb lets Haxorus deal damage much more effectively at the cost of recoil

  • Lum Berry: Lum Berry lets Haxorus safely set up against a foe that may use crippling status moves such as Will-O-Wisp and Spore.

Tera Types

  • Steel: Steel grants good security against opposing Ice-, Fairy-, and Dragon-types.

  • Fairy: Fairy maximizes Haxorus's security against opposing Dragon-types, specifically.

  • Electric: Electric provides a surefire way of dealing with Dondozo thanks to Tera Blast.

zu.overview: Under snow, Beartic is a chillingly threatening sweeper, boasting wide coverage and frightening offensive power while outspeeding the entire unboosted metagame. The Defense boost in snow allows it to tank physical attacks like Primeape's Close Combat and Lycanroc's Stone Edge. Beartic relies on Abomasnow to provide snow, and it forms a deadly offensive core with it, as Abomasnow's Aurora Veil makes Beartic even more difficult to take down. Beartic, however, is hindered by its low Speed and awful defensive typing; even under snow, it can be outsped by faster Choice Scarf users like Hisuian Sneasel and Typhlosion. Even with the Defense boost and Aurora Veil support, Beartic sports minimal defensive utility, owing to its vulnerability to all residual damage and lack of resistances if not running Heavy-Duty Boots, and it also stacks weaknesses with Abomasnow. Outside of snow, Beartic is extremely slow and easy to revenge kill without Terastallization, requiring significant support to perform well as a setup sweeper.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Beartic has no other viable options.

Checks and Counters

Faster Revenge Killers: Even under snow, Beartic is still quite slow and can be picked off by Choice Scarf users like Basculin, Hisuian Sneasel, and Primeape.

Physical Walls: Physical walls like Weezing, Spiritomb, and Sableye can threaten Beartic with Will-O-Wisp, while walls like Regirock and Orthworm can beat it with Iron Defense in a one-on-one scenario.

Residual Damage: Beartic is vulnerable to all entry hazards if not running Heavy-Duty Boots and despises status, all of which heavily cut into its sweeping potential and making it easier to revenge kill.

Wallbreakers: Most wallbreakers not weak to its coverage moves can stomach at least one unboosted attack and retaliate, which is especially prominent if Beartic is not under snow. Examples include Primeape, Vikavolt, and Clawitzer.

Snow Sweeper.description:
The combination of snow and Slush Rush enables Beartic to become one of the scariest setup sweepers under this archetype, boasting high offensive stats and outspeeding the entire unboosted metagame. Icicle Spear's higher power is preferred over Icicle Crash's potential flinch chance if running Loaded Dice, and its multiple hits work well against foes using Substitute like Minior and Whimsicott. Close Combat threatens Ice-resistant targets like Orthworm and Clawitzer while also hitting Regirock hard. Earthquake threatens Magneton, and non-Choice Scarf Typhlosion, while Substitute capitalizes on weak walls like Muk and Dipplin. While an Adamant nature is ideal to maximize its power, Jolly can be used to outspeed Choice Scarf Primeape and Choice Scarf Mesprit under snow. If Beartic is not running Icicle Spear, Life Orb or Heavy-Duty Boots can be chosen to either strengthen all of its moves' power or protect it from entry hazard damage, respectively. Tera Fighting boosts the power of Close Combat and lets Beartic resist priority moves like Sucker Punch and Accelerock, while Tera Ground boosts the power of Earthquake and provides it a Stealth Rock resistance and Electric immunity while still resisting Accelerock; changing into either of these Tera types, however, relinquishes the Defense boost under snow.

Due to Beartic being heavily reliant on snow for wallbreaking, Abomasnow is a mandatory partner to enable Slush Rush and the Defense boost. Pivots like Clawitzer and Primeape can help threaten and force out walls like Regirock and Orthworm, while wallbreakers like Clawitzer and Charizard can be similarly effective. Hattrem is a notable partner, as it supplies paralysis and Healing Wish support, enabling Beartic to clean through teams easier, while providing Magic Bounce support for Beartic's non-Heavy-Duty Boots sets. Spinners like Sandslash and Hitmontop are also valuable partners, providing entry hazard removal support without needing to remove Aurora Veil. Water-types like Clawitzer and Basculin can not only force out Fire-types but also provide pivoting support. Hazard setters like Regirock and Sandslash not only can help rack up residual damage over the course of a game but also provide additional utility with Thunder Wave and Knock Off, respectively. Other setup sweepers like Minior can overwhelm teams and shared checks like Regirock with Beartic.

Fast Pivot.description:
Mienfoo continues its LC dominance with its mixture of defensive fortitude from Regenerator, moveset utility, and its Speed acting as the benchmark for the rest of the tier. Knock Off enables Mienfoo to create consistent progress against opposing Pokemon like Foongus and Mareanie that resist its Fighting-type attacks. U-turn synergizes with Mienfoo's Regenerator ability while also exploiting defensive switches that Mienfoo often causes. Fake Out is a useful move for helping Mienfoo lead against opposing teams and chipping down Choice Scarf users. Taunt is a valuable substitute to Fake Out that can prevent setup as well as status such as Foongus's Spore. Tera Steel grants Mienfoo important resistances to Vullaby's Brave Bird and both of Foongus's STAB move options. Alternatively, Tera Water can be used in order to resist Alolan Sandshrew's Triple Axel and Hisuian Growlithe's Flare Blitz.

Mienfoo's versatility allows it to fit on a large variety of teams. Vullaby is Mienfoo's most common partner because of its ability to manage Foongus and Gothita, which Mienfoo struggles to deal with, while Mienfoo can deal significant damage to Vullaby's switch-ins like Tinkatink. Mienfoo's pivoting power from U-turn allows frailer teammates like Elekid and Alolan Diglett more opportunities to enter the battlefield. Gothita is another excellent partner for Mienfoo, as its Shadow Tag ability allows it to switch in after Mienfoo's U-turn to trap Poison-types like Foongus and Mareanie that Mienfoo has difficulties making progress against. Chinchou is a great teammate for switching into fast offensive threats like Elekid and Wingull that threaten big damage to Mienfoo.

Slow Pivot.description:
Defensive Mienfoo is one of the tier's most reliable pivots, with Regenerator letting it repeatedly sponge hits and Knock Off and U-turn removing Eviolites and maintaining momentum, respectively. Fake Out provides useful chip damage, while High Jump Kick is its STAB of choice, pressuring most of the metagame. The EV spread balances physical and special bulk, letting it withstand hits from threats like Hisuian Growlithe and opposing Mienfoo, with its most notable benchmark being the ability to survive Brave Bird from Adamant Vullaby. Additionally, the physical bulk and lack of Speed investment allows it to exchange Knock Off in the Mienfoo mirror and hit back with High Jump Kick or pivot out with U-turn thanks to its bulk. Tera Steel improves its matchup against Vullaby, while Tera Water lets it check Alolan Sandshrew and Hisuian Growlithe.

Mienfoo pairs well with offensive teammates that benefit from its item removal and slow pivoting, such as Elekid, Gothita, and Alolan Sandshrew; these teammates also help pressure bulky Poisons-types like Foongus and Mareanie. However, its lack of Speed investment leaves it vulnerable to threats like Vullaby, Glimmet, and opposing Alolan Sandshrew, making partners such as Tinkatink, Chinchou, and Mudbray valuable to cover these matchups. Having faster teammates like Elekid or Choice Scarf Gothita paired with Mienfoo also helps maintain offensive pressure and compensate for its lower Speed.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Mienfoo is one of the tier's scariest wallbreakers and sweepers. +2 High Jump Kick will OHKO almost all targets that do not resist it, with the exception of fully healthy Mudbray and Vullaby with at least 156 Defense EVs. Knock Off provides nearly perfect coverage against Ghost-types and Terastallized foes while also applying lasting pressure by removing Eviolites. The last moveslot is flexible, but Substitute is popular for its ability to overpower Foongus by removing Spore from the equation as well as scout Terastallization from foes. Tera Steel is still an excellent defensive Tera type against Vullaby and Wingull sets even with minimal Defense investment and also prevents Foongus from breaking Mienfoo's Substitute in one hit.

Swords Dance Mienfoo sacrifices bulk and pivoting to run this set, so it pairs best with pivots such as Chinchou and Vullaby as well as sturdy defensive Pokemon such as Foongus and Mareanie. Some fast options to help close out games include Alolan Diglett, Stunky, and Elekid, which are needed because Mienfoo is often too slow to close out games on its own but can break huge holes for its teammates. Some Swords Dance Mienfoo sets can also work on hyper offense builds, with supporters such as lead Stealth Rock Alolan Diglett and sweepers such as Nasty Plot Vullaby. These Mienfoo sets often have more variety, as they can specialize to sweep in specific circumstances by being able to run sets such as Reckless Agility + Swords Dance, among others.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Mienfoo's superb Speed tier, in conjunction with its Reckless-boosted High Jump Kick, makes it an excellent wallbreaker capable of OHKOing or 2HKOing most neutral targets. Knock Off removes Eviolite from Fighting-resistant foes like Foongus and Mareanie, wearing them down for later, while hitting Ghost-types and Tera Ghost Pokémon. U-turn lets Mienfoo scout for switch-ins and punish them accordingly. Close Combat is used when a more accurate move is preferred and High Jump Kick’s power isn't needed. Tera Fighting combined with Reckless skyrockets Mienfoo's damage output, letting it OHKO targets like less bulky variants of pivot Mienfoo, Tinkatink, and Vullaby while having a favorable roll to 2HKO Foongus with High Jump Kick after Stealth Rock.

Choice Scarf Mienfoo is best utilized on offensive teams that appreciate its immediate Speed and power. It pairs especially well with Gothita, which can use Shadow Tag to trap and remove bulky Poison-types like Foongus and Mareanie that otherwise check Mienfoo. This synergy allows Choice Scarf Mienfoo to break more freely later in the match without constantly pivoting out. Choice Scarf Mienfoo appreciates teammates that share complementary breaking power, such as Vullaby, Wingull, and Elekid; all of these help pressure Mienfoo's checks. Additionally, Choice Scarf Mienfoo is very frail, so it benefits from being brought in safely by pivots like Chinchou, Elekid, and Vullaby. Choice Scarf Mienfoo also punishes teams expecting a pivot set, blowing up typical checks like Vullaby and Tinkatink. This can open up opportunities for allies such as Grookey, Stunky, and Vullaby.

Offensive Utility.description:
Mienshao is a fast Pokemon with a good support movepool that matches up well into Incineroar, since it is immune to Fake Out and Intimidate. Mienshao can use Fake Out on or OHKO Incineroar with Close Combat before it moves. Feint breaks opposing Wide Guard and Protect, enabling its partner to attack freely while breaking Focus Sashes or KOing opponents brought down to their Focus Sash. Wide Guard protects Mienshao and its partner from common powerful spread moves such as Astral Barrage, Glacial Lance, and Tera Starstorm and spread stat-reducing attacks such as Snarl and Icy Wind. Mienshao uses Focus Sash for extra longevity, allowing it to continue to support its partners. A Jolly nature lets Mienshao outrun Chi-Yu, while an Adamant nature gives Mienshao a high chance to OHKO uninvested Ursaluna-B. Tera Fighting allows Mienshao to guarantee an OHKO onto Ursaluna-B and Choice Specs Terapagos-S and a 2HKO on Zamazenta-C before it Terastallizes.

Mienshao struggles into Ghost-types such as Calyrex-S, Flutter Mane, and Lunala, since it is unable to damage them. This makes Calyrex-S and Chi-Yu great partners, as they can threaten them with their STAB Astral Barrage and Dark Pulse, respectively, with Calyrex-S outspeeding them and Chi-Yu withstanding their attacks. Calyrex-S and Chi-Yu, in return, appreciate Mienshao's support, with Fake Out allowing Calyrex-S to set up Nasty Plot and Feint breaking opposing Wide Guard and Protect, allowing both to freely attack. Mienshao's Wide Guard protects Calyrex-S from opposing Astral Barrage and Tera Starstorm and protects Chi-Yu from Water Spout, Origin Pulse, and Precipice Blades. Mienshao further supports Calyrex-S and Chi-Yu by matching up well against threats such as Incineroar and Terapagos. This, in turn, lets Calyrex-S's other common partners like Clefairy and Rillaboom support Calyrex-S more effectively.

Life Orb.description:
Mienshao functions as an elite offensive pivot that can fire off its high-powered moves while being hard to chip down thanks to Regenerator offsetting Life Orb recoil. It brings value in threatening key Pokemon such as Rotom-W, Skarmory, and Hippowdon. Knock Off in conjunction with U-turn wears down checks such as Clefable and Buzzwole, which is amplified with entry hazards. It also discourages the likes of Aegislash and Slowbro from coming in comfortably because they fear losing their item, ensuring that they are not long-term answers. U-turn lets Mienshao pivot out of unfavorable matchups such as Mega Venusaur and Buzzwole and bring in strong wallbreakers like Mega Aerodactyl, Keldeo, and Iron Moth. Triple Axel grants Mienshao the opportunity to KO switch-ins like Amoonguss, Hydrapple, and Mega Latias. Poison Jab is another option that Mienshao can use to punish Fairy-type switch-ins like Clefable, preventing it from coming in safely and 2HKOing it after losing Leftovers to Knock Off. Fake Out lets Mienshao rack up chip damage on faster foes like Zeraora and Iron Moth while also preventing revenge killing attempts from Lokix's First Impression. Mienshao also has the phenomenal ability to outlast its checks courtesy of Regenerator; Mienshao can run Life Orb freely, as Regenerator offsets the item's recoil damage.

Mienshao fits on both offensive and balance team styles, which appreciate its ability to force progress against targets such as Clefable and Slowbro. Rotom-W values Mienshao's ability to dent checks like Hisuian Goodra and Hydreigon. In return, Rotom-W brings Mienshao in versus its aforementioned checks while also using Will-O-Wisp to chip down Mega Venusaur. Mienshao can have a hard time muscling through checks such as Buzzwole and Slowbro; therefore, it appreciates strong teammates such as Hydrapple, Mega Gardevoir, and Iron Moth to help break through these foes. Mienshao is also quite frail, so it struggles to enter the field safely; therefore, it values pivot support from allies like Slowbro, Rotom-W, and Jirachi.
