Slowbro can provide Future Sight support, discouraging checks like Buzzwole and Mega Venusaur from coming in. Entry hazard support from Pokemon such as Jirachi and Skarmory is mandatory in order to wear down Mienshao's checks like the aforementioned Buzzwole and Amoonguss. Mienshao is still outsped by faster Pokemon such as Enamorus, Iron Boulder, and Mega Aerodactyl. Thus, teammates such as Slowbro, Rotom-W, and Jirachi are valued, as they can defensively answer these foes. Offensive allies like Scizor and Lokix are appreciated due to their ability to revenge kill the aforementioned faster foes with their priority moves.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Mienshao trades some power for speed, expanding its revenge killing capabilities because it is now able to threaten much faster Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl, Serperior, and Zeraora. Knock Off punishes switch-ins like Slowbro and Aegislash, leaving them more vulnerable to entry hazards from teammates like Skarmory and Jirachi. Mienshao can force switches against offensive Pokemon like Iron Boulder and then pivot out of unfavorable matchups such as Buzzwole, Skarmory, Mega Venusaur, and Hippowdon with U-turn. In addition, it brings in strong wallbreakers like Iron Moth and Mega Aerodactyl. Triple Axel threatens Pokemon like Mega Aerodactyl and Serperior, while Poison Jab allows Mienshao to hit Fairy-type Pokemon like Enamorus and Clefable.

Mienshao particularly fits on bulky offense and balance playstyles where its ability to revenge kill faster Pokemon that they might not have many defensive answers to, like Iron Boulder, is appreciated. These teams value Mienshao because it provides speed control, doesn't mind entry hazards, and is an effective late-game cleaner that can maintain momentum mid-game. Since Choice Scarf Mienshao lacks significant power, hazards from teammates like Jirachi, Hippowdon, and Skarmory are much appreciated to help wear down its checks like Mega Venusaur and Buzzwole. It is also quite frail, so it needs pivot support from Pokemon like Slowbro and Rotom-W. While Mienshao functions as an effective revenge killer, it’s still vulnerable to priority users like Rillaboom, Scizor, and Lokix; therefore, it appreciates defensive Pokemon that can respond to these foes like Skarmory and Mega Venusaur.

ru.overview: An incredible Attack stat, offensive typing, and unique coverage options give Golurk a niche as a strong wallbreaker that can dismantle common defensive staples, such as Slowbro, Gastrodon, and Hisuian Goodra. Golurk bears the coveted combination of Dynamic Punch and No Guard, deterring Dark-types like Bisharp and Umbreon from switching in. This, combined with Golurk's Ghost typing, helps it deter Cyclizar from using Rapid Spin for fear of giving it a switch in opportunity, making it a solid option for entry hazard stacking teams as a spinblocker and Stealth Rock setter. Golurk's downfall comes in its terrible Speed and middling bulk, leaving it 2HKOed by a myriad of faster threats, such as Gardevoir, Entei, and Noivern. Golurk's strongest STAB attack, Poltergeist, cannot be used if the target's item is removed by Knock Off, making it somewhat difficult to build around. While its typing is excellent offensively, it also saddles Golurk with a number of common weaknesses, particularly to Water, Ghost, and Dark, with Knock Off being of particular concern. This leaves Golurk vulnerable to many of the tier's premier offensive threats, such as Basculegion-F, Gengar, Krookodile, and Crawdaunt. Golurk also struggles to 2HKO prominent walls like Chesnaught and Gastrodon without the use of Choice Band or Life Orb; the former risks offering the opposing team free switches in by locking Golurk into one move, while the latter's chip damage leaves it even more vulnerable to being KOed by the aforementioned attackers.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Leftovers lets Golurk trade power or insurance against Dark-type attacks for sustainability, especially if it opts to run Substitute. A Choice Scarf set can be used to shore up Golurk's low Speed, letting it outspeed offensive checks like Krookodile and non-Choice Scarf Basculegion-F. Close Combat is a stronger alternative to Dynamic Punch that lets Golurk guarantee an OHKO against Moxie Krookodile and a 2HKO against Wo-Chien without the use of a damage-boosting item, though its lack of a positive secondary effect makes Dynamic Punch more preferable otherwise. Golurk can forgo No Guard for Iron Fist in conjunction with Shadow Punch and Ice Punch; the former is a more reliable, if weaker, STAB move that makes it easier for Golurk's teammates to use Knock Off, whereas the latter guarantees an OHKO on Noivern while also dealing extra damage to Chesnaught. If running Choice Band, Golurk can opt to run Trick in order to lure in and cripple defensive checks, like Quagsire and Chesnaught. Trick can also be used with Klutz and a detrimental item, like Toxic Orb, Flame Orb, or Assault Vest, as an alternative method of crippling its defensive checks; however, Golurk becomes unable to run an item if it runs Klutz, making this option somewhat risky.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Offensive Water-types like Feraligatr and Barraskewda are able to comfortably outspeed Golurk before KOing it with their STAB moves. However, they all struggle to switch in on Golurk's powerful attacks. If Golurk is running Colbur Berry, bulky Water-types like Suicune and Vaporeon are able to avoid being 2HKOed by its attacks and threaten it with Scald.

Ghost-types: Basculegion-F and Gengar are able to outrun Golurk and OHKO it with Shadow Ball, though they must be careful of switching in, especially Gengar due to its weakness to Earthquake. Mimikyu is capable of taking a hit from Golurk thanks to Disguise, letting it set up with Swords Dance to guarantee an OHKO with Shadow Claw.

Physical Walls: Without Choice Band, Golurk is unable to 2HKO physical walls like Chesnaught and Gastrodon, both of whom are able to heal off the damage while wearing it down. Chesnaught, in particular, is able to threaten non-Colbur Berry variants with Knock Off, letting it take Golurk's attacks easier. Gligar is unable to be 2HKOed by even Choice Band Golurk's attacks, though it struggles to repeatedly switch in due to its lack of reliable recovery.

Strong Wallbreakers: Golurk's lacking Speed and bulk leave it vulnerable to being OHKOed or 2HKOed by many of the tier's prominent wallbreakers, such as Gardevoir, Krookodile, and Crawdaunt, though its high power deters many of them from switching in freely.

Wallbreaker.description:
Set Details

Golurk is a niche but effective wallbreaker in the tier, using its powerful STAB moves and coverage options to blow holes through defensive cores with ease. Dynamic Punch, with the accuracy assurance granted by No Guard, allows Golurk to disrupt foes that otherwise wall it and hits Dark-types like Umbreon and Krookodile super effectively. Stone Edge can be used to hit Flying-types like Noivern and Kilowattrel for massive damage. Substitute allows Golurk to scout, such as for a switch-in or status attempt from Umbreon, safely while also disrupting Sucker Punch from slower Bisharp. Stealth Rock sets are quite effective at establishing entry hazards, as Golurk can threaten common hazard removal options like Cyclizar and Noivern. Choice Band allows Golurk to threaten 2HKOs on foes like Gastrodon, Quagsire, and Chesnaught with Stealth Rock chip damage. Life Orb can be used to still hit the Gastrodon 2HKO benchmark without needing to lock into an attack. With a Colbur Berry or Tera Ground and the allocated HP investment, Golurk can take a Golurk can take a Sucker Punch from +2 Bisharp and Knock Off from Choice Band Krookodile. 136 Speed EVs ensure that Golurk outpaces maximum Speed Rhyperior. No Guard allows Golurk to use its most powerful moves without the risk of missing. The Speed investment allows Golurk to outpace Wo-Chien and uninvested Bisharp. Tera Ground removes the weaknesses to Dark and Ghost while pushing the damage output of Earthquake to near unwallable levels, securing a 2HKO on physically defensive Umbreon with Life Orb and after Stealth Rock chip damage. Tera Fighting similarly flips the weakness to Dark, helping non-Colbur Berry sets more effectively take on Bisharp and Krookodile while also increasing the damage of Dynamic Punch enough for Life Orb sets to OHKO Umbreon.

With a potent offensive STAB combination of Ghost / Ground, Golurk is an excellent wallbreaker on balance and offense teams. Choice Band sets work best when given safe entry points against walls like Gastrodon and Slowbro, making teammates like Cyclizar, Jirachi, and Noivern important to lure them in and allow Golurk to fire off its powerful attacks. Empoleon and Jirachi are notable teammates for Golurk for their ability to use Stealth Rock so Golurk can opt to run more offensive sets. Life Orb Golurk is susceptible to getting worn down by its own recoil and chip damage, making teammates like Healing Wish Gardevoir and Wish Umbreon especially valuable to maintain its health. Defensively, Golurk appreciates teammates like Cyclizar and Slowbro, as they can sponge the powerful Ghost- and Water-type attacks thrown at it from foes like Basculegion-F, Gengar, and Barraskewda. Offensive teams that rely on Sticky Web support from Ribombee can slow foes like Magnezone and Hisuian Goodra down enough to let Golurk wallbreak more efficiently, though it does activate Defiant on Bisharp, meaning Sticky Web teams should opt for a Colbur Berry to ensure Golurk can survive the Sucker Punch to remove a powerful threat. Substitute Golurk can afford to use Life Orb, especially on Sticky Web teams where it can bait the Sucker Punch from Bisharp and then throw out powerful attacks uncontested, as well as on teams that can give it safe entry points against slower foes like Registeel and Slowbro often.

Choice Band.description:
Golurk is a potent wallbreaker with limited switch-ins thanks to its incredible STAB combination, which is resisted by only a few Pokemon in the tier. Golurk excels at dismantling common defensive cores thanks to its high Attack and great typing, which let it switch into and force out defensive staples like Galarian Slowbro and Calm Mind Florges. Dynamic Punch lets Golurk 2HKO Wo-Chien while also hitting other Dark- and Normal-types like Alolan Persian and Porygon2 and threatening confusion against everything else. Close Combat can be used as an alternative due to its higher Base Power, which lets it guarantee a 2HKO on Wo-Chien after Leech Seed recovery; however, Golurk misses out on the confusion, and the Defense and Special Defense drops make it more susceptible to being revenge killed. Ice Punch lets Golurk OHKO Bombirdier while also serving as a good middle ground into foes like Brute Bonnet. Stone Edge can be used as an alternative that's stronger versus neutral targets and has a higher chance to land a critical hit. Tera Dark flips Golurk's Ghost and Dark weaknesses while also removing its Water and Ice weaknesses, allowing it to avoid revenge kill attempts from Pokemon like Skuntank, Heracross, and opposing Golurk. Tera Ghost can be used instead to further boost Golurk's power, letting it 2HKO Pokemon like Mudsdale and guaranteeing OHKOs against Pokemon like Rotom-Heat with Poltergeist while still removing its susceptibility to Water- and Ice-type moves to avoid revenge killing attempts from Pokemon like Bruxish and Ice Punch Pawmot.

Golurk works best alongside Pokemon that benefit from its wallbreaking abilities such as Choice Scarf Bruxish and Grimmsnarl, which struggle with Milotic and Mudsdale, respectively. While Golurk has the coverage to hit the likes of Bombirdier, Wo-Chien, and Brute Bonnet, their presence on the opposing team hurts its ability to freely use its STAB moves and forces it to make more predictions, so teammates that can handle these Pokemon like defensive Florges, which checks Bombirdier, and Paldean Tauros-F, which helps against Wo-Chien and Brute Bonnet, make excellent partners. Furthermore, Paldean Tauros-F offensively and defensively checks the Dark-types that threaten Golurk, and other Fighting-types like Pawmot and Hisuian Decidueye are similarly good partners for this purpose. Golurk is also forced out by Water- and Grass-types, so teammates that can switch into these Pokemon, like Milotic for Tatsugiri as well as Skuntank for Choice Scarf Hoopa, are incredible partners for Golurk.

Stealth Rock.description:
Golurk can leverage its usable bulk, defensive and offensive typing, and more importantly, its great power to become one of few good offensive Stealth Rock users. This set is also good at bluffing Choice Band, which can be taken advantage of when setting up Stealth Rock. Ice Punch is optimal coverage for Golurk on this set, letting it hit Pokemon like Bombirdier, which would otherwise be a great check to Golurk. Dynamic Punch is also an option for its higher Base Power, super effective damage against Fighting-weak Pokemon like Wo-Chien and Snorlax, and disruptive confusion spreading. Colbur Berry's main draw is reversing Golurk's matchup against Dark-types like Skuntank and Zoroark, always tanking a Knock Off from them while OHKOing back with Earthquake. The Speed EVs lets Golurk outspeed uninvested Alolan Sandslash, while the bulk investment lets it take two unboosted hits from Rotom-Heat and three from defensive Florges. Tera Dark sheds Golurk's many weaknesses and even turns some of them, like Dark and Ghost, into resistances; namely, it lets it check Ghost-types like Hoopa as well as Dark-types like Zoroark and Hisuian Qwilfish after its Colbur Berry has been used up.

As an offensive Stealth Rock user, Golurk should be used on more offensive teams that do not want to lose momentum from their entry hazard user and not hyper offense teams that rely on leads like Lycanroc and Froslass to get their entry hazards up. Offensive pivots that can bring Golurk in, like Ambipom and Hisuian Electrode are great for this, bringing Golurk in on their switch-ins like Galarian Slowbro and Alolan Sandslash; in return, Golurk provides a way to break past them as well as entry hazards to help wear these switch-ins down. Golurk also appreciates defensive partners that help it deal with Dark-types, such as Hisuian Decidueye and Choice Scarf Florges, which are great at forcing out the likes of Wo-Chien. Bulky Water- and Grass-types like Cramorant and Venusaur to switch into opposing Water- and Grass-types that force Golurk out are also appreciated; Cramorant can also spread paralysis to help Golurk outspeed its offensive checks. Fire-types like Rotom-Heat and Hisuian Typhlosion are good partners, as they can easily pressure Grass-types that threaten Golurk, like Venusaur and Amoonguss. Being a slow bulky Pokemon with no recovery, Golurk naturally struggles against revenge killers like Hoopa and Tastugiri, so speed control that can offensively check these Pokemon like Choice Scarf Zoroark and Heracross are greatly appreciated.

nu.overview: Golurk can be difficult to switch into for balance teams due to its complementary STAB moves and enormous Attack, allowing it to dispose of defensive staples such as Bronzong, Duraludon, and Incineroar. Among Ghost-types, it's unique for its ability to blow past Dark-types such as Overqwil and Scrafty with Earthquake or Close Combat, and this Ghost typing allows it to act as a spinblocker to help keep up the pressure against the opposing team. However, Golurk is weak to the most common spinner, Tsareena, and can't OHKO it; therefore, Golurk requires teammates to help chip it beforehand and not give it too many free switch-ins. Not to mention, Golurk competes with Houndstone and Flygon, two top-tier threats; Houndstone is a better spinblocker, since it more effectively checks Tsareena, especially long-term, and Flygon is simply more flexible as an offensive Ground-type thanks to its movepool and Speed. Furthermore, Brambleghast is yet another spinblocker better than Golurk, since it isn't threatened by Water-types like Vaporeon while being faster than Golurk and having access to utility moves like Spikes, Strength Sap, and Leech Seed. Additionally, Golurk's attacks, while indeed strong, often fail to achieve 2HKOs against bulkier foes like Vaporeon and Gligar without entry hazard chip damage or a damage multiplier like Spell Tag, Choice Band, or Tera Ghost.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Colbur Berry lets Golurk take a Dark-type attack like Knock Off from Grafaiai or Throat Chop from Overqwil so that it can throw off an Earthquake. However, this trashes any chance of Golurk being an effective wallbreaker. Golurk can opt for a Choice Scarf to surprise faster foes with its high-Base Power attacks. However, as a Choice Scarf user, it's often too slow, and after its item has been revealed, it falls short of expectations at times. Trick can be used on Choice item sets, though Golurk struggles to fit the move in its moveset. In a similar vein, Knock Off offers great utility to Golurk, yet it has problems running the move due to needing most of its moveslots for STAB moves and coverage. Golurk can run Klutz with the move Trick while carrying items like Assault Vest and Sticky Barb to cripple walls that would switch in against it such as Tsareena, Gligar, and Vaporeon.

Checks and Counters

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Any decently bulky physical wall or tank not weak to Golurk's STAB attacks, like Dudunsparce, Gligar, Swampert, Vaporeon, Tsareena, or Wo-Chien, works great as a stopgap to Golurk, sapping away all of its momentum. On top of that, many of these Pokemon can set entry hazards, have pivoting moves, or carry progress-making moves like Knock Off to place the pressure back on Golurk and its teammates.

Ghost- and Dark-types: Ghost- and Dark-types faster than Golurk like Chandelure, Houndstone, and Overqwil threaten to KO it with their STAB attacks, either forcing Golurk to give up its Terastallization or hand over a free turn for them to set up or wallbreak. However, switching in against Golurk is quite problematic for them, with Golurk's STAB attacks able to OHKO all of them.

Grass- and Water-types: Many Grass- and Water-type Pokemon are simply faster than Golurk, such as Inteleon, Paldean Tauros-W, Basculegion-M, Tsareena, and Brambleghast. What's worse is that they threaten to KO it, too, forcing Golurk to sacrifice itself or a teammate to their attacks. More defensive Pokemon such as Vaporeon and Amoonguss are just as problematic, as they can tank Golurk's attacks with ease if it doesn't have anything boosting its damage output like Choice Band, Spell Tag, or Tera Ghost.

Wallbreaker.description:
Set Details

Both Dynamic Punch and Close Combat are used to target the main stopgaps to Golurk's powerful STAB attacks, namely Wo-Chien, Brute Bonnet, and Dudunsparce. Dynamic Punch capitalizes on Golurk's No Guard to confuse foes, helping against offensive switch-ins like Paldean Tauros-W and Flygon, whereas Close Combat uses its sheer power to break through these walls. Ice Punch hits common physical walls like Tsareena, Gligar, and Altaria. Spell Tag powers up Poltergeist to 2HKO Amoonguss from full HP, 2HKO Vaporeon after Stealth Rock chip damage, and have a 50% chance to OHKO Flygon from full HP. Choice Band can be used instead, though, for outright wallbreaking, letting Golurk 2HKO Vaporeon without entry hazard chip damage, have a 75% chance to OHKO Wo-Chien after Stealth Rock with Close Combat, and have a favorable roll to 2HKO Gligar with Poltergeist. This can ease move selection at times. The EV spread ensures Golurk outpaces defensive Tsareena so that Golurk effectively spinblocks it. Tera Ghost amps up Poltergeist to 2HKO defensive Tsareena, Vaporeon, and, with Spell Tag, Swampert. Alternatively, Tera Fighting offers Golurk a Dark resistance so that it can take a Crunch from Overqwil or a Knock Off from a speedy Incineroar while also boosting Dynamic Punch and Close Combat. This boost means the former can always 2HKO Wo-Chien and the latter can OHKO Dudunsparce 75% of the time after Stealth Rock. However, Tera Dark offers more defensive benefits, namely allowing Golurk to take an incoming Shadow Ball or Poltergeist and revenge kill Ghost-type foes like Chandelure and Houndstone. In addition, it maintains the Dark resistance from Tera Fighting, helping it versus Incineroar and Brute Bonnet.

Munkidori, Tornadus, and Scyther are all fast pivots that enjoy Golurk's presence, since it can handle common switch-ins for them such as Bronzong, Rhyperior, and Bellibolt. In return, they can take care of Grass-types like Brambleghast and Tsareena that threaten Golurk. Especially as a Choice Band wallbreaker, Golurk is great at weakening defensive Water-, Ground-, and Grass-types such as Swampert, Gligar, and Tsareena. This leads it to synergize well with Incineroar, Galarian Articuno, and Paldean Tauros-W, which enjoy these foes being easier to KO. Partners that can immediately take advantage of the situation at hand are appreciated as well, such as Toxicroak beating Vaporeon, Swords Dance Flamigo capitalizing on Gligar, and Overqwil threatening Wo-Chien. Golurk's lackluster Speed also necessitates that it be paired with some form of speed control; often, this comes in the form of Choice Scarf users like Flamigo and Munkidori that enjoy Golurk's ability to take out their switch-ins, namely Bellibolt and Duraludon. Speed control can come in the form of paralysis-spreading Pokemon, too, though, causing the likes of Thunder Wave Klefki and Duraludon as well as Static Bellibolt to be found beside Golurk.

Entry Hazard Lead (Ghost).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Swords Dance.description:
Pawniard is a solid defensive Pokemon with the potential to win games. Swords Dance can be used against Pokemon such as on Vullaby, Gastly, and Snubbull. Sucker Punch is a strong STAB priority move that allows Pawniard to hit foes that would otherwise outspeed it such as Gastly and Snivy. Tera Flying lets Pawniard beat common Fighting- and Ground-types such as Mienfoo, Mudbray, and Trapinch that would otherwise stop its sweep; Tera Blast cleaves through common Pokemon such as the aforementioned Mienfoo and Foongus. Inner Focus is preferred over Defiant to avoid being flinched by Mienfoo's Fake Out, especially after Terastallizing.

Pawniard's presence helps deal with Gothita, assisting teammates such as Foongus, Mienfoo, and Timburr. Vullaby works well with Pawniard due to Pawniard's good matchup against both Snubbull and Glimmet. Mienfoo can U-turn into Pawniard and is a great partner for luring in Vullaby and Snubbull. While Pawniard can Terastallize to remove its Fighting weakness, teammates such as Snubbull, Koffing, and Gothita help against Mienfoo and Timburr without needing to Terastallize themsleves. Snubbull can also help Pawniard set up with Intimidate.

Stealth Rock.description:
Pawniard is a solid utility Pokemon, pairing its excellent typing that allows it to check common Pokemon like Vullaby with its useful support options in Stealth Rock and Thunder Wave. Thunder Wave keeps Pawniard from being too passive, and it combines well with Iron Head to paraflinch opposing Pokemon. Iron Head lets Pawniard hit both Mienfoo and Vullaby for neutral damage. Sucker Punch is a strong priority move that can pick off setup sweepers such as Shell Smash Shellder or Choice Scarf users like Hisuian Growlithe. Pawniard's EV spread gives it the bulk it needs to handle the aforementioned threats while keeping itself fast and strong enough to deal damage on its own. Pawniard struggles with Fighting- and Ground-type moves from Pokemon like Mienfoo and Mudbray respectively, so Pawniard can use Tera Flying to turn these attacks into a resistance and an immunity, respectively.

Pawniard can complement Vullaby-weak Pokemon such as Foongus, which struggle to deal with Vullaby's STAB moves, with Foongus being able to check Mienfoo, which gives Pawniard trouble. Slow and strong wallbreakers such as Mudbray and Eviolite Hisuian Growlithe can take advantage of Thunder Wave from Pawniard to become more threatening when opposing Pokemon are outpaced by them.

ru.overview: Bisharp stands out as one of the premier setup sweepers in the metagame due its access to Swords Dance, strong priority in Sucker Punch, and impressive Eviolite-boosted bulk. Coupled with a fantastic defensive typing, Bisharp's bulk allows it to tank attacks from some of the most common Pokemon in the tier, including Cyclizar, Noivern, and Jirachi, and use the turn to set up or strike back with its nigh-unresisted STAB combination. Sucker Punch elevates Bisharp into an incredibly threatening late-game cleaner after just one or two turns to set up, which Bisharp can easily gain through Terastallization. However, Bisharp suffers from a mediocre Speed stat that makes it slower than most other offensive threats and sweepers even with maximum Speed investment. The common Fighting-types in RU, including the likes of Terrakion and Flamigo, are therefore able to comfortably outspeed and KO Bisharp while taking little damage from Sucker Punch. Physical walls such as Gastrodon and Chesnaught can similarly tank Bisharp's attacks and strike back with super effective attacks. Lastly, Bisharp often finds itself wanting in terms of special bulk even with Eviolite, and it can often be taken out by strong special wallbreakers after minimal chip damage.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Low Kick is a coverage option that can be used over Throat Chop to threaten opposing Bisharp, Registeel, and Crawdaunt more effectively. Tera Ghost gives Bisharp an immunity to Fighting, which can give it a free turn to set up against Fighting-type threats like Breloom and Terrakion. The Ghost typing is particularly synergistic with Bisharp, as both of its weaknesses are naturally resisted by Bisharp, and it allows Bisharp to act as a spinblocker in a pinch for entry hazard stacking teams. However, Tera Ghost makes Bisharp weak to Knock Off, which can be very dangerous because it also neuters its bulk by removing Eviolite. Tera Fairy is another option that provides valuable resistances to Fighting-, Dark-, and Bug-type attacks from the aforementioned Fighting-types.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: A myriad of Fighting-type wallbreakers, from common presences like Breloom and Terrakion to niche picks like Lucario and Infernape, can comfortably tank even a +2 Sucker Punch and threaten Bisharp in turn with a KO. Chesnaught is a defensive Fighting-type that can reliably check Bisharp with its high physical bulk. However, all of these Pokemon should be wary of Terastallization, which can give Bisharp free turns to set up against them and potentially turn it into a game-ending threat.

Physical Walls: Certain physical walls, including Chesnaught, Quagsire, and Body Press Registeel, are able to tank Bisharp's attacks and threaten it with super effective attacks. Besides Chesnaught, they are usually unafraid of Terastallization due to their access to Unaware and Iron Defense, respectively, that can neutralize Bisharp's ability to set up.

Special Wallbreakers: Strong, bulky special attackers such as Magnezone and Choice Specs Hisuian Goodra are able to threaten Bisharp by targeting its middling special bulk. Magnet Pull Magnezone in particular can trap and eliminate Bisharp if it switches in safely.

Burn: Due to Bisharp's low Speed, it is prone to getting outsped and crippled by fast Will-O-Wisp users including Gengar. While Entei does not appreciate taking a +2 Sucker Punch, Sacred Fire from it can cripple even a Terastallized Bisharp.

Swords Dance.description:
Set Details

Swords Dance allows Bisharp to serve as a fantastic late-game sweeper. Sucker Punch provides strong priority that enables Bisharp to pick off weakened sweepers like Gengar and improves its ability to clean. Eviolite drastically boosts Bisharp's ability to take hits, which can be invaluable for setting up. Defiant deters opposing Pokemon from using Defog and can potentially turn Bisharp into a deadly threat simply by getting Intimidated by Krookodile or switching into and receiving a stat drop from an attack like Gengar's Shadow Ball. 176 Speed EVs allow Bisharp to outspeed Modest Magnezone. Tera Flying flips Bisharp's matchup against Ground- and Fighting-type attacks, allowing it to stay in on Pokemon such as Krookodile, Terrakion, and Breloom and use the turn to set up or grab a KO. Tera Dark is an option that instead boosts two of Bisharp's STAB attacks, which can be helpful for guaranteeing certain KOs such as unboosted Sucker Punch against Basculegion-F and +2 Throat Chop against Empoleon.

Swords Dance Bisharp is able to reliably fill the role of a bulky revenge killer and late-game sweeper on both balance and offense structures. Entry hazard stacking teams, with setters such as Krookodile, Jirachi, and Chesnaught, are able to gradually bring the opposing team into range of Bisharp's attacks by wearing them down, thus easing its job as a cleaner. At the same time, Bisharp fills the role of deterring Defog from users like Noivern. Offense, particularly hyper offense, teams can similarly take advantage of Defiant, as hazards like Stealth Rock and Sticky Web set by Pokemon such as Kleavor and Ribombee are likely to stick around. Other setup sweepers like Gengar, Terrakion, and Mimikyu work well with Bisharp, as they can weaken or take out defensive Pokemon such as Hisuian Goodra, Slowbro, and Gastrodon and improve Bisharp's odds of sweeping. Bisharp is simultaneously able to serve as a revenge killer due to its access to Sucker Punch, which can be instrumental in hyper offense mirror matchups for taking care of threats like Maushold and Gardevoir after they are weakened. A Ghost-type like Mimikyu or Weakness Policy Basculegion-F is also appreciated in these teams to block Rapid Spin from Cyclizar. Lastly, any of the fast Fighting-types in RU, such as Flamigo and Terrakion, can easily tank a Sucker Punch and threaten Bisharp with an OHKO. Therefore, teammates that resist Fighting like Noivern, Slowbro, and Amoonguss can be invaluable partners for Bisharp in bulkier structures to prevent these wallbreakers from making too much progress.

Swords Dance Bisharp is a fearsome wallbreaker and sweeper, utilizing its powerful STAB combination and decent defensive profile to threaten notable defensive staples such as Clefable, Aegislash, and Amoonguss. Besides serving as Bisharp's strongest STAB option to use against neutral targets such as Rotom-W, Celesteela, and Skarmory, Knock Off also comes with the benefit of removing held items from common switch-ins such as Buzzwole and Keldeo, which allows Bisharp to more easily break past them later. Sucker Punch is a powerful priority move that lets Bisharp threaten more offensive teams, notably KOing common attackers such as Iron Boulder and Mega Gardevoir after minimal chip damage or Swords Dance, respectively. Iron Head is Bisharp's strongest STAB option against Mega Venusaur, common Z-Move users such as Hydrapple, and Fairy-types like Clefable. An Adamant nature maximizes Bisharp's power, securing 2HKOs on physically defensive Pokemon such as Tangrowth and Hippowdon after Swords Dance. Alternatively, a Jolly nature lets Bisharp get the jump on faster Rotom-W variants as well as Aegislash with a Speed-boosting nature. Life Orb is Bisharp's item of choice for powering up all of its moves, ensuring that +2 Knock Off can OHKO the bulkiest Rotom-W while giving +2 Iron Head good odds to OHKO offensive Mega Venusaur after Stealth Rock. Alternatively, Black Glasses forfeits the added power on Iron Head in favor of avoiding recoil damage; it should be noted that the power boost it provides on Bisharp's Dark-type attacks can still be crucial, notably allowing it to secure the OHKO on Mega Gallade, Mega Aerodactyl, and utility Excadrill with +2 Sucker Punch. Finally, Eviolite can be used if the added power of the aforementioned options isn't a concern. The added defensive security lets Bisharp survive attacks such as Enamorus's Earth Power and Choice Scarf Hydreigon's Fire Blast from full HP. Additionally, if Bisharp runs the alternative EV spread, it can also take on Excadrill's Earthquake after Stealth Rock and Iron Moth's Fiery Dance while still outpacing Adamant Tyranitar. With its combination of offensive traits, powerful priority, and typing, Bisharp fits on a variety of offense and hyper offense teams. Entry hazard setters such as Mold Breaker Excadrill, Swampert, and Mew make for excellent pairings, as their ability to accrue chip damage on physically bulky Pokemon such as Skarmory and Tangrowth can help a boosted Bisharp break through them more easily; in return, Bisharp can use Defiant ability to capitalize on Defog from utility Serperior and Rotom-W, forcing them into uncomfortable situations. By extension, Ribombee is also a notable partner, as its Sticky Web support can let Bisharp outpace targets such as Life Orb Mienshao and Booster Energy Iron Moth, preventing them from being effective offensive checks. Other setup sweepers such as Autotomize Celesteela, Dragon Dance Mega Aerodactyl, and Swords Dance users such as Aegislash and Scizor work well with Bisharp: in tandem, they can assist each other in overwhelming shared defensive checks such as Buzzwole and Hippowdon. Against more offensive teams, Aegislash and Scizor can also use their own priority attacks to weaken faster Pokemon like Keldeo, Hydreigon, and Okidogi to the pointwhere Bisharp can pick them off with Sucker Punch more easily.

Pursuit Trapper.description: With its good defensive typing and powerful Dark-type attacks, Bisharp is a prime user of Pursuit, able to trap offensive threats like Aegislash and Choice Band Iron Boulder as well as weakened defensive Pokemon like Slowking and Skeledirge. Notably, Bisharp also gains an Attack boost from Aegislash's King's Shield, courtesy of Defiant, making Bisharp much more reliable at trapping Aegislash as a result. Knock Off is Bisharp's strongest STAB option, and it removes held items, permanently crippling Dark-type checks such as Keldeo and Buzzwole. Sucker Punch is a strong priority move that lets Bisharp threaten chipped offensive Pokemon such as Iron Moth, Thundurus, and Zeraora, and it can also OHKO Swords Dance Iron Boulder from full. Additionally, even though Psychic-type Pokemon like Mega Latias and Alakazam have the means to naturally outspeed and threaten Bisharp with Fighting-type coverage, the threat of being KOed by Sucker Punch in doing so means Bisharp can potentially Pursuit trap them as well. Iron Head provides Bisharp with a strong secondary STAB move that hits Fairy-type Pokemon like Clefable and Azumarill as well as other Pokemon that don't mind taking a Knock Off, like Mega Venusaur, for decent damage. Choice Band further inflates Bisharp's huge Attack stat, making it more difficult to check with Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Hippowdon while giving Bisharp an easier time eliminating bulkier targets like Aegislash and Slowbro with Pursuit. Maximum Attack and Speed investment in conjunction with an Adamant nature is used with Choice Band to make Bisharp as fast and strong as possible. However, a Jolly nature trades a portion of said attacking power in favor of outspeeding faster Rotom-W variants as well as Aegislash and Magnezone with Speed-boosting natures. On sets with Eviolite, an alternative EV spread of 52 HP / 244 Atk / 28 SpD / 184 Spe should be used to let Bisharp survive Excadrill's Earthquake after Stealth Rock and Iron Moth's Fiery Dance while still outpacing Adamant Tyranitar. Pursuit Bisharp is best used on bulky offense and balance teams as an offensive threat that also provides valuable utility against Aegislash as well as Psychic-types like Choice Band Iron Boulder, Slowbro, and Slowking, preventing them from making excessive progress throughout the match. Wallbreakers such as Mega Gardevoir, Keldeo, and Iron Moth benefit the most from this support, as Aegislash and several of the aforementioned Psychic-types are often used to answer them in some form. Bisharp removing these threats allows these wallbreakers to become far more offensively threatening, and in return, they can help Bisharp pressure physically defensive checks such as Buzzwole and Skarmory. While Bisharp possesses a strong Sucker Punch to threaten more offensive foes, it can also be quite unreliable, being resisted by common offensive threats such as Mienshao, Enamorus, and Keldeo, and it's easily taken advantage of by setup sweepers like Autotomize Celesteela and Booster Energy Iron Moth. For this reason, Bisharp pairs fantastically with speed control options such as Mega Aerodactyl, Zeraora, and Choice Scarf users like Enamorus that can help check these Pokemon. Lastly, defensive pivots such as Scizor, Rotom-W, and Slowbro are integral to Bisharp's success, allowing it to enter the field safely against its desired targets. Safe entry is especially important when factoring in how some of Bisharp's targets like Aegislash and Slowbro have the means to outright KO or cripple it with Close Combat and Scald burns, respectively, before it can be Pursuit trap them.

monotype.overview:
Dark

Bisharp's Steel typing makes it an inviting piece for Dark teams looking to ease the Fairy matchup, as Bisharp can take on powerful Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Hatterene. In addition, its Defiant deters Defog from the likes of Corviknight and Galarian Weezing. However, Bisharp's middling Speed tier and mediocre bulk make it unable to switch into Fairy-type threats such as Enamorus and Mimikyu, and it needs a Swords Dance boost to reliably OHKO them. It is also helpless against Iron Valiant and other fast Fighting-types. The Defog users that Bisharp wishes to check like the aforementioned Corviknight and Galarian Weezing can similarly threaten Bisharp on a predicted switch with Body Press and Will-O-Wisp, respectively.

Eviolite Swords Dance (Steel).description:
When paired with an Eviolite, Bisharp is capable of taking on the role of a bulky setup sweeper that also discourages the use of Defog. Additonally, Bisharp's Dark typing allows Eviolite to ease the matchup against Ghost teams by letting Bisharp take on their Ghost-type STAB moves better with its improved bulk. Throat Chop serves as its primary Dark-type STAB move and deals great damage to bulkier threats like Sinistcha and Gholdengo. Sucker Punch boosted by Swords Dance allows Bisharp to KO faster Pokemon like Dragapult, Hoopa-U, and Choice item Spectrier, while Low Kick allows it to threaten opposing Bisharp as well as doing good damage to Ting-Lu and defensive Heatran. Iron Head can also be ran as an option over Low Kick to shut down certain Fairy-types like Primarina and Clefable, which would otherwise check Bisharp. 80 HP and 20 Defense EVs paired with Eviolite allow Bisharp to avoid getting 2HKOed by Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel and survive a Belly Drum-boosted Azumarill's Aqua Jet and an Earthquake from most common Garchomp sets. 176 Speed EV allows Bisharp to outspeed Modest Magnezone.

Skarmory is one of Bisharp's greatest allies, as it can defensively switch into Ground- and Fighting-types like Excadrill, Great Tusk, and Urshifu-R easily. Skarmory also sets Spikes, which chips down walls like Hippowdon and Archaludon into Bisharp's KO range and makes picking off frailer Pokemon with Sucker Punch easier. Gholdengo can check scary Fairy-types like Iron Valiant while also absorbing hits from threats like Sneasler and Hisuian Lilligant without risk thanks to Good as Gold blocking a potential Switcheroo or Sleep Powder, respectively. In return, Bisharp can remove opposing Ghost-types like opposing Gholdengo and Choice Scarf Hisuian Zoroark. Heatran is a great partner for Bisharp, as its Fire immunity allows it to take on threats like Volcarona, Iron Moth, and Ninetales while also being able to wear down or KO physical walls like Skarmory, Amoonguss, and Toxapex. Archaludon's utility allows Bisharp to break through its foes more easily with Stealth Rock while also letting it outspeed crucial Pokemon like the Ogerpon formes and Enamorus with Thunder Wave. Archaludon can also use Choice Scarf to help remove checks to Bisharp like Iron Valiant and wear down faster threats like Ogerpon-H so that they are in Bisharp's KO range. Iron Treads's access to Rapid Spin allows Bisharp to not get worn down by entry hazards, and it also checks potential threats to Bisharp like opposing Heatran and Landorus with Earthquake and Ice Spinner.

Eviolite Swords Dance (Dark).description:
Bisharp's extra bulk provided by Eviolite allows it to lure in unsuspecting checks to the non-Eviolite Bisharp set such as Ogerpon-H and Choice Specs Flutter Mane and set up on them with Swords Dance or KO them outright. Furthermore, its Steel typing is incredibly valuable, as it enables it to take Fairy-type attacks for its teammates while also hitting Fairy-types very hard with its own Steel-type STAB move. Defiant allows Bisharp to fulfill its role as a Defog dissuader and also punish the use of Sticky Web from the likes of Galvantula and Araquanid. Throat Chop, when paired with Swords Dance, deals great damage to bulkier threats like Raging Bolt. Sucker Punch lets Bisharp KO fast Pokemon like Dragapult, Hoopa-U, and Choice item Spectrier, while Iron Head removes Fairy-types like Primarina and Hatterene. 80 HP and 20 Defense EVs allow Bisharp to avoid a 2HKO from Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel and survive an Earthquake from non-Choice Band Mamoswine. 176 Speed EVs allow Bisharp to outspeed maximum Speed Modest Magnezone while also surviving Azumarill's boosted Aqua Jet thanks to the bulk granted by Eviolite.

Bisharp appreciates Spikes setters like Ting-Lu and Hisuian Samurott, as the chip damage allows it to break through bulkier targets like Archaludon and Hippowdon more easily. Both Spikes setters also help Bisharp break through the aforementioned walls by wearing them down with Ruination and Sacred Sword. Strong special attackers like Greninja and Darkrai help Bisharp by breaking down physical walls like Skarmory and defensive Great Tusk while also using their high Speed and Psychic-type coverage to remove Fighting-types like Iron Valiant and Keldeo. Sableye acts as a good defensive switch-in to Fighting-type attacks and spreads burns to physical Fighting-type attackers like Sneasler and Iron Hands. Additionally, Sableye crucially can burn Skarmory, which prevents Bisharp from being OHKOed by its Body Press. Sableye also utilizes Encore to disrupt opposing setup attempts, granting Bisharp the ability to safely switch in. Meowscarada can use its Protean-boosted Triple Axel or Play Rough to check speedy threats like Roaring Moon while also breaking through bulkier Pokemon like Great Tusk and Swampert. Mandibuzz acts as a great support for Bisharp, as it can take Fighting- and Ground-type attacks easily thanks to its part-Flying typing, use Defog to remove entry hazards, and pivot with U-turn to get Bisharp safely onto the field. Alolan Muk acts as a good special sponge that can take hits from Enamorus and Kyurem while using Knock Off to remove items like Choice Specs, allowing Bisharp to handle them better with its Eviolite-boosted bulk.

Swords Dance (Dark).description:
Bisharp serves a niche role on Dark teams with its secondary Steel typing and Defiant ability enabling it to take on the bulky Calm Mind Fairy-types of the tier such as Primarina and Clefable and punish Defog from the likes of Mandibuzz or Sticky Web from Araquanid or Galvantula, respectively. At +2 Attack, Iron Head can OHKO Fairy-types such as Hatterene, Galarian Weezing, and Clefable. Throat Chop enables Bisharp to dish out immense damage to the likes of Skarmory and Toxapex. Lastly, Sucker Punch helps mitigate Bisharp's low Speed, allowing it to check threats such as Flutter Mane and Iron Moth. Life Orb gives Bisharp a much desired power boost; however, Black Glasses can be used to allow Bisharp to stick around for a bit longer while still OHKOing Flutter Mane with Sucker Punch after entry hazard chip damage.

Greninja and Darkrai support Bisharp by being able to remove physical walls such as Skarmory, Archaludon, and defensive Great Tusk along with using their Psychic-type coverage to threaten Fighting-types such as Keldeo and Iron Valiant. Sableye provides a crucial Fighting immunity, enabling it to handle threats such as Gallade, Sneasler, and Iron Hands along with being able to burn Skarmory, preventing Bisharp from getting OHKOed by Body Press. Ting-Lu provides entry hazards to wear down physically bulky targets such as Archaludon and Hippowdon. Alolan Muk is also not weak to Fairy and can reliably take on foes such as Enamorus and Primarina along with handling other special attackers like Kyurem. Choice Scarf Meowscarada provides an incredible Speed tier and supports Bisharp by taking out threats such as Quaquaval and Great Tusk while using Protean Play Rough or Triple Axel to handle Dragon-types such as Roaring Moon and Raging Bolt. Mandibuzz is immune to Ground and can safely bring Bisharp in with U-turn and clear hazards with Defog.

Swords Dance (Steel).description:
Bisharp serves as an incredible offensive threat on Steel teams thanks to its Dark typing and strong priority in Sucker Punch, which can enable Bisharp to handle threats such as Dragapult and Hoopa-U. Throat Chop pressures Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Galarian Slowking. Low Kick allows Bisharp to deal with opposing Bisharp along with dealing solid damage to Ting-Lu. Alternatively, Iron Head can be used to deal with Fairy-types like Primarina and Galarian Weezing. Life Orb is used to provide Bisharp a crucial boost, enabling it to OHKO Flutter Mane with Sucker Punch, but Black Glasses can be used to enable Bisharp to stick around longer over the course of a game while still maintaining its ability to 2HKO threats like Toxapex with a +2 Throat Chop.

Bisharp greatly appreciates support from Skarmory, which can come in on Ground- and Fighting-types such as Excadrill, Great Tusk, and Iron Hands and can easily take them on with a combination of Iron Defense and Body Press. Skarmory can also set Spikes, enhancing Bisharp's breaking capabilities by allowing it to power through threats such as Archaludon and Hippowdon. Gholdengo can easily take on Fighting-types like Sneasler, Iron Hands, and Breloom thanks to its Ghost typing along with being able to remove Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Galarian Weezing. In return, Bisharp can remove opposing Ghost-types such as Flutter Mane and opposing Gholdengo. Heatran's Fire immunity lets it handle Fire-types such as Iron Moth, Ninetales, and Volcarona, and it is able to remove physically bulky walls such as Archaludon and Skarmory. Archaludon provides Stealth Rock support along with being able to use Thunder Wave, enabling for Bisharp to outspeed targets such as the Ogerpon formes. Iron Treads provides entry hazard removal to give Bisharp safe entry while being able to remove threats such as Raging Bolt, Heatran, and Okidogi. Hisuian Goodra provides a solid special wall that can take on threats such as Hydreigon and Primarina that can handle Bisharp.

Bulk Up.description: Braviary outpaces offensive Sylveon and Incineroar with its 96 Speed EVs. Tera Electric is a great defensive Tera type, but it doesn't offer as many useful resistances as Tera Ground and Steel do. Defog sets can be run, but there are better forms of removal that aren't as easily taken advantage of by Galarian Articuno such as Rapid Spin Brambleghast, Defog Scyther, and Tidy Up Cinccino.

Physically Defensive (Normal).description:
Braviary serves as good entry hazard removal for Normal teams due to its good bulk and Fighting neutrality, which let it comfortably use Defog in front of foes like Sneasler and Meowscarada. Brave Bird is Braviary's strongest STAB move, threatening to OHKO foes like the Ogerpon formes and Sinistcha. U-turn helps keep momentum going and damage common switch-ins like Ting-Lu and Iron Boulder. Close Combat can be used instead of U-turn to check Steel-, Rock-, and Normal-types like Excadrill, Hisuian Goodra, Tyranitar, and Blissey. Doing so, however, means that Braviary would lack the momentum it gets from U-turn, which is crucial for Normal teams. The EVs above allow Braviary to outspeed Adamant Azumarill while also comfortably taking attacks from Garchomp and Ogerpon-H.

Blissey is a great teammate, as it can tank special hits from Choice Specs users like Greninja, Flutter Mane, and Kyurem while also being able to set up Stealth Rock and spread paralysis with Thunder Wave. Braviary returns the favor by dealing with Choice Scarf users like Galarian Zapdos and Great Tusk for Blissey. Porygon2 is a nice defensive wall when paired with Braviary, being able to wall Ice-types like Weavile and Mamoswine and stop setup users like Scizor and Ceruledge with Foul Play. Choice Scarf Ditto is an excellent revenge killer, using its ability to flip the script on sweepers like Ogerpon-W, Dragonite, and Keldeo late-game. Choice Specs Hisuian Zoroark provides a Fighting immunity for the team while being able to check Ghost- and Steel-types like Gholdengo and Corviknight. Braviary can remove hazards for Hisuian Zoroark while taking out Bisharp and Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott. Choice Scarf Indeedee is another option, which provides more support in the Fighting and Poison matchups due to its part-Psychic typing and ability to set up Psychic Terrain for the team. Indeedee can also blast away threats, such as Urshifu-R, mixed offense Iron Valiant, and Clodsire,in Terrain with Expanding Force. Calm Mind Terapagos, with its colorful moveset, can be a good teammate to pressure defensive Pokemon like Corviknight and Quagsire for Braviary.

Choice Specs.description:
Heat Wave OHKOes Alolan Sandslash, which can be useful for opening up a teammate like Florges. Vacuum Wave still deals heavy damage to Alolan Sandslash and also picks off weakened foes like Zoroark and Ambipom.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

lc.overview: Vullaby is Little Cup's glue gal: splashable and flexible. It is a switch-in to Ground-types, Knock Off absorber, wallbreaker, pivot, and sweeper all bundled into one skull diaper. Vullaby is the main offensive check to most of LC's physical threats because it can punish attacks it survives with Weak Armor. At +2 Speed, it outpaces the entire metagame. Its tremendous natural bulk also allows it to tank most super effective hits from full HP, and with Tera paired with Roost or Tera Blast, it can account for most remaining threats like Chinchou and Elekid. Physically offensive Vullaby is its flagship set because of its immediate wallbreaking power. It can dish out powerful Brave Birds, remove Eviolite from various foes with Knock Off, and pivot out with U-turn or break through its checks with a slew of offensive techs. Its various roles fulfill the needs of many team structures, but it typically forms a balance core with Mienfoo and Foongus or Mareanie. Nasty Plot Vullaby is an alternative option that sacrifices its versatility for sweeping potential. This set is a hyper offense staple and a good surprise option on bulky offense teams when partnered with other Knock Off users like Stunky.
lc.comments:
Other Options

Several options exist to grant physical Vullaby even more immediate wallbreaking power. Tera Blast Ground OHKOes Glimmet and 2HKOes Tinkatink, and it OHKOes Elekid after Stealth Rock damage and deals considerable damage to Chinchou. It is Vullaby's best way to flip around unfavorable defensive matchups, especially on turns where these Electric-types would use Volt Switch. Throat Chop can 2HKO Glimmet without requiring it to Terastallize but risks Vullaby taking massive damage from Power Gem if Vullaby loses the Speed tie or gets a low damage roll. Physical Vullaby may also opt for an Adamant nature, granting it a 75% chance to OHKO less bulky variants of Mienfoo and about an 83.5% chance to KO Mudbray with a Knock Off followed by two Brave Birds. On bulky teams lacking speed control, physical sets may run Choice Scarf over Eviolite. This set typically has an Adamant nature, uses Dual Wingbeat plus Tera Flying, and is paired with entry hazard removal. Choice Scarf Vullaby also fits on teams lacking a Pokemon immune to sleep, as Choice Scarf's Speed boost provides flexibility for Vullaby to use Overcoat over Weak Armor and remain faster than all foes bar faster Choice Scarf users and setup sweepers.

Overcoat Eviolite Vullaby may also use an EV spread of 156 Atk / 156 Def / 156 SpD / 36 Spe plus an Impish nature. This slow, defensive pivot set can switch into Foongus without fear of Sludge Bomb. Defog can be used in the third or fourth moveslot on teams that desire entry hazard removal. Defog Vullaby is typically outclassed by other entry hazard removal options such as Toedscool and Alolan Sandshrew, but it can have tremendous upside against entry hazard stacking teams. Taunt can also be used to deny entry hazards from Mudbray, Tinkatink, and more niche options like Shellos and Chespin.

Checks and Counters

Tinkatink: Pickpocket lets Tinkatink steal Vullaby's Eviolite when hit by Knock Off. Air Balloon Tinkatink variants can also take Vullaby's Eviolite on a U-turn or Brave Bird. Tinkatink walls Dark Pulse variants of Nasty Plot Vullaby. Fast variants of Tinkatink with Encore can shut down Nasty Plot Vullaby or catch physical attacking Vullaby with Draining Kiss, but these variants sacrifice a lot of special bulk and are therefore vulnerable to Heat Wave.

Glimmet: Glimmet can live two hits from Vullaby when healthy and threaten an OHKO with Power Gem after Stealth Rock chip or set entry hazards. Toxic Debris makes it difficult to switch in teammates that are not Poison- or Steel-type, so Vullaby users should manage the HP of Poison-type allies carefully. Glimmet additionally walls Heat Wave variants of Nasty Plot Vullaby.

Mudbray: Mudbray is able to live three hits from physical Vullaby thanks to Stamina. Stone Edge does massive damage to Vullaby and Close Combat KOes -1 Defense Vullaby that try to recover with Roost. However, Mudbray is vulnerable to Air Slash flinches from Nasty Plot Vullaby, especially when combined with Stone Edge's accuracy.

Electric-type foes: Chinchou's offensive typing and Ice Beam coverage threaten Vullaby, making it challenging to switch in typical Electric- or Water-resistant allies like Mudbray. Additionally, Chinchou walls Heat Wave variants of Nasty Plot Vullaby and can KO a chipped Tera Ground Vullaby with Hydro Pump or Ice Beam. Elekid can OHKO Vullaby after Stealth Rock, and good switch-in predictions from Elekid users allow it to wear down its checks or generate momentum with Volt Switch.

Swords Dance Mienfoo: Exploiting Vullaby's ability to switch in and check most Mienfoo sets, Swords Dance Mienfoo can set up and threaten a KO or force a Tera Ghost. 156 Atk Swords Dance Mienfoo sets have a 75% chance to OHKO Vullaby at +2 Attack. Maximum Attack and Reckless variants bump this to a guaranteed OHKO. Tera Steel Substitute sets can set up on Vullaby and scout for Tera Ghost before KOing Vullaby with Knock Off.

Alolan Diglett: The combination of Rock Blast and Sucker Punch is very threatening to Tera Ghost Vullaby and has favorable odds to KO Tera Ground Nasty Plot Vullaby if it attempts to set up. Alolan Diglett may also set up a Substitute if Vullaby switches out.

Strong Choice Scarf users: Hisuian Growlithe's Head Smash deals massive damage into Vullaby, while its Flare Blitz can wear through switch-ins like Mienfoo and Mudbray. Choice Scarf Mienfoo can OHKO Vullaby after Stealth Rock chip with Tera Fighting High Jump Kick, but it struggles if Vullaby Terastallizes into a Ghost-type.

Physical Attacker.description:
Roost allows Vullaby to heal on switches for solid longevity. It can also leverage its natural bulk to recover HP against foes threatening super effective attacks by shedding its Flying typing, which is particularly useful against Volt Switch users after a Weak Armor boost. Using Endure earns Vullaby the chance to KO or remove the items of faster physical attackers and Choice Scarf users like Mienfoo and opposing Vullaby in a pinch. Endure also lets Vullaby survive Fake Out without needing to Terastallize into a Ghost-type. U-turn enables Vullaby to pivot on switch-ins such as Tinkatink, Mudbray, and Glimmet and gain momentum, especially when moving after faster pivots like Mienfoo. Meanwhile, Heat Wave lets Vullaby OHKO Alolan Sandshrew and break through Tinkatink and Tera Steel users. When using Heat Wave, Vullaby should use a Naive nature with 76 Special Defense EVs to guarantee these damage rolls. This spread lets Vullaby live Chinchou's Thunderbolt in exchange for taking more damage from Mudbray's Stone Edge and Hisuian Growlithe's Flare Blitz. Alternatively, if a team is weak to Mudbray or Hisuian Growlithe, Vullaby can move the Special Defense EVs into Defense and use a neutral nature. Tera Ghost, as mentioned, grants Vullaby immunity to Mienfoo's Fake Out and High Jump Kick.

Physical attacking Vullaby easily fits on any team and typically forms cores when paired with Mienfoo and Foongus. These allies support Vullaby by switching in on Rock-type attacks from threats like Glimmet and Mudbray and using Regenerator to shake off other coverage moves. Vullaby should be paired with an Electric-immune teammate. Mudbray can switch into Vullaby checks like Glimmet, Tinkatink, and Alolan Diglett. Offensive pieces such as Elekid and Stunky appreciate Vullaby's ability to wear down checks like Mudbray and Tinkatink. U-turn variants complement frail attackers like Alolan Diglett, which can threaten to KO Glimmet and Tinkatink. Vullaby pairs well with Rapid Spin users like Toedscool and Alolan Sandshrew, especially without Roost. However, Vullaby is notably less dependent on entry hazard control than other Stealth Rock-weak Pokemon like Wingull, since it is bulkier and can make progress or trade when at low HP with Weak Armor.

Nasty Plot.description:
With Air Slash and a coverage move of its choice, a +2 Special Attack Vullaby can OHKO metagame staples like Foongus after Stealth Rock chip damage and try and flinch through other threats with Air Slash. Heat Wave KOes Alolan Sandshrew, does massive damage to bulky variants of Eviolite Tinkatink, and covers for Tera Steel users like Mienfoo. Dark Pulse covers checks that would take Heat Wave such as Chinchou and Glimmet. With Dark Pulse, Vullaby can OHKO these checks after Stealth Rock chip if allowed to reach +4 Special Attack. Tera Blast Ground has huge upside, OHKOing all aforementioned checks, including Tinkatink, but it can completely fail if Vullaby is unable to Terastallize. Roost lets Vullaby recover to set up later and beat Sucker Punch users like Stunky and Alolan Diglett when at low HP or after Terastallizing. Meanwhile, Endure ensures that Vullaby can activate Weak Armor against physical threats. Endure also allows Vullaby to survive incoming Fake Out without using Tera Ghost, which is key for Tera Ground variants.

Due to its threatening coverage, Nasty Plot Vullaby is adept at forcing out defensive Tera types like Steel or Water. This quality lets it fit well on bulky and hyper offense teams. Complementary sweepers that also excel at forcing defensive Terastallization like Swords Dance Mienfoo help Vullaby capitalize on favorable matchups. Since Nasty Plot Vullaby depends on Stealth Rock to KO threats like Foongus, its hyper offense teams should use a consistent entry hazard setting lead like Focus Sash Alolan Diglett. Nasty Plot Vullaby appreciates teammates with Knock Off to overwhelm shared checks. Stunky, for example, wears down Glimmet and Tinkatink. Gothita and Trapinch can trap and remove most of Nasty Plot Vullaby's checks and counters entirely. Trapinch is an especially good trapper on teams where Nasty Plot Vullaby is the main wincon, since it beats all relevant Sucker Punch users and frees Vullaby to Terastallize into a Ghost-type.

Physically Defensive.description:
Mandibuzz has a solid niche in the UU metagame thanks to a unique and solid defensive typing, great mixed walling capabilities, and access to rare utility options like Defog and Toxic that make it a valuable addition to bulkier builds. Foul Play lets it threaten out Pokemon like Metagross, Excadrill, Scizor, and Belly Drum Azumarill. Defog lets Mandibuzz remove entry hazards for its teammates, especially against threats like Metagross and Rhyperior, although the latter might require more precise positioning than the former; it must be hit with Toxic first to be worn down, allowing Mandibuzz to utilize its natural bulk to tank Stone Edge, freely use Defog, and then use Roost to heal off the damage while not being trapped in a healing cycle due to the inability to progress against Rhyperior. Roost keeps it healthy throughout a match, allowing it to repeatedly come in and check Latios, Excadrill, Ogerpon, and Scizor. Toxic alleviates Mandibuzz's passivity a bit, threatening opposing bulky Pokemon like Slowking and Tornadus-T and setup sweepers like Nasty Plot Hydrapple and Calm Mind Tera Electric Latios. U-turn is an alternative to either Defog or Toxic that allows it to act as a slow pivot to maintain momentum against counters like Cobalion and Tinkaton, but Mandibuzz does not usually fit on the offensive structures that necessitate the need of U-turn to keep it from being a momentum sink. Heavy-Duty Boots keeps away the pesky damage from entry hazards. The given Speed investment allows Mandibuzz to outspeed Azumarill, while the Special Defense investment allows it to survive two Soul Dew-boosted Draco Meteors from Latios. Tera Steel helps Mandibuzz better answer foes like Latios and Greninja while flipping the script against foes like Ogerpon-C and shielding it from opposing Toxic. Tera Fairy lets it counter Dragon-types like Latios much more reliably, especially if it chooses to carry Toxic, and allows Mandibuzz to now gain a Fighting resistance while keeping its Ground neutrality against Excadrill.

Mandibuzz best fits on balance and stall builds that enjoy its mixed walling and key utility features. Skeledirge is a great partner, as its typing and ability let it handle annoying Pokemon like Hydrapple and Cobalion somewhat consistently, while also helping against Tera Electric Calm Mind Latios. Toxapex also is a great partner, being a fantastic Knock Off absorber against Tornadus-T and Lokix, while also handling threats like Azumarill and Greninja that Mandibuzz struggles against. Tinkaton can not only act as a secondary check to Latios so that Mandibuzz won't get overwhelmed, but also beat the threatening Ogerpon-C. Rhyperior and Hippowdon can check Hisuian Arcanine, which Mandibuzz struggles against. Excadrill is another Pokemon that can give Mandibuzz trouble, so a check like Hydrapple or Slowking is necessary. Slowking also has the benefit of providing more assurance against Latios.

Defensive.description: 16 Speed EVs allow Mandibuzz to outspeed Adamant Kingambit and Ursaluna.

Physically Defensive (Dark).description:
Mandibuzz is a decent supportive piece for Dark teams with its ability to pivot into physical attackers like Ceruledge, Garchomp, and Excadrill due to its great bulk and U-turn to position its other teammates into favorable matchups. Foul Play punishes strong physical attackers like Ogerpon-W, Dragonite, and Scizor. If the reader feels that Toxic is enough to keep physical setup sweepers at bay, Knock Off allows Mandibuzz to remove key items from Archaludon, Hisuian Goodra, and Toxapex to help Mandibuzz's teammates have an easier time overwhelming these walls. U-turn lets Mandibuzz act as a pivot to escape common switch-ins like Gliscor, Clodsire, and Gholdengo to maintain the offensive momentum of its team. Toxic greatly cuts the longevity of threats like Keldeo and Volcarona, which otherwise switch in and set up on Mandibuzz. Defog lets Mandibuzz prevent its teammates from getting worn down over the course of the match, and if paired with Toxic, lets Mandibuzz pressure entry hazard setters like Great Tusk and Ting-Lu. Overcoat is vital for checking Excadrill on sand-based Ground teams. 23 Speed IVs coupled with a Relaxed nature let Mandibuzz underspeed Skarmory, allowing Mandibuzz to safely bring in a teammate to deal with Skarmory while also breaking its Sturdy with U-turn. Alternatively, an Impish nature with 16 Speed EVs lets Mandibuzz outspeed and use Foul Play against Adamant Azumarill, checking it after it has used Belly Drum. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Mandibuzz get in freely to remove Stealth Rock if running Defog without much issue, but Rocky Helmet racks up chip damage against threats like Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, Excadrill, and Meowscarada and also punishes U-turn users like Sneasler and Roaring Moon.

Mandibuzz's ability to pivot for its teammates greatly benefits wallbreakers like Darkrai, Bisharp, Hisuian Samurott, and Choice Specs Hoopa-U, as it gives them more room to set up or punch holes in opposing teams. Nasty Plot Darkrai, for instance, can start wreaking havoc on Flying, Steel, and Dragon teams after a Nasty Plot, as it forces out Gliscor, Skarmory, and Archaludon, which Mandibuzz lures in. On the other hand, Swords Dance Bisharp benefits from being put in against Toxapex and Clodsire, allowing it to set up and clean weakened Poison and Ground teams, while Hisuian Samurott trades a Poison immunity for the ability to stack Spikes with Ceaseless Edge to eventually overpower Dragon teams late-game. Choice Specs Hoopa-U deals with Ursaluna, Toxapex, and Archaludon and sports a great natural Special Defense to trade with Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Enamorus in the worst-case scenario. Hoopa-U can also use a Choice Scarf to surprise threats like Flutter Mane and Keldeo, which take advantage of Mandibuzz. Choice Scarf Meowscarada forms a decent pivoting core with Mandibuzz and can clean up against types like Ground, Flying, Fairy, and Dragon late-game. Greninja provides more wallbreaking power, dealing with Toxapex, Clodsire, and Ogerpon-H if using a Choice Specs set, or acts as a revenge-killer that outspeeds and eliminates Choice Scarf Enamorus and Sneasler, which can overwhelm Mandibuzz. Ting-Lu complements Mandibuzz, as these complete a defensive core for Dark teams, with Ting-Lu being able to deal with Raging Bolt, Gholdengo, and Flutter Mane while also providing entry hazards. While Mandibuzz slightly overlaps with Sableye due to their role as a physical wall, Sableye is still greatly appreciated thanks to its ability to check IronPress Skarmory, burn Urshifu-R and Barraskewda to let Mandibuzz check these threats safely, and use Encore on setup sweepers like Keldeo, Primarina, and Volcarona, which take advantage of Mandibuzz.

Defog (Flying).description:
Mandibuzz finds a niche on Flying teams thanks to its unique secondary Dark typing and stellar defensive stats, allowing it to run either a specially or physically defensive set to give it a solid role. Foul Play makes use of the high Attack stat of threats like Swords Dance Excadrill, Metagross, and Scizor for its offense. U-turn can be used to threaten Dark-types like Meowscarada and Hoopa-U while also allowing Mandibuzz to pivot into a teammate. Toxic provides solid utility in putting threats like Dragonite, Landorus, and Latios on a timer. Defog supports its fellow Flying-types by removing Stealth Rock along with helping Mandibuzz itself, should Heavy-Duty Boots be knocked off. Both EV spreads have good utility, with the specially defensive spread being better at handling threats such as Choice Specs Dragapult and Spectrier, while the physically defensive spread can more reliably check foes like Ceruledge and Gallade. Both spreads check mixed threats like Hoopa-U. The 16 Speed EVs are used to outspeed Azumarill and check it with Foul Play.

Gliscor and Landorus help immensely by being able to threaten Poison-types like Toxapex and Alolan Muk coming in on Mandibuzz's Toxic, and they can also threaten Electric-types attemping to remove Mandibuzz such as Raging Bolt. Gliscor also appreciates Mandibuzz running Toxic, allowing it to run a different support move such as Taunt. Both Skarmory and Corviknight can threaten Ice- and Rock-types like Weavile, Mamoswine, and Iron Boulder. Skarmory with Body Press can also check Dark-types like Meowscarada, Roaring Moon, and Bisharp thanks to its high Defense. Corviknight with Iron Head can check Fairy-type threats like Flutter Mane, Alolan Ninetales, and Hatterene along with being able to run Defog, allowing Mandibuzz to run Toxic in its moveset. Articuno can threaten problematic Water-types like Primarina, Pelipper, and Rotom-W while enjoying Mandibuzz's ability to threaten physical attackers like Barraskewda and Scizor, should Mandibuzz be physically bulky. Choice Scarf Enamorus appreciates Mandibuzz's ability to remove hazards and threaten Toxic onto walls, including Articuno, that could otherwise shrug off its attacks, enabling Enamorus's sweeping capability. In response, Enamorus can support Mandibuzz by removing Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Bisharp that can easily set up in front of Mandibuzz.

Sablenite.description: Mandibuzz serves as a solid wall thanks to its excellent typing, access to valuable utility moves, and impressive bulk, especially when utilizing Sablenite. It is arguably one of the best answers to powerful yet matchup-reliant Ghost-types such as Arceus-Ghost and Manectite Spectrier, which can otherwise easily dismantle unprepared teams. Foul Play allows Mandibuzz to deal respectable damage to physical setup sweepers such as Pinsirite Dragonite as well as Urshifu-R in dicey situations. It can also deal decent damage to foes such as Lunala. U-turn, combined with the Speed reduction from Sablenite and minimum Speed investment, turns Mandibuzz into a highly effective slow pivot, enabling safe switches to powerful teammates like Urshifu-R, Raging Bolt, Spectrier, Zamazenta, and Iron Crown. Alternatively, Defog can be run to give Mandibuzz entry hazard removal utility on bulky teams; however, it is not fond of switching into Stealth Rock due to its Rock weakness. Toxic is a fantastic option for crippling non-Sablenite defensive Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Garganacl, Arceus formes, and Lunala, particularly Calm Mind variants of the latter two. Mandibuzz fits well on a variety of bulky offense, balance, and stall teams as a wall, Ghost-type check, and slow pivot. Pairing it with physically defensive partners like Magearna and Pecharunt forms a sturdy defensive and pivoting core. Due to its weakness to Stealth Rock, Mandibuzz appreciates hazard removal support from teammates such as Great Tusk and Regieleki, especially when it isn't running Defog. Mandibuzz also synergizes well with hazard setters like Magearna, Great Tusk, Garganacl, and Hisuian Arcanine, as it can force frequent switches with Toxic. Mandibuzz struggles significantly against Fairy-types like Altarianite Regieleki and Dragonite, Arceus-Fairy, and Substitute Audinite Spectrier; thus, teammates like Pecharunt, Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, Ho-Oh, and Eternatus are effective at patching this weakness. Likewise, Electric-type checks such as Arceus-Ground, Altarianite Dragonite, and Hippowdon help deal with threats like Zapdos, Kilowattrel, and Raging Bolt.

Magic Guard.description: Mandibuzz is a solid physical wall with high defensive stats, a useful typing, and valuable utility moves in Defog, Toxic, and Knock Off. Magic Guard circumvents its normally crippling Stealth Rock weakness, letting it act as an excellent Knock Off absorber from the likes of Roaring Moon and Meowscarda, as well as a status absorber from Toxapex, Pecharunt, and opposing Mandibuzz. Foul Play allows Mandibuzz to beat physical setup sweepers such as Dragonite and Ceruledge, while Knock Off can limit the longevity of defensive walls and remove Assault Vests, enabling special attacking teammates like Primarina, Latios, and Azelf. Toxic can cripple walls such as Swampert and Scream Tail and shuts down bulky setup sweepers like Calm Mind Scream Tail and Bulk Up Great Tusk. Defog provides valuable entry hazard control, especially for Stealth Rock-weak wallbreakers Chien-Pao, Ceruledge, and Ogerpon-H, which Mandibuzz can also slow pivot in with U-turn alongside 0 Speed IVs and a Relaxed nature. Leftovers provides passive healing that can't be mitigated by indirect damage, while Rocky Helmet punishes contact moves, most notably U-turn from Corviknight and Roaring Moon. Mandibuzz naturally loses to many of the tier's common physical attackers, including Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-C, exacerbated by the fact that it lacks a true defensive ability or immunity; other physically defensive walls such as Corviknight and Toxapex help shore up these weaknesses. Although Mandibuzz can be an emergency switch-in to Psychic-types like Azelf, Deoxys-S, and Latios, it should generally not be relied on due to its uninvested special bulk and their various super effective coverage moves. Therefore, Mandibuzz appreciates specially defensive walls, such as Empoleon, Manaphy, and Swampert, to check the previously mentioned special attackers along with Gengar and Primarina.

Physically Defensive (Dark).description: As a check to physical attackers with multiple utility options, Mandibuzz is a characteristic component for defensive backbones in Dark teams. Foul Play minimizes passivity, notably 2HKOing all Ogerpon formes, offensive Mega Scizor, Excadrill, and +6 Azumarill. U-turn lets Mandibuzz gain momentum by safely leaving potentially unfavorable matchups, bringing in checks that could struggle to switch in otherwise. Toxic lets Mandibuzz hinder entry hazard setters such as Ting-Lu, Araquanid, and Great Tusk, easing the use of Defog. Brave Bird hits some foes its team can otherwise struggle with, for example, OHKOing Hisuian Lilligant and 2HKOing Tapu Bulu and Buzzwole. The given EV spread allows Mandibuzz to outspeed Adamant Azumarill, with the rest invested in physical bulk to better handle foes such as Dragonite, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Scizor. Ting-Lu can switch into Electric- and Rock-types that can easily force out Mandibuzz like Tapu Koko, Zapdos, and Hisuian Arcanine. Alolan Muk can also further complement a defensive core, as it mitigates a weakness to Fairy-types such as Iron Valiant, Mega Diancie, and Mega Altaria. Offensive Pokemon such as Weavile, Meowscarada, and Hydreigon benefit from Mandibuzz's utility, mitigating its passivity issues.

Defensive.description:
Speed investment outspeeds Specs Primarina and Modest Magnezone. 252 HP / 160 SpD / 96 Spe is an alternative specially defensive spread.

This is a sample set, stay tuned for future updates!

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Mandibuzz could opt to use Mental Herb over Heavy-Duty Boots for the ability to check Taunt variations of Draining Kiss Calyrex-S. However, not using Heavy-Duty Boots renders Mandibuzz vulnerable to Stealth Rock and other entry hazards after Terastallization. Mandibuzz can also use U-turn over the moves in its third slot. Usually, when Mandibuzz switches in against Calyrex-S and forces it to switch out, Mandibuzz loses momentum by staying in. However, with U-turn, Mandibuzz can gain its team the initiative and switch in a teammate that can make its position more advantageous. Although in most cases, the slight increase in momentum Mandibuzz's team gets is insignificant, and other moves can bring more value.

Checks and Counters

Zacian-C: Zacian-C is immune to Mandibuzz's status moves and resists Knock Off. It is also capable of OHKOing Mandibuzz with Play Rough.

Miraidon: Miraidon can OHKO Mandibuzz with Electro Drift and does great damage to the point where Mandibuzz can no longer check Calyrex-S even after Terastallization.

Hatterene: Hatterene's Magic Bounce grants it an immunity to Mandibuzz's Toxic, and it can use Calm Mind in combination with Draining Kiss to deal significant damage to Mandibuzz, healing itself in the process.

Gliscor: Gliscor's Knock Off poses a significant threat to Mandibuzz, as removing Heavy-Duty Boots causes Mandibuzz to be much more vulnerable to Stealth Rock.

Wallbreakers: Wallbreakers, like Kyogre and Koraidon, are capable of dealing significant damage to Mandibuzz, rendering it unable to check Calyrex-S effectively.

Specially Defensive.description:
Mandibuzz is one of stall teams' best Calyrex-S checks, utilizing its Dark typing, special bulk, and access to reliable recovery in Roost to wall all Calyrex-S sets, bar Tera Fairy. Toxic significantly cripples foes by limiting how much they can set up. Whirlwind phazes setup threats like various setup Arceus formes. Defog is a form of emergency entry hazard control, especially useful against Knock Off Pokemon, but Mandibuzz also removes its own team's hazards while using it. Alternatively, Foul Play discourages physical attackers from setting up against Mandibuzz. Knock Off removes Heavy-Duty Boots, making it much easier to chip down Pokemon with the Spikes and Toxic Spikes that Mandibuzz's teammates set. Tera Steel grants Mandibuzz a resistance to Fairy- and Psychic-type moves, allowing it to check non-Taunt Draining Kiss Calyrex-S, as well as Arceus-Fairy, and giving Mandibuzz a Toxic immunity. Mandibuzz has to compete with Alolan Muk for a slot, another Dark-type Calyrex-S check that is much better equipped to deal with Tera Fairy Calyrex-S. However, Mandibuzz has reliable recovery in Roost, unlike Alolan Muk, whose Rest is shut down by Electric Terrain.

Teammates like Dondozo, Skeledirge, and Gliscor appreciate having a reliable switch-in to Calyrex-S, while Blissey appreciates having a fallback method when facing Psyshock variations of Calyrex-S. As Mandibuzz is forced out by the threat of Miraidon's Electro Drift or Kyogre's Water-type moves, it enjoys having teammates like Tera Grass Ho-Oh, Clodsire, and Blissey, all of which can absorb their attacks well. Arceus-Fairy's super effective Judgment poses a great threat to Mandibuzz, forcing it to switch out to teammates like Clodsire, whose Poison typing and access to Toxic make it an excellent check to Arceus-Fairy. Mandibuzz is also very vulnerable to physical attackers, like Zacian-C, which is immune to its Toxic, resists Knock Off, and can OHKO Mandibuzz with Play Rough; or Koraidon, whose Choice Scarf sets can 2HKO Mandibuzz, and Substitute sets use it as setup fodder. Thus, teammates like Skeledirge, Dondozo, and Alomomola work very well with Mandibuzz, as both Skeledirge and Dondozo can fully ignore both setup sweepers' Swords Dance boosts with Unaware, and Skeledirge can cripple them with Will-O-Wisp. At the same time, Alomomola can use its great physical bulk to use Flip Turn and absorb damage the aforementioned Unaware walls would have taken otherwise.

Choice Specs.description:
By donning a Choice Specs, Hydreigon leverages its blend of a high Special Attack, workable Speed, and unique defensive profile to find its niche as a one-of-a-kind wallbreaker capable of dropping metagame staples like Gholdengo, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T on the spot while remaining unbothered by most entry hazards.
