  • Timid versus Modest: Timid is preferred for outpseeding Jolly Annihilape, Timid Hydreigon, and Jolly Baxcalibur, but Modest is fully acceptable if these aren't issues for your team.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: This Volcarona is heavily pressured to start sweeping after it sets up, so Terastallization can widen the opportunities to do so.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is a big help against powerful Dragon-type attacks such as Choice Band Dragonite's Outrage and Baxcalibur's Scale Shot, and it gives Volcarona good coverage against them too with Tera Blast.

  • Water: Terastallizing into the Water typing nullifies Volcarona's most common weakness in Rock-type, and Water-type Tera Blast is also the best option Volcarona has to hit Skeledirge and opposing Volcarona.

  • Rock: Tera Rock lets Volcarona cover Dragonite, Skeledirge, and opposing Volcarona with Tera Blast, and provides a very useful Extreme Speed resistance. When used with Sand Stream from Hippowdon or Tyranitar, it also makes Volcarona quite specially bulky.

  • Grass: The Grass typing strengthens Giga Drain and nullifies Volcarona's weakness to Water-types, most notably helping against Dondozo, Primarina, and Basculegion. Note that this does leave Volcarona walled by Dragonite and opposing Volcarona.

Items

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: It is the best option on Volcarona, as it circumvents its crippling Stealth Rock weakness.

  • Lum Berry: This Volcarona's more offensive nature makes it especially vulnerable to status moves from the likes of Dragonite and Focus Sash Breloom, so Lum Berry is a reasonable way around this.

  • Sitrus Berry: If used with an even HP stat, Sitrus Berry will restore Volcarona's health the moment it switches into Stealth Rock.

SOLAR FLARE (Choiced Attacker).description:
• With its high Speed and immediate power, Volcarona is a good candidate for a choice item that can surprise its usual switch-ins.

  • Fiery Dance: Fiery Dance is a potent cleaning tool thanks to its high chance of boosting Volcarona’s Special Attack.

  • Overheat: Overheat deals good immediate damage, which can allow Volcarona to wear down otherwise annoying walls without much prediction, such as defensive Primarina and Dondozo.

  • Bug Buzz: Bug Buzz is a good secondary STAB move that allows Volcarona to hit foes hiding behind a substitute, with Hydreigon and Tera Water Gliscor being particularly juicy targets.

  • Giga Drain: Giga Drain is Volcarona’s best option to hit troublesome Water-types like Primarina, Dondozo, and Basculegion.

  • Choice Specs versus Choice Scarf: With the extra power offered by Choice Specs, Volcarona becomes even more difficult to wall, with even resistances like Garchomp and Dragapult taking over 50% from it! Choice Scarf on the other hand, allow sVolcarona to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame, allowing it to revenge kill surprising targets such as Meowscarada.

  • Timid versus Modest: Modest's extra damage output is appealing, but it does lead to a speed tie against Jolly Baxcalibur, and being outsped by Jolly Annihilape.

Other Options

  • U-turn: Volcarona can make for a decent pivot with U-turn, but this move becomes far more risky to use against teams with Stealth Rock support.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: This Volcarona takes a more hit-and-run approach compared to other sets, making it especially vulnerable to Stealth Rock damage. Terastallization can solve this issue without needing extra support!

  • Fire: Tera Fire transforms Choice Specs Volcarona into a horrifically powerful wallbreaker, with even physically defensive Dondozo and Primarina that lack Assault Vest taking over 50% from Overheat!

  • Fairy: When paired with Tera Blast, a Fairy Tera type allows Volcarona to better handle the many Dragon-types in the metagame, with the major targets including Dragonite, Garchomp, and Hydreigon.

  • Rock: Tera Rock covers Dragonite, Skeledirge, and opposing Volcarona with Tera Blast, and provides a wonderful resistance to Dragonite's Extreme Speed, at the cost of potentially being revenge killed by Scizor.

  • Grass: A Grass Tera type allows Volcarona to resist the many Water-type attacks aimed at it and gives it a better chance at breaking past Dondozo.

Offensive Quiver Dance.description:
Quiver Dance Volcarona is a powerful wincon for many teams that are able to remove its few checks. This is thanks to Quiver Dance, which can allow it to outspeed and KO a worn-down team. At base 100 Speed, one Quiver Dance boost allows Volcarona to outspeed fast Pokemon like Mega Lopunny and Tapu Koko while also outspeeding common Choice Scarf Pokemon like Tapu Lele and Urshifu-R, meaning offensive counterplay against a boosted Volcarona is quite limited. Flamethrower is a strong, consistent STAB option; however, Fiery Dance gives Volcarona a chance to gain Special Attack boosts while still dealing respectable damage. Bug Buzz is a reliable move that notably lands the most damage on Mega Tyranitar, Ogerpon-W, and Ting-Lu. Hidden Power Ground can be used to hit common checks like Heatran and Toxapex, as they resist Volcarona’s STAB moves and can threaten it with either Toxic or their STAB moves, with Toxapex being able to beat Volcarona by itself with Haze. Physical priority moves, like Mega Lopunny’s Fake Out and Mega Scizor’s Bullet Punch, are commonly used to bypass Volcarona’s Speed boosts and hinder a sweep, and Flame Body is an opportunity to punish them for it. Heavy-Duty Boots is largely used to ignore the effects of Stealth Rock, as it can instantly deplete half of Volcarona’s health; however, negating the effects of Toxic Spikes and Sticky Web are also beneficial to a Volcarona sweep.

Volcarona fits on offensive teams that can wear down or remove specific Pokemon that can prevent its sweep. For example, Pokemon like Moltres, Toxapex, and defensive Garchomp are clear roadblocks to a Volcarona sweep due to their advantageous typing, with the latter two using Toxic to wear Volcarona down. As a result, strong wallbreakers with complementary STABs of Ground or Fairy such as Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Tapu Lele allow such Pokemon to be removed to facilitate a Volcarona sweep. Volcarona also struggles against priority, namely, Sucker Punch from Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott and Fake Out from Mega Lopunny. Tapu Lele acts as a great deterrent to such priority, also shutting down weaker attempts to end Volcarona’s sweep like Urshifu-R's Aqua Jet. Volcarona may have certain matchups where it may struggle to sweep, especially against bulkier teams. However, it can still leverage its potential threat level along with Quiver Dance to remove physical walls, like defensive Great Tusk. This can be taken advantage of by physical sweepers like Dragonite and your own Great Tusk, which both appreciate not needing to spend their Z-Move on it. Entry hazard support from teammates allows Volcarona to muscle through checks like the aforementioned Toxapex as well as offensive checks like Mega Charizard Y and Mega Tyranitar; Pokemon that can do this include Glimmora, Mega Diancie, and Landorus-T. Volcarona’s teammates can also take advantage of Toxapex’s passivity. In particular, sweepers that threaten Toxapex like Mega Latios, Tapu Lele, and Garchomp can force it to switch out, allowing them to grab a free setup turn.

Bulky Quiver Dance.description:
Volcarona's unique typing allows it to check Pokemon such as Iron Valiant, Melmetal, and Rillaboom as well as be a good pivot into Pokemon such as Zamazenta lacking Stone Edge, Mega Lopunny, and Kartana, potentially weakening them with a burn from Flame Body. At the same time, it retains its setup sweeping potential with Quiver Dance. Hidden Power Ground allows Volcarona to hit opposing Fire-types, most notably Heatran, Iron Moth, and Cinderace, as well as Raging Bolt and Toxapex super effectively. However, Bug Buzz is more consistent into other Fire-resists such as Garchomp and Alomomola. Roost gives Volcarona much needed longevity, allowing it to pivot into strong attacks more reliably, such as Choice Specs Iron Valiant's Moonblast while also letting it set up on Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, Mega Venusaur, and Terapagos. The given EV spread allows Volcarona to outspeed Zamazenta after a Quiver Dance; the rest is dumped into physical defense, notably letting it avoid the OHKO from +2 Iron Valiant's Knock Off.

While fitting well on balance and bulky offense builds, Volcarona trades power and coverage for longevity, worsening its weakness against bulky Dragon-types such as Raging Bolt, Dragonite, and Garchomp. Thus, Fairy-type teammates such as Tapu Koko and Tapu Lele are strong partners; the former additionally breaks through bulky Water-types like Toxapex and Alomomola for Volcarona, while the latter protects it from strong priority moves such as Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Urshifu-R's Aqua Jet. Dragon-type teammates, such as the aforementioned Garchomp, also appreciate Volcarona, since they need it to soft-check Fairy- and Steel-types they don't like dealing with, such as Iron Valiant, Mega Scizor, and Gholdengo, both offensively and defensively; Volcarona also takes care of Great Tusk for the former. In return, they are able to break through the bulky Fire-types that Volcarona struggles with, most notably Moltres and Mega Charizard Y, since they're immune to Hidden Power Ground. Garchomp is also able to provide Stealth Rock support, which helps Volcarona dismantle defensive cores including Mega Latios and Mega Tyranitar quicker, making up for the drop in power this set has; other Stealth Rock setters such as Landorus-T are also good options. On the defensive side, Volcarona appreciates bulky Water- and Grass-types such as Tapu Fini, Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Tangrowth that can pivot into strong Water-type attacks from Hisuian Samurott, Urshifu-R, and Barraskewda on Rain teams, with Tapu Fini in particular protecting Volcarona from harmful status conditions such as poison from Alomomola and Gliscor, as well as checking Dragon-types such as Garchomp and Dragonite.

Substitute + Swarm.description:
Volcarona is a premier sweeper on hyper offensive structures, with Quiver Dance pushing its already intimidating STAB combination to nigh unstoppable heights. Traditional counters to Volcarona like Heatran and defensive Garchomp can reliably deal with standard variants, but with Substitute and Swarm, Volcarona is able to muscle through these foes after repeated boosts while blocking crippling status moves like Toxic from Heatran and Toxapex as well as Thunder Wave from Clefable. Buginium Z enables Volcarona to immediately muscle through these aforementioned checks and secure important OHKOs on threatening stopgaps like defensive Landorus-T, Raging Bolt, Assault Vest Alolomola, and Dragonite with Multiscale is broken at +1, as well as specially defensive Gliscor at +2. The Z-Move enables Volcarona to punch through even hard counters like Moltres, Heatran, and Toxapex, as Quiver Dance's Special Defense boosts make moves like Heatran's Magma Storm quickly become unable to break Substitute, subsequently enabling further boosts. Leftovers lets Volcarona play a longer game and make better use of Substitute, but Buginium Z offers absurd power that is sometimes necessary to enable a sweep.

As opposed to the sometimes more straightforward Heavy-Duty Boots set, this Volcarona set aims to activate Swarm by setting up Substitute repeatedly in tandem with one or two boosts. The Z-Crystal activation is important to time as well; otherwise, walls with recovery or disruption like Moltres and Toxapex can either get out of KO range or wipe away important boosts with Haze. Due to the lack of Heavy-Duty Boots, Volcarona heavily requires entry hazard removal and denial from its teammates to ensure it can safely use Substitute. As such, great partners for Volcarona include Magic Bounce users like Mega Diancie and Hatterene, as well as Terapagos for its guaranteed Rapid Spin with Tera Shell. In terms of wallbreaking partners, Volcarona benefits from Pokemon that help overwhelm its checks like Toxapex, Moltres, and Dragonite, so Iron Valiant and Ogerpon-W make for excellent partners. Ogerpon-W, in particular, trivializes the Assault Vest Alolomola matchup, freeing up Volcarona to save the Z-Crystal for a more important target if needed. Fairy-types like Mega Diancie and Tapu Lele pair similarly well, muscling through potential counters in Moltres and Toxapex. Kingambit is a great partner as well, since even if Volcarona's sweep is interrupted, Kingambit greatly appreciates a wounded enemy team and a Supreme Overlord boost to boot. Leads such as Taunt Landorus-T and Mega Diancie are also great allies, as they serve to deny hazards off the bat and set them themselves, making Volcarona's wallbreaking much easier.

Offensive Quiver Dance (Bug).description: Volcarona is one of Bug's strongest setup sweepers, with a respectable Speed stat, high Special Attack, and great coverage. In addition to being one of very few special attacking options on Bug, Volcarona helps apply pressure in a variety of matchups thanks to its strong STAB moves and coverage. Fire Blast can be used over Fiery Dance for more immediate damage output. Giga Drain deals with Water- and Ground-types, most notably Swampert, Gastrodon, and Rotom-Wash. Bug Buzz can be used instead for Volcarona to overwhelm types like Dragon, Dark, and Psychic with Quiver Dance-boosted STAB attacks. Hidden Power Ground hits Heatran, allowing Volcarona to break Steel's immunity-based defensive core that can otherwise give Bug teams problems. Alternatively, Psychic can be used to damage bulky Poison-types, like Toxapex and Mega Venusaur, that can wall physical attackers like Heracross and Buzzwole. These physical attackers, in addition to Lokix and Scizor, are able to break through specially defensive walls, like Chansey and Mantine, that Volcarona struggles against. Araquanid and Armaldo provide helpful entry hazards in Sticky Web and Stealth Rock, respectively, to make sweeping mid- or late-game much easier.

Offensive Quiver Dance (Fire).description: Volcarona is one of the top setup sweepers that Fire has access to, with Quiver Dance allowing it to become a dangerous threat to teams unequipped to deal with it defensively. Psychic allows Volcarona to pressure Fighting and Poison teams, especially after one Quiver Dance, which lets Volcarona outspeed and beat Keldeo, Glimmora, and Crobat. Similarly, Giga Drain does the same to Water and Ground teams after one Quiver Dance, threatening Tapu Fini, Gastrodon, and Hippowdon. Bug Buzz covers the Psychic and Dark matchups very well and allows it to hit Roaring Moon, Ting-Lu, and Latias, which would otherwise be a challenge to deal with. Heavy-Duty Boots prevents Volcarona from being worn down by entry hazards, most notably Stealth Rock, which would otherwise stop Volcarona from being able to set up safely. Psychium Z lets Volcarona OHKO Toxapex with a +1 Shattered Psyche and beat otherwise troublesome threats like +1 Kommo-o, Iron Hands, and Clodsire. Cinderace and Mega Charizard X are especially good partners due to their ability to break through special walls such as Blissey, Clodsire, and Galarian Slowking with relative ease. Entry hazard removers such as Torkoal, Rotom-H, and Court Change Cinderace are near necessities if Volcarona is running Psychium Z. Torkoal and Rotom-H can also provide excellent utility in the form of Stealth Rock and dual screens, respectively, to help Volcarona sweep more easily. Volcanion is also an excellent partner for Volcarona that, thanks to its Water immunity, can act as a strong pivot into Pokemon like Azumarill and Mantine, which could revenge kill it or clear Quiver Dance boosts with Haze.

Setter.description:
Cobalion serves as one of the best Stealth Rock setters in the metagame due to its good matchups into the most common hazard removal options, Excadrill and Mandibuzz, while also being one of the best sponges for Lokix's First Impression. Volt Switch allows Cobalion to pivot out on would-be switch-ins such as Latios and Slowking and bring in a teammate to threaten them out. Thunder Wave can punish Tornadus-T and the aforementioned Latios for switching in, while Stone Edge can be used to hit Flying-types like Thundurus-T super effectively. Leftovers gives Cobalion more longevity, allowing it to check opposing threats for an extended period of time, while Rocky Helmet allows it to punish Lokix and Weavile more easily and get chip damage on other contact moves users such as Scizor and Tyranitar. Shuca Berry is another option that allows Cobalion to switch into or stay in on Earthquakes from unboosted Excadrill. Tera Dragon gives Cobalion a resistance to Water-type attacks such as Surf from Greninja, which is then OHKOed back with Close Combat, while making it neutral to Ground and preserving its Grass resistance so it can still check Ogerpon. Tera Ghost allows it to preserve Stealth Rock in the event the opposing Excadrill uses its Tera to flip the matchup while also making Cobalion neutral to Ground-type attacks and immune to Fighting-type attacks such as Low Kick from Weavile and Close Combat from Scizor and opposing Cobalion. Tera Flying gives it an immunity to Ground-type attacks, allowing it to more easily answer even a Speed-boosted Excadrill. However, Cobalion's base typing is very useful for answering threats like Lokix, Weavile, Scizor, and Tyranitar, so it should usually only Terastalize if there is no other option at the time.

Cobalion fits on Volt Turn offense, bulky offense, and balance teams, utilizing its good matchups into the most common hazard removal options to keep Stealth Rock up for a solid portion of the game while using Volt Switch to bring threats onto the field. Unfortunately, Cobalion doesn't resist Flying and Psychic, so alternative checks to threats like Tornadus-T and Latios are needed. Slowking can check both Latios and Tornadus-T while also providing Thunder Wave support so Cobalion is more free to use Taunt. In return, Cobalion can switch into Lokix and Scizor, which can threaten Slowking. Pivot Tornadus-T can act as a check to Latios while using Knock Off so that foes such as Slowking and Skeledirge are susceptible to Cobalion's Stealth Rock and U-turn to continue the pivot chain. Sandy Shocks and Thundurus-T can help apply pressure on Ground-types like Rhyperior and Excadrill, as well as Cobalion checks like Hydrapple and Latios. Teammates that love Cobalion's ability to check threats like Weavile and Lokix such as Excadrill, Latios, and the previously mentioned Tornadus-T are appreciated. The latter two, alongside Grass-types like Hydrapple and Zarude, also provide a Ground resistance to help cover Cobalion's weakness. Excadrill, on the other hand, provides a Latios check that can remove hazards while also offensively checking Skeledirge and Toxapex. Choice Specs Greninja offensively pressures everything that can threaten Cobalion, and it appreciates Cobalion's ability to draw in foes and pivot on them alongside Stealth Rock for chipping Assault Vest Tornadus-T into Ice Beam range.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

More defensively oriented teams can make use of Levitate Cobalion to check Mamoswine, Iron Treads, and Garchomp, but its poor matchup against Great Tusk leaves something to be desired. Well-Baked Body sets are also an option to annoy Iron Moth, Cinderace, and Desolate Land Moltres. Iron Defense sets are viable thanks to Body Press, and Thunder Wave is also an option to spread status and slow down the opposing team. Regenerator heavily augments its longevity but at the very steep opportunity cost of not being able to run a RegenVest user alongside it due to Single Ability Clause.

Checks and Counters

Faster Special Attackers: Cobalion can easily be forced out by Iron Moth, Deoxys-S, and Latios due to its poor special bulk.

Zapdos: Zapdos can switch into Body Press and Steel Beam, can threaten to OHKO Cobalion, and may also outspeed it depending on both Pokemon's EV spreads.

Gholdengo: Gholdengo can relatively easily force out Cobalion, especially if it carries Choice Scarf to deny Cobalion an opportunity to pivot with Volt Switch.

Magic Guard.description:
Magic Guard Cobalion provides nearly unparalleled role compression, serving as a wallbreaker, pivot, entry hazard setter, and secondary physical check all in one slot. Body Press and Steel Beam, despite their relatively low raw power, provide excellent coverage in the current metagame, as most specially defensive walls and pivots like RegenVest Swampert and Volt Absorb Corviknight risk a 2HKO from Body Press, and most physical walls like Great Tusk and Pecharunt cannot stomach Steel Beam. Body Press also allows Cobalion to invest heavily in Defense without being passive, letting it check Chien-Pao, Roaring Moon, and Kingambit for phsyically defensive cores that may struggle with them. Most of the Pokemon that can switch into both moves like Fluffy Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Toxapex are outsped and pivoted on with Volt Switch. Cobalion is also a decently reliable Stealth Rock setter, as none of Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads can both switch in and reliably keep hazards off against it. The EVs are extremely customizable based on team needs or user preferences; the given spread lets Cobalion outspeed Jolly Landorus-T and maximizes physical defense, but it can also run faster spreads to outspeed Iron Treads and be an even more reliable Stealth Rock setter, slower sets to be an even better wallbreaker while still outspeeding Gholdengo, or less Defense to maintain Speed but power up Steel Beam.

Cobalion is generally found on offensive teams that want a non-passive way to check key threats and set entry hazards. Notably, Cobalion has an excellent matchup against common stall teams, as they rarely have walls that avoid the 2HKO from both Body Press and Steel Beam. Fast offensive pivots like Roaring Moon, Iron Moth, and Cinderace do a great job at getting Cobalion in on walls that it can force out. Cobalion also pairs well with Pecharunt, as it can handle the Dark-types that Pecharunt cannot, although it does not enjoy losing its Life Orb to Roaring Moon. Cobalion does not meaningfully threaten Gholdengo, so a strong switch-in to it like Roaring Moon or Kingambit is strongly recommended. Due to its lack of longevity, Cobalion is only a short-term check to opposing physical attackers; it needs either a more sturdy physical check like Pecharunt or Regenerator Great Tusk that it is assisting or a powerful offensive team that can win before Cobalion is overwhelmed.

Utility (Fighting).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

ru.overview: Terrakion is a superb wallbreaker and hyper offense lead, using its excellent Speed tier, immediate power, great offensive typing, and utility moves like Stealth Rock, Swords Dance, and Taunt to great effect. Focus Sash lead Terrakion can often disrupt opposing leads, like Jirachi and Krookodile, with Taunt before establishing its own entry hazard and potentially racking up damage with its powerful STAB attacks. Swords Dance Terrakion is incredibly threatening, as it can comfortably break past walls like Chesnaught and Gastrodon once they've taken a bit of chip damage. While other hyper offense leads offer more utility, such as Healing Wish Jirachi and Endeavor Lycanroc, Terrakion remains a great option as a lead, setup sweeper, and wallbreaker.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Sacred Sword is an alternative to Close Combat that can surprise IronPress foes like Registeel. X-Scissor can be used to slice through bulky Psychic-types like Reuniclus and Slowbro, which is especially beneficial on Swords Dance sets.

Checks and Counters

Psychic-types: Reuniclus and Slowbro can notably stomach Terrakion's attacks and threaten it back with Psychic Noise and Scald, both of which can comfortably 2HKO it. Cresselia and Necrozma can also sponge attacks from Terrakion well and threaten to set up or take it out.

Faster Wallbreakers and Revenge Killers: While Terrakion is generally fast, it is easily outpaced by other wallbreakers like Barraskewda and Choice Scarf users like Gardevoir and Krookodile; the latter two can find safe entry points against it, as they resist at least one of Terrakion's STAB moves.

Physical Walls: Quagsire, can be an annoyance for Terrakion, comfortably sponging its attacks and threatening to 2HKO it back with Earthquake. Chesnaught can sponge any attack from Terrakion and threaten to KO it back with Body Press.

Golurk: While pretty niche, Golurk counters most Terrakion sets, threatening to KO it with ease, while Terrakion can't do much back.

Stealth Rock.description:
Set Details

Terrakion is an effective lead for hyper offense teams due to its good Speed and great offensive presence, especially against common entry hazard removers like Cyclizar and Maushold. Rock Blast is generally used over Stone Edge to circumvent opposing Focus Sash leads, including Kleavor, though Terrakion is still unfortunately slower than Froslass and Ribombee. Swords Dance makes Terrakion a major wallbreaking threat, hindering physical walls like Slowbro, Chesnaught, and Gastrodon that look to dampen Terrakion's impact as an offensive lead. Taunt inhibits opposing hazard leads like Jirachi, setup users such as Slowbro and Suicune, and Defog Noivern. Focus Sash best ensures Terrakion a turn to set up Stealth Rock or attack. Loaded Dice synergizes with Rock Blast, guaranteeing Terrakion can OHKO Kleavor and giving it a better chance to OHKO Mimikyu through its Disguise. Tera Ghost lets Terrakion spinblock, and the additional Fighting immunity can surprise Mach Punch Breloom and opposing Terrakion.

Stealth Rock set up by Terrakion enables other hyper offense staples, including Bisharp and Maushold. Bisharp is especially noteworthy for punishing Defog Noivern. Mimikyu is another common pick for hyper offense teams, and its Ghost typing helps preserve Terrakion's hazards against Cyclizar while deterring Maushold. Other Ghost-types, such as Gengar and Basculegion-F, can similarly spinblock, and they pressure Psychic-types like Slowbro, Reuniclus, and Necrozma for Terrakion.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Terrakion is a powerful setup sweeper, which boasts almost immediate wallbreaking power. Earthquake acts as an excellent coverage move and allows it to deal with targets such as Jirachi and Golurk easily. Substitute is an alternative that lets Terrakion safely choose whether to set up a Swords Dance or fire off a STAB move after forcing out a Pokemon like Cyclizar or Bisharp. Taunt can be used to stop entry hazards from going up and take away recovery and other status moves from foes such as Slowbro and Quagsire. Air Balloon earns Terrakion a free turn against Ground-types such as Krookodile and can be used alongside Taunt to completely shut down Quagsire. Leftovers is an alternative that allows Terrakion to take better advantage of its decent natural bulk and synergizes particularly well with Substitute. Tera Flying removes its weaknesses to Ground- and Fighting-type attacks, thus giving it opportunities to set up against as well as break checks like Gligar, Chesnaught, and Choice Scarf Krookodile.

Swords Dance Terrakion fits best on offense structures, particularly hyper offense, due to its ability to threaten the majority of the metagame after a single Swords Dance. It shares many of its defensive checks, like Gastrodon, with other common setup sweepers such as Bisharp and Mimikyu. This means that Terrakion can often be sacrificed to deal good damage to these checks before fainting, which enables the aforementioned sweepers to capitalize on the weakened physical walls to potentially pull off a sweep. Its great Speed tier strengthens its ability to chunk holes in the opposing team by taking advantage of common Pokemon like Jirachi and Krookodile, which can often free up teammates like Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Shift Gear Toxtricity to clean up late-game. It pairs well with specially offensive wallbreakers and setup sweepers such as Nasty Plot Gengar and Shift Gear Toxtricity, which can KO common Terrakion checks like Slowbro, Gastrodon, and Chesnaught with ease. Terrakion offers valuable support to teammates like Gengar and Maushold that fear Knock Off greatly, as its ability, Justified, acts as a strong deterrent against it. In addition, Terrakion can work well as a cleaner in entry hazard-stacking team structures, which try to wear down opposing teams, alongside setters such as Jirachi, Gligar, and Chesnaught, as many defensive Pokemon, such as Amoonguss and Suicune, only need to be chipped marginally to be in Terrakion's KO range after a Swords Dance.

Choice Band.description:
Thanks to its high Attack stat and almost unresisted STAB combination, Choice Band Terrakion makes for an excellent wallbreaker that is very difficult to switch into. Earthquake helps it deal with Jirachi and is a great option for picking up weakened targets without suffering from the defense drops or inaccuracy from its STAB moves. Quick Attack gives it a form of priority to deal with faster, weakened Pokemon like Cyclizar and Noivern. Justified allows Terrakion to switch into Dark-type attacks and punish moves like Knock Off from Cyclizar to boost its Attack. Tera Rock boosts Terrakion's Stone Edge even further, making it very difficult to switch into and guaranteeing a 2HKO on Slowbro. Tera Rock helps Terrakion defensively by removing its weaknesses to Fairy and Psychic and giving it a resistance to Flying-type attacks, making it much better into revenge killers like Choice Scarf Gardevoir and Hurricane Noivern. Tera Ghost also removes its weaknesses to Fairy and Psychic, but it also removes its weaknesses to Fighting and Ground, which gives Terrakion an opportunity to take out common Choice Scarf users such as Krookodile and Gengar. Tera Ghost pairs well with Justified, deterring opposing Pokemon from hitting it with super effective Dark-type attacks in fear of boosting its Attack.

Choice Band Terrakion can fit on a plethora of balance and bulky offense teams thanks to its great Speed tier and its excellent power as a wallbreaker. Entry hazard support from Pokemon like Chesnaught, Empoleon, and Krookodile can help it pick up 2HKOs on bulky physical walls like Chesnaught and Slowbro and rack up residual damage on revenge killers like Choice Scarf Gengar and Krookodile switching in. Terrakion appreciates pivot support to get it in safely; therefore, Pokemon like Cyclizar and Jirachi can keep up momentum by pivoting on defensive switch-ins like Empoleon and Krookodile and create opportunities for Terrakion to attack. Terrakion appreciates Future Sight support from Pokemon like Slowbro and Reuniclus, as it can use Close Combat more freely while Future Sight punishes Fairy-, Flying- and particularly Poison-types that switch in like Amoonguss, Noivern, and Gardevoir. Lots of common Choice Scarf users such as Gardevoir and Krookodile can revenge kill Terrakion, making defensive partners that can switch into the aforementioned Pokemon very valuable. Physical tanks such as Gastrodon and Quagsire and special walls like Empoleon can switch into the revenge killers while offering utility like entry hazards and Rocky Helmet chip damage. Terrakion weakening opposing Pokemon like Gastrodon, Jirachi, and Hisuian Goodra allows teammates like Choice Scarf Krookodile and Bisharp to come in afterwards and finish the job.

Choice Scarf.description:
Terrakion's high Speed and access to perfect coverage mean that it is an ideal Choice Scarf user that outspeeds most other Choice Scarf users in the tier, making it an excellent revenge killer. Earthquake helps it deal with Jirachi and is a great option for picking up weakened targets without suffering from the defense drops or inaccuracy from its STAB moves. Rock Slide gives Terrakion a more reliable Rock-type move to use by trading power for accuracy. Stealth Rock allows Terrakion to act as an entry hazard setter that is able to get it up on Pokemon it forces out like Choice Scarf Krookodile locked into Knock Off. Justified allows Terrakion to switch into Dark-type attacks and punish moves like Knock Off from Cyclizar to boost its Attack. Tera Rock helps Terrakion by boosting its Rock-type moves, helping it clean up versus foes that don't resist Rock and threatening a 2HKO on Amoonguss after Stealth Rock. Tera Ground boosts Earthquake's damage and threatens an 2HKO on Golurk while granting it an immunity to common Thunder Wave support like Reuniclus and Cresselia.

Choice Scarf Terrakion fits best on balance and bulky offense teams, as it is a great revenge killer that can outspeed common Choice Scarf users like Gardevoir and Krookodile. Chesnaught and Gastrodon make for good partners that offer utility like entry hazards and Rocky Helmet chip damage that weaken the opposing Pokemon and make it easier for Terrakion to clean. Terrakion struggles into strong physical walls like Quagsire, Slowbro, and Chesnaught, which can stop it from cleaning, so bulky partners like Noivern, Reuniclus, and Wo-Chien are appreciated, as they can take hits for Terrakion and force these walls out. Wallbreakers like Crawdaunt and special attackers like Magnezone and Basculegion-F can also weaken the aforementioned walls while making it much easier for Terrakion to clean up. Future Sight support from Slowbro and Reuniclus makes it harder for physical walls to switch in and particularly punishes Poison-types such as Amoonguss, allowing Terrakion to use its STAB moves more often instead of locking into Earthquake.

Choice Band (Rock).description:
Choice Band Terrakion is one of Rock's best physical wallbreakers thanks to its high Attack, good Speed, and Fighting-type STAB moves, which allow Rock teams to threaten opposing Steel-types like Archaludon and Heatran. Close Combat threatens opposing Dark- and Steel-types such as Ting-Lu, Bisharp, and Corviknight. Earthquake complements Terrakion's Rock-type STAB attacks and targets bulky threats like Toxapex, Clodsire, and non-Air Balloon Gholdengo. Upper Hand allows Terrakion to handle priority moves that it is weak to from Pokemon like Scizor and Breloom while dealing considerable damage to them. Sacred Sword is also an option as a secondary Fighting-type STAB move that doesn't have the drawback of dropping Terrakion's defenses and can ignore Defense boosts from Pokemon like Archaludon. Rock Slide also can be used as a secondary Rock-type STAB option due to its higher accuracy than Stone Edge and chance of flinching.

Hisuian Arcanine is a good teammate for Terrakion, as both Pokemon work well offensively in dismantling Steel-type teams' defensive cores. Terrakion's Close Combat can OHKO Heatran and Archaludon, and Arcanine's Flare Blitz OHKOes Gholdengo and does significant damage to Corviknight and Skarmory. Tyranitar offers a Special Defense boost to Terrakion via its ability Sand Stream, allowing it to tank special attacks it is weak to like Enamorus and non-Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast, letting Terrakion OHKO them in return. In conjunction with entry hazard support in Stealth Rock, Tyranitar's sand is able to chip down opposing walls like Pecharunt, which is 2HKOed by Earthquake after Stealth Rock and sand damage. Terrakion also appreciates Tyranitar's Psychic immunity, which allows it to check threats to Terrakion such as Mew, Indeedee, and Deoxys-S. Ogerpon-C is an essential teammate, threatening opposing Water- and Ground-types like Toxapex, Hippowdon, and Great Tusk thanks to its Grass typing. Glimmora offers Spikes support, which enables Terrakion to break defensive walls like the aforementioned Hippowdon and Great Tusk more easily. Its Poison typing also assists in getting rid of Toxic Spikes, improving Terrakion's longevity, and its Mortal Spin helps Terrakion stay healthy throughout the game, allowing it to switch in without the worry of taking damage from Spikes. Terrakion appreciates Iron Boulder's Speed tier, which threatens Pokemon like Meowscarada, Ogerpon-H, and Choice Scarf Enamorus that Terrakion is slower than and OHKOed by. Iron Boulder also threatens opposing Fighting-types like Sneasler and Keldeo thanks to its Psychic typing. Choice Scarf Kleavor is able to set up Stealth Rock without fear of Magic Bounce using Stone Axe, which helps helps Terrakion deal more damage, and it is able to outspeed threats to Terrakion like Flutter Mane. Kleavor's U-turn can also bring in Terrakion safely. Minior offers a Ground immunity thanks to its Flying typing, and it appreciates Terrakion's ability to break through its checks like Toxapex so it can set up and sweep late-game with Shell Smash.

Swords Dance (Rock).description:
Swords Dance Terrakion is an immensely strong wallbreaker for Rock teams thanks to its incredible STAB combination in conjunction with its good Speed that lets it outspeed common threats to Rock teams such as Iron Treads, Garchomp, and Landorus. Stone Edge allows Terrakion to nail Primarina and Gliscor that could otherwise take on Close Combat. Close Combat complements Stone Edge perfectly and is Terrakion strongest STAB attack, allowing it to target Steel-types such as Archaludon and Iron Treads. Upper Hand lets Terrakion circumvent priority such as Breloom's Mach Punch, Scizor's Bullet Punch, and Keldeo's Vacuum Wave, with +2 Upper Hand OHKOing Scizor and Keldeo after Stealth Rock damage and always OHKOing Breloom. Alternatively, Earthquake can be used over Upper Hand, allowing Terrakion to more easily threaten Gholdengo, Toxapex, and Clodsire super effectively. Life Orb allows Terrakion to clock important OHKOs, such as on Corviknight and Galarian Weezing with Close Combat and Stone Edge, respectively, after Stealth Rock chip damage and a Swords Dance boost.

Hisuian Arcanine forms a potent wallbreaking core with Terrakion against Steel teams. Hisuian Arcanine can also threaten physically defensive Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Sinistcha for Terrakion; In return, Terrakion can weaken some of its checks like Archaludon, Swampert, and Gliscor. Ogerpon-C can threaten Ground- and Water-type Pokemon for Terrakion, such as Hippowdon, Great Tusk, and Primarina, as well as being able to beat common shared checks with Terrakion, such as Toxapex and Landorus-T. Iron Boulder can deal with Poison- and Fighting-types for Terrakion; such as Pecharunt, Okidogi, and Keldeo. Iron Boulder can also use a Choice Scarf to revenge kill faster Pokemon that would otherwise outspeed Terrakion such as Iron Valiant, Meowscarada, and Sneasler. Tyranitar can set hazards up as well as check Psychic-type Pokemon such as Latios and Latias for Terrakion. In return, Terrakion can deal with common Steel-types such as Archaludon and Iron Treads for it. Glimmora can scare out Fairy- and Grass-types such as Hatterene, Clefable, and Hydrapple while also providing Toxic Spikes, which can chip down targets such as Iron Hands and Garchomp, as well as hazard remova, which helps Terrakion not get worn down by hazards. Garganacl can switch into most walls such as Corviknight, Amoonguss, and Toxapex and force progress against them with Salt Cure. Purifying Salt lets it absorb status effects that may be aimed at Terrakion, such as Toxic from Clodsire and Will-O-Wisp from Sableye and Dragapult. Shell Smash users such as Drednaw and Minior appreciate Terrakion's ability to punch holes into the opposing team so that they can sweep more effectively.

Swords Dance (Fighting).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Choice Band.description: Choice Band Terrakion is a fearsome wallbreaker thanks to its good Attack stat, useful offensive typing, high-Base Power STAB moves, and ability to bypass Fluffy. Earthquake allows Terrakion to hit non-Earth Eater Gholdengo and have a slightly stronger and more accurate option against foes like Iron Hands and Pecharunt. Terrakion's last moveslot is very flexible, as it likes to use Close Combat or Stone Edge almost all of the time. Stealth Rock can help wear down the opposing team and chip would-be defensive checks into range of a 2HKO, while Quick Attack can pick off faster, weakened foes, and Poison Jab does more damage to Primarina and Scream Tail. Teammates such as Iron Boulder, Zamazenta, and Roaring Moon appreciate Terrakion's ability to break through Corviknight, which is one of their biggest roadblocks, and can clean up weakened teams. Terrakion is vulnerable to being revenge killed due to its middling Speed stat, so a strong defensive backbone featuring Pokemon like Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Manaphy is recommended. Terrakion fits best on balance and bulky offense teams that need a wallbreaker and can help it switch in safely, so slow pivots like the aforementioned Corviknight and Manaphy make for good teammates. Additionally, special pivots like Azelf and Hisuian Electrode can get it in on special walls such as RegenVest Meloetta and Hisuian Goodra, which it can threaten out.

Choice Scarf (Rock).description: Terrakion is the ideal Choice Scarf user for Rock teams due to its high Speed stat and access to powerful coverage moves in Earthquake and Close Combat. Close Combat provides coverage against Steel-, Normal-, and Dark-types such as Heatran, Mega Lopunny, and Greninja. Earthquake does heavy damage against Electric-types such as Zeraora and Tapu Koko as well as against Poison-types like Toxapex and Clodsire. Poison Jab is able to pressure Grass- and Fairy-types that Rock teams struggle to deal with, being able to OHKO Tapu Bulu and Whimsicott as well as deal high amounts of damage to Azumarill and Tapu Lele. Choice Scarf allows Terrakion to be an amazing revenge killer, outspeeding threats like Mega Lopunny and Zeraora. Terrakion pairs well with Shuckle, as its Stealth Rock and Sticky Web support allows Terrakion to net more KOs and outspeed faster Pokemon like Regieleki, Choice Scarf Meowscarada, and Adamant Barraskewda under rain. Terrakion also pairs well with Mega Diancie, which softens the likes of Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Toxapex for Terrakion thanks to its coverage. Alolan Golem helps Terrakion with the Steel matchup by trapping Pokemon such as Mega Scizor, Corviknight, and Celesteela with its ability Magnet Pull. Nihilego is able to help with the Fairy matchup with Sludge Wave dealing big damage to Pokemon such as Tapu Fini and Clefable. Tyranitar helps Terrakion by setting up sand, which boosts Terrakion's Special Defense stat, allowing it to survive Surf from Choice Scarf Greninja and Dazzling Gleam from Tapu Koko. Tyranitar also provides Pursuit support against faster Choice Scarf users such as Latias while also being able to break walls for Terrakion, allowing it to clean teams more easily.

Swords Dance.description:
Virizion is a niche setup sweeper that finds windows to sweep largely thanks to its unique defensive profile and high Speed relative to other Fighting-types, outpacing foes such as Delphox, Mismagius, and Pawmot. It is also able to set up on physical walls like Rhydon, Bellibolt, and Wo-Chien. Stone Edge is its best option to nail Poison- and Flying-types like Galarian Slowbro, Galarian Articuno, and Altaria. Synthesis is necessary for Virizon to have the longevity to set up Swords Dance multiple times, which can be better than Leaf Blade even against walls like Milotic and Mudsdale. However, Leaf Blade is better for revenge killing and ensures that Virizon is not walled by Golurk and Palossand. Lum Berry is essential, as it is the only way Virizon can reliably set up against status spreaders like Bellibolt. Tera Rock doubles as the best way to buff Virizon's coverage against foes like Florges and Venusaur, getting the OHKO at +2 against the latter, and as a means to get the jump on revenge killers like Salazzle, Choice Scarf Hisuian Typhlosion, and Choice Scarf Skuntank.

Most teams utilize Virizon as an answer to more passive foes in the early-game, sponging weaker hits until it can transition into a late-game sweeper, making it a pick for balance teams that enjoy this role compression. It will need help from offensive teammates like Skuntank and Golurk to get past physical walls like Galarian Slowbro and Florges. In return, Virizon can switch into, set up against, and potentially break through physical walls it has more favorable matchups against, such as Milotic, Bellibolt, and Wo-Chien. Defensive switch-ins to Fairy- and Psychic-types like Florges and Espeon are a necessity, so try using specially bulky Pokemon like Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro and Alolan Sandslash. These walls also work for pivoting around the coverage from bulky offensive threats like Venusaur and opposing Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro that Virizion struggles to break through on its own. As for physically offensive revenge killers like Choice Scarf Paldean Tauros-F and Triple Axel Ambipom, they can be punished with walls like Static Bellibolt, Rocky Helmet Mudsdale, and Flame Body Coalossal. When opting for Synthesis, it is imperative to have teammates like Bombirdier to deter free switch-ins from the likes of Golurk and Palossand, and Water-types like Bruxish and Milotic also help to alleviate the pressure against these Ground-types; Virizon returns the favor by being a solid answer to Electric-types like Belibolt, Hisuian Electrode, and Rotom-C.

zu.overview: Virizion's great Speed tier and threatening offensive typing make it a dangerous offensive threat that can serve as both a wallbreaker and a late-game cleaner. Virizion has access to Swords Dance, which allows it to boost its attack and wallbreak consistently. Its great Speed tier lets it stay threatening versus offensive teams and even clean them up late-game when its checks are weakened or removed. Virizion has naturally high special bulk and a workable defensive typing that allow it to find set up opportunities versus Choice-locked special attackers like Jolteon, Magneton, and Clawitzer, and there is some ambiguity to its sets thanks to its good coverage and ability to run a physical or special set. However, Virizion isn't especially strong without a boost, and it can struggle to break through physically bulky checks like Weezing and Dipplin. Despite that, Virizion retains a very solid niche thanks to its higher Speed tier and its ability to run coverage options like Stone Edge and Zen Headbutt.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Virizion can run a Tera Flying Calm Mind set using Giga Drain, Air Slash, and Focus Blast or Aura Sphere. This turns the tables on many of Virizion's traditional answers such as Dipplin and Weezing. However, Virizion can only boost its Special Attack by one stage at a time with Calm Mind, and it is forced to use weak moves unless it opts for the inaccurate Focus Blast as its Fighting-type STAB move, which makes the set considerably less threatening in practice. A mixed attacker set with Leaf Storm, Close Combat, Stone Edge, and Synthesis with a Life Orb can be threatening to certain offensive and balance teams but fails to make significant progress versus builds packing common walls such as Dipplin, Mesprit, and Muk. Sacred Sword is an interesting alternative to Close Combat that ignores the Defense boosts on IronPress foes such as Regirock, Orthworm, and Naclstack and doesn't lower Virizion's own defenses, but the drop in power is very noticeable. Tera Fairy is a fringe alternative Tera type that gives Virizion a Fighting resistance, allowing it to stave off revenge killing from Choice Scarf Primeape, and an immunity to Dragon Tail, which lets it potentially break past Dipplin after accruing multiple Swords Dance boosts. Tera Poison grants Virizion a generally useful defensive typing to counteract revenge killing attempts from the likes of Whimsicott and Primeape. These are inferior to the other Tera types outside of these specific situations, however.

Checks and Counters

Dipplin: Dipplin's massive physical bulk allows it to handily deal with the standard Swords Dance set. It isn't even 2HKOed by a +2 Close Combat and can use Dragon Tail to phaze Virizion before healing off any damage, which makes it a very reliable answer. It has to be wary of a surprise Calm Mind set, however, and the rare Tera Fairy can turn it into setup fodder.

Poison-types: Bulky Poison-types such as Weezing and Muk resist Virizion's STAB moves and threaten it in return with their STAB moves, or in Weezing's case, a burn from Will-O-Wisp. They must be cautious of Zen Headbutt, however. Hisuian Sneasel is faster than Virizion and can OHKO it with Gunk Shot. Additionally, several Pokemon that Virizion usually threatens, such as Sandslash and Regirock, commonly run Tera Poison and can therefore turn the tables on it.

Revenge Killers: Virizion's Speed tier, while very solid, still leaves it outpaced by several common revenge killers. Choice Scarf Primeape, Whimsicott, Sneasel, and Choice Scarf Typhlosion all outrun Virizion and can threaten to revenge kill it. All but the latter two need chip damage dealt before they can KO Virizion, however, and only Whimsicott and Primeape can directly switch in.

Status: Burns and paralysis are especially threatening to Virizion. Common Pokemon such as Weezing, Mesprit and Charizard are all capable of spreading those status conditions, and Virizion is not capable of OHKOing any of them except for Charizard if it chooses to run Stone Edge. However, Lum Berry allows Virizion to circumvent this and set up on many of these foes fearlessly.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance allows Virizion to break through bulky foes like Mesprit and Regirock. Stone Edge lets Virizion threaten Charizard and Articuno. Zen Headbutt can be used instead to threaten Poison-types like Weezing and Muk. Justified dissuades foes such as Primeape and Poliwrath from attempting to remove Virizion's item via Knock Off. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Virizion to come in multiple times throughout a game without fear of chip damage from entry hazards. However, Lum Berry is a viable alternative on offensive teams, as it allows Virizion to set up safely on foes that might try to cripple it with status, such as Mesprit, Rotom, and Sandaconda. Tera Rock allows Stone Edge to OHKO Whimsicott and 2HKO Weezing after Stealth Rock damage at +2. It also gives Virizion a resistance to Fire- and Flying-type attacks, which lets it deal with Charizard and Typhlosion with more confidence. Tera Psychic lets Zen Headbutt 2HKO Tera Poison Regirock at +2, do significantly more damage to Weezing, removes Virizion's weakness to their Poison-type STAB moves, and gives Virizion a useful Fighting resistance that can foil revenge killing attempts from Choice Scarf Primeape and opposing Virizion.

Virizion's great Speed tier and ability to both wallbreak and sweep depending on the situation make it usable on teams ranging from balanced to hyper offensive team styles. Virizion dislikes facing down extremely bulky physical walls such as Dipplin and Weezing and Iron Defense Pokemon such as Regirock and Orthworm, which can also outlast Virizion should they begin boosting as it comes in. Strong special attackers, such as Nasty Plot Mesprit, Magneton, and Charizard, are therefore good teammates; the former is especially good at disrupting these extremely bulky threats. These teammates appreciate Virizion's Speed tier helping them out against offensive builds and its ability to threaten special walls like Cryogonal. Virizion appreciates entry hazards on the opponent's side, as it tends to force a lot of switches and loves seeing its defensive checks worn down. Stealth Rock setters such as Mesprit and Regirock are good teammates as a result, as are Spikes setters like Orthworm. These bulky hazard setters help to check revenge killers that are dangerous to Virizion; Regirock and Naclstack can help check Choice Scarf Typhlosion; Mesprit helps out versus Choice Scarf Primeape. Virizion pairs well with other physical wallbreakers, especially on offense and hyper offense, as they can work together to break down their shared defensive answers. Teammates such as Swords Dance Sneasel and Beartic work well as a result.

Bulky Tailwind.description:
Set Details

  • Tornadus is one of two viable priority Tailwind setters in the metagame, pairing excellently with Restricted Pokemon like Calyrex-S, Zamazenta-C, and Kyogre that appreciate its combination of weather control, speed control, and Flying-type STAB moves that allow it to threaten Restricted Pokemon like Koraidon as well as non-Restricted Pokemon like Amoonguss, Rillaboom, and the Urshifu formes.
  • Bleakwind Storm is used for strong spread Flying-type STAB damage, while Hurricane is chosen to hit through the Wide Guard used by Zamazenta and Lunala while securing an OHKO on the Urshifu formes. Hurricane is only an option on Kyogre teams due to its inconsistency outside of rain. Rain Dance deactivates Koraidon's Orichalcum Pulse and significantly weakens its Fire-type moves while also setting up the rain for its own Water-type partners like Urshifu-R and Kyogre. Taunt is chosen to prevent status moves like Zamazenta-C's Wide Guard, Amoonguss's Spore, and Calyrex-I or Lunala's Trick Room that would disable or take advantage of Tornadus and its partners, Kyogre and Calyrex-S. Generally, Tornadus runs Protect on non-Covert Cloak sets in order to avoid flinches from Fake Out or on offensive teams that do not need Rain Dance and would prefer the increased staying power generated by Protect.
  • Covert Cloak is chosen to allow Tornadus to set up Tailwind against Fake Out Pokemon like Incineroar and Rillaboom that would otherwise leave it vulnerable to being KOed or pressure it into using Protect . Rocky Helmet is chosen in order to allow Tornadus to punish Urshifu-R and Koraidon, forcing them to take significant recoil.
  • The Speed investment allows Tornadus to outspeed maximum Speed Groudon and Kyogre, while the bulk investment allows Tornadus to survive Tera Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R or Thunderclap from Raging Bolt.
  • Tera Dark is chosen to allow Tornadus to block Taunt from opposing Tornadus and Encore from opposing Whimsicott, while also providing it a key resistance to Calyrex-S's STAB moves.

Teambuilding

  • Raging Bolt and Miraidon threaten to OHKO Tornadus with their STAB Electric-type moves, being able to OHKO it with a Special Attack Protosynthesis-boosted Thunderclap, which takes Tornadus out before it can move, or Volt Switch, which creates momentum for the opposing team, respectively. Tornadus also hates Pokemon that are able to set up Trick Room against it while threatening to OHKO it, with Restricted Pokemon like Calyrex-I and Meteor Beam Lunala being able dissuade Tornadus's Taunt with their offensive pressure. Indeedee-F and Farigaraf also present unique challenges to Tornadus, as the two of them are able to set up Trick Room while also blocking Tornadus's Prankster Taunt with their abilities. While Tornadus can OHKO Whimsicott, its Speed combined with Prankster Encore allow it to shut down Tornadus and punish it for using Tailwind or prevent it altogether with Taunt.
  • Urshifu-R is Tornadus's premier partner, being able to take advantage of both the Tailwind and Rain Dance it sets up in order to do massive damage uncontested by Protect. Rillaboom is able to contest Indeedee-F and Miraidon's Terrains, threatening the former and switching in on the latter while also applying Fake Out pressure, allowing Tornadus to more effectively set Tailwind throughout the course of a game. Landorus is notable for its ability to OHKO both Raging Bolt and Miraidon while appreciating Tornadus's Tailwind allowing it to outspeed threats like Calyrex-S, Zamazenta-C, and the aforementioned Miraidon.
  • Kyogre is another of Tornadus's primary partners, with Tornadus being able to hit Grass-types like Rillaboom, Amoonguss, and the Ogerpon formes super effectively with its Flying-type attacks for it while also being able to reset rain into opposing weather control. Tornadus appreciates Kyogre's ability to output immense damage into Trick Room setters like Calyrex-I, Lunala, Farigiraf, and Indeedee-F, allowing it to freely set Tailwind for its partners. Calyrex-S also greatly appreciates Tornadus's Tailwind, which allows it to gain an advantage against opposing Calyrex-S and Koraidon. Tornadus's Taunt support is vital for both Restricted Pokemon, as it is able to prevent Zamazenta-C and Lunala from using Wide Guard. Zacian-C is a also a notable partner because it appreciates Tornadus's ability to set Tailwind against Miraidon and Calyrex-S while taking advantage of its ability to set rain in the face of Koraidon. Zacian-C is also able to handle a lot of Tornadus's checks, since it is able to outspeed and OHKO Raging Bolt, Miraidon, and most Calyrex-I.

Offensive Support.description:
Set Details

  • Sharp Beak Tornadus is a bulky offensive support Pokemon that can output decent damage with Bleakwind Storm. It has positive matchups versus various metagame staples, such as Koraidon, Rillaboom, and Amoonguss, as well as good neutral matchups into much more of the metagame.
  • Taunt provides disruption, denying otherwise crippling plays from opposing supporting moves; it's especially helpful for Trick Room and Wide Guard users, since negating those allow Tailwind and Bleakwind Storm to be effective.
  • Sharp Beak lets Tornadus be more flexible, since it will be able to deal good chip damage even when Taunted; this allows Tornadus to run more bulk. With the Sharp Beak, it has a chance to OHKO Koraidon and 2HKOes Amoonguss and Rillaboom.
  • The Defense and HP investment allows Tornadus to live a Behemoth Blade from +1 Zacian-C and a Surging Strikes from Mystic Water Urshifu-R; the Special Defense investment allows Tornadus to survive an Astral Barrage or a Psychic from a Life Orb Calyrex-S. The Speed investment lets Tornadus outspeed the entire unboosted metagame under Tailwind, as well as letting partner Smeargle outspeed and use Decorate on Tornadus, letting +2 Tornadus 2HKO bulky Pokemon like Zamazenta-C. The remaining EVs are invested into Special Attack.
  • Tera Dragon lets it live a Water Spout in rain from Kyogre, a Flare Blitz from Koraidon in sun, a Meteor Beam from Lunala, or an Overheat from Modest Chi-Yu.

Teambuilding

  • Tornadus dislikes opposing Whimsicott, since a Taunt or Encore will largely limit Tornadus's usefulness. It's also susceptible to Fake Out users like Incineroar and Iron Hands, as it doesn't have Covert Cloak or Tera Ghost.
  • Tornadus is countered by Raging Bolt, Miraidon, and Calyrex-I, all of which threaten OHKOs on Tornadus both before and after Terastallizing and can easily take Bleakwind Storms multiple times.
  • Tornadus appreciates Smeargle, since Smeargle can redirect dangerous Electro Drifts, Thunderclaps, and Thunderbolts from Miraidon and Raging Bolt, respectively, and can block opposing Glacial Lances, Water Spouts, and Origin Pulses from Calyrex-I and Kyogre, respectively, with Wide Guard.
  • Restricted Pokémon like Zamazenta-C, Calyrex-S, and Kyogre appreciate being around Tornadus, since it can let them outspeed everything with Tailwind, excluding Speed Booster Energy Iron Treads and Flutter Mane. Tornadus can also deny opposing Wide Guard with Taunt, letting Calyrex-S and Kyogre freely fire off Astral Barrage and Water Spout, respectively.
  • Rillaboom acts as a check to Raging Bolt and Miraidon, easily tanking Electric-type damage for Tornadus while getting rid of Electric Terrain. It is also important Fake Out support that moves before Incineroar and Iron Hands.
  • Raging Bolt is also a wonderful partner for Tornadus, since they cover each other great defensively and together have nigh-unresisted coverage; additionally, Raging Bolt can revenge kill Miraidon and opposing Raging Bolt after Tailwind has been set up.

Tailwind Support.description:
Tornadus is used as a support Pokemon that can set Tailwind for its team and deal semi-consistent damage with Bleakwind Storm. It is very good into Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Rillaboom, as Tornadus can easily use Taunt or threaten them with Bleakwind Storm. Tornadus can make use of its weather-setting abilities to help itself hit Bleakwind Storms or support its teammates by boosting or reducing the damage of Water- or Fire-type moves. Icy Wind provides a secondary form of speed control for Tornadus and helps against other Tailwind-based teams. Protect can also help against Fake Out if it holds Rocky Helmet. Covert Cloak allows Tornadus to shine as a supportive piece, as it stops it from being flinched by the common Fake Out. It also prevents it from having its Special Attack lowered by Snarl. Rocky Helmet acts more as a repellent for attacks like Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and Chien-Pao's Ice Spinner. It also can make Pokemon more wary of using Fake Out, as they will be constantly taking chip damage. The EV spread on this Tornadus allows it to take a Tera Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R. This can be really impactful on the Rocky Helmet set, as it forces Urshifu-R down to 50% of its health upon hitting it. It can also take an Astral Barrage from Choice Specs Calyrex-S. Tera Dark is mainly used to stop other Tornadus from using Taunt or Whimsicott from using Encore on it. It can also be used as a defensive Tera against Calyrex-S, as it resists or is immune to both of its STAB attacks. Tera Steel can be used to resist attacks from Pokemon such as Chien-Pao and the occasional Rock-type. It also removes a weakness to Electric, which can make it fare better against Raging Bolt.

Tornadus is a good partner for many Pokemon thanks to its ability to support them through speed control and weather. One example of this is Chi-Yu, which makes use of Tornadus's ability to set sun and Tailwind to blast through opposing teams. Chi-Yu also helps Tornadus's Bleakwind Storms do more damage. Kyogre is another good partner, as Tornadus allows it to outspeed non-Tailwind teams with its below average Speed stat. Tornadus can also help to stop other weather teams from outdamaging Kyogre while letting Kyogre deal with opposing weather attackers. Tornadus benefits other Pokemon with its weather as well such as Urshifu-R, Koraidon and Archaludon. It can also provide a check to weather-setting Pokemon like Koraidon and Groudon with opposing weather. Checks to Tornadus include Miraidon and Raging Bolt. Their ability to resist its attacks and fire back with powerful Electric-type STAB moves can threaten both Tornadus and its common partners. One other check is Kingambit. Often, Tornadus cannot attack with Bleakwind Storm due to the threat of Defiant being activated. It can easily set up in front of Tornadus or, if it has Assault Vest, threaten its partner. Landorus, however, can help to beat some of these checks with strong Sandsear Storms in Rain while being immune to Miraidon's and Raging Bolt's Electric-type STAB moves. Trick Room teams are also a bad matchup, as they flip the Speed stats and make Tailwind useless. Calyrex-I is especially tough for Tornadus, as it can target it down with strong Glacial Lances or set Trick Room right in front of it.

Bulky Tailwind.description:
• Bleakwind Storm provides good damage into Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W. Tailwind is the most effective speed control Tornadus has access to. Taunt helps shut down Amoonguss and helps to manage certain Trick Room Pokemon like Porygon2 and Dusclops, but Protect can be run instead to ensure Tailwind goes up. Rain Dance and Sunny Day serve as weather control, which enables your sweepers and disables opposing weather-based sweepers. Rain Dance pairs well with Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-W while Sunny Day powers up Chi-Yu and Flutter Mane.

  • This given EV spread focuses on bulk, surviving Mystic Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and Tera Fairy Choice Specs Moonblast from Flutter Mane. The low Speed investment ensures that Tornadus sets up its own weather.

  • Rocky Helmet helps against Urshifu-R mirrors and provides good chip into opposing physical attackers making contact. Covert Cloak prevents Fake Out flinches from Incineroar and Rillaboom. It also negates any secondary effects from moves like Rock Slide and Icy Wind. This ensures that Tailwind goes up. Mental Herb helps to shrug off one Taunt.

  • Tera Dark provides an immunity to Prankster Taunt, guaranteeing Tailwind. Tera Steel provides useful resistance to Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane's STAB moves. Both Tera types improve matchups into Psyspam and against Electric-type moves from Pokemon like Raging Bolt, Iron Hands and Archaludon.

Offensive Tailwind.description:
• Focus Sash ensures Tornadus survives one attack and set up Tailwind. Protect becomes important to avoid Fake Out without committing the Tera early.

  • Tornadus rarely Terastallizes, but Tera Ghost can ensure that it can more reliably set up Tailwind by negating Fake Out from Pokemon like Incineroar and Rillaboom, and Extreme Speed from Pokemon like Dragonite and Entei. Tera Flying increases its offensive pressure.

Tailwind.description:
Tornadus is one of the tier's best support Pokemon, providing crucial speed control with Prankster-boosted Tailwind while still having respectable damage output with Bleakwind Storm. Taunt allows Tornadus to shut down foes like Amoonguss and prevent Pokemon like Porygon2 from setting Trick Room. The given EV spread allows Tornadus to live a Psycho Boost from Deoxys-A, and the remaining EVs are dumped into Special Attack. Covert Cloak is used to nullify the flinching effect of Fake Out, allowing Tornadus to set up Tailwind without worrying about foes such as Incineroar and Iron Hands stopping it. Alternatively, Tera Ghost can be used for a similar effect, additionally granting Tornadus immunity to Extreme Speed from foes such as Dragonite and Entei. If Tera Ghost is used, Sitrus Berry should be used to increase Tornadus's survivability. Tera Steel provides Tornadus with a resistance to Rock-type coverage, such as Rock Slide from foes like Tyranitar and Landorus-T. Tornadus struggles against Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Raging Bolt, as they resist Bleakwind Storm and can threaten back with massive damage, so Ground-types like both Landorus formes can help. Weather-setting moves like Rain Dance and Sunny Day are options over Protect on weather teams, ensuring weather can stay up.

Notable Partners

Offensive Threats: Generally strong offensive Pokemon appreciate Tornadus's ability to set Tailwind, as offensive teams can make use of Tailwind the best. Additionally, offensive teams appreciate the chip damage that Tornadus deals with Bleakwind Storm, and the prevention of Trick Room with Taunt.

Support Pokemon: Pokemon that appreciate Prankster like Amoonguss are good partners for Tornadus due to it helping them fulfill their role as support Pokemon better, such as giving Amoonguss’s Spore priority.

Water-, Electric-, and Ground-types: Teammates like Ogerpon-W, Iron Hands, and both Landorus formes appreciate Tornadus’s ability to threaten the many common Grass-type foes such as Amoonguss, Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Sinistcha, with Landorus in particular benefitting from being able to use Bleakwind Storm.

nu.overview: Tornadus's high-Base Power STAB and coverage moves, which are both further bolstered by its gargantuan offenses, and access to amazing utility options like Knock Off and Taunt make it a versatile threat in NU. Its Speed is also enormous, letting it blow past common fast Pokemon like Alolan Ninetales, Munkidori, and Paldean Tauros-W. On top of that, it has access to two amazing abilities that allow it to either be more supportive by getting off a fast Taunt and setting up Rain Dance freely with Prankster or offensive by letting it take advantage of common stat-dropping moves and abilities like Altaria's Defog, Brambleghast's Strength Sap, and both Paldean Tauros-W's and Incineroar's Intimidate. While some Tornadus sets run Heavy-Duty Boots, a fair amount don't, since other items can provide more support at times. Tornadus's weakness to Stealth Rock is further exacerbated on non-Heavy-Duty Boots sets by how much it loves to repeatedly come in, though. As a trade-off for its great offensive prowess, Tornadus has low bulk, which really starts to show when combined with its Stealth Rock weakness, and because of it, Tornadus's useful resistances and immunities are rendered moot, meaning it can be overpowered by Flamigo's Close Combat or KOed by a secondary STAB move like Flygon's Outrage. Tornadus also has to deal with either using unreliable moves like Hurricane and Bleakwind Storm or dealing with adverse contact effects such as paralysis from Bellibolt's Static. Not only that, but Amoonguss, Galarian Slowbro, and Bellibolt often carry Rocky Helmet, worsening Tornadus's situation.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Sludge Bomb allows Tornadus to threaten Fairy-types like Sylveon, Florges, and Tera Fairy Galarian Slowbro, and it can usefully spread poison; however, Tornadus's other moves tend to provide more utility overall. Bulk Up sets can opt for Rest + Chesto Berry alongside Prankster so that they can set up many more times, but losing out on Defiant is quite detrimental with how common Intimidate is. A Choice Specs set with Hurricane / Focus Blast / Dark Pulse / U-turn can be run with Tornadus's enormous Special Attack and Speed as well as its access to pivoting, but its reliance on inaccurate moves can make it inconsistent at times. Tornadus can trade out Rain Dance and Damp Rock for Snowscape, Sunny Day, or Sandstorm and its respective weather-elongating item depending on what weather team it's being run on, but non-rain weather teams aren't as consistent overall.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Bellibolt, Rotom-H, Raikou, and Kilowattrel all can take on Tornadus's Hurricane and Acrobatics and retaliate with super effective STAB attacks. On top of that, they can all use Tornadus for momentum, Bellibolt can spread status with Toxic, Rotom-H and Raikou can set up, and Raikou and Kilowattrel outspeed it naturally. However, they can be easily caught off-guard by Tera Ground.

Steel-types: Copperajah, Registeel, and Bronzong can take multiple hits from Tornadus, and they can capitalize on this by setting up entry hazards or boosting their stats. However, the former two need to watch out for common super effective coverage moves, the latter needs to be cautious of Knock Off, and they all have to watch out for Heat Wave.

Rock-types: Minior, Drednaw, and Diancie can use Tornadus as setup fodder or an opportunity to set up their hazards. However, the latter two need to watch out for super effective coverage moves.

Ice-types: While Alolan Ninetales isn't insanely bulky, it can almost always take one attack from Tornadus, especially from physically oriented sets, and retaliate with a powerful Blizzard. Alolan Ninetales also sets snow, forcing Tornadus to set up rain again. Similarly, physical Tornadus sets struggle to get past Avalugg. However, special attacking Tornadus sets with moves like Hurricane, Bleakwind Storm, and Heat Wave can get past Avalugg without too much of an issue.

Stealth Rock: Tornadus tends to prefer items other than Heavy-Duty Boots, as they can provide more utility. However, this causes Stealth Rock to be an enormous issue, and with how often certain Tornadus sets love to switch in and out, the damage can rack up quickly.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Set Details

Bleakwind Storm is preferred due to its higher accuracy; however, Hurricane is a stronger STAB move to fire off. Knock Off cripples common switch-ins like Bronzong, Brambleghast, and Diancie. Heat Wave lets Tornadus nail Steel-types like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Registeel, while Grass Knot allows Tornadus to hit Ground- and Water-types like Gastrodon and Milotic. On the other hand, Taunt lets Tornadus stop walls like Bronzong, Gligar, and Gastrodon from setting up, getting their entry hazards up, or healing. An alternative EV spread of 116 HP / 140 SpA / 252 Spe can be used to survive common Choice Scarf users' attacks like Chandelure's Overheat and Hisuian Typhlosion's Eruption. Tera Steel allows Tornadus to tank a variety of hits like Cinccino's Tail Slap, Munkidori's Sludge Wave, and Sylveon's Hyper Voice. Alternatively, Tera Ground lets Tornadus take an Electric- or Rock-type attack from Kilowattrel and Diancie.

Tornadus excels at firing off Knock Off and pivoting out, so entry hazard setters like Gastrodon, Bronzong, Orthworm, and Diancie can help capitalize on this trait. Tornadus can take one or two Fighting-type attacks, but it can't switch in consistently. Because of this, Fighting-resistant partners like Galarian Slowbro, Scream Tail, and Sylveon pair well with it. Pivots like Inteleon, Milotic, and Flygon enjoy Tornadus's presence, as it can easily dismantle common Grass-type switch-ins like Decidueye, Amoonguss, and Breloom. Ground- and Steel-types such as Gligar, Gastrodon, Bronzong, and Orthworm can help take on Electric- and Rock-types like Kilowattrel and Diancie that threaten Tornadus. As Tornadus typically lures in Rock-, Electric-, and Steel-types like Diancie, Bellibolt, and Registeel, wallbreakers like Basculegion-M, Choice Band Flygon, Guts Heracross, and Swords Dance Incineroar that capitalize on these Pokemon as entry points synergize extremely well; on top of that, they can also get rid of any neutral special walls trying to check Tornadus like Alolan Muk, Milotic, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro.

Rain Setter.description:
Set Details

U-turn allows Tornadus to bring in a rain sweeper, and it can help create mind games with opposing leads like Galvantula and Cinccino; however, Taunt stops setup sweepers and entry hazard setters from taking advantage of Tornadus. Under rain, Weather Ball is a powerful move that hits Flying-resistant Pokemon like Diancie super effectively while providing strong neutral coverage for others like Copperajah, but Knock Off allows Tornadus to provide more utility, removing important items like Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots while hitting Bronzong and Wind Rider Brambleghast super effectively. Tera Steel provides a strong defensive typing that can let Tornadus have an easier time both setting up rain and pivoting. On the other hand, Tera Ground can turn the tables against Electric- and Rock-types like Kilowattrel and Diancie, which would threaten Tornadus otherwise.

Basculegion-M is a no-brainer when it comes to partners, as it can take advantage of Tornadus's rain-setting capabilities with its Swift Swim and rain-boosted Water-type STAB attacks. Other Swift Swim users like Kingdra, Overqwil, and Ludicolo also pair well while offering unique qualities: Kingdra excels at weakening Water-resistant and -immune Pokemon; Overqwil offers rain teams an easy way to handle Grass-types; and Ludicolo takes advantage of Water-types that rain teams can struggle with like Vaporeon, Gastrodon, and Milotic while acting as a secondary rain setter. As Tornadus is quite offensive, it tends to not have great longevity, so a more defensive rain setter like Klefki is greatly appreciated. On top of being more reliable, Klefki can support its team with both entry hazards and Thunder Wave. Tornadus can't handle Water-types too well, and neither can most Swift Swim users; thus, partners like Toxicroak, Kilowattrel, and Brambleghast are greatly appreciated.

Bulk Up.description:
Set Details

Hammer Arm is the preferred option to take out Steel-types like Copperajah, Registeel, and Tera Steel Sylveon due to its high Base Power, but because of how it drops Tornadus's Speed, Brick Break can be used for a less punishing but weaker alternative. Notably, at +1, Tornadus's Hammer Arm OHKOes Copperajah after one layer of Spikes and 2HKOes both Registeel and Orthworm. Knock Off helps take out Steel-types on low health, and it gives Tornadus a way to easily deal with Bronzong. Sitrus Berry provides some recovery to Tornadus and, when consumed, allows Acrobatics to be at full power. However, no item can be run to automatically have Tornadus at its fullest potential. Defiant lets Tornadus take advantage of common stat-dropping abilities and moves like Overqwil's and Incineroar's Intimidate as well as Vileplume's Strength Sap. Tera Ground allows Tornadus to surprise and take hits from Kilowattrel and Diancie. Tera Steel can be run to gift Tornadus with a typing that better handles common special attackers like Munkidori, Dragalge, and Sylveon that could easily break through it.

Since Defiant is Bulk Up Tornadus's biggest draw, leads like Galvantula, Brambleghast, and Froslass that set entry hazards pair naturally, as they help pressure the opponent's team to use Defog. Ghost-types like Hisuian Typhlosion, Chandelure, and Decidueye make for good partners, as they can create a hazard removal-punishing duo because any of them can spinblock, and Tornadus can punish Defoggers. Tornadus can have issues with KOing Steel-types like Registeel, Bronzong, and Orthworm, meaning teammates like Munkidori, Diancie, Cinccino, and Minior have great synergy, since they can work alongside Tornadus to overwhelm these shared checks. Cinccino is especially good thanks to its Tidy Up clearing Stealth Rock for Tornadus. Fighting- and Ground-types such as Breloom, Toxicroak, Torterra, Paldean Tauros-W, and Flygon work well to take out the aforementioned Steel-types as well as Rock-types like Diancie. The former three can also help take care of pesky defensive Water-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Swampert. Bulk Up Tornadus struggles with OHKOing Alolan Ninetales and breaking through Ice-types like Avalugg, meaning teammates that can switch in and beat them such as Chandelure and Diancie are greatly appreciated.

Nasty Plot.description:
Set Details

Hurricane provides Tornadus with more power, but Bleakwind Storm has higher accuracy. Focus Blast allows Tornadus to better hit Rock-types like Diancie as well as Dark-types like Incineroar, but Heat Wave gives it a more reliable way of taking out Steel-types such as Copperajah and Registeel. Dark Pulse lets Tornadus hit Wind Rider Brambleghast and the Fighting-neutral Bronzong super effectively, which could potentially wall Tornadus otherwise. Tera Steel means Tornadus can take attacks like Inteleon's Ice Beam, Cinccino's Tail Slap, and Munkidori's Psychic, giving it an easier time setting up and firing off attacks. Tera Ground, on the other hand, allows Tornadus to better take on Rock- and Electric-types like Diancie and Kilowattrel. Tera Dark can also potentially be used, as it boosts Dark Pulse and allows Tornadus to have an easier time breaking through Uxie and Bronzong.

Tornadus enjoys partners like Diancie, Munkidori, Uxie, Calm Mind Scream Tail, and Porygon-Z, as they can help to overwhelm shared Steel-type checks like Bronzong, Copperajah, and Registeel. Cinccino is also quite good at this, and it can remove entry hazards for Tornadus, letting it comfortably run a different item. Pokemon like Diancie, Toxtricity, and Weakness Policy Incineroar help bring in Fighting- and Ground-types like Breloom, Flygon, and Swampert, which all give Tornadus free setup opportunities. Since Tornadus will most likely thud into and faint to a Steel- or Rock-type, a teammate like Chandelure, Breloom, Torterra, or Flygon works well to take advantage of the free entry they get afterwards.
