A dedicated lead like Booster Energy Scream Tail, Brambleghast, Eject Pack Flygon, or Focus Sash Infernape is also appreciated to help wear down Tornadus's checks like Diancie, Registeel, and Alolan Muk.

Tailwind Setter.description: • The alternative EV spread of 248 HP / 244 Def / 16 SpA (Bold Nature) survives 3 hits of Icicle Spear (Adamant Nature) from Kyurem-Black.

Bulky Tailwind.description:
• Tornadus takes advantage of a combination of Prankster and Tailwind to set nearly uncontested speed control. This allows it to ensure that its teammates can move first and remove or cripple threats before they can move.
  • Bleakwind Storm allows Tornadus to take on an offensive presence, even after using up all of its support moves.
  • Taunt is the best option for the third moveslot, as it can disrupt the foes' ability to use status moves, effectively crippling support options and ameliorating the risk of a foe setting up or inflicting status. However, priority Rain Dance and Sunny Day can be strong options for teams that are more weather dependent, and they can be beneficial for teams that are afraid of weather by providing the ability to reverse the opponent's weather.
  • Protect allows Tornadus to survive an attack that can potentially KO it or delay setting up Tailwind. This can be particularly useful in Tailwind mirror matches, as setting Tailwind a turn later can allow for an extra turn where your team has Tailwind and the opponent's doesn't. If needed, this slot can be used for weather setting, but losing Protect can make it significantly more difficult for Tornadus to set Tailwind multiple times throughout the match.
  • Covert Cloak allows Tornadus to safely set up Tailwind against Fake Out users such as Rillaboom and Incineroar. Note that Covert Cloak and Tera Ghost should not be used together, since they effectively do the same thing. Sitrus Berry can be used to boost Tornadus's long-term survivability, allowing it to set Tailwind multiple times per match.
  • Tera Steel is an excellent defensive type, and it boosts Tornadus's survivability by giving it a resistance to lethal Ice-type attacks from Chien-Pao and Kyurem as well as common attacks from Pokemon like Gholdengo, Tornadus, Dragonite, and Glimmora. On the other hand, Tera Ghost and Tera Dark both prevent foes from disrupting Tornadus's support options by blocking Fake Out or Prankster Taunt, respectively.
  • Tornadus's bulk allows it to survive significantly more than the other Prankster Tailwind setters. Tornadus needs to maximize its physical bulk in order to survive a Wild Charge from Assault Vest Iron Hands without needing to Terastallize. The physical bulk also allows Tornadus to set Tailwind multiple times per game and allows it to survive physical priority moves that can outprioritize and prevent Tailwind, such as Dragonite's Extremespeed.
  • Tornadus pairs best with offensive threats that have middling Speed. Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Regidrago can take advantage of the boosted speed to outspeed major threats such as opposing Landorus and Chien-Pao.

Focus Sash.description:
• Tornadus is the defining Tailwind user in the DOU metagame. Prankster allows Tornadus to set Tailwind with an incredible degree of consistency. This, combined with its high Special Attack and Bleakwind Storm, has made Tornadus a cornerstone in offensive team compositions.

  • Bleakwind Storm allows Tornadus to threaten the metagame's numerous common Grass-types, among them Ogerpon-W and Sinistcha.

  • Running Focus Sash allows maximum investment into Special Attack and Speed. Critically, having maximum Speed enables Tornadus to outspeed and pressure Ogerpon-W and -H.

  • Icy Wind provides another means of speed control. Though normally quite weak, it is able to 2HKO Landorus, one of the most common Pokemon in the metagame. The damage is also significant against the tier's many Focus Sash users, most notably Glimmora, Chien-Pao, and opposing Tornadus, breaking their Focus Sashes while simultaneously dropping their Speed and allowing Tornadus's partner to follow up. This move is most effective against opposing offensive Tailwind-based teams, as stacking both forms of speed control provides the edge against a team with just Tailwind.

  • Taunt shuts down many support-oriented Pokemon entirely, preventing them from using highly disruptive moves like Spore, Trick Room, and Tailwind. Though because of Prankster, it is unable to affect Dark-types such as Incineroar and Ting-Lu and is blocked by Armor Tail and Psychic Terrain.

  • Sunny Day activates Protosynthesis and boosts Fire-type attackers such as Chi-Yu and Ogerpon-H. Similarly, Rain Dance supports Water-types like Ogerpon-W in addition to increasing the accuracy of Bleakwind Storm and Sandsear Storm. Both of these weather options also have utility in disrupting opposing teams, weakening the corresponding typing and blocking weather-reliant effects like Aurora Veil and Swift Swim.

  • Focus Sash's defensive properties allow Tornadus to forgo a defensive Tera type in favor of the utility of the Ghost typing. Tera Ghost's primary value is in evading Fake Out and the less common Extreme Speed, allowing Tornadus to set Tailwind on a critical turn and resume applying offensive pressure afterwards. In practice, however, Tornadus is not a common user of Terastallization, as it's usually more valuable to save it for one of the team's offensive powerhouses.

  • As Tailwind is a common part of many teams, it is not uncommon to have your Tailwind essentially neutralized by a foe setting their own. In these Tailwind mirror matchups, it's often advised to try and offset your own Tailwind by a turn or two with the aim of having the Speed advantage after their Tailwind has ended. Opting to use Icy Wind can also provide an advantage during matched Tailwinds by lowering the Speed of both foes.

  • Tornadus fits best on teams with offensive Pokemon that need their Speed patched up. Landorus, Gholdengo, and Regidrago are all great examples of offensive powerhouses that find themselves outsped by faster threats such as Chien-Pao and Ogerpon formes. Even slow Pokemon like Iron Hands and Ursaluna-B can greatly benefit from partnering with Tornadus. With some Speed investment, they're able to use the Tailwind to outspeed Landorus and Ogerpon-W while also benefiting from Tornadus's ability to check the Grass-types that trouble them both.

Nasty Plot.description:
Nasty Plot Tornadus-T's role in OU is being a specialized balance breaker, with even the bulkiest teams failing to withstand its attacks and leave permanent damage thanks to its ability Regenerator. Heat Wave is used to hit Steel-types like Gholdengo, Kingambit, Iron Crown, and Corviknight. Grass Knot can be used to hit heavier Pokemon like Ting-Lu, Dondozo, and Garganacl for super effective damage. Focus Blast, on the other hand, provides coverage against Pokemon like Blissey, Hisuian Samurott, and Kingambit while retaining strong hits against Ting-Lu and Garganacl. Knock Off can be used as a more passive yet safer way to deal permanent damage to defensive cores via the removal of items, particularly Heavy-Duty Boots, which, when combined with entry hazard stacking tactics, can be very hard for defensive teams to answer. Life Orb is the recommended item to further magnify its wallbreaking niche, in particular allowing Tornadus-T to OHKO Gliscor with a +2 Bleakwind Storm, and its HP loss is partially nullified by Regenerator. However, Heavy-Duty Boots is an option on teams with poor entry hazard removal. Tornadus-T benefits from Tera Steel because it resists Stone Edge from Zamazenta, Triple Axel from Weavile, Psycho Boost from Deoxys-S, and Draco Meteor from Dragapult; this is important because these Pokemon are faster than Tornadus-T and can force it out or KO it outright. Alternatively, Tera Flying is used to boost its main STAB move. An example of where this power boost is notable is being able to 2HKO Dragonite through Multiscale with Life Orb Tera Flying Bleakwind Storm. Additional options include Dark Pulse alongside Tera Dark, which threatens a KO against Galarian Slowking at +2 with a Life Orb while still providing a coverage for Gholdengo; these variants prefer running Focus Blast on the last slot to not be walled by Kingambit, with the newfound typing letting Tornadus-T take on its Sucker Punch more comfortably as well.

This set is generally featured in bulky offense and balance teams that want a force of nature that can almost single-handedly destroy opposing bulky balance teams. The biggest problem for Tornadus-T is that in exchange for being so good against the defensive Pokemon, it has troubles against the offensive ones. Dragapult, Weavile, Deoxys-S, and Zamazenta are naturally faster and all pack powerful moves that threaten it, and Iron Valiant, a common speed control option, can also pack Thunderbolt. While Tornadus-T normally beats Ogerpon-W, if the latter Terastallizes, it can very easily win a damage trade with Ivy Cudgel. Finally, Tornadus-T is also checked by strong priority users such as Choice Band Scizor, Raging Bolt, and Kingambit. A special mention goes to Zapdos, which is one of the few defensive Pokemon that can scare Tornadus-T away. For these reasons, pair Tornadus-T with Pokemon that can handle offense but can struggle with defense. Physical setup sweepers like Kingambit and Dragonite appreciate Tornadus-T's ability to break through walls like Moltres, Galarian Weezing, Great Tusk, Dondozo, Corviknight, and Skarmory; the removal of these walls mean they can freely spam moves to their heart's content. Kingambit in particular can go toe-to-toe against Tornadus-T checks like Dragapult, as well as Weavile and Deoxys-S. Zamazenta can come in on Scizor while also drawing priority moves aimed at Tornadus-T like Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Dragonite's Extreme Speed. In return, Tornadus-T can work with Zamazenta to overwhelm Galarian Slowking and helps destroy Gholdengo, Pecharunt, and the aforementioned Skarmory and Corviknight. Ogerpon-W can help Tornadus-T in a plethora of ways. It can help overwhelm defensive cores via either its massive damage output or its tools like Knock Off and Spikes, which it can use to chip the opposing walls. Ogerpon-W can also overwhelm shared checks like Zapdos and Raging Bolt the same way. If running Life Orb as the item, consider adding hazard removal support. Great Tusk is a superb option for this, as it can also help handle Pokemon like Kingambit and Dragonite. Iron Treads is another viable option thanks to its ability to check Raging Bolt. Hatterene can also help with Magic Bounce as well as utility moves like Healing Wish and Nuzzle. Corviknight and Galarian Weezing can help with Defog while also appreciating not having to worry about Gholdengo at all. It's also recommended to pair Tornadus-T with Stealth Rock and Spikes users and Knock Off users to help wear down the enemy team. Hisuian Samurott is an excellent partner due to its access to both Ceaseless Edge and Knock Off and can also answer Pokemon like Dragapult and Deoxys-S, and in return, Tornadus-T gets rid of Galarian Weezing, Ogerpon-W, and Corviknight. Clefable has general utility moves in Stealth Rock, Knock Off, and Thunder Wave, and it can do them reliably thanks to Magic Guard. Its Thunder Wave allows Tornadus-T to outspeed faster Pokemon and unleash its wrath on them. Clefable also appreciates having Steel-types out of the way. While they don't have Knock Off, Ting-Lu and Garganacl can be quite effective, since both have entry hazards. The former stonewalls Zapdos and handles Raging Bolt, while the latter can still check Zapdos but can also take on Dragapult.

Boots Pivot.description:
Combining its high Speed, Knock Off, and Regenerator, Tornadus-T becomes an excellent pivot with Heavy-Duty Boots, being able to outlast many of its checks while supporting its teammates. U-turn enables its pivoting prowess while smacking Hisuian Samurott and Darkrai for meaningful chip damage. Knock Off wears down many answers to Tornadus-T such as Zapdos, Kyurem, and Galarian Slowking by removing their Heavy-Duty Boots, as well as Leftovers from Garganacl, Heatran, and Ting-Lu. With entry hazards, it can make Tornadus-T very hard to switch into during longer games. Heat Wave is an option to hit Steel-types like Gholdengo, Corviknight, and Kingambit while dissuading Weavile from switching in. Taunt, however, allows Tornadus-T to prevent Defog from Corviknight and Galarian Weezing, recovery attempts from Alomomola and Moltres, and status such as Gliscor's Toxic and Clefable's Thunder Wave. It also enables Tornadus-T to become a potent stallbreaker that uses Regenerator to outlast bulky walls such as Blissey and Toxapex and prevents Galarian Slowking's Chilly Reception, forcing more predictable plays for teammates to capitalize on. Tera Steel allows Tornadus-T to resist Ice-type attacks from Kyurem and Weavile as well as Enamorus's Moonblast, Dragapult's Dragon Darts and Draco Meteor, and Gholdengo's Make It Rain. Tera Fairy, meanwhile, lets it be more comfortable against Dark-type attacks like Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Darkrai's Dark Pulse while granting an immunity to Dragapult's Dragon Darts and Draco Meteor and Dragonite's Outrage. Tera Fairy also maintains a Fighting resistance for Zamazenta and Iron Valiant.

Tornadus-T's excellent support capabilities slot it onto balance and bulky offense teams, where its teammates can make up for its lack of power. Ting-Lu is an amazing teammate for its ability to stack entry hazards, allowing Tornadus-T to make its Knock Off more punishing. In addition, they form a solid defensive core, with Ting-Lu handling Electric-types like Raging Bolt and Zapdos and Tornadus-T threatening or forcing foes like Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, Great Tusk, and Ogerpon-W to Terastallize. Similar to Ting-Lu, Great Tusk and Iron Treads are great teammates for their ability to check Raging Bolt and, in the case of Iron Treads, Zapdos, while also providing Rapid Spin, allowing Tornadus-T to not fear hazards even after taking a Knock Off. Steel-types like Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Heatran resist Ice, letting them handle threats like Kyurem and, in Heatran's case, Weavile, while the Steel-types appreciate having a solid pivot into Ground-types like Iron Treads. Tornadus-T enjoys having a way to pivot in safely, as it can form a pivoting core to wear down the opposing team over longer games. Thus, it appreciates other pivots such as Galarian Slowking and Alomomola, both of which offer unique utility through Future Sight and Wish, respectively. Alomomola is an especially good teammate, as Tornadus-T provides a check to Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom, while Tornadus-T likes a solid switch-in for Weavile. Galarian Slowking provides a safe switch-in to Kyurem and Raging Bolt, with Tornadus-T in exchange threatening out Great Tusk. Teammates like Kyurem and Iron Valiant appreciate Tornadus-T pivoting them in safely; Kyurem threatens Gliscor and Alomomola, while Iron Valiant can get past Hisuian Samurott and opposing Kyurem. Other strong offensive pivots like Ogerpon-W, Raging Bolt, and Cinderace are able to overwhelm defensive foes like Corviknight and Zapdos. Ogerpon-W can immensely threaten Garganacl, Ting-Lu, and Galarian Slowking and potentially lay Spikes that Tornadus-T can capitalize on with Knock Off, while Ogerpon-W enjoys a soft check for Zamazenta. Raging Bolt similarly can wear down the aforementioned Garganacl, Ting-Lu, and Galarian Slowking while Tornadus-T uses its Ground-type immunity for Iron Treads and Great Tusk. Cinderace, on the other hand, can offer hazard control with Court Change, use Will-O-Wisp to let Tornadus-T have an easier time handling Zamazenta and Ogerpon-W, and immediately threaten Weavile.

Assault Vest.description:
Tornadus-T carves out a strong niche for itself as a Regenerator Pokemon with access to a pivoting move and Knock Off as well as a high Speed tier and Flying typing, which allow it to act as an offensive check to several threatening Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Ogerpon-W. With an Assault Vest, Tornadus-T functions as a key defensive and progress-making piece for various teams, acting as a blanket check to special attackers while bolstering its special bulk enough to reliably switch into several special attackers like mixed Iron Valiant and Choice Specs Dragapult. With its great Speed tier, it can use U-turn to pivot out of would-be threats safely such as Kyurem, Garganacl, and Raging Bolt, with Assault Vest allowing Tornadus-T to survive a Thunderclap from the latter. Knock Off allows Tornadus-T to make progress against most teams by providing item removal, crippling targets that are reliant on their items such as Moltres, Dragapult, and Pecharunt. Heat Wave lets it threaten Steel-types that would otherwise wall it like Corviknight, Iron Treads, Gholdengo, and Kingambit. Icy Wind provides speed control to cripple faster Pokemon such as Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant, Darkrai, and Zamazenta so Tornadus-T can outspeed and threaten them with Bleakwind Storm or let a teammate outrun and revenge kill them. It also hits specially defensive Gliscor for super effective damage, which would otherwise comfortably sit in front of Tornadus-T. Tera Steel flips the script against Ice-types such as Weavile and Kyurem while also granting Tornadus-T a resistance to Dragon, which allows it to more comfortably take attacks like Choice Band Dragapult's Dragon Darts and Dragon Dance Kyurem's Scale Shot. Tera Steel also lets it check the tier's Psychic-types such as Galarian Slowking and Hatterene more easily. Tera Fairy allows Tornadus-T to better check threatening Dark-type attackers such as Darkrai while maintaining a Fighting resistance, still letting it match up well against Zamazenta. It also grants Tornadus-T a Dragon immunity to more comfortably switch into Draco Meteor from Kyurem and Dragapult.

Assault Vest Tornadus-T fits best on balance teams where its several talents in one teamslot are greatly appreciated. It serves as a great partner for Pokemon such as Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Garganacl; all three of them appreciate its ability to answer the tier's Fighting-Types like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant, as well as Ogerpon-W. Tornadus-T also pairs well with entry hazard setters such as the aforementioned Garganacl and Hisuian Samurott as well as Gliscor, as they all appreciate its ability to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from hazard-weak targets. Other Regenerator Pokemon like Alomomola and Galarian Slowking work well with Tornadus-T; the former helps create a strong physically and specially defensive backbone for a team, and the latter provides an extra special wall that can better take on threats such as Zapdos. Its pivoting also facilitates offensive partners such as Zamazenta to hit the field consistently, which appreciates Tornadus-T's ability to check its most common answers such as Gholdengo, Iron Valiant, and Dragapult. Due to the choice of Assault Vest over Heavy-Duty Boots, Tornadus-T needs to be very careful to avoid Stealth Rock, as it can undercut Tornadus-T's Regenerator healing. As a result, Pokemon such as Galarian Weezing prove excellent partners for the temporal genie, and in turn, Galarian Weezing appreciates Tornadus-T's ability to switch in against special attackers that would threaten it such as Gholdengo. Tornadus-T's other glaring weakness is the tier's common Electric-types like Raging Bolt and Zapdos. Partners that can assist in dealing with these two such as Great Tusk and Ting-Lu make for excellent teammates, with the former providing hazard removal as well as checking Garganacl and Raging Bolt, while Tornadus-T can cover for some of its worst matchups such as Iron Valiant, Ogerpon-W, and Sinistcha. Ting-Lu, on the other hand, appreciates Tornadus-T removing Heavy-Duty Boots from opposing Pokemon that would be immune to its hazards, and in turn, it stonewalls Zapdos and helps in taking on a myriad of special attacks. Iron Treads is another option as a Ground-type partner that can also provide hazard control and provide support as a second Knock Off user. Tornadus-T can also struggle with several special walls and Pokemon that it can't pressure significantly with Knock Off, such as specially defensive Gliscor, Ting-Lu, and Garganacl, so partners like Ogerpon-W, Rillaboom, and Weavile can pressure these Pokemon. Tornadus-T helps the former two against Hydrapple and Sinistcha, the latter two against Iron Valiant and Iron Moth, and all three against Zamazenta. Tornadus-T may also face trouble against the few Pokemon that can outrun it, such as Weavile and Dragonite after a Dragon Dance. Pokemon that can provide speed control such as Dragapult, Zamazenta, and Choice Scarf Darkrai can ensure that anything it doesn't outrun is dealt with, allowing it to pivot around slower targets more effectively to stack Regenerator healing over the course of a game.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Bleakwind Storm provides a slightly safer STAB option that hits targets like Iron Valiant more reliably than Hurricane, but its weaker power makes it miss out on crucial KOs, notably being unable to kill any of the Ogerpon formes without prior chip. Sludge Wave provides an attack that doesn't have to worry about accuracy, making it good for picking off weakened targets like Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Alolan Ninetales. However, it comes with the drawback of making Tornadus-T unable to hit Steel-types for good neutral damage. Focus Blast's high power is great at KOing monsters like Archaludon and Bisharp, buts its low accuracy makes it very risky.

Nasty Plot.description:
Tornadus-T makes for a great late-game cleaner by virtue of its access to Nasty Plot, its great coverage, and its Speed allowing it to outspeed the likes of Cinderace, Keldeo, and Volcarona. Nasty Plot-boosted Bleakwind Storm OHKOes the likes of Great Tusk, and Ogerpon-H. Focus Blast threatens the likes of Archaludon, Heatran, and Hisuian Goodra, OHKOing the former and 2HKOing the latter two after a boost. Knock Off removes essential items such as Black Sludge from Toxapex and Clodsire, as well as Heavy-Duty Boots from Articuno and Volcanion. U-turn allows Tornadus-T to act as a great pivot while OHKOing Hoopa-U. However, Focus Blast is usually the preferred move due to its coverage and being boosted by Nasty Plot. Heat Wave covers threats that the other moves can't cover, such as Gholdengo and Articuno.

Tornadus-T appreciates entry hazard support from the likes of Skarmory and Gliscor to wear down Clodsire and Ting-Lu. In addition, Gliscor spreads status with Toxic and, with its part Ground typing, acts as a great switch-in against Electric-types such as Magnezone and Sandy Shocks, while Skarmory handles physical attackers like Roaring Moon and Weavile with Iron Defense and Body Press. Tornadus-T handles problematic threats for them such as Keldeo for Gliscor and Ogerpon-H for Skarmory. Corviknight removes hazards for Tornadus-T with Defog in case its Heavy-Duty Boots is removed, and it is able to pivot Tornadus-T into the likes of Scrafty and Archaludon safely with U-turn. Tornadus-T can handle Fire-types that threaten Corviknight like Heatran and Ogerpon-H in return. Articuno is another great defensive partner, easily brushing off hits from the likes of Choice Scarf Enamorus and Hydreigon thanks to its high special bulk. Articuno also handles Water-types like Keldeo with Freeze Dry, as well as pivot Tornadus-T in with U-turn. Choice Scarf users such as Enamorus and Landorus-T provide great speed control for the team, handling speedy threats that can force Tornadus-T out. In particular, Enamorus handles fast Dragon- and Dark-types such as Dragapult and Choice Specs Greninja, while Landorus-T threatens not only fellow Choice Scarf users like Excadrill, Hisuian Arcanine, and Heatran, but also Alolan Muk and Regieleki. Early-game wallbreakers like Landorus and Choice Band Dragonite can punch holes in the opposing team, removing problematic walls like Toxapex and Clodsire to ease Tornadus-T's late-game cleaning. Dragonite also picks off faster threats with Extreme Speed. Gyarados forms a great cleanup core with Tornadus-T, with Gyarados being able to sweep Fire and Steel teams, while Tornadus-T handles Grass, Fighting, and Dark teams.

Assault Vest.description:
Assault Vest Tornadus-T serves a key role on Flying teams as a great defensive piece thanks its solid bulk, especially when paired with Regenerator. Bleakwind Storm provides a more consistent STAB move to dissuade Iron Valiant and Urshifu-R from staying in and is unaffected by Sun. Alternatively, Hurricane can be considered since its solid damage output is able to OHKO threats like the Ogerpon formes with ease. Heat Wave allows Tornadus-T to handle Steel-types that would otherwise wall it like Gholdengo and Corviknight while also dealing solid damage to Ice-types such as Alolan Ninetales. Knock Off allows Tornadus-T to remove items on incoming special walls such as Hisuian Goodra and Blissey along with special attackers like Latios and Dragapult. Finally, U-turn allows for Tornadus-T to deal chip damage as it pivots out along with being able to escape from trapping moves from the likes of Toxapex, Heatran, and Pecharunt. Tornadus-T's Special Attack investment is required to KO Ogerpon-W and Ogerpon-H with Hurricane consistently, and the rest of its EV investment goes into HP and Speed to give it as much bulk as possible and outspeed Iron Valiant.

Tornadus-T majorly appreciates Corviknight being able to remove Stealth Rock, which allows it to get the most out of Regenerator. Corviknight also helps Tornadus-T by taking out threats like Greninja and Flutter Mane, while Corviknight appreciates the removal of its foes' held items like Rocky Helmet. Skarmory also appreciates Tornadus-T removing Rocky Helmets, allowing Body Press to do as much damage as possible against Ice- and Rock-types that threaten Tornadus-T like Weavile and Iron Boulder. Skarmory can also set entry hazards to help with Tornadus-T's offense. Gliscor's Ground typing and Poison Heal ability allow it to soak up both Electric-type attacks and status moves from the likes of Regieleki, Sandy Shocks, and Clodsire and easily remove them with Earthquake, making Tornadus-T's pivoting much safer. Dragonite appreciates Tornadus-T's ability to soften up teams by removing key threats like Ogerpon-H while staying healthy, which can allow for Dragonite to have an easier time sweeping with Dragon Dance late-game to remove dangerous targets like Raging Bolt. Choice Scarf Enamorus supports Tornadus-T by being able to check faster threats like Dragapult, Walking Wake, and Greninja with ease.

Pivot.description:
Tornadus-T is an effective pivot due to Regenerator, a Speed tier higher than threats such as Iron Valiant and Ogerpon-W, and its ability to effectively switch into Pokemon like Great Tusk and Kartana. Bleakwind Storm is preferred for higher accuracy, but Hurricane, especially when used with Flyinium Z, can be used for the extra power boost; even without the Z boost, it guarantees the OHKO on Ogerpon-W after Stealth Rock. Knock Off is vital to remove items such as Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon like Clefable, Heatran, and Toxapex, hindering their longevity. Heat Wave hits Gholdengo, Ferrothorn, and Mega Scizor. Defog is a potential option if a team does not have another form of entry hazard removal, especially since Tornadus-T has decent matchups against hazard setters such as Landorus-T and Great Tusk. However, losing the coverage to hit the aforementioned Steel-types is less than ideal. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Tornadus-T to gain Regenerator recovery even in the face of Stealth Rock; however, Flyinium Z can also be used to make attempts at revenge killing foes like Garchomp and Mega Charizard Y more efficient. The given EVs help Tornadus-T survive a Stone Edge from Zamazenta after Stealth Rock and outspeed Iron Valiant.

Tornadus-T fits on balance and bulky offense teams where its high Speed and vast amount of utility options are appreciated. Pokemon like Slowbro and Gholdengo appreciate Tornadus-T's ability to switch in on Grass- and Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Ogerpon-W, with the former also creating a Regenerator core that allows the pair to switch back and forth effortlessly against passive foes such as Toxapex and Gliscor. Wallbreakers such as Ogerpon-W and Tapu Lele take advantage of Tornadus-T's ability to pivot on defensive pieces these wallbreakers prey on, such as Gliscor and Toxapex. Electric-types such as Zapdos, Tapu Koko, and Raging Bolt are problematic for Tornadus-T, as they prevent it from gaining momentum easily, so checks to these Pokemon like Gliscor, Heatran, and Ting-Lu are all stellar partners. In return, Tornadus-T can ease matchups against foes like Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Ogerpon-W. Tornadus-T can struggle to force progress against Steel-types such as Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Heatran, so teammates that can take advantage of Tornadus-T pivoting on them such as Urshifu-R and Garchomp are appreciated.

Nasty Plot.description:
Tornadus-T acts as a formidable wallbreaker, taking advantage of its impressive Speed, solid Special Attack, and wide coverage options to set up with Nasty Plot; additionally its decent bulk and Regenerator allow it to exploit passive Pokemon, such as Corviknight and Alomomola, for setup opportunities. Nasty Plot allows Tornadus-T to boost its decent Special Attack to even greater heights, letting it break through defensive Pokemon like Toxapex, Gliscor, and Ferrothorn. Bleakwind Storm is an alternative STAB move with greater accuracy than Hurricane, although it is slightly weaker. Heat Wave hits Pokemon that are not threatened by Tornadus-T's STAB move, such as Gholdengo, Zapdos, and Ferrothorn. Focus Blast provides crucial coverage against Rock- and Steel-type foes that take little damage from Tornadus-T's STAB move and Heat Wave, such as Mega Tyranitar and Heatran, and also hits Ting-Lu for super effective damage. Taunt blocks Toxic from foes like Gliscor and Toxapex and Thunder Wave from Ferrothorn while additionally letting Tornadus-T effectively beat stall by itself. Flyinium Z allows Tornadus-T to secure KOs against the likes of Toxapex, Mega Diancie, and Mega Charizard Y, all of which get OHKOed after one Nasty Plot boost.

Tornadus-T thrives on more offensively oriented team compositions, where it can contribute by setting up and breaking through opposing teams to support its allies. Its ability to pressure foes like Great Tusk, Ogerpon-W, and Iron Valiant opens up teammates such as Gholdengo, Heatran, and Ting-Lu to play more freely. Other Pokemon that appreciate Tornadus-T's wallbreaking capabilities include Urshifu-R and Raging Bolt, as they benefit from Tornadus-T's ability to pressure their respective checks like Slowbro and Ferrothorn. Ting-Lu, Garchomp, and Gliscor are also solid partners thanks to their ability to handle Electric- and Rock-type foes like Zapdos, Tapu Koko, and Mega Diancie that threaten Tornadus-T. Landorus-T also handles these threats, as well as providing Defog support, which Tornadus-T greatly appreciates due to its Stealth Rock weakness. Ferrothorn is another notable partner, as it can switch into any attack from the likes of Tapu Koko while also providing entry hazards for Tornadus-T. Terapagos is also a solid teammate for Tornadus-T because it provides Rapid Spin support, which Tornadus-T greatly appreciates due to its Stealth Rock weakness, and it is also a natural fit for offensive teams that Tornadus-T thrives in.

Assault Vest.description:
Using the Assault Vest in combination with Regenerator makes Tornadus-T a good pivot as well as a stellar blanket check and scout to most special attackers such as Iron Valiant, Tapu Lele, and Terapagos. Its excellent Speed tier also means Tornadus-T can revenge kill threats such as Ogerpon-W, unboosted Roaring Moon, and Iron Valiant lacking Booster Energy. Bleakwind Storm is preferred for its greater accuracy compared to Hurricane and not being hindered by Mega Charizard Y’s sun, but Hurricane can be considered for its greater power, especially on rain teams, as it can OHKO Ogerpon-W after Stealth Rock. U-turn maintains momentum for wallbreakers such as Tapu Lele and Hisuian Samurott. Heat Wave hits a plethora of Steel-types such as Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Ferrothorn. Knock Off allows Tornadus-T to force meaningful progress against balance structures, removing important items from Toxapex, Ting-Lu, Heatran, and Terapagos. The given EVs allow Tornadus-T to outspeed unboosted Roaring Moon while netting a 2HKO on offensive Kingambit.

Tornadus-T can fit on both balance and offensive teams. Wallbreakers such as Raging Bolt and Ogerpon-W appreciate Tornadus-T giving them free entry against foes like Toxapex and Gliscor via U-turn while switching in on revenge killers such as Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele. Pokemon like Toxapex and Slowbro form good Regenerator cores with Tornadus-T, as they, combined with Tornadus-T, can constantly switch back and forth against passive foes such as Ferrothorn and utility Gliscor. Entry hazard removal such as Terapagos, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T ease Tornadus-T’s Stealth Rock weakness, meaning it can more easily gain Regenerator recovery. Steel-types such as Heatran and bulky Gholdengo can stop Tornadus-T in its tracks, so partners like Garchomp and Mega Lopunny are solid teammates, especially because Tornadus-T can pivot them in against these foes. Pursuit users like Mega Tyranitar and Weavile are able to trap Tornadus-T and hinder its ability to consistently check foes like Iron Valiant, so insurance against these Pokemon like Zamazenta and Toxapex is appreciated. Teammates such as Ting-Lu and Ferrothorn also appreciate Tornadus-T removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Toxapex and Alomomola, allowing their hazards to affect them and effectively checking threats such as Iron Valiant and Great Tusk. In return, they stop dangers to Tornadus-T such as Raging Bolt and Zapdos. Finally, Tornadus-T can form VoltTurn cores with Pokemon like Tapu Koko and Iron Crown, which help keep up momentum and rack up chip damage alongside Tornadus-T.

Nasty Plot Wallbreaker.description: A colorful movepool, a great Speed tier, and Regenerator make Tornadus-T one of Flying's best wallbreakers. Bleakwind Storm can be used if Tornadus-T is paired with Mega Charizard Y, as its accuracy is not affected by sun. Focus Blast grants Tornadus-T excellent neutral coverage and is able to hit most Steel- and Rock-types, like Heatran and Tyranitar, hard. Heat Wave, however, has the benefit of nailing Jirachi, Gholdengo, and Corviknight, which makes it a better option against Psychic, Ghost, and, if using Knock Off, Steel teams. In the last slot, Taunt is preferred, so Tornadus-T can safely set up on walls like Toxapex and Ting-Lu, but Knock Off's ability to cripple the likes of defensive Heatran and Galarian Slowking is worth considering. Tornadus-T has a very poor matchup against Electric-types, so Pokemon that can deal with them, such as Landorus-T and Gliscor, are must-haves. They're also able to lay down Stealth Rock and have access to Defog, making them incredible teammates. Similarly, Corviknight and Celesteela stomach most Ice-type attacks aimed at Tornadus-T, thanks to their bulk and Steel typing. Mega Charizard Y forms a terrifying wallbreaking duo alongside Tornadus-T that breaks down shared checks such as Heatran and Blissey. Setup sweepers like Dragon Dance Dragonite and Agility Thundurus-T greatly appreciate Tornadus-T weakening or removing walls for them. 88 HP and 8 Special Defense EVs can be used over Special Attack to ensure Tornadus-T lives an Ice Beam from Choice Scarf Greninja from full health.

Assault Vest.description: Assault Vest Tornadus-T acts as a fast scout for Flying teams to assess their game plan against threats like Greninja, Tapu Lele, and Tapu Koko while also revenge killing Ogerpon-W, Keldeo, and Iron Valiant. Although Tornadus-T lacks the bulk to repeatedly switch into powerful attackers, as it is 2HKOed by threats such as Greninja and Choice Specs Tapu Lele, it can reveal opposing items through the damage it receives. Heat Wave melts Steel-types like Gholdengo and OHKOes Mega Scizor. Knock Off pressures attackers like Choice Specs Tapu Lele and Greninja, as losing their items reduces their ability to break through Flying’s defensive core. It also punishes common switch-ins such as Hisuian Goodra, Galarian Slowking, and Heatran. U-turn lets Tornadus-T preserve momentum, bringing in teammates like Gliscor and Celesteela to deal with its checks such as Mega Diancie. Alternative coverage moves like Icy Wind, Sludge Bomb, and Grass Knot may also be considered; Icy Wind dissuades sweepers like Dragonite from setting up on Tornadus-T and punishes Mega Garchomp, Landorus, and Gliscor. Sludge Bomb hits Tapu Koko and Tapu Lele hard while also supplementing Tornadus-T's low damage output thanks to potentially poisoning opposing Pokemon. Grass Knot is useful as it OHKOes Mamoswine after Stealth Rock damage, with Tornadus-T surviving Choice Band Ice Shard. 92 Special Defense EVs let Tornadus-T survive Choice Specs Kyurem's Ice Beam to remove its item with Knock Off, and the Speed investment allows it to outspeed Iron Valiant. Wallbreakers like Mega Charizard Y, Landorus, and Dragonite love Tornadus-T's pivoting, which gives them more opportunities to pressure opposing teams and benefit from its ability to lure in walls like Blissey and Toxapex. Tornadus-T gets 2HKOed by most wallbreakers, so walls like Corviknight, Celesteela, and Gliscor are wanted, as they can switch in for it depending on the coverage move it scouted. Gliscor also provides entry hazard support, which lets Tornadus-T wear down walls quicker due to their repeated switch-ins and after taking Knock Off. Faster teammates like Choice Scarf Enamorus and Mega Aerodactyl that deal with Mega Lopunny, Tapu Koko, and Zeraora are appreciated, and in return, Tornadus-T scouts potential Choice Scarf users such as Greninja and Iron Moth to determine whether it is safe to stay in.

Support.description:
Thundurus is a good support Pokemon that is capable of disrupting teams like few other Pokemon can. Eerie Impulse can slow down powerful special attackers more effectively than other forms of damage control like Snarl or Vessel of Ruin, which means that Thundurus can completely neutralize the likes of Calyrex-S, Terapagos, Ursaluna-B, and Miraidon. Thunder Wave is a form of speed control that, unlike Tailwind, can generate free turns for Thundurus and its teammates. Taunt shuts down support Pokemon such as Amoonguss, preventing them from messing with Thundurus's team. Rain Dance allows Thundurus to both disrupt sun teams dependent on weather from Groudon or Koraidon and power up its teammate's Water-type attacks. Covert Cloak prevents Thundurus from being stopped by Fake Out from the likes of Incineroar and Rillaboom, so it does not fear them on the first turn and can use its support moves unperturbed. With 252 HP EVs, 156 Defense EVs, and a Bold nature, Thundurus will be able to take Tera Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R or a sun- and Orichalchum Pulse-boosted Flare Blitz from Koraidon, giving it just enough survivability to get off a final support move. 92 Special Defense EVs still give it room to survive many powerful special attacks, including Choice Specs Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage and Choice Specs Beads of Ruin Terapagos-S's Tera Starstorm. Tera Dark gives Thundurus an immunity to Prankster, letting it still get off its support options in the face of faster Prankster Tornadus and Whimsicott. It also gives it a resistance to Calyrex-S's STAB moves, letting it take a move in a pinch.

Unlike Tornadus, Thundurus's form of speed control is both less useful and easier to stop; Thunder Wave can only affect the relative Speed of a single Pokemon on the field, whereas Tailwind will affect both Pokemon. What's more, Dark-, Ground-, and Electric-types, such as Chi-Yu, Landorus, and Miraidon, are completely immune to Thundurus's Thunder Wave, so they can threaten it and its team easily. Chien-Pao deserves a special mention, as it ignores Thunder Wave and threatens Thundurus with an OHKO. Fighting-types like Zamazenta-C and Urshifu-R are great partners for Thundurus because they deal with Dark-types very effectively. Zamazenta-C is able to boost its physical bulk with Iron Defense and benefits from Thundurus reducing the special damage from their foes, making it difficult to bring down. Urshifu-R appreciates the fact that Thundurus can summon rain to boost the power of Surging Strikes. Both appreciate Taunt, which shuts down Amoonguss. Rillaboom is a common partner to assist Thundurus in shutting down Miraidon by replacing the Terrain; it also deals with Ground- and Electric-types that irritate Thundurus by resisting their attacks and threatening them in return with its strong STAB moves and High Horsepower, respectively. Indeedee-F and Farigiraf have the ability to block Prankster support moves, so a Dark-type that scares them away is appreciated; Incineroar and Chien-Pao are common choices for such a role. Calyrex-S is also a solid partner for Thundurus, as it appreciates Thundurus's speed control and damage control, the ability to shut down sun teams with Rain Dance, and the fact that Thundurus answers Amoonguss with Taunt. Eerie Impulse is generally helpful against Terapagos-S, which can give Calyrex-S issues. Though both Calyrex-S and Thundurus dislike Dark-types, Calyrex-S can Terastallize Fairy and use Draining Kiss to improve the matchup. Thundurus's Thunderbolt also doesn't do a lot of damage, so foes can ignore it completely if it is unable to utilize its support moves.

Disruptive Support.description:
• This Thundurus set is mainly used to reduce foes' Speed and Special Attack. Prankster Thunder Wave can be used as speed control, allowing teammates with middling Speed such as Urshifu-R and Dragonite to move first, while introducing the chance to fully paralyze the foe. Eerie Impulse can weaken almost any special attacker, saving its teammates from threats like Flutter Mane and Raging Bolt.

  • Taunt is useful for shutting down Spore from Amoonguss and Trick Room setters like Porygon2. It can also be used to stop Flutter Mane from using its own Thunder Wave to slow down Thundurus's team and fish for full paralysis. Electric Terrain can be used to enable Raging Bolt to do heavy damage with Rising Voltage or deny Spore from Amoonguss even if it has Mental Herb or Tera Dark.

  • Covert Cloak prevents Thundurus from being double targeted by Fake Out and a strong attack, ensuring it can get off a key Thunder Wave or Eerie Impulse.

  • This spread lets Thundurus survive a Tera Water Mystic Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and a Tera Normal Extreme Speed from Choice Band Dragonite with Sword of Ruin active. It also almost always survives an Ice Spinner from Jolly Chien-Pao. The remaining EVs are put into Special Defense to maximize bulk.

  • Tera Water is used to resist Ice-type attacks like Icicle Crash and Ice Spinner from Chien-Pao and Water-type attacks like Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R. It also helps against common attacks like Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-W, as well as Heat Wave from Chi-Yu. Tera Steel similarly provides a resistance to Ice-type attacks, as well as a generally solid defensive profile that grants resistances to Flutter Mane's Fairy-type attacks and Iron Crown's STAB attacks.

Offensive Pivot.description: With its superb Speed tier, colorful coverage options, and Heavy-Duty Boots to not be worn down by entry hazards, Thundurus is a decent offensive pivot in the metagame, getting the jump on other notable offensive threats such as Mienshao, Mega Gallade, Iron Moth, and Keldeo. Knock Off allows Thundurus to cripple Clefable and Assault Vest Tangrowth. Focus Blast allows Thundurus to deal heavy damage to Excadrill, Tyranitar, and Hydreigon, also letting it serve as a decent offensive check to the first under sand. However, Grass Knot and Psychic are powerful coverage options that can 2HKO Gastrodon and Hippowdon and most variants of Mega Venusaur and Amoonguss. U-turn allows Thundurus to maintain momentum but can be exchanged for Volt Switch to maintain damage against Rotom-W and Slowbro at the cost of needing to predict around Ground-types. Alternatively, Thunder Wave in conjunction with Prankster allows Thundurus to act as an emergency check to boosted threats such as Autotomize Celesteela or cripple a faster threat such as Mega Aerodactyl or Iron Boulder, making it easier for its teammates to pick them off. Thundurus fits best on offense teams that can compensate for its frailty and are best suited to its aggressive playstyle. Other offensive pivots such as Victini and Life Orb Mienshao tend to lure in physically defensive targets such as Slowbro and Buzzwole, providing Thundurus with a safe entry point; in return, they can threaten common specially defensive Pokemon such as Blissey and Assault Vest Tangrowth that are typically used to check Thundurus. Thundurus is very vulnerable to Knock Off, which Pokemon such as Clefable and Scizor can potentially use to cripple it. Thus, teammates that can safely absorb these hits such as Skarmory and Slowbro are valuable partners that can also serve to check faster threats like Zeraora, Iron Boulder, and Mega Aerodactyl. Lastly, certain defensive pivots such as Clefable and Tyranitar can support Thundurus with hazards, which makes it much more effective at wearing down other checks such as Garganacl and Mega Venusaur.

Nasty Plot.description: Thanks to Thundurus's wide variety of coverage, access to Nasty Plot, and high Speed that allows it to outspeed Iron Moth and the Ogerpon formes, it functions as a hard-hitting sweeper. Nasty Plot further boosts Thundurus's high Special Attack, allowing it to OHKO Scream Tail, defensive Gholdengo, and RegenVest Manaphy at +2, while Knock Off can be used on Magic Guard sets to remove Assault Vest from Hisuian Goodra, Meloetta, and Iron Hands. Focus Blast gives Thundurus super effective coverage against Roaring Moon, Heatran, and Volt Absorb Empoleon. Psychic enables Thundurus to hit Iron Hands, Great Tusk, and Landorus; alternatively, Grass Knot consistently 2HKOes Ting-Lu and Swampert while still OHKOing Great Tusk, at the cost of Sheer Force sets taking Life Orb recoil. Sheer Force avoids Life Orb chip damage and boosts Thundurus's power, allowing it to 2HKO Deoxys-D and max HP Scream Tail after Stealth Rock, while Magic Guard also avoids Life Orb damage and chip damage from Stealth Rock. Thundurus struggles to sweep opposing teams possessing fast revenge killers such as Roaring Moon, Azelf, and Choice Scarf Gholdengo; therefore, it requires allies like Corviknight and Empoleon that easily switch into these threats and pivot it in. Fast special attacking pivots such as Azelf and Iron Moth appreciate Thundurus's ability to wallbreak, as it allows them to clean more easily.

Thundurus-T's extremely high Special Attack is elevated to terrifying levels using Nasty Plot, such as OHKOing offensive Heatran after Stealth Rock. Agility complements this by letting Thundurus-T outspeed the entire unboosted metagame. Dark Pulse hits Latios and Skeledirge. Focus Blast can be used to hit and remove Excadrill, as well as OHKO specially defensive Heatran and Tyranitar after a Nasty Plot. 100 Speed EVs allow Thundurus-T to avoid being revenge killed by threats like Choice Scarf Latios and Ogerpon-C after an Agility. The HP and Special Defense EVs let it survive Soul Dew Latios's Draco Meteor from full HP, with the remaining the EVs invested into Special Attack. Together with Sitrus Berry’s crucial recovery, the bulk investments also enhance Thundurus-T's survivability, ensuring it can safely reach the ideal sweeping position and begin breaking through the opponent’s team. Tera Steel is an alternative to Tera Flying that prevents threats such as Ogerpon-C and Latios from interrupting Thundurus-T's sweep.

Nasty Plot Thundurus-T is a staple of hyper offense teams, which specialize in pressuring the opponent's resources into opening an opportunity for Thundurus-T and other threats to wreak havoc on foes. Thundurus-T is greatly complemented by entry hazard setters, such as Excadrill, which help weaken foes that would tank a +2 Thunderbolt such as bulky Heatran and Fezandipiti. Excadrill and Donphan provide Rapid Spin support, which prevents Thundurus-T from taking Stealth Rock damage. Taunt users such as Heatran and Grimmsnarl pair well with Thundurus-T, as they can also prevent Stealth Rock. Additionally, Grimmsnarl can set up dual screens to provide easier boosting opportunities. Thundurus-T has excellent synergy with fast offensive threats such as Greninja, which can help overwhelm common checks like Latios, Clodsire, and Tinkaton while appreciating Thundurus-T’s ability to pressure bulky Water-type Pokemon like Toxapex. Physical attackers such as Azumarill, Ogerpon, and Ogerpon-C help overpower Ground-types such as Excadrill and Sandy Shocks as well as Unaware users such as Clodsire. Alternatively, setup sweepers like Take Heart Manaphy and Air Balloon Revavroom can capitalize on Clodsire.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Flying

Nasty Plot can be used over Volt Switch to increase Thundurus-T's wallbreaking power, allowing it to easily break Water- and Flying-type teams. Psychic, Sludge Wave, and Thunder Wave are all options that can be used over Focus Blast to achieve different results. Psychic allows Thundurus-T to hit Clodsire and Amoonguss, Sludge Wave can check Hydrapple and Clefable, and Thunder Wave provides Flying teams with a form of speed control by slowing down foes like Dragonite and Gouging Fire. U-turn can be used over Volt Switch to allow Thundurus-T to reliably pivot against foes with an Electric immunity.

Offensive Pivot (Flying).description:
Thundurus-T finds a solid niche on Flying teams thanks to its incredible Special Attack, solid Speed, and Electric immunity that allows it to find safe entry against Electric-type moves. Thunderbolt is able to threaten Water- and Flying-types such as Toxapex, Pelipper, and Assault Vest Tornadus-T. Volt Switch helps it pivot out on threats attempting to handle it, such as Hisuian Goodra and Blissey. Grass Knot allows Thundurus-T to hit Ground-types like Swampert, Great Tusk, and Ursaluna that would otherwise wall it. Finally, Focus Blast remove Steel- and Rock-types like Iron Treads, Archaludon, and Tyranitar.

Skarmory and Gliscor provide excellent support to Thundurus-T, being able to deal with Rock-types such as Iron Boulder, Kleavor, and Terrakion reliably, as well as setting entry hazards to chip down threats like Hisuian Goodra and Archaludon. Skarmory can also support Thundurus-T by dealing with Ice-types like Weavile and Mamoswine with Body Press. Corviknight can similarly check Ice- and Rock-types with Iron Head and Body Press, use Defog to remove Stealth Rock if Thundurus-T loses its Heavy-Duty Boots, and give Thundurus-T safe entry with U-turn. Articuno provides a comfortable answer to Ground-types like Gliscor and Landorus, which can handle Thundurus-T's Grass Knot. Furthermore, Articuno can come in on special threats such as Kyurem and Greninja that Thundurus-T cannot handle. Dragonite acts a physical wallbreaker, handling specially defensive walls like Blissey, Hisuian Goodra, and Clodsire, while appreciating Thundurus-T's ability to eliminate physically defensive walls such as Galarian Weezing and Sableye. Choice Scarf Enamorus can threaten Dragon-type foes attemping to handle Thundurus-T, such as Dragapult, Kyurem, and Choice Band Roaring Moon. Landorus forms a special wallbreaking core, removing Fire-types like Skeledirge, Hisuian Arcanine, and Heatran with ease. Landorus can also run a Choice Scarf and use U-turn to create a VoltTurn core with Thundurus-T while also OHKOing the Ogerpon formes with Sludge Wave after Stealth Rock damage.

Nasty Plot (Electric).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Pivot.description:
• Thanks to Volt Absorb, Thundurus-T is an excellent offensive pivot that makes masterful use of Terastallization!

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot is highly recommended for dealing massive damage to Ground-types, such as Ting-Lu and Ursaluna, without Terastallizing in addition to being a secondary attack to hit Urshifu-R while Choice locked into an attack.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast has reliability issues, but it's Thundurus-T's best shot of dealing big damage to Hisuian Goodra and Wo-Chien.

  • Sludge Bomb: Sludge Bomb is a more niche option, giving Thundurus-T a more reliable way to deal damage to Wo-Chien and Meowscarada at the cost of doing nothing to Hisuian Goodra.

  • Timid versus Modest: Timid is the best nature, allowing Thundurus-T to outspeed key threats, such as Urshifu-R, and at least Speed tie with opposing Thundurus-T. Modest is usable with Choice Specs, allowing Thundurus-T to outspeed up to Jolly Baxcalibur and Great Tusk, and the extra power can be handy in some situations, such as usually 2HKOing specially defensive Clodsire with Tera Blast Flying.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Thundurus-T is perfectly fine with its base typing, it makes such good use of Terastallization that it'll often Terastallize.

  • Flying: Tera Flying makes Tera Blast a powerful STAB option with very few resistances while gaining no extra weaknesses thanks to Volt Absorb.

  • Ice: Not only does Tera Ice give Thundurus-T powerful coverage against Ground- and Grass-types like Landorus-T and Wo-Chien, it also gives an important resistance to Iron Bundle's and Chien-Pao's Ice-type attacks.

  • Water: Tera Water is a fantastic defensive option, turning Thundurus-T into an excellent check against Regieleki and Zapdos while still giving it a good coverage option against Landorus-T. However, it still retains Thundurus-T's weakness to Freeze-Dry.

Items

  • Choice Specs versus Choice Scarf: Choice Specs makes Thundurus-T difficult to wall without an extremely sturdy special wall, with even Pokemon like Clodsire and Cresselia at risk of a 2HKO. Choice Scarf, on the other hand, allows Thundurus-T to double as a good revenge killer, outspeeding major threats like Iron Bundle and Chien-Pao.

  • Assault Vest: While Thundurus-T isn't known for its bulk, Volt Absorb means Assault Vest makes Thundurus-T more effective at checking other Electric-types, especially when using bulkier EV spreads.

Bulkier EV Spreads

  • 20 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA / 4 SpD / 228 Spe with Timid: This Assault Vest spread outspeeds both Urshifu formes and takes 70% maximum from Timid Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry without sacrificing power.

  • 188 SpA / 68 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid or Modest**: This spread is optimized for Assault Vest, letting Thundurus-T survive Timid Choice Specs Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry without Terastallizing.

Minor Optimizations
  • 0-3 Attack IV: Foes that commonly run Foul Play such as Amoonguss and Rotom-W have more powerful moves to use against Thundurus-T, but there's no drawback to minimizing Foul Play's damage.

Nasty Plot.description:
• Thundurus-T's massive Special Attack stat and array of immunities make it a good user of Nasty Plot.

  • Grass Knot: Grass Knot is integral for potentially OHKOing physically defensive Ting-Lu after a boost and usually OHKOing offensive Ursaluna.

  • Life Orb versus Sitrus Berry: Life Orb is great for wallbreaking, allowing Thundurus-T to potentially OHKO Ting-Lu with a boosted Grass Knot. Sitrus Berry is still a good option, though allowing Thundurus-T to instantly restore some health after being hit by Ruination, as long as its maximum HP is an even number.

Other Options

  • Substitute: When paired with Tera Water, Substitute lets Thundurus-T set up on Garganacl.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast's unreliability makes it hard to recommend for most teams, but it's the only way Thundurus-T will break through Hisuian Goodra without Terastallization.

  • Taunt: Giving up coverage is risky, but Taunt shuts down a lot of defensive counterplay against Thundurus-T such as Whirlwind Ting-Lu and Toxic Clodsire.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Thundurus-T's typing is totally functional for sweeping and wallbreaking, but Terastallization makes it far harder to revenge kill thanks to Volt Absorb.

  • Flying: Tera Flying gives Thundurus-T a powerful STAB option, letting it cleave through specially bulky foes, like Water Absorb Clodsire, particularly easily.

  • Water: While Tera Water does leave Thundurus-T vulnerable to certain Pokemon, such as Water Absorb Clodsire and Hisuian Goodra, it's a fantastic defensive Tera type that lets it deal with other common Electric-types that Terastallize like Regieleki and Zapdos.

  • Ice: Tera Ice is a great offensive option, letting Thundurus-T cleave through most Ground-types that aren't weak to Grass such as Landorus-T and Clodsire. Thundurus-T even makes good defensive use of it, resisting Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry.

Bulkier EV Spreads
  • 108 HP / 4 Def / 140 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid: This EV spread lets Thundurus-T survive Timid Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry, if it doesn't have an offensive item, making it a good choice for more defensive items Thundurus-T may use such as Sitrus Berry.
Minor Optimizations
  • 0-3 Attack IV: Thundurus-T isn't getting hit by Foul Play that often, but a lower Attack IV is marginally useful regardless.

Bolstering an incredible Special Attack stat combined with a great movepool makes Thundurus-T an extremely threatening wallbreaker. Focus Blast nails foes such as Hisuian Goodra, Volt Absorb Empoleon, and Volt Absorb Corviknight. Psychic hits Great Tusk and Iron Hands, while Grass Knot can let Thundurus-T lure in and take out Swampert while still hitting Great Tusk for super effective damage. Nasty Plot boosts Thundurus-T's Special Attack to nuclear levels, allowing it to OHKO Hisuian Goodra and Blissey with Focus Blast after slight chip damage. Fast specially offensive pivots such as Iron Moth, Choice Scarf Azelf, and Latios appreciate Thundurus-T's incredible wallbreaking power, as they can take advantage of weakened special walls such as Swampert, Manaphy, and Meloetta. Thundurus-T loves slow, defensive pivots such as Corviknight, physically defensive Manaphy, and Swampert, as they can take on faster threats such as Iron Boulder, Chien-Pao, and Azelf, which all threaten to KO it, while also being able to safely pivot it in. Entry hazard Removal from the likes of Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Mandibuzz is also helpful, as Thundurus-T is very vulnerable to Stealth Rock. Sticky Web support from a teammate like Smeargle or Ribombee is another option, as it can give Thundurus-T the opportunity to outpace previously mentioned revenge killers.

Electrium Z (Flying).description: Thundurus-T makes for a great setup sweeper on Flying teams thanks to its access to Agility, high Special Attack, and great coverage. Hidden Power Ice forms a great BoltBeam combination with Thunderbolt, threatening Ground-types such as the Landorus formes, Gliscor, and Garchomp, with the removal of the former two allowing it to sweep Flying teams late-game. Grass Knot handles certain Ground-types better than Hidden Power Ice such as Great Tusk, Gastrodon, and physically defensive Ting-Lu. Agility allows Thundurus-T to outspeed and threaten normally faster foes such as Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and rain-boosted Mega Swampert. Gigavolt Havoc allows Thundurus-T to immediately remove bulky threats such as Rotom-W, Hatterene, and Mega Gallade as well as hindrances to its sweep like specially defensive Celesteela, Toxapex, and Ogerpon-W. Gliscor and Landorus make for great partners, as they alleviate pressure from Thundurus-T, cover the Electric matchup, and set up entry hazards. Additionally, Gliscor provides pivoting via U-turn and removes items such as Heavy-Duty Boots from Dragonite and Zapdos, while Landorus's coverage allows it to cover threats such as Mega Charizard X, Tyranitar, and Tapu Bulu. Entry hazard removal from Corviknight and Mantine is appreciated by Thundurus-T due to its vulnerability to Stealth Rock. Additionally, Corviknight and Celesteela handle Fairy- and Rock-types like Tapu Bulu, Mega Diancie, and Iron Boulder. Early-game wallbreakers such as Tornadus-T and Mega Charizard Y remove walls that Thundurus-T struggles with such as Mega Venusaur and Ferrothorn. In return, they appreciate Thundurus-T's Electric immunity. Choice Scarf Enamorus provides great speed control, with it potentially being able to sweep through Dragon and Dark teams that lack a proper answer; it also provides Healing Wish support to potentially re-enable a sweep from Thundurus-T. In return, it handles Steel-types for Thundurus-T like Corviknight and Mega Scizor. Thundurus-T's ability to threaten walls such as Toxapex, Great Tusk, and Ting-Lu can also enable other sweepers like Dragonite, Mega Aerodactyl, and Galarian Moltres to start a sweep of their own.

Setup Sweeper.description:
• Being the sole Electric-type of the tier, Zekrom can remove defensive Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Primal Kyogre, Arceus-Water, and Yveltal. Zekrom's ability, Teravolt, also allows it to break through Dondozo, making it a strong wallbreaker for hyper offense structures.
  • Outrage, when paired with Dragonium Z, becomes a powerful nuke option for Zekrom to use against Pokemon like Primal Groudon, Arceus-Ground, Giratina-O, and Eternatus, all of which resist or are immune to Bolt Strike.
  • Substitute eases predictions, as Zekrom commonly forces switches, and it blocks status moves such as Will-O-Wisp from Giratina-O and Toxic from support Arceus formes. It also helps Zekrom set up more easily against Pokemon like Ho-Oh, which attempts to burn Zekrom with Sacred Fire. Roost can be used to give Zekrom more longevity throughout a match and as it sets up.
  • The given EVs allow Zekrom to always outspeed Deoxys-A after a boost while ensuring it survives uninvested Judgment from Arceus-Fairy and two Earth Powers from utility Arceus formes. Alternatively, the second EV spread allows Zekrom to OHKO Ho-Oh, Mega Mewtwo Y, and Primal Kyogre without any boosts, 2HKO defensive Necrozma-DM and Extreme Killer Arceus, and OHKO Zacian-C and Dondozo at +1. The Adamant nature also gives Zekrom better chances to OHKO Primal Groudon with +1 Devastating Drake after Stealth Rock while always outspeeding Necrozma-DM, but it cannot outspeed Zacian-C after a boost.
  • Zekrom's unique typing allows it to take hits from Mega Salamence, Primal Kyogre, and Necrozma-DM's STAB moves; however, its exploitable weaknesses and lack of ability to serve as a wall make this trait only useful in a pinch, as Zekrom shouldn't be taking many hits if it wants to sweep effectively. In the scenario where Zekrom struggles to set up, unboosted Devastating Drake is a solid option for weakening foes such as Primal Kyogre, Primal Groudon and Giratina-O to let Zekrom's teammates handle them more easily.
  • Primal Kyogre makes a great partner to Zekrom with its ability to check Primal Groudon, wearing it down for Zekrom to clean up with its Z-Move afterwards. Offensive Necrozma-DM breaks through Fairy-types like Arceus-Fairy and Zacian-C for Zekrom to more comfortably use Devastating Drake while also allowing Zekrom to use Outrage once said Fairy-types aren't a factor.
  • Strong physical attackers like Marshadow and Arceus appreciate Zekrom's ability to break through Dondozo, Giratina, and Primal Groudon. Strong special attackers like Calm Mind Arceus formes, Primal Kyogre, and Eternatus also appreciate Zekrom breaking through special walls like Ho-Oh and Chansey, while they can help wear down physical walls like Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground so Zekrom can break through them more easily with Dragonium Z.
  • Suicide leads like Shuckle and Smeargle can set up Sticky Web for Zekrom, assisting the secondary EV spread with its drop in Speed while also setting additional entry hazards to meet important damage thresholds; in return, Zekrom offensively pressures Ho-Oh and Yveltal and dissuades them from using Defog to remove Sticky Web.

Life Orb.description:
• Sheer Force unlocks the full potential of Life Orb, as its damaging recoil is negated by the ability while using moves with secondary effects, like Earth Power and Sludge Wave.
  • Earth Power is Landorus's primary STAB move, handling Steel-types like Metagross and Iron Crown, Electric-types such as Raging Bolt and Iron Hands, and common Poison-types such as Sneasler and Pecharunt.
  • Sludge Wave allows Landorus to have the best matchup against Grass-types such as non-Assault Vest Rillaboom and non-Kebia Berry Serperior, as well as Fairy-types such as Encore + Disable Alolan Ninetales and Iron Valiant lacking Ice-type moves.
  • Smack Down helps Landorus against Flying-types such as Corviknight and Zapdos, as well as common Air Balloon Pokemon like Heatran. It also has a chance to OHKO Volcarona with no defensive investment.
  • Nasty Plot gives Landorus consistency against Weakness Policy Iron Crown and allows it to keep up with Air Balloon Registeel's Amnesia boosts. Alternatively, Protect may be used to beat Custap Berry users such as Skeledirge consistently.
  • Landorus has a great advantage against many top-tier Pokemon, including all Steel-, Electric-, Fire-and Poison-types. This lets it serve as a strong glue to use alongside partners such as Meowscarada and Primarina, which help mitigate its vulnerability to prevalent Water- and Dragon-types like Manaphy, Walking Wake, and Roaring Moon.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ground (Gravity Breaker)

Nasty Plot can allow Landorus to become nearly unwallable, as even the bulkiest special wall, Blissey, will collapse to Landorus's attacks after a single Nasty Plot and minor chip damage. However, this requires giving up either valuable coverage or Gravity, which can hurt Landorus's teammates. Flying (All-out Attacker)

Stealth Rock can be used over Rock Slide to free up moveslots on teammates like Gliscor and Skarmory.

All-out Attacker (Flying).description:
Landorus serves as an incredible offensive threat for Flying teams thanks to its sky high Special Attack when boosted by Sheer Force and Life Orb, easily cleaning through threats like Archaludon, Ceruledge, and Toxapex with Earth Power without worry. Focus Blast nails Ice- and Dark-types such as Kyurem and Ting-Lu along with handling Air Balloon Heatran and Skarmory. Psychic crushes non-Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Galarian Weezing while also popping Gholdengo's Air Balloon. Alternatively, Sludge Wave better handles Fairy-types like Primarina and Hatterene. Finally, Rock Slide removes Articuno and Volcarona.

Landorus greatly appreciates specially defensive Corviknight thanks to it being able to come in on the likes of Latios, Greninja, and Iron Valiant then check them with Iron Head. Corviknight can also remove Stealth Rock with Defog and bring Landorus in with U-turn. Skarmory can check physical attackers that threaten Landorus such as Meowscarada and Mamoswine with Body Press alongside Blissey. Skarmory can also provide entry hazard support with Stealth Rock and Spikes to wear down checks like Assault Vest Gallade, Hoopa-U, and the aforementioned Mamoswine. Gliscor provides a defensive Ground-type more capable of setting Stealth Rock and spreading Toxic to wear down foes such as Tornadus-T, Ogerpon-C, and Dragonite. Assault Vest Tornadus-T can handle foes like opposing Landorus, Choice Specs Hisuian Zoroark, and Iron Moth along with using Knock Off to remove problematic held items from foes like Porygon2's Eviolite and opposing Tornadus-T's Assault Vest. Dragonite provides a strong physical wallbreaker capable of entering in on Water-types such as Barraskewda and Urshifu-R, picking off faster threats such as Iron Valiant and Meowscarada with Extreme Speed, and breaking special walls such as Blissey and Corviknight with options like Outrage and Fire Punch. Articuno can help pressure Water- and Flying-types such as Swampert, Pelipper, and Gliscor with Freeze-Dry while also being capable of coming in on the likes of Latios and Primarina.

Choice Scarf (Flying).description:
With a Choice Scarf, Landorus becomes a devastating revenge killer for Flying teams, being able to outspeed and check the likes of Raging Bolt, the Ogerpon formes, and Volcarona. Earth Power handily removes Steel-, Fire-, and Electric-types such as Archaludon, Iron Moth, and Raging Bolt. Sludge Wave checks the Ogerpon formes after minor chip damage as well as Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Primarina. Rock Slide can enable Landorus to handily deal with +1 Volcarona along with Flying-types such as Moltres and Articuno, while Focus Blast with a Timid nature can deal with Air Balloon threats like Iron Treads and Heatran along with Ice- and Dark-types such as Kyurem and non-Choice Scarf Darkrai. Lastly, U-turn can keep up momentum for Flying teams along with checking Hoopa-U.

Landorus enjoys teammates like Moltres and Skarmory that can come in on faster threats like Triple Axel from Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Ice Shard from Mamoswine and Weavile and pressure them back with Flamethrower and Body Press, respectively. Moltres can further assist Landorus by threatening Skarmory and Corviknight and using U-turn to pivot it in. Skarmory can reliably set entry hazards like Spikes to wear down would-be switch-ins such as Swampert and Assault Vest Gallade and use Whirlwind to prevent setup from the likes of Belly Drum Azumarill. Corviknight can check Flutter Mane for Landorus along with providing Defog support to prevent Landorus from being worn down by Stealth Rock. Gliscor set entry hazards while being able to use Toxic to put checks to Landorus like Mandibuzz, Sinistcha, and Ting-Lu on a timer. Articuno can check Water- and opposing Flying-types such as Walking Wake, Pelipper, and Gliscor with Freeze-Dry while taking Ice Beam from threats such as Latios and Greninja comfortably. Dragonite is a strong physical wallbreaker that is capable of removing special walls like Blissey and Ting-Lu while apprecating Landorus's ability to removal physical walls like Hippowdon and Galarian Weezing. With Dragon Dance and Roost, Dragonite can also serve as a solid gameplan against Water-type threats such Barraskewda. Assault Vest Tornadus-T can sponge special attacks from threats like Choice Scarf Spectrier and Hisuian Zoroark and use Knock Off to deal with them as well as removing Assault Vest from threats like Gallade and and Primarina.

Gravity breaker (Ground).description:
Landorus serves as Ground's premier special wallbreaker and Gravity setter, capable of making otherwise-problematic Flying-types such as Skarmory and Moltres easy prey for both itself and its teammates. Earth Power nails threats such as Hippowdon, Gholdengo, and Avalugg along with removing Skarmory and Corviknight after Gravity. Focus Blast hits Ice-, Dark-, and Normal-types like Kyurem, Scrafty, and Porygon2. Sludge Wave threatens Grass- and Fairy-types like Sinistcha, Hydrapple, and Primarina. Alternatively, Psychic allows Landorus to check Fighting-types like Urshifu-R and Sneasler along with popping Gholdengo's Air Balloon.

Mamoswine and Landorus form a great wallbreaking core, with Mamoswine appreciating Gravity to prevent Icicle Crash from missing and, in return, using Icicle Crash to remove Grass- and Flying-types like Amoonguss, Gliscor, and Tornadus-T. Mamoswine can also use Ice Shard to handle faster threats like Meowscarada and Dragonite. Water Absorb Clodsire can assist against powerful special threats like Keldeo, Walking Wake, and Flutter Mane while also providing Toxic and Toxic Spikes to wear down special walls such as Assault Vest Gallade and Swampert. Hippowdon provides Stealth Rock to wear down Flying-types like Choice Band Dragonite and Enamorus, along with setting sand to further wear down targets. Sand Rush Excadrill can outspeed and check faster foes like Meowscarada and Ogerpon formes for Landorus, along with using Iron Head to handle Ice-types such as Mamoswine and Weavile. Mixed Garchomp can use Draco Meteor to threaten opposing Dragon-types like Kyurem and Dragonite, along with being able to use Fire Blast to remove Bug-types like Scizor. Choice Scarf Great Tusk can outspeed and use Close Combat to handle Dark-type threats like Darkrai and Choice Band Meowscarada, along with using coverage like Knock Off to hit Dragapult and Latios.

Choice Scarf Landorus (Ground).description:
Although Landorus typically runs Sheer Force and Life Orb, Choice Scarf Landorus is a reliable form of speed control alongside its Ground-type friends. Earth Power can check Steel- and Poison-types like Archaludon and Iron Moth while also doing great neutral damage. Sludge Wave is great coverage to deal with Fairy- and Grass-types like Iron Valiant and the Ogerpon formes after minor chip damage. Focus Blast checks threatening Dark-types like Choice Specs Greninja and non-Choice Scarf Meowscarada while also hitting Steel-types like Skarmory that Earth Power can't. Rock Slide with a Naive nature is a good alternative to deal with Flying-types like Articuno and Moltres that Ground can struggle against while also checking Volcarona. U-turn allows Landorus to swap out while also checking Hoopa-U.

This style of set is typically ran on sandless Ground teams, so having a defensive partner like Quagsire is effective, as with Unaware and great Defense investment, Quagsire can take hits from threats like Urshifu-R and Belly Drum Azumarill while also providing status and entry hazard support with Toxic, Spikes, and Stealth Rock. Clodsire is Ground's best Water-immune Pokemon, so having it paired with Landorus in front of other threats like Ogerpon-W and Choice Band Barraskewda is very appreciated as an immediate switch-in. Clodsire also can spread status and set hazards to help Landorus sweep late-game as well. Gliscor can also be a great pairing with Landorus, as it has a plethora of options to either be a defensive partner, a secondary wallbreaker, or an additional status and hazard spreader with reliable recovery thanks to Poison Heal and Toxic Orb along with Protect to scout for Choice-locked users. Iron Treads effectively pairs well with Landorus, as not only can it take Ice-type hits reliably, but it also provides hazard removal with Rapid Spin. Mixed Garchomp complements Landorus as well, as it has access to hazards while also being a reliable check to Dragon-types like Kyurem and Hydreigon with Life Orb Draco Meteor as well as Corviknight with Fire Blast. Great Tusk is an alternative defensive switch-in that has access to hazard removal with Rapid Spin; it can also remove items with Knock Off from faster Choice-locked Pokemon like Meowscarada. Mamoswine pairs as a secondary wall-breaker: although it is slower, it can utilize a Choice Band to defeat Flying-types that threaten Great Tusk like Tornadus-T and Gliscor while also dealing great damage to the Steel / Flying types like Corviknight and Skarmory. Mamoswine is also a great switch-in to Flying teams that use Articuno, thanks to its neutrality to Ice and ability Thick Fat.

Life Orb.description:
Set Details

  • Landorus is a powerful offensive Pokemon able to threaten massive damage to many common metagame fixtures with its Life Orb- and Sheer Force-boosted Earth Power, Sludge Bomb, and Sandsear Storm.
  • Sludge Bomb allows Landorus to threaten super effective damage into Tera Fairy Miraidon, Ogerpon-H, Ogerpon-W, Grimmsnarl, and any other Pokemon that utilize Tera Fairy.
  • Sandsear Storm provides Landorus with powerful, spread Ground-type damage for Miraidon, Zamazenta-C, and Incineroar. Taunt gives Landorus a great option into Pokemon that use dual screens, Wide Guard, or Trick Room, shutting down those options for Pokemon like Grimmsnarl and Lunala.
  • Life Orb and Sheer Force enable Landorus to pick up most of its KOs, most notably OHKOing Miraidon and Incineroar with Earth Power and 2HKOing Rillaboom with Sludge Bomb.
  • The offensive investment allows Landorus to OHKO Urshifu-R with no defensive investment with Earth Power, while Landorus's defensive investment allows it to live a Choice Band Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R when Landorus is Terastallized, as well as living a Choice Specs Miraidon's Draco Meteor when Landorus is behind Light Screen.
  • Tera Poison allows Landorus to remove its weaknesses to Water- and Ice-type attacks like Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and Ice Spinner from Chien-Pao that typically give it a lot of trouble while increasing the power of Sludge Bomb, which most notably turns Sludge Bomb into an OHKO into Rillaboom following Wood Hammer recoil.

Teambuilding

  • Landorus's typing means that it is threatened by Calyrex-I and Kyogre, which can easily OHKO Landorus. Koraidon can also pose an issue to Landorus, as it can outspeed and OHKO Landorus with Flare Blitz.
  • Chien-Pao is another major threat to Landorus, as it threatens to outspeed and OHKO Landorus with its Ice-type attacks. Amoonguss can also be a difficult foe, as Amoonguss always survives any attack Landorus uses and can use Spore to immobilize it.
  • Grimmsnarl partners well with Landorus, giving it some much needed bulk and support with dual screens while slowing down opposing Pokemon such as Koraidon with Thunder Wave, which can allow Landorus to outspeed them and threaten massive damage. This especially supports matchups into Kyogre and Koraidon, as dual screens prevent OHKOs from Flare Blitz and any of Kyogre's moves after Landorus has Terastallized.
  • Incineroar is also a very good partner, as Intimidate weakens the damage output of Calyrex-I and Koraidon, unless they are holding a Clear Amulet, which can be removed with Knock Off. Will-O-Wisp also cripples Calyrex-I's and Chien-Pao's damage output, regardless of what item Calyrex-I runs.
  • Miraidon pairs naturally with Landorus, as it poses a threat to many of the top dangers to Landorus, such as Kyogre and Koraidon, with powerful Electric-, Fairy-, and Dragon-type attacks, while Landorus deals massive damage to some of Miraidon's biggest counterplay in Zamazenta-C and Rillaboom.
  • Landorus also is a great partner to Calyrex-I, as Landorus is able to threaten the Fire-types that scare Calyrex-I, such as Incineroar and Chi-Yu, while Calyrex-I can use Glacial Lance to deal significant damage to Amoonguss and Koraidon.

Landorus is one of the strongest Pokemon in the metagame thanks to its access to strong Ground-type STAB moves in Earth Power and Sandsear Storm, which are further boosted by its ability, Sheer Force. In conjunction with Life Orb, Landorus can OHKO top metagame Pokemon like Incineroar, Zacian-C and Kingambit. Sludge Bomb allows Landorus to OHKO Ogerpon-H while threatening huge damage to Assault Vest Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W. Substitute allows Landorus to stay on the field longer and avoid Amoonguss's Spore, which allows it to deal continuous damage. Tera Poison allows Landorus to OHKO Ogerpon-W with Sludge Bomb, while shedding weaknesses to common attacks like Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and Ice Spinner from Chien-Pao; it also allows Landorus to deal great damage to common Tera Fairy users, like Raging Bolt and Flutter Mane.
