Additionally, Incineroar makes a double Intimidate core, which neutralizes most physical attackers, with Landorus-T; Tornadus provides Prankster-boosted Stealth Rock and speed control with Tailwind; and Amoonguss shares Regenerator. Bulky Setup Pokemon: Bulky setup Pokemon such as Nasty Plot Gholdengo and Dragon Dance Dragonite appreciate the presence of Landorus-T, as it can help increase their survivability with Intimidate and help them secure KOs with entry hazards.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Landorus-T can utilize Desolate Land to both act as a switch-in to Primordial Sea users like Zapdos and Primarina and threaten Steel-types like Corviknight and Skarmory with Weather Ball, although it would be forgoing its pivoting capabilities. Landorus-T can also be used as a fully offensive wallbreaker with Mold Breaker or Sword of Ruin in conjunction with STAB Earthquake and solid coverage options. Well-Baked Body can also be utilized let it act as a defensive pivot against Fire-types like Iron Moth, Moltres, and Heatran.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Strong special attackers like Latios, Gholdengo, and Deoxys-S all OHKO Landorus-T.

Ice-type Coverage: Ice-type moves from Iron Hands, Chien-Pao, and Great Tusk can seriously threaten Landorus-T.

Bulky Water-types: RegenVest Water-types such as Primarina, Swampert, and Manaphy can stomach hits from Landorus-T while also threatening it with Water-type moves or Knock Off in return.

Fluffy.description:
With a solid defensive typing and physical bulk with Fluffy, Landorus-T functions as a physically defensive pivot against some of the tier's most threatening physical attackers in Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Roaring Moon while also having offensive stats to damage many Pokemon in return. Smack Down threatens Flying-types like Corviknight, Zapdos, and Skarmory as well as common Levitate users such as Gholdengo and Tinkaton, while Taunt can prevent Defog and Roost from the aforementioned Corviknight or setup of entry hazards from Pokemon like Great Tusk and Ting-Lu. Rocky Helmet provides chip damage against the strong physical attackers Landorus-T is able to check like Zamazenta as well as Corviknight and Great Tusk, which may be looking to use U-turn or Rapid Spin, respectively. Leftovers can also be used to provide longevity, allowing it to withstand more hits from physical attackers and mitigating the chip damage from Stealth Rock. 8 Speed EVs allow Landorus-T to outspeed Choice Specs Primarina and Hisuian Goodra.

Landorus-T is used mostly on offensive and balanced teams as role compression for both an entry hazard setter and a defensive pivot, being one of the few Pokemon with access to both Stealth Rock and U-turn. Offensive Dark-types like Roaring Moon, Kingambit, and Chien-Pao appreciate Landorus-T's ability to pivot in on Zamazenta and its ability to threaten Corviknight as well. Special attackers like Gholdengo, Primordial Sea Zapdos, and Latios can threaten Landorus-T, so specially defensive pivots like RegenVest Swampert and Iron Hands complement Landorus-T well. Landorus-T can be threatened by Ice-type coverage from both Chien-Pao and Iron Hands, which makes Steel-types like Gholdengo and Kingambit potential allies to alleviate the issue. In return, Landorus-T provides a natural Ground immunity and Fighting resistance for them. Landorus-T appreciates hazard removal, so Pokemon ike Iron Treads, Great Tusk, and Corviknight make for nice teammates. Due to Fluffy, Landorus-T can be susceptible to opposing Fire-types like Cinderace and Ogerpon-H; thus, it values Fire-immune allies like Well-Baked Body Gholdengo and Primordial Sea Zapdos.

Choice Scarf (Flying).description: Choice Scarf Landorus-T is one of the best revenge killers Flying teams have access to, outrunning threats like Tapu Koko, Mega Diancie, and Terrakion while boasting great firepower. It's also very desirable thanks to its defensive traits, which include an immunity to Electric-type attacks and Intimidate. U-turn takes advantage of the switches Landorus-T forces, allowing it to pivot out of walls that come in on it such as Corviknight and Mega Venusaur. Similarly, Knock Off cripples some of the bulky Pokemon it invites in, like Porygon2 and Ferrothorn, by removing their items. Stone Edge notably hits Kyurem the hardest and is Landorus-T's best move versus Flying-types like Zapdos and Pelipper. Alternatively, Explosion lets Landorus-T score a surprise KO against an offensive threat it normally cannot OHKO, such as Keldeo or Mega Lopunny. Special wallbreakers like Galarian Moltres, Tornadus-T, and Mega Charizard Y are great partners to deal with the aforementioned physical walls Landorus-T draws in. Thundurus-T relieves pressure from Landorus-T by acting as a secondary Electric immunity and is a great asset against the Water and Flying teams Landorus-T can't do much to. Mega Aerodactyl is able to form a powerful revenge killing core alongside Landorus-T while providing Stealth Rock support for it to clean teams more easily. Corviknight switches into most Ice-type attacks aimed at Landorus-T, removes Stealth Rock with Defog, and is able to bring Landorus-T safely onto the field via its slow U-turn.

Bulk Up (Ground).description:
Ferrothorn's Power Whip does not break Substitute at +1 Def or -1 Atk from Intimidate.

This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Defensive Pivot.description: Landorus-T is an excellent physically defensive pivot that checks foes such as Koraidon, Zacian-C, Arceus, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground thanks to its rare Spikes immunity, Intimidate, and U-turn. Taunt denies entry hazards and status from Pokemon such as Ting-Lu and Toxapex and prevents foes like Arceus from continuously setting up in front of Landorus-T. Rocky Helmet punishes foes like Koraidon and Zacian-C for attacking by potentially putting them into range of attacks such as +2 Arceus's Extreme Speed, Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage, and Giratina-O's Shadow Sneak. Tera Water grants a resistance to attacks such as Koraidon's Flare Blitz and Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, while Tera Fairy grants an immunity to Dragon, denying Scale Shot Koraidon a Speed boost and less importantly blocking moves like Miraidon's Draco Meteor. Landorus-T best fits on bulky offense teams, where it can support offensive teammates such as Calyrex-S, Zacian-C, Arceus, and Miraidon by setting Stealth Rock, safely pivoting them in to wallbreak, and checking revenge killers like Zacian-C and Choice Scarf Koraidon. Ting-Lu checks Pokemon like Calyrex-S, Miraidon, and Calm Mind Arceus-Ground for Landorus-T and provides its offensive teammates with Spikes support; Landorus-T checks strong physical attackers for it in return. Landorus-T lacks recovery, so partners like Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Ground, and Zacian-C can assist it by checking Koraidon, opposing Zacian-C, and Arceus, respectively, with help from Intimidate; Choice Scarf Koraidon can also revenge kill these foes. Teammates like Koraidon, Giratina-O, and Eternatus deter Kyogre from using its STAB moves to an extent, but Kyogre can still force you to predict whether it will use a Water-type move or Ice Beam in the face of Landorus-T.

ou.overview: Kyurem is one of SV OU's strongest offensive Pokemon, utilizing its powerful mixed offensive stats and solid overall bulk to run a wide variety of sets, each requiring different counterplay. Choice Specs makes Kyurem into a wallbreaker and strengthens its already powerful moves, OHKOing much of the tier and chunking even the bulkiest Kyurem answers, like Gholdengo and specially defensive Moltres. Kyurem can act as a sweeper with Dragon Dance while still capable of hitting would-be checks with its special coverage, making it a menace even against stall teams. Kyurem's natural bulk enables it to run Substitute + Protect sets to take advantage of Pressure to PP stall foes or even run an Assault Vest to trade with common special attackers like Darkrai and Zapdos while being tough to switch into. Unfortunately, Kyurem's mediocre Speed and lackluster defensive typing can make it challenging to position. Faster Pokemon like Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Dragapult can threaten Kyurem with an OHKO and force it out. Kyurem is weak to Stealth Rock and depends on its item slot for damage, meaning it usually cannot afford to run Heavy-Duty Boots and is forced to rely on entry hazard removal. Moreover, some of Kyurem's sets heavily rely on Tera to boost its damage or provide it with necessary coverage, forcing it to compete with the many Tera-reliant offensive Pokemon in the tier like Enamorus and Garganacl. Additionally, bulky Steel-types like Kingambit, Gholdengo, Scizor, and Iron Crown can soft check most Kyurem sets or possibly force a Tera.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Choice Scarf Kyurem is a niche option used to snipe Pokemon like Dragapult and Ogerpon-W, with the downside of being very prediction-reliant, easy to exploit, and pretty weak without a damage-boosting item. On teams with little to no entry hazard control, Heavy-Duty Boots can be run to mitigate its entry hazard—especially Stealth Rock—weakness, but this comes at the cost of its item slot and, as such, a lot of its damage. Choice Specs sets can run Focus Blast to KO opposing Kyurem and Kingambit as well as hit Air Balloon Heatran and Tera Steel Levitate Pokemon like Latios. Flash Cannon is nice on Substitute + Protect sets alongside Tera Steel to hit opposing Kyurem, Assault Vest Hatterene, and Clefable while not crumbling to Ogerpon-W post-Tera, like with Tera Ground. A set with Substitute, Protect, Dragon Dance, and Icicle Spear with Leftovers can be used to become a setup sweeper that can take advantage of Pressure and the high PP of its moves to PP stall the opposition, particularly passive Pokemon like Alomomola, Toxapex, and Terastallized Gliscor; this set can opt for Tera Steel to set up on Pokemon like Iron Crown and Hatterene or Tera Ghost to set up on Zamazenta and Body Press Corviknight.

Choice Specs.description:
When using Choice Specs, Kyurem becomes a devastating wallbreaker thanks to its great offensive typing alongside its naturally sky-high Special Attack. Freeze-Dry helps Kyurem in dealing with bulky Water-types like Assault Vest Alomomola and Primarina, as well as common Tera Water users such as Gliscor and Galarian Slowking. Earth Power allows Kyurem to hit Galarian Slowking hard as well as Pokemon that resist its STAB moves, examples being Heatran, Kingambit, and Gholdengo. Draco Meteor can be forgone for another nuke in Blizzard if Kyurem is paired with Chilly Reception Galarian Slowking; it similarly deals an immense amount of damage to neutral and even resisted targets, particularly letting it overwhelm Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo that try to pivot around its Ice Beam more easily. Especially for Blizzard variants, Tera Ice provides the most amount of damage possible to its Ice-type STAB moves, giving a 2HKO on Galarian Slowking and offensive variants of Gholdengo and Kingambit with Ice Beam or even bulky variants with Blizzard. Meanwhile, Tera Ground can be used to boost up Earth Power, having a chance to OHKO bulky variants of Kingambit and Gholdengo; it additionally provides a resistance against Stealth Rock and an immunity to Thunder Wave from targets like Galarian Slowking. Finally, Tera Fairy provides Kyurem with an immunity to Dragon-type attacks such as Dragapult, Walking Wake, and opposing Kyurem's Draco Meteor, coupled with a newfound Fighting resistance against moves like Iron Valiant and Zamazenta's Close Combat and Corviknight and Skarmory's Body Press. A Timid nature is preferred for its ability to outspeed key threats like Gholdengo and Great Tusk as well as Speed tie opposing Kyurem, but a Modest nature can be used for more firepower, letting Kyurem overwhelm its checks like Galarian Slowking much more easily.

Kyurem often finds itself in bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to destroy common walls. While Kyurem's typing is amazing offensively, defensively it makes Kyurem hard to switch in due to its numerous weaknesses combined with its average Speed tier. To solve this, pair Kyurem with pivot users; Kyurem's best friend is Galarian Slowking, which brings Kyurem in safely and provides snow with Chilly Reception as well as switch into Fairy-types like Enamorus and Iron Valiant. Additionally, Galarian Slowking lets Kyurem run Blizzard reliably. Kyurem needs entry hazard removal to not get worn down quickly by hazard-stacking teams; therefore, Rapid Spin users like Great Tusk and Iron Treads are great partners. Corviknight can take Fairy- and Dragon-type moves, clear out hazards with Defog, and provide a slow U-turn to get Kyurem in safely. Additionally, Cinderace can use Court Change to use the hazards against the opposing team and can also lure in and pivot out of checks such as Toxapex and Gliscor with U-turn for Kyurem. Hatterene is also a good partner for Kyurem, which can deflect hazards with Magic Bounce, slow down faster threats with Nuzzle, and give Kyurem a second chance at wallbreaking with Healing Wish. Galarian Weezing pairs well due to Neutralizing Gas denying Galarian Slowking's Regenerator while also providing Defog support. Physical attackers like Hisuian Samurott can be used to scare away common special walls thanks to its crippling STAB Knock Off to make Kyurem's attacks more impactful. Another strong physical attacker is Kingambit, which threatens some of Kyurem's checks like Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo. In return, Kyurem can break past their defensive checks such as Moltres, Corviknight, and Great Tusk. Gholdengo makes for an amazing partner, as it can switch into super effective moves aimed at Kyurem and threaten Galarian Slowking and Fairy-types with its STAB moves while checking Zamazenta; in return, Kyurem is able to break down Ting-lu. Kyurem can take advantage of hazard-stacking teams to be even harder to wall, so common hazard setters like Skarmory, Ting-Lu, Hisuian Samurott, and Gliscor can be helpful, with the latter two having Knock Off in their arsenal as well to cripple Kyurem's defensive checks.

Mixed Dragon Dance.description:
The mixed set brings out the best of both sides of Kyurem's attacking capabilities, being able to break through would-be checks and thus turn itself into a monstrous wincon. What this set sacrifices in initial power is made up for in its versatility. Physical walls like Dondozo, Alomomola, and Skarmory looking to handle its Icicle Spear get 2HKOed by Freeze-Dry, while special walls like Blissey, Galarian Slowking, and Fezandipiti trying to tank Freeze-Dry take heavy damage from a Dragon Dance-boosted Icicle Spear. Earth Power targets key foes such as Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Iron Crown as well as 2HKOes Pecharunt, all of which could otherwise take Kyurem on. Loaded Dice provides more consistency for Icicle Spear, but Never-Melt Ice is an alternative that also boosts Freeze-Dry. Tera Ice takes advantage of its propensity to spam its Ice-type moves by pushing their power further. Tera Ground instead gives Kyurem a nice boost to Earth Power that ensures the 2HKO on Garganacl and even Assault Vest Iron Crown along with an immunity to Gholdengo's Thunder Wave and Hatterene's Nuzzle. Tera Ground also gives Kyurem a neutrality to Fighting- and Steel-type moves, which can be decisive against Zamazenta, Gholdengo, and Iron Crown. 88 EVs in Special Attack guarantee the 2HKO on physically defensive Gholdengo with Earth Power. A Hasty nature allows Kyurem to live a Moonblast from Iron Valiant, while a Naive nature makes it take less damage from Kingambit's Sucker Punch.

Mixed Dragon Dance Kyurem fits on offensive teams as a wallbreaker capable of breaking past bulkier foes such as Galarian Slowking and Unaware walls such as Dondozo. Kyurem's main roadblock is Zamazenta, which outspeeds Kyurem and only takes neutral damage from Kyurem's attacks while being able to respond with a strong Body Press. Dragapult creates synergy, being able to switch in on Zamazenta's Fighting-type attacks, outspeed it, and force it to switch out. Dragapult can also spread status and overload shared checks like Kingambit to make it easier for Kyurem to sweep. Deoxys-S also makes for a great partner, as it also outspeeds and threatens Zamazenta while providing entry hazard support for Kyurem, which helps to chip down enemies such as bulkier variants of Primarina, Rillaboom, and Great Tusk that could otherwise take a hit. Alternative hazard setters include Great Tusk in more balanced teams and Glimmora or Hisuian Samurott in more offensively lenient teams. Bulky Steel-types that can handle Ground-type attacks like Corviknight, Air Balloon Tinkaton, and Scizor pose a significant problem to Kyurem, and Fire-types like Cinderace can neutralize them at a relatively low cost for themselves, in turn allowing Kyurem to sweep with minimal opposition. When it's opting to run Never-Melt Ice, Kyurem leaves itself exposed to hazards, which minimizes the amount of times it is able to come in a match. Hazard removal in the form of Great Tusk, Cinderace, or even Corviknight can then be helpful to ensure Kyurem has a safe entry to wreak havoc.

Substitute + Protect.description:
By focusing on its natural bulk and typing to utilize the combination of Pressure, Substitute, and Protect, Kyurem's offensive prowess takes on another dimension by slowly suffocating the opposition with PP depletion while still being difficult to switch into due to its attacking options and solid Speed tier. Attacks such as Gholdengo's Make It Rain, Kingambit's Sucker Punch, Raging Bolt's Draco Meteor, and Tinkaton's Gigaton Hammer are at Kyurem's mercy, while higher PP moves like Clefable's Moonblast and Corviknight's Brave Bird aren't safe either. Substitute also helps punish status attempts from foes like Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo and importantly take advantage of the switches Kyurem forces, especially against passive foes like Gliscor, Alomomola, and Clodsire that might not break the Substitute immediately. Moreover, Kyurem's ability to keep a Substitute up consistently against common walls grants it protection against would-be revenge killers like Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Choice Scarf Gholdengo, even preventing the latter and other Choice item users like Darkrai and Meowscarada from crippling it with Trick. On top of accruing more Leftovers recovery, Protect notably wastes PP of Encore from Tinkaton, Iron Valiant, and Ogerpon-W and scouts for faster offensive threats like Dragapult and Iron Crown, which is especially important because all of these can still threaten Kyurem behind a Substitute. Another reason it can afford to run Substitute and Protect is that Freeze-Dry and Earth Power provide sufficient and unresisted coverage. Freeze-Dry is the preferred Ice-type STAB move due to it denting bulky Water-types and Tera Water users like Alomomola, Primarina, Gliscor, and Garganacl and having a lot of PP, letting it fish for freeze in longer games, which Kyurem excels in, more regularly. With its Freeze-Dry handling Ground-type answers like Landorus-T, Zapdos, and Hydrapple, the move is perfectly complemented by Earth Power to pressure Galarian Slowking and Ice-resistant foes such as Kingambit, Gholdengo, Tinkaton, Cinderace, and Iron Moth. Tera Ground boosts the power of Earth Power, granting it enough power to potentially 2HKO Galarian Slowking and OHKO offensive Kingambit and Gholdengo. Defensively, it provides Kyurem with a newfound Stealth Rock resistance and lets it keep a Substitute up against Garganacl's Salt Cure and Galarian Slowking's Sludge Bomb. The HP EVs allow Kyurem to make 101 HP Substitutes, preventing them from being immediately broken by Blissey's Seismic Toss.

Kyurem is most effective on bulkier teams, such as semi-stall and balance, that can afford to play longer games while being able to position it carefully, but it can also find a place on even faster-paced offensive teams. Its extreme vulnerability to entry hazards—specifically Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes—in longer games makes hazard removal very necessary, with common faces like Great Tusk, Corviknight, Galarian Weezing, and Cinderace being important teammates; even running a combination of them at once is recommended on bulky teams where Kyurem is the primary offensive threat. Moreover, Corviknight and Cinderace provide pivoting support by bringing it in safely on Pokemon like Gholdengo, Alomomola, and Gliscor—even popping the former's Air Balloon in the process—while Galarian Weezing can spread poison via Toxic Spikes to further take advantage of Kyurem's knack for stalling out turns while absorbing opposing Toxic Spikes. Cinderace has the added benefit of threatening bulky Steel-types like Tinkaton, Iron Crown, and Scizor that can annoy Kyurem as well as crippling foes like Hisuian Samurott, Ogerpon-W, and Assault Vest Alomomola with a burn, preventing them from breaking Kyurem's Substitute in one hit. The aforementioned Corviknight and Galarian Weezing as well as the tier's other walls like Alomomola, Dondozo, Zapdos, Galarian Slowking, Gliscor, and Ting-Lu provide Kyurem with a defensive backbone to fall back on, especially as they can switch into Pokemon like Zamazenta, Enamorus, Iron Valiant, and Dragapult that can threaten Kyurem out if it's not behind a Substitute. Alomomola, Zapdos, and Galarian Slowking similarly provide pivoting duties, with the former providing Wish support, while the latter sets up snow, whose Defense boost lets it survive Close Combat from Zamazenta and physical Iron Valiant from full HP, and absorbs Toxic Spikes as well. Ting-Lu and Gliscor also provide entry hazards of their own, which is crucial in taking advantage of Kyurem's forced switches, especially against foes trying to pivot around its attacks instead of staying in to not waste PP. On the other hand, offensive teammates like Deoxys-S, Zamazenta, and Darkrai are great late-game cleaners that love Kyurem's ability to suffocate passive walls early-game. They also have a better matchup against faster offensive teams that can otherwise overrun Kyurem before it gets going. On more offensive teams, hazard setters like Landorus-T, Glimmora, and Hisuian Samurott are great options—especially Glimmora with its potential Toxic Spikes—while offensive threats like Great Tusk, Raging Bolt, and Iron Moth can keep up the pressure against the opposition alongside Kyurem and have a greater chance at sweeping once it has done its job. Additionally, Hatterene and the aforementioned Glimmora and Great Tusk valuably provide hazard control, with Iron Moth also capable of absorbing Toxic Spikes for these structures.

Assault Vest.description:
With an Assault Vest, Kyurem uses its natural bulk to serve as a great blanket check for most of the tier's special attackers while being very difficult to switch into due to the near-unresisted combination of Freeze-Dry and Earth Power. The Assault Vest allows Kyurem to comfortably switch into special attackers like Iron Moth, Darkrai, and Zapdos and force them out in return. Ice Beam is mandatory as Kyurem's strongest no-drawback STAB option, with Freeze-Dry to catch Water-types like Ogerpon-W and Primarina and Earth Power to hit Ice-resistant Pokemon like Heatran, Iron Moth, and Gholdengo. Assault Vest Kyurem can run many different options in its last slot. Draco Meteor is used to guarantee an OHKO against Raging Bolt and opposing Kyurem without an Assault Vest and for its devastating power. Dragon Tail is run to phaze Pokemon like Nasty Plot Darkrai and Nasty Plot Pecharunt; it also comes in handy against Assault Vest Alomomola by bypassing Mirror Coat and by phazing whatever Alomomola brings in with Flip Turn. With 252 Defense EVs, Kyurem can run Body Press to catch switch-ins like Kingambit, Tyranitar, and Blissey. This additional Defense investment also allows Kyurem to match up better against threatening physical attackers like Dragonite and Ogerpon-W. Alternatively, Focus Blast can be run to hit Kingambit and Tyranitar, with the downsides of low accuracy and bouncing off Blissey. Other more niche options can be run depending on the specific support or synergy your team needs, like Endeavor, Blizzard, and Ancient Power. 120 HP and 76 Special Defense EVs are run to guarantee surviving a Choice Specs Dragapult Draco Meteor and mixed Iron Valiant Close Combat, with 96 Speed EVs to outspeed Raging Bolt. The spread of 252 Def / 160 SpA / 96 Spe should only be used on variants running Body Press. Another option is a faster spread with a Timid nature to outspeed Gholdengo, Landorus-T, and Great Tusk, though it requires giving up a significant amount of Kyurem's bulk and power. Tera Fairy is run to become immune to Dragapult and Raging Bolt's Draco Meteor, to resist Darkrai's Dark Pulse, and to flip the matchup versus Zamazenta. Similarly, Tera Poison lets Kyurem take hits from Zamazenta and Iron Valiant while also making it immune to the poison (and thereby confusion) of Pecharunt's Malignant Chain and clearing Toxic Spikes. Tera Ground can also be run to boost the power of Earth Power, threatening to KO many Ice-resistant Pokemon, including Gholdengo and Kingambit.

Assault Vest Kyurem fits best on bulky offense structures, where its good bulk and trading power shine most. Kyurem appreciates the support of Healing Wish Pokemon, like Enamorus, Hatterene, and Latias, mitigating its low longevity. Tera Fairy Kingambit works especially well with Kyurem, as Kyurem can significantly chip opposing Steel-types like Heatran, Gholdengo, and opposing Kingambit, enough for Kingambit to be free to use its Tera against Zamazenta without fear of being revenge killed. Additionally, Heatran appreciates Assault Vest Kyurem's ability to threaten opposing Kyurem, while Heatran threatens Kingambit in return and provides the team with Stealth Rock. Due to Kyurem's weakness to Stealth Rock, Assault Vest Kyurem is often paired with Hatterene to block entry hazards or hazard removers like Cinderace, Iron Treads, and Great Tusk. Structures like these like to capitalize on their reliable hazard removal by running hazard-weak Pokemon like Tornadus-T. Nasty Plot Tornadus-T partners well with Kyurem by overloading shared checks like Galarian Slowking, Iron Crown, and Tyranitar. Kyurem appreciates the support and utility of fast pivots like Assault Vest Tornadus-T with Knock Off and Landorus-T with Stealth Rock, which also give Kyurem switch-in opportunities with U-turn. Kyurem is often accompanied by Zamazenta, which switches into and forces out Pokemon that check Kyurem without Body Press, like Kingambit, Tyranitar, and Blissey. Additionally, Kyurem and Crunch Zamazenta work together to overwhelm Galarian Slowking for each other and Galarian Slowking-weak teammates, like Iron Valiant and Primarina. Iron Valiant partners well with Kyurem, as its superb Speed with Quark Drive allows it to threaten faster threats that force Kyurem out, like Dragapult, while also providing Knock Off support. As a relatively slow wallbreaker, Kyurem also appreciates the switch-in opportunities provided to it by slow pivots like Alomomola and Galarian Slowking. Alomomola can provide Kyurem with Wish support, giving Kyurem more longevity, while Galarian Slowking sets snow with Chilly Reception, letting Kyurem run Blizzard and utilize the Defense boost from snow.

SubRoost.description:
Kyurem can easily dismantle various defensive structures found on archetypes ranging from full stall to bulky offense teams by leveraging Pressure and its excellent coverage. Earth Power complements Freeze-Dry well, hitting Steel- and Fire-types super effectively, providing Kyurem with near-perfect coverage, and making it very difficult to switch into. Substitute, when paired with Pressure, allows Kyurem to PP stall its checks, making it very annoying for bulkier teams to deal with. This also provides Kyurem with an immunity to status moves and allows it to get free turns against passive Pokemon such as Alomomola and Ferrothorn. Substitute combined with Roost means Kyurem can beat its checks, such as Ferrothorn and Chansey, by stalling out all of their attacks. Protect can be used in conjunction with Leftovers to stall out offensive threats that Kyurem cannot safely use Roost in front of, such as Mega Lopunny and Tapu Lele, for longer. However, this leaves Kyurem vulnerable to entry hazards and without reliable recovery, which severely lowers its longevity. 56 HP EVs prevent Blissey and Chansey's Seismic Toss from breaking Substitute in one hit, which allows Kyurem to beat them one-on-one.

Kyurem fits on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to dismantle opposing walls and balance archetypes while making up for Kyurem's limited defensive utility. Offensive pivots, like Tapu Koko and Urshifu-R, can bait in walls like Ferrothorn, Toxapex, and Ting-Lu for Kyurem to prey on. In return, Kyurem can help break down the aforementioned checks as well as Galarian Slowking and bulky Dragon-types like Raging Bolt and Dragonite for them, which allows them to more easily clean up late-game. Other offensive Pokemon, such as Zamazenta and Great Tusk, also appreciate Kyurem pressuring Gholdengo, Zapdos, and Alomomola. In return, they can threaten bulky Steel-types such as Kingambit, Mega Scizor, and Melmetal. Due to Kyurem's relatively low Speed stat and somewhat middling bulk, it is easily threatened by strong wallbreakers such as Zamazenta and Tapu Lele, so Pokemon that can switch into them like Gholdengo, Toxapex, and Ferrothorn are appreciated. Its poor Ice typing also means that Kyurem is incapable of checking Mega Charizard Y and Superpower Ogerpon-W, so Pokemon that can do so such as Toxapex, Moltres, and Mega Venusaur are appreciated. If running Leftovers and Protect, Kyurem becomes vulnerable to entry hazards, so hazard removal from Zapdos, Great Tusk, and Terapagos is also appreciated. Alomomola also makes a great teammate, as it can safely pivot Kyurem into Ferrothorn and Toxapex and heal it with Wish. Kyurem also struggles with Melmetal and Mega Scizor because they can switch in relatively safely and threaten it with their strong Steel-type STAB moves, so Pokemon that can switch into them such as Alomomola, Moltres, and Zapdos make good teammates.

Offensive.description:
With Heavy-Duty Boots, Kyurem can leverage its decent natural bulk and perfect movepool to clobber otherwise solid answers. Ice Beam and Freeze-Dry are fantastic STAB options; the latter is able to maul structures reliant on bulky Water-types to stymy the assault of powerful Ice Beams. Hidden Power Fire and Earth Power serve as excellent coverage to hit the Steel-types that would otherwise be able to survive the onslaught, with Hidden Power Fire targeting Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor and Earth Power chunking Gholdengo and Galarian Slowking for more damage while maiming defensive Heatran. Draco Meteor, while less broadly applicable in its targets, can secure important interactions, OHKOing Raging Bolt and Mega Latios which would otherwise survive an Ice Beam from full health. Roost enables Kyurem to shrug off the chip damage it can often accumulate throughout a game at the expense of further offensive prowess.

Kyurem finds itself most fitting on bulkier teams that can provide it with opportunities to switch out reliably. With the ability to outspeed almost every Ground-type in the tier, Kyurem can find ample opportunities to exploit its coverage and extremely powerful STAB combination, especially against bulkier and slower structures. Kyurem is a one-stop-shop to handle common Gliscor and Toxapex structures while also doing extremely well versus offenses reliant on Alomomola and Slowbro to be their defensive backbone. Kyurem is not without weaknesses—its middling Speed tier and weak defensive typing means it is often outpaced and forced out by threatening offensive staples such as Zamazenta and Mega Diancie. Kyurem thus pairs extremely well with teammates that form a strong defensive core that it can rely on to absorb some of the pressure it inevitably incurs. Ting-Lu and Pecharunt serve to stymy the assault from Mega Latios and the aforementioned Zamazenta, respectively. Galarian Slowking is an extremely powerful defensive partner, with invaluable resistances to Fighting- and Fairy-type attacks as well as access to Thunder Wave, crippling the faster threats that would otherwise force Kyurem out. Galarian Slowking also boasts access to Chilly Reception, which provides a slow pivot to get Kyurem onto the field safely with the bonus of snow, boosting its already solid Defense. Pecharunt with Parting Shot serves a similar role, with its Fighting immunity and Fairy resistance making it a reliable answer to the ever-threatening Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, Urshifu-R, and Ogerpon-W that can all force Kyurem into a corner. Bulky Gholdengo provides additional offensive pressure along with a robust answer to Tapu Lele, and it can serve to soften targets for Kyurem to clean through or trade out with offensive powerhouses that would deny Kyurem from wreaking havoc. Bulky Gholdengo retains access to Thunder Wave to provide the aforementioned paralysis that Kyurem exploits so well. Mega Lopunny and Zamazenta make for excellent offensive partners, being able to rely on Kyurem to handle the bulkier structures that they tend to otherwise struggle against.

Choice Specs.description:
Equipped with Choice Specs, Kyurem becomes a vicious, albeit high-maintenance wallbreaker. It can leverage its opportunities against common defensive targets such as Landorus-T, Tornadus-T, and Gliscor to pressure opposing teams with its vicious STAB moves and high Special Attack. Freeze-Dry smashes through Water-types such as Toxapex and Alomomola with ease. Ice Beam provides an alternative Ice-type attack that allows Kyurem to break past Ferrothorn, Galarian Slowking, and other defensive pivots more easily. Draco Meteor provides a secondary STAB move that can OHKO neutral targets such as Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona, and Zamazenta from full HP, preventing them from potentially switching in to force Kyurem out in a vacuum. Lastly, Earth Power forms near-perfect coverage with Kyurem's Ice-type attacks by ploughing through Steel-types including Gholdengo, Melmetal, and Heatran and can also 2HKO Galarian Slowking from full HP. A Timid nature is preferred to Speed tie with opposing Kyurem and Tapu Lele while also outspeeding Terapagos and Great Tusk. However, a Modest nature is also an option to maximize Kyurem's power, notably improving its odds to 2HKO Ferrothorn with Ice Beam and OHKO Zamazenta with Draco Meteor.

Due to its vulnerability to being revenge killed and crippling weakness to entry hazards, Kyurem fits best on offensive teams. Hazard control options including Terapagos, Tornadus-T, and Cinderace are highly valuable teammates for keeping entry hazards off in the face of common hazard setters such as Ferrothorn and Gliscor. Additionally, Tornadus-T and Cinderace tend to invite in defensive Pokemon such as Toxapex and Heatran and can thus use U-turn to provide Kyurem with safe entry into them. Kyurem is also highly prone to being revenge killed by faster threats such as Mega Diancie and priority from the likes of Mega Scizor and Kingambit, making answers such as Toxapex, Zamazenta, and Landorus-T highly worthwhile. Additionally, Kyurem appreciates additional support from defensive pivots, particularly Pecharunt, Slowbro, and Galarian Slowking, to find safe entry against Landorus-T, Alomomola, and other slower targets. Notably, Galarian Slowking can set snow with Chilly Reception to boost Kyurem's Defense, letting it survive attacks such as Close Combat from Zamazenta and Urshifu-R from full HP. Finally, late-game cleaners such as Zamazenta, Volcarona, Iron Valiant, and Swords Dance Kingambit appreciate Kyurem's ability to threaten problematic defensive pieces, particularly Moltres and Toxapex, early in the match, opening them up to tear through teams more effectively.

• Draco Meteor blasts neutral foes, such as slower non-Assault Vest Great Tusk sets and Air Balloon Volcanion, as well as slower Dragon-type Pokemon, such as non-Haban Berry Raging Bolt.
  • Ice Beam hits Ground-types such as Ursaluna, some Landorus-T variants, and Grass-types such as Rillaboom and Serperior, as well as being its best move against Haban Berry Raging Bolt.
  • Freeze-Dry gives it a strong move to use against Water-type foes such as Ogerpon-W and non-Outrage Dondozo.
  • Earth Power gives it consistency against Assault Vest Volcanion, but Flash Cannon may be used instead to defeat Diancie.
  • The EVs allow it to survive Overheat from Modest Choice Specs Volcanion, with the Speed investment allowing it to outspeed Adamant variants of Landorus-T.
  • Kyurem struggles against faster Dragon-types such as Haxorus and Dragapult, Fighting-types such as both Urshifu formes and Iron Valiant, Steel-types such as Metagross and Iron Valiant, and Fairy-types such as Sylveon. Thus, Fairy-types such as Primarina and Fire-types such as Volcanion and Iron Moth pair well with it.

Haban Berry.description:
• Kyurem can utilize Haban Berry to survive important Dragon-type attacks from the likes of Raging Bolt, Garchomp, and Dragapult.
  • Freeze-Dry is a valuable tool that allows Kyurem to win against any variant of Walking Wake, Ogerpon-W, and non-boosted variants of Primarina.
  • Glaciate's ability to lower Speed allows Kyurem to finish off targets, like Substitute + Leech Seed Rillaboom, with Ice Beam later on.
  • Earth Power allows Kyurem to defeat Heatran with ease after attacking once.
  • The special bulk investment allows Kyurem to survive both a Draco Meteor from Special Attack Booster Energy Raging Bolt and a +3 Hurricane from Galarian Moltres while also surviving a Dragon Darts from Choice Band Dragapult on the physical side.
  • Against Galarian Moltres, it is worth noting that the Kyurem user should be wary of the item that the foe is holding. If it's Weakness Policy Galarian Moltres, Kyurem may choose to use Ice Beam instead of Glaciate, which Custap Berry variants would prefer to utilize. While it is a lot more difficult to deal with, it's not impossible to defeat Assault Vest Galarian Moltres with enough luck in the form of Hurricane misses or Ice Beam freezes.
  • Since Kyurem tends to struggle against most Fairy- and Steel-type Pokemon like Metagross and Iron Valiant, good checks to these like Volcanion, Volcarona, and Skeledirge can serve as good teammates.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ice

Focus Blast can be used over Earth Power to OHKO Tyranitar, giving Kyurem an edge in the otherwise difficult Rock matchup. The move also 2HKOes Blissey after slight chip damage or Stealth Rock if its Heavy-Duty Boots can be removed, although its shaky accuracy means these advantages are easily undermined by bad luck. Running Focus Blast also leaves Kyurem completely walled by Gholdengo and Jirachi. Dragon Pulse gives Kyurem a more spammable Dragon-type STAB option, but the combined strength and coverage of its standard moves leave little reason for Kyurem to spam anything else. Ancient Power allows Kyurem to effectively lure Articuno for itself, but its low base power and overlapping coverage with Kyurem's other moves leave few other use cases for it.

Dragon

Flash Cannon is an alternative option for Kyurem, allowing it to take on Fairy-types that resist both its STAB options such as Klefki and Alolan Ninetales. However, most Fairy-type targets of Flash Cannon would outspeed and force Kyurem out.

Choice Specs (Dragon).description:
Kyurem makes for an exceptional special wallbreaker on Dragon teams by virtue of its high Special Attack further boosted by Choice Specs and a strong STAB combination. Ice Beam shreds through defensive Pokemon such as Skarmory, Ting-Lu, Clodsire, and Amoonguss. Freeze-Dry, despite being weaker than Ice Beam, still hits the same walls with the added benefit of taking out Water-types such as Swampert, Toxapex, and Primarina. Focus Blast is strong coverage that targets Steel-types that resist both of its STAB moves such as Heatran and Bisharp, as well as Rock-types such as Tyranitar and Garganacl. Alternatively, Earth Power hits the same targets as Focus Blast along with non-Air Balloon Gholdengo and Poison-types such as Alolan Muk, Galarian Slowking, and Okidogi.

Kyurem appreciates entry hazard support from the likes of Archaludon and Garchomp to wear down foes into OHKO range of one of its attacks. Notably, Kyurem now has a great chance of OHKOing mixed defensive Toxapex sets after Stealth Rock and one layer of Spikes damage and a chance to outright OHKO physically defensive Ting-Lu after one layer of Spikes damage. In return, Archaludon and Garchomp appreciate Kyurem threatening entry hazard removers such as Great Tusk, Gliscor, and Mandibuzz. Thanks to their Steel typing and great bulk, Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra take on Fairy-types; Archaludon takes on Mimikyu and Azumarill, while Hisuian Goodra handles Flutter Mane, Choice Specs Iron Valiant, and Enamorus. Choice Scarf Dragapult spreads paralysis with Thunder Wave, and its faster U-turn allows it to threaten the likes of Choice Scarf Hoopa-U and Choice Scarf Meowscarada, the latter of which can be especially threatening to Dragon teams with its Protean-boosted Play Rough, while Choice Scarf Latias handles Fighting-types such as non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Sneasler. Dragapult and Latias appreciate Kyurem taking out Ting-Lu and Primarina in return. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon provides great speed control, outspeeding and threatening the likes of Flutter Mane, Iron Valiant, Choice Scarf Latias, Gholdengo, and Enamorus while providing pivoting with U-turn. In return, Kyurem deals with Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, Skarmory, and Amoonguss. Late-game sweepers such as Gouging Fire, Swords Dance Garchomp, and Dragonite appreciate Kyurem's wallbreaking that enables their sweep.

Old Man Winter [Choice Specs] (Ice).description:
Kyurem's high offensive stats, access to Freeze-Dry, and surprisingly solid defensive profile make it an unparalleled special wallbreaker for Ice teams, with its resistances and coverage letting it pull its weight against Fire and Water teams by giving it good matchups against the likes of Ogerpon-H and Dondozo among others. STAB Draco Meteor is already a fearsome tool for Kyurem to wield unboosted, but with Choice Specs equipped, it becomes downright nuclear, OHKOing common neutral targets such as Archaludon, Slowbro, and Ursaluna. Ice Beam is the default secondary STAB move for its reliability, giving Kyurem an extremely strong attack that's also spammable; it importantly deals massive neutral damage to many common Draco Meteor switch-ins, securing 2HKOs on Clefable, Hatterene, Corviknight, and Galarian Weezing. Blizzard is a stronger alternative to Ice Beam that achieves incredible damage benchmarks, securing a guaranteed OHKO on Clodsire and 2HKO on Hisuian Goodra after Stealth Rock, two feats that Ice Beam never achieves; however, Blizzard relies on snow being active to be consistent, forcing Kyurem's snow-setting teammate to either run Icy Rock or play far more conservatively than they would otherwise. Freeze-Dry is arguably the most important tool in Kyurem's arsenal, letting it carry the Water matchup on its back by undermining would-be checks like Primarina, Toxapex, and Tentacruel and scoring harder hits on otherwise neutral targets like Quagsire, Rotom-W, and Dondozo. Earth Power rounds out Kyurem's moveset nicely by giving it coverage for the Steel-types that resist its STAB combination, notably OHKOing Bisharp after 1 layer of Spikes and Metagross after Stealth Rock while handily 2HKOing dedicated walls like Empoleon and non-Choice Scarf Jirachi. Earth Power also scores a super effective hit on bulky Poison-types like Alolan Muk, which can give Kyurem a hard time otherwise. A Timid nature is an absolute requirement on Kyurem, since its crowded Speed tier would leave a Modest variant outsped by common threats to it such as Glimmora, Excadrill, and non-Choice Scarf Great Tusk, among others.

Alolan Ninetales is a crucial partner for Kyurem, enabling Blizzard spam and boosting its bulk to ludicrous proportions with snow and Aurora Veil; Kyurem becomes so staggeringly bulky in these conditions that a revenge killing tool as strong as Choice Band Scizor's Bullet Punch will not even 2HKO it after Stealth Rock. Alolan Ninetales's part-Fairy typing is also useful for discouraging Dragon-type revenge killers like Latios, Dragapult, and Walking Wake with Moonblast. Since Kyurem cannot use Heavy-Duty Boots on this set, it must rely on entry hazard removal to maintain its longevity; Alolan Sandslash is a standout choice here thanks to Rapid Spin and its secondary Steel typing, allowing it to switch into common revenge killers like Iron Boulder, Dragapult, and Flutter Mane, as well as threatening Rock- and Fairy-type attackers with its STAB moves. Slush Rush also lets it provide speed control that Kyurem needs to help against threats like Flutter Mane and Weavile. Mamoswine brings Stealth Rock to make Kyurem even harder to switch into, Ice Shard to help with speed control, and an Earthquake that shakes most Steel-types and special walls into Kyurem's KO range or out of the game altogether, notably OHKOing Gholdengo, Klefki, and Hisuian Goodra after Stealth Rock. Froslass can provide further entry hazard support with Spikes, speed control with Thunder Wave, and spinblocking utility while also switching into Fighting-type attacks for Kyurem, and Destiny Bond lets it trade with a problematic target such as Ogerpon-H. Weavile contributes a powerful Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots or Eviolite from certain walls that rely on them such as Articuno and Porygon2, respectively. Avalugg is another hazard removal option that provides a much sturdier fallback against physical revenge killers compared to Alolan Sandslash and serves as a secondary wincon with an IronPress set, but this comes at the cost of being agonizingly slow and useless against most Fairy-types.

Mixed Dragon Dance (Dragon).description:
Kyurem is an incredible setup sweeper for Dragon teams thanks to its good Speed tier and good natural bulk. Known primarily as a special wallbreaker, a physical set is far less expected and harder to check. With Dragon Dance and Loaded Dice, Kyurem threatens special walls like Hisuian Goodra, Clodsire, and Assault Vest Hoopa-U after an attack boost, creates holes in the Flying cores by 2HKOing Corviknight and Skarmory after Stealth Rock, and can break through Ground-types after gaining Speed from Scale Shots and Fire-types once Heatran's Air Balloon is popped. Earth Power allows Kyurem to hit Steel-types that resist its STAB combination, like non-Air Balloon Heatran, and 2HKO defensive Archaludon. A Naive nature lets Kyurem outspeed until base 90 speed mons like Great Tusk and Hisuian Samurott, and with two Speed boosts, it can also outspeed Excadrill under sand, Kingdra under rain, and Choice Scarf Dragapult.

Dragon Dance Kyurem struggles to set up against physical walls such as Dondozo and Skarmory and is pressured by Fighting-type attackers like Iron Valiant, Urshifu-R, and Great Tusk. Teammates that provide speed control and defensive support are essential. Archaludon checks physical attackers such as Dragapult and Dragonite, sets Stealth Rock, and spreads Thunder Wave, slowing fast threats like Meowscarada, Iron Valiant, and Dragapult. Likewise, Latias offers valuable role compression by utilizing a Choice Scarf to eliminate Latios and non-Choice Scarf Sneasler, and Healing Wish to give Kyurem a second chance to sweep. Dragapult supports Kyurem with utility options like Will-O-Wisp, crippling physical checks such as Mamoswine and Great Tusk and creating setup opportunities. Choice Specs Dragapult can outright remove or heavily dent offensive checks like Iron Crown, Walking Wake, and Gholdengo. Latios and Raging Bolt act as strong special wallbreakers, pressuring bulky Poison- and Water-types such as Galarian Weezing, Dondozo, and Toxapex. Raging Bolt's Thunderclap also provides priority against faster threats, picking off Greninja and Sneasler. Kommo-o improves difficult Dark- and Steel-type matchups by pressuring Pokemon like Hisuian Samurott, Bisharp, and Skarmory. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon provides additional speed control and revenge kills threats like unboosted Dragapult. Hisuian Goodra handles special attackers like Flutter Mane, Hatterene, and Greninja.

doublesou.overview: Kyurem boasts monstrous stats, powerful attacks, and a surprisingly useful typing to act as a terrifying threat in the DOU metagame. Its STAB Ice-type attacks hit common threats and utility Pokemon alike, such as Landorus, Rillaboom, and Tornadus, for super effective damage, and Freeze-Dry forces the format's few Water-types to stay on their toes. Earth Power and Flash Cannon both serve as effective coverage moves to keep Ice- and Dragon-resistant Pokemon at bay. Meanwhile, Ice / Dragon is an excellent defensive typing when combined with Kyurem's natural bulk, allowing it to stand strong in the face of Pokemon like Ogerpon-W. Kyurem's Speed stat, while falling short of the format's faster threats, is still high enough to outrun and threaten Pokemon such as Glimmora and Gholdengo. Kyurem's biggest downfall, however, is its utter reliance on snow. Without the 50% boost to its Defense and perfect accuracy on Blizzard, Kyurem struggles to stand out compared to other juggernauts like Iron Hands and Raging Bolt. In addition, many of Kyurem's checks also have strong matchups against the snow setters of the format, turning Pokemon like Gholdengo, Diancie, and Tyranitar from annoyances into serious threats to the team.
doublesou.comments:
Checks and Counters

Incineroar: Thanks to its natural bulk and Blizzard resistance, Incineroar is often able to switch in on Kyurem and threaten any of Fake Out, Knock Off, and Parting Shot, all of which cut into Kyurem's ability to continue dealing damage.

Iron Hands: Assault Vest Iron Hands is bulky enough to shrug off Blizzard and heal off the damage with Drain Punch, preventing Kyurem from using Blizzard if it wants to threaten it.

Steel-types: Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Kingambit can use their Blizzard resistance and STAB Steel-type attacks to force Kyurem to retreat, which grants them the opportunity to set up or deal heavy damage on their own.

Rock-types: Diancie and Tyranitar both have the bulk to take on Blizzard and the damage to beat Kyurem one-on-one. While it needs speed control, Glimmora can also threaten it with powerful Rock-type moves, especially Meteor Beam.

Weather Disruption: Because Kyurem is so reliant on snow, many teams can use their own weather to combat it. Torkoal and Tyranitar can directly threaten Kyurem, while Pelipper and Tornadus can take away snow at a crucial moment and allow a physical partner to deal full damage to Kyurem.

Entry Hazards: Common Stealth Rock setters like Glimmora and Ting-Lu may not beat Kyurem on their own, but Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes can cut severely into Kyurem's health, making it less able to take on their teammates.

Snow Assault Vest.description:
• Snow and Assault Vest's defensive boosts combine to make Kyurem a juggernaut, capable of taking multiple consecutive hits while dealing heavy damage.

  • Blizzard is Kyurem's most consistent damage option in snow, threatening both powerful attackers like Landorus and Dragonite and common support Pokemon like Tornadus and Sinistcha.

  • Freeze-Dry expands Kyurem's reach and lets it threaten Water-types and Tera Water users like Amoonguss and Iron Hands, hitting Ogerpon-W and Pelipper especially hard.

  • Earth Power becomes necessary to threaten Pokemon that take minimal damage from Kyurem's Ice-type attacks, like Gholdengo, Incineroar, Iron Hands, and Kingambit.

  • Flash Cannon is a powerful tool for hitting opposing Diancie, Alolan Ninetales, and any Pokemon that may use Tera Fairy, such as Gholdengo and Raging Bolt.

  • Glaciate can slot over Freeze-Dry or Flash Cannon, providing a surprisingly powerful speed control move greatly appreciated by the likes of Iron Hands or Kingambit.

  • Draco Meteor is Kyurem's most powerful single attack, though a Dragon-type move is entirely optional on this set, and Draco Meteor's Special Attack drop may make it more difficult for Kyurem to stay in and trade hits with the opposing side.

  • This EV spread lets Kyurem outspeed Timid Glimmora, avoid a 3HKO from Iron Hands's Drain Punch with Aurora Veil in snow, and always 2HKO maximum HP Kingambit with Earth Power.

  • Steel is a potent defensive Tera type against Gholdengo and Glimmora and can provide a power boost for Flash Cannon, but it leaves Kyurem more vulnerable to threats like Iron Hands and Landorus. Tera Fairy is a more general option that flips multiple of Kyurem's weaknesses, turning the tables on Pokemon like Iron Hands and opposing Kyurem, but maintains the Steel weakness.

  • Alolan Ninetales is all but required on teams with Kyurem; Snow Warning giving both a Defense boost and an accurate Blizzard is too good to ignore, and its Aurora Veil lets Kyurem double down on its already incredible bulk.

  • This set greatly appreciates partners with healing capabilities to extend its survivability. Rillaboom and Sinistcha are the most common partners for this purpose, but Pollen Puff users like Amoonguss and Mew can provide the same benefit.

Snow Choice Specs.description:
• Choice Specs gives Kyurem a substantial Special Attack boost that it can use to quickly and definitively end games.

  • Choice Specs Blizzard is one of the strongest spread moves currently available in the format, hitting some notable KOs on foes such as Sinistcha that other items cannot.

  • Freeze-Dry cleanly answers Water-type Pokemon that would want to switch in on Blizzard, and Choice Specs helps make up for its lower Base Power.

  • Draco Meteor turns most offensive threats into mush and deals respectable damage to even the bulkiest Pokemon in the format such as Incineroar and Iron Hands.

  • Earth Power hits Steel- and Fire-types, forcing them to make tough decisions about switching in, while Flash Cannon OHKOes Diancie.

  • A Timid nature allows Kyurem to outspeed key Pokemon like Glimmora and Gholdengo, while a Modest nature sacrifices outspeeding those threats in order to maximize damage. Likewise, a little bit of Speed can be dropped from Timid Kyurem for added bulk, but these threats should be kept in mind when doing so.

  • The chosen defensive Tera types enable Kyurem to continue dealing damage; Ghost provides an immunity to Fake Out from Pokemon such as Rillaboom, which is valuable on a Choice item set, but Fairy flips more weaknesses and grants an immunity to moves like Gouging Fire's Breaking Swipe and Raging Bolt's Draco Meteor.

  • Tera Ice can be used to make Blizzard hurt more, and it notably allows Freeze-Dry to OHKO Terastallized Ogerpon-W.

  • Alolan Ninetales is required as a teammate thanks to its Snow Warning ability, but Encore and Icy Wind are particularly useful to keep strong attacks off of Kyurem. Other good teammates include Fake Out users like Incineroar and Rillaboom to create space and more offensive threats such as Landorus to capitalize on Kyurem's damage output.

SubRoost (Dragon).description: Kyurem is an excellent stallbreaker for Dragon teams with its access to Pressure, Roost, and Substitute, allowing it to force out notable bulky pests such as Toxapex and Mega Sableye. Freeze-Dry is a notable move in the Water matchup, as it allows Kyurem to effectively remove Mega Swampert and Pelipper to prevent rain. Earth Power eats away at Steel- and Fire-type competitors like Archaludon, Empoleon, and Heatran. With the given EV spread, Kyurem is able to stay behind its Substitute when hit by a Seismic Toss from Blissey while also being able to survive a Dazzling Gleam from Choice Specs Tapu Koko at full HP. Even with this bulk, Kyurem finds itself being threatened out by Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Tapu Lele, so having teammates like Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra helps greatly because they can swap into incoming physical and special Fairy-type moves. Mega Altaria assists its icy companion by checking Dragon-type threats like the Lati twins and Garchomp with its Fairy typing. Choice Scarf Latias and Roaring Moon can revenge kill threats to Kyurem like Mega Lopunny, Choice Scarf Latias, and Choice Band Sneasler. Mega Latios and Kommo-o are notable wallbreakers that assist versus Steel-type threats like Mega Scizor and Hisuian Goodra. Garchomp complements Kyurem well by utilizing entry hazards so Kyurem has an easier time stallbreaking thanks to the greater chip damage.

Choice Specs (Dragon).description: Choice Specs Kyurem is a terrifying wallbreaker with an impeccable STAB combination and coverage movepool, beating threats to Dragon teams like Toxapex, Dragonite, and Mamoswine. Draco Meteor is Kyurem's most powerful move, notably wearing down typical switch-ins like Mega Sableye and Volcarona. Freeze-Dry is highly effective in the Water matchup by answering would-be checks like Swampert, Gastrodon, and Slowking. Focus Blast catches Ferrothorn and Tyranitar off guard should they expect a STAB move, while Earth Power hits Alolan Muk, Galarian Slowking, and Heatran for more damage. Mega Altaria is heavily appreciated as an answer to Dragon-types like Kommo-o, Roaring Moon, and Walking Wake. Garchomp provides entry hazards like Stealth Rock and Spikes to ease Kyurem's wallbreaking. Latias checks Fighting-types such as Iron Hands, Galarian Zapdos, and Terrakion, is able to replenish Kyurem's health with Healing Wish, and removes troublesome entry hazards—especially Stealth Rock, given Kyurem's Rock weakness—with Defog. Dragalge sets up Toxic Spikes and checks Fairy-types like Tapu Koko and Clefable. Kommo-o checks Steel-types like Heatran and defensive Celesteela and blocks attempts to set hazards with Taunt.

Substitute + Roost (Ice).description: Kyurem is a stellar stallbreaker for Ice teams by utilizing Pressure, Substitute, and Roost to beat or force out walls such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Mega Sableye. Kyurem's good bulk and typing also allow it to function as a defensive pivot, consistently checking threats like Heatran, Rotom-W, and Rillaboom. Moreover, it shrugs a hit from and beats the likes of Galarian Zapdos and Urshifu-R one-on-one if using a Chople Berry. Freeze-Dry lands a strong hit on Water-types like Toxapex and Gastrodon, turning Kyurem into a valuable asset in that matchup. Alongside it, Earth Power grants Kyurem near-perfect neutral coverage by nailing Steel- and Fire-types such as Magnezone and Skeledirge. The given EV spread allows Kyurem's Substitute to live one Seismic Toss from Blissey. Alolan Ninetales provides Snow and Aurora Veil support, bolstering Kyurem's defensive utility while preventing Celesteela and Heatran from breaking its Substitute. Defensive Cloyster is able to remove entry hazards with Rapid Spin, set up Spikes to help Kyurem stallbreak more easily, and switch into physical Steel-type attacks from Mega Scizor and Melmetal. Similarly, Piloswine lays down Stealth Rock and deals with Fire- and Rock-types that Kyurem loses to, such as Volcarona and Mega Diancie. Setup sweepers like Swords Dance Weavile and Shell Smash Cloyster greatly appreciate Kyurem wearing down walls so they can clean up late-game.

ubers.overview: Chillingly powerful is quite the accurate description for Kyurem-B. With an Attack stat that eclipses even Calyrex-I, BoltBeam coverage, Dragon Dance, and Teravolt to boot, Kyurem-B is easily capable of ripping through bulky teams, with even Necrozma-DM struggling to stand up to its Fusion Bolt with Tera Electric and Miraidon's Electric Terrain. Its solid natural bulk also allows it to set up against passive Pokemon like Gliscor and Arceus-Water lacking Will-O-Wisp, and it threatens the specially defensive Ground-types used to stave off Miraidon like Arceus-Ground, Ting-Lu, and Clodsire. Unfortunately, Kyurem-B's part-Ice typing is a massive hindrance defensively, limiting its opportunities to set up despite its solid natural bulk. It can also be outsped by Choice Scarf Koraidon even after a boost or picked off by priority like Arceus's Extreme Speed or Kingambit's Sucker Punch. It also is not exactly the fastest Pokemon in the world, which in conjunction with its meager defensive profile limits what Kyurem-B can accomplish against offensive teams.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Tera Fire with Tera Blast can be used to destroy Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C at +1 while also avoiding burns from Ho-Oh. However, it is largely unnecessary given how strong +1 Tera Electric Fusion Bolt is.

Checks and Counters

Arceus-Fairy: Arceus-Fairy can easily take everything Kyurem-B throws at it, has reliable recovery, and can threaten Kyurem-B with super effective Judgment or Will-O-Wisp.

Ho-Oh: Ho-Oh can survive +1 Fusion Bolt and threaten to burn Kyurem-B with Sacred Fire or phaze it with Whirlwind. Tera Fairy Ho-Oh also survives everything +1 Kyurem-B can throw at it.

Speed Control: Choice Scarf Koraidon outspeeds Kyurem-B even after a Dragon Dance and threatens it in return. Extreme Killer Arceus and Kingambit threaten to pick off Kyurem-B with Extreme Speed or Sucker Punch.

Residual Damage: Kyurem-B has no recovery and is vulnerable to all forms of residual damage, even being weak to Stealth Rock.

Steel-types: While they're not hard counters, Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C resist Icicle Spear, can take +1 Fusion Bolt, and retaliate with super effective STAB moves, and Necrozma-DM can heal off the damage. They must, however, be wary of Kyurem-B Terastallizing into an Electric-type.

Trick Room Pokemon: Pokemon like Necrozma-DM, Calyrex-I, and the rare Necrozma-DW can take boosted attacks from Kyurem-B and turn the tables on it with Trick Room.

Ditto: While it's rare, Ditto can reliably revenge kill Kyurem-B. It must, however, watch out for Substitute on dual screens teams.

Dragon Dance.description:
With Dragon Dance, Kyurem-B can boost its Attack to even greater levels while also fixing its Speed issue. Icicle Spear and Fusion Bolt provide perfect coverage in Ubers, and Fusion Bolt's power can be increased further with Tera Electric and Miraidon's Electric Terrain. Tera Electric is also useful for the Steel resistance it provides, allowing Kyurem-B to set up on and threaten Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM without Earthquake, which would normally check it quite easily. Loaded Dice makes Icicle Spear and Scale Shot reliably strong STAB moves. Scale Shot is usually preferred over Substitute thanks to Kyurem-B's meager defensive profile, but Substitute can be used on dual screens hyper offense teams where its defensive problems are mitigated to set up freely on Gliscor and Arceus-Water and avoid revenge killing attempts from Choice Scarf Koraidon and Extreme Killer Arceus. Jolly is usually the preferred nature to let Kyurem-B outspeed Zacian-C with one Speed boost and Choice Scarf Koraidon with two, but Adamant is superior on Sticky Web teams where its Speed issue is mitigated.

Due to being relatively weak without Terastallization and its defensive shortcomings, Kyurem-B fits best on hyper offense teams. Grimmsnarl's dual screens aid Kyurem-B further with setting up and even allows it to run Subsitute. Ribombee's Sticky Web mitigates Kyurem-B's Speed issue and allows it to run an Adamant nature. On both styles, Miraidon is a near-mandatory partner, setting up Electric Terrain for Kyurem-B to boost its Fusion Bolt and getting it in safely with U-turn. In return, Kyurem-B threatens Ground-types used to check Miraidon, like Gliscor, Ting-Lu, and Arceus-Ground. Necrozma-DM can serve as a check to Zacian-C and Arceus before Kyurem-B is ready to sweep, making it a good partner. Despite not being very apt defensively, Kyurem-B can switch into and set up on Kyogre once, making it a solid partner for Koraidon and Arceus-Ground. Kyurem-B also appreciates these Pokemon immediately threatening Necrozma-DM, which it can struggle against even if Necrozma-DM does not carry Sunsteel Strike.

• Kyurem-B serves as a fearsome physical sweeper, using its monstrous Attack stat to tear apart weakened teams. Kyurem-B is typically used as a late-game wincon on offense teams after its would-be checks such as Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Ho-Oh lose the ability to check it. Kyurem-B can also be used mid-game to break through balance teams due to the difficulty other teams have switching in. Kyurem-B often forces the other team to use their Terastallization to check it. Kyurem-B typically fits best on offense teams, especially hyper offense teams. However, Kyurem-B's downsides can make it difficult to justify on a team, as it often relies on Terastallization to perform its sweep, it competes with other setup sweepers such as Necrozma-DM and Mega Salamence, and it's weak to Stealth Rock.
  • Icicle Spear is Kyurem-B's best Ice-type STAB move, serving as consistent high damage output using Loaded Dice. Icicle Spear is a spammable STAB move due to the tier's abundance of Dragon- and Ground-type Pokemon. At +1 with a Jolly nature, Icicle Spear gets guaranteed 2HKOs on Ho-Oh and offensive Primal Groudon with a chance to 2HKO utility Arceus formes. With an Adamant nature, Icicle Spear can guarantee the 2HKO on utility Arceus formes and become very likely to 2HKO defensive Primal Groudon.
  • Fusion Bolt lets Kyurem-B hit all of the targets that resist Icicle Spear for at least neutral damage. Fusion Bolt 2HKOes defensive Primal Kyogre without needing to use Dragon Dance first. In addition, at +1, Kyurem-B has a chance to OHKO defensive Primal Kyogre and defensive Ho-Oh, and it can beat Dondozo or force it to Terastallize. Fusion Bolt is also Kyurem-B's best coverage move against Necrozma-DM.
  • Substitute lets Kyurem-B dodge status conditions, particularly Toxic from Pokemon such as Alomomola and Primal Groudon, which may threaten to stop its sweep, while also making switching to handle Kyurem-B risky. Kyurem-B's Substitute can survive weaker hits as well such as Giratina-O's Shadow Sneak. In addition, Substitute lets Kyurem-B bypass Trick and Charm from Gothitelle and Imposter from Ditto.
  • Scale Shot can be used as a secondary STAB option, since it is a useful midground option, as defensive cores that combine to resist Icicle Spear and Fusion Bolt will often be hit neutrally by Scale Shot such as a core of Zygarde and Primal Kyogre, allowing you to get around needing to predict defensively. The Speed boost given by Scale Shot may also come in handy, as it allows Kyurem-B to boost past a faster Pokemon while still getting damage such as an opposing Deoxys-A in the back that would threaten to revenge kill it at +1.
  • Tera Electric bolsters the power of Fusion Bolt while also turning incoming Steel-type attacks from a weakness into a resistance. This is incredibly useful in the Necrozma-DM matchup, as Fusion Bolt can 2HKO defensive Necrozma-DM, while Sunsteel Strike from defensive Necrozma-DM can 4HKO Kyurem-B after Stealth Rock, which notably doesn't break Kyurem-B's Substitute. In addition, Tera Electric gives Kyurem-B a favorable roll to OHKO Zacian-C if one layer of Spikes is up.
  • Tera Fairy is a defensive Terastallization option, most notably flipping Dragon-type moves such as Eternatus's Dynamax Cannon from a weakness into an immunity while also turning Fighting-type moves from a weakness into a resistance such as Marshadow's Low Kick.
  • Tera Ground + Tera Blast in the third moveslot hits the Steel-types that Kyurem-B normally struggles to break through, most notably Necrozma-DM, while also letting it threaten Terastallized Giratina-O, as Teravolt lets it ignore Levitate.
  • An EV spread of 40 HP / 252 Atk / 216 Spe with an Adamant nature lets Kyurem-B outspeed Adamant nature Zekrom and other neutral Speed nature Pokemon with a base 90 Speed. In addition, the bulk investment allows Kyurem-B to avoid an OHKO from Stone Edge from physical setup sweeper Arceus-Ground at +1.
  • The 252 Atk / 92 Def / 164 Spe EV spread with a Jolly nature allows Kyurem-B to outspeed Deoxys-A after a Dragon Dance while avoiding an OHKO from +2 Tera Normal Arceus's Extreme Speed and Ultra Necrozma's Stone Edge.
  • Kyurem-B is best used as a mid- or late-game sweeper. While Kyurem-B has usable bulk, enough to take a hit, its Stealth Rock weakness limits its ability to come onto the field, so it is fairly committal to send in. As such, reserve Kyurem-B for when you feel comfortable bringing it in such as in the face of a Pokemon it can hit super effectively.
  • Kyurem-B is also a fearsome wallbreaker, which gives it an important niche versus balance and stall teams. Kyurem-B can punish passive play by using Substitute against defensive Pokemon, which allows it to set up much more safely. Kyurem-B also has good matchups against keystone defensive Pokemon such as defensive Eternatus and Dondozo. Kyurem-B has to be careful about foes using defensive Terastallization to play around it and threaten it back.
  • Kyurem-B wants to use Terastallization often, so you should support Kyurem-B with Pokemon that don't rely on Terastallization such as Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre. Kyurem-B also can force the other team to expend their Terastallization to beat it, removing some prediction for its teammates. Ho-Oh makes a great partner on bulkier offense teams, as it doesn't need to Terastallize that often, and it provides Defog support to remove Stealth Rock for Kyurem-B to come in more easily.
  • Sticky Web support from Smeargle or Shuckle is also great for Kyurem-B, as that allows it to leverage its passable but flawed Speed tier much better.
  • Kyurem-B struggles to break through Steel-types such as Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C, so one should pair Kyurem-B with attackers that can deal with them such as Primal Groudon, Ho-Oh, and Arceus-Ground.

Setup Attacker.description: • The given EV spread allows Kyurem-Black to survive two Seismic Toss from Mega Kangaskhan and maximize its Speed which will outspeed Zeraora after a Dragon Dance. The remaining EVs are invested into its Attack.

Choice Band.description: Kyurem-B's main niche compared to competitors like Mega Garchomp and Ash-Greninja lies in its immensely spammable Glacial Lance, which hits most physical walls for at least neutral damage while also being non-contact to avoid Rocky Helmet and Burning Bulwark. Bolt Strike 2HKOes Fur Coat Water-types like Mega Slowbro and Dondozo in addition to Primordial Sea Registeel. U-turn eases prediction and chips walls like Mega Slowbro. Headlong Rush and V-create both target Steel-types like Zacian-C, with the former OHKOing Primordial Sea Registeel and the latter OHKOing Mega Steelix. Kyurem-B's main weakness is its vulnerability to Stealth Rock, making strong entry hazard removal mandatory. Due to Glacial Lance's excellent neutral coverage and Kyurem-B's raw power, it forces most physical walls to remain healthy to avoid being KOed the next time it attacks, making Strength Sap blockers like Magic Guard Blissey and Magic Bounce users fantastic teammates. Kyurem-B is also very slow for a wallbreaker, making fast Pokemon such as Ash-Greninja and Koraidon desirable. Imposter-proof Kyurem-B with Fur Coat Pokemon such as Arceus-Ghost and Mega Audino.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Kyurem-B can alternatively use Tera Steel with Substitute as its last move as a method of setting up on would-be counters like defensive Arceus formes. This combination can set up on Arceus-Fairy and on Arceus-Water under sun, provided neither of them is using Roar. This set also avoids being revenge killed by Ditto and Arceus, due to the resistances that being a Steel-type provides. However, this set faces usage competition from Koraidon, which can also run a Tera Steel set with Substitute and is generally the more applicable Pokemon.

Checks and Counters

Physically Defensive Arceus Formes: Arceus-Fairy is perhaps the greatest check to Kyurem-B, as it threatens super effective damage with Judgement, its great physical bulk allows it to take multiple hits, and it can incapacitate Kyurem-B with Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave. Despite this, Kyurem-B has a chance to 2HKO Arceus-Fairy with Icicle Spear after one Dragon Dance, as it tanks a Judgement when at full HP, allowing it to trade its health to KO Arceus-Fairy without resorting to Terastallization. Arceus-Water is also a very fearsome check, as the Judgement and Will-O-Wisp combination can deal with Kyurem-B in and out of Tera Fire. Moreover, Dragon Tail can force Kyurem-B out when it is trying to set up. Arceus-Water must be wary of Tera Electric Fusion Bolt, however, especially if Electric Terrain is up.

Choice Scarf Users: Due to Kyurem-B's relatively low speed stat, it is unable to outspeed common Choice Scarf users, such as Koraidon and Calyrex-S, even after it has used Dragon Dance once. Koraidon can threaten an OHKO, and Calyrex-S can outspeed Kyurem-B even when it is at +2.

Steel-Types: Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM are the premier Steel-types in the tier, and both of them threaten an OHKO with their signature moves, forcing Kyurem-B to Terastallize if it wants to set up on them.

Dragon Dance.description:
Kyurem-B boasts an incredibly high Attack stat, which, when boosted by Dragon Dance, enables it to become a very powerful stallbreaker. However, Kyurem-B is generally not used due to the fact that it has a relatively lower Speed stat compared to other offensive Pokemon. It also has poor defensive utility, as the only relevant Pokemon it can check is Kyogre. Kyurem-B most notably is almost entirely outclassed by Koraidon, which has a higher Speed stat, generally stronger moves, and a higher effective Attack stat through its ability. Still, Kyurem-B carves out a niche thanks to Teravolt, breaking through Pokemon with Unaware, such as Skeledirge and Dondozo, that would cause other physical sweepers considerable difficulty. Icicle Spear super effectively or neutrally damages most of the metagame. Fusion Bolt serves as an excellent partner to Icicle Spear, as it can hit Water-types such as Arceus-Water, Kyogre, and Tera Water Arceus-Fairy super effectively as well as 2HKO Zacian-C after a Dragon Dance. For its last move, Kyurem-B can opt to run either Scale Shot or Tera Blast. Scale Shot benefits from Loaded Dice and raises Kyurem-B's mediocre Speed while doing significant damage. Tera Blast can be used in conjunction with Tera Fire, allowing Kyurem-B to super effectively hit Steel-types such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM. Additionally, Tera Fire enables Kyurem-B to set up without fear of being burned by Sacred Fire from Ho-Oh or Will-O-Wisp from defensive Arceus formes and Skeledirge; it also provides a very valuable resistance to Fairy- and Steel-type attacks, most notably from Zacian-C. Tera Electric or Tera Ghost can also be used, which, respectively, either boost the power of Fusion Bolt while still resisting Steel-type attacks or provide an immunity to Extreme Speed from Arceus and to Fighting moves, such as Low Kick from Koraidon. Kyurem-B uses maximum Speed with a Jolly nature to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame after one Dragon Dance or Scale Shot.

Kyurem-B is best used on hyper offense teams. Its remarkable ability to stallbreak makes it a wonderful partner to physically offensive Pokemon that cannot otherwise break through stall, most notably Zacian-C and some Koraidon sets. Due to Kyurem-B's mediocre Speed stat, it benefits greatly from being on a team with Ribombee, which can set up Sticky Web to lower the opposing team's Speed, helping Kyurem-B to avoid getting revenge killed by Choice Scarf users such as Koraidon and Calyrex-S. Kyurem-B can also struggle against physically defensive Pokemon that it cannot hit super effectively, such as Arceus-Fairy and Necrozma-DM. As a result, it benefits from being partnered with strong special attackers, such as Calm Mind Arceus-Ground and Arceus-Fairy, as well as Miraidon, which also boosts Kyurem-B's Fusion Bolt through the Electric Terrain that it sets up. Activating Electric Terrain notably enables Kyurem-B to OHKO Zacian-C and Arceus-Water with Tera Electric Fusion Bolt after a single Dragon Dance. In turn, Kyurem-B can benefit its special attacking partners, as it can switch into the premier special wall, Ting-Lu, and threaten it with Icicle Spear or set up with Dragon Dance.

Offensive Pivot.description:
This Kyurem-W set appreciates the freedom of switching moves as well as the ability to not be as reliant on entry hazard removal. Freeze-Dry allows Kyurem-W to nail Water-types such as Rotom-Wash, Ogerpon-W, and Primarina, while Earth Power rounds out Kyurem-W's coverage, nailing Steel-types such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM. Tera Ice lets Kyurem-W shed its weaknesses to Fairy and Dragon while also supercharging its Ice-type STAB moves; however, Tera Ground allows Kyurem-W to gain STAB on its only coverage move to further pressure the opposing team as well as give Kyurem-W a Stealth Rock resistance should it lose its Heavy-Duty Boots.

As a god, Kyurem-W donates a massive Special Attack stat that Pokemon such as Hisuian Electrode and Landorus appreciate. Hisuian Electrode also has an easier time threatening the Water-types that try to wall Kyurem-W such as Primarina and Dondozo while also utilizing its blistering base 150 Speed to threaten Pokemon that outspeed Kyurem-W. Kyurem-W is also able to donate a respectable base 125 HP stat to Pokemon such as Rotom-Wash, Landorus-T, and Hatterene that appreciate the massive increase in bulk. Landorus-T can threaten Steel-types such as Iron Crown and Necrozma-DM, while Hatterene is especially useful, as it can easily tank Fighting- and Dragon-type attacks aimed at Kyurem-W. Furthermore, Rotom-Wash and Landorus-T can both provide pivoting to allow Kyurem-W to hit the field without fear of being worn down by incoming attacks. Despite Kyurem-W's middling base 95 Speed stat, Pokemon such as Reuniclus and Skeledirge are grateful to be able to outspeed a lot of the common walls. Faster Pokemon such as Sneasler and Iron Moth can also help alleviate Kyurem-W's lackluster Speed stat while also threatening Fairy-types such as Primarina and Arceus-Fairy. Lastly, Kyurem-W slots best into the Defense or Speed slot, as both are its weakest stats to offer to its teammates. Which one Kyurem-W should slot in is highly dependent on whether it is paired with the likes of Galarian Slowking and Primarina, which would appreciate the Defense, or Reuniclus and Skeledirge, which would appreciate the Speed.

Calm Mind.description:
Keldeo uses Calm Mind to become a setup sweeper that is very difficult to take down. Icy Wind is used to deal with Latios, Sinistcha, and Hydrapple. Secret Sword is a reliable STAB move against special walls such as Blissey and Gastrodon as well as opposing Keldeo and Rotom-Wash. Substitute allows Keldeo to take advantage of the switches it forces, giving it setup opportunities against Thundurus-T and Lokix, as well as blocking status from Clodsire, Toxapex, and Mandibuzz. Alternatively, Vacuum Wave can be used to pick off faster threats such as Greninja and Weavile.
