Leftovers gives Keldeo additional recovery over the course of the match and can allow Keldeo to set up multiple Substitutes. A Timid nature is preferred, as it gives Keldeo the ability to outspeed Thundurus-T, Sandy Shocks, and Hydreigon. However, a modest nature can be used for more power, allowing Keldeo to 2HKO Fezandipiti at +1. Tera Steel gives Keldeo resistances to Psychic, Dragon, and Fairy, which is handy against Latios, Choice Scarf Gardevoir, and Fezandipiti.

Keldeo best fits on bulky offense and balance teams. Teammates such as Thundurus-T and Hydrapple can deal with bulky Water-types like Slowking, Gastrodon, and Toxapex. Pivots such as Lokix, Galarian Zapdos, and Slowking can bring Keldeo in safely, as it does not want to switch in directly. Entry hazard removers such as Excadrill and Donphan help to clear Spikes off the field, which is crucial for Keldeo's longevity. They also help in defeating Clodsire, which can stop Keldeo in its tracks. Faster Pokemon, such as Weavile and Greninja, help defeat Latios, which allows Keldeo to use Secret Sword more freely.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Keldeo is a powerful wallbreaker thanks to its great offensive typing alongside good Special Attack and Speed, which allow it to do massive damage to much of the tier. Surf is its most reliable STAB move; Secret Sword does more damage against special walls like Blissey, Gastrodon, Tyranitar, and Assault Vest Conkeldurr. Icy Wind is used as coverage to threaten Pokemon that can deal with its STAB moves like Hydrapple, Sinistcha, and Latios. Vacuum Wave's priority allows Keldeo to revenge kill Pokemon like Sand Rush Excadrill and Weavile. Flip Turn is also an option over Icy Wind or Vacuum Wave, since it allows Keldeo to pivot to a teammate and generate momentum against its checks, though the move can be difficult to fit in. Tera Water increases Surf's damage output and allows Keldeo to consistently OHKO Thundurus-T, Skarmory, and Iron Jugulis.

Choice Specs Keldeo fits on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its consistently powerful damage output. Tyranitar benefits from Keldeo's ability to answer checks like Donphan, Excadrill, and Skarmory, and in return, it pressures some of Keldeo's checks like Latios, Sinistcha, and Slowking. Pivots like Scizor and Lokix are useful, since they can get Keldeo in safely; Volt Switch users such as Thundurus-T and Sandy Shocks also benefit from Keldeo's ability to deal with most Electric immunities like Excadrill, Hippowdon, and Donphan. Since Keldeo is forgoing Heavy-Duty Boots, it's a good idea to run entry hazard removal with it like Rapid Spin Excadrill and Donphan as well as Defog Mandibuzz and Talonflame; the latter two can also run U-turn to bring in Keldeo safely.

Boots Attacker.description:
Keldeo is a great offensive Water-type for balance and bulky offense teams, finding a niche over similar offensive Water-types like Walking Wake and Ogerpon-W thanks to its Fighting typing and access to Vacuum Wave. Aura Sphere is preferred over Secret Sword, as it allows Keldeo to break past Alomomola, but Secret Sword can be used to do more damage to some special walls like Ting-Lu and Blissey. Vacuum Wave is an amazing move, giving Keldeo the ability to pick off many Pokemon including Kingambit, Darkrai, Weavile, and Meowscarada. Flip Turn rounds out its moveset as a very safe option to maintain momentum, but it is notably punishable by Ogerpon-W. Tera Water boosts the power of Surf and sheds its Fairy weakness, allowing it to pick off Iron Valiant and Clefable and secure an OHKO on specially defensive Gliscor after Stealth Rock.

Keldeo fits on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its wallbreaking capabilities. Hazard stacking cores are essential to Keldeo teams, as it often finds itself unable to break bulkier teams on its own when Heavy-Duty Boots are intact or hazards remain off the field. Gliscor fits especially well with Keldeo when running Knock Off + Swords Dance sets, as it provides a great wincon into bulky teams while appreciating Keldeo's ability to heavily threaten offensive teams that can overwhelm Gliscor with direct damage. Gliscor and Ting-Lu are both immune to Electric, guarding Keldeo from threats like Zapdos and Raging Bolt, while Skarmory can check physical threats attempting to use Keldeo as safe entry point like Ogerpon-W and Dragonite. All three Spikes users appreciate Keldeo pressuring Spikes-immune Pokemon like Gliscor and Clefable and Keldeo's ability to use Flip Turn against its counters like Alomomola and Galarian Slowking to give good opportunities for them to set up Spikes. Stealth Rock users like Clefable, Tinkaton, and Ting-Lu are also crucial to ensure maximum damage from entry hazards. Tinkaton in particular is amazing, as its Fairy / Steel typing allows it to check Pokemon that heavily threaten Keldeo like Hatterene, Iron Valiant, and Kyurem if its Air Balloon is still intact, while its Encore serves as a backup check to Kingambit if it uses Tera Ghost on Keldeo's Vacuum Wave. Tinkaton loves Keldeo threatening Ground- and Fire-types like Great Tusk, Moltres, and Cinderace that heavily threaten it. Knock Off users complete hazard cores by removing Heavy-Duty Boots for Keldeo, and Knock Off users that synergize with Keldeo include Clefable and Weavile. Keldeo appreciates how Weavile and Calm Mind + Knock Off Clefable can wear down defensive cores featuring Pokemon like Alomomola, Primarina, and Toxapex. Ogerpon-W is a huge threat for Keldeo, as its Water immunity, access to Knock Off, and higher base Speed can easily lead to Ogerpon-W offensively overwhelming Keldeo and winning the game. To counteract this, Ogerpon-W answers like Dragonite, Dragapult, Pecharunt, and Zamazenta are greatly appreciated. Dragonite is an especially good partner, as its Extreme Speed covers threats that Keldeo cannot revenge kill with Vacuum Wave such as Iron Valiant and Iron Moth, while Keldeo provides a check to Weavile and threatens bulky Ground-types like Gliscor, Ting-Lu, and Great Tusk. All-out attacking Zamazenta provides excellent speed control, appreciates Keldeo wearing down Dragapult, and is a massive threat for offense teams that can overwhelm Keldeo. Sinistcha, Pecharunt, and Dragapult can help Keldeo by being solid spinblockers, allowing hazards to stay up so Keldeo can threaten bulkier cores featuring Pokemon like Assault Vest Primarina, Assault Vest Alomomola, and Toxapex. Sinistcha can additionally serve as a potent win condition that finds opportunities to set up Calm Mind on Water-types Keldeo draws in, while Pecharunt can bring Keldeo in by pivoting out of Ground-types like Ting-Lu and Gliscor and check Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Dragonite for Keldeo. Pecharunt also appreciates Keldeo's ability to threaten the aforementioned Dark-types and provides an answer to Iron Valiant without Shadow Ball, Dragonite, and Ogerpon-W. Most Dragapult sets are major threats to bulkier teams that Keldeo can struggle with, and it appreciates Keldeo being able to threaten Dark-types like Hisuian Samurott, Ting-Lu, and Kingambit.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Keldeo is an effective wallbreaker that can leverage its high Special Attack, decent Speed, and unique STAB move options to break holes into the opposition. Surf is usually preferred for its higher accuracy, but Hydro Pump can be chosen to get a guaranteed OHKO on Enamorus, a chance to OHKO Gholdengo, and a guaranteed OHKO on Hatterene after Stealth Rock. Both Secret Sword and Aura Sphere OHKO threats like Kyurem, Darkrai, Hisuian Samurott, Weavile, and Kingambit. Secret Sword also yields great damage against Blissey, Tera Dark or Steel Clodsire, Tera Water Ogerpon-W, and Assault Vest Iron Crown, while Aura Sphere hits defensive Alomomola and Dondozo significantly harder than Secret Sword would. Vacuum Wave grants Keldeo the opportunity to pick off weakened and faster foes like Raging Bolt, Darkrai, Weavile, and Dragon Dance-boosted Kyurem; it also gives Keldeo an edge over Kingambit trying to use Sucker Punch. Flip Turn allows Keldeo to pivot out of unfavorable matchups like Primarina, Alomomola, Toxapex, and Dragonite. Icy Wind directly threatens switch-ins like Dragonite, Dragapult, and Hydrapple. Tera Water is usually preferred, as it can give a chance to OHKO targets like Garganacl and Enamorus with Surf while also removing Keldeo's Fairy weakness for the latter. Tera Water lets Hydro Pump OHKO Pecharunt, Zapdos, offensive Zamazenta, Clefable, and Ting-Lu. Tera Fighting gives a Keldeo the opportunity to OHKO Ogerpon-W with Secret Sword and Darkrai with Vacuum Wave.

This particular Keldeo set finds its niche on bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to threaten key defensive Pokemon like Ting-Lu, Gliscor, and Moltres. Keldeo appreciates teammates that bring it in safely to effectively wallbreak or handle foes such as Iron Valiant, Dragapult, and Choice Scarf Enamorus, which outpace and threaten it. In addition to pivoting, Galarian Slowking can provide a reliable answer to threats such as Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf Enamorus. It also provides Future Sight, which discourages checks like Toxapex from coming in on Keldeo. Zapdos provides a defensive answer to Grass-type Pokemon that look to revenge kill Keldeo. Dragapult is an effective teammate for Keldeo, as it can bring Keldeo in versus Garganacl and Ting-Lu and take on foes that try to advantage of a Choice-locked Keldeo, like Raging Bolt, Dragonite, and Kyurem. Garganacl and Ting-Lu can serve as effective partners due to their ability to answer Dragapult. Choice Scarf Gholdengo can provide speed control and cripple walls with Trick, pressuring common defensive cores in conjunction with Keldeo's offensive prowess. Dragonite can help answer Ogerpon-W for Keldeo; in return, Keldeo can punch through walls like Corviknight and Ting-Lu for Dragonite. Keldeo also appreciates entry hazard support from partners like Ting-Lu, Tinkaton, Iron Treads, and Great Tusk to further enhance its wallbreaking opportunities, reaching feats such as a guaranteed OHKO on Garganacl with Surf after Stealth Rock. Keldeo can easily be worn down by hazards; therefore, it values entry hazard removal from allies like Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Corviknight.

Choice Specs Keldeo leverages its fantastic offensive and defensive typing to be a reliable wallbreaker, capable of threatening defensive staples like Celesteela, Scizor, and Tyranitar while taking little from their attacks. Hydro Pump is generally preferred on Keldeo, OHKOing Buzzwole and Scizor after Stealth Rock and having odds to 2HKO defensive Celesteela. Surf hits similarly hard, and while it misses these damage thresholds, it provides greater consistency and more PP; this is particularly notable against Celesteela, which can waste Hydro Pump PP with Protect. Air Slash 2HKOes Mega Venusaur and Amoonguss, while Flip Turn is an option alongside Pursuit users like Tyranitar and Bisharp, as they can threaten the aforementioned defensive options as well as other answers to Keldeo like Slowking and Mega Latias. Toxic is an alternative on teams without Pursuit to cripple checks like Slowking and Mega Latias, but it significantly hinders Keldeo's matchup against Mega Venusaur and Amoonguss, making it a niche option. Vacuum Wave provides Keldeo with powerful priority that is able to pick off faster threats like Sand Rush Excadrill as well as weakened targets like Iron Boulder and Mega Aerodactyl. Keldeo is typically seen on offense and sand teams looking for a powerful special attacker that can shore up weaknesses to offensive threats like Mienshao and Iron Boulder. Sand teams in particular utilize Keldeo well, as Tyranitar can Pursuit trap Slowking and Mega Latias with Pursuit and provides sand, preventing Synthesis Mega Venusaur from being a reliable long-term check to Keldeo. Keldeo in return can help force damage onto Rotom-W and handle physical walls like Skarmory and Buzzwole. While Keldeo is powerful, it can struggle against teams with multiple Pokemon resistant or immune to its STAB attacks, which include defensive options such as Mega Venusaur, Slowking, and Mega Latias. It can also be outsped quite easily by the offensive metagame, which consists of Pokemon such as Iron Moth, Iron Boulder, and Mega Aerodactyl. For these reasons, teammates like Scizor and Mienshao are appreciated for their ability to pressure shared checks, use Knock Off to remove important held items like Leftovers from Aegislash and Celesteela, and provide offensive answers to these Pokemon that threaten Keldeo. Teammates like Iron Moth and Zeraora work similarly, pivoting Keldeo in against Ground- and Grass-type Pokemon that it can threaten. Swampert, Skarmory, and Celesteela help provide Keldeo's team with a defensive backbone against options like Iron Boulder and Clefable, with the former two able to set entry hazards to wear down many of its checks.

Calm Mind.description: Calm Mind Keldeo is a fantastic wallbreaker, its formidable offensive typing and ability to run a variety of mixed attacking sets enable it to be a threat against balanced or stall teams, making it an effective setup sweeper versus the likes of Swampert, Tyranitar, and Celesteela. Scald is an excellent Water-type STAB move for Keldeo, as it can burn foes and make it easier to wear down physical attackers like Scizor and Mega Gallade. Hydro Pump, though having lower accuracy, is best used in tandem with Waterium Z to OHKO Swampert after a Calm Mind boost while threatening a KO on both Buzzwole and Scizor with an unboosted Hydro Vortex. Secret Sword is Keldeo's preferred Fighting-type STAB attack, as it hits common pivots to special attacks like Blissey. Substitute, when paired with Leftovers, helps Keldeo set up on defensive switch-ins like Slowking, Gastrodon, and Celesteela. Alternatively, Air Slash could be used for coverage against threatening Grass-type foes and gives Keldeo the ability to run Flyinium Z to OHKO the likes of Hydrapple and Mega Venusaur after a boost. Alternatively, Taunt can be used to prevent bulky Pokemon like Slowbro and Aegislash from spreading status. With this much wallbreaking power, Keldeo is seen on more offensive teams that are lacking in checks against the likes of Scizor and Greninja. Although Keldeo can be seen as a wallbreaking threat, many teams can utilize Pokemon that aren't weak to either STAB attack such as Mega Venusaur and Slowking. There are also quite a few Pokemon that can outspeed and threaten Keldeo such as Zeraora, Iron Boulder, and Serperior. Teamates such as Scizor and Mienshao help against these faster threats and can assist greatly by pressuring checks to Keldeo like Aegislash and Celesteela by removing their Leftovers while also being able to efficiently pivot out with U-turn. In return, Keldeo assists both by pressuring physical walls like Skarmory and Mandibuzz. Teammates that can provide entry hazard support such as Tyranitar and Clefable are appreciated by Keldeo, as chip from entry hazards makes it easier to threaten a OHKO on physical walls. Faster teammates such as Iron Moth and Zeraora can be excellent in baiting in Ground-type threats and pivoting back into Keldeo for more offensive pressure. In return, Keldeo removes Ground-type threats like Excadrill and Hippowdon to make it easier for both to pivot reliably.

Choice Specs (Water).description:
Choice Specs Keldeo is a formidable wallbreaker for Water teams, easily dismantling Flying and Steel defensive cores without setup, which makes it terrifying from the get-go. Hydro Pump 2HKOes popular walls such as specially defensive Corviknight and Gholdengo. Surf is an alternative that ensures consistency against Pokemon with Pressure. Secret Sword sets Keldeo apart from other Water-type attackers by allowing Keldeo to OHKO specially defensive targets such as Hisuian Goodra and to 2HKO Articuno and Alolan Muk. Vacuum Wave can pick off weakened foes such as Roaring Moon, Excadrill, and Meowscarada. Lastly, Icy Wind targets Dragonite and prevents popular Choice Specs users like Dragapult and Latios from switching into Keldeo.

Keldeo appreciates entry hazard setters such as Swampert and Gastrodon, as they bolster Keldeo's attacking prowess and are immune to Electric. Swampert can also run utility moves such as Knock Off and Flip Turn, which makes it the ideal partner to maintain pressure. Toxapex provides a useful Fairy-resistant option for Flutter Mane's Moonblast, removes Toxic Spikes from the field, and has access to utility options such as Toxic, Toxic Spikes, and Haze to support Keldeo. Hisuian Samurott can set up Spikes, provides a useful Psychic immunity, and can remove foes such as Dragapult and Latios with Sucker Punch, which reduces the need for prediction on Keldeo's part. Other excellent offensive teammates include Ogerpon-W and Greninja; Ogerpon-W can deal with Water Absorb Clodsire, Azumarill, and Primarina against which Keldeo is powerless, and Greninja can address any issue Keldeo faces thanks to its huge offensive movepool. Greninja's Sludge Wave hits Grass- and Fairy-types that handle Keldeo like the Ogerpon formes, Primarina, and Iron Valiant, while Extrasensory and Ice Beam can deal with Poison-, Flying-, and Dragon-types. Finally, Keldeo appreciates rain from Drizzle Pelipper, as it allows Hydro Pump to OHKO defensive Gholdengo and Corviknight, while Pelipper's Hurricane can deal with Grass-type foes such as Rillaboom and Amoonguss.

Calm Mind (Water).description:
With Calm Mind, Keldeo turns into a great sweeper that can threaten foes both physically and specially. Vacuum Wave is a strong STAB priority option to pick off faster albeit weakened threats like Meowscarada, Greninja, and Choice Scarf Hydreigon. Surf is highly accurate, targeting slower threats like non-Choice Scarf Landorus and Gliscor, while Hydro Pump, although it has lower accuracy, brings more power, notably 2HKOing physically defensive Corviknight. Secret Sword threatens special walls that Keldeo's other moves do not; it OHKOes Assault Vest Hisuian Goodra and 2HKOes Alolan Muk after a Calm Mind boost. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Keldeo to switch in safely regardless of entry hazards, while Leftovers grants Keldeo a small form of longevity.

Swampert and Gastrodon make for good teammates, as they set up entry hazards that can help Keldeo sweep, and they also both provide an immunity against Electric-types like Magnezone and Regieleki. In return, Keldeo threatens Choice Specs Kyurem for them. Toxapex is another great defensive partner, threatening Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Enamorus with Sludge Bomb; it also absorbs Toxic Spikes for Keldeo when Keldeo isn't running Heavy-Duty Boots. In return, Keldeo handles Ground-types that threaten Toxapex such as Ursaluna and Landorus. Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott outspeeds Pokemon that can shrug off Keldeo's STAB moves, such as Latios and Dragapult, while easily setting up Spikes with Ceaseless Edge. Greninja makes for another great partner, as it outspeeds and threatens the likes of Iron Valiant, Primarina, and the Ogerpon formes with Sludge Wave. In return, Keldeo threatens Hisuian Goodra for it. Ogerpon-W forms an offensive core with Keldeo. It checks Water Absorb Clodsire, Azumarill, and Primarina, while Keldeo threatens Archaludon.

Choice Specs (Fighting).description:
Equipped with Choice Specs, Keldeo makes for a strong wallbreaker on Fighting teams, threatening the likes of Great Tusk and Gliscor with Hydro Pump and outspeeding both Landorus formes and Garchomp. With Secret Sword, Keldeo is able to threaten foes physically and specially; thus, walls that would normally switch into one of Keldeo's other attacks, such as Alolan Muk, Hisuian Goodra, and Articuno, take high damage from it. Vacuum Wave serves as a strong revenge killing option for Keldeo, picking off faster weakened threats like Greninja and Excadrill and KOing Meowscarada after Stealth Rock damage with ease. Icy Wind grants Keldeo coverage against Dragon-types, and with the Speed drop, it is able to counter Dragon Dance attempts from Garchomp. Surf is a great Water-type STAB move that, although weaker than Hydro Pump, has greater accuracy.

Great Tusk is an almost-universal choice for a partner for Keldeo, both setting up Stealth Rock to wear down incoming foes and removing entry hazards with Rapid Spin so Keldeo can switch in safely. Great Tusk also provides an Electric immunity for Keldeo, and it can take out the likes of Iron Hands, Toxapex, and Water Absorb Clodsire. Iron Hands grants Fighting teams coverage against Flying teams, and with its bulk and movepool, it is able to remove the likes of Gyarados, Tornadus-T, and Enamorus. Iron Valiant is another great teammate for Keldeo, outspeeding the likes of Choice Specs Dragapult, Choice Band Roaring Moon, and non-Choice Scarf Meowscarada when equipped with a Choice Scarf. Its mixed sets work well with Keldeo, softening each other's checks while wearing down shared checks like Toxapex. Choice Scarf Sneasler is a fast pivot for Fighting teams with U-turn, and it can aid Keldeo in its wallbreaking with its great status spreading abilities thanks to a combination of Dire Claw and Poison Touch. Sneasler can also take out faster threats that annoy Keldeo such as Meowscarada, the Ogerpon formes, and Iron Valiant. In return, Keldeo is able to remove the Ground-types that annoy Sneasler such as Unaware Clodsire and Great Tusk. Gallade is another great teammate due to its ability to break down Poison teams. Lastly, Keldeo's wallbreaking abilities open up room for sweepers like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant to clean late-game, the two of them also appreciating Keldeo removing walls such as Corviknight.

Calm Mind (Fighting).description:
With Calm Mind; Keldeo can break through the bulkiest of threats such as Archaludon while also dealing heavy damage on Gouging Fire and Ursaluna-B. Keldeo is also able to outspeed Landorus. Secret Sword is Keldeo's best way to break through even the bulkiest of the metagame such as Blissey and Hisuian Goodra, and Keldeo can take advantage of Secret Sword by boosting it with Calm Mind and hitting them on their physical defensive side. Surf threatens Ground-types such as Landorus, Ursaluna-B, Gliscor, and Hippowdon while dealing with physical walls like Skarmory, which Fighting has a difficult time facing. Along with breaking through bulky Pokemon such as Corviknight, Ting-Lu, and Heatran. Vacuum Wave gets rid of faster threats that outspeed Keldeo such as Chien-Pao and Meowscarada. Heavy-Duty Boots keeps Keldeo safe from getting chipped by entry hazards, as removal is very difficult for Fighting.

Great Tusk is an amazing defensive teammate for Keldeo, providing an Electric immunity and the ability to not only set up Stealth Rock but also use Taunt opposing Defoggers, allowing its entry hazards to chip foes. Great Tusk can take out opposing threats to Keldeo such as Iron Hands, Toxapex, and Clodsire. Assault Vest Iron Hands grants coverage against Flying. With its high HP stat and tremendous bulk; it can remove the likes of Enamorus, Gyarados, and Tornadus-T. Choice Scarf Iron Valiant can outspeed Choice Scarf Latias, Choice Specs Greninja, and non-Choice Scarf Dragapult. Iron Valiant can also run a mixed set that gives more coverage to further assist Keldeo by outspeeding the Ogerpon formes and picking up suprise KOs by not being locked into a single move. Choice Scarf Sneasler is an alternative option to pair with Keldeo, as it can use U-turn against threats such as Gliscor and Great Tusk that Keldeo can take advantage of. With Dire Claw, Sneasler can potentially spread status on problematic foes such as Hatterene and Flutter Mane. Sneasler also outspeeds threats to Keldeo such as the Ogerpon formes and Iron Valiant. Choice Band Zamazenta can assist in breaking through faster Pokemon like Choice Specs Greninja and Choice Specs Latios, while its Substitute + Iron Defense set can safely set up and break down teams. Gallade is a unique teammate for Keldeo as well, as it's able to break down Poison teams, a matchup where Keldeo struggles quite a lot.

Choice Specs (Fighting).description: Keldeo stands out as Fighting team's premier Choice Specs user, leveraging its solid typing and unique toolkit to easily break past physical walls such as Mega Sableye and Gliscor that often cause issues for Fighting teams. Hydro Pump is Keldeo's strongest attack, washing away Ground- and Fire-types like the Landorus formes, Great Tusk, and Skeledirge with ease. Secret Sword enables Keldeo to break special walls such as Blissey and Hisuian Goodra that would otherwise wall it. Vacuum Wave serves as a Fighting team's main form of priority, being used to pick off weakened targets such as Sand Rush Excadrill and Meowscarada, which can be a nuisance to Fighting teams. Finally, Keldeo can use Icy Wind to immediately remove threats such as Garchomp and Latios in a pinch. Alternatively, Scald can be used as a completely accurate Water-type STAB move in situations where Hydro Pump's higher power isn't needed, while Hidden Power Electric enables Keldeo to break past Pelipper and Mantine. Iron Hands serves as an excellent partner to Keldeo, as it is able to break through Water-types that can handle Keldeo such as Tapu Fini and Toxapex along with taking on faster Flying-types like Tornadus-T and Mega Pidgeot; in return, it appreciates Keldeo breaking Ground-types such as Gliscor and Great Tusk. Mega Gallade can break through problematic threats that can easily take on Keldeo such as Mega Venusaur and Water Absorb Clodsire, which otherwise wall Keldeo. Iron Valiant deals with Dragon-type threats such as Kommo-o, Mega Altaria, and Latias along with using coverage moves like Shadow Ball to beat Sinistcha. Breloom and Hisuian Lilligant both assist Keldeo by breaking down Water-types like Swampert and Greninja and appreciate Keldeo handling Fire-types like Torkoal and Ceruledge. Great Tusk provides Rapid Spin and Stealth Rock support, enabling Keldeo to get in safely while chipping down switch-ins like Assault Vest Iron Hands, and its Ground typing enables it to handle Electric-types such as Regieleki and Raging Bolt. Sneasler is a fast teammate that can handle Fairy- and Grass-types like Iron Valiant, Tapu Bulu, and Breloom.

Calm Mind (Water).description: Keldeo's ability to break through dedicated special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Blissey and access to priority to trounce revenge-killers like Meowscarada make it a strong setup wallbreaker or late-game cleaner on faster-paced Water teams, like those utilizing rain. Waterium Z-boosted Hydro Pump heavily pressures common checks to Water teams like Toxapex, Mega Venusaur, and Ferrothorn at +1 in rain, making them unable to come in to check other Water-type moves. Alternatively, Surf has better accuracy but has worse chances to OHKO the aforementioned Pokemon with Hydro Vortex. Secret Sword cleaves through special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Dark-types like Hydreigon. With Fightinium Z, Keldeo benefits from the one-time removal of Secret Sword's special effect, letting it OHKO Archaludon and Ferrothorn at +1. Vacuum Wave picks off weakened threats like Meowscarada and Mega Lopunny and KOes them after minimal chip damage at +1. Alternatively, Taunt prevents Toxapex and Skarmory from using Haze or phazing Keldeo. It also stops Clodsire and Celesteela from using Toxic or Leech Seed to wear it down. Keldeo is walled by the likes of Water Absorb Clodsire and Celebi and gets threatened out by faster wallbreakers such as Mega Latios and Ogerpon-W, so Choice Specs Greninja is appreciated as a teammate that can deal with those threats. Pelipper provides rain, which boosts Keldeo's breaking power, and also enables Swift Swim sweepers such as Mega Swampert and Barraskewda. Under rain, they outspeed and remove threats to Keldeo such as Tapu Koko, Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, and Mega Diancie. Hisuian Samurott sets Spikes through Ceaseless Edge, helping Keldeo hit damage breakpoints, and also removes Celebi and Galarian Slowking for it. Defensive teammates like Toxapex and Empoleon provide switch-ins into Tapu Bulu and Greninja, respectively. Both also set entry hazards to help Keldeo reach the chip damage needed to brute force defensive walls and in return love Keldeo's ability to remove offensive Ground-types like Landorus and Ursaluna.

nu.overview: Meloetta's amazing Special Attack and solid special bulk let it feature in several roles as a special wallbreaker, offensive pivot, Calm Mind sweeper, revenge killer, and late-game cleaner. Thanks to Meloetta's range, it can be unpredictable at team preview and early-game. It's also an excellent user of Terastallization, using it to overpower would-be checks such as Duraludon with Tera Ghost Shadow Ball and Incineroar with Tera Fighting Focus Blast. However, Meloetta's offensive STAB moves leave gaps in its coverage against Steel-types like Klefki, Bronzong, and Copperajah, and it struggles to pack a coverage move to hit all of them super effectively. Meloetta's Choice item sets are prediction-reliant and struggle with Focus Blast's inaccuracy as well as Shadow Ball's limited coverage, while Throat Spray sets struggle to find opportunities to use Hyper Voice to set up. Meloetta's Speed tier leaves it behind revenge killers like Paldean Tauros-W, Flygon, and Cinccino, while Scream Tail severely annoys Meloetta's setup sets with its fast Encore. Meloetta also competes with special attackers like Sylveon, Munkidori, and Chandelure, which can offer much more immediate power and pivoting opportunities between the three of them.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Alluring Voice goes through Substitute and provides Meloetta with Fairy-type coverage without requiring it to Terastallize, but common Dark-types like Incineroar and Alolan Muk are hit neutrally by it anyway. Knock Off provides similar utility to Trick against item-dependent Pokemon like Incineroar and Porygon2 without forcing Meloetta to give up its Choice item, but a Choice item tends to be more devastating against these foes. Assault Vest Meloetta has great special bulk for tanking hits from wallbreakers like Toxtricity and Porygon-Z, but it lacks the standout Speed and power of its Choice sets. Meloetta can run a pivot set with Heavy-Duty Boots that avoids the shortcomings of its Choice item sets having to lock into one move and taking entry hazard damage.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Klefki doesn't fear any of Meloetta's coverage moves, Bronzong deals with Meloetta variants that don't have Shadow Ball, and all Steel-types can tank Meloetta's STAB attacks and use it as an opportunity to set up entry hazards. However, Steel-types like Alolan Sandslash and Copperajah must be wary of Focus Blast.

Physically Offensive Revenge Killers: Flygon, Paldean Tauros-W, and Staraptor outpace Meloetta, and they can match its Choice Scarf sets with ones of their own. Scyther and Cinccino even have multi-hit moves to break past Substitute sets.

Bulky Dark-types: Alolan Muk does not struggle with Meloetta's coverage moves, though it can be worn down by repeated hits from Choice Specs sets. Incineroar, Scrafty, and Wo-Chien must be wary of Focus Blast, but they have the bulk to tank one attack and retaliate against Meloetta with Knock Off.

Choice Item.description:
Set Details

Meloetta's STAB moves are quite spammable against defensive staples like Amoonguss, Gastrodon, and Swampert. Psyshock is an alternative to Psychic, allowing Meloetta to nail specially bulky Pokemon like Porygon2, Goodra, Gastrodon, and Sylveon as well as special sweepers like Oricorio-F and Raikou, but Psychic's better damage against Pokemon like Diancie and Paldean Tauros-W makes it preferred. Hyper Voice's ability to go through Substitute is helpful against users like Raikou, Nasty Plot Uxie, and Goodra. Shadow Ball covers Bronzong and hits Scream Tail, Oricorio-P, and Basculegion super effectively. In addition, Shadow Ball has a neat synergy with Serene Grace, improving Meloetta's odds to overwhelm Bronzong and Scream Tail. Focus Blast hits other Steel-types like Alolan Sandslash, Duraludon, and Copperajah super effectively, and it's useful coverage against Dark-types like Incineroar and Scrafty. U-turn lets Meloetta keep up momentum for its team against switch-ins like Klefki, Copperajah, and Bronzong. Meloetta can use Trick to disrupt its defensive switch-ins, as a Choice item is especially devastating to walls like Copperajah and Porygon2. However, Meloetta can drop Trick for U-turn so it can fit a coverage move while still acting as an offensive pivot. Tera Fighting grants Meloetta key resistances to moves like Knock Off and Sucker Punch against foes like Alolan Muk and Toxicroak, and the coverage it provides in conjunction with Tera Blast enables Meloetta to break through Copperajah, Porygon2, and Alolan Sandslash. Tera Fairy shares Tera Fighting's nice resistances against Dark- and Bug-type moves, and it grants Meloetta better defensive matchups against Fighting-types like Scrafty and Heracross when it's in a pinch. Tera Ghost powers up Shadow Ball to nail Bronzong and Scream Tail, and the Fighting immunity it offers is helpful against Body Press users like the aforementioned Bronzong and Diancie.

Meloetta appreciates checks to troublesome Steel-types like Copperajah and Bronzong, so wallbreakers such as Paldean Tauros-W, Paldean Tauros-F, and Basculegion make good teammates. Fighting-types like Scrafty and Toxicroak compensate for Meloetta's difficult matchups against bulky Dark-types like Incineroar and Alolan Muk. Offensive pivots like Flygon, Flamigo, and Kilowattrel can get Meloetta into good positions by bringing it in against defensive Pokemon like Breloom, Amoonguss, and Galarian Slowbro, which is greatly appreciated by Choice Specs variants. Slow, defensive pivots like Vaporeon, Swampert, and Incineroar can go a step further by tanking hits for Meloetta as they switch it in. Entry hazard removers like Cinccino and Altaria help keep Meloetta from being worn down as it pivots on and off the field. Meloetta itself appreciates hazards from setters like Copperajah, Diancie, and Gastrodon for wearing down checks like Alolan Muk, Klefki, and opposing Diancie. Physically defensive Pokemon like Amoonguss, Galarian Slowbro, and Sylveon can switch into physically offensive revenge killers such as Flygon, Paldean Tauros-W, and Scyther to let Meloetta switch out.

Throat Spray.description:
Hyper Voice activates Throat Spray, giving Meloetta an immediate Special Attack boost without locking it into a move allowing it to function as a mid-game wallbreaker or cleaner with more flexibility than Choice-locked sets. Psyshock is generally preferred to pressure specially bulky Pokemon such as Chansey, Sylveon, and Goodra, though Psychic provides stronger immediate damage against targets like Paldean Tauros-W. Shadow Ball provides coverage against Pokemon like Bronzong, Chandelure, and Basculegion while also hitting Psychic-types like Munkidori and Hoopa. Focus Blast is needed to threaten Steel- and Dark-types such as Copperajah, Duraludon, Incineroar, and Scrafty. Tera Fighting further boosts Focus Blast to break through these foes more reliably while also granting useful resistances to Knock Off from Incineroar, U-turn from Flygon, and Sucker Punch from Toxicroak. Tera Ghost strengthens Shadow Ball, allowing +1 Meloetta to 2HKO Duraludon after Stealth Rock and OHKO targets such as Uxie and Munkidori while also providing a useful Fighting immunity.

Despite the immediate boost, Meloetta struggles against dedicated defensive cores, as walls and Dark-types like Tera Dark Chansey and Wo-Chien can reliably pivot into its attacks, so it fits best on offensive teams that can weaken these checks beforehand. Wallbreakers such as Paldean Tauros-F, Flamigo, and Toxicroak help pressure Steel-types and prevent them from comfortably switching in, while Paldean Tauros-W and Swampert wear down Incineroar and Scrafty directly over time; they are repeatedly drawn in by partners like Munkidori, Raikou, and Flygon, which chip them on the switch or pivot out. Heracross is particularly valuable, as it can absorb Knock Off and break through Meloetta's checks. Dedicated hyper offense leads such as Dudunsparce and Infernape provide strong early-game momentum, as Dudunsparce spreads paralysis with Glare, letting Meloetta outspeed common switch-ins, and both can set Stealth Rock. Infernape also removes items like Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers with Knock Off. This ensures entry hazard damage consistently sticks, keeping targets in range for Meloetta, with softer checks like Goodra and Sylveon worn down by repeated switch-ins. Additionally, Infernape pressures the Dark- and Steel-types directly with its STAB attacks that would otherwise threaten Meloetta. On offense, Throat Spray Meloetta can be somewhat inconsistent, so entry hazard support from Klefki and Gligar helps wear down opposing switch-ins such as Brambleghast, Wo-Chien, and Tsareena and brings them into range of Meloetta’s boosted attacks. Pivots like Flygon and Uxie bring Meloetta in safely against passive targets such as Amoonguss, Galarian Slowbro, and Vaporeon, giving it an opportunity to activate Throat Spray.

Choice Specs (Normal).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

RegenVest.description: RegenVest Meloetta is a capable pivot thanks to its ability to switch into most special attackers like Gholdengo, Scream Tail, Deoxys-S, and Iron Moth. Knock Off gives Meloetta an option to support its teammates by removing key items such as Assault Vest from Swampert and Hisuian Goodra, while Thunderbolt hits Manaphy and non-Volt Absorb Corviknight for high damage. Low Kick lets Meloetta chip Hisuian Goodra and Heatran, but Energy Ball can be used instead to 2HKO Swampert after its Assault Vest has been removed. Good teammates include Pokemon like Roaring Moon, Galarian Zapdos, Barraskewda, and Chien-Pao because Meloetta can safely get them into the field with a slow U-turn. Physical attackers like Roaring Moon and Chien-Pao naturally threaten Meloetta out, so Pokemon that can deal with them, like Corviknight, Great Tusk, and defensive Quaquaval, make for good partners. Lastly, Meloetta appreciates entry hazard removal from the likes of Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Mandibuzz, to keep its HP high enough to switch into strong attackers.

Defensive Spikes.description:
Chespin's Grass typing, access to Bulletproof, and reliable recovery in Synthesis allow it to wall staples like Foongus and check Ground-types like Alolan Diglett and Mudbray. It can leverage its bulk to make progress by setting Spikes. Bullet Seed has the benefit of breaking Substitute from Alolan Diglett. As an entry hazard setter, Chespin needs ways to deal with common entry hazard removal Pokemon, using Rock Slide to hit Vullaby super effectively while its Drain Punch stings Alolan Sandshrew. The given EV spread maximizes bulk, allowing Chespin to survive two High Jump Kicks from Mienfoo and two Ice Beams from Chinchou. Tera Steel grants Chespin resistances to Vullaby's Brave Bird and Alolan Sandshrew's Triple Axel as well as an immunity to Stunky's Gunk Shot. Meanwhile, Tera Fairy resists Knock Off and Mienfoo's High Jump Kick.

Pokemon that struggle with Foongus such as Mienfoo and Chinchou appreciate Chespin's ability to switch in and set entry hazards to wear it down. Spikes can chip foes into KO range for wallbreakers such as Stunky and Alolan Diglett. Since Chespin is weak to Vullaby, partners such as Tinkatink and Glimmet can support it by switching in and setting Stealth Rock to limit Vullaby's longevity. These partners can also synergize with Chespin to form a hazard stacking core. Mareanie is a strong partner that can check Mienfoo and Fire-types like Salandit and Hisuian Growlithe. In return, Chespin can check Ground-types.

nfe.overview: In a tier lacking consistent entry hazard removal, Quilladin makes for a great Spikes setter and wall with access to utility moves such as Roar and Super Fang, working well in teams relying on hazards to make progress. Thanks to its good bulk and its ability Bulletproof, Quilladin is able to check Grass- and Ground-types such as Ivysaur, Thwackey, Krokorok, and Gabite. It can also be used as a phazer when running Roar, taking immediate advantage of its own Spikes as well as preventing bulky setup users such as Scraggy and Duosion from making progress.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Rock Tomb can be used to break through Fletchinder, preventing it from removing Quilladin's Spikes, but this means Quilladin gives up an important utility move or its Grass-type STAB move. A specially defensive spread like 252 HP / 252 SpD and a Careful nature allows Quilladin to better check special threats such as Sliggoo-Hisui and Frogadier.

Checks and Counters

Fire-types: Fire-types like Monferno, Raboot and Pignite freely come on Quilladin and threaten to KO it with super effective STAB attacks; however, they do not like being hit by Super Fang. Fletchinder is especially annoying for Quilladin, as it can remove its Spikes with Defog.

Poison-types: Despite Quilladin's immunity to Sludge Bomb, Poison-types relying on other offensive moves such as Glimmet and Stunky threaten it. Koffing also threatens Quilladin despite running Sludge Bomb thanks to its ability Neutralizing Gas, ignoring Bulletproof's effect.

Taunt users: Taunt users like Servine and Fletchinder completely neutralize Quilladin, as it relies on its utility moves.

Setup sweepers: Setup sweepers with Taunt such as Fraxure and Scraggy take advantage of Quilladin's passivity. Additionally, other setup sweepers such as Girafarig and Monferno have a free opportunity to set up on Quilladin if it's not running Roar.

U-turn: Due to Quilladin's Bug weakness, Pokemon with U-turn such as Thwackey, Drakloak, and Monferno can quickly overwhelm Quilladin, forcing it to heal regularly.

Poison: Quilladin likes staying on the field for a long time in order to set as many Spikes as possible, so Pokemon with Toxic such as Dunsparce, Glimmet, and Mareanie heavily threaten it. Additionally, Quilladin does not like coming in on Toxic Spikes, which can be set by Pokemon such as Koffing and Glimmet.

Hattrem: Thanks to Magic Bounce, Hattrem completely prevents Quilladin from setting up Spikes.

Wall.description:
Quilladin is a good wall thanks to its good defensive typing, stats, and utility moves. It takes advantage of Pokemon it checks such as Krokorok and Thwackey to set up Spikes, slowly making progress for the entire team. Wood Hammer is Quilladin's most powerful STAB move, hitting Ground- and Water-types such as Piloswine and Quaxwell. With Roar, Quilladin acts as a phazer, preventing Pokemon such as Scraggy and Duosion from setting up. Additionally, Roar takes advantage of Quilladin's own Spikes, passively doing damage to any grounded Pokemon it forces in. Super Fang does good damage to Pokemon with no recovery such as all-out attacker Hisuian Sliggoo and Pignite. Taunt can be used to help break through defensive cores including Pokemon like Duosion and Dunsparce. Taunt is especially useful when paired with Super Fang to heavily weaken defensive Pokemon while preventing them from healing. Synthesis enables Quilladin to stay on the field for a long time. Bulletproof grants an immunity to bullet moves, such as Sludge Bomb, making Quilladin a counter to Ivysaur.

Quilladin fits best on balance teams looking for a good entry hazard setter and wall to Grass- and Water-types. Pokemon weak to Grass like Quaxwell, Krokorok, and Piloswine appreciate Quilladin checking Pokemon like Servine, Thwackey, and Ivysaur. Similarly, Water-weak Pokemon like Pignite, Piloswine, and Krokorok appreciate it checking Water-types like Seadra and Quaxwell. Thanks to Bulletproof, Quilladin also checks Hisuian Sliggoo, so Pokemon that struggle against it like Koffing and Hattrem benefit from Quilladin. In return, Koffing checks common Fire-types like Fletchinder, Raboot, and Monferno, while Hattrem prevents the opponent from setting entry hazards on the field, letting Quilladin set as many Spikes as possible without having to deal with the opponent's entry hazards too. Quilladin's Spikes help wallbreakers such as Pignite and Choice Band Piloswine to break through defensive cores, while Quilladin appreciates Drakloak blocking Quaxwell from removing its Spikes thanks to its Ghost-type. Due to Quilladin's passivity, many offensive Pokemon can come in on it for free, so it appreciates being part of a solid defensive backbone including Pokemon such as Quaxwell and Seadra to check Fire-types like Raboot, Monferno and Fletchinder, as well as Pokemon like Tinkatuff and Hisuian Sliggoo to check the likes of Girafarig and Drakloak. Thanks to Magic Bounce, Hattrem completely blocks Quilladin, so Pokemon that take advantage of Hattrem's passivity such as Krokorok and Scraggy pair well with it. Similarly, Fletchinder comes in on Quilladin for free and can remove its Spikes, so Pokemon that threaten it such as Hisuian Sliggoo and Seadra make for good partners. Toxic Spikes heavily hinder Quilladin's longevity, so Poison-types such as Koffing and Mareanie are appreciated to remove them.

ru.overview: Chesnaught is a premier physical wall and Spikes setter in RU. With its great bulk and typing that naturally checks threats like Krookodile, Bisharp, and Rhyperior, it can consistently find opportunities to set up entry hazards and chip away at the opposing team itself. With utility moves like Knock Off and Leech Seed, Chesnaught can support its team throughout the game while serving as a wall for many physical attackers. Chesnaught has a great matchup against the best spinner in the tier, Cyclizar, with the ability to OHKO it should it attempt to remove Spikes. Despite Chesnaught's great matchups against many Pokemon in the tier, its typing leaves it with plenty of poor ones; Mimikyu and Entei for instance hit it for super effective damage. Chesnaught's Special Defense is also low, and it will struggle to take any special attacks it does not resist, making it vulnerable to Pokemon like Gardevoir and Basculegion-F. Chesnaught also suffers from a poor matchup against the primary Defog user of the tier, Noivern, which can easily prevent Spikes from staying active.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Chesnaught can use Seed Bomb or Wood Hammer to take advantage of its Grass typing to hit Ground- and Water-types like Gastrodon and Slowbro. Iron Defense can boost Chesnaught's survivability and the damage of Body Press, allowing it to serve as a potential sweeper. Drain Punch is an alternative Fighting-type move that does less damage but doubles as a source of recovery. Close Combat is another option that does more damage than Body Press, enabling OHKOs on Pokemon like Empoleon, Magnezone, and Hisuian Goodra with some Attack investment, although this hinders Chesnaught's role as a tank. Roar can be used to prevent foes like Mimikyu and Feraligatr from setting up. Chesnaught also has access to the incredible setup move Belly Drum, which can make it a very potent setup sweeper should it manage to set up safely. While its Speed is too low to take full advantage of it, Chesnaught can use Trailblaze to boost its Speed or priority Grassy Glide when paired with Grassy Surge Thwackey. Tera Fire grants an immunity to burn and a resistance to Fire, to turn the tables on Fire-types like Entei.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Fairy-types such as Gardevoir and Alolan Ninetales can threaten large damage against Chesnaught, while being able to easily take its attacks. However, both of these can struggle with Knock Off removing their items, and they can be walled by Tera Steel.

Flying-types: Chesnaught's 4x weakness to Flying makes it particularly vulnerable to Brave Bird from Flamigo and Hurricane from Noivern. While it can Terastallize out of this weakness, the best option to resist those attacks is Steel, which is still hit super effectively by Noivern's Flamethrower and Flamigo's Close Combat.

Psychic-types: Gardevoir, Reuniclus, Jirachi, and Slowbro all have attacks that Chesnaught is unable to take. While Knock Off helps, these foes will outspeed Chesnaught or have the bulk to tank it.

Spikes.description:
Set Details

Chesnaught is one of the most reliable Spikes setters and provides a solid defensive backbone for its team. Knock Off hits the Ghost- and Psychic-types like Basculegion-F and Slowbro that aren't afraid of Body Press while also making foes like Entei and Noivern more susceptible to entry hazards by removing their Heavy-Duty Boots. Synthesis provides a reliable means for Chesnaught to heal itself. Leech Seed is a more offensive form of recovery that provides chip damage to Chesnaught's checks and can also heal its allies. Bulletproof provides an immunity to Gengar's Shadow Ball and Amoonguss's Sludge Bomb. Rocky Helmet punishes U-turn attackers that want to pivot away from Chesnaught like Cyclizar and Jirachi. 52 Speed EVs allow Chesnaught to outspeed uninvested Bisharp, and 204 Defense EVs guarantee that Body Press OHKOes Terrakion after Spikes. Tera Ghost prevents Cyclizar from using Rapid Spin while also providing Chesnaught an immunity to Fighting, improving its matchup against Terrakion. Tera Water flips Chesnaught's Fire weakness, allowing it to stand up against Entei. Tera Steel turns the devastating Flying weakness into a resistance to aid against Noivern and Yanmega, in addition to new resistances to Dragon, Fairy, and Psychic which improve its matchup against Cyclizar, Mimikyu, and Jirachi.

Chesnaught can fit comfortably on any team style that needs a defensive presence like balance, bulky offense, or stall. Special walls like Umbreon, Jirachi, and Empoleon are also important due to Chesnaught's poor ability to check the various special attackers of the tier like Gardevoir and Gengar. Chesnaught's natural weakness to Flying-types like Noivern and Tornadus will often invite them in and allow it to use Knock Off to remove their Heavy-Duty Boots, making them vulnerable to Stealth Rock set by Blissey, Registeel, and Rhyperior. Chesnaught is vulnerable to opposing Spikes, so it appreciates hazard removal from allies like Cyclizar and Noivern.

Flame Body.description: Chesnaught's bulk, recovery, and useful resistances let it frustrate several common physical attackers, most notably Roaring Moon, Ogerpon-C, and Barraskewda, and Spikes provides utility in nearly every matchup. Flame Body has a 30% chance to end the usefulness of opposing offensive pivots, again, most notably Roaring Moon, and greatly frustrates Rapid Spin Great Tusk attempting to clear Spikes. Iron Defense is the preferred fourth move to set up alongside Bulk Up Great Tusk and Swords Dance users like Iron Hands and Garchomp, while Knock Off can help remove Heavy-Duty Boots to further accentuate Spikes. The given EV spread lets Chesnaught outpace Corviknight, giving it extra chances to fish for a burn, as Brave Bird will not 2HKO it after Iron Defense. Chesnaught mostly finds its home on stall teams, where it can find plenty of teammates to switch into its common weaknesses, especially Fire and Psychic, and can find multiple switch-in opportunities to try and activate Flame Body, which is one of the few ways for stall teams to punish pivoting. Chesnaught is especially horrified of Fire-types like Ceruledge and Cinderace, as they can obliterate it without fear of a burn, and it cannot touch Ghost-types like Gengar and Hisuian Zoroark without Knock Off, so teammates like Well-Baked Body Mandibuzz are strongly recommended.

Nasty Plot.description:
Delphox casts a spell on PU as an effective sweeper and wallbreaker, having a plethora of good matchups thanks to its high power and relatively high Speed tier. At +2, Fire Blast is able to 2HKO Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro, OHKO Bronzong, and even OHKO Bellibolt after Stealth Rock. While Flamethrower can be more consistent in terms of accuracy, its lower damage output will often lead to Delphox missing important benchmarks. Psyshock gives Delphox a way to reliably damage frailer foes that resist Fire Blast such as Salazzle as well as an option to muscle through special walls such as Florges. It also provides a reliable option to damage Pokemon that may not be hit super effectively by Delphox's other coverage moves, such as Tatsugiri and Coalossal, as well as a way to secure KOs in cases where Fire Blast missing would result in a sticky situation. Delphox's last moveslot is adjustable; Encore allows Delphox to lock foes into undesirable moves like Gastrodon's Stealth Rock and Scrafty's Bulk Up and generate setup opportunities. Grass Knot is a reliable coverage option against bulky Ground-types that may not crumble to a Fire Blast such as Gastrodon, Mudsdale, and Golurk, while Dazzling Gleam deals consistent damage to Bulk Up Paldean Tauros-W and lets Delphox beat Scrafty without prior chip damage. Tera Fairy provides Delphox with a resistance to Dark and prevents it from being revenge killed by Sucker Punch users such as Skuntank and Bombirdier while also removing other problematic weaknesses to Water, Ground, and Ghost and boosting the power of Dazzling Gleam.

Delphox is rather frail, so it needs teammates that can pivot it in safely such as Milotic, Rotom-C, and Gligar. Spikes setters such as Alolan Sandslash and Coalossal can help Delphox to secure damage benchmarks more easily, lessening the number of opportunities Fire Blast has to miss and helping to break through Scream Tail and Arcanine. Sticky Web support from Vikavolt is also valued, allowing Delphox to remedy its sometimes awkward Speed tier. Pokemon that can discourage or absorb Knock Off, like Virizion and Scrafty, also make good partners, as Delphox largely relies on Heavy-Duty Boots to find opportunities to switch in. Checks to Decidueye, such as Ambipom and Bombirdier, are also highly valued, as Delphox is 2HKOed by a Spell Tag-boosted Shadow Sneak. Decidueye itself, alongside Pokemon like Paldean Tauros-W and Scrafty, are also valuable for their ability to take on a myriad of other foes that can threaten Delphox offensively, such as Golurk and Zoroark. Faster revenge killers like Kilowattrel and Salazzle are also threatening, so Pokemon with priority moves like Sucker Punch Zoroark, Aqua Jet Paldean Tauros-W, and Shadow Sneak Decidueye make excellent partners. Choice Scarf users such as Duraludon, Staraptor, and Flamigo can also fulfill this role. In return, Delphox can blow holes in the opposing team, allowing these Pokemon to clean up once their checks have been weakened.

monotype.overview:
Psychic

Delphox suffers from not having the best stats overall, it's not as fast nor as powerful as one would like out of an offensive powerhouse for Psychic, being just barely slower than Iron Treads and struggling to break threats like Ting-Lu and Araquanid. However, if these threats can be dealt with for Delphox, its Speed tier is just good enough to get the jump on the rest of the relevant Steel- and Bug-types in the tier and check them with its Fire-type STAB moves before they become a problem for its teammates.

Nasty Plot (Psychic).description:
Delphox manages to find a place on Psychic teams because of its respectable base 104 Speed and access to Nasty Plot enabling it to eliminate the likes of Corviknight, Heatran, and Scizor, which otherwise prove huge problems for Psychic teams. Fire Blast and Flamethrower melt through problematic Steel- and Ice-types such as Gholdengo, Scizor, and Articuno, with Fire Blast being preferred for its ability to OHKO specially defensive Articuno at +2. After a boost, Focus Blast enables Delphox to handle the likes of Heatran, Hydreigon, and Empoleon. Finally, Delphox has a solid movepool to pull from for coverage and utility options. Encore can allow Delphox to lock the likes of Bisharp and Moltres into moves such as Sucker Punch and Roost, enabling it to set up on them. Alternatively, at +2, Grass Knot eliminates the likes of Swampert, Hippowdon, and Mamoswine, while Psyshock deals with special walls such as Blissey and Assault Vest Tornadus-T.

Delphox greatly appreciates the support of physical attackers like Iron Boulder and Gallade that help break through the Dark-types and special walls it struggles hard against like Ting-Lu, Alolan Muk, and Hisuian Goodra. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder also deals with faster threats such as Choice Scarf Kleavor and Meowscarada, whereas Assault Vest Gallade can come in on special attackers such as Darkrai and Greninja while being able to use Sacred Sword to deal with Garganacl and Blissey comfortably. Choice Specs Latios appreciates Delphox dealing with Steel-types like Scizor and Gholdengo and, in return, it can use its powerful Draco Meteor to beat Dragon-types such as Raging Bolt and Walking Wake for Delphox. Latios is also able to check Ground-types such as Gliscor and Landorus formes with its Levitate ability and Ice Beam. Slowbro provides a Water-type resistance that enables it to come in on the likes of Urshifu-R and Barraskewda, while its high Defense can help it check physical attackers such as Iron Treads and Dragonite. Slowbro also provides Thunder Wave support to slow down threats like Tornadus-T and Choice Scarf Archaludon, enabling Delphox to remove them. Hatterene helps to check opposing Dark- and Dragon-types such as Meowscarada, Roaring Moon, and Latios and greatly appreciates Delphox removing Steel-types like Corviknight for it. Metagross can set Stealth Rock to wear down would-be checks like Alolan Muk and Ogerpon-W, along with using Bullet Punch to pick off faster targets such as Flutter Mane and Weavile for Delphox. Assault Vest Hoopa-U is capable of handling threats like Choice Scarf Gholdengo, Spectrier, and Primarina with options like Knock Off and Thunderbolt.

nfe.overview: Frogadier stands out as a great offensive pivot, revenge killer, and Spikes setter of the metagame thanks to its versatile movepool and great Speed tier. These traits cement Frogadier as a centerpiece in the metagame's most dominant structures, particularly entry hazard-stacking teams with Spikes. Choice Specs Frogadier's offensive potential is matched by few, and the Choice Scarf variant is the fastest Pokemon in the metagame, making it one of the most effective revenge killers. However, it's limited by Thwackey and Water-types, though the latter can be hindered by Choice item variants' Switcheroo. Compared to other Water-types, Frogadier's bulk is lacking even if it runs Eviolite, making it more difficult to run in teams over more defensive Water-types like Quaxwell and Seadra.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Hydro Pump can be used over Surf as a stronger but less accurate option; Hydro Pump 2HKOes Eviolite Girafarig after Stealth Rock, while Surf fails to accomplish this. Gunk Shot over Ice Beam with a Naive nature is an alternative, transforming Frogadier's Grass weakness into a resistance and allowing it to potentially turn the tables on foes like Thwackey. Grass Knot is also a niche option, 2HKOing Quaxwell and Wartortle that have lost their Eviolite after minor chip damage, usually from entry hazards; it also removes Frogadier's Grassy Glide weakness.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Quaxwell and Wartortle can shrug off its moves and use Rapid Spin to clear Spikes. Wartortle, however, has a limit to how long it can keep Frogadier at bay because it lacks a good recovery move. Quaxwell is comparatively better at answering Frogadier long-term thanks to Roost giving it great longevity. Niche Water-types such as Mareanie and Seadra are also decent answers to Frogadier. However, Choice item Frogadier can hinder all these Water-types with Switcheroo.

Grass-types: Thwackey's Grassy Glide is a nightmare for Frogadier. Other Grass-types like Ivysaur and Servine can also check it. These Grass-types, however, do fear switching into Frogadier's Ice Beam.

Special Walls: Frogadier fails to deal significant damage to Pokemon like Dunsparce, Duosion, Clefairy, and Tinkatuff, but all of these can threaten it in return. However, it is worth noting that Tinkatuff can struggle to check Frogadier long-term.

Dragon-types: Hisuian Sliggoo, Choice Specs Drakloak, and First Impression Fraxure can revenge kill Frogadier.

Spikes Pivot.description:
Spikes lets Frogadier heavily pressure the opposing team while also making it immune to Thunder Wave due to Protean. Ice Beam hits Grass- and Dragon-types like Thwackey, Ivysaur, Fraxure, and Drakloak and removes its Grass weakness, allowing it to always survive Eviolite Thwackey's Grassy Glide. U-turn allows it to escape problematic matchups, such as Quaxwell and Wartortle, and generate momentum by bringing its teammates in on advantageous matchups.

Frogadier fits on offense and balance teams focused on setting entry hazards. Ghost-types are nearly mandatory teammates for Frogadier, providing spinblocking support to ensure Spikes stay up on the field in a metagame where Rapid Spin is the primary hazard removal method. Drakloak is a good consideration due to its good typing, Speed tier, and movepool. Pawniard is also a decent partner for Frogadier, punishing Defog attempts from Vullaby with Defiant—even though Defog is relatively uncommon—and using the Attack boost to potentially clean or dent the opposing team. Frogadier pairs excellently with other hazard setters like Tinkatuff, Piloswine, Gabite, and Koffing, supporting it in relentlessly pressuring the opposing team with hazards and other utility or damage-dealing moves. Tinkatuff and Koffing also help Frogadier in dealing with Grass-types, most notably Thwackey, which can easily revenge kill Frogadier with Grassy Glide. Strong Pokemon such as Thwackey, Pikachu, Raboot, Pignite, and Girafarig heavily appreciate Frogadier's Spikes support, which enables them to wallbreak or clean with ease. Thwackey assists Frogadier by dealing with threats like Quaxwell and Wartortle, while Frogadier threatens Fire-types like Raboot, Monferno, and Pignite for Thwackey. Pikachu is a good partner for similar reasons, and it appreciates Frogadier threatening Ground-types such as Piloswine and Gabite. Setup variants of Dunsparce and Duosion are also terrific teammates, being excellent wincons through their bulk, helpful abilities, and reliable recovery. Defensive teammates for Frogadier include Pokemon like Quaxwell and Ivysaur. Quaxwell provides the much-needed Rapid Spin support, ensuring Frogadier's team is unaffected by hazards while the opposing team writhes in agony due to them. Ivysaur fends off pesky Grass- and Water-types for Frogadier.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Frogadier is an extremely threatening wallbreaker that has few long-term checks. Surf and Protean-boosted Ice Beam have few Pokemon that resist both moves, and U-turn allows Frogadier to gain momentum on anything it can't blow past immediately. Spikes is another way to punish Frogadier's defensive checks like Quaxwell and Hisuian Sliggoo by wearing them down with indirect damage. Hydro Pump is worthy of strong consideration with Choice Specs, as it OHKOes Piloswine, which can otherwise OHKO Frogadier back. Switcheroo is a great disruptive tool against both defensive staples like Tinkatuff and Quaxwell and setup sweepers like Dunsparce.

While not limited to hyper offense, Choice Specs Frogadier prefers to be on faster teams that can take advantage of its early wallbreaking power. Thwackey is an excellent offensive partner to pivot to, as it can immediately threaten Quaxwell, Frogadier's most common switch-in. Late-game setup sweepers like Girafarig and Duosion can take advantage of the early-game progress that Frogadier makes against defensive cores. If running Spikes, then a Ghost-type like Drakloak is essential to block Rapid Spin. Piloswine and Tinkatuff can both serve as checks to Hisuian Sliggoo while also being capable of setting Stealth Rock to chip at Frogadier's checks. Lastly, a Grassy Glide switch-in like Girafarig or Ivysaur is important, as Thwackey is a natural revenge killer for Frogadier.

Choice Scarf.description:
With a Choice Scarf, Frogadier becomes the fastest Pokemon in the tier and can act as an excellent pivot, revenge killer, and late-game cleaner. Surf threatens Choice Scarf Monferno and Trailblaze Pignite, while Ice Beam hits Drakloak and Scale Shot-boosted Gabite. U-turn is critically important to pivot on defensive answers to Frogadier like Quaxwell and Tinkatuff. Switcheroo + Choice Scarf can cripple setup sweepers like Wartortle, Duosion, and Girafarig and a few key defensive pieces like Quaxwell and Clefairy. Spikes supports Frogadier's team and is a more valuable way to punish its checks in longer games.

Choice Scarf Frogadier can easily slot into a variety of team structures. Faster builds appreciate its revenge killing capabilities, but slower, more defensively oriented structures can still strongly take advantage of the utility Switcheroo and Spikes give and the potential late-game wincon Frogadier provides. Frogadier synergizes very well with Stealth Rock setters like Piloswine and Tinkatuff, as Frogadier can stop their common offensive checks like Monferno and Gabite. Frogadier also naturally forces a lot of switches, which helps rack up entry hazard damage. Fire-type offensive pivots like Raboot and Monferno can both maintain offensive momentum with U-turn while threatening walls like Dunsparce and Tinkatuff. They also offensively check Thwackey, which is a natural predator to Frogadier thanks to Grassy Glide. Grass-types like Thwackey and offensive Ivysaur both function as strong wallbreakers that punish Quaxwell and Clefairy for switching in and can easily be brought in with U-turn. Ivysaur also functions as a solid defensive check to opposing Thwackey. Despite sharing the same type, Quaxwell is a great teammate, as hazard removal makes Frogadier's pivot-centric playstyle less taxing, and, after a Flip Turn, Frogadier can punish the Ghost-types that Quaxwell invites in like Drakloak with Switcheroo or Ice Beam. If running Spikes, a spinblocking Ghost-type is nearly essential to keep it up.

Choice Specs.description:
With its wide coverage combined with its excellent ability Protean, Choice Specs Greninja is a scary wallbreaker that hits all of the metagame at least neutrally while outspeeding common offensive Pokemon such as Latios and Ogerpon-C. Surf is the best option to deal strong damage, as Hydro Pump can unfortunately miss and lacks PP. However, Hydro Pump could still be an option to inflict more damage, as it can OHKO defensive Excadrill and 2HKO defensive Tyranitar and Tinkaton, though Surf deals with these Pokemon with entry hazards anyway. Ice Beam is able to hit Tornadus-T, Mandibuzz, and Ogerpon-C super effectively, whereas Sludge Wave can surprise common switch-ins like Azumarill and Keldeo and gives Greninja a resistance to Fighting-type moves, such as Secret Sword, allowing it to 2HKO Keldeo. Spikes chips the opposing team in the long term and punishes switch-ins, helping Greninja and its teammates clean more easily. Greninja naturally finds some good opportunities to set up a layer of Spikes or two thanks to the switches it naturally forces. U-turn is an alternative that grants Greninja some momentum, allowing it to pivot out on Pokemon that can wall it such as Empoleon, Gastrodon, and Toxapex. Tera Water is preferred to boost the power of Greninja's Water-type move, guaranteeing an OHKO on Scizor and Cobalion with Surf and a 2HKO on Keldeo with Hydro Pump, although it shouldn't Terastallize outside of an emergency because it'll lose the boost of Protean.

Due to its severe frailty and incapacity to switch in easily, Greninja fits well on bulky offense teams that can afford slow VoltTurn support to bring it safely into battle, and they also provide some defensive backbones for Greninja to rely on. Teammates such as Cobalion, Tornadus-T, and Slowking are thus very appreciated, especially since Slowking can be useful to pressure Toxapex and Gastrodon with Future Sight. Excadrill is a helpful partner that can help Greninja by crushing common Water-resistant Pokemon like Rotom-W, allowing Greninja to spam its Water-type move. Also, Excadrill is capable of removing entry hazards, which can be a little overwhelming for Greninja. In the same way, Knock Off support helps Greninja by removing crucial items such as Assault Vest on Tornadus-T and Heavy-Duty Boots on Slowking and Volcanion. Examples of users would be Tornadus-T and Tinkaton. Since Greninja causes a lot of switches, hazard setters like Sandy Shocks and the aforementioned Cobalion are helpful. Cobalion can also check the powerful Lokix. Lastly, offensive teammates such as Calm Mind Latios and Comfey like the opposing team weakened by Greninja's powerful moves so that they can clean up, while others such as Ogerpon-C and Lokix can overwhelm their shared checks with Choice Specs Greninja, with examples of these being Toxapex, Tinkaton, and Empoleon.

Battle Bond.description:
Battle Bond turns Greninja into one of UU’s deadliest sweepers and revenge killers, as simply getting just one KO alone grants Greninja significant boosts in Special Attack and Speed to become a very difficult-to-wall sweeper that also avoids revenge killing attempts barring priority. Hydro Pump is an option over Surf for greater power, but Surf’s accuracy is much more desirable due to Greninja’s frailty and Hydro Pump's potential to be punished via a miss. Ice Beam allows Greninja to take down Hydrapple, Tornadus-T, and Ogerpon. Sludge Wave is a more specific option that helps versus Azumarill and Quaquaval, hitting them for neutral damage. Extrasensory is an option for the third moveslot to nail checks like Quaquaval and Toxapex. Protect allows Greninja to block First Impression from Lokix and scout attacks from Choice item users such as Latios and Hydrapple. It also can scout reactive Terastallizations from foes like Skeledirge and Tornadus-T. Water Shuriken allows Greninja to pick off faster targets like Sand Rush Excadrill and Choice Scarf Mienshao as well as beating out priority moves from Scizor and Mamoswine and KOing them when they are at low health. Life Orb is key in granting Greninja the power needed to break past foes such as Rotom-W, Slowking, and Assault Vest Tornadus-T despite reducing Greninja's limited longevity. Tera Water removes Greninja’s weakness to Fighting-type moves and gives it a permanently stronger Surf. Tera Stellar gives all of Greninja's moves extra power to take down Assault Vest Tornadus-T, Tera Steel Hydrapple, and Rotom-W late-game, and it gives Greninja a good shot at taking down Sand Rush Excadrill with Water Shuriken.

Greninja best fits on offensive teams and is best supported by teammates that can weaken its checks and counters so that it can have an easier time cleaning up. Latios acts as a secondary wallbreaker, which can force critical damage on foes such as Skeledirge and Toxapex as well as overwhelmed shared checks like Azumarill and Assault Vest Tornadus-T. Mamoswine and Ogerpon-C similarly can punch holes into the opposing team by taking down the likes of Skeledirge and Mandibuzz, and they can wear down checks like Hydrapple for Greninja to clean late-game. Knock Off support from Tinkaton, Tornadus-T, and Ogerpon can cripple checks such as Slowking, Rotom-W, and Assault Vest Tornadus-T to bring them into KO range of Greninja's attacks. Strong Electric-types such as Sandy Shocks and Thundurus-T are essential in punching holes through Water-types such as Keldeo and Azumarill that give Greninja trouble. Entry hazard support is key in putting foes such as Tinkaton, Rotom-W, and Toxapex into KO range, making hazard setters like the aforentioned Sandy Shocks, your own Tinkaton, and Cobalion valuable teammates. Sandy Shocks pressures Tornadus-T while Tinkaton and Cobalion can punish revenge killers like Ogerpon, Choice Scarf Zarude, and Lokix if Greninja lacks Protect. Cobalion also can bring Greninja in with Volt Switch against Hydrapple and Mandibuzz to wallbreak while crippling Tornadus-T with Thunder Wave. Excadrill can remove hazards to avoid worsening the damage Greninja takes from Life Orb, and it offensively handles Rotom-W, Toxapex, and Empoleon while also swapping into Tinkaton.

Owing to its incredible Speed and unique ability, Greninja is a frightening late-game sweeper and cleaner that is capable of snowballing through teams after a one-time boost thanks to Battle Bond. Surf can be used as an alternative to Hydro Pump, trading power for more consistency. Water Shuriken provides good priority for Greninja to revenge kill weakened yet faster threats such as Darkrai and Deoxys-S, as well as letting Greninja bypass revenge killing attempts from Kingambit's Sucker Punch. Ice Beam allows Greninja to hit Dragon-type Pokemon such as Hydrapple and Dragonite and hit Grass-type Pokemon such as Serperior and Rillaboom much harder. Sludge Wave can be used over Ice Beam as an alternative coverage move that can notably 2HKO Assault Vest Primarina after Stealth Rock damage while also having a stronger move to hit Ogerpon-W. Tera Water enhances its Water-type STAB moves and thus improves its cleaning potential. Tera Ghost can be used an alternative Tera type that allows Greninja to bypass Dragonite's Extreme Speed and Zamazenta's Body Press.

Greninja fits best on hyper offense and rain teams as an excellent sweeper and cleaner. On hyper offense teams, leads such as Glimmora, Hisuian Samurott, and Deoxys-S can get up entry hazards to help Greninja grab KOs more easily. Dragonite is an excellent teammate for Greninja, as it can deal with Grass-types such as Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom, while Greninja can eliminate physically defensive Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Garganacl for it. Gholdengo is also a good teammate, as it can help check Zamazenta, which is otherwise a dangerous threat that Greninja can let in; in return, Greninja can help check Fire- and Ground-types such as Cinderace and Landorus-T. On rain teams, Pelipper is a prime teammate, as it sets up the rain and helps Greninja get safe switch-ins with U-turn. Barraskewda is an excellent partner that helps Greninja by keeping momentum with Flip Turn and overwhelming shared checks like Primarina and Kyurem. Raging Bolt is a fantastic teammate for Greninja, as it can break bulky Water-type Pokemon such as Primarina and specially defensive Alomomola, and in return, Greninja can eliminate Ground-type Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Iron Treads for Raging Bolt. Iron Treads is a great teammate, since it can reliably clear hazards to keep Greninja healthy as well as check Raging Bolt for Greninja. Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W are also excellent partners for Greninja, threatening special walls such as Primarina and Blissey.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dark (Scarf)

Extrasensory can be used on Greninja over a different coverage option, as it allows for a clean OHKO on Sneasler; it also eases the Fighting matchup in general and can even sweep said matchup in the proper conditions.

Choice Scarf (Dark).description:
With access to colorful coverage, Greninja makes itself a great revenge killer and potential sweeper when paired with a Choice Scarf. Ice Beam allows Greninja to muscle through opposing Ground- and Flying-type Choice Scarf users such as Great Tusk and Enamorus. Low Kick lets Greninja hit targets that can easily take its other coverage such as Hisuian Goodra. Gunk Shot allows Greninja to defeat Hatterene, Iron Valiant, and the Ogerpon formes after entry hazard damage, while Switcheroo lets Greninja give its Choice Scarf away to neuter defensive Pokemon such as Articuno and Hisuian Goodra. U-turn can be used as an alternative to Switcheroo, as it allows Greninja to retain momentum on a predicted swap without having to give away its item.

Choice Band Meowscarada paired with Greninja make for a synergistic offensive core. Meowscarada is able to handle Pokemon that can shrug off Greninja's attacks such as Swampert and Gastrodon, while with the appropriate coverage, Greninja can return the favor by taking care of Pokemon that can easily switch into Meowscarada such as Ceruledge and Hatterene. Ting-Lu's ability to set a wide array of entry hazards makes Greninja's job of being a late-game sweeper easier; it is also an important defensive backbone that can switch into Pokemon such as the aforementioned Excadrill and Hatterene. Sableye is able to neuter specially defensive Pokemon that shrug off Greninja's attacks such as Corviknight and Articuno with Knock Off and Will-O-Wisp; it also stops setup sweepers such as Corviknight and Dragonite with Encore, all while providing an invaluable Fighting immunity. Both Nasty Plot Darkrai and Hydreigon are also able to wallbreak easily, which makes Greninja's ability to sweep much easier. Darkrai can also cripple defensive Pokemon such as the aforementioned Corviknight and Primarina with Hypnosis, while Hydreigon can readily deal with Archaludon and Alolan Muk. Mandibuzz has access to Defog, which Dark teams lack; it also checks physical setup sweepers such as Dragonite and Gliscor with Foul Play and provides a much-needed Ground immunity for Dark teams. Alolan Muk also stomachs Fairy-type attacks and threatens most Fairy-types for Greninja. In return, Greninja is able to take care of Landorus and Great Tusk.

Battle Bond (Water).description: This is a sample set as we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Choice Specs (Dark).description:
By virtue of its ability to outspeed most threats in the metagame as well as a colorful moveset boosted by Protean, Greninja is one of Dark's best wallbreakers and potential cleaners. Hydro Pump not only takes out non-Choice Scarf Great Tusk, Volcarona, and Mamoswine but also guarantees a 2HKO on specially defensive Corviknight after Stealth Rock damage. While Hydro Pump is preferred due to its superior power, Surf can be used due to its consistency while stilling landing an OHKO on Iron Valiant after Stealth Rock. Sludge Wave eliminates Grass- and Fairy-types such as the Ogerpon formes, Azumarill, Primarina, and Clefable. Alternatively, Grass Knot targets Ting-Lu, Swampert, and Gastrodon but fails to threaten the Fairy-types that many of Greninja's teammates dislike. Ice Beam targets Dragon- and Ground-types such as Dragonite, Garchomp, the Landorus formes, and Clodsire. Extrasensory threatens Poison- and Fighting-types like Toxapex, Okidogi, and Keldeo.

Ting-Lu provides entry hazard support in Stealth Rock and Spikes, an Electric immunity, and support against Fairy- and Dragon-types such as Hatterene, Flutter Mane, Raging Bolt, and Hisuian Goodra; in return, Greninja can take advantage of said hazards to more easily handle Corviknight, which can remove them. Mandibuzz provides a Ground immunity, removes hazards with Defog so Greninja can come in more safely, takes advantage of physical attackers such as Scizor and Ceruledge with Foul Play, and pivots Greninja in with U-turn. In return, it appreciates Greninja handling Rock-types such as Ogerpon-C after Sturdy is broken and Choice Band users like Hisuian Arcanine and Terrakion.
