Sableye provides a Ghost immunity to switch into predicted attacks from Great Tusk and Skarmory, softens physical attackers with Prankster Will-O-Wisp, blocks Rapid Spin to keep entry hazards, and dissuades setup with Encore. Choice Scarf Meowscarada pairs well with Greninja due to their shared access to Protean, allowing them to take on a multitude of threats for their teammates, with Meowscarada handling Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, Choice Specs Flutter Mane, and unboosted Dragapult. Nasty Plot Hydreigon is a solid wallbreaker, removing walls such as Hisuian Goodra and Corviknight.

Choice Specs (Water).description:
Choice Specs Greninja makes for one of Water's best choices for a wallbreaker thanks to its great array of moveset options that are all further boosted by Protean. Furthermore, its great Speed tier allows it to outspeed and take on a myriad of threats such as unboosted Iron Valiant, Latios, and Garchomp. Dark Pulse threatens Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Slowbro, Gholdengo, and Pecharunt. Ice Beam's great offensive coverage allows Greninja to threaten a myriad of threats like Dragonite, Water Absorb Clodsire, and Amoonguss. Extrasensory targets Poison- and Fighting-types like Toxapex, Okidogi, and Iron Hands. Sludge Wave targets both the Ogerpon formes and Fairy-types such as Primarina and Azumarill. Alternatively, Grass Knot can also be used to hit Ting-Lu, Swampert, and Gastrodon. However, Sludge Wave is preferred, since the Ogerpon formes could otherwise pose significant problems to Water teams.

Greninja appreciates entry hazard support from the likes of Swampert and Gastrodon to wallbreak more easily. Notably, their entry hazards break Choice Band Dragonite's Multiscale and Ogerpon-C's Sturdy so that Greninja can eliminate them immediately, and they also provide an Electric immunity to ease that matchup. Additionally, Swampert can bring Greninja in safely with Flip Turn. In return, Greninja deals with troublesome Grass-types for them like the Ogerpon formes, Hydrapple, and Sinistcha. Poison-type teammates like Toxapex and Tentacruel make for great defensive partners, as their great bulk coupled with their typing allows them to handle Fairy-types that pressure Greninja such as Iron Valiant and Flutter Mane, and they are also able to melt Toxic Spikes so Greninja can come in safely. Moreover, Toxapex walls Choice Scarf Meowscarada, which can threaten Greninja, while Tentacruel serves as great role compression, being able to stack hazards with Toxic Spikes and remove entry hazards from foes with Rapid Spin. In return, Tentacruel appreciates Greninja dealing with Poison-types that can melt its Toxic Spikes like Amoonguss, Toxapex, and Okidogi. Ogerpon-W and Greninja form a great wallbreaking duo, with Ogerpon-W handling bulky Fire- and Steel-types such as Heatran and Hisuian Goodra, while it appreciates Greninja taking on Toxapex and Amoonguss in return. Primarina eases the Dragon and Fighting matchups, as its great Calm Mind-boosted bulk lets it take on threats such as Dragapult, Roaring Moon, and Iron Hands. Rain-boosted Barraskewda provides great speed control to threaten faster threats to Greninja like Meowscarada, Sneasler, and Flutter Mane.

With its exceptional movepool and Protean to further bolster its power, Choice Specs Greninja makes for an incredible wallbreaker for Water teams, eliminating threats like Tapu Bulu, Sinistcha, and Mega Latias for the teams. Dark Pulse targets Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo and Latios. Sludge Wave provides crucial coverage, threatening Fairy- and Grass-types like Iron Valiant, Tapu Bulu, and Ogerpon-W. In addition to targeting Grass-types, Ice Beam also targets Dragon- and Flying-types like Dragonite and Zapdos. Extrasensory deals with Poison- and Fighting-types like Mega Venusaur, Toxapex, and non-Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and 2HKOes Assault Vest Iron Hands. When boosted by rain, Hydro Pump provides Greninja with an incredible nuke, allowing it to OHKO threats like Mega Gallade and Mega Scizor and 2HKO Celesteela and non-Assault Vest Alolan Muk. Alternatively, Switcheroo can also be used in the last moveslot, allowing Greninja to punish would-be switch-ins like Ferrothorn and Hisuian Goodra. Physical attackers like Mega Swampert, Choice Band Barraskewda, Urshifu-R, and Ogerpon-W can eliminate special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Alolan Muk. With their secondary Ground typing, Swampert and Mega Swampert can handle Electric-types like Iron Hands and Raging Bolt and provide Stealth Rock support and safe entry to Greninja with Flip Turn. Mega Swampert and Barraskewda also provide valuable speed control, threatening foes like Mega Lopunny, Tapu Koko, and Choice Scarf users like Enamorus, with Barraskewda even outspeeding Choice Scarf variants of Meowscarada and Sneasler. Greninja appreciates Fighting-type coverage from teammates like Urshifu-R, Ogerpon-W, and Barraskewda to break through foes like Ferrothorn and Kyurem. Ogerpon-W can also remove bulky Water-types like Swampert and Gastrodon. Pelipper boosts the power of Greninja's Hydro Pump with its rain, can also provide a safe entry to Greninja with U-turn, and removes entry hazards with Defog. Toxapex offers an important neutrality to Grass and a resistance to Fighting, which allows it to take on foes like Meowscarada and Iron Valiant. Additionally, Toxapex provides valuable team support by setting up Toxic Spikes. Empoleon helps stave off threats like Kyurem and Tapu Lele, provides Stealth Rock support and safe entry to Greninja with its slow Flip Turn, and serves as a Defogger.

Choice Specs (Dark).description: Choice Specs Greninja is one of Dark's best wallbreakers thanks to its amazing Speed and coverage, which is further boosted by Protean. Hydro Pump targets Fire-, Rock-, and Ground-types like Torkoal, Heatran, Mega Diancie, and Hippowdon. Sludge Wave threatens Grass- and Fairy-types such as Tapu Bulu, Mega Altaria, and non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant. Alternatively, Dark Pulse nails Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Gholdengo, Hisuian Zoroark, and Slowbro, while Switcheroo lets Greninja weaken special walls that it cannot threaten otherwise like Alolan Muk, Hisuian Goodra, and Blissey. Sludge Wave is the preferred option out of the three, however, due to nailing threats that many of Greninja's teammates struggle with like Ogerpon-W and non-Choice Scarf Tapu Lele. Ice Beam allows Greninja to handle Dragon- and Flying-types like Garchomp, Mega Latias, and the Landorus formes. Extrasensory targets Poison- and Fighting-types like Toxapex, Mega Venusaur, Okidogi, and Keldeo. Choice Scarf Meowscarada provides speed control and forms a Protean core with Greninja, with it outspeeding and taking on Swampert, Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, and Choice Scarf Iron Valiant. Ting-Lu sets up entry hazards to aid Greninja's wallbreaking, giving Greninja a good chance to OHKO Latias after Stealth Rock damage, and it also handles Steel-types such as Excadrill, Gholdengo, and Iron Crown. Furthermore, it provides an Electric immunity, which allows it to take on Electric-types like Tapu Koko, terrain-boosted Alolan Raichu, and Zeraora. Choice Scarf Hydreigon, Mandibuzz, and Galarian Moltres aid Greninja in the Ground matchup due to their immunities. Hydreigon also deals with Choice Scarf Gholdengo and Choice Scarf Kleavor with its STAB moves; Mandibuzz removes entry hazards with Defog and pivots Greninja in with U-turn; and Galarian Moltres can sweep late-game with Agility and Nasty Plot after Greninja wallbreaks. Alolan Muk's great special bulk helps Greninja deal with Fairy-types like Tapu Koko, Tapu Lele, and Enamorus. In return, Alolan Muk appreciates Greninja taking on Ground-types like Great Tusk and Garchomp. Greninja's wallbreaking opens the door for sweeping and cleaning opportunities from the likes of Galarian Moltres and Weavile.

balancedhackmons.overview: Ash-Greninja's high Speed and solid offensive stats make it an effective attacker. STAB-boosted Surging Strikes and Wicked Blow are excellent options for Choice Band sets, taking advantage of good Attack and Sniper to power through physical walls and force out non-resistant foes. Alternatively, Sheer Force sets can circumvent common Dark-resistant checks, like Mega Audino and Arceus-Fairy, with special attacks like Steam Eruption or super effective coverage like Noxious Torque. Ash-Greninja's main issue is that it requires prediction to do significant damage; Rocky Helmet + Fur Coat users, most of which resist Dark, can mostly stop Sniper sets from doing meaningful damage until a Knock Off lands in the right place. Sheer Force sets are strong but not mind-bogglingly so, meaning constant predictions are necessary to keep up damage. Ash-Greninja also sits in an awkward Speed tier that commonly leaves it forced out by foes like Mega Sceptile and Flutter Mane. Both sets also lack recovery, meaning that entry hazards wear into Ash-Greninja's HP, especially given the Rocky Helmet issue.
balancedhackmons.comments:
Other Options

Sniper sets can occasionally find use in Frost Breath, which gives Ash-Greninja an easier time dispatching Koraidon and other Fur Coat Dragon-types, but these are very seldom used, and Frost Breath is a terrible move to be locked into. Similarly, Tough Claws + Life Orb can be used in place of Sniper thanks to Electro Drift, which both hits Imposter users and dispatches Celesteela and Dondozo, but the damage drop on Ash-Greninja's physical attacks is less than desirable. Magic Guard is an option to retain health much more safely and get use out of Water Spout and Wave Crash, but the set still falters to Fur Coat Dragon-types. Ash-Greninja is also arguably the best rain sweeper with Tinted Lens + Water Spout, but this requires commitment of the entire team and is generally unreliable.

Checks and Counters

Rocky Helmet: Sniper sets are essentially stalled until Rocky Helmet is removed from physical walls, as most ones looking to check Ash-Greninja will resist Dark; if Ash-Greninja wants any instant damage with Surging Strikes, it costs 50% of its HP.

Faster Pokemon: Ash-Greninja's awkward Speed means that Koraidon, Zamazenta, and Miraidon can outspeed and defensively check it should they have Fur Coat. Offensive Pokemon used primarily for their Speed, like Mega Sceptile, Mega Alakazam, and Flutter Mane, can also all chase it out, but they can't switch in.

Strength Sap: While Surging Strikes and Wicked Blow ignore Strength Sap's Attack drops, Ash-Greninja struggles to KO neutral targets from full, and one of its STAB-boosted moves will usually be near-dead weight due to the opponent's Fur Coat user's typing. This limits Ash-Greninja's switch in opportunities and pressures its PP conservation. Sheer Force sets also similarly don't enjoy Bolt Strike and Combat Torque faltering against Ice Scales users.

Entry Hazards: Ash-Greninja's lack of recovery and already-high contact move usage mean entry hazards can largely keep it off the field.

Fur Coat: Fur Coat walls can dodge all 2HKOs from Sniper sets and PP stall them long-term without extensive entry hazard chip damage. Those faster than Ash-Greninja, like Zamazenta, are almost impossible to wear down. These dislike Sheer Force sets, however.

Sniper.description:
Sniper's immense damage buff makes Ash-Greninja a strong Choice Band user, with even the bulkiest physical walls like Fur Coat Arceus-Fairy taking 40% per attack. Flower Trick is largely an Imposter deterrent, but it helps out against the occasional Fur Coat Arceus-Water and Dondozo, albeit needing entry hazard support for the latter. Knock Off allows Ash-Greninja to remove Rocky Helmet for itself, which is its primary bottleneck for dealing damage in most games; removing Heavy-Duty Boots and Eviolite from foes like Mega Audino and Imposter users, respectively, also greatly helps.

Sniper Ash-Greninja is generally best on balance teams as the primary progress maker thanks to its commanding damage output. Slow pivot support is mandatory, as Ash-Greninja cannot afford to take Knock Off and severely dislikes status from moves like Mortal Spin and Glare; this usually comes in the form of RegenVest users, which also help via Stone Axe and Knock Off. A secondary physical wallbreaker can prove useful, as it's possible that Ash-Greninja can get hung up on walls chosen specifically to counter it, namely faster Dark-resistant foes like Koraidon and Zamazenta. Strong hazard removal is highly recommended due to Ash-Greninja's lack of recovery, with Mortal Spin's poison additionally helping to pick off frailer targets. Hazard support is useful, as Ash-Greninja's sheer power allows it to 2HKO most walls, as are allies that limit Strength Sap healing on these walls like Chansey and Blissey.

nfe.overview: In a tier lacking entry hazard removal options, Fletchinder shines as the premier Defogger, preventing teams from being weak to hazards. Fletchinder also provides a very rare Ground immunity, preventing one of the biggest threats of the tier in Choice Band Piloswine from spamming Ground-type moves. Fletchinder's great Speed and defensive typing allow it to check common physical threats such as Raboot and Thwackey and punish them with Flame Body. Fletchinder is best used on balance teams that want a good way of dealing with hazard stack teams and don't want to be blocked from removing hazards by Ghost-types. However, Fletchinder relies on Heavy-Duty Boots in order to remove Stealth Rock; thus, it needs teammates such as Koffing and Dunsparce able to come on Knock Off for it.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Eviolite can be used over Heavy-Duty Boots to provide more bulk to Fletchinder. It is an especially good option if your team has another way of removing entry hazards such as Quaxwell and Wartortle or Hattrem to deter foes from setting them up, as Fletchinder will otherwise suffer heavy damage from Stealth Rock every time it comes on the field. Since Fletchinder comes in on several Knock Off users, Thief can be used to steal a foe's Eviolite, letting it serve as a Knock Off absorber. A bulkier EV spread of 252 HP / 232 Def / 24 Spe with a Impish nature can be used to help Fletchinder check powerful wallbreakers such as Pignite and Piloswine while outspeeding Adamant Pignite. A spread of 252 HP / 136 Def / 120 Spe with a Jolly nature lets Fletchinder outspeed Fraxure to burn it with Will-O-Wisp while notably allowing it to tank Icicle Crash from Choice Band Piloswine.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Seadra, Quaxwell, and Wartortle threaten Fletchinder with Surf while being able to take the momentum with Flip Turn or get a setup opportunity with Shell Smash in Wartortle's case.

Rock-types: Fletchinder has no way of hitting Rock-types such as Glimmet and Naclstack, meaning it won't be able to effectively keep entry hazards off the field as they can both come in and set them up again.

Electric-types: Fletchinder usually does not run a Fire-type move, so Electric-types such as Pikachu, Eelektrik, and Chinchou come freely on it and threaten it with Electric-type moves—notably Volt Switch, which will give the momentum to the opponent.

Special Attackers: Due to Fletchinder usually using utility moves, special attackers such as Drakloak, Hisuian Sliggoo, and Frogadier can come in on it without risk of fainting and threaten it. Furthermore, since it's pretty passive, Fletchinder gives free opportunities to set up for special attackers such as Duosion, Girafarig, and Wartortle.

Utility.description:
Fletchinder's most precious tool is Defog, a very rare move in the tier. With its good Speed and defensive typing, Fletchinder is the best Defogger of the tier, as it has a good matchup against entry hazards setters like Quilladin and Piloswine while checking a lot of physical attackers such as Pignite, the aforementioned Piloswine, Scraggy, Thwackey, Raboot, and Monferno. Brave Bird hits Fighting- and Grass-types, while Roost gives Fletchinder more longevity. U-turn can be used to pivot on Pokemon that come in for free on Fletchinder such as Hisuian Sliggoo and Seadra, thus giving you the momentum. Taunt is an option to help deal with defensive walls such as Tinkatuff and Dunsparce. Will-O-Wisp hinders physical attackers such as Krokorok and Piloswine. With its ability Flame Body, Fletchinder punishes Pokemon that spam U-turn such as the aforementioned Thwackey and Raboot. The given EV spread with a Jolly nature takes advantage of Fletchinder's good Speed, letting it outspeed offensive threats such as Monferno and Servine while being bulky enough to check a plethora of Pokemon.

Fletchinder fits best on balance teams looking for a good way to deal with entry hazards. Seadra is the most common defensive teammate to Fletchinder, as Fletchinder's hazard removal lets your team drop Quaxwell for Seadra, which is bulkier, faster, and more powerful. Seadra helps deal with Pokemon that have access to Knock Off such as Pignite and Monferno, so Fletchinder can keep its much-needed Heavy-Duty Boots. Furthermore, Seadra's Ice resistance helps prevent Choice Band Piloswine from spamming Icicle Crash, while Fletchinder's Ground immunity stops it from spamming Earthquake. These two Pokemon also punish physical attackers thanks to Poison Point and Flame Body, and they can also form a solid VoltTurn defensive core with Flip Turn and U-turn. Hisuian Sliggoo is an excellent offensive partner to Fletchinder, as it is able to check Water-, Rock-, and Electric-types, which all take advantage of Fletchinder's passivity, while checking specially offensive Pokemon that threaten Fletchinder like Drakloak and Frogadier. However, other special walls such as Tinkatuff and Dunsparce are also good options, as they appreciate Fletchinder's ability to check common physical threats such as Pignite and Piloswine, while Fletchinder appreciates their ability to check common special threats such as Girafarig, Drakloak, and Frogadier. Offensive Pokemon that can't afford to hold Heavy-Duty Boots such as Choice Specs Drakloak, Monferno, and Piloswine appreciate Fletchinder's ability to remove hazards. Koffing can serve as a Knock Off absorber for Fletchinder, allowing it to keep its Heavy-Duty Boots, and Fletchinder can check Ground-types that usually take advantage of Koffing such as Krokorok and Piloswine. Glimmet being able to come in on Fletchinder and set hazards up can quickly become overwhelming for your team, so Pokemon that take advantage of it like Hisuian Sliggoo, Girafarig, and Krokorok pair well with Fletchinder. Wallbreakers like Gabite, Choice Specs Girafarig, and Choice Band Piloswine that have a hard time coming on the field appreciate Fletchinder's ability to pivot with U-turn.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance, high Speed, and the Fire / Flying typing allow Fletchinder to serve as a wallbreaker or late-game cleaner that is only outsped by a few Pokemon, including Drakloak, Frogadier, and Girafarig. Brave Bird and Flare Blitz are the two most prominent STAB moves that can hit many Pokémon in the metagame super effectively, including the Grass-types Ivysaur, Thwackey, Quilladin, and Servine, the Fighting-types Monferno, Pignite, and Scraggy, and even the ever-present Tinkatuff. Because these two moves have recoil damage, Roost is an excellent option for longevity. Even though Roost increases Fletchinder's longevity, it is important to note that Fletchinder is quite frail because it runs Heavy-Duty Boots over Eviolite due to its significant weakness to Stealth Rock. Taunt is another excellent option to break through fatter teams, stopping recovery options from the likes of Quaxwell and Dusclops, and completely shut down Tinkatuff.

Due to its frailty and dependence on keeping Heavy-Duty Boots, Fletchinder pairs well with a defensive backbone capable of switching into Knock Off, which includes Pokemon like Tinkatuff, Krokorok, and Koffing. Fletchinder also appreciates teammates like Tinkatuff, Monferno, and Thwackey, among others, that can remove Eviolite from opposing Pokemon, paving the way for a Fletchinder sweep. In the case Heavy-Duty Boots are removed from Fletchinder, Pokemon capable of removing Stealth Rock like Quaxwell or deterring them from being set up like Hattrem are highly appreciated. As stated before, Drakloak, Frogadier, and Girafarig outspeed Fletchinder in normal conditions, and Dunsparce, Quaxwell, and Tinkatuff are capable of switching into them. Water-types like Quaxwell and Seadra and Rock-types like Glimmet and Naclstack are the most prominent Fletchinder checks, which means that Grass-types, including Thwackey, Ivysaur, and Servine, that can switch into them and pressure them pair well with Fletchinder. Hisuian Sliggoo also pairs well with Fletchinder, as it pressures both Water- and Rock-types while checking faster special attackers in Drakloak, Frogadier, and Girafarig. However, Fletchinder can pressure these Water-types if they have been previously crippled by other wallbreakers like Pignite, Krokorok, Gabite, and Monferno. Dunsparce also annoyingly checks Fletchinder due to its bulk and ability to spread paralysis with Body Slam. Fighting-types that can threaten Dunsparce and can spam Knock Off such as Scraggy, Pignite, and Monferno are great parterns as a result.

Defog.description:
Talonflame is an interesting user of Defog, owing to its typing and effectiveness at spreading burn via Flame Body and Will-O-Wisp. As a Defog user, Talonflame is able to dissuade Gholdengo from switching in with the threat of its Fire-type STAB moves and can consistently threaten to burn common entry hazard setters and removers like Landorus-T, Ting-Lu, Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Corviknight to control hazard setting and removal in the long term. Overheat has good odds to 2HKO even bulky Gholdengo, with non-Choice Scarf sets getting outsped and threatened with a KO from Talonflame the next turn; meanwhile, Flamethrower is a more accurate and higher PP alternative that still 2HKOes offensive Gholdengo. Will-O-Wisp lets Talonflame reliably enfeeble foes with burn, especially physical attackers like Kingambit, Dragonite, Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads. 32 Speed EVs let Talonflame outspeed positive base 85 Speed Pokemon like Rillaboom and Hisuian Samurott. Tera Dragon lets Talonflame stave off Ogerpon-W lacking Play Rough in a pinch while remaining neutral against U-turn, and it improves Talonflame's matchup against Hisuian Samurott.

Talonflame finds its flock among stall teams as a Defogger able to threaten Gholdengo and spread burn. Few situations are quite as nightmarish for a Great Tusk or Iron Treads as being burned while attempting to keep entry hazards from the tenacious Gliscor off the field; as such, Gliscor finds Talonflame to be a useful associate. In return, Gliscor staves off Fire-types and certain special attackers such as Iron Moth, Raging Bolt, and Galarian Slowking that would otherwise find free entry against Talonflame; it also pressures Garganacl with Knock Off or Earthquake. Toxapex is an appreciated colleague that holds off Fire-types such as Ceruledge and Moltres, Water-types like Primarina and Ogerpon-W, and Clefable with Knock Off. It also helps switch around Garganacl's Salt Cure. Amoonguss is another teammate that checks the aforementioned Water-types, being an especially consistent check to the threatening Ogerpon-W. Dondozo is a stall mainstay that answers physical attackers like Swords Dance Gliscor, Ceruledge, and Tera Fire Pokemon like Dragonite and Kingambit that can ignore Talonflame's burn. Another stall staple, Blissey, answers special attackers that scare Talonflame out, like Kyurem, Hatterene, Primarina, Calm Mind Clefable, and Walking Wake. Talonflame works well with a secondary Defogger, such as Corviknight or Galarian Weezing. Corviknight is less afraid of taking Knock Off from Great Tusk or Iron Treads, with Talonflame improving the team's matchup against Gholdengo, while Galarian Weezing is a Defogger similarly effective against Gholdengo that appreciates Talonflame holding off Pokemon like Kingambit and Dragonite. Stacking a second hazard remover along with Talonflame to threaten Gholdengo enables the rest of the team to drop Heavy-Duty Boots entirely in favor of items like Leftovers or Rocky Helmet to maximize their longevity and utility.

Defog (Fire).description:
Talonflame, due to its Ground immunity and access to entry hazard removal with Defog, has a great spot on Fire teams. Gale Wings makes Brave Bird a priority move at full HP, which allows Talonflame to take out threats like Ogerpon-W, Choice Scarf Great Tusk, and Keldeo. Will-O-Wisp weakens physical threats like Mamoswine, Garchomp, Iron Treads, and Excadrill; U-turn can be run over Will-O-Wisp to let Talonflame hit Meowscarada and Hoopa-U while also allowing it to pivot into one of its teammates. But doing so will remove the opportunity to weaken the aforementioned physical threats with a burn, which can be a problem for the team. Heavy-Duty Boots is the go-to item that lets Talonflame avoid taking damage from Stealth Rock. The given EV spread lets Talonflame outspeed and OHKO Ogerpon-W with Brave Bird.

All of Talonflame's teammates appreciate the removal of hazards and Ground immunity that Talonflame provides. Swords Dance Ogerpon-H is an amazing teammate for Talonflame, taking out pesky Water- and Rock-types like Primarina, Quagsire, and Rhyperior at +2 with Horn Leech. Swords Dance Ceruledge is a great setup sweeper that can deal with pesky Psychic- and Ghost-types like Iron Boulder and Flutter Mane with Shadow Sneak after a boost. Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine is a great wallbreaker for Talonflame, being able to take out Flying-types like Gyarados, Dragonite, and Skarmory. Volcanion provides a Water immunity for Talonflame while checking Azumarill with Sludge Wave. Heatran tanks special hits from the likes of Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Power Gem while OHKOing it back with Heavy Slam. Heatran also traps walls like Toxapex with Magma Storm and stops them from recovering with Taunt.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Talonflame is most common as the main supportive option on teams that aim to overwhelm the opponent and win quickly, such as hyper offense, where priority speed control in the form of Tailwind is especially valuable. Its most common partner by far is Choice Specs Gholdengo, which, when paired with Covert Cloak Talonflame, prevents Fake Out and makes it difficult to stop a turn one Tailwind + Tera Steel Make it Rain. This duo is also particularly strong with Dondozo and Commander Tatsugiri, softening up teams for Dondozo to clean up in the endgame.
  • Talonflame doesn't particularly need any partners to function well; it instead serves to complement its teammates.
  • Talonflame's main competition is Whimsicott, which doesn't have to worry about about losing access to priority moves thanks to Prankster, as well as having better enabling tools such as Sunny Day for Hisuian Typhlosion and Delphox and Beat Up for Annihilape. Talonflame has more general utility tools with Will-O-Wisp and non-Prankster Taunt, is faster, and can OHKO it first with priority Brave Bird, but it generally isn't as support-oriented as Whimsicott.

Strategy Comments

  • Talonflame's biggest strength is immediate turn one pressure. Take advantage of that. You generally always want to be leading Talonflame and setting up Tailwind; going for an attack is risky before Tailwind is up, as you lose Gale Wings and a significant chunk of Talonflame's health. Once Tailwind is up, sacrificing it for a free switch is usually the play. If you have the opportunity for a safe switch, however, take it, as Talonflame's coverage and Speed makes it a great late-game cleaner.
  • The only real reason to use Talonflame over Whimsicott is coverage and damage, functioning almost like a glass cannon with access to priority Tailwind. Flying- and Fire-type coverage is excellent into the metagame, and its Speed means it's always a credible threat. Go for damage whenever possible after setting up Tailwind.
  • The best way to handle Talonflame is to nullify either its damage or priority speed control. Pokemon with Intimidate severely hamper Talonflame's offensive pressure, and even Pokemon like Electabuzz and Primarina that can eat one of its attacks and return back for strong damage are difficult matchups. Alternatively, nullifying its priority or Speed advantage also works well. Priority attacks like Fake Out and Extreme Speed break Gale Wings, with the former often completely preventing Tailwind from being set up on non-Covert Cloak sets. Priority blocking abilities like both Indeedee's Psychic Surge are difficult but not common. Incineroar is likely the biggest pain spot for Talonflame teams, as it walls Gholdengo, can break Gale Wings with Fake Out, and has Intimidate to cripple Talonflame offensively. If you're playing Talonflame, you have to be careful when leading it into Incineroar and Sneasler teams, and usually, it's best to completely leave it behind in matchups against balance teams.

Offensive Tailwind Support.description:
• Talonflame takes over for Tornadus as the premier offensive Tailwind support, dealing huge damage with its primary STAB attacks that give it immediate offensive pressure as well as having a host of supportive options with Gale Wings Tailwind.
  • Covert Cloak is the most popular item on Talonflame, preventing opposing Fake Outs from slowing down a offensive lead. Talonflame's high Speed means it's usually not too bothered by Gale Wings breaking. Life Orb and Sharp Beak are two sides of the same coin; they are offensive items to pick up OHKOes on foes that Covert Cloak sets don't at the cost of being vulnerable to Fake Out. Life Orb allows for cleaner OHKOes such as OHKOing Rillaboom regardless of its defensive investment as well as boosting Flare Blitz, while Sharp Beak is an option if you prefer not taking recoil at the cost of damage output, such as only having a 60% chance to OHKO the previously mentioned Rillaboom.
  • The choice of Tera type is mostly dependent on personal preference. Tera Ghost prevents Fake Out, Extreme Speed, and other priority moves from breaking Gale Wings. Tera Flying is used for damage, allowing Sharp Beak and Life Orb sets to cleanly OHKO Amoonguss, as well as some frail neutral types such as Delphox and Hisuian Typhlosion, with Brave Bird. Tera Grass gives a resistance to Water, Electric, and an important immunity to powder attacks; this is used to bypass opposing Rage Powders and Taunt an opposing Trick Room user on turn one.
  • Jolly is usually preferred for outspeeding Adamant Dragapult, Whimsicott, and Sneasler, but Adamant is also viable to maximize damage, allowing it to OHKO Amoonguss without Terastallization on Life Orb sets.
  • The last two moveslots are open to player preference and usually mix and matched, the usual 2 are Flare Blitz and Taunt, giving it an additional STAB move and extra utility, respectively, but Will-O-Wisp and Protect are also viable; the former cripples physical threats like Dondozo, and the latter is generally useful.

Magic Guard.description: Despite its low Attack stat, Talonflame carves out a niche as a usable wallbreaker and potent stallbreaker. Roost keeps Talonflame healthy throughout the course of a game, allowing it to reliably act as an offensive check to threats like Ogerpon-H, Great Tusk, and Iron Moth. Bulk Up gives revenge killers like Dragonite and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon a harder time at attempting to revenge kill Talonflame while threatening to let it snowball out of control. Flare Blitz smacks Steel-types like Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Iron Treads, while Swords Dance provides greater damage potential, allowing Talonflame to threaten a 2HKO on Pecharunt and OHKO Dragonite from full HP. Taunt allows Talonflame to reliably act as a stallbreaker, preventing would-be checks like Well-Baked Body Corviknight, Unaware Scream Tail, and Deoxys-D from checking it, while Will-O-Wisp provides more utility, burning switch-ins like Garganacl, Primordial Sea Zapdos, and Archaludon. Talonflame requires support from Pokemon that can wear the opposing team down, so entry hazard setters like Great Tusk, Skarmory, and Empoleon are wonderful teammates for it. Talonflame's unimpressive bulk necessitates good teammates that can switch into revenge killers like Azelf, Barraskewda, and Hisuian Electrode; hence, the aforementioned hazard setters, Iron Moth, and Blissey all work as excellent partners for it. Talonflame also notably requires teammates such as RegenVest Swampert and Meloetta that can deal with Fire-immune Electric- and Steel-types like Well-Baked Body Gholdengo, Primordial Sea Zapdos, and Archaludon.

monotype.overview:
Bug

Vivillon has one powerful trick, Sleep Powder with its accuracy boosted thanks to Compound Eyes, which nearly guarantees that it will be leading the game off and inflicting sleep for strong early momentum. However, as direct competition to Bug's other special attacking options, even ignoring Volcarona, Vivillon stands out as especially outclassed. Frosmoth with the right support can freeze Flying, Ground, and Dragon teams into a fine mist, while Choice Specs Yanmega helps out greatly in breaking Poison teams. Even then, physically attacking Bug-types like Lokix are often better anyway, able when paired together to overwhelm checks like Toxapex and Skarmory.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Bug

Quiver Dance serves as an alternative option over Tailwind, as Vivillon can make use of the free turns granted by Sleep Powder or attempts to mitigate it through the likes of Protect from Gliscor to start setting up and break through a team, notably allowing Vivillon to clean through Fighting teams if it is able to get going. However, such sets are stuck realistically with only Flying-type attacks for reliable offensive pressure, rendering them useless against status absorbers like Gholdengo and incapable of threatening Steel- and Electric-types long term.

Status Utility (Bug).description:
Focus Sash Vivillon finds a singular niche on Bug teams due to its wide variety of status moves and Compound Eyes allowing it to often lead off and immediately make progress. Hurricane deals with annoying Fighting- and Bug-types such as Iron Valiant and Lokix as long as its Focus Sash is still intact. Sleep Powder shuts down opposing leads such as Araquanid and Hippowdon, letting Vivillon then use Stun Spore to threaten switch-ins like Kleavor and Tornadus-T. Finally, Tailwind offers additional speed control as Vivillon goes down to enable teammates such as Scizor, which can use Dual Wingbeat to remove the Ogerpon formes and Urshifu-R.

Setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Scizor and Quiver Dance Volcarona greatly appreciate the free turns granted by Vivillon's Sleep Powder, giving them a much easier time to set up. Both can also check threats for Vivillon should it be used outside of the lead slot, with Scizor handling Rock- and Fairy-types like Kleavor, Hatterene, and Flutter Mane and Volcarona melting through Steel-types like Corviknight and Gholdengo. Choice Scarf Kleavor provides Stealth Rock support through Stone Axe along with eliminating Fire-types like Volcarona and Iron Moth, and it greatly appreciates the Stun Spore and Tailwind support to outspeed opposing Choice Scarf users like Iron Boulder and Greninja. Forretress can remove Stealth Rock with Rapid Spin to preserve Vivillon's Focus Sash while also bringing it in safely with Volt Switch should its talents be needed later in a game. Furthermore, when equipped with Rocky ​Helmet, Forretress can deal with threats attempting to counterlead Vivillon such as non-Punching Glove Urshifu-R and Triple Axel Meowscarada. Araquanid provides Sticky Web, reducing the need for Tailwind in the first place and allowing Vivillon to get the jump on the likes of Choice Band Dragapult and non-Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. Lokix utilizes First Impression to easily remove Meowscarada and Iron Boulder while also using Knock Off to check Gholdengo.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Vivillon works well on offensive teams, acting as a fast sleep support Pokemon while still hitting hard into defensive pieces like Rillaboom and Amoonguss. Sleep Powder can shut down slower foes such as Annihilape and Primarina, keeping the momentum for offensive threats like Garchomp. Vivillon also works well on balance, specifically with Porygon2, redirecting or shutting down attacks for Porygon2 while also sitting next to Ursaluna as it uses Earthquake.

  • Thanks to Vivillon's Flying typing, it can be used next to Garchomp and its easily spammable Earthquake amazingly. Earthquake also forces threats such as Archaludon to go for Tera Grass, which then opens up Vivillon to hit hard with Hurricane. Vivillon can also put foes to sleep for Garchomp, which sets it apart from other Flying-types. Gholdengo is another solid partner for Vivillon, benefiting from redirection.

  • Vivillon loses to Maushold and Annihilape as a duo, as Annihilape threatens Vivillon after it Terastallizes, and Maushold can shut down Vivillon by outspeeding it and using Taunt. It can also struggle with Maushold and Archaludon as a duo, with Maushold this time threatening Population Bomb as well as Taunt while Archaludon can take down Vivillon with Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, and Draco Meteor. Garchomp and Gholdengo can patch up these holes; Garchomp's Earthquake hits hard into all of the aforementioned foes, while Gholdengo can do the same with Shadow Ball and Make It Rain. Garchomp also has the added benefit of Rough Skin, damaging Maushold for attacking.

Strategy Comments

  • Vivillon's main role is to put things to sleep with high Speed, hit decently hard, and redirect attacks to protect allies. Vivillon really shines when next to Garchomp, putting slower foes likes Pelipper to sleep and redirecting attacks such as Moonblast from Primarina and Draco Meteor from Hydreigon.

  • Vivillon can be used best in early-game situations and works really well in the lead or even in the back next to Gholdengo, spamming Sleep Powder while Gholdengo uses Make It Rain or using Rage Powder to allow Gholdengo to set up and sweep. Vivillon can also be used next to Primarina, with Hyper Voice and Sleep Powder forcing Tera Grass from foes such as Incineroar, which can then allow Vivillon to hit hard with Hurricane.

  • Vivillon can struggle with Pokemon like Incineroar chipping it down and breaking Focus Sash, and smart pivoting into Grass-types or Safety Goggles Pokemon can make it hard for Vivillon to do its job. For this, Incineroar can work to remove Safety Goggles with Knock Off and KO Grass-types with Flare Blitz. Tera Ghost is also great at preserving Focus Sash, while Protect and good pivoting of your own can help as well.

Support.description:
• Vivillon is a very good support Pokemon, providing redirection and fast sleep while dealing good damage. Compound Eyes helps make Vivillon more consistent as a support Pokemon, making Hurricane and Sleep Powder more accurate.

  • Hurricane does good damage to foes such as Amoonguss and Rillaboom as well as hitting common Tera Grass users like Archaludon, which are forced to Terastallize due to Sleep Powder. Rage Powder, even with Vivillon's low bulk, is able to soak up one or two attacks for allies such as Garchomp.

  • Focus Sash compensates for Vivillon's rather poor defensive stats, granting more turns for it to support its team, specifically allowing for more sleep opportunities.

  • Tera Ghost denies Fake Out from foes like Rillaboom and Incineroar and Extreme Speed from Dragonite, which helps with Vivillon's survivability, as it stops Focus Sash from being broken.

Choice Scarf.description:
Florges is one of PU's best Choice Scarf users thanks to its high Special Attack stat, strong and spammable STAB move, Trick, and decent bulk for a revenge killer. Synthesis allows Florges to recover health against Pokemon it forces out such as Bombirdier and Tatsugiri; however, it is risky if Florges has not given away its Choice Scarf with Trick. Calm Mind makes Florges become a setup sweeper after using Trick to give away its Choice Scarf. Psychic Noise serves as coverage for Poison-types like Salazzle and also prevents foes from healing, but the higher Base Power of Psychic may be preferred for OHKOing Salazzle and almost always 2HKOing Amoonguss. Finally, Wish gives Florges utility by allowing it to help heal its teammates' HP. Tera Fairy boosts Moonblast to incredible amounts of power, allowing Florges to always 2HKO offensive Rhydon and OHKO threats like Skuntank and Toxicroak with some chip damage. Florges can either opt for an EV spread of 4 Def / 252 SpA / 252 Spe or use a more bulky EV spread of 252 HP / 24 Def / 232 Spe, which allows it to have enough Speed to outpace Jolteon and Adamant Bombirdier as well as Skuntank after Trick, and it can pass bigger Wishes to its teammates. Finally, Tera Poison is a purely defensive Tera type that allows Florges to take attacks from Pokemon like Salazzle and Hisuian Decidueye.

Choice Scarf Florges finds itself mostly on offense and balance teams looking for a reliable form of speed control that can disrupt balance teams thanks to Trick. Florges's unique trait of good bulk while still retaining great offensive pressure makes it a more specialized Choice Scarf user than other choices such as Hoopa and Flamigo. Florges can't reliably break though Steel- and Poison-types such as Alolan Sandslash and Galarian Slowbro, so Pokemon that can take these threats on like Zoroark, Mudsdale, and Paldean Tauros-F all make good partners. Florges's ability to revenge kill Pokemon like Ambipom and Zoroark allows slower wallbreakers that struggle with these faster threats such as Golurk, Rotom-Heat, and Delphox to be more potent attackers. Since it can't run Heavy-Duty Boots and will likely switch in often, Florges appreciates entry hazard control from Pokemon like Coalossal and Tatsugiri so it can become more threatening. In turn, Florges threatens their checks such as Heracross and Bombirdier.

Calm Mind.description:
Florges is one of PU's best bulky setup sweepers thanks to its great defensive typing, wide range of utility options, reliable recovery, and immunity to Milotic's Dragon Tail. Psychic Noise is coverage for Poison-types like Salazzle and Vileplume, and it also prevents specially defensive walls like Milotic and Porygon2 from attempting to stall out Florges with their recovery. Wish allows Florges to provide support for its team and gives it extra PP for recovery to pair with Synthesis; it is primarily used as a wall rather than a primary win condition, although it comes at the cost of not having coverage. Covert Cloak lets Florges freely set up on the likes of Milotic and Vileplume, and it also has utility in more niche matchups such as versus Naclstack. Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers are other options to give Florges more longevity, which may be useful in longer games. The given EV spread allows Florges to obtain as much physical bulk as possible while also outspeeding Adamant Golurk as well as opposing walls such as Wo-Chien and Milotic. Tera Poison is ideal for a strong defensive typing, allowing Florges to set up against Pokemon like Galarian Slowbro and Amoonguss without fear of being poisoned. Tera Water is another generally solid defensive typing that eliminates all of Florges's weaknesses and grants it a resistance to strong attacks like Bruxish's Wave Crash and Paldean Tauros-F's Flare Blitz, though it leaves Florges vulnerable to poison as well as other attacks from foes like Pawmot.

Florges is most commonly used on bulky balance teams looking for a secondary wincon that, when teamed with a primary wincon like Arcanine and Decidueye, can also function as a special wall or a Wish passer if need be. Even with investment, Florges's physical bulk is not good enough to set up against attackers like Rhydon and Paldean Tauros-F, so physical walls like Amoonguss and Palossand make excellent partners. Likewise, in order for Florges to attempt a sweep, Fire- and Steel-types like Delphox and Alolan Sandslash must be chipped or KOed, which can be achieved by Pokemon like Golurk, Bruxish, and Rotom-Heat. In return, Florges can soft check and threaten out their offensive checks like Zoroark and Tatsugiri. Florges's ability to soft check and threaten Dark- and Fighting-types like Grimmsnarl, Zoroark, Scrafty, and Hariyama makes the likes of Galarian Slowbro, Delphox, and one's own Scrafty amazing partners. In return, these three can defensively or offensively check some of Florges's own checks like an opposing Galarian Slowbro and Coalossal. If Florges opts for Wish, the ability to pass Wish is extremely beneficial to offensive partners like Heracross and Paldean Tauros-F, which chip away at opposing walls like Mudsdale that can phaze out Florges, allowing Florges to sweep; Wish is also beneficial for partner walls lacking reliable recovery like Rhydon and Alolan Sandslash.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Florges is a terrifying wallbreaker, being able to utilize its solid bulk, high Special Attack, and limited switch-ins to Moonblast to carve out a solid niche in PU. Trick can cripple special walls such as Milotic and Alolan Sandslash, allowing Florges and its teammates to break through them more easily. Psychic Noise can be used to beat Poison-types such as Amoonguss and Salazzle while also making sure special walls such as Milotic and opposing Florges cannot heal off its damage. Synthesis is used to make sure Florges can keep itself healthy over a match for bulkier teams while letting it help check Pokemon such as Passimian and Tatsugiri, allowing it to continue being a nuisance post-Trick. Draining Kiss lets Florges simultaneously heal and dish out damage and also receives a slight power boost from Tera Fairy, though it does cut into Florges's longevity. Tera Fairy can be used to boost Florges's Moonblast to astonishing power, allowing it to 2HKO both Rotom-Heat and specially defensive Milotic. Florges by large prefers a Modest nature, as the extra damage output can allow it to 3HKO Snorlax and 2HKO Lanturn after Stealth Rock, but a Timid nature can be utilized to outspeed Hoopa, Hisuian Braviary, and Adamant Skuntank.

Florges fits best on bulky offense and balance teams, which appreciate its wallbreaking power and ability to soft check Pokemon such as Tatsugiri and Jolteon. Pokemon such as Lanturn and Bruxish that can take on foes such as Delphox and Alolan Sandslash, which can otherwise take hits from Florges, are great partners for it. Conversely, Pokemon such as Alolan Sandslash and Hisuian Qwilfish that heavily struggle with Fire- and Steel-types love Florges's ability to heavily chip down these Pokemon, which can make them a lot more threatening. Pivot Pokemon such as Rotom-Heat, Zoroark, and Bruxish are great for Florges, as they can help it get in and out of battle easily while also luring in Pokemon such as Wo-Chien and Hisuian Qwilfish that Florges can start spamming Moonblast against. A majority of Florges's checks are Stealth Rock-weak, so Knock Off users such as Ambipom and Alolan Sandslash can help remove their items for it. Paralysis users such as Grimmsnarl and Porygon2 are great partners for Florges, as they can slow down faster foes such as Salazzle and Paldean Tauros-F that would usually be able to outspeed it, while in return, Florges can threaten out common paralysis absorbers such as Milotic, Pawmot, and Mudsdale that they might struggle with.

Wish.description:
Florges is PU's best Wish passer thanks to its incredible special bulk, high Special Attack even without investment, and great defensive typing, allowing it to take on threats such as Tatsugiri, Zoroark, and Scrafty. Synthesis gives Florges reliable recovery, although Protect synergizes well with Wish and allows Florges to scout out attacks from Choice-locked Pokemon such as Bruxish. Psychic Noise lets Florges disrupt walls such as Milotic and Snorlax by preventing them from recovering while also being a decent coverage option against Poison-types such as Salazzle and Toxtricity. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Florges to ignore entry hazards, although Leftovers is an option to give small amounts of recovery that can be helpful in tandem with Protect. The given EV spread allows Florges to outspeed Wo-Chien and Milotic while investing as much into Defense as possible to take advantage of its valuable resistances to Fighting and Dark. Tera Poison grants Florges a resistance to Grass- and Poison-type attacks from Pokemon like Rotom-Mow, Salazzle, and Skuntank.

Florges finds itself on bulky balance teams that like its ability to Wish pass while also being a great mixed wall. Walls lacking recovery like Mudsdale and Orthworm appreciate Florges's ability to keep them healthy throughout the game. Florges can struggle with Poison- and Steel-type Pokemon like Galarian Slowbro, Skuntank, and Alolan Sandslash, which it can't Wish pass safely against, so Pokemon that can check these threats and also benefit from Florges's Wish passing capabilities such as Golurk, Mudsdale, and Salazzle make good partners. Even though it resists Fighting-type attacks, Florges still appreciates other Fighting-resistant teammates like Galarian Slowbro and Cramorant to not be its team's sole switch-in to them. The latter also takes advantage of setup sweepers Florges can't handle on its own, like Salazzle.

Calm Mind.description: You can run Wish + Protect on the Calm Mind set to support teammates, but Florges's main niche over Sylveon comes from its access to Synthesis allowing for extra coverage to be run. 136 Speed EVs allows Florges to outpace Modest Sylveon.

monotype.overview:
=========

Outmatched by Deoxys-S, Meowstic-M is an inferior screens setter option for Psychic. Due to its lack of utility options like Knock Off, Taunt, Stealth Rock, and Spikes, Meowstic provides little outside of dual screens and Thunder Wave. However, with its ability Prankster, Meowstic can reliably set up dual screens in front of faster targets and users of priority moves, namely setting up Reflect before Ceruledge can use Shadow Sneak, unlike Deoxys-S.

Dual Screens Setter.description:
Boasting useful utility in dual screens and a complementary ability in Prankster, Meowstic-M is a niche dual screens setter for Psychic teams. Light Screen and Reflect mitigate damage for teammates attempting to set up, prolonging survivability and amplifying offensive capability. Charm helps deal with physical attackers trying to set up on Meowstic-M such as Dragonite and Ceruledge. Thunder Wave dissuades Pokemon like Volcarona and Dragonite from using Meowstic-M as setup fodder, granting an easier time revenge killing them for teammates. Alternatively, Yawn may be used to encourage the opponent to swap their Pokemon out, creating safe opportunities to set up dual screens. 104 Speed EVs grant Meowstic-M the ability to outpace Ceruledge, allowing it to set up Reflect before Ceruledge can use Shadow Sneak.

Hatterene dissuades entry hazard setters like Ting-Lu, Clodsire, and Skarmory from taking advantage of Meowstic-M and threatens troublesome Dark-types such as Roaring Moon, Hydreigon, and Hisuian Samurott. Hatterene appreciates dual screens support, which allows it to repeatedly set up Calm Mind without fearing hits such as Poison Jab from Clodsire and Heavy Slam from Ting-Lu. Hoopa-U removes Ghost-types like Spectrier, Gholdengo, and Choice Scarf Flutter Mane, appreciating Thunder Wave slowing down faster targets due to its mediocre Speed tier. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder outpaces and eliminates Meowscarada, Greninja, and Choice Specs Flutter Mane as well as threatening out Volcarona,which can set up in front of Meowstic-M. Iron Boulder values Reflect support to mitigate damage from priority moves, notably allowing it to survive Sucker Punch from Bisharp and +2 Hisuian Samurott as well as Aqua Jet from +2 Urshifu-R. Meowstic-M is Armarouge and Iron Crown's biggest benefactor, enabling them to reliably set up and activate Weakness Policy behind dual screens. Choice Scarf Latias can remove Dragapult, preventing it from threatening setup sweepers behind dual screens via Infiltrator. Latias also provides a Ground-type immunity, allowing it to combat Landorus and Great Tusk, which aren't affected by Thunder Wave, and can freely set up Gravity and Stealth Rock, respectively, in front of Meowstic-M. Metagross removes Flutter Mane with Bullet Punch and sets up Stealth Rock in addition to Meowstic-M's dual screens, further enhancing the capabilities of their teammates. Gallade wards off Dark-types like Ting-Lu, Bisharp, and non-Choice Scarf Hoopa-U, appreciating dual screens to aid in setting up Swords Dance and alleviating incoming damage from Sucker Punch from Bisharp and Hisuian Samurott if opting for a Choice Scarf set.

SubToxic.description: Aegislash's valuable defensive profile and immense natural bulk in Shield forme make it perfectly capable of forcing out and setting up on passive Pokemon such as Slowking, Jirachi, and Amoonguss. Substitute allows Aegislash to take advantage of the aforementioned Pokemon's inability to deal sufficient damage to it while also protecting it from potential status moves from these Pokemon; it also allows it to safely land Toxic on incoming defensive walls such as Hippowdon and Gastrodon, stalling them out in conjunction with King's Shield and recovery from Leftovers. Shadow Ball serves as Aegislash's main STAB move, and alongside Aegislash's naturally high Special Attack stat, is useful for putting pressure onto Toxic-immune Pokemon such as Excadrill, and Mega Sableye. The given EV spread allows Aegislash to 2HKO offensive Excadrill with Shadow Ball after Stealth Rock damage and Leftovers recovery, outspeed uninvested Scizor, and avoid the 2HKO from Enamorus's Earth Power and Mega Gardevoir's Mystical Fire after Stealth Rock. SubToxic Aegislash fits best on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its ability to safely set up on and wear down defensive Pokemon while also making use of its ability to simultaneously check offensive threats such as Mega Latias. Due to Aegislash's fear of status moves, like Scald burns from the likes of Slowking, as well as Spore from Amoonguss, pivots such as Flip Turn Keldeo, Teleport Slowbro, and Teleport Blissey are helpful to ensure that Aegislash finds safe opportunities against them. Other defensive Pokemon such as Buzzwole, Skarmory, and Clefable can form notable cores with Aegislash; the former two take advantage of Dark- and Ground-types such as Tyranitar and Hippowdon, while Clefable provides additional support in staving off the likes of Buzzwole, which can potentially nail Aegislash on the switch with Earthquake. Knock Off users such as the aforementioned Clefable and Assault Vest Tangrowth are also helpful, as they can remove items from checks to Aegislash like Leftovers from Celesteela and Heavy-Duty Boots from Scizor, giving it an easier time breaking through them in the long-run.

Offensive Swords Dance.description: Swords Dance turns Aegislash into a potent wallbreaker and sweeper, using its fantastic neutral coverage and bulk in Shield forme to set up against and break through defensive cores. Close Combat is Aegislash's strongest move overall, and it threatens the many Dark-types that would otherwise resist its Ghost-type STAB moves, like Tyranitar Hydreigon. Iron Head is an alternative option that still OHKOes the former two after a boost while also 2HKOing Unaware Clefable. Shadow Sneak is a crucial priority move which at +2 can finish off weakened offensive Pokemon that would normally outspeed and take it out, such as Mienshao and Keldeo, while also being usable to pick off Alakazam without a boost. An Adamant nature is preferred to maximize Aegislash's power, while a Jolly nature can be used instead to get the jump on Pokemon such as Adamant Tyranitar and Bisharp as well as slower variants of Rotom-W. However, this results in Aegislash missing out on certain damage thresholds, such as being unable to OHKO Mega Venusaur at +2 with the combination of Shadow Claw into Shadow Sneak. Ghostium Z is usually preferred to power up STAB Shadow Claw, which, when turned into Never Ending Nightmare, threatens to KO physically defensive Pokemon such as Skarmory and Amoonguss after Swords Dance. However, Air Balloon can be run instead if the team already has a different Z-Move user, and this also allows Aegislash to find free setup opportunities against Ground-types such as Excadrill and Hippowdon, potentially spinblocking the former. Aegislash fits best on more offensive teams that appreciate its defensive utility and ability to break open holes for its teammates early-game. Aegislash also suffers from having terrible bulk in Blade forme, so it is easily revenge killed after attacking, making entry hazard support from the likes of Mew, Swampert, and Tyranitar helpful at chipping down offensive threats like Excadrill into Shadow Sneak range while also pressuring other walls such as Rotom-W.

Mixed Attacker.description: Aegislash's excellent offenses and deep coverage allow it to function as an effective mixed attacker, slicing through a huge portion of the metagame, including defensive staples such as Mega Latias, Slowbro, and Blissey. Additionally, Aegislash's superb defensive traits mean it takes relatively little from their attacks in return, allowing it to find repeated entry against them, as well as soft-check dangerous offensive threats such as Mega Gardevoir, Mega Aerodactyl, and Alakazam. Close Combat forms perfect neutral coverage with Shadow Ball, ensuring Aegislash can consistently threaten the likes of Tyranitar, Bisharp, and Hydreigon. King's Shield provides Aegislash with defensive security against potential revenge killers such as Tyranitar and Hydreigon while scouting Choice item Pokemon such as Keldeo and Iron Boulder. Shadow Sneak gives Aegislash a valuable priority move that can pick off faster threats such as Blacephalon, Iron Boulder, and Mega Gallade. Alternatively, Toxic allows Aegislash to cripple specially defensive Pokemon such as Galarian Moltres and Hippowdon which would otherwise be able to check it, letting Aegislash wear them down effectively in conjunction with King's Shield. Flash Cannon provides a secondary STAB move that consistently threatens Clefable while OHKOing Mega Aerodactyl and Tapu Bulu, something which Shadow Ball into Shadow Sneak cannot do; however, it has little use outside of this. Even with this set's offensively oriented nature, Leftovers is crucial to provide Aegislash with passive recovery, allowing it to leverage its defensive traits and find more opportunities to attack. If longevity isn't a concern, Ghostium Z and Spell Tag are options that can be used on more aggressive teams to boost Shadow Ball's power, letting Aegislash muscle through defensive checks such as Mega Venusaur, Scizor, and Celesteela with greater ease. The given EVs, besides maximizing its Special Attack, ensure Aegislash can 2HKO Chansey with Close Combat after Stealth Rock and outspeed defensive Celesteela, with 240 EVs in HP allowing Aegislash to survive absurdly strong attacks such as Excadrill's Earthquake after Stealth Rock and Tyranitar's Knock Off. Alternatively, Aegislash can opt to run more Speed EVs over HP to outpace various targets, including Scizor, defensive Buzzwole, and Azumarill. However, this comes at the significant cost of cutting into Aegislash's bulk, often compounded by the need to run a Defense-lowering nature. Mixed Aegislash fits best on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its incredible combination of traits, from breaking down defensive cores with its immediate power to checking faster offensive threats such as Alakazam. Defensive Pokemon such as Buzzwole and Clefable synergize well with Aegislash's ability to deal with the likes of Mega Gardevoir and Enamorus. In return, they can help manage threats such as Hydrapple and Tyranitar, which otherwise force Aegislash out, and set entry hazards to help it break through checks such as Celesteela and Hippowdon. Similarly, other wallbreakers such as Iron Boulder, Serperior, and Keldeo greatly benefit from Aegislash's ability to pivot into faster revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Mienshao and Mega Aerodactyl as well as its ability to capitalize on defensive Pokemon that they may struggle to break through in Skarmory and Blissey. Finally, Aegislash greatly appreciates teammates which can help cripple its few defensive checks; Serperior can lure in Mega Venusaur and Hisuian Goodra and paralyze them with Glare, making it easier for Aegislash to overwhelm them. Offensive pivots like Zeraora and Scizor can use Knock Off to cripple checks reliant on their item, such as Celesteela and Assault Vest Tangrowth; these two can also use Volt Switch and U-turn to ensure Aegislash can find safe entry into potential targets such as Buzzwole and Rotom-W.

Bulky Swords Dance.description: Bulky Swords Dance Aegislash serves as a terrifying approach to its traditional role as a wallbreaker and setup sweeper, giving up immediate threat potential for incredible resilience. Notably, Aegislash's bulk and passive healing allow it to take repeated hits from Pokemon such as Hippowdon and Mega Gardevoir, giving it extra turns to set up and break through them late-game. Shadow Sneak, especially once boosted by Swords Dance, gives Aegislash a priority move to clean up weakened teams with; it notably OHKOes Iron Boulder and Mega Gallade at +2 and can OHKO offensive Excadrill at +4. Close Combat is Aegislash's strongest move overall and serves as important coverage against common Ghost-type checks such as Tyranitar and Hydreigon OHKOing the latter at +2. King's Shield reverts Aegislash to its Shield forme, preventing it from being reliably revenge killed by faster threats such as Tyranitar, Hydreigon, and Rillaboom and maximizes the amount of recovery gained from Leftovers. Alternatively, Shadow Claw provides Aegislash with a stronger STAB move that can tear through several weakened Fighting-resistant targets at +2, such as Amoonguss, Clefable, and Buzzwole. This Aegislash variant only fits on bulkier teams due to its lack of immediate offensive output and methodical playstyle. Entry hazards from defensive Pokemon, such as Clefable, Gastrodon, and Skarmory, are critical to its gameplan, weakening common Pokemon such as Excadrill, Mega Venusaur, and Hydrapple to where Aegislash is able to pick them off. In return, Aegislash can use its defensive profile to threaten out offensive Pokemon that may take advantage of their passivity, such as Mega Gardevoir, Reuniclus, and Alakazam. Additionally, as Aegislash is very weak to status conditions such as Will-O-Wisp from Rotom-W and Knock Off from Mega Venusaur and Tangrowth, which can also negate its Leftovers recovery, it appreciates partnering with other defensive teammates that can absorb these effects for it, notably Amoonguss, Slowbro, and Blissey. Slowbro and Blissey also provide Aegislash with slow pivoting in Teleport, allowing it to preserve its HP more effectively when trying to set up. By extension, offensive pivots such as Zeraora, Victini, and Mienshao are also valuable teammates, as they can help weaken or deal with several of Aegislash's checks early in the game, like Hippowdon, Foul Play Amoonguss, and Buzzwole.

Contrary RestTalk.description: 68 Spe allows Malamar to outspeed uninvested Milotic, but it can also fully invest in bulk.

Specially Defensive (Dragon).description: This is a sample set as we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Toxic Spikes Setter (Dragon).description: With its rare typing, access to Toxic Spikes, and ability to safely pivot its teammates in via Flip Turn, Dragalge finds a useful niche on Dragon teams. Due to its part Poison typing and natural special bulk, Dragalge can stomach a large portion of Fairy-type attacks in the metagame, including Choice Specs Tapu Koko’s Dazzling Gleam and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele’s Moonblast. Apart from Fairy-types, Dragalge can answer other threatening special attackers such as Volcarona, Keldeo, and Mega Charizard Y. Toxic Spikes are Dragalge’s most important tool, allowing it to pressure types that struggle to remove them, such as Fairy and Psychic. Even without investment, Adaptability-boosted Gunk Shot can OHKO problematic Fairy-types such as Enamorus and Iron Valiant. Additionally, this attack allows Dragalge to reliably stop Calm Mind Tapu Fini, which would be difficult to deal with otherwise. Sludge Bomb can be run as a more consistent option over Gunk Shot. Protect allows Dragalge to maximize Black Sludge recovery and scout potential Choice item foes like Tapu Lele and Meowscarada. 24 Speed IVs allow Dragalge to underspeed Toxapex so that the teammates it wants to bring in don’t get hit by Toxic or Scald. Dragalge forms an effective defensive core with Archaludon; Archaludon takes on strong physical attackers like Mega Scizor and Iron Boulder as well as certain Psychic-types like the latter for Dragalge. Offensive teammates like Garchomp, Kommo-o, and Roaring Moon appreciate Dragalge’s ability to get them onto the field safely. In return, Kommo-o shatters Steel-types like Heatran and Excadrill, and Roaring Moon does the same to Psychic-types like Jirachi and Victini. Garchomp blows up Poison-types like Toxapex and Clodsire with Earthquake and can threaten opposing Dragon-types like Dragonite and Kyurem with Scale Shot. Mega Latios provides a pivotal Ground-immune and Psychic-resistant ally for Dragalge and can beat threats to Dragalge like Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra with its wallbreaking set. Choice Scarf Latias is another option for a Ground-immune teammate, which can additionally use Healing Wish to grant Dragalge a second chance to check threats if it’s at low HP.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Flash Cannon is Clawitzer's strongest option against Articuno and also hits Whimsicott super effectively, but it has poor coverage and power otherwise. Hydro Pump's high Base Power seems tempting, but its low accuracy makes it unreliable compared to Water Pulse.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: ZU's many Grass-types pose a threat to Clawitzer, as they can easily switch into its Water Pulse and threaten an OHKO. Venusaur and Virizion can switch into Clawitzer multiple times thanks to their higher Speed and recovery in Synthesis. They must be cautious of Dragon Pulse, however. Brute Bonnet, Arboliva, and Whimsicott threaten Clawitzer as well but have to be wary of its coverage moves.

Electric-types: Jolteon, Vikavolt, and Magneton all threaten Clawitzer while also pivoting on it with Volt Switch. However, they struggle to switch directly into Clawitzer due to its powerful attacks.

Faster Attackers: Clawitzer's low Speed means that most offensive Pokemon, such as Toxicroak, Hitmontop, and Skunktank, are able to outrun and KO it. However, these offensive foes are rarely able to switch in directly, and Clawitzer's decent bulk allows it to take a hit from them at high HP.

Wallbreaker.description:
With a high Special Attack and Mega Launcher, Clawitzer makes for a devastating wallbreaker in ZU. Water Pulse has as much power as Surf when boosted by Mega Launcher, with the added benefit of potentially confusing the foe. Dragon Pulse serves as a powerful neutral attack that hits opposing Clawitzer and Venusaur while also destroying Alolan Exeggutor. Aura Sphere hits Cryogonal, Brute Bonnet, and Arboliva hard, which would otherwise be able to switch into Clawitzer's attacks. Clawitzer's last moveslot is rather flexible; Dark Pulse hits Psychic- and Ghost-types like Mesprit and Froslass super effectively, and Sludge Bomb hits most Grass-types super effectively, notably OHKOing Whimsicott. U-turn forfeits coverage in exchange for pivoting on the switches Clawitzer often forces. Tera Dragon flips Clawitzer's Grass and Electric weaknesses while also boosting Dragon Pulse to terrifying levels, most notably 2HKOing Venusaur.

Clawitzer's incredible wallbreaking prowess makes it great on balanced and bulky offense teams. Pivots such as Mesprit, Whimsicott, and Magneton can provide Clawitzer entry on passive walls, such as Orthworm, Weezing, and Sandslash. Clawitzer struggles against opposing Grass- and Electric-types, such as Whimsicott, Magneton, and Jolteon; as such, it appreciates teammates that it can fall back on against these threats. Weezing, Venusaur, and Muk deal with Grass-types, while Sandslash, Camerupt, and Whishcash can handle Electric-types. Fire-types like Charizard and Pyroar in particular make for good teammates, as they can deal with Grass-types for Clawitzer; in return, while it can wear down or remove their checks, such as Naclstack and Regirock. Walls like Regirock, Sandslash and Orthworm can help Clawitzer against faster attackers while providing further utillity such as entry hazards. Special setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Jolteon and Nasty Plot Mesprit appreciate Clawitzer weakening or removing opposing special walls, allowing them to easily clean up the battered teams it leaves behind.

Life Orb.description:
• Coupled with Pixilate and Life Orb, Hyper Beam and Hyper Voice both become powerful STAB moves, destroying most Dragon-, Dark- and Fighting-types, such as Raging Bolt, Galarian Moltres, Darkrai, Iron Valiant, and both Urshifu forms. In addition, Hyper Beam OHKOes Landorus, Iron Hands, Assault Vest Great Tusk, and non-Assault Vest Azumarill and Rhyperior; the combination of the two moves can defeat Bellibolt.
  • Thanks to the additional power and the defensive boost offered by Calm Mind, Sylveon can beat Manaphy, Spectrier, Espathra, non-Clear Amulet Zapdos, Assault Vest Ursaluna-B, Weakness Policy Primarina, and Calm Mind Raging Bolt.
  • The Special Defense drop of Fake Tears is useful against Assault Vest Ursaluna and Azumarill, whereas Quick Attack allows Sylveon to finish off Custap Berry users like Primarina, Galarian Moltres, and Porygon-Z.
  • The given EV spread lets Sylveon OHKO Alolan Ninetales with Hyper Beam and improves its matchup against Choice Band Urshifu-R. Indeed, Jolly Urshifu-R variants can't OHKO Sylveon, while Adamant versions only have low chances of KOing it.
  • Sylveon is unable to eliminate Steel-, Poison-, and Fire-types such as Iron Crown, Metagross, Pecharunt, Iron Moth, Volcarona, and Skeledirge. Therefore, teammates with a favorable matchup against them, like the Ursaluna formes and the Landorus formes, are appreciated.
  • Sylveon also can't face strong attackers such as non-Choice Specs Hoopa-U, boosted Porygon-Z, Ursaluna, and Donphan, so it needs partners like Corviknight and Choice Band Meowscarada to handle them.

vgc2024.overview:
• Sylveon's solid natural bulk as well as access to absurd damage from Pixilate-boosted Hyper Voice makes it a solid setup sweeper. With its pure Fairy typing, Sylveon boasts a better matchup into Ghost- and Dark-type threats such as Flutter Mane and Urshifu-S than its main Fairy-type competition, Flutter Mane.

  • Sylveon appreciates support from Fake Out and Follow Me, allowing it to set up Throat Spray or Calm Mind more easily. Incineroar makes up for Sylveons middling physical bulk with Parting Shot and Intimidate, as well as handling the Steel- and Fire-types that Sylveon struggles against. Ogerpon-W not only provides Follow Me support but similarly to Incineroar is able to handle Steel- and Fire-type attacks safely. Landorus is a great offensive partner, with it and Sylveon covering each other's checks, as well as making up for Sylveon's low initial damage output.

  • Sylveon's biggest issue is that it struggles to find a slot on most teams due to its competition with Flutter Mane, which is more of an immediate threat thanks to its higher single target damage, higher Speed, and Fake Out immunity from its Ghost typing. While Sylveon has use cases thanks to its bulk and pure Fairy typing, Flutter Mane is easier to fit into most compositions and is able to function well with minimal support. Sylveon's middling Speed means it is vulnerable to being overwhelmed by foes, making utilizing its strong setup options difficult.

Throat Spray Sweeper.description:
• Hyper Voice allows Sylveon to utilize Throat Spray as well as being a strong spread move after the boost from Pixilate. Misty Terrain allows Sylveon to block Spore from Amoonguss, while Calm Mind is also viable as another way to further increase Sylveon‘s damage output. Quick Attack picks off Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao, which normally run Focus Sash. If Sylveon is running Tera Fire, Tera Blast is also an option to hit Fairy-resistant foes such as Amoonguss and Gholdengo, as well as being a strong single target Fairy-type move before Terastallization thanks to Pixilate.

  • The invested Defense allows Sylveon to survive Wood Hammer from Rillaboom, as well as Ivy Cudgel from a Terastallized Ogerpon-W. Sylveon is also able to survive a Metal Coat-boosted Make It Rain from Gholdengo. Enough Speed is invested for Sylveon to outspeed Chi-Yu when under Tailwind, with the rest dumped into Special Attack.

  • Both Tera Fire and Water allow Sylveon to check problematic Steel- and Fire-types such as Gholdengo, Incineroar and Assault Vest Kingambit, though Tera Water is generally preferred thanks to having fewer weaknesses to common offensive threats. Tera Fire has valuable resistances to Fairy- and Grass-type moves on top of the coverage with Tera Blast; however, it makes Sylveon weak to more metagame threats, such as Landorus and Ogerpon-W.

nu.overview: Sylveon's great matchup against top threats like Scrafty and Flygon alongside its set versatility makes it one of the premier Fairy-types in NU. Wallbreaking sets can break through common special walls like Alolan Muk and Gastrodon. Sylveon can also run a more defensive set, letting it heal up teammates that it naturally synergizes with like Incineroar, Registeel, and Swampert that lack reliable recovery. Sylveon has great Special Defense, letting it take on special wallbreakers like Inteleon and Diancie with little or no investment. However, both of Sylveon's roles are contested by another Fairy-type, namely Florges, as Florges has access to Trick for Choice Specs sets as a way to decommission Steel-types and special walls, and it has higher Speed, meaning its wallbreaking sets can outpace more threats and Wish passing sets can invest more in its Defense. On top of that, Sylveon must compete with other Wish passers such as Vaporeon and Scream Tail, which can provide more utility at times with the former having access to Haze and Flip Turn, while the latter can provide Thunder Wave and Encore. Sylveon is also walled immensely by Steel-types like Copperajah and Registeel, but their lack of recovery leaves them susceptible to being worn down over the course of a game. Wish sets also tend to be passive and easily taken advantage of by the aforementioned Steel-types and setup sweepers like Munkidori and Incineroar. Sylveon's subpar Defense can also let it be broken through, as it's typically forced to take Knock Off for its team all while being whittled away at by entry hazards.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Due to Choice Specs Sylveon already having all the coverage it needs from its first three slots, it can run many moves for its last. Sylveon can opt for Quick Attack as a means to pick off weakened threats. Hyper Beam can be used as a nuke button that's able to chip away at Steel-types heavily but leaves it open the next turn. Sylveon can even forgo Choice Specs entirely and go for a Pixie Plate set that allows it to bluff Choice Specs, surprising its opponent when it changes up its moves; however, Sylveon's overall power drops. On Wish sets, Moonblast + Cute Charm can be run on bulkier teams, as Moonblast has higher PP than Hyper Voice, and if Sylveon is female, it can fish for immobilization via attraction against Pokemon forced to be male like Hitmonlee and Tornadus.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Registeel, Bronzong, and Copperajah all wall Sylveon and can use it to set entry hazards, as they easily threaten it out with their Steel-type STAB moves. While Klefki can also wall Sylveon, use it to set entry hazards, and paralyze it with Thunder Wave, it's more of a stalemate because Klefki fails to do significant damage to Sylveon unless it carries a rare move like Steel Beam. Bronzong must be cautious of Shadow Ball, though.

Poison-types: Alolan Muk, Munkidori, Amoonguss, and Tentacruel can take a Hyper Voice and threaten back with super effective Poison-type attacks. Dragalge can also take a hit and threaten it, but it can only do this once per game.

Chip Damage: Sylveon, especially when defensive, tends to have to take Knock Off and U-turn for its team, and losing Heavy-Duty Boots or not running it in the first place means entry hazards also chip away at it. All of this combined with Wish taking two turns and possibly being cancelled out due to Roar from Swampert or Whirlwind from Copperajah means that Sylveon can be whittled away at and beaten by wallbreakers it normally beats, like Incineroar and Flygon.

Choice Specs.description:
Set Details

Psychic allows Sylveon to hit Poison-types like Dragalge, Amoonguss, and Toxtricity super effectively. However, Psyshock can be run to hit Tentacruel and both Tera Poison Bronzong harder. Shadow Ball gives Sylveon a strong neutral move for the Steel-types that tend to switch into Sylveon like Klefki, Registeel, and Copperajah, and notably, it hits Bronzong super effectively. As Sylveon's last moveslot is its most flexible one, it prefers to run Draining Kiss as a secondary STAB move so that it doesn't get chipped away at as easily. A Modest nature is preferred for the extra damage output, but Timid can be run to outspeed Adamant Incineroar. Tera Fairy allows Sylveon to reach catastrophic levels of damage with its Hyper Voice, as it's now able to 2HKO Fairy-resistant Pokemon like Rotom-H and Galarian Slowbro.

Sylveon's main roadblock from tearing apart teams is bulky Steel-types like Registeel, Copperajah, and Klefki; however, due to their lack of recovery, there are a few ways its teammates can whittle them down. Entry hazard setters like Brambleghast, Swampert, and Flygon can help to soften up these Steel-types for Sylveon's attacks. Another way to break through these Pokemon is teammates that carry super effective coverage to surprise these Steel-types like Close Combat Staraptor, Focus Blast Munkidori, and Focus Blast Dragalge. It can also go through more straightforward means such as having a partner like Paldean Tauros formes, Incineroar, or Flygon to pressure these Steel-types. Incineroar, Flygon, and Infernape greatly enjoy Sylveon as a partner, as they can pivot it in on physically defensive Water-types like Milotic, Swampert, and Vaporeon that wall them. Choice Scarf users like Munkidori, Meloetta, and Porygon-Z enjoy Sylveon wearing away at Steel-types like Copperajah, Klefki, and Registeel. Sylveon easily dispatches Dark-types like Incineroar, Scrafty, and Alolan Muk. Teammates that benefit from this like Meloetta, Chandelure, and Brambleghast pair well alongside Sylveon, as they can form a wallbreaking core together.

Wish.description:
Set Details

Calm Mind allows Sylveon to use defensive walls like Vaporeon in its favor, as it can set up on them to become more threatening.
