On the other hand, Roar prevents Sylveon from needing to risk certain Calm Mind wars like those versus Scream Tail and Bronzong, and it doubles as a way to get extra chip damage on Steel-types trying to switch in, forcing them out to rack up entry hazard damage. The Speed EVs allow Sylveon to get the jump on Vaporeon, letting Sylveon avoid having its stat boosts thrown away by Vaporeon's Haze before it can get a hit off. Tera Steel is preferred, as it allows Sylveon to better handle Poison- and Steel-types like Amoonguss and Copperajah, provides an immunity to Gligar's Toxic, and lets it soft check many special attackers in a pinch like Munkidori, Porygon-Z, and Toxtricity. Tera Poison, on the other hand, maintains Sylveon's matchup against Fighting-types while keeping Tera Steel's utility against Toxic users and poison from Alolan Muk. Alternatively, Tera Water provides a strong defensive typing that doesn't forfeit Sylveon's matchup against both Ground- and Fighting-types like Flygon and Infernape. Leftovers prevents Sylveon from having to use Wish as often and lets it heal with Protect, but Heavy-Duty Boots is useful to circumvent entry hazard chip damage.

Sylveon's access to Wish means it can support Pokemon without reliable recovery like Swampert, Bronzong, and Incineroar. Pokemon like Basculegion-M, Munkidori, and Registeel that are scared out by Wo-Chien, Flygon, and Heracross enjoy having Sylveon to check these threats. Alongside a specially defensive partner like Alolan Muk, Gastrodon, or Copperajah, Sylveon can help to form a defensive backbone for teams. Sylveon also appreciates wallbreakers like Paldean Tauros-W, Flygon, and Chandelure, as they can pressure Steel-types that typically wall and take advantage of it like Klefki, Copperajah, and Bronzong. Due to Sylveon's reliance on Protect to safely heal, it's vulnerable to setup sweepers like Drednaw, Munkidori, and Paldean Tauros formes, meaning Choice Scarf revenge killers like Ditto or Pokemon with priority like Flygon pair well with it. Sylveon also tends to be a momentum sink, so pivots like Flygon, Incineroar, and Flamigo that do well versus common switch-ins like Alolan Muk, Registeel, and Copperajah can help regain lost momentum. As Sylveon can be easily chipped down by entry hazards and having to switch into Knock Off and U-turn from Pokemon like Incineroar, a second soft check to physical attackers is welcome, so partners like Scyther, Amoonguss, and Dragalge work well to fulfill this role.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis is for the Regulation C format of Battle Stadium Singles, which lasts until June 30th, 2023. For more information on this format and its current events, check out the format page!

If you feel this analysis is missing anything important or needs an update, feel free to suggest any changes here.

Offensive.description:
• With its good natural bulk, Sylveon can serve as a potent special attacker and decent revenge killer.

  • Tera Blast: Tera Blast serves as a good alternate STAB attack once Sylveon has Terastallized, providing highly valuable coverage against the Steel-types that could otherwise exploit it, like Scizor. It also gets around potential users of Throat Chop before Terastallization, such as Chien-Pao and Roaring Moon.

  • Psyshock: This is Sylveon's best shot of dealing with Iron Moth.

  • Shadow Ball: Shadow Ball hits foes such as Mimikyu, Flutter Mane, and Gholdengo super effectively, and it means Sylveon does not have to Terastallize to hit Gholdengo for good damage.

  • Quick Attack: Though it is weak, Quick Attack gives valuable priority for picking off weakened threats, and thanks to Pixilate, surprise users of Tera Ghost aren't able to absorb it. A Quiet nature can be used to increase its power, though this risks Sylveon getting outsped by Kingambit.

Other Options

  • Psychic: Psychic deals more damage to physically defensive Toxapex and Amoonguss, but its lower damage output against Iron Moth makes it disappointing if not using Tera Ground.

  • Hyper Beam: Despite the serious risks from the recharge turn, Hyper Beam's extreme power makes it a good filler move.

Items

  • Assault Vest: Assault Vest lets even offensive Sylveon be specially resilient.

  • Choice Specs: With the boost from Choice Specs, Sylveon is a surprisingly potent wallbreaker, making the most out of its many opportunities to switch in.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpA: This spread capitalizes on Sylveon's good natural bulk while maximizing its power.

  • 4 Def / 252 SpA / 252 Spe: While no bulk investment makes Sylveon more difficult to safely get in, Speed investment allows it to outrun and threaten a wider range of foes, such as Scizor and Corviknight.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Sylveon suffers coverage issues on its own, so its heavily reliant on either Tera Blast or the sheer power of Tera Fairy Hyper Voice to break past them.

  • Fire: Tera Fire allows Sylveon to break past troublesome Steel-types, like Gholdengo and Kingambit, and gives it a key resistance to Ice- and Fire-type attacks from Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu respectively.

  • Water: Tera Water gives good coverage against Fire-types like Iron Moth and Skeledirge, in addition to surprising Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu by resisting their strongest STAB attacks.

  • Ground: Tera Ground doesn't match up quite as well against Steel-types as Tera Fire, but it lets Sylveon turn the tables on Iron Moth, and deal massive damage to Toxapex and Skeledirge.

  • Fairy: Getting an extra boost on Hyper Voice and Hyper Beam makes Choice Specs Sylveon far more difficult to wall, with even resists such as Gholdengo and physically defensive Skeledirge getting 2HKOed by Hyper Voice!

Items

  • Assault Vest: Giving Sylveon extra special bulk lets it take on powerful threats like Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle more reliably.

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs turns Sylveon into a surprising wallbreaker, especially if using Tera Fairy.

  • Throat Spray: With Hyper Voice activating Throat Spray, Sylveon could potentially break apart slower foes in the late-game, though it only gets one shot at this Special Attack boost. This is best used with Tera Blast to give Sylveon an alternative STAB attack that doesn't activate Throat Spray.

CUTESY CRUSADER (Defensive).description:
• With its good bulk and Special Attack and a reasonable healing move in Wish, Sylveon is a good choice for a bulky Fairy-type.

  • Hyper Voice: Hyper Voice gives Sylveon a reliable STAB even when Terastallized, and hits through common Substitute users like Iron Bundle and Wo-Chien. While It's possible to drop this attack for Tera Blast in an attempt to run more coverage, this seriously worsens Sylveon's matchup against Chien-Pao and Ting-Lu.

  • Tera Blast: Beyond just Terastallization, Tera Blast is still impacted by Pixilate, making it a good move to use against foes that sometimes carry Throat Chop, like Chien-Pao and Roaring Moon.

  • Protect: Protect pairs excellently with Leftovers, and makes Wish a more reliable recovery move.

  • Yawn: Sylveon's good bulk makes it a great choice for phazing with Yawn.

  • Psyshock: Psyshock is Sylveon's best hope for Iron Moth switch-ins.

  • Shadow Ball: Shadow Ball offers important coverage on Gholdengo without demanding that Sylveon Terastallize.

  • Leftovers versus Sitrus Berry: Leftovers is the preferred recovery item for its synergy with Protect and Wish, but Sitrus Berry is a reasonable alternative if Protect isn't wanted, or if another teammate needs Leftovers more.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Sylveon's coverage issues are much easier to deal with when using Terastallization, but this set can still be used well defensively without it.

  • Fire: A Fire Tera type grants Sylveon resistances to Steel and Fairy, allowing it to take on foes it would otherwise have to run from, such as Gholdengo, and a good STAB to hit Chien-Pao hard with if not using Hyper Voice. It also works against Scizor, but note that Tera Water is common on that foe. Tera Fire also makes Sylveon far more vulnerable to Ting-Lu.

  • Water: Tera Water is a great mono-attacking option, making it ideal if only running Tera Blast to do decently well against Steel-types. It also gives Sylveon a better matchup against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, and is a safer option against Ting-Lu and Tera Water Scizor.

  • Fairy: If not using Tera Blast, Fairy becomes a reasonable option for boosting Hyper Voice's damage output. Note that Tera Blast is not needed to justify a different Tera Type.

  • Ground: Tera Ground worsens Sylveon's matchup with Chien-Pao, but it does let it deal big damage to Iron Moth, Gholdengo, and Toxapex.

Unburden Sweeper.description:
Hawlucha utilizes Swords Dance, Unburden, and its strong STAB moves to act as a threatening sweeper, late-game cleaner, and even revenge killer on Terrain teams. Thanks to the immediate activation of Unburden, Hawlucha becomes faster than almost everything in the metagame, outpacing Choice Scarf and Booster Energy users like Darkrai and Iron Valiant as well as even other setup sweepers like Venusaur on sun. Its typing along with a boost to its Defense due to the Terrain Seed allows Hawlucha to set up with Swords Dance in front of many common foes, such as Kingambit and Great Tusk. Close Combat's immediate strong power can be forgone for Low Kick's lack of Defense drops, notably preventing it from being picked off by revenge killers like Dragonite and Ceruledge afterwards. It still maintains high damage against targets like Kyurem, Ting-Lu, Garganacl, and Raging Bolt at the cost of being substantially weaker against walls like Corviknight and Skarmory. Encore gives it extra setup opportunities by locking the foe into a resisted attack, setup, or recovery move, such as against IronPress Corviknight. Roost provides longevity, letting it mitigate chip damage from Rocky Helmet from foes like Corviknight as well as Garganacl's Salt Cure, all of which can put it into KO range of revenge killers. Alternatively, Substitute can also give Hawlucha the breathing room it might need to set up against incoming status moves from Gliscor and Alomomola and deny Sucker Punch and Thunderclap from Kingambit and Raging Bolt, respectively. Grassy Seed is ran if Hawlucha is used on Grassy Terrain teams, but Psychic Seed is an alternative on the nicher Psychic Terrain teams, granting it a valuable Special Defense boost that can help it set up in the face of special attackers like Gholdengo. 124 EVs in Speed are enough to outspeed Sand Rush Excadrill after Unburden activates, and the bulk investment allows it to survive a Make It Rain from Gholdengo from full HP. Tera Steel gives it free setup against foes like Pecharunt, Gholdengo, Iron Valiant, and Kyurem. Tera Flying is a great way to enhance Acrobatics's damage output; for instance, after a Swords Dance, Hawlucha can OHKO Zamazenta through Dauntless Shield with Tera Flying. Alternatively, Tera Electric can be used to withstand Zapdos, Raging Bolt, and Gholdengo, disallowing paralysis attempts and resisting their main attacks. Compared to Tera Electric, Tera Ground is an even better option to prevent Raging Bolt's revenge killing attempts at the cost of being vulnerable to Rillaboom's Grassy Glide and Weavile's Ice Shard.

Whenever Hawlucha opts to run Grassy Seed, Rillaboom is always nearby. Rillaboom's terrain-setting ability and slow U-turn is pivotal in unleashing Hawlucha's onslaught. It can additionally spread Knock Off to rid Skarmory and Corviknight of their Rocky Helmet, for instance. Strong partners on Grassy Terrain teams include Pokemon such as Iron Moth and Heatran that can help to pressure some of Hawlucha's checks prior to its sweep such as the aforementioned Skarmory and Corviknight. Entry hazard support in the form of Glimmora, Hisuian Samurott, or Ting-Lu is also much appreciated. Hawlucha faces two big roadblocks in Gholdengo and Raging Bolt. Gholdengo in particular can easily shrug off Acrobatics and Close Combat, and it can take out Hawlucha while keeping itself healthy with Recover. Kingambit or the aforementioned Heatran have positive matchups against Gholdengo, while Pokemon like Hatterene can force Gholdengo in and weaken it while also providing a faster-paced Terrain team with entry hazard control. Raging Bolt, on the other hand, threatens non-Tera Electric Hawlucha with Thunderbolt and Thunderclap. It is therefore important to pair it with partners that can neutralize Raging Bolt such as Iron Valiant and Primarina. While the archetype is more niche, Indeedee is used instead of Rillaboom on Psychic Terrain teams. Rain teams can also handle Hawlucha, as Barraskewda still outspeeds it in the rain. Raging Bolt is a great check to rain teams that synergizes well with Grassy Terrain and can deal with rain's threats prior to Hawlucha cleaning up late-game.

Hawlucha acts as a threatening setup sweeper, being able to use its combination of Unburden and Swords Dance to clean up games. Substitute is used in order to find setup opportunities against foes such as Alomomola and Ferrothorn as well as Ground-types like Landorus-T and Gliscor, allowing Hawlucha to take advantage of their inability to hit it hard enough to break its Substitute. Hawlucha can also avoid Thunderclap from Raging Bolt and Sucker Punch from Kingambit. 228 Speed EVs are used to let Hawlucha outspeed maximum Speed Volcarona at +2 after Unburden activates. Electric, Grassy, and Psychic Seed are used with their respective Terrains in order to activate Hawlucha's Unburden, doubling its Speed as well as boosting the Base Power of Acrobatics to 110.

Hawlucha fits on hyper offense and bulky offense teams, where its ability to clean up games is appreciated. In order to activate Hawlucha's Unburden, it needs Terrain support from a teammate like Tapu Koko for Electric Terrain, Rillaboom or Tapu Bulu for Grassy Terrain, or Tapu Lele for Psychic Terrain. These Pokemon can also whittle down Hawlucha’s checks such as Gholdengo, Toxapex, and Slowbro. Hawlucha struggles to beat Electric-types such as Zapdos and Tapu Koko, meaning Pokemon that can switch into them such as Iron Treads and Ting-Lu are valued. In return, Hawlucha can turn Gliscor and Alomomola into setup fodder, which is appreciated because they would otherwise come in on Iron Treads and Ting-Lu relatively comfortably. If not yet boosted, Hawlucha struggles to break through Psychic- and Fairy-types such as Tapu Lele, Clefable, and Slowbro. All of these foes survive neutral Acrobatics and threaten Hawlucha with their STAB moves, meaning Steel-types such as Melmetal and Gholdengo are enjoyed. In return, Hawlucha can break through other Steel-types such as Heatran for them. Due to Hawlucha struggling to break through bulky Pokemon such as Gholdengo without boosts, entry hazard setters such as Mega Diancie, Iron Treads, and Landorus-T are beneficial, as their residual damage whittles down Hawlucha's checks over the course of a game. Teammates such as Kingambit and Mega Gyarados are also helpful to beat the aforementioned Gholdengo, with Hawlucha in return beating Fighting-types such as Zamazenta and Great Tusk.

nfe.overview: Hisuian Sliggoo is an outstanding tank thanks to its excellent offensive and defensive stats, typing, and movepool. Offensively, its STAB combination is rarely resisted, and the few comfortable enough to switch into its STAB moves, like Quaxwell and Duosion, are threatened by Acid Spray's stat drops. Defensively, its typing and offensive stats allow it to check important Grass-, Water-, and Poison-types in the tier, like Thwackey, Quaxwell, and Koffing, while still being immune to Toxic Spikes and resisting Stealth Rock. These traits allow it to be a threatening tank as an all-out attacker or RestTalk wall. However, Hisuian Sliggoo's Speed is very low, causing it to struggle against offensive and VoltTurn teams, with wallbreakers like Piloswine and Pignite easily forcing it out. Despite its excellent bulk and lack of passivity, its lack of recovery outside of Rest, lack of pivoting, and vulnerability to residual damage makes it deceptively easy to wear down as a defensive Pokemon.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs amps up Hisuian Sliggoo's already notable power to even more dangerous heights, but being locked into a coverage move makes it much easier to switch around, and it loses much of its bulk. Curse sets running Iron Head turn Hisuian Sliggoo into a wincon, enhancing its already strong bulk and power while not really minding the Speed drops. However, these sets make it even more vulnerable to residual damage and even more passive, as it's easily forced out by the threat of Encore and Taunt users, and it has to choose between using two coverage moves and going for RestTalk, which sacrifices more matchups.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types and Fighting-type coverage: Monferno, Scraggy, and Pignite are some of its most difficult matchups, with both needing just some chip damage to outright OHKO Hisuian Sliggoo with Close Combat, and being able to comfortably pivot in on any move but Draco Meteor. While Raboot is not a Fighting-type itself and is frailer, it can use Libero to similarly threaten to OHKO Hisuian Sliggoo with High Jump Kick with some chip and pivot in on non-Draco Meteor moves. Monferno and Raboot can even capitalize on Hisuian Sliggoo switching out with U-turn, bringing in another teammate to take on what would switch into their Fighting-type moves.

Ground-types: While Piloswine and Gabite dislike switching into Hisuian Sliggoo's Flash Cannon and Draco Meteor, respectively, both can significantly threaten it with their Ground-type STAB moves and set up Stealth Rock to capitalize on switches. Krokorok is notable for not being weak to any of Hisuian Sliggoo's standard moves and threatening it with Knock Off and Earthquake.

Residual Damage: Despite Hisuian Sliggoo being immune to Toxic Spikes and resisting Stealth Rock, its lack of recovery outside of Rest combined with being tasked to switch into threats makes it very vulnerable to being worn down by repeated pivoting, burns, and entry hazard damage from Spikes. Phazers like Dragon Tail Drakloak and Roar Quilladin further whittle it down.

Wallbreakers: Should Hisuian Sliggoo be worn down enough, wallbreakers like Fraxure, Stantler, and Choice Specs Drakloak can take advantage of its low Speed and pick it off with ease.

All-Out Attacker.description:
Hisuian Sliggoo's good power, excellent defensive typing, and bulk make it one of the most frightening tanks to face off against. Thunderbolt rattles Quaxwell that may consider weathering Draco Meteor, while Ice Beam threatens popular Grass-types like Ivysaur, Servine, and Thwackey. Acid Spray discourages walls like Dunsparce and Duosion from staying in on it, enabling it to continue threatening the metagame with its attacks. While all of Hisuian Sliggoo's abilities are situational, Gooey stands out for discouraging Thwackey and Fraxure from staying in on it, while Sap Sipper blocks Leech Seed users like Ivysaur and Servine. The Speed EVs enable it to outrun uninvested Piloswine.

Offensive Hisuian Sliggoo works best on balanced and bulky offensive teams, pairing up with teammates that appreciate its defensive and offensive profile. Water-types like Quaxwell and Frogadier pair well with it, with the former providing Rapid Spin support and a defensive answer to Fire-types and Piloswine and the latter offering Spikes and speed control; both offer pivoting. Other entry hazard deterrents like Fletchinder and Hattrem not only ward off hazards set against Hisuian Sliggoo, but both also spread status and provide a backbone against Fighting-types like Monferno and Pignite. Other wallbreakers and setup sweepers in need of Hisuian Sliggoo's wallbreaking capabilties, like Fraxure, Wartortle, and Thwackey, appreciate it softening walls like Duosion and Tinkatuff. Teammates like Piloswine and Wartotle appreciate Hisuian Sliggoo for taking on Grass-types like Thwackey, Ivysaur, and Servine, while physical walls like Koffing and Quilladin likewise appreciate it for taking on special attackers like Girafarig, Drakloak, and Wartortle. While Hisuian Sliggoo beats Tinkatuff in the long run, the combination of its typing, Knock Off, Encore, and Thunder Wave can frustrate its breaking capabilities, so checks to it like Gabite and Krokorok can force it out and set up Stealth Rock against it; the latter can also use its own Knock Off to initiate progress.

RestTalk.description:
Hisuian Sliggoo's excellent typing, offenses, bulk, and high-powered STAB moves allow it to be a fantastic wall, trading away immediate Speed and potential power in exchange for greater longevity. Acid Spray discourages bulkier walls like Dunsparce and Duosion from staying in on it, which pairs well with Flash Cannon's consistent damage output. Draco Meteor and either Flash Cannon or Thunderbolt, on the other hand, shift Hisuian Sliggoo's role to that of a tank, heavily threatening out most of the metagame and dealing significant damage to Water-types like Quaxwell and Wartortle. While Gooey is discourages physical attackers like Thwackey and Fraxure from staying in on it, Sap Sipper allows it to block Leech Seed from Ivysaur and be even more effective against Grass-types like Servine and Thwackey. A Calm nature and a spread of 252 HP / 4 SpA / 252 SpD makes it an extremely durable special wall, while a Modest nature and a spread of 252 HP / 252 SpA / 4 SpD maximizes its offensive power.

This Hisuian Sliggoo set is able to fit on both balance and bulkier builds. Even with increased bulk, it still remains very vulnerable to Fighting-types like Monferno, Scraggy, and Pignite, so checks to them like Seadra, Quaxwell, and Fletchinder are appreciated; the first also covers Hisuian Sliggoo's weaknesses to Ground-types like Piloswine and Krokorok and Fire-types like Monferno and Pignite, while the last provides entry hazard removal to address Hisuian Sliggoo's vulnerability to Spikes. In return, Hisuian Sliggoo can cover for Seadra and Quaxwell's weaknesses to Grass-types and Fletchinder's weakness to Water- and Electric-types. With its reliance on RestTalk for recovery, it remains susceptible to being worn down by residual damage, so hazard deterrents like Quaxwell and Hattrem can preserve its longevity. Offensive partners like Wartortle, Monferno, and Thwackey all appreciate Hisuian Sliggoo covering their weaknesses; the latter two can also provide Knock Off and U-turn support to form offensive cores. While Hisuian Sliggoo beats Tinkatuff in the long run, it hates being paralyzed and getting its Eviolite removed by Knock Off. Switch-ins to Tinkatuff like Piloswine and Gabite are greatly appreciated to absorb Thunder Wave, threaten it away with their STAB moves, and set up Stealth Rock to generate progress. In return, Hisuian Sliggoo can defend against Grass-types with Sap Sipper and cover teammates like Wartortle and Krokrorok that would struggle against them.

nu.overview: Goodra carves out a unique niche thanks to its great utility and good set diversity. Goodra's great Special Defense and typing allow it to check special wallbreakers like Chandelure, Munkidori, and Inteleon. Goodra's solid utility movepool gives it a lot of options to support its team; Knock Off lets it pressure item-reliant Pokemon like Porygon2 and Incineroar, Toxic allows Goodra to cripple defensive foes like Gastrodon and Diancie, and Dragon Tail phazes setup sweepers like Oricorio-P and Toxtricity. Choice Specs makes Goodra a strong wallbreaker that can 2HKO the bulkiest foes that don't resist Dragon like Gastrodon and Alolan Muk after Stealth Rock damage. However, Goodra's average physical bulk makes it very easy to be revenge killed by physical attackers like Flygon, Toxicroak, and Flamigo. Steel- and Fairy-types like Bronzong, Diancie, and Scream Tail can take advantage of Choice Specs Goodra locking into its Dragon-type attacks, letting them set up or force it to switch. Furthermore, Goodra's middling Speed makes it easily revenge killed by faster Pokemon like Flamigo, Paldean Tauros-W, and Flygon. Goodra also lacks any reliable recovery, so its utility sets can be overwhelmed by repeated attacks.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Expert Belt gives a boost to Goodra's super effective coverage attacks. Assault Vest lets it better tank hits from special attackers like Alolan Ninetales and Chandelure, but it often prefers the entry hazard immunity, passive recovery, and extra power granted by Heavy-Duty Boots, Leftovers, and Choice Specs, respectively. Surf can be used over Hydro Pump on Choice Specs sets due to its better accuracy. Power Whip lets it better handle specially defensive Water-types like Gastrodon and Milotic while also capitalizing on a Sap Sipper boost.

Checks and Counters

Physical Wallbreakers: Flygon, Toxicroak, Paldean Tauros-W, and Basculegion-M can put major pressure on Goodra thanks to its average Defense, but none of them enjoy switching into Goodra's attacks. Setup sweepers like Swords Dance Scyther, Shell Smash Drednaw, and Bulk Up Tornadus can easily KO Goodra.

Steel-types: Copperajah, Bronzong, and Klefki can force Goodra to switch, and they can set up their entry hazards, but they must be worried about switching in against its Fire-type attacks.

Fairy-types: Sylveon, Diancie, Alolan Ninetales, and Scream Tail are immune to Goodra's STAB attacks, and they can easily destroy it with their Fairy-type attacks. However, Diancie gets threatened by Hydro Pump, while the other three don't enjoy switching into Sludge Wave or Sludge Bomb.

Heavy-Duty Boots.description:
Set Details

Fire Blast allows Goodra to beat common Steel-types like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Klefki, while Flamethrower can be used for its better accuracy. Sludge Bomb allows Goodra to threaten Fairy-types like Sylveon and Scream Tail and lets it fish for poison. Alternatively, Sludge Wave can be used for the higher power. Toxic cripples defensive walls like Vaporeon, Porygon2, and Scream Tail. Knock Off lets it threaten Pokemon that heavily rely on their item such as Porygon2 and Scyther. Dragon Tail can phaze setup sweepers like Oricorio-P and Toxtricity, while Scald allows Goodra to threaten physical attackers like Paldean Tauros-W and Scyther with a burn. Sap Sipper allows it to be immune to Grass-type attacks from Amoonguss and Decidueye, whereas Gooey can punish physical attackers like Flygon and Paldean Tauros-W, allowing its teammates to outspeed and pick them off. An EV spread consisting of 76 HP / 252 SpA / 180 Spe with a Modest nature allows Goodra to better handle attacks from Munkidori and Chandelure while letting it outspeed Jolly Incineroar as well as Adamant Basculegion-M and Decidueye. Alternatively, Goodra can fully invest in Speed, allowing it to outpace foes like Toxtricity. Tera Poison lets Goodra be immune to any poison attempts from Galarian Slowbro, Amoonguss, and Alolan Muk while letting it better handle Fairy-types like Diancie and Scream Tail. Tera Steel allows it to better handle special wallbreakers like Toxtricity, Scream Tail, and Porygon-Z while giving it useful Fairy, Dragon, and Ice resistances. Tera Fairy is similar to Tera Poison in that Goodra gains a Fighting resistance, but it also gives Goodra a Dragon immunity and a better defensive typing.

Physical wallbreakers like Decidueye, Toxicroak, and Incineroar appreciate Goodra for handling physically defensive tanks such as Avalugg, Galarian Slowbro, and Gligar. In return, they handle special walls like Gastrodon, Porygon2, and Alolan Muk. Goodra partners well with Wish passers like Vaporeon and Sylveon, allowing Goodra to repeatedly switch in against foes like Chandelure and Kilowattrel. Steel-types like Bronzong, Copperajah, and Klefki are great teammates for Goodra, since they can handle Fairy-types such as Alolan Ninetales, Diancie, and Scream Tail. Goodra appreciates physical walls like Galarian Slowbro, Amoonguss, and Swampert; they can handle physical wallbreakers like Toxicroak and Flygon. In return, Goodra checks the common special wallbreakers like Chandelure, Kilowattrel, and Vaporeon. Entry hazard setters and special wallbreakers like Klefki, Swampert, and Inteleon appreciate Goodra's ability to remove Altaria's Heavy-Duty Boots and Porygon2's Eviolite. Wallbreakers like Flamigo, Chandelure, Munkidori, and Scyther appreciate its Toxic, which allows them to overwhelm their checks such as Avalugg, Porygon2, and Diancie.

Choice Specs.description:
Set Details

Fire Blast allows Goodra to hit Steel-types like Copperajah and Bronzong very hard, but Flamethrower can be used for its better accuracy. Sludge Wave lets it hit Fairy-types like Sylveon and Florges; however, Sludge Bomb can be used for its higher chance to poison. Hydro Pump targets Diancie as well as Fire-types like Chandelure and Incineroar. Thunderbolt lets Goodra reliably hit Water-types like Vaporeon and Milotic, but Dragon Pulse can be used for a reliable STAB attack that can be repeatedly spammed. Sap Sipper allows Goodra to be immune to Grass-type attacks from Amoonguss, while Gooey can punish physical attackers like Paldean Tauros-W and Infernape by dropping their Speed, allowing it to revenge kill them. Goodra can invest in fully in Speed, allowing it to outspeed foes like Breloom and Toxtricity, but an alternative EV spread of 76 HP / 252 SpA / 180 Spe with a Modest nature allows Goodra to better handle attacks from Munkidori and Chandelure while still outpacing foes like Jolly Incineroar and Adamant Decidueye. Tera Poison boosts Sludge Wave and Sludge Bomb while giving Goodra the ability to better handle foes like Toxicroak, Sylveon, and Flamigo. On the other hand, Tera Dragon boosts the power of Goodra's STAB attacks, letting it do major damage to threats like Alolan Muk, Gastrodon, and Milotic.

Goodra partners well with entry hazard setters like Bronzong, Klefki, and Overqwil, allowing it to pressure special walls like Porygon2 and Gastrodon. Fairy-types like Sylveon, Diancie, and Scream Tail can force Goodra to switch if it's locked into a Dragon-type attack; thus, Steel-types like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Klefki are good partners to check them. Hazard removers like Scyther, Brambleghast, and Avalugg allow Goodra to not be worn down by hazards. Goodra synergizes with other wallbreakers like Paldean Tauros-W, Incineroar, and Decidueye, allowing them to overwhelm defensive tanks like Galarian Slowbro, opposing Incineroar, and Porygon2. Pivot users like Inteleon, Flamigo, and Infernape can bring in foes like Milotic, Diancie, and Altaria; together, they can overwhelm these foes and let Goodra easily pick them off.

Acid Spray.description:
Set Details

Acid Spray lets Goodra limit special walls like Alolan Muk, Porygon2, and Vaporeon from getting too comfortable about tanking its attacks. Flamethrower gives Goodra the ability to hit Steel-types like Bronzong and Klefki, but Fire Blast can be used for its higher power, allowing it to potentially get a KO. Substitute allows Goodra to take advantage of passive walls like Vaporeon, Gastrodon, and Galarian Slowbro. Sludge Bomb hits Fairy-types like Alolan Ninetales and Scream Tail while letting it fish for poison, but Sludge Wave can be used for the higher power. Leftovers gives Goodra a form of recovery, which is especially useful on Substitute sets, while Heavy-Duty Boots lets it continuously switch into foes like Chandelure and Milotic without getting worn down by entry hazards. Sap Sipper allows Goodra to take advantage of Grass-types like Amoonguss and Decidueye. Alternatively, Gooey can benefit its teammates, allowing them to outspeed faster foes like Flygon and Cinccino. An EV spread of 76 HP / 252 SpA / 180 Spe paired with a Modest nature lets Goodra better tank attacks from threats like Toxtricity and Munkidori while outpacing foes such as Jolly Incineroar and Adamant Decidueye, but it can fully invest into Speed to let Goodra outspeed threats such as Basculegion-M and Toxtricity. Tera Poison gives Goodra useful resistances to Fighting and Fairy and an immunity to any poison status from Alolan Muk and Galarian Slowbro while boosting the power of both Sludge Bomb and Sludge Wave. On the other hand, Tera Steel gives it the ability to better handle special wallbreakers like Sylveon, Munkidori, and Toxtricity.

Goodra best partners with Pokemon like Inteleon, Munkidori, and Kilowattrel, since they can bring in passive threats like Gastrodon, Bronzong, and Porygon2 and allow it to easily take advantage of them. Wish passers such as Vaporeon and Scream Tail give Goodra another form of recovery, allowing it to repeatedly switch in against Chandelure and Basculegion-M. Goodra pairs best with Steel- and Poison-types like Bronzong, Amoonguss, and Klefki, as they can handle Fairy-types like Florges and Diancie. Physical walls like Overqwil, Amoonguss, and Swampert can handle physical attackers like Flygon, Infernape, and Scyther. Goodra can be pressured if it's repeatedly switching into entry hazards; thus, it appreciates hazard removal like Scyther, Brambleghast, and Avalugg. Pokemon like Basculegion-M, Flamigo, and Toxtricity appreciate Goodra's ability to break through common defensive walls like Bellibolt, Wo-Chien, and Gastrodon.

ru.overview: Hisuian Goodra's incredible natural bulk, solid defensive typing, and numerous ways to make progress cement it as one of the most reliable defensive Pokemon in the tier. Hisuian Goodra's Dragon / Steel typing gives it resistances to STAB attacks from the strongest special attackers in the tier, such as Toxtricity and Gardevoir, while its high Special Defense allows it to usually shrug off neutral hits as well. Moreover, there are very few Pokemon in the metagame that can slow Hisuian Goodra down from making progress with its Choice Specs set carrying immense power and its defensive set's access to several coverage and utility options such as Knock Off, Acid Spray, and Protect. However, Hisuian Goodra's low Speed stat holds it back quite a bit, rendering it weak to common offensive threats such as Terrakion, Krookodile, and Gallade and even generally slow Pokemon such as Chesnaught and Golurk. Its lack of reliable recovery also significantly lowers its effectiveness as a defensive sponge, making it vulnerable to getting chipped down by entry hazards and VoltTurn cores over longer games.
ru.comments:
Other Options

An IronPress set with Acid Armor and Body Press can significantly improve Hisuian Goodra's ability to deal with physical attacks and possibly allow it to sweep, though its lack of recovery makes it suboptimal. Fire Blast can be used over Flamethrower to trade accuracy for power, notably allowing bulky attacker Hisuian Goodra to 2HKO Jirachi and guaranteeing Choice Specs Hisuian Goodra an OHKO on Bisharp. Thunderbolt allows bulky attacker sets to hit Water-types like Slowbro, Basculegion-F, and Empoleon.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Many of the Fighting-type Pokemon in the metagame such as Gallade and Terrakion threaten to OHKO Hisuian Goodra. Chesnaught can similarly take it down after some chip damage.

Ground-types: Ground-types like Krookodile and Flygon can outspeed and KO Hisuian Goodra after minor chip damage. Though Rhyperior and Gastrodon are slower, they can usually survive a hit and deal significant damage back.

Bulky Setup Sweepers: Setup sweepers with decent bulk like Bisharp and Registeel can often tank Hisuian Goodra's attacks as well as prepare to KO it back and potentially sweep. Calm Mind sweepers such as Slowbro and Reuniclus can also pose problems to Hisuian Goodra if it lacks Acid Spray. While Dragon Tail can phaze many of these sweepers, it fails against Substitute Suicune and Tera Fairy users.

Entry Hazards: Despite Hisuian Goodra's resistance to Stealth Rock, it is vulnerable to getting chipped down by entry hazards due to its lack of reliable recovery, eventually making it unable to answer special wallbreakers such as Choice Specs Basculegion-F and Toxtricity.

Bulky Attacker.description:
Set Details

Bulky attacker Hisuian Goodra leverages its good natural bulk to consistently tank special attacks and strike back with strong attacks and progress-making moves. Heavy Slam is great for dealing with specially defensive foes such as Blissey and Wo-Chien. Acid Spray is an alternative that can more consistently take down defensive tanks in combination with Draco Meteor, especially ones that can't threaten Hisuian Goodra back like Umbreon and Slowbro. Knock Off is fantastic for making progress against common switch-ins such as Jirachi, Registeel, and the aforementioned Umbreon, as well as enabling Acid Spray by removing Covert Cloak from common users like Slowbro. Earthquake similarly hits Steel-types as well as Poison-type targets such as Toxtricity and Alolan Muk. Flamethrower is an alternative that also helps Hisuian Goodra deal with Pokemon like Wo-Chien and Forretress more easily. Protect is incredibly useful on Leftovers Hisuian Goodra, allowing it to heal up safely while scouting for attacks, especially those from common Choice item users such as Gengar and Krookodile. Dragon Tail is an option that can chip away at switch-ins, especially if entry hazards are set up on the opposing field, and phaze threatening setup sweepers like Bisharp. Although these options are slashed in specific slots, it should be noted that Hisuian Goodra is able to freely mix and match from them to suit the needs of its team. Leftovers is valuable on Hisuian Goodra to make up for its lack of reliable recovery, though Assault Vest can be used to make it a nigh-unbreakable special wall. Sap Sipper allows Hisuian Goodra to wall Grass-types such as Wo-Chien and Amoonguss. Gooey is an alternative that can slow down physical attackers like Jirachi and Maushold to then allow Hisuian Goodra or one of its teammates to outspeed them and strike back, but it should be used with caution due to Bisharp being common in the metagame and able to exploit it with Defiant. The given EVs maximizes Hisuian Goodra's bulk and offense ; however, similar to its moveset, Hisuian Goodra's EV spread and nature can be altered to suit its desired defensive and offensive capabilities. Tera Fairy flips Hisuian Goodra's weakness to Fighting into a resistance, removes its weakness to Ground, and provides a valuable resistance to Knock Off, enabling it to survive hits from physical wallbreakers such as Terrakion and Krookodile and threaten them back with its powerful attacks. Tera Ghost instead provides an immunity to Fighting to help against Fighting-type wallbreakers like Gallade, though Hisuian Goodra should be careful of the acquired weaknesses to Dark- and Ghost-type attacks from common Pokemon such as Krookodile, Bisharp, and Basculegion-F. Tera Water removes Hisuian Goodra's weaknesses while retaining its resistance to Iron Head from Jirachi and Bisharp. Additionally, Tera Water improves Hisuian Goodra's ability to deal with Entei and should be combined with Sap Sipper to nullify the Grass weakness it causes Hisuian Goodra to have. However, Tera Water has the caveat of making Hisuian Goodra unable to deal with Electric-types such as Magnezone and Kilowattrel.

Hisuian Goodra is a fantastic fit on balance and bulky offense teams as a blanket switch-in to most special attackers in the tier such as Yanmega and Basculegion-F. Physically defensive partners such as Chesnaught, Slowbro, and Gastrodon are practically necessities for Hisuian Goodra, as they can tank attacks from physical wallbreakers like Terrakion and Krookodile. On top of that, they also serve as Knock Off absorbers, which Hisuian Goodra appreciates due to often being item reliant, particularly if it's holding Leftovers. Hisuian Goodra greatly appreciates entry hazard removal from Noivern or Cyclizar, due to its lack of reliable recovery; Cyclizar can also be used, though it can be a suboptimal partner due to overlapping roles and sharing the Fighting weakness with Hisuian Goodra. To similarly make up for Hisuian Goodra's lack of recovery, Wish passers like Umbreon and Jirachi can be valuable teammates. Acid Spray Hisuian Goodra pairs well with strong special attackers like Basculegion-F and Gardevoir that can exploit the weakened foe or an unsuspecting switch-in to blow holes in the opposing team. Hisuian Goodra's Knock Off and Dragon Tail can help make progress on hazard-stacking structures, with setters like Krookodile, Jirachi, and Chesnaught, by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from the opposing team and chipping away at them through hazards and phazing. Hisuian Goodra can often struggle to stop bulky setup sweepers such as Bisharp and Suicune; therefore, teammates that can handle them defensively, such as Chesnaught, Umbreon, and Noivern, respectively, as well as those with disruption options, such as Choice Scarf Trick Gardevoir, Encore Jirachi, and Dragon Tail Cyclizar, are important to have.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Hisuian Goodra is a devastating wallbreaker in RU, leveraging its excellent defensive typing to switch into many attacks while using its diverse movepool to hit a wide range of targets. Thunderbolt allows Hisuian Goodra to consistently hit the Water-types of the tier, such as Slowbro, Empoleon, and Suicune. Flamethrower melts the Steel-types that resist both of Hisuian Goodra's STAB moves such as Jirachi, Magnezone, and Bisharp. Choice Specs boosts Hisuian Goodra's power to stupendous heights, allowing it to pick up OHKOs on the likes of Slowbro and Chesnaught that could otherwise stomach a hit from it. Gooey allows Hisuian Goodra to slow down physical attackers, notably crippling Maushold, which can help in late-game situations against wallbreakers such as Gallade and Terrakion. 216 Speed EVs allow Hisuian Goodra to outspeed Adamant Crawdaunt and Golurk. Tera Ghost removes Hisuian Goodra's Fighting weakness, allowing it to break through the likes of Terrakion and Breloom. Tera Dragon boosts the power of Draco Meteor to absurd levels, allowing it to surprise an enemy that could otherwise take the hit, like Gastrodon. However, this makes Hisuian Goodra weak to Ice, Fairy and Dragon, meaning it cannot switch in as easily against Pokemon such as Ice Beam Empoleon, Gardevoir, and Noivern, so it's best used in a late-game scenario or once these foes have been KOed.

Hisuian Goodra fits best on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its ability to check special threats such as Yanmega and Basculegion-F while giving them offensive firepower to help against bulkier teams. Fast sweepers such as Choice Scarf Gengar, Choice Scarf Krookodile, and Barraskewda appreciate Hisuian Goodra's ability to wear down defensive pokemon such as Umbreon, Registeel, and Empoleon early-game in order for them to clean up late-game. Wish support from teammates such as Umbreon and Vaporeon are great for Hisuian Goodra, as they are able to heal off the chip damage that Hisuian Goodra has taken and allow it to continue its assault upon the opposing team. Fighting- and Ground-resistant Pokemon such as Cresselia and Noivern are great partners, as they are able to take on the Fighting- and Ground-types, like Breloom and Krookodile. Other physically defensive teammates such as Amoonguss, Chesnaught, and Gastrodon are also great partners for Hisuian Goodra, similarly taking the strong physical hits that are aimed at it while being able to support it by spreading status and setting entry hazards. Gardevoir is a good offensive and defensive partner to Hisuian Goodra, as it is able to switch into the Fighting-type moves that threaten Hisuian Goodra. In return, Hisuian Goodra is easily able to switch into and take advantage of the Steel-types that check them like Jirachi and Empoleon. Pivots such as Cyclizar and Jirachi can bait in physical walls like Gastrodon, Slowbro, and Chesnaught and pivot into Hisuian Goodra, which can then freely fire off a powerful attack.

Assault Vest.description:
Hisuian Goodra carves out a niche as a special tank with its gargantuan Special Defense augmented by Assault Vest, letting it beat foes like Darkrai, Raging Bolt, and Iron Moth one-on-one. Dragon Tail allows it to phaze the aforementioned threats if they get out of hand and other miscellaneous threats like Kingambit and Swords Dance Gliscor if it lacks the appropriate coverage as well as forcing entry hazard damage against the opposition, while Draco Meteor's nuke can be used to punish the likes of Ogerpon-W, Alomomola, and Cinderace harder and immediately OHKOes foes like Kyurem and Walking Wake. Flamethrower allows Hisuian Goodra to dissuade Steel-types like Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Kingambit from switching. Ice Beam lets it deal heavy damage to Zapdos, Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and particularly specially defensive Gliscor, which would otherwise wall it. However, Knock Off can be used over one of these coverage moves, as it allows Hisuian Goodra to force progress against foes like Galarian Slowking, Moltres, and Garganacl, making them vulnerable to chip damage from entry hazards by removing either their Heavy-Duty Boots or their passive recovery in Leftovers. It's also worth noting that potential Knock Off absorbers like Gliscor and Clefable struggle to take any of Hisuian Goodra's attacks. Sap Sipper is the preferred ability, as it makes Hisuian Goodra immune to Grass-type attacks from Ogerpon-W, Meowscarada, and Rillaboom, allowing it to serve as a more solid check to these foes before and after Terastallizing. On the other hand, Gooey punishes contact moves like Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge and Weavile's Knock Off, giving Hisuian Goodra more chances at dealing damage back and opening up teammates to potentially revenge kill these foes. Tera Fairy gives a key resistance to Fighting-type attacks and an immunity to Dragon-type moves, which lets it beat Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, Raging Bolt, and Dragapult.

Hisuian Goodra primarily fits on balance teams where its defensive and offensive shortcomings are alleviated. Teammates like Landorus-T, Zapdos, and Alomomola can safety pivot Hisuian Goodra so it can force out opponents like Darkrai and Gholdengo. Additionally, Alomomola is an amazing partner thanks to the Wish support it can provide; in exchange, Hisuian Goodra deals with Ogerpon-W. Landorus-T complements Hisuian Goodra's Knock Off with Stealth Rock, while Zapdos provides Thunder Wave, with both of them checking physical foes like Zamazenta and Kingambit. Hisuian Goodra often has problems with longevity, as entry hazards can slowly chip it down to low enough health to be taken out. For this reason, Great Tusk and Cinderace are great teammates, since they offer hazard control through Rapid Spin and Court Change, respectively. On top of that, the former appreciates Hisuian Goodra taking hits from spinblockers like Gholdengo and Dragapult, while the latter can pivot Hisuian Goodra in with U-turn or use Will-O-Wisp to cripple physical threats like Great Tusk and Dragonite for it. Ting-Lu and Gliscor can support Hisuian Goodra through setting hazards, letting it use Knock Off or Dragon Tail more effectively. In return, both appreciate the defensive fallback Hisuian Goodra provides against Ogerpon-W, Hatterene, and Darkrai. Physical attackers like Dragonite and Zamazenta enjoy Hisuian Goodra taking care of key foes such as Fairy-types like Enamorus and Clefable for the former and Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Dragapult for the latter.

Offensive Tank.description: Thanks to its vast movepool, impressive special bulk, and solid defensive typing, Hisuian Goodra is a notable tank on offensive teams for its ability to help check Hydrapple, Enamorus, and specially offensive Aegislash, leveraging its plethora of opportunities against these Pokemon to fire off its disruptive attacks. Flash Cannon is preferred over Heavy Slam due to its greater effectiveness against common Pokemon that are weak to it, such as Tyranitar and Clefable. Flamethrower hits opposing Steel-type Pokemon such as Swords Dance Aegislash and Scizor, preventing them from potentially taking advantage of it. Lastly, Knock Off adds vital utility to Hisuian Goodra's toolkit by allowing it to remove Leftovers from common defensive Pokemon such as Hippowdon and Swampert as well as Heavy-Duty Boots from Amoonguss and Blissey. In particular, thanks to Sap Sipper, Hisuian Goodra is an excellent absorber of Celesteela's Leech Seed and Amoonguss's Spore, which would otherwise be especially irritating for its teammates to handle; in addition, it blocks the former’s recovery in conjunction with Knock Off’s removal of Leftovers. 176 Speed EVs allow Hisuian Goodra to outpace Ursaluna and Azumarill, while 176 Special Attack EVs ensure an OHKO on Hydrapple with Draco Meteor. Due to how well its unique defensive properties complement its offensive potential, Hisuian Goodra partners particularly well with other special attacking teammates such as Aegislash, Enamorus, and Alakazam, which appreciate its ability to sponge hits from checks such as Celesteela and Scizor, making it easier for these Pokemon to get past them long-term. In return, these Pokemon also assist with patching up Hisuian Goodra's weakness to common physical threats such as Mega Aerodactyl, Life Orb Mienshao, and Swords Dance Rillaboom. Additionally, dedicated physical walls such as Rotom-W, Mega Venusaur, and Buzzwole also appreciate Hisuian Goodra's ability to check problematic special attackers such as Hydrapple and Enamorus that would otherwise take advantage of them. Lastly, due to the value Hisuian Goodra's Knock Off provides, entry hazards from the likes of Skarmory and Swampert synergize especially well with it to help overload opposing defensive staples such as Amoonguss, Hippowdon, and Blissey while benefitting from Hisuian Goodra deterring common Knock Off absorbers such as Clefable and Scizor.

Chople Berry.description:
• Draco Meteor is for Dragon-type Pokemon without defensive items like Haban Berry and Assault Vest, such as Raging Bolt, Dragapult, and non-Choice Specs Kyurem.
  • Heavy Slam deals with Fairy-type Pokemon such as Whimsicott, Diancie, and Primarina.
  • Acid Spray is used to drop Special Defense, and the combination of Acid Spray + Draco Meteor can KO Pokemon like Porygon-Z, non-Assault Vest or non-Choice Specs Volcanion, non-Clear Amulet Pecharunt, and Life Orb Spectrier.
  • Counter is for Pokemon with strong physical moves that don't OHKO Hisuian Goodra, usually Choice Band users like Urshifu-R, Iron Valiant, Chien-Pao, and Meowscarada.
  • Hisuian Goodra's EVs maximize HP so that it can tank a Choice Band Close Combat from Iron Valiant and both Urshifu formes while surviving two +1 Life Orb Hexes from Spectrier after chip damage from burn. Its Attack allows it to always OHKO non-bulky sets of Iron Valiant, with the rest of the EVs in Special Attack.
  • Because of Sap Sipper, Hisuian Goodra can win against SubSeed Pokemon such as Whimsicott, Serperior, and Ogerpon-W.
  • Against Encore + Disable Pokemon like Iron Valiant and Alolan Ninetales, it is necessary to use Heavy Slam turn 1 and switch to Acid Spray on turn 2. Using Acid Spray turn 1 will lose the matchup, as it does not threaten a 2HKO on these foes.
  • Since Hisuian Goodra struggles against Ursaluna, Landorus-T, and Donphan, Pokemon like Primarina, Urshifu-R, and Manaphy make good teammates.

Choice Band.description:
• Choice Band Hisuian Goodra looks to use its inferior but still solid Attack stat to surprise and defeat foes such as Hoopa-U, opposing Hisuian Goodra, and Volcarona.
  • Heavy Slam deals tons of damage to Diancie, Sylveon, and Primarina.
  • Skitter Smack is extremely useful for the Hoopa-U matchup, as it can OHKO even the most bulky variants of it. It's also helpful for non-Focus Blast Iron Crown, as it means it's difficult for Iron Crown to break through.
  • Earthquake hits important threats such as non-Counter Hisuian Goodra, Volcarona, Metagross, and non-Air Balloon Heatran.
  • The EV spread allows Hisuian Goodra to live a Choice Band Hyperspace Fury from Hoopa-U as well as two Life Orb Moonblasts from Primarina.
  • Since Ground- and Fighting-type attacks are quite common in the metagame from Pokemon like Iron Valiant, Haxorus, Ursaluna, and Landorus-T, Pokemon with typings that are quite good against these like Primarina are advised for teammates.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dragon

Hisuian Goodra can use a Dragon-type STAB move like Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse over Dragon Tail to punish foes in the mirror matchup as well as take down Will-O-Wisp Dragapult. However, Draco Meteor is less spammable and makes Hisuian Goodra vulnerable to setup sweepers, while Dragon Pulse can be underwhelming, and both prevent Hisuian Goodra from phazing . Flamethrower is a decent coverage move that can be used over Dragon Tail, allowing Hisuian Goodra to lure Steel-type foes like Corviknight and Skarmory and prevent Nasty Plot Gholdengo from setting up.

Specially Defensive (Steel).description:
Hisuian Goodra is a phenomenal special wall on Steel teams, notably sporting a Water resistance, which is a huge help when it comes to dealing with foes such as Greninja and Primarina. Heavy Slam is an incredible option that allows Hisuian Goodra to provide some offensive pressure, notably hitting Primarina and Flutter Mane. Knock Off allows Hisuian Goodra to remove items from Pokemon that would hope to switch in to take advantage of its passivity, such as Archaludon, Iron Hands, and Clodsire. Dragon Tail pairs excellently with entry hazard-stacking Steel teams, racking up an immense amount of damage over the course of a battle while also being able to force out setup sweepers such as Galarian Moltres and Gholdengo. Protect is a great option to scout which moves common Choice item users such as Excadrill, Meowscarada, and Iron Valiant lock themselves into, allowing a switch to be made accordingly, as well as allowing Hisuian Goodra to recover some HP with Leftovers.

Skarmory is an excellent partner for Hisuian Goodra, as the combination of Spikes, Knock Off, and Dragon Tail works extremely well together. Skarmory can also switch into physical moves directed at Hisuian Goodra, such as Close Combat, while Hisuian Goodra can switch into special moves meant for Skarmory, such as Shadow Ball. Archaludon is another fantastic physical wall to pair with Hisuian Goodra, as defensive sets are able to take on physically oriented attackers that Hisuian Goodra struggles with, such as Ceruledge, Dragonite, and Ogerpon-H. Choice Scarf sets can also surprise and OHKO Fighting-type foes that would otherwise be very troublesome for Hisuian Goodra, such as Urshifu-R with one layer of Spikes and Iron Valiant with Thunderbolt and Flash Cannon, respectively. Iron Treads is a great partner for Hisuian Goodra, as it can Rapid Spin away hazards to ensure Hisuian Goodra can switch in repeatedly. Air Balloon Iron Treads can also come in on Pokemon locked into Ground-type moves such as Landorus and Mamoswine. Gholdengo aids in ensuring entry hazards stay up by denying both Rapid Spin and Defog as well as greatly appreciating the damage Hisuian Goodra racks up over the course of a battle, making endgame cleaning easier. Since Hisuian Goodra is neutral to Fire-type attacks, Heatran can opt for a more offensive set such as Choice Scarf. Hisuian Goodra can use Knock Off to remove items from defensive Pokemon that like to switch in on Heatran, such as recovery items from Toxapex, Clodsire, and Ting-Lu, making Heatran's job of cleaning up easier.

Specially Defensive (Dragon).description:
Hisuian Goodra is a staple on Dragon teams, thanks to its exceptional special bulk and typing, which allows it to tank special Fairy-, Ice-, and Dragon-type moves like Moonblast from Clefable, Ice Beam from Greninja, and Draco Meteor from Dragapult. Heavy Slam allows Hisuian Goodra to hit Fairy-type threats like Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Iron Valiant while denting Calm Mind Primarina and Hatterene to prevent them from setting up. Knock Off permits Hisuian Goodra to remove Leftovers from switch-ins like Corviknight, Ursaluna, Archaludon, and opposing Hisuian Goodra. Dragon Tail is a great phazing move, preventing foes like Nasty Plot Gholdengo, Dragon Dance Dragonite, and Scizor from setting up on Hisuian Goodra. Protect grants Hisuian Goodra a form of passive recovery while also permitting it to scout moves from potentially Choice-locked foes like Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Iron Valiant.

Dragapult is a remarkable teammate for Hisuian Goodra, as it provides a much-needed Fighting immunity, meaning it can comfortably switch into attacks from Barraskewda and Skarmory, which Hisuian Goodra is highly susceptible to, and force them out with the threat of Will-O-Wisp. Dragapult also provides Dragon teams with a high Speed tier, allowing it to use U-turn to pivot into Hisuian Goodra before threatening special attackers like Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Hatterene and Greninja can attack it. In return, Hisuian Goodra hits opposing Dragapult and Skeledirge with Knock Off and switches into Moonblast from Choice Scarf Flutter Mane. Garchomp is an astounding lead for Dragon teams, setting up Stealth Rock and Spikes for Hisuian Goodra, which can use Dragon Tail to force foes to take chip damage from the entry hazards Garchomp sets. Garchomp also handles pesky Steel-type foes like Bisharp and Gholdengo, which Hisuian Goodra isn't very good against, with Earthquake. Choice Band Dragonite provides a much-needed Ground immunity for Hisuian Goodra while also serving as a capable wallbreaker and revenge killer with Choice Band Extreme Speed. In return, Hisuian Goodra can come in on attacks like Ice Beam from Greninja and Freeze-Dry from Articuno, which Garchomp and Dragonite are extremely vulnerable to. Archaludon forms a great defensive core with Hisuian Goodra, as not only do they share their typing, but Archaludon also provides outstanding physical bulk. Hisuian Goodra is highly susceptible to physical attacks from foes like Choice Band Meowscarada, Dragon Darts Dragapult, and Azumarill, which Archaludon can comfortably switch into. Archaludon can also set up Stealth Rock for Dragon teams and threaten foes like Weavile and Bisharp, which Hisuian Goodra can't deal with, with Body Press. In exchange, Hisuian Goodra can easily take on attacks like Moonblast from Flutter Mane and Enamorus and Draco Meteor from Walking Wake and Raging Bolt, which Archaludon cannot survive due to its low special bulk. Choice Specs Kyurem showcases its wallbreaking ability by OHKOing foes that Hisuian Goodra cannot touch, like Swampert, Belly Drum Azumarill, and Ogerpon-W, with Freeze-Dry. Raging Bolt and Walking Wake are also potentially capable wallbreakers, Raging Bolt providing priority with Thunderclap and Walking Wake exterminating threats like Garchomp and Great Tusk with Draco Meteor and Scald, respectively. Roaring Moon and Latios are amazing late-game cleaners, Roaring Moon checking threats like Ceruledge and Choice Scarf Enamorus with Knock Off and Iron Head and Latios denting threats like Keldeo, Great Tusk, and Garchomp with Luster Purge and Draco Meteor. Latias provides Healing Wish support to Dragon teams, allowing Hisuian Goodra to last longer in a game with more special attackers. Both Latios and Latias also provide a Ground immunity thanks to Levitate, which Hisuian Goodra appreciates. Kommo-o is a great teammate, as it can set up Stealth Rock and OHKO threats to Hisuian Goodra like Weavile and Bisharp with Vacuum Wave.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This Pokemon is a new addition to the Regulation D format! If you have any questions or feel it needs more updates, feel free to post here.

For more information on Battle Stadium Singles, vist the format page!

Assault Vest.description:
• Hisuian Goodra's incredible special bulk, typing, and useful immunity to Spore via Sap Sipper make it one of the prime choices for Assault Vest!

  • Flash Cannon versus Heavy Slam: Flash Cannon has great synergy with Acid Spray and is a reliable STAB move in general. While Heavy Slam isn't very useful against heavy targets, it's worth using for OHKOing offensive Flutter Mane, one of the biggest threats in the metagame.

  • Draco Meteor versus Ice Beam: Draco Meteor's power makes switching offensive threats like Urshifu-R into Hisuian Goodra tricky, and it is notable for 2HKOing Dondozo. Ice Beam lets Hisuian Goodra punish important Ground-types.

  • Acid Spray: Acid Spray is a useful wallbreaking tool, capable of making even specially bulky foes like Clodsire risk taking massive damage after the Special Defense drop.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is another way to 2HKO physically defensive Dondozo and OHKO offensive Urshifu-R and pairs very well with Ice Beam in terms of coverage.

  • Earthquake: While not particularly strong, Earthquake is highly recommended for 2HKOing Heatran and 3HKOing opposing Assault Vest Hisuian Goodra, as both of these will wall this set otherwise.

  • Flamethrower: For other Steel-types like Gholdengo and Scizor, Flamethrower will deal much more damage than Earthquake.

  • Modest versus Quiet: The importance of mirror matches makes Modest an appealing option for Hisuian Goodra, but Quiet will ensure that all but the bulkiest Flutter Mane will need to Terastallize to avoid an OHKO from Heavy Slam.

Other Options
  • Surf: Surf is a decent option to hit Ground-types and Heatran with one attack, but Surf will, at best, usually only 3HKO Heatran.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Despite Hisuian Goodra's superb typing, its common weaknesses to Ground and Fighting make Terastallization a valuable route for it.

  • Flying: Tera Flying covers Hisuian Goodra's former weaknesses fantastically, even giving it an out against Fissure Dondozo. This comes at the cost of doing much worse against Iron Bundle, Thundurus-T, Zapdos, and Rotom-W though.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy still gives Hisuian Goodra a vital Fighting resistance, as well as being a good defensive typing in general.

  • Water: Tera Water has good synergy with Sap Sipper, giving Hisuian Goodra a sole weakness to Electric, in addition to gaining a useful Ice resistance against Chien-Pao, at the cost of doing worse against Iron Bundle.

Minor Optimizations
  • Female Gender: If using Heavy Slam, there is a a chance that Hisuian Goodra can become infatuated by the very rare Cute Charm Enamorus, making a female gender very slightly superior.

Armor Press.description:
• Hisuian Goodra's bulk lends itself naturally to boosting its Defense for Body Press, especially with a useful immunity to critical hits that gives it a great matchup against Urshifu formes after Terastallization.

  • Heavy Slam: As Flutter Mane is the most dangerous Special Attacker in the format, Heavy Slam is the best Steel-type STAB move, OHKOing all but the most defensive Flutter Mane if they don't Terastallize.

  • Protect: Protect has good synergy with Leftovers for extra healing, though Urshifu formes can ignore it.

  • Draco Meteor versus Ice Beam: If using a Sassy or Relaxed nature, Draco Meteor can threaten to 2HKO physically defensive Dondozo. Ice Beam, on the other hand, is a safer and stronger option against Landorus-T and Garchomp.

Other Options

  • Rest and Chesto Berry: Rest and Chesto Berry combine to give Hisuian Goodra a great way to restore health, though the combination is only reliable once.

  • Life Dew: Life Dew doesn't restore much health even with Leftovers, but it can help Hisuian Goodra last longer against some physical threats after setting up.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Hisuian Goodra's fantastic typing doesn't make Terastallization a requirement, but it does make setting up against major physical threats like Urshifu-R and Landorus-T much more feasible.

  • Flying: Tera Flying not only covers all of Hisuian Goodra's former weaknesses, but it also means Fissure is no longer an option to break through its boosts from the likes of Dondozo or Ting-Lu. The new weaknesses to Electric and Ice can harm it though, since Electric- and Ice-type coverage moves are commonly special.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy gives Hisuian Goodra shielding from both Urshifu formes without giving it the harmful Electric and Ice weaknesses that Flying does, though it can harm mirror matches against Assault Vest Hisuian Goodra.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD / 4 Spe with Careful or Sassy: This specially defensive spread is Hisuian Goodra's best shot at avoiding a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera Fairy Moonblast, assuming extra Leftovers recovery from Protect.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Impish or Relaxed: Maximum physical bulk means Hisuian Goodra won't check Flutter Mane nearly as well, but it let will let Body Press become a better sweeping tool.

Minor Optimizations

  • Acid Armor: Acid Armor is the best option for boosting Defense due to its higher PP, but it requires Hisuian Sligoo to evolve while knowing the move in either Scarlet or Violet, as it's not able to be relearned by Hisuian Goodra. Shelter is still a viable, albeit strictly inferior, option.

  • Female Gender: While very rare, Heavy Slam being a contact move means Hisuian Goodra does risk of activating Enamorus's Cute Charm, making a female gender a marginally better choice.

Specially Defensive (Dragon).description: Hisuian Goodra's impervious shell shields Dragon teams from special attackers like Tapu Lele and Kyurem! With its immense weight, Heavy Slam crushes key threats on Fairy teams, including Mega Diancie and Tapu Koko. Flamethrower synergizes with Heavy Slam, denting switch-ins like Klefki and Skarmory while also dealing respectable damage to Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Gholdengo. Dragon Tail phazes setup sweepers like Volcarona and Galarian Moltres, which Hisuian Goodra can't meaningfully damage, and weakens Heatran, which would otherwise switch into Hisuian Goodra easily for Steel teams. Alternatively, Toxic puts checks like Porygon2 and Iron Hands on a timer while still allowing Hisuian Goodra to annoy the aforementioned setup sweepers. Sap Sipper is the preferred ability, making Hisuian Goodra a near-perfect check to Celesteela and Ferrothorn, ensuring it always makes progress against Steel teams. Hisuian Goodra is taken advantage of by strong mixed attackers like Iron Valiant and Keldeo and is overwhelmed by most physical attackers, like Urshifu-R and Mega Lopunny. Due to this, teammates that can switch into these threats like Mega Altaria, Mega Latias, and Archaludon are heavily appreciated. These options also cover for Hisuian Goodra's passivity, as they can turn into dangerous wincons against Fighting, Fairy, and Normal teams. Kommo-o and Swords Dance Garchomp deal with Heatran, Archaludon, and Toxapex, which sit on Hisuian Goodra, and in return, Hisuian Goodra takes on Gholdengo, Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, and Choice Scarf Nihilego with ease. Choice Scarf Latias can be considered, as it provides Healing Wish, which gives Hisuian Goodra more longevity, and also deals with Fighting-types like Urshifu-R and Keldeo. Alternatively, Choice Scarf Roaring Moon is serviceable, as it lures and removes items from bulky walls like Porygon2 and Celesteela and pivots in Hisuian Goodra to check these while still being able to outspeed and pick off threats like Mega Lopunny and Iron Valiant.

AcidPress (Dragon).description: Hisuian Goodra is a potent defensive backbone for Dragon teams, as thanks to its great typing and defensive stats, it acts as both a solid check to opposing Dragon-, Fairy-, and Ice-types and a special wall to foes such as Kyurem, Tapu Lele, and Mega Latias. Its IronPress combination also lets it act as a win condition. Protect raises Hisuian Goodra's longevity by letting it heal further with Leftovers and scout for super effective coverage from foes, but Rest can be used instead for further longevity at the cost of even more passivity; this can be mitigated with Chesto Berry, however. Shell Armor prevents foes from breaking past Hisuian Goodra's Defense boosts with a critical hit, but Sap Sipper provides an immunity to Leech Seed from foes such as Ferrothorn, Celesteela, and Mega Venusaur. As Hisuian Goodra can struggle with Fighting- and Ground-types such as Great Tusk, Mega Swampert, and Mega Lopunny, Mega Altaria and Latias make for good partners to check them, making a defensive core with Hisuian Goodra. This Hisuian Goodra set can struggle with Ghost-types such as Gholdengo, Ceruledge, and Mega Sableye, so partners such as Kommo-o, Garchomp, and Roaring Moon mitigate Hisuian Goodra's passivity against them. Roaring Moon in particular can also act as an offensive check to Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Mega Diancie, which can otherwise overwhelm Hisuian Goodra.

Specially Defensive (Steel).description: With access to complementary coverage moves and a Steel typing,Hisuian Goodra has found itself to be an exemplary specially defensive staple for Steel teams. Hisuian Goodra makes use of protect to scout Choice item foes such as Mamoswine and Sneasler while also providing passive recovery via Leftovers. Dragon Tail phazes setup sweepers such as Volcarona and Galarian Moltres and chips Steel-type threats like Heatran. Knock Off removes favored items from bulky switch-ins like Galarian Slowking and Porygon2. Ice Beam removes Ground-type switch-ins like Landorus and Garchomp, while Flamethrower can deal heavy damage to the likes of Ferrothorn, Mega Scizor, and Skarmory. Alternatively, Hisuian Goodra can run Flamethrower alongside Earthquake to decimate the Steel-type matchup and pose a threat to Heatran. Toxic can status the likes of Tornadus-T and Iron Hands, putting them on a timer and allowing Hisuian Goodra to become a great annoyance. With the use of Sap Sipper, Hisuian Goodra can be a great check foes like Celesteela and Ferrothorn attempting to use Leech Seed. Gholdengo has a Fighting immunity, is one of Steel's best checks to entry hazard removal, and mixed Fighting-types like Kommo-o without a boost. Since Hisuian Goodra has a difficult time against Fighting-types, Skarmory and Corviknight are great partners, as they both are neutral to Fighting and immune to Ground, which assists versus the likes of Excadrill and Great Tusk, and provide hazard support along with hazard removal depending on which one you choose. Mega Scizor is a fierce wallbreaker that assists in checking foes likeMega Lopunny and Iron Valiant with a +2 Swords Dance. It's also a decent check to the Ogerpon formes too with moves like Superpower. Choice Scarf Iron Treads provides great speed control and deals with Hisuian Arcanine, Zeraora, and Clodsire for Hisuian Goodra. Iron Treads also provides an Electric immunity, which helps prevent Hisuian Goodra from getting worn down over time in the Electric matchup. Ferrothorn can set hazards, spread residual damage, sponge attacks, and provide an optimal switch-in to Mega Swampert and Ogerpon-W, which it can also threaten back with Power Whip.

ru.overview: Klefki's Prankster and excellent defensive typing make it a versatile support Pokemon. Priority Spikes, multiple resistances, and a good matchup against the tier's entry hazard removers like Cyclizar and Noivern mean it will often be able to set at least one layer per game, making it a useful pick on Spikes-stacking and offensive teams alike. Prankster Thunder Wave deters most setup sweepers and fast Pokemon from taking advantage of its passivity and can neutralize threats to its team such as Terrakion, Entei, and Necrozma. However, Klefki is quite passive, and Pokemon like Reuniclus and Bisharp can shrug off its attacks easily and use it as setup fodder. Outside of Spikes and Thunder Wave, it faces stiff competition from the tier's numerous Steel-types such as Jirachi, Registeel, and Hisuian Goodra; while Jirachi and Registeel are particularly effective at setting up Stealth Rock, all three are capable of offensively threatening opposing teams. Klefki also struggles with four-moveslot syndrome, as it must pick which foes are able to take advantage of it depending on which set it runs.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Klefki can run a slow boosting set with Calm Mind, Iron Defense, and Draining Kiss, functioning as a late-game wincon. With a Bold nature, Dazzling Gleam can be used to OHKO Crawdaunt after entry hazards, 2HKO Krookodile, deal more chip damage to threats like Quagsire and Bisharp, and avoid accuracy issues at the cost of some being worse against Assault Vest Cyclizar. Similarly, a specially defensive spread can be used to let Klefki more consistently switch into the likes of Gardevoir, Noivern, and Slowbro, but all of these foes have ways of circumventing Klefki regardless, such as Trick, Taunt, and Calm Mind. Switcheroo can be used with items such as Toxic Orb and Choice Band; Toxic Orb can cripple walls like Slowbro and potentially steal Leftovers recovery, while Choice Band neutralizes bulky setup sweepers like Slowbro and prevents Pokemon like Porygon-Z from sweeping. 16 Speed EVs can ensure that Klefki outpaces paralyzed Noivern and take it out without risking heavy damages from Super Fang or Flamethrower.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Pokemon like Quagsire, Rhyperior, and can switch into non-Magnet Rise Klefki with impunity and threaten it out or set up their own entry hazards. Magnet Rise Klefki can set up Spikes against Ground-types but still cannot do much damage to them, while Air Balloon can only let it wall them in the short term.

Fire-types: Fire-types like Entei, Ninetales, and Scovillain can OHKO Klefki and take little damage from it, although they don't appreciate being paralyzed.

Bulky Setup Sweepers: Pokemon like Slowbro, Reuniclus, and Suicune don't mind or can avoid being paralyzed and take little damage from Foul Play, using Klefki as easy setup fodder.

Paralysis- or Prankster-immune Pokemon: Klefki's main way to force out opposing Pokemon is the threat of Prankster Thunder Wave. Electric-, Ground-, and Dark-types like Kilowattrel, Magnezone, and Bisharp are immune to this threat and can take advantage of Klefki's poor offensive stats.

Spikes.description:
Set Details

This set focuses on laying Spikes and spreading Paralysis. Thunder Wave cripples offensive threats like Terrakion and discourages setup sweepers like Necrozma and Terrakion from boosting against Klefki. Foul Play targets physical attackers like Jirachi and Mamoswine and also prevents physical wallbreakers such as Necrozma and Feraligatr from setting up. Magnet Rise can be used as an alternative to negate Klefki's Ground-type weakness, allowing it to set up Spikes against Krookodile, Mamoswine, and Rhyperior. Air Balloon allows it to switch into these Ground-types directly, which is particularly useful for checking Choice-locked Ground-types like Mamoswine. Alternatively, Leftovers provides Klefki with its only source of recovery. Rocky Helmet makes Klefki a solid Maushold counter. A physically defensive spread lets it more effectively check the plethora of physical threats like Mimikyu and Jirachi. Tera Ghost lets it wall most Normal- and Fighting-types like Terrakion, Breloom, and Maushold and spinblock Cyclizar.

Klefki typically appears on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate Spikes support. Partners that benefit from Spikes, such as Terrakion, Feraligatr, and Gengar, appreciate their checks being whittled down throughout the match. Knock Off users and pivots, like Cyclizar and Tsareena, help Klefki's Spikes rack up more damage by removing Heavy-Duty Boots and forcing repeated switches. Due to its lack of recovery, Klefki can crumble under chip damage, notably from entry hazards, so Rapid Spin users like Cyclizar and Tsareena can help by removing them while keeping Spikes on the opponent's side of the field. Pokemon that can threaten bulky setup sweepers, like Choice Specs Gengar, alleviate Klefki's propensity to become setup fodder. Pokemon such as Terrakion and Krookodile can form hazard-stacking cores with Klefki to force switches and rack up passive damage.

nu.overview: Klefki is an incredibly crafty support Pokemon, making use of its incredible combination of ability, movepool, and typing to bring mayhem to the battlefield. Klefki's Prankster ability lets it scatter Spikes, spread paralysis with Thunder Wave, summon rain and sun, and even boost its own stats before the foe can act; it's a very malleable Pokemon that can find itself on almost any team due to its supportive capabilities. Klefki's highly coveted Steel / Fairy typing makes it a great sponge for special attacks, taking on the likes of Munkidori, Espeon, and Dragalge while also resisting Knock Off and U-turn. Although Klefki has many tricks up its sleeve, offense is not one of them, since it uses paltry base 80 offensive stats and often relies on Foul Play to not be a complete sitting duck. Any means to circumvent Prankster-affected moves such as Magic Bounce, Dark-types, and Taunt can generally spell doom for Klefki. Dark-types like Incineroar, Wo-Chien, and Overqwil can take advantage of Klefki's inability to status them. Despite Klefki's phenomenal defensive typing, its stats often leave much to be desired, meaning some special wallbreakers like Choice Specs Meloetta and Sylveon can eventually overwhelm it even in spite of a type disadvantage.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Klefki can utilize its Prankster ability to run a Double Dance set; boosting its Defense with Iron Defense and special stats with Calm Mind while maintaining its health with Draining Kiss to turn Stored Power into an unwallable attack. Klefki can sport a Damp Rock or Heat Rock along with Rain Dance or Sunny Day, respectively, to facilitate those respective weather teams. Klefki can use Eject Button or Red Card in tandem with Prankster Recycle to repeatedly pivot itself or its foe out of play. Klefki can hold onto a Toxic Orb, which won't affect it, and use Switcheroo to bestow it onto an unsuspecting target like Espeon, which can otherwise set up on Klefki safely.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Ground-types like Swampert, Flygon, Gligar, and Swampert are immune to Klefki's Prankster Thunder Wave and threaten it with Earthquake, although they must be wary of Magnet Rise.

Bulky Setup Sweepers: Bulky setup sweepers that can take advantage of Klefki's passivity can be a huge issue for it. Calm Mind Pokemon like Sylveon, Chandelure, and Florges take minimal damage from Klefki's attacks and can accrue multiple boosts while it flounders helplessly.

Prankster-immune Pokemon: Many Pokemon that can ignore Klefki's Prankster-affected moves in one way or another can take advantage of Klefki's relative passivity. Magic Bounce Espeon, Dark-types, and Thunder Wave-immune Pokemon like Raikou and Flygon find safe entry against Klefki and threaten it.

Spikes Support.description:
Set Details

Foul Play enables Klefki to hit physical attackers for big damage it'd be unable to achieve using its own Attack stat, hitting Pokemon like Brambleghast and Cinccino. Magnet Rise lets Klefki turn the tables on Ground-types like Flygon, Swampert, and Gligar with the former being weak to Dazzling Gleam. Maximum Special Defense investment lets Klefki deal with powerful special attackers in the tier like Munkidori and Goodra. Tera Water lets Klefki take Fire-type attacks from Chandelure and Infernape in a pinch.
