Klefki's specially bulky nature makes it pair excellently with physical walls on balance teams, it is typically seen with Pokemon like Vaporeon and Swampert, as they can handle Fire-types like Infernape and Incineroar. Ghost-types like Chandelure and Brambleghast can block Rapid Spin to maintain Klefki's entry hazards, as do Defog deterrents like Defiant Braviary and Competitive Kilowattrel. Klefki's Prankster Thunder Wave is great speed control for slow, powerful wallbreakers like Choice Specs Chandelure and Choice Band Flamigo and Guts Heracross.

monotype.overview:
Steel

Klefki can serve as a dual screen-setting lead with entry hazard support for Steel teams. However, Steel teams are usually balanced, and Klefki does not bring much defensive utility or longevity to be beneficial long term. It is mostly outclassed by Skarmory as a Spikes setter and Fighting-neutral Pokemon. Skarmory also provides a valuable Ground-immune and potential as a IronPress setup sweeper. On the other hand, Klefki's role compression with dual screens support can be valuable on more offensive teams.

Dual Screens (Fairy).description:
Klefki is an excellent pick for Fairy teams due to its Prankster dual screens and Spikes support, which enables threats such as Azumarill, Primarina, and Hatterene to set up and sweep. Foul Play allows Klefki to punish setup sweepers such as Scizor and Ogerpon-H while preventing Roaring Moon and Excadrill from setting up completely for free. Alternatively, Thunder Wave cripples fast threats such as Sneasler, Iron Moth, and Flutter Mane. Klefki’s Steel typing blocks Mortal Spin and turns annoying matchups against foes like Alolan Muk into an opportunity to set Spikes. Maximum Defense investment allows Klefki to deal with Scizor, which is an extremely dangerous threat for Fairy teams.

Belly Drum Azumarill greatly appreciates Klefki's dual screens support, as it enables Azumarill to easily set up against threats such as Gholdengo and Alolan Muk. Additionally, Spikes provides chip damage to ensure Azumarill OHKOes Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-C with +6 Aqua Jet. Flutter Mane appreciates Klefki's Spikes support wearing down checks like Hisuian Goodra, Alolan Muk, and Toxapex. In return, Flutter Mane blocks Rapid Spin to keep Klefki's Spikes on the field. Iron Valiant appreciates Klefki's ability to slow down foes such as Flutter Mane, Cinderace, and Sneasler with Thunder Wave. In return, Iron Valiant provides offensive pressure on Steel teams while threatening Defoggers such as Corviknight and Mandibuzz with its wide coverage. Primarina appreciates Klefki's dual screens support, allowing it to set up in the face of Pokemon like Iron Treads and Archaludon. Hatterene and Klefki form a strong defensive core, with Hatterene checking walls such as Clodsire and Toxapex while Klefki deals with Scizor. Hatterene is excellent at punishing entry hazard setters that can freely set hazards against Klefki like Ting-Lu and Skarmory. Klefki's dual screens support allows Hatterene to easily take on Pokemon such as Ting-Lu, Toxapex, and Clodsire by serving as a wincon with Calm Mind. Clefable is an excellent teammate, as the two can form an entry hazard-stacking core with Spikes and Stealth Rock. As Klefki is vulnerable to Ground-type attacks, Enamorus makes a great ally.

Dual Screens (Steel).description:
Klefki is a niche choice for Steel teams that brings Prankster dual screens and Spikes to the table, allowing it to serve as a lead and support setup sweepers such as Gholdengo and Iron Crown. Foul Play can be used to punish Dragon Dance sweepers such as Dragonite while also preventing Klefki from being complete setup fodder to Dark- and Ground-types such as Roaring Moon and Excadrill. Thunder Wave can be used instead to hinder fast threats and special setup sweepers such as Cinderace, Flutter Mane, and Volcarona, aiding sweepers that would otherwise be slower.

Gholdengo is one of Klefki's best teammates, as it blocks Defog from Corviknight and Mandibuzz and Rapid Spin from Great Tusk and Terapagos. This is essential in maintaining the progress Klefki makes. Gholdengo also benefits greatly from dual screen supports, as this eases setting up Nasty Plot on otherwise irritating foes such as Flutter Mane and Alolan Muk. Iron Crown, Excadrill, and Scizor also appreciate the dual screens support from Klefki, which eases setup, while the former can more easily activate Weakness Policy without getting KOed by hits such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball and Life Orb Landorus's Earth Power. Klefki cannot check threats such as Bisharp, Volcarona, and Landorus, so defensive stalwarts such as Archaludon, Heatran, and Corviknight are essential. In addition, Corviknight can serve as a Bulk Up wincon or as a valuable U-turn pivot for setup sweepers. Klefki cannot prevent entry hazards from being set by setters such as Ting-Lu and Skarmory, so Rapid Spin support from Iron Treads and Excadrill is valuable.

Iron Defense + Calm Mind (Steel).description: This is a sample set as we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Screen Setter (Fairy).description: Klefki is the ideal dual screens setter on Fairy due to its Steel typing, which negates Poison-type attacks from Nihilego and Alolan Muk and ability to fend off threats like Mega Scizor with Foul Play. Klefki is a better option than Grimmsnarl due to its typing and ability to set up Spikes, which, like its screens, go up quickly with Prankster. This support allows for Pokemon like Tapu Bulu and Azumarill from setting up and sweeping, teams. Foul Play prevents Pokemon like Mega Scizor and Mimikyu to set up and sweep while Thunder Wave cripples foes and allows Mega Diancie to outspeed threats such as +1 Mega Charizard X and Nihilego, which will normally beat Klefki one on one. Setting up Spikes creates solid chip damage on Alolan Muk and Gholdengo, allowing for late-game sweeping from its teammates Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele. Mega Diancie punishes opponents trying to set up entry hazards against Klefki and beats Fire-types such as Heatran and Mega Charizard Y. Tapu Bulu helps Klefki with Grassy Terrain, which halves the damage it takes from Earthquake, making Pokemon such as Iron Treads and Mamoswine not hit as hard.

nu.overview: Avalugg's exceptional physical bulk and access to Rapid Spin and Recover make it one of the best physical walls in the tier for balanced and defensive teams. Avalugg can comfortably take some of the most powerful physical attacks in the tier, such as Basculegion-M's Wave Crash and Staraptor's Brave Bird, as well as super effective attacks from Fighting-types such as Infernape and Paldean Tauros-W. Avalugg can also dish out serious damage by weaponizing its Defense stat with Body Press and hitting hard with moves like Avalanche and Earthquake, thanks to its high Attack stat. However, Avalugg is extremely frail on the special side, which allows special wallbreakers such as Munkidori and Dudunsparce to easily force it out. Avalugg's Ice typing makes it weak to common physical wallbreakers in the tier like Incineroar, Paldean Tauros-F, and Flamigo and heavily reliant on Terastallization to wall many physical threats. Avalugg is also very susceptible to Knock Off, since it relies on Heavy-Duty Boots to circumvent its Stealth Rock weakness.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Running IronPress allows Avalugg to become a very threatening sweeper. However, this forces Avalugg to drop a coverage option or Rapid Spin, the former making Avalugg unable to hit Ghost-types, while the latter significantly reduces its utility. Tera Fighting removes Avalugg's weaknesses and makes Avalugg more offensively threatening. Tera Fighting also lets Avalugg resist Stealth Rock, allowing it to switch in more frequently if its Heavy-Duty Boots is removed.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Special attackers, such as Chandelure, Inteleon, and Munkidori, pose a major threat to Avalugg, since it cannot handle their attacks very well. However, Sturdy can help mitigate this issue by allowing Avalugg to deal damage to special wallbreakers for its partners when necessary.

Fire- and Fighting-type Wallbreakers: Powerful physical attackers such as Incineroar, Paldean Tauros-F, Heracross, and Flamigo threaten Avalugg with their strong STAB moves, forcing it out. Avalugg's sheer bulk allows it to take one hit from even super effective attackers, these Pokemon often run Choice Band or Swords Dance sets, preventing Avalugg from safely switching in and beating them.

Item Displacement: Avalugg's Ice typing means it requires Heavy-Duty Boots to consistently switch in. Avalugg must use Recover more often if Knock Off users like Incineroar and Ambipom or Trick users remove its Heavy-Duty Boots, making it harder for Avalugg to consistently remove entry hazards and wall important foes.

Physical Wall.description:
Set Details

Body Press utilizes Avalugg's Defense stat to threaten 2HKOs or 3HKOs on most offensive threats while hitting bulky Steel-types for super effective damage. Body Press also threatens attackers such as Tera Steel Flygon and Incineroar. Since Avalugg is slower than nearly the entire metagame, Avalanche is a great STAB option. However, Ice Spinner can sometimes be preferable for more consistent damage and can remove Terrain, which helps Avalugg and its team against Psychic Terrain offense teams. Earthquake deals super effective damage to Fire-, Poison-, and Electric-type wallbreakers that try to take advantage of Avalugg, such as Chandelure, Munkidori, and Raikou. Sturdy allows Avalugg to always survive a single attack in a pinch and retaliate. Tera Poison gives Avalugg a great defensive typing, providing it with a resistance to Fighting and making it immune to poison and Toxic, which would otherwise cripple it, from Bellibolt and Amoonguss. Alternatively, Tera Water grants Avalugg important resistances to Fire, Steel, and Water, letting it better withstand attacks from threats like Incineroar, Copperajah, and Basculegion-M.

Avalugg's entry hazard control and high Defense is appreciated by many teamstyles from balance to stall. However, Avalugg's abysmal Special Defense means that it benefits greatly from blanket special walls such as Bronzong, Chansey, and Porygon2, which can switch into the many special attackers that force Avalugg out like Dudunsparce, Sylveon, and Chandelure. Fire- and Fighting-type wallbreakers like Paldean Tauros-F, Flamigo, and Infernape can overwhelm Avalugg, meaning Pokemon that can switch into their attacks, such as Chandelure, Gligar, and Amoonguss, are good partners. Avalugg struggles to threaten Ghost-types like Chandelure with its attacks, especially if it lacks Earthquake, making Dark-types such as Incineroar good partners for it. These two can also burn and poison wallbreakers, making it much easier for Avalugg to outlast them. Water-types, such as Vaporeon, Basculegion-M, and Inteleon can pose a huge problem for Avalugg, as they have strong special attacks and are difficult to switch out of due to the risk of Vaporeon's Scald burning an incoming Pokemon, Basculegion-M's Adaptability boosting its STAB attacks, and Inteleon's U-turn giving it momentum. Water-immune Pokemon such as Vaporeon and Toxicroak can help immensely, while status-immune wallbreakers, such as Facade Braviary and Guts users like Heracross as well as Hariyama, can force them out or set up on them. Alolan Ninetales outspeeds many Fighting-type wallbreakers that threaten Avalugg, such as Flamigo and Paldean Tauros-W and can KO them with Moonblast. It also sets snow for Avalugg, boosting its Defense considerably. In return, Avalugg can draw in and dent Steel-type walls, such as Duraludon and Copperajah, which are difficult for Alolan Ninetales to get past, by using Body Press and Earthquake.

Physically Defensive.description:
Thanks to its sky-high Defense stat, reliable recovery, and excellent utility, Avalugg is a useful defensive piece on Ice teams. It can check physical attackers with great efficiency, in addition to being one of Ice teams' best answers to Barraskewda under rain. Rapid Spin allows Avalugg to clear entry hazards for teammates such as Kyurem and Alolan Ninetales. Body Press allows it to threaten dangerous threats like Scizor and Hisuian Arcanine. Iron Defense works excellently with Body Press, and Avalugg finds plenty of setup opportunities under Aurora Veil and snow. This turns it into a potent wincon against Fighting and Dark teams once checks such as Iron Valiant and Darkrai have been removed. Avalanche can be used instead to deal massive damage to Flying-types like Gliscor and Dragonite and prevent them from setting up on Avalugg. This move also prevents Avalugg from being completely walled by Ghost teams. With Mirror Coat, Heavy-Duty Boots, and Sturdy, Avalugg can be a reliable emergency answer to any snowballing special threats such as Volcarona and Flutter Mane.

Avalugg walls physical threats best with snow and Aurora Veil support. Therefore, Alolan Ninetales is a perfect teammate. In addition, Alolan Ninetales can threaten Keldeo and Kommo-o for Avalugg, while it can switch into and threaten Scizor for Alolan Ninetales. Avalugg is a complete liability against Ghost-type threats, as Gholdengo and Hisuian Zoroark are able to easily set up on it. Therefore, Weavile makes a strong ally to deal with Ghost teams. Similarly, Avalugg struggles to do much to Fire- and Poison-type targets such as Heatran and Okidogi. Mamoswine makes a great teammate, as it can tank hits from these foes while threatening them back with Earthquake. Cloyster is also a great because it can offensively threaten Fire teams after a Shell Smash. Avalugg cannot beat opposing physical walls such as Toxapex and Skarmory. Kyurem makes an excellent teammate, as it is able to remove these walls for it.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Sturdy Support.description:
• With incredible Defense and the ability Sturdy, Avalugg finds a niche on stall-based teams as a physical wall that prevents fishing for OHKOs.

  • Icicle Crash versus Avalanche: While Avalanche has bigger damage potential when Avalugg is attacked head on, its defensive profile normally forces switches. This makes Icicle Crash the more consistent option for overall damage.

  • Toxic Support Partners: Even though Avalugg stops foes such as Dondozo from using Fissure, it lacks the power to cleanly beat these targets on its own. Common stall teammates such as Toxapex and Clodsire can bring Toxic or Toxic Spikes to spread status, allowing Avalugg to simply stall while poison wears down the opposition.

  • EV Spread: Full investment into HP and Defense give Avalugg insane physical bulk. Even Choice Band Chien-Pao’s Sacred Sword isn’t a reliable 2HKO!

Other Options
  • Mirror Coat: Combined with Sturdy, Mirror Coat is a tempting last resort against the special attackers that Avalugg can’t wall. However, this almost assuredly destroys Avalugg’s survivability afterwards, which can compromise the defensive cycle of its team.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Situational: Most commonly a member of stall-based teams, Avalugg’s bad matchups are supposed to be covered by the team’s defensive cycle. Tera is normally only used if it is necessary to prevent the collapse of said defensive cycle.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting balances offense and defense, making Tera Dark targets like Urshifu-S and Choice Band Chien-Pao much easier to deal with while giving a sizable boost to Avalugg’s best attack in Body Press.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy provides both a Fighting- and Dark-type resistance, making it the best defensive type into Urshifu-S. Furthermore, it doesn't have the Flying-type weakness of Tera Fighting, so Tera Flying Dragonite and Landorus-T are still manageable.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost lets Avalugg escape from precarious situations against trapping moves and Gothitelle. It also outright walls Close Combat from the likes of Iron Hands and Iron Valiant, although the new Dark-type weakness significantly worsens its matchup with Chien-Pao.

Items

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: Since Avalugg can expect to do a lot of switching, removing its vulnerability to Stealth Rock damage is extremely important for its longevity and preservation of Sturdy.

  • Rocky Helmet: Avalugg can punish many physical attackers it switches into with Rocky Helmet chip, slowly wearing them down without having to be offensively involved.

Offensive.description:
Thanks to its impressive bulk and monstrous Attack, Hisuian Avalugg finds itself a place in PU as a reliable entry hazard lead, setting itself apart from other options such as Lycanroc and Froslass by eking out extra turns through the combination of Custap Berry and Sturdy. Mountain Gale threatens a multitude of common leads such as Mudsdale and Bombirdier with high damage. Body Press capitalizes on Hisuian Avalugg's gargantuan Defense to punish Steel-types like Alolan Sandslash that it may otherwise struggle with. Alternatively, Stone Edge can be used to deal extra damage to targets like Cramorant and Coalossal while dealing considerable damage to offensive Fire-types such as Rotom-H, Arcanine, and Hisuian Typhlosion. Rapid Spin offers additional role compression and pairs well with Hisuian Avalugg's ability to victimize most common hazard setters, sometimes even letting it remove the opponent's hazards permanently at the beginning of the match. It also gives Hisuian Avalugg some utility outside of being a dedicated lead, although using Hisuian Avalugg for this purpose is generally not optimal, as the damage from opposing hazards breaks Sturdy and makes Hisuian Avalugg exceptionally more vulnerable to opposing wallbreakers. 0 Special Defense IVs in combination with a Naughty nature can be used to ensure that opposing special attackers will nearly always trigger Sturdy, although it is generally not necessary due to Hisuian Avalugg's pitiful Special Defense. Loaded Dice can be used in tandem with Icicle Spear and Rock Blast for increased reliability and getting around Focus Sash leads, though it's worse against foes like Mudsdale and Cramorant and can limit what Hisuian Avalugg gets done on average. Tera Ghost further compounds Hisuian Avalugg's utility by making it immune to Rapid Spin, allowing it to keep hazards up in a pinch against Tatsugiri and Coalossal, while also removing its crippling weaknesses to Fighting and Steel, making it much more effective against foes such as Toxicroak and Copperajah. However, this should be done sparingly, as it is often more ideal to Terastallize more offensive teammates such as Decidueye and Arcanine.

Hisuian Avalugg fits exclusively on hyper offense teams that appreciate its ability to reliably set entry hazards and punish foes for attempting to do so. However, due to the nature of being a hazard lead, it will often faint rather quickly and have few — if any — opportunities to set Stealth Rock again. Therefore, Taunt users like Skuntank and Bombirdier as well as Ghost-types like Decidueye that can stop attempts at hazard removal are highly valuable. Knock Off users such as Zoroark, Skuntank, and Bombirdier are also valuable thanks to their ability to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes, ensuring that Hisuian Avalugg's hazards will be effective. In addition, teammates such as Arcanine and Minior appreciate Hisuian Avalugg's ability to remove hazards, allowing them to utilize items such as Leftovers and White Herb. Pokemon like Scrafty, Toxtricity, and Arcanine also greatly appreciate Hisuian Avalugg's ability to threaten and remove foes like Gligar and Mudsdale that are otherwise extreme nuisances while also being able to act as an emergency stopgap against revenge killers like Flamigo. Powerful wallbreakers such as Delphox and the Paldean Tauros formes also greatly appreciate Hisuian Avalugg's consistency in setting Stealth Rock, further lowering the number of times that Pokemon like Milotic and Florges can switch into their STAB moves.

ru.overview: Noivern swoops into RU as a premier speedy Pokemon that can fill both offensive and defensive roles. Due to Noivern's resistance to common offensive types like Fire, Water, and Fighting, it can be a great defensive sponge by switching into both special and physical attackers such as Volcanion and Gallade. It can then use this opportunity to remove entry hazards with Defog, chunk a switch-in with either Super Fang or Draco Meteor, or pivot on switch-ins with U-turn. It can outspeed and force out Pokemon such as Cyclizar, Gengar, and Raikou, threatening them with Draco Meteor. Noivern can keep itself healthy with Roost, allowing it to come in multiple times per game in order to do its job. However, Noivern struggles with common Choice Scarf users such as Gardevoir and Galarian Zapdos, as they can outspeed and deal massive damage to it. Noivern can also struggle a lot with Fairy-types such as Mimikyu and Gardevoir, which can switch into its main STAB option in Draco Meteor and hit it super effectively. Noivern also immensely struggles with bulky Pokemon such as Umbreon, Jirachi, and Registeel, as they can easily switch into it and either make progress against it or set up on it.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Choice Specs with Boomburst and Tera Normal is an option on Noivern, allowing it to do massive damage to the opposing team once Steel- and Ghost-types have been removed. Switcheroo can be used alongside Choice Specs to cripple defensive Pokemon that Noivern can't break through, such as Chansey or Empoleon. Air Slash is a much more reliable STAB option than Hurricane, though it is much weaker and can fail to 2HKO even Pokemon with mediocre special bulk like Krookodile.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Fairy-types such as Gardevoir and Tera Fairy users like Armarouge and Cresselia are massive pains for Noivern, as they can switch into its main STAB option in Draco Meteor. Mimikyu in particular is extremely irritating for defensive Noivern, as it is immune to both Draco Meteor and Super Fang, meaning it can switch into any defensive Noivern set lacking Hurricane or Psychic Noise without taking any damage and threaten it out.

Steel-types: Noivern can struggle against Steel-types such as Jirachi, Magnezone, and Empoleon, since they can switch into Draco Meteor easily, only really fearing Flamethrower.

Choice Scarf Users and Priority: Common Choice Scarf users such as Gardevoir, Gengar, and Galarian Zapdos can outspeed Noivern and threaten it immensely. Priority users such as Bisharp, and especially Mamoswine, can do big damage to Noivern.

Umbreon: Umbreon is a big pain for Noivern, as Umbreon can easily take its attacks, use Wish to heal off its damage, and threaten it with Toxic. Taunt can prevent Umbreon from using Toxic against Noivern, but Foul Play still forces Noivern to use Roost repeatedly.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Set Details

Draco Meteor provides Noivern with tremendous breaking power, though it does allow Fairy-types such as Gardevoir safe entry points against it; alternatively, Hurricane can be used to hit these Fairy-types, though they are quite scarce and it comes at the cost of less immediate power and unreliable accuracy. Flamethrower melts the pesky Steel-types that resist Noivern's STAB attacks, like Jirachi, Magnezone, and Registeel. U-turn can be used to form VoltTurn cores and provide safe pivots into teammates like Galarian Zapdos; Taunt is an alternative move that can stop setup attempts from Pokemon like Reuniclus and Slowbro, recovery attempts, and entry hazard stacking from walls like Gastrodon and Hippowdon. Roost gives Noivern the longevity needed to stick around and dish out damage while checking big threats like Basculegion-F and Volcanion. Frisk can be used to scout for items, such as Choice items on Pokemon like Mamoswine and Gengar. Infiltrator allows Noivern to hit Pokemon that use Substitute, such as Raikou and Suicune, to prevent them from using Calm Mind freely. Tera Steel can be used to flip the weakness to Dragon, which helps against Hisuian Goodra and opposing Noivern, while providing valuable resistances to Fairy-type attacks from Gardevoir and Cresselia. Tera Fire also provides a Fairy resistance and can bolster the damage of Flamethrower, allowing Noivern to break through Jirachi and Magnezone more effectively. Tera Fairy provides a Dragon immunity, which helps against Cyclizar and opposing Noivern, while maintaining the Bug and Fighting resistances to still check Mienshao. Tera Fairy also provides a key resistance to Dark-type attacks like Knock Off and Sucker Punch, making matchups into Bisharp and Krookodile more comfortable. Tera Water is a fine pick for Noivern, as it maintains the Fire and Water resistances to check Volcanion while providing an Ice resistance to more effectively deal with Mamoswine.

Offensive pivot Noivern is a great choice on balance and bulky offense teams that need to shore up their matchups into one of the biggest threats in the tier, Volcanion. Teammates like Talonflame are much appreciated, as they can provide entry hazard removal and check physical attackers like Bisharp and Galarian Zapdos, threatening to burn either with Flame Body or Will-O-Wisp. In return, Noivern can check Volcanion for Talonflame. Physical wallbreakers that can use the safe entry points provided by U-turn Noivern, such as Crawdaunt and Mamoswine, are valuable to help break through walls such as Chansey and Hisuian Goodra, making Noivern more imposing with its own strong attacks. Noivern appreciates its own hazard support from teammates like Hippowdon and Jirachi, which can help rack up chip damage while Noivern uses either U-turn to pivot between teammates or Taunt to prevent recovery. Noivern is a great member of VoltTurn cores, partnering with powerful wallbreakers like Magnezone and Mienshao to keep the opposition from getting comfortable. Steel-type teammates like Empoleon, Jirachi, and Registeel are valuable to check Dragon- and Fairy-types that can threaten Noivern, like Hisuian Goodra, Alolan Ninetales, and Gardevoir.

Bulky Support.description:
Set Details

Draco Meteor allows Noivern to dent naturally bulky Pokemon such as Slowbro and Hippowdon even without Special Attack investment. Hurricane can be used over Draco Meteor; however, it is less reliable and doesn't threaten Cyclizar as much. Super Fang allows Noivern to make incredible progress against common switch-ins like Jirachi and Registeel. Taunt allows that damage to stick, preventing recovery attempts from Pokemon such as Empoleon and Umbreon while also preventing Thunder Wave from the likes of Slowbro. Defog provides excellent team support, preventing teammates from being chipped by entry hazards. Psychic Noise prevents any form of recovery and does decent damage to Pokemon such as Gastrodon and Volcanion, though it notably fails against Umbreon. Roost allows Noivern to stay healthy throughout a game to make more progress with a combination of Super Fang and Taunt or Psychic Noise. Tera Steel turns Noivern's Fairy-type weakness into a resistance, allowing it to check threats such as Gardevoir and Cresselia. Tera Fairy gives it a Dark-type resistance and a Dragon-type immunity, allowing it to emergency check threats such as Choice Scarf Krookodile and Choice-locked Hisuian Goodra in a pinch. Tera Water allows Noivern to check Mamoswine and Alolan Ninetales as well, while retaining the ability to check Fire- and Water-types such as Volcanion and Barraskewda.

Noivern fits well on balance and bulky offense teams, working as a crucial defensive piece and checking Pokemon like Volcanion. It loves partnering with entry hazard setters such as Hippowdon, Krookodile, Chesnaught, and Quagsire to further suffocate foes with Taunt or Psychic Noise. Noivern also partners well with Reuniclus, as they form a tough Fighting-resistant core that wears the opponent down with entry hazards and Psychic Noise. It also loves partnering with Steel-type Pokemon such as Jirachi and Registeel, checking common Fire- and Fighting- types like Volcanion and Mienshao for them, while they cover its Ice and Fairy weaknesses. Choice Scarf users like Gardevoir, Krookodile, and Galarian Zapdos enjoy Noivern's ability to chip the opposition so that they can clean up with ease. Fighting-types like Mienshao and Galarian Zapdos enjoy Noivern's ability to batter away at Fighting-resistant foes like Gardevoir. Similarly, special attackers like Armarouge and Gengar really enjoy Taunt Noivern's ability to shut down Umbreon. Rotom-H and Slowbro are great teammates that check Mamoswine, one of the biggest threats to Noivern.

monotype.overview:
Dragon

Noivern is heavily outclassed both offensively and defensively by fellow Dragon-types like Latios and Archaludon, which can put far more pressure on opposing teams. However, Noivern comes packing with a useful Flying typing and, more importantly, a crucial Speed tier, outspeeding targets like Iron Valiant, which Latios cannot, along with being one of the only answers to entry hazards Dragon teams have.

Utility (Dragon).description:
Noivern finds a niche on Dragon teams thanks to its blazing Speed stat, allowing it to blitz past threats such as Iron Valiant and non-Choice Scarf Greninja, along with having access to Defog to provide a form of entry hazard removal. Hurricane allows it to check Fighting-types like Iron Valiant, Sneasler, and Gallade with ease. U-turn provides fast pivoting, allowing safe entry for setup sweepers. Alternatively, Flamethrower can be used to allow Noivern to threaten Steel- and Ice-types like Gholdengo, Skarmory, and Froslass, while Draco Meteor provides another strong offensive tool, which can prove useful in the mirror matchup. A defensive EV spread is preferred, allowing Noivern to stick around reliably throughout a game, as it can take two Dark Pulses from Hydreigon and a Power Gem from Glimmora. Alternatively, it can run an offensive spread to assuredly OHKO targets like Latios and the Ogerpon formes.

Archaludon can take on powerful physical Ice- and Rock-type attackers that threaten Noivern such as Weavile, Cloyster, Kleavor, and Iron Boulder and can respond with Flash Cannon. Archaludon can also support Noivern by using Thunder Wave to allow Noivern to outspeed Meowscarada. Hisuian Goodra, meanwhile, can take on special Dragon- and Fairy-types like Hex Dragapult, Kyurem, Flutter Mane, and Primarina. Hisuian Goodra can also switch into special Ice-type attacks from foes like Greninja and Kyurem, which Noivern is highly susceptible to. Both Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra appreciate Noivern's hazard removal, allowing them to get the most out of their Leftovers and giving them a chance to come in repeatedly. Dragapult provides an incredible Speed tier, being able to handle threats such as Flutter Mane and Latios. Choice Specs Latios and Kyurem can deal with foes attempting to make use of Noivern's passivity like Gliscor and Raging Bolt while also being extremely significant in the mirror matchup, allowing Noivern to forego Draco Meteor. Garchomp provides an Electric immunity and a Rock resistance, which makes it capable of taking on threats like Regieleki, Hisuian Arcanine, and Iron Boulder.

Offensive Pivot.description: Investment in defense helps it stomach a hit from Choice Scarf Zarude. Can go max max offensive too.

Specially Offensive.description:
• Yveltal's amazing STAB combination, which is only resisted by Zacian-C and niche Pokemon like Mega Diancie, in conjunction with Life Orb makes it a potent wallbreaker and stallbreaker for balance, bulky offense, and hyper offense teams alike. This is to the point where it is deemed mandatory on Sticky Web teams due to its efficiency and role compression as a source of priority and strong damage dealer as well as its sheer versatility with its movepool and Terastallization options.

  • Yveltal's Speed tier outside of Sticky Web is also fantastic, outspeeding the majority of the defensive metagame including Pokemon such as Primal Groudon, Zygarde, and Ho-Oh and only being outsped by Calm Mind Arceus formes and Eternatus.

  • It also carries useful defensive traits against Pokemon such as Ultra Necrozma, Deoxys-A, and Marshadow, despite it being weak to Stealth Rock. This makes it more flexible compared to other wallbreakers like Rayquaza and the aforementioned Deoxys-A, which rely much more on pivot support and revenge killing opportunities; this is all while simultaneously being good against opposing offense teams and not being prediction reliant.

  • Oblivion Wing provides Yveltal with a source of longevity, making up for its Stealth Rock weakness and the Life Orb recoil it takes while being useful against foes such as Marshadow, Alomomola, Arceus-Fairy, and Arceus-Dark, with Oblivion Wing being needed to beat the latter two under Sticky Web.

  • Taunt is mandatory on Yveltal, since it allows it to make progress much more easily by punishing more passive Pokemon such as Coil Zygarde, Ferrothorn, and Alomomola. This lets it avoid status conditions such as paralysis and Toxic poison while preventing any setup opportunities from Zygarde, Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Ground, and Zacian-C. It also ensures that entry hazards such as Sticky Web stay up against common Defog users such as defensive Ho-Oh and Giratina-O, especially with Tera Fire for the former to resist Sacred Fire.

  • Sucker Punch allows Yveltal to revenge kill Ultra Necrozma after a single layer of Spikes, Deoxys-A, and Mega Mewtwo Y, making Yveltal good at handling opposing offense teams.

  • Knock Off allows for better wallbreaking against balance and stall teams, notably removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Ho-Oh and opposing defensive Yveltal alongside removing Eviolite from Chansey, all of which Yveltal's teammates can take advantage of.

  • Heat Wave should only be used with Tera Fire and on Sticky Web teams, but it allows Yveltal to snipe Zacian-C, removing one of Yveltal's sturdy checks, but it is significantly less useful than the other two options otherwise.

  • A Naive nature is preferred over Hasty on the first EV spread, since it allows Yveltal to withstand pressure from Marshadow more reliably. It also allows Yveltal to avoid an OHKO from Deoxys-A's Rock Slide even after Stealth Rock chip damage.

  • The secondary EV spread allows Yveltal to avoid several OHKO rolls including Choice Band Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent, Zacian-C's Wild Charge, and Choice Specs Lunala's Moonblast; uninvested Arceus-Fairy's Judgment and defensive Primal Groudon's Overheat after one round of Life Orb recoil; and defensive Primal Kyogre's Ice Beam after Stealth Rock chip damage and one round of Life Orb recoil. This is all while still outspeeding base-95 Speed Pokemon such as Rayquaza and Kyurem-B with a Timid nature, at the cost of not outspeeding Lunala anymore. A Modest nature is not encouraged since outspeeding Rayquaza on Sticky Web teams, as well as maximum Speed Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre, Kyurem-B, and Zekrom outside of Sticky Web, is heavily important for Yveltal's effectiveness as a wallbreaker.

  • Tera Dark is the primary Tera type on Yveltal, bringing its damage to all new heights. It notably lets Yveltal OHKO Eruption Primal Groudon and Rayquaza and 2HKO defensive Primal Kyogre and Ho-Oh, all with Dark Pulse. It also lets Yveltal more reliably OHKO Ultra Necrozma with Sucker Punch, which is necessary for the second EV spread, as it runs a Timid nature. Tera Dark also removes Yveltal's weakness to Stealth Rock, giving it more longevity despite struggling slightly more against Marshadow, since it no longer takes neutral damage from Low Kick.

  • Tera Flying boosts the power of Oblivion Wing, letting Yveltal 2HKO Arceus-Fairy after Stealth Rock and defensive Yveltal as well as have a small chance to 2HKO Calm Mind Arceus-Dark after Stealth Rock, thus allowing it to muscle through these Arceus formes under Sticky Web. Removing the Dark-type from Yveltal is especially useful to punish Arceus-Fairy harder, although Yveltal no longer resists Ghost-type attacks from Marshadow and Lunala.

  • Tera Fire lets Heat Wave OHKO Zacian-C while letting Yveltal more safely deal with defensive Ho-Oh and the aforementioned Arceus-Fairy. This arguably makes Tera Fire the best Terastallization option for Sticky Web teams, since Yveltal is strong enough without Tera Dark, although it does not let Yveltal quickly muscle through Arceus-Fairy like Tera Flying does. Tera Fire must only be used on Sticky Web teams, however, since that's the only situation where Heat Wave is useful, and beating Ho-Oh and Arceus-Fairy is only worth exhausting Terastallization for when Yveltal is encouraged to use Taunt to maintain Sticky Web against the former and it is able to outspeed and use Taunt against the latter to win the one-on-one.

  • It is ideal to avoid status conditions as much as possible, especially since Yveltal has poor longevity. Toxic from Eternatus and defensive Arceus-Dark reduces Yveltal's longevity drastically, while Oblivion Wing struggles to make up for it. Paralysis from Zygarde and Giratina-O means Yveltal cannot outspeed bulky targets anymore, notably Primal Groudon, Ho-Oh, and Zygarde. Burns from Ho-Oh and Giratina-O drastically weaken Sucker Punch, notably preventing it from OHKOing Mega Mewtwo Y and Ultra Necrozma, even with Tera Dark, although this weakness is heavily mitigated for Tera Fire variants.

  • Outside of hyper offense teams, Yveltal works best early-to-mid game, where it is able to break through physically defensive walls such as Primal Groudon and Zygarde for its teammates. While it appreciates pivot support from Pokemon such as Alomomola and Landorus-T, Yveltal can be used aggressively against moves it is immune to, such as Primal Groudon's Precipice Blades and Lunala's Psyshock; this is extremely risky, however, and it is not ideal to do this frequently since Yveltal is easy to KO with Overheat from Primal Groudon or Moonblast from Lunala, with both OHKOing after one round of Life Orb damage.

  • On Sticky Web teams, wallbreaking is Yveltal's main purpose, and so it should be used early-game to break through physically defensive walls such as Primal Groudon and Zygarde while maintaining Sticky Web and other hazards against Defog users such as Giratina-O and Ho-Oh with Taunt.

  • Against teams with Ultra Necrozma, Deoxys-A, and Mega Mewtwo Y, it is necessary to preserve Sucker Punch Yveltal in order to revenge kill these threats and prevent them from getting out of hand. If Yveltal is running Knock Off instead, not only is it important to run another form of priority, such as Marshadow's Shadow Sneak, but Yveltal may want to play more aggressively with double switches to stop these threats from setting up safely as well as to wallbreak harder against defensive cores including Ho-Oh, Eternatus, and Zygarde.

  • Yveltal is walled by Calm Mind Arceus-Dark, Arceus-Fairy, defensive Eternatus, and Fezandipiti. On hyper offense and bulky offense teams, Behemoth Blade Zacian-C handles all four of these and checks Extreme Killer Arceus, which would otherwise easily revenge kill Yveltal after Life Orb chip damage. Zacian-C appreciates Yveltal breaking through Primal Groudon and Dondozo for it in return.

  • Sticky Web support from Smeargle or Shuckle helps Yveltal prevent Calm Mind Arceus-Dark from setting up on it, letting Yveltal beat it and even Arceus-Fairy as well with Tera Flying or Fire one-on-one. Smeargle also removes Stealth Rock with Mortal Spin or Rapid Spin, assisting in Yveltal's longevity.

  • Meteor Beam Eternatus is able to break past Arceus-Fairy and opposing Eternatus and snipe Ho-Oh with Meteor Beam while appreciating Yveltal breaking through Necrozma-DM. Finally, Chi-Yu can help overwhelm common checks with Yveltal, such as Arceus-Fairy and Eternatus; it too has Taunt to maintain Sticky Web.

  • On bulky offense and balance teams, Primal Groudon is a great partner, since it appreciates Yveltal breaking past Zygarde and Giratina-O for it and Primal Groudon can check Arceus-Fairy, Zacian-C, and defensive Primal Kyogre while supporting Yveltal with entry hazards. Offensive Ho-Oh is a similar case, checking Arceus-Fairy and Arceus-Dark, and it helps deal with Yveltal's weakness to Stealth Rock with Defog support while potentially weakening foes such as Eternatus with Thunder Wave for Yveltal to punish later.

  • Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and Dragon Dance Zygarde appreciate Yveltal breaking through common defensive walls such as Primal Groudon, Coil Zygarde, and Giratina-O for their late-game sweeps, while Coil Zygarde is useful for paralysis support and as a blanket check to physical threats such as Primal Groudon and offensive Ho-Oh that may want to trade with Yveltal.

Defensive.description:
• Yveltal's great typing and bulk allow it to be a functional check to Psychic- and Ghost-types. Unlike defensive Arceus-Dark, Yveltal can serve as a soft check to Marshadow as well, while having unique moves such as Sucker Punch, which aid its defensive capabilities further.

  • Compared to the Choice Scarf variant, defensive Yveltal has more longevity across longer games and offers more utility against opposing bulkier teams that the former would struggle against.

  • Defensive Yveltal is rather passive against special attackers barring offensive Primal Kyogre, often being setup fodder against Eternatus and Calm Mind Arceus formes. Despite this, Yveltal is a solid check to a lot of threats in the tier for balance and bulky offense teams.

  • Foul Play boosted by Dark Aura makes defensive Yveltal difficult to deal with for a lot of physical attackers in the tier due to its high damage, such as against Swords Dance Primal Groudon, Extreme Killer Arceus, and Mega Salamence. It also prevents Zacian-C and offensive Primal Kyogre from directly switching into Yveltal, preventing the former from setting up freely while 2HKOing the latter.

  • Toxic allows Yveltal to wear down opposing walls, such as defensive Ho-Oh, Zygarde, Arceus-Fairy, and Arceus-Dark. Alternatively, Taunt can be used to deny setup and utility, such as Zygarde's Coil and Ferrothorn's Spikes, as well as prevent status condition-causing moves that would hinder Yveltal's longevity significantly such as Toxic from Alomomola and defensive Primal Groudon.

  • Sucker Punch allows Yveltal to snipe frailer foes, such as Deoxys-A, Mega Mewtwo Y, and weakened Ultra Necrozma, preventing them from removing Yveltal with super effective coverage. Knock Off makes progress into bulkier teams, notably removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Ho-Oh and Alomomola, as well as Leftovers from Zygarde and Ferrothorn. It also removes offensive items from would-be switch-ins, such as Life Orb from opposing Yveltal and Eternatus as well as Choice Band from Chien-Pao, weakening them significantly for Yveltal's teammates to handle.

  • The combination of Taunt and Toxic allows Yveltal to annoy bulky balance and stall teams by outlasting foes such as Alomomola, Chansey, and Dondozo with Roost and preventing their recovery with Taunt, making this set difficult to handle for Pokemon that cannot directly threaten it.

  • U-turn can be considered to gain momentum against Yveltal's switch-ins such as Eternatus and Arceus-Fairy for teammates such as Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C.

  • Defog is another option that allows Yveltal to remove entry hazards set by opposing Pokemon such as Swords Dance Primal Groudon and the more niche Landorus-T. However, Yveltal suffers from four-moveslot syndrome, so it struggles to fit all these moves effectively.

  • The first EV spread allows Yveltal to outspeed positive-natured base 90 Speed Pokemon such as Primal Groudon, Primal Kyogre, and the more niche Choice Band Ho-Oh. The rest is dumped into Defense, notably preventing +1 Dragon Dance Zygarde from 2HKOing with Thousand Arrows.

  • The second EV spread trades Speed for more Defense, allowing Yveltal to survive +2 Extreme Killer Arceus's Double Edge and +2 Arceus-Ground's Stone Edge while minimizing the odds of +1 Zacian-C's Play Rough OHKOing. The Speed EVs ensure Yveltal can outspeed Adamant Necrozma-DM.

  • Tera Steel allows Yveltal to check Extreme Killer Arceus and Ultra Necrozma more effectively, since it notably removes Yveltal's weakness to Stone Edge from the latter. Tera Steel additionally protects Yveltal from Toxic poison inflicted by defensive Eternatus and Alomomola, improving its longevity.

  • Tera Poison offers the same benefit but also gives a resistance to Deoxys-A's and Marshadow's Low Kick, allowing Yveltal to check them more easily. Tera Poison additionally enables Yveltal to check Play Rough variants of Zacian-C without being weak to Close Combat. However, gaining a weakness to Psychic-types Yveltal would otherwise check may not be ideal, especially against the aforementioned Deoxys-A. Tera Ghost is an alternative that can catch both Marshadow and Extreme Killer Arceus off guard, but still leaves Yveltal vulnerable to poison.

  • This set is relatively simple to use; a physical wall that aims to punish Pokemon such as Ultra Necrozma, Swords Dance Primal Groudon, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground. However, Yveltal is not the most consistent physical wall in the tier, and unlike other defensive behemoths such as Zygarde and the more niche Dondozo, it is easier to overwhelm with status conditions such as burn from Ho-Oh and Toxic poison from defensive Primal Groudon. It is ideal to avoid getting statused to maintain Yveltal's longevity, ensuring it can check what it needs to without being severely weakened beforehand, as even paralysis from Zygarde's Glare can prevent Yveltal from revenge killing Primal Groudon and Primal Kyogre.

  • Yveltal's passivity against Eternatus and Calm Mind Arceus formes means offensive Ho-Oh is a strong teammate for it, since it can deal with these special attacking threats while Yveltal handles physical attackers such as Ultra Necrozma and Extreme Killer Arceus. Defensive Primal Groudon is a strong teammate too, beating Primal Kyogre and Zacian-C for Yveltal as well as offensive variants of Ho-Oh, while appreciating the two dealing with opposing Ground-types such as Arceus-Ground and Zygarde.

  • Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy synergizes well with Yveltal, since it appreciates the latter checking Necrozma-DM for it, while Arceus-Fairy can assist Yveltal in checking Marshadow and Zygarde more easily. Marshadow itself is also a good teammate, removing Yveltal's need to run Sucker Punch for Ultra Necrozma and checking Calm Mind Arceus-Dark. In return, Yveltal helps overwhelm shared counterplay in opposing Arceus-Fairy and defensive Ho-Oh. Zacian-C checks Calm Mind Arceus formes and Eternatus for Yveltal; it appreciates Yveltal beating Necrozma-DM and wearing down Ho-Oh, similarly to Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Yveltal is an excellent revenge killer and Defogger, making it an anti-offense staple that finds place across offense, bulky offense, and balance teams that struggle to answer common setup sweepers like Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM, and Arceus-Ground. Yveltal's weakness to Stealth Rock, however, limits the number of times it can enter the field, which is exacerbated by the vulnerability of being Choice-locked.

  • Foul Play is a very threatening move, with many relevant Pokemon in the tier being at least 3HKOed by it. Combined with Yveltal's great Speed tier, Foul Play lets it reliably revenge kill many threatening setup sweepers after a boost such as Zacian-C, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, Necrozma-DM, and Kyurem-B, while also 2HKOing offensive Ho-Oh, Double Dance Primal Groudon, and wallbreaker Primal Kyogre.

  • While Foul Play's damage is considerable, it fails to threaten bulkier Pokemon such as Coil Zygarde, Eternatus, and special attacking Arceus variants, especially Arceus-Dark and Arceus-Fairy, meaning that Yveltal can be easy to take advantage of.

  • U-turn allows Yveltal to pivot and gain momentum against switch-ins such as Zygarde and Eternatus. U-turn can also occasionally allow Yveltal to scout moves from Choice-locked Pokemon such as Marshadow and Lunala, as well as Tera Fairy from the latter.

  • Yveltal is a situationally excellent user of Defog, as there is very little that any Pokemon can do to stop it. However, its poor longevity makes it bad at removing entry hazards multiple times, so it is often run alongside other forms of hazard control.

  • Yveltal's final moveslot is highly flexible: Toxic gives Yveltal an option to threaten Pokemon that are otherwise undaunted by it such as Calm Mind Arceus formes that have not yet Terastallized to Poison, as well as Zygarde. Knock Off is another option that forces progress via item removal against Pokemon such as Coil Zygarde, Ho-Oh, Eternatus, Ferrothorn, and Garganacl, which rely heavily on their items. Eternatus also takes more damage from Knock Off than Foul Play, potentially opening up avenues to clean up games where Foul Play wouldn't suffice.

  • Roost is a niche option that can help keep Yveltal healthy by taking advantage of the switches it forces. Sucker Punch lets Yveltal revenge kill weakened Ultra Necrozma and Agility Lunala after a Speed boost; otherwise, they can outspeed and KO Yveltal.

  • 224 Speed EVs and a Jolly nature let Yveltal outspeed Dragon Dance Kyurem-B and Zygarde at +1. The remaining EVs are put into physical bulk, giving Yveltal a high chance to survive Mega Salamence's +1 Double Edge and Arceus's +2 Silk Scarf Tera Normal Extreme Speed. Additionally, Yveltal survives Primal Groudon's Stone Edge after Stealth Rock and Necrozma-DM's Searing Sunraze Smash.

  • Tera Dark is Yveltal's most common Tera type for its ability to boost Foul Play's damage even further, letting it OHKO +3 Zacian-C, +2 Arceus, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, and Marshadow after any chip damage. The general power increase also has more situational applications, such as OHKOing Kyurem-B after a layer of Spikes, 2HKOing defensive Primal Kyogre after minimal chip, and to threaten Pokemon such as offensive Ho-Oh, wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, and Double Dance Primal Groudon even more. Tera Dark also lets Yveltal reliably check Ultra Necrozma lacking Outrage by keeping its Psychic immunity while removing its weakness to Stone Edge.

  • Tera Ghost and Tera Steel are alternative options that allow Yveltal to better check Extreme Killer Arceus, with Tera Ghost protecting it completely from Extreme Speed, while Tera Steel grants a resistance to Stealth Rock and the option to throw off Pokemon such as Double Dance Primal Groudon, Ultra Necrozma, Arceus-Ground, and Mega Salamence for a turn while still providing an Extreme Speed immunity.

  • Yveltal is very powerful against hyper offense teams, especially Sticky Web teams, not only due to its ability to clear entry hazards with ease but also because it threatens most Pokemon on these archetypes. Yveltal is best used to clear Sticky Web against opposing Yveltal and Chi-Yu, and doing so should leave it with enough health to still serve as a revenge killer later in the game.

  • While Yveltal apreciates Tera to more easily deal with certain threats and remove its Stealth Rock weakness, it should still be used with some caution against hyper offense structures, as doing so removes its immunity to both Spikes and Sticky Web, the latter of which notably preventing it from outspeeding many key threats like Zacian-C and various boosted threats.

  • Yveltal's anti-offense traits enable it to find occasional use on balance and bulky offense teams, as they tend to be vulnerable to Sticky Web, thus making a hazard removing core with other common hazard removers like Ho-Oh and Giratina-O, with the former helping against Calm Mind Arceus formes, while the latter eases the matchup against Coil Zygarde.

  • Against Pokemon such as Eternatus, Arceus-Fairy, and Fezandipiti that wall Yveltal, partners such as Primal Groudon, Zacian-C, and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM that take care of them are appreciated, so Yveltal can finish off opposing teams late-game. Mega Diancie is an especially good teammate for Yveltal on offensive structures, as it provides additional entry hazard control while being a solid wallbreaker. Additionally, U-turn alleviates Mega Diancie's lackluster longevity by providing it with a safe switch-in against foes such as Arceus-Dark and Coil Zygarde coming in on Yveltal, immediately allowing it to threaten them.

  • Most of the Pokemon Yveltal struggles to threaten such as Zygarde, defensive Ho-Oh, and opposing Yveltal are checked by one or more Eternatus sets, making it a great partner for Yveltal, and the variety of sets Eternatus has lets it assist Yveltal on offense and balance teams. In return, Yveltal checks foes such as Zacian-C, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, and Deoxys-A.

Coil.description:
• Coil Zygarde is a nigh irreplaceable staple on balance and bulky offense teams due to blanket checking the vast majority of the metagame's physical attackers while providing disruption and a bulky wincon against a variety of structures. Zygarde’s unparalleled bulk enables it to counter some of the scariest wallbreakers in Choice Band Marshadow and Swords Dance Primal Groudon. Furthermore, Zygarde’s immaculate synergy with Terastallization allows it to extend its defensive reach to wall Pokémon such as Zacian-C and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM. Due to its immense defensive role compression and consistency, Zygarde can support a dazzling variety of Pokémon. Consequently, every balance and bulky offense team should consider Zygarde at some point in the teambuilding process, while every team needs to be able to contain it.

  • Thousand Arrows's ability to damage Flying-types enables Zygarde to forgo the need for additional attacking moves and delve into its utility movepool to best support its team. Furthermore, the dearth of Grass- and Bug-types in National Dex Ubers means that Thousand Arrows hits nearly every relevant Pokemon for neutral damage.

  • Glare is immensely spammable and provides team support in addition to facilitating Zygarde itself to sweep late-game once its checks have been appropriately chipped. If Zygarde is using Glare, slower teammates such as Primal Groudon and Ho-Oh should consider some minor Speed investment to outspeed paralyzed foes such as Eternatus and Zacian-C. Dragon Tail provides Zygarde the means to phaze Pokemon that may set up on it such as the Arceus formes as it bypasses Taunt, or avoid being trapped by non-Tera Fairy Gothitelle. Toxic is an additional option that annoys opposing Coil Zygarde and Ho-Oh while helping slightly against stall. However, forgoing the utility of Dragon Tail or Glare enables Pokemon such as Swords Dance Primal Groudon, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, and Zacian-C to easily set up on and muscle past Zygarde.

  • Zygarde's immense bulk, especially after transformation, enables it to utilize Rest and stay healthy throughout the course of a game, enabling it to be a serviceable status absorber. This is further facilitated by free turns granted by Glare. However, Zygarde is quite vulnerable while asleep and can provide opportunities for Pokemon such as Taunt Calm Mind Arceus formes and Primal Kyogre to enter safely.

  • The full physical bulk investment in the first EV spread is required to enable Zygarde to serve as a blanket physical wall, as it otherwise crumples against physical attackers such as Swords Dance Primal Groudon and boosted Zacian-C. The second EV spread enables Zygarde to more effectively take on special attackers aiming to exploit its lower Special Defense such as Eruption Primal Groudon and defensive Primal Kyogre while outspeeding paralyzed Zacian-C after transformation and being able to survive Tera Dragon Eternatus's +1 Dynamax Cannon after Terastallization. Although Zygarde is still an excellent physical wall and Marshadow counter, it is significantly more vulnerable to the most powerful physical attacks such as Zacian-C's +3 Behemoth Blade and Double Dance Primal Groudon's +2 Precipice Blades.

  • Zygarde is perhaps the Pokemon that is most synergistic with Terastallization due to its ability to flip Zygarde's exploitable Ice-, Dragon-, and Fairy-type weaknesses. It often uses Terastallization to soak an attack and paralyze or phaze boosted Pokemon that would otherwise threaten it such as Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and Play Rough Zacian-C. Tera Fairy and Water each have their merits, as they enable Zygarde to handle specific threats and should not be used interchangeably.

  • Tera Water is Zygarde's most generally useful option. Despite the Electric-type weakness, Zygarde is able to stomach Zacian-C's +3 Wild Charge, while Zygarde's obscene bulk enables it to continue being an immovable physical wall despite a lack of notable resistances. However, maintaining a resistance to Primal Groudon's Overheat and resisting Necrozma-DM's +1 Searing Sunraze Smash, which would otherwise OHKO Zygarde, is appreciated.

  • Tera Fairy is also an option that should be considered. Despite Tera Fairy introducing weaknesses to Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, and Eternatus's Sludge Bomb, it is still extremely good. Dragon Dance Zygarde is immensely threatening to the bulky offense and balance structures Coil Zygarde anchors and is able to use Tera Water Zygarde as setup fodder. Tera Fairy Zygarde is one of the few options for defensive counterplay available to these structures while also being able to turn the tables and use Dragon Dance Zygarde to facilitate its own setup. Tera Fairy also helps Zygarde defensively against Calm Mind Arceus-Dark and physical Giratina-O, preventing the latter from phazing Zygarde with Dragon Tail.

  • Coil Zygarde is an integral part of the defensive backbone of most bulky offense and balance teams and finds switch-in opportunities on Pokemon such as Primal Groudon and Marshadow. However, Zygarde's special bulk is middling, and it should be used cautiously against special attackers such as Primal Kyogre, Lunala, and Eternatus even if it is able to survive a hit, as relying on Rest leaves it quite vulnerable. Additionally, due to Zygarde's low Speed and reliance on status moves, it struggles with Taunt users such as Yveltal and the Arceus formes. Calm Mind Arceus formes especially often use Zygarde as setup fodder. As Zygarde lacks offensive investment, its Thousand Arrows is quite weak and struggles to threaten most Pokemon for meaningful damage until it has accumulated multiple Coil boosts.

  • Against hyper offense teams Zygarde should focus on attempting to check or trade with a single Pokemon such as Extreme Killer Arceus, Primal Groudon, or Zacian-C, as it will rarely be given enough turns to become offensively threatening. Additionally, Zygarde is entirely deadweight against stall teams, as it is completely walled by Dondozo, but it can still provide value as a status sponge, pivot, and cleaner once Dondozo has been removed. Although Zygarde cannot make meaningful progress against stall teams, it is not threatened by stall in return with the exception of Eternatus's Dynamax Cannon, which 2HKOes it.

  • While Zygarde may be a blanket physical wall, it is not impenetrable. Notably, Ultra Necrozma's +1 Light That Burns the Sky is capable of OHKOing Zygarde. Consequently, Zygarde requires teammates that are capable of offensively or defensively checking Ultra Necrozma such as Calm Mind Arceus-Dark, Marshadow, and Yveltal. Defensive Arceus-Dark should not be used with Coil Zygarde, as they are offensively overwhelmed by Pokemon such as Taunt Calm Mind Arceus formes, Life Orb Yveltal, and Primal Kyogre, which easily exploit the passive structures that result from this pairing. Calm Mind Arceus-Dark is sufficient Ultra Necrozma counterplay while also using Pokemon that beat Zygarde such as special utility Giratina-O, Life Orb Yveltal, and wallbreaker Eternatus to set up itself.

  • Defensive or Swords Dance utility Primal Groudon provides a Primal Kyogre switch-in and entry hazards. Primal Groudon is also able to beat Dondozo via Overheat and eases the burden on Zygarde by excellently checking Zacian-C, which can muscle through a chipped Zygarde. Both Giratina-O and Ho-Oh provide hazard control as well as status support and phazing. which synergize to create a strong defensive backbone capable of supporting most offensive Pokemon.

  • As Zygarde is deadweight against stall, stallbreakers such as Choice Specs Lunala, Choice Band Rayquaza, and defensive Primal Kyogre are great allies that also decimate bulkier balance teams, which easily contain Zygarde. However, Zygarde does not require a dedicated stallbreaker, as Pokemon such as Taunt Calm Mind Arceus formes and wallbreaker Eternatus more than suffice if they're positioned properly. Zacian-C is also a good option due to its ability to blanket check Taunt Arceus formes, which hinder Zygarde, while being a fast Pokemon and a thorn in the side of hyper offense teams, which can overwhelm Zygarde. As Zacian-C is similarly futile against stall, more dedicated stallbreakers are recommended alongside this duo.

Dragon Dance.description:
• With its good typing, Dragon Dance Zygarde is one of the tier's best cleaners, since access to Thousand Arrows allows it more freedom to run other moves that help it set up and sweep. This makes Zygarde more difficult to stop compared to other setup sweepers such as Mega Salamence, especially combined with the great bulk from Power Construct.

  • Despite the opportunity cost of not running the Coil variant, Dragon Dance Zygarde is a fantastic late-game sweeper for balance and bulky offense teams alike.

  • Substitute allows Zygarde to set up on passive Pokemon, blocking moves such as Toxic, Leech Seed, and Salt Cure from Alomomola, Ferrothorn, and Garganacl, respectively. It additionally allows Zygarde to activate Power Construct more easily, which is essential for handling revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Yveltal that would otherwise pick off Zygarde with ease.

  • Substitute helps against specially offensive Giratina-O, since it cannot break Zygarde's Substitute after Power Construct via unboosted Hex and is thus forced to waste power using Draco Meteor instead, eventually giving Zygarde a free setup opportunity once Giratina-O is forced to switch.

  • Dragon Tail punishes phazing attempts from defensive Ho-Oh's Whirlwind and opposing Zygarde's Dragon Tail; it prevents opposing Zygarde and Garganacl from setting up alongside Zygarde unless they use Tera Fairy.

  • Dragon Tail also forces entry hazard damage against physical walls such as Dondozo and defensive Arceus-Dark, maintaining Zygarde's offensive pressure by wearing them down repeatedly. Glare is a niche alternative that punishes offensive checks such as Mega Salamence, with paralysis potentially giving Zygarde more setup chances.

  • The given EV spread allows Zygarde to survive an Ice Beam from uninvested Arceus formes, outspeed Eternatus and Mewtwo at +1 after Power Construct, and maximize Leftovers recovery.

  • Groundium Z is a niche alternative, with Tectonic Rage notably OHKOing offensive Primal Kyogre and defensive Primal Groudon after a boost, although access to Terastallization is generally preferred.

  • Tera Ground powers up Thousand Arrows, further improving Zygarde's otherwise mediocre damage. It notably allows boosted Zygarde to OHKO Marshadow and wallbreaker Primal Kyogre after Stealth Rock, as well as 2HKO Giratina-O and Calm Mind Arceus formes after Stealth Rock.

  • Tera Ground also provides defensive benefits for Zygarde, letting it get easier setup opportunities by dropping its weaknesses to Dragon and Fairy, notably enabling Zygarde to set up against Mega Diancie and unboosted offensive Eternatus. However, Zygarde losing its Fire-type resistance may be an issue when dealing with Tera Grass Ho-Oh.

  • Despite Zygarde typically handling physical threats such as Arceus, Mega Salamence, and Marshadow, the Dragon Dance variant is unable to check most of these threats barring defensive Primal Groudon, meaning it is ideal to keep Zygarde out of harm's way.

  • Keeping this set as a surprise to the opponent is a major factor in what makes Dragon Dance Zygarde powerful because many would expect Coil Zygarde on balance and bulky offense teams; setting up on foes that would ordinarily switch out, such as defensive Primal Groudon and unboosted Necrozma-DM, after switching in safely, is ideal.

  • Although Zygarde is relatively bulky after triggering Power Construct, the lack of recovery means Zygarde typically only gets one chance to set up and break through an opposing team. It is ideal to wear down teams before going in with Zygarde, even with the intent of using Tera Ground.

  • Scouting against opposing Zygarde may be ideal before committing to Tera Ground, since opposing Tera Fairy Zygarde counters Dragon Dance Zygarde, an issue that is quite common on opposing balance and bulky offense teams. This could be done by initially phazing opposing Tera Fairy Zygarde or by using other offensive threats such as Chien-Pao.

  • Dragon Dance Zygarde requires the opposing team to be worn down before attempting to sweep, which can be done in multiple ways. Entry hazard support from defensive Primal Groudon and Ferrothorn can help wear down Arceus formes and opposing Zygarde late-game, where Zygarde performs best.

  • Additionally, defensive Primal Groudon can threaten opposing Tera Fairy Zygarde with Overheat, punishing it for trying to check Zygarde. On the other hand, Ferrothorn can check defensive Primal Kyogre and Arceus-Water for Zygarde, two threats that may attempt to trade with Zygarde. In return, Zygarde threatens opposing Primal Groudon and offensive Ho-Oh, which threaten Ferrothorn and defensive Primal Groudon.

  • There are a lot of Pokemon that synergize with Dragon Dance Zygarde offensively. Swords Dance Primal Groudon, Marshadow, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground can all overwhelm opposing Coil Zygarde in conjunction with Zygarde. The latter two have a great matchup against opposing offense teams with threats such as Extreme Killer Arceus, something Zygarde struggles against.

  • Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM can punish opposing Tera Fairy Zygarde and Dondozo, while Zygarde can use their checks like opposing Tera Water Zygarde and defensive Primal Groudon as setup fodder.

  • Special attackers such as Primal Kyogre, Eternatus, and Calm Mind Arceus formes appreciate Dragon Dance Zygarde breaking past specially defensive walls such as Ferrothorn, Chansey, and defensive Ho-Oh, while they handle checks to Zygarde such as opposing Tera Fairy Zygarde, Tera Fairy IronPress Garganacl, and Dondozo.

  • Eternatus is notable because not only does it threaten these physical walls after Tera Fairy, but it also absorbs Toxic Spikes, maintaining Zygarde's longevity for it to have a better chance at sweeping; defensive Eternatus variants can additionally wear down soft checks to Zygarde such as defensive Primal Kyogre via Toxic poison over longer games.

  • Although Dragon Dance Zygarde is best on balance and bulky offense teams due to its Terastallization reliance and its overall lack of immediate power without it, Zygarde can still be used on hyper offense teams that want to utilize Extreme Killer Arceus over Arceus-Ground.

  • Dedicated leads such as Deoxys-S and Glimmora can help wear down checks such as opposing Zygarde and Arceus formes, similarly to Ferrothorn and defensive Primal Groudon. Grimmsnarl provides dual screens support, allowing Zygarde to set up on more threats such as offensive Primal Groudon, unboosted Mega Salamence, and Rayquaza.

Trapper.description:
• Trapper Zygarde is a unique set that trades the defensive utility of Coil sets to take on a more situational setup sweeper role, often winning games on the spot if it finds a suitable target to trap, such as non-Tera Fairy Zygarde, defensive Primal Groudon, Ferrothorn, and Dondozo lacking a Water-type move. It best fits on balance and offense teams that have other means to deal with Ho-Oh, since this Coil set struggles specifically against Ho-Oh.

  • Scale Shot's Speed boost gives Zygarde a means of deterring revenge kill attempts from faster threats such as Spectral Thief Marshadow, Eternatus, and offensive Primal Kyogre after two Speed boosts. At +6 Attack, it OHKOes offensive Yveltal and offensive Ho-Oh with 4 hits and OHKOes defensive Ho-Oh with 5 hits.

  • 44 SpD EVs allow Zygarde to survive an unboosted Dynamax Cannon from Eternatus from full, while the rest of the EVs are invested to maximize physical bulk in order to set up on foes such as Primal Groudon safely.

  • Tera Fairy notably prevents phazing attempts from opposing Zygarde's Dragon Tail. Moreover, Zygarde-Complete's great special bulk with minimal investment lets it trap and set up on Arceus-Dark and defensive Arceus-Fairy lacking Taunt. In a pinch, it also grants an immunity to Ultra Necrozma's Outrage and Eternatus's Dynamax Cannon.

  • The lack of utility moves such as Glare and Dragon Tail renders Zygarde worse into physical attackers such as Swords Dance Primal Groudon, Zacian-C, Mega Salamence, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground. It is thus necessary not to rely on Zygarde for checking the aforementioned threats, and it should be treated as a setup sweeper instead of a wall.

  • Opposing Tera Fairy Zygarde prevents Trapper Zygarde from getting Speed boosts, with Glare and Toxic variants in particular being problematic due to higher PP and depleting Rest quickly, respectively. However, non-Tera Fairy sets are easily trapped. Furthermore, Primal Groudon users that occasionally stay in on Zygarde to set Stealth Rock or use Toxic are also great targets for trapping with Thousand Waves. Similarly, Calm Mind Arceus-Dark can potentially lose against Tera Fairy Zygarde, as Scale Shot lets the latter bypass Taunt.

  • Teammates such as Primal Groudon, defensive Primal Kyogre, and IronPress Garganacl are good partners that can compensate for the lack of defensive capabilities, particularly against threats like Zacian-C, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, and Ho-Oh.

  • Revenge killers such as Ditto and Choice Scarf Yveltal aid Zygarde by stopping setup sweepers like Arceus-Ground and Eternatus from getting out of hand. They are especially valuable for covering the hyper offense matchup, in which Zygarde tends to be mostly deadweight, barring niche cases such as trapping lead Ribombee after Terastallizing.

  • Zygarde's trapping capabilities work excellently with wallbreakers like Swords Dance Zacian-C, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, and Eruption Primal Groudon, which appreciate its capability to force Terastallization from opposing Zygarde and weaken the opposing defensive core by eliminating walls such as Zygarde and Primal Groudon.

Choice Band.description: Zygarde-10% finds a niche as a Ground-type wallbreaker with a strong matchup into typical responses to Ground-type Pokemon. Despite its frailty and the immense competition it faces from Sand Rush Excadrill, Thousand Arrows allows Zygarde-10% to differentiate itself by allowing it to overwhelm common responses to Ground-types such as Skarmory, Celesteela, and Rotom-W that its competition struggles with. Extreme Speed offers priority that lets Zygarde revenge kill faster offensive threats such as Alakazam and Booster Energy Iron Moth. Outrage has solid neutral coverage with Thousand Arrows and is a valuable STAB move to hit walls like Buzzwole and Mega Venusaur. Toxic allows Zygarde-10% to punish and potentially overwhelm physically defensive walls like Rocky Helmet Tangrowth, Slowbro, and Buzzwole. A Jolly nature is crucial for allowing Zygarde-10% to outspeed important metagame threats like Mega Latias, Iron Moth lacking Booster Energy, and Thundurus. Zygarde-10% finds itself on offensive teams that appreciate its wallbreaking capabilities against common defensive cores like Celesteela and Rotom-W. These teams can further support Zygarde-10%, which partners well with offensive pivots such as Scizor, Slowbro, and Rotom-W that can help Zygarde-10% hit the field. In addition, Slowbro provides Future Sight support, which can be valuable in breaking through answers such as Buzzwole. In return, Zygarde-10% pressures walls that give these Pokemon issues such as Rotom-W and Celesteela. Grass-types like Tapu Bulu and Tangrowth are the most consistent pivots into Zygarde-10% and, as such, it appreciates support from Pokemon that force Grass-types out such as Victini, Iron Moth, Mega Venusaur, and Celesteela. Physically defensive walls such as Hippowdon, Buzzwole, and Slowbro can withstand hits from Zygarde-10% and can either deal hefty damage or inflict status. Special attackers like mixed Aegislash and Iron Moth can exploit these physically defensive walls, and in exchange, they appreciate Zygarde-10% dishing out massive damage to specially defensive walls like Chansey, Blissey, and Celesteela. As most of Zygarde-10%'s checks are vulnerable to entry hazards, entry hazard support from Excadrill, Skarmory, and Tyranitar allows Zygarde-10% to achieve favorable damage rolls on its would-be answers like Buzzwole and Tangrowth. In exchange, Zygarde-10% pressures hazard removal from the likes of Excadrill and Rotom-W, ensuring that hazards stay up in the long term.

Lead.description:
• Mega Diancie is a great lead for offense teams thanks to its STAB combination that threatens the main Defoggers in the metagame, which include Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Yveltal, combined with its ability Magic Bounce, which allows it to serve as an anti-lead to all other suicide leads in the tier, notably including Deoxys-S, Shuckle, Smeargle, and Glimmora.

  • Once Mega Diancie can't do much else in the field, Explosion allows it to KO itself, wear down a foe, and let an ally safely come in afterwards. Earth Power is an alternative to OHKO Glimmora and situationally hit common switch-ins in Primal Groudon, Zacian-C, and Necrozma-DM.

  • The given EV spread lets Mega Diancie avoid an OHKO from Choice Band Tera Flying Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent and Choice Band Marshadow's Low Kick after Stealth Rock as well as a 2HKO from Life Orb Yveltal's Dark Pulse while ensuring that it outspeeds neutral-natured foes with base 120 Speed, such as Palkia-O and Mega Salamence, on top of OHKOing specially offensive Yveltal with Moonblast.

  • Especially against non-hyper offense teams, if at Team Preview it's clear that Mega Diancie's relative lack of Speed and frail nature for the metagame may render it outsped and OHKOed, it should be kept for the mid-game, where it can come into foes such as Yveltal, Ho-Oh, and Giratina-O to force a switch while setting at least one entry hazard.

  • Mega Diancie has significantly higher bulk before Mega Evolving, so it may be desirable to Mega Evolve it later on to withstand an attack such as unboosted Mega Salamence's Earthquake or defensive Arceus-Ground's Judgment. In very niche scenarios where Sticky Web manages to get into its side of the field, preserving Diancie's Mega Evolution to keep Clear Body for the mid-game can help preserve Diancie's Speed. Clear Body can also be used to avoid being hindered by Glimmora's Mud Shot, but this also can let Glimmora lay entry hazards instead in the event of an incorrect prediction.

  • Faster foes such as Zacian-C, offensive Arceus-Water, and Deoxys-A can prevent Mega Diancie from doing anything by immediately OHKOing it. Allies such as Primal Groudon, Yveltal, and Necrozma-DM act as good partners to mitigate this issue by providing alternatives to play around them.

  • Mega Diancie can become setup fodder to foes such as Necrozma-DM, Primal Groudon, and Zacian-C. Ditto is a solid partner to punish setup sweepers and mitigate the potential vulnerability to them.

Wallbreaker.description:
• Mega Diancie's unique typing allows it to be a powerful mixed wallbreaker in the tier, since its coverage is quite difficult to pivot around for standard defensive structures, which include Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Zygarde, Arceus-Dark, Yveltal, and Giratina-O. Mega Diancie's typing also has niche defensive utility, allowing it to soft-check Yveltal, Chi-Yu, Rayquaza, and unboosted Mega Salamence. Its ability in Magic Bounce plays a vital role against hyper offense structures barring Trick Room, since being able to deny entry hazard leads such as Deoxys-S, Smeargle, and Shuckle, effectively anti-leading them, is great for defensive partners such as Primal Groudon and support Arceus formes that cannot hold Heavy-Duty Boots. Mega Diancie is also fantastic against stall because of this ability, since it counters Giratina and non-Sludge Bomb Eternatus. This role compression makes Mega Diancie a fantastic tool for bulky offense and balance teams that need a Pokemon that does well against all playstyles in the tier if positioned correctly.

  • Earth Power is necessary to hit Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Zacian-C super effectively, allowing Mega Diancie to punish them for recklessly switching in.

  • Substitute enables Mega Diancie to ease prediction against potential switches, as well as giving Mega Diancie the chance to wallbreak further thanks to the Substitute protecting it from faster threats such as Arceus-Ground and Zacian-C. Substitute also lets Mega Diancie block Nuzzle from Smeargle, effectively walling it while denying Sticky Web. Alternatively, since Mega Diancie is able to beat all the common Defoggers in the tier, including Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Yveltal, it makes for a powerful Stealth Rock user, as it is able to make progress against a predicted switch from Arceus-Dark or Rayquaza. Spikes is also a viable option, but Mega Diancie's poor longevity means it cannot stack multiple Spike layers throughout a game consistently, even if the second layer aids greatly in wallbreaking similarly to Stealth Rock.

  • The default EV spread allows Mega Diancie's Diamond Storm to 2HKO Lunala after Stealth Rock, and OHKO Rayquaza. Mega Diancie's SpA EVs enable Moonblast to OHKO defensive Zygarde after a layer of Spikes, and to 2HKO Dondozo, with Earth Power also 2HKOing defensive Primal Groudon. The defensive investment avoids a 2HKO from Chi-Yu's Flamethrower after Stealth Rock, and from offensive Ho-Oh's Brave Bird, all while also outspeeding neutral-natured base-120 Speed Pokemon such as Arceus, Mega Salamence, and Palkia-O. The alternate spread enables Mega Diancie to also avoid an OHKO from Pheromosa's Triple Axel, but it shouldn't be used alongside Substitute as it has an even amount of HP, which hinders the usage of such move.

  • Mega Evolving Diancie should be done as soon as possible to make the most out of Magic Bounce, which is needed to bounce back status conditions from Giratina-O, Alomomola, and Eternatus, as well as deny entry hazards from Ferrothorn and Primal Groudon, even if the latter is quite risky due to Mega Diancie's poor bulk. It should be noted that Mega Diancie can induce mind games against Mud Shot Glimmora when anti-leading it, since Clear Body pre-Mega Evolution protects Diancie from Mud Shot's Speed drop, meaning Mega Diancie can decide not to Mega Evolve to more easily 2HKO Glimmora and deny it from setting up entry hazards.
