This process is quite risky to pull off though, since it is effectively a coinflip as to whether Glimmora uses Stealth Rock or Mud Shot.

  • Although Mega Diancie can easily switch Ho-Oh and remove it via Diamond Storm, it should be careful around Ho-Oh, since Sacred Fire possibly burning Mega Diancie is a massive hinderance to its wallbreaking capabilities, especially against stall teams, where Pressure from Giratina and Eternatus quickly drains Diamond Storm's limited PP. Diamond Storm should not be recklessly spammed, as its needed to actually break through these cores in stall and bulky balance teams.

  • Mega Diancie struggles against Primal Groudon, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Primal Kyogre, since they are all able to withstand its attacks and OHKO it back with ease, or in Zacian-C's case, it can outspeed and set up on it first. On the bulky offense teams Mega Diancie fits well on, a defensive backbone is essential to control these threats. Zygarde is able to control Primal Groudon with ease; Tera Water sets can also contain Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM for Mega Diancie, while Tera Fairy variants shut down Dragon Dance Zygarde, which is able to use Mega Diancie as setup fodder thanks to Tera Ground removing its Moonblast weakness. Yveltal can either utilize Choice Scarf to revenge kill Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and boosted Zacian-C for Mega Diancie, or it can use its Life Orb set with Sucker Punch to revenge kill Ultra Necrozma and Deoxys-A for Mega Diancie; Yveltal and Mega Diancie additionally form a potent wallbreaking duo for the team. Finally, defensive Primal Groudon can form a strong entry hazard-stacking core with Mega Diancie, while Mega Diancie beats Giratina-O for it. Offensive Primal Groudon sets appreciate Mega Diancie setting entry hazards for it to more easily wallbreak. Both Primal Groudon sets are able to handle Zacian-C and Primal Kyogre for Mega Diancie.

  • Choice Scarf Yveltal is an especially good teammate, since it can pivot into Mega Diancie via U-turn, which is an important need for Mega Diancie due to its poor bulk. Yveltal can pivot Diancie in against bulkier foes such as Coil Zygarde and defensive Ho-Oh that switch in place of Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM. Another pivoting teammate includes Landorus-T, which checks Zacian-C and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground for Mega Diancie while letting Mega Diancie run Substitute or Spikes, as Landorus-T commonly runs Stealth Rock. Life Orb Yveltal and other offensive teammates such as Choice Band Marshadow and Meteor Beam Eternatus appreciate Mega Diancie setting entry hazards for them to break through defensive cores more easily, with the latter two Pokemon also appreciating Mega Diancie pressuring stall teams early on for them to clean up afterwards.

Weakness Policy.description:
• Diancie's typing and access to Encore let it find a niche in the 1v1 metagame as a bulky attacker that matches up well against several of the tier's Fighting- and Dark-type Pokemon, such as Iron Valiant and Hoopa-U.
  • Diamond Storm hits Pokemon like Volcarona and Kyurem.
  • Both Play Rough and Moonblast can threaten Dragon- and Dark-type Pokemon like Haxorus, Raging Bolt, and Hoopa-U, with the former threatening Hoopa-U a lot more and the latter being more helpful against Raging Bolt.
  • Trick Room is incredibly useful for Diancie, as it enables the use of a fast Encore after the first turn of the battle, which locks several stall and setup Pokemon, like Alolan Ninetales and Espathra, into using only one of their moves.
  • The Special Defense EVs are enough to let Diancie survive two Thunderbolts from Special Attack Booster Energy Raging Bolt, while the Attack EVs allow it to OHKO most Hoopa-U with Play Rough. Finally, the Defense EVs allow Diancie to survive two Choice Band Spirit Breaks from Jolly Iron Valiant.
  • Diancie can also run an EV spread of 252 HP / 16 Atk / 240 Def with a Relaxed nature, which gives it the best odds to survive a Choice Band Flower Trick from Adamant Meowscarada. It is better to run Moonblast on this variant as it grants Diancie better odds against Raging Bolt.
  • Since Diancie tends to struggle with Steel- and Grass-type Pokemon like Iron Crown and Ogerpon-W, Fire-type teammates like Volcanion can be useful.

Choice Specs.description:
• Moonblast defeats a wide range of threats like Hoopa-U, Raging Bolt, and Choice item Iron Valiant.
  • Power Gem allows Diancie to beat non-stall Zapdos variants and Volcarona even after it has boosted once with Quiver Dance.
  • Earth Power should be used against Iron Moth and Heatran.
  • Psychic lets Diancie defeat Air Balloon Pecharunt and guarantees an OHKO against Normal Gem Sneasler. Alternatively, Flash Cannon can be used against opposing Diancie.
  • The EV spread allows Diancie to tank two Thunderbolts from Special Attack Booster Energy Raging Bolt.
  • Diancie struggles against Steel-type foes like Metagross, Iron Crown, and Hisuian Goodra; therefore, teammates like Volcarona, Ursaluna, and Volcanion are appreciated.
  • Diancie also struggles against Encore + Disable variations of Alolan Ninetales and Iron Valiant, so it's mandatory to have a teammate that can handle both of them, such as Volcarona and Iron Crown.

Trick Room Setter.description:
• The given EV spread allows Diancie to survive Steam Eruption from Volcanion and Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-Wellspring.
  • The alternative EV spread allows Diancie to outspeed Tornadus and the Ogerpon formes in Tailwind.

Wallbreaker.description:
Mega Diancie is a very potent wallbreaker that applies a lot of offensive pressure to bulky offense and balance builds, threatening Pokemon such as Zapdos, Raging Bolt, and Great Tusk. Mega Diancie’s coverage further cements its role as a wallbreaker; for example, Earth Power hits foes such as Heatran, Gholdengo, Melmetal, and Toxapex that would otherwise come in safely on its STAB moves. Mystical Fire provides even more coverage, hitting foes such as Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor. Power Gem avoids the drawback of possibly forcing Mega Diancie to run a nature that decreases Defense or Special Defense, improving its ability to take on Pokemon such as Raging Bolt. Mega Diancie does well versus common forms of entry hazard removal such as Terapagos lacking Earth Power, Great Tusk, Zapdos, and Tornadus-T. Mega Diancie is a unique hazard setter that can set up hazards while denying common opposing hazard setters in Heatran and Mega Tyranitar. 28 Attack EVs allow Mega Diancie to 2HKO Galarian Slowking with Diamond Storm.

Mega Diancie fits on bulky offense teams and pairs well with Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Ferrothorn, and Landorus-T that appreciate it due to its ability to threaten and force out Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona, Zapdos, and Hisuian Samurott with its STAB attacks. In return, Great Tusk and Landorus-T check threats such as Mega Lopunny, Iron Head Kingambit, and Assault Vest Melmetal, which threaten Mega Diancie directly. Landorus-T also brings Mega Diancie in safely with a U-turn against Pokemon that like to come in on it such as Tornadus-T, Mega Charizard Y, and Great Tusk, which Mega Diancie punishes. Mega Diancie tends to struggle with fast offensive Water-types such as Ogerpon-W, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, and Mega Swampert in the rain. Thus, Pokemon such as Dragonite, Raging Bolt, and Ferrothorn can keep these foes in check.

Lead.description:
Mega Diancie functions as an amazing hyper offense lead, being able to set up Stealth Rock behind Substitute while also denying opposing entry hazards via Magic Bounce. Mega Diancie's main niche over other hazard setters is its ability to deny hazards from Pokemon such as Glimmora and Landorus-T, as well as blocking Taunt and Encore from Pokemon like Tornadus-T and Iron Valiant, making it harder for them to deny hazards. Endeavor lets Mega Diancie heavily chip Moonblast switch-ins like Moltres, Corviknight, and Heatran when at low HP. Staying in base forme is often an option in order to set Stealth Rock on faster Pokemon due to Diancie's superior bulk. 240 HP EVs allow Mega Diancie to set Substitute four times as opposed to three, leaving Mega Diancie at 1 HP to use Endeavor with.

Being a hyper offense lead, Mega Diancie's main function is to set entry hazards to enable one of the archetype's many sweepers to punch through defensive cores and win the game, often being able to give them a free switch in by wearing itself down via Substitute. Examples of Pokemon that benefit from these hazards include Kingambit, Volcarona, and Great Tusk, since they all appreciate Stealth Rock chipping down Pokemon such as Corviknight, Heatran, and Landorus-T for them to break through more easily. However, lead Mega Diancie can sometimes be threatened by super effective attacks from faster foes such as Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, as well as by strong priority moves from Pokemon such as Choice Band Rillaboom and Mega Scizor. These can be taken care of by partners such as Dragonite, which can safely switch in on Urshifu-R, Landorus-T, and Rillaboom, and Volcarona, which switches in on and threatens Rillaboom and Mega Scizor with its strong STAB moves.

Trick Room Attacker.description:
• Diancie is a premier Trick Room attacker due to its fantastic bulk that allows it to set Trick Room for itself repeatedly. It also allows Diancie to snowball out of control while stacking Defense boosts from Diamond Storm, which hits a majority of the metagame for at least neutral damage and makes Diancie extremely difficult to remove with physical attacks.

  • Diancie's ability, Clear Body, provides crucial immunity to Intimidate that would otherwise be a nuisance to Diancie's damage output throughout the game.

  • Defense boosts from the aforementioned Diamond Storm create a threatening combination with Body Press, allowing Diancie to deal strong single target damage that the majority of the metagame does not resist and trade damage with opposing Trick Room attackers like Iron Hands.

  • Diancie runs Hard Stone to further boost the spread damage of STAB Diamond Storm. Hard Stone also allows Diancie to make consistent progress into one of its biggest checks, Landorus. Hard Stone can often be replaced with Covert Cloak to assist with its capability to set and make the most of Trick Room. It is used to block Fake Out, which would otherwise inhibit Diancie's ability to position itself to fire off attacks or set Trick Room. Conversely, Leftovers are used to increase Diancie's longevity and make use of its immense natural bulk.

  • Diancie has two premier Tera types. Tera Dragon is the most common and used to resist Water- and Grass-type attacks while being better into Landorus Sludge Bomb. Another thing to consider with Tera Dragon is the lack of threatening Fairy-type attacks in the metagame to punish it. Tera Grass is used to let Diancie resist Ground-, Grass-, and Water-type attacks, as well as improving its matchup into Amoonguss, which moves before Diancie in Trick Room.

  • Minimum Speed investment with 0 Speed IVs is optimal on most Diancie sets due to its threatening presence in Trick Room; once the dimensions have been twisted, it moves before threats like Ursaluna-B.

  • Common checks to Diancie include Gholdengo and Landorus because of their consistent ability to OHKO Diancie. Gholdengo is especially threatening to Diancie because it is immune to Body Press and resists Diamond Storm while threatening a OHKO back. Ogerpon formes deal threatening Grass-type damage, and Ogerpon-W in particular has a super effective Ivy Cudgel. The Ursaluna formes are also threatening for Diancie, threatening OHKOes before Diancie has Terastallized and Speed tying Diancie in Trick Room, making them troublesome for it to defeat. Okidogi can also prove difficult for Diancie, as it resists both its attacking moves and threatens large damage in return.

  • Good teammates for Diancie include Pokemon that can threaten its checks, which include Gholdengo and Iron Hands. Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-W are often paired with Diancie due to Follow Me redirection, and their strong STAB combinations complement Diancie. Ogerpon-H is often paired with Diancie to threaten Gholdengo, and Ogerpon-W threatens Landorus.

  • Roaring Moon and Landorus are strong additions to Diancie cores to provide a faster mode and threaten aforementioned threats to Diancie like Okidogi and Gholdengo. Trick Room attackers like Ursaluna and Torkoal that take advantage of Diancie's ability to set Trick Room and healing partners like Sinistcha and Amoonguss that increase Diancie's longevity are also greatly appreciated.

  • Fake Out support from Pokemon like Rillaboom and Incineroar is appreciated by Diancie, allowing it to use Trick Room more easily. The latter is able to enhance Diancie's natural bulk due to its Intimidate.

Mixed Wallbreaker (Rock).description: Mega Diancie is the ideal Mega Evolution for Rock teams due to its ability to check Dragon-types like Kommo-o, punish passive Pokemon and entry hazard setters such as Toxapex and Klefki with Magic Bounce, and be a mixed wallbreaker that threatens Great Tusk and Galarian Slowking. Diamond Storm does considerable damage to special walls like Blissey and Alolan Muk and can also provide a Defense boost. Psychic heavily damages Mega Venusaur, Toxapex, and Nidoking, which eases the matchup against Poison teams. Earth Power deals heavy damage to Steel-type Pokemon like Heatran and Iron Treads and is paired nicely with Mystical Fire to damage Skarmory and Corviknight. On a hyper offensive team, Mega Diancie runs four attacks for coverage. With Shuckle's Sticky Web up, its good Speed tier becomes more devastating and outspeeds Pokemon like Mega Gallade and Zeraora. Mega Diancie also pairs well with Omastar and Terrakion, as Omastar takes care of the Ground matchup with a well-timed Shell Smash, while Terrakion's access to Earthquake and Close Combat takes care of most Steel-types. On bulky offense, Mega Diancie prefers to run Spikes, as the chip damage sets up a potential late-game cleanup from more offensive Pokemon on the team like Terrakion and Nihilego. Garganacl pairs well with Spikes, as Salt Cure forces a lot of Pokemon to switch out and take additional chip damage.

Mixed Wallbreaker (Fairy).description: Mega Diancie is a valuable asset to Fairy teams, featuring Magic Bounce to deflect entry hazards and status, wide coverage, and strong offensive capabilities with its high Speed. Diamond Storm often increases Mega Diancie's bulk and threatens foes like Enamorus and Mega Charizard Y. Moonblast handles threats like Mega Sableye and Latias. Earth Power can be used to counter Steel teams, OHKOing Heatran, Excadrill, and Magnezone, while dealing heavy damage to the likes of Skeledirge and Garganacl. Mystical Fire targets Steel-types that don't mind Earth Power, such as Ferrothorn, Celesteela, and Mega Scizor under Psychic Terrain. Alternatively, Mega Diancie can run Nature Power and use the various terrains set by its teammates to expand its wallbreaking abilities. Stealth Rock can be used to allow Mega Diancie to set its own hazard, but four attacks are recommended given Mega Diancie's wide coverage. Klefki provides Spikes and dual screens support which allows Mega Diancie to OHKO threats like Gholdengo, and it can also carry Thunder Wave to let Mega Diancie outspeed and take out threats like Mega Gallade and Mega Aerodactyl. Tapu Koko takes on Water-types and aids in the Steel matchup by forcing out Corviknight and Celesteela. Tapu Bulu counters Ground- and Water-types like Great Tusk and Urshifu-R, while Tapu Lele takes on Poison-types and prevents priority moves from Azumarill and Mega Scizor. Iron Valiant is a great partner for the Steel matchup, but it also benefits from Tapu Koko's Electric Terrain to outspeed and take out faster threats such as Zeraora and Greninja. All of these teammates appreciate Mega Diancie's ability to bounce hazards back to the opponent, as Fairy teams do not possess entry hazard removal.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Hoopa is an effective wallbreaker and cleaner thanks to its astronomically high Special Attack stat combined with its great STAB moves and solid movepool that lets it threaten common defensive Pokemon such as Galarian Slowbro and Venusaur. Psyshock is the generally superior Psychic-type move, letting it more easily break through common specially defensive Pokemon like Florges and Lanturn. Alternatively, Psychic has more power, hitting the likes of Mudsdale and Rhydon stronger than Psyshock. Focus Blast synergizes well with Hoopa's STAB moves, hitting Dark-types such as Bombirdier and Wo-Chien that would otherwise hinder Hoopa's offensive progress. Trick is a useful utility move, hampering Pokemon such as Milotic and Porygon2 that Hoopa would otherwise do lackluster damage to. Tera Fighting further powers up Focus Blast, letting it do things such as 2HKO Grimmsnarl and Snorlax as well as potentially OHKO Skuntank and physically defensive Wo-Chien. It also presents amazing defensive benefits, giving Hoopa a resistance to Sucker Punch from Skuntank and Zoroark and lets it tank +2 Spell Tag-boosted Shadow Sneak from Tera Ghost Hisuian Decidueye at full health. Alternatively, Tera Ghost further powers up Shadow Ball, letting Hoopa 2HKO Alolan Sandslash and OHKO Salazzle while improving Hoopa's ability to clean late-game.

Choice Scarf Hoopa fits best on offensive teams as both a form of speed control and a fast wallbreaker and capable of overwhelming both offensive and defensive foes alike. Hoopa's STAB moves are resisted by Dark-types, which leaves it vulnerable to being taken advantage of by Pokemon like Bombirdier and Zoroark, relying on the inaccurate Focus Blast to hit them. As a result, Pokemon that can beat Dark-types such as Florges, Paldean Tauros-F, and Pawmot make for excellent partners, beating these threats while appreciating Hoopa's ability to break through the likes of Galarian Slowbro, Palossand, and Mudsdale. Additionally, these Pokemon appreciate Hoopa's speed control, opening them up to performing other roles. They can also absorb Knock Off, which lets Hoopa both maintain its speed control and its longevity. Entry hazard setters such as Mudsdale and Alolan Sandslash heavily appreciate Hoopa's capability as a spinblocker while helping chip down foes such as Rotom-Heat and Coalossal for Hoopa to KO. Other wallbreakers such as Shaymin and Sneasel can help wear down Dark-types such as Skuntank, Hisuian Qwilfish, and Grimmsnarl while appreciating Hoopa's high Speed with Choice Scarf.

Choice Specs.description:
Hoopa is one of the most powerful special wallbreakers thanks to its spammable Ghost- and Psychic-type STAB moves. Its good special bulk gives it opportunities to switch in and threaten foes like Florges, Galarian Slowbro, and Tatsugiri. Psyshock's advantage over Psychic is targeting specially bulky Pokemon like Snorlax, and it also circumvents the Special Defense boosts of setup sweepers like Calm Mind Florges and Quiver Dance Frosmoth. Focus Blast nails Dark-types like Brute Bonnet, and Hoopa can use it to blast past bulky Fighting-weak Pokemon like Rhydon, Naclstack, and specially defensive Coalossal. Trick punishes passive walls Hoopa might otherwise struggle to break through, such as Hisuian Qwilfish, and it also disrupts slower setup sweepers like Curse Snorlax. Tera Fighting remedies Hoopa's major vulnerability to Dark-type moves, notably Sucker Punch and Knock Off, while powering up its Focus Blast to the point it can OHKO Wo-Chien.

VoltTurn teams appreciate Hoopa as a strong wallbreaker they can bring in using pivots like Rotom-Heat, Hisuian Electrode, and Alolan Persian, and it's especially noteworthy for busting through problematic tanks and walls like Rhydon, Golurk, and Mudsdale. Slow and bulky pivots like Milotic and Eject Button Amoonguss are especially helpful at managing Hoopa's poor physical bulk by bringing it in safely against physical attackers like Passimian and Hisuian Decidueye. Hoopa's solid special bulk makes it a useful check to special attackers like Florges and Rotom-Heat, which is much appreciated by specially frail Pokemon like Tatsugiri, Golurk, and Mudsdale. Psychic-weak Pokemon, such as Paldean Tauros-F, similarly benefit from Hoopa checking many foes like Galarian Slowbro and Mesprit. Hoopa's 4x Dark and Ghost weaknesses make it reliant on teammates like Florges, Skuntank, and Hisuian Qwilfish. Physically offensive revenge killers like Bruxish and Pawmot are a major pain for Hoopa, which can be mitigated by having switch-ins like Palossand and Vileplume at the ready. Hoopa is quite slow for a wallbreaker, so it benefits from paralysis users like Grimmsnarl and Cramorant; notably, Grimmsnarl can ease Hoopa's ability to hit the field safely with Parting Shot.

Assault Vest.description:
Hoopa-U takes advantage of its staggering mixed attacking stats, coverage options, and STAB Knock Off and Psychic Noise to become a solid stallbreaker in the metagame. Simultaneously, the Assault Vest and physical bulk investment slightly improve its matchup against offensive teams, capable of trading hits decently well; in particular, Assault Vest magnifies Hoopa-U's natural special bulk to soft check common threats like Gholdengo, Darkrai, Kyurem, and Raging Bolt. Knock Off can remove valuable items like Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from foes like Ting-Lu and Alomomola, while Psychic Noise can shut down the recovery of Gliscor and Clefable, with an even wider range of Pokemon falling victim to both moves, including common defensive staples like Garganacl, Moltres, Clodsire, and Dondozo. Psychic Noise has the added benefit of stopping Hatterene and Primarina's Draining Kiss, letting Hoopa-U potentially win the one-on-one. Aside from providing Hoopa-U with decent longevity, Drain Punch reliably hits Dark-types like Ting-Lu, Darkrai, and Kingambit as well as common Tera Dark users like Clodsire, which can attempt to heal in the face of Hoopa-U's Psychic Noise. Thunderbolt immediately nails physically defensive Water- and Flying-types like Alomomola, Dondozo, Moltres, and Corviknight. On top of working well with Tera Poison, Gunk Shot is another option to threaten common Fairy-types and Tera Fairy users like Primarina, Hatterene, Clefable, Raging Bolt, and Gholdengo while netting the OHKO against Ogerpon-W; the poison chance is also handy against foes like Ting-Lu. The Special Attack EVs allow Hoopa-U to OHKO Keldeo with Psychic Noise, with the remaining Defense EVs letting it reach benchmarks such as surviving Ogerpon-W's Power Whip after Stealth Rock, +1 Tera Normal Dragonite's Extreme Speed after Stealth Rock, and +1 Speed Booster Energy Great Tusk's Headlong Rush. If not running Gunk Shot, then a spread of 252 HP / 156 Def / 100 SpA can be used instead, running enough Special Attack to OHKO Enamorus with Thunderbolt. Tera Fairy provides a generally valuable defensive typing against the metagame's Dragon- and Dark-types like Dragapult, Raging Bolt, Kyurem, and Weavile, while Tera Poison flips its Fairy weakness from foes like Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Primarina. Both Tera types provide a crucial U-turn resistance against pivots like Landorus-T, Dragapult, Cinderace, and Rillaboom as well as letting it stomach otherwise fearsome Fighting-type attacks from Zamazenta and physical Iron Valiant.

Hoopa-U works well on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its role compression as a strong stallbreaker and special tank. Defensive pivots like Galarian Slowking, Alomomola, Corviknight, Zapdos, and Moltres are necessary teammates; aside from bringing Hoopa-U into the field safely, they can deal with and switch into troublesome offensive threats that can overrun Hoopa-U, such as Enamorus, Hisuian Samurott, and Weavile. Moreover, Moltres, Zapdos, and Corviknight can punish otherwise no-drawback U-turns aimed at Hoopa-U from foes like Rillaboom, Landorus-T, and Ogerpon-W with Flame Body, Static, and Rocky Helmet, while Alomomola provides crucial Wish support for Hoopa-U. The aforementioned Corviknight as well as other entry hazard control options like Great Tusk and Cinderace also keep Hoopa-U healthy by removing troublesome hazards. The team's own entry hazards from setters like Garganacl, Gliscor, and Clefable are similarly important, as they take advantage of the switches that Hoopa-U forces and further exacerbates its ability to suffocate defensive teams, especially because it makes Heavy-Duty Boots users like Alomomola and Moltres vulnerable to them with Knock Off. Landorus-T is a phenomenal partner on bulky offense teams that similarly covers all of the aforementioned traits; it brings Hoopa-U in safely via U-turn, sets Stealth Rock, and switches into physical attackers like Great Tusk, Cinderace, and opposing Landorus-T. Other wallbreakers like Gholdengo and Raging Bolt can further pressure the opposition together with Hoopa-U, with Gholdengo also capable of defensively covering for its weaknesses against Iron Valiant. Hoopa-U works well with late-game cleaners like Zamazenta that appreciate its positive matchup against bulky teams that they tend to struggle with; in particular, Hoopa-U's ability to either threaten or overwhelm the likes of Dondozo, Moltres, and Clefable makes it take over games more easily. Furthermore, it also complements Hoopa-U by excelling against offensive teams that Hoopa-U has a harder time keeping up with, either offensively threatening or defensively handling foes like Kingambit and Weavile. Other offensive threats like Dragapult are great teammates too, with it in particular capable of bringing Hoopa-U on the field safely via U-turn and crippling foes like Kingambit with status to improve Hoopa-U's matchup against them.

Choice Band.description:
Hoopa-U finds itself a niche as a powerful wallbreaker that leverages its STAB moves and coverage to decimate defensive Pokemon like Toxapex, Gholdengo, and Alomomola. Hyperspace Fury is a spammable option with Choice Band that ensures Pokemon like Alomomola and Gliscor cannot scout safely, as it bypasses Protect, leaving them unable to properly check Hoopa-U. Drain Punch targets foes like Kingambit and Heatran while increasing Hoopa-U's longevity. Gunk Shot eviscerates Clefable and Tapu Fini, which would otherwise check Hoopa-U. Knock Off is another option that can remove key items from foes like Landorus-T, Zapdos, and Moltres. Hoopa-U can run an Adamant nature to get guaranteed OHKOs on Toxapex with Zen Headbutt and Slowbro with Hyperspace Fury. However, this means it gets outsped by foes like defensive Landorus-T, offensive Heatran, and Timid Raging Bolt.

Hoopa-U is used on bulky offense and balance teams, as they value its ability to pressure common defensive cores including Pokemon such as Gliscor, Toxapex, and Heatran. However, Hoopa-U is very frail and provides little defensive value, so it appreciates teammates like Alomomola, Landorus-T, and Corviknight that can help it safely pivot into Pokemon it does well against, such as Gholdengo and Gliscor. Hoopa-U is also vulnerable to faster threats with U-turn like Landorus-T and Mega Lopunny; therefore, it appreciates defensive pieces that can take a hit such and provide slow pivoting such as Corviknight and Alomomola. Hoopa-U also has a very middling Speed tier, leaving it outsped by Pokemon like Mega Medicham, Volcarona, and Tapu Lele. Therefore, teammates like Iron Valiant, Garchomp, and Mega Scizor are appreciated to help offensively pressure them. In return, Hoopa-U handles Pecharunt, Slowbro, and Clefable for them. Hoopa-U is vulnerable to Pursuit trapping from Pokemon like Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar that target its weaker Defense stat; thus, Pokemon that can check them such as Zamazenta, Corviknight, and Great Tusk make for good partners. The latter two also provide crucial entry hazard removal to maintain Hoopa-U's longevity. Galarian Slowking is another partner that can get Hoopa-U in safely via Chilly Reception and set Future Fight to assist with breaking through bulkier teams while also being a solid check to foes like Iron Valiant and Tapu Koko, which force out Hoopa-U.

Assault Vest.description:
Hoopa-U's outstanding offensive stats make it an excellent wallbreaker against foes such as Toxapex, Galarian Slowking, and Gholdengo. With Assault Vest, Hoopa-U's improved special bulk lets it trade against other wallbreakers such as Raging Bolt, Mega Latios, and the aforementioned Gholdengo, bolstering its matchup against offensive teams. Knock Off serves as a spammable STAB move, removing items such as Heavy-Duty Boots from Alomomola and Moltres, while Psychic Noise shuts down the longevity of Pokemon such as Gliscor, Clefable, and Mega Scizor. The latter also prevents Landorus-T or Fighting-types such as Zamazenta and Great Tusk from switching directly into Knock Off. Drain Punch hits Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott, Kingambit, and Mega Tyranitar while improving the longevtiy of Hoopa-U. Thunderbolt damages Alomomola, Moltres, and Corviknight, preventing them from pivoting in and enabling revenge killers as easily. Gunk Shot snipes Fairy-types, such as Clefable, Tapu Fini, and Tapu Koko, that would otherwise switch in and take out Hoopa-U. Hyperspace Fury is a stronger Dark-type move against Ghostium Z Gholdengo and Mega Latios, additionally being able to OHKO Mega Medicham after a layer of Spikes. It is also able to break through Gliscor's and Alomomola's Protect, shutting them down as reliable checks. However, the reduced Defense cuts into Hoopa-U's survivability. 252 HP EVs and 56 Special Defense EVs let Hoopa-U survive a Never-Ending Nightmare from +2 Gholdengo when at full HP. 64 Attack EVs let it OHKO Kingambit with Drain Punch after Stealth Rock, and 16 Speed EVs let it outspeed Adamant Kingambit. The rest is dumped into Special Attack, letting Hoopa-U OHKO Kommo-O after a layer of Spikes with Psychic Noise and giving it a chance to 2HKO specially defensive Moltres with Thunderbolt.

Hoopa-U's sheer power and trading capabilites make it a decent option on bulky offense and offense teams. Although Hoopa-U can fight against a lot of special attackers, it struggles heavily against physical blows. This makes physically defensive Pokemon such as Landorus-T and Alomomola very valuable teammates, especially against faster foes such as Mega Lopunny and Weavile that may try to revenge kill Hoopa-U. These two teammates can additionally pivot, providing Hoopa-U safe entry against foes it does well against, such as Zapdos and Gholdengo, while Alomomola in particular can make up for Hoopa-U's lack of recovery with Wish support. Despite having Drain Punch, Hoopa-U struggles heavily with Dark-types, especially Ting-Lu, since it is unable to damage Ting-Lu significantly. This makes Fighting- and Fairy-type teammates, such as Zamazenta, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Diancie, useful allies, since they're able to punish and break past Ting-Lu with ease; the latter can also prevent entry hazards from being set up, which improves Hoopa-U's longevity. In return, Hoopa-U is able to break past Poison-types such as Toxapex, Galarian Slowking, and Pecharunt, which these teammates don't like dealing with. Great Tusk has good synergy with Hoopa-U, since it removes hazards for Hoopa-U and can handle Dark-types such as Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar, and both can overwhelm shared checks such as Clefable and Alomomola. Additionally, Great Tusk, alongside Ferrothorn and Heatran, can set up hazards to help Hoopa-U break through Pecharunt and Landorus-T more easily, while they appreciate it removing Heavy-Duty Boots off of foes such as Moltres and Tornadus-T. Furthermore, Ferrothorn and Heatran help against Fairy-types, such as Iron Valiant and Tapu Lele, making them more appreciated. Gholdengo and Volcarona also check these Fairy-types while appreciating Hoopa-U's wallbreaking power, which allows them to clean late-game more easily. Volcarona, alongside Rocky Helmet users such as Landorus-T and Garchomp, can punish U-turn users that force out Hoopa-U, such as Mega Lopunny and Choice Scarf Landorus-T.

Choice Band.description:
• Hyperspace Fury targets Psychic-types like Iron Crown and Metagross as well as Ghost-types such as Skeledirge and Pecharunt.
  • Gunk Shot deals with Fairy-types such as non-Kebia Berry Azumarill, non-Custap Berry Primarina, and Sylveon.
  • Hoopa-U's last two moveslots are highly customizable. Zen Headbutt can handle Poison-types like Okidogi. Drain Punch allows Hoopa-U to beat Darkrai. Fire Punch beats non-Occa Berry Scizor, while Ice Punch is for non-Weakness Policy Galarian Moltres as well as Landorus; however, it should be noted that both Landorus formes can run U-turn to beat Hoopa-U.
  • Hoopa-U's HP and Special Defense EVs are to survive a Timid Choice Scarf Porygon-Z's Hyper Beam, with the rest put in Attack and Speed.
  • Hoopa-U can utilize an alternative EV spread of 240 HP / 252 Def / 16 Spe with an Impish nature to survive strong physical attacks from Meowscarada while also outspeeding Adamant Donphan and Iron Hands.
  • Hoopa-U struggles against Fairy- and Bug-type foes such as Iron Valiant and Volcarona, so Fire-type teammates such as Skeledirge and Volcanion are appreciated. Fast Choice Band Hoopa-U also struggles against faster physical attackers such as Ogerpon-W and Meowscarada; therefore, physical walls as partners like Pecharunt are helpful.

Choice Specs.description:
• Psychic Noise is used over Psychic, as it allows Hoopa-U to defeat Serperior.
  • Dark Pulse should be used against non-Disable Spectrier and Cresselia.
  • Thunderbolt allows Hoopa-U to beat Corviknight.
  • Grass Knot is for Rhyperior, while Focus Blast is strong into Hisuian Goodra.
  • Choice Specs Hoopa-U can use 52 HP EVs to survive Leaf Storm twice from non-Special Attack-invested Serperior. Additionally, 252 Speed EVs without a boosting nature allow Hoopa-U to outspeed Corviknight while also having the best odds against opposing Choice Specs Hoopa-U. The rest of the EVs and a Modest nature allow for maximum damage output.
  • Choice Specs Hoopa-U can also use an EV spread of 228 HP / 252 Def / 12 SpA / 16 Spe to survive Giga Impact from Assault Vest Ursaluna while outspeeding Adamant Donphan. The remaining EVs and a Modest nature allow for the best damage output while running this spread.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Hyperspace Fury should be used against Cresselia, Dragapult, Serperior, and Pecharunt.
  • Gunk Shot is for non-defensive Ogerpon-W and Meowscarada.
  • Focus Blast is for Chien-Pao and Porygon-Z.
  • Thunderbolt is for non-Maranga Berry Corviknight, while Rock Tomb is for non-bulky Volcarona.
  • The HP and Special Defense EVs let Hoopa-U survive Timid Choice Scarf Porygon-Z's Hyper Beam. Maximum Speed EVs and a Jolly nature allow Hoopa-U to outspeed Modest Choice Scarf Porygon-Z and Dragapult and Speed tie opposing Choice Scarf Hoopa-U. The remaining EVs are in Attack.
  • Hoopa-U should use the strongest move it has in most cases. Other cases include trying to outplay a potential Custap Berry foe like Custap Berry Porygon-Z, picking a more accurate move in case two moves can KO, and using Hyperspace Fury to bypass Substitute and Protect.

Assault Vest.description:
• Assault Vest Hoopa-U is a strong check to powerful special attackers like Porygon-Z and Volcanion.
  • Psychic Noise deals strong damage to Fighting-types like Iron Valiant, as well as threatening victories against Pokemon that make use of their recovery to win battles, such as stall Azumarill and Pecharunt.
  • Knock Off allows Hoopa-U to damage other Psychic-types like Cresselia and Iron Crown while removing important items like Custap Berry from Sylveon and Life Orb from Porygon-Z that could otherwise threaten Hoopa-U's ability to win the matchup.
  • Gunk Shot threatens KOs against Fairy-type Pokemon like Primarina and Sylveon.
  • Drain Punch is used to defeat various Pokemon that Hoopa-U may want to recover HP from, such as non-Chople Berry Hisuian Goodra and Porygon-Z.
  • The HP and Special Defense EVs are used to bulk +2 Life Orb Porygon-Z's Hyper Beam after Knock Off, and the Speed EVs outspeed neutral-natured maximum investment base 50 speed Pokemon like Donphan. The rest of the EVs are dumped into Attack.
  • This set aims to act as a blanket check to many special attackers in the tier, such as Primarina and Porygon-Z. However, Assault Vest Hoopa-U may lack the immediate fire power to deal enough damage to Pokemon like Corviknight or have enough Speed to defeat other Pokemon like faster Hoopa-U.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dark (Choice Specs)

A Timid nature allows Hoopa-U to outspeed Rash Kommo-o and Timid Heatran, which it can OHKO with Psychic and Focus Blast. It also enables Hoopa-U to punish common base 80 Speed Pokemon that are running an Attack-boosting nature like Adamant Dragonite and Mamoswine.

Dark (Choice Scarf)

Gunk Shot is great for threatening Fairy- and Grass-types like Primarina, Hatterene, and the Ogerpon formes. Focus Blast is another option to OHKO Archaludon, but its low accuracy is unappealing. Destiny Bond is a weird catch-all move that notably lets you trade with the Ogerpon formes, but it is very unreliable.

Psychic (Assault Vest)

Expanding Force can be used over Psychic and Psychic Noise if Hoopa-U is being paired with Indeedee-M. Gunk Shot can enable Hoopa-U to easily remove Hatterene and Primarina without any issues; however, its shaky accuracy and lack of use cases outside of hitting slow Fairy-types aren't ideal.

Choice Specs (Dark).description:
Hoopa-U is an unparalleled wallbreaker in the metagame, 2HKOing even the bulkiest walls like Corviknight and Empoleon with Dark Pulse, and its coverage also packs a punch to beat its would-be checks. Psychic OHKOes Fighting- and Poison-type Pokemon such as defensive Great Tusk, Iron Hands, Okidogi, and Toxapex. Psyshock can help break past Calm Mind users such as Primarina as well as physically defensive Quiver Dance Volcarona, Flutter Mane if it tries to switch in, Assault Vest Gallade, and Blissey. Thunderbolt OHKOes physically defensive Mandibuzz and Hisuian Samurott if the latter tries to switch in while also having a chance to OHKO Corviknight after Stealth Rock. Focus Blast can 2HKO Dark-types like Ting-Lu, Scrafty, and Alolan Muk that can otherwise stomach all of Hoopa-U's attacks while also being able to 2HKO Hisuian Goodra. 8 Special Defense EVs allow Hoopa-U to always tank Choice Scarf Flutter Mane's Moonblast from full HP.

Choice Specs Hoopa-U should be safely brought into battle via U-turn from Mandibuzz or Meowscarada. Mandibuzz switches into physical threats such as Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-H, easily healing with Roost and walling them. It also provides a ton of utility for Hoopa-U, being able to clear entry hazards with Defog. On the other hand, Choice Scarf Meowscarada can safely bring in Hoopa-U with U-turn by forcing switches into physical walls that Hoopa-U can break. It can also handle faster threats such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Roaring Moon, and Urshifu-R, which otherwise OHKO Hoopa-U. Ting-Lu sets Stealth Rock, allowing Hoopa-U to OHKO Pokemon such as Corviknight and Assault Vest Tornadus-T, while easily tanking special attacks. In particular, it can take Moonblast from Choice Scarf Flutter Mane and OHKO back with Heavy Slam. Choice Specs Greninja can take care of threats such as non-Choice Scarf variants of Sneasler and Iron Valiant with Extrasensory, Ogerpon-H and Hatterene with Sludge Wave, and Ceruledge with Surf. It can also help Hoopa-U pressure Flying and Dragon teams with Ice Beam. Choice Scarf Greninja can offensively check faster threats, including Dragapult and common Choice Scarf users like Landorus and Great Tusk. The Spikes that Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge sets help Hoopa-U force progress throughout the game. Additionally, Hisuian Samurott can break past Pokemon such as Hisuian Goodra and Alolan Muk that can give it trouble while also helping Hoopa-U apply pressure and win late-game scenarios against Ghost and Dragon teams.

Assault Vest (Psychic).description:
Assault Vest Hoopa-U serves as a great defensive and offensive piece for Psychic teams, easily handling the likes of Kyurem and Gholdengo for its teammates. Psychic is Hoopa-U's strongest offensive option, handling threats like Iron Moth and Walking Wake. Alternatively, Psychic Noise, while a drop in power, enables Hoopa-U to greatly impede the likes of Hatterene and Calm Mind Primarina by denying them access to Draining Kiss. Knock Off threatens opposing Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo, Flutter Mane, and Latios, along with hindering checks to Hoopa-U and its teammates reliant on their held items such as Assault Vest Tornadus-T and Alolan Muk. Focus Blast rips through Steel- and Dark-types like Archaludon, Heatran, and Darkrai. Drain Punch can also be used over Focus Blast to better handle Blissey and Hisuian Goodra. Finally, Thunderbolt shocks Flying- and Water-types such as Skarmory and Slowbro. The given EV spread allows Hoopa-U to outspeed Modest Magnezone while only having a minor chance of being 2HKOed by Choice Scarf Flutter Mane's Moonblast after a layer of Spikes.

With its low physical bulk and less-than-stellar Speed, Hoopa-U is greatly reliant on teammates such as Hatterene and Slowbro to come in and check foes like Kleavor while providing speed control through Nuzzle and Thunder Wave, respectively, allowing Hoopa-U to outspeed threats such as Hisuian Zoroark and opposing Hoopa-U. Hatterene checks Dark-types like Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Roaring Moon for Hoopa-U, along with preventing status and entry hazards from foes such as Gliscor and Ting-Lu with Magic Bounce. Slowbro, meanwhile, can assist against Fire- and Water-types like Cinderace, Hisuian Arcanine, and Urshifu-R and use Body Press to help break through Dark-types like Hisuian Samurott if using a Colbur Berry or go itemless to handle Ceruledge and physical Hisuian Zoroark. Metagross provides Stealth Rock for Hoopa-U, wearing down checks such as Scizor and Tornadus-T and using Bullet Punch to pick off faster targets like Mamoswine, Iron Valiant, and Flutter Mane. Choice Specs Latios provides a nice Ground immunity through Levitate, enabling it to help ward off Landorus and Gliscor while also using options such as Draco Meteor to cleanly remove the likes of Kyurem and Dragonite. Choice Scarf Indeedee-M can check Ghost-types like Ceruledge and Spectrier due to its Normal typing, along with using Healing Wish to keep Hoopa-U healthy in a pinch. Indeedee-M also sets Psychic Terrain with its ability Psychic Surge, preventing Hoopa-U from being picked off by Aqua Jet Azumarill. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder provides incredible speed control, handling faster threats like Ogerpon-H, Kleavor, and Meowscarada for Hoopa-U while greatly appreciating Hoopa-U removing physical walls like Skarmory.

Assault Vest (Dark).description:
Hoopa-U, when paired with an Assault Vest, can leverage its incredible Special Defense, enabling it to come in on threats like Kyurem and Heatran and proceed to cause immense havoc with its incredible base attacking stats. Psychic and Psyshock handle Poison- and Fighting-types like Toxapex and Iron Hands for Hoopa-U's teammates; Psychic OHKOes Galarian Weezing, while Psyshock removes Flutter Mane after Stealth Rock. Knock Off cripples special walls attempting to come in such as Alolan Muk, Tornadus-T, and Articuno, making it much easier for Hoopa-U and teammates like Greninja to wear them down. Focus Blast slams Steel- and Dark-types like Archaludon, Heatran, and Darkrai. Finally, Thunderbolt handles Water- and Flying-types such as Primarina, Pelipper, and Skarmory. The given EV spread allows Hoopa-U to outspeed Modest Magnezone while only having a minor chance of being 2HKOed by Choice Scarf Flutter Mane's Moonblast after a layer of Spikes.

Hoopa-U greatly appreciates support from Mandibuzz to make up for its poor Defense, with it checking threats like Choice Scarf Great Tusk, Excadrill, Scizor, and Ogerpon-W, along with pivoting Hoopa-U in safely with U-turn. Ting-Lu can provide entry hazard support that helps to wear down would-be switch-ins like Corviknight and Assault Vest Gallade, and its Ground typing makes it great at checking Raging Bolt. Choice Band Meowscarada is a strong wallbreaker able to check Ground- and Water-types such as Ting-Lu, Swampert, and Hisuian Samurott with Flower Trick while also using Triple Axel to handily check Gliscor and Dragonite. Choice Scarf Greninja greatly enjoys Hoopa-U breaking down special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Assault Vest Gallade and in return can outspeed and check threats such as Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, the Landorus formes, Enamorus, and Iron Valiant with options like Ice Beam and Sludge Wave. Hisuian Samurott and Bisharp can provide speed control with Sucker Punch picking off faster targets like physical Dragapult and Choice Specs Flutter Mane. Hisuian Samurott can also set Spikes with Ceaseless Edge and use Sacred Sword to check Blissey comfortably, while Bisharp can handle Fairy-types like Hatterene and Clefable. Sableye packs a helpful Fighting immunity, enabling it to safely come in on the likes of Sneasler and Hisuian Lilligant and hinder them with Will-O-Wisp. Sableye can also use Encore to trap walls like Articuno and Clodsire into their recovery options, allowing Hoopa-U to get onto the field safely.

Choice Band (Psychic).description:
Hoopa-U is one of Psychic's best physical wallbreakers. Its strong offensive STAB combination coupled with great coverage allows it to muscle through bulky Pokemon such as Skeledirge, Toxapex, Iron Hands, and Amoonguss, and with its great special bulk, it can prove useful against Ghost teams. Drain Punch grants Hoopa-U super effective coverage against Dark- and Steel-types such as Ting-Lu and Heatran. Brick Break can also be run as Hoopa-U's Fighting-type move, as this allows it to remove dual screens set by Fairy- and Dark-type teams. Trick is a great option for Hoopa-U to hinder Pokemon that can take a hit like Sableye and Klefki, as well as potentially disrupt Pokemon reliant on their items such as Moltres. Gunk Shot is another great option, as it allows Hoopa-U to threaten Fairy-types like Azumarill and to OHKO Hatterene. By investing 8 EVs in Special Defense, Hoopa-U can live a Moonblast from Choice Scarf Flutter Mane.

Azelf and Scream Tail make for great partners, as they can set up entry hazards for Hoopa-U to be able to wallbreak more easily. Azelf can also run Taunt to prevent Defog users like Corviknight removing its hazards, while Scream Tail can also set up dual screens for both Hoopa-U and its teammates and provide Wish support. Because of Hoopa-U's lack of longevity outside of Wish, it can get easily worn down by hazards. Hence, Hatterene is a great partner, as it is able to provide great hazard control for Psychic teams through Magic Bounce. Galarian Slowking is another great partner for Hoopa-U, as it provides Hoopa-U a switch-in to Fairy-types and aids Hoopa-U's wallbreaking through Future Sight. Galarian Slowking can also set up Toxic Spikes to annoy Hoopa-U's switch-ins such as Azumarill, and its Poison typing allows it to remove Toxic Spikes to prevent Hoopa-U from getting worn down by poison. Indeedee is another great addition to Psychic teams, as its Normal typing grants it an immunity to Ghost. Aside from this, Indeedee can set up Psychic Terrain to allow Hoopa-U to threaten Bisharp with Drain Punch without fearing Sucker Punch. Lastly, late-game sweepers such as Gallade and Armarouge appreciate Hoopa-U beating their checks such as Azumarill for the former and Galarian Slowking for the latter.

Choice Scarf (Psychic).description:
Boasting stellar offenses, Choice Scarf Hoopa-U grants Psychic teams a form of speed control as well as a threatening wallbreaker, outspeeding the whole unboosted metagame bar Deoxys-S and Regieleki, especially key targets such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Choice Band Dragapult. Hyperspace Fury OHKOes both Flutter Mane and Dragapult and can be used to break through special tanks such as Hisuian Goodra and Galarian Slowking. Dark Pulse complements it nicely by offering a powerful neutral attack against physically bulky Steel- and Water-types like Archaludon, Iron Treads, Scizor, and Toxapex. Alternatively, Focus Blast targets Dark-type foes like Darkrai and Bisharp. Psychic covers Fighting and Fairy matchups, preventing threats like Iron Valiant and Great Tusk from switching in safely. Expanding Force is a viable alternative if the team uses Psychic Terrain, transforming Hoopa-U into a killing machine for the Terrain's duration. The last moveslot aims at targeting specific foes. Thunderbolt deals with Hisuian Samurott and Greninja, while Gunk Shot helps against the Ogerpon formes. 8 Special Defense EVs allow Hoopa-U to always survive a Moonblast from Choice Scarf Flutter Mane from full health.

Hoopa-U immensely benefits from Galarian Slowking and Hatterene; they can both support Hoopa-U in multiple ways. Galarian Slowking strengthens the wallbreaking potential of Hoopa-U with Future Sight and a slow pivoting option in the form of Chilly Reception. Hatterene can send entry hazards back to the opponent; paralyze the target with Nuzzle; take care of most Dark-types such as Roaring Moon, Hisuian Samurott, and Meowscarada; and provide Healing Wish support to Hoopa-U. Slowbro helps mitigate Hoopa-U's poor physical bulk by absorbing physical moves, spreading burns with Scald, and effectively hard-countering physical bulky setup sweepers such as Dragonite with its IronPress combination. Indeedee-M sets up Psychic Terrain, effectively negating any priority move for the Terrain's duration and massively boosting Hoopa-U's potential with Expanding Force, and has access to Healing Wish in case of need. Lastly, Hoopa-U appreciates other sweeper teammates such as Latios, Metagross, and Iron Boulder that can weaken defensive cores of types like Fairy, Flying, and Fire to allow a proper Hoopa-U sweep. Latios is especially threatening to Flying teams with access to BoltBeam coverage and a powerful STAB move in Draco Meteor, while Metagross and Iron Boulder can both offer a breaking potential similar to Latios's in Fairy and Fire matchups, respectively, with access to Heavy Slam, Bullet Punch, and Stealth Rock for Metagross and Mighty Cleave on top of naturally outspeeding both Meowscarada and Greninja for Iron Boulder.

Choice Scarf (Dark).description:
Choice Scarf Hoopa-U is an amazing option on Dark teams thanks to its great Attack stat. Knock Off allows Hoopa-U to not only remove items from foes like Alolan Muk and Articuno but also takes out threats like Choice Specs Flutter Mane. Drain Punch deals with Dark-, Normal-, Steel-, and Ice-types like Greninja, Blissey, Hisuian Goodra, and Weavile, while Psychic cleans up Poison- and Fighting-types like Galarian Weezing, Okidogi, mixed attacker Iron Valiant, and Choice Specs Keldeo. Thunderbolt is a great coverage move, handling Flying- and Water-types like Skarmory, Corviknight, and Gyarados. Trick can be run over Thunderbolt to Choice-lock foes like Calm Mind Primarina, Ting-Lu, and Archaludon; however, without Thunderbolt Hoopa-U cannot reliably deal with Skarmory, which can then wall it. The given EV spread allows Hoopa-U to survive a Moonblast from Choice Scarf Flutter Mane and retaliate back with Knock Off. Its special bulk is also notable, allowing it to trade blows with the likes of Iron Valiant.

Alolan Muk is a great special wall, easing the Fairy matchup thanks to its Poison typing while dealing with Primarina and Hatterene with Poison Jab. Choice Scarf Meowscarada deals with Water-, Ground- and Fighting-types like Urshifu-R, Quagsire, and Choice Scarf Iron Valiant with Flower Trick and Play Rough. Choice Specs Greninja covers a lot of matchups thanks to Protean, notably taking out the Ogerpon formes, Hatterene, and the Landorus formes with Sludge Wave and Ice Beam. Sableye provides a Fighting immunity while also weakening physical threats like Excadrill, Sneasler, and Choice Scarf Great Tusk with Will-O-Wisp. Sableye can also use Encore on setup sweepers like Zamazenta and spread paralysis with Thunder Wave so Hoopa-U can outspeed faster threats. Mandibuzz provides entry hazard removal for Hoopa-U with Defog and slow pivoting with U-turn. Mandibuzz also checks Swords Dance sweepers like Ogerpon-H and Scizor with Foul Play. It's also worth mentioning that Mandibuzz provides a Ground immunity, which allows it to come in on Choice Scarf Great Tusk's Headlong Rush for Hoopa-U. Ting-Lu is a great wall that can lay down hazards with Stealth Rock and Spikes, which chip down threats like Iron Valiant and Zamazenta. Ting-Lu also handles Steel-types like non-Air Balloon Heatran and Hisuian Goodra with Earthquake and phazes setup sweepers like Swords Dance Garchomp and Dragon Dance Dragonite with Whirlwind. Hydreigon also sets hazards with Stealth Rock while taking out Dragon-types like Archaludon with Draco Meteor. In return, Hoopa-U deals with Skarmory, Galarian Weezing, and Iron Valiant for its teammates.

Offensive / Trapper.description:
Volcanion is a powerful wallbreaker with phenomenal coverage, making it extremely difficult to switch into, that provides great defensive utility by checking threats like Skeledirge and Scizor. Sludge Bomb nails Azumarill and Hydrapple for super effective damage. It is also Volcanion's best way to wear down Slowking, Latios, and Assault Vest Tornadus-T, especially with the high chance to inflict poison. Taunt allows Volcanion to shut down Pokemon like Toxapex and Slowking, preventing recovery from both, Toxic from the former, and the ability to pivot with Chilly Reception from the latter. Tera Blast Fairy helps Volcanion threaten Quaquaval and Latios better. Earth Power is an alternative that can 2HKO Toxapex and Fezandipiti and also hits the rarer Empoleon hard, too. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Volcanion to capitalize on its typing and ability to check Pokemon like Greninja and Azumarill. A Modest nature is generally preferred for the increased damage output, though a Timid nature can be considered if Volcanion needs to outspeed Mamoswine or offensive Heatran. Tera Fairy allows Volcanion to take a Dark Pulse or Close Combat from Greninja and Quaquaval, respectively, allowing it to check both of them in a pinch while punishing Choice-locked Latios and Hydrapple.

Volcanion fits best on bulky offense and balance teams that value its ability to check dangerous foes like Greninja and Azumarill while being a powerful wallbreaker itself. Although it is a solid answer to the Pokemon mentioned previously, Volcanion does appreciate having partners such as Tornadus-T, Mandibuzz, and Skarmory. Tornadus-T and Mandibuzz can also allow Volcanion to fire off powerful attacks by bringing it in safely against Pokemon like Heatran and Tinkaton. Cobalion and Sandy Shocks are other pivots that can be paired with Volcanion but also can provide entry hazard support, which is key to wearing down Assault Vest Tornadus-T. Cobalion can also provide Thunder Wave support to cripple Tornadus-T and Latios, making it easier for Volcanion to pressure them; it is also an excellent check to Ogerpon-C, which threatens Volcanion. Despite beating Slowking and Toxapex, breaking through them is a slow process, so partners like Thundurus-T, Zarude, and Hydrapple are appreciated for removing them. Thundurus-T can act as a strong offensive pivot to get Volcanion in on the likes of Hydrapple and defensive Heatran; the last two are able to force out Latios, with Zarude in particular also being a strong response to Greninja and Rotom-W, which can pressure Volcanion. Due to Volcanion commonly wanting to pivot into Azumarill and Scizor, it has the tendency to get hit by Knock Off, leaving it susceptible to hazards. Excadrill pairs well to remove them. Excadrill is also a great check to Latios and can apply pressure to Electric-types like Rotom-W that typically threaten Volcanion.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Volcanion acts as a deadly wallbreaker that can hit common defensive Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Heatran for super effective damage while also crippling Pokemon such as Dragonite and Dragapult that could otherwise take an attack with a nasty burn from Steam Eruption. Sludge Bomb allows Volcanion to 2HKO Primarina and even OHKO Ogerpon-W, as well as hitting Pokemon such as Assault Vest Alomomola and Latios that might otherwise check it. Earth Power slams Raging Bolt and Toxapex that could otherwise tank Volcanion's attacks easily. Tera Water gives Steam Eruption a massive boost in power, allowing Volcanion to 2HKO Assault Vest Galarian Slowking, Kyurem, and Raging Bolt, while Tera Ground gives Volcanion an Electric immunity to take on Pokemon such as Zapdos and Raging Bolt more easily. This also gives it a chance to OHKO Galarian Slowking after Stealth Rock with Earth Power. Tera Fairy can instead be considered to give Volcanion a valuable Fighting- and Dark-type resistance to help it take a hit from Pokemon such as Zamazenta, Kingambit, and Darkrai. Additionally, Tera Fairy allows Volcanion to be completely immune to Walking Wake's STAB moves. A maximum HP spread with minimum Speed and a Quiet nature can be used on Trick Room teams to give Volcanion the ability to outspeed a large majority of the metagame under Trick Room.

Choice Specs Volcanion fits best on bulky offense and balance teams, which heavily appreciate its ability to check Pokemon such as Primarina and Ogerpon-W while also helping it get in consistently against a variety of threats. Volcanion suffers from a crippling weakness to Stealth Rock when using Choice Specs; therefore, entry hazard removal options such as Hatterene, Galarian Weezing, Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads are great partners for it. While Volcanion can certainly hit common Dragon-types such as Dragonite and Raging Bolt hard, they can typically stomach the attack and hit it back for massive damage. Therefore, Pokemon such as Hatterene, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu that can check the aforementioned Dragon-types are heavily appreciated by Volcanion, while in return, Volcanion can check Pokemon such as Cinderace and Corviknight. Revenge killers such as Iron Valiant, Deoxys-S, and Dragonite pair nicely with Volcanion, as they can either outspeed or in the case of the latter, use priority moves against common threats to Volcanion such as Ogerpon-W and Enamorus; in return, Volcanion can help chip down bulkier foes such as Galarian Slowking and Zamazenta that they can struggle against. Pivot Pokemon such as Zapdos, Dragapult, and Tornadus-T are great for Volcanion, as they can help get it in safely against threats such as Tyranitar and Ting-Lu, while in return, Volcanion can threaten common answers to the Pokemon mentioned above such as Kingambit and Enamorus. Hazard setters such as Deoxys-S and Landorus-T are useful partners for Volcanion, as they can help it pressure switch-ins such as Assault Vest Alomomola and Galarian Slowking, deny hazards with Taunt, and set up dual screens and pivot out to it, respectively. Ground-type Pokemon such as Landorus-T, Iron Treads, and Great Tusk are immensely threatening to Volcanion, as while they cannot directly switch into it, they can outspeed and do massive damage to it as well as set up Stealth Rock. Therefore, Pokemon such as Corviknight, Zamazenta, and Rillaboom can be great partners for Volcanion by answering each of these Ground-types, respectively. Rillaboom, in particular, is a great partner, as not only can it easily pivot to Volcanion, but its Grassy Terrain can provide passive healing to Volcanion while also reducing the power of Earthquake. If Volcanion is run on a Trick Room team, then partners such as Cresselia, Mimikyu, and Hatterene are great for not only setting up Trick Room, but then getting it in safely. Hatterene, in particular, is a great partner, as it is able to keep off Stealth Rock, which otherwise cuts into Volcanion's bulk. Fellow Trick Room attackers such as Ursaluna, Kingambit, and Enamorus-T are also valued, as they overwhelm teams with their sheer power.

Utility Attacker.description:
Volcanion brings a niche as a strong bulky attacker that can reliably switch into foes like Primarina and Alomomola with its Water Absorb ability, spreading burns through its powerful Steam Eruption. Sludge Bomb is used to hit targets like Primarina and Ogerpon-W for super effective damage while spreading poison onto checks like Alomomola and Dragapult. Taunt lets Volcanion prevent setup opportunities from Pokemon like Primarina while also preventing status moves such as Galarian Slowking's Chilly Reception and Alomomola's Wish; Taunt notably irritates walls like Blissey and Toxapex. Will-O-Wisp, meanwhile, actively cripples physical attackers like Ogerpon-W, Zamazenta, and Dragonite. It pairs especially well with Steam Eruption, as usual Will-O-Wisp absorbers like Moltres, Heatran, and Gliscor cannot switch into Volcanion safely. Fire Spin is an alternative move over Flamethrower that can be used in combination with Taunt to trap foes like Blissey and Alomomola to stallbreak incredibly well. Earth Power can also be used to hit Raging Bolt and Galarian Slowking. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Volcanion reliably switch in on foes like Ogerpon-W and Primarina without dealing with entry hazard chip damage. Roar can be used to phaze attackers such as Kingambit, Iron Valiant, and Primarina. On teams with solid hazard control, Leftovers and Shuca Berry can be used. The former is able to passively heal to better leverage Volcanion's fantastic natural bulk, while the latter lets it tank a Ground-type attack from Dragonite, Great Tusk, and Enamorus and fire back with an attack or Will-O-Wisp. Custap Berry is an alternative option that is able to leverage Volcanion's trading ability to take out revenge killers like Great Tusk and Iron Moth. Maximum Special Attack and Speed lets Volcanion get the jump on Gliscor, Moltres, and Tyranitar, giving it opportunities to deal heavy damage. However, a bulkier spread that can let Volcanion outspeed Adamant Kingambit can be used, allowing it to be able to survive uninvested Great Tusk's Headlong Rush and offensive Landorus-T's Earthquake while becoming a better check to Primarina, Iron Valiant, and Cinderace. 112 Defense EVs can be used alongside maximum HP to let Volcanion survive maximum Attack Great Tusk's Headlong Rush. Tera Ghost lets Volcanion spinblock against Great Tusk and Iron Treads, check Zamazenta, and be immune to Blissey's Seismic Toss on Fire Spin sets. Tera Fairy gives Volcanion an improved matchup against Fighting- and Dragon-types like Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, and Dragapult while being a better neutral defensive typing and, notably, becoming immune to both of Walking Wake's STAB moves.

Volcanion slots in nicely on offensive teams, as it can take advantage of its defensive qualities to fire off intense damage. Volcanion enjoys entry hazard setters like Hisuian Samurott, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu as teammates, as they can shore up its lack of boosting item, with Flamethrower being able to OHKO bulky Kingambit after a single layer of Spikes or Stealth Rock. Landorus-T and Ting-Lu protect Volcanion from Zapdos and Raging Bolt while also sponging physical and special attackers, respectively. Landorus-T can switch into Great Tusk and Iron Treads, while Ting-Lu switches in on Dragapult. In return, Volcanion helps both handle Weavile and Hatterene. Volcanion without Heavy-Duty Boots struggles against hazards, making Hatterene, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads desirable as teammates. Great Tusk and Iron Treads can also set hazards and check Raging Bolt, while Hatterene can paralyze foes like Enamorus with Nuzzle; in return, Volcanion scares Corviknight out. Fast teammates like Deoxys-S and Calm Mind Iron Valiant make up for Volcanion's poor Speed, scaring out faster threats like Tornadus-T and Stone Edge Zamazenta. Volcanion, in return, wears down shared checks like Galarian Slowking and Garganacl. Similarly, other special attackers like Darkrai, Gholdengo, and Pecharunt appreciate Volcanion beating down their checks like Ting-Lu and Assault Vest Hisuian Samurott. Fairy-types like the aforementioned Iron Valiant and Enamorus are excellent teammates for their ability to get rid of Dragapult and Dragonite. Steel-types like Air Balloon Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Iron Crown assist Volcanion against Kyurem. Kingambit, notably, aides against Ghost-types like Dragapult and Pecharunt, provides a strong Sucker Punch for threats like Deoxys-S, and gets rid of Galarian Slowking. In return, Volcanion targets annoyances to Kingambit such as Corviknight, Ting-Lu, and Cinderace.

Air Balloon.description:
• Volcanion uses Air Balloon to lure Ground-types, such as Landorus-T, Ursaluna and Donphan, while maintaining its strong matchups against Fairy- and Steel-type Pokemon.
  • Steam Eruption is Volcanion's most consistent STAB move. It hits the Ground-types that Air Balloon lures as well as Fire Types like Volcarona and Skeledirge.
  • Sludge Wave hits Primarina, which Volcanion walls with its ability and typing, super effectively. It also offers an essential second coverage option against Encore + Disable Alolan Ninetales and Iron Valiant.
  • Substitute tanks Ursaluna's Giga Impact and Choice Band Donphan's Head Smash, allowing Volcanion to attack freely after the recharge turn and recoil damage respectively.
  • The defensive EVs allow Volcanion to survive Adamant Choice Band Meowscarada's Giga Impact and Timid Choice Specs Iron Valiant's Focus Blast. 96 Speed EVs allow Volcanion to outpace Adamant Ursaluna while maximizing its Special Attack. 232 Speed EVs let it outpaces fast Corviknight.
  • It should be noted that while Air Balloon flips a lot of matchups, it does not automatically beat all powerful Earthquake users. Garchomp and Haxorus are both still highly favored to win against Volcanion.
  • Iron Valiant is a classic partner with Volcanion. Iron Valiant covers the Dragon-types that Volcanion struggles with, while Volcanion covers the Steel and Fairy-types that Iron Valiant loses to. Air Balloon lets it synergizes particularly well, as it covers the few Ground-types that can present issues for Iron Valiant without an offensive set.
  • Despite its typing, Volcanion can struggle against Iron Crown without the help of a stat-boosting item like Assault Vest or Life Orb. Therefore, Dark-types such as Hoopa-U and Urshifu-S make for strong partners.

Choice Specs.description:
• Volcanion uses its unique typing and high Special Attack to carve its role as a strong, bulky attacker.
  • Steam Eruption is a strong STAB move to OHKO Pokemon such as Volcarona, Skeledirge, and non-Speed invested Ursaluna.
  • Overheat hits Corviknight, Metagross, Meowscarada, and non-specially defensive Iron Crown.
  • Sludge Wave is solid coverage to use versus Primarina, Ogerpon-W, Sylveon, and non-Encore + Disable Iron Valiant.
  • Hyper Beam hits Haxorus for an OHKO.
  • The defensive EVs allow Volcanion to survive an Earthquake from Choice Band Haxorus while also taking Sylveon's Hyper Beam after Fake Tears.
  • Volcanion struggles to defeat Dragon-types such as Raging Bolt and Hisuian Goodra. It can therefore be paired with Pokemon such as Iron Valiant, Iron Crown, and Sylveon to cover these weaknesses.

Life Orb.description:
• The combination of Life Orb and Flame Charge allows Volcanion to consistently beat Iron Crown, chipping Weakness Policy sets into Overheat range and scouting against Assault Vest Metal Burst sets. Flame Charge is also useful against SubSeed users such as Ogerpon-W and Serperior.
  • The defensive EVs allow it to survive Adamant Choice Band Meowscarada's Giga Impact and Timid Choice Specs Iron Valiant's Focus Blast. 232 Speed EVs let it outpace Ogerpon-W after a Flame Charge boost as well as fast Corviknight .
  • Volcanion's powerful STAB combination hits prominent Steel and Fire-types such as Metagross and Volcarona.
  • Sludge Wave is necessary Water-types with a dual typing such as Primarina and Ogerpon-W.
  • Combined with its natural ability to check Fairy- and Fire- type Pokemon, a Volcanion set specialized for the most threatening Steel-types in the tier is most appreciated by Fairy-type Pokemon such as Alolan Ninetales and, in particular, Iron Valiant. Offensive Iron Valiant sets can check various threats to Volcanion such as Hisuian Goodra and Hoopa-U. Alolan Ninetales easily handles Ground-types like Landorus-T and Garchomp.

Sitrus Berry.description:
• Will-O-Wisp and a Sitrus Berry allow Volcanion to turn the tables against Urshifu-S, a common Pokemon other Volcanion sets are not as consistent against.
  • Overheat and Steam Eruption are necessary on all Volcanion sets as primary STAB moves.
  • Sludge Wave allows Volcanion to be consistent against most Fairy-types, especially the likes of Primarina and Azumarill, which resist both of its STAB moves.
  • The Defense investment allows Volcanion to survive two Close Combats from Adamant Choice Band Urshifu thanks to Sitrus Berry's recovery and a burn from Will-O-Wisp. With the additional Special Defense investment, Modest Choice Specs Iron Valiant also fails to OHKO Volcanion with Thunderbolt.
  • To defeat the Urshifu formes, use Will-O-Wisp and then attack with either Sludge Wave against Urshifu-R or Steam Eruption against Urshifu-S. It should be noted that Urshifu-R usually defeats this Volcanion set with Choice Band Low Kick, but this sequence gives good chances against other sets like IronPress and Assault Vest.
  • Make sure to swap moves between turns when against a potential Encore + Disable user like Iron Valiant or Alolan Ninetales. Otherwise, Volcanion will end up locked into a disabled move with Encore and forced to use Struggle. To avoid this fate, use Sludge Wave followed by Steam Eruption against Iron Valiant and Overheat followed by Sludge Wave against Alolan Ninetales.
  • Volcanion is an excellent teammate for many high-tier Pokemon that struggle against Steel- or Fairy-types like Iron Valiant, Alolan Ninetales, Urshifu-S, Annihilape, and Garchomp. In return, these Pokemon can cover various top threats that Volcanion doesn't usually defeat such as Pecharunt, Hoopa-U, Ursaluna, Raging Bolt, and Hisuian Goodra.

monotype.overview:
Water

Volcanion is a solid option for Water teams thanks to its unique typing and outstanding offenses. What it lacks in utility, it makes up for in sheer power if given the right opportunities to wallbreak, easily dismantling common defensive cores on Steel and Flying. However, Water has no shortage of great special wallbreakers like Walking Wake, Keldeo, and Choice Specs Greninja, which are all faster and easier to get onto the field. Volcanion also struggles to break through common Dragon-types like Latios and Raging Bolt while freely letting them make progress.

Wallbreaker (Water).description:
Volcanion’s best traits are its unique offensive typing and signature move, which give it substantial natural wallbreaking capabilities, especially against Steel teams, and allow it to run Heavy-Duty Boots instead of a boosting item. Steam Eruption is an excellent STAB option that has a high chance to burn, dissuading Water-resistant physical attackers like Dragonite and Dondozo from switching in. Earth Power is essential coverage to hit switch-ins like Toxapex and Hisuian Goodra as hard as possible. Substitute generally eases prediction against targets that are likely to switch out and enables more sustained pressure against teams with multiple soft checks, such as Ground and Water teams. Sludge Bomb allows Volcanion to solidly check Azumarill and Primarina while also functioning as it's strongest move against one of Water teams' biggest threats, Ogerpon-W.

Defensive pivots are great for getting Volcanion on the field safely. Rotom-W checks opposing Ground-types like Sand Rush Excadrill, and Swampert checks opposing Electric-types like Iron Hands. Urshifu-R is an exceptional offensive pivot that can threaten Blissey and Hisuian Goodra while using U-turn on its checks, such as Corviknight and Mandibuzz, to bring Volcanion in for free. Ogerpon-W has great offensive synergy with Volcanion, as they can overwhelm each other's mutual checks like Toxapex. Hisuian Samurott can help wear down switch-ins like Alolan Muk and Assault Vest Iron Hands with Spikes while also threatening certain Dragon-types like Dragapult and Latios with Sucker Punch. After Multiscale is broken, Choice Scarf Greninja can use Ice Beam to revenge kill +1 Dragonite, which otherwise sets up on Volcanion easily. Even when running Choice Specs, Greninja still functions as an excellent late-game cleaner once walls like Hisuian Goodra have been worn down while also making progress against Volcanion's defensive checks such as Clodsire and Toxapex with Extrasensory. If running Substitute, Toxapex is greatly appreciated for its ability to handle Primarina and Ogerpon-W, both of which set up on a weakened Volcanion, as well as threats such as Keldeo and Kleavor.

Water Absorb (Fire).description:
Volcanion is a useful Pokemon on Fire teams mainly thanks to its ability, Water Absorb, offering the type an immunity to one of its most common weaknesses. Steam Eruption is Volcanion's preferred Water-type move, with it being able to burn its switch-ins like Alolan Muk, Hisuian Goodra, and Iron Hands, reducing their overall longevity. Earth Power allows Volcanion to threaten opposing Volcanion, Toxapex, and Heatran. Sludge Bomb allows Volcanion to revenge kill Azumarill after a Belly Drum and threaten other Fairy-type Pokemon like Hatterene and Enamorus. It is also able to target Walking Wake and Rotom-W, which resist Volcanion's STAB attacks, potentially crippling them thanks to the 30% poison chance. Flamethrower is preferred over Fire Blast since it doesn't miss, and the reduced damage is not too significant if Volcanion is under sun, but Fire Blast can be used in order to 2HKO Hisuian Goodra under sun. 96 Speed EVs let Volcanion outspeed Adamant Azumarill in order to revenge kill it with Sludge Bomb, and the rest of the EVs are put in HP to improve Volcanion's overall bulk.

Torkoal is a solid partner for Volcanion that assists it with Stealth Rock support, chipping down its switch-ins like Rotom-W and Alolan Muk and working well in conjunction with Steam Eruption's burn chance. Torkoal can also use Rapid Spin to clear away entry hazards for Volcanion if its Heavy-Duty Boots get removed by Alolan Muk or Meowscarada. Furthermore, Torkoal provides Volcanion with sun thanks to Drought, which boosts Volcanion's Fire-type attacks. In return, Volcanion can switch into Water-type attacks from Barraskewda and Pelipper, which threaten Torkoal. Scovillain helps out Volcanion by threatening Water-immune Pokemon like Clodsire and Gastrodon, and its damage onto the former allows Volcanion to revenge kill it and proceed to threaten slower Ground-types like Quagsire and Ting-Lu. Cinderace is able to threaten Hisuian Goodra with Libero High Jump Kick, whose Assault Vest set easily shrugs off Earth Power from Volcanion and chips it down with Draco Meteor. Cinderace can also steal dual screens from Klefki with Court Change in the Fairy matchup, which supplement Volcanion's naturally good bulk, letting it take hits better. In return, Volcanion offers an answer to Belly Drum Azumarill and threatens Cinderace's defensive answers like Toxapex and Skeledirge. Choice Scarf Hisuian Arcanine offers a solution to handle opposing Dragon-types like Baxcalibur, which can use Volcanion as setup fodder, and also threatens Dragapult and non-Choice Scarf Hydreigon. Rotom-Heat provides an invaluable Ground immunity for Volcanion to avoid Earthquake from Pokemon like Iron Hands, Iron Treads, and Landorus-T and threatens all 3 of them with a burn from Will-O-Wisp. Rotom-H is also able to threaten defensive Water-types like Toxapex and offensive Water-types like Hisuian Samurott and Quaquaval if it opts for a Choice Scarf. Heatran can help Volcanion deal with Poison teams with its stallbreaker set, which allows it to trap and beat Pokemon like Toxapex one-on-one. Choice Scarf Iron Moth can revenge kill weakened Dragon-types like Walking Wake and Baxcalibur.

Bulky Attacker.description:
Volcanion is a strong, bulky attacker that provides a Water immunity to teammates with Water Absorb. Haze lets Volcanion remove stat boosts from foes such as Gholdengo and Iron Hands, while Earth Power hits foes such as Iron Hands and Archaludon. Roar can be used as an alternative to Haze that's especially good on more defensive and entry hazard stack teams that Volcanion fits well on. Leftovers allows Volcanion to slowly heal itself, making it harder for it to be overwhelmed. Heavy-Duty Boots removes Volcanion's weakness to Stealth Rock, particularly benefiting more defensive teams, as it is harder for them prevent entry hazards from being set up, as well as helping Volcanion to pivot around more easily. Ability Shield is an alternative option that allows Volcanion to keep its Water-type immunity against teams with a Mold Breaker user. If Volcanion is being used on a team with Tailwind, then using 108 Speed EVs is recommended, as this allows it to outspeed Chien-Pao in Tailwind. Volcanion struggles with strong attackers such as Landorus and Raging Bolt due to its middling Speed allowing it to be overwhelmed easily. Tera Fairy is used as an all-round good defensive typing, giving useful resistances to moves such as Chien-Pao's Dark-type coverage and Dragon-type coverage from Pokemon like Walking Wake, Latios, and Kingdra. However, Tera Fairy can leave Volcanion vulnerable to foes such as Gholdengo. Tera Ground is an alternative option that turns Volcanion's weakness to Electric-type moves from foes like Raging Bolt and Iron Hands into an immunity while also powering up its Earth Power. In a pinch, Volcanion can support its ally by targeting it with Steam Eruption, healing it due to Water Absorb.

Notable Partners

Ground-types: Ground-types such as Ting-Lu and both Landorus formes are great partners for Volcanion, as it can protect them from Water-type attacks with Water Absorb. Additionally, Ting-Lu and Landorus-T increase Volcanion's bulk with their abilities, while Landorus increases the power of Volcanion's attacks with Sheer Force, and Volcanion gives it Fire- and Water-type coverage in return. These Ground-types also are very strong against Electric-type foes such as Raging Bolt and Iron Hands that Volcanion struggles with.

Physical Attackers: Physical attackers like Rillaboom and Chien-Pao appreciate Volcanion being strong against Incineroar. The two examples given are also strong against the Ground-type foes such as Landorus and Landorus-T that threaten Volcanion.

Entry Hazard Setters: Volcanion appreciates teammates such as Mew, Ting-Lu, and Deoxys-D that can set entry hazards, as they can help chip down foes into range of Volcanion's attacks and take advantage of Pokemon trying to pivot around Volcanion. Additionally, entry hazards can force damage onto any foes that are forced to switch in due to Roar.

Prankster Users Prankster Pokemon like Tornadus, Grimmsnarl, and Whimsicott can help Volcanion by giving priority to Haze, allowing it to negate stat boosts before setup foes deal any meaningful damage.
