Wallbreaker.description: Volcanion's unique Water / Fire typing allows it to be a very threatening wallbreaker on balance and bulky offense teams with strong defensive utility, capable of checking threats such as Scizor and Clefable while also pressuring the likes of Hippowdon, Buzzwole, Skarmory, and Celesteela. Steam Eruption, in addition to being a powerful STAB option, is also very useful at spreading burns in order to weaken potential checks such as Mega Venusaur and Slowking. Sludge Bomb is used in order to break Clefable while also heavily damaging switch-ins such as Mega Latias and Hydreigon with a chance to poison them. Alternatively, Hidden Power Grass can be used in order to combat Slowbro and Gastrodon that would otherwise easily switch into Volcanion. Volcanion also offers some utility with Defog, being able to use its offensive capabilities to force out common entry hazard setters such as Tyranitar, Skarmory, and Hippowdon and clear hazards as they flee. Taunt is another utility option that allows Volcanion to shut down the likes of Calm Mind Clefable and Leech Seed Celesteela more efficiently while also preventing Slowking and Slowbro from using Teleport and Slack Off. Alternatively, Volcanion can forego its utility options in exchange for Earth Power in order to target threats such as Okidogi and other Volcanion. Heavy-Duty Boots is Volcanion's main item of choice in order to avoid damage from entry hazards, but it can also run Shuca Berry on more offensive playstyles in order to lure threats attempting to use Ground-type attacks against it, such as Excadrill and Enamorus. Wallbreakers like Hydreigon make for a solid offensive core with Volcanion, as Volcanion can switch into and pressure their checks in Clefable while they handle its checks in Slowking. Physical attackers such as Mega Aerodactyl also enjoy Volcanion's Water-type immunity, allowing it to absorb Scald from the likes of Slowbro and Gastrodon. Volcanion is capable of pressuring a ton of offensive threats such as Mega Aerodactyl and Zeraora, as they are unable to switch into it properly, but unfortunately the inverse can also be said for it, since its mediocre Speed leaves it outpaced by the aforementioned threats and others, such as Iron Moth. To mitigate this, speed control options such as Choice Scarf Hydreigon and Enamorus are vital in order to force them out more easily. In return, Volcanion can help pressure defensive checks such as Amoonguss and Celesteela. Volcanion hates dealing with offensive Ground-types such as Excadrill due to its inability to switch into them, so partners like Skarmory are very useful at keeping them at bay. In return, Volcanion can handle threats that would try to take advantage of Skarmory such as Aegislash. Electric-types such as Thundurus and Zeraora are also incredibly annoying for Volcanion, so partners such as Gastrodon, Mega Latias, Mega Venusaur, and Tangrowth are good at handling them. In return, Volcanion can pressure threats such as Amoonguss and Celesteela for them. Although Volcanion can beat Rock-types in theory, Tyranitar and Mega Aerodactyl can pressure it really easily if on the field. Partners such as Scizor are great at forcing them out, and in return, Volcanion can deal with Iron Defense Skarmory and Amoonguss for them. Dragon-type wallbreakers such as Hydreigon and Mega Latias can also take advantage of Volcanion by merit of resisting both its STAB moves. Partners such as Celesteela, Clefable, and Tyranitar can effectively force them out for Volcanion.

Leveraging its good Special Attack stat, STAB combination, and coverage, Volcanion functions as a powerful wallbreaker that can muscle past structures with common defensive pieces such as Gliscor, Ferrothorn, and Toxapex. Thanks to its good typing, ability in Water Absorb, and decent bulk, Volcanion finds a few opportunities to switch in on threats like Hisuian Samurott and offensive Gholdengo. However, due to Volcanion's lackluster Speed tier, it is often outclassed by faster wallbreakers like Tapu Lele and Ogerpon-W. Fire Blast is the preferred Fire-type STAB option because it scores a guaranteed OHKO on Gholdengo after Stealth Rock, while Flamethrower is a more accurate option. Earth Power targets Pokemon that resist Volcanion's STAB moves like Raging Bolt and Toxapex. Taunt prevents passive walls like Alomomola, Slowbro, and Toxapex from damaging Volcanion due to its ability, Water Absorb. The combination of Fire Spin and Taunt can be used to completely remove the aforementioned walls by trapping them. Substitute can be used over Taunt to use Alomomola and Toxapex as fodder, though it has the drawback of making Volcanion more prone to chip damage. Heavy-Duty Boots nullifies Volcanion's glaring weakness to entry hazards. A Timid nature is preferred, as it allows Volcanion to outspeed Gliscor, Gholdengo, and Landorus-T with little to no Speed investment, though a Modest nature allows Volcanion to secure a guaranteed 2HKO on Hisuian Samurott with Earth Power after Stealth Rock.

Volcanion is primarily found on bulky offense teams, where its ability to pressure defensive staples like Gliscor and Toxapex is greatly appreciated by other offensive threats like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant. In return, they can revenge kill faster foes that Volcanion struggles against such as Ogerpon-W and Mega Latios. Landorus-T is also an effective teammate, as it can switch into Ground-type attacks from Garchomp and opposing Landorus-T that Volcanion is weak to. Additionally, Landorus-T can bring Volcanion in using U-turn, giving it more opportunities to enter the field. Volcanion can also act as an effective partner for Landorus-T, as it can threaten Gliscor and Ferrothorn. Other pivots like Pecharunt and Tapu Koko are also appreciated; Pecharunt can often switch into Mega Lopunny and Zamazenta, while Tapu Koko can revenge kill the likes of Garchomp and Great Tusk. Sturdy defensive backbones like Ferrothorn and Ting-Lu can comfortably switch into Pokemon that can revenge kill Volcanion like Raging Bolt and Tapu Koko. Additionally, both of them set entry hazards, enhancing Volcanion's wallbreaking capabilities. As a teammate, Volcanion can offensively threaten Gholdengo and Cinderace, which Ferrothorn struggles against. Fire Spin sets are excellent teammates for offensive staples like Great Tusk and Dragonite that appreciate Volcanion's ability to remove their checks, notably Alomomola and Slowbro. In return, Great Tusk can effectively remove hazards, which Volcanion becomes vulnerable to if damaged by Knock Off.

Primordial Sea.description: Primordial Sea Volcanion excels as a fantastic wallbreaker with its great Special Attack and offensive typing. Rain-boosted Steam Eruption combined with Choice Specs allows Volcanion to 2HKO most Pokemon in tier, including most specially defensive walls such as RegenVest Garchomp, Meloetta, and Alolan Muk. Weather Ball dissuades promient Desolate Land users that might want to switch in to Volcanion such as Cinderace and Iron Moth. Earth Power is a more reliable way to deal with Desolate Land users like Iron Moth and Heatran, and it's a reliable way to hit Hisuian Goodra without missing. Focus Blast 2HKOes a would-be check in RegenVest Roaring Moon, as well as Hisuian Goodra after Spikes chip. Volcanion pairs well with entry hazard setters like Ting-Lu and Garchomp, which help wear down common RegenVest Pokemon like Goodra and Hisuian Goodra, and hazards also guarantee a 2HKO on Meloetta. Due to Volcanion's Stealth Rock weakness it pairs well with hazard removers like Corviknight and Quaquaval, which can also help pivot it in safely. Volcanion also pairs well with offensive pivots like Zapdos and Roaring Moon, which can help bring it in on targets like Corviknight.

Wallbreaker (Fire).description: A unique and powerful STAB combination, useful coverage moves, and a high Special Attack stat all help Volcanion succeed as a wallbreaker for Fire teams. Water Absorb is an excellent ability for Fire teams, allowing Volcanion to block dangerous Water-type moves like Hydro Pump from Greninja and Flip Turn from Mega Swampert. Steam Eruption threatens Ground- and Rock-types like Great Tusk, Tyranitar, and Garganacl while also potentially inflicting burns, which cripple dangerous physical attackers like Garchomp and Ogerpon-C. Sludge Bomb threatens Azumarill, Mega Altaria, Iron Valiant, and Ogerpon-W. Earth Power is strong against Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra, as well as bulky Electric- and Poison-types like Iron Hands and Toxapex. As an alternative, Defog lets Volcanion act as a form of entry hazard removal for Fire teams, pairing especially well with Heavy-Duty Boots if Volcanion opts for it. Hidden Power Grass is another option to threaten Water-types like Gastrodon and Mega Swampert, and Hidden Power Ice snipes Dragonite and Garchomp. Air Balloon helps Volcanion better threaten Ground-types like Excadrill and Ting-Lu. Heavy-Duty Boots can instead be used to allow Volcanion safer entry against hazards. The given Speed investment lets Volcanion outspeed Jolly Azumarill and Ursaluna. Mega Charizard X is a great partner for its ability to threaten Dragon- and Electric-types like Kommo-o, Mega Latios, Tapu Koko, and Raging Bolt after a single Dragon Dance, and it helps with breaking down specially defensive Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Hisuian Goodra. Cinderace is a viable partner that can also break down these specially defensive Pokémon while also providing hazard control with Court Change. In return, Volcanion helps these physical attackers against physically defensive Pokemon like Great Tusk, Gliscor, and Swampert. Heatran traps and removes specially defensive Pokemon like Blissey and Mega Latias with the combination of Magma Storm and Taunt or Toxic, givng opponents fewer safe switch-ins to Volcanion. It also checks, in a pinch, faster Rock-types that beat Volcanion like Mega Aerodactyl and Nihilego. Volcanion assists Heatran by threatening faster Ground-types like Excadrill and Iron Treads when holding an Air Balloon and other Fire-types like opposing Air Balloon Heatran and Moltres. Torkoal powers up Volcanion's Flamethrower by setting sun, allowing Volcanion to 2HKO Mega Sableye, and aids it by setting Stealth Rock and removing hazards with Rapid Spin. Similarly, Ninetales threatens Water-types like Gastrodon and Urshifu-R with Solar Beam and uses Healing Wish to give a weakened Volcanion an additional chance to wallbreak.

nu.overview: Decidueye is an incredibly powerful physical attacker, using Swords Dance-boosted Spirit Shackle, Poltergeist, and Leaf Blade to do massive damage to opposing walls, such as Amoonguss, Duraludon, and Gligar, and revenge killing faster foes like Munkidori and Chandelure with Shadow Sneak. It also serves as one of the few viable users of Defog in the tier, taking advantage of the fear its powerful physical sets create to find turns to clear entry hazards. Its typing allows it to switch in on common attackers like Paldean Tauros-W and Flygon, and it often finds turns to set up in front of common defensive Water-types like Swampert and Vaporeon. Its ability to throw out powerful attacks is only enhanced by Long Reach, which allows it to avoid the threats of Chandelure's Flame Body, Bellibolt's Static, and Rocky Helmet. Decidueye does struggle with its mediocre Speed though, particularly on offensive sets. Even Swords Dance-boosted Shadow Sneak does not often pick off neutral targets from full HP without Tera Ghost, leaving Decidueye open to being revenge killed by many faster and Ghost-immune foes such as Cinccino, Ambipom, and Meloetta. Decidueye's STAB types are also walled by two common Pokemon, namely Overqwil and Incineroar. Defog sets must also be careful of several Competitive and Defiant Pokemon, such as Kilowattrel, Braviary, and Tornadus.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Decidueye can run Low Kick instead of Leaf Blade or Shadow Sneak in order to hit Incineroar, other Dark-types, and Registeel for super effective damage, but it loses either priority or its Grass-type STAB move in return. Decidueye can also run a special attacking set of Nasty Plot / Shadow Ball / Giga Drain, Leaf Storm, or Energy Ball / Roost, but this set can be easily revenge killed because it lacks priority.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types and Dark-type Attacks: Common Dark-types like Overqwil and Incineroar wall Decidueye's STAB moves, and weaken it further with Intimidate. Many other Pokemon such as Toxicroak and Cinccino threaten Decidueye with Knock Off as well.

Fire-types and Fire-type Attacks: Fire-types, such as the previously mentioned Incineroar along with Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion, threaten to blow Decidueye away with powerful Fire-type attacks. However, the latter two can be threatened with Shadow Sneak. Speedy attackers like Scream Tail and Flygon can also run Fire Blast to threaten Decidueye.

Flying-types: Decidueye must be wary of powerful Flying-type Pokemon like Scyther, Flamigo, Kilowattrel, and Tornadus. The latter three also threaten Defog sets with Competitive and Defiant boosts. However, none of them want to switch into Poltergeist and Spirit Shackle, and they can also be picked off with Shadow Sneak.

Swords Dance.description:
Set Details

Spirit Shackle lets Decidueye hit and trap foes without fear of missing, while +2 Poltergeist lets it potentially OHKO checks like Amoonguss after Stealth Rock damage. However, Poltergeist limits Decidueye's teammates' ability to utilize Knock Off, as it requires the foe to have an item. Shadow Sneak lets Decidueye pick off and revenge kill faster foes, particularly Ghost-weak ones like Chandelure, Hisuian Typhlosion, and Munkidori. Tera Ghost lets Shadow Sneak OHKO Inteleon, Kilowattrel, and, after Stealth Rock damage, Flamigo, while Tera Fairy and Water act defensively to give Decidueye a chance to set up in front of Dark-types like Scrafty and Fire-types like Incineroar, respectively.

Decidueye appreciates teammates like Munkidori and Chandelure that are also checked by Dark- and Fire-types, since it can work together with these partners to wear down shared checks like Incineroar. Particularly when using Spirit Shackle over Poltergeist, entry hazard support from teammates like Klefki, Duraludon, Swampert, and Bronzong can be helpful to wear down checks and guarantee KOs. Backup physical attackers can work to overwhelm solid physical walls like Amoonguss and Bellibolt, so the Paldean Tauros formes, Toxicroak, and Flygon can support Decidueye very well. On top of that, they can capitalize on Pokemon that Decidueye might faint against like Incineroar and Overqwil. Decidueye can occasionally find getting a turn to set up difficult, so teammates that facilitate opportunities, such as Encore users like Cinccino and Scream Tail and Memento Chandelure, can be very helpful.

Wallbreaker.description:
Set Details

Choice Band- or Spell Tag-boosted Poltergeist provides the most immediate power, but it can miss and limits Decidueye's teammates' ability to use Knock Off. Spirit Shackle provides a completely accurate Ghost-type STAB move and allows Decidueye's teammates to use Knock Off more freely. U-turn allows Decidueye to pivot out on potential checks like Overqwil and Incineroar. Tera Ghost further boosts its powerful Ghost-type STAB moves, letting it 2HKO Gligar with Poltergeist. Tera Fairy and Tera Water work defensively to allow Decidueye to survive attacks from powerful Dark- and Fire-types, respectively, such as Scrafty and Chandelure.

Decidueye requires teammates that can switch in on powerful Fire- and Dark-type attacks from foes like Chandelure and Incineroar, so Vaporeon and Swampert can be valuable. Other physical attackers like Flamigo, Flygon, and Paldean Tauros-W appreciate Decidueye's ability to weaken opposing physical walls like Amoongus and Bellibolt. Special attackers, particularly ones that can pivot like Munkidori and Kilowattrel, can also combine with Decidueye to repeatedly pivot on checks and wear them down. Decidueye does not resist Stealth Rock and is not immune to Spikes, so entry hazard removers like Tatsugiri, Altaria, and Scyther are appreciated to ensure Decidueye can repeatedly enter the field and threaten foes.

Defog.description:
Set Details

Giga Drain, along with Roost, provides Decidueye with additional longevity, but Leaf Storm can provide immediate power to surprise opponents expecting physically offensive Decidueye sets. U-turn allows Decidueye to pivot on opposing Competitive and Defiant Pokemon like Kilowattrel and Tornadus that might otherwise take advantage of Defog, but Decidueye can also choose to run Shadow Ball to hit Grass-resistant Pokemon like Kilowattrel and Tornadus for neutral damage. With an Impish nature, Knock Off can be run as Decidueye's main attack, since it lets Decidueye threaten item-reliant Pokemon like Kilowattrel, Tornadus, and Incineroar that would otherwise easily take advantage of it. The given EV spread allows Decidueye to outspeed Adamant Incineroar, which otherwise threatens it with Knock Off. Tera Fairy allows Decidueye to resist Dark-type attacks from foes like Incineroar, Scrafty, and Toxicroak, as well as Flamigo's Scrappy Close Combat, while Tera Water protects it from Fire-types like Chandelure and Infernape. Tera Poison is an all-around solid defensive option, removing all of Decidueye's original weaknesses and specifically letting it resist Flamigo's Scrappy Close Combat.

Decidueye requires teammates capable of checking Incineroar, as Defog lets it in for free. Vaporeon and Swampert resist Incineroar's STAB moves and can patch up Decidueye's weakness to Fire- and Flying-types like Chandelure and Kilowattrel. Entry hazard-weak teammates appreciate Decidueye's Defog, particularly Fire- and Flying-types like Choice item users such as Chandelure as well as Staraptor and itemless Tornadus. Decidueye also checks Paldean Tauros-W, which Water- and Fighting-weak Pokemon like Swampert, Gligar, Incineroar, and Duraludon appreciate.

Choice Scarf.description:
When equipped with a Choice Scarf, Hisuian Decidueye is a threatening physical attacker and cleaner thanks to its unique traits of a good STAB combination, an incredibly spammable STAB move in Triple Arrows, and a great ability in Scrappy. U-turn allows Hisuian Decidueye to pivot out of awkward matchups like defensive Florges, Uxie, and Galarian Slowbro and keep up momentum as it revenge kills Psychic-types like Bruxish and Espeon. Leaf Blade is a useful secondary STAB move that pressures Grass-weak physical walls like Rhydon, Mudsdale, and Milotic. Brave Bird is useful to target Amoonguss, opposing Hisuian Decidueye, and Paldean Tauros-F, while Close Combat 2HKOes Rotom-H and OHKOes Brute Bonnet. Tera Fighting boosts the power of Triple Arrows and Close Combat to great levels, allowing Hisuian Decidueye to 2HKO Rhydon and Arcanine and OHKO Frosmoth and Dudunsparce with Triple Arrows.

While strong, Hisuian Decidueye can struggle to deal with a few threats that resist its STAB moves such as Galarian Slowbro, Galarian Articuno, and Delphox, so checks to these threats such as Rhydon, Rotom-H, and Goodra are good partners to have. Even with a Choice Scarf, some threats such as Salazzle, Sneasel, and Floatzel still outspeed Hisuian Decidueye, so having switch-ins to these threats such as Coalossal and Milotic are useful to have. Hisuian Decidueye's ability to wear down common switch-ins to it such as Uxie and Mudsdale can help enable partners also checked by these walls, such as Bruxish, Grimmsnarl, and Ambipom. Hisuian Decidueye can often have difficulty to get onto the battlefield safely due to its many weaknesses, so slower pivots such as Frosmoth and Bombirdier can help bring it in safely while forming a strong VoltTurn core with Hisuian Decidueye. Hisuian Decidueye enjoys support from entry hazard control from the likes of Alolan Sandslash and Cramorant, as Hisuian Decidueye is easily worn down from entry hazards as a pivot.

Swords Dance.description: The first EV spread lets Hisuian Decidueye outpace defensive Tsareena, while the second one allows it to be as offensive as possible.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Amoonguss works exceptionally well with Incineroar, protecting it from Water- and Fighting-type attacks such as Basculegion’s Wave Crash and Annihilape’s Drain Punch. Amoonguss also provides Incineroar with much appreciated healing. In return, Incineroar can handle Gholdengo and switch into Fire-types like Talonflame and Volcarona as well as removing opposing Safety Goggles with Knock Off.
  • Incineroar also works well with Gholdengo, providing Intimidate and Fake Out support to help it set up safely. Gholdengo also takes advantage of Incineroar’s ability to do great damage to Kingambit, considering Gholdengo can blow up Clefable and Sneasler that may attempt to protect Kingambit.
  • Porygon2 and Ursaluna can set up Trick Room and Substitute more easily thanks to Incineroar’s support. Ursaluna can then blow up Pokemon Incineroar struggles to damage like Archaludon and opposing Incineroar.
  • Incineroar can struggle to do its job against Pokemon that threaten it such as Pelipper, the Ursaluna formes, and Annihilape. Bulky support Incineroar can also feel passive at times because of its lackluster damage output, especially when it can’t use Parting Shot because of redirection or Taunt. Therefore, offensive Pokemon like Gholdengo and Ursaluna that can take on these threats and make up for Incineroar’s poor damage output are greatly appreciated.

Strategy Comments

  • Incineroar is an effective support Pokemon and pivot thanks to Fake Out, Intimidate, and its pivoting moves. This makes Incineroar strongest when it can switch in and slow down threats like Sneasler and Rillaboom. When using Taunt or Will-O-Wisp, Incineroar can shut down opposing wincons like Porygon2’s Trick Room and Kingambit. Rage Powder from Amoonguss makes it easier for Incineroar to pivot in and out.
  • Incineroar is strong throughout the entire game; it's usually preserved throughout the game, as even switching it in is impactful, and a late-game Fake Out can be crucial regardless of how injured Incineroar is. Incineroar is notably strongest as a lead where it can threaten Fake Out and weaken opposing threats without risking any damage. Against Annihilape and Kingambit however, Incineroar likes to be paired with pieces that force them out before coming in, such as Gholdengo and Ursaluna. Assault Vest Incineroar can afford to stay in and do invaluable damage as an offensive piece occasionally, though it notably has to be a lot more careful against Amoonguss.
  • Incineroar’s biggest weaknesses are Annihilape and Kingambit, as they take advantage of Intimidate and can prove to be dangerous wincons with support. Pelipper and Ursaluna-B also prove troublesome, as they are powerful attackers unaffected by Intimidate. Incineroar relies on teammates such as the aforementioned Gholdengo and Ursaluna to handle these threats along with Fake Out support. When Incineroar pivots in, it can also lead to a loss of momentum against setup Pokemon that can’t be flinched with Fake Out, such as Bulk Up Annihilape, Nasty Plot Gholdengo, and Substitute Ursaluna, so it must be careful when pivoting. Bulky support Incineroar’s damage output can often feel underwhelming, especially against opposing Incineroar. Assault Vest Incineroar has a tougher time providing support, notably having more trouble getting setup sweepers into position, since it lacks Parting Shot. This can make the mirror matchup tougher, as opposing Incineroar can position their threatening allies better.

Bulky Support.description:
• Incineroar excels as a support Pokemon and pivot thanks to its vast supportive movepool, Intimidate, and great typing, providing Incineroar with resistances to Gholdengo’s, Rillaboom’s, and Kingambit’s STAB moves.
  • Incineroar can utilize Taunt over Flare Blitz to shut down support Pokemon like Amoonguss and Trick Room from Porygon2. Incineroar can also use Will-O-Wisp over Flare Blitz to weaken physical attackers like Garchomp and especially Kingambit, which punishes Intimidate.
  • Safety Goggles is preferred, so Incineroar can reliably check and ignore Amoonguss. Sitrus Berry’s burst healing helps Incineroar avoid 2HKOs from attacks like Choice Specs Gholdengo’s Make it Rain and Pelipper’s Weather Ball after Terastallization.
  • Tera Ghost is preferred to grant Incineroar an immunity to Sneasler’s Close Combat and Dragonite’s Extreme Speed as well as a crucial immunity to Fake Out from opposing Incineroar and Rillaboom. Tera Grass can be used instead to grant Incineroar resistances to Water- and Ground-type moves such as Basculegion’s Wave Crash and Garchomp’s Stomping Tantrum. Tera Grass also provides an immunity to Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss if Safety Goggles have been removed with Knock Off or Incineroar is using Sitrus Berry.
  • The defensive EVs allow Incineroar to survive Garchomp’s Life Orb-boosted Stomping Tantrum and, after using Tera Ghost, Gholdengo’s Life Orb-boosted Shadow Ball and Choice Band Basculegion’s 100-Base Power Last Respects after Intimidate.

Assault Vest.description:
• Assault Vest Incineroar is a fantastic pivot thanks to its exceptional defenses and access to Fake Out. The extra bulk enables Incineroar to play more offensively with respectable Attack and Speed investment.
  • Assault Vest helps Incineroar take attacks from Pelipper, Ursaluna-B, and Archaludon.
  • Tera Grass is preferred due to the Spore and Rage Powder immunity on top of the valuable resistances to Ground- and Water-type moves, such as Basculegion’s Wave Crash and Garchomp’s Stomping Tantrum.
  • The Attack EVs allow Incineroar to almost always 2HKO Kingambit with Flare Blitz after Intimidate. The defensive investment ensures that Incineroar takes Annihilape’s +1 Drain Punch and avoids the 2HKO from Choice Scarf Hisuian Typhlosion’s Heat Wave after Terastallization. The Speed EVs enable Incineroar to outspeed Sneasler under Tailwind.
  • Bulky support Incineroar is more flexible and can use Parting Shot as its pivot move of choice. Assault Vest Incineroar trades this flexibility in exchange for vastly more special bulk and offensive prowess. Bulky support Incineroar doesn’t have to burn Terastallization to handle Amoonguss and can use Tera Ghost instead.

Bulky Support.description:
Incineroar is the premier non-Restricted Pokemon in the Regulation G metagame thanks to Intimidate and its ability to check centralizing threats such as Calyrex-S for its team. Its access to Fake Out and Parting Shot combined with its great natural bulk make for a strong combination, demanding respect from foes lest they be forced to switch out, leaving themselves vulnerable to Incineroar's allies, or stay on the field outputting negligible damage. Incineroar is naturally blessed with a typing that lets it take on both Restricted Pokemon, such as Lunala and Calyrex-S, and strong non-Restricted Pokemon like Chien-Pao, Rillaboom, and Chi-Yu. Will-O-Wisp ruins IronPress Zamazenta-C and Clear Amulet Calyrex-I; this is of great value, as they normally are not hindered by Intimidate, since the former relies on its Defense stat to deal damage and the latter almost always runs Clear Amulet. Alternatively, Flare Blitz provides high damage output against Rillaboom and Amoonguss and OHKOes Chien-Pao. Taunt can also be utilized on specific teams, such as those with Calyrex-I, to shut down Amoonguss. Knock Off is crucial to OHKO Calyrex-S while removing items such as Safety Goggles from opposing Incineroar to aid its own partner Amoonguss. Holding Safety Goggles itself allows Incineroar to have a better matchup against Amoonguss, letting it ignore Spore and Rage Powder, but Sitrus Berry can viably be run to provide crucial longevity to Incineroar in this powerful metagame. The given EV spread allows Incineroar to always survive a Jolly Close Combat from Mienshao. As an added bonus, it also takes a +1 Defense Body Press from Zamazenta-C, allowing it to use Will-O-Wisp or get better positioning against Zamazenta-C's allies. The special bulk EVs allow Incineroar to avoid a 2HKO from +1 Life Orb Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage, letting it retaliate with Knock Off. 27 Speed IVs are run in order to get a slower Parting Shot than opposing Incineroar, allowing the user's Incineroar's Parting Shot to go off onto a freshly switched-in opposing Pokemon for greater value. Tera Ghost allows Incineroar to ignore Fake Out from opposing Incineroar or Rillaboom, Close Combat from Mienshao and either Urshifu forme, and Body Press from Zamazenta-C. Tera Grass lets Incineroar resist Water Spout from Kyogre while being immune to Amoonguss's Spore and Rage Powder, essentially functioning as a built-in Safety Goggles. Alternatively, Tera Water can be used to keep the resistance to Water Spout and resist Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance in exchange for a neutral matchup against opposing Incineroar and being unable to ignore Amoonguss.

Incineroar pairs well with virtually every Restricted Pokemon, providing Fake Out support in conjunction with solid bulk and damage reduction. As useful as Incineroar is, it is severely threatened by Pokemon such as Koraidon and Kyogre, the former of which is immune to Intimidate thanks to Clear Amulet and can easily OHKO Incineroar with Collision Course. The latter is Incineroar's worst matchup, as it easily gets OHKOed by Water Spout and even Origin Pulse if rain is on the field. Miraidon is also a huge nuisance when used with Choice Specs, as it can either potentially OHKO Incineroar with Electro Drift or pivot around it with Volt Switch, chipping it or its allies down. The susceptibility to Koraidon can be mitigated by having Flutter Mane or Tera Fairy Raging Bolt as a partner, as both take advantage of Koraidon's sun via Protosynthesis and force it to Terastallize. Incineroar should also be carefully preserved against Calyrex-I because it commonly runs Clear Amulet and High Horsepower, which can 2HKO Incineroar. Incineroar also struggles against a top non-Restricted Pokemon in Urshifu-R, so allies such as Rillaboom and/or Amoonguss are appreciated to keep it and other threats like Kyogre and Miraidon in check.

Assault Vest.description:
Incineroar is a bulky pivot that uses its good defensive typing, defenses that are bolstered by Assault Vest, and Intimidate to allow its teammates to switch in safely as well as being a check to Pokemon such as Calyrex-S, Zacian-C, and Rillaboom. U-turn allows Incineroar to switch out and get more use out of Intimidate and Fake Out. Assault Vest lets Incineroar survive attacks such as Ursaluna-B's Tera Normal Blood Moon and Pelipper's Weather Ball at the cost of not being able to use common moves like Parting Shot, Will-O-Wisp, and Taunt. The defensive EVs allow Incineroar to take Choice Specs Miraidon's Electro Drift, Landorus's Earth Power, and Mienshao's Close Combat as well as Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance after Incineroar Terastallizes. Tera Grass lets Incineroar resist moves such as the former two's STAB attacks as well as Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes, which lets Incineroar remove their items with Knock Off or bring in teammate with U-turn while making Incineroar immune to Amoonguss's Spore and Rage Powder.

Incineroar struggles against Pokemon that can threaten it with super effective damage and ignore Intimidate such as Urshifu-R, Koraidon, Landorus, and Pelipper, with the latter three still hitting it super effectively after it Terastallizes. Partners like Miraidon and Lunala can help against Pokemon that threaten Incineroar such as Urshifu-R, Pelipper, and Landorus. Incineroar pairs well with Pokemon like Miraidon that benefit from being able to pivot and can make sure that Electric Terrain is active. Incineroar also uses Flare Blitz to threaten Grass-types like Rillaboom and Amoonguss that resist Miraidon's STAB Electric-type moves. Lunala is another strong partner for Incineroar, as Fake Out can help Lunala set up Trick Room while Incineroar can help strong Trick Room sweepers such as Ursaluna switch in safely. Incineroar also threatens Calyrex-S, which Lunala otherwise struggles against, with Knock Off.

Assault Vest Pivot.description:
• Assault Vest makes Incineroar even bulkier at the cost of utility in not running Parting Shot or Safety Goggles.

  • The given EV spread allows Incineroar to avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast and take Landorus's Earth Power, while the Defense EVs let Incineroar survive Close Combat from the Urshifu formes with Sword of Ruin active.

  • Tera Grass is preferred because it flips Incineroar's weaknesses and allows it to be a consistent Amoonguss answer, ignoring Spore and Rage Powder. Incineroar can also use Tera Fairy as a more all-round defensive typing and as a way to check Urshifu-S.

nu.overview: The combination of Knock Off, good typing, and Intimidate makes Incineroar a great wallbreaker while being a solid defensive Pokemon. Swords Dance sets can make Incineroar into a great wallbreaker, since many defensive staples like Amoonguss, Galarian Slowbro, and Copperajah just drop to its Swords Dance-boosted STAB attacks. Also, Incineroar easily checks the common Ghost-, Grass-, and Steel-types like Chandelure, Decidueye, and Klefki, meaning it can take advantage of its utility moves with a defensive pivot set if it wishes. It has Will-O-Wisp and Knock Off to cripple incoming physical wallbreakers like Toxicroak, Flygon, and Paldean Tauros-W and item-reliant Pokemon like Altaria, Houndstone, and Swampert. Defensive Incineroar is also solid for handling special wallbreakers such as Chandelure, Uxie, and Heavy-Duty Boots Munkidori. However, Incineroar's low Speed stat makes it very easy for wallbreakers with a middling Speed tier like Basculegion-M, Flamigo, and Heracross to outspeed and destroy it with their own STAB attacks. Incineroar's reliance on Heavy-Duty Boots can be felt, since it has to be wary of switching into opposing Knock Off from Tsareena, Copperajah, and Wo-Chien. It even has to worry about switching into the Pokemon it checks best, Chandelure, which carries Trick to cripple it. Incineroar also lacks any form of recovery, making it easily worn down over the course of a battle.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Close Combat is an option to hit many foes neutrally like Swampert and Rhyperior while also hitting opposing Incineroar super effectively. Flame Charge gives Incineroar the opportunity to become a late-game cleaner after picking off a weakened threat. Alternatively, Trailblaze can be used alongside Tera Grass to hit Water-types super effectively, but it's pretty reliant on Terastallization to do good damage. Iron Head can be used on Swords Dance Incineroar to surprise Sylveon and Florges, but the ability to pivot, boost its Speed, or use a high-Base Power coverage move tends to be better overall. Weakness Policy + Power Trip sets can be used on hyper offense teams, letting Incineroar become a dangerous sweeper. Incineroar has a bunch of usable defensive Tera types, but they are really inconsistent for many teams. Tera Flying helps Incineroar take on Fighting- and Ground-type attacks, but it retains its weakness to Stealth Rock. Tera Grass gives Incineroar a resistance to Water- and Ground-type attacks but gives it a bad matchup against opposing Fire-types like Chandelure, Infernape, and Hisuian Typhlosion.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Vaporeon and Swampert can switch into its Flare Blitz and threaten Incineroar back with their own STAB attacks, but they have to be wary about switching into a boosted Knock Off from Swords Dance sets. Offensive Water-types like Inteleon and Basculegion-M, while they have to be worried about switching into its Knock Off, can easily destroy it.

Ground-types: Flygon, Swampert, and Rhydon destroy Incineroar with their STAB Earthquake, but they have to be wary about switching into Will-O-Wisp from bulkier sets.

Fighting-types: Paldean Tauros-W, Toxicroak, and Flamigo outspeed Incineroar and destroy it with their STAB Fighting-type attacks. Infernape and Paldean Tauros-W resist both of Incineroar's STAB attacks and use it as setup fodder.

Item Displacement: Common Knock Off users like Tsareena, Copperajah, and Wo-Chien can threaten Incineroar by removing its Heavy-Duty Boots, making it a lot weaker to entry hazards. On top of this, Pokemon it would love to switch into like Chandelure, Munkidori, and Meloetta often carry Trick to cripple it.

Swords Dance.description:
Set Details

U-turn allows Incineroar to pivot on, chip away at, and not get taken advantage of by its checks like Swampert. Earthquake, on the other hand, provides a powerful attack with no drawback that also hits the common Rock-, Poison-, and and Fire-types like Rhyperior, Tera Poison Vaporeon, and opposing Incineroar An Adamant nature can be used to allow Incineroar to OHKO Vaporeon and Swampert after one layer of Spikes, but a Jolly nature is useful for outspeeding foes like Modest Choice Specs Sylveon and Adamant Decidueye. A specially defensive spread of 248 HP / 212 SpD / 48 Spe with a Careful nature can alternatively be used on Swords Dance sets, letting it better pivot into foes like Chandelure, Munkidori, and Uxie; the Speed EVs let Incineroar outpace Vaporeon. Tera Poison gives Incineroar an immunity to poison from Munkidori and Amoonguss while having a resistance to Fighting-type attacks. However, Tera Fairy provides a more well-rounded defensive typing that isn't weak to Ground-type attacks while still resisting Fighting-type attacks. Tera Ghost allows Incineroar to completely blank Close Combat, and it helps to revenge kill Cinccino. This comes at a trade-off of it having no other useful resistances, though.

Incineroar can partner with other pivots like Flygon and Swampert, which tend to draw in Grass-types like Amoonguss and Tsareena for Incineroar to prey on and form a VoltTurn core able to chip away at each other's checks. Entry hazard removers like Brambleghast, Scyther, and Cinccino can be great partners, since they can remove entry hazards if Incineroar loses its Heavy-Duty Boots. Incineroar can struggle against bulky Water-types like Vaporeon and Swampert that can tank its STAB attacks, so it pairs with Pokemon like Toxicroak and Amoonguss, as they can check the aforementioned Water-types. Fairy- and Poison-types like Sylveon and Munkidori appreciate Incineroar for checking Steel-types like Copperajah, Klefki, and Bronzong; in return, they can check Fighting-types like Paldean Tauros-W and Flamigo.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Set Details

Will-O-Wisp allows Incineroar to cripple its common switch-ins like Rhyperior, Swampert, and Paldean Tauros-W. Parting Shot lets Incineroar weaken foes, pivot, and provide safety for setup sweepers. However, U-turn can be used because it avoids activating Tornadus's and Braviary's Defiant as well as Kilowattrel's Competitive. The given EV spread allows Incineroar to get the jump on Vaporeon while having as much special bulk as possible. Tera Fairy provides it the ability to check Dragon- and Fighting-types like Flygon and Heracross while also letting it resist the omnipresent U-turn. Alternatively, Tera Dragon gives Incineroar the ability to check a myriad of special attackers like Kilowattrel and Inteleon. Tera Water is similar to Tera Dragon but replaces a Grass resistance for an Ice resistance, making Incineroar better against Inteleon.

Grass-types like Decidueye, Brambleghast, and Amoonguss are great partners for Incineroar, since they can handle bulky Water- and Ground-types such as Vaporeon, Swampert, and Rhyperior. Fighting-types like Flamigo, Toxicroak, and Infernape can force Incineroar to switch, so it best pairs with physically defensive Pokemon like Galarian Slowbro, Bellibolt, and Sylveon that can handle the aforementioned Fighting-types. Additionally, Sylveon can provide Incineroar with recovery by passing it a Wish. Wallbreakers like Inteleon, Munkidori, and Decidueye appreciate Incineroar's slow Parting Shot, as they can get a free entry on Rock-, Fighting-, and Water-types that tend to switch in on Incineroar. Setup sweepers like Swords Dance Toxicroak and Dragon Dance Flygon similarly appreciate Incineroar's Parting Shot weakening foes and it giving them more opportunities to set up. Incineroar's longevity is limited and can be cut severely if it loses its Heavy-Duty Boots, so it pairs well with entry hazard removers such as Scyther, Cinccino, and Brambleghast.

Assault Vest.description:
• Assault Vest Incineroar functions as a bulky specially defensive pivot, switching into a variety of common threats—most notably Calyrex-S, as Incineroar resists its STAB combination—while using Intimidate to weaken physical attackers, particularly Chien-Pao.

  • Knock Off: Knock Off is crucial to this set's strength; the move is able to OHKO Calyrex-S, furthering Incineroar's ability to successfully check it, and provide immense value with item removal.

  • Flare Blitz: Flare Blitz's raw power and STAB make it a powerful option against Chien-Pao, Calyrex-I, and Zacian-C.

  • U-turn: U-turn is Incineroar's best move, allowing it to chip foes for decent damage while switching out to reset Intimidate and get a powerful partner in.

  • Bulldoze: Bulldoze can provide decent value in its speed control, enabling Incineroar to slow down foes before pivoting to a powerful and now faster attacker with U-turn.

  • Teammates: Incineroar fits on a variety of teams but pairs best with Calyrex-S and Flutter Mane, as it can check the Ghost-types that can threaten them, while in return, they can pivot into and threaten the Fighting-types that are particularly problematic for Incineroar, most notably Koraidon.

Other Options

  • Fake Out: Fake Out does small chip damage to foes for free, notably breaking Focus Sash and Sturdy on the likes of Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-C.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Very Situational: Incineroar only requires Terastallization in a pinch for difficult type matchups, as its regular typing is crucial to its defensive abilities, particularly handling Calyrex-S, and it can pivot out of bad type matchups with U-turn.

  • Water: Tera Water allows Incineroar to resist Water-type attacks, notably Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R, while giving it a generally strong defensive typing.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy provides a resistance to Fighting-type attacks like Close Combat from Koraidon, as well as an immunity to Draco Meteor from Miraidon.

  • Fire: Tera Fire bolsters Incineroar's damage output, allowing it to potentially OHKO Calyrex-S and Calyrex-I, while dropping its Fighting-type weakness.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD / 4 Def with Careful or Sassy: This spread maximizes Incineroar's special bulk to allow it to answer opposing threats much better, particularly letting it survive Electro Drift from Modest Tera Electric Choice Specs Miraidon the majority of the time. A Careful nature allows Incineroar to outspeed important threats in Speed-invested Ursaluna-B and Calyrex-I, while a Sassy nature allows it to pivot more slowly in mirror matches.

  • 252 HP / 212 Atk / 44 SpD with Adamant: This more offensive spread allows Incineroar to have a much greater offensive presence, notably OHKOing Flutter Mane and 2HKOing Calyrex-I with Flare Blitz, while still enabling it to take a Tera Blast Fighting from Choice Specs Calyrex-S.

Pivot.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD with Impish or Relaxed: Maximizing Defense gives Incineroar around a 90% chance of avoiding a 2HKO from Choice Band Chien-Pao's Sacred Sword. A lower Speed IV can be used to underspeed more threats, but this can be risky against Ursaluna-B.

  • 252 HP / 44 Def / 212 SpD with Careful or Sassy: When used with Sitrus Berry, this spread avoids a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

Support.description:
Incineroar stands clear as the best supportive Pokemon in the metagame with its amazing ability in Intimidate and a seemingly endless number of supportive moves. Its stellar defensive typing and great bulk allow it to easily stand up to some of the most common threats such as Ogerpon-H and Gholdengo without blinking. Intimidate is particularly devastating in Partners in Crime due to Incineroar's partner also activating the ability on switch-in, meaning a well-timed double switch can lead to three Intimidates in a single turn, effectively neutralising physical threats. Fake Out is one of Incineroar's main talking points, allowing its partner free turns to set up, use Trick Room, or simply just get an extra turn of damage against the foe. Flare Blitz gives it some form of offensive pressure. Parting Shot is Incineroar's best pivoting move, allowing it to further reduce foes' damage. Knock Off removes key items such as Iron Hands's Clear Amulet and Porygon2's Eviolite. Snarl and Will-O-Wisp are ways for Incineroar to reduce foes' damage output even further, while Helping Hand allows it to make up for its sometimes lacking offensive presence. Both Tera Grass and Tera Poison are good options for Incineroar, with the former both giving it a Spore immunity and turning its Water- and Ground-type weaknesses into resistances. Poison is helpful in resisting Iron Hands's Drain Punch while also being a generally solid type overall. The given EV spread allows Incineroar maximum survivability against Timid Landorus's Sandsear Stormwhile while also easily surviving Drain Punch from Iron Hands and Sacred Sword from Adamant Tera Stellar Chien-Pao. The Speed investment also allows Incineroar to outrun Kyurem while in Tailwind.

Notable Partners

Setup Attackers: The combination of Fake Out and all of Incineroar's damage reduction tools make setup attackers such as Nasty Plot Gholdengo and Swords Dance Iron Hands appreciative partners. Flare Blitz and Knock Off also provide the physical setup attackers with valuable coverage they'd otherwise struggle to fit.

Allies with Recovery Abilities: Pokemon such as Sinistcha and Amoonguss make great partners for Incineroar thanks to its desire to pivot in order to reset Intimidate and Fake Out. Sinistcha switches in to heal Incineroar and itself while also gaining the aforementioned tools. Amoonguss allows Incineroar to heal with Regenerator every time it uses Parting Shot.

Trick Room Users: Trick Room users such as Porygon2 and Hatterene often need as much time and space as possible to launch into Trick Room, and both Fake Out and Intimidate offer these easily. Additionally, when in Trick Room, Parting Shot is great for pivoting in stronger slow attackers such as Iron Hands and Araquanid.

Fake Out Support.description:
• The given EV spread allows Incineroar to survive a Drain Punch from Iron Hands after taking damage from Stealth Rocks and outspeed Ogerpon during Tailwind. The remaining EVs are allocated to Attack.
  • When Darkinium Z is used with Parting Shot, Incineroar is able to fully heal the ally it switches into, allowing bulky setup Pokemon like Tapu Fini and Diancie a second chance to sweep.

Defensive Pivot.description:
• Incineroar's combination of Intimidate, Fake Out, and Parting Shot is one of the strongest utility toolkits in the tier, facilitating both defensive and offensive play by maintaining good positioning and increasing the longevity of its teammates. While it is a top-tier supportive piece, Incineroar lacks strong damage output against neutral targets and relies on the teammates it supports to win the game.
  • Fake Out generates free turns for teammates, providing opportunities for a teammate like Kingambit to set up with Swords Dance. Alternatively, it can allow a teammate to safely switch in, take a KO, or use a supportive move like Tailwind or Trick Room.
  • Flare Blitz and Knock Off are strong, consistent damaging options. Flare Blitz offers more immediate damage that can OHKO Chien-Pao and threatens common Pokemon like Gholdengo and Rillaboom. On the other hand, Knock Off adds to Incineroar's utility, removing items like Clear Amulet, Porygon2's Eviolite, and Choice items. With Incineroar's low Speed stat, Parting Shot will often go last, so teammates can enter the field without the risk of being hit.
  • The given EV spread allows Incineroar to survive Volcanion's Steam Eruption and Ogerpon-W's Tera Water Ivy Cudgel after Intimidate. However, Incineroar's EV spreads are extremely flexible depending on the needs of a team, whether it be offensive investment, more defensive EVs, or a higher Speed tier.
  • Tera Ghost stops opposing Fake Out and grants an immunity to Fighting-type moves such as Iron Hands's Drain Punch. Tera Grass flips matchups against threatening foes such as Ogerpon-W and Landorus and grants a Spore immunity.
  • Incineroar fits easily on any team, but it is quite commonly paired with Rillaboom to have constant Fake Out and repositioning options or Ogerpon-W, which provides redirection support and further adds to the team's defensive capabilities while maintaining a strong offensive presence on its own. Strong attackers such as Landorus,Chien-Pao, and slower, setup-based teammates like Swords Dance Kingambit greatly appreciate Incineroar's utility.

Assault Vest.description:
Assault Vest Primarina is a great special tank while being a remarkable offensive threat itself, capable of trading hits against offensive teams. It can check threats like Walking Wake, Dragapult, Darkrai, and Iron Valiant and stomach even strong super effective hits from foes like Iron Moth and Raging Bolt, all while having a decent matchup against common physical attackers like Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Cinderace. Psychic Noise hits Toxapex super effectively and blocks healing from walls like Blissey, Clodsire, and Clefable, allowing Primarina to chip them down for itself and its partners. It also lets Primarina pick off Zamazenta and Iron Moth behind a Substitute. Draining Kiss's recovery provides valuable longevity, which pairs extremely well with its hit-taking capabilities. Flip Turn turns Primarina into a pivot, letting it bring in a teammate in safely, either after being attacked or on predicted switches to gain momentum. Whirlpool can be used to stallbreak by trapping the likes of Blissey and Toxapex that may otherwise outlast Primarina, especially in conjunction with Psychic Noise to keep them low. While Torrent is preferred, Liquid Voice can be used on sets that forgo Surf to still maintain a strong STAB move from Psychic Noise; this also allows Primarina shut down even Tera Dark Blissey. Tera Poison and Steel improves its matchup against Iron Valiant, provides a poison immunity from foes like Pecharunt and Clodsire, and flip Primarina's Poison and Grass weakness against moves like Rillaboom's Wood Hammer and Iron Moth's Sludge Wave. Tera Poison lets Primarina maintain its decent matchup against Zamazenta and is better against Iron Moth and Focus Blast Darkrai, while Tera Steel lets it check Deoxys-S, Hatterene, and Galarian Slowking better and pivot more freely in the face of Stealth Rock. Tera Grass aids Primarina's matchup into Ogerpon-W and can help it against Raging Bolt in a pinch too. 48 Special Defense EVs allow Primarina to survive two Tera Water Choice Specs Walking Wake's Hydro Steam under sun. A more offensive spread is also an option, such as going for 80 HP / 252 SpA / 176 Spe; the Speed lets Primarina outspeed Adamant Kingambit and Ursaluna, with the remaining HP EVs allowing Primarina to still reach feats such as surviving Protosynthesis Thunderbolt from Raging Bolt, +1 Speed Booster Energy Iron Moth's Sludge Wave, +2 Gliscor's Earthquake, and two Heavy Slams from Zamazenta.

Assault Vest Primarina is best used on bulky offense teams that appreciate a Pokemon that has both offensive and defensive prowess, generally teams that are particularly weak to special attackers. Landorus-T provides Intimidate and checks the physical attackers that Primarina struggles with like Kingambit and Great Tusk. Great Tusk is another great teammate, as it provides entry hazard removal and checks Galarian Slowking, which tends to threaten Primarina. In return, Primarina can handle threats like Darkrai and Walking Wake. Kingambit and Weavile appreciate support from Primarina that can switch in on and threaten Pokemon like Iron Valiant and Zamazenta. Furthermore, both of these Pokemon help check Galarian Slowking for Primarina, along with resisting Grass-type attacks. Gholdengo appreciates Primarina's ability to check Fire-types like Cinderace and Heatran, as well as Walking Wake. Primarina struggles with Grass-types like Ogerpon-W, Meowscarada, and Rillaboom, so it's essential to have checks to these such as Rillaboom, Cinderace, and Kingambit. Cinderace, aside from resisting Grass-type attacks, can also help with hazard removal with Court Change, allowing Primarina to switch in more often. Dragapult and Cinderace can form a great pivoting core with Primarina, and they can also spread burn in order to help improve Primarina's matchup against physical attackers like Great Tusk.

Calm Mind.description:
Primarina’s excellent defensive typing and stats provide it with solid survivability, with which it can set up Calm Mind boosts and sweep. Thanks to Liquid Voice, Psychic Noise becomes a STAB move while also blocking the recovery of foes like Garganacl, Clefable, and Corviknight. On the other hand, Surf is a stronger STAB option and is usually paired with Torrent. While Moonblast is Primarina's strongest move, OHKOing Darkrai and Dragapult, using the weaker Draining Kiss trades a bit of damage for a solid recovery option, letting it accrue even more Calm Mind boosts. Substitute to help it gather Calm Mind boosts while blocking crippling status moves like Thunder Wave and Trick from walls like Galarian Slowking and revenge killers like Gholdengo. Having Psychic Noise as the fourth move alongside Surf can be a useful combo to ensure Primarina has an option to deny opposing recovery, as well as providing it a Psychic-type coverage option to break through Toxapex and hit opponents like Iron Moth even behind a Substitute. This EV spread forgoes Primarina’s lackluster Speed to max out its HP, increasing its bulk and survivability, especially with access to Draining Kiss. 8 Special Defense EVs let it guarantee survive two Choice Specs Protosynthesis Timid Walking Wake's Hydro Steam under sun after Leftovers. Primarina can benefit from alternate EV spreads as well; running Modest 252 HP / 172 SpA / 84 Spe allows it to outspeed Sinistcha, particularly when running Psychic Noise, and 176 Spe can help outspeed and beat Adamant Kingambit. Tera Poison gives Primarina a resistance Galarian Slowking’s Sludge Bomb and an immunity to Toxic; Tera Steel can grant a Poison immunity, but cannot grant Toxic Spikes absorption like Tera Poison can. Both can also reverse Primarina's weakness to Grass, helping it take on Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W. Tera Ghost is an alternative if the team could use another way to block Rapid Spin in a pinch as well as to wall Blissey's Seismic Toss.

Primarina excels on bulky offense teams alongside other Pokemon that can both take and dish out hits. Offensive Steel-type staples like Kingambit and Gholdengo are perfect partners for Primarina thanks to their immunity to the Poison-type moves that threaten it. Both of these teammates also can put holes in the opposing team to help Primarina sweep late game, weakening checks like Galarian Slowking that it struggles with. Entry hazard setters like Great Tusk and Ting-Lu can set Stealth Rock and Spikes, which support Primarina’s sweeping late-game. Primarina does a good job of breaking through foes that maintain longevity in face of those hazards like Gliscor, Corviknight, and Clefable using Psychic Noise. Primarina’s biggest threats are the Ogerpon formes; Ogerpon-W is immune to its Water-type moves thanks to Water Absorb, all formes have a powerful Grass-type STAB move such as Power Whip or Ivy Cudgel that can dispatch Primarina quickly, and all formes of Ogerpon have access to Encore, which can take advantage of Primarina trying to use Calm Mind or Substitute. Teammates that can outspeed Ogerpon or Ogerpon-W and use Will-O-Wisp like Cinderace, Dragapult, and Galarian Weezing can help weaken their power, while bulky wallbreakers like Zamazenta can take hits and threaten them out. Other powerful opposing physical attackers like Kingambit and Focus Sash Ceruledge can survive hits from even Calm Mind-boosted Primarina and dispatch it in short order; switching to a teammate like Landorus-T with Rocky Helmet can weaken them with Intimidate and help wear them down over the course of a game. Primarina is also very vulnerable to hazards itself, so teammates like Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Cinderace are useful to remove them with Rapid Spin and Court Change.

Bulky Calm Mind.description:
Possessing decent bulk and a stellar typing, Calm Mind Primarina can sweep teams with its near-perfect offensive coverage. With valuable resistances to offensive typings like Dark and Fighting, Primarina can check common Pokemon such as Urshifu-R and Hisuian Samurott and even set up on them. Although Primarina competes with Tapu Fini for the same role, it has useful traits that separates it. Scald is a consistent damaging move that works well alongside Calm Mind, giving it chances to burn switch-ins such as Ferrothorn, Galarian Slowking, and Toxapex. Scald should be paired with Torrent for an extra damage boost at low health, guaranteeing the OHKO on Mega Diancie and, when Calm Mind-boosted, breaking through Galarian Slowking and Z-Move Gholdengo. Psychic Noise combined with Liquid Voice is slightly weaker than Scald but lets Primarina stop healing from Pokemon like Alomomola, Toxapex, and Zapdos; it also allows Primarina to beat other setup Pokemon like Substitute Volcarona in a one-on-one. Draining Kiss helps Primarina stay healthy and gives it more chances to sweep through teams, while Moonblast has a much better damage output, keeping Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Tapu Lele from coming in as freely. Leftovers offsets damage taken from Substitute. 124 Speed EVs allow Primarina to outspeed 0 Speed Mega Scizor and Raging Bolt and other Pokemon around its Speed tier, like Clefable and Corviknight, which Primarina can boost up on behind a Substitute.

Primarina provides good value for bulky offense teams; it checks Dark-type Pokemon such as Hisuian Samurott and Weavile and Fighting-types like Urshifu-R and Zamazenta while also threatening sweeps of its own. Weavile itself and Kingambit make nice teammates, as they appreciate Primarina's help against Urshifu-R and annoying Fire-types like Moltres and Volcarona, and in return, they Pursuit trap threats to Primarina's sweep like Galarian Slowking. Dragonite defends against Ogerpon-W and Kartana in exchange for Primarina weakening and potentially burning Steel-types like Ferrothorn, Mega Scizor, and Melmetal and chipping Fairy-types such as Hatterene, Iron Valiant, and Tapu Fini. Primarina has a hard time breaking through Grass-types like Ogerpon-W and Ferrothorn, so teammates such as Rillaboom and Volcarona can be paired with Primarina to give it better odds of breaking through or finishing off weakened teams. Rillaboom notably provides Grassy Terrain, which provides additional healing and makes Primarina better defensively against Ground-types like Garchomp and Landorus-T. Rillaboom is also good at baiting in Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Toxapex and weakening them for Primarina, which switches well into threats to Rillaboom like Cinderace and Dragonite. Poison-types like Toxapex and Galarian Slowking can be tough for Primarina, so it can pair with Heatran and Gholdengo while pressuring their checks such as Hisuian Samurott and Ting-Lu. Primarina can struggle with entry hazards due to its lack of immediate recovery, so it appreciates hazard removers like Great Tusk and Landorus-T. These Pokemon can scare out Galarian Slowking, Raging Bolt, and bulky Steel-types like Melmetal, while Primarina can beat Urshifu-R and Alomomola and pressure Flying-types like Corviknight and Moltres for them.

Assault Vest.description:
Thanks to its good special bulk and defensive typing, Primarina with an Assault Vest can function as a defensive pivot capable of checking powerful special attackers like Mega Latios, Tapu Lele lacking Psyshock, and Volcarona. It can also check some physical attackers like Urshifu-R and Zamazenta. It performs a crucial offensive role alongside its vital defensive role, being able to exert pressure on common defensive backbones like Gliscor, Ting-Lu, and Moltres. Despite Primarina's excellent special bulk, it often competes with less entry hazard-prone pivots with good longevity like Alomomola and Pecharunt, although it can exert more offensive pressure. Scald is preferred over other Water-type attacks like Surf and Hydro Pump, as it can burn physical attackers like Melmetal, Kingambit, and Mega Scizor, hindering their offensive presence. Flip Turn lets Primarina generate momentum for its teammates and pivot out of healthy checks like Galarian Slowking and Ferrothorn. Psychic Noise is a coverage move that allows Primarina to super effectively target and deny recovery for Poison-types like Pecharunt, Toxapex, and Mega Venusaur on the switch in as well as being able to prevent Alomomola from Wish passing. Torrent is the preferred ability, as it further increases Primarina's damage output and trading capabilities, allowing it to score a guaranteed OHKO on Tapu Koko and Tornadus-T after Stealth Rock. A Modest nature increases Primarina's damage output, allowing it to OHKO maximum HP Landorus-T after Stealth Rock. 176 Speed EVs ensure that Primarina outspeeds Adamant Kingambit.

Primarina fits best on offense and bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to serve as a specially defensive blanket and pressurize the likes of Gliscor and Heatran. Potent wallbreakers like Mega Diancie and Tapu Lele appreciate Primarina's ability to muscle through the aforementioned defensive Pokemon. In return, they break common defensive backbones in Zapdos and Toxapex that Primarina struggles to force progress against. Powerful wallbreakers and sweepers such as Volcarona, Ogerpon-W, and Urshifu-R benefit from Primarina's ability to threaten Dragon-types, including Dragonite and Mega Latios. Primarina appreciates their ability to threaten Steel-types such as Melmetal and Ferrothorn in return. Primarina's glaring weakness to entry hazards means it appreciates excellent hazard removal options like Great Tusk, Terapagos, and Defog Landorus-T. Additionally, Great Tusk can switch into common physical attackers such as Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar, while Landorus-T can switch into Electric-type Pokemon like Tapu Koko lacking Hidden Power Ice and Raging Bolt, which Primarina struggles against defensively. In return, Primarina can comfortably switch into wallbreakers like Iron Valiant and Mega Latios, which the aforementioned hazard removal options in Great Tusk and Landorus-T struggle against. Viable revenge killers such as Zamazenta, Mega Lopunny, and Weavile are also appreciated, as they threaten defensive staples that Primarina cannot consistently pressurize like Ferrothorn and Galarian Slowking. As a teammate, Primarina can prevent defensive pieces that check the aforementioned revenge killers like Mega Venusaur and Pecharunt from remaining healthy. Primarina struggles against Grass-types such as Ogerpon-W and Serperior, which means that Grass-type answers such as Dragonite and Melmetal are appreciated. In return, Primarina acts as a check to certain foes that can revenge kill Dragonite, such as Urshifu-R and Tapu Lele, and Fire-types like Volcarona and Heatran, which Melmetal cannot defensively answer.

Life Orb.description:
• This spread allows Primarina to beat Pokemon that it usually can't, such as Timid Weakness Policy Iron Crown and non-Agility Corviknight.
  • Generally, the sequence against Iron Crown is to use Encore on the first turn to lock it into using Calm Mind, then use Icy Wind twice to lower its Speed so Primarina can lock it with Encore back into Calm Mind in the following turn, then use Moonblast once and use Encore once again, then alternate between Hydro Cannon and Encore, keeping the recharge turn and Life Orb damage in mind. In case Iron Crown uses Tachyon Cutter on the first turn, it activates Torrent on turn two, which allows Primarina to OHKO it with Hydro Cannon.
  • This spread allows Primarina to survive a Poison Jab or Sludge Wave from Adamant Choice Band Urshifu formes and Timid Life Orb Landorus and then OHKO them with Moonblast or Icy Wind, respectively.
  • An alternative EV spread of 56 HP / 192 Def / 8 SpA / 252 Spe lets Primarina bulk Jolly Choice Band Urshifu formes' attacks but not Adamant Choice Band variants, dropping that matchup in order to gain a more consistent Iron Crown matchup, since Primarina's higher Speed stat means it can outspeed Iron Crown after a single Icy Wind and threaten Special Attack Booster Energy variants with a Torrent-boosted Hydro Cannon if Iron Crown decides to go for an attack. This spread also allows Primarina to outspeed Ursaluna and OHKO it with Hydro Cannon.
  • Against Spectrier, use Encore on turn one. If Spectrier attacks on turn one, use Hydro Cannon on turn two. If Spectrier uses a status move, use Icy Wind thrice with the main spread or twice with the alternative spread, then use Encore to lock Spectrier into a status move while dealing damage with Moonblast and Hydro Cannon.
  • Moonblast allows Primarina to beat commonly used Dragon- and Fighting-type Pokemon, such as Roaring Moon, Dragapult, the Urshifu formes, and Iron Valiant.
  • Since Primarina is weak to Poison-type or STAB attacks from foes such as Sneasler, Pecharunt, Volcanion, Hoopa, Raging Bolt, and Ogerpon-Wellspring, it is suggested to pair Primarina with Dragon- and Steel-type Pokemon such as Roaring Moon, Iron Crown, and Metagross to form the well-known Dragon / Fairy / Steel core.

Weakness Policy.description:
• Primarina is one of the strongest Pokemon in 1v1 thanks to its unique typing, important role compression, and variety of sets.
  • The combination of Weakness Policy and Charm or Reflect allows Primarina to take care of slower threats that aim to defeat it with their super effective moves, such as Iron Hands with Supercell Slam and Donphan and Ursaluna with Gunk Shot.
  • Charm can work multiple times, which can help if Primarina is trying to stall a foe or to get to Torrent range to fire off an extremely strong Hydro Cannon, while Reflect can take care of Clear Amulet Pokemon, an item these Pokemon can run to be a hard counter to the Charm variant.
  • Hydro Cannon can KO Ursaluna and Donphan after a boost from Weakness Policy on the former and a Draining Kiss on the latter.
  • Draining Kiss and Moonblast can threaten both Urshifu formes, and while Draining Kiss is especially helpful for the Donphan matchup, Moonblast can also be utilized for overall damage against Haxorus.
  • Calm Mind lets it set up in front of potential threats like Clear Amulet Cresselia.
  • Thanks to its huge investment in Speed, Primarina can outrun Ursaluna, Iron Hands, and Donphan while threatening KOs in return, with its Defense and HP maximized for the best rolls against Choice Band Haxorus.
  • Primarina should be used in teams where its weaknesses to Grass, Electric, and Poison are patched up, so it really likes pairing with Dragon-types like Raging Bolt, Steel-types like Corviknight and Hisuian Goodra, or Psychic-types like Hoopa-U and Iron Crown.

Choice Specs.description:
• Hydro Cannon is Primarina's strongest attack and should be used against both Landorus formes, non-Custap Berry Skeledirge, and non-Substitute Volcarona.
  • Moonblast defeats Haxorus and Garchomp.
  • Energy Ball should be used against Rhyperior and is Primarina's best way to deal with non-Sap Sipper Azumarill.
  • Liquid Voice + Uproar makes Primarina defeat Registeel and gives it an option to defeat Custap Berry Skeledirge and Substitute Volcarona, while Psychic Noise + Torrent allows it to beat Whimsicott reliably. Torrent Primarina is also more consistent agaisnt bulkier Choice Specs Hoopa sets, as Moonblast does not always OHKO them.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Primarina to survive Earthquake from Choice Band Landorus-T, while the Special Defense EVs allow it to survive Sludge Wave from Timid Choice Specs Landorus.
  • Choice Specs Primarina, unlike other Primarina sets, loses to Encore + Disable Iron Valiant sets, so it is important to use a teammate that can defeat the aforementioned sets.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Fairy (Calm Mind)

Heavy-Duty Boots may be used over Leftovers due to Fairy having poor hazard control, but Primarina finds it a bit harder to set up without passive recovery. Alternatively, Covert Cloak may be used to prevent Alolan Muk's Poison Jab or Sneasler's Dire Claw from inflicting status on Primarina. Chilling Water lets Primarina take on physical attacking walls like Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra, as it lowers their Attack to manageable levels, but the greatly reduced base power compared to Surf makes Primarina lose out on OHKOing Landorus and Ursaluna-B and 2HKOing Gholdengo and Skeledirge at +1. An EV spread of 252 HP / 64 Def / 192 Spe with a Bold nature may be considered, as it lets Primarina outspeed and KO Modest Ursaluna-B which otherwise severely damages Primarina with Blood Moon, but the reduced bulk is detrimental to Primarina's ability to check Gouging Fire. If one opts for a fast variant of Primarina, Encore over Draining Kiss or Psychic Noise may also be considered to lock threats such as Belly Drum Azumarill and Bulk Up Corviknight into unfavorable moves. Liquid Voice may be considered to compress the effects of Psychic Noise and Surf into one move, making it easier to fit Encore, but being unable to hit Water Absorb Clodsire is undesirable. Substitute over Draining Kiss can also be considered to dodge status and force damage on switch-ins, but the lack of recovery apart from Leftovers can be detrimental.

Fairy (Assault Vest)

Draining Kiss can be used over Psychic Noise to grant Primarina a form of recovery. However, this comes with the cost of being walled by Poison-types like Toxapex and Amoonguss. Alternatively, Primarina can run Psychic Noise with Liquid Voice, which can block the healing of Dark-types like Alolan Muk, but this restricts its coverage and allows Water Absorb Clodsire to wall it.

Calm Mind (Fairy).description:
With an excellent typing and serviceable Speed and bulk, Primarina is one of the better users of Calm Mind for Fairy teams, as it deals with common roadblocks for Fairy like Corviknight, Clodsire, and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. Psychic Noise prevents all forms of recovery, making it harder for walls like the aforementioned Clodsire and Articuno to keep up with Primarina. Coincidentally, Psychic Noise also helps Primarina muscle past other bulky setup sweepers like Dragonite and Clefable. Draining Kiss improves Primarina's longevity and threatens Dragon- and Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Weavile. Surf sweeps away Heatran, Skarmory, and Choice Scarf Landorus, all of which are nuisances for Fairy teams. 60 Speed EVs let Primarina outspeed Corviknight and prevent it from recovering with Psychic Noise, making it easier to wear down, while the rest of the EVs are invested in Defense and HP to improve Primarina's matchup against Steel teams.

Due to Primarina's relatively low Defense stat, dual screens support from Klefki is vital for its success, as it lets Primarina check Swords Dance Ceruledge and Bisharp. In return, Primarina deals with Clodsire and Corviknight, which all take advantage of Klefki. Iron Valiant deals with Ogerpon formes, Kyurem, and Landorus, which overwhelm Primarina, and also deals with bulky Steel-types like Bisharp and Hisuian Goodra with Close Combat and Ice Punch. In return, Primarina checks Volcarona, which can take advantage of Choice-locked Iron Valiant. Choice Specs Flutter Mane outspeeds and vaporizes Choice Specs Greninja, Choice Specs Latios, Spectrier, and Ogerpon-H; in return, Primarina breaks down defensive Pokemon such as Articuno, Corviknight, Clodsire, and Skarmory for it. Entry hazards, especially Toxic Spikes, greatly hinder Primarina's ability to set up, so Primarina greatly appreciates Hatterene's ability to bounce back entry hazards with Magic Bounce. Hatterene also has a wide array of supportive moves like Nuzzle and Healing Wish which help circumvent Primarina's low Speed and give it a second chance to sweep. For instance, being able to slow down Articuno and Tornadus and subject Corviknight and Toxapex to the prospect of getting fully paralyzed makes Primarina's job easier. Belly Drum Azumarill is a secondary sweeper that deals with Hisuian Goodra and Alolan Muk, which Primarina struggles to beat, and it's also able to threaten Bisharp and Gliscor more. Choice Scarf Enamorus deals with fast threats like Dragapult and Choice Specs Greninja with Moonblast and loves Primarina being able to soften up opposing teams. Enamorus also provides Healing Wish, which gives Primarina a second chance to threaten opposing teams. Clefable can form a Calm Mind core with Primarina to overload special walls like Articuno and Alolan Muk, or it can set Stealth Rock and slow down the opposing team for Primarina with Thunder Wave. Mimikyu provides a failsafe against sweepers like Ceruledge due to Disguise, and it can use a Swords Dance set to clean up opposing teams late-game.

Calm Mind (Water).description:
With Calm Mind, Primarina turns into a great option for Water teams against Fighting and Dragon teams, being able to threaten the likes of Scrafty and Hydreigon. When running Liquid Voice, Psychic Noise turns into Primarina's main Water-type STAB move, while running Torrent makes it great coverage against Clodsire. Draining Kiss is Primarina's main source of longevity, being especially effective against the aforementioned Fighting- and Dragon-types. When running Liquid Voice, Primarina can run Ice Beam to threaten Garchomp, Gliscor, and both Landorus formes. Surf is the better option for Primarina when it chooses to run Torrent so it has a stronger Water-type STAB attack. Alternatively, Encore can be used to take advantage of slower walls like Ting-Lu by locking them into an undesirable move. 60 Speed EVs allow Primarina to outspeed Corviknight.

Primarina struggles against Poison-types such as Alolan Muk and Sneasler; therefore, it appreciates teammates such as Swampert and Gastrodon to check them. The two of them also provide an Electric immunity and entry hazard support. Toxapex absorbs Toxic Spikes while dealing with Grass-types that Primarina struggles with such as Meowscarada and the Ogerpon formes. In return, Primarina deals with some of Toxapex's checks like Great Tusk and Mamoswine. Keldeo and Urshifu-R are great offensive teammates that can muscle through Steel-types such as Archaludon, Hisuian Goodra, and Bisharp. Primarina deals with Iron Valiant in return. Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott handles Ghost-types like Gholdengo, Dragapult, and Spectrier, and in return, Primarina threatens Fighting-types like Urshifu-R and Keldeo. Choice Specs Greninja handles threats that Primarina struggles against, such as the Ogerpon formes, opposing Primarina, Amoonguss, and Okidogi. Ogerpon-W pairs well offensively with Primarina, handling Landorus, Ursaluna, and Iron Treads, while Primarina deals with various Fighting-, Dragon-, and Dark-types like Urshifu-R, Roaring Moon, and Sableye.

Choice Specs (Fairy).description:
Packing tremendous power with its high Special Attack and excellent STAB moves, Choice Specs Primarina is one of Fairy's deadliest wallbreakers. Hydro Pump is Primarina's most powerful STAB move, threatening Fairy-resistant foes such as Gholdengo and Alolan Muk and OHKOing Flutter Mane when Primarina is in Torrent range. Alternatively, Surf can be used for more accuracy at the cost of power. Moonblast tears through Dragon-, Dark-, and Fighting-type Pokemon such as Dragapult, Garchomp, Hoopa-U, and Iron Valiant while wearing down its supposed checks in Hisuian Goodra and Ting-Lu thanks to its raw power. Psychic Noise lets Primarina damage Amoonguss, Toxapex, and Water Absorb Clodsire, which would otherwise shrug off its STAB moves. Flip Turn lets Primarina maintain momentum, pivoting out of bad matchups like Blissey and Empoleon while sending in a teammate. The 88 Speed EVs allow Primarina to outpace Skarmory and Corviknight, while the rest are invested in Special Attack and bulk. Its bulk in particular can stand out because Primarina takes moderately strong attacks from the likes of Dragapult, Flutter Mane, and Gholdengo while trading with them.

Klefki is an excellent teammate for Primarina, providing dual screens and entry hazard support in one; the former lets Primarina check Swords Dance Ceruledge and Choice Band Scizor, while the latter allows Primarina to get the KOs it wouldn't otherwise get. Klefki can also switch in on Grass- and Poison-types like Ogerpon-C, Meowscarada, and Sneasler that otherwise pressure Primarina. Choice Specs Flutter Mane can also form a great offensive core with Primarina, as it can outspeed and pressure Choice Specs Greninja and Ogerpon-H with options like Thunderbolt and Power Gem and eventually overwhelm shared checks in Articuno, Hisuian Goodra, and Ting-Lu. Choice Scarf Flutter Mane can also provide excellent speed control, outspeeding Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Sneasler. In return, Primarina threatens Corviknight and Choice Scarf Gholdengo, both of which pose a threat to Flutter Mane. Swords Dance Iron Valiant benefits from Primarina luring in Steel-types, while Iron Valiant helps break past special walls including Blissey, Empoleon, and Hisuian Goodra with Close Combat. Hatterene can provide important entry hazard control with Magic Bounce, allowing Primarina to avoid being worn down by entry hazards. Hatterene can also provide paralysis support via Nuzzle to slow down foes such as the Ogerpon formes and Cinderace. Primarina also appreciates Trick Room support from Hatterene, letting Primarina act as a more potent wallbreaker, while Hatterene can act as a potent cleaner with Calm Mind once Primarina has broken past its checks. Azumarill can stand out as a physically offensive counterpart to Primarina; its Belly Drum set ensures that it is able to break through Articuno and Assault Vest Hisuian Goodra, while Primarina can overwhelm physical walls such as Archaludon and Skarmory, both of which Azumarill struggles against. Tinkaton is also a great partner for Primarina, providing Stealth Rock and paralysis support via Thunder Wave, as well as Pickpocket support that takes away Leftovers or Assault Vest from Hisuian Goodra and Alolan Muk; Tinkaton can also use Encore on Raging Bolt, which Primarina otherwise struggles with. Enamorus shines as a partner, as it is able to lure in Rock-types like Hisuian Arcanine, Coalossal, and Garganacl that Primarina can threaten while also providing Healing Wish support to give Primarina more chances at wallbreaking. In return, Primarina removes Steel-types like Iron Treads, Gholdengo, and Tinkaton.

Assault Vest (Water).description:
