Assault Vest Primarina is a solid offensive pivot for Water teams capable of taking hits from threats like Darkrai and Dragapult comfortably. Moonblast nails Fighting-, Dark-, and Dragon-types such as Kommo-o, Darkrai, and Archaludon. Surf handles Steel-types like Gholdengo and Heatran. Psychic Noise catches would-be checks like Toxapex and Water Absorb Clodsire. Finally, Flip Turn can safely pivot in teammates such as Urshifu-R and Hisuian Samurott on walls that check Primarina like Hisuian Goodra and Galarian Slowking. The EV spread enables Primarina to outspeed Corviknight while preventing it from being 2HKOed from Choice Scarf Archaludon's Thunderbolt after Stealth Rock.

Assault Vest Primarina fits best onto more offensive-leaning teamstyles such as rain, making teammates like Barraskewda and Kingdra great partners. While rain is up, they are able to outspeed and check faster threats such as Meowscarada and Kyurem. Barraskewda also uses its strong coverage to break through special walls Primarina struggles with like Hisuian Goodra and Water Absorb Clodsire with Close Combat and Psychic Fangs, respectively. Pelipper enables rain through Drizzle, and its Ground immunity helps against threats like Landorus-T and Great Tusk while being able to pivot Primarina in with U-turn. Hisuian Samurott provides Spikes support with Ceaseless Edge to wear down foes like Alolan Muk and Flutter Mane while using Sucker Punch to catch faster threats like Latios and Spectrier. Choice Scarf Urshifu-R can outspeed and handle threats like Choice Specs Flutter Mane and the Ogerpon formes for Primarina. Swampert provides a strong defensive support, being able to take on Poison- and Electric-types such as Galarian Slowking, Sandy Shocks, and Raging Bolt. Toxapex can handle Grass-types such as Meowscarada and the Ogerpon formes for Primarina, as well as use Toxic to wear down bulky targets like Iron Hands. Alomomola can support Primarina by being able to take hits from physical attackers such as Mamoswine and Kleavor and use Wish to keep Primarina healthy.

Assault Vest (Fairy).description:
With an Assault Vest, Primarina leverages its natural special bulk to serve an incredible role on Fairy teams as a special tank, being able to take hits from the likes of Gholdengo, Iron Moth, and Landorus. Surf hits problematic Fire-types for Fairy such as Heatran and Iron Moth while also being able to force out Gholdengo and Spectrier before it uses Calm Mind. Moonblast hits Water-resistant foes like Hydrapple and Kyurem. Flip Turn gives Primarina a solid pivoting tool to switch out on threats it cannot handle, such as Alolan Muk, Articuno, and Hisuian Goodra. Finally, Psychic Noise allows Primarina to hit Poison-types like Amoonguss, Toxapex, and Okidogi. The EV spread used lets Primarina outspeed threats like Adamant Azumaril. The alternative EV spread is a bulkier set that outspeeds Corviknight and makes it more reliable against threats like Choice Specs Latios and Flutter Mane.

With Primarina's limited recovery options, Hatterene provides excellent support, being able to keep entry hazards off the field and allowing Primarina to come in safely. Hatterene can also spread paralysis against threats like Gholdengo, Tornadus-T, and Gallade using Nuzzle. Klefki can provide hazard and dual screens support, allowing Primarina to combat special walls like Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra. Clefable can provide hazard support in Stealth Rock, along with Wish support to heal Primarina. Flutter Mane appreciates Primarina's neutrality to Steel-type attacks from the likes of Choice Scarf Gholdengo, while Primarina appreciates Flutter Mane's strong movepool that can hinder problematic threats like Articuno, Ogerpon-H, and Raging Bolt. Flutter Mane also enjoys Primarina's Flip Turn to grant it safe entry. Primarina values physical Iron Valiant's ability to remove special walls like Blissey, Galarian Slowking, and Clodsire. In return, Iron Valiant takes advantage of Primarina's ability to take on threats like Choice Scarf Latios, Choice Specs Dragapult, and Choice Scarf Enamorus. Mimikyu appreciates Primarina's pivoting to grant it safe entry and setup opportunities. In exchange, Primarina welcomes Mimikyu's ability to remove threats like Flutter Mane and Iron Hands. Choice Scarf Enamorus can remove fasters threats like Sneasler and Iron Valiant and provide Healing Wish support.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Primarina fits well on balance teams, as it benefits from utility moves like Fake Out, healing, and redirection support that allow it to attack freely while other Pokemon cover its weaknesses.
  • Primarina synergizes well with Sneasler, as Sneasler covers its Grass-type weakness. Additionally, Rillaboom offers Fake Out utility and passive Grassy Terrain recovery, benefiting a bulkier attacker like Primarina.
  • Electabuzz is an effective redirector, shielding Primarina from threats like Archaludon and Sneasler while also redirecting Spores from Amoonguss thanks to its Vital Spirit ability and providing speed control with Electroweb. Similarly, Magmar makes a great partner with its access to Vital Spirit and Follow Me. In addition, Magmar resists Rillaboom's Grass-type attacks and can use Will-O-Wisp to compensate for Primarina’s lower physical bulk.
  • Though Primarina sits in an awkward Speed tier, it can operate on teams with a Trick Room mode such as compositions with Porygon2 and Ursaluna.
  • Kingambit is a strong offensive partner for Primarina. With Primarina's chip damage, Kingambit can more easily secure KOs with Sucker Punch. Additionally, most Kingambit sets include Swords Dance, allowing it to punish passive plays and forcing the opponent to choose between Primarina or Kingambit to target.
  • Gholdengo is another common partner for Primarina, as they effectively cover each other's weaknesses. Primarina threatens Pokemon like Incineroar and Garchomp, which can beat Gholdengo, while Gholdengo walls and pressures threats like Sneasler, Rillaboom, and Amoonguss.

Strategy Comments

  • As a slower-paced offensive piece, Primarina excels when it's positioned to safely chip away at opponents. For instance, being alongside a redirection Pokemon allows it to unleash substantial chip damage with Hyper Voice. Due to its respectable bulk, Primarina can often continue using Hyper Voice until a Pokémon that poses a significant immediate threat, such as Rillaboom, enters the field.
  • The strategy with Primarina is to wait for the opportunity to establish a strong offensive position. Typically, this involves pivoting it around until it can come in and clean up effectively mid- or late-game.
  • As mentioned earlier, Rillaboom and Archaludon are significant threats; however, Sneasler effectively counters both. When facing opposing Sneasler or setup sweepers like Gholdengo or Volcarona, it's crucial to position Primarina correctly—either by placing it next to a redirector, so it can attack freely, or by utilizing other Pokemon to apply more immediate pressure. This is because Primarina is most effective when its consistent spread chip damage is sufficient to prevent it from being outpaced on offense.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Primarina excels at dealing consistent damage and wearing down opposing Pokemon. Its strong offensive typing, high Special Attack, and ability to take advantage of STAB Hyper Voice with Liquid Voice make it a formidable threat. Additionally, it puts pressure on common metagame Pokemon like Incineroar and Garchomp.
  • Haze prevents setup Pokémon from exploiting Primarina's slower offensive pace. More importantly, it's often used to counter the Dondozo and Tatsugiri matchup.
  • While Throat Spray provides a power boost after using Hyper Voice, Life Orb offers more immediate damage, making it better suited for more aggressive teams. For example, Life Orb guarantees an OHKO on Hisuian Typhlosion with Hyper Voice while allowing Primarina to 2HKO Sneasler and Choice Specs Gholdengo with Hyper Voice. Sitrus Berry, on the other hand, enables Primarina to take on a more passive role, consistently enhancing its survivability. For instance, Sitrus Berry's recovery enables it to live two Stomping Tantrums from Life Orb Garchomp.
  • Tera Poison allows Primarina to resist both of Sneasler's STAB moves and, unlike the other two recommended Tera types, doesn't introduce many common weaknesses. Tera Steel gives Primarina an immunity to Poison-type moves like Sneasler's Dire Claw and a resistance to Steel-type attacks, making it particularly effective against Gholdengo's Make it Rain. Tera Grass, like Tera Poison and Tera Steel, offers a resistance to Grass-type moves from Pokemon like Rillaboom. It also provides a resistance to Electric-type attacks like Electro Shot from Archaludon, and an immunity to Spore, preventing Amoonguss from shutting it down.
  • With the given Defense and HP investment, Primarina is guaranteed to survive Grassy Glide from maximum Attack Rillaboom and a 100-Base Power Last Respects from non-Adaptability Choice Band Basculegion. The Special Defense investment ensures it can withstand Tera Steel Make it Rain from Choice Specs Gholdengo, Blood Moon from Life Orb Ursaluna-B, and two Freeze-Dry hits from Alolan Ninetales. The Special Attack investment gives Primarina a good chance to OHKO Garchomp with Moonblast and non-bulky Talonflame with Hyper Voice, while the Speed investment is designed to outspeed maximum Speed Maushold in Tailwind.

Little Mermaid.description:
• With its great bulk, power, and typing, Primarina is a fantastic offensive and defensive presence in the BSS metagame.

  • Sparkling Aria: Sparkling Aria allows Primarina to get around Substitute attempts from foes like Garganacl that might try to stall out Moonblast.

  • Psychic Noise: Psychic Noise can allow Primarina to potentially muscle through walls such as Toxapex by preventing them from healing off its attacks. Additionally, it allows Primarina to better stand up to Ogerpon formes running Horn Leech as their Grass-type STAB move.

  • Energy Ball: Energy Ball provides Primarina with coverage to hit other Water-types, being particularly useful against Ogerpon-W and other Primarina.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet can allow Primarina to finish off weakened foes that might otherwise outspeed it, notably allowing Assault Vest variants to more consistently win the Flutter Mane matchup.

  • Flip Turn: Flip Turn allows Primarina to scout switches and provide safe entry for its teammates.

Other Options

  • Perish Song: If utilizing Choice Specs, Perish Song can allow Primarina to pressure foes that might otherwise wall it and disrupt attempts at Baton Pass use.

  • Tera Blast: If using Tera Fire, Tera Blast grants Primarina coverage to hit opposing Grass-types such as Serperior.

Items

  • Assault Vest: Assault Vest accentuates Primarina’s excellent special bulk, allowing it to more effectively trade hits with threats such as Flutter Mane.

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs allows Primarina to more effectively leverage its fantastic STAB combination, turning it into a shockingly powerful wallbreaker.

EV Spreads

  • 180 HP / 252 SpA / 76 Spe with Modest: This spread maximizes power and bulk while allowing Primarina to keep pace with uninvested base 70 Pokemon like Wo-Chien.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependancy - Low: Primarina’s incredible base typing allows it to go head to head with many prominent metagame threats without needing to Terastallize.

  • Fire: Tera Fire grants Primarina important Grass, Fairy, and Steel resistances while maintaining its all important Ice resistance.

  • Poison: Tera Poison allows Primarina to deny Toxic attempts from the likes of Toxapex and Gliscor while still granting it a Fairy resistance.

  • Water: Tera Water grants an extra boost to Sparkling Aria while remaining a good defensive typing.

Calm Mind.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • Psychic Noise and Liquid Voice: Liquid Voice turns Psychic Noise into a Water-type attack, giving up Sparkling Aria's power under Torrent in exchange for better match-ups against defensive Pokemon like Toxapex.

Focus Sash.description:
• Using a Focus Sash on Primarina may seem like a waste, but Primarina's high Special Attack, Sparkling Aria ignoring Substitute, and Torrent make it very tricky for offensive teams to check.

  • Aqua Jet: Despite it being weak, Aqua Jet's ability to pick off faster Focus Sash foes like Iron Bundle makes it essential.

  • Encore: Thanks to the Speed investment, this Primarina is especially good at catching normally faster, bulky Pokemon like Calm Mind Raging Bolt and Stamina Archaludon off guard.

  • Psychic Noise: Psychic Noise is Primarina's best option for shutting down Toxapex, Porygon2, and defensive Dragonite's walling capabilities, and it even punishes Horn Leech Ogerpon-H.

  • Energy Ball: Energy Ball improves Primarina's odds of winning mirror matches, and it deals more damage than anything else to Alomomola and Swampert.

  • Calm Mind: Calm Mind's boost lets Primarina potentially OHKO bulkier Assault Vest Ursaluna-B variants.

  • Speed EVs: Maximizing Primarina's Speed lets variants with a Modest nature outspeed up to Landorus-T with no Speed investment. While the power drop from Timid loses a guaranteed OHKO on offensive Ursaluna-B, it does let Primarina outspeed the rare but very dangerous Adamant Breloom.

Other Options

  • Icy Wind: Icy Wind's speed control comes in handy against defensive Dragon Dance Dragonite, but Primarina's low Speed makes it a lesser option.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Primarina will usually only Terastallize to improve its power or gain certain immunities, since Focus Sash makes this Pokemon rather disposable. Otherwise, it's best to leave Terastallization for other teammates.

  • Water: Tera Water's boost to Sparkling Aria makes it the easiest choice to recommend.

  • Stellar: Since Primarina rarely terastallizes anyways, Tera Stellar's flexibility can make sense for late-game sweeping scenarios.

  • Ground: Tera Ground saves Primarina from Electric-type attacks, with Raging Bolt and Tera Electric Chien-Pao being particularly good foes to flip.

  • Ghost: Despite Primarina's low Speed, most Extreme Speed Dragonite sets are slower than this set, letting Tera Ghost potentially ruin a revenge kill attempt.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

On RegenVest sets, Psychic can be used instead of Psychic Noise for a chance to 2HKO Iron Moth but is generally less useful due to the latter's denial of HP recovery. Hydro Pump can also be considered for more immediate damage on RegenVest sets in place of Energy Ball or Surf. Primarina does have a few niche sets, mainly a physically defensive set with the Stamina ability and Leftovers. This set aims to rack up stat boosts through its ability and the move Calm Mind to sweep with the move Stored Power.

Checks and Counters

Electric Types: Electric-types like Zapdos and Sandy Shocks force out Primarina with their strong attacks, often 2HKOing RegenVest sets and OHKOing offensive Primarina.

Desolate Land Users: Desolate Land users such as Heatran and Moltres can deny Primarina's Flip Turn and take all of Primarina's attacks relatively easily.

Grass-Types: Primarina is threatened by several Grass-types that are staples on teams in the tier. On the physical side, it is threatened by Power Whip from the Ogerpon formes and Flower Trick from Sword of Ruin Meowscarada. On the special side, Sinistcha threatens Primarina with Matcha Gotcha and can often KO it after a Calm Mind boost.

Choice Specs.description:
Primarina is one of the strongest special wallbreakers in the tier, with an excellent typing that gives it opportunities to switch in and spam its powerful and reliable STAB moves. Primordial Sea boosts Weather Ball and lets Primarina check Desolate Land users such as Moltres, non-Discharge Iron Moth, and non-Gunk Shot Cinderace. However, these same threats are also great checks to Primarina if they negate Primordial Sea, so Psychic is helpful as the strongest option against them, particularly Iron Moth, while Psychic Noise is a weaker alternative that prevents recovery moves from Moltres and Iron Moth. Flip Turn lets Primarina pivot on special walls such as Manaphy and Bulletproof Iron Treads, generating momentum for its team.

Primarina fits well on balance and bulky offense teams, where its mix of defensive utility and offensive pressure is put to good use. It resists the STAB moves of many common Choice item wallbreakers such as Chien-Pao and Zamazenta, though it still needs backup from physical walls like Corviknight and Pecharunt, especially against the Ogerpon formes. Great Tusk and Corviknight can also provide entry hazard removal, letting Primarina stay healthy so it can threaten out the aforementioned Choice Band wallbreakers. Faster special attackers such as Zapdos, Latios, and Deoxys-S are also problematic, so special walls such as Iron Treads and Swampert are good teammates. In exchange, Primarina can deter Fire-type moves that threaten Corviknight and Iron Treads. Primarina struggles against special walls like Manaphy and the aforementioned Desolate Land users, especially specially defensive Moltres, so it appreciates physical attackers like the Ogerpon formes and Roaring Moon.

RegenVest.description:
An excellent type combination, good natural bulk and access to Flip Turn allow Primarina to function as a solid RegenVest user . Psychic Noise hits Desolate Land Iron Moth and Moltres for a good chunk of damage and denies recovery as well. Energy Ball is useful against Swampert, Manaphy, and opposing Primarina. This moveslot may also be swapped for Surf or Hydro Pump to provide a second powerful STAB option for more reliable neutral damage against Corviknight and Skarmory. This set runs a Speed-reducing nature and 0 Speed IVs to ensure that Primarina is the slowest Pokemon on the field and can safely pivot to bring in teammates using Flip Turn.

RegenVest Primarina performs well as a bulky pivot on offensive archetypes due to its excellent mixed defensive profile, checking tier staples both on the physical and special side. Although it cannot learn Knock Off, unlike other RegenVest Water types, Primarina is able to counter the likes of Roaring Moon, Chien-Pao, Great Tusk, and Zamazenta with its Fairy typing, as well as handling specially offensive threats such as Gholdengo and Latios quite well. This set must be wary of potential Knock Off users as its ability to take special hits is crippled if it loses its Assault Vest. Therefore, Primarina appreciates support from teammates like Great Tusk and Corviknight to absorb Knock Off; they can also aid Primarina with entry hazard removal. Strong Electric-type attackers like offensive Iron Hands, Zapdos, and Sandy Shocks can pressure and break through Primarina, so it could use Electric-immune teammates like Great Tusk, Iron Treads and Volt Absorb Corviknight. Desolate Land users such as Heatran or Moltres can deny Primarina Flip Turn pivots and immediately threaten it with Solar Beam. Primordial Sea Zapdos or Well-Baked Body Gholdengo can switch into these threats and give Primarina safe entry.

nfe.comments:
Other Options

RestTalk Charjabug can serve as a consistent defensive resource at the cost of utility or coverage. For its fourth move, Lunge beats even Choice Band Piloswine, while Volt Switch is great for preserving momentum.

Checks and Counters

Entry Hazards: Because it is weak to Stealth Rock and affected by Spikes / Toxic Spikes, Charjabug's defensive utility is effectively negated by entry hazards. Charjabug also gives common setters like Glimmet and Tinkatuff free opportunities to set up entry hazards.

Fire-Type Attackers: While Charjabug's impressive bulk allows it to survive most Fire-type attacks from full, it still does not appreciate taking hits from prominent Fire-type Pokemon such as Monferno, Raboot, and Pignite.

Hattrem: Magic Bounce deters Sticky Web from ever being used, and Hattrem's physical bulk means that it doesn't mind switching in on even Charjabug's STAB Bug-type attacks.

Sticky Web.description:
Charjabug is the tier's premier Sticky Web setter thanks to its great bulk, solid typing, and access to secondary tools that make it much more than a suicide lead. It has utility moves in Thunder Wave, Lunge, and Skitter Smack, which make it difficult to set up on, while Volt Switch enables Charjabug to generate and conserve momentum. With its natural bulk, Charjabug checks and threatens prominent Grass- and Water-types including Thwackey and Quaxwell. This also means that Charjabug can often set up Sticky Web multiple times in a game.

Charjabug operates best on offensive structures, paired with offensive powerhouses that can take advantage of Sticky Web such as Pignite, Girafarig, and Fraxure. It also appreciates Ghost-types like Drakloak, which can block Rapid Spin. Charjabug struggles against opposing Fire-types such as Pignite and Monferno. Fire-resistant Pokemon like Wartortle and Gabite therefore make for great teammates. Finally, Magic Bounce makes Hattrem a huge problem for Charjabug, and RestTalk variants outlast its Bug-type attacks. Charjabug therefore appreciates Dark-types that can switch in on and punish Hattrem such as Krokorok and Scraggy.

zu.overview: Vikavolt distinguishes itself as a powerful Sticky Web setter, pressuring Hattrem and entry hazard removers like Sandslash and Lurantis with its STAB and coverage moves. Levitate and a Bug / Electric typing make Vikavolt a surprisingly good tank against common Grass-types like Arboliva, Venusaur, and Virizion. Vikavolt's offensive typing, powerful special attacks, and coverage even let it deter opposing hazard setters like Mesprit, Sandslash, and Orthworm. What's more, Vikavolt's special wallbreaking potential enables it to capitalize on its own Sticky Web. However, Vikavolt's poor Speed is a major hindrance, leaving it easily outsped and picked off once it's weakened. Taunt leads like Froslass and Primeape can prevent Vikavolt from setting up Sticky Web and get their own hazards up. Fire-types like Charizard and Typhlosion are major specially offensive threats that take advantage of Vikavolt's lower special bulk and lack of recovery. Special walls like Muk and Cryogonal can withstand Vikavolt's strong attacks, and the latter can even remove Sticky Web with Rapid Spin. Beyond Sticky Web, Vikavolt tends to compete with other Electric-types like Jolteon, Magneton, and Rotom, which offer more Speed, utility, and defensive value, respectively.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Tera Electric leaves Vikavolt free of weaknesses and powers up Vikavolt's STAB Electric-type attacks, but it doesn't offer as much defensive utility as the resistances and immunities of Tera types like Ghost and Steel. Tera Dragon helps Vikavolt catch Fire-types like Charizard off guard, and it even improves Vikavolt's matchups against Water-types like Poliwrath while retaining Vikavolt's Grass and Electric resistances. Vikavolt can aim to be a sweeper with Agility and Throat Spray, but it requires multiple turns of setup to be threatening compared to setup sweepers like Minior, Jolteon, and Mesprit. Vikavolt's poor Speed, both before and after Agility, is also a major hindrance to it as a sweeper.

Checks and Counters

Special Walls: Muk and Magneton can tank Vikavolt's attacks, while Cryogonal can remove Vikavolt's Sticky Web.

Fire-types: Charizard, Houndoom, and Typhlosion melt Vikavolt with their Fire-type STAB moves, though they don't switch into its Electric-type attacks safely.

Faster Attackers: Fast wallbreakers like Sneasel and Hisuian Sneasel pressure Vikavolt and can pick it off with just a bit of prior damage. Even attackers with middling Speed like Alolan Exeggutor, Clawitzer, and Hitmontop can blow past Vikavolt.

Sticky Web Lead.description:
Vikavolt is a threatening Sticky Web lead thanks to its offensive typing and massive Special Attack. Volt Switch enables Vikavolt to bring a partner in safely once it's set Sticky Web, and Vikavolt's low Speed makes it more likely that it can bring its teammates in without forcing them to take a hit. Volt Switch also helps break the Focus Sash of a Taunt lead like Primeape or Froslass so one of Vikavolt's teammates can come in and dispose of them. Thunderbolt's advantage over Volt Switch is that it doesn't force Vikavolt to switch out against Pokemon it wants to threaten, such as Primeape, Articuno, and Clawitzer. Energy Ball covers Electric-immune Pokemon like Sandslash, and it nails Regirock. Vikavolt can opt for Thunderbolt over Energy Ball so that it doesn't have to choose between a pivot move and a reliable Electric-type STAB move across matchups against foes like Orthworm, Muk, and Weezing. Additionally, Vikavolt's STAB moves already hit most of the metagame for neutral damage. Tera Ghost turns Vikavolt into a spinblocker, ensuring its Sticky Web stays up against spinners like Sandslash, Cryogonal, and Hitmontop. Alternatively, Tera Steel has defensive synergy with Levitate, makes Vikavolt a good check to Psychic- and Fairy-types like Mesprit and Whimsicott, and turns the tables on Regirock for a key turn. Focus Sash makes Vikavolt a dedicated lead, while Heavy-Duty Boots makes Vikavolt more flexible throughout the game as a Sticky Web setter and pivot.

Vikavolt can feature on hyper offense teams thanks to Sticky Web, but it's a good fit for offense and bulky offense teams as well due to the speed control Sticky Web offers. Wallbreakers like Clawitzer, Charizard, and Arboliva thrive with Sticky Web up, and they also benefit from being brought in safely by Vikavolt's Volt Switch. Setup sweepers with middling Speed like Mesprit and Charizard also benefit from the ability to outspeed more threats. Knock Off users like Primeape, Mesprit, and Sandslash help ensure Heavy-Duty Boots is removed from all foes so that the entire opposing team is subjected to Sticky Web, and the item removal support they offer helps against checks to Vikavolt like Muk and Cryogonal. Ghost-types like Spiritomb and Froslass act as spinblockers to keep up Vikavolt's Sticky Web, while Defiant Pokemon, such as Primeape and Primeape, can deter and punish Defoggers. Spinners like Hitmontop, Cryogonal, and Sandslash help keep opposing entry hazards off the field without removing Vikavolt's Sticky Web. Vikavolt's poor matchups against Fire-types make teammates like Regirock and Muk vital.

Sticky Web Pivot.description:
Vikavolt is an effective wallbreaker, pivot, and Sticky Web setter because of its unique typing and monstrous Special Attack. Energy Ball hits foes like Sandslash and Regirock especially hard; if Vikavolt is using a Modest nature, it consistently 2HKOes Regirock. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Vikavolt to function as a bulky slow pivot more reliably. A Bold nature with full Defense investment can be used to let Vikavolt better take attacks from physical attackers like Primeape, Hitmontop, and Virizion; alternatively, a Modest nature with full Special Attack investment can maximize its damage output at the cost of taking on opposing leads less effectively. Tera Steel is used to provide a resistance to Psychic, which helps it take on Mesprit after it Terastallizes, and flip its weakness to Rock into a resistance, taking Rock Blast and Stone Edge from foes like Regirock and Virizion more comfortably.

Vikavolt, despite being a Sticky Web setter, is a good fit for bulky offense and offensive structures alike. With its good natural bulk and massive power even without EV investment, Vikavolt can reliably come in and pivot a few times each game, using its wallbreaking proficiency to lure in foes like Muk for teammates like Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel. Similarly, setup sweepers like Poliwrath and Mesprit can overcome their relative slowness with Sticky Web support, threatening to clean late-game after one boost. Stealth Rock setters like Regirock pair well with Vikavolt, with the former taking on foes like Sneasel reliably and the latter taking on Fire-types like Charizard and Typhlosion. Vikavolt is a notable VoltTurn partner for Clawitzer and Primeape, as they can lure in Arboliva and Mesprit for it, while it can provide entry points for them against walls like Muk and Muk. Defog deterrents, like Malamar and Primeape, make for excellent teammates, leveraging the Sticky Web set by Vikavolt to become devastating wallbreakers if positioned well. Knock Off users that can aid further in this endeavor, like Primeape and Sneasel also help soften up Vikavolt checks such as Muk.

Bulk Up.description: Crabrawler is a fantastic bulky attacker that checks dangerous threats such as Hisuian Growlithe and Toedscool, and can sweep teams with Bulk Up. Coverage moves such as Ice Punch, Thunder Punch, and Earthquake offer Crabrawler extreme flexibility in the threats it needs to cover. Ice Punch hits Foongus, Wattrel, and Toedscool, while Thunder Punch hits Mareanie, Wingull, and Quaxly; both options also hit Drifloon super effectively. Earthquake allows Crabrawler to hit Mareanie and Fuecoco and is its strongest neutral option against Hisuian Zorua. Tera Fire makes Crabrawler immune to burns, while Tera Electric makes Thunder Punch stronger against Water-types and gives it defensive utility against threats like Hisuian Voltorb and Wingull. Crabrawler hates dealing with opposing Ghost-types such as Hisuian Zorua, Greavard, and Drifloon, as well as Gothita. Hisuian Growlithe checks these threats and makes an excellent teammate for Crabrawler, as do Ghost-types such as Hisuian Zorua and Drifloon that benefit from the removal of opposing Pawniard.

Bulky Quiver Dance Sweeper.description: 44 Speed EVs ensure that Oricorio will outpace Kilowattrel after a Quiver Dance.

ru.overview: Ribombee flutters its way into RU as a powerful Sticky Web setter that can use its access to Stun Spore to hinder foes that threaten to clear its Sticky Web, Cyclizar and Maushold. Ribombee's ability to outspeed Pokemon such as Cyclizar, Noivern, and Maushold is invaluable, as it can threaten them with either Moonblast or Stun Spore, which cripples them immensely. It is able to leverage its high Speed in order to reliably get up Sticky Web, which can support slow wallbreakers such as Gallade, Toxtricity, and Feraligatr in order to sweep effectively. Ribombee can also utilize a wide variety of support moves in order to cripple the opposing team such as Trick and Stun Spore, which is incredibly useful due to its ability to outspeed Pokemon such as Noivern, Maushold and Gengar. Ribombee is mainly held back by its inability to damage Steel-types like Registeel and Empoleon and reliance on Sticky Web.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Quiver Dance can make Ribombee much more threatening, as not only can it allow it to outspeed every Choice Scarf user, it can also be kept around until late game once Steel-types such as Registeel and Empoleon have been dealt with to clean up a team. Choice Specs is an option alongside Trick in order to cripple foes such as Registeel and Empoleon while dealing impressive damage against neutral targets.

Checks and Counters

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Registeel and Jirachi can easily take Ribombee's attacks.

Defiant and Competitive Pokemon: Pokemon with the Defiant or Competitive ability, such as Bisharp and Empoleon, are major annoyances for Ribombee and its team, as they can use Sticky Web Speed drop in order to boost and start dealing large damage. Bisharp in particular is incredibly threatening, as its access to Sucker Punch means it can bypass the Speed drop from Sticky Web.

Sticky Web.description:
Set Details

Ribombee is an effective Sticky Web lead, enabling slower setup sweepers such as Toxtricity, Gallade, and Feraligatr. Stun Spore can cripple foes that want to set up against Ribombee, such as Bisharp and Kleavor. Psychic Noise deals with Poison-types such as Amoonguss very effectively while also making sure that Ribombee cannot be used as setup fodder by bulky Pokemon such as Calm Mind Reuniclus and Calm Mind Slowbro. Focus Sash ensures Ribombee can get off Sticky Web and lets it have a chance to use a second move in order to further cripple the foe. Shield Dust ensures that Ribombee isn't affected by the secondary effects of moves such as Iron Head from Choice Scarf Jirachi in order to reliably get up Sticky Web. Tera Ghost allows Ribombee to act as a temporary spinblocker if needed against Cyclizar and Forretress.

Ribombee fits best on hyper offense teams, where it can lead off games in order to get off Sticky Webs. Ghost-type partners such as Basculegion-F and Mimikyu pair well with Ribombee, as they can spinblock for it and stop Sticky Web from being removed. Defiant Bisharp pairs well with Ribombee, as it can punish Defog attempts from Noivern. Slow, strong wallbreakers such as Gallade, Toxtricity, and Breloom love Ribombee's Sticky Web, as they can use it to outspeed faster foes they might otherwise struggle with such as Maushold and Krookodile.

Ribombee carves a niche for itself as a consistent suicide lead and the tier's most reliable Sticky Web setter due to its excellent Speed tier and strong STAB Moonblast to punish Great Tusk. Sticky Web cripples opposing hyper offense, as the archetype tends to rely heavily on various sweepers' Speed stats to function effectively. Sticky Web is also extremely disruptive against fast Paradox Pokemon aiming to get a Speed boost from their ability like Booster Energy Iron Valiant and Iron Moth as well as Walking Wake on sun teams. Stun Spore, though inaccurate, can cripple faster threats like Darkrai and Ribombee to set up Sticky Web the next turn. Skill Swap allows Ribombee to steal Hatterene's Magic Bounce and set up Sticky Web against it, and it can also remove Gliscor's Poison Heal and force it to switch out. Psychic Noise, alternatively, threatens Glimmora while having the added utility of neutralizing recovery attempts from walls like Clodsire and Blissey, which are generally unafraid of Sticky Web. More importantly, however, Psychic Noise threatens Substitute Iron Moth, which otherwise has an extremely lopsided matchup against Sticky Web teams featuring Ribombee by virtue of being able to set up a Substitute for free against it and fish for two Fiery Dance boosts against it thereafter, possibly winning the game on the spot. Shield Dust is a wonderful ability that blocks secondary effects from moves like Galarian Slowking and Darkrai's Sludge Bomb and Moltres's Flamethrower, consistently giving Ribombee a minimum of two turns to both set Sticky Web and either attack or paralyze a threat with Stun Spore to force more long-term progress before fainting. Tera Ghost is preferred to allow Ribombee to block Rapid Spin from threats like Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Excadrill, ensuring that Sticky Web remains active; however, Tera Steel is a perfectly fine alternative that allows Ribombee to block Glimmora's Mortal Spin while occasionally giving it some added longevity against threats like Iron Crown and Galarian Slowking.

Ribombee is the cornerstone of Sticky Web offense, and as such its best teammates tend to be powerful offensive threats that can best capitalize on the entry hazard's Speed control. Gholdengo is a nearly mandatory teammate, since its typing and Good as Gold collectively neutralize all of Rapid Spin, Mortal Spin, and Defog and ensure that Sticky Web remains active throughout the game. Gholdengo's high damage output and access to Nasty Plot let it threaten defensive teams that do not care as much about Sticky Web, while its middling Speed tier is circumvented by Sticky Web to the point that it can now reliably outspeed Great Tusk and Ogerpon-W, making it a prime beneficiary of the entry hazard. Iron Moth is an excellent teammate; with Sticky Web support it can opt to forego its standard speed Booster Energy spread of 124 Def / 132 SpA / 252 Spe in favor of a harder-hitting EV spread of 4 Def / 252 SpA / 252 Spe amplified further by a Special Attack boost from Booster Energy and a Modest nature. A set like this not only lets Iron Moth greatly threaten Cinderace with its powerful Sludge Wave but also effectively utilizes Tera Ghost to spinblock in a pinch, which is an especially useful trait given that it naturally absorbs Toxic Spikes. Swords Dance Ogerpon-W is another excellent abuser of Sticky Web; it naturally boasts an excellent matchup against bulkier teams and greatly appreciates Sticky Web support to circumvent its less-consistent matchups against fast threats like Darkrai and fast Booster Energy users like Iron Moth and Iron Valiant and get the jump on opposing Ogerpon-W that would otherwise Speed tie with it. Raging Bolt is also a useful teammate, as it naturally has great bulk and a massive damage output; its Speed is decent enough to take great advantage of Sticky Web, but it can still function effectively should Ribombee's Sticky Web be removed thanks to Thunderclap's ability to threaten fast threats like Zamazenta, Darkrai, Iron Valiant, and Deoxys-S. Meteor Beam Glimmora is a premiere abuser of Sticky Web, as it can forego Rock Polish in favor of Dazzling Gleam's coverage or Power Gem's consistency, and it hits incredibly hard after a Meteor Beam boost, obliterating Cinderace seeking to use Court Change and punishing any of its attempts to attack Glimmora directly thanks to Toxic Debris. Low Kick Kingambit and Roar Zamazenta are excellent teammates that appreciate Sticky Web support, in part because the hazard can provide them with crucial Speed advantages in mirror matches. Bulk Up Great Tusk can fulfill many roles for Sticky Web teams, both by providing Rapid Spin support and by being a setup sweeper that can snowball late-game that still provides valuable defensive utility by virtue of resisting Kingambit's Sucker Punch, being immune to Raging Bolt's Thunderclap, and being naturally bulky enough to withstand Dragonite's Extreme Speed if needed. Hisuian Samurott is a solid teammate; its Ceaseless Edge allows it to set Spikes, which are otherwise incredibly difficult to fit on Sticky Web teams, and its Knock Off is very threatening against offensive Heavy-Duty Boots users like Weavile, Ogerpon, and various Darkrai and Great Tusk sets that otherwise match up favorably against Sticky Web teams. Lastly, Serperior and Choice Specs Enamorus are good Sticky Web sweepers that can quickly snowball out of control. Both appreciate being faster than the likes of Deoxys-S and Booster Energy Iron Valiant and greatly punish Defog with Contrary; Serperior takes advantage of opposing Sticky Web with Contrary, while Enamorus can also outspeed Ogerpon-W after Sticky Web and rip through teams with its powerful Moonblast.

Ribombee is the fastest Sticky Web setter in the tier, able to outspeed other leads like Mew to ensure that Sticky Web will go up before Mew can use Taunt. Stun Spore allows Ribombee to paralyze faster threats like Speed Booster Energy Iron Moth and Choice Scarf Enamorus while also ruining setup sweepers that may use it as setup fodder. Tailwind is a great option for Ribombee if it will be immediately KOed after setting Sticky Web, as it allows most partners to outspeed the entire metagame after Sticky Web. U-turn is another option that can scout for switches and create setup opportunities for teammates. While niche, Shield Dust is more relevant than any of Ribombee's other abilities, allowing it to avoid being inflicted with poison or burn from moves like Sludge Bomb and Flare Blitz, giving it another turn to use Stun Spore or Tailwind. Focus Sash allows Ribombee to survive any hit from a faster attacker to ensure Sticky Web goes up. Ribombee works only as a lead on Sticky Web offense teams. Teammates like Mienshao appreciate Sticky Web, as it allows them to outspeed and OHKO threats like Keldeo before they get a chance to retaliate. Defiant users like Bisharp are also useful to punish attempts to use Defog to remove Sticky Web. Ribombee struggles to set entry hazards against Excadrill and Mega Aerodactyl due to Rapid Spin and Dual Wingbeat respectively, so checks to these threats like Celesteela are appreciated. Air Balloon Aegislash is recommended with Ribombee as well, as it can help prevent Excadrill from using Rapid Spin to clear Sticky Web. The turn Ribombee uses to set Sticky Web can be exploited by threats like Swords Dance Scizor and Aegislash, so offensive partners that can handle these threats like Victini and Bisharp are recommended to prevent these threats from sweeping.

Sticky Web Lead.description:
• Ribombee sets itself apart from other Sticky Web leads thanks to its excellent matchup against all Sticky Web leads. In addition to this, Ribombee has a valuable Speed tier and great ability in Shield Dust. Its Speed tier allows it to outspeed common Taunt users such as Arceus formes and Yveltal. Thanks to Shield Dust, Ribombee can stay in against Smeargle to serve as a status absorber for teammates. However, since Ribombee is unable to deny entry hazards from Deoxys-S and Glimmora leads, it is a niche anti-Sticky Web lead on hyper offense teams.

  • Imprison allows Ribombee to prevent leads such as Smeargle and Shuckle from setting Sticky Web. Skill Swap allows Ribombee to bypass Magic Bounce from Mega Diancie in order to set Sticky Web. In addition, it also provides utility in stealing Primordial Sea and Desolate Land from Primal Kyogre and Primal Groudon, respectively, allowing teammates such as Zacian-C to tank an Origin Pulse and Yveltal to take Heat Crash better.

  • Stun Spore is a nuisance for the majority of the tier such as Arceus formes, Yveltal, and Ho-Oh due to Ribombee's Speed tier. It is especially valuable against Ho-Oh, as it prevents Ho-Oh from freely Defogging. In addition, Stun Spore cripples threats such as Zacian-C and Eternatus, preventing them from using Ribombee to easily set up. Moonblast is an option to allow Ribombee to KO Smeargle without risking status for a switch-in. In addition, Moonblast directly threatens Yveltal, Giratina-O, and Dragon Dance Zygarde.

  • The given EV spread is for Moonblast sets and allows Ribombee to outspeed all base 120s while maximizing Moonblast damage. For example, it can always 2HKO physical Giratina-O. The secondary EV spread allows Ribombee to avoid an OHKO from Pheromosa's Triple Axel, and minimizes the odds from being OHKOed after Terastallizing from +1 Kyurem-B's Icicle Spear.

  • Tera Steel allows Ribombee to block Mortal Spin from Smeargle and Glimmora in order to maintain Sticky Web. However, since the use cases are rare, Ribombee should not usually Terastallize. It is also wise to wait for Smeargle to reveal Mortal Spin before Terastallizing, as sets carrying Rapid Spin will cause Ribombee to waste the Terastallization.

  • Ribombee is an excellent anti-Sticky Web choice thanks to its excellent matchup against Smeargle and Shuckle. However, its lead matchups against threats such as Mega Diancie, Deoxys-S, and Glimmora are more challenging. If Ribombee has a bad lead matchup, such as against Deoxys-S or Grimmsnarl, it can wait to set Sticky Web later thanks to its excellent Speed tier. Ribombee can also be preserved if it survives after setting Sticky Web. This is useful so that it can serve as a sack to bring a teammate in or used to revenge kill threats such as Yveltal.

  • Pokemon that appreciate Sticky Web support such as Zacian-C, wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, specially offensive Yveltal, and Chi-Yu are excellent teammates. Zacian-C can easily run through bulkier offense teams and appreciates the ability to outspeed opposing Zacian-Cs. Primal Kyogre is able to greatly threaten Arceus formes and Eternatus thanks to Sticky Web support. Specially offensive Yveltal appreciates being able to outspeed checks such as Zacian-C and Arceus formes. In return, Yveltal provides devastating breaking power and an unmatched ability to keep Sticky Web. Chi-Yu greatly gains from Sticky Web support slowing down checks such as Arceus-Dark and -Fairy. In exchange, Chi-Yu provides the most devastating wallbreaking power in the tier and greatly aids the matchup versus stall teams. Extreme Killer Arceus and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground are both excellent teammates for Ribombee. Arceus is able to blow through walls such as Primal Groudon and Zygarde with Double Edge while soft-checking Marshadow with Sticky Web support. Arceus-Ground is an excellent answer to Zacian-C and Double Dance Primal Groudon, which can easily threaten to reverse sweep; in addition, it also threatens Ho-Oh.

  • Due to Ribombee's inability to deny entry hazards, Pokemon that are weak to Stealth Rock such as Chi-Yu and Mega Salamence should be picked sparingly as teammates. The exception to this is Yveltal, as its ability to keep Sticky Web up is too valuable. Eternatus is extremely valuable as a teammate due to its ability to absorb Toxic Spikes, as they can cripple hyper offense teammates such as Arceus, Primal Groudon, and Primal Kyogre. Extreme Killer Arceus can easily set up on Ribombee, so Marshadow and Zacian-C are appreciated in order to check it. Although Ribombee can annoy Ho-Oh with Stun Spore, it cannot prevent Ho-Oh from Defogging, so Pokemon that threaten Ho-Oh out such as Meteor Beam Eternatus or can Taunt it such as Tera Fire specifically offensive Yveltal are appreciated.

Sticky Web Lead (Bug).description: Ribombee is the fastest Sticky Web setter in the metagame making it a great lead option on Bug teams. With its unique secondary Fairy typing Ribombee can take on Dark- and Dragon-type threats like Mega Latios, Kommo-o, and Greninja with Moonblast, as well as anti-lead the two prominent Magic Bounce users in Mega Diancie and Mega Sableye. Stun Spore is a useful option for punishing opposing leads and ruining fast threats to Bug teams such as Cinderace, Tornadus-T, and Volcarona while also crippling faster Pokemon like Choice Scarf Iron Boulder and Blacephalon in a pinch thanks to Focus Sash. Alternatively, Psychic Noise is an option that respectably damages Poison-types such as Toxapex and Clodsire and prevents recovery from walls like Blissey and Skarmory, making them easier to bypass. U-turn allows Ribombee to keep momentum up after setting Sticky Web, letting it pivot into its more offensive teammates. Ribombee's excellent 124 Speed allows it to outrun Choice Scarf users such as Meowscarada and Roaring Moon under Sticky Web, giving it good value as a revenge killer. Volcarona is a great partner for Ribombee, benefitting greatly from the speed control it provides to outspeed threats like Regieleki and Mega Swampert under rain after a single Quiver Dance. In return, Volcarona melts Steel-types like Skarmory and Ferrothorn that Ribombee struggles against. Similarly, Choice Scarf Kleavor becomes faster than most grounded targets affected by Sticky Web and slices through Fire-types like Iron Moth and Blacephalon with Stone Axe. Physical wallbreakers like Scizor, Mega Scizor, and Mega Pinsir demolish special tanks like Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra that Ribombee struggles with while also having an easier time sweeping teams with Sticky Web support.

Sticky Web.description:
Ribombee's ability to set up Sticky Web facilitates a whole host of strong attackers that may struggle to outspeed fast Pokemon, and its high Speed allows it to set up the entry hazard in the face of common Taunt users. Moonblast is the preferred attacking move to hit common lead Pokemon like Zamazenta and Hisuian Samurott, as well as deterring Great Tusk from using Rapid Spin to clear Sticky Web. Skill Swap allows Ribombee to potentially bypass Magic Bounce from Hatterene and Mega Diancie and set up Sticky Web. Stun Spore allows Ribombee to hinder faster Pokemon, especially those unaffected by Sticky Web, such as Dragonite, Choice Scarf Landorus-T, and Tornadus-T. Ribombee tends to use Stun Spore before Sticky Web, as paralyzing Pokemon has a large payoff at times despite the chance of Stun Spore missing. Focus Sash grants Ribombee a guaranteed turn to set up Sticky Web. 192 Defense EVs guarantee Ribombee to survive Choice Scarf Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes, one of the few Pokemon that outspeed Ribombee and bypass Focus Sash. Shield Dust has various niche uses, such as preventing Mega Lopunny's Fake Out from flinching, which would otherwise deny Sticky Web.

Ribombee fits on hyper offense teams built around Sticky Web. Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Tapu Lele, and Raging Bolt set up easily with Swords Dance or Calm Mind, and their decent Speed tiers are elevated thanks to Sticky Web. Ogerpon-W in particular fits well due to its ability to counter rain teams, as Pokemon like Swift Swim Barraskewda and Mega Swampert are largely unaffected by Sticky Web in rain. Raging Bolt also acts as a great counter to Flying-type threats, resisting the STAB moves of Tornadus-T, Zapdos, and Mega Charizard Y, which are problematic Pokemon due to them not being hindered by Sticky Web. In the same vein, teammates that can handle Levitate Pokemon are appreciated; because Mega Latios is the only common one, partners like Tapu Lele, Weavile, and Gholdengo do the job well. Gholdengo is an especially great teammate, as it denies most entry hazard removal, such as Defog from Corviknight and Zapdos and Rapid Spin from Terapagos and Great Tusk. Gholdengo also poses an immense threat itself thanks to Nasty Plot, threatening Pokemon such as Heavy-Duty Boots Zamazenta, Corviknight, and Ferrothorn. Ceruledge can also be used to deny hazard removal, matching up better against Terapagos; however, it only blocks Rapid Spin and not Defog, notably worsening the matchup against Defoggers like Zapdos, Moltres, and defensive Tornadus-T, which can use Defog with relative safety. Teammates like Booster Energy Speed Great Tusk and Scale Shot Garchomp can threaten Heavy-Duty Boots Cinderace, denying it from being able to use Court Change. Even if Cinderace does pull off Court Change, Serperior acts as a great teammate to gain a Speed boost from Sticky Web while also punishing Defog attempts. Finally, in the case that Sticky Web gets removed, teammates that function well outside of Sticky Web are also appreciated. Volcarona, Mega Charizard X, and Booster Energy Speed Iron Valiant all pack great Speed tiers and can often win games without Sticky Web due to their ability to boost their Speed. Great Tusk is also a great teammate for Ribombee and the Sticky Web archetype, as it can remove entry hazards that can be greatly detrimental to its teammates' health, greatly benefiting sweepers such as Mega Charizard X, Tornadus-T, and Weavile.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Bug

Ribombee can also run a dual screens + Light Clay set to further facilitate its team's setup attempts, dropping Stun Spore and Quiver Dance; however, the loss of Focus Sash is notable and getting both Reflect and Light Screen up at times can be difficult due to Ribombee's very lacking bulk. Skill Swap can be used over Quiver Dance in order to force Gliscor out by removing its Poison Heal, since Gliscor is a major problem for Bug teams.

Sticky Web Lead (Bug).description:
Ribombee is the premier Sticky Web setter for Bug teams thanks to its high Speed, access to further utility in Stun Spore, and Shield Dust letting it always get Sticky Web up against threats such as Choice Scarf Sneasler without worrying about status conditions. Moonblast allows Ribombee to hit Dark- and Fighting-types such as Darkrai and Great Tusk, which can either outspeed Ribombee or remove Sticky Web thanks to Rapid Spin. Stun Spore allows Ribombee to annoy threats such as Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Heatran, letting its teammates outspeed and remove said foes later on in the game. Quiver Dance allows Ribombee to exert pressure throughout a game while potentially turning it into a win condition in the Dragon and Fighting matchups if it is not needed as a lead. Focus Sash lets Ribombee get Sticky Web up as a lead without having to fear being OHKOed due to its poor bulk.

Choice Scarf Kleavor is an excellent teammate for Ribombee, as it appreciates being able to outspeed nearly everything in the metagame under Sticky Web, including opposing Choice Scarf users such as Roaring Moon and Meowscarada. It also appreciates Ribombee hitting Fighting-types, such as Iron Hands and Iron Valiant, with Moonblast, allowing it to spam Stone Axe late-game to clean up weakened teams. In return, Kleavor threatens Fire-types like Moltres that Bug teams struggle to break through. It also compounds with Ribombee's entry hazard pressure thanks to Stone Axe setting Stealth Rock. Swords Dance Scizor is another good teammate for Ribombee, as it appreciates being able to hit normally-faster threats that don't mind Bullet Punch, like Heatran and Urshifu-R, hard thanks to Sticky Web not forcing it to rely on Bullet Punch for damage. In compensation, Scizor uses its Poison immunity to come in on threats such as Choice Scarf Sneasler that would otherwise threaten Ribombee and use them as a setup opportunity. It also removes Hatterene, which is invaluable to let Ribombee set up Sticky Web. Slither Wing is another great teammate, as it removes common Steel-types such as Hisuian Goodra and Empoleon that Ribombee wouldn't be able to do much against. Volcarona benefits greatly from Sticky Web, as after one Quiver Dance, it outspeeds Choice Scarf users that would otherwise attempt to revenge kill it, such as Roaring Moon and Urshifu-R. Ribombee, in turn, appreciates the fact that Volcarona can switch in on threats such as Gholdengo and stay healthy while being able to hit Steel-types with a strong Fiery Dance. Lokix can clean teams weakened by Ribombee thanks to its strong U-turn and First Impression while hitting Ghost-types such as Skeledirge and Gholdengo that pose large roadblocks for Bug teams and amplifying the effects of Sticky Web with Knock Off. In exchange, Lokix appreciates being able to outspeed common threats such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane under Sticky Web. Heracross can, in a similar vein to Slither Wing, deal with Steel-types such as Heatran and Bisharp while also using Knock Off to both remove key items from defensive behemoths such as Toxapex and increase the effects of Sticky Web on the opposing team. It appreciates Sticky Web to patch up its lackluster Speed. Finally, Frosmoth is another Quiver Dance user that has massive special bulk thanks to Ice Scales that also appreciates Sticky Web patching up its low Speed. Forretress can keep hazards off of the field to enhance Ribombee's late-game sweeping potential and preserve its Focus Sash while being able to set hazards itself and take on threats such as Bisharp with Body Press. It also, similarly to Kleavor, can add to the hazard pressure by setting Spikes.

Sticky Web Lead (Any).description:
Ribombee finds its place as a consistent Sticky Web setter with a solid Speed tier and STAB Moonblast to deter Great Tusk, the tier's best entry hazard remover. Sticky Web disrupts frailer offensive Pokemon as well as Speed Booster Energy Pokemon like Iron Hands and Iron Moth. Moonblast nails the aforementioned Great Tusk and Iron Hands while also acting as a consistent damage source. Psychic Noise hits Poison-types such as Pecharunt and Iron Moth but more importantly denies recovery from Pokemon like Rest Dondozo and Recover Clodsire. Stun Spore slows down and cripples foes including Flying-types and Pokemon holding Heavy-Duty Boots, which ignores Sticky Web Speed drops. On the other hand, Skill Swap allows Ribombee to set up Sticky Web on Hatterene as well as temporarily remove important abilities such as Regenerator. Shield Dust allows Ribombee to avoid secondary effects such as Salt Cure from Garganacl and Malignant Chain from Pecharunt, which, combined with Focus Sash, nearly always guarantees it two turns on the field to set up Sticky Web, do damage with Moonblast or Psychic Noise, or paralyze a foe. While Ribombee should rarely Terastallize, Tera Ghost allows it to spinblock Pokemon like Iron Treads in a pinch.

Ribombee should typically be placed in a dump slot that no teammate really wants. Although it appreciates a donation of high Special Attack from gods like Kyurem-W, it is often better to grant that damage increase to other wallbreakers or sweepers on the team. Wallbreakers with mediocre Speed such as Kyurem-W, Manaphy, Hoopa-U, and Urshifu-S are all beneficiaries of Ribombee's Sticky Web, with the latter three allowing them to be utilized in non-Speed slots while maintaining their ability to attack first. Sticky Web also lets faster wallbreakers such as Iron Moth, Zamazenta, Roaring Moon, and Ogerpon-W to forgo a Speed-boosting nature for increased damage. Roaring Moon and Ogerpon-W are especially useful, as they offer strong Knock Offs to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from faster threats such as Iron Treads, Hisuian Electrode, and Eternatus, allowing Ribombee's slower teammates to overwhelm them. Since Ribombee's value lies almost entirely in Sticky Web, Ghost-types such as Pecharunt, Sinistcha, and Arceus-Ghost, which can block Rapid Spin, are incredibly important, while Pokemon that can deter Defog such as Ogerpon and Enamorus should also be considered.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Baton Pass can be used to pass stat boosts from Quiver Dance onto Ribombee's teammates, mainly special attackers like Calyrex-S and Miraidon. Psychic Noise and Psychic are niche options that allow Ribombee to hit Glimmora super effectively.

Checks and Counters

Heavy-Duty Boots Users: Heavy-Duty Boots is a very common item, with many naturally fast Pokemon like Calyrex-S and Miraidon running it, nullifying the effect of Sticky Web entirely.

Taunt Users: Taunt prevents Ribombee from setting up Sticky Web; however, the most common Taunt users of Miraidon, Deoxys-S, and Grimmsnarl must all be wary of Moonblast.

Glimmora: Glimmora directly counters Ribombee, as it resists Moonblast and can use Mortal Spin to remove Sticky Web.

Ditto: Ditto ignores the Speed drop from Sticky Web upon transforming, potentially allowing it to countersweep your team with Choice Scarf.

Hatterene: Hatterene can prevent Ribombee from setting up Sticky Web with its Magic Bounce ability and is able to break Ribombee's Focus Sash. It has to be wary of Skill Swap and Quiver Dance-boosted Moonblast.

Sticky Web.description:
Ribombee is the best Sticky Web setter in AG thanks to its Speed tier letting it outspeed and avoid Taunt from Arceus formes as well as its Fairy typing, which makes it immune to Koraidon's Scale Shot. Moonblast allows Ribombee to threaten Pokemon like Miraidon and Grimmsnarl that may try to use Taunt against it. Stun Spore and Pounce both let Ribombee's allies set up and sweep safely without worrying about the opposing Pokemon outspeeding them. Stun Spore paralyzes the likes of Ho-Oh, whereas Pounce offers a safer alternative while also avoiding Taunt from the likes of Arceus-Ground and Miraidon. Skill Swap allows Ribombee to set up Sticky Web in front of Magic Bounce Hatterene. Alternatively, Quiver Dance boosts the power of Ribombee's Moonblast, allowing it to break Substitute from Zacian-C and deal with Tera Steel Koraidon, both of which may attempt to set up in front of Ribombee; it also allows Ribombee to 2HKO Hatterene. Choice Scarf lets Ribombee outspeed Taunt users like Deoxys-S and Miraidon, with Trick to cripple Glimmora and stall Pokemon. However, it gives Ribombee a shakier matchup into Zacian-C while still being outsped by Jolly Choice Scarf Koraidon. Tera Ghost gives Ribombee an immunity to Extreme Speed from Arceus, whereas Tera Steel provides an immunity to Glimmora's Mortal Spin while still keeping a resistance to Extreme Speed.

Common hyper offense Pokemon such as Calyrex-S, Zacian-C, and Arceus-Ground greatly benefit from Ribombee's Sticky Web. The Speed drop prevents Choice Scarf Koraidon from revenge killing Calyrex-S and Zacian-C, and in Arceus-Ground's case, allows it to outspeed Choice Scarf Calyrex-S after a Dragon Dance boost. Glimmora can provide the team with Spikes support while punishing physical attacks such as Dual Wingbeat, U-turn, and Flare Blitz from Koraidon; Sacred Fire from Ho-Oh; and Extreme Speed from Arceus by setting up Toxic Spikes. It also provides entry hazard control through Mortal Spin, clearing away Spikes that may have been set by Ting-Lu in front of Ribombee, while its Poison typing allows it to clear Toxic Spikes from Eternatus, since their teammates tend to be vulnerable to entry hazards. Arceus in particular enjoys Glimmora's Toxic Spikes and hazard removal, as it allows Arceus to run items like Mental Herb and Lum Berry. It also appreciates Sticky Web, as they strengthen Arceus's middle-level Speed stat.

zu.overview: With its high Speed, good movepool, and powerful offensive typing, Lycanroc has secured a great spot in ZU as a positively potent offensive sweeper as well as an adept entry hazard lead. Its access to a unique priority move in Accelerock lets it bury faster targets like Sneasel as well as boosted threats like Charizard. Swords Dance Lycanroc is a prolific wallbreaker and sweeper, while lead sets can start games off with Stealth Rock, deny opposing hazards with Taunt, and severely weaken foes with Endeavor. However, Lycanroc is hounded by several issues. Its severe lack of bulk means that any strong neutral attack will likely take it out, hampering its opportunities to set up and sweep. Lycanroc also lacks in power if it can't hit a foe super effectively, which can leave it defenseless against certain foes like Regirock and especially Dipplin. Lycanroc's sweep is easily put down by many revenge killers like Whimsicott and Choice Scarf Primeape, which aren't as afraid of Accelerock. The dedicated lead set faces competition from Froslass, which has access to Spikes and a more effective trading tool in Destiny Bond.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Lycanroc can opt out of Accelerock on sand teams, since it outruns everything with Sand Rush active. Choice Band may seem tempting to use on Lycanroc; however, none of its moves are spammable, making the set heavily prediction reliant, and Lycanroc prefers switching moves to deal super effective damage. Crunch allows Lycanroc to hit Palossand hard, which would otherwise be a perfect counter, while Psychic Fangs nails Weezing. Play Rough hits Fighting-types slightly harder than Psychic Fangs and is Lycanroc's best bet at breaking past Dipplin. However, dropping Close Combat leaves Lycanroc unable to break past Orthworm, Magneton, and Regirock, which are generally more common.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Faster Fighting-types like Choice Scarf Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel resist Accelerock and can cleanly take Lycanroc out with Close Combat. Hitmonchan has a strong Mach Punch to pick it off.

Ground-types: Sandaconda and Sandslash resist Lycanroc's Rock-type attacks and can all tank a boosted move from Lycanroc before KOing it back in return with a Ground-type attack.

Water-types: Clawitzer and Poliwrath can tank Lycanroc's unboosted attacks and KO it in return.

Physical Walls: A healthy Dipplin completely walls Lycanroc and threatens it back with Giga Drain. Weezing isn't very keen on taking Stone Edge but can burn Lycanroc in retaliation. Orthworm and Regirock can Terastallize out of their Fighting-type weakness and threaten Lycanroc back with Body Press.

Status Conditions: Burn from Weezing and Charizard hampers Lycanroc's offensive capabilities, while paralysis from Mesprit and Magneton worsens its great Speed as well as potentially stopping it from attacking, which is fatal for a Pokemon as frail as Lycanroc.

Swords Dance.description:
Lycanroc's high Speed and excellent Attack make it a deadly revenge killer, wallbreaker, and setup sweeper. The many switches it forces on foes like Charizard and Sneasel lets it grab a Swords Dance boost and potentially sweep. Stone Edge, while innacurate, is Lycanroc's strongest STAB attack. Alternatively, Rock Blast in conjunction with Loaded Dice is more accurate, but it results in Lycanroc losing Life Orb's extra power boost on its other moves. Lycanroc has a wide array of coverage moves to pick and choose from, with Close Combat being the most reliable choice for its high power and coverage against foes like Orthworm, Regirock, and Magneton. Accelerock lets Lycanroc pick off Rock-weak foes like Sneasel and Choice Scarf Typhlosion as well as weakened targets like Jolteon. Sand Rush is the optimal ability for Lycanroc, as on sand teams, Sand Rush allows Lycanroc to outspeed everything in the metagame, while on non-sand teams, it gives Lycanroc a positive matchup into opposing sand teams. A Jolly nature is generally preferred to outrun Charizard and Froslass, but Adamant is an option on sand teams because of Sand Rush doubling Lycanroc's Speed. Tera Fighting gives Lycanroc immense power on Close Combat, notably cleanly OHKOing Orthworm and Regirock at +2. Tera Ghost flips Lycanroc's Fighting weakness, letting it blank a Choice Scarf Primeape's and Hisuian Sneasel's Close Combat.

Offense and hyper offense teams enjoy Lycanroc's powerful wallbreaking and sweeping potential as well as the assurance it provides against opposing offense with Accelerock, especially against sun teams. Pivots like Primeape, Mesprit, and Whimsicott help Lycanroc hit the field safely. Whimsicott is a particularly good partner, as it handles many of Lycanroc's answers like Dipplin and Sandaconda, and its Prankster Encore can give Lycanroc a chance to sweep. In return, Lycanroc threatens many of Whimsicott's checks like Charizard, Magneton, and Articuno. Other physical wallbreakers like Sneasel, Hisuian Sneasel, and Beartic play well with Lycanroc, working to create gaping holes in the opponent's team for each other to exploit. Dipplin is a near-perfect wall to Lycanroc, so teammates that can exploit it like Charizard and Magneton are quite handy. Lycanroc is quite frail, so defensive teammates like Weezing are helpful for it to fall back on. Lycanroc loves entry hazard setters like Sandslash and Orthworm, as the chip damage from Spikes softens up many of its answers like Dipplin and Sandaconda, helping Lycanroc secure its KOs much more easily. On sand teams, Sand Spit Sandaconda is necessary to set sand, and fellow sand sweepers like Sandslash can band together with Lycanroc to break the opposing team down. As Lycanroc struggles with Fighting-types, teammates that can deal with them like Weezing and Whimsicott are its best friends. Other sweepers on hyper offense teams are useful partners for Lycanroc as well, since many of them like Nasty Plot Mesprit and Swords Dance Virizion exploit Lycanroc's answers in Sandaconda and Regirock. Physical sweepers like Swords Dance Hisuian Sneasel benefit from the holes in the opponent's team left behind by Lycanroc, easing their sweeps. Healing Wish support from Mesprit and Hattrem allows Lycanroc to go for a second round of sweeping.

Lead.description:
With Taunt and its high Speed, Lycanroc makes for an excellent entry hazard-setting lead. Taunt lets Lycanroc deny hazards from being set by Pokemon like Regirock, Orthworm, and Sandaconda as well as stop Defog attempts from Lurantis. Focus Sash is vital to guarantee that Stealth Rock is set even versus foes that would outspeed and OHKO Lycanroc. Endeavor pairs beautifully with Focus Sash, letting Lycanroc bring a foe's health down with it and potentially rendering that opposing Pokemon near useless. Rock Blast lets Lycanroc OHKO lead Froslass through Focus Sash, which allows it to simultaneously preserve its own while completely denying Spikes from going up. Close Combat nails opposing Lycanroc, and Accelerock lets Lycanroc chip faster foes before going down, possibly taking them out completely when combined with Endeavor beforehand. This also makes the mirror against opposing lead Lycanroc easier. Tera Ghost lets Lycanroc spinblock, but it is generally better to preserve Terastallization for Lycanroc's teammates, as it is intended to sacrifice itself.

Lycanroc is best used on hyper offense teams, where it can lead the charge for its pack of setup sweepers. It notably is incredibly annoying for opposing hyper offense teams that use Froslass as their lead, as Lycanroc can one-shot Froslass through Focus Sash with Rock Blast. Mesprit is just one example of the many sweepers that appreciate Stealth Rock chipping away at their checks. On sun teams, Lycanroc denying hazards can free up Fire-type teammates like Charizard and Typhlosion to run items like Choice Specs and Choice Scarf instead of Heavy-Duty Boots. Lycanroc notably struggles to face lead Sandslash, so a teammate that can deal with it, like Virizion, can help Lycanroc in this regard. Since Lycanroc ideally sacrifices itself to get Stealth Rock up, teammates that deter hazard removal are great to make sure that Stealth Rock can stay up. Ghost-types like Spiritomb can block Rapid Spin attempts from Sandslash and Cryogonal, and Defog punishers like Primeape and Malamar make foes think twice about trying to clear Stealth Rock.

Entry Hazard Lead.description:
Lycanroc's niche as a Stealth Rock lead stems from it being the fastest Pokemon with Stealth Rock, Taunt, and a multi-hit move, ensuring that it will prevent entry hazards from opposing leads such as Froslass, Vikavolt, and Hisuian Avalugg while breaking their Focus Sashes. Endeavor is useful for ensuring Lycanroc whittles down bulky Pokemon switching in when its Focus Sash has been broken. Accelerock can also be used as a devastating follow-up for Endeavor, always ensuring that Lycanroc will at least trade with something; however, this comes at the downside of having worse matchups versus opposing entry hazards leads. Maximum Attack investment gives Lycanroc better rolls on Rock Blast, always OHKOing Froslass and Smeargle in 3 hits as opposed to requiring 4, and this investment helps Lycanroc break its Focus Sash easier in conjunction with minimal HP, Defense, and Special Defense IVs. Tera Ghost is used to prevent opposing Rapid Spin users like Alolan Sandslash and Coalossal from removing entry hazards, but it should be used only in dire situations, as the types of teams Lycanroc fits on can rarely afford to use Terastallization too early.

As an entry hazard lead, Lycanroc fits exclusively on hyper offense teams that can take advantage of the pressure Stealth Rock provides and the lack of Stealth Rock on their side, so partners include Pokemon such as Arcanine, Zoroark, Paldean Tauros-W, and Decidueye, all of which are very strong choices on hyper offense. Ghost-types like the aforementioned Decidueye and Houndstone can stop Rapid Spin users like Coalossal and Tastugiri from removing Stealth Rock, though they are only consistent at this short-term. Lycanroc is also often removed by faster Pokemon like Ambipom, Salazzle, and Choice Scarf Rotom-C, so Pokemon that can set up on them like Paldean Tauros-F and Toxtricity are greatly appreciated. Being a fast Rock-type with Taunt also greatly helps in preventing Defog from Pokemon like Scyther and Altaria, which hyper offense staples like Arcanine and Skuntank appreciate.

Choice Band.description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

ru.overview: With its high Attack and Speed, solid movepool, and access to priority in the form of both Accelerock and Sucker Punch, Lycanroc-D can act as a decent wallbreaker and setup sweeper for a variety of teams. Thanks to Tough Claws and a solid offensive typing, it can smash through defensive staples like Umbreon and Reuniclus as well as pick off weakened offensive threats like Gengar and Gardevoir with priority. Its wide variety of coverage moves also makes it somewhat difficult to answer defensively, as it can break through common walls like Amoonguss with Psychic Fangs or Slowbro with Crunch. However, Lycanroc-D is prone to being worn down by physically bulky Pokemon, most notably Rocky Helmet Hippowdon—especially if it takes chip damage from Life Orb and entry hazards as well. Its poor bulk also makes it vulnerable to getting picked off by faster threats that can take on its somewhat weak priority, such as Choice Scarf Mienshao and Krookodile. Lycanroc-D also struggles against opposing priority: Barraskewda can naturally outspeed Lycanroc-D and KO it with Aqua Jet, while Bisharp resists both Accelerock and Sucker Punch, letting it use its own Sucker Punch safely. Additionally, Lycanroc-D faces competition from Terrakion as an offensive Rock-type due to its better bulk and part Fighting-typing.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Lycanroc-D can function as a dedicated lead for offensive teams with Focus Sash and a set of Stealth Rock / Taunt / Endeavor / Accelerock; however, Terrakion and Kleavor give it stiff competition. Trailblaze can be used to lure in and deal significant damage to the likes of Swampert and specially defensive Gastrodon while also making Lycanroc-D difficult to outspeed, though—even Tough Claws-boosted—it's rather weak.

Checks and Counters

Physical Walls: Slowbro and Quagsire are able to take attacks from Lycanroc-D fairly well before retaliating with a super-effective move. Chesnaught and Gastrodon can wear down Lycanroc-D with Rocky Helmet while taking its attacks and threatening it with Body Press and Earthquake, respectively.

Ground-types: Hippowdon can take even boosted attacks from Lycanroc-D and wear it down with a combination of Rocky Helmet chip damage and Earthquake. Gligar resists Close Combat and can similarly KO Lycanroc-D with Earthquake, though Gligar dislikes taking a boosted Stone Edge. Swampert and Rhyperior can also take on Lycanroc-D, though they can't switch in to a Swords-Dance boosted Close Combat.

Revenge Killers: Choice Scarf Pokemon like Mienshao, Terrakion, and Krookodile outspeed Lycanroc-D and can take an Accelerock or Sucker Punch before KOing it with their STAB moves.

All-Out Attacker.description:
Lycanroc-D is one of RU's fiercest wallbreakers, boasting excellent STAB priority and a wide coverage movepool. Accelerock provides crucial priority that helps in revenge killing deadly sweepers like Armarouge. Tough Claws Close Combat deals immense damage to physical walls like Hippowdon and crushes Krookodile. Crunch deals with the tier's many Psychic-type Pokemon, particularly Slowbro. Choice Band allows Lycanroc-D to threaten the likes of Chesnaught and Slowbro with the slightest bit of chip damage such as that from entry hazards. Life Orb scores an OHKO on important targets such as Umbreon after Stealth Rock damage. Tera Fighting lets Close Combat 2HKO Hippowdon and Chesnaught, while Tera Dark Crunch OHKOes Slowbro with slight chip damage from hazards. It also gives Lycanroc-D a Psychic immunity, allowing it to switch into Psychic-type moves from the likes of Cresselia and Choice-locked Gardevoir.

Lycanroc-D fits best on bulky offense teams that have a lot of pivots to bring it in safely against Pokemon such as Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and Umbreon. Thus, specially offensive Pokemon such as Noivern, Basculegion-F, and Magnezone make great teammates, and they also threaten checks to Lycanroc-D such as Chesnaught and Hippowdon. Physical sweepers such as Mimikyu and Maushold appreciate Lycanroc-D's ability to weaken physical walls like the aforementioned Hippowdon as well as Chesnaught. Pokemon such as Thunder Wave Jirachi, Slowbro, and Rotom-H slow down Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Gardevoir, Gengar, and Noivern to prevent Lycanroc-D from getting revenge killed. Cyclizar and the aforementioned Noivern provide entry hazard removal support, which is particularly valuable for Life Orb Lycanroc-D variants, preventing it from getting further chipped by hazards. Lycanroc-D also enjoys Knock Off support from the likes of Cyclizar, Chesnaught, and Mienshao for removing any potential Rocky Helmet. Due to its tendency to be easily revenge killed by Choice Scarf users like Gardevoir and Krookodile, defensive Pokemon like Jirachi and Hippowdon are appreciated, with the latter's Sand Stream also boosting Lycanroc-D's Special Defense, letting it survive a hit in a pinch.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Lycanroc-D is a terrifying wallbreaker in RU, able to rip through defensive teams after a single boost, that packs priority in order to deal with faster teams. Close Combat is Lycanroc-D's strongest move due to Tough Claws and hits Steel-types such as Bisharp and Registeel. Accelerock is good against fast Rock-weak foes, such as Talonflame and Noivern, and can hit foes without them using an attacking move, allowing it to catch foes switching in or using a status move such as Roost from Talonflame, Encore from Maushold, or Trick from Scarf Gengar and Gardevoir. Sucker Punch does more damage against neutral targets such as Barraskweda and the likes of Slowbro and Reuniclus while OHKOing Choice Scarf Gengar and Basculegion-F from full. Life Orb boosts Lycanroc-D's power level to be able to get crucial rolls such as getting an OHKO on Krookodile after an Intimidate. Tera Fighting boosts the power of Close Combat to obscene levels; after a Swords Dance, it will OHKO Chesnaught and has good odds to OHKO Hippowdon. Tera Dark boosts the power of Sucker Punch, meaning at +2, it can always OHKO Slowbro.

Lycanroc-D can fit on offense teams ranging from bulky offense to hyper offense, as they appreciate its ability to heavily damage walls such as Hippowdon and Gastrodon after a boost, and its access to priority means it can revenge kill faster threats such as weakened Gengar and Noivern. Lycanroc-D pairs well with other physically offensive cleaners such as Barraskewda and Bisharp, as they can wear down their shared checks such as Slowbro and Hippowdon in order for one of them to sweep late-game. Lycanroc-D is so naturally powerful that it can be used as a fast revenge killer or late-game cleaner without a boost. Lycanroc-D appreciates special wallbreakers such as Armarouge and Basculegion-F that can threaten its defensive checks such as Slowbro and Chesnaught. Lycanroc-D likes to be paired with pivot move users, such as Basculegion-F, Talonflame, Noivern, Empoleon, and Gligar, as they can not only chip down its checks in Hippowdon and Chensaught but also bring it in safely against Pokemon such as Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon, which would otherwise be a struggle due to Lycanroc-D's poor bulk and limited resistances. Lycanroc-D appreciates entry hazard setters such as Hippowdon and Klefki, as the extra chip damage from their hazards can push targets into range to be KOed by Lycanroc-D; for example, Hippowdon is OHKOed by +2 Tera Fighting Close Combat after Stealth Rock. Healing Wish users such as Jirachi and Gardevoir are great partners to Lycanroc-D, as they allow it to come back after being worn down from chip damage from sources like Life Orb and entry hazards.

Choice Band (Rock).description:
Lycanroc-D is a great choice for Rock teams thanks to its offensive presence and good Speed tier, which allows it to outspeed and get rid of threats like Urshifu-R, Walking Wake, and Iron Treads. An excellent ability combined with a STAB priority move in Accelerock allows Lycanroc-D to revenge kill foes that greatly threaten Rock teams like Chien-Pao, Belly Drum Azumarill, and Shell Smash Cloyster. With Choice Band, Stone Edge 2HKOes Corviknight. Close Combat deals with Normal-, Rock-, Dark- and Steel-types like Ursaluna, Tyranitar, Ting-Lu, Iron Treads, and Hisuian Goodra.
