Psychic Fangs not only breaks screens in the Fairy matchup, but it also deals with Fighting- and Poison-types like Urshifu-R, Great Tusk, Toxapex, Amoonguss, and Clodsire. Play Rough is another option to deal with Dragon- and Dark- types like Walking Wake, Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Sableye.

Garganacl pairs well with Lycanroc-D, as Salt Cure wears down defensive Pokemon Lycanroc-D struggles with such as Quagsire and Corviknight. In return, Garganacl benefits from Lycanroc-D's ability to remove wallbreakers such as Walking Wake and Urshifu-R which threaten Garganacl's Iron Defense + Body Press set. Tyranitar is an essential teammate as it sets up sand to further chip down walls and checks threats like Flutter Mane, Latios, and Bisharp due to its sheer bulk and great coverage in Heavy Slam, Crunch, and Low Kick. Hisuian Arcanine's wallbreaking power covers walls that are harder for Lycanroc-D to take down, dealing with Toxapex and Corviknight with Head Smash and Flare Blitz, respectively. Kleavor is a great lead, as Stone Axe sets up Stealth Rock to break through any opposing Focus Sash, allowing Lycanroc-D and Hisuian Arcanine to clean teams more easily. It can also pivot into Lycanroc-D with U-turn, luring in foes like Toxapex, Iron Treads, and Heatran in the process. Choice item Glimmora's colorful moveset helps against walls like Quagsire and Toxapex through the use of Energy Ball and Earth Power, with Choice Scarf allowing Glimmora to outspeed and take down fast offensive threats such as Iron Valiant and Greninja if they aren't running Choice Scarf. Coalossal removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin, checks Scizor and Bisharp with Flamethrower and Body Press, and can burn threats with Flame Body. Iron Defense + Calm Mind Diancie can check Garchomp with Moonblast. Shell Smash Air Balloon Drednaw provides a temporary Ground-type immunity and appreciates defensive walls being worn down by Lycanroc-D. In return, it readily cleans weakened Flying and Ground teams, eliminating threats like Landorus-T and Great Tusk.

Physical Wall.description:
Physically defensive Mareanie is a bulky pivot that enters the game on strong attacks, such as Mienfoo's High Jump Kick. Once on the field, its good coverage can threaten various foes. Ice Beam threatens an incoming Foongus or Toedscool, Mud Shot hits opposing Mareanie and slows incoming Pokemon that would be faster than itself. Mareanie invests in bulk in order to stomach Flare Blitz from Hisuian Growlithe and High Jump Kick from Mienfoo even after its Eviolite has been removed. Its Special Defense EVs allow Mareanie to check Wingull and survive Gothita's Psychic from full HP. Tera Dragon provides insurance against the Electric-types in Elekid and Chinchou. Mareanie also has the option of using Tera Ghost to escape being trapped by Shadow Tag Gothita and to surprise a Choice Scarf Mienfoo, which is expected to 2HKO after Spikes with Reckless-boosted High Jump Kick.

Mareanie and Mienfoo form a double Regenerator core. Nearly everything benefits from Mareanie's ability to check Mienfoo, notably Rock and Steel-types like Glimmet and Alolan Sandshrew. Mareanie partners well with Toedscool, which is OHKOed by Flare Blitz from Hisuian Growlithe. Mareanie is weak to Spikes, Electric-types, and Ground-types, all which Toedscool covers in return. Mareanie and Tinkatink also make good partners because of their capacity to cover the dual threat of Mienfoo and Vullaby; with Mareanie taking High Jump Kick for Tinkatink, which absorbs Knock Off and takes Brave Bird. Gothita can be a huge thorn because it threatens to trap and remove Mareanie. It is wise to pair Mareanie with a Dark-type like Vullaby or Stunky to take advantage of a Choice Scarf Gothita locked into Psychic.

Offensive Wall.description:
Offensive Mareanie leverages its natural bulk, typing, and Regenerator to invest in its Special Attack, making it much more threatening. Mud Shot allows Mareanie to hit a variety of Pokemon: Elekid, Chinchou, Stunky, Tinkatink, Glimmet, and opposing Mareanie, with the bonus of making Mareanie faster than the latter two after one hit. Ice Beam hits Ground- and Grass-types like Mudbray, Toedscool, and Foongus as well as Vullaby super effectively. Sacrificing some of its Special Defense, Mareanie invests heavily into its Special Attack, which improves its damage rolls against much of the tier, notably allowing it to 2HKO Foongus with Ice Beam after Stealth Rock. Due to the loss of bulk, however, Mareanie has a harder time defending against Pokemon like Alolan Sandshrew and Stunky. Tera Dragon protects Mareanie from Elekid and Chinchou, while Tera Ghost allows it to escape Gothita's Shadow Tag and block Rapid Spin from Toedscool and Alolan Sandshrew.

Mareanie complements Pokemon that are threatened by Mienfoo, such as Alolan Sandshrew. In return, Alolan Sandshrew can remove entry hazards with Rapid Spin, which helps Mareanie last longer despite its lessened bulk. Grookey is a great partner, as it can check the Ground-types that threaten Mareanie, with the Grassy Terrain it provides keeping Mareanie healthy and halving the power of Earthquake. Toedscool fills a similar role to Grookey, as it can check Ground-types while being a better switch-in to Electric-types than Grookey, in addition to its ability to clear hazards. Dark-type teammates that can take advantage of a Gothita trapping Mareanie are also appreciated.

Mixed Defense.description:
Toxapex holds a niche as a strong mixed wall, being able to effectively hold the line against a plethora of strong neutral hits and healing off large portions of damage through a combination of Recover and Regenerator. Compared to Liquidation, Surf allows Toxapex to achieve a 3HKO against Lokix, and does more damage to Rhyperior while also having more PP. Liquidation deals more damage to Tyranitar and bulkier variants of Excadrill, and it also allows Toxapex to utilize its bulk by fishing for Defense drops. Toxic and Haze form a potent combination and prevent Toxapex from being vulnerable to setup sweepers like Hydrapple and Quaquaval while also making it a reliable stopgap against Battle Bond Greninja. Toxic also allows it to threaten bulkier foes like Slowking, Tornadus-T, and Hippowdon by putting them on a timer. Heavy-Duty Boots expands Toxapex's longevity, while Rocky Helmet can be used to punish physically oriented pivots like Scizor and Lokix. Leftovers provides passive recovery that compounds with Regenerator and alleviates the need to use Recover. The given EV spread allows Toxapex to avoid being 2HKOed by Hisuian Arcanine's Head Smash as well as avoiding the OHKO from non-Choice Specs Latios's Luster Purge. Toxapex's Tera type is largely customizable based on the needs of the team; Tera Fairy is a strong neutral defensive typing that maintains Toxapex's resistances to Bug and Fighting while giving it an immunity to Dragon, while Tera Ground gives Toxapex an immunity to Electric-type moves from Sandy Shocks and Thundurus-T. Options such as Tera Steel to maintain Toxapex's Steel and Fairy resistances and immunity to Toxic are also viable.

Toxapex fits best on balance teams that appreciate the unique options it provides over Slowking, most notably Haze and Toxic. For this reason, it pairs exceptionally well with Pokemon that struggle against Slowking, such as Rhyperior, Tinkaton, and Tornadus-T, creating a solid defensive backbone with the former two and a Regenerator core with the latter. Tinkaton and Tornadus-T in particular are appreciated due to their ability to check Latios, which can power through Toxapex with ease. Hydrapple is a strong partner thanks to its Ground resistance and its ability to form a Regenerator core with Toxapex. Mandibuzz is a particularly good partner thanks to its ability to remove entry hazards with Defog and function as a backup check to Quaquaval and Latios while also appreciating Toxapex's ability to stave off Belly Drum Azumarill. In a similar vein, Toxapex is also appreciated on sand teams because it can cut into the longevity of bulkier foes, especially when Toxic is compounded with the chip damage from sand, making it easier for Pokemon like Excadrill and Ogerpon-C to bulldoze the opposing team. In return, these Pokemon can remove troublesome foes like Thundurus-T and opposing Excadrill that threaten Toxapex with heavy damage. Cobalion makes a good partner, as it can reliably check Swords Dance Ogerpon-C and Non-Terastillized Swords Dance Zarude, both of which can muscle through Toxapex with relative ease. In addition, Toxapex can struggle against other offensive staples like Zarude and Thundurus-T, so revenge killers such as Lokix and Scizor or bulkier teammates that are not as vulnerable to these foes, such as Hippowdon and Rhyperior, are greatly appreciated.

Defensive.description: Toxapex's access to Regenerator, good defensive typing, and formidable bulk lets it excel at keeping physical threats like Zacian and Palafin at bay. Haze prevents foes like Ogerpon-H and Zacian from boosting repeatedly and subsequently breaking past Toxapex. While on the field, Toxic Spikes keep threats like Palkia-O, Kyurem-W, and Palafin from coming in lest they be put on a timer. Alternatively, Toxic is an option to make Toxapex a more threatening presence on the field, although it means Substitute from Pokemon like Palkia-O ruins it. Infestation lets Toxapex trap poisoned foes, forcing them to accumulate passive damage. Alternatively, Sludge Bomb gives Toxapex a means of pressuring Calm Mind + Taunt Arceus formes. If no other check is available, Toxapex can use Tera Dark to absorb a Psystrike or Kowtow Cleave from Mewtwo or Kingambit and neutralize it with Haze or Toxic. In a similar fashion, it can use Tera Grass to stomach a hit from Landorus, Arceus-Electric, or Great Tusk and cripple it with Toxic. Toxapex is a natural fit on bulky balance and is a staple on stall, as its staying power shines best in the long games such teams often face. Being a physical wall, Toxapex can form a strong defensive core with special walls like Solgaleo, Blissey, Arceus-Dark, and Magearna. Pokemon susceptible to passive damage like Landorus-T and Arceus formes appreciate Toxapex absorbing chip damage in their place so that they can be in top shape when they're needed. Toxapex is vulnerable to Pokemon like Great Tusk, Landorus, and Mewtwo; pair it with teammates that can cover these threats, such as Landorus-T, Skarmory, and Solgaleo.

Physical Wall.description:
• Toxapex is an excellent physically defensive wall capable of taking on foes such as Koraidon and Zacian-C.
  • Haze shuts down boosting attempts from the likes of Swords Dance Koraidon, Arceus, and Zacian-C.
  • Toxic prevents checks like Miraidon, Groudon, and Arceus-Ground from coming in freely and forcing Toxapex out while also putting setup sweepers on a timer.
  • If Toxapex runs Toxic Spikes, teammates such as Arceus-Ground can pressure Toxic Spikes absorbers like Eternatus and Clodsire. Poison Jab spreads poison to foes like Arceus-Fairy and Flutter Mane, and Ice Beam helps Toxapex greatly with Rayquaza while also helping against Landorus-T, Koraidon, and Gliscor.
  • Rocky Helmet is preferred to chip down physical attackers and most pivots. Mental Herb is an alternative that helps Toxapex deal with Taunt Arceus formes.
  • Tera Fairy makes Toxapex immune to Dragon-type moves, letting it deal with Scale Shot Koraidon, while Tera Ground helps Toxapex against Wild Charge Zacian-C.
  • Toxapex makes good partners with other defensive Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Clodsire, which can check threats like Miraidon. In return, Toxapex can help deal with threats like Koraidon and Zacian-C.
  • Offensive pivots like Miraidon, Koraidon, and Landorus-T also pair well with Toxapex, as they can bring it in more freely to handle their checks.
  • Gliscor can switch into Ground-types such as Ting-Lu, non-Ice Beam Arceus-Ground, and Heavy-Duty Boots Miraidon, spread entry hazards, and check Koraidon and Zacian-C, preventing Toxapex from being worn down.

The Pex (Defensive).description:
Toxapex is a resilient defensive Pokemon that makes good use of its typing, great mixed bulk, and Regenerator to check a plethora of offensive threats, including Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, and Enamorus. Toxic's immediate way to put foes on a timer can be forgone for Toxic Spikes, which greatly punishes teams lacking a grounded Poison-type; however, forgoing Toxic makes it more exploitable by foes like Dragonite, Tornadus-T, and Heavy-Duty Boots users like Dragapult and Ogerpon. Haze can shut down all manner of setup sweepers looking to overpower through Toxapex, like Iron Valiant, Ogerpon-W, Ceruledge, and Zamazenta; in conjunction with Recover, Haze makes it much easier for Toxapex to stall out foes via poison. Haze also prevents Toxapex from being exploited by setup sweepers immune to Toxic, like Swords Dance Gliscor, Calm Mind Clefable, and Nasty Plot Gholdengo, making it easier for teammates like Blissey and Gliscor to answer them. Alternatively, Infestation lets Toxapex trap and wear down an otherwise strong switchin in Galarian Weezing as well as other passive walls and poison-immune targets like non-U-turn Corviknight, Pecharunt, Gholdengo, and opposing Toxapex. Another option is Baneful Bunker, which lets Toxapex punish Ogerpon-W's Power Whip, safely scout foes, absorb Future Sight along with Tera Steel, and punish U-turn from the likes of Cinderace and Dragapult. Poison Jab can be used to immediately threaten Ogerpon-W, particularly Taunt variants, and foes like Hatterene, Clefable, and Substitute Primarina, even their Calm Mind sets; this variant should opt for an Impish nature instead. Heavy-Duty Boots gives Toxapex more reliability as a pivot on teams using little or no entry hazard removal, while Leftovers is an alternative item choice on teams with multiple hazard removers like Galarian Weezing, Corviknight, and Talonflame, granting greater longevity and making Toxapex an even more effective pivot. Black Sludge is an alternative option similar to Leftovers; while it can be detrimental if Toxapex decides to Terastallize, this allows Toxapex to punish Trick from Choice item users like Gholdengo and Darkrai, which can be very punishing to stall teams. Tera Grass improves Toxapex's matchup against Ogerpon-W while also granting a resistance to Ground to better check Great Tusk and Iron Treads and a resistance to Electric to sponge Volt Switch from Raging Bolt and Iron Crown. Tera Steel is a great defensive type that lets Toxapex deal with Galarian Slowking and Hatterene, which can be annoying for stall teams, while retaining its poison immunity against foes like Pecharunt and opposing Toxapex.

Toxapex is a fantastic asset to stall teams as a Toxic-spreading Regenerator pivot and a scout against unpredictable threats like Iron Valiant, Dragapult, and Kyurem. Dondozo and Blissey are two great partners that appreciate Toxapex's ability to scout Kyurem, thanks to its ability to survive every attack other than Choice Specs Tera Ice Freeze-Dry. Once scouted, Dondozo answers most variations of Dragon Dance Kyurem, while Blissey answers Choice Specs and Heavy-Duty Boots Kyurem. The two also appreciate Toxapex answering utility Dragapult, which otherwise gets free entry on both. Toxapex's opportunities to badly poison physical sweepers like Swords Dance Iron Valiant and Dragonite make it much easier for Dondozo to answer them over the course of a game, with Dondozo checking Kingambit in return. Blissey appreciates Toxapex scouting potential Trick users like Gholdengo and Darkrai, ensuring it can consistently answer them without being crippled by Trick. Toxapex answers mixed wallbreakers like Iron Valiant and Keldeo and relieves Blissey of pressure from Primarina and Walking Wake's pivoting moves, while Blissey walls special attackers that threaten Toxapex like Raging Bolt and Iron Moth. Clodsire is another special wall that appreciates Toxapex absorbing a potential Trick from Gholdengo so that it can be a consistent check. Specially defensive Gliscor is another wonderful teammate that answers wallbreakers like Raging Bolt and Iron Moth and Ground-types that threaten Toxapex like Landorus-T and Ting-Lu, and it sets entry hazards to keep up pressure against Ogerpon-W. Gliscor is also useful for absorbing Knock Off from Pokemon like Tinkaton and Clefable, ensuring that Toxapex can retain its Heavy-Duty Boots and maximize its pivoting capabilities. In return, Toxapex answers threats to Gliscor like Primarina and Weavile, negating their setup attempts with Haze. Corviknight is another ally that provides entry hazard removal and absorbs Knock Off from Pokemon like Weavile and Great Tusk while also being a great check to opposing Gliscor. Toxapex appreciates the presence of Galarian Weezing thanks to its ability to punish opposing Gliscor and Clefable, which would otherwise wall Toxapex. Its ability to consistently remove hazards in the face of Gholdengo increases Toxapex's longevity should it lose its Heavy-Duty Boots and frees it to run Leftovers to grant further longevity. In return, Toxapex helps spread Toxic poison to more quickly wear down hazard setters like Great Tusk and Landorus-T and special wallbreakers that threaten Galarian Weezing like Primarina and Kyurem. Between Galarian Weezing's Will-O-Wisp and Toxapex's Haze and Regenerator, the two work well together to hold off the otherwise threatening Curse Garganacl. Similarly, Galarian Weezing's ability to burn Ogerpon-W makes Toxapex a much more reliable check to it, while Toxapex's ability to badly poison Ogerpon-W leaves it more quickly worn down by Galarian Weezing.

Assault Vest.description:
Assault Vest increases Toxapex's already amazing Special Defense to even greater heights, and although it comes at the cost of utility moves, Toxapex makes up for that with a diverse set of attacking moves. Toxapex easily switches into top special attackers like Iron Valiant, Dragapult, Enamorus, Iron Moth, and Primarina while also threatening them with super effective attacks. Regenerator's healing is typically enough for Assault Vest Toxapex to shrug off almost any special attack, making for an excellent bulky pivot. Sludge Bomb is the best attacking move Toxapex has; it not only covers notable Grass- and Fairy-types such as Ogerpon-W, Enamorus, Iron Valiant, and Primarina, but it can also potentially inflict debilitating status on would-be switchins like Alomomola. Surf allows Toxapex to pick up noteworthy 2HKOs on Cinderace, defensive Moltres, and Iron Moth. Ice Beam rounds out Toxapex's offensive coverage, namely hitting Dragon-types like Dragapult, Raging Bolt, and Dragonite as well as Landorus-T and Gliscor for even greater damage. Infestation lets it trap and wear down foes like Corviknight, Galarian Weezing, and Garganacl, with Toxapex able to outstall their recovery options due to Infestation's high PP. For teams particularly weak to Calm Mind Magic Guard Clefable or Curse Garganacl, Acid Spray is an alternative option over Infestation, letting Toxapex or its teammate overwhelm them one-on-one more easily.

Tera Steel covers up Assault Vest Toxapex's extreme weakness to Psychic-type moves from the likes of Iron Crown, Galarian Slowking, and Deoxys-S. It also provides Toxapex with the added bonus of resisting Stealth Rock and Ogerpon-W's Power Whip, which would otherwise OHKO Toxapex. Tera Fairy is a solid alternative, particularly against mixed Dragapult, or Dark-types such as Weavile, Darkrai, and Hisuian Samurott. Tera Dark similarly lets Toxapex resist the aforementioned Dark-types while also providing an immunity to threatening Psychic-type moves like Psyshock from Iron Crown and making the Dragapult and Gholdengo matchups more favorable. A Modest nature is preferred to boost Toxapex's attacks, which guarantees that Sludge Bomb OHKOes Iron Valiant and Enamorus after Stealth Rock damage. However, Bold can also be used for extra defensive bulk, allowing Toxapex to avoid the guaranteed OHKO from Great Tusk's Headlong Rush and offensive Landorus-T's Earthquake after Stealth Rock.

Assault Vest Toxapex can only fit on stall and defensive balance archetypes due to its subpar damage output in conjunction with competition against other bulky Regenerator pivots like Alomomola, Tornadus-T, Galarian Slowking, and Hydrapple, all of which fit better on even moderately offensive teams. As a result of Toxapex's place on bulky balance and stall teams, Assault Vest Toxapex pairs well with other defensive Pokemon like Gliscor, Corviknight, Dondozo, and Galarian Weezing. With Knock Off being a major problem for Assault Vest Toxapex, Gliscor's utility in absorbing Knock Off is extremely valuable to it. Furthermore, Gliscor's defensive profile lines up nicely, swapping into Zapdos and Raging Bolt. Meanwhile, Toxapex switches into Water- and Ice-type threats such as Walking Wake, Primarina, and Weavile. Corviknight and Dondozo are also excellent defensive teammates, able to handle physical threats like Great Tusk, Kingambit, and Landorus-T, which Toxapex struggles with. Furthermore, Corviknight acts as a Knock Off absorber while also clearing entry hazards with its Defog, preventing Toxapex from being worn down easily. In return, Toxapex can wall Fire-types like Cinderace, Iron Moth, and Moltres for Corviknight, and powerful special attackers like Primarina, Darkrai and Walking Wake for Dondozo. Gholdengo can still deny Corviknight's Defog, which is exactly why Galarian Weezing is a fantastic partner with its own unblockable Defog. It can also defensively answer Hisuian Samurott, which threatens Spikes and Knock Off against Toxapex. As for more offensive teammates, Great Tusk and Iron Treads work well thanks to their ability to remove hazards with Rapid Spin and threaten Raging Bolt and Galarian Slowking for Toxapex. In return, Toxapex helps both Great Tusk and Iron Treads by absorbing Will-O-Wisp and handling threats like Iron Valiant, Moltres, and Enamorus. Ting-Lu forms a nice core too, as Toxapex baits in Pokemon Ting-Lu can take advantage of such as Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Raging Bolt. Meanwhile, Toxapex absorbs Toxic Spikes for Ting-Lu and handles its checks like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant. There's also Gholdengo—a solid teammate for Assault Vest Toxapex, since it has favorable matchups against Iron Crown and Galarian Slowking, while conversely Toxapex does work for Gholdengo by answering Dragapult, Darkrai, and Iron Moth.

The Pex.description:
Armed with a superb defensive typing, excellent mixed bulk, one of the best abilities in the game, and an extremely disruptive support movepool, Toxapex entrenches itself as a staple defensive piece in the metagame. These traits allow Toxapex to counter several dangerous Pokemon, such as Zamazenta, Mega Charizard Y, and Urshifu-R. Scald lets Toxapex reliably spread burn onto several Toxic-immune Pokemon, notably Melmetal, Ferrothorn, and Kingambit. On the other hand, Knock Off can remove important items from the likes of Zapdos, Moltres, and Melmetal. Toxic combines with Scald or Knock Off to make Toxapex quite challenging to switch into and allows it to ruin threats such as Dragonite, Ogerpon-W, and Moltres. Toxapex is also the tier's best user of Toxic Spikes, which are very challenging for common Pokemon like Great Tusk, Raging Bolt, and Ogerpon-W to deal with. Haze allows Toxapex to sit on boosting threats such as Volcarona, Zamazenta, and Iron Valiant. Recover keeps Toxapex healthy while staying in battle, combining with Regenerator to make Toxapex extremely hard to wear down. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Toxapex to pivot into entry hazards without fear of being worn down, letting it more easily check threats such as Mega Charizard Y. Rocky Helmet can be used to chip physical attackers such as Zamazenta and Hisuian Samurott while also punishing U-turn attempts from the likes of Mega Lopunny, Mega Scizor, and Urshifu-R. Black Sludge gives Toxapex passive recovery, allowing it to better stay healthy versus opponents such as Volcarona and Mega Lopunny, and it has niche use versus Trick users such as Iron Valiant and Gholdengo. The given EV spread allows Toxapex to take a +2 Power Whip from Ogerpon-W at full health, while the rest of the EVs are dumped into Special Defense to improve matchups versus Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona.

Toxapex is a staple on bulkier playstyles thanks to its absurd longevity and ability to force progress through spreading chip damage. Gliscor is a notable teammate, as it has great defensive synergy with Toxapex; it appreciates Toxapex checking Water-types such as Urshifu-R and Hisuian Samurott, while in return it deals with Electric-types such as Raging Bolt and Zapdos. The two are also generally hard to break thanks to their immense longevity when paired together, and they can outlast many common threats such as Landorus-T, Ogerpon-W, and Great Tusk if played well. Toxapex does well on hazard stack teams, as it forces quite a few switches, uses Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes such as Great Tusk, Terapagos, and Zapdos, and punishes many of the tier's hazard removal options with Toxic or a Scald burn. Ferrothorn is an exemplary partner that can set Stealth Rock and Spikes while also checking certain Grass-types that Toxapex has to be very careful around, most notably Ogerpon-W. Gholdengo is another excellent partner, as it checks dangerous Psychic-types like Tapu Lele and Mega Medicham and prevents opposing hazard removal thanks to Good as Gold and its Ghost typing. Gholdengo, as well as the previously mentioned Ferrothorn, appreciate Toxapex pivoting into dangerous Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona. Slow-paced, bulky wincons, such as Swords Dance Gliscor, bulky Volcarona, and Calm Mind Clefable, appreciate Toxapex spreading chip damage and synergize very well with Toxic Spikes, as they become very hard to beat when the opponent's team is getting slowly worn down while they stay healthy with their recovery moves and boost up.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Water

Eject Button is a solid choice Toxapex can run on rain teams, as it allows for Toxapex to become a one-time pivot to keep up offensive momentum. Eject Button can still be ran without rain, but its need for momentum preservation is less desired and can lead to Toxapex being forced out against a threat it would need to land Toxic or Haze against such as Sinistcha.

Poison

Air Balloon can serve a crucial niche, allowing Toxapex to wall Ceruledge once its Air Balloon is popped, along with granting it a temporary Ground immunity that allows it to pivot in on Choice-locked Ground-types like Excadrill and Mamoswine safely. Baneful Bunker can be used over Toxic and Toxic Spikes with Infestation and Black Sludge, enabling Toxapex to easily trap and wear down targets like Choice Band Gouging Fire and Barraskewda, as Baneful Bunker can spread poison and help Toxapex recover with Black Sludge simultaneously. Using both Surf and Infestation is a viable tactic that allows Toxapex to trap and eliminate Toxic-immune targets such as Klefki and Galarian Weezing while also wearing down certain targets greatly, such as Archaludon and Alolan Muk, during Infestation's trapping turns to either remove or cripple checks to teammates such as Okidogi and Iron Moth.

Water (Physically Defensive)

Liquidation and Surf allow Toxapex to not be countered by opposing Steel-types, being able to hit targets like Scizor and Skarmory. Of course, this gives up one of Toxapex's valuable utility options or even its Poison-type STAB moves, which can hinder Toxapex in other matchups.

Mixed Wall (Water).description:
A spread with mixed bulk investment can allow Toxapex's walling capabilities to be expanded to more reliably check special attackers such as Flutter Mane while still taking on physical threats like Meowscarada. Poison Jab puts pressure onto Grass- and Fairy-types like Hisuian Lilligant, Primarina, and Enamorus. Toxic forces bulkier foes such as Iron Hands and Dragonite on timers. Finally, Haze prevents the likes of Calm Mind Clefable and Swords Dance Hisuian Samurott from using Toxapex as a setup opportunity. Black Sludge allows Toxapex to stick around longer without requiring the usage of Recover, but Heavy-Duty Boots can be used to allow Toxapex safe entry in the face of entry hazards. The EV spread prevents a 2HKO from Meowscarada's Flower Trick and Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

Ogerpon-W serves as a wonderful teammate, as it is neutral to Electric-type attacks, can lock Raging Bolt into a setup move with Encore, and threatens Ground-types that handle Toxapex such as Great Tusk and Sandy Shocks while appreciating Toxapex's Poison Jab removing Grass-types like Meowscarada and Hisuian Lilligant that otherwise wall it. Swampert is immune to Electric and can use Earthquake to check Poison- and Steel-types that wall Toxapex such as Alolan Muk, Galarian Slowking, Heatran, and Gholdengo. Greninja can outspeed and remove Psychic-types such as Latios and Metagross and uses coverage such as Sludge Wave to deal with Grass-types Toxapex cannot handle such as the Ogerpon formes and Hydrapple or Ice Beam to break through Clodsire. Alternatively, Hisuian Samurott can be ran as the team's Dark-type, with Ceaseless Edge being a more reliable way of taking on Hoopa-U while setting up Spikes to wear down Toxapex's checks like Choice Specs Iron Moth. Keldeo and Urshifu-R provide solid ways to break Steel-types like Empoleon and Hisuian Goodra along with handling Kyurem. Primarina appreciates Toxapex absorbing Toxic Spikes and using Toxic to wear down targets such as Iron Hands and opposing Primarina, and in return, it can take on Dragon-types like Garchomp and Roaring Moon.

Physically Defensive (Poison).description:
Thanks to its Water typing and incredible combination of defensive stats in tandem with Regenerator, Toxapex serves as a pivotal wall for Poison teams, taking on several key offensive threats such as Scizor, Barraskewda, and Weavile. Surf provides a consistent form of damage for Toxapex and threatens Fire- and Rock-types like Moltres, Hisuian Arcanine, and Kleavor. Infestation can trap and wear down foes such as Hisuian Samurott and Keldeo, especially when paired with Toxic. Alternatively, Chilling Water can lower the Attack of would-be threats like Dragon Dance Gouging Fire and Bulk Up Okidogi, preventing them from sweeping the team. Haze enables Toxapex to remove buffs from setup sweepers such as Ceruledge, Scizor, and Urshifu-R. Toxic allows Toxapex to check Dragon Dance Gouging Fire and Volcarona, putting them on timers and enabling Poison teams to outlast them. Alternatively, Toxic Spikes can be used on teams already having a Toxic user to more reliably wear down types lacking good entry hazard removal, such as Dark and Ghost, forcing the majority of the opposing team on a timer. Heavy-Duty Boots prevents Toxapex from getting worn down when switching into threats such as Iron Boulder and Cloyster. Alternatively, Rocky Helmet punishes contact attackers such as Sneasler and allows Toxapex to counter Tidy Up Maushold. Finally, Black Sludge pairs well with Infestation, enabling Toxapex to stay in on trapped foes more reliably.

Amoonguss and Galarian Slowking pair excellently with Toxapex, creating a defensive Regenerator core for Poison teams, with Toxapex being the sturdiest physical wall out of the trio, handling threats like Meowscarada and Cloyster, which the other two cannot handle. In return, Amoonguss can come in on Ground- and Electric-types like Great Tusk, Sandy Shocks, and Regieleki to handle them with its Grass-type STAB moves, as well as dealing with setup sweepers such as Dragon Dance Dragapult and Swords Dance Ogerpon-W with Foul Play. Assault Vest Galarian Slowking complements Toxapex by being a specially bulky Regenerator wall, taking on the likes of Heatran, Latios, and Zapdos for Toxapex. Alolan Muk provides an incredible special wall, capable of taking on Psychic- and Ghost-type threats such as Galarian Slowking, Hatterene, Flutter Mane, and Spectrier. Galarian Weezing provides incredible Ground and Dragon immunities, which help it check threats like Mamoswine, Garchomp, and Hydrapple while spreading burns with Will-O-Wisp, making it easier for Toxapex to wall physical attackers like Kleavor. Galarian Weezing also appreciates Toxapex's Water typing to take on Steel-types attacks from the likes of Scizor and Tinkaton. Iron Moth enjoys Toxapex's ability to come in on Water-type moves from the likes of Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Barraskewda. In return, Iron Moth can remove Steel- and Ice-types like non-Choice Scarf Iron Treads, Gholdengo, Alolan Sandslash, and Alolan Ninetales with its Fire-type STAB moves while also dealing with Landorus and Kyurem with Choice Specs-boosted Overheat. Sneasler and Okidogi can remove special walls that can absorb Toxapex's Toxic, such as Blissey, Hisuian Goodra, and Alolan Muk, with their powerful Fighting-type STAB moves, while appreciating Toxapex's Toxic wearing down physical walls like Sableye, Moltres, and Slowbro. Choice Scarf Sneasler can also reliably check threats such as Choice Scarf Hoopa-U, Iron Valiant, and the Ogerpon formes for Toxapex.

Physically Defensive (Water).description:
With its incredible bulk and Grass neutrality, Toxapex provides an essential check to many physical attackers such as Meowscarada and Sneasler. Its Poison-type STAB moves enable Toxapex to take on threatening Grass- and Fairy-types such as Meowscarada, Hisuian Lilligant, Primarina, and Hatterene, with Poison Jab being preferred over other Poison-type STAB moves thanks to its ability to beat bulky Calm Mind users such as Primarina and Hatterene. Haze prevents setup from Skarmory and Bisharp, forcing them to attack into Toxapex's Rocky Helmet and take chip damage. Toxic can be used to force bulkier foes such as Sinistcha and Iron Hands onto dangerous timers; alternatively, Toxic Spikes can be used to force immediate pressure onto targets such as the Ogerpon formes upon entry and punish teams without solid entry hazard removal like Dragon and Water. Heavy Duty-Boots prevents Toxapex from being worn down, so it can continually find safe entry into foes like Meowscarada and Iron Boulder. However, Rocky Helmet punishes the plethora of contact attackers such as Scizor and Kleavor, while Black Sludge racks up recovery over time, enabling Toxapex to stay in longer against threats like Dragonite.

Swampert and Gastrodon make for an excellent defensive core, being able to take on many of the Electric-types that are tasked with removing Toxapex such as Raging Bolt, Magnezone, and Iron Hands and wear down Toxapex's checks like Kyurem with Stealth Rock support. Empoleon can similarly provide Stealth Rock support along with more reliably taking on the special Grass-types that Toxapex struggles against like Sinistcha and Hydrapple and being able to check Kyurem. Greninja provides a crucial Psychic immunity, threatens foes like Latios and Metagross, and uses its colorful coverage and blazing Speed tier to remove problematic offensive threats like the Ogerpon formes and Dragonite while apprecating Toxapex's ability to switch into faster physical targets like Meowscarada and Dragapult. Alternatively, Hisuian Samurott can take the role of the team's Dark-type attacker, being able to set up Spikes with Ceaseless Edge and more reliably remove targets like Hoopa-U and Gallade. Ogerpon-W is able to take on foes like Sandy Shocks and Rotom-W that check Toxapex otherwise while apprecating Toxapex's ability to wear down Grass-types that wall it such as Hydrapple. Keldeo and Urshifu-R are powerful wallbreakers that can handle Steel-types like Heatran, Hisuian Goodra, and Gholdengo that hardwall Toxapex otherwise. Primarina enjoys Toxapex being able to put targets like Ting-Lu and opposing Primarina onto timers while absorbing Poison-type moves from the likes of Sneasler and Alolan Muk, and in return, Primarina can take on powerful Dragon-types like Roaring Moon and Garchomp that can overwhelm Toxapex.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Return Of The Pex.description:
• Toxapex stands out as a masterful spreader of poison to support its teammates, and an effective bulky pivot against common foes like Urshifu-R as well.

  • Toxic: Toxic is the most reliable way to spread the deadliest version of poison and is especially effective against Taunt users like Annihilape and Serperior if using Mental Herb.

  • Toxic Spikes: Toxic Spikes makes the team less reliant on Toxapex to spread status directly, and acts as excellent support for stalling teammates like Ting-Lu, Dragonite and Gliscor.

  • Haze: Even with Toxapex's great bulk, powerful setup sweepers like Dragonite and Urshifu-S quickly get out of control for it, so Haze is the best solution to prevent Toxapex from being setup bait.

  • Liquidation versus Poison Jab: Liquidation isn't particularly strong but it allows Toxapex to 2HKO Chi-Yu and is a great option for breaking Substitute against targets like Flutter Mane. Poison Jab leaves Toxapex completely walled by Steel-types, but it does preform better against Water-types like Primarina and Ogerpon-W.

  • Baneful Bunker: If using Black Sludge or Leftovers, Baneful Bunker is a fantastic way to spread poison against physical attackers and get some extra recovery with one moveslot, but keep in mind that this won't work against Urshifu-R. It's also key for scouting dangerous uses of Trick from the likes of Gholdengo and Latios.

  • Physically Defensive versus Specially Defensive: Physically defensive Toxapex does well against some hard-to-check threats, such as Urshifu-R and Chien-Pao. Maximizing Special Defense on the other hand, almost always lets Toxapex survive Tera Normal Life Orb Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon.

Other Options

  • Infestation: Infestation is Toxapex's best chance of doing chip damage to Toxic-immune threats, such as Corviknignt and Gholdengo, and the trapping works fairly well against foes that do have problems with Toxic. It also prevents double switching from being an issue for Toxapex.

  • Chilling Water: Chilling Water gives Toxapex another tool against physical sweepers, but makes it much more vulnerable to Substitute in general.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: While Terastallization can help Toxapex beat a new set of threats, its bulk and good defensive typing usually makes it a rare occurrence compared to its teammates.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy removes all of Toxapex's weaknesses and can save it from taking massive damage from Chi-Yu's Dark Pulse. It also does well against powerful Dragon-type attacks such as Choice Band Dragonite's Outrage and Choice Specs Archaludon's Draco Meteor.

  • Grass: Tera Grass gives Toxapex an important Ground resistance while still preforming well against Urshifu-R, with the bonus of stopping Breloom's Spore.

  • Poison: Besides making Toxapex far less vulnerable to Electric, which Chien-Pao often Terastallizes into, Tera Poison retains the ability to restore health with Black Sludge.

  • Normal: While Normal isn't an impressive defensive type, Tera Normal can punish Choice locked Ghost-types, such as Flutter Mane and Gholdengo.

  • Bug: While the Stealth Rock weakness can be an issue, Tera Bug is a niche way to resist Ground-type attacks while being neutral to both Ice- and Electric-type moves, unlike other methods.

  • Flying: Tera Flying not only protects Toxapex from its irritating Ground-type weakness but also means Fissure Dondozo will no longer pressure Toxapex. However, this typing makes Toxapex much worse into general offense.

Items

  • Mental Herb: With Mental Herb providing one-time protection from Taunt, Toxapex can surprise foes like Annihilape and Serperior with Toxic, which is especially helpful if not running an attack. It also provides some cushioning against common Encore users like Dragonite and Primarina.

  • Black Sludge versus Leftovers: Having passive healing is wonderful, especially with Baneful Bunker. Black Sludge is a clever way to get around Item Clause, but Leftovers gives Toxapex less drawback when using Tera types that aren't Poison.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet makes Toxapex a superb response to Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, and generally lets it punish common users of contact moves like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S.

Physical Wall.description: Toxapex leverages its high defensive stats and plethora of useful utility moves to act as a stout defensive wall and disruptor. Prankster + Haze lets Toxapex shut down threatening setup sweepers such as Ogerpon-Wellspring, Manaphy, and Stored Power Iron Crown. Corrosion + Toxic gives Toxapex the ability to punish Steel-types such as Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Desolate Land Heatran, which can otherwise shrug off Toxapex's attacks, while Toxic Spikes can pressure more offensively oriented teams lacking their own Poison-type. Chilling Water deters physical attackers such as Iron Hands and Great Tusk from switching into Toxapex, while Infestation can rack up chip damage on bulkier foes such as Corviknight and Empoleon. Black Sludge give Toxapex greater longevity, while Rocky Helmet punishes physical attackers such as Chien-Pao and Barraskewda, as well as general U-turn spam. Toxapex fits best on stall teams due to its passivity and ability to check setup sweepers that could potentially run rampant. Certain wallbreakers such as Iron Boulder, Garchomp, and Iron Hands are able to power through Toxapex, so teammates that can check these such as Great Tusk and Corviknight are greatly appreciated; Toxapex can in return take on Chien-Pao and Fire-types such as Cinderace and Ogerpon-H. Toxapex is shocked by Electric- and Psychic-types such as Zapdos, Deoxys-S, and Azelf, so teammates that can reliably take these on such as Hisuian Goodra, Mandibuzz, and Meloetta are helpful.

Physically Defensive (Water).description: Toxapex is an incredible asset to Water teams due to its great defensive profile and wide range of utility options. Scald burns physical attackers such as Dragonite and Mega Lopunny, as well as Garchomp and Mega Gallade attempting to switch in. Poison Jab threatens Fairy- and Grass-types like Tapu Bulu, Iron Valiant, and Rillaboom. Toxic Spikes enhances offensive teammates such as Barraskewda, Mega Swampert, and Greninja, while Toxic lessens Toxapex's passivity, putting Gastrodon, Tornadus-T, and Mega Altaria on a timer. Haze allows Toxapex to shut down setup sweepers like Mega Scizor, Mimikyu, and Mega Altaria. Knock Off bothers item-reliant walls such as Porygon2, Galarian Corsola, and Celesteela. Black Sludge allows Toxapex to outlast tankier foes with the help of chip damage from Toxic Spikes and Toxic, while Heavy-Duty Boots enables it as a pivot, letting it sponge attacks without worrying about entry hazards. Teammates appreciate Toxapex absorbing Toxic Spikes and fighting off Grass-types like Meowscarada and Breloom. Toxapex appreciates Slowking and Rotom-W taking Psychic- and Ground-type moves, respectively. Mega Swampert switches into Electric-types like Tapu Koko, Zapdos, and Magnezone and threatens Poison-types like opposing Toxapex, Clodsire, and Nidoking. Gastrodon forms a great defensive core with Toxapex, taking on the aforementioned Electric-types and providing entry hazards to further chip down pivots such as Meowscarada, Mega Lopunny, and Iron Moth. Greninja checks Ground-types like Clodsire, Garchomp, and Landorus and aids in the Flying matchup. Urshifu-R checks Pokemon like Kyurem and Hydreigon, which take advantage of Toxapex. Pelipper provides a Ground immunity against Landorus-T, Iron Treads, and Great Tusk and synergizes well with Toxapex against Grass teams.

Z-Haze (Poison).description: Toxapex is a main-stay on Poison teams due to its defensive typing, impeccable ability, ridiculous bulk, and utility moves like Toxic, Knock Off, and Haze. Scald allows Toxapex to spread burns on physical attackers such as Landorus-T, Dragonite, and Mega Scizor. Toxic puts threats like Rotom-W, Baxcalibur, and Urshifu-R on a timer and spreads chip damage on offensive teams like Dragon, Psychic, and Fire. Knock Off is another great option to bother Pokemon like Galarian Corsola and Celesteela. Haze, paired with Icium Z, shuts down setup sweepers like Z-Happy Hour Jirachi and Clangorous Soulblaze Kommo-o, immediately regaining its health to continue walling them. Toxic Spikes are an option instead of Toxic or Knock Off; however, Toxapex has other teammates capable of setting them up and it increases Toxapex's passivity. The given EV spread avoids an OHKO from +1 SpA Jirachi's Psychic, allowing Toxapex to activate its Z-Crystal. Mega Venusaur and Crobat are excellent teammates due to their Ground-type neutrality and immunity, respectively, checking Landorus-T, Great Tusk, and Mamoswine, while the former also threatens Ferrothorn with Hidden Power Fire. Due to Toxapex's Psychic-type weakness, Alolan Muk and Galarian Slowking are notable teammates, checking Tapu Lele, Deoxys-S, and Latias; Galarian Slowking, in particular, forms a very strong Regenerator core with Toxapex. Clodsire and Nidoking patch up Toxapex's Electric-type weakness, and Nidoking specifically threatens Steel teams with its wide array of coverage. Galarian Weezing provides another Ground-type immunity and removes entry hazards with Defog as well as serving as a concrete answer to Baxcalibur. Sneasler appreciates Toxapex's ability to chip down foes, offering more opportunities for setup. Iron Moth threatens Steel-types like Celesteela, Ferrothorn, and Gholdengo, which are otherwise difficult to break for Poison teams.

lc.overview: With access to excellent coverage moves and a sky-high Attack stat, Mudbray possesses the tools required to be a threat offensively. This enables Mudbray to trade damage well with opposing Pokemon once it comes on the field. Additionally, owing to an excellent defensive ability in Stamina paired with solid defensive stats, Mudbray is one of the best entry hazard setters and defensive Pokemon in Little Cup.
lc.comments:
Other Options

Mudbray can run Heavy Slam as a coverage move instead of Stone Edge to reliably threaten Vullaby, since it has better accuracy, though it has a smaller damage output. When paired with Grookey, whose Grassy Terrain halves the power of Earthquake, Mudbray can run High Horsepower as an alternate move. Counter is a niche option for Mudbray to deal double damage against foes that hit it with strong physical attacks. Choice Scarf is also an option for Mudbray, since it boasts high Attack, can outspeed the entire unboosted metagame, and, notably, Speed ties Choice Scarf Gothita. It is wise to run Tera Ground on a Choice Scarf set, as Earthquake is the most reliable move Mudbray has. RestTalk is a set that trades immediate offensive pressure for longevity. The plan for RestTalk Mudbray is to get rid of opposing special attackers and rely on Stamina to make it resilient to physical attackers. Both RestTalk and Choice Scarf sets forego Stealth Rock, which forces the team to either sacrifice entry hazards or add another teammate with access to them.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Pokemon like Toedscool, Grookey, Foongus, and Chespin can switch into Mudbray with ease, resist Earthquake, and threaten back with Grass-type attacks.

Water-types: Chinchou and Wingull are massive threats, as they outspeed Mudbray and threaten it with super effective Water-type attacks.

Mudbray: Both teams using their Mudbray to trade damage is a common occurence in the Little Cup metagame. It is important to note that Mudbray can only act as a check to any opposing Mudbray and only one party stands to gain from such a trade. Before using Mudbray to check the opposing Mudbray, keep in mind that it has to check multiple targets, and without a reliable recovery option, chip damage from Pokemon like Vullaby will prevent it from doing so.

Offensive Stealth Rock.description:
Mudbray is a reliable Stealth Rock setter that doubles as a sturdy physical tank. Earthquake is the strongest and most consistent STAB move, hitting majority of the tier hard and threatening OHKOs on Pokemon like Glimmet, Mareanie, and Tinkatink. Stone Edge covers the Flying-types such as Vullaby and Wingull that would otherwise be immune to Earthquake. Close Combat provides coverage against foes that resist Mudbray's primary moves such as Toedscool and Grookey. Roar allows Mudbray to phaze out setup sweepers like Nasty Plot Vullaby. An Impish nature is preferred for extra physical durability, but an Adamant nature can be used for greater offensive presence. Tera Steel improves its matchup against Grass- and Ice-type attacks such as Giga Drain from Foongus and Toedscool and Triple Axel from Alolan Sandshrew, as well as Brave Bird from Vullaby. Tera Water helps Mudbray resist Water- and Ice-type attacks such as Hydro Pump and Surf from Chinchou and Wingull, respectively, while allowing Mudbray to survive Flare Blitz from Hisuian Growlithe in a pinch.

Mudbray can switch into Elekid and Stunky and tank multiple hits while threatening an OHKO with Earthquake. Mudbray has to be wary of Vullaby, which aims to remove Mudbray's Eviolite with Knock Off and then either pivot out with U-turn or damage Mudbray with Brave Bird. Vullaby can do this knowing that it only gets 2HKOed by Stone Edge. Vullaby itself pairs seamlessly with Mudbray, as it can cover Grass-types like Grookey, Toedscool, Foongus, and Chespin that check Mudbray. In exchange, Mudbray handles Rock- and Steel-types like Tinkatink and Glimmet that cause Vullaby trouble. Foongus is another great partner that can take care of Water-types for Mudbray, and in return, Mudbray can handle Steel- and Poison-types that wall Foongus, including Tinkatink and Stunky. Alolan Diglett and Mudbray combine to become a formidable Ground-type spam core that pressures each others checks. Mudbray can tank hits and Alolan Diglett is fast and runs Life Orb for heavy damage output.

Physical Wall.description:
With a great ability in Stamina and access to helpful utility moves such as Stealth Rock and Roar, Mudsdale cements itself as a helpful wall in PU that keeps physically offensive Pokemon like Paldean Tauros-F, Pawmot, and Rhydon in check. Body Press lets Mudsdale put Stamina to good use, allowing it to get decent damage off on Scrafty, Wo-Chien, and Hisuian Avalugg. Heavy Slam, on the other hand, hits Flying-types and Heracross neutrally while also letting Mudsdale hit Fairy-types that could otherwise easily set up in front of it like Florges and Alolan Ninetales. However, Stone Edge hits Flying-types like Bombirdier and Cramorant super effectively while also threatening Rotom-Heat. Roar deters setup sweepers like Bulk Up Scrafty, Hariyama, and Calm Mind Galarian Slowbro before they get out of hand. Leftovers improves Mudsdale's longevity, while Rocky Helmet punishes physical attackers like Heracross. Tera Water allows Mudsdale to deal with Fire- and Water-type wallbreakers like Salazzle, Bruxish, and Tatsugiri in a pinch, but it can no longer check Pawmot as easily as before. On the other hand, Tera Steel grants Mudsdale the ability to check Florges, boosts Heavy Slam's damage output, and helps its matchup versus Mesprit and Alolan Ninetales. However, this leaves Mudsdale open to being preyed on by Ground-, Fire-, and Fighting-types like Golurk, Emboar, and Heracross, which it checked beforehand.

When paired with a specially defensive Pokemon like Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro, Milotic, or Snorlax, Mudsdale can form a strong defensive core that's quite difficult to break through. These Pokemon are all also capable of pressuring Rotom-Heat, which is notable, since Mudsdale is unable to consistently block its Volt Switch. Mudsdale easily checks Fire- and Fighting-types like Paldean Tauros-F and Scrafty, so Pokemon weak to those types like Rotom-Mow, Hisuian Decidueye, and Hoopa can take advantage of its defensive capabilities. Mudsdale tends to falter against Water- and Grass-types like Tatsugiri and Rotom-Mow, making partners that can take on these threats like Milotic, Wo-Chien, and Amoonguss strong defensive options. With Mudsdale's lack of reliable recovery, it greatly appreciates Wish support from Pokemon like Florges to circumvent this issue. Entry hazards also highlight Mudsdale's lack of reliable recovery, so partners like Defog Cramorant and Rapid Spin Alolan Sandslash help work around this weakness.

Substitute.description: The EV spread allows Araquanid's Substitute to not be broken by Palossand's Shadow Ball, ensures it outpaces Chansey, and maximizes Attack.

Sticky Web.description:
Araquanid carves a niche as one of the tier's reliable Sticky Web user due to its good typing, serviceable bulk, and amazing offensive and defensive matchups against notable threats to Sticky Web teams such as Iron Moth, Iron Treads, and Cinderace while still matching up well against Great Tusk, similar to Ribombee. Surf is not only a very consistent STAB move for reliable damage, but it also prevents Glimmora from setting up Toxic Spikes via Toxic Debris and allows Araquanid to deal with Taunt Landorus-T that might try to prevent Araquanid from setting Sticky Web. With Endeavor, Araquanid can chip the notable Water-type checks of the tier like Ogerpon-W and Primarina, and using it with Custap Berry allows Araquanid to deal sudden damage to threatening sweepers such as Kyurem and Dragonite before being KOed. Endure can be used to activate Custap Berry more consistently in the face of counter leads such as Raging Bolt and powerful Choice Band users such as Rillaboom and Zamazenta, while Lunge prevents foes like Dragonite from using it as setup fodder while dealing strong damage against anti-leads like Ogerpon-W and foes like Hisuian Samurott. Mirror Coat can alternatively be opted for to deal massive damage to special attackers such as Zapdos and Raging Bolt, and Leech Life is a similar option to Lunge to deal with opposing leads, trading a helpful Attack drop for some much-appreciated recovery. Custap Berry almost guarantees that Araquanid will find an additional turn on lead to compensate for its low Speed and is the preferred item on Endure variants. Mental Herb is an alternative that ensures Araquanid can set up Sticky Web in the face of Taunt users like Landorus-T and Deoxys-S. Red Card uses its bulk to phaze setup sweepers like Dragonite and Darkrai. 40 Defense EVs and maximum HP investment guarantees Araquanid will take two Ceaseless Edges from Hisuian Samurott, with the rest of its remaining EVs in Special Attack allowing Araquanid to 2HKO physically defensive Hatterene with Surf even after Leftovers recovery, preventing it from blocking Sticky Web via Magic Bounce safely. A Quiet nature should only be used on Lunge variants. An alternative and more defensive EV spread of 252 HP / 4 Atk / 136 Def / 4 SpA / 112 SpD with a Sassy nature is also an option; this specially defensive spread allows it to survive a Thunderbolt from Protosynthesis Raging Bolt, 2HKO Ogerpon-W with Lunge, and OHKO offensive Great Tusk with Surf. Araquanid can also invest 28 EVs into Speed to outpace Ting-Lu. Alternatively, sets with a Speed-lowering nature can drop their Speed IVs to 28 to underspeed Garganacl and Toxapex, allowing Araquanid to weaken them with Endeavor after they use Recover just before it faints to Salt Cure or Toxic. Although Terastallizing Araquanid should generally be avoided in order to preserve Terastallization for offensive teammates that generally take advantage of it more, Tera Ghost allows Araquanid to spinblock Iron Treads and Great Tusk in emergencies to guarantee Sticky Web stays up and also allows Araquanid to get a guaranteed Endeavor off against Extreme Speed Dragonite if it is in Custap Berry activation range.

Araquanid has found its home as a reliable entry hazard setter on Sticky Web hyper offense teams, and as such, setup sweepers with middling Speed tiers greatly appreciate its presence. Gholdengo is an almost-required teammate on such structures and allows Sticky Web teams to block hazard removal from Rapid Spin, Glimmora's Mortal Spin, and Defog thanks to its ability. Gholdengo is also invaluable in dismantling the bulkier team structures that hyper offense teams in general struggle against greatly. Other Ghost-types such as Pecharunt and Ceruledge also block Rapid Spin attempts, with Pecharunt's bulk proving valuable against the likes of Zamazenta and Ogerpon-W, while Ceruledge offers extra speed support thanks to Weak Armor. Setup sweepers with middling Speed tiers such as Attack Booster Energy Great Tusk, Raging Bolt, and Meteor Beam Glimmora also pair excellently with Araquanid. Great Tusk’s hazard removal can allow Araquanid to come in multiple times per match, and its typing allows for it to check anti-leads to Araquanid, namely Raging Bolt. Iron Treads can also be considered on Sticky Web teams heavily weak to Raging Bolt. Meteor Beam Glimmora can assist Sticky Web structures by absorbing Toxic Spikes and setting Stealth Rock for its teammates while also still maintaining heavy offensive pressure. Iron Moth is another potent sweeper that Sticky Web teams can employ, as Sticky Web being set up lets Iron Moth run maximum Special Attack investment and a Modest nature, granting it a Special Attack boost from its Booster Energy and allowing it to do more consistent damage even without boosts from Fiery Dance. Kingambit can also take great advantage of Sticky Web, as it allows for Kingambit to get the jump on opposing Jolly Kingambit and, if Kingambit itself opts to run a Jolly nature, maximum Speed Great Tusk without Heavy-Duty Boots. Ogerpon-W is excellent on Sticky Web teams, as with Swords Dance and an Adamant nature, which it can now run thanks to Araquanid relieving it from the pressure of Speed ties with opposing Ogerpon-W, it forms a strong core with Gholdengo that can throttle the bulkier team structures that hyper offense teams tend to struggle with.
The Speed EVs help to outpace Vaporeon.

Sticky Web Setter.description: Araquanid establishes itself as one of the best Sticky Web setters in the tier, finding a niche in the metagame by means of leveraging its wide support movepool to disrupt other leads and ability to threaten one of the best forms of entry hazard removal in Excadrill. When paired with Custap Berry, Endure guarantees the setting of Sticky Web, even in the face of Mega Aerodactyl and Choice Band Rillaboom threatening an OHKO. Toxic ensures Araquanid cannot be hard walled by Water-type Pokemon, namely Slowbro and Volcanion, which it would otherwise not be able to do damage to. Pounce is another option to slow down faster lead Pokemon for its teammates to exploit. Endeavor pairs nicely with Endure and Custap Berry, putting an opposing Pokemon in range to be picked off by a teammate like Aegislash and Scizor. Magic Coat turns the tables on foes like Mew attempting to either disrupt Araquanid with Taunt, preventing Sticky Web from going up, or Pokemon like Clefable and Hippowdon attempting to set up hazards. Mental Herb can be used over Custap Berry to flip the matchup against Taunt users like Mew and Serperior attempting to shut down the usage of Sticky Web. 252 HP EVs paired with 228 Defense EVs and an Impish nature allow for Araquanid to live Adamant Tyranitar's Stone Edge. Araquanid is best utilized on hyper offense teams, with Sticky Web facilitating setup sweepers and wallbreakers such as Iron Moth, Iron Boulder, Galarian Moltres, and Blacephalon by means of allowing them to outspeed faster foes and limiting opportunities to revenge kill its teammates. Serperior and Bisharp are great partners, either deterring the usage of Defog or exploiting the activation of their respective abilities to start snowballing. Ghost-types like Air Balloon Aegislash and Ghostium Z Pecharunt work as spinblockers against Excadrill, while Sticky Web makes up for their lackluster Speed stats. Mega Aerodactyl and Heavy-Duty Boots Zeraora are immune to Sticky Web, so checks for them are mandatory; Celesteela, Scizor, and Booster Energy Speed Iron Crown work well against Mega Aerodctyl, while Serperior, Rillaboom, and Sinistcha can handle Zeraora.

Sticky Web (Bug).description: Araquanid is the best defensive Sticky Web setter and a staple on Bug teams, as its ability Water Bubble combined with its high Special Defense gives it valuable defensive utility against Fire-types and special attackers. Liquidation threatens Fire- and Ground-types as well as physically frail Pokemon that don't resist Water like Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Sneasler. Toxic punishes bulky switch-ins like Mantine, Rotom-W, Porygon2, and Volcanion. Magic Coat counters entry hazards and status spread from Pokemon like Shuckle, Celesteela, and Klefki that will attempt to exploit Araquanid's passivity. Leech Life is a niche option that gives Araquanid minor recovery and threatens Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Hydreigon, Latios, and Latias. Mirror Coat is an option for Water-resistant foes and omniboost sweepers like Pelipper, Kommo-o, and Hisuian Zoroark, as Araquanid can comfortably take an attack and OHKO them in return. The given EV spread maximizes Araquanid's bulk while also outspeeding base 50 Speed Pokemon with no investment like Ursaluna, Ting-Lu, Hippowdon, and Alolan Muk, which are all threatened by Liquidation. Araquanid synergizes best with teammates that utilize the speed control Sticky Web provides and appreciate the elimination of Pokemon it counters. Volcarona greatly benefits from the removal of Fire-types like Heatran and Victini, making the opening for a sweep easier. With the Sticky Web speed decrease, Volcarona is able to outspeed its checks after only one Quiver Dance and deals with the Grass and Electric types Araquanid is countered by. Choice Scarf Kleavor is a great Stealth Rock setter that takes out Hisuian Arcanine, provides momentum with U-turn, and benefits from Sticky Web. Strong physical attackers like Heracross, Scizor, and Mega Pinsir break walls that Araquanid can't touch like Toxapex, Tapu Fini, and Ferrothorn; they also excel with Sticky Web support, letting them set up and outspeed their checks like Kyurem, Ceruledge, and Tapu Lele.

Sticky Web.description:
Araquanid functions as the tier's premier Sticky Web setter, leveraging its good natural bulk and access to Magic Coat to reliably get up Sticky Web while also denying entry hazards. Surf is usually used in order to OHKO Landorus-T and Great Tusk, preventing the latter from removing Sticky Web, while Liquidation hits Ting-Lu and Gliscor for greater damage. Bug Buzz and Leech Life are also both options in order to hit Ogerpon-W, which would otherwise use Araquanid as setup fodder and can give Sticky Web teams some trouble otherwise. Endure combines well with Custap Berry, allowing Araquanid to get an extra hit off on foes or potentially get Sticky Web up again against Rapid Spin or Defog users such as Great Tusk and Landorus-T. Endeavor is also an option, pairing well with Endure and Custap Berry to bring foes that resist Araquanid's Water-type attacks, such as Ferrothorn and Kyurem, down to low HP. Magic Coat is used in order to prevent hazards from foes such as Ting-Lu and Ferrothorn while also stopping Taunt from foes such as Landorus-T. 40 Defense EVs allow Araquanid to survive two of Jolly Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edges from full health.

Araquanid fits solely on Sticky Web hyper offense structures. Slower wallbreakers such as Raging Bolt and Hisuian Samurott appreciate Araquanid's Sticky Web compensating for their below-average Speed stats, letting them outspeed and threaten foes such as Iron Valiant and Zamazenta. Gholdengo blocks Rapid Spin and Defog, helping to keep Sticky Web up, and benefits from Sticky Web allowing it to sweep with Nasty Plot more easily. Other setup sweepers such as Ogerpon-W and Great Tusk also appreciate the Sticky Web support Araquanid provides, preventing Pokemon such as Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant from revenge killing them as easily. As Araquanid often struggles to get Sticky Web up in the face of Mega Diancie, Flying-types such as Tornadus-T, Electric-types such as Tapu Koko, and Steel-types such as the aforementioned Gholdengo and Mega Scizor are appreciated. In return, they benefit from Sticky Web slowing down foes such as Heatran and Hisuian Samurott while also appreciating Araquanid providing a switch-in against Fire-type foes such as Heatran, Volcarona, and Cinderace.

Sticky Web (Bug).description:
Araquanid makes for a good Sticky Web setter for Bug teams due to having more bulk than other Sticky Web setters, such as Galvantula and Ribombee, as well as being a huge asset to Bug teams with its Water Bubble ability, resisting Fire-type moves and hitting Fire-type Pokemon super effectively. Liquidation is a strong STAB move capable of 2HKOing common entry hazard removers such as Great Tusk and Iron Treads. Infestation helps trap and check Pokemon, such as Ting Lu and Klefki. Mirror Coat is used to take advantage of Araquanid's naturally good special bulk to OHKO threats such as Raging Bolt and Zapdos.

Choice Scarf Kleavor is a great teammate for Araquanid because it can deal with Fire- and Flying-types such as Ogerpon-H, Moltres, and Articuno. Kleavor's Stone Axe also synergizes nicely with Araquanid’s Sticky Web, as more entry hazards further help the sweepers and wallbreakers on the team while also breaking Ceruledge's Focus Sash, which would otherwise be a huge problem for Bug teams. Scizor is another great teammate for Araquanid, as Sticky Web enables it to set up with Swords Dance easier and also allows it to take out Iron Treads Bisharp, and Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine. Volcarona also benefits from Sticky Web, as it outspeeds faster threats like Greninja and Iron Valiant at -1. Slither Wing and Lokix both appreciate Sticky Web, as it helps them revenge kill faster threats such as Gholdengo, Ogerpon-H, and Hisuian Arcanine. Forretress provides a strong physical wall on Bug teams, removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin, and is a slow pivot for Araquanid with Volt Switch to ensure its safe entry so it can repeatedly set up Sticky Web if needed.

Choice Band (Bug).description: This is a winning set from the Monotype Rising sets project. This will be updated as we work on new analyses. Stay tuned!

zu.overview: Lurantis differentiates itself from other entry hazard removal options, since if it's let ignored, it can quickly spiral out of control and become difficult to switch into or take a hit from thanks to Contrary boosting Lurantis's stats as it goes for Leaf Storm and Superpower, which together allow Lurantis to tear through all hazard setters, including Regirock, Orthworm, and Sandslash. It also finds ample opportunities to come in with its mono-Grass typing, helping it switch in against common threats such as Jolteon, Rotom-Mow, Lanturn, and Whimsicott. However, these moves along with Synthesis come with low PP, often leading to Lurantis being stalled out by walls like Articuno and Dipplin, and Lurantis is not as offensive as it wishes to be without prior boosts. Even with its good resistances, Lurantis can find itself overwhelmed if it's being attacked on the defensive stat that it didn't invest in. For example, Snorlax can 2HKO specially defensive Lurantis with Heat Crash, and physically defensive Lurantis is vulnerable to Whimsicott due to how its Choice Specs Moonblast always nets a 2HKO. On top of that, its typing also lets it down quite often when facing down many top threats, such as Charizard, Hisuian Sneasel, and Vikavolt, and Lurantis can be forced to heal constantly with how easily it's chipped down by switching into foes that often use pivoting moves like Rotom-Mow, Lanturn, and Jolteon.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Lurantis can forgo Defog for Knock Off, which allows it to simultaneously threaten common switch-ins to it like Charizard while still threatening entry hazard setters such as Orthworm. However, with the limited options for entry hazard removal in ZU, having to burden another teammate with that role is often impractical.

Checks and Counters

Vikavolt: Vikavolt resists both Leaf Storm and Superpower from Lurantis, granting it plenty of opportunities to switch in. From there, Vikavolt threatens Lurantis with its STAB Bug Buzz; can keep up the momentum with Volt Switch as Lurantis switches out, simultaneously accruing chip damage; and can set Sticky Web up on Lurantis every time it comes in, effectively ignoring its Defog. Vikavolt is weak to entry hazards, though, so if Lurantis can catch Vikavolt switching in with a Knock Off, then Vikavolt gets a limit on the number of times it can switch in with Stealth Rock up.

Fire-types: Charizard, Oricorio-F, and Typhlosion all are very threatening to Lurantis, especially the former two due to how they resist both Leaf Storm and Superpower. However, these Fire-types are quite vulnerable to Knock Off with how weak they are to Stealth Rock.

Ice-types: Abomasnow and Beartic are fairly common, and both outspeed Lurantis, threatening it with their Blizzard and Icicle Crash, respectively. Not only that, but they can capitalize on Lurantis switching out with status moves such as Aurora Veil and Swords Dance. Similarly, Sneasel can also take advantage of switches with Swords Dance, but it can also force progress through powerful attacks. Froslass is quite problematic, too, as it's a hazard setter that beats Lurantis and can cripple it along with any other switch-ins with status via Will-O-Wisp and deny Defog with Taunt. On top of that, Articuno and its Pressure can easily PP stall Lurantis out of all of its attacks if it isn't careful. However, when these Ice-type foes switch in, they must be cautious of not getting hit by a Superpower or Knock Off.

Poison-types: Hisuian Sneasel and Muk can take all of Lurantis's attacks without issue, and the latter doesn't mind Knock Off thanks to Sticky Hold. Additionally, they all easily spread poison, which forces Lurantis to become even more passive than it would be otherwise because it now needs to constantly heal with Synthesis on top of clearing hazards. This can often force Lurantis to Terastallize into the Poison-type, depriving its teammates of that resource. Against Weezing, though, Lurantis has a fighting chance with Weezing's low Special Defense and lack of reliable recovery, making it vulnerable to being worn down by Leaf Storm.

Grass-types: With how Lurantis relies on Leaf Storm for damage most of the time, other Grass-types that don't mind Knock Off or Superpower can use Lurantis as a switch-in. This often leads to Lurantis having to switch out so that its team can deal with an opposing Whimsicott, Dipplin, or Shaymin, the latter two of which can heal off any chip damage Lurantis may deal to them. Dipplin is especially troiublesome, since it can simply phaze Lurantis and put its Contrary boosts to waste.

Defog.description:
Thanks to Lurantis's decent defenses, good resistances, lack of passivity thanks to Contrary, and positive matchups against common entry hazard setters like Regirock and Sandslash, it makes for a fine hazard remover with Defog. Superpower complements Leaf Storm quite well, both helping to overpower walls and nailing switch-ins to Lurantis like Abomasnow, Magneton, and Snorlax, and the Defense boost it offers also helps with Lurantis's longevity and survivability. However, Knock Off allows Lurantis to better punish more offensive foes like Charizard, Vikavolt, and Oricorio-F. With Contrary, Lurantis circumvents the issues of other walls like Orthworm, Lanturn, and Weezing, able to become a threat in its own right with the offensive boosts from Leaf Storm and Superpower. Lurantis's EV spread can go in either a specially defensive direction or a physically defensive one. Becoming specially bulky allows Lurantis to better stomach attacks from Clawitzer, Magneton, and Whimsicott. Alternatively, a physically defensive spread lets Lurantis handle physical attackers like Basculin and Sandslash more easily. Tera Poison offers Lurantis many useful resistances, namely to Fighting, Fairy, and Poison. This newfound defensive profile allows Lurantis to more comfortably handle Poison-types such as Hisuian Sneasel, Muk, and Weezing while improving its matchup against Whimsicott, making it able to stomach Moonblast better. By becoming a Poison-type, Lurantis can act as a Fighting-type check, switching into Passimian and Hitmontop while doubling as a Toxic Spikes absorber, aiding its team against users like Weezing. Tera Poison also sheds Lurantis's weakness to Ice-type attacks, meaning Lurantis can take out foes such as Abomasnow and Beartic when they have low health in a pinch, though Tera Poison ruins Lurantis's matchup against Mesprit.

Lurantis mainly offers Defog support, and it's often lacking in the bulk department, meaning it needs teammates that can better handle attacks than it can, as well as offensive partners that don't need entry hazards to break through the walls that it's bound to bring in. Offensive pivots such as Basculin, Jolteon, and Passimian appreciate Lurantis keeping hazards off the field, allowing them to continually switch in and pressure walls that Lurantis calls in like Muk and Dipplin. Charizard, Oricorio-F, and Vikavolt are notable for having great synergy with Lurantis, handling the pesky Ice-, Steel-, and Grass-types that give Lurantis trouble, like Articuno, Orthworm, and Dipplin. In return, Lurantis takes out counters to them, namely Regirock, Lanturn, and, with Superpower, Magneton. On top of that, Lurantis's Defog aids these three if they happen to lose their Heavy-Duty Boots due to Knock Off. Lurantis is also quite weak to opposing Oricorio-F and Charizard, so partners like Lanturn, Snorlax, and Regirock pair well with it. In a similar vein, Pokemon such as Poliwrath and Orthworm are good teammates to fend off Ice-type foes like Sneasel and Beartic. Lurantis capitalizing on the top bulky Water-type in Lanturn opens many doors for teammates like Lycanroc, Sneasel, and Clawitzer. Stealth Rock users such as Regirock, Mesprit, and Sandslash pair best with Lurantis, as its Defog isn't as detrimental as it would be on Spikes-stacking teams, and unlike spinners like Hitmontop and Sandslash, Lurantis can still clear hazards in front of Ghost-types like Mismagius and Spiritomb. Poison-types like Muk, Weezing, and Hisuian Sneasel are quite common and very problematic for Luranatis. This often leads it to pairing up with Pokemon like Sandslash, its own Hisuian Sneasel, Mesprit, and Spiritomb. Lurantis is easily taken advantage of by other Grass-types like Whimsicott, Dipplin, and Virizion; for this reason, it synergizes with Pokemon such as Charizard and Weezing.

Special Attacker.description:
Salandit is a strong special attacker due to its solid offensive typing combination and respectable 18 Speed, outpacing and maiming balance pieces like Mienfoo, Vullaby, and Mudbray with its powerful moves in Fire Blast and Sludge Wave. For checks that Salandit does not immediately threaten with its STAB attacks, such as Mareanie and Glimmet, it can break through with Tera Blast. Tera Ground also lets Salandit OHKO Stunky and Chinchou after entry hazard chip damage, though it risks a Speed tie with the former if it does not have Substitute up. Meanwhile, Tera Psychic lets Salandit OHKO Mienfoo and survive Gothita's Psychic. Protect and Substitute give Salandit the chance to scout for defensive Tera types. Protect also shields Salandit from Mienfoo's Fake Out, while Substitute lets Salandit set up if foes switch out. With 3 IVs and no EVs in HP, Salandit takes less damage from Life Orb recoil and Stealth Rock.

Salandit, among other offensive Fire-types, makes a great wallbreaker and cleaner on balance and bulky offense teams that benefit from its ability to pressure Foongus and deal massive neutral damage to metagame staples like Vullaby and Mienfoo. Since Salandit is frail, it appreciates the defensive support balance teams provide. Tinkatink, Toedscool, and Mareanie make a great defensive core to pair with Salandit. Tinkatink can switch in on Vullaby and set Stealth Rock. Toedscool is Ground-resistant and Electric-immune, giving Salandit an out against Mudbray, Alolan Diglett, Elekid, and Chinchou while also providing valuable hazard removal to improve Salandit's longevity. Finally, Mareanie can switch in on Mienfoo and Stunky, common checks that can shut down Salandit with Knock Off. Salandit has trouble breaking through foes that resist its STAB moves and its Speed lags behind that of other fast attackers. Thus, Salandit pairs well with trappers like Gothita and Trapinch. Trapinch can switch in and trap Glimmet and Elekid, a wall and a fast threat, respectively. Meanwhile, Gothita can trap and KO bulky checks like Mareanie and Mienfoo as well as fast attackers like Wingull and a chipped Elekid. Mudbray also makes a more versatile teammate, as it can switch in on Glimmet and Elekid while setting Stealth Rock or threatening massive damage.

Nasty Plot.description:
Nasty Plot Salazzle is one of PU's most threatening setup sweepers and wallbreakers thanks to its great STAB combo, ability to outspeed naturally fast attackers such as Zoroark and Ambipom, and wide variety of utility moves to benefit its sweep. Fire Blast's higher Base Power gives Salazzle an easier time breaking through foes like defensive Bombirdier, but Flamethrower's higher accuracy makes it more reliable. Salazzle's final moveslot is very flexible; Encore can turn opposing setup sweepers like Scrafty and walls such as Florges and Lanturn into setup fodder and potentially deter them. Toxic cripples potential switch-ins like Rhydon and Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro as well as the aforementioned setup sweepers and walls. Finally, Endeavor is an option on Focus Sash variants to immediately bring foes like Milotic to low health, thus opening up Salazzle's teammates. Substitute is a potential option to capitalize on the switches Salazzle forces on Pokemon like Wo-Chien and Alolan Sandslash, letting it either set up safely or fire off a strong attack. Like Encore, it also allows Salazzle to work around its mediocre bulk. Focus Sash gives Salazzle an easier time setting up and securing KOes and lets it serve as an emergency check to a threat like Choice Scarf Heracross. It should only be used on hyper offense teams, since other playstyles are more likely to let entry hazards go up and ruin Salazzle. Tera Dark allows Salazzle to gain a valuable defensive typing, allowing it to more easily set up on Psychic-types like Delphox and Hoopa. Alternatively, Tera Steel lets Salazzle keep its Fairy resistance while also guarding it against Psychic-type moves. Tera Ghost also provides Salazzle setup opportunities—particularly against Choice-locked Fighting-types like Paldean Tauros-F and Emboar—and can allow it to be immune to priority from Ambipom, although it comes at a cost of being weak to other priority such as Sucker Punch from Bombirdier and Skuntank.

Nasty Plot Salazzle finds itself on offense and hyper offense teams as well as on balance teams looking for a reliable wincon and attacker that can be valuable before setting up by spreading Toxic or enabling other setup sweepers with Encore.
