While strong, Salazzle can find itself struggling to break against offensive and defensive Water-types like Milotic and Cramorant, so checks to these threats like Shaymin and Rotom-Mow make good partners. In return, Salazzle can aid these Pokemon by chipping down their checks like Galarian Slowbro and Wo-Chien. Salazzle's relative frailty means that slow pivots like Bombirdier and Hisuian Decidueye that can sponge a hit for it and bring it onto the battlefield safely are also valued. Other offensive teammates that can struggle to reliably break through Water-types like Rhydon and Sneasel can form a solid backbone with Salazzle, as they work together to take down their shared checks. Although fast, Salazzle itself can still be revenge killed by faster threats such as Jolteon and priority from Floatzel and Grimmsnarl; thus, checks to these threats such as Wo-Chien, Milotic, and Mudsdale all make good partners.

Utility.description:
With Salazzle's deep utility movepool, it can act as great support Pokemon that lacks passivity thanks to its high Speed and its nearly unresisted STAB combination's damage output. Fire Blast is preferred for pure damage, but Flamethrower can be used instead for higher accuracy. Toxic + Corrosion allow Salazzle to break through bulkier Pokemon in the tier that other Pokemon simply can't like Galarian Slowbro and Hisuian Qwilfish. Encore helps Salazzle take advantage of Pokemon that would otherwise wall it like Milotic and Mudsdale. Protect can be used to rack up additional Toxic damage on foes and scout what move Choice users like Bruxish go for. Knock Off is another option to cripple item-reliant Pokemon like Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro and Rhydon, and it also OHKOes Hoopa. Salazzle can viably run Substitute, in tandem with Protect and Leftovers, to try and stall teams out with its nigh-unblockable Toxic. Substitute + Toxic Salazzle is rather niche, though, since it relies on surprise factor and is more high-maintenance due to its crippling Stealth Rock weakness. Tera Dark makes it less easy for revenge killers like Sucker Punch Bombirdier, Shadow Sneak Hisuian Decidueye, and Choice Scarf Hoopa to pick Salazzle off. On the other hand, Tera Steel still helps out against Psychic-type attacks without leaving Salazzle weak to Choice Scarf Florges's Moonblast. Tera Ghost can also be used to ignore Fake Out and Facade from Ambipom and Heracross, respectively. In tandem with Encore, Tera Ghost can force these foes to continually do no damage to Salazzle, letting it attack freely.

Salazzle easily handles Steel-types like Alolan Sandslash and Orthworm, so Pokemon that are checked by these walls work well alongside it like Florges and Grimmsnarl. If running Knock Off, Salazzle can help to chip away at opposing teams alongside entry hazard setters like Rhydon, Alolan Sandslash, and Spikes Heracross. On top of this, Salazzle is also quite easily revenge killed by Choice Scarf users and naturally fast Pokemon like Bruxish, Paldean Tauros-F, and Hisuian Electrode, so walls like Palossand and Wo-Chien help it defensively.

nu.overview: The combination of Nasty Plot, a good typing both offensively and defensively, and solid Special Attack and Speed lets Salazzle carve out a niche in NU as a setup sweeper, and its typing gives it setup opportunities against Pokemon such as Sylveon, Heracross, and Brambleghast. It's also a very difficult Pokemon to switch into thanks to its high-Base Power STAB moves, such as Fire Blast and Overheat, and it can cripple its checks like Flygon and Swampert with Sludge Bomb's poison chance. Salazzle also has a very malleable Tera type selection, helping its team as much as possible while having a great disruptive movepool in Encore, Knock Off, and Toxic, allowing it to help its team as much as possible. However, Salazzle's reliance on prediction means finding setup opportunities is difficult. Its absurd frailty leaves it easily prone to priority moves such as Aqua Jet from Basculegion-M and Paldean Tauros-W, Shadow Sneak from Choice Band Brambleghast, and Sucker Punch from Toxicroak and Brute Bonnet. Furthermore, Salazzle's typing leaves it very vulnerable to common Pokemon like Flygon, Rhyperior, Munkidori, Vaporeon, and Swampert, all of which can also force it out if they are not poisoned by Sludge Bomb.
nu.comments:
Other Options

A utility set consisting of Fire Blast / Toxic / Sludge Bomb or Protect / Knock Off or Encore can be ran, but Salazzle's terrible bulk means finding opportunities to utilize Toxic is difficult, and Steel-types such as Copperajah are rarely staying in on it. Flamethrower is an alternative Fire-type STAB option that can be used over Fire Blast or Overheat for more consistency, but it fails to OHKO Bellibolt after Stealth Rock and lacks power overall. Tera Flying gives Salazzle an immunity to Earthquake and Spikes, but it is fairly one-dimensional compared to other Tera types, as it keeps Salazzle weak to Stealth Rock and does not provide the same useful defensive profile as Tera Grass or Tera Steel.

Checks and Counters

Ground-types: Flygon, Rhyperior, and Swampert can shrug off everything Salazzle throws at them and are able to threaten it back with their STAB Ground-type moves. They can force Salazzle out while setting up entry hazards, and Flygon and Rhyperior can set up against it. Swampert can also remove Salazzle's Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off, pressure it with Earthquake, or keep momentum with Flip Turn.

Water-types: Basculegion-M can switch in on Salazzle's STAB moves and can pivot out with Flip Turn or threaten it with Water-type STAB moves. Salazzle must also be wary of Vaporeon, which can handle its hits and can threaten it with either Scald for immediate damage or Flip Turn for momentum.

Faster Attackers: Due to Salazzle's absolutely awful defenses, it's easily prone to faster attackers and Choice Scarf users such as Chandelure, Flamigo, and Munkidori. The latter can threaten it with its Psychic-type STAB moves, while the former two can easily force it out. However, the latter two do not appreciate switching into its STAB-boosted Fire Blast.

Nasty Plot.description:
Set Details

Fire Blast is Salazzle's primary Fire-type STAB move for its sheer power, but Overheat is a stronger and more accurate alternative that can be run with the drawback of the Special Attack drop. Encore allows Salazzle to shut down opposing Wish users, namely Scream Tail and Vaporeon, while also punishing setup sweepers such as Flygon and Scrafty. Knock Off is another option that lets it punish common switch-ins such as Swampert, Incineroar, Basculegion-M, and Chansey by removing items like Leftovers, Heavy-Duty Boots, and Eviolite. Toxic is a reliable way of poisoning the Ground-, Water-, and Fire-type foes that try to switch in on Salazzle, including Rhyperior, Swampert, and Incineroar, and putting them on a timer. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Salazzle switch in without taking damage from entry hazards, especially Stealth Rock, but Salazzle is also able to run Focus Sash to have an easier time setting up if it is on a more offensive team. Tera Grass lets it resist Basculegion-M's Aqua Jet and Vaporeon's Flip Turn as well as Flygon's and Rhyperior's Earthquake. Tera Steel lets it keep its resistance to Fairy-type moves while also granting it a resistance to attacks such as Dudunsparce's Boomburst and Munkidori's STAB moves, as well as providing a resistance to Stealth Rock. Tera Dark improves Salazzle's matchups against the Psychic-types it struggles with, such as Meloetta and Munkidori.

Salazzle is a nice addition to offense and hyper offense teams, especially ones where its sweeping capabilities are heavily appreciated. Salazzle's ability to break through Steel- and Fairy-types like Copperajah, Bronzong, Sylveon, and Florges is appreciated by Cinccino, Scyther, Goodra, and Flygon. As Salazzle struggles to break through opposing special walls such as Goodra and Vaporeon, it benefits from physical attackers such as Basculegion-M, Brute Bonnet, Toxicroak, and Flamigo, which can break through these threats. Basculegion-M in particular is one of Salazzle's best partners; it is able to let Salazzle hit the field safely with a slow Flip Turn and can check the opposing Ground-types such as Gligar and Rhyperior that Salazzle struggles against. In return, Salazzle checks the Grass-types such as Brambleghast and Decidueye that Basculegion-M fails to deal with. Water-type wallbreakers, including Inteleon and Paldean Tauros-W, are complemented by Salazzle checking the aforementioned Grass-types, which they are unable to stay in against. Encore Salazzle further helps Pokemon like Flygon, Heracross, and Basculegion-M that struggle with Wish users such as Scream Tail, Sylveon, and Vaporeon. Dark-types, most notably Wo-Chien and Scrafty, are good pairings for it that can help check Meloetta and Munkidori, both of which force it out. Scrafty also admires Salazzle checking Sylveon, which it struggles against. If Salazzle is running Focus Sash, it benefits from entry hazard control from dedicated hyper offense leads, such as Taunt Infernape and Froslass as well as Tidy Up Cinccino. As a partner, Brambleghast checks the Ground- and Water-type wallbreakers that Salazzle can struggle against. In return, Salazzle is able to check Amoonguss, Wo-Chien, and Scyther, which Brambleghast fails to deal with. It also benefits from pivots such as Basculegion-M and Meloetta, all of which can bring Salazzle in safely against Steel-types such as Bronzong and Duraludon. Entry hazard support from Duraludon, Flygon, Rhyperior, Gligar, and Klefki helps put Salazzle's checks into KO range, and Knock Off variants pair especially well with hazard stacking, since removing Heavy-Duty Boots makes this chip damage unavoidable. Duraludon can safely switch in on Munkidori and Uxie while running Thunder Wave to aid Salazzle's sweeping capabilities. Meanwhile, Flygon can safely switch in on Earthquake and is able to bring Salazzle in safely against Fairy-types, most notably Sylveon, via U-turn. Rhyperior can take most priority attacks, including Fake Out from Ambipom and Munkidori, and can set up Stealth Rock easily.

monotype.overview:
Poison

Salazzle provides great disruption with moves like Encore and Corrosion Toxic, applying immense pressure against walls, and it's the second fastest Poison-type, which lets it outspeed the Ogerpon formes. Despite this, Glimmora can also provide Corrosion Toxic along with providing entry hazard support, and Iron Moth will generally act as a superior Fire-type option thanks to having a superior set of coverage options and vastly increased Special Attack.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Poison

Overheat can be run with an EV spread of 112 HP / 144 SpA / 252 Spe to OHKO defensive Gholdengo and Torterra.

Toxic Spreader (Poison).description:
With Corrosion, Salazzle can inflict Toxic onto key defensive threats like Heatran, Empoleon, Amoonguss, and Toxapex, greatly decreasing their longevity. Flamethrower gives Salazzle some offensive pressure, letting it force out Steel-, Grass-, and Ice-type threats like Gholdengo, Brambleghast, and Alolan Sandslash. With Salazzle's high Speed, Encore can prevent threats like Sinistcha, Gliscor, Okidogi, and Hydreigon from setting up, as well as lock Ogerpon formes into Swords Dance. Substitute paired with Black Sludge can allow Salazzle to accumulate Toxic damage on slower threats like Hisuian Goodra, along with finding repeated chances to safely set up Substitutes against foes that cannot break through them like Galarian Weezing and Amoonguss to effortlessly spread Toxic. Protect racks up Black Sludge healing and allows safe scouting against Choice-locked threats like Iron Valiant, Greninja, and Flutter Mane. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Salazzle to come in safely and land a Toxic.

With Salazzle's crippling Ground-type weakness, Galarian Weezing serves as a crucial ally thanks to its Ground immunity, being able to safely switch in on threats like Great Tusk, Mamoswine, and Quagsire, and ability to remove Stealth Rock to give Salazzle safe entry. Amoonguss helps to force out pesky Ground- and Water-types like Great Tusk, Gastrodon, and Ogerpon-W with Giga Drain and Foul Play. It can also use Spore to allow Salazzle safe entry to get up a free Substitute, while in return Amoonguss appreciates the removal of Steel-types like Gholdengo and Corviknight, which can use it as setup fodder. With its immense physical bulk and access to STAB Surf and Haze, Toxapex can deal with threats such as Scizor and Kleavor, while Salazzle limits foes like Articuno and Thundurus-T that majorly threaten Toxapex. Unaware Clodsire checks special setup sweepers like Kommo-o and Volcarona while also providing additional chip damage with Stealth Rock. Alolan Muk's superb special bulk and access to Knock Off and Poison Jab allow it to easily handle Ghost-type threats that force Salazzle out like Flutter Mane and Hisuian Zoroark. Overqwil, while not as specially bulky, can still serve as a solid Psychic- and Ghost-type response and works much better against threats like Gallade, Ceruledge, and Dragapult thanks to its high physical bulk and Intimidate. Galarian Slowking can create Future Sight traps to force in the team's opposing Dark-type or special walls like Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra, which Salazzle can take advantage of by getting in safely to either land a Toxic or set up a Substitute. Galarian Slowking also helps Salazzle by dealing with deadly special attackers like Volcanion, Iron Moth, and Walking Wake. Okidogi majorly appreciates Salazzle's Toxic shutting down bulky walls like Skeledirge, Quagsire, and Galarian Weezing by putting them on timers, and in return Okidogi handles threats like Heatran, Garganacl, and Bisharp with Drain Punch. Sneasler can use U-turn to bring Salazzle in on walls like Amoonguss, Klefki, and Toxapex and use them as an opportunity to get up a Substitute or land a critical Toxic. Meanwhile, Sneasler removes threats like Enamorus, Iron Valiant, and Latios. Choice Specs Icy Wind Gengar helps majorly in removing Gliscor, which can effortlessly switch into Salazzle thanks to Poison Heal. Thanks to STAB Shadow Ball and Thunderbolt, Gengar also helps in removing key threats like Landorus, Hatterene, and Dondozo, which majorly threaten Salazzle.

Defensive Spinner.description: 120 Speed EVs allow Tsareena to outpace Adamant Crawdaunt and Golurk.

nu.overview: Tsareena is a decent entry hazard remover: it easily beats the plethora of Grass-weak hazard setters like Rhyperior, Swampert, and Mudsdale, and even Steel-types such as Klefki are inconsistent at beating it one-on-one. While offensive Tsareena profiles as a solid wallbreaker that can take over games thanks to Rapid Spin's Speed boost, defensive sets are fantastic at checking the swathes of offensive Ground-types in NU, especially Golurk and Flygon, and its access to Synthesis helps differentiate it from Brambleghast, its primary competition. Tsareena faces some very real struggles defensively, though, as almost every Ground-type it aims to check carries super effective coverage, like Fire Punch or Fire Blast from Flygon and Megahorn from Rhyperior, that threatens to KO it with minimal chip damage required. Offensive sets aren't very fast without a Speed boost and easily pressured by other wallbreakers like Chandelure and Munkidori as well as fast utility options in Kilowattrel and Ambipom. Meanwhile, defensive sets are quite easy to exploit due to their reliance on Knock Off with Pokemon like Galarian Slowbro, Scrafty, and Bellibolt.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Tsareena has other usable Tera types than the ones listed, but they lack consistency across teams. Tera Dark is good for teams that lack a Ghost resistance and amps up Knock Off's damage, but it offers little else. Tera Ghost is a harder answer to Fighting-types than Tera Poison, but it's just as bad into Flygon and gives Tsareena a horrible Incineroar matchup. Tera Fire is similar to Tera Dragon in helping Tsareena against Fire-types, although Tsareena gains a Water weakness.

Checks and Counters

Flying-types: All of Scyther, Staraptor, and Tornadus outspeed Tsareena and beat it with relative ease. They all hate losing their items, though, and they are vulnerable to Triple Axel from offensive sets.

Poison-types: Galarian Slowbro is a great Tsareena answer. Other Poison-types like Amoonguss and Munkidori are good checks but less consistent. The former doesn't want to take a Knock Off followed by Triple Axel, while the latter is too frail to take Knock Off from either Tsareena set.

Fire-types: Incineroar counters Tsareena with ease, only fearing the rare High Jump Kick. Although Knock Off obliterates Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion, they both can spinblock Tsareena, tank its Power Whip, and OHKO it with their Fire-type attacks barring a well-timed Terastallization.

Offensive.description:
Set Details

Tsareena doubles as a source of entry hazard removal and a potent wallbreaker. Knock Off punishes switch-ins such as Chandelure, and Triple Axel deletes opposing Grass-types like Brambleghast, Whimsicott, and Rotom-C as well as Flygon. If you wish to tap further into Tsareena's utility movepool, U-turn is optional over Triple Axel, still giving it an out against any of its checks, especially Houndstone, while enabling its stronger teammates. High Jump Kick is another coverage move you can try, as it's Tsareena's best option for hitting Steel-type hazard setters like Copperajah and Duraludon and does good damage to Incineroar. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Tsareena bypass hazard damage, which increases its proficiency as a spinner, but Lum Berry helps against Bellibolt's Static and Vaporeon's Scald. Tsareena usually shouldn't be Terastallizing, but Tera Dragon potentially lets it KO a Chandelure with Knock Off and gives Tsareena a good sun matchup, while Tera Steel blanks Munkidori's STAB moves.

Tsareena is great at luring in and beating certain checks to Fighting-types like Amoonguss, Gligar, and Whimsicott with Triple Axel; make sure to pair it with teammates like Flamigo, Infernape, and Paldean Tauros-W that can take advantage of this. Furthermore, Flamigo especially, as well as other physical attackers like Paldean Tauros-W, appreciate Tsareena removing Brambleghast's Heavy-Duty Boots and making it easier to overwhelm with Stealth Rock up. Similarly, teammates like Choice Specs Chandelure appreciate Tsareena's Rapid Spin, and it can beat Steel-type checks like Klefki, Copperajah, and Bronzong for Tsareena.

Defensive.description:
Set Details

Bulky Tsareena is one of the tier's few good answers to the plethora of offensive Ground-types in NU, such as Flygon and Rhyperior. Although they possess super effective coverage moves for it, they can't OHKO it, and Synthesis keeps Tsareena healthy throughout the game so it can stay out of KO range from these threats. The biggest boon to this set, though, is destroying Klefki; it can't do enough damage with Foul Play thanks to the bulk investment, and Power Whip or Trop Kick will slowly beat it down. Trop Kick can be used over Power Whip for its accuracy. Tsareena will rarely want to Terastallize, but Tera Poison is nice to consistently answer Fighting-types like Flamigo and makes Tsareena immune to poison from Munkidori at the cost of becoming weak to Psychic; Tera Dragon aids against Fire-types like Chandelure and retains several resistances to types like Water, Grass, and Electric; and Tera Steel is useful for checking Fairy- and Poison-types such as Sylveon and Uxie.

Tsareena creates great defensive cores with common entry hazard setters like Flygon and Rhyperior. They resist Fire and Flying for Tsareena, while it takes on Water- and Ground-type attacks in return. Its Knock Off support is also favored by many offensive Pokemon, specifically Fighting-types like Flamigo, Paldean Tauros-W, and Infernape, since Tsareena so frequently draws in Brambleghast and removes its Heavy-Duty Boots. Stealth Rock-weak Pokemon like Choice Specs Chandelure and Choice Band Staraptor also desire Tsareena for its Rapid Spin.

Calm Mind.description:
With access to Triage, Draining Kiss, and Terastallization granting it perfect offensive coverage, Comfey is a formidable sweeper in UU, taking down dangerous offensive foes like Lokix, Quaquaval, and Greninja. Calm Mind amplifies the power of Comfey's Draining Kiss while also making it harder to take down, finding setup chances against common foes like Hydrapple, Tornadus-T, and Rotom-W. Tera Blast Ground allows Comfey to now target Steel-types, including Metagross, Excadrill, and Tinkaton as well as other Fairy-resistant Pokemon such as Toxapex, Pecharunt, Skeledirge, and Hisuian Arcanine. Tera Ground also grants Comfey the ability to set up on foes like Sandy Shocks and Thundurus-T and resist Poison-type attacks from Pecharunt. Taunt denies recovery chances against foes like Slowking, Toxapex, and Mandibuzz, notably blocking Toxic attempts from the latter two, allowing Comfey to set up Calm Mind more easily and capitalize on forced switches. Giga Drain is an option over Taunt to get heavy damage on Water-types such as Azumarill and Slowking as well as other foes like Mamoswine, Rhyperior, and Hisuian Arcanine. A Life Orb grants Comfey an immediate power boost and works in tandem with the self-healing nature of Draining Kiss. 16 Speed EVs let Comfey outspeed foes such as Volcanion and Metagross, with the remaining investment in HP and Special Attack to maximize bulk and power.

Comfey best fits on offense teams that wear down its checks to pave way for a sweep. Entry hazard leads like Mew and Excadrill provide key support in wearing down foes like Azumarill and Assault Vest Tornadus-T into Comfey's KO range. Mew in particular can cripple enemy Excadrill with Will-O-Wisp, allowing Comfey to no longer fear revenge killing attempts, while Excadrill can take out Tera Steel Latios. Ogerpon-C and Mimikyu are great teammates that offensively pressure bulky Pokemon such as Skeledirge and Slowking that trouble Comfey as well as wear down Tinkaton into range of Tera Blast Ground. Greninja and Azumarill are able to put pressure on the likes of Scizor and Hisuian Arcanine and are generally not reliant on Terastallization, meaning Comfey can use the mechanic more easily. Revavroom can take advantage of checks like Toxapex, Scizor, and Pecharunt and power through them while opening up holes against the enemy team for Comfey to clean. Quaquaval and Thundurus-T can take out Steel-types like Tinkaton and Metagross in the event Tera has already been used to still ensure Comfey can sweep; the former switches into Hisuian Arcanine, while the latter powers through Toxapex. Serperior and the aforementioned Quaquaval also threaten annoyances like Excadrill, Mamoswine, and Rhyperior.

zu.comments:
Other Options

With a Choice Band equipped, Passimian 2HKOes physically defensive Sandaconda with Close Combat. However, Passimian's base 80 Speed leaves it very susceptible to faster offensive Pokemon like Jolteon, Typhlosion, and Whimsicott.

Checks and Counters

Physically Defensive Pokemon: Dipplin and Sandaconda have the longevity and bulk to withstand repeated attacks from Passimian, and neither are particularly punished by Knock Off or its coverage moves. Gunk Shot can threaten Dipplin, but it suffers from poor accuracy and fails to 2HKO it. Weezing is a standout defensive check to Passimian between having great physical bulk, threatening to Will-O-Wisp Passimian, and punishing U-turn with Rocky Helmet.

Ghost-types: Sableye and Spiritomb cause Passimian to lose momentum when it's locked into Close Combat, and both can burn it. Spiritomb dislikes losing its Leftovers to Knock Off though. Rotom can use Passimian to set up if it's locked into Close Combat or Earthquake, but it can't switch into Knock Off.

Status: Will-O-Wisp from Rotom and Mismagius debilitates Passimian, though they struggle to switch into its coverage moves safely. Paralysis leaves Passimian easily outsped and makes it poor speed control, so Regirock can punish Passimian trying to switch in on it with Thunder Wave.

Faster Choice Scarf Users: Rotom, Typhlosion, and Hisuian Sneasel can outspeed and deal significant damage to Passimian, though none of them switch into the combination of Close Combat and Knock Off safely.

Fairy-types and Tera Fairy Pokemon: Whimsicott resists or takes neutral damage from most of Passimian's moves but must be wary of Gunk Shot, and Close Combat can 2HKO it after Stealth Rock damage. Tera Fairy users like Mesprit, Farigiraf, and Jolteon can take advantage of Passimian's limited coverage to take a hit from it and KO it at the cost of burning Terastallization. Even Pokemon vulnerable to Passimian such as Arboliva can use Tera Fairy to defensively flip their matchups and wall Passimian, opening opportunities for themselves to set up.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Passimian is an excellent fast offensive pivot and revenge killer thanks to its strong STAB attacks, good physical bulk, and Stealth Rock resistance. Passimian OHKOes fast offensive threats like Sneasel and can KO Hisuian Sneasel after Spikes damage or a Defense drop. Knock Off makes Mesprit and Froslass unsafe switch-ins to Passimian, and it makes helpful progress by removing items from defensive checks like Weezing and Spiritomb. U-turn lets Passimian keep up momentum against switch-ins like Dipplin and Sableye. Earthquake is Passimian's best coverage move for Poison-types like Neutralizing Gas Weezing, Hisuian Sneasel, and Muk. Gunk Shot OHKOes Whimsicott, is Passimian's best move against Dipplin, and keeps Passimian offensively relevant against Tera Fairy users like Jolteon. Tera Fighting allows Passimian to outright OHKO offensive foes like Virizion and Typhlosion and 2HKO defensive foes like Regirock and Sandaconda with Close Combat after one layer of Spikes. Tera Dark improves Passimian's matchups against Mesprit and Farigiraf, powers up Knock Off to hurt Spiritomb more, and denies Prankster-boosted moves from Sableye. Defiant is Passimian's only viable ability, but it's useful punishing Sticky Web teams.

Passimian punishing Defog with Defiant and removing Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off makes it a great team player for entry hazard-stacking teams that include Orthworm or Sandslash. Passimian's momentum is greatly appreciated by wallbreakers like Typhlosion, Clawitzer, and Alolan Exeggutor. Passimian luring in physically defensive Pokemon like Sandaconda and Dipplin enables partners like Mesprit and Whimsicott to take advantage of them when Passimian pivots out with U-turn, and in turn, Passimian threatens Steel-types like Orthworm and Magneton for them. Ghost-types like Rotom and Froslass can exploit Passimian locked into Close Combat, Earthquake, or Gunk Shot, so teammates like Cryogonal and Naclstack are great teammates. Likewise, Passimian appreciates specially offensive teammates like Mesprit, Farigiraf, and Typhlosion that can exploit physically defensive Pokemon like Weezing and Dipplin that it lures in. Once Passimian can form pivot cores with Pokemon like Jolteon, Magneton, and Whimsicott, it can trap foes in the vortex and wear down mutual Ground-type checks such as Sandaconda and Sandslash. Physical wallbreakers like Choice Band Sneasel and Swords Dance Lycanroc can open up holes in defensive cores to pave the way for Passimian to clean up late-game.

ru.overview: With a rare defensive typing as well as access to reliable recovery in Shore Up, Palossand carves out a niche as a Stealth Rock setter that can block Rapid Spin attempts from Cyclizar. Palossand's solid natural bulk lets it tank anything Cyclizar throws at it and take on dangerous wallbreakers like Kleavor, Terrakion, Entei, and Toxtricity, threatening all of them with Scorching Sands. However, Palossand often finds itself threatened by dangerous wallbreakers like Krookodile and Crawdaunt; while it can thwart them with Scorching Sands, Palossand will find itself at their mercy if they find a safe entry point against it. Palossand's passivity means that many of the Pokemon it's supposed to check, like Cyclizar and Kleavor, can pivot out on it with U-turn, letting the aforementioned wallbreakers come in on it safely; this also means that setup sweepers like Suicune can use it as fodder to rack up boosts. As a defensive Ground-type capable of setting Stealth Rock, Palossand competes directly with other Ground-types like Quagsire and Rhyperior; the former has Unaware for setup pertinent sweepers like Bisharp and Mimikyu, while the latter lacks reliable recovery but has a much stronger offensive presence.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Rocky Helmet allows Palossand to better wear down physical attackers like Flamigo as well as punish U-turn attempts from pivots like Cyclizar or Jirachi. Hex can be used as an alternative to Shadow Ball on teams that rely on statusing the opponent's team, in addition to synergizing well with Scorching Sands, though Shadow Ball's reliable power makes it preferred in most other scenarios. Sludge Bomb targets Grass-types like Wo-Chien and Breloom, in addition to its poison chance making it easier to wear them down. However, it's quite situational outside of hitting Grass-types and requires Palossand to give up a STAB move in order to run it. Palossand can forgo Scorching Sands' burn chance for Earth Power's higher base power, guaranteeing a 2HKO on Bisharp and offensive Empoleon, though Palossand's passivity means that it usually prefers Scorching Sands' ability to spread burns. Palossand can lure in and cripple defensive Pokemon like Umbreon and Wo-Chien with a Choice Specs Trick set; however, Palossand's passivity makes it sub-optimal offensively, rendering it dead weight until Choice Specs is removed.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Suicune and can take just about anything Palossand throws at it, taking advantage of its passivity to rack up multiple boosts in preparation for a sweep. Although, Suicune dislikes being burned by Scorching Sands. Basculegion-F and Empoleon are also able to threaten it offensively by targeting its lower Special Defense stat, though they must be mindful of Palossand's attacks.

Dark-types: Wo-Chien resists both Scorching Sand and Shadow Ball and can wear Palossand down with Leech Seed, Knock Off, and Ruination. Umbreon similarly doesn't mind Palossand's attacks and can cripple it with Toxic, while Krookodile and Bisharp threaten it offensively. However, aside from Wo-Chien, none of these Pokemon appreciate being burned by Scorching Sands.

Special Wallbreakers: Palossand's poor special bulk means that strong special attackers, like Necrozma, Gengar, and Gardevoir, threaten to OHKO or 2HKO it. However, all but Noivern struggle to switch in on Palossand's STAB moves.

Defensive.description:
Set Details

Palossand's good bulk, access to reliable recovery, and Ghost typing let it act as a Stealth Rock setter that can stop Cyclizar from freely using Rapid Spin. Scorching Sands lets Palossand burn and cripple physical attackers, particularly those that could otherwise come in on it freely, like Krookodile and Maushold. Heavy-Duty Boots makes Palossand less reliant on Shore Up, letting it utilize its other moves more easily. Colbur Berry can instead be used as a safeguard against Dark-type attacks from the likes of Krookodile and Bisharp, letting Palossand check them in a pinch. Tera Water is a solid defensive typing that lets Palossand use Water Compaction more easily, turning it into a solid check against Water-type attackers like Barraskewda and Empoleon . Tera Fairy is an alternative that grants Palossand a resistance to Knock Off from Krookodile and Crawdaunt, while its Dragon immunity lets it take on non-Flash Cannon Hisuian Goodra in a pinch. Tera Poison grants it an immunity to Umbreon's Toxic and Alolan Muk's Poison Touch, preventing it from being crippled by chip damage. Tera Poison also lets Palossand check Mimikyu and Breloom by granting it a neutrality to Ghost and a resistance to Fairy for the former and a resistance to Grass while maintaining its Fighting resistance for the latter.

Palossand's ability to block Rapid Spin and set Stealth Rock means that it finds itself right at home on entry hazard stack and balance teams. Spikes users such as Quagsire and Chesnaught appreciate Palossand keeping their hazards up against Cyclizar, with Chesnaught in particular making for a good partner due to its ability to check Dark-types like Krookodile and Bisharp. Cyclizar itself makes for a solid teammate thanks to its ability to check Basculegion-F, while appreciating Palossand's ability to deter Fighting-types like Terrakion from freely using Close Combat. Colbur Berry variants also appreciate Cyclizar removing hazards on its team's side while also keeping up Palossand's Stealth Rock. Palossand's lacking special bulk means that specially defensive Pokemon like Hisuian Goodra, Wo-Chien, and Blissey pair well with it, appreciating Palossand's ability to shore up their own defensive shortcomings. The former two are able to check Water-types like Slowbro and Basculegion-F, while the latter keeps Gengar in check and appreciates not having to run Stealth Rock itself. Umbreon makes for a fantastic partner due to its ability to check Gyarados, one of Palossand's best counters, as well as its ability to stop opposing Ghost-types like Gengar and Basculegion-F while wearing down the opposition with Toxic. In return, Palossand checks dangerous Fighting-types like Terrakion for it. On hazard stack teams, offensive powerhouses like Gardevoir and Entei can use Taunt and Encore users, such as Noivern and Jirachi, respectively, to find switch-in opportunities. In exchange, Palossand is able to wear down the opposing team with Stealth Rock and Scorching Sand burns while also checking opposing offensive threats, like Kleavor and Maushold.

Physically Defensive.description:
Physically defensive Palossand is an exceptional addition to teams looking to shore up their defensive answers to the physical sweepers in the metagame, like Arcanine and Heracross, as well as most Toxtricity sets. Using its natural bulk and resilience to entry hazards, Palossand can establish its own hazards into many of the dominant physical attackers in the metagame while maintaining its health to function as a physical sponge with Shore Up. Shadow Ball allows Palossand to hit Ghost-types like Decidueye and Hoopa for solid damage, preventing them from using it as setup fodder. Sludge Bomb gives Palossand the coverage to hit Grass-types like Rotom-C and Wo-Chien, with the chance to inflict poison on them and secure valuable chip damage against switch-ins like Bombirdier, Gastrodon, and especially Wo-Chien. Scorching Sands is a STAB move that has a chance to inflict burn, which is run alongside Shadow Ball and preferred over Sludge Bomb to not accidentally inflict poison on something that it would rather burn. Similarly, Earth Power is used in conjunction with Sludge Bomb to not risk an accidental status effect from Scorching Sands. Colbur Berry can make Knock Off and other Dark-type attacks from Pokemon like Skuntank and Zoroark much easier to switch into. Rocky Helmet punishes pivoting attempts and physical attackers as a whole, wearing down foes without access to recovery like Ambipom and Staraptor. Having no item is a niche option that allows Palossand to comfortably switch into strong Poltergeists from Golurk while also reducing damage taken from Knock Off. Tera Water is used to flip the weakness to Water-type attacks into a resistance, capitalizing on its ability to get a Defense boost thanks to Water Compaction while comfortably taking on threats like Bruxish and Paldean Tauros-W. Tera Water does create a weakness to Electric, however, making matchups into Kilowattrel, Rotom-H, and Toxtricity much more difficult. Tera Dark converts weaknesses to Dark and Ghost into resistances, notably helping with the slew of strong Dark- and Ghost-types in the tier like Decidueye, Hoopa, Skuntank, and Zoroark. Tera Dark makes the matchup into wallbreakers like Flamigo, Heracross, and Paldean Tauros-W much more difficult, though.

Palossand is a good choice for balance and bulky offense teams in need of a reliable spinblocker and Stealth Rock setter. Teammates like Florges, Scream Tail, and Wo-Chien pair well with Palossand, providing a partner that can switch into the special attackers in the tier like Goodra, Rotom-C, and Zoroark. Palossand works especially well on Spike stacking cores, with Coalossal and Alolan Sandslash providing hazard-stacking and hazard removal in one slot. Being able to spinblock opposing Coalossal is valuable, as it can be threatened out while maintaining hazards for teammates to capitalize on. Offensive pivots appreciate Palossand as a safe switch-in to threats like Heracross and Lycanroc, making Ambipom, Flamigo, and Toxtricity great supporting Pokemon that can rely on their defensive backbones to wear down their checks and counters like Bronzong, Coalossal, and Mudsdale. Florges and Zoroark appreciate Palossand for its ability to wear down physical sweepers like Arcanine and Heracross, giving them late-game sweeping potential with Calm Mind and Nasty Plot, respectively. Venusaur is a common switch-in against Palossand, so teammates like Delphox and Paldean Tauros-F are valuable to check it offensively.

Shell Smash.description:
Minior is a colorful setup sweeper with its decent offensive stats, unrivaled Speed once boosted, and access to one of the best setup moves in the game: Shell Smash. Minior's unique ability can make it easier to set up with its Meteor forme's higher bulk and immunity to status moves, though it can be unreliable when trying to change to base forme and sweep. With Acrobatics and Earthquake having near-perfect neutral coverage, Stone Edge offers a secondary STAB move that hits foes that resist these moves such as Rotom-H and Kilowattrel as well as dealing more damage to certain walls like Altaria and Houndstone. Alternatively, Substitute helps Minior find turns to set up, makes it harder to revenge kill, and punishes moves like Sucker Punch from Skuntank and Bombirdier. 30 HP IVs activates Minior's Shields Down after two Substitutes, allowing it to be much more self-sufficient. An Adamant nature gives Minior an easier time sweeping, as once boosted and in its base forme, Minior outspeeds the entire metagame. However, a Jolly nature makes Minior slightly less reliant on setting up, since unboosted Adamant Minior's base forme Speed ties with base 105 Speed foes like Zoroark and Pawmot and is outsped by Pokemon like Salazzle, Virizion, and Whimsicott. Furthermore, a Jolly nature means its Meteor forme after a Shell Smash no longer Speed ties with Hisuian Electrode and isn't outsped by Choice Scarf users like Flamigo and Rotom-C. Tera Flying eases Minior's matchup against walls like Mudsdale and Milotic while sweeping and is preferred if not running Stone Edge for a stronger way to hit Altaria and Rotom-H. Tera Flying also allows Minior to tank certain priority moves like Pawmot's Mach Punch and Bruxish's Aqua Jet when at 50% HP. Alternatively, Tera Ground allows Minior to break through Flying-resistant foes such as Bellibolt, Hisuian Avalugg, and Duraludon. It can also give Minior chances to set up when baiting Electric- and Rock-type moves like Bellibolt's Volt Switch, Kilowattrel's Thunderbolt, and Coalossal's Power Gem. Both of these options come at the cost of Minior's resistance to priority moves like Staraptor's Quick Attack and Arcanine's Extreme Speed.

Minior fits well on offensive teams as a secondary sweeper, since it lacks the raw strength needed to break healthy walls and often relies on having low HP to win. Defensive walls that can tank its boosted attacks like Mudsdale, Houndstone, and Bronzong should be worn down with their checks like Decidueye and Paldean Tauros-F and special wallbreakers like Toxtricity. If not running Stone Edge, Pokemon like Rotom-H and Kilowattrel can also tank a hit, so their own checks like Tatsugiri and Duraludon can come in handy. Pokemon like Rotom-C and Scyther can also lure in many of these walls in, and while they don't do much damage, they can eventually put these threats in range for Minior. The wide array of priority move users like Skuntank, Bombirdier, Hariyama, and Paldean Tauros-W should also be accounted for, especially if not running Substitute for the former two, as they easily KO Minior in its base forme, immediately putting a stop to its sweep. Encore and Trick users like Delphox, Calm Mind Scream Tail, and Rotom-C can help Minior come in safely and get an opportunity to set up. Offensive pivots like Decidueye and Kilowattrel can give Minior setup opportunities by luring in setup bait like Altaria and Gligar.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

(Rock)

Power Gem with a Naive nature allows Minior to hit Skarmory while also having an 100% accurate Rock-type move. Can instead run Earth Power with 8 Special Attack EVs and a Naive nature to OHKO Archaludon after a Shell Smash boost and Stealth Rock. However, Earthquake targets are more common, and running Earth Power notably makes Minior miss out on hitting Hisuian Goodra and Alolan Muk.

Shell Smash (Rock).description:
Shell Smash Minior is a great sweeper for Rock teams due to its great Speed, being able to take out Choice Scarf users like Iron Valiant, Sneasler, and Meowscarada after a boost. Minior is also appreciated on Rock teams as a Ground-immune Pokemon. Stone Edge at +2 is able to take out targets like Pelipper and Landorus. Acrobatics after a Shell Smash + White Herb boost is a hard-hitting STAB move, which allows Minior to take out Sneasler, Iron Valiant, and Ogerpon-W. Earthquake deals with weakened Poison- and Steel-types like Toxapex, Alolan Muk, and Hisuian Goodra at +2. White Herb allows Minior to revert its negative stats back to neutral after a Shell Smash. It is also the easiest way to boost the Base Power of Acrobatics when compared to other items. Shields Down allows Minior to survive a Close Combat from Choice Scarf Great Tusk when above 50 of its HP, allowing it to be able to set up a Shell Smash afterwards; Minior also can't be statused when above 50 percent of its HP, which makes it very safe to set up against Toxapex or Clodsire.

Swords Dance Ogerpon-C is an amazing teammate, being able to take out Water-, Rock-, and Ground-types like Primarina, Azumarill, Garganacl, and Ursaluna at +2. Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine provides immediate wallbreaking power for Minior by being able to take out Corviknight and Skarmory with Flare Blitz. Alternatively, a defensive Hisuian Arcanine can handle the Steel matchup more effectively, notably taking out Scizor. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder outspeeds and takes out fast threats if Minior has not gotten the opportunity to set up, notably eliminating Greninja and Meowscarada with Close Combat. Furthermore, Minior complements Iron Boulder by weakening Iron Hands, which allows Iron Boulder to pick it off with Zen Headbutt. Glimmora, with its coverage options, takes out a plethora of threats like Archaludon, Hatterene, and Quagsire. With Toxic Debris, Glimmora also sets Toxic Spikes upon being hit, putting foes on timers. Furthermore, Glimmora removes Stealth Rock for Minior while also poisoning non-Steel- and Poison-types with Mortal Spin. IronPress Garganacl is a great stallbreaker that can set up on passive Water and Steel teams and wearing them down over time with Salt Cure. Coalossal is a nice wall for Minior, removing entry hazards with Rapid Spin and checking threats like Scizor, Bisharp, and Weavile with Flamethrower and Body Press. In return, Minior takes out Iron Valiant, Sneasler, and Meowscarada with Acrobatics after a Shell Smash. Rhyperior is able to take out Scizor with Fire Punch.

zu.comments:
Other Options

A special set can be run with moves like Meteor Beam, Power Gem, and Earth Power, but the reduced power and lack of Acrobatics can make this an inferior option beyond the surprise factor. Minior also has access to some utility moves, such as Stealth Rock and U-turn, but it is better off as a sweeper because its poor defensive typing leaves any support role it could play done better by other entry hazard setters like Mesprit, Sandslash, and Regirock.

Checks and Counters

Physically Bulky Pokemon: Even when boosted, physical walls like Regirock, Alolan Persian and physically defensive Mesprit can tank a hit or two from Minior and respond with significant damage. Alolan Persian can serve as a strong defensive response, tanking hits with Fur Coat and KOing Minior with Foul Play.

Priority: Without expending Terastallization, Minior has no way to play around priority, and moves like Basculin's Aqua Jet and Lycanroc's Accelerock both can easily KO Minior once it is in Core forme. With few resistances to common priority in ZU, Minior can often be KOed by a revenge killer ignoring Speed boosts entirely. While Hitmontop do not carry super effective priority, they can KO a sufficiently weakened Minior.

Faster Threats: Even at +2, Meteor forme Minior can often by outsped and KOed by a revenge killer like Jolteon or Choice Scarf Rotom.

Encore: Slower Encore users like Mesprit can disrupt Minior as it tries to set up. If Prankster Encore users like Whimsicott, Sableye, and Grafaiai switch in as Minior uses Shell Smash, they can lock Minior into repeated uses of the move, forcing a switch out and wasting its White Herb.

Haze and Phazing: Pokemon like Weezing, Cryogonal, and Articuno can remove Minior's boosts entirely, forcing it to deal unboosted damage or attempt a predictions game on trying to get boosts back, with the added problem of the Defense drops. The latter two, however, need to watch out for Stone Edge if not Terastallized. Alternatively, Charizard, Dipplin, and Hippopotas can use Roar, Dragon Tail, and Whirlwind to remove Minior from the battlefield entirely.

*Stealth Rock: Minior prefers being in control of when it changes formes when possible, and Stealth Rock dealing unignorable chip just for switching in can significantly impede its ability to manage the forme transformation, on top of it making Minior much easier to KO.

Shell Smash.description:
Minior serves as a late-game setup sweeper, providing teams a self-sufficient cleaner via Shell Smash and Shields Down to outspeed the entire metagame once in base forme with Jolly, in addition to hitting hard off of its boosted Attack. Acrobatics synergizes with the White Herb consumption after a Shell Smash, Earthquake provides a strong attack against Flying-resistant Pokemon like Regirock and Jolteon, and Stone Edge overpowers Rock-weak threats like Articuno, Beartic, and Vikavolt. Substitute provides a way of reaching Core forme safely at the cost of needing to make contact to hit Pokemon such as Mesprit and Weezing. Jolly is used if Minior needs to outspeed certain Pokemon when unboosted, such as Timid Whimsicott and neutral base 110s if Minior is in Meteor forme, but Adamant can be used for the additional power instead, such as to assure a 2HKO on Regirock and confirming an OHKO on Spiritomb without Stealth Rock. Tera Grass can be used to tank a hit from Pokemon like Clawitzer, Jolteon, and Lycanroc and KO them, is the best typing against common moves from priority users like Hitmontop, Basculin, and Lycanroc, and can turn interactions against Clawitzer and Arboliva into setup opportunities. Alternatively, Tera Ground can be used for extra power for breaking through Regirock, as well as providing Minior with an accurate, non-contact STAB move. However, this option leaves Minior vulnerable to Basculin's Aqua Jet.

Minior works best either on snow teams alongside Abomasnow setting Aurora Veil, where Minior can provide an answer to Charizard and other Fire-types. Minior serves as a cleaner on more bulkier teams at the end once its teammates have weakened the opposing team over time, and it can also work on defensive teams as a primary wincon in a similar fashion. Wallbreakers like Clawitzer, Jolteon, Arboliva, and Magmortar all can appreciate Minior, as they deal significant damage to walls like Weezing and Regirock over the course of a game, allowing for Minior to clean up late-game. Hisuian Sneasel or Beartic in snow can serve as a bit of a double-threat option alongside Minior, where defensive structures are often able to take on one major threat but find themselves insufficient to wall both threats over the course of a game. Minior cannot sweep if strong priority from Pokemon like Hitmontop and Lycanroc remain in play, so removing those with teammates before sweeping is a necessity. Minior can take advantage of Pokemon that do not carry super effective coverage, such as Charizard and Weezing, as setup opportunities, so Pokemon that bring them in, such as Arboliva and Primeape, can help enable Minior to set up. Pokemon with access to entry hazard removal, such as Hitmontop on more offensive teams and Sandslash elsewhere, can remove Stealth Rock, which otherwise poses a serious threat to Minior's sweep. Taunt can also accomplish this task, with Alolan Persian on more offensive teams and faster Weezing elsewhere , but this risks Stealth Rock going up if outplayed.

Swords Dance.description:
Mimikyu is a valuable asset to hyper offense teams as a mid- to late-game sweeper with its great type combination and ability to be a one-time check to nearly anything with Disguise, including deadly foes such as Latios, Quaquaval, Greninja, and Lokix. It also serves as an emergency spinblocker to preserve entry hazards on these teams. Drain Punch is an alternative over Shadow Claw to get super effective damage on the likes of Excadrill, Mamoswine, and Cobalion, notably also granting Mimikyu recovery, and offsetting Life Orb recoil. Shadow Sneak picks off faster targets like Latios, Thundurus-T, and Ogerpon-C. Life Orb amplifies Mimikyu's wallbreaking, letting it reliably 2HKO Tinkaton with Shadow Claw at +2 as well as Latios with an unboosted Shadow Sneak. Alternatively, Red Card grants Mimikyu the ability to phaze out sweepers like Ogerpon-C and Greninja in tandem with Disguise and is able to generate a turn of setup with this, but the drop in power is notable even with the Adamant nature. Jolly is the preferred nature to get the jump on Hisuian Arcanine and Excadrill, but Adamant is an alternative for extra power at the cost of now being outsped by these threats. Tera Ghost amplifies the power of Shadow Claw and Shadow Sneak, letting Mimikyu OHKO Latios at +2 with the latter move even with Red Card as well as just offering greater damage in general against walls like Toxapex, Zapdos, and Tinkaton. Alternatively, Tera Fire grants Mimikyu an immunity to Will-O-Wisp from Skeledirge as well as a resistance to Steel-type attacks from Tinkaton, Scizor, and Metagross. It should be noted that only Tera Fire should be used for Drain Punch rather than Tera Ghost with the intended purpose of Tera Ghost largely being to boost the power of Shadow Claw specifically.

Mimikyu best fits on hyper offense builds thanks to its unique ability to disrupt other offensive teams with Disguise while also functioning as an emergency spinblocker against Excadrill. Entry hazard support from Mew and Excadrill is essential in softening up foes like Toxapex and Tinkaton to get broken past by Mimikyu; additionally, Excadrill offensively pressures them and provides Rapid Spin support to keep entry hazards from wearing down Life Orb Mimikyu. Tinkaton and Excadrill are Mimikyu's largest issues, being able to take its STAB moves and bypass Disguise with Mold Breaker. As such, powerful sweepers like Quaquaval and Ogerpon-C are useful in dispatching these foes and can overwhelm walls like Skeledirge and Hippowdon for Mimikyu to clean late-game. Quaquaval also handles Scizor, while Ogerpon-C can wear down Okidogi into range of +2 Play Rough. Belly Drum Azumarill can wallbreak to remove foes like Toxapex, take on the likes of Excadrill and Hisuian Arcanine, allowing Mimikyu to afford an Adamant nature, and pressure the sand archetype as a whole as well. Greninja can offensively check threats such as Sandy Shocks and Scizor and wears down Tinkaton to where Mimikyu can bypass it more easily. Skeledirge can help handle opposing offense teams thanks to Unaware and its bulk, being a key teammate Mimikyu can fall back on when handling these teams.

ru.overview: Mimikyu holds an interesting place in the tier, as its excellent ability and good STAB combination help gear it towards offensive structures as a revenge killer and late-game cleaner. Disguise gives Mimikyu a free turn that it can use to reliably set up Swords Dance. Disguise can also be used to revenge kill opposing Pokemon or force them out with Red Card, making Mimikyu a rather consistent answer to setup sweepers. Mimikyu is mainly held back by its mediocre stats; a low base Attack for its role leaves Mimikyu really struggling to break through some bulky Pokemon even at +2 like Magnezone and Registeel. Most of its defensive utility comes from its ability, so setting up Swords Dance can be difficult with its low base HP after Disguise is broken. Its mediocre Speed and frailty make it prone to being revenge killed by faster threats that survive Shadow Sneak, such as Entei, Terrakion, and Choice Scarf Krookodile.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Wood Hammer helps Mimikyu break past physically defensive walls like Gastrodon and Quagsire, but the recoil can greatly wear down Mimikyu, especially if it's holding Life Orb.

Checks and Counters

Physical Walls: Common physically defensive Pokemon such as Gastrodon and Quagsire can tank hits from Mimikyu and wear it down with Rocky Helmet chip damage or cripple it with attacks or status.

Burn: Getting burnt from Entei's Sacred Fire or Slowbro's Scald can cripple Mimikyu's already mediocre damage output and make it pretty easy to take care of.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Mimikyu occupies a unique place in the metagame as a setup sweeper and late-game cleaner that is used primarily because of the utility provided by its ability, Disguise, rather than purely because of its firepower. Since there are no viable Mold Breaker Pokemon in the tier, Disguise almost always guarantees Mimikyu a free turn to set up Swords Dance, which is incredibly valuable. Drain Punch helps against Steel-types that can take a hit from Mimikyu like Bisharp, Empoleon, and Hisuian Goodra while recovering any recoil from Life Orb. On the other hand, Play Rough ensures that Umbreon and Chesnaught cannot check Mimikyu. Life Orb provides Mimikyu with much-needed extra firepower that can come in handy when attempting to dispatch offensive threats such as Feraligatr and Kleavor or sweep after a Swords Dance. Red Card is an alternative that offers insurance by phazing out bulkier threats and setup sweepers that Mimikyu may not be able to easily take out such as Calm Mind Suicune, Swords Dance Bisharp, and Shift Gear Toxtricity; it also has the added possibility of bringing in a Pokemon like Cyclizar or Noivern that Mimikyu could use as setup fodder, in return for decreasing its damage. A Jolly nature with maximum Speed ensures that Mimikyu can outspeed a large chunk of the tier and, in particular, Kleavor and Krookodile. Tera Ghost strengthens Mimikyu's power as a sweeper and allows it to dish out heavy-hitting Shadow Sneak at +2, which can clean worn-down Pokemon like Noivern, Terrakion, and Gardevoir.

Mimikyu fits best on hyper offense and offensive structures that rely on setup sweepers and strong attackers to overwhelm the opposing team and thus may not have the defensive resources necessary to easily take out a fast revenge killer or prevent a reverse sweep. Other notable setup sweepers such as Bisharp and Swords Dance Crawdaunt pair well with Mimikyu by chunking holes in the opposing team and possibly removing some of its key defensive checks such as Gastrodon and Registeel, thus bolstering Mimikyu's ability to clean late-game. Mimikyu can act as a decent spinblocker against teams reliant on Cyclizar for entry hazard removal. It also appreciates its own hazards support, thus pairing well with Stealth Rock leads such as Kleavor and Terrakion, as they ease Mimikyu's job as a cleaner by wearing out the opposing team, which brings them closer to KO range after a Swords Dance. Mimikyu synergizes well with Future Sight users such as Slowbro and Reuniclus, as it prevents some Poison-type checks like Amoonguss from switching in.

Swords Dance (Ghost).description: Mimikyu is an outstanding asset to Ghost teams, boasting both a valuable part-Fairy typing and a unique ability that complements revenge killing and late-game cleaning. Play Rough hits threatening Dark- and Dragon-types like Galarian Moltres, Mandibuzz, and Kommo-o. Shadow Claw notably allows Mimikyu to threaten Psychic teams even under Psychic Terrain, while Drain Punch deals more damage to Steel-types such as Iron Treads, Magnezone, and Excadrill and can mitigate Life Orb recoil. Shadow Sneak enables Mimikyu to revenge kill weakened foes and pick off faster threats like Blacephalon, Gengar, and Victini. Disguise almost always allows Mimikyu to set up a Swords Dance or revenge kill faster foes that Shadow Sneak cannot deal enough damage to. Mega Sableye is heavily appreciated due to its ability Magic Bounce, which adds to Mimikyu's longevity by bouncing back entry hazards and status moves aimed at it. Wallbreakers like Gholdengo wear down bulkier teams by checking walls such as Corviknight, Mega Venusaur, and Toxapex, which lets Mimikyu have an easier time cleaning up late-game. Blacephalon and Skeledirge threaten the Steel-types Mimikyu struggles against, like Ferrothorn, Corviknight, and Mega Scizor. They can also cripple troublesome walls such as Toxapex and Gastrodon with Trick and Will-O-Wisp, respectively. Hisuian Zoroark is deeply valued for its Ghost-type immunity, as it can catch Gholdengo and Gengar off guard.

Choice Scarf (Ghost).description: Choice Scarf Mimikyu spooks fast threats like Iron Valiant, Zeraora, and Greninja for Ghost teams! Equipped with a Choice Scarf, Mimikyu is able to outspeed and pick off wallbreakers like Mega Altaria, Weavile, and Mega Gallade, allowing it to use Disguise offensively by tricking the opponent for a trade in exchange for a broken Disguise. Destiny Bond surprises fast threats like Zeraora, which Mimikyu can't OHKO or forcibly remove walls like Archaludon and Mandibuzz late-game. Trick lets Mimikyu fool walls like Hippowdon, Archaludon, and Celesteela swapping in to check its more common Swords Dance set, greatly benefiting its team mates like Ceruledge, Sinistcha, and Gholdengo that setup. Alternatively, Will-O-Wisp limits threats like Choice Band Excadrill, Ogerpon-W, and Zeraora, which Mimikyu can't deal meaningful damage against. An Adamant nature is preferred as it gets important damage breakpoints, namely OHKOing Mega Lopunny and Iron Valiant with Play Rough after Stealth Rock damage, but a Jolly nature outspeeds and picks off Clangorous Soulblaze Kommo-o. Mimikyu's damage is extremely low, being walled by most Steel- and Poison-types like Ferrothorn and Toxapex and even failing to 2HKO Slowbro. Due to these, wallbreakers like Sinistcha, Ceruledge, and Gholdengo are great team mates, with Sinistcha dealing with Toxapex and Slowbro while also taking on Mega Swampert and Great Tusk, Ceruledge eliminating Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Celesteela as well as premier walls like Toxapex and Hippowdon if using a Z-move, and Gholdengo checking Poison-types like Toxapex and Mega Venusaur. Mega Sableye acts as a Knock Off absorber against faster threats like Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Roaring Moon, and prevents entry hazards from getting up to wear down Mimikyu. Galarian Corsola provides Stealth Rock, which allows Mimikyu to OHKO the aforementioned threats, and is a special wall that handles Nidoking and Tapu Koko. Hisiuan Zoroark provides a Ghost immunity and can run a number of sets such as Nasty Plot or Swords Dance to weaken opposing teams, enabling Mimikyu to pick them off.

Swords Dance (Fairy).description: This is a sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Mimikyu is one of Fairy's premier setup sweepers thanks to Disguise near guaranteeing one free turn to set up Swords Dance to boost its Attack. Play Rough is Mimikyu's strongest STAB move and allows Mimikyu to secure an OHKO on Iron Hands after a Swords Dance and also deals with bulky Great Tusk. Shadow Sneak lets Mimikyu revenge kill weakened offensive threats like Iron Moth and faster Ghost-type Pokemon such as Flutter Mane and Dragapult. Shadow Claw lets Mimikyu break past bulkier Ghost-type Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Skeledirge more readily compared to Shadow Sneak, while Drain Punch is an alternative that threatens opposing Steel-types such as Magnezone and Bisharp. Mimikyu's preferred item is Life Orb to boost its damage output as much as possible.

One of Mimikyu's best partners on Fairy teams is Klefki. Mimikyu appreciates Spikes from Klefki, which allows Mimikyu to take down Pokemon easier after a Swords Dance boost. In return, Mimikyu can block Rapid Spin, allowing Klefki's hazards to stay up during the course of the game. Flutter Mane is often paired with Mimikyu since it can threaten physically defensive pokemon that give Mimikyu a hard time like Amoonguss, Quagsire, and Forretress and also faster offensive threats like Iron Moth and Kilowattrel. Mimikyu is able to break through specially defensive Pokemon like Dragalge which gives Flutter Mane an easier time. Hatterene is also a good partner for Mimikyu, as it can bounce back debilitating status conditions like Will-O-Wisp from Sableye and Thunder Wave from Klefki and also bounces back hazards, which helps with Mimikyu's longevity since it runs Life Orb. Furthermore, Mimikyu with its Disguise up can check opposing Ghost-type Pokemon like Flutter Mane and Gholdengo for Hatterene. Iron Valiant is also one of Mimikyu's best offensive teammates, as special sets are able to threaten other physically defensive Pokemon like Dondozo. Additionally, Iron Valiant is useful for Mimikyu in the Ground matchup, where a Choice Specs set can check answers to Mimikyu, such as Quagsire and Clodsire, using Psyshock. Azumarill can use Belly Drum against Steel teams and weaken foes like Orthworm and revenge kill Iron Treads with Aqua Jet.

Swords Dance (Ghost).description:
Mimikyu is a staple on Ghost-type teams, as Disguise allows it to deal with Dark-types and faster threats such as Barraskewda. Swords Dance can further take advantage of Disguise. Play Rough threatens Dark- and Fighting-types such as Meowscarada, Krookodile, and Quaquaval. Shadow Sneak picks off faster threats that could otherwise revenge kill Mimikyu, such as Dragapult and Flutter Mane. Drain Punch helps against Steel-types like Bisharp and offers some recovery—Disguise's recoil, entry hazards, and Life Orb damage can wear Mimikyu down pretty easily. Wood Hammer can potentially be used over Drain Punch to hit Pokemon such as Quagsire better, but the recoil damage isn't appreciated. Mimikyu's mediocre Attack forces it to use Life Orb to significantly damage neutral targets.

All of Mimikyu's teammates appreciate its ability to take on Dark-type teams. Froslass and Brambleghast can place Spikes to help Mimikyu clean up and use Taunt or Rapid Spin, respectively, so opposing entry hazards don't wear it down. Choice Scarf Flutter Mane helps Mimikyu against both Dark- and Dragon-type teams by taking down faster threats that could KO it after Disguise has been removed, such as Meowscarada and Chien-Pao, which resist Shadow Sneak. Nasty Plot Gholdengo deals with bulkier teams like Ground and Poison teams, as well as absorbing Toxic from bulky walls such as Toxapex. Furthermore, Gholdengo can also run Trick with a Choice item, which can cripple annoying walls such as Quagsire and Dondozo to help Mimikyu deal with them. Polteageist can clean up Poison teams after Skuntank is KOed, as well as Ground, Water, and Fighting teams. Spiritomb can tank some Dark-type attacks so that Mimikyu needn't waste Disguise's protection. Skeledirge can take some hits from foes like Iron Valiant and Dragalge for the same benefit. Dragapult can use a Dragon Dance set to boost against faster Pokemon that threaten Mimikyu, such as Iron Moth.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the return of the Regulation G format and its powerful restricted threats!

Trick Scarf.description:
• Mimikyu might seem like an odd user of Choice Scarf with its low offenses, but with Trick and Disguise, it becomes a very disruptive Pokemon.

  • Play Rough: Play Rough is the best single attack option, as it has no defensive immunities and can hit frail attackers like Chien-Pao hard.

  • Curse: Curse lets Mimikyu further disrupt Pokemon after using Trick or can be used as an emergency way to stop a sweeper while it's still holding Choice Scarf.

  • Destiny Bond: Mimikyu's good Speed makes it a good option for making trades with Destiny Bond, especially against Restricted Pokemon. Mimikyu can even surprise normally faster targets by using it with Choice Scarf.

  • Using a neutral nature with a Mint: Mimikyu should have a neutral nature with the appropriate Mint used on it. This way, Mimikyu can't be confused by eating any Berry after using Trick.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: This Mimikyu's supportive nature means it'll only Terastallize under specific conditions.

  • Normal: Tera Normal is particularly useful for catching Calyrex-S off guard, potentially preventing the start of a Grim Neigh sweep.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy gives enough of a boost to Play Rough to OHKO Chien-Pao while also resisting Sucker Punch.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar works best for keeping the right Curse typing as well as giving a one-time boost to Play Rough.

Swords Dance.description:
• While not as strong versus restricted Pokemon, Mimikyu is still a decent revenge killer and sweeper in Battle Stadium Singles, being particularly apt at revenge killing Calyrex-S and Flutter Mane with Shadow Sneak if Terastallization is not available.

  • Shadow Claw: While not a particularly powerful STAB, Shadow Claw is Mimikyu's most reliable attack against targets such as Ogerpon-H.

  • Curse: Curse gives Mimikyu an out against particularly bulky foes like Dondozo, albeit at the expense of its own survivability.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is usually preferred over Jolly for maximum power, as many targets close to Mimikyu's Speed bracket often don't run full Speed.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Terastallization can clinch in some key win conditions in certain situations, but Mimikyu functions perfectly fine without it.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar can grant the extra edge Mimikyu needs to close out fights.

  • Normal: Tera Normal can even the playing field against the dreaded Calyrex-S.

  • Ghost: The extra damage on Shadow Sneak gives Mimikyu better overall cleaning potential.

Curse Stall.description:
• The combination of Curse, Substitute, and Pain Split can be devastating against key defensive Pokemon such as Dondozo.

  • Play Rough: Play Rough is the most consistent single attack option due to having no immunities, and does well against the large amount of Dark-type and Dragon-type Pokemon like Koraidon, Miraidon, Chien-Pao, and Ting-Lu.

  • Thunder Wave: The chance of full paralysis can be devastating for opposing teams, potentially making Mimikyu even harder to break.

  • EV Spread: This bulkier EV spread gives Mimikyu an odd HP number that it can take advantage of if it uses Curse without its Disguise being broken, letting it use Curse again without KOing itself the next turn or using Substitute twice after using Curse. The rest is placed in Defense to wall top physical sweepers as best as possible.

Items

  • Bright Powder: While not particularly reliable, even one miss against Mimikyu can be devastating!

  • Figy Berry: Figy Berry and its other counterparts give Mimikyu another method of healing after using Substitute enough times.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: This Mimikyu rarely Terastallizes, as it needs to keep the damaging effect of Curse at almost all times.

  • Normal: Tera Normal can help prevent Calyrex-S from going unchecked, buying a turn to gain extra Curse damage or to land Thunder Wave.

  • Fairy: Terastallizing this Mimikyu for extra damage output is fairly situational, but getting a bit of extra power can help late game.

Do Not Touch! (Rocky Helmet + Curse).description:
• By combining Disguise with Rocky Helmet and Curse, Mimikyu can quickly overwhelm physical attackers like Koraidon and Zacian-C with enormous passive damage.

  • Endure versus Protect: Endure not only stalls turns for additional Curse damage but also allows physical attackers to make contact and take additional Rocky Helmet damage. It also has an advantage over Protect in that it isn't bypassed by the Urshifu formes, making it particularly dangerous to Urshifu-R that lack Punching Glove. On the other hand, Protect can block pivoting moves that would otherwise reset Curse, and it's generally better at stalling out effects such as Terrains and Trick Room.

  • Thunder Wave: Thunder Wave is a good fallback that can permanently cripple targets, especially those that don't fear Rocky Helmet.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Mimikyu already has the tools it needs to perform its role without Terastallization. On the rare occasion that Terastallization is used, keep in mind that any Tera type that sheds Mimikyu's Ghost typing will remove Curse's damaging effect.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar provides a good one-time boost on the rare occasions it's needed while maintaining Mimikyu's original typing.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost keeps Mimikyu's most important typing for Curse while powering up Shadow Sneak.

  • Ground: Tera Ground, particularly when it's used late-game, can cause big issues for Choice item Miraidon.

  • Normal: Tera Normal's Ghost-type immunity is great for gaining extra turns against Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage.

  • Water: Tera Water allows Mimikyu to survive Tera Water Surging Strikes from Choice Band Urshifu-R, potentially forcing it to take even more Rocky Helmet chip damage. It is also strong against Koraidon's Flare Blitz.

  • Steel: Tera Steel is a more niche option that makes it easier to cushion Zacian-C and rack up additional damage.

EV Spreads

  • Odd HP Number: Though the situation rarely comes up, an odd HP number is desirable so that Mimikyu can use Curse twice from full health.

  • 12 Speed EVs: Because Mimikyu is only 1 base Speed point lower than Urshifu, it is not uncommon to redistribute some EVs from Attack into Speed to outspeed bulky Urshifu. 12 Speed EVs is the minimum needed, though further investment is recommended, since even bulky Urshifu formes will bump their Speed by a few points.

  • 228 HP / 252 Atk / 20 Def / 4 SpD / 4 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread survives Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash after Disguise has been broken. The HP investment is also optimized to reduce residual damage from the likes of Stealth Rock.

  • 148 HP / 196 Atk / 164 Def with Adamant: The extra physical bulk now allows Mimikyu to survive Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash after both Stealth Rock damage and a Disguise break. If Disguise is still active, it almost always survives against Adamant Punching Glove Urshifu-R's Tera Water Surging Strikes.

  • 228 HP / 28 Atk / 252 Def with Impish: Full physical bulk can help Mimikyu live a little longer against threats like Assault Vest Koraidon that lack Flare Blitz. The HP investment is optimized to reduce residual damage from sources like Stealth Rock. The leftover EVs are put into Attack.

Trick Room Support.description:
• Thanks to Disguise, Mimikyu is a very consistent Trick Room setter.

  • Curse: Curse is used as a way to sacrifice Mimikyu and safely bring in a Trick Room sweeper.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp can cripple attackers that have already set up prior to deploying Trick Room. Disguise helps cover the fact that Mimikyu is using a slower Will-O-Wisp, but be wary of Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: While dealing damage isn't this set's focus, Rocky Helmet is still useful for wearing down bulky physical attackers like Koraidon and Urshifu-R that might otherwise pose problems for common Trick Room sweepers.

  • Mental Herb: Mental Herb foils Taunt usage meant to stop Mimikyu from setting Trick Room.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb allows Mimikyu to function better as a secondary attacker, especially when the opponent is trying to stall out Trick Room.

  • Covert Cloak: Covert Cloak is for targets that rely on flinching to stop Mimikyu, such as Icicle Crash Chien-Pao.

  • Ability Shield: Ability Shield can stop Moongeist Beam Lunala and Mold Breaker Ogerpon-H from knocking out Mimikyu through Disguise.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Mimikyu usually wants to keep its original typing, both for maintaining Curse's Ghost-type effect and for the Scale Shot immunity versus Koraidon and Dragonite.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar keeps all the benefits of Mimikyu's superior typing while giving a little extra offensive power.

  • Normal: Tera Normal's Ghost-type immunity helps Mimikyu control momentum against Calyrex-S.

  • Water: Tera Water combined with Rocky Helmet can cause fits for the likes of Flare Blitz Koraidon and Surging Strikes Urshifu-R.

EV Spreads

  • 0 Speed IV with a Relaxed or Brave Nature: Mimikyu generally wants the slowest Speed possible for moving first in Trick Room. The main disadvantage to this Speed outside of Trick Room is not being able to outrun uninvested Dragonite. If Mimikyu is running standard uninvested Speed, use an Impish or Adamant nature instead.

  • 228 HP EVs: All spreads below optimize HP to take as little damage as possible from sources like Stealth Rock and Disguise breaks.

  • 228 HP / 28 Atk / 252 Def with Relaxed: Focusing on physical bulk makes it so that even Tera Water Choice Band Urshifu-R will struggle to OHKO Mimikyu. It also survives Adamant Scizor's Bullet Punch even after accounting for Stealth Rock damage and a Disguise break.

  • 228 HP / 252 Atk / 28 Def with Brave: This spread gives Mimikyu a much better offensive presence for when it's needed. Enough physical bulk is maintained to survive Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash after Disguise is broken.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Bruxish is a great choice for a mid-game wallbreaker or late-game cleaner because of its dynamic STAB combination, access to priority, excellent Speed tier, and exceptional coverage that is largely boosted by Strong Jaw. Choice Scarf Bruxish notably outpaces other Choice Scarf users in the tier like Florges, Heracross, and Rotom-Mow. Flip Turn is a great momentum move, as Bruxish uses its fast pivoting abilities to allow slower teammates like Golurk to enter the field safely and wear down its checks like Galarian Slowbro, Wo-Chien, and Alolan Persian. Crunch hits Psychic-types like Galarian Slowbro and opposing Bruxish for massive damage. Aqua Jet is a strong STAB priority option that allows Choice Scarf Bruxish to reliably revenge kill other Choice Scarf users like Paldean Tauros-F. Ice Fang is a strong coverage option to chip away at Grass-types like Wo-Chien and Brute Bonnet. Strong Jaw is an outstanding ability for Bruxish, as a lot of its attacks like Psychic Fangs, Ice Fang, and Crunch are benefitted by the large boost it provides. Dazzling is a secondary choice for ability on Bruxish and prevents priority against it, stopping Sucker Punch and Shadow Sneak from the likes of Skuntank and Hisuian Decidueye, respectively, along with Fake Out from Ambipom and Parting Shot from Grimmsnarl. While Dazzling is a solid ability and prevents Bruxish from being taken out with priority, it does miss potential rolls that Strong Jaw provides such as a 2HKO on Calm Mind Florges and an OHKO on Tatsugiri with Psychic Fangs. Tera Psychic boosts Psychic Fangs to nearly unwallable levels when combined with Strong Jaw, providing 2HKOs into Galarian Slowbro and Milotic after minimal chip. Tera Water can be run to bolster Wave Crash, Flip Turn, and Aqua Jet damage, notably giving Wave Crash the boost needed to 2HKO Alolan Persian after some chip and OHKO Paldean Tauros-F after an Intimidate drop while also removing the weaknesses to Dark and Ghost, which is especially important on Strong Jaw sets.

Choice Scarf Bruxish can fit on all sorts of teams, being found mainly on balance and offense as a form of Speed control and breaking power. With access to Flip Turn, VoltTurn cores with teammates like Rotom-Heat and Hisuian Decidueye can be incredibly difficult for teams to manage throughout a game. Entry hazard stacking teams similarly use the threat of Flip Turn and strong breaking power to rack up hazard chip, appreciating support from Knock Off users like Bombirdier and Skuntank to remove Heavy-Duty Boots. Bombirdier is a notable teammate for Bruxish because of its access to Stealth Rock and U-turn, and it is usually easy to slot one of these on Bombirdier. Bombirdier also resists Dark- and Ghost-type attacks, so the duo has immense upside as a capable VoltTurn duo that has a lot of utility and coverage. Other teammates like Choice Specs Florges and Toxicroak can help break through bulky checks to Bruxish, such as Wo-Chien and Alolan Sandslash, and can provide another mid-game breaker or late-game cleaner for teams that strive to keep offensive pressure up. To break through physical walls more efficiently, teams using Choice Scarf Bruxish can often slot a strong special attacker like Hoopa, Zoroark, or Magneton to support its endeavors to break teams down, with the latter two having access to pivot moves to further build off the VoltTurn structure. Bruxish's ability to threaten every Ground-type in the tier is also important for teammates like Salazzle, which become very threatening late-game when Ground-types are removed.

Choice Band.description:
Bruxish serves as one of PU's most frightening wallbreakers thanks to its high Attack and alright Speed stat, its access to Strong Jaw, great move options with a great STAB combination, priority, pivoting moves, and coverage options. It 2HKOes a vast majority of the tier's staple walls, like Mudsdale, Galarian Slowbro, and Milotic, with its terrifying STAB attacks. Aqua Jet is used to deal with faster weakened threats and setup sweepers, such as Salazzle and Sneasel. Finally, Flip Turn lets Bruxish safely switch out of bad matchups, such as Wo-Chien and Brute Bonnet. Tera Psychic can be used to let Psychic Fangs OHKO Pokemon like bulky Florges, and it removes Bruxish's weaknesses to the Grass- and Electric-types that litter the tier. Tera Water can be used to OHKO foes like Alolan Sandslash after Stealth Rock chip damage. It also removes Bruxish's Ghost and Dark weaknesses, making Pokemon like Swords Dance Hisuian Decidueye easier to deal with.

Due to Bruxish's pitiful defenses and rather mediocre Speed stat, it fits best on bulky balance and offense teams to make up for its lackluster hit-taking abilities.
