Bruxish struggles with faster or bulkier Dark-type Pokemon such as Zoroark and Wo-Chien, so it really appreciates Fighting-type Pokemon like Hariyama and Scrafty, which also provide a valuable Knock Off-resistant teammate. Defensive Ground-types like Palossand work well with Bruxish, as they remove deadly threats like Paldean Tauros-F, while Bruxish can deal with Pokemon that check them like Hoopa and Rotom-Heat. Faster Grass- and Electric-type Pokemon, such as Shaymin, Choice Scarf Rotom-Mow, and Pawmot, threaten Bruxish immensely, so teammates that resist their moves such as defensive Bombirdier and Venusaur are great teammates, along with being more reliable checks to Delphox and Palossand than Bruxish. In return, Bruxish can take out the Poison- and Rock-type Pokemon that threaten them such as Salazzle, Galarian Slowbro, and Coalossal. Teammates such as Choice Scarf Heracross and Zoroark appreciate Bruxish, as it can remove the bulky Pokemon that wall them such as Mudsdale and Coalossal. Thanks to Bruxish's wallbreaking ability, it makes for a great teammate for late-game sweepers and cleaners, such as Salazzle and Ambipom.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dragon (Choice Specs)

Focus Blast can be considered over Aura Sphere due to its obscene damage, which prevents Hisuian Goodra and Ting-Lu from tanking any additional hits while 2HKOing Mandibuzz and Blissey. However, Focus Blast's accuracy makes it a less reliable option than Aura Sphere.

Mixed Wallbreaker (Dragon).description:
With its decent mixed offensive prowess, Kommo-o can use a mixed set with Close Combat to put more pressure on the defensive cores of opposing Steel, Dark, and Dragon teams. Close Combat pulverizes Hisuian Goodra, Heatran, Ting-Lu, and Empoleon that otherwise can try and scout other Kommo-o sets. Close Combat also deals with Scrafty, which is troublesome for most Dragon teams. Clanging Scales punishes switch-ins like Dragapult, Sableye, and Archaludon, 2HKOing the last two defensive walls. Flamethrower deals with Steel team's switch-ins in Skarmory and Gholdengo. Vacuum Wave picks off faster threats like Meowscarada and Greninja. 92 Atk EVs coupled with Expert Belt ensures Kommo-o OHKOes Hisuian Goodra with Close Combat. A Rash nature is preferred, as it lets Kommo-o 2HKO non-specially defensive Gholdengo with Flamethrower and reduces the prior damage needed for Vacuum Wave to KO Hisuian Samurott and Greninja late-game.

Mixed Kommo-o struggles with bulkier defensive cores such as those of Flying and Water teams, and it is unable to 2HKO specially defensive Corviknight, so wallbreakers such as Choice Specs Dragapult and Latios make for great teammates. Dragapult also deals with faster threats like Choice Specs Flutter Mane and non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and loves Kommo-o's ability to punch through special walls like Ting-Lu and Hisuian Goodra. Latios deals with Poison-types like Clodsire and pressures Flying and Fighting teams. It can even run Flip Turn if using a Choice Scarf to pivot Kommo-o in against Ting-Lu, Empoleon, and Gholdengo, all of which check Latios. Both of them appreciate Kommo-o's ability in Bulletproof, as it covers for their weakness to Shadow Ball. Kyurem and Raging Bolt devastate the defensive cores of Water and Flying teams and love Kommo-o's ability to remove their checks in Iron Treads, Ting-Lu, and Empoleon. Kyurem deals with Clodsire, while Raging Bolt zaps Corviknight and Toxapex for Kommo-o. Hisuian Goodra and Archaludon are notably not weak to any of Dragon's weaknesses, with Hisuian Goodra dealing with Primarina, Flutter Mane, and Greninja and Archaludon covering for physical threats like Roaring Moon and Meowscarada. Hisuian Goodra can also use Knock Off to remove items from walls, allowing Kommo-o to plausibly 2HKO specially defensive Corviknight after Stealth Rock. Archaludon also provides Stealth Rock, which help chip down speedy threats to the point where Kommo-o can safely remove them with Vacuum Wave. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon deals with faster threats like non-Choice Scarf Dragapult and Flutter Mane, and it also pivots Kommo-o in against walls like Skarmory. Swords Dance Garchomp appreciates Kommo-o's ability to break down Steel and Dragon teams, which paves a way for Garchomp to sweep. It also deals with Volcarona and Articuno, which wall Kommo-o. Other setup sweepers like Dragonite benefit from Kommo-o breaking its checks in Skarmory and Archaludon.

Choice Specs (Dragon).description:
Choice Specs Kommo-o is a great wallbreaker for Dragon teams thanks to its incredible STAB combination and access to Vacuum Wave, which allows it to force out problematic threats like Greninja and Darkrai. Clanging Scales complements Kommo-o's coverage, punishing switch-ins like Dragapult, Mandibuzz, and Toxapex that can shrug off its Fighting-type moves, and it also damages Substitute Spectrier and Volcarona. Flamethrower rounds out Kommo-o's coverage against Steel teams by roasting Gholdengo and Corviknight. Vacuum Wave lets Kommo-o pick off massive threats to Dragon teams like Meowscarada, Choice Band Excadrill, and Hisuian Samurott. Bulletproof lets it switch into and nullify Shadow Ball from Choice Specs Spectrier and Hisuian Zoroark. A Timid nature lets Kommo-o outspeed Jolly Mamoswine and damage it with Vacuum Wave before it can be picked off by Ice Shard, as well as allowing Kommo-o to outspeed and remove Dragonite and Adamant Lokix. Alternatively, a Modest nature enables Kommo-o to OHKO Greninja and Meowscarada with Vacuum Wave after Stealth Rock damage and guarantees a 2HKO on specially defensive Corviknight and Hisuian Goodra.

Both Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra help with Kommo-o's debilitating Fairy weakness by dealing with physical and special attackers, respectively: Archaludon deals with Azumarill and Mimikyu, which can use Kommo-o as a setup opportunity, while Hisuian Goodra can sponge attacks from the likes of Flutter Mane, Choice Specs Greninja, and Primarina. Archaludon also provides Stealth Rock support, a welcome tool to help Kommo-o break through and revenge kill foes. Both Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra can handle opposing Dragon-types as well; Archaludon can cover against Dragon Dance Dragapult, while Hisuian Goodra can handle Latios. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon appreciates Kommo-o's ability to threaten Steel-types that can take it on like Skarmory, and in return, it provides speed control, removing Choice Specs Dragapult and Choice Scarf Hoopa-U, which readily deal with Kommo-o. Dragapult can run a variety of sets from Choice Specs to further pressure special walls alongside Kommo-o, Choice Band to lure and weaken Hisuian Goodra and Clodsire, and status-spreading sets to slow down opposing teams. In return, Kommo-o overpowers Dark-types like Bisharp and Hisuian Samurott. Both Latios and Latias are great teammates, as they provide speed control and help in the Poison and Fighting matchups, two major struggles for Kommo-o. Latios can use an Expert Belt set to further pressure Water and Flying teams, while Latias also provides very helpful utility in the form of Healing Wish and Trick to render checks like Galarian Slowking much less potent. Garchomp can pack Spikes or Stone Edge to help Kommo-o's wallbreaking prowess or deal with Moltres and Volcarona for Dragon teams. In return, Kommo-o deals with Corviknight and Skarmory for Garchomp. Dragonite forms a priority core with Kommo-o and loves Kommo-o's ability to remove pesky Steel-types like Archaludon and Skarmory, allowing it to clean up Dragon and Flying teams late-game.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Kommo-o greatly appreciates redirection from Pokemon like Electabuzz and Amoonguss, allowing it to safely set up. Electabuzz can also use Taunt to prevent Haze from removing Kommo-o's boosts. Damage reduction like Intimidate and Will-O-Wisp from Incineroar and Magmar can also aid Kommo-o in setting up. Aurora Veil and dual screens from Alolan Ninetales and Grimmsnarl, respectively, can also help in damage reduction. Fake Out and healing from Rillaboom and its Grassy Terrain are helpful in helping with safe setup and longevity, respectively.
  • Gholdengo is a good partner, as it threatens Fairy-types like Hatterene and Clefairy. Sneasler can also threaten Fairy-types with Dire Claw. Kingambit is another good offensive partner, threatening Ghost-types like Dragapult that would otherwise wall out Body Press Kommo-o sets. Tyranitar can threaten Flying-types like Dragonite and Talonflame.
  • Kommo-o can struggle immensely against Fairy-types like Primarina and Psychic-type spam teams that include Pokemon like Indeedee-M. Dragonite is another issue, dealing a lot of damage and using Haze to remove Kommo-o's boosts. Dragonite also has Multiscale, weakening Kommo-o's damage. Steel-types like Gholdengo threaten good damage into the Fairy-types, while Dark-types like Incineroar can easily take attacks like Expanding Force from Psychic-type spam teams. Allies like Porygon2 and Grimmsnarl can threaten Dragonite for good damage with Ice Beam and Spirit Break, respectively.

Strategy Comments

  • Kommo-o's main role is to get set up and sweep or clean up. Kommo-o works best when next to support that helps it set up like redirection and Fake Out.
  • Kommo-o works well as a cleaner during the late-game, so aiming to remove pieces that might stop it like Dragonite is helpful. Reserving support like Electabuzz for Kommo-o can also be helpful, as it helps Kommo-o set up.
  • Haze is a big issue for Kommo-o, punishing it for setting up. Fast and powerful attackers like Dragapult can deal major damage before Kommo-o sets up or attacks. Fast Taunt from foes like Maushold is a check to Kommo-o, that is, if you predict correctly whether or not Kommo-o sets up. Haze can be stopped by Taunt, and fast breakers or Taunt can be stopped by redirection from allies like Electabuzz.

Clangorous Soul.description:
• Clangorous Soul Kommo-o aims to set up and sweep or deal great amounts of damage to the majority of the metagame. It avoids Spore thanks to Overcoat or becomes immune to attacks like Hyper Voice thanks to Soundproof while enjoying the fact that there aren't that many Fairy-types in the format, allowing Clanging Scales to hit almost everything in the format for solid damage.
  • Clangorous Soul allows Kommo-o to set up, which can be aided with redirection. Clanging Scales can deal good spread damage while also boosting Kommo-o's Special Attack with Throat Spray if it hasn't used Clangorous Soul. Flamethrower can threaten Steel-types like Gholdengo that resist Clanging Scales while hitting hard into metagame threats like Rillaboom and Alolan Ninetales. Aura Sphere, on the other hand, is a good STAB option that also hits Steel-types, doing good damage into Pokemon like Archaludon and Kingambit.
  • Throat Spray's extra Special Attack boost in conjunction with Clangorous Soul allows Flamethrower to OHKO Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Alolan Ninetales or Aura Sphere to OHKO Tyranitar. Leftovers is good to heal back the damage dealt from Clangorous Soul, increasing its longevity.
  • Tera Fire grants a resistance to Fairy-type attacks and Make it Rain and gives Flamethrower a STAB boost. Tera Steel grants more defensive properties, letting it resist Dragon- and Flying-type attacks from Pokemon such as Hydreigon and Dragonite.
  • 188 Speed EVs let Kommo-o outspeed Pelipper while outpacing Sneasler after a Clangorous Soul. The Special Attack investment lets the first Kommo-o set OHKO Kingambit with +2 Flamethrower while also OHKOing Archaludon with Aura Sphere after the same boosts. The alternative EV spread outspeeds Rillaboom without any boosts while taking under 50% from Scale Shot from Dragonite when Terastallized into Fire.
  • Although Clangorous Soul sets are more destructive than Iron Defense sets, losing health early can lead to Kommo-o easily getting KOed by strong neutral attacks. Unlike Iron Defense, Clangorous Soul is not an easily spammable move and is really only used once per game.

Iron Defense.description:
• With Iron Defense, Kommo-o is able to set up and stay on the field for a long time, taking attacks from Pokemon like Sneasler and Rillaboom.
  • Iron Defense and Body Press are Iron Defense Kommo-o's main source of damage, hitting a lot of the metagame really well, like Porygon2 and Ursaluna-B.
  • Leftovers increases Kommo-o's longevity, making it incredibly difficult to remove.
  • The EVs are physically defensive to deal more damage with Body Press, OHKOing both Ursaluna formes after a Iron Defense. The Special Defense EVs let it survive a Life Orb-boosted Blood Moon from Ursaluna-B. The second EV spread can survive Tera Fire Choice Specs Eruption from Timid Hisuian Typhlosion.
  • Iron Defense Kommo-o is quite vulnerable to special attacks, with no way to boost its Special Defense. It can also be quite slow, so faster threats can remove Kommo-o before it gets boosts or disrupt Kommo-o, preventing set up.

vgc2024.overview:
• Kommo-o is a strong setup sweeper thanks to its excellent defensive stats and access to STAB Body Press. Its defensive typing gives it critical resistances to the signature moves of both Urshifu formes, which ignore the Defense boosts from Iron Defense. With proper support, Kommo-o is capable of becoming extremely difficult to remove once it starts setting up Iron Defense, making it an extremely effective sweeper.

  • Kommo-o appreciates teammates that help it set up more easily. Incineroar and Amoonguss are great at this, with Incineroar being able to cycle Fake Out and Parting Shot, while Amoonguss provides Spore as well as redirection support. Both give Kommo-o turns to set up and more room to maneuver, and they also have strong defensive synergy with Kommo-o. Ting-Lu is another great partner, as it can whittle down foes with Ruination, and its ability Vessel of Ruin makes Kommo-o harder to remove.

  • Ironically, one of Kommo-o's biggest weaknesses is its typing. While its numerous resistances are valuable, namely into the Ogerpon and Urshifu formes, in exchange, it is weak to a whole host of common offensive types. Strong attackers such as Flutter Mane, Raging Bolt, and Chien-Pao hit Kommo-o for super effective damage, with the former two being special attackers and the latter using Sacred Sword, meaning they all ignore Iron Defense boosts. Kommo-o is often forced to Terastallize, and requires careful positioning around threats to conserve its HP for a late game sweep.

Iron Defense Sweeper.description:
• Iron Head is used to hit Flutter Mane, which is immune to Body Press.

  • Leftovers is used for extra recovery, since Kommo-o will be on the field for long periods of time.

  • Overcoat is picked for an immunity to powder moves, allowing it to ignore Amoonguss, which can otherwise redirect a resisted Body Press and slow it down with Spore.

  • The Special Defense investment allows Kommo-o to live a Blood Moon from Life Orb Ursaluna-B and makes Shadow Ball from Special Attack Booster Energy Flutter Mane a 3HKO. On the physical side, the Defense investment allows Kommo-o to comfortably live Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash, as well as making Urshifu-S's Wicked Blow a 3HKO after Terastallizing into Steel. The Attack investment gives the best chance for an OHKO on Flutter Mane with Iron Head after Terastallizing into Steel.

  • Tera Steel has the best synergy with Kommo-o's original typing since it provides resistances to every type that Kommo-o is weak to. It also gives STAB to Iron Head, allowing for a favorable roll to OHKO Flutter Mane

Offensive Z-Move.description:
Kommo-o is an unorthodox wallbreaker and setup sweeper that can blow past certain team structures with ease while also providing its team with notable defensive utility thanks to its typing and ability. However, Kommo-o's terrible matchup versus the tier's common Fairy-types such as Clefable and Tapu Lele limits its utility and means it requires significant support to be a consistent choice. Clanging Scales combines with Kommonium Z to give Kommo-o access to Clangorous Soulblaze, a powerful Z-Move that also boosts all of Kommo-o's stats one stage and notably OHKOes Great Tusk and offensive Landorus-T after Stealth Rock. Close Combat is preferred for its power, notably OHKOing Heatran at +1 and improving damage rolls against Melmetal and Mega Diancie. Drain Punch, although much weaker, gives Kommo-o some form of recovery and can let it heal off damage it may have taken while setting up on Pokemon such as Ferrothorn. Flamethrower hits Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Mega Scizor, preventing them from reliably trading with Kommo-o. Kommo-o is a decent Stealth Rock setter, as it dissuades common entry hazard removers such as Great Tusk, Terapagos, and Landorus-T from directly switching into it thanks to its Z-Move. Taunt is another option that allows Kommo-o to shut down Pokemon like Toxapex, Gliscor, and Galarian Slowking that might try to stop it via status or Haze. Clangorous Soul lets Kommo-o set up boosts reliably against teams with a Fairy-type, although it still won't sweep them easily, as Fairy-types like Tapu Lele, Clefable, and Tapu Fini can still take Kommo-o's boosted moves fairly comfortably. Additionally, while setting up both boosts is potentially devastating, it is often difficult to do so and unnecessary in a lot of situations due to Kommo-o's power at +1 often being sufficient. The other two moves are therefore often preferred. Bulletproof is very useful against foes such as Mega Charizard Y and Gholdengo variants lacking Make it Rain, since it lets Kommo-o effectively counter them, turning them into setup fodder.

Kommo-o's threatening nature lets it fit well on offensive teams that want to keep the pressure on while appreciating Kommo-o's ability to check Hisuian Samurott, Mega Charizard Y, and Heatran. Kommo-o struggles greatly against Fairy-types such as Mega Diancie, Tapu Lele, and Clefable, as they easily block its Z-Move while not being appreciably threatened by its coverage moves. Teammates that can take advantage of these Fairy-types are therefore required. Steel-types like Gholdengo, Melmetal, and Corviknight can come in on these Fairy-types and make progress via exerting significant offensive pressure from the former two or pivoting out and gaining momentum with the latter. Gholdengo also assists Stealth Rock variants of Kommo-o by blocking Rapid Spin and Defog attempts from Terapagos, Tornadus-T, and Zapdos. Kommo-o in turn can switch into Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y and Heatran, which threaten these Steel-types. Frail wallbreakers and cleaners, such as Iron Valiant, Urshifu-R, and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele love Kommo-o providing defensive utility on top of keeping up the offensive pressure for its teammates. Taunt variants work especially well with these teammates, as Kommo-o becomes adept at breaking down defensive cores consisting of Pokemon such as Toxapex, Gliscor, and defensive Landorus-T for these faster teammates. Kommo-o's access to Stealth Rock is useful for these offensive teams, as they sometimes struggle to fit Stealth Rock setters elsewhere, and they don't mind Kommo-o's limited longevity preventing it from setting up Stealth Rock multiple times over the course of a longer game. It notably frees up a moveslot on teammates such as Ferrothorn, Heatran, and Landorus-T. Hyper offense teams can often afford the Clangorous Soul variant of this set, as they generally have a dedicated lead devoted to setting entry hazards up. Teammates such as Iron Valiant, Roaring Moon, and Kingambit often fit on these teams and can pair with Kommo-o to exert immense offensive pressure on the opposing team and beat down their shared checks such as Tapu Lele, Clefable, and Toxapex.

Defensive.description:
Kommo-o is a unique Stealth Rock setter and special wall. Its Dragon typing combined with Bulletproof allows it to withstand hits from powerful attackers such as Mega Charizard Y, Ogerpon-W, and Volcarona, making it a solid check to all of them, as well as Gholdengo variants lacking Make It Rain. Body Press enables Kommo-o to threaten immediate damage on its targets such as Ogerpon-W and Serperior, as well as mauling Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Heatran. Toxic lets Kommo-o threaten common Body Press answers, notably Moltres, Tapu Lele, Zapdos, and Landorus-T. Stealth Rock allows Kommo-o to make long-term progress and enables the breakdown of many common offensive pieces, especially the 4x Rock-weak Mega Charizard Y and Buginium Z Volcarona. Protect lets Kommo-o recover HP for free with Leftovers, force foes to take an additional turn of poison damage, and scout threatening moves from Choice-locked Pokemon such as Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and Choice Specs Iron Valiant. Earthquake enables Kommo-o to not get stonewalled by Gholdengo, as well as threatening Galarian Slowking, Clodsire, and Tapu Koko. 32 Defense EVs with an Impish nature let Kommo-o take Mega Lopunny's Close Combat twice from full HP after Stealth Rock damage. 52 Speed EVs allow Kommo-o to outspeed uninvested Landorus-T, and 176 Special Defense EVs allow it to survive a Luster Purge from Mega Latios at full HP.

Kommo-o fits best on bulky offense and balance teams that can give it the specific support it needs to thrive. It can stave off offensive Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y and Ogerpon-W, but it generally thuds against more defensive builds featuring Toxapex and Gliscor. Conversely, Kommo-o can be overwhelmed defensively by the threats it checks due to its lack of reliable recovery, so it requires a strong backbone and partners that it can rely on to cover its most glaring weaknesses, notably Fairy-types such as Iron Valiant and Hatterene. For this reason, Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo are excellent partners. Offensively, the ability to break past defensive pieces with Future Sight and Nasty Plot,respectively, gives teams a way to threaten the Toxic-immune Toxapex and Pecharunt, and Kommo-o can in turn serve to step in versus the Dark-types that force out both its teammates such as Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott. Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo also patch up the weakness to Psychic- and Fairy-type Pokemon, most notably Tapu Lele and Mega Latios. In a similar vein, Clefable helps against Dragon-types, serving to deny Garchomp and Dragonite the ability to obliterate Kommo-o with their powerful Z-Moves. Clefable can use Thunder Wave to make the Speed tiers of threatening sweepers like Ogerpon-W and Kartana more manageable for Kommo-o, and it can use Knock Off to remove the Heavy-Duty Boots that ignore Kommo-o's Stealth Rock. In turn, Kommo-o can deny the otherwise troublesome Ogerpon-W and Mega Charizard Y the opportunity to break through Clefable's otherwise robust defensive profile.

Galvanize.description: Kommo-o finds a decent niche on offensive teams as a mixed attacker with strong coverage. Boomburst scares off walls such as Mandibuzz, Corviknight, and Manaphy. Clanging Scales threatens Great Tusk, Iron Hands, and Pecharunt, while Close Combat notably allows Kommo-o to smack special walls like Blissey, Swampert, and Volt Absorb Empoleon attempting to check it. Stealth Rock synergizes well with Kommo-o's ability to scare away entry hazard removers like the aforementioned Mandibuzz and Corviknight. Clangorous Soul allows it to act as a passable setup sweeper instead, preventing threats like Roaring Moon and Iron Boulder from revenge killing it while increasing its offensive capabilities. Life Orb is typically preferred for its consistent damage boost, but Throat Spray can be used on Clangorous Soul sets to avoid recoil. Kommo-o's lack of longevity necessitates either teammates that can make up for its absent defensive utility like Corviknight and Manaphy or offensive teammates that can keep up the pressure like Iron Moth and Chien-Pao. Select revenge killers like Dragonite, Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, and Azelf naturally outspeed Kommo-o even after a Clangorous Soul, so answers to them like Kingambit, Great Tusk, and Roaring Moon make for good partners. Kommo-o appreciates pivots like Azelf, Sandy Shocks, and Roaring Moon because they can pivot out on their checks like Blissey, Empoleon, and Corviknight and safely bring it in to start threatening the opposing team. Kommo-o greatly appreciates dual screens support from setters like Corviknight and Deoxys-S allowing it to have an easier time setting up with Clangorous Soul or supporting its teammates with Stealth Rock; alternatively, Sticky Web from Smeargle and Ribombee can help it outspeed Choice Scarf revenge killers like Latios, Azelf, and Roaring Moon after a Clangorous Soul.

Clangorous Soul.description: • This EV Spread survives a Chien-Pao Ice Spinner and outspeeds Dragapult after Clangorous Soul.

Setup Sweeper (Fighting).description: An incredible asset for Fighting teams, Kommo-o is often the best wincon on the type thanks to Clangorous Soulblaze, which helps it overcome otherwise difficult matchups such as Dragon, Flying, and Water. Flamethrower takes care of Steel-type Pokemon neutral to Drain Punch like Mega Scizor and Corviknight. Taunt allows Kommo-o to block status moves from defensive Pokemon like Toxapex, Swampert, and Gliscor, preventing them from resetting its boosts with Haze or statusing it with Toxic. Alternatively, Clangorous Soul powers up Kommo-o without using its Z-Move, letting its Clangorous Soulblaze outright OHKO Toxapex and Hippowdon, at the cost of longevity. Bulletproof is Kommo-o's preferred ability to better handle Gholdengo or Aegislash in the Steel matchup. Unboosted Kommo-o's average Speed tier leaves it outsped by threats to Fighting teams like Tornadus-T and Tapu Lele, so Choice Scarf users like Galarian Zapdos and Terrakion are great partners to assist it against them. Iron Valiant's Fairy typing and wide coverage movepool lets it deal with opposing Dragon-types, and it forms a wallbreaking core with Kommo-o by pressuring the likes of Mega Sableye and Ting-Lu. Cobalion and Great Tusk provide Stealth Rock, which maximizes Kommo-o's opportunities to wallbreak after using Clangorous Soulblaze. Great Tusk can also remove entry hazards for Kommo-o with Rapid Spin, and Cobalion has the added bonus of checking Fairy-types like Mega Diancie. Mega Gallade can pressure Poison-, Ground-, and Flying-types like Toxapex, Ting-Lu, and Landorus-T for Kommo-o. It can also outspeed and revenge kill offensive threats to it like Kyurem and Garchomp.

Mixed Omni-Boost Sweeper (Dragon).description: Kommo-o is an exceptional setup sweeper due to its great mixed offensive stats, respectable defenses, and exclusive access to Clangorous Soulblaze; this makes it an amazing tool to clean up Steel, Dark, and Dragon teams late-game. Drain Punch threatens Steel- and Normal-types like Heatran, Blissey, and Porygon-2 as well as increasing Kommo-o's longevity, making it harder for revenge killers to shut it down after using its Z-Move. Additionally, Drain Punch is Kommo-o's best move to hit Ditto, as it copies its ability Soundproof. Flamethrower targets Fighting-resistant or -immune Steel-types such as Mega Scizor, Celesteela, and Aegislash. Taunt is preferred to shut down phazers like Haze Toxapex and Hippowdon and bulky walls like Porygon2 and Clodsire, which can inconvenience Kommo-o with Toxic. Meanwhile, Clangorous Soul allows for more boosts and breaking power, notably enabling Clangorous Soulblaze to OHKO the aforementioned Hippowdon and Toxapex. Furthermore, Clangorous Soulblaze allows Kommo-o to set up on Fairy-types and Soundproof Pokemon like Alolan Ninetales, Trace Porygon2, and opposing Kommo-o. Soundproof prevents revenge killing attempts from Ditto or opposing Kommo-o, and a Naive nature permits Kommo-o to outpace Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Lopunny, and Zeraora after obtaining the omni-boost. Mega Altaria is a wonderful teammate, as it helps weaken and clean up opposing Dragon teams; In return, it appreciates Kommo-o dealing with the aforementioned Steel-types. Kyurem aids in matchups against Flying-types like Tornadus-T, Mantine, and Dragonite, as well as Fairy-types such as Azumarill, Tapu Fini, and Mega Altaria. Choice Scarf Latias and Roaring Moon provide speed control; the former offers healing and setup opportunities with Healing Wish, while the latter checks Psychic-types like Deoxys-S, Victini, and Latias. Garchomp offers entry hazards support to pressure and chip down Kommo-o's switch-ins and aids in the Steel matchup with Earthquake. Hisuian Goodra is a huge help in the Fairy matchup, taking on Tapu Lele, Iron Valiant, and Mega Diancie. Mega Latios threatens Flying-type threats with its BoltBeam coverage; in addition, when paired with Garchomp, it puts a lot of pressure on Poison teams, which Kommo-o tends to struggle against. Cyclizar provides entry hazard control with Rapid Spin and extra protection for Kommo-o with Shed Tail, encouraging the use of Clangorous Soul over Taunt. Baxcalibur is excellent in the Dark and Flying matchups, dispatching threats like Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Enamorus with its Swords Dance or Dragon Dance set, and it also ravages Poison teams with Galarian Slowking, which Kommo-o might not be able to handle. In return, Kommo-o removes the aforementioned Steel- and Normal-types that can easily wall Baxcalibur or use it to reverse sweep, specifically Ditto.

Choice Specs (Electric).description: Tapu Koko is a dominant force within Electric teams due to its exceptional ability, Electric Surge, which its teammates benefit from. Tapu Koko further boasts a good Speed tier and valuable Fairy-typing, rendering it a menacing threat in its own right. Dazzling Gleam levels the playing field in the Dragon matchup, eliminating foes such as Kommo-o, Roaring Moon, Baxcalibur, and Mega Altaria, but it's also useful against threats like Mega Lopunny and non-Choice Scarf Great Tusk. Grass Knot provides much needed coverage against troublesome Ground-types, most notably taking care of Swampert, Quagsire, Gastrodon, and Mamoswine. Volt Switch pairs wells with Tapu Koko's speed, allowing it to escape unfavorable matchups and bring in teammates like Zapdos against the likes of Mega Venusaur or Mega Scizor. Hidden Power Ice can be used to deal with Ground-types that aren't threatened by Grass Knot such as Garchomp and Landorus-T. Alternatively, Thunderbolt can be run to increase Tapu Koko's damage output, giving it a chance to OHKO foes like Mega Diancie. Rotom-W and Zapdos are excellent partners to Tapu Koko, as they provide a necessary Ground immunity as well as Defog support, which allows Tapu Koko to pivot more freely. Rotom-W further helps by handling Ground-types and spreading burns to strong physical attackers like Mega Garchomp, Iron Valiant, Dragonite, and Mega Swampert in rain, while Zapdos walls and makes use of Heat Wave to deal with Steel-types like Ferrothorn and Iron Treads and Hurricane to counter pesky Grass- and Fighting-types like Tapu Bulu, Mega Venusaur, and Mega Gallade. Alolan Raichu's Surge Surfer fully capitalizes on Electric Terrain, turning it into a serious revenge killer, capable of outspeeding threats such as Sand Rush Excadrill, Mega Aerodactyl, and Iron Valiant under Quark Drive. Iron Hands and Zeraora are prominent partners for Tapu Koko complementing it as Physical breakers, both being able to take care of foes such as defensive Zapdos, Ursaluna and Alolan Muk which hinder Tapu Koko and other Special attackers. Iron Hands has more bulk and longevity, but Zeraora brings near unmatched Speed to the table. Both of them also appreciate Tapu Koko's ability to remove Mega Sableye and Skeledirge and luring in and critically damaging Landorus-Therian with Hidden Power Ice. Regieleki brings raw Electric-type power in the form of a boosted Rising Voltage, which is capable of sweeping teams that don't have an answer to it, and it also provides hazard removal thanks to Rapid Spin. Magnezone provides an immunity to Poison, which Tapu Koko appreciates, and more importantly traps and removes threats such as Mega Scizor and Excadrill with Hidden Power Fire.

Fast Pivot (Fairy).description: Boasting a great Speed tier and solid coverage, Tapu Koko not only provides Electric Terrain to enable Iron Valiant, but also provides a means to deal with Flying's defensive core for Fairy teams thanks to its access to Thunderbolt and Hidden Power Ice. Thunderbolt is Tapu Koko's most spammable attack, which it uses to eliminate roadblocks such as Corviknight, Celesteela, and Toxapex, but Discharge can be used to spread paralysis against faster foes. Hidden Power Ice threatens Ground-types such as Landorus and Gliscor. U-turn is its preferred pivot option, as Tapu Koko lures in Ground-types like Ursaluna and Great Tusk that block Volt Switch, which Iron Valiant and Tapu Bulu can then handle. That said, it can also run Toxic to wear down walls like Zapdos and Hippowdon, or Taunt to shut down entry hazard and dual screens setters like Klefki, Jirachi, and Galvantula or setup sweepers like Volcarona. Roost extends Tapu Koko's longevity and thus its opportunities to pivot. Heavy-Duty Boots pairs well with Tapu Koko's role as a pivot, but Expert Belt increases its chances to OHKO Landorus with Hidden Power Ice and Toxapex with Thunderbolt. Tapu Koko's partner in crime on Fairy teams is Iron Valiant, which appreciates being pivoted into for Quark Drive to be activated and returns the favor by dealing with Steel-types like Heatran and Hisuian Goodra, and even some Poison-types like Alolan Muk and Mega Venusaur when using a Fightinium Z and Psychium Z, respectively. Mega Diancie provides some form of hazard control with Magic Bounce, which Tapu Koko especially appreciates if it's not running Heavy-Duty Boots, and it can handle troublesome Flying- and Fire-types such as Volcarona and Mega Charizard Y. Klefki is another great partner, as it sets up screens, allowing Tapu Koko to pivot more freely, and provides a valuable immunity to Poison. Tapu Lele and Tapu Bulu serve as powerful wallbreakers that can weaken the opposing team to allow Tapu Koko to clean late-game. Tapu Lele handles foes such as Clodsire, Mega Venusaur, Nidoking, and even Mega Scizor when running Hidden Power Fire, while Tapu Bulu powers through Ground-types that don't fear Tapu Koko's Hidden Power Ice, such as Mega Swampert, Gastrodon, and Hippowdon. Belly Drum Azumarill also helps in the Ground matchup,and it can utilize its priority move Aqua Jet to eliminate faster threats such as Gengar and Nihilego.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Tapu Koko is a very consistent offensive pivot that can fit on a variety of teams, threatening a plethora of Water- and Flying-types such as Toxapex, Slowbro, Tornadus-T, and Zapdos. Tapu Koko also has a remarkable ability to consistently switch into the tier's Electric-types such as Zapdos and Raging Bolt, the aforementioned Flying-types, and Fighting-types such as Zamazenta while also having a Speed tier that outruns many threats such as Ogerpon-W and Tornadus-T. Hidden Power Ice enables Tapu Koko to hit foes such as Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Garchomp while also doing significant damage to Great Tusk. Dazzling Gleam can be used to hit foes such as Raging Bolt and Great Tusk much harder than Hidden Power Ice, though it is significantly weaker against Gliscor and Landorus-T. U-turn allows Tapu Koko to pivot out of Pokemon that handle it defensively such as Galarian Slowking and Ting-Lu while also wearing them down. Volt Switch can be used to avoid chip from contact while dealing decent damage, though it is able to be blocked by Ground-type Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Landorus-T. Electrium Z is used to give Tapu Koko a one-time boost to its already strong Thunderbolt and help it pick off weakened threats such as Melmetal and Heatran and OHKO Pokemon such as Ogerpon-W and Mega Diancie. Fairium Z can be used as an alternative to immediately OHKO foes such as Great Tusk and Raging Bolt.

Pokemon such as Iron Valiant and Hawlucha appreciate Tapu Koko’s Electric Surge setting Electric Terrain and activating their abilities. The former also appreciates Tapu Koko beating defensive Pokemon such as Toxapex and Tornadus-T. Landorus-T also likes Tapu Koko as a partner, as it likes its Flying-type checks such as Tornadus-T, Zapdos, and Corviknight being answered by Tapu Koko. In return, Landorus-T brings it in with a U-turn on Pokemon such as Tornadus-T and it immediately threatens Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking, which walls Tapu Koko. Tapu Koko struggles to break through specially bulky Pokemon such as Ferrothorn, Galarian Slowking and Ting-Lu, so it appreciates powerful physical wallbreakers such as Mega Medicham, Urshifu-R as well as Pursuit support from Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar. In return, Tapu Koko is able to easily pivot them in with U-turn on these aforementioned checks in addition to checking the Flying-type Pokemon that they struggle with.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Tapu Koko makes use of its fast Speed and explosive power to act as a great early-game wallbreaker, dealing out large damage even against neutral targets like Tapu Lele, Gholdengo, and Zapdos. Tapu Koko's Speed allows it to outspeed Pokemon already considered fast, such as Ogerpon-W, Mega Diancie, and Mega Charizard Y. As Tapu Koko breaks down walls like Alomomola and Slowbro, Pokemon like Hawlucha can use that opportunity to clean up easily late-game. Either Volt Switch or U-turn allows Tapu Koko to exert pressure while providing pivoting for the team, with the former being a respectable offensive move itself, while the latter is undeterred by Ground-types such as Garchomp. Hidden Power Ice allows Tapu Koko to do massive damage to Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Great Tusk, notably OHKOing Landorus-T.

Tapu Koko fits best on offensive teams, as its Speed, wallbreaking power, and pivoting options are most appreciated by its offensively minded teammates. Due to Tapu Koko's Electric Terrain and its wallbreaking prowess, Quark Drive Pokemon are the clearest beneficiaries, especially those that seek to sweep late-game like Swords Dance Iron Valiant and Iron Moth. Other sweepers also synergize with Tapu Koko, largely since it puts major pressure on some of their checks. For example, Hawlucha appreciates the removal of Slowbro, Moltres, and Toxapex, while Dragonite appreciates the removal of Corviknight and Moltres. Tapu Koko's STAB moves can be walled by several Pokemon, such as Clodsire, Ferrothorn, and Iron Treads. As a result, it appreciates help from the likes of Mega Medicham, Weavile, and Great Tusk. Mega Medicham especially makes for a fierce wallbreaking duo with Tapu Koko, with the former able to dismantle Galarian Slowking and Ferrothorn, two Pokemon that can easily wall Tapu Koko. In return, Tapu Koko can pressure Pokemon that Mega Medicham may struggle to hit, notably Gholdengo and Slowbro.

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Tapu Koko serves as a potent special attacker and wincon, thanks to Terrain-boosted Thunderbolt and its great Speed stat, allowing it to outspeed common foes that are considered fast, such as Mega Diancie and Ogerpon-W. Using its Calm Mind boosts, Tapu Koko deals a great amount of damage to neutral targets, such as Ogerpon-W, Gholdengo, and Tapu Lele. Tapu Koko can even OHKO Electric-resistant and -immune threats, such as Raging Bolt and Gliscor after Stealth Rock chip using Twinkle Tackle boosted by Fairium Z after one Calm Mind boost. Calm Mind boosts make Tapu Koko capable of setting up in front of foes like Clefable and Raging Bolt. Roost offers reliable recovery, increasing Tapu Koko's longevity by shrugging off attacks from foes like Raging Bolt and healing off entry hazard damage.

Calm Mind Tapu Koko fits well on balance teams that appreciate its ability to both revenge kill fast threats like Ogerpon-W and act as a wincon late-game. Pokemon like Urshifu-R and Volcarona benefit from Tapu Koko's ability to pressure bulky Water- and Flying-type foes, such as Toxapex and Moltres; Urshifu-R appreciates the removal of Toxapex and Alomomola while Volcarona appreciates the removal of Moltres and Toxapex. In return, Volcarona and Urshifu-R deal with troublesome walls like Ferrothorn and Ting Lu. Entry hazards like Stealth Rock and Spikes synergize incredibly with Tapu Koko, as they help it secure KOs more reliably and clean up late-game, wearing down checks like Heatran and Ferrothorn. Therefore, entry hazard setters like Ferrothorn, Ting-Lu, and Gliscor are solid partners. Ferrothorn is a notable hazard-setting partner, as it is also able to switch in on troublesome foes for Tapu Koko, such as Melmetal and Ting Lu. There are several Pokemon that can take on Tapu Koko's STAB combination even after Calm Mind boosts, such as Galarian Slowking and Heatran. As a result, Tapu Koko appreciates teammates that threaten these Pokemon, such as Great Tusk and Mega Medicham. Tapu Koko is vulnerable to Ground-types, such as Choice Scarf Landorus-T and Iron Treads, especially because the latter can also take hits from Tapu Koko; therefore, defensive checks like Alomomola and Zapdos are great partners due to their ability to switch in on these Ground-types.

Dual Screens.description:
Tapu Koko's high Speed allows it to act as a good dual screens lead for hyper offense structures. U-turn gives Tapu Koko a source of momentum for and way to pivot into its teammates, notably being able to pivot against Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Great Tusk that Tapu Koko struggles with. Taunt allows Tapu Koko to deny opposing setup from foes, whether it be entry hazards like Spikes from Ferrothorn or boosting moves like Quiver Dance from Volcarona; this is essential so that Tapu Koko is not completely passive as it sets up, which is especially important to make sure its teammates are not overwhelmed by hazards or boosted threats afterwards.

Because of its ability to set Electric Terrain as it sets up dual screens, Quark Drive Pokemon such as Iron Valiant, Iron Moth, and Iron Crown make for fantastic partners, which are able to utilize Tapu Koko's dual screens to set up more comfortably. Iron Moth in particular is able to threaten Corviknight from removing screens via Defog and check Gholdengo, which sets up on Tapu Koko thanks to Good as Gold ignoring Taunt. Similarly, Hawlucha makes for a fantastic teammate, since it is able to reliably set up on the Ground-types that Tapu Koko doesn't like, such as Landorus-T and Iron Treads, while having Taunt to prevent Defog attempts from Zapdos and Tornadus-T; in return, Tapu Koko's Electric Terrain triggers Unburden for Hawlucha through Electric Seed to outspeed threats like Mega Swampert in rain, and boosted Iron Valiant, letting the two handle opposing offense teams more comfortably. Typical offensive threats such as Garchomp, Gholdengo, and Volcarona all appreciate dual screens support for their setup, with the former also being able to set up Stealth Rock to soften up walls while Gholdengo helps maintain dual screens by blocking Defog from Tornadus-T and Corviknight. Terapagos is a strong partner too, being able to remove hazards that Tapu Koko cannot deny safely, such as from Landorus-T, Great Tusk, and Gliscor.

Psychic Terrain Setter.description:
• Despite being relatively slow and having underwhelming stats compared to the rest of the tier, Tapu Lele's Psychic Surge can be incredibly useful to many powerful Psychic-types, increasing their power while protecting them from otherwise-crippling priority such as Sucker Punch from Yveltal, Shadow Sneak from Marshadow and Giratina-O, and Extreme Speed from Arceus.
  • Taunt prevents slower Pokemon such as Ho-Oh from using Defog against Tapu Lele and also stops entry hazards from setters such as Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Glimmora. This can be particularly handy against Smeargle, as blocking it from setting Sticky Web prevents foes from outspeeding teammates such as Deoxys-A and Ultra Necrozma.
  • Moonblast threatens Dark-types such as Yveltal and Arceus-Dark, preventing them from aggressively switching into Tapu Lele or anti-leading against it, and the move also hits Giratina-O for a good amount of damage to dissuade it from switching into Tapu Lele, especially if it has already been dealt chip damage from a teammate.
  • Either Psyshock or Psychic can be used to threaten most switch-ins that don't really mind Moonblast, particularly Eternatus and Primal Groudon; Psychic hits harder and hits Pokemon like Primal Groudon, but Psyshock does more damage to specially defensive Pokemon like Ho-Oh, Chansey, and Calm Mind Arceus formes.
  • Nature's Madness makes it unsafe for virtually any Pokemon, including Chansey and Ho-Oh, to sit on Tapu Lele in an attempt to stall out Psychic Terrain turns, allowing it to unconditionally weaken such foes if they are left in and possibly even put them into OHKO range for its other moves.
  • Terastallizing Tapu Lele should only be done if absolutely necessary, as many Psychic Terrain sweepers strongly value Tera. Tera Normal can allow Tapu Lele to defeat Marshadow one-on-one in a pinch and blank Deoxys-A's Shadow Ball and Lunala's Moongeist Beam, which can be particularly handy when facing opposing Psychic Terrain and Ditto. Tera Steel can work to block Mortal Spin from Glimmora, which can be particularly handy when Tapu Lele is paired with Sticky Web. Tera Fairy lets Tapu Lele's Moonblast OHKO offensive Yveltal while doing a strong amount of damage to defensive ones, and it lets Tapu Lele relatively easily handle Arceus-Dark by itself by giving it a resistance to its STAB move and doing extremely heavy damage to it.
  • While Tapu Lele has usable Special Attack and benefits from Psychic Terrain itself, its power pales in comparison to Pokemon such as Deoxys-A and Ultra Necrozma, so it should stay in for as few turns as possible to maximize the number of turns teammates have to use Psychic Terrain. However, even though its bulk and typing are sufficient to let it switch into many attacks, Tapu Lele's lack of pivot and self-sacrifice moves along with the general fraility and common shared weaknesses of most potential teammates can turn this into a double-edged sword after it is sent in; it can sometimes get stuck on the field for multiple turns after coming in, consuming precious turns of Psychic Terrain without being able to meaningfully make progress, and it can also become setup fodder for Dragon Dance Ultra Necrozma and Arceus-Ground. As such, achieving maximum turns of Psychic Terrain often involves risky play that leads to either sacrificing Tapu Lele or, because there is value to preserve Tapu Lele later to reset Psychic Terrain, a teammate. To minimize this, opportunities to save a suicide lead, if run, after it has set entry hazards by switching Tapu Lele into attacks that it can survive such as Sacred Fire from Ho-Oh, Low Kick from Marshadow, and Judgment from support Arceus formes and immediately switching back into the lead on the next attack can beneficial for this purpose.
  • Preserving Tapu Lele in stall matchups can allow it to stallbreak with Nature's Madness and Taunt.
  • When resetting Psychic Terrain, it can be appropriate to just use Tapu Lele as death fodder against offensive teams, as it only needs to survive entry hazard damage to set Psychic Terrain, allowing teammates to use the maximum amount of Psychic Terrain turns. However, there is some merit in switching it into priority moves, particuarly against common Choice Band users such as Rayquaza and Marshadow. This dynamic can also dissuade priority users from using priority moves even if Psychic Terrain is not active for fear of giving Tapu Lele a safe switch to reset the Terrain for free yet again.
  • It may be useful to keep Tapu Lele in if it can do something meaningful, such as using Taunt to prevent opposing entry hazards, Defog, or setup from slower Speed boosters such as Rock Polish Primal Groudon and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM.
  • Tapu Lele's influence comes from the Pokemon it enables. Meteor Beam Deoxys-A is the biggest beneficiary of Psychic Terrain, as it deeply appreciates priority protection of all sorts due to its nonexistent bulk while often taking out Pokemon such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal with its Meteor Beam, at which point it can spam an absurdly powerful Expanding Force that is sufficient to OHKO almost everything it hits neutrally at +1, including defensive Primal Groudon, offensive Arceus formes, offensive Primal Kyogre, and Terastallized Eternatus. Additionally due to the Psychic Terrain, Deoxys-A being less reliant on Tera to avoid priority makes it even easier to fit onto teams. Ultra Necrozma's bulk in base forme, powerful Light That Burns the Sky, and ability to set up with Dragon Dance complement the general fast, frail special attackers otherwise used as teammates, warding against counterplay in specially defensive Pokemon like Ho-Oh and Primal Kyogre while not being overly reliant on Psychic Terrain to sweep like Expanding Force users. Ultra Necrozma also particularly enjoys protection against Marshadow's Shadow Sneak and Yveltal's Sucker Punch and the potential of teammates and Tapu Lele itself to threaten Yveltal and Arceus-Dark.
  • Glimmora can also be a good teammate, as it is very consistent at setting various entry hazards to put bulkier Pokemon such as Arceus formes into OHKO range for teammates while preventing opposing hazards and threatening Ho-Oh and Yveltal with its Power Gem. Alternatively, while they are less consistent at getting Stealth Rock up, Sticky Web from setters such as Smeargle and Shuckle may provide some added insurance against opposing opposing speedy or otherwise dangerous threats such as Deoxys-A, Ultra Necrozma, Zacian-C, and Booster Energy Flutter Mane. Sticky Web can be particularly helpful in allowing for the freer use of potential teammates such as Lunala, Basculegion, and Mega Mewtwo Y while also potentially freeing up team members such as Deoxys-A to not run Speed-boosting natures for more power. Ditto may be appropriate to handle Speed boosters such as Arceus-Ground as well as Sticky Web sweepers.

Choice Specs (Psychic).description: Choice Specs Tapu Lele is an invaluable asset for Psychic teams thanks to its monstrous Special Attack, secondary Fairy typing, and Psychic Terrain to further bolster the power of it and its teammates' Psychic moves while also blocking priority moves like Sucker Punch from Hisuian Samurott and Bisharp. These traits let it serve as a potent wallbreaker that can batter down Dragon-, Normal-, and Water-type defensive cores. Moonblast hits foes like Ting-Lu, Alolan Muk, and Slowking. Focus Blast covers Steel-types like Heatran, Ferrothorn, Hisuian Goodra, and Empoleon that would otherwise comfortably switch into its STAB moves. Thunderbolt nails Steel / Flying types like Celesteela and Corviknight as well as bulky Water-types like the aforementioned Empoleon and Slowking, while Psyshock targets special walls like Galarian Slowking and Blissey. Hidden Power Fire can also be used to OHKO Mega Scizor and Ferrothorn while also 2HKOing Gholdengo. Choice Specs Tapu Lele fits best on bulky offense and hyper offense teams. Mega Gallade and Victini improve the Steel matchup, handling foes like Hisuian Goodra and Gholdengo while eliminating special walls like Alolan Muk. Mega Gallade also assists in Ground and Flying matchups with its access to Triple Axel, while Victini takes care of certain Steel-types like Mega Scizor and Celesteela. In return, Tapu Lele can break through the likes of Mega Sableye, Slowbro, and Zapdos for them. Jirachi can bring Tapu Lele in safely with U-turn and set Stealth Rock to wear down checks to it like Alolan Muk and Corviknight. Slowbro can take on physical attackers like Excadrill, Sneasler, and Mega Aerodactyl. Both teammates can also spread paralysis to slow down foes like Tornadus-T, making it easier for Tapu Lele to break past them. Slowbro can also run Colbur Berry. which can better enable it to either cripple Dark-types like Meowscarada and Roaring Moon with paralysis or severely weaken or eliminate them with Body Press or Ice Beam, with the latter also hitting Mega Altaria. On hyper offense teams, Tapu Lele appreciates both entry hazards and dual screens support from Deoxys-S. Iron Crown is an excellent partner, benefiting from Tapu Lele's Psychic Terrain powering up its Stored Power and blocking revenge killing attempts from priority users while it eases Fairy and Electric matchups in return. Choice Scarf Latias and Iron Boulder provide valuable speed control, handling threats like Mega Lopunny and Choice Scarf Blacephalon; Latias also offers additional utility in the form of Trick and Healing Wish, while Iron Boulder can threaten +1 Volcarona and even outspeed faster Choice Scarf users like Roaring Moon and Meowscarada.

Choice Scarf (Psychic).description: Choice Scarf Tapu Lele is one of Psychic teams' greatest revenge killers. Its decent Speed tier and astounding offensive prowess combined with its great typing makes it extremely threatening because with access to STAB Moonblast, it is Psychic's best check to most Dark-type threats. Tapu Lele's presence also sets up Psychic Terrain, shielding itself and its team from dangerous priority such as Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak and Mega Scizor's Bullet Punch. Focus Blast lets it easily take care of the pesky Steel-types that resist its STAB attacks such as Ferrothorn, Heatran, and Iron Treads. Future Sight lets Tapu Lele set up an attack for later and then switch out to a teammate such as Victini or Mega Gallade to help it set up or get a KO. Shadow Ball lets it beat Gholdengo and clean up against Psychic and Ghost teams, while Thunderbolt gives it general coverage versus foes like Mantine and Celesteela. Tapu Lele is often not able to beat specially defensive walls such as Alolan Muk and Blissey; hence, it appreciates partnering up with Mega Gallade to eliminate them. Mega Alakazam is a good partner, as it helps in the Electric and Water matchups courtesy of Trace copying Surge Surfer and Swift Swim, respectively, and it appreciates Tapu Lele's Psychic Terrain boosting its Expanding Force. Slowbro sponges hits from faster Choice Scarf users such as Terrakion and Galarian Zapdos, and can also pivot Tapu Lele in with Teleport to wreak havoc. Victini and Armarouge can eliminate Steel-types, especially Aegislash and Gholdengo, easing the burden for Tapu Lele. Jirachi can slow teams down with Thunder Wave and pivot Tapu Lele into physical walls such as Mandibuzz and Slowbro with U-turn.

Choice Scarf (Fairy).description: Tapu Lele's Psychic Surge ability and complementary STAB types along with excellent coverage moves allow it to shine as a cleaner on Fairy teams. Psychic is its preferred Psychic-type STAB move, which it uses to take out Poison-types such as Toxapex, Nidoking, and Mega Venusaur, though it can also run Psyshock to hit Clodsire harder. Moonblast deals with Dark- and Dragon-types like Mega Sableye, Galarian Moltres, Kommo-o, and Latias. Focus Blast checks threats such as Heatran and Iron Treads. Hidden Power Fire OHKOes most Mega Scizor sets, while Thunderbolt threatens a wider selection of Water- and Flying-types like Celesteela, Mantine, and Mega Charizard Y. Shadow Ball could also be used to provide coverage against Aegislash and Gholdengo. Thanks to Psychic Surge, Tapu Lele shuts down priority moves from revenge killers and setup sweepers such as Mega Scizor's Bullet Punch, Azumarill's Aqua Jet, and Dragonite's Extreme Speed, allowing it to KO them with Hidden Power Fire, Thunderbolt, and Moonblast, respectively. Choice Scarf allows Tapu Lele to outspeed threats such as Zeraora, Choice Scarf Excadrill, Tapu Koko, and Mega Lopunny. Tapu Lele pairs well with wallbreakers like Tapu Bulu and Azumarill that can weaken or eliminate its checks, with the former taking care of Meowscarada, Rotom-W, and Gastrodon, while the latter handles Volcarona, Choice Scarf Blacephalon, and Landorus. Tapu Koko helps in the Water- and Flying-type matchups by dealing with Landorus and Corviknight and offers a great Speed tier and coverage. Iron Valiant answers Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra and uses All-Out Pummeling to eliminate Dark-types like Alolan Muk, one of the best counters to Tapu Lele, and Ting-Lu, which could tank a few hits from Tapu Lele and threaten it with Poison Jab or Heavy Slam. The duo of Tapu Koko and Iron Valiant further assists Tapu Lele's late-game cleaning, as Tapu Koko activates Iron Valiant's Quark Drive, allowing it to outspeed common Choice Scarf users that are faster than Tapu Lele like Terrakion, Blacephalon, and Nihilego. Klefki's utility moves, such as Spikes, Thunder Wave, and dual screens, make it an excellent supporting partner. Thanks to Foul Play, Klefki is also able to answer bulky Swords Dance Mega Scizor, which could otherwise tank a Hidden Power Fire from Tapu Lele and KO it. Mega Diancie contributes to keeping Tapu Lele healthy by threatening hazard setters with Magic Bounce as well as Fire-types like Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona, which can be troublesome to deal with for Tapu Lele. Mimikyu is a great partner in the Ghost matchup, being able to threaten fast foes such as Blacephalon. Ribombee's Sticky Web allows Tapu Lele to outrun faster Choice Scarf users such as Sneasler, Iron Valiant, and Gengar.

Calm Mind (Fairy).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Tapu Lele functions as a great speed control option while still retaining its devastating STAB combination and good wallbreaking power. Its STAB moves threaten a myriad of foes such as Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and unboosted Garchomp that would otherwise outspeed Tapu Lele, while Focus Blast nails Steel-types like Melmetal, Ferrothorn, and Kingambit. Hidden Power Fire allows Tapu Lele to hit Mega Scizor and Gholdengo super effectively, while Psyshock lets Tapu Lele break through specially defensive walls, 2HKOing Galarian Slowking as an example. Future Sight allows Tapu Lele to set up its teammates that otherwise struggle with Poison-types and physical walls, like Zamazenta or Mega Lopunny, to pose an even larger threat considering their best checks like Toxapex and Alomomola are reticent to switch in lest they get blasted.

Tapu Lele fits well on balance teams looking for a way to solve their speed control problems while retaining good power. Fighting-types like the aforementioned pair as well as Urshifu-R make natural partners for Tapu Lele, as both break one another's checks; the Fighting-types break through troublesome Steel-types like Ferrothorn and specially defensive Heatran so that Tapu Lele does not have to risk Focus Blast's accuracy woes while Tapu Lele scares out Poison-types like Toxapex to let the trio of Fighting-types break through. Said Fighting-types also help wonders against Pursuit trappers such as Mega Tyranitar and Kingambit attempting to trap and remove Tapu Lele. Mega Tyranitar is another great partner for Tapu Lele, as it removes a pair of Tapu Lele's biggest checks in Gholdengo and Galarian Slowking thanks to Pursuit while dealing major damage to specially defensive stopgaps such as Heatran. Hazard setters like Gliscor and Ferrothorn also pair well with Tapu Lele, as they weaken Tapu Lele's checks like offensive Gholdengo and Ferrothorn into range of being KOed by one of Tapu Lele's STAB options or Hidden Power Fire, lessening its burden of prediction.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Tapu Lele functions as a potent wallbreaker, being able to muscle through common defensive cores with its STAB move combination and coverage. Moonblast and Psychic largely cover each other's weaknesses, making it difficult for defensive pieces such as Ting-Lu and Toxapex to switch in. Psyshock hits Pokemon with high Special Defense, such as Blissey and Galarian Slowking. Focus Blast targets Steel-types such as Kingambit, Heatran, and Melmetal, while Hidden Power Fire threatens Mega Scizor, Gholdengo, and Ferrothorn more reliably. Focus Blast is generally preferred to avoid getting fully walled by Heatran, which can otherwise switch in reliably.

Fighting-types such as Urshifu-R and Zamazenta appreciate Tapu Lele's ability to punch through checks such as Toxapex and Mega Venusaur. In return, both teammates break through Steel-types, and Urshifu-R beats Moltres, enabling Tapu Lele to use its STAB moves more freely; they also beat Pursuit trappers that can sometimes be problematic for Tapu Lele. Tapu Lele also appreciates Pursuit users such as Mega Tyranitar and Kingambit trapping Ghost-types such as Gholdengo. Tapu Lele often finds itself vulnerable to faster threats such as Ogerpon-W and Weavile, meaning fast teammates such as Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant are appreciated. Tapu Lele also appreciates Spikes setters such as Ting-Lu and Ferrothorn, with Ting-Lu providing a good switch-in to Gholdengo, which Tapu Lele struggles with. Tapu Lele values Spikes, as it chips common checks such as Heatran, allowing Tapu Lele to clean up games more easily. In general, setup sweepers benefit from Psychic Terrain support, notably including Dragonite, Scale Shot Garchomp, and Volcarona, as it gives them an immunity to powerful priority moves from Pokemon such as Kingambit and Mega Lopunny. Tapu Lele also breaks Pokemon such as Ting-Lu for these teammates.

Offensive Z-Move.description:
Tapu Lele is a fearsome wallbreaker, attributing its success to its Psychic Terrain-boosted attacks, ability to threaten metagame staples such as Gliscor, Toxapex, Raging Bolt, and Great Tusk, and lack of prediction mandated by a Choice item. Focus Blast allows Tapu Lele to hit the Steel-types that would plague it, such as Melmetal, Kingambit, Ferrothorn, and Heatran. Psyshock is an option over Psychic to hit Pokemon like Volcarona, Galarian Slowking, and Blissey; however, Psychic is usually preferred due to its higher damage against targets like Moltres and Gliscor. Hidden Power Fire and Future Sight are other options over Calm Mind; the former is a consistent way of hitting Ferrothorn, Mega Scizor, and Gholdengo, whereas the latter pairs well with wallbreakers like Zamazenta and Ogerpon-W while also being Tapu Lele’s strongest form of Shattered Psyche. Psychium Z gives Tapu Lele a burst of power that guarantees the OHKO on Pokemon like Clefable, Tornadus-T, and Gliscor. With Fightinium Z, Tapu Lele OHKOes Melmetal lacking Assault Vest and Assault Vest Kingambit while also having a favorable roll to OHKO Ferrothorn after Stealth Rock.

Tapu Lele is a good option on offense and bulky offense teams that appreciate it punching holes in fat and balance teams, which have limited ways of pivoting around it. Pokemon like Kingambit, Zamazenta, and Ogerpon-W like Tapu Lele breaking through their checks such as Toxapex, Raging Bolt, and Great Tusk. These Pokemon also appreciate the potential Future Sight support Tapu Lele can give. Tapu Lele likes Pursuit from Weavile, Mega Tyranitar, and Kingambit, as they help remove checks such as Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Assault Vest Tornadus-T. Tapu Lele has a middling Speed tier that allows threats like Ogerpon-W and Mega Charizard Y to easily outpace and revenge kill it. Therefore, teammates like Garchomp, Ferrothorn, and Kingambit are appreciated. However, it should be noted that Psychic Terrain blocks Kingambit’s Sucker Punch.

Assault Vest.description:
This set aims to bolster Tapu Lele's special bulk, allowing it to soft-check Pokemon like Raging Bolt and opposing Tapu Lele while still breaking through physically defensive foes such as Landorus-T and Great Tusk. Psychic is good at chunking physical walls like Garganacl and Gliscor, while Psyshock works well against Galarian Slowking, Blissey, and Clodsire. Focus Blast lets Tapu Lele beat out most Steel-types like Kingambit and Iron Treads along with Mega Tyranitar, while Hidden Power Fire enables Tapu Lele to incinerate Mega Scizor, Ferrothorn, and Gholdengo. 176 Speed EVs on Tapu Lele allow it to outrun Adamant maximum Speed Rillaboom and Hisuian Samurott.

Assault Vest Tapu Lele fits well on offensive teams that need it to sponge special attacks while also threatening foes like Great Tusk and Raging Bolt. It also has the ability to block priority moves, which is appreciated by Gholdengo and Iron Valiant, since they're protected against Kingambit and Mega Scizor, respectively, among others. Steel-type teammates like Melmetal and Heatran pair nicely with Tapu Lele, due to it threatening out Fighting-types like Great Tusk and Iron Valiant that these Pokemon would otherwise lose to; in return, they beat foes like Roaring Moon and Gholdengo for it. Tapu Lele is weak to physical attacks, so physical walls like Landorus-T and Great Tusk are a good fit with it to cover for physical threats like Heavy Slam Zamazenta and Garchomp, while Tapu Lele takes special attacks from the likes of Kyurem and Raging Bolt. Pivoting moves like U-turn from the aforementioned Landorus-T and Moltres are also appreciated for safely bringing in Tapu Lele. Hawlucha is good to consider with Psychic Seed, allowing it to activate Unburden and clean Steel-types like Melmental and Kingambit, while Tapu Lele helps it deal with Poison-types like Toxapex and Clodsire with its Psychic-type STAB moves.

Swords Dance.description: Tapu Bulu's strong offenses, access to Swords Dance, and Grassy Terrain-boosted STAB attacks make it a potent physical wallbreaker, being able to tear through prominent Ground- and Water-types in the tier such as Hippowdon, Slowbro, and Gastrodon. On top of this, Tapu Bulu's solid defensive profile also allows it to serve as an effective check to certain offensive threats such as Thundurus, Zeraora, and Keldeo, while Grassy Surge allows it to support its team with additional passive recovery, as well as lessening the damage of Earthquake, a common attacking move seen on Pokemon such as Excadrill and Mega Aerodactyl. However, Tapu Bulu's common weaknesses to attacking types such as Fire, Flying, and Steel, mediocre Speed tier, and heavy reliance on prediction to get past certain walls such as Mega Venusaur and Celesteela tend to limit its consistency in the long run. In addition, Grassy Terrain, while beneficial, can also backfire due to it healing opposing grounded Pokemon as well. Stone Edge gives Tapu Bulu a way to hit Fire- and Flying-types such as Victini and Thundurus; when powered up by Rockium Z, it turns into a perfectly accurate move that also deals enormous damage to natural targets such as Celesteela, Amoonguss, and Mega Latias at +2, letting it break through them. High Horsepower gives Tapu Bulu a way to hit Steel-types such as Aegislash, Excadrill, and Bisharp super effectively. The given EV spread maximizes Tapu Bulu's bulk, whilst allowing it to outspeed Adamant Tyranitar and Modest Celesteela. Alternatively, a spread of 252 Atk / 4 SpD / 252 Spe can be used to maximize Tapu Bulu's offensive potential, most notably ensuring a guaranteed OHKO on maximum HP Aegislash with High Horsepower and defensive Celesteela and Amoonguss with Contential Crush at +2. By virtue of its defensive qualities, Tapu Bulu is best suited to defensive teams which can capitalize on its long-term prowess. Pokemon such as Aegislash, Excadrill, and Slowking each appreciate the residual effects brought on by Grassy Terrain, which can allow them to play more aggressively; in return, these Pokemon can help pivot into several of Tapu Bulu's answers, such as Celesteela and Mega Venusaur, while Slowking also helps check Fire-types such as Victini. Additionally, other defensive Pokemon such as Slowbro, Clefable, and Hippowdon can also benefit from Grassy Surge while supporting Tapu Bulu's team against offensive threats such as Iron Moth, in addition to providing entry hazards and pivoting support. However, it should be noted that Hippowdon will often need to run alternative Ground-type STAB options to remain effective under Grassy Terrain. Faster teammates such as Choice Scarf Hydreigon, Zeraora, and Choice Scarf Mienshao can assist in revenge killing Tapu Bulu’s checks, and they benefit from Tapu Bulu's ability to help them overwhelm pivots such as Celesteela, Tangrowth, and Amoonguss.

Swords Dance (Fairy).description: Tapu Bulu is a fearsome wallbreaker, boasting synergistic coverage moves that help Fairy teams in a variety of matchups like Water, Electric, and Ground. Close Combat targets Steel-types like Heatran and Ferrothorn. Should Fightinium Z be used, All-Out Pummeling heavily damages the likes of Celesteela and Corviknight after a Swords Dance boost. High Horsepower heavily damages Aegislash and Gholdengo and lets Tapu Bulu be a massive asset against Steel and Water teams by hitting Toxapex for heavy damage. Substitute allows Tapu Bulu to set up on passive Pokemon such as Toxapex, Swampert, and Mega Sableye, while Zen Headbutt is its best move against Mega Venusaur and Crobat. Klefki is a great teammate, as it sets up Spikes to ease Tapu Bulu's wallbreaking as well as Reflect and Light Screen to provide more setup opportunities. Mega Diancie threatens Flying- and Fire-types like Zapdos, Dragonite, and Volcarona for Tapu Bulu. In return, Tapu Bulu checks Gastrodon, Heatran, and Clodsire, letting Mega Diancie have more leeway on its moveset. Similarly, Tapu Koko is heavily appreciated, as it also deals with Flying-types like Tornadus-T and Mega Charizard Y and relieves Tapu Bulu of having to use Fightinium Z, or waste its Z-Move, to threaten Corviknight and Celesteela.

Choice Scarf (Water).description: Choice Scarf Tapu Fini is a reliable revenge killer for Water teams that is especially effective at threatening Dark and Dragon teams thanks to its Fairy typing; it also brings valuable utility to the team in the form of Defog and Misty Terrain. Moonblast targets Dark-, Dragon-, and Fighting-types like Greninja, Hydreigon, and Kommo-o. Ice Beam allows Tapu Fini to reliably hit Flying- and Ground-types like Tornadus-T and the Landorus formes without relying on Hydro Pump’s faulty accuracy. Alternatively, Trick can be used to neuter defensive switch-ins like Ferrothorn and Blissey. Knock Off can be used when Trick is not to punish common switch-ins like Hisuian Goodra, Galarian Slowking, and Articuno by removing Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots, cutting down on their longevity. Defog lets Tapu Fini support its teammates with entry hazard removal. Swampert and Mega Swampert make excellent partners for Tapu Fini, leveraging their Electric immunity to take on threats like Iron Hands and Regieleki. They can also set Stealth Rock, generate momentum with Flip Turn, and threaten Poison-types like Toxapex and Alolan Muk. Choice Specs Greninja can use Sludge Wave and Extrasensory to target Grass- and Poison-types like Ogerpon-W, Mega Venusaur, and Toxapex while also eliminating Galarian Slowking. Greninja also synergizes well with Tapu Fini to break down Dragon teams. Keldeo, Ogerpon-W, and Barraskewda provide Fighting-type coverage to tear through walls like Ferrothorn and Hisuian Goodra as well as eliminate Kyurem. Toxapex's high physical bulk, neutrality to Grass, resistance to Steel and Poison, and access to Haze and Scald allow it to check threats like Meowscarada, Mega Scizor, and Sneasler. Empoleon can handle foes like Choice Specs Kyurem and Tapu Lele while also providing Stealth Rock, Flip Turn, Knock Off, or Defog support, relieving Tapu Fini of Defog duties in the latter scenario.

Calm Mind.description: • Calm Mind Tapu Fini is the premier setup sweeper in the tier.

Choice Specs.description:
• The given EV spread allows Tapu Fini to survive Wild Charge from Iron Hands.
  • Hydro Pump allows Tapu Fini to OHKO non-Assault Vest Incineroar.

Support.description: • Support Tapu Fini is primarily used for its defensive profile on sun teams.

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Tapu Fini acts as a threatening wincon and defensive piece, answering common offensive threats such as Zamazenta, Urshifu-R, and Weavile with ease. Misty Surge allows it and its teammates to set up and pivot without fearing status. Draining Kiss, when coupled with Calm Mind, can turn Tapu Fini into a dangerous wincon that can damage and recover health against foes such as Alomomola and Slowbro. Taunt is used to deny recovery from foes such as Toxapex, pivoting from Galarian Slowking and Slowbro, and status such as Ferrothorn's Leech Seed as well as Toxapex's and Alomomola's Toxic after Misty Terrain has ended. 192 Speed EVs are used in order for Tapu Fini to outspeed maximum Speed Modest Heatran. Leftovers improves Tapu Fini's longevity across a game, making up for its lack of reliable recovery.

Calm Mind Tapu Fini fits primarily on bulky offense teams, where its role as a bulky wincon and switch-in to Dark- and Fighting-types is appreciated. Teammates such as Gholdengo and Pecharunt that struggle with Dark-types like Weavile and Hisuian Samurott therefore appreciate Tapu Fini's defensive capabilities, with both in return providing a switch-in to Grass-types such as Rillaboom and Serperior. Other good partners include Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Heatran, both of which provide another Grass-type resistance, with the former being able to answer Ogerpon-W decently well; they also offer a Steel-type resistance against opposing Mega Scizor and Melmetal. In return, Tapu Fini provides a Fighting-type resistance to moves from foes such as Zamazenta and Urshifu-R. Tapu Fini also often finds breaking down Steel-types difficult, meaning teammates such as Zamazenta and Fire-types such as Volcarona are greatly appreciated. In exchange, Tapu Fini can switch in on and find setup opportunities against Water-types such as Toxapex and Slowbro that could otherwise prove troublesome. Tapu Fini struggles to break through Assault Vest Alomomola, making Ogerpon-W which can prevent it from gaining momentum and immediately threaten it with Power Whip, an excellent partner. In exchange, Tapu Fini can threaten Dragon-types like Dragonite that would otherwise be able to set up on Ogerpon-W. Another problem Tapu Fini can have is against Electric-types such as Tapu Koko and Raging Bolt, meaning Ground-types such as Ting-Lu and specially defensive Gliscor are excellent partners; in return, Tapu Fini provides an excellent Water-type resistance that helps against Urshifu-R and Scald Toxapex, neither of which the aforementioned Ground-types would want to stay in against. Tapu Fini is able to break through common Fighting-types such as Zamazenta and Great Tusk as well as Dark-types like Hisuian Samurott, meaning Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit enjoy Tapu Fini's presence. Additionally, Tapu Fini's Misty Terrain makes them less vulnerable to burns from foes such as Toxapex and Moltres as well as Static from Zapdos. In exchange, these Dark-types can muscle their way through Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking and Slowbro, which Tapu Fini can otherwise struggle with. Fighting-types like Zamazenta, Urshifu-R, and Mega Lopunny that can break through Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Kartana also make good teammates, with Tapu Fini in return providing a soft check against foes such as Dragonite.

Specially Defensive.description: Specially defensive Solgaleo is one of the tier's premier special walls, is an amazing pivot, and is even a solid phazer. Knock Off hits Psychic- and Ghost-type Pokemon like Mewtwo, Deoxys, and Giratina, though Sunsteel Strike can be used instead as strong STAB move, to deal more damage to opposing Arceus and threaten Zacian. Knock Off's item-removing effect synergizes excellently with Roar's phazing, allowing Solgaleo to remove Heavy-Duty Boots and force foes to take repeated entry hazard damage. Roar also prevents sweepers like Zacian, Mewtwo, and Zamazenta-C from setting up on it. Tera Water removes Solgaleo's Fire and Ground weaknesses, allowing it to check Pokemon like Arceus-Fire, Trailblaze Ogerpon-H, and Great Tusk. Tera Dark, on the other hand, allows it to check Dark- and Ghost-types, like Spectrier, Giratina, and Chi-Yu. Teleport assists in getting powerful wallbreakers like Chi-Yu, Deoxys, and Kyurem-W onto the field safely. Solgaleo can have trouble with Pokemon like Chi-Yu, Kingambit, Palafin, and Landorus, so Pokemon like Kyurem-W, Great Tusk, Zamazenta-C, Palkia-O, and Arceus-Dark that can check these threats are excellent partners.

Trick Room Setter.description: Solgaleo is one of the tier's best Trick Room setters due to its amazing defenses, pivoting with Teleport that can let it bring in its teammates safely, and good typing. Knock Off can be used instead of Sunsteel Strike to hit Psychic- and Ghost-type Pokemon like Mewtwo and Deoxys; its item-removing effect also makes Solgaleo pair well with entry hazard setters like Great Tusk, as it can remove Heavy-Duty Boots to make hazards more potent. Tera Water removes Solgaleo's Fire and Ground weaknesses, which can let it check Pokemon like Arceus-Fire, Landorus, and Great Tusk. Solgaleo synergizes excellently with Pokemon like Magearna and Dialga, as they can help set up Trick Room for each other. Solgaleo also pairs well with Pokemon that can take advantage of Trick Room like Ursaluna, Kingambit, and Palkia, as it can pivot them in safely to help deal with threats like Chi-Yu, Spectrier, and Arceus-Fire. Solgaleo can often be threatened out by Pokemon like Kingambit, Chi-Yu, and Arceus-Fire, which makes partners like Zamazenta-C, Arceus-Dark, and Palkia appreciated. Solgaleo can also pair well with other slow pivots like Dialga and Galarian Slowking, as they can pivot each other in to help deal with Pokemon like Choice-locked Kyurem-W and Zamazenta-C.

Primordial Sea.description: Primordial Sea Solgaleo is most notable for its ability to wall Eternatus, and it also serves as a solid defensive answer to threats like Ultra Necrozma, Desolate Land Mega Blaziken, and non-Headlong Rush Kyurem-B. Psychic Noise deals respectable damage against Eternatus and prevents it, along with potential switch-ins like Arceus formes, from using Strength Sap. Flip Turn is boosted by Primordial Sea and can deal minor chip damage, while Teleport provides slow pivoting despite Solgaleo's high Speed. Gigaton Hammer pressures Fairy-types like Mega Audino and dissuades Blissey from attempting to block Strength Sap. Spikes can help reduce Solgaleo's passivity against many defensive Pokemon. An Impish nature guarantees Solgaleo isn't 2HKOed by Sheer Force Ultra Necrozma's Bolt Strike, while Jolly allows Solgaleo to outrun Mega Blaziken and Mega Gardevoir. Solgaleo is useful when paired with threats like Ultra Necrozma, which usually require specific allies to Imposter-proof. Defensively, Solgaleo struggles against threats like Moongeist Beam users, Ash-Greninja, and Mega Garchomp, making walls like RegenVest Primal Kyogre and Fur Coat Fairy-types good teammates. Solgaleo can be Imposter-proofed by numerous options, but RegenVest users in particular do not care about Psychic Noise and can maintain momentum.

Bulky Support.description:
Set Details

  • Lunala leverages its high bulk with Shadow Shield and wide movepool to support its team, mainly protecting it from spread attacks such as Astral Barrage and Glacial Lance with Wide Guard. Its high Special Attack and strong Ghost- and Fairy-type attacks allow it to weaken the opposing team over the course of a game, allowing its partners to clean up after it.
