This also guts any opportunities Cinderace would have against Primordial Sea users. Lastly, in combination with Taunt, Super Fang gives Cinderace a potent way to break down tougher walls; however, this pairing leaves Cinderace with fewer options against frailer teams that appreciate their Pokemon never being knocked out by Super Fang. There are also many ways around Super Fang, namely Regenerator and Ghost-type Pokemon.

Checks and Counters

Fire-immune Pokemon: Cinderace is unable to make much progress when facing common Fire-immune Pokemon like Well-Baked Body Gholdengo and Iron Treads as well as Primordial Sea Zapdos.

Primarina: Primarina is able to tank any attack Cinderace can throw at it while either healing with Regenerator or threatening Cinderace out with Primordial Sea.

Court Change.description:
Desolate Land allows Cinderace to offensively check Water-type attackers like Ogerpon-W and Primarina while also boosting the power of its Fire-type moves, namely Pyro Ball. Meanwhile, Magic Guard sacrifices some of Cinderace's firepower compared to Desolate Land but allows it to use Life Orb; avoid taking damage from entry hazards; and take advantage of the more reliable Flare Blitz, which can notably threaten Bulletproof Pokemon like Iron Treads and Gholdengo at the cost of dealing less damage than Pyro Ball to Fluffy users. U-turn allows for Cinderace to play a fast pivot role, being able to bait in and switch out on its checks like Pecharunt and Great Tusk, while Swords Dance provides it the ability to pressure its checks with serious damage or act as a late-game cleaner aided by its great Speed tier. Court Change lets Cinderace act as an extra form of entry hazard control for its team, allowing it to take advantage of hazard stacking or Sticky Web teams by flipping the hazards back to the other team. Will-O-Wisp grants it a way to cripple any non-Well-Baked Body Pokemon attempting to take it on. On the other hand, Taunt aids it in breaking down tough walls by preventing them from healing, with the exception of Regenerator Pokemon, and prevents Defog users from clearing any hazards switched onto their side with Court Change. High Jump Kick is another option that lets Cinderace threaten Well-Baked Body Pokemon like Cobalion and Iron Treads.

Cinderace pairs well with attackers such as Chien-Pao, Deoxys-S, and Roaring Moon, providing all of them easy entry points through its entry hazard control and pivoting while also weakening or beating their checks like Cobalion, Ting-Lu, and Levitate Gholdengo. With Court Change, Cinderace provides unique support to offensive teams, not only removing a major hindrance to offensive staples like Deoxys-S, Zamazenta, and all-out attacker Iron Moth with its ability to move Sticky Web off of its side, but also helping these Pokemon by inflicting Sticky Web onto the opposing team. Cinderace mostly struggles to deal with Fire-immune Pokemon like Well-Baked Body Landorus-T as well as Primordial Sea Zapdos and Primarina, so having teammates like Zapdos, Roaring Moon, and Hisuian Goodra will help it out immensely.

Offensive Utility.description: Cinderace acts as role compression on Fire teams, being able to apply offensive pressure on foes like Azumarill and non-Choice Scarf Hydreigon with its coverage, remove entry hazards with Court Change, and revenge kill faster threats such as Iron Boulder and Ceruledge with Sucker Punch. Pyro Ball and Gunk Shot can be used over Sucker Punch, with the former handling Bug- and Steel-types like Scizor and Corviknight and the latter taking on Fairy-types like Clefable and non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant. High Jump Kick allows Cinderace to deal with Normal-, Rock-, and Dark-types such as Blissey, Mega Tyranitar, and Ting-Lu. Iron Head is a niche option that allows Cinderace to lure in and remove Mega Diancie in the Fairy matchup. With U-turn, Cinderace can pivot out of unfavorable matchups such as Toxapex and Great Tusk and bring in a teammate that can deal with them. Heatran and Iron Moth are such teammates, with the former handling Toxapex by trapping it with Magma Storm and removing it with Earth Power and the latter taking Great Tusk out with Energy Ball. When it forgoes Sucker Punch, Cinderace appreciates Choice Scarf Blacephalon taking on Ghost-types such as Gholdengo and Ceruledge, which can switch into High Jump Kick, and in return, Cinderace takes on Dark-types for Blacephalon. Torkoal sets up sun to boost Pyro Ball when it's being run and places Stealth Rock to further aid Cinderace. Notably, sun-boosted Pyro Ball 2HKOes Mega Sableye. When Cinderace runs Sucker Punch, its ability to revenge kill faster and weakened threats like Iron Boulder enables setup sweepers such as Mega Charizard X, Volcarona, Z-Celebrate Victini, and Ceruledge to start their own sweep, and the latter two specifically appreciate Court Change support so they can find an opportunity to switch in.

Swords Dance.description: Boasting an exceptional Speed tier, a diverse array of coverage options, and its unique ability, Cinderace is an exemplary wallbreaker that greatly threatens Water, Ground, and Flying teams, outpacing foes such as Ogerpon-W, Iron Treads, and Iron Valiant. At +2, Pyro Ball OHKOes walls like Empoleon, Hisuian Goodra, and Clodsire after Stealth Rock damage. Breakneck Blitz allows Cinderace to catch walls such as Toxapex, Mandibuzz, and mixed Hippowdon off guard and instantly remove them. Gunk Shot targets Fairy-types like Tapu Fini, Iron Valiant, and Azumarill, while Sucker Punch may be used to prevent revenge killing attempts from Iron Boulder, Latias, and Barraskewda, OHKOing them at +2. Alternatively, High Jump Kick removes Ting-Lu at +2 after Stealth Rock Damage, Mega Tyranitar, and Heatran. Torkoal offers Stealth Rock to wear down switch-ins like Rotom-W and Porygon2, sets up Drought to boost Pyro Ball's power output, and removes entry hazards via Rapid Spin to allow Cinderace to pivot freely. Victini and Mega Charizard X appreciate Cinderace luring in and eliminating the previously mentioned Sucker Punch targets while heavily weakening shared checks like Slowbro, Toxapex, and Great Tusk. Volcarona appreciates Cinderace's ability to remove special walls like Clodsire, Blissey, and Galarian Slowking. In return, Volcarona threatens walls such as Gastrodon, Ting-Lu, and Slowbro. Heatran provides Stealth Rock support and uses its stallbreaking ability to remove Toxapex, preserving Cinderace's Normalium Z to use in a pinch. Like Volcarona, Blacephalon appreciates Cinderace weakening special walls to let it clean up late-game; it can also break problematic foes like Slowbro and Skeledirge. Iron Moth scares away Ground-types such as Great Tusk, Gastrodon, and Swampert via Energy Ball and threatens Tapu Fini for Cinderace if it doesn't run Gunk Shot. Volcanion is a great switch-in against Water-types like Barraskewda, Basculegion-F, and Ogerpon-W and appreciates Cinderace's ability to remove Ground-types such as Landorus, Garchomp, and Clodsire. Mega Charizard Y and Scovillain help break down physically defensive Pokemon and remove the aforementioned Ground- and Water-type walls via Grass-type coverage, with the former also providing Drought. In exchange, Cinderace threatens Clodsire, Hisuian Goodra, and many of the aforementioned special walls so Mega Charizard Y can freely throw out attacks incautiously, while Scovillain can clean up late-game using Chlorophyll under sun.

Choice Scarf.description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

nu.overview: Inteleon's Speed tier and sky-high Special Attack make it a formidable threat in NU. Not only is it blazing fast, but with Choice Specs, it's also quite powerful and can 2HKO many common special walls like Scrafty, Copperajah, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro on the switch with Hydro Pump. Even when facing Water-immune Pokemon like Toxicroak and Vaporeon, Inteleon still has a way to flip the matchup in its favor in its U-turn, which lets it bring in teammates like Scyther, Flygon, and Toxicroak to take advantage of these checks. On the other hand, Inteleon does face a bit of competition from Basculegion-M and Paldean Tauros-W, as the former can switch up its moves because it largely uses Mystic Water, the latter has Intimidate, and both have access to priority and easily fit coverage for Toxicroak; however, it isn't hindered by contact punishment such as Bellibolt's Static and Galarian Slowbro's Rocky Helmet. It also has to deal with not being able to use its strongest move when up against teams with Water-immune Pokemon, which greatly halts Inteleon's progress-making, as it's almost always forced to use U-turn against them if it doesn't want to give up momentum.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Inteleon can also run a Scope Lens + Sniper set that is similar to its Choice Specs moveset except with Hydro Pump being traded out for Snipe Shot. When landing a critical hit, Inteleon can dent many Pokemon, but its unreliability makes it weaker overall. Choice Scarf Inteleon reaches a blisteringly fast Speed tier and, with its high Special Attack and U-turn, easily revenge kills many setup sweepers and can create momentum. A moveset of Hydro Pump or Scald / Ice Beam / U-turn / Taunt can be run alongside Heavy-Duty Boots to bother passive Pokemon that would easily take advantage of Inteleon otherwise like Wo-Chien, Vaporeon, and Bronzong. Inteleon can drop U-turn in favor of running a second STAB move, like Surf or Snipe Shot, alongside Hydro Pump, letting it choose the right move depending on its situation; however, losing momentum versus Water-immune and -resistant Pokemon can be annoying at times. Tera Dark can be used to boost Dark Pulse, letting Inteleon have a chance against checks like Vaporeon, especially after they've been chipped.

Checks and Counters

Water-immune Pokemon: Both Vaporeon and Toxicroak blank Inteleon's STAB attack, and the former can take the rest of Inteleon's attacks decently well, though the latter drops to Ice Beam. However, with access to U-turn and strong coverage moves, Inteleon can find ways around these matchups.

Water- and Dragon-types: Basculegion-M can switch into Inteleon's Hydro Pump and Ice Beam and proceed to use it for momentum, but it doesn't enjoy switching in on a Dark Pulse. Similarly, Goodra can take Inteleon's Hydro Pump decently but dislikes having to take an Ice Beam.

Grass-types: Brambleghast and Decidueye can take Inteleon's Hydro Pump and proceed to KO it with their Grass-type STAB moves, but they can't do this repeatedly. Similarly, bulkier Grass-types like Brute Bonnet and Whimsicott can switch into Hydro Pump and threaten with Seed Bomb or Giga Drain, respectively; however, their lack of recovery leads them to being overwhelmed. On top of this, all of these Grass-types must fear Ice Beam.

Revenge Killers: Due to Inteleon's frailty, faster Pokemon like Kilowattrel and Choice Scarf users like Flamigo and Munkidori easily threaten Inteleon with a KO and can use it for momentum, but they fail to switch in reliably with their lack of bulk.

Choice Specs.description:
Set Details

Hydro Pump is the preferred STAB option due to its power, but it can be unreliable at times. Alternatively, Surf can be run for accuracy in exchange for power. Ice Beam complements Inteleon's Water-type STAB move really well by hitting Grass- and Dragon-types like Decidueye, Wo-Chien, and Goodra super effectively. Dark Pulse provides Inteleon with a coverage move so that it isn't completely useless against Water-types like Vaporeon and Basculegion-M. U-turn allows Inteleon to pivot on even Water-immune Pokemon like Gastrodon and Vaporeon. Instead of Ice Beam or Dark Pulse, Inteleon could opt for Air Slash to better target Toxicroak and Paldean Tauros-W, but its lower Base Power means that it's worse at breaking through other Water-immune and -resistant Pokemon. Tera Water boosts Inteleon's STAB move to insane levels, but Tera Ghost allows Inteleon to avoid priority like Ambipom's Fake Out and resist Flygon's First Impression while blanking high-Base Power attacks like Cinccino's Tail Slap and Infernape's Close Combat.

Inteleon forces in bulky Water-immune and -resistant Pokemon like Vaporeon, Wo-Chien, and Goodra, and it can capitalize on this with U-turn, letting it bring in a threat that takes advantage of them like Toxicroak, Incineroar, or Flygon. Toxicroak is an especially noteworthy partner, as it walls the most common Inteleon switch-in in Vaporeon and can use it as either setup fodder or a chance to throw out high-Base Power attacks. In return, Inteleon handles Fire- and Ground-types for the former two and can easily overwhelm physical walls Flygon brings in. Inteleon is quite powerful, but to achieve any of its 2HKOs, especially those against Water-type checks like Vaporeon and Tera Water Galarian Slowbro, it requires entry hazards to chip away at its foes; Copperajah, Bronzong, Gligar, and Klefki all synergize well to fill this role. Even without entry hazards, however, most special walls that do not resist Inteleon's STAB attacks like Bronzong, Copperajah, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro have a hard time switching in, as Bronzong is 2HKOed right away, and Copperajah and Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro are 2HKOed after minimal chip damage. Special attacking partners like Munkidori, Life Orb Flygon, and Nasty Plot Toxicroak make for good teammates, as they greatly appreciate Inteleon's ability to overwhelm their checks. Inteleon is threatened by Grass- and Electric-types like Brambleghast, Decidueye, and Kilowattrel, so Grass-types and Flying-resistant Pokemon like Wo-Chien, Wind Rider Brambleghast, and Rhyperior make for strong switch-ins to these threats. With Inteleon's frailty, it prefers to have slow pivots like Whimsicott, Bellibolt, and Incineroar, as they can draw out Fire- and Ground-types for Inteleon to threaten.

Primordial Sea.description: Inteleon is a decent cleaner and wallbreaker thanks to its high Special Attack and Speed, threatening many offensive Pokemon like Great Tusk, Scream Tail, and Gholdengo. U-turn lets it pivot out of unfavorable matchups like RegenVest Manaphy and Primarina and forms a VoltTurn core with other pivots like Roaring Moon and Meowscarada. Mud Shot threatens Fire-types like Iron Moth and Cinderace that could otherwise utilize Desolate Land to comfortably switch into a Weather Ball and OHKOes Heatran. Ice Beam snipes Dragon-types like Roaring Moon and Latios. Physical teammates like Zamazenta and Roaring Moon appreciate Inteleon's ability to threaten their switch-ins like Pecharunt and Great Tusk, respectively, letting them rip massive holes in the opponent's team once these foes are removed; in return, they can threaten walls like Empoleon and Manaphy, which Inteleon struggles against. Entry hazard support from the likes of Scream Tail and Ting-Lu helps Inteleon against special walls like Empoleon and RegenVest users like Manaphy and Primarina, which it otherwise struggles to break through. Inteleon is also vulnerable to being worn down by hazards, so teammates that can remove them like Corviknight and Great Tusk are good partners. Furthermore, Inteleon's frailty leaves it severely threatened by faster revenge killers like Chien-Pao and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, making teammates that can deal with them like the aforementioned Corviknight and Great Tusk greatly appreciated.

Defensive.description:
Corviknight is a valuable defensive pivot for many teams thanks to its great defensive typing letting it be immune to Spikes and natural bulk that lets it check Pokemon like Tapu Lele, Landorus-T, Kingambit, and Kartana. Brave Bird threatens the Grass- and Fighting-types Corviknight often checks, like Great Tusk, Ogerpon-W, and Urshifu-R. Iron Defense allows Corviknight to better take hits from powerful physical attackers that boost their offensive stats like Zamazenta and Dragonite. Corviknight uses U-turn to keep up momentum. Corviknight can use Body Press to threaten damage on the Steel-types it checks like Melmetal, Kingambit, and Iron Treads, as well as other Pokemon like Kyurem, using its high Defense stat, which can be boosted by Iron Defense. Corviknight could run Defog, allowing it to somewhat reliably remove entry hazards for its teammates, but it can be very easily blocked from doing this by Gholdengo. Corviknight always uses Roost, which lets it better check foes such as Tapu Lele over the course of a game. The first EV spread is designed to allow Corviknight to take two Close Combats from Mega Lopunny after Stealth Rock, while the other EV spread allows it to better check special attackers like Tapu Lele and Kyurem. Pressure allows stall teams to PP stall Pokemon like Kyurem, Zamazenta, and Landorus-T.

Corviknight is most common on balance, stall, and many offense teams. Balance and stall teams allow defensive Pokemon to cover Corviknight's bad matchups and vice versa. On offense teams, Corviknight can take attacks well and then pivot in a teammate with U-turn, allowing the team to keep momentum. Corviknight struggles with Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona, which Water-types like Toxapex and Assault Vest Alomomola check. In return, Corviknight can check the Ground- and Grass-types that Toxapex and Alomomola struggle with. Corviknight also struggles with powerful Electric-types like Tapu Koko and Raging Bolt. This makes Ground-types that can take their attacks, like Ting-Lu and Gliscor, valuable partners. In return, Corviknight can take the Grass- and Ice-type attacks, like from Kartana and Kyurem, the aforementioned Pokemon dislike. Corviknight also resists Fairy- and Psychic-type attacks, like from Tapu Lele and some Mega Diancie and Iron Valiant sets, causing Fighting- and Dragon-types like Zamazenta, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Latios to greatly appreciate Corviknight on their team. Special walls, such as Blissey and Ting-Lu, greatly value Corviknight on slower-paced teams, as it can take physical hits well, while Blissey and Ting-Lu can take on the special attackers like Mega Charizard Y and Gholdengo. Corviknight functions well on stall due to its aforementioned good defensive profile and how it works well with previously mentioned stall staples like Blissey and Gliscor. It can help PP stall using Pressure, and its excellent defensive typing lets it stay in on many sweepers. In addition, Corviknight can use Iron Defense to threaten sweepers attempting to break a stall teamwhile threatening said sweepers back with Body Press. Corviknight also is greatly appreciated as a Defogger for these defensive teams, which is easier on stall teams because Corviknight has more chances to use Defog and because it has teammates like Clodsire and specially defensive Gliscor that can deal with Gholdengo.

Maranga Berry.description:
• Iron Defense lets Corviknight boost its Defense against physical attackers like non-Thunder Punch Meowscarada, non-Trick Choice Scarf Metagross, and Haxorus to then outheal them with Roost.
  • Taunt lets Corviknight beat setup Pokemon like Iron Crown, Calm Mind Primarina, and Registeel.
  • Running Agility on Corviknight over Body Press can allow it beat Curse Pecharunt, Encore + Disable Alolan Ninetales, and some Icy Wind variants of Primarina.
  • Compared to Agility, Body Press has much less chances of getting hit by a critical hit, allows Corviknight to beat Chien-Pao while reducing the chances of getting flinched, and is less forced to use Roost more than it has to against Ursaluna and Ursaluna-B thanks to not worrying about Roost letting it get hit by a Ground-type move or critical hit.
  • Maranga Berry allows Corviknight to beat special attackers such as Kyurem, Primarina, and Espathra.
  • Corviknight can reduce its chances of receiving a critical hit with Pressure, which is valuable on a stall Pokemon because its effect gives foes half as many chances to land a critical hit.
  • The 200 speed EVs allow Corviknight to outspeed neutral-natured base 60 Speed Pokemon such as Choice Specs Primarina and Sylveon and prevent them from setting up with Taunt, and the rest of the EVs are put into its defenses.
  • Good partners to Corviknight are Ground- and Dragon-types like Ursaluna and Roaring Moon that can beat the Fire- and Electric-types that threaten Corviknight super effectively.

Pressure Stall.description:
• Corviknight aims to use Pressure to deplete the PP of slower Pokemon without Speed-boosting moves, forcing them to damage themselves with Struggle.
  • The combination of Protect and Substitute allows Corviknight to stall most moves powerful enough to OHKO or 2HKO it, such as those used by Iron Hands and Donphan.
  • Taunt will prevent Pokemon such as non-Life Orb Primarina, Pecharunt, and Cresselia from using setup or status moves to overpower Corviknight.
  • The HP EVs allow for the maximum number of Substitutes, factoring in Leftovers and Protect, while maximum Speed EVs allow Corviknight to outrun Primarina as well as non-Timid Raging Bolt and Volcanion.
  • In order to mitigate Corviknight's weakness to Fire- and Electric-type moves from foes such as Volcanion, Raging Bolt, and Volcarona, it can be advantageous to pair it with Pokemon such as Hisuian Goodra, Haxorus, and Dragapult.

Physically Defensive (Flying).description:
Corviknight is a great physical wall for Flying teams, capable of handling the likes of Meowscarada and Iron Boulder while providing Defog support. Body Press makes use of Corviknight's respectable Defense to remove Steel- and Ice-types like Iron Treads, Bisharp, and Mamoswine. Iron Head handles foes not particularly bothered by Body Press such as Kleavor, Iron Boulder, and Enamorus. Alternatively, Brave Bird can OHKO threats like Lokix and Sneasler, OHKO Ogerpon-W after minor chip damage, and put immense pressure on Urshifu-R. 12 Attack EVs are used with Iron Head to allow Corviknight to OHKO Flutter Mane; otherwise, going for maximum Defense investment.

Gliscor and the Landorus formes' Electric immunity enables them to handle the likes of Raging Bolt and Iron Hands; they can also check Fire-types such as Iron Moth and Cinderace for Corviknight, along with setting Stealth Rock. Gliscor can further assist Corviknight by using Toxic to wear down opposing physical walls like Great Tusk and Sinistcha. Meanwhile, the Landorus formes equipped with a Choice Scarf can deal with Volcarona, Ogerpon-H, Gholdengo, and the aforementioned Iron Moth for Corviknight. Specially defensive Articuno can help tank Ice Beams from threats like Kyurem and Greninja and, thanks to Freeze-Dry and Haze, apply pressure to opposing Flying teams along with Water-types such as Pelipper and Primarina. Assault Vest Tornadus-T can assist against powerful special attackers like Iron Valiant and Hisuian Zoroark and provide Knock Off support to remove Rocky Helmet from foes like Ting-Lu and Skarmory. Choice Band Dragonite helps to handle Fire-types like Ceruledge and uses Extreme Speed to pick off fast foes like Meowscarada and Urshifu-R while appreciating Corviknight handling Ice- and Rock-types. Choice Scarf Enamorus can break through Dragon- and Dark-type threats like Choice Specs Dragapult, Kyurem, and Darkrai. Lastly, Nasty Plot Galarian Moltres can check the likes of Gholdengo and Pecharunt that Corviknight struggles to touch while enjoying Corviknight using Iron Head to remove Fairy-types like Enamorus. Gyarados can help to handle physical attackers like Mamoswine and Ceruledge thanks to Intimidate along with threats like Volcarona.

Specially Defensive (Flying).description:
Specially defensive Corviknight serves an important role on Flying by being able to sponge special attacks from the likes of Frosmoth, Greninja, and Flutter Mane. Iron Head threatens the Fairy- and Ice-types that can scare Flying, like Hatterene, Iron Valiant, and Kyurem. U-turn allows for Corviknight to safely pivot in teammates. Defog eases entry for teammates like Choice Band Dragonite. The given EV spread maximizes Corviknight's special bulk while allowing it to OHKO Flutter Mane with Iron Head.

The Landorus formes can check problematic Electric-, Fire-, and Steel-types like Raging Bolt, Hisuian Arcanine, and Gholdengo for Corviknight while appreciating it being able to take on special Ice-type attacks from the likes of Articuno and Darkrai. Choice Scarf variants of the Landorus formes can also outspeed and remove Flutter Mane and Hoopa-U. Gliscor threatens Electric- and Steel-types like Sandy Shocks and Heatran while also providing Toxic support to wear down bulky targets like Swampert and Pelipper. Skarmory serves as a solid defensive partner for Corviknight, being able to comfortably take on physical Rock- and Ice-types like Kleavor and Cetitan, as well as other physical threats like Meowscarada, along with providing entry hazard support. Dragonite greatly appreciates Corviknight handling Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Hatterene. In return, Dragonite can easily remove Fire-types such as Iron Moth and Ninetales and pick off threats like Meowscarada with Extreme Speed. Assault Vest Tornadus-T assists Corviknight by using Knock Off to remove Choice Specs from the likes of Flutter Mane, giving Corviknight an easier time handling them. Additionally, Tornadus-T can use its Flying-type attack to remove Iron Valiant and Ogerpon-W. Zapdos can handle Water-types that resist Corviknight's Iron Head like Toxapex, Empoleon, and Swords Dance Urshifu-R along with checking opposing Corviknight. Choice Scarf Enamorus deals with Dragon- and Dark-types like Choice Specs Dragapult, Choice Specs Greninja, and Hisuian Samurott along with providing Healing Wish for Corviknight if necessary. Gyarados can help to stave off physical threats like Cinderace, Barraskewda, and Gallade along with spreading paralysis, enabling Corviknight to outspeed Glimmora, which makes it easier to check.

Bulk Up (Steel).description:
Bulk Up Corviknight serves as a solid wincon for Steel teams thanks to its solid natural bulk and Flying typing, granting it a key immunity and neutrality to Ground and Fighting, respectively. Brave Bird is Corviknight's main offensive tool, easily removing Fighting-types like Gallade, Sneasler, and Scrafty along with dealing with other problematic foes like Dragapult and Ogerpon-W. Body Press provides a solid complement to Brave Bird, helping to deal with the Steel- and Rock-types that resist Brave Bird such as Bisharp, Empoleon, and Ogerpon-C. Alternatively, Taunt can be used to stop attempts to handle Corviknight with opposing threats such as Whirlwind Hippowdon and Haze Toxapex; otherwise, Substitute enables Corviknight to easily set up in front of the likes of Dragon Tail Garchomp, punishes defensive pivots such as Mandibuzz and opposing Corviknight, and grants it a safety net against wallbreakers that would otherwise threaten it out. The main EV spread maximizes Corviknight's special bulk, while the alternative EV spread can be used to let Corviknight outspeed Skarmory and use Taunt against it before it can set up Iron Defense or Roost, enabling Corviknight to eventually win.

Heatran serves as an excellent teammate, easily taking on the Fire-types that would handle Corviknight such as Iron Moth, Skeledirge, and opposing Heatran along with absorbing Will-O-Wisp from the likes of Dragapult and Moltres. Iron Treads's Ground typing allows it to easily handle the Electric-types that threaten Corviknight like Raging Bolt and Sandy Shocks; it also removes Landorus with Ice Spinner, preventing it from grounding Corviknight with Gravity. Gholdengo can help Corviknight by using Thunder Wave to slow down threats like Ogerpon-W as well as handling foes such as Iron Valiant and Pecharunt. Archaludon can handle physical attackers that threaten to break Corviknight like Ogerpon-H and Urshifu-R thanks to Stamina. Alternatively, Choice Scarf Archaludon can outspeed and remove threats such as Keldeo with Thunderbolt. Hisuian Goodra is a nice special wall capable of taking on threats like Flutter Mane, Latios, and Dragapult along with being able to use Knock Off to remove Rocky Helmet from the likes of Toxapex and Skarmory. Bisharp can remove problematic Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Sableye as well as use Sucker Punch to check fast threats like Hoopa-U.

Defog (Steel).description: This is a sample set as we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Defog (Flying).description:
Corviknight is an invaluable part of Flying teams by virtue of its incredible defensive typing and access to utility options that many of its teammates appreciate. Defog removes Stealth Rock so that its teammates that don't run Heavy-Duty Boots or had theirs removed have an easier time switching in. Defog also removes dual screens set by foes, allowing its wallbreaking teammates to remove various threats. Iron Head threatens Rock- and Ice-types that can threaten its teammates such as Iron Boulder, Ogerpon-C, and Alolan Ninetales. Body Press handles Rock- and Ice-types as well, and in addition, it handles Steel- and Dark-types such as Excadrill, Bisharp, and Greninja. Alternatively, U-turn allows Corviknight to pivot out of bad matchups such as Fire- and Electric-types. Pressure allows it to punish Sableye using Encore. On the other hand, Mirror Armor can be used to punish attacks such as Bleakwind Storm from Tornadus-T and Moonblast from the likes of Iron Valiant and Enamorus. A Careful nature along with 252 HP EVs and 144 Special Defense EVs allow Corviknight to survive two Shadow Balls from Choice Specs Flutter Mane, and 12 Attack EVs let it OHKO back with Iron Head.

Landorus appreciates Corviknight removing Stealth Rock, which would otherwise wear it down over time due to its lack of recovery. In return, Landorus takes out Fire-types such as Heatran, Ceruledge, and Hisuian Arcanine, and its Electric immunity eases that matchup, handling the likes of Raging Bolt and Magnezone. Skarmory is another beneficiary of Corviknight's removal of entry hazards, as it preserves Sturdy so it is able to set its own entry hazards. Articuno, with its great special bulk, takes on Water-types such as Choice Specs Greninja and Primarina and threatens them back with Freeze-Dry. In return, it appreciates Corviknight handling Rock-types. Choice Specs Zapdos and Choice Band Dragonite are two more offensive teammates that appreciate the removal of entry hazards, which would otherwise weaken them. Zapdos also appreciates Corviknight taking out Rock-types such as Ogerpon-C and Kleavor, while Dragonite appreciates the removal of Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Hatterene. In return, Zapdos handles Primarina, while Dragonite takes on Fire-types such as Ogerpon-H and Heatran. Choice Scarf Enamorus provides great speed control for Flying teams, outspeeding and threatening the likes of Dragapult and Choice Specs Iron Valiant. In return, Enamorus appreciates Corviknight taking on Steel- and Ice-types such as Excadrill, Empoleon, and Weavile. Setup sweepers such as Double Dance Galarian Moltres and Dragon Dance Dragonite appreciate Corviknight walling and removing their threats so they can find opportunities to set up and sweep late-game.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Pivot Knight.description:
• Corviknight's fantastic typing makes it a great physically defensive pivot, easily getting dangerous teammates in such as Chien-Pao, Flutter Mane, and Ogerpon-H in.

  • Body Press versus Iron Head: Body Press has decent damage output and helps massively against common Dark-types like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S. Meanwhile, Iron Head ensures that Corviknight will not be walled by Flutter Mane.

  • Taunt: Corviknight might not be fast, but it's fast enough to shut down most other defensive Pokemon with Taunt, such as Ting-Lu and Toxapex.

  • Brave Bird: Brave Bird's recoil is unwelcome, but it's a fantastic response against Ogerpon-H, who otherwise will scare Corviknight off.

  • Neutral Speed Natures versus Negative Speed Natures with a Speed IV of 4 or 5: Negative Speed natures are handy for giving very slow U-turns when used in conjunction with lower Speed IVs, as well as not risking getting hit by Ursaluna-B's Earth Power while using Roost. Just note that going any lower than 4 Speed IVs will underspeed Ting-Lu before it can be shut down by Taunt, and powerful Special attackers like Primarina outspeeding Corviknight can be a problem for some teams.

Other Options
  • Tailwind: Tailwind is an incredible support move for making powerful sweepers like Urshifu-R even more difficult to revenge kill, though its short time span can make it tricky to fully take advantage of.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Corviknight's defensive typing is fantastic, so don't Terastallize too hastily, or else it'll lose to threats it normally checks.

  • Dragon: Dragon and Fairy weaknesses are devastating, but in the late-game, resisting Electric and Fire can give Corviknight new win conditions against foes such as Ogerpon-H that lack Play Rough and Tera Water Urshifu-R. Just note that Modest Tera Fire Choice Specs Chi-Yu can still OHKO with Overheat.

  • Fire: Tera Fire may not seem like a good fit for a pivot due to the Stealth Rock weakness, but it vastly improves Corviknight's chances of defeating Ogerpon-H and Tera Electric Chien-Pao, making it a worthy defensive choice. Do note that this won't help much against Choice Specs Chi-Yu.

  • Flying: While this set doesn't always use Brave Bird, Tera Flying lets Corviknight keep its typing while using Roost, meaning Earthquake and Fissure can no longer hit Corviknight while its restoring health. It also improves Corviknight's chances against Ogerpon-H.

  • Water: With Tera Water, Corviknight consistently survives all but Modest Tera Fire Choice Specs Chi-Yu's Overheat, letting it deal serious damage with Body Press. It also gains a key resistance to Ice for Chien-Pao and Water for Tera Water Urshifu-R.

  • Fighting: Getting STAB on Body Press can give Corviknight a surprisingly decent chance at cleaning weakened teams, though this makes it especially vulnerable to Flutter Mane.

  • Electric: While turning Corviknight's incredible Ground-type immunity into a weakness is unfortunate, Tera Electric otherwise improves a wide variety of match-ups, with Tera Electric Chien-Pao and Raging Bolt being particularly major ones.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: This lets Corviknight wear down physical threats more quickly while pivoting.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers's consistent recovery can be quite helpful for taking repeated hits from Ruination when attempting to stall it out with Pressure.

Abilities

  • Mirror Armor: Mirror Armor's ability to punish Flutter Mane for using Mystical Fire makes it a great ability choice on Corviknight.

  • Pressure: Corviknight's excellent bulk and Taunt makes Pressure a good alternative for stalling out foes such as Gliscor and Ting-Lu.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 76 Def / 180 SpD with Impish or Relaxed This spread has enough bulk to avoid a 2HKO from Timid Iron Bundle's Hydro Pump as long as they lack an offensive item, which can be especially useful if using Pressure. Just beware of Iron Bundle's Encore.

  • 252 HP / 20 Def / 236 SpD with Careful or Sassy: This specially defensive spread won't check major physical threats like Dragonite nearly as well, but it does avoid a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

IronPress.description:
• Corviknight stands out as one of the best choices around for sweeping with Iron Defense and Body Press, thanks to its excellent typing and Roost.

  • Iron Head versus Brave Bird: Iron Head ensures Flutter Mane isn't a reliable check to Corviknight, in addition to making it an even better Swords Dance Mimikyu check. Brave Bird is less reliable at beating Flutter Mane, but severely punishes Ogerpon-H switch-ins.

  • U-turn versus Taunt: While U-turn with this set may seem strange, Corviknight is still a decent pivot even if it must give up Taunt. Just note that this keaves Corviknight completely walled by Ghost-types like Flutter Mane. Taunt on the other hand, lets Corviknight effectively shut down slower defensive Pokemon, such as Ting-Lu and Dondozo. Note that both options leave Corviknight hopelessly walled by Flutter Mane.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Corviknight has a fantastic defensive typing, so only Terastallize if you need to win certain matchups, especially since it becomes vulnerable to Toxic.

  • Fighting: With a Fighting Tera type, Body Press is easier to sweep with, with many Ting-Lu variants now being 2HKOed by boosted Body Press. It also gets rid of enough of Corviknight's common weaknesses that foes like Ogerpon-H and Raging Bolt will check Corviknight far less reliably.

  • Water: Tera Water gives Corviknight a way to resist both Chien-Pao's and Chi-Yu's most powerful STAB attacks, though Modest Tera Fire Choice Specs Chi-Yu can still OHKO with Overheat. It also stops Tera Water Urshifu-R from cleaving through Corviknight's Iron Defense with Surging Strikes.

  • Dragon: A Dragon Tera type lets Corviknight resist common attacks aimed at it, such as Electric- and Fire-type attacks from foes like Raging Bolt and Ogerpon-H respectively. However, the new weaknesses to Fairy and Dragon make this an especially reactive Terastallization.

  • Fire: While Tera Fire leaves Corviknight extremely vulnerable to Urshifu-R, in exchange it retains the important Fairy-type resistance and does well against Ogerpon-H.

  • Flying: A Flying Tera type lets Corviknight retain its Flying typing even when using Roost, making it a more reliable check to Fissure users such as Dondozo and Garganacl.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: The passive damage from Rocky Helmet against foes like Dragonite give Corviknight a much easier time using U-turn over Iron Head.

  • Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers: Since this Corviknight attempts to sweep, Sitrus Berry's burst of quick recovery can make it less pressured to spend a turn using Roost. Leftovers on the other hand, will still keep healing Corviknight even after being hit by Ruination, so it can make sense with Pressure.

  • Maranga Berry: A Special Defense boost granted from Maranga Berry makes it far more difficult for foes like Flutter Mane to revenge kill Corviknight, and it can even be paired with Terastallization to defeat Raging Bolt!

  • Covert Cloak: When paired with Taunt, Covert Cloak makes Corviknight an effective Garganacl check provided that it isn't Tera Ghost, though note Corviknight will no longer drop Flutter Mane's Special Attack with Mirror Armor.

Abilities

  • Mirror Armor: Mirror Armor means Flutter Mane can't use Mystical Fire without getting its Special Attack dropped, unless Corviknight is holding Covert Cloak.

  • Pressure: Corviknight's ability to take powerful, low PP moves such as Close Combat after Iron Defense makes Pressure a viable alternative, in addition to giving Corviknight a better chance of dealing with Ruination from Ting-Lu effectively.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 76 Def / 180 SpD with Impish The Special Defense investment stops Iron Bundle from 2HKOing Corviknight with Hydro Pump, especially useful if revenge killing one with Body Press. Just remember that Encore means Corviknight is still vulnerable to Iron Bundle ruining set up attempts.

  • 252 HP / 20 Def / 236 SpD with Careful: While Body Press will be significantly weaker on this specially defensive spread, it does avoid a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball, making this spread especially effective with Iron Head and Mirror Armor.

Bulk Up.description:
• With Bulk Up giving an Attack boost, Corviknight is free from having to use Body Press for good damage output, making it easier to run Taunt against defensive foes without fear of being walled by Ghost-types like Flutter Mane.

  • Iron Head versus Brave Bird: Iron Head reliably 2HKOs Chien-Pao without a boost and is a fantastic tool against Flutter Mane, while Brave Bird is a great response against Ogerpon-H and the only hope of 2HKOing Chi-Yu.

  • Physically Defensive versus Specially Defensive: Physically Defensive Corviknight takes on common Pokemon like Dragon Dance Dragonite and Urshifu-R more comfortably, while focusing on Special Defense stops Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane from 2HKOing Corviknight with Shadow Ball.

Other Options
  • Power Trip: Power Trip takes several boosts to get powerful, but it's Corviknight's best shot at dealing decent damage to Gholdengo. It also makes Corviknight a viable option on Baton Pass Blaziken teams, especially since it relies less on Terastallization to defeat Dark-types than Latias.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Remember that most of Corviknight's good Tera types leave it vulnerable to Toxic, so Terastallize carefully and only win a win condition is clear.

  • Water: Tera Water is an effective tool against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, though note that Choice Specs Chi-Yu can OHKO with Tera Fire boosted Overheat. It also prevents Urshifu-R from revenge killing Corviknight with Tera-boosted Surging Strikes.

  • Flying: This Tera type lets Corviknight retain its Flying typing while using Roost, meaning Fissure users such as Dondozo are much easier to handle, and giving Brave Bird a healthy boost in power.

  • Dragon: Once Fairy-, Ice-, and Dragon-types are out of the way, the Dragon Tera type allows Corviknight to turn the tables on most Ogerpon-H.

  • Fire: There are few better Tera-types to use against Ogerpon-H than Tera Fire, which unlike Tera Dragon, will retain an important Fairy resistance. It does make Urshifu-R a huge problem as a drawback.

  • Dark: If using Power Trip, Tera Dark is highly recommended to boost its damage output.

Abilities

  • Mirror Armor: In addition to punishing Flutter Mane for using Mystical Fire when not using Covert Cloak, Mirror Armor stops pivoting Intimidate foes like Landorus-T and Incineroar from softening Corviknight's damage output.

  • Pressure: Pressure is a reasonable alternative for whittling down PP, which can be especially helpful against Ting-Lu's troublesome Ruination.

Items

  • Covert Cloak: When paired with Taunt, Corviknight can effectively take down Garganacl.

  • Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers: Sitrus Berry is preferred due to the quicker burst of recovery better fitting a sweeper, but Leftovers can work very well with Pressure in an attempt to out-stall Ruination.

  • Maranga Berry: Maranga Berry's Special Defense boost can stop Special Attacking foes like Flutter Mane from 2HKOing physically defensive Corviknight.

Bulky Setup.description: Corviknight is a potent setup user thanks to its fantastic bulk, useful defensive utility and typing, and ability to punish opposing physical setup from the likes of Dragonite and Great Tusk. IronPress allows for more instant anti-setup pressure, notably switching into and beating Fire Punch Dragonite without issue, while physically defensive Bulk Up + Brave Bird is better at dealing more instantaneous damage, especially Flying-weak or Fighting-resistant Pokemon like Urshifu-RS and Spectrier. U-turn in combination with Sablenite allows Corviknight to keep its ability to bounce entry hazards without hassle while bringing in frailer teammates like Urshifu-RS and Dragapult, while Defog is a better option on fatter teams where momentum isn't as necessary. Specially defensive variants can use both a Relaxed and Sassy nature depending on the team's needs, while physically defensive variants should always use a Relaxed nature. Venusaurite is useful on physically defensive Bulk Up + Brave Bird variants to answer the likes of Hisuian Arcanine and Iron Moth in a pinch while denying Stealth Rock from the former in conjunction with Defog. Corviknight fits best on balance and stall teams, with some viability on bulky offense teams thanks to its defensive prowess. Teammates like Urshifu-R and Raging Bolt adore Corviknight's ability to slow pivot them onto the field while blocking most entry hazard-setting attempts from the likes of Magearna, faster Garganacl variants, and the Arceus formes. Corviknight fears Garganacl's Salt Cure, notably chunking it every turn for 1/4 of its health, so answers like Lopunnite Iron Boulder, Great Tusk, and Urshifu-RS are greatly appreciated; Substitute Arceus-Ghost can also use non-Pinsirite Garganacl as setup fodder. Stronger Fire-types like Heatran, along with Iron Moth and Hisuian Arcanine when excluding Venusaurite, greatly pressure Corviknight, so answers like Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, Arceus-Water, and Ho-Oh are necessary. Electric-types like Regieleki and Raging Bolt are also extremely problematic for Corviknight, so answers like non-Fighting-type Great Tusk, Arceus-Ground, Eternatus, and Altarianite Dragonite are essential. Venusaurite variants should be paired with an alternative Sablenite user like Blissey, Hippowdon, or Cresselia, as entry hazard denial is especially important on bulkier teams.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Physically Defensive Corviknight sets can use Well-Baked Body to check a wide variety of Fire-types, including Cinderace, Ogerpon-H, Moltres, Heatran, and Iron Moth lacking Discharge; however, it loses a lot of bulk and results in worse matchups against Roaring Moon, Zamazenta, and offensive Great Tusk. Specially defensive sets can use Water Absorb to check Ogerpon-W, Manaphy, and Choice Specs Primarina while preventing Swampert and Primarina from pivoting out with Flip Turn or Bulletproof to let Corviknight check Cinderace, Moltres, Choice Specs Primarina, and Gholdengo lacking Thunderbolt, but Corviknight often gets getter value out of its other abilities. Corviknight can run a set with Bulk Up, Agility, Roost, and Power Trip with an immunity ability such as Volt Absorb on hyper offense teams to surprise opponents and potentially sweep teams if lacking appropriate checks.

Checks and Counters

Electric-type Moves: Without Volt Absorb, Corviknight gets destroyed by Electric-types like Zapdos and Sandy Shocks as well as Electric-type move coverage like Thunderbolt Latios and Deoxys-S.

Fire-types: Without Well-Baked Body, Fire-types like Iron Moth, Moltres, Cinderace, and Heatran easily defeat Corviknight.

Strong Special Attackers: Choice Specs Gholdengo and Primarina can 2HKO Corviknight even if it's running maximum HP and Special Defense EVs.

Physically Defensive.description:
Corviknight's great defensive typing and solid utility moves make it a defensive staple in the tier, checking physical threats like Roaring Moon, Zamazenta, and Great Tusk. Fluffy is the generally preferred ability, as it provides Corviknight with more physical bulk, letting it have a much easier time checking the aforementioned physical attackers, along with Kingambit. Intimidate gives Corviknight a better matchup into Chien-Pao, Mold Breaker Great Tusk, and the Ogerpon formes excluding Ogerpon-H. Corviknight favors Brave Bird due to its higher power and ability to deal significant damage to Great Tusk and Zamazenta, but Body Press can be used to hit Ting-Lu, Iron Treads, and Kingambit. U-turn helps Corviknight's allies by generating momentum, Roost gives it longevity, and Defog removes entry hazards to aid Stealth Rock-weak partners like Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-H. Rocky Helmet punishes Great Tusk and non-Magic Guard Roaring Moon and Zamazenta as well as the many U-turn pivots like Corviknight in the tier, while Leftovers provides Corviknight with extra longevity. Corviknight runs 0 Speed IVs and a Relaxed nature to grants its allies safe entry with U-turn.

Corviknight is used mostly on balance structures that appreciate its defensive prowess, entry hazard removal, and ability to provide slow pivoting. Specially defensive Pokemon like Swampert, Manaphy, and Moltres are heavily reliant on their held items, so Corviknight serves them well by functioning as a Knock Off absorber from attackers like Roaring Moon, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads. Special attackers like Gholdengo, Zapdos, and Iron Moth are quite threatening to Corviknight, so the aforementioned specially defensive pokemon can form a strong defensive core with Corviknight - further upheld by their capacity to tank attacks from Fire-types like Cinderace and Heatran, as well as non-contact physical attackers like Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-W if using Fluffy. If using Intimidate, Corviknight benefits from a Fighting-type resist such as Pecharunt or Scream Tail to take on strong Sword of Ruin attackers equipped with a Choice Band like Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Slither Wing.

Dual Screens.description:
With its remarkable defensive profile and utility options, Prankster Corviknight becomes an effective lead at setting dual screens to support its teammates. Prankster-boosted Taunt allows Corviknight to shut down foes like Great Tusk, Skarmory, and Deoxys-Speed from setting their entry hazards or own dual screens; stop Cinderace and opposing Corviknight from removing its dual screens with Court Change and Defog; prevent offensive threats like Zamazenta, all Ogerpon formes, and Iron Boulder from using it as setup fodder; block Trick from Choice item users like Scream Tail and Gholdengo that would otherwise cripple it; and additionally stop defensive Pokemon like Gholdengo, Scream Tail, and non-Prankster Pecharunt from healing freely, letting its teammates overwhelm them more easily. U-turn makes use of Corviknight's middling Speed tier to support its teammates by bringing them in safely after stomaching an attack, and it's especially valuable against Dark-type foes like Chien-Pao, Kingambit, and Taunt Roaring Moon that can otherwise set up in front of or even shut down Corviknight.

Corviknight is exclusively found on dual screens hyper offense teams. As a result, high caliber offensive threats like Tail Glow Manaphy, IronPress Zamazenta, and Dragon Dance Roaring Moon pair well with it, as they appreciate Corviknight bringing them in safely through U-turn and its dual screens to set up more easily. Double Dance sweepers such as Iron Crown and Galarian Moltres benefit from said dual screens even more, as they require multiple turns of setup before wreaking havoc. Other setup sweepers like Iron Boulder, Iron Hands, and Kingambit have the added benefit of threatening Cinderace and Defoggers like opposing Corviknight and Mandibuzz—especially since Mandibuzz can use Defog freely even in the face of Corviknight—preventing them any free opportunities of ever removing Corviknight's dual screens. Since other foes like Zapdos, Iron Moth, and Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Kingambit can also use Corviknight as entry points, teammates that can come in afterwards to either threaten or use them as setup fodder are also beneficial, with the aforementioned Iron Boulder, Deoxys-S, Zamazenta, and Great Tusk capable of doing so. Furthermore, Corviknight's ability to prevent Stealth Rock from going up with Taunt also gives setup sweepers like Ogerpon-Hearthflame and Chien-Pao more opportunities to get rolling.

Immunity.description:
Corviknight's great utility and defensive typing, further bolstered by an immunity-granting ability, make it an excellent special wall and defensive pivot. Volt Absorb lets it counter Electric-types such as Zapdos and Sandy Shocks and helps against special attackers that rely on Electric-type coverage, such as Deoxys-S, Latios, and Iron Crown. Similarly, Well-Baked Body shuts down Ogerpon-H, Moltres, and non-Discharge Iron Moth. Brave Bird is the go-to STAB move, while Body Press is an option on Well-Baked Body sets to take advantage of the Defense boosts. U-turn generates momentum for Corviknight’s teammates, and Defog provides valuable hazard control. A Sassy nature with 0 Speed IVs is crucial for Corviknight's role as a slow pivot.

Corviknight fits on balance and bulky offense teams, where its longevity and consistency gives it a niche over Iron Treads. Corviknight can pivot in more offensive teammates like Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-H, which also appreciate its ability to remove entry hazards. Corviknight is threatened by physical wallbreakers such as Zamazenta and Ogerpon-W, making physically defensive walls like Great Tusk and Pecharunt good teammates. Corviknight can also be overwhelmed by neutral special attacks from Gholdengo and Primarina, so it needs backup from RegenVest users like Manaphy and Swampert. In exchange, Volt Absorb Corviknight helps Manaphy answer Electric-types, while Well-Baked Body helps Swampert answer Fire-types carrying Grass-type coverage like Iron Moth and Heatran.

Physically Defensive.description:
• Corviknight's high physical bulk gives it a strong defensive presence in the tier. It is one of the few consistent counters to strong Ground-types like Great Tusk, physical attackers like Chien-Pao, and some special attackers like non-Choice Specs Iron Bundle. Furthermore, its access to Defog also makes it a solid entry hazard remover, though it struggles against Gholdengo.
  • Body Press provides Corviknight with a way to leverage its high Defense stat, doing significant damage to Fighting-weak Pokemon.
  • Brave Bird allows Corviknight to threaten Flutter Mane and Great Tusk. Alternatively, Iron Head can be used to threaten the former while avoiding recoil damage.
  • Maximum HP investment and enough Defense to check Chien-Pao is combined with Leftovers and 96 Special Defense EVs, which allows Corviknight to take two Mystical Fires from most Flutter Mane, as well as giving it the ability to take on non-Choice Specs Iron Bundle and weaker attacks like Freeze-Dry from Choice Specs Iron Bundle.
  • Tera Steel or Flying can be used to shed the weaknesses of Corviknight's dual typing: Tera Steel allows Corviknight to resist Ice-type attacks from Chien-Pao, while Tera Flying allows Corviknight to resist Great Tusk's Fighting-type attacks. Depending on your choice, Terastallization also amplifies the power of either Iron Head or Brave Bird.
  • Corviknight works well as a part of a defensive core with Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Blissey, which can handle threats like Miraidon that obliterate Corviknight. Additionally, Corviknight makes a great partner for offensive threats like Chi-Yu, which appreciate a teammate that easily switches into Ting-Lu, or Great Tusk, which appreciates opposing Great Tusk being worn down.

Specially Defensive.description:
• Specially defensive Corviknight can switch into foes like Flutter Mane, Iron Bundle, Gholdengo, and Glimmora.
  • U-turn is used to make Corviknight an effective defensive pivot that can maintain momentum against foes that force it out such as Miraidon and Koraidon.
  • Mirror Armor allows Corviknight to check Mystical Fire Flutter Mane, which would otherwise beat it. Alternatively, when paired with Pressure, Protect enables Corviknight to avoid being 2HKOed by Hydro Pump from Choice Specs Iron Bundle, as well as allowing Corviknight to deplete PP with Pressure more effectively.
  • Corviknight can use Tera Steel to get rid of its weakness to Electric and better take on Ice-type moves from Iron Bundle. Alternatively, it can opt to use Tera Ground to become immune to Miraidon's powerful Electro Drift.
  • Specially defensive Corviknight needs help dealing with strong physical wallbreakers such as Chien-Pao from teammates like Dondozo and Scream Tail. Furthermore, Pokemon that are especially threatened by Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle, such as Koraidon, Great Tusk, and Skeledirge, are able to rely on specially defensive Corviknight as a consistent switch-in.

Defensive.description:
With a wonderful resistance-laden defensive typing, as well as the ability to ignore most entry hazard damage, Corviknight is a premier defensive staple in the tier. Brave Bird hits Ogerpon-W, Rillaboom, and Iron Valiant hard while doing decent damage to Great Tusk and Enamorus. Brave Bird is generally best used on balance teams that struggle with Ogerpon-W and already contain solid answers to late-game Kingambit. Body Press hits Kingambit, Kyurem, and Ting-Lu especially well. It also has immediate synergy with Iron Defense, allowing Corviknight to more confidently handle physical setup sweepers such as Dragonite, Gliscor, and Kingambit, especially with Pressure to more quickly stall out their attacks' PP. Defog allows Corviknight to fulfill the role as the team's hazard remover, with Corviknight often finding ample opportunities to remove hazards against common setters such as Iron Treads, Ting-Lu, and Gliscor. Defog Corviknight can also beat them in the long term, as Pressure makes their hazard move's PP drain faster than Defog's. Defog is best used on teams with another form of hazard control, which allow Corviknight to act as the secondary hazard remover to alleviate the pressure on its teammate; this is especially valuable against non-Gholdengo teams. With U-turn, Corviknight becomes an exceptional pivot, using its excellent bulk and defensive typing to safely bring in teammates after taking a hit. The move is often best used on bulky offensive and balance teams that appreciate the momentum swing Corviknight adds, especially as an opportunity to bring terrifying wallbreakers onto the field. In addition to the provided combinations, a nicher set using Iron Defense, Body Press, Brave Bird, and Roost can be used on teams that want maximum proactivity from Corviknight, notably guaranteeing the matchup against even Tera Ghost Kingambit, though the lack of team support is noticeable. Corviknight generally prefers a physically defensive spread to better handle Dragonite, Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Kingambit, though 120 Speed EVs can also be run on IronPress variants to outspeed Adamant variants of Kingambit and Ursaluna. Alternatively, balance teams that struggle to handle Kyurem and Darkrai while having other checks for the aforementioned physical threats may appreciate a more specially defensive spread with 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 SpD and a Sassy nature. When running this variant, Corviknight should pick Brave Bird as its main attack, since the lower Defense investment will make Body Press much more ineffectual. Rocky Helmet is generally the preferred item to punish contact moves such as Landorus-T's and opposing Corviknight's U-turn and Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge, but Leftovers is also acceptable to help keep Corviknight slightly healthier, particularly helping to mitigate Stealth Rock damage, especially on specially defensive sets. Corviknight generally prefers Tera Dragon to resist Ogerpon-W's STAB attacks, as well as Fire-type attacks such as those from Cinderace and Heatran in a pinch. Tera Fighting can be used on Iron Defense + Body Press sets to make Corviknight a more reliable late-game Kingambit answer. Tera Water provides Fire and Water resistances similarly to Tera Dragon, but it also grants a better matchup against Weavile and Dragon Dance Kyurem. Many other defensive Tera types can be used for complementing specific team structures. For example, Tera Ice can be used on specially defensive sets to handle special Kyurem for bulkier balance teams with good hazard control, and Tera Ghost lets Corviknight beat Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta on teams without another sufficient answer to it.

Corviknight's flexibility in its moves and Tera type, as well as the role it fulfills, makes it a welcome choice on a myriad of team structures, ranging from stall to bulky offense. Stall teams will appreciate Corviknight for its ability to absorb Knock Off, remove hazards, switch into Great Tusk, and act as extra insurance against Kingambit. In return, Corviknight appreciates Blissey absorbing strong special attacks from threats such as Darkrai and Iron Moth, Galarian Weezing helping remove entry hazards against Gholdengo, and Dondozo checking physical setup threats such as Zamazenta. On balance and bulky offense teams, Galarian Slowking, Ting-Lu, and Garganacl are good teammates to help absorb strong special attacks from Zapdos, Raging Bolt, Iron Moth, and Heatran well; in return, Corviknight can switch into Great Tusk, Hisuian Samurott, Ogerpon-W, and Kingambit, which they fear. Corviknight and Galarian Slowking can also form a pivoting core together to bring in offensive teammates via U-turn and Chilly Reception, respectively, enhancing their synergy. Furthermore, Corviknight helps limit hazards with Defog and absorbs the debilitating Knock Off to enhance their longevity. Corviknight pairs well with wallbreakers such as Dragapult, Kyurem, and Ogerpon-W, as it can keep them healthy with hazard removal and find opportunities to bring them onto the field via U-turn, allowing them to continue to make progress for the team. Corviknight can additionally switch into common answers to these teammates such as Ting-Lu, Galarian Slowking, and Dragonite, respectively, further patching up the team's weaknesses. Cinderace is a great teammate on these squads to form a dual hazard removal core, with Cinderace threatening out and removing hazards against Gholdengo for Corviknight. Cinderace also can take a Fire-type attack such as Heatran's Magma Storm in a pinch and threaten slower wallbreakers like Ogerpon-W for Corviknight, while Corviknight can handle Landorus-T and Gliscor for Cinderace, especially as they're hazard setters that Cinderace is scared of.

Defensive Pivot (Flying).description: With crucial neutralities to Rock and Ice, as well as several other resistances that let it wall several metagame threats such as Mamoswine, Mega Lopunny, and Iron Boulder, Corviknight is a solid entry hazard remover and pivot that mitigates the weakness to Stealth Rock commonly found on Flying teams. Body Press minimizes its passivity, notably hitting foes such as Mega Lopunny, Weavile, and Ogerpon-C, but Iron Head can be used instead to hit Fairy-types like Iron Valiant, Mega Diancie, and Alolan Ninetales. Pressure ensures that Corviknight doesn't run out of Defog PP as easily because it can switch into foes setting up Stealth Rock and lower their PP, such as Piloswine, Archaludon, and Ferrothorn, but Mirror Armor can be used instead to avoid a 2HKO from Mega Diancie's Mystical Fire. The first EV spread, even if Corviknight loses Leftovers, avoids a 2HKO from Mega Gallade's Close Combat, a 2HKO from Mega Lopunny's Close Combat after Stealth Rock, and an OHKO from Great Tusk's +1 All-Out Pummeling. However, the alternate EV spread still avoids a 2HKO from Mega Lopunny's Close Combat, and it avoids a 2HKO from Choice Specs Protean Greninja's Ice Beam with Leftovers recovery. Mantine is a solid partner for Corviknight, as it can switch into Fire-types such as Mega Charizard Y, Volcarona, and Heatran, and it also forms a defensive core by more consistently handling special attackers for it. Corviknight's role compression also allows Mantine to run Toxic over Defog, or if Mantine is desired as a Defogger instead, Corviknight can run Iron Head + Body Press. Gliscor and Landorus are also good allies to switch into Electric-types that force out Corviknight such as Zapdos, Raging Bolt, Zeraora, and Alolan Raichu, in turn also forming a pivoting core with Corviknight. Offensive Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y, Mega Aerodactyl, and Tornadus-T appreciate Corviknight's slow pivoting to safely be brought onto the field; in return, they act as offensive checks to foes that Corviknight can't threaten by itself such as Great Tusk, Mega Gallade, and Ogerpon-W.

Shell Smash (Rock).description:
Drednaw is a fierce setup sweeper, capable of turning the tide against unfavorable matchups like Ground, Steel, and Water. Stone Edge is Drednaw's hardest hitting move, dealing with Pelipper and Dragonite. Liquidation hits troublesome Ground-types like Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Ting-Lu. Earthquake threatens Water Absorb Clodsire, Toxapex, and Bisharp, while Strong Jaw-boosted Crunch nails switch-ins such as Slowbro, Brambleghast, and Air Balloon Gholdengo. Swift Swim is preferred to aid Rock in the matchup against Water rain teams; however, Strong Jaw allows Drednaw to muscle through the aforementioned roadblocks when using Crunch. Air Balloon improves Drednaw's performance in the Ground matchup, allowing for more setup opportunities, while White Herb retains Drednaw's defensive stats to have an improved chance against priority move users like Azumarill, Mimikyu, and Bisharp.

Garganacl's ability to pressure Gastrodon, Quagsire, and Corviknight with Salt Cure is heavily appreciated, easing Drednaw's time sweeping. Swords Dance Ogerpon-C works alongside Drednaw to overwhelm types such as Flying, Water, and Ground by breaking down walls such as Skarmory, Toxapex, and Clodsire. Hisuian Arcanine deals with Steel types like Scizor and Skarmory. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder outspeeds and removes Choice Scarfed threats like Meowscarada, Roaring Moon, and Greninja which outspeeds and revenge-kills Drednaw even after a Shell Smash. Glimmora's colorful movepool allows it to check a myriad of threats like Breloom, Meowscarada, and Iron Valiant with Sludge Wave, Great Tusk, Quagsire, and Quaquaval using Energy Ball, Gholdengo, Toxapex, and Toxicroak with Earth Power, and finally Hydreigon and Gallade using Dazzling Gleam. Choice Band Tyranitar heavily dents walls such as Corviknight, Slowbro, and Toxapex and sets up sand to increase Drednaw's bulk. Lycanroc aids in the Dark matchup due to its useful coverage in Close Combat and Play Rough and takes out faster foes like Enamorus and Flutter Mane with Accelerock. Coalossal provides entry hazards in Spikes and Stealth Rock, removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin, and helps against Gholdengo and Meowscarada due to its Fire typing.

Physically Defensive (Rock).description:
Coalossal is a decent defensive wall that fits well on Rock teams due to it being able to tank physical hits from Scizor and Meowscarada, which greatly threaten Rock teams. Coalossal does well in the Steel matchup, as it threatens Gholdengo, Corviknight, and Skarmory. Flame Body allows it to fish for burns to weaken physical threats like Kleavor, Scizor, Bisharp, Mimikyu, and Meowscarada. Body Press is a great move thanks to Coalossal's high Defense stat that allows it to deal incredible damage to Bisharp. Rapid Spin combined with Heavy-Duty Boots allows Coalossal to come in and remove hazards without taking any chip damage, so its teammates won't get worn down. Will-O-Wisp allows Coalossal to burn physical threats such as Kleavor, Hoopa-U, and Iron Hands. Spikes is another option to run on Coalossal over Will-O-Wisp to help Rock teams stack hazards and wear down foes.

Garganacl helps Coalossal by dealing with defensive Pokemon like Quagsire, Gastrodon, and Heatran with Salt Cure. In return Garganacl appreciates Coalossal checking Meowscarada. Air Balloon Shell Smash Drednaw is another good teammate for Coalossal, providing a soft Ground-type immunity and dealing with Ground- and Steel- types like Landorus-T, Sandy Shocks, Iron Treads, Heatran, and Hisuian-Goodra. Choice Scarf Glimmora with its diverse moveset is another option to pair with Coalossal, as it can outspeed and threaten to OHKO non-Choice Scarf users like Iron Valiant and Greninja. Glimmora can also deal with Water-, Fighting-, Dark-, and Dragon- Types like Quagsire, Hisuian Liligant, Hisuian Samurott, and Hydreigon with its various coverage moves. Furthermore, Glimmora run Air Balloon to act as an alternative Ground-type immunity that can deal with threats like Quagsire and Great Tusk. Tyranitar sets sand for Coalossal to boosts its Special Defense, which can allow Coalossal to tank special attacks from Choice Scarf Gholdengo and Choice Specs Magnezone and threaten them in return. Choice Band Lycanroc-D is a good revenge killer that can help out Coalossal by taking out threats such as Enamorus and Cloyster with Accelerock and Urshifu-R and Clodsire with Psychic Fangs. Hisuian Arcanine is another good revenge killer with Extreme Speed and can act as a wallbreaker, taking out foes such as Toxapex and Clodsire with Head Smash and Flare Blitz, respectively. Kleavor is a good lead for Rock teams, as it can deal damage while setting up Stealth Rock with Stone Axe, which helps with hazard stacking. In return, Coalossal complements Kleavor by dealing with Scizor. Diancie can ease the Fighting match by dealing decent damage to Gallade and Iron Valiant with Moonblast and by being able to take Fighting-type moves due to its Fairy-typing. In return, Coalossal helps Diancie by dealing with Scizor, Bisharp, and Meowscarada.

zu.overview: Sandaconda is a good defensive Pokemon in SV ZU thanks to its bulk and Shed Skin. The increased reliability of Rest as recovery lends Sandaconda the longevity to check Pokemon like Muk and Primeape. Options like Stealth Rock, Glare, and Coil diversify Sandaconda into a great support Pokemon or a bulky setup sweeper. Sandaconda is an excellent Terastallization user to boot, enhancing its defensive profile to become even tougher to break or enabling its own sweeps. However, Shed Skin does not make Rest perfectly reliable, hampering Sandaconda's consistency. Physical attackers with super effective STAB moves like Beartic and Virizion are very problematic for Sandaconda and coerce it to burn Terastallization for its team. Despite its Electric immunity, Sandaconda's lower special bulk can leave it to be overwhelmed by coverage and additional STAB attacks from Jolteon, Magneton, and Rotom. Sandaconda also faces competition from Regirock, another Stealth Rock setter that much more reliably takes on physical attackers like Hitmontop, Beartic, and Sneasel.
zu.comments:
Other Options

Sandaconda has access to Body Press, which does hit Orthworm harder, but Rock Blast and Scale Shot provide better general coverage against most Pokemon immune to Ground.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Most Grass-types take little damage from Earthquake and threaten Sandaconda out with their STAB moves. Dipplin, Appletun, and Lurantis can wall Sandaconda in longer games. Lurantis and Toedscruel can remove Sandaconda's Stealth Rock and Rocky Helmet. Whimsicott and Calm Mind Virizion can easily take advantage of Sandaconda, though they don't appreciate Glare hurting their great Speed stats. Tera Dragon and Scale Shot can give Coil Sandaconda some recourse against some Grass-types but can make its position against Pokemon like Dipplin and Whimsicott worse.

Pokemon Immune to Ground: Ground-immune walls like Articuno and Dipplin can walk on Sandaconda, while Orthworm can use it as fodder for setting up Coil or entry hazards. Mesprit can use Sandaconda to set up, block its Glare with Substitute, and use Tera Fairy to completely wall sets with Scale Shot. However, Ground-immune Pokemon weak to Rock, such as Charizard and Minior, must be wary of Rock Blast or Stone Edge. Only Vikavolt and Rotom are immune to Glare.

Special Attackers: Sandaconda's lower special bulk leaves it easily overwhelmed by Typhlosion, Jolteon, and Magneton, though all of them are OHKOed by Earthquake and must be wary of Sandaconda catching them with a defensive Terastallization.

Water-types: Clawitzer, Poliwrath, and Veluza hit Sandaconda for strong super effective damage and generally tolerate an Earthquake.

Ice-types: Sneasel is powerful enough to overwhelm Sandaconda with a boost or some chip damage and can pick off Sandaconda's offensive Scale Shot set with Ice Shard even if Sandaconda has a boost, though it takes a lot of Rocky Helmet chip damage from Sandaconda when it uses Triple Axel.

Physical Wall.description:
Sandaconda is a great wall thanks to its natural bulk, Shed Skin, and Ground typing. Common physical attackers like Muk, Primeape, and Regirock struggle to break through Sandaconda, and its great defensive profile enables it to consistently set up Stealth Rock. Rock Blast lets Sandaconda strike foes such as Articuno, Charizard, and Mesprit that it cannot touch with Earthquake. Alternatively, Glare lets Sandaconda spread paralysis and punish Pokemon like Dipplin, Orthworm, and Virizion that it would deal little damage to anyway. Rest and Shed Skin can keep Sandaconda healthy, although the inconsistency of Shed Skin can leave it out to dry. Rocky Helmet helps Sandaconda further wear down physical attackers like Muk and Regirock trying to break through it, and it enables Sandaconda to punish U-turn from pivots like Mesprit and Primeape. Tera Poison makes Sandaconda a more reliable wall to physical attackers like Primeape, Brute Bonnet, and Virizion. Tera Ghost makes Sandaconda an even more sturdy wall to physical setup sweepers like Toxicroak and Regirock, improves its matchups against Fighting-types like Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel, and lets it spinblock Sandslash and Hitmontop. Tera Water helps Sandaconda handle physically offensive Ice-types like Sneasel, Beartic, and Froslass.

Sandaconda is a good physical wall for balanced teams looking to compress entry hazard setting on a teammate that isn't bothered as much by residual damage and status compared to Regirock, Orthworm, and Sandslash. Bulkier offensive teams also benefit from the utility and bulk Sandaconda offers in Glare and absorbing status from Weezing and Muk for offensive teammates. Sandaconda's Water weakness makes special walls like Cryogonal, Whimsicott, and Eelektross helpful for managing Clawitzer. Sandaconda is not offensively threatening to walls like Dipplin and Articuno, so teammates like Magneton and Charizard can compensate for Sandaconda's poor matchup against them and have an easier time against said targets if Sandaconda has paralyzed them with Glare. Sandaconda invites in hazard setters like Mesprit and Orthworm due to its passivity, so teamamates that can remove hazards like Lurantis and Hitmontop make good partners for Sandaconda.

Coil.description:
Sandaconda serves as a deadly late-game threat with the powerful combination of Coil, Rest, and Shed Skin. Earthquake hits most of the tier for at least neutral damage, while Sandaconda's other attacking move hits Pokemon that are immune to Earthquake like Charizard and Dodrio. Scale Shot allows Sandaconda to boost its Speed, outspeeding the entire unboosted metagame except for common Choice Scarf users like Typhlosion at +2. Alternatively, Stone Edge doesn't drop Sandaconda's Defense and has more immediate potential to threaten Flying-types like Minior, Articuno, and Charizard. Rest acts as excellent recovery to keep Sandaconda healthy and combines well with Shed Skin to make it more reliable and help it serve as a wall in early- and mid-game scenarios, especially when combined with Tera Dragon to flip matchups on common Water- and Grass-types like Poliwrath and Venusaur. Coil Sandaconda can opt to run less Speed in exchange for more bulk, with 224 Speed EVs and a neutral nature being enough to outpace base 110 Speed Pokemon at +1. Sandaconda can also opt to run Attack investment instead of HP, but this makes it more difficult to wall the foes it's tasked with setting up on late-game.

Levitate users such as Mesprit and Rotom serve as potentially problematic Pokemon, since they are immune to Earthquake and can become fully immune to Sandaconda's moves, if it's running Scale Shot, with Tera Fairy, so specially bulky teammates like Naclstack and Mesprit can be extremely helpful to counteract them. Orthworm poses similar issues due to Earth Eater and Iron Defense, so wallbreakers that threaten it like Charizard and Typhlosion are invaluable as teammates. These two as well as Dodrio and Beartic also threaten Grass-types, which cause problems for Sandaconda pre-Terastallization. Water-types pose similar issues while also often carrying super effective coverage for Terastallized Sandaconda, so teammates like Poliwrath and Virizion benefit it greatly. In return for all of these potential partners' help, Sandaconda turns many physical attackers into setup fodder. Some common examples of Pokemon completely walled by it late-game include Primeape, Muk, and Regirock; after Terastallization, this list expands to include other threats like Poliwrath and Brute Bonnet.

Defog.description:
Despite its poor base stats, Cramorant shines as an entry hazard remover thanks to a unique ability that can provide constant pressure on an opposing team as well as spread status in Gulp Missile, pressuring common entry hazard setters like Mudsdale and Palossand, and a defensive typing that lets it check common foes like Arcanine, Hariyama, and Salazzle. Brave Bird synergizes well with Gulp Missile, taking advantage of its Defense drops and forcing out Pokemon like Florges and Milotic that would otherwise not mind staying in on Cramorant. Hurricane avoids the issue of Brave Bird dealing recoil damage and making contact while also hitting Amoonguss harder, but it is prone to missing due to its low accuracy and doesn't take advantage of Gulp Missile's Defense drops. The given EV spread allows Cramorant to avoid a 2HKO from Choice Band Paldean Tauros-F using Close Combat or Flare Blitz while outspeeding Adamant Golurk, while the rest is put into Special Defense to better check special threats like Tastugiri. Tera Steel is recommended to remove Cramorant's Rock and Electric weaknesses while giving it many relevant resistances to the STAB moves of Pokemon such as Florges and Alolan Ninetales and preventing it from being poisoned by foes like Skuntank and Amoonguss.

Cramorant fits best on balance teams that appreciate its ability to remove entry hazards while being able to shore up its poor defenses with multiple defensive partners and support offensive Pokemon by spreading paralysis via Gulp Missile. Its biggest weakness is to Electric-types like Pawmot and Rotom-H, which struggle to come in but consistently force it out, so Grass- and Ground-types like Amoonguss and Rhydon,respectively, are heavily recommended to be able to deal with them. Other Ground-types such as Palossand and Mudsdale can also switch into Rock-type moves such as Stone Edge from Paldean Tauros-F and opposing Rhydon as well as scout the occasional Wild Charge from Arcanine, taking some pressure off of Cramorant. In return, Cramorant can switch into Water-types like Choice item Bruxish locked into Wave Crash and Floatzel, and both Palossand and Mudsdale can help handle Fighting-types such as Hisuian Decidueye and Emboar. Dark-types like Skuntank and Hisuian Qwilfish can also switch into Bruxish's Psychic Fangs with the added benefit of switching into Toxic for Cramorant.

nu.overview: Cramorant's access to Defog and amazing defensive typing make it one of NU's premier entry hazard control options. Unlike Altaria, which is quite passive, Cramorant can utilize its ability Gulp Missile to spread chip damage and paralysis onto most opposing Pokemon. Gulp Missile, paired with its STAB combination of Water- and Flying-type attacks, also gives Cramorant favorable matchups against many common hazard setters such as Bronzong, Copperajah, and Swampert. Cramorant is also great against offensive teams because it can take on common Fighting-types such as Heracross and Paldean Tauros-W, and Infernape. Despite Cramorant's potency at removing hazards, it is very weak to Electric-type attacks from common Pokemon such as Bellibolt and Raikou.
