Calm Mind enables Hatterene to stand off against threats such as Volcarona and Greninja. Psyshock threatens special walls and Calm Mind sweepers such as Blissey, Clodsire, and Primarina. Draining Kiss provides a reliable form of recovery along with enabling Hatterene to handle Dark-types like Hisuian Samurott. Finally, Mystical Fire gives Hatterene an option to torch Steel-types such as Corviknight and Iron Treads. Alternatively, Nuzzle acts a support option to slow down problematic targets such as Meowscarada, the Ogerpon formes, and Tornadus-T. The EV spread maximizes Hatterene's physical bulk while outspeeding Toxapex, enabling it to use Psyshock before Toxapex has a chance to use Haze or Recover.

Klefki serves as an incredible teammate for Hatterene, as its secondary Steel typing enables it to check Poison- and Steel-types that handle Hatterene such as Sneasler and Scizor. It also provides dual screens support to enable Hatterene to have an easier time setting up against otherwise overwhelming attackers like the Landorus formes and Greninja. Similarly, Tinkaton can serve as a solid partner with its Steel neutrality and Poison immunity and can more reliably check threats like Alolan Muk, Glimmora, and Corviknight; it is also able to use Thunder Wave to let Hatterene comfortably run Mystical Fire. Iron Valiant's Close Combat can easily remove problematic Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra and Heatran, while coverage options such as Knock Off and Ice Punch can check threats such as Gholdengo and Gliscor, respectively. Flutter Mane easily blasts through faster threats attempting to handle Hatterene such as non-Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, Pecharunt, and Articuno. Azumarill can easily break through threats capable of handling Hatterene such as Hisuian Goodra, Flutter Mane, and Ceruledge while appreciating its use of Nuzzle to slow down would-be checks like Sinistcha and Ogerpon-W. Primarina is a secondary Calm Mind attacker capable of taking on the Steel- and Fire-types that threaten Hatterene like Archaludon, Bisharp, and Cinderace.

Offensive Trick Room (Fairy).description:
Offensive Trick Room Hatterene is a fearsome sweeper that can quickly snowball in games against offensive team structures, such as Dark and rain-centric Water builds. Calm Mind and STAB Draining Kiss make Hatterene very hard to take down without threatening to OHKO it with a physical attack. When under Trick Room, even a damaged +1 Hatterene becomes impossible to be revenge killed by frail threats such as Greninja and Dragapult. While this set primarily seeks to be a wincon, it can still serve as an important utility piece in less favorable matchups like Ground and Steel thanks to Magic Bounce preventing opposing entry hazards. Heavy-Duty Boots allows the user to be more conservative with Hatterene's HP, making it less necessary to switch Hatterene into entry hazard setters like Gliscor and Clodsire, which can wear it down with their attacks. Leftovers is also a great option for passive healing, as Hatterene will naturally take multiple turns to properly set up. At +1, Psychic will OHKO physically defensive Toxapex. Alternatively, Psyshock fares better against Volcarona and opposing Calm Mind users like Primarina.

Klefki supports Hatterene with dual screens and Spikes while also serving a crucial defensive role as a stopgap for threats like Sneasler and Scizor. Offensive Primarina variants pair phenomenally, as they can come in on Steel-types, like Heatran and Corviknight, and immediately threaten to make progress under Trick Room. Mixed Iron Valiant functions as an effective wallbreaker against the Steel-type defensive core of Corviknight, Heatran, and Hisuian Goodra, which Hatterene cannot break. Flutter Mane is one of Fairy's best threats and is essential offensive counterplay for offensive threats that don't immediately fold to a boosted Hatterene, such as Gholdengo and Ogerpon-H. Tinkaton is another solid support option that can set Stealth Rock and create setup opportunities with Encore.

Calm Mind (Psychic).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

anythinggoes.overview: Hatterene carves itself a niche in AG as one of the few viable forms of hazard control. By beating most common hazard setters, such as Deoxys-Speed, Ting-Lu, and Gliscor, Hatterene provides its team with increased longevity. Hatterene fits best on balance and bulky offense teams where it can enable teammates that would otherwise run Heavy-Duty Boots to run other items instead.
anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Pain Split Hatterene can occasionally run Rocky Helmet, which trades some longevity for the ability to rapidly chip Koraidon and Ho-Oh. Usually, this isn't worth it, but on some sufficiently aggressive teams, the game ends too quickly for the loss of longevity to be impactful. Healing Wish is a fringe option that lets Hatterene generate momentum on Trick Room teams or heal a teammate on balance, but the cost of using it outside of Trick Room teams is too high to justify frequent usage.

Checks and Counters

Calyrex-S: Calyrex-S comes in freely on all of Hatterene's moves except for Nuzzle and reliably forces it out.

Steel-types: Common Steel-types like Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Tera Steel Koraidon can all come in relatively freely on Hatterene and force it out or use it as setup fodder, although they must be wary of Nuzzle.

Ho-Oh: Defensive Ho-Oh consistently beats Calm Mind Hatterene, taking minimal damage and blocking Hatterene's recovery from Draining Kiss while doing heavy damage with Sacred Fire and Brave Bird. Ho-Oh can even use Whirlwind to block attempts to pass boosts to teammates, although this can be a high-risk play if Hatterene stays in, thanks to Magic Bounce.

Arceus-Ground: Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground switches in comfortably to on any of Hatterene's moves and sets up in front of it or forces it out.

Miraidon: Hatterene can barely damage Miraidon, even with Draining Kiss, so Miraidon can switch in safely and force Hatterene out several times a game.

Support.description:
Hatterene serves a valuable support role thanks to its ability to slow pivot with Baton Pass and potentially take advantage of slow Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Gliscor to pass boosts to teammates. Calm Mind can be dropped for Pain Split, which provides extra longevity at the cost of removing Hatterene's ability to pass boosts. Draining Kiss is vital to provide Hatterene with recovery, notably allowing it to out-heal Ting-Lu's Earthquake and OHKO Koraidon while simultaneously healing back to nearly full health after surviving a Flare Blitz. Psyshock lets Hatterene beat Calm Mind Arceus-Ground and -Fairy if they start boosting at the same time while also ensuring that it beats Glimmora and Quiver Dance Ribombee. Alternatively, Nuzzle can be used to make Hatterene harder to switch into by crippling potential switch-ins like Ho-Oh or Calyrex-S. Tera Steel is the preferred Tera option, since it allows Hatterene to block Glimmora's Mortal Spin or Eternatus's Sludge Bomb while also letting it more reliably beat Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy, although this comes at the cost of forfeiting any ability to check Koraidon or Ting-Lu. Tera Water can be used instead to resist Flare Blitz, allowing it to beat Choice Band Koraidon or survive a hit if it's been chipped. Tera Normal is also a decent option, since it lets Hatterene become an emergency check to Calyrex-S by becoming immune to Astral Barrage. Leftovers is the preferred item for Hatterene, since it increases its longevity, especially against Calm Mind Arceus formes and Ting-Lu, although Ability Shield can be used instead to block the admittedly rare Skill Swap from Deoxys-Speed or Ribombee and improve the matchup against hyper offense teams. The given EV spread maximizes physical bulk for Calm Mind sets while outspeeding Ting-Lu, which allows Hatterene to use Draining Kiss before it takes any damage from Ting-Lu. Pain Split sets don't need the Speed investment and therefore should run an alternate spread without it.

Hatterene fits best on bulky offense teams that can provide a sturdy defensive backbone to ensure it doesn't have to take many big hits. Ideal defensive teammates include Ting-Lu, which checks Calyrex-S, Miraidon, and Arceus-Ground, as well as Ho-Oh and defensive Arceus-Water, either of which can check Arceus and potentially the Steel-types Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM that could otherwise take advantage of Hatterene. Both Ho-Oh and Arceus-Water also appreciate Hatterene's ability to serve as a backup check to Koraidon and deter Choiced sets from locking into Outrage. Notably, Ho-Oh is an especially good teammate, since Hatterene's ability to block Stealth Rock frees it up to either run alternate defensive items like Rocky Helmet and Leftovers or more safely run offensive items like Choice Band or the rarer Choice Scarf. Arceus is also an excellent teammate, since Hatterene allows it to run Mental Herb to beat Encore or Taunt from Calyrex-S. In return, Arceus provides a solid check to Calyrex-S, which would otherwise come in safely and force Hatterene out. Teammates that can be good receivers for Hatterene's Baton Passed boosts include Miraidon, which Hatterene notably frees up to run Life Orb or Choiced sets, Calyrex-S, which Hatterene allows to run Life Orb, Focus Sash, or Choiced sets more comfortably, and Calm Mind Arceus-Ground or -Fairy. Another good teammate for Hatterene is Choice Scarf Kyogre, which benefits substantially from both Hatterene's ability to get it in safely, either with slow pivoting or passing boosts, and Hatterene's ability to block Spikes, keeping Kyogre's Water Spout powered up.

Bulk Up.description:
Grimmsnarl is a threatening sweeper thanks to its ability to set up and use Substitute with priority because of Prankster. Thanks to its ability, Grimmsnarl can invest fully in its bulk, allowing it to take multiple hits before fainting. Grimmsnarl's STAB combination is also difficult to switch into, as it's unresisted by the entire tier. Sucker Punch helps Grimmsnarl pick off fast frail Pokemon like Kilowattrel and Salazzle. Substitute allows it to take advantage of walls like Milotic, Gastrodon, and Bellibolt, letting it ignore status and set up freely. On top of this, it also helps Grimmsnarl scout Choice-locked Pokemon like Florges and Duraludon. Tera Steel grants it a resistance to Fairy-type attacks, as well as gaining a multitude of other resistances, notably helping Grimmsnarl versus Toxtricity's Boomburst, Staraptor's Brave Bird, and Bronzong's Heavy Slam. Similarly, Tera Poison helps Grimmsnarl take on Fairy-type attacks from Florges, but it trades Tera Steel's wide array of resistances for a resistance to common Fighting-type attacks from faster Pokemon like Heracross and Flamigo. However, it now has to deal with super effective Psychic Noise from both Scream Tail and Florges.

Due to having to rely on Sucker Punch to hit Steel-types like Alolan Sandslash, Grimmsnarl commonly struggles against them; because of this, Grimmsnarl appreciates teammates that can pressure them like Salazzle, Delphox, and Golurk. Grimmsnarl's Substitute is easily broken by powerful wallbreakers like Paldean Tauros-F and Staraptor, or it can be ignored by Toxtricity. So, Milotic, Bellibolt, and Bronzong make for great partners, being able to check these strong offensive threats. Grimmsnarl easily takes advantage of and sets up against special attacking walls like Gastrodon and Bellibolt. In order to get Grimmsnarl in against these Pokemon, it must be paired with teammates that force these walls in and can pivot like Grafaiai and Flamigo. Grimmsnarl, due to being slow and having to rely on Sucker Punch to take care of faster threats, likes to have cleaners alongside it such as Choice Scarf users like Staraptor, Rotom-C, and Bruxish to finish up games after it's beaten the bulkier Pokemon. Grimmsnarl also struggles with sweeping early-game, so wallbreakers like Meloetta, Paldean Tauros-F, and Hariyama pair well to overwhelm shared checks such as Coalossal, Mudsdale, and Qwilfish. Scream Tail and Florges are both annoyances for Grimmsnarl, as they can both lock it into a move with Encore and Trick, respectively. In order to deal with these threats, partners like Skuntank, Salazzle, and Toxtricity work well in tandem with Grimmsnarl.

Dual Screens Support.description:
Set Details

  • Grimmsnarl's main role is to set up Light Screen and Reflect to increase the bulk of its partners. Grimmsnarl can also be an annoying disruptor with Thunder Wave and sometimes Parting Shot. Setting up dual screens is very effective against hyper offensive teams using Koraidon and Calyrex-S, as these teams are normally quite frail, and surviving one extra attack can often be the difference maker in those matchups.
  • Thunder Wave is a good option for disruption and speed control, allowing partners like Miraidon and Urshifu-R to outspeed Calyrex-S and Koraidon, while Parting Shot is good for further weakening foes and giving Grimmsnarl a strong pivoting option, which helps partners like Ho-Oh and Ursaluna activate their abilities of Regenerator and Guts, respectively, with less risk. Spirit Break OHKOes Koraidon before it Terastallizes, as well as being able to threaten both Urshifu formes, and it reduces the Special Attack of Pokemon such as Calyrex-S and Lunala. Foul Play allows Grimmsnarl to do significant damage to Calyrex-I, Calyrex-S, and Lunala.
  • Light Clay allows Reflect and Light Screen to last longer, allowing for prolonged damage mitigation even after Grimmsnarl has fainted.
  • The Special Defense investment allows Grimmsnarl to live a Moonblast from Timid Flutter Mane when Light Screen isn't up, and Grimmsnarl can also live a Choice Specs Miraidon Electro Drift when Light Screen is up. The Defense EVs let it survive Ursaluna's Guts-boosted Facade when behind Reflect.
  • Tera Ghost helps Grimmsnarl avoid Fake Out from Iron Hands, Rillaboom, and Incineroar, which can be crucial to allow Grimmsnarl to get dual screens up or use an extra Thunder Wave. It also gives it an immunity to Zamazenta-C's Body Press and removes the Heavy Slam and Behemoth Bash weaknesses.

Teambuilding

  • Urshifu-R ignores all of Grimmsnarl's damage mitigation with Surging Strikes, and some Choice Band variants can also OHKO Grimmsnarl with Surging Strikes. Taunt from Incineroar and Flutter Mane can effectively shut down Grimmsnarl's supportive ability, leaving it stuck using either Spirit Break or Foul Play. Galarian Weezing's Neutralizing Gas prevents Grimmsnarl from getting its dual screens off immediately, allowing Koraidon, which is usually paired with Galarian Weezing, to easily OHKO it with Tera Fire Flare Blitz.
  • Dark-, Electric-, and Ground-types like opposing Grimmsnarl, Incineroar, Miraidon, and Landorus are immune to Prankster Thunder Wave, reducing Grimmsnarl's effectiveness on the field. Fake Out from Rillaboom, Iron Hands, and Incineroar is also detrimental to Grimmsnarl, as it stops Grimmsnarl from supporting its team. Spore from Amoonguss and Brute Bonnet can make it difficult for Grimmsnarl to get both screens up in a game.
  • Grimmsnarl's dual screens are able to support most teams, but Miraidon, Ho-Oh, Lunala, and Calyrex-I especially enjoy Grimmsnarl's support because they typically favor bulkier playstyles. Miraidon is able to quickly remove Urshifu-R while also protecting Grimmsnarl from Spore with Electric Terrain, and Ho-Oh is a great check for Koraidon, as it resists all of its moves and threatens an OHKO with Brave Bird. Incineroar and Iron Hands provide support with Fake Out, which makes it easier to get both screens up, and Urshifu-R can threaten Taunt Incineroar and other Dark- and Ground-types, which are immune to Thunder Wave, with Close Combat and Surging Strikes.

Light Clay.description:
Grimmsnarl is a reliable defensive support tool for teams in Regulation G. Spirit Break threatens Koraidon and the Urshifu formes, and it also lowers the Special Attack of strong Pokemon like Terapaos and Calyrex-S. Foul Play is also good insurance against both Calyrex-S and Calyrex-I, forcing them to Terastallize if they don't want to take a lot of damage. Thunder Wave provides speed control to allow Grimmsnarl's allies to outspeed foes after they've been paralyzed. Light Clay makes Reflect and Light Screen last longer, allowing it to utilize its other two moves more often. The EVs put into Defense allow Grimmsnarl to always survive a Behemoth Blade from Zacian-C through Reflect after an Intimidate and almost always survive Tera Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R. The EVs put into Special Defense give Grimmsnarl the bulk to survive Electro Drift from Choice Specs Miraidon through Light Screen. Tera Ghost is used to avoid Fake Out, which ruins Grimmsnarl's momentum.

Fake Out is often used to prevent Grimmsnarl from setting Light Screen and Reflect up and can lead to being KOed by double targeting before it moves. To work around Fake Out, exert pressure using Grimmsnarl's partner. Grimmsnarl is typically paired with Terapagos or Kyogre to allow them to shrug off hits as they sweep. Rillaboom and Incineroar are other good options to pair with Grimmsnarl, as their support kit adds to the overall longevity of the team, allowing for stronger Pokemon to get more attacks off. Rillaboom in particular is one of the fastest Pokemon in the metagame that uses Fake Out, which makes it a great option to lead alongside Grimmsnarl to ensure dual screens are set up. Iron Hands and Urshifu-R are also common partners for Grimmsnarl. Iron Hands also provides Fake Out support and a pivoting move, and its Fighting-type STAB option is useful for doing damage to opposing Incineroar, which can use Taunt to disable Grimmsnarl's support moves. Urshifu-R can remove threats to Grimmsnarl like Incineroar and use Taunt to stop foes from using status moves like Taunt and Spore, which stop Grimmsnarl from using its support tools.

Dual Screens.description: • 112 Special Defense EVs allow Grimmsnarl to live a Gholdengo Make It Rain.

ubers.overview: Grimmsnarl finds its place in Ubers as a part of hyper offense teams thanks to its ability to set dual screens with Prankster, allowing more powerful threats to set up safely. Grimmsnarl does not have any viability outside of these team structures due to its middling stats, but the strength of these team styles thanks to the abundance of setup sweepers in Ubers makes it an important consideration in the metagame.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Grimmsnarl can run Thunder Wave to slow down opposing offensive Pokemon, especially Zacian-C that try to set up in front of it; however, other top threats like Miraidon and Arceus-Ground are immune to Thunder Wave, and Grimmsnarl typically finds more utility with Taunt. Grimmsnarl can opt to run Spirit Break over Play Rough, trading some power for a guaranteed Special Attack drop on the opposing Pokemon. Foul Play is another offensive option that can take advantage of Attack-boosting foes like Koraidon and Calyrex-I, but Grimmsnarl is often threatened out by these Pokemon instead.

Checks and Counters

Steel- and Fairy-types: Grimmsnarl is threatened by a plethora of the metagame's top Pokemon, including Zacian-C, Arceus-Fairy, Kingambit, and Necrozma-DM, all of which can deal significant damage to it or threaten set up in front of it and keep it from setting up screens for its teammates.

Taunt: While it is immune to Taunt from opposing Grimmsnarl, other Pokemon such as the Arceus formes, Miraidon, and Landorus-T often carry it, quickly and easily shutting down Grimmsnarl, especially if it isn't running an attacking move.

Phazers: While Grimmsnarl itself isn't necessarily threatened by phazers, the teammates it supports are, as they are prevented from setting up behind the provided screens.

Toxic Spikes: Toxic Spikes are particularly effective against screens-based hyper offense teams, as they put Pokemon on a timer regardless of the extra defenses and setup opportunities provided by the screens, almost requiring a teammate like Eternatus that can absorb them.

Dual Screens.description:
Grimmsnarl's main and only utility is as a dual screens setter on hyper offense teams. It makes use of Taunt to shut down entry hazard setters like Landorus-T and Glimmora, block Defog from Giratina-O, stop opposing Taunt users like various Arceus formes, and prevent Pokemon like Zacian-C, Koraidon, and Miraidon from setting up. Play Rough lets Grimmsnarl threaten Dark-types like Ting-Lu and opposing Grimmsnarl that are immune to Prankster Taunt as well as dealing decent damage to both Koraidon and Miraidon. Parting Shot can be used instead to generate momentum and setup opportunities for Grimmsnarl's teammates. 80 Special Defense EVs allow Grimmsnarl to live two Electro Drifts from Miraidon through Light Screen, with the rest invested to maximize physical bulk. Grimmsnarl should rarely, if ever, be the target of Terastallization, but Tera Ghost can be used to allow it to spinblock Iron Treads and lets it take advantage of the Ghost type's immunities against Choice-locked Koraidon and Extreme Speed from Arceus, while Tera Steel also helps Grimmsnarl avoid being revenge killed by Arceus while flipping its Fairy and Poison weaknesses.

Grimmsnarl is exclusively found on hyper offense teams, where it pairs well with setup sweepers that make use of the screens and pivoting it provides, such as Koraidon, Miraidon, and Calyrex-I. In turn, hyper offense teams that rely on Grimmsnarl benefit from the ability of these powerful teammates to remove Steel-types like Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C that Grimmsnarl struggles to set up screens against. Ting-Lu and Ho-Oh can both use Whirlwind to phaze out sweepers, with the former able to set up entry hazards without much issue in front of Grimmsnarl and the latter able to pivot into attacks and stall out screen turns with Regenerator. Koraidon and Miraidon, respectively, can force out these Pokemon and use them as setup opportunities.

• Grimmsnarl distinguishes itself from Deoxys-S with the ability to pivot with Parting Shot, giving it better longevity while letting teammates set up easier. Grimmsnarl also has a good defensive typing versus Chien-Pao and Marshadow, both of which can revenge kill Grimmsnarl's teammates, making it a decent switch-in. Unfortunately, Grimmsnarl is unable to do much if it does get Taunted itself by Magic Coat Deoxys-S, and because it's unable to prevent Yveltal from using Defog or Calm Mind Arceus-Dark and Chi-Yu from setting up alongside it, Grimmsnarl can become passive against certain team structures; regardless, Grimmsnarl is still good at setting up dual screens for hyper offense teams.
  • Taunt is useful to ensure opposing Pokemon like Arceus, Primal Groudon, Zacian-C, and Zygarde cannot set up alongside Grimmsnarl as it sets dual screens. It's also useful to prevent opposing leads such as Glimmora and Smeargle from setting up entry hazards, letting Grimmsnarl protect its teammates.
  • Parting Shot allows Grimmsnarl to pivot, increasing momentum while allowing for easier setup for the teammate with its stat drops. Spirit Break prevents Yveltal and Arceus-Dark from completely walling Grimmsnarl while also stopping the latter from setting up alongside Grimmsnarl. Thunder Wave is a niche option that allows Grimmsnarl to punish foes like Meteor Beam Eternatus, Arceus-Fairy, and Zacian-C more directly, benefitting its teammates to let them sweep more easily while avoiding a potential sweep.
  • The given special bulk investment allows Grimmsnarl to survive defensive Primal Groudon's Overheat, with the rest of the EVs being dumped into Defense to survive attacks such as 300-Base Power Basculegion-M's Last Respects and Arceus-Ground's unboosted Tectonic Rage without Reflect. However, with both screens up, Grimmsnarl can survive attacks such as Zacian-C's Play Rough and Eternatus's +1 Sludge Bomb.
  • Tera Ghost allows Grimmsnarl to avoid getting hit by Arceus's Extreme Speed, which is useful for slowing down its attempt to sweep through Grimmsnarl's team, allowing it to set up Reflect more reliably. However, Grimmsnarl's teammates are better off using Terastallization, since they benefit from it more. Grimmsnarl should only Terastallize in emergency situations.
  • It is usually best to lead with Grimmsnarl to set up screens early for the team. If there is an opposing Arceus-Dark or Yveltal present though, it may be desirable to lead with something else, such as Eternatus, and play more aggressively with Grimmsnarl around them to ensure that Grimmsnarl isn't direct setup fodder for them. A similar idea applies against Shuckle, since Grimmsnarl cannot deny Sticky Web from going up due to Mental Herb.
  • It's important to set the correct screen against a foe. Physical threats like Marshadow and Rayquaza should be dealt with Reflect, while special threats like Arceus-Fairy and Palkia-O are dealt with Light Screen. This is necessary to ensure Grimmsnarl can set both screens up as opposed to just one, since it will never be OHKOed behind the correct screen.
  • Grimmsnarl works best on hyper offense teams that can capitalize on the extra longevity provided by dual screens, giving them multiple setup opportunities. Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground can reliably take care of Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM, both of which would be an issue for Grimmsnarl, while also having Taunt and Stone Edge to prevent Defog users from removing dual screens. Kyurem-B has a similarly good matchup versus standard Defog users such as Ho-Oh and Giratina-O while also having a good matchup against Dondozo, something Grimmsnarl cannot help with against stall teams because it cannot provide hazard control. It also appreciates the additional bulk to let it set up with Dragon Dance twice, notably letting it outspeed Zacian-C.
  • Teammates that can generally dissuade hazard removal options like Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Yveltal are great for Grimmsnarl. These teammates include Primal Kyogre, Double Dance Primal Groudon, Arceus, Yveltal, and Play Rough Zacian-C, with all five of them needing dual screens support to set up more easily or, in Yveltal's case, dish out more damage versus Ho-Oh and opposing Yveltal. Additionally, Zacian-C does well versus Arceus-Dark and Yveltal, especially since it avoids the OHKO from +3 Tera Dark Foul Play from Choice Scarf Yveltal behind Reflect.

Dual Screens (Dark).description:
Grimmsnarl's access to Prankster, as well as Reflect and Light Screen, makes it invaluable on hyper offensive variants of Dark teams and as a way to take on opposing Dark teams. Prankster lets Grimmsnarl set up priority Reflect and Light Screen, making it easier for teammates to set up. Grimmsnarl's access to Parting Shot allows it to bring in a teammate immediately, but Taunt is also a viable option to prevent Defog and opposing leads setting up entry hazards. Thunder Wave also can be used as a form of speed control. Spirit Break lets Grimmsnarl threaten opposing Dark-type setup sweepers such as Hydreigon and Darkrai that may leverage their Prankster immunity to set up on Grimmsnarl. Grimmsnarl should be used aggressively early-game to capitalize on its teammates' sweeping potential.

Teammates such as Nasty Plot Galarian Moltres, Nasty Plot Hydreigon, Swords Dance Bisharp, and Dragon Dance Roaring Moon all appreciate Grimmsnarl reducing the damage they take while setting up with dual screens. Entry hazard setters like Ting-Lu can be useful to help wear down opposing defensive Pokemon so that Grimmsnarl's teammates can sweep. Choice Scarf Meowscarada is appreciated for being able to revenge kill Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Iron Valiant. Darkrai and Bisharp can utilize Grimmsnarl's dual screens to break through opposing teams, and Hydreigon can break through Steel-types that may threaten Grimmsnarl out. Greninja can threaten out Cinderace and prevent it from using Court Change while also being able to revenge kill Iron Valiant.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Defensive Pivot.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • 244 HP / 252 Def / 12 SpD with Impish: This spread avoids a OHKO from Timid Choice Specs Iron Bundle.

  • 236 HP / 4 Atk / 252 Def / 12 SpD / 4 Spe with Adamant: This spread sacrifices some physical bulk in exchange for KOing Chien-Pao with Fake Out + Spirit Break. It also survives Timid Choice Specs Iron Bundle from full health.

Dual Screens.description:
• With Prankster and the movepool to use it, Grimmsnarl is a good alternative to Alolan Ninetales for setting up dual screens, useful for setting up dangerous sweepers such as Dragonite or Urshifu-R.

  • Parting Shot: Parting Shot is not only useful for dropping stats, but the pivoting action can let Grimmsnarl come in later to set up screens if it's in a bad matchup.

  • Thunder Wave: This is a reasonable alternative for crippling fast foes that may be problematic for sweeps.

  • Taunt: Taunt shuts down phazers and opposing Taunts that could stop the dual screens from being set up.

  • Spirit Break versus Foul Play: Hitting foes like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S makes Spirit Break a good offensive move. Alternatively, Foul Play is notable for breaking Gholdengo's Substitute and punishing physical setup sweepers like Dragonite.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Very Low: This Grimmsnarl should almost never Terastallize, since it's trying to support sweepers rather than deal serious damage on its own.

  • Steel: Tera Steel protects Grimmsnarl against Fairy-type attacks in the extremely rare event that it needs to Terastallize against Flutter Mane in the late-game.

  • Fire: Tera Fire provides both a resistance to Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Ogerpon-H's Ivy Cudgel in the rare event Terastallization is needed.

• The given EV spread and nature allow Grimmsnarl to survive a Swords of Ruin-boosted Extreme Speed from a Choice Band Tera Normal Dragonite, then invests the remaining EVs into Special Defense.

This is a sample set as we work on proper analyses. Stay tuned!

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Grimmsnarl could opt to use Spirit Break over Play Rough, as it has a greater accuracy and reduces the Special Attack of Pokemon it hits. Yet, due to its inability to 2HKO Ting-Lu and its secondary effect being irrelevant most of the time, Play Rough is the better option. Grimmsnarl could also opt to use Sucker Punch, which can OHKO Calyrex-S before it attacks. However, it is not worth using most of the time, as Calyrex-S sometimes runs Tera Fairy, and running Sucker Punch disallows it from using a much more valuable move. Grimmsnarl may also use Thunder Wave, which can cripple certain threats like Nasty Plot Calyrex-S and Scale Shot Koraidon, as well as pestering defensive Pokemon like Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Water, and Ho-Oh. Nonetheless, using Thunder Wave prevents Grimmsnarl from using the more consistent Parting Shot or Play Rough, which have far broader use cases in helping preserve a low HP Grimmsnarl and attacking Ting-Lu, respectively.

Checks and Counters

Ting-Lu: Ting-Lu is immune to Grimmsnarl's Prankster Taunt, and it can freely set up spikes on non-Play Rough Grimmsnarl without any repercussions.

Ribombee: Ribombee can threaten to use Sticky Web, forcing Grimmsnarl to Taunt it while it attacks with a powerful super effective Moonblast.

Zacian-C: Zacian-C threatens a KO on Grimmsnarl with Behemoth Blade, forcing it to use Reflect; however, the opponent can potentially take advantage of this interaction to set up a Swords Dance.

Dual Screens.description:
Light Screen and Reflect, in combination with Prankster, make Grimmsnarl an excellent hyper offense suicide lead. Taunt prevents Pokemon like Calyrex-S, Koraidon, Arceus, and various other sweepers from using Grimmsnarl as setup fodder and stops entry hazard setters like Eternatus, Gliscor, and Deoxys-S from using Spikes and Toxic Spikes. Parting Shot gives Grimmsnarl an excellent method of pivoting while also reducing damage taken for the Pokemon switching in. Alternatively, Grimmsnarl could opt to use Play Rough with an Adamant Nature and maximum Attack investment to have a good chance to 2HKO Ting-Lu, which, being unaffected by Taunt, could otherwise freely set up Spikes in the face of Grimmsnarl. Tera Steel prevents Glimmora from using Mortal Spin and grants Grimmsnarl a resistance to Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade and Arceus's Extreme Speed. The default EV spread allows Grimmsnarl to live an Extreme Speed from a boosted Arceus after a layer of Spikes, with the rest dumped into Special Defense to take hits from Calyrex-S better.

Grimmsnarl is somewhat one-dimensional. As its only role is being a suicide lead, it only fits on hyper offense teams. Sweepers like Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, Tera Fairy Calyrex-S, Double Dance Miraidon, and Swords Dance Koraidon all especially appreciate Grimmsnarl's screens support, as they all value the extra bulkthat makes it easier to set up. Bulkier sweepers like Arceus and Necrozma-DM also benefit from Grimmsnarl's dual screens, as it makes them much more difficult to revenge kill. Since Grimmsnarl is unable to set up entry hazards on its own, it pairs very well with teammates like Glimmora, whose hazards combined with Grimmsnarl's dual screens support make it far easier for its team to sweep. Furthermore, Glimmora can use Mortal Spin to remove opposing Ribombee's Sticky Web and keep off Spikes against Ting-Lu, both of which may prove to be issues for hyper offense teams that do not frequently use Heavy Duty-Boots. Glimmora's Poison- typing enables it to remove Eternatus's Toxic Spikes, which may otherwise cripple setup sweepers. If not running Play Rough, Grimmsnarl is also quite vulnerable to Ting-Lu, which is immune to Grimmsnarl's Prankster Taunt and can freely set up Spikes. Thus, Grimmsnarl appreciates having teammates like Koraidon, which can threaten to cause great damage to Ting-Lu and force it to switch out.

Double Dance.description:
Alcremie faces competition from Fairy-types like Florges and Grimmsnarl, but its access to Acid Armor, STAB Draining Kiss for recovery, and Stored Power keeps it relevant as a bulky setup sweeper. Draining Kiss is good for additional staying power against Fairy-weak Pokemon like Pawmot and Wo-Chien. Stored Power deals with Fire- and Poison-types like Hisuian Typlosion and Venusaur, and it's preferred over Psyshock since it does more damage to Steel-types like Alolan Sandslash and Orthworm. Aroma Veil protects Alcremie from the heal blocking of Psychic Noise from Florges or Uxie to let it continue using Draining Kiss, and it allows Alcremie to set up in the face of Encore users like Whimsicott and Uxie as well as Taunt users like Grimmsnarl and Hisuian Electrode. Leftovers lets Alcremie to slightly increase its staying power on top of recovery from the healing of Draining Kiss, while Grassy Seed is an option for Grassy Terrain teams. The EV spread allows Alcremie to outspeed Wo-Chien and Sandaconda. Tera Poison improves Alcremie's matchups against Poison-types like Salazzle while preserving its good matchups against Fighting-types like Scrafty. Tera Steel also gives Alcremie a poison immunity, flips its Steel weakness into a resistance, and lets it match up counter Fighting- and Fire-types. Steel also gives Alcremie a poison immunity, flips its weaknesses into resistances, and lets it matchup up better against Flying-, Fairy-, and Psychic-types like Galarian Articuno, Florges, and Hisiuan Braviary.

Alcremie has small niches on hyper offense, bulky offense, and Grassy Terrain teams. Pokemon that counter the Steel-types like Pawmot and Arcanine are favorable partners for Alcremie. Toxic, is annoying for Alcremie, but it can be absorbed by Poison- and Steel-types like Salazzle, and Alolan Sandslash as well as Shed Skin Scrafty. Alcremie is bothered by Haze users like Milotic, so it will be essential to knock them out before using Alcremie. Being very susceptible to Trick + Choice Item users, like Florges Delphox or Hoopa Alcremie relies on partners like Espeon as well as Choice item users like Hoopa to deal with them.

Defog.description:
The given spread maximizes Frosmoth's odds of 2HKOing Tatsugiri with Ice Beam while ensuring it isn't KOed by the combination of +2 Surf and Draco Meteor.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ice

Frosmoth can invest 208 EVs into Defense to prevent Corviknight's Iron Head from breaking Substitute under snow and Aurora Veil. However, Frosmoth needs 252 Special Attack EVs to OHKO Skarmory after Stealth Rock if it uses a Timid nature so it doesn't get phazed by Whirlwind.

Quiver Dance (Bug).description:
Quiver Dance Frosmoth is an incredibly threatening setup sweeper thanks to its ability to do massive damage in matchups that Bug struggles with such as Flying and Dragon as well as find opportunities to set up on numerous special attackers like Choice Specs Iron Valiant and Spectrier thanks to Ice Scales. Substitute allows Frosmoth to take advantage of special attackers like those aforementioned as well as dodge status from Pokemon such as Galarian Weezing that cannot break Frosmoth's Substitute. Giga Drain allows Frosmoth to hit troublesome Water-types like Empoleon that can otherwise take it on while allowing it to run away with the Ground matchup by annihilating Quagsire and Mamoswine after a Quiver Dance boost. Ice Beam easily muscles past Ground-, Flying-, and Dragon-types like Gliscor, Dragonite, and Raging Bolt that otherwise pose problems for Bug teams. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Frosmoth to avoid its debilitating Stealth Rock weakness while giving it more opportunities to set up thanks to avoiding Toxic Spikes.

Kleavor is a great teammate for Frosmoth, as it takes care of Fire-types that trouble Frosmoth like Ogerpon-H, Skeledirge, and Gouging Fire as well as setting up entry hazards through Stone Axe to soften defensive checks to Frosmoth such as Heatran. In return, it appreciates Frosmoth taking advantage of revenge killing attempts from the likes of Choice Scarf Latias and Choice Scarf Iron Valiant to set up. Scizor ravages Rock- and Fairy-types that Frosmoth does not appreciate, like Garganacl, Iron Boulder, Flutter Mane, and Choice Band Iron Valiant, with its strong Bullet Punch. In return, it appreciates Frosmoth freezing checks to it like Quagsire and Skarmory. Volcarona melts Steel-types like Gholdengo and Corviknight that trouble Frosmoth, while Slither Wing takes out Heatran and Blissey, making both good teammates. Araquanid provides a pseudo-Fire resistance with Water Bubble and can deal with Fire-types like Heatran, Gouging Fire, and Volcarona. Forretress is a decent teammate, acting as a physically defensive sponge with a good typing as well as a great option in the hazard war, removing hazards with Rapid Spin while setting its own up with Spikes.

Quiver Dance (Ice).description:
Frosmoth is a dangerous setup sweeper on Ice teams when given snow and Aurora Veil support. Quiver Dance allows Frosmoth to be a dangerous wincon when given free turns against passive walls like Amoonguss. Hurricane allows Frosmoth to sweep through Fighting teams after two Quiver Dance boosts while allowing it threaten Fire-types such as Volcarona. Substitute can be used instead to avoid status conditions and easily set up against more passive walls such as Amoonguss and Rotom-W. Giga Drain provides Frosmoth with longevity in sweeping, deals with bulky Water-types like Primarina and Gastrodon, and threatens troublesome Rock teams. Frosmoth's ability to deal large amounts of damage to physical walls like Garganacl and Skarmory is very important to ease the job of other setup sweepers like Weavile and Cloyster. A Timid nature is preferred, as it allows Frosmoth to outspeed threats such as Cinderace, Ogerpon formes, and Iron Valiant after a Quiver Dance. A Modest nature can be used to break past threats such as Empoleon and Alolan Muk

Frosmoth needs snow and Aurora Veil support in order to easily set up on threats like Primarina and Archaludon. Therefore, Alolan Ninetales makes an excellent teammate. Alolan Ninetales can also use Encore to provide Frosmoth with free switch-in opportunities. Frosmoth tends to be slow even after a Quiver Dance boost due to its low initial Speed stat. At +1, it is easily revenge killed by Choice Scarf Iron Boulder, Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, and Choice Scarf Sneasler, so switch-ins to these threats such as Avalugg and Mamoswine are appreciated. Speed control options such as Slush Rush Alolan Sandslash and Thunder Wave Froslass support Frosmoth excellently. Froslass provides Spikes support to chip down checks such as Hisuian Goodra and Galarian Slowking. Sandslash can deal with Hatterene and Articuno for Frosmoth while clearing entry hazards with Rapid Spin, should Frosmoth's Heavy-Duty Boots get Knocked Off. Frosmoth can struggle to break through Haze Toxapex and Articuno, so Kyurem and Weavile make excellent teammates. Frosmoth and Kyurem can work together to overwhelm their shared checks such as Corviknight and Galarian Slowking. Weavile is able to pressure the Fire-types Frosmoth can't break past such as Rotom-H and Heatran with Knock Off and Mamoswine's Stealth Rock support. Cloyster is also a great ally, as it can shred through Fire teams with Rock Blast after a Shell Smash, notably dealing with Ceruledge, which otherwise is extremely difficult to face.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Indeedee-M pairs well with speed control or redirection that allow it to use Expanding Force without being KOed.
  • Priority Tailwind setters like Talonflame pair well with Indeedee-M, as they let it move first while also supporting the offensive teammates like Ursaluna-B that can weaken teams before Indeedee-M cleans up. Electabuzz provides speed control with Electro Web and redirects attacks with Follow Me.
  • Gholdengo completely walls Indeedee-M. Partners like Throat Chop Sneasler and Ursaluna-B can help with this, threatening Gholdengo and forcing it to Terastallize out of its resistance to Expanding Force.

Strategy Comments

  • Indeedee-M is primarily a cleaner with Expanding Force. It is at its best when the foes are weakened and in range of Expanding Force.
  • Since it wants to clean up, Indeedee-M thrives late-game once a partner like Ursaluna-B has dealt large amounts of damage.
  • Indeedee-M struggles with Psychic-resistant foes, specially bulky foes, or some combination of these like Incineroar, Kingambit, or Archaludon. Partners like the Ursaluna formes can help with the Steel- and Dark-types that resist Expanding Force, directly threatening Steel-types and taking advantage of the fact that most Dark-types are weak to Ground like Kingambit and Incineroar. Sneasler can threaten specially defensive foes like Assault Vest Kingambit and Archaludon with Close Combat or Dire Claw if they Terastallize, letting Indeedee-M finish them off late-game. Rillaboom is another threat, overriding Psychic Terrain and threatening Indeedee-M with Wood Hammer. Sneasler helps with this, pressuring Rillaboom with Dire Claw.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Indeedee-M is a fast Psychic Terrain setter that can both boost its partner's Psychic-type damage and use its Psychic Terrain for itself.
  • Expanding Force is Indeedee-M's main method of dealing damage, while the combination of Trick Room and Imprison lets it both set Trick Room against faster teams and deny it against opposing Trick Room. Choice Scarf sets opt for Dazzling Gleam as a spread damage attack to hit Dark-type Pokemon, Trick to potentially cripple Trick Room setters like Porygon2, and Tera Blast as an option for a Normal-type STAB attack. Protect can be used on Focus Sash sets for increased flexibility.
  • Focus Sash lets Indeedee-M survive at least one strong attack, letting it invest fully in Special Attack and Speed, while Choice Scarf lets it outspeed Pokemon like Sneasler and Dragapult.
  • Tera Psychic guarantees Expanding Force OHKOes Amoonguss, while Tera Blast Fighting lets Indeedee-M threaten Dark-types that otherwise wall it.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Normal

Shadow Ball can be run instead of Trick to hit Gholdengo and Ceruledge, helping in the Ghost matchup. Doing so will lose Indeedee-M the ability to Choice-lock walls like Corviknight and Ting-Lu, which can be a pain to break through.

Psychic (Scarf)

Psyshock can be used over Trick to make Indeedee-M more effective against some Calm Mind users and special walls like Primarina and Blissey, respectively, but the overlapping coverage with Expanding Force can often feel wasteful in comparison to Trick or Shadow Ball. Encore can let Indeedee-M act as a failsafe against bulkier setup sweepers that it can't immediately KO, such as Calm Mind Primarina and Nasty Plot Spectrier; this also gives more setup opportunities to Indeedee-M's own frail teammates. However, the opportunity cost of dropping Trick or Healing Wish is extremely high. Terrain Extender is another item that can be used on Indeedee to provide Psychic Terrain longer for its teammates like Armarouge and Hoopa-U, allowing them to use Expanding Force and increase their destructive power.

Psychic (Terrain Setter)

Terrain setter Indeedee-M may use Shadow Ball over Encore to threaten Gholdengo as well as opposing Psychic-types; however, the coverage is minimally useful. Additionally, Indeedee-M can opt for Trick Room to enable slow and powerful teammates such as Hatterene, Choice Band Hoopa-U, and Metagross to remove otherwise faster threats such as Meowscarada, Dragapult, and Flutter Mane; however, using Trick Room is heavily unreliable as a win condition and requires very specific battle conditions for it to succeed. Furthermore, Encore and even Shadow Ball have significantly more value in typical circumstances and should rarely be dropped for Trick Room unless the team is specifically designed for its usage.

Terrain Setter (Psychic).description:
Indeedee-M is an excellent option on Psychic teams due to its ability Psychic Surge, immunity to Ghost-type moves, and useful support arsenal in Encore and Healing Wish. Expanding Force in conjunction with Psychic Surge makes up for Indeedee-M's mediocre Special Attack stat, notably OHKOing Dragapult, the Ogerpon formes, and Mamoswine after minor chip damage. Dazzling Gleam allows Indeedee-M to hit Dark-types such as Roaring Moon, Hydreigon, and Scrafty attempting to switch into Expanding Force. Encore is a great utility option that can deter setup sweepers Indeedee-M can't OHKO like Spectrier, Focus Sash Ceruledge, and Primarina, granting teammates opportunities to switch in and get set up themselves. Healing Wish can give vital teammates such as Hoopa-U and Latios a second chance while also preserving momentum to keep Psychic Terrain going. Terrain Extender is crucial to prolong Psychic Terrain, as the Terrain prevents Ceruledge, Bisharp, and Hisuian Samurott from using their dangerous priority moves.

Hatterene is an impeccable teammate for Indeedee-M, as its ability Magic Bounce and Fairy typing allow it to comfortably bounce back entry hazards from Ting-Lu while also offensively threatening Hydreigon, Roaring Moon, and Assault Vest Gallade. In return, Hatterene appreciates Indeedee-M's ability to take on Spectrier and Hisuian Zoroark as well as Psychic Terrain boosting Hatterene's Psyshock. Hoopa-U and Indeedee-M together are capable of terrorizing Ghost-type teams, as Choice Scarf Hoopa-U threatens Flutter Mane, bulky Gholdengo, and Choice Specs Dragapult. Meanwhile, Indeedee-M prevents Ceruledge from using Shadow Sneak, boosts Hoopa-U's Psychic-type coverage to better combat Pecharunt, and further threatens Ghost with Expanding Force. Indeedee-M is Deoxys-S's biggest benefactor, enabling Deoxys-S's own Expanding Force; disabling Sucker Punch from Bisharp, which Deoxys-S removes via Superpower; and providing a switch-in to Choice Scarf Flutter Mane and Dragapult's Shadow Ball. Deoxys-S provides excellent utility, setting up Stealth Rock, Spikes, or dual screens while also removing Dark-types such as the aforementioned Bisharp. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder is a great teammate to have in the Dark matchup, threatening Meowscarada, Greninja, and Darkrai with Close Combat while also removing Fire-types such as Cinderace, Volcarona, and Hisuian Arcanine. Latios greatly aids in the Ground, Flying, and Dragon matchups, removing threats like Landorus, Dragonite, and Archaludon while providing a Ground-type immunity with Levitate. Slowbro can serve as a check to Hisuian Samurott and Bisharp using a combination of Colbur Berry and Body Press, and it also provides status support by burning threats like Excadrill with Scald and paralyzing fast Dark-type foes such as Roaring Moon, Greninja, and Meowscarada via Thunder Wave. Jirachi sets up Stealth Rock and is neutral to Bug-type moves like U-turn from Scizor, which lets it retaliate with Fire Punch. It also offers Wish support to keep Indeedee-M alive longer, prolonging Psychic Terrain for the team. Jirachi heavily appreciates Indeedee-M threatening Mamoswine and Great Tusk as well as cleric support from Healing Wish, as being burned is detrimental for Jirachi.

Choice Scarf (Normal).description:
Indeedee-M is a good Choice Scarf user on Normal teams due to its decent Speed stat, being able to outspeed threats like Keldeo and Okidogi. Thanks to its part-Psychic typing, it is able to take out foes like Iron Valiant and Urshifu-R with Expanding Force. Combining Psychic Surge with Expanding Force allows Indeedee-M to take out threats like Keldeo, Great Tusk, Iron Hands, and Toxapex. Dazzling Gleam lets Indeedee-M pressure Dark-, Fighting-, and Dragon-types like Choice Specs Greninja, Scrafty, and Hydreigon. Trick can punish common walls like Ting-Lu, Corviknight, and Empoleon, while Healing Wish provides support for the team.

Choice Specs Hisuian Zoroark is a nice teammate for Indeedee-M, being able to check Ghost-, Steel- and Psychic-types like Ceruledge, Archaludon, and Metagross. Hisuian Zoroark also provides help by using Trick to Choice-lock walls like Alolan Muk and Assault Vest Iron Hands. Indeedee-M returns the favor by taking out bulky foes like Clodsire and Toxapex and providing immunity against Sucker Punch Bisharp while the Psychic Terrain from its ability remains active. Ditto helps Indeedee-M as a late-game wincon by transforming into Chien-Pao, Garchomp, and Gouging Fire in the Dark, Dragon, and Fire matchups, respectively, reverse sweeping when possible. Smeargle is a nice entry hazard setter, providing Spikes and Sticky Web for Indeedee-M to slow down fast Choice Scarf users like Sneasler, Urshifu-R, and Roaring Moon. Calm Mind Ursaluna-B deals with specially defensive Pokemon that Indeedee-M can't break like Alolan Muk, Hisuian Goodra, and Tyranitar. In return, Indeedee-M takes out Iron Valiant and Urshifu-R without Choice Scarf for Ursaluna-B and Smeargle. Blissey is a nice teammate that can tank special hits from foes like Greninja and Flutter Mane while also setting Stealth Rock and spreading paralysis with Thunder Wave. Porygon2 is a good defensive wall that is able to tank hits from Ogerpon formes, Gouging Fire, and Ceruledge while also checking them with Foul Play. Porygon2 also pressures Flying-types like Corviknight, Dragonite, and Mandibuzz with Discharge and Ice Beam. Indeedee-M doesn't like hazards, so Braviary is a great option that can remove hazards with Defog while taking out foes like Lokix and Hisuian Samurott with Brave Bird and Close Combat, respectively. Terapagos is another option due to its colorful moveset, including BoltBeam coverage that can take out Skarmory, Garchomp, and Landorus, and it can also remove hazards for the team with Rapid Spin. Terapagos's signature move Tera Starstorm allows Terapagos to dent bulky Pokemon. Loaded Dice Cinccino can be a physical sweeper and hazard remover with Tidy Up. Cinccino also has great coverage, including moves that can deal with Ground-, Water-, Flying-, Dragon-, and Ice-types with Bullet Seed, Triple Axel, and Rock Blast.

Choice Scarf (Psychic).description:
Choice Scarf Indeedee-M's exclusive access to Psychic Surge immediately gives it a niche on Psychic teams as a Terrain setter, and its solid support options, decent offenses, and immunity to Ghost ensure it isn't dead weight outside of that. Expanding Force effectively has 156 Base Power under Psychic Terrain before factoring in STAB, easily making up for Indeedee-M's middling Special Attack with its devastating strength. This makes Indeedee-M a brutally effective revenge killer, picking off most neutral targets, like the Ogerpon formes and Choice Specs Dragapult, after some chip damage. Dazzling Gleam is critical coverage for Dark-types that try to switch into Expanding Force, notably OHKOing Hydreigon, Lokix, and non-Choice Scarf Roaring Moon after Stealth Rock damage. Trick prevents Indeedee-M from becoming dead weight against teams with bulky special walls like Blissey, Alolan Muk, and Hisuian Goodra, letting it hinder them with an unwanted Choice item. Alternatively, Shadow Ball gives Indeedee-M an option to hit Gholdengo with, which can prove useful for Psychic teams, and it also hits opposing Psychic-types like Hatterene super effectively. However, a lack of Trick will make Indeedee-M far easier to handle with the aforementioned special walls. Finally, Healing Wish is an extremely powerful support tool that lets Indeedee-M give a dangerous teammate like Calm Mind Latios a second chance at sweeping. A Timid nature is required, since it lets Indeedee-M outspeed other common Choice Scarf users like Kleavor and Great Tusk.

Steel-types are the bane of Indeedee-M's existence, since it lacks any kind of coverage for them, so having a fallback plan against them is essential. Slowbro is a great switch-in against Steel-type attackers like Excadrill and Heatran, resisting their STAB moves and threatening a powerful Body Press in return; its great physical bulk also helps the team play around other major threats like Tyranitar and Mamoswine. In return, Indeedee-M takes out Hydreigon for Slowbro. Hatterene doesn't fare as well against Steel-types defensively, but it can threaten them with Mystical Fire and give Indeedee-M's team a potent wincon that's made more threatening if Indeedee-M cripples a special wall like Alolan Muk with Trick; reflecting entry hazards with Magic Bounce also improves Indeedee-M's longevity and helps to chip foes into cleanup range. Swords Dance Iron Boulder is a terrifying setup sweeper that can plow through bulkier Pokemon that Indeedee-M struggles with, especially Blissey and Bisharp with Close Combat, and Psychic Terrain is incredible support for it, since it otherwise fears common priority moves. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder is also a great option to cover faster Choice Scarf users that Psychic struggles with like Meowscarada. Choice Band Hoopa-U is another physical wallbreaker that can deal with specially bulky Pokemon, notably OHKOing Bisharp and Gholdengo with Drain Punch and Knock Off. Indeedee-M returns the favor by taking out Choice Scarf Great Tusk and mixed Iron Valiant for Hoopa-U, and it becomes much harder to KO when shielded from Bisharp's Sucker Punch and other priority moves. Offensive Deoxys-S becomes incredibly threatening under Psychic Terrain, since it can use Expanding Force for its STAB move, making Choice Specs and Nasty Plot sets far more threatening. Latios doesn't directly benefit from Psychic Terrain, but it provides a useful Ground immunity for the team, and it enjoys the speed control and Ghost immunity Indeedee-M provides to help it against threats like Flutter Mane. Entry hazard support can greatly help to nudge foes into Indeedee-M's KO range, letting it clean up late-game more easily; Jirachi and Metagross are both decent Stealth Rock setters that can help with this, and Deoxys-S can provide even more hazards thanks to Spikes at the cost of defensive utility. The former two can also switch into common threats to Indeedee-M, like Scizor and Iron Boulder, and Jirachi can use them to generate momentum with U-turn and get Indeedee-M on the field more easily.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Terrain Setter.description:
• Indeedee-M's Psychic Surge sets up powerful allies like Psychic Seed Sneasler and Expanding Force Iron Crown.

  • Dazzling Gleam: While generally weak, Dazzling Gleam is the best way to pressure Dark-types like Chien-Pao and Roaring Moon that are immune to Expanding Force.

  • Encore: Encore helps prevent Indeedee-M from getting set up on while also creating openings for its teammates.

  • Shadow Ball: Shadow Ball is almost exclusively for hitting Gholdengo, which can otherwise be troublesome for common Indeedee-M cores.

  • Healing Wish: Healing Wish is used less for its healing and more for its ability to pivot teammates in safely though at the cost of Indeedee-M itself.

  • Terrain Preservation: Targets such as Ice Spinner Urshifu-R and Grassy Surge Rillaboom can remove Indeedee-M's terrain. For this reason, it is sometimes better to lead with a teammate that can scout for these threats.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Common partners like Sneasler tend to be far more Terastallization hungry than Indeedee-M, so it should be preserved outside of fringe cases.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy turns Indeedee-M's Dark- and Bug-type weaknesses into resistances while giving Dazzling Gleam a nice boost.

  • Psychic: Tera Psychic is a simple offensive option, pushing Expanding Force's power even farther.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar lets Indeedee-M diversify its offensive profile, such as making it easier to 2HKO semi-bulky Gholdengo with Shadow Ball.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 76 Def / 180 Spe with Timid: This bulky EV spread survives Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon and almost always survives Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash and Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquake. The Speed EVs outspeed Adamant Urshifu formes and Modest Iron Crown.

  • 12 HP / 44 Def / 196 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid: This offensive EV spread avoids the OHKO from defensive Landorus-T's Earthquake. It goes less bulky, however, because it wants to be OHKOed by Jolly Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash; this helps secure the most turns of Psychic Terrain possible for teammates.

Choice Scarf Support.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • Support Moves: Encore is generally best used if also using Trick. It's even possible to use all 3 support moves at the cost of a decent matchup against Urshifu-S.

Terrain Setter.description:
Reflect is the preferred screen on Indeedee-F, since its teammates commonly run Psychic Seed, which already boosts their Special Defense. Indeedee-F can viably run Special Attack investment to reduce its passivity and better wear foes down for its teammates. Doing so comes at the cost of bulk, though, which tends to make Indeedee-F less reliable.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Indeedee-F works best on dedicated Trick Room teams, using Follow Me to almost always guarantee its partner to set up Trick Room as well as pairing well with Trick Room sweepers. It sets up Psychic Terrain to prevent Fake Out from disturbing your team's Trick Room setup as well as preventing priority attacks from threatening its partners.

  • Ursaluna and Ursaluna-B are common partners for Indeedee-F. Trick Room can help with the speed control both Ursaluna formes need, and Follow Me can protect them from non-spread moves while allowing them to deal Normal-type damage with Blood Moon and Facade and Ground-type damage with Headlong Rush, Earthquake, and Earth Power. Other Trick Room sweepers, such as Hatterene and Torkoal, are the best Trick Room partners for Indeedee-F. Hatterene can threaten the opponent's team with heavy Psychic-type damage from Expanding Force, and Torkoal can threaten heavy Fire-type damage with Eruption, Weather Ball, and Heat Wave. Gallade can threaten Dark-type Pokemon with Sacred Sword and provide Wide Guard support to protect its side of the field from spread moves. Sneasler pairs nicely with Indeedee-F because Sneasler can hold the Psychic Seed, activating its Unburden ability.

  • Kingambit will decimate any opposing Indeedee-F. Even if Indeedee-F Terastallizes into a Fairy-type, Kingambit will still do significant amount of damage to it. Therefore, a Fighting-type Pokemon like Sneasler should be used to threaten Kingambit, as it can almost always guarantee a OHKO on Kingambit with Close Combat. Rillaboom is another threat to watch out for, as it can set up Grassy Terrain, which can override the Psychic Terrain that Indeedee-F sets up.

Strategy Comments

  • Indeedee-F is a support Pokemon. It redirects attacks with Follow Me, provides speed control with Trick Room, provides important chip damage with Psychic or Dazzling Gleam, and helps partners spam Expanding Force.

  • Indeedee-F is best used early-game. As a lead, it is really good to get a head start at initializing your strategy. Sneasler, Ursaluna-B , and Ursaluna are all common Pokemon to lead alongside Indeedee-F. The Sneasler + Indeedee-F lead doesn't require Trick Room to be utilized and does not require any other setup. The Ursaluna-B + Indeedee-F lead does not have to be in Trick Room, depending on the Speed investment of Ursaluna-B, and it unleashes some of the largest amount of special damage in the metagame. Ursaluna and Indeedee-F have to be in Trick Room and need Ursaluna's Guts boost to be utilized thoroughly. However, this lead provides some of the largest amount of physical damage in the metagame.

  • The biggest weakness Indeedee-F has to deal with is the move Taunt. Taunt prevents Indeedee-F from setting up Trick Room and doing its job as a supportive Pokemon. The most reliable way to get rid of Taunt is to switch Indeedee-F out. Sometimes, Indeedee-F has to rely on its ally to set up Trick Room instead. Because it is a Trick Room Pokemon, it is vulnerable to being double targeted, which prevents Trick Room from being set up. Fortunately, it has Follow Me, which can redirect non-spread moves to it, allowing its ally to set up Trick Room.

Bulky Support.description:
• Indeedee-F is a support Pokemon that mainly redirects attacks with Follow Me and sets up Trick Room. The Psychic Terrain that it sets up supports its teammates by protecting them from opposing priority moves like Sucker Punch and Fake Out.

  • Follow Me provides redirection so that an allied Pokemon can safely set up Tailwind or Trick Room or set up with moves such as Annihilape's Bulk Up, Kingambit's Swords Dance, and Kommo-o's Clangorous Soul. Imprison prevents Trick Room from being set up by foes and shuts down the opponent's Follow Me Pokemon. Dazzling Gleam is mainly used to break opposing Pokemon that hold Focus Sash.

  • Safety Goggles provides immunity to Amoonguss's Spore and Rage Powder while allowing Indeedee-F to use Follow Me to redirect Spore. Psychic Seed ensures that it takes attacks like Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon better. Rocky Helmet punishes any Pokemon that attack it with contact-making moves or have said attacks redirected to it. Some of these contact moves are Annihilape's Drain Punch and Rage Fist, Rillaboom's Wood Hammer, and Sneasler's Dire Claw and Close Combat. Rocky Helmet also has the ability to break Focus Sashes and threaten any Pokemon that use multi-hit moves, such as Maushold and its Population Bomb. Sitrus Berry helps out Indeedee-F's longevity by allowing it to survive moves like +4 Archaludon's Body Press and Pelipper's Weather Ball.

  • Fairy is the best Tera type for Indeedee-F. It provides resistances to Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch, Archaludon's Body Press, and Sneasler's Close Combat and Throat Chop and an immunity to Dragon-type moves from Archaludon, Dragonite, Garchomp, and Dragapult. As a little bonus, it offers a STAB boost to Dazzling Gleam. Tera Grass gives Indeedee-F a resistance to Grass-type moves such as Rillaboom's Wood Hammer and Water-type moves such as Basculegion-M's Wave Crash and Pelipper's rain-boosted Weather Ball, which are its partners' most common weaknesses. Tera Grass also provides immunity to Amoonguss's Spore and redirection. However, if Indeedee-F uses Safety Goggles, Tera Grass is not recommended.

Trick Room Support.description:
Set Details

  • Indeedee-F is a great support option for many teams, utilizing its Normal typing to take no damage from Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage and Lunala's Moongeist Beam while also setting Psychic Terrain to not only shut off Miraidon's Electric Terrain but also to guard its teammates from priority moves such as Fake Out, as well as Sucker Punch and Thunderclap from Chien-Pao and Raging Bolt, respectively.
  • Psychic provides Indeedee-F with a way to deal consistent damage, while Alluring Voice scares off Dark-types like Chien-Pao and Tera Dark Calyrex-S.
  • Safety Goggles is useful for Indeedee-F to safely redirect Spore from Amoonguss and Smeargle, while Rocky Helmet punishes certain physical attackers, most notably Urshifu-R. Psychic Seed, although less common, is a good choice to help take on special attackers like the aforementioned Calyrex-S and Raging Bolt.
  • If running a Trick Room team, a Relaxed Nature and 0 Speed IVs let Indeedee-F override Grassy Terrain against uninvested Rillaboom if both are sent on the field at the same time; it also lets Indeedee-F be as slow as possible for operating under Trick Room.
  • Tera Water grants Indeedee-F a great defensive typing, helping it stomach moves such as Glacial Lance and Surging Strikes from Calyrex-I and Urshifu-R, respectively. Tera Fairy, on the other hand, most notably lets Indeedee-F resist Dark-types like Chi-Yu, Incineroar, and Chien-Pao. Although niche, Tera Fairy also boosts the power of Alluring Voice, letting it almost always OHKO Koraidon and securing the OHKO on Urshifu-S.

Teambuilding

  • Indeedee-F is very vulnerable to Taunt from the likes of Incineroar and Flutter Mane, as it severely hinders Indeedee-F's supportive capabilities and stops it from redirecting attacks or setting up Trick Room.
  • Without Terastallization available, Dark-type attacks like Wicked Blow from Urshifu and Dark Pulse from Chi-Yu threaten Indeedee-F with a potential OHKO. Chien-Pao in particular is a big threat to Indeedee-F, as it not only threatens Indeedee-F with Crunch, but it can also remove Psychic Terrain with Ice Spinner.
  • Miraidon and Rillaboom are able to override Indeedee-F's Psychic Terrain with their own respective Terrains, forcing Indeedee-F to switch out if it wants to set up Psychic Terrain again.
  • Packing multiple Trick Room setters like Calyrex-I and Lunala can ensure that Taunt won't shut down Trick Room altogether. Said Trick Room setters benefit from Indeedee-F's access to Follow Me and Trick Room, potentially setting up Trick Room for the aforementioned Restricted Pokemon and protecting them while they sweep via redirection.
  • Partners such as the Urshifu formes and Zamazenta-C are able to threaten Dark-types with a KO with Close Combat and Body Press, respectively. Zamazenta-C is notably able to almost completely wall out Chien-Pao, unless it has Sacred Sword. Running Alluring Voice or using Whimsicott can also help with Dark-types to an extent. Indeedee-F can help these partners more easily achieve these KOs with Helping Hand, or it can protect its allies from faster threats with Follow Me.
  • Calyrex-I is able to easily take out Miraidon and Rillaboom, which can be achieved even easier thanks to Indeedee-F's access to Trick Room and Helping Hand.
  • Calyrex-S and Lunala highly appreciate Indeedee-F's assistance, enabling powerful Expanding Forces with Psychic Terrain whilst helping Calyrex-S set up with Nasty Plot and Lunala set up Trick Room, thanks to Follow Me. Lunala in particular appreciates Indeedee-F's ability to set Trick Room. In return, Calyrex-S and Lunala can KO powerful threats such as Koraidon, which can threaten Indeedee-F with an OHKO.

Bulky Support.description:
Indeedee-F's typing, ability, and movepool make it an excellent support Pokemon. Its Normal / Psychic typing allows it to deal with Calyrex-S well, and Psychic Surge has immense utility in Regulation G, as it blocks priority moves like Fake Out from Incineroar and Rillaboom and Prankster Taunt from Tornadus while also denying the Terrains that power up Miraidon and Rillaboom. The combination of Follow Me and Trick Room allows Indeedee-F to threaten either setting up Trick Room itself or redirecting away attacking moves and Taunt to enable a partner to set up Trick Room. Once the dimensions have been twisted, it can use Helping Hand to make a partner Trick Room sweeper even more threatening. Its last move is usually an attacking move to make it less prone to Taunt; Dazzling Gleam pairs well with Tera Fairy and lets it damage both foes, while Psychic gives it a strong Psychic Terrain-boosted STAB move regardless of Tera type. Alluring Voice is an acceptable alternative to Dazzling Gleam, letting Indeedee-F punish setup sweepers like IronPress Zamazenta-C and Nasty Plot Calyrex-S while also bypassing the prominent Wide Guard. The Fairy-type attacks allow Indeedee-F to break Focus Sashes on Dark-types like Chien-Pao, Chi-Yu, and Urshifu so its partner can remove them quickly. However, Psychic allows Indeedee-F to OHKO Urshifu-R. Psychic Seed complements Psychic Surge well, as it reinforces Indeedee-F's special bulk. Safety Goggles allows it to bypass Amoonguss's Rage Powder and redirect away Spore for the benefit of its teammates, while Rocky Helmet lets it damage physical attackers whose contact moves it can redirect; Rocky Helmet can even break a Focus Sash from an Urshifu or Chien-Pao and severely punish Urshifu-R for using Surging Strikes. Tera Fairy allows Indeedee-F to resist the Dark-type attacks that would otherwise threaten it such as Incineroar's Knock Off and Urshifu's Wicked Blow while powering up Fairy-type moves that it may carry. Alternatively, Tera Grass lets it bypass Amoonguss's disruption and become immune to its Spore without having to use Safety Goggles while also granting a resistance to Water- and Electric-type attacks from the likes of Urshifu-R and Miraidon.

With Indeedee-F's utility, it can fit on a variety of teams that appreciate Psychic Terrain, redirection, or its ability to set Trick Room. Calyrex-S appreciates Psychic Terrain blocking priority moves, namely Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch, and powering up its Psychic-type attacks; it is even able to run the devastating Expanding Force with Indeedee-F. Calyrex-S also takes advantage of Indeedee-F's redirection to fire off more of its brutal attacks without fear of retaliation and also benefits from Helping Hand pushing its damage potential up to eleven. Calyrex-I pairs well with Indeedee-F, as it is both a Trick Room setter and a sweeper, meaning that the opponent is hard-pressed to stop either Pokemon from setting up Trick Room with Indeedee-F's support, and once it is set up, Indeedee-F immediately enables Calyrex-I to deal big damage with Helping Hand. Other Trick Room sweepers like Ursaluna, Ursaluna-B, and Torkoal appreciate that Indeedee-F can support them with Helping Hand and Follow Me on top of its ability to set up Trick Room. Indeedee-F is very vulnerable to Dark-types like Urshifu, Chi-Yu, and Incineroar, as the threat of their powerful moves makes it more hesitant to use Follow Me. It also hates Taunt, which completely shuts down all of its utility and thus its field presence. Rillaboom can also interfere with strategies predicated on Psychic Terrain blocking Fake Out.

Redirection Support.description:
• Indeedee-F carves itself out a spot in the metagame as one of the only currently legal Pokemon with possession of Psychic Surge. With this, it is able to amplify the power of Pokemon using Expanding Force to extreme heights. Indeedee-F is also a generally great support option with access to redirection and speed control in Follow Me and Trick Room, respectively.

  • To assist in its supportive capabilities, Indeedee-F can use Sitrus Berry to heal up, which lets it avoid 2HKOs from Sandsear Storm from Landorus, Ivy Cudgel from any Ogerpon forme, and Tera Normal Life Orb Ursaluna-B. Alternatively, Indeedee-F can use Safety Goggles to redirect Spore from Amoonguss, or it can use Psychic Seed to boost its survivability by allowing it to withstand powerful attacks such as Tera Normal Life Orb Blood Moon from Ursaluna-B.

  • Trick Room gives Indeedee-F access to a crucial form of speed control, allowing allies like Hoopa-U and Ursaluna to move before their foes. Helping Hand helps boost the power of the aforementioned allies; Protect can be run over either option to help with positioning and defensive play.

  • Psychic OHKOes Assault Vest Okidogi and 2HKOes non-Assault Vest Iron Hands thanks to the Psychic Terrain boost. Dazzling Gleam, on the other hand, can be used to deal chip damage across the field, breaking Focus Sash on Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu.

  • The given EV spread, with Psychic Seed, lets Indeedee-F avoid a 2HKO from Earth Power from Landorus, with the rest going into Defense.

  • Indeedee-F uses Tera Fairy to avoid getting KOed by powerful Dark-type attacks like Kowtow Cleave from Kingambit and Knock Off from Roaring Moon. Tera Fairy additionally gives Indeedee-F a useful resistance to Fighting-type attacks like Drain Punch from Iron Hands and Bug-type attacks like U-turn from Rillaboom all the while providing an immunity to Dragon-type attacks like Dragon Energy from Regidrago. Additionally, Tera Fairy allows Indeedee-F to completely wall most Calm Mind Raging Bolt sets, using Follow Me to redirect Dragon Pulse and shutting down Thunderclap with both Follow Me and Psychic Terrain.

  • Indeedee-F is typically used on fast-paced teams consisting of Expanding Force users such as Hoopa-U and Hatterene, both of which appreciate its ability to set Trick Room and use Follow Me to let them set Trick Room and punch holes in the opposing team. Alternatively, Indeedee-F can be paired with Iron Crown, using Follow Me to protect it as Iron Crown launches Expanding Force or sets up with Calm Mind.

  • Because of Indeedee-F's crippling Dark weakness, allies like Diancie and Iron Hands are greatly appreciated, as they can remove opposing Dark-types with Body Press and Drain Punch, respectively. These allies can also switch in on Dark-type attacks, allowing Indeedee-F to reset Terrain if it runs out, is removed by Ice Spinner from Chien-Pao, or is overridden by Rillaboom's Grassy Surge.

  • Torkoal and Iron Crown are great partners for Indeedee-F, as they can threaten Rillaboom, which overrides Indeedee-F's Terrain with its own, and Chien-Pao, which threatens to remove Psychic Terrain with Ice Spinner, respectively. Chien-Pao also threatens huge damage into Indeedee-F with Throat Chop.

  • Ogerpon-H is also a great partner, effectively removing Steel-types like Gholdengo and Kingambit to allow allies like Iron Crown and Regidrago to sweep more easily.

nu.overview: Copperajah stands out from the other Steel-types for being a defensive tank that packs both firepower and utility. It checks special wallbreakers like Sylveon, Munkidori, and Dudunsparce. Additionally, Copperajah's deep movepool gives it a lot of utility options. For example, Knock Off allows it to hit item-reliant Pokemon that commonly switch into it like Incineroar, letting Copperajah's entry hazards chip away at them, and Whirlwind lets it phaze setup sweepers like Nasty Plot Uxie. However, Copperajah's biggest problem is the lack of reliable recovery, making it a lot harder to consistently switch into special wallbreakers that have STAB attacks that it doesn't resist like Inteleon and Basculegion-M. Copperajah also struggles to break through physical walls like Amoonguss, Vaporeon, and Gligar, as they can tank its attacks and threaten it back with status.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Tera Water lets Copperajah better handle Ground- and Water-types like Flygon and Inteleon, but Tera Dragon is preferred for not giving it a weakness to Grass- and Electric-type attacks from Breloom and Kilowattrel. Tera Ghost gives Copperajah a useful immunity to Fighting-type attacks from foes like Paldean Tauros-W and Toxicroak while spinblocking Tsareena and Brambleghast. However, these Pokemon usually can then proceed to hit it with super effective attacks like Knock Off and Poltergeist.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Flamigo, Toxicroak, Heracross, and Infernape destroy Copperajah with their STAB Close Combat, but none of them want to switch directly in. Paldean Tauros-W resists Copperajah's STAB attacks, allowing it to either destroy Copperajah with its STAB Close Combat or force Copperajah to switch, giving it a free opportunity to use Bulk Up.

Physical Walls: Amoonguss and Vaporeon can tank Copperajah's attacks very well and threaten it back with status. Orthworm is notable for also taking Copperajah's attacks very well and either using it to set up entry hazards or hitting it back with Body Press.

Ground-types: Flygon, Swampert, and Gligar can KO Copperajah with their STAB Earthquake, but they don't enjoy switching into its Knock Off, and Flygon takes a lot of damage from its Iron Head.

Fire-types: Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion can put a lot of pressure on Copperajah with their STAB attacks, but they have to be cautious about switching into its Knock Off. Incineroar can force Copperajah to switch out, allowing it to freely set up with Swords Dance, or destroy Copperajah with its STAB Flare Blitz.

Stealth Rock.description:
Set Details

Knock Off allows Copperajah to target item-reliant foes like Chandelure, Kilowattrel, and Incineroar. For its last move, Copperajah commonly runs Whirlwind, allowing it to phaze bulky setup sweepers like Calm Mind Dudunsparce and Sylveon. Alternatively, Protect allows Copperajah to scout out Choice item attackers like Flygon, Flamigo, and Munkidori and gives it more Leftovers recovery. Earthquake hits Fire- and Poison-types like Chandelure and Galarian Slowbro and Steel-types like Duraludon, Klefki, and opposing Copperajah. The Speed investment allows Copperajah to outpace Bronzong. Tera Dragon gives Copperajah a useful resistance to Fire-type attacks from foes like Chandelure and Scovillain, while Tera Fairy gives it a better matchup against Flygon and Fighting-types like Flamigo and Scrafty.

Wish passers like Vaporeon and Sylveon provide massive recovery for Copperajah, letting it repeatedly switch into foes like Munkidori and Dudunsparce. Copperajah best synergizes with physical walls like Galarian Slowbro, Bellibolt, and Vaporeon, as they can handle physical wallbreakers like Toxicroak, Paldean Tauros-W, and Basculegion-M. In return, Copperajah checks special wallbreakers like Munkidori, Kilowattrel, and Sylveon.
