Copperajah is forced out by Fire-types like Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion, as they can destroy it with their Fire-type attacks. Thus, it pairs well with Water- and Dragon-types like Vaporeon and Goodra to check them. Copperajah also appreciates partners like Sylveon, Gligar, and Swampert, as they can handle checks like Heracross, Flygon, and Incineroar. Wallbreakers such as Flygon, Overqwil, and Paldean Tauros-W appreciate Copperajah's strength, since unlike other Steel-types such as Bronzong and Klefki, it can wear down physical walls like Gligar, Galarian Slowbro, and Swampert.

Assault Vest.description:
Assault Vest turns Copperajah into a solid wallbreaker and allows it to better handle special attackers such as Meloetta and Goodra. Knock Off lets Copperajah remove Heavy-Duty Boots from Scyther and Tornadus while catching Chandelure and Uxie on the switch in. Earthquake is a vital coverage move to hit Electric- and Poison-types such as Bellibolt and Galarian Slowbro while allowing it to pick off Incineroar, Duraludon, and opposing Copperajah. Supercell Slam provides a way to damage Flying- and Water-types like Tornadus and Vaporeon, whereas Play Rough is an option to better hit Fighting- and Dragon-types such as Flamigo, Flygon, and Goodra. Copperajah can run two different EV spreads; the first one ensures that it outpaces defensive Sylveon and non-Speed invested Incineroar. Alternatively, the second spread provides Copperajah more bulk to tank hits from Inteleon and Munkidori while still outspeeding Bellibolt. Tera Dragon lets Copperajah resist Fire-type attacks from Chandelure, Incineroar, and Salazzle, but this comes at the price of failing against bad matchups such as Sylveon, Duraludon, and Goodra. Tera Fairy provides an immunity to Dragon-type attacks from Goodra while improving the matchup against Fighting-types like Paldean Tauros-W and Flamigo. However, Copperajah loses the ability to check Munkidori and Galarian Slowbro.

Due to Copperajah's lack of recovery, it appreciates Wish support from the likes of Vaporeon and Scream Tail, allowing it to repeatedly switch in on Dudunsparce's Boomburst, Duraludon and Goodra's Draco Meteor, and Munkidori's attacks. Scream Tail can also provide Thunder Wave support to paralyze the likes of Brambleghast and Meloetta, as well as Encore to cripple Bulk Up Scrafty and Calm Mind Raikou. In return, Copperajah is able to switch in on the Poison-type attacks from Munkidori while checking both it and Uxie with Knock Off. Physically defensive teammates such as Houndstone and Galarian Slowbro can complement Copperajah's Assault Vest-boosted Special Defense by helping against the stronger physical attackers like Choice-locked Flygon and Tidy Up Cinccino. Houndstone, in particular, can neuter the former two with Will-O-Wisp. In return, Copperajah is able to threaten attackers like Munkidori and Raikou that otherwise threaten Houndstone. Since Copperajah finds itself forced out by Fire-type attackers such as Chandelure and Incineroar, it appreciates Water- and Dragon-type teammates such as Vaporeon, Swampert, and Goodra to independently check them. It is also complemented by Ghost- and Psychic-types like Basculegion-M, Brambleghast, and Uxie, which are able to check Choice item Infernape and Paldean Tauros-W that are locked into Close Combat. Ground-types like Flygon and Rhyperior force Copperajah to switch or use its Tera; thus, it partners well with Grass- and Water-types like Brambleghast, Tsareena, and Vaporeon to handle the aforementioned threats. It also appreciates entry hazard support from Flygon and Gligar, utilizing its Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from hazard-weak foes like Incineroar while wearing them down with Stealth Rock and Spikes, respectively.

Slush Rush (Ice).description:
A Naughty nature lets Arctozolt OHKO Physically Defensive Toxapex with Bolt Beak after Stealth Rock damage and should be in tandem with Freeze-Dry to fully threaten Water teams as it deals with Swampert. On the other hand, a Naive nature lets Arctozolt outspeed Zeraora and Choice Scarf Excadrill under Snow, making Stomping Tantrum a better choice if using the aforementioned nature.

This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

nu.overview: Duraludon carves out a great niche in NU thanks to its utility and offense. Eviolite allows it to better tank attacks from physical attackers like Basculegion-M and Tsareena, while its typing makes it a good check to special attackers like Inteleon and Munkidori. Duraludon's great utility makes it difficult to take advantage of, as Body Press hits foes like Incineroar and Copperajah while Roar stops Nasty Plot from Uxie and Wish from Vaporeon. However, Duraludon can get overwhelmed by powerful attackers such as Sylveon, Chandelure, and Flygon due to its poor special bulk and lack of any reliable recovery. Duraludon faces competition from Steel-types like Bronzong, Copperajah, and Klefki, since they can handle those special attackers and offer more utility at times with Levitate, Knock Off, and Prankster Thunder Wave, respectively. Duraludon can get walled depending on its moveset: Substitue Uxie can use it as setup fodder if it doesn't have Roar, and without Thunder Wave, Duraludon fails to do anything against faster Pokemon like Inteleon and Munkidori.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Iron Defense pairs well with Body Press while letting Duraludon better handle physical wallbreakers like Flygon, Incineroar, and Rhyperior. However, Duraludon often prefers to run Thunder Wave or Roar for the utility they offer. Eject Pack can be used on both offense and hyper offense teams, allowing Duraludon to set up Stealth Rock and pivot into a wallbreaker like Swords Dance Incineroar or Choice Specs Chandelure.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Specially defensive and Eviolite sets can be overwhelmed by powerful wallbreakers like Choice Specs Sylveon, Chandelure, and Tornadus due to Duraludon repeatedly switching in to check them. However, they must be cautious of switching into its STAB attacks. Setup sweepers like Munkidori, Dudunsparce, and Meloetta can use Duraludon switching out as free setup while being able to destroy it with their coverage, although none of them enjoy switching into Thunder Wave.

Specially Defensive Tanks: Specially defensive Pokemon like Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro, Incineroar, Wo-Chien, and Chansey can tank Duraludon's attacks, while both Incineroar and Wo-Chien can threaten to remove its Eviolite. Bulky Water-types like Vaporeon can shrug off Duraludon's attacks while recovering off the damage. Scrafty can tank Duraludon's attacks and use it as setup fodder but doesn't enjoy switching into a Body Press. However, all of these Pokemon can be worn down by the combination of Roar and entry hazard chip damage.

Ground-types: Flygon, Rhyperior, Gligar, and Swampert threaten Duraludon with their Earthquake, while the former can use it as free setup after a Draco Meteor Special Attack drop. However, Flygon and Rhyperior don't enjoy switching into Duraludon's STAB attacks, while both Gligar and Swampert are cautious about repeatedly switching into its attacks.

Steel-types: Copperajah and Bronzong can tank Duraludon's STAB attacks, allowing them to set up their own entry hazards, with the former threatening to remove Duraludon's Eviolite as well. However, neither of them enjoys switching into Body Press. Klefki is immune to Duraludon's Dragon-type attacks and takes neutral damage from Body Press, letting it set up Spikes or hit Duraludon back with Dazzling Gleam.

Offensive Support.description:
Set Details

Draco Meteor dents bulky walls like Bellibolt, Houndstone, and opposing Duraludon. Flash Cannon offers a decently powered STAB attack to chip foes like Gligar and Tsareena while hitting Sylveon and Scream Tail super effectively. Thunder Wave threatens fast foes like Munkidori, Flamigo, and Paldean Tauros-W, aiding slower teammates such as Chandelure. Stealth Rock can be run to make Duraludon into an entry hazard setter. Alternatively, Roar works to phaze out setup sweepers like Uxie and even Fairy-types such as Scream Tail while preventing Vaporeon from receiving its Wish. Alternatively, Body Press allows Duraludon to hit Steel-types like Copperajah that can tank its STAB attacks while handling Dark-types such as Incineroar and Scrafty. The EV ensures Duraludon can OHKO Cinccino with Draco Meteor. Duraludon can opt to run 56 Speed EVs to outpace foes like bulky Sylveon and Rhyperior. Light Metal is preferred over Heavy Metal to minimize Low Kick damage from Ambipom and Decidueye. Tera Fairy gives Duraludon a better matchup against Pokemon like Flygon and Flamigo, while Tera Ghost gives it an immunity to Fighting-types and lets it simultaneously block and threaten Rapid Spin users like Tsareena and Brambleghast. Tera Flying allows it to maintain the Fighting resistance while making it immune to Ground-type attacks from Pokemon like Swampert, Gligar, and Flygon.

Duraludon synergizes greatly with Pokemon like Incineroar, Swampert, and Sylveon, as they can better handle wallbreakers like Chandelure, Munkidori, and Goodra. Physical tanks like Galarian Slowbro, Houndstone, and Amoonguss help Duraludon deal with wallbreakers like Flygon, Toxicroak, and Heracross. Gligar is especially notable, acting as a Ground- and Fighting-type check against Rhyperior and Flamigo while also providing Knock Off and Toxic support as well as extra entry hazard stacking in Spikes. On hazard-stacking teams, Duraludon benefits from spinblockers like Brambleghast, Chandelure, and Houndstone to maintain its hazards. Wallbreakers like Toxicroak, Basculegion-M, and Munkidori support Duraludon by breaking down bulky walls like Vaporeon, Chansey, and Wo-Chien. Offensive setup sweepers like Incineroar, Munkidori, and Uxie appreciate Duraludon's Thunder Wave allowing them to outspeed fast threats like Paldean Tauros-W, Ambipom, and Choice Scarf Flamigo. In particular, Uxie is a great partner for Duraludon, since it can freely set up Nasty Plot against walls like Bronzong and Vaporeon while checking Fighting- and Ground-types like Flamigo and Gligar. In exchange, Duraludon can deal with Electric-types like Bellibolt and Kilowattrel. Wish passers such as Vaporeon, Sylveon, and Scream Tail benefit from Duraludon checking Pokemon like Cinccino and Overqwil. In return, their Wish support allows it to repeatedly switch into foes like Munkidori, Basculegion-M, and Gligar.

nfe.overview: Drakloak is NFE's premier Ghost-type and an elite choice for speed control. Boasting the highest unboosted Speed in the metagame alongside a variety of utility options, Drakloak is an excellent phazer capable of disrupting attackers and walls alike with Dragon Tail, Night Shade, and status while also doubling as a spinblocker. Additionally, Drakloak is a great wallbreaker, leveraging its high-powered coverage and Speed to disrupt foes expecting utility sets, like Gabite and Naclstack. Drakloak is also an excellent screens setter for hyper offense teams thanks to its excellent Speed and wide utility. However, its frailty and typing make it very vulnerable to Knock Off, making matchups like Monferno and Thwackey difficult. Night Shade sets are walled by Normal-types like Dunsparce and Girafarig, while Choice Specs sets can suffer from being too weak even against foes like Tinkatuff and utility Dunsparce.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

Hydro Pump can be used on the Choice Specs set to surprise Piloswine and Naclstack while maintaining good coverage against Fire-types, though it loses out on either Fire Blast's wider overall coverage or U-turn's pivoting. For Utility Drakloak sets, Rocky Helmet is an item option that punishes Quaxwell's Triple Axel and U-turn from Pokemon like Fletchinder and Raboot, and Clear Body can be used to ignore Sticky Web and to block Parting Shot from Morgrem.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Drakloak heavily struggles against Fairy-types like Tinkatuff and Clefairy with both sets, with only Fire Blast being threatening against physically bulky Tinkatuff variants. Clefairy particularly does well, recovering any damage with ease and disrupting Drakloak with its own utility moves or Moonblast. However, the RestTalk set can outlast the Fairy-types, though it doesn't enjoy losing Eviolite to Knock Off and being locked into unfavorable moves with Encore.

Normal-types: Dunsparce is one of the most consistent answers to Drakloak, being immune to Night Shade and forcing it to use Draco Meteor or Dragon Tail phazing to threaten notable damage. Dunsparce can recover the damage away with Slack Off and use Drakloak as setup fodder. Girafarig is similarly effective against Night Shade sets but struggles a lot more against Choice Specs sets.

Piloswine: Piloswine can tank any hit from Drakloak with ease and revenge kill it; Ice Shard against Choice Specs sets requires minimal chip damage for it to KO.

Dark-types: Defensive Dark-types like Scraggy and Alolan Grimer perform excellently against Drakloak, taking its STAB moves well and threatening it back with their own. While unable to switch in, Krokorok and Dragon Dance Scraggy can stomach at least one of its attack and again threaten Drakloak back with their attacks.

Naclstack: While relatively rare, Naclstack is immune to status conditions and can whittle Drakloak down with Salt Cure, only fearing the rare Hydro Pump.

Faster Pokemon and Priority Moves: While Drakloak is the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the metagame, it struggles to deal with Choice Scarf users like Frogadier and Girafarig that can outspeed it with a boost. Sucker Punch users like Raboot and Pignite remain similarly dangerous in spite of their lower Speed tiers, alongside Piloswine's Ice Shard.

Utility Pivot.description:
Drakloak is the fastest Pokemon in the tier and helps revenge kill offensive threats such as Frogadier and Girafarig while blocking Quaxwell from removing entry hazards with Rapid Spin. Draco Meteor is Drakloak's strongest move for immediate power, while Hex does consistent damage after status has been spread on the opposing team. Thunder Wave allows Drakloak to spread paralysis to its common checks such as Tinkatuff and Dunsparce, potentially creating some key opportunities in long games. Will-O-Wisp helps deal with Piloswine and Krokorok, which cannot be paralyzed, as well as other physical attackers like Thwackey, providing a more consistent effect with burn compared to paralysis. Drakloak also serves as a fantastic offensive pivot with U-turn, as it comes in on defensive Pokemon such as Koffing and Quaxwell and pivots on its common answers to bring in wallbreakers such as Pignite and Thwackey. Eviolite is an option to give Drakloak more bulk; however, it dislikes hazards being up, especially Toxic Spikes, which hinder it permanently. In addition to Eviolite, Drakloak can use Cursed Body, but Infiltrator is usually the preferred option, giving Drakloak a good matchup against dual screens hyper offense teams and letting it hit Pokemon behind Substitute such as Servine and Girafarig.

Drakloak perfectly fits in teams that lack speed control, especially if paired with wallbreakers like Pignite, Fraxure, and Piloswine, which make great partners, as they appreciate its ability to pivot on defensive Pokemon to give them opportunities to wallbreak while threatening Drakloak's common answers such as Scraggy and Hisuian Sliggoo. Pokemon that use pivoting moves such as Raboot, Monferno, and Thwackey also make great teammates for Drakloak, helping to keep momentum and applying offensive pressure with ease. Stealth Rock users such as Tinkatuff, Piloswine, and Krokorok and Spikes users like Quilladin and Glimmet appreciate Drakloak's ability to block Quaxwell from spinning and keep entry hazards on the field, allowing them to make consistent progress. Drakloak is weak to Piloswine, so Pokemon that consistently check Piloswine are much appreciated, such as Quaxwell, Seadra, and Dunsparce. Knock Off absorbers such as Koffing and Tinkatuff cover Drakloak's weakness to Knock Off. Drakloak appreciates Pokemon that are able to break special walls like Pignite, Krokorok, and Piloswine.

RestTalk.description:
The combination of Night Shade and Dragon Tail alongside Drakloak's high Speed and valued typing makes it a premier phazer. RestTalk gives it longevity, making it a good status absorber for burns, paralysis, and poison from status users like Koffing and Hattrem, all while allowing Drakloak to continue phazing, spinblocking, and chipping foes. 216 Speed EVs enable Drakloak to outspeed non-Choice Scarf Frogadier and make it the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the metagame, while the 40 EVs in Defense enable it to always survive Knock Off from Life Orb Thwackey and Icicle Crash from non-Choice Band Piloswine. While Drakloak's abilities are all useful, Clear Body stands out by not having Drakloak's Speed be lowered by Sticky Web, as well as stopping Memento from lead Glimmet sets.

Drakloak tends to fit on many balanced and bulky teams, being integral to stopping Rapid Spin attempts from Quaxwell. Entry hazard setters like Piloswine, Frogadier, and Quilladin all pair well with it, forming a hazard-stacking core while providing utility in their own right. Fairy-types like Tinkatuff and Clefairy can be tricky to deal with, able to lock Drakloak into unfavorable moves with Encore and chip away at it with their utility moves. Checks to them like Gabite and Ivysaur can significantly threaten them back while taking paralysis relatively well. Normal-types like Dunsparce and Girafarig are immune to Night Shade and can threaten super effective coverage or powerful Psychic-type STAB moves; Steel-types like the aforementioned Tinkatuff and Hisuian Sliggoo are excellent answers to them. While Drakloak has a good defensive profile, its frailty makes it unreliable at answering certain Pokemon like Monferno and Thwackey; Koffing makes for an excellent Knock Off absorber while completing hazard cores with Toxic Spikes and potentially stealing other Eviolites with Thief. Wallbreakers and revenge killers like Fraxure and Raboot can take advantage of Drakloak's spinblocking capabilities to more easily break down defensive titans like Quaxwell and Koffing from the accumulated residual damage. Given Drakloak's vulnerability to Piloswine, checks to it like Quaxwell and Dunsparce are also appreciated; Quaxwell can pivot and remove hazards with Rapid Spin.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Drakloak is an effective wallbreaker and, with a Timid nature, speed control option, using its powerful STAB moves in conjunction with great coverage options to break through even the sturdiest of checks. Hydro Pump can be used to break past Fire- and Ground-types like Pignite and Piloswine, while Surf can be used as a less powerful but more reliable option. Thunderbolt is an effective coverage option that can zap Water-types like Quaxwell and Wartortle efficiently. Alternatively, if teams have status-spreading support from teammates like Glare Servine, Toxic Spikes Koffing, Glare or Body Slam Dunsparce, Drakloak can opt to use Hex, which is more powerful than Shadow Ball against foes with status. Infiltrator can prevent Substitute users like Wartortle and offensive Gabite from being safe against Drakloak, allowing it to function more effectively as a revenge killer. A Modest nature can help Drakloak break more efficiently at the cost of being slower than Frogadier and Raboot; it does secure a 2HKO on Quaxwell with Draco Meteor after taking entry hazard chip damage, which can be valuable on sets without Thunderbolt.

Choice Specs Drakloak functions best on balance and bulky offense teams that have Knock Off and entry hazard support, using its powerful STAB attacks to clean late-game once its checks like Dunsparce and Tinkatuff are worn down. Clefairy and especially Tinkatuff are excellent teammates for Drakloak, providing Knock Off and Stealth Rock support to go along with their immunity to Dragon-type attacks from opposing Drakloak and other threats like Choice Scarf Gabite and Frogadier. Monferno similarly provides Knock Off and Stealth Rock support while being able to threaten Tinkatuff. Quaxwell can provide hazard removal, check Piloswine, and give Drakloak safe entry points with its Flip Turn. Piloswine is a great teammate because it provides Stealth Rock support, while Drakloak can spinblock and check Quaxwell for Piloswine in return. Drakloak has to be wary of Dunsparce and Piloswine, as both can tank its attacks and use the opportunity to dish out high damage in return. Wartortle is another problem for Drakloak, as it can use the Special Attack drop from Draco Meteor as an opportunity to set up with Shell Smash. Teammates that can help with these threats include Dunsparce, which can help sponge attacks from Piloswine, and Thwackey, which can provide safe entry points with U-turn and has the powerful Grassy Glide to take down Piloswine and Wartortle if they take some chip damage first. Pignite is a great teammate, as it can use its STAB attacks to help break through bulky Normal- and Steel-types, such as Dunsparce and Tinkatuff, while providing Knock Off support. Raboot can also help in these endeavors; it lacks Knock Off but can still use U-turn to give Drakloak entry points against Pokemon like Quaxwell. Koffing can help check Clefairy while boosting the damage of Hex by spreading Toxic Spikes, and other status spreaders like Glare Servine and Thunder Wave can Tinkatuff also provide this support.

Dual Screens.description:
On hyper offense builds, Drakloak is arguably the best dual screens setter thanks to being the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the tier and its diverse utility options. Both Reflect and Light Screen soften the damage taken by teammates that aim to set up or attack like Fraxure, Wartortle, and Scraggy. Utility Pokemon looking to disrupt it with Defog or Knock Off are in for a nasty surprise in Curse, discouraging them from staying in while preventing Drakloak from becoming setup fodder for opposing setup sweepers like Girafarig and Monferno. Thunder Wave is the preferred last slot to further disrupt walls as well as other faster attackers, while U-turn can be elected to allow Drakloak to continue setting up screens later in the game. While all of Drakloak's abilities are niche, Clear Body is preferred to have an easier time setting up screens early- to mid-game, though if opposing Sticky Web teams are not a concern, Cursed Body can prevent opposing threats from freely spamming their attacks, which can force switches.

Drakloak is best suited for offensive and hyper offense builds, aiding setup sweepers like Fraxure, Girafarig, and Monferno in setting up. Offensive entry hazard setters like Piloswine and Glimmet can keep offensive pressure up with their powerful STAB moves. Additionally, Glimmet threatens out Fletchinder by retaliating with its own entry hazards while also absorbing Toxic Spikes on its own side of the field, a significant weakness otherwise. In return, Drakloak prevents opposing Quaxwell from removing entry hazards by spinblocking. Running Thunder Wave allows slower teammates like Pignite and Fraxure to be less reliant on screens for setup. Screens removers like Fletchinder and Knock Off users like Tinkatuff can be problematic in how they either completely remove or reduce screens' duration, so teammates that can threaten them out like Wartortle and Krokorok are appreciated.

Boots Pivot.description:
Dragapult's supportive capabilities provide it a unique role in SV OU as the fastest user of both status moves and U-turn in the tier. Dragon Darts can deal massive damage to special walls like Blissey and Calm Mind users like Latios and Raging Bolt, and its multi-hit property makes it more threatening versus Dragonite. Draco Meteor is an alternative Dragon-type STAB move that allows Dragapult to 2HKO Great Tusk and heavily injure more physically defensive Pokemon like Zapdos, Moltres, and Hydrapple. Hex is used over Shadow Ball to complement Dragapult's ability to spread status, but it also allows Dragapult to punish Gliscor attempting to absorb status for its team, and unboosted Hex is still strong enough to 2HKO both Gholdengo and Pecharunt. Will-O-Wisp can be used to burn physical attackers like Zamazenta, Dragonite, Kingambit, and Ogerpon-W. Thunder Wave, on the other hand, can paralyze fast Pokemon like Darkrai, Iron Moth, and Tornadus-T for Dragapult's teammates to take advantage of. Lastly Dragapult has the fastest U-turn in the tier, which allows it to quickly pivot and keep momentum for its teammates while also hitting Dark-types like Tyranitar and Ting-Lu. Depending on the choice of moves taken, the EVs should be set to either 4 Attack and a Naive nature for Dragon Darts or 4 Special Defense and a Timid nature for Draco Meteor. Infiltrator is the preferred ability, as it allows Dragapult to both hit and cripple foes regardless of if they are behind a Substitute, like Kyurem, or screens, like Galarian Moltres. For Terastallization options, Tera Ghost allows Dragapult to boost Hex to scary levels of damage, as it cleanly 2HKOes specially defensive Gliscor, OHKOes Ceruledge after Stealth Rock damage, and 2HKOes a statused Iron Defense Zamazenta. Tera Fairy, on the other hand, lets it withstand Dark-type moves, most commonly Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave and Zamazenta's Crunch, and also gives it an immunity to Dragon-type moves from threats like Kyurem, Dragonite, and Walking Wake, potentially getting off a status move or strong Dragon-type attack in return. Tera Steel keeps the Dragon-type resistance but lets Dragapult take a Moonblast from Iron Valiant and Enamorus while also letting it shrug off Ice-type attacks from Weavile and the aforementioned Kyurem.

This set finds itself on balance and bulky balance teams as a support Pokemon, especially on Heavy-Duty Boots-spam structures, supporting its teammates and acting as speed control. Dragapult invites in Pokemon like Tyranitar and Hisuian Samurott, letting it use U-turn to bring in answers like Ogerpon-W to wreak havoc. Dragapult can also U-turn on Ting-Lu, allowing it to bring in Weavile or Kyurem and make progress. Dragapult is a frail Pokemon incapable of taking more than one hit from almost anything in the tier, so having defensive partners able to switch in hard on its threats is much appreciated. Corviknight checks Kingambit and has slow pivoting with U-turn, letting Dragapult get back on the field safely. Galarian Slowking can make Dragapult even harder to switch into with Future Sight, which can be good to bait Dark-types like Kingambit or Hisuian Samurott and threaten them with status. Galarian Slowking can bring Dragapult in with Chilly Reception while checking Fairy-types like Primarina and Iron Valiant. Garganacl has both Salt Cure and Stealth Rock to add on to the passive damage pressure, but it also helps Dragapult by taking on Ghost-type moves from Pecharunt and opposing Dragapult. Entry hazard setters help to stack up chip damage due to the many switches that Dragapult forces. Hisuian Samurott in particular has Knock Off to remove Leftovers from Ting-Lu and Heavy-Duty Boots from Great Tusk, allowing Will-O-Wisp's damage to not go unnoticed. Ting-Lu also has hazards, walls Deoxys-S, Gholdengo, and Darkrai, and can chip down switch-ins like Hisuian Samurott and Gliscor to help Dragapult sweep; Dragapult has natural synergy as the spinblocker of the team. Offensive Pokemon also like Will-O-Wisp support, as setup sweepers like Kingambit benefit from Great Tusk and Zamazenta being burned, Kyurem benefits from Zamazenta being crippled, and Gholdengo can turn the tables against Ting-Lu thanks to reduced Earthquake damage. Packing Thunder Wave can mean the world for slower wallbreakers like Ogerpon-W, Kyurem, and Hoopa-U. Ogerpon-W can wipe problem matchups like Darkrai and Tornadus-T, Kyurem can demolish Ting-Lu and can now outspeed a paralyzed Iron Valiant, and Hoopa-U's coverage becomes nightmarish once fast U-turn users like Cinderace and opposing Dragapult can no longer outspeed it Dragapult lacks instantaneous wallbreaking power against defensive Pokemon, relying on status and Hex for damage. Garganacl is therefore Dragapult's biggest counter, as it takes pitiful damage from any of its moves. Therefore, Pokemon such as Gliscor, Clefable, and Great Tusk that can switch in and threaten out Garganacl are great partners, with the former two being able to mitigate its Salt Cure damage and the latter being able to get up Stealth Rock in its face. Bulky Fairy-types like Clefable and Primarina can take hits and eliminate Dragapult with Moonblast, so pairing it with strong wallbreakers like Ogerpon-W and Gholdengo can help versus these foes. Zamazenta is an amazing partner, since it can hit Garganacl, Heatran, and Ting-Lu with Close Combat while also providing backup speed control for Dark-type threats like Weavile and Darkrai. Pairing Dragapult with other status spreaders, like Gliscor, Moltres, and Galarian Slowking, can boost Hex's damage output in the long run. Alomomola is another status spreader that can support Dragapult with Wish, allowing Dragapult to stay healthy in longer games where its defensive qualities may be required.

Choice Specs.description:
Equipped with Choice Specs, Dragapult combines its great Speed and lethal STAB combination with the high Base Power of Draco Meteor and the disruptive nature of Shadow Ball's Special Defense drops to become one of OU's premier wallbreakers. Flamethrower targets Kingambit, the only OU Pokemon that resists both of Dragapult's STAB moves, and OHKOes the likes of Scizor and offensive Iron Treads. Fire Blast may be used instead to ensure OHKOs against offensive Kingambit while further pressuring Corviknight and bulky variants of Iron Treads at the cost of accuracy. U-turn allows Dragapult to safely pivot on predicted switches, easing the need of prediction while chipping at the likes of Ting-Lu and Blissey in the process. A Timid nature allows Dragapult to get the jump on Zamazenta, Darkrai, and +1 Adamant Dragonite as well as Speed tie with opposing Dragapult; a Modest nature may be considered to enhance Dragapult's wallbreaking power, with Draco Meteor netting OHKOs against the likes of Tornadus-T and Ogerpon-W. Infiltrator proves effective against Substitute users such as Kyurem and Iron Moth, both of which Dragapult threatens to KO with Draco Meteor, as well as against Aurora Veil and dual screens teams, which often use Pokemon like Darkrai and Gholdengo that can't stand Dragapult's attacks. Clear Body may also be used as a countermeasure against Sticky Web teams while using Pecharunt's Parting Shot as an entry point to reverse momentum. Tera Ghost boosts Dragapult's Shadow Ball, netting 2HKOs against Clefable and Assault Vest Tornadus-T after Stealth Rock, while also removing its weaknesses to attacks such as Iron Valiant and Enamorus's Moonblast and Weavile's Ice Shard. Similarly, Tera Dragon boosts Dragapult's Draco Meteor, allowing it to 2HKO Garganacl and heavily chip at Ting-Lu, while removing its weaknesses to Kingambit's Sucker Punch, Darkrai's Dark Pulse, and Ceruledge's Shadow Sneak.

Choice Specs Dragapult often finds itself on bulky offense and offense teams where its wallbreaking prowess and speed control shine. Ogerpon-W appreciates Dragapult's ability to scare Dragon-types such as Raging Bolt, Kyurem, and Hydrapple; in turn, it aids Dragapult against specially defensive walls such as Ting-Lu, Blissey, and Assault Vest Alomomola and Primarina, with both being able to bring each other safely on the field with U-turn. Similarly, Kingambit appreciates Dragapult pressuring physical walls such as Dondozo, Great Tusk, and Zamazenta, while it assists Dragapult against opposing Ghost-types such as Gholdengo and Pecharunt when Dragapult is locked into an undesirable move and against Tera Fairy Garganacl, which can take on both of Dragapult's STAB moves. Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Corviknight aid against Kingambit, which may use a Choice-locked Dragapult as an opportunity to set up, and they can either remove or prevent entry hazards from being set up and weakening Dragapult, thanks to Rapid Spin, Taunt, and Defog, respectively. Furthermore, Great Tusk and Landorus-T provide Stealth Rock support to chip foes such as Assault Vest Tornadus-T and Enamorus to put them in range of Dragapult's attacks, while Landorus-T and Corviknight can act as pivots with U-turn to bring Dragapult safely on the field. Galarian Slowking and Iron Crown can deal with Fairy-types such as Clefable and Galarian Weezing looking to exploit Dragapult being locked into Draco Meteor. Iron Valiant aids Dragapult against Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott, Ting-Lu, and Kingambit, as well as weakening shared checks such as Primarina and Assault Vest Tornadus-T. With Booster Energy, Iron Valiant is also able to provide extra speed control alongside Dragapult, particularly outpacing foes faster than Dragapult such as Deoxys-S, Choice Scarf Gholdengo, and +1 Kyurem.

Mixed Offensive.description:
Dragapult uses its unique STAB combination and mixed attacking power to more quickly break through many common defensive cores. It can pressure physically defensive foes like Great Tusk, Gholdengo, Zamazenta with its Shadow Ball and Draco Meteor, while its Dragon Darts easily targets common Assault Vest users like Tornadus-T and Hisuian Samurott as well as sturdy special walls in Blissey and Clodsire, 2HKOing all of them. Fire Blast targets Steel-types such as Kingambit, Iron Treads, Corviknight, and Tinkaton that might otherwise be able to take Dragapult's STAB attacks. Will-O-Wisp similarly does this by crippling Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Assault Vest Alomomola while still permanently shutting down Kingambit, doing so safely by bypassing the latter's Sucker Punch. Clear Body can allow Dragapult to completely ignore Sticky Web, Intimidate from Landorus-T, and Parting Shot from Pecharunt, whereas Infiltrator helps Dragapult against dual screens while allowing it to hit through Substitute users like Iron Moth, Kyurem, Zamazenta. Tera Dragon boosts the power of both Dragon Darts and Draco Meteor to improve its wallbreaking duties; this particularly allows Dragapult to OHKO Multiscale Dragonite with Dragon Darts as well as OHKO Ogerpon-W and 2HKO Iron Defense Zamazenta with Draco Meteor. It also sheds Dragapult of its Dark weakness, allowing it to take unboosted Kingambit's Sucker Punch from full HP.

Mixed offensive Dragapult fits best on hyper offense and offense teams, which appreciate its high Speed and wallbreaking prowess. Dark-types such as Kingambit and Darkrai appreciate Dragapult's power while also being able to take on Pokemon that might be able to revenge kill Dragapult like Choice Scarf Gholdengo and opposing Kingambit. Gholdengo and Kingambit can help against Clefable, Tera Fairy Garganacl, and Toxapex, which can stomach Dragapult's attacks, and in return, they appreciate Dragapult's ability to threaten the likes of Cinderace and Great Tusk. Gholdengo in particular can also stomach Moonblast from Enamorus and Iron Valiant that try to revenge kill Dragapult. Entry hazard setters such as Ting-Lu, Glimmora, and Landorus-T are great partners for Dragapult, as the damage from hazards can chip common answers into KO range of its attacks. Dragapult struggles immensely with entry hazards, as they further cut into its limited longevity; as a result, hazard removal options like Iron Treads, Great Tusk, and Glimmora pair nicely with it, allowing it to get in more often in order to wallbreak. Pokemon that can take on Ting-Lu such as Ogerpon-W and Zamazenta are incredibly valuable for Dragapult, as Ting-Lu otherwise hard walls this set. Ogerpon-W can also help take on Assault Vest Alomomola, Primarina, and Garganacl, while Dragapult in return can help take on Dragonite, Raging Bolt, Kyurem, and Pecharunt, which trouble Ogerpon-W. Pokemon such as Hisuian Samurott and non-Dazzling Gleam Iron Moth that can struggle with Dragon-types like Raging Bolt and Dragonite immensely appreciate Dragapult threatening them. Iron Valiant is an excellent partner for Dragapult, as it can not only weaken Ting-Lu but can also take on Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Weavile, which may try to revenge kill Dragapult with their priority moves. In return, Dragapult can take on Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking, Gholdengo, and Moltres that might wall Iron Valiant.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dragon

Spell Tag lets Dragapult OHKO Iron Valiant after it has been inflicted with status, which can be crucial in the Fighting matchup. However, Dragapult becomes much easier to wear down and will have a harder time overcoming bulkier types like Water or Poison. U-turn can be used over Substitute or Thunder Wave if using Heavy-Duty Boots to pivot in its teammates like Walking Wake to take advantage of switch-ins like Ting-Lu and Heatran, but not having Substitute means Dragapult cannot stallbreak as well.

Choice Band (Dragon).description:
Choice Band Dragapult is a formidable wallbreaker and late-game cleaner for Dragon teams with its high Attack and incredible Speed, powerful STAB combination, and great ability in Infiltrator. Dragon Darts is a strong and reliable STAB option, which with Stealth Rock damage, OHKOes foes like Greninja and Darkrai and 2HKOes Toxapex. Psychic Fangs threatens Poison- and Fighting-types like Galarian Weezing and Iron Valiant, potentially OHKOing the latter. Sucker Punch, on the other hand, allows Dragapult to pick off weakened faster threats like Choice Scarf Latias, Iron Boulder, and opposing Dragapult. With U-turn, Dragapult can pivot out of unfavorable matchups against foes like Toxapex, Archaludon, and Skarmory, bringing in teammates like Choice Specs Latios and Raging Bolt.

With their exceptional bulk and typing, Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra provide a defensive backbone for Dragapult. Archaludon handles physical attackers like Ceruledge, Weavile, the Ogerpon formes, and Choice Scarf users like Meowscarada and Roaring Moon while also providing Stealth Rock support. Hisuian Goodra takes on Fairy-types like Primarina and Clefable and can safely switch into and threaten Choice Specs Greninja and Flutter Mane. Kyurem and Latios break through bulky Ground- and Flying-types like Hippowdon, Gliscor, and Mandibuzz and eliminate physical walls like Archaludon, Skarmory, and Dondozo. Latios and Latias threaten bulky Poison- and Fighting-types like Toxapex, Galarian Weezing, Great Tusk, and Iron Hands; Latias cripples the aforementioned foes with Trick and also provide Healing Wish support. Garchomp can set Spikes, which makes it easier for Dragapult to break through bulky foes, and handles Steel- and Poison-types like Heatran and Toxapex. Choice Scarf Roaring Moon can eliminate common Choice Scarf users like Latias, Enamorus, and Gholdengo as well as opposing non-Choice Scarf Dragapult.

Hex (Dragon).description:
Dragapult provides great offensive support for Dragon teams, being an effective form of status spreading thanks to its great Speed and ability, Infiltrator. This allows it to bypass Substitute to inflict status on foes hiding behind them. Furthermore, Infiltrator allows Dragapult to render dual screens useless, thus improving the Fairy matchup. Will-O-Wisp weakens common switch-ins to Dragapult like Iron Hands, Alolan Muk, and Hisuian Goodra, reducing their offensive capabilities. Hex takes advantage of Dragapult's great status spreading to deal high damage to afflicted foes. Draco Meteor can be run over Dragon Darts, both when Substitute is not being used and if it needs to handle Archaludon in a better way. However, Dragon Darts is preferred, since the Special Attack drop from Draco Meteor is undesirable when run alongside Substitute. Substitute allows Dragapult to take advantage of passive walls such as Toxapex and Clodsire to spread status more safely. Alternatively, Thunder Wave can be used to target faster threats such as +1 Volcarona and Choice Scarf Sneasler. However, Substitute is the preferred option, since most foes that outspeed Dragapult can OHKO it outright, but Substitute must only be run with Leftovers as an item. 148 Special Attack EVs allow Dragapult to OHKO Flutter Mane with Hex after it is statused, while 108 Attack EVs further improve the power of Dragon Darts.

Early-game wallbreakers such as Choice Band Dragonite and Choice Specs Latios appreciate Dragapult's status spreading, with Latios fearing less from Iron Hands's Ice Punch. Dragonite threatens Corviknight, Alolan Muk, Hisuian Goodra, and Heatran, while Latios targets Toxapex and Iron Hands. Steel-type partners such as Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra can take hits from offensive threats to Dragapult, with Archaludon taking hits from Bisharp and Meowscarada and threatening back with Body Press, further helped by Stamina, as well as setting up Stealth Rock. Hisuian Goodra threatens a multitude of Fairy-types including Iron Valiant, Flutter Mane, and Enamorus. Raging Bolt handles Water-types that can cause Dragapult trouble such as Azumarill and Empoleon. Lastly, Dragapult's ability to stallbreak and weaken walls with status opens the door for setup sweepers like Roaring Moon, Garchomp, and Raging Bolt to sweep late-game.

Choice Specs (Dragon).description:
Dragapult makes for a great special wallbreaker and late-game cleaner on Dragon teams by virtue of its great coverage and high Speed, making it the fastest unboosted Pokemon in the metagame. Furthermore, a great ability in Infiltrator allows it to be effective against types that commonly run dual screens like Fairy and Ice, and it can bypass Substitute from setup sweepers such as Spectrier. Draco Meteor and Shadow Ball form an incredible STAB move combination that targets a great number of threats and is only resisted by a few. Flamethrower targets Ice-types like Alolan Sandslash, Frosmoth, and Alolan Ninetales, as well as Steel-types like Corviknight, Scizor, and Klefki. Thunderbolt threatens bulky Water- and Flying-types such as Toxapex, Primarina, and Mandibuzz. U-turn allows Dragapult to bring in one of its teammates safely into foes that check it like Swampert, Alolan Muk, and Ting-Lu. However, Thunderbolt is preferred, since it doesn't render Dragapult entirely helpless against Primarina and Azumarill.

Archaludon provides Stealth Rock support and grants defensive coverage against Bisharp. Early-game wallbreakers such as Nasty Plot Hydreigon, Choice Specs Latios, and Choice Specs Kyurem make for excellent partners, as they remove Dragapult's checks so that it can easily clean up late-game. Hydreigon handles Articuno, Latios threatens bulky Poison-types like Galarian Weezing and Clodsire, and Kyurem targets bulky Ground-types like Clodsire, Gliscor, and Ting-Lu, as well as Heatran. Garchomp is a great partner, as it sets up Spikes to aid Dragapult's wallbreaking and cleaning, and it can potentially sweep late-game with Swords Dance and Scale Shot. Dragapult appreciates speed control from Choice Scarf users like Roaring Moon and Latias, as Roaring Moon threatens Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, Latias, and Gholdengo, while Latias not only outspeeds and threatens Choice Scarf Great Tusk and Walking Wake, but it can also give its Choice Scarf to a wall with Trick. In addition, it provides Healing Wish support for Dragapult. Dragapult's role as a wallbreaker is appreciated by setup sweepers like Raging Bolt and Dragonite, which benefit from the removal of Alolan Ninetales and Sableye so they can safely sweep late-game.

Choice Scarf (Dragon).description:
Choice Scarf Dragapult is an exceptional revenge killer due to its incredible Speed tier and ability to pressure opposing Dragon teams. Infiltrator allows Dragapult to threaten sweepers behind Substitute like opposing Dragapult as well as ignore Aurora Veil, dealing with Kyurem. Dragon Darts is Dragapult's most reliable Dragon type move, boasting a great Base Power and the ability to easily clean Dragon teams late-game. Phantom Force targets Ghost-types like Flutter Mane and Spectrier, removing them in a pinch. Alternatively, Shadow Ball may be used instead for a one-turn Ghost-type move; however, most foes need to be chipped down, as the move uses Dragapult's lower Special Attack stat, unlike Phantom Force. U-turn enables Dragapult as a fast pivot, allowing it to escape unfavorable situations as well as lure in Dark types like Hoopa-U and Meowscarada. Thunder Wave and Will-O-Wisp allow Dragapult to hinder offensive threats that its other moves don't threaten; the former slows down Choice Scarf Enamorus and Iron Valiant, while the latter weakens Bisharp. Fire Blast may be used as a substitute to threaten Steel- and Ice-types such as Skarmory, Alolan Sandslash, and Weavile. A Jolly nature grants Dragapult the ability to outpace other Choice Scarf users like Flutter Mane, Darkrai, and Spectrier, while a Hasty nature may be used should Shadow Ball or Fire Blast be opted for.

Archaludon provides great physical bulk, taking on threats such as Dragonite and Mimikyu as well as setting up Stealth Rock, enhancing Dragapult's revenge killing ability. In return, Dragapult offers a Fighting immunity, combating threats such as Sneasler and Keldeo. Latias and Latios scare away Poison-type walls like Okidogi, Toxapex, and Galarian Weezing as well as take on Ground types such as Great Tusk, Landorus, and Clodsire. Kyurem appreciates Dragapult's aforementioned Fighting immunity and ability to remove faster Dragon-types like Roaring Moon and Latias. In exchange, Kyurem breaks walls like Toxapex, Mandibuzz, and Hippowdon as well as removes Archaludon once pivoted in by U-turn. Raging Bolt breaks Water- and Flying-type threats like Primarina, Corviknight, and Galarian Moltres. Additionally, Thunderclap allows Raging Bolt to remove faster threats such as Choice Scarf Enamorus, Greninja, and Barraskewda. Hisuian Goodra provides an answer to Ice- and Fairy- types like Kyurem, Articuno, and Hatterene and gives Knock Off support to ease Dragapult's cleaning late-game.

Hex (Ghost).description:
Dragapult carries a plethora of utility options in its movepool to hinder the opposition. It leverages its high Speed to outspeed and threaten Hisuian Samurott and Flutter Mane with status for its teammates. Heavy-Duty Boots also enables Dragapult to switch in much more often. Will-O-Wisp weakens physical attackers that pose a threat to Ghost teams, such as Great Tusk, Urshifu-R, and Hisuian Samurott, while Thunder Wave disrupts faster opposition such as Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott, Ogerpon-H, and Spectrier. Hex is also a great choice for beating Gliscor and other Pokemon affected by Dragapult spreading status. U-turn is another great form of support as it lets Dragapult, scout switches and bring in its teammates safely. Dragapult's ability, Infiltrator, also grants it the capability to ignore dual screens set up by Klefki in the Fairy matchup. The given EV spread allows Dragapult to guarantee a 2HKO against Hatterene after recovery from Leftovers and always outspeed Flutter Mane.

Flutter Mane is the biggest beneficiary of Dragapult's services, as it can outspeed Choice Scarf users crippled by Thunder Wave or live a few physical attacks from foes burned by Will-O-Wisp such as Earthquake from Landorus-T and Dire Claw from Sneasler. Flutter Mane repays Dragapult by blasting through Dark-types that give Ghost teams trouble such as Greninja, Choice Scarf Darkrai, and, if using a Choice Scarf, Roaring Moon. Spectrier is another great teammate for taking advantage of the status spread by Dragapult by threatening to win games with Hex. Dragapult's status also allows Spectrier to freely run Substitute and Nasty Plot together without needing to run Will-O-Wisp. Dragapult also safely pivots both Flutter Mane and Spectrier in, which is useful as both are quite frail. Gholdengo is an excellent choice, as with a Hex set, it is able to use the status spread by Dragapult to great effect and enhance its power. Skeledirge is a good choice as well, as it can withstand hits and reply back with a boosting Torch Song while also posing a threat to Heatran with Earth Power. Skeledirge also threatens Ice-types such as Alolan Ninetales and Frosmoth. Hisuian Zoroark is a much appreciated Ghost immunity that can deceive opponents into thinking it may be Dragapult or its vulnerable teammates, then take advantage of that to unleash powerful attacks against opposing Spectrier and Ceruledge or cripple walls such as Toxapex and Empoleon with Knock Off. Substitute Sinistcha is another choice to take care of one of Ghost's biggest problems in Hisuian Samurott. Dragapult's spreading of status also allows for Mimikyu and Ceruledge to set up much more easily to threaten Fighting-types like Iron Hands and Steel-types like Corviknight, respectively. Mimikyu is also a one-time check to Bisharp with Disguise, both of which greatly threaten Ghost teams. Brambleghast can set up Spikes, which can wear down the opposition quickly in conjunction with burns from Dragapult's Will-O-Wisp, while Gengar can set up Toxic Spikes, letting Dragapult and Spectrier use Hex much more often.

Dragon Dance + Weakness Policy (Ghost).description: This is a winning set from the Monotype Rising sets project. This will be updated as we work on new analyses. Stay tuned!

Dragon Dance (Ghost).description:
Dragon Dance gives Dragapult the ability to not just boost its fantastic Speed to new heights, allowing it to outspeed fast Choice Scarf users such as Meowscarada and Roaring Moon, but also beef up its decent Attack stat. Dragon Darts is a reliable, hard-hitting Dragon-type STAB move that allows Dragapult to break Breloom's Focus Sash and Dragonite's Multiscale. Phantom Force is Dragapult's best choice for Ghost-tpye STAB move, as otherwise it is walled by any Fairy- or Steel-type, while Disable can disrupt Choice-locked Pokemon from potentially breaking its Substitute or attacking Dragapult in general. Substitute allows Dragapult to ease prediction and also adds a layer of protection against status moves, allowing it to set up on more passive Pokemon such as Toxapex and Amoonguss. It also synergizes well with Disable, allowing Dragapult to set up with ease. Will-O-Wisp is another option over Disable to allow Clodsire and Quagsire to become setup bait, while also crippling Bisharp and Ting-Lu; however, Disable is more consistent. Leftovers allows Dragapult to use Substitute multiple times throughout a game and be more annoying overall with Disable, while Dragon Fang is a good choice to boost Dragon Darts.

Skeledirge is a fantastic partner, as it can wall Fairy-types such as Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Hatterene while also threatening foes like Bisharp that can easily take out Dragapult with their STAB priority moves. Gholdengo is another fantastic partner that can threaten Fairy-types like Klefki and Flutter Mane, if Gholdengo uses a Choice Scarf, and take care of physical walls such as opposing Skeledirge. Brambleghast is another good partner, as it can keep entry hazards off of the field, allowing Dragapult to come in multiple times, as well as providing Spikes support to soften up Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Iron Treads. Hisuian Zoroark provides the team with not just a Ghost immunity, but also can easily use Illusion to disguise itself as Dragapult and lure in foes that would normally threaten it, such as Bisharp, Archaludon, and opposing Dragapult, to open up for a potential Dragapult sweep. Flutter Mane is another great partner thanks to its ability to handle opposing Dragon-types such as Baxcalibur, Roaring Moon, and Walking Wake. It can also provide immediate speed control if need be to take care of other Choice Scarf users that could revenge kill Dragapult before it gets a Dragon Dance up. Mimikyu is an amazing wallbreaker that can either help wear down physical walls for Dragapult to clean up or can take advantage of Dragapult punching holes in the opponent's team to clean up itself. Mimikyu can also heavily threaten opposing Ghost-types for Dragapult like Choice Scarf Flutter Mane, Dragapult, and Choice Scarf Gholdengo thanks to its STAB priority in Shadow Sneak. It also provides a one-time check to setup sweepers such as Bisharp and Ceruledge thanks to its ability Disguise.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Dragapult is a common attacker on balance teams with bulky redirectors, such as Electabuzz, Magmar, and Clefable. Redirectors are vital, since they assist in keeping Dragapult around for longer, which is especially important because Dragapult is frail and is weak to Sucker Punch from threats such as Kingambit. Additionally, Dragapult appreciates Fake Out support from the likes of Rillaboom, as it gives free turns for Dragapult to get extra attacks off, and it works nicely with Phantom Force, preventing a foe from attacking Dragapult after it lands the attack.
  • Dragapult appreciates partners that can cover its weaknesses offensively or that can reliably switch into its checks; some examples are Sneasler and Primarina. Sneasler is a fast attacker that can outspeed and threaten Dark- and Fairy-types such as Incineroar, Kingambit, and Primarina. Primarina is a slower, bulkier attacker that can switch into attacks easier while still having the ability to OHKO threats such as Incineroar.
  • Dark-types such as Kingambit and Incineroar are the biggest checks to Dragapult, as they can easily shrug off its attacks and threaten it with an OHKO. The aforementioned partners can help against these threats by threatening them and redirecting attacks, buying more time for Dragapult to switch out safely or overwhelm them with strong Dragon-type attacks. Tailwind teams can also be a big problem to Dragapult, as it relies on being faster than its foes and getting lots of damage off before they can move. Partners such as Rillaboom and Kingambit can help against Tailwind teams, since they can attack foes with strong priority moves, stall turns with smart pivoting, and, in Rillaboom's case, use Fake Out.

Strategy Comments

  • Dragapult is a sweeper, and it requires a lot of smart positioning to use it to its maximum potential. Dragapult shines in positions where its partners can support it either offensively by threatening its checks or defensively by aiding in its longevity. U-turn is a great tool in this regard, as it allows Dragapult to escape from tricky positions while doing chip damage to a foe.
  • Dragapult utilizes Terastallization to get major damage on enemy Pokemon throughout the course of the game. Dragapult can be utilized early-game to get off powerful Tera Dragon Dragon Darts or Tera Blast Ghost, or it can be utilized late-game to clean the enemy team with Dragon Darts and Phantom Force.
  • Dragapult's biggest weakness is Pokemon that resist its STAB attacks, such as Kingambit, Alolan Ninetales, and Incineroar. Dragapult utilizes its partners to help against these threats until they are weakened to a point where Dragapult can finish them off. Priority attacks such as Sucker Punch from Kingambit and forms of speed control, such as Tailwind and Trick Room, are threatening to Dragapult, as it is frail and relies on its high damage output and outspeeding foes. Against priority attacks, Dragapult pivots partners in or utilizes an ally with redirection to take the attacks for it. Against Tailwind and Trick Room teams, Dragapult again uses smart pivots and defensive tools such as Follow Me and Fake Out to stall out turns of Trick Room, allowing it to clean up late-game.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Dragapult uses its powerful STAB attacks, phenomenal Speed, and solid Attack stat to outrun almost every Pokemon in the game and deal massive damage to the opposing team.
  • Dragon Darts is great at consistently chipping down the opposing team. Phantom Force is Dragapult's strongest Ghost-type STAB move that can also shatter Protect, but it allows foes to switch due to its charging turn. Tera Dragon sets prefer Outrage to nuke foes, albeit inconsistently. On the other hand, Tera Blast Ghost is a reliable one-turn Ghost-type STAB move. U-turn allows Dragapult to get chip damage on foes and pivot out of tricky matchups while dealing respectable damage to threats such as Rillaboom.
  • Choice Band boosts Dragapult's Attack stat to great levels, which pairs excellently with its high Speed.
  • Tera Dragon allows Dragapult to OHKO Garchomp and Hydreigon with one hit from Dragon Darts and Incineroar, Electabuzz, and Magmar with Outrage. Additionally, Tera Dragon removes Dragapult's weakness to Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Tera Ghost is used, since it gives Dragapult a consistent physical Ghost-type attack in Tera Blast Ghost while also allowing it to OHKO Volcarona and Primarina with Phantom Force.
  • An Adamant nature allows Dragapult to always OHKO Volcarona with Outrage and almost always OHKO a Terastallized Hisuian Typhlosion with Phantom Force. A Jolly nature allows Dragapult to outspeed Jolly Talonflame, Adamant Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, and opposing Adamant Dragapult.

Status Spam.description: Dragapult is a solid utility Pokemon thanks to its blistering Speed, strong offensive and defensive typing, and excellent support movepool. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers looking to switch in, like Zacian, Arceus-Poison, and Palafin. Hex capitalizes on Dragapult's status spreading, as well as doing huge damage to sleeping Giratina. Thunder Wave can cripple common switch-ins and setup sweepers, like Dragon Dance Arceus formes and Baxcalibur, as well as the aforementioned Zacian. Substitute allows Dragapult to block Thunder Wave and Will-O-Wisp from Arceus formes and Giratina, and it also capitalizes on its resistances to U-turn and Volt Switch. U-turn allows Dragapult to pivot out on Pokemon like Zacian and Arceus-Dark and bring a threatening teammate in, like Zamazenta-C or Zacian. Tera Fairy flips Dragapult's Dragon-type weakness on its head, making it immune to Dragon-type moves from Palkia-O, Arceus-Dragon, and Dialga; Tera Fairy also lets it resist Dark-type moves from Urshifu-S and Kingambit. Dragapult enables Pokemon like Zacian and Dragon Dance Arceus formes through its endless status spreading, so they partner fantastically with it. Dragapult struggles to break through walls and is particularly annoyed by Garganacl and Gholdengo, as both are immune to its status moves, meaning it appreciates Ground-type partners like Landorus, Chi-Yu, Kyurem-W, and Bulk Up Great Tusk, which can wallbreak for Dragapult and capitalize on the weakened opposing team.

Choice Band.description:
• Outrage is for non-Choice Scarf and non-Haban Berry Dragon-type Pokemon and can be used to deal massive STAB damage against Pokemon such as Volcarona, Porygon-Z, and Zapdos.
  • Dragon Darts is specifically used to break Substitute from Pokemon like Espathra.
  • Phantom Force covers Ghost-type Pokemon like Spectrier, Pecharunt, Annihilape, and non-physically defensive Skeledirge.
  • U-turn deals with physically defensive Hoopa-U.
  • Dragapult's ability Clear Body allows it to ignore stat changes from Landorus-T and Pecharunt.
  • Dragapult's Ghost typing allows it to safely attack without having to worry about getting hit by Counter from Defensive Ogerpon-W.
  • While Adamant nature allows Dragapult to deals maximum damage and allows it to have better odds against other Pokemon such as Metagross and Skeledirge, Jolly nature allows it to outspeed Spectrier, Darkrai, and Chien-Pao.
  • Dragapult struggles against Dark-, Dragon-, or Fairy-type Pokemon such as Urshifu-S, Primarina, and Speed Booster Energy Roaring Moon. Pokemon like Sylveon and Iron Valiant, which cover for Dragapult's Dark and Dragon weaknesses, and Scizor and Corviknight, which cover for Dragapult's Fairy and Dark weaknesses are good teammates.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis is for the Regulation C format of Battle Stadium Singles, which lasts until June 30th, 2023. For more information on this format and its current events, check out the format page!

If you feel this analysis is missing anything important or needs an update, feel free to suggest any changes here.

Physical Attacker.description:
• Dragapult's blistering Speed makes it a very effective hit-and-run attacker.

  • Phantom Force: This is risky due to the two turns making Dragapult vulnerable to Normal-types and surprise Terastallization, but it still makes an effective late-game cleaning move.

  • Sucker Punch: Despite Dragapult's dynamite Speed stat, Sucker Punch still makes sense to pick off common Choice Scarf holders like Gholdengo, and play around priority from other foes.

  • Shadow Ball: With a Naive nature, Shadow Ball is an easy way to 2HKO Gholdengo, Flutter Mane, and incoming Skeledirge.

Other Options
  • Dragon Dance: Dragon Dance is fairly difficult to set up without Focus Sash, and it can lead to coverage issues. That being said, outspeeding Pokemon that commonly have their Speed boosted via an item, such as Flutter Mane, Gholdengo, and Iron Bundle, can lead to surprising win conditions.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Dragapult's cleaning capabilities are improved quite a bit by Terastallization, though it doesn't need to rely on it to be functional.

  • Dragon: Boosting the power of Dragon Darts makes Dragapult very effective at shredding through Focus Sash Pokemon such as Chien-Pao, in addition to removing the annoying Sucker Punch weakness.

  • Steel: Steel has a fantastic synergy with Dragapult's former typing, giving it a far better match-up against foes such as Flutter Mane, Iron Bundle, and Mimikyu.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost is notable for letting Dragapult use a less risky STAB move in Tera Blast.

  • Fire: Tera Fire gives a valuable Fairy-type resistance and is a more powerful tool against Steel-types at the cost of a Stealth Rock weakness.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy's Dragon-type immunity can help win Tera wars against foes like Garchomp, Great Tusk, and Roaring Moon.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting vastly improves Dragapult's match-up against Kingambit, Chi-Yu, Chien-Pao, and Choice Scarf Meowscarada.

Items

  • Choice Band: Choice Band guarantees that Breloom is OHKOed through its Focus Sash with Dragon Darts, and gives a 75% shot to the same happening to Chien-Pao.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb makes Sucker Punch a less risky option.

  • Focus Sash: Dragaoult's bulk isn't terrible, but Focus Sash will save it from the huge amount of top tier Pokemon that are capable of OHKOing it, such as Chien-Pao, Chi-Yu, and Gholdengo.

  • Choice Scarf: This may seem like overkill, but Choice Scarf gives Dragapult the edge over Booster Energy users such as Iron Bundle, Roaring Moon, and Flutter Mane, and other Choice Scarf foes such Gholdengo.

Special Attacker.description:
• Despite the lower offensive stat, the higher base power of Dragapult's special attacks makes it a serious threat.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is the recommended coverage move for hitting Corviknight and Dondozo hard.

  • U-turn: Even though it's weak, U-turn is a reasonable consideration for pivoting and breaking Mimikyu's Disguise.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: While Dragapult can use Terastallization to surprise its checks, the high power of Draco Meteor and good coverage Shadow Ball provides mean it isn't reliant on it to function.

  • Dragon: Tera Dragon makes Draco Meteor nearly impossible to wall without a resistance, with even specially defensive Ting-Lu taking nearly 50% from it!

  • Fire: The Fairy-type resistance and powerful Flamethrower can make the Stealth Rock weakness worth it.

  • Steel: Tera Steel covers much of Dragapult's common weaknesses, and gives it a good Tera Blast to use against Fairy-types.

  • Ghost: Powering up Shadow Ball is perfect for cleaning up late-game, with only Normal-types and bulky resistances such as Ting-Lu, Wo-Chien, and Garganacl taking it well.

  • Fighting: The resistance to Sucker Punch Tera Fighting provides can be key in stopping Chien-Pao and Kingambit.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy improves Dragapult's match-up against other Dragon-types, Great Tusk, and resists Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch.

Bulky Status.description:
• With usable bulk bolstered by Will-O-Wisp, this Dragapult can severely punish its weaker offensive checks, and surprise common users of Sucker Punch such as Kingambit and Chien-Pao.

  • Disable and Substitute: Disable makes Dragapult rely on Will-O-Wisp for Normal-types, but when combined with Substitute, it defeats Choice-locked foes and those that rely on one specific move to beat Dragapult.

  • Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor improves Dragapult against other Dragon-types, such as Dragonite and Garchomp.

  • Flamethrower: This lets Dragapult deal decent unconditional damage to Steel-types, with Kingambit being the biggest target.

  • Dragon Darts: With a Naive nature, Dragon Darts gives Dragapult a consequence-free Dragon-type attack and decent mixed attacking potential.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Dragapult's typing gives it a lot of weaknesses, so Terastallization can help it stick around much longer, though the lack of good recovery means this isn't always the correct choice.

  • Fairy: With a Fairy Tera type, Dragapult preforms better against Dark-types it may still struggle with after Will-O-Wisp, such as Chien-Pao and Ting-Lu.

  • Steel: Steel Tera type is great for general defense and Fairy-types such as Azumarill and Mimikyu.

Dual Screens.description:
• Dragapult's high Speed combined with Reflect and Light Screen make it an effective dual screens lead.

  • Curse: Curse reduces Dragapult's HP to get it off the field quickly once it has set up screens. It also forces opponents to use recovery moves or switch out, allowing Dragapult's teammates to get in and set up safely. Curse is Dragapult’s best option to bypass Substitute, Protect, and Mimikyu.

  • Shadow Ball: This breaks Focus Sash, hits Ghosts like Gholdengo and Flutter Mane that normally threaten it, and breaks Mimikyu's Disguise. Notably Gholdengo stops Curse with Good as Gold, making Dragapult totally helpless against it if it does not carry Shadow Ball.

  • Dragon Darts: Dragon Darts can be used for more power to make Dragapult more self-sufficient when it has to stay on the field, and breaks Focus Sash as well. Its dual-hit nature makes it bypass most Substitutes.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Will-O-Wisp can be used to cripple physical attackers. In tandem with Reflect, this can be a potent strategy to allow the next Pokemon to set up nearly risk-free.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Very Situational: As a dual screens lead, Terastallizing can compromise its teammates sweeping abilities, so it should only be done in emergencies.

  • Ghost / Dragon: If you are in a bad spot, Ghost and Dragon power up its STAB move of choice.

  • Steel: A defensive typing like Steel can allow Dragapult to survive certain moves like Iron Bundle's Ice Beam, boosted Cloyster's Icicle Spear, and boosted Baxcalibur's Glaive Rush and retaliate.

  • Fairy: A Fairy Tera type is useful for enemy Infiltrator Dragapult's Dragon Darts.

Items
  • Focus Sash: While Light Clay is standard, Focus Sash nearly guarantees setting at least one screen without having to Terastallize, in the event Dragapult leads off against Choice Scarf users like Gholdengo, Hydreigon, and Meowscarada.

cap.comments:
Checks and Counters

Garganacl: Garganacl is immune to any status, and the secondary effect of Purifying Salt makes it take less damage from Ghost-type moves, which forces Dragapult out and allows Garganacl to either use Salt Cure on a teammate or set up Stealth Rock.

Fairy-types: Dragapult can barely touch Fairy-types, as they always threaten it out on the field; notably, bulky defensive Fairy-types like Clefable and Cresceidon can spread paralysis and slow Dragapult down. However, Cresceidon doesn't like to be statused in return. Faster threats like Booster Energy Iron Valiant & Pixilate Extreme Speed Hemogoblin can outspeed and KO Dragapult. Iron Valiant, however, can only check Dragapult one time with Booster Energy, while Hemogoblin's Extreme Speed has limited PP.

Dark-types: Kingambit, Ting-Lu, Darkrai, and Hisuian Samurott are key threats that can hit Dragapult with a super effective attack or be reliable switch-ins to Hex due to their Ghost resistance. Additionally, Knock Off users like Weavile and Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott can not only get rid of Dragapult's item but also hit it super effectively. However, status can hinder these foes, as Darkrai doesn't enjoy being paralyzed, while Ting-Lu and Hisuian Samurott fear being burned, and all of these Pokemon except Kingambit take a decent chunk of damage from U-turn.

Shox: Shox is one of the best counters to Dragapult, as it has an immunity to Ghost-type moves and Thunder Wave, and it carries moves like Ice Beam, Knock Off, and Encore.

Hex.description:
Set Details

Dragapult is an excellent offensive pivot thanks to U-turn paired with an incredibly high Speed stat alongside powerful status moves such as Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave. This deadly combination allows it to maneuver around slower threats and cripple foes consistently over the course of a match. Hex is a great way for Dragapult to check Poison Heal Pokemon like Gliscor and Snaelstrom, using their own status against them while also exploiting its own status moves as well. Will-O-Wisp can be used to neutralize threatening physical attackers such as Kitsunoh, Great Tusk, and Zamazenta, while Thunder Wave can be used to cripple Pokemon that have an immunity to burns like Iron Moth and Mollux and slow down fast attackers like Darkrai, Stratagem, and Cresceidon, allowing its teammates to switch in and effectively deal with them, while also giving Dragapult the ability to set up its own status to empower Hex. Dragon Darts is a reliable and strong STAB attack that can pressure specially defensive Pokemon such as Blissey while also hitting Raging Bolt and Multiscale Dragonite. Alternatively, Draco Meteor nails opposing Dragon-types such as Walking Wake, Miasmaw, and Chuggalong without Clangorous Soul's boosts. Tera Fairy helps with Dragapult's weakness to Dragon-types like Chuggalong by granting a Dragon immunity while also allowing it to become resistant to Dark-type attacks from the likes of Darkrai and Kingambit. Tera Ghost is a great alternative to power up Hex while also dropping Dragapult's weakness to Dragon- and Fairy-types like Hemogoblin. The first given EV spread allows Dragapult to always 2HKO Hisuian Samurott with Dragon Darts.

Dragapult is a great pick for offensive balanced teams, being a complement to entry hazard setters such as Arghonaut, Gliscor, and Mollux that can assist it by chipping down foes that don't have Heavy-Duty Boots or reliable hazard removal. In return, Dragapult can assist these Pokemon by being a reliably fast Pokemon with potential speed control that can switch in and spread status or deal good damage then pivot. Knock Off users like Colossoil and Kitsunoh pair greatly with Dragapult to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from opposing Pokemon to help force further chip damage when coupled with Will-O-Wisp alongside hazards. Fairy-type Pokemon like Hemogoblin and Cresceidon threaten Dragapult around every corner, making Pokemon like Venomicon and Galarian Slowking great teammates to let Dragapult safely pivot out. Galarian Slowking pairs well with Dragapult thanks to Chilly Reception, allowing it to form a solid pivot core. In return, Dragapult removes Ghost- and Dragon-type threats to them with its powerful dual STAB moves, though when using Hex, Dragapult needs to spread status first and foremost. Although Dragapult has a Speed tier almost unmatched in the metagame, Booster Energy users like Iron Valiant and Iron Moth can threaten Dragapult, so bulky defensive teammates like Equilibra can efficiently be switched in to take a super effective hit aimed at Dragapult. The aforementioned Fairy-type Pokemon also partner well with Dragapult, as they can help ease pressure against opposing Dragon-types while powering up Dragapult's Hex with their own status moves. Shox is one of Dragapult's struggles, as it is immune to status besides burns and can handle either Dragon Darts or Draco Meteor and recover with Slack Off; Dragapult can't really do much to it and other status-immune Pokemon like Garganacl, so having teammates like Great Tusk and Equilibra that can threaten them out with super effective Fighting-, Steel-, and Ground-type moves is greatly appreciated. Dragapult is threatened out by the likes of Knock Off users like Gliscor, so having teammates such as Arghonaut, which can handle taking Knock Off, and Alomomola, which can defensively handle them, helps Dragapult greatly.

Other Options

An alternative way to utilize Dragapult's power is by using a Choice Specs set to let it act as a wallbreaker, though this typically isn't seen as much, as spreading status is much more preferred.

Defensive.description: Zacian's niche lies in its excellent Speed, allowing it to outspeed threats like Ash-Greninja, Flutter Mane, and Ultra Necrozma and thus check them better than its competition like Arceus-Fairy. Fur Coat lets Zacian check threats like Ash-Greninja and Mega Garchomp, while Ice Scales lets it soft check Flutter Mane and Ultra Necrozma. Strength Sap is generally preferred for its higher healing output and useful Attack drops, but Shore Up can be used on Ice Scales sets to more reliably heal against low Attack Pokemon such as Mega Alakazam and Flutter Mane. Magical Torque's higher damage output is useful against Pokemon like Mega Garchomp and Mega Alakazam, but Spirit Break is more effective to stave off boosting special attackers like Nasty Plot Flutter Mane and non-Poison-type move Eternatus. Glare and Topsy-Turvy both serve as tools against setup, with the former more effective and disruptive but also more difficult to Imposter-proof and useless against Flare Boost Flutter Mane. Spikes and Stone Axe help reduce Zacian's passivity by providing entry hazard support. Leftovers is useful to reduce the frequency that Zacian needs to recover, while Rocky Helmet harshly punishes Ash-Greninja. Ability Shield is a niche choice that improves its matchup against Moongeist Beam and non-STAB-boosted Sunsteel Strike users. Fur Coat Zacian can struggle against certain physical attackers like Zacian-C and Mega Lucario, so teammates that can cover them such as Fur Coat Arceus-Electric and Mega Swampert are appreciated. Ice Scales Zacian has trouble with Eternatus and repeated attacks from Mega Alakazam and Flutter Mane, making secondary special walls like RegenVest Primal Kyogre good teammates. Zacian can be Imposter-proofed by Pokemon like Fur Coat Take Heart Arceus formes, Imposter Chansey, and Magic Bounce Ho-Oh.

Bulky Attacker.description:
Set Details

  • Zacian-C has a unique niche in Regulation I thanks to its blistering Speed and excellent typing, allowing Zacian-C to threaten OHKOs on metagame staples like Miraidon, Koraidon, and Grimmsnarl.
  • Swords Dance is in Zacian-C's standard moveset, as it allows Zacian-C to boost its Attack faster than Incineroar's Intimidate would drop it and ensures Zacian-C remains a threat. Sacred Sword can be used instead to score 2HKOs on Zamazenta-C and Incineroar, which Zacian-C otherwise struggles to handle. Substitute is a good alternative, as it provides a superior matchup against Will-O-Wisp Incineroar and maintains momentum by protecting Zacian-C from being flinched by Fake Out. Thanks to Zacian-C's Speed, Substitute can also act as a secondary form of Protect and help Zacian-C scout opposing Protect and Terastallization, such as Tera Fairy Miraidon.
  • The EV spread ensures Zacian-C survives Flare Blitz from Life Orb Koraidon and Guts-boosted Headlong Rush from Ursaluna after Terastallization, as well as surviving Volt Switch from Choice Specs Miraidon and avoiding the 2HKO from Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage. The Speed investment allows Zacian-C to outspeed base 135s like Chien-Pao, Koraidon, and Miraidon. Finally, the Attack investment picks up an OHKO on Grimmsnarl behind Reflect with a Behemoth Blade.
  • Tera Fairy is an incredibly consistent Tera type, ​as it sheds Zacian-C's weaknesses and bolsters its damage output, achieving feats such as OHKOing maximum HP Miraidon with Play Rough at +0 Attack.

Teambuilding

  • Zacian-C especially struggles with Incineroar, as it can mitigate Zacian-C's damage output in various ways. Volcarona and Ogerpon-H are other problematic Pokemon, as they redirect and resist Zacian-C's STAB moves; Volcarona possesses the potential to permanently cripple Zacian-C with Flame Body, while Ogerpon-H threatens to OHKO with Tera Fire Ivy Cudgel.
  • Calyrex-S is an issue, as a lot of Zacian-C's viability comes from its Speed tier, so Calyrex-S compositions will have a much easier time supporting Calyrex-S and countering Zacian-C than vice versa. Zamazenta-C is difficult for Zacian-C without Sacred Sword, as Zamazenta-C comfortably wins one-on-one.
  • Kyogre and Urshifu-R are exceptional partners, as they blast all the Fire-types that frustrate Zacian-C. In return, Zacian-C can threaten the problematic Dragon-types like Raging Bolt, Koraidon, and Miraidon. Kyogre helps Zacian-C further by negating its weakness to Fire-type moves through setting up rain.
  • Amoonguss and Incineroar are useful partners, as they can help Zacian-C set up safely. Incineroar can greatly aid with Calyrex-S and Ogerpon-H, pressuring them with its STAB attacks and Parting Shot. Amoonguss makes Zamazenta-C far easier to take on and can shut down Incineroar that aren't holding Safety Goggles with Spore and Rage Powder.
  • Chien-Pao and Landorus form great offensive synergies with Zacian-C. Chien-Pao increases Zacian-C's damage output with Sword of Ruin and pressures Calyrex-S before it can move with Sucker Punch. With Sword of Ruin, Zacian-C can OHKO bulky Kyogre with Tera Fairy Play Rough and almost always 2HKOes Zamazenta-C at neutral Attack. Chien-Pao notably threatens Rillaboom and Amoonguss, meaning it also synergizes with other common Zacian-C partners. Landorus has more direct synergy, as it can threaten OHKOs on Incineroar, Zamazenta-C, and Ogerpon-H and provides a safer Miraidon endgame as a Ground-type. Both Pokemon help force pins on Miraidon and Raging Bolt, as Zacian-C can cover for Tera Fairy.

Offensive.description:
Zacian-C is a strong Restricted Pokemon in Regulation G, thanks to its superb typing as well as great Attack and Speed stats, which allow it to remove fast metagame threats such as Miraidon, Flutter Mane, and Koraidon. Play Rough threatens Koraidon and common Steel-resistant foes like Raging Bolt, Iron Hands, and Urshifu-R. Swords Dance allows Zacian-C to boost past Incineroar's Intimidate and remain a strong threat on the field. Sacred Sword can be used over either of these to threaten a 2HKO on Pokemon Zacian-C may otherwise struggle to break through, such as Incineroar and Zamazenta-C. Tera Blast can be used in conjunction with Tera Ground to also threaten Incineroar and Zamazenta-C, as well as Tera Electric Miraidon, Tera Fire Koraidon, and Gholdengo. However, Tera Blast can't break through IronPress Zamazenta-C and requires Zacian-C to commit to Terastallizaion.
