Another common partner is Rillaboom, setting its Terrain to give Zamazenta-C even more survivability with its healing and allow it to survive Choice Specs Electro Drift from Miraidon.

Zamazenta-C is a bulky offensive Pokemon that benefits from its good offensive and defensive typing and utility. It has a great balance of bulk and offensive presence with Dauntless Shield-boosted Body Press allowing it to effectively pressure key metagame threats such as Incineroar, Ogerpon-C, and Terapagos. Heavy Slam is used to OHKO Flutter Mane and Whimsicott. Wide Guard's utility enables Zamazenta-C to handle both Calyrex formes, Kyogre, and Groudon by protecting its side from Astral Barrage, Glacial Lance, Origin Pulse, and Precipice Blades, respectively. This support allows its teammates to safely attack these threats. The 164 Speed EVs allow Zamazenta-C to outspeed maximum Speed Landorus and Chi-Yu. Its bulk investment not only boosts Body Press, enabling it to almost always OHKO Incineroar and 2HKO opposing Zamazenta-C, but it also almost always ensures it survives a +1 Tera Fire Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-H and two Sacred Swords from Chien-Pao. On the special side, it is guaranteed to withstand a Sandsear Storm from Life Orb Landorus. Tera Dragon gives Zamazenta-C resistances to Fire- and Water-type moves, helping into threats like Chi-Yu, Urshifu-R, and Ogerpon-H. Additionally, removing its Ground and Fighting weakness helps it withstand attacks from Landorus, Groudon, opposing Zamazenta-C, and Iron Hands.

Zamazenta-C's more passive playstyle makes it struggle against bulky disruption Pokemon like Amoonguss, which can put it sleep with Spore or redirect its attacks with Rage Powder, and Incineroar, which often uses Tera Ghost and Will-O-Wisp to hinder its effectiveness. For the same reason, Zamazenta-C can also get outpaced offensively by hard-hitting threats like Calyrex-S, which can freely set up with Nasty Plot and sweep, and Miraidon. Landorus is another huge threat to Zamazenta-C because it threatens to OHKO it with Earth Power. Chien-Pao is Zamazenta-C's most common partner, as Sword of Ruin enhances Body Press's damage output. Additionally, Chien-Pao helps cover Zamazenta-C's weaknesses by handling threats such as Landorus, Amoonguss, Miraidon, and Calyrex-S. Speed Booster Energy Flutter Mane is another strong partner, providing speed control with Icy Wind and Thunder Wave to help Zamazenta-C outspeed Pokemon like Chien-Pao and common Choice Scarf users such as Landorus and Chi-Yu. Additionally, it pressures Calyrex-S with Shadow Ball and threatens Miraidon and Urshifu with Moonblast while helping with the aforementioned Amoonguss and Incineroar problem with Taunt. Rillaboom offers valuable utility with Fake Out and helps against Miraidon by changing the Terrain, weakening Miraidon's attacks. Amoonguss also synergizes well with Zamazenta-C, as it slows the pace of the game with Spore, while Zamazenta-C can protect it from Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance, which can be crucial in that matchup. Lastly, Choice Scarf Chi-Yu provides immediate offensive pressure, threatening both Calyrex formes, Amoonguss, and opposing Zamazenta-C. In return, Zamazenta-C helps cover some of the Pokemon that resist Chi-Yu's attacks like Incineroar and Roaring Moon.

IronPress.description: Zamazenta-C leverages its Fighting / Steel typing and high Defense and Speed to be a decent Body Press sweeper that's able to switch in and set up on common Pokemon like Corviknight, Chien-Pao, and Roaring Moon. Stone Edge helps against Zapdos, Iron Moth, and Ceruledge, while Substitute helps it set up against would-be switch-ins like Iron Hands and Great Tusk as well as shielding it from status afflictions from moves like Manaphy's Scald and Corrosion Pecharun't Toxic. Zamazenta-C plays best on offensive teams, so it appreciates entry hazards from Pokemon like Skarmory and Deoxys-D and dual screens support from Pokemon like Corviknight and Deoxys-S, which help it take KOs and set up, respectively. Zamazenta-C also appreciates Pokemon like Chien-Pao, Roaring Moon, and Gengar that are able to take down Deoxys-D, Gholdengo, and Pecharunt, as otherwise it is unable to make progress at all.

Meteor Beam.description:
• Meteor Beam Eternatus is one of the premier specially offensive Pokemon in the tier for hyper offense, leveraging its unique mixture of an excellent Speed tier, solid defensive traits, and great coverage. Eternatus is one of the fastest special threats in the tier while maintaining respectable bulk, making revenge killing it challenging. Additionally, as one of the few viable Poison-types in the tier, Eternatus provides a Toxic Spikes absorber for hyper offense teams.

  • Meteor Beam provides Rock coverage to OHKO Ho-Oh and Yveltal, which are otherwise bothersome to remove. Given this, Meteor Beam should be reserved for these targets when possible. However, if these threats are sufficiently weakened, Meteor Beam may also be used to KO weakened Pokemon such as Primal Groudon, allowing Eternatus to leverage the Special Attack boost immediately with its other moves.

  • Sludge Bomb hits Arceus-Fairy and Mega Diancie, as well as Tera Fairy Pokemon, such as Zygarde, aiming to blank Eternatus. Additionally, against bulkier opponents, Sludge Bomb's poison chance is incredibly useful in helping Eternatus muscle through. Examples of such targets include many soft checks such as Calm Mind Arceus formes, Ho-Oh after Meteor Beam has been used, and Primal Kyogre, especially its defensive variants.

  • Fire Blast, at +1, OHKOes Zacian-C as well as Calyrex-I after Stealth Rock. Flamethrower is a niche alternative that can be paired with Tera Fire. However, the damage loss is noticeable as it fails to achieve either of the aforementioned benchmarks without Tera. Unboosted Flamethrower also fails to OHKO Ferrothorn.

  • Tera Dragon boosts +1 Dynamax Cannon to absurd levels, OHKOing defensive staples such as defensive Primal Groudon after three layers of Spikes, Tera Water Zygarde after Stealth Rock, and offensive Yveltal. Additionally, Tera Dragon allows +1 Dynamax Cannon to 2HKO Ho-Oh and muscle through Arceus-Dark if it switches in on Meteor Beam. After a Sludge Bomb poisoning, unboosted Tera Dragon Eternatus can 2HKO Calm Mind Arceus formes. Tera Dragon additionally removes Eternatus's Ground and Psychic weaknesses, helping against the likes of Groudon, Zygarde, Ultra Necrozma, and Necrozma-DM. Please note that Ultra Necrozma's Light That Burns the Sky still OHKOes Eternatus after Terastallization, and Deoxys-A's Psycho Boost has a favorable roll to OHKO as well.

  • As previously mentioned, Tera Fire is an alternative option to boost Eternatus's Fire coverage while also flipping the defensive type matchup against Zacian-C, Calyrex-I, and the rarer Arceus-Fairy. Tera Fire enables Fire Blast to OHKO Zacian-C without a boost and Flamethrower to OHKO Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM after a boost and minimal chip damage. Tera Fire also allows Eternatus to survive Zacian-C's +3 Behemoth Blade, Calyrex-I's +1 Glacial Lance, and Choice Band Chien-Pao's Ice Spinner.

  • Meteor Beam Eternatus fits best on entry hazard stacking hyper offense teams capable of providing it the necessary hazard support to break through some of the walls in the tier. In turn, Eternatus offensively pressures every relevant Defogger with an OHKO unless they defensively Terastallize. However, a well-timed defensive Terastallization from the likes of Ho-Oh and Giratina-O can allow them to use Thunder Wave, crippling Eternatus's Speed and enabling them to use Defog after. Eternatus is also an effective mid-to-late-game cleaner due to its natural bulk, making it challenging to revenge kill.

  • Eternatus also fits well on Sticky Web teams that allow it to outpace otherwise faster threats, but the lack of entry hazard damage reduces its effectiveness versus bulkier teams. Furthermore, Eternatus faces stiff competition from fellow Meteor Beam user Lunala, which can block Extreme Speed and Rapid Spin and has access to Psyshock.

  • Eternatus pairs well with physical attackers such as Extreme Killer Arceus and Dragon Dance Ultra Necrozma that appreciate its ability to break physical walls and revenge kill Marshadow. In turn, their access to priority or Speed boosting moves, respectively, helps pressure the special walls and naturally faster Pokemon Eternatus struggles with.

  • In addition to requiring Meteor Beam to OHKO Pokemon such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal, Eternatus is deceptively weak without the Special Attack boost. As such, it is often important to position Eternatus to commit to wallbreak or sweep lest the one-time use of Power Herb go to waste. In the event Eternatus is forced out after using Meteor Beam without making meaningful progress, Eternatus becomes far less threatening and is largely relegated to late-game cleaning or revenge killing.

  • Despite being a powerful threat capable of brute forcing through many defensive staples, Meteor Beam Eternatus struggles considerably against stall due to its lack of longevity. Due to this, Eternatus should be paired with dedicated stallbreakers, wallbreakers, and teammates that otherwise fare better against such teams, such as offensive Yveltal with Knock Off, Chi-Yu, Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, Meteor Beam Lunala, and Kyurem-B. Additionally, Eternatus uniquely absorbs Toxic and Toxic Spikes from opposing defensive Eternatus.

  • Some common defensive checks to Eternatus include Calm Mind Arceus forms and Fezandipiti. Eternatus is additionally hard-walled by Chansey. Given this, Eternatus appreciates teammates that can punish them, such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM, and allies that can help overwhelm these shared checks such as wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, offensive Yveltal, and Meteor Beam Lunala.

Wallbreaker.description:
• Wallbreaker Eternatus is an immensely threatening wallbreaker, and not only maintains resiliency to passive damage that would wear down other offensive sets against bulkier teams but also lacks the passivity of defensive sets. This amalgamation of offensive and defensive traits provides valuable role compression for many bulky offense and balance teams, which appreciate Eternatus's consistency against both offensive and defensive playstyles.
  • Recover provides Eternatus immense flexibility relative to other offensive sets. Eternatus often finds turns to use Recover on the switches it forces or against more passive Pokemon that struggle to meaningfully damage it such as Ho-Oh, Ferrothorn, or Yveltal attempting to KO with Sucker Punch.
  • Meteor Beam provides Eternatus with the ability to easily remove Flying-types such as Ho-Oh and Yveltal. Meteor Beam also dissuades Pokemon that would otherwise switch into Eternatus such as Primal Kyogre or Primal Groudon, as they are unable to handle Eternatus's boosted attacks afterwards.
  • Fire Blast is used over Flamethrower for increased damage, notably OHKOing Zacian-C at +1 and being able to 2HKO defensive Necrozma-DM. Fire-type coverage is run to easily handle Steel-types and Pokemon that utilize Tera Steel that would wall or set up on Eternatus such as Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Giratina-O.
  • Tera Fairy is the primary Tera type used. It enables Eternatus to comfortably switch into specially offensive Yveltal and prevents it from being revenge killed by Ditto. Eternatus can also Terastallize in a pinch to remove its Ground weakness against Pokemon aiming to revenge kill it such as Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground. Eternatus's newfound Dragon immunity also helps against Giratina-O, Palkia-O, and opposing Eternatus.
  • Eternatus tends to enter the battle mid-game against defensive Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, utility Arceus-Fairy, and Ferrothorn. Eternatus can use these as an opportunity to boost, wallbreak, or both. It does not need to micromanage its health, as it often finds opportunities to use Recover against defensive Pokemon, so it is capable of sponging a hit beyond what is required in order to set up. Eternatus also has a great matchup into stall teams, as Chansey is often left with too little PP to stave off other special attackers such as Primal Kyogre after dealing with Eternatus thanks to Pressure.
  • Alomomola is a fantastic teammate for Eternatus thanks to its ability to provide a slow pivot into Pokemon that Eternatus can beat but is otherwise hesitant to switch directly into, such as Zygarde and defensive Eternatus. Zygarde is also an excellent partner for Eternatus, as it is the tier's best blanket physical wall to handle Pokemon such as Primal Groudon and Tera Blast Ground Zacian-C. Zygarde's paralysis support also enables Eternatus to easily revenge kill Pokemon such as Zacian-C and Ultra Necrozma with minimal risk.
  • Choice Band Marshadow can handle the few specially defensive Pokemon that Eternatus struggles with such as Calm Mind Arceus formes and defensive Primal Kyogre. Zacian-C is another option, which handles Calm Mind Arceus formes that can otherwise use Eternatus for setup fodder.

Defensive.description:
• Defensive Eternatus stands out as a top-tier defensive staple, as it is able to completely wall Arceus-Dark, is immune to Toxic, and can simultaneously serve as one of the few Knock Off absorbers in the tier. Its Speed tier allows it to outpace Arceus formes and Marshadow while maintaining enough bulk to withstand hits and provide a soft check against threats like Ho-Oh and Primal Kyogre. Moreover, Pressure enables Eternatus to PP stall moves like Water Spout from Primal Kyogre, Judgment from Arceus-Fairy, Sacred Fire and Defog from Ho-Oh, and Dynamax Cannon from opposing Eternatus. Finally, its capability to spread status adds another layer of utility, making Eternatus a premier choice for balanced team compositions.
  • Toxic Spikes in conjunction with Pressure gives Eternatus a distinct advantage in breaking opposing teams, thanks to its ability to set entry hazards and PP stall Defog from prevalent Defoggers like Ho-Oh and Giratina-O. Toxic serves as a potent tool for gradually wearing down Pokemon such as Calm Mind Primal Kyogre without Rest, Yveltal, and Arceus. Additionally, it ensures gradual damage against defensive Arceus formes lacking Refresh, Primal Groudon, and Ho-Oh.
  • Sludge Bomb finds its primary utility in targeting Arceus-Fairy. Additionally, it offers the potential to poison Pokemon that are immune to Toxic Spikes, notably Ho-Oh and Giratina-O, which would otherwise clear entry hazards against Eternatus.
  • Flamethrower acts as a countermeasure against Steel-types, such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM, that would attempt to take advantage of Eternatus, since they are immune to being poisoned. Alternatively, Mystical Fire serves a similar purpose by punishing Steel-types while also limiting Calm Mind Arceus formes. However, it's important to note that Mystical Fire's damage output is weaker than Flamethrower, and as a result, Mystical Fire fails to secure a 2HKO against Zacian-C after Stealth Rock. Flamethrower is also favored as a tool against Necrozma-DM, since it has the potential to inflict a burn, rendering Mystical Fire less effective.
  • Combining Toxic with Toxic Spikes forms another viable strategy that affects all prevalent Defoggers immune to Toxic Spikes, making it easier to maintain entry hazards throughout the match. However, relying solely on these moves without coverage options can leave Eternatus vulnerable against Steel-types like Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Ferrothorn.
  • Leftovers is the preferred item to help Eternatus handle burns from Ho-Oh and mitigate the damage from attacks such as Ice Beam from Primal Kyogre and most attacks from Marshadow. Heavy-Duty Boots serves as a good alternative to avoid entry hazard damage, particularly if the team lacks Defoggers.
  • Eternatus's EV spread enables it to outspeed a fully invested Yveltal while not being 2HKOed by specially offensive Yveltal's Dark Pulse and Choice Band Marshadow's Spectral Thief. An EV spread of 80 HP / 252 SpD / 176 Spe with a Timid nature makes it possible for Eternatus to outspeed fully invested Arceus formes while still not be 2HKOed by specially offensive Yveltal's Dark Pulse at the cost of physical bulk. An alternative spread of 40 HP / 252 Def / 216 Spe, which is faster than Marshadow, can deal with physical threats such as Ho-Oh, Marshadow, and Arceus. However, another dedicated wall is necessary to check specially offensive threats like Primal Kyogre and Arceus-Fairy.
  • Tera Fairy enhances Eternatus's capability against Palkia-O, Life Orb Yveltal, Giratina-O, and Calm Mind Arceus-Dark, while Tera Water improves Eternatus's matchup against Necrozma-DM, Primal Groudon, and Arceus-Ground.
  • Eternatus should freely switch into Yveltal and Ho-Oh lacking Thunder Wave and aim to set up Toxic Spikes to threaten Primal Groudon and defensive Arceus formes. It's best to reserve Terastallization as a last resort, since it compromises Eternatus's valuable Toxic immunity.
  • Ho-Oh synergizes well with Eternatus, especially in the presence of Toxic Spikes, as it can phaze foes with Whirlwind and provides an immunity to Ground. Arceus-Dark is another good partner since it can deal with Necrozma-DM, which is immune to Toxic, and Mega Mewtwo Y.
  • Zygarde-C is another excellent choice as a teammate, offering the ability to safely switch in against Primal Groudon and Marshadow. Additionally, a specially defensive Zygarde-C can utilize Glare against opposing Eternatus, ensuring that it maintains the speed advantage. Giratina is another valuable teammate that is capable of dealing with Primal Groudon. It also has Pressure, which significantly enhances the PP stall strategy when paired with Eternatus.
  • When utilizing physically defensive Eternatus, it's crucial to include another Primal Kyogre check on the team, such as Primal Groudon, Ferrothorn, or Chansey. Ferrothorn can offer valuable entry hazard support by setting up Spikes and Stealth Rock, and it appreciates Eternatus switching in to handle Ho-Oh. Additionally, Chansey can effectively handle most special attackers and use Heal Bell to cure eventual paralysis on Eternatus, further increasing Eternatus's longevity throughout the match.

Choice Specs.description:
• Choice Specs Eternatus serves as a more specialized variant that aims to fully capitalize on its offensive potential as a wallbreaker with ample opportunity to outpace and cleave through prominent defensive cores over the course of a game. It successfully combines the unresisted coverage of the Power Herb variants and packs more immediate power while lacking the recoil of Life Orb, giving it a distinct niche.

  • The ability to include Sludge Bomb is one of this set's most appealing traits, giving Eternatus a strong secondary STAB move to heavily threaten Tera Fairy Zygarde, IronPress Garganacl, and Arceus-Fairy. Additionally, its poison chance can prove vital in overpowering the likes of setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Arceus-Dark and defensive pivots such as Ho-Oh, which can otherwise outheal the damage dished out.

  • Fire Blast provides important coverage against Steel-types such as Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM, and Ferrothorn. It is used over Flamethrower due to its higher Base Power that allows Eternatus to OHKO Zacian-C.

  • The secondary option of Draco Meteor serves as another major draw behind this set. The immediate power offered by Draco Meteor allows Eternatus to KO important targets that Dynamax Cannon would otherwise come up short against, such as weakened Ho-Oh, Calm Mind Arceus formes and Alomomola, freeing it from the need to Terastallize against them. Being able to outright remove these Pokemon at designated HP thresholds, rather than letting them hang on by a thread, can mean the difference between their continued persistence and permanently removing them to the benefit of Eternatus's teammates later in the match.

  • Alternatively, Toxic Spikes allows Eternatus to take advantage of its ability to force switches to lay down entry hazards to support its teammates, which can be especially useful for crippling setup sweepers such as Dragon Dance Zygarde, Swords Dance Arceus, and Calm Mind Arceus formes even when Eternatus is not on the field, but is more situational as the presence of common Poison-types like other Eternatus, Fezandipiti and Tera Poison Calm Mind Arceus formes limit its usability.

  • Tera Dragon strengthens Eternatus's already strong Dynamax Cannon and Draco Meteor, notably allowing Dynamax Cannon to consistently 2HKO Arceus-Dark through a Calm Mind boost, defensive Primal Kyogre, and Ho-Oh, while allowing Draco Meteor to OHKO maximum HP Arceus formes after Stealth Rock, defensive Primal Groudon, and Tera Water Zygarde before Power Construct. It also crucially removes Eternatus's Ground-type weakness, allowing it to survive hits from Primal Groudon in a pinch. However, Eternatus will lose its ability to absorb Toxic Spikes and Toxic.

  • Choice Specs Eternatus fits best on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its ability to act as a strong wallbreaker with some additional defensive utility via absorbing poison from defensive pivots such as Alomomola. It also serves as an offensive check to other offensive threats such as Marshadow and Life Orb Yveltal.

  • While Eternatus is an effective wallbreaker against opposing bulky offense and balance teams commonly featuring the likes of Primal Groudon, Arceus formes, and Terastallized Zygarde, it tends to struggle the most against extreme playstyles such as hyper offense and stall. Hyper offense teams can overwhelm Eternatus with setup sweepers such as Dragon Dance Ultra Necrozma, Dragon Dance Necrozma DM, and Zacian-C that take advantage of it being Choice-locked, while stall teams tend to pack Pokemon that hard wall it such as Chansey.

  • Eternatus's ability to break open defensive cores is best complemented by setup sweepers that appreciate the gaping holes it tends to leave behind; the likes of Zacian-C and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground fit well on more offensive teams, while Coil Zygarde benefits similarly on more balanced structures. In return, these Pokemon can greatly assist with more offensive teams that might give Eternatus trouble wallbreaking, such as against hyper offense structures loaded with miscellaneous offensive threats such as Dragon Dance Mega Salamence and Rock Polish Primal Groudon that can outspeed and OHKO Eternatus after setting up.

  • Eternatus greatly detests the presence of entry hazards such as Stealth Rock and Spikes, which are set by common Pokemon such as Primal Groudon and Ferrothorn and heavily cut into its longevity. Teammates that can help manage these factors consist of Defog users such as Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Mega Salamence, which can reliably remove these conditions throughout the match. In return, Eternatus helps break past defensive Pokemon that these partners can otherwise struggle with long term, such as Zygarde, defensive Primal Groudon, Garganacl, and Alomomola.

  • Additional options against Sticky Web are mandatory in particular due to how they entirely ruin Eternatus's ability to wallbreak by compromising its Speed tier to where it is unable to handle the likes of Chi-Yu, Yveltal, and Lunala on the archetype. As a result, anti-lead Pokemon such as Dragon Dance Zygarde and defensive Primal Kyogre are excellent for their ability to punish the most common Sticky Web setter in Smeargle, while additional support from revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Yveltal and Extreme Killer Arceus that aren't affected by Sticky Web can assist Eternatus with picking off several of the aforementioned offensive Pokemon mid-game.

  • Without proper prediction, Eternatus has trouble breaking through teams that carry multiple Pokemon with appropriate resistances to its moves such as Zacian-C, Fezandipiti, and Arceus-Ground, which can take advantage of it being Choice-locked when paired with pivots like Ho-Oh that can safely scout it. As such, checks such as defensive Primal Groudon, defensive Primal Kyogre, and Ho-Oh are necessary to provide a safety net against these Pokemon and minimize the degree to which Eternatus is punished. Zacian-C in particular is a notable threat, as it is fully immune to both of Eternatus's STAB types and can both outspeed and set up Swords Dance against it. As a result, Eternatus also occasionally appreciates being paired with revenge killers such as Ditto and Choice Scarf Yveltal.

  • Lastly, as Eternatus prefers not to directly switch into targets such as offensive Ho-Oh, Arceus-Dark, and Giratina-O, which can often cripple it with status, pivots such as defensive Yveltal, Landorus-T, and Alomomola are strong teammates that can help Eternatus get onto the field safely against these Pokemon. Yveltal can cripple several of Eternatus's switch-ins such as Chansey and Ho-Oh with Knock Off and Taunt, while Alomomola can use Wish to compensate for Eternatus's lack of recovery and susceptibility to being worn down throughout a match.

  • Secondary pivots to Calm Mind Arceus formes are also notable, as after a Calm Mind boost, Arceus-Dark and Arceus-Fairy will be able to outheal the damage Eternatus can dish out and commonly run Tera Poison to gain an immunity to poison; Choice Band Marshadow forms an effective offensive pairing with Eternatus and can force these Pokemon out with Spectral Thief's ability to steal boosts, while Ho-Oh can safely switch into and apply pressure to these Pokemon with status from Sacred Fire and Thunder Wave.

Shuca Berry.description:
• Shuca Berry Eternatus fully maximizes its poison-spreading potential, being able to use Toxic and set Toxic Spikes on Primal Groudon and Arceus-Ground with relative safety after luring them in. Shuca Berry also comes with the added benefit of letting Eternatus check Choice Band Marshadow much more effectively, as once it is used, Poltergeist will be unable to hit it. This set still performs defensive Eternatus’ s standard roles effectively as a check to foes such as Calm Mind Arceus sets lacking Refresh and Yveltal, but it can struggle long term against Arceus-Fairy and Life Orb Yveltal due to being prone to being worn down without Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots. Furthermore, as it is unable to use both Dynamax Cannon and Flamethrower, it can be used as setup fodder for Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM, or opposing Eterrnatus depending on its choice.
  • With Shuca Berry, Eternatus can safely stay in on Ground-types like Primal Groudon and use Toxic against it, and it also is key to pressuring Ho-Oh and defensive Arceus sets, letting Eternatus constantly set Toxic Spikes against them. Toxic also allows Eternatus to wear down Calm Mind Primal Kyogre and Zygarde, forcing them to use Rest more frequently. Toxic Spikes lets Eternatus put pressure on defensive Arceus formes, Primal Groudon, and Primal Kyogre, wearing them down and enabling its teammates to break through them more easily.
  • Dynamax Cannon lets Eternatus directly hit Ground-types like Primal Groudon, Arceus-Ground, and Ho-Oh, and it most importantly dissuades opposing Eternatus from switching in and absorbing its Toxic Spikes. Flamethrower can be used if Necrozma-DM and Zacian-C are an issue to the team but makes the set less effective overall due to the lack of a STAB option, as it is harder to pressure Ho-Oh and Zygarde.
  • The given EV spread allows Eternatus to avoid the 2HKO from Zygarde’s Thousand Arrows with Shuca Berry, avoid the 2HKO from Life Orb Yveltal’s Dark Pulse, and outspeed specially offensive Yveltal.
  • Tera Fairy lets Eternatus take Dragon-type attacks from opposing Eternatus and Palkia-O while also being an all-around great defensive type that turns its former Ground and Psychic weaknesses into neutralities and keeps its Fighting resistance against Marshadow.
  • Shuca Berry Eternatus works best early- to mid-game, as if it can lure Primal Groudon or Arceus-Ground with Toxic, it can start putting a lot of pressure on the opposing team. Using its item early is also the best case scenario when fighting a Marshadow so it can pivot into it without worry. Hard switching in Eternatus is often discouraged, as it can lose its Shuca Berry and be KOed after without being able to use Toxic or Dynamax Cannon. Toxic Spikes can easily be set up, as Eternatus can pressure all Defoggers by way of Toxic and Dynamax Cannon.
  • This set works best on balance and bulky offense structures that appreciate Eternatus spreading poison on Ho-Oh and Primal Groudon, greatly cutting into their longevity.
  • Shuca Berry Eternatus works best with teammates that greatly appreciate Ground-types being poisoned or KOed, such as Calm Mind Arceus-Water, Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy, and offensive Primal Groudon. Eternatus is easily worn down by entry hazards, so teammates that can remove them like Ho-Oh, Yveltal, and Giratina-O are great partners. Eternatus must be paired with good Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM checks if running Dynamax Cannon, so defensive Primal Groudon and Zygarde-C are good teammates. If running Flamethrower, then teams must have a way to pressure or take advantage of opposing Eternatus such as Choice Band Marshadow or offensive Yveltal.

Life Orb.description:
• Life Orb Eternatus is a niche offensive variant that trades its longevity and ability to soft check foes like Marshadow and Primal Kyogre to instead enhance its offensive capabilities. Its biggest draw lies in the immediate and dependable power boost granted to its attacks, allowing Eternatus to wallbreak multiple times throughout a game without relying on the two-turn nature of Meteor Beam. Its ability to harass bulky structures while also sporting a decent matchup against hyper offense makes it a worthwhile addition to balance and bulky offense teams alike.
  • Dynamax Cannon is Eternatus’s STAB move of choice, with consistent damage output to net crucial 2HKOs against many defensive targets. This allows Eternatus to pressure foes such as Primal Groudon, Yveltal, and Zygarde; after one layer of Spikes, opposing Eternatus and support Arceus formes are brought into OHKO and 2HKO range respectively.
  • Sludge Bomb threatens Arceus-Fairy with major damage while crippling targets with its valuable poison chance, making switch-ins such as Ho-Oh unable to stave off repeated blows long-term. If such targets are well-handled by its teammates, Toxic Spikes can instead be used to punish switches by setting grounded threats like Lunala, Primal Groudon, and Primal Kyogre on a timer.
  • Fire Blast decimates Steel-types attempting to switch into its STAB moves, notably OHKOing Zacian-C and 2HKOing defensive Necrozma-DM after a layer of Spikes, while blasting apart Ferrothorn without the need for entry hazards.
  • Recover takes advantage of forced switches to reliably heal Eternatus from chip damage and Life Orb recoil, allowing it to switch out and remain healthy enough to wallbreak at a later point in the match.
  • Tera Dragon launches Dynamax Cannon to new heights, letting Eternatus 2HKO Ho-Oh, Primal Kyogre, and Tera Water or Poison Zygarde as well as OHKOing most offensive Primal Groudon variants after Stealth Rock. Tera Dragon secondarily sheds crucial weaknesses to Ground and Psychic, allowing Eternatus to take on threats such as Arceus-Ground, Primal Groudon, and an unboosted Ultra Necrozma at the cost of becoming vulnerable to Toxic.
  • Tera Fire is an alternative that boosts its coverage, letting Eternatus more easily dispatch Zacian-C and offensive Necrozma-DM with a nuclear Fire Blast. Defensively, Tera Fire improves the matchup against Fairy- and Ice-types, allowing Eternatus to better check a boosted Arceus-Fairy and Choice-locked Chien-Pao as well as dodging Sacred Fire burns from Ho-Oh in a pinch, at the expense of a newfound weakness to Stealth Rock.
  • Eternatus functions well as an early- to mid-game wallbreaker as well as a cleaner owing to its excellent Speed and offensive presence. However, its inability to safely switch into Poltergeist and Knock Off users in addition to demanding careful HP management due to Life Orb recoil means Eternatus appreciates pivoting support from offensive and defensive allies alike to find opportunities to safely enter the battle; therefore, Pokemon such as Yveltal, Mega Latios, and Alomomola synergize well with it.
  • Eternatus appreciates allies that can set hazards to facilitate its wallbreaking, making teammates such as Primal Groudon, Arceus-Water, and Ferrothorn excellent partners; the former two pressure Defoggers like Ho-Oh and Yveltal with the threat of status moves and super effective coverage, while the latter punishes support Arceus formes and Giratina-O with Leech Seed.
  • This set struggles against stall teams due to its low-PP moves as well as Life Orb recoil inevitably forfeiting momentum to use Recover, so teammates such as Choice Band Rayquaza and Overheat Primal Groudon help Eternatus in overwhelming special walls like Chansey and Ho-Oh, while Eternatus threatens Dondozo and Arceus-Dark in return. Rayquaza is a particularly useful ally due to its access to U-turn, allowing Eternatus to safely enter the field and wreak havoc.

Cosmic Power.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • EV Spread" The given EV spread outspeeds Jolly Urshifu formes and Timid Chi-Yu.

Offensive.description:
Offensive Eternatus leverages its amazing Special Attack and Speed to form devastating offensive cores with the receivers of those two stats. After boosting its Special Attack with Meteor Beam, Eternatus can tear through weakened teams with its strong STAB combination and good coverage. Dynamax Cannon is a reliable STAB move that will deal great damage to most neutral targets. Sludge Bomb hits Fairy-types such as Clefable, Primarina, and Arceus-Fairy, which are immune to Dynamax Cannon. Fire Blast is super effective against Steel-types like Necrozma-DM, Excadrill, and Iron Treads, which resist Eternatus's STAB moves. Meteor Beam offers super effective coverage against various Fire- and Flying-types and gives Eternatus a power boost for the rest of its moves. Tera Dragon allows Eternatus to survive Earthquake from the likes of defensive Great Tusk and defensive Landorus-T and boosts the power of Dynamax Cannon, allowing it to OHKO the Urshifu formes and 2HKO offensive Great Tusk that received a base Special Defense stat up to 130 at +0. Alternatively, Tera Fire allows Fire Blast to OHKO the aforementioned Steel-types after a Meteor Beam boost. A set with Life Orb and Recover over Meteor Beam offers Eternatus more longevity compared to Power Herb sets. Power Herb sets, however, allow Eternatus to use Meteor Beam immediately without taking damage from Life Orb, but Eternatus can only do this once before switching out.

Eternatus has one of the highest Speed stats of any god in the metagame, making it a great donor for receivers like Urshifu-S and Landorus-T, which all give special walls a hard time. Eternatus also possesses exceptional Special Attack, which is great for fast attackers like Hisuian Electrode and Greninja or setup sweepers like Nasty Plot Landorus and Calm Mind Comfey, which, in tandem with Eternatus, can overwhelm special walls. Eternatus also possesses a massive HP stat, which can be utilized to great effect by defensive teammates like Rotom-W, Skarmory, and Sinistcha. Setup sweepers like Iron Defense Zamazenta, Calm Mind Iron Crown, and Nasty Plot Darkrai can also use the extra HP to set up more easily. Eternatus struggles to break through walls that can weather its STAB moves and don't care about Fire Blast such as Ting-Lu, Heatran, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowking, so teammates that pressure these Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, as well as the aforementioned Landorus-T and Urshifu-S, are extremely appreciated. Finally, Eternatus appreciates entry hazards from the likes of Great Tusk, Skarmory, and Landorus-T to help it get KOs more easily.

Defensive.description:
With amazing stats, strong attacks, utility moves, and a useful defensive typing, Eternatus can be the cornerstone of a difficult-to-break defensive team without entirely sacrificing a team's offensive presence. Even uninvested, its base 145 Special Attack provides meaningful damage when paired with STAB moves. Toxic Spikes provide an advantage to Eternatus's team by limiting a lot of defensive counterplay to its offensive teammates or necessitating turns spent removing the entry hazard, while Recover allows it to extend its longevity significantly. The EVs maximize Eternatus's ability to move ahead of most Pokemon without a Speed donation. HP is maximized to avoid problems with Stealth Rock after Knock Off, allowing Eternatus to reliably take hits on both sides of the damage binary without necessarily specializing in one or the other. The remaining EVs are put in Special Attack to increase damage ever so slightly. Heavy-Duty Boots and Tera Ghost serve much of the same defensive purpose, with the former allowing Eternatus to reliably switch in and out without worrying about entry hazards and the latter allowing it to change its defensive profile while preventing Rapid Spin from removing its Toxic Spikes. Black Sludge and Toxic are not joined at the hip in the same way; the former allows Eternatus to stay in for longer, while the latter provides a more direct way for Eternatus to disrupt foes.

Eternatus should be placed in the Attack slot and paired with Pokemon that can enable a more defensive playstyle while retaining one or two options for more aggressive plays. Defensive Pokemon like Zamazenta, Rotom-Wash, and Skarmory appreciate an HP donation, while Hydrapple, Gholdengo, and even Urshifu-R appreciate Eternatus's great Speed. Base 95 in Defense and Special Defense is average compared to other gods; however, it can be used by Pokemon such as Clefable and Great Tusk to shore up a weaker defensive stat. Pokemon that can get Eternatus in safely via pivoting, such as Rotom-Wash and Corviknight, reduce the amount that Eternatus needs to heal throughout the game. Gholdengo stops removal of Toxic Spikes entirely, though Ground-types can put pressure on absorbers of Toxic Spikes, ensuring Eternatus doesn't waste turns setting them up. Finally, Steel-types serve as a major roadblock to Eternatus's ability to deal damage, so teammates like both Landorus formes and the Urshifu formes can provide additional damage output while covering that deficiency, while Electric-types can handle Skarmory and Corviknight.

Eternatus is a premier defensive staple in the tier due to its solid typing, excellent bulk, and useful utility options. It consistently checks prominent Extreme Speed users, including Altarianite Regieleki, Dragonite, Hisuian Arcanine, and Entei, as well as other physical wallbreakers like Urshifu-R and Zamazenta. Both its STAB moves, Sludge Bomb and Dynamax Cannon, are highly spammable and devastating; the former, in particular, threatens Altarianite users and applies pressure to defensive foes with its high poison chance. Eternatus uses Flamethrower to avoid being completely walled by Steel-types like Magearna, Corviknight, Kingambit, and Aggronite or Rusted Sword Zamazenta. It can also choose Toxic over one of its STAB moves to immediately pressure defensive threats and setup sweepers like various Arceus formes, Ho-Oh, and non-Sablenite variants of Garganacl, Alomomola, and Mandibuzz. Alternatively, Toxic Spikes helps spread poison on foes and limits common VoltTurn cores such as Urshifu-R + Raging Bolt; however, it is heavily countered by Magic Bounce users. Rocky Helmet is the preferred item for punishing most physical attackers, especially Urshifu-R when it uses Surging Strikes. Heavy-Duty Boots is a reasonable choice to prevent entry hazard chip damage on Eternatus, while Black Sludge offers some passive recovery. The Speed EVs enable Eternatus to outspeed Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk and bulky variants of the Arceus formes. Eternatus fits well on bulky offense and balance teams. Specially defensive partners like Magearna, Ho-Oh, and Garganacl create strong cores with Eternatus; Magearna benefits from its ability to check Fire-types like Entei and Hisuian Arcanine, while Ho-Oh and Garganacl rely on it to handle Urshifu-R. Non-Heavy-Duty Boots variants are susceptible to hazards and greatly benefit from hazard removers like Great Tusk, Regieleki, Mandibuzz, and Corviknight. Hazard setters like Garganacl, Magearna, Clodsire, and Great Tusk, combined with Eternatus's own chip damage, effectively wear down multiple threats such as Urshifu-R, Hisuian Arcanine, Zamazenta, and the Arceus formes. Ground-type checks, such as Ho-Oh, Arceus-Water, and Milotic, are valuable teammates for covering one of Eternatus's biggest weaknesses. Ho-Oh can also threaten Magearna, which is one of Eternatus's biggest checks. Eternatus pairs well with teammates such as Urshifu-R, Raging Bolt, and Zamazenta by providing them with free switches against Pixilate Extreme Speed users.

Life Orb.description: Life Orb Eternatus is one of the strongest special wallbreakers in the metagame, taking advantage of its incredible damage output and movepool to punish defensive staples such as Milotic, Magearna, and Pecharunt. Fire Blast is its strongest option against Steel-types like Magearna and Iron Crown, though it can instead opt to run the weaker but more accurate alternative in Flamethrower. Recover helps Eternatus mitigate Life Orb chip damage, improving its longevity. Eternatus fits well on bulky offense and balance archetypes. It synergizes extremely well with other offensive pieces like Urshifu-R, Zamazenta, and Spectrier, forming deadly offensive cores that can overwhelm common defensive foes like Magearna, Pecharunt, and Arceus formes. Eternatus appreciates entry hazard setters to aid it in wallbreaking, making Pokemon like Magearna, Hisuian Samurott, and Great Tusk stellar teammates, as even a single layer of Spikes can let Dynamax Cannon 2HKO bulky targets like Arceus-Ground. Eternatus gets worn down fairly easily by Life Orb recoil and hazards, so it heavily appreciates teammates that remove hazards such as Regieleki and the aforementioned Great Tusk as well as Sablenite users like Garganacl and Milotic. Arceus formes like Arceus-Ghost, Arceus-Fairy, and Arceus-Water also make excellent partners, helping to handle potential revenge killers such as Iron Crown and Extreme Speed users while posing major threats themselves with Calm Mind.

Eternatus has solidified itself as the premier special attacker in the Ubers tier. Eternatus thrives on its exceptional bulk, great typing, and consistent damage output, allowing it to adapt to many team compositions. A Timid nature mainly helps Eternatus to keep its Speed advantage against most foes except Koraidon and Deoxys-A, while Modest secures critical KOes such as Fire Blast OHKOing Zacian-C and Dynamax Cannon having a 70% chance to 2HKO maximum HP Kyogre. Not only does Sludge Bomb threaten lethal damage to Arceus-Fairy, but it also pressures passive checks like Ho-Oh and Blissey by threatening poison, which drains their recovery PP and enables Eternatus to win prolonged encounters. Tera Dragon amplifies Dynamax Cannon, enabling feats like 2HKOing physically defensive Ho-Oh and 3HKOing Ting-Lu. It is best suited for wallbreaking, as it offers minimal defensive utility aside from removing its Psychic and Ground weaknesses. Tera Fire, on the other hand, grants STAB on Fire Blast and eliminates its Dragon and Psychic weaknesses, which is crucial against Koraidon, Mewtwo, and opposing Eternatus. It also lets Eternatus resist Steel and Fairy-type attacks, easing pressure against Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM.

Eternatus's versatility lets it thrive on diverse array of team structures. On hyper offense, it serves as a durable pivot that pressures teams early with Life Orb-boosted attacks and Recover, which stalls out their attacking PP and opens them up to other special attacking teammates. On balance or bulky teams, it acts as a late-game sweeper, supported by entry hazards and status to wear down foes. Its ability to absorb Toxic Spikes is invaluable for teammates like the Arceus formes and Koraidon. Notably, Koraidon's sun support enhances Fire Blast's potency, while Eternatus's resistances to Fire and Water aid Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM in handling Ho-Oh and pivoting into Kyogre, though caution is advised against Kyogre, as it 2HKOes Eternatus with Choice Scarf Water Spout or negates its Speed advantage through Thunder Wave. Special attackers like Arceus with Judgment and Mewtwo appreciate Eternatus overwhelming shared checks such as Blissey, Ho-Oh, and Ting-Lu. Eternatus's combination of raw power, status-spreading utility, and unmatched bulk makes it a nightmare for defensive teams, especially with the low PP of recovery moves and absence of cleric support in the tier. Pressure synergizes seamlessly with Recover, enabling it to stall out the moves of foes over time.

anythinggoes.overview: Eternatus is a versatile Pokemon that is mostly used on passive balance and bulky offense teams due to its access to Toxic and Toxic Spikes. Thanks to its unique typing and great defensive stats, it is a reliable answer to Kyogre, Ho-Oh, Arceus-Water, and Arceus-Fairy and can absorb Toxic Spikes set by opposing Glimmora, Eternatus, and Gliscor. With the lack of good entry hazard control options and Poison-types, it can also quickly wear down opposing teams, often forcing them to use Tera Poison to remove Toxic Spikes. However, it is weak to other Dragon-types such as Miraidon and Koraidon because they can outspeed and OHKO it, and it typically struggles with Steel-types such as Zacian-C and Necrozma-DM, which can easily set up on it if it's lacking a Fire-type attack. Additionally, other strong physical attackers such as Calyrex-I and Arceus-Ground can force Eternatus out with their super effective STAB moves, so a lot of defensive support is necessary when running it.
anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Life Orb Eternatus can be a decent wallbreaker, but it is easily chipped down by the combination of recoil from Life Orb and entry hazard damage, and despite running Life Orb, it's unable to do good damage to Ting-Lu. Reflect can be used in conjunction with Toxic to allow Eternatus to beat Ting-Lu, offensive Ho-Oh, and Extreme Killer Arceus one-on-one, and it can also help Eternatus's teammates take hits better. Other attacks like Sludge Bomb to threaten Hatterene and Arceus-Fairy and Shadow Ball to more immediately threaten Calyrex-S can also be used. Haban Berry + Draco Meteor can also be helpful to let Eternatus survive an Outrage or Draco Meteor from Koraidon or Miraidon and OHKO it back without any investment, but this leaves Eternatus vulnerable to Spikes. Dragon Tail can be used to phaze anything that tries setting up on Eternatus like Tera Poison Calm Mind Kyogre or Arceus-Fairy. Fire Spin is sometimes used to trap walls such as Blissey and bulky Arceus formes as well as Kyogre Choice-locked into a move like Ice Beam against Tera Steel Eternatus, but both Dragon Tail and Fire Spin are incredibly niche options, as they do not get many opportunities to be used. Most of the aforementioned options also require dropping Toxic Spikes, which is much more valuable in most scenarios.

Checks and Counters

Tera Poison Users: Tera Poison on Ting-Lu and defensive Arceus formes gives them an immunity to Toxic and Toxic Spikes, making it difficult to spread poison and break through teams, as they remove Toxic Spikes and take very little damage from Dynamax Cannon. Calm Mind Kyogre likes to run Tera Poison in conjunction with Thunder Wave to use Eternatus as setup fodder. Calm Mind Arceus-Fairy can similarly turn Eternatus into setup fodder by running this Tera type.

Steel-types: Without Fire Blast or Flamethrower, Eternatus is walled by Steel-types such as Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM, and Kingambit, as they take little to no damage from Dynamax Cannon and are immune to poison.

Dragon-types: Faster Dragon-types like Miraidon and Koraidon can easily threaten and force out Eternatus with their powerful Dragon-type attacks but are unable to safely switch into it.

Ground-type Coverage: Earthquake from offensive Ho-Oh, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, and Ting-Lu as well as Ground-type Judgment from the aforementioned Arceus-Ground can threaten Eternatus for large amounts of damage and force it out.

Calyrex-S: Calyrex-S can threatren Eternatus with its powerful Psychic-type attacks or lock it into Toxic Spikes or Recover with Encore and can threaten to sweep if not dealt with properly.

Calyrex-I: Calyrex-I can OHKO Eternatus with Glacial Lance and become extremely threatening if it sets up Trick Room.

Hatterene: Hatterene is able to completely wall Eternatus by blocking status moves, bouncing back Toxic Spikes, and being immune to Dynamax Cannon; it can also paralyze Eternatus with Nuzzle but must be wary of coverage like Sludge Bomb or sun-boosted Fire-type attacks.

Specially Defensive.description:
Eternatus is an excellent blanket check to Kyogre, defensive Ho-Oh, Arceus-Water, and Arceus-Fairy that pressures opposing teams with Toxic Spikes and Toxic. Toxic Spikes is one of Eternatus's greatest assets, as it weakens the opposing defensive core and especially overwhelms hyper offense teams because it quickly chips down their sweepers due to them not having a way to remove it. Fire Blast or Flamethrower can be used instead to threaten Steel-types such as Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM, and Kingambit, with the former guaranteeing a 2HKO on Zacian-C and having a chance to OHKO it in sun and the latter providing more consistent damage at the cost of reduced firepower. However, this means dropping Toxic Spikes, which makes spreading poison much more difficult. Dynamax Cannon is Eternatus's preferred STAB move, but Draco Meteor can be run instead, trading consistency for the ability to OHKO both Koraidon and Miraidon. The given EV spread allows Eternatus to outspeed maximum Speed Kyogre and survive offensive Arceus-Ground's Earthquake from full HP. Tera Fairy allows Eternatus it to block Miraidon's Draco Meteor and Koraidon's Scale Shot or Outrage in an emergency but makes it more vulnerable to Steel-type attacks from Zacian-C and Kingambit and Flare Blitz from Koraidon. Tera Steel gives it valuable resistances to Kyogre's Ice Beam, Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance, Arceus's Extreme Speed, Arceus-Fairy's Judgment, and Psychic-type moves from Calyrex-S. Although, using Tera Steel makes Eternatus weak to Fire-type attacks such as Flare Blitz and Sacred Fire from Koraidon and Ho-Oh, respectively, as well as Koraidon's Low Kick and Zacian-C's Close Combat. Tera Dark is another option, albeit niche, that may be used to improve a team's matchup against Calyrex-S, but it makes Eternatus weak to Arceus-Fairy's Judgment and Koraidon's Low Kick. All three Tera types also reduce Eternatus's ability to check Kyogre and Ho-Oh, so the user must be wary before committing to Terastallizing.

Eternatus fits on more passive balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to act as both a Toxic Spikes absorber and spreader that can take on threats like Kyogre, Ho-Oh, Arceus-Water, and Arceus-Fairy. Koraidon and Miraidon are both excellent partners, as the former can threaten Steel-type Pokemon, and the latter helps to break bulky Ground-types such as Ting-Lu and Arceus-Ground. In return, Eternatus helps check Kyogre and puts their checks, such as bulky Arceus formes and Ting-Lu, on a timer with poison. They both also appreciate Eternatus's ability to soak up status effects, and Koraidon in particular enjoys Eternatus reliably switching into defensive Arceus formes like Arceus-Fairy and Ho-Oh. Eternatus is vulnerable to Koraidon and Miraidon, which force it out with strong Dragon-type attacks, so Pokemon that can check them such as Ho-Oh, Arceus-Fairy, and Ting-Lu also make good teammates. Ting-Lu also helps Eternatus by switching into Calyrex-S, which can deal massive damage to Eternatus with its Psychic-type moves or lock it into Toxic Spikes or Recover via Encore. If Eternatus isn't running Fire Blast or Flamethrower, it is incapable of hitting Steel-types like Zacian-C, Necrozma-DM, and Kingambit, so Ground-types that force them out like Arceus-Ground and Landorus-T are also recommended. Arceus-Water can check the aforementioned Steel-types and Koraidon, as well as switching into Calyrex-I, Arceus-Ground, and Extreme Killer Arceus. Arceus helps to check Calyrex-S and benefits from Eternatus weakening the opposing defensive structure so it can clean up late-game. Eternatus also struggles with Hatterene, as it blocks Toxic and Toxic Spikes and is immune to Dynamax Cannon, so Pokemon that can beat Hatterene like Ho-Oh and Arceus-Ground are appreciated. Although, Fire Blast under sun can 2HKO Hatterene. Setup sweepers like Scale Shot Koraidon, Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground, and Swords Dance Zacian-C can easily force Eternatus out and set up on it, so reliable checks to them like defensive Arceus-Fairy and Arceus-Water are recommended.

Glass Cannon.description:
Set Details

  • Urshifu-S utilizes its STAB attacks to threaten Restricted Pokemon like Calyrex-S, Calyrex-I, and Terapagos alongside other metagame staples like Chien-Pao, Ursaluna, and Chi-Yu.
  • Focus Sash allows Urshifu-S to take two attacks before it is KOed to maximize its on-field presence. Covert Cloak provides Urshifu-S with a strong matchup against Calyrex-S and Terapagos team compositions featuring dual Fake Out cores.
  • Covert Cloak sets use an EV spread of 132 HP / 236 Atk / 4 Def / 76 SpD / 60 Spe with and Adamant nature. This spread is designed to let Urshifu-S survive at least two Astral Barrages from Life Orb-boosted Calyrex-S and outrun maximum Speed Incineroar, with the remainder of the EVs invested into Attack and Defense.
  • Tera Stellar guarantees Urshifu-S's Wicked Blow OHKOes Lunala through Shadow Shield.

Teambuilding

  • Urshifu-S struggles to sufficiently damage Tera Fairy foes such as Miraidon, Lunala, and Raging Bolt, as well as being threatened by Fairy-type attacks like Dazzling Gleam from Miraidon, Moonblast from Lunala and Flutter Mane, and Play Rough from Zacian-C.
  • Fighting-type attacks are problematic for Urshifu-S. Koraidon and Zamazenta-C outspeed and easily KO Urshifu-S with Collision Course and Body Press after its Focus Sash has been broken. Meanwhile, Urshifu-R and Iron Hands can survive Urshifu-S's attacks and KO it in return with Close Combat and Drain Punch, respectively.
  • Incineroar is threatening, since Urshifu-S struggles to remove it before its damage output is hindered by Intimidate and Will-O-Wisp.
  • A partner Miraidon threatens opposing Miraidon, Raging Bolt, and Koraidon with Draco Meteor and Dazzling Gleam, as well as dealing good damage with Electro Drift to them and Incineroar after they Terastallize.
  • Calyrex-I survives Electro Drift, Draco Meteor, and Thunderbolt from Miraidon and Raging Bolt and easily KOes them alongside Koraidon with Glacial Lance. Urshifu-S returns the favor by checking Calyrex-I's threats like Lunala and Calyrex-S with Wicked Blow and Sucker Punch.
  • Landorus can easily threaten Miraidon, Raging Bolt, and Incineroar with Earth Power and Sandsear Storm in addition to threatening Tera Fairy users with Sludge Bomb. Meanwhile, Urshifu-S threatens the foes that can attack before Landorus or survive its onslaught like Calyrex-S and Lunala.
  • Amoonguss pairs well with Urshifu-S, comfortably surviving and redirecting Fairy- and Fighting-type attacks for it on top of disrupting foes with Spore.

Choice Band.description:
Set Details

  • Choice Band Urshifu-S uses Wicked Blow to reliably OHKO foes like Calyrex-I, Lunala, Volcarona, and Farigiraf while maintaining its naturally good matchups against Calyrex-S and Indeedee-F.
  • With Close Combat, Urshifu-S is able to threaten KOs on Incineroar, Ursaluna, and even Defense Protosynthesis-boosted Brute Bonnet.
  • U-turn allows Urshifu-S to pivot out in situations that may not be favorable for it while doing significant damage to Brute Bonnet and Indeedee-F. Additionally, U-turn can be used to play around defensive Terastallization from Pokemon like Calyrex-I, Lunala, and Farigiraf.
  • While Choice Band does have the obvious downside of locking Urshifu-S into a move, its newfound ability to OHKO Calyrex-I and Lunala with Wicked Blow, alongside its generally higher damage output, allows it to be much more threatening.
  • Urshifu-S should use either a Brave Nature with 252 HP and Attack EVs or an Adamant Nature with 252 Attack and Speed EVs depending on if it is being used on a team that focuses on Trick Room or not. Trick Room teams should run 0 IVs in Speed, while teams not utilizing Trick Room should use 31 IVs in Speed.
  • Tera Grass is the most common Tera type, as it allows Urshifu-S to avoid Rage Powder and Spore from opposing Pokemon like Volcarona and Amoonguss, respectively.

Teambuilding

  • Choice Band Urshifu-S is weak to Fighting-types like Urshifu-R, Iron Hands, and Zamazenta-C, as they can all survive Urshifu's Close Combat and OHKO it back. However, Urshifu-S can OHKO Zamazenta-C with Close Combat if its Dauntless Shield boost is no longer active.
  • Choice Band Urshifu-S is also susceptible to opposing Pokemon's use of Terastallization, as Pokemon like Calyrex-I and Lunala can use a defensive Tera type to survive a hit from Urshifu-S. Lunala is especially scary for Urshifu-S in these scenarios, as it can sometimes run Tera Fairy and Moonblast to survive a hit and OHKO Urshifu-S in return.
  • Choice Band Urshifu-S is strongest on Trick Room teams that feature Restricted Pokemon like Lunala and Calyrex-I, as those teams can use it to threaten OHKOs on Pokemon like Calyrex-I, Calyrex-S, and Lunala. Lunala and Calyrex-I can assist Urshifu-S in return by setting up Trick Room and allowing it to move before Pokemon like Chi-Yu and Zamazenta-C.
  • Another good teammate for Urshifu-S is Indeedee-F, as it appreciates Urshifu-S's ability to threaten Ursaluna before Trick Room goes up. Indeedee-F supports Urshifu-S well by providing Trick Room and redirection, which both allow Urshifu-S to more effectively take KOs.

Offensive Sweeper.description:
Urshifu-S is used as a generally strong attacker, its Wicked Blow deals massive damage to much of the metagame and ignores Attack drops and Protect, minimizing counterplay. It is a versatile pick on many compositions, as its kit does not need much support and is mainly used to enhance a team's offensive pressure with strong attacks. With Tera Dark, Urshifu-S is capable of OHKOing Pokemon such as both Calyrex formes and Flutter Mane as well as bringing most other targets down to low HP, such as Miraidon and Tornadus. Focus Sash helps Urshifu-S remedy its poor defensive typing, while Sucker Punch is able to somewhat bypass Urshifu-S's middling Speed tier.

Urshifu-S functions well on many teams, but those with strong speed control are where Urshifu-S shines, particularly Trick Room compositions with Calyrex-I, which appreciate the immediate pressure. Trick Room lets Urshifu-S outspeed threats such as Flutter Mane and Zamazenta-C. Additionally, Unseen Fist ignoring Protect means that it is more risky for foes to attempt to stall out Trick Room turns. Urshifu-S struggles against Pokemon that resist Dark, such as opposing Incineroar and Urshifu, as they nullify Urshifu-S's main benefit in dealing big damage with Wicked Blow. While Close Combat is strong, it's less consistent because it doesnt bypass Intimidate and drops Urshifu-S's defenses. Additionally, many of these threats also outspeed and Urshifu-S for super effective damage, such as the Zamazenta-C and Urshifu-R. However, Pokemon like Amoonguss and Incineroar are able to somewhat make up for these weaknesses. Amoonguss provides redirection, resists Fairy and Fighting, and threatens foes with Spore, while Incineroar offers general utility and Fake Out, which foes can't block with Protect at risk of a attack from Urshifu-S. Tera Fairy is also a popular Tera type, used by foes like Raging Bolt and Calyrex-S, which are problematic for Urshifu-S as it cannot break through Tera Fairy users because they resist its STAB combination

Focus Sash.description:
• Close Combat hits common Dark-resistant Pokemon such as Incineroar and Kingambit. Sucker Punch provides priority and makes up for Urshifu-S's average Speed tier.

  • Urshifu-S uses Tera Dark to fire off strong Wicked Blows or Tera Stellar to boost the damage output of its STAB moves. Tera-boosted Close Combat OHKOes common Incineroar at -1 Attack, and both Tera types will allow Urshifu-S to OHKO Flutter Mane, provided its boost is still intact for Dark-type moves.

  • Focus Sash allows Urshifu-S to survive any one attack, making up for its poor defensive typing. In contrast to Choice items, it gives Urshifu-S the freedom to switch moves and use Detect when threatened, which is especially strong against Fake Out leads.

  • The extra EVs in Defense are to maximize Urshifu-S's chance of surviving a use of Surging Strikes from Tera Water Mystic Water Urshifu-R.

Choice Band.description:
• Choice Band is used to guarantee an OHKO on common targets like Landorus, Ogerpon-H, Flutter Mane, and even Tornadus that are not invested heavily in physical bulk. Even naturally bulky Pokemon such as Dragonite and Walking Wake can be OHKOed or put in the range for minimal damage to KO them.

  • Poison Jab is excellent coverage, hitting the problematic Fairy-types that Urshifu-S normally struggles with. After Terastallization, you can guarantee an OHKO on almost all Rillaboom, Terastallized Flutter mane, and even bulkier pokemon like Tera Fairy Indeedee-F. U-turn is also a viable move as a pivot option.

  • The Attack investment and Adamant nature are necessary to get the KOs mentioned earlier, such as the OHKO on Landorus and Tornadus. The Defense investment allows Urshifu-S to survive the combination of Tera Normal Choice Band Dragonite's Extreme Speed and Sucker Punch from Adamant Chien-Pao. The Special Defense EVs allow Urshifu-S to take a variety of strong attacks such as Earth Power from Landorus and Bleakwind Storm from Tornadus. The remaining EVs are placed in Speed.

  • Tera Poison is chosen to resist the Fighting- and Fairy-type moves that would otherwise hit Urshifu-S super effectively. Urshifu-S is naturally immune to Psychic and has Dark-type moves to cover for the weakness, and it also naturally threatens Psychic-types like Farigiraf. Tera Dark is also an option, as the extra damage combined with Choice Band is absurd and, combined with good Tailwind support and redirection, is a good choice. However, it requires more careful positioning around threats, as Urshifu-S won't be able to Terastallize out of it's Fairy- and Fighting-type weaknesses.

Assault Vest.description:
• Assault Vest helps Urshifu-S to survive special hits from Pokemon that it would usually struggle against, like defensive Iron Crown, Porygon-Z, and Volcarona.
  • Wicked Blow damages Iron Crown, Pecharunt, and Cresselia.
  • Close Combat hits non-Chople Berry Hisuian Goodra, both Ursaluna formes, and Porygon-Z.
  • Sucker Punch allows Urshifu-S to attack first against threats like Custap Berry Skeledirge and Spectrier in case it needs to do so.
  • Rock Tomb is utilized to have a mostly guaranteed matchup against Volcarona.
  • Counter helps against physically defensive Pokemon like Donphan; Urshifu-S can't deal much damage to them, but Counter helps it to mitigate this.
  • Its EV spread is designed so that it can always beat Porygon-Z. Its Speed EVs allow it to outspeed maximum Speed Choice Specs Porygon-Z, while its Special Defense investment enables it to survive a Hyper Beam from Modest Choice Scarf variants. The remaining EVs are invested into Attack.
  • Urshifu-S struggles heavily against Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Sylveon. Due to this, Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon like Scizor and Iron Moth make for good partners.

Chople Berry.description:
• Urshifu-S can utilize the Chople Berry to maximize its overall bulk, allowing it to survive non-STAB Fighting-type attacks from the likes of Darkrai, Iron Crown, and Ursaluna.
  • Sucker Punch can be utilized to hit Pokemon like Moonblast Cresselia and Custap Berry Hoopa-U.
  • Bulk Up is used as a tool for Pokemon that use Defense-boosting moves like Manaphy, which is usually difficult to break through without the move, while the Defense increase helps Urshifu-S take hits from Ursaluna.
  • The EVs allow Urshifu-S to outspeed Modest Hoopa-U and survive a Choice Specs Focus Blast from it as well as an unboosted Close Combat from Adamant Haxorus.
  • Fighting- and Fairy-type Pokemon like Iron Hands, Sneasler, and Sylveon are still quite rough for Urshifu-S to handle, so Pokemon like Pecharunt and Metagross are quite useful for Urshifu-S to have as teammates.
  • Despite the bulk investment, it's still difficult for Urshifu-S to handle common special attackers like Primarina and Raging Bolt, so specially bulky Pokemon like Florges and Hisuian Goodra can also be nice teammates

Dancing Bear.description:
• After boosting its power through Swords Dance, Urshifu-S can leverage its complementary set of STAB moves to smash through the opposing team.

  • Close Combat versus Drain Punch: Close Combat offers Urshifu-S the maximum sweeping power. However, if using Focus Sash or a defensive Tera type, Drain Punch is handy for restoring enough health after a boost to prevent priority attacks from easily knocking Urshifu-S out.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash can help Urshifu-S more reliably get off a Swords Dance boost. It can survive hits from Fairy-types like Flutter Mane as well as powerful special attackers like Iron Bundle. With an Adamant nature, Urshifu-S can reliably beat offensive Tera Fairy Flutter Mane with Wicked Blow + Sucker Punch, provided Focus Sash is still intact.

  • Black Glasses versus Punching Glove: Both items boost the power of Urshifu-S's signature move, Wicked Blow. Black Glasses gives a slightly stronger boost, while Punching Glove helps to protect Urshifu-S from contact effects like Rocky Helmet and Zapdos's Static. Urshifu-S is much less vulnerable to these effects compared to Urshifu-R due to lack of a multi-hit move. Finally, despite the name, Punching Glove does not boost the power of Sucker Punch, while Black Glasses does.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Typically, Urshifu-S will utilize Terastallization offensively to bolster the power of its Dark-type moves, but this set can benefit more from a defensive Tera type in order to stay on the field longer and make use of its ability to switch moves, which the Choice-locked attacker set cannot.

  • Dark: Tera Dark strengthens Wicked Blow and allows Urshifu-S to power its way through opposing walls. After a Swords Dance boost, Tera Dark-boosted Wicked Blow is a guaranteed OHKO on physically defensive Zapdos, while Close Combat has a high chance to OHKO Ting-Lu.

  • Poison: This Tera type allows Urshifu-S to survive common Fairy-type and Fighting-type attacks that would otherwise threaten to KO Urshifu-S.

  • Ghost: For Focus Sash sets, Tera Ghost blocks Normal-type priority from the likes of Dragonite, Ogerpon formes, or Entei from picking Urshifu-S off.

One Punch!.description:
• Urshifu-S can punch holes in the opposing team with its strong combination of STAB moves. Additionally, Urshifu-S can benefit from team preview against opponents who mistakenly assume it to be Urshifu-R.

  • U-turn: This move allows Urshifu-S to pivot out of bad matchups and scout out potential Tera types.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head can cover opposing Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Mimikyu, which threaten Urshifu-S.

  • Poison Jab: Poison Jab is Urshifu-S's strongest option against Primarina and the rare Azumarill.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Generally, Urshifu-S will utilize Terastallization offensively in order to extend the reach of its signature move Wicked Blow.

  • Dark: Tera Dark allows Urshifu-S to supercharge its Wicked Blow and muscle its way past various physically defensive foes. Notably, it gives Choice Band Urshifu-S a high chance to 2HKO Dondozo through Leftovers recovery, giving Urshifu-S an advantage against many stall teams.

  • Poison: This is a defensive Tera type that removes Fairy-type and Fighting-type weaknesses, and also absorbs Toxic Spikes.

  • Steel: This Tera type allows Urshifu-S to resist Fairy-type attacks and additionally boosts the power of Iron Head.

Choice Band (Spe).description:
Choice Band Urshifu-S is a potent offensive wallbreaker with an excellent STAB combination against the metagame. With a Speed donation, Urshifu-S is able to threaten out a lot of frail Pokemon that it wouldn't otherwise. Urshifu-S can choose to inherit in the Attack slot, becoming far stronger, but it prefers the Speed slot because it is relatively slow, it already has high Attack, and Attack-inheriting sets are more awkward to fit onto teams. In terms of moves, Wicked Blow and Close Combat are mandatory. U-turn allows Urshifu-S to generate momentum off the many switches it can force. Poison Jab is great at threatening Fairy-types such as physically defensive Clefable and Primarina, while Sucker Punch is a viable alternative to provide speed control in a pinch, and it is preferred when inheriting from gods slower than Eternatus. Tera Dark is preferred to further boost damage on Wicked Blow and Sucker Punch, allowing Urshifu-S to OHKO fully invested Arceus-Ghost. Tera Poison boosts Poison Jab to achieve a 2HKO on Arceus-Fairy and Clefable with base 115 Defense and it is a good defensive Tera for Urshifu-S. Finally, Tera Fighting boosts the damage of Close Combat.

Zacian-C and Eternatus are excellent gods for Urshifu-S to inherit from. Zacian-C appreciates having a strong offensive wallbreaking partner to overwhelm shared checks such as Clodsire and Skarmory, while Eternatus provides Urshifu-S with a partner that can inherit great Special Attack such as Hisuian Electrode or Landorus, taking advantage of the physically defensive walls Urshifu-S invites in and being a solid progress maker itself. Finally, Arceus is rarely a bad choice of a god, and Urshifu-S fits comfortably onto Arceus structures as a fast wallbreaker. Urshifu-S is quite frail, so it appreciates having solid defensive pieces, like Clodsire and Skarmory, to swap into powerful attacks it cannot take itself—especially Fairy-type attacks. Pokemon like Landorus-T, Pecharunt, and Rotom-W can bring Urshifu-S in safely by forming a VoltTurn core with it so it doesn't have to worry about using its middling bulk to hit the field. These three in particular can take on Zacian-C and Zamazenta, two Pokemon Urshifu-S cannot usually beat. Urshifu-S also likes to be paired with physical attackers that can clean easily, like Sneasler, that benefit greatly from the holes it punches in the opposing team. Finally, entry hazard support from the likes of Hisuian Samurott, Great Tusk, Glimmora, and so forth isn't necessarily mandatory but helps Urshifu-S secure key rolls against walls, such as HP-inheriting Skarmory and physically defensive Primarina.

Choice Band.description:
• Surging Strikes deals with Landorus-T, Skeledirge, and Volcarona.
  • Close Combat targets Assault Vest Urshifu-S, non-Choice Scarf Porygon-Z, non-Choice Scarf Kyurem, and Registeel.
  • Iron Head is for non-Life Orb Alolan Ninetales, since Urshifu-R can get past Encore + Disable variants by ignoring Protect.
  • Poison Jab is for Whimsicott and non-bulky Primarina.
  • Thunder Punch 2HKOes opposing Urshifu-R without having to drop Urshifu-R's Defense with Close Combat.
  • Against Ursaluna and Ursaluna-B, Surging Strikes is the best option, since both can carry Chople Berry.
  • Since Urshifu-R struggles against Psychic- and Fairy-type Pokemon like Metagross, Iron Crown, and Iron Valiant, Pokemon such as Meowscarada, Volcanion, and Volcarona make for good teammates.

IronPress.description:
• The IronPress combination allows Urshifu-R to wall Pokemon it otherwise wouldn't be able to handle, like Metagross, while also dealing with common physical stalwarts like Ursaluna and Registeel.
  • Surging Strikes hits Volcarona, Landorus-T, and Rhyperior.
  • Taunt can be used to prevent foes like Registeel and non-Brave Bird Corviknight from setting up or using recovery moves.
  • Sitrus Berry allows Urshifu-R to usually survive two Psychic Fangs from Choice Band Metagross after an Iron Defense boost so it can respond with two +2 Body Press in return.
  • Urshifu-R can struggle with Grass- and Electric-type Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Zapdos, and as a result, partners like Raging Bolt are recommended.
  • Urshifu-R can struggle against special attackers like Spectrier and Porygon-Z due to its poor Special Defense, so Pokemon like Hisuian Goodra and Assault Vest Ursaluna can make for good partners.

Choice Band (Water).description:
With a Choice Band, Urshifu-R becomes a devastating wallbreaker for Water teams, easily able to blow past threats like Ting-Lu and Mandibuzz without requiring setup. Close Combat shreds the likes of Archaludon, Kyurem, and Hisuian Samurott. Surging Strikes easily washes away foes such as Ceruledge and Gliscor along with 2HKOing Iron Hands and Clefable, which can often prove infurating for Water teams to handle. Ice Spinner nails Grass- and Dragon-types that attempt to come in on Urshifu-R's STAB moves like Sinistcha and Dragonite. Alternatively, U-turn can be used to keep up momentum. Finally, Aqua Jet can let Urshifu-R clean up against faster threats like Flutter Mane and Volcarona. Jolly is the recommended nature to allow Urshifu-R to outspeed the likes of Terapagos and Kyurem, while Adamant lets it reliably OHKO threats such as Ting-Lu and Archaludon and consistently 2HKO Corviknight and Mandibuzz.

Urshifu-R greatly appreciates Swampert thanks to it pivoting Urshifu-R in safely with Flip Turn, providing Stealth Rock support to chip would-be checks like Meowscarada and Dragapult, using Knock Off to remove Skarmory's Rocky Helmet, and checking Electric-types such as Raging Bolt and Sandy Shocks. Toxapex can assist Urshifu-R by taking on Fairy- and Grass-types like Enamorus and Meowscarada on top of providing Toxic support to wear down bulkier targets like Araquanid and Primarina. Choice Scarf Greninja provides vital speed control, enabling it to check fast Psychic- and Ghost-types such as Latios, Latias, and non-Choice Scarf Spectrier with Dark Pulse, alongside using coverage moves such as Sludge Wave to deal with the Ogerpon formes and Enamorus. Swords Dance Hisuian Samurott provides Spikes support with Ceaseless Edge to wear down foes like Raging Bolt, along with being able to check threats such as Dragapult with Sucker Punch. Calm Mind Primarina can check annoying foes for Urshifu-R like Walking Wake while greatly appreciating Urshifu-R handling Steel-types such as Empoleon and Hisuian Goodra, which Primarina cannot. Nasty Plot Rotom-W provides a nice immunity to Ground that can help against Flying- and Water-types that threaten Urshifu-R such as Tornadus-T, Pelipper, and Primarina. Alternatively, Rotom-W can pivot Urshifu-R in with Volt Switch.

Choice Scarf (Fighting).description:
Choice Scarf Urshifu-R is a solid option for Fighting teams wanting speed control with great offense thanks to its nice coverage options. Urshifu-R is a potent force to reckon with in matchups like Dragon and Flying, where its direct competitors, Keldeo and Choice Scarf Sneasler, would struggle to make progress. Reaching a respectable 483 Speed, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R outspeeds the whole unboosted metagame, barring Regieleki and Deoxys-S, as well as some common Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Kleavor, and Hoopa-U. Surging Strikes OHKOes Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Hisuian Zoroark, Choice Scarf Hoopa-U, and Focus Sash Ceruledge. Close Combat destroys Dark- and Steel-types such as Choice Specs Greninja and Choice Scarf Archaludon. U-turn lets it pivot out safely against its checks like Toxapex and Primarina. Lastly, Ice Spinner deals with Dragon-types such as Dragapult, Latios, and Dragonite and provides a safe option to hit Water Absorb Clodsire.

With numerous utility options such as Rapid Spin, Stealth Rock, and Knock Off, Great Tusk is a teammate of choice for Urshifu-R, preventing it from being injured by entry hazards and removing Choice Scarf from the likes of Landorus and Greninja, with the help of Focus Sash, to ensure Urshifu-R keeps the Speed advantage. Assault Vest Iron Hands and Gallade are two other solid partners that can withstand special hits from Choice Specs Latios and Dragapult for Urshifu-R ; they also significantly improve some of the tough matchups of Urshifu-R, namely Water and Poison, by dealing with Primarina, Toxapex, and Amoonguss. By virtue of its revenge killer status, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R pairs well with most Fighting-type wallbreakers, including Iron Valiant, Sneasler, Okidogi, and Scrafty. Iron Valiant leverages its fantastic movepool and offensive stats to patch any offensive shortcoming the team may have. Thanks to its access to BoltBeam coverage and highly synergetic STAB moves, Iron Valiant dominates the Flying, Dragon, and Water matchups, easily removing Skarmory, Defensive Gyarados, Latios, and Toxapex. Unburden Sneasler helps to get the upper hand in matchups like Fighting and Fairy, destroying both types after one Swords Dance. Lastly, Okidogi and Scrafty are two potent Bulk Up wallbreakers that can make the difference in the Ghost, Dragon, and Poison matchups. With its solid defensive typing and great bulk, Okidogi puts heavy pressure on Ghost teams, addressing the likes of Dragapult and Gholdengo while preventing Flutter Mane from making any progress, thanks to its Fairy neutrality. Its utility is also much appreciated in the Poison matchup where its typing lets it come repeatedly on the field to absorb Toxic and Toxic Spikes while threatening the opposing defensive core with Knock Off. Blessed with a Psychic immunity, Scrafty is a considerable asset in the Dragon and Ghost matchups where its immunity and resistances are useful by preventing Choice Specs Latios from progressing through Luster Purge spamming and leaving both Dragapult and Latios with Draco Meteor only to make progress.

Choice Scarf (Water).description:
With a Choice Scarf, Urshifu-R can act as a solid form of speed control for Water teams, being able to outspeed threats such as Tornadus-T, Choice Specs Flutter Mane, and Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott. Close Combat handles Steel- and Dark-types such as Archaludon and Choice Specs Greninja. U-turn allows for Urshifu-R to keep up momentum against would-be checks like Toxapex. Finally, Ice Spinner allows Urshifu-R to threaten Grass- and Dragon-types such as Hydrapple, Dragapult, and Dragonite. Alternatively, Poison Jab can be used to pick off Ogerpon-W and Fairy-types like Primarina.

Choice Specs Greninja and Urshifu-R form a devastating wallbreaking core, with Greninja being able to remove physical walls that hamper Urshifu-R such as Amoonguss, Skarmory, and Galarian Weezing with ease while Urshifu-R removes special walls that check Greninja such as Hisuian Goodra and Blissey. Greninja also provides a check to Psychic- and Ghost-type threats such as Latios and Sinistcha that could easily take Urshifu-R's attacks.
