Similarly, Swords Dance Hisuian Samurott can act as a check to Ghost- and Psychic-types along with providing Spikes with Ceaseless Edge and being able to use Sucker Punch to pick off faster targets like Choice Scarf Latias. Toxapex can handle Grass- and Fairy-types such as Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Hatterene and set Toxic Spikes to put bulky targets like Slowbro and Primarina on timers. Swampert can take on Electric-type threats such as Iron Hands, Sandy Shocks, and Regieleki. Swampert also provides support with Stealth Rock to wear down foes like Dragapult and Archaludon. Empoleon likewise can provide Stealth Rock support while dealing with threats such as Kyurem and Hatterene. Swampert and Empoleon can also both provide Urshifu-R safe entry with their slow Flip Turns. Pelipper provides rain, granting Urshifu-R the power boost to take out threats like Gholdengo, Zapdos, and Iron Valiant with Surging Strikes. Ogerpon-W appreciates Urshifu-R dealing with Tornadus-T and Lokix, and in return, Ogerpon-W can remove Water-types such as Primarina and Dondozo that would otherwise effortlessly wall Urshifu-R. Primarina provides a solid check to Dragon-type threats such as Archaludon and Walking Wake that naturally check Urshifu-R.

Swords Dance (Water).description:
Swords Dance Urshifu-R is a good choice on Water teams thanks to its high Attack - further boosted by Swords Dance - and decent Speed tier, allowing it to dispatch many of the metagame's defensive staples such as Unaware Clodsire, Alolan Muk, and Corviknight. Swords Dance allows Urshifu-R to set up on a predicted switch. Surging Strikes is a generally powerful move that allows Urshifu-R to muscle past threats such as Bulk Up Corviknight and defensive Gholdengo after a Swords Dance. Close Combat hits Dark- and Steel-types such as Hydreigon and Hisuian Goodra that try to switch in on Surging Strikes, while Drain Punch is weaker but provides some much-appreciated recovery. Finally, Urshifu-R has many viable options for its 4th moveslot; Aqua Jet deters Iron Valiant and Flutter Mane from attempting to revenge kill Urshifu-R, Thunder Punch hits Flying-types such as Pelipper as well as heavily damaging Toxapex, and Ice Punch hits Water Absorb Clodsire, Garchomp, and Flying-types such as Zapdos and Dragonite. Zen Headbutt can be run to damage Amoonguss and do well against Poison teams. Punching Glove allows Urshifu to gain a small boost to its punching moves while being protected from Zapdos's Static and other contact-punishing abilities.

Greninja and Hisuian Samurott are great teammates for Urshifu-R, as they take Psychic-type attacks such as Choice Scarf Indeedee's Psychic and Choice Band Hoopa-U's Zen Headbutt with impunity and punish them with Dark Pulse and Ceaseless Edge, respectively. Hisuian Samurott also sets Spikes to aid in Urshifu-R's wallbreaking efforts, while Greninja can threaten Fighting-types that Urshifu-R struggles with such as Choice Specs Iron Valiant and Sneasler with Extrasensory. In return, Urshifu-R can take Bug-type attacks such as Choice Band Scizor's U-turn and Choice Scarf Kleavor's X-Scissor, as well as threaten opposing Dark-types such as Weavile. Pelipper provides rain support to augment Urshifu-R's already scary wallbreaking abilities as well as a Grass neutrality to take Choice Scarf Meowscarada's Flower Trick. Toxapex and Quagsire take Fairy- and Electric-type attacks, respectively, while both wearing attackers down with Toxic. Toxapex also removes Toxic Spikes, which can put Urshifu-R on a timer. Gastrodon is an alternative Electric immunity, sacrificing physical bulk for a better specially defensive profile. Rotom-W does well in the Water mirror matchup, as well as doing good damage to Toxapex with Volt Switch. Additionally, it can create setup opportunities for Urshifu-R by burning physical attackers such as Dragonite and Great Tusk thanks to Will-O-Wisp. Barraskewda provides a good source of speed control as well as respectable power, while Basculegion-F is a good special attacker that can blow through common Urshifu-R checks such as physically defensive Toxapex and Quagsire. Both of these appreciate Urshifu-R breaking through their checks: Bulk Up Corviknight for Barraskewda and Gastrodon for Basculegion-F. Finally, Walking Wake can blow through defensive staples such as Toxapex, Rotom-W, and Amoonguss with Choice Specs-boosted Draco Meteors. In exchange, Urshifu-R takes care of Hisuian Goodra.

Swords Dance (Fighting).description:
Urshifu-R is a great wallbreaker on Fighting teams thanks to its deadly STAB combination, decent Speed tier, and access to Swords Dance, allowing it to be a good asset versus types like Poison, Water, and Fire. Close Combat is preferred due to its superior damage output; however, Drain Punch may be used instead for recovery and to ignore adverse contact effects thanks to Punching Glove. Aqua Jet threatens frailer revenge killers, taking out faster targets like Flutter Mane, Sandy Shocks, and Volcarona after a Swords Dance boost. Alternatively, Thunder Punch may be used to better deal with Azumarill, Pelipper, and Toxapex, while Zen Headbutt hits Amoonguss in addition to Toxapex and Clodsire. Surging Strikes notably deals with Landorus-T, Skeledirge, and Great Tusk as well as threatening Bulk Up Corviknight and Iron Defense Zamazenta. Other options include Ice Punch to hit Amoonguss while also threatening Dragon-types such as Dragonite and Dragapult and Taunt to prevent Toxapex, Quagsire, and Water Absorb Clodsire from using recovery moves as well as Toxic and Haze. Heavy-Duty Boots improves the matchup against hazard stacking teams like Poison; however, Punching Glove is preferred to use Surging Strikes freely without activating Rocky Helmet chip or Static, easing the Flying matchup and minimizing the need for predictions.

Great Tusk is an amazing teammate, providing Stealth Rock to enhance Urshifu-R's wallbreaking abilities and removing entry hazards with Rapid Spin if Urshifu-R isn't using Heavy-Duty Boots. Furthermore, Great Tusk deals with Toxapex if Urshifu-R isn't using coverage to hit it. Iron Hands provides a buffer in the Flying, Water, and Fairy matchup, threatening Corviknight, Pelipper, and Basculegion-F as well as hitting Flutter Mane, Hatterene, and Iron Valiant with Heavy Slam. Furthermore, Assault Vest Iron Hands acts as a great pivot into special attacks, as Urshifu-R's Special Defense is rather lackluster. In return, Urshifu-R deals with the Ground-types such as Great Tusk and Iron Treads along with Skeledirge. Sneasler is great in the Fairy matchup and provides pivoting and Toxic Spikes to accentuate Urshifu-R's wallbreaking potential. Zamazenta appreciates Urshifu-R heavily wearing down teams to allow it to easily clean up late-game with Iron Defense. Iron Valiant removes threats such as Hisuian Lilligant, Meowscarada, and Greninja while also being a huge asset in the Flying matchup thanks to Thunderbolt. Iron Valiant also values Urshifu-R's ability to break Clodsire and lure in Toxapex.

Choice Locked.description:
Set Details

  • Urshifu-R is one of the format's top offensive threats, thanks to its high Attack and strong STAB moves. Unseen Fist allows Urshifu-R to circumvent foes' Protect, which reduces the number of defensive plays the opponent can go for if you can position Urshifu-R correctly. Urshifu-R has especially strong matchups against Incineroar, Chi-Yu, Chien-Pao, and Terapagos.
  • U-turn allows Urshifu-R to reposition while dealing chip damage to threats such as Rillaboom. Aqua Jet allows Urshifu-R to pick off faster foes at low HP. Coaching can be used to boost the Attack and Defense of teammates, usually Calyrex-I. Rock Tomb is a more niche option that can be used for speed control, and it's especially appreciated by Calyrex-S in the mirror matchup.
  • Urshifu-R's Choice Scarf allows it to outspeed most of the metagame, most importantly Calyrex-S, ensuring it can get strong attacks off. Choice Band is a more niche option to boost Urshifu-R's damage output further, allowing it to 2HKO Calyrex-I with Surging Strikes or Close Combat.
  • The allocated bulk allows Urshifu-R to survive Incineroar's Fake Out into Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage, while the Attack investment allows Tera Water Choice Scarf Urshifu-R to OHKO most Calyrex-S.
  • Tera Water boosts the damage of Surging Strikes, which allows Choice Scarf Urshifu-R to OHKO most Calyrex-S. It also removes Urshifu-R's weakness to Psychic- and Fairy-type attacks. Tera Ghost gives an immunity to Fake Out as well as Zamazenta-C's Body Press and opposing Urshifu formes' Close Combat.

Teambuilding

  • Raging Bolt can OHKO Urshifu-R with its priority Thunderclap. Flutter Mane and Whimsicott also threaten to OHKO Urshifu-R with Moonblast, with the former outspeeding it and the latter resisting all its STAB attacks. Amoonguss can safely redirect all of Urshifu-R's attacks and potentially deal damage back with Rocky Helmet.
  • Koraidon's sun weakens the damage of Surging Strikes, while Life Orb Close Combat will OHKO Urshifu-R. Choice Specs Miraidon OHKOes Urshifu-R with any of its attacks.
  • Rillaboom and Incineroar's pivot moves allow Choice Scarf Urshifu-R to get in position safely. Strong speed control options such as Tornadus's Prankster Tailwind and Lunala's Trick Room can ensure Choice Band Urshifu-R is always moving first.
  • Tornadus's Bleakwind Storm and Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash threaten the Grass-types that are strong against Urshifu-R as well as Miraidon and Raging Bolt.
  • Kyogre and Pelipper set the rain to power up Urshifu's Surging Strikes as well as overriding Koraidon's sun. Calyrex-I benefits from Urshifu-R's Coaching, which allows Calyrex-I to better take on Koraidon and Groudon.

Glass Cannon.description:
Set Details

  • Urshifu-R serves as an offensive threat within the metagame, being able to raise the offensive pressure of the battle with its Unseen Fist ability deterring Protect while hitting hard with powerful STAB moves. It has a good matchup against Incineroar, as Surging Strikes does not get slowed down by Intimidate, as well as Flutter Mane, as Focus Sash allows Surging Strikes to reliably KO it.
  • Aqua Jet is a reliable priority move for finishing off low HP targets. Taunt cripples the supportive capabilities of Pokemon such as Amoonguss, Indeedee-F, and Grimmsnarl, as well as blocking Calyrex-I and Farigiraf from setting Trick Room up.
  • Focus Sash allows Urshifu-R to retaliate against certain Pokemon that would normally outspeed and OHKO it before Urshifu-R could attack, such as Calyrex-S and Flutter Mane.
  • Tera Stellar provides Urshifu-R offensive variety because it boosts Close Combat, allowing it to OHKO non-Defense Protosynthesis Brute Bonnet. However, since the boost is only provided one time to each attack, Tera Water could be preferred, as it consistently boosts the damage output of Surging Strikes, allowing it to OHKO Ursaluna, Chien-Pao, Ogerpon-C, and Calyrex-S after Life Orb chip damage while also removing its Psychic, Flying, and Fairy weaknesses to give it some survivability if Focus Sash is broken.

Teambuilding

  • Urshifu-R heavily struggles against Raging Bolt and Rillaboom, which easily threaten it with Thunderclap and Grassy Glide, respectively, and resist Surging Strikes. Amoonguss and Indeedee-F can disrupt Urshifu-R from attacking ideal targets via redirection and potentially break Urshifu-R's Focus Sash if they hold a Rocky Helmet. Indeedee-F's Psychic is able to KO Urshifu-R if Focus Sash is broken; Amoonguss notably takes pitiful damage, as it resists both of Urshifu-R's STAB moves, allowing it to easily put Urshifu-R to sleep with Spore.
  • Koraidon and Miraidon both outspeed and threaten Urshifu-R while resisting Surging Strikes. On top of this, Koraidon's sun reduces Surging Strikes's damage output, and Miraidon can pivot with Volt Switch while breaking Focus Sash easily.
  • Urshifu-R heavily appreciates Calyrex-I, which threatens Rillaboom, Amoonguss, Koraidon, Miraidon, and Raging Bolt with Glacial Lance, while Urshifu-R can, in return, threaten Dark-types such as Incineroar, Chi-Yu, and Chien-Pao that threaten Calyrex-I. Calyrex-I's Trick Room allows Urshifu-R to stay ahead of opposing Pokemon that would otherwise outspeed it, such as the aforementioned Miraidon and Koraidon.
  • Tornadus threatens the Grass-types such as Rillaboom and Amoonguss that annoy Urshifu-R and can Taunt the Amoonguss, preventing it from disrupting Urshifu-R. Tornadus can also remove Koraidon's sun with Rain Dance, decreasing Koraidon's damage output while increasing that of Urshifu-R's Water-type attacks. Tornadus's Bleakwind Storm paired with Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes forces Koraidon to take super effective damage whether it Terastallizes or not.
  • Urshifu-R complements Miraidon and Lunala compositions as a reliable attacker that counters Incineroar, a problematic threat to these compositions. Meanwhile, Urshifu-R's coverage against Dark-types also benefits Lunala; in exchange, Lunala's Moongeist Beam is threatening to Ghost-types like opposing Lunala. Miraidon's Draco Meteor can quickly remove the Dragon-types such as Raging Bolt and Koraidon that resists Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes.
  • Rillaboom and Incineroar work well with Urshifu-R, as Fake Out and pivoting moves create opportunities for Urshifu-R to safety switch in without breaking Focus Sash, and their typing allows them to tank moves that Urshifu-R would be threatened by, such as Wood Hammer from Rillaboom, Psychic from Calyrex-S, and Electro Drift from Miraidon. Incineroar also threatens sizable damage towards Psychic-types like Indeedee-F and Lunala with Knock Off. Rillaboom helps reduce Miraidon's damage output by removing Electric Terrain while also being able to threaten Fake Out.

Mystic Water.description:
Set Details

  • Mystic Water Urshifu-R is a highly versatile and offensive Pokemon that performs well against foes like Terapagos, Incineroar, and Chien-Pao by threatening them all with Surging Strikes and Close Combat.
  • Taunt prevents Trick Room from foes like Calyrex-I and Lunala, setup from Volcarona and Terapagos, and moves like Rage Powder and Spore from Pokemon like Volcarona and Amoonguss. Aqua Jet is also a great option to finish off weakened foes and deal chip damage before Urshifu-R faints.
  • Mystic Water gives Urshifu-R the ability to OHKO Pokemon it otherwise could not, such as Chien-Pao, Incineroar, and bulky Flutter Mane with Surging Strikes.
  • The EV spread lets it take Life Orb-boosted Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S, Life Orb-boosted Earth Power from Landorus, Horn Leech from Ogerpon-C, Sword of Ruin-boosted Body Press from Zamazenta-C, and Sword of Ruin-boosted Grassy Glide from Rillaboom. The Speed EVs let it outpace Pokemon like Miradon and Chien-Pao after a Speed drop.
  • Tera Water functions as both an offensive and defensive Tera type by removing its Psychic, Fairy, and Flying weaknesses while also boosting its Water-type moves to let Urshifu-R OHKO Calyrex-S and most Grimmsnarl with Surging Strikes as well as Chi-Yu with Aqua Jet.

Teambuilding

  • Urshifu-R struggles against Restricted Pokemon like Koraidon, which weakens Surging Strikes by setting sun. It also has a hard time versus Miraidon, which can outspeed and threaten an OHKO with Volt Switch or Electro Drift.
  • Non-Restricted Pokemon that can take Urshifu-R's attacks like Iron Hands, Raging Bolt, and Rillaboom, which also threaten Urshifu-R before and after Terastallization, are very effective against it as well. Amoonguss can redirect and easily survive Urshifu-R's attacks and punish Surging Strikes if Amoonguss is holding a Rocky Helmet. Ogerpon-H and -C pose an offensive threat to Urshifu-R with potential OHKOs using Wood Hammer or Power Whip.
  • Urshifu-R heavily benefits from Tailwind, making setters like Whimsicott and Tornadus great partners. Tornadus also provides Rain Dance to boost its Water-type attacks significantly, while Whimsicott can provide Light Screen support, which lets Urshifu-R survive attacks such as a Protosynthesis-boosted Thunderclap from Raging Bolt and Flutter Mane's Moonblast.
  • Miraidon is a strong Restricted partner for Urshifu-R, as it prevents Spore from Amoonguss and can threaten Water- and Dragon-type foes that Urshifu-R struggles to damage, like Koraidon and opposing Urshifu-R. Urshifu-R also supports Miraidon by helping against Ground-types like Ursaluna and Landorus.
  • Calyrex-I and Lunala are also strong Restricted partners for Urshifu-R because they can set Trick Room to provide another form of speed control. Calyrex-I also helps cover Miraidon by threatening it with powerful Ground- and Ghost-type coverage, while Urshifu-R supports them by checking Incineroar.
  • Kyogre benefits Urshifu-R by setting rain, increasing the power of its Water-type moves.
  • Chien-Pao boosts Urshifu-R’s attacks with Sword of Ruin, allowing it to OHKO Ogerpon-H with Surging Strikes while also threatening Miraidon, Raging Bolt, and Rillaboom with Ice Spinner or Icicle Crash.
  • Balance staples like Rillaboom and Incineroar also support Urshifu-R, as they can pivot into attacks Urshifu-R would rather avoid and provide Fake Out pressure that synergizes well with Unseen Fist.

Glass Cannon.description:
Urshifu-R is one of the strongest physical attackers in the format and can punish defensive plays with its ability Unseen Fist. It has a great matchup into Incineroar, since it ignores Intimidate with its signature move Surging Strikes, can switch into Chien-Pao and Calyrex-I, and is able to deal significant damage to Terapagos with Close Combat. Aqua Jet is almost unstoppable with Unseen Fist and can pick off Pokemon low on HP or deal damage before Urshifu-R gets KOed. Taunt gives it a much better matchup into Amoonguss, shutting it down almost completely, and it prevents Calyrex-I from setting up Trick Room. Focus Sash gives it more survivability and helps with its relatively low Special Defense. Tera Water allows Urshifu-R to deal incredibly high damage with Surging Strikes, allowing for an OHKO against common threats such as Flutter Mane and Chien-Pao through Focus Sash. Tera Stellar lets it OHKO Terapagos-S with Close Combat but loses the consistency of Tera Water, since Urshifu-R can no longer use boosted Surging Strikes repeatedly.

Urshifu-R works incredibly well in Calyrex-S teams, since it can threaten the Normal- and Dark-types that Calyrex-S struggles with, such as Terapagos and Incineroar. In exchange, Calyrex-S can deal with Raging Bolt, which is one of the most common checks to Urshifu-R, as Raging Bolt can use Thunderclap before Urshifu-R can move to bring it down to Focus Sash while also being able to switch-in on Surging Strikes. Urshifu-R synergizes well with Rillaboom and Incineroar, since Fake Out and Unseen Fist are a deadly combination, punishing passive plays such as Protect that try to avoid the flinching turn. Their typings also have incredible synergy with each other, allowing them to switch in on many attacks that Urshifu-R is threatened by. With its great physical bulk and natural type advantage, Rillaboom is a great check to it, slowing Urshifu-R down with Fake Out or doing high damage to it with Wood Hammer or Grassy Glide. Urshifu-R also struggles with Amoonguss, which is able to completely wall it while protecting its teammates with Rage Powder or putting it to sleep with Spore. Tornadus is a good partner for Urshifu-R, helping with its average Speed stat by setting up Tailwind, heavily increasing the damage Urshifu-R does while making the Koraidon matchup easier by using Rain Dance and threatening the Grass-types which could otherwise be problematic such as Amoonguss and Rillaboom with Bleakwind Storm. Koraidon and Miraidon are some of the Restricted Pokemon that have the best matchup into Urshifu-R, as Koraidon is able to set up sun and greatly reduce its damage, while Miraidon is able to outspeed it and bring it down to Focus Sash while also pivoting out with Volt Switch.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Urshifu-R is an excellent revenge killer and cleaner against many offensive Pokemon. The Choice Scarf lets Urshifu-R outspeed the dangerous Calyrex-S, meaning that the vast majority of offensive teams get naturally outsped and destroyed by its powerful Surging Strikes or Close Combat, and with Unseen Fist, these teams cannot even attempt to outplay it with Protect. U-turn lets Urshifu-R use the threat of its powerful attacks to pivot out, letting its team maintain momentum even when the opponent tries to switch around its attacks while also letting it 2HKO Ogerpon-W. Aqua Jet lets Urshifu-R bypass opposing speed control and priority moves when revenge killing an opposing threat, whereas Coaching makes partner Calyrex-I a significantly bigger threat. Tera Water powers up its Surging Strikes, letting it destroy foes like Calyrex-S. It also lets Urshifu-R shed its weaknesses to Psychic and Fairy, letting it potentially take attacks like Flutter Mane's Dazzling Gleam and Calyrex-S's Psychic-type moves. This set maximizes both Urshifu-R's Attack and Speed to make it as fast and strong as possible, but an EV spread of 60 HP / 156 Atk / 20 Def / 20 SpD / 252 Spe with an Adamant nature can be also used to survive Rillaboom's Grassy Glide and Mystic Water Kyogre's Water Spout.

Redirectors such as Rage Powder Amoonguss and Follow Me Ogerpon-W disrupt Urshifu-R very effectively, interfering with it attacking vulnerable targets. Rillaboom's Grassy Glide bypasses Urshifu-R's great Speed and threatens it with an OHKO. Miraidon and Raging Bolt both threaten Urshifu-R with their powerful Electro Drift and Thunderclap, respectively. Koraidon, Groudon, and even Tornadus can set up sun, weakening Surging Strikes so that Urshifu-R can be played around more easily. Additionally, a good way to subvert Urshifu-R's great Speed is with opposing speed control. Users include Tailwind Tornadus, Icy Wind Flutter Mane, and Trick Room Calyrex-I or Farigiraf. Urshifu-R's best partner is Tornadus, as it can support Urshifu-R with Tailwind to counter opposing speed control, Rain Dance to boost the power of Urshifu-R's Water-type STAB moves, and Bleakwind Storm to threaten opposing Grass-types like Rillaboom that would threaten Urshifu-R. It can also use Taunt to ensure that Amoonguss cannot use Spore or Rage Powder to disrupt Urshifu-R. Pelipper provides rain with its ability and has a STAB Flying-type attack in Hurricane to threaten Grass-types, and it can use Wide Guard to protect Urshifu-R from the variety of spread moves in the format, including Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S and Water Spout from Kyogre. It also can support Urshifu-R with Helping Hand. Amoonguss can handle Electric- and Grass-types that would threaten Urshifu-R by redirecting attacks away from it with Rage Powder. Urshifu-R forms a formidable pivoting core with Rillaboom and Incineroar, with the three spamming U-turn or Parting Shot to stay ahead of the opponent's switches, reactivate Fake Out, cycle Intimidate, and let Urshifu-R choose new moves to lock into. Incineroar helps take on opposing Rillaboom and Amoonguss for Urshifu-R, while Rillaboom deals with Kyogre and opposing Urshifu-R well and slows down Miraidon. Both of them can use Fake Out to prevent one of the opposing Pokemon from attacking, letting Urshifu-R attack the other without interference. Fake Out also often forces foes to use Protect, which Urshifu-R can attack through.

Bulky Attacker.description:
Urshifu-R is an excellent offensive Pokemon that can threaten metagame staples such as Incineroar, Chien-Pao, and Terapagos thanks to its fantastic typing and STAB moves, enabled by Unseen Fist. Taunt is utilized to shut down supportive Pokemon and Trick Room setters such as Amoonguss and Farigiraf as well as prevent Pokemon like Calm Mind Terapagos and Raging Bolt from setting up. Aqua Jet is a great alternative to get around Raging Bolt's Thunderclap and pick off weakened foes, which is especially useful, as Urshifu-R ignores Protect. Urshifu-R may opt for Swords Dance to become a deadly sweeper, allowing it to OHKO Rillaboom and, after Intimidate, Terapagos-S with Close Combat. Mystic Water boosts Urshifu-R's STAB moves without drawback and allows it to OHKO Incineroar through Sitrus Berry. Safety Goggles lets Urshifu-R ignore Amoonguss's Spore and Rage Powder, which is significant, as Amoonguss resists Urshifu-R's STAB moves; this also provides opportunities for Urshifu-R to set up. The given EV spread enables Urshifu-R to almost always OHKO Chien-Pao with Surging Strikes, survive Rillaboom's Miracle Seed-boosted Grassy Glide and almost always survive Raging Bolt's Thunderclap, and outspeed Pelipper and -1 Modest Miraidon. Tera Poison is the best defensive Tera as it provides key resistances to Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Rillaboom's Grassy Glide, as well as resisting Fighting-type moves from Zamazenta-C and opposing Urshifu. Tera Water still sheds Urshifu-R's weaknesses to Flutter Mane's Fairy-type STAB moves, Calyrex-S's Psyshock, and Pelipper's Hurricane, and greatly boosts its damage output, allowing it to 2HKO Calyrex-I with Surging Strikes and OHKO Chi-Yu with Aqua Jet once Terastallized.

Urshifu-R struggles against Rillaboom and Raging Bolt, which take its attacks exceptionally well and threaten it with strong priority STAB moves. Ogerpon-W is also an issue, as it can redirect Surging Strikes and is faster, allowing it to hit Urshifu-R for huge damage with Horn Leech. This makes Tornadus and Amoonguss great partners, as Tornadus can threaten the Grass-types, and Amoonguss can protect Urshifu-R from Raging Bolt with Rage Powder. Tornadus can also provide speed and weather control, making up for Urshifu-R's mediocre Speed tier and handling the otherwise problematic Koraidon, which can significantly weaken Urshifu-R with the sun it sets up. Taunt is another great tool that allows Tornadus to shut down Amoonguss for Urshifu-R. Urshifu-R can take on threats like Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu for the two in return. Alternatively, Rillaboom is an excellent pick, as it can pivot in Urshifu-R and threaten Ogerpon-W. Incineroar can pair with Urshifu-R and either Amoonguss or Rillaboom to create a fantastic pivot core, switching in on threats like Rillaboom. Rillaboom and Incineroar also bring Fake Out, which synergises with Unseen Fist. Urshifu-R is also a great asset to Calyrex-S, as it has the ability to remove Ghost-resistant foes like Incineroar and Terapagos.

Damage-Boosting Item.description:
• Boosting Urshifu-R's damage allows it to pick up KOs it couldn't do otherwise, such as Chien-Pao, no-bulk Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-C, and other Pokemon defensively trained to survive Urshifu-R's non-boosted attacks, such as Sitrus Berry or physically bulky Incineroar, with Surging Strikes.

  • Aqua Jet gives Urshifu-R access to priority, which allows it to pick off low HP foes.

  • Life Orb allows Urshifu-R to OHKO Archaludon and non-bulky Ogerpon-W. It also boosts Surging Strikes's damage rolls, allowing you to KO Pokemon defensively trained to survive Mystic Water Surging Strikes, such as Bold Flutter Mane, Defense-invested Chien-Pao and Ogerpon-H, though this comes at the cost of Urshifu-R's longevity.

  • The Attack investment allows for Urshifu-R to OHKO Chien-Pao with Surging Strikes. The allocated bulk allows Urshifu-R to survive a Thunderclap from most Assault Vest Raging Bolt, an Earth Power from most Landorus, or a Terrain-boosted Grassy Glide from Ogerpon-H. The Speed investment allows Urshifu-R to outspeed Modest Regidrago and Adamant Dragonite.

  • Tera Water is strong both defensively and offensively, allowing Urshifu-R to remove its Fighting-type to survive moves such as Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Tornadus's Bleakwind Storm. The boost to Surging Strikes can allow Urshifu-R to KO Pokemon it otherwise couldn't, such as Bold Flutter Mane and bulky Ogerpon-H. Tera Steel allows Urshifu-R to flip its matchup against Farigiraf, Flutter Mane, and Rillaboom. The Normal-type resistance is also useful against Extreme Speed Dragonite and can be used in a pinch against both Ursaluna formes. Tera Fire has some similar properties to Tera Steel but can also flip Urshifu-R's matchup against Ogerpon-H and give Urshifu-R immunity to burn. Both Tera Steel and Tera Fire make Urshifu-R weak to opposing Urshifu-R, with Close Combat and Surging Strikes respectively.

Focus Sash.description:
• Focus Sash allows Urshifu-R to be played much more aggressively in front of threats like Raging Bolt, Rillaboom, and the Ogerpon formes, due to the guaranteed survival from one attack.

  • Taunt is sometimes used over Aqua Jet in order to shut down threats like Amoonguss and prevent Trick Room.

  • Focus Sash allows Urshifu-R to simply maximize its Attack and Speed.

  • Tera Stellar may be used instead of Tera Water, giving Urshifu-R a damage boost to Close Combat that allows it to OHKO non-bulky Ogerpon-W while still boosting Surging Strikes and Aqua Jet. Tera Stellar does, however, prevent multiple Water-type moves from being boosted. These boosts enable Urshifu-R to OHKO Chien-Pao and bulkless Ogerpon-C and Ogerpon-H with Surging Strikes.

Choice Band (Water).description: Choice Band Urshifu-R is a strong wallbreaker on Water teams, taking on bulky foes like Ferrothorn, Archaludon, Kyurem, and Mandibuzz. Aqua Jet is a strong priority option to pick off faster albeit weakened sweepers and cleaners such as Ceruledge and Sneasler. Thunder Punch targets Water- and Flying-types like Toxapex, Pelipper, and Mantine, while Ice Spinner handles Dragon- and Ground-types such as Dragonite and Clodsire. However, Aqua Jet is preferred, since it stops opposing sweepers and cleaners in their tracks to enable its teammates to sweep or clean late-game. U-turn allows Urshifu-R to pivot out of unfavorable matchups, such as against Mantine and Dragonite, and bring a teammate in to deal with them. Pelipper is not only neutral to Grass, but it also sets up rain to boost Urshifu-R's Water-type STAB attacks, turning it into a potential late-game cleaner with rain-boosted Aqua Jet. It notably has a good chance of OHKOing Alolan Raichu with Aqua Jet under rain, and rain further makes Surging Strikes harder to switch into. Additionally, Pelipper removes entry hazards with Defog and pivots it in safely with U-turn. Swift Swim users such as Mega Swampert and Barraskewda thus make for great teammates as well, as they appreciate Urshifu-R's wallbreaking so they can clean late-game. Mega Swampert also provides an Electric immunity to deal with the likes of Tapu Koko, Regieleki, and Zeraora. Toxapex and Empoleon are great defensive partners due to their part-Poison and part-Steel typings, respectively, that allow them to take on Fairy-types such as Mega Diancie and Alolan Ninetales, which Urshifu-R dislikes. Additionally, they can stack entry hazards with Toxic Spikes and Stealth Rock, respectively, to aid Urshifu-R in wallbreaking, and Toxapex also removes boosts from setup sweepers with Haze. Greninja forms a strong wallbreaking duo with Urshifu-R, with it taking on the likes of Sinistcha, the Ogerpon formes, and non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant for Urshifu-R, while it appreciates the removal of Ferrothorn and Empoleon in return. Ogerpon-W eases the Ground matchup thanks to its resistance, handling the Landorus formes and Garchomp in the process.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Urshifu-R is a good late-game cleaner and revenge killer due to its ability to threaten defensive Pokemon like Heatran, Gliscor, Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Ferrothorn with its powerful STAB moves. It also sports a great Speed stat, allowing it to outspeed the majority of the unboosted metagame, including Mega Lopunny and Zamazenta. Surging Strikes's guaranteed critical hit chance means Urshifu-R ignores the Attack drop from Landorus-T's Intimidate and the Defense boost from Zamazenta's Dauntless Shield. U-turn helps Urshifu-R to keep up momentum throughout the course of a game, and also take advantage of defensive switch-ins like Toxapex and Alomomola for its teammates to set up on. Aqua Jet allows Urshifu-R to pick up KOs on Pokemon that are at low HP but outspeed it, like Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant and Unburden Hawlucha. Ice Spinner is a great tool in assuring high damage on important targets like Dragonite and Mega Latios.

Urshifu-R is a great choice on more balance-oriented teams as the speed control option, and it loves the company of teammates like Landorus-T, which helps Urshifu-R by setting up Stealth Rock and forming a good pivoting core with it. Mega Diancie is great at helping Urshifu-R deal with bulky Dragon-types like Dragonite and Kyurem, and it can take a Choice Specs Moonblast from Iron Valiant and KO it back; it can also set up entry hazards. While Landorus-T only has the option of setting up Stealth Rock, Gliscor can choose to be a Spikes setter helping to cut into the health of the bulky Water-types that wall Urshifu-R even further. Urshifu-R has the ability to break most Steel-types, most notably Ferrothorn, so it can pave the way for Steel-weak Pokemon like Tapu Lele; in return, Tapu Lele is able to help Urshifu-R with most Dragon-types, most notably Dragonite, which it struggles to hit if it is not running Ice Spinner. One of the biggest Urshifu-R checks is Iron Valiant, which can take all of its attacks and KO it back with Moonblast. Mega Scizor can safely switch into Iron Valiant's moves and threaten high damage with Bullet Punch. Urshifu-R's powerful Close Combat neutralizes Dark-types such as Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar, which paves the way for teammates like Mega Latios and Mega Latias. Their strong special STAB moves are also a boon for Urshifu-R, as they can take advantage of bulky Water-types like Alomomola and Toxapex, which otherwise wall it. Electric-types like Raging Bolt and Tapu Koko are also great in this regard, with Urshifu-R being able to help with Ground-types like Iron Treads and Gliscor in return. Urshifu-R is heavily hindered by abilities and items that punish it for making contact, most notably Static from Zapdos and Flame Body from Moltres, as they are able to switch into Urshifu-R's Close Combat and U-turn and punish it via status conditions. Bulkier Gholdengo sets are also a big Urshifu-R deterrent, as it can tank both of its STAB moves and hit back hard with Shadow Ball or ruin it with Thunder Wave. Thus, Urshifu-R appreciates the presence of Pokemon like Mega Tyranitar and Kingambit, as they can Pursuit trap Gholdengo, with Mega Tyranitar also being able to safely get rid of Zapdos and Moltres.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Urshifu-R functions as an amazing late-game cleaner due to its ability to boost its Speed with Trailblaze and its Attack with Swords Dance. Trailblaze allows Urshifu-R to outspeed the majority of the tier, including common Pokemon such as Mega Lopunny and even Choice Scarf users such as Tapu Lele and Landorus-T; it is best used to finish off low HP foes as a way to safely boost Speed. Aqua Jet is also an option in order to revenge kill Mega Diancie, Volcarona, and Tapu Koko at low HP. Protective Pads is used in order to ignore Static from Zapdos, Flame Body from Moltres and Volcarona, and contact damage from Ferrothorn, allowing it to break more freely.

Urshifu-R fits primarily on hyper offense and bulky offense teams, where its strong STAB moves coupled with Swords Dance allow it to shred through defensive structures with ease. Urshifu-R is able to break through defensive pieces such as Landorus-T, Great Tusk, and Gliscor with its strong Surging Strikes, which is appreciated by teammates such as Gholdengo and Kingambit. In return, Gholdengo can beat problems such as Toxapex and Iron Valiant, and Kingambit can put pressure on switch-ins such as Slowbro. Urshifu-R is also able to threaten Steel-types such as Kingambit and Melmetal with its STAB boosted Close Combat, allowing teammates such as Tapu Lele to break through teams more easily. In return, Tapu Lele breaks through Toxapex and Mega Venusaur for Urshifu-R. Urshifu-R finds itself weak to Grass-types such as Ogerpon-W and Kartana, both of which outspeed unboosted Urshifu-R, meaning switch-ins such as Raging Bolt and Ferrothorn are appreciated. As well as this, Ferrothorn can set Stealth Rock for Urshifu-R, chipping switch-ins such as non Heavy-Duty Boots Dragonite and Raging Bolt. Urshifu-R also has trouble setting up against opposing offense and can easily be revenge killed by Pokemon such as Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele before setting up, meaning switch-ins such as Gholdengo and Galarian Slowking are appreciated, with the latter also being able to bring Urshifu-R in safely via Chilly Reception.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band Urshifu-R acts as a formidable wallbreaker, boasting a high Attack stat, an excellent offensive typing, and a great combination of coverage moves to break through weakened teams. Thanks to its typing, Urshifu-R can effectively break down defensive Pokemon like Ting-Lu, Garganacl, and Ferrothorn. Urshifu-R generates momentum with U-turn, pivoting out of unfavorable matchups like Toxapex while dealing considerable chip damage to foes like Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom. Aqua Jet revenge kills weakened faster threats like Volcarona, Iron Moth, Tapu Koko, and Iron Valiant. Alternatively, Urshifu-R can use Ice Spinner to threaten Pokemon, which resist both its STAB moves, like Dragonite and Mega Latias, while Thunder Punch targets bulky Water-types, such as Toxapex and Alomomola.

Urshifu-R's wallbreaking ability and pivoting are appreciated by offensive and balanced teams. Iron Valiant and Tapu Lele form a great offensive core with Urshifu-R, as they benefit from Urshifu-R's ability to remove their checks like Ferrothorn and Moltres. In return, Iron Valiant and Tapu Lele can deal with troublesome foes like Raging Bolt. Volcarona appreciates Urshifu-R's ability to deal with the likes of Heatran and Ting-Lu while easily pivoting into Grass-types such as Rillaboom. Pokemon like Tapu Koko and Landorus-T form a solid pivoting core, bringing each other in on their checks. Urshifu-R comes in against foes like Ferrothorn and Melmetal while Tapu Koko and Landorus-T come in against switch-ins like Toxapex and Raging Bolt. Entry hazard setters, such as Landorus-T and Ferrothorn, are great partners for Urshifu-R, as it benefits from Stealth Rock and Spikes wearing down switch-ins like Ogerpon-W late-game. Ferrothorn also switches into Tapu Koko and Iron Valiant, which would revenge kill Urshifu-R with ease.

Offensive.description:
• With its excellent typing and Surging Strikes breaking through Focus Sash, Urshifu-R is among the premier physical attackers of the metagame!

  • Close Combat versus Drain Punch: Close Combat's power makes it worth the defensive drops most of the time, especially with the protection of Focus Sash. Drain Punch is usually preferred for bulkier Punching Glove sets to improve Urshifu-R's survivability.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet is perfect for picking off weakened foes that are faster than Urshifu-R, such as Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane.

  • Swords Dance: With Swords Dance, Urshifu-R becomes far more difficult to wall by its defensive checks, though Dondozo is a notable exception.

  • Ice Spinner versus Ice Punch: Ice Spinner is more powerful when not using Punching Glove, and it also ruins terrain set up from the likes of Miraidon and Rillaboom. Ice Punch should always be used with Punching Glove, as it prevents Rocky Helmets users like Dragonite from passively wearing Urshifu-R down.

  • Substitute: Substitute with Punching Glove let's Urshifu-R take advantage of Alomomola that try to wear down Urshifu-R with Rocky Helmet, and is also effective at foiling slower status users.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is the preferred nature for giving Urshifu-R as much breaking power as possible. Maximizing Speed with Jolly is often not needed for most matchups, but it does surpass some key targets in Jolly Mimikyu, Jolly Gliscor, and Modest Chi-Yu.

Other Options

  • Bulk Up: Bulk Up takes advantage of Urshifu-R's underrated physical bulk, but it's far less consistent against powerful special attackers like Miraidon and Calyrex-S.

Items

  • Punching Glove: Punching Gloves protects Urshifu-R from taking devastating damage by hitting Rocky Helmet or Rough Skin with Surging Strikes, in addition to boosting other punching moves. Just note that these moves will now be blocked by Protect and other variants.

  • Focus Sash: While it might seem strange with Urshifu-R's good physical bulk, Focus Sash lets it survive extremely powerful physical moves such as Chien-Pao's Electric Tera Blast without investing in bulk, as well as letting it survive powerful special attackers from Flutter Mane, Miraidon, and Calyrex-S.

  • Protective Pads: Protective Pads are a niche alternative to Punching Glove, not boosting any attacks but letting Surging Strikes bypass Protective moves from foes like Garganacl.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Urshifu-R is able to function perfectly fine without Terastallization, though it has both offensive and defensive uses for it.

  • Water: The Tera Water boost to Surging Strikes makes Urshifu-R even more difficult to wall, with even Ting-Lu that lack Sitrus Berry being OHKOed by +2 Surging Strikes. It also makes Aqua Jet a more effective cleaning move.

  • Normal: Tera Normal is often paired with Punching Glove to block Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S, potentially letting it get off a devastating Surging Strikes against it.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar with Adamant is notable not only for taking advantage of Urshifu-R's great offensive coverage, but also because Tera Stellar Close Combat into Tera Stellar Aqua Jet will OHKO offensive Miraidon variants.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 108 HP / 252 Atk / 148 Def with Adamant: Not only does this EV spread maintain maximum power, but the physical bulk let's Urshifu-R survive Adamant Chien-Pao's super-effective Tera Blast 87.5% of the time.

Choice Item Attacker.description:
• With its high-powered STAB attacks and access to U-turn, Urshifu-R is a strong option for a Choice item pivot.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet is a good way for Choice Band Urshifu-R to clean up weakened teams. That being said, with high Speed and priority attacks being so prevalent in the current climate, Aqua Jet can still find a place on Choice Scarf sets.

  • Ice Spinner: Urshifu-R greatly appreciates having a move that prevents it from being walled by Dragonite, and it can also foil terrain-based strategies from Miraidon.

  • Choice Scarf versus Choice Band: Choice Scarf transforms Urshifu-R into an effective revenge killer, outspeeding important threats such as Chien-Pao, unboosted Miraidon, and Flutter Mane that lack Booster Energy. Choice Band, on the other hand, makes Urshifu-R a far more effective wallbreaker, letting it deal massive damage to foes like Ting-Lu, Scizor, Ho-oh, and Calyrex-I.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is far and away the preferred option for getting the most damage out of each attack. However, Choice Band does have a use for Jolly when it comes to outrunning and breaking Jolly Gliscor, and using it with Choice Scarf guarantees that Urshifu-R outruns Modest Choice Scarf Chi-Yu.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low / Medium: Urshifu-R has both offensive and defensive uses for Terastallization that can greatly influence the outcome of a match, but it isn't always vital for it to function.

  • Water: Tera Water removes Urshifu-R's troublesome Fairy-type weakness and gives Surging Strikes a healthy boost in power. With Choice Scarf, Urshifu-R can OHKO Focus Sash Chien-Pao before it has a chance to attack. With Choice Band, Surging Strikes becomes practically unwallable by anything that doesn't resist it.

  • Normal: Tera Normal with Choice Band can blindside offensive Calyrex-S that attack with Astral Barrage, letting Urshifu-R handily dispatch it with Surging Strikes.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 108 HP / 252 Atk / 148 Def with Adamant: When using Choice Band Urshifu, this spread's physical bulk can be worth it against Tera Blast Electric from Chien-Pao, surviving 87.5% of the time.

Wallbreaker.description: Thanks to its impressive stats and splendid movepool, Urshifu-R is one of the best physical attackers of the metagame, capable of fulfilling both wallbreaking and sweeping roles; its access to Swords Dance alongside two solid Mega Stone options grants it flexibility to adjust its set to best fit the team's needs. Close Combat hits foes like Arceus, Arceus-Water, and Kingambit. Ice Spinner hits Dragon-types like Dragonite and Eternatus. U-turn makes Urshifu-R an excellent pivot and helps it escape bad matchups such as Pecharunt and Arceus-Fairy. Swords Dance can be considered over Close Combat or U-turn to turn it into a dangerous cleaner and potentially even break past physical walls like Pecharunt and Eternatus, though it has its drawbacks. Dropping Close Combat makes it weak to Arceus-Water, whereas dropping U-turn means that it can no longer generate momentum for the team. Metagrossite should be used with a Jolly nature to allow Urshifu-R to outspeed foes such as fast variants of Eternatus and Arceus formes, while Aerodactylite with an Adamant nature is a slower but more powerful alternative, achieving feats like 2HKOing Arceus-Fairy with minor chip damage. Urshifu-R synergizes extremely well with offensive staples such as Raging Bolt and Kingambit; Raging Bolt, in particular, is a standout partner, forming a formidable VoltTurn wallbreaker duo with it. Entry hazard setters such as Magearna, Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, and Garganacl are amazing partners, aiding Urshifu-R in maintaining crushing offensive pressure against the opposing team. Urshifu-R also appreciates entry hazard removers such as Regieleki, non-Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, and Corviknight as teammates, as they help it maximize its impact by removing hazards and keeping it healthy throughout the game.

Choice Band.description:
• Knock Off hits Pokemon such as Pecharunt, Spectrier, and non-Weakness Policy Metagross for large damage, alongside removing items such as Choice Band from Pokemon like Hoopa-U.
  • Power Whip deals with Pokemon like Ursaluna, Manaphy, and non-Custap Berry Primarina.
  • Rock Slide can OHKO Volcarona.
  • Bullet Seed lets Zarude beat Donphan and Counter Ogerpon.
  • Low Kick can be a helpful tool against some Hisuian Goodra variants.
  • The EVs allow Zarude to survive a Gunk Shot from Adamant Hoopa-U as well as outspeed Garchomp.
  • Zarude struggles against physically defensive Pokemon such as Corviknight and Landorus-T as well as foes that can outspeed it such as Iron Valiant, Choice Band Dragapult, and Walking Wake. Pairing Zarude with Pokemon such as Primarina and Sylveon can mitigate these weaknesses.

Choice Band (Grass).description:
Zarude can serve as a physical wallbreaker with a great Speed tier and Choice Band, which allow it to outspeed and beat Pokemon like Gholdengo, Skeledirge, and Heatran, as well as a great pivot with U-turn. Power Whip is an excellent STAB move that allows Zarude to 2HKO Toxapex and Hatterene. Drain Punch grants Zarude a form of recovery while still 2HKOing Hisuian Goodra and Heatran, whereas Close Combat grants Zarude a stronger Fighting-type coverage. Alternatively, Jungle Healing allows Zarude access to longevity and removing its own status safely, as it forces many switches.

Amoonguss is a great defensive partner for Zarude, as it is able to resist Fighting- and Fairy-type attacks from Flutter Mane, Sneasler, and Iron Valiant, melt Toxic Spikes, and spread status for more offensive teammates with either Toxic or Spore. In return, Zarude can threaten the Psychic-types Amoonguss loses to, like Hatterene, Armarouge, and Iron Leaves. Choice Scarf Meowscarada makes for another good teammate, as it can outspeed and threaten Dragon-types such as Dragonite, Dragapult, and Hydreigon with Play Rough. In return, Zarude can handle the aforementioned Steel-types that Meowscarada struggles with, and the two of the form a strong U-turn core to complement their teammates. Hisuian Electrode and Rotom-C is a great addition on any Grass team, as thanks to its Speed tier and Electric typing, it can threaten slower Flying-types such as Corviknight and Enamorus as well as Water-types like Toxapex and Volcanion. Zarude's wallbreaking and support role enables sweepers like Hisuian Liligant to sweep Flying thanks to the latter's access to Ice Spinner as well as being able to clean Steel teams. Brambleghast and Toedscruel make for great teammates, as they can set up hazards to wear down incoming Pokemon for Zarude to break easier and remove them with Rapid Spin to enhance Zarude's pivoting ability. Toedscruel also has enough Special Defense to survive a Flamethrower from Choice Scarf Iron Moth and OHKO it back. On the other hand, Brambleghast's Ghost typing also allows it to spinblock, thus preserving hazards on the field, and thanks to its ability Wind Rider, it can switch into anticipated Flying-type attacks. Iron Leaves makes for another great partner, being able to provide Grass teams a positive matchup against Fighting and Poison teams. In return, Zarude can threaten the Ghost-types it struggles with, like Skeledirge and Gholdengo.

Swords Dance (Grass).description:
Decent in the Steel matchup. Black Glasses lets it 2HKO Skeledirge with Crunch.

This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Swords Dance.description: Bulk Up can be run in order to give Zarude more bulk while setting up.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Zarude provides a solid speed control option with a decent amount of defensive utility. Zarude's Speed grants it the ability to pressure Latios, Greninja, and Serperior. U-turn allows Zarude to pivot out against opposing switch-ins like Tinkaton and Cobalion, allowing it to bring in teammates that can threaten them. Close Combat gives Zarude super effective coverage for Ogerpon-C and Cobalion and an option to consistently hit Skarmory, while also OHKOing Excadrill, whereas Jungle Healing grants Zarude the ability to shrug off status from Slowking, Rotom-W, and Skeledirge. However, locking Zarude into Jungle Healing is very risky, due to the fact that the opponent will be able to switch anything in for free. Tera Dark gives Knock Off an extra boost in power, notably 2HKOing Serperior even after its item is removed, while Tera Fighting boosts Close Combat and makes Zarude less susceptible to revenge kill attempts from Lokix. However, Zarude loses its defensive utility when it Terastallizes, so it should only Terastallize when it is necessary to either revenge kill an opposing threat or clean up the rest of the game.

Choice Scarf Zarude fits on offense teams that appreciate its compression as a revenge killer and Ground-resistant Pokemon. However, as a Choice item user, Zarude struggles with foes that can sponge its attacks and switch to a resist such as Hydrapple or Toxapex. As a result, it appreciates teammates that it can pivot to to pressure these foes such as Latios and Thundurus-T. Latios also outspeeds and pressures Skarmory and Cobalion, allowing Zarude to more easily slot Jungle Healing, while Thundurus-T can form a powerful pivoting core with Zarude. More offensively capable foes such as Enamorus-T can also switch into Zarude, so it appreciates defensive teammates that can withstand their attacks, like Tornadus-T and Skarmory. Zarude also appreciates teammates that can handle the tier's Flying-types in Mandibuzz and opposing Tornadus-T. Heatran and Excadrill help against these Pokemon, as well as Tinkaton, and can provide Stealth Rock to help wear down the aforementioned Flying-types after Zarude removes their Heavy-Duty Boots. Heatran also offensively pressures Tornadus-T and Mandibuzz, while Excadrill provides entry hazard removal to prevent Zarude from being worn down by opposing hazards. Sandy Shocks can act as a switch-in to Tornadus-T and Tinkaton while also offensively pressuring Mandibuzz and Enamorus-T. Sandy Shocks, alongside other potential teammates like Tornadus-T, Rotom-W, and Slowking, also functions as a pivot that can bring Zarude in on foes it can pressure out such as Latios.

-ate Speed.description: Regieleki is the premier -ate Speed user, entry hazard remover, and speed control, having incredible role compression that is unmatched. Volt Switch creates progress against switch-ins like Eternatus and Magearna, especially with entry hazard support, while Rapid Spin removes entry hazards to support its teammates. Explosion removes nearly every Pokemon in the tier upon use, notably removing chipped Calm Mind Arceus formes, while Supercell Slam can lure and remove Ho-Oh, an otherwise-decent Regieleki switch-in. Supercell Slam can be used over Rapid Spin to allow Regieleki to have even more offensive pressure on teams where Rapid Spin is less necessary. Maximum Attack and Speed investment is preferred to negate Speed ties, but 8 HP and 60 Defense EVs can be allocated to allow Regieleki to survive opposing Altarianite Regieleki's Extreme Speed and KO back with a Rapid Spin into Extreme Speed or straight Extreme Speed after Stealth Rock. Glalitite is a fringe option when Altarianite is used up with a spread of 252 Atk / 160 SpA / 96 Spe to outspeed opposing Regieleki and remove entry hazards reliably at the cost of being offensively pathetic in comparison to Altarianite. Regieleki fits on a wide range of teams, from offense to semi-stall, and its teammate support reflects that. Pivots and setup attackers like Urshifu-R, Raging Bolt, Spectrier, and Calm Mind Arceus formes all benefit from Regieleki's Explosion threats and notable Volt Switch, either answering switch-ins like Arceus-Ground, Blissey, Pecharunt, and Magearna or capitalizing off of Regieleki removing these roadblocks via Explosion to let them clean up games. Regieleki struggles to make progress versus the likes of Magearna, Eternatus, and Ground-types like Clodsire and Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, so answers to these walls like Lunala, Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, and Arceus-Ground are necessary. Entry hazards also weaken grounded variants of those listed, so setters like Magearna, Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, and Garganacl are enjoyed. While Regieleki is certainly the best Rapid Spin user in the tier, it despises switching into entry hazards, and, as such, Sablenite users like Magearna, Mandibuzz, and Swampert are incredibly helpful.

Dual Screens.description: With the highest base Speed in the game, Regieleki can enable high-powered setup sweepers like Manaphy, Kingambit, and Iron Hands on hyper offense teams as a dual screens lead, though it's more niche than other dual screens setters. With Refrigerate, Rapid Spin is a guaranteed way to remove entry hazards even in the face of Ghost-types like Gholdengo and Pecharunt. However, Regieleki isn't the best to rely on for Rapid Spin all of the time, so teammates like Great Tusk and Quaquaval can help as additional spinners. Explosion lets Regieleki get its teammates in safely, do massive damage to foes like Swampert, Great Tusk, and Roaring Moon, and prevent dual screens removal via Defog. Many setup sweepers, most notably Gholdengo and Iron Hands, appreciate Regieleki's dual screens support while also fending off priority from Pokemon like Slither Wing and Prankster Corviknight, which would otherwise prevent it from setting dual screens. Regieleki similarly doesn't enjoy Choice Scarf Roaring Moon and Meowscarada, as they are the only relevant Pokemon able to outspeed it instantly, so having checks to them such as Kingambit, Iron Hands, and Zamazenta can help. As a final note, Regieleki is exclusively a hyper offense lead meant to support Pokemon such as Iron Boulder, Gengar, and Kingambit by providing them with extra opportunities to set up and win the game.

Terrain Attacker.description: Regieleki functions as a fearsome wallbreaker on Electric teams thanks to its blistering Speed alongside a stunningly powerful Electric-type STAB move in Terrain-boosted Rising Voltage, being able to 2HKO even the most stalwart of neutral checks such as Assault Vest users like Galarian Slowking and Alolan Muk as well as slightly less specially sturdy Electric-resistant Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Mega Altaria. Thunderbolt offers a secondary STAB option for consistent Electric-type damage outside of Electric Terrain, while Volt Switch allows Regieleki to soften up its answers such as Porygon2 and bring in partners to either set up Electric Terrain for it or deal with the foe currently on the field. Ancient Power hits Volcarona harder than an Electric-type STAB move would while also giving Regieleki a chance to become more threatening with an omniboost. Rapid Spin allows Regieleki to have some utility outside of its sheer attacking prowess, letting it help its team if there is a Ground-type switching into it. Choice Specs allows Regieleki to annihilate nearly anything that isn't Blissey or a very specially bulky Electric-resistant foe, while Heavy-Duty Boots lets Regieleki function much better as a Rapid Spin user as well as a pivot, and Magnet allows Regieleki to not get punished as much for clicking a move. Tapu Koko is a mandatory teammate, as it deals very good damage to Ground-types like Great Tusk, Landorus, and Mamoswine that otherwise stuff Regieleki, and it sets up Electric Terrain to boost Regieleki's Rising Voltage to the heights of its power. Zapdos and Rotom-W both deal with Ground-types such as Great Tusk and Landorus-T with Hurricane and Hydro Pump while giving Regieleki a pivot to bring it in. Furthermore, both come with unique benefits as well—Zapdos deals with Grass-types like the aforementioned Ferrothorn and Mega Venusaur if Regieleki cannot immediately break through them, while Rotom-W offers entry hazard control through Defog as well as a stopgap to dangerous physical attackers like Iron Boulder thanks to Will-O-Wisp. Iron Hands provides both a way to deal with pesky special walls like Blissey and Hisuian Goodra as well as a slow pivot for Regieleki. Zeraora pairs well with Regieleki, as both are incredible attackers physically and specially, respectively, and they chip down each other's checks well. In particular, Zeraora deals with Blissey and Hisuian Goodra, major annoyances for Regieleki, while Regieleki sweeps away physically defensive Mega Venusaur.

ru.overview: Regidrago's access to Dragon Energy paired with its decent Speed and monstrous HP allows it to be a great sweeper late-game while still having utility as a revenge killer mid-game. Regidrago's ability, Dragon's Maw, is amazing, strengthening its already powerful STAB Dragon Energy even further so that it OHKOes threats like Terrakion, Armarouge, and Basculegion-F. While Regidrago has enormous HP and its typing has many useful resistances, aiding it against Pokemon like Volcanion, Raikou, and Armarouge, it can't put either of them to good use, as it needs to conserve its HP to ensure Dragon Energy stays as strong as possible. Additionally, Regidrago's lack of coverage moves forces it to rely on Terastallization to even hit most Fairy-types for good damage. Regidrago is quite slow for a Choice Scarf user, too, underspeeding the majority of Choice Scarf foes such as Jirachi, Krookodile, Galarian Zapdos, and Gengar.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Dragon Pulse provides Regidrago with a reliable STAB move that it can use repeatedly, though it is weaker than Draco Meteor and—depending on Regidrago's current HP—Dragon Energy. Regidrago can run Choice Specs instead of Choice Scarf to more easily break through bulkier teams; however, Dragon Energy is typically powerful enough without any further boosts, and Choice Specs leaves Regidrago open to being revenge killed or taking damage much more easily. Regidrago can become a setup sweeper with Loaded Dice and a set of Dragon Dance / Scale Shot / Earthquake / Tera Blast Steel, capitalizing on its gargantuan HP to find multiple turns to set up, but it's quite reliant on Terastallization to get past certain Fairy-types like Air Balloon Klefki.

Checks and Counters

Fairy-types: Regidrago's most powerful moves, Dragon Energy and Draco Meteor, are both entirely useless against Fairy-type Pokemon like Gardevoir, Air Balloon Klefki, and Mimikyu. Additionally, Air Balloon Klefki is immune to Earth Power, forcing Regidrago to either use Tera Blast Steel to hit it or switch out. Not only that, but Mimikyu's Disguise gives it insurance against Regidrago, protecting Mimikyu even if Regidrago goes for a coverage move. However, the majority of them need to watch out for Tera Blast Steel.

Steel-types: Specially defensive Steel-types such as Jirachi, Empoleon, Registeel, and Magnezone cause the most issues for Regidrago, since they can switch in and set up entry hazards in front of it.

Priority and Faster Choice Scarf Users: Due to Dragon Energy's power being heavily dependent on Regidrago's HP, Regidrago hates anything that could make it take damage before it attacks. For this reason, it's highly susceptible to Bisharp's Sucker Punch and especially Mamoswine's Ice Shard as well as common Choice Scarf foes such as Galarian Zapdos, Krookodile, Gengar, and Mienshao.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

Regidrago is a threatening late-game sweeper, with its powerful Dragon Energy cleanly OHKOing many offensive foes such as Krookodile, Galarian Zapdos, and Feraligatr. However, Dragon Energy can be unreliable at times due to its insistence on Regidrago maintaining high HP. Draco Meteor provides a consistently strong attack regardless of Regidrago's current HP, though it's not as spammable as Dragon Energy due to its Special Attack-dropping effect. Earth Power complements Regidrago's Dragon-type STAB moves nicely, hitting Steel-types like Jirachi, Magnezone, and Empoleon super effectively. Similarly, Tera Blast Steel targets Fairy-types such as Gardevoir and Mimikyu, which Regidrago immensely struggles against. Additionally, Tera Steel allows Regidrago to take on Fairy-, Dragon-, and Ice-type attacks in a pinch from Pokemon like Gardevoir, Hisuian Goodra, and Mamoswine.

Regidrago thrives on balance and bulky offense structures that can keep it healthy through providing entry hazard control as well as switch-ins to faster threats while being able to chip its checks to open it up for a sweep late-game. Fairy-types like Gardevoir, Klefki, and Mimikyu are Regidrago's biggest roadblock to sweeping teams. Because of this, Regidrago greatly appreciates support from Steel-type partners that can handle them with ease, such as Bisharp, Registeel, Jirachi, and Magnezone. However, when these same Steel-type Pokemon are on the opposing team, they can cause problems for Regidrago. This means Magnezone is an especially good teammate, since it can provide extra support through Magnet Pull, locking in and KOing pesky opposing Steel-types for Regidrago. Additionally, other Pokemon that beat Steel-types like Krookodile, Mienshao, and Volcanion work well alongside Regidrago. What's more, Krookodile can surprise Fairy-types with its Gunk Shot; Mienshao is great at chipping and crippling Fairy-types with its U-turn and Knock Off, respectively; and Volcanion acts as a decent defensive switch-in to Fairy-types for Regidrago. Since Regidrago's chance at a sweep is heavily reliant on its ability to repeatedly throw off a powerful Dragon Energy, hazard control is vital. Defoggers like Talonflame complement Regidrago quite well, being decent switch-ins to Fairy-types like Gardevoir and Mimikyu while not overlapping with its typing unlike other hazard clearers such as Cyclizar and Noivern. In a similar vein, Wish passers and Healing Wish users like Umbreon, Jirachi, and Gardevoir as well as Lunar Dance Cresselia are great at keeping Regidrago healthy. Pivots like Magnezone, Galarian Zapdos, and Talonflame synergize well alongside Regidrago, as they can provide it with safe entry through their pivot moves, simultaneously keeping it healthy and maintaining Dragon Energy's power. On top of that, these three partners can threaten bothersome foes like Gardevoir, Registeel, and Mimikyu, respectively. Another issue with Regidrago is that the majority of Choice Scarf users outspeed Regidrago and, by dealing damage to it, threaten its chance at sweeping with Dragon Energy. This means that answers such as Slowbro and Gastrodon to Choice Scarf foes like Jirachi, Galarian Zapdos, and Krookodile are recommended. Pokemon like Klefki, Empoleon, and Rhyperior make for especially strong partners, as their hazards can wear down the opposing team to the point where Regidrago can sweep it without issue.

Choice Specs.description:
Modest nature guarantees the 2HKO on Corviknight with Dragon Energy.

Three Attacks.description:
Regidrago is an offensive threat with great damage potential thanks to the combination of Dragon's Maw and its amazing Dragon-type STAB options. Draco Meteor gives Regidrago a powerful single-target burst option, being able to do massive damage to a majority of the format. While Dragon Pulse is weaker, it deals consistent damage over time, making it better for situations where the power of Draco Meteor is not necessary. Earth Power brings solid coverage into Regidrago's moveset for opposing Steel-types at the cost of not doing great damage due to it not being STAB- or Dragon's Maw-boosted. Tera Blast pairs well with Tera Ghost to threaten Ghost-weak Pokemon such as Calyrex-S and Gholdengo. Life Orb helps increase Regidrago's damage output to insane levels, with the drawback of making Dragon Energy weaker over time; Dragon Fang, on the other hand, sacrifices higher damage output for the lack of recoil, giving Regidrago's Dragon Energy and bulk more consistency. Tera Dragon pushes Regidrago's damage even further, allowing it to pick up KOs on extremely bulky Pokemon like Calyrex-I with Draco Meteor and Helping Hand-boosted Dragon Energy, as well as Amoonguss and Incineroar with Tera Dragon Dragon Energy. Tera Ghost provides Regidrago with a Fake Out immunity, helping in its hyper-aggressive gameplan; it also has the extra benefit of removing its weaknesses.

Regidrago's biggest weakness is Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane and Zacian-C, as well as Tera Fairy Pokemon like Calyrex-S and Raging Bolt. Faster Pokemon like Miraidon, Koraidon, and Chien-Pao are other huge threats for Regidrago because they can outspeed and OHKO it. Zacian-C is a great partner for Regidrago, utilizing its typing to threaten Fairy-types. Terapagos is another good partner Restricted Pokemon, being an alternative spread move attacker that can punish opposing Tera Fairy Pokemon that Regidrago would struggle against. Tailwind setters like Tornadus and Whimsicott cover for Regidrago's middling Speed tier and provide it with the ability to outspeed faster threats, drastically increasing its snowball potential. Indeedee-F and Farigiraf are other great partners, blocking priority moves like Fake Out and Sucker Punch with their abilities, setting up Trick Room to help against certain matchups like opposing Tailwind teams, and using Helping Hand to make Regidrago stronger. Indeedee-F is especially helpful thanks to its access to Follow Me, providing redirection support for Regidrago.

Dragon Fang.description:
*Draco Meteor allows Regidrago to pick OHKOs when Dragon Energy isn't dealing much damage at low HP, and Earth Power allows it to damage to Steel types like Gholdengo and Kingambit.

*Regidrago boosts its damage output with Dragon Fang that stacks on Dragon Maw and does insane damage.

*Tera Steel is a great defensive Tera that allows it to resist its original weaknesses.

Dragon Energy.description:
• With Draco Plate and Dragon's Maw, Regidrago's Dragon Energy hits most of the metagame for incredibly high neutral spread damage, offering great sweeping opportunities and removing important threats for its teammates.
  • Draco Meteor gives Regidrago an option when not at full HP, and being a single-target move, it offers an even higher damage output.
  • Earth Power, while often not getting 2HKOs, hits the Pokemon that resist Dragon Energy like Diancie and Gholdengo.
  • Tera Dragon helps Dragon Energy pick up KOs, notably getting the OHKO on bulky Ogerpon-W, while Tera Steel gives Regidrago resistances to a lot of common moves like Tornadus's Bleakwind Storm and Gholdengo's Make It Rain and also improves the matchup against Chien-Pao + Dragonite by letting it resist Extreme Speed and Ice Spinner.
  • Due to its middling Speed, Regidrago heavily relies on Tornadus's Tailwind support to hit first while being healthy and get maximum value from Dragon Energy. Tornadus can also use Icy Wind for additional speed control.
  • Regidrago greatly appreciates Pokemon that can strongly hit opposing targets that resist Dragon Energy, like Gholdengo and Diancie, in return for its ability to blow through Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Incineroar. Gholdengo can deal with Fairy-types like Alolan Ninetales and with Pokemon like Raging Bolt that often Terastallize into the Fairy typing to not get hit by Dragon-type moves. Ground-types like Landorus on Tailwind teams and Ursaluna-B on Trick Room teams are also great to remove Steel-types and Diancie.
  • Ogerpon-H is one of the main beneficiaries of Regidrago's ability to remove Fire-types, in return removing Steel-types, improving the snow matchup, and offering Follow Me support to help Regidrago dodge Sucker Punch and keep itself healthy. Ogerpon-W can also be an option that offers more reliable Follow Me support on defensive teams.
  • Regidrago is often paired with Farigiraf or Indeedee-F, which disincentivizes priority moves like Fake Out and Sucker Punch, and they can use Trick Room against Tailwind users or to reverse Trick Room from opposing users.

Swords Dance.description:
Wielding nigh-unparalleled Attack, immense bulk, great coverage, a snowballing ability, and Swords Dance, Glastrier is a solid physical wallbreaker in PU. Glastrier's STAB Icicle Crash is valuable for pressuring common bulky Ground- and Grass-types like Mudsdale and Wo-Chien, which other attackers like Paldean Tauros-F and Rhydon can struggle against. Close Combat nails Steel-types like Alolan Sandslash and Orthworm and deals solid damage to other Ice-resistant foes like Milotic and Rotom-H. High Horsepower 2HKOes Galarian Slowbro, Bellibolt, and Qwilfish after some chip damage and also deals with Arcanine, Hisuian Typhlosion, and Bruxish. Heavy-Duty Boots is the better item choice, especially on bulkier teams, because it allows Glastrier to freely switch around and play at whatever pace is most comfortable for it. Glastrier can use Custap Berry on hyper offense teams to capitalize on its bulk and Stealth Rock weakness, turning the tables on an unsuspecting revenge killer like Salazzle before being KOed. However, Custap Berry requires careful maintenance of Glastrier's HP to come into play, making it less reliable than Heavy-Duty Boots. 124 Speed EVs let Glastrier move before Bellibolt and other walls such as Palossand. Tera Poison flips Glastrier's bad matchup against Fighting-types like Pawmot and Hisuian Decidueye while making it immune to Bellibolt's Toxic. However, it makes Glastrier weak to Ground- and Psychic-type moves, sacrificing its naturally good matchups against the likes of Galarian Articuno and Golurk. Tera Water offers Glastrier an all-around solid defensive typing that notably helps out versus Rhydon, Bruxish, and Delphox. Finally, Tera Fire prevents Glastrier from being burned, flips the script on Steel-types like Magneton, and still helps out against Fire-types.

Glastrier's pitiful Speed, horrid defensive typing, and tendency to want to Terastallize mean that it generally has to be built around, with bulky offensive teams being the best at supporting it. With that said, Glastrier can also serve as an early-game wallbreaker on certain hyper offensive teams, where its ability to shred roadblocks like Mudsdale and Dudunsparce matters more than its inherent flaws. Milotic is incredibly difficult for Glastrier to deal with, since it withstands even +2 Close Combat and can neuter Glastrier with either Haze or a Scald burn. Electric- and Grass-types like Pawmot, Brute Bonnet, and Venusaur match up well against Milotic, with the latter two even being able to directly switch into it. These Pokemon appreciate Glastrier removing threats like Espeon and Skuntank and get nice openings to attack after Choice item users, such as Goodra and Hisuian Decidueye, lock into a move to try and KO Glastrier. Tatsugiri is another option for punishing Milotic that removes entry hazards, which Glastrier benefits from if it loses its Heavy-Duty Boots or runs Custap Berry, and soft checks Fire-types like Salazzle. Pivots such as Bellibolt, Bombirdier, and Grimmsnarl are important teammates to have on bulky offense teams, allowing Glastrier to hit the field more safely and conserve as much HP as possible. Bellibolt and Grimmsnarl can also spread paralysis to make Glastrier's low Speed less of an issue. While not required, Wish support from Florges helps to sustain Glastrier so it can constantly pressure defensive cores. Physical sweepers like Choice Scarf Paldean Tauros-F, Scrafty, and Arcanine have a much easier time finishing teams off with Glastrier overwhelming walls like Qwilfish and Palossand.

240 Speed EVs outspeeds Corviknight.

Life Orb.description:
• Being an extremely fast and powerful Ghost-type with access to Calm Mind and Will-O-Wisp, Spectrier is able to flexibly set up on many different attackers.
  • After a Will-O-Wisp, Hex is Spectrier's strongest Ghost-type move. The doubled Base Power of Hex allows Spectrier to remain advantaged in Calm Mind wars against Cresselia and Iron Crown and against burned Pokemon that would otherwise be able to KO Spectrier such as Annihilape and Metagross.
  • Hyper Beam allows Spectrier to OHKO frail Pokemon such as Meowscarada and Haxorus.
  • Calm Mind allows Spectrier to tank moves from strong special attackers such as non-Assault Vest Volcanion and KO back after one or two Calm Mind boosts with Hyper Beam.
  • The Speed EVs let Spectrier outspeed all Meowscarada sets, while the Special Attack EVs let it OHKO standard Haxorus with Hyper Beam. The rest of the EVs are placed in Defense for the best odds against Choice Scarf Haxorus.
  • Spectrier struggles to deal with Pokemon that do not mind being burned such as Guts Ursaluna and Hisuian Goodra, anti-setup Pokemon like Volcarona and Primarina, faster Pokemon that can OHKO it such as Chien-Pao and Dragapult, and Dark-type Pokemon such as Urshifu-S and Hoopa-U. Therefore, Pokemon like Primarina and Iron Valiant make great partners.

Specstrier.description:
Choice Specs helps Spectrier take full advantage of its phenomenal Special Attack stat by making sure it is able to repeatedly OHKO any Pokemon after they have been damaged by chip damage or entry hazards, allowing Spectrier to sweep easily with the assist of Grim Neigh. Shadow Ball destroys Ghost-types like Sinistcha and Gholdengo with ease and breaks bulky threats like Toxapex, Archaludon, and physically defensive Corviknight. Draining Kiss is a great coverage move for hitting Dark-types such as non-Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, Hydreigon, and non-Choice Scarf Meowscarada. With the help of status spreading from Gholdengo and Pecharunt, Hex effectively breaks Poison Heal Gliscor and decimates statused special walls like Clodsire and Articuno. Will-O-Wisp also burns Alolan Muk, Ting-Lu, and Hisuian Goodra to cripple them severely before breaking them despite the type resistances. Psychic can check Poison- and Fighting-types like Iron Moth, the aforementioned Clodsire, and defensive Great Tusk while also being the strongest move to threaten Normal-types. Hyper Beam cleanly OHKOes Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-W after chip damage.

Physical Dragapult is a phenomenal teammate, pressuring foes that Spectrier struggles to break, such as Assault Vest Iron Hands, Hoopa-U, and Hisuian Goodra, all of which would otherwise threaten Spectrier in the long run. Choice Scarf Flutter Mane destroys Dark-types such as Roaring Moon and Choice Specs Dragapult with Moonblast while being able to use coverage options such as Thunderbolt to eliminate Barraskewda outside of rain. Swords Dance Hisuian Zoroark grants its allies an immunity to Ghost-type moves and can disguise itself as Spectrier with Illusion to trick opponents. After a foe fallsfor the bait, then threatens physically frail checks to Spectrier such as Ting-Lu, Blissey, and Heatran with a +2 Low Kick. Bulky Gholdengo can weaken numerous foes such as Garganacl and Alolan Muk that Spectrier can’t OHKO while also being able to absorb status moves from status spreaders using its infamous ability Good as Gold. Pecharunt pivots Spectrier in with Parting Shot to let it come in on a foe that it cannot beat while also checking physical attackers such as Azumarill with Malignant Chain. Brambleghast can set entry hazards to make it easier for Spectrier to KO its respective Fire-type checks in Heatran and opposing Ceruledge. Brambleghast can also act as a spinner to allow Spectrier safer entry from entry hazards. Focus Sash Ceruledge is an amazing physical wallbreaker that can easily set up a Swords Dance before attacking with its priority, picking off opposing Flutter Mane in the event of a Ghost mirror matchup. It's also a great check against Alolan Muk and Articuno, which can both be dangerous special walls if not handled quickly. Finally, Skeledirge not only checks Scizor, Lokix, and Weavile but also spreads Will-O-Wisp burns to Dragonite and Azumarill to guarantee a safer sweep late-game.

Nasty Plot.description:
Spectrier is a deadly special attacker that is able to quickly snowball against teams thanks to its high Speed, outrunning some of the metagame's fastest threats like Greninja and Iron Valiant. Spectrier utilizes Draining Kiss to hit Dark-type Pokemon that would otherwise resist its STAB Shadow Ball like the aforementioned Greninja as well as non-Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Roaring Moon. Draining Kiss also serves as a secondary recovery option to help heal off the damage taken by setting up a Substitute. Nasty Plot is used to elevate Spectrier's Special Attack to incredible heights without having to KO foes beforehand. Spectrier shines best when it is able to set up a Substitute, and subsequently a Nasty Plot, in the face of a more passive foe like Toxapex, then begin spamming its scarcely resisted Shadow Ball + Draining Kiss combination. Leftovers is used to provide more substantial recovery than Draining Kiss, but Colbur Berry is an option to take a Dark-type attack from Pokemon like Choice Scarf Great Tusk, Roaring Moon, and Barraskewda. Will-O-Wisp should be used instead of Substitute if Colbur Berry is the item of choice, as it allows Spectrier to capitalize on surviving an attack from these extremely potent physical threats. If Will-O-Wisp is preferred over Substitute, Hex can also be used to deal more damage to burned threats.

Skeledirge can switch into strong physical attacks from Pokemon that threaten Spectrier such as Choice Scarf Gallade, Scizor, Ceruledge, and Mimikyu lacking Shadow Claw, then scare them with Will-O-Wisp.
