  • The HP and Defense investment guarantees Ursaluna-B's survival against Jolly Sneasler's Close Combat, and with the Special Defense investment, Ursaluna-B can survive devastating special attacks like Life Orb Hatterene's Expanding Force under Psychic Terrain, +2 Gholdengo's Make It Rain, and Choice Specs Alolan Ninetales's Ice Beam.
  • The combination of Yawn and Leftover's slow HP recovery can be quite overwhelming if the opponent isn't cautious, letting Ursaluna-B chip foes for its teammates to secure KOs or put foes to sleep, allowing Ursaluna-B's teammates to safely attack or set up. Taunt and Encore can disturb Ursaluna-B's strategy of using Yawn and Protect, ruining its main form of pressure. This set's attacks also aren't quite as threatening as others due to the lack of investment and Life Orb, making Ursaluna-B far easier to switch into.

TailRoom Sweeper.description:
Ursaluna-B has great offensive prowess thanks to its STAB combination, threatening Pokemon like Raging Bolt, Miraidon, Incineroar, and Calyrex-S with its Normal / Ground typing and Mind's Eye ability. Blood Moon is used to OHKO Pokemon like Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-W, while Hyper Voice is a consistent Normal-type STAB spread move that can be used while Blood Moon is disabled. Earth Power threatens Pokemon like Incineroar, Miraidon, Raging Bolt, and Gholdengo while also pressuring Pokemon that run Tera Fire like Calyrex-I and Rillaboom. Life Orb allows Ursaluna-B to pick up OHKOs on Pokemon like Urshifu-R with Tera Normal Hyper Voice, while it lets Earth Power OHKO Gholdengo as well as Zacian-C. A Timid nature allows Ursaluna-B to outspeed Pokemon like Calyrex-S, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, and Miraidon in Tailwind and threaten huge damage. Tera Normal is used to amplify Ursaluna-B's damage, allowing for guaranteed OHKOs on Flutter Mane, Amoonguss, and Incineroar, and Calyrex-S with Blood Moon while also becoming neutral to previously super effective attacks like Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and Wood Hammer from Rillaboom.

Trick Room teams with slower Pokemon like Amoonguss create trouble for Ursaluna-B, as it can put it to sleep with Spore. Ursaluna-B also faces difficulty against Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao, as both utilize Focus Sash to survive one hit and OHKO Ursaluna-B with Close Combat and Icicle Crash respectively. Iron Hands is a good partner for Ursaluna-B, as it is able to easily tank the attacks from Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao and slow their momentum down with Fake Out. Pokemon with Prankster Tailwind like Whimsicott make for strong partners, allowing Ursaluna-B to take full advantage of its Timid nature, helping it outspeed Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. Farigiraf is a great partner for Ursaluna-B thanks to its ability to set up Trick Room for more flexibility and negate Fake Out with Armor Tail. Miraidon synergizes well with Ursaluna-B due to its immunity to Discharge while also preventing the aforementioned Spore from affecting Ursaluna-B thanks to Electric Terrain. It also OHKOes Urshifu-R and brings Pokemon like Mienshao down to their Focus Sash, helping Ursaluna-B sweep more easily.

Trick Room Sweeper.description:
• Hyper Voice provides Ursaluna-B with a more spammable Normal-type STAB attack, especially during Blood Moon's cooldown.

  • Life Orb is recommended, as it provides Ursaluna-B with a boost to its attacks, and Ursaluna-B doesn't mind the recoil due to its great bulk and ability to consistently move first under Trick Room.

  • The given EV spread lets it live a Tera Fairy Moonblast from a Special Attack Booster Energy Flutter Mane. 0 Speed IVs and a Quiet nature allow it to function better under Trick Room.

  • Ursaluna-B may opt for an EV spread of 84 HP / 252 SpA / 172 Spe to outspeed Adamant Chien-Pao under Tailwind.

  • Tera Normal can be used to boost the damage output of Blood Moon and Hyper Voice to nuclear levels.

Freddy (Offensive).description:
• With its great bulk, power, and coverage thanks to high-powered Normal-type STAB moves and amazing ability in Mind’s Eye, Ursaluna-B is a formidable special attacker.

  • Blood Moon: Blood Moon gives Ursaluna-B incredibly high neutral damage. It's a great way to cover a switch or predicted Terastallization, but it requires some forethought to maximize efficiency because it cannot be used on consecutive turns.

  • Vacuum Wave: Vacuum Wave is highly valuable for revenge killing foes, notably hitting Chien-Pao. It can hit Calyrex-S due to Mind's Eye.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power gives great coverage against the Steel-types that resist Blood Moon, making Ursaluna-B nearly unwallable except by non-grounded Steel-types like Corviknight.

  • Hyper Voice: Hyper Voice is a more spammable Normal-type STAB move that can bypass Substitute, allowing Ursaluna-B to thwart attempts to Substitute stall out Blood Moon, like Tera Garganacl.

Items

  • Assault Vest: Assault Vest remedies Ursaluna-B's middling Special Defense, allowing this slow but hard-hitting Pokemon to survive longer.

  • Silk Scarf: Silk Scarf can be used instead of Assault Vest to boost the power of Ursaluna-B’s Normal-type STAB attacks, making it more difficult to switch into, though this makes match-ups against special attackers like Flutter Mane shakier.

  • Life Orb: If using Ursaluna-B on a Trick Room team, Life Orb can be worth the recoil for the highest possible chance of sweeping.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash may sound absurd with Ursaluna-B's bulk, but it can allow more offensive variants to turn the tables on extremely powerful Special Attackers like Choice Specs Flutter Mane, and more easily justify faster EV spreads.

Assault Vest EV Spreads

  • 36 HP / 228 SpA / 244 SpD with Modest: This spread survives an opposing Life Orb Ursaluna-B's Tera Normal Blood Moon.

  • 100 HP / 164 SpA / 244 SpD with Modest: This spread survives Timid Tera Water Iron Bundle's Hydro Pump, even if Ursaluna-B doesn't Terastallize!

  • 244 HP / 52 Def / 196 SpA / 12 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This spread will never be OHKOed by Adamant Choice Scarf Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes unless it Terastallizes.

Other Item EV Spreads

  • 148 HP / 4 Def / 132 SpA / 220 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This EV spread gives Ursaluna-B enough bulk to survive Tera boosted Choice Specs Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast on all but the highest damage roll, as well as the same odds for surviving Jolly Urshifu-R's Close Combat. If used with paralysis support, 32 EVs can be moved from Special Attack to Speed to outspeed paralyzed Modest Chi-Yu.

  • 20 HP / 4 Def / 172 SpA / 60 SpD / 252 Spe with Timid This outspeeds up to -1 Speed Garchomp, and also often outspeeds Pokemon that focus on bulk such as Dragonite, Scizor, and Primarina. The defensive EVs survive Choice Specs Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Life Orb Adamant Chien-Pao's Sacred Sword if Ursaluna-B sticks with Tera Normal.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Ursaluna-B often uses Terastallization to compensate for its lackluster defensive typing; however, it is often capable of functioning without Tera. Because many different Tera types are viable on it, it can play guessing games with opponents.

  • Normal: Tera Normal removes all weaknesses associated with Ursaluna-B’s Ground typing and boosts Blood Moon to phenomenal levels of power, making it ideal on Trick Room teams.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy allows Ursaluna-B to handle the Urshifu formes and Choice Band Dragon-types like Dragonite and Koraidon better while generally being a very solid defensive Tera type.

  • Poison: Tera Poison improves Ursaluna-B’s matchup against Flutter Mane, all Ogerpon formes' Horn Leech, and all Urshifu formes, while preventing Toxic from wearing Ursaluna-B down.

  • Water: Tera Water allows Ursaluna-B to fare better against the likes of Urshifu-R, Chien-Pao, and Chi-Yu.

Hibernation (Yawn).description:
• Yawn doesn't transform Ursaluna-B into just a mere support Pokemon. When used in conjunction with Blood Moon, the bloodmoon beast becomes a master of putting offensive teams between a rock and a hard place: either the opponent's check falls asleep, or they switch out and something far less suited against Ursaluna-B gets shredded by Blood Moon!

  • Moonlight: Moonlight will require sacrificing either coverage or priority, but it makes Ursaluna-B far longer lasting and less vulnerable to lures like Grass Knot Landorus-T. It's a particularly strong choice on teams with strong hit-and-run Pokemon like Choice Specs Flutter Mane.

  • Vacuum Wave: While not amazingly powerful, Vacuum Wave is lovely for picking off Chien-Pao and cleaning up late-game in general. This is to the point where giving up reliable recovery can make sense for some more offensive teams that often can't afford to switch Ursaluna-B out often.

  • Leftovers versus Sitrus Berry: Leftovers is best paired with Moonlight, giving Ursaluna-B maximum longevity. If using Vacuum Wave, Sitrus Berry's quicker burst of recovery suits Ursaluna-B better and provides a better matchup against Urshifu-R. Sitrus Berry is also a reasonable alternative to Leftovers if another teammate needs it.

  • EV Spread: The HP investment ensures Annihilape will not OHKO Ursaluna-B with Final Gambit, and the Defense EVs stop Choice Band Tera Water Urshifu-R from OHKOing Terastallized Ursaluna-B. This spread survives Modest Choice Scarf Chi-Yu's Overheat and Tera-boosted Moonblast from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane on all but the highest damage roll. Offensively, the Special Attack EVs ensure that Blood Moon OHKOes offensive Urshifu formes.

Other Options

  • 20 Speed EVs: 20 Speed EVs let Ursaluna-B outspeed paralyzed Adamant Urshifu formes at the cost of some bulk. This may seem to conflict with Yawn, but paralysis is often a viable secondary playstyle for teams with this set to deal with more offensive threats.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Ursaluna-B's typing is fairly good, but its weakness to common threats like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-R means Terastallization is often needed.

  • Poison: Tera Poison has excellent synergy with Ursaluna-B's playstyle, not only granting it an important resistance to Urshifu-R's Close Combat and Flutter Mane's Moonblast but also ensuring that poison status will not wear it down.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy doesn't help against Flutter Mane, but it does transform Ursaluna-B into a very strong Urshifu-S check, in addition to avoiding Choice Specs Miraidon's wrath.

  • Normal: Tera Normal only helps defensively against Ice, Grass, and Water types, but the power boost to Blood Moon makes Ursaluna-B far more difficult to wall, with defensive Primarina in particular usually being put into Earth Power's KO range.

  • Water: Tera Water offers a useful Ice resistance to flip Chien-Pao matchups more easily, but it doesn't help against Raging Bolt and Grass Knot users like Landorus-T.

Smarter than the Average Bear (Calm Mind.description:
• With its immense defensive profile and access to reliable recovery, Ursaluna-B lends itself very well to a Calm Mind set.

  • Blood Moon: Even though the cool down time can be annoying for a Calm Mind set, the massive amount of power is still strongly recommended for being able to OHKO Urshifu-R without a boost using the given EV spread.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt can be used to shut down utility moves and attempts to stall out Ursaluna-B from the likes of Ting-Lu and slow Dragonite.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus berry allows Ursaluna-B to recover a significant chunk of health, which can be useful to set up boosts against special attackers.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers improves Ursaluna-B's general longevity.

  • Kee Berry: Kee Berry boosts Ursaluna-B's physical bulk, allowing it to keep pace with physical threats such as Dragonite.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Despite its immense bulk, Ursaluna-B’s typing leaves it vulnerable to many common attacks, so a good defensive Tera type is essential for survivability and durability.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy provides a good defensive typing that synergizes well with Ursaluna-B's natural weaknesses, allowing it to stick around.

  • Poison: Tera Poison grants an immunity to Toxic, Making Toxic Spikes less of an issue. It also grants a Fighting resistance, allowing it to better handle Urshifu.

  • Normal: Tera Normal boosts the power of Blood Moon, which improves the matchup against opposing Calm Mind Flutter Mane. It leaves only a Fighting weakness, making Ursaluna-B quite hard to KO.

  • Water: Tera Water aids against both Chien-Pao and Choice Specs Gholdengo, in addition to being a great defensive typing in general.

Ancient Defense (Physical Wall).description:
• Backed by Terastallization, Ursaluna-B can use its incredible physical bulk to wall even the mighty Koraidon!

  • Moonlight: Under Koraidon's sun, Moonlight's increased recovery makes Ursaluna-B that much harder to topple!

  • Earth Power: Earth Power is strong against Steel-types like Scizor and Archaludon that otherwise resist Blood Moon, and it's also super effective against many of Koraidon's most popular Tera types.

  • Hyper Voice: While it doesn't provide extra coverage, Hyper Voice is the best option to prevent Substitute Gliscor from completely shutting down Ursaluna-B.

  • Vacuum Wave: Vacuum Wave is a solid option for picking off weakened threats, especially Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu.

  • Calm Mind: Weaker physical attackers like Assault Vest Koraidon provide great opportunities to set up with Calm Mind.

  • EV Spread: With full defensive investment and a neutral Tera type, a five-hit Scale Shot from +2 Koraidon only has about a 25% chance to OHKO. Even without Terastallization, this Ursaluna-B is so bulky that Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash into Ice Shard only has about a 6.25% chance to knock out Ursaluna-B! The leftover EVs are usually allocated to Speed; keep in mind that Ursaluna-B often Speed creeps, so reallocating some EVs for even a few more points in Speed can be useful in the mirror matchup.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet punishes many common attacks from Koraidon and Zacian-C, though Scale Shot from Koraidon is a notable exception.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's burst recovery can be useful against Swords Dance Koraidon, guaranteeing that Ursaluna-B survives a +2 Scale Shot at five hits even if one of the hits is a critical hit.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Ursaluna-B has to change its typing in order to properly take on Koraidon and other physical threats it targets.

  • Fire: Tera Fire deters Koraidon from spamming its destructive Tera Fire Flare Blitz while remaining neutral against its powerful STAB attacks. Beyond that, it helps Ursaluna-B wall a litany of other physical threats like Calyrex-I, Zacian-C that lack an appropriate Tera Blast, Ogerpon-H, and Assault Vest Rillaboom. The Fairy-type resistance is also excellent against Flutter Mane, a common Koraidon teammate.

  • Water: Compared to Tera Fire, Tera Water is an alternative for resisting Koraidon's Flare Blitz that doesn't sacrifice Ground-type matchups like Landorus-T. It also helps Ursaluna-B against Urshifu-R when used against other types of teams. But without Tera Fire's Fairy-type resistance, Flutter Mane becomes harder to withstand if Ursaluna-B is not running Calm Mind, and Grass-types such as Ogerpon and Rillaboom will be much more threatening.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Ursaluna-B can run a number of other immunity abilities like Storm Drain, Well-Baked Body, Bulletproof, and even Sap Sipper if the team needs the immunity, but they all have a much narrower range of setup opportunities compared to Fluffy. To beat Ground-immune Ghost-types, Ursaluna-B can either run Snarl at the expense of Calm Mind or Moonlight or run Mold Breaker or Mind's Eye to still hit them with its main moves. Substitute lets it punish slow pivots without having to predict, but it is generally less useful than its main moves. Offensive wallbreaking sets like Tinted Lens and Adaptability can be run on more offensive teams to provide more immediate power, but they mostly beat the same threats as Fluffy, just more quickly. Lastly, Steam Engine Weakness Policy Ursaluna-B is very funny on dual screens hyper offense, as it outspeeds everything at +6 and OHKOes almost everything at +2, but it is very unreliable.

Checks and Counters

Earth Eater Ghost-types: Most Ursaluna-B sets are utterly unable to damage Ground-immune Ghost-types, notably Gholdengo and Pecharunt.

Non-contact Physical Attackers: Ogerpon formes, Chien-Pao, and Cinderace can all OHKO Ursaluna-B, as they bypass Fluffy.

Special Wallbreakers: While they can be hard to switch in safely, special wallbreakers like Latios, Iron Moth, and Gholdengo have no trouble forcing Ursaluna-B off the field, often even after a Calm Mind.

Bulky Calm Mind.description:
Ursaluna-B is an unusual combination of wallbreaker and physical wall, leveraging its outstanding bulk with Fluffy to check important threats like Roaring Moon and Kingambit, set up with Calm Mind, and break open defensive cores that usually cannot slow pivot against it with boosted Blood Moon. With Fluffy, it can even tank hits from Zamazenta and Great Tusk and OHKO back with Blood Moon. Water Absorb is an alternative that lets it block Flip Turn from Swampert and Primarina, turn Manaphy into setup fodder, and check Choice Specs Primordial Sea users, but makes it much less reliable of a physical check. Blood Moon and Earth Power have excellent neutral coverage, letting it run both Calm Mind and Moonlight to set up comfortably on more passive teams. With 13 Speed IVs, it underspeeds level 99 Corviknight; this turns what would be a reliable pivot into setup fodder, as Corviknight cannot Roost or pivot safely without the switch-in risking a Blood Moon.

Ursaluna-B fits well on balance and offensive teams, as it provides a notable defensive presence while still putting pressure on or holes in opposing teams. Faster special attackers like Deoxys-S, Zapdos, and Gholdengo appreciate Ursaluna-B wearing down and potentially breaking through common shared checks like RegenVest Manaphy. Even physical attackers benefit from it, as Corviknight and Great Tusk will commonly come in on it to recover or attempt to revenge kill it, only to find themselves chipped, KOed, or set up on. Ursaluna-B's special bulk is very poor, even with a Calm Mind up, so solid specially defensive teammates like its own RegenVest Manaphy are highly appreciated. Due to Fluffy's drawbacks, Ursaluna-B is unable to check some common physical attackers, especially the Ogerpon formes, Chien-Pao, and Pyro Ball Cinderace; at least one other reliable secondary physically defensive Pokemon like Pecharunt, Corviknight, or Regenerator Primarina is near-mandatory. Ursaluna-B is unable to hit Earth Eater / Levitate Ghost-types like Pecharunt and Gholdengo, so a Dark-type like Roaring Moon or Ting-Lu is also recommended.

doublesou.overview: Ursaluna-B utilizes its extremely high special wallbreaking power to power through DOU. It is a threatening force due to few Pokemon in the tier resisting its STAB combination with the help of Mind's Eye, and it fits on both Trick Room and Tailwind-centric teams. Pokemon that would normally Terastallize into Ghost-types to be immune to its Normal-type STAB moves, such as Incineroar, Chien-Pao, and opposing Ursaluna-B, no longer have this option, allowing Ursaluna-B to fire off strong STAB moves like Blood Moon and Hyper Voice against foes for neutral damage. Ursaluna-B uses Earth Power to hit foes like Incineroar, Kingambit, Diancie, Iron Hands, and Gholdengo super effectively. Additionally, it has phenomenal natural bulk, often boosted by Assault Vest. However, Ursaluna-B frequently struggles against defining Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Chien-Pao, and its brethren Ursaluna due to type matchups and its Speed tier.
doublesou.comments:
Checks and Counters

Gholdengo: Gholdengo is a premier threat to Ursaluna-B due to its high power and Make It Rain, hitting its lower Special Defense stat.

Ogerpon-W: Ogerpon-W's strong STAB attacks can prove troublesome, and its ability to Terastallize and receive a +1 Special Defense boost reduces Ursaluna-B's effectiveness in damaging it.

Chien-Pao: Chien-Pao reduces Ursaluna-B's defensive capabilities due to Sword of Ruin, fires off super effective Ice-type STAB attacks, and punishes Tera Ghost with Dark-type attacks.

Chi-Yu: Chi-Yu reduces Ursaluna-B's defensive capabilities due to Beads of Ruin, hitting it with strong Fire-type STAB attacks and allowing partners like Gholdengo and Tornadus to hit it for more damage.

Assault Vest.description:
• Assault Vest allows Ursaluna-B to enhance its immense natural bulk and improve matchups against faster special attackers like Gholdengo, Chi-Yu, and Landorus.
  • Vacuum Wave priority allows Ursaluna-B to pick off Pokemon that commonly run Focus Sash like Chi-Yu, Tornadus, and Chien-Pao, threatening an OHKO on the latter after any Stealth Rock or Fake Out chip damage. Vacuum Wave also allows Ursaluna-B to maneuver around Sucker Punch users like Chien-Pao and Kingambit, which it 2HKOes.
  • The best Tera types for Assault Vest Ursaluna-B are Ghost, Fairy, and Normal. Tera Ghost provides an important Fake Out and Fighting immunity, while Fairy is a strong defensive option for teams that may be weak to Chien-Pao and other Dark-types. Tera Normal boosts its already strong STAB moves, allowing it to OHKO Sinistcha, Ogerpon-W, and Dragonite after Stealth Rock chip damage.
  • Sinistcha is a natural partner, providing healing and redirection for attacks that would threaten Ursaluna-B, such as Iron Hands's Fighting-type moves and Ogerpon-W's STAB moves after Terastallization.
  • Ogerpon-W is a common partner due to its ability to redirect opposing attacks and its Water immunity.
  • Speed control is a necessity with Ursaluna-B due to its low Speed tier. Pokemon like Sinistcha and Tornadus provide Trick Room or Tailwind to help its offensive pressure.
  • The first EV spread allows Ursaluna-B to outspeed Tornadus and the Ogerpon formes in Tailwind. 100 HP EVs with the help of Assault Vest allow it to survive +2 Make It Rain from Gholdengo, Overheat from Modest Chi-Yu, and Icicle Crash from Adamant Chien-Pao.
  • On more Trick Room-dominant teams, Ursaluna-B can opt to run no Speed EVs and invest fully in its HP.

Life Orb.description:
• Life Orb boosts Ursaluna-B's already immense wallbreaking power, allowing it to pick up KOs on Pokemon it would normally be shy of OHKOing such as Landorus and Gholdengo.
  • Protect provides Ursaluna-B with a way to stall out remaining Tailwind or Trick Room turns, which can be crucial for momentum and offensive pressure.
  • Tera Normal is the premier choice for Life Orb Ursaluna-B, boosting STAB attacks for more damage and removing weaknesses to Ice, Water, and Grass; however, it keeps its weakness to Fighting, making it vulnerable to foes like Iron Hands.
  • Tera Ghost provides an important Fake Out and Fighting immunity but makes Ursaluna-B weaker to common threats like Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu and reduces overall damage output compared to Tera Normal. Tera Ghost is also beneficial because common threats like Iron Hands, Diancie, and Ursaluna can underspeed Ursaluna-B in Trick Room, so it benefits from an immunity to Fighting- and Normal-type moves from these Pokemon.
  • Speed control is a necessity due to its low Speed. Pokemon like Sinistcha, Diancie, and Cresselia provide Trick Room, and Roaring Moon and Tornadus set Tailwind to help Ursaluna-B's offensive pressure.
  • The first EV spread allows Ursaluna-B to outspeed both the Ogerpon formes and Tornadus in Tailwind, as well as survive an Adamant Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao and Heat Wave from Modest Tera Fire Chi-Yu.
  • No Speed investment allows Ursaluna-B to underspeed most common threats in the tier and should be run on Trick Room sets. However, Iron Hands, Diancie, and Ursaluna can underspeed it in Trick Room.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Swift Swim sets only appear on rain teams, as otherwise Basculegion-M would be playing without an ability. The Choice Scarf Adaptability set typically appears on balance teams that benefit heavily from getting a quick OHKO against foes like Incineroar. The Focus Sash set can fit on either balance teams or on rain teams with speed control options, as it appreciates rain boosting the weaker Liquidation. Both the Choice Scarf and Focus Sash Adaptability sets can still benefit heavily from being on a rain team thanks to the Water-type damage amplification, despite not having Swift Swim.
  • Pelipper’s Drizzle ability allows Swift Swim Basculegion-M to outspeed nearly the entire metagame, as well as boosting the damage of its Water-type attacks, while Pelipper itself can pressure opposing Grass-types with Hurricane. Archaludon can cover Basculegion-M’s weakness to Dark-type Pokemon such as Kingambit using Body Press, round out the offensive core of a rain team, and serve as a bulky pivot to be sent out after using Flip Turn, resisting attacks from Rillaboom and Kilowattrel.
  • Incineroar can be used to ensure Rillaboom’s Grassy Glide will never OHKO even if Rillaboom has Miracle Seed and stop opposing Basculegion-M from getting an OHKO with unboosted Last Respects.
  • Amoonguss and Sinistcha can use Rage Powder to redirect attacks that threaten to OHKO Basculegion-M, such as Kingambit’s Sucker Punch and Kowtow Cleave, while improving the team’s matchup against Trick Room. Additionally, Sinistcha's Hospitality and Life Dew can be used to bring Basculegion-M back to full health to make use of Focus Sash, stay out of range of attacks like Grassy Glide from Rillaboom, and heal recoil damage from Wave Crash.
  • Grass-type Pokemon like Amoonguss and Rillaboom stop Basculegion-M from sweeping through teams with Wave Crash, as Amoonguss can redirect and resist the attack, while Rillaboom is always threatening an OHKO with Wood Hammer. Pelipper can use Hurricane to hit these Pokemon for massive damage, or Basculegion-M outside of rain teams can be paired with Fire-types like Volcarona and Talonflame. Dark-type Pokemon like Incineroar and Kingambit threaten an OHKO against Basculegion-M and prevent it from sweeping with Last Respects, making Close Combat Sneasler a worthwhile partner. A Commander-boosted Dondozo can survive multiple Last Respects and resist any Water-type attacks. Archaludon can threaten Dondozo with Electro Shot, and Pelipper can punish Tera Grass Dondozo with Hurricane. Alternatively, teams can use Incineroar and Rillaboom along with Basculegion-M's Flip Turn to cycle Intimidate and Fake Out, or Multiscale Dragonite to safely remove Dondozo's stat boosts with Haze. Alolan Ninetales pairs well with the Choice Scarf set because it can hit Grass-types with Blizzard and Water-types like Dondozo with Freeze-Dry, while Basculegion-M covers for Alolan Ninetales's weakness to Fire-type Pokemon such as Incineroar. Opposing Archaludon are unlikely to be knocked out even by a maximum power Last Resepcts, so Fighting-type coverage from Annihilape and Sneasler and Ground-type coverage from Ursaluna-B is appreciated.

Strategy Comments

  • Basculegion-M functions as a late-game cleaner or early-game wallbreaker with high Speed and damage. The Swift Swim sets need its team to set up rain to activate Swift Swim, or else it can be taken out by a quicker foe. It can secure endgames with high-Base Power Last Respects if its teammates have done enough damage to the opposing team. It can bail out of positions with Flip Turn while its teammates take out the foes that are preventing it from sweeping. In the early-game, it can remove the Ursaluna formes, which can allow a teammate like Archaludon to sweep.
  • Basculegion-M can be used early or late in a battle, but it must be saved for the late-game if maximizing the damage of Last Respects is necessary. It can be used effectively in the early-game by knocking out a Pokemon such as Incineroar, which can allow a teammate like Gholdengo to sweep the opposing team. The Focus Sash set can clinch an endgame using combinations of Liquidation and Last Respects, but the Choice item sets must be more careful to leave foes that can be swept by one move for last.
  • Sun teams can mitigate Basculegion-M’s Speed and offense, particularly for the Swift Swim set. Pokemon that set up sun upon switching in like Torkoal can be countered by keeping Pelipper in the back and switching it in when sun is up to overwrite it. Manual sun setters like Whimsicott must be taken out by a teammate like Incineroar with Flare Blitz or Archaludon with Flash Cannon, as switching in Pelipper will set up rain first, which will be canceled by Whimsicott’s Sunny Day. Alolan Ninetales can change rain to snow, take a hit from Basculegion-M and return damage with Freeze-Dry, and use Disable to nullify a Choice item set or Aurora Veil to mitigate its damage output. Basculegion-M can use Flip Turn to reposition until rain is set, and Pelipper can be lead into Alolan Ninetales because it is slower and so will activate Drizzle after Snow Warning, though an Alolan Ninetales in the back can still switch in to cancel rain. Tyranitar can overwrite rain with Sand Stream and can switch into Last Respects while breaking Focus Sash. Pelipper should expect to be faster than Tyranitar, so sand will be set up after rain. Thus, Pelipper is more likely to successfully set rain if it is reserved in the back or if Tyranitar is knocked out by Basculegion-M's teammates.

Rain Sweeper.description:
• Basculegion-M uses its high-Base Power STAB attacks like Wave Crash and Last Respects to claim knockouts in the early-game and secure wins in the late-game, respectively, as well as its Swift Swim ability to outspeed nearly the whole unboosted metagame under rain, giving it positive matchups against metagame staples such as Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Volcarona.
  • Last Respects can reach an incredible Base Power of 200, threatening nearly every Pokemon that does not resist Ghost-type attacks with an OHKO. Aqua Jet allows Basculegion-M to pick off a foe at low health while avoiding Sucker Punch from Kingambit. Flip Turn allows it to deal damage and retreat to safety before being attacked.
  • Choice Band maximizes Basculegion-M’s damage, notably improving the chance for Last Respects with two fainted teammates to OHKO Rillaboom.
  • Tera Water maximizes the damage output of Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks, guaranteeing an OHKO against almost any Gholdengo set, and removes its weakness to Dark-type attacks such as Kingambit’s Sucker Punch. Tera Grass allows Basculegion-M to survive any attack from Rillaboom, resist Electro Shot from Archaludon, and ignore Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss.
  • The defensive investment allows Basculegion-M to survive a Grassy Glide from Rillaboom. With the Attack investment, Basculegion-M will always OHKO Incineroar in the rain with Wave Crash even after Intimidate. The Speed investment allows it to always outspeed Primarina.
  • Choice-locked sets are inherently more risky to use, as being locked into the wrong move can lose an endgame. The Swift Swim set is riskier in terms of speed control, as it relies on its team to set up rain. This set has the potential to be faster than the Choice Scarf set, but without rain, its Speed and damage output can be underwhelming. It has the advantage of Choice Band providing a higher damage boost than Adaptability. This set, as well as the Choice Scarf set, are risky to use over the Focus Sash set as they can be knocked out with one hit.

Choice Scarf Sweeper.description:
• Choice Scarf Basculegion-M can be used on a team that does not have a way to set up rain to outspeed foes in any situation. Adaptability can make up for the decreased damage output. This set can finish off damaged teams with Last Respects without needing a Speed boost from rain.
  • Because of Choice Scarf, Basculegion-M is likely to outspeed its foes, so it can use Flip Turn to switch into a bulkier ally when threatened. Tera Blast is only intended for the Tera Fighting set, in order to hit Kingambit and Archaludon.
  • Tera Water can be used to amplify Basculegion-M's damage. Tera Fighting is used with Tera Blast to pressure Kingambit with an OHKO while resisting its Sucker Punch, and it also lets Basculegion-M resist Knock Off from Incineroar and Tyranitar.
  • A Jolly nature with maximum Speed is necessary for the Choice Scarf set to outspeed Dragapult.
  • Adaptability is always useful due to always providing a boost in some way, whereas Swift Swim is contingent on rain being active for Basculegion-M to benefit. However, this set will not do as much damage as the Choice Band set. The Choice Scarf set may not perform well against opposing speed control such as Trick Room, as it cannot use Protect to stall out turns of Trick Room.

Focus Sash Sweeper.description:
• The Focus Sash set allows Basculegion-M to take a hit and return with strong attacks such as Liquidation and Last Respects.
  • Liquidation is used over Wave Crash in order to avoid taking recoil damage and breaking Focus Sash.
  • Tera Ghost is used with this set, as Last Respects is likely to become stronger than its weaker Water-type attacks.
  • This set can survive a fast attack under Tailwind or Trick Room and use Protect to stall them out, making it generally better against opposing speed control compared to the other sets. However, it will not do as much damage as the Choice Band set and is unlikely to be able to threaten an early-game OHKO because it lacks Wave Crash. It can fit on a variety of teams due to it being self-sufficient in terms of damage output and not necessarily needing speed control.

ru.comments:
Other Options

Tera Blast Ghost provides Basculegion physical Ghost-type coverage, but Shadow Ball tends to hit targets like Slowbro hard enough without making Basculegion reliant on exhausting a resource as valuable as Terastallization. A Choice Scarf can remedy Basculegion's mediocre Speed, but Basculegion-F generally outclasses Basculegion as a Choice Scarf user. Psychic Fangs is boosted by Choice Band, nails Amoonguss and Chesnaught, and 3HKOes Volcanion, but Basculegion is most effective as a wallbreaker across matchups when it's using all of its moveslots for its spammable STAB moves.

Checks and Counters

Water-immune Pokemon: Volcanion is a hard wall to Basculegion and prevents it from pivoting, and the threat of burns from Steam Eruption easily forces Basculegion out. Vaporeon and Storm Drain Gastrodon also outright wall Basculegion.

Bulky Water-resistant Pokemon: Chesnaught easily sponges Water-type attacks and absorbs Shadow Ball. Amoonguss and Wo-Chien can repeatedly tank Basculegion's powerful Wave Crash. Slowbro can use Regenerator to repeatedly pivot into Basculegion's Water-type attacks while threatening Basculegion with a Scald burn.

Burn: Scald users like Slowbro and Suicune can fish for burns against Basculegion. Talonflame is a relevant Flame Body user that might exhaust Terastallization or sacrifice itself to burn Basculegion for its teammates. A burn from Sacred Fire from Entei can also heavily reduce Basculegion's damage output, but does usually mean Entei is being KO'd in return if it does not Terastallize.

Faster Threats: Basculegion's tendency to wear itself out with Wave Crash recoil and entry hazard damage opens it up to revenge killers like Galarian Zapdos, Noivern, and Gengar. Priority users like Bisharp and Mimikyu even hit Basculegion super effectively.

Choice Band.description:
Set Details

Basculegion differentiates itself from Basculegion-F with its greater Attack, offering plenty of damage with its powerful STAB Wave Crash and other physical Water-type moves to overpower physical walls like Hippowdon and specially defensive Water-resistant Pokemon like Empoleon and Hisuian Goodra. Flip Turn helps Basculegion keep up momentum, especially against defensive switch-ins like Slowbro, Chesnaught, and Empoleon. Aqua Jet compensates for Basculegion's poor Speed and enables it to pick off faster foes like Galarian Zapdos, Krookodile, and Weak Armor-boosted Armarouge. Although Shadow Ball isn't boosted by Choice Band, it's still Basculegion's strongest move against Slowbro and only effective move against Volcanion. Adaptability cranks up Basculegion's power even further, enabling it to potentially 2HKO bulky Hisuian Goodra with Wave Crash and guaranteeing a 2HKO on Slowbro with Shadow Ball. Alternatively, Swift Swim nets Basculegion a spot on rain teams; the boost from Swift Swim compensates for Basculegion's middling Speed, and the rain provides a comparable boost to Adaptability for Basculegion's Water-type moves. Tera Water lets Basculegion's Wave Crash OHKO Cyclizar, while increasing the damage output of Aqua Jet and Flip Turn. Basculegion also enjoys shedding its weaknesses to Sucker Punch from Bisharp and Shadow Sneak from Mimikyu. The extra damage Tera Ghost provides Shadow Ball helps Adaptability variants of Basculegion finish off Slowbro more quickly, though the trade-off of losing the Adaptability boost for Basculegion's Water-type moves can make it less potent as a revenge killer and offensive pivot.

VoltTurn teams appreciate Basculegion as a powerful wallbreaker that functions as an offensive pivot, and it forms great pivot cores with Pokemon like Galarian Zapdos, Cyclizar, and Raikou. Knock Off users like Cyclizar, Hisuian Goodra, and Chesnaught threaten to cap Basculegion's damage output if they don't KO it directly, so Basculegion relies on Knock Off absorbers like Wo-Chien and Amoonguss. If Basculegion joins rain teams, it will be reliant on Politoed to get the rain up. Politoed and other Water-types on rain teams, such as Barraskewda and Kingdra, work with Basculegion to overload checks to Water-types like Slowbro and Suicune. On these rain teams, Kilowattrel can threaten bulky Water-types and Water-immune Pokemon, including Slowbro and Volcanion, for Basculegion. Healing Wish and Lunar Dance users like Jirachi, Gardevoir, and Cresselia give Basculegion a second chance wallbreaking or cleaning up, healing off any burns Basculegion's taken and making up for the massive amount of damage Basculegion tends to accrue from recoil and entry hazards. Basculegion itself appreciates hazards being up to wear down Wo-Chien and non-Heavy Duty Boots variants of Slowbro and Amoonguss, so Krookodile, Rhyperior, and Kleavor can support it. Spikes support from Chesnaught and Klefki goes even further than Stealth Rock for wearing down Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and other checks to Basculegion that forego Heavy-Duty Boots.

nu.overview: Basculegion-M's solid Attack stat, supported by two amazing abilities and high-Base Power STAB moves, makes it one of the most potent wallbreakers available in the tier. An Adaptability-boosted Wave Crash is capable of doing immense damage to bulky walls like Registeel and Swampert and even gets good chip on bulky Water-resistant Pokemon like Milotic and Tsareena. Alternatively, Basculegion-M can opt for Swift Swim on rain teams, becoming an extremely menacing Pokemon that can outspeed and power through bulky and offensive teams alike. While not having much in terms of type coverage, Basculegion-M has access to a solid movepool. Most notably, access to Aqua Jet lets it act as a revenge killer, picking off faster Pokemon such as Cinccino, Infernape, and Munkidori with ease. However, the lack of a reliable physical Ghost-type STAB move hurts Basculegion-M greatly, making it susceptible to Pokemon that it otherwise would have a chance against, namely bulky Water-types or Dragon-types such as Vaporeon and Duraludon. Additionally, Basculegion-M's Speed is rather average, leaving it susceptible to being revenge killed by common Pokemon such as Kilowattrel and Brambleghast as well as Choice Scarf users like Infernape, Rotom-C, and Munkidori as well.
nu.comments:
Other Options

A mixed attacking Assault Vest set can function as a decent bulky offensive pivot, leveraging Basculegion-M's solid special bulk against common special attackers like Munkidori. However, Basculegion-M's typing leaves it vulnerable to common special attackers such as Chandelure, Kilowattrel, and Rotom-C, making its defensive use somewhat inconsistent. Additionally, the lack of reliable recovery makes it prone to being chipped down over time, forcing it to be paired with a Wish user and making it much less efficient into common threats. Choice Specs Basculegion-M is a decent option, with its stronger coverage options in Shadow Ball and Ice Beam, alongside Adaptability, compensating for its otherwise middling Special Attack stat. This set can threaten typical counterplay to physical Basculegion-M sets such as Vaporeon, Toxicroak, Duraludon, and Amoonguss with either Shadow Ball or Ice Beam.

Checks and Counters

Water-immune Pokemon: Vaporeon is an excellent answer to Basculegion-M thanks to Water Absorb making it immune to Basculegion-M's Water-type STAB moves alongside strong physical bulk with investment making it hardly deterred by any of Basculegion-M's coverage moves. Toxicroak can also switch into Basculegion-M's Water-type moves courtesy of Dry Skin and use Basculegion-M as fodder for setting up Swords Dance. However, Psychic Fangs obliterates Toxicroak, so it must be mindful of Basculegion-M's choice of coverage.

Water- and Dragon-types: Milotic is generally a solid check to Basculegion-M thanks to Recover giving it extremely important longevity as well as Flip Turn letting Milotic use Basculegion-M as a chance to gain momentum. Inteleon can generally switch into Basculegion-M once and, in return, outspeed and OHKO Basculegion-M with Dark Pulse after some chip damage. Duraludon's solid physical bulk lets it come in on Basculegion-M's Water-type STAB moves and threaten Stealth Rocks, Thunder Wave, or finish it off with Draco Meteor. Paldean Tauros-W's high physical bulk combined with Intimidate and Bulk Up lets it easily come in on Basculegion-M's Water-type STAB moves, but it must exercise caution against sets with Psychic Fangs.

Grass-types: Bulky Grass-types like Amoonguss and Tsareena are able to handle Basculegion-M's Water-type moves outside of rain quite effectively and can overwhelm it with their STAB moves. Amoonguss in particular can also take advantage of Basculegion-M's presence for longevity with Giga Drain and Toxic. However, both of these Pokemon must be wary of Choice Band Ice Fang, as they are vulnerable to being 2HKOed by it. Amoonguss also must look out for Psychic Fangs.

Faster Pokemon: Basculegion-M's bulk, while decent, leaves it vulnerable to various faster Pokemon with super effective coverage. Dark-types and Pokemon with Dark-type coverage such as Infernape, Cinccino, and Inteleon can all OHKO Basculegion-M with their respective Dark-type attacks after some minor chip damage. Other faster offensive Pokemon such as Tsareena, Kilowattrel, and Rotom-C can overwhelm Basculegion-M with super effective moves. However, all of these Pokemon have to be wary of Basculegion-M under rain, and non-Choice Scarf variants have to fear a possible Choice Scarf on Basculegion-M, as the majority of them are susceptible to being OHKOed by Basculegion-M's Wave Crash.

Substitute.description:
Set Details

Basculegion-M can opt for either a physical or special set, and they both come with their benefits and drawbacks. A physical set is more easily walled, but its Liquidation gets to come off its higher Attack. Additionally, Phantom Force being a two-turn attack means it may not always hit Basculegion-M's desired target, though it always gets a free turn of healing from Leftovers. On the other hand, a specially oriented Substitute Basculegion-M has access to reliable moves for both of its STAB types, isn't as held back by four-moveslot syndrome as physical sets are, and can surprise physical walls. However, this comes at a price of its noticeably lower Special Attack. Aqua Jet lets Basculegion-M safely pick off foes like Cinccino, Munkidori, and Infernape at low health, ensuring neither it nor its Substitute takes damage. Endeavor capitalizes on Substitute lowering Basculegion-M's HP, letting it cut down the HP of walls that it can struggle with like Vaporeon, Avalugg, and Amoonguss. On the other hand, Pain Split lets Basculegion-M simply recover some HP while simultaneously dealing damage. Leftovers is preferred, since it provides passive healing, mitigating Substitute's impact on Basculegion-M's HP. However, Metronome can capitalize on Substitute giving Basculegion-M free turns, letting it continually attack and more easily beat Vaporeon. Heavy-Duty Boots means Basculegion-M doesn't need to worry about constant chip damage from entry hazards, though this forces Basculegion-M to run Pain Split if it wishes to have any form of recovery. Jolly and Timid natures can also be used so that Basculegion-M outspeeds Tsareena and Toxicroak, but the wallbreaking power of Adamant and Modest is typically better. Tera Water increases the power of both Liquidation and Surf, letting Basculegion-M break through walls more easily, while Tera Dark allows it to take Ghost-type attacks from Chandelure and opposing Basculegion-M as well as Dark-type moves like Incineroar's Knock Off if necessary.

Duraludon and Roar Vaporeon are the main roadblocks for Basculegion-M, so partners that can help pressure them like Flamigo, Toxicroak, and Freeze-Dry Alolan Ninetales make for good pairings. In return, Basculegion-M can whittle down Bellibolt for Flamigo as well as take care of Galarian Slowbro and Bronzong for Toxicroak and Alolan Ninetales. Pivots like Munkidori, Swampert, Flygon, and Whimsicott that draw in Pokemon that Basculegion-M can set Substitute on and take advantage of, like Bronzong, Vaporeon, and Toxicroak, are greatly appreciated, though Basculegion-M must be cautious of Toxicroak's Knock Off sets. Substitute Basculegion-M sets excel at weakening defensive Water-resistant Pokemon like Amoonguss, Milotic, and Tentacruel, meaning it can pave the way for partners like Flygon, Incineroar, and Paldean Tauros-F. Avalugg is often a hard check to get past for Basculegion-M, but specially oriented sets are good at luring it in and dealing great damage. This can be capitalized on by physical attackers like Overqwil, Scyther, and Flygon. Faster Ghost-types such as Hisuian Typhlosion, Chandelure, and Brambleghast can be problematic for Basculegion-M, causing Ghost-resistant and -immune teammates like Incineroar, Scrafty, Porygon2, and Dudunsparce to be necessary. Powerful Grass-, Electric-, and Dark-type Pokemon like Tsareena, Kilowattrel, and Incineroar can stop Basculegion-M from keeping up its Substitute, so checks to these Pokemon such as Amoonguss, Bellibolt, and Diancie make for good partners.

Rain Sweeper.description:
Set Details

Liquidation acts as a recoil-free alternative to Wave Crash at the cost of lower power. This is especially useful late-game, where Basculegion-M can wreck through weakened foes while still maintaining some health as to not be too vulnerable to revenge killers.Aqua Jet has more use outside of rain, being a useful priority tool to revenge kill faster Pokemon like Infernape, Munkidori, and Cinccino. Psychic Fangs can be used as an alternative to hit Vaporeon neutrally while also hitting checks like Toxicroak and Amoonguss super effectively. Ice Fang is another option that hits Dragon- and Grass-types like Goodra, Tsareena, and Amoonguss attempting to switch into Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks.Tera Water can further boost Basculegion-M's already monstrous offensive profile, letting it 2HKO bulky Water-resistant Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Tsareena with Wave Crash or even Houndstone after Stealth Rock chip.

Choice Band Basculegion-M is a premier threat on rain teams thanks to its immense power and Swift Swim boosting its Speed. As a result, rain setters such as Klefki and Tornadus are necessary picks. In addition to setting rain, the former has access to a vast array of utility moves such as Thunder Wave, which cripples Choice Scarf users like Infernape and Inteleon, and Spikes, while the latter can use rain itself to break through Grass-types like Amoonguss, Wo-Chien, and Tsareena. Other Swift Swim Pokemon such as Kingdra, Overqwil, and Ludicolo have solid synergy with Basculegion-M. Kingdra can overwhelm Vaporeon, Toxicroak, and Duraludon, making it less needed for Basculegion-M to Terastallize to hit these Pokemon. Overqwil can function as a late-game cleaner that appreciates Basculegion-M's insane wallbreaking letting it finish off games more easily, as it's able to finish off weakened foes. Ludicolo's Grass-type STAB moves and Ice-type coverage can be monumental in turning the tides against bulky Water-, Grass-, and Dragon-types like Vaporeon, Swampert, Tauro-Paldea-W, Amoonguss, and Altaria. Other entry hazard setters such as Gligar, Flygon, and Swampert make for good teammates, further bolstering Basculegion-M's wallbreaking capabilities.

All-out Attacker.description:
Set Details

Aqua Jet gives Mystic Water sets a way to pick off faster Pokemon like Chandelure, Cinccino, and Munkidori, while Liquidation helps out Choice Scarf sets by providing a less risky version of Wave Crash with more PP and no recoil. Aqua Jet can even find use on Choice Scarf variants as a means to combat faster Choice Scarf users like Munkidori. Psychic Fangs provides solid coverage, hitting Poison-types that can take Water-type moves like Toxicroak and Amoonguss. Ice Fang instead targets Grass- and Dragon-types like Tsareena, Amoonguss, Flygon, and Altaria, albeit being weaker into the aforementioned Poison-type Pokemon. Mystic Water in tandem with Adaptability makes Basculegion-M's Water-type STAB moves extremely menacing while allowing it to switch its moves. This is further boosted by Tera Water, which makes Basculegion-M's Water-type attacks monstrously strong, doing immense damage to even the bulkiest of physically defensive Pokemon like Avalugg. Alternatively, Choice Scarf patches up Basculegion-M's otherwise average Speed and makes it a formidable revenge killer in its own right. Despite this, Basculegion-M's average Speed stat prevents it from being consistent as a revenge killer, as other Choice Scarf users such as Flygon, Infernape, Munkidori, and Porygon-Z can effectively outspeed and threaten it.

All-out attacker Basculegion-M benefits many balance, bulky offense, and offense teams thanks to its ability to easily wallbreak and, if carrying Choice Scarf, its surprise factor as well. Entry hazard setters like Flygon, Swampert, and Diancie can set up Stealth Rock and Spikes, whittling down foes for Basculegion-M to more easily overwhelm. Hazard removal from the likes of Cinccino, Avalugg, and Tsareena is heavily appreciated, increasing Basculegion-M's longevity and making it more capable offensively late-game. Basculegion-M tends to draw in bulky Water- and Grass-types like Vaporeon, Amoonguss, Wo-Chien, and Tsareena. As a result, offensive Pokemon that can capitalize on these foes, namely Toxicroak, Incineroar, Rotom-C, and Staraptor, can form potent wallbreaking cores with Basculegion-M. Additionally, the last three Pokemon can reliably bring Basculegion-M in with their pivot moves, giving Basculegion-M an easier time entering battle. Dark-types like Incineroar, Scrafty, and Bombirdier can counteract opposing Dark- and Ghost-types and use their presence as an opportunity to generate offensive momentum through pivoting, wearing down foes over time with Knock Off, and, in the case of the first two, status. Setup Pokemon that can boost Speed such as Dragon Dance Flygon and Tidy Up Cinccino, as well as those that increase their physical bulk like Iron Defense Registeel and Bulk Up Scrafty, can pose a problem to Choice Scarf Basculegion-M, as either Basculegion-M's average Speed stat or the lack of an additional power boost can let it down against these threats. Thus, Pokemon that can check these foes such as Orthworm, Chandelure, and Sylveon are appreciated, providing some solid defensive backbone for Basculegion-M to fall back upon. In return, these Pokemon heavily appreciate Basculegion-M's strong offensive presence.

Choice Band (Water).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Choice Scarf Sweeper.description:
• Basculegion-M is a niche sweeper on hyper offense teams, primarily those utilizing Psychic Terrain and Sticky Web, due to its mediocre Speed tier and susceptibility to priority moves. Basculegion-M’s viability is tied to it being the strongest user of Last Respects, letting it OHKO or 2HKO almost the entire tier when it's the last Pokemon. Bulky Ghost-resistant Pokemon such as Yveltal and Arceus-Dark can also be 2HKOed by 300-Base Power Last Respects, leaving only Arceus as a safe switch-in. While fast, Basculegion-M is still outsped by Zacian-C and Deoxys-S, so it can only sweep once both of those Pokemon have fainted.
  • Wave Crash lets Basculegion-M wear down Arceus, 2HKOing it after Stealth Rock damage. Tera Blast Fighting puts even more pressure on Arceus, being able to OHKO it after some chip damage while also 2HKOing bulkier variants of Arceus-Dark, which is important because both otherwise prevent Last Respects from being a roll.
  • Flip Turn can be used to generate momentum if Arceus switches in or if Arceus-Dark or Yveltal switch in if Last Respects is not at full power. Aqua Jet lets Basculegion-M pick off threats like a weakened Arceus-Ground that outspeeds it after a Dragon Dance.
  • Tera Fighting makes Basculegion-M resistant to Yveltal’s Sucker Punch and neutral to Marshadow's Shadow Sneak, preventing it from being revenge killed by them; it also synergizes best with Tera Blast to hit Arceus harder than Wave Crash.
  • Basculegion-M should almost always be sent out once most, if not all, of its teammates have fainted, maximizing Last Respect’s power. Generally, using Basculegion-M is fairly straightforward, as 300-Base Power Last Respects should OHKO everything left, but it has to Terastallize in order to beat a healthy defensive Yveltal or Arceus-Dark. If Arceus is on the opposing team, the main priority would be to either KO it with a partner like Arceus-Ground or Deoxys-A or poison it such as with Glimmora's Toxic Spikes, limiting its longevity.
  • Due to Basculegion-M’s susceptibility to priority, it functions best on Psychic Spam teams utilizing Tapu Lele and Deoxys-A to punch holes early on. Glimmora is a solid partner, as it can set Toxic Spikes and Spikes to wear down Arceus and Arceus-Dark, enabling Basculegion to sweep in the late game.
  • Sticky Web teams with Shuckle or Smeargle can also utilize Basculegion, as the Sticky Webs let Basculegion outspeed Deoxys-A and Zacian-C, as well as other boosted Pokemon. Wallbreakers such as Swords Dance Necrozma-DM and Ultra Necrozma are great partners, as they lure and remove both Yveltal and Arceus-Dark easily.
  • While Basculegion-M is strong, it is still unable to OHKO extremely physically bulky Pokemon such as Zygarde-C and defensive Primal Groudon, so the aforementioned entry hazards help wear them down, alongside teammates that put pressure on them like Taunt Arceus-Ground and Zacian-C.

Swift Swim.description:
• The given EV spread allows Basculegion to survive Grassy Slide from Rillaboom and outspeed scarfed Chi-Yu during Rain or Tailwind.
  • Tera Grass helps Basculegion to avoid super effective damage from priority users such as Raging Bolt and Rillaboom while also preventing Amoonguss from redirecting Basculegion's attacks or putting it to sleep.

Choice Scarf.description: • Jolly nature is required to outspeed Flutter Mane.

Offensive.description:
• With a good offensive typing and Adaptability pushing its already high-power STAB attacks past the heavens, Basculegion-M is a horrifyingly powerful wallbreaker that only gets stronger in the later stages of the game!

  • Last Respects: After just one teammate is KOed, Last Respects already becomes a strong STAB move. When it's the last Pokemon standing, this vengeful attack will 2HKO almost anything that doesn't resist it at minimum, with the big exceptions being defensive Dragonite if Multiscale is intact and Dondozo if not using Life Orb.

  • Endure and Custap Berry: Endure can be used to put Basculegion-M into Custap Berry's activation range against many powerful attacks, letting it fire off Last Respects on the top of its priority bracket. This can be a devastating surprise late-game, turning what could be a sure loss into new avenues to sweep!

  • Flip Turn: Adaptability turns Flip Turn into a powerful pivoting move, giving Basculegion-M more utility early-game.

Other Options

  • Psychic Fangs: While hitting Urshifu-R extra hard isn't a bad deal, the real use for Psychic Fangs is to get rid of dual screens that would otherwise stop Basculegion-M from sweeping.

  • Mold Breaker: Mold Breaker can be tempting for cleaving through Multiscale Dragonite, offensive Sturdy Archaludon, and the occasional Mimikyu with Last Respects, but Dragonite's habit of using Tera Normal and the big overall damage reduction makes it a rather niche option, especially since Mold Breaker announces its presence, removing any sort of surprise value.

Items

  • Life Orb: Life Orb may compromise Basculegion-M's decent bulk, but it turns the fish into an absolute scourge against bulky Pokemon, with Last Respects now 2HKOing Dondozo at its maximum power and Tera Ghost even potentially 2HKOing defensive Dragonite through Mulitscale if it lacks Leftovers!

  • Assault Vest: When used with specialized EV spreads, Basculegion-M can send common revenge killers like Flutter Mane and Gholdengo to an early grave.

  • Focus Sash: Even with Wave Crash's recoil, Focus Sash is good for winning unexpected matchups against threats like Chi-Yu and Chien-Pao, though note that this item benefits best from a more specialized set.

General EV Spreads

  • 28 HP / 252 Atk / 228 Def with Adamant: This physically bulky EV spread lets Basculegion-M survive Adamant Ogerpon-H's Horn Leech on all but the highest damage roll and does the same for Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon. It also always dodges a 2HKO from Adamant Choice Band Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes, usually survives +1 Jolly Dragonite's Scale Shot at five hits, and survives Jolly Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Def with Adamant: This spread always lets Basculegion-M survive Adamant Ogerpon-H's Horn Leech, but it now has around a 19% chance of being OHKOed by Modest Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Adamant: While maximizing Speed makes Basculegion-M notably frail, it does outspeed some otherwise troublesome foes like Modest Raging Bolt, although it needs to watch out for Thunderclap and the rare but deadly Adamant Breloom.

  • Brave Nature Reducing Basculegion-M's Speed can give it an edge in mirror matches when used on Trick Room teams with setters like Porygon2 and Mimikyu, but note that going as far as using a Speed IV of 0 can harm Basculegion-M's matchups against normally slower foes like Scizor, Primarina, and Corviknight, so using a Speed IV of 31 is the most flexible option.

Assault Vest EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 172 Def / 68 SpD / 12 Spe: This bulky spread allows Basculegion-M to avoid an OHKO from Jolly Ogerpon-H's Horn Leech, survive Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball, and outspeed paralyzed Adamant Dragonite even after one Dragon Dance.

  • 212 Atk / 244 Def / 52 SpD: This spread lets Basculegion-M survive all but the highest damage from Adamant Ogerpon-H's Horn Leech and Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball at the cost of some Attack.

  • 244 Atk / 68 SpD / 196 Spe: This enables Basculegion-M to avoid an OHKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball while still outspeeding Adamant Breloom.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Terastallization is a more of a double-edged sword than usual due to Adaptability, which only gives its damage bonus if Basculegion-M's current typing matches the attack. Because of this, while Terastallizing makes sense for Basculegion-M, it will lower the power of at least some of its attacks!

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy trades Basculegion-M's wallbreaking power for a defense against Dark-types. With Tera Blast, this can even stop Urshifu-S!

  • Water: Tera Water makes Aqua Jet a potent late-game cleaning tool and lets Basculegion-M survive most Choice Specs Flutter Mane's attacks as a bonus, with the exception of rare variants with Thunderbolt or Tera Blast Stellar.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost transforms Last Respects into a truly outrageous wallbreaking attack when Basculegion-M is the last fish swimming, with even Dondozo taking over 50% from it!

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting is a more niche option against Dark-types, leaving Basculegion-M vulnerable to Fairy-type attacks in exchange for a stronger matchup against Archaludon and Urshifu-S via Tera Blast.

  • Don't Use Tera Stellar!: Basculegion-M may seem like a perfect candidate for Tera Stellar, but don't be fooled: Adaptability has no interactions with the Stellar type, making it completely useless unless Basculegion-M is using the niche Mold Breaker!

Swift Swim Sweeper.description:
• With such powerful attacks and the game-ending Last Respects, Swift Swim Basculegion is the king of rain teams!

  • Last Respects: Last Respects is the key to sweeping late-game if common Water-resistant foes such as Urshifu-R are still around, but even after one teammate is KOed, it's a good coverage attack.

  • Setting Up Rain: Pelipper is almost required support for this Basculegion, not only providing the needed rain to gobble teams up but even providing Tailwind so Basculegion can outspeed extremely speedy foes like Booster Energy Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle.

  • Substitute: Substitute ruins Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S for daring to use Sucker Punch and helps against Raging Bolt's Thunderclap as well.

  • Head Smash: While not very reliable, this is Basculegion's most powerful attack against Dragonite and Roaring Moon and rips Iron Bundle to shreds too.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is the most reliable nature for sweeping, but Jolly does outspeed +1 Jolly Roaring Moon and Choice Scarf Latios.

  • Life Orb versus Focus Sash: Life Orb is preferred for maximizing Basculegion's late-game sweeping potential. If Life Orb is needed elsewhere, Focus Sash can be a reasonable shift in focus, making Basculegion easier to use outside of rain, which makes benching Pelipper for some matchups easier to justify.

Other Options

  • Liquidation or Waterfall: Wave Crash's constant recoil wears Basculegion down quickly, so Liquidation saves Bascluegion's scales if a foe is already in its KO range. Waterfall is a tad weaker, but the 20% chance to flinch can lead to huge upsets in a battle!

  • Rain Dance: Setting up Rain Dance usually shouldn't be a job for Basculegion, but it does severely punish Torkoal's attempt to change weather.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Basculegion can function without Terastalliztion, its often the star sweeper of rain teams, making it a likely choice to Terastallize.

  • Water: Tera Water boosts Wave Crash to truly obscene power, with offensive Roaring Moon in particular being OHKOed 75% of the time by Adamant Wave Crash!

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy not only saves Basculegion from Sucker Punch foes like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S, but it also shreds Roaring Moon if it doesn't Terastallize with Tera Blast Fairy.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar is a flexible method for sweeping, with the one-time boost to Last Respects reaping Urshifu-R's soul when Basculegion is the lone teammate alive!

  • Ghost: While it doesn't have amazing synergy with rain, Tera Ghost still boosts Last Respects into a ghoulish wallbreaking tool regardless of the weather, being particularly useful against Urshifu-R, defensive Primarina, and Dondozo

Choice Scarf.description:
• With Choice Scarf and the powerful Adaptability-boosted Flip Turn under its fins, Basculegion is an effective revenge killer and offensive pivot with an important immunity to Extreme Speed.

  • Jolly Nature: While Adamant's power may be tempting, Jolly is needed for outspeeding Iron Bundle, Adamant Dragonite after Dragon Dance, and the rare Dragapult.

  • Last Respects: Last Respects transforms Basculegion into a vindictive sweeper once its allies have passed on to the afterlife!

  • Head Smash: While the accuracy can be worrisome, this is Basculegion's most powerful attack against Dragonite and Roaring Moon and does a reasonable job of revenge killing Choice Specs Iron Bundle when Last Respects is still weak.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet may seem ridiculous with a Choice Scarf, but it can pick off weakened priority users like Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Terastallization is nice when a game-ending sweep is in sight, but reducing the power of at least one of Basculegion's STAB attacks can make it a bit situational.

  • Water: Wave Crash is the least risky move to lock Basculegion into, so Tera Water is a reasonable cleaning option.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost Last Respects is an excellent cleaning tool when Basculegion is the final soul remaining, but watch out for Ursaluna-B, Porygon2, and Tera Normal Dragonite.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy reducing the power of both STAB attacks is a big issue, but it saves Basculegion against Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S's Sucker Punch, and Tera Blast Fairy still deals good damage.

  • Don't Use Tera Stellar!: Because Adaptability does not take Tera Stellar into account, this Tera Type is fool's gold and should be ignored.

Agility.description:
• Agility and the terrifying Last Respects transform Basculegion into a ferocious late-game sweeper once its friends are sleeping with the fishes!

  • Last Respects and Late-game: This set is extremely focused on sweeping late-game with Agility, so while Basculegion's Water-type attacks don't make it useless earlier in the game, its best to save it as your last Pokemon to transform Last Respects into a slaughterous showstopper!

  • Wave Crash: Even if using Focus Sash, Wave Crash's power is far too good to pass up, since Basculegion isn't guaranteed to be sweeping every game.

  • Aqua Jet: A priority attack may seem pointless on a Speed boosting set, but beyond letting Basculegion revenge kill weakened Pokemon, it also ruins Sucker Punch attempts from Chien-Pao and Urshifu-S.

  • Liquidation: If using Focus Sash, Liquidation is a reasonable alternative STAB attack to let Basculegion live another day.

  • Substitute: While risky and not a great fit with Focus Sash, Substitute punishes Sucker Punch attempts from Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao and could even turn the tables on Raging Bolt's Thunderclap.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant is the easiest nature to score sweeps with, but Jolly can be worth it if outspeeding Jolly +1 Roaring Moon and Choice Scarf Latios is important.

  • Focus Sash versus Life Orb: Focus Sash is the most reliable way to set up Agility, making it the best option. Life Orb can pull off sweeps with less damage though and is a reasonable alternative if another teammate already has Focus Sash.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Terastallization guaranteeing that at least one of Basculegion's STAB attacks gets a downgrade is a bummer, but this set focuses so heavily on late-game sweeping that it's likely to go that route regardless.

  • Ghost: Even though Tera Ghost doesn't offer much defensive benefit, boosting Last Respects is often a key ingredient for sweeping.

  • Water: Tera Water gives Basculegion more flexibility in sweeping without the lives of its teammates being over, though Last Respects can become a disappointing cleaning tool later in the match.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy provides insurance against Sucker Punch throwers like Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao, but both STAB attacks receiving a power downgrade is a big problem. If doing this, seriously consider Tera Blast to rip Dark-types to shreds.

  • Don't Use Tera Stellar!: Tera Stellar is a siren song, having no impact on Basculegion's power at all due to Adaptability's mechanics.

Choice Scarf.description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

ru.overview: Thanks to its good Special Attack, Adaptability, and a STAB combination that is unresisted when paired with Ice Beam, Basculegion-F serves as one of the strongest special wallbreakers in the metagame. Its access to Flip Turn allows its Choice item sets to synergize with other pivots like Flamigo and Magnezone to form powerful VoltTurn cores that can easily wear out opposing teams. Basculegion-F can also become extremely threatening under rain with Swift Swim or on Sticky Web teams with Weakness Policy. However, Basculegion-F's mediocre Speed means that even Choice Scarf sets can be outsped and threatened by other common Choice Scarf users like Krookodile, Gengar, and Gardevoir. Furthermore, the ubiquity of specially defensive Pokemon like Umbreon, Empoleon, and Assault Vest Cyclizar often results in Basculegion-F relying on physical wallbreaker teammates like Terrakion to start making progress.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Basculegion-F can utilize its threat as a wallbreaker to run a Substitute + Leftovers set, which aims to set up Substitute while the opponent switches to a Pokemon like Cyclizar or Wo-Chien, allowing Basculegion-F to make progress without needing to predict. A Modest nature can be used for more firepower on Choice Scarf sets, with the risk of failing to outspeed Jolly Barraskewda.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Bisharp and Krookodile can safely take Basculegion-F down by using priority Sucker Punch and outspeeding it, respectively, though Krookodile needs a Choice Scarf of its own to outspeed Choice Scarf Basculegion-F. Defensive Dark-types, such as Umbreon and Wo-Chien, can easily tank Basculegion-F's attacks and threaten it with super effective damage.

Special Walls: Specially defensive Pokemon such as Empoleon, Gastrodon, Assault Vest Cyclizar, and Hisuian Goodra can reliably switch into Basculegion-F's attacks and either heal off the damage or strike back with Draco Meteor and Knock Off. However, they should all be wary of Choice Specs Basculegion-F, as it can 2HKO them with the right move.

Faster Wallbreakers: Many of the strong Choice Scarf users in the tier, such as Krookodile, Gengar, and Gardevoir, can outspeed and threaten Basculegion-F. Gardevoir in particular can cause trouble, as Trace can copy Basculegion-F's Adaptability and boost Gardevoir's firepower.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Basculegion-F is a strong option for speed control thanks to its powerful Adaptability-boosted attacks and good defensive typing. Its bulk and resistances offer it many opportunities to enter the field against common Pokemon like Slowbro, Jirachi, and Registeel. Choice Scarf enables Basculegion-F to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame, including Jolly Barraskewda and Noivern. Ice Beam is important to hit the Dragon- and Grass-types that resist Basculegion-F's STAB attacks like Cyclizar and Bulletproof Chesnaught. Flip Turn allows Basculegion-F to pivot out against special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Empoleon while still dealing respectable damage thanks to Adaptability. It is not recommended to Terastallize Basculegion-F, as the damage boost is minimal, and Adaptability will no longer apply to its old typings. For this reason, it uses either Tera Ghost or Water, and it should be Terastallized primarily for the defensive benefits. Tera Ghost means that Basculegion is no longer weak to Electric- and Grass-type attacks from Hisuian Goodra, Raikou, and Amoonguss, while Tera Water sheds the vulnerability to Sucker Punch from Bisharp and Shadow Sneak from Mimikyu.

Choice Scarf Basculegion-F is most comfortable on bulky offense teams that appreciate its speed control while also making use of its defensive qualities to serve as a pivot. Since it is expected to enter the field multiple times, entry hazard removal options such as Cyclizar and Noivern are valuable allies, with Cyclizar being able to survive Electric- and Grass-type attacks from Choice-locked Hisuian Goodra and Amoonguss, while Noivern can tank physical attacks from faster Choice Scarf users like Krookodile and Flamigo. Basculegion-F can form a VoltTurn core with teammates like Flamigo and Flygon that want to attack the special walls like Umbreon and Hisuian Goodra that answer Basculegion-F. These Fighting-types can also take Knock Off from Pokemon like Krookodile while threatening the Dark- and Dragon-types that can switch into Basculegion-F such as Umbreon, Hisuian Goodra, and Cyclizar. As Basculegion-F often needs help breaking through bulky Water- and Grass-types like Empoleon, Gastrodon, and Wo-Chien, other special attackers like Gardevoir and Hisuian Goodra have the power and coverage to create holes in the opposing team for Basculegion-F to exploit. Hazards set by Pokemon such as Krookodile, Chesnaught, and Jirachi can weaken checks into KO range of Basculegion-F's attacks and rack up extended damage as it forces switches and pivots out.

Agility.description:
Agility Basculegion-F is a potent special wallbreaker with an excellent and near-unresisted STAB combination for the tier. Ice Beam allows it to break through Dragon-types like Cyclizar and Noivern and Grass-types like Amoonguss and Chesnaught. Weakness Policy sets are particularly strong against a weak Knock Off from utility Pokemon like Cyclizar, Empoleon, and Chesnaught. On the other hand, Life Orb is a more reliable but less powerful option for powering up Basculegion-F's attacks. Its natural bulk along with this EV spread allows it to survive several key benchmark hits. 52 Defense EVs ensure Basculegion can comfortably survive a Sucker Punch from max Attack Bisharp from full health. Choice Scarf Gengar outspeeds Basculegion-F even after one Agility boost, but with 24 Special Defense EVs, Basculegion-F is guaranteed to take one Shadow Ball from Gengar from full health and fire back with its own Shadow Ball or use Agility a second time. 196 Speed EVs allow unboosted Basculegion-F to outspeed Bisharp and Timid Magnezone. Adaptability makes Basculegion-F a subpar user of Terastallization, as the additional power boost from either Tera Ghost or Water is minimal and comes at the expense of losing its Adaptability boost on its other STAB type. However, Basculegion-F can utilize either Tera Ghost or Water in a pinch to squeeze out some extra damage or remove one of its weaknesses against foes such as Magnezone or Krookodile.

Agility Basculegion fits well on offensive structures in search of a powerful special attacker and potential mid- to late-game sweeper. It appreciates rain support from Politoed to boost the power of its Water-type moves. Entry hazard support from Pokemon like Terrakion, Krookodile, and Chesnaught enable Basculegion-F's ability to clean late-game as well. Chesnaught is an excellent partner for Basculegion-F on Spikes-stacking teams, as Chesnaught can tank the Dark- and Electric-type moves that threaten the fish while enjoying Basculegion-F's natural immunity to Rapid Spin from Cyclizar. Weakness Policy Basculegion-F sets can subsequently take advantage of Cyclizar by baiting a careless Knock Off and setting up with Agility or firing back with a boosted Ice Beam. Basculegion-F's ability to deny hazard removal from Cyclizar makes it an excellent addition to Sticky Web teams as well. Specially defensive Pokemon like Empoleon, Wo-Chien, and Hisuian Goodra are problematic for Basculegion-F, as they can comfortably stomach any of its unboosted attacks. Therefore, powerful Fighting-type wallbreakers like Terrakion and Lucario pair well with Basculegion-F in helping to eliminate these threatening foes. Basculegion-F in turn aids these Fighting-type wallbreakers by threatening their defensive answers like Quagsire and Slowbro. Basculegion-F is notably vulnerable to paralysis from status spreaders like Amoonguss and Jirachi, since the speed drop from paralysis neuters its ability to set up and sweep teams. Therefore, partners that can absorb paralysis like Magnezone can be helpful teammates. If Basculegion-F is unable to use Agility, then Choice Scarf Gardevoir can take advantage of it due to Trace copying Adaptability. As a result, Steel-type stalwarts like Jirachi and Registeel are helpful in keeping Gardevoir at bay. Basculegion-F is also appreciative of teammates like Gastrodon, Chesnaught, and Krookodile that can deal with strong priority users like Sucker Punch Bisharp and Shadow Sneak Mimikyu. Basculegion-F should be paired with allies like Hisuian Goodra, Bisharp, and Krookodile that can manage revenge killers that outspeed and KO a weakened Basculegion-F after one Agility, such as Choice Scarf Gengar and opposing Bisharp.

Choice Specs.description:
Set Details

Choice Specs Basculegion-F is an incredibly powerful wallbreaker that can use the threat of forcing out common Pokemon like Slowbro, Jirachi, and Chesnaught to its advantage. Hydro Pump trades accuracy for power, notably allowing Basculegion-F to OHKO Magnezone. Ice Beam is important coverage for threatening Dragon- and Grass-types like Cyclizar, Noivern, and Wo-Chien. Flip Turn is useful for pivoting out of special walls like Assault Vest Hisuian Goodra and Umbreon into Pokemon that can exploit them like Terrakion. Adaptability boosts Basculegion-F's power to immense heights, while Swift Swim can be used under rain to turn Basculegion-F into a frightening sweeper with few switch-ins. While Adaptability means Basculegion-F rarely wants to use Terastallization, it can occasionally be used to secure KOs on crucial foes; for example, Tera Ghost guarantees a 2HKO on Choice Specs Hisuian Goodra. Tera Water can be particularly useful for Swift Swim Basculegion, as when paired with rain, it boosts its Water-type attacks enough to even guarantee a 2HKO on Assault Vest Cyclizar after Stealth Rock without needing to click Ice Beam.

Choice Specs Basculegion-F fits well on balance and bulky offense structures, as well as niche but threatening rain teams, that are in search of a special wallbreaker that can almost always force progress with incredibly powerful attacks. Pivot partners such as Flamigo, Noivern, and Magnezone can form powerful VoltTurn cores with Basculegion-F that can make progress by luring in relatively passive Pokemon that it can exploit, such as Slowbro and Jirachi, or wearing down shared checks, like Gastrodon and Hisuian Goodra. In particular, Fighting-type pivots like the aforementioned Flamigo are beneficial for Basculegion-F, as they can check Dark-types like Krookodile, Bisharp, and Umbreon that threaten it and absorb Knock Off from Pokemon like Cyclizar. On rain teams, wallbreaker teammates like Barraskewda and Kilowattrel can similarly pivot around with Basculegion-F while wearing down or eliminating its checks like Umbreon and Empoleon. Entry hazard support from partners like Krookodile and Chesnaught can help further in chipping away at the opposing team. In offensive structures, setup sweepers and cleaners such as Porygon-Z, Feraligatr, and Choice Scarf Krookodile particularly appreciate Basculegion-F's ability to blow holes in the opposing team that they can use to pull off a sweep.
