CRITTY CAT.description:
• With its good Attack, Speed, and access to Flower Trick and Knock Off, Meowscarada is a potent cleaner that is also hard to switch into.

  • Flower Trick: With its guaranteed critical hit, Flower Trick is a dangerous cleaning move once foes resistant to it have been sufficiently chipped.

  • U-turn: If using Protean, U-turn lets Meowscarada be a pivot that does far more damage than most other users, and it helps Choice Scarf Meowscarada get out of some tricky early-game situations such as Serperior leads.

  • Trick: Trick can help Choice-locked sets incapacitate an annoying wall, such as Corviknight or Dondozo, by locking them into a single move. It also has the bonus of Protean letting Meowscarada resist Fighting-type attacks after using it.

  • Triple Axel: Triple Axel may not be the most reliable move out there, but it strikes fear into the heart of Dragonite and offensive Mimikyu, which can both be big offensive issues for Meowscarda.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: Jolly is usually preferred for the Speed tie in mirror matches, but Adamant's extra power can be justified on Choice Scarf Meowscarada, since it still outspeeds boosted Garchomp.

  • Choice Band versus Choice Scarf: Choice Band-boosted Meowscarada hits incredibly hard, and with its naturally high Speed, it can serve as a cleaner and a potential wallbreaker, especially against common Defense-boosting foes such as Bulk Up Annihilape and Tera Fairy Archaludon. With the Speed offered via Choice Scarf, Meowscarada can threaten otherwise faster foes, such as Dragapult and +1 Garchomp, potentially putting more pressure on offensive teams.

  • Protean versus Overgrow: Protean’s type shifting allows Meowscarada to make the most of its colorful movepool, particularly on Choice-locked sets, where the limitation to only changing types once is effectively nullified. If you intend to make use of a Tera type other than Grass or Stellar, Overgrow is worth considering, as it allows Meowscarada more flexibility with its moves by not changing type and removing STAB from Flower Trick or Knock Off.

Other Options

  • Play Rough: Compared to Triple Axel, Play Rough isn't nearly as good at handling Dragon-types besides Hydreigon, but it does stop Terastallized Dragonite, Garchomp, and Baxcalibur from grabbing a Speed boost with Scale Shot.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch is a strong priority attack, but it can be rather risky with a Choice item.

  • Brick Break: Low Kick's superior damage output against Ursaluna-B usually makes it the better Fighting-type coverage move, but with Choice Band, Brick Break still OHKOes Kingambit and breaks Alolan Ninetales's Aurora Veil.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Terastallization overriding Protean means Meowscarada should usually only Terastallize to clean a weakened team late-game.

  • Grass: While Terastallizing does override Protean, Tera Grass Meowscarada can be used to power through teams ill-prepared for it. Dual screens teams in particular are especially vulnerable to the sheer power of Choice Band-boosted Tera Grass Flower Trick.

  • Dark: Tera Dark-boosted Knock Off isn't as reliable at sweeping as Flower Trick, but it can surprise bulky Steel-types such as Scizor and Archaludon, as well as deal incredible damage to bulky Volcarona.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost is a defensive option to stop Dragonite's Extreme Speed from revenge killing Meowscarada.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar's one-time boost per attack can give Meowscarada more flexible cleaning options. If Meowscarada Terastallizes after using Protean, the type it currently is will get the double-Base Power boost, which can lead to unexpectedly powerful coverage moves!

  • Fire: Tera Fire gives Meowscarada a Will-O-Wisp immunity and Fire resistance to combat bulky Volcarona.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 76 HP / 228 Atk / 108 Def / 4 SpD / 92 Speed with Jolly: This bulkier Choice Scarf spread allows Meowscarada to outspeed Jolly Garchomp while avoiding an OHKO from Breloom's Mach Punch and Choice Band Dragonite's Extreme Speed.

Minor Optimizations

  • Neutral Natures and Trick: Make sure to use a neutral nature and a Jolly or Adamant Mint on Meowscarada, so it won't get confused by eating any Berry after using Trick.

Focus Sash.description:
• With its good Speed and wide movepool, Meowscarada makes for a potent lead.

  • Triple Axel: Triple Axel prevents Meowscarada from getting set-up on by Dragonite, and ruins Garchomp and Hydreigon.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch allows Meowscarada to better handle fast foes such as Dragapult and Choice Scarf Gholdengo.

  • Toxic Spikes: Meowscarada is an excellent offensive choice to lay Toxic Spikes, since it puts immense pressure on Ursaluna-B leads.

  • Low Kick: Low Kick is Meowscarada's only way through Kingambit, with the bonus of dealing immense damage to Tera Normal Ursaluna-B.

  • Protean versus Overgrow: Protean offers the most offensive flexibility. For more supportive sets with Toxic Spikes, Overgrow lets it keep STAB on its attacks after it uses its support moves.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Thanks to its good Speed, Meowscarada makes particularly excellent use of Taunt, though two big targets, Archaludon and Annihilape, will put Meowscarada in immense danger.

  • Play Rough: While Triple Axel deals with most Dragon-types better, Play Rough can be a huge upset against Terastallized Scale Shot users like Dragonite and Garchomp!

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: This Meowscarada has very little use for Terastallization, only using it in late-game situations where it can sweep.

  • Grass: When paired with an Overgrow boost, Tera Grass lets Flower Trick deal a huge amount of damage.

  • Dark: Tera Dark makes Knock Off even more difficult to switch into, especially hitting Volcarona hard.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar is the more flexible option for late-game sweeping. Just remember that moves only get the double BP boost if they match Meowscarada's current typing.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost saves Meowscarada from Normal-type priority, which can flip the match on unsuspecting Dragonite!

Offensive Pivot (Atk).description:
Meowscarada is a powerful offensive pivot, utilizing a combination of Protean and high-powered attacks to thrive in the metagame. With an Attack donation, Meowscarada gains a much-needed power boost alongside its naturally high Speed, allowing it to hit hard and fast. Move-wise, Flower Trick and Knock Off are Meowscarada's most spammable moves, while Triple Axel nails would-be switch-ins such as Landorus-T and Mandibuzz. U-turn allows Meowscarada to create momentum to exploit the offensive pressure it is able to apply. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Meowscarada to pivot in multiple times throughout the game, while Choice Band boosts Meowscarada's power to higher levels, and Choice Scarf improves Meowscarada's speed control potential. Tera Grass is chosen to amplify Flower Trick to even higher levels, although Tera Dark is still a viable option to boost Knock Off.

High Attack gods like Calyrex-I and Groudon are excellent for Meowscarada to inherit from. Furthermore, Calyrex-I and Groudon both appreciate Meowscarada's ability to break bulky Water-types such as Rotom-W, while Groudon also breaks Steel-types such as Heatran in turn. However, other Gods such as Zacian-C and Ho-Oh are acceptable alternatives, as they grant small but still noticeable Attack increases. Though Meowscarada functions as a powerful offensive pivot, it is quite frail, thus making defensive pivots such as Rotom-W, Landorus-T, and Pecharunt highly appreciated to allow Meowscarada to enter the field. Meowscarada also appreciates special attackers such as Iron Moth, Hisuian Electrode, and Landorus to break opposing physical walls such as Skarmory, Moltres, and Clefable as well as Pokemon walling all of its coverage like Zacian-C, with the former two also forming a VoltTurn core with Meowscarada. Lastly, Stealth Rock and Spikes users such as Skarmory and Ting-Lu are advantageous, as Meowscarada is able to remove foes' Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off and accumulate chip damage through entry hazards and U-turn.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Heavy-Duty Boots and Magic Guard + Life Orb sets are niche options that can fit on bulkier teams that appreciate the longevity of such sets given Meowscarada's propensity to pivot often, though the loss in power is often noticeable such as being unable to 2HKO Pecharunt. Mixed sets with Adaptability + Life Orb and Dark Pulse are a niche option to bait checks such as Corviknight. Spikes and Toxic Spikes can also be considered as options to accrue chip damage or force entry hazard removal by Corviknight. Sucker Punch can be considered on Choice Band sets if a team needs priority to check faster threats such as Deoxys-S and Choice Scarf Gholdengo. Lash Out is a niche option that allows Meowscarada to better threaten Intimidate Corviknight and Skarmory.

Checks and Counters

Corviknight and Skarmory: With their significant bulk and 4x resistance to Grass, Meowscarada can struggle greatly in breaking through these counters alone, particularly Fluffy variants, and so requires support from teammates to weaken or remove these foes.

Faster Threats: Meowscarada's lack of bulk and poor defensive typing means Choice Band sets are vulnerable to most offensive threats that outspeed it such as Chien-Pao, Zamazenta, and Deoxys-S as well as various Choice Scarf users such as Roaring Moon and Azelf. Choice Scarf sets are also vulnerable to priority from the likes of Chien-Pao and Kingambit.

Choice Item.description:
With its good Attack and great Speed tier, Meowscarada serves as a strong offensive pivot and wallbreaker that is able to exploit and outspeed common defensive and offensive staples such as Great Tusk, Roaring Moon, and Gholdengo. Choice Band enables Meowscarada to secure OHKOs against foes such as Scream Tail, Pecharunt, and Great Tusk as well as pressure checks such as Corviknight. Choice Scarf guarantees Meowscarada is able to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame and threaten other Choice Scarf users such as Roaring Moon, Latios, and Scream Tail. U-turn lets Meowscarada scout switch-ins and accumulate chip damage against checks such as Corviknight. Triple Axel threatens checks such as Mandibuzz and defensive Zapdos while also OHKOing targets like Landorus and Garchomp. Low Kick alternatively allows Meowscarada to hit bulky Steel-types such as Cobalion, Heatran, and Kingambit. Both Triple Axel and Low Kick OHKO Roaring Moon. Trick cripples checks such as Corviknight or setup sweepers such as Fluffy Roaring Moon, Iron Crown, and Kingambit.

Meowscarada can fit on a variety of balanced and more offensive teams that appreciate it as a wallbreaker and value its Speed tier above other dangerous offensive threats. Meowscarada can struggle to get onto the field due to its lack of bulk and so appreciates slow pivots like Corviknight, Swampert, and Pecharunt that can also absorb revenge killing attempts from the likes of Chien-Pao, Deoxys-S, and Zamazenta. Meowscarada can also benefit from the presence of offensive pivots like Cinderace, Moltres, and Azelf that provide it with opportunities against switch-ins like Great Tusk, Manaphy, and Swampert. Meowscarada can struggle with breaking through Corviknight and Skarmory and so pairs well with other strong wallbreakers such as Zamazenta, Chien-Pao, and Ogerpon-W that can pressure and overload them. Similarly, it can benefit from strong hazard setters such as Great Tusk, Landorus, Ting-Lu, and Heatran that can chip and weaken Corviknight and other checks like Iron Hands and Zamazenta. Alternatively, Meowscarada can be paired with other strong wallbreakers such as Choice Specs Gholdengo and that can take advantage of a free switch into Corviknight or Skarmory.

Choice Scarf (Dark).description: Thanks to its fantastic movepool and Protean, Choice Scarf Meowscarada is the best revenge killer available for Dark teams, outrunning the likes of Regieleki, Speed-boosted Kommo-o, and Mega Swampert under rain. Flower Trick is Meowscarada's most powerful move, picking off weakened foes such as Tapu Lele and Terrakion. Play Rough is essential, as it deals with many threats to Dark teams like Galarian Zapdos, Mega Gallade, and Iron Valiant. U-turn allows Meowscarada to switch out of unfavorable situations, pivoting into powerful teammates such as Galarian Moltres and Mega Tyranitar while keeping momentum for the team. Knock Off cripples defensive switch-ins—such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Clefable—as well as offensive Pokemon like Zeraora and Iron Treads. Toxic Spikes can be run instead to better pressure Normal, Fairy, and Fighting teams. Meowscarada's teammates appreciate its ability to check a myriad of threats as well as its revenge killing capabilities. Wallbreakers like Galarian Moltres and Hydreigon are great partners to deal with physical walls like Celesteela and Mega Venusaur. Ting-Lu and Tyranitar provide entry hazard support for Meowscarada—ensuring it is able to net more KO's—and are great defensive pivots for it to fall back upon. Similarly, Mega Sableye provides a Fighting immunity, bounces back status moves, and prevents entry hazards from going up, letting Meowscarada switch in unscathed.

Choice Scarf (Grass).description: Meowscarada is an excellent choice for Grass teams thanks to its high Speed and Protean, enabling it to be a threatening revenge killer that can outspeed common threats such as Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Gholdengo. Flower Trick is Meowscarada's best STAB option and is capable of dealing with weakened Pokemon like Clodsire and Spectrier. Flower Trick's guaranteed critical hit is also very useful in the Fairy matchup and lets Meowscarada revenge kill Azumarill and a weakened Tapu Lele behind Reflect. U-turn allows Meowscarada to maintain an advantage against its defensive checks like Corviknight by being able to pivot into its teammates like Scovillain. Knock Off is a tool to cripple Meowscarada's defensive switch-ins like Toxapex and Klefki in addition to the aforementioned Corviknight. Play Rough is a strong coverage option to threaten opposing Dragon-type Pokemon like Kommo-o, Kyurem, and Latios, which Grass teams tend to struggle against. Low Kick is a less frequent option but lets Meowscarada OHKO Bisharp while threatening Heatran with a 2HKO; however, Play Rough is preferred to have an easier time against Dragon teams. Meowscarada has an easier time revenge killing foes with entry hazard support from Ferrothorn and Cradily. Ferrothorn appreciates Meowscarada's ability to check Fighting-types like Mega Gallade, Iron Valiant and Galarian Zapdos with STAB Play Rough. Hisuian Lilligant is also a fantastic offensive partner for Meowscarada. It is able to check the Flying-types that switch into Meowscarada like Celesteela and Landorus-T while also assisting in the Dragon matchup, outspeeding common Pokemon like Garchomp and Dragonite. Hisuian Lilligant also makes the Steel matchup easier for Grass; its ability to threaten Heatran is appreciated by Meowscarada, while Meowscarada can threaten Gholdengo with Knock Off, which Lilligant cannot beat. Mega Venusaur is also a mandatory defensive partner for Meowscarada; its Bug neutrality and bulk allows it to act as a consistent check to Mega Scizor, which easily switches into any move of Meowscarada, and Venusaur is able to check it with Hidden Power Fire. Mega Venusaur also checks opposing Fairy-types for Meowscarada like Tapu Koko, Mega Diancie, and Iron Valiant, while Meowscarada is able to threaten the Psychic-types that force out Mega Venusaur such as Latios, Mega Alakazam, and Victini. Whismicott is one of the best hazard removal options on Grass, and Meowscarada appreciates not having Stealth Rock and Spikes chip it down, because it comes in often to threaten a KO. Whimsicott's Fairy typing also allows Meowscarada and its teammates not to be overwhelmed by Dragon-types like Garchomp, and it can encore Calm Mind Mega Latias. Celebi with Nasty Plot and Groundium Z can break defensive Steel-types like Heatran and Hisuian Goodra while also being able to threaten opposing Poison-types like Alolan Muk and Toxapex.

Defensive.description:
Hex can be used on sets packing Will-O-Wisp to deal massive damage to burned foes, notably letting Skeledirge OHKO Slowking at +1 after burn damage, while also helping put a lot of pressure on Pokemon such as Tornadus-T and Rotom-W that may try to pivot around Skeledirge once they have been burned. Shadow Ball is a more reliable option to deal consistent damage early-game. Will-O-Wisp allows Skeledirge to put pressure on physical attackers such as Lokix and Donphan, while Earth Power can hit Heatran for large damage as well as forcing Fezandipiti to expend Roost's PP, allowing Skeledirge to safely get teammates in. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Skeledirge to ignore its otherwise ruinous Stealth Rock weakness. The EV spread allows Skeledirge to take on a wide variety of both physical and special attackers; for example, it has good odds to survive two Earth Powers from Gastrodon and has a chance to survive two High Horsepowers from Revavroom. Tera Fairy allows Skeledirge to take on Dark-types such as Lokix and Zarude while also giving it an immunity to Latios's and Hydrapple's Draco Meteors. Tera Poison gives Skeledirge an immunity to Toxic from both Fezandipiti and Toxapex; the typing lets it check Ogerpon-C and Greninja and helps it check Dark-types such as Lokix and Hydreigon. However, Tera Fairy makes Skeledirge unable to check Revavroom, while Tera Poison leaves it unable to check Latios. Both Tera types also make Skeledirge unable to block Rapid Spin from Excadrill and Donphan in a pinch.

Skeledirge primarily fits best on a variety of playstyles ranging from bulky offense to stall teams, which appreciate its ability to soft check a wide array of Pokemon such as Thundurus-T, Latios, and Revavroom. Knock Off absorbers such as Skarmory and Fezandipiti are great for Skeledirge, as they can take on Pokemon such as Zarude and Lokix that Skeledirge may not be comfortable switching into for fear of losing its Heavy-Duty Boots. Water-type switch-ins such as Slowking, Hydrapple, and Rotom-W are perfect partners for Skeledirge, as they can take on Water-types such as Greninja and Keldeo that Skeledirge might struggle with, while in return, Skeledirge can take on Pokemon such as Thundurus-T that said Water-type switch-ins might struggle against. Slowking and Rotom-W in particular are great partners, as they can spread burns or paralysis to boost the power of Hex. Flying-types such as Skarmory and Tornadus-T are great for Skeledirge, as they can take on Ground-types such as Excadrill that Skeledirge may not be comfortable staying in on, while in return, Skeledirge can check Pokemon such as Thundurus-T said Flying-types can struggle against. Pivot Pokemon such as Tornadus-T and Choice Scarf Zarude are heavily enjoyed by Skeledirge, as they can safely get it in against Pokemon such as Skarmory and Slowking so that it can start pressuring opposing teams' defensive cores. Paralysis spreaders such as Slowking, Tinkaton, and Bellibolt allow Skeledirge to outspeed foes such as Fezandipiti and Manaphy while also boosting the power of Hex.

ubers.overview: Skeledirge in Ubers is a unique check to one of the most threatening Pokemon in the tier, Koraidon, thanks to its access to Unaware. Koraidon must be careful against Skeledirge, as it can burn Koraidon or potentially OHKO it with Alluring Voice, all while Skeledirge has the option to Tera Fairy to avoid Scale Shot. While Skeledirge is at risk of being 2HKOed by Koraidon's Scale Shot, this is reliant on Koraidon getting 9 total hits of Scale Shot over two turns with sun up. Due to these factors, while Skeledirge cannot always handle Koraidon reliably by itself, Skeledirge's mere presence on the team forces opposing Koraidon to play very carefully, often preventing Koraidon's setup opportunities entirely. Outside of Koraidon, Skeledirge is excellent against most physical threats in the tier; notably, it can counter Zacian-C and take on Extreme Killer Arceus and Calyrex-I quite well. Torch Song provides Skeledirge with a way to not be too passive, and it can let it sweep in certain late-game scenarios. This, however, does not prevent Skeledirge from easily being taken advantage of by special threats such as Miraidon and Kyogre.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Other Tera types such as Tera Flying are possible, but typically, Tera Fairy is too useful against Koraidon to give up. Alluring Voice may seem tempting to use, but it fails to OHKO Koraidon and is generally outclassed by other options.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Miraidon, Kyogre, Eternatus, and other special attackers don't take too much damage from switching in on Skeledirge and can easily force it out with their strong attacks. Kyogre in particular doesn't mind any coverage move and can take great advantage of Skeledirge.

Ho-Oh: Ho-Oh is immune to burns and can wall Skeledirge with its titanic special bulk.

Taunt: Taunt prevents Skeledirge from healing or using Will-O-Wisp, though predicted Taunts can be taken advantage of by Torch Song.

Tera Fire: Tera Fire prevents burns and provides a resistance to Torch Song, though Tera Fire users must be wary of Earth Power or Alluring Voice's confusion.

Physical Wall.description:
Hex is a strong attacking option that takes advantage of Will-O-Wisp and does great damage against Gliscor, 2HKOing at +1. Earth Power nails Miraidon on the switch, and it gives Skeledirge a good way to damage Tera Fire users like Koraidon, Arceus, and Calyrex-I. Will-O-Wisp's burns can do useful chip damage against nearly anything that switches in, and it cripples any physical attacker hit by it. Tera Fairy is mandatory for Skeledirge to take on Koraidon should Skeledirge be too low on HP. Care should be taken when facing Koraidon, as ideally, Tera Fairy should only be used as a last resort. If Skeledirge only takes four hits of Scale Shot upon switching in, it can repeatedly use Slack Off in order to stall out sun turns, or to hope for a Scale Shot miss. In general, being aware of when sun fades is very useful, as Koraidon cannot hope to break Skeledirge without it.

Skeledirge needs teammates that can handle the special attackers that it is weak to. Checks to Miraidon like Ting-Lu and Arceus-Ground are great options, while Eternatus, Koraidon, Miraidon, and Clodsire help against Kyogre. Necrozma-DM and Arceus-Ground are some of few physical attackers that can get past Skeledirge, so checks to them like Arceus-Water, Arceus-Dark, Kyogre, and Bulldoze Gliscor are valuable partners.

Defensive.description:
Due to its great natural bulk, unique defensive typing, and access to Unaware, Skeledirge manages to be a fantastic defensive presence that is able to stave off the likes of Iron Moth, Iron Valiant, and Zamazenta. Moreover, Torch Song prevents it from being too passive, even letting it clean late-game with enough boosts as the foes might fail to KO it in return. Will-O-Wisp quickly neutralizes physical attackers like Dragonite and Zamazenta in addition to powering up Skeledirge's Hex. Maximizing its HP and Special Defense enables Skeledirge to more reliably check Iron Moth, Enamorus, and special Iron Valiant; conversely, maximizing its HP and Defense turns Skeledirge into an immensely sturdy physical wall, forgoing its reliance on spreading burn by leveraging its raw physical bulk to check potent setup sweepers, particularly Dragonite and Zamazenta. Tera Fairy provides Skeledirge with a much-appreciated resistance to Dark while being an overall strong defensive typing, allowing it to safely check Pokemon such as Weavile, Dragapult, and Great Tusk. Tera Water improves its matchup against Gholdengo and Kingambit while still maintaining its good matchup against Iron Moth and Cinderace.

Skeledirge fits on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to force progress while staving off opposing threats. It dislikes taking Knock Off due to its reliance on Heavy-Duty Boots, so it appreciates teammates such as Clefable and Skarmory that can safely switch into Knock Off from Weavile and Iron Valiant. Skeledirge also enjoys having Clefable in particular absorb Salt Cure from Garganacl; Clefable also appreciates Skeledirge's reliability in forcing out Galarian Slowking and Iron Moth. Rillaboom and Galarian Slowking are much-appreciated teammates for Skeledirge, as Rillaboom provides Skeledirge with Grassy Terrain to bolster its longevity in addition to forcing out Ogerpon-W that would otherwise threaten it, whereas Galarian Slowking can pivot into and around powerful wallbreakers such as Kyurem and Walking Wake. It also enjoys entry hazard support from Gliscor and Skarmory wearing down Pokemon such as Choice Specs Kyurem that would otherwise threaten Skeledirge and its team. Skarmory also assists Skeledirge in answering Choice Band Rillaboom, which otherwise threatens it with Knock Off, reliably checks Kingambit for it and appreciates having a consistent check to Iron Moth. Gliscor can spread status with Toxic to power up Skeledirge's Hex and relishes in having a sturdy switch-in to Serperior. Skeledirge also benefits from pairing with fast wallbreakers such as Weavile, Dragapult, and Ogerpon-W, providing them with a sturdy defensive backbone and appreciating having them weaken the opposing team's defenses, as they open up Skeledirge to sweep late-game with Torch Song; it also greatly enjoys pairing with Dragapult in particular, as Dragapult is capable of spreading status effects to a multitude of Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Landorus-T for Skeledirge to take advantage of with its Hex.

Unaware Wall.description: Skeledirge is a defensive wall with a solid typing against threats like Iron Moth and Victini and the ability to act as a bulky win condition thanks to Torch Song. Torch Song is the Fire STAB move of choice, allowing Skeledirge to break through defensive Pokemon like Clefable. Will-O-Wisp cripples physical attackers and induces passive damage, allowing Skeledirge to outlast opposing Pokemon. Scorching Sands is an option to hit Iron Moth and Victini for super effective damage while retaining a chance to cripple Tyranitar and Hydrapple on the switch. Hex synergises with Will-O-Wisp and offers a powerful STAB option that threatens even status absorbers like Clefable. Encore lets Skeledirge set up on defensive walls and punish opposing set up attempts. Heavy-Duty Boots are preferred, as they help Skeledirge avoid entry hazard damage, thereby contributing to its longevity. 44 Defense EVs ensure that Skeledirge lives Rock Blast from Mega Heracross, with the rest of the investment being dumped into Special Defense to better withstand attacks from Iron Moth. Skeledirge finds its home on balance teams that appreciate its ability to compress a solid defensive profile with the ability to snowball against bulkier teams. Knock Off switch-ins are vital for Skeledirge to function optimally. Thus, it appreciates being paired with Pokemon that ignore item removal, such as Mega Venusaur, Clefable, and Z-move users like Hydreigon. Offensive threats such as Excadrill, Mega Aerodactyl, and Aegislash can all muscle through Skeledirge, and thus Skeledirge should be partnered with other physically defensive walls and pivots, such as Slowbro and Mega Venusaur. Specially defensive partners such as Chansey, Assault Vest Tangrowth, and Tyranitar can help stave off special wallbreakers like Alakazam and Thundurus that would otherwise overwhelm Skeledirge. Finally, certain defensive Pokemon such as Garganacl and Tyranitar can repeatedly come in on Skeledirge and force it out with phazing moves or the threat of status or item removal. Teammates that can exploit these Pokemon, such as Excadrill and Serperior, are greatly appreciated.

Air Balloon.description:
• The powerful stallbreaking combination of Torch Song and Unaware breaks through practically any setup threat such as Volcarona or Cresselia with ease. It also allows Skeledirge to attack Weakness Policy users, namely Iron Crown and Metagross without fear.
  • Air Balloon allows Skeledirge to use Will-O-Wisp on physical attackers like Garchomp and Iron Hands without fear of Ground-type coverage, letting it stall them out with Slack Off.
  • Encore is useful against stall Pecharunt and to prevent non-Choice Band Ursaluna from using its Ground-type STAB moves.
  • Maximum HP and Defense EVs ensure that Skeledirge never loses to highly offensive variants of certain attackers, such as Garchomp and non-Encore Annihilape, that it is expected to check.
  • Because Encore itself is not affected by opposing Encore, Skeledirge performs favorably against common Encore + Disable users such as Alolan Ninetales and non-Spirit Break Speed Booster Iron Valiant. Skeledirge should always use Encore first and then alternate between Torch Song and Encore until an opposing Disable is used. After that, Skeledirge is free to use Will-O-Wisp and then continue the sequence to an eventual KO.
  • Choice Band Meowscarada and Hisuian Goodra can dispatch threats to Skeledirge such as Primarina and Raging Bolt while greatly appreciating its additional security against Ursaluna and Iron Crown, which they cannot always handle reliably.

Maranga Berry.description:
• Torch Song is Skeledirge's best option to deal with Iron Crown, Volcarona, Registeel, and Serperior.
  • Skeledirge should immediately use Slack Off against Galarian Moltres and Choice Specs Zapdos, as its Maranga Berry allows it to not be 2HKOed by those threats.
  • Encore should be used against Sylveon and Alolan Ninetales.
  • Will-O-Wisp is for Iron Hands and non-Choice Band Metagross, while Blast Burn is for Choice Band Metagross.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Skeledirge to survive Psyshock twice from Special Attack Booster Energy Iron Crown. The remaining EVs are invested in Special Defense for maximum bulk.
  • Against Encore + Disable Iron Valiant, Skeledirge's best play is to use Encore on the first turn followed by alternating between Torch Song and Encore. While Skeledirge notably does not beat Encore + Disable Iron Valiant sets that use Spirit Break as an attacking move, its Maranga Berry allows it to defeat Moonblast sets.
  • Maranga Berry Skeledirge, while being able to reliably defeat Galarian Moltres, is not able to reliably defeat other Dark-types, such as Hoopa-U, Chien-Pao, and Darkrai. Additionally, it struggles against Water-types, like Manaphy and Ogerpon-W, and Ground-types, like Ursaluna and Landorus-T. Pokemon like Zarude, Iron Hands, and Assault Vest Great Tusk make for good teammates because they defeat some of these threats to Skeledirge while appreciating its ability to defeat Pokemon like Iron Crown and Alolan Ninetales reliably.

monotype.overview:
Ghost

Skeledirge carves out a unique niche for itself on Ghost teams as a physical wall that applies immense pressure on bulkier teams with Torch Song and the combination of Will-O-Wisp + Hex; however, Ghost teams are generally offensively oriented, and Skeledirge is outclassed as a bulky Ghost-type by Gholdengo and Pecharunt. Both of these Ghost-types can spread status, and the former provides immediate wallbreaking power with Nasty Plot and a nearly unresisted STAB combination and the latter can punish physical attackers with Foul Play and provide a safe switch-in to teammates with Parting Shot. Ceruledge can provide the role of a Fire-type for the team, which, with its access to Swords Dance, can make for a powerful wallbreaker and setup sweeper.

Physically Defensive (Ghost).description:
Skeledirge makes for an excellent physical wall on Ghost teams due to its remarkable bulk, access to reliable recovery, and a great ability in Unaware. Torch Song is an incredible STAB move option that pressures teams like Fairy, Steel, and Flying. Will-O-Wisp allows Skeledirge to punish physical attackers like Dragonite, Great Tusk, and Weavile, as well as chipping Clodsire and weakening Earthquake, making it easier for teammates like Gholdengo and Flutter Mane to overwhelm it. Earth Power provides great coverage and targets foes like Heatran, physically defensive Toxapex, and non-Air Balloon Heatran, which resist or are immune to Torch Song. Hex, paired with Will-O-Wisp, provides a decent STAB move option, while Shadow Ball provides more reliable damage in the long run.

Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Swords Dance Mimikyu are excellent partners that can eliminate Dark-types like Greninja, Hydreigon, and non-Choice Scarf Hoopa-U. Dragapult acts as a fast status spreader and can provide incredible wallbreaking power with its exceptional coverage and immense Speed when utilizing Choice Specs to eliminate walls like Dondozo and Toxapex. Furthermore, Flutter Mane and Dragapult can use a Choice Scarf set to revenge kill opposing Choice Scarf users like Meowscarada, Greninja, Roaring Moon, and Iron Boulder, with the latter also removing opposing Choice Scarf Flutter Mane. In return, Skeledirge can handle Steel-types like Corviknight and Skarmory for Mimikyu and Hisuian Goodra for Flutter Mane and Dragapult. Sinistcha boasts Water and Ground resistances, with which it can take on foes like Ogerpon-W, Dondozo, Great Tusk, and the Landorus formes. In return, Skeledirge can handle Fire-types like Cinderace, Volcarona, and Ogerpon-H. Hisuian Zoroark provides a Ghost immunity and, with its ability Illusion, can lure in and remove opposing Ghost-types and ruin walls like Blissey and Clodsire, which Skeledirge struggles against, by tricking them a Choice Scarf or Choice Specs. Gholdengo handles Rock-types like Iron Boulder and Ogerpon-C and provides safe switch-in against status moves like Toxic from Toxapex and Clodsire. With Air Balloon, Gholdengo can switch into Ground-type moves from foes like Great Tusk, Gliscor, and the Landorus formes aimed at Skeledirge, threatening them back with its boosted STAB moves.

Physically Defensive (Fire).description:
Skeledirge is a great choice for Fire teams as a non-passive physically defensive wall. With Will-O-Wisp and Unaware, it can check physical set-up sweepers such as Dragon Dance Dragonite or Belly Drum Azumarill that threaten Fire. Additionally, Torch Song lets Skeledirge fire back against these threats while raising its Special Attack and reducing passitivity. Hex pairs incredibly well with Will-O-Wisp, as it threatens large amounts of damage on burned foes, while Shadow Ball is a more consistent STAB option that hits opposing Skeledirge for more immediate damage. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Skeledirge avoid entry hazards chipping away at it whenever it switches in.

Volcarona is a great teammate for Skeledirge, as it can threaten Dark-types that annoy Skeledirge such as Ting-Lu and Roaring Moon. In return, Skeledirge can burn physical attackers, like Dragonite, giving Volcarona more setup opportunities. Paldean Tauros-F is also a good teammate, since it can threaten the aforementioned Dark-types with its Fighting-type STAB attacks while also having Intimidate to help neutralize physical attackers that Skeledirge cannot handle on its own, such as Roaring Moon. Additionally, its Choice Scarf set can outspeed and KO Greninja. Torkoal pairs well with Skeledirge due to its ability to both remove entry hazards with Rapid Spin and set them up, all while also powering up Skeledirge's Torch Song. Cinderace is a fairly good partner as well due to High Jump Kick, letting it remove Dark-types aiming to threaten Skeledirge, while also being able to remove entry hazards with Court Change and hit Poison-types such as Clodsire and Toxapex with Zen Headbutt. Scovillain is a good partner, since it can remove Water-types such as Dondozo and Rotom-W with its Grass-type STAB attacks. Both Talonflame and Air Balloon Iron Moth alleviate Skeledirge's weakness to threats such as Great Tusk and Ting-Lu.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Defensive Gator.description:
• Thanks to instant recovery, Unaware, and the snowballing potential of Torch Song, Skeledirge is a viable alternative to Dondozo.

  • Will-O-Wisp versus Yawn: Will-O-Wisp vastly improves Skeledirge's match-up against fearsome physical foes such as Kingambit, while Yawn works exceptionally well with Stealth Rock support.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power hits Chi-Yu switch-ins hard and is the best option into Terastallized Ogerpon-H. This is usually the preferred coverage move if using Skeledirge on a stall team.

  • Substitute: Substitute is a good way around status, especially Garganacl's Salt Cure. It also becomes effective when used on Toxic Spikes teams.

Other Options
  • Encore: When paired with Substitute, Skeledirge can seriously punish passive Pokemon, though at a serious cost in coverage.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Skeledirge's defensive typing isn't without its merits, but the wide variety of weaknesses it has often forces Skeledirge to Terastallize to check major threats like Chien-Pao and Dragonite.

  • Fairy: Terastallizing into the Fairy typing removes Skeledirges glaring weakness to Dark and provides an overall superior defensive typing, making Chien-Pao and Ting-Lu far more reasonable to deal with. It also provides a neutral typing for the inevitable Shadow Balls that will be thrown at Skeledirge, like from Flutter Mane or Gholdengo.

  • Water: A Water Tera type lets Skeledirge take on opposing Water-type attacks, providing a valuable turn to burn foes like Urshifu-R. It should be noted that Tera Water tends to be a safer option versus the common Gholdengo, as it does not often run Thunderbolt.

  • Normal: While Tera Normal isn't fantastic defensively, it lets Skeledirge severely punish attempts from special attacking Ghost-types such as Flutter Mane and Gholdengo to check it.

  • Dragon: A Dragon Tera type let's Skeledirge check Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-H simultaneously, though it will likely need help from teammates covering its newfound Fairy-type weakness.

Items

  • Leftovers versus Sitrus Berry: Residual recovery helps Skeledirge use Torch Song more freely. Leftovers is the best option since Skeledirge has instant recovery, but Sitrus Berry with an even HP stat can be used to restore some health after getting hit by Ruination.

  • Ability Shield: Ability Shield keeps Unaware active in the face of Mold Breaker users like Swords Dance Ogerpon-H, which can overwhelm Skeledirge with enough boosts.

  • Covert Cloak: Covert Cloak ignores the secondary effects of Garganacl's Salt Cure as well as stopping stat drops from Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball and Ogerpon-H's Rock Tomb.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: This makes Skeledirge less pressured to Terastallize to rid itself of its Stealth Rock weakness.

Blunder Song.description:
• With Blunder Policy, this Skeledirge provides a unique approach to offense: it'll either put important foes to sleep or threaten to snowball into a sweep with Speed and Special Attack boosts!

  • Shadow Ball: Even with Skeledirge's wide variety of viable Tera types, Shadow Ball is still an excellent secondary STAB attack for hitting Dragapult, Flutter Mane, and opposing Skeledirge.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power is Skeledirge's best option against Garganacl and Chi-Yu, and it makes checking Iron Moth feasible.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Beyond the many weaknesses Skeledirge's typing has, it only has one shot of having +2 Speed, so Terastallizing is preferred over switching when possible.

  • Fairy: With this Skeledirge's more offensive nature, Tera Fairy's immunity to powerful Dragon-type attacks is a big help, and it makes Tera Blast an effective tool against bulky foes such as Ting-Lu, Baxcalibur, and Garchomp.

  • Water: Besides being a fantastic defensive typing, Tera Water gives Skeledirge the chance to pick off weakened Iron Bundle as they use Hydro Pump and gives it a good attack against Chi-Yu, Garganacl, and Iron Moth.

  • Fire: In addition to removing the troublesome Ghost-type weakness, Tera Fire makes sweeping with Torch Song require less setup.

  • Normal: Tera Normal gives Skeledirge a key Ghost-type immunity, taking advantage of common Choiced Ghost-types such as Gholdengo.

  • Grass: Tera Grass vastly improves Skeledirge's matchup against Breloom, Rotom-W, and Brute Bonnet.

EV Spreads

  • All EV spreads for this set should outspeed Dragapult after missing Sing.

  • 204 HP / 4 Def / 132 SpA / 4 SpD / 164 Spe with Modest: The HP investment in this spread lets Skeledirge survive one Earthquake from Garchomp or one Throat Chop from Jolly Focus Sash Chien-Pao when staying not Terastallizing, and one Choice Specs Hydro Pump from Iron Bundle when Tera Fairy or Tera Normal.

  • 92 HP / 252 SpA / 164 Spe with Modest: This spread sacrifices bulk for being able to OHKO Iron Bundle with Torch Song after Stealth Rock damage and doing the same to Kingambit with Tera Fire.

  • 164 HP / 180 Def / 164 Spe with Bold: This defensive spread allows Tera Skeledirge to always avoid a 2HKO from Jolly Choice Band Dragonite's Extreme Speed and avoids getting 2HKOed by Baxcalibur's 4-hit Icicle Spear when Tera Normal or Fairy.

  • 4 Def / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Modest or Timid: A huge sacrifice in bulk makes it harder for Skeledirge to set up, but the Speed investment does allow it to outspeed several major Choice Scarf threats after missing Sing. Modest variants will outspeed up to Modest Choice Scarf Chi-Yu and Jolly Choice Scarf Annihilape, while Timid sets will Speed tie with +1 Espathra.
