Physically Defensive (Ghost).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Defensive.description: Skeledirge is a good physical wall, acting as an important check to Koraidon, Zacian-C, and Extreme Killer Arceus. It can switch into these powerful Swords Dance sweepers, beating them or halting their sweep. Torch Song allows it to potentially sweep a weakened team late-game. Earth Power is an option that chips Miraidon and Eternatus as well as giving it a super effective hit against Tera Fire Zacian-C and Koraidon. Fairy is the ideal Tera type, giving Skeledirge an immunity to Koraidon's Dragon-type attacks and removing its weaknesses to Ground- and Ghost-type attacks from foes like Arceus-Ground, Calyrex-S, and Giratina-O. Tera Flying is a niche option that further improves its matchup against Arceus-Ground while avoiding super effective Behemoth Blade from Zacian-C. Skeledirge is a good fit on balance teams that appreciate it checking common setup threats and carrying teammates that make up for its shortcomings and bad matchups. Skeledirge is very vulnerable to Miraidon, Kyogre, Calyrex-S, and Arceus-Ground, so it appreciates teammates like Ting-Lu, Eternatus, Wo-Chien, and Giratina-O to handle these powerful attackers. Likewise, Skeledirge pairs well with fast attackers and priority users such as Calyrex-S, Choice Scarf Koraidon, and Extreme Killer Arceus, which can threaten the foes that force Skeledirge out and revenge kill Pokemon it checks if it is overwhelmed.

Offensive Rapid Spin.description:
Quaxly fills a niche as an offensive spinner on teams weak to Pokemon like Hisuian Growlithe and Alolan Diglett. Investing 196 EVs into Speed brings Quaxly to the 14 Speed benchmark required to outspeed every unboosted Pokemon after a Rapid Spin boost. Brave Bird allows Quaxly to KO a knocked Foongus after Stealth Rock damage. Quaxly can Terastallize into a Flying-type to 2HKO knocked Mareanie or OHKO Eviolite Foongus after a Rapid Spin boost. Aqua Jet revenge kills many sweepers in the tier such as Tera Ground Vullaby, Hisuian Growlithe, and Alolan Diglett. Moxie can help Quaxly snowball and sweep as it gains boosts.

Quaxly is best paired with Pokemon that appreciate entry hazard removal. Wingull is a good example due to its powerful STAB move combination can help Quaxly overwhelm its checks. Quaxly struggles to deal with Chinchou, so pairing it with Alolan Diglett or Choice Scarf Gothita is wise. Quaxly can also have a hard time picking up KOs on its own, so supporting it with entry hazards and Knock Off users such as Mudbray and Mienfoo is beneficial.

nfe.comments:
Other Options

252 HP / 156 Def / 100 Spe with a Jolly or Timid nature can be used to let Quaxwell outspeed Pignite at the cost of it being frailer as a physical wall.

Checks and Counters

Grass-types: Servine, Ivysaur, and Thwackey all greatly threaten Quaxwell with their Grass-type attacks and Knock Off.

Strong Special Attackers: Girafarig, Duosion, Pikachu, and Hisuian Sliggoo can exploit Quaxwell's weaker Special Defense and general passivity.

Item Disruptors: Pignite, Monferno, and Tinkatuff can lure Quaxwell in and remove its Eviolite, making it easier to take down later in the game. Trick or Switcheroo users like Hattrem, Clefairy, and Frogadier can also greatly cripple Quaxwell by taking Eviolite and potentially giving it a Choice item. Quaxwell also has to be wary of using Rapid Spin against Tinkatuff because of Pickpocket.

Water-immune Pokemon: While uncommon, Water Absorb users like Chinchou and Paldean Wooper blank Flip Turn and can retaliate back with Electric-type STAB moves or utility, respsetively, though Paldean Wooper must be careful of Triple Axel variants.

Defensive.description:
Quaxwell is a staple for NFE, being a crucial backbone to many teams for its ability to remove entry hazards, check top physically offensive threats, and provide defensive pivoting. Quaxwell is the best hazard removal option due to its great defensive typing, good matchup against entry hazard setters, and reliable recovery. Triple Axel can be used to punish Drakloak from trying to block its Rapid Spin and threaten out Grass- and Dragon-type switchins like Thwackey, Servine, Gabite, and Fraxure. Surf gives Quaxwell a better way to punish the likes of Piloswine, Pignite, and Monferno without being forced to pivot with Flip Turn. Encore can be used over Surf on teams that need counterplay to setup users like Scraggy, Duosion, and Wartortle that might otherwise take advantage of Quaxwell's passivity. A Bold nature is preferred if Surf is chosen over Encore.

Quaxwell fits in most team structures except offense and hyper offense, where Wartortle might be favored. It plays an important role in checking top threats like Piloswine, Pignite, and Wartortle, which teammates like Tinkatuff and Koffing appreciate. Eviolite is the most used item in the metagame, meaning entry hazard stacking is a very strong strategy for taking down Quaxwell's teammates, so it is vital in stopping hazard setters like Piloswine, Frogadier, and Tinkatuff. Quaxwell likes to be paired with Pokemon like Hisuian Sliggoo, Koffing, and Tinkatuff, since they can check common Grass-types like Thwackey, Servine, and Ivysaur. Teams that have Drakloak can stop Quaxwell from removing hazards, so teammates such as Girafarig and Monferno are great for being able to switch in and punish them. Quaxwell struggles against heavy-hitting special attackers like Girafarig and Hisuian Sliggoo, so teammates like Dunsparce and Tinkatuff help by keeping them at bay. Keeping its Eviolite is very important for it being able to check all of these threats it is tasked with handling, so Knock Off absorbers such as Koffing and Tinkatuff are greatly appreciated.

Choice Scarf (Fighting).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Rapid Spin (Water).description:
Quaquaval is a decent choice for Water teams thanks to its access to Rapid Spin to remove hazards for its teammates as well as a potential setup tool in Aqua Step in tandem with Moxie. Close Combat targets Dark- and Steel-types such as Hydreigon, Bisharp, and Hisuian Goodra. Alternatively, Brick Break hits the same targets while removing screens in the Grass, Fairy, and Ice matchups. Aqua Step potentially allows Quaquaval to sweep thanks to the Speed boost, getting the jump on the likes of the Ogerpon formes, Volcarona, and Flutter Mane after it is used once. Knock Off can be used to remove crucial items such as recovery items from Corviknight and Toxapex while also targeting Ghost-types that block Rapid Spin like Gholdengo and Dragapult. 164 Speed EVs allow Quaquaval to outpace non-Choice Scarf Flutter Mane after either an Aqua Step or Rapid Spin boost and OHKO it back with Aqua Step.

Quaquaval appreciates entry hazard support from the likes of Gastrodon and Swampert, and their Electric immunity makes them great against threats such as Regieleki, Raging Bolt, and Iron Hands. Toxapex aids Quaquaval in its potential sweeping by inflicting poison on threats such as Iron Valiant, Breloom, and Meowscarada. In return, Quaquaval deals with Ground-types such as Ting-Lu, Gliscor, and Mamoswine. Early-game wallbreakers such as Greninja and Ogerpon-W pair well with Quaquaval, as they handle walls that it struggles with so it can set up late-game. Greninja notably handles Poison-types such as Toxapex, Water Absorb Clodsire, and Amoonguss with Protean-boosted Extrasensory, while Ogerpon-W threatens Dark- and Water-types like Hydreigon and Swampert with Play Rough and Horn Leech. Primarina makes for another great partner, as it serves as a potential wincon by challenging Dragon-types like Garchomp, Gouging Fire, and Latias with its great bulk and access to Calm Mind. Pelipper provides an immunity to Ground with its Flying typing, which allows it to take on Great Tusk and Grass-types such as Breloom, Meowscarada, and Ogerpon-H. Barraskewda serves as a late-game cleaner when boosted under rain, taking on a multitude of speedy threats like Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Iron Valiant, and Sneasler.

(Regulation C) Moxie Sweeper.description:
• Aqua Step and Moxie give Quaquaval a niche as a late-game sweeper that doesn't always need a turn of setup.

  • Aqua Jet: Aqua Jet's ability to pick off weakened threats pairs very well with Moxie, giving it new potential win conditions.

  • Ice Spinner: This is Quaquaval's best way of dealing big damage to Dragonite and Garchomp.

  • Encore: Encore lets Quaquaval punish slower foes such as Corviknight by getting an easy setup opportunity or by simply forcing them to switch.

Other Options

  • Wave Crash: While Wave Crash is Quaquaval's strongest Water-type attack, the recoil can be problematic for Focus Sash sets.

  • Roost: Recovery might seem odd on such an offensive Pokemon, but it helps Quaquaval avoid getting worn down against bulkier teams.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: With Moxie and Aqua Step boosting its offensive output, Quaquaval doesn't always have to rely on Terastallization.

  • Water: Boosting Aqua Step's and Aqua Jet's power opens up new sweeping chances late-game.

  • Electric: Tera Electric lets Quaquaval deal massive damage to Azumarill and wear down Dondozo switch-ins with Tera Blast.

  • Steel: Tera Steel can let Quaquaval get the jump on Fairy- and Dragon-types such as Flutter Mane and Garchomp by resisting their attacks.

Items

  • Focus Sash: With Focus Sash, Quaquaval trades potential wallbreaking for getting surprise sweeps against more offensive teams.

  • Assault Vest: Even without defensive investment, Assault Vest can let Quaquaval take a super-effective hit against some naturally faster threats, such as Psychic Chi-Yu and Energy Ball Iron Moth.

  • Mystic Water: The power increase to Aqua Step and Aqua Jet makes sweeping easier, especially when paired with Tera Water.

(Regulation C) Bulky.description:
• While Quaquaval's bulk is only serviceable, having both Roost and a great support movepool makes it a reasonable defensive option that does particularly well against Kingambit.

  • Taunt and Bulk Up: Taunt pairs particularly well with Bulk Up, letting it set up on surprising foes such as Corviknight.

  • Substitute: Substitute lets Quaquaval stall out OHKO moves from the likes of Dondozo, and it protects it from Garganacl's Salt Cure.

  • Encore: Not only does Encore give Quaquaval new chances to set up, but it also punishes passive play from Unaware walls such as Skeledirge.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Setup Quaquaval will often have to use Terastallization to deal with the checks switching into it.

  • Steel: Tera Steel gives Quauqaval a better matchup against Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle, who can be fairly problematic otherwise.

  • Flying: While it has very little defensive synergy with Quaquaval's previous typing, Tera Flying lets Quaquaval effectively stall out Dondozo if using Taunt, or Substitute and Encore together.

  • Grass: Tera Grass makes Quaquaval's match-up against Rotom-W much smoother.

  • Fairy: With a Fairy Tera type, Quaquaval can set up against most defensive Garchomp thanks to the Dragon Tail immunity.

Items

  • Leftovers: The passive recovery from Leftovers works great with Substitute sets in particular.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet pairs well with Taunt and Tera Flying, letting Quaquaval easily play around Dondozo and Corviknight while setting up Bulk Up.

  • Covert Cloak: If running Substitute isn't possible, Covert Cloak is Quaquaval's best shot at defeating Garganacl.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 156 SpD / 100 Spe with Jolly: This EV spread allows Quaquaval to outspeed Meowscarada after an Aqua Step while raising its special bulk. If not using Bulk Up, running Defense EVs is also viable instead.

  • 244 HP / 4 Atk / 28 Def / 164 SpD / 68 Spe with Careful: The Special Defense investment and Careful nature let Quaquaval survive Timid Flutter Mane's unboosted Moonblast at full health, and the Speed lets it outspeed Garchomp after Aqua Step.

  • 252 HP / 4 Def / 252 Spe with Jolly: Maximizing Speed ensures that Quaquaval outspeeds Choice Scarf Gholdengo, Iron Bundle, Flutter Mane, and Dragapult after using Aqua Step.

Revenge Killer.description:
Nymble functions as a priority attacker capable of being both a revenge killer and a potential late-game cleaner that takes advantage of Tinted Lens and Life Orb-boosted Bug-type moves. First Impression threatens to revenge kill most of the metagame's offensive threats with proper chip damage. Leech Life lets Nymble stay in and make progress while offsetting Life Orb recoil and easing entry hazard chip damage. U-turn supports Nymble's role on momentum-heavy structures allowing switches into bulkier answers to be handled by teammates, and maintaining momentum while racking up chip damage that pushes future First Impression or Leech Life rolls into KO range. Agility allows Nymble to turn into a threatening cleaner that can outrun nearly every relevant Choice Scarf user once it sets up, while Sucker Punch trades that late-game sweeping potential for a more repeatable priority move that punishes full-attacking sets after First Impression has been used. An Adamant Nature with 228 EVs maximizes Nymble's Attack to capitalize on Life Orb and Tinted Lens, while 236 EVs in Speed allow it to hit 14 Speed, letting it outpace some defensive switch-ins, such as Mudbray, Mareanie, and Foongus. Agility allows for sweeping potential and a way to outplay the potential switch outs that Nymble forces. The leftover EVs in Defense help to ease damage against common priority moves such as Fake Out and Sucker Punch. Tera Bug amplifies Nymble's main game plan by further boosting First Impression, Leech Life, and U-turn, turning previously manageable rolls into guaranteed KOs and making it much harder for even bulky Bug-resistant foes to pivot around its attacks once Tera Bug is committed.

Nymble fits best on offensive structures and VoltTurn-style teams that value the combination of strong priority, chip damage, and momentum it provides. It pairs well with pivots like Mienfoo and Chinchou that spread chip damage with U-turn and Volt Switch to take advantage of softened teams that are forced to play conservatively around Tinted Lens-boosted First Impression. Life Orb recoil and frequent switching quickly wear Nymble down, so it appreciates reliable entry hazard control from spinners like Toedscool and Alolan Sandshrew, which keep Stealth Rock and Spikes from limiting the number of times it can safely enter the field. Nymble struggles against bulky Pokemon that can cripple its damage via Knock Off, hampering its revenge killing potential, or threaten to knock it out. Vullaby is an example of both, able to comfortably stomach both First Impression and Sucker Punch while threatening to OHKO with Brave Bird, Air Slash, or Heat Wave. Tinkatink is another such bulky Pokemon that offers resistance to all of Nymble's common moves while threatening to heal off the chip damage with Draining Kiss or punish its momentum-based game plan with Stealth Rock. Nymble appreciates partners like Glimmet and Toedscool that weaken foes into range of Nymble's First Impression or Sucker Punch via entry hazards and pack coverage to address the bulky checks. Other strong partners include Vullaby, Tinkatink, Mareanie, and Alolan Sandshrew; who's coverage are able to help alleviate pressure by threatening Nymble's common bulky checks. In return, Nymble offers immediate revenge killing, strong tempo, and a dangerous late-game presence when its answers have been adequately chipped.

Pivot.description:
Lokix uses First Impression to effectively remove offensive Pokemon like Ogerpon-C, Greninja, Latios, and Zarude. Tinted Lens prevents some of the aforementioned threats from Terastallizing to survive First Impression and lets Lokix still do considerable damage to Bug-resistant foes such as Thundurus-T. For example, Tera Bug First Impression will still be able to KO Tera Steel Latios after a bit of chip damage. Knock Off is good for punishing common switch-ins such as Skarmory, and Sucker Punch allows Lokix to pick off faster threats even after its first turn on the field. This can be important for many fast defensive Pokemon that can sponge a First Impression, like Tornadus-T. Taunt allows Lokix to keep foes like Skarmory and Fezandipiti low. Tera Bug is crucial in order to effectively KO threats such as Excadrill and Thundurus-T. Heavy-Duty Boots is important, as it allows Lokix to come in multiple times even in the presence of Stealth Rock. An Adamant nature is used to maximize First Impression damage.

Lokix fits very well on balance and offense structures, playing the important role of revenge killing many threats. Pokemon like Latios and Greninja appreciate Lokix using U-turn to safely bring them in versus Cobalion, Skarmory, and Heatran. Lokix enjoys being paired with Slowking, as Slowking is able to use Chilly Reception to safely bring Lokix in on Pokemon that threaten Slowking, like Zarude and Greninja. In return, Slowking can help handle Pokemon that Lokix struggles with, like Heatran and Keldeo. Lokix, in general, likes to pair with other pivots. Heavy-Duty Boots Thundurus-T and Tornadus-T are able to check Skarmory and Cobalion for Lokix. Defensive pivots such as Slowking and Rotom-W can check threats such as Tornadus-T for Lokix and bring it in on Pokemon like Zarude. Entry hazard setters, such as Skarmory and Gastrodon, appreciate Lokix's ability to remove foes' Heavy-Duty Boots, and they can check Pokemon like opposing Lokix, Revavroom, and Heatran.

Choice Band.description:
Lokix serves as an unorthodox wallbreaker and anti-offense revenge killer by virtue of its boosted Attack and ability, which limits the number of foes that can resist its attacks. First Impression enables Lokix to move faster than most of the metagame while dealing massive damage to them, including Bug-resistant foes such as Zamazenta and Cinderace. It also allows Lokix to revenge kill offensive threats like Darkrai, Ogerpon-W, Raging Bolt, and Kyurem. U-turn allows Lokix to pivot out of bad matchups like Zamazenta and Corviknight and give some momentum to the rest of its team. Knock Off helps it limit the longevity of threats that rely on Heavy-Duty Boots like Dondozo, Zapdos, and Zamazenta while also hitting foes like Pecharunt. Leech Life provides it with longevity even if it's taking residual damage from Rocky Helmet and entry hazards. Tera Bug provides an extra boost of power, which can allow Lokix to take down foes like Dragapult and a chipped Dragonite with First Impression.

Lokix fits best on bulky offense and balance teams. Teaming up with Pokemon like Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Hisuian Samurott can create entry hazard-stacking cores, making it easier for Lokix to clean up with First Impression. Lokix can also spam Knock Off easily, getting rid of Heavy-Duty Boots from foes and making them vulnerable to its teammates' hazards. Lokix's typing and lack of Heavy-Duty Boots make it extremely susceptible to entry hazards, thus, Great Tusk can help thanks to its bulk and access to Rapid Spin. Hatterene and Iron Treads are also great hazard control options. Other specially offensive teammates like Kyurem, Enamorus, and Raging Bolt can help consistently apply pressure, especially against more physically defensive opponents that Lokix struggles against, such as Gliscor, Zamazenta, and Skarmory. Zamazenta and Gliscor make solid teammates for Lokix, being brought in by Lokix's U-turn and sweeping with their Iron Defense and Swords Dance sets, respectively. Lokix's priority can also help support slower teammates like Iron Crown and Galarian Slowking by picking off fast threats that they struggle with, like Weavile and Darkrai. On more balanced teams, Lokix can be supported by other pivots to continue carrying momentum. Defensive options such as Alomomola, Landorus-T, and Corviknight can provide additional bulk for the team and resist threats to Lokix like Enamorus, while Lokix deals with foes like Ogerpon-W, Darkrai, and Gholdengo. Iron Crown is an offensive pivoting option that forms a solid VoltTurn core with Lokix, taking care of each other's threats; Lokix handles Darkrai and Iron Crown handles Clefable and Tera Fairy users like Raging Bolt. Dragapult is a fast pivot option, taking care of Zamazenta and Dragonite, while Lokix helps it keep Ting-Lu in check.

Boots Attacker.description:
Lokix acts as an incredible revenge killer in the tier, able to utilize its ability in Tinted Lens and having access to a strong priority move in First Impression. First Impression can get around Lokix's modest base Speed to revenge kill Pokemon such as Darkrai and Dragapult by hitting them for considerable damage. U-turn allows Lokix to pivot out of common switch-ins such as Corviknight, Gliscor, and Alomomola, while gaining momentum for the rest of its team. Knock Off removes key items like Rocky Helmet and Heavy-Duty Boots from potential switch-ins such as Landorus-T and Moltres, while hitting Pecharunt and Gholdengo for super effective damage. Sucker Punch can act as a secondary priority move for Lokix, and the combination of Bug- and Dark-type priority moves coupled with its ability makes it doubly effective. Adamant allows Lokix to get the maximum amount of damage from First Impression and Sucker Punch: for example, allowing Lokix to OHKO Cinderace from full HP with First Impression into Sucker Punch and giving Sucker Punch good odds to 2HKO Enamorus, while Jolly allows Lokix to outspeed Pecharunt, Hisuian Samurott, and Gholdengo. Tera Bug allows Lokix to further increase the damage output of both First Impression and U-turn, allowing First Impression to 2HKO Kyurem and unboosted Zamazenta.

This Lokix set fits best on bulky offense and balance teams, as they heavily appreciate its revenge killing abilities and access to key moves like U-turn and Knock Off. Hazard-stacking teams also love Lokix, as it can perform multiple roles such as being a strong Knock Off user, momentum gainer, and revenge killer. Therefore, entry hazard support from Pokemon such as Ting-Lu, Landorus-T, and Gliscor are heavily appreciated, as they can help Lokix against bulkier squads it might otherwise struggle against; Lokix can utilize Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots and eventually wear down its checks such as Moltres and Heatran through hazards. Spinblockers such as Air Balloon Gholdengo and Pecharunt also pair well with Lokix, as they can prevent Rapid Spin from Great Tusk and Iron Treads from removing entry hazards. Pivoting Pokemon such as Landorus-T, Pecharunt, Galarian Slowking, and Iron Crown pair well with Lokix, as they can get it in safely, and in return, Lokix can revenge kill the offensive threats that threaten these teammates such as Ogerpon-W and Darkrai. Iron Crown in particular is a very good Lokix partner, as they can form an effective pivoting core, which can heavily pressure defensive teams. Lokix particularly struggles with faster Pokemon that have a 4x resistance to Bug, such as Iron Valiant and Iron Moth. Therefore, teammates that can handle these Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Moltres for the former and Garganacl and Galarian Slowking for the latter, are heavily appreciated. Slower wallbreakers like Primarina and Raging Bolt help Lokix against bulkier teams, and in return, Lokix can help against offensive structures they may struggle with. Primarina in particular is an amazing Lokix partner, as it can help deal with Gliscor, Corviknight, and Garganacl that Lokix struggles with, while Lokix can punish Ogerpon-W and Galarian Slowking that trouble Primarina. Zamazenta pairs well with Lokix as an offensive partner, as it is able to soft-check the various physical attackers that Lokix might struggle to KO reliably, while Lokix can threaten faster Pokemon such as Deoxys-S and Dragapult that threaten Zamazenta.

Offensive Pivot.description: Lokix stands out as an offensive pivot thanks to Tinted Lens allowing it to pressure standard U-turn switch-ins such as Buzzwole and Aegislash far more consistently than other pivots. Its powerful offensive typing also lets it wear down threats such as Scizor, Tyranitar, and Slowbro. Lokix sports good priority moves such as First Impression and Sucker Punch, which allow it to revenge kill threats such as Mega Latias, Iron Boulder, and Alakazam. Knock Off allows Lokix to force progress against Buzzwole, Clefable, and Celesteela by removing their Leftovers while also being able to punish more offensive checks such as Iron Moth and Mienshao for switching in. Leech Life can be an alternative to Sucker Punch to retain Lokix's longevity against bulkier teams. As a pivot, Lokix values Heavy-Duty Boots to prevent it from being worn down from entry hazards as it comes in and out of the field. Lokix typically runs an Adamant nature to maximize its power, but a Jolly nature can be run to pivot against Excadrill more easily; however, it doesn't have many uses aside from that. Despite having Tinted Lens and a solid offensive typing, many physical walls like Skarmory, Clefable, and Mega Venusaur can still easily halt Lokix's progress, so strong special attackers such as Victini, Alakazam, and Iron Moth can easily serve to deal with them. Other Pokemon that 4x resist Lokix's moves like Iron Moth can still be a chore for Lokix to face, since they can switch in on its Bug-type moves and immediately threaten Lokix and its team with their high-powered attacks. To rectify this, partnering Lokix with threats such as Iron Boulder is necessary to properly deal with with those respective foes. All of them greatly appreciate Lokix's ability to pivot and safely get them onto the field in return. Magnezone in particular is a great partner to easily dispatch Skarmory, Celesteela, and Scizor for Lokix. Entry hazard setters such as Skarmory and Clefable are also good partners to help Lokix break threats such as Mega Venusaur.

monotype.overview:
Dark

Lokix finds itself outclassed by other Dark-type setup sweepers including Bisharp and Hisuian Samurott due to its lack of defensive utility. They both have better offensive stats and matchups, Bisharp has a better typing, and Hisuian Samurott has a better Dark-type STAB move in Ceaseless Edge. Lokix is also weak to Stealth Rock and vulnerable to other entry hazards, meaning it'll be worn down overtime. However, it does possess a positive over the two, and that is Tinted Lens, which allows Lokix to be a frightening setup sweeper for unprepared teams; it can overwhelm Pokemon that resist one of its STAB attacks such as Toxapex and Iron Treads with Leech Life. This combined with two priority moves in First Impression and Sucker Punch to threaten Choice Scarf Meowscarada and Barraskewda gives Lokix a good niche on Dark teams.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Bug

Choice Band can be used over any aforementioned item for its immediate wallbreaking power that allows it to threaten KOs on Flutter Mane with no assistance and Ogerpon-H after Stealth Rock. This power does come at the cost of Lokix's freedom to use any move it wants for the situation, and its teammates like Scizor and Kleavor can handle the aforementioned threats for the team as well.

Swords Dance (Dark).description:
Lokix is a strong, albeit niche revenge killer and setup sweeper thanks to its STAB combination with priority in First Impression and Sucker Punch. Leech Life provides healing for Lokix, letting it gain longevity that consequently helps it set up and snowball more easily. Knock Off neuters Pokemon that are reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots, especially Toxapex and Moltres that try to switch in on it. Sucker Punch allows Lokix to pick off Dragapult, Flutter Mane, and Spectrier as well as Psychic-types, notably Iron Boulder, and revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Meowscarada. Silver Powder boosts Lokix's STAB Bug-type moves with +2 Leech Life OHKOing Ting-Lu after Stealth Rock and First Impression OHKOing bulky Darkrai. Life Orb is an alternative option that lets it obtain the KOs it wouldn't normally obtain with Silver Powder, like Sucker Punch OHKOing Choice Band Excadrill at +2. An Adamant nature can be used for maximum damage output, but Jolly ensures that it outspeeds Timid Gholdengo and Hisuian Samurott.

Mandibuzz is an excellent partner, providing entry hazard removal via Defog and slow U-turn support to bring Lokix in safely, and it checks foes that Lokix struggles with, particularly Ogerpon-H and Scizor with Foul Play. In return, Mandibuzz appreciates Lokix checking opposing Meowscarada and Weavile. Lokix appreciates entry hazard support from Ting-Lu and Hisuian Samurott, letting it grasp the KOs it wouldn't normally get, namely First Impression having a roll to OHKO Ogerpon-H after Stealth Rock with Life Orb. Ting-Lu's titanic Special Defense lets it check such foes as Heatran, Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, and Choice Scarf Archaludon. Hisuian Samurott's excellent Ceaseless Edge and Water typing also provide a ton of utility. Not to mention, its access to Sacred Sword lets it threaten Archaludon and Heatran, and Aqua Cutter allows it to weaken Moltres and Skarmory, all of which Lokix struggles with. Choice Specs Greninja and Choice Scarf Meowscarada form a great offensive core with Lokix. Greninja destroys Fire- and Fairy-types such as Volcarona, Primarina, and Iron Valiant and can support Lokix by luring in special walls, notably Hisuian Goodra and Galarian Slowking. On the flip side, Lokix can threaten Flutter Mane and Meowscarada with its STAB moves. Choice Scarf Meowscarada provides excellent speed control, and with its coverage selection, it can threaten Dragon- and Flying-types, such as Dragonite, non-Choice Scarf Dragapult, Enamorus, and the Landorus formes.

All out Attacker (Bug).description:
Armed with its unique Dark typing, Lokix can look to KO dangerous threats to Bug like Dragapult, Roaring Moon, and Choice Scarf Gholdengo with its powerful priority moves in Sucker Punch and First Impression. U-turn allows Lokix to pivot against walls or checks to it like Toxapex and Heatran, allowing its teammates to come in safely. Knock Off is used as its primary Dark-type STAB move due to its overall power and utility in removing key items from Pokemon like Skarmory's Rocky Helmet or Leftovers and Archaludon's Leftovers. Life Orb allows Lokix to hit the hardest it can against Pokemon like Brambleghast and Gholdengo, which it cannot threaten OHKOs against without it. Heavy-Duty Boots can be used instead to allow Lokix to operate with entry hazards present on the field. Silver Powder is also a strong option that allows Lokix to get a good power boost to its Bug-type STAB move without needing to suffer from Life Orb recoil while also allowing Lokix to bluff having a Choice item.

Lokix appreciates the support of Pokemon that give it opportunities to come into the field safely, so Forretress and its Volt Switch work very well with it. Forretress also comes with the added benefit of removing entry hazards and giving Lokix hazards to work with, notably three layers of Spikes allowing Lokix to comfortably check Flutter Mane. Offensive pivots like Scizor, Kleavor, and Slither Wing all work well with Lokix, as they form a strong U-turn core that bombards the opposing team with strong U-turns as well as their powerful secondary STAB moves. Scizor hits Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Iron Valiant incredibly hard, while Choice Scarf Kleavor destroys Fire- and Flying-types like Ninetales, Ogerpon-H, and Tornadus-T with ease. Slither Wing can also assist with the First Impression pressure while also using its Fighting-type STAB move to break down troublesome Steel-types like Hisuian Goodra and Heatran. Volcarona in particular appreciates Lokix getting rid of offensive checks to it like Roaring Moon and Gallade, as they can stifle its sweep very easily. Araquanid is also an excellent teammate, as its invaluable Sticky Web support allows Lokix to outspeed several Pokemon that would normally outrun it, such as non-Choice Scarf Flutter Mane and Iron Crown.

Swords Dance (Bug).description:
Thanks to Tinted Lens, Swords Dance Lokix can break through the sturdiest walls the tier has to offer such as Toxapex and Gliscor. Although First Impression can only be used once per switch-in, it remains a solid option to revenge kill Roaring Moon and Ogerpon-W. Conversely, Leech Life forgoes the priority effect for consistency, being able to 2HKO Toxapex and defensive Gouging Fire at +2. Sucker Punch OHKOes Choice Specs Dragapult, Latios, and Choice Scarf Iron Boulder while also OHKOing Meowscarada and Greninja at +2. Lastly, Knock Off deals with Gholdengo, can OHKO specially defensive Heatran and Hisuian Goodra at +2 with Stealth Rock up, and removes Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from walls such as Toxapex and Archaludon. Heavy-Duty Boots can be chosen to improve Lokix's longevity and let it switch in multiple times, although its raw power will be hampered in the process. An Adamant nature lets Lokix secure an OHKO on Barraskewda with First Impression, as well as OHKOing specially defensive Corviknight with Knock Off at +2 after Stealth Rock, but this comes at the cost of being outsped by Ceruledge, Jolly Mamoswine, and Great Tusk.

Lokix benefits much from its teammates breaking holes in the opposing team. Thanks to Bullet Punch and great physical coverage options in Close Combat and Trailblaze, Scizor can lead the offensive in matchups that Lokix struggles with such as Fairy and Rock as well as be a driving force in the Steel matchup. In return, Lokix helps Scizor to break the Steel defensive core by taking care of Gholdengo. Choice Scarf Kleavor supports Lokix's rampage with Stone Axe and provides an edge in the Fire matchup by wrecking Volcarona, Cinderace, and Ninetales. Bulky Quiver Dance Volcarona is an incredible teammate for Lokix, as it can set up on Pokemon that would otherwise prove deadly for Lokix such as Skarmory and Iron Hands, spread burns to physical attackers to facilitate Lokix's setup, and swiftly remove opposing Scizor and Archaludon. Similarly, Frosmoth can set up on special sweepers that Lokix cannot reliably OHKO like Raging Bolt, Kyurem, and non-Choice Specs Flutter Mane, eliminating the physical walls that would prevent Lokix from sweeping in the process. Being prone to entry hazard damage, Lokix appreciates Forretress's ability to remove them from the field. Forretress also supports Lokix by setting up Spikes and slow pivoting in Lokix while being bulky enough to come in on opposing Lokix. Araquanid is another key support Pokemon for Lokix, as it can set Sticky Web to let Lokix outspeed Choice Scarf Kleavor as well as checking Volcarona and Ninetales and KO them back. Other Sticky Web users include Galvantula and Ribombee. Galvantula improves the Water matchup with its access to Energy Ball to hit Swampert and Gastrodon, while Ribombee comes with a solid Speed tier to guarantee Sticky Web setup and the ability to paralyze targets.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to the next generation of Battle Stadium Singles! In this new and exciting metagame, new ideas are constantly developing, so this analysis will constantly be updated to reflect metagame trends.

If you feel this analysis is not up to date, feel free to check out the thread for this Pokemon and post suggestions. For more resources on Series 1 in general, check out this thread.

Tinted Offense.description:
• The combination of First Impression and Tinted Lens make Lokix one of the most threatening revenge killers in the format, able to outprioritize and KO foes regardless of resistance.

  • First Impression is Lokix's most important attack, but it can only be used as the first attack after it switches in.

  • U-turn can be punishing against offensive and slow teams as the lack of resists means Lokix can keep switching in and dealing big damage with First Impression, at the cost of making it vulnerable to hazards.

  • Leech Life is the strongest Bug-type move Lokix learns outside of First Impression, with the added benefit of healing recoil damage.

  • Sucker Punch is a powerful STAB priority move, enabling Lokix to outprioritize foes even after it has used First Impression.

  • Axe Kick is the only coverage move of note in Lokix's moveset due to its high Base Power. Be wary of the low accuracy and recoil that occurs should it miss.

  • Throat Chop is the most powerful Dark-type move Lokix learns. It also has the side benefit of disabling Roar from Hippowdon and Hyper Voice from Sylveon.

  • Swords Dance is an option to make Lokix a sweeper instead of a revenge killer.

Items

Life Orb: Life Orb enables easier revenge kills at the cost of recoil.

Silver Powder: Silver Powder raises the power of First Impression without the recoil from Life Orb, and it also frees up Life Orb for a teammate to use instead.

Tera Types

Bug: A Bug Tera Type increases the damage of First Impression, allowing Lokix to OHKO foes it could not otherwise, such as Dragapult.

Revenge Killer (Atk).description:
Lokix functions as a revenge killer, leveraging its strong priority options to keep offensive threats in check. First Impression is Lokix’s main weapon, boasting immense power and benefiting from Tinted Lens, which allows it to deal heavy damage even to Bug-resistant foes. Knock Off provides excellent utility by removing key defensive items such as Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from common switch-ins like Corviknight and Zapdos, making them easier to wear down throughout the game. Sucker Punch complements First Impression by granting Lokix a secondary priority move, and U-turn rounds out the set by allowing Lokix to maintain momentum and safely bring in teammates like Hisuian Electrode and Gholdengo that can threaten Lokix's checks. Heavy-Duty Boots ensures Lokix can pivot in and out throughout the match, although Silver Powder can be used as an alternative when the team has entry hazard removal. Tera Bug further enhances Lokix's revenge killing power, turning First Impression into a nuke that can even threaten neutral targets after minimal chip damage.

Lokix appreciates high-Attack gods such as Ho-Oh and Necrozma-DM, which greatly amplify its First Impression damage and improve its revenge killing reliability. However, Lokix can also pair well with lower-Attack gods like Kyurem-W and Arceus, as it benefits from any Attack boost while offering valuable priority and pivoting support in return. Lokix fits best on slower balance and bulky offense teams that struggle with faster offensive threats, as it provides a reliable emergency button against sweepers like Roaring Moon, Ogerpon-W, and Darkrai. In return, the defensive teammates give Lokix the turns it needs to wear down opposing checks. Lokix thrives alongside pivoting partners that can get it onto the field safely. Offensive pivots like Hisuian Electrode form strong VoltTurn cores that apply continuous pressure, while defensive pivots such as Rotom-W and Corviknight can take hits and bring Lokix in safely for revenge kills. Because of the lack of a boosting item, Lokix appreciates chip damage to push targets into OHKO range. Thus, teammates able to provide passive chip damage such as Garganacl and Sinistcha make good partners. Furthermore, entry hazard support from setters such as Skarmory, Clefable, and Ting-Lu are very appreciated, especially since Lokix's Knock Off removes foes' Heavy-Duty Boots, allowing its team's hazards to be more effective.

Kamen Rider (Swords Dance) (Bug).description: Access to Swords Dance, a nearly unresisted STAB combination thanks to Tinted Lens, and priority options in Sucker Punch and First Impression make Lokix an excellent wallbreaker and cleaner for Bug teams. Leech Life allows Lokix to take advantage of and beat passive walls, 2HKOing Gliscor, Blissey, and Ting-Lu at +2 while keeping itself healthy. Knock Off lets Lokix makes progress against defensive switch-ins like Archaludon, Skarmory, and Great Tusk by removing their items. Alternatively, First Impression is an excellent tool to pick off faster threats like Alolan Raichu, Greninja, and Ogerpon-W. Sucker Punch lets Lokix function as an effective late-game sweeper, picking off weakened threats like Iron Boulder, Sneasler, and Tapu Koko or outright KOing them at +2. Furthermore, when boosted by Darkinium Z, it allows Lokix to KO or heavily dent walls like Heatran, Mega Sableye, and Celesteela. Choice Scarf Kleavor uses its Rock typing to serve as a revenge killer that targets Flying- and Fire-types like Tornadus-T, Mega Charizard Y, and Cinderace while also setting Stealth Rock with Stone Axe. Araquanid and Galvantula provide Sticky Web support, allowing Lokix to outspeed threats like the Ogerpon formes, Mega Gallade, and Nidoking. Araquanid leverages its high special bulk and Fire resistance to handle foes like Volcarona and Iron Moth, while Galvantula pressures Flying- and Water-types like Skarmory and Toxapex. Volcarona threatens Steel-types like Skarmory, Celesteela, and opposing Mega Scizor. Mega Scizor eliminates Rock- and Fairy-types like Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Diancie, and Iron Valiant. Mega Pinsir eases Fighting matchups, threatening foes like Keldeo and Kommo-o, and it can also break through walls like Toxapex and Mega Venusaur that Lokix struggles with.

Offensive.description:
Pawmot finds a niche over other Fighting-type wallbreakers such as Paldean Tauros-F and Heracross thanks to its great STAB combination that hits Pokemon like Milotic and Cramorant; wide variety of coverage and utility options; great Speed; and useful abilities. It is also the only physical Electric-type in the tier. Ice Punch provides coverage for defensive Grass-types such as Amoonguss and Venusaur as well as Golurk, and it also does more damage to other Pokemon like Colbur Berry or itemless Palossand. Knock Off provides utility by removing items from Pokemon like Galarian Slowbro and Mudsdale while still providing coverage for Ghost-types such as Golurk and Palossand. Pawmot has a wide variety of options in for its final moveslot; Mach Punch gives Pawmot valuable priority against weakened attackers and Choice Scarf users such as Zoroark, Ambipom, and Rotom-Cut. Rest should be paired with Natural Cure takes advantage of Pokemon that Pawmot forces to switch out like Bombirdier and Milotic. Finally, Volt Switch allows Pawmot to pivot against Pokemon like Goodra and Rotom-Heat and should be run with Heavy-Duty Boots. Life Orb allows Pawmot to achieve rolls such as having a chance to 2HKO Assault Vest Galarian Slowbro with Knock Off and OHKOing Delphox with Double Shock, but Heavy-Duty Boots lets it switch in more safely. Iron Fist boosts the power of Ice Punch and Mach Punch, but Natural Cure naturally pairs well with Rest and can allow Pawmot to recover from burn and poison. It should should be used when not running Ice Punch or Mach Punch. Volt Absorb can allow Pawmot to operate as an Electric immunity for its team, but this is generally not needed, and its other abilities are more viable. Tera Electric boosts the power of Double Shock, allowing Pawmot to OHKO Skuntank and Milotic, and makes the move spammable thanks to cancelling out the type loss from Double Shock. It also provides a useful Flying resistance, which is helpful against Pokemon like Choice Scarf Bombirdier.

Pawmot finds itself on offense and balance teams looking for a strong wallbreaker that can also function as a utility Pokemon with Knock Off, pivoting, and revenge killing. Pawmot struggles to break through certain physical walls such as Amoonguss, Palossand, and Mudsdale, so checks to these threats like Galarian Slowbro and Wo-Chien make excellent partners. Pawmot appreciates entry hazard control from Pokemon like Cramorant, Tatsugiri, and Coalossal due to it switching out often due to Double Shock, especially if it is running Life Orb. Cramorant and Coalossal can also sponge hits from faster foes that threaten Pawmot such as Choice Scarf Heracross and Ambipom, while Tatsugiri can form a potent wallbreaking core with Pawmot. In turn, Pawmot takes care of their checks such as Snorlax and Scrafty. Pawmot's ability to revenge kill Pokemon like Paldean Tauros-F, Delphox, and Bruxish means that walls checked by these threats like Alolan Sandslash and Florges are excellent partners.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Electric

All-out Attacker: Leppa Berry can be used over Punching Glove to allow Pawmot to use Revival Blessing twice in one game.

All-out Attacker (Electric).description:
Pawmot is a great wallbreaker on Electric teams, outspeeding foes like Garchomp, Landorus, and Sandy Shocks. Close Combat does not receive the benefits of Pawmot's ability and item, but it helps beat pesky foes like Ursaluna-B, Hisuian Goodra, and Baxcalibur, which are immune to or resist its Electric-type attacks. Close Combat is also a good move to beat foes like Ting-Lu and Hisuian Goodra which Pawmot's teammates might struggle against. Thunder Punch is an alternative STAB move, as it hits common walls like Corviknight and Toxapex while also threatening Pelipper on rain teams, thus preventing the opponent from setting up rain for Barraskewda repeatedly. Thunder Punch also helps versus Belly Drum Azumarill, preventing it from setting up. Mach Punch is Pawmot's preferred second STAB move, as it offers strong priority, securing an OHKO on foes like Chien-Pao, Meowscarada, and Greninja after a single layer of Spikes. Mach Punch also nullifies Bisharp's Sucker Punch by outspeeding it with priority. Revival Blessing is another alternative that can be used over Mach Punch, as it offers a unique and valuable type of utility by allowing a teammate to be revived. This may prove to be a huge benefit in some matchups like the Electric mirror, where Pawmot can revive teammates like Sandy Shocks after the opposing Rotom-W is low on HP or has already fainted. Ice Punch hits foes like the Landorus formes, Gliscor, Clodsire, and mixed Amoonguss. The last coverage move is Seed Bomb, as it hits Pokemon like Gastrodon, Quagsire, and Rotom-W, which can prove troublesome for Pawmot's teammates to break. Seed Bomb also compounds with Thunder Punch to hit every Water-type in the game for super effective damage, making Pawmot incredibly powerful in the Water matchup. Punching Glove helps Pawmot avoid chip damage from Rocky Helmet on foes like Rough Skin Garchomp while also avoiding status effects like burn from foes like Flame Body Volcarona, Moltres, and Talonflame.

Pawmot greatly benefits from teammates like Regieleki, which can use Rapid Spin to remove entry hazards for Pawmot and pivot well into other teammates with the help of Volt Switch. Regieleki's extremely high Speed tier also allows it to revenge kill foes like Enamorus, weakened Walking Wake, and, if using Magnet and Wild Charge, Flutter Mane. In return, Regieleki appreciates Pawmot dealing with Ground-type Pokemon, like Quagsire and Gliscor, with the help of Seed Bomb and Ice Punch due to Regieleki's lack of coverage moves. Iron Hands is another great teammate, as it allows Pawmot to run alternative sets, like Thunder Punch over Fighting-type STAB moves, since Iron Hands can run these moves in its stead. Assault Vest Iron Hands also has immense bulk and acts like a sponge for special attacks from foes like Choice Scarf Flutter Mane and Volcarona, which can cause great problems for Pawmot, since it is relatively frail. Iron Hands can also slow pivot into Pawmot with the help of Volt Switch. In return, Pawmot deals with walls like Quagsire and offensive Rotom-W, which Iron Hands may face difficulty in breaking. Sandy Shocks sets hazards like Stealth Rock and Spikes to boost Pawmot's wallbreaking potential by providing necessary chip on foes while also being able to provide a Ground immunity thanks to Air Balloon, thus behaving like a switch-in against foes like opposing Sandy Shocks, Choice Scarf Iron Treads, Gholdengo, and Skeledirge. In exchange, Pawmot helps break foes like the Landorus formes and Gliscor that wall Sandy Shocks completely. Pawmot also threatens foes like Baxcalibur, Dragonite, mixed Amoonguss, and Galarian Slowking, which can cause problems for Sandy Shocks. Rotom-W is an essential teammate for Pawmot, as it provides a much-needed Ground immunity while also offering great utility with its defensive sets that run Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave. Hydro Pump on Rotom-W deals with pesky Ground-types like Great Tusk and Mamoswine, which Pawmot struggles against. Defensive Rotom-W benefits from Pawmot's ability to take down foes like Water Absorb Clodsire and Gastrodon. Thus, together they form a strong core on Electric-type teams. Teammates like Thundurus, Thundurus-T and Zapdos provide a Ground immunity for Pawmot while also threatening strong Fighting-type foes like Zamazenta and Great Tusk. Zapdos can break these physically bulky Pokemon with the help of Hurricane, while Thundurus-T can use Psychic as a coverage move for Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and physically defensive Amoonguss. In return, they appreciate Pawmot's ability to break specially defensive walls that hinder Zapdos and Thundurus-T's wallbreaking capability. Thundurus provides great support with Prankster Thunder Wave, paralyzing fast foes like Dragapult and Flutter Mane and allowing Pawmot to outspeed them. Magnezone pairs well with Pawmot, as it can act like a sponge for Fairy-type moves from foes like Hatterene, Iron Valiant, and Flutter Mane and force them out with Flash Cannon. In return, Pawmot helps to break special walls like Galarian Slowking and Clodsire, which Magnezone can't break.

Choice Scarf (Electric).description:
Pawmot is a great Choice Scarf user on Electric teams by virtue of its coverage and utility, being able to deal with Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane. With Revival Blessing, Pawmot can give second chances to fallen offensive Pokemon such as Iron Hands and Choice Specs Zapdos to punch holes in opposing teams. Double Shock allows Pawmot to OHKO threats such as Flutter Mane and Azumarill as well as finishing off Iron Valiant, but this comes with the downside of Pawmot immediately being forced out after using the move. Ice Punch allows Pawmot to deal decent damage to Ground-types that resist both its STAB moves, notably OHKOing both Landorus formes as well as 2HKOing both Iron Leaves and Clodsire. Volt Switch allows Pawmot to pivot out of a check such as Amoonguss into one of its teammates to deal with it. Play Rough and Seed Bomb are usable alternatives, with Play Rough being able to 2HKO Sableye while still hitting Dragon-types and Seed Bomb dealing with Water/Ground types that most Electric-type Pokemon cannot handle efficiently. Notably, Seed Bomb OHKOes specially defensive Gastrodon and 2HKOes physically defensive Quagsire. Grass Knot can also be used, being able to 2HKO Quagsire as well as Great Tusk.

Sandy Shocks provides great hazard support to wear down incoming foes for Pawmot to take advantage of. Ground-immune Pokemon such as Zapdos and Rotom-W are appreciated by Pawmot, being able to switch into an anticipated Ground-type attack from the likes of Great Tusk and Landorus-T. Zapdos can also threaten Grass-types such as Amoonguss, while Rotom-W together with Pawmot can overwhelm Quagsire. In return, Pawmot can revive one of them so it can continue checking Ground-types when needed. Regieleki provides hazard removal and a fast pivot for Electric teams, and in return it appreciates Ground-types being lured in and removed by Seed Bomb Pawmot variants. Assault Vest Iron Hands is another great teammate, being able to switch into attacks that could OHKO Pawmot such as Dragapult's Draco Meteor and Enamorus's Moonblast. Iron Hands can also OHKO the latter when running Heavy Slam. In return, Pawmot can run Seed Bomb to handle Water/Ground types Iron Hands cannot efficiently threaten such as Quagsire, and Swords Dance variants of Iron Hands appreciate it removing Flutter Mane and wearing down Sableye. Magnezone is a great partner, being able to threaten the Fairy-types that can threaten Pawmot such as Hatterene and Flutter Mane.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis is for the Regulation C format of Battle Stadium Singles, which lasts until June 30th, 2023. For more information on this format and its current events, check out the format page!

If you feel this analysis is missing anything important or needs an update, feel free to suggest any changes here.

Offensive Utility.description:
• Pawmot separates itself from Iron Hands by having an excellent support movepool and a good Speed tier.

  • Double Shock and Close Combat: Double Shock and Close Combat are its most important attacks, but note that it can only use Double Shock once without Terastallizing. Once Terastillized, Pawmot you can use Double Shock continuously for big damage, even on foes that resist it.

  • Mach Punch: Priority allows Pawmot to revenge kill better, hitting Meowscarada, Roaring Moon, and Iron Bundle super effectively.

  • Ice Punch: Ice Punch gives Pawmot coverage against Ground-types, most notably Great Tusk, Clodsire, and Garchomp, in addition to hitting Dragonite for lots of damage before it Terastallizes.

  • Revival Blessing: Revival Blessing's one shot of reviving a teammate gives Pawmot an extremely unique niche in turning battles around, though it doesn't fit all offensive teams.

  • Nuzzle: This is notably one of the few ways to inflict paralysis on Gholdengo. Nuzzle is best when used with a Focus Sash, as Pawmot can paralyze the foe and outspeed it the next turn, getting another move off before it faints.

  • Encore: Encore does a great job of punishing passive play, and prevents easy setup from slower defensive foes such as Garganacl.

Other Options
  • Fake Out: This can be used to get an edge against common Focus Sash leads such as Meowscarada.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Situational: Terastallizing is only needed if Pawmot is on the field long enough for repeated uses of Double Shock.

  • Electric: An Electric Tera Type allows Pawmot to continuously use Double Shock, making it an effective late-game cleaner.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash trades the damage boost from the other items for better opportunities to use support moves.

  • Life Orb: Life Orbs enables easier revenge kills at the cost of recoil.

  • Magnet: Magnet will power up Double Shock without the recoil from Life Orb, and it also frees up Life Orb for a teammate to use instead.

Abilities

  • Iron Fist: This boosts the power of Mach Punch and Ice Punch, giving Pawmot more powerful priority and coverage.

  • Volt Absorb: Volt Absorb's Electric immunity stops Magnezone, Rotom-W, and Rotom-H from using Volt Switch to create safe switch-ins.

  • Natural Cure: This allows Pawmot to take status moves more freely, such as Yawn from Dondozo or Will-O-Wisp from Skeledirge.

Offensive.description:
• Pawmot's good offensive stats and unique support movepool give it a good niche in the metagame.

  • Double Shock and Close Combat are its most important attacks, but note that it can only use Double Shock once without Terastallizing. Once Terastillized, Pawmot you can use Double Shock continuously for big damage, even on foes that resist it.

  • Mach Punch allows Pawmot to revenge kill better, hitting Meowscarada, Choice Scarf Hydreigon, and Tera Steel Dragapult super effectively.

  • Ice Punch gives Pawmot coverage against Ground-types, most notably Clodsire and Garchomp, in addition to hitting Dragapult for lots of damage.

  • Revival Blessing's one shot of reviving a teammate give Pawmot an extremely unique niche in turning battles around, though it doesn't fit all offensive teams.

  • Nuzzle paralyzes foes, and it's notably one of the few ways to inflict paralysis on Gholdengo. This move is best when used with a Focus Sash, as Pawmot can paralyze the foe and outspeed it the next turn, getting another move off before it faints.

  • Encore does a great job of punishing passive play, and prevents easy setup from slower defensive foes such as Garganacl.

  • Fake Out can be used to get an edge against common Focus Sash leads such as Meowscarada.

Abilities

  • Iron Fist: This boosts the power of Mach Punch and Ice Punch, giving Pawmot more powerful priority and coverage.

  • Volt Absorb: Volt Absorb's Electric immunity stops Magnezone, Rotom-W, and Rotom-H from using Volt Switch to create safe switch-ins.

  • Natural Cure: This allows Pawmot to take status moves more freely, such as Yawn from Dondozo or Will-o-Wisp from Skeledirge.

Items

  • Life Orb: Life Orbs enables easier revenge kills at the cost of recoil.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash trades the damage boost from the other items for better opportunities to use support moves.

  • Magnet: Magnet will power up Double Shock without the recoil from Life Orb, and it also frees up Life Orb for a teammate to use instead.

Tera Types

  • Electric: An Electric Tera Type allows Pawmot to continuously use Double Shock, making it an effective late-game cleaner.

Fighting-type Pikachu (All-Out-Attacker).description: Using its STAB combination, Speed, coverage moves, and ability Iron Fist, Pawmot punches its way through Dark, Normal, Flying, and Dragon teams. Close Combat allows Pawmot to demolish Pokemon that its teammates may struggle with beating such as Blissey, Hisuian Goodra, and Ursaluna. Ice Punch targets Ground-, Dragon-, and Grass-types such as Garchomp, the Landorus formes, and Tapu Bulu. Thunder Punch alongside Ice Punch gives Pawmot perfect coverage to demolish Flying teams. Double Shock may be used as an alternative to Thunder Punch for more damage output that can enable Pawmot to OHKO Volcarona while Electric Terrain is up, though it can only be used once and forces Pawmot to switch out in order to use Double Shock again. Mach Punch picks off Sand Rush Excadrill, Meowscarada, Greninja, and Roaring Moon. Alternatively, Seed Bomb is an option that completes Pawmot's coverage against Water teams. Punching Glove provides a boost to Thunder Punch, Ice Punch, and Mach Punch while allowing Pawmot to avoid taking Rough Skin and Rocky Helmet damage when using Ice Punch against Garchomp. Expert Belt can be used to enhance Pawmot's wallbreaking capabilities, allowing Pawmot to OHKO Blissey, Ursaluna, defensive Garchomp, Gliscor, and Mega Swampert if utilizing Seed Bomb. Tapu Koko forms a nice offensive core with Pawmot that can overwhelm Dark, Flying, and Dragon teams. Tapu Koko also sets up Electric Terrain to amp up Pawmot's Electric-type STAB, giving Pawmot the potential to OHKO physically defensive Pokemon such as Slowbro, Corviknight, and Toxapex if using Double Shock and Expert Belt while Electric Terrain is up. In turn, Pawmot deals with specially defensive Pokemon such as Blissey, Hisuian Goodra, and Alolan Muk for Tapu Koko. Regieleki and Alolan Raichu are valuable teammates, as they provide speed control, with Alolan Raichu outspeeding Mega Aerodactyl, Mega Swampert under rain, and Sand Rush Excadrill while Electric Terrain is up. Special attackers in general such as Regieleki, Alolan Raichu, and Tapu Koko appreciate Pawmot dealing with specially defensive Pokemon. Pawmot likes having Zapdos and Rotom-W around as teammates due to their immunity to Ground-type attacks. Zapdos decimates Grass-types such as Mega Venusaur, Celebi, and Iron Leaves for Pawmot. Rotom-W provides a switch-in that helps ease the Ground matchup while providing entry hazard removal and pivoting support with Defog and Volt Switch. Pawmot helps Rotom-W deal with Ground-types through its coverage moves and can make progress against Ground-types Rotom-W can't beat such as Clodsire and Gastrodon.

ru.overview: Boasting the incredibly strong Technician Population Bomb along with the ability to set up and remove hazards in a single turn, Maushold stands out as one of the most threatening setup sweepers in the metagame. Due to its ability to outspeed and OHKO the majority of the tier after a single turn of boosting, it is imperative for every non-hyper offense team to have an answer to Maushold. Unfortunately for Maushold, this can be done incredibly easily by having any decently defensive Pokemon hold Rocky Helmet, as the multihit nature of Population Bomb simultaneously serves as its greatest strength and its Achilles' heel. Maushold's relative frailty also means that it can be easily dealt with by strong priority users and bulkier Pokemon that are able to survive a hit and KO it back.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Maushold's greatest weakness, contact effects, can be neutralized with Protective Pads, albeit at the cost of drastically decreasing Population Bomb's reliability. Loaded Dice is an alternative to Wide Lens that improves Bullet Seed's reliability while still guaranteeing at least 4 hits with Population Bomb.

Checks and Counters

Rocky Helmet: Any of the physical walls in the tier, including Chesnaught, Gastrodon, and Slowbro, can eliminate Maushold with the help of Rocky Helmet, with the interaction causing Maushold to faint after hitting just 6 times from full health.

Faster Wallbreakers: Faster offensive Pokemon such as Barraskewda and Choice Scarf users such as Flamigo and Krookodile can revenge kill an unboosted Maushold.

Steel-type Wallbreakers: Powerful Steel-types such as Hisuian Goodra and Choice Specs Magnezone can survive a hit from Maushold and KO it back. Hisuian Goodra in particular can temporarily cripple Maushold with Gooey and therefore allow its teammates to deal with it even if Maushold has accrued several Tidy Up boosts.

Mimikyu: In the hyper offense mirror matchup, Mimikyu is one of the only Pokemon that can consistently deal with Maushold thanks to its immunity to Population Bomb. Mimikyu does, however, need to be wary of Bite that can take it out with enough flinches and Bullet Seed that can potentially KO Mimikyu past Disguise after Maushold gets one or two Attack boosts.

Tidy Up.description:
Set Details

Tidy Up offers incredible utility, as it allows Maushold to set up and unpreventably remove hazards in a single slot. Bite is a go-to coverage option, as it allows Maushold to hit Ghost-types like Basculegion-F and Gengar. Bullet Seed is an alternative that can similarly hit the aforementioned Ghost-types as well as Rocky Helmet Slowbro, which is one of Maushold's most common checks, at the cost of fizzling against Gengar. Encore can provide Maushold with free turns by locking an opponent into a useless move, which can often be game-winning due to Maushold's unrivaled power. Low Kick is another coverage option that enables Maushold to deal with bulky Steel-types such as Hisuian Goodra, Registeel, and Eviolite Bisharp. Wide Lens is crucial for Maushold to improve Population Bomb's consistency, as otherwise it only has an approximate 35% chance to hit 10 times. Technician boosts all of Population Bomb, Bite, and Bullet Seed, enabling Maushold to be incredibly threatening despite its low Attack stat. Tera Ghost provides Maushold with valuable immunities to Fighting and Normal and a resistance to Bug, which can prevent it from getting revenge killed by Fighting-type attacks, including Body Press from Chesnaught and Close Combat from Terrakion, as well as Entei's Extreme Speed. This can be capitalized on with Encore to give Maushold incredibly valuable free turns to set up. Tera Normal can be used instead to boost Population Bomb's power, which allows Maushold to OHKO bulky Pokemon like Wo-Chien and specially defensive Umbreon without needing to set up.

Maushold fits best on offense, particularly hyper offense, structures, primarily due its ability to remove hazards despite already being an incredibly powerful setup sweeper. Because of this, it synergizes with other setup sweepers like Throat Spray Yanmega and Mirror Herb Entei that are weak to Stealth Rock. While Maushold can be easily punished with physical walls holding Rocky Helmet such as Gastrodon, Slowbro, and Chesnaught, it can often deal massive amounts of damage to them before fainting, which can give other physically offensive setup sweepers such as Bisharp and Mimikyu the wiggle room to pull off a sweep later in the game. Maushold particularly benefits from specially offensive teammates like Toxtricity and Gardevoir that can exploit any of the aforementioned physical walls hoping to get rid of Maushold. On generally offensive structures, Maushold can act as the primary setup sweeper and therefore greatly appreciates Knock Off support from Pokemon like Krookodile and Crawdaunt to remove Rocky Helmet from opposing physical walls.

Tidy Up Sweeper.description:
Tidy Up Maushold is a good setup sweeper for Normal teams, as it is able to outspeed and take out threats like non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant, non-Iron Defense Zamazenta, and Urshifu-R. At +1 Attack, Population Bomb becomes a fierce move, taking out a plethora of threats not running Rocky Helmet, notably Toxapex and Gouging Fire. Bite allows Maushold to threaten Ghost-types like Dragapult and Hisuian Zoroark at +1, while Encore lets Maushold lock foes into moves such as locking Corviknight into Defog and Bisharp into Sucker Punch; this allows Maushold to get a potential Tidy Up turn. Low Kick can be run over Encore to hit pesky Steel- and Rock-types like Bisharp, Hisuian Goodra, Heatran, and Tyranitar. Play Rough threatens Dark- and Dragon-types like Hydreigon, Sableye on a switch in, and unboosted Roaring Moon, but running it leaves Maushold vulnerable to Bisharp. Wide Lens is the best item for Maushold to ensure Population Bomb is accurate as possible.

Hisuian Zoroark is a great teammate for Maushold, providing a Fighting immunity while also fooling its foes due to Illusion. It also takes out physically bulky Pokemon like Gholdengo and Archaludon with Shadow Ball and Focus Blast and can use Trick to lock walls like Sableye into undesirable moves by giving them Choice Specs, which eases Maushold's sweeping capabilities. Ditto reverse sweeps against potential setup sweepers like Chien-Pao and Ceruledge, while Maushold provides entry hazard removal via Tidy Up, keeping Ditto as healthy as possible. Indeedee eases the Fighting matchup by dealing with Zamazenta and Choice Specs Keldeo with Expanding Force. It also provides Healing Wish support, allowing one of its teammates a second chance to sweep, and sets up Psychic Terrain so that Maushold does not fear revenge killing attempts from the likes of Scizor and Keldeo. Ursaluna-B is a great bulky teammate, taking out Steel- and Poison-types like Archaludon and Sneasler, which would otherwise be troublesome to Maushold. Calm Mind Terapagos with BoltBeam coverage deals with pesky Flying- and Dragon-types like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Dragonite for Maushold. Blissey is an amazing special wall, tanking special hits from Flutter Mane and Greninja while also spreading paralysis via Thunder Wave. It also provides hazard support with Stealth Rock, which gives Maushold chance to OHKO Gliscor.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Maushold can support various teams. It is most commonly used on rain and balance teams featuring Annihilape.
  • On rain teams, Maushold uses Beat Up to assist Archaludon in gaining Defense boosts from Stamina as well as increasing the damage of Rage Fist from Annihilape. It also provides redirection, allowing Annihilape to set up further with Bulk Up and other partners such as Basculegion-M to attack safely.
  • On balance teams, Maushold provides the same support to Annihilape and additionally supports partners such as Gholdengo and Kingambit with redirection, allowing them to safely set up with Nasty Plot and Swords Dance, respectively.
  • Maushold is threatened by Fighting-types such as Sneasler. Partners such as Annihilape and Gholdengo are difficult for Sneasler to KO and can easily KO Sneasler in return. Maushold is also walled by Ghost-types like Gholdengo. Incineroar can comfortably survive attacks from Gholdengo and threaten it with Knock Off. Taunt easily disrupts Maushold, requiring Maushold to switch out to remove the effect.

Strategy Comments

  • Maushold performs best when it redirects attacks and enabling its partners to set up safely and sweep. Leading Maushold is often a great choice, allowing its partners to take early-game KOs.
  • Maushold can be used flexibly. Follow Me is vital for granting its partner a turn to safely set up or take a KO at any point during the game, and the offensive set can sometimes deal just enough damage to take a surprising KO on a big opposing threat.
  • Maushold is easily disrupted by Taunt, so it needs to Taunt the opposing support Pokemon itself or rely on its partners to take out opposing Taunt users. Offensive Maushold is additionally threatened by Rocky Helmet and Rough Skin, both of which KO it after it has used Population Bomb.

Offensive Support.description:
• Offensive Maushold aims to soften up foes or take surprising KOs with Technician Population Bomb while also providing redirection and disruption support.
  • Population Bomb allows Maushold to deal devastating damage, especially with ten hits, which is enough to remove threats such as Dragonite. Taunt shuts down Trick Room setters like Porygon2 and opposing support Pokemon like Amoonguss.
  • Tera Ghost makes Maushold immune to Close Combat from Sneasler, Fake Out from Incineroar, and Extreme Speed from Dragonite. Tera Grass grants Maushold an immunity to Spore and Rage Powder. Tera Grass also provides useful resistances to Water- and Electric-type attacks such as Wave Crash from Basculegion and Electro Shot from Archaludon.
  • Wide Lens is used to increase the accuracy of Population Bomb, greatly increasing the chance of landing ten hits.
  • While this set is capable of dealing high damage, it is reliant on landing enough Population Bomb hits to take out or weaken threats. This set lacks defensive investment, so it is not expected to be able to redirect attacks throughout the battle.

Bulky Support.description:
• As a bulky support Pokemon, Maushold aims to redirect attacks for its partners as well as disrupt its foes. Maushold additionally has Friend Guard, increasing the survivability of its allies.
  • Beat Up is used to increase the power of Rage Fist from a partner Annihilape and grant Defense boosts to a partner Archaludon with Stamina; it can also be used to break Focus Sashes. Taunt disrupts Trick Room setters and opposing support Pokemon like Porygon2 and Electabuzz.
  • Tera Ghost makes Maushold immune to Close Combat from Sneasler, Fake Out from Incineroar, and Extreme Speed from Dragonite. Tera Fairy turns Maushold's weakness to Close Combat into a resistance and provides an immunity to Outrage from Dragonite. Tera Fairy is also a great defensive typing into the metagame.
  • Safety Goggles grants Maushold an immunity to Spore and Rage Powder.
  • This Maushold set is capable of taking multiple attacks; however, it is easily disrupted by Taunt, forcing Maushold to be switched out to remove the effect. The set is also very passive and deals very low damage.

Physically Defensive (Normal).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Assault Vest.description:
• With a superb special stat line, Seed Sower, and good moveset coverage, Arboliva can be a deceptively strong and long-living Assault Vest user!

  • Seed Sower: Once activated, Grassy Terrain’s passive recovery and boosting of Grass-type attacks like Giga Drain can help Arboliva survive longer than expected. Grassy Terrain also halving Earthquake’s power is greatly appreciated by bulky teammates like Skeledirge, Arcanine, and Iron Hands.

  • Dazzling Gleam: This move keeps Arboliva from becoming setup bait against foes like offensive Dragonite, and is also your best move into Wo-Chien before Tera.

  • Tera Blast: Tera Blast is a great option for hitting types that Arboliva lacks natural coverage for. Tera Fire lets Arboliva hit Steel-types like Scizor and Tera Electric punishes Tera Flying users like Gholdengo. Both Tera Fire and Tera Electric cover Corviknight as well.

  • Mirror Coat: This set’s massive special bulk can make getting one-shots with Mirror Coat awkward, but it is still a great option, particularly against boosted or super effective hits. Bear in mind though that this won’t work against Chi-Yu as long as it keeps its Dark typing.

  • Leaf Storm: Leaf Storm trades consistency for a single turn of high burst damage and can be worth it if investing in Special Attack.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Arboliva’s raw special stats make it capable of tanking super effective hits without using Tera. Nonetheless, Tera is still a strong tool to extend Arboliva’s uptime and contest matchups that would otherwise capitalize on its mediocre defensive typing.

  • Fire: Tera Fire can flip matchups against Focus Sash Chien-Pao and Choice Scarf Chi-Yu when healthy. If running Tera Blast, it also gives Arboliva the opportunity to contest Steel-types more effectively. Be aware, though, that this significantly worsens other key matchups, like Rotom-W.

  • Poison: Tera Poison is a solid defensive option, especially into Toxic abusers like Toxapex and Clodsire. Notably, it flips several weaknesses, blocks Toxic, and allows for absorbing Toxic Spikes later in the match.

  • Electric: Tera Electric is Gholdengo's worst nightmare. It gives a resistance to Make It Rain, blocks Thunder Wave from defensive sets, and punishes Tera Flying usage that is meant to get around Earth Power. On top of that, Arboliva still hits Corviknight very hard.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is another great defensive option for neutralizing most of Arboliva's weaknesses, and the extra power behind Dazzling Gleam can make it easier to break defensive Dragonite variants.

  • Grass: Tera Grass removes Arboliva’s Fighting weakness while maintaining Spore immunity, letting it check Breloom. If both Tera and Grassy Terrain are active, Modest Giga Drain can even 2HKO Breloom!

  • Ground: While not as strong defensively, invested Tera Earth Power can OHKO uninvested Chi-Yu and Gholdengo.

EV Spreads

  • 236 HP / 4 Def / 140 SpA / 124 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This spread balances bulk and power, avoiding the 2HKO from Choice Specs Gholdengo's Make It Rain and almost always surviving Modest Chi-Yu’s Fire Blast before Tera! If running Tera Ground, there are enough Special Attack EV’s to turn Earth Power into an OHKO against uninvested Chi-Yu and Gholdengo. The Speed EV's Speed tie with 4 Speed Gastrodon.

  • 236 HP / 252 SpA / 20 SpD with Modest: This simple spread still provides plenty of bulk while maximizing Special Attack, working nicely with Leaf Storm and Tera Types that boost Arboliva's coverage moves. If Grassy Terrain is present, fully invested Leaf Storm has a 75% chance of OHKOing 4 Special Defense Garchomp. The bulk investment lets Arboliva always avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Mystical Fire after Grassy Terrain recovery.

  • 236 HP / 20 SpD / 252 Spe with Modest: While maximum Speed investment may seem a bit strange, it can be worth it when running Tera Fire Tera Blast to get the jump on Scizor, Corviknight and the rare Timid Amoonguss.

  • 236 HP / 4 Def / 148 SpA / 20 SpD / 100 Spe with Modest: This alternative Speed spread gives Arboliva a nice boost in Special Attack while still letting it outrun 4 Speed Azumarill. This is usually more than enough Speed to outrun Ting-Lu as well.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Eject Pack allows for a one-time free entry for Arboliva's teammates after a Leaf Storm; however, with how long Arboliva tends to stay on the field, missing out on Leftovers recovery ends up not being worth it most of the time. On top of that, it is mostly outclassed as a bulky Eject Pack user by Alolan Exeggutor, which is equipped with more threatening Draco Meteor and a better defensive typing, and Venusaur, which doesn't miss Leftovers as much thanks to Synthesis. An EV spread that invests in Defense instead of Special Attack can be used to help bolster the team's defensive core against Pokemon such as Basculin. However, in this case, Grass-types such as Venusaur and Dipplin are preferred for their better matchup into Fighting-types like Hitmontop and Primeape.

Checks and Counters

Venusaur: Arboliva is never able to threaten a Venusaur above half HP, and Venusaur tends to be difficult to switch into, with even its checks usually disliking being hit by Knock Off, Leech Seed, or Sludge Bomb, especially with the latter's poison chance.

Poison-types: Muk can shrug off Arboliva's attacks and retaliate with Knock Off and Poison Jab to disassemble Arboliva. Hisuian Sneasel and Toxicroak can switch in at least once and fire back with their strong Poison-type STAB moves.

Special Walls and Tanks: Cryogonal, Orthworm, and Articuno can all stomach Arboliva's hits and respond back with super effective moves. The likes of Magneton and Vikavolt can switch in and immediately threaten Arboliva back, since it's so slow.

Quiver Dance Sweepers: Arboliva is unable to do much to stop Quiver Dance sweepers such as Masquerain and Lilligant. It gives them a free opportunity to set up and relies on its teammates to prevent a sweep.

Choice Specs.description:
Arboliva serves as a devastating wallbreaker, utilizing its excellent STAB combination and solid coverage to OHKO or 2HKO almost the entire tier. Hyper Voice serves as an excellent neutral attack, dealing massive damage to foes like Charizard and Whimsicott. Leaf Storm is preferred as its Grass-type STAB, maximizing damage against special walls like Cryogonal while potentially OHKOing foes like Mesprit and Spiritomb. Earth Power helps Arboliva hit Perrserker and Muk while Alluring Voice serves as effective coverage against the likes of Virizion and Lurantis while being an excellent tertiary STAB option post Terastallization. Tera Fairy is used for survivability reasons, flipping its matchup against foes like Primeape and the previously mentioned Virizion. The given EV spread allows Arboliva to outpace Regirock and Weezing to avoid being threatened by their super effective attacks before it can break them.

Arboliva greatly appreciates pivoting teammates that can help safely bring it in like Basculin, Vikavolt, and Primeape, with it working alongside them to break down opposing teams. Physically offensive teammates like Hisuian Sneasel, Hitmontop, and Lycanroc appreciate Arboliva's ability to threaten massive damage to defensive foes like Regirock and Spiritomb; in turn, they pressure walls Arboliva struggles with like Cryogonal. Entry hazard support from the likes of Sandslash and Mesprit help augment Arboliva's wallbreaking, making damage stick on the likes of Muk while potentially pushing them into range to be 2HKOed by Leaf Storm and Hyper Voice, respectively. Defensive Mesprit is a particularly excellent teammate for Arboliva, as it is able to provide a variety of utility options between Knock Off to remove Eviolite and Leftovers, U-turn for momentum, hazard support with Stealth Rock, and Encore to stop Muk in its tracks. It also works well with Arboliva defensively, where the former handles Fighting-type foes, while the latter handles Ghost-types like Trevenant and Spiritomb.
