Defensive teammates like Regirock and Weezing help cover for Arboliva’s weaknesses to common threats like Charizard, Sneasel, and Virizion.

Bulky Attacker.description:
Arboliva is a solid bulky attacker in ZU due to its incredible longevity from the combination of Leech Seed, Leftovers, and Grassy Terrain and formidable defensive and offensive stats. Outside of Steel-types, such as Magneton and Orthworm, and Trevenant, both of which still do not enjoy switching into Arboliva's attacks, the combination of Leaf Storm and Hyper Voice is unresisted in ZU. Giga Drain is a solid alternative to Leaf Storm that helps in prolonged one-on-ones but lacks immediate power; Leaf Storm can pickup 2HKOs on foes like Mesprit and Whimsicott. Leech Seed helps Arboliva fend off many Pokemon, especially in tandem with Strength Sap, which is great when up against physical attackers such as Lycanroc and Perrserker. Protect can be ran instead, which lets Arboliva safely accumulate healing. 92 Speed EVs let Arboliva outspeed base 50 Speed Pokemon such as Muk and Regirock. Tera Poison and Tera Ghost help Arboliva turn the tables on the plethora of Fighting-types in ZU such as Primeape and Hisuian Sneasel. While Ghost provides a Fighting immunity, Poison is usually preferred due to its immunity to poison and neutrality to Dark.

Bulky attacker Arboliva fits on slower-paced bulky offense and balance teams and works best when paired with Pokemon that are able to make great use of the Grassy Terrain it provides such as Muk and Spiritomb. Arboliva's worst matchup is Venusaur, which is immune to Leech Seed, is able to shrug off Arboliva's Grass-type attacks, and make progress with Knock Off or Sludge Bomb, so Pokemon who are well equipped at dealing with Venusaur such as Muk, Cryogonal and Orthworm make for solid teammates. Spiritomb provides a solid switch-in to Fighting- and Poison-type attacks, while Grassy Terrain creates many setup opportunities for it. Other Fighting- and Poison-resistant Pokemon like Sandslash and Weezing also work well. Regirock and Muk are great switch-ins to Fire-types such as Charizard and Magmortar, and they also enjoy the passive recovery Grassy Terrain provides. Arboliva is often a liability against setup sweepers, especially against Quiver Dance users like Lilligant, which makes some sort of setup prevention, like Prankster Encore from Whimsicott and Sableye or Roar from Charizard, preferred.

Specially Defensive.description:
Specially defensive Naclstack is a formidable defensive pivot and wall, checking many of PU's best offensive options like Salazzle and Rotom-Heat while being capable of absorbing attempts at status. Salt Cure accrues massive amounts of residual damage, and nothing wants to stay in and get worn down by its effect. Protect scouts attacks from Choice-locked Pokemon like Hoopa and Passimian while racking up Salt Cure damage. Curse can be used to bolster its already excellent Defense, giving Naclstack the ability to excel in late-game situations as an impenetrable wall. Stealth Rock is an option for Naclstack, as it can use its defensive utility to establish hazards repeatedly throughout a game while freeing up a slot for teammates that prefer other options over Stealth Rock, like Bombirdier and Golurk. Tera Water is generally a good Tera type for defensive walls and works especially well for Naclstack, giving it much better matchups into the strong Fighting- and Water-types in the tier like Paldean Tauros-F and Tatsugiri and also removing its weakness to Focus Blast from both Hoopa and Hisuian Typhlosion. Tera Ghost similarly helps with Fighting-type attacks and can prevent attempts at Rapid Spin from Coalossal and Tatsugiri, though it comes at the expense of becoming much weaker to Knock Off and its inability to boost with Curse.

Balance and bulky offense teams appreciate Naclstack greatly as a specially defensive wall capable of sponging hits, absorbing status, and functioning as an entry hazard setter that can get them up multiple times a game. Hazard stacking cores with teammates like Palossand and the Qwilfish formes are incredibly efficient in wearing teams down with gradual chip damage, though they need support in the form of Knock Off from offensive teammates like Ambipom and Skuntank to help remove Heavy-Duty Boots. With Salt Cure, Naclstack can often prevent defensive walls like Milotic and Alolan Sandslash from getting too comfortable against it, allowing teammates to get momentum through forcing multiple switches. Once it is able to get a Salt Cure off, Naclstack will often force switches, and to avoid it being face-to-face with a wallbreaker like Golurk or Heracross, it's a good idea to double switch into an offensive teammate like Bombirdier or Paldean Tauros-F. These two also appreciate Naclstack for its ability to stack chip damage to the walls that may switch into Naclstack, like Mudsdale and Palossand. Naclstack can sometimes be reliant on Tera to function as the immovable object it desires to be, so pairing it with teammates that can use their natural defensive typing well, like Hisuian Decidueye, Rotom-Mow, and Skuntank, is important to get the most out of Naclstack.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Iron Defense can be run on Naclstack in conjunction with Body Press to allow it to serve as a late-game setup sweeper. Compared to Regirock, another Rock-type running the combination of Iron Defense and Body Press, Naclstack offers a burn immunity and access to Recover, which allows it to switch into special Fire-types throughout the game without compromising its sweeping potential. However, Naclstack has to choose between giving up Stealth Rock and Salt Cure in order to fit Iron Defense onto its moveset, and its reliance on Eviolite for its special bulk makes Naclstack especially vulnerable to Knock Off when compared to Regirock.

Checks and Counters

Knock Off Users: Because Naclstack is so dependent on Eviolite for its bulk, Knock Off users such as Toxicroak, Sandslash, and Skuntank can compromise Naclstack's longevity.

Grass-type Pokemon: Grass-type Pokemon like Venusaur and Whimsicott can offensively threaten Naclstack. Venusaur and Whimsicott additionally threaten to remove Naclstack's Eviolite through Knock Off or Switcheroo, and Whimsicott can bring in another offensive threat with U-turn.

Water-type Pokemon: While the risk of Salt Cure's increased chip damage dissuades Water-type Pokemon from switching directly into Naclstack, Water-type attackers like Basculin and Clawitzer threaten to OHKO Naclstack with super effective attacks. Clawitzer notably threatens both Tera Fairy and Tera Water Naclstack as well, still breaking through it with Sludge Bomb or Tera Dragon Dragon Pulse, respectively.

Mesprit: With a combination of Knock Off to remove its Eviolite, Psychic Noise to prevent healing from Recover, and Encore to lock Naclstack into an unfavorable move like Recover, Mesprit can weaken Naclstack and make it unable to function as a wall.

Fighting-type Pokemon: Close Combat allows Fighting-type Pokemon like Primeape, Toxicroak, and Hisuian Sneasel to threaten Naclstack, while all three run Poison-type coverage that threatens Tera Fairy Naclstack. The latter two are especially strong against Naclstack due to their resistance to Body Press, access to Knock Off or Switcheroo to remove Naclstack's Eviolite, and access to Swords Dance to set up on Naclstack's Protect turns.

Stealth Rock.description:
Naclstack sets itself apart from other Stealth Rock setters because of its great defensive typing, solid bulk, and immunity to status with Purifying Salt. It can to use these qualities to enter the field against foes like Charizard and force progress through setting Stealth Rock or by accumulating damage via Salt Cure and Protect. Running Body Press over Protect gives Naclstack a more immediate way to deal damage to special attackers like Jolteon and is useful on bulky offensive teams that appreciate a faster way to make progress than with Salt Cure and Protect. Tera Fairy Naclstack gains resistances to the Dark-type, Fighting-type, and Dragon-type, which are helpful against OTR Spiritomb, Focus Blast Charizard, and non-Sludge Bomb Clawitzer. Tera Fairy Naclstack does exchange a weakness to physical Fighting-type attacks such as Close Combat for a resistance, but it also opens up a weakness to the Poison-type attacks commonly paired with Close Combat, such as Toxicroak's Gunk Shot. Tera Water Naclstack gains a Water-type resistance that can help it check or force Tera from Choice Specs Clawitzer, as Clawitzer needs Tera Dragon to 2HKO a full health Naclstack. More importantly, Tera Water's Ice-type and Water-type resistances improve Naclstack's matchup against physical attackers such as Basculin, Hitmontop, and Beartic, without leaving Naclstack weak to any common physical attacks.

Running Stealth Rock on Naclstack is appreciated by teammates such as Mesprit and Sandslash, which can use the open moveslot for extra utility moves like Healing Wish and Spikes, respectively. Naclstack's ability to check Fire-types like Charizard is appreciated by Grass-types like Venusaur, which in turn resists the Water-type and Grass-type moves that threaten Naclstack. It also pairs well with Pokemon that can switch into physical Fighting-type attacks like Mesprit and Sableye, both of which threaten to cripple those Fighting-types with a Knock Off or an Encore. A dependence on Eviolite makes Naclstack especially vulnerable to Knock Off itself, so teammates able to switch into a Knock Off like Skuntank and Toxicroak are appreciated. Naclstack is especially bad against physically defensive Mesprit, since it does not want to take any of Encore, Knock Off, and Psychic Noise, so teammates able to switch into a Mesprit like Skuntank are appreciated.

Garganacl is an exceptional Stealth Rock setter and wall thanks to its great bulk, amazing ability in Purifying Salt, and access to Salt Cure. As a setter, Garganacl is very good at outlasting and pressuring common removal options like non-Leftovers Great Tusk, Corviknight, and Iron Treads with Salt Cure. Protect also stalls turns, which works well in conjunction with Salt Cure and allows Garganacl to chip its foes as much as possible; it's also useful at scouting moves from foes such as Choice Band Dragapult, Lokix, and Meowscarada and maximizing passive recovery from Leftovers. However, Ice Punch is a niche option to immediately nail Hydrapple and Gliscor, as they can be huge threats in the balance mirrors in general and shrug off Salt Cure's passive damage with Regenerator and Poison Heal. Additionally, the move also lets Garganacl chunk foes like Meowscarada, Dragapult, and Latios immediately. Heavy-Duty Boots is an option on teams with little to no hazard removal at the cost of crucial Leftovers recovery. 52 Defense EVs allow Garganacl to survive Ogerpon-W's Power Whip, and the rest of the EVs are invested in HP and Special Defense to maximize its special bulk to help it take on threats such as Dragapult in a better fashion. Tera Fairy enables it to handle threats such as Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Dragapult better; in addition, the Grass neutrality helps it against foes like Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Meowscarada. Tera Water helps it against foes like Gholdengo and Water-types like Barraskewda and Hisuian Samurott. Both of these Tera types are useful at handling non-Swords Dance Gliscor as well, as Garganacl also acts as a Toxic absorber.

Garganacl fits well on bulky offense and balance teams that need a bulky entry hazard setter; Salt Cure is great at making progress for its teammates to capitalize on. Setup sweepers such as Kingambit, Weavile, and Nasty Plot Gholdengo appreciate Garganacl's ability to chip and force damage on the opposing team with Stealth Rock and Salt Cure, especially against threats such as Skarmory and Primarina. In return, they offensively pressure Garganacl's switch-ins such as Galarian Slowking, Rillaboom, and Clefable, as it's reliant on Salt Cure for damage and is thus very passive. Gholdengo also deserves a special mention because of its ability to block hazard removal attempts from foes like Great Tusk and Corviknight. Garganacl also forms amazing cores with Spikes setters such as Gliscor, Hisuian Samurott, and Skarmory, further helping its offensive teammates by dominating the hazard game. Moreover, Gliscor and Skarmory also help it in checking Ground- and Fighting-types like Landorus-T and Zamazenta. Knock Off users such as Clefable and the aforementioned Weavile are also good teammates due to removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes such as Galarian Slowking and Dondozo; removing Leftovers from foes like Zamazenta and Ting-Lu is also useful so that they take maximum damage from Salt Cure and Stealth Rock. In addition, Clefable and the aforementioned Gliscor also support Garganacl by acting as Knock Off absorbers, as Garganacl likes to keep its Leftovers intact—Protect and Leftovers form a strong combination that makes Garganacl very tough to break down. Galarian Slowking also makes a great partner that supports Garganacl with Future Sight, punishing Fighting-types such as Zamazenta and Iron Valiant, as well as providing pivoting support with Chilly Reception. Garganacl also appreciates hazard removal support, as its foes such as Gliscor, Clefable, and Ting-Lu may use it as fodder for setting up hazards, especially Spikes; as such, Pokemon like Great Tusk make nice teammates. Due to its relatively poor base typing, Garganacl is weak to a variety of threats including Great Tusk, Iron Valiant, Kingambit, and Ogerpon-W; thus, partners such as Ogerpon-W, Skeledirge, Zamazenta, and Dragapult, respectively, are appreciated. Rillaboom also synergizes well with Garganacl, as its Grassy Terrain can weaken Earthquake from foes like Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Gliscor for Garganacl as well as helping it deal with Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Barraskewda; in return, Garganacl supports Rillaboom with hazard and deals with foes like Iron Moth for it.

Curse.description:
Garganacl's incredible defensive stats and access to Salt Cure make it a potent Curse user, letting it beat threatening physical attackers such as Weavile and Dragon Dance Dragonite while acting as a pseudo-sweeper. Earthquake lets Garganacl hit threats such as Gholdengo, Raging Bolt, and Galarian Slowking, with its high-Base Power giving Garganacl offensive presence so it doesn't have to rely solely on Salt Cure for damage, which is especially useful since Raging Bolt commonly runs Leftovers and Galarian Slowking's Regenerator can mitigate Salt Cure damage as well. 52 Defense EVs lets Garganacl survive Ogerpon-W's Power Whip without the need for Curse boosts or Terastallization. Tera Water turns Garganacl's Water weakness into a resistance, letting it better handle Water-types such as Barraskewda and Hisuian Samurott. It also lets Garganacl check offensive Steel-types such as Gholdengo, with Purifying Salt letting it resist Shadow Ball. On the other hand, Tera Fairy gives Garganacl an immunity to Draco Meteor from Dragapult as well as Dragon Pulse from Raging Bolt. It also grants Garganacl a resistance to Fighting-type moves from Pokemon such as Zamazenta and Great Tusk and removes its Grass weakness, improving its matchup against Meowscarada. Both options remove Garganacl's weakness to Ground-type moves, letting it better handle foes that rely on Earthquake for coverage such as Dragonite.

Garganacl fits well on bulky offense or balance teams. Due to not running Heavy-Duty Boots, Garganacl appreciates entry hazard removal from the likes of Great Tusk and Corviknight; Great Tusk in particular appreciates Garganacl checking spinblockers such as Dragapult and, with Tera Water, Gholdengo. Rillaboom makes for a great partner thanks to Garganacl appreciating the recovery from Grassy Terrain, which alleviates entry hazard chip damage, as well as the reduction in Earthquake's damage, letting it check Pokemon like Dragonite better. It should be noted that Garganacl's own Earthquake will deal less damage as a result of Grassy Terrain and Salt Cure's chip damage will be mitigated by Grassy Terrain's healing when combined with Leftovers, however. As Substitute blocks Salt Cure, Pokemon that can punish the use of the move, such as Encore Dragonite, Infiltrator Dragapult, and Whirlwind Ting-Lu, are appreciated teammates. Ogerpon-W makes for a great partner with Garganacl thanks to Water Absorb and its ability to force Ground-types like Gliscor out with Ivy Cudgel. It can also punish Substitute with Encore and remove items like Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots with Knock Off, accentuating the chip damage done by Salt Cure. In exchange, it appreciates Garganacl deterring defensive Pokemon like Skarmory with Salt Cure, as well as its ability to handle Dragon-types like Dragonite and Dragapult. Unaware Clefable forms a good defensive core with Garganacl, denying other setup sweepers the opportunity to set up on Garganacl while also appreciating its ability to absorb status from Pokemon like Galarian Slowking, Dragapult and Skeledirge. Garganacl also benefits from Clefable's ability to check Ting-Lu. Opposing Clefable can check Garganacl with both of its abilities, so Pokemon that can dispatch it, like Gholdengo and Heatran, make for good partners. Garganacl also enjoys Knock Off and hazard support, as the removal of items like Heavy-Duty Boots and the additional chip from hazards makes it harder to play around due to the chip damage from Salt Cure having more of an impact on Pokemon like Galarian Slowking, Alomomola, and Ting-Lu. Gliscor has access to Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Knock Off while also resisting Ground-type moves; in exchange, Garganacl checks Hex Dragapult, one of Gliscor's best checks. Finally, specially defensive Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking and Clodsire appreciate Garganacl's physical walling capabilities while making up for its inability to consistently handle special attackers like Primarina and Enamorus.

Iron Defense.description:
With fantastic bulk, Salt Cure, Purifying Salt's status immunity, the combination of Iron Defense and Body Press, and reliable recovery, Garganacl establishes itself as a potent win condition. Iron Defense lets Garganacl boost its Defense to nearly unbreakable levels. Body Press allows Garganacl to threaten the likes of Kingambit, Ting-Lu, and Weavile, and with Iron Defense boosts, Garganacl's Body Press becomes more threatening, 2HKOing the likes of Iron Treads and Kyurem after just one boost. In tandem with Salt Cure, Gliscor can eventually be beaten with enough Iron Defense boosts. Salt Cure pressures would-be switch-ins like Ogerpon-W, Gholdengo, and Dondozo. Leftovers adds even more to Garganacl's excellent survivability, allowing it to conserve valuable Recover PP, further complemented by Iron Defense boosts that enhance its ability to take physical attacks. Tera Water allows Garganacl to resist Steel- and Water-type moves that threaten it, such as from Pokemon like Gholdengo, Iron Crown, Hisuian Samurott, and Walking Wake. Tera Fairy provides a better typing against threats like Zamazenta, Kyurem, Dragapult, and Ogerpon-W. Tera Electric grants a Steel resistance while lacking weaknesses, and the singular Ground weakness it has is offset by most Ground-type attacks being physical, which, with Iron Defense boosts, can be offset. However, Ground-type coverage from Enamorus and Kyurem still threatens Garganacl.

Garganacl fits on balance and bulky offense teams that can support its Iron Defense sweeps and cover its vulnerability to entry hazards. Hazards set by Ting-Lu, Ogerpon-W, and Clefable complement Garganacl's Salt Cure pressure and the switches it forces with Iron Defense boosting. Ogerpon-W in particular can pressure Great Tusk, Gliscor, and Ting-Lu, allowing Garganacl to preserve HP for other physical threats, and can function as a pivot by virtue of forcing out these Ground-types and using U-turn to bring Garganacl in safely or as a wallbreaker that threatens Hatterene and Calm Mind Clefable, both of which Garganacl struggles against. In return, Garganacl can take on Dragapult and, if Garganacl Terastallizes, Dragonite, both of which can check Ogerpon-W. Great Tusk and Iron Treads synergize nicely with Garganacl, as their Rapid Spin does not clear away hazards set by other teammates such as Ogerpon-W and Clefable. In return, Garganacl checks Dragapult and Zapdos for Great Tusk and Fire-types such as Cinderace and Ceruledge for Iron Treads. Gholdengo checks many of Garganacl's difficult matchups, such as Clefable, Hatterene, Galarian Slowking, and Galarian Weezing, which all threaten or cripple Garganacl. Defoggers such as Corviknight and Galarian Weezing are great partners as well, as both can compress the roles of hazard remover and check to Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Zamazenta, which greatly threaten this Garganacl set without any Defense boosts. While they don't remove hazards, Moltres, Tornadus-T, and Dragapult can all similarly function as checks to some of the aforementioned Pokemon as well as to other Grass-types such as Hydrapple and Sinistcha, while Garganacl checks Zapdos for the first two and Choice Scarf Enamorus for the latter. While this Garganacl set fully invests in Special Defense, special walls such as Galarian Slowking and Ting-Lu can cover for special attackers such as Raging Bolt, Iron Crown, and Gholdengo that would greatly weaken Garganacl otherwise.

IronPress.description:
Garganacl eases the Water and Steel matchups thanks to its signature move, Salt Cure. Iron Defense allows Garganacl to set up, tanking super effective physical hits due to its astronomical base 130 Defense, while also boosting the power of Body Press, which helps nail Dark- and Steel-types such as Ting-Lu, Darkrai, and Bisharp. Curse is another option that can buff its Attack, boosting the damage of Salt Cure, but it prevents Garganacl from easily stonewalling physical attackers—such as Dragonite and defensive Quaquaval—and also lowers Garganacl's Speed. Salt Cure is a fantastic STAB move, neutering setup sweepers such as Mimikyu, Corviknight, and Hatterene, as it puts them on a timer, which Garganacl can potentially stall out as it sets up or heals via Recover. Purifying Salt is particularly useful, as it allows Garganacl to absorb incoming status moves such as Toxic from Quagsire or Toxapex as well as Will-O-Wisp from Dragapult or Sableye and punish them with Salt Cure. Garganacl is also able to tank Ghost-type STAB moves from the likes of Choice-locked Flutter Mane and Dragapult. Leftovers is the best item to provide passive recovery; however, Heavy-Duty Boots can allow Garganacl to come in without taking entry hazard damage, as entry hazard stacking is extremely common. As an alternative to the given EVs, 52 Defense EVs with an Impish nature let Garganacl potentially overwhelm Choice Band Scizor, Tinkaton, and defensive Quaquaval if used with Iron Defense.

Tyranitar is an amazing partner for Garganacl, as it sets sand. Tyranitar can also be used as one of the few special attackers Rock teams have access to to nail physical walls such as Great Tusk with Ice Beam; it is also Rock's best check to Bisharp due to it being able to survive a boosted Sucker Punch and OHKO back with Fire Blast. Choice Scarf Glimmora can take on Grass- and Fighting-types such as Breloom and Iron Valiant that may threaten Garganacl out. Glimmora also has fantastic coverage, being able to take on Steel-types such as Gholdengo with Earth Power and Water-types such as Gastrodon and Quagsire with Energy Ball. Glimmora can also provide Toxic Spikes support thanks to its ability, Toxic Debris, which can help Garganacl further wear down and pressure the opposing Pokemon. Teammates that utilize Air Balloon such as Iron Thorns and Drednaw can switch into powerful Ground-type attacks aimed at Garganacl. Drednaw can also utilize its Water-type STAB move to take out opposing Ground-types such as Iron Treads, Unaware Clodsire, and Ting-Lu. Furthermore, Drednaw can also turn the tide against rain Water teams thanks to its ability, Swift Swim. Lycanroc-D is also a really good partner for Garganacl that appreciates its ability to wear down foes so it can clean up late-game. Coalossal is also a good partner that can not only burn foes but also lay down entry hazards. Coalossal can also clear its side of the field as well with Rapid Spin, alleviating chip damage on the team. It also acts as a soft check to Scizor and Meowscarada due to its neutralities and can potentially neuter them with Flame Body.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon has been updated to reflect the new Pokemon that The Indigo Disk has brought!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Salty Stall.description:
• With some entry hazard support, this Garganacl can be very difficult to outstall, thanks to the constant passive damage from Salt Cure.

  • Protect: Not only does Protect scout for surprise Tera types, but it also goes well with the passive healing from Leftovers.

  • Stealth Rock: Since this set benefits so much from Stealth Rock support, running it on its own is a reasonable sacrifice if Garganacl needs to be more self-sufficient.

  • Substitute: This makes Garganacl even more difficult to properly switch into, providing protection against Trick, OHKO moves, and opposing Salt Cure.

  • Fissure: Garganacl's great bulk makes it a prime candidate for fishing with Fissure itself, though its low PP can be an issue in mirror matches.

Other Options

  • Fling with Light Ball, Toxic Orb, or Flame Orb: Although the loss of Leftovers can be a huge blow for Garganacl, Fling and its associated status inducing items can be a devastating surprise for some of its checks, such as Annihilape and Urshifu formes. Just note that Covert Cloak will still block these statuses.

  • Sturdy and Custap Berry: Getting rid of Garganacl's status immunity and Ghost resistance is a huge sacrifice, but it can let Garganacl lead against some surprising Pokemon effectively without needing to Terastallize, like Choice Specs Chi-Yu and Iron Bundle. Custap Berry's pseudo-priority can also lead to surprising Stealth Rock set-ups.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Rock may be an awful defensive typing, this Garganacl's complete focus on taking advantage of Salt Cure means that in some scenarios, it can get away without Terastallizing.

  • Poison: Tera Poison's Fighting and Fairy-type resistance vastly improves Garganacl's match-up against Flutter Mane, Ogerpon-H, and Urshifu-R, making it a prime Tera choice. As a bonus, this also lets Garganacl absorb Toxic Spikes.

  • Water: Tera Water gives Garganacl a better matchup against Chien-Pao, Urshifu-R, and Gholdengo, in addition to being an excellent defensive typing.

  • Ghost: While removing Purifying Salt's Ghost resistance is a shame, Tera Ghost does wonderfully against Archaludon and opposing Garganacl due to the Body Press immunity, and in general removes all of Garganacl's common weaknesses. Tera Ghost also can make foes paranoid of it being the Curse set.

  • Flying: Tera Flying gets rid of the Ground and Fighting weaknesses, giving it a far better chance of beating Landorus-T and Ursaluna-B. It also makes Fissure no longer an issue from Ting-Lu, Dondozo, and opposing Garganacl.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy lets Garganacl tank powerful Fighting coverage such as Chien-Pao's Scared Sword, and shrug off powerful Dragon-type attacks from Latios and Roaring Moon.

Curse.description:
• With Curse's well-known different effect for Ghost-types being brought into play by Terastallization, Garganacl makes dangerous and diverse use of the move! Boosting Salt Cure's meager power can also help against frailer Substitute users such as Flutter Mane.

  • Tera Ghost Curse: If using Tera Ghost, Curse will change its effect, which drastically changes Garganacl's playstyle. While the 50% health cut can make it a tad risky, the Curse affliction is very powerful at wearing down Pokemon, including major foes that take advantage of Salt Cure, such as Covert Cloak Pokemon, bulky Substitute users, and Blaziken Baton Pass chains. When combined with Salt Cure, it can even overwhelm bulky Pokemon with recovery, such as Dragonite.

  • Curse and Earthquake: Ghost Curse unfortunately does not work against Gholdengo, so using regular Curse alongside Earthquake makes Garganacl far less passive against against Gholdengo and frail Substitute users such as Flutter Mane. This is especially recommended if using other Tera types.

  • Protect versus Substitute: Protect is perfect for getting some extra Leftovers recovery, but Substitute comes in handy against Dragon Tail users like Archaludon and Garchomp.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Salt Cure means Garganacl can still without Terastallization, but to truly take advantage of either facet of Curse, expect to Terastallize it often.

  • Ghost: In addition to being a great defensive typing that leaves Garganacl with only a weakness to Dark thanks to Purifying Salt, this is the Tera type that enables the unique properties of Curse.

  • Poison: Tera Poison is Garganacl's best option against Flutter Mane, ensuring it resists both STAB attacks. Absorbing Toxic Spikes is also helpful against stall teams.

  • Water: If messing with Gholdengo is the goal, Tera Water is an excellent choice, resisting the powerful Make It Rain and being a good defensive typing in general.

  • Fairy: Beyond being a great typing that offers a Fighting-type resistance, it also means Garganacl no longer has to worry about Dragon Tail from Archaludon. This doesn't improve Garganacl's match-up against Gholdengo though.

  • Flying: Tera Flying has excellent synergy with Garganacl's former typing, making it immune to Landorus-T and Ursaluna-B's Ground-type attacks, and even removing any worry about Fissure from Ting-Lu and Dondozo. However, this comes at the cost of still making it vulnerable to Iron Bundle.

Defensive.description:
• With Purifying Salt making it immune to status and Salt Cure providing useful chip damage, especially against Water- and Steel-types, Garganacl is a dangerous defensive setup Pokemon.

  • Iron Defense and Body Press: Body Press is the best option for consistency against offensive teams.

  • Fissure: Fissure severely punishes passive play against Garganacl, at the cost of forcing it to rely on Salt Cure residual damage against offensive teams.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Rock has a huge amount of weaknesses as a defensive typing, so Garganacl will usually want to Terastallize to make sweeping more feasible.

  • Poison: Tera Poison is the prime pick to combat Flutter Mane, with it making Garganacl resist both Moonblast and Shadow Ball. The Fighting-type resistance against Urshifu formes and Toxic Spikes absorption is also quite helpful.

  • Water: Tera Water vastly improves Garganacl's chances of defeating Gholdengo, Urshifu-R, and Chien-Pao.

  • Ghost: A Ghost Tera type gives Garganacl an immunity to Body Press, giving it the edge against Archaludon and opposing Garganacl, especially when paired with Leftovers. It can also fool players into thinking Garganacl is using the Curse set.

  • Flying: A Flying typing lets Garganacl take on new foes such as Landorus-T, Ursaluna-B, and Garchomp, though it makes Garganacl fairly weak to Iron Bundle and Chien-Pao

  • Fairy: Fairy is a good defensive type for Garganacl, giving it a useful Fighting and Dark resistance to help against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, and no longer worrying about powerful Dragon-type attacks. However, Garganacl still remains vulnerable to powerful Steel-type attacks from foes like Gholdengo. EV Spreads ========

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD / 4 Spe with Careful: Maximizing Special Defense is the best choice for easier setup.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Impish: In addition to powering up Body Press, a focus on Defense makes setting up on powerful setup sweepers such as Dragonite an easier task.

  • 252 HP / 84 Def / 172 SpD with Careful: This EV spread allows Tera Steel Garganacl to avoid a 2HKO from Breloom's Mach Punch after Iron Defense.

Iron Defense.description:
Garganacl's great bulk and exceptional ability in Purifying Salt make Garganacl a threatening, status-immune bulky setup sweeper that is able to check threatening Pokemon such as Iron Moth, Victini, and Blacephalon. Iron Defense makes Garganacl very difficult to overcome, even with super effective physical moves, while also boosting the power of Body Press, its main tool when sweeping. Salt Cure allows Garganacl to wear down potential checks, such as Rotom-W, Serperior, and Iron Crown; generate progress for its team; and punish Pokemon attempting to boost alongside it, namely Aegislash, Scizor, and Mega Latias. Curse is an alternative over Iron Defense to also boost Salt Cure's power at the cost of a lower gain in Defense; it also allows Garganacl to beat Pokemon such as Clefable and Enamorus that would otherwise check it by using Heavy Slam. Notably, Heavy Slam allows it to beat Magic Guard Clefable which is otherwise able to boost up alongside it thanks to being immune to Salt Cure's secondary effect.

This Garganacl set is best suited to balance teams, which appreciate it checking Pokemon such as Iron Moth and special variants of Aegislash while acting as a capable wincon that can make progress for its team. Since it beats most physical attackers after a boost or two, Garganacl highly values teammates that can handle the powerful special attackers that threaten it, namely Hydrapple, Keldeo, and Serperior, so Pokemon like Celesteela, Mega Latias, and Slowking make for valuable partners. Despite its impressive bulk, Garganacl's lack of useful resistances, low Speed, and large number of weaknesses to common attacking types mean it often struggles to come in safely, so slow pivots such as Scizor, Slowking, and Pecharunt are important allies to get it in. Pecharunt, in particular, can spread Toxic poison via Malignant Chain, amplifying the progress Salt Cure generates; Pecharunt also creates more setup opportunities via Parting Shot. Powerful physical attackers with super effective STAB moves such as Buzzwole, Rillaboom, and Life Orb Mienshao can threaten Garganacl even at +2, so Garganacl appreciates partners that can deal with these threats, such as Mega Venusaur, Skarmory, and Clefable. Knock Off can eliminate Garganacl's passive recovery, so Knock Off absorbers such as Clefable, Mega Pokemon like Mega Venusaur and Mega Aerodactyl, as well as Z-Move users like Hydrapple and Keldeo, are good choices to partner with Garganacl. Knock Off users on Garganacl's side, however, can remove Leftovers from opposing Pokemon like Hippowdon and Serperior that might otherwise limit Garganacl wearing the opposing team down with Salt Cure. Rillaboom's Grassy Terrain can create additional setup opportunities against Mega Aerodactyl and Toxic Hippowdon while giving some passive healing, letting Garganacl remain slightly healthier during the sweep, while Rillaboom itself can remove items with Knock Off and offer additional pivoting support via U-turn. When running Body Press, Pokemon that can threaten Clefable, such as Excadrill, Celesteela, and Iron Moth, are crucial, as Clefable is Garganacl's biggest roadblock.

Defensive Stealth Rock.description:
Garganacl can opt to be an effective Stealth Rock setter, using Salt Cure to punish common entry hazard control options like Rotom-W and Excadrill that would otherwise switch into it, as well as generate decent progress for its team. Protect is run in order to stall for additional rounds of Salt Cure damage and gain additional Leftovers recovery, additionally letting Garganacl scout out threatening moves like Tyranitar's Superpower and Iron Moth's Energy Ball. The 32 Defense EVs allow it to avoid being OHKOed by Choice Band Tyranitar's Superpower.

This set is best suited to balance teams looking for a reliable Stealth Rock user that checks special-attacking Aegislash sets and Iron Moth. As it is mostly reliant on Salt Cure's secondary effect to do damage, Garganacl is commonly exploited by Pokemon that either ignore or don't mind the chip damage such as Magic Guard Clefable and Regenerator users like Hydrapple and Mienshao. Therefore, Pokemon that check or exploit these threats such as Celesteela, Iron Crown, and Iron Moth are valued support. Garganacl struggles to switch in directly to many Pokemon due to its plethora of weaknesses to common types, so pivots such as Scizor, Pecharunt, and Slowking are greatly appreciated. Meanwhile, Garganacl can wear down the other team either via entry hazards or Salt Cure, giving these pivots an easier time forcing a switch to gain momentum for other teammates. Knock Off absorbers such as Z-Move users and Clefable are good picks, ensuring that Garganacl can retain its passive recovery while using Protect. Conversely, Knock Off users such as Clefable, Rillaboom, and Mienshao can support it by removing Leftovers from opposing Pokemon, which might otherwise dampen the passive damage of Salt Cure and prevent it from wearing down the opposing team to assist wallbreakers such as Mienshao, Hydrapple, and Buzzwole. Rillaboom in particular supports Garganacl with its Grassy Terrain, increasing its passive recovery even further and weakening Earthquakes that may otherwise threaten Garganacl while being able to get Garganacl in via U-turn.

IronPress.description:
• Garganacl's longevity allows it to act as a stallbreaker and a win condition against bulky teams thanks to the threat of Salt Cure. However, as it often heavily relies on Terastallizing to fix its vulnerability to Ground-types, combined with being easy to force out by special attackers, Garganacl is a niche pick for dedicated balance teams.
  • The IronPress combination ensures that Garganacl can check several physical foes such as defensive Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Extreme Killer Arceus without having to Terastallize, notably preventing itself from becoming setup fodder if an opponent such as Zygarde uses Substitute.
  • The given EV spread avoids a 2HKO from Basculegion-M's 300-Base Power Last Respects after Leftovers recovery, Dragon Dance Zygarde's Thousand Arrows, and special utility Giratina-O's Draco Meteor. This amount of bulk also avoids a 2HKO from Double Dance Primal Groudon's Precipice Blades after Garganacl has Terastallized.
  • Tera Water allows Garganacl to more comfortably come into Steel- and Water-types vulnerable to Salt Cure such as Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Arceus-Water. Tera Fairy makes Garganacl hard wall Marshadow, support Arceus-Dark, and Giratina-O, and grants an immunity to Dragon Tail from foes such as Giratina-O and Zygarde, letting Garganacl preserve Iron Defense boosts.
  • Garganacl's main priority is to spread Salt Cure, wearing down the opposing team and granting its allies momentum as the opposing team is put into uncomfortable positions. Mid-game, Garganacl can be used as a check to physical attackers, as its status-absorbing capabilities also let it easily come into foes such as Ho-Oh, Alomomola, and Giratina-O. Late-game, it may try to apply offensive pressure with IronPress to threaten a sweep, as special attackers that can threaten Garganacl such as Yveltal and Eternatus are more vulnerable to Garganacl after getting worn down.
  • Against offensive team structures, Garganacl can find use against foes it can wall such as Extreme Killer Arceus and Rayquaza thanks to the IronPress combination, preventing it from being as easy to overwhelm on the physical side as it forces a switch, but if the momentum is disfavorable for it, Garganacl can still be used to hinder setup sweepers such as Necrozma-DM, Primal Kyogre, and Zacian-C, putting them on a timer and preventing them from doing much else without sacrificing momentum.
  • Garganacl has a positive matchup against the most common entry hazard removers in the metagame, notably including Ho-Oh and Giratina-O, so its presence can actively discourage them from entering the field, meaning that entry hazard setters such as Eternatus, Primal Groudon, and Ferrothorn make formidable allies.
  • Garganacl is generally vulnerable to special attackers such as Yveltal, Arceus-Fairy, and Primal Kyogre, so checks to them such as defensive Eternatus and Ferrothorn are notable options to mitigate this issue. Zacian-C is also a notable partner that can put offensive pressure on Garganacl's checks such as the previously mentioned foes.
  • Unless it has already Terastallized, Garganacl is vulnerable to Ground- and Fighting-type foes such as Primal Groudon, Arceus-Ground, and Marshadow. Pokemon such as Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Yveltal act as switch-ins to them for Garganacl to rely on early-game, with Garganacl in return limiting the longevity of their checks such as Chien-Pao and Extreme Killer Arceus.

Stealth Rock.description:
• Garganacl is an excellent option for bulkier balance teams in search of a resilient hazard setter. It is one of the best punishers of Defog in the tier and consequently is excellent at winning the hazard war. Garcanacl's excellent bulk, use of Tera, and ability to force progress via Salt Cure makes it a sturdy part of defensive cores. Unfortunately, Garganacl's reliance on Terastallizing requires specific support and hinders its splashability. As such, Garganacl works best when built with it in mind rather than slapping it on a team, especially given that its Tera type plays a huge role in what it is able to check.
  • Salt Cure has scarce switch-ins and prevents Garganacl from being passive while also punishing Defog attempts from Ho-Oh, Giratina-O, and Choice Scarf Yveltal, none of which meaningfully hurt Garganacl.
  • Protect allows Garganacl to scout Choice-locked Pokemon such as Marshadow, Rayquaza, and Lunala. Additionally, it provides Garganacl with some minor healing and can accrue Salt Cure chip.
  • The given EV spread allows Garganacl to survive Life Orb Deoxys-A's Psycho Boost after Stealth Rock and avoid the 2HKO from Choice Band Tera Flying Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent. Additionally, it enables Garganacl to survive +1 Zacian-C's Close Combat and defensive Primal Groudon's Precipice Blades. 18 Speed IVs enable Garganacl to outspeed Calyrex-I under Trick Room.
  • Tera Water enables Garganacl to wall defensive Primal Kyogre. Tera Water Garganacl shrugs off any attack from it, and Salt Cure chip prevents Primal Kyogre from accumulating the boosts it needs to threaten Garganacl. Because Tera Water Garganacl also survives wallbreaker Primal Kyogre's Thunder after Stealth Rock, it can use Salt Cure to leave Primal Kyogre easily revenge killed or otherwise force it out. Additionally, Tera Water enables Garganacl to safely stall out defensive Primal Groudon and Zacian-C with Protect and Salt Cure in a pinch.
  • Tera Fairy Garganacl completely shuts down every Defogger. Although Garganacl isn't bothered by Giratina-O's Draco Meteor, preserving Recover PP is great for longer games. Tera Fairy also provides Garganacl with the unique trait of resisting Marshadow's STAB combination, which is highly valued by bulky teams worried about Choice Band Marshadow. Tera Fairy Garganacl can still survive an attack from wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, but has a harder time with defensive Primal Kyogre as it is 2HKOed by +1 Scald.
  • Garganacl has a presence in every stage of most games. Early-game, it will often set Stealth Rock while punishing switch-ins with Salt Cure. Garganacl is content to repeat the process mid-game, and it can act as a win condition end-game using Protect and Recover to allow Salt Cure chip to accumulate.
  • Garganacl partners well with Pokemon such as Ferrothorn and Eternatus to create a hazard stacking core where Salt Cure can prevent Pokemon such as Alomomola and Taunt Arceus formes, which can usually hinder hazard setters playing a similar role, from taking advantage of Garganacl. Forgoing a Defogger and relying on the pressure from entry hazards to pressure opponents to Defog is valid, but Ho-Oh nevertheless makes a good partner thanks to its consistency and defensive prowess, while Choice Scarf Yveltal partners well due to its ability to position with U-turn, revenge kill Pokemon such as Marshadow and Zacian-C, and consistently Defog at least once per game.
  • Garganacl often appreciates a teammate that can apply a direct source of offensive pressure to act as a win condition such as a Calm Mind Arceus forme or Zygarde. Although these Pokemon are self sufficient, their offensive presence is accentuated by Salt Cure chip. They appreciate Garganacl helping against Pokemon such as Ho-Oh and Primal Kyogre while Garganacl appreciates the help against Primal Groudon and Eternatus. Ditto also fills this role due to its ability to revenge kill most Pokemon on hyper offense teams that threaten to overwhelm Garganacl. Additionally, most Pokemon appreciate Garganacl's ability to act as a status sponge against defensive threats such as Ho-Oh and Eternatus.

Garganacl is a viable defensive Pokemon with access to its amazing ability in Purifying Salt, allowing it to find entry points on common defensive staples such as Toxapex and Heatran while also boasting its naturally high bulk; it excels at walling some of the metagame staples in Terapagos, Volcarona, and Zapdos. Salt Cure helps it handle Pokemon with no recovery options, like Great Tusk and Terapagos. Also, Salt Cure allows it to slowly chip the annoying Steel-types in Ferrothorn, Iron Treads, and Gholdengo, as well as Water-types like Toxapex and Alomomola. Additionally, Protect synergizes well with Salt Cure, allowing further chip damage and helping scout super effective Z-Moves from the likes of Kyurem and Heatran. Garganacl is an effective Stealth Rock setter, since it is exceptional at outlasting common removal options like Great Tusk, Terapagos, and Corviknight, as most of these removal options don't have reliable recovery or hate switching into Salt Cure. Heavy-Duty Boots is also an option on teams with little to no entry hazard removal, but is not optimal due to the necessity of Leftovers recovery. 52 Defense EVs allow Garganacl to survive a Power Whip from Ogerpon-W at full health.

Garganacl fits best on balance or bulkier teams, which can provide better support and work around its bad typing, making good use of its utility and role compression with setting entry hazards. Partners like Kingambit and Kyurem appreciate Garganacl chipping down Pokemon like Corviknight, Landorus-T, and Great Tusk for the former, and Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Melmetal for the latter. In return, they pressure Garganacl's switch-ins like Clefable, Gliscor, and Galarian Slowking. Gholdengo is also a great partner, being able to block Rapid Spin from the likes of Great Tusk and Terapagos, keeping up hazards that Garganacl set up. Knock Off users like Weavile and Clefable make excellent partners by removing crucial items like Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon such as opposing Clefable and Galarian Slowking. The loss of such items makes the hazards and Salt Cure damage more valuable over time. Garganacl also works well with teammates such as Ogerpon-W and Ferrothorn, who struggle with common Flying-types such as Tornadus-T and Zapdos which allow Garganacl entry points to start racking up chip damage or set Stealth Rock. Garganacl has an unfavorable base typing in Rock, being weak to common types like Water, Fighting, and Ground, which can be seen as common picks in the metagame in Hisuian Samurott, Zamazenta, Landorus-T, and others. Slowbro makes a great partner, walling the aforementioned Fighting- and Water-types while also pivoting into Garganacl, making it more effective. Additionally, Flying-types like Zapdos make great partners, being immune to Ground-type attacks.

SpDef Wall (SpD, HP).description:
Garganacl is a premier wall that leverages its incredible bulk, unique ability, and decent utility to consistently wear down opponents over time. Salt Cure is the cornerstone of the set, providing chip damage every turn. When combined with Protect, Garganacl can safely stall turns to rack up Salt Cure damage and Leftovers recovery, making it extremely difficult to outlast. Recover gives Garganacl the reliable healing it needs to continually check powerful special attackers like Iron Moth and Darkrai across a long battle. Stealth Rock is generally preferred on Garganacl, but if the team already has the move covered, it can also run Curse, acting as a late-game wincon that becomes extremely bulky on both ends. When running Curse, Garganacl should also use Earthquake, which prevents it from becoming overly passive and allows it to hit targets like Necrozma-DM, Eternatus, and Galarian Slowking. Tera Water is the most consistent choice for Garganacl, removing its Steel and Water weaknesses while being an all-around good defensive typing. Alternatively, Tera Fairy flips its Fighting weakness, while Tera Ghost lets Garganacl spinblock Great Tusk while maintaining synergy with Purifying Salt.

Garganacl fits comfortably on balance and stall teams that appreciate its ability to spread passive damage and blanket check special attackers such as Iron Moth, Eternatus, and Darkrai. It thrives with high Special Defense donations from gods such as Calyrex-I and Ho-Oh, amplifying its already exceptional resilience and letting it wall powerful neutral hits with ease. However, HP donations from gods like Eternatus and Arceus are also acceptable. Since Garganacl thrives on chip damage, it appreciates Spikes setters like Hisuian Samurott, Ting-Lu, and Ogerpon, as well as spinblockers such as Pecharunt and Sinistcha to keep entry hazards up. Knock Off support is invaluable for Garganacl, since removing Heavy-Duty Boots, Leftovers, and Covert Cloak is very important for racking up chip damage. Thus, teammates like Iron Treads, Darkrai, and Weavile that can remove key items are highly appreciated.

Specially Defensive.description: Garganacl stands out as one of the tier's premier special walls, boasting exceptional bulk that grants it the ability to check special attackers such as Raging Bolt and Eternatus. With Sablenite, Garganacl's defenses are elevated even further while also granting it Magic Bounce, punishing attempts to set entry hazards except against Mold Breaker foes and allowing it to exploit common Pokemon such as Latiasite Magearna. Alternatively, Tyranitarite provides Garganacl with the Sand Stream ability, so it can increase its Special Defense even further and inflict additional chip damage through sand, which synergizes effectively with Salt Cure and hazards. Earthquake hits foes like Raging Bolt and non-Latiasite Magearna and Pecharunt, granting it somewhat of an offensive presence. Curse enhances Garganacl's ability to check physical attackers and can also be utilized to sweep opposing teams all while making it incredibly difficult to KO. Garganacl can even fulfill the role of a Stealth Rock setter by leveraging its ability to force switches and accumulate chip damage through Salt Cure. Garganacl thrives on balance teams and provides them with outstanding defensive utility; thus, pairing it with other bulky partners such as Magearna, Pecharunt, Arceus-Ground, and Ho-Oh creates a formidable core. Magearna has noteworthy synergy, as it also sets Spikes and capitalizes on Garganacl's ability to force switches through Salt Cure. Pokemon such as Arceus-Water, Urshifu-R, and Pinsirite Great Tusk as well as Latiasite users like Pecharunt and Magearna help Garganacl against troublesome Ground-type foes such as Arceus-Ground and Great Tusk. Offensive partners like Regieleki and Dragonite also form effective pairings with Garganacl, as they appreciate its capacity to wall threats like Eternatus, while in return, they can check foes such as Urshifu-R and Iron Boulder.

The Salt Cure.description: Garganacl is a tough defensive wall that uses Salt Cure to wear down defensive Pokemon, like Swampert, Great Tusk, and Corviknight, and utilizes its ability selection to check a variety of different Pokemon. Fluffy allows Garganacl to check Kingambit and Iron Boulder, Water Absorb lets it reliably switch in on defensive Manaphy as well as help with checking Choice-locked Water-types like Barraskewda and Primarina, and Earth Eater lets it check Roaring Moon and Dragonite running Earthquake. Stealth Rock lets Garganacl support its teammates by providing entry hazards, while with Iron Defense or Curse, Garganacl can set up on and more easily check Pokemon like Iron Hands, Ceruledge, and Dragonite, and boost Body Press or Earthquake, depending on the set. When using Body Press, Garganacl can more efficiently take on Chien-Pao as well as a majority of other Pokemon, while with Earthquake, it can deal with Iron Boulder and Pecharunt. Protect lets Garganacl deal extra damage with Salt Cure active as well as gain some extra Leftovers recovery. Garganacl can either use Leftovers or Heavy-Duty Boots, the former letting it gain more recovery through Protect and the latter helping Garganacl switch in more often. Garganacl provides great defensive support to frail offensive Pokemon, like Iron Moth, Gengar, and Galarian Zapdos, as a to check faster Pokemon like Roaring Moon, Dragonite, and Iron Boulder. Garganacl can struggle against special attackers, such as Deoxys-S, Azelf, and offensive Gholdengo, so having specially defensive teammates, like Hisuian Goodra, Manaphy, and Blissey, can help. Garganacl enjoys being on more defensive teams for having teammates that can take on physical attackers with it, such as Pecharunt, Mandibuzz, and Primarina, as it struggles to reliably check Pokemon like Chien-Pao, Zamazenta, and Barraskewda.

Iron Defense.description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Tera Fairy allows Garganacl to wall Koraidon fully, but since it prevents Garganacl from walling Arceus and Substitute Ho-Oh, this set is not regularly used. Garganacl could also opt to use Curse, increasing the damage of Salt Cure while simultaneously allowing Garganacl to keep up with boosting threats. Yet, the additional Salt Cure damage is inconsequential, and it takes many more turns for Garganacl to do the same amount of damage with Body Press if it were instead using Iron Defense.

Checks and Counters

Special Attackers: Special attackers like Kyogre, Miraidon, and Calyrex-S can easily exploit Garganacl's poor special defenses to threaten massive damage.

Koraidon: Koraidon's super effective Low Kick does great damage to Garganacl, forcing it to switch out even after an Iron Defense boost.

Knock Off Users: Knock Off users like Gliscor significantly cripple Garganacl's defensive capabilities, causing it to be much less effective in checking Pokemon like Earthquake Ho-Oh after some entry hazard chip damage.

Zacian-C: Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, especially in combination with Swords Dance, tears through even boosted Garganacl's HP and forces it to switch out.

Necrozma-DM: Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, in combination with a move like Dragon Dance or Swords Dance, threatens great damage to Garganacl, forcing it to switch out.

Defensive.description:
Salt Cure puts a timer on any Pokemon attempting to set up against Garganacl while also breaking offensive Ho-Oh's Substitute and dealing considerable damage to Zacian-C, Giratina-O, and Kyogre that try to switch in. Iron Defense allows Garganacl to keep up with Swords Dance Arceus and also allows it to check Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground after Terastallization. The IronPress combination allows Garganacl to do significant damage to Pokemon like Arceus and anything else that attempts to switch in. Alternatively, Stealth Rock further chips defensive Arceus formes and Choice Scarf users, allowing Garganacl to aid its team. Body Press, usually used in conjunction with Iron Defense, allows Garganacl to become a late-game sweeper while also dealing considerable damage to more offensive Pokemon like Arceus, Arceus-Ground, and Koraidon. Protect lets Garganacl safely scout Choice item users, like Choice Band Koraidon and Choice Specs Kyogre, as well as provide an additional turn of Salt Cure chip damage. Tera Flying gives Garganacl an immunity to Arceus-Ground, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu's Earthquake, as well as a resistance to Koraidon's Low Kick and Calyrex-S's Grass Knot. On the other hand, Tera Water gives Garganacl a resistance to Zacian-C's Behemoth Blade, Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike, Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance, and Kyogre's Water-type attacks in a pinch. Garganacl is an especially effective Ho-Oh check, as Purifying Salt nullifies its Sacred Fire burns.

Physically frail Pokemon like Blissey and Clodsire enjoy having Garganacl on their team, as it excels in checking both Extreme Killer and Bulk Up Arceus. Even physically defensive Pokemon like Gliscor, various bulky Water-types, and Skeledirge appreciate Garganacl for its ability to wall both offensive Ho-Oh sets and Giratina-O with ease. However, although Garganacl can wall many physical threats, its special defenses are lacking. Powerful special attackers like Kyogre, Miraidon, and Calyrex-S can easily break through Garganacl. Thus, Garganacl appreciates having teammates like Blissey, Specially Defensive Ho-Oh, and Clodsire, which find it far easier to handle special-attacking threats. Although Garganacl has excellent defenses, it still cannot handle super effective hits from Koraidon, Zacian-C, Arceus-Ground, and Necrozma-DM. Pokemon like Alomomola, Skeledirge, and Gliscor, which switch into their attacks, are very effective when paired with Garganacl.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Psychic

Psyshock can be used over Stored Power, which allows Armarouge to break through special walls like Blissey and Clodsire. Destiny Bond can be used as the last move, which allows Armarouge to take foes like Alolan Muk or Ting-Lu down with it, opening up opportunities for teammates like Deoxys-S.

Endure + Weakness Policy (Psychic).description:
With Weakness Policy, Endure, and a Speed boost from Weak Armor, Armarouge becomes a fast and hard-hitting late-game sweeper, outspeeding and removing threats like Kleavor, Choice Band Meowscarada, the Landorus formes, and Choice Scarf Urshifu-S. At +2 Special Attack, Focus Blast allows Armarouge to OHKO Heatran, Darkrai, and Ursaluna while also 2HKOing threats switching into Armarouge such as Hisuian Goodra and Blissey. Aura Sphere can be used over Focus Blast for its accuracy; however, it trades off Focus Blast's higher power, making it miss out on OHKOing specially defensive Heatran after a Weakness Policy activation. Stored Power can be used over Expanding Force for higher breaking power after Weakness Policy and Weak Armor have activated, but this comes at the cost of being weaker without their previously mentioned boosts. Flamethrower allows Armarouge to melt Steel-types like Corviknight and Gholdengo, while Armor Cannon has higher breaking power and is capable of OHKOing Gliscor and non-Assault Vest Tornadus-T after a Weakness Policy boost.

Indeedee-M is a crucial teammate due to its ability to set Psychic Terrain and its switch into Ghost-type attacks. Setting Psychic Terrain allows Armarouge to use a greatly strengthened Expanding Force that can KO Swampert and Assault Vest Gallade after Stealth Rock chip damage and Weakness Policy's activation. It also protects Armarouge from powerful priority attacks like Bisharp's Sucker Punch and Azumarill's Aqua Jet. Deoxys-S is another great partner with Armarouge due to its access to Spikes and Stealth Rock, which allow Armarouge to break through bulkier Pokemon like the Ogerpon formes and Ting-Lu and bypass Sturdy and Focus Sash from Ogerpon-C, Forretress, and Great Tusk. Deoxys-S can also set dual screens for Armarouge, allowing it to live a hit from Pokemon like Weavile, Lokix, and Excadrill and OHKO them back with Weakness Policy-boosted moves without the need for Endure. Hoopa-U and Gallade are great offensive partners for Armarouge the former handles Ghost-types like Spectrier and Flutter Mane while the latter deals with Dark-types like Alolan Muk and Ting-Lu. Hatterene is a good partner due to its imperative access to Magic Bounce, granting Armarouge some relief from hazards, and, if holding a Kasib Berry, Hatterene can paralyze fast Ghost-types like Dragapult and Spectrier with Nuzzle. Iron Boulder and Latios both appreciate Armarouge's ability to eliminate annoying Steel-types like Corviknight and Scizor. In return, the former checks fast threats like Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Greninja, and Roaring Moon, while the latter uses its Ground immunity and BoltBeam coverage to eliminate walls like Empoleon and Gliscor. Slowbro is a good defensive partner for Armarouge, as it uses its Water resistance to take hits from Barraskewda and Gyarados and can deal with Ceruledge if it chooses to forgo an item.

Calm Mind (Psychic).description:
With its great defensive stats, access to Calm Mind and Stored Power, and Weak Armor ability, Armarouge becomes a potent setup sweeper on Psychic teams. Flamethrower complements Armarouge's Stored Power, allowing it to hit Steel-types like Scizor, Gholdengo, and Iron Treads. Iron Defense increases Armarouge's survivability against physical attacks, negating Defense drops from Weak Armor as well as letting it survive super effective moves like Earthquake from defensive Great Tusk, activating its Weakness Policy. At +1, Focus Blast allows Armarouge to OHKO Dark-types like Roaring Moon, Hydreigon, and potentially Tyranitar while also 2HKOing Hisuian Goodra and specially defensive Heatran. Aura Sphere can be used over Focus Blast for its accuracy; however, it trades off Focus Blast's higher power, requiring multiple boosts to OHKO common foes like Roaring Moon. Weak Armor boost allows Armarouge to outspeed faster threats like Dragapult, Flutter Mane, and Choice Scarf users like Roaring Moon, Hisuian Samurott, and Landorus while also boosting the power of Stored Power.

Deoxys-S is an excellent partner for Armarouge, providing dual screens support for easier setup and setting entry hazards, making it easier for Armarouge to break through bulky foes. Indeedee sets up Psychic Terrain, which boosts the power of Armarouge's Psychic moves and blocks priority moves like Bisharp's Sucker Punch and Azumarill's Aqua Jet. Indeedee can also provide Healing Wish support, giving Armarouge a second chance to sweep. Latios provides a Ground immunity and a Water resistance and threatens foes with these types back with its BoltBeam coverage. Gallade threatens Dark-types like Ting-Lu and Alolan Muk, while Hoopa-U deals with Ghost-types like non-Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Skeledirge, and Spectrier. Armarouge also appreciates the pair's ability to break through special walls such as Hisuian Goodra, Swampert, and Blissey. Hatterene provides hazard control thanks to Magic Bounce, and Choice Scarf Iron Boulder deals with faster threats like Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Greninja, and Roaring Moon. Both appreciate Armarouge handling Steel-types like Archaludon, Scizor, and Corviknight.

Expanding Force.description:
• Armarouge's combination of powerful STAB moves, excellent coverage, Weak Armor, and Psychic Terrain makes it a strong candidate to use Focus Sash.

  • Psychic Terrain: Psychic Terrain is a powerful setup move for Armarouge thanks to Expanding Force; it also protects Armarouge from priority moves after Weak Armor triggers.

  • Expanding Force: Expanding Force under Psychic Terrain especially with Tera Psychic, is a devastatingly powerful move.

  • Armor Cannon: This helps Armarouge defeat Steel-types as well as Chien-Pao and Wo-Chien, who all resist or block Expanding Force.

  • Aura Sphere: While Armor Cannon covers several prominent Dark-types, Aura Sphere is needed if you want to threaten Chi-Yu or Roaring Moon.

  • Destiny Bond: This is a good alternative to forcefully take down threats that Armarouge can’t easily KO, and it works very well with Weak Armor.

  • Energy Ball: Energy Ball hits the specially defensive Water-types Armarouge might struggle to defeat otherwise, most notably Gastrodon.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low / Medium: Between Focus Sash and Psychic Terrain blocking priority moves, Armarouge is well-equipped to play without Tera. On the other hand, Armarouge can specialize to handle certain matchups better, at which point Tera can become more necessary.

  • Grass: This Tera typing turns Armarouge's Water- and Ground-type weaknesses into resistances, and gives a vital Spore immunity against opposing Breloom.

  • Psychic: With a boost from Tera Psychic, Expanding Force OHKOes even relatively bulky foes such as Garchomp and Flutter Mane. With Stealth Rock, Expanding Force still achieves most notable KOs without Tera Psychic, but the extra damage is still appreciated.

  • Fairy: In cases where setting up Psychic Terrain proves to be more difficult, Tera Fairy grants a resistance to Sucker Punch and makes disrupting other Dark-types like Chi-Yu easier. Its also just a solid defensive typing that neutralizes all of its other weaknesses.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting is a more niche option for a Dark-type resistance that also powers up Aura Sphere.

Abilities

  • Weak Armor: This ability takes full advantage of Focus Sash, guaranteeing you live a single hit from a physical attacker and granting a big Speed boost thereafter.

  • Flash Fire: While more situational, Flash Fire is worth considering with certain Tera Types like Grass, keeping momentum against revenge killers who use Fire-type attacks. It can also be used with Tera Fairy or Tera Fighting to shut down many variants of Chi-Yu.

Offensive.description: • This set does not have a full write-up yet. If you'd like to finish this, feel free to reserve it here!

Swords Dance.description:
With Swords Dance, Weak Armor, and an excellent STAB combination, Ceruledge is a solid setup sweeper and late-game cleaner. Bitter Blade's additional benefit of allowing Ceruledge to recover HP lets it survive revenge killing attempts and gives it even more setup opportunities. Shadow Sneak allows Ceruledge to finish off faster and weakened foes like Ogerpon-W and Dragapult if Weak Armor hasn't been activated yet. Poltergeist gives Ceruledge a powerful STAB move that hits Pecharunt and neutral foes like Alomomola, Primarina, Moltres, and Dragonite. Close Combat complements its STAB moves to hit Hisuian Samurott and Garganacl, which would otherwise wall it, while giving it a strong nuke against Ting-Lu and Kyurem. Solar Blade with Tera Grass can be used on sun teams to hit checks such as Alomomola, Dondozo, and Garganacl. Life Orb augments Ceruledge's damage output while also working well with Bitter Blade to offset the recoil; in particular, this lets Ceruledge threaten OHKOs against the likes of Gliscor and Zapdos with +2 Poltergeist. Air Balloon lets it emergency check threats like Kyurem and Enamorus and flip the script on foes like Great Tusk and Landorus-T; this can put them in a checkmate, as hitting Ceruledge with weak moves like Ice Spinner and U-turn to pop the item would only give it a trouble-free Weak Armor boost. Focus Sash allows Ceruledge to survive attacks from faster foes such as Great Tusk, Ogerpon-W, and Darkrai as well as revenge killing attempts from Kingambit, and it synergizes well with Weak Armor to gain the Speed Boost against the aforementioned physical attackers. Heavy-Duty Boots makes Ceruledge less reliant on keeping entry hazards off the field, particularly on teams that lack sturdy hazard removal. Tera Ghost is preferred on Poltergeist and Life Orb variants and enhances its offensive prowess further, reaching feats like OHKOing Dragonite through Multiscale with +2 Poltergeist and OHKOing Enamorus and Ogerpon-W after minor chip damage with +2 Shadow Sneak. Tera Fairy is used to enhance Ceruledge's defensive properties for easier setup; this is particularly helpful against problematic Dark-types like Darkrai and Hisuian Samurott while still being a great defensive typing against threats like Dragapult. When running Close Combat, Tera Fighting is recommended to enhance its power, notably letting Ceruledge secure an OHKO on Ting-Lu after a Swords Dance. Tera Fighting also grants Ceruledge a Dark resistance similar to Tera Fairy. The power from an Adamant nature is preferred, especially because Weak Armor and Shadow Sneak can mitigate the lower Speed, but a Jolly nature can be used to outspeed Gholdengo and Speed tie Rillaboom and Hisuian Samurott as well as outpace Booster Energy Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf Darkrai at +2. Adamant Ceruledge can also run lesser Speed EVs for more bulk, such as an EV spread of 80 HP / 252 Atk / 176 Spe that runs enough Speed to outpace Raging Bolt; this is a more viable option if running Air Balloon or Heavy-Duty Boots, as these synergize better with the extra bulk.

Ceruledge's offensive tools means it best fits on hyper offense teams where it finds its home as a sweeper that appreciates entry hazards and the presence of other sweepers such as Dragonite, Zamazenta, Gholdengo, and Darkrai. Great Tusk and Iron Treads are excellent partners; both offer reliable hazard control to keep Ceruledge's Focus Sash intact, while Ceruledge can eliminate their common checks. Ceruledge also pairs well with hazard setters such as Glimmora and Hisuian Samurott, which can allow Ceruledge to secure KOs it would fall short of, especially when utilizing a Jolly nature, such as OHKOing Ting-Lu and Garganacl with a +2 non-Tera Fighting Close Combat. Additionally, Ceruledge can deny Rapid Spin from opposing Iron Treads and Great Tusk while threatening Corviknight. Ceruledge generally appreciates special sweepers such as Calm Mind Iron Valiant and Raging Bolt, threatening its checks and counters such as Garganacl and Dragonite. In return, Ceruledge can handle Blissey and Galarian Slowking, which would otherwise deny a sweep from these special sweepers. Ceruledge is also a consideration on sun teams alongside a setter in Ninetales or Torkoal, since Ceruledge becomes extremely threatening with sun-boosted Bitter Blade paired with Solar Blade, the latter of which rips apart its usual checks in Great Tusk and Alomomola. Walking Wake and Ceruledge form a nearly unwallable duo, as Walking Wake can deal heavy damage to Pokemon that would otherwise wall Ceruledge like Dragonite and Zamazenta. Other sun partners such as Slither Wing and Hatterene provide pivoting and other utility that can support a Ceruledge sweep. Another hyper offense archetype Ceruledge can fit on is Sticky Web teams with setters like Ribombee and Araquanid. On these teams, Ceruledge acts as a spinblocker and sweeper that pairs excellently with its previously mentioned teammates.

Swords Dance (Fire).description:
Ceruledge is an exceptional wallbreaker on Fire teams with its access to strong STAB moves and priority. Swords Dance allows it to set up quickly, enabling it to break walls like Iron Hands and Hisuian Goodra with relative ease. Bitter Blade allows Ceruledge to re-enable its Focus Sash if it's not already consumed. Poltergeist hits foes that resist Bitter Blade like Archaludon, Toxapex, and Heatran. Shadow Sneak allows Ceruledge to check faster threats like Dragapult, Iron Boulder, and Flutter Mane. Jolly Nature makes Ceruledge faster than threats like Choice Scarf Iron Boulder and Choice Scarf Landorus after a boost from Weak Armor, checking the former with Poltergeist and the latter with +2 Bitter Blade.

Both sun setters, Ninetales and Torkoal, are amazing teammates for Ceruledge. Ninetales has access to utility moves such as Encore and Healing Wish to ensure Ceruledge can come safely on the field and can also use Solar Beam to punish Gastrodon and Swampert, while Torkoal can set Stealth Rock up and remove opposing entry hazards with Rapid Spin. Sun is especially primordial for Ceruledge, as it boosts the power of Bitter Blade and enhances Ceruledge's wallbreaking capabilities, notably allowing it to OHKO specially defensive Gliscor after a Swords Dance. Cinderace provides support with Court Change, ensuring Ceruledge's Focus Sash remains intact, and can take out Dark-type foes such as Hydreigon and Tyranitar with High Jump Kick. Ogerpon-H is a great wallbreaking partner for Ceruledge, hitting Heatran whose Air Balloon has been popped as well as Water- and Ground-type threats such as Hisuian Samurott, Keldeo, Swampert, and Hippowdon. Air Balloon Heatran is another great partner, providing a Ground immunity and dealing with Flutter Mane. Finally, Volcarona is a valuable teammate, as it can ease Ceruledge's job by disposing of Toxapex and Urshifu-R while benefiting from the breaches Ceruledge can create against opposing special walls such as Gliscor and Clodsire.

Swords Dance (Ghost).description:
Ceruledge is an impeccable wallbreaker and late-game setup sweeper on Ghost teams, boasting a great Attack stat, a useful ability in Weak Armor, and a hard-hitting STAB combination. Poltergeist is Ceruledge's hardest hitting STAB move, notably OHKOing walls like Clodsire, Sinistcha, and Pecharunt after a Swords Dance. Alternatively, Close Combat may be used to threaten Dark-types such as Ting-Lu, Roaring Moon, and Hisuian Samurott as well as Steel-types such as Heatran and Archaludon. However, Ceruledge without a powerful Ghost-type STAB move will be walled by Skeledirge, Garchomp, and Toxapex. Bitter Blade allows Ceruledge to eliminate Steel-types like Skarmory, and Iron Treads as well as recover any chip damage so Focus Sash can be properly utilized. Furthermore, Bitter Blade can be used to trade with threats like Alolan Muk, Weavile, and Meowscarada. Shadow Sneak scares away faster Ghost-types such as Flutter Mane, Dragapult, and Spectrier, OHKOing them after Ceruledge boosts its Attack stat. A Jolly nature enables Ceruledge to outpace Choice Scarf users like Darkrai, Iron Boulder, Greninja, and Meowscarada after a Weak Armor boost, while an Adamant nature allows Ceruledge to OHKO Archaludon and Rotom-W after a Swords Dance and Stealth Rock damage.

Flutter Mane is a great teammate due to its ability to check Dark-types like Mandibuzz, Hydreigon, and Greninja while in return, Ceruledge takes out specially defensive walls such as Heatran, Clodsire, and Hisuian Goodra. Air Balloon Gholdengo breaks past threats like Ursaluna and Toxapex should Ceruledge not opt for Poltergeist. In exchange, Ceruledge threatens the aforementioned Steel-types and breaks past specially defensive walls like Blissey and Swampert. Sinistcha leverages its resistance to Ground and Water to switch into attacks from Ogerpon-W, Excadrill, and Keldeo, and it can also spread burns via Matcha Gotcha to weaken walls. Dragapult spreads status ailments through Thunder Wave and Will-O-Wisp to chip down physically defensive walls and threatens Dragon-types such as Kommo-o, Raging Bolt, and Dragonite. Spectrier also spreads burns with Will-O-Wisp and appreciates Ceruledge weakening teams so it can easily clean late-game by setting up Calm Mind repeatedly or sweeping via a Choice Scarf set. Brambleghast removes entry hazards with Rapid Spin to maintain Ceruledge's Focus Sash and provides the same resistances that Sinistcha does. Hisuian Zoroark offers a Ghost-type immunity and the ability to remove Dark-types like Hydreigon and Hisuian Samurott via Focus Blast. Froslass provides Spikes support to wear down foes and prevents hazards from being set by using Taunt. Golurk offers Stealth Rock support and can set up beneficial trades using Berries or a Focus Sash.

Endure + Weakness Policy (Ghost).description: This is a winning set from the Monotype Rising sets project. This will be updated as we work on new analyses. Stay tuned!

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
With Paradox Pokemon being introduced, Series 2 is bringing big changes to Battle Stadium Singles! This is a modified Series 1 analysis that takes Paradox Pokemon into account. We will update this overview and analysis again once the metagame settles more. For more information on Series 2, check out the resource thread.

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Bulk Up Sweeper.description:
• Bulk Up Ceruledge makes excellent use of both its respectable bulk and Bitter Blade's high recovery. By changing its typing to a more defense oriented one, while maintaining the Fire immunity thanks to Flash Fire, Ceruledge can set up Bulk Ups on a variety of common Pokemon, ranging from Corviknight, Kingambit, Azumarill and Gholdengo.

  • Taunt: Taunt lets Ceruledge set up Bulk Up without needing to fear common phasing moves (with the exception of attacking moves such as Dragon Tail), as well as opposing setup moves such opposing Bulk Up and Iron Defense, provided you outspeed.

  • Shadow Sneak Priority of some form is always nice to have on a Pokemon, which makes Shadow Sneak an easy contender for the last move. Gaining extra added strength against Pokemon such as Flutter Mane, Dragapult and Annihilape is certainly charming.

  • Grass Tera Blast: This allows Ceruledge to eliminate Dondozo more quickly. While Taunt can shut down Dondozo's Yawn, it cannot shut down Fissure. The only way to beat Dondozo would be to eliminate it as quickly as possibly, which Grass Tera Blast aids with.

  • Flame Charge: Flame Charge provides Ceruledge an extra net of safety against potential Scarf users and Annihilape, who are capable of turning the tides against it. While normally, Ceruledge is prone to faster Taunt + Bulk Up users and Scarfed Trick, Flame Charge helps mitigate both of those weaknesses.

  • Will-O-Wisp: Ceruledge can be a status spreader in games where it can't set up as easily. It also helps Ceruledge set up more easily against threats such as Unaware Clodsire.

Tera Types

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy helps Ceruledge's matchup against prominent Dark-types such as Roaring Moon and Hydreigon.

  • Grass: An immunity to Spore and a resistance to Water makes Grass the most notable Tera type for this set. Flash Fire eliminating one of Grass's many weaknesses is also noteworthy.

  • Fire: Increasing Bitter Blade's power will always be a valuable trait. Eliminating Ghost's weaknesses to Ghost and Dark also allows Ceruledge to set up more comfortably.

  • Bug: Tera Bug is similar to Tera Grass, but in exchange for losing the Water resistance and maintaining the Rock weakness of Fire / Ghost, Ceruledge can tank Volcarona's Bug Buzz with significantly more ease.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 Def with Impish: Investing into Defense prepares Ceruledge and its mediocre physical bulk for the physical-biased metagame. Bulk Up will boost its Defense, but it can struggle to take some physical hits even after a boost, and its special bulk is naturally high.

  • 252 HP / 252 Spe with Jolly: A faster spread helps Ceruledge outspeed other Bulk Up users, like Annihilape opting to invest in bulk. Being faster, more often than not, lets Ceruledge win these matchups with ease.

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD with Careful: While most threats in the metagame at the moment are physical, a specially defensive spread is still noteworthy for its ability to surprise Hydreigon.

Focus Sash Attacker.description:
