• With a stellar offensive typing, a unique set of attacks, Weak Armor allowing it to outspeed a large part of the metagame, and its immunity to Extreme Speed and Mach Punch, Ceruledge proves itself to be a very solid Focus Sash option.

  • Bitter Blade: Bitter Blade's recovery can make Focus Sash usable even if entry hazards chip it. If Ceruledge is brought down to 1 HP, a +2 Bitter Blade can heal it to the point that it can tank an extra attack.

  • Close Combat versus Shadow Claw: Close Combat hits the Normal-, Dark-, and Rock-types that resist Ceruledge's STAB combination. Still, Shadow Claw is a noteworthy choice to guarantee the KO on Mimikyu and let Ceruledge pressure Skeledirge. Note, however, that maximum Defense Skeledirge can recover more than Shadow Claw's damage, barring critical hits, and a Terastallized Skeledirge can completely wall this set.

  • Swords Dance versus Destiny Bond: As powerful as Swords Dance boosted attacks from Ceruledge are, the abundance of Unaware Pokemon, primarily Dondozo, has made some players opt to use Destiny Bond to snag surprise kills. Destiny Bond can also make the matchup against KOing common Sucker Punch Pokemon, such as Meowscarada and Kingambit, easier to win without having to rely on predictions.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant's added damage output is valuable, but Jolly allows Ceruledge to outspeed non-Scarf Gholdengo, and gives it a chance at outspeeding Modest Rotom formes and Glimmora. All of the mentioned examples are Special Attackers, meaning Ceruledge's Weak Armor often does not trigger in these matchups.

Tera Types

  • Fire: Giving Bitter Blade an extra push in damage is quite useful, giving Ceruledge more recovery.

  • Normal: Normal is an exceedingly common Tera Type on Ghost types due to the immunity it brings to the table. Ceruledge makes particularly excellent use of Normal Tera by resisting both Steel and Fairy, making it very difficult for Gholdengo and Mimikyu to click anything other than a Ghost type move when facing off against Ceruledge.

  • Fighting: Giving extra reach power to Close Combat, a powerful option against Pokemon such as Hydreigon, makes Fighting a solid choice for a Tera Type.

Swords Dance (Ghost).description: With access to Swords Dance and a nuclear-strength Never-Ending Nightmare, Ceruledge is the premier physical wallbreaker for Ghost teams. At +2, Poltergeist outright OHKOes non-Unaware Clodsire and OHKOes Mega Sableye, Swampert, and defensive Heatran after Spikes damage. While boosted, Ceruledge with Ghostium Z can take out an even wider range of defensive foes with Never-Ending Nightmare, securing OHKOs on Toxapex and Mega Venusaur while being favored to OHKO Archaludon and Dragonite through Multiscale. Opting for Focus Sash weakens Ceruledge's potential damage output, but it allows Ceruledge to activate Weak Armor and beat dangerous physical threats such as Ogerpon-C and Iron Treads that would otherwise simply outspeed and OHKO it. Shadow Sneak allows Ceruledge to pick off weakened faster foes like Iron Boulder, Barraskewda, and opposing Ceruledge, while Close Combat lets it surprise foes it otherwise struggles to beat, such as Roaring Moon and Porygon2. Ceruledge appreciates Sableye's dual screens support, as the increased durability allows it to set up in more situations while making the healing from Bitter Blade even more significant. On bulkier Ghost teams, Mega Sableye also makes a good teammate for Ceruledge; it keeps hazards off the field and freely switches in on physical walls that Ceruledge forces in like Ting-Lu, Archaludon, and Mandibuzz. Sinistcha works well with Ceruledge as a special setup threat that handles Water- and Ground-type foes like Keldeo and Landorus-T; in return, Ceruledge handles bulky Steel- and Grass-types like Mega Scizor and Tapu Bulu for Sinistcha. Brambleghast can fulfill a similar defensive role, trading Sinistcha's setup potential for the ability to set and remove hazards in order to keep Ceruledge healthy and ease its wallbreaking duties. Hisuian Zoroark and Ceruledge can work together to break down physically defensive foes, as Hisuian Zoroark lures foes like Moltres and Tyranitar while disguised as Ceruledge and then hits them with Focus Blast or Shadow Ball. Mega Banette has particular synergy with Ceruledge on offensive teams, where it forces opponents to send out their answers to its brutally strong Poltergeist and trades with them using Destiny Bond, enabling Ceruledge to wreak havoc later. Similarly, Mimikyu is a great partner, as it can use Swords Dance, Drain Punch, and Play Rough to help Ceruledge overwhelm Normal- and Dark-type foes that would handle Ceruledge's Poltergeist. Choice Scarf Mimikyu can also support Ceruledge by spreading burns, using Trick to cripple opposing physical walls that switch in fearing Mimikyu's Swords Dance set, and hitting faster Dark-types such as Hydreigon and Greninja with Play Rough.

Swords Dance (Fire).description: Ceruledge is a strong late-game sweeper on Fire teams that checks Ghost- and Psychic-types thanks to its powerful STAB moves, setup in Swords Dance, and a great ability in Weak Armor, punishing physical attackers that hit it. At +2, Ceruledge 2HKOes Great Tusk and has a good chance to OHKO Gliscor after Stealth Rock damage with Poltergeist. Shadow Sneak allows Ceruledge to take out boosted albeit weakened Pokemon like Dragonite, Alolan Raichu, Iron Boulder, and opposing Ceruledge. With Focus Sash, Ceruledge ensures its Weak Armor is activated from most physical attacks, and it lets Ceruledge set up Swords Dance once. Cinderace and Torkoal are great partners for Ceruledge, as they provide entry hazard control with Court Change and Rapid Spin, respectively, so that its Focus Sash is kept intact. Additionally, Torkoal sets up sun to further boost Ceruledge's Bitter Blade and Stealth Rock to aid its sweeping, while Cinderace targets Dark-types such as Ting-Lu, Hydreigon, and Tyranitar, which can pose challenges to Ceruledge's sweeping. Wallbreakers such as Choice Band Victini and Mega Charizard X remove bulky Pokemon that Ceruledge dislikes. Victini takes on Water-types such as Tapu Fini, Urshifu-R, and Dondozo, while Mega Charizard X breaks past Heatran. In return, Victini appreciates Ceruledge handling Psychic-types like Iron Boulder and Mega Latias. Hisuian Arcanine revenge kills boosted sweepers such as Roaring Moon so that Ceruledge can sweep, and it can threaten Flying-types such as Galarian Moltres and Zapdos. Ceruledge can also enable other sweepers and cleaners such as Volcarona by removing Pokemon that threaten them such as Skeledirge so they can start their own sweep.

ru.overview: Bellibolt bounces its way into RU as a serviceable defensive Pokemon in the tier, taking on powerful threats such as Flamigo and Bisharp. Bellibolt's moveset is very flexible, letting it aid its team in a variety of ways. Unlike other walls, Bellibolt can cripple switch-ins with Static, keep up momentum with Volt Switch, simultaneously damage opponents while healing with Parabolic Charge, and force out Pokemon that would usually beat it such as Ground-types like Krookodile with Muddy Water. Static is a great ability on Bellibolt to punish physical attackers and the many U-turns in the tier. Bellibolt's main issue is that it struggles against bulky Steel-types such as Magnezone and Hisuian Goodra, as they can easily tank its hits and make progress against it. Despite it having options against them, Ground-types are also a pain for Bellibolt, as if they can get in against it, they can do large damage with Earthquake and threaten it out. Bellibolt can also be overwhelmed by strong neutral attacks such as Terrakion's Close Combat and Bisharp's Throat Chop, as its typing doesn't give it many resistances.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Leftovers allows Bellibolt to passively heal off chip damage from weak attacks such as U-turn, giving it much better longevity, especially if it chooses to use Parabolic Charge. Chilling Water is an option in order to reduce the damage from opposing physical attackers attack stat while still hitting Ground-types, though it is very weak and can give a Defiant or Competitve boost to either Bisharp or Empoleon.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Steel-types: Bulky Steel-types such as Assault Vest Magnezone, Registeel, and Hisuian Goodra can easily take Bellibolt's hits, not worrying about Toxic and making progress through Knock Off, Stealth Rock, or pivoting.

Ground-types: Although Ground-types such as Krookodile, Flygon, and Golurk cannot switch into Toxic or Muddy Water, they can switch into Bellibolt's STAB options and threaten it out with Earthquake.

Cyclizar: Cyclizar can easily take Bellibolt's hits, including Toxic, and use it to make progress. This can be via Rapid Spin, Knock Off, or U-turn, which lets Cyclizar get in teammates that threaten out Bellibolt like Torterra and Krookodile.

Mr. Belli.description:
Set Details

Volt Switch can do solid damage to foes while pivoting Bellibolt out, whereas Parabolic Charge can help Bellibolt stay healthy, especially in combination with Electromorphosis to boost its power. Muddy Water can hit the Ground-types that can switch into its Electric-type moves such as Krookodile and Rhyperior. Soak allows Bellibolt to threaten switch-ins with massive damage from its Electric-type moves, allow it to badly poison Steel- and Poison-types that would usually be immune to it such as Hisuian Goodra and Amoonguss, and reduce the damage of STAB attacks such as Earthquake from Krookodile and Sacred Fire from Entei. Toxic allows Bellibolt to threaten specially defensive switch-ins such as Umbreon and Wo-Chien that would otherwise not care too much about its attacks. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Bellibolt to ignore entry hazards to take on threats more easily. Rocky Helmet allows Bellibolt to counter Maushold and accrue chip damage against the many U-turn users in the tier such as Noivern, Jirachi, and Cyclizar. Static can punish contact attempts from physical attackers such as Terrakion and Gallade by inflicting them with paralysis. Electromorphosis can turn Bellibolt into quite a dangerous attacker that can deal impressive damage to opponents with its Electric-type moves. It pairs especially well with Parabolic Charge, as it can not only deal more damage, but also increase the amount of HP Bellibolt recovers. Tera Water boosts the power of Bellibolt's Muddy Water while removing its weakness to Ground and giving it a solid defensive typing. Tera Fairy gives Bellibolt a Fighting resistance to help take on Pokemon such as Flamigo and Terrakion and can help it take on Ground-types such as Krookodile and Flygon.

Bellibolt is a niche pick on bulky offense and balance teams, where it can act as a reliable defensive piece, taking on Pokemon such as Flamigo and Kilowattrel that these teams might struggle against. Ground-immune and Fighting-resistant partners such as Wo-Chien, Noivern, and Chesnaught can take on the Ground-types such as Krookodile and Rhyperior that threaten Bellibolt out as well as Fighting-types such as Flamigo and Terrakion, while Bellibolt can take on the Flying-types such as Kilowattrel and non-Taunt Noivern. U-turn users such as Flamigo and Jirachi can pair well with Bellibolt to form VoltTurn cores, allowing them to wear down combined checks, such as bulky Ground-types for Flamigo and Steel-types for Jirachi, so that they can be finished off at low health. Water-, Fighting-, and Fire-type wallbreakers pair well with Bellibolt, as it can threaten out the bulky Water-types such as Slowbro and Vaporeon that wall them. In return, Water-type wallbreakers such as Barraskewda and Feraligatr beat Ground-types like Gastrodon and Krookodile; Fighting-type wallbreakers such as Gallade and Terrakion beat Steel-types such as Hisuian Goodra and Magnezone; and Entei beats Grass- and Steel-types such as Amoonguss and Jirachi. Entry hazard control options such as Cyclizar and Noivern pair well with Bellibolt as they can remove entry hazards that might otherwise heavily chip Bellibolt and allow Pokemon such as Terrakion and Choice Band Entei to 2HKO Bellibolt.

nu.overview: Bellibolt carves out a niche for itself thanks to being a bulky Electric-type, which lets it checks dangerous Flying-types like Flamigo, Kilowattrel, and Scyther better than any other wall can. On top of that, it easily punishes the omnipresent U-turn as well as other contact moves like Cinccino's Tail Slap with both Static and its Rocky Helmet, and unlike other walls or tanks, Bellibolt doesn't give up momentum as easily because of its access to Volt Switch, letting it pivot out of bad matchups. Bellibolt's ability to pivot also means that it complements wallbreakers extremely well, giving them a myriad of opportunities to come in. However, this affinity for pivoting can also lead to Bellibolt's downfall, making it quite susceptible to entry hazards if it lacks Heavy-Duty Boots, and if Bellibolt runs that item, then it misses out on the extra chip damage granted by Rocky Helmet, allowing it to be attacked without as great of a concern as otherwise. Additionally, even though Bellibolt can use Toxic to chip away at Ground-types like Flygon and Gastrodon, they still force it out, which grants them a free turn to set hazards or start boosting. Another glaring issue with Bellibolt is its lack of resistances; although a physically defensive Flying-resistant wall with reliable recovery is rare, Bellibolt is often designated as the main physical wall for its team, needing to stomach repeated powerful neutral attacks such as Flamigo's Close Combat and Paldean Tauros-W's Wave Crash. This situation can be worsened even more so if these attackers carry a Choice Band, which they often do, and poison-immune setup sweepers like Toxtricity, Munkidori, and Toxicroak can use Bellibolt as setup fodder, since all it can do is use Volt Switch.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Acid Spray lets Bellibolt threaten decent chip damage on walls, and it can help partners as well thanks to Bellibolt's Volt Switch. However, it doesn't let Bellibolt rack up chip damage on Ground-types like Toxic does. Parabolic Charge or Discharge can be used, but Bellibolt prefers the pivoting that Volt Switch offers. Bellibolt can run other moves in its last moveslot to aid itself and its team like Reflect, Light Screen, and Thunder Wave, but this leaves it walled by Gligar. Tera Water boosts Muddy Water and Chilling Water, but more importantly, it removes Bellibolt's Ground weakness while giving it Water and Fire resistances, aiding Bellibolt versus Paldean Tauros-W and Infernape. However, these resistances aren't as useful as the ones provided by Tera Fairy or Flying. Tera Poison lets Bellibolt become immune to poison and resist Fighting-types like Heracross and Flamigo. It maintains Bellibolt's Ground weakness, though. Leftovers can be used on Bellibolt for extra recovery, but the punishment of Rocky Helmet and the security of Heavy-Duty Boots are usually preferred.

Checks and Counters

Electric-immune Pokemon: Flygon, Gastrodon, Gligar, and Volt Absorb Kilowattrel pose a threat to Bellibolt, as they block its Volt Switch from working, forcing it to switch out manually, give these foes a free turn, and allow them to boost their stats, set up entry hazards, or capitalize on Bellibolt's manual switch and pivot with U-turn, consequently allowing them to gain more momentum. However, Toxic is annoying for Flygon, Gastrodon, and Kilowattrel to deal with long-term, and Gligar is often overwhelmed by having to repeatedly take Muddy Water on top of hazard chip damage.

Wallbreakers and Setup Sweepers: Bellibolt's lack of resistances leaves it open to being overwhelmed by common wallbreakers, including physical attackers like Choice Band Paldean Tauros-W and Guts Heracross. Additionally, setup sweepers like Flygon, Substitute Raikou, Toxicroak, Munkidori, and Toxtricity can easily take advantage of Bellibolt, the first of which does that by threatening an Earthquake, whereas the other four simply aren't affected by Toxic and can comfortably take a Volt Switch.

Defensive.description:
Set Details

Bellibolt's last moveslot is very flexible due to Volt Switch already getting Bellibolt out of bad matchups such as those versus Toxtricity and Toxic punishing Ground-types that want to switch in on it like Gastrodon. This leaves its only significant adversary to be Gligar, which can't be poisoned due to Immunity. For this reason, Bellibolt often goes with Muddy Water to deal good damage to it and fish for accuracy drops against foes. On the other hand, when Soak is used against an incoming Ground-type, it allows Bellibolt to keep up momentum and immediately pivot with Volt Switch. Additionally, it allows Bellibolt to use Toxic against Steel- and Poison-types like Bronzong, Copperajah, and Amoonguss, helping its team out. Chilling Water offers a way to stave off bulky setup sweepers like Bulk Up users such as Scrafty and Poison Heal Breloom. The choice between Rocky Helmet and Heavy-Duty Boots usually comes down to if Bellibolt's team has entry hazard removal: if it does, Rocky Helmet is preferred due to how it lets Bellibolt punish U-turn, Flamigo, and other physical attackers with chip damage, but if there is no removal, Heavy-Duty Boots ensures Bellibolt stays healthy even in the face of hazards. Static complements Rocky Helmet's contact-punishing effects especially well, but its also just Bellibolt's best ability with how it threatens paralysis on all foes that use a contact move. Tera Fairy offers Bellibolt a Fighting resistance, which lets it more easily take a Close Combat from Flamigo, Heracross, and Paldean Tauros-F, and it offers a solid defensive typing that eases its matchup against Flygon and Scrafty. Tera Flying grants Bellibolt a Fighting resistance and a Ground immunity, meaning it can handle a Close Combat when needed from the aforementioned Fighting-types and avoid an Earthquake from Flygon. However, this leaves it open to Stealth Rock chip damage if it lacks Heavy-Duty Boots.

One of Bellibolt's biggest issues is with Ground-types like Gastrodon, Flygon, and Gligar, as they block its Volt Switch. This leads to teammates like Decidueye, Alolan Ninetales, and Vaporeon pairing well alongside it. Additionally, thanks to Bellibolt constantly drawing in Ground-types and being able to accumulate chip damage with Toxic, Pokemon that can struggle with breaking past them such as Paldean Tauros-F, Toxicroak, and Diancie enjoy Bellibolt's presence. Entry hazard removers like Tsareena, Altaria, and Avalugg help out non-Heavy-Duty Boots Bellibolt sets, which can be easily overwhelmed by hazards. In a similar fashion, physical wallbreakers like Flamigo, Heracross, and Paldean Tauros-F can blow through Bellibolt with their strong neutral attacks, leading to secondary physical walls like Galarian Slowbro, Sylveon, and the aforementioned Altaria being welcomed as partners. Bellibolt's slow Volt Switch can facilitate the entry of many wallbreakers, and since it commonly draws in Decidueye, Amoonguss, and Duraludon, teammates such as Swords Dance Incineroar, Calm Mind or Choice Specs Chandelure, and Choice Band Flygon synergize well, capatilizing on these switch-ins. A complementary special wall like Wo-Chien, Swampert, or Goodra pairs well with Bellibolt, as it can handle special wallbreakers like Basculegion-M, Toxtricity, and Chandelure for it, while Bellibolt can take on physical ones such as Cinccino, Flamigo, and Paldean Tauros-F.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
With Paradox Pokemon being introduced, Series 2 is bringing big changes to Battle Stadium Singles! This is a modified Series 1 analysis that takes Paradox Pokemon into account. We will update this overview and analysis again once the metagame settles more. For more information on Series 2, check out the resource thread.

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Tactical Bellibolt.description:
• Bellibolt can be quite unassuming, and specially offensive Pokemon such as Hydreigon and Rotom may see it as a free opportunity to get into position. Assault Vest turns the tides against them with Electromorphosis + Parabolic Charge, which makes Bellibolt seem impossible to remove for certain Pokemon. It's also a decent check against Iron Bundle.

  • Grass- or Fairy-type Tera Blast: Tera Blast is important coverage to have; with a Fairy Tera type, Bellibolt reliably checks non-Tera Steel Dragon-types.

  • Muddy Water versus Chilling Water: Muddy Water should be used with Tera Electric for much-needed coverage. Alternatively, Chilling Water weakens common switch-ins such as Garchomp and Baxcalibur, allowing you to reposition your team more safely.

  • Acid Spray: This threatens non-Steel type switch-ins, and it also lets Bellibolt effectively use Electromorphosis without having to take damage first. It's also a powerful tool against Unaware walls such as Skeledirge.

  • Sucker Punch: While weak, Sucker Punch snipes Pokemon that activate Focus Sash and/or deals chip damage when Bellibolt is guaranteed to go down.

Tera Types

  • Fairy-type: Tera Fairy Bellibolt offensively checks big threats like Roaring Moon and Dragapult by walling their non-Terastal sets and nabbing surprise KOs.

  • Grass-type: Tera Grass Bellibolt can stay in versus common Pokemon such as Hippowdon and Breloom, sponge their attacks, and either chunk them or survive and reposition.

  • Electric-type: Maximizing Parabolic Charge damage is a viable option.

EV Spreads

  • 228 HP / 28 Def / 180 SpA / 44 SpD / 28 Spe: This spread is to avoid the 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Rotom-W and Hydreigon's Hydro Pump and Draco Meteor. 28 Speed EVs allow Bellibolt to outspeed 4 Speed EV Hippowdon. 28 Defense EVs are enough to survive Focus Sash Garchomp's Earthquake, which notably becomes a 3HKO if Bellibolt Terastallizes into a typing without a weakness to Ground.

  • 228 HP / 156 SpA / 124 SpD: This EV spread avoids a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Iron Bundle's Hydro Pump. This spread can also use a Quiet nature and 0 Speed EVs for the slowest possible Volt Switch.

  • 228 HP / 52 Def / 180 SpA / 44 SpD / 4 Spe: This spread sacrifices outspeeding Hippowdon for surviving a +1 or Choice Band Dragonite Earthquake.

Fat Bellibolt.description:
• Bellibolt's stats allow it to be deceptively bulky, and a pure Electric typing is not terrible on a defensive Pokemon with reliable recovery and pivoting.

  • Parabolic Charge: Parabolic Charge gives Bellibolt a more constant stream of recovery, though it is much less punishing than Discharge.

  • Volt Switch: Volt Switch maintains initiative when predicting switches after bringing Bellibolt in on something that it walls, such as defensive Gholdengo or Corviknight.

  • Chilling Water: Chilling Water punishes Garchomp and Hippowdon on the switch.

  • Thunder Wave: This disrupts opponents if Bellibolt doesn't have Discharge.

  • Fairy-type Tera Blast: Tera Blast hits common Dragon-types such as Garchomp and Baxcalibur after Terastallizing into the Fairy typing.

  • Soak: Soak catches Electric-resistant foes on the switch and forces them to either switch out or Terastallize early, with major targets including Garchomp and Baxcalibur.

Tera Types

  • Grass: Terastallizing into the Grass typing flips the matchup against Ground-types like Hippowdon and Garchomp on its head, turning their super effective attacks into resisted hits that still activate Electromorphosis. Tera Grass Bellibolt also absorbs Spore versus Breloom and Amoonguss, effectively walling them as well.

  • Fairy: Fairy Tera Bellibolt comfortably walls Dragon-types, removing a lot of their offensive pressure.

  • Water: Water is just generally good to have as a defensive Tera type. It also gives Bellibolt STAB on Chilling Water for slightly more damage.

EV Spreads

  • 228 HP / 244 Def / 4 SpA / 4 SpD / 28 Spe: This EV spread allows Bellibolt to survive two Glaive Rushes from Adamant Baxcalibur if it is not in a position to Terastallize. The physical bulk lets Bellibolt always survive Life Orb Garchomp's Earthquake, and after Terastallization into a neutral type, it becomes a 3HKO. 28 Speed EVs allow it to outspeed 4 Speed EV Hippowdon.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers provides long-term passive recovery alongside Slack Off, which can make Bellibolt very difficult to remove. Leftovers also removes any chance of a 2HKO from powerful physical threats such as Baxcalibur.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry is a good backup option if Leftovers is already in use.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet Bellibolt can switch into and passively punish physical attackers; the chip damage can also break Focus Sash and weaken foes into range of Electromorphosis-boosted attacks.

Bespectacled Bellibolt.description:
• With such good natural bulk, Bellibolt can easily survive hits from common threats and nab surprise KOs in return with a cheeky Choice Specs set.

  • Discharge / Thunderbolt: Discharge or Thunderbolt is the preferred primary STAB move, as either one takes advantage of Choice Specs more than Parabolic Charge. With an Electromorphosis boost, Bellibolt can 2HKO common switch-ins without having to Terastallize, like Dragapult.

  • Fairy Tera Blast: Tera Blast is important for coverage; with a Fairy typing, Bellibolt reliably checks non-Tera Steel Dragon-types. Muddy Water should be used with Tera Electric.

  • Muddy Water versus Parabolic Charge: Muddy Water lets Bellibolt win one-on-one against Hippowdon. Parabolic Charge should be used alongside Muddy Water if running Tera Electric.

Tera Types

  • Fairy-type: Tera Fairy lets Bellibolt turn the tables on bulky Dragon-types such as Baxcalibur and Roaring Moon by scoring a surprise KO on a potential setup attempt.

  • Grass-type: Tera Grass turns Bellibolt's only weakness into a resistance, and Tera Blast gets surprise OHKOs on threats such as physically defensive Hippowdon.

  • Electric-type: Tera Electric + Choice Specs turns Bellibolt into an offensive behemoth, and with an Electromorphosis boost it can OHKO resistant Pokemon like Dragapult, Hydreigon, and specially defensive Garganacl.

EV Spreads

  • 228 HP / 28 Def / 196 SpA / 28 SpD / 28 Spe: This EV spread allows Bellibolt to survive Choice Specs-boosted Draco Meteor from Hydreigon and Earthquake from Focus Sash Garchomp; Garchomp's Earthquake becomes a 3HKO if Bellibolt Terastallizes into a typing without a weakness to Ground. The Speed EVs outspeed 4 Speed EV Hippowdon, while the Special Attack EVs are enough to OHKO physically defensive Hippowdon with Muddy Water.

ru.overview: Kilowattrel swoops into RU as a niche option that has great Speed and good power, which when combined with its great typing allow it to take on Ground-, Water-, and Grass-types such as Krookodile, Slowbro, and Chesnaught. Kilowattrel is one of the fastest Pokemon in the tier, only being outsped by Barraskewda, and it can use its blistering Speed stat in order to pivot in and out of battle via Volt Switch or U-turn. Kilowattrel's STAB moves are also incredibly valuable, as they can hit Pokemon such as Chesnaught and Slowbro for super effective damage. However, Kilowattrel struggles against Ground-types like Gastrodon and Rhyperior. It also struggles with faster common Choice Scarf users such as Terrakion and Gardevoir, which can Trace Volt Absorb to block Volt Switch attempts as well. Kilowattrel can be incredibly frail even against resisted attacks such as Flamigo's Close Combat, and its power is lacking against bulky Pokemon such as Umbreon and Hisuian Goodra. Kilowattrel is also incredibly susceptible to Knock Off, which makes it take Stealth Rock damage, forcing it to use Roost more often, which means that it would not use Volt Switch as often as it would like to.
ru.comments:
Other Options

Endeavor lets Kilowattrel take foes down to low health alongside it in order to help teammates clean up easier that they might otherwise struggle with. Thunder Wave can be used to help slow down foes and cripple switch-ins such as Cyclizar. Air slash is a more reliable Flying-type STAB option on Kilowattrel, but it is much weaker and usually not worth it, as it doesn't reliably 2HKO Krookodile. Choice Specs can be used to make up for Kilowattrel's only okay damage output, but being affected by Stealth Rock heavily decreases its longevity.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Ground-types: Bulky Ground-types such as Gastrodon, and especially Rhyperior can wall Kilowattrel pretty easily, as they can block its Volt Switch while not minding Hurricane from it. They can threaten it back with Ice Beam or Stone Edge, or set up entry hazards against it.

Electric-types: Electric-types such as Magnezone, Raikou, and Bellibolt can easily take Kilowattrel's STAB options and hit it back for decent damage. While it can switch into their Electric-type moves, it has to immediately switch out, as they can threaten it with other moves such as Flash Cannon, Scald, and Toxic, respectively.

Faster Wallbreakers and Priority: Choice Scarf users such as Gardevoir and Terrakion heavily threaten Kilowattrel, as they can outspeed it and hit it for large damage. Additionally, faster wallbreakers and priority users such as Barraskewda and Bisharp can outspeed Kilowattrel and threaten it for large damage.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Set Details

Thunder can be used on Kilowattrel on rain teams to allow it to hit even harder. Volt Switch allows Kilowattrel to not only do solid damage but also pivot out against common switch-ins like Cyclizar and Hisuian Goodra. U-turn allows Kilowattrel to pivot out while not being blocked by Ground-types, which works especially well with Spikes support. Weather Ball can also be used on rain teams to allow Kilowattrel to hit the Ground-types that usually wall it such as Rhyperior. Roost allows Kilowattrel to heal off chip damage it sustains over the course of a battle. Volt Absorb allows Kilowattrel to switch into other Electric-types such as Magnezone and Raikou and heal itself from them, while Competitive allows it to punish Defog from Talonflame and Noivern while also benefitting from Intimidate from foes like Krookodile, allowing it to 2HKO Pokemon such as Gastrodon and Raikou that it would otherwise struggle with. Tera Flying allows Hurricane to 2HKO Cyclizar, while Tera Water allows Kilowattrel to take Ice-type attacks from Pokemon such as Cetitan and boosts the power of Weather Ball in rain.

Kilowattrel fits best on offense and bulky offense, able to leverage its good typing and Speed in order to pivot in and out of battles and take on Pokemon such as Krookodile and Yanmega. U-turn users such as Flamigo and Jirachi can form VoltTurn cores with Kilowattrel to chip defensive cores. Jirachi can also set Stealth Rock and paralyze foes with Body Slam to allow Kilowattrel to sweep easier. Entry hazard setters such as Krookodile and Chesnaught can pair very well with Kilowattrel, as not only can it make use of entry hazard chip damage to break through its checks easier, such as 2HKOing Cyclizar with Stealth Rock and a layer of Spikes, but with Competitive, it can also punish Defog from Pokemon such as Talonflame and Noivern. Entei pairs well with Kilowattrel, as it can lure in and burn Rhyperior with Sacred Fire and check Grass-types. In return, Kilowattrel can punish bulky Water-types such as Slowbro and Empoleon. Rain partners such as Politoed and Barraskewda pair well with Kilowattrel, as Politoed allows it to boost its Thunder and Weather Ball, while Barraskewda forms a nice VoltTurn core with it to pressure defensive switch-ins.

nu.overview: Kilowattrel's high Speed, great STAB combination, and access to two great abilities make it a great pivot that can benefit many teams. Volt Absorb makes it a decent soft check to opposing Electric-types like Bellibolt, Raikou, and Toxtricity, and with Tera Steel it can full-on wall these foes; additionally, with how common stat-dropping moves and abilities are in NU, Kilowattrel's Competitive is quite useful, allowing it to capitalize on Brambleghast's Strength Sap and both Paldean Tauros-W's and Incineroar's Intimidate. On top of that, Kilowattrel being able to fire off a powerful Volt Switch or an unblockable U-turn helps it keep up pressure and momentum, and this aids Kilowattrel with wearing down checks like Diancie, Copperajah, and Bronzong. Kilowattrel's counters aren't that common; however, whenever Kilowattrel comes across one like Bellibolt, it struggles to deal with them and is forced to pivot, giving away free turns. Kilowattrel's low bulk also can be detrimental, as any neutral hit can easily 2HKO it, such as Jolly Barraskewda's Liquidation or Loaded Dice Flygon's Scale Shot. Even Pokemon Kilowattrel would normally take out can beat Kilowattrel one-on-one if they have access to priority moves, like Sucker Punch Toxicroak and Aqua Jet Basculegion-M, due to its disappointing bulk.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Kilowattrel can opt for a Choice Specs set to more easily wallbreak, but its weakness to Stealth Rock combined with how much it loves to pivot leads to it usually being worn down too quickly. Alternatively, Life Orb can by used on more offensive teamstyles that can both keep up enough pressure to prevent Stealth Rock from being set up and take advantage of the extra boost it gives Kilowattrel. Kilowattrel can run Weather Ball on rain and snow teams to hit Ground-types like Swampert, Gligar, and Flygon harder than Air Slash can, and notably, Weather Ball on snow teams lets Hurricane Kilowattrel easily dispatch Wind Rider Brambleghast. Thunder is also great for more power on rain teams, taking advantage of the weather. Tera Blast Fairy can even be used, as it lets Kilowattrel hit Flygon super effectively while blanking its Outrage and Scale Shot. On top of that, it lets Kilowattrel maintain its Fighting resistance and gives it a solid defensive typing. Tera Blast Ground is another option that lets Kilowattrel dispatch Diancie, Bellibolt, and Copperajah, since they can be annoying for Kilowattrel to get past at times. Tera Ghost can be used to avoid a powerful Close Combat from Choice Scarf Infernape, Heracross, and Paldean Tauros-W; however, the defensive utility that Tera Steel or Fairy gives Kilowattrel is usually preferred.

Checks and Counters

Electric-types: Bellibolt, Raikou, and Volt Absorb Kilowattrel all can switch into Kilowattrel, wall it repeatedly, and capitalize on their free turn by gaining momentum or, in Raikou's case, setting up.

Steel-types: Copperajah and Bronzong easily switch in to Kilowattrel's Air Slash and Hurricane. Since Kilowattrel has to pivot or switch out after they switch in, they can take advantage of their free turn by setting entry hazards or boosting their stats.

Faster Pokemon and Priority Users: Kilowattrel's frailty leaves it open to being quite easily revenge killed by even neutral hit from Choice Scarf users like Munkidori's Sludge Wave and Inteleon's Hydro Pump. Additionally, priority users like Toxicroak and Mystic Water Basculegion-M can heavily threaten Kilowattrel, since the former can OHKO it at +2 with a Tera Dark-boosted Sucker Punch, and the latter can 2HKO it with Aqua Jet.

Rock-types: Diancie can tank Kilowattrel's attacks quite well, and it can use it as an opportunity to set up Trick Room or set its entry hazards up. Rhyperior stonewalls Kilowattrel and forces it out, leaving Rhyperior free to use Swords Dance, Stealth Rock, or simply firing off a powerful attack on that turn.

Offensive Pivot.description:
Set Details

Air Slash is preferred, as it is more accurate and can hit Wind Rider Brambleghast, but Hurricane can be used on teams that can handle it through other means. U-turn helps it keep up momentum in the face of Ground-types like Gligar, Flygon, and Swampert; however, Volt Switch lets Kilowattrel take advantage of Competitive's Special Attack boosts better. Roost allows Kilowattrel to continually pivot and gain value from its Competitive. Heavy-Duty Boots is preferred to let Kilowattrel come in safely and repeatedly during a match. Volt Absorb can be run to take advantage of Raikou, Bellibolt, and opposing Competitive Kilowattrel. On the other hand, Competitive allows Kilowattrel to capitalize on common Pokemon's abilities and moves like both Overqwil's and Incineroar's Intimidate as well as Brambleghast's Strength Sap. 160 HP EVs allows Kilowattrel to reliably revenge kill all Flamigo, surviving two Close Combats or Brave Birds from its Choice Scarf set so that it can retaliate with a Thunderbolt. Alternatively, an EV spread of 92 Def / 164 SpA / 252 Spe could be used to achieve the same goal at the cost of lower bulk but better offensive presence. Tera Steel allows Kilowattrel to resist many common attacks like Cinccino's Tail Slap, Inteleon's Ice Beam, and Munkidori's Sludge Wave and Psychic.

Entry hazard setters like Klefki, Flygon, Copperajah, and Gligar are great partners for Kilowattrel, as their hazards can punish the opponent's switches, while Kilowattrel helps keep the hazards up by pressuring stray Defoggers like Cramorant, Scyther, and Decidueye. Similarly, Kilowattrel can work with hyper offense leads like Cinccino, Lycanroc, and Froslass. While Kilowattrel can pressure Defoggers, it fails to stop spinners like Brambleghast, Avalugg, and Tsareena, so pairing it with a Ghost-type like Basculegion-M, Decidueye, or Chandelure is a good idea. Kilowattrel can pressure Water-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Basculegion-M quite easily, meaning Pokemon that struggle dealing with them or can force them in like Flygon, Incineroar, and Inteleon have good synergy. Special walls like Diancie, Copperajah, and Bronzong can be difficult to take down alone, so physical wallbreakers like Breloom, Flygon, and Incineroar are great to deal with them, and Kilowattrel can form VoltTurn cores with many of them. Electric- and Rock-types like Bellibolt, Volt Absorb Kilowattrel, and Diancie are difficult for Kilowattrel to KO; because of this, Ground-type teammates like Flygon, Rhyperior, and Gligar make for good partners.

Choice Specs (Flying).description:
Kilowattrel is an essential component to Flying teams, providing an Electric immunity, pivot support, an excellent Speed tier that allows it to outspeed Choice Specs Greninja and Iron Valiant, and a range of hard-hitting attacks. With rain support, Thunder can be used as Kilowattrel's hard-hitting STAB attack to hit Pokemon—such as Toxapex—that Flying teams can struggle to take down. Thunderbolt is a fine substitute on Flying teams that do not utilize rain. Volt Switch allows Kilowattrel to pivot, making use of Kilowattrel's high Speed tier to get off damage while not being Choice locked. Hurricane couples with the preceding moves to cover Kilowattrel's STAB combination, specifically hitting Ground-types such as Quagsire and Gastrodon. The last slot depends on whether rain is being taken advantage of: on rain teams, Weather Ball can be used to hit Ground-types such as Unaware Clodsire, while Air Slash is another option for non-rain teams that can make up for Hurricane's lower accuracy. Choice Specs allows Kilowattrel to hit extremely hard, letting it OHKO Pokemon such as Azumarill with Volt Switch and Amoonguss with Hurricane. Volt Absorb provides the only Electric immunity for Flying-type teams.

Corviknight is one of Kilowattrel's greatest assets; beyond providing a neutral switch-in to Ice-type attacks—especially in the cases of Chien-Pao and Choice Scarf Greninja—Corviknight provides a physical wall that Kilowattrel can pivot into. It is also Flying's most common Defogger, which is essential, as Kilowattrel is susceptible to Stealth Rock damage, hindering its pivoting. Pelipper is very useful in supporting Kilowattrel, as rain support ensures accuracy of Kilowattrel's Thunder and Hurricane, and U-turn on Pelipper ensures safe pivoting. Talonflame is another defensive supporter, covering Kilowattrel's weakness to Ice-types and offering another Defogger. Dragonite hits the specially defensive walls that Kilowattrel struggles with such as Clodsire and Blissey. Gyarados finds great support from Kilowattrel; as Kilowattrel punches holes in defensive Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Toxapex, Gyarados will have a better chance to sweep late-game. While Kilowattrel has excellent Speed itself, Choice Scarf users such as Flamigo and Salamence can revenge kill Pokemon such as Dragapult and Flutter Mane that outspeed Kilowattrel. Bombirdier offers Stealth Rock support and uses Knock Off to remove key items such as Leftovers on Gastrodon, which puts it into 2HKO range of Hurricane after Stealth Rock damage.

Unburden Sweeper.description:
Shroodle functions as a potent setup sweeper on hyper offense teams, using Grassy Terrain to outspeed the entire metagame thanks to Unburden. Grassy Seed triggers Unburden while providing a much-needed Defense boost, which aids Shroodle in setting up. Swords Dance allows Shroodle to reach threatening levels of Attack, which help it secure OHKOs on metagame staples like Mienfoo, Vullaby, Foongus, and Toedscool. Gunk Shot threatens heavy damage on most foes at the risk of lower accuracy, while Knock Off removes Eviolite from walls like Mareanie. Alternatively, Double-Edge is an accurate STAB move that allows Shroodle to hit Mudbray and Mareanie for huge damage without burning its own Terastallization at the cost of recoil damage. Acrobatics pairs well with Grassy Seed, gaining a power boost after Shroodle consumes Grassy Seed and allowing it to pressure key threats like Mienfoo and Foongus. Tera Flying provides Shroodle with an immunity to Ground-type attacks from Mudbray and Alolan Diglett, making it easier for it to set up and boosting Acrobatics for late-game cleaning. On the other hand, Tera Ground with Tera Blast lets Shroodle muscle past Steel- and Rock-types such as Tinkatink and Glimmet that resist its STAB moves.

Shroodle is best supported by teammates that help it activate Unburden and cover its defensive gaps. Grookey is mandatory to set Grassy Terrain to activate Grassy Seed, weaken the power of Earthquake, offer valuable passive recovery, and act as a pivot. Shroodle appreciates Mienfoo's ability to pressure bulky Ground-types such as Mudbray. In return, Shroodle threatens foes like Foongus, Mareanie, and opposing Mienfoo that hinder Mienfoo's sweep. Shroodle can also be paired with another Unburden sweeper in Drifloon that forms a Grassy Terrain core along with Grookey. Other offensive partners like Alolan Diglett can help handle foes that trouble Shroodle, such as Tinkatink and Glimmet, while also punishing defensive Terastallization attempts, such as Tera Steel on Mienfoo that Shroodle can bait out.

nu.overview: Brambleghast is a premier Rapid Spin user in NU thanks to its high-Base Power STAB moves, typing that lets it beat common entry hazard setters like Swampert, Rhyperior, and Bronzong one-on-one, and solid Speed. Brambleghast's useful Wind Rider ability lets it block a possible Hurricane from Kilowattrel and Tornadus. Additionally, Brambleghast is a great wallbreaker, since not many Pokemon can take both of its STAB attacks. Choice Band makes Brambleghast into a dangerous threat, as defensive foes like Amoonguss and Tsareena get 2HKOed by Poltergeist on the switch. However, Brambleghast's poor bulk makes it poor at checking wallbreakers like Heracross, Flygon, and Paldean Tauros-W, as they can threaten it with a 2HKO from their coverage or Choice Band-boosted attacks, forcing Brambleghast to constantly use Strength Sap. Additionally, Brambleghast's typing leaves it weak to common Dark- and Fire-types like Incineroar and Chandelure. While Brambleghast does have good Speed, it's still outsped and revenge killed by foes like Inteleon and Munkidori or by priority attacks like Sucker Punch Toxicroak and Shadow Sneak Decidueye.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Infiltrator lets Brambleghast target Substitute users like Basculegion-M, Flygon, and Paldean Tauros-W and -F. Brambleghast can go itemless, reducing the power of Knock Off from Tsareena and walling opposing Brambleghast. A set with Spikes / Poltergeist / Rapid Spin / Curse and a Focus Sash turns Brambleghast into a solid lead hazard setter, as it can set up Spikes and punish foes like Incineroar with Curse damage. Tera Water gives it a useful resistance against Fire-type attacks, but it makes Brambleghast weak to other Grass-types like Tsareena.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Incineroar and Bombirdier resist both of Brambleghast's STAB attacks and can destroy it with their own STAB attacks.

Fire-types: Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion destroy Brambleghast with their STAB attacks. Hisuian Typhlosion can outspeed Brambleghast, while Chandelure requires a Choice Scarf to outspeed it, but they are wary of switching into its Poltergeist and can be picked off by Shadow Sneak. Infernape outspeeds Brambleghast, and it can threaten it back with a KO from its Flare Blitz. However, Infernape doesn't enjoy directly switching into Poltergeist.

Physical Walls: Amoonguss and Avalugg can tank Brambleghast's attacks and both of them having recovery makes it a lot more difficult for Brambleghast to break through them. However, Amoonguss can't directly switch into Choice Band Brambleghast, as it gets 2HKOed. Other physical walls like Dragalge, Galarian Slowbro, and bulky Tsareena can tank Choice Banded Brambleghast's attacks and threaten it back with their own attacks, but they have to predict correctly or they take significant damage.

Revenge Killers: Faster foes like Inteleon, Munkidori, and Air Slash Kilowattrel can threaten Brambleghast with their attacks due to its poor bulk or use it for momentum, but they don't enjoy switching into Brambleghast's STAB attacks. Priority users like First Impression Flygon and Sucker Punch Toxicroak can easily revenge kill Brambleghast after it's been weakened.

Offensive Utility.description:
Set Details

Strength Sap lets Brambleghast check physical wallbreakers like Flygon, Paldean Tauros-W, and Breloom. However, Spikes can be used instead, letting Brambleghast become a solid entry hazard setter. Alternatively, Shadow Sneak lets it revenge kill weakened foes like Flygon, Munkidori, and Infernape. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Brambleghast ignore entry hazards, meaning it can more reliably remove them, while Colbur Berry lets it tank Dark-type attacks such as Infernape's Knock Off and Toxicroak's Sucker Punch, letting Brambleghast use Strength Sap on them or hit them back with its STAB attacks. Brambleghast can run a defensive set with an EV spread of 252 HP / 80 Def / 176 Spe and a Jolly nature on utility sets, as it lets Brambleghast better handle physical wallbreakers like Paldean Tauros-W, Flygon, and Breloom while letting it outspeed base 80 Speed Pokemon like Chandelure. Tera Fairy provides a Dark resistance while not throwing away its matchup into Fighting-types and Flygon. Alternatively, Tera Ghost gives both Poltergeist and Shadow Sneak a power boost, letting it 2HKO foes like Amoonguss, Dragalge, and Copperajah with the former.

Fighting-types like Infernape, Toxicroak, and Heracross are great partners for Brambleghast, as they can check Dark-types like Incineroar, Scrafty, and Wo-Chien; in return, Brambleghast pressures Ghost- and bulky Psychic-types like Chandelure, Uxie, and Galarian Slowbro. Incineroar is an exceptionally great partner for Brambleghast due to how it beats Grass-, Steel-, and Dark-types for Brambleghast, and in return, Brambleghast can check Fighting-, Ground-, and Water-types for Incineroar. Fire-types like Choice Scarf Chandelure and Infernape outspeed Brambleghast and destroy it with their STAB attacks. Thus, it best pairs with bulky Water-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Tentacruel to check the aforementioned Fire-types. Faster Pokemon like Flygon, Infernape, and Kilowattrel can easily revenge kill Brambleghast, so it synergizes well with defensive tanks like Sylveon, Galarian Slowbro, and Duraludon that check them. Brambleghast appreciates special wallbreakers like Munkidori, Inteleon, and Kilowattrel for handling physical walls like Vileplume and Avalugg. Brambleghast can spinblock for hazard setters like Bronzong, Klefki, and Swampert. Stealth Rock-weak Pokemon like Chandelure, Hisuian Typhlosion, and Staraptor that won't have Heavy-Duty Boots appreciate Brambleghast for its hazard removal.

Choice Band.description:
Set Details

Choice Band allows Brambleghast to 2HKO Amoonguss with Poltergeist and OHKO Vaporeon with Power Whip. Shadow Sneak lets Brambleghast pick off weakened foes like Flygon and Breloom. Rapid Spin allows Brambleghast to still have utility against foes like Incineroar.

Ground-types like Flygon, Gligar, and Swampert appreciate Brambleghast for checking Water-types like Vaporeon, Milotic, and Paldean Tauros-W; in return, they can handle Fire-types like Incineroar and Chandelure. Brambleghast appreciates Fighting-types like Toxicroak and Heracross for checking Dark-types like Incineroar and Overqwil. Physical walls like Amoonguss, Avalugg, and Tera Fairy Galarian Slowbro can tank many of Brambleghast's attacks very well, so it best synergize with special wallbreakers like Kilowattrel, Munkidori, and Chandelure to handle the physical walls. Brambleghast partners well with Pokemon like Munkidori, Meloetta, and Incineroar, as they can overwhelm shared checks like opposing Incineroar.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Grass

Spell Tag is an alternative over Heavy-Duty Boots, as it allows Adamant Brambleghast to OHKO Flutter Mane with Shadow Sneak.

Entry Hazard Control (Ghost).description:
Brambleghast's unique attributes allow it to act not only as an entry hazard setter but as a hazard remover as well. Spikes helps offensive teams deal extra chip damage to Pokemon that would otherwise stifle progress, such as Ting-Lu and Alolan Muk. Rapid Spin removes opposing hazards, helping preserve offensive teammates as well as keeping Ceruledge's Focus Sash intact. Rapid Spin also allows teammates to forgo Heavy-Duty Boots in favor of different items. Power Whip is a great way of making sure Brambleghast is not completely passive, allowing it to hit foes like Swampert, Glimmora, and Primarina for solid damage. Strength Sap not only allows Brambleghast to recover HP, but it also weakens physically oriented foes that fail to OHKO it, such as Great Tusk, Barraskewda, and Hisuian Samurott. Additionally, Brambleghast outspeeds Adamant Azumarill and OHKOes with Power Whip. An offensive EV spread with an Adamant nature can be used to surprise opponents expecting defensive Brambleghast. In this case, Shadow Sneak is an option to OHKO Flutter Mane after Spikes damage. Infiltrator is preferred on offensive sets because it allows Brambleghast to ignore Reflect.

Offensive teammates greatly appreciate Brambleghast's Spikes damage helping them muscle through opposing teams. Choice Specs Flutter Mane thrives when its would-be switch-ins, notably Hisuian Goodra and Alolan Muk, are weakened by Spikes, turning 3HKOs into 2HKOs. Additionally, Flutter Mane is able to take out Dark- and Fire-type Pokemon, such as Mandibuzz, Greninja, and Ogerpon-H, via Moonblast and Power Gem. Spectrier is another Pokemon that thrives with entry hazard support, as it becomes increasingly difficult for opposing teams to switch into Shadow Ball as the Grim Neigh boosts begin to stack. Ceruledge pairs nicely with Brambleghast, as Rapid Spin ensures that Ceruledge's Focus Sash will be kept intact, and it can be used to the best of its ability. Ceruledge is also able to take out Steel-type Pokemon that Brambleghast is unable to deal with. Sinistcha is a great setup sweeper that can utilize Spikes support to steamroll through teams once it gets some Calm Mind boosts. Gholdengo also pairs nicely with Brambleghast, as not only is Gholdengo immune to Rapid Spin, but it also blocks Defog with Good as Gold, ensuring Spikes stays up. Choice Scarf Dragapult is able to deal with faster threats that would otherwise take care of Brambleghast, such as Meowscarada and Hoopa-U. Dragapult's set variety keeps the opponent guessing, which makes switches very punishing. Hisuian Zoroark is a great teammate, as it can freely disguise itself as Gholdengo and not have Stealth Rock damage give the illusion away. Skeledirge is a nice defensive teammate for Brambleghast, as it is able to deal with Steel-type Pokemon and setup sweepers that Brambleghast struggles with.

Spooky Spinner [Entry Hazard Support] (G.description:
Brambleghast finds a position on Grass teams thanks to its unique set of properties in access to Rapid Spin and Spikes, which, along with its part Ghost typing, allows it to set entry hazards reliably while spinblocking Pokemon such as Iron Treads and Great Tusk. Wind Rider allows Brambleghast to check Zapdos and Tornadus-T. Poltergeist lets Brambleghast threaten Ghost- and Psychic-types like Gholdengo, Sinistcha, and Hatterene. Shadow Sneak provides Brambleghast with a much needed from of priority, allowing it to pick off weakened targets such as Dragapult, Iron Boulder, and Latios. Strength Sap can be used over Spikes, as it allows Brambleghast to weaken physical threats like Iron Hands while providing a form of recovery. Adamant is preferred thanks to allowing Brambleghast to OKHO Flutter Mane after minimal chip damage and 2HKO Skarmory after an Attack boost from Hurricane and Stealth Rock damage. Jolly can be used, as it allows Brambleghast to outspeed and check Gholdengo with Poltergeist.

Choice Scarf Meowscarada is a crucial ally for Brambleghast due to it being able to threaten opposing Ghost- and Dark-types like Flutter Mane, Spectrier, and Greninja with Knock Off and Play Rough. Hisuian Lilligant and Breloom can take care of Dark- and Steel-types such as Alolan Muk, Bisharp, and Heatran. Both Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-C can be used to threaten Bug- and Ice-types such as Galvantula, Frosmoth, and Articuno; on top of that, Ogerpon-H also handles Steel-types such as Corviknight, Gholdengo, and Scizor, while Ogerpon-C deals with Flying- and Fire-type threats such as Enamorus and Volcarona. Amoonguss can support Brambleghast by threatening Fairy-types out such as Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Primarina with its Sludge Bomb along with being able to use Spore to give Brambleghast safe entry. Hydrapple provides a Fire neutrality and can use Earth Power to deal with Fire-types like Heatran and Volcanion. Sinistcha appreciates Brambleghast setting up Spikes, and in return, it can act as a second spinblocker that reliably checks threats such as Iron Hands and Skarmory.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Spikes can be used over Skitter Smack and Rapid Spin to take advantage of the switches that Brambleghast forces, helping to wear down the opposing team.

Checks and Counters

Bulky Dark- and Grass-resistant Pokemon: Bulky Pokemon that resist both of Brambleghast's STAB attacks such as Mandibuzz, Kingambit, and Roaring Moon are difficult to deal with, as they can switch in safely and threaten to OHKO Brambleghast due to its low bulk.

Faster Offensive Threats: Since Brambleghast is so frail, faster offensive Pokemon such as Cinderace, Latios, and Zamazenta can all OHKO it without fear.

Choice Band.description:
The combination of Choice Band and its powerful offensive typing makes Brambleghast a dangerous wallbreaker. Poltergeist threatens common defensive Pokemon such as Pecharunt, Corviknight, and Scream Tail, while Power Whip OHKOes non-Fluffy Great Tusk, Ting-Lu , and common Water-types such as Manaphy and Primarina. Skitter Smack is used to OHKO Roaring Moon variants , that can otherwise switch in, live one hit, (AC) and then force Brambleghast out. Rapid Spin allows Brambleghast to take advantage of the switches it forces to clear entry hazards. Rapid Spin is especially useful, (AC) as Ghost-types that could otherwise block Rapid Spin do not want to switch into Brambleghast. Shadow Sneak is used to revenge kill weakened, faster Pokemon such as Deoxys-S, Latios, Iron Crown, and Iron Moth. Sword of Ruin is the preferred ability because it allows Brambleghast to hit hard with both its STAB moves and coverage, while Adaptability can be used instead if a teammate is running Sword of Ruin. An Adamant nature is used to maximize its wallbreaking ability.

Due to Brambleghast's frailty, it often struggles to switch into even defensive Pokemon, making slow pivot move users such as U-turn Corviknight and RegenVest Primarina valuable teammates. Many special attackers such as Latios, Gholdengo, and Iron Crown pair well with Brambleghast, as it threatens most of the common specially defensive Pokemon in the tier. Physical attackers that rely on contact moves such as Slither Wing and Zamazenta also make good partners because Brambleghast's Poltergeist does not make contact, allowing it to beat walls such as Fluffy Corviknight and Great Tusk. Fast Pokemon such as Deoxys-S and Chien-Pao or priority users such as Kingambit can clean up teams after Brambleghast has weakened opposing walls.

Entry Hazard Support (Ghost).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Utility.description:
Toedscool is a capable utility option offering role compression, excellent entry hazard control, good coverage, solid Speed, and relevant immunities to both Electric-type attacks and Spore. At 17 Speed, Toedscool is the fastest Pokemon in the tier with access to Rapid Spin. Its Speed, coupled with Knock Off, allows it to consistently cripple switch-ins and make progress against a wide variety of team structures. Dazzling Gleam is a fantastic coverage option to punish common switch-ins like Vullaby and faster variants of pivot Mienfoo, both of which can otherwise take advantage of Toedscool’s usual coverage. Spikes is another way for Toedscool to make progress and typically replaces Giga Drain first but can replace Earth Power or Knock Off in rare instances. Toedscool's high Special Defense allows it to check special Electric-types like Elekid, comfortably taking on its special coverage while preventing it from freely whittling teams down with Volt Switch. The Speed investment lets Toedscool Speed tie with key 17 Speed threats like Mienfoo and Chinchou, while its Defense investment allows it to reliably check common physical hazard setters such as Mudbray by allowing it to live 2 Close Combats; it also allows Toedscool to live a U-turn from Mienfoo. Tera Water lets Toedscool flip common Ice- and Fire-type matchups, while Tera Fairy offers a more offensive option that enhances Dazzling Gleam and improves its resilience against Dark-types.

Toedscool fits best on teams that appreciate its utility and defensive profile. Mareanie benefits greatly from Toedscool's Electric-type immunity, Ground resistance, ability to remove entry hazards, and immunity to Spore. Flying-type Pokemon like Vullaby and Wingull also appreciate the Stealth Rock removal and Electric-type immunity. Other Stealth Rock-weak Pokemon, such as Hisuian Growlithe, similarly appreciate Toedscool's hazard removal and Ground resistance. Toedscool is much weaker to Mienfoo and Vullaby, especially when it lacks Dazzling Gleam. Choice Scarf Hisuian Growlithe can OHKO Toedscool with Flare Blitz. Additionally, Pokemon with surprise coverage options, such as Ice Punch Elekid and Ice Hammer Tinkatink, can OHKO Toedscool that attempt to make progress via Spikes, Rapid Spin, or Knock Off. Shellos walls Ice- and Fire-type attacks while preventing progress from Knock Off with its ability Sticky Hold. Shellos appreciates Toedscool's hazard removal to keep it healthy enough to reliably live attacks from both Mienfoo and Vullaby. Toedscool partners well with Mareanie, which also comfortably absorbs Ice- and Fire-type attacks and switches into Mienfoo. Tinkatink rounds out an excellent core with Mareanie and Toedscool, covering for Toedscool's weaknesses to Vullaby and Mienfoo, stacking hazards with Stealth Rock, and providing speed control with Thunder Wave. Toedscool switches into both Ground-type attacks and Spore for Tinkatink and Mareanie, using these moves to open opportunities to remove entry hazards for the core or make progess with Spikes and Knock Off. Glimmet is another notable partner that can absorb Toxic Spikes for Toedscool, set Stealth Rock, and handle Vullaby.

Entry Hazard Support (Grass).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

nu.overview: Scovillain is one of the sun archetype's strongest soldiers. In the sun, Chlorophyll makes Scovillain one of the fastest Pokemon in the metagame, outpacing prominent Choice Scarf users like Munkidori and Paldean Tauros-W. Its STAB, sun-boosted Fire-type attacks are almost impossible to switch in on, overpowering Fire-resistant Pokemon like Flygon and Rhyperior. Even sturdier special walls such as Incineroar and Goodra cannot take repeated hits from Scovillain, since they are significantly weakened in the process. This creates opportunities for fellow sun abusers like Venusaur and Brute Bonnet to clean up later in the game. However, Scovillain is a bit of a one-trick pony, entirely reliant on the sun to weaken Fire-resistant Pokemon like Goodra and outspeed Pokemon that threaten it like Infernape and Galarian Articuno. Furthermore, it is walled by Chansey, which can outheal its strongest attacks and threaten it back with Thunder Wave. It is also troubled by Flash Fire Chandelure, which stops it from spamming its Fire-type attacks. Scovillain requires a lot of support, demanding teammates that can set up the sun manually, apply consistent offensive pressure, deal with entry hazards, and find ways to get it in safely such as Memento.
nu.comments:
Other Options

While it typically runs Choice Specs to maximize its wallbreaking capabilities, there are other, very niche items such as Heavy-Duty Boots, Life Orb, and Charcoal that allow Scovillain to run Growth and become a scary setup sweeper. With these items, it can also run mixed sets with Stomping Tantrum to catch special walls like Goodra and Chansey as well as Fire-types like Incineroar and Chandelure.

Checks and Counters

Special Walls: Chansey comfortably tanks and outheals anything Scovillain can throw at it while threatening either paralysis or raw damage with Seismic Toss that outpaces Giga Drain's recovery. Goodra, Incineroar, and Altaria are able to take hits from Scovillain and threaten it back with strong attacks, though the former two lack reliable recovery and therefore get worn down by repeated hits.

Entry Hazards: Since it is grounded and weak to Stealth Rock, Scovillain's opportunities to enter the field are greatly limited by entry hazards. This is especially troublesome, since the sun teams it thrives on do not tend to have space for hazard removal.

Priority Moves: Because of its mediocre defensive stats, Scovillain can be easily revenge killed by priority moves once it is chipped. This includes First Impression from Flygon, Aqua Jet from Basculegion and Paldean Tauros-W, Sucker Punch from Brute Bonnet and Toxicroak, and Fake Out from Ambipom.

Sun Sweeper.description:
Set Details

Fire Blast can overwhelm most Pokemon in the tier with its sheer power. Overheat is Scovillain's single strongest attack in the sun at the cost of follow-up damage, securing the OHKO on Duraludon without Terastallizing and dealing massive amounts of damage to Goodra and Incineroar. Flamethrower is a safer option to reliably clean up teams once their special walls have been dealt with. Solar Beam OHKOes notable Fire-resistant Pokemon such as Vaporeon and Flygon. Giga Drain grants Scovillain some longevity and importantly provides it with a Grass-type move to click outside of the sun. A Timid nature ensures that, in the sun, Scovillain outspeeds Choice Scarf Munkidori, Speed Booster Energy Scream Tail, and Cinccino after a Tidy Up. Alternatively, a Modest nature maximizes raw damage output, enabling Scovillain to 2HKO Goodra and specially defensive Incineroar with Tera Fire-boosted Fire Blast.

Scovillain needs teammates that can set up the sun. Pokemon with the Prankster ability such as Klefki, Tornadus, Grafaiai, and Whimsicott, are particularly reliable in this role. Klefki also provides entry hazard support with Spikes, while the other three Pokemon have pivoting options in U-turn, Parting Shot, and Memento to help Scovillain enter the field safely. Uxie is another great sun setter, since it can both set up Stealth Rock and pivot with either U-turn or Memento. Offensive threats like Sylveon and Paldean Tauros-W can help lure bulky Steel- and Water-type Pokemon that Scovillain takes advantage of, like Copperajah and Vaporeon. Scovillain also has excellent synergy with fellow sun abusers like Venusaur and Chandelure, since they collectively overwhelm shared checks like Goodra, Incineroar, and Chansey. Brute Bonnet is another sun sweeper that directly takes on these checks while appreciating Scovillain's wallbreaking to finish off teams. Finally, since it is grounded and weak to Stealth Rock, Scovillain appreciates hazard control from the likes of Rapid Spin Brambleghast and Tidy Up Cinccino.

Sun Sweeper (Fire).description:
Scovillain is one of Fire's best sweepers thanks to Chlorophyll. Under sun, Scovillain outspeeds a multitude of threats such as non-Choice Scarf Greninja and Chien-Pao. Growth is run for Scovillain to boost its damage output while under sun, letting it secure KOs more easily. Giga Drain threatens Pokemon like Ting-Lu, allowing Scovillain's teammates to break through them late-game, and it also aids in improving Scovillain's longevity by recovering its HP. Fire Blast can be used to have a chance of 2HKOing Skeledirge and Clodsire under sun, but Flamethrower is the preferred Fire-type STAB move, since its accuracy is higher than Fire Blast's. Stomping Tantrum hits opposing Fire-types such as Iron Moth. Solar Beam is an alternative to Stomping Tantrum, OHKOing the aforementioned Ting-Lu and Toxapex after Growth in sun. Life Orb and 32 Attack EVs maximize Scovillain's power, letting it 2HKO specially defensive Clodsire with Stomping Tantrum after Stealth Rock damage. If opting for Solar Beam, the remaining EVs go into HP. A Naive nature allows Scovillain to outspeed Choice Scarf users like Great Tusk and Iron Moth under sun while not losing out on Stomping Tantrum damage.

Torkoal is a mandatory partner for Scovillain, as its ability to set up sun allows Scovillain to outspeed many faster threats like Iron Treads, Iron Jugulis, and Quaquaval, dealing heavy chip damage or outright KOing them. Scovillain appreciates Torkoal getting rid of entry hazards; in return, Scovillain deals with Water- and Ground-types like Gastrodon, Quagsire, and Sandy Shocks. Paldean Tauros-F is a great offensive partner for Scovillain, granting benefits such as breaking dual screens from Pokemon like Klefki and Grimmsnarl, which impede Scovillain's sweeping ability. Paldean Tauros-F is also able to check specially defensive walls like Blissey; in return, Scovillain breaks past bulky Water-types like Slowking and Toxapex after one Growth under sun. Cinderace can offer alternate entry hazard removal with Court Change, which helps Scovillain's longevity. Furthermore, Cinderace's Speed tier allows it to handle offensive Pokemon that naturally outpace Scovillain outside of sun like Hydreigon and Iron Treads, the former of which Scovillain cannot hit neutrally. Scovillain also appreciates Volcarona as an offensive partner thanks to its non-weather-reliant sweeping potential in Quiver Dance, dealing with Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Garchomp, while Scovillain can weaken Volcarona's checks like Ting-Lu, Unaware Clodsire, and Toxapex throughout the course of the game.

Choice Specs (Fire).description:
Scovillain turns up the heat on its Fire Blast with a Choice Specs set, burning up Clodsire and Skeledirge, which usually have no problem with its Growth set. It's notably also strong enough to score a 2HKO on physically defensive Toxapex after minimal chip damage, allowing Scovillain to beat Poison teams if it hits every move. Alternatively, Overheat has better accuracy and still 2HKOes Skeledirge and Clodsire, but the Special Attack drop makes it less spammable. Giga Drain threatens a 2HKO on Pelipper, which may be tempted to come into Scovillain to block Solar Beam, and also provides Scovillain a form of recovery. A Timid nature lets it outspeed threats such as Choice Scarf Gengar and Protosynthesis-boosted Choice Specs Walking Wake to burn them to a crisp, while a Modest nature has better odds of 2HKOing Toxapex with Giga Drain and OHKOing Baxcalibur with Flamethrower at the cost of outspeeding only up to non-Speed boosting Choice Scarf Sandy Shocks.

Torkoal is a mandatory teammate, as it sets sun, which Scovillain needs to boost its Speed with Chlorophyll, and provides entry hazard support with its ability to set Stealth Rock and remove entry hazards with Rapid Spin. Other forms of entry hazard support in Defog Talonflame and Court Change Cinderace are also appreciated; they also have access to U-turn, which allows Scovillain to get in more times to wallbreak. Ceruledge packs Shadow Sneak to deal with Flutter Mane, which otherwise outspeeds and dispatches Scovillain with ease. In return, Scovillain obliterates bulky Unaware walls like Quagsire, Dondozo, and Skeledirge, all of which hinder Swords Dance Ceruledge from cutting down Water and Ghost teams. Similarly, Volcarona and Iron Moth love Scovillain's ability to eliminate bulky walls like Clodsire and Ting-Lu, allowing them to clean up Poison and Ground teams late-game.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
With Paradox Pokemon being introduced, Series 2 is bringing big changes to Battle Stadium Singles! This is a modified Series 1 analysis that takes Paradox Pokemon into account. We will update this overview and analysis again once the metagame settles more. For more information on Series 2, check out the resource thread.

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Sun Attacker.description:
• Tera Fire Scovillain's damage under sun is absurd, managing to barely KO even Fire-resistant targets. Most notably, its ability to defeat most Pokemon, even powerful Dragon-types, without fearing surprise Terastallizations makes Scovillain a charming offensive option.

  • Overheat and Fire Blast: Overheat combined with Tera Fire and Choice Specs guarantees the KO on Garchomp without bulk EVs, and OHKO offensive Roaring Moon after Stealth Rock damage. Against the frailer Dragapult, Tera Fire and Fire Blast is enough to earn the KO. It's recommended to run both Fire STAB moves because Overheat's added damage can be necessary to guarantee certain KOs, but its stat drop can be fatal.

  • Solar Beam versus Leaf Storm: Solar Beam nails the few bulky Water-types that can survive Scovillain's absurd attacks, most notable examples being notably Gastrodon and Assault Vest Azumarill. However, Leaf Storm can be used in its stead for the ability to OHKO Hippowdon, despite it summoning sand.

  • Flamethrower: Flamethrower is perfectly accurateand is typically more than enough to nip off frailer foes.

  • Substitute: In spite of the type matchup, Scovillain is deceptively weak to Kingambit thanks to Sucker Punch. Additionally, many Pokemon will use Protect in front of Scovillain to waste sun turns— most notably Espathra and Dondozo. Against all of these foes, a well-timed Substitute can guarantee the win.

Tera Types

  • Fire: It is almost mandatory to run Tera Fire on this Scovillain set. Tera Fire guarantees KOs on most Dragon-types.

  • Ghost: The abundantly common Dragonite is incredibly strong against Scovillain. Should Stealth Rock support be deemed enough to let Scovillain sweep teams reasonably, even without Tera Fire, using Tera Ghost to gain an immunity to Extreme Speed can be very useful.

  • Rock: Tera Rock with Tera Blast can be a decent alternative to Tera Fire, as it gives Scovillain excellent coverage and also provides a much-needed countermeasure to Dragonite's Extreme Speed.

Moody Ace.description:
• The metagame's abundance of Unaware Pokemon makes it difficult to maneuver Moody Pokemon in general. On top of that, Scovillain is held back by the powerful Dragon-types that resist its STAB combination. However, Scovillain still carves a niche for itself by being the only Moody Pokemon with excellent recovery moves, Leech Seed and Ingrain, allowing it to win a variety of matchups.

  • Protect and Substitute: Protect and Substitute are mandatory to get the most opportunities to activate Moody. Once you gain enough Defense or Special Defense boosts that Scovillain's Substitute can tank an attack without breaking, it tends to be easy to win the game. Note, however, that Protect, Substitute, and Leftovers's animation make Scovillain very vulnerable to losing via timer.

  • Flamethrower: With enough Moody boosts, Scovillain's Flamethrower tends to be enough to break through an entire team. There are very few Pokemon that are immune or quadruply resistant to Fire, and Flamethrower has good PP and accuracy, which makes it an easy pick.

  • Giga Drain: Unlike Flamethrower, Giga Drain gets shrugged off by a lot of Pokemon, even at +6, notably Corviknight and Dragonite. However, an attacking move that helps recover HP lost from Substitutes gives Scovillain more mileage off of Moody. Giga Drain is also notable to more reliably defeat Dondozo, one of the Unaware Pokemon that would give Scovillain a lot of trouble otherwise.

  • Leech Seed: Leech Seed combined with Protect, Substitute, and Leftovers helps Scovillain restore HP while collecting Moody boosts, as well as chipping Pokemon it'd otherwise have trouble against, such as Clodsire.

  • Ingrain: Ingrain is an alternative recovery option that makes Scovillain impervious to phazing moves. When purely considering recovery, it's more reliable than the inaccurate 90% accurate Leech Seed.

  • Fairy Tera Blast: Tera Blast with Tera Fairy is an excellent option that helps remedy Scovillain's Dragon susceptibility, particularly making the Infiltrator Dragapult and Roaring Moon matchup easier.

Tera Types

  • Water: The Water resistance helps Scovillain beat Dondozo. Even though Dondozo ignores Scovillain's Defense boosts via Unaware, with Tera Water, Scovillain's Substitute can tank a Wave Crash. Tera Water also keeps the Scovillain's Steel resistance, unlike Tera Grass, which makes it easier to check Scizor—a common priority user that people attempt to use to check Moody Pokemon.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy mitigating Scovillain's weakness to Dragon-types is massively helpful.

EV Spreads

  • 180 HP / 220 Def / 4 SpA / 4 SpD / 100 Spe with Bold: This spread bolsters Scovillain’s physical bulk. Notably, Tera Water Scovillain's Substitute manages to survive Dondozo's Wave Crash with this spread. The Speed allows Scovillain to outspeed slow Baxcalibur and Gholdengo, as well as Dragapult with one Moody Speed boost. The HP is adjusted to make maximum use of Leftovers, with the resulting stat having a remainder of 1 when divided by 16. The remaining EVs are split between Special Attack and Special Defense because, at level 50, investing 8 EVs in either stat has no benefit over investing 4.

Calm Mind.description: 12 speed EVs allow you to outspeed base 120 Speed Pokemon at +1

Stall.description:
• Espathra can utilize the Clear Amulet to stop any Speed drops from Primarina and Special Defense drops from Sylveon and non-Knock Off Hisuian Goodra.
  • Calm Mind, in conjunction with Speed Boost, allows Espathra to fire off tremendously powerful Stored Powers after setting up, letting it deal with Primarina and Manaphy.
  • Feather Dance is vital for surviving hits on the physical side, allowing Espathra to survive important attacks like Choice Band-boosted Giga Impact from Ursaluna and Earthquake from Donphan.
  • Roost helps as a major recovery tool against the previously mentioned Pokemon, allowing Espathra to be a potent threat as long as it doesn't get critically hit.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Espathra to take a -2 Choice Band-boosted Giga Impact follow by a -4 Choice Band-boosted Giga Impact after a Roost from Ursaluna. The Speed EVs ensure that Espathra outspeeds maximum Speed Modest Raging Bolt. The rest of the EVs and nature are placed into Special Defense to give Espathra the best odds against Primarina and Sylveon.
  • As its only attacking move is Psychic-type, Espathra naturally struggles against Dark-type Pokemon like Hoopa-U, Meowscarada, and Darkrai; therefore, Iron Valiant and Chien-Pao work well as teammates because they threaten these foes.
  • Espathra can also struggle against Steel-type Pokemon, like Metagross, Heatran, and Iron Crown, so Ground-type Pokemon like Flame Orb Ursaluna and Smack Down Landorus-T are great teammates for it.
  • Taunt users like Counter Ogerpon-W and Raging Bolt are an issue, so faster Dragon-type Pokemon like Haxorus and Walking Wake can help in these matchups.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis is for the Regulation C format of Battle Stadium Singles, which lasts until June 30th, 2023. For more information on this format and its current events, check out the format page!

If you feel this analysis is missing anything important or needs an update, feel free to suggest any changes here.

Calm Mind.description:
• With Calm Mind and Speed Boost rapidly increasing Stored Power's damage output, Espathra is a dangerous wincon against bulkier teams, as it even overwhelms Unaware foes.

  • Tera Blast versus Dazzling Gleam: Dazzling Gleam provides coverage against Dark-types such as Chien-Pao and Roaring Moon without having to Terastallize. However, Tera Blast provides more flexible coverage that can also cover Steel-types.

  • Protect versus Substitute: Protect is the most reliable way to get a free turn of Speed Boost. Substitute is a riskier option for Speed Boost stalling, but it severely punishes passive Pokemon and works extremely well on dual screen teams.

  • Roost: Roost can make it incredibly difficult for special attackers to break Espathra after its used Calm Mind.

  • Bold versus Timid: The given EV spread allows Espathra to outspeed Choice Scarf Garchomp after two turns of Speed Boost and unboosted Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle after one turn. If running Timid over Bold, you can reallocate 8 Speed EVs elsewhere.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium / High: Tera Blast sets will almost always require Terastallization to have adequate offensive coverage. Having Dazzling Gleam as coverage makes Terastallization less necessary, but Espathra's weaknesses to common types such as Ghost and Dark will remain problematic without it.

  • Fighting: When paired with Tera Blast, Tera Fighting is Espathra's best hope of defeating Ting-Lu, Chi-Yu, and Kingambit.

  • Fire: Tera Fire and Tera Blast roast Scizor, and deal massive damage to Chien-Pao, Gholdengo, and Kingambit.

  • Fairy: A Fairy Tera type flips the Dark-type weakness to a resistance and severely punishes Choice-locked Dragon-types like Dragonite, but at the cost of making Espathra even more vulnerable to Steel-types.
