Pivots like Vullaby and Elekid or trappers like Gothita can maintain offensive pressure or threaten to trap these foes, respectively. Spikes Glimmet enables late-game cleaners that appreciate chip damage like Alolan Diglett and Hisuian Growlithe. Dark-type allies like Stunky can punish Gothita after it has trapped and KOed Glimmet with Psychic.

nfe.overview: As one of the few viable Pokemon with access to Stealth Rock and Spikes, Glimmet is one of the premier entry hazard setters in the NFE metagame. The uniqueness of its niche means that it comfortably finds places on both hyper offense and slow hazard stacking team compositions. Toxic Debris punishes weak physical attacks like the omnipresent Knock Off and stops the likes of Quaxwell and Monferno from gaining momentum with Flip Turn and U-turn. Corrosion importantly enables the use of Toxic on Steel-types like Tinkatuff and Hisuian Sliggoo, putting them on a timer and ensuring that they cannot check Glimmet and its teammates forever. Despite all this, Glimmet has a generally poor defensive profile with weak bulk and crippling weaknesses to Ground-, Water-, and Psychic-type attacks. It also faces competition as a Poison-type from Koffing and Ivysaur, which both have greater longevity and access to utility moves like Will-O-Wisp and Knock Off, respectively.
nfe.comments:
Other Options

An offensive set with Power Herb and Meteor Beam does an obscene amount of damage by NFE standards, OHKOing Choice Band Piloswine and specially frail Eviolite holders like Monferno and Koffing while doing serious damage to sturdy defensive pieces like like Quaxwell and Ivysaur. However, Glimmet lacks the coverage to be a consistent wallbreaker, and it strongly prefers a longevity-increasing item instead. While situational, Dazzling Gleam stops Scraggy from using Glimmet as setup fodder and does notable damage to Krokorok and Gabite. On the hazard lead set, Mud Shot can be used to better punish Monferno and Pignite, while also being invaluable against opposing Glimmet.

Checks and Counters

Water-types: Because they are slower, Quaxwell and Wartortle can both use Rapid Spin to clear away Glimmet's hazards without worrying about Toxic Debris and can OHKO it with Surf after. Frogadier is also able to easily dispatch with Glimmet while preserving momentum with U-turn and Spikes.

Ground-types: While they do not stop Glimmet from setting at least one layer of entry hazards, Piloswine, Gabite, and Krokorok can all easily KO Glimmet and take minimal damage from its attacks.

Hattrem: Hattrem prevents the setting of entry hazards with Magic Bounce and forces Glimmet out with its Psychic-type STAB moves. However, without RestTalk, Hattrem needs to be wary of getting worn down by Glimmet's attacks.

Setup Sweepers: Swords Dance Gabite and Dragon Dance Fraxure can both take advantage of lead Glimmet to set up and start making progress, as they can block Memento with Substitute or Taunt. Bulky Calm Mind users like Dunsparce and Duosion can threaten Glimmet without worrying about Toxic Debris and can also freely set up in front of it.

Defoggers: Fletchinder and the rare Vullaby are able to remove entry hazards without worrying about getting blocked by a Ghost-type teammate.

Hazard Lead.description:
Glimmet is a natural choice for a dedicated lead because Toxic Debris severely limits the ways an opponent can effectively respond, creating more opportunities to set Spikes. Sludge Wave lets Glimmet have some form of direct damage, stopping Thwackey and Servine from setting up in front of it. Power Gem has limited utility as coverage but crucially OHKOes Fletchinder. Stealth Rock is a preferred option to have in cases where Glimmet can only set two layers of entry hazards. Memento is can be used to stop a slower Rapid Spin or Defog from succeeding. It also neutralizes opposing offenses and can create a free turn for a sweeper to set up. Focus Sash is preferred on builds that expect to always lead Glimmet, as it guarantees a turn to act. However, Eviolite is a solid option in cases where another offensive hazard setter like Krokorok or Gabite is accompanying Glimmet.

Drakloak is an indispensable partner, as it can easily block Rapid Spin from Quaxwell, which is very commonly seen on most balance structures, and easily pivot into threats or wallbreak itself. Generally, any offensive Pokemon that appreciates entry hazards will be a good partner for Lead Glimmet, common offensive staples such as Pignite, Thwackey and Hisuian Sliggoo all fit comfortably next to it. Fast Choice Specs users like Frogadier and Girafarig do not fear Flame Body and can KO Fletchinder before it has the chance to use Defog. Explosive setup sweepers like Shell Smash Wartortle and Dragon Dance Fraxure can take great advantage of Memento and threaten to end the game quickly. Shed Skin Scraggy and Krokorok can both freely counter Hattrem without worrying about Nuzzle. Offensive Ground-types like Piloswine and Gabite are great to threaten opposing Poison-types that will otherwise absorb the Toxic Spikes from Toxic Debris.

Physically Defensive.description:
This set runs Corrosion and bulk in order to have more long-term utility in balance and bulky team structures. With Corrosion, Toxic becomes one of Glimmet's most powerful tools to force progress, stopping it from being used as setup fodder and putting Steel- and Poison-type defensive pieces like Tinkatuff, Hisuian Sliggoo and Ivysaur on timers. Spikes is essential for long-term pressure and forcing progress against already poisoned Pokemon. Power Gem is necessary to OHKO Fletchinder and stop it from using Defog in front of Glimmet. Stealth Rock helps accrue more passive damage. Sludge Wave is also a viable option to soft-check Thwackey.

Despite running maximum physical bulk, Glimmet is still rather frail and requires defensive partners to handle common attackers like Monferno, Raboot and Pignite more than once. Dusclops and RestTalk Drakloak are both oppressive partners that blanket check most physical attackers and spinblock Quaxwell while healing off any chip damage from Flip Turn and entry hazards that could wear them down long-term. A defensive Water-type like Quaxwell or Seadra is essential to check Piloswine. Offensive threats that are walled by Steel-types like Girafarig, Hisuian Sliggoo, and Duosion all greatly appreciate the timer that Corrosion Toxic forces on their checks. Offensive Thwackey and Servine both take great advantage of Poison-types like Ivysaur and Koffing being affected by Toxic. If Glimmet is not running Stealth Rock, Tinkatuff and Krokorok both make for solid Stealth Rock setters that can wear down foes with Knock Off. Tinkatuff, alongside Hisuian Sliggoo, additionally acts as a reliable defensive check to Psychic-type sweepers like Girafarig and Duosion that Glimmet creates openings for. Piloswine can also reliably set Stealth Rock or use Choice Band to easily break through a badly poisoned Quaxwell.

vgc2024.overview:
• Glimmora is a strong offensive threat with access to a good STAB combination and the powerful move Meteor Beam, which, when used with the Power Herb, can melt many targets, such as Assault Vest Entei and Incineroar. With Toxic Debris and signature move Mortal Spin, Glimmora can punish physical attackers and passive play, and, when combined with the threat of Meteor Beam, make it impossible to ignore while also requiring careful positioning to properly handle.

  • Glimmora has traditionally fit best on Dondozo teams, as the combination of Toxic Debris and Mortal Spin means your foes almost guaranteed to be afflicted with poison, putting your opponent on a timer. Assault Vest on Glimmora is especially effective on Dondozo teams, as the extra longevity helps it spread poison better and stall out even longer, making up for the lowered damage output.

  • With Meteor Beam, Glimmora can utilize its high Special Attack stat and good offensive typing as a damage dealer. Tornadus and Ogerpon-W are good partners; Tornadus provides speed control and can launch powerful Bleakwind Storms into Fighting-types that resist Meteor Beam and Ogerpon-W redirects potential Water- or Ground-type attacks while pressuring threats like Urshifu-R and Landorus. In return, Glimmora can threaten Grass-types, which resists both Ogerpon-W's STAB moves.

  • Glimmora's poor defensive typing, combined with its middling bulk and average Speed, makes Glimmora a glass cannon. Glimmora is weak to many prominent offensive threats such as Urshifu-R, Landorus, and Gholdengo. Glimmora also struggles to handle Rock-resistant foes such as Iron Hands, Kingambit, and Urshifu-R. Even then, many of these foes will concede Toxic Spikes while taking out Glimmora; for instance, Urshifu-R will set up both layers of Toxic Spikes if it attacks Glimmora. Amoonguss is another difficult match up, as it absords Toxic Spikes and takes Glimmora's attacks comfortably, while threatening a Spore.

Meteor Beam.description:
Meteor Beam's power against most neutral targets is devastating. The Special Attack boost allows Glimmora to output offensive pressure with Sludge Bomb even after Power Herb is consumed.

  • Earth Power is used as coverage for the Steel-types that resist Glimmora's STAB combination. Energy Ball is also an option to utilize the Tera Grass STAB boost and to hit Pokemon that resist Meteor Beam such as Urshifu-R but makes it so that Steel-types resist all of Glimmora's attacks.

  • The Special Attack investment along with the Modest nature is necessary to pick up a OHKO on Landorus, Walking Wake, and Terastillized Urshifu-R with Meteor Beam. The OHKO on Landorus and Urshifu turns the match up against hyper offensive teams completely on its head, especially with speed control support from Tornadus.

  • The Defense investment is enough to guarantee surviving Rillaboom's Wood Hammer and a favourable roll of taking Kingambit's Iron Head. The Special Defensive investment lets it live Gholdengo's Make It Rain and Latias's Mist Ball. The rest of the EVs are invested into Speed, which allows Glimmora to outspeed Choice Scarf Landorus-T when in Tailwind.

  • Tera Grass has better synergy with Glimmora's original typing and provides an immunity to spore, but gives Glimmora weakness to common threats such as Chien-Pao. Tera Water, defensively, is a stronger neutral type into the metagame, but has fewer relevant resistances to common threats.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Both Earth Power and Energy Ball are fine options, but Energy Ball can do more damage against neutral targets if Glimmora Terastallizes into a Grass type.

  • Mortal Spin is used as the final move for a more consistent method to spread poison than Toxic Debris.

  • The Assault Vest gives Glimmora much more longevity, as it allows it to comfortably tank special attacks while still dissuading physical attackers with the threat of Toxic Spikes. On teams where being able to spread poison is important, Assault Vest is a good option.

  • The special bulk allows Glimmora to live many strong super effective attacks, such as Choice Specs Gholdengo's Make It Rain; it also makes Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball a 3HKO. Glimmora still lives a Rillaboom Wood Hammer with the HP investment.

ubers.overview: Glimmora is one of the best suicide leads in the Ubers metagame due to its ability to set multiple sets of entry hazards quickly while preventing opposing leads from setting their own. Its movepool allows it to match up well against other standard Ubers leads. Its decent Special Attack and Speed allow it to move before uninvested Pokemon, safely set hazards, and put down chip damage before fainting without being used as setup fodder. Many Ubers Pokemon, such as the various Arceus formes, cannot run Heavy-Duty Boots, leaving them vulnerable to entry hazards, especially Toxic Spikes. Due to the limited distribution of viable hazard control in the tier, it can be difficult for offensive teams to deal with Glimmora, forcing them to avoid hitting it with a physical attack to prevent Toxic Debris from activating.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

An alternative spread of 76 Def / 180 SpA / 252 Spe with a Timid nature improves the lead matchup against Koraidon. An 84 EV Special Attack Dazzling Gleam has an unfavorable roll to OHKO Koraidon, so increasing Special Attack greatly improves the odds. However, this comes at the cost of giving five-hit Scale Shot from Jolly Koraidon having a chance to KO Glimmora, and Glimmora always faints to a five- hit Scale Shot from Adamant Koraidon.

Earth Power can be run over Mud Shot for its increased base power on offensive EV spreads. This additional damage can result in certain moves being an OHKO instead of a 2HKO with Mud Shot, most notably non-Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM, as well as 2HKOing Zacian-C. In the vast majority of situations, the speed control provided by Mud Shot is preferred.

Checks and Counters

Heavy-Duty Boots: Pokemon with Heavy-Duty Boots ignore the hazards Glimmora sets.

Steel-types: Steel-types like Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, Kingambit, Orthworm, and Corviknight ignore the Toxic Spikes placed by Glimmora's ability and block it from using Mortal Spin to clear hazards.

Necrozma-DM: Necrozma-DM blocks Mortal Spin and can use Glimmora to set up. Defensive sets can set up Stealth Rock before healing off damage with Morning Sun and threaten Knock Off on Glimmora's teammates. Glimmora can use Mud Shot to prevent Dragon Dance sets from setting up, but the super effective hit and Speed reduction are both beneficial for Trick Room sets. It can also use Covert Cloak to ignore the Speed drops from Mud Shot and freely set up on Glimmora.

Entry Hazard Removal: Giratina-O can use Defog to remove hazards and can use Tera Steel to prevent Glimmora using Mortal Spin to poison it or remove hazards. Corviknight is immune to Glimmora's Ground-type attacks and resists its common attacking options, allowing it to freely set up Iron Defense or use Defog. Iron Treads can use Rapid Spin to break Focus Sash and negate the Speed drop from Mud Shot while simultaneously removing hazards.

Opposing Poison-types: Once Glimmora has fainted, opposing Poison-types like Eternatus and Clodsire can switch in and remove the Toxic Spikes laid by Toxic Debris. The same is true in the other direction, as Glimmora can enter the field to clear hazards laid by opposing Toxic Spikes setters.

Suicide Lead.description:
Mortal Spin is used to remove opposing entry hazards such as Ribombee's Sticky Web and cripple opposing bulky Pokemon such as Kyogre and various Arceus formes. Mud Shot provides extremely valuable disruption, allowing Glimmora to outspeed opposing leads such as Deoxys-A, Miraidon, and Zacian-C after a Speed drop and get up hazards. Mud Shot also prevents Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM from using Glimmora as setup fodder. 172 Defense EVs allow Glimmora to always live a five-hit Scale Shot from Jolly Koraidon and retaliate with a super effective Dazzling Gleam. Memento can be used instead to let Glimmora sacrifice itself to give its team valuable offensive momentum. Tera Ghost prevents Glimmora's entry hazards from being removed by Rapid Spin but is almost never used due to its status as a suicide lead.

Glimmora is limited in usage to hyper offense teams, where its ability to set hazards and provide diruption is unmatched. It is generally paired with powerful wallbreakers such as Choice Scarf Koraidon, Zacian-C, and Miraidon, as well as setup sweepers such as Necrozma-DM, Kyurem-B, Scale Shot Koraidon, Kingambit, Miraidon, and Extreme Killer Arceus.

Lead.description:
Glimmora is one of the tier's premier leads thanks to its ability to set up Stealth Rock and deny opposing entry hazards with Mortal Spin, all while scaring foes from activating Toxic Debris in the process. Mortal Spin's side effect of inflicting poison detracts Pokemon such as Ting-Lu from setting up entry hazards multiple times and Hatterene from trying to deny Stealth Rock with Magic Bounce. Earth Power allows Glimmora to hit Steel-types such as Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Iron Treads, which otherwise are able to block Mortal Spin; pressures Poison-types like Pecharunt and opposing Glimmora hard, preventing them from safely absorbing its Toxic Spikes; and chunks Great Tusk and Cinderace, punishing them from switching in and removing its hazards freely. Power Gem provides a decent STAB move, letting Glimmora hit Cinderace even harder and notably chipping at Corviknight, Skarmory, and Gliscor that would otherwise wall Glimmora, with Corviknight also removing its entry hazards with Defog. However, Glimmora can also run Spikes to further support its teammates with even more entry hazards. Red Card allows Glimmora to make use of its bulk and typing against common offensive foes like Iron Valiant and Iron Moth by taking a hit and phazing them after, preventing its team from getting overrun by boosted offensive threats. Red Card is also useful to force a foe in to take Stealth Rock damage or Toxic Spikes poison. An alternative EV spread of 252 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe alongside a Timid nature can be used for more offensive presence; particularly, this allows it to outspeed and pressure Gholdengo and Hisuian Samurott while also improving the matchup against opposing Glimmora, even offensive variants. This set should opt for Focus Sash instead due to the lack of extra bulk, guaranteeing it can set up hazards against faster threats, especially Deoxys-S, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads. Tera Ghost grants Glimmora with an immunity to Rapid Spin from the likes of Great Tusk and Iron Treads, denying their attempts from removing Glimmora's entry hazards.

Glimmora finds its home on hyper offense teams that enjoy it starting the match strong by setting up Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes from the beginning. Kingambit greatly appreciates this, as even Pokemon that resist Sucker Punch like Darkrai and Enamorus can potentially get KOed by +2 Sucker Punch after a round or two of Stealth Rock, while physically defensive walls trying to switch in like Skarmory and Corviknight have to contend with not only Kingambit's attacks but also with the chip damage from Stealth Rock. Iron Valiant similarly enjoys Glimmora's entry hazards chipping at the foes for it and the rest of the team to win late-game, while it also provides Knock Off support to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from Pokemon like Dondozo, Alomomola, and Clodsire, making them susceptible to its hazards. Gholdengo may be used alongside Glimmora, as its Ghost typing and Good as Gold ability let it block Rapid Spin and Defog attempts, thus making sure Glimmora's entry hazards stay up. Glimmora may also play a defensive role on occasion, as its good matchup against Skeledirge lets it assist teammates like Iron Moth and Zamazenta that can struggle against it.

Offensive.description:
Due to a strong STAB Meteor Beam alongside decent offensive stats, Glimmora acts as a solid wallbreaker that can also compress roles as an entry hazard remover and setter. Moreover, Glimmora excels against opposing offense, as many of them struggle with Toxic Spikes, meaning the opponent must be careful with how they attack Glimmora. This careful play can be punished by breaking through common bulkier threats that fit well on offense, such as Zamazenta and Gholdengo. Earth Power deals with problematic Steel-types like Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Iron Treads, which otherwise wall it and can block its Mortal Spin. The move also helps pressure Poison-types like Galarian Slowking and Pecharunt, which can otherwise absorb its Toxic Spikes, more reliably, especially if its Power Herb has been consumed. On top of removing opposing hazards, Mortal Spin can also cripple checks like Ting-Lu and Assault Vest Alomomola. If the team has another Stealth Rock setter, then Glimmora can opt for Spikes instead. Dazzling Gleam alongside Tera Fairy is also an option, granting it super effective coverage against foes like Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Ting-Lu while gaining a good defensive typing against the likes of Dragapult and Kingambit's Sucker Punch. A Timid Nature is used to Speed tie opposing Glimmora and outspeed crucial targets like Gholdengo and Ceruledge, but a Modest nature—especially if Glimmora is ran on Sticky Web teams—is also an option for more power, notably letting it OHKO defensive Landorus-T and having good odds to do so against Corviknight. Tera Ghost lets it importantly spinblock Great Tusk and Iron Treads while letting it take on Zamazenta in a pinch.

Glimmora's niche makes it a good fit on hyper offense teams. Gholdengo is a great partner, as it can block hazard removal to keep Glimmora's entry hazards up; it also provides good defensive utility by checking Galarian Slowking and Hatterene. Kingambit is a great offensive partner that can take advantage of the entry hazards that Glimmora sets up and clean up late-game after Glimmora has broken through the opposing team. Other setup sweepers like Dragonite, Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Raging Bolt are also similarly useful, as they can keep up the pressure against the opposition while making use of Glimmora's entry hazards. In return, they also appreciate Glimmora's ability to remove opposing hazards and absorb Toxic Spikes. Glimmora struggles against checks like Ting-Lu and bulkier teams that make use of Heavy-Duty Boots, particularly ones with Blissey and Clodsire; as such, Glimmora appreciates the presence of Knock Off users such as Ogerpon-W, Hisuian Samurott, Iron Valiant, and the aforementioned Great Tusk. Other entry hazards can also help wear them down over time, which the likes of Landorus-T and the aforementioned Ogerpon-W and Hisuian Samurott can provide, with Glimmora complementing them with its own hazard. Sticky Web variants of hyper offense teams anchored by Ribombee or Araquanid as the hazard setter can help compensate for Glimmora's average Speed tier.

Suicide Lead.description:
• Having the ability to set all entry hazards without becoming passive thanks to Toxic Debris and to cripple a good portion of its checks and remove hazards with Mortal Spin, Glimmora is a potent hazard setter for hyper offense teams.

  • Power Gem allows Glimmora to super effectively hit common Defoggers in Ho-Oh and Yveltal, applying pressure to keep entry hazards on the field.

  • Mortal Spin gives Glimmora a chance to remove entry hazards from other suicide leads such as Shuckle, Mega Diancie, and opposing Glimmora, and it cripples foes such as support Arceus formes without Refresh, Zygarde, and Primal Groudon.

  • Mud Shot hinders foes that try to set up on it such as Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Zacian-C; additionally, it eases the matchup against Eternatus by causing it to become easier to revenge kill, punishing it switching in to remove Toxic Spikes. With it, Glimmora can outspeed opposing Glimmora and Mega Diancie and potentially finish them off with Mortal Spin to prevent any hazards from staying on its side of the field, but this limits its ability to set entry hazards out of a lack of move slots.

  • The given EV spread avoids after Stealth Rock a OHKO from Choice Band Tera Flying Rayquaza's Dragon Ascent, and +1 Zacian-C's Close Combat while also outspeeding -1 Zacian-C, offensively also ensuring a OHKO on specially defensive Yveltal with Power Gem after Stealth Rock. It's to be noted that this spread can't outspeed Pheromosa after a Speed drop from Mud Shot. An alternate spread of 32 Def / 236 SpA / 244 Spe fixes this, now avoiding a 2HKO from Ferrothorn's Power Whip and ensuring a 2HKO on other Glimmora with Power Gem.

  • Tera Steel prevents opposing Glimmora from removing entry hazards with Mortal Spin; Glimmora, however, shouldn't usually Terastallize, as other Pokemon it's partnered with generally make better use of Terastallizing.

  • If the opposing team has a Poison-type like Glimmora or Eternatus, setting Toxic Spikes shouldn't be a priority, as they will get quickly removed as soon they enter the field, thus making it desirable to focus on setting Stealth Rock or Spikes. Similarly, as Glimmora can remove Toxic Spikes by switching in as long it survives entry hazards, it can still become useful mid-game after getting worn down in such matchups.

  • Against Trick Room teams, Glimmora should be kept mid-game, as it can't set hazards on their usual lead in Hatterene due to its Magic Bounce ability, especially as Toxic Spikes hinder the longevity of such teams, and can prove useful to stall out Trick Room turns by being sacked.

  • Against stall teams, setting Toxic Spikes and using Mortal Spin should be priorities to hinder the longevity of such teams, especially as Glimmora can do this multiple times across the match out of not taking damage as quickly as in other matchups.

  • Wallbreakers such as Zacian-C, Double Dance Primal Groudon, and Necrozma-DM appreciate the entry hazards set by Glimmora to ensure more KOs, they also act as counterplay to Eternatus to limit its capability to come in to remove Toxic Spikes with offensive pressure.

Lead.description:
Glimmora functions as a niche hyper offense lead, being able to utilize its unique ability in Toxic Debris as well as its access to Stealth Rock to consistently stack entry hazards to aid its teammates in wallbreaking. It also has access to Mortal Spin, allowing it to remove hazards from foes such as Great Tusk and Landorus-T. Power Gem is used in order to hit Flying-types such as Moltres and Zapdos, which could otherwise remove Glimmora's hazards with Defog. Earth Power is used in order to hit Steel-types such as Heatran, Kingambit, and Gholdengo, all of which would use Glimmora as setup fodder. Focus Sash is used most of the time in order to set up multiple layers of Toxic Spikes and almost always guarantees Stealth Rock to be set. Red Card, meanwhile, can be used in order to punish anything attacking Glimmora and to rack up more hazard chip damage while also potentially getting a poison off on foes such as Mega Tyranitar and Ting-Lu.

Glimmora fits solely on hyper offense teams, where its ability to stack Toxic Spikes and Stealth Rock is appreciated by its teammates. Dark-types such as Kingambit and Weavile enjoy the poison damage whittling down Fighting-types such as Great Tusk, Urshifu-R, and Mega Lopunny, allowing them to clean through opposing teams more easily. Raging Bolt and Tornadus-T also appreciate Glimmora's Toxic Spikes, which help wear down Ting-Lu , letting them overwhelm it more easily. Gholdengo is appreciated in order to block Rapid Spin from Great Tusk and Terapagos as well as Defog from Tornadus-T and Zapdos. Glimmora struggles with opposing leads such as Iron Treads and Landorus-T, which can effectively set and deny entry hazards against Glimmora, meaning that Flying-types such as Dragonite and the aforementioned Tornadus-T are appreciated. Glimmora also struggles with Poison-types, notably Galarian Slowking and Toxapex, due to their ability to remove Toxic Spikes, so Ground-types that threaten them such as Landorus-T and Garchomp function as good teammates. Glimmora has difficulty with faster foes that can break its Focus Sash such as Urshifu-R and Tachyon Cutter Iron Crown, meaning teammates that help against them such as Dragonite and Raging Bolt are appreciated. Glimmora has trouble breaking through Ferrothorn, who which can use it as fodder to set Spikes up on, meaning Fire-types such as Volcarona are appreciated. In return, Volcarona appreciates Glimmora's hazards chipping down would be switch-ins such as Heatran and Raging Bolt.

monotype.overview:
Poison

Glimmora is enticing; its respectable Special Attack combined with a strong movepool—containing powerful support options like Stealth Rock, Mortal Spin, and Corrosion Toxic and hard-hitting offensive tools like Sludge Wave and Earth Power—should make it a powerhouse. However, it is never going to be the best at making use of its supportive and offensive options. Its low bulk makes it far too frail to consistently spread Toxic poison, keep entry hazards up, or remove them with Mortal Spin, making its support unreliable in the long term. Meanwhile, its Special Attack is only just respectable, and it is unable to threaten types like Flying and Fire as much as it would like without major support to wear teams down first. It also demands a Choice Scarf; otherwise, it isn't fast enough to check threats such as Cinderace and Ogerpon-H comfortably.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Rock

Choice Specs can be run over Choice Scarf to become a fierce wallbreaker, taking on Toxapex, Rotom-W, and Ursaluna-B easier. However, this makes Glimmora vulnerable to faster threats, such as Greninja, Iron Valiant, and Chien-Pao, and will likely require some other form of speed control. Spikes can be used to allow Glimmora to rack up entry hazard damage on forced switches against foes such as Iron Valiant and Quagsire.

Toxic Spreader (Poison).description:
Glimmora provides useful utility for Poison teams thanks to its unique set of tools in entry hazard support and Corrosion Toxic, which is capable of putting walls such as Toxapex and Corviknight on a timer. Power Gem is used to threaten problematic Flying- and Fire-types like Articuno, Zapdos, Torkoal, and Iron Moth. Earth Power allows Glimmora to deal solid damage to Steel-types like Gholdengo and Heatran after their Air Balloon is popped. Alternatively, Mortal Spin can be run to spread poison onto Hatterene, which cannot be poisoned otherwise thanks to Magic Bounce, and remove entry hazards.

Due to Glimmora's immense weakness to Ground- and Water-type attacks, Amoonguss is a valuable partner, taking on dangerous threats such as Great Tusk, Swampert, and Urshifu-R with ease. Toxapex can similarly assist against Water-types like Barraskewda and Keldeo, Steel-types like Scizor and Corviknight, and Fighting-types like Zamazenta and Sneasler. Toxapex can also run Toxic Spikes to assist Glimmora with hazard stacking. Galarian Weezing provides a solid Ground immunity thanks to Levitate, allowing it to come in on threats like Clodsire, Garchomp, and Ting-Lu, and it provides solid hazard removal with Defog. Overqwil pairs well with Glimmora, providing both Spikes and Toxic Spikes, which allows it to complete the hazard stacking-core while also taking on foes like Iron Boulder, Gallade, and Dragapult thanks to Intimidate. Alolan Muk provides Knock Off support to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes such as Dragonite, Iron Moth, and Volcarona, increasing the threat of Glimmora's Stealth Rock; it can also deal with Psychic- and Ghost-type threats like Espathra, Hatterene, and Flutter Mane. Galarian Slowking's Future Sight can lure in special walls such as Alolan Muk and Hisuian Goodra, which Glimmora can take advantage of to spread Toxic. Galarian Slowking can also check threats like Heatran and Terapagos, which prove problematic for Glimmora. Okidogi and Sneasler greatly appreciate Glimmora's ability to put physical walls like Pecharunt, Toxapex, and Sableye on timers with Toxic, while Glimmora appreciates their ability to check troublesome Steel-types like Kingambit, Hisuian Goodra, and Empoleon.

Choice Scarf (Rock).description:
Glimmora is a decent Choice Scarf user for Rock teams due to its high Special Attack and Speed to take on threats like Ogerpon-W, Hisuian Lilligant, and non-Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. Earth Power threatens Steel- and Poison-types like Gholdengo, non-Air Balloon Heatran, Iron Moth, and Sneasler. Sludge Wave is a strong STAB move that can take on Fairy- and Grass-types such as Hisuian Lilligant, Ogerpon-W, Ogerpon-H, and non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant. Dazzling Gleam takes out Dark-, Dragon-, and Fighting-types like Sableye, Hydreigon, and Kommo-o. Energy Ball allows Glimmora to deal with Water- and Ground-types like Quagsire and non-Choice Scarf Greninja and Great Tusk. Mortal Spin can be run over Energy Ball to help remove entry hazards and poison foes in the process. Power Gem can be run instead to deal with Weavile, Volcarona, and Choice Scarf Kleavor.

Tyranitar provides sand and a Psychic immunity while also taking on special attackers for Glimmora such as Spectrier, Slowking, and Hisuian Zoroark. Thanks to the sand Tyranitar provides, Glimmora can survive a Choice Specs Draco Meteor from Dragapult due to the Special Defense boost and 2HKO it with Dazzling Gleam. In return, Glimmora also takes out Hisuian Samurott, Quagsire, and Ogerpon-W for Tyranitar. Ogerpon-C can compensate for Glimmora's Ground weakness, and, after setup, it can eliminate Ursaluna, Dragonite, and Landorus. Glimmora aids Ogerpon-C by handling threats such as Kleavor when running Power Gem, Iron Valiant, and Hisuian Lilligant. Glimmora can further aid Ogerpon-C with Mortal Spin by removing entry hazards to help prevent Ogerpon-C's Sturdy from breaking. Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine is a strong wallbreaker that can deal with Corviknight, Clodsire, and Toxapex. Coalossal can serve as entry hazard control to allow Glimmora to drop Mortal Spin; it can additionally support the team with Spikes, facilitating Glimmora's cleaning. Coalossal also deals with Scizor, Bisharp, Weavile, and Corviknight. Glimmora returns the favor by threatening Clodsire and Toxapex, which can threaten Coalossal. Lead Kleavor can set up Stealth Rock and potentially break opposing Ceruledge's Focus Sash. In exchange, Glimmora eliminates physical walls like Quagsire and non-Air Balloon Heatran for Kleavor. Iron Defense Garganacl is a stallbreaker that can force progress with Salt Cure in matchups against defensive Pokemon like Toxapex, Hisuian Goodra, and Galarian Slowking. Glimmora dispatches Choice Band Mamoswine after Stealth Rock, entry hazard chip and Urshifu-R, which can threaten Garganacl. Alolan Golem can trap and eliminate Steel-types like Scizor and Corviknight. Diancie can set up Stealth Rock while also OHKOing Weavile with Body Press and Kommo-o with Moonblast if Glimmora is not running Dazzling Gleam.

Choice Scarf (Poison).description:
Choice Scarf allows Glimmora to become a potent offensive threat on Poison teams, being able to outspeed several key targets like Iron Valiant, Ogerpon-H, and Choice Specs Greninja and swiftly remove them. Power Gem picks off the threatening Flying- and Fire-types of the tier including Articuno, Ceruledge, and Cinderace. Sludge Wave is Glimmora's strongest move and can KO threats like the Ogerpon formes, Iron Valiant, and Alolan Ninetales. Earth Power hits the Steel-types that would effortlessly switch into Glimmora's STAB moves such as non-Air Balloon Heatran, Gholdengo, and Archaludon. Finally, Energy Ball threatens Choice Specs Greninja and Ground-types like Mamoswine and Ursaluna. Alternatively, Stealth Rock can be used to help further pressure types like Fire and Ice.

Choice Scarf Glimmora greatly enjoys Parting Shot Pecharunt, which can be used to pivot it onto the field safely along with helping against physical attackers that can check Glimmora such as Scizor, Choice Scarf Iron Boulder, and Assault Vest Iron Hands. Galarian Slowking can similarly help get Glimmora onto the field with Chilly Reception and can use Future Sight to help pressure would-be switch-ins like Clodsire and Assault Vest Gallade. Sneasler is capable of breaking special walls like Ting-Lu, Blissey, and Hisuian Goodra for Glimmora with Close Combat, and its U-turn can bring Glimmora in on threats Glimmora can handle like Archaludon and Zapdos. Amoonguss can help against Water-types like Swift Swim Barraskewda and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, which outspeed and remove Glimmora, while also being able to use Spore to put opposing threats to sleep and get Glimmora in safely. Galarian Weezing can come in against faster and bulkier Ground- and Dark-types Glimmora cannot deal with like Choice Scarf Great Tusk, Clodsire, and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon while helping break through Dark- and Dragon-types such as Ting-Lu and Garchomp with Strange Steam. Alolan Muk can come in on faster special attackers like Flutter Mane, Spectrier, and Choice Scarf Greninja for Glimmora and threaten Knock Off to remove their Choice Scarf; Knock Off also deals with Gholdengo's Air Balloon, allowing Glimmora to check it with Earth Power. Iron Moth can serve as an offensive complement to Glimmora, being able to deal with the Steel-types Glimmora struggles against such as Corviknight and Gholdengo while appreciating Glimmora's Power Gem handling Ceruledge and Ninetales.

Bulky Support.description:
• With its good utility, ability, and coverage, Glimmora is one of the best supportive Pokemon in Regulation J.

  • Mortal Spin: Mortal Spin provides entry hazard removal and also spreads poison, chipping down bulky Pokemon like Arceus-Fairy and Ho-Oh.

  • Power Gem: Power Gem hits Pokemon such as Chien-Pao and the aforementioned Ho-Oh.

  • Mud Shot versus Endure: Mud Shot is a solid option to tickle Steel-types like Archaludon while crucially lowering foes' Speed. Endure ensures that Glimmora survives a move such as Earthquake from Landorus-T, allowing it to get another layer of Toxic Spikes down before getting KOed.

  • Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock gives Glimmora even more utility by applying pressure to Pokemon such as Dragonite.

Other Options

  • Toxic Spikes: Toxic Spikes is nice for bulkier teams, namely Lugia teams, as they depend more on the passive chip damage to break through opposing walls. Choosing this does give up the invaluable entry hazard control option in Mortal Spin, however.

  • Sludge Wave: Sludge Wave is a very strong STAB option for Glimmora, hitting foes like Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom. Using Sludge Wave, however, means dropping valuable utility in Stealth Rock or dropping Power Gem, which hits far more important targets such as Ho-Oh harder than Sludge Wave can.

  • Energy Ball: Energy Ball is a great coverage option for Glimmora, annoying Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Dondozo more than poison can. This does, however, come at the cost of dropping an important utility option or STAB move.

Items

  • Red Card: Red Card forces foes to take extra entry hazard damage and potentially shuts down setup sweepers if Glimmora survives a hit.

  • Air Balloon: Glimmora's severe Ground-type weakness gets patched up by Air Balloon, letting it set up in front of Ground-types along the lines of Landorus-T and Ting-Lu.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Being a supportive Pokemon, Glimmora typically doesn't need to Terastallize despite its pretty bad defensive typing; Terastallization would be better spent on a more offensive ally.

  • Grass: Tera Grass provides Glimmora with Ground- and Water-type resistances, notably letting it take hits from the likes of Ursaluna-B and Kyogre, while also granting it a Electric-type resistance for pesky Miraidon.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy allows Glimmora to come in on Koraidon's Scale Shot, preventing it from running away with the game after Scale Shot's boosts.

EV Spreads

  • 244 HP / 236 Def / 28 SpD with Bold: This is the recommended EV spread, letting Glimmora avoid a 2HKO from Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash.

  • 244 HP / 76 Def / 188 SpD with Bold: This more specially defensive spread lets Glimmora avoid a 2HKO from Choice Specs Tera Fairy Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast and generally avoid a 2HKO from Jolly Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash.

Debris Lead.description:
• With a solid early-game Speed tier, utility, high Special Attack, and decent coverage options, Glimmora can set the tone of a battle with its entry hazard setting and removing options.

  • Earth Power: Earth Power ensures that Glimmora is not walled by common Steel-types such as Gholdengo and Archaludon.

  • Mortal Spin: If you're using Stealth Rock-weak teammates like Dragonite and Volcarona, clearing the hazards with Mortal Spin can be quite useful, though it's not required for this set to function.

  • Sludge Wave versus Energy Ball: Sludge Wave deals plenty of damage to Primarina, while Energy Ball deals more damage to Ursaluna-B and pairs well with Tera Grass.

  • Toxic Spikes Partners: While Toxic Debris doesn't mean Toxic Spikes will be set up, it's still good to consider running a teammate with it in mind. Defensive Dragonite sets, Stamina Archaludon, Annihilape, and Gliscor are good examples to consider.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: While Glimmora can use Terastallization to improve match-ups against foes like Ursaluna-B and Primarina, other teammates will usually want the Terastallization option more.

  • Grass: A Grass Tera type is the best option, letting Glimmora survive attacks from common Ground-type Pokemon such as Ursaluna-B and Garchomp, in addition to nullifying Breloom's Spore.

  • Flying: Tera Flying vastly improves Glimmora's matchup against Ground-types with a potential to retain Focus Sash, though this doesn't help Glimmora as much offensively as Tera Grass.

Items

  • Focus Sash: This is the most reliable item for setting up Stealth Rock.

  • Air Balloon: With Air Balloon, Glimmora vastly improves its matchup against Ground-type leads such as Garchomp.

Meteor Beam.description:
• With Power Herb and Meteor Beam combined, Glimmora gains a huge amount of power compared to its other sets, making its softer checks such as Assault Vest Ursaluna-B and Assault Vest Kingambit far less reliable. This set is also less reliant on leading, though Toxic Debris still makes it a natural at this role.

  • Earth Power: Coverage against Steel-types such as Gholdengo, Archaludon, and Kingambit is required for Glimmora to potentially sweep.

  • Energy Ball: Energy Ball is Glimmora's most damaging attack against Ursaluna-B, and it pairs greatly with Tera Grass.

  • Sludge Wave versus Dazzling Gleam: While Poison coverage may not seem particularly useful, it deals more damage to Primarina than Energy Ball, potentially preventing a revenge kill. Dazzling Gleam on the other hand, knocks out Hydreigon and deals serious damage to Garchomp.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Since Meteor Beam only has one shot of boosting Special Attack without a charge-up turn, Terastallization is often key to prevent Glimmora's vulnerability to Ground-type attacks from ruining its shot at sweeping.

  • Grass: Tera Grass stands out as the best option, boosting Energy Ball to the point where even some Assault Vest Ursaluna-B risk getting OHKOed after a boost while twisting the Ground-type weakness into a resistance. As a bonus, this also stops Breloom's Spore from derailing a potential sweep.

  • Flying: Tera Flying's Ground-type immunity is worth considering, and it also grants the bonus of not worrying about Toxic Spikes. However, it provides far less offensive benefit than Tera Grass.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is mainly useful for stopping Scale Shot users like Dragonite and Garchomp from setting up a sweep and revenge kill on Glimmora in one turn as well as punishing Choice-locked Dragon-types such as Choice Band Dragonite and Choice Specs Hydreigon. However, retaining the Steel-type weakness is a big problem against Gholdengo and Scizor.

Assault Vest.description:
• Wearing an Assault Vest takes advantage of most opponents aiming to avoid Toxic Debris's activation, giving this set good luring potential against revenge killers like Gholdengo.

  • Earth Power: Hitting Gholdengo and Archaludon super effectively is essential for Glimmora to truly take advantage of Assault Vest and Terastallization.

  • Energy Ball: Ursaluna-B is a high-value target for this set, making Energy Ball the best coverage move for the job.

  • Mortal Spin versus Sludge Wave: Mortal Spin is another unique selling point, giving Glimmora far more support potential than most Assault Vest tanks. Sludge Wave is still worth considering for the extra damage done to Primarina and common Tera Fairy Pokemon such as Archaludon and Garchomp.

  • Dazzling Gleam: Dazzling Gleam is a reasonable option for OHKOing Hydreigon and dealing huge damage to Garchomp.

  • EV Spread: The given EV spread ensures that maximum HP Ursaluna-B is OHKOed by Tera Grass Energy Ball, while Glimmora will survive Tera Normal Ursaring-B's Silk Scarf-boosted Blood Moon. The Speed EVs let Glimmora outspeed Jolly Ursaluna and Jolly Kingambit, both rare but major threats to it.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependecy - High: Glimmora's awkward defensive typing means Terastallization is often key for surprising common revenge killers like Gholdengo and Ursaluna-B.

  • Grass: Tera Grass is a powerful defensive and offensive option, letting Glimmora tank against foes like Ursaluna-B, Gholdengo, and Primarina while boosting Energy Ball's power.

  • Ground: Tera Ground isn't as amazing as Tera Grass defensively due to retaining the Water-type weakness, but it ensures that Earth Power will now OHKO offensive Gholdengo and deal massive damage to defensive Archaludon.

Meteor Beam.description:
• Meteor Beam is one of the most powerful single-turn attacks in the tier when used in conjunction with Power Herb to remove the charge turn and immediately get a +1 Special Attack increase.

  • Sludge Bomb is a more reliable STAB attack that threatens Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Ogerpon-H. Earth Power provides solid coverage that hits Steel-types like Kingambit and Gholdengo, which its STAB moves fail to hit effectively. Spiky Shield serves as an enhanced Protect that keeps Glimmora safe from damage while damaging foes that target it with contact moves.

  • Glimmora's ability, Toxic Debris, serves as a way of punishing the foe for landing physical attacks on Glimmora by setting a layer of Toxic Spikes on their side.

  • Both Toxic Debris and Spiky Shield discourage foes from targeting Glimmora with physical moves, as the chip damage from either of them can break Focus Sash and allow Glimmora and its teammates to nab KOs that would be missed otherwise.

  • Tera Grass turns Glimmora's Ground and Water weaknesses into resistances while also giving it Rage Powder and Spore immunity. Tera Flying can be used instead to provide Glimmora with a full Ground-type immunity.

  • While there may be some instances where it is better to be cautious in using Meteor Beam, as it can only be used once reliably, Glimmora generally wants to use it as soon as possible to get the Special Attack boost and allow for more powerful attacks on subsequent turns.

  • Prankster Tailwind users like Tornadus and Whimsicott are great teammates for providing immediate speed control to make up for Glimmora's mediocre Speed. Pokemon that outspeed and OHKO Landorus before it can OHKO Glimmora like Ogerpon-W and Chien-Pao are also greatly appreciated partners. Chi-Yu also works well alongside Glimmora, boosting its damage output with Beads of Ruin and using Fire-type moves to hit Steel-types hard.

Focus Sash.description:
• Glimmora's ability, Toxic Debris, discourages physical attackers from attacking it with physical moves. Setting up Toxic Spikes is invaluable against bulky teams, crippling common threats like Ting-Lu, Iron Hands, and Diancie.

  • Stealth Rock allows Glimmora to break Tornadus's and Chien-Pao's Focus Sash and punishes switches; the cumulated chip damage from both Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes is not to be underestimated, especially against snow teams and Pokemon weak to Stealth Rock like Incineroar without Heavy-Duty Boots and Ogerpon-H.

  • Glimmora setting Toxic Spikes and Stealth Rock makes it the best partner for Chien-Pao + Dragonite teams, putting a lot of Pokemon in range of Extreme Speed and weakening Iron Hands, Diancie, and Incineroar, which are difficult for the core to remove. Ting-Lu is another great Pokemon to use in combination with Glimmora, as its great bulk and access to Whirlwind make the most out of the entry hazards set by Glimmora.

  • Roaring Moon is a great partner for Glimmora, threatening Gholdengo and setting Tailwind, which allows Glimmora to outspeed Ogerpon formes and Gholdengo. Tornadus is another great partner for the same reason.

  • Earth Power OHKOes opposing Glimmora, chips Iron Hands and Incineroar, and 2HKOes Gholdengo, the latter of which is the main way to remove Glimmora without triggering Toxic Debris and is a great threat to Chien-Pao + Dragonite teams.

  • Sludge Bomb greatly threatens Grass-types, notably OHKOing Ogerpon-W after Stealth Rock damage and 2HKOing Assault Vest Rillaboom, which would otherwise pressure Ting-Lu and Landorus. Power Gem is an alternative to Sludge Bomb that allows Glimmora to hit Tornadus harder and deal damage to Landorus.

  • Spiky Shield allows for additional chip damage and helps to preserve Focus Sash against Fake Out. Mortal Spin removes entry hazards and can be useful to poison Pokemon when Toxic Spikes are not set yet.

  • Focus Sash allows Glimmora to always take a hit, making sure it can set Stealth Rock or threaten Pokemon like Gholdengo and Ogerpon-W.

  • Glimmora's Timid nature makes sure that it is faster than maximum Speed Gholdengo and Speed ties against opposing Glimmora.

  • Poison-types like opposing Glimmora, Okidogi, and Amoonguss can easily remove Toxic Spikes by entering the field, so Earth Power from Landorus and Bleakwind Storm from Tornadus can help remove those Pokemon before Glimmora sets Toxic Spikes.

  • Tera Grass flips Glimmora’s Ground and Water weaknesses into resistances, letting it survive Landorus’s Earth Power and Ogerpon-W’s Ivy Cudgel while also taking neutral damage from Gholdengo’s Make It Rain. It additionally enables Glimmora to bypass Rage Powder from Sinistcha. Tera Flying, while giving Glimmora less resistances, lets it gain a Ground immunity, which allows it to preserve the Focus Sash against Landorus's Ground-type attacks and helps stall Trick Room turns against Ursaluna.

Entry Hazard Support (Rock).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

anythinggoes.overview: Glimmora is one of the best suicide leads, utilizing Stealth Rock and Spikes to pressure opposing Pokemon with chip damage and enabling teammates to secure KOs more leisurely. Glimmora's Poison typing allows it to clear Toxic Spikes set by Eternatus, opposing Glimmora, and Gliscor, which are usually incredibly threatening to the hyper offense teams Glimmora is found on. Finally, Glimmora's Toxic Debris ability deters attacks from Pokemon like Koraidon, Arceus, and Ho-Oh. However, although Glimmora is an excellent lead, it struggles against faster Substitute Pokemon like Tera Flying Zacian-C and Eternatus, causing tough situations that can be very hard to recover from.
anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Power Gem could be considered because it does significant damage to Ho-Oh, yet Ho-Oh does not frequently stay in against Glimmora, thus rendering it useless the vast majority of the time. Glimmora could also consider using Toxic, which chips down walls and sweeps faster than regular poison. Sludge Bomb could also be used over Memento, hitting Hatterene and Arceus-Fairy, but once again, it isn't ideal due to the moves mentioned in the above set being much more important.

Checks and Counters

Eternatus: Eternatus's Poison typing allows it to absorb the Toxic Spikes Glimmora sets while 2HKOing Glimmora with Dynamax Cannon and taking minimal damage from Mud Shot.

Deoxys-S: Deoxys-S leads threatens to break Glimmora's Focus Sash with Psycho Boost while also threatening to use Taunt, putting Glimmora in an unfavorable situation.

Hatterene: Hatterene's Magic Bounce makes it a profound threat to Glimmora hyper offense teams. However, it still needs to be cautious about the extremely niche but usable Sludge Bomb.

Substitute Tera Flying Zacian-C: Substitute Tera Flying Zacian-C is an excellent counterlead to Glimmora, as it is unaffected by Mud Shot after Terastallization and can potentially sweep after a Swords Dance boost, all while behind its Substitute.

Suicide Lead.description:
Spikes is Glimmora's most reliable entry hazard, chipping Koraidon, Zacian-C, Ting-Lu, and various Arceus formes. Alternatively, Stealth Rock hits targets like Landorus-T and Giratina-O, yet many Pokemon weak to Stealth Rock run Heavy-Duty Boots, so Spikes is the superior option the majority of the time. Memento allows Glimmora to disallow many sweepers like Calm Mind Tera Poison Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Ground, and Covert Cloak Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM from setting up, while Dazzling Gleam discourages Swords Dance Koraidon from setting up. Mud Shot stops setup attempts from powerful sweepers like Nasty Plot Calyrex-S and Zacian-C, letting Glimmora's teammates safely enter the field. Mortal Spin removes hazards from Glimmora's side, in particular Ribombee's Sticky Web, making it an effective counterlead against Sticky Web teams. In addition, Mortal Spin poisons frequent targets like Ting-Lu, various Arceus formes, and Ho-Oh, putting them on a timer and making a potential sweep far easier. Glimmora's EV spread allows it to survive five Scale Shot hits from Jolly Koraidon and four Scale Shot hits from Adamant Koraidon. Tera Ghost disallows Rapid Spin users like Iron Treads from clearing hazards, while Tera Steel stops opposing Glimmora from using Mortal Spin. Tera Flying offers Glimmora immunity to Ground-type moves, in particular opposing Glimmora's Mud Shot.

Due to Glimmora being a suicide lead exclusively used on hyper offense teams, potent sweepers like Arceus, Scale Shot Koraidon, and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground appreciate the entry hazards that Glimmora sets, which wear down their main checks in defensive Arceus formes. Furthermore, Calyrex-S also works very well with Glimmora, as one of its main checks in Ting-Lu does not usually hold Heavy-Duty Boots, making Ting-Lu vulnerable to Glimmora's hazards. Glimmora is also frequently used on Grimmsnarl dual screens teams, where Glimmora discourages Ribombee leads while providing valuable hazards.

nu.overview: Houndstone establishes itself in NU as an incredibly reliable spinblocker and defensive presence, being able to prevent Rapid Spin from the likes of Tsareena while taking on dangerous attackers such as Flamigo and Scyther effortlessly. Houndstone is able to utilize its switch-in opportunities to generate progress via Night Shade, Roar, or Will-O-Wisp. Houndstone primarily struggles with its unreliable recovery options, as it has to either use the passive Rest or the inconsistent Pain Split. Houndstone also struggles immensely with special attackers like Munkidori and Meloetta, as they can take advantage of its weaker Special Defense for massive damage. Unless it is running Body Press, Houndstone is vunerable to Dark-types such as Incineroar and Scrafty, which can use Knock Off to remove its item and potentially use it as setup fodder if it is not running Roar.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Protect can be used to allow Houndstone to gain even more Leftovers healing, though this may not fit into its moveset. Assault Vest can be used to turn Houndstone into a decent special tank, though it thrives off its utility movepool, and this set has no recovery options. Air Balloon alongside Thief can be used on Houndstone to allow it to steal an opponents item. However, Thief must be used with caution so that Houndstone doesn't accidentally cripple itself with a Choice-item or Life Orb, and often, it prefers running other moves like Body Press, Roar, and Pain Split. Tera Poison can be used to prevent Houndstone from being poisoned from the likes of Overqwil and Amoonguss while giving it a Fairy resistance to check Sylveon.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Dark-types such as Wo-Chien, Incineroar, and Scrafty are a pain for Houndstone to deal with, as they can use Knock Off to remove it's item. Additionally, the latter two force Houndstone out for fear of being set up on. However, they do have to be careful of Body Press, which can significantly damage them.

Fire-types: Fire-types such as Incineroar, Paldean Tauros-F, Chandelure, and Infernape can all hit Houndstone for large damage due to Fluffy doubling the power of Fire-type attacks. They can also easily switch into Will-O-Wisp from Houndstone, with Chandelure in particular getting a Flash Fire boost from it.

Special Attackers: Special attackers such as Chandelure, Munkidori, and Raikou can all hit Houndstone for considerable damage on its weaker special side, and due to Houndstone's passivity, and they are not immediately threatened in return.

Offensive Spinblocker.description:
Play Rough lets Houndstone take out foes like Flygon and Paldean Tauros-W while ensuring Scrafty can't take advantage of it. Alternatively, Body Press allows Houndstone to put its Defense investment to good use to target Scrafty as well as switch-ins like Incineroar, Copperajah, and Dudunsparce. Shadow Sneak lets Houndstone pick off weakened, frail foes such as Munkidori, Tornadus, and Flamigo. Pain Split uses Houndstone's low HP to punish and capitalize on foes with reliable recovery. Notably, it helps Houndstone spinblock Tsareena more consistently. The given EV spread allows Houndstone to outspeed Klefki while maximizing, firstly, its Attack and, secondly, Body Press's power, notably 2HKOing offensive Incineroar, and it means Houndstone can simultaneously be bulky while healing as much as possible with Pain Split. Tera Fairy ensures Houndstone maintains its matchup against Fighting- and Dragon-types like Heracross, Goodra, and Flygon; gives it a resistance to Incineroar's Knock Off; and boosts Play Rough so that Houndstone can OHKO Flygon and, after a bit of chip damage, Paldean Tauros-W as well. Tera Fighting powers up Body Press to ensure a 2HKO on defensive Incineroar, and it gifts Houndstone a useful resistance to Dark-type moves such as Knock Off. Tera Dark works better to slow down Ghost-types like Decidueye and Chandelure while still offering a resistance to Knock Off. However, opting for Tera Dark leaves Houndstone more easily beaten by the same Fighting-type foes it once checked like Toxicroak and Paldean Tauros-W while being significantly worn down by U-turn. Heavy-Duty Boots lightens the pressure on Houndstone's team to remove entry hazards, allowing them to set even more hazards and consequently increase its efficacy. Weakness Policy takes advantage of Houndstone's increased bulk from Fluffy to let it become a reverse sweeper after getting hit by a Knock Off either from a Fighting-type like Heracross or a foe like Tsareena.

Houndstone's main job is to stop spinners like Tsareena. Because of this, it synergizes greatly with entry hazard setters like Spikes Gligar and Klefki as well as Stealth Rock Duraludon, Copperajah, and Rhyperior. In return, especially for the last three, Houndstone acts as an offensive check to Fighting-types like Flamigo, Heracross, and Scrafty. Calm Mind users such as Sylveon and Uxie are great at capitalizing on and pressuring bulkier foes that Houndstone can struggle to break through like defensive Tsareena, Vaporeon, and Dudunsparce. In a similar vein, Houndstone appreciates Knock Off users like Gligar, Swampert, and Copperajah, since they can draw in Tsareena, allowing the combination of hazards plus Houndstone's Poltergeist to overwhelm it. Speed control in the form of Heavy-Duty Boots users like Munkidori and Ambipom as well as Choice Scarf Flamigo can circumvent hazards, which is necessary on Spikes stacking teams using Houndstone, as its Speed is quite low. Houndstone flails against Normal- and Dark-types like Dudunsparce, Overqwil, and Incineroar, so partners that can take advantage of them such as Scrafty, Rhyperior, and Paldean Tauros-F complement it quite well. In addition, Houndstone appreciates the latter two being able to take a Fire-type attack in a pinch. However, bulkier Fire-resistant teammates such as Vaporeon, Goodra, Incineroar, and Rhyperior work better to switch into dangerous foes like opposing Incineroar, Chandelure, and Salazzle.

Defensive.description:
Set Details

Roar allows Houndstone to phaze setup sweepers such as Flygon and Scyther while also causing entry hazard damage against a new foe. Will-O-Wisp can be used to cripple physical attackers that otherwise might beat Houndstone such as Drednaw and Rhyperior. Houndstone can use the combination of RestTalk, allowing it to consistently handle foes such as Flygon, Rhyperior, and Paldean Tauros-W. Pain Split can be used to free up a moveslot on Houndstone while also working exceptionally well on high-HP targets such as Vaporeon and Copperajah. Body Press allows Houndstone to hit common Dark-types such as Incineroar and Scrafty for big damage. Rocky Helmet deals chip damage against Pokemon such as Flygon and Flamigo, Heavy-Duty Boots allows Houndstone to ignore entry hazards to take on Pokemon such as Scyther more easily, and Leftovers can help keep Houndstone healthy over the course of the game. Tera Water lets Houndstone resist Water-type attacks from Pokemon such as Basculegion-M and Paldean Tauro-W while also resisting Fire-type attacks from Incineroar and Infernape. Tera Fighting boosts the power of Body Press while also giving Houndstone a Dark resistance that helps it against Overqwil and Scrafty. Tera Fairy makes Houndstone immune to Dragon-type attacks from the likes of Flygon, allows it to resist Dark-type moves, and still lets it easily take on Fighting-types such as Paldean Tauros-W, Flamigo, and Hariyama.

Houndstone primarily fits on bulky offense and balance teams, particularly Spike stack teams, as they heavily appreciate its ability to check Pokemon such as Flamigo and Basculegion-M while also stopping Rapid Spin from Tsareena. Entry hazard setters such as Klefki, Rhyperior, and Gligar pair well with Houndstone because they appreciate its reliability in keeping up hazards against teams that rely on Rapid Spin. In return, Houndstone appreciates the passive chip damage against checks such as Flamigo and Flygon. Hazard removal options such as Tsareena and Cramorant are heavily appreciated by Houndstone, as they can allow Rocky Helmet or Leftovers variants to stay healthy over the course of a game. Special walls such as Copperajah and Goodra pair extremely well with Houndstone, as they love its ability to check common physical attackers such as Flamigo and Paldean Tauros-W. They can then handle special attackers that Houndstone might struggle with such as Munkidori and Chandelure. Due to Fluffy doubling the power of Fire-type attacks, Houndstone can immensely struggle against Pokemon such as Chandelure and Incineroar. Therefore, Fire-resistant Pokemon such as Vaporeon, Altaria, and Incineroar are especially appreciated. Wish passers such as Vaporeon and Sylveon are great for Houndstone. Wish can help keep Houndstone healthy without having to use the unreliable Rest or Pain Split, and Houndstone can check powerful wallbreakers the wish passers might otherwise struggle with such as Choice Band Flamigo and Rhyperior. Fighting-types such as Paldean Tauros-F, Scrafty, and Toxicroak can help take on Dark-types that Houndstone commonly struggles with like Overqwil and Wo-Chien, and in return, Houndstone can help with Pokemon they can struggle against such as Flamigo.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Flamigo works nicely alongside Earthquake users like Ursaluna and Garchomp, threatening the Grass-types that can easily take on Earthquake while also being immune to it. Redirection can help keep Flamigo away from attacks, considering its fragility.

  • Ursaluna and Garchomp can easily threaten Electabuzz and Magmar, which redirect Flamigo's attacks away from Pokemon Flamigo is meant to threaten like Gholdengo. The aforementioned Ground-types can also avoid redirection with Earthquake. Porygon2 can hit Flying-types with Ice Beam and Thunderbolt. Gholdengo can threaten Fairy-types like Sylveon and Hatterene, which resist Flamigo's Close Combat.

  • Multi-hit moves like Scale Shot from Dragonite are a major issue, as they can OHKO Flamigo through Focus Sash. These multi-hit moves can be redirected with the help of Amoonguss, while the damage can be mitigated with Intimidate from Incineroar.

Strategy Comments

  • Flamigo's main role is to be a wallbreaker that can threaten top Pokemon like Gholdengo and Incineroar. Flamigo really shines when against Steel-types like Gholdengo and Kingambit, threatening them with Close Combat.

  • Flamigo is meant to be brought first, but it can be saved in certain matchups, such as the Psychic-type spam matchup, since Wide Guard is able to deny Expanding Force and Eruption from foes such as Indeedee-M and Hisuian Typhlosion, respectively.

  • Faster Pokemon like Dragapult are some of the biggest threats to Flamigo, as they can bring Flamigo down to Focus Sash or double target Flamigo and KO it. Physically bulky Pokemon such as Dondozo can also be an issue, as they can take hits and deal good damage back. Bulky Flying-types like Dragonite and Corviknight can take on attacks from Flamigo while hitting hard back. Powerful special attackers like Gholdengo can take down the physically bulky foes. Electric- and Ice-type attacks like Thunderbolt and Ice Beam from Porygon2 can threaten these Flying-types, while Clear Smog Amoonguss does well into Dondozo.

Glass Cannon.description:
• Flamigo both hits hard and is decently fast, doing particularly well into threats such as Incineroar, Gholdengo, and Sneasler thanks to its ability Scrappy and good offensive typing.

  • Dual Wingbeat is a respectably strong attack that is able to OHKO Pokemon through Focus Sash, notably Sneasler. Brave Bird is able to pick up OHKOes onto Pokemon such as Rillaboom and is more consistent than Dual Wingbeat, but it breaks Flamigo's own Focus Sash, leaving it vulnerable to attacks. Wide Guard can protect Flamigo and its partners from powerful spread attacks like Eruption from Hisuian Typhlosion, Make It Rain from Gholdengo, and Expanding Force from the likes of Indeedee-M and Hatterene.

  • Focus Sash allows Flamigo to guarantee surviving at least one attack, which is especially useful with its low bulk and the stat drops from Close Combat.

  • Tera Ghost lets Flamigo ignore Fake Out, being able to OHKO many sturdy threats such as Rillaboom and Incineroar without being at risk of their partner's attack. Tera Ghost also stops Extreme Speed from knocking out Flamigo when its health has been lowered, as well as preventing Extreme Speed and Fake Out from breaking Focus Sash. Tera Stellar increases Flamigo's damage output, notably OHKOing Archaludon with Close Combat.

nu.overview: Flamigo's unique offensive typing and access to U-turn to pivot make it stand out from the other Fighting-types in NU. Scrappy allows Flamigo to hit Ghost-types like Chandelure and Hisuian Typhlosion as well as Tera Ghost users like Cinccino, Inteleon, and Ambipom, which would usually block its Close Combat. Choice Scarf allows Flamigo to consistently revenge kill faster threats like Inteleon, Kilowattrel, and Tornadus, while Choice Band gives Flamigo the ability to 2HKO defensive tanks like Galarian Slowbro and Vaporeon with entry hazard support. However, faster Choice Scarf users, such as Flygon and Munkidori, threaten and can easily revenge kill Flamigo with their STAB attacks. Additionally, Flamigo’s STAB attacks can be easily played around thanks to it being Choice-locked and its STAB moves inviting common switch-ins like Galarian Slowbro, Bronzong, and Gligar. Flamigo also faces competition from other Fighting-types like Toxicroak, Paldean Tauros-W, and Infernape, since they offer better defensive typings and the ability to run other sets.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Swords Dance Flamigo can use Protective Pads to avoid adverse contact effects such as paralysis from Bellibolt's Static and chip damage from Galarian Slowbro's Rocky Helmet. However, this forces Flamigo to rely on Brave Bird instead of the more reliable Acrobatics, needing to take recoil and, consequently, use Roost constantly, which can make Flamigo more passive than it would prefer.

Checks and Counters

Revenge Killers: Faster threats like Flygon, Munkidori, and Infernape can outspeed Flamigo and KO it or use it for free momentum, but none of them can directly switch in against Flamigo's attacks. Additionally, they all often run Choice Scarf, outspeeding Flamigo's own Choice Scarf sets. Priority users like Basculegion-M, Staraptor, and Decidueye can pick off Flamigo after it has been weakened.

Fairy-types: Sylveon, Florges, and Scream Tail can tank Flamigo's attacks, threaten it back with their STAB attacks, and set up on it. However, the three must be cautious about directly switching into Flamigo's Brave Bird.

Electric-types: Kilowattrel, Raikou, and Bellibolt can destroy Flamigo with their Electric-type attacks, and the former two can outspeed non-Choice Scarf variants. Bellibolt is a common switch in and threatens to cripple Flamigo with Static.

Psychic-types: Fast Psychic-types like Munkidori can outpace and threaten to KO Flamigo. Bulkier Psychic-types like Uxie and Galarian Slowbro can take advantage of Choice-locked Flamigo by using it as free setup fodder, and the former can outspeed Choice Band sets.

Choice Item.description:
Set Details

Flamigo easily forces out Steel-, Fighting-, Grass-, and Dark-types like Copperajah, Paldean Tauros-W, Amoonguss, and Incineroar, which grants it free turns to use Roost, allowing it to maintain longevity and use Brave Bird more often. Throat Chop can be run so that Flamigo can better threaten Bronzong as well as users of sound moves like Sylveon, Scream Tail, and Meloetta. Choice Scarf allows Flamigo to outspeed normally faster Pokemon like Inteleon and Cinccino. Alternatively, Flamigo can run Choice Band, making it a very strong wallbreaker that can overwhelm defensive tanks like Galarian Slowbro, Bellibolt, and Gligar. Tera Fighting gives Close Combat a bit of a push, letting Flamigo pressure foes like Swampert and Vaporeon. Tera Flying, on the other hand, gives Brave Bird an extra power boost, allowing it to 2HKO foes like Overqwil and OHKO Sylveon, Tornadus, or Munkidori with scarf. Tera Electric, however, offers a paralysis immunity, helping its matchup into Prankster Thunder Wave Klefki and Static Bellibolt. Plus, it provides an Electric and Flying resistance for Choice Band sets to pick up a surprise KO on foes like Raikou, Tornadus, and opposing Flamigo.

Choice Band Flamigo pairs greatly with other pivots like Flygon, Munkidori, Incineroar, and Raikou, as they can draw in Amoonguss, Copperajah, opposing Incineroar, and Goodra for it while putting pressure on many of its checks like Scream Tail, Overqwil, Vaporeon, and Gligar. Psychic-types like Munkidori, Uxie, and Meloetta appreciate Flamigo for checking Steel- and Dark-types like Duraludon, Copperajah, Incineroar, and Scrafty; in return, they handle Poison-types like Galarian Slowbro, Munkidori, and Tera Poison Vaporeon. Flamigo appreciates Steel-type teammates like Copperajah, Bronzong, and Klefki for checking Fairy-types such as Sylveon and Scream Tail. The aforementioned Steel-types also help Flamigo handle faster Choice Scarf users like Flygon and Munkidori, since they can easily revenge kill them. Choice Scarf Flamigo synergizes greatly with special wallbreakers like Nasty Plot Munkidori, Throat Spray Dudunsparce, Calm Mind or Choice Specs Chandelure, and Choice Specs Inteleon, since they can handle common physically defensive Pokemon like Swampert, Bellibolt, Avalugg, and Gligar. In return, Flamigo can threaten common specially defensive foes like Meloetta, Incineroar, and Goodra.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Flamigo aims to capitalize on passive foes such as Wo-Chien and Swampert to set up and then throw off boosted attacks to break through the opposing team. On balanced teams, Flamigo uses Roost so that it can repeatedly come in regardless of Stealth Rock being up and take advantage of the aforementioned walls, not worrying about their Leech Seed and Knock Off. In contrast, Flamigo runs Agility on hyper offense teams so that it can run through faster teams, outspeeding even Choice Scarf users such as Flygon, Munkidori, and Paldean Tauros-W . Not running an item allows Flamigo to use the drawback-free Acrobatics over the health-wasting Brave Bird, whereas Sitrus Berry eases setup for Flamigo on hyper offense builds while allowing it to still use Acrobatics later. The second EV spread is for Flamigo on hyper offensive teams, as it maximizes its Attack and, after an Agility, allows it to outspeed Speed Booster Energy Scream Tail. Tera Steel lets Flamigo take a hit from Munkidori, Choice Scarf Flamigo, and Sylveon in a pinch so that it can retaliate with an Acrobatics or, in Sylveon's case, capitalize on them better. Alternatively, Tera Electric and Ground give Flamigo an immunity to Klefki's Thunder Wave. However, for a paralysis immunity, Tera Electric is better, as Bellibolt's Static can circumvent Tera Ground. Additionally, Tera Electric lets Flamigo use Kilowattrel as setup fodder and allows it to take a Brave Bird from opposing Flamigo in a pinch. Tera Ground offers a full immunity to Electric-type moves from Kilowattrel and Bellibolt, though, meaning Flamigo won't be getting constantly chipped like it would be with Tera Electric.

Flamigo's biggest enemy is Bellibolt, and because of this, it appreciates any way to wear it down, whether that be through entry hazard stacking with aid from setters such as Spikes Klefki, Duraludon, and Swampert as well as Stealth Rock Flygon, in tandem with Knock Off users like Incineroar and Cinccino, or by checking it with Ground-types like Gligar, Flygon, and Swampert. Pivots like Munkidori, Cinccino, Basculegion-M, and Flygon pair well with Roost Flamigo, bringing in Steel- and Grass-type foes like Copperajah, Wo-Chien, and Amoonguss, which it can take advantage of. Flamigo's middling Speed leads it to rely on partners like Rhyperior, Bronzong, and Bellibolt on balance teams so that it can better position itself around common offensive threats like Kilowattrel, Munkidori, and Tornadus. Double Dance Flamigo sets love dual screens Klefki as well as Aurora Veil Alolan Ninetales, since they help lessen the burden on Flamigo's bulk to survive turns as it sets up. On these dual screens teams, partners often are fellow setup sweepers such as Flygon, Munkidori, Scream Tail, and Cinccino. Flygon and Munkidori can capitalize on Bellibolt and Galarian Slowbro, which Flamigo often falls against; Flygon, Ambipom, and Cinccino can work in tandem with Flamigo to chip away at walls like Gligar, Swampert, and Duraludon; and Dudunsparce and Scream Tail can nail physically defensive Pokemon such as Gligar and Bellibolt for Flamigo while it takes care of special walls like Gastrodon and Copperajah for them.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to the next generation of Battle Stadium Singles! In this new and exciting metagame, new ideas are constantly developing, so this analysis will constantly be updated to reflect metagame trends.

If you feel this analysis is not up to date, feel free to check out the thread for this Pokemon and post suggestions. For more resources on Series 1 in general, check out this thread.

Scrappy Choice Item.description:
• Scrappy gives Flamigo a unique niche, letting it throw out powerful Close Combats that are unsafe for Gholdengo and Dragapult to take!

  • Throat Chop is a decent filler move, letting Flamigo shut down Sylveon's Hyper Voice and Skeledirge's Torch Song. Note that Close Combat still does more damage to most Ghost-types.

  • Tailwind is a filler move that gives Flamigo's team some extreme speed control before it goes down.

Tera Types

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting lets Flamigo fully take advantage of Scrappy, giving Choice Scarf sets a 81.3% chance to OHKO offensive Dragapult.

  • Fire: Tera Fire makes Flamigo immune to Will-O-Wisp, letting Choice Band sets more easily break through Skeledirge, and gives Flamigo the option to 2HKO Corviknight with Tera Blast.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: With Choice Scarf, Flamigo outspeeds major threats such as Dragapult and Hydreigon, making it a more effective late-game cleaner.

  • Choice Band: Choice Band lets Flamigo deal massive damage, giving it a shot at 2HKOing Skeledirge with Close Combat.

Belly Drum.description:
Cetitan's unique combination of Slush Rush and Belly Drum make it a great snow sweeper for Ice teams. Cetitan is able to use Belly Drum in combination with Slush Rush to boost its Attack and Speed to some of the highest in the tier. Icicle Crash is Cetitan's best way of attacking, shredding most foes that aim to stand in its way. Ice Shard is used to pick off the few Choice Scarf users that outspeed Cetitan, such as Meowscarada, Enamorus, and Flutter Mane. Earthquake is useful for hitting the Steel-, Water- and Fire-types that resist Icicle Crash and Ice Shard, such as Heatran, Toxapex, and Ceruledge. Sitrus Berry is used to restore some of Cetitan's HP after Belly Drum, increasing its longevity.

Since Cetitan needs snow to be able to fulfill its role, Alolan Ninetales is a mandatory teammate. Not only can Alolan Ninetales provide snow support, but it can also provide Aurora Veil support, further helping Cetitan stay on the field. Since Cetitan opts to use Sitrus Berry instead of Heavy-Duty Boots, teammates that can remove entry hazards are great support, such as Avalugg and Alolan Sandslash. Avalugg serves better as a dedicated defensive wall, while Alolan Sandslash can also take advantage of Slush Rush, Swords Dance, and Knock Off. Kyurem is excellent at dealing with Unaware walls that would otherwise ignore Cetitan's Belly Drum boost; it is able to use Freeze-Dry and defeat walls such as Quagsire and Dondozo while also having access to Earth Power, which defeats Skeledirge. Mamoswine is a good teammate, as it can provide hazard support to break Focus Sash and secure OHKOs on targets such as Corviknight, as well as soften the blow from Fire-type attacks.

Cetitan, with its combination of Slush Rush and Belly Drum, is an exceptional wallbreaker and setup sweeper for Ice teams. Normalium Z allows Cetitan to use Z-Belly Drum, which gives it easier setup opportunities. Icicle Crash is the preferred STAB move because of its higher Base Power and the ability to ignore contact effects like Skarmory's Rocky Helmet and Ferrothorn's Iron Barbs; alternatively, the weaker Ice Spinner can be used for its higher accuracy. Earthquake targets Steel- and Fire-types like Gholdengo, Archaludon, Heatran, and Victini as well as Toxapex. Alternatively, Knock Off provides Cetitan with a way to threaten Slowbro and Rotom-W. Ice Shard, after a Belly Drum boost, allows Cetitan to pick off Choice Scarf foes like Sneasler and Iron Boulder, which outspeed it even in snow. A Jolly nature can also be used to allow Cetitan to outspeed Choice Scarf users like Blacephalon, Iron Moth, and Iron Treads in snow. Alolan Ninetales is an essential teammate for its ability to set snow and provide Aurora Veil support, facilitating Cetitan's sweeping capabilities. Kyurem and Alolan Ninetales also break through bulky Water-types like Slowbro and Rotom-W, which Cetitan may struggle against. With entry hazard support from Piloswine and Cloyster, Cetitan can OHKO threats like Skarmory, Corviknight, and Ferrothorn. Furthermore, Cloyster also provides hazard removal with Rapid Spin, increasing Cetitan's longevity.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • The sweeper set tends to be strong on hyper offensive teams that can force trades, weakening Dondozo's checks into range of its attacks.
