  • 236 HP / 76 Attack / 4 Def / 12 SpD / 180 Spe with Jolly: This spread OHKOes up to Hippowdon with Final Gambit, while outspeeding Jolly Dragonite, and outspeeding Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle after a Speed drop from Rock Tomb. The Special Defense EVs dodge a OHKO from Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

  • 252 HP / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Jolly: Beyond at least reaching a speedtie with opposing Annihilape, this spread avoids a OHKO from Timid Flutter Mane's unboosted Moonblast and even outspeeds paralyzed Speed boosted Flutter Mane. It also outspeeds paralyzed Iron Bundle after Booster Energy, but note that it often uses Substitute to block Fling.

Bulk Up.description:
• Thanks to great bulk and the dangerous Rage Fist, Annihilape is a powerful bulky setup sweeper of Battle Stadium Singles.

  • Taunt: Taunt helps you deal with annoying support Pokemon like Whirlwind Ting-Lu, Thunder Wave Archaludon, and Hippowdon to mention a few, forcing them to attack and boost Rage Fist. This can work on Toxapex, but be warned that Toxapex commonly carries Mental Herb, which could get Annihilape poisoned if it doesn't Terastallize.

  • Encore: Encore is an interesting alternative to Taunt, not able to directly shut down defensive answers to Annihilape, but it severely punishes them when Annihilape switches into a support move.

  • Defiant versus Vital Spirit: Defiant is the best option for this set, stopping Charm Flutter Mane from eeking out a win, and punishing common ways of dropping Annihilape's Attack such as Intimidate Landorus-T and Breaking Swipe Gouging Fire. Vital Spirit is easier to stop, but, it lets Annihilape can absorb sleep moves from foes like Yawn Ursaluna-B, Yawn Hippowdon, and Spore Breloom without needing Taunt.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Terastallization is quite helpful at saving Annihilape from certain extremely powerful wallbreakers such as Chien-Pao, Chi-Yu, and Flutter Mane, but Annihilape is perfectly functional without it.

  • Poison: Tera Poison offers a better matchup against Flutter Mane, does well against Meowscarada's Flower Trick, and lets Annihilape freely switch into Toxic and Toxic Spikes later in the match. This also drastically reduces the risk of Taunting Toxapex, which makes this Tera type a menace against stall teams!

  • Fire: In addition to giving a useful resistance to Fairy-, Fire-, and Ice-type attacks from dangerous foes like Flutter Mane, Ogerpon-H, and Chien-Pao, Tera Fire also protects Annihilape from burns.

  • Water: Tera Water is a fantastic response to Urshifu-R, who otherwise can use Tera Water Surging Strikes to break through Annihilape regardless of Bulk Up boosts. It also works great against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, two powerful wallbreakers.

  • Steel: Steel turns Annihilape's Psychic , Flying,and Fairy weakness into resistances, as well as being an excellent defensive type overall. It lets Annihilape deal with foes like Flutter Mane, Latios, and Iron Crown far more effectively at the cost of having issues with Ogerpon-H and Urshifu formes.

  • Flying: Flying is an effective Tera against stall teams for avoiding Fissure from Dondozo , forcing it to attack with moves that boost Rage Fist.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers's residual recovery eases the long-game of setting up.

  • Sitrus Berry and 244 HP EVs: Reducing the HP EVs to 244 gives Annihilape an even HP stat, which lets Annihilape recover its health with Sitrus Berry the moment it gets hit by Ruination. This makes dealing with Ting-Lu and Wo-Chien an easier task.

  • Covert Cloak: Covert Cloak makes Annihilape immune to being Salt Cured, making it a great check against Garganacl if using Taunt to prevent the deadly Tera Ghost Curse. It also gives peace of mind, avoiding potential flinches from Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, or Special Defense drops from Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Jolly: Maximum Speed mainly helps Annihilape outspeed Timid Archaludon, Timid Gholdengo, Adamant Urshifu formes, and Modest Chi-Yu. The 4 Special Defense EVs are just enough to avoid being OHKOed by Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

  • 252 HP / 244 SpD / 12 Spe with Careful: More special bulk can make it much more difficult for special attackers such as Flutter Mane and Chi-Yu to revenge kill Annihilape. This spread in particular has a 62.5% chance of surviving Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

  • 244 HP / 164 Def / 100 SpD with Careful: This EV spread avoids an OHKO from +2 Chien-Pao, which can be especially helpful with Covert Cloak blocking the flinch chance.

  • 252 HP / 156 SpD / 100 Spe with Careful: This EV spread outspeeds Adamant Breloom while still giving Annihilape good special bulk.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Thanks to Final Gambit and a decent Speed stat, Choice Scarf Annihilape can cause shocking upsets by revenge killing even bulky sweepers, such as Dragonite and Gouging Fire!

  • Shadow Claw versus Rage Fist: Shadow Claw is weak, but it's a reliable Ghost-type STAB move that can reliably OHKO offensive Flutter Mane even when using minimum Attack investment. Rage Fist is still preferred for being the more flexible option though, letting Annihilape potentially clean a weakened team if Final Gambit doesn't work out.

  • Defiant: While Vital Spirit's Sleep immunity increases Annihilape's switch-in potential, Defiant is the better ability for protecting it from being set up on by Charm Flutter Mane.

  • U-turn U-turn turns Annihilape into a reasonable pivot and gets it out of unpredictable lead situations against unpredictable early-game offensive foes like Chien-Pao and Dragonite, though this will often lead your opponent to assume Annihilape is holding Choice Scarf even against naturally slower Pokemon.

  • Stealth Rock: Stealth Rock is risky on a Choice Scarf Pokemon, but it can be useful early-game if Annihilape leads against foes it commonly scares out like Ting-Lu.

  • Encore: Encore is an emergency way to punish set-up Pokemon Annihilape can switch into, such as Dragonite and Urshifu-S.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Since Annihilape often sacrifices itself with Final Gambit, Terastallization should only be done if Final Gambit isn't the path to winning the match, and is usually better with Rage Fist's increased late-game potential.

  • Water: Tera Water stops Choice Scarf Urshifu-R from OHKOing Annihilape with Tera Water Surging Strikes, potentially turning a check into a sweeping vector with the now 200 BP Rage Fist!

  • Steel: Tera Steel covers Annihilape's weakness to Fairy, Psychic, and Flying, all weaknesses that some potentially faster Speed boosted threats like Booster Energy Flutter Mane, Choice Scarf Landorus-T, and Choice Scarf Latios seek to exploit.

  • Normal: Tera Normal gives Annihilape an immunity to Ghost-type attacks, potentially getting it a revenge kill against a bulky Flutter Mane it wouldn't otherwise.

  • Ghost: While not very useful defensively, Tera Ghost seriously juices up Rage Fist's late-game sweeping potential, while still maintaining an important Normal-type priority immunity against Dragonite, Ogerpon-H, and Entei.

Assault Vest.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • 252 HP / 76 Atk / 180 Spe with Jolly: This spread outspeeds Jolly Dragonite and survives Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

  • 244 HP / 196 SpD / 68 Spe with Careful: This survives Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera-boosted Moonblast on all but the highest damage roll, while outspeeding Jolly Ogerpon formes after a Speed drop from Rock Tomb.

Bulk Up.description:
• Annihilape is a solid setup sweeper due to its good Attack stat, decent bulk, and unresisted STAB combination. It can take advantage of Pokemon such as Corviknight, Blissey, and Clodsire.
  • Bulk Up gives Annihilape the potential to sweep while also making it progressively harder to KO.
  • Taunt allows Annihilape to stay healthy and also stops bulkier Pokemon such as Corviknight, Clodsire, and Toxapex from recovering their health. Rest can alternatively be used with Chesto Berry to get rid of status and recover health, but it fails when Electric Terrain is up.
  • Drain Punch allows Annihilape to recover health and damage foes such as Ting-Lu and Iron Treads.
  • Rage Fist, along with Taunt, makes Annihilape incredibly threatening for slow walls such as Dondozo and Ting-Lu, as their attacks do little damage to Annilhilape while also boosting Rage Fist's power.
  • Tera Water allows Annihilape to take hits from special attackers such as Iron Bundle, Chi-Yu, and Flutter Mane while also letting it resist Flare Blitz from Koraidon.
  • Tera Fairy gives Annihilape an immunity against Dragon-type moves from Koraidon and Miraidon while also letting Annihilape take neutral damage from Ghost-type moves from Gholdengo and Flutter Mane, OHKOing them in return with boosted Rage Fist.
  • Annihilape reaches its full potential on dual screens hyper offense teams, where it can easily take hits while setting up.
  • Special walls such as Ting-Lu and Corviknight are good teammates on balance teams, as Pokemon such as Miraidon, Flutter Mane, and Iron Bundle threaten Annihilape. Corviknight is also able to remove entry hazards for Annihilape. Kingambit as a teammate overwhelms Alomomola and Skeledirge, which are common checks to it and Annihilape.
  • Entry hazard setters such as Glimmora, Froslass, Toxapex, and Clodsire can lure in Corviknight, presenting Annhilape with a great setup opportunity by forcing Corviknight to either use Defog and activate Annihilape's Defiant or give Rage Fist a boost by attacking.

Unaware.description:
Clodsire is an entry hazard setter that can act as a defensive switch-in to both Thundurus formes, halting their momentum from Volt Switch. Toxic more reliably punishes Latios and Donphan, while Poison Jab allows it to still threaten Taunt Hydreigon. Clodsire often finds opportunities to set Stealth Rock or stack multiple layers of Spikes thanks to its bulk. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Clodsire routinely switch in without accumulating hazard damage. Clodsire can act as a great blanket check to special-attacking setup sweepers such as Calm Mind Sinistcha and Nasty Plot Hydreigon thanks to Unaware. 84 Defense EVs let it switch in on Life Orb Scizor, while 176 Special Defense EVs and a Careful nature allow it to reliably tank Earth Power from Booster Energy Iron Jugulis and Hydro Pump from uninvested Rotom-Wash. The Special Defense investment also lets it avoid being 2HKOed by Draco Meteor from Soul Dew Latios when using Tera Dark. Tera Dark helps Clodsire against Soul Dew Latios by providing an immunity to Luster Purge and Psychic Noise. It also removes Clodsire's Water weakness, improving its matchup against Greninja and Rotom-Wash.

Clodsire is often found on stall and semi-stall teams. Mandibuzz is a reliable wall that can switch in on Earthquake from Excadrill and Donphan as well as Luster Purge from Choice-locked Latios, while Clodsire covers for Mandibuzz's weakness to Thundurus. Blissey alleviates Clodsire's weakness to Choice Specs users and heavy-hitting special attackers like Hydrapple, Greninja, and Latios. Skarmory can be an Earthquake-immune teammate that also helps to wall Metagross. Together, Clodsire and Skarmory can form an entry hazard-stacking core with Stealth Rock and Spikes. Clodsire appreciates Toxapex for checking Scizor and Keldeo simultaneously.

ubers.overview: Clodsire, despite its low base stat total, has a niche in Ubers thanks to the large amount of role compression it offers. Along with Ting-Lu and Arceus-Ground, Clodsire is one of the main checks to Miraidon. Compared to them, Clodsire sports both reliable recovery and the ability to run an item. Thanks to Water Absorb, Clodsire is also a decent check to Kyogre, and due to its Poison typing, it can absorb and set Toxic Spikes. However, Clodsire certainly suffers from being a "jack of a trades, master of none"; its low bulk compared to other Miraidon checks leaves it having to use Recover more often than not, which can make it a large momentum drain. This low bulk leaves Clodsire reliant on Terastallization to check certain setup Miraidon and Kyogre sets. It also has a pathetic offensive presence, relying on Toxic alone to dissuade switch-ins. It's critical to use Clodsire for its great role compression to free up the rest of its teammates to gain more momentum.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Poison Jab is an alternative to Toxic that can still inflict poison while being usable under Taunt. Mental Herb allows Clodsire to avoid Taunt, which is often used against it from Miraidon. Ideally, this will let Clodsire set up entry hazards early-game, but it comes at the risk of Clodsire being easily worn down by Spikes damage. Counter is a niche option that may catch physical attackers off guard. Unaware might seem tempting to use against boosting Miraidon, but it also means Draco Meteor remains full power against Clodsire. It also loses Clodsire's valuable matchup against Kyogre.

Checks and Counters

Poison-immune Pokemon: Clodsire's main way to threaten switch-ins is through Toxic, so Pokemon immune to Toxic can easily take advantage of it. Necrozma-DM and Gliscor are the most prominent examples, but other Pokemon such as Corviknight and Skarmory exist as well. Giratina-O may use Tera Steel on Clodsire to Defog on it with impunity.

Taunt: Without a Mental Herb, Clodsire is nearly completely shut down by Taunt. Commonly, Miraidon may use Taunt against Clodsire after it switches-in on Draco Meteor to prevent Recover, though this does put Miraidon at risk of being hit by Earthquake. Other Taunt users such as Arceus-Fairy have little to fear from Clodsire.

Heavy-Duty Boots: Outside of Toxic, Clodsire is heavily reliant on setting entry hazards to do damage long-term, so teams with many Heavy-Duty Boots users are problematic for it.

Physical Attackers: While Clodsire's physical bulk is not terrible, it is unable to take on the vast majority of the strong physical attackers in Ubers.

Freeze: Boosted Kyogre sets can break past Clodsire outright, but they cannot break a Terastalized Clodsire. Still, Kyogre may attempt to get past Clodsire by repeatedly using Ice Beam against it and hoping to freeze it.

Special Wall.description:
Clodsire uses its decent special bulk to pivot in on Miraidon, Kyogre, or Eternatus and set up entry hazards. Toxic is Clodsire's best option to do any significant damage to switch-ins like Ho-Oh and Ting-Lu, and it allows Clodsire to check Kyogre more reliably. Spikes is Clodsire's most exclusive entry hazard option, but Stealth Rock and Toxic Spikes are also valid choices, especially if it is paired with another entry hazard setter like Gliscor. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Clodsire avoid Spikes damage entirely. Leftovers is an option, as it provides Clodsire more longevity against teams whose only entry hazard options are Stealth Rocks or Toxic Spikes. Tera Steel and Fairy let Clodsire take on Miraidon's Dragon-type moves in a pinch while also making Kyogre's Ice Beam do pitiful damage to it. While Tera Fairy's immunity to Dragon can allow Clodsire to take more advantage of Miraidon on the turn it Terastallizes, Steel keeps Clodsire's Poison immunity and gives it a useful Ice resistance.

While Clodsire provides strong role compression, it works much better when given teammates that can help take the edge of off its worse matchups. A Fairy-type like Arceus-Fairy, Zacian-C, or Flutter Mane is highly recommended, as this allows for pivoting opportunities against Miraidon, forcing it to predict between its Dragon- and Electric-type moves. Furthermore, additonal Ground-types such as Arceus-Ground, Gliscor, and Iron Treads are much appreciated for their help against Miraidon. Switch-ins to Necrozma-DM and Gliscor are highly recommended, as both are immune to Toxic and don't care about Earthquake. Arceus-Water, Ho-Oh, and Arceus-Dark are good options against Necrozma-DM, while your own Necrozma-DM or Gliscor can help against opposing Gliscor. Corviknight notably is good against both. All of the aforementioned teammates greatly enjoy Clodsire's ability to pivot into Kyogre.

Defensive.description:
With high special bulk, a useful typing, and an excellent ability in Unaware, Clodsire is one of the best special walls in OU, checking special setup sweepers like non-Draco Meteor Raging Bolt, Darkrai, and Iron Moth. Toxic puts the aforementioned threats on a timer, as well as otherwise safe switch-ins and foes that can threaten it out like Ogerpon-W, Landorus-T, and Great Tusk. Poison Jab trades this reliability for an alternative way of spreading status with greater PP, also giving Clodsire a way to deal with Toxic-immune threats like Clefable, Hatterene, and Substitute Enamorus that would otherwise wall it. Amnesia bolsters Clodsire's Special Defense to staggering heights, ensuring powerful special attackers like Raging Bolt and Gholdengo or Stored Power users like Iron Crown and Hatterene cannot break through. If the team lacks another Stealth Rock setter, then Stealth Rock can be run instead, especially because entry hazard removers like Great Tusk and Cinderace hate getting crippled by Toxic and thus lose to it long-term. Similarly, Spikes is also another option if another Stealth Rock setter is present on the team. Tera Steel gives Clodsire a valuable shift to its defensive profile that allows it to comfortably handle Gholdengo's Make It Rain, check Psyshock users like Hatterene and Iron Valiant, and maintain both its Fairy resistance and poison immunity against them and Pecharunt, respectively. Alternatively, Tera Dark gives Clodsire a Psychic immunity, crucial for checking Stored Power, Psychic Noise, Future Sight, and Psyshock users like Iron Crown, Galarian Slowking, and Hatterene more reliably.

Due to Clodsire's passive nature, it slots best onto stall and bulkier balance teams, which appreciate the defensive capabilities it brings. Teammates like Dondozo and Alomomola appreciate Clodsire's ability to check threatening sweepers like Raging Bolt, while Clodsire can rely on them to check physical attackers like Great Tusk and Landorus-T. Another teammate that Clodsire pairs especially well with is Blissey, as together they form an extremely potent defensive core that can wall almost any special attacker. Clodsire covers threats like Serperior and Gholdengo that can boost past Blissey's sheer bulk, while Blissey beats special attackers like Primarina, Iron Crown, and Walking Wake that can hit Clodsire for super effective damage. Gliscor and Clefable can serve as Knock Off absorbers, as well as setting entry hazards, allowing Clodsire to run Amnesia. On bulkier balance teams, Clodsire pairs well with Skarmory as the defensive backbone of the team, setting hazards and forcing switches to chip down offensive threats like Great Tusk, Darkrai, and especially Gliscor, which Clodsire is completely helpless against. Corviknight also excels as a partner, absorbing Knock Off that can cripple Clodsire, as well as beating Gliscor, Skarmory, and opposing Corviknight, all of which Clodsire struggles against. Garganacl can soak up status from threats like Hex Dragapult and Cinderace while providing physical bulk that Clodsire appreciates. Offensive partners like Dragapult and Zamazenta threaten Pokemon that Clodsire can't handle such as Walking Wake, while Clodsire walls threats like Iron Valiant and Enamorus that its partners would otherwise struggle against. Another good teammate is Kingambit, which can absorb Future Sight and other Psychic-type attacks that would threaten Clodsire, while Clodsire beats Pokemon that Kingambit struggles against, like Raging Bolt, Moltres, and Iron Moth.

monotype.overview:
Poison

Clodsire has a lot of tools going for it on Poison such as Stealth Rock, Unaware or Water Absorb, and the best special bulk of any viable Poison-type, making it the perfect counter to Flutter Mane, Hydreigon, or Walking Wake, depending on the chosen ability. However, Alolan Muk and Galarian Slowking offer more in terms of a special wall, with Alolan Muk offering an immunity to Psychic and a resistance to Ghost, while Galarian Slowking is a Regenerator wall that can take on Latios and has a flurry of coverage options that may make them more appealing to the reader.
monotype.comments:
Other Options

Ground

Gunk Shot can be used instead of Poison Jab for more power, notably 2HKOing Primarina.

Physically Defensive (Poison).description:
Leaning more into its Defense allows Clodsire to become a surprisingly adept check to physical setup sweepers like Scizor, Ceruledge, and Bisharp, which otherwise cause immense issues for Poison teams. Earthquake enables it to pressure the aforementioned threats as well as Kleavor and Hisuian Goodra. Toxic pressures Flying-types like Latios and Moltres, which otherwise come in on Clodsire. The EV spread maximizes Clodsire's physical bulk while still letting it take two offensive Volcarona Psychic's from full HP.

With Clodsire's vastly decreased special bulk, Alolan Muk serves as an even more vital partner to handle special attackers Clodsire no longer beats like Flutter Mane, Darkrai, Greninja, and Hydreigon. Similarly, Assault Vest Galarian Slowking helps greatly against the likes of Kyurem, Choice Specs Terapagos, and Zapdos. Toxapex is a great complementary partner to Clodsire, being able to take on the likes of Weavile, Meowscarada, and Hisuian Arcanine. Amoonguss can help handle the Water- and Ground-types Clodsire cannot like Urshifu-R, Swampert, and Great Tusk. Galarian Weezing can handle threats like Swords Dance Garchomp and Mamoswine for Clodsire along with using Will-O-Wisp to cripple physical attackers like Lokix. Pecharunt checks hard-hitting attackers capable of easily breaking through Clodsire like Gliscor and Choice Band Meowscarada. Iron Moth can beat Ice-types that terrify Clodsire like Alolan Ninetales, Articuno, and Frosmoth along with removing Skarmory and Corviknight in the Steel matchup. Okidogi and Sneasler appreciate Clodsire's Stealth Rock wearing down Flying-types like Enamorus and the Landorus formes and in return can threaten Normal- and Dark-types like Ursaluna, Porygon2, and Hisuian Samurott.

Water Absorb (Ground).description:
Due to its remarkable bulk, rare dual-typing, and fantastic ability, Clodsire is a mainstay on Ground teams. Water Absorb stops common Water-type threats like Keldeo, Toxapex, and Primarina in their tracks. Poison Jab hits threats like Primarina, Enamorus, and Iron Valiant. Haze can be used to slow down opposing setup sweepers such as Hatterene and Volcarona. Toxic Spikes eases the Dragon and Fairy matchups due to their lack of entry hazard removal and applies pressure on teams in general, completing Ground's entry hazard stacking core. Toxic may be used instead to punish Pokemon like Latios and Mandibuzz, which freely switch into Clodsire otherwise. The given EV spread avoids the 2HKO from Choice Scarf Greninja's Ice Beam, Choice Scarf Meowscarada's Flower Trick, and Ogerpon-W's unboosted Horn Leech.

Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Excadrill appreciate Clodsire checking the aforementioned Water-types as well as other threats such as Iron Valiant and Flutter Mane. In return, Choice Scarf Great Tusk pressures Ice- and Dark-types like Hydreigon, Kyurem, and Choice Specs Greninja. Iron Treads clears entry hazards and threatens Hatterene, as well as being able to switch into Psychic-type attacks from Pokemon like Indeedee and Latios. Excadrill appreciates Clodsire's ability to switch into Water-type attackers that it cannot OHKO, such as Primarina, Urshifu-R, and Keldeo. Landorus and Gliscor are both great teammates for Clodsire because they can switch into Ground-type attacks from Pokemon such as Excadrill, Great Tusk, and Garchomp. In return, Landorus is capable of dealing with Grass-type Pokemon such as Breloom and Rillaboom, while Gliscor can stack more hazards. Unaware Quagsire pairs well with Clodsire, as it checks setup sweepers such as Azumarill, Ceruledge, and Dragonite. Furthermore, Quagsire is capable of using Toxic, allowing Clodsire to freely run Toxic Spikes, adding to the team's hazard stacking prowess. Ting-Lu not only forms a potent hazard stacking core with Clodsire but can switch into Psychic-type attacks.

The Clod (Special Wall) (Poison).description:
Due to its amazing Special Defense and ability in Unaware, Clodsire is a wall that can check the multitude of special setup sweepers in the tier such as Hydreigon, Volcarona, and Raging Bolt. Earthquake deals solid damage to threats like Volcarona, Gholdengo, and Heatran. Low Kick allows Clodsire to deal with Hydreigon and pop Air Balloon on the likes of Heatran and Raging Bolt. Stealth Rock can chip Flying-types like Corviknight, Enamorus, and Galarian Weezing that wall it. Alternatively, Spikes can be used to provide more reliable chip damage on threats such as Okidogi, Great Tusk, and Excadrill, which majorly threaten Clodsire. Alternatively, Curse can let Clodsire boost its Defense, turning it into a threatening wincon, and allow it to comfortably handle physical attackers like Iron Hands and Azumarill. Furthermore, other defensive invested variants can be explored but should still opt for Careful to check Raging Bolt.

Amoonguss and Toxapex assist Clodsire by being defensive walls capable of taking on Water-type threats such as Barraskewda, Quaquaval, and Keldeo. Amoonguss can also take on Ground-types that threaten Clodsire like Great Tusk and Swampert, while Toxapex can handle Ice-type threats like Weavile and Cloyster. Overqwil can handle threats like Iron Boulder and Gallade, and it can complement Clodsire by running Spikes and Toxic Spikes to create an entry hazard-stacking core. Galarian Weezing provides entry hazard removal with Defog and burns physical setup sweepers like Iron Hands, allowing Clodsire to easily wall them. Alolan Muk is a teammate with a Psychic immunity that can handle threats like Hatterene, Hoopa-U, and Deoxys-S. Clodsire appreciates Glimmora being able to spread Corrosion Toxic onto walls like Skarmory and Corviknight, which sit on Clodsire, along with being able to threaten Flying-types like Zapdos and Moltres with Power Gem. Iron Moth helps to remove Ice-type threats like Alolan Ninetales, Mamoswine, and Frosmoth. Okidogi and Sneasler help break down Ice- and Steel-type threats Clodsire cannot handle such as Kyurem, Alolan Sandslash, and Skarmory.

battlestadiumsingles.overview: This Pokemon has been updated for the return of the Regulation G format and its powerful restricted threats!
battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Specially Defensive Benchmarks

  • If shoring up Clodsire's low Defense is a priority, here are some of the Special Defense benchmarks to keep in mind when shifting EVs.

  • 252 HP and 52+ SpD: This avoids the 2HKO from Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball.

  • 252 HP and 108+ SpD: This avoids the 2HKO from Timid Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage.

  • 252 HP and 124+ SpD: This avoids the 2HKO from Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball after taking Stealth Rock damage.

  • 252 HP and 148+ SpD: This avoids the 2HKO from Modest Kyogre's Ice Beam without having to Terastallize.

  • 252 HP and 180+ SpD: This avoids the 2HKO from Timid Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage after taking Stealth Rock damage.

  • 252 HP and 220+ SpD: This avoids the 2HKO from the rare Modest Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage.

Special Wall.description:
• Clodsire's incredible bulk and typing make it a fantastic special wall against top restricted Pokemon like Miraidon, while boasting an equally fantastic support movepool.

  • Earthquake versus Earth Power: Earthquake easily surpasses Earth Power in terms of general power. However, Earth Power has a useful niche in that it can deal big damage to Glimmora without triggering Toxic Debris, as well as being more consistent into Stamina Archaludon.

  • Toxic Spikes versus Stealth Rock: Toxic Spikes support is fantastic on Clodsire, making it more difficult for opposing teams to play around getting poisoned. On the other hand, Stealth Rock can be used to pressure Poison- and Flying-types that might otherwise think they are safe from Clodsire's hazards, as well as being good support in general against Dragonite, Lunala and Focus Sash users.

  • Amnesia: Amnesia elevates Clodsire's Special Defense to crazy levels, potentially shutting out special attacking aces like Miraidon and Terapagos, as well as Lugia when paired with Tera Dark.

Other Options

  • Protect: In addition to benefiting from Leftovers and Black Sludge, Protect can pair well with the passive damage caused from either Toxic or Toxic Spikes.

Abilities

  • Water Absorb: Water Absorb has fantastic defensive utility in the current format against Urshifu-R’s Surging Strikes, Kyogre’s Water Spout, and Alomomola’s Flip Turn, and can even be combined with Terastallization to further disrupt Water-type Pokemon like the above.

  • Unaware: Unaware make Clodsire more consistent against the likes of Nasty Plot Calyrex-S and Calm Mind Miraidon.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Even with Clodsire's high Special Defense, the burst healing from Sitrus Berry goes a long way. With full special bulk investment, Sitrus Berry let's Clodsire always avoids the 2HKO from Choice Specs Miraidon's Draco Meteor after the Special Attack drop.

  • Black Sludge versus Leftovers: Black Sludge may seem appealing, but it punishes Clodsire for Terastallizing unless it becomes Tera Poison, so Leftovers is preferred unless Leftovers is already on something else.

  • Covert Cloak: If running something other than a Dark-type Terastallization, Covert Cloak is an alternate option to preventing Psychic Noise's heal block.

  • Mental Herb: Clodsire's support focus often draws in Taunt users, so Mental Herb is one way to make sure a critical turn of Toxic or Toxic Spikes use still happens.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low / Medium: Clodsire is often a part of defensive cycles that help cover its weaknesses, but Terastallization can generate big momentum when used at the right time.

  • Dark: Lugia's Psychic Noise is an issue for Clodsire, so Tera Dark can flip the tables on it as well as resisting Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S and Shadow Ball from Flutter Mane; keep in mind though that both Calyrex-S and Flutter Mane can heavily punish Clodsire's new Fairy-type weakness, so timing is key. Finally, Tera Dark also prevents Prankster Grimmsnarl from shutting down Clodsire with Taunt.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost's Fighting-type immunity combined with Water Absorb can make Urshifu-R miserable even if Clodsire hasn't invested in physical bulk. It also allows Clodsire to escape from Shadow Tag Gothitelle.

  • Normal: Tera Normal's Ghost-type immunity makes walling Calyrex-S even easier and, unlike Tera Dark, avoids gaining a Fairy-type weakness.

  • Poison: With Tera Poison, Clodsire maintains its ability to absorb Toxic Spikes and can also safely run Black Sludge to punish users of Trick.

  • Electric: While Water Absorb prevents Kyogre from using its powerful Water-type attacks, Tera Electric goes further by taking away Clodsire's weakness to Ice Beam while still being strong against Thunder and paralysis.

Alternative EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 100 Def / 156 Spe with Careful or Calm: This spread sacrifices some special bulk in order to avoid the 2HKO from Adamant Tera Normal Dragonite's Extreme Speed.

Support.description:
• While Clodsire is lacking in physical bulk compared to Dondozo and Skeledirge, it makes up for it in having a fantastic support movepool.

  • Yawn: Yawn is very effective at forcing switches, which is especially dangerous if Stealth Rock is set up.

  • Protect: In addition to benefiting from Leftovers, Protect pairs well with Yawn.

  • Low Kick: This prevents Clodsire from being totally walled by Tera Steel Hydreigon.

  • Amnesia: With Amnesia, Clodsire has a far better match-up against powerful special attacking foes such as Hydreigon and Iron Bundle.

  • Black Sludge versus Leftovers: Black Sludge may seem appealing, but it punishes Clodsire for Terastalliizing unless it becomes Tera Poison, so Leftovers is preferred unless Leftovers is already on something else.

Tera Types

  • Flying: With a Flying Tera type, Clodsire no longer has to worry about Earthquake or Fissure.

  • Steel: A Steel Tera type allows Clodsire to take on powerful Dragon-type attacks, without the worry of Gholdengo dealing massive damage.

  • Poison: With Tera Poison, Clodsire not only becomes a better check to Grass- and Water-types such as Meowscarda and Rotom-W, but it can also safely run Black Sludge to punish users of Trick.

  • Fairy: A Fairy Tera type will stop powerful Dragon-type attacks cold without making Clodsire weak to Earthquake, but it comes at the cost of compromising its ability to check Gholdengo.

  • Dark: Espathra's Stored Power is a big issue for Clodsire, so Tera Dark can flip the tables on it.

Abilities

  • Unaware: If you're planning to use Clodsire to its fullest defensive potential, Unaware is the best bet against setup foes.

  • Water Absorb: Water Absorb sacrifices overall defensive potential in exchange for being able to wall Rotom-W without needing to Terastallize. If setting up Stealth Rock is important, this can be worth it.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD / 4 Spe with Careful: Maximizing Special Defense is Clodsire's best hope for handling powerful special attackers such as Choice Specs Hydreigon.

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Impish: Clodsire's Defense may be mediocre, but with maximum investment, it can pull stunts such as usually avoiding a 2HKO from Jolly Dragonite's Outrage with Leftovers.

Water Absorb (Ground).description: Due to its incredible bulk and the ability to neutralize Water-type moves with Water Absorb, Clodsire is a staple for Ground teams, as it is able to stop threats such as Pelipper, Tapu Fini, and Rotom-W. Poison Jab not only spreads status but also lets it hit Grass- and Fairy-type Pokemon such as Tapu Bulu, Ogerpon-W, and Enamorus. Pairing Haze up with Icium Z allows Clodsire the ability to recover any damage from setup sweepers such as Volcarona, Ogerpon-W, and Kommo-o. The given EV spread allows Clodsire avoid a 2KHO from Choice Scarf Meowscarada with Flower Trick, unboosted Ogerpon-W with Horn Leech, and Choice Scarf Greninja with Ice Beam. Landorus provides an immunity to Ground-type moves that threaten Clodsire and offensively threatens Pokemon like Tapu Bulu, Celebi, and Archaludon. Hippowdon is a phenomenal defensive teammate, as it provides Stealth Rock support along with setting sand upon switching in. Hippowdon also defensively supports Clodsire by checking the likes of Ceruledge, Great Tusk, and Iron Hands. Excadrill, in conjunction with sand, is a powerful wallbreaker for Clodsire that can outspeed many Pokemon and deal raw damage with a Choice Band, checking threats such as Tapu Lele, Greninja, and Mega Gallade. Garchomp is an effective teammate that assists by checking Dragon-type threats such as Kommo-o and Kyurem. Mamoswine is another great teammate for Clodsire, as its Ice typing and powerful STAB moves assists in checking threats like the Landorus formes and Dragonite. Both Mamoswine and Garchomp deal offensive pressure to Steel- and Flying types such as Celesteela and Corviknight, which Clodsire cannot do on its own.

Unaware (Poison).description: Clodsire is an incredible specially defensive wall for Poison teams thanks to its solid stats and ability in Unaware, making it a solid check into special threats such as Hydreigon, Volcarona, and Gholdengo. Low Kick is used to break Hydreigon's Substitute along with popping Air Balloon from Heatran, while Poison Jab can be used to spread poison and do consistent damage to Flying-types like Zapdos and Tornadus-T. Clodsire's access to both Spikes and Stealth Rock provides it with good opportunities to set entry hazards, with Stealth Rock being preferred because it damages every Pokemon. Alternatively, Curse can patch up Clodsire's poor physical stats and make it a win condition. Mega Venusaur serves as a great defensive compliment to Clodsire with its ability to handle Water- and Ground-types like Barraskewda, Urshifu-R, Great Tusk, and Excadrill. Alolan Muk supports Clodsire by dealing with special attackers that threaten Clodsire like Latios, Tapu Lele, and Celebrate Victini. Crobat provides a solid Ground immunity, Defog to remove entry hazards while checking threats like Mega Gallade and Ogerpon-W, and Toxic to help outlast opponents. Choice Scarf Nihilego supports Clodsire by removing Ice- and Flying-types like Weavile, Mega Aerodactyl, the Landorus formes, and Mega Charizard Y. Choice Scarf Sneasler can help remove problematic faster threats like Choice Scarf Excadrill, Weavile, and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele while greatly appreciating Clodsire's hazards to damage Porygon2 and Rotom-W, along with its ability to use Switcheroo to force an unwanted Choice Scarf onto targets like Corviknight.

Specially Defensive.description: Clodsire's solid special bulk, access to entry hazards, and ability to absorb Toxic Spikes give it a niche in checking Miraidon, Arceus-Fairy, and some variants of Calyrex-S. However, it faces competition from Ting-Lu, which similarly checks Miraidon and Calyrex-S, has more offensive pressure, and gets Spikes up more easily. Spikes and Toxic Spikes give Clodsire a way to exert offensive pressure, alongside Earthquake which punishes Miraidon and Zacian-C on switch-in and hits Eternatus and Glimmora. Poison Jab can be used over Toxic or Toxic Spikes to potentially punish Taunt variants of Arceus-Fairy and Tera Fairy Calyrex-S along with Magic Bounce Hatterene, but it is generally outclassed by the other options. Water Absorb makes Clodsire a more solid check to Miraidon, since Unaware ignores Draco Meteor's Special Attack drop, and lets Clodsire check Arceus-Water and Kyogre. Unaware is an alternative that checks Calyrex-S more consistently. Tera Steel flips Clodsire's weakness to Ice- and Psychic-type attacks such as Kyogre's Ice Beam and Calyrex-S's Psyshock, while making Clodsire more reliable into Miraidon's Draco Meteor. Tera Dark makes Clodsire weaker to Arceus-Fairy and Miraidon, but checks Calyrex-S without Draining Kiss, as well as Calm Mind Arceus-Ground. Clodsire's ability to both absorb Toxic Spikes and check various special attackers gives it a niche on balance and stall teams. Clodsire pairs well with physical walls such as Gliscor, Alomomola, Dondozo, and Skeledirge, as they can check Koraidon, physical variants of Arceus formes, and Zacian-C. Secondary special walls such as Blissey and Tera Grass Ho-Oh are appreciated to ease the burden on Clodsire against Calyrex-S, Calm Mind Arceus-Ground, and Kyogre. Arceus is another partner for Clodsire that can pivot into Calyrex-S on balance teams, and appreciates Clodsire setting Spikes and clearing Toxic Spikes for it.

Offensive Trick Room.description:
Farigiraf is a relatively niche but potentially very lethal Trick Room sweeper in PU. Although it suffers stiff competition from other, more reliable offensive Psychic-types such as Espeon, Hoopa, and Hisuian Braviary, Farigiraf makes up for it thanks to having incredible bulk, a solid typing that gives it openings to set up on Pokemon like Hoopa, Espeon, and Palossand, and most notably Armor Tail, allowing it to completely bypass Sucker Punch attempts from the likes of Skuntank, Zoroark, and Brute Bonnet as well as other priority moves from Pawmot and Arcanine. Psyshock allows Farigiraf to muscle through specially defensive threats like Goodra and Florges more easily. Psychic is an alternative which gives Farigiraf a tougher matchup against special walls in exchange for allowing it to hit Rhydon without Terastallizing, as well as hitting Amoonguss and Qwilfish harder. Hyper Voice offers Farigiraf neutral coverage for Dark-types such as Wo-Chien and Hisuian Qwilfish and opposing Psychic-types like Delphox. Dazzling Gleam puts more pressure on Dark-types and synergizes well with Tera Fairy, while Thunderbolt smashes Milotic and similarly pairs well with Tera Electric. These options are not STAB-boosted, though, and so opting for them makes Farigiraf more dependent on Tera to function.

Farigiraf is a solid option on offense and hyper offense teams looking for a late-game setup sweeper that can turn the tables on an opposing team thanks to Trick Room. Farigiraf can often struggle to take down two of the most common defensive Pokemon in the tier, Milotic and Rhydon. As such, teammates which threaten these two, like Brute Bonnet and Hisuian Decidueye, or have shared checks with Farigiraf, like Arcanine and Delphox, can be useful to get these Pokemon worn down and allow Farigiraf to sweep. Pivots like Bruxish and Jolteon can help Farigiraf find safe positions to set up for a sweep versus Pokemon like Espeon, non-Encore Alolan Ninetales, and Rotom-Heat. Knock Off-resistant teammates like Paldean Tauros-F and Skuntank can be helpful to have due to Farigiraf's extreme weakness to the move, and they can chip down checks like Goodra and Alolan Sandslash into range for Farigiraf. Finally, Farigiraf pairs well with other slow teammates that benefit from Trick Room like Golurk and Glastrier. In fact, Farigiraf can serve as a setter and sweeper for the uncommon dedicated Trick Room teams.

Electric Seed.description:
Set Details

  • Farigiraf is a great supportive pick for a team. Its good defensive typing makes it a solid Calyrex-S check, and with Electric Seed, it can also match up well into Calyrex-I. Farigiraf also has the ability to block various priority moves such as Fake Out, Sucker Punch, and Thunderclap, keeping Farigiraf and its partners safe.
  • Foul Play can hit both Calyrex formes for heavy damage while dealing solid damage to other strong physical attackers such as Koraidon, Ogerpon, and Ursaluna. Psychic can be used to reliably hit Urshifu-R and Amoonguss, while Psychic Noise can stop recovery from Rillaboom's Grassy Terrain and Terapagos's and Ho-Oh's Leftovers and prevent Iron Hands from using Drain Punch.
  • Electric Seed helps Farigiraf have a much better matchup against strong physical attacks such as Wood Hammer from Rillaboom and Throat Chop or Crunch from Chien-Pao. Electric Seed can also weaken the power of Knock Off from Incineroar, which Farigiraf would normally struggle against.
  • The EV spread allows Farigiraf to live a Crunch or Throat Chop from Chien-Pao, Flare Blitz from Life Orb Koraidon, or Body Press from Zamazenta-C comfortably while letting it take a Draco Meteor from Special Attack Booster Energy Raging Bolt.
  • Tera Water is great against Urshifu-R because it will resist Surging Strikes, and it lets Farigiraf more comfortably take Glacial Lance from Calyrex-I. Tera Dark packs a resistance to Wicked Blow from Urshifu-S, while letting Foul Play OHKO low bulk Calyrex-S and deal hefty damage to Calyrex-I, though it can be vulnerable to Close Combat from both Urshifu formes and Koraidon and Body Press from Zamazenta-C.

Teambuilding

  • The Urshifu formes can bypass the Electric Seed Defense boost with Surging Strikes and Wicked Blow, with Urshifu-S being able to OHKO Farigiraf. Farigiraf can also be vulnerable to strong special attacks like Electro Drift from Miraidon, Dark Pulse from Chi-Yu, and Water Spout and Origin Pulse from Kyogre. Dark-types such as Incineroar, Chien-Pao, and Grimmsnarl are good checks, since Farigiraf does negligible damage back. Taunt from Flutter Mane and Incineroar can also shut down Farigiraf's supportive capabilities.
  • Miraidon is mandatory to pair alongside this set, helping Farigiraf activate Electric Seed and easily removing the Urshifu formes with Electro Drift and Dazzling Gleam while greatly appreciating Farigiraf's ability to block Fake Out and Sucker Punch, which may hinder Miraidon. Iron Hands and Calyrex-I like Farigiraf's ability to reliably set Trick Room and support with Helping Hand while having a good matchup into opposing Iron Hands and Calyrex-I. In return, Iron Hands can remove the Dark-types that Farigiraf struggles against.

Bulky Support.description:
Farigiraf's main role is as a bulky support piece and Trick Room setter, and its ability to block priority is incredibly valuable in a format full of moves like Fake Out, Grassy Glide and Thunderclap. Due to its typing, it has a good matchup into Calyrex-S, and its Psychic-type STAB moves are generally good into the metagame but especially into Amoonguss and Urshifu-R. Tera Blast is often used in the second moveslot, as both before and after Terastallization, it gives Farigiraf a consistent single-target STAB move. Foul Play is used to give Farigiraf a way to hit both Calyrex formes for super effective damage, being able to 2HKO both. Electric Seed is used in tandem with Miraidon and gives Farigiraf more bulk, allowing it to stick around longer to support the team with Helping Hand and Armor Tail. Sitrus Berry allows Farigiraf to disrupt the opponent for longer than it would be able to without it. It can also help it take some double-ups to help safely get Trick Room up, such as Surging Strikes + Knock Off from Urshifu-R and Incineroar. Safety Goggles is viable if your team has a particularly bad matchup into Amoonguss and you want Farigiraf to be able to set up Trick Room without being put to sleep without Electric Terrain support from Miraidon. The HP and Special Defense EVs allow Farigiraf to tank a Choice Specs Beads of Ruin single-target Tera Starstorm from Terapagos, and the rest is put into Defense. Tera Ground is used next to Miraidon to allow it to freely use Discharge, and Tera Fairy allows it to resist the Dark- and Bug-type moves it'd otherwise be weak to like Knock Off and U-turn from Incineroar and Rillaboom, while also resisting Fighting-type attacks and gaining an immunity to Dragon-type moves, like Collision Course and Draco Meteor from Koraidon and Miraidon, respectively.

Farigiraf really doesn't like Restricted Pokemon that can OHKO it and potentially prevent Trick Room, such as Kyogre or Tera Fire Koraidon. It also struggles against fast Taunt users, such as Speed Booster Energy Flutter Mane, due to them being able to prevent Trick Room from going up, and bulky Dark-types like Incineroar, as Farigiraf can't hit them very hard without Tera Ground. Incineroar in particular can force it to Terastallize with Knock Off. Miraidon and Farigiraf are great partners for each other, as Farigiraf stops Miraidon from being interrupted by Fake Out, which is particularly important for the Choice Specs set, and Miraidon can activate the Electric Seed to make Farigiraf even bulkier; furthermore, as previously mentioned, Farigiraf can even Tera Ground so Miraidon can freely click Discharge next to it, while the Electric Terrain makes Farigiraf immune to Amoonguss's Spore. Farigiraf itself benefits from partners that can help it set Trick Room, such as bulky Fake Out users like Incineroar and Rillaboom as well as redirectors like Amoonguss and the Ogerpon formes. Trick Room sweepers also like having Farigiraf as a partner; for example, Calyrex-I loves the boost from Helping Hand, and so does Ursaluna-B. Another great partner is Iron Hands on the aforementioned Miraidon teams, as Farigiraf enjoys having a Fake Out user as a partner, and its Helping Hand lets Iron Hands do insane levels of damage with Quark Drive.

Throat Spray.description:
Farigiraf functions well as a supportive and offensive Pokemon. After a Throat Spray boost, Psychic OHKOes Amoonguss and 2HKOs Flutter Mane. Twin Beam reliably OHKOes Focus Sash and Psychic-weak Pokemon like Urshifu-R and Mienshao. Hyper Voice deals consistent damage and activates Throat Spray. The EV spread allows Farigiraf to survive Adamant Koraidon’s Flare Blitz and Kyogre’s Water Spout. Throat Spray powers up Farigiraf's already powerful attacks after a Hyper Voice. This allows it to then pick up KOs on foes like Koraidon. Tera Fairy is used on Farigiraf to resist powerful super effective attacks from Dark-types like Urshifu-S and Chi-Yu along with Fairy being a great neutral type in the metagame. Tera Normal sheds Farigiraf's Dark weakness and allows it to deal massive damage with Hyper Voice, 2HKOing on Pokemon like Miraidon and Clefairy.

Farigiraf has to be careful of powerful Dark-type attacks from Chi-Yu and Incineroar. A great partner for Farigiraf is Kyogre because it appreciates Farigiraf blocking powerful Grassy Glides and Thunderclaps as well as Fake Out. Other Pokemon like Incineroar and Rillaboom are also great partners, as they offer Fake Out support, allowing Farigiraf to set up Trick Room and, through Hyper Voice, Throat Spray. Urshifu-R is another amazing partner because it can hit the annoying Steel- and Dark-types that keep Farigiraf in check while also synergizing well with the aforementioned partners. It also appreciates Farigiraf's nullification of Fake Out, Thunderclap, and Grassy Glide as well as it removing Amoonguss.

Offensive.description:
• Hyper Voice activates Throat Spray to inflict a lot of damage and boost subsequent Psychics. Psyshock deals less damage than Psychic overall, but it allows Farigiraf to hit Flutter Mane and Assault Vest Pokemon like Rillaboom harder.

  • Throat Spray allows Farigiraf to put really good amounts of pressure unlike other Trick Room setters. Life Orb allows for more immediate damage and more pivoting ability, as you wont lose the damage boost when switching out, but provides less damage overall.

  • The HP and Special Defense EVs allow Farigiraf to survive Tera Fairy Moonblast from Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Tera Normal Helping Hand-boosted Hyper Voice from Life Orb Ursaluna-B, as well as non-Tera Life Orb Blood Moon. The heavy amount of Special Attack investment allows Farigiraf to serve its role as an offensive Pokemon very well, especially after a Throat Spray boost. The Defense investment allows Farigiraf to take Surging Strikes from Tera Water Choice Scarf Urshifu-R.

zu.comments:
Other Options

Tera Fairy blunts the damage from Knock Off and other Dark-type moves from Sneasel, Spiritomb, and Primeape, and it also denies Dragon Tail from Dipplin and Appletun. Tera Fighting beats Steel-types, hits Cryogonal harder and sooner than Stored Power can with limited boosts, and also flips Farigiraf's Dark and Bug weaknesses. A Weakness Policy on Stored Power sets can take advantage of weaker attacks like Knock Off and U-turn from Mesprit but is situational, tough to activate, and limits Farigiraf's longevity. Cud Chew, with a Sitrus Berry, can give Farigiraf more concentrated recovery than Leftovers, and, with a Lum Berry, it can help it more comfortably set up against Glare Sandaconda and Toxic Toedscruel. Sap Sipper can provide Farigiraf with setup opportunities against Whimsicott and Arboliva locked into Grass-type moves. However, Armor Tail best enables Farigiraf as a sweeper by guarding it from priority moves. Farigiraf can run an offensive Trick Room set, though Alolan Exeggutor often does this role better because of its greater power and coverage. Farigiraf has other options in its movepool such as Future Sight, Wish, and Roar but struggles to support teams with its mediocre defensive typing.

Checks and Counters

Dark-types: Malamar has enough special bulk to take a boosted hit from Farigiraf and retaliate with their Dark-type STAB moves, Sneasel outspeeds Farigiraf before an Agility and hits it hard with Knock Off, and Alolan Persian can Taunt Farigiraf before it can set up. Although Sableye and Spiritomb don't deal much damage to Farigiraf on their own, they can force it to exhaust Terastallization or totally counter it if it's no longer available.

Steel-types: Farigiraf lacks coverage to beat Steel-types like Magneton, Orthworm, and Perrserker on its own.

Bulky Pokemon: Naclstack and Regirock can stomach Farigiraf's hits unless it's accumulated multiple boosts for Stored Power. Dipplin and Appletun can phaze Farigiraf with Dragon Tail; similarly, Articuno can use Haze to clear away Farigiraf's boosts or Roar to phaze it, and it has the bulk and recovery to repel Farigiraf repeatedly.

Taunt: With Taunt, Skuntank, Froslass, and Persian-Alola can prevent Farigiraf from setting up, which is especially disruptive if Farigiraf lacks boosts and has Stored Power, and they can set up on it in return.

Double Dance.description:
Farigiraf can reach great heights as a setup sweeper thanks to its great bulk and solid Special Attack. Psyshock hits specially bulky Pokemon such as Naclstack and Articuno and ignores Special Defense boosts on sweepers like Lilligant and Jolteon. As Farigiraf accumulates multiple boosts, though, Stored Power helps it become a taller order for teams to check, and it hits physically bulkier Pokemon like Regirock and Sandaconda harder. However, Stored Power provides less immediate damage for breaking teams and is more inflexible by requiring Farigiraf to spend multiple turns boosting. Dazzling Gleam covers Dark-types like Spiritomb and Sneasel, and after Terastallizing Tera Fairy Farigiraf, it becomes even stronger. Armor Tail aids Farigiraf's sweep by denying priority attacks like Aqua Jet from Accelrock from Lycanroc and Ice Shard from Sneasel. Armor Tail also saves Farigiraf from being locked into its setup by Prankster Encore from Whimsicott and Sableye. Farigiraf can invest fully in its Special Attack to become immediately more threatening, potentially sweeping just off of Agility, but full investment in HP gives it better opportunities to use multiple setup moves; Psyshock is better tailored for sets with maximum Special Attack investment, compared to Stored Power, which works better on maximum HP sets where it can more comfortably accumulate multiple boosts.

Farigiraf fits on hyper offensive teams as a setup sweeper. Fellow setup sweepers such as Virizion and Toxicroak greatly appreciate partnering with Farigiraf, given its positive matchups against Prankster disruptors like Whimsicott and Sableye. Powerful offensive partners like Clawitzer, Virizion, and Typhlosion can break holes in teams for Farigiraf to more easily sweep. Farigiraf has to exhaust Terastallization in order to beat Spiritomb, so it appreciates partners that can deal with it, such as Whimsicott and Magneton. Hyper offense leads like Froslass and Lycanroc can set up entry hazards to help weaken foes like Regirock and Dipplin to better enable Farigiraf to sweep. Orthworm is a tough target for Fargiraf to break on its own, so it appreciates help from Fire-type teammates like Charizard and Typhlosion that can pressure it. Fighting-type partners like Primeape, Virizion, and Hitmontop can handle Orthworm as well as another obstacle to Farigiraf in Regirock. Hisuian Sneasel is a standout partner for Farigiraf by checking all three aforementioned stops to it, while Fargiraf pressures its defensive answers such as Weezing and Muk.

nu.overview: Calm Mind turns Dudunsparce into a extremely threatening special sweeper that utilizes the raw power of Boomburst to clean up weakened teams while being difficult to KO due to Roost, good natural bulk, and a generally solid defensive typing. Dudunsparce can also punish the use of Knock Off with Rattled, meaning that removing its item can sometimes help it sweep. This means that Dudunsparce is exceptional at taking advantage of passive Pokemon such as Swampert, Tsareena, and Gligar, as they cannot use Knock Off to remove its item without giving it a Speed boost. Dudunsparce does struggle with Fighting-types such as Flamigo and Toxicroak, which can easily threaten it out if Terastallizing is not an option for it. Steel-types such as Copperajah and Bronzong can easily take its STAB Boomburst and threaten it out with Whirlwind or Body Press, respectfully. Additionally, Dudunsparce has a poor Speed stat, which means even slow wallbreakers such as Rhyperior and Sylveon can land huge attacks on Dudunsparce, potentially cutting a sweep short.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Dudunsparce has a wide array of coverage options, including Ice Beam and Earth Power, to hit Pokemon such as Altaria and Incineroar that might otherwise give it trouble. Dudunsparce can utilize a defensive Stealth Rock set, which can act as a check to Pokemon such as Chandelure while crippling entry hazard removal options such as Tsareena with either Toxic or Glare. Coil sets can be used in order to turn Dudunsparce into a dangerous physical sweeper, allowing it to take on Pokemon such as Copperajah more easily. Covert Cloak can be used on sweeping sets to ignore secondary effects such as Vaporeon's Scald and Munkidori's Toxic Chain.

Checks and Counters

Rock-types: Rock-types such as Rhyperior and Drednaw are a massive pain for Dudunsparce, as they can easily stomach both Boomburst and Shadow Ball while threatening massive damage with moves like Earthquake and Stone Edge. If Dudunsparce switches out, they can use the opportunity to set up entry hazards such as Stealth Rock and Spikes, further impeding Dudunsparce's sweeping potential if it is not using Heavy-Duty Boots.

Fighting-types: Fighting-types such as Flamigo, Toxicroak, and Paldean Tauros-W can threaten immense damage on Dudunsparce, typically forcing it out. However, most of these struggle against Dudunsparce if it decides to use Tera Poison, allowing Dudunsparce to potentially set up on them.

Steel-types: Steel-types such as Bronzong, Copperajah, and Klefki can typically wall Dudunsparce, and they can set Stealth Rock or Spikes to make progress or force good damage on it with Body Press or Iron Head. However, Dudunsparce can typically outlast them and threaten good damage with Shadow Ball.

Status Conditions: Pokemon that can afflict poison such as Amoonguss, Munkidori, and Bellibolt are major annoyances for Dudunsparce, as poison further impedes its sweeping capabilities, forcing it to either Terastallize into a Poison-type or constantly use Roost. While a burn is less impactful, it can still force Dudunsparce to waste Roost PP.

Phazing Moves: Phazing moves such as Roar from Vaporeon and Whirlwind from Copperajah can impede Dudunsparce's sweep, negating any boosts it has acquired. However, this is not a foolproof solution, as the negative priority forces the phazer to take a powerful attack from Dudunsparce, and phazing is ineffective if Dudunsparce is the last Pokemon on the team.

Scream (Calm Mind).description:
Set Details

Calm Mind Dudunsparce can utilize the immense power of Boomburst to become an incredibly difficult setup sweeper to remove. Shadow Ball can hit Pokemon such as Chandelure, Basculegion-M, and Bronzong that are either immune to or resist Boomburst. Roost allows Dudunsparce to keep sustaining itself over the course of a game and accruing boosts whenever it can. Leftovers can help keep Dudunsparce healthy so that it doesn't expend Roost PP too early, while Heavy-Duty Boots can allow Dudunsparce to get on the field easier while hazards are down. Rattled can allow Dudunsparce to punish the various U-turn and Knock Off users in the tier to gain a Speed boost. 100 Speed EVs enable Dudunsparce to outspeed Incineroar and Vaporeon and hit them with Boomburst before they use Parting Shot and Haze, respectively. They also let Dudunsparce outspeed neutral-nature Basculegion-M after a Rattled boost. Tera Poison gives Dudunsparce a Fighting resistance, and it also comes with the benefit of not letting Dudunsparce get poisoned by Pokemon such as Munkidori and Amoonguss. Tera Ghost gives Dudunsparce an immunity to Fighting-type attacks from Pokemon such as Paldean Tauros-W while also boosting the power of Shadow Ball. Additionally, it's a better Tera type against Bronzong because, unlike Tera Poison, it makes Dudunsparce not weak to Psychic Noise and immune to Body Press.

Calm Mind Dudunsparce fits primarily on bulky offense and balance teams, which love its ability to set up easily on many common defensive Pokemon like Vaporeon, Gligar, and Tsareena. Therefore, Pokemon such as Paldean Tauros-W, Flygon, and Swampert enjoy Dudunsparce's presence and can bring these foes in so that Dudunsparce can use them as setup fodder. Fighting-type answers such as Galarian Slowbro and Amoonguss are heavily appreciated by Dudunsparce, while in return, Dudunsparce can help against Pokemon they may struggle with such as Basculegion-M and Kilowattrel. Entry hazard removers such as Tsareena and Altaria are much appreciated by Dudunsparce, as they allow it to reliably run Leftovers to further aid its sweeping potential. Pokemon that are walled by Bronzong such as Munkidori and Flygon heavily appreciate Dudunsparce, as it can reliably chip or set up on Bronzong, allowing them a much easier time for wallbreaking. In return, they can help against Pokemon such as Flamigo that might otherwise trouble Dudunsparce. Due to its Ghost immunity, Dudunsparce is often tasked with switching into Shadow Ball from Chandelure. However, it struggles with switching into Fire Blast, so Dudunsparce appreciates partners such as Basculegion-M and Altaria that can take Chandelure's Fire-type attacks.

Glare.description:
Dudunsparce is a reliable Stealth Rock lead on hyper offense and paralysis-spreading wallbreaker on offensive builds that combines strong immediate pressure with good natural bulk. Glare cripples faster threats such as Munkidori, Flygon, and Scyther, allowing both Dudunsparce and its teammates to outspeed them. Hex takes advantage of this by heavily punishing paralyzed targets like Bronzong and Basculegion, while Earth Power is an alternative option that more directly pressures bulkier Pokemon such as Copperajah, Duraludon, and Incineroar. However, Hex is generally preferred to avoid being walled by Bronzong, Brambleghast, and Decidueye once they are paralyzed. Stealth Rock helps hyper offense teams by chipping foes into range of a KO, but Roost allows Dudunsparce to last longer on offense teams to check the likes of Chandelure and Houndstone. Chople Berry improves its consistency as a lead by letting it survive super effective Fighting-type attacks from wallbreakers such as Infernape and Heracross, allowing Dudunsparce to cripple them with Glare in return. Throat Spray is an alternative option that gives Dudunsparce immediate wallbreaking power after a Boomburst at the cost of reliability. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Dudunsparce to constantly switch in and out of the field without worry of entry hazards, but this item is negligible when Dudunsparce is ran on hyper offensive teams. 140 Speed EVs let Dudunsparce outspeed uninvested bulky Pokemon such as Vaporeon, Wo-Chien, Houndstone, as well as defensive Tsareena. After a Rattled boost, it can outspeed Pokemon such as Incineroar, Sylveon, Adamant Basculegion-M, and Adamant Toxicroak, letting it cripple them with Glare or pressure them with its attacks. The remaining HP investment improves its overall bulk, helping it more reliably take hits at full health. Tera Ghost further boosts Hex and gives Dudunsparce a useful Fighting immunity, letting it avoid attacks from Heracross and Paldean Tauros-W if it lacks a Chople Berry or after the Berry has been consumed. Tera Water gives Dudunsparce useful resistances to Water- and Fire-type attacks while making it neutral to Fighting-type attacks, helping it stomach hits from threats such as Basculegion-M, Chandelure, and Paldean Tauros-F.

Dudunsparce fits best on offense teams that appreciate its ability to set Stealth Rock; spread paralysis with Glare; and heavily chip common walls such as Altaria, Vaporeon, Copperajah, Duraludon, Swampert, and Scream Tail with Boomburst. Additional support from teammates like Klefki, which can set Spikes or dual screens, helps further stack entry hazard damage and aid teammates in setting up. Wallbreakers like Munkidori, Chandelure, Staraptor, Heracross, and Flamigo benefit from Dudunsparce getting Stealth Rock up early and spreading paralysis, which slows down faster attackers like opposing Munkidori, Choice Scarf Flamigo, and Tornadus. In return, they wear down defensive staples like Swampert, Wo-Chien, and Vaporeon. However, Dudunsparce often struggles against specially bulky Pokemon such as Goodra and Chansey, which can stomach its attacks and force it out. After setting Stealth Rock and spreading paralysis, Dudunsparce often faints to Fighting-types, giving teammates like Munkidori, Uxie, Chandelure, and Meloetta a free switch to regain momentum, while setup sweepers such as Scyther and Scrafty take advantage of the slowed opposing team. Psychic-types such as Uxie and Munkidori especially enjoy Dudunsparce, since it chips Steel-types like Duraludon and Copperajah, easing their sweep. Paralysis lets these teammates set up or clean without being forced out by faster attackers that would otherwise revenge kill them, such as Infernape and opposing Scyther for Scrafty, Paldean Tauros-W and Flygon for Chandelure, and Tornadus for Munkidori and Scyther. As a result, Munkidori and Chandelure can find setup opportunities more easily, Scrafty needs fewer Dragon Dance boosts to outspeed these revenge killers, Scyther can drop priority moves for options like Trailblaze, and Meloetta becomes much harder to revenge kill. If Dudunsparce lacks Stealth Rock, it can be paired with Swampert and Duraludon, the former of which carries utility in Knock Off and can be a Fighting-type check while the latter offers Roar and Thunder Wave to contribute to the paralysis-spreading nature of Dudunsparce.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Coverage for Fighting-, Fairy-, and Dark-types such as Primarina, Incineroar, and Sneasler is almost necessary when teambuilding with Kingambit. Both sets enjoy having redirection on their side, including the likes of Clefable, Electabuzz, and Amoonguss, which can easily take in Fighting-type attacks from threats like Annihilape and Sneasler. Swords Dance Kingambit can take advantage of redirection to a greater extent, since this can open windows for setup opportunities.

  • Rillaboom is a really good partner for Kingambit, providing setup opportunities with Fake Out and threatening Ground-types such as the Ursaluna formes. Dark-resistant Pokemon like Incineroar and even opposing Kingambit can be covered by Primarina, which also has great defensive synergy with Kingambit. Sneasler also works at removing Dark-types while also removing Fairy-types and providing another source of Fake Out support for Kingambit.

  • Kingambit, thanks to its typing, is extremely weak to Fighting-types, including Annihilape, Sneasler, and Flamigo, which prove to be an issue. The aforementioned Amoonguss and Clefable can take in these Fighting-type attacks. Primarina, as mentioned before, has great defensive synergy with Kingambit, taking Fighting- and Fire-type attacks with ease, while Kingambit can cover for it against Grass- and Poison-type attacks.

Strategy Comments

  • Kingambit's main role is either a setup sweeper with Swords Dance or a defensive pivot piece with Assault Vest. Swords Dance Kingambit's main goal is to set up and stay healthy; redirection and Fake Out support are usually necessary in achieving this. With Tera Dark and at +2, it's very easy for Kingambit to pick up momentum quickly and blitz through careless players. Don't be greedy with using Swords Dances, as it's easy for Kingambit to be OHKOed or brought to low health with careful positioning around Sucker Punch, especially in a format with Fighting-type coverage everywhere.

  • Kingambit succeeds as a setup sweeper thanks to its typing, bulk, and on Assault Vest sets, coverage. Its typing has many resistances to top types like Dragon, making Kingambit an amazing counter to Dragapult and Hydreigon. Kingambit's bulk, especially when it's paired with Assault Vest, is really good, allowing Kingambit to withstand hits and potentially turn the tables in a losing late-game position.

  • Dark-resistant Pokemon are a huge issue for Kingambit, easily taking Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch even if they're boosted. These Pokemon can be taken care of by partners such as Primarina and Sneasler. Fighting-types, including the likes of Annihilape, can be a massive issue, easily using Kingambit to set up. Sneasler in particular can be a problem, only taking notable damage from Iron Head. Fighting-type coverage moves are also rather prevalent in the metagame, with Pokemon like Low Kick Tyranitar and Body Press Archaludon being common. For this, Ghost-type switch-ins like Dragapult or redirection can be helpful in deterring Fighting-type attacks. Additionally, opposing Sneasler can be picked off by Dragapult. Offensive Fairy-types such as Primarina can scare Kingambit away from Terastallizing into a Dark-type, as Moonblast would otherwise easily chunk Kingambit. Sneasler can easily deal with Fairy-types by hitting them hard with Dire Claw.

Offensive.description:
• Kingambit is easily able to steamroll through teams, having a great typing both offensively and defensively and easily defeating metagame staples like Gholdengo as well as decimating foes thanks to Swords Dance. Swords Dance bolsters Kingambit's Attack such that it can pick up OHKOs on bulky Pokemon such as Rillaboom, Ursaluna-B, and Amoonguss using Kowtow Cleave, with the latter two requiring Tera Dark.

  • Sucker Punch compensates for Kingambit's low Speed while also immediately either forcing out or pinning Choice item attackers and Assault Vest users. On top of that, Sucker Punch can cause mind games, with Kingambit potentially just using Kowtow Cleave while forcing a switch with the threat of Sucker Punch. Low Kick can defeat Tyranitar and opposing Kingambit as well as Incineroar. Iron Head can be used as coverage for Dark-resistant Pokemon like Primarina and Sneasler, but it's generally harder to pilot and use.

  • Black Glasses is used to boost the main two moves on Kingambit, Kowtow Cleave and Sucker Punch. It allows +2 Kowtow Cleave to OHKO Rillaboom outright and Archaludon with Tera Dark as well as letting Kingambit pick off Volcarona with a +2 Sucker Punch. Safety Goggles stops Sucker Punch from getting redirected and negated by Rage Powder, which can be a huge issue for Kingambit. Safety Goggles can also deny Spore, allowing Kingambit to use Amoonguss to set up. Safety Goggles can miss key OHKOs on the Pokemon shown in the aforementioned calculations.

  • Tera Dark boosts Kingambit's damage further, allowing for OHKOs on Maushold and Gholdengo with Sucker Punch, as well as removing Kingambit's Fire weakness and 4x Fighting weakness, proving to be useful against threats like Incineroar, which Kingambit otherwise struggles to get rid of, and certain Fighting-type coverage and Pokemon like opposing Kingambit's Low Kick and Annihilape, which otherwise OHKO Kingambit.

  • Kingambit is really difficult to stop after a Swords Dance boost and Terastallizing, OHKOing Ursaluna with Kowtow Cleave. This set struggles with four-moveslot syndrome, as having to pick between the flexibility of Swords Dance and a coverage move is difficult. Another issue that this set has is that it can be really difficult to take Dark-resistant Pokemon down, such as Incineroar. For this, setting up in front of another Pokemon or removing the Dark-resistant Pokemon can help Kingambit thrive.

Assault Vest.description:
• Assault Vest Kingambit is great at taking strong hits while hitting back hard thanks to its high Attack stat. Its typing works amazing defensively thanks to the lack of good Ground- and Fighting-types, which is even better considering Assault Vest Kingambit works well as a bulky switch-in to many metagame staples such as Gholdengo. Defiant is very powerful on this set due to the lack of Swords Dance.

  • Low Kick is used as coverage for Dark-types, beating Pokemon such as Incineroar and opposing Kingambit.

  • Assault Vest allows Kingambit to take attacks like Earth Power from Ursaluna-B and Electro Shot from Archaludon as well as surviving extremely powerful attacks such as +1 Fiery Dance from Volcarona.

  • Fire is arguably the best Tera type on this set, providing a resistance to Fire while also removing Kingambit's weakness to Fighting. As a bonus, Tera Fire grants Kingambit a burn immunity, being very useful when facing foes like Talonflame. Tera Flying removes both Kingambit's Ground- and Fighting-type weaknesses, turning them into an immunity and a resistance, respectively. Tera Dark boosts Kingambit's Dark-type STAB moves, which can be very necessary due to not using Swords Dance.

  • The physical bulk investment lets Kingambit survive a Drain Punch from Annihilape and a rain-boosted Wave Crash from Basculegion-M. With the given special bulk, Kingambit can survive a +1 Fiery Dance from Volcarona and an Earth Power from Ursaluna-B. The offensive investment lets Sucker Punch OHKO Gholdengo with a Defiant boost while OHKOing Dragapult 75% of the time without it.

  • Assault Vest Kingambit is more flexible in move choices compared to Swords Dance variations, able to freely carry Iron Head and coverage moves as well as generally being more flexible in playstyle. With Assault Vest, this set has great survivability. However, Assault Vest Kingambit doesn't have much sweeping potential due to not running Swords Dance. Not being able to run Protect is also a noteworthy issue, as in a metagame where Trick Room and weather are everywhere, this drawback can make it difficult to position Kingambit and its allies.

Kingambit is a slow attacker that uses its good bulk and typing to tank hits from Pokemon like Calyrex-S, Lunala, and Terapagos, then respond with Dark- and Steel-type STAB attacks. Sucker Punch gives Kingambit a priority attack that it can use to get around its low Speed and that threatens Pokemon like the Calyrex formes. Tera Blast pairs with Tera Fairy to hit the Pokemon that wall Kingambit such as Urshifu-R and Iron Hands as well as Pokemon like Miraidon and Urshifu-S, while Low Kick is used to hit Pokemon that resist Steel- and Dark-type attacks such as Incineroar and Zamazenta-C. Assault Vest lets it survive attacks like Mystic Water Kyogre's Water Spout as well as getting 4HKOed by Calyrex-S's Astral Barrage most of the time. Tera Fairy gives Kingambit a resistance to Fighting-type attacks in addition to being a good defensive type that is neutral to most of the metagame.

Kingambit struggles into bulky Pokemon like Amoonguss and Incineroar that can easily survive an attack and respond with status moves like Will-O-Wisp or Spore. Offensive partners like Ursaluna-B and Miraidon help with this by threatening to OHKO Amoonguss and Incineroar, allowing Kingambit to clean up an endgame with Sucker Punch. Urshifu-R is another check for Kingambit, as it resists Kingambit's STAB attacks and can threaten it with Close Combat. Miraidon can threaten Pokemon like Mienshao and the Urshifu formes that threaten Kingambit. Miraidon also has the added benefit of blocking Spore from Amoonguss with Electric Terrain, which allows Kingambit to play more offensively. Calyrex-S is a good partner for Kingambit, as it appreciates Kingambit helping into opposing Calyrex-S and opposing Incineroar while Calyrex-S can threaten the Fighting-types that Kingambit struggles with like Mienshao. Calyrex-I can set Trick Room that Kingambit works well in while Calyrex-I threatens Amoonguss. Farigiraf is a good partner for Kingambit, as it prevents Fake Out and can set Trick Room for Kingambit while Incineroar, a Pokemon Farigiraf struggles with, doesn't want to switch into Kingambit and give it a Defiant boost.

Offensive.description:
• Swords Dance significantly raises the pressure Kingambit exerts, allowing it to deal significant damage even against resisted targets. However, Iron Head can be used to cover for Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane.

  • Black Glasses provides extra damage, allowing for an OHKO on Flutter Mane at +1 with Sucker Punch; Safety Goggles, however, gives Kingambit a better match-up against Amoonguss.

  • Tera Dragon is chosen to grant resistances to the Ogerpon formes' STAB attacks and other metagame threats that resist Dark, such as Urshifu-R and Chi-Yu. Tera Fairy is also a strong option as a neutral typing, and it also allows Kingambit to wall Urshifu-S and other Fighting-types.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• The given EV spread allows Kingambit to survive Life Orb Ursaluna-B's Earth Power or an Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-H as well as avoid the 3HKO from Raging Bolt's Thunderbolt. The Speed investment allows Kingambit to outspeed Landorus in tailwind.

  • Low Kick allows Kingambit to threaten Dark-Types such as Incineroar and opposing Kingambit; however, Tera Blast can also be used to cover for Dark- and Fighting-Types at the cost of needing to Terastallize.

Bulky Wallbreaker.description:
• With its unique typing, Kingambit serves as a powerful defensive tool against Pokemon such as Giratina-O lacking Will-O-Wisp, Yveltal, Arceus, and Choice Specs Lunala while also retaining a strong offensive presence thanks to Supreme Overlord, providing bulky offense and fat balance teams with a range of role compression courtesy of its valuable Ghost-, Psychic-, Dark- and Dragon-type resistances, access to priority, and even its ability to act as a late-game cleaner. Unfortunately, Kingambit lacks reliable recovery, which combined with its mediocre bulk relative to the tier, means it is prone to being overwhelmed easily.

  • Knock Off provides Kingambit with a source of utility by removing items such as Heavy-Duty Boots, preventing Pokemon such as Ho-Oh from reliably switching in. It also removes Life Orb from offensive Yveltal, weakening it severely, as well as removing items off other targets such as Zygarde, Arceus, Ferrothorn, and Alomomola, which can help teammates out in the long term. It helps Kingambit against stall teams too, since these structures are often reliant on items, such as the aforementioned Heavy-Duty Boots and Chansey's Eviolite, for their longevity. Especially considering that Kingambit often uses Sucker Punch for damage-dealing due to being outpaced by almost the entire metagame, having Knock Off to punish switch-ins against Kingambit is more useful on a regular basis than the slight and situational extra two hit damage provided from Kowtow Cleave.

  • Iron Head allows Kingambit to hit Fairy-types such as Arceus-Fairy and Zacian-C as well as Tera Fairy Zygarde and Eternatus. Sucker Punch is essential to make up for Kingambit's poor Speed, allowing it to remove foes such as Ultra Necrozma, Deoxys-A, and Mega Mewtwo Y before they can OHKO it instead. Low Kick can be considered to allow Kingambit to threaten Arceus-Dark, but it leaves Kingambit unable to threaten Arceus-Fairy or Tera Fairy Lunala.

  • Swords Dance allows Kingambit to punish the switches it forces, letting it wallbreak or be a strong late-game cleaner against more offensive teams, especially those lacking Zygarde or defensive Primal Groudon, such as against opposing hyper offense teams. It notably lets Kingambit OHKO Arceus-Fairy with Iron Head after Stealth Rock with no Supreme Overlord boosts and also OHKO Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM with Sucker Punch after a layer of Spikes. Alternatively, Pursuit is able to trap foes Kingambit switches into, such as Giratina-O and Choice-locked Lunala, wearing them down for offensive partners such as Primal Groudon. It is also good at trapping worn-down checks, such as Ho-Oh and support Arceus formes.
