  • Supreme Overlord is preferred over Defiant due to its reliable damage boost, such as being able to 2HKO Arceus via Knock Off with 4 fainted allies. However, Defiant can be used, notably punishing Sticky Web structures and Defog attempts from Giratina-O and Ho-Oh. However, it is difficult to activate anywhere else, reducing Kingambit's damage overall.

  • The given EV spread maximises Attack and allows Kingambit to outspeed Gothitelle, preventing it from using Taunt or Charm reliably, while ensuring Tera Fairy variants cannot safely 1v1 Kingambit. This is especially useful for Pursuit variants that may be more passive into Gothitelle. The rest is dumped into HP, notably allowing Kingambit to survive Life Orb Yveltal's Heat Wave from full.

  • Kingambit's typing is essential to its use on a team, and thus doesn't often use Terastalization. Regardless, Tera Dark is its best option, removing Kingambit's Ground- and Fire-type weakness while weakening the damage taken from Fighting-type attacks. This helps Kingambit stomach Earthquake from Necrozma-DM, Ultra Necrozma, and Arceus, along with Heat Wave from Yveltal, while even letting it survive Deoxys-A's Life Orb Low Kick, allowing Kingambit to trade more effectively. Offensively, Tera Dark lets Kingambit OHKO Marshadow with Knock Off and Ultra Necrozma with Sucker Punch. It also makes Kingambit more threatening late-game, since it is able to OHKO Ho-Oh and defensive Primal Groudon with +2 Tera Dark Sucker Punch and five Supreme Overlord boosts. However, it should be emphasized that Kingambit relies on its Steel typing to resist attacks from Giratina-O and Arceus more easily and to not be as weak to Fairy-type attacks from Arceus-Fairy and Tera Fairy Lunala.

  • Swords Dance variants of Kingambit are primarily used late-game, being able to clean up weakened teams after its teammates have wrecked havoc. Due to its middling bulk, this will usually happen after a teammates has fainted, since this prevents Kingambit from getting worn down as badly while it sets up Swords Dance. The only time Kingambit should come out in the early-to-mid game is to tank resisted hits such as Lunala's Moongeist Beam and Giratina-O's Draco Meteor; otherwise, preserving Kingambit's HP by avoiding unnecessary damage from neutral hits is ideal to ensuring it can clean up effectively.

  • Pursuit variants of Kingambit are more aggressive than the Swords Dance counterpart; it's ideal to abuse double switches from teammates such as Primal Groudon, Zygarde, and Arceus-Ground, since all three of these typically invite in Giratina-O, from which Kingambit can easily Pursuit trap it, wearing it down for teammates to break through more easily afterwards. This variant, however, still doesn't appreciate being unnecessarily worn down, since otherwise it may be unable to reliably trap Pokemon such as Choice-locked Lunala and Marshadow and be forced to click Sucker Punch instead so as to not get KOed by their powerful attacks.

  • Defensive walls, such as Primal Groudon, Zygarde, and the more niche Dondozo, all easily stop Kingambit without significant boosts or Tera Dark to help it and threaten it with either STAB moves or, in Dondozo's case, Body Press. Giratina-O is able to handle all three of these, while it appreciates Kingambit switching into the Ghost- and Ice-type attacks Giratina-O doesn't like, such as against Choice Band variants of Marshadow and Chien Pao, notably preventing the former from mindlessly spamming its Ghost-type STAB moves. Kingambit also makes for a solid Yveltal and Arceus-Dark switch-in due to its resistances. Giratina-O is also able to remove hazards, assisting greatly in Kingambit's longevity, while relieving pressure off of Kingambit by checking Arceus itself.

  • Due to the utility of Knock Off, Kingambit works great with hazard setters such as defensive Primal Groudon in removing Heavy-Duty Boots off of targets like Ho-Oh and Alomomola, making wearing them down late-game easier for Kingambit itself or teammates. Primal Groudon is also able to check Zacian-C for Kingambit, while Kingambit in return harasses Giratina-O with Pursuit. There is also Landorus-T, which is similar to Giratina-O in soft-checking Arceus as well as Arceus-Ground, Zacian-C, and Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM. Its access to U-turn also allows it to bring in Kingambit safely against Pokemon it struggles with, such as Giratina-O and Yveltal, both of which can abuse Landorus-T's inability to threaten them back meaningfully.

  • Offensive partners such as Swords Dance Primal Groudon, Primal Kyogre, and Meteor Beam Eternatus, are all able to break through and wear down opposing teams, enabling Kingambit to sweep much more easily. The former is able to overwhelm Zygarde for Kingambit to muscle past it more easily afterwards, while the latter two are powerful special attackers capable of breaking through Zygarde, Ho-Oh and opposing Primal Groudon for Kingambit. In return, Kingambit provides a powerful revenge-killer and sweeper against opposing hyper offense teams that these three Pokemon don't like dealing with.

Swords Dance.description:
Kingambit is a highly threatening sweeper thanks to Swords Dance boosting its already high Attack, powerful STAB priority in Sucker Punch, and a unique ability in Supreme Overlord. Kingambit also provides a team with notable defensive utility, as it checks dangerous foes such as Gholdengo, Mega Latios, and Iron Crown thanks to its typing and access to Sucker Punch. Knock Off is Kingambit's most powerful STAB move under most circumstances, and it can remove items from Pokemon that check it, such as Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Landorus-T. Sucker Punch is mandatory to make up for Kingambit's low Speed, allowing it to revenge kill faster threats such as the aforementioned Gholdengo and Mega Latios as well as others such as Ogerpon-W, Volcarona, and Iron Moth. Low Kick is the preferred coverage to hit foes such as opposing Kingambit, Melmetal, Ferrothorn, and Ting-Lu, as it OHKOes all of them after Stealth Rock at +2. Iron Head is an alternative that hits Clefable and Mega Diancie, but its targets are generally less important and Kingambit must be very healthy if it hopes to beat the latter one-on-one. Black Glasses gives Kingambit a notable boost to its Dark-type STAB moves, letting it hit important benchmarks such as OHKOing offensive Gholdengo as well as, at +2, Ogerpon-W with Sucker Punch and greatly improving Knock Off's damage rolls into important defensive Pokemon such as Alomomola and Toxapex, especially with Supreme Overlord active. Air Balloon gives Kingambit a one-time opportunity to dodge revenge killing attempts by or set up in the face of Ground-types such as Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Garchomp. Leftovers gives Kingambit passive recovery and improves its longevity, letting it check Gholdengo throughout a game for its team. An Adamant nature is preferred to hit as hard as possible, but Jolly allows Kingambit to, at worst, Speed tie with opposing Kingambit as well as outrun a few other notable threats such as Moltres, Ursaluna, and Mega Mawile. Supreme Overlord powers up Kingambit as its allies faint; this becomes incredibly dangerous in late-game scenarios, as Kingambit gains a large damage boost if many or all of its teammates have been taken down. Defiant can be situationally useful on certain hyper offense teams that value its ability to punish Defog attempts from Gliscor, Zapdos, and Landorus-T, as well as punishing Intimidate from the last one; this is generally best used with Air Balloon to protect Kingambit from Gliscor and Landorus-T. However, Supreme Overlord is generally more consistent, and hyper offense teams often have better ways to punish or outright deny Defog.

Kingambit fits on many offensive teams thanks to the immense amount of pressure it exerts while also giving such teams a check to dangerous Ghost- and Psychic-types such as Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and Mega Latios. Kingambit's presence as a top threat in the metagame means that every team has a method of dealing with it, usually through faster Dark-resistant Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Hisuian Samurott; these are often backed up by secondary answers such as defensive Landorus-T, Alomomola, and Moltres. Kingambit can help itself out early-game by spamming Knock Off into these threats in order to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Alomomola. This strategy pairs very well with entry hazard setters, making teammates such as Landorus-T, Ferrothorn, and Gliscor great partners. The latter two are also capable of setting Spikes, which wear down Fighting-types like Urshifu-R for Kingambit. A teammate that can pivot into Fighting-types is also mandatory, as Kingambit tends to invite them into battle. Zapdos, Moltres, defensive Landorus-T, and Toxapex are good teammates as a result. Psychic- and Fairy-type offensive teammates also pair well with Kingambit, since they scare many of its Fighting- and Dark-type answers. Mega Latios, Iron Crown, Mega Diancie, or Iron Valiant combine with Kingambit to create a brutal offensive core, while the Psychic-types in particular appreciate Kingambit threatening Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo. Despite being a Steel-type, Kingambit fears Tapu Lele due to Psychic Terrain blocking Sucker Punch and it commonly carrying coverage moves that target Kingambit's weaknesses, so solid Tapu Lele checks such as Gholdengo and Melmetal are good teammates.

Offensive Utility.description:
Leveraging its great natural bulk alongside significant defensive investment and an item to further boost its longevity, Kingambit is able to act as a powerful defensive tool against Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Terapagos while remaining a threatening late-game cleaner. Knock Off is Kingambit's main STAB option, boasting a high Base Power and a powerful secondary effect, particularly against Heavy-Duty Boots users such as Zapdos and Moltres and Rocky Helmet users such as Alomomola and Landorus-T. Pursuit allows Kingambit to forcibly remove most Gholdengo sets while also heavily limiting most dedicated special walls, such as Blissey, Clodsire, and Galarian Slowking, and guaranteeing that Terapagos's Tera Shell is broken. Sucker Punch allows Kingambit to bypass its middling Speed stat, deterring fast and offensive Pokemon that would otherwise be problematic for Kingambit, such as offensive Volcarona, Mega Charizard Y, Focus Blast variants of Gholdengo, and Mega Medicham, while also allowing it to pick off weakened foes such as Garchomp and Ogerpon-W. Low Kick is used mainly to hit opposing Kingambit while also hitting Ting-Lu and Ferrothorn and OHKOing Mega Tyranitar. Iron Head is an alternative option, allowing Kingambit to immediately threaten Iron Valiant, Tapu Koko, and Clefable while also quickly wearing down Great Tusk and all-out attacker Zamazenta. Leftovers is the premier item for utility Kingambit, allowing it to stick around for longer games. Most Kingambit should use Supreme Overlord for its excellent and consistent effect, though Defiant is a viable alternative to specifically punish Landorus-T, KOing it with Knock Off into Sucker Punch, both at +1 Attack, and also punish Defog attempts from the likes of Zapdos and Corviknight. The EV spread allows Kingambit to outspeed Clefable lacking Speed investment.

Pokemon such as Mega Medicham and Tapu Lele benefit from Gholdengo's absence. Iron Defense variants of Zamazenta and Mega Medicham particularly benefit from Kingambit's ability to deal with the aforementioned Ghost-types, as they are difficult for them to break while also being able to cripple them with status effects. Access to Knock Off allows Kingambit to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes such as Alomomola, Zapdos, and Moltres for the benefit of hazard-setting teammates such as Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Mega Diancie. Kingambit struggles against faster Pokemon such as Zamazenta, Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Kartana. Partners such as Zapdos and Moltres can aid Kingambit by answering multiple of these Pokemon at once. Bulkier Pokemon such as Melmetal, Ting-Lu, and Toxapex are able to consistently answer Kingambit defensively, so Tapu Lele, Ogerpon-W, and Raging Bolt are greatly appreciated for their ability to immediately threaten these Pokemon. It is worth noting that a significant majority of the Kingambit checks mentioned are susceptible to losing their item to Knock Off.

ubers.overview: Supreme Overlord, a high Attack stat, access to Swords Dance and Sucker Punch, and a wide variety of items and Tera types at its disposal make Kingambit one of the most dangerous late-game sweepers in the tier, being able to use Terastallization to lure in and beat Pokemon that would normally check it and completely take games at the drop of a hat. It also has an amazing defensive typing that lets it easily set up on metagame staples like Lunala and Necrozma-DM to start its sweep. However, the abundance of common Dark-resistant Pokemon in the tier makes making complete comebacks harder, as Pokemon like Koraidon, Zacian-C, and Arceus-Fairy, among others, can take a Sucker Punch and end its attempt at a sweep either by OHKOing it or burning it, though this can be circumvented with Terastallization. Kingambit is also forced into not coming in for the majority of the game, as it's heavily reliant on using up its HP or Terastallization to sweep, and when no teammates have fainted, it is weak compared to the rest of the metagame.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Tera Flying can be used to become immune to Ground, allowing it to constantly come in on Ground attacks from Arceus-Ground and Landorus-T without sacrificing the item slot for Air Balloon. Tera Ghost can also be used for an immunity to Fighting-type attacks and Extreme Speed, but Kingambit is resistant to Extreme Speed anyway and the Fighting immunity isn't that worth it over other Tera types like Fire. Heavy-Duty Boots can be used to prevent Kingambit from being chipped down by entry hazards over the course of a game on a bulky offense team.

Checks and Counters

Dark-resistant Pokemon: Pokemon that resist Kingambit's Sucker Punch, like Koraidon, Zacian-C, and Arceus-Fairy, are very common, so Kingambit can have a hard time breaking through these Pokémon. There are also a lot of Pokémon that can Terastallize into a Dark-resistant type, like Lunala and Ho-Oh, among others.

Ho-Oh: Ho-Oh can easily shrug off Kingambit's Sucker Punches, outspeed it, and retaliate with Sacred Fire. Kingambit can circumvent this with Lum Berry or Tera Fire, but it still needs to be wary of Whirlwind.

Defensive Arceus Formes: Arceus-Fairy, Arceus-Ground, and Arceus-Water can all easily take Kingambit's attacks and threaten Kingambit with either burn from Will-O-Wisp or damage with Judgement, especially if Kingambit has already Terastallized into a Dark- or Fire-type. Kingambit has ways of playing around these, though, like Lum Berry, Air Balloon, or just pressuring them with entry hazard chip damage.

Landorus-T: Landorus-T’s Intimidate can make Kingambit thud in the face of it and can use these free turns to set up Stealth Rock, stop it from setting up with Taunt, or just threaten an Earthquake, all while racking up chip damage with Rocky Helmet. However, Landorus-T lacks reliable recovery, so it can get chipped down over the course of the game to the point where Kingambit is able to break through.

Swords Dance.description:
Every part of this set aims to make sure Kingambit can finish off the opposing team with Sucker Punch, as due to the massive damage output of Ubers, Kingambit only gets one chance to sweep. Black Glasses makes Kingambit's Dark-type moves hit astronomically hard, especially with Tera Dark, being able to OHKO Tera Fire Calyrex-I and Zacian-C as well as Koraidon with minimal chip damage with Sucker Punch after a Swords Dance boost and 5 Supreme Overlord boosts. Air Balloon allows Kingambit to come in on the multitude of Ground-type attacks from Arceus-Ground, Landorus-T, and Necrozma-DM, allowing it an opportunity to set up. Lum Berry allows it to absorb burns from Ho-Oh and defensive Arceus formes, allowing Kingambit to forgo Tera Fire for another Tera type. Tera Dark powers up Kingambit's Dark- type moves even further, allowing Kingambit to, crucially, OHKO Ho-Oh and Arceus-Ground with a Swords Dance boosted Sucker Punch with 5 Supreme Overlord boosts. Tera Fire grants Kingambit a burn immunity and a Fire resistance while removing its Fighting weakness, which allow it to set up on Pokemon like Ho-Oh, Koraidon, and Zacian-C.

Kingambit fits best on hyper offensive teams that need a late-game cleaner and a revenge killer for Pokemon like Calyrex-I, Necrozma-DM, and Eternatus. As it's fairly weak without a significant amount of teammates fainted, entry hazard setters like Glimmora and Deoxys-S are useful for weakening checks like Zacian-C and Koraidon for Kingambit to sweep. In terms of offensive teammates, Koraidon and Zacian-C are amazing teammates, as they can wear down or force common checks such as Ho-Oh, Landorus-T, and defensive Arceus forms to Terastallize, allowing Kingambit to sweep later. Extreme Killer Arceus can force Koraidon and Kyogre to Terastallize into a Ghost-type, allowing Kingambit to beat them with Sucker Punch, and one can wear down checks like Kyogre and defensive Arceus formes for the other to break through. Necrozma-DM can lure in Ho-Oh and cripple it with either Knock Off or Stone Edge, allowing Kingambit to muscle through. Meteor Beam Eternatus can also force in and damage Ho-Oh while also threatening Arceus-Fairy and Arceus-Water, while Kingambit can deal with Mewtwo and Necrozma-DM for Eternatus.

ou.overview: Kingambit shines as one of the tier's most dangerous sweepers thanks to its solid STAB combination, superb defensive typing, high Attack stat, access to Swords Dance, and incredible ability in Supreme Overlord. Its access to Sucker Punch allows it to compensate for its low Speed and serve as a potent revenge killer, picking off a wide range of faster targets such as Dragapult, Deoxys-S, and Iron Moth. It can also customize its EV spread, item choice, and Tera type selection to tailor itself to what its team desires and overcome many would-be answers. For example, Tera Flying and Air Balloon improve Kingambit's matchup against Ground-types, Tera Fire and Lum Berry let it foil attempted burns from Will-O-Wisp, and Tera Ghost flips its Fighting weakness and turns the tables on Body Press Corviknight and Fighting-types like Zamazenta and Great Tusk. Thanks to these traits and flexibility, Kingambit is welcomed by nearly every offensive archetype in the tier. However, it is heavily burdened by a crippling weakness to Fighting, as well as common attacking types like Fire and Ground. This leaves it struggling against common threats like Zamazenta and Great Tusk without Terastallizing, and plenty of Pokemon like Gholdengo, Deoxys-S, and Iron Crown often slap on Fighting-type coverage to deal with it. Additionally, these Pokemon, as well as Corviknight and Dondozo, often utilize Tera Fighting specifically to turn the tables on Kingambit. Tera Fairy is also commonplace in the tier, as Pokemon like Gholdengo, Raging Bolt, and Iron Moth sometimes utilize it in part to avoid being revenge killed by Kingambit's Dark-type attacks. Additionally, Kingambit's low Speed forces it to rely on Sucker Punch to deal with faster teams and play carefully around Encore from foes such as Ogerpon-W, Dragonite, and Iron Valiant. Relying on Sucker Punch also makes Kingambit vulnerable to well-timed status moves such as Will-O-Wisp, Substitute, and recovery moves from Pokemon like Darkrai, Dragapult, Kyurem, and Iron Moth. The ubiquity of priority moves, such as Raging Bolt's Thunderclap and Dragonite's Extreme Speed, is also an issue for Kingambit's Sucker Punch. On top of this, Kingambit lacks reliable recovery, and it struggles to fit all the moves it wants in one set to threaten targets like Great Tusk, opposing Kingambit, and Hisuian Samurott.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Kingambit has a few other Tera types that it can make use of. Tera Grass flips the matchup against Ogerpon-W and lets Kingambit set up on Ground-types like Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Iron Treads. Tera Poison grants Kingambit a Fighting resistance while keeping its immunity to Toxic and has the benefit of absorbing Toxic Spikes for teams that are otherwise at a disadvantage against them. Black Belt can be used on Tera Fighting + Low Kick sets, with the boost in particular letting it 2HKO Dondozo with five Supreme Overlord boosts. Clear Amulet is another item option to ignore Landorus-T's Intimidate and disrupt Parting Shot from Pecharunt to stop it from switching out. Thunder Wave can be used to cripple incoming switch-ins, such as Zamazenta and Moltres, and it synergizes well with Iron Head's chance to flinch.

Swords Dance.description:
Kingambit is a potent late-game cleaner with Swords Dance, Sucker Punch, and Supreme Overlord. Kingambit can drop one of its STAB moves for Low Kick, which hits Hisuian Samurott and opposing Kingambit super effectively while netting crucial benchmarks such as potentially OHKOing Ting-Lu at +2, especially because common Fighting-resistant Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Pecharunt want nothing to do with Kingambit; Low Kick should only be used on maximum Speed variants to try and hit opposing Kingambit first. However, dropping Iron Head means it is walled by Fairy-types and Tera Fairy users such as Clefable, Galarian Weezing, Gholdengo, and Moltres, while dropping Kowtow Cleave makes Kingambit struggle to beat neutral walls like Corviknight, Alomomola, and Zapdos. Leftovers takes further advantage of its defensive profile and works well with Sucker Punch, as foes attempting to play around it will just grant Kingambit more health. Leftovers is especially more effective on variants running the bulky EV spread. Lum Berry mainly prevents Kingambit from being shut down by a burn from the likes of Dragapult, Darkrai, Alomomola, and Moltres. Black Glasses and Tera Dark together should exclusively be used with Kowtow Cleave, as these propel Kingambit's offensive pressure further; with five Supreme Overlord boosts under its belt, Kingambit can reach feats such as 2HKOing even Dondozo with Kowtow Cleave and OHKOing Dragonite through Multiscale with Sucker Punch at +2. Air Balloon allows Kingambit to set up on would-be checks in Landorus-T and most Great Tusk; become a sturdy switch-in to offensive threats like Kyurem and Dragonite that mostly rely on their Ground-type coverage to hit it; and gain an immunity to Spikes, which is one of the ways to limit Kingambit's health before it gets going. The latter reasoning thus makes Heavy-Duty Boots an appealing alternative option to combat entry hazards in general, especially on hazard-stacking teams that lack reliable hazard removers while aiming to play a longer game. Similar to Air Balloon, Shuca Berry can be used instead for its matchup against the aforementioned Ground-types and Ground coverage moves; it gives Kingambit more freedom to take on other attacks before if necessary and it hides Kingambit's item from the opponent at the cost of a complete immunity to Ground, even against Spikes. Tera Ghost flips its Fighting weakness, letting it go toe-to-toe against otherwise solid checks in IronPress users like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Zamazenta more reliably, especially because it naturally puts fear in the likes of Dragapult and Gholdengo from trying to exploit its newfound Ghost weakness. Tera Fighting can be used on Low Kick variants, boosting the move to pressure Ting-Lu, Dondozo, and Great Tusk hard. Tera Fire provides a burn immunity from Moltres and Will-O-Wisp users like Dragapult and Darkrai, even flipping its Fire weakness against the aforementioned Moltres and other threats like Cinderace and Iron Moth. Tera Flying is an option for its complete immunity to Ground moves from checks like Great Tusk and Landorus-T, especially on sets without Air Balloon. An Adamant nature is preferred for its power, with maximum Speed investment to Speed tie opposing Kingambit; going even further with a Jolly nature gives better odds in winning this interaction while also outspeeding some Speed-invested variants of Skarmory, Primarina, and Corviknight. A bulkier EV spread further takes advantage of Kingambit's hit-taking abilities, remarkably reaching feats such as surviving Great Tusk's Headlong Rush, Choice Specs Kyurem's Earth Power, and +1 Glimmora's Earth Power.

Kingambit's late-game potential and defensive utility make it a near staple on any offensive archetype, ranging from bulky to hyper offense, while still being capable of fitting on balance teams. Physically offensive teammates like Ogerpon-W, Zamazenta, Dragonite, and Swords Dance Iron Valiant are helpful to overwhelm shared checks like Zamazenta, Landorus-T, Moltres, and Dondozo. Simultaneously, special attackers like Calm Mind Iron Valiant, Gholdengo, Dragapult, Iron Moth, Kyurem, and Raging Bolt are similarly helpful to handle and pressure these checks, preventing them from getting free turns to set up or recover health. Additionally, their synergy doesn't stop there, as Zamazenta and some Iron Valiant variants appreciate Kingambit's ability to switch into and threaten Gholdengo and Galarian Slowking; Dragonite can take on Iron Moth and provide a Ground immunity against Landorus-T; Gholdengo can switch into and check Zamazenta for Kingambit; Dragapult can check Zamazenta and bring Kingambit safely via U-turn; and Kyurem and Raging Bolt can threaten and force damage, respectively, onto Kingambit's Ground-type checks in Landorus-T, Great Tusk, and Ting-Lu. Dark-type offensive threats in Darkrai and Hisuian Samurott, in particular, are notable in forming a Dark-type spam core together with Kingambit, which is capable of overwhelming Dark-resistant Pokemon like Zamazenta and Tera Fairy users like Gholdengo, Garganacl, and Moltres together. Moreover, the aforementioned Hisuian Samurott helps chip foes into Kingambit's KO range with its entry hazards, whether it's softening walls like Ting-Lu or potential revenge killers like Ogerpon-W and Iron Moth into Sucker Punch range; thus, other hazard setters like Landorus-T, Glimmora, Deoxys-S, and Ting-Lu are similarly valuable. Defensive pivots like Landorus-T, Zapdos, Pecharunt, and Galarian Slowking are common faces on bulky offense teams that help switch into threats like Cinderace, Landorus-T, Great Tusk, and Zamazenta for Kingambit and are great at bringing it in safely onto the field, especially with Intimidate and Parting Shot to ease its setup; in return, Kingambit helps check Darkrai, Gholdengo, and Dragapult for Galarian Slowking and Pecharunt. Other and more specific offensive playstyles like Sticky Web, dual screens, and the fringe Trick Room can also mesh well with Kingambit. Sticky Web from Ribombee and Araquanid compensates for Kingambit's low Speed against faster threats like Raging Bolt, Hisuian Samurott, and Great Tusk if Kingambit runs a Jolly nature, even making it less reliant on Sucker Punch mind games. Dual screens from Alolan Ninetales give Kingambit an easier time setting up and let it stomach even super effective hits from Iron Moth and Darkrai. Similar to Sticky Web, Trick Room set by teammates like Hatterene can compensate for Kingambit's poor Speed tier, especially against fast foes like Iron Valiant and Encore Ogerpon-W. On balance teams, a sturdier defensive backbone with the likes of Skarmory, Corviknight, Clefable, Gliscor, and Alomomola is similarly appreciated, as on top of switching into Kingambit's aforementioned checks and revenge killers, they can also set entry hazards and bring it in safely via slow pivots; Alomomola can also provide Kingambit with Wish support, while Gliscor and Clefable can further weaken walls with Knock Off. Outside of its utility set, Swords Dance Gliscor, in particular, is also a strong setup sweeper that complements Kingambit well.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
This analysis is for the Regulation C format of Battle Stadium Singles, which lasts until June 30th, 2023. For more information on this format and its current events, check out this page!

If you feel this analysis is missing anything important or needs an update, feel free to suggest any changes here.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Kingambit sets itself apart from most other Dark-types with its bulk and typing, which make it a reasonable check against Gholdengo that lack Focus Blast, and less vulnerable to Flutter Mane.

  • Guillotine: This makes Kingambit far more difficult to wall with foes such as Dondozo and Ting-Lu.

  • Brick Break versus Low Kick: Low Kick is Kingambit's best option against Tera Normal Dragonite and other Kingambit, but Brick Break is preferred because it deals far more damage to Chi-Yu.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Kingambit has a good typing, but its vulnerability to Fighting-type attacks or need to boost its power for late-game sweeps means it benefits a lot from Terastallization.

  • Dark: Tera Dark makes Kingambit even harder to wall and removes its irritating Ground weakness, though powerful Fighting-type attacks can still be a problem.

  • Flying: Tera Flying covers Kingambit's issues with Fighting- and Ground-type attacks very well and lets it deal big damage to Fighting-types like Annihilape and Great Tusk with Tera Blast.

  • Fairy: With Tera Fairy and Tera Blast, Kingambit improves its matchup against Chien-Pao and can deal serious damage to Iron Hands and Great Tusk, but it becomes vulnerable to Gholdengo.

Abilities

  • Supreme Overlord: This ability makes Kingambit a deadly cleaner in late-game scenarios, and is generally the most consistent ability.

  • Defiant: Defiant prevents Kingambit from falling to Charm Flutter Mane, and is a good option for punishing speed control options like Rock Tomb.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 108 HP / 252 Atk / 148 Spe: This EV spread has enough Speed to outspeed most Corviknight and Skeledirge, and it still has enough bulk to survive one unboosted Body Press from Corviknight. Since this is a fairly congested Speed range, feel free to move some Attack EVs to Speed.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe: Using maximum Speed might seem absurd on such a slow Pokemon, but outspeeding most Skeledirge, Corviknight, and opposing Kingambit can make this worth it.

Items

  • Assault Vest: Kingambit's bulk is perfect for Assault Vest, letting it perform well against Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle.

  • Black Glasses: While its boost to Dark-type attacks isn't as high as Life Orb's, Black Glasses is a better fit for Kingambit's bulk due to the lack of recoil.

  • Sitrus Berry and 244 HP EVs: The burst of recovery helps Kingambit check Gholdengo better. Make sure to run 244 HP EVs to have an even HP stat. This will make Sitrus Berry activate after one use of Ruination.

Stealth Rock Support.description:
• Kingambit's excellent bulk and offensive presence make it a good, if unexpected, setter of Stealth Rock.

  • Brick Break versus Low Kick: While weak, Brick Break is the preferred fighting move for hitting Chi-Yu hard. Low Kick does more damage to Ting-Lu, other Kingambit and Tera Normal Dragonite.

  • Thunder Wave: Thunder Wave isn't a particularly common move on Kingambit, potentially letting it surprise some switch-ins like Iron Moth and Annihilape.

Other Options

  • Guillotine: With Guillotine, passive play from foes like Corviknight and Dondozo becomes far more risky.

  • Taunt: Taunt is effective at shutting down common support Pokemon such as Dondozo and Toxapex.

  • Tera Blast: Tera Fairy Blast is Kingambit's best shot against Iron Hands, one of its biggest checks. It also makes sense with Tera Flying to hit Great Tusk hard.

  • Metal Burst: If using Focus Sash, Metal Burst deals serious damage against a wide variety of leads.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: While Terastallization is fully viable, this Kingambit's focus on setting up Stealth Rock early means it's not needed to function.

  • Flying: Tera Flying covers Kingambit's Fighting- and Ground-type weaknesses, making it do especially well against

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy can help prevent Iron Hands, one of the best Kingambit checks in the game, from OHKOing it.

  • Dark: When using Sucker Punch, Tera Dark gives Kingambit some late-game cleaning potential.

Items

Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's quick burst of recovery keeps Kingambit more relevant in the later stages of the game. Make sure to use an even HP stat so that Ruination will activate Sitrus Berry.

  • Black Glasses: Kingambit's bulk and support options make Black Glasses a preferable option over Life Orb for more power, especially when using Sucker Punch.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash will let Kingambit survive even the strongest Fighting-type attacks, if Stealth Rock desperately needs to be set up.

  • Chople Berry: Chople Berry eases Kingambit's devastating Fighting-type weakness, though note powerful STAB users of Close Combat such as Iron Hands require massive Defense investment to survive. 252 HP and 12 Defense EVs can be used to survive Iron Valiant's Close Combat.

Abilities

  • Supreme Overlord: Even though this Kingambit is often set out early-game to set up Stealth Rock, Supreme Overlord gives it the flexibility to function later in the game if Stealth Rock isn't needed or if it manages to set up Stealth Rock without much harm to itself.

  • Defiant: Besides punishing the rare use of Intimidate, Defiant lets Kingambit defeat Charm Flutter Mane.

EV Spreads

  • 244 HP / 252 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 4 Spe: This EV spread gives Kingambit an even HP stat, letting Sitrus Berry activate on the first use of Ruination.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe: Maximizing Speed lets Kingambit get the jump on opposing Kingambit and slower variants of Wo-Chien, Skeledirge, Corviknight, and Iron Hands.

Swords Dance.description:
• Swords Dance, mixed with Kingambit's naturally high Attack as well as access to Defiant to scare off Intimidate users and priority in Sucker Punch, makes it one of the most effective setup sweepers in the metagame. Its respectable bulk, especially its base 120 Defense, often allows it to set up multiple Swords Dances in one match.
  • Kowtow Cleave offers strong and consistent damage. It OHKOes Gholdengo and Indeedee-F without a boost and decimates bulky Pokemon like Amoonguss and Entei at +2, netting guaranteed KOs after minimal chip damage.
  • Sucker Punch compensates for Kingambit's low Speed, OHKOing faster attackers such as Landorus and Ogerpon-W after a boost. It also allows Kingambit to revenge kill weakened foes when entering the field.
  • Dread Plate (or Black Glasses) is vital for Kingambit to secure numerous benchmarks for OHKOs or 2HKOs on Pokemon such as Landorus with Sucker Punch and Ogerpon-W with Kowtow Cleave. Other items can be used in niche scenarios, such as Leftovers for gradual health recovery and Grassy Seed on teams with Rillaboom to become resilient to most physical attacks.
  • Kingambit has a multitude of options for its Tera type. Tera Dark can be used to strengthen its attacks and reduce its weakness to Iron Hands's Fighting-type attacks to only 2x while removing its weaknesses to Incineroar's Flare Blitz, Ogerpon-H's Ivy Cudgel, and Landorus's Earth Power. Tera Dragon allows Kingambit to resist attacks from Ogerpon-H, Ogerpon-W, and Chi-Yu. Tera Flying grants an immunity to Landorus's Ground-type moves as well as another way to resist Iron Hands's attacks, but it gives Kingambit a much worse matchup against the faster Raging Bolt and Chien-Pao.
  • Kingambit appreciates partners that can create space for it to set up a Swords Dance; this includes Fake Out users, such as Incineroar, Rillaboom, and Iron Hands, and redirection support from the likes of Sinistcha and Ogerpon-W. One bonus of running Incineroar is that it actually improves Kingambit's matchup against opposing Incineroar, as it can easily switch into Flare Blitz if necessary or at least reduce the damage Kingambit takes from an opposing Incineroar's Flare Blitz. Landorus fends off some of Kingambit's biggest threats like Iron Hands and Entei, while it appreciates Kingambit's ability to remove some of its threats like Ogerpon-W with a boosted Sucker Punch. Landorus is also one of Kingambit's best offensive checks due to its strong Earth Power, so Kingambit appreciates the support of Jolly Ogerpon-W and Chien-Pao to threaten it offensively.
  • Kingambit's Defiant supports strong physical attackers such as Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Chien-Pao by deterring opposing Intimidate users. Its Steel typing and opportunity to get a Defiant boost from Bleakwind Storm also make it one of the strongest Tornadus checks in the tier, which is appreciated by the aforementioned Grass-types. Gouging Fire can further boost Kingambit's Attack with Howl, while Kingambit deters Intimidate users, creating room for multiple turns of boosting.

anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Mental Herb can be used to allow Kingambit to set up in front of Pokemon running Taunt or to avoid getting locked into an unfavorable move by Encore Calyrex-S. Lum Berry is also another option that allows Kingambit to avoid getting burned by defensive Arceus formes and Skeledirge without having to Terastallize. Defiant can also be used to help against Sticky Web teams and Landorus-T but is usually suboptimal, as it does nothing in other matchups.

Checks and Counters

Dark-resistant Pokemon: Koraidon and Zacian can take Kingambit's Dark-type attacks fairly well and threaten an OHKO with their strong Fighting- and Fire-type attacks, usually forcing Kingambit to switch out.

Bulky Ground-types: Ting-Lu, Arceus-Ground, and Landorus-T can all take an attack from Kingambit and threaten it back with their super effective STAB moves. However, they must be wary of Tera Flying.

Physical Walls: Physical walls like defensive Arceus formes and Ho-Oh can switch into Kingambit's attacks and cripple it with burn, though they must be wary of Tera Fire.

Encore Calyrex-S: If Kingambit isn't running Mental Herb, then Calyrex-S can use Encore to lock it into Swords Dance or Sucker Punch and set up Nasty Plot for free.

Swords Dance.description:
With the help of Supreme Overlord and strong priority in Sucker Punch, Kingambit serves as an excellent late-game sweeper. Its typing also grants it the ability to soft check Calyrex-S and Extreme Killer Arceus, two of the most prominent Pokemon in AG. Kowtow Cleave gives Kingambit a reliable Dark-type STAB move and lets it hit Ho-Oh, Miraidon, and Kyogre harder on the switch. Low Kick can be used instead to better check Arceus and hit Ting-Lu harder, OHKOing Arceus after a Swords Dance and Ting-Lu with one Supreme Overlord boost, while also allowing Kingambit to check opposing Kingambit. Leftovers improves Kingambit's longevity and improves its ability to check Calyrex-S and Extreme Killer Arceus, while Black Glasses increases Kingambit's damage even further, notably giving Sucker Punch a very good chance to OHKO 120 HP Miraidon with two Supreme Overlord boosts and a Swords Dance. Air Balloon can be used instead to give Kingambit an easier time versus Ground-type Pokemon such as Arceus-Ground, Ting-Lu, and Landorus-T by giving it a temporary immunity to their super effective Ground-type attacks. Kingambit also has great flexibility with its Tera type. Tera Fire gives Kingambit an immunity to burn and a resistance to Fire-type attacks from Koraidon and Ho-Oh; it also lets Kingambit avoid an OHKO from Koraidon's Low Kick from full HP. On the other hand, Tera Dark boosts Kingambit's Dark-type attacks to ridiculous levels and can be used in conjunction with Black Glasses to give Kingambit's +2 Sucker Punch a 50% chance to OHKO Koraidon after one layer of Spikes and five boosts of Supreme Overlord. Tera Flying is yet another option that gives Kingambit an immunity to Ground-type attacks from Arceus-Ground and Ting-Lu and a resistance to Fighting-type attacks from Koraidon and Zacian-C. Kingambit must be wary of Terastallizing, however, as it removes its resistance to Arceus's Extreme Speed, making it vulnerable to being revenge killed. The given EV spread allows Kingambit to outspeed uninvested Skeledirge.

Due to its lack of recovery, Kingambit fits best on offensive teams that appreciate its ability to check Calyrex-S and Extreme Killer Arceus short-term, as well as its efficacy into Sticky Web teams due to its strong priority. Funnily enough, Calyrex-S and Extreme Killer Arceus also make some of Kingambit's best partners. Calyrex-S appreciates Kingambit's ability to check opposing Arceus and, in return, helps break through Ting-Lu and Ho-Oh. Meanwhile, Arceus creates a strong priority spam core with Kingambit that overwhelms their shared checks such as Zacian-C, Ho-Oh, and defensive Arceus formes. Arceus and Kingambit also both check Calyrex-S, which is helpful because it helps avoid bad situations created by Encore. Kingambit can also benefit from the fact that Arceus often forces the opponent to Terastallize their Koraidon into the Ghost-type, which makes it easier for Kingambit to sweep late-game. Other physical wallbreakers such as Koraidon and Zacian-C also have excellent synergy with Kingambit, as they can help wear down opposing physical walls such as the aforementioned Ho-Oh and defensive Arceus formes as well as Landorus-T. Swords Dance Koraidon in particular is a great partner, since it often forces Ho-Oh to Terastallize into the Fairy-type, which makes Ho-Oh vulnerable to Iron Head. In return, Kingambit can switch into Calyrex-S and Arceus trying to revenge kill Koraidon. As Kingambit is often forced out by Fire- and Fighting- type attacks from wallbreakers such as Koraidon and Zacian-C, a strong defensive core is necessary. Landorus-T can switch into both Zacian-C and Koraidon and rack up chip damage on them with Rocky Helmet and Stealth Rock. Stealth Rock also helps chip down walls like support Arceus formes and opposing Landorus-T. Defensive Arceus formes like Arceus-Fairy and Arceus-Water can also switch into these threats and spread burn, which can help rack up chip damage and make it easier for Kingambit to set up. Ting-Lu switches into Miraidon and Arceus-Ground, acts as another check to Calyrex-S, and can set up Spikes that helps break down defensive Arceus formes and Koraidon over the course the game.

Offensive Utility.description:
Great Tusk is a behemoth of role compression. It provides an imposing offensive presence, access to entry hazards and hazard removal, and a defensive profile that enables it to check certain physical attackers such as Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar all in one slot. Rapid Spin enables the removal of hazards in the face of nearly every hazard setter in the tier such as Heatran, Garchomp, and Ting-Lu, which is specially given the difficulty of spinblocking Great Tusk, which is able to threaten massive damage on Gholdengo and Pecharunt. Additionally, Ice Spinner is necessary for threatening Flying-types such as Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Zapdos. Great Tusk is a good Stealth Rock setter given its ability to force switches against foes such as Galarian Slowking and Gholdengo and to threaten removal options such as Landorus-T and opposing Great Tusk if carrying Icium Z. Close Combat can be run to deny Ogerpon-W a safe switch in and better pressure Skarmory, Corviknight, and Rotom-W. Alternatively, Knock Off is an option for making progress against Great Tusk's checks, such as through removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Alomomola, Moltres, and Zapdos, as well as hitting Air Balloon Gholdengo for more damage. Stone Edge OHKOes Moltres and Volcarona, as well as 2HKOes Zapdos without making contact. Heavy-Duty Boots protects Great Tusk from Spikes and particularly Toxic Spikes, which is important given its role as hazard removal. Leftovers is another source of longevity, providing passive recovery for longer matchups in exchange for increased vulnerability to offensive hazard pressure. Booster Energy makes Great Tusk nigh unwallable, enabling it to threaten 2HKOs on standard Alomomola, Corviknight, and Rotom-W with its STAB options. Booster Energy sets should always carry Close Combat to maximize wallbreaking potential. Subzero Slammer lets Great Tusk OHKO Tornadus-T and Zapdos, as well as Landorus-T even after Intimidate, while weakening the effect of Knock Off from the likes of Kingambit and Mega Tyranitar. Finally, Rocky Helmet provides a source of chip damage against the physical attackers Great Tusk switches into, including punishing U-turn from pivots such as Landorus-T and Mega Scizor.

Great Tusk's ability to perform a plethora of roles leads it to fit best on offense and bulky offense due to its lack of longevity. However, it is also effective on balance teams, especially with the right teammates such as Alomomola, as its traits are highly coveted nonetheless. Great Tusk is often forced out by special attackers, such as Tapu Lele and Mega Charizard Y, meaning teammates such as Melmetal and Toxapex are strong teammates. Great Tusk is also not a blanket check to physical attackers, as its somewhat double-edged defensive typing leaves it with common weaknesses to attacks from Ogerpon-W, Weavile, and Kartana. As a result, defensive Pokemon with complementary typings such as Ferrothorn and Alomomola are effective partners. In particular, the latter can also provide Great Tusk with Wish support to mitigate its lack of longevity. With regards to its offensive profile, Great Tusk appreciates the ability of powerful special wallbreakers such as Raging Bolt and Tapu Lele to break through its checks such as Alomomola and Skarmory. In return, Great Tusk can exploit their checks such as Ting-Lu, Ferrothorn, and Melmetal as opportunities to set up Stealth Rock or remove entry hazards with ease. On offense teams, Great Tusk can pair well with other physical attackers such as Kingambit and Swords Dance Iron Valiant, being able to overwhelm or threaten common switch-ins such as Landorus-T and Moltres. Finally, Great Tusk forms a powerful core with Mega Charizard Y, providing premium hazard removal to address its crippling Stealth Rock weakness, the ability to switch into powerful physical attackers such as Mega Tyranitar, and threatening Mega Charizard Y's checks such as Dragonite, Toxapex, and Raging Bolt. In exchange, Mega Charizard Y's Drought provides Great Tusk with a Protosynthesis boost at no cost to the item slot while using Great Tusk's switch-ins such as Alomomola and Slowbro as wallbreaking opportunities.

Defensive.description:
Defensive Great Tusk acts as important glue on teams due to its incredible role compression by acting as a defensive wall, setting entry hazards, and clearing them. Utilizing its high bulk and HP, defensive Great Tusk acts as a great check to many metagame staples such as all-out attacker Zamazenta, Kingambit, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Tyranitar. Earthquake is the preferred STAB move on Great Tusk, but Headlong Rush can also be run for better damage rolls, such as an OHKO on offensive Gholdengo and a 2HKO on Kartana, at the cost of lowering its defenses. Moreover, Headlong Rush isn't weakened by Grassy Terrain. Ice Spinner is used mainly to threaten Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Dragonite while also hitting Zapdos and opposing Great Tusk super effectively. Great Tusk can freely remove hazards, since spinblockers like Dragapult and Gholdengo are threatened by moves such as Ice Spinner and Earthquake, respectively, and Knock Off. The last slot on this set is flexible; running Stealth Rock turns Great Tusk into an effective hazard setter, threatening most hazard removal options such as Landorus-T and opposing Great Tusk with Ice Spinner. Knock Off can also be run to remove key items, like Heavy-Duty Boots from the likes of Zapdos, Tornadus-T, and Moltres as well as Leftovers from Landorus-T and opposing Great Tusk, with the added benefit of being able to hit Air Balloon Gholdengo and Dragapult super effectively. Body Press is an option in the final slot to surprise Ferrothorn, Ting-Lu, and Terapagos that has had its Tera Shell broken. 40 Speed EVs allow defensive Great Tusk to outspeed base 90s like Moltres as well as other prominent threats such as uninvested Landorus-T and bulky Gholdengo. Heavy-Duty Boots prevents Great Tusk from taking too much chip damage from hazards, while Leftovers helps in checking the threats and increases Great Tusk's longevity. Rocky Helmet is another item that can be run on Great Tusk to punish many physical attackers that either attack it recklessly or try to gain momentum like Landorus-T, Zamazenta, and Kingambit.

Defensive Great Tusk fits best on balance and bulky offense teams, which value its role compression. The main attributes hindering Great Tusk are its typing and lack of longevity. Thus, Great Tusk appreciates partners like Alomomola, which helps with its lack of longevity by Wish passing; additionally, Alomomola is able to switch into common Water-types like Hisuian Samurott and Urshifu-R. It also appreciates Pokemon such as Volt Switch Raging Bolt and Zapdos that can reliably switch in against common Flying-types such as Zapdos, Tornadus-T, and Mega Charizard Y and Water-types like Ogerpon-W while also threatening them offensively. Steel-type partners like Mega Scizor and Melmetal are greatly valued due to their ability to switch into fast Fairy-type foes like Tapu Lele. Moreover, the hazards set up by Great Tusk pressure many switch-ins on entry, forcing progress over time. Being able to remove the items on checks to Raging Bolt like Leftovers from Ting-Lu and Assault Vest from Melmetal allows Raging Bolt to break through switch-ins with its STAB moves aided by Great Tusk's hazards. Furthermore, these teammates appreciate Great Tusk's ability to spin away hazards for them and can continue to check threats to Great Tusk. Defensive Great Tusk also pairs extremely well with Mega Charizard Y, which appreciates Great Tusk removing Stealth Rock and checking Pokemon such as Mega Tyranitar. In return, Mega Charizard Y is able to break through walls like Alomomola, Clefable, Skarmory, and Corviknight. Mega Charizard Y also sets up sun, granting Great Tusk a Defense boost due to Protosynthesis, which allows it to better wall physical attackers.

Bulk Up.description:
Great Tusk's already great Attack and physical bulk combined with Bulk Up make it a premier setup sweeper that can use its bulk to set up with ease on Pokemon like Dragonite, Garchomp, and Mega Scizor. Ice Spinner takes care of most Pokemon immune to Headlong Rush like Landorus-T, Zapdos, Mega Latios, and Gliscor, among others, while also dealing with Grass-types like Rillaboom and Meowscarada. Rapid Spin is an amazing utility move for Great Tusk, as the extra boosts to Great Tusk's Speed help it avoid revenge killing attempts from Speed Booster Energy Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and let it boost Speed after its Booster Energy is used up. Rapid Spin also removes entry hazards for Great Tusk's teammates to clean up after it. The EV spread guarantees Great Tusk gains a Speed boost from its Booster Energy, allowing it to threaten Pokemon it would normally be threatened by, like Mega Diancie, Dragapult, and Mega Medicham.

Bulk Up sets are most commonly used on hyper offense teams that appreciate another setup sweeper that can threaten common Pokemon like Landorus-T, Kingambit, and Raging Bolt for its teammates to cleave through. These teams also appreciate Great Tusk's ability to remove entry hazards, which is extremely helpful for Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Z-Move Dragonite. Great Tusk is easily revenge killed by Pokemon like mixed Iron Valiant and Choice Scarf users like Tapu Lele and Urshifu-R even with the Speed boost. Therefore, Pokemon that can switch into these Pokemon such as Mega Scizor for Tapu Lele and Kartana and Dragonite for Urshifu-R are appreciated. Great Tusk is weak to special attackers like the aforementioned Iron Valiant, Tapu Lele, Terapagos, and Volcarona, so Pokemon like Kingambit, Raging Bolt, Roaring Moon and your own Terapagos can be useful. Great Tusk also thuds into Pokemon that can take both of its moves, like Ogerpon-W, Moltres, Slowbro, and Alomomola, so Pokemon like your own Ogerpon-W, Raging Bolt, and Gholdengo are great partners that can chip down these Pokemon for Great Tusk to sweep.

Speed Booster.description:
• By using the Speed boost from Booster Energy, Great Tusk is able to outspeed Pokemon such as Meowscarada, Dragapult, Chien-Pao, and Spectrier.
  • Headlong Rush deals with Pokemon like Metagross and Iron Hands.
  • Close Combat is for Dark-type Pokemon such as Urshifu-S, Chien-Pao, Meowscarada, and Darkrai.
  • Bulk Up allows Great Tusk to set up and win against Pokemon such as Metagross and Ursaluna while also improving the chances to win against Pokemon like Pecharunt and Annihilape.
  • Megahorn is used for Hoopa-U, and it can be used to OHKO Ogerpon-W after a Bulk Up. Alternatively, Knock Off can be used to deal with Spectrier, offensive Dragapult, and Pokemon with Chople Berry such as Urshifu-S and Hisuian Goodra. Great Tusk can also run Ice Spinner for a guaranteed win against both Landorus formes and Garchomp. Taunt is also a viable option for better odds against Corviknight, Pecharunt, and stall Pokemon in general.
  • The EV spread gives Great Tusk the Speed boost from Booster Energy and the maximum possible Attack while letting it survive an Overheat from Modest Heatran.
  • While this set outspeeds most threats in the tier, it lacks the power to secure KOs against most bulky Pokemon like Raging Bolt and Volcanion; it also struggles against Fairy- and Water-type Pokemon like Sylveon, Primarina, Manaphy, and Walking Wake. Therefore, Pokemon like Hisuian Goodra, Metagross, Hoopa-U, and Iron Crown that can make up for Great Tusk's low initial power and low Special Defense are great partners for it.

Choice Band.description:
• Choice Band Great Tusk takes advantage of its unique typing and offensive power to deal great amount of damage to foes like Iron Hands, Roaring Moon, and Diancie.
  • Headlong Rush's damage gives Great Tusk better chances against foes like non-Weakness Policy Primarina if it's lacking Supercell Slam; if it doesn't have Heavy Slam, the move also has a chance to OHKO Sylveon and maximum Defense Diancie.
  • Earthquake is an alternative to Headlong Rush that, despite making Great Tusk lose some matchups due to the lack of immediate power, helps against the Roaring Moon matchup if it's lacking Ice Spinner.
  • Close Combat OHKOes Ursaluna and non-Chople Berry Urshifu-S.
  • Megahorn is for defensive Ogerpon-W and slower Hoopa-U.
  • Ice Spinner OHKOes Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Roaring Moon.
  • Supercell Slam targets Water-types like non-Weakness Policy Primarina.
  • Heavy Slam may be used for Diancie and Sylveon.
  • The EV spread allows Great Tusk to tank a Power Whip from Jolly Ogerpon-W and outspeed Raging Bolt.
  • Headlong Rush is a better option than Close Combat against foes like Hisuian Goodra, since it is able to defeat Great Tusk with the combination of Chople Berry + Counter.
  • Against Corviknight, Close Combat is preferred against Agility or faster variants. Supercell Slam is better suited for slower, bulkier sets.
  • Great Tusk often struggles against Fairy-type foes like Alolan Ninetales and Iron Valiant; therefore, teammates like Volcanion and Metagross are appreciated.

Offensive Utility (Fighting).description:
With an impressive physical statline, Great Tusk smashes through the competition, providing great utility and offensive presence all in one slot. Focus Sash synergizes well, as it lets Great Tusk take an attack from Flutter Mane and KO it in return and get rid of popular Air Balloon users such as Glimmora, Heatran, and Raging Bolt through the combination Rapid Spin and Earthquake. Earthquake is Great Tusk's key STAB move, threatening Poison-, Electric-, and Fire-types like Toxapex, Iron Hands, non-Air Balloon Heatran, and Ceruledge. Headlong Rush is another option to secure an OHKO on Greninja after Stealth Rock. Knock Off hits both Dragapult and Latios hard while providing general utility against the rest of the tier such as removing Choice Scarf, Rocky Helmet, and Heavy Duty Boots from the opposing team. Alternatively, Ice Spinner can be used to improve the Flying matchup, as it deals with Dragonite and Gliscor. Rapid Spin plays an important role by removing entry hazards from Great Tusk's side and boosting its Speed, allowing Great Tusk to outspeed many prominent threats such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Dragapult, and Latios. Taunt can be used instead to notably prevent Skarmory, Ting Lu, and Corviknight from setting up entry hazards, setting up itself, or using utility moves like Defog, Roost, and Whirlwind. Lastly, Great Tusk can set Stealth Rock up, ensuring opposing Focus Sashes will not impede the team's progress in the game.

Assault Vest Iron Hands and Gallade are both great partners, as they can absorb special hits that would OHKO Great Tusk from foes like Hatterene, Choice Scarf Greninja, and Choice Scarf Enamorus. They also aid Great Tusk, should its Focus Sash be disabled, by checking and OHKOing in retaliation popular Choice Specs users like Dragapult, Latios, and Flutter Mane, while they both appreciate Great Tusk's ability to remove entry hazards from the field. They both come with their matchups of predilection: Flying and Fairy for Iron Hands and Poison and Water for Gallade. Iron Hands takes on Primarina, Hatterene, and Corviknight, while Gallade slashes through Amoonguss, Galarian Weezing, and Keldeo. Choice Scarf Sneasler can deal with Grass- and Fairy-types such as the Ogerpon formes, Primarina, and Iron Valiant while retaining momentum with U-turn. With its especially large movepool, Iron Valiant can help Great Tusk in many ways, from getting rid of Flying-type Pokemon with BoltBeam coverage like Landorus, Corviknight, and Gliscor to deleting physical walls such as Sableye and Hippowdon with STAB Moonblast, and it appreciates Great Tusk's ability to remove Assault Vest from Tornadus-T. Water-type wallbreakers like Keldeo and Urshifu-R also synergize quite well with Great Tusk, as Great Tusk provides a useful Electric immunity, allowing them to focus on dismantling opposing defensive Pokemon such as Corviknight and Skarmory. Finally, Hisuian Lilligant provides some utility in the form of Sleep Powder and can also aid offensively in the Flying, Water, and Ground matchups with its Victory Dance set, effectively suppressing the likes of Urshifu-R, Swampert, and Landorus.

Defensive Utility (Fighting).description:
Boasting impressive bulk, Great Tusk takes the physical wall role for Fighting teams, being able to tank multiple hits from physical attackers such as Dragonite and Ceruledge. Earthquake threatens Poison-, Electric-, and Fire-types like Clodsire, Iron Hands, and non-Air Balloon Heatran. Knock Off hits Earthquake switch-ins such as Air Balloon Gholdengo, Latios, and Tornadus-T and removes their item. Alternatively, Ice Spinner can threaten Gliscor and Dragonite, preventing them from setting up on Great Tusk. Rapid Spin provides entry hazard control and boosts Great Tusk's Speed, which can allow it to weaken offensive foes such as Latios. Taunt can be used instead to notably prevent Skarmory, Ting-Lu, and Hippowdon from setting up hazards and prevents Corviknight's Defog. Lastly, Great Tusk can set Stealth Rock up, breaking Focus Sash on Ceruledge and Breloom and greatly helping the team progress in the game. The EV spread lets Great Tusk outspeed maximum Speed Modest Raging Bolt while maximizing Great Tusk's physical bulk.

Defensive Great Tusk appreciates teammates that can make up for its abysmal special bulk like Assault Vest Iron Hands and Assault Vest Gallade. Assault Vest Iron Hands deals with Flying- and Fairy-types threats such as Primarina, Hatterene, and Gyarados. Gallade gives Fighting teams the edge in troublesome matchups like Poison and Water by slashing through Keldeo, Amoonguss, and Galarian Weezing. In return, they both appreciate Great Tusk dealing with Excadrill. Defensive Great Tusk also synergizes well with popular Fighting team sweepers such as Iron Valiant, Keldeo, and Sneasler, removing entry hazards and taking physical hits for them, while they break through the opponent's team. Iron Valiant can delete Fighting-, Dark-, and Dragon-types like Keldeo, Sableye, and Choice Specs Latios with Moonblast while threatening Flying teams thanks to its access to BoltBeam. Keldeo appreciates the Electric immunity Great Tusk comes with, as it lets it focus more on overwhelming defensive cores like Corviknight and Skarmory. Sneasler takes on Fairy- and Grass-types threats such as Enamorus, Iron Valiant, and Ogerpon formes while providing U-turn support to bring Great Tusk in on physical threats such as Gliscor. Hisuian Lilligant can put a foe to sleep and dispose of Ground- and Water-types foes with its Victory Dance set such as Landorus, Swampert, and Urshifu-R.

Choice Scarf (Ground).description:
A Choice Scarf combined with high-power STAB moves, great physical bulk, and high Attack makes Great Tusk one of the best options on Ground teams for a wallbreaker and late-game cleaner, threatening the likes of Choice Scarf Gholdengo and Bisharp. Close Combat hits different threats to Ground teams like Choice Specs Greninja and Hoopa-U. Headlong Rush OHKOes Flutter Mane. Earthquake can be used over Headlong Rush despite its lower power due to not causing Defense and Special Defense drops, making it better for sweeping. Ice Spinner targets the likes of Garchomp, Dragonite, Gliscor, and Landorus. Alternatively, Stone Edge targets Flying- and Bug-types such as Articuno, Talonflame, and Volcarona. Megahorn can also be used to target Grass- and Psychic-types such as Ogerpon-W, Latios, and Slowbro; Slowbro is notably 2HKOed by it after Stealth Rock damage. Knock Off prevents Air Balloon Gholdengo from walling Great Tusk, and it also removes items from foes such as Heavy-Duty Boots from Gyarados and Brambleghast and Leftovers from Corviknight.

Clodsire, Ting-Lu, Hippowdon, and Gliscor provide entry hazard support in wearing down foes to aid Great Tusk, guaranteeing a 2HKO on specially defensive Corviknight and an OHKO on the Ogerpon formes. Additionally, Clodsire provides a Water immunity, and its Poison typing allows it to melt Toxic Spikes and threaten Grass- and Fairy-types such as Meowscarada, Flutter Mane, and Clefable; Ting-Lu phazes setup sweepers such as Volcarona and Dragonite with Whirlwind; Hippowdon sets up sand to wear down foes further; and Gliscor spreads status with Toxic and shuts down passive walls with Taunt. In return, they appreciate Great Tusk dealing with Ice-types like Kyurem. Sand-boosted Excadrill takes out Choice Scarf users such as Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Iron Boulder. In return, Great Tusk deals with Dragon-types like Garchomp. When Great Tusk chooses to forego Ice Spinner, Mamoswine makes for a great teammate to cover Dragon- and Flying-types like Choice Scarf Latias, Dragonite, and Landorus. Landorus makes for another great partner, as with its colorful coverage, it takes on the likes of Primarina and Clefable, and it can also provide Gravity support so Great Tusk fares better against Corviknight and Skarmory. Landorus appreciates Great Tusk taking out Ice-types in return. Iron Treads provides immense utility that helps Great Tusk, such as hazard removal and pivoting via Volt Switch, and it appreciates Great Tusk taking out Excadrill in return. Garchomp is a great late-game sweeper that appreciates Great Tusk's ability to take out bulky Pokemon such as Articuno, Ting-Lu, and Gliscor with the appropriate coverage, which in turn allows Garchomp to sweep much more easily.

Offensive.description:
• Great Tusk's primal physical prowess and great support options make it a good choice for a bulky Fighting-type.

  • Earthquake versus Headlong Rush: Headlong Rush's defensive drops and vulnerability to Rocky Helmet make it a riskier option than Earthquake, but the extra power OHKOes maximum HP Gholdengo.

  • Ice Spinner: This is highly recommended to avoid getting walled by Dragonite before it Terastallizes, while also dealing good damage to common Tera Flying Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Kingambit.

  • Rapid Spin: Great Tusk is one of the best Rapid Spin users, being able to take advantage of it offensively and heavily pressuring Ting-Lu to Terastallize or switch out.

  • Knock Off: Beyond the usefulness of removing items, this is Great Tusk's best move against Air Balloon Gholdengo.

Other Options

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb is a good speed control option, great for breaking through Dragonite's Multiscale while nullifying its potential Speed boost, while letting other teammates take advantage of speed control. It also lets Great Tusk hit troublesome Focus Sash Ghost-types such as Flutter Mane and Gengar, something Rapid Spin can't do.

  • Iron Head: If using Tera Steel, Iron Head is a decent option for OHKOing Flutter Mane without using Headlong Rush, and it deals heavy damage to Baxcalibur and Tera Fairy Rotom-W.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Terastallization can help with Great Tusk's poor special bulk by resisting certain hits, but it works fine without it.

  • Steel: Tera Steel greatly aids against the many Fairy-, Ice-, and Flying-types that would otherwise prey on Great Tusk, such as Mimikyu, Iron Bundle, and Tera Flying Dragonite.

  • Water: Tera Water massively improves the matchup against Chien-Pao, and can let Great Tusk survive an encounter with offensive Iron Moth or Chi-Yu that lack Choice Specs.

  • Ground: The furious increase in power Tera Ground provides can be useful late game, giving Earthquake a high chance to OHKO even defensive Gholdengo and Headlong Rush the ability to 2HKO Terastallized Skeledirge.

  • Fighting: Not only does Tera Fighting improve the Chien-Pao matchup, but it OHKOs even the bulkiest Ting-Lu with Close Combat.

Items

  • Assault Vest: This patches up Great Tusk's poor Special Defense, which can be paired with the correct Tera Type to help against foes like Iron Bundle, Flutter Mane, Iron Moth, and Chi-Yu.

  • Booster Energy: When saving Great Tusk for late-game sweeps, Booster Energy is preferred over Life Orb for preserving its HP against priority attacks.

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash on such a bulky Pokemon may seem wasteful, but it vastly improves Great Tusk's matchups against special attackers such as Rotom-W and makes setting up Stealth Rock a far simpler task. If using Focus Sash, consider using the first alternate EV spread below.

Alternate EV Spreads
  • 4 HP / 12 Def / 236 Atk / 252 Spe with Jolly: This EV spread survives Adamant Focus Sash Meowscarada's Flower Trick followed by Sucker Punch, making it a good spread to use if using Focus Sash and Rapid Spin.
Assault Vest EV Spreads

  • All of these EV spreads will at least avoid a 2HKO from Modest Flutter Mane's Mystical Fire if using Tera Steel. If using a different Tera type, 16 Special Defense EVs can be redistributed.

  • 52 HP / 148 Atk / 4 Def / 164 SpD / 140 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread outspeeds Adamant Breloom, and the rare Timid Abomasnow.

  • 4 HP / 44 Atk / 4 Def / 164 SpD / 244 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread is for Rapid Spin, outspeeding Iron Bundle after a Speed boost.

Bulk Up.description:
• Great Tusk's fantastic Defense stat makes it a great option for setting up Bulk Up late-game.

  • Taunt versus Substitute: Taunt preys on defensive Pokemon such as Wo-Chien and Corviknight, while Substitute protects Great Tusk from Garganacl's Salt Cure. Dragon Tail from Garchomp and Dragonite, and OHKO moves from the likes of Dondozo and Kingambit.

  • Ice Spinner: Dragonite is such a problematic foe that hitting it hard is worth more than a Fighting-type STAB move.

Other Options

  • Body Press: Although it is difficult to fit in without sacrificing utility or coverage, Body Press is a reasonable option if a Fighting-type STAB move is needed.

  • Close Combat: Close Combat does not gel well with the defensive nature of this set, but it deals far more damage to Ting-Lu than any of Great Tusk's other options.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Great Tusk is a good bulky sweeper on its own, but Terstallization makes it far more difficult to revenge kill.

  • Water: Not only is Tera Water an excellent option against Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu, but it also means Dondozo will never break Great Tusk's Substitute with Wave Crash, and Assault Vest Azumarill become an easy target to set up on.

  • Steel: Tera Steel is a great option for dealing with Great Tusk's weaknesses, such as Fairy-types and makes Iron Bundle usually fail to 2HKO specially defensive Great Tusk without Choice Specs.

  • Poison: Tera Poison is a decent alternative to Tera Steel, providing the vital Fairy-type resistance without the weaknesses to Fighting- and Fire-type attacks and an extremely useful immunity to being poisoned that eases the match-up against Toxic Spikes foes such as Clodsire and Meowscarada.

  • Fire: Fire is not a great defensive type; however, not only does it do well against Fairy-types such as Flutter Mane, it also protects Great Tusk from fast Will-O-Wisp users such as Dragapult, Mimikyu, and Volcarona.

Items

  • Leftovers: The residual recovery from Leftovers best suits the slow set-up of this set, especially if using Substitute.

  • Booster Energy: Depending on the EV spread, Booster Energy can boost Attack or Speed to increase Great Tusk's late-game cleaning potential.

  • Covert Cloak: If a Garganacl check is desperately needed, Covert Cloak Great Tusk is up for the task.

EV Spreads

  • 188 HP / 140 Atk / 4 Def / 36 SpD / 140 Spe with Adamant: This EV spread outspeeds Adamant Breloom and the rare Timid Abomasnow, survives Timid Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry, and has a very good chance of avoiding a 2HKO from Adamant Azumarill after using Bulk Up. The Attack EVs OHKO Chien-Pao and defensive Gholdengo with Earthquake after Bulk Up.

  • 4 HP / 252 SpD / 252 Spe with Jolly: This spread gains a Speed boost from Protosynthesis, making Great Tusk an even better late-game sweeper at the cost of physical bulk.

  • 244 HP / 20 Atk / 84 Def / 20 SpD / 140 Spe with Impish: This EV spread is meant for use with Tera Steel or Tera Poison, maintaining Great Tusk's Substitute against Dondozo's Wave Crash after Terastallization. It also outspeeds Adamant Breloom and the rare Timid Abomasnow, and survives Timid Iron Bundle's Freeze-Dry.

  • 252 HP / 4 Atk / 252 SpD with Careful: Maximum investment in special bulk makes Great Tusk much more difficult to revenge kill with the likes of Gholdengo and Iron Bundle. The 4 Attack EVs gives an Attack boost from Protosynthesis, which is preferred for improving the Skeledirge matchup and sweeping more easily.

Choice Item.description:
• Great Tusk's high power attacks make it a fine Choice item holder.

  • Headlong Rush versus Earthquake: Headlong Rush is preferred for stampeding over maximum HP Gholdengo, but Earthquake avoids chip damage from Rocky Helmet and makes Great Tusk far less vulnerable to priority attacks from foes like Dragonite, Chien-Pao, and Palafin-H.

  • Ice Spinner: Great Tusk should never leave its cave without a move to hit Dragonite hard!

  • Knock Off: Knock Off deals massive damage to Air Balloon Gholdengo and is almost guaranteed to OHKO offensive Dragapult after Stealth Rock damage.

  • Jolly versus Adamant: A Jolly nature ensures that Great Tusk outspeeds Gholdengo, and Choice Scarf variants outspeed Dragapult. Adamant is still a reasonable option for more power since Great Tusk will still outpace Breloom, and if using Choice Scarf, Iron Bundle, Flutter Mane, and Chien-Pao.

Other Options
  • Iron Head: If using Tera Steel, this is a reasonable option over Knock Off if Tera Fairy Rotom-W is an issue.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: While Terastallization can help it clean more easily, it's not an important aspect of this set otherwise.

  • Ground: Tera Ground is the best option for late-game cleaning, dealing significant damage to Dondozo and OHKOing Dragapult with Headlong Rush.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting threatens to 2HKO Corviknight, an otherwise decent check to Great Tusk, and OHKO even the bulkiest Ting-Lu.

  • Steel: While Great Tusk's special bulk is mediocre, Tera Steel can prevent it from being OHKOed by foes such as Iron Bundle and Flutter Mane.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Since it outspeeds other major Choice Scarf Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Rotom-W, Great Tusk makes for a good revenge killer.

  • Choice Band: Choice Band is a more niche option due to being extremely vulnerable to revenge kills, but does a much better job of wall-breaking, with Tera boosted Great Tusk even being able to 2HKO a maximum Defense Dondozo with Close Combat or Headlong Rush!

Pinsirite.description: Pinsirite Great Tusk cements itself as the metagame's premier entry hazard remover while also being a respectable offensive threat. Body Slam potentially cripples common switch-ins like Arceus-Water and Latiasite Pecharunt with paralysis. Bulk Up makes Great Tusk a formidable cleaner that's difficult to revenge kill, especially in conjunction with Rapin Spin. Smack Down can be used over Body Slam or Bulk Up to threaten Ground-immune targets such as Latiasite variants of Magearna and Pecharunt as well as Corviknight and Ho-Oh. 204 Speed EVs allow Pinsirite Great Tusk to outspeed Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk, while 144 HP EVs enable it to survive two maximum Attack Altarianite Dragonite Extreme Speeds after Stealth Rock. Strong wallbreakers such as Urshifu-R, Hisuian Arcanine, Raging Bolt, Entei, and Iron Moth benefit from Great Tusk's ability to remove hazards, potentially giving them more opportunities to hit the field. Defensive staples like Garganacl, Pecharunt, and bulky variants of Arceus-Water and Arceus-Fairy also appreciate it removing hazards and maximizing their longevity. Great Tusk struggles against Arceus-Water and Latiasite users like Magearna, so pairing it with answers such as Ho-Oh, Hisuian Arcanine, and Entei for Magearna as well as Eternatus and Raging Bolt for Arceus-Water is crucial. Great Tusk also appreciates specially bulky teammates such as Magearna and Garganacl because special attackers, especially Ice Beam users like Lunala, are troublesome for it.

Stealth Rock.description: Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk is a fantastic entry hazard setter thanks to Hearthflame Mask providing Mold Breaker, which ignores all Magic Bounce stones being used while also punishing teams that use said ability as their only form of entry hazard control. Knock Off allows Great Tusk to rid switch-ins such as Ho-Oh and Lunala of their Heavy-Duty Boots. Head Smash still handles Ho-Oh while also 2HKOing Sablenite Mandibuzz at the cost of recoil damage. Stone Edge is a slightly weaker option that doesn't wear down Great Tusk as fast; however, it misses out on some key benchmarks, such as 2HKOing Sablenite Mandibuzz. Ice Spinner rounds out Great Tusk's coverage, nailing opposing Ground-types such as non-Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk and Arceus-Ground. Temper Flare is an alternative for a secondary STAB move that nails Corviknight specifically. Rapid Spin can also be slotted in the last slot as emergency hazard control; however, due to lacking an -ate ability, this set struggles to be a reliable spinner. Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk pairs extremely well with more offensive behemoths such as Metagrossite Urshifu-R and Raging Bolt thanks to its Fairy resistance, which lets it handle the likes of Magearna and Altarianite Hisuian Arcanine, and ability to provide chip damage for the aforementioned threats to achieve better benchmarks when aiming to KO the foe. Furthermore, Urshifu-R can threaten Ground-types such as opposing Great Tusk and Arceus-Ground, while Raging Bolt can handle the Water-types that threaten Great Tusk such as Arceus-Water and opposing Urshifu-R. Other good partners include specially defensive walls like Lunala, Garganacl, and Magearna, as they can shore up Great Tusk's weaker defensive stat and form a nice defensive core alongside Great Tusk.

Rusted Sword.description: Rusted Sword Great Tusk is an incredibly powerful wallbreaker and sweeper thanks to its strong STAB moves in Headlong Rush and Behemoth Blade (Iron Head turns into Behemoth Blade upon switch-in), along with Intrepid Sword. It also offers great utility, with access to Rapid Spin and Stealth Rock. Great Tusk can also forgo Stealth Rock for Bulk Up to become a far more devastating sweeper or instead use a wide range of coverage moves such as Ice Spinner, Stone Edge, and Supercell Slam. Great Tusk fits especially well on hyper offense teams, where it can not only support its teammates by keeping entry hazards off the field while setting its own but also apply heavy offensive pressure as a lead. Great Tusk struggles against common Water-types such as Urshifu-R, Hisuian Samurott, and Arceus-Water; thus, teammates like Dragonite, Regieleki, and Raging Bolt help cover these weaknesses while further applying pressure against the opposing team. In return, Great Tusk helps check common Extreme Speed users, particularly those with Altarianite, that threaten the aforementioned Pokemon thanks to its Steel typing and STAB Behemoth Blade. Setup sweepers, such as Spectrier, Calm Mind Arceus formes, and the aforementioned Dragonite, greatly benefit from the hazard support that Great Tusk provides. Similarly, offensive pivots like Regieleki, Barraskewda, Raging Bolt, and Iron Crown force constant switches from foes, helping to rack up damage from Stealth Rock. Great Tusk can also be used on rain teams, where it more easily withstands Fire-type attacks from threats like Eternatus, Ho-Oh, and Entei. This makes Pelipper a great partner, providing both weather support and the ability to handle Ground- and Fighting-types such as opposing Great Tusk and Metagrossite Urshifu-R. Other Water-type attackers, such as Greninja and Basculegion, also pair well with Great Tusk, as they can also handle Ground-type foes like Arceus-Ground and opposing Great Tusk while also benefiting greatly from the rain.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Wandering Spirit is a niche ability on physically defensive sets that prevents Regenerator Pokemon like Swampert and Roaring Moon from regaining their HP when they pivot out while also letting Great Tusk gain Regenerator. Magic Guard + Life Orb is a great combination for offensive sets, as this prevents Great Tusk from being chipped down by Rocky Helmet and poison from Malignant Chain or Toxic Spikes; it also lets Great Tusk make use of Supercell Slam to hit Corviknight and Skarmory as well as Head Smash for Zapdos and Moltres without taking any recoil. Mold Breaker is used on offensive sets to allow Great Tusk to bypass Fluffy used on Pokemon like Corviknight, Skarmory, and Great Tusk as well as Levitate and Earth Eater on Gholdengo and Pecharunt. Earth Eater gives Great Tusk immunity to Earthquake from Ting-Lu, Swampert, and opposing Great Tusk while also letting it counter Sandy Shocks. Great Tusk can opt for an EV spread of 252 HP / 4 Atk / 252 Spe to make it a fast utility Pokemon while still retaining its defensive prowess.
