The Special Attack investment allows Gholdengo to always 2HKO Zamazenta-C with +2 Shadow Ball, while the defensive investment allows Gholdengo to survive Origin Pulse from Mystic Water Kyogre and Flare Blitz from Incineroar. The Speed investment allows Gholdengo to outspeed Pelipper. Tera Normal is used to give Gholdengo an immunity to threatening Ghost-type moves such as Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S and Shadow Ball from Flutter Mane, while Tera Water is used because it is a good defensive typing overall while allowing Gholdengo to resist Fire-type attacks.

Common checks to Gholdengo consist of Incineroar, Chi-Yu, Assault Vest Raging Bolt, and Calyrex-S. Chi-Yu and Calyrex-S outspeed and threaten to OHKO Gholdengo. Assault Vest Raging Bolt easily shrugs off attacks from Gholdengo, while Incineroar walls it and can hit back with super effective Knock Off and Flare Blitz. Common partners for Gholdengo include Amoonguss, Incineroar, and Ogerpon-C, which help Gholdengo defensively by aiding in its setup with redirection and Pollen Puff healing as well as Fake Out and Intimidate, respectively. Urshifu-R and Pelipper are also great partners, as they can deal with Calyrex-S, Chi-Yu, and Incineroar thanks to Pelipper's combination of Drizzle, Wide Guard, and Weather Ball and Urshifu-R's ability to outspeed and threaten all three of them with Surging Strikes. Calyrex-I and Koraidon are strong Gholdengo partners, since Gholdengo can help deal with threats such as Zamazenta-C and Zacian-C and appreciates how the two threaten Incineroar. Koraidon especially appreciates Gholdengo, as it can take on Calyrex-I + Amoonguss teams incredibly well.

Choice Specs.description:
Gholdengo is a strong special attacker that uses its great ability to switch into moves like Amoonguss's Spore and Incineroar's Parting Shot, allowing it to attack without being slowed down. Gholdengo is also used as a check to Pokemon like Zamazenta-C and Zacian-C, since it walls them. Trick is used to cripple support and setup Pokemon like Amoonguss and Terapagos or force Pokemon that set Trick Room such as Calyrex-I to switch out. Nasty Plot gives Gholdengo the option to set up once it has used Trick. Power Gem hits Fire-types that resist Make It Rain such as Incineroar, Chi-Yu, and Ogerpon-H. Alternatively, Dazzling Gleam threatens Pokemon like Miraidon and Koraidon. Choice Specs allows Gholdengo to use its strong Steel- and Ghost-type attacks to immediately threaten Pokemon like Calyrex-I, especially if it uses Tera Steel. The EV spread allows Gholdengo to survive Choice Specs Miraidon's Volt Switch, Incineroar's Flare Blitz, and Kyogre's Mystic Water-boosted Origin Pulse and OHKO bulky Flutter Mane sets with Shadow Ball. The Speed EVs let it outspeed the Ogerpon formes when they are at -1. Tera Steel lets Gholdengo OHKO Landorus and Tera Fairy Assault Vest Raging Bolt, and if Gholdengo is paired with speed control providers such as Tailwind Tornadus and Icy Wind Flutter Mane, it can run it to boost Make It Rain even further. Tera Dragon allows Gholdengo to resist Fire-type attacks such as Koraidon's Flare Blitz and Groudon's Heat Crash as well as Miraidon's Electro Drift and Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes. Tera Water also lets Gholdengo resist Fire- and Water-type attacks like Kyogre's Water Spout and Koraidon's Flare Blitz while not making it weak to Ice- and Fairy-type attacks such as Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash and Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

Incineroar resists Gholdengo's STAB combination while threatening it with Flare Blitz and Knock Off. Chi-Yu similarly checks Gholdengo while also outspeeding and threatening an OHKO on it with Dark Pulse or Overheat. Assault Vest Raging Bolt resists Make It Rain and avoids the 2HKO from Shadow Ball. As for teammates, Gholdengo pairs well with Terapagos, since Gholdengo walls Zamazenta-C, while Terapagos matches up well against Calyrex-S and can switch into Ghost-type attacks. Gholdengo also pairs well with Calyrex-I, since it can check Zamazenta-C and Zacian-C, which Calyrex-I struggles with. Gholdengo additionally has great synergy with Pelipper due to rain reducing Gholdengo's weakness to Fire and Pelipper threatening Fire-types that resist Make It Rain such as Incineroar and Chi-Yu. Finally, Chien-Pao and Calyrex-I are both good partners for Gholdengo, since they can threaten Raging Bolt.

Nasty Plot.description:
Gholdengo stands out as one of the best setup attackers, with its already massive Special Attack stat and reasonable bulk bolstered further by Nasty Plot and Recover. Additionally, it provides plenty of support thanks to Good as Gold making both itself and its partner immune to status moves including Amoonguss's Spore and Incineroar's Parting Shot. Make It Rain is Gholdengo's standout move as an exceptionally high-powered spread attack, taking down the likes of Chien-Pao and Glimmora easily as well as Rillaboom at +2. Shadow Ball pressures other Ghost-types such as Sinistcha and opposing Gholdengo effectively while also hitting Steel-resistant foes such as Ogerpon-H well. Gholdengo can choose to run Recover in lieu of Protect if the rest of the team can provide the latter, making it incredibly hard to remove. As Gholdengo wants to sit on the field for as long as possible, Leftovers is the primary recovery item chosen to maximize healing; however, Sitrus Berry is a fine option for more immediate HP recovery. Gholdengo's inability to hit Incineroar for any meaningful damage make partners such as Ogerpon-W and Landorus greatly appreciated. The given bulk EVs allow Gholdengo to survive Landorus-T's Stomping Tantrum, Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch, and Heatran's Flash Fire-boosted Lava Plume. Its Speed allows it to outrun Choice Scarf Landorus-T in Tailwind. Tera Dragon is generally preferred to resist both Ogerpon-H's and Ogerpon-W's STAB moves; however, Tera Water is also fine as a good defensive typing overall.

Notable Partners

Bulky Support Pokemon: The likes of Incineroar, Amoonguss, and Indeedee-F help make Gholdengo shine, with Intimidate nullifying physical attackers almost entirely and Fake Out, Rage Powder, and Follow Me providing safe opportunities to use Nasty Plot.

Other Setup Pokemon: Swords Dance Iron Hands and Cosmic Power Deoxys-D both appreicate Good as Gold granting them an immunity to common disruption such as Will-O-Wisp, Spore, and Taunt. Deoxys-D particularly appreciates Nasty Plot in order to boost its Stored Power damage even further.

Pokemon With Immunity Abilities: Pokemon such as Heatran and Latios provide Gholdengo with Flash Fire and Levitate, respectively, making it immediately immune to types it would otherwise be weak to.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs turns Gholdengo into a behemoth of a special attacker, with it 2HKOing bulkier Pokemon such as Indeedee-F and Dragonite with its Tera Steel-boosted Make It Rain. Choice Specs also helps turn Shadow Ball into an OHKO against the likes of Latios, Sinistcha, and bulky Gholdengo. Dazzling Gleam is one of the best coverage options for Gholdengo, allowing it to deal significant damage to the plethora of Dragon-types in the metagame such as Raging Bolt and Walking Wake. Thunderbolt and Power Gem are alternative coverage options that improve Gholdengo's chances against Volcanion and Incineroar. Trick is an option that disrupts Trick Room setters such as Porygon2 as well as setup attackers like Iron Hands. Steel is Choice Specs Gholdengo's best Tera type, as it further boosts its strongest attack while also retaining its Dragon and Fairy resistances. Choice Specs is particularly good in Partners in Crime, as it allows Gholdengo to lock into its partner's move then later break the Choice lock by having its partner switch.

Notable Partners

Tailwind Users: Whimsicott and Tornadus are Choice Specs Gholdengo's best friends, with Tailwind allowing it to deal massive damage immediately and its Good as Gold providing Whimsicott and Tornadus with a Taunt immunity. Whimsicott also offers Fake Tears to further boost Gholdengo's damage.

Setup Pokemon: Pokemon that require setup to be as threatening as possible such as Swords Dance Rillaboom appreciate the immediate bursts of damage that Gholdengo can provide.

Strong Special Attackers: Given that Gholdengo can break its Choice lock at any time by having its partner switch, a strong special attacker such as Volcanion and Landorus makes for a great partner. These also happen to pass it invaluable coverage for Fire- and Steel-types, letting it stand up to Incineroar and Heatran more easily.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Choice Scarf Gholdengo outspeeds the entire unboosted metagame, can use Trick to weaken defensive teams, and also blocks Defog and Rapid Spin to keep pressure on defensive Pokemon with entry hazards.
  • Focus Blast deals more damage to Ting-Lu, Chi-Yu, and Iron Treads, while Nasty Plot and Recover can be used after Gholdengo's Choice Scarf has been removed via Trick to turn it into a setup sweeper or give it longevity, respectively.
  • Tera Fighting powers up Focus Blast, which allows Gholdengo to potentially 2HKO Ting-Lu. Alternatively, Gholdengo can use Tera Steel on sets not using Focus Blast to boost Make It Rain and remove its weaknesses to Flutter Mane's and Chien-Pao's STAB moves.
  • Gholdengo should almost always be switched in if Corviknight is on the field and be used sparingly against Great Tusk and Iron Treads if a Rapid Spin is predicted, but this is risky due to its Earthquake weakness.
  • Spikes setters like Ting-Lu and Clodsire on balance teams as well as Froslass on hyper offense teams appreciate Gholdengo keeping up Spikes and it acting as a revenge killer for their respective archetypes.
  • Pokemon like Calm Mind Miraidon, Calm Mind Flutter Mane, and Swords Dance Chien-Pao also benefit from Gholdengo using Trick on defensive Pokemon, forcing them to either heal or be locked into an unfavorable attack while they set up. Gholdengo can also clean up weakened teams if these Pokemon are used to wallbreak first.

Nasty Plot.description:
• Nasty Plot + Recover Gholdengo is the best option for preventing entry hazard removal in the tier.
  • Tera Steel bolsters Make It Rain's power, allowing Gholdengo to overwhelm threats such as Koraidon, defensive Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and bulky Tera Fairy Miraidon after a Nasty Plot boost while removing its Ghost typing.
  • Tera Normal blocks incoming Ghost-type attacks from the likes of Flutter Mane, Choice Scarf Houndstone, and opposing Gholdengo.
  • Air Balloon provides a temporary measure against Ground-type attacks from Pokemon such as Great Tusk and Iron Treads, allowing Gholdengo to sometimes switch into them.
  • Gholdengo best fits on hyper offense and balance teams that aim to preserve their own entry hazards for as long as possible.
  • Frail leads such as Froslass and Masquerain appreciate their entry hazards staying intact against Great Tusk, Iron Treads, Corviknight, and Glimmora.
  • Glimmora and Ting-Lu make for good teammates on balance teams in particular, as they provide similar entry hazard support while having sufficient power and bulk to punish threats.
  • Wallbreakers such as Miraidon, Koraidon, and Chi-Yu appreciate multiple entry hazards to further overwhelm the opposition with their tremendous attacks and power.

ou.overview: With an excellent typing, moveset, and ability, Gholdengo stands out as an incredibly valuable Pokemon that can act as both a defensive and offensive glue on virtually any team style from hyper offense to balance. Its typing allows Gholdengo to check numerous relevant threats such as Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, Kyurem, and Galarian Slowking, and Good as Gold allows it to take on status users like Clefable and Zapdos, phazers like Ting-Lu, and Encore or Taunt from foes like Ogerpon-W, Iron Valiant, and Deoxys-S; both of these combined also makes Gholdengo one of the sturdiest methods to stop entry hazard removal, as it prevents some of the most common formes in Corviknight's Defog, Glimmora's Mortal Spin, and Great Tusk and Iron Treads's Rapid Spin. Gholdengo's moveset also gives it many options; Nasty Plot allows it to act as a wincon and wallbreaker, letting it overwhelm foes with excellent coverage and the longevity provided via Recover. It is also an excellent status spreader with Thunder Wave, giving Gholdengo a way to cripple faster foes such as Zamazenta, Darkrai, and Dragapult, synergizing well with its Hex. Choice Scarf patches up its middling Speed and lets it act as a team's speed control, which also lets it run Trick to cripple setup sweepers like Dragonite and Zamazenta as well as defensive switch-ins against bulkier teams. Gholdengo, however, suffers from an awkward Speed tier without a Choice Scarf, as it is slower than many relevant threats such as Darkrai, Kyurem, Cinderace, and Great Tusk. It also often invites in common Pokemon that can threaten it directly such as Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott, and special walls such as Ting-Lu, Assault Vest Tornadus-T, and Clodsire can give it trouble.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Covert Cloak is an option to take on Garganacl's Salt Cure and Hatterene's Nuzzle, as well as avoid the Defense drop from Zamazenta's Crunch. Ability Shield lets Gholdengo ignore Galarian Weezing's Neutralizing Gas, allowing Good as Gold to continue blocking Defog. Thunder Wave is an option on Choice Scarf sets in order to surprise and cripple threats such as Ogerpon-W and Tornadus-T. Choice Specs can be used to wallbreak while still having the utility of Trick, with the immediate power boost letting it 2HKO Ting-Lu with Focus Blast after Stealth Rock, although this set is notably held back by Gholdengo's Speed. Salac Berry fixes the Speed issue on Nasty Plot Gholdengo in a pinch and allow a potential sweep late-game. Red Card takes advantage of its bulk to act as a one-time phazer against boosted threats such as Iron Valiant. Eject Pack allows Gholdengo to pivot once after using Make It Rain, providing team support by keeping up momentum. Custap Berry is another option to mitigate its Speed issue, and it can be used to surprise foes and hit back against would-be revenge killers like Dragapult and Iron Valiant.

Offensive Nasty Plot.description:
Thanks to Good as Gold and excellent defensive typing that lets it set up on Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Clefable, Nasty Plot Gholdengo is a premier wallbreaker in the metagame. Shadow Ball gives it a no-drawback and spammable STAB move to hit most foes neutrally, particularly valuable against opposing Gholdengo. Make it Rain's sheer power is great against Garganacl and Kyurem while hitting neutral threats like Ting-Lu, Zamazenta, and Great Tusk hard. Thunderbolt takes care of Moltres, Hisuian Samurott, and Alomomola. Dazzling Gleam hits foes like Hisuian Samurott, Ting-Lu, and Raging Bolt reliably while being a solid STAB move when paired with Tera Fairy. Focus Blast hits the many Dark-types in the tier; it notably targets Kingambit while hitting Ting-Lu and Hisuian Samurott harder than Dazzling Gleam. Recover gives Gholdengo a way to stay in the battle for longer, particularly against chip damage like Garganacl's Salt Cure, and leverage its defensive utility against the aforementioned threats. Psyshock turns it into a stallbreaker, as it is useful for breaking through special walls that would otherwise contest with Gholdengo, like Calm Mind Blissey and Clodsire. The Ground immunity granted by Air Balloon allows Gholdengo to set up in the face of Gliscor, spinblock Great Tusk and Iron Treads, become a sturdier switch-in against foes like Kyurem and Dragonite, and avoid damage from Spikes. Metal Coat alongside Tera Steel can be used on Make It Rain variants to propel its power to overwhelm checks like Ting-Lu and even OHKO resistant ones like bulky Kingambit and Moltres at +2. On bulkier teams that lack any entry hazard removal, Heavy-Duty Boots can be used instead due to Air Balloon's temporary immunity to Spikes being less appealing with Gholdengo's necessity to switch around more often. Shuca Berry is an option to lure in Ground-type revenge killers like Great Tusk and Landorus-T to flip the matchup against them; the lack of immunity over Air Balloon is made up for Gholdengo's freedom to take on other attacks early in the game as well as hiding Gholdengo's item from the opponent. Gholdengo can make great use of a wide variety of Tera types, both for offensive and defensive purposes: Tera Fairy boosts Dazzling Gleam and gives it a sudden resistance to Dark, potentially mitigating the damage from moves like Knock Off, Crunch, and Sucker Punch from Iron Valiant, Zamazenta, and Kingambit, respectively. Tera Fighting is an option to boost its Focus Blast, notably having good odds to OHKO Ting-Lu at +2, while also providing a Dark resistance similar to Tera Fairy.

Any team can make great use of Gholdengo’s ability to spinblock and prevent Defog, but an offensive team would make the best use of its wallbreaking power. Offensive hazard-stacking cores featuring Pokemon such as Glimmora, Hisuian Samurott, and Deoxys-S can use Gholdengo’s help to keep the pressure on, with Gholdengo in return preventing foes from removing said hazards easily. Powerful wallbreakers like Ogerpon-W and Darkrai provide support for Gholdengo to whittle down defensive cores together. Without using Tera, Gholdengo struggles against the Dark-types and Ghost-types that are so common in the tier, such as Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Dragapult. Having teammates that can check them, like Zamazenta, Enamorus, and Hisuian Samurott give Gholdengo some extra protection and a way to strike back against them. Even if it's using Air Balloon, having another Ground-immune Pokemon, such as Gliscor or Tornadus-T, is extremely helpful to mitigate that weakness. Gholdengo is vulnerable to fast threats such as Dragapult, Walking Wake, and Weavile. Having some form speed control on the team, such as Choice Scarf Enamorus and Meowscarada or priority users like Weavile and Raging Bolt, to counteract these threats is extremely valuable.

Bulky Nasty Plot.description:
Gholdengo's ability to block entry hazard removal while checking key metagame threats is exacerbated greatly by defensive investment, and this bulk can make a boosted Gholdengo all the more deadly. Dual STAB moves hit a majority of the OU tier, with Make It Rain's high base power making up for a lack of offensive investment by OHKOing targets like Landorus-T after a single boost. Dazzling Gleam is an alternative to handle Dark-types without the Special Attack drop and notably gives Gholdengo a way to hit Hisuian Samurott, though the loss in power leaves Gholdengo unable to OHKO even an unboosted Iron Valiant. Thunderbolt can instead be used to handle Hisuian Samurott while immediately threatening pivots like Corviknight and Alomomola, and it also hits Moltres for massive damage after a boost. However, running Thunderbolt with Shadow Ball has the caveat of leaving Gholdengo walled by Ting-Lu and Ursaluna, and pairing it with Make it Rain instead solves this but makes Gholdengo weaker against Raging Bolt and Iron Treads. Focus Blast can OHKO Kingambit while dealing with other Dark-types, though no offensive investment means Pokemon like Iron Treads and Darkrai often withstand a single hit. Gholdengo's versatility extends to its item choice; Air Balloon is its best option to facilitate spinblocking against foes like Great Tusk and Iron Treads and let it act as a one-time check to Kyurem or a weakened Dragonite. Leftovers more directly enhances its longevity, putting it out of range of a 2HKO from attacks like Life Orb Zamazenta's Crunch and Pecharunt's Shadow Ball. Heavy-Duty Boots is an alternative on teams lacking consistent entry hazard removal and means Gholdengo doesn't rely on Air Balloon for a Spikes immunity. Grassy Seed is an excellent option on Grassy Terrain teams to further bolster Gholdengo's bulk while also weakening Knock Off, and Shuca Berry can let Gholdengo lure in and eliminate foes like Great Tusk and Kyurem. 60 Speed EVs ensure that Gholdengo will always outspeed Jolly Kingambit, with the remaining EVs invested fully in HP and Defense. A Bold nature means that Gholdengo is never OHKOed by Jolly Great Tusk's Headlong Rush. Gholdengo's Speed can be dropped further, with a spread of 252 HP / 244 Def / 12 Spe still outspeeding uninvested Cresselia and guaranteeing that Gholdengo will always live Iron Valiant's +2 Knock Off. If using Grassy Seed, Gholdengo can instead opt for some Special Defense investment; for example, 252 HP / 108 Def / 88 SpD / 60 Spe with a Calm nature is enough to survive a Tera Ghost Shadow Ball from opposing Gholdengo. Tera Fairy is Gholdengo's most consistent defensive Tera type, flipping its matchup against Dark-type attacks from foes like Hisuian Samurott, Darkrai, and Swords Dance Iron Valiant. This boosts Dazzling Gleam significantly, letting Gholdengo OHKO bulkier targets such as Zamazenta and Raging Bolt after a single Nasty Plot. Tera Water is an alternative typing that lets Gholdengo wall Cinderace and beat Ceruledge after its Air Balloon has been consumed, also making it a more useful Pokemon into sun and being neutral to the attacks of most of the metagame. However, weaknesses to Freeze Dry Kyurem and Ogerpon-W are not always desirable. Tera Flying can be considered to more permanently deal with Gholdengo's Ground weakness and surprise foes like Great Tusk while letting it set up on Ting-Lu, though a weakness to Stealth Rock and STAB options from common OU foes like Kyurem, Raging Bolt, and Zapdos leaves Gholdengo less able to perform its role as both defensive stalwart and wincon.

With such heavy bulk investment, Gholdengo provides teams with an excellent way of preventing opponents from removing entry hazards. It therefore finds a home on bulky offense and balance teams that make use of its defensive profile and ability to act as a wincon. Ting-Lu is Gholdengo's best friend, able to set up both Stealth Rock and Spikes while checking Darkrai, Iron Moth, and opposing Gholdengo with ease. In return, Gholdengo's typing lets it switch into Zamazenta, as well as Fairy-type attacks from Iron Valiant, Hatterene, and Enamorus. Gliscor is another bulky entry hazard setter that likes being paired with a Kyurem check, with Gholdengo appreciating it absorbing Knock Off, removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes like Great Tusk and Galarian Weezing, and annoying Cinderace and Moltres. Landorus-T is an alternative Stealth Rock setter that can switch in on and force damage against Great Tusk, and Hisuian Samurott finds utility outside of just setting Spikes with its ability to check Iron Moth and opposing Gholdengo; Hisuian Samurott also has Knock Off to increase the value of hazards Gholdengo keeps up against Heavy-Duty Boots users like Alomomola, Zapdos, and Galarian Weezing. Gholdengo's vulnerability to Dark-types and particularly Kingambit necessitates dedicated support, with Great Tusk being a powerful option that can also set Stealth Rock or use Knock Off if required. Zamazenta is another Kingambit answer with a better matchup against Hisuian Samurott, and its propensity to invite in foes like Galarian Slowking and Clefable provides free setup opportunities for Gholdengo. Zamazenta has further synergy as a late-game cleaner on the bulkier hazard stack teams that Gholdengo thrives on, and sets packing Roar can even shuffle foes over the entry hazards that Gholdengo keeps up. On bulkier teams, Moltres makes for a solid check to Kingambit as well as Cinderace, while Clefable can switch in on Great Tusk and Gliscor with relative ease, set up Stealth Rock, and use Knock Off on Pokemon like Galarian Slowking and Pecharunt that are reliant on Heavy-Duty Boots. Even Skarmory can be considered to comfortably answer Kingambit while providing Spikes support to synergize with Gholdengo. Offensively, Gholdengo's ability to keep hazards up helps other sweepers like Dragonite, with Gholdengo walling Corviknight and Iron Defense Zamazenta that Dragonite cannot break through alone. Dragonite also checks Ogerpon-W and Ceruledge to an extent, Pokemon that Gholdengo cannot answer despite its defensive investment. Ogerpon-W is an offensive partner that can work in tandem with Gholdengo to break Raging Bolt and Dragonite, and its Knock Off can maximize the impact of the hazards that Gholdengo protects by removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes like Zapdos, Tornadus-T, and Pecharunt. Darkrai similarly provides Gholdengo with a fast, strong partner that can weaken Ting-Lu and use Knock Off, notably on specially defensive foes like Clodsire and Blissey, and it very much appreciates Gholdengo's ability to check Zamazenta. One archetype that Gholdengo fits on is Grassy Terrain offense, as the Terrain's effect pairs with Grassy Seed to significantly weaken Earthquake from Pokemon like Dragonite and Ting-Lu. Rillaboom also gives Gholdengo entry points against Corviknight and Galarian Weezing, and it can help weaken or eliminate shared checks such as Cinderace, Moltres, and Raging Bolt.

Choice Scarf.description:
Choice Scarf Gholdengo is a great speed control option in the tier capable of outrunning and revenge killing premier offensive threats like Dragapult, Zamazenta, Dragonite, Kyurem, and Enamorus. Trick is a good utility move that allows it to Choice-lock Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Gliscor looking to check it as well as shutting down healthy setup sweepers like Dragonite and Zamazenta, hampering their effectiveness. Recover can be utilized to keep Gholdengo healthy, especially in the face of entry hazards, once it has used Trick, allowing it to check bulky foes like Clefable and some variants of Zamazenta more consistently. Alternatively, Nasty Plot can be used to turn Gholdengo into a decent wallbreaker once it has successfully used Trick to get rid of its Choice Scarf. Focus Blast enables Gholdengo to hit Dark-types like Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Ting-Lu. Thunder Wave provides even more form of speed control for the team, particularly helpful against healthy threats it can't immediately OHKO yet like Ogerpon-W and Darkrai, especially as the former is immune to Trick. Tera Ghost boosts the power of its spammable Shadow Ball, letting it clean up late-game more easily; similarly, Tera Steel can be used to better sweep through weakened foes with Make It Rain and is helpful in letting it revenge kill neutral foes like Ogerpon, Darkrai, and Great Tusk more easily with an OHKO. Tera Fighting gives Gholdengo a resistance to Dark-type moves, most notably Sucker Punch from Kingambit, and it gives Focus Blast a STAB boost.

Gholdengo fits well on bulky offense and balance teams, where it functions as a great revenge killer. Teammates that benefit from Gholdengo's presence include Pokemon that appreciate its ability to handle fast and strong offensive threats. For instance, setup sweepers like Calm Mind Raging Bolt and Bulk Up Great Tusk can capitalize on Gholdengo's ability to revenge kill and weaken opposing threats like Dragapult and Choice Specs Enamorus, creating opportunities for Gholdengo's partners to set up and sweep. Great Tusk's access to Rapid Spin also synergizes well with Gholdengo, which is punished by Spikes, so getting rid of them gives Gholdengo more opportunities to switch in. Entry hazard setters like Gliscor, Skarmory, and Ting-Lu also benefit from Gholdengo's ability to serve as an emergency spinblocker. Due to its vulnerability to Dark-type Pokemon like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott, exacerbated by its reliance on the inaccurate Focus Blast and the inherent risk of being Choice-locked, Gholdengo greatly benefits from the support of teammates that check the aforementioned foes, such as Zamazenta and Iron Valiant. Rillaboom also deserves a special mention as a teammate, as its Grassy Terrain weakens the super effective Earthquake, in addition to acting as a check to foes like Ting-Lu. In return, Gholdengo helps Rillaboom by handling threats that would otherwise be problematic for the latter, such as Corviknight and Skarmory.

Thunder Wave + Hex.description:
Gholdengo combines its defensive typing and solid bulk to become a prolific status spreader, using Thunder Wave to check threats like Zamazenta, Dragonite, and Ogerpon-W. Hex perfectly combines with Thunder Wave, giving Gholdengo the power to nearly always 2HKO uninvested paralyzed Zamazenta. It also prevents Gliscor from switching in freely on Thunder Wave and attempting to set up entry hazards on it. Recover augments Gholdengo's survivability, giving it the ability to repeatedly switch into Zamazenta's Crunch and Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel. Make It Rain strikes those that would normally switch into Thunder Wave well such as Great Tusk, Garganacl, and Hatterene. It additionally hits Kyurem, Enamorus, and Glimmora super effectively. Other options can be used over Make It Rain, however. Dazzling Gleam hits Dark- and Dragon-types like Darkrai, Hisuian Samurott, Raging Bolt, and Dragonite. Focus Blast, meanwhile, is the strongest option against Kingambit; Focus Blast also hits Darkrai and Hisuian Samurott much harder than Dazzling Gleam, with it being able to OHKO Darkrai after Stealth Rock, while also hitting Iron Treads for super effective damage. Air Balloon allows Gholdengo to switch into attacks like Great Tusk's Headlong Rush, Kyurem's Earth Power, and Dragonite's Earthquake. Air Balloon also lets Gholdengo spinblock effectively in front of Great Tusk and lets it be immune to Spikes. Other options such as Leftovers allows Gholdengo to further boost its longevity and preserve Recover PP; Leftovers lets Gholdengo always be able to take two Life Orb Crunches from Zamazenta. Shuca Berry grants Gholdengo the ability to take on Dragonite's Earthquake and Great Tusk's Headlong Rush in order to either paralyze or hit back; Shuca Berry has the advantage of being harder to play around with other attacks compared to Air Balloon. Similarly, Colbur Berry lets Gholdengo brawl against Swords Dance Iron Valiant's Knock Off and Darkrai's Dark Pulse. Rocky Helmet wears down foes using contact moves such as Zamazenta's Crunch while punishing U-turn from Tornadus-T, Corviknight, and Rillaboom. Tera Fairy gives Gholdengo the ability to stand up to attacks like Iron Valiant's Knock Off, Hisuian Samurott's Ceaseless Edge, and Kingambit's Sucker Punch. Tera Fairy additionally maintains the ability to check Zamazenta after it has Terastallized and has the side benefit of powering up Dazzling Gleam to be able to 2HKO Assault Vest Hisuian Samurott. Tera Water lets Gholdengo resist Fire-type moves like Cinderace's Pyro Ball and Iron Moth's Fiery Dance while being better into threats like Walking Wake. 60 Speed EVs are used to let Gholdengo outspeed Jolly Kingambit while maximizing its Defense, letting it take hits like Great Tusk's Headlong Rush and two Ogerpon-W's Knock Offs. Outspeeding Kingambit also lets Gholdengo get the jump on foes like Moltres and Bold Pecharunt. Alternatively, Gholdengo can run a spread of 248 HP / 232 Def / 28 Spe to outspeed paralyzed Dragapult. The added bulk allows Gholdengo to take an Adamant Tera Dark Choice Band Crunch from Zamazenta and survive an offensive Cinderace's Pyro Ball after a layer of Spikes.

Gholdengo usually finds itself on bulky offense teams, which appreciate its ability to repeatedly be a nuisance for the opponent while being a efficient spinblocker. These teams additionally like the paralysis support Gholdengo brings to allow strong wallbreakers to make progress more easily. Entry hazard setters such as Hisuian Samurott, Great Tusk, and Ting-Lu all appreciate Gholdengo blocking Corviknight's Defog and Great Tusk's Rapid Spin; they also appreciate Gholdengo checking threats like Zamazenta, Kyurem, and Dragonite. Dark-types like Kingambit and Darkrai appreciate Gholdengo handling Fighting-types like Iron Valiant and Zamazenta, while Gholdengo appreciates them being able to safely deal with Ghost-types like Dragapult and opposing Gholdengo. Additional support from teammates like Zamazenta and Moltres creates a magnificent defensive core with Gholdengo. In particular, Moltres handles Cinderace and Great Tusk effectively, and Zamazenta can safely deal with Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott. Gholdengo in return is able to reliably face Ogerpon-W and Iron Valiant. Fast teammates like the aforementioned Zamazenta and Iron Valiant enjoy Gholdengo targeting Galarian Slowking and slower variants of Pecharunt with both paralysis and a super effective Hex, ensuring they are able to sweep without any potential walls. Teammates that can directly target Ground-types like Ting-Lu and Gliscor, such as Ogerpon-W and Kyurem, are highly appreciated, giving Gholdengo the ability to spread paralysis freely into their checks like Zamazenta and Iron Crown, respectively. In addition, Ogerpon-W is able to lay Spikes that Gholdengo can spinblock for and threatens Iron Treads effectively. Kyurem, meanwhile, is able to shred Zapdos and has the side benefit of handling Ogerpon-W; its ability to deal with them allow Gholdengo to preserve its health.

Offensive Nasty Plot.description:
Gholdengo is a good wallbreaker and glue for offense and hyper offense teams thanks to its access to Nasty Plot, its ability, Good as Gold, and its typing, which blocks entry hazard removal from Terapagos and Tornadus-T while also having useful resistances to threats such as Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant. Nasty Plot allows Gholdengo to OHKO Pokemon such as Heatran and Tapu Koko at +2. Make It Rain is a powerful STAB move that can allow a boosted Gholdengo to take down Pokemon that Shadow Ball can't, such as Gliscor, offensive Garchomp, and Landorus-T, OHKOing all of them after a boost. Recover can be slotted over Make It Rain in order to increase Gholdengo’s longevity, allowing it to check threats like Iron Valiant and Tapu Lele for longer. Focus Blast is a move that complements Gholdengo’s Ghost-type STAB moves, punching holes into would-be switch-ins like Kingambit, Ting-Lu, and Heatran. Air Balloon allows Gholdengo to spinblock and threaten Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and Terapagos lacking Flamethrower. Ghostium Z is a powerful option, and when used in tandem with Nasty Plot, it allows Gholdengo to OHKO specially defensive Garchomp, Moltres, and Toxapex while also OHKOing the previously mentioned Heatran without relying on the shaky accuracy of Focus Blast. Fightinium Z is another option that allows Gholdengo to bypass Focus Blast’s limited accuracy, notably OHKOing Ting-Lu and Assault Vest Melmetal after a boost.

Gholdengo acts as a valuable asset for most offensive team structures with its ability to deny hazard control while also having incredible wallbreaking potential. Pokemon such as Glimmora, Ting-Lu, and Hisuian Samurott benefit from Gholdengo’s ability to keep hazards up. Additionally, the latter two enjoy Gholdengo’s unique typing, which can help blanket check Fairy- and Fighting-type foes such as Tapu Lele and Mega Medicham. Other Pokemon that enjoy Gholdengo’s wallbreaking capabilities include Raging Bolt and Urshifu-R, as they benefit immensely from Gholdengo removing and overwhelming checks like Ferrothorn and Slowbro. Gholdengo fears Pokemon such as Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott; therefore, Pokemon that can reliably deal with these Dark-types, such as Great Tusk and Zamazenta, are greatly appreciated. Having Pokemon immune to Ground-type attacks is helpful against threats such as Great Tusk and Garchomp, even if Gholdengo is holding an Air Balloon. As such, Pokemon like Landorus-T, Zapdos, and Moltres are outstanding partners. Moltres is an especially great teammate due to its ability to check the fearsome Fire-types in the metagame that Gholdengo struggles against, like Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona.

Bulky Nasty Plot.description:
Bulky Nasty Plot Gholdengo functions as a great defensive piece thanks to its amazing typing, access to reliable recovery, and its near-complete shutdown of entry hazard removal methods, as well as being a reliable offensive threat. Nasty Plot allows Gholdengo to take advantage of the foes it forces out, like Corviknight, Zamazenta lacking Crunch, and Toxapex, to enable it to break apart bulkier special walls such as Assault Vest Melmetal. Focus Blast nails otherwise-impassable Dark- and Normal-types like Ting-Lu, Hisuian Samurott, Kingambit, and Ursaluna, preventing them from either setting up entry hazards or Pursuit trapping it. It also destroys Steel-types like specially defensive Heatran and Ferrothorn after a boost. Recover allows Gholdengo to stay healthy in the face of weak attacks from foes like Toxapex, Ferrothorn, and Alomomola, letting it get more setup opportunities without fearing being chipped down. It also allows Gholdengo to check threatening Fighting-, Fairy-, and Psychic-types like Zamazenta, Tapu Lele, and Galarian Slowking throughout the game. The given EV spread allows Gholdengo to take a Choice Scarf Landorus-T's Earthquake from full health as well as outspeed defensive Landorus-T and Jolly Kingambit. Ghostium Z and Fightinium Z give Gholdengo one-time options to remove most foes in its path: Ghostium Z blasts specially defensive Toxapex and Assault Vest Tornadus-T, denying them the ability to utilize Regenerator to check Gholdengo's teammates later in the game, while Fightinium Z allows for Gholdengo to beat back its otherwise-solid answers in Ting-Lu and Blissey while ignoring Focus Blast's accuracy woes. Leftovers lets Gholdengo conserve Recover PP against the likes of Toxapex, while Air Balloon lets Gholdengo stuff Gliscor, gain setup opportunities against Landorus-T, and block Rapid Spin from Great Tusk to keep hazards on the field.

Gholdengo's great typing, which lets it deal with troublesome Fighting-, Fairy-, and Psychic-types like the aforementioned Zamazenta and Tapu Lele, as well as its amazing offensive power after a boost and its ability to block hazard removal attempts, lets it find a home on balance teams. Gholdengo greatly appreciates teammates like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant, as they are able to ward off the dangerous Dark-types like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott that take advantage of Gholdengo. In return, Gholdengo threatens the Poison-types like Toxapex that wall them to setup and wreak havoc, as well as checking threatening Psychic- and Fairy-types like Choice Scarf Tapu Lele. Hazard setters like Gliscor and Hisuian Samurott are great partners as well due to Gholdengo's near-complete dominance over most hazard control options. Both also offer unique defensive pairings with Gholdengo; Gliscor deals with Ground-types like Ting-Lu and Landorus-T by putting them on a timer with Toxic, while Hisuian Samurott takes on Fire-types like Heatran. Hazard removal options for Gholdengo like Moltres and Great Tusk allow Gholdengo to check the threats it needs to, like all-out attacking Zamazenta and Choice Specs Iron Valiant, without dealing with Spikes damage. Another good defensive partner for Gholdengo is Heatran, as it is able to put Volcarona and Moltres on a timer with Toxic while setting up Stealth Rock to chip down Gholdengo's checks like Hisuian Samurott over time.

Thunder Wave + Hex.description:
Gholdengo is a premier defensive piece due to its incredible ability and typing, which helps it check threats like Tapu Lele, Mega Medicham, and Zamazenta while also being immune to Great Tusk and Terapagos’s Rapid Spin and Defog from Tornadus-T and Zapdos. Focus Blast allows Gholdengo to hit would-be checks in Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Terapagos without Tera Shell. Thunder Wave allows Gholdengo to slow down Pokemon such as Terapagos, Ogerpon-W, and Heatran. Hex is boosted to new heights because of Thunder Wave, and it severely damages Gliscor. Ghostium Z allows Gholdengo to greatly harm Pokemon that are unable to be paralyzed by Thunder Wave such as Raging Bolt, Zapdos, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T. Leftovers allows Gholdengo to have an easier time switching in against Pokemon like Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant repeatedly. Fightinium Z helps Gholdengo secure OHKOs on Assault Vest Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Terapagos without Tera Shell while also being more reliable to hit with than Focus Blast. Air Balloon allows Gholdengo to be completely immune to Ground-type attacks from the likes of Gliscor and Great Tusk and block Rapid Spin from Great Tusk more effectively. The given EVs allow Gholdengo to outspeed uninvested Landorus-T and Jolly Kingambit while avoiding the OHKO from Choice Scarf Landorus-T.

Gholdengo fits on various playstyles where its paralysis support and incredible defensive utility are valued. Teammates that set up entry hazards like Hisuian Samurott and Ting-Lu are perfect partners for Gholdengo because of it being an effective blocker of hazard removal from Terapagos and Great Tusk, especially if it is holding Air Balloon. Wallbreakers such as Mega Medicham and Ogerpon-W benefit from Gholdengo checking revenge killers like Tornadus-T, Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, and Zamazenta while also slowing down these faster threats with Thunder Wave. Gholdengo is unable to consistently break through Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Volcarona and is passive against Zapdos and Raging Bolt if it is unable to use a Z-Move. It is also easily outpaced by threats like Roaring Moon, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Charizard Y, limiting its ability to stay on the field safely. Teammates like Dragonite, Mega Tyranitar, and Zamazenta are great partners to help work around these issues. Iron Valiant is also a great partner for Gholdengo, as it appreciates Gholdengo paralyzing faster revenge killers like Tapu Lele and Tornadus-T, and in return, it takes care of Pokemon like Hisuian Samurott and Kingambit for Gholdengo.

battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Speed EV Benchmarks

  • 4 Spe: This outspeeds maximum Speed Modest Ursaluna-B.

  • 68 Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Ursaluna and Jolly Kingambit.

  • 84 Spe: This outspeeds Timid Ursaluna-B.

  • 148 Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Breloom.

  • 164 Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Tyranitar.

  • 228 Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Dragonite.

  • 244 Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Breloom.

  • 188+ Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Baxcalibur.

  • 220+ Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Dragonite.

  • 228+ Spe: This outspeeds maximum Speed Modest Archaludon.

Paralysis EV Benchmarks

  • 20 Spe: This outspeeds paralyzed +Speed Dragapult.

  • 28 Spe: This outspeeds paralyzed Choice Scarf Basculegion.

  • 36 Spe: This outspeeds paralyzed +1 Speed Jolly Dragonite and paralyzed Choice Scarf Gallade.

  • 84 Spe: This outspeeds paralyzed +1 Speed Jolly Baxcalibur.

  • 108 Spe: This outspeeds paralyzed Choice Scarf Annihilape.

  • 140 Spe: This outspeeds paralyzed Choice Scarf Mimikyu

  • 156 Spe: This outspeeds paralyzed Choice Scarf Hydreigon.

  • 172 Spe: This outspeeds paralyzed +1 Speed Volcarona.

  • 220+ Spe: This outspeeds paralyzed Choice Scarf Meowscarada.

Choice Item.description:
• With Trick and an immunity to status moves, Gholdengo is a dangerous Choice item attacker for offensive and stall teams alike!

  • Nasty Plot: This can be used to give Gholdengo more bite against defensive, slower teams after using Trick.

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt OHKOes Pelipper and matches Make It Rain for damage against Primarina. It also stops Tera Water Garganacl from walling Gholdengo. It does make Gholdengo very vulnerable to Ground-types like Ursaluna-B and Garchomp though.

  • Focus Blast: Focus Blast slices through Kingambit, who otherwise walls Gholdengo, but the accuracy can be a big issue in close matches.

Other Options

  • Power Gem: Power Gem severly punishes Volcarona switch-ins, who otherwise can be very difficult to deal with. Otherwise, most Pokemon weak to Rock-type attacks will take more damage from Make It Rain.

  • Dazzling Gleam: Dazzling Gleam can be paired with Tera Fairy to crush Hydreigon, though Make It Rain deals more damage to most other Dragon-type targets like Dragonite and Garchomp.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: With this, Gholdengo outspeeds key threats such as Garchomp, Dragapult, and Hydreigon. It also outspeeds Meowscarada, but beware of Sucker Punch.

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs make Gholdengo much more difficult to wall, with Assault Vest Ursaluna-B in particular being much easier to break through.

EV Spreads

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Timid or Modest: Gholdengo mirror matches are common enough that maximizing Speed is usually a wise idea. Choice Scarf Gholdengo particularly needs Timid to outspeed Dragapult. If using Choice Specs, Modest becomes easier to justify for cracking through Ursaluna-B more reliably.

  • 172 HP / 252 SpA / 84 Spe with Modest: This spread focuses on outspeeding Timid Ursaluna-B, Jolly Ursaluna, and Jolly Kingambit, all of whom are uncommon but very deadly to Gholdengo.

  • 212 HP / 236 Def / 52 SpA / 4 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This bulky Choice Specs spread survives Dragonite's +1 Earthquake, while outspeeding maximum Speed Modest Ursaluna-B.

  • 244 HP / 4 Def / 12 SpA / 244 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This extremely bulky spread allows Tera Flying Choice Speccs Gholdengo to survive Tera Normal Ursaluna-B's Blood Moon followed by Vacuum Wave.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Choice Gholdengo is perfectly functional without Terastallizing, it's particularly vulnerable to common Pokemon that Terastallization can solve such as Hydreigon, Garchomp, and Ursaluna-B.

  • Flying: With a Flying Tera type, Gholdengo gains an extremely useful immunity to Ground, which is especially useful on Choice Specs sets against Ursaluna-B and Garchomp.

  • Water: This Tera type gives Gholdengo a valuable resistance to Fire and Water, massively improving the matchup against Primarina and Volcarona.

  • Steel: Make It Rain becomes very powerful with a Tera boost, giving Choice Specs the chance to OHKO several Ursaluna-B variants in particular.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting saves Gholdengo from Kingambit's Sucker Punch, and can be paired with Tera Blast for a far more reliable Fighting-type attack than Focus Blast.

  • Normal: A Normal Tera type gives Gholdengo the edge against opposing Ghost-types, potentially flipping the table against hard to check sets like Trick Mimikyu.

Minor Optimizations

  • Neutral Nature and Nature Mints: Use a neutral nature Gholdengo that has a Timid or Modest Mint used on it. This way, Gholdengo can eat any Berry without being confused after Trick.

Nasty Plot.description:
• Nasty Plot makes Gholdengo a terror against slower teams, especially with its good bulk, unpredictable coverage, and diverse Tera Types.

  • Substitute: Substitute lets Gholdengo avoid residual damage from Garganacl's Salt Cure and eases prediction in general.

  • Focus Blast: Despite its reliability issues, Focus Blast OHKOes Kingambit, who otherwise is a great check against Gholdengo, in addition to ripping through Ursaluna-B switch-ins.

Other Options

  • Psyshock: Psyshock lets Gholdengo break through Clodsire more easily as well as OHKOing Sneasler without a boost. It often isn't particularly useful outside of stall match-ups though.

Items

  • Covert Cloak: Covert Cloak prevents Salt Cure from chipping down Gholdengo, making it far easier for it to run Recover against Garganacl.

  • Leftovers: This is the most reliable option for keeping Gholdengo healthy and pairs especially well with Substitute.

  • Air Balloon: Air Balloon prevents Dragonite and Ursaluna-B from hitting Gholdengo particularly hard until its popped. It also ruins Breloom's chances of winning the lead war against Gholdengo and makes Hippowdon easy set-up bait.

EV Spreads

  • 156 HP / 124 SpA / 228 Spe with Modest: This spread outspeeds Adamant Dragonite, while having the same Special Attack stat as a fully invested Timid Gholdengo to disguise itself as the Choice Scarf set.

  • 84 HP / 252 SpA / 172 Spe with Timid: This outspeeds up to Modest Archaludon and Jolly Dragonite, two foes that otherwise can revenge kill Gholdengo.

  • 212 HP / 236 Def / 52 SpA / 4 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: This physically bulky spread survives Dragonite's boosted Earthquake, which can be particularly helpful from stopping a Choice Band Dragonite revenge kill.

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Timid: Maximizing Speed is useful on more offensive sets to at least speedtie with opposing Gholdengo, and outspeeding several threats close to this Speed tier, such as Dragonite.

  • 244 HP / 4 Def / 12 SpA / 244 SpD / 4 Spe with Modest: Focusing on special bulk allows Tera Flying Gholdengo to survive Tera Normal Ursaluna's Blood Moon followed by Focus Blast.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Gholdengo may have a great typing, but common Pokemon such as Garchomp, Hydreigon, and Meowscarada will usually revenge kill it without Terastallization.

  • Flying: Flying Gholdengo gets the jump on dangerous offensive Ground-types like Ursaluna-B and Garchomp, as well as Pokemon that use Ground-type coverage like Dragonite.

  • Water: With this Tera type and Tera Blast, Gholdengo can severely punish Volcarona, who otherwise is very dangerous to this set.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting is a good stop to Dark-types such as Kingambit, as well as making Tera Blast into a far more reliable alternative to Focus Blast.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy stops defensive Archaludon from being able to phaze Gholdengo at all, in addition to saving it from Dark-type attacks. This comes at the cost of losing the mirror match up though, as well as being easily revenge killed by offensive Archaludon.

  • Normal: While it's a much worse defensive typing, Tera Normal does let Gholdengo surprise faster Ghost-types like Mimikyu and opposing Gholdengo, at the cost of being revenge killed by Annihilepe and faster Gallade.

Defensive.description:
• While Gholdengo's defensive stats aren't remarkable, it's fantastic typing and immunity to status moves like Taunt make it a great defensive Pokemon, and a horrifically effective spreader of paralysis!

  • Hex versus Shadow Ball: Hex gives this Gholdengo a good offensive kick against paralyzed foes, but Shadow Ball is worth considering for its consistency.

  • Make It Rain versus Focus Blast: Make It Rain is Gholdengo's most consistent way of dealing damage to Garganacl, but this set's defensive nature makes it difficult to win the one-on-one. Focus Blast isn't nearly as reliable, but it's Gholdengo's best shot at making it past Kingambit.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet takes advantage of Gholdengo's excellent typing against physical moves, making it a good way to punish contact moves such as Outrage from Dragonite.

  • Covert Cloak: This is Gholdengo's best shot of outstalling Garganacl, since it grants an immunity to Salt Cure's effect.

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is at its best with specially defensive Gholdengo, letting it withstand Ursaluna-B's Earth Power followed by Vacuum Wave without requiring Terastallization.

  • Weakness Policy: While this might seem strange on a defensive Pokemon, Weakness Policy lets Gholdengo beat opposing Gholdengo as long as they lack Choice Specs.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 220 Def / 20 Spe with Bold: The given EV spread will outspeed up to paralyzed Dragapult and paralyzed +1 Speed Jolly Dragonite.

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD / 4 Spe with Calm: This offers Gholdengo the best shot of surviving Ursaluna-B's Earth Power followed by Vacuum Wave after Leftovers recovery.

  • 252 HP / 84 Def / 172 Spe with Bold: The Speed investment allows Gholdengo to outspeed Choice Scarf Hydreigon and Speed-boosted Volcarona with the magic of paralysis.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Despite Gholdengo's fantastic typing, foes like Garchomp and Hydreigon are easily able to break through any Gholdengo that doesn't Terastallize.

  • Flying: Avoiding Earthquake against foes like Garchomp makes Tera Flying extremely useful for Gholdengo; this also gives it protection against Fissure from the likes of Dondozo and Garganacl.

  • Water: Tera Water is the best Fire-type resistant Tera type for Gholdengo, letting it potentially survive an assault from Volcarona and Choice Specs Primarina, though its coverage moves can still seriously damage Gholdengo.

  • Fighting: Tera Fighting flips the tables on Kingambit, who otherwise only fears full paralysis, while turning Tera Blast into reliable Fighting-type coverage. It's also useful against Meowscarada, though its coverage moves can still deal serious damage to Gholdengo.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Focus Blast is an option over any damaging move for its ability to dispatch Kingambit and Heatran effectively, which would otherwise be able to stave Gholdengo's attacks off. A more offensive version of Gholdengo utilizing Nasty Plot with maximum Special Attack and Speed investment and a Timid nature serves as a potent setup sweeper and can be used on teams utilizing Sticky Web to have Gholdengo act as a hard-hitting spinblocker. Choice item sets can run an immunity ability like Well-Baked Body or Levitate to serve as a quick stopgap to Fire- and Ground-type. Psyshock is a niche option on Choice Specs sets that allows Gholdengo to 2HKO the special walls that would usually check it, like Blissey, RegenVest Swampert, and Iron Hands.

Checks and Counters

Special Walls: Common special walls like RegenVest Roaring Moon, Swampert, and Bulletproof Iron Treads can easily switch into Gholdengo and force it out.

Dark-types: Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Kingambit irritate Gholdengo with their ability to switch into it and force it out.

Fire-types and Ground-types: Gholdengo cannot nullify its weakness to both Fire- and Ground-type moves when opting for an immunity ability, causing it to be weak to one type or the other.

Choice Item.description:
Choice item Gholdengo acts a strong wallbreaker and speed control option, boasting a spammable STAB move and nuke in Shadow Ball and Make It Rain, respectively. Recover should exclusively be used on Choice Scarf sets to allow Gholdengo to take advantage of its good natural typing and above-average bulk, allowing it to consistently switch into offensive threats like Scream Tail, Iron Boulder, and Assault Vest Iron Crown, outspeed them, and force them out while offsetting any damage it may have taken in the process. Dazzling Gleam threatens Dark-types like Roaring Moon while still being a solid middle-ground option against Chien-Pao and Kingambit, and it is Gholdengo's strongest attack against Iron Hands. Thunderbolt is a strong coverage option that lets Gholdengo hit RegenVest Manaphy while being the best move against Kingambit. Lastly, Trick is a good option on Choice Scarf sets that allows Gholdengo to cripple would-be checks like Iron Treads, RegenVest Manaphy, and Swampert, debilitating them while opening itself and other special attacking teammates up later in the game. Adaptability is preferred on sets that only use Gholdengo's STAB moves as damaging moves, as it allows Gholdengo to feint other abilities, but Hadron Engine is preferred on sets with Dazzling Gleam or Thunderbolt to increase their damage output. Choice Specs and a Modest nature turn Gholdengo into a ferocious wallbreaker, allowing it to OHKO RegenVest Manaphy and Roaring Moon with Hadron Engine-boosted Thunderbolt and Dazzling Gleam while almost always OHKOing or 2HKOing every Pokemon in the tier that lacks a Steel-resistance or excellent special bulk. Choice Scarf instead allows it to act as a great speed control option and revenge killer, allowing it to outspeed notable threats like Zamazenta, Chien-Pao, and non-Choice Scarf Roaring Moon.

Gholdengo best fits on balance and bulky offense teams, where its capabilities of acting as either a potent wallbreaker or speed control option are much appreciated. Gholdengo struggles to break past special walls like Blissey, RegenVest Swampert, and Bulletproof Iron Treads, making physical wallbreakers that can put a dent in them like Zamazenta, Roaring Moon, and Chien-Pao good teammates; these physical wallbreakers may struggle with their inability to break past physical walls as well as their Fairy-type checks, all of which Gholdengo helps to cover, bolstering the effectiveness of using them together. Gholdengo struggles against wallbreakers that either outspeed it or survive a hit and threaten it back in return, notably Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, Kingambit, and Deoxys-S, making defensive partners like Corviknight, RegenVest Manaphy, and Roaring Moon good teammates.

Physically Defensive.description:
Physically defensive Gholdengo serves as an excellent spinblocker and physical wall, leveraging its great typing and useful movepool to either spread paralysis with Thunder Wave or set up with Nasty Plot and break holes in the opposing team. Dazzling Gleam dispatches Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Chien-Pao while dealing decent damage to Kingambit, while Hex is an option when used with Thunder Wave that also deals good damage to Bulletproof Iron Treads. Nasty Plot turns Gholdengo into a potent bulky wallbreaker, allowing it to potentially OHKO RegenVest Roaring Moon with Dazzling Gleam after a boost. Thunder Wave allows Gholdengo to power up Hex while slowing down threats for its offensive teammates like the Ogerpon formes, Iron Moth, and Kingambit, which appreciate their offensive checks like Roaring Moon and Zamazenta being slowed down and having the opportunity to be broken past. The given EV spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Great Tusk without Speed investment. Levitate turns Ground-types like Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and the Landorus formes into setup fodder or an opportunity to spread paralysis on an incoming switch-in while also allowing Gholdengo to almost always deny Rapid Spin attempts from the aforementioned Great Tusk and Iron Treads. Fluffy turns Gholdengo into a hard-to-KO threat that can set up with ease or spread paralysis while watching most physical moves bounce off it. Well-Baked Body allows Gholdengo to check Fire-types like Moltres, Ogerpon-H, and Cinderace and turns them into setup or paralysis fodder. Colbur Berry allows Gholdengo to lure in Dark-types like Roaring Moon and Chien-Pao, OHKOing them with a boosted Dazzling Gleam or Make It Rain, while Leftovers provides Gholdengo with passive recovery that grants it with good longevity. Heavy-Duty Boots is an option on non-Levitate sets that allows them to offset entry hazard chip damage, allowing them to switch in more frequently while opening up Earth Eater as a potential ability option that punishes Ground-type moves even further.

Gholdengo fits best on bulky offense teams, where its spinblocking capabilities and general utility is much appreciated. Furthermore, bulky offense teams that can stack numerous entry hazards are where Gholdengo can truly shine as a spinblocker that can last throughout the course of a game. Thus, hazard setters like Ting-Lu, Skarmory, and Great Tusk pair well with it. Gholdengo's limit of one ability leaves it prone to Ground-types, Fire-types, or even both depending on its ability, thus, Pokemon that can switch into Ground-types frequently like Corviknight, Zapdos, and the Landorus formes make for good teammates, while Pokemon that can switch into Fire-types like Primordial Sea Zapdos as well as physically defensive Manaphy pair well with it. Gholdengo's mediocre Special Defense leaves it prone to strong special attackers like Zapdos, Thundurus-T, and opposing Gholdengo, making special walls like RegenVest Roaring Moon, Swampert, and Manaphy good partners.

Nasty Plot.description:
• Nasty Plot allows Gholdengo to become a potent wincon, capable of cleaning up weakened teams with its powerful spread damage. Its good defensive typing and incredible ability in Good as Gold give it plenty of opportunities to set up in front of common Pokemon such as Rillaboom, Tornadus, Whimsicott, and Amoonguss, since it resists all of their STAB moves and is not affected by Fake Out, Taunt, Encore, or Spore.

  • Make It Rain becomes incredibly powerful when boosted by Nasty Plot and can severely damage anything that doesn't resist it. However, it drops Gholdengo's Special Attack after being used and is resisted by several common Pokemon, such as Incineroar and Iron Hands, meaning that it can't be freely used repeatedly, as opponents can play around Make It Rain until Gholdengo runs out of steam. This makes Make It Rain most effective when used against weakened teams that have their switch-in options limited, or in positions where the opponent is unable to protect their neutral targets from it.

  • Shadow Ball gives Gholdengo an option against Steel-resistant Pokemon such as Iron Hands, Raging Bolt, and Ogerpon's Wellspring and Hearthflame Formes, allowing it to preserve its Nasty Plot boost and still maintain offensive pressure. Dazzling Gleam, in combination with Tera Fairy, is able to completely flip the script on Iron Hands and provide a neutral damage option against Incineroar and Swords Dance Kingambit.

  • The given EV spread guarantees Gholdengo will survive a Sucker Punch from full from Adamant Chien-Pao while also allowing it to outspeed Modest Choice Scarf Chi-Yu when in Tailwind. Gholdengo's longevity can be increased with Leftovers, which becomes especially impactful when paired with Rillaboom's Grassy Terrain, doubling the amount of passive recovery received per turn. Alternatively, Metal Coat turns Make It Rain into even more of a nuke, which is useful on teams focused more around immediate offensive power.

  • Tera Dragon grants Gholdengo crucial resistances to Fire and Water while maintaining its resistance to Grass, allowing it to resist all the STAB moves of both Ogerpon-W and Ogerpon-H. However, the gained weaknesses to Dragon, Ice, and Fairy leave it in a precarious spot against strong Dragon-types such as Regidrago and Raging Bolt while also making it vulnerable to foes it can normally beat such as Chien-Pao, Kyurem, and Whimsicott. Alternatively, Tera Fairy provides Gholdengo with a useful resistance to Dark and serves as a generally good defensive typing. Lastly, Tera Steel can be used to further strengthen Make It Rain while also dropping Gholdengo's weakness to Dark. The loss of Gholdengo's Ghost typing should always be kept in mind when considering whether to Terastallize it, as becoming vulnerable to Fake Out can severely hinder it in certain matchups.

  • Incineroar and Kingambit are bulky foes that resist both of Gholdengo's STAB moves and threaten it back with super effective moves, so it appreciates teammates that can deal with these threats such as Landorus and Iron Hands. Speed control is very important for Gholdengo, as it prefers to move first despite its mediocre Speed tier teammates that provide Tailwind support such as Tornadus and Whimsicott make for natural partners. Teammates that provide redirection support, such as Ogerpon-W, Indeedee-F, and Amoonguss are also useful, as they can provide Gholdengo with free turns to set up and increase its longevity by keeping it safe. The same applies to Pokemon that can provide Fake Out support such as Rillaboom and Incineroar.

Choice Specs.description:
• Choice Specs Gholdengo provides more immediate offense compared to Nasty Plot variants. Choice Specs-boosted Tera Steel Make It Rain can quickly overwhelm the opposing team, leaving the opponent scrambling to bring in their few Steel-resistant Pokemon. Shadow Ball acts as the secondary STAB move, hitting key targets such as Archaludon and opposing Gholdengo.

  • Power Gem and Focus Blast provide answers to some of the common foes that resist Gholdengo's STAB coverage. Both moves hit Incineroar and Chi-Yu super effectively, while Focus Blast specifically lets it threaten Kingambit. Power Gem is usually the preferred option because of its consistency. Trick is able to severely disrupt the opponent's support or setup-oriented Pokemon such as Amoonguss. Trick can also be utilized against Sucker Punch users, causing their attack to fail and locking them down with a Choice item.

  • Tera Steel is the Tera type of choice to push Make It Rain's damage even further. It also provides defensive benefits in removing Gholdengo's weakness to Ghost- and Dark-type attacks, notably opposing Gholdengo's Shadow Ball and the Sucker Punches coming from Chien-Pao and Kingambit.

  • The EV spread maximizes Gholdengo’s Special Attack to focus on heavy damage output. The HP and Defense investment allow it to survive Jolly Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch without the need to Terastallize defensively. The Speed makes Gholdengo faster than Booster Energy Gouging Fire and Modest Choice Scarf Chi-Yu under Tailwind.

  • Good as Gold allows Gholdengo to switch in against status-reliant Pokemon almost completely unthreatened by them. This most notably includes Amoonguss, as its presence in the metagame often demands teams to have Spore-immune answers.

  • Gholdengo's Speed leaves it outpaced by many of the metagame's major threats, such as Landorus and Ogerpon-H; because of this, it is very frequently paired with Tailwind users to support it. Tornadus and Whimsicott both have the Prankster ability that make them particularly ideal in this role.

  • Pokemon that can assist Gholdengo in breaking down the tougher Steel-resistant Pokemon are helpful. For instance, Landorus is particularly effective at taking down the Fire-, Electric-, and Steel-types with its powerful Ground-type STAB moves. Ogerpon-W is another strong partner for Gholdengo, offering Follow Me for redirection support in addition to being able to offensively threaten Landorus and many Fire- and Water-types. Rillaboom is also a fantastic partner, as it's efficient in removing Water-types. In addition, it's effective at luring in the Fire- and Steel-types that resist its Terrain-boosted Grass-type moves, wearing them down for Gholdengo to break through. Further still, Rillaboom is an effective pivot that can help secure Gholdengo's safe entrance onto the field.

Levitate (Chimecho / Latios / Latias).description: Keep in mind that due to how Inheritance works, when using this set any combination of moves you wish to run must be legal on either Chimecho, Latios, or Latias.

Spikes + Spin (Bramblin).description: 100 Speed EVs allows it to outspeed uninvested Gliscor

Fur Coat + SubPlot (Persian-Alola).description: Maximum HP investment combined with 4 Defence EVs prevents Knock Off from Assault Vest Snorlax from ever breaking a Substitute. 100 Speed EVs allows it to outspeed uninvested Gliscor

Bulky Nasty Plot (Steel).description: Boasting a Fighting immunity, the ability to deny status moves, reliable recovery, and the potential to spike the cortisol levels of any opponent, Gholdengo is a versatile and powerful Pokemon that serves as the backbone of nearly all Steel teams. With Ghostium Z and heavy investment into physical bulk, Gholdengo becomes a sturdy set up sweeper and defensive piece that has both incredible longevity and strong immediate offensive presence. Nasty Plot and Recover allow Gholdengo to find setup opportunities multiple times throughout a match, as it can setup safely in front of the many Pokemon—like Swords Dance Iron Valiant, Mega Scizor, and Sneasler—that cannot 2HKO it. Make It Rain heavily dents most Ghost-resistant and immune Pokemon, such as Roaring Moon and Porygon2. Hex and Thunder Wave can be run over Shadow Ball and Make It Rain, which allows Gholdengo to spread paralysis to the aforementioned Pokemon it checks while also crippling switch-ins like Volcarona at the cost of not being able to damage Normal-type Pokemon. When powered up by Ghostium Z, both Hex and Shadow Ball deal massive damage, nearly always OHKOing offensive Great Tusk unboosted and being similarly favored to OHKO Hisuian Samurott and most Toxapex sets after a Nasty Plot boost. Gholdengo's EVs maximize its bulk, notably allowing it to survive Mega Lopunny's Close Combat from full HP while outpacing Jolly Ursaluna and Azumarill. Spikes Skarmory and Stealth Rock Heatran are fantastic teammates for Gholdengo, as they form an entry hazard-stacking immunity core that covers Gholdengo defensively while wearing down those of its checks that must switch in multiple times such as Hisuian Goodra, Ting-Lu, and Clodsire. Skarmory handles Ground-type foes and the few Fighting-types Gholdengo cannot, such as Mega Lopunny and Great Tusk, while Heatran absorbs Fire-type moves from Volcarona and Victini. In return, Gholdengo ensures hazards stay on the field and helps Skarmory and Heatran not get overwhelmed by Fighting-types and other dangerous foes such as Superpower Ogerpon-C. Another good choice to help Gholdengo defensively is Hisuian Goodra, which shrugs off strong moves from special attackers like Choice Specs Greninja and Hydreigon. Hisuian Goodra can also use Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes, and its Dragon Tail racks up chip damage from the hazards Gholdengo stops foes from removing. Iron Treads removes hazards, threatens to OHKO foes like Landorus and Heatran that outspeed and OHKO Gholdengo, and uses Knock Off to further the efficacy of hazard-stacking cores.

Z-Move (Ghost).description: Having a typing with a lot of relevant resistances, an immunity to status moves thanks to Good as Gold, and great longevity by virtue of having Recover, Gholdengo is a potent stallbreaker for Ghost teams. Shadow Ball hits most foes for neutral damage, with Never-Ending Nightmare at +2 OHKOing foes such as Mega Sableye, Galarian Slowking, and Corviknight. Make It Rain lets Gholdengo hit foes such as Alolan Muk, Mandibuzz, and Kommo-o, as well as OHKO Ice- and Fairy-type foes such as Mamoswine, Alolan Ninetales, and Iron Valiant, and at +2, this move OHKOes Gliscor, Hippowdon, and Ursaluna. The given EV spread allows Gholdengo to outspeed Adamant Mamoswine and avoid a 2HKO from Mega Scizor's Knock Off, Ogerpon-C's Knock Off after Stealth Rock, and Choice Specs Tapu Lele's Thunderbolt. Mega Sableye forms a good defensive core with Gholdengo, as Mega Sableye mitigates its vulnerability to Dark- and Ghost-type foes such as Meowscarada, Greninja, and Hisuian Zoroark, while Gholdengo handles Fairy-types including Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant. Sinistcha can switch into Ground-types such as Garchomp, Mega Swampert, and Great Tusk that Gholdengo is vulnerable to. Fire-types such as Ceruledge and Skeledirge are solid partners that can check other Fire-types that force out Gholdengo such as Cinderace, Victini, and Volcarona.

Choice Scarf (Steel).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Specially Defensive.description:
Wo-Chien leverages its massive bulk, ability, and utility movepool to serve as an effective wall and disruptor by removing items from and chipping away at the opposing team. Foul Play gives Wo-Chien a means of punishing physical setup sweepers like Maushold and Bisharp, which attempt to exploit its relative passivity. Ruination pressures Wo-Chien's defensive answers like Chesnaught and is generally a useful progress maker against Pokemon lacking reliable recovery like Hisuian Goodra and Suicune. Leech Seed serves as Wo-Chien's secondary source of recovery and pairs nicely with Ruination, allowing Wo-Chien to wear down foes over the course of the match regardless of their Defense. Protect gives Wo-Chien an additional turn to recover health and scout moves from Choice item users like Basculegion-F, Gardevoir, and Gengar. Leftovers is essential for maximizing Wo-Chien's longevity and make up for its lack of recovery moves. While its defensive EVs are fairly customizable depending on the needs of the team, the Special Defense investment makes Wo-Chien a particularly strong answer to Calm Mind users like Slowbro, Suicune, and Necrozma. Tera Poison patches up Wo-Chien's Fighting-, Fairy- and Bug-type weaknesses while denying poison from Pokemon like Amoonguss and Umbreon, which would otherwise threaten Wo-Chien's longevity. Tera Ghost similarly removes Wo-Chien's weaknesses to Bug- and Fighting-type moves but instead allows it to spinblock against Cyclizar and more effectively answer Maushold, Yanmega, and Ribombee.

Wo-Chien fits nicely on balance teams that enjoy its ability to sponge hits while making progress with Knock Off and Leech Seed. Hazard-stacking teams particularly enjoy Wo-Chien's ability to remove items like Heavy-Duty Boots and Leftovers from opposing Pokemon, thus maximizing damage output from entry hazards over time. Therefore, entry hazard setters like Gligar, and Gastrodon pair nicely with Wo-Chien. In addition, entry hazards cause Regenerator Pokemon like Slowbro and Cyclizar to take more damage than what they recover with every switch, preventing them from stalling out Wo-Chien. Because of its weakness to Fighting-, Bug-, and Fairy-type moves, Wo-Chien appreciates teammates that complement its defensive profile like Registeel, Talonflame and Slowbro. Physically defensive teammates like Rocky Helmet Hippowdon and Bellibolt are also useful partners, as they can switch in on and punish U-turns and Knock Offs directed at Wo-Chien. Status moves are especially troublesome for Wo-Chien, as they threaten its ability to sit in on other Pokemon and recover health throughout the battle, so Pokemon that are immune to or don't mind status conditions like Magnezone can be helpful as teammates. Pokemon that can spread burn like Will-O-Wisp Talonflame, Scald Slowbro, and Sacred Fire Entei are beneficial for Wo-Chien too, allowing it to more comfortably endure physical attacks and retaliate with Foul Play. Wo-Chien benefits greatly from entry hazard removal, as it will likely be switched in and out throughout the course of the battle. Therefore, Pokemon that can remove entry hazards like Cyclizar, Noivern, and Talonflame make for nice partners. Cyclizar is a particularly good partner on hazard-stacking teams, since Rapid Spin does not clear entry hazards on the opponent's side, thus improving Wo-Chien's ability to chip down the opposing team through Knock Off and Leech Seed. Wo-Chien often lures in Poison- and Fighting-types that can be exploited by Future Sight users like Slowbro and Reuniclus. Because of its relative passivity, Wo-Chien can easily get overwhelmed by opposing wallbreakers and setup sweepers, especially if it's unable to Terastallize. As such, potent revenge killers and priority users like Choice Scarf Gengar and Gardevoir and Extreme Speed Entei are appreciated as well.

Defensive.description:
Foul Play threatens physical setup sweepers like Rhydon and Hisuian Decidueye with heavy damage, while Ruination is better at putting pressure on foes like Scrafty and Florges that can otherwise take advantage of Wo-Chien. Leech Seed punishes teams for trying to maneuver around Wo-Chien and synergizes well with Protect. Protect is also useful for scouting Choice users such as Paldean Tauros-F and Hoopa. Rest + Sleep Talk offers Wo-Chien consistent staying power, making it less afraid of status and allowing it to check multiple Pokemon for longer.

Sample set. Stay tuned for updates!

nu.overview: Wo-Chien's excellent bulk, typing, and great ability give it a unique place in NU, allowing it to consistently handle powerful wallbreakers such as Basculegion-M, Flygon, and Barraskewda. Additionally, it can exploit common walls like Vaporeon, Bronzong, and Galarian Slowbro. Furthermore, Wo-Chien can make some great progress thanks to its access to both Knock Off and Leech Seed. Unfortunately, Wo-Chien's typing also makes it weak to many common threats such as Flamigo, Munkidori, and Chandelure, while the Pokemon it was supposed to check like Flygon and Decidueye can threaten it by hitting back with U-turn. Wo-Chien struggles to do anything against certain walls like Amoonguss and Poison Heal Breloom due to them being immune to its Leech Seed and their access to recovery. Wo-Chien's lack of recovery can force it to use Protect or RestTalk, allowing Pokemon like Munkidori, Scrafty, and Raikou to freely set up or put some pressure on Wo-Chien with chip damage.
nu.comments:
Other Options

Stun Spore can be used for slowing down faster foes like Flamigo and Overqwil, but Wo-Chien prefers to run other utility options. Wo-Chien can run a fully physically defensive spread, letting it better handle foes like Flygon, Drednaw, and Rhyperior; however, it makes Wo-Chien worse against threats like Inteleon and Amoonguss. Tera Water maintains the Water-type resistance while giving Wo-Chien a better matchup against Fire- and Ice-types like Paldean Tauros-F and Alolan Ninetales, but it gives Wo-Chien a weakness to Electric- and Grass-type moves from Raikou and Breloom.

Checks and Counters

Fighting-types: Toxicroak, Flamigo, Breloom, and the Paldean Tauros formes easily threaten Wo-Chien with their Fighting-type attacks, but they must be cautious about switching into Leech Seed and Ruination. Scrafty can use Wo-Chien as complete setup fodder while forcing it to use up its Tera. However, Scrafty must be cautious about switching into its Leech Seed and Ruination.

Fire-types: Chandelure, Arcanine, and Incineroar can do major damage against Wo-Chien with their Fire-type attacks, and the latter two can use it as setup fodder. However, none of them enjoy switching into its Knock Off, Leech Seed, and Ruination.

Fairy- and Poison-types: Sylveon, Alolan Ninetales, and Diancie can overwhelm Wo-Chien with their attacks, but they need to cautious about switching into Leech Seed and Knock Off. Poison-types such as Galarian Slowbro and Overqwil can threaten Wo-Chien with status, while the latter can tank its STAB attacks; however, both of them can’t repeatedly switch into Leech Seed and Ruination.

Bulky Grass-types: Amoonguss completely walls Wo-Chien thanks to its access to Synthesis and Regenerator, which allows it to repeatedly switch in against Wo-Chien. It can also threaten Wo-Chien with Toxic or Sludge Bomb poison. Tsareena and Poison Heal Breloom can be major roadblocks for Wo-Chien, since Tsareena can threaten it with Knock Off and U-turn, while Breloom can use it as free setup fodder; however, the former must be cautious about switching into Ruination.

Specially Defensive.description:
Set Details

Foul Play gives Wo-Chien a great advantage against physical wallbreakers like Swords Dance Rhyperior and Basculegion-M, while Ruination can be used for solid chip damage and to threaten walls such as Galarian Slowbro and Diancie. Giga Drain can be used to answer Rhyperior most effectively. Protect allows Wo-Chien to scout out any Choice item users like Flamigo and Chandelure while giving it extra Leftovers recovery. Wo-Chien can run a RestTalk set, letting it consistently handle foes like Barraskewda, Flygon, and Cinccino as well as dealing with any status attempts. Leech Seed can wear down foes such as Overqwil and Scrafty that Wo-Chien struggles to make progress versus otherwise. Leftovers provides Wo-Chien extra recovery, whereas Heavy-Duty Boots allows it to not be worn down by repeatedly switching into entry hazards. 16 Speed EVs let Wo-Chien outrun Adamant Rhyperior and potentially threaten it with Foul Play or Giga Drain. Tera Poison offers Wo-Chien a resistance against both Fighting- and Poison-type attacks from foes like Flamigo, Toxicroak, and Overqwil.
