Tera Ghost lets Wo-Chien spinblock Tsareena, and it gives Wo-Chien a useful immunity against Fighting-type moves from Pokemon like Infernape and Paldean Tauros-W, while Tera Fairy offers a Fighting-type resistance with a trade-off for better handling foes like Flygon, Heracross, and Incineroar. On top of that, Tera Poison, Ghost, and Fairy allow Wo-Chien to better handle U-turn from Flygon and Cinccino. Alternatively, Tera Dragon lets Wo-Chien better handle Fire-types such as Chandelure, Infernape, and Arcanine.

Wo-Chien best partners with defensive teammates such as Bellibolt, Rhyperior, and Galarian Slowbro, since they can better handle threats like Flamigo, Arcanine, and Toxicroak. Fire-resistant teammates such as Vaporeon, Diancie, and Altaria can help Wo-Chien handle foes like Chandelure and Infernape. Pokemon like Toxtricity, Basculegion-M, and Kilowattrel appreciate its Knock Off for threatening foes that heavily rely on their item like Porygon2, Rhyperior, and Klefki. Additionally, Wo-Chien struggles to break through Pokemon like Amoonguss, Goodra, and Poison Heal Breloom; thus, it pairs with teammates like Kilowattrel, Scrafty, and Diancie to handle them. Entry hazard removers like Altaria and Cramorant are crucial for helping Wo-Chien to better switch in against Pokemon like Basculegion-M and Barraskewda without getting worn down. Hazard setters like Rhyperior, Duraludon, and Gligar appreciate Wo-Chien's Knock Off making their hazards more effective against foes like Altaria, Cramorant, and Bellibolt. In return, they can handle Flying- and Fighting-types like Kilowattrel and Flamigo, while Wo-Chien can threaten Ground- and Water-types such as Flygon and Vaporeon.

Mixed Wall (Grass).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

Bulky Support.description:
Wo-Chien is a multifaceted support Pokemon that uses its ability and support toolkit to neutralize opposing threats. Leech Seed and Ruination allow it to chip down foes. Pollen Puff lets Wo-Chien do the reverse and heal up its allies. Snarl weakens special attackers unaffected by Tablets of Ruin, breaks Focus Sashes, and deals serious chip damage to Calyrex-S. Foul Play punishes physical attackers that boost their Attack stats to get around Tablets of Ruin while threatening both Calyrex formes. Wo-Chien generally runs Leftovers but can also run Sitrus Berry to avoid getting 2HKOed by Moonblast from Booster Energy Flutter Mane. The Speed EVs allow Wo-Chien to outspeed bulky Kyogre; this allows it to boost Kyogre's Water Spout damage by using Pollen Puff on it before it can move. With 44 Defense EVs, Wo-Chien almost always survives Adamant Close Combat from Urshifu, and the rest of its EVs are invested in Special Defense. Tera Poison gives Wo-Chien resistances to Fighting-, Fairy-, and Bug-type moves that would normally threaten it and a strong defensive typing. Tera Water gives Wo-Chien resistances to Fire- and Ice-type moves and a similarly useful typing.

Wo-Chien struggles into special attackers that can hit it super-effectively such as Tornadus, Flutter Mane, and Amoonguss. It is also chipped heavily by U-turn from Pokemon such as Rillaboom and Urshifu-R. Wo-Chien is almost always paired with Kyogre, which appreciates Tablets of Ruin boosting its Defense and getting its Water Spouts powered up by fast Pollen Puffs. Wo-Chien is also often partnered with Incineroar and Grimmsnarl; Grimmsnarl can boost Wo-Chien's defenses further through its screens and weaken special attackers with Spirit Break, while Incineroar helps Wo-Chien stay on the field longer with Fake Out, Intimidate, and Parting Shot and matches up favorably into several Pokemon Wo-Chien struggles with, such as Amoonguss and Chien-Pao.

Leech Seed.description:
• With excellent bulk and a unique array of moves to support it, Wo-Chien stands out as a dangerous user of Leech Seed and a prime Pokemon to stall matches out with.

  • Foul Play versus Knock Off: Foul Play is Wo-Chien's most consistent offensive move that also happens to punish setup sweepers, while Knock Off's support is especially helpful against Trick users such as Gholdengo and Rotom-W. Note that both are viable together if you're willing to give up a support move.

  • Substitute: When paired together with Toxic Spikes, Protect and Substitute makes even foes that should beat Wo-Chien get worn down before they can KO it, such as Chi-Yu. Substitute itself protects Wo-Chien from slow users of Yawn such as Dondozo and Hippowdon, and slow OHKO moves from Ting-Lu, Dondozo, and Kingambit.

  • Ruination: Ruination gives Wo-Chien powerful chipping down potential, though it should never be used as Wo-Chien's only attack due to it being extremely difficult to KO with. When paired with Knock Off, it's especially useful against Wo-Chien mirror matches.

  • Giga Drain: With Stealth Rock support, Giga Drain OHKOes Iron Bundle and almost always 2HKOes Chien-Pao. If you allocate 60 EVs to Special Attack, Giga Drain will OHKO Iron Bundle regardless of Stealth Rock.

  • Taunt: Taunt does an excellent job of surprising other Taunt Pokemon switching in, such as Annihilape and Corviknight.

  • Toxic Spikes Partners: Wo-Chien becomes far more deadly with Toxic Spikes support, letting it quickly wear down a wide variety of foes even faster. Toxapex is one of the best options thanks to its good defensive synergy with Wo-Chien, but other options include Iron Moth, Glimmora, Clodsire, Focus Sash Meowscarada, and the niche Gengar.

Other Options

  • Snarl: Snarl makes fearsome special attackers such as Flutter Mane and Chi-Yu far easier to switch into when Wo-Chien needs to escape, though Wo-Chien will need to have the correct Tera Type to outstall these foes itself.

  • Ingrain: In addition to providing some extra recovery, Ingrain makes phazers such as Ting-Lu and Hippowdon fail to stop Wo-Chien consistently, though Wo-Chien being trapped is a serious drawback.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Despite Wo-Chien's fantastic bulk, its vulnerability to Toxic Spikes and poor defensive typing mean it must often Terastallize to stall out teams.

  • Poison: Tera Poison provides a vital resistance to Fairy and Fighting, and it also lets Wo-Chien absorb Toxic Spikes.

  • Fairy: Besides being a great defensive type, Tera Fairy helps Wo-Chien against Fighting-types that'd normally beat it.

  • Water: Tera Water provides Ice and Fire resistances, helpful against Baxcalibur, Chien-Pao, and Chi-Yu.

  • Fire: Tera Fire gives useful resistances to Fairy, Fire, and Ice, which help against major threats like Flutter Mane, Baxcalibur, Chi-Yu, and Chien-Pao.

Items

  • Leftovers: Wo-Chien's stalling playstyle makes Leftovers the most consistent recovery item.

  • Big Root: If another Pokemon desperately needs Leftovers, Big Root is a viable alternative for getting extra recovery from Leech Seed and Giga Drain.

EV Spreads and Adjustments

  • 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 Spe with Impish or Bold: Maximizing Wo-Chien's physical bulk lets it pull off some incredible stunts, such as avoiding a 3HKO from Breloom's Mach Punch with Leftovers and, after Terastallization, avoiding a 2HKO from Choice Band Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash.

  • 252 HP / 252 SpD / 4 Spe with Careful or Calm: With the correct Tera Type and maximum Special Defense, Wo-Chien can take on Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle much more effectively.

  • Using 60 SpA EVs: If you're willing to give up a bit of bulk, this investment is required to OHKO Iron Bundle with Giga Drain with either a Bold or a Calm nature.

  • Using 100 Speed EVs: With some sacrifice to bulk, this Speed investment lets Wo-Chien outspeed Adamant maximum Speed Kingambit, and it can be vital in Wo-Chien mirror matches after Terastallization makes it vulnerable to Leech Seed, due to Substitute blocking Leech Seed.

Specially Defensive.description: Wo-Chien's unique typing and movepool backed by its high, Tablets of Ruin-boosted bulk grants it a solid place in the metagame, checking threats such as Calyrex-S, Arceus-Ground, and Kyogre. Leech Seed reduces Wo-Chien's passivity while allowing teammates to heal after switching in. Ruination hits foes like Arceus-Fairy, Ting-Lu, and Giratina-O. Foul Play is a stronger alternative against physical attackers like Arceus and Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground that also does a decent chunk of damage to Koraidon and Zacian-C and allows Wo-Chien to punish physical attackers that have Taunt. Knock Off gives Wo-Chien more of a niche due to relevant Pokemon that learn it being rare, and it is useful against foes like Ting-Lu and Landorus-T. However, Arceus formes, which can absorb Knock Off without losing their items, are quite omnipresent. Protect lets Wo-Chien safely rack up Leftovers and Leech Seed recovery. Alternatively, Taunt shuts down setup and entry hazard Pokemon such as Arceus formes and Ting-Lu on the switch. Tera Poison gives Wo-Chien key resistances to attacks like Koraidon's Low Kick, Zacian-C's Play Rough, Double Dance Miraidon's Dazzling Gleam, and the omnipresent U-turn from foes like Landorus-T, Koraidon, and Miraidon while also offering an immunity to Toxic and letting Wo-Chien absorb Toxic Spikes. However, Tera Poison also makes Wo-Chien weak to Ground-type moves from Arceus-Ground and Psychic-type moves from Calyrex-S, respectively. Wo-Chien fits best on balance and bulky offense teams that appreciate its ability to check Calyrex-S and Arceus-Ground while offering good recovery via Leech Seed to teammates. Wo-Chien benefits from teammates such as Skeledirge, Toxapex, and Landorus-T, which check Koraidon and Zacian-C for it. Special attackers in Arceus-Fairy, Substitute Kyogre, and Eternatus trouble Wo-Chien, so offensive checks to them such as Zacian-C, Choice Scarf Koraidon, Arceus, and Calyrex-S are appreciated. Water Absorb Closdire as a defensive teammate checks Arceus-Fairy, Kyogre, and Eternatus while setting up hazards.

Choice Band.description:
• Icicle Crash deals with Ground-, Dragon-, and Flying-type Pokemon like Landorus-T, Garchomp, and Galarian Moltres.
  • Throat Chop is a powerful Dark-type STAB move, which beats stall Skeledirge without Blast Burn by blocking its Torch Song and Pecharunt.
  • Giga Impact deals massive neutral damage to Pokemon that resist Chien-Pao's STAB moves, such as Volcarona, and frailer Pokemon like non-Choice Scarf Porygon-Z.
  • Sacred Sword is good against Dark- and Steel-type Pokemon, such as non-Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Choice Specs Darkrai, and Hisuian Goodra without Chople Berry or Custap Berry.
  • Ice Shard is used to OHKO certain Pokemon that are faster than Chien-Pao, such as Dragapult and Choice Scarf Meowscarada.
  • Despite its offensive power, Chien-Pao still struggles against bulky Pokemon like Volcanion and Corviknight and Pokemon that outspeed it, such as Speed Booster Iron Crown and Speed Booster Iron Valiant. Therefore, Pokemon like Raging Bolt, Landorus-T, and Volcarona make good teammates.

Glass Cannon.description:
Set Details

  • Chien-Pao uses its high Speed and Ice- and Dark-type STAB attacks to threaten foes like Miraidon and Calyrex-S. Sword of Ruin bolsters its already high Attack stat, elevating the damage it can deal. Sword of Ruin additionally increases the damage its partners can deal, notably allowing Zamazenta-C to achieve more KOs with Body Press.
  • Sucker Punch is used to threaten foes naturally faster than Chien-Pao such as Calyrex-S, while Crunch is used when Chien-Pao moves before its foe like when it is up against Lunala. Taunt is used to disrupt supportive foes such as Lunala and Amoonguss, preventing them from using Trick Room and Spore, respectively. Icicle Crash deals more damage and doesn't make contact, keeping Chien-Pao's Focus Sash intact against Rocky Helmet users like Amoonguss, with the downside of having the potential to miss. While Ice Spinner deals less damage, it won't miss and has the benefit of removing Terrain, weakening the damage dealt by Miraidon and its partners.
  • Focus Sash guarantees Chien-Pao can survive at least one hit so it can revenge kill faster foes and be positioned flexibly. Life Orb increases the damage Chien-Pao deals, guaranteeing it can OHKO bulky Miraidon variants with Ice Spinner.
  • The defensive investment allows Chien-Pao to survive Surging Strikes from Choice Scarf Urshifu-R. A Jolly nature allows Chien-Pao to outrun non-maximum Speed Miraidon, whereas an Adamant nature lets Chien-Pao OHKO Rillaboom with Icicle Crash.
  • Tera Stellar boosts Chien-Pao's damage to greater heights, allowing it to OHKO Ursaluna with Icicle Crash and Tera Grass Ho-Oh with Ice Spinner. Tera Ghost, meanwhile, prevents Fake Out disruption while keeping Focus Sash intact and provides Chien-Pao with an immunity to Close Combat from Koraidon and Body Press from Zamazenta-C.

Teambuilding

  • Bulky Restricted Pokemon like Zamazenta-C, Ho-Oh, and Kyogre are problematic for Chien-Pao. They threaten Chien-Pao, and it can't sufficiently damage them if they haven't Terastallized.
  • Chien-Pao struggles to damage Dark-types like Incineroar and Grimmsnarl. They can also reduce Chien-Pao's damage with Intimidate, Will-O-Wisp, and Parting Shot from Incineroar and Reflect from Grimmsnarl.
  • A partner Zamazenta-C synergizes well with Chien-Pao. Zamazenta-C threatens opposing Zamazenta-C, Incineroar, and Grimmsnarl, while Chien-Pao provides Sword of Ruin, letting Zamazenta-C OHKO Ogerpon-H with Body Press. Zamazenta-C also protects Chien-Pao from Kyogre's Water Spout and Origin Pulse with Wide Guard, forcing them to deal little damage with Ice Beam against Chien-Pao.
  • Miraidon works well with Chien-Pao, KOing Ho-Oh and Kyogre while Chien-Pao threatens Rillaboom, which Miraidon struggles to damage.
  • Urshifu-R appreciates Sword of Ruin letting it OHKO Ho-Oh with Surging Strikes; it also threatens Incineroar and Grimmsnarl while Chien-Pao removes Grass-types like Rillaboom and Amoonguss.

Chien-Pao is a fast physical attacker that uses its good Speed tier and strong STAB attacks to threaten popular Pokemon like Koraidon, Miraidon, and Calyrex-S. Ice Spinner is used as a consistent Ice-type STAB move that can remove Terrains that Pokemon like Indeedee-F, Miraidon, and Rillaboom set up. Removing Psychic Terrain can allow Chien-Pao to threaten Calyrex-S with a super effective Sucker Punch. Alternatively, Icicle Crash hits less consistently, but it avoids Rocky Helmet damage, can cause foes to flinch, and keeps up Terrains that would benefit Chien-Pao. Sucker Punch gives Chien-Pao a priority option that can KO faster Pokemon such as Speed Booster Energy Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle. Sacred Sword allows Chien-Pao to hit Pokemon that resist its STAB moves like Incineroar and Zamazenta-C. Chien-Pao can run Throat Chop as a consistent Dark-type STAB attack that can hit Lunala and Calyrex-S even if they didn't use an attacking move. Throat Chop also prevents Incineroar from using Parting Shot. Focus Sash allows Chien-Pao to survive at least one attack and to give it the opportunity to use another move due to its high Speed. Chien-Pao can use Tera Ghost to become immune to Fighting while also avoiding priority attacks like Fake Out and Extreme Speed that would otherwise break its Focus Sash. Tera Stellar is a more offensive option that allows Chien-Pao to pick up KOs that it would otherwise miss out on like bulky Flutter Mane.

The best check for Chien-Pao is Incineroar, as it resists both STAB types and packs Intimidate. Zacian-C also resists Chien-Pao's STAB moves and threatens it with all of its attacks. Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Flutter Mane can threaten to bring Chien-Pao down to Focus Sash or OHKO it, with the former resisting Chien-Pao's STAB combination and the latter also threatening to slow it down with Icy Wind. Chien-Pao pairs well with physical attackers like Zacian-C and Rillaboom, as Sword of Ruin makes them even more potent threats and they can handle Urshifu-R and Flutter Mane for Chien-Pao. However, they also struggle against Incineroar and opposing Zacian-C. This makes Urshifu-R and Zamazenta-C also good options for Chien-Pao, since they can threaten Incineroar and Zacian-C while taking advantage of Sword of Ruin. Chien-Pao can threaten Grass- and Dragon-types that resist Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes such as Rillaboom and Raging Bolt, as well as making quick work of Ghost-types that are immune to Body Press such as Calyrex-S.

Choice Band.description:
• Holding a nearly unresisted STAB combination, Chien-Pao is a potent wallbreaker and revenge killer that outspeeds most of the metagame, notably including Ultra Necrozma, Eternatus, and Marshadow; however, its minimal defensive utility, weakness to Stealth Rock, and vulnerability to Zacian-C limit its viability to dedicated balance teams.
  • Ice Spinner is a reliable STAB option that can remove Tapu Lele's Psychic Terrain, hindering the momentum of teams reliant on the field effect. While Icicle Crash is less accurate, it's an alternative that hits slightly harder, always OHKOes defensive Eternatus and 2HKOes defensive Ho-Oh, and avoids making contact with Ferrothorn.
  • Ice Shard and Sucker Punch can be run at the same time to minimize mind games when revenge killing setup sweepers, with the former OHKOing Mega Salamence and Rayquaza and the latter OHKOing Mewtwo and Ultra Necrozma. Sacred Sword ensures a 2HKO on Arceus-Dark and Zacian-C.
  • The given EV spread outspeeds Eternatus and avoids an OHKO from +1 Adamant Kyurem-B's Fusion Bolt, Jolly Zekrom's Outrage, Calyrex-I's Glacial Lance after a layer of Spikes, Life Orb Tera Normal Rayquaza's Extreme Speed, uninvested Primal Groudon's Precipide Blades, and Silk Scarf Tera Normal Arceus's Extreme Speed while also avoiding a 2HKO from Life Orb Tera Dark Yveltal's Sucker Punch, and Galarian Darmanitan's Icicle Crash, with the rest going to Attack to maximize damage output, notably ensuring an OHKO on Galarian Darmanitan with Sucker Punch.
  • Tera Dark removes Chien-Pao's weakness to Stealth Rock; prevents physical Ultra Necrozma at +1 from OHKOing with any attack but the uncommon Outrage; and lets Crunch OHKO wallbreaker Primal Kyogre, defensive Necrozma-DM after Stealth Rock, and Rayquaza, as well as letting Sucker Punch OHKO Marshadow and offensive Necrozma-DM after Stealth Rock. Tera Ice is an alternative to 2HKO defensive Arceus-Fairy and OHKO defensive Arceus-Ground with either Ice Spinner or Icicle Crash, as well as OHKO Ultra Necrozma with Ice Shard after a layer of Spikes.
  • It's not recommended to immediately try to OHKO Zygarde with an Ice-type STAB move, as it will often Terastallize and flip its matchup against Chien-Pao. Unless another Pokemon on the opposing team has already Terastallized, it's best to try to bait it into Terastallizing by positioning Chien-Pao as if it could just attack Zygarde, then hard switch to a more defensive check such as Arceus-Fairy or Alomomola.
  • Chien-Pao's typing has the minimal defensive utility of resisting Marshadow's Shadow Sneak and Yveltal's Sucker Punch; therefore, it's desirable to preserve its health so it can revenge kill them.
  • As Chien-Pao is setup fodder for Zacian-C, dedicated checks such as Primal Groudon, Ho-Oh, and Necrozma-DM are solid allies, with Chien-Pao in exchange acting as an offensive check to foes such as Arceus-Ground, Rayquaza, and Marshadow.
  • Chien-Pao struggles to come into the field, as it has minimal defensive utility, so defensive pivots such as Alomomola, Landorus-T, and Yveltal can provide the momentum that Chien-Pao requires to switch in safely and minimize the risk of being KOed on the switch.
  • Chien-Pao is weak to Stealth Rock and can have longevity issues because of this; therefore, Defoggers such as Yveltal, Ho-Oh, and Giratina-O are formidable partners that can remove entry hazards for it, with Yveltal in particular also compressing pivoting and solidifying the matchup against Ultra Necrozma.

Physical Attacker.description: • A Naive nature is used alongside Icy Wind in order to 2HKO Landorus

RUINOUS ATTACKER.description:
• With its high Attack and Speed, and incredible ability in Sword of Ruin, Chien-Pao is one of the strongest physical attackers in the game.

  • Icicle Crash: While Ice Spinner is perfectly accurate, Icicle Crash's higher power and flinch chance makes it the preferred attack. Additionally, not being a contact move allows Chien-Pao to avoid unnecessary chip damage from Rocky Helmet users.

  • Sucker Punch: Sucker Punch offers priority with a strong base power. While it comes with the cost of necessitating prediction, it is effectively mandatory for putting extreme pressure on Calyrex-S.

  • Sacred Sword: Sacred Sword provides coverage for Pokemon that resist one or both of Chien-Pao's STAB attacks, like Chi-Yu and other Chien-Pao. Additionally, ignoring defense boosts allows Chien-Pao to deal more consistent damage to foes who boost their Defense like Archaludon and Garganacl.

  • Tera Blast: With Chien-Pao's incredible power, Tera Blast can be used to surprise would-be checks with powerful super-effective attacks!

  • Crunch: Crunch is a more standard Dark-type attack that can pressure switch-ins as well as passive targets like Skeledirge.

  • Brick Break: While Brick Break isn't as powerful as Sacred Sword, it does break dual screens and still provides excellent damage against opposing Chien-Pao.

  • Swords Dance: Swords Dance boosts Chien-Pao's Attack to unwallable levels, making it an even more potent sweeper.

  • Sheer Cold: While an OHKO move may look out of place on Chien-Pao and ultimately rely on luck, it cannot be understated how powerful it is to flip a matchup like Dondozo or Ho-oh on its head.

  • Ice Shard: Ice Shard is a more consistent albeit weaker priority move compared to Sucker Punch that doesn't require attack prediction.

  • Adamant versus Jolly: Adamant gives Chien-Pao a significant power boost for sniping Pokemon with Sucker Punch, but Jolly is important for Speed tying with Flutter Mane and opposing Chien-Pao.

  • 0-1 SpA IV: If using Tera Blast on Jolly Chien-Pao, make sure to use a SpA IV that's 0-1. This is because if Flutter Mane uses Charm, any SpA IV that's higher will result in Tera Blast becoming a Special Attack.

Other Options

  • Psychic Fangs: Psychic Fangs is an alternative to Brick Break for dealing with dual screens while also dealing good damage to Urshifu-R.

  • Lash Out: Lash Out is a situational but powerful response to Charm Flutter Mane thanks to the doubled BP on the turn Chien-Pao's Attack is lowered.

Items

  • Focus Sash: This is the most reliable item for Chien-Pao, almost always guaranteeing Chien-Pao at least one attack and flipping many potential match-ups such as offensive Flutter Mane.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb makes Chien-Pao a terrifying sweeper and wall-breaker in one!

  • Sitrus Berry: While Sitrus Berry may seem strange on such an offensive Pokemon, it can save Tera Electric Chien-Pao from being OHKOed by Adamant Choice Scarf Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes. 36 HP and 36 Defense EVs can be used to guarantee this, but even without investment, Chien-Pao has around a 93% chance of surviving.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low / Medium: Chien-Pao offers power in spades without needing to Terastallize, but it ultimately comes down to how much Chien-Pao relies on Tera Blast for coverage.

  • Electric: Tera Electric can be used in tandem with Tera Blast to improve Chien-Pao's matchup against key threats such as Urshifu-R, Kyogre, and Primarina, while also making it immune to paralysis.

  • Stellar: Stellar's one-time boost per attacking type can open up new sweeping opportunities for Chien-Pao. Maintaining its Dark typing is also strong in consideration of the Calyrex-S matchup.

  • Dark: Tera Dark boosts Sucker Punch to extreme power levels while making Crunch difficult to switch into without a resistance.

  • Fire: Tera Fire provides Chien-Pao with a host of new resistances against Flutter Mane's Moonblast, Ogerpon-H's Ivy Cudgel, and Scizor's Bullet Punch. These surprise resistances work particularly well with finding a turn to use Swords Dance.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost doesn't offer much offensive benefit, but it allows Chien-Pao to dodge Normal-type priority from Dragonite and the Ogerpon formes, which can be particularly useful if using Swords Dance.

  • Ice: Tera Ice can allow Chien-Pao to finish foes off with Ice Shard from higher ranges and makes Icicle Crash an even more formidable tool. If combined with Life Orb, even offensive Urshifu-R can be 2HKOed!

Choice Band Breaker.description:
• Choice Band transforms Chien-Pao into one of the most bloodthirsty wall-breakers in the metagame!

  • Ice Shard versus Sucker Punch: Ice Shard is the weaker but more reliable priority move for cleaning late-game. Sucker Punch is one of the most powerful priority moves in the metagame, but falters against support moves like Substitute and Thunder Wave. Thanks to Choice Band Chien-Pao's insane power, it is entirely possible to sacrifice coverage and run both if desired.

  • Sacred Sword versus Brick Break: Sacred Sword gives Chien-Pao useful coverage against bulky foes like Archaludon, as well as opposing Chien-Pao. Brick Break is less powerful but the utility of breaking dual screens can be worth it for some teams.

Other Options

  • Tera Blast: Chien-Pao can still opt for extra coverage to pressure would-be checks. However, this can require prediction because of the move lock, and often Chien-Pao will do more than enough damage hammering targets with Tera-boosted STAB attacks.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Chien-Pao is already plenty powerful, Choice Band combined with Tera can make some of the strongest walls in the game fold before Chien-Pao.

  • Dark: Tera Dark turns Choice Band Crunch into a devastating wallbreaker move that few can withstand, OHKOing checks like Scizor if using an Adamant nature. Neutralizing Chien-Pao's Steel-type weakness also makes it less vulnerable to Scizor's Bullet Punch.

  • Ice: Tera Ice gives Choice Band Icicle Crash enough power to challenge even physically defensive Ting-Lu, having approximately a 69% chance to OHKO if using an Adamant nature; be warned, however, that Ting-Lu often Terastallizes in front of Chien-Pao, making this inconsistent. The extra power behind Ice Shard is also a welcome boost.

Offensive.description:
Chien-Pao is undoubtedly the best naturally offensive Pokemon in Partners in Crime thanks to its amazing Speed, good Attack, and Sword of Ruin. The last of these is appreciated by every Pokemon in the metagame due to Pokemon with Sword of Ruin not being affected by the ability. In particular, physical attackers take the best advantage of the ability, as their own damage output is boosted. Ice Spinner is Chien-Pao's preferred Ice-type STAB move thanks to its consistency over Icicle Crash and the ability to disrupt Indeedee-F's Psychic Terrain. Icicle Crash is a marginally stronger option that can be used if the team features a Terrain it wishes to preserve, which also comes with a flinch chance that is often felt due to Chien-Pao's high Speed. Sucker Punch is a must-have on Chien-Pao, as it allows it a form of damage even when playing against opposing Tailwind or Trick Room teams, notably pressuring the likes of Gholdengo effectively. Sacred Sword is generally preferred as a means to hit Pokemon that resist its STAB moves such as Incineroar and Heatran while also ignoring defensive boosts from the likes of IronPress Kommo-o. Haze is a great alternative to shut down opposing setup such as Gholdengo's Nasty Plot and Rillaboom's Swords Dance. Throat Chop is a stronger Dark-type option that also shuts down moves such as Incineroar's Parting Shot. Focus Sash is Chien-Pao's best item, as it helps patch up its otherwise mediocre bulk; meanwhile, Clear Amulet helps to staveoff Intimidate from Incineroar and Landorus-T. Tera Ghost is Chien-Pao's preferred Tera type, turning its Fighting weakness into an immunity while granting it a Fake Out immunity to help preserve its Focus Sash. Tera Stellar is a more offensive option that takes advantage of the plethora of uniquely typed moves that can be shared with Chien-Pao.

Notable Partners

================

Strong Priority Users: Extreme Speed users such as Dragonite and Entei make for great partners with Chien-Pao thanks to Sword of Ruin raising their Extreme Speeds' damage to exorbitant heights. Other priority moves such as Rillaboom's Grassy Glide are also good, while all of the aforementioned Pokemon appreciate Ice Spinner from Chien-Pao to clear Psychic Terrain.

Bulky Setup Pokemon: As Sword of Ruin grants the user immunity to the ability, bulky setup Pokemon such as Nasty Plot Gholdengo and Dragon Dance Dragonite appreciate the presence of Chien-Pao.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Adaptability can be used on non-Sacred Sword sets, obtaining a similar power boost while allowing Chien-Pao's teammates like Roaring Moon and Ceruledge to run the ability instead; it has the notable benefit of hiding Chien-Pao's ability from the opponent. Lash Out is an option on the Choice Band set to immediately dent Intimidate users like Corviknight and Skarmory on the switch but lacks power otherwise while missing out on valuable Defense drops. Psychic Fangs is another option for Choice Band variants to punish Zamazenta and Iron Hands on the switch, potentially 2HKO a would-be check in physically defensive Primarina after Stealth Rock, and remove dual screens set by foes like Regieleki and Corviknight, letting its team match up better against dual screens hyper offense teams. Ice Spinner may seem like an appealing option on Swords Dance sets for a little extra consistency, but the additional power, contact avoidance, and flinch chance of Icicle Crash makes it entirely preferable, leaving Ice Spinner unviable. Serene Grace sets are an option to fish for Icicle Crash flinches or Crunch Defense drops, but this set lacks power and is generally inferior to damage amplification abilities.

Checks and Counters

Faster Threats: Foes like Zamazenta and Psychic Surge Deoxys-S can outspeed and OHKO Chien-Pao while not being particularly afraid of its priority moves.

Bulky Fighting-types: Bulky foes like Iron Hands, Cobalion, and Zamazenta can often easily switch in on Chien-Pao's Dark-type moves and use it to either pivot with Volt Switch or as setup fodder.

Primarina: Bulkier Primarina sets can switch in easily against Chien-Pao's STAB moves and either force it out with Moonblast or use it as Calm Mind fodder.

Entry Hazards: Entry hazard setters like Skarmory, Great Tusk, and Heatran can cause immense problems for non-Magic Guard sets due to their frailty being compounded by their hazard vulnerability.

Swords Dance.description:
Chien-Pao's incredible Speed and excellent offensive STAB combination let it function as threatening setup sweeper and late-game cleaner. Magic Guard protects Chien-Pao from Life Orb recoil and nullifies passive damage from Stealth Rock, Rocky Helmet, and poison from Pecharunt. Heavy-Duty Boots is another option to circumvent Chien-Pao's Stealth Rock weakness, along with making it immune to Sticky Web and letting it run Sword of Ruin for a similar power boost to Life Orb. Throat Chop shuts down Boomburst Scream Tail and denies Parting Shot from Pecharunt. Sucker Punch threatens Deoxys-S, Choice Scarf Gholdengo, and Surge Surfer Manaphy, although Ice Shard is usually the preferred option to hit Zamazenta as well as Choice Scarf Roaring Moon and Meowscarada.

Chien-Pao fits well on offense and hyper offense teams, where its checks can be worn down with the help of other offensive teammates, letting Chien-Pao sweep or clean up. Partners such as Kingambit, Roaring Moon, and the Ogerpon formes can help weaken physically defensive walls such as Corviknight, Iron Hands, and Primarina, as well as putting Zamazenta in KO range of a Swords Dance-boosted Ice Shard. Chien-Pao is threatened by Kingambit and the aforementioned Zamazenta and Iron Hands, so it needs physically defensive walls such as Great Tusk and Pecharunt. Faster Psychic Surge users like Deoxys-S and Choice Scarf Azelf can threaten Chien-Pao without fear of its priority moves; therefore, specially defensive walls such as Manaphy, Swampert, and Iron Treads are appreciated.

Choice Band.description:
Thanks to its high Attack boosted further by Sword of Ruin, strong STAB combination, and access to priority moves, Choice Band Chien-Pao is one of the metagame's deadliest wallbreakers and revenge killers. On top of a valuable Speed tier to threaten and chase out common tier staples like Roaring Moon, Cinderace, and Iron Boulder, it has the immediate power to 2HKO walls like physically defensive Manaphy as well as Fluffy Corviknight and Skarmory after Stealth Rock. Sacred Sword immediately threatens Steel-type foes such as Kingambit, Cobalion, Heatran, and Iron Treads. Either priority move allows Chien-Pao to revenge kill faster threats like Hisuian Electrode and Choice Scarf Latios; Sucker Punch is more punishable but targets non-Psychic Surge Deoxys-S, Choice Scarf Gholdengo, and Agility Iron Crown hard, while Ice Shard handles foes like Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, Meowscarada, and weakened Zamazenta.

Though it can function on a wide range of team styles, Chien-Pao fits best on fast-paced offensive teams that can best take advantage of its wallbreaking prowess while mitigating its lack of defensive utility. Powerful special wallbreakers like Deoxys-S, Gholdengo, and Primarine stand out as star teammates for their ability to immediately threaten physical walls like physically defensive Manaphy, Skarmory, and Iron Hands that can give Chien-Pao trouble. Also notable are Latios, Iron Moth, and Iron Crown, which are powerful special pivots able to bring Chien-Pao in to threaten their switch-ins like Swampert, Ting-Lu, and Roaring Moon. Chien-Pao also works well in tandem with other powerful wallbreakers like Roaring Moon, Zamazenta, and Iron Boulder, with Chien-Pao wearing down their checks like non-Intimidate Corviknight, Landorus, and Pecharunt, while its teammates pressure Manaphy, Iron Hands, and defensive Primarina. Bulky pivots like Pecharunt, Swampert, and Corviknight can also make good teammates, tanking hits and allowing the frail Chien-Pao to more easily get on the field against foes like Roaring Moon, Zapdos, and Scream Tail; Pecharunt is especially notable for its ability to wall Zamazenta, which is otherwise a great check to Chien-Pao, while Corviknight alongside Great Tusk and Iron Treads are noteworthy for their entry hazard removing capabilities, making it far easier for Chien-Pao to repeatedly hit the field.

ubers.overview: Chien-Pao possesses the coveted-yet-crowded base 135 Speed tier and can even get the jump on its peers with Ice Shard and Sucker Punch, making it a nice revenge killer and late-game cleaner; Ice Shard in particular stands out in a metagame with numerous fast Dragon-types. Its Dark / Ice STAB combination matches up well into defensive staples like Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Ground, and Ting-Lu, and Icicle Crash can also potentially flinch through otherwise solid counterplay like Ho-Oh. However, Chien-Pao is exceedingly frail and entry hazard-weak, making getting it onto the field safely, let alone multiple times, quite difficult. This also means it offers exactly no defensive utility to its team. Due to the low Base Power of its moves, it is also relatively weak by Ubers standards without finding a turn to use Swords Dance, which is hard to find due to its frailty. Chien-Pao is also scared to death of Zacian-C, which outspeeds it and resists both STAB types. Kingambit also provides heavy competition, as it has substantially better bulk, resists Stealth Rock, and boasts an even stronger Sucker Punch late-game, at the cost of much worse Speed. Ultimately, Chien-Pao's Speed, priority, and STAB combination make it a noteworthy cleaner, but it still finds itself more limited compared to metagame staples like Koraidon and Zacian-C.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

An all-out attacker set with Heavy-Duty Boots can be used for the maximum amount of coverage and priority while still changing moves in the early- and mid-game, but it generally lacks power compared to the above sets and struggles to even 2HKO defensive staples like Arceus. Sacred Sword provides coverage for Arceus and Kingambit and does non-pitiful damage to Zacian-C, but Chien-Pao struggles to justify it over its primary STAB moves and priority options. Tera Ghost can catch out Extreme Speed Arceus but otherwise is far worse than damage-amplifying Tera types. Focus Sash can be run on hyper offense structures to take a hit but requires significant entry hazard counterplay.

Checks and Counters

Zacian-C: Zacian-C outspeeds Chien-Pao and resists its STAB combination.

Defensive Arceus: Arceus-Water and -Fairy avoid the 2HKO from almost any of Chien-Pao's attacks and can retaliate with Will-O-Wisp or Judgement. Arceus-Fairy has a low chance to be 2HKOed by Life Orb Tera Ice Icicle Crash, however.

Extreme Killer Arceus: Extreme Killer Arceus completely nullifies Chien-Pao's Speed and priority advantages while not being OHKOed by any common move.

Choice Scarf users: Choice Scarf users like Koraidon can revenge kill Chien-Pao, especially with a well-timed Tera.

Iron Bundle: Iron Bundle outspeeds Chien-Pao, can force 50/50s with Encore, and KOes it after some chip.

Zamazenta: Zamazenta’s bulk lets it take any attack and OHKO with Body Press.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Chien-Pao is a threatening late-game cleaner once Arceus formes that are not weak to Chien-Pao's STAB moves have been chipped sufficiently. Icicle Crash is Chien-Pao's strongest STAB move, provides key coverage against the plethora of Ground-types, and can provide a flinch in a pinch all while dodging Rocky Helmet. Crunch is Chien-Pao's most reliable secondary STAB move, hitting Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Water, and Kyogre, while Sucker Punch is its strongest priority move by far against neutral targets. Ice Shard is notable to revenge kill Koraidon and Miraidon while also not failing against setup moves and can be run over either Dark STAB move. Life Orb is the preferred item to secure the OHKO against defensive Necrozma-DM and 2HKO against Arceus-Water after Swords Dance, and given Chien-Pao’s frailty, the recoil is often insignificant. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Chien-Pao to be played aggressively in the early-to-mid-game to help break down the opposing core itself and pick off weakened targets, while Black Glasses still secures key KOs like Necrozma-DM without recoil. Jolly is the preferred nature to Speed tie Koraidon, Miraidon, and opposing Chien-Pao while outspeeding Arceus, Mewtwo, and +1 Necrozma-DM and Iron Treads, but Adamant is an option, especially on double priority sets that care less about the Speed tier.

Chien-Pao thrives best when it is tasked with cleaning up a weakened team. As such, powerful physical wallbreakers like Koraidon and Arceus-Ground that can lure in and weaken their shared checks like Arceus-Fairy are excellent teammates. Chien-Pao also loves entry hazards being up on the opposing side, making teammates like Gliscor and Ting-Lu wonderful partners. Chien-Pao is helpless against Zacian-C, making a strong answer to it like Ho-Oh a great teammate. Additionally, strong opposing priority users like Arceus offset Chien-Pao's biggest advantage, so a reliable answer to it like defensive Arceus-Ground is recommended. Especially if running Life Orb, Chien-Pao struggles to get onto the field without taking tremendous chip damage, making pivoting teammates like Gliscor, Koraidon, and Miraidon valuable partners; Miraidon especially draws in the Ground-types like Ting-Lu and Gliscor that Chien-Pao feasts on. Extreme Killer Arceus is an excellent teammate, as they form a strong priority core together; Arceus also often forces Tera Ghost on opposing setup sweepers, making them weaker to Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch. Glimmora is a useful partner especially on hyper offense teams to provide entry hazard support and clear Stealth Rock with Mortal Spin.

Choice Band.description:
Choice Band gives Chien-Pao the best chance to 2HKO walls like Necrozma-DM and revenge kill Miraidon and Koraidon after moderate chip. Icicle Crash is the main STAB option thanks to its flinch chance and better Base Power while also avoiding Rocky Helmet, while Ice Spinner doesn't miss and can reset Miraidon's Electric Terrain. Crunch is its most reliable Dark-type STAB move, hitting Arceus-Water, Kyogre, and Necrozma-DM. Double priority in Sucker Punch and Ice Shard lets it pack both power and coverage, nailing anything that might be faster including Iron Bundle, Miraidon, and even Calyrex-I in Trick Room. Tera Dark and Ice can both be used to power up Chien-Pao's STAB attacks; Tera Ice has a chance to OHKO both Miraidon and Koraidon with Ice Shard, while Tera Dark secures the 2HKO against Ho-Oh and has a high chance to 2HKO Arceus-Water.

Choice Band Chien-Pao is a useful revenge killer and wallbreaker for offensive teams. Since it forgoes Heavy-Duty Boots and would love to switch in multiple times to mitigate the effect of Choice-lock, it pairs well with Iron Treads, which can clear entry hazards and even pivot Chien-Pao in. Zacian-C can easily revenge kill Chien-Pao and even grab a Swords Dance if locked into Sucker Punch or Ice Shard, making strong counterplay like Landorus-T and defensive Arceus-Ground or revenge killers like Choice Scarf Koraidon mandatory teammates. Physically offensive teammates like Koraidon and Necrozma-DM appreciate being able to clean teams Chien-Pao has weakened; alternatively, they can punch holes for Chien-Pao to clean up. Extreme Killer Arceus is an excellent teammate, as it forms a powerful priority core with Chien-Pao and can draw out Tera Ghost for it.

Focus Sash Attacker.description:
• Ice Spinner can threaten to OHKO Tornadus and Landorus while also removing Rillaboom's Grassy Terrain and Indeedee-F's Psychic Terrain, allowing Chien-Pao to use Sucker Punch, while Icicle Crash has a decent chance to make foes flinch and avoids contact damage from Spiky Shield and Rocky Helmet, keeping Focus Sash intact against Ogerpon and Rocky Helmet Amoonguss.

  • Sucker Punch can pick off targets that are on low HP and faster threats such as opposing Chien-Pao and Pokemon benefitting from Trick Room or Tailwind. Throat Chop can be used over Sucker Punch for a reliable Dark-type STAB move, since it is not negated by Follow Me from Ogerpon-W and Indeedee-F and can hit Pokemon setting up like Gholdengo while also preventing Ursaluna-B from using Hyper Voice and Incineroar from using Parting Shot.

  • Sacred Sword is great coverage against Pokemon that resist or tank Chien-Pao's STAB combination such as Incineroar, Kyurem under snow, and opposing Chien-Pao. Throat Chop can be used over Sacred Sword for a better matchup against Nasty Plot Gholdengo and redirection users in exchange for a worse matchup against Kingambit, Incineroar, and opposing Chien-Pao.

  • Tera Ghost makes Chien-Pao immune to Fake Out, dodging the flinch effect and preventing Fake Out from breaking the Focus Sash, while also becoming immune to Fighting-type attacks from Iron Hands and opposing Chien-Pao. Tera Stellar provides a helpful power boost and can let it generally OHKO Amoonguss, Ursaluna-B, and most Raging Bolt with Ice Spinner or Icicle Crash.

  • Teams that have Chien-Pao have a lot of offensive pieces that benefit from Sword of Ruin lowering the Defense of opposing Pokemon, increasing the chances of OHKOs from offensive threats such as Ogerpon-W, Ogerpon-H, Iron Hands, and priority users such as Choice Band Dragonite packing Extreme Speed.

  • Chien-Pao appreciates Pokemon like Landorus, Landorus-T, and Ogerpon-W that offensively threaten Fire-types like Gouging Fire and Incineroar, among other key problems for Chien-Pao such as Diancie and Iron Hands.

  • Gouging Fire can be a good partner, supporting Chien-Pao with Howl to negate Intimidate while accentuating the physically focused offense already passively bolstered by Sword of Ruin.

Offensive Icy Wind.description:
• Icy Wind Chien-Pao is able to provide excellent speed control for its teammates such as Landorus, Ogerpon-H, and Ogerpon-W, allowing them to outspeed and OHKO threats like opposing Chien-Pao, Tornadus, and opposing Ogerpon formes.

  • Chien-Pao's primary Ice-type STAB move is largely determined by its partners; Ice Spinner for its ability to clear Grassy and Psychic Terrain, while Icicle Crash is chosen for its increased power, ability to avoid Rocky Helmet chip damage that would break its Focus Sash, and inability to clear your own Terrain when run with Indeedee-F or Rillaboom.

  • Sucker Punch is chosen to give Chien-Pao a priority option, allowing it to pick off weakened threats or squeeze off an extra hit after being brought down to its Focus Sash.

  • Throat Chop gives Chien-Pao a way of hitting Pokemon like Farigiraf and Indeedee-F super effectively while also allowing it to attack Gholdengo and Terastallized Ogerpon-H without having to risk Sucker Punch failing.

  • Icy Wind Chien-Pao is notable for its ability to function as the primary mode of speed control for priority-spam teams while also being able to excel in conjunction with Tailwind-setting teammates like Roaring Moon and Tornadus.

  • Icy Wind allows Chien-Pao to aid its partners in preventing Toxic Debris or Aurora Veil from Glimmora and Alolan Ninetales, respectively. Icy Wind can break a possible Focus Sash on either Pokemon and enables Chien-Pao's slower partners like Gholdengo, Landorus, and Glimmora to outspeed and OHKO either Pokemon after Icy Wind chip damage.

  • The Naive nature is chosen to allow Chien-Pao to guarantee the 2HKO against bulky Landorus with Icy Wind.

  • Tera Ghost grants a crucial immunity to Fake Out, opposing Chien-Pao's Sacred Sword, Dragonite's Extreme Speed, and Iron Hands's Fighting-type attacks.

  • Dragonite is one of Chien-Pao's premier partners, with Icy Wind support allowing Dragonite to more effectively use its non-priority options, allowing for more versatile Dragonite sets like Loaded Dice.

  • The Ogerpon formes are another of Chien-Pao's preferred partners, with Icy Wind and Sword of Ruin support allowing the Ogerpon formes to eliminate key threats to themselves like Focus Sash Tornadus and opposing Ogerpon formes before they're able to retaliate.

  • Chien-Pao also works extremely well alongside Landorus because Landorus pressures Chien-Pao's common checks like Incineroar and Iron Hands, and additionally, Chien-Pao is able to slow down Landorus's most common check, Ogerpon-W.

Bulky Support.description:
Set Details

  • Ting-Lu serves as a support member to its team, able to mitigate incoming special damage with Snarl and Vessel of Ruin while chipping foes with Ruination and Sand Tomb. Its high bulk allows it to stay on the field for a long time, letting it spread more damage and protect its teammates with Vessel of Ruin longer. It has good matchups into several key threats, such as Terapagos, Miraidon, and Raging Bolt.
  • Snarl is used to further help its team members take special attacks, while Ruination and Sand Tomb can chip down foes to let its teammates pick up easier KOs. Ting-Lu can use either Throat Chop or Stone Edge to improve matchups into several Restricted Pokemon, including Calyrex-S, Ho-Oh, and Calyrex-I. Sand Tomb can also be used to trap foes on the field so a teammate with a good matchup or a move such as Yawn to take advantage.
  • Ting-Lu uses Assault Vest to bolster its lower Special Defense. Stacking this Special Defense multiplier with Vessel of Ruin and Snarl lets it take a lot of special attacks such as Dazzling Gleam from Choice Specs Miraidon, Moonblast from foes such as Flutter Mane and Tera Fairy Lunala, and Tera Starstorm from a Calm Mind-boosted Terapagos, allowing Ting-Lu to be 3HKOed, instead of 2HKOed, by most of these.
  • Ting-Lu's Attack investment allows it to 2HKO Electric Seed Lunala most of the time with Throat Chop. Its Special Defense investment allows it to survive two Modest Choice Specs Tera Fairy Miraidon Dazzling Gleams inside of Electric Terrain most of the time, as well as Mystic Water Kyogre's Water Spout in the rain. Its Defense investment allows it to live Rillaboom's Wood Hammer in Grassy Terrain, Zamazenta-C's Body Press, and Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash, as well as Urshifu-R's Tera Water Surging Strikes most of the time.
  • Ting-Lu uses Tera Fairy to drop its weaknesses to Fighting-type attacks such as Body Press from Zamazenta-C and Close Combat from the Urshifu formes, as well dropping Ting-Lu's weakness to Grass-, Water-, Fairy-, and Ice-type attacks. Additionally, it gives Ting-Lu an immunity to Miraidon's Draco Meteor.

Teambuilding

  • Ting-Lu may struggle against strong physical attackers such as Urshifu-R, Rillaboom, and Chien-Pao, which force it to Terastallize and are unhindered by Vessel of Ruin. It is also vulnerable to Amoonguss, due to Ting-Lu often having no protection against Spore and not threatening a KO by itself.
  • If Terastallization is not available, Ting-Lu can also struggle heavily against Restricted Pokemon such as Zamazenta-C and Koraidon, which threaten a 2HKO and OHKO with Body Press and Close Combat or Collision Course, respectively. Calyrex-I is also able to 2HKO it with Glacial Lance.
  • Ting-Lu is often run with Zamazenta-C, as it allows Zamazenta-C to survive special attacks such as Electro Drift from Miraidon and Earth Power from Landorus. It is also able to chip down Pokemon Zamazenta-C may struggle to OHKO, such as Miraidon and Calyrex-S.
  • Ting-Lu thrives on bulky teams, where it is able to both protect its partners and chip foes down for them to take KOs, mainly seeing usage on teams with Calyrex-S and Zamazenta-C. Calyrex-S and Chien-Pao can threaten Amoonguss with Psychic- and Ice-type attacks to stop it from threatening Ting-Lu, and Zamazenta-C has a great matchup into the aforementioned Chien-Pao and Rillaboom, which would otherwise threaten a 2HKO. In return, Ting-Lu can chip down foes to help Calyrex-S take KOs, allowing it to gain Grim Neigh boosts. It also helps other partners take special attacks, such as Raging Bolt and Amoonguss, further bolstering their bulk. This allows Amoonguss to help Ting-Lu chip down foes with the combination of Amoonguss's Spore and Ting-Lu's Sand Tomb, while Raging Bolt threatens both Kyogre and Urshifu-R.
  • Ting-Lu can also be run with Calyrex-I, helping it take special attacks such as Electro Drift and Astral Barrage, which would otherwise threaten it heavily. It also helps Calyrex-I take KOs by dealing chip damage, allowing Calyrex-I to get Chilling Neigh boosts quickly and start to snowball out of control. Sand Tomb also stops foes from switching and removing Calyrex-I's Leech Seed.

vgc2024.overview:
• Thanks to its naturally high base stats and Vessel of Ruin, Ting-Lu is a powerful wall, able to tank most attacks in the format and retaliate with solid damage. Additionally, thanks to its deep supportive movepool with options like Sand Tomb and more niche moves like Taunt, Ting-Lu works as a great bulky supportive option.

  • Ting-Lu's main role is to abuse its bulk to stop common threats such as Gholdengo, Raging Bolt, and Iron Crown. Allies such as Dondozo and Gouging Fire heavily appreciate Ting-Lu's ability to suppress opposing special attackers, covering for their lower Special Defense. Dondozo in particular is able to use Yawn in combination with Ting-Lu's Sand Tomb to force sleep onto foes.

  • Ting-Lu's typing does, however, leave it vulnerable to some of the most popular physical attackers in the format, such as the Urshifu formes, the Ogerpon formes, Chien-Pao, and Rillaboom. Allies such as Sinistcha can switch into their attacks and redirect them away from Ting-Lu, while Gouging Fire can use Breaking Swipe to lower these foes' offensive prowess. Dondozo also helps here, soaking up physical attacks easily and punishing most of them with Rocky Helmet.

  • Ting-Lu can struggle with its field presence, being easily ignorable by many foes when using more supportive sets. It struggles to hit common Pokemon like Landorus and Rillaboom hard, making it easy for them to switch into Ting-Lu's attacks or ignore it entirely. Allies with Coaching and Howl, namely Galarian Zapdos and Gouging Fire, can help boost Ting-Lu's attack, making it harder to ignore. Options like Ruination and Body Press make it so Ting-Lu isn't entirely passive, dealing large chunks of damage and using Ting-Lu's high Defense stat, respectively.

Sand Tomb Support.description:
• Sand Tomb is able to trap in opponents so they can't escape disruption like Yawn. Ruination and Rocky Helmet act as the main damage dealing methods, with Stomping Tantrum used as its STAB move and Body Press as a consistent source of damage when Intimidated. Taunt can be used to shut down Amoonguss and other status moves.

  • The Special Defense investment allows Ting-Lu to live Moonblast from Choice Specs Tera Fairy Flutter Mane. The Defense investment allows Ting-Lu to survive Wood Hammer from Rillaboom and Ivy Cudgel from a Terastallized Ogerpon-W.

  • Tera Poison is the most consistent Tera type for Ting-Lu, as it provides a resistance to Flutter Mane's Moonblast, the STAB moves of Rillaboom, and Close Combat from the Urshifu formes.

Assault Vest.description:
• Heavy Slam allows Ting-Lu to OHKO Flutter Mane, while Ruination and Body Press provide consistent damage. Alternatively, Throat Chop can be used as a reliable Dark-Type STAB move that can also prevent Parting Shot from Incineroar and Hyper Voice from Ursaluna-B.

  • Ting-Lu uses Assault Vest to bolster its special bulk. The EV spread allows Ting-Lu to survive 3 Moonblasts from Flutter Mane, and it also almost always lives Surging Strikes from Tera Water Urshifu-R. The Attack investment ensures an OHKO on Flutter Mane with Heavy Slam.

  • Tera Poison is the most consistent Tera type for Ting-Lu, as it provides a resistance to Flutter Mane's Moonblast, the STAB moves of Rillaboom, and Close Combat from the Urshifu formes.

Bulky Attacker.description:
• Clear Amulet Ting-Lu aims to be a tank, sitting in front of many Pokemon such as Landorus and Raging Bolt while firing back with strong attacks, trading damage well with them while racking up damage throughout the course of a battle.

  • Earthquake is used for strong spread damage, synergizing well with Clear Amulet Ting-Lu's common partners, such as Galarian Zapdos, Thundurus, Orthworm, and Dragonite. Throat Chop is a good STAB option that threatens foes such as Indeedee-F and common Tera Ghost Pokemon, including Incineroar and Ursaluna. Tera Blast with Tera Poison hits the common Grass-types in this format, namely Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Ogerpon-H. Tera Poison Tera Blast and Earthquake also pin most Raging Bolt sets, as if they don't Tera, they get hit by Earthquake, and if they do, they get hit by Tera Poison Tera Blast.

  • Clear Amulet prevents Intimidate from Incineroar as well as Breaking Swipe Attack drops from Gouging Fire and Roaring Moon, ensuring that Ting-Lu remains powerful throughout the duration of the game. While more niche, ally Sinistcha running Strength Sap can use it on Ting-Lu and heal up for free, since Clear Amulet will prevent the Attack drop.

  • With the given EVs, Ting-Lu survives a Tera Stellar Icicle Crash from Adamant Chien-Pao, Tera Water Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-W, Wood Hammer from Rillaboom, and Tera Fairy Moonblast from Special Attack Booster Energy Flutter Mane. The Speed investment allows Ting-Lu to outspeed Kingambit, and the rest of the EVs are dumped into Attack to ensure Ting-Lu is hitting as hard as possible.

  • Tera Poison not only grants Ting-Lu a way to threaten Grass-type Pokemon with Tera Blast but also gives it resistances to common attacks like Wood Hammer, Horn Leech, Close Combat, and Moonblast from Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, the Urshifu formes, and Flutter Mane, respectively. Tera Poison does, however, make Ting-Lu weak to Landorus's Earth Power and Iron Crown's Expanding Force, so it is best to remove these threats before Terastallizing.

Support.description:
Ting-Lu finds its niche as a bulky support Pokemon due to Vessel of Ruin, impressive defenses, and great natural typing. It is able to slow down powerful special attackers like Terapagos with Snarl and use its typing to have a positive matchup against Calyrex-S, Miraidon, and Raging Bolt. Ruination provides constant damage, while Throat Chop can threaten to OHKO Calyrex-S and prevent Parting Shot from Incineroar. Stomping Tantrum allows it to threaten Incineroar, Miraidon, and Raging Bolt. Heavy Slam is used on Assault Vest sets to threaten Fairy-type Pokemon like Flutter Mane and Tera Fairy Calyrex-S, whereas Protect sees play on Rocky Helmet sets. Assault Vest allows Ting-Lu to bolster its special bulk even more, making special attacks like Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Calyrex-S's Draining Kiss a 4HKO. Rocky Helmet threatens constant chip damage on Pokemon like Urshifu-R. The EV investment allows Ting-Lu to survive a Wood Hammer from Assault Vest Rillaboom and take two Moonblast from Speed Booster Energy Flutter Mane for the Rocky Helmet set. The Attack investment allows Ting-Lu to OHKO Flutter Mane with Heavy Slam and to 2HKO Raging Bolt and bulky Farigiraf with Stomping Tantrum and Throat Chop, respectively. Tera Poison is utilized to resist the Urshifu formes's Close Combat, Rillaboom's STAB moves, and Flutter Mane's Moonblast. Tera Fairy sees usage thanks to its defensive nature, allowing Ting-Lu to have great matchup into the Urshifu formes while also becoming immune to Draco Meteor from Raging Bolt and Miraidon.

Ting-Lu sees usage with Restricted Pokemon like Calyrex-I and Zamazenta-C, allowing both to benefit from Ting-Lu's special damage reduction capabilities. Calyrex-I appreciates Ruination chip and Ting-Lu benefits from Trick Room set by Calyrex-I, while Zamazenta-C provides Wide Guard support, improving the matchup against opposing Calyrex-I. Ting-Lu can be slowed down by Pokemon like Incineroar, which makes Ting-Lu passive by reducing its damage output significantly thanks to Intimidate. Zamazenta-C helps in this regard because it can OHKO Incineroar with Body Press. Koraidon, Zamazenta-C, and Calyrex-I have a great matchup into Ting-Lu and are able to remove it from the field without taking much damage from its STAB moves. Therefore, Pelipper proves to be a great partner for Ting-Lu, providing rain support and Wide Guard, which slow down Pokemon like Koraidon and Calyrex-I, and threatening great damage on Incineroar with Weather Ball. Ting-Lu struggles against strong super effective attacks from Pokemon like Rillaboom, Kyogre, and the Urshifu formes. Raging Bolt is a great partner to Ting-Lu, as it can threaten Urshifu-R and Kyogre for super effective damage and resist Grass-type STAB moves from Rillaboom. Incineroar and Amoonguss are a great duo that support Ting-Lu well. Incineroar slows down Rillaboom thanks to Intimidate and threatens super effective damage with Flare Blitz. Amoonguss can redirect super effective moves like Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and provide Pollen Puff healing. Ting-Lu, in return, checks Pokemon like Chi-Yu and Flutter Mane, which can be troublesome for Amoonguss.

ubers.overview: Ting-Lu's titanic bulk makes it the premier special wall and check to Miraidon in Ubers. Unlike Arceus-Ground and Clodsire, Ting-Lu is able to take on Miraidon and generate momentum in the process thanks to Vessel of Ruin and a fantastic support movepool featuring Spikes, Ruination, and Whirlwind. Other special threats such as Calm Mind Arceus-Ground and offensive Eternatus are hurt in viability by Ting-Lu's presence alone. Ting-Lu's physical bulk should not be underestimated either, as it can take on threats like Dragon Dance Necrozma-DM and Zekrom when needed. These incredible defenses come at the cost of lacking any form of reliable recovery, making Ting-Lu extremely vulnerable to entry hazard damage, Knock Off, and status. As such, some teams may prefer either Clodsire due to its superior role compression in checking Kyogre, absorbing Toxic Spikes, and ability to run Heavy-Duty Boots or Arceus-Ground for its better offensive presence and reliable recovery. Effective use of Ting-Lu requires careful management of its HP so that it fulfills its role of setting entry hazards early-game and staying healthy enough to check threats late-game.
ubers.comments:
Other Options

Heavy-Duty Boots may be run over Leftovers, as it better preserves Ting-Lu's longevity should Spikes be set on its side of the field. However, Leftovers is usually preferred, as Ting-Lu itself likes to tank some hits early-game to set its own Spikes, and Heavy-Duty Boots removes Ting-Lu's only form of healing. Taunt is an option to harass opposing Ting-Lu and prevent setup from incoming Pokemon such as Gliscor, but Whirlwind can achieve similar results and offers more utility for checking threats.

Checks and Counters

Gliscor: Gliscor is the most notable threat to Ting-Lu, as it can heal off any Ruination damage with Poison Heal and use it as an easy chance to set entry hazards or use Toxic.

Chip Damage: Ting-Lu is completely vulnerable to all forms of entry hazard and status effect chip damage, which can rack up quickly thanks to its lack of recovery.

Knock Off: Knock Off from Necrozma-DM and Gliscor removes Ting-Lu's only form of recovery, devastating Ting-Lu's longevity.

Physical Attackers: Despite Ting-Lu's massive physical bulk, it is vulnerable to super effective coverage from strong physical attackers like Koraidon, Zacian-C, Calyrex-I, Kyurem-B, and Chien-Pao. Also, Ho-Oh is immune to Earthquake and can heal off Ruination damage with Regenerator while being able to cripple Ting-Lu with a burn from Sacred Fire. These threats may come in on Ting-Lu easily with support from U-turn Miraidon.

Kyogre: Kyogre is one of the few special attackers that is not bothered by Ting-Lu thanks to its rain-boosted STAB Water-type attacks, although it hates directly switching in.

Taunt: Taunt prevents Ting-Lu from using Spikes and Whirlwind, so Taunt users like Arceus-Ground and Landorus-T can prove severely annoying.

Special Wall.description:
Whirlwind prevents opposing setup threats such as Double Dance Miraidon and Calm Mind Arceus-Ground from snowballing out of control. This can also rack up entry hazard damage and is a decent way to maintain momentum against an incoming Gliscor. Protect can also be used in this moveslot, which allows for more Leftovers recovery and scouting of Choice item users and Tera types. Stealth Rock may be chosen in the fourth slot to save moveslots for Ting-Lu's teammates, but it makes Ting-Lu less reliable at checking threats in general. Ting-Lu will very rarely need to Terastallize, as its natural typing provides a strong Electric immunity against Miraidon. Tera Steel provides a Fairy and Dragon resistance, which can be critical for handling Calm Mind + Tera Fairy or Tera Dragon Miraidon sets. It has the additional benefit of an immunity to Toxic from Gliscor and Eternatus. Tera Fairy provides a Dragon immunity against Miraidon, allowing Ting-Lu to better answer Tera Dragon sets holding either Calm Mind or Choice Specs while making Ting-Lu resistant or immune to Koraidon's STAB moves. However, this comes at the expense of not resisting Fairy versus Tera Fairy Miraidon. Tera Poison is useful against Koraidon, Zacian-C, and Tera Fairy Miraidon, and it allows Ting-Lu to absorb Toxic Spikes. Tera Water allows Ting-Lu to take Kyogre's STAB moves while also resisting Koraidon's Flare Blitz and Necrozma-DM's Sunsteel Strike. It also lets Ting-Lu check the rare, but otherwise hard to check, Chi-Yu and Walking Wake.

Ting-Lu struggles against physical threats such as Koraidon, Zacian-C, and Arceus, so it is best paired with Pokemon that can switch into them reliably such as defensive Necrozma-DM, Arceus-Fairy, Gliscor, Arceus-Water, Skeledirge, and Landorus-T. Gliscor deserves special mention, as it can allow Ting-Lu to run Stealth Rock or alternatively allow Gliscor itself to run Toxic Spikes, forming an impressive hazard-stacking core. Necrozma-DM is also notable for having Knock Off, which makes Ting-Lu's Spikes even more deadly. Fairy-types like Arceus-Fairy, Zacian-C, and Flutter Mane are useful for their Dragon immunity, which forces Miraidon to predict between its Dragon- and Electric-type coverage, potentially allowing Ting-Lu to switch in for free. Eternatus and Arceus-Grass are valuable teammates for their ability to take on Kyogre, with Eternatus notably absorbing Toxic Spikes, which severely threaten Ting-Lu. Giratina-O is a great partner that can check Arceus-Ground and Extreme Killer Arceus while providing Defog support, which massively increases Ting-Lu's longevity. Revenge killers like Choice Scarf Koraidon and Miraidon greatly appreciate chip damage from Ting-Lu's Ruination and Spikes for cleaning up weakened teams, and they may take on Miraidon should Ting-Lu not be healthy enough to do so.

ou.overview: With an incredible typing, fantastic bulk, and an amazing ability in Vessel of Ruin, Ting-Lu is one of the best special walls in the tier, being able to check threats like Darkrai, Raging Bolt, Gholdengo, and Iron Moth while possessing immense natural physical bulk to take on even Pokemon like non-Low Kick Kingambit and Dragonite. With access to Stealth Rock, Spikes, and Whirlwind—compounded by its absurd bulk—it is one of the tier’s most reliable entry hazard setters and phazers. While it has immense amount of utility, it can also focus more on its ability to wall foes with its Rest set, even doing so long-term. All of these make Ting-Lu a valuable piece on many manner of team playstyles, ranging from hyper offense, balance, and everything else in between. Unfortunately, as a defensive Pokemon without any recovery moves outside of Rest, Ting-Lu is very reliant on Leftovers for longevity, making it especially weak to Knock Off, unlike similar bulky Ground-types like Gliscor or Clodsire. This lack of reliable recovery also makes it highly vulnerable to chip damage like entry hazards and status, such as from foes like Pecharunt, Galarian Slowking, and Dragapult that it often switches into, as well as being overwhelmed by the number of strong special attackers it must check, especially multiple of them in the same team. The tier is also filled with common offensive Pokemon like Zamazenta, Ogerpon-w, Rillaboom, and special attackers that threaten it, like Kyurem, Iron Valiant, Enamorus; even ones it's tasked to check can still highly damage it, such as Focus Blast Darkrai and Solar Beam Raging Bolt. Additionally, reliable hazard control options like Magic Bounce Hatterene and Defog Corviknight are common options that can switch in and prevent Ting-Lu from keeping hazards on the field.
ou.comments:
Other Options

Ting-Lu can utilize Weakness Policy to further take advantage of its bulk, activating it against Pokemon like Hatterene, Clefable, Ogerpon-W, and Ice Spinner Dragonite before launching a +2 Earthquake, Payback, and even Stone Edge or Heavy Slam in return. This set is most appreciated on faster-paced teams that would appreciate Ting-Lu trading with certain Pokemon that could be problematic for the rest of the team, catching your opponent by surprise, while still providing utility with its entry hazard and defensive profile. In a similar sense, Custap Berry is an option on faster teams to lay an additional layer of Spikes or surprise your opponent with an attack like Ruination or Earthquake, particularly helpful if Ting-Lu has been chipped down in the matchup against Raging Bolt. Ting-Lu can run Attack investment to hit certain benchmarks, like 2HKOing Darkrai and OHKOing maximum HP Cinderace with Earthquake. With Speed investment, Ting-Lu can run Taunt not only to prevent Pokemon like Galarian Weezing and Corviknight from using Defog but also to prevent Pokemon like Corviknight and Clefable from using recovery moves; it also allows Ting-Lu to outspeed Adamant Kingambit and hit it with Earthquake. Tera Grass is a niche option to resist Ogerpon-W's attacks and get entry hazards up against it. Lastly, even with its lower Base Power, Ting-Lu can choose to run Throat Chop over Payback to prevent Pecharunt from switching out via Parting Shot.

Defensive Utility.description:
Ting-Lu's titanic bulk and terrific typing not only make it the tier's premier special wall but also let it set entry hazards easily. If a Stealth Rock setter is present on the team, then Ting-Lu can run Spikes instead, and vice versa; running Stealth Rock also makes Ting-Lu less passive, as it can use its other disruptive moves more freely without spending its turns stacking Spikes. Earthquake gives it a solid STAB move to pressure foes it's tasked to check, like Iron Moth, Raging Bolt, and Gholdengo. Ruination allows Ting-Lu to apply immediate pressure, giving it a safe and consistent tool to wear down any foe, particularly those that resist or are immune to its Earthquake like Ogerpon-W and Landorus-T or bulky targets like Alomomola and opposing Ting-Lu. Whirlwind serves double duty, both allowing Ting-Lu to force out threatening boosted foes like Calm Mind Clefable and Swords Dance Gliscor as well as making any foes lacking Heavy-Duty Boots that are forced in take hazard chip damage. Compressing Ting-Lu as the hazard setter for both Stealth Rock and Spikes is also a good option, particularly on more offensive teams, which highly appreciate the hazard support more than its other moves. Ting-Lu can use Heavy Slam to pressure Hatterene, which would otherwise switch in and prevent Ting-Lu from making progress thanks to Magic Bounce, while also hitting foes like Clefable and Enamorus hard. Leftovers allows Ting-Lu to constantly recover health, something greatly appreciated given its lack of reliable recovery, while Rocky Helmet lets it punish contact moves, particularly Rapid Spin, albeit costing Ting-Lu some of its longevity. Red Card is an alternative option on offensive teams that allows Ting-Lu to instantly force out boosted threats like Dragonite and Kingambit. This also frees up the Whirlwind moveslot to more easily allow the use of both hazards. Ting-Lu can run an Impish nature to become a sturdier mixed wall, notably having good odds to survive two +1 Dragonite's Ice Spinner from full health. It can even go further with 252 HP / 252 Def / 4 SpD to aid Ting-Lu's matchup against physical threats like Ceruledge, Kingambit, and Great Tusk at the cost of its matchup against the special attackers. Physical bulk is most effective on Rocky Helmet sets in order to make sure Ting-Lu can chip physical attackers like Kingambit even further. Tera Water allows Ting-Lu to rid itself of its Water and Ice weaknesses, helping it deal with attacks like Walking Wake's Hydro Steam and Weavile's Triple Axel. Tera Poison allows Ting-Lu to shed its Fairy and Fighting weaknesses, helping it deal with threats like Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Zamazenta, as well as blocking Toxic from Pecharunt and Gliscor that would otherwise threaten to wear Ting-Lu down. Tera Ghost can be used instead to completely nullify any incoming Fighting-type attacks like boosted Body Press from Zamazenta as well as blocking Rapid Spin, allowing Ting-Lu to both set hazards and block hazard removal.

Ting-Lu is an incredibly versatile Pokemon that fits well on nearly every offense, bulky offense, or balance team. Ting-Lu's entry hazard-setting prowess allows it to pair with OU's resident removal blocker extraordinaire Gholdengo, ensuring that whatever hazards it sets stay up in the face of Rapid Spin and Defog. Other spinblockers like Pecharunt and Dragapult also can pair with Ting-Lu nicely. Pecharunt in particular forms a good defensive core with Ting-Lu: Ting-Lu takes care of Darkrai and Gholdengo, which would otherwise beat Pecharunt, while Pecharunt helps to manage Swords Dance Iron Valiant, Ogerpon-W, and Zamazenta that would otherwise use Ting-Lu as setup fodder. Ting-Lu’s hazards are greatly appreciated by any attacker, allowing it to pair well with powerful offensive allies like Darkrai and Kyurem. Ogerpon-W in particular benefits from hazards chipping down the few Pokemon that can face the power of its Ivy Cudgel, and Ting-Lu’s defensive traits allow it to take care of Pokemon like Dragapult, Iron Moth, and Raging Bolt that would otherwise check Ogerpon-W. Ting-Lu pairs nicely with physically defensive Pokemon like Dondozo and Galarian Weezing, providing a bulwark against special threats that would otherwise tear through them such as Gholdengo, Iron Moth, and Raging Bolt. Ogerpon-W is an incredibly threatening foe for Ting-Lu, so Pokemon such as Dragonite and Zamazenta that can switch into and threaten it out are greatly appreciated, especially as Ting-Lu complements them by switching into foes that would threaten to wall them like Pecharunt for both or Galarian Slowking for Zamazenta. Additional hazard-setting teammates like Garganacl, Gliscor, and Great Tusk can form a hazard-stacking core with Ting-Lu, allowing it to freely run Whirlwind. The prevalence of Heavy-Duty Boots means Ting-Lu also appreciates Knock Off users like Weavile, Ogerpon-W, and Gliscor to remove them, letting its hazards continuously chip down foes. Ting-Lu's reliance on Leftovers for health recovery can make it vulnerable to hazard chip damage, so it benefits greatly from hazard removal like Great Tusk's or Iron Treads’s Rapid Spin as well as Galarian Weezing's or Corviknight's Defog for teams that are willing to remove the hazards Ting-Lu sets. Galarian Weezing in particular also helps pressure out Gliscor, one of the most reliable switch-ins to Ting-Lu. Ting-Lu's aforementioned Leftovers reliance for recovery also means it greatly appreciates Knock Off absorbers like Gliscor and Corviknight, enabling it to keep its precious Leftovers to avoid being easily worn down. Status absorbers like Gliscor and Clefable are also greatly appreciated, helping Ting-Lu avoid any damaging status that could either nullify or outdamage its Leftovers recovery. Wish support from teammates like Clefable and Alomomola greatly increases Ting-Lu's longevity, giving it extra healing besides Leftovers. Ting-Lu’s bulk, while enormous, can still struggle against powerful super effective attacks like Kyurem's Ice Beam and Enamorus's Moonblast, so teammates like Gholdengo and Galarian Slowking that can cover Ting-Lu’s weaknesses complement it well.

Resting-Lu (Rest).description:
Ting-Lu is a solid defensive tank that can be used to answer threats like Dragapult, Gholdengo, and Raging Bolt. Rest allows Ting-Lu to fully utilize its walling potential, giving it more longevity than it otherwise would have by making it much more consistent against foes such as Pecharunt and Will-O-Wisp Dragapult, hazards from the likes of Gliscor and opposing Ting-Lu, and other chip damage such as Garganacl's Salt Cure and Heatran's Magma Storm. Ruination is used to chunk switch-ins such as Landorus-T and provide consistent damage. Payback, an alternative to Ruination, allows Ting-Lu to deal damage to foes weak to Dark, namely Dragapult and Deoxys-S. Sleep Talk's reduced passivity makes Ting-Lu harder to set up on, creating fewer free turns for Pokemon such as Kingambit, Dragonite, and Ogerpon-W. At the cost of being a bit more passive, Ting-Lu can forgo Sleep Talk to compress roles as the team's entry hazard setter by running Stealth Rock if it lacks one. Tera Water allows Ting-Lu to deal with moves from foes such as Kyurem, Walking Wake, and Iron Moth. Tera Poison enables it to become immune to poison from foes it likes to switch into such as Galarian Slowking and Pecharunt while enabling it to come in and out to absorb Toxic Spikes. Furthermore, it allows Ting-Lu to now handle Fighting-types like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant and Grass-type moves from Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W.

Ting-Lu fits on a variety of different balance and stall teams. Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Galarian Slowking appreciate Ting-Lu's presence, as it can check faster foes these Pokemon are weak to, such as Dragapult and Darkrai. In return, Gholdengo checks foes that it struggles against like Zamazenta, and Galarian Slowking checks special variants of Iron Valiant and Primarina for Ting-Lu while providing a safe entry point for Ting-Lu through Chilly Reception when baiting in foes like Dragapult. Spikes Gliscor can be used to wear down Ting-Lu checks like Great Tusk. Ting-Lu also struggles with Flying-types such as Dragonite, Landorus-T, and Gliscor because it has to rely on Ruination or Payback to damage them. Dragonite and Gliscor can also use it as setup fodder, so teammates that threaten these Pokemon, such as Kyurem and Ogerpon-W, are appreciated. Dragonite is also a good partner, as it appreciates a Pokemon that can handle Will-O-Wisp Dragapult in addition to checking foes like Ogerpon-W for Ting-Lu. These Pokemon help with Ting-Lu's passivity with the ability to muscle through foes such as Gliscor and Great Tusk. Dondozo is also a great partner on stall teams, stopping any setup attempts from physical threats like Low Kick Kingambit and Dragonite. Dondozo's walling attempts can get punished by Raging Bolt, so Ting-Lu's ability to answer Raging Bolt is appreciated. Clefable is able to provide utility through Knock Off, which, in conjunction with Ting-Lu's Stealth Rock, helps wear down the opposition; in return, Ting-Lu handles Gholdengo for it.This set is easily worn down by entry hazards, so hazard removal through Defog from partners such as Corviknight and Galarian Weezing is appreciated. Pokemon like Zamazenta appreciate Ting-Lu's ability to take on foes such as Will-O-Wisp Dragapult, being able to sponge status and force it out. This set is also used on pivot balance teams alongside Dragapult, Corviknight, and Galarian Slowking, as these Pokemon pivot on Pokemon Ting-Lu can force damage on or set up Stealth Rock against such as opposing Ting-Lu. These teams appreciate Ting-Lu being able to handle foes such as Dragapult, Raging Bolt, and Darkrai.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dark

Rocky Helmet is an alternative to ensure Ting-Lu wins its duel against most Rapid Spin users like Great Tusk and Forretress.

Dark (Special Tank)

Leftovers can be used to give Ting-Lu more longevity at the cost of decreasing its ability to punish contact moves like Meowscarada's U-turn and Hatterene's Draining Kiss. Heavy Slam can help Ting-Lu patch its weakness against Fairy-type Pokemon such as Hatterene and Flutter Mane, and Spikes is an option for Dark teams not using Hisuian Samurott. However, using Spikes or Heavy Slam comes at the cost of dropping a valuable utility move like Whirlwind, which can stop setup sweepers like Volcarona from stealing the game.

(Ground)

Earthquake threatens Pokemon such as Gholdengo, Ninetales, and Volcarona. However, Throat Chop and Ruination target more threatening foes to Ground teams, and Earthquake typically overlaps with the team's coverage greatly.

Defensive Hazard Setter (Ground).description:
Ting-Lu's exceptional bulk and utility options make it an invaluable asset to Ground teams, allowing it to wall threats like Dragapult, Latios, and Spectrier.
