Throat Chop hits Latios, shuts down Air Balloon Gholdengo, and hits Ghost-types such as Dragapult, Spectrier, and Hisuian Zoroark, notably OHKOing the latter. Ruination allows Ting-Lu to quickly wear down the likes of opposing Ting-Lu, Hatterene, and Dragonite. Spikes, in conjunction with Whirlwind and Stealth Rock, sets Ting-Lu apart from other entry hazard setters; it's capable of wearing down the opponent's defensive core and weakens threats such as Greninja, Meowscarada, and Ogerpon-W. Additionally, Whirlwind phazes threatening sweepers like Dragonite and Ceruledge. The given EV spread allows Ting-Lu to take Low Kick from Life Orb Hisuian Zoroark after Swords Dance while preserving special bulk to better combat Gholdengo, Dragapult, and other aforementioned special attackers. Leftovers grants Ting-Lu passive recovery and increases its longevity, while Rocky Helmet punishes contact moves like Draining Kiss from Hatterene and Spectrier as well as U-turn from Meowscarada and Greninja.

Ting-Lu's entry hazards are heavily appreciated by Choice Scarf Great Tusk, which threatens out Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Greninja, as well as Gallade. Landorus and Mamoswine also benefit from hazards, with the former threatening Skarmory, Corviknight, and Moltres via Gravity and the latter removing Gliscor and Sinistcha while acting as a buffer against Ice-types like Articuno, Kyurem, and Alolan Ninetales due to Thick Fat. Furthermore, Choice Scarf Great Tusk removes Heavy-Duty Boots from Sableye and Brambleghast via Knock Off to enhance Ting-Lu's phazing, which enables Ting-Lu's and Clodsire's hazards to wear down threats such as Greninja and Ceruledge more efficiently. Water Absorb Clodsire adds a Water immunity; can switch into attacks from Greninja, Urshifu-R, and Sinistcha; and helps wear down the opposing team with Toxic Spikes or Toxic. Iron Treads eases Ting-Lu's pivoting by removing entry hazards with Rapid Spin and checks Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Hatterene. Gliscor aids in wearing down foes alongside Ting-Lu's entry hazards by spreading Toxic and removing Heavy-Duty Boots from foes such as Tornadus-T, Sinistcha, and Zapdos. Quagsire provides great utility, freeing up a moveslot for Ting-Lu by running an entry hazard, spreading Toxic, and walling the likes of Hisuian Samurott, Swords Dance Weavile, and Azumarill.

Special Tank (Dark).description:
Ting-Lu is a must-have on Dark teams due to its great bulk and utility. Earthquake prevents Ting-Lu from becoming too passive and deals with common targets such as Ceruledge, Hisuian Goodra, and Clodsire. Ruination is an extremely useful tool, especially when paired with entry hazards, as it allows Ting-Lu to wear down foes and prevent threats such as Hatterene from sweeping Dark teams. Stealth Rock is the preferred hazard option, as Hisuian Samurott can offensively set Spikes for Dark teams. Lastly, Whirlwind can be used to phaze dangerous setup sweepers such as Volcarona, Azumarill, and Skarmory while also helping rack up chip damage on the opposing team from hazards. The investment in HP and Special Defense allows Ting-Lu to sponge attacks from threats such as Raging Bolt, Flutter Mane, and Greninja. Rocky Helmet allows Ting-Lu to punish contact moves such as U-turn from Roaring Moon and Meowscarada, Close Combat from Iron Valiant, and Draining Kiss from Hatterene.

Swords Dance Hisuian Samurott is a fantastic partner, forming an entry hazard-stacking core with Ting-Lu thanks to Ceaseless Edge. Furthermore, its access to priority in Sucker Punch and coverage in Sacred Sword allows Hisuian Samurott to easily deal with Dragon, Ground, Normal, and Steel teams. In return, Ting-Lu handles Raging Bolt for Hisuian Samurott. Meowscarada and Greninja are an incredible duo in dealing with a plethora of threats for Ting-Lu; Choice Scarf Meowscarada takes out Flutter Mane, Azumarill, and Enamorus, whereas Choice Specs Greninja removes Gliscor, Galarian Weezing, Iron Valiant, and the Ogerpon formes. Nasty Plot Darkrai becomes an amazing wallbreaker with the help of Ting-Lu's Stealth Rock, as it can OHKO Assault Vest Tornadus-T, Ogerpon-W, and, if using Thunder, specially defensive Corviknight after a boost. Mandibuzz punishes setup sweepers like the Ogerpon formes, Belly Drum Azumarill, and Scizor with Foul Play while also putting Iron Hands on a timer with Toxic. Mandibuzz can also pivot Ting-Lu in on Gholdengo via U-turn. Sableye, thanks to its part-Ghost typing, stops Rapid Spin users that are trying to remove Ting-Lu's Stealth Rock while also checking Fighting-type threats like Sneasler and Great Tusk via Will-O-Wisp. Additionally, Sableye removes key items like Heavy-Duty Boots from Moltres and Articuno, making them extremely prone to Stealth Rock. Bisharp eases the Fairy matchup for Ting-Lu by getting rid of Flutter Mane and Hatterene while also dissuading Defog attempts thanks to Defiant.

Defensive Hazard Setter (Dark).description:
Gifted with a fantastic defensive statline, amazing ability in Vessel of Ruin, and great utility options, Ting-Lu holds the ground even against special attackers such as Enamorus and Flutter Mane, making it a key asset for Dark teams. With access to both Stealth Rock and Spikes, Ting-Lu can chip down the opposing team to let its teammates break through sturdier defensive cores. Whirlwind can be used over Spikes to phaze setup sweepers and further chip down the opposing team. Thanks to its base 110 Attack, Earthquake hits most of the metagame for decent damage even with no Attack investment, 2HKOing Greninja, Hisuian Goodra, and Clodsire. Heavy Slam deals with Fairy-types that would otherwise overpower Ting-Lu, such as Flutter Mane, Enamorus, and Iron Valiant, while also threatening Hatterene trying to bounce back entry hazards. Alternatively, Ruination can wear down threats like Archaludon and Corviknight to facilitate its teammates' sweep.

Despite possessing formidable defensive capabilities, Ting-Lu cannot heal itself except with Leftovers; pairing it with physically defensive Pokemon, such as Sableye and Mandibuzz, to ease its defensive burden is thus strongly recommended. Sableye's Ghost typing brings an invaluable Fighting-type immunity to the team along with blocking Rapid Spin from Forretress and Great Tusk. It also comes with nice utility options in the forms of Will-O-Wisp, Knock Off, and Encore to cripple physical attackers and prevent setup sweepers, like Gouging Fire and Keldeo, from wreaking havoc. On the other hand, Mandibuzz grants a precious Ground-type immunity to the team and can slowly pivot with U-turn while handling Breloom and Rillaboom. Ting-Lu also pairs well with wallbreakers such as Greninja, Meowscarada, Darkrai, Hisuian Samurott, and Bisharp, as they highly value its entry hazard-setting capabilities. Choice Scarf Greninja provides speed control and deals with numerous threats with its coverage options, such as Ice Beam to handle Dragonite and Zapdos and Sludge Wave to check the Ogerpon formes and Iron Valiant. Choice Band Meowscarada can muscle through Ground and Water defensive cores, disposing of Hippowdon and Primarina with Flower Trick while threatening Flying-types like Tornadus-T and Gliscor with Triple Axel. Thanks to Hypnosis and Nasty Plot, Darkrai pressures Flying and Steel defensive cores. Swords Dance Hisuian Samurott can set up Spikes with Ceaseless Edge to let Ting-Lu run Whirlwind and can revenge kill weakened foes such as Dragapult and Latios with Sucker Punch. Lastly, Bisharp can punish attempts from Mandibuzz and Corviknight to remove hazards with Defog while checking Fairy-types like Clefable and Galarian Weezing with Iron Head.

Stealth Rock Support.description:
• Ting-Lu's absurd bulk and excellent support movepool make it the premier Stealth Rock setter in the metagame!

  • Ruination: Ruination gives Ting-Lu the most consistent option for damage output, without resorting to offensive investment.

  • Taunt: While Ting-Lu's Speed is awful compared to most Taunt users, using Taunt against foes like Urshifu formes on the switch is still useful, plus Ting-Lu can use some specialized Speed EVs to outspeed certain paralyzed threats. Note that while using Taunt against Toxapex can be useful, it is highly likely to run Mental Herb, which risks getting Ting-Lu poisoned.

  • Protect: Protect with Leftovers is a strong choice when running Ting-Lu with high sustain teammates such as Toxapex, and can keep Ting-Lu's health up when its in risky situations like trapped by Dragonite's Fire Spin.

  • Heavy Slam: Heavy Slam deals serious damage to Fairy-types, with Flutter Mane in particular needing a huge amount of defensive investment to avoid being OHKOed by it.

Other Options

  • Fissure: Fissure lets Ting-Lu potentially punish passive Pokemon without Substitute, such as Toxapex.

  • Spikes: Getting Stealth Rock and Spikes together makes Whirlwind a very effective damage dealing tool, in addition to supporting other offensive Pokemon. However, it can be difficult to set up without compromising Ting-Lu's damage output.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Even with Ting-Lu's fantastic bulk, Terastallization greatly increases the amount of Pokemon it can beat one-on-one, such as Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle.

  • Poison: Tera Poison gives Ting-Lu an important resistance to Fairy and Fighting, and it lets it absorb Toxic Spikes.

  • Fairy: In addition to a useful Fighting resistance, Tera Fairy helps Ting-Lu against powerful Dragon-types like Choice Band Dragonite and Choice Band Gouging Fire.

  • Water: With Tera Water, Ting-Lu has a significantly better matchup against Urshifu-R. The Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu matchups can also benefit, but be mindful of potential Tera Blast coverage.

  • Steel: Tera Steel retaining a Fighting weakness is unfortunate, but in exchange, Heavy Slam will OHKO even most bulky Flutter Mane, and it gives Ting-Lu a good matchup against Iron Bundle.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry versus Leftovers: Ting-Lu's lack of reliable recovery usually makes Sitrus Berry the most reliable method of surviving an extra attack. Leftovers is a good alternative if Sitrus Berry is needed somewhere else, and even preferable if running Protect.

  • Mental Herb: Mental Herb can be used to nullify one use of Taunt or Encore, which Ting-Lu is fairly vulnerable to, at the cost of reducing its lifespan with a lack of any recovery.

EV Spread Information

  • Physical Defense versus Special Defense: Specializing in one defensive stat depends on which threats Ting-Lu needs to handle, with physically defensive variants preforming better against threats like Dragonite and Roaring Moon, and when Terastallized, Chien-Pao, Ogerpon-H, and Urshifu-R. For specially defensive variants, major targets include Gholdengo and Latios, and when Terastallized, Flutter Mane, Iron Bundle, and Chi-Yu.

  • HP Stat Adjustments with Sitrus Berry: When using a Sitrus Berry, running an even HP number is the best option, so Ting-Lu will eat its berry right after being hit by Ruination.

  • 252 HP / 156 Def / 100 SpD with Impish: When Terastallized to a neutral typing and holding a Sitrus Berry, Ting-Lu survives up to four Icicle Crashes from Jolly Focus Sash Chien-Pao. It also avoids a 2HKO from Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast even without Terastallizing thanks to Sitrus Berry.

  • 140 HP / 116 Def / 252 SpD with Careful: This Specially Defensive spread withstands even Modest Choice Specs Chi-Yu's Overheat!

Speed Benchmarks With Taunt

  • Investing in Speed may seem absurd, but with paralysis support, Ting-Lu can realistically outspeed some major threats!

  • 60 Speed EVs: This outspeeds up to paralyzed Jolly Dragonite, which can save Ting-Lu from Encore.

  • 76 Speed EVs: This outspeeds up to paralyzed Adamant Urshifu-R, and many variants of Ursaluna-B.

  • 92 Speed EVs: This outspeeds up to paralyzed Modest Chi-Yu.

Assault Vest.description:
• Assault Vest and Vessel of Ruin combine to make Ting-Lu an especially formidable tank.

  • Heavy Slam: Heavy Slam deals far more damage to Flutter Mane and Mimikyu than any other attack, with even Bold Flutter Mane having a good shot at being OHKOed after Stealth Rock damage.

  • Fissure: Fissure is Ting-Lu's best shot at KOing bulky foes like Stamina Archaludon and Ursaluna-B.

  • Payback versus Throat Chop: Payback will usually deal more damage thanks to how slow Ting-Lu is, but Throat Chop will punish Pokemon that switch in more.

  • EV Spread: The given EV spread maximizes Ting-Lu's Attack and special bulk.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Ting-Lu doesn't need Terastallization to function, it makes it far more effective at beating a wide variety of Pokemon one-on-one.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy not only helps Ting-Lu against powerful Dragon- and Fighting-type attacks, but it also gives Ting-Lu a good Tera Blast to hit Dragonite and Roaring Moon with.

  • Poison: Tera Poison gives Ting-Lu a vital Fairy resistance against Flutter Mane and Mimikyu, and it lets it absorb the dreaded Toxic and Toxic Spikes. It still makes a reasonable Tera Blast option for hitting Primarina and Serperior hard as well.

  • Water: Tera Water is a fantastic defensive typing, letting Ting-Lu avoid a 2HKO from Tera Fire Choice Specs Chi-Yu's Overheat.

  • Steel: Tera Steel gives Ting-Lu a powerful STAB Heavy Slam, giving it a great matchup against Flutter Mane and Iron Bundle. It does become an issue against common Fire-types like Ogerpon-H and Gouging Fire though.

Defensive Hazard Setter.description:
Ting-Lu's enormous HP combined with Vessel of Ruin makes it a fantastic defensive anchor against Pokemon such as Gholdengo, Mega Latios, and Raging Bolt. This makes Ting-Lu a strong entry hazard setter as well, since many hazard removal options such as Terapagos and Zapdos can't dissuade Ting-Lu from setting up hazards on them due to its bulk. To ensure it isn't completely passive against Flying-types, Ruination is necessary, which combined with hazard support allows Ting-Lu to force recovery from defensive Pokemon like Corviknight and Moltres. Alternatively, Rock Slide can be used to threaten frailer Ground-immune Pokemon, such as Mega Charizard Y and Nasty Plot Tornadus-T, while Payback can be used to hit Mega Latios and Air Balloon Gholdengo more effectively. Spikes can be used instead of Stealth Rock if the team already has a Stealth Rock setter. Spikes also does better long-term damage if all three layers are set, especially to Pokemon that don't run Heavy-Duty Boots such as Gholdengo, Ferrothorn, and Mega Venusaur. Whirlwind is needed to ensure Ting-Lu isn't setup fodder against threats that don't mind taking Ruination such as bulky Volcarona and Swords Dance Gliscor while also helping wear down opposing teams with Ting-Lu's hazards. Finally, Leftovers provides Ting-Lu with passive recovery, healing off weak attacks such as Tornadus-T's U-turn and Zapdos's Hurricane while also allowing it to survive attacks it otherwise wouldn't, such as avoiding the 2HKO from Choice Specs Tapu Koko's Dazzling Gleam.

A major downside of Ting-Lu is its complete lack of recovery options, making Alomomola a fantastic partner that can also pivot into Water-types such as Urshifu-R and Barraskewda while healing Ting-Lu up with Wish. In return, Ting-Lu makes up for Alomomola's passivity against Gholdengo and Raging Bolt with its defensive profile combined with Whirlwind, wearing them down rapidly. Alomomola also handles Great Tusk for Ting-Lu, which would otherwise threaten Ting-Lu while removing its hazards easily. Another excellent defensive partner is Mega Venusaur, which is able to come in against the Water-, Fighting-, and Grass-types that threaten out Ting-Lu such as Kartana and Iron Valiant while appreciating Ting-Lu's hazard support to wear down opposing teams faster with its wide coverage. On offensive teams where they may not mind Ting-Lu's lack of longevity, Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Raging Bolt all appreciate the chip damage Ting-Lu provides with hazards wearing down defensive switch-ins such as Landorus-T, Mega Venusaur, and Kingambit. Gholdengo in particular is also able to block Defog attempts from Tornadus-T and Corviknight and Rapid Spin from Great Tusk especially if it is holding Air Balloon. Partners like Weavile and Ogerpon-W are also notable, since they can use Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from targets like Alomomola and Toxapex, making them much easier to wear down in the long run.

Specially Defensive.description:
Ting-Lu is an absolute stalwart in the Special Defense slot, as it's now able to check almost every special attacker, including Eternatus and Gholdengo. Spikes is a crucial entry hazard that Ting-Lu can easily set up thanks to its ability to tank multiple hits. Whirlwind allows Ting-Lu to avoid being setup fodder but also rack up chip damage once even one layer of Spikes has been set. Rest is a fantastic alternative, as it is Ting-Lu's only form of recovery and can be a solid option alongside Sleep Talk should the team have entry hazards elsewhere. Tera Poison gives Ting-Lu a resistance to Fairy-, Bug-, and Fighting-type moves and an immunity to poison, while Tera Water helps ease the sun and rain matchups that it may otherwise struggle with.

Ting-Lu is solely fitting in the Special Defense slots on teams, as most of the bigger Special Defense donations from the likes of Arceus formes and Zacian-C allow Ting-Lu to leverage its ability and typing to the absolute fullest. Other entry hazard setters such as Clefable, Landorus-T, and Skarmory allow Ting-Lu to opt for RestTalk over Spikes and Whirlwind; however, they do form a fantastic entry hazard stacking core should Ting-Lu opt to run Spikes. Pokemon that can apply heavy offensive pressure such as Hisuian Electrode and Gholdengo appreciate the chip damage from Spikes that Ting-Lu can reliably set. Spinblockers such as the aforementioned Gholdengo and Sinistcha are fantastic partners, as they can ensure the Spikes Ting-Lu sets up are not removed. Lastly, Knock Off users such as Clefable and Tornadus-T can rid foes of their Heavy-Duty Boots to help stack the chip damage that Spikes can provide.

Hazards Tank.description: Ting-Lu's Attack investment allows it to 2HKO Nasty Plot Gholdengo with Stomping Tantrum, its HP and Defense allow it to survive Rillaboom's Wood Hammer.

RegenVest.description: RegenVest Ting-Lu leverages its massive mixed bulk, unique typing, and low Speed tier to act as a pivot into several of the tier's special attackers as well as defensive Pokemon to fire off its utility moves. U-turn and Knock Off are staple moves for RegenVest users. Nuzzle is primarily for Eternatus, which is otherwise difficult to punish, but if Ting-Lu can pivot into a revenge killer such as Mega Alakazam or Mega Sceptile, then Salt Cure can be opted for to annoy Take Heart Arceus formes. Stone Axe provides entry hazard support, while Mortal Spin poisons Imposter users and can act as a decent option for hazard removal, especially if paired with Salt Cure. Ting-Lu requires its Assault Vest to switch into any reasonably strong special attack it doesn't resist, so it needs secondary Knock Off absorbers like Take Heart Arceus formes and Imposter users. It is also vulnerable to threats like Flutter Mane, Palkia-O, and Ultra Necrozma with Magical Torque or Mountain Gale, so it appreciates a specially defensive teammate like Ice Scales Arceus-Fairy, and in return Ting-Lu scouts powerful attacks like Psycho Boost and Moongeist Beam. Depending on its moves, Ting-Lu can be Imposter-proofed by Take Heart Arceus formes or Electric-types like Arceus-Electric and Iron Hands.

Defensive.description: Ting-Lu leverages its typing, massive defensive stats, and ability to counter Final Gambit Lunala to find use as a reasonable utility Pokemon. Fur Coat allows Ting-Lu to counter threats like Mega Garchomp, Ho-Oh, and Arceus-Ghost. Knock Off forces progress, removing items from foes such as Mega Audino. Salt Cure's residual damage limits Take Heart Arceus formes' ability to set up in front of Ting-Lu and reduces its passivity, while Parting Shot can still deal with Pokemon such as Arceus-Ghost when in combination with a revenge killer like Mega Alakazam. Topsy-Turvy neutralizes setup threats like Arceus-Ghost and Mega Garchomp. Covert Cloak protects Ting-Lu from Mortal Spin and Salt Cure. Ting-Lu best fits on teams looking for a good blanket physical wall and Simple Ghost-type answer. Ting-Lu struggles against Mega Lucario and Ash-Greninja, so backup checks like Fur Coat Celesteela are mandatory. Imposter-proof Ting-Lu with Knock Off absorbers like Arceus formes; Magic Bounce can also be useful against Parting Shot variants.

Mixed Wall (Dark).description: Ting-Lu finds itself a home on Dark teams as a sturdy special wall and entry hazard setter, capable of staving off foes like Mega Charizard Y, Nasty Plot Tornadus-T, Tapu Koko, and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele and threatening them out. Heavy Slam alongside 32 Attack EVs allows Ting-Lu to OHKO Choice Scarf Tapu Lele as well as dissuade other Fairy-types such as Tapu Bulu from switching in for free. Ruination allows Ting-Lu to deal consistent damage to opposing walls such as Corviknight and Porygon2 and force them to use up their recovery moves' PP, softening them up in the long run for a teammate like Meowscarada or Hydreigon. Rock Slide allows Ting-Lu to OHKO Mega Charizard Y and Quiver Dance Volcarona, which can be an issue if not running Whirlwind. Whirlwind allows Ting-Lu to stop setup sweepers such as the aforementioned Volcarona as well as Swords Dance Garchomp, Nasty Plot + Substitute Hydreigon, and Z-Celebrate Victini from using it as setup fodder, while both Spikes and Stealth Rock allow Ting-Lu to chip down defensive pieces like the previously talked-about Porygon2 as well as Ferrothorn, Hisuian Goodra, and Clodsire every time they attempt to answer a threat. Offensive teammates such as Meowscarada, Hydreigon, and Weavile appreciate Ting-Lu setting hazards to chip down their answers into range of their attacks. Alolan Muk provides a Fairy neutrality to answer threats like Tapu Lele and Enamorus alongside Knock Off support to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from foes like Corviknight, Tornadus-T, and Staraptor. Mega Sableye offers hazard control to let Ting-Lu maximize its longevity and come in safely to check threats, combats Mega Gallade and Sneasler thanks to its Fighting immunity, blocks Rapid Spin from the likes of Iron Treads and Terapagos, and provides Knock Off support to help whittle down the aforementioned Heavy-Duty Boots users. Hisuian Samurott pairs nicely with Ting-Lu if not running Spikes thanks to its ability to set up Spikes itself with Ceaseless Edge while appreciating the general chip damage Ting-Lu's hazards do to its answers like Tapu Bulu.

Physically Defensive (Ground).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

anythinggoes.overview: Ting-Lu is a dominant presence in Anything Goes, filling the role of the metagame's most crucial defensive glue while simultaneously providing indispensable offensive support. Ting-Lu is blessed with a fantastic typing that—in tandem with its titanic, Vessel of Ruin-boosted bulk—makes it the single best switch-in to Miraidon, one of the most consistent Calyrex-S checks, and a soft check to Necrozma-DM, Eternatus, and a plethora of other threats. This incredible defensive profile grants Ting-Lu many opportunities to set multiple layers of Spikes, making it that much harder for the foes to weather hits from its teammates. This unrivaled combination of traits means that Ting-Lu should be used on nearly every team bar hyper offense ones. Though, as fantastic as Ting-Lu is, its omnipresence means that methods to limit its impact or take advantage of it are common. Koraidon and Kyogre are able to exploit Ting-Lu to facilitate their wallbreaking, and common Pokemon like Miraidon and various Arceus formes can use Taunt to prevent Ting-Lu from setting Spikes. Furthermore, Ting-Lu is entirely reliant on Leftovers for healing, so Knock Off or any status condition greatly reduces its longevity.
anythinggoes.comments:
Other Options

Ting-Lu has plenty of fringe options. Fissure can be used in a similar vein to Ruination, punishing switch-ins and OHKOing bulky sweepers that would typically beat Ting-Lu, though its inherent inconsistency and inability to touch Ho-Oh mean that it is generally inferior. Protect can be used to gain additional healing from Leftovers and scout Choice Scarf Koraidon's attacks, though this means giving up a valuable moveslot for minimal upsides. Stealth Rock can be used to stack additional passive damage on top of Spikes, though the difficulty of fitting it into Ting-Lu's moveset and lack of general effectiveness over Spikes mean that it is usually better delegating Stealth Rock to a partner like Arceus-Water, if it's run at all. Similarly, Taunt can be used, with some extra Speed investment, to gain an advantage over opposing Ting-Lu, though this has minimal other use and struggles to fit into Ting-Lu's cramped moveset. A wide variety of Tera types can be used, such as Steel and Fairy, to fill whatever niche is required; these have far less overall use than Tera Grass or Tera Poison though.

Checks and Counters

Koraidon: Koraidon heavily threatens Ting-Lu with its powerful Low Kick and can switch into it with relative safety, though it doesn't appreciate getting hit by Ruination or Earthquake.

Kyogre: Kyogre deals massive damage to Ting-Lu and can typically use it as an entry point; Tera Grass Ting-Lu can turn the tables against it though.

Ho-Oh: Ting-Lu is incapable of doing much damage to Ho-Oh, and it can get crippled by a Sacred Fire burn or take a lot of damage from offensive sets. Ho-Oh doesn't immediately force Ting-Lu out though, and it can often allow multiple layers of Spikes to go up.

Entry Hazard Support.description:
Massive bulk, a great movepool, and an absolute godsend of a typing cement Ting-Lu as a core part of the metagame, checking key threats like Calyrex-S, Miraidon, and Necrozma-DM. Spikes are an essential part of Ting-Lu's kit, chipping key defensive walls like Arceus-Ground, Arceus-Water, and opposing Ting-Lu into KO range of the powerful wallbreakers that it is often paired with, in addition to limiting common revenge killers like Choice Scarf Calyrex-S and Koraidon; futhermore, the dearth of relevant entry hazard removal means that each layer of Spikes is usually permanent. Earthquake does large amounts of damage to Miraidon and Eternatus and is a decently strong hit on most neutral targets. Ruination is an important tool for limiting Ting-Lu's switch-ins and forcing Arceus formes to use Recover, as well as being the best move to weaken opposing Ting-Lu. Payback can be run over either Earthquake or Ruination to OHKO Calyrex-S for teams that are weaker to it, though this will result in Ting-Lu either struggling against Miraidon or failing to punish switch-ins, depending on which move is replaced. Whirlwind allows Ting-Lu to handle setup sweepers like Necrozma-DM and Arceus-Ground, as well as racking up additional damage from Spikes. Tera Grass can turn the tables on Kyogre and makes Ting-Lu an effective check to Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground. Tera Poison instead lets Ting-Lu resist Koraidon's Low Kick and Fairy-type attacks from Zacian-C and Arceus-Fairy, be immune to Eternatus's Toxic, and remove Eternatus's Toxic Spikes, albeit at the cost of becoming weak to Psychic- and Ground-type attacks from Calyrex-S, Necrozma-DM, and Arceus-Ground. Both Tera types additionally let Ting-Lu resist Calyrex-S's Grass Knot.

Ting-Lu is so incredible that it's hard to find reasons not to use it. It can slot into any playstyle besides hyper offense and likely improve the team. That being said, Ting-Lu's glaring weakness to Koraidon necessitates partners that can handle it, such as Ho-Oh and defensive Arceus formes. Kyogre is another troublesome wallbreaker, so teammates that can pivot into it like Eternatus, Koraidon, and Miraidon are greatly appreciated, with Eternatus additionally absorbing Toxic Spikes for Ting-Lu. Reliance on Leftovers for healing means that Ting-Lu can be overwhelmed by Miraidon and Calyrex-S, so backup checks to them like Arceus-Ground for the former and Ho-Oh or Arceus for the latter are very important. Almost every offensive threat benefits from Ting-Lu's Spikes digging into its checks, as well as the backbone it provides against Calyrex-S and Miraidon. Koraidon and Miraidon are especially notable partners, as they can maintain momentum with U-turn to accrue additional entry hazard damage on defensive Arceus formes and Ting-Lu, respectively, with Koraidon also taking advantage of opposing Ting-Lu attempting to trade hazards with Ting-Lu. Necrozma-DM is another teammate that benefits greatly from Ting-Lu's Spikes support weakening opposing teams to the point where it can sweep with Dragon Dance, and it provides additional support as a check to Zacian-C and another pivot for Eternatus, while Ting-Lu can check Calyrex-S for it.

Choice Scarf.description:
Set Details

  • Choice Scarf Chi-Yu functions as a fast and powerful attacker that can threaten many common Restricted Pokemon with heavy damage, including both Calyrex formes, Zamazenta-C, and Lunala, while bolstering its teammates' special damage output with Beads of Ruin.
  • Although Snarl is Chi-Yu's weakest move, it allows it to chip foes while shutting down many Restricted Pokemon offensively, including Miraidon and Lunala, and breaking Focus Sash, which is notably used by Flutter Mane.
  • Choice Scarf allows Chi-Yu to outspeed the majority of the format, notably including Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R.
  • Tera Ghost allows Chi-Yu to avoid Fake Out and alleviate some of Chi-Yu's weaknesses; it particularly provides an immunity to Fighting-type attacks from Zamazenta-C and Iron Hands. Tera Fire can be used as an alternative on teams with priority-blocking measures such as Indeedee-F and Farigiraf to bolster the damage of Heat Wave and Overheat, including guaranteeing an OHKO against Brute Bonnet and Zacian-C with Heat Wave and against Flutter Mane with Overheat.

Teambuilding

  • Common metagame threats such as Incineroar, Urshifu-R, and Koraidon can resist its STAB moves and, in the case of the latter two, threaten to OHKO Chi-Yu. Raging Bolt and Iron Hands, due to their bulk and power, can also pressure Chi-Yu.
  • Without Tera Ghost, Chi-Yu is vulnerable to Fake Out from the likes of Rillaboom and Incineroar. Opposing speed control, in the form of Tailwind and Trick Room, can cause many threats like Urshifu-R, Ogerpon-C, and Ursaluna to outspeed Chi-Yu and take advantage of its weak defenses.
  • Additionally, Wide Guard users like Zamazenta-C and Lunala can take advantage of Chi-Yu locked into Snarl or Heat Wave.
  • Due to its lack of bulk, priority moves can threaten Chi-Yu severely, namely Aqua Jet from Urshifu-R, Sucker Punch from Chien-Pao after Terastallizing, and Thunderclap from Raging Bolt.
  • Strong partners for Chi-Yu include powerful special attackers, such as Calyrex-S and Miraidon, which can take advantage of its Beads of Ruin while threatening Urshifu-R and Koraidon.
  • Koraidon also pairs very well with Chi-Yu, as not only do they form a powerful core offensively, with Chi-Yu threatening Lunala and Calyrex-S and Koraidon threatening Incineroar and Urshifu-R, but Koraidon also provides sun to bolster Chi-Yu's Fire-type attacks.
  • Flutter Mane is another common partner for Chi-Yu, as it benefits from Beads of Ruin to bolster its damage output, while Flutter Mane can run Taunt to deny Wide Guard and Trick Room.
  • Chi-Yu also appreciates redirection support to alleviate its frailty, commonly from Brute Bonnet and Indeedee-F, which can also provide support with Spore and Psychic Terrain, respectively.

Choice Item Attacker.description:
Chi-Yu is a phenomenal glass cannon; it has a strong offensive typing and good Special Attack, aided by its ability. These qualities along with proper speed control allow it to pressure common metagame Pokemon including both Calyrex formes, Rillaboom, Amoonguss, and Zamazenta-C. Snarl threatens a common Restricted core that revolves around redirection—Calyrex and Clefairy—and it can be used to chip away and weaken the damage output of bulkier specially offensive threats like Raging Bolt and Terapagos. Choice Specs allows Chi-Yu to pick up OHKOs on Pokemon like Assault Vest Rillaboom and Calyrex-I with Heat Wave and bulky Pelipper with Dark Pulse. Choice Scarf enables Chi-Yu to outspeed common fast metagame staples such as Chien-Pao, Calyrex-S, and Flutter Mane without Protosynthesis Speed activated. The defensive investment guarantees that Chi-Yu survives Surging Strikes and Tera Water Aqua Jet from Urshifu-R when Chi-Yu has used Tera Ghost, High Horsepower from most Assault Vest Rillaboom, and Tera Starstorm from Terapagos-S at +2. The Speed EVs allow Chi-Yu to outspeed maximum Speed Adamant Urshifu formes, and it also outspeeds Caylrex-S if running Choice Scarf. Special Attack EVs allow Choice Scarf Chi-Yu to threaten an OHKO on Ogerpon-H with Overheat. Tera Ghost is absolutely necessary for Chi-Yu because it can avoid Fake Out and Fighting-type moves like Body Press from Zamazenta-C.

Incineroar completely walls Chi-Yu and is able to pivot in and out with Parting Shot, while Urshifu-R is able to simply tank a hit and OHKO Chi-Yu. Kyogre and Pelipper are also definite Chi-Yu answers, as they weaken its Fire-type moves with Drizzle and can retaliate with an OHKO with Water Spout or Origin Pulse and Weather Ball, respectively. Chi-Yu has a plethora of great partners; Choice Specs Terapagos and Miraidon both take great advantage of the power boost provided by Beads of Ruin and are able to pressure Pokemon like Kyogre and Incineroar. Koraidon is another good partner for it because it sets up the sun, overriding rain from Pelipper and Kyogre and boosting Chi-Yu's Fire-type attacks. This also mitigates its weakness to Water-type moves, aiding in Chi-Yu's matchup against the aforementioned threats. Chi-Yu can also function by itself with speed control from Prankster Tailwind setters like Whimsicott and Tornadus, which can also set up the sun.

Glass Cannon.description:
Chi-Yu is an incredibly strong special attacker, and because of its ability Beads of Ruin, it's able to support other special attacking teammates while still dealing a lot of damage. It matches up well against some common restricted Pokemon such as both Calyrex formes and Zamazenta-C and it can also pressure common Pokemon such as Rillaboom, Gholdengo, and Amoonguss with its STAB moves. Snarl keeps special attacking threats such as Calyrex-S and Terapagos in check and still does respectable spread damage, while Dark Pulse provides strong and consistent damage. Overheat is an instant burst of damage that allows Chi-Yu to OHKO even bulky threats like Rillaboom and Zamazenta-C while also getting around Wide Guard. Since it is very frail, Focus Sash helps Chi-Yu survive for longer, whereas Life Orb gives it a significant damage boost, allowing it to OHKO Flutter Mane with Overheat and 2HKO Miraidon with Dark Pulse. Tera Ghost allows it to avoid Fake Out and gain an immunity to otherwise threatening Fighting-type attacks from Koraidon and the Urshifu formes.

Chi-Yu pairs well with strong special attackers such as Flutter Mane and Terapagos, since both of them benefit a lot from Beads of Ruin. Chi-Yu struggles with its average Speed stat and appreciates speed control from Tornadus, since it allows Chi-Yu to outspeed threats such as Koraidon, Miraidon, Flutter Mane, and Calyrex-S and deal respectable amount of damage with Beads of Ruin-boosted Bleakwind Storm. Chi-Yu also has problems with Urshifu-R, since it can switch-in on both Heat Wave and Dark Pulse and OHKO Chi-Yu back with Surging Strikes. Amoonguss helps with that issue, by redirecting away Fighting- and Water-type attacks from Urshifu-R, letting Chi-Yu deal damage more consistently. Pelipper is a strong Chi-Yu answer, since it sets up rain and is able to protect teammates from Chi-Yu's attacks with Wide Guard. Incineroar and Assault Vest Raging Bolt can take hits from it easily, meaning that the former can pivot out with Parting Shot and the latter is able to use Snarl, do high damage to it, or take advantage of Beads of Ruin and attack its partner.

Offensive Support.description:
Chi-Yu's excellent damage output, Beads of Ruin support, and great tools in Snarl and Taunt allow it to be especially strong against Amoonguss, Terapagos, and the Calyrex formes and grant Chi-Yu a unique niche as a supportive Pokemon in Regulation G. Snarl is preferred to weaken threats such as Terapagos, Calyrex-S, Raging Bolt, and opposing Chi-Yu; however, Chi-Yu can opt instead for Dark Pulse for a more consistent STAB option against Farigiraf and Pelipper. Overheat is used for burst damage, enabling Chi-Yu to OHKO Calyrex-I and Assault Vest Rillaboom. Taunt is an excellent way for Chi-Yu to shut down Amoonguss as well as Trick Room from setters like Farigiraf and Calyrex-I. This is further enhanced by Covert Cloak's Fake Out immunity, and Covert Cloak also provides Chi-Yu with a valuable immunity to Snarl and Icy Wind stat drops. The EV spread allows Chi-Yu to survive Discharge from Choice Specs Miraidon, Earth Power from Choice Specs Terapagos, and after Terastallization, Close Combat from Urshifu-R. The Special Attack EVs with a Modest nature ensure an OHKO on Zamazenta-C with Overheat, and the Speed EVs enable Chi-Yu to outspeed Terapagos and Adamant Urshifu formes. Tera Water provides a resistance to Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and Pelipper's Weather Ball while improving Chi-Yu's matchup against Calyrex-I.

Because Chi-Yu has relatively poor bulk and a mediocre Speed tier, it struggles with fast, powerful threats such as Miraidon, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, Koraidon, and Chien-Pao. This makes Rillaboom an exceptional partner, as it can mitigate Miraidon's damage output and threaten Urshifu-R with Wood Hammer and priority Grassy Glide. Rillaboom also appreciates not only Chi-Yu's ability to threaten Steel- and Grass-types like Gholdengo and opposing Rillaboom but also its Taunt shutting down Will-O-Wisp and Parting Shot from Incineroar. Clefairy is also a good partner, enhancing Chi-Yu's bulk and redirecting away attacks to allow Chi-Yu to survive extra crucial turns against Urshifu-R and Chien-Pao. Calyrex-S is a great restricted partner, outspeeding and threatening Miraidon, Koraidon, and Chien-Pao, while also taking advantage of Beads of Ruin. Clefairy and Calyrex-S both appreciate how well Chi-Yu handles Amoonguss and Terapagos. Exceptionally bulky attackers like Kyogre and especially Assault Vest Iron Hands can exploit Chi-Yu's frail defenses, so the above mentioned Rillaboom can be a great help to threaten it and Iron Hands for major damage.

Choice Attacker.description:
• Snarl is used as utility and a way to check special attacking compositions such as Farigiraf + Ursaluna-B. Overheat is appreciated as a single target nuke, hitting almost twice as hard as Heat Wave.

  • Choice Specs is used to give Chi-Yu maximum offensive pressure and allow it to pick up OHKOes on Amoonguss and Kingambit with Heat Wave. Alternatively, Chi-Yu can opt for Choice Scarf to outspeed threats like Landorus, Chien-Pao, and Flutter Mane.

  • The HP EVs allow for Chi-Yu to avoid the 2HKO from Flutter Mane's Moonblast and once Terastallized into the Ghost-type, almost always survive -1 Adamant Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch. The Speed EVs allow Chi-Yu to outspeed the Adamant Urshifu formes.

  • Chi-Yu prefers Tera Ghost to remove its Fighting weakness and be immune to common priority moves like Fake Out and Extreme Speed, which is crucial to preserve momentum. Although Chi-Yu can utilize Tera Fire to significantly increase its damage output, allowing Choice Scarf Chi-Yu to OHKO Ogerpon-W and Flutter Mane with Overheat and Choice Specs variants to remove Assault Vest Kingambit and Rillaboom with Heat Wave.

Choice-Yu.description:
• With a Choice item, Chi-Yu can choose to become either a spicy revenge killer or a scorching wallbreaker!

  • Flamethrower versus Lava Plume: Flamethrower's higher power makes it the better cleaning tool, but Lava Plume's higher burn chance gives Chi-Yu a good shot of punishing major physical attacking fores such as Dragonite, Azumarill, and Garchomp that resist Fire.

  • Psychic: This is Chi-Yu's most powerful attack against Urshifu-R and Toxapex and can pick off weakened Annihilape without Overheat's Special Attack drop.

  • Tera Blast: Even before Terastallizing, Tera Blast is a decent coverage move that hits Primarina and Roaring Moon.

  • Modest versus Timid: Modest is generally preferred since Chi-Yu's Speed isn't too impressive, but Timid does ensure that Chi-Yu outspeeds Urshifu formes, Annihilape, and Mimikyu, who are fully capable of revenge killing Chi-Yu that lack Choice Scarf.

Other Options

  • Fire Blast: Fire Blast's shaky accuracy can be an issue, but it's a far better sweeping tool than Overheat.

  • Memento: Support isn't Chi-Yu's forte, but Memento lets Choice Scarf sets potentially set-up a sweeper in exchange for KOing itself.

Items

  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf patches up Chi-Yu's lukewarm Speed into something usable for revenge killing and also makes bulkier builds easier to use.

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs trades revenge killing for terrifying wallbreaking power. With Tera Fire, the heat gets so extreme that even Blissey is 2HKOed by Overheat!

Bulkier EV Spread

  • 228 HP / 12 Def / 124 SpA / 4 SpD / 140 Spe with Modest: This is a bulky spread meant for Choice Scarf, outspeeding up to Iron Bundle. The bulk investment survives Breloom's Mach Punch, Mimikyu's Play Rough followed by Shadow Sneak, and has a good shot of surviving Tera Normal Choice Band Dragonite's Extreme Speed. 40 EVs can be moved from Special Attack to Speed to outspeed Dragapult at a serious cost to power.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Chi-Yu's damage output is red hot even without Terastallization, making it a fairly flexible Pokemon.

  • Fire: Tera Fire Overheat is extremely difficult to wall without a resistance, making it an easy choice for Chi-Yu. It also lets Tera Blast become a powerful STAB move while Chi-Yu is locked into using it, letting it get around the normal limitations of using a Choice item.

  • Grass: Tera Grass is a good response to Urshifu-R and Primarina, and lets Chi-Yu avoid being OHKOed by Iron Bundle's Hydro Pump.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is Chi-Yu's best shot of defeating Roaring Moon and and gives it an important Fighting-type resistance.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost lets Chi-Yu surprise common users of Normal-type priority such as Dragonite, Ogerpon-H, and Entei, with the bonus of blocking Breloom from an easy revenge kill.

  • Dark: While Tera Dark is nowhere near as impressive as a boosted Overheat, Dark Pulse has excellent coverage and also removes Chi-Yu's troublesome Stealth Rock weakness.

  • Water: Getting a Water-type resistance is always useful against Urshifu-R, but the real key for Tera Water is that it helps Chi-Yu in the mirror match-up, especially against Assault Vest Chi-Yu.

Offensive.description:
• Chi-Yu's sizzling offensive power lets it get away with a wide variety of options that wouldn't fit on a Choice item set.

  • Flamethrower versus Lava Plume: Flamethrower's greater power makes it the better option in most instances, but Lava Plume's higher burn rate is good at punishing switch-ins like Roaring Moon and Dragonite.

  • Flame Charge: Chi-Yu is powerful enough that even without an offensive item, getting a Speed boost makes cleaning teams late-game very achievable.

  • Psychic: Psychic is Chi-Yu's best option against Urshifu-R and Toxapex. Note that Overheat will out-damage targets like Annihilape though.

Other Options

  • Will-O-Wisp: If not using Assault Vest, Will-O-Wisp severely punishes bulky physical threats like Roaring Moon and Dragonite that may switch in and works great with Terastallization to surprise other bulky threats such Ting-Lu.

Items

  • Assault Vest: Chi-Yu has shockingly decent Special Defense, so Assault Vest lets it preform much better against Flutter Mane and opposing Chi-Yu.

  • Life Orb: Life Orb lets you get away with playing this set far more offensively at the cost of being even weaker to priority attacks than usual.

  • Focus Sash: If using a more offensive spread, Focus Sash can be worth it to flip the tables on fast offensive foes such as Iron Bundle.

  • Eject Pack: This turns Overheat into a one-use pivot move, surprising foes with a momentum shift in your favor.

EV Spreads

  • 228 HP / 12 Def / 124 SpA / 4 SpD / 140 Spe with Modest: This bulky spread is perfect for Assault Vest and Flame Charge, letting Chi-Yu outspeed Iron Bundle after a boost and avoid an OHKO from Breloom's Mach Punch. It also avoids a KO from Mimikyu's Shadow Sneak following Play Rough and often survives Tera Normal Dragonite's Choice Band Extreme Speed. If outspeeding the rare Dragapult after Flame Charge is a priority, 40 Special Attack EVs can be moved to Speed.

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Modest or Timid: When using more offensive items like Life Orb or Focus Sash, going a more offensive route makes Chi-Yu a better late-game sweeper. Modest is preferred for the damage output, but Timid outspeeds Urshifu formes and Annihilape.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Chi-Yu has a ton of weaknesses to common attacking types, so while Terastallization isn't needed to function, it can especially help bulkier Chi-Yu check more threats and otherwise focus less on hit-and-run attacking.

  • Fire: Beyond giving Overheat soul-melting damage output, Tera Fire gives Chi-Yu a vital Fairy-type resistance against Flutter Mane and a good shot of OHKOing even bulky Flutter Mane with Overheat.

  • Grass: Tera Grass is a huge help against Urshifu-R and Primarina, and can save Chi-Yu from Choice Scarf Landorus-T revenge kills as long as it doesn't use Flying Tera Blast.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy has good synergy with Chi-Yu's former typing, giving it a vital Fighting-type resistance and ensuring Chi-Yu is not walled by Roaring Moon.

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost is Chi-Yu's best hope against Dragonite and Entei's Extreme Speed, as well as blocking snipes from Ogerpon-H's Quick Attack.

  • Water: Tera Water works great on Assault Vest Chi-Yu with Tera Blast, ironically turning it into a decent check against other Chi-Yu! It also eases the matchup against Urshifu-R.

Nasty Plot.description:
• While not easy to sweep with due to it's Speed, Chi-Yu becomes a a hot wallbreaker after setting up Nasty Plot!

  • Overheat: Overheat's Special Attack drop may conflict with Nasty Plot, but it'll deep-fry almost any Pokemon slower than Chi-Yu, making it a worthy wallbreaking tool.

  • Psychic: Psychic shatters Urshifu-R, a common revenge killer against Chi-Yu.

  • Substitute: Substitute does a great job of punishing common status users such as Archaludon. If Terastallized, Chi-Yu has a good chance of retaining its Substitute against Salt Cure as well.

  • Timid versus Modest: While this Chi-Yu is more focused on extreme wall-frying than sweeping, Timid is nice for outspeeding Urshifu formes and Annihilape, whom certainly can't handle boosted attacks well.

Items

  • Focus Sash: Focus Sash makes setting up Nasty Plot much easier, at the cost of power.

  • Life Orb: While it makes Chi-Yu even more vulnerable to priority moves, Life Orb is otherwise an excellent wallbreaking item, notably giving Chi-Yu a better matchup against stall teams.

Alternate EV Spreads

  • 24 HP / 12 Def / 220 SpA / 252 Spe with Timid or Modest: If using Substitute, this spread prevents Garganacl with 4 Attack EVs from breaking a Terastallized Chi-Yu's Substitute with Salt Cure. Note that Body Press and Earthquake will still break the Substitute unless using the correct Tera Type.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Chi-Yu's poor defensive typing can make it fairly easy to revenge kill, so having Terastallization free gives Chi-Yu much more KO opportunities beyond cooking slower threats.

  • Fire: Tera Fire makes Overheat an insane wall-breaking move, with Life Orb threatening to OHKO Blissey after a boost!

  • Ghost: Tera Ghost covers Chi-Yu's Fighting-type weakness and helps against Extreme Speed and Quick Attack, making it much harder to stop its sweep.

  • Grass: With Tera Grass, Chi-Yu can threaten to OHKO Primarina after a boost in addition to resisting Urshifu-R's Aqua Jet.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy gives Chi-Yu a helpful Fighting-type resistance and a better match-up against powerful Dragon-types like Dragonite and Roaring Moon.

  • Dark: With Nasty Plot and Life Orb, Tera Dark Chi-Yu is capable of OHKOing even the most specially defensive Annihilape with Dark Pulse!

  • Water: Tera Water lets Chi-Yu deal with opposing Chi-Yu more comfortably.

Feesh (Offensive Wallbreaker).description:
• Overheat hits extremely hard and can 2HKO even the bulkiest of Pokemon. Fire Blast and Flamethrower can be used to KO foes without Chi-Yu suffering a Special Attack drop, with Flamethrower having perfect accuracy.
  • The only reason to run Timid over Modest is to outspeed Jolly Great Tusk, Jolly Annihilape, and fast Iron Treads with Special Defense investment.
  • Tera Fire allows Chi-Yu to turn 2HKOs to OHKOs, for example OHKOing opposing Chi-Yu with Overheat. Tera Fire also lets it 2HKO any prominent special wall, including Toxapex, Blissey, and Ting-Lu, OHKOing them with sun.
  • Choice Specs Chi-Yu is a wallbreaker, suited best for offensive teams. Koraidon is an excellent teammate because it sets sun and pivots Chi-Yu in with U-turn. Koraidon and Chi-Yu also threaten each other's checks, like Koraidon threatening Blissey and Garganacl and Chi-Yu threatening Skeledirge and Dondozo.
  • Helpful teammates are those that can get Chi-Yu in safely and force out its few checks. Corviknight and Koraidon are noteworthy examples, pivoting into special walls such as Ting-Lu. Lures such as Heavy Slam Koraidon and Great Tusk, which beat Dachsbun, and Psyshock Flutter Mane, which beats Toxapex and Blissey, are also appreciated teammates.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Fire Blast is Chi-Yu's strongest STAB move without any stat drops. Psychic is an alternative that 2HKOes common switch-ins such as Dachsbun and Toxapex. Overheat facilitates revenge killing, hitting even Pokemon that resist it such as Koraidon hard, and is a better midground play.
  • Memento serves as a way to facilitate sweepers like Swords Dance + Flame Charge Koraidon that Chi-Yu is usually paired with.
  • Tera Fire powers up Flamethrower and Overheat to nuclear levels, turning 2HKOs against Pokemon such as Koraidon into OHKOs. Tera Dark nullifies Chi-Yu's Stealth Rock weakness while making Dark Pulse 2HKO Dachsbun and Toxapex. Tera Grass should only be used with Tera Blast; it gives Chi-Yu nice resistances to Ground and Water and allows Chi-Yu to OHKO Great Tusk and 2HKO Ting-Lu after Spikes damage.
  • Choice Scarf Chi-Yu is a revenge killer best suited for offensive teams.
  • Pokemon that can get Chi-Yu safely into the field, such as Koraidon, Miraidon, and Corviknight, are excellent teammates for it. Koraidon also sets up sun, further boosting Chi-Yu's Fire-type attacks.
  • Ting-Lu and Glimmora can set entry hazards to guarantee some 2HKOs, such as against opposing Ting-Lu.

Nasty Plot.description:
• Nasty Plot Chi-Yu can threaten to KO foes it couldn't otherwise, such as Ting-Lu and Blissey. Overheat hits extremely hard and threatens to OHKO Ting-Lu at +2. Flamethrower is valuable for its perfect accuracy.
  • A Modest nature alongside Life Orb lets Chi-Yu OHKO Ting-Lu at +2. Heavy-Duty Boots can be used instead to give Chi-Yu more opportunities to switch in, but the loss of power is notable.
  • Chi-Yu fits best on offensive teams with Pokemon such as Cyclizar and Grimmsnarl that can facilitate its setup. Sticky Web support from Masquerain is also useful, as it lets Chi-Yu outrun Pokemon like Koraidon and Miraidon and KO them at +2.
  • Chi-Yu's best partner is Koraidon, since it sets up sun, can safely bring Chi-Yu into play with U-turn, and threatens Blissey. Other good partners are special attackers that benefit from special walls being neutered by Chi-Yu, such as Miraidon, Flutter Mane, and Gholdengo. Great Tusk is also greatly appreciated, as it can remove Stealth Rock and threatens Blissey and Ting-Lu for Chi-Yu. Chi-Yu can deal with Corviknight and Dondozo in return.

• Chi-Yu's solid offensive stats combined with Beads of Ruin make it a powerful wallbreaker in the tier, with its unresisted STAB combination threatening out key Pokemon such as Necrozma-DM, Zacian-C, and Lunala. However, Chi-Yu's mediocre Speed tier means it is easily revenge killed by Pokemon like Marshadow and Palkia-O, especially since it is quite frail, meaning it needs team support to position itself safely, so Sticky Web structures are needed for it to thrive.

  • Fire Blast allows Chi-Yu to OHKO offensive Necrozma-DM and 2HKO Dragon Dance Arceus-Ground unboosted while also OHKOing Extreme Killer Arceus after a Nasty Plot boost. Flamethrower has less power but improved accuracy.

  • Black Hole Eclipse enables Chi-Yu to OHKO Double Dance Primal Groudon, Palkia-O, and Mega Salamence unboosted while also allowing Chi-Yu to OHKO Ho-Oh, defensive Primal Kyogre, Zacian-C, and defensive Eternatus after a boost, greatly benefitting it in wallbreaking opposing balance teams.

  • Taunt allows Chi-Yu to stop status conditions such as Toxic poison and paralysis from Pokemon such as Ho-Oh and Giratina-O, letting it wallbreak more comfortably. Overheat lets Chi-Yu break through Chansey after hitting it with boosted Black Hole Eclipse, as well as giving Chi-Yu a greater offensive presence outside of Nasty Plot, letting it OHKO Marshadow and defensive Necrozma-DM after a layer of spikes, although the latter is not guaranteed.

  • Chi-Yu is a very strong attacker, so a lot of the time its presence alone can threaten out Pokemon like Necrozma-DM, enabling either free damage or a Nasty Plot boost. Chi-Yu should be careful with its Z-Move, since it's ideally used to target Pokemon such as Ho-Oh or defensive Eternatus, rather than using it wastefully against Pokemon such as Marshadow or Mega Mewtwo Y. In a situation where Chi-Yu cannot use Nasty Plot reliably, using Black Hole Eclipse unboosted is still quite powerful, as the chip damage alone is enough in some situations where a teammate can clean up walls like Ho-Oh, Eternatus, and support Arceus formes.

  • Chi-Yu works best on hyper offense structures that revolve around Sticky Web, meaning setters such as Shuckle and Smeargle are greatly appreciated; the latter also comes with the benefit of removing entry hazards with Mortal Spin for Chi-Yu, since it cannot hold Heavy-Duty Boots, while they both can set additional hazards such as Stealth Rock or Spikes which help Chi-Yu reach important damage thresholds.

  • Teammates that can threaten out specially defensive walls such as Ho-Oh, Eternatus, and Arceus-Fairy are greatly appreciated by Chi-Yu since it can wallbreak easier, so teammates such as offensive Primal Groudon, Necrozma-DM, and Marshadow are good for this; these Pokemon also appreciate Chi-Yu breaking through physical walls like opposing Primal Groudon, Zygarde, and support Arceus formes.

doublesou.overview: Chi-Yu poses itself as one of the most menacing special attackers in DOU, with its high Special Attack, near unresisted STAB combination, and Beads of Ruin allowing it to hit the majority of the metagame extremely hard. Beads of Ruin also not only indirectly makes Chi-Yu hit harder but also empowers its special attacking teammates, with Iron Bundle and Gholdengo in particular being excellent partners due to their ability to either overwhelm shared checks like Ting-Lu or outright beat some of Chi-Yu's checks, such as Garchomp for the former and Glimmora for the latter. Furthermore, Chi-Yu has very good Speed, allowing it to naturally outspeed a considerable portion of the metagame. However, Chi-Yu is not without glaring weaknesses, as its HP and Defense are absurdly low, which leaves it vulnerable to common priority moves such as Palafin's Jet Punch and Dragonite's Extreme Speed. In addition, despite Dark / Fire being a good type combination offensively, it leaves Chi-Yu vulnerable defensively, as its weaknesses to Ground-, Rock- and Water-type moves in addition to Stealth Rock compromise its ability to switch in and fire off more attacks. Finally, Pokemon such as Glimmora, Ting-Lu, and Garchomp have the ability to potentially switch into Chi-Yu and threaten it out, with Ting-Lu's Tablets of Ruin being a particular annoyance due to it offsetting Beads of Ruin. However, it is important to note that Chi-Yu's strength is still to the magnitude that it can 2HKO all the aforementioned Pokemon under the right circumstances.
doublesou.comments:
Other Options

EV investment into Chi-Yu's HP and Defense allows it to survive a significant number of moves it would normally be OHKOd by, notably Dragonite's Extreme Speed, while a Modest nature can be used on both sets to further increase the amount of damage Chi-Yu can do overall. However both options can cut into Chi-Yu's Speed, with the former also potentially lowering the amount of damage Chi-Yu can do depending on the amount of investment.

Choice Scarf.description:
• Heat Wave allows Chi-Yu to pick off Pokemon like Choice Scarf Gholdengo and Chien-Pao, as well as being a good method of spreading damage.

  • Dark Pulse can hit Ghost- and Psychic-types like Dragapult and Armarouge, as well as Pokemon that resist Fire-type moves, like Glimmora.

  • Flamethrower and Overheat both give Chi-Yu the ability to focus its damage on a singular Pokemon, with Overheat being significantly stronger but far more punishing than Flamethrower.

  • Snarl is useful for spread damage when both Pokemon on the field can take Heat Wave, as well as supporting its team.

  • Choice Scarf lets Chi-Yu outrun almost the entire tier, allowing it to either threaten out Pokemon like Dragapult and Chien-Pao and pick off weakened targets.

  • The EV spread and a Timid nature both maximizes the number of Pokemon Chi-Yu can outspeed along with its damage output.

  • Tera Fire allows Chi-Yu to pick up KOs it normally wouldn't be able to otherwise, such as Amoonguss with Heat Wave, while Tera Ghost grants an immunity to Fake Out and Extreme Speed, blocking two common methods to stop Chi-Yu, as well as making it immune to Fighting-type moves, which it would normally be weak to, like Drain Punch from Iron Hands.

All Out Attacker.description:
• Heat Wave provides excellent spread damage severely threatening Steel- and Grass-types like Gholdengo and Amoonguss while still being able to scorch neutral targets.

  • Dark Pulse hits several Pokemon that resist Heat Wave, such as Glimmora, as well as Ghost- and Psychic-types like Armarouge and Dragapult hard, as well as just being a solid STAB move

  • Flamethrower and Overheat deal more damage to a single target than Heat Wave, which can allow Chi-Yu break past Pokemon it normally wouldn't be able to, such as Ting-Lu. Overheat allows Chi-Yu to deal an insane amount of damage, accomplishing feats such as OHKOing Tera Normal Dragonite, while Flamethrower is weaker than Overheat by a significant margin but doesn't have the Special Attack drop and imperfect accuracy.

  • Snarl provides a secondary spread attack that can hit deceptively hard, in addition to debuffing the opposing team, while Tera Blast can be utilized with Tera Grass in order to give Chi-Yu an option to hit Pokemon like Palafin and Iron Bundle. Protect should only be used with Life Orb, but can keep Chi-Yu safe for a turn while a teammate either repositions or sets speed control to assist it.

  • Choice Specs and Life Orb both boost Chi-Yu's damage output to absurd levels, with the former allowing Chi-Yu to switch moves in exchange for the recoil and loss of power.

  • Tera Fire exponentially increases the strength of Fire-type moves for Chi-Yu, while Tera Grass patches up Chi-Yu's weakness to Water-type moves, and Tera Ghost prevents Fake Out and Extreme Speed from slowing down or picking off Chi-Yu, in addition to turning the Fighting-type weakness to an immunity.

Attack Booster.description:
• Outrage is Roaring Moon's most powerful STAB move against neutral threats like Hisuian Goodra, while also hitting other Dragon-types such as Raging Bolt and Walking Wake super effectively.
  • Knock Off hits both Psychic-types, such as Iron Crown, and Ghost-types, such as Skeledirge and Spectrier. Importantly, it removes the item from foes such as offensive Hoopa-U, which would otherwise KO Roaring Moon.
  • Acrobatics is a powerful move to hit foes such as non-physically defensive Ogerpon-W, bulkier Volcarona sets, and Fighting-types such as both Urshifu formes.
  • Substitute allows Roaring Moon to safely avoid a knockout from Draco Meteor users, such as Haban Berry Raging Bolt and non-Choice Band Hisuian Goodra. It further allows Roaring Moon to avoid stat dropping moves from foes such as Pecharunt.
  • Alternatively, Dragon Dance can be used to secure the knockout against bulkier foes, such as Weakness Policy Metagross, Annihilape, and bulkier Ogerpon-W sets.
  • The EV spread lets it survive a Focus Blast from Modest Hoopa-U, allowing it to beat all Hoopa-U sets by using Knock Off. The Speed EVs outspeed maximum Speed Ogerpon-W.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

A set with Dragon Dance, Jaw Lock, Taunt, and Roost, in tandem with Shed Shell and an alternate EV spread of 112 HP / 116 Atk / 96 Def / 184 Spe can also be used as more of a niche setup sweeper option. Jaw Lock is able to trap bulky Pokemon on switching in, such as Toxapex and Gliscor, and then Roaring Moon can afflict them with Taunt in order to prevent them from using Haze or Toxic to stop it, thus making them ideal targets to set up on. Shed Shell is used because Jaw Lock traps the user as well, allowing Roaring Moon to freely switch out if it traps an unideal target. The given alternate EV spread allows Roaring Moon to outspeed Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Gholdengo at +1 while also allowing it to beat Gliscor one-on-one. Iron Head can also be used over Roost and Taunt in order to defeat Pokemon that can easily deal with Knock Off and Earthquake such as Galarian Weezing and Iron Valiant.

Choice Scarf (Dragon).description:
Choice Scarf allows Roaring Moon to outspeed and defeat threatening foes to Dragon-type teams such as Choice Specs Greninja and Flutter Mane. Knock Off aids Roaring Moon in removing items from Pokemon that can reliably switch into it such as Heavy-Duty Boots from Corviknight and Leftovers from Great Tusk while also obliterating Gholdengo as well as a prominent threat in Flutter Mane. Iron Head allows Roaring Moon to combat Fairy-type Pokemon that are able to switch into both of its STAB moves such as Iron Valiant, Enamorus, and Alolan Ninetales. U-turn allows Roaring Moon to retain momentum in battles by pivoting out of common switch-ins such as Skarmory, Hippowdon, and the aforementioned Corviknight.

Choice Specs Kyurem forms a great offensive core with Roaring Moon, as it can reliably take out Pokemon that switch into Roaring Moon easily, such as the aforementioned Steel- and Ground-type physical walls in Skarmory, Corviknight, Great Tusk, and Hippowdon. In return, Roaring Moon grants Kyurem safe entry against passive Pokemon with U-turn while also taking out faster Fairy-type threats such as Flutter Mane and Iron Valiant. Archaludon is a great defensive teammate for Roaring Moon, as it is able to sponge physical attacks from Ogerpon-H, Meowscarada, and Scizor, while Roaring Moon is able to take out threatening special attackers that can take advantage of Archaludon like Gholdengo. Archaludon also provides entry hazard support in Stealth Rock while also threatening Bisharp and Meowscarada with Body Press. Dragapult is another offensive teammate capable of spreading status in Will-O-Wisp, neutering threats such as offensive Great Tusk and Hisuian Samurott, which alleviates pressure on Roaring Moon's breaking capabilities. Hisuian Goodra is another defensive teammate that pairs well with Roaring Moon, as it can readily take special Ice- and Fairy-type attacks from speedier threats like Choice Scarf Greninja and Choice Scarf Flutter Mane while also being able to phaze setup sweepers such as Dragon Dance Dragapult with Dragon Tail.

Dragon Dance (Dark).description:
With Dragon Dance, Roaring Moon becomes an oppressive sweeper capable of taking on many threatening Pokemon at +1 such as Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Iron Valiant, and non-Choice Scarf Greninja. Knock Off is Roaring Moon's strongest STAB move, which also helps remove items like Leftovers and Heavy-Duty Boots from their holders, such as Landorus-T and Corviknight, respectively, which allows Roaring Moon to muscle past and sweep them more easily. Earthquake allows Roaring Moon to hit defensive foes that can otherwise wall it even at +1, such as Toxapex and Torkoal. Roost allows Roaring Moon to retain HP and set up further if needed, while Taunt can be used to stop foes such as Mandibuzz and Toxapex from neutering Roaring Moon with status moves, such as Toxic and Haze.

Ting-Lu also pairs nicely with Roaring Moon, as it is able to provide support in its colorful access to entry hazards, which aid in Roaring Moon's sweeping capabilities, while also being able to stomach Fairy-type attacks from Iron Valiant and the aforementioned Flutter Mane and hit them back with Heavy Slam. Sableye, in tandem with Knock Off and Will-O-Wisp, is able to help make progress against bulky Pokemon that generally shrug off Roaring Moon's attacks such as Skarmory and Corviknight while also providing an invaluable Fighting immunity. Additionally, Prankster paired with Encore allows Sableye to deny setup sweepers such as Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta and Dragon Dance Gouging Fire. Choice Scarf Meowscarada is able to outspeed the likes of Dragapult and Choice Scarf Latios and OHKO them with Knock Off to alleviate pressure on Roaring Moon. Choice Specs Greninja, with its plethora of coverage options, aids the Fighting-, Dragon-, Ground-, and Flying-type matchups, which Roaring Moon can struggle with immensely on its own. Mandibuzz is another defensive option that pairs well with Roaring Moon, as it is the only consistent hazard removal that Dark teams have access to, which prevents Roaring Moon from getting chipped down over time while also providing pivoting through U-turn to allow Roaring Moon's safe entry if need be. Alolan Muk can be paired with Roaring Moon to help deal with strong Fairy-types such as Primarina and Choice Specs Iron Valiant. Bisharp is a necessary teammate, as it is able to handle Fairy-types that can neutralize Roaring Moon before a boost such as Flutter Mane and Hatterene, while Roaring Moon can deal with Fire-type Pokemon that threaten Bisharp such as non-Air Balloon Heatran and unboosted Gouging Fire. Lastly, Weavile can help weaken Ground-type foes that can wall Roaring Moon such as Hippowdon and Great Tusk while also revenge killing Dragonite and Meowscarada with Ice Shard, thus giving Roaring Moon more room to set up.

Offensive Support.description:
Set Details

  • Booster Energy Roaring Moon is a fast Tailwind setter that supports its Restricted partners. With Prankster Tailwind users like Tornadus and Whimsicott offering more immediate speed control, Roaring Moon sets itself apart by providing meaningful offensive pressure and role compression. Roaring Moon outspeeds and threatens to OHKO Calyrex-S with Knock Off while also comfortably taking Astral Barrage.
  • Acrobatics lets Roaring Moon threaten Pokemon like Rillaboom, Amoonguss, and Urshifu-R. Knock Off allows Roaring Moon to threaten Lunala and Calyrex-S while also disrupting foes by removing their items.
  • Booster Energy lets Roaring Moon outspeed threats like Calyrex-S and even Modest Choice Scarf Miraidon, allowing it to pressure them with Knock Off or set up Tailwind before they move.
  • The Attack investment allows Roaring Moon to deal maximum damage and still receive a Speed boost from Protosynthesis, with the remaining EVs allocated to HP.
  • Tera Flying is used to remove Roaring Moon's Fighting-, Dragon-, Bug-, and Fairy-type weaknesses, aiding it against Pokemon like Zamazenta-C, both Urshifu formes, and Flutter Mane. It also boosts the power of Acrobatics, allowing Roaring Moon to score OHKOs on Rillaboom and non-bulky Urshifu-R.

Teambuilding

  • Tera Fairy Lunala and Miraidon are difficult for Roaring Moon to remove, and they can OHKO it with Moonblast and Dazzling Gleam, respectively. Flutter Mane is also problematic because it can outspeed Roaring Moon with its own Protosynthesis boost and OHKO it with Moonblast or slow it down with Icy Wind.
  • Ice-types like Calyrex-I and Chien-Pao threaten Roaring Moon before and after Terastallization. Calyrex-I can also punish Tailwind from Roaring Moon by setting Trick Room and threatening an OHKO with Glacial Lance.
  • Zamazenta-C and Zacian-C wall Roaring Moon and can OHKO it with Body Press and Play Rough, respectively.
  • Incineroar is troublesome for Roaring Moon, weakening its damage output with Intimidate and Will-O-Wisp while taking little in return. Grimmsnarl limits Roaring Moon’s field impact with Reflect to reduce its damage and Spirit Break to threaten an OHKO.
  • Roaring Moon is commonly paired with Kyogre, providing Tailwind support to let Kyogre outspeed threats like Calyrex-S and Zamazenta-C and fire off full-power Water Spout. Roaring Moon threatens Grass-types like Rillaboom and Amoonguss that Kyogre struggles against.
  • Roaring Moon pairs well with Zacian-C, helping it outspeed threats like Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Miraidon with Tailwind. In return, Zacian-C covers for Roaring Moon's weakness to Fighting-, Dragon-, and Fairy-types like Flutter Mane and Miraidon with its STAB moves. Alternatively, it can be paired with Zamazenta-C, which also appreciates the speed control while handling Fairy-types as well as Incineroar, which Roaring Moon struggles against.
  • Urshifu-R benefits from Roaring Moon’s Tailwind support, capitalizing on its unprotectable attacks. Roaring Moon checks Calyrex-S, Rillaboom, and Amoonguss for it, while Urshifu-R pressures Chien-Pao in return.
  • Chien-Pao pressures threats like Miraidon, Raging Bolt, and Koraidon for Roaring Moon, while Roaring Moon handles Urshifu-R and Volcarona. Chien-Pao bolsters Roaring Moon's offensive pressure with Sword of Ruin, even allowing it to OHKO Ogerpon-H with Acrobatics.
  • Amoonguss can safely redirect Fighting- and Fairy-type attacks from Zamazenta-C and Zacian-C that would otherwise threaten Roaring Moon.

Roaring Moon is a fast Tailwind user that utilizes its Speed, access to Knock Off, and Tera Flying Acrobatics to spread damage and check some of the most defining threats in the metagame such as both Urshifu formes, Calyrex-S, and Rillaboom. Its Speed with the Protosynthesis boost allows it to get the jump on Choice Scarf users such as Urshifu-R and Landorus and either remove their items with Knock Off or set up Tailwind so that its partners can outspeed and secure a KO. Its high special bulk allows it to function as a good check to special attacking Restricted Pokemon such as Kyogre, Terapagos, and Calyrex-S, with it being able to remove Leftovers on Calm Mind Kyogre or Terapagos and threaten to OHKO Calyrex-S with knock off before it Terastallizes. With the Speed investment, Roaring Moon outspeeds Timid Chi-Yu and Landorus as well as Modest Regieleki with Protosynthesis activated, and the Attack EVs allow Tera Flying Acrobatics to almost always OHKO the Urshifu formes. Finally, the bulk investment allows Terastallized Roaring Moon to survive two Astral Barrages from Calyrex-S, two Heat Waves from Chi-Yu, or Tera Water Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R. Tera Flying allows it to threaten an OHKO on Amoonguss, Rillaboom, and Ogerpon-H with STAB Acrobatics.

Roaring Moon has seen numerous top placements alongside Calm Mind Kyogre, which appreciates its fast Tailwind and Knock Off support, ability to hit Grass-types super effectively with Acrobatics, and capability to check Calyrex-S. It has also been used on Calyrex-S and Galarian Weezing compositions to help them work better against mirror matchups and as a fast Tailwind setter for Speed-invested Calyrex-I. Roaring Moon has a very hard time taking on Miraidon structures, with Choice Specs Miraidon being able to OHKO Roaring Moon with Dazzling Gleam before it Terastallizes, Electro Drift or Volt Switch after it Terastallizes, and Draco Meteor regardless. Roaring Moon also struggles with Iron Hands, as Iron Hands is able to take a hit and OHKO it in return. Speed Booster Energy Flutter Mane outspeeds Roaring Moon and threatens to OHKO it with Moonblast or reduce its Speed with Icy Wind and Thunder Wave. Roaring Moon also struggles defensively against Chien-Pao and Calyrex-I, which are able to hit it super effectively even if it's Terastallized, and Zamazenta-C, which OHKOs Roaring Moon with Body Press and does not take much damage from Tera Flying Acrobatics in return. Roaring Moon’s weakness to Zamazenta-C and Miraidon makes Landorus one of its premier partners for its ability to OHKO both Restricted Pokemon. Additionally, Roaring Moon appreciates strong offensive pieces such as Urshifu-R and Ogerpon-H that are able to handle Flutter Mane, Chien-Pao, and Calyrex-I when paired with its Tailwind or offensive support. Roaring Moon can also function alongside more defensive pieces such as Rillaboom, Incineroar, and Amoonguss that provide support in Fake Out, Intimidate, or Rage Powder and Spore, helping Roaring Moon to more effectively set Tailwind and spread damage safely.

Dragon Dance Sweeper.description:
• Dragon Dance allows Roaring Moon to be an effective sweeper and helps reset Intimidate Attack drops, making it harder to slow down.

  • Roaring Moon utilizes Attack Booster Energy to activate Acrobatics, allowing for an OHKO on many centralizing Fighting- and Grass-types, such as the various Urshifu and Ogerpon formes, as well as Amoonguss after Terastalization.

  • After Terastalization, the bulk investment allows Roaring Moon to always survive a Tera Water-boosted Surging Strikes from Urshifu-R and a Thunderclap from a Special Attack Booster Energy Raging Bolt. The Speed investment allows Roaring Moon to outspeed Adamant Urshifu formes.

  • Roaring Moon uses Tera Flying to obtain a resistance to Fighting-type moves and to gain STAB on Acrobatics.

Tailwind Support.description:
• Roaring Moon utilizes Breaking Swipe to weaken the metagame's plethora of physical attackers such as the Ogerpon formes and Rillaboom.

  • Roaring Moon uses Speed Booster Energy to outspeed the entire unboosted metagame and get off Tailwind and Breaking Swipe more consistently.

  • The HP combined with the Defense EVs allow for Roaring Moon to take Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash at -1. The Special Defense EVs allow Roaring Moon to almost always survive unboosted Flutter Mane's Dazzling Gleam, as well as a Dragon Pulse from Raging Bolt. The Speed investment lets Roaring Moon outspeed Speed Booster Energy Iron Crown, as well as Adamant Dragonite under Tailwind,

  • Roaring Moon uses Tera Poison to obtain resistances to Fairy- and Fighting-type moves it was originally weak to, which is also a great neutral typing into the metagame.

Offensive Dragon Dance.description:
• With great special bulk, Speed, and Booster Energy juicing up one of its stats, Roaring Moon is a great choice for late-game sweeping!

  • Acrobatics: When powered-up by Tera Flying and Booster Energy, Acrobatics becomes a very powerful STAB that puts foes like Ogerpon-H and Urshifu-R in their places.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head is Roaring Moon's best shot of slicing up bulky Flutter Mane, and is an especially good fit with Tera Steel.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake lets Roaring Moon smack Incineroar, Archaludon, and Garganacl hard without resorting to Outrage lock-ins.

Other Options
  • Scale Shot and Loaded Dice: This is an alternative way to give Roaring Moon a Dragon-type STAB and a way to boost its Speed, though it makes it even more vulnerable to priority than usual.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - High: Roaring Moon's great special bulk is offset by its awkward typing, meaning Terastallization is highly recommended to aid its set up.

  • Flying: Tera Flying has fantastic synergy with Roaring Moon, giving it a vital Fighting resistance and soaring the power of Acrobatics into the stratosphere!

  • Steel: Tera Steel's good match-up against Fairy- and Dragon-types makes it a prime choice, with Flutter Mane in particular being a huge target.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is an excellent way to set-up on fearsome Dragon-types such as Gouging Fire and Choice Scarf Latios, and it gives Roaring Moon a vital Fighting-type resistance against otherwise troublesome foes like Urshifu-S. Speaking of Urshifu-S, Tera Blast with this typing also transforms Roaring Moon into a good check against it.

  • Fire: With Tera Fire, Roaring Moon gains a useful resistance to Bullet Punch and Fairy-type attacks. The Will-O-Wisp immunity helps too, but the Stealth Rock weakness does makes this a more niche option overall.

EV Spreads

  • 220 Atk / 36 Def / 252 Spe with Jolly: This spread gives Roaring Moon a Speed boost from Protosynthesis, making it a good revenge killer.

  • 4 HP / 252 Atk / 252 Spe with Jolly: This simple spread makes Protosynthesis boost Attack, perfect for unleashing brutal Acrobatics right off the bat!

Choice Attacker.description:
• It's great Speed and powerful STAB attacks make Roaring Moon a fearsome offensive pivot!

  • Outrage: Outrage is a risky move, but it excels at cleaning teams in the late game.

  • Iron Head: Iron Head is good coverage against bulky Flutter Mane and common Tera Fairy types like Dragonite and Gouging Fire.

  • Torkoal and Sun Teams: Roaring Moon functions perfectly fine on its own, but it also just so happens to be a fantastic option on Sun teams! If using this archetype, consider Torkoal, who can support Roaring Moon with Stealth Rock to make late-game cleaning even easier.

Other Options
  • Choice Scarf: Choice Scarf gives Roaring Moon the chance to get some shocking revenge kills against threats like Chien-Pao and Choice Scarf Urshifu-S, though its quite a bit more vulnerable to strong priority attacks compared to popular alternatives like Landorus-T and Gouging Fire.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: This Roaring Moon goes for immediate all-out strength, so its defensive typing isn't as key as other sets. Still, Roaring Moon's nerve-wracking weakness to Fairy coverage makes Terastallization a good idea.

  • Steel: Tera Steel gives Roaring Moon a good match-up against Fairy types like Flutter Mane with Iron Head, and the Stealth Rock resistances lets it pivot out with less consequences.
