Ogerpon-H also threatens foes that resist Glacial Lance like Zamazenta-C, Urshifu-R, and opposing Calyrex-I. Groudon also works particularly well with Ogerpon-H, threatening super effective damage on Incineroar and Raging Bolt with Precipice Blades, while bolstering Ogerpon-H's damage output with sun. Ogerpon-H can support Groudon by redirecting attacks from Rillaboom and Chien-Pao while also threatening Kyogre with its Grass-type STAB attacks, all of which are difficult matchups for Groudon. Powerful setup sweepers such as Calyex-S and Calm Mind Terapagos also make great use of Ogerpon-H. Ogerpon-H can help them set up by redirecting away powerful attacks such as Urshifu-S's Sucker Punch and Drain Punch from Iron Hands as well as disruptive moves like Amoonguss's Spore and Incineroar's Parting Shot. Ogerpon-H is also helpful offensively, as it can threaten otherwise problematic Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Urshifu-R with Ivy Cudgel and its Grass-type move of choice respectively.

Offensive.description:
• Horn Leech trades Wood Hammer's power for greater longevity.

  • Follow Me is by far the best third move on this Pokemon, but if the team does not require a redirector, Ogerpon-H can use Grassy Glide; if this is the case, it is almost always paired with Rillaboom to ensure Grassy Glide is a priority move. Alternatively, Stomping Tantrum allows it to hit opposing Fire-types such as Entei and Chi-Yu.

  • The Speed EVs allow Ogerpon-H to outspeed Modest Landorus and Adamant Urshifu-R. The Attack EVs with the Adamant nature allow it to OHKO Flutter Mane after Terastallization even when Ogerpon-H is Intimidated.

  • The bulk investment allows Ogerpon-H to live most Choice Scarf Urshifu-R's Tera Water Surging Strikes while having a favorable roll to survive Timid Landorus's Sludge Bomb.

Swords Dance.description: Ogerpon-H is an incredibly potent stallbreaker and sweeper in Ubers UU due to Mold Breaker and Swords Dance. Trailblaze allows Ogerpon-H to boost its Speed past that of usually faster Pokemon, such as Deoxys, Dragapult, Zacian, Choice Scarf Chi-Yu, and Choice Scarf Landorus. Power Whip and Horn Leech can be run as stronger Grass-type moves to hit Palafin and Great Tusk for super effective damage. Ivy Cudgel gives Ogerpon-H a strong, non-contact Fire-type STAB move to hit Magearna and Skarmory with while avoiding Rocky Helmet chip damage. Play Rough is for Dragon-types like Giratina and Reshiram that resist its STAB moves, whereas Knock Off is for general utility and hits Mewtwo and Lugia. Terastallizing Ogerpon-H gives it an Attack boost, letting it grab OHKOs on bulky neutral Pokemon like Zacian and Dialga without a Swords Dance boost. Ogerpon-H is best dealt with using offensive counterplay that takes advantage of its poor bulk, as Pokemon like Deoxys, Zacian, Choice Scarf Landorus, Chi-Yu, and Palafin can outrun and KO it. Defensively, almost nothing can take Ogerpon-H on, as Mold Breaker ignores Unaware, so only the likes of Moltres can safely handle it. Entry hazards are also a huge problem for Ogerpon-H, as it cannot hold Heavy-Duty Boots, meaning it will take significant chip damage when hitting the battlefield. Ogerpon-H especially appreciates support from Corviknight, which can help Ogerpon-H safely hit the field and remove hazards. Ogerpon-H also forms strong offensive cores with priority users like Rillaboom, Palafin, and Arceus formes due to them being able to eliminate the few faster threats in the metagame. Ogerpon-H also pairs uniquely well with Sticky Web Galvantula, as the foes' Speed drops let it move before everything in the unboosted metagame besides priority users, making it much more threatening.

All-out Attacker.description: Ogerpon-H is a fearsome wallbreaker and late-game cleaner in Ubers UU. Power Whip is a strong STAB option, hitting important damage thresholds on Great Tusk, Toxapex, and Arceus formes, but Horn Leech's healing effect can offset chip damage from entry hazards, making it a solid alternative. Play Rough hits Dragon-types like Giratina and Palkia-O hard. Trailblaze boosting Ogerpon-H's Speed allows it to outpace most of the metagame, notably Zacian, Mewtwo, Deoxys, and Arceus formes. Tera Fire boosts Ogerpon-H's damage meteorically, allowing it to OHKO Pokemon like Zacian, Landorus, and Palkia-O. Ogerpon-H can have issues breaking through Pokemon like bulky Arceus formes and Giratina without Terastalizing, as they can shrug off its coverage moves, so Pokemon that can break through these threats like Palkia-O, Zacian, and Ice Beam Mewtwo are excellent partners. Ogerpon-H's wallbreaking prowess makes it an excellent partner to late-game cleaners like Zacian, Chi-Yu, and Kyurem-W, which appreciate it beating Pokemon like Dondozo, Solgaleo, and Magearna that could otherwise stop their sweep. Ogerpon-H's also cannot hold Heavy-Duty Boots, as it is locked into using Hearthflame Mask, so hazard control from Great Tusk and Giratina is appreciated.

ALL STAR.description:
• With its great offensive presence and incredible ability in Mold Breaker, Ogerpon-H is one of the premier threats in Battle Stadium Singles.

  • Ivy Cudgel: Ivy Cudgel offers a consistent STAB move with an elevated critical hit rate, allowing Ogerpon-H to power through even foes that resist Fire.

  • Horn Leech VS. Trailblaze: Horn Leech provides a consistent Grass-type STAB move and a form of healing to assist in longevity; however, Trailblaze’s Speed boost can allow Ogerpon-H to take over games on the spot if given the chance.

  • Play Rough VS. Rock Tomb: Play Rough is good coverage for foes such as Dragonite and the Urshifu formes, as well as Pokemon that might try to use Tera Dragon to resist Ogerpon-H’s STAB combination. Rock Tomb doesn't hit as many Dragon-types, but in exchange offers speed control and is Ogerpon-H's best attack against Fire-types like Ho-Oh and Incineroar.

  • Swords Dance: Swords Dance boosts Ogerpon-H’s Attack to frightening levels, and thanks to Mold Breaker, it cannot be ignored by the likes of Unaware Dondozo.

  • Quick Attack: While difficult to run without giving up Swords Dance, Quick Attack is great for cleaning up late game with Embody Aspect.

Other Options

  • Knock Off: Knock Off provides team support with its item removal, removing pesky items like Porygon2's Eviolite and the rare Skeledirge's Ability Shield. It's coverage isn't as good as the other options though.

  • Encore: Ogerpon-H’s good Speed allows it to make decent use of encore to lock foes into utility moves, providing itself or its teammates turns to set up.

  • Substitute: Substitute when paired with Swords Dance is a huge help against Dragon Tail Archaludon, though this will come at the cost of coverage.

EV Spreads

  • 252 HP / 100 Atk / 92 Def / 60 Spe with Adamant: This spread outspeeds Iron Bundle after Trailblaze while avoiding a 2HKO from Focus Sash Chien-Pao's Sucker Punch; however, it will no longer outspeed Urshifu.

Tera Types

The Hearthflame Mask grants Ogerpon-H a Fire Tera type. When Ogerpon-H Terastallizes, it is given a new ability, Embody Aspect, Which boosts Ogerpon-H’s attack. However, it will no longer have access to Mold Breaker.

Bulky-pon.description:
• Ogerpon-H's incredible power in Embody Aspect, unique typing, and utility-laden movepool make it the crown jewel of bulky Fire-types!

  • Rock Tomb: Rock Tomb provides fantastic speed control and punishes common switch-ins like Dragonite and Ho-Oh.

  • Quick Attack: Quick Attack pairs beautifully with Embody Aspect to pick off weakened foes late-game.

  • Encore: Even without Swords Dance to set up with, Encore is still a great way to punish support moves from Pokemon that Ogerpon-H otherwise struggles with such as Archaludon and Tera Poison Garganacl.

  • Swords Dance: Even with this set's focus on bulk, Ogerpon-H is fully capable of charging through slower teams after a boost, with common stall team members like Dondozo being particularly juicy targets thanks to Mold Breaker.

  • Synthesis: Synthesis is Ogerpon-Hs most reliable form of recovery, sacrificing offensive utility for longevity.

Other Options

  • Taunt: Taunt is a good way to stop Stealth Rock from flying up from the likes of Ting-Lu and Archaludon, in addition to making Clear Amulet Dragonite switch ins easier to handle.

  • Power Whip: The accuracy can be a big issue, but in addition to greater power, it won't be blocked by Psychic Noise from Primarina and Lugia like Horn Leech

EV Spreads

  • Ogerpon-H is very customizable in terms of EVs, so only take these as examples. For more exact fine-tuning, feel free to experiment with our damage calculator!

  • 252 HP / 4 Atk / 60 Def / 36 SpD / 156 Spe with Adamant: This spread survives Adamant Choice Scarf Urshifu-R's Tera Water Surging Strikes while outspeeding the more problematic Adamant Punching Glove Urshifu-R. The Special Defense EVs give Ogerpon-H a high chance of surviving both Blood Moon and Vacuum Wave from Ursaluna-B that lack an offensive item.

  • 252 HP / 4 Atk / 156 Def / 36 SpD / 60 Spe with Adamant: This spread sacrifices some Speed to survive even Adamant Punching Glove Urshifu-R's Tera Water Surging Strikes while still usually surviving Blood Moon followed by Vacuum Wave from Assault Vest Ursaluna-B. The Speed investment outspeeds Modest Gholdengo, Jolly Breloom, and up to Timid Iron Bundle after Rock Tomb.

  • 236 HP / 212 Defense / 60 Spe with Impish: This extremely defensive spread sacrifices plenty of power and some reliability against Ursaluna-B, but makes Ogerpon-H so physically durable that even Jolly Focus Sash Chien-Pao will fail to 2HKO Ogerpon-H! The bulk also gives Ogerpon-H its 2nd-best ah shot at surviving Jolly Choice Band Tera Water Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes at around 69%, while the Speed EVs outspeed Timid Iron Bundle after being smacked by Rock Tomb's Speed debuff.

Tera Types

  • Embody Aspect: Ogerpon-H is locked into a Tera Fire, but it trades that and Mold Breaker in exchange for an Attack boost via Embody Aspect! This is perfect for cleaning up teams late-game and saving Ogerpon-H from opposing Ogerpon-H, but note that it completely nullifies Ogerpon-H's potential to check Urshifu-R rc and can open it up to being picked off by other Aqua Jet users like Basculegion and Primarina late-game.

almostanyability.comments:
Other Options

Other options on Swords Dance sets include U-turn to pivot out of bad matchups; Stomping Tantrum to punish grounded Fire-immune Pokemon switching into Ivy Cudgel; Play Rough to KO Dragon-types like Roaring Moon on the switch in; Trailblaze to serve as a surprise wincon; Superpower or Low Kick to nail immunity Kingambit and provide a midground for Ting-Lu, Roaring Moon, and Hisuian Goodra; or Synthesis to improve Ogerpon-H's longevity and trade on its decent special bulk. The most common other ability option is Magic Guard, which eliminates Ogerpon-H's entry hazard weakness and allows it to run Wood Hammer, but at the cost of significant power, especially since it cannot run Life Orb. Sword of Ruin provides a significant boost to Ogerpon-H’s coverage moves, but at the cost of a weaker Ivy Cudgel. All-out attacker sets can pick two of its plethora of other options, such as running both Knock Off and Rock Tomb, to weaken or eliminate a wider range of threats at the cost of not breaking through dedicated walls like Pecharunt as quickly. Trailblaze sets can serve as an alternative wincon against offensive teams, while Spikes can be run alongside Synthesis, U-turn, and/or Taunt to turn Ogerpon-H into an unusual hazard setter and stallbreaker that still has decent power.

Checks and Counters

Fire-Immune, Grass-Resistant Pokemon: Primordial Sea Zapdos and Well-Baked Body Corviknight and Gholdengo can stonewall Ogerpon-H's STAB moves and have reliable recovery, although Zapdos and Gholdengo can struggle with coverage moves and Corviknight and Gholdengo cannot check Turboblaze.

Pecharunt: Pecharunt can tank even a +2 Desolate Land Ivy Cudgel and seriously wound Ogerpon-H with Malignant Chain; it can also run Intimidate or Well-Baked Body to check it even harder. However, non-Fire-immune sets can still be OHKOed by a critical hit from +2 Ivy Cudgel, which has a high critical hit rate, and without Toxic poison from Malignant Chain, it will still lose switching into Swords Dance.

Entry Hazards: Ogerpon-H is vulnerable to all forms of entry hazards and not terribly hard to force out via revenge killers, so entry hazard setters greatly limit its longevity.

Swords Dance.description:
Ogerpon-H is a righteous bastard that you're lucky is limited to one ability and four moves, as it has an answer for all of your answers. Swords Dance- and Desolate Land-boosted Ivy Cudgel OHKOes every neutral wall frailer than Pecharunt, which is all of them, and doubly takes advantage of the ever-common Fluffy by searing its users with a non-contact Fire move. Turboblaze is an alternative that, while notably weaker into neutral targets and more susceptible to Primordial Sea, absolutely demolishes teams planning to check Ogerpon-H with Well-Baked Body. Power Whip handles the common Regenerator Water-types like Manaphy, Swampert, and Primarina while also offering more damage into common Ground-types like Great Tusk and Ting-Lu. Solar Blade and Wood Hammer can be considered for a more accurate Grass move, but the former's terrible matchup against Primordial Sea and the latter's recoil are generally worse trade-offs. The last move is highly customizable based on what your team needs to beat. Knock Off is the most common option to annoy Pecharunt and Well-Baked Body Gholdengo while still offering progress into Fire-immune threats, while Rock Tomb is a powerful option to nail Moltres and Primordial Sea Zapdos, both of which otherwise are solid answers to Ogerpon-H; Rock Tomb can also offer a handy Speed drop on aggressive switches in by Roaring Moon.

Ogerpon-H is an excellent wallbreaker that helps faster physical attackers like Roaring Moon and Zamazenta shine by cleaning up defensive staples like Great Tusk, Gholdengo, and Corviknight. These attackers can also get chip damage onto Pecharunt for Ogerpon-H. Ogerpon-H also pairs well with common special attackers like Latios and Iron Moth, as they draw in the RegenVest Water-types that it feasts on. Its single biggest limitation, however, is entry hazards; it is weak to Stealth Rock and Spikes, cannot run Heavy-Duty Boots, and generally cannot afford to run recovery, meaning it really needs reliable removal from Corviknight or Great Tusk to get multiple switches in. Depending on its last coverage move, it also does have some common answers like Moltres, Primordial Sea Zapdos, and Well-Baked Body Gholdengo. Teammates like immunity Corviknight and RegenVest Manaphy that can reliably switch into whatever Ogerpon-H cannot are strongly recommended.

Cudgel Bonk.description:
• Ogerpon-H uses Wood Hammer to deal huge damage, allowing it to OHKO Diancie and both Ursaluna formes. Horn Leech can be used instead to increase its longevity at the cost of dealing a lot less damage.
  • Ogerpon-H provides redirection, allowing its allies to set up or position safely. Ogerpon-H is particularly good at redirecting Spore from Amoonguss due to its immunity.
  • Focus Energy can be run over Follow Me to increase Ogerpon-H's offensive prowess. This allows Ivy Cudgel to always be a critical hit, letting Ogerpon-H ignore Attack drops from Incineroar's Intimidate and damage reduction from Alolan Ninetales's Aurora Veil.
  • When Ogerpon-H Terastallizes, Embody Aspect enables it to easily threaten Kyurem in snow through Aurora Veil with Ivy Cudgel, and it loses its weakness to Sludge Bomb from Landorus and Bleakwind Storm from Tornadus. Ogerpon-H is capable of OHKOing Landorus and 2HKOing Iron Hands and Cresselia with Ivy Cudgel thanks to Terastallization.
  • Ogerpon-H is primarily used as an offensive threat, capable of OHKOing prominent offensive and support Pokemon, such as Gholdengo, Rillaboom, Amoonguss, and Sinistcha.
  • Ogerpon-H synergizes well with Chien-Pao, since it can easily threaten Landorus and Tornadus, which Ogerpon-H is offensively threatened by due to their strong STAB move. Ogerpon-H threatens Steel-types Chien-Pao struggles against such as Gholdengo and Kingambit.
  • Ground-types such as Landorus and Ursaluna-B greatly appreciate Ogerpon-H's ability to threaten Rillaboom, which threatens both with its potent Wood Hammer and Grassy Glide. Meanwhile, both can easily dispatch Raging Bolt, which Ogerpon-H struggles against.
  • Dragon-type partners, such as Raging Bolt and Regidrago, appreciate Ogerpon-H KOing threats like Chien-Pao and Alolan Ninetales as well as common redirectors like Amoonguss and Sinistcha. Ogerpon-H's redirection utility additionally allows Raging Bolt to easily set up with Calm Mind. In return, Raging Bolt can easily dispatch Ogerpon-W, opposing Raging Bolt, and Roaring Moon, which threaten Ogerpon-H and are tricky for it to defeat. Meanwhile, Regidrago's Dragon Energy can remove Dragon-types that Ogerpon-H struggles to damage.
  • Ogerpon-H supports Steel-types like Gholdengo and Kingambit exceptionally well. Ogerpon-H threatens opposing Steel-types its teammates struggle to damage as well as Ground-types that threaten them like the Ursaluna formes. In return, Gholdengo provides a strong special offensive presence to complement Ogerpon-H's physical offense, and Kingambit dissuades Intimidate cycling from Incineroar thanks to Defiant.
  • Ogerpon-H works very well on a core of Gholdengo, Tornadus,and Regidrago, taking advantage of their offensive coverage and Tailwind support as well as providing its own offensive coverage as well as redirection.

Swords Dance.description:
Ogerpon-C can use Swords Dance to become a usable wallbreaker in the tier, wielding high-power moves and decent coverage options. Ogerpon-C finds ample opportunities to set up a boost, as its decent Speed tier and potentially helpful ability in Sturdy can often force switches. Ivy Cudgel is Ogerpon-C's main weapon, threatening even defensive Pokemon like Corviknight and Skarmory. For any Pokemon like Zamazenta or Garganacl that can handle Ivy Cudgel, Power Whip offers even higher power at the cost of a slight decrease in accuracy. With these two moves, a boosted Ogerpon-C threatens to OHKO or 2HKO almost everything in the tier, including common physical walls such as Landorus-T, Gliscor, Zamazenta, Alomomola, and Great Tusk. Power Whip also notably 2HKOes Unaware Dondozo, a common problem for other physical wallbreakers. Horn Leech is an option for a more reliable STAB move that gives Ogerpon-C longevity, letting it heal from chip damage to make use of Sturdy more effectively. Low Kick is a valuable coverage on common foes like Kingambit and Tera Normal Dragonite among others. Knock Off hits Gholdengo and Iron Crown while crippling walls like Galarian Weezing and Okidogi on the switch. Maximum Speed with a Jolly Nature is chosen to speed tie other Ogerpon and Iron Moth, as well as outspeeding Walking Wake, Ninetales-Alola, Iron Treads, and Enamorus. Ogerpon-C's Tera type is locked to Rock, which boosts Ivy Cudgel's power to ridiculous levels while also gaining a permanent +1 boost to Defense. For example, +2 Ivy Cudgel after Terastallization has a very high chance to OHKO maximum defense Skarmory and Corviknight after Stealth Rock damage, and it even gains a chance to OHKO defensive Gliscor from full health. While Ogerpon-C does lose access to Sturdy, Terastallization can still be a useful emergency button to boost Ogerpon-C's wallbreaking abilities or to avoid a timely revenge kill from moves such as Weavile or Meowscarada's Triple Axel.

Ogerpon-C functions best on offensive teams, which appreciate its ability to break holes in many common defensive structures so that its teammates can clean up later in the game. Common physical cleaners such as Zamazenta, Dragonite, and Kingambit appreciate their primary answers like Skarmory, Gliscor, and Dondozo being weakened and can help finish the job against Pokemon that can escape a one-on-one versus Ogerpon-C with their HP intact, like a defensive Gholdengo or Zamazenta. Ogerpon-C's main problem is its middling Speed tier versus other offensive threats, which can prevent setup opportunities. Opposing attackers such as Weavile and Darkrai threaten an outright OHKO, with Weavile even ignoring Sturdy, so Ogerpon-C appreciates teammates that can tank hits from these attackers such as Primarina and Zamazenta. Offensive utility Pokemon are also a problem, with foes such as Dragapult and Cinderace threatening to cripple Ogerpon-C with status moves like Will-O-Wisp or pivot out with U-turn for high damage. To handle this, Ogerpon-C appreciates teammates that can absorb or punish utility moves like Landorus-T, Corviknight, or Gliscor. Similarly, Gholdengo can OHKO Ogerpon-C with Make it Rain or cripple it with Thunder Wave while also being able to survive all of Ogerpon-C's main moves, so partners like Ting-Lu can be useful to switch in on and pressure Gholdengo. Finally, entry hazards pose an annoyance to Ogerpon-C, negating the benefits of Sturdy and causing unrecoverable damage, so hazard removal from teammates like Cinderace or Great Tusk can be helpful.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Rock

Play Rough is another good option over Superpower, as it hits Kommo-o and gets a guaranteed OHKO on Roaring Moon without a Swords Dance boost; however, it leaves Ogerpon-C without coverage for Steel-types. Knock Off can be used to hit Gholdengo, Jirachi, and create permanent progress by removing items. Low Kick can be used over Superpower as an alternative option that doesn't drop Ogerpon-C's stats while still threatening Steel types. Taunt allows Ogerpon-C to set up in front of Toxapex and prevents burns from Galarian Weezing.

Grass

Ogerpon-C can make use of Knock Off to disrupt Pokemon reliant on Leftovers for its teammates to beat later, as well as take care of Gholdengo on its own without help from Meowscarada. It is able to set Spikes to wear down incoming threats and defensive Pokemon over the course of a game. Play Rough is another option that can be used to take care of the Dragon-types that can annoy Ogerpon-C such as Walking Wake and Raging Bolt. Zen Headbutt can be used to beat opposing defensive Poison-types such as Amoonguss and Clodsire that can outlast Ogerpon-C otherwise. U-turn is another good choice to bring in teammates against the defensive switch-ins Ogerpon-C forces. Encore and Taunt are also both great disruption tools that allow Ogerpon-C to either boost itself or bring in a teammate like Calm Mind Sinistcha and set up with much ease. Ogerpon-C's vast coverage and disruption can be used in the fourth moveslot to complement its STAB moves; meanwhile, U-turn can also be used over Swords Dance to use Ogerpon-C as an offensive pivot.

Swords Dance (Rock).description:
Ogerpon-C is an excellent wallbreaker and setup sweeper for Rock teams, not only because of its neutrality to Ground- and Water-type moves, but also because it is able to outspeed and deal with threats like Great Tusk, Gastrodon, and Mamoswine. Sturdy allows Ogerpon-C to take a hit from and remove faster threats like Barraskewda, as well as Choice Scarf Great Tusk and Choice Scarf Galarian Zapdos after a Swords Dance. Ivy Cudgel deals with threats like Ogerpon-H and Enamorus while also OHKOing Dragonite and Heatran after a Swords Dance. Horn Leech is a good Grass STAB move, being able to hurt Ground- and Water-types like Quagsire and Ting-Lu and OHKO Walking Wake after a boost. Horn Leech's recovery is useful for extending Ogerpon-C's longevity and can let Sturdy be used again if it brings Ogerpon-C back to full HP. Superpower is a strong coverage move as it is able to deal with Steel- and Dark-types like Iron Treads, Archaludon, and Darkrai.

Choice Scarf Glimmora, with its colorful moveset, deals with faster threats that outspeed Ogerpon-C like non-Choice-Scarf Greninja, Kommo-o, and Iron Valiant. In return, Ogerpon-C deals with Azumarill and Ursaluna for Glimmora. Air Balloon Glimmora can switch into threatening Ground-type moves while taking on foes like Great Tusk, clear entry hazards with Mortal Spin to make sure Ogerpon-C's Sturdy isn't broken, and sets its own hazards to enable Ogerpon-C's sweep. Tyranitar sets up sand to allow Ogerpon-C to set up easier due to the Special Defense boost, allowing Ogerpon-C to survive a Draco Meteor from Choice Specs Walking Wake. Tyranitar also acts as a specially defensive tank for Ogerpon-C and deals with Flutter Mane, Dragapult, and Spectrier. Ogerpon-C aids Tyranitar by dealing with Landorus-T and non-Choice Scarf Hisuian Samurott. Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine is a strong wallbreaker, using Head Smash and Flare Blitz to break through walls like Gholdengo and Corviknight. Hisuian Arcanine appreciates Ogerpon-C being able to deal with pesky Water- and Ground-types like Belly Drum Azumarill, Landorus, and Sandy Shocks. Coalossal is a decent physical wall that can remove hazards, which prevents Ogerpon-C's Sturdy from breaking, and deals with Weavile, Bisharp, Scizor, and Corviknight. Coalossal also sets up Spikes to enhance Ogerpon-C's wallbreaking. Ogerpon-C takes care of Ursaluna and Manaphy for Coalossal. Iron Defense + Body Press Garganacl can act as a defensive stallbreaker, using Salt Cure to weaken impediments to Ogerpon-C sweeping, like Skeledirge, Dondozo, and Hisuian Goodra. Ogerpon-C shuts down Choice Band Mamoswine, which would otherwise destroy Garganacl. Lead Kleavor is another option that can set Stealth Rock with Stone Axe, potentially breaking a Focus Sash on Ceruledge, Breloom, and Ribombee that can hinder Ogerpon-C's sweeps otherwise. Assault Vest Diancie eases the Fighting and Dragon matchups by being able to take on Iron Valiant and Dragapult. Alolan Golem can trap and eliminate Steel-types such as Corviknight and Scizor for Ogerpon-C. In return Ogerpon-C destroys Ground-types like Quagsire and Mamoswine.

Swords Dance (Grass).description:
Ogerpon-C is a distinct pick on Grass teams that has its place over its other formes. Its Rock typing, coupled with its amazing Speed and offenses, makes it a formidable force, allowing it to nail any Flying- and Fire-type threats to Grass teams such as Galarian Moltres, Ogerpon-H, and Volcarona with the powerful and accurate Ivy Cudgel. Swords Dance can boost Ogerpon-C's Attack further, allowing it to beat Dragonite through Multiscale at +2 as well as brute force through Heatran if Ogerpon-C lacks Fighting-type coverage. Horn Leech is a great STAB move that allows Ogerpon-C to retain Sturdy by virtue of healing; however, Power Whip is another option if Ogerpon-C wants more power, such as to OHKO Iron Treads after a Swords Dance. Sturdy also allows Ogerpon-C to survive the likes of Choice Specs Greninja, Darkrai, and Ceruledge and retaliate with Ivy Cudgel. Trailblaze lets Ogerpon-C boost its Speed and outspeed the likes of Choice Scarf Enamorus as well as Speed tie Choice Scarf Iron Moth. Low Kick is an alternative choice to take care of pesky heavy Steel-types that Ogerpon-C is otherwise useless against, such as Heatran and Hisuian Goodra, but Superpower is an alternative choice that is more reliable against targets that are not heavy, specifically Archaludon.

Ogerpon-C appreciates help from its teammates to help beat down its checks and counters. Choice Scarf Meowscarada can take care of any Dragon-types in sight, such as Latios, Dragapult, and Roaring Moon, with its Protean-boosted Play Rough and Triple Axel, as well as remove Leftovers from Corviknight with Knock Off. In return, Ogerpon-C takes out Moltres for Meowscarada. Amoonguss and Hydrapple are great defensive partners, withstanding strong attacks from the likes of Sneasler and Iron Valiant for the former and Heatran and Cinderace for the latter; they can also retaliate with a variety of options and heal the damage off with Regenerator. Amoonguss is able to put Ogerpon-C's checks to sleep, as well as outright beat Iron Valiant with Sludge Bomb; it also comes with the added benefit of being able to remove Toxic Spikes, which allows Ogerpon-C to preserve its Sturdy. In exchange, Ogerpon-C beats Dragonite and Articuno, which trouble Amoonguss and Hydrapple. Hisuian Lilligant and Breloom are more great partners, both being able to boost and beat down Steel-types with powerful STAB Fighting-type moves, alongside having access to sleep and Upper Hand to catch Weavile off guard when it uses Ice Shard. Sinistcha is a great teammate that can be a wincon with Calm Mind after Ogerpon-C has weakened the opposition enough, and it is also able to beat down defensive threats that trouble Ogerpon-C such as Skarmory and Iron Hands. Serperior is another choice that can paralyze faster threats such as Flutter Mane and Iron Valiant with Glare, alongside providing passive healing to Ogerpon-C to maintain Sturdy via Leech Seed and being a threat with Contrary Leaf Storm if it gets going. Abomasnow is another partner that can set up Aurora Veil for Ogerpon-C, which provides it with ease of setup, as well as beat Dragon-types like Latias and non-Choice Specs Dragapult with Ice Shard. Lastly, Brambleghast is a great partner to remove entry hazards and retain Ogerpon-C's Sturdy, as it is unable to hold Heavy-Duty Boots, while blanking Tornadus-T and Zapdos's Hurricanes by virtue of Wind Rider. Brambleghast also has the added benefit of being able to set Spikes, which punishes the switch-ins forced by Ogerpon-C and helps it in knocking foes out.

Offensive Redirector.description:
Set Details

  • Ogerpon-C serves as an offensive threat with its strong STAB moves while providing redirection support paired with Sturdy, which guarantees Ogerpon-C can take a minimum of two hits, allowing for reliable redirection support in keeping its partners healthy. It also threatens Pokemon such as Chi-Yu, Tornadus, Kyogre, and Ho-Oh. Furthermore, Ogerpon-C mitigates Amoonguss and Brute Bonnet's effectiveness, as it is immune to Spore and can safely redirect Spore while ignoring Rage Powder, allowing it to maintain offensive pressure on their partners.
  • Power Whip is used over Horn Leech, as it is able to achieve OHKOs where Horn Leech would not, with examples including Kyogre and Urshifu-R. Power Whip also deals no recoil damage unlike Wood Hammer, which would break Sturdy. However, Power Whip's main drawback is its lack of accuracy, making it a less consistent attacking option compared to its alternatives. Follow Me's great synergy with Sturdy allows for reliable redirection, which gives Ogerpon-C's partner a safer opportunity to switch in or set up.
  • Terastallization can be a secondary supporting option if Ogerpon-C is not at full health, as removing its Grass Typing and gaining Embody Aspect would make Ogerpon-C able to wall specific foes like Ho-Oh, Tornadus, and Incineroar.

Teambuilding

  • Ogerpon-C struggles against opposing Steel-types such as Zamazenta-C and Zacian-C, which can easily threaten Ogerpon-C without taking any meaningful damage in return.
  • Urshifu-R can act as a check to Ogerpon-C, as Choice Scarf variants can easily OHKO it with Tera Water Surging Strikes or break Sturdy with U-turn. Iron Hands counters Ogerpon-C, threatening to break Sturdy with Fake Out and threatening it with a KO afterward with Drain Punch.
  • Ogerpon-C performs well on Calyrex-S and Terapagos teams; it can help Terapagos set up safely with Follow Me while also putting Koraidon in a difficult position, as Koraidon is KOed by Psychic from Calyrex-S if Koraidon doesn't Terastallize into a Fire-type, and it is KOed by Ivy Cudgel from Ogerpon-C if it does.
  • Incineroar has good synergy with Ogerpon-C in supporting their partners, as its slow Parting Shot allows Ogerpon-C to switch in safely without breaking Sturdy, and it also threatens Zacian-C with Flare Biltz. Incineroar is also able to mitigate Iron Hands's effectiveness with Intimidate, Fake Out, and Parting Shot, reliably keeping it in check.
  • Ogerpon-C is a good option on Lunala compositions, since it can provide Follow Me support to let Lunala set up Trick Room and allows for a fast mode without Trick Room on those teams. Miraidon also pairs well with Ogerpon-C, as Follow Me can redirect Ground-type attacks from Landorus and Ursaluna while also threatening them back with Grass-type attacks, allowing Miraidon to have more opportunities to use Electro Drift, which threatens Zamazenta-C and Urshifu-R.

Ogerpon-C is an offensive redirector, keeping allies such as Miraidon and Calyrex-I safe while eliminating common foes like Ogerpon-H, Tornadus, and Chi-Yu. Ogerpon-C has an excellent matchup into Amoonguss, as it can redirect Spore. Follow Me allows Ogerpon-C to keep its partner safe. Power Whip is used to do big damage to Pokemon like Groudon and Urshifu-R while keeping Sturdy intact. Alternatively, Horn Leech can be used to sacrifice power for recovery, allowing Ogerpon-C to reactivate Sturdy, while Wood Hammer is used for a burst of damage, but it breaks Sturdy.

Ogerpon-C struggles to damage common Steel-type Pokemon such as Zamazenta-C and Gholdengo, which can set up on it or threaten to bring Ogerpon-C down to Sturdy. Due to its great ability to redirect attacks, Ogerpon-C is commonly seen on hyper offense Tailwind or Trick Room teams supporting Restricted Pokemon like Miraidon and Calyrex-I. Ogerpon-C also adds a fast mode on Trick Room teams and has great damage output while removing problematic foes like Incineroar. Ogerpon-C pairs well with Koraidon, as it can effectively remove Pelipper and Tornadus and prevent them from disrupting Koraidon's weather. Ogerpon-C can also reliably redirect Spore from Amoonguss and threaten Calyrex-I regardless of Terastallization. In return, Koraidon can remove the plethora of opposing Steel-types. Some good partners for Ogerpon-C, aside from Calyrex-I, Miraidon, and Koraidon, are Whimsicott, Tornadus, and Farigiraf. Whimsicott or Tornadus can set Tailwind for Ogerpon-C to outspeed faster Pokemon like Flutter Mane, Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, and Chi-Yu, threatening to OHKO them. Finally, Farigiraf blocks Fake Out, letting Ogerpon-C deal a lot damage; Ogerpon-C can also help Farigiraf set Trick Room thanks to Follow Me support.

Redirection Support.description:
• Ivy Cudgel synergizes well with Ogerpon-C's Grass-type moves, hitting Fire- and Flying-types like Tornadus, Incineroar, and Chi-Yu.

  • Horn Leech provides Ogerpon-C with recovery, while Power Whip hits targets harder, threatening an OHKO on Urshifu-R.

  • Follow Me lets it redirect moves away from its teammates like Sucker Punch and Spore from Chien-Pao and Amoonguss, respectively.

  • Tera Rock bolsters Ivy Cudgel's damage, letting it guarantee an OHKO on Entei, and the Defense boost thanks to Embody Aspect can let it almost always survive Close Combat from Choice Scarf Urshifu-R.

Swords Dance.description:
Ogerpon-C's most prominent feature as a wallbreaker is its unique STAB combination, which, when paired with its complementary coverage, becomes very difficult to resist. Additionally, Ogerpon-C boasts a sufficient Speed tier to outspeed foes like Kyurem and non-Choice Scarf Kartana as well as powerful Cornerstone Mask-boosted attacks, which help it further threaten Flying-types such as Mega Charizard Y and Zapdos, Water-types such as Alomomola and Slowbro, and Ground-types such as Great Tusk and Ting-Lu. Swords Dance is able to take advantage of this, augmenting Ogerpon-C's Attack to astronomical levels that allow it to more easily take on checks such as Landorus-T and Corviknight while scoring a 2KHO on Gholdengo and an OHKO on Gliscor both with Power Whip. Superpower nails pesky Steel-types such as Ferrothorn and Melmetal, while the more niche Knock Off catches Gholdengo by surprise while also generally supporting its team by removing the items off of common switch-ins such as Toxapex and Landorus-T. A valuable ability in Sturdy allows Ogerpon-C to act as an advantageous crutch against dangerous sweepers such as Iron Valiant, especially if they have already set up.

Ogerpon-C shines brightest on offensive structures, where it's given as many wallbreaking opportunities as possible. Mega Scizor can support Ogerpon-C with Knock Off and make use of its impressive bulk to stave off revenge killers such as Choice Scarf Landorus-T and Mega Lopunny while also letting Ogerpon-C take care of threatening Fire-types such as Volcarona. Moltres's defensive profile also complements Ogerpon-C, providing pivoting with U-turn and deterring checks such as Iron Valiant and Gholdengo. Additionally, entry hazard removal from the likes of Terapagos, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T or hazard deterrents such as lead Mega Diancie and Iron Treads can help keep Ogerpon-C's Sturdy intact.

Pseudo-Sash.description:
• Ogerpon-C is a great Sturdy Pokemon, being much faster and having access to set-up moves compared to Archaludon, though using both together is certainly possible.

  • Horn Leech: While it has stronger Grass-type STAB moves, Horn Leech's recovery can bring Ogerpon-C back to full health while taking advantage of Sturdy.

  • Knock Off: This is Ogerpon-C's best option against Gholdengo.

  • Swords Dance and Encore: Swords Dance gives Ogerpon-C more use in late-game situations, with Sturdy making Swords Dance easy to use provided hazards have not been set up.

  • Encore: Encore greatly punishes support moves, especially Stealth Rock users since Ogerpon-C in team preview may make setting up hazards a priority for your opponent.

  • Quick Attack: While weak, Quick Attack gives Ogerpon-C the edge against Focus Sash foes with priority such as Urshifu-R and speedy Focus Sash users like Iron Bundle.

  • Rock Tomb: Dropping a foe's Speed with Rock Tomb can be a useful and unexpected way to revenge kill them after Ogerpon-C is KOed and prevents Terastallized Dragon Dance foes like Dragonite and Baxcalibur from setting up easily.

Alternate EV Spreads
  • 252 HP / 124 Atk / 68 Def / 4 SpD / 60 Spe with Adamant: This bulkier spread allows Ogerpon-C to survive Jolly Punching Glove Urshifu-R's Tera Water Surging Strikes and outspeeds Iron Bundle after Rock Tomb's Speed drop. It also naturally outspeeds Jolly Breloom, Modest Archaludon, and Modest Gholdengo, while also outspeeding Timid Iron Bundle after a Speed drop from Rock Tomb.
Other Options

  • Trailblaze: Ogerpon-C is not nearly as effective at sweeping with Trailblaze as Ogerpon-H, but it's still a potential win condition that can work well with Sturdy due to ease of setup.

  • Leech Seed: While Rock is not a good defensive typing, both Sturdy and Embody Aspect can make good use of Leech Seed's recovery.

  • Spikes: Sadly Ogerpon-C doesn't learn Stealth Rock, so this is the best alternative. While Spikes aren't bad, their failure to hit important floating Pokemon like Dragonite and Landorus-T means they aren't a perfect replacement for Stealth Rock.

Embody Aspect

Ogerpon-C is locked into a Rock Tera type, with the bonus of getting a Defense boost via Embody Aspect. While the Defense boost can be useful, note that Ogerpon-C loses Sturdy, which ironically can make it easier to OHKO! If needing the Defense boost, it's usually best to do this if Ogerpon-C is not at full health or needs a boosted Ivy Cudgel to KO a threat.

Setup Sweeper (Grass).description: Ogerpon-C is a formidable choice on Grass teams that holds its own over its Rock typing, coupled with it's amazing Attack and Speed, makes it a formidable threat to the Bug-, Fire-, Ice-, and Flying-types that threaten Grass teams such as Volcarona, Mega Charizard Y, Alolan Ninetales, and Tornadus-T with the powerful and accurate Ivy Cudgel. Swords Dance can boost Ogerpon-C's Attack to a threatening level, boosting Ivy Cudgel even more to break through formidable walls such as Corviknight and Celesteela. Horn Leech grants recovery for Ogerpon-C while also regaining Sturdy once it gets back to full. At +2, Superpower breaks through Steel- and Dark-type Pokemon like Archaludon, Heatran, and Hydreigon. Choice Scarf Meowscarada can handle any threatening Dragon-types for Ogerpon-C such as Roaring Moon, MegaAltaria, and Kommo-o with its Protean-boosted Play Rough while also removing Heavy-Duty Boots from Dragonite and Leftovers from Corviknight with Knock Off. Mega Venusaur is a defensive teammate for Ogerpon-C that can take threatening Fire- and Ice-type moves with its ability, Thick Fat, such as Meowscarada's Triple Axel. Ferrothorn is another defensive teammate that can provide entry hazard support and take on physical threats such as Melmetal and Weavile. Sinistcha is a great late-game setup sweeper that can become a wincon alongside Ogerpon-C with access to Calm Mind and Strength Sap. Breloom provides a form of priority with Technician-boosted Mach Punch and can put foes to sleep with Spore.

Swords Dance (Rock).description: With good stats and a part-Grass typing that lets it beat common threats to Rock such as Manaphy, Ursaluna, and Swampert, Ogerpon-C is a potent sweeper for Rock teams. Horn Leech is a STAB move that grants Ogerpon-C longevity, mitigating chip damage to more reliably trigger Sturdy, and it threatens common checks to Rock teams such as Gastrodon, Ting-Lu, and Rotom-W. Knock Off 2HKOes foes such as Sinistcha and Gholdengo while also removing Heavy-Duty Boots to make foes vulnerable to entry hazards. Superpower is an alternative option to hit Steel-types that could otherwise wall Ogerpon-C, and after a Swords Dance, it OHKOes Ferrothorn and, after Stealth Rock, Archaludon as well. Shuckle and Mega Diancie can set entry hazards to let Ogerpon-C more easily apply offensive pressure; the former's Sticky Web allows Ogerpon-C to outspeed foes such as Mega Gallade, Zeraora, and Mega Lopunny. As Ogerpon-C struggles with taking care of Fighting-types such as Kommo-o, Mega Lopunny, and Sneasler, partners like Mega Diancie and Iron Boulder, which can simultaneously take advantage of Shuckle's Sticky Web and offensively check these threats, pair well. Ogerpon-C can struggle with Steel-types as well, so allies that can more easily overwhelm them such as Hisuian Arcanine and Z-Crystal Iron Boulder are also appreciated.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Steel

Flash Cannon lets Archaludon deal with Iron Valiant and Enamorus, while also providing a consistent source of damage against Gliscor. However, Archaludon's teammates, like Gholdengo and Iron Treads, usually have these these threats covered, and they would rather Archaludon check Ceruledge or Azumarill instead.

Dragon

44 Special Defense EVs may be used to let Archaludon avoid an OHKO from Choice Specs Flutter Mane while still making it very likely that Archaludon survives Choice Band Excadrill's Earthquake. 56 Special Attack EVs can be invested to OHKO Enamorus with Flash Cannon, as Archaludon survives any one of Enamorus moves once, but decreased Defense investment can impair Archaludon's ability to be a strong physical wall. Archaludon has a variety of options for its fourth move, namely Thunder Wave to punish switch-ins like Primarina and Volcarona, Dragon Pulse to consistently damage opposing Dragon-types, and Metal Burst to get a surprise OHKO on threats like Flutter Mane, Ceruledge, and Hoopa-U. However, all these moves are usually inferior to the above-mentioned options.

Choice Scarf (Steel).description:
Choice Scarf Archaludon serves as a solid revenge killer and lure for threats like Hydreigon and Choice Specs Dragapult, which take advantage of Archaludon's defensive variant. Draco Meteor not only OHKOes these Dragon-types but is also powerful enough to OHKO Urshifu-R and Darkrai after minimal chip damage. Thunder Wave lets Archaludon limit threats such as Ogerpon-H, Keldeo, and Spectrier, preventing them from sweeping Steel teams. Flash Cannon OHKOes Iron Valiant and allows Archaludon to pick off Flutter Mane after some damage. Thunderbolt prevents Skarmory and Moltres from gaining free entry into Archaludon. Alternatively, Foul Play OHKOes Ceruledge and Ogerpon-H at +2 after Stealth Rock damage.

Since Choice Scarf Archaludon relies on surprise to bait the opponent, entry hazards need to be off the field to avoid revealing that it is not carrying Leftovers. Iron Treads can handle this with Rapid Spin and also serves as a fast teammate that deals with Landorus and Hisuian Goodra for Archaludon. Alternatively, a Choice Band Iron Treads set can be used to remove Iron Hands, Okidogi, and opposing Archaludon while also weakening defensive cores of Ground, Dark, and Poison teams for Archaludon to exploit. Gholdengo benefits from Archaludon providing speed control, allowing it to use more a powerful set like Choice Specs or Nasty Plot to punch holes in opposing teams, overwhelming Gliscor and Hisuian Goodra. In return, Gholdengo provides a Fighting-immune teammate and deals with Iron Hands and Galarian Slowking. Air Balloon Heatran can check opposing Heatran and sets Stealth Rock, which this Archaludon cannot. Heatran also deals with Ceruledge once its Air Balloon is popped, covering for Archaludon's inability to check it without defensive investment. Skarmory provides a Ground-immune, sets entry hazards, and serves as a wincon once special attackers like Dragapult and Hydreigon are baited and removed by Archaludon. Scizor and Bisharp appreciate Archaludon's ability to keep their checks, such as Skarmory, Moltres, and Hydreigon, at low HP or eliminated, and in return, they can clean through opposing teams and remove Flutter Mane and Gholdengo with their priority moves, respectively. Corviknight is an alternative Ground-immune teammate that provides Defog and pivoting in U-turn, which facilitates Archaludon's ability to tear through Dragon teams.

Physically Defensive (Steel).description:
Archaludon is the defensive glue for Steel teams, taking on threats such as Dragonite, Ogerpon-W, and Ceruledge. Draco Meteor lets Archaludon gain the upper hand against Dragon teams. Body Press complements Draco Meteor well by heavily damaging Hisuian Goodra, the main check to Draco Meteor for Dragon teams. Aside from this, Body Press also weakens Steel- and Normal-types such as Heatran and Blissey, which can comfortably take Draco Meteor. The synergy between Body Press and Stamina allows Archaludon to handle bulky threats like Ting-Lu and Gliscor effectively. Thunder Wave slows down threats like the Ogerpon formes, Keldeo, and Iron Valiant, which Archaludon can survive a hit from but cannot OHKO back, and also lets Archaludon take further advantage of the switches it forces. Stealth Rock lets Archaludon capitalize on forcing out physical attackers like Dragonite and Iron Boulder further. Alternatively, one can forgo Stealth Rock to broaden the number of targets Archaludon checks. Foul Play enables Archaludon to OHKO Ceruledge and dissuade Dragon Dance Dragonite from boosting further. It can also use Thunderbolt to revenge kill Azumarill and dissuade Skarmory from setting entry hazards against it. 52 Speed EVs let Archaludon outspeed Jolly Azumarill while using the remaining EVs to maximize Archaludon‘s bulk.

Archaludon's lackluster Special Defense is its glaring weakness, so specially defensive teammates like Hisuian Goodra, Heatran, and Empoleon are appreciated. Hisuian Goodra can trade blows with Raging Bolt and Primarina; Heatran provides an immunity to Fire-type moves that lets it check Volcarona and deal with Gholdengo, Spectrier, and Flutter Mane; and Empoleon provides Stealth Rock, checks Walking Wake and Heatran, and is able to Knock Off Choice Specs from Hydreigon. Gholdengo provides a Fighting immunity, prevents opposing teams from removing Stealth Rock that Archaludon sets, and can choose to utilize a specially defensive spread to improve the matchup against Dragapult and Keldeo. Gholdengo and Heatran can also choose to run more offensive sets, with Air Balloon Heatran putting opposing Heatran on a stalemate and Nasty Plot Gholdengo dealing with Ursaluna and Iron Valiant. Skarmory is a physical wall that complements Archaludon, as it swaps into predicted Ground-type moves from Excadrill and Great Tusk, sets Spikes to pair with Archaludon's Stealth Rock, and has Whirlwind to further chip down opposing teams and to phaze IronPress users like opposing Skarmory. Bisharp appreciates Archaludon's ability to check Dragonite and Encore Ogerpon-W, as well as the entry hazards Archaludon sets to set up and attempt to sweep Dragon, Water, and Dark teams late-game. Iron Treads can soft check Raging Bolt, remove entry hazards, pivot, and outspeed and remove Landorus and Garchomp with Ice Spinner in a pinch. Corviknight is an alternative Ground-immune teammate that loves Archaludon's ability to put a stop to Dragonite and Ogerpon-W, potentially overpowering Dragon and Water teams afterward when using a Bulk Up set.

Entry Hazard Support (Dragon).description:
Archaludon bridges the gap between offense and defense with its well-rounded stats that let it beat Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Dragon Dance Dragapult, and Bisharp for Dragon teams. Body Press pairs well with Stamina and lets Archaludon check Bisharp and Weavile. Flash Cannon pelts Fairy- and Ice-types like Hatterene and Froslass coming in on it, and it also deals enough damage to knock out Iron Valiant in a worst-case scenario. Stealth Rock chips down opposing teams and provides Dragon teams with more breathing room against threats like Enamorus and Swords Dance Ceruledge. The final moveslot is highly flexible and is mainly dependent on Archaludon's teammates. Protect is the most consistent choice, letting Archaludon rack up more Leftovers recovery and scout opposing Choice item users like Excadrill and Enamorus, while Draco Meteor lets Archaludon excel in the Dragon matchup, punishing physical attackers like Dragonite and physically inclined Dragapult that cannot deal with Archaludon. On the other hand, Roar takes advantage of Archaludon's ability to force out most physical attackers and defensive Pokemon and lets Archaludon further wear down opposing teams. Thunderbolt hits Skarmory and Toxapex, which would otherwise take advantage of Archaludon by setting up entry hazards, and chunks Azumarill enough to deter it from using Belly Drum. Stamina punishes weak attacks such as pivoting moves from Corviknight, Meowscarada, and Dragapult. The Defense boost also lets Archaludon overpower Ground-type attackers such as Gliscor lacking Swords Dance and Ting-Lu that cannot break through it after a few boosts. 52 Speed EVs let Archaludon outspeed Jolly Azumarill, allowing Archaludon to check these threats readily. The remaining EVs are used to make Archaludon as physically bulky as possible, notably allowing it to survive an OHKO from Choice Band Excadrill's Earthquake.

Although Archaludon can take physical hits with ease, it has trouble taking neutral special attacks, as it is 2HKOed by Choice Scarf Iron Valiant's Moonblast and Dragapult's Draco Meteor and outright OHKOed by Choice Specs Flutter Mane and Hydreigon. Because of this, Hisuian Goodra is a great teammate, as it sponges these attacks reasonably well, forming a great defensive core with Archaludon. Dragapult is immune to Fighting and OHKO Flutter Mane, Urshifu-R, and non-Choice Scarf Iron Valiant if using Choice Specs, and pivot in Archaludon against walls it can take advantage of like Ting-Lu and Blissey. Latios deals with Landorus and Enamorus with Ice Beam, and it can utilize a Choice Specs or Expert Belt set to break down types such as Poison and Ground that Archaludon struggles with. Latias is immune to Ground thanks to Levitate, deals with Fighting-types such as Keldeo and Okidogi, and provides Healing Wish, which gives Archaludon a second chance at walling Meowscarada, Mimikyu, and non-Superpower Ogerpon-W. Dragonite is immune to Ground by typing instead of ability, which helps against Excadrill. It can also make use of Multiscale to let it take on and revenge kill Enamorus and Ceruledge in a pinch, and it can utilize a Choice Band set to clean opposing teams with Extreme Speed after Archaludon has chipped them down. Raging Bolt deals with pesky Water- and Flying-types like Primarina and Enamorus with Thunderclap and also benefits from Archaludon's Stealth Rock.

vgc2025.comments:
Teambuilding

  • Archaludon's Electro Shot doesn't require a turn to charge while in rain, so Pelipper is a staple partner because of its ability Drizzle. Pelipper can help Archaludon deal with Fighting- and Ground-type threats such as Sneasler, Annihilape, Ursaluna, and Ursaluna-B with its STAB moves and provide speed control with Tailwind.
  • Basculeigon-M is a common Swift Swim Pokemon used with Archaludon, mainly due to its synergy with Pelipper. Basculegion-M offers immediate damage to an otherwise slow-paced core of Pelipper and Archaludon, and it can goad Rillaboom into using Grassy Glide into a Stamina Archaludon switching in.
  • Dragonite and Maushold commonly use multi-hit moves like Scale Shot, Population Bomb, and Beat Up. As allies, they can target Archaludon with these moves to instantly gain multiple Defense boosts with Stamina. Dragonite can also provide speed control with Tailwind and pressure targets such as Sneasler and Flamigo, which threaten Archaludon with Close Combat.
  • Sinistcha and Amoonguss can both heal and redirect dangerous Fighting- and Ground-type attacks away from Archaludon. Sinistcha offers immediate healing on a switch in and an additional layer of speed control in Trick Room, while Amoonguss's Spore is generally disruptive, and Pollen Puff heals Archaludon more than Hospitality and Life Dew from Sinistcha can. These two Grass-types also benefit from Pelipper's rain, as it reduces Fire-type damage.
  • Incineroar's Intimdate and Fake Out help with Archaludon's physical weaknesses to Sneasler and Ursaluna, and Knock Off removes items such as Assault Vest and Eviolite, which then allows Archaludon to better combat threats such as Porygon2 and opposing Archaludon.

Strategy Comments

  • Assault Vest Archaludon's goal is to gain stat boosts and then sweep with powerful Body Presses or STAB options. Archaludon's superb defensive typing makes it worthwhile to switch in on resisted hits to get a Stamina boost. It is particularly complementary with Pelipper, which resists Fighting and is immune to Ground, while Archaludon resists Pelipper's Electric weakness.
  • When boosted, Archaludon may have problems with Haze users, particularly Haze Dragonite, which often outspeeds bulkier Archaludon. While the common Loaded Dice set does not enjoy using Scale Shot on Stamina Archaludon, it can later remove all of Archaludon's accumulated boosts. Archaludon can hit Dragonite itself with STAB Dragon Pulse or Draco Meteor, as well as the common Tera Fairy Dragonite with Flash Cannon, though for clean KOs without boosts, Multiscale should be broken first.
  • Archaludon can be OHKOed by a strong Close Combat, the most common user of which is Sneasler. Strategies for dealing with Stamina Archaludon in this way involve either targeting around it for fear of giving it too many Defense boosts or chipping Archaludon enough to keep it in range of Close Combat even after a few boosts. Terastallization and utilizing Amoonguss or Sinistcha's redirection and healing are good defensive tools to combat this.
  • Special attackers, particularly Ursaluna-B and Tera Blast Fighting Porygon2, threaten Archaludon's more vulnerable Special Defense while not taking much damage in return. Archaludon's own Snarl can help keep these threats at bay, particularly when combined with Terastallization.
  • Changing the weather on Archaludon preparing an Electro Shot is a good way to reposition around it. Torkoal, Tyranitar, and Alolan Ninetales are the premier opposing weather setters of the format. Athough Archaludon itself can threaten all three with Body Press or an appropriate STAB move, their presence alone helps their partners, such as Charizard and Excadrill, handle Archaludon and other members of its rain core. Jumpluff and Whimsicott stand out as common users of Sunny Day, which prevents Archaludon from firing single-turn Electro Shots and has the added benefit of weakening any Water-types paired with Pelipper and Archaludon such as Basculegion-M. When facing these Pokemon, it is important to preserve Pelipper until opposing weather setters are dealt with.
  • Sturdy Archaludon is more straightforward to use, as it relies less on constant boosting in favor of utilizing one boost to its fullest. Opposing teams will aim to outspeed it, deal chip damage to get around Sturdy, then land a powerful move such as Sneasler's Close Combat or Ursaluna-B's Earth Power to KO it, so Tailwind from Pokemon such as Pelipper or Icy Wind from Alolan Ninetales can help Archaludon outspeed and KO such threats.

Assault Vest.description:
• Assault Vest patches up Archaludon's low Special Defense, and when this is paired with Stamina's Defense boosts and Electro Shot's Special Attack boosts, Archaludon can easily snowball.
  • Central to this snowball strategy is Electro Shot, as it allows Archaludon to simultaneously boost while threatening Water-types such as Basculegion-M and Dondozo. Body Press takes advantage of Stamina boosts, threatening other Assault Vest Pokemon and Dark-types such as Incineroar and Kingambit. Flash Cannon helps Archaludon deal with Fairy-types such as Alolan Ninetales and Whimsicott. Snarl is an option to help mitigate damage from special attackers such as Gholdengo, which may wall Archaludon outside of rain otherwise, and Ursaluna-B, as well as hampering opposing Archaludon should Body Press be ineffective due to Terastallization or redirection.
  • Dragon Pulse is a consistent STAB move, while Draco Meteor without boosts secures OHKOs against other Dragon-types such as Hydreigon and Dragonite without Multiscale, which Dragon Pulse misses out on without prior boosts.
  • Tera Grass allows Archaludon to avoid Spore and Rage Powder from Amoonguss, as well as resisting Ground-type moves from Ursaluna and Garchomp. Tera Bug grants a resistance to both Sneasler's Close Combat and both Ursaluna formes' Ground-type moves while maintaining neutralities to other types such as Ice, which is relevant against Porygon2 and Alolan Ninetales. Tera Fighting grants a resistance to Dark, denying Kingambit its chance to OHKO Archaludon before Stamina comes into play, while also powering up Body Press.
  • The EVs focus on making Archaludon bulky while allowing it to outspeed Modest Pelipper, and the rest is dumped into Special Defense to maximize value from Assault Vest.

Power Herb.description:
• With Power Herb, Electro Shot isn't as reliant on Pelipper's rain, allowing Archaludon to use it as a single-turn move once. While the rain is still useful to repeatedly use Electro Shot, Power Herb adds flexibility and doesn't require Pelipper to make an appearance before Archaludon can use Electro Shot. This flexibility and immediate power allows Power Herb Archaludon to actively deal more damage, whereas a bulkier Assault Vest set can sometimes need a turn or two of setup. Sturdy acts as a free Focus Sash, which lets Archaludon invest fully into its Speed and Special Attack.
  • Thunderbolt, combined with Tera Electric, turns Archaludon into a premier Electric-type attacker, threatening common Water-types such as Basculegion-M and Dondozo while not having to rely on Electro Shot for repeated Electric-type damage once Power Herb has been used. Draco Meteor's high Base Power and the hyper offensive nature of this set tend to make it the more appealing option; however, Dragon Pulse is a good option in case Archaludon needs to use its Dragon-type STAB move multiple times without losing the Electro Shot boost. Flash Cannon is another STAB option to use against Fairy-types such as Alolan Ninetales and Tera Fairy Dragonite.
  • Tera Stellar is an alternate option to Electric when Archaludon opts for Flash Cannon in particular, as Tera Stellar boosts both Electro Shot and its STAB moves on their first use. While Tera Electric is more useful for repeated boosted Thunderbolts, the Tera Stellar boost to Draco Meteor in particular is notable for letting Archaludon score OHKOs on bulky threats such as Ursaluna at +1.
  • A Timid nature allows Archaludon to outspeed key threats such as Gholdengo, while a Modest nature maximizes damage output. The latter notably guarantees OHKOs on bulkier Nasty Plot Gholdengo variants with Tera Electric Electro Shot and most Amoonguss with Tera Stellar Draco Meteor after an Electro Shot boost.

vgc2024.overview:
• Archaludon can utilize its above-average bulk, solid Special Attack stat, and great Ability in Stamina to check and OHKO threats such as Urshifu-R, Incineroar, and Raging Bolt.

  • Archaludon's access to Stamina and Body Press combined with its resistances and great physical bulk make it an amazing check to Pokemon such as Rillaboom and the Ogerpon formes and also allow it to act as a wincon.

  • Archaludon appreciates teammates like Amoonguss and Sinistcha that provide it with recovery through Pollen Puff and Hospitality, as well as Rage Powder for redirection. Rillaboom provides Fake Out support, as well as passive healing through Grassy Terrain and priority with Grassy Glide that discourages the opponent from leading with Urshifu-R. Dual screens from Grimmsnarl and damage reduction from Incineroar's Intimidate or Snarl are also useful for keeping Archaludon alive to stack Stamina or Electro Shot stat increases.

  • Archaludon fits well on rain teams thanks to its Grass and Electric resistances. It appreciates teammates such as Pelipper that can check opposing Ground- and Fighting-types like Landorus and both Urshifu formes; Pelipper's rain support also allows Electro Shot to charge in one turn, OHKOing Urshifu-R and Tornadus. Archaludon also functions well on Trick Room teams due to many of its checks being faster than it, such as both Urshifu formes, Landorus, and Chien-Pao running Sacred Sword. Farigiraf pairs notably well with Archaludon on Trick Room teams due to the protection from priority it provides and its access to Psychic Noise, which disables Iron Hands's Drain Punch.

Rain Sweeper.description:
• Archaludon's Defense EVs allow it to survive Adamant Choice Scarf Urshifu-R's and Urshifu-S's Close Combat, meaning it can take a hit, boost itself with Electro Shot, and OHKO Urshifu-R on the same turn, provided rain is currently active. The Special Defense investment prevents it from being 2HKOed by Special Attack Booster Energy Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

  • Archaludon does not particularly require Special Attack investment thanks to Electro Shot boosting this stat, but 36 Special Attack EVs with a Modest nature give Archaludon an extra point in Special Attack because of how stat calculation works.

  • 28 Speed EVs are to outspeed Choice Scarf Urshifu-R, Urshifu-S and Landorus-T when Archaludon is under Tailwind.

  • Draco Meteor and Electro Shot OHKO Pokemon such as Raging Bolt, Urshifu-R, and Tornadus. Flash Cannon OHKOes Flutter Mane after one Electro Shot boost, and Body Press is good to threaten an OHKO on Chien-Pao, and significant damage on Incineroar, especially after a Stamina boost.

  • Tera Grass gives Archaludon a resistance to Ground-type moves such as Landorus's Sandsear Storm and Earth Power, and immunity to Spore and Rage Powder. Meanwhile, Tera Fairy gives it a Fighting resistance and Dragon immunity to beat Urshifu and opposing Dragon-types respectively.

Archaludon is an excellent rain sweeper and wallbreaker thanks to the combination of its movepool, typing, and ability allowing it to threaten a large part of the metagame with super effective damage while withstanding a lot of damage thanks to Stamina and Assault Vest. Electro Shot allows Archaludon to increase its Special Attack while in rain and provides valuable coverage against Skarmory and Dondozo, and the combination of Body Press and Stamina allows it to deal damage to specially defensive Pokemon like Blissey and Dialga, which it would otherwise struggle against. Tera Fairy allows Archaludon to resist Fighting-type attacks and gives it a Dragon-type immunity, flipping the matchup against Pokemon like Palkia-O and Zacian. Tera Flying can be used instead, giving it a Ground-type immunity to avoid getting revenge killed by Landorus-I or Great Tusk, although this comes with the significant drawback of making it weak to Stealth Rock. The HP and Defense EVs allow Archaludon to take Close Combat from a +1 Zacian after one layer of Spikes, and 124 Speed EVs allow it to outspeed Palafin. Archaludon requires rain support to be at its fullest potential, which makes Pelipper the ideal partner with its access to Drizzle and U-turn to pivot Archaludon into the game. Strong Water-types like Palafin appreciate Archaludon's ability to defeat walls they struggle with such as Giratina and Toxapex. Archaludon struggles against faster Ground-types like offensive Great Tusk and Landorus, so Flying-types like Corviknight and faster offensive Water-types that can take care of them like Palkia-O and Barraskewda are excellent teammates. Additionally, Fighting-types like Zamzenta-C can give Archaludon trouble, so having Pokemon that can handle these threats like Giratina and Zacian is important. Archaludon is also very weak to hazards, making a hazard remover like Regieleki or Giratina being good teammate.

Assault Vest.description: • The given EV spread allows Archaludon to survive Earth Power from Landorus and outspeed Zeraora in Tailwind.

Rain Wallbreaker.description:
Thanks to Electro Shot, Archaludon becomes a staple wallbreaker for rain teams with huge snowball potential while possessing valuable defensive utility that turns it into a strong tank for the archetype. Its typing alongside Stamina and Assault Vest makes it difficult to take down both physically and specially, letting it accumulate boosts with Electro Shot and wallbreak with its offensive movepool more consistently while taking on the tier's offensive foes comfortably; it checks common threats to rain like Ogerpon-W and Zapdos and can even trade with and prevent revenge killing attempts from a huge slew of more threats, including Pokemon like Tapu Koko, Terapagos, and Weavile. Electro Shot also provides Archaludon with a strong neutral nuke against Steel-types like Gholdengo and Iron Crown that resist its STAB combination and neglect its Fighting coverage, but more importantly, an immediate and reliable way to nail bulky Water-types like Toxapex and Alomomola that can slow down the onslaught of rain-boosted Water-type moves from its teammates. Aura Sphere makes use of Electro Shot boosts and hits Kingambit and Ferrothorn hard, even ignoring the latter's Iron Barbs, but a Stamina-complemented Body Press can be considered instead to hit Blissey harder, drastically improving Archaludon's matchup against stall teams. Either Fighting-type coverage also hits other Steel-types like Heatran and Melmetal outside of rain and pressure Mega Tyranitar more than Flash Cannon, preventing it from replacing the weather more freely. 176 Speed EVs let Archaludon outpace neutral-natured base 75 Speed foes like Raging Bolt and Mega Scizor.

Archaludon's expertise makes it the perfect fit for rain teams and rain teams only. Pelipper is undoubtedly the best teammate, as it reliably sets the rain with Drizzle for Archaludon to use Electro Shot. Moreover, it pivots Archaludon in safely against switch-ins like Zapdos and Toxapex via U-turn and switches into troublesome revenge killers like Urshifu-R, Great Tusk, and Zamazenta. Offensive Water-types found on rain teams like Mega Swampert, Urshifu-R, and Barraskewda can keep up the pressure against the opposition; they appreciate Archaludon exploiting the aforementioned bulky Water-types that they can pivot it into while pressuring bulky Ground-types such as Gliscor and Ting-Lu that are otherwise tough to break through and keeping up with faster offensive threats like Mega Diancie, Garchomp, and Mega Medicham that can overrun Archaludon. Zapdos is a strong offensive threat in rain itself that can also handle Mega Lopunny, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T for Archaludon defensively, with its Static potentially allowing Archaludon to outspeed otherwise faster foes like Dragonite, Urshifu-R, and Kartana; together, they can also overwhelm shared checks like Gliscor and Ting-Lu. Ferrothorn and Iron Treads provide entry hazards to take advantage of Archaludon's forced switches and check Ogerpon-W and Zapdos, respectively, so it's not overwhelmed easily. Iron Treads and the aforementioned Pelipper can also provide hazard removal, keeping Archaludon healthy to let it fully make use of its hit-taking abilities. In return, Archaludon handles threats like Ogerpon-W and Hisuian Samurott for Iron Treads.

Defensive Support.description:
• Archaludon's magnificent typing, superb ability, and beautiful movepool make it a golden bridge to Stealth Rock in the BSS metagame!

  • Iron Head vs. Flash Cannon vs. Heavy Slam: Archaludon should always take advantage of its Steel-type STAB moves to whack Fairy-types. Iron Head has excellent synergy with Thunder Wave thanks to its flinch rate and easily 2HKOes most Flutter Mane. Flash Cannon sets risk getting set up on by Calm Mind Flutter Mane but deal more damage to Tera Fairy Pokemon like Calyrex-S and opposing Archaludon. Finally, Heavy Slam crushes all but the most bulky Flutter Mane but does poorly against heavy foes like Arceus-Fairy.

  • Body Press: Body Press works great with Stamina to make Archaludon a less passive threat.

  • Thunder Wave: Archaludon's decent Speed means it outspeeds almost anything that lacks a Choice Scarf after paralyzing them, which can be especially frightening when paired with Iron Head's flinch rate stacking with full paralysis.

  • Dragon Tail vs. Roar: Archaludon is a fantastic phazer that also happens to outspeed most other phazers. Dragon Tail is easy to recommend, being usable through Taunt and dealing extra chip damage, but Roar is required to force out Fairy-types and Pokemon behind Substitute.

Other Options

  • Mirror Coat: While it can be tricky to fit in, Mirror Coat on specially defensive Archaludon can cause huge upsets against foes like Flutter Mane and Calyrex-S.

  • Draco Meteor: Draco Meteor deals massive damage to opposing Dragon-types and Ursaluna-B that lack Assault Vest, but it's rather tricky to fit in without losing some utility or running a Speed-decreasing nature.

  • Rest and Chesto Berry: Rest and Chesto Berry give Archaludon even more time to rack up Defense boosts and also make Yawn foes like Dondozo and Hippowdon less momentum-killing. Both the move and item require giving up more generally useful slots, though.

EV Spreads

  • When using Sitrus Berry, make sure Archaludon's HP is an even number at Level 50 so that one hit by Ruination activates it. This can easily be done with 244 HP EVs.

  • 244 HP / 164 Def / 100 SpD Impish or Bold: This Sitrus Berry-optimized spread avoids a 2HKO from Timid Flutter Mane's unboosted Moonblast and also survives two hits of Earthquake from Jolly Landorus-T thanks to Stamina.

  • 244 HP / 252 Def / 12 SpD Impish or Bold: Maximizing Defense means it takes Adamant Choice Band Landorus-T to have a good shot of OHKOing Archaludon, with other Landorus-T variants usually failing to OHKO it, at the cost of a worse Flutter Mane matchup.

  • 244 HP / 12 Def / 252 SpD Careful or Calm: This specially defensive spread lets Archaludon almost always survive Modest Miraidon's Draco Meteor after Stealth Rock damage and has a good chance of avoiding a 2HKO from Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast with Sitrus Berry recovery.

Items

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry has excellent synergy with Stamina, letting Archaludon take on foes it normally wouldn't dream of, such as Landorus-T and Arceus with the correct EV spread!

  • Leftovers: Leftovers's gradual recovery rewards Archaludon that manage to get multiple Stamina boosts, making it even more difficult to take down than usual! This can usually be done by switching into a weak priority attack like Primarina's Aqua Jet.

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet is an effective tool against physical attackers, being especially helpful on Tera Flying Archaludon to force Tera Normal Dragonite to use Extreme Speed.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Archaludon's fantastic typing can make Terastallization a net negative, so make sure to Terastallize only if it's needed for the matchup.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy solidifies Archaludon against Urshifu-S and Chien-Pao, making Sacred Sword far less of a problem, and saves it from powerful Draco Meteors from foes like Miraidon.

  • Flying: Tera Flying fixes up its weakness to Ground- and Fighting-type attacks, which can save Archaludon from Ursaluna-B for a turn. Just note that losing its Blood Moon resistance could be detrimental in the long run without a boosted Body Press.

  • Water: Tera Water is Archaludon's best option against Urshifu-R, removing its Fighting weakness while allowing it not to worry about Surging Strikes ignoring Defense stages.

Pseudo-Sash.description:
• This Archaludon takes advantage of Sturdy to get around Item Clause for Focus Sash, making it a surprising offensive support Pokemon or revenge killer depending on the matchup!

  • Thunder Wave: Thunder Wave is especially brutal with Custap Berry, letting Archaludon fire off one last priority Thunder Wave to support an incoming teammate.

  • Electro Shot and Power Herb: Electro Shot's Special Attack boost when combined with Power Herb's recharge removal makes Archaludon far more difficult to wall, with offensive Gholdengo in particular being in KO range of Flash Cannon afterwards!

  • Heavy Slam VS. Mirror Coat: Heavy Slam OHKOes all but the bulkiest of Flutter Mane, giving Archaludon even more early-game power. Mirror Coat is the riskier option, since Archaludon must get hit, but it can lead to a shocking demise for many a special attacker!

  • Modest VS. Timid: Modest is preferred to get as much power out of Archaludon as possible, but Timid happens to outspeed Gholdengo and Adamant Urshifu formes.

Other Options

  • Steel Beam: Steel Beam is an insanely powerful kaboom to go out with, but Archaludon's reasonable bulk even when uninvested makes it a rather constraining move to slot in.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is Archaludon's strongest attack against Gholdengo but does little else, especially if using Power Herb and Electro Shot.

  • Rock Tomb: This Archaludon is fast enough to fully take advantage of the speed control Rock Tomb provides. While not as devastating as paralysis, it is less vulnerable to Lum Berry, Taunt, and Encore, in addition to breaking Iron Bundle's Substitute. Just make sure to use a Timid nature so Iron Bundle will be outsped after the Speed drop.

  • Dragon Tail or Roar: Phazing with such an offensive set may seem odd, but it makes Archaludon less passive after using Draco Meteor.

  • Metal Burst: Metal Burst is a seemingly less risky alternative to Mirror Coat, but its lack of negative priority doesn't bode well against slower special attackers like Ursaluna-B.

  • Naive with 0 IVs in HP, Defense, and Special Defense: Going this route is the most likely way to get Custap Berry to activate on Archaludon, but the bulk loss makes it less flexible overall.

Items

  • Custap Berry: Custap Berry gives Archaludon a pseudo-priority move in the situation it gets hit hard, giving it a chance to completely ruin gameplans or even revenge kill later in the game!

  • Jaboca Berry: This Berry guarantees that the first physical attack to hit Archaludon will deal damage to its foe, potentially ruining common Focus Sash leads such as Chien-Pao and Urshifu formes.

  • Sitrus Berry: Archaludon's great physical bulk means even if Sturdy is activated, it's capable of surviving resisted priority attacks from foes like Adamant Urshifu-R, Dragonite, and Entei while at 26% of its health.

  • Red Card: Red Card makes early-game setup foes like Dragonite much less of a worry when Sturdy is intact.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency: Very Low: Since this Archaludon is usually used in the early parts of the game to support the rest of the team, Terastallization isn't usually a good idea unless a matchup absolutely requires it.

  • Flying: A Ground immunity can come in handy against Landorus-T, a common early-game Stealth Rock setter that can give Archaludon some issues.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is a big surprise to powerful Dragon-type wallbreakers like Choice Band Dragonite and Choice Specs Latios.

  • Stellar: In the rare situation Terastallization is needed, Tera Stellar's one-time power boost for each attack could be situationally useful for cleaning up late-game.

Choice Specs.description:
• With a Choice Specs in tow, Archaludon becomes a surprising and powerful wallbreaker that can ruin the days of its usual defensive checks like Ting-Lu!

  • Thunderbolt: Thunderbolt is not only good coverage against Steel-types like Corviknight, but it also 2HKOes Assault Vest Primarina, an otherwise troublsome foe for other offensive Archaludon.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse 2HKOes bulky Gholdengo, and it even has a shot at OHKOing offensive Gholdengo. It also deals decent damage to uncommon Steel-types that are immune to Thunderbolt like in Excadrill and Iron Treads.

  • Steel Beam: Steel Beam is absurdly powerful, with even bulky Steel-resistant Pokemon like Scizor needing Assault Vest to avoid a 2HKO! This does come at the cost of ruining Sturdy by losing half of Archaludon's health, though.

  • Aura Sphere: While risky to be locked into because of Ghost-types, Aura Sphere deals plenty of damage to Chi-Yu and opposing Archaludon without committing to a Special Attack drop from Draco Meteor.

  • Dragon Pulse: Dragon Pulse is a less risky back-up to Draco Meteor, making the revenge killing of Dragon-types like Dragonite less risky.

  • Sturdy: While Stamina is potentially workable with Archaludon's good bulk, Sturdy is highly recommended for ensuing very few Pokemon can OHKO it without Stealth Rock support, making it far more difficult to check offensively!

  • Modest versus Timid: Modest's extra power is preferred if using Dark Pulse for a potential OHKO on offensive Gholdengo, but Timid is a reasonable consideration for outspeeding Adamant Urshifu formes, Timid Gholdengo, and Jolly Dragonite.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Archaludon focuses so much on offense that Terastallization is best for either dealing more damage or giving it useful immunities.

  • Stellar: Tera Stellar's one-time boost per type makes Archaludon a fearsomely flexible wallbreaker, with even support Landorus-T sets being OHKOed by Draco Meteor and Steel Beam!

  • Flying: Floating with Tera Flying is a strong way to punish attempts to revenge kill Archaludon with Ground-type attacks, with Landorus-T and and Ursaluna-B in particular being ripe targets. The Fighting resistance also comes in handy if Sturdy is broken by a weak attack.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy ruins strong special attacking Dragon-types like Choice Specs Latios, and it makes Archaludon a solid Urshifu-S check even when Sturdy isn't in play.

  • Dragon: Tera Dragon's defensive benefits aren't strong beyond resisting Ogerpon-H's STAB attacks, but a consistently powerful Draco Meteor makes it a good offensive choice.
