  • Steel: Tera Steel's Fairy resistance can save Archaludon from revenge kills if a weak attack has broken Sturdy, but its main use is for firing off an extremely powerful Steel Beam twice.

Assault Vest.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • Heavy Slam: Despite the Natures, Heavy Slam is a good idea for OHKOing all Flutter Mane except for extremely defensive variants.

  • 252 HP / 180 SpA / 76 SpD with Modest: This spread avoids a OHKO from Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Tera-boosted Moonblast.

  • 252 HP / 52 SpA / 204 SpD with Calm or Modest: This spread with Calm avoids a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast, while still letting Draco Meteor deal over 50% to most Ursaluna-B that lack Assault Vest. If surviving Ursaluna-B's Earth Power is the main concern, Archaludon can use a Modest nature instead with this spread.

Rain Sweeper.description: • 176 Speed outspeeds max Speed Modest Raging Bolt, while the Special Attack allows Archaludon to 2HKO Porygon2 with Electro Shot after starting at +1.

Physically Defensive.description: With Regenerator, a solid defensive typing, and high physical bulk, Archaludon acts as a good physical wall that can wear down the opposing team. Dragon Tail phazes setup sweepers like Iron Hands, Dragonite, and all Ogerpon formes, and Heavy Slam hits Fairy-types such as Scream Tail and Florges. Alternatively, Iron Defense benefits Body Press's damage output and renders Archaludon's matchup against physical setup sweepers better. As Archaludon forces switches with Dragon Tail, Stealth Rock further increases the chip damage it deals to the opposing team. Rocky Helmet lets Archaludon wear down pivots such as Barraskewda, Cinderace, and Roaring Moon. Archaludon covers a variety of physical attackers such as all Ogerpon formes, Roaring Moon, and Barraskewda, but it is overwhelmed by offensive wallbreakers like Great Tusk, Zamazenta, and Galarian Zapdos, so allies such as Fluffy Corviknight and Skarmory are much appreciated. Archaludon also appreciates Pokemon like Hisuian Electrode and the Ogerpon formes beating Swampert, which it can't make much progress against. Archaludon has poor Special Defense, which makes it vulnerable to special wallbreakers such as Heatran, Iron Moth, and Gengar, so it appreciates specially defensive allies like Blissey and Empoleon.

Offensive Entry Hazard Setter.description: Archaludon acts as a niche Stealth Rock setter that scares away common entry hazard removal options like Corviknight, Mandibuzz, and Great Tusk with the combination of Electro Shot and Draco Meteor. Furthermore, Electro Shot + Primordial Sea allows Archaludon to threaten to snowball at a moment's notice. Earthquake smacks Desolate Land Iron Moth and Heatran attempting to come in on Electro Shot, while Body Press chunks checks like Blissey and Volt Absorb Empoleon. Primordial Sea allows Archaludon to offensively counter Iron Moth and grants it a one-turn Electro Shot. Additionally, Archaludon's good typing and natural physical bulk allow it to take on Zapdos and all Ogerpon formes in a pinch, but it should never be relied on to check them. Archaludon greatly struggles with its lack of Speed; as a result, fast offensive pivots that can bring it in safely like Roaring Moon, Azelf, and Walking Wake pair well with it, especially considering its ability to force hazard damage on their switch-ins, like Corviknight, Empoleon, and Manaphy. Archaludon's low Special Defense and Speed cause it to be susceptible to special attackers like Walking Wake, Azelf, and Pixilate Scream Tail, making pivots that can safely switch in to them like Empoleon, RegenVest Manaphy, and Swampert good partners.

Physically Defensive (Dragon).description: With its secondary Steel typing, remarkable physical bulk, and access to a great ability in Stamina, Archaludon becomes an exceptional physical wall for Dragon teams, capable of handling foes like Meowscarada, Weavile, and Roaring Moon. Flash Cannon targets problematic Fairy-types like Mimikyu and Mega Altaria, in addition to OHKOing Iron Valiant and Mega Diancie. Body Press synergizes with Stamina, providing Archaludon with a way to threaten Steel-, Dark-, and Ice-types like Hisuian Goodra, Roaring Moon, and Cetitan. Stealth Rock wears down foes, aiding against offensive threats like Enamorus and Ceruledge. Thunder Wave punishes switch-ins by slowing them down, making it easier for teammates to revenge kill them. Foul Play allows Archaludon to eliminate Ceruledge as well as punish other physical attackers like Ogerpon-W and Mega Scizor. Lastly, Protect allows Archaludon to capitalize on Leftovers recovery and potentially scout against Choice-locked foes like Tapu Lele and Greninja. The EV spread allows Archaludon to outspeed defensive Great Tusk and survive Mega Diancie's Earth Power. Due to its low Special Defense, Archaludon is threatened by special attackers like Tapu Lele, Kyurem, Hydreigon, and Greninja, making Hisuian Goodra a valuable teammate that can handle these foes. Mega Altaria, Latias, and Latios are excellent partners for their ability to deal with Fighting-types like Mega Gallade, Kommo-o, and Keldeo. Latias and Latios also provide a Ground immunity and, along with Kyurem, can deal with Ground-types like Clodsire and Hippowdon; Garchomp, Kommo-o, and Raging Bolt are exceptional wallbreakers that help take out foes like Volcarona, Gholdengo, Ferrothorn, and Celesteela. All of these Pokemon also help Archaludon deal with Toxapex.

Offensive Nasty Plot.description:
Hydrapple serves as a solid balance breaker, using its bulk and offensive prowess to handle threats like Excadrill while also being scary for foes like Tornadus-T and Metagross once it has set up Nasty Plot. It also has Regenerator to heal off any damage taken while checking these threats, allowing it to potentially repeat this process later in the game. Fickle Beam is an alternative move over Draco Meteor so Hydrapple can avoid the Special Attack drop while having a chance to deal more damage than Draco Meteor, allowing it to maintain its Nasty Plot boosts and to remain a big threat after firing it off. However using Fickle Beam means Hydrapple can miss out on KOs against foes like Zarude and Tornadus-T if the boost doesn't activate. Earth Power provides coverage for Steel-types like Tinkaton and Heatran so that they cannot easily come in to cause issues for Hydrapple. Heavy-Duty Boots serves to make Hydrapple's healing from Regenerator more effective while improving its longevity by removing its vulnerability to entry hazards, as it commonly has to utilize its great typing to switch into powerful wallbreakers like Excadrill and Ogerpon. Maximum HP and 92 Defense lets Hydrapple avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Keldeo's Secret Sword as well as making it incredibly difficult for physical attackers to break, letting it better soak up U-turn from Scizor, Lokix, and Zarude as well as powerful hits from wallbreakers like Ogerpon-C or Excadrill so that it can more easily set up Nasty Plot. Tera Steel improves its matchup against Ogerpon-C while also giving it a Toxic immunity to help against Toxapex and Mandibuzz, a Flying resistance so it can set up Nasty Plot in front of Tornadus-T, and a Fairy resistance useful for dodging an OHKO from Choice Band Azumarill's Play Rough in case of emergency. Tera Fairy lets it set up more easily on Latios and opposing Hydrapple without gaining weaknesses to Quaquaval and Weavile. However, Terastallizing Hydrapple removes its beneficial resistances to Ground and Electric, making it tougher to handle Volt Switch users such as Sandy Shocks and Rotom-W.

Hydrapple acts as a solid wallbreaker for balance and bulky offensive playstyles, using its defensive profile to switch into foes that are offensively threatening or tough to break and then becoming a threat of its own. Slowking is a nice partner for it, forming a double Regenerator core that helps work around some problems for Hydrapple such as Tornadus-T and Tinkaton while acting a secondary Water resist in the event Hydrapple needs to Tera. Slowking also slow pivots to Hydrapple with Chilly Reception after soaking up a hit, allowing Hydrapple to either be a bigger threat due to having more HP or get its HP back from Regenerator more easiliy. Additionally, Slowking can use Thunder Wave against foes like Tinkaton and Mandibuzz to make them slower than Hydrapple, allowing it to more easily set up Nasty Plot. Cobalion is also a good teammate, defensively answering Scizor and Lokix, which can pose problems with their strong U-turn should they switch in on Hydrapple when it’s chipped. Hydrapple appreciates teammates that can help wear down Tinkaton into Earth Power range such as Lokix and Tornadus-T. It also appreciates Pokemon that can help pressure or defensively answer Flying-types such as Tyranitar or Rhyperior. Hydrapple appreciates Stealth Rock setters like the previously mentioned Cobalion and Rhyperior to get targets into range of its boosted attacks more easily. Sand teams appreciate Hydrapple's defensive profile in tandem with Regenerator, it can use an Eject Button to safely bring in Excadrill and act as check to opposing Excadrill and Keldeo, which can be scary for sand teams otherwise.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Hydrapple is a dangerous wallbreaker that provides a lot of defensive utility through its typing to answer threats like Excadrill, Sandy Shocks, and Ogerpon. Leaf Storm and Draco Meteor are powerful and spammable STAB moves despite the Special Attack drop drawback. Earth Power provides coverage against Steel-types like Tinkaton and Heatran. Hydrapple lacks coverage outside of Earth Power, so Fickle Beam is usually preferred to have a secondary Dragon-type STAB move that doesn't have the ramification of lowering its Special Attack. Similarly, Giga Drain is another option to provide a secondary Grass-type STAB move that doesn't force Hydrapple to switch out and provides it with more longevity. Regenerator helps Hydrapple answer Excadrill and the Ogerpon formes and provides ample opportunities for Hydrapple to get into a position to wallbreak by keeping it healthy across a match. The EV spread allows Hydrapple to outspeed Azumarill and Ursaluna while maximizing its damage output. Tera Steel should primarily be used for its defensive value to flip the matchup against threats like Latios, Weavile, and Scizor. Tera Fairy allows Hydrapple to combat Latios and opposing Hydrapple. However, Hydrapple should only Terastallize when necessary, as giving up its great defensive typing greatly hinders its matchup against Pokemon like Rotom-W and Excadrill.

Hydrapple fits best on offensive teams that can help it get in safely and take pressure off it being the sole answer to the likes of Excadrill and Ogerpon. Pivots such as Tornadus-T and Cobalion are fantastic partners for these reasons; the former forms a Regenerator core, while the latter can punish Pokemon like Scizor and Lokix with Thunder Wave, crippling them for Hydrapple to outspeed. Steel-types like Tinkaton and Metagross prevent Hydrapple from easily locking into its STAB moves, so Pokemon like Excadrill, Slowking, and Sandy Shocks can help check and apply pressure on them. Excadrill notably provides Rapid Spin support to prevent Hydrapple being worn down by entry hazards and can act as a check to Latios, allowing Hydrapple to preserve the option to Terastallize. Sandy Shocks can provide Spikes support to wear down Pokemon like specially defensive Tyranitar and Toxapex into OHKO range while also checking Tornadus-T. Assault Vest Tornadus-T is a fairly consistent pivot into Hydrapple, so it is essential to have means to overwhelm it. Tyranitar, Tinkaton, and Rhyperior can provide Stealth Rock support to restrict Tornadus-T's ability to pivot into Hydrapple while being great defensive checks to Tornadus-T. Tinkaton can also provide Knock Off support to help remove key items like Tornadus-T's Assault Vest. Other Knock Off users like Scizor and Lokix can also achieve this while also getting Hydrapple in against Pokemon they struggle to get through like Toxapex and Cobalion.

Nasty Plot.description:
Hydrapple is a strong wallbreaker courtesy of its incredible bulk, Nasty Plot, and Regenerator, making it a notable threat against balance and bulky offense playstyles while also providing valuable defensive utility, particularly as a check to the otherwise dangerous Ogerpon-W. It can find easy entry points and setup opportunities against common walls like Alomomola, Ting-Lu, and Garganacl and even muscle past more bulky foes like Gliscor, Moltres, and Clefable after. While Fickle Beam's lack of drawback is preferred, a niche alternative in Draco Meteor can be considered for the guaranteed high damage output, notably OHKOing threats like Dragonite, Ogerpon-W, and Zamazenta after minor chip damage at +2, at the cost of expending Nasty Plot boosts. Earth Power gives Hydrapple a way to hit Galarian Slowking and Steel-types like Gholdengo and Kingambit super effectively.

Heavy-Duty Boots is Hydrapple's preferred item to grant it resilience into entry hazards, letting it switch around freely to maximize Regenerator. However, on teams with sturdy entry hazard control, Hydrapple can run Rocky Helmet to further spread damage, particularly punishing U-turn attempts from Pokemon it checks like Rillaboom, Ogerpon-W, and Landorus-T as well as Flip Turn from Alomomola. Tera Poison improves its matchup against foes like Zamazenta, Iron Moth, Pecharunt, and Fairy-types like Iron Valiant and Clefable as well as gain an immunity to poison from foes like Toxic Gliscor. Tera Fairy also maintains the great matchup against Zamazenta while also giving Hydrapple a better matchup against Ice Spinner Great Tusk and Dragon-types like Dragapult and Raging Bolt. Tera Steel also provides a poison immunity and better matchup against Pecharunt and most Fairy-types similar to Tera Poison, but it also makes Hydrapple sturdier against Psychic-types like Galarian Slowking, Hatterene, and Hoopa-U. 12 EVs let Hydrapple outspeed Ting-Lu. At the cost of its defensive utility, Hydrapple can go for a more offensive route wih a spread of 244 HP / 252 SpA / 12 Spe and a Modest nature alongside Leaf Storm as its Grass-type STAB move and Life Orb to exacerbate Hydrapple’s wallbreaking niche; this lets it potentially OHKO even specially defensive Galarian Slowking and Gliscor at +2 as well as 2HKO Clodsire after minor chip damage, and works well with Regenerator to compensate for the item's recoil.

Hydrapple acts as a wallbreaker on balance and bulky offense teams, being able to punch holes in opposing balance teams due to its ability to punish passivity and its great matchup into common balance picks like Alomomola, Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Garganacl. Defensive pivots such as Galarian Slowking, Alomomola, Moltres, and Corviknight help enable and defensively reinforce Hydrapple, taking on threats such as Great Tusk, Iron Valiant, Primarina, and Weavile. Galarian Slowking and Alomomola in particular are amazing partners for it, forming double Regenerator cores on balance teams to outlast all of the offensive threats that threaten them while boasting excellent defensive synergy. Moltres answers Great Tusk more reliably, being able to punish its Ice Spinner targeted toward Hydrapple with Flame Body, which would allow Hydrapple to avoid getting 2HKOed by it.

Entry hazard setters like Gliscor and Ting-Lu are great partners because their hazards are essential for chipping foes into KO range for Hydrapple like Ogerpon-W and Assault Vest Iron Crown. Gliscor uses its combination of entry hazards and Knock Off to remove Heavy-Duty Boots from these Pokemon while baiting in Ogerpon-W for Hydrapple to respond to, causing it to take hazard chip every switch-in and putting it on a timer. Ting-Lu uses its gargantuan bulk to check Dragon-types like Dragapult and Raging Bolt for Hydrapple. Hydrapple also pairs nicely with offensive teammates like Kingambit, Great Tusk, Cinderace, and Iron Crown. Kingambit greatly appreciates Hydrapple being able to scare off Great Tusk from staying in and benefits Hydrapple by being extremely good at switching into and annihilating Air Balloon Gholdengo, one of Hydrapple's better switch-ins. Great Tusk itself is a good teammate for it, being able to keep hazards off in case Hydrapple gets its Heavy-Duty Boots removed by common threats like Rillaboom, Hisuian Samurott, and Gliscor while also being great into its most common check in Galarian Slowking. Cinderace also keeps hazards off with Court Change, baits in Water- and Ground-types for Hydrapple to easily set up on, and reduces the need for Heavy-Duty Boots, giving Hydrapple more room to run a more powerful item to make progress like Life Orb, since its removal can't be blocked. Hydrapple also baits in Steel-types like Gholdengo and Corviknight for Cinderace to quickly dispose of. Assault Vest Iron Crown is able to switch into Pokemon like Iron Valiant, Kyurem, and Hatterene for Hydrapple, while Hydrapple matches up well into Hisuian Samurott and Ting-Lu, two Pokemon Iron Crown does not like taking on. Tinkaton and Hydrapple can also work in tandem with each other, since Tinkaton is a Pokemon that can set Stealth Rock and check Kyurem and Darkrai for Hydrapple, two special attackers that carry Ice-type moves to quickly dispose of Hydrapple, while Hydrapple is able to check Pokemon that can wall and threaten Tinkaton like Iron Treads, Tera Water Garganacl, and specially defensive Heatran. Rillaboom pairs decently well with Hydrapple on teams that take advantage of Grassy Terrain, powering up Hydrapple's already hard-hitting boosted Giga Drain while providing it with additional passive recovery every turn it is active. Hydrapple also finds a niche on sand teams as an answer to Water- and Grass-types that are able to consistently threaten Excadrill and Tyranitar, which are staples of this archetype. It sets itself apart from its competition for its role as a bulky Grass-type because, unlike Sinistcha and Chesnaught, Hydrapple has a much more notable offensive presence and greater longevity thanks to Regenerator.

With fantastic natural bulk and Special Attack, Hydrapple is a powerful setup sweeper and wallbreaker capable of easily remaining healthy throughout games thanks to Regenerator. Its typing enables it to sit on defensive staples like Slowbro, Celesteela, and Rotom-W as well as offensive threats like Iron Boulder, Zeraora, and Aegislash. Draco Meteor is typically preferred alongside Dragonium Z to maximize Hydrapple's power, allowing it to break past defensive answers in Celesteela, Blissey, and Scizor at +4, but Fickle Beam can be used as a more accurate attack that lets Hydrapple retain its boosts after multiple uses. Leaf Storm allows Hydrapple to OHKO Keldeo and Iron Boulder unboosted and threaten Dragon-immune options like Enamorus and Mega Gardevoir. Recover bolsters Hydrapple's already impressive longevity, notably allowing it to more reliably defeat Celesteela and Scizor, but Earth Power is also a great option to decimate Iron Moth attempting to switch in and eliminate Aegislash and Magnezone more easily. While Dragonium Z is preferred to help Hydrapple heavily damage potential checks like Mega Venusaur on the switch in, Heavy-Duty Boots can be utilized on teams without entry hazard control options so Hydrapple can more reliably utilize Regenerator to remain healthy. Eject Pack is a niche option on offense teams that can maintain momentum, turning Hydrapple into an one-time offensive pivot. Hydrapple's EV spread allows it to outspeed and OHKO Magic Guard Clefable with Leaf Storm at +2 and survive a neutral Iron Moth Sludge Wave from full health while not being 2HKOed by Choice Scarf Mienshao's Close Combat. Thanks to its offensive prowess and defensive profile, Hydrapple can be used on nearly any team, helping offense teams shore up matchups against dangerous threats like Iron Boulder and Zeraora while helping defensive teams break through opposing defensive structures. While Hydrapple can take on nearly any threat from full health, options like Draco Meteor Mega Latias and Buginium Z Scizor threaten to KO it from high, if not full, health. Strong Steel-type teammates like Scizor, Celesteela, and Aegislash can help against these threats, and Hydrapple can work in tandem with them to wear down shared checks like Celesteela as well as handle threats like Zeraora and Rotom-W that tend to switch in against them. Hydrapple also appreciates offensive pivots such as Mienshao and Iron Moth to bring it in against their defensive checks like Buzzwole and Slowking; Hydrapple can handle these as well as faster threats like Iron Boulder and Zeraora for them. Magnezone is also a notable partner for Hydrapple; given that the two most reliable Hydrapple checks are Scizor and Celesteela, removing them can often allow Hydrapple to decimate the remainder of the opposing team. Hydrapple also covers Magnezone's Ground-type weakness, easily switching into Hippowdon and Excadrill.
12 Speed EVs allow Hydrapple to outspeed Ting-Lu.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Additional coverage moves like Hydro Pump and Body Press fill gaps on Assault Vest sets, which allow Hydrapple more effectively pivot into special attacks while making use of Regenerator.

Special Wallbreaker (Dragon).description:
Hydrapple is a good potential wallbreaker for Dragon teams with its two amazing STAB moves in Giga Drain and Fickle Beam, both of which can ease the matchup against Water and Ground teams. At +2, Giga Drain keeps Hydrapple healthy in battle while also hitting pesky Water- and Ground-types like Swampert, Ursaluna, and Great Tusk. Fickle Beam after a Nasty Plot boost threatens Dragon-types such as Garchomp, as well as having a chance to dish out double the damage to land an OHKO on Dragonite. Earth Power can be run over Fickle Beam to threaten Fire-, Steel-, and Poison-types like non-Air Balloon Heatran, Iron Treads, and Sneasler. Substitute works great in tandem with Hydrapple’s decent bulk and HP, making it easy for Hydrapple to set up on Pokemon such as Great Tusk, Hippowdon, and Dondozo. The given EV spread allows Hydrapple to outpace Hisuian Goodra while also maximizing its bulk.

Garchomp is another good offensive Pokemon to pair with Hydrapple, as it can give entry hazard support while also checking Poison-, Steel-, and Fire-types for Hydrapple, like Alolan Muk, Hisuian Goodra, and Hisuian Arcanine. Hisuian Goodra is a great special wall to pair with Hydrapple, as it’s able to take hits from Flutter Mane and Greninja. Choice Specs Dragapult can help outspeed and defeat other threats to Hydrapple, such as Gholdengo, Flutter Mane, and Hatterene. With a +1 Thunderclap, Raging Bolt can take care of fast Flying-types that would threaten Hydrapple, like Enamorus. Latios is also a great teammate for Hydrapple, as it has access to Calm Mind and can help alleviate the matchup against Poison-types such as Galarian Weezing. Latias can be used as an alternative to Latios, as it can provide further utility in Healing Wish. Archaludon is a strong physical wall that can check Weavile and provide entry hazard support in Stealth Rock. In return, Hydrapple can take out troublesome Ground-types for the team like Quagsire, Great Tusk, and Ursaluna.

Special Wallbreaker (Grass).description:
Hydrapple provides a crucial neutrality to Fire-type attacks for Grass teams, making use of its amazing bulk, coverage, and ability to take on threats to its teammates like Heatran and Ogerpon-H. Draco Meteor is a far more common STAB option for Hydrapple due to its consistent BP, but Fickle Beam can tickle your gambling addiction if you're feeling lucky, with the added benefit of not reducing Special Attack. Earth Power makes for excellent coverage in the face of Fire-types like Ninetales and Cinderace, as well as Steel-types like Heatran and non-Air Ballon Gholdengo, while Giga Drain grants a nice secondary STAB to keep Hydrapple healthy, especially if it forgoes Recover for Substitute. Substitute takes advantage of passive foes like Toxapex and Quagsire to accrue Nasty Plot boosts. The given Speed EVs let Hydrapple outpace uninvested Tyranitar and Azumarill.

Hydrapple appreciates being paired with Meowscarada and Ogerpon-C for their coverage against Dragon- and Flying-types, and the latter of which can threaten Fire- and Ice-types as well. Ogerpon-H is a perfect answer to Steel-types like Scizor and Heatran, while also outputting a general exerting pressure that can even threaten Flying-types. Amoonguss provides a neutrality to Poison and Bug, taking on physical Bug-types like Scizor with Foul Play while dissuading other Bug-types like Volcarona and Frosmoth from switching in with the threat of Toxic. Amoonguss also has the added benefit of incapacitating shared threats between it and Hydrapple with Spore, like Mamoswine and Galarian Zapdos. Heatproof Sinistcha alleviates some pressure from Hydrapple as a sole Fire neutrality, while also being neutral to Bug like Amoonguss. Breloom is a powerful Focus Sash lead, trading with Dark-type threats like Weavile and Roaring Moon, and even Flying-types with both Spore and Rock Tomb. Rotom-C is a solid teammate thanks to its Flying neutrality, threatening Flying-types with Electric STAB and offering disruption with Trick and Will-O-Wisp. Iron Leaves and Hisuian Lilligant are both potent setup sweepers, making use of their great speed and coverage if given a single setup opportunity, augmented further by Spore support. Rillaboom is a great partner for Grass teams, offering passive healing with Grassy Terrain and picking off weakened foes with priority Grassy Glide. Brambleghast offers great hazard control, setting up Spikes and using Rapid Spin to support Hydrapple should it have its Heavy-Duty Boots removed.

Eject Pack Pivot.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • EV Spread: This survives Horn Leech followed by Ivy Cudgel from Terastallized Adamant Ogerpon-H thanks to a jump point in Defense, and is not OHKOed by Modest Choice Specs Gholdengo's Make It Rain.

  • 0 Speed IV: This is used in conjunction with Eject Pack and a Special Attack dropping move to pivot as late as possible, underspeeding Garganacl before it uses Curse in particular.

Nasty Plot (Speed).description:
Hydrapple is an absolute menace in the Speed slot thanks to great all-around stats that allow it to not only consistently set up with Nasty Plot but also soft check bigger threats such as Ogerpon-W and Eternatus. Fickle Beam is a slightly more consistent Dragon-type STAB move that has the capability to hit extremely hard, especially after a Nasty Plot boost, while Draco Meteor gives more initial power but is less consistent over a long period. Giga Drain allows Hydrapple to keep itself healthier in longer matchups, while Leaf Storm allows for more immediate damage at the cost of forcing Hydrapple out a lot more often. Earth Power is Hydrapple's best coverage move, as it nails Poison- and Steel-types such as Clodsire, Galarian Slowking, Necrozma-DM, and Gholdengo. Tera Steel lets Hydrapple check opposing Dragon- and Fairy-types like Eternatus and Arceus-Fairy while making it immune to Toxic from Clodsire and flipping its 4x Ice-type weakness to a resistance, which can aid with beating Kyurem-W one-on-one, while Tera Ground allows Hydrapple to gain STAB on Earth Power as well as dampening its Ice weakness. The given EV spread aims to maximize Hydrapple's bulk to help it check the likes of Ogerpon and Great Tusk while also optimizing its Speed from multiple different donations. 56 Speed EVs and a Timid nature lets it outspeed Landorus-T and uninvested base 90 Pokemon with base 90 Speed; Timid Kyogre, Kyurem-W, and their receivers with base 120 Speed; and finally, base 110s like the Ogerpon formes and Latios with a base 138 Speed donation. With base 138 Speed specifically, the latter EV spread is more efficient, as Hydrapple will outspeed Ogerpon and can therefore be more of an initial threat.

Hydrapple fits best on offense teams that tend to be a bit bulkier, so gods such as Arceus-Ghost and Zacian-C not only donate a fantastic Speed stat but also pair well with Hydrapple, as the former can pressure opposing Steel-types, while the latter can pressure opposing Dragon-types. While Hydrapple can sweep, entry hazards from the likes of Hisuian Samurott and Ting-Lu help Hydrapple have an easier time sweeping by softening up its checks. On that note, Knock Off users such as the aforementioned Hisuian Samurott and Clefable can rid foes of their Heavy-Duty Boots to allow the chip damage from the hazards to stick.

Nasty Plot (Grass).description:
172 Speed EVs lets Hydrapple outspeed Pelipper.

This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

vgc2024.overview:
• Gouging Fire is a solid offensive support Pokemon with a good defensive typing. Breaking Swipe and Burning Bulwark give it a great matchup against physical attackers such as Rillaboom and Chien-Pao.

  • Kingambit is one of the most prominent partners for Gouging Fire, because it prevents Incineroar from crippling Gouging Fire with Intimidate. Ogerpon-W fits well with Gouging Fire as well, as with Follow Me it can protect Gouging Fire from Ground- and Water-type moves, both of which Ogerpon-W resists.

  • The Urshifu formes counter Gouging Fire, since they ignore Burning Bulwark and Breaking Swipe. Incineroar is also a good counter to Gouging Fire, cycling Intimidate and Parting Shot repeatedly until Gouging Fire is a sitting duck. Gouging Fire also struggles against special attackers like Flutter Mane and Landorus, which can hit it for big damage, the latter threatening it for an OHKO.

Offensive Support.description:
• Heat Crash is a reliable way of dealing damage, and because Gouging Fire is so heavy, it will almost always do good damage against most of the metagame. Howl can be used to take advantage of passive playstyles and partially negate Intimidate, and with a Speed Booster Energy, it can support the Kingambit and Ogerpon-W in return.

  • 252 HP and 20 Defense EVs allow you to always live two Wicked Blows from Adamant Urshifu-S, and 164 Speed EVs with a Jolly Nature allow you to and outspeed Adamant Choice Scarf Landorus-T and Chien-Pao once the Booster Energy has been consumed.

  • Tera Grass is a good defensive Tera type for Gouging Fire, as it lets Gouging Fire resist Ground-type moves like Landorus's Earth Power and makes it immune to Spore, which is crucial since Burning Bulwark doesn't Protect Gouging Fire from status moves. Tera Fairy is also a good option as well, as it lets Gouging Fire resist both of Urshifu-S's STAB moves and take neutral damage from the majority of the metagame.

battlestadiumsingles.overview:
Welcome to Battle Stadium Singles Regulation F! This Pokemon is a new addition from the Indigo Disk that happens to be relevant!

If you feel that this analysis is missing important information, feel free to leave feedback here.

Offensive Dragon Dance.description:
• With nearly unresisted coverage and reasonable bulk, Gouging Fire is a fearsome Speed boosting sweeper!

  • Heat Crash VS. Flare Blitz: Heat Crash hits plenty of targets for high power thanks to Gouging Fire's high weight without compromising its bulk like Flare Blitz. However, beware that some heavy targets that sometimes use Tera Fairy like Ting-Lu, Ursaluna-B, and opposing Gouging Fire will take very little from Heat Crash compared to Flare Blitz.

  • Scale Shot and Loaded Dice: Scale Shot with Loaded Dice not only gives Gouging Fire an alternate way to boost its Speed but also provides it with a way to bust through Focus Sash Pokemon after a boost, such as Chien-Pao.

  • Outrage VS. Dragon Claw: Outrage is preferred for maximum late-game sweeping potential, but Dragon Claw is a safer option if you don't always bring good Fairy-type checks like Scizor.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake is a good response to bulky Fire-types like Incineroar and the rare Heatran, and it is the strongest attack against Toxapex.

  • Substitute: Substitute lets Gouging Fire block Yawn from troublesome foes like Swampert and Torkoal and not worry about Thunder Wave from slow, bulky foes like Gholdengo and Porygon2.

  • Booster Energy: If not using Scale Shot, Booster Energy's power or Speed boost is the most useful for late-game sweeping without compromising Gouging Fire's good bulk like Life Orb would.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Gouging Fire's typing is fine defensively, but the high profile weaknesses to Ground and Dragon mean Terastallizing gives it far more versatile setup opportunities.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy turns the tables on fearsome Dragon-type attacks from the likes of Latios and Dragonite and is a good defensive typing in general.

  • Fire: Tera Fire gives Gouging Fire plenty of extra power and a useful Fairy resistance against Flutter Mane, even if the irritating Earthquake weakness remains.

  • Water: Tera Water is a godsend against Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes and gives a setup opportunity against Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash as well.

  • Grass: Although it's awkward against several targets like Tera Flying Landorus-T and opposing Gouging Fire, Tera Grass's Earthquake resistance and Spore immunity give it a niche.

Alternate EV Spreads
  • 84 HP / 164 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Jolly: With this spread, Gouging Fire gets a Speed boost with Protosynthesis, letting it become a competent revenge killer with Booster Energy or have an extra use on sun teams. The defensive investment allows Gouging Fire to survive Tera-boosted Adamant Chien-Pao's Choice Band Crunch

Choiced.description:
• Gouging Fire's deadly STAB combination makes it a great user of Choice items and gives it an especially strong role on sun teams as a cleaner and revenge killer!

  • Raging Fury VS. Heat Crash: Gouging Fire's bulk is commendable enough that in a late-game stage, locking it into Raging Fury may make it less vulnerable to revenge kills than Flare Blitz's recoil. Heat Crash fulfills a similar purpose, though heavy threats like Ting-Lu and Ursaluna-B will take very little from it.

  • Dragon Claw VS. Breaking Swipe: Dragon Claw is the most powerful option for a no-drawback Dragon-type STAB move, but Breaking Swipe's Attack drop can open up some support opportunities for Gouging Fire's teammates.

  • Earthquake: Earthquake hits Incineroar and bulky Tera Fire users like Scizor hard, though it can be a risky move to choose with the large number of Ground-immune foes in the metagame.

  • Torkoal: If using this set on a sun team, Torkoal is among the best options for setting up sun for Gouging Fire thanks to its access to Stealth Rock and Yawn, which can soften up foes for a sweep.

  • Choice Scarf Vs. Choice Band: Choice Scarf functions the best outside of sun teams and is able to outspeed major threats like Chien-Pao and Iron Bundle. Choice Band is harder to clean with outside of sun teams, and it can use a specialized EV spread to get a Speed boost in sun.

Other Options
  • Double Kick: If using Choice Scarf, Double Kick can be used to OHKO Chien-Pao through its Focus Sash in a surprise revenge kill. It's too weak to be used for much else though.
Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Low: Since Gouging Fire is focused on cleaning and revenge killing, defensive Terastallization isn't usually an important factor for it.

  • Fire: Tera Fire makes Gouging Fire even more difficult to wall, especially in late-game scenarios. It also gives Gouging Fire a handy Fairy resistance.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy can turn the tables on other Dragon-types, making it by far the most useful defensive Tera type for this set.

Alternate EV Spreads
  • 84 HP / 164 Atk / 4 Def / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Jolly: This spread gives Gouging Fire a Speed boost with Protosynthesis, allowing potentially easier cleaning with Choice Band sets in sun. The bulk investment allows Gouging Fire to survive Choice Band Tera-boosted Crunch from Adamant Choice Band Chien-Pao.

Bulky Dragon Dance.description:
• Gouging Fire's incredible dual STAB coverage and good defensive stats make running a bulky Dragon Dance set a great choice!

  • Breaking Swipe VS. Dragon Claw: Dragon Claw is the more reliable late-game cleaning attack, but Breaking Swipe eases Gouging Fire's setup against physical threats.

  • ** Heat Crash VS. Flare Blitz**: Gouging Fire is heavy enough for Heat Crash to be just as powerful as Flare Blitz against several lightweight targets, such as Flutter Mane and Gholdengo. However, common, heavy foes like Ursaluna-B and Ting-Lu will only take 40 Base Power of damage from it, which can justify Flare Blitz's recoil for some teams. Checking our damage calculator can help decide if Heat Crash or Flare Blitz is better for your team!

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: While Gouging Fire's typing isn't bad defensively, its common weaknesses to Ground- and Dragon-type attacks mean Terastallization will greatly increase its setup opportunities.

  • Fairy Tera Fairy is a fantastic defensive choice, fending off Dragon-type attacks that can break through Gouging Fire and making it a great option against Urshifu-S.

  • Water: Tera Water vastly eases the matchup against Urshifu-R, which can bypass Breaking Swipe with Surging Strikes otherwise. It also makes dealing with Chien-Pao easier.

  • Fire: Fire isn't an impressive defensive choice beyond the useful Fairy resistance and losing the Dragon weakness, but the power boost still makes it worth considering.

  • Grass: Tera Grass is awkward against opposing Fire-types and Tera Flying Landorus-T, but the Ground resistance and Spore immunity do give it a niche.

EV Spreads
  • Minimum Speed EVs: Gouging Fire's EV spreads are fairly customizable, but usually it's best to have at least 212 Speed EVs with a neutral nature or 116 EVs with a Jolly nature. This ensures that Gouging Fire outspeeds Iron Bundle, Flutter Mane, and Chien-Pao after one use of Dragon Dance. If the rare Dragapult is a special concern, 252 Speed EVs with a neutral nature or 148 Speed EVs with Jolly can be run to outspeed that after Dragon Dance.
Physically Defensive Spreads

  • 244 HP / 4 Atk / 44 Def / 4 SpD / 212 Spe Impish: This spread avoids a 2HKO from Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes.

  • 108 HP / 188 Def / 212 Spe Impish: This spread is the second most physically defensive spread possible with the given Speed, sacrificing some special bulk to have about an 85% chance of avoiding a 2HKO from Jolly Choice Band Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash with Leftovers recovery. The HP investment is worth it over making Gouging Fire slightly more physically bulky for some extra cushioning against special attacking threats, such as surviving Choice Specs Gholdengo's Shadow Ball after Stealth Rock damage.

Specially Defensive Spreads

  • All of these spreads avoid a 2HKO from Flutter Mane that lack Choice Specs, provided Stealth Rock is off the field.

  • 188 HP / 204 SpD / 116 Spe Jolly or 188 HP / 108 SpD / 212 Spe Careful: These identical spreads usually allow Gouging Fire to survive Blood Moon followed by Vacuum Wave from Modest Ursaluna-B when taking Stealth Rock damage and Leftovers recovery into account.

  • 116 HP / 52 Atk / 4 Def / 220 SpD / 116 Jolly or 116 HP / 52 Atk / 4 Def / 124 SpD / 212 Spe Careful: These identical spreads sacrifice some overall bulk to get an Attack boost from Protosynthesis, which can be helpful against sun teams or when using Booster Energy.

  • 252 HP / 108 SpD / 148 Spe Jolly: This spread gives Gouging Fire a Speed boost with Protosynthesis, which is especially helpful for outspeeding Booster Energy Flutter Mane after a Dragon Dance.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers is best for easing Gouging Fire's setup, especially when paired with Breaking Swipe.

  • Booster Energy: Booster Energy can be used with the specialized EV spreads above to boost a specific stat once.

  • Rocky Helmet: When using physically defensive spreads or Breaking Swipe, Rocky Helmet is an effective passive damage dealer against threats like Dragonite and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R.

  • Clear Amulet: Clear Amulet prevents Landorus-T and Incineroar from obstructing Gouging Fire with Intimidate cycling.

  • Heavy-Duty Boots: While not as cripplingly weak to Stealth Rock as something like Volcarona, Heavy-Duty Boots lets Gouging Fire check threats more consistently overall.

  • Covert Cloak: Covert Cloak makes losing to Garganacl far less likely and prevents dreaded flinch scenarios from Chien-Pao and Chi-Yu.

Offensive Support.description: • 132 Attack EVs guarantee an OHKO on Landorus at +1, while the Speed EVs ensure a Speed boost from Protosynthesis

Physical Support.description:
• Heat Crash gives Gouging Fire a powerful Fire-type STAB move, reaching its maximum Base Power against common foes like Chien-Pao, Ogerpon, and Gholdengo. Flare Blitz can instead be used for more consistent damage into heavy foes like Iron Hands and Terastallized Raging Bolt at the cost of significant recoil damage.

  • Breaking Swipe allows Gouging Fire to cripple opposing physical attackers, such as Ogerpon and Iron Hands, while dealing sizeable chip damage, particularly against opposing Dragon-types like Raging Bolt and Roaring Moon that resist Heat Crash.

  • Howl enables both Gouging Fire and common physical partners offensively, allowing them to sweep while offsetting the Attack drop from Intimidate.

  • Burning Bulwark can heavily punish physical attackers targeting Gouging Fire with a burn, most notably Fake Out from the likes of Iron Hands and Rillaboom. However, Burning Bulwark doesn't block status moves, so it can be bypassed by foes like Incineroar and Amoonguss with Parting Shot and Spore, respectively. Due to this, Protect is a viable option to mitigate this vulnerability.

  • Booster Energy activates Protosynthesis to give Gouging Fire a vitally important boost to Speed, allowing for it to outspeed the majority of the metagame, most notably Chien-Pao and the Ogerpon formes. The Attack investment allows Protosynthesis to boost Speed while maximizing Gouging Fire's damage output. The remaining EVs are placed in HP.

  • Tera Fairy provides an immunity to Dragon-type moves, namely Draco Meteor from Raging Bolt, Dragon Energy from Regidrago, and Breaking Swipe from both Roaring Moon and opposing Gouging Fire, while also letting Gouging Fire resist Fighting- and Dark-type moves from the likes of Iron Hands, Chien-Pao, and Chi-Yu.

  • Gouging Fire is best utilized as a support piece for physical attackers, using its offensive and defensive support tools to enable them. However, Gouging Fire can lack immediate damage output, particularly against heavy foes that take minimal damage from Heat Crash, so it's important to position partners to maintain strong offensive pressure throughout the game.

  • Gouging Fire is seriously threatened by special attackers, namely Landorus, Raging Bolt, and Glimmora; thus, it greatly appreciates partners that can improve its survivability through damage reduction or healing to help alleviate such pressure. Namely, Grimmsnarl and Alolan Ninetales can set dual screens to reduce the damage of opposing attackers, and Rillaboom and Sinistcha can provide healing with Grassy Surge and Hospitality, respectively.

  • Chien-Pao pairs phenomenally with Gouging Fire, as it can threaten Landorus and Raging Bolt for Gouging Fire while bolstering its damage output with Sword of Ruin. In return, Gouging Fire can threaten the opposing Steel- and Ice-types that resist Chien-Pao's Ice-type STAB moves like Kingambit and Alolan Ninetales while furthering Chien-Pao's offensive presence with Howl. Landorus can threaten Diancie and Incineroar for Gouging Fire, which hits Ice-types like Chien-Pao for Landorus. Dragonite is a powerful recipient of Howl, particularly for boosting the power of Extreme Speed, and Dragonite can pivot into Ground-type moves like Earth Power from Landorus.

  • Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom also greatly benefit from Howl while providing Gouging Fire support in the form of redirection and Fake Out, respectively. In the case of Ogerpon-W, it also threatens common checks to Gouging Fire in Landorus and Glimmora and offers a way to remove Incineroar. Ting-Lu is able to shore up Gouging Fire's weaker special bulk, while Gouging Fire can reduce physical damage through Breaking Swipe and Burning Bulwark, forming a potent duo defensively that can both deal sizeable damage, particularly when amplified by Howl. Gouging Fire greatly threatens Rillaboom, which can be problematic for both Ting-Lu and Ogerpon-W.

Fire Lash DD (Salazzle).description: 152 Speed EVs lets it outrun Darkrai at +1

Calm Mind.description:
Calm Mind Raging Bolt is one of the metagame's top setup sweepers and wallbreakers. Its natural bulk and unique typing not only allows it to check common offensive threats like Ogerpon-W and Cinderace, but also to gain multiple entry points and setup opportunities as well. On top of a potent STAB combination that hits most of the metagame at least neutrally, its signature move Thunderclap prevents Raging Bolt's sweep from being cut short by faster threats and opposing priority users like Enamorus, Walking Wake, and Kingambit and lets it act as a revenge killer, too. Dragon Pulse is preferred for its consistent damage output, but Draco Meteor can be used to propel Raging Bolt's niche as a wallbreaker further, letting it overwhelm checks like Ting-Lu and Clodsire much more easily and netting benchmarks such as OHKOing defensive Landorus-T and Dragonite through Multiscale, all after a Calm Mind. A reliable Electric-type STAB move lets Raging Bolt prevent foes like Primarina, Gholdengo, and Calm Mind Enamorus from setting up freely and makes it less vulnerable to Encore users like Iron Valiant and Hisuian Samurott. Thunderbolt's consistency is preferred in this regard, but other options can be used as well. Discharge allows Raging Bolt to potentially cripple specially defensive walls like Galarian Slowking and slow down faster threats like Gholdengo, Darkrai, and Zamazenta, which helps to reduce its reliance on Thunderclap. Exclusively on rain teams, the stronger option in Thunder can also be used instead for similar reasons. Raging Bolt can lean towards the weather further by running Weather Ball instead if used on either a sun or rain team; it allows Raging Bolt to hit Iron Treads super effectively, with rain Weather Ball pressuring Raging Bolt's other Ground-type checks like Gliscor and Landorus-T more reliably, while sun Weather Ball cleanly OHKOes even bulky Kingambit and Gholdengo unboosted, all at the expense of the ability to immediately threaten Calm Mind Primarina. Alternatively, Taunt can be used to let Raging Bolt overwhelm walls like Blissey and Toxic Galarian Slowking. Booster Energy provides Raging Bolt with a damage boost, letting it reach feats such as OHKOing Iron Valiant with Thunderclap after a layer of Spikes and specially defensive Gliscor with +1 Draco Meteor, as well as having significant rolls to 2HKO Clodsire with Draco Meteor. Leftovers gives it more longevity to set up more easily and further take advantage of its defensive profile. Air Balloon is another option to prevent revenge killing attempts from its Ground-type checks like Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu. Tera Fairy gives Raging Bolt an immunity to Dragon-type attacks from foes like Dragapult and opposing Raging Bolt that don't fear its Thunderclap; it is also generally a good neutral typing against foes like Weavile and Iron Valiant. Tera Bug gives a Ground resistance without being weak to Kyurem and opposing Raging Bolt while also providing a Fighting resistance against Zamazenta. Tera Ghost is also an option to give offensive teams an emergency check to IronPress Zamazenta and, if used with Taunt, beat Blissey one-on-one. Tera Flying can be used for an outright immunity to Ground, letting it flip its matchup against Great Tusk and Landorus-T; this can be combined with Taunt to beat bulky Ground-type checks like Gliscor, Clodsire, and Ting-Lu. An EV spread of 64 HP / 28 Def / 252 SpA / 164 Spe is an alternative option; it runs enough Speed to get the jump on Gliscor, with the extra bulk letting Raging Bolt survive Speed Booster Energy Great Tusk's Headlong Rush from full, though this significantly worsens its matchup against opposing Raging Bolt.

Raging Bolt fits on a variety of offensive teams, ranging from hyper offense to weather-based archetypes in sun and rain. It pairs well with other strong special attackers like Gholdengo, Iron Moth, and Darkrai; on top of keeping up the pressure against the opposition, they can work with Raging Bolt to wear down and overwhelm shared checks like Ting-Lu, Clodsire, Galarian Slowking, and Blissey. Physical setup sweepers like Kingambit, Ogerpon-W, Great Tusk, Dragonite, and Zamazenta are similarly important, as they can threaten out the aforementioned special walls and force damage against Landorus-T and opposing Great Tusk; some of these physical attackers can even switch into the Ground-types, and Raging Bolt uses their checks like Skarmory, Alomomola, and Dondozo as entry points and setup opportunities. Rillaboom also deserves a special mention; on top of providing Grassy Terrain to increase Raging Bolt's longevity and let it stomach Earthquake from foes like Landorus-T and Ting-Lu, Rillaboom can also bring Raging Bolt in safely via U-turn against switch-ins like Moltres, Corviknight, and Zapdos for setup opportunities. Entry hazard setters like Deoxys-S, Hisuian Samurott, Landorus-T, and Glimmora are highly appreciated, as hazards help put foes and especially its checks into KO range, with Landorus-T also capable of switching into Great Tusk, Iron Treads, and opposing Landorus-T that threaten Raging Bolt out; in return, Raging Bolt can take advantage of and pressure common hazard removal Pokemon like Corviknight and Cinderace to maintain said hazards. Raging Bolt can benefit from Drought users like Torkoal and Ninetales; the sun allows Raging Bolt to freely forgo Booster Energy and gives it the option to run Weather Ball. Raging Bolt also synergizes well with other sun wallbreakers; Walking Wake can exploit Ground-types like Ting-Lu, Iron Treads, and Gliscor while assisting Raging Bolt in pressuring Galarian Slowking and Blissey. This is especially strong because going for Tera Water to deal with Walking Wake makes them vulnerable to Raging Bolt. Great Tusk can complement Raging Bolt's breaking power by dealing with its special walls and overwhelming shared checks like Landorus-T and Great Tusk, with Raging Bolt handling the likes of Skarmory, Alomomola, and Tera Water Gliscor in return. Raging Bolt can also be used on rain teams, benefiting from Pelipper's Drizzle to run options like Weather Ball and Thunder. It forms a great core with Barraskewda, as Barraskewda can position Raging Bolt against its bulky Water-type checks like Alomomola and Tera Water Garganacl via Flip Turn; in return, Barraskewda alongside other rain wallbreakers like Overqwil can pressure and overwhelm Ground-types like Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Iron Treads for Raging Bolt. Defensively, Raging Bolt can check Rillaboom and Ogerpon-W, which are otherwise problematic for rain teams, while Pelipper is capable of switching into Ground-types like Landorus-T, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads that force Raging Bolt out. Though more niche, Raging Bolt can also fit on other hyper offense structures. Dual screens setters like Deoxys-S, Alolan Ninetales, and Grimmsnarl provide Raging Bolt with an easier time setting up against even super effective hits and prevent it from being revenge killed by foes like Weavile, Landorus-T, and Dragonite. Sticky Web from Ribombee can slow down would-be revenge killers like Great Tusk, minimizing the risk of Thunderclap mindgames against foes like Encore Iron Valiant and Substitute Iron Moth.

Choice Specs Pivot.description:
With Choice Specs, Raging Bolt becomes a terrifying wallbreaker that is capable of chunking even bulkier walls such as Gliscor, Garganacl, and Assault Vest Hatterene while also capable of providing strong pivot support and revenge killing capabilities to further pressure its foes. Volt Switch is used to help Raging Bolt maintain momentum for the team, racking up chip damage on walls or switchins Raging Bolt cannot immediately OHKO or even 2HKO, like Garganacl, Blissey, and Assault Vest Galarian Slowking. Thunderclap lets it revenge kill or force out faster threats such as Ogerpon-W, Iron Valiant, and Enamorus, and it also helps Raging Bolt beat slower priority users such as Kingambit and Scizor. Draco Meteor is the Dragon-type STAB move of choice, making immediate progress on bulky Pokemon such as Galarian Slowking, Iron Treads, Ting-Lu, and Clodsire, even 2HKOing the latter due to its Unaware. Other common Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Great Tusk heavily fear Draco Meteor even more, so Raging Bolt can often use Volt Switch freely to gain momentum early-game without worrying too much about an immunity stifling it. Raging Bolt wants to run as much Speed investment as possible without compromising on power in order to Speed tie or outspeed opposing Raging Bolt and is especially important when factoring in Thunderclap. However, if this is not a major concern, bulkier EV spreads that use less Speed EVs to take resisted hits such as Ogerpon-W's Ivy Cudgel and Rillaboom's Grassy Glide better is also an option; an EV spread of 200 HP / 252 SpA / 56 Spe is just enough to outpace Adamant Kingambit or going for 92 HP / 252 SpA / 164 Spe to outspeed uninvested Gliscor, giving Raging Bolt a better matchup into one of the few Ground-types that might dare to switch in. Tera Fairy gives a solid defensive typing that is immune to fearsome incoming Dragon-type attacks from foes like Dragapult and Walking Wake while also resisting Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Zamazenta's Body Press. However, Tera Dragon can be used to further intensify the power of Draco Meteor, while, like Tera Fairy, also removing the weakness to incoming Ground-type attacks such as Great Tusk's Headlong Rush and Dragonite's Earthquake.

Balanced and bulky offensive teams most appreciate the hole-punching power of Choice Specs Raging Bolt. Pokemon with pivoting moves such as Corviknight, Galarian Slowking, and Pecharunt make great teammates for this set, as they help bring in Raging Bolt to start breaking apart the opponent's core. This set also often risks losing momentum, as Raging Bolt gets locked into a move against a Pokemon immune to it or becomes non-threatening due to Special Attack drops from Draco Meteor, so it appreciates the defensive backbone these Pokemon can provide. Corviknight is a standout, as it is immune to Ground-type attacks from the likes of Landorus-T and Great Tusk that check Raging Bolt, while Raging Bolt threatens Moltres and Zapdos that can annoy Corviknight. This Raging Bolt set can also heavily pressure specially defensive Pokemon on the opposing team such as Ting-Lu and Galarian Slowking, chunking them and greatly limiting their longevity. Special attackers such as Gholdengo, Iron Moth, Darkrai, and Enamorus can be paired with Raging Bolt to overwhelm and KO specially defensive Pokemon via their combined assaults. Teammates such as Ting-Lu, Garganacl, and Gliscor can enable Raging Bolt by setting entry hazards to further chip opposing Pokemon such as Ting-Lu, Ogerpon-W, and Garganacl into KO range. Ting-Lu and Garganacl also help by switching into Pokemon like Dragapult and Deoxys-S looking to revenge kill Raging Bolt. Removing hazards also greatly extends Raging Bolt's lifespan and gives opportunities to aggressively switch it in to make progress, so teammates such as Hatterene, Great Tusk, and Galarian Weezing are appreciated for that purpose. Cinderace is a particularly noteworthy teammate, as it removes hazards on Raging Bolt's side of the field, puts them on the opponent's side, and performs timely pivots to bring Raging Bolt in. All moves on this set have immunities, so with good prediction, Fairy-types and Ground-types will completely shut down this set. Protect from Pokemon such as Gliscor, Garganacl, and Alomomola will ease predictions by forcing Raging Bolt to lock into a given move, allowing for more reliable counterplay. Teammates that can take advantage of the passive turn of Protect to enter the field such as Ogerpon-W, Kyurem, and Primarina can ease these potentially troublesome matchups. These Pokemon are also excellent at handling Ground-types that may annoy Raging Bolt, and Ogerpon-W and Primarina can also run U-turn and Flip Turn, respectively, to form a pivoting core that helps Raging Bolt enter the field. In return, Raging Bolt can pressure defensive Pokemon such as Hydrapple and Toxapex for these teammates. Landorus-T can be a helpful teammate for many of the aforementioned reasons, as it handles Ground-types well, puts up Stealth Rock, pivots with U-turn, and threatens out specially defensive checks to Raging Bolt such as Galarian Slowking and Clodsire while Raging Bolt can threaten Pokemon that annoy Landorus-T such as Alomomola and Corviknight. Lastly, teammates such as Kingambit and Zamazenta can work with Raging Bolt to overwhelm shared checks such as Great Tusk and Landorus-T, as well as deter these Ground-types from switching into Raging Bolt. These Pokemon additionally threaten specially defensive Pokemon such as Blissey and Galarian Slowking while Raging Bolt can take on Dondozo, Moltres, and Corviknight.

All-Out Attacker.description:
Raging Bolt makes use of its plentiful coverage options to serve as a potent and immediate wallbreaker and revenge killer, using its bulk, typing, and priority to deal with dangerous foes like Ogerpon-W, Cinderace, and Hisuian Samurott. Thunderclap threatens key targets like Enamorus and Tornadus-T and picks off numerous other faster foes like Darkrai, Deoxys-S, Iron Moth, and the aforementioned Cinderace and Ogerpon-W; it is also helpful for playing mind games against Kingambit's Sucker Punch, potentially stopping it from pulling off a late-game sweep. Dragon Pulse provides a consistent Dragon-type STAB option, while Draco Meteor takes solid chunks out of bulky foes like Ting-Lu, Clodsire, and Galarian Slowking; unlike Dragon Pulse, a Life Orb-boosted Draco Meteor under the sun also threatens to cleanly OHKO maximum HP Dragonite with Multiscale intact. Weather Ball provides a solid coverage option depending on which weather team Raging Bolt is used on; under the sun, Weather Ball scorches Steel-types like Gholdengo, Kingambit, and Scizor, and when boosted by a Life Orb, it has a favorable chance to 2HKO Clodsire. Meanwhile, the rain version of the move washes away Ground-type checks like Great Tusk, Gliscor, and Landorus-T. The move under both weather conditions also threatens Iron Treads, which otherwise handles Raging Bolt very well. Thunderbolt provides a reliable Electric-type STAB option to threaten bulky Water-types like Alomomola and Toxapex, ease the matchup against Encore users like Iron Valiant and Hisuian Samurott, and help prevent sweepers like Nasty Plot Gholdengo and Calm Mind variants of Enamorus and Primarina from using Raging Bolt as setup bait. Solar Beam allows Raging Bolt to blast apart common foes like Garganacl, Ting-Lu, and Great Tusk without relying on Draco Meteor and should exclusively be used on sun teams to avoid its two-turn drawback. Thunder provides a stronger Electric-type option over Thunderbolt and has similar consistency under the rain, letting Raging Bolt use the move without worrying about missing; after consuming Booster Energy, Thunder has a small chance to OHKO a fully invested Assault Vest Alomomola after Stealth Rock. If Raging Bolt is used on sun archetypes, Life Orb is recommended, as its boost stacks with Protosynthesis to make the most of Raging Bolt's wallbreaking capabilities. Outside of sun, Booster Energy provides a one-time power boost. Tera Flying is used to flip the matchup against annoying Ground-types like Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, Gliscor, Landorus-T, and Iron Treads. Tera Fairy gives Raging Bolt a solid defensive profile, making it immune to Dragon-type attacks from foes like Dragapult, Walking Wake, and opposing Raging Bolt and providing resistances to Kingambit's Sucker Punch and Zamazenta's Fighting-type STAB options. Tera Grass grants Raging Bolt a Ground resistance while maintaining a resistance to Ogerpon-W's STAB options; under the sun, it gives a Life Orb-boosted Solar Beam a favorable chance to OHKO a fully invested Ting-Lu after Stealth Rock. Tera Ghost lets Raging Bolt block Rapid Spin from Great Tusk and Iron Treads and check IronPress Zamazenta and Extreme Speed Dragonite in a pinch. On sun archetypes, Raging Bolt can opt for Tera Fire to amplify Weather Ball's damage output and flip its weaknesses to Ice and Fairy, improving its matchup against foes like Kyurem, Weavile, and Iron Valiant. Tera Dragon is another option, removing Raging Bolt's Ground weakness and giving its Life Orb-boosted Draco Meteor under the sun the highest possible chance to OHKO a fully invested Galarian Slowking and Clodsire. While a Modest nature is preferred to maximize Raging Bolt's damage output, it can also opt for a Timid nature to outpace Adamant Rillaboom and Dragonite at the cost of missing out on the aforementioned OHKOs. If Raging Bolt does not need to Speed tie with opposing Raging Bolt, it can reduce its Speed investment to 144 EVs to outspeed Adamant Tyranitar or 132 EVs to outpace Jolly Kingambit, investing the remaining EVs in its bulk.

Raging Bolt is a solid choice for sun and rain teams, which enable Weather Ball as a powerful coverage option. On sun archetypes, pairing Raging Bolt with Ninetales or Torkoal is mandatory, as either can set sun to activate Protosynthesis, allowing Raging Bolt to run Life Orb and bombard opposing teams with its boosted attacks. Ninetales also provides crucial support with Encore to disrupt passive foes and Healing Wish to grant Raging Bolt a second chance at finishing the game, while Torkoal sets up Stealth Rock and keeps opposing entry hazards off the field with Rapid Spin. Walking Wake goes hand-in-hand with Raging Bolt, as their combined offensive firepower can enable either to clean up. Additionally, it blows through troublesome answers like Ting-Lu and Clodsire and provides Raging Bolt with a free switch through Flip Turn. Raging Bolt's wallbreaking gives Walking Wake room to opt for a Speed Protosynthesis set and serve as a late-game cleaner against fast offensive teams. Walking Wake can even forgo Choice Specs in favor of items like Mystic Water or Wise Glasses, allowing it to freely switch between moves. Sun sweepers like Ceruledge and Venusaur also become deadly cleaners once Raging Bolt weakens the opposing team early-game. Great Tusk and Hatterene are also beneficial for Raging Bolt, utilizing Rapid Spin and Magic Bounce, respectively, to ensure that hazards stay off the field. Great Tusk also helps soften shared answers like Landorus-T and opposing Great Tusk and sets up Stealth Rock to help Raging Bolt secure KOs against foes like Ting-Lu. Meanwhile, Hatterene uses an Eject Button to take an attack and bring Raging Bolt in safely while also providing Healing Wish to rejuvenate it. In return, Raging Bolt deals with foes like Dondozo, Corviknight, and Skarmory for Great Tusk while handling Gholdengo for Hatterene. Utility Cresselia is another noteworthy teammate for Raging Bolt, as it can reliably switch into Ground-type attacks from foes like Great Tusk, Landorus-T, and Dragonite and threaten them with Ice Beam. It can also completely revitalize Raging Bolt with Lunar Dance and spread paralysis with Thunder Wave to cripple otherwise faster foes like Dragapult, Walking Wake, and Iron Valiant. On rain archetypes, Pelipper is a mandatory teammate, as Drizzle lets Raging Bolt use Thunder without worrying about missing and turns Weather Ball into a Water-type coverage option. Pelipper can also utilize a slow U-turn to bring Raging Bolt in unscathed. Raging Bolt then provides a solid answer to Ogerpon-W and Zapdos, both of which are very annoying for rain teams to deal with. Swift Swim users like Barraskewda and Overqwil form a deadly offensive core with Raging Bolt on rain archetypes, helping Raging Bolt overwhelm fast offensive checks like Zamazenta, Dragapult, and Iron Valiant. Barraskewda can also draw in bulky Water-type answers like Alomomola, Toxapex, and Tera Water Gliscor and pivot out with Flip Turn, letting Raging Bolt pressure them. Meanwhile, Overqwil provides extra security against Kingambit and Rillaboom, both of which pose a major threat to the rain archetype. Hazard support from Iron Treads helps Raging Bolt secure crucial KOs against foes like Assault Vest Alomomola; Iron Treads also removes opposing hazards with Rapid Spin and provides pivot support with Volt Switch, giving Raging Bolt more opportunities to wreak havoc. Kingambit is another important partner for Raging Bolt, breaking past special walls like Blissey, forming a dangerous double priority duo with Raging Bolt to overcome fast-paced teams, and benefiting from Raging Bolt's wallbreaking to clean up late-game. In return, Raging Bolt deals with physically bulky foes that trouble Kingambit like Dondozo and Corviknight.

Boots Pivot.description:
Raging Bolt acts as a powerful offensive pivot and revenge killer that can also provide defensive utility thanks to its solid natural bulk and good typing. Thunderclap is one of the strongest options for priority in the metagame, allowing Raging Bolt to overcome its lackluster Speed tier and act as a strong revenge killer against the likes of Ogerpon-W, Enamorus, Darkrai, Deoxys-S, and Kingambit. Volt Switch makes Raging Bolt hard to pin down, allowing it to pivot on and wear down specially defensive walls such as Galarian Slowking, Iron Crown, and Blissey as they switch in. Draco Meteor is a viable alternative to Dragon Pulse for more immediate power, hitting some benchmarks like OHKOing opposing Raging Bolt and having a chance to OHKO bulky Great Tusk in exchange for a severe Special Attack drop. Taunt is an option that allows Raging Bolt to more effectively deal with special walls by stopping recovery attempts from the likes of Blissey and Clodsire and blocking utility moves from Clefable, Ting-Lu, and Galarian Slowking. Other options include Thunderbolt for a consistent Electric-type STAB move, 2HKOing neutral targets such as Clefable after little prior chip damage, defensive Zapdos, and Gholdengo while not forcing Raging Bolt to switch out, and Weather Ball on weather teams or alongside Galarian Slowking for alternative Ice-type coverage. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Raging Bolt to hit the field multiple times without worrying about entry hazards, which is especially good on teams that rely on ignoring hazards altogether or lack any form of removal. Tera Fairy allows Raging Bolt to turn the tables on matchups like Iron Defense Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, Dragapult, Kyurem, and Walking Wake. Another option is Tera Flying, granting an even better matchup against the likes of Great Tusk, Iron Treads, Landorus-T, and Ting-Lu, though it gives Raging Bolt some problematic weaknesses against opposing Raging Bolt, Zapdos, Weavile, and Meowscarada.

Raging Bolt fits best on balance and bulky offense teams, which appreciate its ability to pivot in and out of the field while dealing heavy damage and threatening boosted sweepers with its priority move. Raging Bolt can form great offensive cores when it's paired with other offensive pivots like Ogerpon, which can apply pressure with U-turn in a similar fashion to Raging Bolt's Volt Switch, punish Ground-types with its strong Grass-type STAB moves, remove items with Knock Off to accumulate entry hazard damage, and punish setup moves with Encore. Embody Aspect's Speed boost also helps Ogerpon cover for Raging Bolt's poor Speed against the likes of Great Tusk, Darkrai, and Dragapult. In return, Ogerpon appreciates Raging Bolt's help in pressuring physically defensive Pokémon such as Zapdos, Moltres, and Corviknight. Ogerpon-W is even more effective at dealing with Ground-types, trading Ogerpon's ability to hold an item and boost its Speed for a harder-to-resist STAB combination and wallbreaking power, pressuring defensive cores such as Sinistcha + Gliscor and Galarian Slowking + Corviknight more easily with pivoting support from Raging Bolt. Meowscarada offers a stronger U-turn and Knock Off as well as an even better Speed tier, especially with Choice Scarf variants acting as a revenge killer for faster threats such as Iron Valiant. Weavile has a strong Knock Off as well, and its Ice Shard complements Thunderclap perfectly against offensive cores, hitting threats Raging Bolt struggles with like Ogerpon and Tera Ground Dragonite. Hisuian Samurott can pivot with Flip Turn and deal with the likes of Ting-Lu, Iron Treads, Iron Crown, and Galarian Slowking while also providing Spikes with Ceaseless Edge, which, alongside its own Knock Off removing Heavy-Duty Boots from opposing Pokémon, makes it extremely effective against bulkier cores like Alomomola + Galarian Slowking or Ting-Lu, Toxapex + Gliscor or Ting-Lu, and Dondozo + Gliscor or Blissey. Pelipper's Drizzle can give Raging Bolt the options to run Thunder and Weather Ball, letting it hit would-be checks in Ting-Lu, Clodsire, Great Tusk, and Iron Treads with Water-type coverage. Barraskewda is a great partner on rain teams, as it's extremely hard to switch into and able to pivot with Flip Turn, and it loves Raging Bolt's ability to pressure Water-types like Alomomola, Dondozo and Primarina. Raging Bolt fits similarly on sun teams, synergizing with Torkoal and Ninetales' Drought, which activates Protosynthesis and allows it to hit the likes of Rillaboom and Iron Treads with sun-boosted Weather Ball, and with Walking Wake, which pressures Ground-types and shared checks like Galarian Slowking and Blissey. Raging Bolt also appreciates a defensive backbone to fall onto when its Volt Switch is blocked or after revenge killing a Pokemon. Flying-types like Corviknight and Gliscor check Ground-types such as Landorus-T and Ting-Lu, with the former offering hazard removal in Defog and the latter offering hazard support. Clefable's physical bulk allows it to take on Great Tusk, Ting-Lu, and Gliscor while setting up Stealth Rock; it can also cripple walls like Galarian Slowking, Clodsire, and Blissey with Knock Off and switch into Knock Off well itself. Alomomola makes a good partner thanks to its great physical bulk and longevity with Wish and Regenerator, which it can use in conjunction with Flip Turn to keep Raging Bolt healthy, and it appreciates the help in beating Ogerpon-W. Steel-types like Assault Vest Iron Crown and Tinkaton can threaten Iron Valiant and Kyurem, while Galarian Slowking can check them as well as offering a slow pivot and a powerful Future Sight. Lastly, hazard removal options like Great Tusk, Cinderace, and Iron Treads can clear the field for Choice Specs Raging Bolt.

Special Attack Booster Energy.description:
• Thunderbolt is Raging Bolt's most consistent STAB attack and beats Primarina, non-Assault Vest Metagross, and Volcanion.
  • Draco Meteor is Raging Bolt's strongest STAB attack and should be used against Skeledirge.
  • Thunderclap allows Raging Bolt to get KOs after using Thunderbolt and Draco Meteor and helps in matchups against some Hoopa-U sets as well as against Custap Berry users like Primarina and the Urshifu formes.
  • Taunt allows Raging Bolt to beat Pecharunt and Ogerpon-W.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Raging Bolt to survive the Choice Band Urshifu formes' Close Combat, while the Special Defense EVs allow it to survive a Hyper Beam from Timid Porygon-Z. The Speed EVs allow Raging Bolt to outspeed Modest Primarina. The remaining EVs are put in Special Attack to maximize power for best odds against specially defensive Primarina.
  • Draco Meteor into Thunderclap is stronger than Thunderbolt into Thunderclap, so in matchups where there is no recovery from the foe, such as against non-Sitrus Berry Annihilape, it is better to use Draco Meteor into Thunderclap.

Haban Berry.description:
• Thunderbolt is the main Electric-type STAB move, but Thunder makes Raging Bolt more reliable against Primarina, as Thunder can OHKO it, so you don't have to worry about potential Weakness Policy or Encore after using Calm Mind or Charge. Thunderbolt should be used when it does neutral or super effective damage against frailer foes like Primarina, Corviknight, and Metagross without an Assault Vest. Against foes that can survive Draco Meteor followed by Thunderclap like Hoopa-U and Urshifu-S, it is safer to use Thunderbolt or Thunder into Draco Meteor.
  • Draco Meteor hits Electric-resistant foes like Rillaboom and should be used against bulkier foes like Hoopa-U and Skeledirge. It also 2HKOes Unaware Skeledirge.
  • Thunderclap is a priority move that helps to KO low HP Pokemon like non-Assault Vest Metagross after one use of Thunderbolt. Draco Meteor into Thunderclap does slightly more damage than Thunderbolt into Thunderclap against neutral targets, but Thunder into Thunderclap does more. Thunderclap also counters Custap Berry users like Primarina and Hoopa-U by attacking on the turn they use their Custap Berry.
  • Calm Mind and Charge are both here to boost Raging Bolt's power and special bulk. Both moves especially help against Primarina, though Charge is more reliable against it and Calm Mind is useful in more matchups like against Rillaboom, Iron Hands, and Spectrier.
  • Haban Berry allows Raging Bolt to win against Dragon-types such as Walking Wake, as it can OHKO them after surviving a Dragon-type move. However, if those Dragon-types are holding a Haban Berry, Raging Bolt can't OHKO them and is 2HKOed back.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Dragon

Dragon Fang lets Raging Bolt outright OHKO Gliscor and OHKO Swampert, Iron Treads, and Hisuian Goodra after minimal chip damage with +1 Draco Meteor, but Raging Bolt is usually more likely to use Electric-type moves throughout a match. Dragon Fang also forces Raging Bolt to forego Leftovers, making it much easier to wear down. Heavy-Duty Boots is an alternative item that can be taken to help Raging Bolt deal with entry hazards consistently in order to prevent it from being worn down. Dragon Pulse can be used over Draco Meteor to prevent Raging Bolt from becoming setup fodder while still 2HKOing most of the targets Draco Meteor hits, such as Quagsire. However, the move's significant decrease in overall power against Raging Bolt's targets can result in it taking an extra hit or status move that it didn't need to before, most notably against Gliscor. An alternative EV spread of 252 HP / 92 Def / 108 SpA / 56 Spe with a Modest nature lets Raging Bolt avoid a 2HKO from Gliscor and Quagsire, always 2HKO both with Dragon Pulse, and outspeed Adamant Azumarill.

Dragon (Choice Specs)

Dragon Pulse can be used over Draco Meteor, as it has superior accuracy while still 2HKOing important threats like Gliscor and Quagsire, disallowing them from switching into Raging Bolt safely. A Modest nature can be used instead to nearly OHKO Gliscor without entry hazards and threaten 2HKOs against Gastrodon and Swampert, though this will leave Raging Bolt outsped by defensive Great Tusk sets.

The Dog of Thunder (Choice Specs) (Drago.description:
When donning a Choice Specs, Raging Bolt's powerful STAB moves become even more dangerous to bulkier teams, threatening usual switch-ins like mixed defensive Clodsire and Assault Vest Gallade with 2HKOs. With this immediate boost in power, Draco Meteor becomes strong enough to OHKO Gliscor after Stealth Rock chip damage and 2HKO Swampert, Gastrodon, and Hisuian Goodra, limiting the number of options bulkier teams have for switch-ins. Thunderbolt eliminates common Water-types like Toxapex, Assault Vest Tornadus-T, and specially defensive Corviknight after chip damage while threatening to 2HKO bulky Gholdengo sets and OHKOing Scizor after Stealth Rock chip damage. Thunderclap, when boosted by Choice Specs, allows Raging Bolt to OHKO Iron Valiant after chip damage while removing threats such as Enamorus and Hisuian Samurott. Volt Switch allows Raging Bolt to make use of its overwhelming presence and ability to force switches to pivot into one of its powerful teammates while also dealing damage. Maximum investment in Speed with a Timid nature allows Raging Bolt to outspeed threats like Modest or Adamant Hoopa-U, Adamant Dragonite, and physically defensive Great Tusk sets.

Raging Bolt appreciates the defensive backbone that Archaludon and Hisuian Goodra provide. Archaludon's access to Stealth Rock allows Raging Bolt to nab KOs that it normally wouldn't get consistently, like against the aforementioned Gliscor and Scizor. Archaludon also takes hits from Roaring Moon and Meowscarada while threatening them back with Body Press and Flash Cannon. Hisuian Goodra handles threats on the special side, namely Fairy- and Dragon-types, such as Hatterene, Flutter Mane, and Choice Specs Dragapult. It also uses Knock Off to remove items from defensive Pokemon that would hope to switch in on Raging Bolt like Iron Hands's Assault Vest and opposing Hisuian Goodra's Leftovers. Furthermore, Hisuian Goodra also uses Dragon Tail to force out Pokemon that use Raging Bolt as setup fodder after a Draco Meteor, like Volcarona. Dragapult can support Raging Bolt by burning threats like Meowscarada and Mamoswine with Will-O-Wisp or slowing down foes like Iron Valiant and Ogerpon-H with Thunder Wave. It can also opt to run a physically offensive set to take advantage of the special walls that Raging Bolt lures in, like Gastrodon and Assault Vest Hoopa-U. Dragapult can also utilize U-turn with a Choice item to form a powerful pivoting core with Raging Bolt, crucially luring in Pokemon like physically defensive Great Tusk and Archaludon. Garchomp provides additional entry hazards with Spikes, which pairs well with Choice Specs Raging Bolt's switch-forcing playstyle, while dealing with problematic Pokemon like Hisuian Goodra and Clodsire with Earthquake. In return, Raging Bolt can break through checks to its Swords Dance set by removing Corviknight, Dondozo, and Gliscor. Latias allows Raging Bolt to play very recklessly, as its Healing Wish enables Raging Bolt to trade health to get rid of threats to Dragon teams. Dragonite and Roaring Moon both benefit from Raging Bolt's ability to wear down physical walls like the aforementioned Dondozo. In return, these Pokemon can wear down special walls like Galarian Slowking and Hisuian Goodra.

Calm Mind (Dragon).description:
With its Electric-type STAB moves and access to Calm Mind, Raging Bolt finds itself as a powerful setup sweeper for Dragon teams capable of dealing with threats like Primarina, Greninja, and Enamorus. Draco Meteor threatens Ground-types like Gliscor that come into Raging Bolt's Electric-type moves, notably having a favorable chance of OHKOing it after Stealth Rock with one Calm Mind.
