Thunderbolt allows Raging Bolt to strike down Calm Mind Primarina, Dondozo, and defensive Gyarados, and Thunderclap lets it pick off faster threats like Greninja, Enamorus, and Hisuian Samurott. After a Calm Mind boost and Stealth Rock damage, Thunderclap is also capable of OHKOing neutral targets like Iron Valiant. Leftovers allows Raging Bolt to slowly heal itself and prevent it from being worn down too much from any chip damage. Air Balloon can be run over Leftovers to avoid Ground-type moves from Pokemon like Choice Scarf Landorus-T and Choice item Iron Treads, and use them as setup opportunities. The given EV spread lets Raging Bolt outpace Adamant Bisharp and survive Flutter Mane's Moonblast after a Calm Mind.

Setup sweepers like Roaring Moon and Kommo-o form a dangerous offensive core with Raging Bolt, as they deal with dedicated walls Raging Bolt is unlikely to break through such as Galarian Slowking and Hisuian Goodra, respectively. Archaludon sets up Stealth Rock, checks Weavile with Body Press, and switches into physical threats like Meowscarada and Azumarill. In return, Raging Bolt deals with special attacking threats like Greninja and Keldeo, which Archaludon detests. Dragapult can utilize a variety of sets to support Raging Bolt, as it can spread status with Will-O-Wisp and Thunder Wave to let Raging Bolt set up easier, don a Choice Scarf to revenge kill threats like Meowscarada with Draco Meteor or U-turn, or use a Choice Specs set to batter special walls like Alolan Muk alongside Raging Bolt. Garchomp provides more entry hazards with Spikes and deals with Hisuian Goodra and Clodsire with Earthquake, and it can use a Swords Dance set that thrives once Raging Bolt removes nuisances like Corviknight, Dondozo, and Gliscor. Choice Scarf Latias provides a Ground immunity, Trick to take advantage of shared checks in Ting-Lu and Galarian Slowking, which creates more setup opportunities for Raging Bolt, and Healing Wish, which lets Raging Bolt be more reckless in taking heavy damage to forcibly eliminate roadblocks for its teammates. Latias also deals with fast threats like Choice Scarf Great Tusk and Garchomp for Raging Bolt. Dragonite provides a Ground-type immunity that is not vulnerable to Mold Breaker Excadrill as well as powerful priority in Extreme Speed, which is extremely threatening once Raging Bolt removes Skarmory and Quagsire. Hisuian Goodra swaps into opposing Draco Meteor and forces progress by removing Heavy-Duty Boots and recovery items from key walls with Knock Off.

Calm Mind (Electric).description:
Raging Bolt makes for a strong wallbreaker on Electric teams, with Calm Mind boosting its already high Special Attack stat. Draco Meteor is a strong and reliable nuke that allows it to weaken and eventually remove bulky walls that most Electric staples struggle against Archaludon and potentially Gliscor after one Calm Mind boost and potentially Gliscor without a boost. Thunderclap is a strong priority option that allows it to OHKO faster threats such as Barraskewda and Choice Scarf Enamorus as well as pick off weakened faster threats such as Iron Valiant. Equipped with Air Balloon, Raging Bolt is able to switch into predicted Ground-type attacks and can take advantage of threats that are Choice locked into a Ground-type move to set up a Calm Mind or use an attack against a predicted switch-in. Air Balloon's consumability also lets Raging Bolt wall Ceruledge once it pops, as Ceruledge is rendered unable to use Poltergeist. Heavy-Duty Boots is another option to prevent it from getting worn down easily by entry hazards. Leftovers can also be used so that Raging Bolt gets access to a form of recovery With 124 EVs invested into HP, Raging Bolt is able to survive a Moonblast from Choice Scarf Flutter Mane. An alternate spread with full investment into Speed allows it to outspeed Torterra and some Gholdengo, Gliscor, and Great Tusk variants.

In order to wallbreak more efficiently, Raging Bolt appreciates entry hazard support from the likes of Galvantula's Sticky Web and Sandy Shocks's Stealth Rock and Spikes. Regieleki makes for another great teammate, being able to remove hazards with Rapid Spin so that Raging Bolt is able to switch in more safely. Regieleki is also able to spread paralysis with Thunder Wave reliably with its high Speed, allowing Raging Bolt to outspeed normally faster threats such as the Ogerpon formes. Rotom-W and Zapdos make for great additions for any Electric team, providing a Ground immunity while being able to check the likes of Great Tusk and Iron Treads. Rotom-W is also able to handle Excadrill under sand, which Raging Bolt doesn't like to face. Magnezone makes for another great teammate, providing a resistance against Fairy-types that Raging Bolt dislikes such as Hatterene and Flutter Mane. In return, Raging Bolt can handle the likes of Azumarill, Gliscor, and Gastrodon. Iron Hands is a strong, bulky teammate that can somewhat help in the Ground matchup, as with a combination of Shuca Berry and Ice Punch, it can eliminate offensive Ground-types that can easily sweep through Electric teams such as Landorus and Garchomp. Additionally, its Fighting typing helps against various Dark- and Normal-types such as Meowscarada, Weavile, Bisharp, and Blissey. In return, Raging Bolt is able to revenge kill boosted rain sweepers such as Kingdra and Barraskewda. Lastly, Pawmot is able to provide support with Revival Blessing, allowing Raging Bolt or any of its other teammates a second chance to punch holes in opponents' teams. Pawmot is also able to handle the likes of Hisuian Goodra, Air Balloon Heatran, and Weavile with either Close Combat or Mach Punch. Choice Scarf variants of Pawmot can handle speedy threats like Flutter Mane and Choice Scarf Landorus.

Bulky Special Attacker.description:
Set Details

  • Raging Bolt has phenomenal natural bulk and Special Attack, allowing it to stay on the field while chipping foes, and with priority in Thunderclap, it can finish off low-HP targets. Its potent STAB moves and survivability give it favorable matchups against Kyogre, Urshifu-R, Tornadus, and Koraidon.
  • Although Draco Meteor can miss and weakens Raging Bolt's damage output afterwards, it's used for a higher burst of damage, notably OHKOing non-Assault Vest Miraidon and Raging Bolt as well as Tera Dragon Zamazenta-C. Dragon Pulse is more consistent, lacking those drawbacks, but doesn't offer the same immediate power.
  • Magnet is the most consistent item since Raging Bolt primarily uses Electric-type STAB moves, which get boosted. Life Orb offers a higher damage increase than Magnet and applies to all moves but reduces survivability. Additionally, both Life Orb and Magnet stack with the power boost from Protosynthesis in sun. Booster Energy provides the same boost as Life Orb without the recoil, but the boost is lost after switching out.
  • The Defense investment allows Raging Bolt to live Close Combat from Life Orb Koraidon, Glacial Lance from most Calyrex-I, and almost always live Ice Spinner from Adamant Chien-Pao. The Speed investment enables Raging Bolt to outspeed maximum Speed Koraidon, Chien-Pao, and Miraidon in Tailwind. The rest is put into Special Attack to maximize its damage output.
  • Tera Electric is used to boost its Electric-type STAB moves, notably allowing it to score valuable chip damage on Pokemon like Zamazenta-C with Thunderbolt, even putting it in range of a Thunderclap. It also allows Raging Bolt to OHKO Kyogre with Thunderbolt and the Life Orb and Booster Energy variants to almost always 2HKO non-Leftovers Calyrex-I with Thunderbolt. Tera Electric can also help it live Dragon-, Ice-, and Fairy-type moves such as Draco Meteor from non-Choice Specs Miraidon, Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao, and Moonblast from Flutter Mane.

Teambuilding

  • Raging Bolt struggles against Chien-Pao, which threatens it with Icicle Crash and Ice Spinner, and it can pick Raging Bolt off with priority Sucker Punch, which outspeeds Thunderclap under normal circumstances.
  • Landorus is problematic because it can outspeed and threaten Raging Bolt with Earth Power. Similarly, Ursaluna moves before Raging Bolt under Trick Room and threatens it with Headlong Rush.
  • Calyrex-I and Miraidon teams are major threats, as Glacial Lance and Draco Meteor force Raging Bolt to Terastallize. Additionally, Choice Specs Miraidon can OHKO with Draco Meteor even if Raging Bolt Terastallizes.
  • Zacian-C threatens to OHKO Raging Bolt with Play Rough, and Iron Treads pressures it with High Horsepower while not taking much damage in return.
  • Grimmsnarl's damage mitigation via Light Screen and Spirit Break make it difficult for Raging Bolt to get Pokemon low on HP and finish them off with Thunderclap. Terapagos can tank Raging Bolt's attacks fairly well, especially after setting up with Calm Mind, and it can later pressure with Earth Power. Similarly, Assault Vest Ting-Lu is hard to break; it takes even less from Raging Bolt's Dragon-type moves and can wear it down with Sand Tomb and Snarl.
  • Amoonguss and Brute Bonnet can be troublesome for Raging Bolt, as it can't OHKO them and risks being put to sleep by Spore. They can also redirect Raging Bolt's Thunderclap with Rage Powder, preventing it from hitting their partners.
  • Koraidon is a great partner for Raging Bolt, boosting its damage output through Protosynthesis in sun. It also helps cover several of Raging Bolt’s problem matchups, threatening Amoonguss and Calyrex-I with Flare Blitz and Ting-Lu and Terapagos with Close Combat or Collision Course. In return, Raging Bolt pressures Kyogre with its Electric-type STAB moves.
  • Raging Bolt fits well on Calyrex-S and Zamazenta-C balance teams. Calyrex-S can chip foes into Thunderclap range with Astral Barrage, and Raging Bolt can do the same for Calyrex-S, allowing it to receive Grim Neigh boosts. Zamazenta-C helps against Chien-Pao and Terapagos and can block Glacial Lance from Calyrex-I with Wide Guard. Incineroar's Intimidate and Parting Shot can help Raging Bolt survive some of the aforementioned attacks.
  • Rillaboom and Raging Bolt both take hits well and apply priority pressure with Grassy Glide and Thunderclap, respectively. Chien-Pao also synergizes with Raging Bolt by threatening Amoonguss, Brute Bonnet, Miraidon, and Landorus with Icicle Crash or Ice Spinner while also contributing strong priority pressure, making it difficult for foes to attack freely.

Assault Vest.description:
Set Details

  • Assault Vest Raging Bolt is a great bulky special attacker with excellent versatility and longevity thanks to the Assault Vest and its great natural bulk. It has good matchups against Restricted Pokemon like Koraidon, Kyogre, Lunala, and Calyrex-S and non-Restricted threats such as Urshifu-R, Tornadus, and Ogerpon-H.
  • Draco Meteor can be inconsistent, but it has the power to consistently OHKO threats like Miraidon and opposing Raging Bolt, something Dragon Pulse cannot do. Dragon Pulse, while more reliable, lacks that same level of immediate power. Electroweb gives Raging Bolt a form of speed control that still deals meaningful damage, letting it outspeed Pokemon like Kyogre, Chi-Yu, the Urshifu formes, and Lunala after one Electroweb. Snarl allows Raging Bolt to disrupt special attackers like Calyrex-S, Kyogre, Landorus, Terapagos, and Lunala, as well as dealing good damage to Calyrex-S and breaking Lunala's Shadow Shield.
  • Assault Vest lets Raging Bolt take considerably more special attacks from Pokemon such as Calyrex-S, Lunala, Landorus, and Terapagos, such as being able to survive two of Life Orb Calyrex-S's Astral Barrages and two of Lunala's Moongeist Beams.
  • The EV spread allows Raging Bolt to survive Glacial Lance from 116 Attack Adamant Calyrex-I, Icicle Crash from Jolly Chien-Pao, and Close Combat from Life Orb Koraidon. The Special Defense investment lets Raging Bolt survive Life Orb Landorus's Earth Power, two of Life Orb Calyrex-S's Astral Barrages, and Miraidon's Draco Meteor and Electro Drift after Terastallizing. The Speed investment lets Raging Bolt outspeed Landorus after a speed drop while outspeeding Calyrex-S and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R in Tailwind.
  • Tera Electric is a great option to let Raging Bolt consistently 2HKO Flutter Mane, Calyrex-S, and Incineroar with Thunderbolt. Tera Fairy is a good general defensive typing to let it take Zamazenta-C's Body Press and become immune to Dragon-type moves from Miraidon and opposing Raging Bolt.

Teambuilding

  • Raging Bolt can struggle against Pokemon such as Focus Sash Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane, as both can survive attacks from Raging Bolt and hit it for big damage with Ice Spinner, Icicle Crash, or Moonblast.
  • Raging Bolt has bad matchups against Ground-type Pokemon like Landorus and Ursaluna, which are immune to Electric-type attacks and threaten Raging Bolt. Pokemon with Fake Out, such as Incineroar and Iron Hands, can also do well against this set, as it cannot use Protect to get around Fake Out, and both can take Raging Bolt's attacks well, allowing them to use Parting Shot or Low Kick in return.
  • Raging Bolt synergizes with sun setters like Koraidon, as sun boosts Raging Bolt's Special Attack through Protosynthesis while Raging Bolt provides support for Koraidon against Kyogre. Raging Bolt also supports Pokemon like Calyrex-S against Tornadus and Urshifu-R with Thunderclap and helps Pokemon such as Calyrex-I and Zamazenta-C in the Koraidon matchup.
  • Non-Restricted Pokemon like Urshifu-R and Chien-Pao pair nicely with Raging Bolt by hitting Ground- and Grass-type Pokemon such as Landorus and Rillaboom that Raging Bolt may be bad against. Incineroar is another great partner for Raging Bolt, being able to switch into threats like Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane and weaken Iron Hands and the aforementioned Chien-Pao with Intimidate. Encore Calyrex-S and Incineroar as well as other Fake Out users like Rillaboom help combat opposing Fake Out with Encore or their own Fake Out.

Bulky Attacker.description:
Raging Bolt is an incredibly bulky special attacker that can stay on the field and survive hits from Restricted Pokemon, and threaten them back with its huge Special Attack stat and weaken their team with stat reducing moves. It matches up incredibly well into Urshifu-R, keeping it in check with Thunderclap, Koraidon, since it commonly doesn't run Dragon-type moves, common Fire / Water / Grass cores, which usually have Incineroar, Rillaboom, and Urshifu-R or Ogerpon-W, and multiple strong special attackers with Snarl, such as Kyogre, Calyrex-S, and Terapagos. Electroweb gives Raging Bolt a solid speed control option while still dealing relevant damage. Thunderbolt is a consistent and strong STAB option, and Volt Switch gives it a strong way to reposition itself. Assault Vest allows it to survive hits more easily from strong special attackers such as Calyrex-S, Terapagos, Kyogre, Flutter Mane, and opposing Raging Bolt while punishing them with a Snarl, Electroweb, or stronger attacking move. The EV spread allows it to avoid the 2HKO from Choice Specs Astral Barrage from Calyrex-S, survive an Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao, and outspeed -1 Gholdengo and Adamant Urshifu. Tera Electric significantly increases the damage it does at the cost of remaining vulnerable to strong Ground-type attackers such as Landorus and Groudon, while Tera Fairy allows it to gain an immunity to threatening Dragon-type attacks from the likes of Miraidon and opposing Raging Bolt while still having a very strong defensive typing into the current metagame.

Raging Bolt synergizes well with multiple Pokemon and can work on many team structures, but some notable partners are Incineroar, since it can reduce the threat from physical moves that Raging Bolt cannot weaken, Koraidon, since it activates Raging Bolt's ability Protosynthesis by setting up sun, and Urshifu-R, which checks multiple strong threats to Raging Bolt like Calyrex-I, Flutter Mane, Chien-Pao, and Landorus. Another Pokemon that checks Raging Bolt is Amoonguss, since Raging Bolt can't stop a Spore from going off and Raging Bolt's attacks can be redirected by Rage Powder without many issues. It is also vulnerable to Fake Out, since Raging Bolt is unable to use Protect to block it because of its Assault Vest, and variants without Draco Meteor can't threaten Incineroar for high damage, allowing it to use Parting Shot and pivot out relatively safely.

Three Attacks.description:
Raging Bolt is a strong special attacker that uses its good natural bulk and offensive typing to survive attacks and respond with strong Electric- and Dragon-type moves. Draco Meteor gives Raging Bolt a one-time nuke, while Dragon Pulse is a more consistent option for Life Orb sets. Thunderclap allows Raging Bolt to threaten faster Pokemon like Choice Scarf Urshifu-R before they can move. Booster Energy and Life Orb both allow Raging Bolt to deal more damage at the cost of either losing its boost on switch or taking recoil. Life Orb is used on sun teams, as its boost can stack with the Protosynthesis boost. Tera Electric boosts Thunderbolt and Thunderclap, allowing Raging Bolt to OHKO Pokemon such as bulky Kyogre with Thunderbolt and Urshifu-R with Thunderclap if Urshifu-R Terastallizes into a neutral type, as well as 2HKOing Calyrex-I with Thunderbolt. Tera Fairy makes Raging Bolt immune to Dragon-type attacks like Miraidon's Draco Meteor in addition to being a good neutral type.

Raging Bolt struggles into bulky Pokemon such as Amoonguss and Ting-Lu that resist or are immune to Thunderbolt, survive Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse, and respond with Spore or a super effective attack. Faster offensive Pokemon like Miraidon, Zacian-C, and Landorus are also a problem for Raging Bolt, as they can threaten to OHKO it. Calyrex-I threatens the Grass-, Ground-, and Dragon-types that resist Thunderbolt, as well as setting up Trick Room to help Raging Bolt with faster threats. Raging Bolt can also hit the Water-types that resist Glacial Lance with Thunderbolt or Thunderclap. Pokemon that can set up sun such as Koraidon also pair well with Raging Bolt, as they allow it to get a Protosynthesis boost in addition to Life Orb. Raging Bolt can support them by threatening Water-types that resist Flare Blitz or by removing Pelipper, which is a common check to sun teams.

Calm Mind.description:
Raging Bolt's good natural bulk allows it to function well as a bulky setup sweeper. It has good matchups against Kyogre and Urshifu-R due to STAB Thunderclap. Dragon Pulse is commonly used to break Pokemon that resist Thunderclap, like opposing Raging Bolt and Miraidon. Dragon Pulse may also aid against Pokemon with redirection like Ogerpon-W or Armor Tail Farigiraf that blocks Thunderclap. Leftovers is the preferred item on Calm Mind Raging Bolt due to the increased longevity, especially when paired with Grassy Terrain support from Rillaboom. Alternatively, Raging Bolt can use Booster Energy for an immediate power boost, threatening an OHKO on Miraidon and a 2HKO on Calyrex-S. 244 HP and 52 Defense EVs allow Raging Bolt to survive Adamant Chien-Pao's Ice Spinner. The HP and Special Defense EVs allow +1 Special Defense Terastallized Raging Bolt to survive two attacks from both Modest Flutter Mane's Moonblast and Landorus's Earth Power. 92 Speed EVs allow Raging Bolt to outspeed 4 Speed Rillaboom. Tera Fairy is the Tera type of choice because it provides Raging Bolt an even matchup into most of the format.

Good partners for Calm Mind Raging Bolt include Rillaboom because it can provide Grassy Terrain and create free turns with Fake Out, allowing Raging Bolt to set up more safely. Similarly, Incineroar is often paired with Raging Bolt, since it can offer damage reduction and Fake Out support. Redirection, such as Ogerpon-W's Follow Me, is greatly appreciated by Raging Bolt. Groudon and Koraidon are also good partners for Raging Bolt, since they can activate its Protosynthesis ability and check Pokemon like Amoonguss and Zacian-C, which are common checks for Raging Bolt. Amoonguss threatens Raging Bolt's Thunderclap via Rage Powder redirection and Spore. Zacian-C, Groudon, Choice Specs Flutter Mane, Calyrex-I, and Landorus can threaten Raging Bolt before and after it Terastallizes.

Assault Vest.description:
• Electroweb is sometimes run over Thunderbolt for speed control. Volt Switch allows for Raging Bolt to become a bulky pivot and pairs well with Draco Meteor, allowing it to switch out after the Special Attack drop. Snarl weakens opposing special attackers, enabling it to sit on the field for longer and deal damage. Tera Blast gives Raging Bolt a strong option into bulky Dark-types and Fighting-types like Ting-Lu and Iron Hands.

  • Assault Vest allows Raging Bolt to fully take advantage of its amazing bulk, letting it sit on the field and tank hit after hit all while dealing respectable damage and disrupting the foe with moves like Snarl and Electroweb.

  • The defensive investment allows Raging Bolt to always survive Icicle Crash from Adamant Chien-Pao and Moonblast from Choice Specs Flutter Mane. The Speed investment allows Raging Bolt to outspeed Glimmora and Modest Chi-Yu after an Electroweb. The rest of the EVs were put into offensive investment.

  • Tera Fairy is just an incredibly strong neutral Tera type, especially for a Pokemon with as much bulk as Raging Bolt has, and provides a resistance to Urshifu-S's STAB moves.

3 Attacks.description:
• Thunderbolt provides good consistent damage, especially with Tera Electric, while Thunderclap helps make up for Raging Bolt's middling Speed. Draco Meteor is a more powerful option, being able to OHKO Pokémon like Landorus when used with Booster Energy. However, it can be forced to switch out after a Special Attack drop and lose the boost.

  • Booster Energy is a strong option, as boosting Raging Bolt's already huge base Special Attack even further turns it into an absolute nuke. Safety Goggles prevents Amoonguss from redirecting Thunderclaps away from Urshifu-R.

  • The Speed investment allows Raging Bolt to outspeed Dragapult, Flutter Mane, and Chien-Pao while under Tailwind, allowing it to hit them with its stronger options like Thunderbolt and Draco Meteor.

  • Tera Grass is a good option to not only resist Ground-type moves from Landorus but also ignore Amoonguss's Spore and redirection with Rage Powder without running Safety Goggles. Tera Electric will often be a consistent option for just raw damage output.

Assault Vest.description: -The given EV spread allows Raging Bolt to survive Icicle Crash from Chien-Pao and outspeed Flutter Mane during Tailwind, allocating the remaining EVs into Special Attack.

Offensive.description: • The alternative EV spread allows Raging Bolt to outspeed the vast majority of Tapu Fini in order to immediately threaten an OHKO with Thunderbolt.

Calm Mind.description:
Raging Bolt's amazing bulk, high Special Attack stat, and great typing both defensively and offensively allow it to become a dangerous wallbreaker and sweeper, threatening common defensive pieces like Toxapex, Moltres, and Zapdos. Draco Meteor brings Raging Bolt exceptional power, allowing it to OHKO Ground-types like Landorus-T, Garchomp, a Great Tusk trying to switch into it, the former with a Calm Mind boost. However, Dragon Pulse is a great option if you want consistent damage, threatening the opposition for longer at a time. Weather Ball is an amazing option when paired with weather teams, as it removes Grass-types like Ferrothorn and Rillaboom in sun and threatens Ground-types like Ting-Lu and Iron Treads in rain. Dragonium Z gives Raging Bolt a one-time nuke, letting it obliterate most non-resistant foes, such as Gliscor and Galarian Slowking, with a Calm Mind boost, opening up its teammates. Do note that Dragonium Z should only be used with Draco Meteor, as the damage reduction with Dragon Pulse is quite noticeable. Booster Energy boosts Raging Bolt's Special Attack, allowing it to get OHKOs on Pokemon that it would normally run from, such as Iron Valiant with Thunderclap and Gliscor with Draco Meteor, both at +1. Leftovers lets it switch into Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y and Ogerpon-W more consistently, allowing it to set up easily.

Raging Bolt is best on more offensive teams that appreciate it wearing down other Pokemon like Toxapex, Moltres, and Ting-Lu. Its main weakness is Ground-types like Ting-Lu, Gliscor, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T, as they can come in on a Thunderbolt and threaten it out with a super effective Earthquake. Pokemon like Urshifu-R, Ogerpon-W, and Hisuian Samurott can help remove these foes for Raging Bolt, and in return, it can eliminate bulky Water-types like Toxapex, Alomomola, and Slowbro. Hisuian Samurott in particular, along with Ferrothorn and Heatran, can set up entry hazards for Raging Bolt in order to chip down Pokemon like Ferrothorn and Ting-Lu into KO range of its attacks quicker. Raging Bolt doesn't have the best Speed stat, and that can be taken advantage of by Pokemon like Weavile and Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, which can bypass its Thunderclap either through their own priority for the former or Psychic Terrain for the latter and threaten to KO it. Steel-types like Melmetal, Kingambit, and Mega Scizor help in this regard, as well as absorbing Fairy-type attacks from Pokemon like Mega Diancie and Iron Valiant; Kingambit can also threaten Galarian Slowking and Mega Latios, two Pokemon that Raging Bolt has trouble with. In return, Raging Bolt can chip down Toxapex, Moltres, and Zamazenta for Kingambit’s own sweep later in the game. Finally, Raging Bolt fits very well on weather-based teams. On sun teams, Raging Bolt's Protosynthesis is activated, allowing it to hit harder; it also synergizes well with Mega Charizard Y, as Mega Charizard Y can switch into the Ground-type moves that Raging Bolt baits out while also dealing with Ferrothorn. In return, Raging Bolt can deal with Toxapex, Moltres, and Dragonite, which would otherwise give Mega Charizard Y trouble. Rain, on the other hand, gives Raging Bolt a Weather Ball capable of demolishing the Ground-types that would otherwise give it much trouble. In return, Raging Bolt provides a check for Grass- and Electric-types like Rillaboom, Zapdos, and Ogerpon-W that would give rain teams trouble.

Pivot.description:
Raging Bolt is an excellent pivot, using its stellar offensive presence and ability to force out Pokemon such as Toxapex, Zapdos, and Moltres to gain momentum for its teammates. Not only that, Raging Bolt's solid defensive typing makes it have favorable matchups against Pokemon like Ogerpon-W and Mega Charizard Y. Thunderclap is a useful form of priority, being the main way Raging Bolt threatens out faster threats such as Urshifu-R, Iron Valiant, and Mega Medicham. Draco Meteor gives Raging Bolt the ability to hit Pokemon that would effortlessly block Volt Switch, such as Landorus-T and Gliscor. Taunt is an option over Thunderbolt, allowing Raging Bolt to stop entry hazards from being set up by the likes of Heatran and Ferrothorn and deny recovery for Pokemon like Mega Scizor, Blissey, and Garganacl. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Raging Bolt pivot safely in the face of hazards, particularly Spikes, while Dragonium Z gives Raging Bolt the ability to OHKO Gliscor and Landorus-T and muscle through weakened checks like Garganacl and Mega Tyranitar. Alternatively, Leftovers grants Raging Bolt more longevity to check Pokemon like Mega Charizard Y, Ogerpon-W, and Urshifu-R more consistently. When using Heavy-Duty Boots, an EV spread with maximum Special Attack and Speed is preferred. However, the second EV spread ensures Raging Bolt outspeeds defensive Landorus-T while also surviving a Landorus-T's Earthquake after Stealth Rock.

Raging Bolt fits best on bulky offense and balance teams, where its pivoting abilities are much appreciated to keep momentum and bring in wallbreakers such as Mega Medicham and Kingambit against Pokemon like Ferrothorn, Galarian Slowking, and Mega Tyranitar. Raging Bolt checking Ogerpon-W and Tornadus-T is appreciated by teammates such as Alomomola and Great Tusk. In return, Alomomola provides Wish support, making up for Raging Bolt's poor longevity, and Great Tusk removes Spikes, which cut into Raging Bolt lacking Heavy-Duty Boots. Due to Raging Bolt's lack of power, it loves the Spikes set by teammates like Samurott-H and Ferrothorn, chipping down its checks such as opposing Ferrothorn and Heatran. Raging Bolt is also hindered by Ground-types that easily outpace it such as Garchomp and Great Tusk, since they also block its Volt Switch, stopping it from gaining momentum. Teammates that check these foes, such as Moltres and Landorus-T, are good partners for Raging Bolt.

battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Offensive EV Benchmarks

  • 44 SpA: This lets Thunderclap OHKO offensive Urshifu-R.

  • 140 SpA: This 2HKOes Modest Ursaluna-B that have maximum HP and Special Defense investment with Tera Blast + Draco Meteor if using Booster Energy.

  • 204 SpA: This lets +2 Thunderbolt OHKO offensive Flutter Mane.

Defensive EV Benchmarks

  • 140 HP This is the minimum amount of HP needed to survive Annihilape's Final Gambit.

  • 148 HP / 20 Def: This lets Raging Bolt survive +1 Jolly Ogerpon-H's Play Rough.

  • 140 HP / 76 SpD: This avoid a 2HKO from Timid Flutter Mane after Sitrus Berry Raging Bolt has a Calm Mind boost.

  • 140 HP / 108 Def: This survives Adamant Choice Band Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch.

  • 140 HP / 180 Def: This survives Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquale and Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash.

  • 20 HP / 172 Def: This is the most EV efficient way to survive Adamant Choice Band Chien-Pao's Tera-boosted Crunch, at the cost of being OHKOed by Annihilape's Final Gambit.

Assault Vest EV Benchmarks

  • 140 HP / 92 SpD: This survives Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast.

  • 140 HP / 132 SpD: This avoids a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast after Stealth Rock damage if Raging Bolt is Terastallized.

Speed EV Benchmarks

  • 44 Spe: This outspeeds minimum Speed Dragonite.

  • 76 Spe: This outspeeds maximum Speed Modest Ursaluna-B.

  • 132 Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Ursaluna, a rare but powerful threat against Raging Bolt.

  • 156 Spe: This outspeeds Timid Ursaluna-B.

  • 220 Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Breloom, a rare threat that can stop Raging Bolt's sweeps with Spore.

  • 196+ Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Basculegion.

  • 204+ Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Dragonite.

  • 244+ Spe: This outspeeds Modest Archaludon.

Bulky Offense.description:
• Raging Bolt's decent defensive typing, hefty bulk, and booming priority in Thunderclap make it an excellent bulky offensive Pokemon.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge versus Volt Switch: Volt Switch makes Raging Bolt a great pivot, but it does mean that Raging Bolt lacks a reliable Electric-type STAB move or has worse coverage, making Thunderbolt a reasonable alternative. Discharge's higher paralysis chance can make the power drop worth it if using slow teammates like Ursaluna-B.

  • Heavy Slam: When used with a Quiet nature, Heavy Slam OHKOes offensive Flutter Mane! If using Modest, it'll still put most Flutter Mane into Thunderclap's KO range as well.

  • Modest versus Quiet: Quiet is mainly used for OHKOing offensive Flutter Mane with Heavy Slam, but even with that move, Modest makes sense if your team requires Speed investment.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Raging Bolt's good typing means Terastallization does have some drawbacks, such as making Urshifu-R harder to switch-into, but it has enough common weaknesses to types like Ground and Fairy that mean Terastallization will often be optimal.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is a fantastic defensive typing, making Raging Bolt a spectacular check to most Urshifu-S and prancing around strong Dragon-type attacks.

  • Steel: Retaining the common Ground weakness is unfortunate, but Tera Steel makes up for it by tanking Fairy-type attacks and shredding Flutter Mane with Heavy Slam.

  • Ice: When used with Tera Blast, Tera Ice chills Landorus-T to the bone and deals tremendous damage to Ursaluna-B without firing off Draco Meteor.

  • Water: Tera Water gives Raging Bolt a cool resistance to Ice-type attacks from the likes of Chien-Pao while still retaining the Surging Strikes resistance against Urshifu-R. Just watch out for Tera Electric Chien-Pao.

  • Electric: Tera Electric makes sense for making Thunderclap an even more effective revenge killing tool and ridding Raging Bolt of its Fairy and Dragon weaknesses.

  • Bug: This niche Tera type grants Raging Bolt a resistance to Ground without making it weak to Ice.

EV Spread Examples

  • 148 HP / 156 Def / 204 SpA with Modest or Quiet: This survives both Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquake and Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash on all but the highest roll of damage, and it also OHKOes offensive Flutter Mane with +2 Thunderbolt.

  • 148 HP / 20 Def / 180 SpA / 4 SpD / 156 Spe with Modest: This spread outspeeds the rare but dangerous Timid Ursaluna-B while avoiding an OHKO from Timid Flutter Mane's unboosted Moonblast and +1 Ogerpon-H's Play Rough.

  • 140 HP / 236 SpA / 132 SpD with Modest or Quiet: These EVs are optimized for Assault Vest, letting Terastallized Raging Bolt to avoid a 2HKO from Timid Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Moonblast after Stealth Rock damage.

Items

  • Rocky Helmet: Rocky Helmet lets Raging Bolt punish Urshifu-R that lack Punching Glove for using Surging Strikes, since most Urshiu-R will switch out from Raging Bolt.

  • Booster Energy: Booster Energy gives Raging Bolt a useful increase in power, with Thunderbolt now OHKOing Primarina that lack Assault Vest. However, it doesn't work well with Volt Switch and will usually tell your opponent that you aren't carrying it.

  • Weakness Policy: Raging Bolt is bulky enough to take full advantage of Weakness Policy, turning Thunderclap into a vicious cleaning tool!

  • Assault Vest: Raging Bolt's excellent bulk and pivoting prowess make it a great user of Assault Vest.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry's quick burst of recovery is especially helpful when Terastallized into a type that doesn't resist Water against Urshifu-R. Just make sure to use an even HP number to eat the Berry after being hit by Ruination once.

  • Choice Specs: Choice Specs transforms Raging Bolt into a fearsome wallbreaking pivot! However, it makes Thunderclap even riskier to use.

Calm Mind.description:
• Raging Bolt's incredible bulk and access to the crackling Thunderclap make it one of the most dangerous special attackers in the metagame!

  • Dragon Pulse versus Draco Meteor: Dragon Pulse is a reliable STAB attack against Ground-type foes. Draco Meteor is harder to sweep teams with, but it severely damages Assault Vest Ursaluna-B enough that it's worth considering.

  • Thunderbolt versus Discharge: A reliable Electric-type attack ensures that the risky Thunderclap isn't Raging Bolt's only option against Water-types, with Thunderbolt offering a tad more power, while Discharge's 30% paralysis rate is helpful for slow teammates like Ursaluna-B and Basculegion.

  • Volt Switch with Draco Meteor: Volt Switch may seem completely contrary to sweeping with Calm Mind boosts, but it can be combined with Draco Meteor to transform Raging Bolt into a wallbreaking pivot rather than a bulky sweeper.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Medium: Raging Bolt's common weaknesses like Ground and Fairy, combined with its awesome bulk, makes it a good candidate for Terastallization to prevent revenge kills.

  • Fairy: Tera Fairy is a brilliant defensive typing, ruining Dragon-type attacks and transforming Raging Bolt into a good Urshifu-S check in a pinch.

  • Water: Tera Water is perfect for soaking up Ice-type attacks from Chien-Pao while still resisting Urshifu-R's Surging Strikes.

  • Electric: In addition to removing the annoying Fairy and Dragon weaknesses, Tera Electric makes Thunderclap an even more fearsome priority attack!

  • Ice: Tera Ice is awful defensively, but when paired with Tera Blast, Raging Bolt can freeze specially defensive Landorus-T's smug grin off with an OHKO!

  • Steel Steel unfortunately retains that annoying Ground weakness, but the resistance to Dragon and Fairy is good enough to consider it against threats like Flutter Mane and offensive Archaludon.

  • Bug: This niche Tera type gives Raging Bolt a Ground resistance without an Ice weakness that would doom it against Chien-Pao like Tera Flying would.

Items

  • Leftovers: Leftovers rewards Raging Bolt's longevity more than any item, making it the prime cut of items.

  • Rocky Helmet: With Rocky Helmet, Raging Bolt can consistently punish Choice Scarf Urshifu-R for using Surging Strikes, giving it the perfect chance to set up Calm Mind as Urshifu-R switches out.

  • Sitrus Berry: Sitrus Berry can be used with specalized EV spreads to prevent some useful 2HKOs. Just make sure to use an even HP stat so it's eaten after Raging Bolt is hit by Ruination one time.

  • Booster Energy: Booster Energy is a more immediately offensive approach to Raging Bolt, letting it deal good damage without needing to set up Calm Mind.

  • Figy, Aguav, Mago, Iapapa, or Wiki Berry: These berries restore more health than Sitrus Berry, though the 25% HP activation does make them riskier.

EV Spread Examples

  • 140 HP / 180 Def / 44 SpA / 140 SpD / 4 Spe: This spread survives Annihilape's Final Gambit, Adamant Landorus-T's Earthquake, and Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash. It also OHKOes offensive Urshifu-R with Thunderclap and survives Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast after Stealth Rock damage.

  • 148 HP / 20 Def / 180 SpA / 4 SpD / 156 Spe with Modest: This Raging Bolt is fast enough to outspeed Timid Ursaluna-B, a rare but potentially game-ending threat! The defensive investment ensures that Raging Bolt survives a +1 Play Rough from Jolly Ogerpon-H and Moonblast from Timid Flutter Mane.

  • 140 HP / 4 Def / 244 SpA / 76 SpD / 44 Spe: This lets Sitrus Berry Raging Bolt avoid a 2HKO from Timid Flutter Mane's Moonblast after Raging Bolt boosts with Calm Mind, and it also outspeeds minimum Speed Dragonite.

Wallbreaker.description: Raging Bolt stands out as one of the premier special wallbreakers in the tier, boasting exceptional offensive stats and a formidable STAB combination. Lucarionite further amplifies its breaking power by granting it Adaptability and substantial stat boosts, whereas Diancite can be used to significantly raise its Speed stat, albeit at the cost of some firepower and bulk. Timid nature helps Diancite Raging Bolt outspeed Great Tusk, Arceus formes, and Eternatus; a Modest nature allows Lucarionite Raging Bolt to reach feats like OHKOing offensive Arceus-Ground after minimal entry hazard chip damage. Raging Bolt utilizes Draco Meteor for its immense firepower and hit-and-run potential with Volt Switch. Thunderbolt and Discharge provide options for either dealing more damage or fishing for paralysis, respectively. Additionally, Thunderclap allows Raging Bolt to reverse kill Pokemon such as Urshifu-R and Basculegion formes, and Volt Switch enables it go function as a strong pivot. Raging Bolt may also utilize moves such as Calm Mind and Substitute to serve as a devastating progress maker at the cost of Volt Switch's utility or Thunderclap's priority. It synergizes exceptionally well with pivots like Urshifu-R, Magearna, and Pecharunt to form incredible VoltTurn cores; Urshifu-R and the Latiasite versions of the latter two also deal with Ground-types such as Arceus-Ground and Great Tusk, with the former being able to check Blissey as well. Offensive partners such as Spectrier, Calm Mind Arceus formes, and Zamazenta also aid in dismantling opposing defensive cores and thus synergize well with Raging Bolt. Pairing Raging Bolt with hazard setters such as Hearthflame Mask Great Tusk and Magearna helps it secure KOs more efficiently, especially against foes such as Arceus formes. It faces troubles against Pixilate Extreme Speed users such as Dragonite and Regieleki; thus, it is usually paired with Pokemon such as Pecharunt and Arceus-Ground to deal with them.

doublesou.overview: Assault Vest Raging Bolt makes the most of its titanic statline to check a variety of threats in the tier while leveraging disruptive utility moves to dictate the pace of battle for its teammates. Its monstrous Special Attack stat allows it to put out high damage with minimal investment and focus on maximizing its bulk, stat checking a large variety of special attackers present in the format. However, Raging Bolt sports an abysmal matchup against Landorus and a poor matchup against Ursaluna-B, two of the most common special wallbreakers in the format, as it can't threaten enough damage to incapacitate them or use its powerful Electric-Type STAB moves safely around them. Additionally, Raging Bolt's low Speed leaves it vulnerable to Ice-types and other Dragon-types in the format, having to rely on its titanic bulk or Terastallization to survive these matchups. Overall, while Raging Bolt's impressive stats and excellent movepool give it a fantastic toolkit that can impact almost any board, its typing hinders it against a large portion of the Doubles metagame's strongest attackers and prevents it from being truly elite.

Assault Vest.description:
• Thunderclap is a useful strong priority attack to clean up weakened foes and circumvent Raging Bolt's middling Speed stat and opposing teams' speed control.

  • Draco Meteor is Raging Bolt's strongest attack, allowing it to OHKO some of the tier's many prominent Dragon-types such as Gouging Fire, Dragonite, and Roaring Moon and providing a solid way to chunk incoming Ground-types such as Landorus.

  • Thunderbolt is Raging Bolt's most consistent STAB move, allowing it to OHKO maximum HP Tornadus with the given EVs and 2HKO Terastallized Ogerpon-W.

  • Snarl is a fantastic disruptive tool that allows Raging Bolt to prevent opposing special attackers from making significant progress, letting it exploit its stellar bulk and typing to enter battle against common special attacking threats in Chi-Yu, Gholdengo, and Iron Crown. Snarl also makes it difficult for common special wallbreakers like Landorus, Ursaluna-B, and Regidrago to find entry points on Raging Bolt to remove it, having their damage severely reduced if they switch in directly.

  • Electroweb is a good disruptive STAB option to hinder speed control from Tornadus, hit both foes for solid damage, and make it difficult for non-Ground-types to find safe entry.

  • Volt Switch is an option to allow Raging Bolt to use its great bulk and low Speed to act as a pivot, providing safe entry points for aggressive partners such as Landorus and Chien-Pao against targets such as Gholdengo.

  • Snarl is a great option for bulky structures centered around Pokemon like Diancie and Okidogi that don't like facing the tier's common special wallbreakers. Electroweb is typically best on teams centered around strong wallbreakers like Landorus and Ogerpon-H that focus on maintaining a Speed advantage to burst through enemy teams. Volt Switch is best on offensive teams that appreciate Raging Bolt's fantastic bulk to slowly pivot and bring in devastating threats like Choice Scarf Chi-Yu and Chien-Pao.

  • Tera Fairy is recommended to make Raging Bolt immune to STAB attacks from the plentiful amount of Dragon-types in the format, including Regidrago, opposing Raging Bolt, and Dragonite, and leverage Raging Bolt's ability to threaten them back; Tera Fairy also provides useful neutralities against Ground- and Ice-type attacks from Landorus, Kyurem, and Chien-Pao. Tera Water is an option for teams that wish to preserve Raging Bolt's ability to check Gholdengo while still providing a typing neutral against Ground-type attacks at the cost of its matchup against the Ogerpon formes and Rillaboom.

  • The given EV spread allows Raging Bolt to survive two Blizzards from Modest Kyurem and almost always withstand Adamant Chien-Pao's Icicle Crash.

  • Assault Vest Raging Bolt leverages its Dragon typing incredibly well against Ogerpon-H and Ogerpon-W by resisting their STAB moves, which allows it to trade incredibly well with them using strong neutral STAB attacks.

  • Raging Bolt is an incredibly potent switch-in to Gholdengo and Iron Crown, as it resists their Steel-type moves and uses Snarl to do solid damage and greatly reduce their damage output, all while largely ignoring their most common partners in Ogerpon and Indeedee-F, respectively. Raging Bolt's incredible bulk and access to priority and Snarl also make it a premier check to Trick Room special attackers, notably using Torkoal's own sun against it for a damage boost and being able to strongly damage it with Thunderclap to mitigate Eruption damage while resisting Fire-type attacks. Snarl also irritates Expanding Force users on full Trick Room teams like Hatterene, Necrozma, and Hoopa-U by lowering their damage output and wasting Trick Room turns, greatly disrupting their gameplan.

  • Raging Bolt greatly benefits from Pokemon that can deal with the powerful Ground-types of the format, as even with Snarl access and Assault Vest, Landorus and Ursaluna-B can quickly break it down. Some ideal partners include Ogerpon-W and Chien-Pao.

  • Teammates like Diancie, Alolan Ninetales, and Rillaboom appreciate Assault Vest Raging Bolt's help in shutting down special attackers like Gholdengo, Tornadus, and Chi-Yu with Snarl. Teammates that can provide healing such as Sinistcha and Amoonguss also appreciate Raging Bolt's ability to slow down the pace of games with Snarl and provide space to heal the team.

  • While not greatly threatened by them, Assault Vest Raging Bolt struggles to make meaningful progress against some of the tier's bulkiest physical attackers such as Ting-Lu, Kingambit, and Iron Hands. All of these Pokemon are largely unfazed by any disruptive or damaging tools Raging Bolt can offer and will require other pieces of the team to deal with them.

  • Assault Vest Raging Bolt can struggle against Chien-Pao, which can use its Speed to circumvent Thunderclap's priority with Sucker Punch and can massively damage Bolt with powerful physical STAB Ice-type moves.

Calm Mind.description:
• Thunderclap lets Raging Bolt circumvent its mediocre Speed to get the jump on offensive threats that otherwise would force it out, such as Chien-Pao, and nab revenge KOs on weakened foes. Thunderbolt can also be used in place of Thunderclap, as the latter can be exploited by redirection like Follow Me as well as Dragon-resistant Pokemon, such as Gholdengo, using stat-boosting moves, like Nasty Plot.

  • Dragon Pulse gives Raging Bolt a way to deal with common Dragon-types, such as Dragonite, Regidrago, and Gouging Fire, as well as the Grass- and Ground-types that aren't threatened by its Electric-type coverage.

  • Calm Mind boosts Raging Bolt's already high Special Attack stat while increasing its special bulk, letting it function as a dangerous win condition that can quickly snowball out of control if left unchecked. Raging Bolt's natural typing also allows it to resist attacks from common physical attackers, such as Ogerpon-W, Ogerpon-H, and Rillaboom, which provides Raging Bolt more opportunities to set up with Calm Mind.

  • Leftovers gives Raging Bolt more staying power, as the passive recovery it provides in conjunction with the stat boosts from Calm Mind makes Raging Bolt harder to KO. It also helps to negate any chip damage that Raging Bolt may receive. Booster Energy provides Raging Bolt with more immediate power at the cost of forgoing the added longevity provided by Leftovers. Covert Cloak can also be used to allow Raging Bolt to ignore the secondary effects of Fake Out, Mortal Spin, and Snarl, which can otherwise be quite troublesome.

  • Tera Fairy offers Raging Bolt a useful immunity to the Dragon-type moves that normally threaten it; this allows it to completely flip the matchup against Regidrago, which would otherwise pose as a big obstacle. Tera Fairy also gives Raging Bolt a more neutral type matchup across the board, aiding it in its role as a bulky setup sweeper. Tera Grass provides Raging Bolt with a resistance to Ground-type moves, which improves its matchups against Landorus and Ursaluna-B, as well as useful immunities to Spore, Rage Powder, and Sleep Powder.

  • The EV spread allows Raging Bolt to survive an Ice Spinner from Life Orb Chien-Pao and a +2 Kowtow Cleave from Kingambit.

  • Raging Bolt pairs well with Pokemon that provide it with opportunities for setting up with Calm Mind, such as Fake Out users like Rillaboom and Incineroar as well as redirection support from the likes of Ogerpon-W and Amoonguss. Raging Bolt also pairs well with Landorus, which can beat the Steel- and Fairy-types such as Kingambit, Diancie, and Gholdengo that Raging Bolt struggles with; conversely, Raging Bolt is strong against the Flying-types that can freely switch in on Landorus's Ground-type STAB moves and the Water-types such as Ogerpon-W that offensively threaten it. Raging Bolt also pairs well with Sinistcha, as the latter provides additional longevity with its ability Hospitality while helping to cover for the former's Ground-type weakness with the redirection provided by Rage Powder.

Calm Mind (Electric).description: Calm Mind Raging Bolt is a potent wallbreaker and setup sweeper for Electric teams, possessing a high Special Attack, excellent defenses, and incredible priority in Thunderclap to pick off faster foes like Sneasler and Ceruledge. With Devastating Drake, Raging Bolt breaks through bulkier targets like Mega Venusaur and Archaludon, and it also applies tremendous pressure on bulky Ground-types, having a high chance to KO Gliscor without a boost, OHKOing specially defensive Swampert at +1, and providing good odds to OHKO Water Absorb Clodsire at +1. With its typing, Raging Bolt switches in against foes like Mega Charizard Y and Ogerpon-W and threatens them out with its STAB moves. Thunderclap lets Raging Bolt revenge kill faster threats like Greninja and Enamorus as well as Iron Valiant at +1. 136 Speed EVs allow Raging Bolt to outspeed Jolly Ursaluna and specially defensive Heatran. Rotom-W and Zapdos provide crucial Ground-immune teammates for the team. Rotom-W can take on threats like Sand Rush Excadrill, Mega Swampert, and Choice Scarf Landorus-T, and Zapdos can remove foes like Ferrothorn and Tapu Bulu and serve an offensive or defensive role, assisting against Ground and Fighting teams. Tapu Koko threatens Dragon- and Dark-types like Latios, Hydreigon, and Weavile, and with Grass Knot and Hidden Power Ice, it helps in alleviating Ground matchups, removing threats like Landorus. Tapu Koko also sets Electric Terrain to boost Raging Bolt's Electric-type moves, most notably allowing it to OHKO bulkier threats like Mega Diancie and Galarian Darmanitan with +1 Thunderclap. Iron Hands and Choice Band Zeraora eliminate special walls like Hisuian Goodra and Blissey as well as Ferrothorn while also covering Ice- and Dark-types like Kyurem and Mega Tyranitar. Regieleki and Alolan Raichu offer valuable speed control. Regieleki possesses incredible natural Speed, outspeeding Choice Scarf Tapu Lele, Iron Valiant, and +1 Volcarona, while Alolan Raichu can outspeed +1 Roaring Moon, Choice Scarf Meowscarada, and even Sand Rush Excadrill when under Electric Terrain. Raging Bolt appreciates entry hazard control from teammates like Rotom-W, Zapdos, and Regieleki.

Swords Dance.description:
Swords Dance Iron Boulder is a usable setup sweeper and speed control in the current metagame, outspeeding already fast and common threats like Booster Energy Iron Valiant and Iron Moth. Earthquake lets it hit Gholdengo, Pecharunt, and Kingambit. Zen Headbutt can be used to improve the matchup against Great Tusk and Zamazenta while hitting Pecharunt harder as well as provide a reliable means of revenge killing Iron Valiant. Close Combat targets Ting-Lu and Kingambit much harder. Substitute is also a viable option to ease Iron Boulder's matchup versus Sucker Punch from Kingambit, with the added benefit of letting it avoid status like Thunder Wave from Galarian Slowking and Will-O-Wisp from Galarian Weezing as it sets up. However, its main use case is with Tera Flying, as the combination allows Iron Boulder to circumvent Gliscor—which otherwise would be a solid check—and turn it into setup fodder by avoiding both Toxic and Earthquake. Running Taunt over Substitute is also an option; aside from still beating Gliscor one-on-one with Tera Flying, it also allows Iron Boulder to overwhelm Skarmory by preventing its Iron Defense and Roost attempts. Tera Fighting boosts the power of Close Combat, notably helping Iron Boulder brute force its way past Skarmory, while also allowing it to OHKO Ting-Lu after a Swords Dance. It also provides a Sucker Punch resistance, which helps versus Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott. Tera Ground can be used to boost the power of Earthquake, guaranteeing the OHKO on bulkier variants of Gholdengo at +2 as well as helping Iron Boulder avoid being picked off by Raging Bolt's Thunderclap.

Iron Boulder's power and its top-tier speed, alongside its good coverage and access to Swords Dance, make it very suitable for hyper offense teams. Teammates such as Kingambit appreciate the weakening of shared checks such as Landorus-T and Skarmory. The same goes for Iron Moth but with Ting-Lu and Gliscor. Iron Valiant also appreciates Gliscor being weakened and can whittle down shared checks such as Gholdengo to make it easier for Iron Boulder to sweep later. Iron Boulder struggles with entry hazard damage putting it in KO range of priority moves such as Kingambit’s Sucker Punch and Rillaboom’s Grassy Glide after Tera. Teammates that are effective at keeping hazards off your side such as Taunt Deoxys-S, Glimmora, Hatterene, or Great Tusk are good partners. The first two also provide their own hazards, facilitating the weakening of Iron Boulder's checks. Iron Boulder also has difficulty overcoming Dondozo. Partners that can weaken it or take advantage of it, such as Kingambit or Ogerpon-W, respectively, are good partners.

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Psychic

Iron Head can be run in order to hit Fairy-types such as Choice Scarf Iron Valiant and Clefable as well as prevent Aurora Veil being set up for Ice teams by threatening Alolan Ninetales, but it doesn't do too much outside of that matchup. It also guarantees an OHKO on Flutter Mane, which Mighty Cleave does not do.

Choice Scarf (Psychic).description:
Iron Boulder is a good Choice Scarf user on Psychic teams thanks to its great Speed tier, allowing it to outspeed other threatening Choice Scarf users like Roaring Moon, Meowscarada, and Hisuian Samurott and threaten them with its respectable power and colorful coverage options. Mighty Cleave is Iron Boulder's main STAB move, allowing it to revenge kill common threats such as non-Choice Scarf Weavile, Choice Specs Flutter Mane after Stealth Rock damage, and Enamorus. Megahorn can be run on this set over Zen Headbutt in order to hit Hoopa-U, Slowbro, and Ogerpon-W. Earthquake provides valuable coverage against Steel-types immune to Close Combat such as non-Air Balloon Gholdengo and Heatran, as well as Poison-types immune to Zen Headbutt like Alolan Muk. Finally, Close Combat allows Iron Boulder to threaten Dark-types such as Greninja and Meowscarada as well as hit most Steel-types for good damage. It also targets major annoyances for Psychic teams such as Blissey and Hisuian Goodra.

Latios is a great teammate for Iron Boulder, as it provides a Ground immunity with Levitate and breaks through threats such as Corviknight and Gliscor with Thunderbolt and Luster Purge. It can also pivot Iron Boulder into threats that it cannot break down on its own, such as Dark-types like Ting-Lu and Bisharp, with Flip Turn. Indeedee is another good pick alongside Iron Boulder, as it offers a Ghost immunity to take on Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball as well as Psychic Terrain support, preventing Iron Boulder from being revenge killed by priority moves such as Sucker Punch from Hisuian Samurott or Aqua Jet from Urshifu-R. Indeedee also provides Healing Wish support to let Iron Boulder clean up weakened teams late-game. Hoopa-U is a dangerous wallbreaker that appreciates Iron Boulder giving it speed control. In return, it can take on Ghost-type attacks such as Choice Scarf Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball pretty handily thanks to its decent Special Defense, while threatening those Ghost-types in return. It can also break through defensive cores Iron Boulder can struggle to beat, such as Corviknight and Landorus-T on Flying or Air Balloon Gholdengo and Corviknight on Steel. Deoxys-S can either soften up opposing teams with its entry hazard support or become a fearsome wallbreaker with Expanding Force while in Psychic Terrain, while threatening Corviknight and Gliscor with Thunderbolt and Ice Beam, respectively. Slowbro is a great physical wall, being able to swallow physical attacks aimed at Iron Boulder like Earthquake from Excadrill and Liquidation from Barraskewda. Slowbro can also serve as a pseudo-check to Ceruledge if it has used its Eject Button, which can give a safe switch-in opportunity for Iron Boulder to take advantage of. Finally, Slowbro can deal with some Dark-types like Ting-Lu one on one with Body Press. Both Metagross and Jirachi can set Stealth Rock to soften up answers to Iron Boulder like Corviknight and Gliscor, and both have other advantages: Metagross has Knock Off to further weaken defensive checks and Bullet Punch to threaten Flutter Mane, while Jirachi can pivot Iron Boulder onto the field with U-turn. Hatterene prevents Iron Boulder from having to take chip damage from hazards when it has to revenge kill a threat while doing fairly well into the majority of Dark-types thanks to its part-Fairy typing.

Choice Scarf (Rock).description:
Iron Boulder is an amazing Choice Scarf user on Rock teams due to its amazing Speed tier and part-Psychic typing, which gives it a key role in the Fighting matchup. Choice Scarf Iron Boulder outspeeds and OHKOes common Choice Scarf users like Sneasler, Meowscarada, and Enamorus; it also outspeeds Regieleki, which can be an issue for Rock teams. Mighty Cleave allows Iron Boulder to take out Choice Scarf Enamorus after Stealth Rock, Ogerpon-H, and Weavile. Zen Headbutt lets Iron Boulder deal with Fighting- and Poison-types like Iron Valiant and Sneasler. Earthquake deals with Heatran, Alolan Muk, and Gholdengo, while Close Combat OHKOes Greninja, Meowscarada, and Roaring Moon.

Choice Band Hisuian Arcanine can act as a wallbreaker for Iron Boulder, being able to take on physical walls such as Toxapex, Corviknight, and defensive Gholdengo with Head Smash and Flare Blitz. Hisuian Arcanine can also run a Heavy-Duty Boots set with Will-O-Wisp to annoy Bisharp. Swords Dance Ogerpon-C is an excellent partner, being able to handle Ground- and Water-types such as Mamoswine, Quagsire, and Keldeo. Glimmora is a nice special attacker that deals with walls Iron Boulder can't break through, like Quagsire and Sableye, with its colorful coverage. Glimmora's Toxic Debris comes in handy in the Fairy matchup as well, and it even removes entry hazards with Mortal Spin. Shell Smash Minior can act as a setup sweeper, being able to dent holes in Great Tusk and Iron Hands so that Iron Boulder can pick them off late-game; providing a Ground immunity for the team is also much appreciated. Kleavor can set up Stealth Rock with Stone Axe, breaking Focus Sashes on common users like Ceruledge and Cloyster. Terrakion can take out Ursaluna, Bisharp, Archaludon, and Hisuian Goodra for Iron Boulder. Ghost-types like Dragapult, Spectrier, and Choice Scarf Flutter Mane hurt Iron Boulder's chances of sweeping, so Tyranitar serves as a great partner by checking them and providing sand to boost the team's Special Defense. Coalossal is a good partner, being able to check threats like Scizor, Corviknight, and Skarmory, which would threaten Iron Boulder. Coalossal also removes hazards and can set up its own hazards to ease Iron Boulder's sweeping. In return, Iron Boulder takes out Sneasler, Greninja, and Meowscarada for Tyranitar and Coalossal. IronPress Garganacl can act as a stallbreaker for the team, wearing down defensive Water- and Steel-types such as Gastrodon and Corviknight.

Swords Dance.description: With phenomenal base Speed, Iron Boulder is able to outspeed nearly every threat in the tier, making it a powerful wallbreaker and cleaner for offensive teams. Swords Dance is mandatory for Iron Boulder to break past defensive options like Slowbro and Skarmory. Close Combat allows Iron Boulder to threaten Pokemon such as Tyranitar and Excadrill, which otherwise resist both of its STAB moves. Zen Headbutt lets Iron Boulder immediately threaten Mega Venusaur and Buzzwole, especially at +2, but Earthquake can be used instead to threaten Aegislash. Rockium Z allows Iron Boulder to secure OHKOs against the aforementioned Skarmory and Slowbro, as well as most other neutral targets, like Celesteela and Rotom-W, that would otherwise be able to stomach a +2 Mighty Cleave and threaten Iron Boulder in return. Psychium Z is an alternative, letting Iron Boulder OHKO Mega Venusaur without a Swords Dance boost and threaten certain Rock-resistant foes like Hippowdon, but is generally less consistent. Booster Energy is an option on hyper offensive teams, allowing Iron Boulder to outspeed all Choice Scarf users, at the cost of Iron Boulder's wallbreaking power provided by Z-Crystals. Swords Dance Iron Boulder is generally seen on teams that appreciate its natural Speed and can take advantage of Iron Boulder removing common defensive staples like Clefable and Slowbro. Teammates such as Mienshao and Scizor can take advantage of holes left in the opposing team to sweep and can also weaken these defensive Pokemon to allow Iron Boulder to sweep later. Iron Boulder also appreciates entry hazard support, as even at +2, it can fail to KO many defensive options without hazard damage, so hazard setters like Hippowdon and Excadrill are appreciated. Iron Boulder is also relatively frail, so it appreciates pivots such as Iron Moth and Mienshao that can give it entry against foes such as Skeledirge and Clefable. Given its poor defensive typing, Iron Boulder is also weak to revenge killers such as Scizor, Rillaboom, Mega Aerodactyl, and Azumarill, so teammates that can take hits from these threats, such as Celesteela and Mega Venusaur, are good teammates.

Choice Band.description: With Choice Band, Iron Boulder forgoes sweeping potential to become an instantly threatening, incredibly fast wallbreaker and revenge killer that can consistently threaten out foes like Thundurus and Alakazam while still threatening defensive options like Clefable and Celesteela. The ability to run all of Close Combat, Earthquake, and Zen Headbutt allows Iron Boulder to threaten Garganacl, Aegislash, and Mega Venusaur at the same time. Choice Band Iron Boulder can 2HKO all of these threats, as well as immediately threatening Mega Latias and Celesteela with 2HKOs. Given its phenomenal Speed and instant power, Choice Band Iron Boulder can fit on most teamstyles that can provide it with safe entry. Defensive pivots like Rotom-W, Slowbro, and Clefable can provide it with a solid defensive backbone into options like Azumarill and Mega Aerodactyl that can threaten Iron Boulder while also providing entry points against Pokemon like Mega Venusaur and Celesteela. Alternatively, offensive pivots like Greninja and Iron Moth can take advantage of the defensive options that Iron Boulder lures in, such as Hippowdon and Quagsire, as well as the holes it can leave in an opposing team. In return, they provide entry points against foes like Skeledirge and Tyranitar. Despite Iron Boulder's power, it can fail to 2HKO certain defensive options, such as Skarmory, Quagsire, and Hippowdon. Therefore, entry hazard support from Clefable and Skarmory is appreciated. Teammates that can break through these physical walls, such as Iron Moth and Hydrapple, are also good partners.

Swords Dance.description:
Iron Boulder is a niche sweeper, sporting an excellent Speed stat that allows it to threaten out slower Pokemon like Iron Moth, Latios, and Azelf, as well as allowing it to find opportunities to set up a Swords Dance to sweep or clean up teams with its extremely strong Sharpness-boosted Mighty Cleave and Psycho Cut. Sacred Sword gives Iron Boulder a way to take down Ting-Lu, Kingambit, and Iron Treads that otherwise wall both of its STAB moves; Earthquake lets Iron Boulder still hit Iron Treads while also taking down non-Levitate Gholdengo; and Throat Chop mainly allows for Iron Boulder to take down Levitate Gholdengo, although it is important to note that most Levitate Gholdengo sets use Colbur Berry and can survive a Swords Dance-boosted Throat Chop, so removing the Colbur Berry off of Gholdengo ahead of time is advised.

Iron Boulder provides great support for stronger wallbreakers such as Kingambit, Iron Hands, and Zamazenta, with Iron Boulder either being able to weaken or take down their checks such as Great Tusk, Pecharunt, and Manaphy as well as take on Pokemon faster than them like Roaring Moon and Cobalion. Iron Boulder is also helpful for being able to clean up after they've weakened everything on the opponent's team. Iron Boulder struggles to find a way onto the battlefield as well as deal with most Pokemon that are faster than it such as Chien-Pao, Zamazenta, and Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, so having defensive Pokemon that can check them like Manaphy, Pecharunt, and Corviknight while also providing entrances for Iron Boulder through pivoting is very appreciated.

Swords Dance (Psychic).description: With a high Speed tier and a diverse movepool complemented by a Z-Crystal, Swords Dance Iron Boulder solidifies itself as one of Psychic's premier wallbreakers and cleaners, threatening otherwise difficult to answer foes like Ting-Lu and Celesteela. Mighty Cleave is a strong and spammable STAB option that threatens Fire-, Flying-, Bug-, and Ice-types like the Mega Charizard formes, Tornadus-T, Volcarona, and Kyurem, making it a valuable asset against these teams. Continental Crush provides Iron Boulder with an incredible nuke, outright OHKOing Gliscor and Celesteela at +2 and OHKOing Slowbro and Mega Venusaur at +2 after minimal chip damage. Close Combat targets Steel‑, Rock-, and Dark‑types such as Hisuian Goodra, Mega Tyranitar, and Hydreigon, while All-Out Pummeling allows Iron Boulder to OHKO Archaludon and physically defensive Ting‑Lu at +2. Earthquake, in addition to hitting the aforementioned Steel‑ and Rock-types, also threatens Gholdengo, Poison‑types like Alolan Muk, and Electric‑types like Iron Hands. If running Rockium Z, Iron Boulder can struggle against Archaludon and Ting-Lu, and if it opts for Fightinium Z, it struggles to break through bulky foes like Slowbro, Celesteela, Gliscor, and Mega Venusaur. Teammates such as Mega Gallade, Tapu Lele, Mega Alakazam, Victini, and Deoxys-S can help circumvent these threats. Alternatively, Deoxys-S can set up dual screens for easier setup and provide entry hazard support, making it easier for Iron Boulder to break through them. Tapu Lele eliminates Mega Sableye and sets up Psychic Terrain to block priority moves like Sucker Punch from Bisharp and Cinderace, Aqua Jet from Azumarill, and Bullet Punch from Mega Scizor; it can also outright remove Mega Scizor if it runs Hidden Power Fire. Similarly, Victini can support Iron Boulder by eliminating Mega Scizor. Choice Scarf Latias provides excellent speed control, handling Choice Scarf users like Blacephalon while also offering valuable utility in Healing Wish and Trick, which let it give Iron Boulder a second chance to sweep or neuter its checks like Skarmory. Slowbro leverages its physical bulk and access to Scald and Thunder Wave to support Iron Boulder against threats like Mega Aerodactyl, Choice Scarf Roaring Moon, and Sand Rush Excadrill. Celebi boasts valuable resistances to Ground and Water, which allow it to handle offensive threats like Mega Swampert and Barraskewda, and with Natural Cure, Celebi can also switch into Scald and Toxic, making it a reliable pivot against bulkier targets like Hippowdon and Slowbro.

Choice Scarf (Psychic).description: Choice Scarf Iron Boulder cleaves through speedy threats like opposing Choice Scarf users such as Meowscarada, Enamorus, and Roaring Moon as well as generally fast Pokemon like Ogerpon-W, Mega Lopunny, and Mega Aerodactyl. Close Combat smashes Steel-types aiming to take on Mighty Cleave such as Heatran and Hisuian Goodra and is Iron Boulder's main way to revenge kill the aforementioned Dark-types. Earthquake threatens Alolan Muk, which can swap in against Iron Boulder due to its immunity to Zen Headbutt, and OHKOes Electric-types like Alolan Raichu and Regieleki. Megahorn deals with Ogerpon-W, which greatly threatens Psychic's most common physical wall in Slowbro, while Zen Headbutt lets it clean Fighting teams late-game. Alternatively, Iron Boulder can choose to run Throat Chop to deal with Ghost-types more effectively or Iron Head to finish off Mega Altaria and OHKO Alolan Ninetales and Mega Diancie. Strong wallbreakers like Mega Gallade, Nasty Plot Deoxys-S, Choice Specs Tapu Lele, and Choice Band Victini support Iron Boulder by either greatly weakening or outright removing defensive walls like Celesteela, Archaludon, and Porygon2, which helps it clean Flying, Dragon, and Normal teams late-game. Entry hazards from Jirachi and Deoxys-S are helpful to offset Iron Boulder's mediocre damage. Jirachi can pivot Iron Boulder in with U-turn. Celebi swaps into Ground- and Water-types like Mega Swampert and Ogerpon-W and can utilize a Nasty Plot set to break through Water and Ground teams. Mega Latias swaps into predicted Ground- and Grass-type moves and appreciates Iron Boulder weakening or removing Alolan Muk to attempt to set up a sweep with Calm Mind.

Swords Dance (Rock).description: With the title of being one of Rock's fastest attackers, Iron Boulder can make use of Swords Dance and a Z-Move to become a threatening wallbreaker versus the likes of Fighting- and Steel-types such as Iron Hands with Shattered Psyche and Archaludon with All-Out Pummeling. Iron Boulder can use Shattered Psyche to tear through Fighting- and Poison-types such as Great Tusk, Iron Hands, and Toxapex. Mighty Cleave and Close Combat complement each other, allowing Iron Boulder to deal with Volcarona, Hisuian Goodra, and Galarian Moltres. After a boost, All-Out Pummeling can even break the likes of Archaludon and Ting-Lu. Shuckle can easily set entry hazards to make it easier on Iron Boulder to set up and threaten defensive checks like Heatran. With its secondary Grass typing, Ogerpon-C can break through Water- and Ground-types like Hippowdon and Mega Swampert more easily while also being a secondary setup sweeper that pairs well with Iron Boulder. Mega Diancie, in conjunction with Iron Boulder, can break through Fighting and Dark teams with its Fairy typing and powerful Moonblast, being the best way to remove the likes of Mega Sableye. Thanks to its Fire typing, Hisuian Arcanine can assist in breaking through Steel- and Grass-types such as Gholdengo, Ferrothorn, and Tapu Bulu with Flare Blitz. Mega Aerodacty can assist in the matchup versus the likes of Excadrill once Sticky Web is set , assisting in removing the few foes that outspeed Iron Boulder.

Choice Scarf (Rock).description: As an offensive check to Fighting-types that also compresses speed control by holding a Choice Scarf, outspeeding foes such as Choice Scarf Meowscarada, Choice Scarf Enamorus, and Regieleki, Iron Boulder is a solid ally for Rock teams. Zen Headbutt threatens foes such as Iron Valiant, Sneasler, and Mega Lopunny. Earthquake and Close Combat provide coverage to ease the matchup against certain foes, with the former hitting Jirachi, Alolan Muk, and Tapu Koko, while the latter handles foes such as Ferrothorn, Meowscarada, and Hydreigon. Entry hazards from Pokemon such as Mega Diancie and Shuckle can wear down foes to ease the act for Iron Boulder to KO them; the former can also help offensively handle Dark-types for Iron Boulder. Hisuian Arcanine and Ogerpon-C also can be offensive checks to foes that can force out Iron Boulder as it gets locked into an undesirable move by KOing a foe or causing an outpredicted switch, with the former covering Steel- and Grass-types and the latter checking Water- and Ground-types. These Pokemon also complement each other at overwhelming shared checks such as Iron Hands, Kommo-o, and Skarmory.

Choice Specs.description:
Leveraging its high Special Attack, the strong STAB move in Tachyon Cutter, and good coverage, and pivoting option, Choice Specs Iron Crown is a solid wallbreaker and pivot. Tachyon Cutter being a multi-hit move also lets Iron Crown threaten Kyurem behind a Substitute and Dragonite with Multiscale active. Psyshock lets Iron Crown take on specially defensive walls like Galarian Slowking, Clodsire, and Blissey more easily as well as pressure boosted Calm Mind users like Raging Bolt and Primarina, while Psychic Noise can be used instead to shut down walls like Corviknight and Zapdos from healing in front of it. Volt Switch lets Iron Crown pivot out of Pokemon it would otherwise struggle against while also dealing significant damage to the likes of Corviknight, Alomomola, and Tera Water Garganacl. Focus Blast helps Iron Crown deal with Steel-types like Kingambit and Iron Treads and is its best option to highly damage Ting-Lu. Tera Steel increases the power of Tachyon Cutter, giving it odds to 2HKO even resistant targets like Zapdos and offensive Gholdengo that can otherwise switch in safely. Tera Fighting boosts Focus Blast to the point of guaranteeing a 2HKO on Ting-Lu while also providing a crucial Dark resistance against foes like Kingambit, Darkrai, and Hisuian Samurott.

Choice Specs Iron Crown needs physically offensive teammates like Zamazenta and Dragonite that can reliably remove specially defensive Pokemon like Ting-Lu and Blissey. In return, they benefit from Iron Crown being able to handle physical walls like Clefable and Dondozo. Because Iron Crown will be consistently locked into one move, it's easier to revenge kill, so it needs defensive teammates such as Primarina and Landorus-T that can switch into faster offensive Pokemon like Darkrai and Zamazenta while also providing pivot support for Iron Crown. Alomomola is another good teammate for Iron Crown, pivoting it into favorable matchups and keeping it healthy with Wish. Gholdengo is especially annoying for Iron Crown, as it resists both of its STAB moves and can easily heal off damage, so teammates like Kingambit and Great Tusk that can easily take care of it are useful. Finally, Iron Crown benefits from entry hazard setters like Hisuian Samurott that can soften up foes and allow it to clean them up easier.

Assault Vest.description:
Assault Vest Iron Crown serves as a strong offensive pivot and sturdy check to a bevy of special attackers like Calm Mind Iron Valiant, Kyurem, and Enamorus. Tachyon Cutter's multi-hit properties allow it to bypass Glimmora's Focus Sash to OHKO it before it can set up any entry hazards. Future Sight's delayed damage puts a tremendous amount of pressure on the opposing team, since Dark-types switching in to block Future Sight or Steel-types and special walls trying to sponge the attack will have to survive powerful physical attacks from teammates like Great Tusk, Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, Zamazenta, and Weavile; Psychic Noise offers lower but more immediate damage while simultaneously nullifying recovery attempts from Gholdengo, Blissey, Corviknight, Garganacl, and Clodsire, allowing Iron Crown and its teammates to force significant damage against these threats. Focus Blast rounds out Iron Crown's coverage by hitting Kingambit, Ting-Lu, and Tera Steel Clodsire super effectively, and it is also its strongest attack against opposing Iron Crown. Volt Switch allows Iron Crown to capitalize on its ability to force out most special attackers and gain momentum for its team and has great synergy with Future Sight by safely pivoting in the aforementioned powerful physical attackers that can take advantage of the chip damage or switches it forces. Assault Vest greatly boosts Iron Crown's special bulk, allowing it to better handle special attackers like Calm Mind Iron Valiant and Enamorus. Tera Fighting turns Iron Crown's weakness to Dark-type attacks into a resistance, allowing it to survive Kingambit's Sucker Punch in a pinch while boosting its Focus Blast to 2HKO Ting-Lu and physically defensive Corviknight; Tera Fairy also offers a Dark resistance, but the Dragon immunity, Fighting resistance, and Fairy neutrality it provides allow Iron Crown to better check Dragapult and more reliably handle mixed and physical Iron Valiant sets without compromising its ability to check Calm Mind variants as heavily.

Iron Crown is best run on bulky offense teams, which can both cover Iron Crown's defensive shortcomings and maintain a similar level of offensive pressure, often in the form of additional pivoting options to maintain momentum. Hisuian Samurott is a spectacular teammate; it can form a VoltTurn core with Iron Crown using Flip Turn, reliably set Spikes with Ceaseless Edge, and even remove Heavy-Duty Boots with its strong STAB Knock Off to allow the duo to rack up massive amounts of lasting damage through Spikes and Future Sight or Psychic Noise. The two share excellent defensive synergy, as Hisuian Samurott's Ghost and Dark resistances cover Dragapult, Gholdengo, and opposing Hisuian Samurott while Iron Crown's Grass and Fairy resistances cover Rillaboom and Iron Valiant. Ceaseless Edge and Knock Off have impeccable synergy with Future Sight, and Hisuian Samurott's Razor Shell hits Dark-types like Ting-Lu and Kingambit very hard, rendering Iron Crown's Future Sight much more difficult to switch in against. Landorus-T is another great teammate; it also forms a powerful VoltTurn core with Iron Crown, can blanket check most physical attackers with Intimidate and Rocky Helmet to complement Iron Crown's ability to blanket check most special attackers with Assault Vest, can set up Stealth Rock, and the two also boast impeccable defensive synergy courtesy of Iron Crown checking Ice Beam users like Deoxys-S and Landorus-T checking physical Iron Valiant and Heatran. Together, Iron Crown, Hisuian Samurott, and Landorus-T form an extremely powerful core that resists every type in the game, utilizes multiple pivoting options, sets up both Stealth Rock and Spikes, and can blanket check many physical and special attackers alike. Calm Mind Primarina is a good teammate that can run Psychic Noise itself, allowing Iron Crown to more freely run Future Sight, and can take advantage of Iron Crown's ability to wear down teams over time to set up for a late-game sweep once threats like Encore Iron Valiant are dealt with.
