Physically defensive Moltres is another solid teammate, as it can reliably check most physical attackers by spreading burn with Will-O-Wisp and Flame Body and heavily punishes Dark-types like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott and Steel-types like Gholdengo aiming to switch into Future Sight, and appreciates Iron Crown's ability to temporarily keep special attackers like Deoxys-S and Walking Wake at bay. Kingambit itself makes for a strong teammate, as with Iron Crown's Future Sight support, Kingambit has a much easier time both finding opportunities to set up with Swords Dance and muscle past physical walls like Dondozo and Alomomola, which are quickly overwhelmed by the combination of Future Sight and powerful Dark-type attacks possibly boosted further by Black Glasses, Tera Dark, and Supreme Overlord. Kingambit additionally resists Ghost- and Dark-type attacks from the likes of Gholdengo and opposing Kingambit lacking Low Kick, which Iron Crown greatly appreciates. Zamazenta and Weavile also greatly appreciate both Iron Crown's Future Sight support and its pivoting capabilities, allowing them to be brought in safely and giving them opportunities to fire off a powerful Body Press or Knock Off that, when paired with Future Sight, can prove nearly impossible to switch in against.

Calm Mind.description:
With solid bulk, a one-time Speed boost, and near-perfect coverage, Calm Mind Iron Crown is a solid sweeper and late-game cleaner. Tachyon Cutter has the benefit of hitting twice, allowing Iron Crown to OHKO common Focus Sash leads in Glimmora and Ribombee, giving it an alternate use as an anti-lead that denies entry hazards. Tachyon Cutter also allows Iron Crown to break Substitutes while chipping the Pokemon hiding behind it; it can break Zamazenta’s Substitute after one Calm Mind and Kyurem’s without any Calm Mind boosts. After one Calm Mind, Iron Crown can hit several important ranges with Tachyon Cutter such as an OHKO on Kyurem and a good chance to KO offensive Landorus-T; it also secures a 2HKO against defensive Landorus-T variants while not being 2HKOed by Earth Power. The choice of Psychic-type STAB move depends on the team's needs: Psyshock targets the lower Defense of Galarian Slowking, Ogerpon-W, and Primarina, while Psychic Noise prevents walls such as Dondozo, Pecharunt, Alomomola, and Corviknight from spamming recovery to outlast Iron Crown. Stored Power is an option that can reach astonishing power levels, capable of breaking past almost any non-immune wall; however, it requires several turns of setup and has no benefit other than raw damage. Focus Blast complements Iron Crown's STAB combination by providing excellent neutral and super effective coverage against everything in the metagame except Gholdengo. It is Iron Crown's best way of hitting Ting-Lu and Steel-types like Kingambit and Iron Treads. The EV spread maximizes Iron Crown's offensive capabilities while letting Booster Energy enhance its Speed; the leftover EVs are invested into HP for increased survivability, notably allowing Iron Crown to survive a Choice Specs Kyurem Earth Power. Tera Fighting and Tera Fairy remove Iron Crown's original weaknesses, most notably both turning its weakness to Dark-type moves such as Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott’s Sucker Punch into a resistance to give it an easier time sweeping. Tera Fighting strengthens Iron Crown's Focus Blast, OHKOing Darkrai 2HKOing on Ting-Lu at +1. Tera Fairy is a more defensive Tera type that, unlike Tera Fighting, gives it fewer weaknesses. It further improves Iron Crown’s matchups against Walking Wake, Raging Bolt, and Dragapult by turning the Dragon resistance into an immunity.

Calm Mind Iron Crown best fits on offense teams that appreciate its unique traits as a sweeper. Due to its low initial damage output, Iron Crown will struggle against bulky threats such as Ting-Lu, Galarian Slowking, and Gholdengo, which require significant chip damage for it to break through them. Teammates such as Hisuian Samurott and Ogerpon-W significantly threaten these bulky foes, and in return, Iron Crown can deal with Kyurem and Rillaboom. Iron Crown is also extremely vulnerable to many offensive threats, many of which can survive almost any hit from an unboosted Iron Crown such as Hisuian Samurott, Landorus-T, and Kingambit; they can either force a Tera or outright KO Iron Crown. Ogerpon-W and Iron Moth also resist Tachyon Cutter and threaten a clean 2HKO on Iron Crown. As such, Iron Crown appreciates pivots such as Pecharunt, which walls Ogerpon-W and weakens it with Parting Shot, and Alomomola, which can take hits from Weavile, Hisuian Samurott, and other physical threats and threaten a burn with Scald to enable Iron Crown set up on them. Furthermore, special walls like Blissey and Clodsire using Tera Dark completely wall Iron Crown, as Focus Blast does insufficient damage. Because of this, Iron Crown appreciates physically offensive teammates, such as Hisuian Samurott, Great Tusk, and Zamazenta, that can deal with its checks; in return, they appreciate Iron Crown's removal of Fairy- and Fighting-type threats such as Enamorus, Hatterene, and Great Tusk. Hisuian Samurott and Great Tusk also set entry hazards to accumulate chip damage, which can compensate for this set's low initial power and allow Iron Crown to clean up or sweep earlier than expected.

Fast Weakness Policy.description:
• Fast Weakness Policy Iron Crown aims to switch up otherwise disadvantageous matchups such as Haxorus as well as Choice Band Ground-types such as Landorus-T by boosting itself with Iron Defense, then obtaining a Weakness Policy boost to threaten an OHKO on the next turn with Stored Power.
  • Tachyon Cutter is Iron Crown's best Steel-type STAB move, being able to immediately pressure Fairy-Type Pokemon such as Iron Valiant and Sylveon. Tachyon Cutter has other niches in breaking foes' Substitute, such as against SubSeed Ogerpon-W and Serperior.
  • Upon activation of Weakness Policy, Stored Power's Base Power increases by 80. Combined with any prior boosts Iron Crown may have obtained, this makes Stored Power its strongest Psychic-type STAB option.
  • Psyshock can be used to disrupt the matchup versus other Calm Mind users that resist Stored Power such as opposing Iron Crown and Cresselia, albeit using Psyshock may miss out on important KOs that Stored Power would otherwise obtain.
  • Psychic Noise may be used to prevent recovery moves from Pokemon such as Cresselia that would otherwise be able to deal with Iron Crown. Psychic Noise also deals additional damage to Iron Valiant and Alolan Ninetales compared to Iron Crown's other Psychic-type options.
  • Calm Mind is used in matchups versus special attacking Pokemon such as Primarina and Cresselia in order to boost up Iron Crown's Special Attack and Special Defense to a point where it does not take much damage from their attacks while threatening KOs with Tachyon Cutter and Stored Power.
  • The EVs are used to outspeed maximum Speed Haxorus and to tie the mirror matchup versus opposing Iron Crown. The bulk is meant to tank an Adamant Choice Band Great Tusk Headlong Rush after one Iron Defense.
  • An alternative EV spread of 96 HP / 112 Def / 48 SpA / 252 Spe with a Timid Nature can be used to have a slightly better chance against Donphan with Tachyon Cutter after a Weakness Policy boost while still surviving Choice Band Great Tusk's Headlong Rush. However, this makes Iron Crown less reliable into Choice Specs Primarina.

Defensive Weakness Policy.description:
• Defensive Weakness Policy Iron Crown uses Iron Defense and Calm Mind to boost its defenses to survive strong hits and KO back with Weakness Policy-boosted Stored Power.
  • Stored Power obtains a massive boost in Base Power when combined with Weakness Policy and stat-boosting moves.
  • Alternatively, Psyshock can be used for matchups Pokemon that have enough Special Defense to not be threatened by Stored Power, such as Cresselia and Pokemon that Iron Crown can't boost in front of like Iron Valiant.
  • Tachyon Cutter is hits Fairy-types such as Sylveon and Iron Valiant, and can break Substitute from Pokemon such as Serperior.
  • Calm Mind is used for matchups where boosting Special Attack and Special Defense is necessary, such as against Assault Vest Ursaluna-B.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Iron Crown to have a 75% chance to survive Adamant Choice Band Meowscarada's Knock Off in order to kill it with +2 Tachyon Cutter, as well as having favorable rolls to survive two Choice Band Ursaluna's Earthquake to boost with Iron Defense up to +4 and KO with Stored Power. The remaining EVs are placed in Speed for the mirror matchup and to base 50 speed Pokemon such as Ursaluna.
  • 36 Speed EVs can be used instead to outspeed Max Speed Primarina.
  • While this set is able to bulk many attacks, it is notably slower than faster Choice Band users like Landorus-T, making Defensive Iron Crown lose the matchup against them. Faster teammates that can deal with these Pokemon are ideal, such as attackers like Meowscarada.

Specially Defensive Weakness Policy.description:
• This specially defensive EV spread allows Weakness Policy Iron Crown to take special hits from very powerful special attackers such as Timid Choice Specs Darkrai, Raging Bolt, and Choice Specs Dragapult.
  • Psyshock is vital for matchups such as Calm Mind Raging Bolt, Iron Valiant, and Alolan Ninetales, as it helps hit the weaker physical side on the former and assists against Disable variants on the latter two.
  • The Defense EVs let Iron Crown survive Adamant Choice Band Knock Off from Meowscarada, while the Special Defense is enough to survive two Thunderbolts into a Thunderclap from Raging Bolt after a Calm Mind boost, since it would use Taunt on Iron Crown on the first turn. The Special Attack investment is enough to OHKO Haxorus with Tachyon Cutter after the Special Defense drop from Close Combat.
  • This Iron Crown set can struggle a lot against opposing Iron Crown due to the lack of Stored Power and matches up poorly against common Fire- and Ground-types and other miscellaneous threats like Hoopa-U and Corviknight, so it's recommended to utilize strong partners such as Air Balloon Volcanion and Ogerpon-W.

Special Attack Booster Energy.description:
• Calm Mind allows Iron Crown to compete with Pokemon like Raging Bolt, Cresselia, and opposing Iron Crown.
  • Psyshock enables Iron Crown to hit specially defensive foes, empowers it against Calm Mind users such as Weakness Policy Iron Crown and Clear Amulet Cresselia, and is important against Alolan Ninetales.
  • Tachyon Cutter exerts pressure on Fairy-type foes like Iron Valiant and Sylveon.
  • Focus Blast lets Iron Crown take on foes including Ursaluna-B and Hisuian Goodra. Alternatively, Psychic Noise can be used to check foes that rely on recovery moves, especially Pecharunt and Clear Amulet Cresselia. Moreover, Stored Power + Calm Mind allows Iron Crown to handle foes like Manaphy. Finally, Psychic allows Iron Crown to deal increased damage to foes such as Iron Hands and Speed Booster Energy Walking Wake.
  • The bulk EVs allow Iron Crown to survive Knock Off from Adamant Choice Band Meowscarada and Hydro Cannon from Timid Choice Specs Primarina, with the rest of the EVs being put into Special Attack.
  • Primarina is a great partner for Iron Crown, since Iron Crown is weak to Ground- Fire- and Dark-type attacks from foes like Landorus, Volcarona, and Urshifu-S; in return, Iron Crown provides an immunity to Poison. On top of this, Iron Crown's weakness to Ghost-type attacks can be remedied by using other Dark-types, such as Roaring Moon.

Speed Booster Energy.description:
• This set relies on outspeeding key threats such as Chien-Pao and Speed Booster Energy Great Tusk, using the Speed boost from Booster Energy to flip otherwise unfavorable matchups for Iron Crown.
  • Psychic is Iron Crown's strongest Psychic-type STAB move, which allows it to hit Pokemon like Iron Hands and Great Tusk. On the other hand, Psyshock is the best option against Pokemon like Raging Bolt, where both Pokemon typically use Calm Mind six times.
  • The HP and Defense EVs allow Iron Crown to tank an Earthquake from Adamant Choice Band Iron Hands and a Hydro Cannon from +3 Torrent Primarina at +4 Special Defense. The Speed EVs help it outspeed Porygon-Z, and the remaining EVs are invested in Special Attack.
  • Because Fire- and Dark-type Pokemon like Darkrai, Skeledirge, Hoopa-U, and Iron Moth are difficult for Iron Crown to deal with by itself, Primarina and Donphan work as good partners for Iron Crown.

Double Dance Sweeper (Psychic).description:
Iron Crown is an amazing Stored Power setup sweeper for Psychic due to its access to multiple useful setup moves, like Calm Mind and Agility, and a type combination that lets it activate Weakness Policy easily. On top of that, its typing means it's immune to Toxic and also has important resistances to types such as Dragon and Fairy. Calm Mind and Agility allow Iron Crown to boost its stats and Stored Power while also punishing opponents that play passively, trying to stall out dual screens. Behind dual screens, Iron Crown survives attacks like Fiery Dance from Choice Specs Iron Moth, Earth Power from Life Orb Landorus, and Knock Off from Alolan Muk, allowing it to capitalize on its weaknesses by activating Weakness Policy and boosting the power of Stored Power. Additionally, after activating its Weakness Policy and using a single Agility, Iron Crown can take on walls like Skarmory and Galarian Slowking, OHKOing the former after Stealth Rock damage and 2HKOing the latter; similarly, in this position, it makes quick work of offensive foes like Choice Band Dragapult, Landorus-T, and Ogerpon-H and -W. Tachyon Cutter is a secondary move that is meant to hit foes that are immune to Stored Power, such as Alolan Muk and Meowscarada, and it also bypasses enemies with Focus Sash and Sturdy, such as Glimmora and Ogerpon-C, respectively. Focus Blast can be used in place of Tachyon Cutter or Calm Mind to hit Steel-type foes, which resist Stored Power, and Dark-type foes, which are immune to it. Once Weakness Policy is activated, Focus Blast can eliminate special walls such as Ting-Lu and Heatran after they are mildly chipped. However, it is considered risky, as Focus Blast can miss. A Timid nature is preferred, since it lets Iron Crown outspeed Choice Scarf Dragapult after an Agility. However, a Modest nature can also be considered, as it still outspeeds Choice Scarf Meowscarada after an Agility, and at +2 Special Attack, Iron Crown can OHKO Heatran.

Deoxys-S and Scream Tail set up entry hazards and dual screens, allowing Iron Crown to survive hits and set up successfully. Indeedee-M is immune to Ghost and sets Psychic Terrain for Iron Crown, shielding it from priority moves such as Ceruledge's Shadow Sneak and Hisuian Samurott's Sucker Punch. It also provides Healing Wish support to bring Iron Crown back into shape if it gets worn down. Galarian Slowking assists Iron Crown by spreading poison through Toxic Spikes or Toxic, pressuring bulky special walls such as Ting-Lu, while also providing pivoting with Chilly Reception. Hatterene prevents foes from setting up hazards, allowing Iron Crown to come in safely, and it can also help weaken Dark-types. Iron Boulder heavily damages special walls that trouble Iron Crown such as Heatran and Hisuian Goodra. Additionally, Iron Boulder checks Fire-type threats such as Ogerpon-H, Volcarona, and Cinderace while also dissuading Cinderace from using Court Change to steal dual screens. Choice Specs Flutter Mane overwhelms Iron Crown, but Choice Scarf Iron Boulder outspeeds it and removes it. Latios provides a switch-in to Ground-type moves thanks to its immunity to them, and it removes Dragon-type foes such as Garchomp and Walking Wake. Hoopa-U helps in removing Ghost-types such as Gholdengo and Flutter Mane. Slowbro chips opposing Fire-type threats such as Hisuian Arcanine while also burning physical attackers, such as Barraskewda and Choice Band Excadrill, and setup sweepers, like Dragonite and Scizor, with Scald. Armarouge removes Steel-type threats that resist Iron Crown's STAB moves, such as Forretress and Iron Treads, with the combination of Aura Sphere and Armor Cannon.

Choice Specs (Steel).description:
Iron Crown provides Steel teams breathing room against Fighting matchups, threatening intimidating foes such as Okidogi, Great Tusk, and Urshifu-R. Tachyon Cutter takes out threats like Focus Sash Breloom and Mimikyu, which normally don't get OHKOed. Volt Switch makes Iron Crown a fast and offensive pivot, allowing it to pivot out of foes such as Gholdengo and Alolan Muk, which otherwise threaten a ton of damage. Volt Switch can also heavily dent Flying and Water teams, damaging foes like Pelipper and Skarmory. Psychic allows Iron Crown to handle Fighting-type Pokemon like Urshifu-R, Iron Hands, and Great Tusk. Focus Blast breaks through Ursaluna, Hisuian Goodra, Empoleon, and Heatran, which are hard to deal with for Steel teams.

Corviknight and Skarmory provide Iron Crown with a keen immunity to Ground-type moves. Corviknight removes entry hazards and offers a slow pivot through U-turn, whereas Skarmory sets hazards and phazes setup sweepers such as Swords Dance Sneasler and Dragon Dance Dragonite. Archaludon handles physical attackers such as Ceruledge and Ogerpon-H and exerts pressure on Dark-type foes such as Meowscarada and Bisharp, which threaten Iron Crown. Archaludon also spreads Thunder Wave to slow down fast foes like Tornadus-T and Greninja and sets Stealth Rock. Heatran provides an immunity to Fire-type moves from Ninetales and Volcarona while also setting Stealth Rock. Gholdengo, due to Good as Gold, prevents foes such as Blissey and Sableye from slowing down Iron Crown through Thunder Wave and also provides a Fighting immunity. Hisuian Goodra, thanks to its sheer special bulk, provides a safe switch-in against strong special attacks from threats like Greninja and Moltres. Iron Treads removes hazards and threatens Ground-types Pokemon such as Garchomp, Landorus-I, and Gliscor. With the help of priority in Sucker Punch, Bisharp shoves off Ghost-types such as Flutter Mane and Dragapult. In return, Iron Crown deals with Toxapex, Okidogi, and Great Tusk.

vgc2024.overview:
• Iron Crown is an excellent choice for offensive teams looking to take advantage of the powerful move Expanding Force thanks to its well-rounded stats and access to Booster Energy. It performs best against frailer offensive teams consisting of Pokemon that do not resist Expanding Force, such as Tornadus, Landorus, and Urshifu-R.

  • Although it can be used as a sweeper early-game to soften opposing teams, it is usually better to save Iron Crown for the late-game when its checks have been sufficiently weakened for it to sweep.

  • Indeedee-F is by far Iron Crown's best teammate, offering role compression as a Psychic Terrain setter and redirector. Access to Helping Hand also further amplifies its partner's ridiculous damage output.

  • Iron Crown's best counters are Dark- and Steel-types, namely Incineroar, Kingambit, Archaludon, and Gholdengo, all of which resist both of Iron Crown's STAB moves.

  • Therefore, Iron Crown appreciates Pokemon that can help remove these threats consistently, such as Landorus, Entei, and Urshifu-R. In return, Iron Crown can pressure opposing Urshifu-R and Amoonguss.

  • Rillaboom is another noteworthy check, as it is able to safely pivot in and override Psychic Terrain, weakening Expanding Force significantly. Other Pokemon with access to Ice Spinner like Chien-Pao and Dragonite can also be used to remove Psychic Terrain.

  • Faster Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Flutter Mane serve as good checks as well, but they have to watch out for Follow Me from Indeedee-F as they are vulnerable to Tachyon Cutter.

Booster Energy.description:
• Expanding Force is Iron Crown's go-to STAB move, allowing it to devastate foes under Psychic Terrain.

  • Tachyon Cutter helps secure the OHKO on Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Whimsicott, which commonly hold Focus Sash.

  • Tera Water is a naturally good defensive typing that, when coupled with Tera Blast, gives Iron Crown an out against the aforementioned Dark- and Steel-type Pokemon, which otherwise counter it. Focus Blast can be used over Tera Blast to secure the OHKO on Kingambit, but is rather inconsistent and is unable to hit Gholdengo.

  • An alternative spread of 76 HP / 4 Def / 172 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe allows Iron Crown to outspeed Flutter Mane and Chien-Pao thanks to Speed Booster Energy.

  • This set can also be run with a Modest nature to maximize Iron Crown's damage output, at the risk of underspeeding opposing Pokemon in the same Speed tier such as Modest Landorus and both Urshifu formes.

Calm Mind.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • EV Spread: This gives Iron Crown a Speed boost with Quark Drive, and is faster than Jolly Urshifu formes.

Offensive.description:
• This set's write-up has not started yet, but here's some basic info to get you started!

  • 44 HP / 36 Def / 172 SpA / 4 SpD / 252 Spe with Modest or Timid: This spread survives Jolly Punching Glove Urshifu-R's Tera Water Surging Strikes, and Modest Choice Specs Flutter Mane's Shadow Ball if using Assault Vest.

Psychic Terrain Sweeper.description: • EV spread gets a Speed boost from Quark Drive

Setup Sweeper.description:
Functioning as a niche setup sweeper, Iron Crown can leverage its good natural bulk and excellent coverage to effectively sweep. Psychic Noise is used to prevent healing from foes such as Gliscor and Moltres while being a more reliable STAB option when Iron Crown is not yet set up. As an alternative, Stored Power can be used in conjunction with Iron Defense in order to make Iron Crown a threatening Double Dance sweeper. Focus Blast is used to hit Steel-types such as Heatran and Ferrothorn, which could otherwise comfortably take its STAB moves. Tachyon Cutter is used to hit Fairy-types such as Hatterene and Tapu Lele, which would otherwise be able to switch in on Iron Crown. Iron Defense boosts the power of Stored Power while also making Iron Crown more resistant against physical attackers such as Zamazenta, Melmetal, and Dragonite, letting it turn them into setup fodder. 172 Special Attack EVs are used in order to grant Iron Crown Quark Drive's Speed boost with Booster Energy, letting it outspeed most foes.

This Iron Crown set fits exclusively on hyper offense teams where its ability to clean late-game is appreciated. Due to often lacking the bulk to set up reliably, dual screens support from teammates such as Zamazenta and Tapu Koko are appreciated, with the latter also activating its Quark Drive, potentially enabling Iron Crown to run a different item. Another good teammate is Tapu Lele, as Psychic Terrain provides Iron Crown with an immunity to priority moves from foes such as Kingambit and also boosts the power of its Psychic-type moves. In return, Iron Crown can threaten foes such as Hatterene and opposing Tapu Lele. Iron Crown struggles to beat Gholdengo, meaning Fire-type teammates that can threaten it such as Volcarona and Mega Charizard X are appreciated. In return, Iron Crown can threaten Toxapex and set up on Alomomola for them, as both of them could otherwise come in on these Fire-types comfortably. Iron Crown also struggles with Ground-types such as Choice Scarf Landorus-T and Gliscor, meaning Flying-types such as Dragonite and your own Landorus-T make excellent teammates; Landorus-T also effectively damages Steel-types, making it easier for Iron Crown to sweep. Iron Crown can repay Landorus-T by breaking through Flying-types such as Zapdos and Tornadus-T, which would otherwise be able to wall it. Iron Crown struggles to beat Ting-Lu, meaning Fighting-type teammates such as Zamazenta and Iron Valiant are appreciated, with Iron Crown in return beating Fairy-types such as Mega Diancie, Clefable and Hatterene. Dark-types like Kingambit and Hisuian Samurott also make great partners, with both being able to threaten Iron Crown's main answer in Gholdengo and Hisuian Samurott also setting up Spikes to let Iron Crown break teams with greater ease.

Assault Vest.description:
Assault Vest Iron Crown functions as a niche defensive pivot; with the item's boost, it can leverage its high Special Defense to be able to reliably switch in on and answer foes such as Tapu Lele, Raging Bolt, and Calm Mind Iron Valiant. Psychic Noise prevents healing from foes such as Zapdos, Alomomola, and Iron Defense + Body Press Zamazenta, which often carries Substitute. Volt Switch lets Iron Crown pivot out of bad matchups while also having the bonus of hitting foes such as Moltres and Corviknight decently hard. Focus Blast is used to hit Steel-type targets such as Ferrothorn and Heatran for meaningful damage. On Electric Terrain teams, an EV spread with 172 Special Attack EVs can be used in order to grant Iron Crown with a Speed boost under Electric Terrain courtesy of Quark Drive, letting it outspeed the entirety of the unboosted tier.

Assault Vest Iron Crown fits primarily on bulky offense and offense teams, where its ability to check foes such as Tapu Lele and special Iron Valiant is greatly appreciated. Teammates that are vulnerable to the aforementioned Fairy-types, such as Dragonite, Garchomp, and Hisuian Samurott, all value Iron Crown's defensive capabilities. In return, all three can effectively pressure opposing Steel-types such as Heatran and Gholdengo. Iron Crown struggles with Ground-type foes such as Garchomp, Landorus-T, and Gliscor, meaning Flying-type teammates such as Zapdos and Moltres are appreciated. In return, Iron Crown can be a good switch-in against Electric-types such as Raging Bolt and Tapu Koko, which could otherwise threaten them. Iron Crown also struggles to break bulky Dark-types such as Ting-Lu; therefore, Fighting-types like Zamazenta, Iron Valiant and Urshifu-R can make good teammates. Iron Crown can support them by being a reliable answer to Psychic- and Fairy-types, including the aforementioned Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant, as well as pivoting them in against Steel-types such as Ferrothorn. Tapu Koko can also make an excellent partner due to its ability to set Electric Terrain, allowing Iron Crown to be able to outspeed and threaten foes such as Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Zamazenta, while also forming a pivoting core with it. Landorus-T and Great Tusk also form an excellent defensive core with Iron Crown, with Iron Crown being able to switch in on threats such as Tapu Lele and, in turn, these allies being good answers to common Ground-types such as Gliscor and opposing Landorus-T.

Fast Calm Mind Sweeper.description:
• Iron Crown is one of the best sweepers of the tier that, thanks to Expanding Force, hits really hard even without boosts! With Booster Energy, Iron Crown outspeeds almost everything in the metagame, and while in Psychic Terrain, it can gain a significant advantage early-game or close games easily after Dark- and Steel-types in its path have been removed.

  • Tachyon Cutter hits harder than Expanding Force when Psychic Terrain isn't up and helps against snow teams, OHKOing Alolan Ninetales before it can set up Aurora Veil. Notably, its two-hit nature allows Iron Crown to remove Focus Sash Pokemon like Chien-Pao and Glimmora with one move.

  • Calm Mind makes Iron Crown hard to remove with special attackers, especially if it Terastallized, and also helps to KO bulkier Pokemon like Terastallized Assault Vest Iron Hands, Assault Vest Rillaboom, and Gholdengo.

  • The EV spread is made to get the boost in Speed with Quark Drive while getting the maximum Special Attack possible, and the bulk investment is used to take a Flare Blitz from Incineroar.

  • Iron Crown pairs perfectly with Indeedee-F by setting up Psychic Terrain, helping it set up Calm Mind with Follow Me, and enabling it with Helping Hand to pick up KOs on foes like Terastallized Ogerpon-W after a boost. Iron Crown appreciates Follow Me for setup, and for this reason, it's usually paired with Ogerpon-W or Ogerpon-H. Ogerpon-W helps in dealing with Landorus and Fire-types like Incineroar and Chi-Yu, which can threaten Iron Crown, while Ogerpon-H can remove Steel-types like Gholdengo and Kingambit, which would otherwise prevent a sweep. Both Ogerpon formes can also threaten Ting-Lu, a foe that's otherwise hard to remove.

  • Landorus is another Pokemon that helps to remove Steel- and Fire-types. Tornadus is great too, since it threatens Rillaboom with Bleakwind Storm and makes sure that Iron Crown is always the fastest Pokemon by matching the Tailwind from opposing Tornadus and Roaring Moon.

  • Tera Psychic increases Expanding Force's damage output further, helping to get KOs and putting a lot of pressure on the opponent, especially after a Calm Mind. It also allows Iron Crown to take neutral damage from Landorus's Earth Power, Incineroar's Flare Blitz, and Ogerpon-H's Ivy Cudgel. Tera Dragon allows Iron Crown to wall both Ogerpon-W and Ogerpon-H's STAB moves and take neutral damage from Gholdengo's Shadow Ball and Dark-type moves from Kingambit and Chien-Pao. The added resistances are especially useful in the Rillaboom matchup, since the STAB boost from Tera Psychic isn't as relevant without Psychic Terrain.

Calm Mind (Psychic).description: Iron Crown charges into battle on offensive Psychic teams as a threatening Calm Mind setup sweeper with a useful defensive typing and decent bulk. With Calm Mind, Agility, and Stored Power, Iron Crown can quickly snowball out of control and muscle its way through Psychic-resistant foes while outrunning would-be revenge killers such as Meowscarada and Landorus-I. Weakness Policy is Iron Crown's preferred item, as activating it hugely increases Stored Power's Base Power without requiring multiple turns of setup. Once boosted, Iron Crown can easily use Tachyon Cutter to trample Steel-weak teams like Fairy, Rock, and Ice, while Stored Power blasts through teams typically lacking specially bulky Psychic-resistant or -immune Pokemon like Electric and Ground lacking Ting-Lu. Focus Blast can lure specially defensive phazers that usually stop Iron Crown like Ting-Lu, Hisuian Goodra, and Empoleon. Iron Crown's EVs allow it to activate Speed Quark Drive in Electric Terrain, which is very useful to outspeed fast Electric types like Tapu Koko and Zeraora that typically use Electric-type attacks freely against Psychic teams. Iron Crown greatly appreciates dual screens support, so a dedicated setter like Deoxys-S is a great help. With dual screens active, Iron Crown can survive and activate Weakness Policy against dangerous attacks like Gholdengo's Never-Ending Nightmare, Mega Charizard Y's Flamethrower, and Choice Band Excadrill's Earthquake. Tapu Lele is another notable partner, as it provides Psychic Terrain, blocking dangerous priority moves that could threaten Iron Crown like Sucker Punch and Shadow Sneak. In return, Iron Crown provides a switch-in to Poison-type moves targeting Tapu Lele and helps break through shared checks like Alolan Muk. Mega Gallade is another synergistic teammate that clobbers threats to Iron Crown like Hisuian Goodra, Blissey, Hisuian Samurott, and Bisharp. In turn, Iron Crown can break through physical walls that frustrate Mega Gallade like Dondozo, Quagsire, and Slowbro. Latias, sporting a Ground immunity and a Fire-type resistance, can not only cover these weaknesses for Iron Crown, but also can utilize Healing Wish to get it back in the race if a previous sweep attempt was halted via damage or status.

Choice Specs (Steel).description: This is the sample set before we work on new analyses. This will be updated as the metagame continues to develop. Stay tuned!

monotype.comments:
Other Options

Normal (Offensive Entry Hazard Remover)

Terapagos has no shortage of moves it can run, such as Earth Power, which lets it deal with Archaludon and Ceruledge; Scorching Sands, which lets it fish for burns against Alolan Muk and Clodsire; and Dazzling Gleam for Sableye. However, Terapagos would lose the coverage needed to OHKO Gliscor or threaten Corviknight and Gholdengo, in addition to Tera Starstorm's damage being comparable with super effective coverage if the opposing Pokemon is not 4x weak to Terapagos's coverage. Even though Calm Mind is tempting to use with Rapid Spin, losing crucial coverage hampers Terapagos's ability to keep entry hazards off.

Choice Specs.description:
Choice Specs Terapagos leverages its incredibly powerful Normal-type STAB option in Tera Starstorm, a good Special Attack stat, and a plethora of coverage moves to become a fearsome wallbreaker on Normal teams. Tera Starstorm seriously damages neutral targets, OHKOing Galarian Weezing and 2HKOing physically defensive Toxapex and bulky Gouging Fire variants. Ice Beam wrecks Flying- and Ground-types like Gliscor, Dragonite, and Landorus-T. Earth Power hits Steel- and Rock-types like Archaludon and Garganacl, while Flamethrower hits Steel-types that don't fear Earth Power like Air Balloon Gholdengo and Corviknight. Tera Shell allows Terapagos to greatly increase its bulk while at full health, letting it come in on strong attacks and return the favor. It also enables it to revenge kill threats like Choice Scarf Urshifu-R and Choice Specs Iron Valiant.

Ursaluna-B is a great teammate for Terapagos, as they each break through what the other cannot. Both possess incredibly strong Normal-type STAB moves, and Ursaluna-B scares off Steel-types like Heatran and Gholdengo for Terapagos. In return, Terapagos hits the Grass- and Flying-types that Ursaluna-B struggles with, such as Rillaboom, Hydrapple, and Gliscor. Hisuian Zoroark is another great partner, as it provides a very handy Fighting immunity to take on threats like Body Press Archaludon and Choice Specs Kommo-o. In return, Terapagos can break through bulky answers to Hisuian Zoroark like Toxapex and Alolan Muk with its sheer power. Blissey provides Stealth Rock support and is a great special sponge for threatening special attacks like Flutter Mane's Moonblast. It can also use Thunder Wave to slow down opposing threats like Choice Specs Dragapult and Choice Specs Greninja for Terapagos to blast them with Tera Starstorm and Ice Beam while easing the burden of prediction for Terapagos by switching in on special threats like the aforementioned Greninja as well as Latios if Terapagos gets a prediction incorrect. Braviary can remove entry hazards for Terapagos with Defog, ensuring that Tera Shell stays active while being able to switch into and handle threats like Sneasler and Meowscarada for Terapagos. It can also bring Terapagos in safely with U-turn. Choice Scarf Indeedee helps massively in the Fighting and Poison matchups, hitting threats like Zamazenta, Iron Hands, and Clodsire hard to pave the way for Terapagos to break. Indeedee also provides Healing Wish support for Terapagos and blocks revenge killing attempts from Mach Punch Breloom and Sucker Punch Bisharp with Psychic Terrain. Ditto is an excellent reverse sweeper, surprising opponents trying to set up after forcing Terapagos out like Swords Dance Breloom and Dragon Dance Dragapult. Porygon2 can deal major damage to major threats like Gouging Fire and Scizor with Foul Play, letting Terapagos break them down with repeated assaults. It also functions as a blanket switch-in to many threatening attackers like Gholdengo if Terapagos mispredicts, making Terapagos's coverage moves much easier to click without fear of mispredicting. Cincinno is a scary physical sweeper and hazard remover with Tidy Up complemented by its colorful coverage, hitting Rock-types with Bullet Seed, Flying-types with Triple Axel and Rock Blast, and Fire-types with Rock Blast.

Offensive Entry Hazard Remover.description:
Terapagos acts as a great form of entry hazard removal due to its ability to immediately threaten and outspeed most entry hazard setters like Gliscor, Skarmory, Forretress, and Great Tusk. Tera Starstorm removes weakened threats like Keldeo and Ogerpon-W and OHKOes Iron Valiant. Flamethrower roasts Steel-types, especially Gholdengo, which can come into Terapagos to spinblock it. Ice Beam OHKOes Landorus and Gliscor after Stealth Rock damage, allowing Terapagos to exert pressure against Flying teams. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Terapagos retain its ability in spite of entry hazards, letting it be a one-time check to threats like Hisuian Lilligant, Ursaluna-B, and Zamazenta. A Modest nature is preferred to hit as hard as possible, as it already outspeeds most relevant entry hazard setters without a Speed-boosting nature.

It's vital for Terapagos to have teammates that can that can wall strong attackers, meaning Terapagos does not have to give up its ability to emergency check a foe using Tera Shell. Blissey and Braviary fulfill these roles, with Blissey dealing with special attackers like Raging Bolt, Latios, and Flutter Mane, and Braviary dealing with strong physical attackers like Sneasler and Hisuian Samurott. Blissey also provides Stealth Rock and Healing Wish to support Terapagos, and Braviary appreciates Terapagos taking Braviary's job of removing entry hazards, as it lets Braviary run Close Combat for Bisharp. Ursaluna loves Terapagos's ability to take down Corviknight and Gliscor and break Gholdengo's Air Balloon. In return, Ursaluna deals with Steel- and Poison-types like Archaludon, Heatran, and Toxapex. Hisuian Zoroark provides a Fighting immunity and deals with Keldeo and Archaludon. Furthermore, Hisuian Zoroark can disguse itself as Terapagos, forcing out foes that cannot break its Tera Shell and survive an attack, which brings in walls like Iron Hands and Hisuian Goodra that Hisuian Zoroark can inconvenience with Will-O-Wisp or Trick. Porygon2 is a defensive wall that can be run alongside Terapagos to further improve the Flying and Dragon matchup, and it has Foul Play to deal with Ceruledge and Choice Band Excadrill. Ditto is able to check threats like Gouging Fire and Ceruledge that Terapagos does not have coverage for.

Bulky Setup Sweeper.description:
Set Details

  • With its good natural bulk, a good matchup against Calyrex-S and Lunala thanks to being immune to their Ghost-type attacks, and Tera Shell, Terapagos can find many opportunities to get on the field and start setting up with Calm Mind. Terapagos can also disrupt and hinder Pokemon and strategies featuring weather and Terrain, making it have a good matchup against Miraidon while also disturbing Koraidon, Groudon, and Kyogre.
  • Earth Power gives Terapagos a reliable way to hit Zamazenta-C and Incineroar, and it's also a way to get around Wide Guard against Zamazenta-C and Lunala.
  • Leftovers increases Terapagos's longevity further and can reactivate Tera Shell, especially when paired with Grassy Terrain from Rillaboom, while Covert Cloak can prevent Fake Out flinches and Special Attack drops from Miraidon, Chi-Yu and Raging Bolt's Snarl and Spirit Break from Grimmsnarl.
  • The EV spread alongside a Bold nature helps Terapagos live a Close Combat from Life Orb Koraidon and +1 Body Press from Zamazenta-C after Terastallizing, and the Speed investment helps Terapagos outrun Calyrex-S after being paralyzed. The investment in HP optimizes the recovery of Leftovers and Grassy Terrain. The investment in Speed on the second spread allows Terapagos to outrun faster versions of Incineroar, and with a Modest nature, Terapagos can hit Zamazenta-C, Miraidon, and Incineroar much harder with Earth Power after Terastallizing with a Calm Mind boost, though it does lose the ability to not reliably survive Life Orb Koraidon's Close Combat after Terastallizing.

Teambuilding

  • Terapagos can struggle against teams featuring Zamazenta-C, as it resists base Terapagos's Tera Starstorm, can use Wide Guard to protect its teammates from Terapagos-S's Tera Starstorm, and threatens super effective damage with Body Press. Koraidon also has the ability to completely remove or inflict massive damage onto Terapagos and force it to Terastallize in order to remove Koraidon's sun. Other Fighting-types such as Iron Hands and both Urshifu formes can also do well against Terapagos, hitting it hard with Drain Punch and Close Combat, respectively.
  • Taunt and Encore from the likes of Flutter Mane, Tornadus, Whimsicott, and Calyrex-S can prevent Terapagos from setting up with Calm Mind and shut it down. Snarl from Miraidon, Raging Bolt, and Chi-Yu and Spirit Break from Grimmsnarl can repeatedly negate Calm Mind boosts, which can slow down non-Covert Cloak Terapagos. Grimmsnarl can also use Light Screen to reduce Terapagos's damage output even further. Spore from Amoonguss and Brute Bonnet can also slow down Terapagos's progress.
  • Calm Mind Terapagos relies heavily on its teammates support to help it sweep because of Calm Mind's slow nature and Terapagos's generally low damage output without Calm Mind, and without its support Terapagos can fall behind when it comes to Speed and power.
  • Calyrex-S can use Disable to stop Fighting-type moves from Koraidon and Zamazenta-C that threaten Terapagos and Wide Guard from the likes of Zamazenta-C and Lunala, making the aforementioned checks more managable for Terapagos. It can also use Encore to lock Pokemon into moves like Fake Out, Taunt, Encore, Wide Guard, and Grimmsnarl's Light Screen or a disabled move, rendering them useless.
  • Incineroar and Rillaboom can provide Fake Out support alongside pivoting moves such as Parting Shot and U-turn; Incineroar also has Intimidate and Will-O-Wisp to weaken physical threats like Koraidon and Iron Hands, while Rillaboom sets Grassy Terrain, increasing Terapagos's longevity further.
  • Amoonguss and Ogerpon-C provide redirection in Rage Powder and Follow Me, respectively, keeping Terapagos safe. Amoonguss is an annoyance for the likes of Zamazenta-C, Urshifu-R, and Iron Hands by resisting their Fighting-type STAB moves while also taking Zamazenta-C's Heavy Slam and Behemoth Bash comfortably. Amoonguss can also heal Terapagos and restore Tera Shell with Pollen Puff. Ogerpon-C can redirect Spore from the likes of Amoonguss and Brute Bonnet, which Terapagos would normally struggle against, while threatening Urshifu-R with Power Whip.
  • Flutter Mane can use Thunder Wave to allow Terapagos to outspeed common threats such as Calyrex-S, Zamazenta-C, and Koraidon. Flutter Mane can also threaten Koraidon, Iron Hands, and both Urshifu formes with Moonblast. Taunt can prevent Wide Guard, foes' Taunt, and Encore from being used.

Power Herb.description:
Set Details

  • Power Herb Terapagos is a hyper offensive threat, firing off Meteor Beam to boost its offense and dealing unresisted damage with Tera Starstorm after Terastallizing. Terapagos has a great matchup against Miraidon and Kyogre, as it is capable of surviving attacks from them thanks to Tera Shell and then removing terrain and weather upon Terastallizing with Teraform Zero.
  • Meteor Beam OHKOs Volcarona, Ogerpon-H, and Chi-Yu and deals significant damage to Calyrex-I and Incineroar, allowing Terapagos to finish them off with Tera Starstorm on the following turn. Earth Power lets Terapagos threaten 2HKOs against Miraidon and Zamazenta-C when at +1.
  • Power Herb Terapagos sets run maximum Speed EVs with a Timid nature to outrun Adamant Urshifu sets.
  • Tera Stellar transforms Tera Starstorm into a spread Stellar-type attack and increases the damage of Meteor Beam and Earth Power, guaranteeing an OHKO on non-Assault Vest Incineroar with Meteor Beam and a 2HKO on Assault Vest Miraidon with Earth Power at +1.

Teambuilding

  • Fighting-types are generally problematic for Terapagos. Koraidon and Choice Scarf Urshifu-R outspeed Terapagos and threaten it with Collision Course and Close Combat, respectively. Zamazenta-C and Iron Hands threaten Terapagos with Body Press and Drain Punch while surviving its Earth Power.
  • Ghost-types such as Calyrex-S, Lunala, and Flutter Mane are difficult for Terapagos to damage. They pressure Terapagos to terastallize in order to sufficiently damage them with Tera Starstorm, while they can easily chip away at Terapagos with their Psychic- and Fairy-type attacks.
  • On top of their type advantages, Zamazenta-C and Lunala can disrupt Terapagos further with Wide Guard protecting them and their allies from Tera Starstorm when Terapagos has Terastallized.
  • Damage mitigation by Whimsicott and Grimmsnarl's Light Screen as well as Miraidon and Chi-Yu's Snarl severely weakens Terapagos's damage output.
  • Amoonguss can be annoying since it can comfortably withstand attacks from Terapagos, redirect its attacks, and put it to sleep with Spore.
  • Terapagos is often paired with Choice Scarf Miraidon. Miraidon deals solid damage with Electro Drift and Draco Meteor to bulky foes like Zamazenta-C and Lunala, softening them up for Terapagos to finish off with Tera Starstorm. Miraidon additionally supports Terapagos by threatening Koraidon and Urshifu-R with its STAB moves. Miraidon's Electric Terrain is also handy for preventing Amoonguss from slowing down Terapagos's offensive pressure with Spore. Miraidon's Snarl can threaten Calyrex-S and Lunala while hindering their damage output.
  • Incineroar works well with Terapagos, reducing the damage of the Fighting-type threats like the Urshifu formes and Iron Hands with Intimidate as well as threatening Ghost-types like Calyrex-S and Lunala with Knock Off, forcing them to Terastallize; afterwards,Terapagos can threaten them with Tera Starstorm.
  • Amoonguss comfortably takes Fighting-type attacks and redirects them away from Terapagos. It also disrupts these foes with Spore and can heal Terapagos with Pollen Puff, allowing it to regain Tera Shell if it hasn't Terastallized.
  • Volcarona can also be found on teams with Power Herb Terapagos, where it is often used as a setup sweeper rather than redirection support. Volcarona can resist attacks from Zamazenta-C and can threaten it with Fiery Dance alongside Amoonguss.

Calm Mind.description:
Terapagos is a bulky setup sweeper, with Tera Shell boosting its already great longevity with its high natural bulk. In addition to this, Tera Starstorm becomes a powerful unresisted spread move when Terapagos Terastallizes. Earth Power is ran to allow Terapagos to deal significant damage to Steel-types and Wide Guard users it otherwise would struggle to defeat, notably Zamazenta-C. Leftovers benefits Terapagos's longevity when it does not have a partner to heal it, allowing Tera Shell to be reactivated. Covert Cloak is also a great item, as it prevents Terapagos's Special Attack from being lowered by opposing Snarl and provides the bonus of making it immune to flinch from Fake Out. Clear Amulet is used similarly to Covert Cloak but also prevents Parting Shot lowering Terapagos's Special Attack. Terapagos matches up very well against Calyrex-S, as it is immune to Astral Barrage, and damage from Draining Kiss and Expanding Force can be mitigated by its massive bulk bolstered by Tera Shell, Special Defense boosts from Calm Mind, and partners such as Amoonguss with Rage Powder and Pollen Puff. Teraform Zero disrupts strategies revolving around Miraidon, Groudon and Kyogre's terrain and weather setting abilities. The given EV spread allows Terapagos to survive Collision Course from Koraidon on the physically defensive side and Electro Drift from Choice Specs Miraidon on the specially defensive side with Tera Shell active or while Terastallized. With the bulk the spread provides, Electro Drift becomes a guaranteed 3HKO with Leftovers recovery after Electric Terrain is removed. The Special Attack investment maximizes the value of Terapagos's Calm Mind boosts, the Speed investment lets it outpace 4 Speed investment Rillaboom, and the HP EVs maximize the recovery gained from Leftovers.

Rillaboom is a great partner for Terapagos, providing Grassy Terrain recovery and Fake Out to allow it to gain Calm Mind boosts. Incineroar is another great partner, as it can assist Terapagos in defeating Steel- and Ghost-types with Flare Blitz and Knock Off, as well as providing defensive utility through Intimidate, Parting Shot, and Will-O-Wisp on top of Fake Out. Amoonguss supports Terapagos very well, providing HP recovery with Pollen Puff. Its Rage Powder and Spore also allow Terapagos to safely use Calm Mind. Terapagos struggles to defeat Calyrex-I-centred teams, as it is very reliant on a partner Incineroar to reduce the physical damage it takes and deal super effective damage to Calyrex-I. Zamazenta-C can use Wide Guard, preventing Terapagos from dealing damage with Tera Starstorm while Terastallized, and Terapagos is very reliant on Earth Power as well as partners like Incineroar to deal super effective damage to it. As a result, Gholdengo pairs well with Terapagos, since it reliably checks both Calyrex-I and Zamazenta-C with its natural typing. Koraidon can be troublesome, as it can outdamage Terapagos's teammates' recovery while it is setting up with Calm Mind. Taunt Flutter Mane sets cause huge problems for Terapagos, since it cannot damage Flutter Mane significantly if Flutter Mane has not Terastallized, and Terapagos deals little damage without Calm Mind boosts.

Choice Specs.description:
Terapagos can be used as a hyper offensive threat with its high Special Attack and powerful spread move, Tera Starstorm. Choice Specs immediately boosts the damage output from Tera Starstorm, allowing Terapagos to pick up early-game KOs, which the more common Calm Mind set cannot. Its natural bulk in addition to Tera Shell allows it to withstand powerful attacks that other hyper offensive threats may not be able to. Terapagos has a very good matchup into the oppressive Calyrex-S with an immunity to Astral Barrage. Teraform Zero disrupts strategies revolving around Miraidon, Groudon and Kyogre's Terrain- and weather-setting abilities. Tera Starstorm is the attack Terapagos will want to use most of the time, but Earth Power and Dark Pulse provide coverage for Steel- and Ghost-types that its partners may not be able to comfortably defeat, like Zamazenta-C and Calyrex-S. Hyper Beam allows Terapagos to pick up KOs around Wide Guard users while Terastallized. Sleep Talk allows Terapagos to continue dealing significant damage even when put to sleep from moves such as Amoonguss's Spore.

With a middling Speed stat, Terapagos greatly benefits from Tailwind support, which allows it to outspeed and significantly damage its foes more effectively. Tornadus is the best priority Tailwind setter in the format, so it is naturally a great partner for Choice Specs Terapagos. It also deals super effective damage to Fighting-types that threaten Terapagos like the Urshifu formes. Tornadus can utilize priority Taunt to shut down Wide Guard users, most Trick Room setters, and Spore from opposing Amoonguss. Zamazenta-C is very difficult for Terapagos to defeat because of its natural typing and Wide Guard, so it relies on a partner Chi-Yu to defeat it or cripple its offense with Will-O-Wisp. Chi-Yu easily defeats Steel- and Ghost-types that Terapagos struggles against and provides Beads of Ruin support. Amoonguss provides great redirection support with Rage Powder in the face of threats such as Mienshao and both Urshifu formes, and it can shut down threats with Spore. Pollen Puff benefits Terapagos with healing, reactivating Tera Shell. Flutter Mane can check Koraidon with its natural typing as well as provide Icy Wind and Taunt support. Lunala is tough to break with its high natural bulk and Shadow Shield alongside Wide Guard, but a partner Incineroar can weaken its Special Attack and KO it with Snarl and Knock Off. Ting-Lu's great special bulk thanks to Assault Vest and Vessel of Ruin is very difficult for Terapagos to break through, and it can reduce Terapagos's Special Attack further with Snarl. This makes Urshifu-R a great partner, forcing Ting-Lu to Terastallize to remove its weakness to Urshifu-R's STAB moves while gaining a weakness to Terapagos. Koraidon can survive Tera Starstorm and threaten an OHKO on Terastallized Terapagos in return. A partner Flutter Mane forces Koraidon to Terastallize, making it weak to Terapagos. Pelipper is tough for Terapagos to break due to its access to Wide Guard and immunity to Earth Power, so it appreciates partners such as Raging Bolt to threaten Pelipper.

All-Out Attacker.description: An exclusive ability, powerful STAB Tera Starstorm, and access to a wide variety of coverage moves make Terapagos stand out as an incredible asset for Normal teams. By virtue of Tera Shell, full health Terapagos can check threats of the caliber of Mega Scizor, Iron Valiant, and Sneasler by taking a hit and dispatching them with the appropriate move afterwards. The combination of Flamethrower and Earth Power nails the Steel- and Rock-types resistant to Tera Starstorm such as Corviknight, Archaludon, and Mega Diancie. They also turn Terapagos into a notorious threat to Steel teams. Alternatively, Ice Beam OHKOes all Gliscor variants and targets important Dragon-, Flying-, and Ground-types like Dragonite, Zapdos, and both Landorus formes. Terapagos's offensive prowess allows it to have a good matchup against Gholdengo and some of the metagame's best entry hazard setters like Skarmory, Gliscor, and Hippowdon, thus making it an excellent user of Rapid Spin. The move also boosts Terapagos's Speed, letting it act as a revenge killer or sweep weakened teams late-game. The given EV spread maximizes Terapagos's power while letting it outrun Adamant Dragonite and Mamoswine, as well as Tapu Koko after a Rapid Spin. Physical wallbreakers like Mega Lopunny and Ursaluna are must-have partners, as they smash through the specially bulky Pokemon that trouble Terapagos such as Alolan Muk and Ting-Lu. Mega Pidgeot greatly appreciates Terapagos's hazard removal and, in turn, takes pressure off of Terapagos by revenge killing Fighting-types like Mega Gallade and Keldeo. Blissey and Porygon2 are sturdy walls that can soak most attacks thrown at Terapagos once Tera Shell is not active and they're able to bring it onto the field safely via Teleport. In particular, Blissey also lays down Stealth Rock and may replenish Terapagos's Tera Shell by using Wish to get it back at full health.

Offensive Utility.description:
Acting as a top-tier entry hazard remover with its unique ability and vast movepool, Terapagos is a solid addition to many teams that appreciate its perks. Ice Beam can be used in order to OHKO Landorus-T, Gliscor, and Garchomp, as well as significantly damaging Raging Bolt. Calm Mind allows Terapagos to become very threatening and hard to take down, 2HKOing Moltres, Mega Charizard Y, and Toxapex with Tera Starstorm after a boost. The Special Defense raise allows Terapagos to use its bulk to challenge foes such as Tapu Lele and Gholdengo that can otherwise OHKO Terapagos lacking Tera Shell by using Fightinium Z. Flamethrower smacks Air Balloon Gholdengo as well as hits Ferrothorn and Mega Scizor for crippling damage. Earth Power allows Terapagos to nail Heatran and Glimmora while also hitting Mega Tyranitar for chip damage. Rapid Spin lets Terapagos assist its team with hazard removal while boosting Speed to allow it to threaten faster Pokemon like Tapu Koko, Mega Lopunny, and Zamazenta, setting it up for a potential sweep when used in conjunction with Calm Mind. Heavy-Duty Boots is vital in allowing Terapagos to keep its ability in the face of hazards, which can be useful for guaranteeing a Rapid Spin or stopping a potential sweep, such as one from Dragonite if packing Ice Beam.

Terapagos fits on bulky offense and balance teams that appreciate its reliability in entry hazard removal, benefitting Pokemon such as Mega Charizard Y and Volcarona lacking Heavy-Duty Boots. Terapagos's Normal typing allows it to switch into Ghost-type moves, which is vital in being a stopgap against Pokemon such as Gholdengo. Due to Terapagos's below average Speed and reliance on its ability, a defensive backbone is much appreciated with Pokemon such as Gholdengo and Zapdos, which can cover for Terapagos's Fighting weakness. Alomomola is a great teammate that can provide Wish passing, which is extremely valuable, as it allows Terapagos to regain Tera Shell if it has lost health beforehand.

battlestadiumsingles.comments:
Speed EV Benchmarks

  • 60 Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Ursaluna.

  • 76 Spe: This outspeeds Timid Ursaluna-B.

  • 100 Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Choice Scarf Landorus-T after using Rock Polish.

  • 140 Spe: This outspeeds Jolly Choice Scarf Urshifu formes after using Rock Polish.

  • 196 Spe: This outspeeds Speed-boosted Iron Treads after using Rock Polish.

  • 244+ Spe: This outspeeds Calyrex-S after a Speed boost from Rapid Spin.

  • 252+ Spe: This outspeeds Adamant Urshifu formes.

Double Dance.description:
• With an incredible ability to resist any attack at full HP and the completely unresisted Tera Starstorm after Terastallization, Terapagos is one of the most terrifying bulky sweepers in the game!

  • Rock Polish: Rock Polish ensures that Terapagos outspeeds most of the metagame, with only extremely fast Speed-boosted Pokemon such as Koraidon, Miraidon, Calyrex-S, and Flutter Mane outspeeding it.

  • Protect: Protect pairs excellently with Leftovers and Toxic Spikes support to whittle down foes and give Terapagos an even longer lifespan.

  • Earth Power versus Flamethrower: Using a coverage move over Protect doesn't make Terapagos as long-lasting, but it makes Terapagos less of a liability if a different Pokemon needs to Terastallize in a given match. Earth Power ruins Glimmora and does big damage to Miraidon and Zacian-C, while Flamethrower still hits Zacian-C and roasts the irritating Knock Off Scizor.

  • Leftovers: Besides benefitting Terapagos's impressive bulk, getting any chance to gain Tera Shell's effect back is devastating enough to seriously consider Leftovers.

Other Options

  • Rest and Chesto Berry: When Rest and Chesto Berry are combined, Terapagos has an easy way to gain Tera Shell's protection back! However, this combination won't work nearly as well with Toxic Spikes as Protect does and is very vulnerable to Knock Off.

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse nails Calyrex-S regardless of whether or not Terapagos is Terastallized, though the great coverage isn't all that useful after Terastallization.

  • Rapid Spin and an Attack IV of 31: Terapagos is great at removing entry hazards with Rapid Spin, especially since most foes won't expect it, plus Terapagos can still boost its Speed even if it's Taunted. As a bonus, Rapid Spin breaks Focus Sash on powerful users like Sneasler. However, Terapagos will now need 244 Speed EVs and a Timid nature to outspeed Calyrex-S after a Speed boost.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Almost Required: Terapagos is heavily dependent on Terastallization to transform into the incredibly bulky Terapagos-S. This is especially the case if Tera Starstorm is its only attack, meaning Terastallization is necessary to hit Ghost-types.

  • Terapagos-S: Tera Stellar is the only possible option for Terapagos, but thankfully Terapagos-S's incredible bulk and perfect coverage make Terastallizing worth it. However, Tera Shell is a fantastic ability for enabling setup, and Tera Starstorm actually does more damage to neutral targets when Terapagos is not Terastallized, so it shouldn't be in a rush to Terastallize either. Also, take special note of Teraform Zero; while its not the main selling point of Terapagos-S, clearing Koraidon's sun or Miraidon's Electric Terrain at the correct times can have a huge impact on the match!

EV Spreads

  • 172 HP EVs: This HP investment gives Terapagos maximum Leftovers recovery before Terastallizing and minimizes Terapagos-S's damage from entry hazards. It also ensures that +1 Psyshock from Calyrex-S will not 2HKO Terapagos-S after Leftovers recovery.

  • 100 Speed EVs versus 140 Speed EVs: 100 Speed EVs let Terapagos outspeed Jolly Choice Scarf Landorus-T, a common revenge killer. 140 Speed EVs will require losing some power, but they do enable Terapagos to outspeed Jolly Choice Scarf Urshifu formes, which can potentially revenge kill Terapagos-S with Close Combat.

Choice Specs.description:
• Terapagos's offensive power may seem underwhelming compared to most Restricted Pokemon, but Tera Starstorm hitting every Pokemon neutrally in its Stellar forme makes it a strong and easy-to-use Choice Specs threat!

  • Dark Pulse: Dark Pulse is Terapagos's best attack against Calyrex-S, making it especially important when Terapagos is not Terastallized.

  • Power Gem: Power Gem hits Ho-Oh and Tera Fire Koraidon without needing to Terastallize.

  • Dazzling Gleam versus Ice Beam: Dazzling Gleam ruins Koraidon that don't Terastallize, while Ice Beam does more damage to other Dragon-types, with Dragonite being a big target.

  • Earth Power versus Flamethrower: Earth Power deals huge damage to Tera Fire Koraidon while keeping Tera Shell in play, and it's good coverage against Steel-types like Zacian-C. Flamethrower goes all in against Steel-types, roasting Scizor and Corviknight in particular.

  • Healing Wish / Lunar Dance Support: A Healing Wish or Lunar Dance teammate lets Terapagos go on another Tera Starstorm rampage, pairing well with its superb bulk. Some good users of these include Latias, Cresselia, and Indeedee formes.

Other Options

  • Flash Cannon: Flash Cannon is Terapagos's most damaging attack against Flutter Mane, but its coverage is otherwise poor.

Tera Types

  • Tera Dependency - Very High: Terapagos needs to Terastallize into Terapagos-S in order to gain perfect coverage and bulk. However, if the flow of the match suggests a different Pokemon should Terastallize, Terapagos still has the useful Tera Shell and good coverage as backup, even if it's rather mediocre without Terastallization.

  • When to Terastallize: Before Terastallization, Tera Starstorm is actually more powerful, and the superb Tera Shell lets Terapagos revenge kill a wide variety of weakened Pokemon. Terastallizing before Terapagos has taken damage is often not advised, but it makes sense if predicting your opponent is difficult.

EV Spreads

  • 196 HP / 252 SpA / 60 Spe with Modest: This spread lets Terapagos outspeed the extremely powerful Jolly Ursaluna, which can OHKO it through Tera Shell with boosted Facade.

  • 236 HP / 68 Def / 204 SpA with Modest: This spread lets Terapagos survive Adamant Koraidon's Collision Course after it Terastallizes to get rid of the sunny weather.

  • 4 HP / 252 SpA / 252 Spe with Timid: Maximizing Speed allows Terapagos to outspeed Adamant Urshifu formes, which otherwise revenge kill Terapagos-S.

Pivot.description:
Pecharunt's insanely high Defense, valuable typing, and reliable recovery make it an excellent defensive pivot, wall, and support Pokemon, letting it check threats like Zamazenta, Ogerpon-W, Dragonite, and Rillaboom. Parting Shot keeps up momentum for the team and is a great way to safely bring in its teammates, especially by weakening the opposition beforehand. Malignant Chain is a powerful STAB move that, more importantly, can spread status, particularly against switch-ins like Ting-Lu and setup sweepers like Zamazenta and Dragonite, which Pecharunt can take advantage of further with its Poison Puppeteer. Similarly, Toxic can be used to cripple the aforementioned targets even more reliably and with greater PP to make it better at spreading status in longer games, coming at the cost of being walled by Clefable and lacking immediate damage against crucial foes in Ogerpon-W and Rillaboom. Shadow Ball gives it a consistent and decently strong move that pressures Pokemon immune to poison like Gholdengo, Iron Crown, and opposing Pecharunt hard. Foul Play punishes setup sweepers it's tasked to check hard, like Dragonite, Kyurem, and even Terastallized Ogerpon-W. Particularly preferred on teams with lack of hazard removal, Heavy-Duty Boots blocks residual damage from entry hazards that Pecharunt would have otherwise been susceptible to as it pivots in and out. Rocky Helmet lets it chip physical attackers it's supposed to check, punishing pivoting attempts from Cinderace, Ogerpon-W, and Rillaboom and improving its matchup against Zamazenta. Air Balloon is a good alternative to mitigate Pecharunt's Ground weakness, which is especially helpful for taking on Great Tusk, while providing an invaluable Spikes immunity similar to Heavy-Duty Boots. Tera Ghost removes its Ground weakness to totally spinblock Great Tusk and Iron Treads, with the added benefit of boosting its Ghost-type STAB move. Pecharunt can benefit greatly from two distinct EV spreads, with one maximizing Defense and the other Speed; a physically defensive spread allows it to take more hits from the likes of Zamazenta, Great Tusk, and Ogerpon-W, running enough Speed to get the jump on Jolly Kingambit, but maximum Speed investment ensures that Pecharunt is fast enough to outspeed Great Tusk and Gholdengo as well as Speed tie opposing Pecharunt.

The support provided by Pecharunt's ability to spread status and pivot to gain momentum makes it an excellent teammate for many teams, ranging from balance to offense. Pecharunt forms solid cores with Dark-type Pokemon, such as Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Darkrai; these Dark-type spam teams are extremely weak to Zamazenta, which Pecharunt can completely wall, and Iron Valiant, which Pecharunt can switch in on and threaten with Malignant Chain. On the other hand, these exact same Dark-types are threats to Pecharunt itself; having Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Ting-Lu as teammates can help deal with them. Pecharunt's Ghost typing allows it to block Rapid Spin from opposing Great Tusk and Iron Treads, providing support for teammates like Hisuian Samurott to spread their entry hazards and keep them up throughout the game. Bulky Ground-types like Landorus-T, Great Tusk, and Ting-Lu also synergize well with Pecharunt, taking advantage of its ability to block Rapid Spin to spread entry hazards of their own, and they help deal with Iron Moth, which is otherwise able to set up on Pecharunt quite easily. Pecharunt can also remove Toxic Spikes from the field, clearing the path for setup sweepers without Heavy-Duty Boots, such as Booster Energy Iron Valiant and Leftovers Zamazenta. Pecharunt struggles against some of the special attackers in the tier that can outspeed and prevent it from making any progress, such as Darkrai and Choice Scarf Gholdengo. Having powerful teammates like Iron Valiant and Kingambit can provide much-needed offensive support while also taking advantage of Pecharunt's Parting Shot to switch in on foes and set up safely. Landorus-T and Iron Treads can threaten Pecharunt significantly with their Ground-type attacks, and Gliscor can use Swords Dance to outpace the damage Pecharunt could do. Running Air Balloon, having a Ground-immune teammate like Landorus-T, or pivoting to a teammate like Kyurem or Ogerpon-W, can cover for this weakness and allow it to turn the matchup around in its favor. Pecharunt is also almost completely walled by Kingambit; Zamazenta and Great Tusk are great teammates to check Kingambit, and they can both be brought in safely with Parting Shot. Defensive teammates like Assault Vest Alomomola and Corviknight can cover for its defensive shortcomings to check foes like Great Tusk, Darkrai, and Iron Moth. They also form a solid VoltTurn core together with Pecharunt to support their offensive teammates, with Corviknight in particular also providing entry hazard removal.

Nasty Plot.description:
Pecharunt's good defensive typing, excellent physical bulk, and otherwise well-rounded stats make it a uniquely effective and highly disruptive wallbreaker with Nasty Plot. Recover provides longevity and ensures that Pecharunt can blanket check most physical attackers throughout a game. Alternatively, Destiny Bond can be run to trade Pecharunt for a KO, which can be especially useful after Pecharunt has already served its purpose and eliminated an opposing Great Tusk or Iron Treads beforehand. Heavy-Duty Boots lets Pecharunt switch in throughout a game without getting worn down by entry hazards. Air Balloon grants Pecharunt a temporary Ground immunity, making it a good spinblocker against Great Tusk and Iron Treads without needing to Terastallize and forcing threats like Dragonite and Enamorus to pop Pecharunt's Air Balloon and tank an attack before threatening it with their Ground-type attacks. Shuca Berry can accomplish a similar goal of temporarily sponging Ground-type attacks by letting Pecharunt survive a single Headlong Rush from Great Tusk, an Earth Power from Choice Specs Kyurem and Enamorus, or even a +2 Dragonite's Earthquake before hitting these threats back very hard. Shuca Berry also lets Pecharunt bluff Heavy-Duty Boots if entry hazards are not up, letting it more easily bait in Ground-type attacks and retaliate. The last two items have the added benefit of reducing Pecharunt's damage taken by Iron Valiant's Knock Off after they are consumed, allowing Pecharunt to check it more easily. Covert Cloak is an option that lets Pecharunt set up freely on one of its greatest checks, Garganacl, while also being handy in preventing Zamazenta's repeated Crunch from overwhelming it with the drops. Tera Ghost boosts Shadow Ball's damage output, allowing Pecharunt to OHKO both Iron Treads and Great Tusk after a Nasty Plot. Tera Water grants Pecharunt a solid neutral typing to take on common threats like Great Tusk, Kingambit, Gholdengo, and Ceruledge. A bulkier EV spread with maximum HP investment is used to handle foes like Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Ogerpon-W more easily while gaining more setup opportunities. However, a fully offensive EV spread can be used to guarantee the OHKO on foes like bulky Gholdengo, opposing Pecharunt, and Great Tusk after minor chip damage. In addition, with maximum Special Attack investment, Pecharunt notably 2HKOes Zamazenta with Malignant Chain.

Nasty Plot Pecharunt fits reasonably well on bulky offense and hyper offense teams. Teammates that struggle with Zamazenta and Iron Valiant, such as Kingambit, Hisuian Samurott, and Darkrai, make for strong teammates. Kingambit appreciates Pecharunt softening up walls like Iron Defense Corviknight, while Hisuian Samurott can utilize Ceaseless Edge's entry hazard support to make Pecharunt's wallbreaking capabilities even more fearsome or can itself serve as a secondary wallbreaker alongside Pecharunt. Teammates that check and force out the aforementioned Dark-types, like Enamorus, Iron Valiant, and Zamazenta itself make for strong partners. Iron Valiant and Zamazenta are especially useful against Kingambit, which Pecharunt struggles immensely against. Physically bulky Stealth Rock-setting Ground-types like Ting-Lu, Great Tusk, and Landorus-T are great teammates that appreciate Pecharunt's ability to keep their entry hazards up, and in return, they tend to handle opposing Ground-type attacks well. Kyurem and Ogerpon-W are strong teammates that can handle bulkier, Poison-immune threats that Pecharunt struggles to break past, such as Garganacl, Gliscor, and Clodsire. Ogerpon-W and Kyurem greatly appreciate Pecharunt's ability to handle Zamazenta and Iron Valiant in return. Lastly, while it lacks Gholdengo's coveted Defog and Mortal Spin immunities, Pecharunt is a good alternative spinblocker for Sticky Web teams since it outspeeds and greatly threatens Great Tusk, ensuring that Sticky Web remains against teams that rely on it as their only form of hazard removal.

Defensive Pivot.description:
Boasting a sky-high Defense stat, Pecharunt provides amazing role compression for offensive and balance teams needing a reliable pivot and spinblocker. Many of the fastest offensive threats such as Zamazenta, Iron Valiant, and Mega Lopunny can easily pick off unprepared offense teams, and Pecharunt provides a stopgap to them while also keeping up momentum for its own team. Even the tier's prominent Ground-types like Great Tusk and Landorus-T don't want to switch into Malignant Chain, given the threat of being badly poisoned and reducing their defensive capabilities immensely. Similarly, Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott and Mega Tyranitar don't appreciate switching directly into Pecharunt because of Malignant Chain. Parting Shot allows Pecharunt to take a hit and switch out into a hard-hitting teammate, such as Urshifu-R, to threaten Pecharunt's checks like Mega Tyranitar and Kingambit. Heavy-Duty Boots allows Pecharunt to pivot more effectively without having to worry about entry hazards putting it in range of being OHKOed by attacks it would otherwise withstand. Alternatively, Pecharunt can run Black Sludge to increase its longevity if the team has sturdy hazard removal. Air Balloon is used to more effectively block Rapid Spin against Great Tusk and Iron Treads, and to add a Ground immunity to offensive teams. Darkinium Z paired with Parting Shot is a niche option that allows Pecharunt to give a low HP teammate a second chance at breaking through defensive structures or sweeping against already weakened teams.

Pecharunt fits well on offensive and balance teams for its ability to threaten poison and confusion on defensive Pokemon such as Landorus-T and Moltres and to keep up momentum for powerful wallbreakers, especially for teams needing a solid check to Fighting-types, most notably Zamazenta and Mega Lopunny. Pecharunt pairs well with Dark-type Pokemon, which cover Pecharunt's weakness to Psychic-types like Tapu Lele, Mega Latios, and Galarian Slowking in exchange for safety against Fighting-types. Mega Tyranitar, Hisuian Samurott, and Ting-Lu in particular form nice cores with Pecharunt as they can check Psychic- and Ghost-types while also setting up entry hazards for Pecharunt to even further weaken its checks upon switching in. Pecharunt can be paired with Gholdengo holding Ghostium Z to threaten the likes of Ferrothorn, Galarian Slowking, and Iron Crown that might switch into it trying to absorb a Malignant Chain. Late-game sweepers like Iron Valiant love Pecharunt's ability to spread status and pivot them in safely. Finally, Kingambit isn't threatened by Pecharunt's STAB moves, so it's good to Parting Shot out into a Fighting-type teammate like Zamazenta, Urshifu-R, or Great Tusk that can easily deal with it, though Pecharunt should be mindful of the occasional Defiant or Pursuit Kingambit.

Nasty Plot.description:
Pecharunt's outstanding bulk and typing alongside its solid STAB combination give it prime opportunities to sweep. With access to Nasty Plot, Pecharunt becomes very hard to switch into, especially when combined with Malignant Chain's ability to badly poison and limit the defensive utility of Ground-types like Landorus-T and Ting-Lu. Hex can be used over Shadow Ball to do more damage to Gliscor and already poisoned Pokemon, but there are many Steel- and Poison-type Pokemon such as Melmetal, Heatran, and Toxapex that take little damage from an unboosted Hex, so Shadow Ball is preferred for consistency. Recover can provide repeated defensive utility on teams that have a tough time dealing with Fighting-types like Zamazenta and Urshifu-R, both of which Pecharunt can set up on safely. Ghostium Z is used to power up Pecharunt's Shadow Ball to insane heights, and can lure checks to its much more common pivot set like Ferrothorn, Melmetal, and Heatran and free them up for teammates like Tapu Lele and Iron Valiant. At +2 Special Attack, Never-Ending Nightmare OHKOes Ferrothorn and Toxapex. Pecharunt's EV spread allows it to survive a Headlong Rush from offensive Great Tusk or two Earth Powers from Terapagos at full health to spinblock more effectively as well as OHKO Great Tusk back with unboosted Never-Ending Nightmare. 168 Speed EVs lets it outspeed Modest Heatran.

Pecharunt fits well on bulky offense teams needing a spinblocker that can double as a set-up sweeper. Mega Latios and Mega Diancie are two partners that work in tandem with Pecharunt to break each other's checks. Mega Latios appreciates Pecharunt's ability to bruise Ting-Lu, Mega Tyranitar and Galarian Slowking, and Mega Diancie similarly dislikes these as well as Toxapex and Assault Vest Melmetal, all of which Pecharunt can deal with or severely dent. In turn, Mega Latios can pressure Mega Charizard Y and Ground-types like Great Tusk and Landorus-T, while Mega Diancie threatens Dark-types such as Hisuian Samurott and can often wallbreak so that Pecharunt is able to clean up. Pecharunt threatens Fighting-types like Zamazenta and Iron Valiant and therefore pairs well with Dark-type teammates like Mega Tyranitar, Hisuian Samurott, and Ting-Lu that can set up entry hazards that Pecharunt can spinblock for. Landorus-T and Gliscor are potential teammates that can avoid Ground-type attacks and function as a hazard setter and pivot for Pecharunt and its teammates to come in safely. Without Heavy-Duty Boots or Air Balloon mitigating hazards, Pecharunt is less consistent against what it normally checks, and this set lacks the utility to Parting Shot out of these Pokemon for momentum. This also means Pecharunt becomes less effective as a spinblocker against opposing Great Tusk and Terapagos, making hazard removal from Great Tusk, Zapdos, and Landorus-T good for Pecharunt's longevity. Pecharunt's STAB moves are stonewalled by Kingambit, Mega Tyranitar, and Ursaluna as well as other Dark-types like Ting-Lu, so it should be paired with Zamazenta or Great Tusk to cover these threats. Lastly, Pecharunt is outsped by many special attackers in the tier and therefore likes support from allies like Assault Vest Melmetal, Kingambit, and Ting-Lu in checking Tapu Lele, Mega Latios, and offensive Gholdengo.

Air Balloon.description:
• Malignant Chain can threaten common Fairy- and Grass-type Pokemon like Iron Valiant and Ogerpon-W. Its high poison chance can also wear down bulky Pokemon without relying on Curse.
  • Curse lets Pecharunt whittle down any foe behind Substitute regardless of typing, including Registeel and SubSeed Ogerpon-W.
  • The combination of Parting Shot and Recover lets Pecharunt neutralize virtually all non-Taunt, neutrally effective attackers like Iron Hands and non-Choice Specs Primarina while keeping itself healthy.
  • The Speed investment lets Pecharunt outspeed neutral-natured base 60 Speed Pokemon like Primarina and Maximum investment base 50 Speed Pokemon like Donphan and Ursaluna. The remaining investment is in HP and Defense for maximum bulk for powerful Ground-type attackers like Assault Vest Landorus-T.
  • Air Balloon prevents an opposing Ground-type move from being used on Pecharunt once , which can completely shut down Choice-locked Ground-types like Choice Band Landorus-T and Choice Band Ursaluna or can provide an opportunity for a Parting Shot to be used on Pokemon like Assault Vest Ursaluna.
  • Against SubSeed Ogerpon-W, Curse shouldn't be used until after Parting Shot to minimize the damage from Ivy Cudgel so that Curse can be used safely.
  • Despite Air Balloon, Pecharunt still struggles with Ground-types like Landorus-I, Life Orb Landorus-T, and or Attack Booster Great Tusk, so pairing it with a Water- or Ice-type like Primarina or Chien-Pao can be helpful.

Leftovers.description:
• Malignant Chain can seriously threaten Iron Valiant and Ogerpon-W.
